11104521.label: Major findings and research outcome
11104521.value: • Target specificity of plasticity: NO enhanced both excitatory and reduced inhibitory synaptic protein density in L1. Optogenetic mapping revealed that enhanced recurrent excitation onto SP cells is matched by decreased PV mediated inhibition, indicating coordinated circuit level scaling. • Molecular correlates: NO enhanced both excitatory and reduced inhibitory synaptic protein density in L1. • Causality of TNF α: Genetic loss of function blocked coordinated EPSC/IPSC scaling, demonstrate that TNF α is necessary for the observed homeostatic adjustments. Part of this GRF’s work was published in (1) a research article, Guo & Lau, 2022; DOI: 10.3389/fnins.2022.824454, documenting the core TNF α findings; (2) a virtual poster entitled, “TNF α orchestrates experience-dependent plasticity of excitatory and inhibitory synapses in the anterior piriform cortex, CG Lau, A Guo” at an online conference, AChemS meeting (Association for Chemoreception Sciences), in February, 2022; (3) a poster entitled, “Activation of parvalbumin interneurons in the anterior piriform cortex alleviates seizures in temporal lobe epilepsy” at the Gordon Research Conference 2023: Inhibition in the CNS, Switzerland, in 2023, where the PI (Lau) was the presenter. Follow up manuscripts detail circuit mapping and receptor specificity. This GRF supported the travels and dissemination of research work of PhD student, Huiqi ZHANG, for her travels to the Society for Neuroscience meeting in Washington, DC, US in 2023. Collectively, these outcomes advance understanding of molecular to circuit mechanisms of sensory plasticity and suggest new avenues for exploring cytokine roles in learning, sensory dysfunction, and neuroimmune interactions in cortical circuits. In this project, I hired three CityUHK undergraduate students as Campus Internship Scheme (CIS) student helpers, training them to perform experiments in the lab (CHU Wen Kei, LEUNG Chung Yan, and KHAN Abdul Raffay). I taught them how to perform, analyze and evaluate immunofluorescent microscopy of fixed brain sections, and to present these results in a coherent manner. CHU Wen Kei graduated from CityUHK with a First-Class Honors in BSc in Biological Sciences degree. LEUNG Chung Yan graduated from CityUHK with a First-Class Honors in BEng in Biomedical Engineering degree (with a minor in Creative Media). KHAN Abdul Raffay graduated from CityUHK with a BEng in Biomedical Engineering. Additionally, I recruited a PhD student, LI Nanqin, to perform research in my lab on this GRF project (PhD studies still on-going).

11104521.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11104521.value: This GRF started on 1 September 2021 and was scheduled to end on 31 Aug, 2024. We applied for, and were pleased to be granted, an extension of six months with a new completion date of 28 February, 2025. We have achieved 100% of the proposed objectives. However, research activity was hampered by COVID-19 and student access to the laboratory was limited during times, which slowed our research progress. Moreover, many conferences were delayed or canceled, restricting the dissemination our results and reducing exposure of students to intense scientific discussions and learning experience. To further explore the role of neuro-immune interactions APC synaptic plasticity, we can examine (1) the mechanisms by which TNF-α alters the physiology of astrocyte and microglia in APC and (2) the precise neural activity by which TNF-α and its promoter is activated by using different activation patterns controlled by electrical or optogenetic stimulation in vivo.

11104521.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11104521.value: The anterior piriform cortex (APC), the largest area of the brain dedicated to processing smells, plays a crucial role in how we perceive and learn about different odors. However, the ways in which its neural circuitry is influenced by experiences and immune molecules remain unclear. In this study, we explored how blocking one nostril — a method known as naris occlusion — affects the excitatory and inhibitory synapses that form the fundamental components of local cortical circuits. Within the APC, there are two primary types of output neurons: SL and SP neurons. Here we revealed that naris occlusion coordinately regulates their excitatory and inhibitory synapses, with distinct effects in different cortical layers. Additionally, we discovered that naris occlusion has a more pronounced impact on a specific subtype of inhibitory interneuron, known as parvalbumin interneurons, compared to the somatostatin interneurons. Importantly, using genetic knockout technology, we identified an unexpected connection between the immune molecule TNF α and synaptic plasticity in the APC — plasticity effects were completely abrogated. Overall, our findings reveal a novel form of plasticity in the APC that depends on the immune molecule TNF α, opening new avenues for understanding its role in olfactory perceptual learning.

11104821.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11104821.value: The frequency of the occurrence, and geographic expansion, of benthic dinoflagellates, have been affected by global climate change and human activities, and pose a great threat to human health and marine ecosystems. Benthic dinoflagellates such as the genus Gambierdiscus, Prorocentrum and Amphidinium are sources of potent marine toxins, including ciguatoxins (CTXs), okadaic acid, dinophysistoxins and amphidinols. CTXs are the most common non-bacterial algal toxins infecting humans. It is estimated that hundreds of thousands of people are affected annually, often with significant long-term health effects. “HABs in Benthic Systems” was launched as a Core Research Project in the Global Ecology and Oceanography of Harmful Algal Blooms research program; and benthic algae and ciguatera fish poisoning (CFP) as new research topics have attracted a high level of concern for international marine research institutions and governments. Studies show that the majority of toxigenic benthic dinoflagellates are distributed between the 35° north and south latitudes, but recent studies have documented their presence in subtropical and even temperate areas, together with novel species of toxic dinoflagellates. These benthic dinoflagellates attach on marine substrates, macroalgae and coral rubble in coral reef ecosystems, and are easily accessible to marine herbivores and filter feeders. Lipophilic algal toxins are shown to be bio-transferred and -transformed along trophic levels, which eventually threaten human lives upon seafood consumption. The aim of our project is to conduct a joint sampling effort with our collaborators in Hong Kong, mainland China, Malaysia, and Taiwan, where toxic dinoflagellates have often been reported. Benthic dinoflagellates will be isolated and identified using both molecular analysis and chemical profiling to reveal the relationship of toxin production and biogeographic characteristics in the coral communities of the Asian region. Combined with traditional toxicity analysis, the bioaccessibility model will reveal trophic transformation and transfer of toxins, which contribute to the fate and chemical kinetics of detoxification in marine ecosystems. With the successful large-scale cultivation of targeted microalgae, potential novel algal toxins will be identified and isolated using high resolution mass spectrometry techniques as a region-specific source. This study will promote the understanding of algal toxins in Asian waters and establish standard operational procedures for bioactive screening of benthic dinoflagellates and their associated microbiota and thus contribute to seafood safety assessment. 受全球氣候變化和人類活動的影響，底棲甲藻的發生頻率增加，發生區域擴大，對人類健康和海洋生態系統構成巨大威脅。底棲甲藻，如 Gambierdiscus、Prorocentrum 和 Amphidinium 等種屬是強力海洋毒素包括雪卡毒素、岡田酸、鰭藻毒素和兩性酚等的來源。 雪卡毒素是最常見的感染人類的非細菌藻毒素。據估計，每年有數十萬人中毒，而且通常會對人類健康產生長期影響。“底棲生態系統中的有害藻華”作為有害藻華研究計劃的全球生態學和海洋學核心研究項目啟動。底棲藻類和雪卡魚中毒作為新的研究課題引起了國際海洋研究機構和政府的高度關注。研究表明，大多數產毒底棲甲藻分佈在北緯和南緯 35°之間，但最近的研究發現在亞熱帶甚至溫帶地區也存在底棲甲藻以及其新物種。這些底棲甲藻附著在珊瑚礁生態系統中的海洋基質、大型藻類和珊瑚碎石上，並且很容易被海洋食草動物和濾食動物捕食。親脂性藻毒素沿著營養級進行生物轉移和轉化，最終影響及威脅人類的健康與生命。 本項目將與合作夥伴分別在亞洲多個有有毒甲藻報告的海域進行聯合採樣。我們將使用分子和化學手段來分離與鑒定底棲甲藻，以揭示亞洲地區珊瑚群落中有毒甲藻毒素產生和生物地理特徵的關係。結合傳統的毒性分析，生物利用度模型揭示毒素的營養轉化和轉移，這有助於了解毒素在海洋生態系統中的歸趨和化學動力學。隨著目標微藻的成功大規模培養，我們將使用高解析度質譜技術來識別和分離潛在的新型藻毒素，了解毒素成分的地區特異性。本研究將促進對亞洲海域藻類毒素的瞭解，並為底棲甲藻及其相關微生物的生物活性篩選建立標準操作方法，從而有助於海產品的安全評估。

11200121.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11200121.value: 由於窗戶的光學管理和隔熱能力不佳，在建築中造成了大量的能源消耗（20-40%）。過往的研究研發出了多款原理不一的智能窗戶，如熱致變色/電致變色/光致變色智能窗戶，以減少窗戶帶來的熱量獲得/損失。然而大多數窗戶均由玻璃製成的，具有重量大、易破碎和隔熱差等缺點。在這項研究中，我們提出把一種新型的熱致變色透明木質複合材料 (TTWC)運用到智能窗戶中，在夏季阻擋太陽輻射降低室内溫度，而在冬季則允許太陽輻通過以保持溫暖的室內環境，減少室內製冷、供暖和照明所需的能源。TTWC具有高太陽光透過率及調節能力、隔熱性能好、重量輕、機械性能優越、延展性高（可消除安全問題），以及可持續等眾多優點。該項目旨在開發 TTWC 並基礎地研究它的光學和熱致變色特性，從微觀角度理解木材結構中產生的光散射所形成的熱致變色現象。我們初步成功製備了具有智能調光能力的TTWC，其平均可見光透過率為 ~61% ，同時太陽光調製能力（冷熱狀態之間的太陽光透過率差異）為~38%，表明其可以達到預期的透明度和熱致變色能力。 儘管取得了良好的結果，但由於熱致變色材料對木材光學管理能力的影響尚不明晰，TTWC的太陽光調製能力仍有待提升，以及衆多技術難題仍需解決。因此，本研究將首先建立全面的光學模型用於基礎地研究具有不規則木纖維形狀的木材中的光散射。接下來，該光學模型將被進一步考慮由熱致變色材料分散在TTWC中造成的米式散射。一些與模型相關的參數，如具有不同折射率的多種木製材料，以及熱致變色材料的種類、濃度和顆粒大小等都將包含在該模型中來研究TTWC 的光學和熱致變色特性。在該模型的指導下，我們將進一步製備、表徵和優化TTWC。模型計算結果也將與實驗結果進行對比以驗證模型。最後，經優化的TTWC將被安裝使用在樣板房中，並在不同條件下進行實地試驗以評估其應用於智能窗戶中的節能效果。總的來說，這項研究不僅可以揭示熱致變色材料對分級微結構材料的影響及其相對應的光學和熱致變色特性，也開闢了研發熱致變色智能窗戶的新方向。

11200121.label: Realisation of objectives
11200121.value: Realization of Objective 1 To achieve objective 1, we successfully developed an optical model capable of describing light propagation within transparent wood, with a specific focus on the realistic, irregular morphology of wood fibers. The optical model development commenced by utilizing Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM) to observe the specific geometry of wood fibers, including fiber diameter and cell wall thickness of the wood species used. These morphological parameters served as direct inputs into a Gaussian random fiber model, which successfully generated realistic, irregular wood fiber shapes for simulation. Using these generated geometries, we employed a Monte Carlo ray-optics method to calculate the light scattering coefficient and light absorption coefficient. In this method, a massive number of light rays were generated in varying directions and propagated through the simulated fibers to count the rays absorbed or scattered. The refractive indices of the wood and the matching materials were precisely measured using a spectroscopic ellipsometer to ensure simulation accuracy. Then, a four-flux radiative transfer model was developed to simulate the light propagation in the transparent wood, considering both collimated and diffuse fluxes in forward and backward directions. We solved the differential equations governing these fluxes by calculating the total absorption and scattering coefficients as a sum of the contributions from the refractive-index matching material and the statistical average of the wood fibers. By solving for the collimated and diffuse light fluxes and applying Fresnel Equations, we successfully determined the broadband optical transmittance and reflectance spectra. To verify this model, various transparent wood samples were fabricated by delignifying wood and infiltrating it with refractive-index matching polymers, including PVA, PVP, PMMA, and epoxy. The experimental optical properties, specifically the luminous transmittance and optical haze, were characterized using a UV-Vis-NIR spectrophotometer equipped with an integrating sphere. The experimental results showed a strong correlation with the modeling outputs and matched the simulated spectra. Realization of Objective 2 For objective 2, the optical model developed in objective 1 was modified to incorporate the Mie scattering effect induced by thermochromic particles, enabling a fundamental investigation of light propagation in Thermochromic Transparent Wood Composite (TTWC). The thermochromic particles included W-doped VO2 and hydrogels, which have particle sizes that are comparable to the wavelength of incident light. We updated the four-flux model by introducing new terms to the absorption and scattering coefficients to explicitly represent the volume fraction, absorption coefficient, and scattering coefficient of the thermochromic particles. The specific optical parameters of these particles were derived by inputting their refractive indices (measured via ellipsometry) and particle sizes (measured via Transmission Electron Microscopy, TEM) into the Mie scattering solution of the Helmholtz Equation. In this way, the optical behavior of composites containing various concentrations and types of thermochromic materials with the irregular wood fiber matrix were successfully simulated. Then, we fabricated TTWC samples using the proposed thermochromic materials and characterized their switching performance. We measured the luminous transmittance at both the cold state and the hot state using a UV-Vis-NIR spectrophotometer. Furthermore, we calculated the solar modulation ability by integrating the solar transmittance spectra over the 300 nm to 2500 nm range, covering both visible and near-infrared regions. The transition temperature was also determined by analyzing the first derivative of transmittance versus temperature. The simulated luminous transmittance and solar modulation ability aligned well with the experimentally measured results. The modified optical model provided a deep understanding of how particle size and concentration influence the luminous transmittance and solar modulation ability. Realization of Objective 3 To achieve objective 3, we conducted optimization of TTWC and fabricated the optimized TTWC based on the theoretical study and the optical model developed in objective 1 and 2. The optimization process involved extensive simulations using the developed optical model to analyze a matrix of design parameters, including wood species, thickness, and the concentration of thermochromic particles. We identified a critical trade-off: increasing the concentration of thermochromic particles improved the solar modulation ability but reduced the luminous transmittance. Hence, we established an optimization criterion to maximize luminous transmittance while maintaining a solar modulation ability sufficient for effective energy savings. Following the fabrication of the optimized TTWC, we conducted a comprehensive characterization of its mechanical and thermal properties. For mechanical properties, the optimized TTWC was subjected to tensile testing using a universal testing machine to generate the stress-strain curve, based on which, Young's Modulus and toughness were calculated. Results showed that the optimized TTWC maintained the structural integrity of the wood, yielding stress values comparable to original wood. For thermal properties, we measured the thermal diffusivity of the optimized TTWC. By multiplying the thermal diffusivity with the specific heat capacity measured via Differential Scanning Calorimetry (DSC) and the density, the thermal conductivity of the optimized TTWC was determined. The results confirmed a low thermal conductivity value, significantly superior to conventional glass. Furthermore, durability tests were conducted by cycling the material between hot and cold states. The optimzied TTWC exhibited stable optical switching performance over repeated cycles, validating its potential for long-term application. Realization of Objective 4 For Objective 4, an indoor test in a controlled environment and an outdoor field test were conducted to evaluate the energy-saving performance of the optimized TTWC. For the indoor test, we constructed four identical model houses using acrylic and placed them within a Controlled Environment Chamber (CEC). To simulate solar radiation, we employed a Class BBB Solar Simulator. The four model houses were equipped with a conventional glass window, a traditional thermochromic smart window, a multi-pane glass window, and the optimized TTWC window for comparison. Thermocouples and lux meters were placed both inside and outside the model houses to continuously monitor the air temperature and illuminance. By varying the ambient air temperature and humidity within the CEC, we simulated different climatic conditions to assess the TTWC's energy-saving performance in different climate conditions. For the outdoor test, the four model houses were placed in an outdoor open area to account for real-world environmental variables. A weather station positioned near the model houses provided real-time data on solar irradiance, ambient temperature, humidity, and wind velocity. The outdoor test was conducted over a full day across different seasons to capture a wide range of weather conditions. By comparing the indoor air temperature of the TTWC-equipped house against the house with conventional glass, we quantified the reduction in heat gain during hot periods and heat loss during cold periods. The data demonstrated that despite the TTWC having slightly lower optical transmittance compared to clear glass, it offered superior energy efficiency due to its thermochromic regulation and low thermal conductivity. The reduced indoor temperature fluctuations implied a significant decrease in the energy required for HVAC systems. Furthermore, we assessed the scalability and practicality of the technology. The compatibility of the fabrication process with rotary-cut wood veneer suggests that the TTWC technology is scalable for industrial manufacturing. The results of this objective confirmed that the TTWC is not only a scientifically novel material but a feasible, energy-efficient alternative to traditional glazing in the building construction industry.

11200121.label: Major findings and research outcome
11200121.value: Concerning the optical study, we established a rigorous optical modeling framework based on the Mie scattering theory and Maxwell’s equations to simulate light proppagation within novel functional materials such as the thermochromic transparent wood composite. The effect of structural parameters, such as the size distribution and concentration of scattering centers, on the optical properties of the material were investigated, demonstrating that a multi-dispersed system of scattering centers yields superior broadband scattering efficiency compared to monodispersed systems, which is essential for optimizating thermochromic transparent wood composite with irregular fiber shapes and thermochromic particles. Besides, our fundamental study on the anisotropic scattering effect of the transparent wood confirmed the importance of the wood’s internal microstructure in light management, and a cross-ply lamination technique was found to control the orientation of the wood fibers and effectively tune the angular distribution of light scattering. Specifically, the work demonstrated that the anisotropic scattering inherent to the wood structure can significantly enhance the light utilization of the composite by directing incident light. The ability to manipulate light scattering via fiber orientation is a key structural finding that can be applied to the design and optimization of thermochromic transparent wood composite [item 2 in the table in Part C]. After optical study, we successfully designed, fabricated, and characterized a mechanically robust thermochromic transparent wood composite. The optimzied thermochromic transparent wood composite showed a good solar modulation ability of 21.6% and good stability by enduring 200 heating-cooling cycles without performance degradation. This thermochromic transparent wood composite exhibited enhanced mechanical properties, reporting a high tensile strength of 71.4 MPa and flexural strength of 93.1 MPa, along with superior thermal insulation evidenced by a low thermal conductivity of 0.247 W/(m⋅K). Next, the feasibility and energy-saving performance of the thermochromic transparent wood composite were estimated through both field testing and numerical simulation. The model house field tests demonstrated a significant indoor air temperature reduction of up to 5.40 ℃ compared to normal glass. Based on the field tests results, numerical simulations were conducted via EnergyPlus, showing an energy savings of 12.4% for HVAC systems in the Hong Kong climate [item 1 in the table in Part C]. Furthermore, we found fabrication techniques of using transparent wood as a robust host for various functional materials [item 3 and 4 in the table in Part C].

11200121.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11200121.value: While this project establishes the fundamental feasibility of Thermochromic Transparent Wood Composite (TTWC), bridging the gap between laboratory prototypes and commercial building applications requires addressing specific material limitations. Unlike glass, the wood-based substrate is inherently combustible and hygroscopic. Therefore, a critical course of action for future development involves the investigation and application of non-flammable and waterproof coatings. It is essential to rigorously test whether these protective layers degrade the optimized optical performance achieved in this study. Furthermore, to ensure practical viability, comprehensive durability studies must be conducted. TTWC's UV stability, hardness, and stiffness when subjected to environmental stressors such as strong winds and heavy rain should be evaluated. To confirm the environmental sustainability of TTWC, the end-of-life recyclability of TTWC should also be accessed. Beyond the material aspect development of TTWC, the novel optical model developed in this research holds significant potential for broader scientific application. The proposed course of action includes adapting this model to investigate light scattering and optical transmittance in other hierarchically micro-structured materials, such as glass fiber composites or anisotropic polymers, thereby extending the project's impact beyond wood applications.

11200121.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11200121.value: In this project, we have successfully demonstrated the feasibility of using a Thermochromic Transparent Wood Composite (TTWC) as a smart window for energy-efficient buildings. The results indicated that the unique optical properties of the TTWC effectively regulated indoor temperature, promoting energy savings in air conditioning systems. Fundamental studies have also been conducted to investigate the light propagation mechanism in TTWC with the irregular wood fiber structure containing thermochromic particles. The results revealed that accurately modeling the light scattering effects, i.e., Mie scattering of thermochromic particles, was essential to optimize the balance between high transparency for visual comfort and effective solar heat blocking for energy saving. In addition, we have fabricated and tested an optimized TTWC window in a model house environment. Also, the thermal conductivity of the TTWC was found to be significantly lower than that of conventional glass, offering superior insulation. Overall, applying this smart window can automatically manage solar heat gain, leading to enhanced indoor comfort and energy efficiency. Therefore, this project helps to explore new directions for sustainable building materials, promoting the commercialization and application of eco-friendly alternatives to traditional glass windows.

11200421.value: 先進的第四代核反應爐的發展對結構材料提出了嚴格的要求，需要承受高溫和高輻射劑量。因此，先進核能的研發迫切需要能夠滿足這些要求的新材料，包括合金和陶瓷材料等。受最近開發的高熵合金中熵穩定概念的啟發，熵穩定的多主元過渡金屬碳化物 (MTMC) 由於其獨特的物理性質而受到越來越多的關注，例如低導熱率、高納米硬度、良好的抗氧化性，和出色的抗輻照性。在這些具有岩鹽結構的 MTMC 中，多種過渡金屬元素隨機佔據陽離子晶格位置，導致極端的化學無序和局部晶格畸變。與 高熵合金類似，預計化學無序對 MTMC 的輻照性能將產生深遠的影響。然而，儘管最近的實驗報導了一些 MTMCs 具有良好的抗輻照性，到目前為止，MTMCs 的無序狀態和輻照損傷機制仍然不清楚，尤其是無序的陽離子亞晶格和有序的碳亞晶格的混合如何有助於提高 MTMC 的抗輻照性能。 在這項研究中，我們旨在通過計算模擬揭示 MTMC 的輻照損傷機制，尤其是組元複雜性帶來的效應。通過系統地研究 (Nb0.25Ta0.25Ti0.25Zr0.25)C 系統及其衍生子系統，包括二元、三元和四元 MTMC，我們將解決有關 MTMC 輻照性能的三個關鍵科學問題。首先，我們將評估元素數量和元素種類對 MTMC 穩定性的影響。對於穩定相，我們將探索組元複雜性對不同 MTMC 的結構特性、晶格畸變、熱導率和成鍵特性的影響。其次，我們將揭示不同 MTMC 中的缺陷能量狀態和缺陷演化機制，揭示缺陷行為的控制性因素。最後，基於這些結果，我們將提出可能的方法來調整 MTMC 的組成和濃度，以進一步提高其耐輻照性。在這些研究中，我們將考慮非化學計量比的影響。 該項目的成功實施將促進對新型MTMCs輻照回應的全面瞭解，有利於抗輻照碳化物的設計和開發。該專案成果將為應用于未來核能系統中的先進陶瓷的研發提供必要的理論指導。

11200421.label: Major findings and research outcome
11200421.value: This research project establishes a comprehensive, integrated framework for the rational design of multicomponent transition metal carbide (MTMC), namely, high-entropy ceramic carbide (HECC) materials with tailored properties for extreme environments, specifically under irradiation and oxidation conditions. The work systematically addresses the grand challenge of navigating the immense compositional space of these materials by combining advanced computational modeling with experimental validation. A foundational understanding of atomic-scale behavior was first developed. Ab initio studies revealed that the partially disordered cation sublattice in MTMCs influences key defect properties. Specifically, carbon vacancies form more easily, promoting off-stoichiometry, while the kinetics of defect evolution are altered, explaining experimental observations of delayed damage accumulation. Furthermore, the generalized stacking fault energies in these complex ceramics were found to follow a rule of mixture, simplifying their prediction. For irradiation tolerance, a critical parameter—the Frenkel pair recombination barrier—was identified as the key indicator in rocksalt ceramics, with high-entropy carbonitrides showing significant improvement over simpler carbides. Building on this atomic-scale insight, machine learning (ML) models were developed to efficiently explore the vast compositional landscape. One model accurately predicts the single-phase formability of both equiatomic and non-equiatomic HECCs, enabling the rapid identification of new, stable compositions and the construction of comprehensive phase diagrams. A separate ML model was created to predict mechanical properties and structural distortions, leading to new design principles. This approach identified that local lattice distortions, linked to elemental adaptability to the crystal structure, govern mechanical characteristics, and recommended high-strength V-Nb-Ta-based compositions. Finally, this knowledge was applied to optimize oxidation resistance—a critical property for high-temperature applications. A computational framework identified that regulating preferential oxidation by tuning the oxygen adsorption energy of constituent elements is key. Multi-objective optimization balanced this with thermodynamic stability to pinpoint compositions with intrinsic oxidation immunity. The theory-guided strategy of depleting elements with high oxygen adsorption energy (e.g., Nb, Ta) was experimentally validated, demonstrating superior performance in designed HECs compared to their equiatomic counterparts. In conclusion, this integrated multi-scale methodology, bridging atomic-scale simulation, data-driven discovery, and experimental proof, paves a broad avenue for the rational design of next-generation high-entropy ceramics with exceptional and tunable properties for applications in extreme environments. As a result of the project support, a total of 14 SCI papers were published, and one research student has graduated and obtained here PhD degree.

11200421.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11200421.value: Further development of the research will mainly rely on experimental validations. A primary course of action is the experimental validation and property mapping of the newly proposed compositions, such as the high-strength V-Nb-Ta-based carbides and oxidation-resistant NbTa-depleted HECs, under real-world thermo-mechanical and corrosive conditions. The framework itself can be expanded by integrating the separate ML models for phase stability, mechanical properties, irradiation resistance, and oxidation resistance into a unified multi-objective optimization platform. This would allow for the simultaneous design of ceramics that are stable, strong, and oxidation/irradiation-tolerant. Furthermore, the principles should be extended beyond carbides and carbonitrides to other ceramic families (e.g., borides, oxides) to test their universality.

11200421.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11200421.value: Instead of using one or two main components, high-entropy materials are produced by mixing multiple components (as many as four or five) together to form a new class of materials. This class of materials usually outperforms their single-component counterparts. The problem is, with so many ingredients, finding the best recipe is like searching for a needle in a haystack. Our project tackled this by using computer simulations and artificial intelligence to quickly sort through thousands of possible combinations. We discovered the secret rules that make these mixtures stable, strong, and resistant to extreme radiation in environments of nuclear reactors. It's like finding the perfect cake recipe by understanding how each ingredient works together, rather than just guessing. We then used these rules to design new, superior high-entropy carbide materials and proved in the lab that they perform even better than standard versions. This work provides a smart, fast blueprint for creating next-generation high entropy ceramics materials that will enable technological leaps in areas from aerospace to clean energy, making future technologies safer and more powerful.

11200621.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11200621.value: 退化是指產品/系統性能特徵隨著時間的累積衰退過程，例如輪胎磨損和電池容量減少等。 大數據時代使同時監測與系統健康狀態密切相關的多個退化信號成為可能，多源數據獲取更為便捷，但從混雜數據中挖掘有用資訊成為了新的問題，也亟待提出針對性的系統可靠性評估和管理分析方法。 當前基於多元退化數據的可靠性分析研究主要側重於類比多個退化特徵量的依賴性，而如何正確地將動態異質性納入多元退化模型，是一個重要而具有挑戰性的問題。 此外，為防止發生災難性故障以確保系統安全，開展系統可靠性分析和預測性維護等相關研究也具有重要的意義。 本項目通過研究新的可靠性分析和管理框架來彌補這一差距。 首先我們將構建隨機過程模型來描述多元退化和可觀測動態中變數的影響因素，如相對濕度和工作模式，可用於預測在複雜環境下隨時間變化的系統壽命。 基於實際工程應用中常見的設備維護策略，我們亦將制定新的統計模型，以量化維護策略的效果。 以數據驅動的方式對新模型的參數估計和統計推斷方法開展研究。 之後再提出一個在線/即時壽命預測框架，旨在減少意外故障造成的系統停機損失，形成更優的維護計劃。 工況動態性導致數據異質性，致使機器學習模型泛化能力差，從而無法精確評估系統可靠性，為此，該專案還將改進前沿機器學習方法，以應對異質性和動態性對建模與評估帶來的若干挑戰。 該專案中提出的方法將從理論和實踐兩個角度推進退化建模及系統健康評估與管理的研究和應用。

11200621.label: Realisation of objectives
11200621.value: We have engaged PhD students and postdocs to work on this project. Some also had very relevant experience. The objectives are fully achieved with some additional issues considered. Below is a detailed description of the work done for each objective. Objective 1: To develop a multivariate degradation model with consideration to the influence of dynamic covariates The development of comprehensive multivariate degradation models has been accomplished through two complementary approaches that effectively incorporate dynamic covariates. The primary contribution involved creating an integrated control model that captures the mutual influence between production processes and system deterioration. A comprehensive framework based on an infinite-horizon Markov decision process was established, incorporating condition monitoring data as dynamic covariates to enable real-time decision-making adjustments (Zhang et al., 2025). This model addresses a critical gap in existing literature by moving beyond unidirectional dependencies to consider bidirectional relationships between production activities and degradation states. Monotonic structural properties of total profit and maintenance actions relative to machine state were established and proven, providing theoretical rigor to the framework. To address computational challenges, an improved value iteration algorithm was developed that significantly reduces computational space requirements. The multivariate degradation framework was further extended to two-phase systems where degradation characteristics change dynamically over time. An innovative approach was implemented that incorporates physical damage observations alongside traditional sensor measurements as dynamic covariates, creating a more comprehensive degradation model (Cai et al., 2024). A bijective function matrix was developed and a novel RUL prediction framework with distinct offline training and online prediction processes was created. To enhance model adaptability, change point detection algorithms were implemented that improve the accuracy of phase transition identification. The multivariate degradation models integrate dynamic covariates through both production-deterioration interactions and multi-phase system considerations. Performance validation through extensive numerical experiments demonstrates significant improvements over traditional approaches, with the integrated maintenance-production model showing substantial profit increases compared to isolated optimization methods. Objective 2: To study the effect of maintenance on the multivariate degradation Comprehensive studies examining maintenance effects on multivariate degradation have been conducted from multiple perspectives. Fundamental research established how maintenance actions influence both individual component degradation and system-wide performance in multivariate environments. The complex interactions between maintenance interventions and production processes were quantified, demonstrating that maintenance effects extend far beyond simple restoration to include intricate system-level dependencies (Zhang et al., 2025). This research revealed how optimal maintenance policies must consider these mutual influences to achieve maximum effectiveness. A distributionally robust optimization framework was developed for high-consequence systems where maintenance decisions have critical safety implications. This approach handles epistemic uncertainty in degradation processes, providing risk-averse maintenance scheduling even when degradation parameters are not precisely known (Zhang et al., 2024). A two-stage integer distributionally robust model with moment-based ambiguity sets was formulated, enabling simultaneous optimization of system design and maintenance scheduling. A sample-based adaptive large neighborhood search algorithm was developed to solve large-scale problems. Maintenance effects were also investigated through hierarchical intervention strategies. The research distinguished between partial and full maintenance interventions, quantifying how different maintenance intensities affect degradation trajectories (Zhang et al., 2023). A comprehensive maintenance model was developed that incorporates performance information from both partial inspections (functional verification) and full inspections (complete state assessment). The model enables condition-based maintenance decisions while maintaining cost-effectiveness through strategic intervention timing. Objective 3: To construct an online remaining useful life prediction framework for prognostic and health management of industrial systems A comprehensive online RUL prediction framework has been constructed to address the critical challenges of real-time prognostics in industrial environments through multiple complementary methodological approaches. The theoretical foundation centers on advanced Bayesian inference methods for online degradation analysis. Nonlinear exponential-dispersion process models were developed that accommodate various degradation patterns (Ding et al., 2022). A dual approach enables uncertainty quantification while maintaining computational efficiency suitable for online applications. An adaptive RUL prediction method was developed to address the challenges of multi-dimensional sensor data in online environments, based on novel health index construction. This approach leverages data fusion techniques combined with genetic algorithm optimization to create composite health indices from multiple sensor streams (Li et al., 2022). Adaptive extended Kalman filter algorithms were integrated for real-time parameter identification in diffusion process models, enabling continuous model adaptation as new data becomes available. The framework includes a fitness metric for intelligent feature selection, ensuring optimal utilization of available sensor information. Reinforced noise-resistant correlation methods were developed specifically for harsh industrial environments to address the critical challenge of noise interference in online monitoring systems. This approach constructs new periodic signals through segmentation and averaging techniques to suppress noise interference while maintaining sensitivity to incipient faults (Fan et al., 2023). Novel correlation functions were developed that capture hidden periodicities, with health indices constructed based on discrete correlation functions. The method includes theoretical analysis of healthy state values, providing reliable benchmarks for online condition assessment and RUL prediction. The constructed online RUL prediction framework provides a complete solution for real-time industrial prognostics. All framework components have been validated using real-world datasets including solid-state drives and bearing degradation data, demonstrating practical viability and superior performance across different industrial applications. Objective 4: To demonstrate the implementation procedure and performance improvement with real data Implementation procedures and performance improvements have been comprehensively demonstrated through extensive real-world case studies across multiple industrial domains. The most substantial implementation demonstration involved feedwater heating systems in nuclear power plants, representing high-consequence systems where optimization benefits have critical safety and economic implications (Zhang et al., 2024). Detailed implementation procedures were provided for the distributionally robust optimization framework, showing how to integrate system design decisions with maintenance scheduling under uncertainty. The two-phase degradation modeling approach was validated through comprehensive real-world case studies that demonstrate both implementation procedures and performance improvements (Cai et al., 2024). The implementation includes detailed workflows for offline training processes using historical physical damage observations and sensor measurements, followed by online prediction procedures that transform real-time sensor data into virtual damage observations. Performance comparisons with traditional sensor-only approaches showed substantial improvements in RUL prediction accuracy, particularly in capturing phase transition dynamics. Online RUL prediction framework implementation was demonstrated using real-world solid-state drive datasets from data centers, providing complete implementation workflows from data collection to final RUL predictions (Li et al., 2022). The case study showed the practical application of data fusion techniques, genetic algorithm optimization, and adaptive Kalman filtering in operational environments. Additionally, noise-resistant correlation methods were demonstrated using both simulated degradation processes and real accelerated bearing degradation datasets, showing practical implementation in rotating machinery applications (Fan et al., 2023). The demonstrations included step-by-step procedures for signal processing, correlation function computation, health index construction, and RUL prediction. Performance comparisons with classical health indices confirmed superior noise suppression capabilities while maintaining sensitivity to incipient faults. All developed methodologies have been implemented and validated using real-world industrial data. The comprehensive demonstrations provide clear implementation procedures and quantify substantial performance improvements over existing approaches, confirming the practical value and industrial applicability of the research outcomes across multiple domains.

11200621.label: Major findings and research outcome
11200621.value: This research project has achieved all four primary objectives, delivering significant theoretical contributions and practical solutions for multivariate degradation modeling and prognostic health management in industrial systems. Below is a summary of major findings and outcomes. Multivariate degradation modeling with dynamic covariates: A comprehensive framework was developed incorporating dynamic covariates. The integrated control model captured bidirectional relationships between production processes and system deterioration (Zhang et al., 2025). Additionally, a two-phase degradation model was created that dynamically adapts to changing degradation characteristics over time (Cai et al., 2024). Maintenance effects on multivariate degradation: Extensive studies quantified maintenance impacts across multiple system configurations. A distributionally robust optimization framework was developed for high-consequence systems (Zhang et al., 2024). A sample-based adaptive large neighborhood search algorithm was developed for large-scale problem solving. The research distinguished between partial and full maintenance interventions, with comprehensive maintenance models developed that incorporate performance information from both functional verification and complete state assessment (Zhang et al., 2023). Online RUL prediction framework: A complete real-time prognostics approach was constructed using advanced Bayesian inference methods. Nonlinear exponential-dispersion process models accommodated various degradation patterns (Ding et al., 2022). The framework integrated adaptive extended Kalman filtering for real-time parameter identification with genetic algorithm optimization for composite health indices construction (Li et al., 2022). Reinforced noise-resistant correlation methods were developed specifically for harsh industrial environments, constructing new periodic signals through segmentation with correlation functions capturing hidden periodicities (Fan et al., 2023). Implementation and performance validation: Comprehensive demonstrations across multiple industrial domains confirmed practical viability (Zhang et al., 2024). Two-phase degradation modeling validation using real-world datasets demonstrated substantial RUL prediction accuracy improvements (Cai et al., 2024). Online framework implementation using solid-state drive datasets from data centers provided quantitative evidence of superior performance (Li et al., 2022). Noise-resistant correlation methods were demonstrated using accelerated bearing degradation datasets (Fan et al., 2023). The research outcomes provide industry-ready solutions, theoretical rigor through practical implementation procedures validated across diverse industrial applications including nuclear power systems, data centers, and rotating machinery. These contributions significantly advance the field of prognostic health management while addressing real-world industrial challenges.

11200621.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11200621.value: Future research could focus on combining different types of data, such as visual data (e.g., infrared or thermal images), vibration data, and operational logs, with traditional sensor readings. Using multiple data sources together could provide more information about system health and improve the accuracy of RUL predictions. Some students and graduates are already engaged to carry out further research.

11200621.value: This research aims to improve how we monitor and maintain industrial systems, such as machines and equipment, to make them more reliable. By creating models that predict how systems wear down over time, the research helps identify when maintenance is needed before failures happen, reducing unexpected downtime and repair costs. The main findings show that factors like working conditions, system usage, and the environment can significantly improve predictions of when a system might fail. The research combines various types of data, including sensor readings and physical damage information, to create more accurate models. It also emphasizes the importance of adjusting maintenance strategies based on the health state of the system. Furthermore, the study developed a real-time system to predict how much longer equipment will last, with the ability to update predictions as new data becomes available. Through testing these methods with real-world data, the research proves that these predictive models can be used in many industries, from managing batteries to data storage systems. The value of this research is in making industrial systems more dependable, helping to avoid costly breakdowns and ensuring they work efficiently for longer.

11200721.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11200721.value: Network slicing has emerged as a promising technique to realize provision of specialized and dedicated virtual networks, called slices, to provide efficient networking solutions that support their customers’ QoS requirements. Slices are built on a common physical network infrastructure using network function virtualization (NFV) and software defined networking (SDN) technologies. Multiple layers are needed because of the complexity and heterogeneity of internet traffic, customers and their QoS requirements. Telecommunications networks are traditionally layered (e.g. OSI model). Modern and future wireless networks are expected to simultaneously support a multitude of diverse mobile applications including IoT applications that require services at multiple networking layers. The internet customers themselves are layered where a higher layer customer further virtualizes its own virtual network to smaller layered virtual networks. Multi-layered network slicing can be viewed as a generalization of multi-layered virtual network embedding (MVNE) over optical networks where a network slice is a set of networking (wireless and wireline), storage and/or computational resources. This project will provide a software tool that includes novel algorithms for efficient multi-layered network slicing and virtualization. A key novel feature of the algorithms is their general nature that enables considerations of realistic traffic conditions and many technologies, e.g. elastic optical networks (EONs). Specific novel features include: (i) the consideration of Variable Bit Rate (VBR) traffic modeled by Long Range Dependent (LRD) processes and statistical multiplexing, (ii) MVNE over WDM or Elastic Optical Network (EON) with an arbitrary set of layers and realistic traffic models, (iii) MVNE over EON (MVNE/EON) with adaptive modulation, and (iv) asymptotically optimal algorithms for layered network slicing. We will build on ideas from our earlier work on the multilayer market algorithm (MMA) (which has polynomial complexity), and results from reinforcement learning and multi-armed bandit problems for which asymmetrically optimal solutions are proved only for a very special case for a single layer. This approach will lead to solutions that meet customer QoS requirements in multi-layered MVNE and network slicing. We seek to maximize earnings before interest and tax (EBIT) with consideration to OPEX and amortized CAPEX, network resource utilization effects, and service disruption penalties. Heuristic algorithms that generate provable bounds on the quality of solutions, and that scale to large instances beyond those handled by integer linear programming (ILP) will be provided for validation. Our tool will have a friendly user interface for network inputting, editing and visualization to extend our industry and education impact. 網絡切片已成為一種能實現專用虛擬網絡(或稱之為切片)、並提供能滿足用戶QoS需求的高效網絡解決方案的可靠技術。這些切片通過網絡功能虛擬化 (NFV) 和軟件定義網絡 (SDN) 技術在通用物理網絡基礎設施上實現。由於互聯網流量、客戶及其 QoS 要求的複雜性和異構性，上述網絡需要被設計為多層網絡。電信網絡傳統上也是分層設計的（例如 OSI 模型）。現今以及未來的無線網絡將同時支持多種不同的移動應用，諸如需要在不同網絡層獲取服務的物聯網應用。互聯網客戶本身亦可以是分層的，高層客戶可將自己的基於下層網絡的虛擬網絡進行進一步映射。多層網絡切片可以被視為多層虛擬網絡映射 (MVNE) 在光網絡上的泛化，其中網絡切片可看做一種網絡資源（無線和有線）、存儲資源和/或計算資源。本項目將以軟件工具的方式提供包括用於高效多層網絡切片和虛擬化的新穎算法。算法的關鍵新特性是將考慮現實網絡環境中的流量條件和許多技術，例如彈性光網絡 (EON)。算法具體的新功能包括：(i) 考慮由長程相關 (LRD) 過程及統計復用建模的可變比特率 (VBR) 流量，(ii)基於 WDM 或彈性光網絡 (EON) 可實現任意網絡層數並參考現實流量模型的MVNE，(iii)基於自適應調製EON (MVNE/EON)的MVNE，以及 (iv)分層網絡的漸近最優切片算法。基於我們早期的關於多層商業化算法 (MMA)（具有多項式級別的算法複雜度）以及強化學習的研究結果、和對於可延展類算法在多臂老虎機問題（單層網絡）中漸進最優性的證明，我們將提出相關研究思路。該研究提供的解決方案將滿足客戶在多層 MVNE 和網絡切片中的 QoS 要求。我們尋求最大化息稅前利潤(EBIT)，兼顧執行成本（OPEX）、分期償還型投資成本（ CAPEX）、網絡資源利用效應和服務中斷處罰。本項目將提供性能退化程度有限的啟發式算法並提供對於性能退化程度有限性的證明，並將該啟發式算法擴展到超出整數線性規劃 (ILP) 處理能力的大型實例，以進行驗證。我們的軟件工具提供友好的用戶界面，用於網絡輸入、編輯和可視化，以提高我們的商業性和教育界影響力。

11200721.label: Realisation of objectives
11200721.value: We have formulated and solved a general multilayered network problem considering long-range dependent (LRD) traffic that aims to minimize costs subject to meeting grade of service (GoS) and fault tolerance requirements. For details, see Journal Paper 4 entitled "GoS-Aware Optimization of a Multi-Layered Network for Cost Effectiveness and Fault Tolerance". The new algorithms that solve this problem were implemented in a Netml tool with a user interface that provides a convenient way to enter the data, network/data editing, and visualization. One key methodology that was utilized for network slicing was the multi-armed bandit problem. Journal Paper 1, entitled "A Restless Bandit Model for Energy-Efficient Job Assignments in Server Farms," demonstrates its applicability to server farms. Then, the conference paper, entitled "Energy-Efficient Offloading in Edge Slicing with Non-Linear Power Functions" and its extended version, Journal Paper 3, entitled "Network Slicing in MEC-based RANs With Nonlinear Cost Rate Functions," demonstrate their applicability to network slicing. A scalable solution for service function chaining embedding in hybrid optical-electronic networks was provided in Journal Paper 2. The significant theoretical and experimental work in Journal Papers 1-3 was time-demanding, so we did not have the time and resources to implement all the algorithms in Neml. Nevertheless, the multi-layered algorithms that consider Long Range Dependent (LRD) traffic, Grade of Service (GoS), and fault tolerance, provided in Journal Paper 4, were implemented in Netml. We did not conducted new research on adaptive modulation, but we did conduct above and beyond research of LRD traffic modeling, of which the results are still unpublished (the relevant paper is still in preparation) and we also provide in paper 5 a way to reduce the variance of the traffic which leads to savings of required resources.

11200721.label: Major findings and research outcome
11200721.value: Paper number 4, entitled "GoS-Aware Optimization of a Multi-Layered Network for Cost Effectiveness and Fault Tolerance," presents two innovative algorithms for the fault-tolerant design of multi-layered networks that consider LRD traffic, which is known to characterize internet traffic behavior. These algorithms enhance the previously published multi-layered market algorithm (MMA) by incorporating additional resources for use during network failures. The new algorithms are named resilient MMA (RMMA) and failure-traffic MMA (FTMMA). RMMA operates iteratively and independently for each failure scenario, while FTMMA treats each failure as a type of traffic, facilitating more efficient resource sharing within the network. Both algorithms address a variety of single physical link failures and aim to maximize earnings before interest and tax (EBIT). The costs factored into the EBIT evaluation include amortized capital, operational expenditures, and penalties for service degradation. Focusing on optimizing resource provisioning, particularly capacity assignment, RMMA and FTMMA are designed for fault-tolerant and cost-effective multi-layered networks. Key innovations of these algorithms include the integration of variable bit rate traffic streams in the design process and the goal of maximizing EBIT. Validation is achieved by comparing the designs produced by RMMA and FTMMA against those generated by an integer linear programming benchmark for small networks. Numerical results indicate that FTMMA allocates capacity more efficiently across various failure events by enabling resource sharing. The third paper, entitled “Network Slicing in MEC-based RANs With Nonlinear Cost Rate Functions,” explores network slicing in a Multi-Access Edge Computing (MEC)-enabled Radio Access Network (RAN) with diverse edge nodes. It focuses on optimizing resource allocation for arriving slice requests to maximize the long-term average Earnings Before Interest and Taxes (EBIT) of the system. By formulating the problem as a Restless Multi-Armed Bandit (RMAB) challenge with a nonlinear cost rate function, a novel policy named PFA (Prioritizing-the-Future-Approximated earning per request) is introduced. PFA prioritizes resource allocation based on future impacts to boost earnings efficiently. The scalability of PFA in large networks is highlighted through numerical simulations, demonstrating its superior performance in maximizing long-term average EBIT compared to baseline policies under various scenarios. These results provide valuable insights for network operators when selecting resource allocation strategies. In the first paper, we devised an energy-efficient job assignment policy for a large server farm with diverse storage and computing components. These components operate in varying power modes, each with distinct service and energy consumption rates. Given the complexity arising from these differences, finding optimal solutions becomes challenging. By employing the Whittle relaxation technique, we developed a near-optimal and scalable job assignment policy. We demonstrated that under certain conditions regarding server characteristics, our policy approaches optimality as the system size grows towards infinity, making it asymptotically optimal. Through numerical simulations in practical scenarios, we demonstrated the superior performance of our policy over existing methods, highlighting its resilience to heavy-tailed job-size distributions. Network Function Virtualization (NFV) employs software and general-purpose devices for service function chaining (SFC) in network services. Hybrid optical-electronic networks integrate optical and electronic advantages to enhance communication efficiency. In the 2nd paper, we have focused on embedding SFC in such networks, proposing a scalable algorithm optimizing bandwidth and resource allocation. The numerical results have demonstrated the algorithm's strong performance and scalability. In the fifth paper, we provided a new control theory method for the traffic schedulers of the UAV-IoT network slicing system, and we designed a proportional–integral–derivative controller to facilitate explicit traffic rate control and adjustment and adaptive resource schedule at each scheduler, to achieve effective traffic transmission and resource utilization optimization over the entire network.

11200721.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11200721.value: One future direction is to focus on the evolving Internet, the Internet of Vehicles (IoV), and Autonomous Vehicles (AVs) within the Multi-access Edge Computing (MEC) framework. This will facilitate AV connectivity to cloud and edge resources, enabling efficient real-time data processing for optimized path planning and obstacle avoidance. Our novel approach used in the present project, which utilizes (restless) multi-armed bandit methods to enhance AV task offloading in MEC, can be applied to IoV for the development of scalable algorithms with established performance boundaries. By focusing on maximizing earnings before income tax (EBIT) during operational cycles and considering task priorities with penalties for non-compliance, we will be able to efficiently allocate resources and achieve a fault-tolerant network design. We can incorporate energy costs, sustainability concerns, and both capital and operating expenditures into our strategy. Through extensive simulations using SUMO, we will be able to compare our methodologies with existing practices, offering valuable insights for future edge network design and fostering collaborative efforts within the industry. In essence, this future research direction will concentrate on IoV and AVs, leveraging MEC to bolster safety, efficiency, and resource optimization, while simultaneously addressing sustainability, fault tolerance, and cost-effectiveness aspects.

11200721.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11200721.value: Network slicing provides specialized and dedicated virtual networks, called slices, to provide efficient networking solutions that support their customers’ quality of service requirements. Modern and future networks are expected to support a multitude of diverse applications that require services at multiple networking layers. Internet traffic is bursty and is known to have Long Range Dependent (LRD) characteristics. This implies that additional spare capacity must be provided to users to avoid data loss and delays due to the traffic burstiness. In this project, we have formulated and solved a general multilayered network problem considering LRD traffic that aims to minimize costs subject to meeting grade of service (GoS) and fault tolerance requirements. GoS measures the probability that traffic will be blocked or delayed due to limited network capacity. The multilayered network design algorithms developed under this project were implemented in a software tool with a user interface that provides a convenient way to enter the data, network/data editing, and visualization. We also provided a novel and efficient policy for network slicing in edge computing. Additional results on efficient network solutions have been developed. These results provide valuable algorithms, software and insights for network operators optimizing their network operation.

11201421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11201421.value: Machine type communication (MTC) is an important service for the 5th and 6th generation (5G and 6G) cellular systems. MTC is characterized by a large number of mobile terminals (MTs), sporadic traffic, multiple concurrently active MTs and very short data messages. MTC brings about new challenges. Consider the following basic receiver functions at a base state (BS): (i) identify active MTs who have information to transmit, (ii) estimate the channels from active MTs, and (iii) decoding information bits. A random-access system, such as ALOHA or CSMA, completes these functions in a single phase. However, collisions of multiple concurrently active MTs seriously affect the throughput in ALOHA or CSMA. The existing cellular system, on the other hand, separates these functions into multiple phases, among which four phases are for function (i) (such as RACH in 4G for connection setup), and one additional phase for functions (ii) and (iii) (using pilot and data slots). In MTC, the amount of data per session is typically small. Then the overhead due to connection setup becomes a serious burden. Recently, a two-phase massive-access scheme attracted wide research interests for MTC, in which functions (i) and (ii) are carried out jointly in the first phase, and function (iii) in the second phase. This two-phase structure is sub-optimal. We can see such optimality by noting that the outputs of function (iii) can be used to enhance the accuracy of functions (i) and (ii). For example, a decoding failure indicates a high probability of error in activity detection. If this information is utilized, we may refine the outputs of the first phase. In this project, we will work on this idea and develop a scheme that can complete the functions (i) – (iii) in a single phase. Our focus is on the orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) platform. OFDM is the underlying technology for 5G, and possibly for 6G as well. The sub-carriers in an OFDM system are typically strongly correlated. The existing AMP based schemes cannot perform well in such correlated environments. Our recent work on the orthogonal approximate message passing (OAMP) algorithm revealed an efficient treatment for the correlation problem. In this project, we will develop a joint OAMP and FEC decoding scheme to complete functions (i) – (iii) in a single phase. It will provide a reliable and low-cost implementation technique for MTC. The outputs of this project may find useful applications in future cellular systems. 机器通信 (MTC) 是第 5 和第 6代蜂窝系统（5G 和 6G）的重要服务类别。MTC 的特点是大量的移动终端、零星流量、多个同时活跃移动终端 和非常短的数据帧。 MTC 带来了新的挑战。以下是基站的基本接收功能 (i) 确定有信息要传输的活跃移动终端， (ii) 估计来自活跃移动终端的信道，以及 (iii) 信息解码。 现有的随机接入系统，如 ALOHA 或 CSMA，可以在一个步骤完成这些功能。在ALOHA 或 CSMA中，多个同时活跃的移动终端的碰撞严重影响了吞吐量。另一方面，现有的蜂窝系统用多个步骤完成这些功能，其中四个步骤（如4G中的为建立连接RACH过程）用来完成功能（i）。 再加一个步骤（涉及导频和数据帧）完成功能 (ii) 和 (iii)。在MTC中，每个帧的数据量通常很小。那么建立连接的开销成为严重的负担。 最近，两步骤大规模接入MTC方案引起了广泛的研究兴趣。在这个方案中，第一步骤同时完成功能 (i) 和 (ii) ，然后第二步骤完成功能(iii)。这个两步骤方案并不是最佳的。这是因为函数 (iii) 的输出可以用来进一步提高函数 (i) 和 (ii) 的准确性。例如，解码失败表明活跃移动终端的检测错误的可能性很高。如果利用到这信息，我们可以提高第一步骤的输出可靠度。本项目的目标是制定一个可以完成这个设想的方案。 我们的计划是在一个步骤完成功能（i），(ii) ，(iii)。我们的工作重点是使用正交频分复用 (OFDM) 平台。OFDM是 5G 的基本技术，也可能是 6G 的基本技术。OFDM 信道通常是强相关的。现有的基于 AMP 算法的方案不能在这种相关的信道中有良好表现。 我们最近在正交近似消息传递 (OAMP) 算法方面的取的很多进展。在本项目中，我们将开发联合 OAMP 和 FEC 解码方案以一步完成功能 (i) – (iii)。这将为MTC提供可靠且低成本的实现技术。该项目的成果可能会在未来的蜂窝系统中找到有用的应用。

11201421.label: Realisation of objectives
11201421.value: Following the work reported in the mid-term progress report, we continue the project to fully achieve the three objectives of the project. We have worked on OAMP in massive-access in multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) and OFDM environments. We have extended OAMP to statistical problems with multiple measurement vectors (MMVs) and multiple transforms (MTs). We refer the resulting algorithms as OAMP-MMV and OAMP-MT, respectively, and their combination as augmented AMP (A-OAMP). We have demonstrated that the MMV and MT models are widely applicable to signal processing and communications. Compared with existing methods, OAMP offers an efficient solution with excellent performance. This work is report in Ref [1]. Furthermore, we continued our work on capacity limits for massive random-access. We have developed two single-input-single-output variational transfer functions for OAMP with Lipschitz continuous local estimators, facilitating an analysis of achievable rates. Furthermore, when the state evolution of OAMP has a unique fixed point, we revealed that OAMP can achieve the constrained capacity predicted by the replica method of LUIS based on matched FEC coding, regardless of the signal distribution. The replica method is rigorously validated for LUIS with Gaussian signaling and certain sub-classes of LUIS with arbitrary signal distributions. Several area properties are established based on the variational transfer functions of OAMP. In addition, we developed a replica constrained capacity-achieving coding principle for LUIS. This principle serves as the basis for optimizing irregular low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes specifically tailored for binary signaling in our simulation results. The performance of OAMP with these optimized codes exhibits a remarkable improvement over the unoptimized codes and even surpasses the well-known Turbo-LMMSE algorithm. This work is report in Ref [2]. [1] Y. Cheng, L. Liu, S. Liang, J.H. 11201421.label: Major findings and research outcome
11201421.value: OAMP can achieve the constrained capacity predicted by statistical physics replica methods for large unitarily invariant systems with arbitrary signal distributions. Also, it outperforms conventional algorithms like Turbo-LMMSE in various scenarios, achieving near-capacity bit error rates for QPSK. The OAMP algorithm is extended to handle problems involving multiple measurement vectors (MMV) and multiple transforms (MT), improving the performance in complex signal processing applications such as MIMO relay systems with correlated sources and clipping. The proposed framework and algorithms significantly improve performance in complex signal processing applications such as MIMO relay systems with correlated sources and clipping. OAMP with orthogonal errors achieves superior stability and accuracy in practical communication and signal processing problems. The publications arising this project is listed in Part C.

11201421.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11201421.value: Various turbo/EP/AMP-type algorithms can be transformed into equivalent forms with orthogonal local estimators. Hence they can be unified under a common orthogonal framework. A householder dice method has recently been proposed for effectively simulating the dynamics on Haar random matrices. It will be interesting to see how the householder dice technique may be used to demonstrate the SE of OAMP.

11201421.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11201421.value: Machine type communication (MTC) is an important service for the 5th and 6th generation (5G and 6G) cellular systems. MTC is characterized by a large number of mobile terminals (MTs), sporadic traffic, multiple concurrently active MTs and very short data messages. Our focus is on the orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) platform. OFDM is the underlying technology for 5G, and possibly for 6G as well. The sub-carriers in an OFDM system are typically strongly correlated. The existing approximate message passing (AMP) based schemes cannot perform well in such correlated environments. Our work on orthogonal AMP (OAMP) provides a universal coding principle and demonstrates significant performance gains over existing methods, highlighting its importance for next-generation wireless communications and data transmission systems. It also provides stronger theoretical assurance for accuracy and shows significant advantages over previous methods. These advances help make wireless and data communication technologies more powerful and reliable.

11201721.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11201721.value: The development of high performance ultra-elastic metals with superb strength, a large elastic strain limit and temperature insensitive elastic modulus (Elinvar effect) is important to a variety of industrial applications. Plastic deformation through dislocations, twinning and/or grain boundary sliding commonly limit the elastic strain of bulk crystalline metals to ~0.2% at room temperature. Because bulk amorphous alloys lack crystal defects, they may achieve ~2% elastic strain at room temperature. However, the high cooling rate required to form most amorphous metallic alloys provides severe limits on the size that can be produced, thereby seriously hindering their industrial application. On the other hand, shape memory alloys and Gum metals may achieve elastic strain limit up to several percent. However, this high strain limit is associated with reversible martensitic transformations which are accompanied by large mechanical hysteresis and energy dissipation. Interestingly, we recently discovered a high entropy alloy, which possessed a severely distorted lattice and exhibited hysteresis free super-elasticity with an unusual Elinvar effect. These results are intriguing and promising, which indicates that the notion of high entropy alloy is also applicable to the design of super-elastic materials. However, a few fundamental issues remain yet to be addressed. For example, one may ask whether there is a general rule to guide the design of super-elastic high entropy alloys and, if there is, how one can optimize the compositions of the high entropy alloys to enhance their super-elastic properties. In this project, we aim to address these fundamental issues by forming a research team that has already developed its strengths via the research of decades in alloy design and development, theoretical modeling, nano- and micro-mechanical testing, in-situ high energy X-ray diffraction experiments coupled with mechanical testing and atomistic simulations. Once this project was funded, we would achieve the following goals through the combined efforts from experiments, theoretical modeling and atomistic simulations, which include (1) to understand the fundamental deformation mechanisms that give rise to the super-elasticity of the designed high entropy alloys, (2) to understand the composition-processing-property correlations for this special class of super-elastic high entropy alloys, and (3) to provide a protocol that can guide the design and development of super-elastic high entropy alloys. In the long run, because of the unusual super-elastic behavior of high entropy alloys, the outcome of the research may lead to a great expansion of their applications in actuators, medical devices, and high precision instruments. 開發具有超強強度、大彈性應變極限和溫度不敏感彈性模量（埃林瓦效應）的高性能超彈性金屬對各種工業應用非常重要。通過位錯、孿晶或晶界滑動實現的室溫塑性變形通常使得大塊晶體金屬的彈性應變限製在~0.2%或者以下。由於塊狀非晶合金沒有晶體缺陷，它們在室溫下可以達到~2% 的彈性應變。然而，由于形成大多數非晶金屬合金所需的高冷卻速率，可以生產的合金尺寸有嚴格的限製，從而嚴重阻礙了它們的工業應用。另一方面，形狀記憶合金和膠金屬(Gum Metal)可以達到高達幾個百分點的彈性應變極限。然而，這種高應變極限與可逆馬氏體轉變有關，并且伴隨著大的機械滯後和能量耗散。有趣的是，我們最近發現了一種高熵合金，它具有嚴重扭曲的晶格，並表現出無滯後超彈性和不尋常的艾林瓦效應。這些有趣的結果表明高熵合金的概念也適用於超彈性材料的設計。然而，一些基本問題仍有待解決。例如，人們可能會問是否有指導超彈性高熵合金設計的一般規則。如果有，如何優化高熵合金的成分以增強其超彈性性能。在這個項目中，我們的目標是通過組建一個研究團隊來解決這些基本問題，該團隊將結合合金設計和開發、理論建模、納米和微機械測試、原位高能 X射線衍射實驗，機械測試和原子模擬來實現以下目標，包括 (1) 了解導致高熵合金超彈性的基本變形機製, (2) 了解這種特殊類型的超彈性高熵合金的成分-加工-性能相關性，以及 (3) 提供可以指導超彈性高熵合金的設計和開發的準則。從長遠來看，由於高熵合金具有不尋常的超彈性行為，研究成果可能會極大地擴展其在執行器、醫療器械和高精度儀器中的應用。

11201721.label: Realisation of objectives
11201721.value: Task 1: To characterize the structure and elastic properties of the Co-Ni-Hf-Ti-Zr high entropy alloy and the derived alloys with the composition of Co-Ni-Hf-Ti-Zr-X, where X stands for an alloying element. Our work successfully demonstrates a tunable Elinvar effect in severely distorted single-phase B2 high-entropy alloys. We fabricated a series of (CoNi)50-x(TiZrHf)50Fex alloys and established that for the single-phase B2 compositions (x ≤ 10), the temperature range of the Elinvar effect is directly and positively correlated with the overall lattice distortion. A key finding was that the terminal temperature of the effect, T_EL, decreases from approximately 900 K for Fe0 to 500 K for Fe10 as the Fe content increases and the lattice distortion, quantified by RMS strain, is reduced. We rigorously ruled out other mechanisms for the effect, as our samples showed no magnetic response or phase transitions, pointing exclusively to a structural origin. To explain this, we proposed a physical model based on the interstitialcy theory. The model posits that the severe lattice distortion in these HEAs acts as a high concentration of structural defects. The Elinvar effect arises because thermal expansion at elevated temperatures reduces this distortion, which counteracts the inherent thermal softening of the lattice. Ultimately, our study confirms that high-entropy alloys with severe lattice distortion are exceptional candidates for Elinvar applications, outperforming other known alloys by maintaining a constant elastic modulus over an exceptionally wide temperature range. This provides a new pathway for designing tunable, non-magnetic Elinvar alloys for demanding environments like space missions. Subsequently, through the machine learning (ML) method we developed (first for eutectic alloys and afterwards extended to B2 alloy), we have obtained a number of B2 multi-principal element alloys (MPEA). These alloys include not only the Co-Ni-Hf-Ti-Zr-X system, but also other Ti rich systems. After confirming the single-phase B2 structures of the ML-discovered MPEIs, we further investigated whether they exhibited Elinvar behavior (near-constant elastic modulus over specific temperature range) and high strength, similar to previously reported B2 MPEIs. All newly discovered MPEIs exhibit Elinvar effect over the temperature range of 300–750 K. Notably, except for CoNiTiZr and (CoNi)50(TiZrHf)50, all B2 MPEIs exhibit slight elastic softening, with Co17Ni32.9Ti36.1Zr9Hf5 showing the most pronounced softening among them. Task 2: To understand the fundamental deformation mechanisms of the high entropy alloys developed for this study Our work successfully demonstrates that severe lattice distortion in a single-phase B2 high-entropy intermetallic alloy, (CoNi)50(TiZrHf)50, overcomes the long-standing strength-ductility trade-off that has plagued traditional intermetallics. We show that this alloy exhibits exceptional strength, with a yield strength of ~1.5 GPa, and significant compressive plasticity of ~8% at room temperature. Crucially, it resists the precipitous thermal softening typical of B2 alloys, maintaining high strength and stable plastic flow up to homologous temperatures of 0.7. A key finding is that the severe lattice distortion induces isotropic-like mechanical behavior, with minimal dependence of elastic modulus and yield strength on crystal orientation. This distortion enables the activation of multiple slip systems ({110}<111> and {010}<100>), with nearly identical critical resolved shear stresses, a phenomenon absent in conventional B2 alloys. Our experimental and atomistic simulation results reveal a dynamic hardening mechanism: dislocation glide triggers local structural transitions, causing amorphization at low temperatures and forming crystal-like obstacles at high temperatures, which stabilizes plastic deformation. Furthermore, the distorted lattice imposes similar resistance on screw and edge dislocations, promoting ductile behavior. These findings establish lattice distortion as a powerful design parameter for creating strong, ductile, and thermally stable intermetallic alloys for demanding high-temperature applications. Task 3: To study the influence of chemical composition and processing routes on the elastic properties of the developed high entropy alloys Through a series of experiments, we successfully developed a cost-effective, single-phase B2 multi-principal element intermetallic (MPEI) with the equiatomic composition CoNiTiZr. This alloy demonstrates exceptional thermal stability, maintaining its single-phase B2 structure even after prolonged annealing at temperatures up to 1273 K, and exhibits a strong Elinvar effect and a high elastic strain limit. Our experimental screening of the (CoNi)50±x(TiZr)50∓x system revealed that the single-phase B2 structure is uniquely stable at the precise equiatomic composition, as even minor deviations lead to the formation of secondary intermetallic phases. Critically, we identified a significant gap in existing empirical models, which failed to predict the formation of this stable B2 phase. To address this, we developed a novel pseudo-binary system (PBS) model that explicitly accounts for the chemical long-range order across the two distinct sublattices of the B2 structure, combined with random mixing within each sublattice. This model effectively distinguishes single-phase B2 MPEIs from other phases like solid solutions or metallic glasses by utilizing two key thermodynamic parameters. Our findings provide a robust, physics-informed framework that moves beyond traditional solid-solution-based criteria, enabling the targeted design of single-phase B2 MPEIs with tailored properties. Furthermore, we elucidate the physical origin of the Elinvar effect in multi-principal element B2 intermetallics, establishing that it stems from intrinsic lattice distortion rather than magnetic transitions. Our key finding is that lattice distortion arises from two distinct sources: atomic size mismatch, which creates localized strain fields, and sublattice frustration driven by valence electron concentration (VEC) fluctuations, which delocalizes strain and stabilizes the B2 phase. Critically, we develop a sublattice engineering model that quantitatively links composition to lattice strain and accurately predicts the temperature-dependent elastic modulus. The model reveals a strong distortion-modulus coupling in the B2 structure, attributable to covalent bonding contributions, which is more pronounced than in body-centered cubic alloys. This framework provides a physics-based strategy for designing Elinvar alloys with superior thermoelastic stability by tailoring lattice distortion through compositional control. Task 4: To develop a protocol that enables the design of the hysteresis free super-elastic high entropy alloys with a strong elinvar effect Our research has successfully established a comprehensive protocol for designing hysteresis-free, super-elastic high-entropy alloys (HEAs) with a strong Elinvar effect, centered on the strategic use of severe lattice distortion in single-phase B2 multi-principal element intermetallics (MPEIs). The key to this protocol is our discovery that a highly distorted crystalline lattice, achieved through careful compositional design in alloys like (CoNi)50(TiZrHf)50 and CoNiTiZr, is the fundamental origin of these unique properties. We developed a physics-informed ML framework that integrates a pseudo-binary sublattice model to efficiently navigate complex compositional spaces and predict single-phase B2 formability. This model was crucial, as it moves beyond traditional solid-solution criteria by accounting for the chemical long-range order essential for B2 stability. Our experimental validations confirmed that the resulting alloys exhibit an exceptionally wide Elinvar temperature range (up to 900 K), high strength, and significant plasticity, even at high homologous temperatures. The protocol is underpinned by our physical model which explains the Elinvar effect through the thermal alleviation of lattice distortion counteracting normal elastic softening. Furthermore, we demonstrated that the activation of multiple slip systems within the distorted lattice enables the high elastic strain limit and super-elastic behavior without the phase transitions that typically cause hysteresis. This integrated approach, from theoretical modeling and machine learning to experimental synthesis and characterization, provides a robust and accelerated pathway for designing next-generation high-performance thermoelastic alloys
