11201721.label: Major findings and research outcome
11201721.value: Our research program has successfully established a new paradigm for designing high-performance, non-magnetic high-entropy alloys (HEAs) with a unique combination of properties: a strong Elinvar effect (near-constant elastic modulus over a wide temperature range), super-elasticity, and high strength. The cornerstone of our discovery is the strategic use of severe lattice distortion in single-phase B2 multi-principal element intermetallics (MPEIs), such as (CoNi)50(TiZrHf)50 and CoNiTiZr. We demonstrated that this lattice distortion is the fundamental origin of the Elinvar effect, which we showed can be tuned by composition; for instance, the temperature range of the effect extends from 500 K to 900 K by varying iron content. Crucially, we ruled out magnetic origins, attributing the behavior instead to a structural mechanism where thermal expansion alleviates distortion, counteracting normal elastic softening. Furthermore, we uncovered that the distorted lattice enables a dynamic hardening mechanism and activates multiple slip systems, granting these traditionally brittle intermetallics exceptional plasticity and strength retention even at high homologous temperatures, without the hysteresis associated with phase transformations. To accelerate the discovery of these complex alloys, we developed a physics-informed machine learning framework. This framework integrates a novel pseudo-binary sublattice model that moves beyond traditional solid-solution criteria to accurately predict single-phase B2 formability. This tool has enabled the high-throughput identification of new alloy compositions with tailored properties. The outcomes of this research have been disseminated in high-impact publications, including papers in Nature Communications, Advanced Materials, and ACS Nano, with a further manuscript under revision at Nature Communications. The intellectual property has been protected through a granted US patent. The project has also served as an excellent training platform for students and postdocs, contributing to the development of the next generation of materials scientists. This integrated body of work provides a robust, accelerated pathway for designing next-generation high entropy alloys for demanding applications in aerospace and precision engineering.

11201721.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11201721.value: Building on our established protocol, the immediate path involves refining our machine learning framework to incorporate property-specific targets, such as maximizing the Elinvar temperature range or optimizing high-temperature strength. This will accelerate the discovery of next-generation alloys with enhanced performance. A key research thrust will be to scale up the synthesis of the most promising compositions, like CoNiTiZr, to produce bulk components for real-world testing in demanding environments, such as aerospace actuators or precision instruments. Concurrently, we will deepen our fundamental understanding by probing the atomic-scale mechanisms of deformation and elasticity using advanced in-situ techniques. This will provide crucial feedback to improve our predictive models. Exploring the functional potential beyond thermo-mechanical properties, such as corrosion resistance or radiation tolerance, could open new application domains. This proposed course of action, combining targeted computational design, scalable processing, and fundamental characterization, will translate our foundational discoveries into tangible technological advancements and solidify leadership in the field of high-performance alloys.

11201721.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11201721.value: Imagine creating a new type of metal that doesn't expand or contract with heat like ordinary metals do. This research project did just that. We developed special alloys that keep their shape and stiffness perfectly stable across a huge range of temperatures, from room temperature up to the heat of a jet engine. This is a game-changer for high-precision technology. Think of a watch that never loses time or a satellite component that works perfectly whether it's in sunlight or shadow, without needing constant adjustment. Unlike previous materials that relied on magnetism, our alloys achieve this through a unique internal structure, making them more reliable and versatile. The significance is twofold: we not only created these promising new materials but also developed a smart computer method to design them quickly, bypassing years of trial and error. The value lies in enabling future breakthroughs in aerospace, robotics, and anywhere extreme precision under varying temperatures is critical.

11202021.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11202021.value: Intradermal and transdermal delivery of oligonucleotide therapeutics is a preferred administration route for treating skin disorders and vaccination. Unfortunately, delivery of naked oligonucleotides across the stratum corneum is challenging. Unmodified oligonucleotides are rapidly degraded by nucleases and have low membrane permeability because of their high molecular weight and negative charges. Nanoparticle-based topical formulations have been positioned to tackle this issue. However, there is a lack of precision in controlling the skin penetration depth of existing nanoformulations. This proposal aims at developing a platform technology for the precise intradermal/transdermal delivery of oligonucleotides using Framework Nucleic Acids (FNAs) as carriers. Our preliminary experiments have demonstrated the efficacy of topically applied FNAs to penetrate into the skin and to deliver molecular therapeutic agents for managing pathological skin diseases. The skin penetration depth of FNAs is tightly regulated by their sizes and can be further improved with ionic liquid (IL) formulation. Here we will develop strategies for integrating therapeutic antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs) and small interfering RNA (siRNA) into FNAs. By taking skin fibrosis as a disease model, both ASOs and siRNA will target Transforming Growth Factor beta 1 in skin fibroblasts to modulate the expression and deposition of collagen. Finally, ASO-FNAs and siRNA-FNAs will be formulated with ILs. The therapeutic effect will be examined in the hypertrophic scar rabbit ear model and be benchmarked to topical corticosteroid treatment. Short-term and long-term safety will be examined in this process as well. Upon project completion, the FNA formulation will have broad applicability since therapeutic oligonucleotides can be designed to modulate any gene alteration responsible for other diseases, including psoriasis, atopic dermatitis, and skin cancers. It can also be used to deliver DNA/RNA vaccines against infectious diseases. 經皮給藥是利用寡核苷酸藥物來治療皮膚疾病和接種疫苗的首選給藥途徑。但是未經修飾的寡核苷酸分子量大且載有負電性，因而它很難穿透過角質層，也很難通過細胞膜進入細胞。另外寡核苷酸藥物的生物學穩定性也差，會被核酸酶迅速降解。目前業界正致力於開發以納米材料為基礎的藥物製劑來解決這個問題，但市面上現有的納米製劑在控制皮膚滲透深度方面缺乏精準性。 本項目旨在開發一種以框架核酸（Framework Nucleic Acids，FNAs）為載體的寡核苷酸經皮遞送平台。我們的前期實驗已經證明了局部塗抹於皮膚上的框架核酸能滲透進入皮膚，它在皮膚中的滲透深度可以通過控制其尺寸大小來調整。另外如果在製劑中加入離子液體配方（Ionic Liquid，ILs），那麼就可以進一步增強框架核酸的經皮效率。本項目將在我們前期工作基礎上，利用框架核酸來實現治療性反義寡核苷酸（antisense oligonucleotide，ASO）和小干擾RNA（small interfering RNA，siRNA）的精準經皮遞送。作為概念驗證，我們將針對皮膚纖維化，來設計基於框架核酸的ASOs和siRNA藥物，並最終通過增生性瘢痕兔耳模型來檢驗治療效果。 我們期望通過本項目開發出基於框架核酸的光譜性經皮給藥平台，從而提高寡核苷酸藥物的療效。

11202121.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11202121.value: Subsurface stratigraphy depicts the occurrence and spatial distribution of different subsurface soil/rock strata as an image and provides indispensable information for design and construction of geotechnical structures. It is developed from site investigation data and often supplemented by prior geological knowledge and engineering judgement. However, site investigation data from a specific site are often quite limited (e.g., a few boreholes) in engineering practice, and the obtained stratigraphy might be inaccurate, leading to the most frequently encountered problem in geotechnical construction: unexpected site conditions. For example, unexpected subsurface granite was encountered during the construction of the Guangzhou-Shenzhen-Hong Kong Express Rail Link project commissioned in 2018, which delayed the project by more than 2 years and increased the cost by HK$20 billion. This problem is exacerbated for Building Information Modelling (BIM) or digital twins of civil infrastructures in which high-resolution 3D stratigraphy is required to represent the subsurface soils and rocks. The goal of this project is to resolve this long-standing problem of developing accurate subsurface stratigraphy from sparse measurements by recognizing that stratigraphy is an image and can be leveraged using an image-based deep machine learning method called Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN). However, direct application of CNN to subsurface stratigraphy is not feasible because millions of images are required to train a CNN model and abundant measurements are required for predictions using the trained CNN model. Neither millions of images nor abundant measurements are available in geotechnical practice. In this project, a novel iterative CNN model is proposed to tackle these difficulties. In the proposed model, only one training image is needed for iteratively extracting its spatial stratigraphic patterns from large to small scales progressively. The extracted patterns at different scales are used together with limited site-specific measurements to iteratively develop the stratigraphy. The PI has developed a preliminary iterative CNN method for 2D geological cross-sections and obtained promising results. This project will enhance the developed 2D method, systematically extend it to 3D cases, compile a database of training stratigraphy with different geological origins, and develop computer software to facilitate its application to engineering practice. The output from this project will be a game changer that transforms the current engineering practice of manually developing highly simplified subsurface stratigraphy into automatic generation of high-resolution subsurface stratigraphy with uncertainty quantification. The research outcomes will benefit geotechnical practice worldwide and in Hong Kong specifically, where many large-scale infrastructure projects are currently in progress. 地質地層圖描述各類岩石和土壤的地下空間分佈，在岩土工程實踐中是必不可少的。它通常從稀疏、有限的地質勘探數據分析而產生。由於地質勘探數據的稀疏性，地質地層圖往往有很大的不確定性，常常出現地質地層圖描述的地質狀況與施工期間發現的實際地質狀況有很大的差別，導致工程項目的延誤和預算的超支。本項目將基於卷積神經網絡，對稀疏地質勘探數據進行多尺度迭代分析，結合先驗地質信息，開創性地開發多尺度的地質地層圖機器學習方法，科學地建立最可能的地質地層圖，並量化其不確定性。

11202721.label: Realisation of objectives
11202721.value: In this research project, all proposed objectives have been successfully achieved. An accurate and computationally efficient model was developed to predict the heating and cooling behaviors of laminated glass facades exposed to fire. This model significantly reduces the computational cost associated with simulating heat transfer in layered structures incorporating a down-flowing water film. A novel three-dimensional finite difference method (3DFDM) was introduced, demonstrating high numerical stability when solving heat transfer equations involving both water film and air convection. To efficiently track moving water particles, a unique particle-labeling algorithm was developed. Unlike conventional meshfree methods, this approach eliminates the need for time-consuming neighbor searches and ensures each particle interacts only with a limited set of neighbors without requiring weight functions, drastically reducing computational effort. The 3DFDM was validated through experimental heating and cooling tests, with its thermal predictions showing excellent agreement with results from commercial software, confirming both its efficiency and accuracy. The model was then applied to investigate the influence of polyvinyl butyral (PVB) interlayer thickness on the thermal response of laminated glass, particularly focusing on the temperature of the second (ambient-side) glass layer. Simulations revealed that each 0.38 mm increase in PVB thickness reduces the temperature of the second glass layer by approximately 7°C and delays its cooling by about 4 seconds. Additionally, the effect of water film release time (WFRT) on cooling behavior was examined, revealing that the exposed surface cools significantly faster than other surfaces, particularly the ambient side. The cooling rate was also found to increase with longer WFRT. Notably, WFRT was shown to have a greater impact on cooling behavior than PVB thickness, highlighting the critical importance of early water film release in preventing laminated glass failure. These findings provide valuable guidance for optimizing water film parameters (including WFRT) to enhance the fire resistance of laminated glass. Furthermore, a three-dimensional meshfree framework based on peridynamic (PD) theory was developed to assess the fire resistance and mechanical performance of laminated glass. This framework enables the simulation of thermomechanical cracking in laminated glass through two key advancements: (1) the development of uniform and non-uniform temperature field strategies to address incomplete experimental thermal boundary data, and (2) the integration of a PD interface model for laminated glass along with stochastic defect distributions. The framework was validated using a benchmark test of crack path selection in borosilicate/steel bi-material beams under thermal loading. Further validation was conducted by comparing simulated thermal cracking in laminated glass with experimental temperature histories and crack patterns, demonstrating strong agreement. A series of numerical experiments explored the effects of glass tensile strength and defect density on crack propagation. Results indicate that lower glass strength or higher defect content leads to increased island formation in the central glazing region, raising the risk of glass fall-out during fire exposure. Thus, improving glass strength and minimizing defects are essential strategies for enhancing structural integrity in fire conditions. The proposed computational framework offers a powerful tool for analyzing thermal breakage in laminated glass, supporting the design of safer engineering structures and advancing digital manufacturing applications. This research has resulted in the publication of four high-quality papers in peer-reviewed international journals.

11202721.label: Major findings and research outcome
11202721.value: A precise and efficient computational framework has been developed to predict the heating and cooling behaviors of laminated glass facades exposed to fire and equipped with a down-flowing water film. Based on the three-dimensional finite difference method (3DFDM), this framework ensures high numerical stability when solving heat transfer equations involving water film and air convection. The 3DFDM was validated through experimental heating and cooling tests, with its thermal results compared against those from commercial software. The model was then applied to investigate the effects of polyvinyl butyral (PVB) interlayer thickness and water film release time (WFRT) on the thermal response of laminated glass. Simulations revealed that each 0.38 mm increase in PVB thickness reduces the temperature in the second glass layer by approximately 7 °C. The cooling rate was found to be highest on the fire-exposed surface compared to other surfaces, particularly the ambient side, with the rate increasing as WFRT increased. Notably, WFRT had a greater influence on cooling behavior than PVB thickness, highlighting the importance of early water film release in preventing glass failure. These findings provide critical insights into optimizing water film parameters (including WFRT) to enhance the thermal and fracture resistance of laminated glass during fire incidents. Additionally, a three-dimensional meshfree peridynamic (PD) framework was developed to assess the fire resistance and mechanical performance of laminated glass facades, focusing on thermomechanical cracking under realistic thermal boundary conditions, including the presence of a down-flowing water film. The framework incorporates both uniform and non-uniform temperature field strategies, a PD interface model for laminated glass, and stochastic defect distribution. Validation against experimental data confirmed the model's accuracy in predicting temperature history and crack patterns. Numerical studies examined the effects of glass tensile strength and defect content on crack propagation. Results indicated that lower glass strength or higher defect density leads to more fragmented islands in the glazing’s central region, increasing fall-out risk during fires. Thus, improving glass strength and minimizing defects are essential for enhancing structural integrity in fire conditions. This PD framework serves as a valuable tool for understanding thermal breakage mechanisms and designing safer glass facades, offering practical and theoretical guidance for improving fire performance in engineering applications. The above summarizes the key findings and research outcomes of this project.

11202721.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11202721.value: Further studies on thermal boundary conditions involving water-film-protected glass facades could benefit from meshfree-based modeling methods. These frameworks are well-suited for predicting heat transfer, thermomechanical deformation, stress distribution, crack initiation, propagation, and breakage in various types of glass facades developed in recent decades to meet architectural design demands. Future research should focus on a detailed investigation of glass facades protected by water films at different release rates, incorporating more accurate thermal boundary conditions under fire exposure. Based on the findings, an optimization procedure can be developed to derive a mathematical formula for the optimal design of water-film-protected glass facades. The resulting guidelines will support practical engineering applications, including the design of glass facades and advanced water film-release systems in modern buildings such as exhibition centers, office towers, and shopping malls. Additionally, the influence of fixture configurations on fire resistance should be examined. By gaining deeper insights into glass facade breakage behaviors under varying fire loads and installation conditions, safer and more innovative façade structures and fire-resistant systems can be developed, ultimately enhancing the resilience of buildings against fire hazards.

11202721.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11202721.value: We have developed a finite difference-based meshfree computational framework to predict the thermal behavior of laminated glass facades under a down-flowing water film. The framework's efficiency and accuracy were validated through experiments and comparisons with commercial software. By evaluating the influence of interlayer thickness and water film release time on the cooling behavior of laminated glass during a fire, we gained comprehensive insights into the effects of the down-flowing water film. This framework offers practical guidance for optimizing water film parameters to prevent laminated glass failure in fire incidents. Additionally, we established a peridynamics (PD)-based meshfree framework to model thermomechanical cracking in laminated glass. The proposed PD framework was validated against experimental data, and parametric studies identified key factors leading to crack-induced islands in the glazing’s central region—a phenomenon that increases the risk of glass fall-out in fire conditions. Our findings highlight the importance of reducing material defects to enhance the structural integrity of laminated glass under fire exposure. Together, these modeling frameworks serve as powerful computational tools for assessing the fire resistance and mechanical performance of laminated glass facades subjected to a down-flowing water film.

11203321.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11203321.value: 網絡控制系統安全的定位与检测

11203321.label: Project Objectives
11203321.value: Developing a geometric control framework to identify system’s structural vulnerability and localize stealthy cyber attacks, with measures of system vulnerability and attack stealthiness, and the detectability of attacks---------- Industrial networked control systems are an important class of cyber physical systems (CPSs) and are of enormous industrial, environmental, and societal impact. Unfortunately, industrial control systems (ICSs) typically operate over unprotected communication links such as SCADA systems and are vulnerable to malicious attacks. Recent analysis of cyber attacks on networked systems, e.g., the power plant in Ukraine and the uranium enrichment plant in Iran indicates that these attacks were launched in a stealthy manner on the system. In this objective, we seek to develop a control-theoretic framework based on the geometric control theory, linking the system vulnerability and attack stealthiness to control-theoretic concepts such as controllable and observable subspaces, and in the more general scenario, to feedback-invariant subspaces, which can be used as measures of detectability to identify and localize where the system may be vulnerable and where the attack may potentially be launched. Developing scalable characterizations and detectability conditions for stealthy threats in large-scale, distributed multi-agent systems (MASs), with measures of cardinality requirements, network connectivity and scalability constraints, together with detection algorithms and defense strategies----------As opposed to centralized control architecture considered in Objective 1, distributed control systems such as MASs pose more difficult and also more realistic security challenges, since distributed actuators and sensors expose them to attacks of a higher cardinality. Moreover, because of the sheer scale and complexity of MASs, the detection algorithms must be scalable. Network centrality and network controllability/observability will be brought in to develop algorithms for identifying and localizing the critical, sensitive nodes, which will be further enhanced by scalable actor-critic learning methods. Developing an integrated model-based control-theoretic and data-driven machine-learning approach for detection, estimation, and defense of stealthy attacks, with learning-enhanced subspace identification and Kalman filtering algorithms--------- In nearly all the current model-based CPS security studies, it is assumed that the adversary has full or partial knowledge of the system. Likewise, in model-based detection and defense methods, the system operator is assumed to have knowledge of the attack. Neither of these assumptions is practical, since the knowledge of the system model and attack model are both difficult to obtain. To reinforce the control-theoretic framework, we develop machine learning techniques to learn the models and to develop learning-enhanced detection and estimation algorithms. Deep learning and reinforcement learning algorithms will be developed in conjunction with subspace identification and Kalman filtering algorithms. Conducting simulation studies for evaluating and validating the models, theories, methods and algorithms developed in the project----------The benchmark, industry-standard Tennessee Eastman (TE) process will be employed to guide and validate our theoretical development. The TE simulator is a well-known benchmark industrial control testbed that emulates real-world chemical process control problems, and it has been recently adopted by US National Institute of Standards and Technology as an ICS cyber security testbed. The TE process is suitable for its reconfigurability and other desirable features, and simulations on the process ensure that the developments in this project be practically relevant. In summary, the project is motivated by challenges facing today’s industrial networked control systems security, and it seeks to provide answers and solutions addressing the challenges. The project, while relevant to general CPS security problems, targets specifically the domain of ICSs and attempts to develop domain-specific techniques. Leveraging upon the PI’s successes on networked, multi-agent systems and ongoing studies on CPS security, a cohesive research plan is carved out, which seeks to fuse model-based control-theoretic analysis with data-driven machine-learning analytics. Preliminary investigations show that the proposed approach is potentially feasible and may deliver results of significance, which has the promise to lead to practically relevant detection and defense techniques that together with traditional IT technologies such as authentication and encryption, will bring the security protection of industrial networked control systems to a higher level and a fuller extent.
rows: Developing a geometric control framework to identify system’s structural vulnerability and localize stealthy cyber attacks, with measures of system vulnerability and attack stealthiness, and the detectability of attacks---------- Industrial networked control systems are an important class of cyber physical systems (CPSs) and are of enormous industrial, environmental, and societal impact. Unfortunately, industrial control systems (ICSs) typically operate over unprotected communication links such as SCADA systems and are vulnerable to malicious attacks. Recent analysis of cyber attacks on networked systems, e.g., the power plant in Ukraine and the uranium enrichment plant in Iran indicates that these attacks were launched in a stealthy manner on the system. In this objective, we seek to develop a control-theoretic framework based on the geometric control theory, linking the system vulnerability and attack stealthiness to control-theoretic concepts such as controllable and observable subspaces, and in the more general scenario, to feedback-invariant subspaces, which can be used as measures of detectability to identify and localize where the system may be vulnerable and where the attack may potentially be launched.

Developing scalable characterizations and detectability conditions for stealthy threats in large-scale, distributed multi-agent systems (MASs), with measures of cardinality requirements, network connectivity and scalability constraints, together with detection algorithms and defense strategies----------As opposed to centralized control architecture considered in Objective 1, distributed control systems such as MASs pose more difficult and also more realistic security challenges, since distributed actuators and sensors expose them to attacks of a higher cardinality. Moreover, because of the sheer scale and complexity of MASs, the detection algorithms must be scalable. Network centrality and network controllability/observability will be brought in to develop algorithms for identifying and localizing the critical, sensitive nodes, which will be further enhanced by scalable actor-critic learning methods.

Developing an integrated model-based control-theoretic and data-driven machine-learning approach for detection, estimation, and defense of stealthy attacks, with learning-enhanced subspace identification and Kalman filtering algorithms--------- In nearly all the current model-based CPS security studies, it is assumed that the adversary has full or partial knowledge of the system. Likewise, in model-based detection and defense methods, the system operator is assumed to have knowledge of the attack. Neither of these assumptions is practical, since the knowledge of the system model and attack model are both difficult to obtain. To reinforce the control-theoretic framework, we develop machine learning techniques to learn the models and to develop learning-enhanced detection and estimation algorithms. Deep learning and reinforcement learning algorithms will be developed in conjunction with subspace identification and Kalman filtering algorithms.

11203321.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11203321.value: This project initiates, from a systems and control perspective, an investigation into security issues of networked control systems with an orientation toward industrial control. Our goal is to develop a control-theoretic approach integrated with machine learning techniques, for the development of detection algorithms and defense strategies against cyber attacks found in networked control systems. We propose a cohesive research plan consisting of four synergistic technical objectives, leading progressively to an integrated control-theoretic and machine-learning approach. First, we seek to develop a geometric control characterization and localization scheme for detectability of stealthy cyber attacks. This unique scheme will enable us to identify and localize the structural vulnerabilities of a system where it may be vulnerable and the attack may be stealthy. Second, we attempt to develop detection algorithms and defense strategies for large-scale interconnected multi-agent systems (MASs) controlled by distributed controllers. The security of MASs poses more difficult and also more realistic a challenge, since distributed actuators and sensors expose them to attacks of a higher cardinality. Because of the scale and complexity of such systems, the detection algorithms must be scalable. We investigate fundamental requirements on sensor placements for detection and prevention of attacks, in both cardinality and geometry. In tight synergy with the above objectives, we shall also develop machine learning techniques to reinforce the control-theoretic approach, with the goal of developing integrated model-based control-theoretic and data-driven machine-learning algorithms for detection and estimation. Finally, the benchmark, industry-standard Tennessee Eastman process will be employed to guide and validate our theoretical development. Industrial networked control systems are omnipresent in civil and industrial infrastructures, including, e.g., power grids, chemical processes, intelligent manufacturing, and hence are of enormous industrial, environmental, and societal impact. Unfortunately, networked control systems are also vulnerable to cyber attacks. The project, while relevant to general cyber-physical system security problems, is motivated by and targets at challenges facing today’s industrial control systems security, and it seeks to provide answers and solutions addressing the challenges. We hold the viewpoint that the understanding generated from this project will contribute toward the advance and application of security studies for industrial networked control systems. The technical approach is built on the PI’s research results on networked control, multi-agent systems and ongoing studies on cyber-physical security. 11203521.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11203521.value: 本項目考慮了時變網絡上的多智能體分佈式優化（DMAO）問題。在 DMAO 中，每個多智能體被賦予一個本地目標函數，網絡的主要任務是通過本地計算和通信共同最小化節點的目標函數之和。 DMAO因其在機器學習、傳感器網絡、智能電網、分佈式控制系統等領域的廣泛應用而備受關注。基於隨機梯度 (SG) 的優化方法是凸/非凸優化中最基本的方法。在集中優化場景中，基於隨機子梯度的方法已被廣泛研究。近年來，一些經典的隨機梯度方法如隨機梯度下降、隨機鏡像下降、隨機對偶平均法、隨機坐標下降等得到了很好的發展。在這些方法中，為了描述由 SG 方法生成的序列逼近最優解的行為，收斂速度是最重要的主題之一。對於基於 SG 的方法，在不同背景或假設下得出最佳收斂速度對於研究發展至關重要。例如，在非光滑凸優化中，設計基於 SG 的方法是必不可少的，其收斂速度為 O(1/sqrt(T))，迭代步長為 T。然而，在許多現實世界的網絡系統中，在很多複雜且集中設置的情況下SG方法通常不能直接用於應對網絡引起的優化問題。這些研究是非常需要解決，特別是要為這些設置開發有效的優化方法並在集中設置中恢復最佳收斂速度。本項目旨在為時變網絡上的多智能體網絡優化開發不同類型的分佈式優化算法。 此外，與以前的基於分佈式 SG 的方法相比，這些方法都是獨立且同分佈（i.i.d.）隨機擾動梯度性的，本項目將研究非 i.i.d.隨機梯度背後的隨機性對分佈式優化方法性能的影響。將收斂性能在應用領域進行分析。特別是，本提案中開發的分佈式優化算法將應用於分佈式在線正則化回歸問題。 本項目中產生的理論成果，將為包括隨機優化、統計機器學習在內的廣泛領域的發展奠定堅實的基礎。特別是對非 i.i.d 的調查。項目中基於 SG 的分佈式優化算法將為未來改進現有 i.i.d 的工作提供基本的技術程序。

11203521.label: Realisation of objectives
11203521.value: All objectives have been achieved. 1/ Distributed Optimization with limited information [Realization of Objectives 1, 2, and 3] In [1], the problem of solving distributed online Optimization over a network that consists of multiple interacting nodes. Each node in the network is endowed with a sequence of loss functions, each of which is revealed to the node after a decision has been made. The goal of the network is to minimize the cumulative loss functions of nodes in a distributed fashion while subject to two types of information constraints, namely, message quantization and bandit feedback. A distributed online bandit optimization algorithm is proposed by adopting a random quantization operation and a one-point gradient estimator. [Realization of Objectives 1 and 3]. In [2], a mirror descent algorithm with delayed subgradient information is established based on the theory of Bregman divergence. With a non-Euclidean Bregman projection-based scheme, the proposed method essentially generalizes many previous classical Euclidean projection-based distributed algorithms. [Realization of Objectives 1 and 3]. In [5], the convex-constrained Optimization over a time-varying multiagent network is investigated in the non-Euclidean sense, where the bandwidth limitation of the network is considered. Thus, to save network resources by reducing communication costs, an event-triggered (ET) strategy is applied in the information interaction of all the agents over the network. Then, an event-triggered distributed stochastic mirror descent algorithm is developed. [Realization of Objectives 1, 2, and 3]. 2/ Distributed Optimization with time-delay [Realization of Objectives 1 and 3] Communication delays are unavoidable in electronic engineering problems. In [4], a distributed optimization problem (DOP) over the time-varying communication network topology with communication delays is studied. Hence, the proposed generic algorithm framework has wide applications in these fields. The generic algorithm framework is applied to the mirror descent algorithm and dual averaging algorithm. 3/ Applications of Optimization with sampling process under various constraints with non-i.i.d features [Realization of Objectives 2]. Many factors affect the features of non-i.i.d data, such as user preferences, data collection methods, and client characteristics. We studied different applications and investigated their characteristics in the estimation and learning process. In [3], a practical scheme of the desired controller under the lossy digital network is designed by introducing a dynamic coding and packet-length optimization strategy. The goal is to improve the accuracy of coding with limited information in a network. In [6], the distributed joint state and fault estimation issue for a class of nonlinear time-varying systems over sensor networks constrained by energy harvesting. It is assumed that data transmission between sensors requires energy consumption, and each sensor can harvest energy from the external environment. In [7], the distributed maximum correntropy estimation issue for nonlinear time-varying systems over energy-harvesting-constrained sensor networks in non-Gaussian noises is considered. A cost function based on the maximum correntropy criterion rather than the conventional minimum covariance is the optimization index to improve the estimation effect in non-Gaussian environments. In [8], the distributed filtering problem for a class of nonlinear systems under edge-based event-triggered (ET) communication. A dynamic edge-based ET mechanism for the sender-receiver ET scheme is proposed. This scheme allows the receiver node to be privileged to receive or reject the incoming state information, which is more conducive to reducing the transmission of redundant state information from the sender.

11203521.label: Major findings and research outcome
11203521.value: Eight papers have been published in Automatica and IEEE journals. The results of the developed Distributed Optimization Problem (DOP) are based on different methods under various scenarios. (I) DOP with limited information[1]: We studied the problem of online bandit optimization over a multi-agent network, where the nodes can only exchange quantized information with their neighboring nodes. We have developed a quantized distributed online bandit optimization algorithm that requires only functional evaluations of the loss functions. (II) DOP with delayed subgradient information constraints[2]: Paper [2] has studied the mirror descent algorithm with delayed subgradient information under adaptive quantization. We design an adaptive quantization method to solve the limited communication channel and analyze the convergence of the algorithm with different stepsizes and quantization parameters. The optimal convergence rate can be obtained under appropriate conditions. This article has improved many previous works in various aspects. (III) Communication delays in DOP[4] A generic algorithm framework is proposed for solving DOPs with communication delays. This is the first paper to deal with networks with communication delays. This algorithm can be applied to many important distributed Optimization algorithms, such as the mirror descent algorithm and dual averaging algorithm, (IV) Event-Triggered Distributed Stochastic Mirror Descent for Convex Optimization[5] Furthermore, we investigated distributed optimization over event-triggering schemes to relieve the burden of network bandwidth occupation. A non-Euclidean distance is first considered in the projection process, and this has extended to solve a larger class of problem sets and shows key contributions to the work. (V) Quantization communication in DOP[3] This work studied the network communication problem during optimization. This work has comprehensively considered the adverse impacts of the coding error and the packet loss on the control performance under lossy digital networks. (VI) Applications: (i) Distributed Energy-Based Estimation Over Harvesting-Constrained Sensor Networks[6] Under a set of energy harvesting constraints, the proposed estimator only uses local and neighbor data to simultaneously estimate the system state and the fault, thereby establishing a distributed estimation framework. (ii) Distributed Estimation Under Energy Harvesting Constraints Over Sensor Networks[7] The distributed maximum correntropy estimation technique for nonlinear time-varying systems over energy-harvesting-constrained sensor networks in non-Gaussian noises is proposed. A new energy-based estimator is constructed under non-Gaussian noise environments. (iii) Sender-Receiver under edge-based Event-Triggered Schemes for Distributed Filtering[8] This scheme provides a new design for the receiver nodes to control the triggering conditions. This further reduces the redundant information sent from the sender nodes.

11203521.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11203521.value: (i) Online bandit optimization: A possible future direction is to derive a more relaxed version of the random quantization scheme. It would also be of interest to investigate whether the regret bounds can be further refined by either adopting a more sophisticated analysis technique or exploiting the smoothness or strong convexity of the loss functions. (ii) Distributed Constrained Optimization With Delayed Subgradient Information: For future work, we can consider how to use adaptive methods in other settings, such as dual averaging algorithms and online composite optimization. (iii) Distributed Optimization over the Time-Varying Network with Communication Delays: The work can be extended from fix time-delays in each node to various time-delays. (iv) Event-triggered DOP: Our future studies will focus on the algorithm with asynchronous communications, the algorithm with communication delays, the online algorithm, and the mirror descent-based distributed algorithm under the unbalanced network. (v) Energy harvesting sensor networks: Future directions worthy of research include applying the proposed distributed energy-based estimator to sensor networks that allow energy sharing among sensors and time-varying sensor networks. (vi) Future research topics include extending the proposed energy-based distributed maximum correntropy estimator to various systems, such as power grids and relay networks.

11203521.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11203521.value: This proposal considers the problem of distributed multi-agent optimization (DMAO) over the time-varying network. In DMAO, each agent is endowed with a local private objective function, and the main task of the network is to collectively minimize the sum of the objective functions of nodes through local computations and communications. DMAO has attracted much attention due to its widespread applications in areas such as machine learning, sensor networks, smart grids, and distributed control systems. This project considers distributed constrained optimization with delays, limited Information, and quantization, which are crucial issues in DMAO. In addition, the event-triggered scheme is developed to save resources in optimization. New optimal convergence rates for various scenarios are guaranteed by rigorous theory. Further applications of distributed optimization techniques are investigated under sensor networks as follows: (i) Under a set of energy harvesting constraints, a proposed estimator uses local and neighbor data to simultaneously estimate the system state and the fault, thereby establishing a distributed estimation framework. (ii) A new energy-based estimator is constructed under non-Gaussian noise environments via a distributed maximum correntropy estimation technique. (iii) A new edge-based design is constructed to allow receiver nodes to avoid redundant Information sent by senders.

11203721.label: Project Objectives
11203721.value: In view of the distributed nature of devices in HVAC systems, the first objective of the proposed research is to develop recurrent neural network approaches to sensor-actuator deployment via distributed and global optimization for deploying HVAC systems. Specifically, collaborative neurodynamic optimization based on multiple recurrent neural networks and swarm intelligence techniques will be explored for system performance optimization such as minimizing power consumption subject to load and other physical constraints. In face of the multi-modality of devices in HVAC systems, the second objective is to develop neurodynamics-driven approaches to receding-horizon planning for optimal operations of HVAC systems. Particularly, collaborative neurodynamic optimization will be exploited for distributed load dispatching and device coordination by minimizing operation and maintenance costs such as switching frequency of devices. In presence of nonlinearity and uncertainty of thermodynamics/fluid dynamics and intricacy of disturbances, the third objective is to develop an intelligent methodology based on neural computation and machine learning for dynamic modeling and distributed control of networked HVAC systems. Specifically, the state-of-the-art methods of neurodynamic optimization and supervised learning will be developed and applied for HVAC system identification, disturbance estimation, and robust control. Its completion will substantially improve the modeling and control performances for energy saving and comfort preservation. In pursuit of the practical applicability of the expected outcomes for the proposed research, the last objective is to implement and integrate the proposed neurodynamics-driven distributed optimization and control methods in a cyber-physical system on an experimental platform to demonstrate their viability for real-world HVAC applications.

11203721.value: 供暖、通風和空調 (HVAC) 系統是調節住宅、工業和商業建築室內環境以滿足人類舒適度和空氣質量要求的重要設施。據香港機電工程署報告，暖通空調系統消耗了香港商業住宅領域 26% 的能源。在全球範圍內，暖通空調系統分別約占美國和全球能源消耗的 20% 和 10%。在全球城市化進程中，預計暖通空調系統將佔據越來越大的能源消耗部分。 與具有少量氣動、熱力和電氣設備的傳統 HVAC 系統相比，大型建築物中的現代 HVAC 系統由數百到數千個多模式設備組成。隨著物聯網 (IoT) 技術的進步，許多此類設備都配備了計算和通信功能，可促進暖通空調系統的優化和控制，以進行負載調度、系統監控和控制。鑑於可用的物聯網技術和全球對提高生活質量、減少能源消耗和碳排放的需求，在智慧城市樓宇自動化中開發智能暖通空調系統在技術上是可行的，在經濟上是有利的。 作為人工智能的支柱，神經計算近年來因其在許多智能係統的建模、優化和控制方面的成功應用而備受關注。特別是，我們最近關於全局優化和智能控制的協作神經動力學方法的研究結果證明了它們在暖通空調系統中的巨大應用潛力。 在此项擬議的研究中，將从事基於神經計算的暖通空調系統的優化和控制進行系統研究。研究將由四個連貫的部分組成。第一部分將側重於開發神經動力學方法，以在網絡暖通空調系統中優化傳感器-執行器部署。第二部分將重點開發協作神經動力學方法，以在各種操作約束下對多模式暖通空調設備進行分佈式負載調度和協調。第三部分將重點開發基於神經網絡的智能方法，用於對受到各種干擾下的物聯網設備和暖通空調系統進行建模和控制。第四部分將重點驗證所提出的神經動力學驅動方法在調節環境熱狀態和提高網絡物理系統在各種環境中的能源效率方面的功效。預計擬建項目的順利完成將大大推進智能暖通空調系統的研發。

11203721.label: Realisation of objectives
11203721.value: The goals set by the four objectives are attained with varied success. The first goal is mostly attained. We developed several data processing and optimization methods based on recurrent neural networks for the purpose of sensor-actuator deployment. In addition, we developed a scheme for IoT-based distributed chiller loading to minimize energy consumption via neurodynamics-driven distributed global optimization. The second goal is successfully attained. We developed several schemes for planning the operations of chiller systems with different types of devices via collaborative neurodynamic optimization based on homogeneous and heterogeneous recurrent neural networks. The third goal is also successfully attained. We developed a hybrid model predictive control method for turning chillers on and off to achieve the most economical energy consumption and regulating the thermal energy flow to meet demand, thereby minimizing operational wattage. The fourth goal is partially attained. The proposed neurodynamics-driven methods are simulated and tested based on real data from the literature and compared with the state-of-the-art methods to substiante their superiority in solution quality for wattage-saving and optimization efficiency.

rows: In view of the distributed nature of devices in HVAC systems, the first objective of the proposed research is to develop recurrent neural network approaches to sensor-actuator deployment via distributed and global optimization for deploying HVAC systems. Specifically, collaborative neurodynamic optimization based on multiple recurrent neural networks and swarm intelligence techniques will be explored for system performance optimization such as minimizing power consumption subject to load and other physical constraints.

In face of the multi-modality of devices in HVAC systems, the second objective is to develop neurodynamics-driven approaches to receding-horizon planning for optimal operations of HVAC systems. Particularly, collaborative neurodynamic optimization will be exploited for distributed load dispatching and device coordination by minimizing operation and maintenance costs such as switching frequency of devices.

In presence of nonlinearity and uncertainty of thermodynamics/fluid dynamics and intricacy of disturbances, the third objective is to develop an intelligent methodology based on neural computation and machine learning for dynamic modeling and distributed control of networked HVAC systems. Specifically, the state-of-the-art methods of neurodynamic optimization and supervised learning will be developed and applied for HVAC system identification, disturbance estimation, and robust control. Its completion will substantially improve the modeling and control performances for energy saving and comfort preservation.

In pursuit of the practical applicability of the expected outcomes for the proposed research, the last objective is to implement and integrate the proposed neurodynamics-driven distributed optimization and control methods in a cyber-physical system on an experimental platform to demonstrate their viability for real-world HVAC applications.

11203721.label: Major findings and research outcome
11203721.value: In this project, we developed several data processing methods based on recurrent neural networks. Specifically, we developed several clustering algorithms based on recurrent neural networks [13. 15, 19-21]. These algorithms are viable for learning data in an unsupervised manner to analyze HVAC systems. Moreover, we developed several dynamic optimization models or systems based on recurrent neural networks and multi-agent systems [8, 10-12, 24] for global and distributed optimization. These optimization methods are applied to planning and controlling HVAC systems [1-7]. Additionally, we developed a semi-supervised feature selection method based on information-theoretic measures and neurodynamic optimization models [14]. We also developed feature extraction methods via matrix factorization [9, 18]. We also applied the feature selection method for the fault diagnosis of HVAC systems [C1]. Furthermore, we developed machine learning models and algorithms [9, 18] for the supervised learning of image segmentation and classification. They are also applicable to the modeling of HVAC systems. To ensure model stability and algorithm convergence, we analyzed the stability of recurrent neural networks and derived several stability conditions [16, 23]. These results provide guidelines for designing and applying recurrent neural networks to model and optimize HVAC systems. In addition, we developed a scheme for IoT-based distributed chiller loading to minimize energy consumption via neurodynamics-driven distributed global optimization [1, 6]. We proposed several schemes for planning the operations of chiller systems with heterogeneous HVAC devices via collaborative neurodynamic optimization based on homogenous and heterogeneous recurrent neural networks (i.e., Hopfield networks and projection networks) [5, 6]. We developed a hybrid model predictive control method for turning chillers on and off to achieve the most economical energy consumption and regulating the thermal energy flow to meet demand, thereby minimizing operational wattage [5]. The proposed neurodynamics-driven methods are simulated and tested using real data from the literature, and their performance is compared with that of state-of-the-art methods to substantiate their superiority in terms of solution quality for wattage savings and optimization efficiency [1-6].

11203721.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11203721.value: Many avenues are open for further investigations. For example, the proposed methods may be implemented in GPU-based CUDA systems to equip them with real-time computational power in real-world applications. The proposed methods may also be extended to other applications of HVAC systems, such as planning and control of heating systems. Furthermore, more advanced technologies based on deep learning may be developed and applied to the modeling, planning, and controlling of intelligent HVAC systems.

11203721.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11203721.value: Heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) systems are essential facilities for regulating the indoor environment in residential, industrial, and commercial buildings, ensuring specified human comfort and air quality requirements are met. In the global warming and global urbanization processes, it is anticipated that HVAC systems would take up an increasing portion of energy consumption. As a backbone of artificial intelligence, neural computation attracts significant attention in recent years due to its successful applications for modeling, optimization, and control of many intelligent systems. In the project, a systematic investigation was conducted for the AI-powered planning and control of chiller systems based on neural computation. The project consists of four coherent parts, focusing on developing AI-powered approaches to distributed deployment in networked chiller systems, to distributed load dispatching with different types of devices under various operational constraints, to modeling and control of IoT-based chiller systems subject to various disturbances, and to the validating the efficacy of the methodologies in regulating ambient thermal states and improving energy efficiency in various settings. It is believed that the results of the project could promote or advance the research and development of intelligent HVAC systems.

11203821.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11203821.value: 適用於高效熱分析和模擬的統一時空等幾何配點法及其在增材製造中的應用

11203821.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11203821.value: This project investigates and develops alternative methods for producing unified space-time solutions based on isogeometric collocation methods (ST-IGA-C). Both spatial and time dimensions are integrated as a single extended computation space. The computation space and the solution space are further represented using the same non-uniform rational B-splines (NURBS) basis functions. Isogeometric collocation methods (IGA-C) are finally applied for producing the IGA solutions. The main idea of IGA-C rests on the discretization of the governing partial differential equations (PDEs) in strong form at designated collocation positions. The use of the IGA-C method leads to the use of a reduced number of evaluations needed for solution matrix formation to only one-per-degree of freedom and further reduces the computational cost for isogeometric analysis. In addition, other algorithms based on blockwise solutions and smooth adaptive knots will also been developed for producing efficient unified space-time IGA-C solutions. Main areas of research in the proposed project include (1) the development of a general framework on isogeometric collocation methods for unified space-time IGA-C solutions using NURBS, subdivision schemes and other compatible spline spaces for unstructured quadrilateral meshes, (2) efficient blockwise solutions along the time dimension for unified space-time IGA-C solutions, (3) smooth adaptive knots for field-aligned space-time IGA-C solutions with improved per-degree-of-freedom accuracy for application specific solutions, and (4) application of the resulting parameterization in thermal analysis and simulation with a particular emphasis on process modeling and simulation for 3D/4D printing. The proposed methods will contribute to isogeometric analysis with added capability in producing efficient unified space-time IGA-C solutions and with extended applications in time-dependent thermal analysis and simulation, especially in process simulation and optimization for metal additive manufacturing and other 3D/4D printing processes to be addressed in the project. The research outcomes can also be further extended for simulation in mechanics of soft and responsive materials and for producing efficient time-dependent solutions for many other applications in connection with heat transfer and fluid flow simulation. 本項目研究並開發基於統一時空等幾何配點法(ST-IGA-C)的系統求解方法。解的空間和時間維度會集成為一個單一的擴展計算空間，計算空間和解空間統一使用相同的基函數、如非均勻有理 B 樣條 (NURBS) 基函數，等幾何配點法 (IGA-C) 最終用於生成系統的等幾何分析(IGA) 解。等幾何配點法(IGA-C)的主要思想為，在指定的配點位置嚴格滿足給定的偏微分方程 (PDE) ，進而實現其離散化求解。使用 IGA-C 方法可以將求解矩陣形成所需的評估次數減少到每個自由度僅一個，因而進一步降低了等幾何分析的計算成本。此外，本項目還將創建基於分塊求解及平滑自適應結點及其他算法，以產生高效的統一時空 IGA-C 解。項目的主要研究領域包括： (1) 創建一套可用 NURBS、細分及與其兼容而定義於非結構化四邊形網格的其它樣條空間，基於統一時空IGA-C求解的一般框架；(2) 統一時空 IGA-C 沿時間維度的高效分塊求解算法；(3) 適用於場對齊統一時空 IGA-C 求解且可達到每自由度更高精度的平滑自適應節點生成算法；以及 (4) 統一時空 IGA-C 求解在熱分析和模擬中的應用，如3D/4D 打印的過程建模和模擬。本課題的研究將進一步擴展等幾何分析的功能，為其增加高效的統一時空 IGA-C 求解方法，並用於瞬態熱分析和模擬中，如金屬增材製造和其它 3D/4D打印過程的模擬與優化。其研究成果還可以進一步擴展到軟體及響應材料的力學模擬，以及與熱傳導和流體模擬相關的許多其它應用。

11204821.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11204821.value: In many data analysis tasks, we need to match two sets of features. For example, in a content-based image search, we match object features in the source and target images. To predict whether two biomolecules will interact with each other, we can study surface curvature and charge distributions of the molecules and match these features. Given two sets of features, we can match them with different orders. When matching at order r, we consider the compatibility or affinity between r features from the source and r features from the target. Then we solve a problem of graph or hypergraph matching. In general, higher-order methods using hypergraph models are more robust for noisy data. However, the size of the compatibility tensor grows exponentially as the matching order r increases. This complexity makes it prohibitive to deal with large feature sets in terms of computer memory and computing time. This project will develop a novel method for hypergraph matching with large sets of features based on adaptive CUR decomposition. Our strategy is to consider the data redundancy of the compatibility tensor, which has a low rank, and we can explore this property to perform more efficient matching. In the CUR decomposition, we can eliminate redundancies and only retain a small number of column, row, and tube fibers, for example, in a third-order tensor, so that the computer memory and computing time requirements can be reduced significantly. We will investigate how to compute adaptive CUR decomposition of tensors to ensure a high matching accuracy. The structural and relational properties of the feature sets will be considered so that we can choose vertex pairs and hyperedges in the source and target hypergraphs effectively. Graph wavelets will be used to compute the compatibility coefficients. Efficient algorithms will be studied for fast updates of CUR decomposition if we need to add or remove hyperedges. Robust methods will be developed to deal with noisy and distorted features. A significant advantage of our approach over the commonly used singular value decomposition (SVD) based technique is that we deal with the compatibility coefficients directly with CUR decomposition in the matching process. In addition to scientific contributions to hypergraph models, tensor theories, and novel data matching methods, our research will find many practical applications. It will deliver powerful computational tools for image analysis, computer vision, and biomolecular modeling. In many data analysis tasks, we need to match two sets of features. 11205221.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11205221.value: Distributed coordination of networked multiple dynamical systems has attracted much attention due to its broad application in many areas including formation control of unmanned aerial vehicles, rendezvous of multiple mobile robots, deployment of sensor networks, and so on. Networked multiple dynamical systems are often referred to as networked multi-agent systems. Compared with single systems, networked multi-agent systems have the benefits of robustness and scalability, which can tolerate failures of agents or called subsystems and allow addition of new agents or subsystems. In many real-world applications, the parameters of agent models might be unknown due to various reasons, for example, they might be difficult to obtain accurately or they might be slowly time-varying. This motivates researchers to investigate and develop cooperative adaptive control approaches to those networked multi-agent systems with unknown parameters. However, most of existing works on cooperative adaptive control focus on very simple networked multi-agent systems such as minimum phase multi-agent systems with uniform relative degrees subject to neither disturbances nor unmodeled dynamics, which may not be the case for many real-world applications. In fact, the recent literature review reveals that there are still many issues yet to be addressed on the topic of cooperative adaptive control of networked multi-agent systems with unknown parameters. The issues include (i) how to deal with cooperative adaptive control of more general networked heterogeneous multi-agent systems with unknown parameters; (ii) how to deal with cooperative robust adaptive control of networked heterogeneous multi-agent systems with unknown parameters subject to external disturbances and/or unmodeled dynamics; and (iii) how to deal with cooperative adaptive control of networked heterogeneous multi-agent systems with unknown parameters subject to various communication constraints such as time-delays and bandwidth limits which would naturally arise in networked environments and are known to have great adverse impact on the system performance. This project, by addressing those issues, will investigate and develop novel approaches and methodologies for cooperative adaptive control of networked heterogeneous multiple dynamical systems with unknown parameters subject to disturbances and/or unmodeled dynamics as well as communication constraints. The outcomes of this project are expected to be novel theories and methodologies for cooperative adaptive control of networked multiple dynamical systems with unknown parameters which would provide more solid design tools for engineers in real-world applications. 網絡化多動力系統的分佈式協調因其在無人機編隊控制、多移動機器人會合、傳感器網絡部署等諸多領域的廣泛應用而備受關注。網絡化多動態系統通常被稱為多智能體系統。與單個系統相比，網絡化的多智能體系統具有鲁棒性和可擴展性的優點，可以容忍智能體或被稱為子系統的故障，並允許添加新的智能體或子系統。在許多實際應用中，智能體模型的參數可能由於各種原因而未知，例如，它們可能難以準確獲取或它們可能隨時間緩慢變化。這促使研究人員研究和開發針對那些具有未知參數的聯網化多智能體系統的協同自適應控制方法。然而，大多數關於協同自適應控制的現有工作都集中在非常簡單的網絡化多智能體系統上，例如具有統一相對度的最小相位多智能體系統，既不受干擾也不受未建模動力學的影響，這在許多實際應用中可能並非如此。最近的文獻綜述表明，在未知參數的網絡化多智能體系統的協同自適應控制方面，仍有許多問題需要解決。主要問題包括（i）如何處理具有未知參數的更一般的網絡化異構多智能體系統的協同自適應控制，（ii）如何處理具有未知參數且受外部干擾和/或未建模動態影響的網絡化異構多智能體系統的協同魯棒自適應控制，以及（iii）如何處理具有未知參數且受到各種通信約束的網絡化異構多智能體系統的協同自適應控制，典型通信約束包括網絡環境中自然出現的時間延遲和帶寬限制，他們會對系統性能有很大的不利影響。該項目將研究和開發新的方法解決這些問題。該項目的成果有望成為具有未知參數的網絡化多動力系統協同自適應控制的新理論和方法，為工程師在實際應用中提供更可靠的設計工具。

11205221.label: Major findings and research outcome
11205221.value: We have investigated cooperative adaptive control of networked heterogeneous multiple dynamical systems with unknown system parameters. We have developed a novel cooperative robust adaptive control approach to heterogeneous minimum-phase discrete-time multi-agent systems with unknown agent parameters subject to unknown external disturbances. By introducing a distributed adaptive observer and a reference model, a novel framework is proposed to convert the complicated cooperative tracking problem of unknown heterogeneous multi-agent systems into a cooperative tracking problem of the reference model to the leader and a local robust model reference adaptive control problem. It is shown that under the adaptive controller designed based on the proposed framework, the tracking errors between the outputs of all the agents and the output of the leader converge to a residual set. It is also shown that the tracking errors will converge to zero asymptotically when the disturbances are absent. We have also developed a distributed adaptive pole placement control scheme for heterogeneous linear multi-agent systems with unknown agent parameters under directed graphs. The dynamics of agents are allowed to be non-minimum phase with unknown arbitrary individual relative degrees. This is contrary to many existing works on distributed adaptive control schemes where agent dynamics are required to be minimum phase and often of the same relative degree. The distributed adaptive pole placement control scheme consists of a distributed observer and an adaptive pole placement control law. It is shown that under the proposed distributed adaptive control scheme, all signals in the closed-loop system are bounded and the outputs of all the followers track the output of the leader asymptotically. In addition, we have developed a novel distributed robust adaptive pole placement control scheme for unknown heterogeneous continuous-time non-minimum phase linear multi-agent systems with unmodeled dynamics and external disturbances under directed graphs. The novel distributed robust adaptive pole placement control scheme consists of an adaptive distributed observer and a robust adaptive pole placement controller. It is shown that the robust leader-following output consensus problem of the concerned multi-agent system can be solved by the proposed distributed robust adaptive control scheme under some sufficient conditions. It is also shown that the exact output consensus can be achieved if the unmodeled dynamics and external disturbances vanish as time goes to infinity. In the process of achieving the objectives of this project, in addition to those results on cooperative adaptive control of networked heterogeneous multi-agent systems with unknown agent parameters, some other results on cooperative control of multi-agent systems have also been obtained. Extensive simulations via various multi-agent systems including networked mobile robots have been conducted to illustrate the effectiveness of the obtained results. As a result of our research effort, several journal papers have been either published or accepted.

11205221.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11205221.value: This project has investigated cooperative adaptive control of networked heterogeneous multiple dynamical systems with unknown system parameters. However, we have only considered linear agent dynamics, either minimum-phase or non-minimum-phase. It would be interesting to investigate cooperative adaptive control problems of networked heterogeneous multi-agent systems with nonlinear agent dynamics. In addition, we have only considered cooperative adaptive control of heterogeneous multi-agent systems with unknown agent parameters under fixed graphs. It would be interesting to investigate cooperative adaptive control problem of heterogeneous multi-agent systems with unknown agent parameters under switching graphs.

11205221.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11205221.value: Distributed coordination of networked multiple dynamical systems has attracted much attention due to its broad application in many areas including formation control of unmanned aerial vehicles, rendezvous of multiple mobile robots, deployment of sensor networks, and so on. In many practical applications, the parameters of agent models might be unknown due to various reasons, for example, they might be difficult to obtain accurately or they might be slowly time-varying. This motivates researchers to investigate and develop cooperative adaptive control approaches to those networked multi-agent systems with unknown parameters. The recent literature review reveals that most of existing works on cooperative adaptive control focus on very simple networked multi-agent systems such as minimum phase linear multi-agent systems with uniform relative degrees subject to neither disturbances nor unmodeled dynamics. This project has thus investigated cooperative adaptive control problems of more general networked multi-agent systems with unknown parameters. In particular, we have investigated and developed a novel cooperative robust adaptive control scheme for heterogeneous discrete-time minimum-phase linear multi-agent systems with unknown parameters subject to unknown external disturbances. We have also investigated and developed a novel distributed adaptive pole placement control scheme for heterogeneous non-minimum-phase linear multi-agent systems with unknown agent parameters under directed graphs. Furthermore, we have investigated and developed a novel distributed robust adaptive pole placement control scheme for unknown heterogeneous continuous-time non-minimum phase linear multi-agent systems with unmodeled dynamics and external disturbances under directed graphs. We have also carried out extensive simulations to illustrate the effectiveness of the obtained results. The outcomes of this project are expected to consolidate theoretical foundation and also to enhance application potential of cooperative adaptive control for networked multi-agent systems with unknown agent parameters.

11205421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11205421.value: Prostate cancer is the third most common cancer in Hong Kong and the most common non-skin cancer in the United States. Multiparametric MRI (mpMRI) is currently the workhorse for assessing patients with suspected prostate cancer and MRI-targeted biopsy is a standard way for diagnosing prostate cancer. Lesion risk assessment and segmentation are the most important tasks in mpMRI interpretation. Triaging patients based on mpMRI assessment reduces the number of unnecessary biopsies. Lesion segmentation is necessary for patients selected for MRI-targeted biopsy and focal therapies, which target localized lesions and spare patients from aggressive treatments. The current manual workflow for mpMRI interpretation is time-consuming and the analysis result depends on the observer’s experience. More importantly, although radiologists can assess lesions with mpMRI, Gleason grading can only be done reliably through biopsy. Therefore, an automated, non-invasive method for grading and segmenting lesions accurately will provide a leap in patient management. A multi-task convolutional neural network is proposed for automated lesion grading and segmentation. The framework allows collaboration between the grading and segmentation components to improve the performance in both tasks. The framework is developed specifically for fusing different mpMRI modalities at each layer. Propagation of fused feature maps enriches features available to deeper layers and is expected to improve segmentation/grading performance. This proposal also addresses the difficulty of obtaining sufficient images with manual segmentation for fully-supervised learning. A semi-supervised, adversarial lesion segmentation framework is proposed to allow training with a combined set of data consisting of images with and without manual segmentation. The evaluation network drives the segmentation network towards producing similar segmentation results for images with and without manual segmentation, thereby improving the performance on both image sets. The diagnostic role of dynamic contrast-enhanced (DCE) imaging is becoming questionable, with recent investigations showing that it does not improve diagnostic accuracy. Removal of DCE from mpMRI would save imaging time, cost and eliminate patient risks associated with the use of contrast agent. The performance of the proposed framework with and without DCE will be compared in this project. The proposed framework increases the reproducibility and efficiency of mpMRI interpretation, and will have a significant impact on cancer diagnosis, treatment selection and planning. The semi-supervised framework allows calibration for small differences in MR parameters, thereby making the network trained in one centre transferrable to other medical centres/clinics. This automatic interpretation tool will especially benefit medical clinics in which mpMRI expertise is less available. 前列腺癌是香港第三大常見癌症以及美國最常見的非皮膚癌。 多參數 MRI （mpMRI） 目前是評估潛在前列腺癌患者的主力方法，而 MRI 靶向活檢是診斷前列腺癌的標準方法。 病變風險評估和分割是 mpMRI 解析中最重要的任務。 基於 mpMRI 評估對患者進行分類，可減少不必要的活檢。 對於被選擇進行 MRI 靶向活檢和局灶治療的患者，病變分割是必要的。 局灶治療針對局部病變，使患者免於激進治療。 當前用於 mpMRI 解析的手動工作流程十分耗時，且分析結果取決於觀察者的經驗。 更重要的是，雖然放射科醫生可以使用 mpMRI 評估病變，但 Gleason分級只有通過活檢才能被可靠地完成。 因此，一種用於準確分級和分割病變的自動化、非侵入性方法將為患者管理帶來飛躍式進步。 本文提出一種用於自動分級和分割病變的多任務卷積神經網路。 該框架允許分級和分割兩個元件之間協作，以同時提高兩個任務的性能。 該框架尤其為了實現在每一層對不同的 mpMRI 模式進行融合而開發。 融合后的特徵圖往後傳播，為更深的層豐富了可用的特徵，有望提高分割/分級性能。 為解決需要手動分割足夠圖像才可進行的全監督學習的困難, 此項目提出一種半監督的對抗性病變分割框架，允許使用由有或沒有手動分割的圖像組合而成的數據集進行訓練。 評估網路會驅動分割網路對有或沒有手動分割的圖像產生相似的分割結果，因而提高兩個圖像集的性能。 動態對比增強 （DCE） 成像的診斷作用受到越來越多的質疑，因為近期調查表明它並沒有提高診斷準確性。 從 mpMRI 中去除 DCE 將節省成像時間、成本，並為患者消除使用造影劑相關的風險。 此項目將對我們提出的框架在使用DCE或不使用DCE兩種情況下的性能進行比較。 本項目提出的框架將提高 mpMRI 解析的可重複性和效率，且對癌症診斷、治療選擇和規劃有重大影響。 半監督框架允許校准 MR 參數的微小差異，從而使得在一個中心訓練的網路可以轉移到其他醫療中心/診所。 這種自動解析工具將特別有益於一些mpMRI 專業知識較少的醫療診所。

11205421.label: Realisation of objectives
11205421.value: The network described in Objective 1a, which we call MSFusion Net, has been published in Medical Physics (Journal Publication 1). In this paper, we developed a multi-stream fusion encoder to facilitate multiscale fusion of features from three imaging streams for prostate lesion segmentation. The imaging inputs consist of the T2-weighted (T2W) and diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI). The images acquired by DWI was analyzed as two image modalities: the apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) map, which characterizes the amount of water diffusion computed from DW images with different b values, and the DW images acquired with high b values (DWIhb), which provide better visualization of clinically significant prostate cancers. The proposed multistream fusion segmentation network was implemented as a three-stream network processing the T2W, ADC and DWIhb images. The multistream encoder fuses features extracted from the three imaging streams at each layer of the network, thereby allowing for better integration of the feature maps propagating downstream and benefiting segmentation performance. We demonstrated that the proposed framework outperformed single-stream networks and three recently proposed multistream networks, attaining F1 scores of 82.2 and 87.6% in the lesion and patient levels, respectively. The development of the multistream Gleason score classification CNN, described in Objective 1b, and its integration with MSFusion Net were described in a SPIE Medical Imaging conference paper (Conference Publication 1). MSFusion Net first segmented the lesion from T2W, ADC and DW1hb images. The region of interest (ROI) enclosing the segmented lesion was fed to a weakly supervised classification network, which predicted the Gleason grade of the lesion and provided a class activation maps (CAM) corresponding to each MRI modality. Finally, the three MR images with the corresponding CAMs were fed to a six-stream network to generate an enhanced lesion mask. Our experiments showed that the CAM generated from the classifier improves segmentation results. The framework also produces good results for lesion classification with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.88. Another approach we developed is to map multiview features to a latent space and classify lesions using features represented in the latent space. Multiview features refer to image features of the lesions extracted from T2W, ADC and DWIhb images. The projection of features from different views allows correlations among views to be represented; classification based on the latent space representation is shown to improve lesion classification performance compared to feature concatenation. This work has been published in a paper in IEEE Transactions on neural networks and Learning Systems (Journal Publication 2), a highly prestigious journal ranked first in the Journal Citation Reports (JCR) category “Computer Science, Hardware and Architecture” in the most recent report (2021). We further refined this method by developing a framework that enforces consensus and complementarily among views. The paper describing this method has been published in IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man and Cybernetics: Systems (Journal Publication 3). Regarding Objective 2, we have developed a semi-supervised prostate lesion segmentation network that integrates semi-supervision and prototype-based learning, as described in Journal Publication 6. The lesion representative prototypes extracted from labeled and unlabeled data serve as a bridge to enable bidirectional flow between the student and mean teacher networks, thereby improving the model’s generalization ability. The experimental results show that the proposed algorithm outperforms state-of-the-art semi-supervised methods with limited labeled data. For example, the trained model, when applied to segment prostate lesions of an external dataset, attains a Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) that is 10% higher than the mean teacher model. We also investigated the involvement of user interaction in prostate lesion segmentation and published our results in Journal Publication 4. Our approach involves the use of a UNet to provide a coarse segmentation of the lesion. We proposed a rejection network to assess the segmentation quality of the coarse segmentation without involving the ground truth segmentation. The rejection network flags low-quality segmentation and invites an observer to provide a bounding box enclosing the lesions, while for high-quality segmentation, the bounding box was generated from the coarse segmentation. The resulting bounding box was used as a prompt encoder for the Segment Anything Model (SAM) to generate the final segmentation. Our approach achieved at least 24% improvement in DSC by flagging approximately 20% of the images for manual intervention. With the bounding boxes of only half of the images manually provided, the final segmentation accuracy is statistically indistinguishable from the results generated when the manual bounding boxes of all images were provided. Therefore, by including human in the loop, segmentation performance can be improved cost-effectively. Aside from our work in direct prostate lesion segmentation, we also published an article (Journal publication 5) to segment the peripheral zone (PZ) and central gland (CG) of the prostate. The motivation for this zonal segmentation of the prostate is that prostate lesions have different characteristics in MR images. In fact, when a radiologist identifies a lesion, their first task is to determine whether it is in the PZ or CG as there are different workflows for assessing lesions in PZ and CG. This distinction can be challenging given the ill-defined boundaries between zones. We developed a boundary-aware semantic clustering network (BASC-Net) for PZ and CG segmentation. Although methods have been proposed for prostate zonal segmentation, they focused on segmenting the salient inner body region of each zone and failed to segment zonal boundaries accurately. In this study, we propose a network called boundary awareness and semantic clustering network (BASC-Net) addressing the above issues. The central hypothesis behind our approach is that prostate zonal segmentation performance can be improved by first analyzing the inner body and regions close to the edge of each zone separately, followed by fusing the features extracted from the inner body and boundary regions of the same zone so that pixels inside these two subregions would be classified into the same zone. BASC-Net was evaluated on the NCI-ISBI 2013 Challenge and Prostate158 datasets. An inter-dataset evaluation was conducted to evaluate the generalizability of the proposed method. BASC-Net outperformed nine state-of-the-art methods, attaining Dice similarity coefficients of 79.9% and 88.6% for PZ and CG, respectively, in the NCI-ISBI dataset, 80.5% and 89.2% for PZ and CG, respectively, in Prostate158 dataset, and 73.2% and 87.4% for PZ and CG, respectively, in the inter-dataset evaluation.
