11205421.label: Major findings and research outcome
11205421.value: This project successfully achieved all proposed objectives and produced a set of deep-learning frameworks for prostate cancer analysis from multiparametric MRI, including multistream fusion networks, weakly supervised pipelines for lesion classification, semi-supervised segmentation models, an interactive human-in-the-loop segmentation approach, and a boundary-aware prostate zonal segmentation approach. Detailed descriptions and quantitative results are provided in Section 5.3. 1. Multistream Segmentation and Classification We developed MSFusion Net, a multistream fusion encoder–decoder that integrates features from T2W, ADC, and DWIhb modalities on a layer-by-layer basis. This model achieved superior lesion segmentation performance compared with single-stream and existing multistream methods. A Gleason score classification network was further introduced, using class activation maps (CAMs) to refine segmentation and demonstrate that classification-derived spatial cues improve lesion delineation. Together, these works constitute a unified segmentation-classification framework for prostate lesion analysis. 2. Multiview Latent Feature Learning Two additional studies explored multiview latent representations of T2W/ADC/DWIhb features. By projecting features extracted from different modalities into shared latent spaces and enforcing correlation, consensus, and complementarity, we improved lesion classification over traditional feature concatenation. These contributions advance the theoretical and practical use of multiview learning in prostate MRI. 3. Semi-Supervised Lesion Segmentation A semi-supervised prototype-guided framework was developed to leverage both labeled and unlabeled data. Prototype representations enable effective information exchange between student and mean-teacher networks, resulting in significant performance gains—particularly when labeled data are limited. 4. Interactive Human-in-the-Loop Segmentation We proposed a cascaded approach incorporating automated segmentation quality assessment and selective user input. When prompted, an observer provides a simple bounding box, which is used as guidance for the Segment Anything Model (SAM). This strategy substantially improves segmentation while minimizing human effort. 5. Prostate Zonal Segmentation To support clinically relevant lesion assessment workflows, we introduced BASC-Net, a boundary-aware semantic clustering network for segmenting the peripheral zone PZ and CG. By jointly modeling inner-region and boundary features, BASC-Net delivers state-of-the-art accuracy and robustness across datasets. Overall Impact The project delivered a complete suite of algorithms covering segmentation, classification, semi-supervision, interaction, and anatomical modeling. These methods significantly advance automated prostate MRI analysis and lay groundwork for broader clinical translation and extension to other imaging tasks.

11205421.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11205421.value: There are two important areas of development: 1. Prostate lesions in PZ and CG are analyzed differently. We developed a zonal segmentation framework in the hope that the availability of PZ and CG boundaries will improve prostate lesion segmentation performance. A new framework should be developed that uses the PZ and CG boundaries segmented automatically by our BASC-Net described in Journal Publication 5. 2. Although the interactive segmentation approach we described in Journal Publication 4 was only evaluated in segmenting prostate lesions, we believe that our approach would benefit other medical imaging segmentation applications. Further verification studies on other application are therefore required.

11205421.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11205421.value: Prostate cancer is common, and multiparametric MRI is now widely used to decide who needs a biopsy and to guide targeted treatments. Radiologists must judge how risky a suspicious region is and outline it precisely, but this manual process is slow, varies between clinicians, and cannot reliably determine cancer grade without biopsy. This project developed computational tools that automatically grade and segment prostate lesions using a multi-task deep-learning framework that fuses several MR imaging modalities. The grading and segmentation components support each other, improving accuracy in both tasks. To reduce reliance on large annotated datasets, we also introduced a semi-supervised method that learns from both labeled and unlabeled scans, making the system more transferable across hospitals with different MRI settings. We further created an interactive segmentation approach that checks the quality of an automated result and asks the clinician for a simple bounding box only when necessary. This greatly boosts segmentation accuracy while keeping human effort low. In addition, a boundary-aware zonal segmentation network was developed to separate the prostate into its key anatomical zones—important because cancers behave differently depending on location. Together, these tools improve the consistency, speed, and clinical utility of prostate MRI interpretation, particularly in centers with limited prostate MRI expertise.

11206821.label: Project Objectives
11206821.value: We will generalize our recent results on online optimization under inventory constraints in [2] to develop a framework for optimizing storage-assisted demand response under peak-demand charge. The generalized framework will take renewable generation, storage capacity, charging/discharging limits, real-time pricing, and peak-demand charge into consideration when designing online algorithms with optimized worst-case performance (namely competitive ratio). The framework, once successfully developed, can find many applications beyond the demand-response scenario. The smallest possible competitive ratio also characterizes the price of uncertainty (PoU) of the problem. The PoU is a fundamental measure of a problem that captures the benefits of accurate prediction and modeling of the load demand and real-time prices. 2. We will incorporate an adaptive decision-making mechanism to develop adaptive online algorithms to improve the average-case performance. We will also leverage short-term prediction to further improve the algorithms’ performance. These can address two common concerns of worst-case orientated online algorithm design. Using the obtained results, we will characterize how the competitive ratio changes as a function of the prediction window size and the prediction errors’ impact. We will extend the framework and prediction-aware algorithms to the general storage-assisted demand response problem with both (re-)charging and discharging, under real-time pricing with peak-demand charge. These results, once established, not only address a fundamental problem with theoretical contributions but also lead to practical schemes useful for real-world implementation. We will carry out numerical experiments based on real-world traces to evaluate our algorithms’ performance under realistic settings. We will empirically investigate the average-case performance of our algorithms and the benefits of accurate and noisy pre- diction of the inputs (i.e., renewable generation, load demand, and real-time prices). We will also compare our algorithms’ performance with conceivable alternatives, including those requiring short-term predictions or statistical knowledge.

11206821.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11206821.value: 我們將開發具有性能保證的在線算法，在需量電費以及实时定价下，以最大限度地降低具有儲能的大負荷客戶的電力成本。 項目背景 電力用戶根據電網的價格或激勵信號調整消費的需求響應是電力系統運營商更有效地平衡供需的一種現代機制。在圖 1 所示的新興需求響應場景中，大型電力客戶（例如商業、工業和市政）在實時定價和需量電費下利用儲能來減少電費。這裡的需量電費是客戶支付電費的峰值費率，可以達到電費的 50%-80%。同時，由於負載曲線趨於平坦，以及在供應稀缺或昂貴時消耗的減少，客戶的價格響應努力也有利於電力系統。 然而，在實踐中實現這種雙贏的利益在算法上並非易事。用戶擁有的間歇性可再生能源加劇了淨需求和峰值使用的不可預測性，導致在線（成本）優化，而未來信息很少或沒有。雖然在線優化是一個經過充分研究的主題，但事實證明，具有庫存限制和高峰費用的版本很困難。由於存儲容量限制和高峰需求充電，跨時間段的在線充電/放電決策的耦合使該問題具有獨特的挑戰性。直到最近，特殊情況的部分結果才可用；參見例如，[#lin2019competitive]。迄今為止，在幾乎沒有或根本沒有未來信息的情況下，在需量電費下優化存儲輔助需求響應在很大程度上仍然是未解的。 項目描述 我們將填補空白，開發峰值感知在線算法，實現雙贏。我們的計劃是四重的。首先，我們將概括我們在 [#lin2019competitive] 中庫存約束下在線優化的理論結果，以開發一個在需量電費下優化存儲輔助需求響應的框架。該框架將考慮存儲容量、充電/放電限制和需量電費來設計具有最壞情況性能保證（即競爭率）的在線算法。該框架一旦開發成功，就可以在其他問題領域找到應用。其次，我們將自適應決策機制納入框架，以提高所獲得算法的平均情況性能。第三，我們將利用短期預測信息來進一步提高算法的性能。這些可以解決面向最壞情況的在線算法設計的兩個常見問題。 項目初步成果及意義 我們開發了一種優化的在線算法，用於在需量電費下實現燃料電池輔助成本最小化。在基於真實世界軌蹟的案例研究中，與基線替代方案相比，我們的算法在沒有未來知識的情況下提高了 19% 的成本節約，包括基於歷史推斷的那些，甚至那些具有大量預測信息的那些。我們將在初步成功的基礎上，為大型電力客戶在高峰需求充電下的儲能奠定理論基礎並生成在線成本最小化的算法。獲得的策略也可作為未來調查的基準。

11207121.label: Project Objectives
11207121.value: Power electronics converters have been increasingly deployed in power networks for controlling power flows and maintaining the necessary power flow quality from sources to distribution buses, and from distribution buses to loads. The use of power electronics converters is inevitable in new power source systems such as maximum power trackers for photovoltaic panels, fuel cells, battery storage systems, and doubly-fed induction generators in wind power plants. Power electronics are also necessary in loading systems, such as EV battery chargers, household appliances, motor drives, power adaptors, etc. However, conventional synchronous generators are predominantly controlled by traditional speed governors, with regularly slow dynamics, for connections to AC buses using frequency, voltage and rotor speed as control variables. As more power electronics converters are deployed in power networks at various locations and with different performance objectives, incompatibility in dynamic performances of conventional and power electronics components raises serious concerns on stability of the connected systems. The first objective is to therefore establish an effective model that can conveniently describe a mixed conventional-machine-driven and power-electronics driven system that can permit in-depth analysis of the impact of power electronics penetration in power networks. On the local device level, our initial focus will be the grid-following and grid-forming converters, and develop models that adequately describe the operation, dynamics and interaction with the grid. On the global network level, the architecture that connects all the components should realistically contain a number of clustered subnetworks and the inter-subnetwork links which mostly deploy DC transmission. When power electronics installations represent only a small share of the overall power system, the effect on stability is not significant. However, as more power electronics converters are present, their mutual interactions through coupling at common points on distribution buses have been shown to be causes of unstable operation. One typical situation is the mutual presentation of active loads that jeopardises the stability of the originally well designed converters as a result of fast power regulation that effectively manifests as anti-damping or negative resistance. Thus, varying degrees of stability threats exist for different degrees of power electronics penetration into power networks. The challenge in identifying the effects of power electronics penetration lies in the complete lack of effective characterizing parameters that can be used to assess the level of penetration as well as a set of effective stability indicators. The second objective is thus to develop appropriate assessment parameters and performance indicators based on existing observable variables including the grid frequency, grid voltage and rotor angle, plus other emerging stability parameters such as the magnitude of sub-synchronous oscillation. Based on the model developed under the first objective, we will perform analysis to study the effects of power electronics penetration in terms of the new assessment parameters under varying percentage of power-electronics-driven power components. Extensive simulations will be conducted to produce a comprehensive set of data covering different combinations of relative percentages of renewable and conventional sources, and different power flow trading demands among various power distribution clusters which are inevitably power electronics driven. The third objective is targeted to application in real power networks. The models and analysis procedures developed under objectives 1 and 2 will be applied to some real systems such as China's power distribution networks. The aim is to uncover possible scenarios that may pose serious stability and reliability threats to the vital power distribution infrastructure. Currently, China has 7 clusters of power distribution networks, which are arranged according to geographic locations, and neighbouring clusters are connected by DC transmission lines. Power electronics are necessary for control of power flows among clusters as well as within clusters, especially where renewable sources are significantly deployed. In this project, we initially focus on the assessment of the China's power networks, and possibly other power networks, aiming to generate findings that will clearly pinpoint the major design pitfalls in deploying power electronics converters and provide design-oriented criteria for limiting the performance of power electronics equipment in order to reduce the risk of instability and eliminate threats to a robust power infrastructure.

11207121.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11207121.value: This proposal is a resubmission addressing the key criticisms of the referees on last year's proposal. The proposed project aims to study the penetration of power electronics into power generation and distribution systems, as prompted by the increasing use of renewable sources, quest for higher performance in the control of power conversion, as well as the increasing influence of economical plans that necessitate power trading among different regions or clusters of power distribution. As a result of the increased use of power electronics for controlling power flows in power systems, interactions of power electronics systems and conventional synchronous machines' dynamics would inevitably cause stability and robustness concerns. In this resubmission, we focus on specific types of analysis, as requested by the referees, while retaining the three-step investigation into the impact of power electronics penetration on the stability and robustness of power networks. First, the lack of an adequate model that can conveniently describe a mixed conventional-machine-driven and power-electronics-driven system has obstructed any in-depth analysis of the impact of power electronics penetration in power networks. Thus, a model that includes the salient system components, consisting of conventional machines, grid-following and grid-forming converters and their associated control systems will be developed. When the networked system is considered, the connection architecture will realistically contain a number of clustered subnetworks and the inter-subnetwork links which mostly deploy DC transmission (e.g., in China). Second, we will develop new assessment parameters and performance indicators based on existing observable variables including the grid frequency, grid voltage and rotor angle, plus other emerging stability parameters such as the magnitude of sub-synchronous oscillation. The key type of analysis focuses on the effects of power electronics penetration in terms of the new assessment parameters under varying percentage of power-electronics-driven power components. Extensive simulations will be conducted to produce a comprehensive set of data covering different combinations of relative percentages of power electronics installations, and different power flow trading demands among various power clusters which are inevitably power electronics driven. Third, the models and analysis procedures developed will be applied to real systems such as China's power networks. The aim is to uncover possible scenarios that may pose serious stability threats to the vital power generation and distribution infrastructure. The proposed study deals with vital infrastructure in all developed and developing economies, and is expected to produce impactful results that will shed light on the ongoing development of power distribution networks. 本項目針對新能源應用及智能電網發展帶來的挑戰，集中應對高比例電力電子對電網的穩定性及堅固性的影響進行系統性研究。硏究包括連接電網的各種電力電子變換器對電網穩定性的影響，以及大型電網整體的級聯故障分析。硏究結果將對未來智能電網運作的安全性及持續發展具有重大意義。

11207321.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11207321.value: This proposed project will involve novel interdisciplinary research spanning the fields of fundamental geomechanics and computer vision to develop a hybrid feature-aided volumetric digital image correlation method to measure and compute the full-field strain distribution of fine-grained soil mixtures. A fine-grained soil mixture (FGSM) is a natural soil with varying proportions of clay, silt, and sand. The major thrust of this proposed project will be to extend and adapt a series of well-developed object-recognition and image-matching techniques for feature detection, recognition, and matching of volumetric images acquired from in-situ X-ray microtomography scans of FGSMs subjected to external loading. The specific set of image matching techniques will include the three-dimensional (3D) speeded-up robust feature, 3D shape context, spherical harmonics-based particle morphological invariant and point-cloud registration. Depending on the soil compositional and microstructural characteristics, these image-matching techniques will be appropriately integrated to establish a powerful, efficient, and robust digital image correlation system that can be applied to any type of FGSM. This proposed project will generate important impacts in fundamental and applied research in a variety of fields, such as geotechnical engineering, construction materials, material science, computer vision and pattern recognition, concomitant with high economic and societal impacts. The research impacts will primarily derive from the newly established hybrid feature-aided digital image correlation tool, which will enable accurate, efficient, and robust computation of the full-field displacement and strain of FGSMs. Furthermore, advances in the knowledge frontiers of object recognition and image matching will lay the foundation for future interdisciplinary research in these areas. Economic and societal impacts will be achieved from the use of the newly developed digital image correlation tool in geotechnical engineering activities, such as site investigation, design, infrastructure construction and maintenance, or in the manufacturing, handling and processing of engineering materials in relevant industries. The results will contribute to the development of optimized engineering activities and processes, subsequently leading to improvements in geotechnical infrastructure, construction management, hazard warning and mitigation systems in Hong Kong and worldwide. 本研究項目是一項涉及基礎岩土力學和計算機視覺領域的新型的跨學科研究。擬開發一種混合特徵輔助的數字圖像相關方法，用於測量和計算細顆粒土體混合物 (FGSM) 的全場應變分布。FGSM是一種含有不同比例的粘土、淤泥和砂子的天然土體。這項研究的重點是擴展和修改一系列完備的目標識別和圖像匹配技術，以對從加載條件下FGSM的原位X射線微斷層掃描中採集得到的體積圖像進行特徵檢測、識別和匹配。具體的圖像匹配技術將包括3D SURF、三維形狀上下文、基於球諧函數的粒子型態不變和點雲配準技術。根據土體組成和微觀結構特徵，這些圖像匹配技術將被適當的結合起來，以建立一個強大、高效和魯棒的數字圖像相關系統，可應用於任何類型的FGSM。 本研究項目將在岩土工程、建築材料、材料科學、計算機視覺和模式識別等多個領域的基礎研究和應用研究中產生重要影響，同時產生可觀的經濟和社會影響。本研究的影響主要來自於新建立的混合特徵輔助的數字圖像相關工具，它將對FGSM的全場位移和應變進行準確、高效和可靠的計算。此外，目標識別和圖像匹配前沿認知的提升將為今後在這些領域內的跨學科研究奠定基礎。在諸多岩土工程實踐活動，例如現場勘查、設計、基礎設施建設和維護，或相關行業的工程材料製造、處理和加工中，使用新開發的數字圖像相關工具將產生經濟和社會影響。研究結果將有助於開發優化的工程實踐和工藝，進而改善香港及全球的岩土基建、建築管理、災害警告和緩減系統。

11207621.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11207621.value: 鉴于诸如侦察和运输等可预见的应用场景，针对小尺寸、人机友好的飞行器的研究受到了来自科学家和工程师群体的大量关注。这些小型机器人将会对民用机器人的应用产生革命性的影响。然而，在复杂、受限环境内的自主飞行和导航依旧是一个主要的技术障碍。对于有效载荷和计算能力严重受限的小型平台来说，该问题更加严重。 目前针对避撞飞行的方法主要依靠传感器来绘制标定环境和周围的障碍物。当前最先进的方法通常采用基于视觉的定位或光流辅助算法进行姿态估计，规划和飞行控制。作为这些检测和绘制策略的补充，轻量化的保护结构和机械式的弹性机身已经被开发出来，用于飞行机器人应对碰撞或随后坠落带来的影响。到目前为止，针对避免碰撞的感知和估计算法的作用和用于减轻碰撞后果的弹性机构的作用是显著分开且独立的。 在本项提出的研究中，我们引入了一种空气力学方法，使得飞行机器人可以被动的避免碰撞，而无需直接的感知或指令解算。本研究将分三步解决有效载荷和计算资源有限的小型空中机器人的反应式导航问题。首先，当机器人在一个垂直表面附近飞行时，为了引入一个空气力学响应，飞行器采用了向内倾斜的涵道螺旋桨。我们初步的测量结果表明该螺旋桨产生的下洗尾流和墙壁之间存在着显著的空气力学作用。在飞行测试中，该作用会导致推力的水平分量发生明显变化，即使在没有位置反馈或控制的情况下，该分量也会使机器人被动地稳定在离墙壁的一定距离处。其次，针对结合了描述螺旋桨表面受力的气动模型的姿态动力学和螺旋桨指令的分析，得出了一个简单的障碍物检测的观测器。因此，我们设计了一种高效的、基于非接触式墙壁跟踪策略飞行方案，用于小型飞行机器人的反应式导航。最后，我们提出通过开发可变形的机身来削弱由于采用倾斜螺旋桨带来的关于飞行能量消耗方面的不利影响。可重构性使得机器人在安全环境中运行时采用传统的螺旋桨布置以节省能源，或在杂乱空间中采用倾斜的螺旋桨布置方案实现无碰撞飞行。 可以看出，本报告中所提出的研究通过引入基于力学的导航方案，将促进小型飞行机器人的发展并扩大其使用范围。其科学价值将来自于：（i）在多旋翼飞行器动力学框架下，增进对于螺旋桨表面空气动力学效应或趋近效应的理解。（ii）开发具有最小感知和计算需求的新型反应式导航策略。（iii）使用可重构结构来提高小型多旋翼飞行器的飞行时长和防撞能力。

11207621.label: Realisation of objectives
11207621.value: Introduction The primary aim of this project was to advance the fundamental understanding and practical application of proximity effects in multirotor aerial vehicles equipped with tilted and ducted propellers. The proposed research objectives spanned the aerodynamic modeling of propeller-surface interactions, integration of these effects into flight dynamics, and the development of novel estimation and navigation strategies for visionless, contact-free wall following. The following sections detail the realization of each objective, supported by experimental results and peer-reviewed publications, and highlight the progression from theoretical modeling to practical demonstration. Completion of Objective 1 Objective 1 of this project was to “investigate, model, and characterize the aerodynamic interactions between a tilted and ducted propeller and a nearby surface, and demonstrate the use of the proximity effects as a passive mechanical strategy for preventing a collision between a multirotor robot and a wall”. This objective has been fully achieved, as detailed in the paper “Passive wall tracking for a rotorcraft with tilted and ducted propellers using proximity effects” published in IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters. The paper systematically addresses the core elements of Objective 1. First, it develops an aerodynamic model—primarily based on momentum theory—to predict how the thrust generated by a tilted and ducted propeller is affected by the proximity of a vertical surface. The model elucidates how both the magnitude and direction of propeller thrust change as the rotorcraft approaches a wall, providing a quantitative framework for understanding the proximity effect. These theoretical predictions were rigorously validated using benchtop force and power measurements, which confirmed the model’s accuracy in capturing the essential aerodynamic interactions. Building upon this foundational understanding, the paper introduces a novel rotorcraft platform equipped with tilted and ducted propellers, specifically designed to exploit the proximity effect. Through a combination of modeling, experimental characterization, and real-world flight experiments, the study demonstrates that the aerodynamic interaction between the propeller wake and a nearby vertical surface creates a passive repulsive force. This force stabilizes the robot at a predictable and controllable distance from the wall, effectively preventing collisions without the need for active sensing or complex control algorithms. Significantly, the research shows that by only controlling the robot’s attitude and altitude, the equilibrium distance from the wall can be manipulated through the attitude setpoint. Flight experiments validated the passive wall-following strategy, showing stable, contact-free flight alongside a wall and confirming the utility of proximity effects as a reliable mechanical collision avoidance mechanism. This approach leverages physical intelligence, embedding the collision avoidance capability directly into the vehicle’s aerodynamics and mechanical design. Completion of Objective 2 Objective 2 focused on incorporating the aerodynamic model describing the influence of a vertical surface on the flight dynamics of a multirotor vehicle. This objective has been fully achieved, as documented in the npj Robotics paper, which presents a comprehensive treatment of how proximity effects between a tilted and ducted propeller and a nearby wall can be systematically modeled and integrated into the dynamic analysis of multirotor platforms. Unlike the previous work, which concentrated on characterizing and demonstrating the proximity effect as a passive collision avoidance mechanism, the npj Robotics paper advances the research by embedding the aerodynamic model directly into the vehicle’s flight dynamics. The study provides a detailed mathematical framework that quantifies the changes in force and moment acting on the robot as a function of its distance and orientation relative to a vertical surface. The model extends beyond static thrust characterization by explicitly analyzing how these proximity-induced aerodynamic effects influence the translational and rotational behavior of the entire multirotor system during flight. Benchtop experiments and controlled flight tests were used to validate the fidelity of the aerodynamic model, confirming that the predicted force and moment variations closely match empirical observations. These results underscore the practical accuracy of the model for real-time flight dynamics prediction, supporting its integration into higher-level vehicle control and planning algorithms. A key distinction from the previous paper/objective is that the npj Robotics work is not limited to demonstrating the existence of a stable, passively maintained wall-following distance. Rather, it systematically incorporates the proximity-effect-induced aerodynamic terms into the full equations of motion for the vehicle, enabling a more generalizable and quantitative understanding of how wall effects shape the flight dynamics in both nominal and perturbed conditions. This lays the groundwork for subsequent estimation and navigation strategies but remains focused on the physical modeling and its direct impact on vehicle behavior. Completion of Objective 3 Objective 3 aimed to devise an estimation and navigation strategy that enables a robot, operating without vision, to follow a wall contour toward a destination in a contact-free and visionless manner, and to realize this strategy in flight. The npj Robotics paper makes a substantial contribution to this objective by presenting both the methodological framework and experimental results for a filtering-based estimation scheme and a passive collision avoidance strategy uniquely tailored to the aeromechanical properties of the platform. The estimation component centers on leveraging the proximity effect as a proprioceptive cue. Specifically, as the multirotor platform approaches a vertical surface, the aerodynamic model (developed in Objective 2) predicts a distinct, distance-dependent change in the vehicle’s lateral force and yaw moment. The paper details the design of a filtering algorithm that uses onboard inertial measurements—primarily lateral accelerations and yaw rates—to infer the proximity to the wall. This estimation framework operates without any vision or external ranging sensors, relying exclusively on the physical interaction between the vehicle’s propulsion system and the environment. The filtering algorithm is implemented as a recursive estimator, which continually refines its estimate of the wall distance by comparing measured flight dynamics against the expected aerodynamic responses from the model. The estimator demonstrated reliable convergence in both simulation and experimental flight trials, with wall distance estimates maintaining an error below 10 cm across a range of operating conditions. This level of precision proved sufficient for robust collision avoidance and wall-following, even in the presence of sensor noise and moderate environmental disturbances. Building upon the estimation capability, the navigation strategy exploits the passively generated repulsive force as a mechanical constraint, while modulating the desired heading to guide the robot along the wall contour. The controller adjusts the vehicle’s attitude setpoint to either maintain or vary the equilibrium distance, allowing the robot to navigate turns and follow complex wall geometries without direct sensing of the environment. Experimental results validated the approach: the robot successfully performed stable, contact-free wall following in both straight and curved segments, achieving continuous navigation toward a designated endpoint without collisions or loss of control. This was accomplished without recourse to vision or external mapping, demonstrating the practical feasibility and robustness of the proposed estimation and navigation framework. Conclusion In summary, the project has successfully met all original research objectives, culminating in the development and validation of a proximity-effect-based framework for passive collision avoidance and wall following in multirotor robots. The outcomes not only deepen the scientific understanding of rotorcraft-surface aerodynamics but also demonstrate robust, minimal-sensing navigation strategies with practical relevance to robotics applications in cluttered or GPS-denied environments.

11207621.label: Major findings and research outcome
11207621.value: The project has resulted in several key scientific and technological advances, primarily detailed in Ding et al. 2022 and Ding et al. 2024, that collectively establish a new proximity-effect-based framework for passive collision avoidance and wall following in multirotor robots. 1. Fundamental aerodynamic characterization: Ding et al. 2022 provided the first systematic investigation into the aerodynamic interactions between tilted and ducted propellers and nearby vertical surfaces. The study developed a momentum-theory-based model that quantitatively describes how the proximity of a wall alters both the magnitude and direction of thrust generated by the rotorcraft. This model was validated through benchtop force and power measurements, confirming the presence of a stable, repulsive force when the vehicle operates near a surface. This proximity-induced aerodynamic effect enables the robot to passively maintain a safe distance from walls with minimal sensing and control requirements. 1. Integration into flight dynamics: Building on this foundation, Ding et al. 2024 advanced the research by embedding the proximity-effect aerodynamic model directly into the full flight dynamics of the multirotor platform. The paper presented a comprehensive mathematical framework that incorporates the changes in force and moment as a function of the robot’s pose relative to a wall, enabling accurate prediction of system behavior in both nominal and perturbed flight conditions. The model was validated through both benchtop and in-flight experiments, demonstrating close alignment between predicted and observed vehicle responses in proximity to vertical surfaces. 1. Visionless estimation and wall-following strategy: A significant outcome, as described in Ding et al. 2024, is the development of a filtering-based estimation algorithm that uses only onboard inertial measurements to infer wall proximity, eliminating the need for external vision or ranging sensors. This estimator maintained a wall distance estimation error below 10 cm during flight trials, enabling robust and contact-free wall following even in cluttered or unstructured environments. The navigation strategy exploited the passive mechanical repulsive force and modulated vehicle heading to follow both straight and curved wall segments, achieving reliable collision avoidance and stable navigation toward designated goals. Summary: Collectively, these findings significantly advance both the theoretical understanding and practical application of proximity effects in aerial robotics. The project outcomes, as detailed in Part C (Ding et al. 2022, Ding et al. 2024), establish a new paradigm for minimal-sensing, physically intelligent navigation and set the stage for further research and technology transfer in the field.

11207621.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11207621.value: Building on the demonstrated passive proximity-based wall following and collision avoidance, future research could aim to generalize the aerodynamic modeling to encompass a broader range of surface geometries, such as curved or textured walls, and dynamic environments with moving obstacles. An important extension is to model and control flight in settings where multiple surfaces are present simultaneously, such as navigating within or along air ducts, pipes, or narrow passageways. These scenarios are highly relevant to real-world inspection applications, where robots must maneuver in confined, cluttered, or industrial environments with complex boundary conditions. Integrating additional onboard sensors, such as low-cost time-of-flight, tactile, or airflow sensors, could further enhance estimation accuracy and enable robust navigation in more challenging or cluttered configurations. This would allow the system to reliably detect and react to a variety of surface types, dynamically changing boundaries, and even moving obstacles, which is critical for autonomous inspection, maintenance, and search-and-rescue tasks. To support these research and development directions, significant funding opportunities. The Innovation and Technology Fund (ITF) is particularly suited to projects that aim to translate fundamental research into industrial applications.

11207621.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11207621.value: This research project explores how small flying robots, like drones, can safely navigate close to walls and obstacles without needing cameras or complex sensors. By studying the effects that nearby surfaces have on the air pushed by the robot's tilted and ducted propellers, the team discovered a way for the drone to “feel” the presence of walls using only its own flight dynamics. The project developed new mathematical models to predict how these aerodynamic interactions work, and built a drone that uses these effects to keep a safe distance from obstacles—almost like having a built-in invisible bumper. This approach allows the robot to follow walls and avoid collisions passively, requiring less electronics and making it lighter, more robust, and able to operate in dark, smoky, or cluttered environments where vision-based methods fail. Real-world experiments showed the system could reliably keep away from walls and navigate along them, opening up new possibilities for safer inspections, search-and-rescue, and exploration in tight or hazardous spaces. Ultimately, this work lays the foundation for smarter, simpler, and more efficient flying robots that can work safely alongside people and in challenging environments.

11207821.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11207821.value: 全世界每年都有許多新的癌症病例。在香港，2018 年有超過 14,000 人的死亡與癌症有關，而且每年新增癌症患者的人數都在增加。當患者在早期得到診斷時，他們有很大機會治愈。然而，當癌症在晚期才被檢測到，患者的存活率會低很多。當癌細胞由於血源擴散而遷移出原發腫瘤並侵入其他器官時，就會發生癌症轉移。轉移性癌症很難被治療，尤其是當侵襲性細胞已經擴散到多個器官時。患者不僅身心受苦，還要支付高昂的醫療費用。因此，開發一種可以在癌症擴散發生之前及早發現癌症的生物傳感系統是重要的。 這項研究提出了一種新的三維 (3D) 微結構的開發，該微結構被納米結構包圍，用作生物傳感器。通過對所提出的傳感系統進行適當的設計和利用納米製造技術，可以高效地捕獲和高敏地探測細胞和生物分子。檢測循環腫瘤細胞 (CTCs) 和相關的小生物分子，如微泡 (MVs)，對於早期癌症診斷很重要。 CTCs 和 MVs 是癌症的重要指標，但它們的濃度通常較低。因此，一個即使濃度很低也能檢測到它們的生物傳感系統在早期癌症診斷中非常有用，從而提高存活率。 本研究將開發一種新方法以創建完全被納米結構覆蓋的 3D 微結構。這樣的設計將促進細胞和生物分子附著微結構及納米結構3D 系統。通常，表面形貌或傳感器只能建立在頂部表面上。通過本研究所提出的利用形狀記憶聚合物的特殊特性的技術，納米形貌和生物傳感器不僅可以在頂部表面形成，還可以沿側壁和底部表面形成，使系統能更有效地捕獲 CTCs 和 MVs。此外，規律地圍繞 3D 微結構的納米結構將集成為納米等離子體傳感器，從而提供密集的檢測器陣列進行傳感。結合了內置生物傳感器的微結構和納米結構將達到檢測低濃度 CTCs 和 MVs 所需的高效捕獲和高敏檢測系統。本研究所提出的傳感系統可以提供早期癌症診斷所需的高靈敏度和高效率。

11208121.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11208121.value: Multiobjective optimization problems naturally arise in many real-world applications, where more than one objective is needed to optimize. Multitask learning and many engineering design problems can be treated as multiobjective optimization problems. Very often, no single solution can optimize all the objectives simultaneously. In the past two decades, many multiobjective optimization algorithms have been proposed to find a single Pareto solution or a finite set of Pareto solutions with different trade-off preferences among all objectives. However, many multiobjective optimization problems have an infinite number of Pareto optimal solutions, and a finite set cannot approximate them very well. This project will study how to learn the whole Pareto set in the decision space by a single math model. Using the learned model, decision makers can obtain their preferred Pareto solutions with specific trade-offs in real time. In recent multitask learning and some engineering applications, it is highly desirable that the Pareto optimal solutions for different preferences have common components. For example, when we build one neural network for multiple tasks with different preferences, for the sake of robustness and cost-effectiveness, we require that some weights in the neural network are the same for all the preferences, and others vary from preference to preference. We call it the structure constraint. In multiobjective modular design, such constraints can arise naturally as well. No effort has been made to study it. We will investigate this constraint and develop algorithms for finding the best trade-off solution set subject to the structure constraint. The proposed algorithms in this project can be used in a wide range of real-world applications, such as flexible multitask learning with real-time adjustment, robust multitask network building, as well as personalized manufacturing and robust modular design in industry engineering applications. The outcome of this project will bridge multitask learning and multiobjective optimization, and lead to a breakthrough in these areas. We will use the proposed algorithms to design multiobjective recommendation systems and base station antennas. 許多實際應用都會涉及到同時優化多個目標。譬如，大量工程設計任務都可以被視為多目標優化問題。多数情况下，沒有单個方案可以同時優化所有目標。在過去的20多年裡，研究者已提出不同的多目標優化算法，來尋找單個帕累托解或有限个帕累托解，用以代表所有目標間的不同權衡偏好。然而，許多多目標優化問題有無數個帕累托最優解，有限个帕累托解並不能很好地逼近它們。本項目將研究如何通過單個數學模型學習決策空間中的整個帕累托集。通過使用我們提出的模型，決策者可以實時獲得滿足其特定偏好的帕累托解。 在最近的多任务學習和工程設計應用中，決策者希望針對不同偏好的帕累托最優解可以共享部分結構。例如, 在構建一個針對多個偏好的多任務神經網絡系統時, 考慮到魯棒性及成本，我們要求對于不同偏好，一些權重系數是相同的，其余系數可隨偏好變化。我們稱此類約束為結構約束。在多目標模塊設計中，也常遇到此類約束。據我們所知，目前並沒有針對這些結構約束的研究。本項目將系統地研究多目標優化中的結構約束，並開發相關算法尋找滿足特定結構約束的帕累托解集。 該項目中提出的算法將可用於廣泛的實際應用中，例如支持實時調整的靈活多任務學習、穩健的多任務網絡構建，以及工業工程應用中的個性化製造和模塊化設計。該項目的成果將溝通多任務學習和多目標優化這兩個不同的領域。我們所提出的算法也會用於設計高性能天線。

11208121.label: Realisation of objectives
11208121.value: We have carried out the following research activities to fully achieve all the project objectives: Objective 1 Aggregation and Preference Vector Design 1.1 Hypervolume-Guided Decomposition for Multiobjective Optimization This work integrates hypervolume-based EI with the MOEA/D framework and propose a novel EI, named the expected directionbased hypervolume improvement (DirHV-EI). The DirHV-EI only measures the hypervolume improvement within each axisparallel box induced by the modified Tchebycheff scalarization. Thus, it has a simple analytical expression that can be easily computed. Theoretical analysis indicates that the maximization of our proposed improvement function can help to maximize both the weighted hypervolume and the Tchebycheff improvement metrics. Using DirHV-EI, we design a decomposition-based Bayesian optimization algorithm, called DirHV-EGO, for solving expensive multiobjective optimization problems. At each iteration, the MOEA/D is used to maximize the DirHV-EI values with respect to a number of direction vectors in a collaborative manner, and a number of candidate solutions can be obtained. Then, a submodularity-based greedy selection strategy is used to select multiple query points from the candidates. Objective 2 Approximate Model for Pareto Set 2.1 Pareto Set Learning for Neural Multi-Objective Combinatorial Optimization In this work, we generalize the idea of neural combinatorial optimization, and develop a learning-based approach to approximate the whole Pareto set for a given multiobjective combinatorial optimization problem without further search procedure. We propose a single preference-conditioned model to directly generate approximate Pareto solutions for any trade-off preference, and design an efficient multiobjective reinforcement learning algorithm to train this model. Our proposed method can be treated as a learning-based extension for the widely-used decomposition-based multiobjective evolutionary algorithm (MOEA/D). It uses a single model to accommodate all the possible preferences, whereas other methods use a finite number of solutions to approximate the Pareto set. 2.2 Pareto Set Learning for Expensive Multi-Objective Optimization This work develops a novel learning-based method to approximate the whole Pareto set for Multi-objective Bayesian optimization (MOBO), which generalizes the decomposition-based multi-objective optimization algorithm (MOEA/D) from finite populations to models. We design a simple and powerful acquisition search method based on the learned Pareto set, which naturally supports batch evaluation. In addition, with our proposed model, decision-makers can readily explore any trade-off area in the approximate Pareto set for flexible decision-making. This work represents the first attempt to model the Pareto set for expensive multi-objective optimization. Objective 3 Structure Constraints for Multiobjective Optimization 3.1 Evolutionary Competitive Multitasking Optimization This article introduces a special multitasking optimization problem (MTOP) called the competitive MTOP (CMTOP). Its distinctive characteristics are that all tasks’ objectives are comparable, and its optimal solution is the best one among the optimal solutions of all the individual problems. This article proposes an evolutionary algorithm with an online resource allocation strategy and an adaptive information transfer mechanism to solve the CMTOP. 3.2 Offline and Online Objective Reduction via Gaussian Mixture Model Clustering This work proposes to produce several different sets of essential objectives in objective reduction. More specifically, we use the Gaussian mixture model clustering to classify the obtained nondominated front into different subsets and perform objective reduction on each subset. Both an offline objective reduction method and an online objective reduction method are developed. 3.3 Improving Pareto Local Search Using Cooperative Parallelism Strategies for Multiobjective Combinatorial Optimization Pareto local search (PLS) is a natural extension of local search for multiobjective combinatorial optimization problems (MCOPs). In our previous work, we improved the anytime performance of PLS using parallel computing techniques and proposed a parallel PLS based on decomposition (PPLS/D). In PPLS/D, the solution space is searched by multiple independent parallel processes simultaneously. This article further improves PPLS/D by introducing two new cooperative process techniques, namely, a cooperative search mechanism and a cooperative subregion-adjusting strategy. In the cooperative search mechanism, the parallel processes share high-quality solutions with each other during the search according to a distributed topology. In the proposed subregion-adjusting strategy, a master process collects useful information from all processes during the search to approximate the Pareto front (PF) and redivide the subregions evenly. 3.4 Bilevel Optimization via Collaborations among Lower-Level Optimization Tasks In this work, we develop a bilevel metaheuristic with the collaborations among lower-level optimization tasks. Specifically, a population is evolved to solve the lower-level optimization tasks for all upper-level solutions collaboratively at each generation. In the population, each solution is associated with a lower-level optimization task. In such a way, all lower-level optimization tasks can be solved in a single run. To capture the individual features of different lower-level optimization tasks, we construct a lower-level search distribution for each lower-level optimization task based on all solutions in the population. In addition, an information-sharing mechanism is proposed to share good solutions among lower-level optimization tasks. Objective 4 High-performance based Antenna Design 4.1 Design of Wideband Base Station Antenna by Involving Fragment-Type Structures on Dipole Arms Base station antenna usually requires dual-polarization operation with satisfactory input return loss, adequate dual-polarization isolation, stable gain, and half-power beamwidth (HPBW) in a wide bandwidth covering the entire or part of the mobile communication bands. Such comprehensive requirements provoke great challenges in antenna design. A novel design scheme is proposed by involving fragmenttype structures (FTSs) in antenna and seeking for the optimal FTS by multiobjective optimization searching. The technique is demonstrated by improving crossed dipoles for operation in band ranging from 1.7 to 3.8 GHz. Part of the dipole arms can be gridded into cells and reconfigured by using FTS elements. For automatic optimization searching, a binary coding scheme for both the FTS distributions and canonical dipole structure dimensions is proposed. 4.2 Ensemble Learning-Based Multi-Objective Optimization for Antenna Design An ensemble-learning-based multiobjective optimization is proposed for antenna design. By integrating the local search into multiobjective evolutionary algorithm based on decomposition (MOEA/D) and selecting appropriate solutions of the local search acquired with different offspring reproduction (OR) operators, the MOEA/D combined with ensemble OR (MOEA/D-EOR) is presented. Parallel local OR operators based on samples are also merged, for the first time, by exhaustively mining the evolution data of the optimization searching. The diversity and convergence of MOEA/D-EOR are verified by several widely used benchmark problems. The efficiency of MOEA/D-EOR is demonstrated by designing a high-performance bow-tie multiple-input and multiple-output (MIMO) antenna, which saves at least 25% of the optimization time. The overall performance of MOEA/D-EOR is further demonstrated by designing a 2x2 MIMO patch antenna in a compact size, which achieves a high isolation of 24 dB in an operation band of 4.95–5.07 GHz.

11208121.label: Major findings and research outcome
11208121.value: Based on the comprehensive research conducted throughout this project, we have achieved significant findings and research outcomes across four project objectives, all of which have been documented in high-impact peer-reviewed international journals or conferences. For Objective 1 (Aggregation and Preference Vector Design), our major outcome is the successful integration of hypervolume-based Expected Improvement (EI) with the MOEA/D framework. We developed the novel Expected Direction-based Hypervolume Improvement (DirHV-EI), which features a simple analytical expression for efficient computation. Building upon DirHV-EI, we proposed the DirHV-EGO algorithm, a decomposition-based Bayesian optimization method for expensive multi-objective problems that simultaneously maximizes both weighted hypervolume and Tchebycheff improvement metrics. This work has been published in IEEE Transactions on Evolutionary Computation. For Objective 2 (Approximate Model for Pareto Set), we proposed the Pareto set learning framework that uses a single preference-conditioned model to effectively approximate the entire Pareto set for multi-objective optimization problems. We also generalized this idea for both combinatorial and expensive optimization problems. This approach is as a novel learning-based extension of MOEA/D that transitions from finite populations to models, which represents a promising new approach for multi-objective optimization. These contributions were published in top-tier international machine learning conferences ICLR and NeurIPS. For Objective 3 (Structure Constraints for Multiobjective Optimization), we identified novel problem structures and proposed corresponding optimization strategies. Key innovations include the formulation of Competitive Multitasking Optimization (CMTOP) and the development of cooperative parallelism and bilevel optimization via task collaboration. The outcomes are efficient evolutionary algorithms with online resource allocation, information transfer mechanisms, and objective reduction techniques using Gaussian Mixture Model clustering, which leads to in multiple publications in IEEE Transactions on Evolutionary Computation and IEEE Transactions on Cybernetics. For Objective 4 (High-performance Antenna Design), our research demonstrates that integrating fragment-type structures (FTSs) and ensemble learning with multi-objective optimization can effectively address complex design challenges for antenna design. The key outcome is the development of a wideband base station antenna and a high-performance bow-tie multiple-input and multiple-output (MIMO) antenna. These designs achieved significant performance improvements, which are validated through two publications in IEEE Transactions on Antennas and Propagation. In summary, this project has produced an integrated suite of advanced algorithms and practical design methodologies that substantially advance the state-of-the-art in multi-objective optimization.

11208121.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11208121.value: Based on the research outcomes achieved in this project, several promising research directions emerge for future work: Extension 1. More Powerful Pareto Set Learning The proposed Pareto set learning and structure constraint handling techniques can be extended to address more complex problems, such as large-scale multiobjective optimization and dynamic optimization problems where environments change over time. We should develop more efficient model architectures and training strategies to these challenging scenarios while reducing computational demands. In addition, we also plan to strengthen the theoretical foundations of our approaches. Extension 2. Learning-based Optimization There is also considerable potential to integrate our algorithms with emerging artificial intelligence technologies, particularly deep learning and reinforcement learning, to develop more adaptive and intelligent optimization methods. We will also investigate more efficient learning-based approach to uncover and better leverage various structure constraints for different multiobjective optimization problem. Extension 3. More Applications Beyond antenna design, we will explore applications in emerging fields such as artificial intelligence, supply chain management and smart manufacturing. We will seek interdisciplinary collaborations with domain experts to validate and enhance our methods in these practical scenarios. We will also open-source software platforms to facilitate wider adoption and collaboration within the research community.

11208121.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11208121.value: This project developed intelligent optimization algorithms to solve complex problems involving multiple competing goals. Consider designing a car where you aim to maximize both speed and fuel efficiency, where these objectives are conflicted and finding the best compromises poses significant challenges. Our research centered on two key breakthroughs. First, we proposed a novel approach to approximate the whole Pareto Set , which contains all optimal solutions representing different trade-offs among objectives, such as balancing performance and cost. Instead of finding just a few good trade-off solutions, our methods build a single math model to show users all the best possible solutions to choose from, enabling more informed and efficient decision-making. Second, we developed techniques to handle complex structure constraints, which represents hidden rules or hierarchies within an optimization problem. Our algorithms can automatically identify and manage these structures to enhance optimization efficiency. Moreover, the uncovered structures help decision-makers gain deeper insights into optimization problem they face. The value of this work lies in its broad applicability. We have successfully applied these methods to design high-performance antennas for mobile communications, and the same core algorithms can be extended to fields such as logistics, manufacturing, and artificial intelligence.

11209021.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11209021.value: 开发能够承受更高剂量和温度的材料已成为实施先进反应堆的关键问题。近年来，高熵合金（HEAs）由于具有良好的机械性能、优异的耐腐蚀性和抗氧化性以及良好的耐辐射性，作为潜在的结构材料受到了广泛的关注。增加主要元素的数量可以有效地减少电子和声子的平均自由程，从而改变缺陷的形成并延迟缺陷的演化，从而提高抗辐照能力。 然而，目前对 HEA 的辐照研究主要集中在单相（FCC 或 BCC）材料上。由于其固有特性，单相 HEA 的性能仍然不能令人满意。 FCC 合金具有延展性，但通常在高剂量下容易发生空隙膨胀。 BCC 合金强度更高，但容易发生辐射引起的脆化。自然，精心设计的 FCC-BCC 复合结构可以实现这种平衡。这项拟议的研究旨在设计一类新型抗辐照 FCC-BCC 共晶 HEAs (EHEA)，其具有平衡的强度和延展性以及改进的抗辐照性。两相的体积分数、层间距和组成将经过精心设计，以实现机械性能和抗辐照性之间的平衡。然后将研究高温重离子辐照下的缺陷演变，特别是相界的影响将被表征。共晶结构的稳定性和每个相内的相稳定性将使用互补透射电子显微镜 (TEM) 和原子探针断层扫描 (APT) 进行表征。基于系统的实验研究，将揭示 EHEAs 的辐照耐受机制。 该提案的成功实施将导致对 EHEAs 的辐照行为有一个全面的了解，但尚未记录在案。这些成果将为加速设计用于先进核应用的抗辐照 HEA 提供有效指导。

11209021.label: Realisation of objectives
11209021.value: Nuclear energy plays an increasingly crucial role in meeting global energy demands as well as reducing carbon emissions and fostering sustainable developments. However, the hostile environments (e.g. ultrahigh dose and high temperature) in the advanced nuclear reactors inevitably bring about serious degradation of materials, posing great threat on the safety and sustainability of the nuclear reactors. In this project, we proposed a novel strategy to eliminate the irradiation-induced damages via developing eutectic high-entropy alloys with high-density uncoherent FCC/BCC interfaces. Five objectives were proposed to realize this aim, and all the proposed objectives have been successfully realized. The details of objectives realization were illustrated as follows: 1. To design eutectic high entropy alloys (EHEAs) with BCC-FCC phases and fine lamellar structures. We first designed two kinds of eutectic high-entropy alloys based on the CALPHAD (CALculation of PHAse Diagrams) technique and experimental verification, i.e., Fe47Ni26Al17Cr10 (abbreviated as Fe47), Fe42Ni31Al17Cr10 (abbreviated as Fe42), [in atomic percentage (at %)]. By adjusting the relative content between Fe and Ni, the phase structure and microstructural morphology can be controllably tailored. We demonstrated that the Fe47 EHEA consists of BCC+B2 phase structures, while Fe42 EHEA is composed of FCC + BCC/B2 phase structures based on EBSD and TEM methods. Element Ni is considered as a stabilizer for the FCC phase. Thus, with the decrease of Ni content in EHEA, the stability of FCC phase decreases significantly, leading to the formation of BCC phase. Meanwhile, both the Fe47 and Fe42 EHEAs exhibit very fine lamellar structures, leading to ultra-high yield strength about 1.2 GPa at room temperature. 2. To reveal the irradiation defects in both phases and phase boundaries of the novel EHEAs and corresponding mechanisms. The designed EHEAs were first irradiated by 275 keV He ions under a defocus beam model with a fluence of 5.14 × 1020 ions/m2 under a vacuum of 5 × 10−5 Pa at 1073 K. Overall, the BCC+B2 constituted Fe47 EHEA displayed a superior radiation tolerance to that of FCC + BCC/B2 constituted Fe42 EHEA, in terms of bubble formation. The different responses to the irradiation are highly related to the vacancy dominated He diffusion behaviors, which are greatly affected by the phase compositions and structures. Oversized solute atoms tend to exchange with vacancies to promote the He diffusion, leading to a low irradiation resistance of FCC and BCC phases, which are rich in large-sized Fe and Cr. The slight decrease of ordering degree of B2 phase in irradiated Fe47 EHEA indicates a strong chemical bonding between Ni and Al atoms, which also contributes to a lower vacancy dominated He diffusion. The analysis on the width of bubble denuded zone along the phase boundary further suggested a higher energy barrier for the vacancy migration in the B2 phase. The findings of this work will provide guidance for the design of a new generation of radiation-resistant materials. We further studied the irradiation responses of the Fe42 and Fe 47 EHEA to the heavy Ni ion irradiations. Both the EHEAs were irradiated at 873 K for 5, 30, and 100 dpa to study the irradiation dose on the irradiation defects formation. We found that the designed EHEA exhibited superior irradiation resistance even under a severe irradiation dose of 100 dpa. The Fe42 EHEA consisted of FCC + BCC/B2 phase structure, which shows different irradiation behaviors between them. Some of the dislocation lines, stacking faults, micro void can be observed in the FCC phase, while no irradiation-induced defects can be observed in the BCC/B2 phase region. This indicates that the BCC/B2 phase structure possesses superior irradiation resistance to the FCC phase. So, by optimizing the chemical composition, we achieved a fine BCC + B2 phase structure, i.e. Fe47 EHEA that are nearly irradiation-immune to the irradiation-induced damages. 3. To investigate the microstructural stability of the EHEAs after irradiation and thermal exposure. The microstructural stability of the EHEAs was systematically studied after irradiated by He or Ni ions at elevated temperatures. It is found that the microstructures of both Fe42 and Fe47 EHEAs are basically unaffected by the He or Ni ions irradiation even under a high irradiation dose of 100 dpa. Meanwhile, both EHEAs exhibit superior microstructural stability below 873 K. As the temperature increased to 1073 K, obvious coarsening of the eutectic microstructure occurred. The rapid coarsening of the eutectic microstructure can be attributed to high-density interfaces and low melting points of the eutectic structures. We further studied the oxidation resistance of the both EHEAs at elevated temperatures. The Fe42 and Fe47 EHEAs exhibit excellent oxidation resistance by forming dense and continuous Al2O3 layer even at a low temperature of 873 K. 4. To clarify the synergistic effect of irradiation and thermal exposure on the phase stability of EHEAs. The synergistic effects of irradiation and thermal exposure on the phase stability of Fe42 and Fe47 EHEAs. As mentioned above, the bulk FCC phase in Fe42 EHEA is more sustainable susceptible to the heavy Ni ion irradiation. Some dislocation loop with stacking fault, micro voids can be only observed in the FCC phase when irradiated at 873 K, which may lead to the phase instability of the FCC phase. The Fe47 EHEA was thus designed to further eliminate the irradiation-induced defects via introducing high-density BCC/B2 interfaces, which can act as effective sinks for the recombination of the interstitials and vacancies. With the increase of irradiation temperatures, although the density of phase interfaces decreased due to the obvious coarsening, most of the irradiation-induced damage can self-healing at higher temperatures. When the temperature was above 973 K, the BCC phase in the Fe42 EHEA was disappeared, resulting in an FCC+B2 phase structure. On the other hand, the irradiation also has a slight effect on the ordering degree of B2 phase. The ordering degree of the irradiated B2 phase in Fe42 and Fe47 EHEAs had a decrease of ~16.7%, and 5.2%, respectively, compared with the unirradiated B2 phase, indicating that the B2 phase in Fe47 EHEA is more stable than that in Fe42 EHEA. 5. To obtain a EHEA with balanced irradiation resistance and mechanical properties and understand the underlying mechanism. Based on the current research results, we proposed an innovative approach to developing high-performance, superior irradiation-resistance high-entropy alloys via introducing high-density phase interfaces. The designed EHEAs are nearly irradiation-immune to the irradiation-induced damages, and exhibit superior mechanical properties. The excellent radiation resistance of the EHEAs can be attributed to a large number of interfaces, which act as giant sinks to absorb vacancies and interstitials. These defects can occur recombination at these interfaces, improving the resistance to irradiation. Meanwhile, the designed EHEAs also exhibit excellent tensile properties. The ultrahigh strength can be attributed to the fine lamellar microstructure. However, the fine lamellar microstructure inevitably occurs serious coarsening at elevated temperatures above 1073 K, resulting in a significant decrease in the density of interfaces and related mechanical properties. In summary, this project provides an effective method to design nuclear structural materials with superior irradiation-resistance and mechanical properties via introducing high-density phase interfaces.

11209021.label: Major findings and research outcome
11209021.value: (1) The relatively contents of Fe and Ni have a significant effect on the phase constitution of the FeNiCrAl EHEA. Increasing Ni content can promote the phase transformation from FCC phase to BCC phase. The Fe47Ni26Al17Cr10 EHEA containing B2 and BCC phases shows superior irradiation resistance to the Fe42Ni31Al17Cr10 EHEA containing B2 and FCC phases. The different responses to the He ion irradiation are highly related to the vacancy dominated He diffusion behaviors, which are greatly affected by the phase compositions and structures. Oversized solute atoms tend to exchange with vacancies to promote the He diffusion, leading to a low irradiation resistance of FCC and BCC phases, which are rich in large-sized Fe and Cr. The slight decrease of ordering degree of B2 phase in irradiated Fe47 EHEA indicates a strong chemical bonding between Ni and Al atoms, which also contributes to a lower vacancy dominated He diffusion. The analysis on the width of bubble denuded zone along the phase boundary further suggested a higher energy barrier for the vacancy migration in the B2 phase. (2) Under heavy Ni ion irradiation, the bulk FCC phase is more vulnerable than the BCC phase, resulting in obvious dislocation loop with stacking fault and micro void in the FCC phase region. At a relatively low temperature of 873 K, the high-density interface can act as effective sinks for the recombination of irradiation-induced interstitials and vacancies, and thus greatly reduce the irradiation damages. Meanwhile, the high-density interface also contributes to the achievement of high strength by impeding the dislocation movement. However, with the increase of irradiation temperatures, the interface density was decreased significantly, leading to a decrease of tensile strength. The designed EHEAs can still maintain superior irradiation resistance due to the self-healing behavior at elevated temperatures.

11209021.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11209021.value: This project has proposed an innovative way to design high-performance nuclear structural materials via introducing high-density phase interfaces. However, the fine lamellar microstructure inevitably occurs serious coarsening at elevated temperatures above 1073 K, resulting in a significant decrease of interface density and related mechanical properties and irradiation resistance. Thus, future work can be focused on the improvement of the stability of eutectic structures, such as introducing refractory elements to improve the melting points or developing carbide eutectic alloys. The strategy can also be extended to other types of alloys, such as L12 nanoparticles strengthened high-entropy alloys, which also possess high density FCC/L12 coherent interfaces and superior thermal stability up to 1273 K. However, the deep mechanisms of the irradiation resistance for these materials still need further research.

11209021.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11209021.value: As global energy challenges intensify and environmental pollution worsens, the need for sustainable clean energy to reach carbon neutrality has become increasingly urgent. Among the many available options, fourth-generation nuclear energy systems distinguish themselves through their superior safety, efficiency, and sustainability. However, the harsh operating environments of the fourth-generation nuclear energy systems, characterized by elevated temperatures (up to 1000 °C), intense neutron irradiation (over 100 displacements per atom, dpa), place extremely stringent demands on the structural and fuel-cladding materials. Most of the existing materials inevitably undergo serious degradations under such extreme conditions. Thus, in this project we proposed a strategy to design a kind of eutectic high-entropy alloy with high-density interfaces that can eliminate the irradiation-induced defects and improve the irradiation resistance and durability of the designed alloy under severe irradiation conditions. This research is of great significance to the advancement of fourth-generation nuclear energy technology, as it provides a promising material solution to overcome the critical bottleneck of material degradation under extreme operating conditions.

11209421.label: Project Objectives
11209421.value: Fabrication of a facile and easily scalable omniphobic-slippery membrane surface: we will mimic the springtail cuticle by creating a concave-structured Polystyrene (PS) coating using electrospraying technology followed by application of a thin-film lubricant. Revealing the underlying mechanisms of the omniphobic slippery membrane: we will provide an in-depth study of wetting, scaling and fouling during MD operation through our novel detection and characterization methods which will enable real time monitoring of wetting intrusion and the progression of fouling and scaling, providing early detection which will prolong MD operation, overcoming one of the main bottlenecks. This will allow us to identify any potential tradeoffs between improved fouling, scaling, and wetting resistances and water vapor permeability.

11209421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11209421.value: 為了應對日益嚴重的水資源短缺和更加嚴格的排放標準，非常規水資源的開發開始得到關注，如海水、鹵水和廢水，並急需研發新型技術來增加供水。作為一種熱驅動的基於膜的分離過程，膜蒸餾是當前一種較有前途的技術，用於處理來自不同行業無法通過壓力驅動的反滲透和傳統技術進行處理的高濃度鹽水。 儘管膜蒸餾技術具有實際優勢並引起人們的廣泛興趣，但仍存在許多必須克服的技術障礙，因此當前膜蒸餾技術尚未達到可商業化的階段。具體而言，在處理高濃度鹽水時，疏水膜的孔潤濕、礦物結垢和膜污染等問題會降低膜蒸餾系統的性能，甚至導致工藝失效。因此，對這些問題的基本原理探究和開發有效的膜污染潤濕檢測系統是推動其商業化發展的關鍵。其中，由材料科學的最新進展而推動的先進膜研發，使其具有對於低表面能液體的高抗潤濕性成為了一種有效的應對策略。 在過去的十年中，各種具有特殊抗潤濕性能的新型膜，如疏水膜、超疏水膜、疏水疏油膜或不對稱潤濕膜已被作為潛在的解決方案。其中，疏水疏油膜因其對低表面張力液體的優異抗濕性而受到關注。然而，其製造工藝的高成本和復雜性，以及對造成環境污染的含氟材料的使用限制了疏水疏油膜的實際應用。因此，研發一種簡易環保的疏水疏油膜製造工藝仍是一個挑戰，使膜能夠防潤濕、防結垢和防污染的同時保持高耐用性。 在這項研究中，我們提出了一種簡便且易於擴展的表面改性方法，從根本上解決了傳統製備疏水疏油膜所遇到的局限性。從大自然中汲取靈感，特別是跳蟲的角質層和豬籠草，我們通過靜電噴塗技術在聚偏二氟乙烯基材的基礎上沉積了具有凹形內陷結構的聚苯乙烯微顆粒，來創建一種可重入雙內嵌結構的超疏水潤滑表面。該項目的成功將易潤濕的平滑膜表面轉變為高度粗糙的疏水疏油潤濕膜表面，有效提高了膜的抗潤濕性，抗污染性以及抗結垢性。此外，我們所研發的新型檢測和表徵方法將實現對膜污染，結垢和潤濕過程的實時監測，提供潤濕預警系統，從而在膜潤濕前提前採取措施，延長膜蒸餾系統的運轉時間和使用壽命，也克服了阻礙其工業化發展的主要瓶頸之一。

11210621.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11210621.value: 太赫茲技術將成為新一代 IT 工業發展的必要部分之一。這個高頻段（0.1 到 10 THz）產生了超寬帶寬、超快數據速率、超密集網絡和大規模安全連接的獨特功能。國際電信聯盟 (ITU) 確定了 0.275 至 0.450 THz 的太赫茲頻率可用於未來的無線通信，特別是第六代移動通信 (6G) 及其服務。全球ICT領導者已經開始探索在未來通信網絡中如何有效利用太赫茲波技術的可行性。太赫茲市場預計到 2029 年將達到 35 億美元，從 2020 年到 2029 年的複合年增長率為 27%。然而，要充分發揮太赫茲通信的潛力，仍有一些根深蒂固的挑戰需要解決。例如，太赫茲傳播在大氣中是高損耗的，這限制了通信距離；另太赫茲器件的製造過程非常昂貴。科學家和工程師正在尋找高效、低成本的太赫茲天線方案來實現未來太赫茲通信及其應用。 在這個研究項目中，我們將提出新穎的太赫茲天線設計，並實現高增益、寬帶、波束成形和具有成本效益的天線解決方案來解決太赫茲通信的瓶頸。我們的專用天線技術將支持新興和未來無線系統（例如 6G 及更高版本）的需求。本項目將調查三個確定的研究目標。首先，我們將研究用於太赫茲頻率定向波束輻射的寬帶和高效平面天線陣列。其次，將進行磁電偶極子與波導喇叭天線集成的寬帶太赫茲探頭。太赫茲探頭的這項發明在其寬工作帶寬內提供了極好的輻射源，用於開發太赫茲波段的高增益反射陣列。最後，將展示由 GeTe 功能材料形成的可重構元原子復合而成的有源波束形成反射陣列。使用光學激活來控制元原子狀態的方法發現有效地在反射陣列的超表面上產生編碼圖案以操縱反射光束輻射的方向。本項目的成果將為太赫茲技術提供最先進的高頻天線解決方案，以支持現有和未來的通信系統，並將造福香港、大灣區和全球的學術界和工業界。

11211221.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11211221.value: 从有源域数据到无源域数据的无监督域适应病变分割模型

11211221.label: Project Objectives
11211221.value: To design a robust domain adaptation model for lesion segmentation with WCE images to deal with limited training data and noise effects. Deep neural networks have achieved remarkable success in lesion segmentation at the expense of laborious training data annotation. But large WCE medical datasets are not readily available due to proprietary and privacy concerns. One of the techniques to address this dilemma is unsupervised domain adaptation, which transfers knowledge from a labeled dataset (source domain) to another unlabeled one (target domain). However, existing domain adaptation models target natural images and ignore the negative effect of noise features in medical images, which may lead to biased segmentation performance. Therefore, we propose a hierarchical domain adaptation model to mitigate the influences of noise for lesion segmentation. To investigate intrinsic structure relationships in the unsupervised domain adaptation models to support the accurate lesion segmentation. Existing unsupervised domain adaptation models utilize only features from the last layer of deep learning models to represent images, which may not accurately represent complex WCE images. Moreover, they don't consider the underlying geometric information from the input data, which is crucial for describing the relationships among samples from colonoscopy images and WCE ones. Thus, we will introduce a graph guided feature aggregated module and a graph guided prototype alignment module on top of the designed domain adaptation model for lesion segmentation. The graph guided feature aggregation module enables features from different layers to benefit each other by graph aggregation, while the graph guided prototype alignment module enhances the robust characterizations with category information for lesion segmentation. To reduce the dependence on source data and develop a robust source-free prototypical unsupervised domain adaptation model for lesion segmentation. The majority of existing domain adaptation models need to access the source data during the training to adapt, which is not efficient for data transmission and may violate data privacy policies. Therefore, this proposal makes adequate use of the pre-trained source model together with unlabeled WCE images, and develops a novel source-free domain adaptation model for lesion segmentation. This proposal proposes a self-supervised pseudo label generator to enable training in the target domain and designs novel strategies and constraints to utilize the unlabeled WCE images. To test and verify the proposed automatic lesion segmentation models based on real clinical datasets and construct an integrated segmentation visualization system for practical clinical applications. We will further extend the designed unsupervised domain adaptation models to supervised domain adaptation by involving labeled WCE image into the training stage to further improve the segmentation performance.

11211221.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11211221.value: Wireless capsule endoscopy (WCE) is an effective technique to detect colorectal lesions, which are precursors of colorectal cancer (CRC). Automatic lesion segmentation from WCE images is of great importance to provide valuable information for both CRC diagnosis and further surgery. Deep learning based approaches have achieved significant progress but at the expense of laborious large-scale data annotation. One possible solution to address this issue is unsupervised domain adaptation, which transfers knowledge from labeled datasets in a source domain to an unlabeled target domain. In this proposal, we aim to tackle the important but technically challenging problem of efficiently utilizing the public available colonoscopy images (source domain) to guide lesion segmentation with WCE images (target domain). There are several challenges in applying existing domain adaptation models for lesion segmentation. (1) The majority of these methods directly minimize feature distances in two domains, to enable the model trained with source images to obtain superior performance in the target domain. But WCE images inevitably include noise with inaccurate features due to complex imaging situations, which may deviate the segmentation performance. (2) These models lack comprehensive feature representations and explicit structure relationships between the source domain and the target domain. (3) Current domain adaptation approaches assume that samples from source and target domains are freely accessible during the training phase. However, this assumption is usually impractical in medical-related applications due to data privacy issues. To deal with these challenges, we propose comprehensive unsupervised domain adaptation models from source-available to source-free for automatic lesion segmentation. Firstly, we propose a hierarchical prototype based domain adaptation model with a self-training strategy to refine features, thus mitigating noise issues. Secondly, learnable graph structures are introduced to the hierarchical model exploiting intrinsic structural relationships among multi-scale features and prototypes of different domains. Moreover, we propose a source-free prototypical domain adaptation model capable of exploiting unlabeled WCE images and the pre-trained model with colonoscopy images, to deal with data privacy issues. Finally, we will evaluate and validate the proposed models with collected WCE images and videos, and implement a graphical user interface to display segmentation results. Our preliminary experiments have already demonstrated both the feasibility and the effectiveness of the proposed models. This project represents the first attempt to develop domain adaptation models for lesion segmentation with WCE images. It will produce high impacts on academic research of medical image analysis, and provide practical solutions to precision medicine in society and industry. 無線膠囊內窺鏡是一種檢測結直腸癌的有效技術。內窺鏡圖像中病變的自動分割為結直腸癌診斷和手術提供重要信息。基於深度學習的病變分割方法取得了顯著進展，但需要大量有標註的數據。解決該問題的方案是無監督域自適應算法，它將知識從源域的有標記的信息遷移到無標記的目標域。該項目旨在解決一個重要但技術上具有挑戰性的問題，即有效利用公共可用的結腸鏡圖像(源域)來指導無線膠囊內窺鏡圖像(目標域)的病變分割。 利用現有的域自適應模型進行病變分割存在如下挑戰。(1)這些方法大多直接最小化源域和目標域間的特徵距離，使得源圖像訓練的模型在目標域獲得好的性能。但由於複雜的成像環境，無線膠囊內窺鏡不可避免地包含了噪聲信息，影響分割性能。(2)現有模型缺乏全面的特徵表示源域與目標域之間的結構關係。(3)目前的域自適應算法假設在訓練階段可以自由獲取來自源域和目標域的樣本。然而，由於醫學數據隱私問題，這種假設在醫療相關應用中通常是不切實際的。 為了應對這些挑戰，我們提出了全面的無監督域自適應模型，用於自動病灶分割。首先，我們提出了一個具有自訓練策略的層次域自適應模型來細化特徵，從而緩解噪聲問題。其次，在層次模型中引入可學習圖結構，建模不同域的多尺度特徵和原型之間的內在結構關係。此外，我們提出了一個無源的域自適應模型，能夠利用未標記的無線膠囊內窺鏡圖像和預訓練的結腸鏡圖像模型實現病灶分割，以解決數據隱私問題。最後，我們將利用採集的無線膠囊內窺鏡圖像對所提出的模型進行評估和驗證。我們的初步實驗已經證明了該模型的可行性和有效性。本項目首次嘗試開發用於無線膠囊內窺鏡圖像病變分割的域自適應模型。它將對醫學圖像分析的學術研究產生重要影響，並為精准醫學提供實用的解決方案。

rows: To design a robust domain adaptation model for lesion segmentation with WCE images to deal with limited training data and noise effects. Deep neural networks have achieved remarkable success in lesion segmentation at the expense of laborious training data annotation. But large WCE medical datasets are not readily available due to proprietary and privacy concerns. One of the techniques to address this dilemma is unsupervised domain adaptation, which transfers knowledge from a labeled dataset (source domain) to another unlabeled one (target domain). However, existing domain adaptation models target natural images and ignore the negative effect of noise features in medical images, which may lead to biased segmentation performance. Therefore, we propose a hierarchical domain adaptation model to mitigate the influences of noise for lesion segmentation.

To investigate intrinsic structure relationships in the unsupervised domain adaptation models to support the accurate lesion segmentation. Existing unsupervised domain adaptation models utilize only features from the last layer of deep learning models to represent images, which may not accurately represent complex WCE images. Moreover, they don't consider the underlying geometric information from the input data, which is crucial for describing the relationships among samples from colonoscopy images and WCE ones. Thus, we will introduce a graph guided feature aggregated module and a graph guided prototype alignment module on top of the designed domain adaptation model for lesion segmentation. The graph guided feature aggregation module enables features from different layers to benefit each other by graph aggregation, while the graph guided prototype alignment module enhances the robust characterizations with category information for lesion segmentation.

To reduce the dependence on source data and develop a robust source-free prototypical unsupervised domain adaptation model for lesion segmentation. The majority of existing domain adaptation models need to access the source data during the training to adapt, which is not efficient for data transmission and may violate data privacy policies. Therefore, this proposal makes adequate use of the pre-trained source model together with unlabeled WCE images, and develops a novel source-free domain adaptation model for lesion segmentation. This proposal proposes a self-supervised pseudo label generator to enable training in the target domain and designs novel strategies and constraints to utilize the unlabeled WCE images.

To test and verify the proposed automatic lesion segmentation models based on real clinical datasets and construct an integrated segmentation visualization system for practical clinical applications. We will further extend the designed unsupervised domain adaptation models to supervised domain adaptation by involving labeled WCE image into the training stage to further improve the segmentation performance.

11211221.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11211221.value: Wireless capsule endoscopy (WCE) is an effective technique to detect colorectal lesions, which are precursors of colorectal cancer (CRC). Automatic lesion segmentation from WCE images is of great importance to provide valuable information for both CRC diagnosis and further surgery. Deep learning based approaches have achieved significant progress but at the expense of laborious large-scale data annotation. One possible solution to address this issue is unsupervised domain adaptation, which transfers knowledge from labeled datasets in a source domain to an unlabeled target domain. In this proposal, we have tackled the important but technically challenging problem of efficiently utilizing the public available colonoscopy images (source domain) to guide lesion segmentation with WCE images (target domain). We proposed several models from unsupervised domain adaptation to source-free domain adaptation. Recently, with the development of large language models and foundation models, we aim to develop the foundation model for endoscopy video data analysis. Moreover, as the text information can provide critical features for learning, we plan to integrate the online open medical books and articles into knowledge graph, and further guide the feature learning.
