11211421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11211421.value: Robotic microinjection has high accuracy at the single-cell level; thus, it could avoid immunogenicity, chemical toxicity, and high mortality. However, the process has the disadvantage of low throughput compared with other transfection methods. The throughput of most existing robotic microinjection systems ranges from several hundred to one thousand cells within a production cycle, far less than the number required for clinical use. Low throughput remains the bottleneck problem for successful implementation of robotic microinjection in practical applications. In this work, we will develop new high-throughput robotic microinjection technologies that will hit a record of injecting 4000 cells per hour, with a corresponding high success rate and survival rate for macrophages (e.g., > 80%). This high throughput could be achieved using a microinjection strategy of coordinated dual micromanipulator system (here denoted a dual module system) and deep learning-enhanced cell detection and segmentation. The flux of 4000 cells per hour is estimated on the basis of the time interval between two coordinated injections in the system, the time required for intelligent processing steps, and our previous research result on the single-module injection system (1500 cells per hour). Macrophages are important immune effector cells, and therefore they will be used as exemplary cells for our cell transfection studies by microinjection. We will conduct this research in three aspects. First, we will develop dual-module robotic microinjection system that uses two coordinated micromanipulators on the same cell processing platform to inject cells on the basis of injection sequence optimization to increase productivity. The two micromanipulators insert cells synergistically in an optimal injection path leading to substantially increased throughput. Second, we will develop an attentive single shot multi-box detector to detect cells and a U-Net framework to segment cells, which could considerably improve the operation efficiency and subsequently increase the throughput. The use of deep learning algorithms for cell detection and segmentation will avoid not only the monotonous preparation for cell staining but also the issues associated with dye toxicity and potential interference with injection samples. Third, we will apply the developed robotic microinjection system to inject gene-editing plasmids into macrophages and construct immune-enhanced cell lines with tumor-killing ability. We will study in-vitro and in-vivo tumor models to verify the antitumor effects of LR4-overexpressed macrophages. The successful realization of high-throughput injection will make robotic microinjection a competitive tool in many biomedical applications, such as plasmid DNA transfection, and promote the precise cell therapy in Hong Kong. 在這項工作中，我們將開發新的高通量機器人顯微注射技術，該技術將創下每小時注射將近4000 個細胞的記錄，並具有相應的高成功率和巨噬細胞存活率。這種高通量將通過使用雙模組系統和深度學習強化細胞檢測和分割的注射策略來實現。我們將從三個方面進行這項研究。首先，我們將開發雙模組機器人顯微注射系統，在同一細胞處理平臺上使用兩個協調的顯微操作器並優化注射序列，以提高生產率。兩個顯微操作器在最佳注射路徑中協同插入細胞，從而顯著提高輸送量。其次，我們將開發一個單發多盒檢測器來檢測儲存格和一個 U-Net 框架來分割儲存格，這可以顯著提高操作效率並隨後增加輸送量。使用深度學習演算法進行細胞檢測和分割不僅可以避免繁瑣而單調的細胞染色準備工作，還可以避免染料毒性相關問題以及對注射樣品的潛在干擾。第三，我們將應用開發的機器人顯微注射系統將基因編輯質粒注入細胞，構建具有腫瘤殺傷能力的免疫增強細胞系。

11211521.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11211521.value: Multi-objective bilevel optimization problem involves two hierarchically nested multi-objective optimization tasks (known as the upper- and lower-level problems) considering the trade-off among several conflicting criteria. It is widely existed in many real-world applications across multiple disciplines from public to private sectors. For example, in a multiuser cooperative mobile edge computing offloading system running under a multiuser interference environment, in which delay-sensitive tasks may be executed on local devices, cooperative devices, or the primary mobile edge computing server, the joint optimization of the offloading decision and computation resource allocation for minimizing the total energy consumption of all mobile users under the delay constraint and maximizing the quality of service essentially has a bilevel structure, where the offloading decision generated in the upper-level is coupled with the optimal allocation of computational resources in the lower-level. Although there have been some research efforts on bilevel optimization, there is a gap between existing methodologies in academia and their further uptake in industry mainly because of its poor scalability: (i) Existing works generally consider small-scale problems, e.g., with up to 10 decision variables and less than 3 objective functions, which are way below the requirement of real-world black-box systems; (ii) Due to the nested structure of two levels of coupling optimization processes, bilevel optimization is known to be strongly NP-hard and highly computationally expensive thus hardly scalable and applicable to large-scale scenarios; (iii) Due to the lack of well-established solution procedures (even for single-objective bilevel optimization), most efforts have been dedicated to simplifying a bilevel optimization problem into a single-level format which incurs inevitable errors and further aggravates the solvability. The aim of this project is to develop a data-driven computational framework for bilevel multi-objective optimization focusing on its scalability to a large number of decision variables and objective functions. It consists of five major tasks: (i) Develop foundations for bilevel multi-objective optimization including extensible benchmark problems mimicking real-world challenges and a performance evaluation platform; (ii) Build surrogate models from a Bayesian perspective to alleviate the high computational cost incurred by the two nested optimization processes; (iii) Develop effecitve transfer optimization techniques to improve the computational efficiency through knowledge transfer; (iv) Develop a multi-space optimization paradigm and GPU-based multi-space algorithms to improve the computational scalability of bilevel multi-objective optimization; (v) Validate the effectiveness of the developed technologies via two real-world complex optimization problems in the domains of software engineering and logistics. 多目标双层优化问题包含两层嵌套的多目标优化任务。其中每层优化任务都需要考虑多个相互冲突的目标函数间的权衡关系。该类问题广泛存在于许多不同领域的实际应用场景。例如，在多用户协作的移动边缘计算中系统卸载环境存在多用户干涉影响。其中对延迟需求高的任务通常于局部设备中运行，而关于卸载决策与计算资源分配的联合优化问题通常具有一个双层优化结构。其中卸载决策是上层优化问题的产物；而对于每一个决策，相应的最优资源分配则由下层优化获得。另外，系统需要同时考虑最小化所有移动端用户能量损耗，并最大化服务质量且应满足延迟约束。 尽管目前在双层优化方面已经引起了研究者广泛兴趣，然而现有计算方法受限于可扩展性差的缺陷无法广泛应用于实际工业场景。主要存在三方面问题：i) 现有方法通常只考虑小规模问题（例如最多考虑10个变量和3个目标函数），远不符合实际黑盒系统情况；ii) 鉴于双层优化问题嵌套结构，它们通常是NP难问题而且计算代价巨大，因此无法满足大规模场景需求；iii) 由于缺少有效求解方法，大部分工作仍试图将双层优化问题简化为单层优化问题，这样无疑带来逼近误差甚至会导致问题无法求解。 本项目主要目的是研究一种数据驱动的计算框架用于求解大规模多目标双层优化问题。它主要包含五个主要任务：i) 研究多目标双层优化问题基础理论，其中包括设计一系列可扩展的测试问题用于模拟实际工程问题中各种挑战，以及一个性能评价平台；ii) 设计基于贝叶斯定理的代理模型用于缓解双层嵌套优化过程高昂计算代价；iii) 设计有效的迁移优化技术用于提高计算效率；iv) 设计多空间优化框架及其GPU实现，用于提高多目标双层优化可扩展性；v) 在软件工程以及物流实际复杂场景下验证方法有效性。

11211521.label: Realisation of objectives
11211521.value: Overall, the project has systematically investigated scalable multi-objective bilevel optimization by developing foundational bilevel search paradigms, scalable multiobjective learning techniques, transfer optimization methodologies, multitask evolutionary frameworks, and representative complex optimization applications. The completed work addresses key challenges inherent to bilevel optimization, including complex leader-follower interactions, scalability to high-dimensional decision spaces, efficient reuse of knowledge across related tasks, and practical applicability under limited computational budgets. These contributions collectively establish a solid and well-supported basis for further research on scalable, data-efficient bilevel multi-objective optimization. For Objective 1, the project has delivered extensive foundational results related to bilevel and multiobjective optimization, supported by multiple complementary studies. A multi-form evolutionary search paradigm was proposed to explicitly address bilevel multi-objective optimization by coordinating different evolutionary search components within a unified framework, enabling more effective handling of complex upper–lower interactions and search dependencies. This work provides one of the core algorithmic contributions of the project and demonstrates clear performance advantages on standard bilevel multiobjective benchmark problems. In parallel, a local model-based Pareto front estimation method was developed for general multiobjective optimization, showing that constructing local surrogate models around promising search regions can significantly improve the accuracy and convergence of Pareto front approximation on complex landscapes. This modelling approach is directly relevant to bilevel optimization, where response landscapes are often expensive and irregular. In addition, the project established a suite of multiobjective sequential transfer optimization benchmark problems, together with standardized experimental protocols and baseline results. These benchmarks enable systematic evaluation of transfer behaviors across sequences of related multiobjective tasks and provide essential experimental infrastructure for studying transfer-aware bilevel optimization. Finally, a comprehensive survey on learnable evolutionary algorithms for scalable multiobjective optimization was conducted, synthesizing existing methodologies, learning mechanisms, and scalability strategies. This survey clarifies the current state-of-the-art, identifies key limitations, and provides a theoretical and methodological reference that informs the design of scalable bilevel optimization algorithms in the project. For Objective 2, the project addressed scalability challenges arising in large-scale multiobjective optimization through learnable and data-driven techniques. An autoencoder-based problem transformation framework was proposed, in which high-dimensional decision variables are encoded into a low-dimensional latent space learned directly from data. Evolutionary search conducted in this latent space was shown to substantially reduce optimization difficulty while preserving solution quality, leading to improved performance on large-scale multiobjective benchmark problems. This work provides a concrete and effective strategy for handling high-dimensional decision spaces, which are common in practical bilevel optimization settings. In addition, a supervised local learning framework with augmented auxiliary networks was investigated, providing a scalable mechanism for improving local learning rules in deep models. Although this study was not formulated as a bilevel optimization method, it contributes directly to the project by supplying scalable learning techniques that can be integrated into learnable evolutionary algorithms, particularly where full global training is computationally prohibitive. For Objective 3, the project delivered an extensive and well-supported body of work on evolutionary multiform transfer optimization. A comprehensive review was first conducted to systematically organize existing transfer optimization methods according to transferable knowledge forms, transfer scenarios, and task relationships, offering a clear conceptual framework and identifying key sources of negative transfer. Building upon this foundation, an ensemble of domain adaptation-based knowledge transfer methods was developed for evolutionary multitasking, where multiple adaptation models are combined to better capture diverse cross-task relationships and improve robustness in heterogeneous environments. To further enhance transfer reliability, a lower confidence bound-based solution selection strategy was proposed, enabling uncertainty-aware decisions on when and how solutions should be transferred across tasks. In addition, a large-scale empirical study on sequential solution transfer investigated the effectiveness of solution-level transfer across different problem settings, providing practical insights into task similarity requirements, transfer timing, and filtering strategies. These complementary contributions jointly establish a comprehensive realization of transfer optimization in both multitask and sequential contexts. For Objective 4, the project focused on scalable evolutionary optimization frameworks through multitasking and learning-aided mechanisms. A distributed knowledge transfer framework was proposed for evolutionary multitask multimodal optimization, allowing task-specific subpopulations to exchange information selectively while preserving multimodality and population diversity. This framework was shown to improve search efficiency and solution coverage across complex multimodal multitask problems. To address large-scale combinatorial settings, a centralized learning-based evolutionary multitasking framework was further developed, where shared learning components are trained across tasks to guide evolutionary search more efficiently than isolated single-task approaches, which addresses the core scalability challenge and can be directly adopted within bilevel or multi-task search processes. In addition, learning-aided evolutionary search and selection strategies were investigated for scaling constrained multiobjective optimization, incorporating learned models to assist feasibility assessment and selection under limited evaluation budgets. Together, these studies provide scalable algorithmic infrastructures that support large-scale, multimodal, and constrained optimization scenarios relevant to bilevel settings. For Objective 5, the project demonstrated the practical applicability of its methods through representative complex optimization problems. In logistics optimization, a fast vehicle routing approach based on knowledge transfer in a reproducing kernel Hilbert space was developed, enabling effective reuse of solution knowledge across related routing instances and effectively improving the convergence behaviour on both benchmark and real delivery datasets. In the context of neural architecture search, an evolutionary multitask convolutional neural architecture search framework was proposed, enabling multiple computer vision tasks to share architectural knowledge while dynamically controlling negative transfer. Experimental results showed that the multitask approach can achieve competitive or superior performance while substantially reducing the overall search cost. These applications confirm that the project’s methodological contributions are effective beyond synthetic benchmarks and transferable to practical, high-impact domains.

It consists of defining knowledge via landscape analysis; efficient transfer optimization techniques to implement knowledge transfer at both genetic- and model-level; and similarity measures that inform the adaptive transferability of task knowledge.
To develop algorithms and infrastructure to support scalability to high-dimensional problems. It consists of largescale optimization via multi-space search and its GPU implementation.
To apply the scalable bi-level multi-objective optimization approaches developed in this project to two real-world complex applications in software engineering and logistics.

11211521.label: Major findings and research outcome
11211521.value: The project has produced a series of significant research outcomes that advance the understanding and methodology of scalable multi-objective bilevel optimization and related evolutionary optimization paradigms. A major finding of the project is that explicitly structured evolutionary search frameworks are critical for effectively handling complex optimization problems involving hierarchical decision dependencies, high-dimensional search spaces, and heterogeneous task relationships. One key outcome is the demonstration that multi-form evolutionary search mechanisms can significantly improve performance on bilevel multi-objective problems. By coordinating different search processes within a unified paradigm, the project showed that evolutionary algorithms can more effectively cope with leader–follower interactions and complex bilevel landscapes than conventional single-form approaches. This insight clarifies the importance of search structure design in bilevel optimization and provides practical guidance for future algorithm development. Another major finding is that learnable and data-driven mechanisms can substantially enhance the scalability, even without explicitly modeling bilevel structures. The project demonstrated that autoencoder-based problem transformation can reduce the effective dimensionality of large-scale multiobjective problems, leading to improved convergence behavior and computational efficiency. Complementary studies on supervised local learning further showed that scalable local learning rules can provide effective model updates under constrained computational budgets, supporting the integration of learning components into evolutionary optimization frameworks. The project also delivered important outcomes in transfer optimization, showing that the effectiveness of knowledge reuse depends strongly on how transferable knowledge is represented, selected, and filtered. The project established that multiform and ensemble-based transfer mechanisms can improve robustness across heterogeneous tasks, while uncertainty-aware strategies such as lower confidence bound–based selection are effective in reducing negative transfer. The empirical analysis of sequential solution transfer provided evidence-based guidelines for identifying when transfer is beneficial, emphasizing the importance of task similarity and transfer timing. In terms of algorithmic scalability, the project confirmed that evolutionary multitasking combined with learning-aided mechanisms offers a viable path for tackling complex multiobjective problems. Distributed knowledge transfer frameworks were shown to preserve diversity and improve exploration in multimodal settings, while centralized learning approaches reduced redundancy and improved efficiency in large-scale complex optimization. Learning-aided search and selection mechanisms further enhanced scalability under strict constraints. Finally, through complex applications in vehicle routing and neural architecture search, the project demonstrated theoretical soundness and practical effectiveness. The empirical results showed clear reductions in computational cost and improvements in solution efficiency, confirming that evolutionary transfer and multitask optimization techniques can deliver tangible benefits in realistic problem settings.

11211521.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11211521.value: The results of this project provide a solid basis for several directions of further development. First, the multi-form evolutionary search paradigm and associated studies on bilevel multi-objective optimization can be extended to more challenging scenarios, such as higher-dimensional bilevel problems and settings with more complex interactions between decision levels. Further analysis of convergence behavior and robustness under uncertainty would strengthen the theoretical understanding of such methods. Second, the learnable and data-driven techniques developed for large-scale multiobjective optimization offer clear opportunities for improvement. The autoencoder-based problem transformation framework may be enhanced through more expressive representation learning models, while supervised local learning mechanisms could be more tightly integrated into evolutionary algorithms to improve scalability under limited computational budgets. Third, the extensive work on evolutionary multiform transfer optimization suggests further exploration of adaptive transfer control and transferability assessment. Building on ensemble and uncertainty-aware strategies, future research could refine task similarity measures and transfer scheduling to improve reliability across diverse optimization scenarios. Finally, the multitask and learning-aided frameworks, together with validated applications in vehicle routing and neural architecture search, indicate strong potential for extension to other real-world optimization domains, such as scheduling and resource allocation, where efficiency and generalization are critical.

11211521.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11211521.value: This project studies advanced methods for solving complex optimization problems that involve multiple competing objectives and, in some cases, hierarchical decision structures. Such problems frequently arise in real-world applications where decisions must be made efficiently under limited computational resources, large decision spaces, and changing problem conditions. The project developed new evolutionary optimization frameworks and learning-based techniques to address these challenges. It proposed structured evolutionary search methods for complex optimization settings, scalable techniques for handling high-dimensional problems, and mechanisms that allow knowledge gained from previous tasks to be reused in new but related problems. These approaches were carefully evaluated through theoretical analysis, benchmark studies, and extensive experimental validation. An important outcome of the project is a deeper understanding of how learning and knowledge transfer can improve optimization efficiency without sacrificing solution quality. The project also demonstrated that multitask and transfer-based evolutionary optimization can significantly reduce computational cost when solving sequences or sets of related problems. The practical relevance of the research was validated through complex applications, including vehicle routing and neural architecture search, where the proposed methods achieved faster convergence and improved efficiency compared with conventional approaches. Overall, the project contributes reliable and well-validated techniques that support more efficient decision-making in complex optimization problems, providing a solid foundation for future research and practical deployment.

11211721.value: 為了滿足大數據流量的持續增長，未來以毫米波頻率運行的地面無線通訊、傳感、雷達和衛星通信系統需要電子波束可控的高增益天線。反射面天線和陣列天線增益高，但波束只能通過機械方式来掃描。雖然相控陣天線是電子控制的，但需要昂貴的數字控制移相器。這大大增加了天線的複雜性、成本和物理尺寸。 反射陣列是一種很有前途的高增益天線替代方案。波束掃描可以通過適當的相位補償方案實現，同時保持簡單的空間饋源，而無需複雜的饋源網絡。通過在陣列元件中加入低成本PIN二極管開關，可以改變其反射相位。一個或幾個開關可以實現分辯率為一比特或幾比特的離散相位控制。透射陣列天線由相位調整單元單元陣列組成，用於補償饋源和接收天線元件之間的空間相位延遲差，以產生聚焦波束。由於具有平面結構、無饋電阻塞效應和低製造成本的優點，透射陣列適用於毫米波應用。設計方法類似於反射陣列，使用二極體調整單元的相位。 在大多數反射陣列和透射陣列中，微帶天線被用作固有帶寬狹窄的基本元件。使用較厚的基底或疊層貼片可以提高頻寬，但由於表面波的强烈激勵，天線效率會降低。陣列結構的複雜性也增加了。 磁電偶極子天線是一種很有前途的寬帶天線技術，用於微波和毫米波頻率的無線通訊、傳感和雷達應用。近年來，人們研製了一種以基本磁電偶極子為輻射元件的固定輻射波束的反射陣列和透射陣列。寬帶和高效率已經被證明。這一成就為開發使用新型可重構磁電偶極子的寬帶電子束控反射陣列和透射陣列提供了動力。該項目的成功將有助於提高未來工作在毫米波頻率的商用無線通訊和傳感系統的效能，因為這項新技術對於許多商業應用來說非常經濟且價格負擔得起的。

11211721.label: Realisation of objectives
11211721.value: With the support of two outstanding and hardworking Ph.D. students, the three objectives have been achieved with encourage results. In fact, we have done more as planned, further confirming that the ME dipole can provide better performance in reconfigurable two-dimensional reflectarrays and transmitarrays designs for microwave and millimeter wave applications. Not only the bandwidth is wider compared to those designs based on dipole, slot or microstrip patch antennas, the scanning angles can also be substantially wider, which is an attractive feature of beam steerable high gain antennas. For objective 1, we have successfully developed reconfigurable 1-bit and 2-bit circularly polarized reflectarrays based on newly designed ME dipoles. The study gave us the inspiration to develop a 1-bit linearly polarized reconfigurable reflectarray with attractive performance. For objective 2, we have developed several high-performance reconfigurable linearly polarized transmitarrays. Both 1-bit and 2-bit deisgns are achieved. In addition, one design can be used with dual-polarization with high isolation, which is highly attractive for mobile communications. Techniques for suppressing the side lobe levels and increasing the aperture efficiency has been invented. For objective 3, we originally planned to adopt an antenna array to feed a reconfigurable transmitarray of ME dipoles to achieve wideband low-profile high gain performance. Subsequently, we found that the folded transmitarray structure is a better approach as the feed network loss can be avoided. We have successfully developed a number of high-performance folded transmitarrays with novel ME dipole elements.

11211721.label: Major findings and research outcome
11211721.value: For enhancing the aperture efficiency of reconfigurable circularly polarized reflectarrays, we have proposed a modified ME dipole element with 2-bit reconfigurable capability. Excellent performance with 43% AR<3 bandwidth, 21 dBi gain, 44.6% aperture efficiency and 38% gain bandwidth is achieved for a 12 by 12 array design. In parallel, we have been able to design a linearly-polarized ME dipole element for reflectarrays with 1-bit resolution. The element is simple in structure as only one p-i-n diode is needed to change the reflecting phase. A design operating at 12 GHz with 16 by 16 elements and exhibiting 38% in gain bandwidth and 24% in aperture efficiency was developed. The attractive feature is its wide scanning angles ranging from -60 degree to +60 degree in the E-plane and from 0 degree to +60 degree in the H-plane within the entire operating frequencies [1]. In general, the transmitarray has better performance than the reflectarray as blockage of radiation from the feed can be avoided. To improve the performance of the previous 1-bit design, a 2-bit fixed-beam transmitarray with 12 by 12 ME dipoles for millimeter-wave vehicular communications has been designed with over 40% aperture efficiency over 34% impedance bandwidth [3]. A reconfigurable version of 2-bit transmitarray antenna with cross-polarization suppression was developed with a +/- 50 degree scanning range [6]. Substantial amount of results has been achieved in the development of folded transmitarrays using ME dipoles. This approach is good for realizing low profile wideband beam steerable high gain antennas effectively. A 1-bit reconfigurable transmitarray antenna with linear polarization based on a novel element consisting of two centrally fed ME dipole was developed. Each element has two p-i-n diodes for changing the state of the phase. Through multiple reflection between the feed source plane and the reflectarray, the height-to-diameter ratio can be reduced to one-third of the thickness of the conventional transmitarray. A prototype consisting of 12 by 12 elements was designed with +/- 40 degree scanning range in both E and H planes, 32% impedance bandwidth, 19 dBi gain, and 20% aperture efficiency [2]. As a by-product of this research, a low profile, wide bandwidth, high aperture efficiency folded transmitarray with broadside radiation using a true-time-delay structure [4]. A fixed-beam low-profile ME dipole transmitarray with dual-polarized feeds was also developed [5]. A review article on the development of ME dipole transmitarrays and reflectarrays contributed by my team was accepted for publication [8].

11211721.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11211721.value: Over the past three years, we have demonstrated that the ME dipole element is highly useful to improve the performance of the conventional reconfigurable reflectarray and transmitarray antenna designs. The bandwidth and scanning angles can be increased. The required active elements can be reduced to achieve low-cost fabrication. A number of prototypes were built to confirm the attractive features when operating at microwave and millimeter wave frequencies. The investigation can be extended for applications in the terahertz frequencies for future wireless systems if appropriate low-cost switching elements can be developed.

11211721.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11211721.value: To meet the exponential growth of data traffic in the AI era, electronically beam-steerable high-gain antennas are needed for future terrestrial wireless communication, sensing, radar and satellite communication systems operating at millimeter-wave frequencies. Reflector antennas and array antennas are high in gain but the directive beam can only be scanned mechanically. Although phased array antennas are electronically steerable, expensive digitally controlled phase shifters are required. This increases substantially the complexity, costs, and the physical dimensions of the antenna. The reflectarray and transmitarray are a promising alternative of high gain antennas. Beam scanning can be achieved by an appropriate phase compensation scheme while maintaining the simple spatial feed without the need of a complex feed network. By incorporating low-cost PIN diode switches in an array element, its reflection phase can be changed. The magneto-electric dipole antenna is a promising wideband antenna technology for wireless communications, sensing and radar applications at microwave and millimeter-wave frequencies. In this project, we have developed a number of reconfigurable reflectarrays and transmitarrays, employing novel magnetoelectric dipoles as radiating elements. Wide bandwidth, large scanning angles and high efficiency have been demonstrated. The designs will be useful to enhance the performance of future commercial wireless communication and sensing systems operating at millimeter-wave frequencies, as this new technology will be very economical and affordable for many commercial applications.

11212021.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11212021.value: Energy harvesting is a nascent micro-energy technology developed to capture wasted ambient mechanical energy and convert it into electricity. Along with the development of the Internet of Things and wearable devices, piezoelectric energy harvesters (PEHs) have attracted much attention as promising long-lifespan power alternatives to batteries. However, most PEHs cannot generate adequate power for their potential applications. By closely analyzing the relevant literature on design and vibration theory, we find that PEH designs are largely limited to straight-beam structures, such as cantilevers, fixed-fixed beams, and buckling beams, and existing theories can only analyze straight-beam PEHs. However, not all applications can provide sufficient space for straight-beam harvesters, such as smartwatches and fitness trackers. The large size, poor environmental adaptability, and low output power hinder the practicability of piezoelectric energy harvesters. To improve energy harvester performance, this project proposes to establish a widely applicable comprehensive theoretical framework for curved PEHs. The framework will help to extend the design scope of energy harvesters from 2D straight beams with flat piezoelectric elements to a broader domain of 3D curved structures. Curved PEHs will yield more alternatives to address the space limitation of diverse applications, and further possess such characteristics as high bending stress, large deformation, and low resonance frequency, which are beneficial for the performance enhancement. For demonstration, we will develop high-performance curved PEHs and integrated them into self-powered smartwatches. To develop the theoretical framework, the following critical engineering challenges and scientific issues must be addressed: 1) mathematically describing the deeply curved piezoelectric composites with variable curvatures and the electromechanical coupling effect, which is much more complex than the existing theories for straight-beam PEHs; 2) modeling segmented curved piezoelectric composite harvesters and developing solution methods; 3) gaining insights into the stress concentration effect of curved structures and its enhancing effect on PEHs; 4) exploring the intricate nonlinearity of piezoceramics under high mechanical stress; and 5) developing effective fabrication and experimental procedures for curved piezoceramics and PEHs. Details of our methodologies to address these issues are presented in the proposal. The proposed research adds a new design dimension to PEHs and lays the foundation for developing new harvesters with curved piezoelectric composite laminates. The established theoretical and experimental framework will greatly advance the research fields of energy harvesting, composite structures, vibration, and sensors. Further, this work will promote the development of self-powered wearable devices, the Internet of Things, and other wireless devices. 能量俘獲是一個新興的微能源技術，用來俘獲環境中廢棄的能量並轉化為電能。隨著物聯網和可穿戴技術的蓬勃發展，壓電俘能器作為電池替代技術獲得了大量關註。然而，當前大部分壓電能量采集器不能夠產生足夠的電量。究其原因，我們發現當前能量采集器的設計局限於直梁結構。然而很多應用如智能手表沒有空間安裝這類直梁能量采集器。體積大、環境適應性差、產電量低等因素極大的限製了壓電能量采集器的應用。本項目力圖解決這些實際問題，引進3D 曲面結構到壓電采集器中，建立系統的理論框架。3D曲面梁結構將能夠很好 的適應不同應用的安裝需求，同時提高應變程度、提高壓電輸出。為了開發這一重要的理論框架，我們必須解決以下這些工程挑戰。1如何數學上描述深度彎曲壓電符合梁結構並同時考慮變化曲率和壓電耦合效應；2如何建模分析分段變曲率復合梁結構；3如何獲得應力集中效應在曲面壓電符合梁中的壓電輸出規律；4如何利用壓電固有非線性提高能量產出；5如何高效加工和實驗測試3D曲面符合梁能量采集器。詳細的研究方法請查看 申請書。本項目擬定建立的理論和實驗框架將極大的促進壓電能量采集的發展，同時有助於物聯網、可穿戴設備及其它無線傳感器設備的進步。

11212021.label: Realisation of objectives
11212021.value: The 4 objectives as per the original application have been realized completely. I will explain our achievements from both the theoretical and experimental aspects. Theoretical contributions: A: We developed a theoretical model for studying curved PEHs with variable curvature. Based on Euler-Bernoulli beam theory, the distributed-parameter electromechanical coupling equations are obtained and solved by the Rayleigh-Ritz method. To demonstrate the formulations, the ellipse is chosen as the profile of the PEHs. The convergent study showed that the theoretical solutions are in good agreement with the FE simulation. The theoretical results are also validated by experiments; the relative errors between them are within 10%. Furthermore, parametric studies show the following: 1. A larger proof mass increases the voltage output of the system due to the inertia effect. 2. The voltage output reaches the maximum of about 12.5 V when the mass is located at theta = -0.47 and 0.63; the local minimum is reached at theta = 0. 3. The open-circuit voltage output reaches the maximum of 13.94 V when Young’s modulus of the substrate is 163 MPa. 4. In the given case, the voltage output of 7.23 V occurs at = 0.68 5. Compared to other parameters, the change of curvature is less significant. 6. The design with a circular profile is not optimal. The analytical solution can be applied to various curved curvature-variable unimorphs such as parabolas, catenaries, and cycloids, and can be readily extended to variable-curvature bimorphs. This work can be beneficial in developing and broadening new PEHs and can help in the design and optimization of the structures. B. We presented an analytical study for the dynamic response of a performance-enhanced arc-shaped PEH with discontinuously varying curvature. An analytical model based on the Timoshenko beam theory has been built. The analytical formulation presented is applicable for both thin and moderately thick laminated arc-shaped beams; the analysis can be readily extended for other composite curved beam systems with variable curvatures. In addition to the system resonant frequencies and eigenmodes, the mechanical and electrical responses are accurately determined by solving the coupling equations. An FE analysis is conducted and good agreement with the analytical model’s prediction is presented. A curved harvester prototype is also fabricated, and the analytical model is experimentally validated. By applying the developed model, moreover, a parametric study is conducted and the effects of the length of the straight beam, thickness ratio, and Young’s modulus on the electrical responses of PEHs are articulated. The results show that the optimal arc-shaped harvester can achieve a maximum output voltage of 50 V under an acceleration of 0.3 g. This analytical work provides a useful guideline for modeling PEHs with segmented variable-curvature laminated beams. It may play an important role in the optimization of energy harvesting behaviors of laminated arc piezoelectric beams and may help design new PEHs. Experimental contributions: Woodpecker-mimic Two-layer Band PEH with a Piezoelectric Array for Powering Wrist-worn Wearables Wrist-worn smart devices such as smartwatches and wristbands are rapidly penetrating our daily life for health, security and fashion purposes. However, the battery-powered wearables have a limited lifetime and need to be frequently recharged, which degrades user experience and further poses environmental problems. Inspired by the structure of the woodpecker’s head, supported by this GRF grant, we developed a bionic two-layer band piezoelectric energy harvester for self-powered smartwatches and wristbands. An inner band and an outer band of the harvester mimic two branches of the hyoid bone of the woodpecker. The energy harvesting unit employs a piezoelectric array structure. A finite element analysis is conducted to identify the optimal positions of piezoelectric patches in the array and an improved rectifier circuit is developed to manage the multiple AC inputs. We design two operation modes, i.e., movement mode and impact mode, to accommodate energy harvesters in different human activities. A maximum power output of 15.41 mW is achieved in experiments when tapping the prototype, corresponding to an equivalent power density of 1049.01 μW/cm3, around five times higher than previous wrist-worn harvesters. The design demonstrates its capability of continuously powering a watch and a screen during a normal walking process. The concept of shifting from the watch body to watch bands provides the design of energy harvesters a larger space and higher user-friendliness, which, fused with the piezoelectric array method, shows the potential to merge the gap of the power generation of energy harvesters and the power consumption of wrist wearables.

11212021.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11212021.value: Along with the development of the Internet of Things and wearable devices, piezoelectric energy harvesters (PEHs) have attracted much attention as promising long-lifespan power alternatives to batteries. However, most PEHs cannot generate adequate power for their potential applications. To greatly improve PEHs' power output, we proposed to shift from commonly used flat beam structures to curved beams. In this project, we built a comprehensive theoretical and experimental framework for supporting the development of curved-beam PEHs. The developed distributed-parameter model can accurately estimate the dynamic mechanical and electrical responses of energy harvesters. Furthermore, inspired by woodpeckers, we invented a double-layer curved PEHs that outputs 15.4 mW power and five times higher power density than the state of the art.

11212121.label: Project Objectives
11212121.value: Investigate the working mechanism of a newly developed wide impedance- and gain-bandwidth on-chip antenna (OCA) operating at 0.3THz with chip-integrated dielectric resonator (CIDR). This OCA consists of a planar feeder antenna, a rectangular DR devised from the high-dielectric-constant silicon substrate of the 65-nm CMOS technology. The bottom of the DR is backed by a conductor, which together with its four equivalent magnetic walls forms a cavity. The interplay of the feeder antenna, high-order DR modes and cavity modes needs to be thoroughly understood. Further enhance OCA performance by investigating different feeder antenna geometries, optimizing the DR dimensions and forming cavities with different combinations of electric and magnetic walls as well as enlarging the cavity through chip packaging. Extend the operating frequency of the OCA to 1THz. Initial simulation results suggest that achieving wide impedance- and gain-bandwidth is entirely feasible. Based on the element design, 2×2 OCA arrays are proposed for gain enhancement with emphasis on the feeding network having manageable insertion loss. Exploit the increased electrical dimensions of the chip size at 1THz to design inset dielectric waveguide (IDW) leaky-wave antennas (LWA) for frequency beam scanning either in the elevation or azimuth direction with applications in chip-to-chip and machine-to-machine communications.

11212121.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11212121.value: While the first deployments of 5G were only made in April 2019, several countries, including China and Finland already spearheaded their research on 6G with frequencies in the terahertz (THz) realm, initially at 0.252 to 0.325 THz. 6G will have the speed equality of fiber at terabit-per-second, microsecond latency and almost unlimited bandwidth for the connectivity of numerous mobile and Internet-of-Things devices in the vicinity. The first 6G Wireless Summit was already held in Finland in March 2019. The deployment of 6G is expected in 2030 to satisfy the unfulfilled demands not met with by 5G. As China is leading in 5G technologies, it is envisaged that other countries would step up their efforts in 6G, a more level playing field. In fact, an eight-year, €250 million 6G Flagship program has been established at the University of Oulu with support from the Finnish government and industrial partners including Nokia. A 6G wireless link requires THz antennas. In this project, we embark on designing THz on-chip antennas (OCAs) and arrays using TSMC 65-nm CMOS technology. OCA eliminates the parasitic effects and uncertainty introduced by interconnections with the chip leading to enhanced performance, smaller overall system size and lower cost. Conventional OCAs are impeded with high losses, unstable patterns and low gain. Their bandwidth is also limited as the separation between the bottom (M1) and top (M10) metal layer is less than 9µm, which is only 0.0096 free-space wavelength (λo) at 0.325 THz. In contrast, this thickness translates to 0.032λo at 1 THz which allows for the realization of antenna arrays or frequency-scanning antennas with affordable chip size. In this project, we propose wide impedance- and gain-bandwidth OCAs with chip-integrated dielectric resonators (CIDRs). CIDRs exploit the inherent high-dielectric-constant silicon substrate in CMOS technology, a prevailing challenge in OCA designs, as a rectangular DR excited by a planar antenna. Our preliminary design reveals a -10dB simulated impedance bandwidth of 50%, 3dB gain bandwidth of 34.5% and peak gain of 6.5 dBi at 0.305 THz. We propose to conduct in-depth investigation on its radiation mechanism and extend the operating frequency to 1 THz for CIDR arrays. The increased electrical thickness at 1 THz also allows us to realize antennas with other functionalities such as frequency scanning. Through this project, we aim at contributing to providing enabling technologies for the Greater Bay Area including Hong Kong to develop critical components for the future 6G communications. 5G 的首次部署剛在2019 年 4 月進行，包括中國和芬蘭在內的幾個國家就已經率先開展了對太赫茲 (THz) 頻段的 6G 研究。其最初的太赫茲研究頻率為 0.252 至 0.325 THz。 6G 將具有每秒 Tbit 的光纖速度、微秒延遲、幾乎無限的頻寬，其用於連接附近的眾多移動和物聯網設備。 首屆6G無線峰會已於2019年3月在芬蘭舉行。預計2030年6G的部署將滿足5G無法達到的需求。 由於中國在 5G 技術方面處於領先地位，預計其他國家將在 6G這一更加平等的競爭平台加大投資。 事實上，在芬蘭政府和包括諾基亞在內的工業合作夥伴的支援下，奧盧大學已經建立了一項為期八年、耗資 2.5 億歐元的 6G 旗艦計畫。 6G無線鏈路離不開太赫茲天線。在這個項目中，我們將使用65nm CMOS技術設計太赫茲片上天線（OCA）和陣列。OCA消除了晶片互連帶來的寄生效應和不確定性，從而提高了性能，減小了總體系統尺寸，降低了成本。傳統的OCA存在高損耗、不穩定模式和低增益等缺點。由於底部（M1）和頂部（M10）金屬層之間的間距小，在0.325THz對應0.0096自由空間波長（λo），因此傳統的OCA的頻寬受到限制。相比之下，該厚度在1THz時為0.032λo，具有可實現天線陣列或頻率掃描天線的晶片尺寸。在這個項目中，我們提出了寬阻抗和增益頻寬的OCA晶片集成介質諧振器（CIDR）。CIDR 利用 CMOS 技術中固有的高介電常數矽襯底作為由平面天線激發的矩形諧振器。 我們的初步設計揭示了該CIDR具有50% 的-10dB阻抗頻寬、34.5% 的 3dB 增益頻寬和 0.305 THz 時 6.5 dBi 的峰值增益。 我們將對其輻射機制進行深入研究，並將 CIDR 陣列的工作頻率擴展到 1 THz。1 THz 時增加的電尺寸厚度也使我們能夠實現具有其他功能的天線（如頻率掃描天線）。 通過這個項目，我們旨在為包括香港在內的大灣區提供支撐技術，為未來的 6G 通信開發關鍵性器件。

11212121.label: Realisation of objectives
11212121.value: We have investigated the working mechanism of the proposed wide impedance- and gain bandwidth on-chip antenna (OCA) operating at 0.3 THz with a chip-integrated dielectric resonator antenna (CIDR). After getting the initial results for the proposal, we continued to work on understanding the operating modes of the OCA with CIDR. The study helped us revise our paper entitled “Wide impedance-bandwidth and gain-bandwidth terahertz on-chip antenna with chip-integrated dielectric resonator,” which was published in IEEE Transactions on Antennas and Propagation in August 2021. Since the paper was published before the project commenced on January 1, 2022, it is not included as an output of the project. However, the research work led to a patent application, which was eventually granted after a few revisions. The patent titled “On-Chip Antenna and On-Chip Antenna Array”, US 11848499B2 was awarded on Dec. 19, 2023 (please see Part C, Item 11, No. 2). We developed a one-port de-embedding method for extracting the dielectric constant of SiO2 in standard complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) at terahertz frequencies. This method can eliminate the effects of the feeding network and other repeatable errors, thereby simplifying calibration and enhancing measurement accuracy. Simulations and experiments are conducted at 140, 300, and 450 GHz using 180-nm and 65-nm CMOS processes. The findings were reported in the journal paper J1. We developed a 450-GHz on-chip antenna with a wide impedance bandwidth under an extremely low profile of 1.3% of the free-space wavelength. The design entails two radiating patches, each with an I-slot. It has two resonances across the operating band; the lower resonance corresponds to the TM10 mode, and the upper resonance corresponds to the TM10 mode. We modified the dual patch with C-slot and tuning stubs to yield a filtering response. The findings were published in the journal paper J6. We designed a wideband terahertz on-chip sequential-phase-fed circularly-polarized (CP) antenna that incorporates highly compact reactance-loaded delay lines. A novel side-shorted patch unit forms the radiating element. This patch unit, through the effective utilization of both a physical electrical wall and an equivalent magnetic wall, exhibits the resonant properties of both a patch antenna and an SIW cavity, resonating in unique half TM01 and quarter TE201 modes. The employment of these two distinct modes expands the antenna impedance bandwidth and significantly reduces the overall size compared to complete TM01 and TE201 modes. A four-port sequential phase feed network is incorporated to generate CP. The requisite 90-degree sequential phase difference is attained by deploying the reactance-loaded delay line. This method significantly reduces the size of the sequential phase feed network while achieving the desired sequential phases. The findings were reported in the journal paper J5. Two key figures of merit for IC are chip size and radiated power. The former dictates the cost of the IC fabrication, and the latter the range in communications or resolution in imaging. The resonators and on-chip antennas are passive in J1, C1, and C2. To address the comments from the proposal reviewers and to demonstrate that our designed antenna can work well with the active circuitry, we exploited our leading antenna technologies to enhance the active circuit performance. In journal paper J2, we aim to achieve the highest radiated power per unit area at THz frequencies. A differentially-fed shared aperture patch antenna with on-chip power combining and radiation function was proposed for a compact terahertz (THz) source design. A high-density parallel coupled oscillator topology is proposed to feed the antenna for realizing high area efficiency. This design achieves good performances in terms of dc-to-THz efficiency, area efficiency, and EIRP beyond 600 GHz. As the turnaround time for IC fabrication is at least three months and the cost has continuously increased substantially, for the demonstration of field manipulation using leaky-wave antennas, we employed the proposed design process but pushed the frequency up to optical frequencies. In the proposal, we proposed to use amplitude-modulated leaky-wave antennas to demonstrate frequency beam scanning. The gap width of the gap waveguide is modulated sinusoidally. We developed holographic amplitude-modulated leaky-wave antennas utilizing this amplitude modulation technique for both near-field and far-field applications at millimeter-wave frequencies. This technique has been employed at optical frequencies in journal papers J3 and J4 for optical chip applications. Here, optical wavefront shaping by holographic metal-insulator-metal plasmonic gap waveguides is reported in J3. The amplitude and phase information of an arbitrary free-space wave can be recorded in the waveguide through the amplitude variation of the guided wave. By carefully designing the plasmonic gap waveguide, the guided waves can be shaped into any desired free-space light field, thereby enabling complex free-space functions, including highly directional beams, dual beams with arbitrarily tailorable power ratios and radiation angles, focusing beams, and Airy beam generation. Side-lobe level (SLL) is one of the most crucial parameters in antenna design. In J4, a plasmonic optical leaky-wave antenna with low SLL is reported. Shifting the spatial frequency by periodically modulating the electric-field amplitude in a plasmonic gap waveguide enables a free-space-coupled wave to emerge from the antenna. Simultaneously, precise control of the aperture fields by the modulation depth allows for reducing SLL. Simulation results indicate that the proposed design can achieve a high directivity of 15.8 dB and a low SLL of -20 dB at the wavelength of 1550 nm. A low SLL of -15 dB or lower is experimentally demonstrated within the wavelength range of 1527 nm to 1570 nm. In addition, the low-SLL property is further verified by comparing it with a uniformly modulated antenna. By modulating the guided waves in the plasmonic gap waveguide in different forms, the aperture fields can be flexibly arranged to achieve arbitrary wavefront shaping. It bridges the gap between guided and free-space waves, empowering plasmonic integrated devices to control free-space light and thus enabling various free-space functions.

11212121.label: Major findings and research outcome
11212121.value: We have investigated the working mechanism of the proposed wide impedance- and gain-bandwidth on-chip antenna (OCA) operating at 0.3 THz, utilizing an on-chip antenna as a feeder for the dielectric resonator and an independent radiator. The research work resulted in the US patent, US 11848499 B2. A precise extraction methodology for the dielectric constant of SiO2 in CMOS at terahertz frequencies was developed, and extractions were carried out at 140, 300, and 450 GHz using 180-nm and 65-nm CMOS processes. The findings were reported in the journal paper J1. In the journal paper J6, we developed two 450 GHz on-chip dual-patch antennas. The dual patch excites TM10 mode at lower frequencies and TM01 mode at higher frequencies. An I-slot was introduced in each patch for impedance matching, frequency tuning, and size reduction. Replacing the I-slot with a C-slot and modifying the feed line created radiation nulls, resulting in a filtering antenna. With an extremely low profile of 0.013 λo, the designed antennas have an impedance bandwidth of over 15%. In the journal paper J5, we developed a highly compact on-chip sequential-phased circularly polarized (CP) antenna with 19% overlapped impedance-axial-ratio (-AR) bandwidth. The long delay line in the conventional sequential-rotation approach was replaced by a compact reactance-loaded sequential-phase feed, realized by equivalent capacitors and inductors. The THz on-chip antennas and arrays presented in J5 and J6 achieved the state-of-the-art bandwidth with an extremely low profile. In the journal paper J2, we presented a differentially fed, oversized, shared-aperture patch antenna. A high-density parallel coupled oscillator topology was developed to feed the antenna, achieving a high core area efficiency of 1.95 mW/mm². Integrated with a lens, the peak EIRP is 29.6 dBm with a frequency tuning range of 4.9% from 584.8 to 614.3 GHz. In journal papers J3 and J4, we extended the on-chip antenna design to optical chips that can be fabricated in-house. Based on the radiation pattern synthesis approach presented in the proposal, we were able to manipulate the radiation patterns utilizing the leaky-wave antenna concept. By modulating the gap width and periodicity of the gap waveguide, the guided waves were molded into highly directional beams, dual beams with arbitrary, tailorable power ratios and radiation angles, focusing beams, and Airy beam generation as presented in J3. Similarly, we can suppress the sidelobe levels of the antenna radiation patterns as reported in J4.

11212121.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11212121.value: For 6G, THz transmitters (TXs), receivers (TRs), and transceivers (TRXs) are indispensable. They require on-chip antennas and arrays for signal transmission and reception. The experience gained in this project paved the way for developing THz ICs for 6G and B6G. Traditionally, slot antennas and silicon lenses are used for THz ICs, as the bandwidth of patch antennas is very limited due to the extremely thin SiO2 substrate in CMOS. The disadvantages of using the slot antennas include the issue of heat dissipation and the need for an expensive silicon lens. The antenna designs in J5 and J6 demonstrated that patch antennas, with clever designs, can alleviate the bandwidth issue previously confronted. The on-chip power combining approach developed in J2 eliminates the need for a complex feeding network, which can limit the overall bandwidth of typical arrays, such as on-chip phased arrays. A salient feature of 6G is the integration of sensing and communication, where beam scanning plays a crucial role. We have already utilized our leaky-wave antenna (LWA) design methodology, presented in J3 and J4, for on-chip LWA integration with active circuits. Some of these preliminary findings have been included in an initial proposal for a long-term, large-scale research program.

11212121.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11212121.value: The operating bandwidth of high-frequency integrated circuits (ICs) is often limited by that of the on-chip antennas and arrays due to the limited thickness of the chip substrate. In this project, we demonstrated that such limitations can be alleviated with novel antenna designs. For on-chip arrays used for power combining, we have demonstrated that both the antenna elements and their feeding network can be made compact by integrating our expertise in antenna and IC design, thereby achieving a high area efficiency for reduced IC fabrication costs. Beam manipulation, a crucial feature in future 6G applications, is demonstrated using the beam synthesis method we developed, which utilizes a leaky-wave antenna implementation. These leaky-wave antennas (LWAs) allow for one-dimensional beam steering and manipulation. On-chip power combining incorporated with active circuits, as demonstrated in our research output, enhances the communication range. With novel designs in LWA elements and active circuits, one can extend beam steering into the two-dimensional hemispherical space, meeting the application demands of future 6G.

11212321.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11212321.value: 微機器人細胞注射系統自動化研究

11212321.label: Project Objectives
11212321.value: Develop a fully automated adherent cell injection system for measurement of gap junctional intercellular communication (GJIC) and drug screening. Key functions in the proposed system include structural patterning of the cells into 2D arrays, microscopic image processing for automated recognition of cells, and reconstruction of the 3D model by combining the 2D morphological information with vision-based contact detection. Design and fabricate surface acoustic wave devices for patterning the cells into 2D arrays. The cells will be patterned to have close contact (<5 um) between adjacent cells in the same column and large gaps (> 20 um) between columns. This design will ensure the cells in the same column to establish functional gap junctions while avoiding cross communications between cells from different columns. Develop machine learning algorithms for automated recognition of the cells from 2D microscopic images. We will investigate the convolutional neural network models for real-time detection of target cells. The structural information from acoustic patterning will serve as a priori to reduce the computational complexity. Reconstruct the 3D model of adherent cells by contacting multiple locations on the cells. The reconstructed cell model will be used for 3D morphological analysis and individualized microinjection. Conduct measurement of gap junctional intercellular communication (GJIC) by using the newly developed microrobotic system. The dye transfer distance and the number of dye-coupled cells are used as the metric to quantify the GJIC functions. Conduct pharmacologic screening of rationally selected drug libraries for rescuing the GJIC and treatment of cardiac arrhythmias. We will carefully select drug libraries and apply them to the cardiomyocyte cell line (i.e., HL-1 cells) and assess their effects on the alteration of the GJIC to identify the optimal treatment for cardiac arrhythmias.

11212321.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11212321.value: 突發性心臟猝死通常由心律失常引起，是香港和全球男性和女性死亡的主要原因。危及生命的心律失常從根本上歸因於間隙連接細胞間通訊障礙。細胞通訊的測量和藥物篩選通常需要將熒光染料顯微注射到單個細胞中並監測染料從注射細胞轉移到相鄰細胞。此外，顯微注射是細胞生物學、生命科學和臨床應用中必不可少的技術。微型機器人的最新進展為單細胞的自動化操作提供了有效的解決方案。然而，現有的解決方案大多側重於大型懸浮細胞的操作，自動化程度低，因此尚未達到大規模實施。貼壁細胞的自動化操作在很大程度上未被充分探索，因為貼壁細胞在形態上非常不規則並且比懸浮細胞小得多，這使得細胞識別具有挑戰性。為了解決現有解決方案的局限性並構建用於操作貼壁細胞的全自動系統，我們建議將表面聲波與微型機器人相結合，以實現高通量顯微注射。在這項研究中，我們將應用新的微型機器人系統將熒光染料注入單個細胞。注射後，通過監測從注射細胞轉移到鄰近細胞的熒光信號，微型機器人系統可以測量細胞間通訊並篩選藥物庫，以確定心律失常的最佳治療方法。擬議的研究課題具有改變微型機器人細胞操作以產生更廣泛影響的巨大潛力。該項目的成功將為下一代微型機器人技術建立理論和實驗基礎，最大限度地減少人為乾預並提高系統效能。

11212621.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11212621.value: 基於單晶鈮酸鋰薄膜之電光模式控制器件

11212621.label: Project Objectives
11212621.value: The first objective is to design, fabricate, and characterize electro-optic (EO) mode switches on lithium niobate on insulator (LNOI) for operation within the C-band (1530 – 1570 nm). An EO mode switch allows fast dynamic conversion between two modes of a few-mode waveguide and is an important device in a reconfigurable mode-division-multiplexing (MDM) system. To achieve the mode switching function, an EO grating generated in a waveguide formed on an LNOI wafer is proposed. The research work involves a detailed analysis of the parameters of the waveguide and the grating electrodes for optimizing the switching function. Several different designs will be produced and verified experimentally. The switching voltages of the devices are expected to be ~10 V and the switching speeds are shorter than 100 ns. The second objective is to design, fabricate, and characterize EO switchable mode (de)multiplexers with mode conversion on LNOI for operation within the C-band. An EO switchable mode (de)multiplexer with mode conversion allows a dynamic control of spatial separation of two modes and the higher-order mode is converted into the fundamental mode after switching. To achieve this function, an asymmetric directional coupler formed with a two-mode waveguide and a parallel single-mode waveguide is proposed, where the EO effect is used to deactivate light coupling between the two waveguides. The research work involves a detailed analysis of the parameters of the waveguides and the electrodes for optimizing the switching function. Several different designs will be produced and verified experimentally. The switching voltages of the devices are expected to be lower than 10 V and the switching speeds are shorter than 100 ns. The third objective is to design, fabricate, and characterize EO switchable mode (de)multiplexers without mode conversion on LNOI for operation within the C-band. In mode routing applications, the mode identities need to be maintained after switching. To achieve spatial switching without mode conversion, a symmetric directional coupler formed with two parallel identical two-mode waveguides is proposed, where the EO effect is used to deactivate light coupling between the two waveguides. The research work involves a detailed analysis of the parameters of the waveguides and the electrodes for optimizing the switching function. Several different designs will be produced and verified experimentally. The switching voltages of the devices are expected to be lower than 10 V and the switching speeds are shorter than 100 ns.

11212621.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11212621.value: Mode-division multiplexing (MDM), which allows different modes of a few-mode fiber/waveguide to carry different signals, is evolving into a promising technology to expand the transmission capacity of the current single-mode fiber technology. There have been a number of experiments showing the great potential of MDM for various applications, such as long-haul telecommunication, short-distance data transmission (as in data centers), and on-chip optical interconnection. The advancement of the MDM technology depends critically on the development of mode-controlling devices, which play very much the same roles as the counterpart wavelength-controlling devices in current wavelength-division-multiplexing systems. Over the last six or seven years, there have been many demonstrations of passive mode-controlling devices, such as mode converters, mode (de)multiplexers, and mode filters and PI’s team has contributed much to the development of these devices with the polymer waveguide platform. It is envisaged that future MDM systems require not only passive mode-controlling devices but also active mode-controlling devices that can effectively switch and route fiber/waveguide modes. PI’s research team has demonstrated some mode-controlling devices by making use of the large thermo-optic (TO) effect of polymer waveguides, but the switching speeds of TO devices are slow. To increase the switching speed, PI’s research team has explored the electro-optic (EO) effect of lithium niobite (LN) and demonstrated several novel mode-switching devices using bulk LN. However, the waveguide technology based on bulk LN presents significant difficulties in the device design and the driving voltages required are also too high for practical applications. In this project, the PI plans to explore a new waveguide platform based on LN on insulator (LNOI) for the development of EO mode-controlling devices. In particular, two types of devices are studied: mode switches and switchable mode (de)multiplexers (with or without mode conversion), which are basic components in reconfigurable MDM systems. The availability of commercial LNOI wafers in recent years has made possible the development of efficient high-speed EO modulators with a small footprint, which is particularly important for on-chip applications. It is expected that the use of LNOI can significantly lower the driving voltages of the few-mode devices proposed in this project. The outcome of the project will advance not only the MDM technology, but also the LNOI technology. Equipped with extensive research experience in the development of both passive and active mode-controlling devices, PI’s research team has all the capacity to complete this project and deliver the proposed devices. 利用少模光纖/波導的不同模式承載不同信號的模分複用（MDM）技術，可以擴展當前單模光纖技術的傳輸容量，正在發展成為一種具有巨大前景的傳輸技術。大量實驗表明，MDM 在各種應用中具有巨大潛力，例如長途通信、短距離數據傳輸（如在數據中心）和片上光互連。MDM 技術的進步在很大程度上取決於模式控制器件的發展，模式控制器件與當前波分複用系統中的對應波長控制器件起著非常相似的作用。 在過去六七年中，已經有許多無源模式控制器件的演示，例如模式轉換器、模式（解）復用器和模式濾波器等，而 PI 的研究團隊亦利用聚合物波導平台研製了這類器件。預計未來的 MDM 系統不僅需要無源模式控制器件，還需要能夠有效切換和路由光纖/波導模式的有源模式控制器件。PI 的研究團隊利用聚合物波導比較强的熱光 (TO) 效應展示了一些模式控制器件，但 TO 器件的開關速度較慢。為了提高開關速度，PI 的研究團隊探索了鈮酸鋰 (LN) 的電光 (EO) 效應，並展示了幾種使用塊狀 LN 的新型模式切換器件。然而，基於塊體 LN 的波導技術在器件設計上存在很大困難，並且所需的驅動電壓對於實際應用來說也太高。在本項目中，PI 計劃探索一種基於生長於絕緣體上的單晶 LN 薄膜 (LNOI) 的新型波導平台，用於研製 EO 模式控制器件，特別是研製可重構 MDM 系統中的兩種基本器件：模式開關和可切換的模式（解）復用器（帶或不帶模式轉換）。近年來，商用 LNOI 晶片已應用於研製具有小尺寸的高效高速 EO 調製器，這些調制器對於片上應用尤為重要。預計使用 LNOI 晶片可以顯著降低本項目所提出的少模式器件的驅動電壓。本項目的成果不僅可以推進 MDM 技術，還可以推進 LNOI 技術。PI 的研究團隊在無源和有源模式控制器件的研製方面都擁有豐富經驗，有足夠能力完成本項目並交付所提出的器件。

11212621.label: Realisation of objectives
11212621.value: The primary objectives of the project are to develop electro-optic (EO) mode-controlling devices on the lithium-niobate-on-insulator (LNOI) platform, which is an emerging waveguide platform for the implementation of high-density integrated photonic circuits for on-chip optical signal processing. The EO devices investigated in the project include mode switches, mode converters, and mode (de)multiplexers, which are formed with waveguide structures, such as directional couplers and long-period gratings (LPGs). We carried out a series of theoretical studies on these devices based on rib and strip-loaded waveguides. Our theoretical results show the possibility of achieving EO mode conversion between the TE00 mode and the TE10 mode with a driving voltage of around 10 V by using an LPG structure. We also carried out theoretical studies on EO directional coupler devices for mode (de)multiplexers with and without mode conversion and came up with design recipes. The theoretical studies appeared to be encouraging. On the experiment side, we put a tremendous amount of time and effort in developing the technology for the fabrication of rib waveguides and strip-loaded waveguides on LNOI. We are now able to fabricate rib waveguides to support both the TE and the TM polarizations with low losses. Our fabricated strip-loaded waveguides, however, suffer from huge losses for the TM polarization and can only operate for the TE polarization. The reason for the huge TM loss is still unclear; it may be related to the uniformity of the SiO2 strip deposited on the LNOI wafer (limited by our facility). In the fabrication of almost every device, we usually added a waveguide taper at one end of the device to facilitate the excitation of the fundamental mode. In the beginning, we did not realize that the waveguide taper could generate significant spurious mode couplings and destroyed the function of the device. It took us quite some time to understand this problem (which is caused by the hybridization of modes with close effective indices) through extensive numerical simulation. We now know how to design waveguide tapers to avoid this problem for our devices. To form EO devices, it is necessary to deposit electrodes on LNOI waveguides. We faced serious challenges in the fabrication of electrodes for our devices, because of the non-planar waveguide geometry. Our collaborators in University of Electronic Science and Technology of China (UESTC) provided much help in electrode fabrication. In fact, after many rounds of failure in our laboratory, we decided to send our samples to UESTC to do electrode deposition, which was the final step in the fabrication process. We measured a number of fabricated EO mode converters based on LPG electrodes formed on strip-loaded waveguides. The experimental results were poor. While we could observe strong EO-induced mode conversion, the voltage required was high (>60 V) and the mode conversion effect was unstable. The mode conversion dynamics were highly complicated and nowhere near the theoretical predications. We suspect that ion migration in LNOI and the large capacitance of the electrodes account for our observed phenomena. At the time of writing, we are still working with UESTC with the hope that we may understand or even solve these problems. As such, the experimental studies on EO devices are behind the schedule and many problems remain to be solved before we can deliver any decent results. We underestimated the difficulty in the realization of fast mode-switching devices on the LNOI platform. Although our experimental studies on EO devices did not progress well, we gained much experience and insight in the waveguide fabrication techniques and the characteristics of the LPG structures during our process of developing the LNOI technology. Our insight led to the demonstration of new LPG-based devices. We achieved ultrabroadband conversion between the TE00 and TE10 modes with a z-cut LN few-mode waveguide. The study is published in Optics Letters (C. Lu, W. Jin, and K. S. Chiang, “Long-period gratings on lithium-niobate waveguides: phase-matching turning points for ultra-broadband mode conversion,” Opt. Lett., vol. 47, pp. 3984, August 2022). A typical device provides a mode extinction ratio >20 dB from 1550 nm to a wavelength >1700 nm, and another one provides a mode extinction ratio >10 dB from 1464 nm to a wavelength >1700 nm. Recently, we demonstrated the feasibility of designing LPGs for achieving conversion of modes of orthogonal polarizations, namely conversion between the TE00 mode and the TM00 mode by exploiting the spatial overlap between the major and minor field components of two orthogonally polarized modes in a high-index-contrast waveguide. Our device fabricated on an LNOI rib waveguide with a compact 330-mm long dual SiO2 grating structure achieves a polarization mode conversion efficiency of ~99% at 1550 nm. Our study extends the conventional functions of LPGs as mode converters for the same polarization and opens up new possibilities in the development of polarization-controlling devices for applications in high-density integrated photonics. The design principle for our LPGs is novel and the function achieved is highly useful. The study has been accepted for publication in Optics Letters (M. Wang, W. Jin, K. Chen, and K. S. Chiang, “Long-period grating on thin-film lithium-niobate waveguide for polarization mode conversion,” Opt. Lett. 2025, to appear). The most important result achieved in this project is the proposal of anisotropy engineering enabled by the proton-exchange (PE) process as an approach for the development of compact ultrabroadband devices on the LNOI platform. We designed and fabricated three exemplary devices based on this approach: a TE-pass polarizer, a TM-pass polarizer, and a polarization splitter. All of these devices are capable of providing ultrabroadband operation with high performance. The process of fabricating these devices is simple and robust, as it allows a single PE process to be employed to assist in waveguide etching and, at the same time, modify the anisotropic index profiles of selected areas. In principle, the PE process allows the anisotropy of practically any LNOI structures to be modified, which opens up new opportunities for achieving new optical functions or improved device performances. Anisotropy engineering enabled by the PE process could become an important design methodology in the development of photonic integrated devices on the LNOI platform. The study has been accepted for publication in Optica (W. Jin and K. S. Chiang, “Thin-film lithium-niobate waveguide devices based on proton-exchange-induced anisotropy,” Optica, 2025, to appear). In collaboration with UESTC, a new and effective technique to solve the bias problem for EO modulators on LNOI was demonstrated experimentally. Compared with existing techniques, our technique, which relies on our special Mach-Zehnder interferometer design combined with thermo-optic compensation for fabrication errors, provides more stable and faster operation and consumes much less electric power. Our approach can greatly advance the development of practical EO modulators. The study is published in Optics Express (M. Wang, J. Li, H. Yao, X. Li, J. Wu, K. S. Chiang, and K. Chen, “Thin-film lithium-niobate modulator with combined passive bias and thermo-optic bias,” Opt. Express, vol. 30, pp. 39706, Oct. 2022). The paper is selected as an “Editor’s Pick” by the journal for its excellent scientific quality.
