rows: The first objective is to design, fabricate, and characterize electro-optic (EO) mode switches on lithium niobate on insulator (LNOI) for operation within the C-band (1530 – 1570 nm). An EO mode switch allows fast dynamic conversion between two modes of a few-mode waveguide and is an important device in a reconfigurable mode-division-multiplexing (MDM) system. To achieve the mode switching function, an EO grating generated in a waveguide formed on an LNOI wafer is proposed. The research work involves a detailed analysis of the parameters of the waveguide and the grating electrodes for optimizing the switching function. Several different designs will be produced and verified experimentally. The switching voltages of the devices are expected to be ~10 V and the switching speeds are shorter than 100 ns.

The second objective is to design, fabricate, and characterize EO switchable mode (de)multiplexers with mode conversion on LNOI for operation within the C-band. An EO switchable mode (de)multiplexer with mode conversion allows a dynamic control of spatial separation of two modes and the higher-order mode is converted into the fundamental mode after switching. To achieve this function, an asymmetric directional coupler formed with a two-mode waveguide and a parallel single-mode waveguide is proposed, where the EO effect is used to deactivate light coupling between the two waveguides. The research work involves a detailed analysis of the parameters of the waveguides and the electrodes for optimizing the switching function. Several different designs will be produced and verified experimentally. The switching voltages of the devices are expected to be lower than 10 V and the switching speeds are shorter than 100 ns.

The third objective is to design, fabricate, and characterize EO switchable mode (de)multiplexers without mode conversion on LNOI for operation within the C-band. In mode routing applications, the mode identities need to be maintained after switching. To achieve spatial switching without mode conversion, a symmetric directional coupler formed with two parallel identical two-mode waveguides is proposed, where the EO effect is used to deactivate light coupling between the two waveguides. The research work involves a detailed analysis of the parameters of the waveguides and the electrodes for optimizing the switching function. Several different designs will be produced and verified experimentally. The switching voltages of the devices are expected to be lower than 10 V and the switching speeds are shorter than 100 ns.

11212621.label: Major findings and research outcome
11212621.value: The major findings and research outcome are summarized below: (1) Our theoretical analyses show possibility of designing efficient electro-optic (EO) mode-controlling devices on the LNOI platform. The analyses have led to design receipts for EO mode switches and mode (de)multiplexers. The theoretical analyses, however, are too ideal to explain the experimental results that involve migration of ions in LNOI. (2) Experimental realization of EO mode-controlling devices on the LNOI platform is technologically challenging. The switching dynamics of our experimental devices are highly complicated and cannot be captured by the theoretical analyses. It is yet to demonstrate good performances with the proposed EO devices. (3) After the project proposal had been submitted (before it was approved), we already started to work on long-period gratings (LPGs) formed on LNOI rib waveguides [J3]. During the project period, two new LPG designs for mode conversion have been proposed and demonstrated experimentally. One is an ultrabroadband TE00-TE10 mode converter formed on a graded-index LN waveguide [J2] and the other is a TE00-TM00 mode converter on a LNOI rib waveguide [J5]. The TE00-TM00 mode converter, in particular, extends the conventional functions of LPGs as mode converters for the same polarization and opens up new possibilities in the development of polarization-controlling devices for applications in high-density integrated photonics. (4) Anisotropy engineering enabled by the proton-exchange (PE) process has been proposed as a new approach of designing polarization mode manipulating devices on the LNOI platform [J4]. Three exemplary devices based on this approach: a TE-pass polarizer, a TM-pass polarizer, and a polarization splitter, have been designed and demonstrated experimentally. All of these devices are capable of providing ultrabroadband operation with high performance. PE-enabled anisotropy engineering has the potential to become an important technology for the development of functional waveguide devices on the LNOI platform. (5) In collaboration with UESTC, a new and effective technique to solve the bias problem for high-speed EO modulators on LNOI has been demonstrated experimentally. Compared with existing techniques, our technique, which relies on our special waveguide design and thermo-optic compensation for fabrication errors, provides more stable and faster operation and consumes much less electric power [J1].

11212621.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11212621.value: We have not yet succeeded in demonstrating high-performance EO mode-controlling functions with our proposed devices. The challenges in realizing such devices perhaps explain why EO mode-controlling devices on LNOI (EO mode switches and EO mode (de)multiplexers) are very scarce. Our experimental results revealed very complicated switching dynamics that cannot be explained by theoretical analyses. Much work needs to be done to understand such dynamics. It is a high-risk undertaking to go deep into this area of research, which involves material science, waveguide structure design, and electrode design/deployment, as there is no guarantee of generating high-quality publishable results. Our studies on LPGs and PE-enabled anisotropy engineering on LNOI have been fruitful. The function of the LPG structure has been extended to allow polarization mode conversion. There are well-established LPG designs that can be employed to tailor the transmission characteristics of LPGs. PE-enabled anisotropy engineering allows the anisotropy in selected areas of LNOI to be modified and opens up a new direction of designing waveguide devices on LNOI. These new developments have the potential to be further explored for realizing new functional devices on LNOI. PE-enabled anisotropy engineering could be developed into a low-cost process for mass production of LNOI devices.

11212621.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11212621.value: Lithium-niobate on insulator (LNOI) is an emerging platform for the development of photonic chips. The incorporation of mode-division multiplexing (MDM) in this platform, where different spatial modes of LNOI waveguides carry different signal channels, is a promising technology for increasing the signal processing capacity of LNOI chips. The development of this technology relies on the availability of various active and passive mode-controlling devices. The primary objective of this project is to develop mode-controlling devices on LNOI. We have conducted both theoretical and experimental studies of various mode-controlling devices on LNOI. We have achieved only limited success in the development of active devices based on the electro-optic effect of lithium niobate. Our experimental devices exhibited complicated switching characteristics that cannot be explained by theoretical analyses, which points to a new direction for further studies. On the other hand, we have succeeded in demonstrating several high-performance passive mode-controlling devices on LNOI based on periodic structures and our proposed idea of anisotropy engineering. These passive devices are highly useful components in LNOI circuits for on-chip signal processing. The device structures and the fabrication process we have developed could be further explored for the implementation of more functional devices on LNOI.

11212721.label: Project Objectives
11212721.value: Selective mode-splitting engineering in a thin-film LN microresonator. To arbitrarily control the wavelength span of a resonant electro-optic (EO) comb, we propose to introduce periodic width modulation to a microring resonator to create mode splitting at the desired resonant modes. The first objective here is to thoroughly investigate the dependence of mode-splitting on the amplitude and period of width modulation in a LN microresonator, through both numerical simulations as well as actual device fabrication and characterization. Mode splitting with arbitrary strengths and at arbitrary mode numbers will be experimentally realized. Modeling and optimization of EO frequency comb generation in a selectively mode-split LN resonator. A numerical model of resonant EO comb generation will be developed, taking into account the presence of mode splitting at certain wavelengths. The required width-modulation profile will be optimized to realize a flat-top EO comb generation with programmable wavelength span, by disrupting and cutting off the comb generation process at the designed mode-split wavelengths. Flat-top EO comb generation with programmable wavelength span. Based on the optimized design in Objective 2, width-modulated thin-film LN microresonators integrated with microwave electrodes will be fabricated. Flat-top EO frequency comb with a designed wavelength span will be generated by optically pumping at a certain resonance mode and electrically driving the system using a microwave source. EO comb sources with DWDM-compatible channel spacing (i.e. 25 GHz and 50 GHz) and channel number will be realized. Proof-of-concept demonstration of a DWDM optical transmitter system using the proposed EO comb source. The DWDM-compatible EO comb demonstrated in Objective 3 will be tested in a proof-of-concept DWDM data transmission system. Individual comb lines will be de-multiplexed and modulated to test the high-speed data transmission performances. The effects of power variation between comb lines, noise properties and system stability will be investigated to evaluate the performance of the proposed system in a practical telecommunications application scenario.

11212721.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11212721.value: 隨著全球互聯網數據流量不斷增加，當前用於長距離通信和數據中心的光纖互連正面臨巨大挑戰。集成光學致力於將多樣化的光學元件小型化並集成於同一芯片上，可望為未來光通信系統提供急需的更緊湊、低成本、高速率和低功耗的光互連解決方案。例如，一個片上集成的電光頻率梳源可以產生一系列頻率等間距的光學信號，從而取代現有波分複用光通信系統中所需的大量分立的激光器，大大降低成本與控制複雜度。 當前片上電光頻梳用於波分複用系統的一個主要挑戰在於頻梳寬度和功率均勻性難以兼得。為此，我們提出一種新的器件設計，在特定諧振模式處引入模式劈裂來精確控制產生的頻梳形狀。通過週期性改變鈮酸鋰微環諧振器的寬度，我們可以選擇性地在特定波長產生模式劈裂並截斷級聯的邊帶發生過程，從而將產生的電光頻梳功率限制在設計的頻譜範圍內。 項目負責人此前已研發了一系列鈮酸鋰光頻率梳器件，包括梳齒數量超過900條、展寬超過80納米的電光頻率梳，和孤子鎖模態克爾光頻梳。初步仿真結果顯示，本方案產生的電光頻梳與常用波分複用系統在通道間距、系統總帶寬和頻譜均勻度等方面具有良好的兼容性，且無需苛刻的諧振器質量係數，可實現性較高。 本項目的成功實施將實現一種小型化、低功耗和兼容波分複用系統的片上電光頻率梳源。該頻率梳源更可進一步與其他鈮酸鋰光學元件集成於同一芯片上，從而實現具有超高帶寬和超低功耗的集成波分複用光發射芯片，可望應用於未來數據中心通信網絡。同時，其優異的頻譜可編程性亦可應用於包括光譜分析、遙距傳感和精密測量在內的廣泛場景。

11212721.label: Realisation of objectives
11212721.value: Objective 1: Selective mode-splitting engineering in a thin-film LN microresonator (100%) We have successfully completed Objective 1 by performing a systematic theoretical and experimental study of the mode-splitting engineering in thin-film LN resonators, especially the behavior in x-cut LN with anisotropic refractive indices along different propagation directions. We propose a gradient photonic crystal ring (PhCR) resonator design that precisely compensates for variations in both refractive index and perturbation strength, and demonstrate, for the first time, PhCR resonators in anisotropic material platforms. We experimentally show controllable frequency splitting at single and multiple selected resonances, and further combine the gradient PhCR with active electro-optic modulation to construct a frequency “mirror” and realize the arbitrary control of electro-optic comb spectral shapes. The results were summarized as a journal paper and published in Advanced Materials (Section C.8, item 6), and presented as a conference paper at CLEO 2024 (Section C.9, item 7). Objective 2: Modeling and optimization of EO frequency comb generation in a selectively mode-split LN resonator (100%) We have performed a comprehensive theoretical investigation of the EO frequency comb generation process in a mode-split resonator system, which could also be understood as a mirror-induced reflection in the frequency domain (or a frequency crystal). The results were summarized as a journal paper and published in Nature Communications (Section C.8, item 2). The design strategy was also experimentally implemented to control the EO spectral shapes based on selective mode splitting, as summarized in (Section C.8, item 6). Objective 3: Flat-top EO comb generation with programmable wavelength span (100%) In this project, we have performed substantial investigation on the chip design, fabrication and characterizations of EO comb generators in the thin-film LN platform. We have demonstrated the power-efficient generation of EO combs using a multi-loop design, lowering the RF power consumption of EO comb generators by an experimentally measured factor of 15. The results were summarized as a journal paper and published in Communications Physics (Section C.8, item 1) and also a conference paper presented at CLEO 2023 (Section C.9, item 1). To facilitate the multi-loop design, we have also performed a systematic investigation on waveguide crossing designs, which was summarized as a journal paper in Optics Letters (Section C.8, item 3) and presented at CLEO 2023 (Section C.9, item 2). We have further combined this power-efficient phase modulator with an amplitude modulator to achieve flat-top EO comb generation, which is subsequently used in the DWDM system demonstration to be discussed in Objective 4. In addition, the power-efficient EO comb generator developed in this project has become a workhorse for chip-scale photonic systems in a variety of applications, including millimeter-wave frequency mixer, coherent LiDAR, and real-time RF spectrum sensing systems. These results were published/under review as journal papers in Electromagnetic Science and Nature Communications (Section C.8, item 11, 16 & 17) and presented at CLEO 2025 (Section C.9, item 9 & 11). Objective 4: Proof-of-concept demonstration of a DWDM optical transmitter system using the proposed EO comb source (100%) We have applied the flat-top EO comb chip developed in the previous objectives for DWDM data transmission over a 53/100-km field-deployed fiber link in Hong Kong. In 2024, we demonstrated that using 18 comb lines spaced at 50 GHz as DWDM light source, the TFLN chip could empower ultrahigh-volume data transmission at a total bit rate of 6.48 Tbit/s over a 53-km field deployed fiber link in Hong Kong, traversing diverse terrains including urban streets, mountains, and underwater tunnels across Victoria Harbour. The fiber link connects two universities and two datacenters in Hong Kong, validating its practical utility for inter-datacenter links. The results were presented at OFC 2024 (Section C.9, item 5). Recently, we have further demonstrated the monolithic integration of on-chip EO comb source, wavelength demultiplexers, and high-speed modulators. Using 46 wavelength channels generated by two lasers and a 50-GHz on-chip electro-optic comb, we achieve 16.56 Tb/s coherent data transmission over a 100-km field-deployed link. To showcase the WDM grid flexibility of our scheme, we further interleave the comb into 100-GHz spacing via an on-chip de-multiplexer, demonstrating 10-channel, 80-Gbaud coherent data transmission at 6.4 Tb/s. Finally, we present a proof-of-concept on-chip WDM transmitter by monolithically integrating the electro-optic comb with a high-speed modulator, delivering 19-channel, 45-Gbaud intensity-modulation direct-detection (IM/DD) data transmission at a total bit rate of 1.71 Tb/s. These results have been summarized as a journal paper to be submitted shortly (Section C.8, item 18). Other achievements in this project: Under the support of this project, we have also developed a number of key photonic components in the thin-film LN platform that are not only crucial to EO comb generators but also other applications, including inverse-designed photonic devices, high-speed waveguide-integrated 2D material photodetectors, thermo- and electro-optic tunable microring filters, ultrabroadband EO modulators, single-sideband modulators, and microwave-resonator-based EO combs. These device-level building blocks have also been applied to a number of system-level demonstrations, including optical vector analysis, photonic millimeter-wave radar, multi-format microwave signal generation, and full-spectrum wireless communications. The relevant results have led to 10 journal articles and 5 conference papers that can be found in Section C.8 and C.9.

11212721.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11212721.value: The power-efficient and flat-top EO comb generators developed in this project have laid important foundation for the continuous development of thin-film LN photonics in PI’s team, especially toward larger-scale photonic systems on chip (e.g. ultrawideband real-time RF spectrum sensing, under review at Nature Communications). The device design and experimental knowhow for high-speed electro-optic modulation and optical delay lines have been adopted in the development of various novel electro-optic devices, e.g. THz-optic modulators operating at up to 500 GHz in Nature Communications, 16:10330, 2025, with further experiments to extend the modulation frequency to 1 THz underway. Further development of the research toward the realization of scalable and efficient THz photonic transmitter and receiver circuits is currently underway with the support of another GRF fund (CityU 11204022) and an STG fund (STG3_E-104_25-N).

11212721.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11212721.value: The rapid expansion of datacenters and AI clusters urgently demands more compact, lower cost, higher speed and more energy-efficient optical interconnect solutions. Chip-based electro-optic frequency comb source that generates a series of equally spaced frequency lines could address these demands by simultaneously powering many wavelength channels of a dense wavelength-division multiplexing (DWDM) optical communication system. A major challenge for current on-chip electro-optic combs in DWDM applications is the trade-off between the comb span and the power flatness. To address this challenge, we have proposed a novel gradient photonic crystal ring resonator design with controllable frequency splitting, and applied this design to realize the arbitrary control of electro-optic comb spectral shapes. We have also demonstrated the power-efficient generation of electro-optic combs using a multi-loop design, lowering the RF power consumption by 15 times. We further demonstrated ultrafast DWDM data transmission based on these electro-optic combs and their monolithic integration with on-chip wavelength demultiplexers, and high-speed modulators, with total data rates up to 16.56 Tbit/s over a 100-km field-deployed fiber link in Hong Kong. The compact, energy-efficient and DWDM compatible chip-based electro-optic combs could provide cost-effective solutions for future datacenter communication networks and applications beyond, including microwave photonics, spectroscopy, and precision metrology.

11213721.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11213721.value: 用於人機交互界面的智能電子皮膚

11213721.label: Project Objectives
11213721.value: To develop flexible sensors for body motion detection. Accurate sensing system is very important for human machine interfaces, since the sensing signals serves as the cognitive commend to manipulate to the robot/machine to do the tasks. Despite the advances of recent progress of flexible strain sensors, the size, weight, stiffness, comfortability with skin and stability are still need to further improve for application in human machine interfaces. The first objective is to develop flexible sensors for body motion detection. The sensor will be based on piezoelectric composite with length < 5mm, width < 2 mm and thickness < 0.1 mm, and can be long-term integrated with skin without irritation and delamination. The body motion caused strain changes at joints, wrist knuckles radial will be detected by the sensor and converted into voltage signals. To develop miniaturized haptic feedback system. To develop a close loop HMI, incorporating haptic interfaces is very important as which can timely and effectively provide tactile feedbacks that sensed by robots. The second objective is to develop haptic feedback system based on mechanical actuators. . We are going to adopt the mechanical vibrational actuators that driven by electromagnetic field as the haptic interface, and develop ultra-thin, skin-conformable miniaturized mechanical vibration actuators as haptic feedback interfaces. The haptic actuators will be with be with the diameter < 5mm, and thickness <1.5mm, working at frequency between 50 Hz to 300 Hz, providing travel amplitude > 0.5 mm. To integrate system level human machine interfaces and realize wireless function. The final objective is to integrate the flexible sensors, haptic system and wireless electronics into a thin, soft, wearable electronics skin format. The proposed human machine interface will based on stretchable Cu serpentine interconnects and circuits, wireless chargeable, controllable and programmable. Motions of the body will be in real time detected and converted into digital signals to control robots. The haptic system will provide tactile information to the user to simulate the interactions between the robot and external world. The final electronic skin human machine interface will be ultra-thin, flexible, stretchable with thickness less than 1.5 mm, great stretchability compatible with extreme deformation of skin and joints. The targeted device will be able to wear on various locations of body without additional fixtures, and will be stable for long-term application to 3 days.

11213721.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11213721.value: 機器人在我們生產生活中有著重要的作用，從先進製造到醫療等多個方面為生活提供便利。下一代機器人需要擁有智慧的感知系統用以實現多功能性。人機交互介面正是為人和機器提供交互的系統，因此可以作為發展機器人領域的重點方向。控制和感知系統集成在機器人上可以有效的控制機器人在諸多領域執行任務。但是這類智慧人機交互介面的研究目前是十分匱乏的。目前大部分人機交互是通過操控杆借助視覺化資訊完成的。而這類交互介面存在兩個主要的問題。第一，操控系統通常比較笨重並且是通過諸如搖杆來操作，這一點與我們實地使用雙手完成任務區別是很大的。第二，目前的人機交互系統缺乏觸覺回饋資訊，大部分情況使用者僅僅可以感受單一的振動回饋。因此，開發一種新型智慧化的人機交互系統勢在必行，這種系統應該具備柔軟、輕薄、無線和可穿戴等特點，從而可以將人和器件人有機的結合起來。 這裡我們提出一種皮膚集成人機交互系統的概念。基於材料和器件的選擇優化實現可拉伸感測器和觸覺回饋器用於即時和閉環系統的柔軟、輕薄、無線和可穿戴的人機交互介面。這種人機交互系統將採用多通路無線感測器作為操控端用於探測和捕捉人體的動態資訊。這些感測器件可以貼附與身體的各個部位用於控制機器人。同時器件人所收到的外部物理刺激資訊會通過機器人身上的感測器將信號發送給使用者。這樣使用者可以通過身上的觸覺回饋系統感受這些資訊。這樣，這種新型人機交互介面可以應用在諸多領域中，從醫療機器人用於非接觸式生物樣品採集，到極端條件的營救作業等諸多場景。

11213721.label: Realisation of objectives
11213721.value: To achieve the objectives, we conduct research on the following 3 parts: 1. The development of flexible sensors for body motion detection. 2. The engineering of a multimodal haptic feedback system. 3. The integration of a system-level wireless Human Machine Interface (HMI). Here is how we achieve these objectives. We developed stable, sensitive, and fatigue-resistant flexible strain sensors by in-situ scraping of a liquid metal slurry onto substrate, e.g. a nitrile glove. The resulting sensing circuits, which can be patterned over various joints with a width less than 2 mm and a thickness of less than 0.1 mm, demonstrated an excellent response to strain (ΔR/R₀ ~35% at 100% strain). The fabrication process, completed by soft silicone encapsulation, is environmentally benign as it involves no toxic chemicals, thus imposing no strict requirements on the operating environment. The final strain-sensing glove enables real-time, sensitive, and accurate monitoring of finger motions, offering both high performance and wearing comfort. A wireless haptic interface was developed based on actuator arrays to provide multimodal tactile feedback. This system incorporates three distinct feedback modes, mechanical, electrotactile, and thermal, designed to selectively activate different cutaneous receptors and provide users with diverse haptic sensations. For mechanical tactile representation, we implemented electromechanical actuators based on the Lorentz force to create physical skin deformation and high-frequency vibration. These actuators, configurable in different sizes, operate at an adjustable frequency of 0–300 Hz. A 5-mm diameter, 1.56-mm thick actuator achieved a maximum travel amplitude above 0.8 mm at its resonant frequency of approximately 200 Hz. These devices are designed for direct interface with various body locations, including the wrist, arm, and palm to provide tactile feedback timely and effectively. We developed enhanced human machine interface based on skin-integrated multimodal sensing and feedback devices. This system captures hand gestures and wrist movements for the intuitive, rapid, and precise control of machines, such as unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). The integrated tactile actuator array translates the drone’s posture into 2D tactile information, enhancing the operator's situational awareness. Furthermore, an integrated obstacle detection system, coupled with neuromuscular electrical stimulation, provides force feedback for collision avoidance and flight path correction. The control unit, constructed from a flexible printed circuit board (FPCB) with microcontroller and Bluetooth Low Energy chip, and encased in a silicone film, is affixed to the user’s skin using stretchable and replaceable hydrogel. To ensure wearability, the system employs a thin (500 μm), stretchable electronic design featuring a serpentine structure that allows for up to 50% stretching, effectively addressing the bulkiness of traditional systems. To maintain functionality and comfort during extended use, we developed a Fully Integrated Breathable Haptic Textile (FIBHT) system. This system utilizes an electrospun poly(styrene-block-butadiene-block-styrene) (SBS) fiber substrate, integrated with liquid metal (LM) circuits and hydrogel skin interfaces. The FIBHT system exhibits exceptional stretchability (400%) and superior permeability, with rates exceeding 657 g/m²/day for moisture and 40 mm/s for air, which keeps the skin dry and comfortable and prevents itchiness or inflammation. The LM-hydrogel-skin interface adheres firmly to the skin and remains stable after seven days of use. In conclusion, this research has successfully realized a comprehensive HMI system that advances the state of the art in terms of sensitivity, multimodal feedback, intuitive control, and, critically, long-term wearability through its superior permeability, stretchability, adhesiveness, and system-level integrity.

11213721.label: Major findings and research outcome
11213721.value: This project has established a comprehensive framework for intelligent electronic skin (e-skin), integrating a class of materials, devices, and system-level strategies for a thin, soft, and wearable format for advanced human machine interfaces. We developed a cohesive platform that synergistically combines flexible sensors, haptic feedback systems, and wireless electronics. This integration was achieved through the strategic use of liquid metal slurry for highly sensitive and stretchable circuits, bioadhesive hydrogels for robust skin interfacing, breathable substrates for long-term comfort, and serpentine structural designs for exceptional mechanical durability and stretchability. Together, these elements ensure the system possesses superior permeability, stretchability, adhesiveness, and long-term wearability on various parts of the body. The system's performance was rigorously validated through comprehensive experimental and computational studies focusing on mechanical design, sensitivity, operational stability, signal fidelity, and long-term reliability. These investigations confirm the platform's capability for accurate body motion detection and realistic haptic reproduction, forming a stable foundation for closed-loop HMI control. Furthermore, to enhance the functionality and user experience of the system, we implemented machine learning algorithms for advanced data interpretation and developed an intuitive graphical user interface compatible with commercial virtual reality headsets. Such a system provides users with a more realistic, intuitive, and immersive interaction environment, fully leveraging the capabilities of the developed hardware. In summary, this project delivers a system-level solution for intelligent electronic skin, demonstrating a significant advancement in creating comfortable, stable, and highly functional interfaces for effective HMI.

11213721.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11213721.value: The potential for improvement lies in creating a seamless, cognitive partnership between the human and the machine where the electronic skin serves as a bidirectional channel for physical intelligence. We believe electronic skin technology will serve as an important platform for embodiment intelligence. The future course of action will focus on developing highly adaptive interfaces and predictive algorithms, enabling the system to learn user intent, self-calibrate in response to changing physiological conditions, and make collaborative decisions in real-time. The ultimate objective is to dissolve the boundary between user and machine, transforming the technology from an external tool into a perceptually and functionally integrated extension of the human body. This will foster a unified system where human intuition and machine precision synergize, enabling unprecedented capabilities in fields from advanced prosthetics and surgical robotics to immersive teleoperation.

11213721.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11213721.value: This project created thin, soft, permeable, comfortable, and wearable electronic devices allowing for a natural and intuitive two-way interaction with machines. It works by sensing your body's movements with high precision, letting you control devices like a robot or drone with a simple gesture. At the same time, it can communicate back to you by creating realistic sensations of touch, vibration, or warmth on your own skin. This technology makes our interaction with technology feel effortless and connected. By making the device soft, wireless, and comfortable enough for long-term wear, we are bridging the gap between human and machine, making advanced control feel as simple as using your own body.

11214121.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11214121.value: Strong materials are desired for advanced technologies in i transportation, energy, aerospace, medical and civil industries. So far, one of the most effective approaches to process ultra-strong materials is grain refinement by severe plastic deformation (SPD). SPD methods are capable of processing bulk nanostructured materials with superior strength, but their scaling up for industrial production is still challenging. Recently, we have produced a new type of heterostructured nano-lamellar material at low cost using readily available industrial facilities [1]. The key to effective and low-cost processing of nano-lamellar material lies in two novel concepts– (1) tuning strain incompatibility in heterostructured materials, and (2) segregating solute atoms to lamellar boundaries to stabilize the nano-lamellae. Using these two concepts, we have successfully processed an ultrastrong low-carbon nanosteel by a simple warm rolling process. The work presents a viable industrial method for processing bulk nanostructured materials, but also raises some fundamental issues that need to be addressed: (1) How does the strain incompatibility in heterostructured materials was accommodated by the local deformation mechanisms? (2) To what extent, the local stress state and the local strain have accelerated the grain refinement process? (3) What are the major effects of segregation on grain refinement and structure stabilization? Here we propose to address the above issues using a low-carbon steel with a nominal composition (weight %) of 0.19 C-1.01 Mn-1.46 Si as the model material. A designated processing route involving pre-heat-treatment and warm rolling will be carried out to produce the nanosteel. Systematic microstructural characterization will be performed to reveal the detailed microstructural evolution and grain refinement processes under the warm rolling condition. State-of-art in-situ microstructural characterization methods will be conducted to analyze the relationship between deformation mechanisms and the local strain. Ex-situ atom probe tomography will be used to investigate the segregation effects induced by warm rolling with increasing strain. This project is expected to lead to an in-depth understanding of heterostructured materials, including the deformation mechanisms, grain refinement process and the character of strain incompatibility. Furthermore, it will offer a scientific knowledge for establishing effective grain refinement methods for other heterostructured materials, thus to expand the industrial applications of heterostructured materials. 高强度结构材料是交通、能源、航空航天、医疗和民工工业等领域的前沿研究的重要研究对象。目前，剧烈塑性变形（SPD）是公认最为有效的制备超高强度块体结构材料技术。然而，剧烈塑性变形设备和生产成本要求高，其制备的块体结构材料尺寸放大仍然是难以攻克的重要挑战。近期，我们提出了一种以异构材料设计理念制备新型纳米层片材料的新思路，有望实现低成本纳米结构材料的工业化制备[1]。该纳米化技术的核心创新性有以下两点：（1）提出在塑性变形加工中，精确调控异构材料的塑性应变不匹配，促进组织纳米化；（2）提出以溶质原子界面偏析稳定纳米层片结构，抑制纳米组织回复与长大。据此，我们利用温轧成形技术，成功的制备了一种超高强度纳米低碳钢。该工作不但为工业化制备纳米结构材料提供了可行方案，还提出了一些值得深入研究的基础科学问题：（1）异构材料中的局部变形不匹配如何协调？（2）局部应力-应变状态促进组织纳米化作用机制是什么？（3）合金元素的界面偏析对促进晶粒细化和提高结构稳定性的具体影响是什么？ 本研究拟以一种低碳钢（具体成分：0.19 C-1.01 Mn-1.46 Si）为模型材料，设计异构化退火+温轧的新型工艺，制备纳米低碳低合金异构钢。拟对异构化退火和温轧的全过程进行了系统的微观组织演化研究；利用先进的原位电子显微学技术分析局部应变与变形机制的相关性；通过三维原子探针重构技术，深入研究由温轧变形引起的元素偏析，及其对纳米化效应的影响机制。 在对异构材料在变形机制、晶粒细化、应变配分等方面的深入机理性认识的基础上，进一步拓展关于其他类型异构材料纳米化的共性问题研究，最终推进各类异构材料产品的工业化进程。

11214121.label: Realisation of objectives
11214121.value: (1)Revealed the underlying strain hardening mechanisms of heterostructured dual-phase steel. In-situ EBSD and SEM-DIC techniques have been used to explore the deformation mechanisms and HDI strain hardening mechanisms. (i) Deformation mechanisms investigated by in-situ EBSD. A Fe-0.19C-1.46Mn-1.01Si steel was subjected to intercritical annealing to control the distribution and volume fraction of ferrite and martensite in two DP steels (HS740 and HS780). Compared with the HS740, the HS780 sample showed a higher strain hardening rate and a simultaneous increase in strength and uniform elongation. The in-situ EBSD results showed that the grains of the HS740 steel were elongated significantly along the loading direction. However, due to the strong constraint effect of martensite, the configuration of grains for the HS780 sample almost kept unchanged, showing a stable grain structure under the same low strain level. Due to the existence of dual-phase heterostructures, higher density of small angle boundaries formed in the grain interior of the HS780 sample, providing excellent HDI strain hardening. (ii) Strain hardening mechanisms investigated by in-situ μ-DIC. In order to clarify the strain hardening mechanisms, an heterostructured lamellar dual-phase steel was produced where the ferrite grains were fully surrounded by martensite. The modified C-J analysis shows a three-stage strain hardening of the heterostructured dual-phase steel due to the deformation incompatibility between ferrite and martensite. The heterostructured DP steel shows higher strain hardening rate than the full martensite structure during the entire strain stage, contributed by the extraordinary HDI hardening which occupies about 60% of the total strain hardening rate. To study the HDI hardening mechanism, in-situ μ-DIC was performed. The results indicated the strain was nonuniformly distributed in the interior of the lamellar ferrite structure. Both strain partitioning and strain gradients increased with tensile strain. The increasing heterogeneous deformation promotes the generation of geometrically necessary dislocations, and consequently help with increasing the HDI stress. As a result, extra strain hardening was produced, resulting in the enhanced mechanical properties. (2)Investigated the effect of interfacial segregation on the thermal stability of the nano-steel To achieve this object, the effects of deformation temperatures on microstructural refinement and mechanical properties of heterostructured dual-phase steels have been investigated. Specifically, low carbon heterostructured dual-phase steels were rolled to a thickness reduction of 80% under different deformation temperatures (25-500℃). With the increase of temperature from 25 to 300℃, the average lamellar thickness reduced to a minimum of 22 nm. Correspondingly, the sample’s microhardness and strength increased to 601 HV and 2.1 GPa, respectively, at 300℃. This anomalous phenomenon is related to the microstructural refinement determined by the diffusion of carbon atoms in martensite. The oversaturating carbon in martensite at room temperature results in its higher strength than ferrite. Thus, the martensite cannot be deformed sufficiently. Warm deformation at 300 ℃ can enhance the mobility of carbon atoms, leading to the segregation of carbon near the boundary of lamellar interface and dislocations. The segregated carbon atoms interact with defects to enhance the accumulation of dislocations, improving the thermal stability of nano-lamellar structure and helping grain refinement. Nevertheless, when the temperature increased to 500 ℃, carbon atoms were precipitated in the form of carbides, and the thickness of lamellar structure increased due to recovery and recrystallization. The results indicated that the interfacial segregation helps with enhancing thermal stability at the rolling temperature and promoting grain refinement. (3)Clarified the stress transfer and strain partition in the heterostructured dual-phase steel. In this project, in-situ SEM and DIC tests were carried out the clarify the strain partitioning and stress transfer in two heterostructured DP steels (HS740 and HS780). In HS740 steel, most of the ferrite grains are chained with each other, whereas the grains are mostly isolated by the hard F-M interfaces in HS780 steel. The mechanical incompatibility between ferrite and martensite results in significant strain partitioning and propagating strain bands, which are typical deformation characteristics of heterostructured dual-phase steels. The strain bands nucleate in the ferrite and then propagate along the preferential shear direction induced by the stress transfer from ferrite to martensite. In such a dual-phase heterostructure, ferrite first deforms plastically via dislocation slipping under the applied shear stress, whereas martensite remains elastic during this stage. GNDs inside the ferrite piles up at the F-M interfaces, producing back stress in the ferrite. Before martensite yields, internal stresses increase with straining, resulting in a stress concentration near the interfaces. Once the stress concentration reaches a critical level, the surrounding martensite is compelled to deform together with ferrite. As deformation proceeds, the strain bands propagate along the preferred shear orientation. In both HS740 and HS780 steels, the average partitioned strain of ferrite is larger than that of martensite, resulting in strain partitioning. It is found that volume fraction and distribution of constituent phases have great influences on the strain bands and strain partitioning. Higher VM and dispersed F-M lead to finer and denser strain bands in HS780 steel, as well as stronger strain partitioning. The larger strain partitioning produced larger strain gradient near F-M interfaces, leading to more GNDs pile-ups, and building up higher HDI stress. (4)Investigated the effects of shear bands on grain refinement of heterostructured dual-phase steel. Shear bands play a significant role in grain refinement of heterostructured dual-phase steel during deformation. In order to clarify the effects of shear bands on the grain refinement, the dual-phase structure was rolled at different temperatures (25-500 °C) with 80% thickness reduction. The results reveal that the formation of shear bands is related to the deformation compatibility between ferrite and martensite. At room temperature, the refinement of the martensitic phase is not sufficient because the strong martensitic phase only carries a small fraction of global plastic strain, which is induced by the significant stain partitioning. At elevated temperature to 300 °C, the deformation compatibility improves, resulting in the co-deformation of two phases, thus creating high density co-shear bands. This makes ferrite and martensite carry large plastic strain, promoting grain refinement. At higher temperature of 500 °C, stretched microstructure along the rolling direction formed due to the co-deformation of ferrite and martensite, but with a decrease in the shear band’s density. (5)Developed a low-cost processing route for making nano-steels, and to establish an industrial procedure or guidelines for the production of high strength nano-steels. Ultrastrong materials can notably help with improving the energy efficiency of transportation vehicles by reducing their weight. Grain refinement by severe plastic deformation is, so far, the most effective approach to produce bulk strong nanostructured metals, but its scaling up for industrial production has been a challenge. In this project, we produced the ultrastrong low-carbon nanosteel (>2 GPa) through commercial warming rolling under a lower equivalent strain. Two typical rolling methods are proposed in this project, i.e., warm rolling and cyclic annealing & cold rolling, to produce the bulk nano steel. The underlying grain refinement mechanisms of these methods are: (i) improving deformation compatibility of dual-phase heterostructure by adjusting warm rolling temperature and (ii) segregating carbon atoms to lamellar boundaries to stabilize the nanolamellae. This kind of approach is applicable to most low-carbon, low-alloy steels for producing ultrahigh strength materials in industrial scale.

As a result, extra strain hardening was produced, resulting in the enhanced mechanical properties. (2) Stress transfer and strain partitioning induced by mechanical incompatibility Mechanical incompatibility between ferrite and martensite results in significant strain partitioning and propagating strain bands, which are typical characteristics of heterostructured dual-phase steels during deformation. Volume fraction of martensite and distribution of constituent phases have great influences on the strain bands and strain partitioning. Higher VM and dispersed F-M lead to finer and denser strain bands, as well as stronger strain partitioning. This produces larger strain gradient near F-M interfaces, leading to more GNDs pile-ups, and building up higher HDI stress. (3) Interfacial segregation promotes grain refinement of low carbon steel The microstructural refinement of dual-phase steel is determined by the diffusion of carbon atoms in martensite. The oversaturating carbon in martensite at room temperature results in its higher strength than ferrite. Thus, the martensite cannot be deformed sufficiently. Warm deformation at 300 ℃ can enhance the mobility of carbon atoms, leading to the segregation of carbon near the lamellar interfaces and dislocations. The segregated carbon atoms enhance the accumulation of dislocations and improve the thermal stability of nanostructure, thus helping with grain refinement. (4) Developed a low-cost procedure for producing bulk Nano steels In this project, we produced the ultrastrong low-carbon nanosteel (>2 GPa) through commercial warming rolling under a lower equivalent strain than conventional severe plastic deformation methods. The underlying grain refinement mechanisms are: (i) improving deformation compatibility of dual-phase heterostructure by adjusting warm rolling temperature and (ii) segregating carbon atoms to lamellar boundaries to stabilize the nanostructure. This kind of approach is applicable to most low-carbon, low-alloy steels for producing ultrahigh strength materials in industrial scale.

11214121.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11214121.value: The dual-phase heterostructure can significantly improve the strength-ductility synergy of the low carbon steel. The improved mechanical properties result from the synergetic interaction of the soft and hard zones. It is found the dispersed micro shear bands are typical deformation characteristic of the heterostructured DP steels. It can suppress strain localization and improve ductility. However, the nucleation, propagation and mutual interactions of the micro shear bands are not clear. Therefore, the future research would focus on the inter-zone synergetic effects induced by the interactions of heterogeneous zones. Advanced in-situ ECCI, TEM and finite element modeling will be used to explore the underlying mechanisms related to the dispersed micro shear bands. In addition, the potential industrial applications of the high-strength nano and heterostructured DP steels should be explored in the further development.

11214121.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11214121.value: This project proposes a novel "two-step" method for comprehensively strengthening and toughening low-carbon low-alloy steels. First, thermally driven control regulates the distribution of interstitial carbon atoms, which interact strongly with deformation defects, stabilize the nanostructure, and significantly enhance grain refinement efficiency. Bulk nanocrystalline low-carbon low-alloy steel sheets can be produced using industrial rolling technology, enabling substantial improvements in material strength limits while strictly controlling raw material costs. Second, based on structural design criteria for heterostructured materials, appropriate heat treatment processing routes are explored to develop heterostructured dual-phase steels. The coupling deformation of soft-hard components is fully leveraged to provide additional strain hardening, thereby substantially increasing both strength and ductility. Through this pioneering research project, a more comprehensive understanding of the potential strengthening and toughening mechanisms in nano and heterostructured steel materials can be achieved. A key feature of this project is its focus on frontier scientific challenges in metal materials, flexible application of traditional basic strengthening and toughening theories, and expansion of research on high-performance nano and heterostructured steels using novel insights and methods.

11214221.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11214221.value: 過去十年來，住宅和辦公樓的能源成本不斷上漲，加上對環保建築的追求，建築設計師們非常關注如何改進和節約能源。據估計，建築部門約佔用電量的76%，40%的能源消耗與溫室氣體排放有關。因此，對更環保的建築和隔熱材料的需求及減少建築物的能源負荷更是日益增長。噴霧聚氨酯泡沫 （SPF）能提高住宅和商業建築能源效率，是最經濟高效的手段。其在住宅和商業建築中帶來的得益尢為出色。而且它具備良好的耐化學性、高強度與重量比、低密度、低導熱性（於0.017-0.023）、成本效益和相對高效節能源的特性。此外， SPF 對弱酸和鹼具有抗預能力。因此，在極端環境中有很好的表現。然而，阻燃性差以及SPF在火災中釋放出濃煙和有毒揮發物，是它在應用上的主要挑戰，有可能在火災事故中，導致巨大的傷亡和經濟損失。本研究旨在開發一種新型阻燃SPF，能減少煙/毒氣的生成、且具備高隔熱性和出色的節能、結構完整特性。在本項目中，以磷改性二維碳異位素-石墨（GDY）為基礎，研發出PGDY/SPF複合物作為一種創新的阻燃劑。本研究的另一亮点是利用分子動力學（MD）和採用CFD大渦模拟（LES）配于熱解模型並結合多燃料燃燒算法，開創針對PGDY/SPF複合物阻燃材料的一企創新火場模型，並對其應用於建築火災情景進行綜合火災風險分析。

11215021.label: Realisation of objectives
11215021.value: The project concluded slightly earlier than the official completion date of August 31, 2024, as the Principal Investigator (PI) retired at the end of June 2024. Consequently, the project's total duration was shortened from the original 36 months to 34 months. In this case, finding a replacement for the PI was not deemed critical. Despite the shortened duration, the project's ultimate aims were largely achieved. The project's findings were disseminated at three prestigious conferences/symposiums in the tribology field and through three publications in international journals. Specific achievements of all objectives: Obj. 1) To acquire an in-depth understanding of the 3D-CTG patterns for enabling unidirectional oil flow to enhance oil replenishment. (Details in Conference Papers [C1, C2] and Paper [3] in Part C.) This objective was achieved through experimental studies. The three-dimensional comb tooth groove (3D-CTG) patterns were fabricated using femtosecond laser ablation on steel blocks. The geometric parameters of the comb teeth (length, width, depth) were examined and characterized using a white light interferometer. The movement of oil droplets on these surfaces was measured to determine spreading distance and velocity. The study detailed the relationship between groove parameters and oil transport properties, highlighting the importance of capillary forces and wettability gradients in achieving unidirectional oil flow. The capillary forces resulting from the gradient drive the oil flow, facilitating effective replenishment. Obj. 2) To update an existing optical elastohydrodynamic lubrication test rig to incorporate ball-on-raceway contact. (Details in Conference Paper [C3] and Paper [1] in Part C.) We modified the conventional optical ball-on-disk tester by replacing the original single-ball structure with three equidistant balls, creating a multi-point optical lubricating film thickness test rig resembling a thrust ball bearing. This test rig can easily accommodate more balls if needed. Film thickness was measured by optical interferometry, evaluating the effect of the wettability gradient created on either side of the lubrication track. The multi-point optical lubricating film thickness test rig allows for observing the oil replenishment process. Obj. 3) To optimize the 3D-CTG patterns design from the perspective of multi-scale surface morphology and the depth of the grooves to increase lubricating film generation under limited lubricant supply (LLS). (Details in Conference Papers [C1, C2] and Paper [3] in Part C.) Varying the geometric parameters such as groove length, depth, and width creates multi-scale surface morphology that significantly affects oil droplet movement. The optimal groove parameters that enhance capillary forces to increase spreading velocity and driving force for oil droplets were determined. Results showed that deeper grooves initially increase transport velocity but can decrease it if excessively deep, indicating an optimal depth for effective oil transport. The optimal CTG patterns were ablated on the inner ring raceway of bearings, which were subsequently tested for friction torque and temperature rise under different speeds and loads with limited oil supply (LLS). Bearings with CTG-patterned surfaces exhibited lower friction torque and temperature rise under LLS conditions, indicating better performance and reduced wear. Tests using an optical ball-on-disk test rig measured lubricating film thickness, showing that CTG patterns improve film thickness, particularly under high-speed conditions and with high-viscosity oils. The CTG surface effectively directs oil back to the lubrication track and reduces oil leakage, improving lubrication under starved conditions. Obj. 4) To build a lubrication model (incorporating elastohydrodynamic effect, surface effect and partial oil/air mixture films) and develop an efficient procedure to theoretically explain the experimental findings. (Details in Conference Paper [C3] and Papers [1, 2] in Part C.) The model incorporates CTG domains on either side of the lubrication track to create a wettability gradient, dragging oil droplets towards the track. The surface is modelled with an oleophilic lubrication track sandwiched between oleophobic domains. Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) was used to simulate the unidirectional spreading of oil droplets, with the FLUENT package solving three-dimensional Navier-Stokes and continuity equations using a Volume of Fluid model. The simulation showed that oil droplets spread preferentially in the entrainment direction on the oleophilic track compared to a non-patterned surface. The unidirectional driving forces provided by the oleophobic areas on either side of the track drag the oil back towards the track, enhancing the spreading in the entrainment direction. The spreading speed is influenced by the difference in wettability between the oleophobic and oleophilic areas. High-viscosity oils exhibited slower spreading in the entrainment direction. Oil droplets off the patterned track centerline struggle to replenish in time. Deviation distance from the track centerline and oil viscosity are critical factors limiting oil replenishment. Overall, the simulated results agree with the experimental findings, validating the effectiveness of CTG patterns in enhancing lubrication through unidirectional oil flow. However, we deviated from our initial plan by not conducting the starved elastohydrodynamic lubrication (EHL) analysis. Instead, we focused on an experimental study of oil droplet lubrication. A recent theoretical study conducted by our research group# on LLS lubrication revealed that supplying oil to EHL contacts in the form of droplets outperformed a uniform layer of oil. The finding aligns with the practical experience of the superiority of air-oil lubrication, which involves impacting oil droplets on bearing contacts. To better understand LLS lubrication, we slightly adjusted our focus to study the effect of oil droplet distribution. We examined the key characteristics of oil spreading under controlled oil droplet supply. Specifically, we focused on the impact of symmetrically arranged double oil drop pairs around the central axis of the bearing track. Key factors examined include oil viscosity, entrainment velocity, and droplet distribution. Results showed that a single oil droplet increased central film thickness. In contrast, properly distributed double droplets led to a more uniform thickness across the surface. Low-viscosity oils were easier to facilitate the formation of convergent oil pools, leading to a full film in the contact area. High entrainment speeds limited oil droplet merging, reducing the effectiveness of capillary forces and spreading. # Li S., Guo F., Wong P.L. and Li X., “Numerical analysis of lubrication of conformal contact with discontinuous oil droplets”, Tribology International, 173, 107632, Sep. 2022. Obj. 5) To design and commission a rolling bearing prototype with 3d-CTG patterns for LLS. (Details can be found in Conference Papers [C2, C3] and Papers [1, 3] in Part C.) A self-aligning bearing was selected to fabricate the CTG surface on its inner ring raceway, resulting in a new structure named replenishment-augmented rolling element bearings (RaREB). The process began by running the bearing for two hours under high-speed and high-load conditions to identify the bearing track through wear marks on the raceway. The bearing was disassembled, and the inner ring was mounted onto a four-degree-of-freedom platform driven by a stepping motor. CTG patterns were ablated on both sides of the lubrication track. The bearing’s parts are cleaned and dried, creating wettability gradients on both sides of the lubrication track. The new inner ring was then reassembled with the other bearing components, resulting in a bearing with an oleophilic track (the original bearing steel surface) sandwiched by two CTG arrays. Four bearings were tested simultaneously on a bearing tester under LLS conditions. The findings demonstrate that the 3D-CTG surface enhanced lubrication and reduced bearing friction under starvation or LLS conditions. A rolling bearing prototype incorporating 3D-CTG patterns was successfully designed and commissioned.

11215021.label: Major findings and research outcome
11215021.value: 1. Enhancing Bearing Lubrication with 3D-CTG Patterned Surfaces (Paper [3]) Our research has successfully investigated the unidirectional movement of oil droplets on 3D-CTG patterned surfaces through experiments and CFD modelling. This study allowed us to determine the optimal groove parameters that enhance oil droplets' spreading velocity and driving force. The effectiveness of these new 3D-CTG patterns in enhancing oil replenishment for improved bearing lubrication was demonstrated through a series of bearing tests conducted under limited lubricant supply (LLS) conditions. 3D-CTG patterns were accurately ablated on the inner raceway of real rolling element bearings. The results revealed significant benefits, including a reduction in friction torque and temperature during bearing operations under LLS conditions. 2. A New Multi-Point Optical EHL Test Rig for Enhanced Bearing Analysis (Paper [1]) We have successfully developed a novel optical EHL test rig resembling a thrust ball bearing. Unlike conventional optical EHL test rigs, which typically facilitate only a single-bearing contact, this innovative design incorporates multi-point contacts. The multi-point contact design provides a more stable structure, enabling the test rig to withstand high loads and ensuring accurate and reliable testing under various load conditions. Additionally, the configuration increases the frequency of bearing roll-over at each contact point for a given rolling speed, allowing for improved analysis and evaluation of bearing lubrication performance. 3. Understanding of Oil Droplet Lubrication (Paper [2]) Previous theoretical research indicated that supplying oil to EHL contacts in droplet form outperforms a uniform oil layer, aligning with the practical experience of air-oil lubrication. To understand LLS lubrication, we studied the effect of oil droplet distribution. The study involved examining oil spreading characteristics under a controlled droplet supply. Results showed that a single oil droplet increased the central film thickness, while properly distributed double droplets led to a more uniform thickness across the surface. Low-viscosity oils facilitated the formation of convergent oil pools, ensuring a full film in the contact area. High entrainment speeds hindered droplet merging, reducing the effectiveness of capillary forces and spreading, ultimately resulting in shorter lubrication times and inadequate film formation due to starvation. 4. A New Rolling Element Bearing Structure (Paper [1, 3]) We successfully designed and commissioned a rolling bearing prototype incorporating 3D-CTG patterns, named replenishment-augmented rolling element bearings (RaREB). The 3D-CTG surface significantly enhanced lubrication and reduced bearing friction under LLS conditions, demonstrating the potential for significant advancements in lubrication technology and bearing performance.

11215021.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11215021.value: This project has demonstrated the potential of 3D-CTG patterns to enhance bearing performance under limited lubricant supply (LLS) conditions. However, several areas require further investigation. Firstly, the development of the lubrication model incorporating elastohydrodynamic lubrication (EHL) effects, surface effects, and partial oil/air mixture films should be completed to explain the experimental findings theoretically. Secondly, the impact of different ablation process parameters on the wettability of the patterns needs to be investigated. Thirdly, it is important to broaden the application scope of CTG patterns on different bearing types and other components to assess potential performance improvements. Lastly, the research has primarily examined short-term lubrication performance, leaving gaps in understanding the longevity and reliability of CTG-patterned bearings, so it is necessary to conduct long-term durability tests. By addressing these areas, the research can further optimize the performance of CTG-patterned bearings and explore broader applications, leading to significant advancements in lubrication technology.

11215021.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11215021.value: In advanced bearing applications, it is widely accepted that using less oil for lubrication is beneficial. Making the most of the available lubricant is a common goal. This project proposes a new surface pattern called the 3-dimensional comb tooth groove (3D-CTG), which can greatly improve bearing performance and lubrication efficiency. This helps the bearings last longer and work more reliably. An array of triangular comb tooth grooves creates a surface with a wettability gradient where oil spreads more effectively. When an oil droplet falls anywhere on this pattern, it gets moved by the surface forces. This new design is superior to the simple wettability step design, which requires oil droplets to land exactly where two different wettability surface areas meet. The project also figured out the best pattern design for maximizing oil replenishment in the bearing. This led to a new type of bearing called replenishment-augmented rolling element bearings (RaREB). The idea is to add the 3D-CTG patterns on both sides of the bearing track. When oil lands on these patterns, the surface forces move it towards the track, improving oil replenishment. Tests with the new bearings confirmed that they were successfully designed and worked as intended.

11215121.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11215121.value: Optical characterization techniques operating in the UV-Vis-NIR spectral range offer great potential to design powerful and affordable in-situ and in-operando (ISIO) strategies that can be of use, for example, to better understand the complex dynamic processes in green energy applications such as rechargeable batteries, fuel cells, catalysis, and others. However, despite much consensus on their advantages and opportunities, so far optical ISIO techniques remain underused and underdeveloped. We will use the synergetic and complementary expertise of the research team to overcome this stalemate by developing sensitivity-enhancing strategies for optical ISIO techniques based on optical cavity, plasmonic, and nanostructured effects. These sensitivity-enhancing strategies will then be applied to correlated spectroscopic ellipsometry (SE) and Raman spectroscopy (RS) as synergetic and complimentary optical techniques to study the evolution of the electrode–electrolyte interface in electrochemical processes. Furthermore, we will apply the knowledge generated to advanced optical strategies such as imaging, ultrafast (100 fs) and vacuum UV (6-35 eV) SE enabling detail information to unravel, for example, the reaction pathway selectivity in catalytic applications. Short-range chemical order can be identified from the vibrational spectrum signature of materials measured by RS, to unravel the chemical phase evolution of bulk phases and interfaces. Meanwhile, SE measures changes in the polarization of light after being reflected from a sample. Because ellipsometry is phase-sensitive and self-referenced, it is capable of high-precision measurements of, for example, thickness changes of a fraction of a monolayer. SE measurements thus determine the thickness evolution and spectral optical properties, (n,k) as function of wavelength, which are sensitive to several material properties including, for example, composition, density, and phase. The correlation of SE with RS is thus highly synergetic: RS provides additional information on chemical phases, which assist in the development of the SE optical models, while the SE models help to elucidate the location (i.e., depth) of the phases identified with RS. The correlated ISIO RS-SE to be developed will provide important insights on the processes that occur at electrochemical interfaces, such as changes in structure, composition, and morphology, phase transitions, and surface chemical state evolution including adsorption and interface formation. They are intensively used in a wide range of scientific and industrial fields (e.g., medicine, pharmacology, food, bioengineering). In the medium to short term, we foresee that multidisciplinary efforts will be able to take advantage of the developed strategies, e.g., in artificial photosynthesis, protein film voltammetry, and transparent battery materials. 紫外-可見-近紅外光譜的光學表徵原位策略擁有功能強大且價格合理的發展潛力，例如，可以用作研究綠色能源應用中的複雜動態過程，包括可充電電池、燃料電池、催化等。 然而，儘管普遍認同其優勢和機會，但迄今為止，光學原位技術仍未得到充分利用和發展。 我們將透過研究團隊的合作和專業知識互補，透過開發基於共振腔、等離子體和納米結構效應的光學原位靈敏度增強策略來克服這弱點。 這些靈敏度增強策略將應用於相關光譜橢偏和拉曼光譜技術，作為協同和互補的光學技術來研究電化學過程中電極-電解質界面的演變。此外，我們將把相關知識應用於先進的光學策略，如成像、超快 (100 fs) 和真空紫外橢偏儀 (6-35 eV)，從而了解更詳細的信息，例如催化應用中的反應途徑選擇性。 通過拉曼光譜測量，可從材料的振動光譜特徵中識別化學短程序，以解開體相和界面的化學相演變。 同時，光譜橢偏儀測量光從樣品反射後的偏振變化。由於橢偏儀具有相位敏感和自參考特性，因此能夠提供高精度測量, 例如單層的一小部分的厚度變化。因此，光譜橢偏儀能測量厚度變化和光譜光學特性(n,k)。(n,k)作為波長的函數，並對多種材料特性敏感，例如成分、密度和相位。因此，光譜橢偏儀與拉曼光譜的相關性是高度協同的：拉曼光譜提供了關於化學相的附加信息，這有助於光譜橢偏儀光學模型的開發，而光譜橢偏儀模型有助於闡明拉曼光譜識別的相位（即深度）。即將開發的原位拉曼光譜-光譜橢偏儀將為電化學界面上發生的過程提供重要信息，例如結構、組成和形態的變化、相變和表面化學狀態演變，包括吸附和界面形成。它們被廣泛應用於科學和工業領域（例如，醫學、藥理學、食品、生物工程）。在中短期內，我們預計已開發技術能應用於多學科領域，例如人工光合作用、蛋白質膜伏安法和透明電池材料。

11215621.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11215621.value: 建築能耗通常占不同地區總能耗的20-40%，而香港建築電耗的比例更是超過90%。可再生能源和廢熱廣泛用於節能減排，但能源供應的間歇性和建築負荷的時變性造成了供需匹配困難。蓄熱技術可有效實現供需平衡，將在建築節能中發揮重要作用。在各類蓄熱技術中，吸收式蓄能在蓄能密度、蓄能效率和蓄能溫度方面性能優異，且釋放的能量可靈活地用於供冷、供熱或除濕。這些優點均能夠促進可再生能源和廢熱在建築中的有效利用。 然而，吸收式蓄能系統的推廣應用需解決三大問題：(1) 提高反應器緊湊性以增大蓄能密度；(2) 降低蓄能溫度以利用常規系統無法利用的低溫熱源；(3)避免H2O/鹽工質對結晶以提高可靠性。因此，很有必要研發佔用空間小、投資成本低、能源效率高、無結晶風險的新型吸收式蓄能技術。為實現這些目標，本專案致力於研發微通道膜式納米離子液體反應器，用於高密度、低溫度和無結晶吸收式蓄能。該微通道膜式反應器具有較大的比表面積，並複合了溶液和製冷劑流體，能顯著提高系統的緊湊性。水分子在多孔膜中的直接擴散也可降低蓄能溫度。離子液體具有較低的熔點，是很有潛力的無結晶吸收劑。此外，納米離子液體和結構優化能進一步改善傳熱傳質和系統性能。 本項目將採用模擬和實驗方法開展如下研究：(1) 基於新型反應器的緊湊吸收式蓄能系統模型建立與樣機研發；(2) 新型反應器中雙向脫附/冷凝和吸收/蒸發過程的性能表徵與關聯擬合；(3) 新型吸收式蓄能系統的動態蓄能/釋能特性和迴圈性能研究；(4) 反應器結構的機器學習多目標優化以實現蓄能性能最優。所提研究對於小型化、高效率、無結晶吸收式蓄能的研發具有重要意義，能夠促進高效、經濟、低碳的蓄能技術在香港及全球的推廣。

11215621.label: Realisation of objectives
11215621.value: We set four project objectives and carried out a lot of activities focused on these objectives. These activities can contribute to (1) model development of the novel microchannel membrane-based ionanofluid reactor; (2) prototype development of the novel ATES module; (3) characterization of dynamic behaviors and storage performance for the novel ATES; (4) machine-learning multi-objective optimization of the reactor geometry. All the project objectives have been successfully achieved as planned, with details summarized as follows. 1. To develop the model of the compact ATES using the novel microchannel membrane-based ionanofluid reactor. In a typical membrane-based microchannel absorber, water vapor diffuses into the solution through the membrane-solution interface, driven by the pressure potential. The water vapor is absorbed by absorption working fluids, with both heat and mass transfer through the membrane. The novel reactor involves complex heat and mass transfer in the coupled desorption/ condensation and absorption/evaporation processes, occurring asynchronously in opposite directions. To guide the optimization of the absorber structural design as well as the screening of novel working fluids, we established a model of the membrane-based absorber using novel ionanofluid. It can be used to investigate the heat and mass transfer processes along the channel length, including the dynamic distribution of the temperature, velocity, and concentration in the solution channel. The property model of a wide range of novel ionanofluid has been established with proven high accuracy. The continuity, momentum, energy, and species transport equations are employed in the model. The partial pressure difference is a driving force, based on which the mass transfer flux across the membrane can be calculated. The simulation results were compared with the reference data. The temperatures predicted by the CFD model are in good agreement with the reference, and the maximum relative error is only approximately 0.1%. As for the pressure potential along the flow direction, the relative error is less than 1%. 2. To build the novel ATES prototype using the novel microchannel membrane-based ionanofluid reactor. A microchannel membrane-based module consists of four plates. The membrane is glued on the membrane support plate using the method from the reference. The four plates are assembled by screws and gaskets between plates. Based on the designed experimental loop, the developed experimental setup of a microchannel membrane-based absorber is further developed for performance measurement. This experimental setup is also suitable for the microchannel membrane-based desorber if it is replaced by a microchannel membrane-based desorber. For the absorber experiment, it requires stable inlet parameters, so three PID controllers are applied to regulate the entering solution/refrigerant/cooling water inlet temperatures. The solution feed tank supplies the solution with pre-mixed concentration while the solution recovery tank recovers the solution leaving the absorber. Temperature sensors, pressure transducers, flow meters, absorbent concentration meter are used to measure different streams. With these measurements, the heat transfer rate, absorption rate, and pressure drop can be obtained. Uncertainty analysis has been conducted for these derived performance indexes. These experimental studies have been used to validate the models and demonstrate the merits of the novel absorber including: enhanced performance, compactness, and crystallization-free operation. 3. To characterize the cycle performance and dynamic behaviors of the novel reactor and the ATES performance. This intensive research focused on establishing a robust and detailed set of empirical correlations that precisely describe the complex behaviors of heat transfer, mass transfer, and internal pressure drop dynamics within various compact absorber configurations. These newly derived relationships are important for the accurate design, advanced thermal analysis, and performance optimization of high-efficiency, compact absorbers and ATES systems. An experiments measured and quantified the influence of six key operational parameters, which includes the magnitude of the vapor pressure, solution temperature, solution concentration, solution flow velocity, cooling water temperature, and cooling water flow velocity. The resulting data yielded key operational insights, specifically revealing that the heat and mass transfer processes are substantially and positively affected by strategic adjustments, such as increasing the solution flow rate, elevating the driving force of the vapor pressure, boosting the solution concentration, or employing a lower cooling water temperature. Following a comprehensive statistical analysis of all gathered experimental data, new correlations were developed. These predictive equations address the Nusselt number (Nu) for heat transfer, the Sherwood number (Sh) for mass transfer, and the friction factor (f) for solution pressure drop, respectively. Rigorous validation procedures emphatically verified that these newly formulated correlations dramatically enhance the prediction accuracy. When compared directly to conventional correlations, the predictive accuracies for the overall heat transfer coefficient (U) are improved by an 72.39%, for the absorption rate (J) by 78.55%, and for the total pressure drop (DP) by 64.56%. This unparalleled level of predictive accuracy and reliability achieved by these correlations represents a highly significant contribution to the fundamental science and engineering practice involved in the effective design, thorough evaluation, and ultimate optimization of both efficient and compact ATES. 4. To optimize the reactor geometry for ATES improvement using machine-learning method. This research advances the development of compact ATES systems by applying Machine Learning (ML) techniques to both optimize the design and improve the predictive models of key membrane-based components. Firstly, the plate-and-frame membrane-based absorber was optimized using ML assisted by experimental design and CFD simulations. An Artificial Neural Network (ANN) model was selected for its high accuracy in performance prediction, which was then used in a multi-objective optimization to establish the Pareto front between absorption rate (J) and pressure drop (DP). The resulting optimized structures, identified via TOPSIS and LINMAP methods, demonstrated excellent performance trade-offs. For instance, the LINMAP-optimized case achieved a 1.41 times higher volumetric cooling capacity while reducing the pressure drop by 1.30 times compared to the base structure. Secondly, to address the limited accuracy of existing empirical correlations for microchannel membrane-based desorbers and absorbers, three ML methods—Random Forest (RF), LS-SVM, and GABPNN—were employed to develop superior predictive models for the Nusselt number (Nu), Sherwood number (Sh), and friction factor (f). Among these, the Random Forest method performed exceptionally well, achieving accuracy improvements of up to 30.47% for the friction factor over previous correlations. Furthermore, the RF model drastically enhanced the prediction accuracy for critical parameters like the overall heat transfer coefficient (U) and sorption rate (J), showing an improvement of 79.66% and 81.52% for the absorber, respectively. These combined ML-assisted efforts are crucial for facilitating the simulation, design, and ultimate optimization of more efficient and compact ATES systems.
