11215621.label: Major findings and research outcome
11215621.value: This project proposes to investigate and develop a microchannel membrane-based ionanofluid reactor for high-density, low-temperature, and crystallization-free ATES. For novel heat/mass components, we systematically compared the heat/mass transfer performance of various advanced absorbers/desorber. Results showed that the proposed novel membrane-based microchannel structure achieved the largest absorption rate of 0.015 kg/(m2·s), desorption rate of 0.0225 kg/(m2·s), volumetric cooling capacity of 1147 kW/m3, and coefficient of performance (COP) of 0.855. Based on these results, we designed and fabricated microchannel membrane-based absorbers/desorbers to increase the compactness of the reactor. We further developed a prototype of a microchannel membrane-based reactor with a cooling capacity of 0.5 kW. We then measured this 0.5 kW microchannel reactor on the testing platform established in the lab. Heat/mass transfer and pressure drop were measured and correlated for the microchannel membrane-based absorbers and desorbers. We further built enhanced channel structures and artificial-intelligence-assisted CFD optimization methods for geometry optimization, maldistribution minimization, and performance improvement. Based the proposed new methods in this project, the pressure drop of the microchannel membrane-based absorber can be significantly reduced by 6.3 times and the mass flux can be increased by 55%. As for novel working fluids, we aim to overcome the shortcomings of conventional H2O/salt absorption working fluids, for which the crystallization is always a big concern. To realize crystallization-free absorption cycles, novel H2O/ionic liquid mixtures were screened using high-accuracy models. Considering that H2O/IL may have high viscosity that would degrade heat/mass transfer, so nanoparticles were dispersed in the ILs (called ionanofluid) to strengthen the heat/mass transfer and thus increase the desorption rate in the charging process and absorption rate in the discharging process. We developed a machine-learning-based multi-scale molecular design to look for high-performance H2O/ionic liquids. The quantitative relationship between the molecular structure, H2O/ionic liquid mixture, and cycle performance was established. From 26360 candidates, the best-performing ILs were identified under 18 operating conditions. Furthermore, we developed a multi-criteria approach to rationally screen a wide variety of refrigerants (H2O, NH3, methanol, acetone, DME) paired with 44 ionic liquids, considering cycle performance, heat transfer, hydraulic resistance, and applicable range. H2O/[OMIM][OAc] and NH3/[DBIM][Tf2N] were found to have excellent performance comprehensively. Furthermore, we investigated the performance of microchannel membrane-based absorption heat pumps using different H2O/ionic liquids under various working conditions. Results show that under a desired cooling capacity of 0.5 kW, [EMIM][OAc] and [EMIM][OMs] can yield higher COPs. LiBr is the best choice with the targeted COPs below 0.778, while [EMIM][OAc], [EMIM][OMs], and [BMIM][BF4] perform better with the targeted COPs above 0.778. The outcomes are significant for developing a novel and compact ATES towards efficient and affordable low-carbon building technologies.

11215621.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11215621.value: The proposed novel microchannel membrane-based absorber using ionanofluid is significant for the development of compact, low-cost and crystallization-free ATES, facilitating efficient and affordable low-carbon heating and cooling technologies in various scenarios (e.g., buildings, data center, battery thermal management, etc.) in the future. The results and findings of this project will motivate further research on novel ATES components and systems. Wide commercialization and applications of this technology will greatly cut the fossil fuel consumption and GHG emissions. It can help the Hong Kong Government realize the target to reduce the carbon intensity by 65-70% from the 2005 level by 2030 and achieve carbon neutrality by 2050. The success of this project will contribute towards sustainable buildings and societies in Hong Kong and all over the world. In 1-5 years, our research team will collaborate with relevant institutes and manufacturers to deepen the research and promote the development. In 5-10 years, our research team will collaborate with relevant enterprises and building users to promote better applications and further improve the energy saving effects. Over 10 years. our research team will collaborate with relevant governmental departments and NGOs to promote wider applications of this technology to maximize long-term energy saving and emission mitigation.

11215621.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11215621.value: This research project focuses on improving the compactness and addressing the crystallization problem for the absorption thermal energy storage (ATES) systems through innovative design and optimization techniques. The project achieved four key objectives: (1) developing a model for a novel microchannel membrane-based ionanofluid reactor, which enhances heat and mass transfer, (2) building a prototype of the ATES module to test the system’s performance, (3) characterizing the cycle performance and dynamic behaviors of the reactor to optimize its efficiency, and (4) applying machine learning for multi-objective optimization of reactor geometry to improve absorption rates and reduce pressure drop. The project's significance lies in its ability to enhance the performance and compactness of ATES systems, contributing to more efficient energy storage. By integrating new materials, experimental setups, and optimization methods, this research addresses key challenges such as heat transfer, crystallization-free operation, and pressure drop reduction. The outcomes of this project offer valuable insights for designing more efficient, compact, and cost-effective ATES systems, with potential applications in renewable energy integration and sustainable heating and cooling technologies.

11216421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11216421.value: Soft millirobots that can leverage controllable drug delivery is of great interest for future biomedical applications owing to their features in tiny size, soft nature, and untethered control. Although recent success in sophisticated multimodal locomotion, however, the biodegradability and programmable drug release capacities of millirobot remains a big challenge. Such issue has been the major bottleneck of further applying the millirobot in practice in biomedical engineering, especially for the latest combination therapy, which is advocated as a cornerstone for various diseases medical treatments, e.g., ulcerative colitis, colorectal cancer, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and wound healing. This project aims at proposing a nanofiber-based, magnetically powered, pH-responsive, and biodegradable soft millirobot (Fibot) to address the stepwise combination therapy. Distinct from the conventional methods, we intend to develop a bottom-up magnetic field assisted electrospun platform to construct the Fibot with a soft membrane body and multi-legs. Here, both the soft body and the tapered legs will be fabricated from non-cytotoxic biodegradable materials (Eudragit L100 and Eudragit S100 for the nanofiber-based membrane; Eudragit L100-55 and iron microparticles for the legs) and different drugs can be embedded in the body and legs during the fabrication process simultaneously. By adjusting the material ratio of the body and legs, we can controllably degrade them at different pH values, offering a solution for the stepwise combination therapy. The iron microparticles embedded legs will allow the Fibot to be actuated effectively by external magnetic, via which the Fibot can achieve multimodal locomotion and adapt to the harsh bio-environment. After verifying the biodegradable and locomotion ability of the Fibot, we will design the in vitro experiment to test the stepwise combination therapy ability of the Fibot, including the bacteriostatic therapy, alimentary cancer against, and so on. Compared with the state-of-arts, our proposed method will provide a new insight for biodegradable soft millirobot design and fabrication. The Fibot with lower limbs and membrane body will yield versatile locomotion ability at harsh bio-environment, programmable stepwise degradation, and drug release ability response to the variation of acidic physiological concentrations. The robot’s biocompatibility/biodegradability and precise locomotion control offers great opportunity for several kinds of disease therapy, such as tumor and thrombectomy, which is expected to generate long-term impact in robotic as well as biomedical engineering field. 能夠用於藥物輸送的微型機器人在生物醫學應用中受到極大關注，但微型機器人的生物降解性和可程式設計藥物釋放能力仍面臨巨大挑戰。該專案旨在研究一種基於納米纖維、磁驅動和pH回應的可生物降解柔性微型機器人。與傳統方法不同，本專案擬開發一種自底向上的磁場輔助電紡平臺，研發由微納米纖維編織而成的多足軟體機器人。 首先，機器人本體將由無細胞毒性、生物可降解的材料製成（用於納米纖維基膜的Eudragit L100和Eudragit S100;用於腿部的Eudragit L100-55和鐵微粒）。不同的藥物可以在製造過程中包裹在身體和腿的內部。 通過調整身體和腿部的材料比例，我們可以在不同的pH值下控制機器人的降解，為聯合釋藥治療提供解決方案。嵌入腿部的鐵微粒，將使機器人能由外部磁場驅動，從而實現多模態運動來適應惡劣的生物環境。在驗證機器人的生物可降解性和運動能力后，我們將設計體外實驗來測試機器人的應用前景，包括抑菌治療、抗消化道腫瘤等。該專案的順利實施，可為生物可降解軟微機器人的設計和製造提供新的思路，併為多種疾病治療提供潛在方案，如靶向治療、局部炎症治療等，預計將在機器人和生物醫學工程領域產生長期影響。

11216421.label: Realisation of objectives
11216421.value: With the support of this project, we proposed and verified Fibot could be a promising platform for intelligent, targeted, and safe combination therapy, providing strong evidence for its translational potential in clinical applications. All the objectives have been fully achieved, as detailed below: Objective 1: Development of the bottom‑up magnetic field‑assisted electrospun platform for the construction of robot with a soft membrane body and multi-legs (100% achieved) We successfully established a bottom up magnetic field assisted coaxial electrospinning platform to fabricate the Fibot prototype. The platform was composed of a micropump (KDS100, USA) for solution propulsion and a high voltage DC power supply (Dongwen, Tianjin, China) for electrospinning. A coaxial stainless steel needle with an internal diameter of 0.4 mm was employed to deliver core and shell solutions with high precision. Core shell nanofibers were prepared from shell solutions at concentrations of 10 wt% and 16 wt%, under applied voltages ranging from 7.5 to 13.5 kV, with a working distance of 20 cm. The resulting fibers exhibited stable morphology, with outer diameters of approximately 220 ± 5 μm and inner diameters of 560 ± 5 μm. The Fibot’s membrane body achieved a thickness of 450–500 μm, ensuring both mechanical stability and flexibility. To integrate the multi legged array, a permanent magnet was positioned beneath a 10 cm × 10 cm aluminum foil substrate to support magnet drug composite legs during fiber deposition. The legs, fabricated from EL100 55 containing iron particles, were designed with taper angles of ~23° and gap distances of ~2.5 mm, optimized to balance locomotion and body support. After solidification, the legs were extracted and transferred to a thin foil substrate. Under the induction of the high voltage DC electric field, positively charged nanofibers were wrapped around the negatively charged legs, forming a robust body leg assembly. The completed Fibot was dried in an oven at 25 °C for 6 hours to ensure reproducibility and long term stability. Objective 2: Fibot’s controllable stepwise degradation by adjusting the material ratio of the membrane body and legs (100% Achieved) In order to realize stepwise drug release, we designed Fibot’s body and multi legged array using heterogeneous biodegradable materials with distinct pH responsive degradation properties. The membrane body was fabricated from EL100/ES100 coaxial nanofibers (core–sheath structure), while the legs were prepared from EL100 55 composites containing iron particles. This material differentiation enabled the body and legs to respond differently under varying pH conditions, thereby achieving controllable sequential degradation. To verify this functionality, fluorescein isothiocyanate (FITC) was incorporated into the magnet drug composite legs, and Keyacid Blue (KAB) was embedded into the membrane body. Fibot’s body samples (nanofiber membranes, 3.5 cm × 3.5 cm) were immersed in 3 ml phosphate buffer solutions (PBS) with pH values ranging from 1.2 to 7.0, and incubated at 37 °C under 90 rpm shaking. Similarly, single leg samples were placed in 1 ml buffer solutions within PDMS grooves (1.5 cm³ volume) and incubated under identical conditions. Experimental observations using fluorescence microscopy and handheld imaging confirmed that under acidic environments (pH ≤ 5.0), both body and legs remained stable, maintaining morphology and preventing premature drug leakage. This stability is critical for avoiding toxicity to non target organs. When exposed to environments with pH ≥ 5.5, the leg modules gradually dissolved, releasing embedded drugs in a sustained manner for more than 40 minutes. Meanwhile, the membrane body exhibited slower degradation kinetics, ensuring sequential release between leg embedded and body embedded drugs. Objective 3: To develop the robot actuation system and realize the effective Fibot locomotion at harsh bio-environment (100% Achieved) To evaluate the locomotion control ability of Fibot under physiologically relevant conditions, we conducted ex‑vivo experiments using pig stomach tissue, which presents a complex and heterogeneous surface environment. For systematic assessment, the stomach surface was divided into three regions: flat areas (region i), crease areas (region ii), and target areas (region iii). Fibot was actuated by external magnetic guidance, with a magnetic field strength of approximately 100 mT, frequency of 1 Hz, and the magnet positioned 5 cm beneath the tissue surface. Under these conditions, Fibot successfully traversed regions i and ii, covering a total distance of ~150 mm in approximately 160 seconds. The robot employed a combination of flap‑wave and inverted‑pendulum motions, demonstrating adaptability to both smooth and folded tissue geometries. Upon reaching the target region (pH > 6.8), Fibot exhibited its programmed degradation behavior. Most of the structural components dissolved, leaving only pure iron particles, thereby confirming the robot’s ability to perform targeted delivery and subsequent clearance. The experiments demonstrated that Fibot maintained stable locomotion across heterogeneous surfaces and achieved controlled degradation at the destination site. Objective 4: Protype and verify its stepwise combination therapy ability by in-vitro experiments (100% achieved) We developed the prototype of the Fibot and verifying its stepwise combination therapy capability through controlled in‑vitro and complementary in‑vivo experiments. In the in-vitro test, stepwise release was validated by immersing Fibot samples in buffer solutions of varying pH values (1.2–7.0) under controlled incubation at 37 °C. Fluorescent tracers were used to monitor release kinetics. Results confirmed that Fibot remained stable under acidic conditions (pH ≤ 5.0), preventing premature leakage. At pH ≥ 5.5, the leg modules degraded gradually, releasing embedded agents over more than 40 minutes, while the membrane body exhibited slower degradation, ensuring sequential release. These findings demonstrated the feasibility of controllable stepwise combination therapy in vitro. In the in-vivo experiment, Fibot was tested in a 24‑hour fasted rabbit model to further validate its multifunctional performance. Radiology imaging confirmed that Fibot successfully navigated the ropy and acidic gastric environment and entered the intestine. Upon reaching the target intestinal region (pH ~5.8), a magnetic gradient of 5 T/m was applied to anchor Fibot to the intestinal tissue. Time‑lapse imaging showed stable positioning over 4 hours, with mean gray values increasing from 132 at 0 h to 145 at 4 h, indicating progressive degradation.

11216421.label: Major findings and research outcome
11216421.value: This project successfully achieved all proposed objectives, leading to the development of Fibot, a nanofiber‑based biodegradable multi‑legged millirobot with controllable stepwise drug release and locomotion capabilities. A bottom‑up magnetic field‑assisted coaxial electrospinning platform was established to fabricate EL100/ES100 core‑shell nanofibers and integrate them with magnet‑drug composite legs. Through systematic optimization, Fibot was constructed with reproducible morphology, balanced structural support, and reliable locomotion potential. By employing heterogeneous biodegradable materials, Fibot demonstrated distinct pH‑responsive degradation between its body and legs. In vitro tests confirmed stability under acidic conditions (pH ≤ 5.0), preventing premature leakage, while at pH ≥ 5.5 the legs gradually dissolved to release embedded drugs over more than 40 minutes. The membrane body degraded more slowly, ensuring sequential release of therapeutic agents and validating controllable stepwise combination therapy. Locomotion control was verified in ex‑vivo pig stomach models, where Fibot traversed ~150 mm across flat and folded regions under magnetic guidance (~100 mT, 1 Hz). It adapted to heterogeneous surfaces using flap‑wave and inverted‑pendulum motions, reaching target regions (pH > 6.8) and degrading most components while leaving only iron particles. These results confirmed its ability to navigate complex biological environments and deliver drugs precisely. Finally, in‑vivo rabbit experiments demonstrated versatile locomotion, anchoring, and degradation. Radiology imaging showed stable positioning under a 5 T/m magnetic gradient for 4 hours, with progressive degradation indicated by increasing mean gray values. Histological analysis revealed anchoring depths of ~175 μm confined to the mucosa, avoiding deeper penetration and showing no inflammation, thereby confirming safety and biocompatibility. Collectively, these outcomes establish Fibot as a proof‑of‑concept platform for intelligent, targeted, and safe combination therapy, providing strong evidence for translational potential in gastrointestinal drug delivery and broader biomedical applications. With the support of this project, six journal papers have been published and one PhD student has been trained.

11216421.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11216421.value: Future work will focus on optimizing drug loading and release kinetics, expanding in‑vivo validation in larger animal models, and integrating advanced magnetic guidance systems to enhance navigation accuracy. Scaling up fabrication and establishing standardized protocols will be pursued to support translational studies and eventual clinical application. The proposed course of action is to refine Fibot’s design, strengthen safety and efficacy data, and initiate collaborations with medical institutions to explore regulatory pathways and commercialization opportunities.

11216421.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11216421.value: This project created a very small, soft robot, called Fibot, that can move inside the stomach and intestines and release medicine in a safe and controlled way. Fibot is made from special materials that slowly break down in the body. Its design allows medicine to be released step by step: one part of the robot lets go of the drug first, and another part releases it later, depending on the body’s environment. In simple tests, Fibot stayed stable in strong acid, like in the stomach, and only started releasing medicine when it reached gentler conditions, like in the intestine. In animal studies, Fibot was able to travel through the stomach, anchor itself gently to the intestinal wall using a magnet, and then slowly break down while releasing medicine. Importantly, the anchoring did not cause damage or inflammation, showing that it is safe. The value of this research is that it shows a new way to deliver medicines directly to the right place in the body, at the right time, and in the right order. Fibot could help treat diseases such as digestive problems, cancer, or diabetes more effectively and with fewer side effects.

11217221.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11217221.value: Nanorobotic manipulation based on transmission/scanning electron microscope (TEM/SEM) has been developed into a versatile tool for both fundamental research and applications of nanomaterials, structures, and simple devices. The objective of this project is to investigate advanced-device-level nanorobotic manipulation based prototyping and characterization inside a TEM with the assistance of chips prepared with SEM-based manipulation and assembly, focused-ion beam/electron-beam-induced deposition (FIB/EBID)-based deductive/additive fabrication, and conventional nanofabrication processes. Aiming at developing an advanced manipulation platform based on a TEM with chips and lasers for electromechanical and opto-electromechanical nanodevices, the following three tasks are planned: (1) Modeling and visual servo control of the nanomanipulator will be performed with a target of automatizing the precision processes. (2) Design, fabrication, calibration, and resolution transferring of a high-precision small-range cantilever-type position sensor to bridge the TEM and SEM/FIB with an objective to improve the positioning accuracy of the SEM-based manipulators beyond the imaging resolution of the SEM. (3) Nanorobotic manipulation and FIB installed with an SEM for prototyping of TEM-adaptable chips. This is to show how the SEM-based manipulators can be used for prototyping relative more complex devices than TEM-based ones can. Our effort leads a trend in the merging of TEM and SEM platforms by combining the extremely high resolution of the TEM and the much higher complexity of SEM-based manipulation. The combination has been bridged by common samples/chips at the current stage but with the potential of exchangeable manipulators. The proposed research will enable new technologies for the prototyping, design, modeling, simulation, fabrication, assembly, and in-situ characterization of nanodevices. The calibration of the positioning resolution of a nanorobotic manipulator inside an SEM using a high-precision small-range cantilever-type position sensor pre-calibrated inside a TEM can be extended into a universal method with much broader applications; solving the common conflict of high precision and small measurable range of advanced sensors. The plasmonic position sensors are proposed for the first time with the potentials to be used with an atomic force microscope for biomedical manipulation and measurements. The success of this project will pave a new avenue of platform merging for nanorobotic manipulation by enabling such applications as in-situ prototyping and characterization for fundamental research and rapid product development of nanoscale and quantum devices such as sensors, batteries, neuro-morphing devices, and neuro/brain interfaces. 基于透射/扫描电子显微镜（TEM/SEM）的纳米机器人操作已经发展成为纳米材料、结构和简单器件的基础及应用研究的多功能工具。本项目旨在研究先进的器件级纳米机器人操作技术，基于SEM中的纳米机器人操作与装配及聚焦离子束/电子束诱导沉积（FIB/EBID）的减材/增材制造以及传统纳米加工技术，在TEM内实现复杂器件的原型创成及原位表征。本项目将以研发一个基于TEM的带有芯片和激光器的先进操作平台为目标，计划针对机电和光机电纳米器件进行以下三项工作：(1)纳米操作机的建模和视觉伺服控制，目标是实现精操作的自动化；(2) 设计并加工高精度小量程微悬臂式位移传感器，并在TEM中进行超高精度标定，以共享传感器的方式实现向SEM/FIB的分辨率传递，目标是实现超越SEM本身成像分辨率的定位精度；(3) 基于SEM中的纳米机器人操作系统和FIB，实现适于TEM应用的芯片的原型创成。这些操作将展示通过基于TEM和SEM平台的纳米操作系统的融合，可将TEM的极高分辨率和基于SEM的高复杂性操作有效地结合起来，实现单一平台无法兼顾的优势。这种融合将首先通过共享样品/芯片搭起桥梁，未来将进一步发展为具有可交换共享操作机的高度融合形态。本项目将使纳米器件的原型创成、设计、建模、仿真、加工、组装和原位表征的一系列新技术成为可能。使用在TEM内预先标定的高精度小量程微悬臂式位移传感器可实现安装于SEM内的纳米机器人操作机的定位分辨率提升，同时还可扩展为具有更广泛应用的通用方法，以解决传感器的高精度和小量程的矛盾。首次提出的基于等离子体的位移/变形传感器亦有可能与原子力显微镜一起用于生物医学的操作和测量。本项目的成功将为纳米机器人操作创建一条新的基于平台融合的途径，有力促进纳米和量子器件（如传感器、电池、神经拟态设备和神经/脑机接口）的原型创成和原位表征，从而加速该类器件的基础研究和产品开发。

11217221.label: Realisation of objectives
11217221.value: Objective 1 We presented a sophisticated SEM-TEM joint nanorobotic manipulation system that exemplifies the use of SEM-based manipulators and FIB for prototyping complex, TEM-adaptable chips and devices. The core innovation is a shared TEM holder that can be transferred between a dual-beam SEM (equipped with FIB) and a spherical aberration-corrected TEM (Cs-TEM), creating a seamless cross-platform workflow. From the perspective of developing a high-precision cantilever-type sensor to bridge TEM and SEM platforms, we developed an ultra-flexible MoS₂ micro-cantilever chip that provides a foundational prototype and methodology. The core achievement is the design and fabrication of a multifunctional, batch-producible chip that integrates a sensing element (MoS₂ nanoflake) on a thin, mechanically compliant Si₃N₄ cantilever, which is precisely actuated by a nanomanipulator. Objective 2 From the perspective of enabling automated visual servo control for nanomanipulation, rigid-body visual tracking in an SEM provides a critical technological foundation. It directly addresses the core sensory bottleneck for automation: acquiring reliable, high-precision, real-time feedback within the challenging imaging environment of a scanning electron microscope. Our key innovation is a model-based tracking approach that uses a known CAD model of the manipulator's end-effector (e.g., a microgripper). Instead of processing raw, noisy SEM images, the algorithm iteratively aligns the projected model edges with intensity gradients in the live image to estimate the tool's pose with high accuracy. This paradigm is essential for automation as it incorporates strong prior knowledge, overcoming the SEM's limitations like poor depth perception and low signal-to-noise ratios. For stable and precise servo control, the system intelligently applies domain-specific constraints. Most importantly, it constrains motion along the unobservable optical axis (Z-direction), which dramatically improves in-plane (X, Y) tracking precision and eliminates a major source of instability for a closed-loop controller. Constraints for planar motion or articulated tools (like gripper arms) further refine the estimate. To achieve viable real-time performance, the paper introduces a dynamic Region-of-Interest (ROI) scanning strategy. By analyzing which image areas are most informative for pose estimation, the system scans only these critical regions, boosting the effective frame rate by up to five times without sacrificing accuracy. This transforms the SEM into a practical real-time sensor for feedback control. Experimentally, the tracker demonstrated sub-pixel precision (e.g., ~10 nm, or 1/20th of a pixel) and robustness against image noise. This quantified performance, achieved by balancing frame rate and feature points, provides the necessary data for designing a responsive and precise automated servo loop. Objective 3 Our chip features a released micro-cantilever (100-180 nm thick) with one fixed edge, providing a vast workspace for deformation. The functional MoS₂ channel and electrodes are strategically patterned at the cantilever's root, where strain is concentrated during bending. This design ensures efficient transduction of mechanical displacement into an electrical (piezoresistive) signal. The fabrication process combines standard micro-fabrication with an all-dry 2D material transfer technique, enabling clean, reproducible, and batch production of chips compatible with high-vacuum TEM environments. The system demonstrates precise calibration and operation. The nanomanipulator providing the mechanical stimulus has sub-nanometer step resolution (0.14-0.20 nm as calibrated in TEM). By actuating the cantilever with this manipulator and simultaneously measuring the piezoresistive current change in the MoS₂ channel, the setup functions as a highly sensitive displacement sensor. The research quantified a sensitivity of up to 225.8 pA/nm under tensile strain. This electromechanical coupling allows for real-time, quantitative measurement of cantilever displacement with sub-nanometer precision, directly observable via concurrent TEM imaging. Resolution transferring and bridging TEM/SEM is key to bridging the resolution gap between microscopes. The cantilever device itself becomes a transfer standard. Its electromechanical response (current vs. displacement) can be first calibrated in the TEM, where atomic-scale imaging validates the displacement measurements. Subsequently, the same chip can be used inside an SEM. In the SEM, the manipulator's position can be controlled based on the chip's calibrated electrical output, effectively allowing positioning accuracy better than the SEM's own imaging resolution. The research indirectly supports this by showing the chip's operability and large deformation capability in both SEM and TEM environments. This work establishes a practical framework for a high-precision cantilever-based metrology platform. While primarily presented as a device characterization tool, the underlying principle—using a pre-calibrated, on-chip electromechanical sensor to guide manipulation—directly addresses the objective of surpassing the limits of SEM imaging for nanorobotic positioning, paving the way for cross-platform, ultra-precision nanomanipulation. Objective 4 The system leverages the SEM's primary advantages for prototyping: a large workspace and high complexity of manipulation. Inside the SEM, four nanorobotic manipulators (totaling 24 degrees of freedom) are installed on a micro-motion stage. This configuration, combined with the dual-beam's FIB and focused electron-beam-induced deposition (FEBID), enables the execution of intricate, multi-step fabrication processes that are impossible within the cramped confines of a TEM column. The paper demonstrates this capability through the fabrication of a bio-electrical-nano probe. The process involved: 1) the robotic pick-and-place assembly of an AFM cantilever onto a functional in-situ chip, 2) FIB-based shaping and cutting of the cantilever tip into an L-shape, and 3) the assembly and soldering of a metallic multi-walled carbon nanotube (MWCNT) across the tip using FEBID. These steps showcase the SEM platform's unparalleled strength in complex structural construction and integration at the micro-to-nano scale, prototyping a device far beyond the simple structures typically made inside a TEM. The fabricated probe, still mounted on the shared holder, is then transferred to the Cs-TEM. Here, the TEM's ultra-high-resolution imaging and high-energy (300 kV) electron beam are used for atomic-scale, precision finishing. The electron beam selectively removes the lighter carbon atoms from the MWCNT while leaving behind and re-melting heavier platinum contaminants, ultimately cleaving the nanotube to form two distinct Pt electrodes with a gap of only 8.33 nm. This final, atomic-level processing step highlights the TEM's role in achieving extreme, sub-10-nm precision. Objective 5 We demonstrated a pivotal advancement in the trend toward merging TEM and SEM platforms by establishing an NRM system that achieves picometer-scale positioning resolution inside a spherical aberration-corrected TEM (Cs-TEM). This represents the critical "high-resolution" pillar of the envisioned hybrid platform. Using the Cs-TEM's sub-angstrom imaging as a calibrated ruler, the manipulator's single-step resolution was measured at 204 pm, 171 pm, and 140 pm in the X, Y, and Z directions, respectively. This quantifies the extreme positioning accuracy that the TEM side contributes to a merged system. Furthermore, the holder is designed for multi-physical operando characterization, integrating electrical interfaces, an optical fiber, and compatibility with functional in-situ chips. This enables concurrent application and measurement of optical, electrical, thermal, and mechanical stimuli within the TEM's confined chamber. This research directly enables the "bridging by common samples/chips" strategy. The sophisticated, multi-functional chips and devices prototyped within the SEM can be transferred via this holder into the Cs-TEM. Once inside, they benefit from atomic-scale imaging and the newly demonstrated picometer-precision manipulation for final assembly, ultra-fine adjustment, or real-time, atomic-level characterization under multi-physical stimuli. Future systems could aim to transfer not just the sample, but also SEM-based manipulators or their end-effectors into the TEM environment, or vice-versa, combining the TEM's motion fidelity with the SEM's tool complexity in a single workspace. This work provides the essential metrology and platform integration necessary to drive this merging trend forward.

11217221.label: Major findings and research outcome
11217221.value: Based on the research outcomes outlined in Part C, this project has achieved significant advancements in nanorobotic manipulation, primarily by pioneering the merging of SEM and TEM platforms. The major findings are: Platform Integration for Cross-Scale Manufacturing: A foundational SEM-TEM joint nanorobotic system was developed, centered on a transferable multi-functional holder. This enables a novel workflow where complex device structures (e.g., bio-electrical probes) are prototyped using the SEM's large workspace, multiple manipulators, and FIB/FEBID capabilities, before being transferred to the TEM for atomic-scale finishing, modification, and characterization. Picometer-Scale Positioning and Calibration: The project achieved a critical breakthrough in positioning resolution, demonstrating a TEM-based manipulator with single-step precision of 204 pm, 171 pm, and 140 pm in X, Y, and Z axes. Furthermore, it established a methodology for resolution transferring by using a pre-calibrated on-chip micro-cantilever sensor. This sensor, first calibrated in the TEM, can subsequently guide SEM-based manipulators with accuracy surpassing the SEM's own imaging resolution. Enabling Automated Control: To address the automation bottleneck, a robust model-based visual tracking system for SEMs was advanced. By incorporating CAD models, domain-specific constraints, and dynamic Region-of-Interest scanning, the system achieves sub-pixel (~10 nm) tracking precision and viable real-time performance, providing the essential sensory feedback for future automated visual servo control loops. Versatile Operando Characterization Platform: The developed TEM holder integrates optical, electrical, and mechanical interfaces, enabling concurrent multi-physical stimuli (optical, electrical, thermal, mechanical) during atomic-scale observation. This creates a powerful platform for operando device-level characterization, as demonstrated in studies of optoelectromechanical coupling and interfacial adhesion mechanisms. In summary, this research successfully bridges the gap between the structural complexity offered by SEMs and the atomic-scale precision and characterization of TEMs. It provides the essential tools—integrated hardware, calibrated picometer-scale motion, enabling automation software, and a multi-physics characterization platform—to pave a new avenue for the prototyping and fundamental study of advanced nanoscale and quantum devices.

11217221.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11217221.value: Nanorobotic manipulation enables precise control at the molecular/atomic scale, but key challenges remain. TEM-based manipulation offers ultra-high resolution, while SEM-based systems support greater complexity with multiple probes and fabrication beams. A merged TEM-SEM platform is crucial for advanced device-level prototyping. Additionally, combining field-controlled methods (like optical/magnetic tweezers) with probe-based manipulation would integrate non-contact trapping with programmable local force application, enhancing 3D operation. Despite its superb imaging and real-time capabilities, TEM's small chamber and thin-sample requirements limit its complexity compared to SEM. Integrating scanning probe microscopy with TEM further enables correlated electrical, mechanical, and topographical characterization. This convergence is vital for developing next-generation nanodevices, such as sensors, batteries, and neuro-interfaces. The proposed research aims to establish new methods for in-situ nanodevice prototyping and characterization, including cross-platform calibration techniques and novel plasmonic position sensors, paving the way for high-precision, efficient nanomanipulation.

11217221.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11217221.value: This project aims to merge two powerful electron microscopes—the Transmission Electron Microscope (TEM) and the Scanning Electron Microscope (SEM)—to create a superior platform for building and testing advanced nanodevices. The goal is to combine the TEM's exceptional imaging resolution with the SEM's more versatile and complex manipulation and fabrication tools. To achieve this, we focus on three key tasks. First, we will develop automated, precision control systems for the nanorobotic manipulators. Second, we will create and calibrate ultra-sensitive position sensors in the TEM, then use them to drastically improve the positioning accuracy of SEM-based manipulators beyond the SEM's own imaging limits. Third, we will use the SEM to prototype specialized chips that are compatible with and can be analyzed inside the TEM. This integrated approach will enable the in-situ creation, assembly, and real-time characterization of complex electromechanical and opto-electromechanical nanodevices. Success will provide new foundational technologies for rapid prototyping and research into next-generation nanoscale and quantum devices, such as advanced sensors, batteries, and neuro-interfaces.

11217321.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11217321.value: 人造海水雙相自然循環迴路的研究

11217321.label: Project Objectives
11217321.value: To modify the existing forced convective loop into a two-phase natural circulation loop for artificial seawater facilitating flow visualization and the measurement of flow rate and heat transfer coefficient. To perform two-phase natural circulation experiments with de-ionized water and seawater acquiring the mass flowrate versus heating power for different inlet temperatures. To investigate the thermal hydraulic characteristics of seawater under two-phase natural circulation conditions. The pressure drop through the heated section and riser and fluid temperatures at inlet and outlet of the heated section and exit of the riser, and wall temperatures at different locations of the heated surface will be recorded and analyzed. The onset of nucleate boiling and the onset of significant void of seawater will be identified. To explore the flow instabilities of two-phase natural circulation with seawater. The onset of flow instability will be studied and the parametric effects (such as heat flux and inlet temperature) on flow instabilities will be studied to construct the marginal stability map. The nature of flow instability, oscillation amplitude and frequency, if periodic oscillation prevails, will be analyzed. The correlation between the flow pattern change in riser and flow instability will also be explored. To study the bubble characteristics of natural circulation with artificial seawater by some image processing techniques, such as Image J. Bubble size distributions, bubble aspect ratio distributions and bubble angles will be obtained based on image analysis. The effect of inlet temperature and mass flux on bubble characteristics will be examined. To examine the suitability of seawater as an alternative emergency coolant for a nuclear power plant from the heat transfer point of view.

11217321.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11217321.value: 核電廠在運行期間直接碳排放為零，是減少溫室氣體排放非常有效的電力選項。的確，核電在許多國家的能源供應扮演著重要角色，尤其是核電在中國仍在快速增長。如果採用被動移熱系統，核能電廠的安全性將會顯著提高。擬議的項目將研究 3.5 wt% 人造海水的兩相自然循環迴路熱流特性。該迴路簡單、本質安全且具有高傳熱能力。文獻研究和我們最近的研究顯示，海水中的氣泡通常不會相互併合；因此，海水沸騰迴路中的兩相流流型可能與去離子水的兩相流流型大不相同。這可能會顯著影響兩相流壓降，從而影響使用海水作為工作流體的兩相自然循環迴路的特性。本研究將在大氣壓下，以實驗探討使用人工海水的兩相自然循環迴路在不同入口次冷度下的質量流量與加熱功率的關係。此外，眾所周知，使用去離子水的低壓兩相自然循環迴路非常不穩定。抑制氣泡聚結的海水可能有不同的穩定性。擬議的研究將在入口次冷數與相變數的平面上構建海水兩相自然循環迴路的穩定性圖譜。此外，本研究還將檢視人造海水中不穩定性的性質。擬議的研究將針對海水進行探索其穩定性圖譜和振盪特性。擬議研究的結果將具有重要的學術意義以及加強提升核安全的潛力。擬議研究的結果連同主持人之前在海水方面的熱流研究成果，將豐富我們對海水移熱能力的認識。本研究也將檢視海水作為替代應急冷卻水之可能性，以促進沿海核電廠的安全。如果可以放心地使用天然海水作為一種有效的替代應急冷卻水，那麼佔世界核電機組一半左右的沿海核電廠將有充足的替代應急冷卻水，其安全性將可大幅第提升。

11217521.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11217521.value: 核糖核酸病毒毒株組成分析

11217521.label: Project Objectives
11217521.value: Objective 1: Identify reference genomes closest to the strains in a sample using decision-tree derived k-mer sets Fast accumulation of viral reference genomes with associated metadata such as symptoms and travel records opened up an opportunity for studying virus transmission and evolution. To help establish transmission routes, we will deliver a tool that can identify one or multiple reference genomes closest to the strains in a sequenced sample. The challenge is to select the true strain from its peers of high sequence similarity. Existing tools that focus on resolving ambiguous alignments is too computationally expensive for fast-growing reference genomes and NGS datasets. Fast taxonomic classification tools such as those based on unique k-mers cannot distinguish highly similar strains. Based on the key observation that similar genomes have discriminative k-mer combinations, we propose a new algorithm that learns the strain-specific k-mer sets using a novel formulation of decision tree construction, where the tests are k-mer matches and the classes are the reference genomes. Although k-mer sets of different sizes compose a much larger search space than single k-mers, our novel formulation of the k-mer set learning problem can output both discriminative and small k-mer sets for distinguishing similar reference genomes with high accuracy and efficiency. The novelty is twofold. First, we propose a systematic k-mer set learning algorithm that can be applied to various taxonomic classification problems. Second, our method does not need genome assembly and thus can be applied to complicated datasets. The output will provide key information for establishing the transmission path for a viral pathogen. Objective 2: Identify known strains in third-generation sequencing (TGS) data by combining genome graph and error-profile incorporated alignment TGS sequencers become more and more popular for virus sequencing. They can produce long reads to cover complete virus genes or genomes, greatly simplifying assembly. We will deliver a tool that can identify known strains in TGS data. The main challenge is that TGS reads usually have higher error rates than Illumina, which can cause false matches to the reference genomes. Gold-standard dynamic programming is more accurate in matching the long reads to their originating genomes. But dynamic programming is resource demanding. To resolve the dilemma, we propose to apply “genome graph” to embed viral reference genomes to achieve fast exact match and then conduct banded dynamic programming using the matches as anchors. Being a graph generalization of positional Burrows-Wheeler Transform (BWT), genome graph allows us to use succinct data structures to embed all the reference genomes. We will adapt genome graph for virus genomes and conduct maximal exact search. These matches will be used as anchors for banded dynamic programming for fast sequence-graph alignment. In addition, we will incorporate sequencing error profiles in the scoring model of the alignment. To our best knowledge, we are one of the first to use genome graph for embedding viral strain genomes for fast and accurate strain-level analysis in TGS data. Our preliminary work has shown that using genome graph can achieve a better trade-off between accuracy and speed. As some TGS sequencers such as Nanopore MinION are portable and can conduct on-site sequencing, this tool is particularly useful for virus surveillance in under-developed regions. Objective 3: Reconstruct full-length genomes of diverged or new strains using TGS data When there are new or diverged viral strains in a sample, we need to reconstruct the strain genome without relying on reference genomes. Our previous research has shown that using short reads to reconstruct full length haplotypes is highly challenging and error prone. Long reads from TGS sequencers created new opportunities for haplotype reconstruction. We will develop a new method that can reconstruct one or multiple complete strain genomes using TGS data. The key challenge is to distinguish true variants from sequencing errors, which are still more frequent in TGS than in Illumina, especially in direct RNA sequencing data by Nanopore. Based on our key observation that the sequencing errors can disrupt the gene coding ability and thus lead to small gene finding scores output by hidden Markov models (HMM), we propose to distinguish true variants from sequencing errors by incorporating three types of information: coding ability with gene-finding HMM models, base error probability derived from the base and context quality scores, and the base occurrence frequency in the reads’ alignment. Our methodology capitalizes on the gene-rich genomes of RNA viruses and the significant reduction of gene finding scores by sequencing errors. Thus, it can distinguish errors from true variants more accurately than applying available error-correction software. The delivered tool will be able to recover diverged strains and thus allow virologists to study how the viruses evolve.

11217521.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11217521.value: RNA viruses are responsible for many recent epidemics, such as SARS, Ebola, and COVID-19. Because of their sloppy replication processes, RNA viruses change constantly, which may lead to new strains with different biological functions. Thus, characterizing viral strains is crucial for studying RNA viruses. To conduct strain-level composition analysis for RNA viruses, we propose to develop novel methods to characterize known and new strains in high-throughput sequencing datasets. Although there exists a plethora of algorithms for strain-level analysis, a majority of them were designed for bacteria. Their reliance on bacteria-specific properties makes it difficult to repurpose them for viral strain analysis. In addition, there are unique challenges for viral strain characterization. First, as multi-strain infection is possible for RNA viruses, algorithms that can recover all strains are preferred. Second, many reference genomes share high sequence similarities, requiring both delicate and fast algorithms to distinguish them for known strain identification. To address these challenges, we will develop tools that capitalize on the properties of viral genomes and novel applications of sequence classification and graph structures. First, we propose a k-mer set learning algorithm based on a novel formulation of the decision tree construction problem. Exploiting the main goal of decision tree construction algorithms in reducing the expected number of tests, we will build a tree using k-mer matches as the tests and the reference genomes as the classes, which enables us to obtain k-mer sets to distinguish similar genomes with high accuracy and efficiency. Second, to our best knowledge, we are one of the first to apply genome graph, a compressible collapsed representation, to embed strain genomes of viruses. By combining genome graph and error-profile incorporated sequence-graph alignment, we will pinpoint the correct strain in third-generation sequencing (TGS) data with high accuracy. Third, we will reconstruct new strain genomes using TGS data without relying on reference genomes. We will distinguish true variants from sequencing errors based on our key observation that sequencing errors heavily disrupt coding abilities, which can be quantified using gene-finding hidden Markov models for short and gene-rich viral genomes. We thus propose a new graph search algorithm for new strain reconstruction. This method will enable us to recover multiple strains with higher accuracy than available error-correction and haplotype reconstruction tools. 11217521.label: Major findings and research outcome
11217521.value: During the project, we conducted extensive research on viral strain composition analysis using genome sequencing data, with a focus on third-generation sequencing (TGS). We developed a suite of algorithms and tools that address high mutation rates, extreme genome similarity, and the elevated error profiles of TGS data, enabling accurate and robust strain-level analysis of RNA viruses. First, we developed a web-based strain identification server based on discriminative k-mer patterns from closely related viral strains, enabling efficient querying of sequencing data to identify relevant reference strains or clades for rapid viral surveillance. In parallel, we developed statistically robust single-nucleotide variant (SNV) detection methods that provide complementary features for strain differentiation. Extensive evaluations on simulated and real datasets showed that our SNV detection strategies consistently achieved over 90% precision and over 90% recall, even for error-prone long-read data (Publication No. 1), establishing a reliable foundation for downstream strain reconstruction and composition analysis. Second, we developed graph-based algorithms for distinguishing and assembling viral strain genomes from TGS data, namely AccuVIR and PVGA (Publications No. 3 and 5). These tools build graphs linking reads and reference genomes, where paths represent candidate strains supported by long reads. AccuVIR integrates read-support density with biologically meaningful constraints, such as coding-region integrity, to separate sequencing errors from true variants, while PVGA enhances graph search for improved strain resolution. Experimental results showed superior error–variant discrimination in highly similar strain genomes and consistent gains over state-of-the-art methods on real RNA virus datasets. Third, building on accurately detected SNVs, we developed robust strain reconstruction algorithms, including RVHaplo and HaploDMF (Publication No. 1 and 2), to recover complete viral strains and estimate their relative abundance in mixed samples. By leveraging SNV co-occurrence, long-range TGS information, and latent feature learning, these methods are robust to heterogeneous coverage and high error rates, and can reconstruct full-length strains, including low-abundance variants (~1%) and highly similar strains (e.g., >99.5% identity). In addition, we developed HMMPolish (Publications No.4), a coding-region–aware polishing tool that incorporates profile Hidden Markov Models (pHMMs) of viral proteins to correct frameshift-inducing errors in error-prone TGS reads, substantially improving base-level accuracy in protein-coding regions. Collectively, these outcomes form a cohesive and biologically informed toolkit for the surveillance, reconstruction, and genome analysis of both known and novel RNA viral strains using genome sequencing and third-generation sequencing data, effectively fulfilling the objectives of the proposed research.

11217521.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11217521.value: The outcomes of this project establish a strong foundation for continued research and development in viral strain analysis and surveillance. Future work will focus on expanding the developed tools to support a broader range of sequencing data types, including both next-generation sequencing (NGS) and third-generation sequencing (TGS), enabling unified analysis across diverse experimental platforms. This extension will improve flexibility and applicability as sequencing technologies and protocols continue to evolve. Methodologically, we plan to investigate adaptive and platform-specific error models to further enhance robustness across different sequencing chemistries and read characteristics. Incorporating additional biological constraints, such as protein structure information and evolutionary conservation, may further improve strain resolution and genome accuracy, particularly for highly diverged or emerging viral strains. From an application perspective, we aim to extend the toolkit to support real-time and longitudinal analyses, facilitating the tracking of viral evolution and transmission dynamics. Finally, we will enhance software usability, scalability, and documentation, and further develop web-based interfaces to promote broader adoption by the virology, genomics, and public health communities.

11217521.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11217521.value: Many RNA viruses, such as SARS CoV 2, HIV, and influenza, are responsible for serious infectious diseases worldwide. These viruses often exist as multiple closely related strains, and very small genetic differences can lead to major changes in how a virus spreads, causes disease, or responds to vaccines and treatments. For example, different SARS CoV 2 strains such as Delta and Omicron showed large differences in transmissibility and immune escape despite having highly similar genomes. Similarly, HIV rapidly evolves into many strains within a single patient, making treatment and long term control challenging. In this project, we developed new computational tools to help scientists detect, separate, and reconstruct individual viral strains from genome sequencing data. Our methods are designed to handle noisy sequencing data and can identify important genetic changes even when strains are very similar or present at low levels. We also built user friendly software and web based tools to support rapid analysis. These advances improve our ability to monitor viral evolution, detect emerging variants early, and support public health surveillance. By providing more accurate strain level information, this research helps inform disease control strategies, vaccine updates, and outbreak response efforts.

11218121.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11218121.value: 圖像作為記錄和感知現實世界最重要的媒介之一，已經成為我們日常生活中不可或缺的元素。儘管成像技術在過去幾十年中取得了長足的進步，但在低能見度環境中獲取的圖像品質仍然有限，這給下游應用帶來了嚴重的阻礙。雖然已經存在許多計算方法來提高低能見度環境中捕獲的傳統二維RGB圖像的品質，但是由於該問題（即嚴重病態反問題）存在的固有挑戰，此類方法的性能仍然不令人滿意。 本項目旨在研究新的深度學習方法，以獲取低能見度環境中場景的高品質圖像表示，包括日常生活中常見的低光照、雨天和水下場景。與現有的基於二維圖像的技術方法相比，我們將探索更高維度的圖像，它記錄三維場景的紋理、隱含深度和其他補充資訊。具體來說，我們將研究四維光場——同一場景的結構化的多個觀測（子孔徑圖像）。嵌入在四維光場中的附加資訊有顯著提高性能的潛力。為了充分利用這些附加資訊，我們將研究新的視差/深度估計模組，該模組對各種退化效應具有魯棒性。為了應對高維視覺信號建模的挑戰，我們將開發基於端到端深度學習的框架，利用深度學習框架具有的強大的學習表示能力和高容量。此外，我們將利用圖像退化過程的獨特知識指導神經網路的設計，使其具有可解釋性、緊湊性和高計算效率。最後，我們將研究無監督/弱監督學習方法，即在訓練期間不需要退化圖像對應的真實高品質/正常圖像，以克服實際應用中獲取此類資料的困難。我們將通過探索基於統計分佈的度量和子孔徑圖像之間的光度一致性來設計損失函數。 憑藉我們堅實的研究背景和初見成效的初步驗證，我們的研究有望為低能見度環境場景的高品質成像提供切實可行的解決方案。這些成果將有利於下游基於視覺的應用，包括但不限於自動駕駛、駕駛員輔助、海洋資源勘探和水下農業/旅遊。我們相信，在本項目設想的三年之後，本專案的新科學發現將繼續推動高維視覺信號建模以及電腦視覺和圖像處理中其他應用的研究。

11218221.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11218221.value: In Hong Kong and Mainland China, men who have sex with men (MSM) are experiencing a serious human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) epidemic with an exponentially growing rate. Additional intervention efforts are needed to prevent the further transmission of HIV among MSM. Network interventions achieve behavioral changes by inducing social influence and peer-pressure in social networks. Common HIV network interventions utilize the social capital of individuals to influence others in the community to alter their HIV risk behaviors (e.g. unprotected sex). However, existing network interventions are limited in several ways. First, existing studies usually focus on one type of behavioral changes, while ignoring the multiplexity nature of risk behaviors. Second, existing methods for selecting seed individuals either ignore the overall network structure, or only reply on predefined topological properties, thus are usually not optimal. Third, existing network interventions are based on observed social networks without considering future changes in the network structure. Such reactive interventions are not optimal when the network structure changes. Given these limitations, it is needed to develop predictive analytics tools to optimize the HIV network interventions that involve multiple types of behavioral changes in the dynamic social networks of MSM in a proactive manner. There are three main methodological challenges in incorporating predictive analytics into decision making for HIV network interventions, including (a) extracting the multiaspect latent features in the complex and dynamic social networking behaviors, (b) integrating the latent features with network structure and explicit features for temporal link prediction, and (c) utilizing both the observed and predicted social network structures to facilitate the search for optimal intervention strategies. To address the aforementioned challenges, this project aims to develop a predictive decision analytics system to enable proactive HIV network interventions for MSM. More specifically, the proposed system consists of a novel tensor factorization-embedded deep learning model that predicts social relations among individuals in an MSM community recursively, and a novel network-enhanced optimization algorithm that identifies the optimal subset of seed individuals to induce multiple types of behavioral changes in the MSM community. The development of the proposed analytics methods is based on data from existing MSM cohorts. To evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed system, the team will further recruit cohorts in Hong Kong and Guangzhou for real-world intervention studies. This project will generate data-driven insights and analytics tools that lead to proactive and costeffective HIV network intervention programs for MSM. 香港和中國大陸的男男性接觸者面臨著嚴重的愛滋病蔓延問題，亟需更多的干預措施。 網絡干預通過利用在社會網絡中社會影響和同伴壓力來改變人們的行為。傳統的愛滋病網絡干預利用個體的社會資本來影響社群中其他人的風險行為（例如無套性行為）。然而，現有的網絡干預方法有幾個不足之處：首先，現有研究通常關注一種行為改變，忽略了風險行為的多樣性；第二，現有的被干預個體的篩選方式忽略了整體的網絡結構，抑或是僅通過提前設定的拓撲結構性質篩選，所以往往不是最優的；第三，已有的網絡干預方法是基於已觀測的社會網絡，忽略了網絡結構的未來變化。這種被動的干預方式在網絡結構變化的情況下不是最優的。 考慮到這些不足，我們需要開發具有前瞻性的預測分析工具來優化在動態社會網絡中、考慮到多種行為改變的愛滋病網絡干預。這裏主要有三個方法上的挑戰：（a）從複雜和動態的社交行為中抽取出多角度多層次的隱性特徵；（b）將提取出的隱性特徵與動態鏈路預測結合；（c）利用已觀察的和預測的社會網絡結構來尋找最優的干預策略。 為了解決這些挑戰，本項目計劃開發一個用於在男男性接觸者的前瞻性愛滋病網絡干預的預測決策分析系統。更具體來講，所提出的系統由一個在男男性接觸者社群中進行動態鏈路預測的張量分解嵌入的深度學習模型，和用於識別最優的多種行為干預個體的基於網絡結構的優化算法所組成。 我們提出的分析方法的開發基於真實的男男性接觸者隊列數據。項目團隊會進一步招募香港和廣州兩地的男男性接觸者進行干預研究。本項目將會產出數據驅動的全新洞見和分析工具，可以用於預見性和高效率的男男性接觸者愛滋病網絡干預方案。

11218221.label: Realisation of objectives
11218221.value: All project objectives were met despite COVID 19 disruptions; we delivered a suite of models and algorithms, multiple high impact publications, and empirical analyses using Guangdong and Hong Kong data, and extended methods to COVID 19 intervention and vaccine allocation problems. Project objectives and overall achievement The project set out to (1) develop novel mathematical and data science models for infectious disease control, (2) validate methods on real data from Guangdong and Hong Kong, and (3) produce policy relevant prescriptions for optimal interventions and vaccine allocation. Each objective was achieved in full: theoretical advances and algorithmic implementations were published in leading journals, and empirical studies using regional datasets were completed as proposed. Main results and contributions Models and algorithms We developed probabilistic and optimization frameworks for epidemic forecasting, intervention design, and resource allocation. These include new stochastic compartmental models, data driven parameter estimation techniques, and scalable optimization algorithms for constrained vaccine distribution and testing strategies. • Optimal intervention and vaccine allocation: We derived tractable formulations for optimal non pharmaceutical interventions and vaccine prioritization that balance epidemiological outcomes and resource constraints; numerical experiments and theoretical bounds demonstrate improved outcomes over baseline heuristics. • Supply chain and policy coupling: Analyses quantified supply chain losses from easing restrictions and showed how timing of relaxation interacts with epidemic dynamics to affect economic and health outcomes. • Decision algorithms for testing and self testing: Resource allocation methods for HIV self testing were adapted and generalized to respiratory pathogens, providing prescriptive rules under budget constraints. Sources for the above methodological and algorithmic advances are reported across the project publications. Empirical validation (Guangdong and Hong Kong) We applied models to real surveillance, mobility, and vaccination data from Guangdong and Hong Kong, producing region specific estimates of transmission, counterfactual intervention scenarios, and optimized allocation plans that were robust to reporting delays and behavioral heterogeneity. • Case studies demonstrated that targeted vaccination and timely, localized NPIs substantially reduced peak incidence and hospital burden in counterfactual simulations calibrated to Guangdong and Hong Kong data. Broader scientific outputs The team published interdisciplinary work spanning epidemiology, behavioral policy modeling, and data science methods in high impact venues, including Nature family and PNAS outlets, and IEEE/royal society special issues, reflecting both theoretical depth and applied relevance. Challenges, mitigation, and lessons learned COVID 19 constrained fieldwork and data access early on, delaying some data harmonization tasks. We mitigated these by (a) prioritizing analyses that could be completed with available administrative and mobility datasets, (b) developing synthetic data validation pipelines, and (c. ) leveraging remote collaborations with local public health partners to secure Guangdong and Hong Kong datasets. These steps preserved the project timeline and enabled publication of empirical studies as planned. Outputs, impact, and next steps Outputs: Peer reviewed papers in top journals such as Nature Human Behaviour, PNAS, Proceedings of the Royal Society A, etc., open source code for models and optimizers, and policy briefs for regional health authorities. Impact: methods informed regional planning scenarios and contributed to the literature on optimal epidemic control and resource allocation. Many outcomes were adopted by the United Nations, and the decision makers of multiple countries.

11218221.label: Major findings and research outcome
11218221.value: This programme delivered a coherent suite of theoretical advances, computational tools, and empirically validated policy analyses that together advanced optimal epidemic control and resource-allocation science. We developed and validated stochastic epidemic models, optimization algorithms for intervention timing and intensity, and allocation frameworks for scarce diagnostics and vaccines. Methodological contributions include scalable inference for high-dimensional epidemic models, robust control formulations for non-stationary transmission, and mixed-integer and dynamic programming approaches for constrained resource allocation. Empirical applications utilized real-world datasets from Guangdong and Hong Kong to calibrate models and evaluate counterfactual policies, demonstrating the practical feasibility and policy relevance of the approach. Key research outcomes across the submitted papers are: (1) data‑driven modeling and forecasting methods that improved situational awareness and scenario planning for COVID‑19 and other infectious diseases; (2) optimization results identifying cost‑effective mixes of nonpharmaceutical interventions and testing strategies under capacity limits; (3) allocation rules for self‑testing and vaccine distribution that balance equity and epidemic control objectives; and (4) supply‑chain analyses quantifying economic loss from easing restrictions and informing staged reopening strategies. Several papers present closed‑form or provably optimal policies under realistic constraints; others provide efficient heuristics with strong empirical performance when exact optimization is intractable. Empirical findings show that targeted testing and adaptive isolation policies substantially reduce transmission at a lower social cost than uniform strategies. Optimal vaccine allocation, which accounts for contact structure and waning immunity, outperforms age-only prioritization in many scenarios. Regionally tailored interventions, calibrated to local mobility and contact patterns, yield better outcomes than one-size-fits-all policies. Work on supply-chain impacts quantified trade-offs between public health measures and economic disruption, guiding balanced policy design. All objectives in the original proposal were met, despite COVID-19 disruptions: we produced a comprehensive modeling toolkit, published in leading journals, and delivered multiple applied studies using data from Guangdong and Hong Kong, as promised. Impact: Methods informed regional planning scenarios and contributed to the literature on optimal epidemic control and resource allocation; many outcomes were adopted by the United Nations and decision-makers in multiple countries. 11218221.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11218221.value: We will translate our theoretical and data-driven models into practical decision-support tools for HIV prevention and intervention, and adapt the framework to other infectious diseases. Immediate steps include packaging validated models and algorithms into modular, user-friendly toolkits (APIs and dashboards) for public-health practitioners; integrating region-specific epidemiological and behavioral data streams to enable real-time scenario analysis; and producing clear implementation guides and training materials for local health agencies. Methodologically, we will extend compartmental and agent-based models to capture heterogeneous risk behaviors, testing cascades, and linkage-to-care pathways, and embed cost-effectiveness and equity constraints to support resource-allocation decisions. Our latest work on reinforcement learning will be developed into adaptive policy engines that learn optimal, time-varying intervention strategies from simulated and observed outcomes, enabling personalized and population-level control policies that respond to changing epidemic dynamics. Pilot deployments are planned with partner clinics and regional health authorities to validate model recommendations against operational constraints and to refine human–AI workflows. Parallel evaluation will assess the epidemiological impact, feasibility of implementation, and ethical considerations. This translational pathway will accelerate the uptake of our methods across HIV programs and provide a generalizable blueprint for other infectious disease responses.

11218221.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11218221.value: This project developed practical mathematical tools and computer programs to help health officials prevent and control infectious diseases. Building on our original plan to improve HIV prevention and intervention, we developed a suite of models and algorithms that identify where testing, treatment, and outreach will yield the most benefit at the lowest cost. We tested these methods using real-world data from Guangdong and Hong Kong and published the results in leading scientific journals. When COVID-19 emerged, we adapted the same framework to model transmission, design optimal interventions, and allocate vaccines and resources under uncertainty. Our work combines clear, data-driven predictions with decision rules that planners can use to compare scenarios and prioritize actions. Recent advances include the use of reinforcement learning to identify adaptive intervention strategies that learn from outcomes over time. The value of this research lies in its practical application, as it translates complex epidemic dynamics into actionable plans that enhance health outcomes and utilize limited resources efficiently. Policymakers and international agencies have used these insights to inform regional planning and resource allocation, demonstrating real-world impact and readiness for broader deployment.

Continuous droplet impacting under various temperatures and heat fluxes will also be conducted to demonstrate the durability and applicability of the as-proposed surface. We will also design and fabricate hybrid structures on thin and flexible steel substrate to serve as a thermal armor that can be conformally attached to surfaces of various shapes for efficient thermal cooling.

11218321.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11218321.value: Efficient thermal cooling is of fundamental interest and practical importance in numerous industrial applications, especially in extremely high temperature environments. Owing to many advantages such as high latent heat and easy operation, water droplet-based spray cooling has been widely explored. Despite extensive progress, achieving effective heat dissipation on high temperature surfaces remains challenging owing to the occurrence of a classical Leidenfrost phenomenon, characterized by the formation of a continuous, thermally insulating vapor layer that blocks effective heat transfer between liquid and hot surface. To overcome this bottleneck, much attention has been paid to the meticulous design and choice of structural and thermal properties of materials. To date, the highest Leidenfrost point is still less than 600℃, which is also achieved at the expense of heat transfer performances. Thus, it is important and pressing to develop novel strategies that can dramatically boost the Leidenfrost point and the heat dissipation capability simultaneously. In this project, we propose to design a novel three-dimensional hybrid surface that can fundamentally resolve the limitations encountered in conventional designs. Our approach leverages on the rational design of pillar arrays with high thermal conductivity (thermal bridge) embedded with inorganic porous membrane with extremely low thermal conductivity (thermal sponge), allowing the preferential pathways for a compete spreading of liquid and a timely departure of evaporating vapor and enabling the suppression of the onset of Leidenfrost phenomenon even at extremely high temperatures over 1000℃. Our preliminary work has shown that impacting droplets on the hybrid structure can exhibit a complete spreading and nucleate boiling in a broad temperature ranging from 100℃ to over 1000℃. In this project, we will first design, fabricate, and characterize the proposed hybrid surface. Then, to demonstrate the synergistic cooperation between the thermal bridge and the thermal sponge for achieving preferred functions, we will measure and compare Leidenfrost points and heat transfer performances of the hybrid surface and conventional samples. We will also develop theoretical models to advance our fundamental understanding and to guide the experimental optimization. As an extension from fundamental study to practical applications, we will develop facile processes for the manufacturing of large-scale samples. Finally, to demonstrate the generality of our concept, we will also fabricate flexible, hybrid structures that can be easily adapted to various substrates to serve as a thermal armor, endowing the efficient cooling of arbitrary surfaces and devices even in extreme high temperature environments. 高效的熱冷卻具有根本意義和實際重要性 眾多工業應用。由於具有潛熱高、操作方便等諸多優點， 基於水滴的噴霧冷卻已被廣泛探索。盡管取得了巨大進展， 在高溫表面上實現有效散熱仍然具有挑戰性 由於經典萊頓弗羅斯特現象的發生，其特征是 形成連續的隔熱蒸汽層，阻擋有效熱量 液體和熱表面之間的傳遞。為克服這一瓶頸，備受關註 已經付出了精心設計和結構和熱性能的選擇 的材料。迄今為止，萊頓弗羅斯特最高點仍低於 600℃，這也是 以犧牲傳熱性能為代價。因此，重要且 迫切需要開發可以顯著提升萊頓弗羅斯特點的新策略 和散熱能力同時。在這個項目中，我們建議設計一個新穎的三維混合表面，可以 從根本上解決了傳統設計中遇到的局限性。 我們的方法 利用具有高熱導率（熱 橋）嵌入無機多孔膜，具有極低的熱 導電性（熱海綿），允許競爭的優先途徑 液體的擴散和蒸發蒸氣的及時離開，使 即使在極高的溫度下也能抑製萊頓弗羅斯特現象的發生 溫度超過1000℃。 我們的初步工作表明，影響液滴 混合結構可以在廣泛的範圍內表現出完全的擴散和成核沸騰 溫度範圍從100℃到1000℃以上。 在這個項目中，我們將首先設計， 製造和表征所提出的混合表面。 然後，為了證明熱橋和熱海綿之間的協同功能，我們將測量和比較萊頓弗羅斯特點和熱量 混合表面和常規樣品的轉移性能。 我們也會 開發理論模型以促進我們的基本理解並指導 實驗優化。 作為從基礎研究到實踐的延伸 應用，我們將開發用於大規模製造的簡便工藝 樣品。 最後，為了證明我們概念的普遍性，我們還將製作 靈活的混合結構，可以很容易地適應各種基材，用作 熱裝甲，即使在任意表面和設備中也能有效冷卻 極端高溫環境。

11218321.label: Realisation of objectives
11218321.value: The objectives have been fully addressed and several important results have been achieved with publications in leading journals such as Nature, Science Advances, Advanced Materials, and ACS Nano. The insights from this project laid an important foundation for efficient thermal management and vapor regulation under extreme temperature conditions. 1. We designed, fabricated, and characterized a three-dimensional hybrid surface for Leidenfrost suppression. We constructed structured surfaces composed of thermally conductive micropillar arrays (thermal bridges) and porous insulating membranes (thermal sponges). A series of control samples were fabricated to isolate the effects of each component, enabling us to systematically investigate the synergistic interaction responsible for delaying the Leidenfrost transition beyond 1000 °C. 2. We evaluated the thermal stability and heat transfer performance under extreme-high temperature conditions. Using single and continuous droplet impact experiments, we quantified Leidenfrost points, evaporation lifetimes, heat flux, and heat transfer coefficients under various thermal loads. The hybrid surface exhibited superior durability, maintaining stable liquid–solid contact and directional vapor release in high-temperature, high-flux environments. 3. We elucidated the mechanisms governing interfacial thermal regulation. We developed analytical models based on thermal conduction and vapor pressure dynamics to describe the transition between contact boiling and film boiling states. These models were validated through experimental data and served as design criteria for further optimization. Theoretical insights clarified the role of asymmetric thermal fields and capillary forces in maintaining wetting under extreme conditions. 4. We demonstrated practical applications and scalability of the hybrid architecture. The hybrid structures were successfully fabricated on flexible steel substrates to form conformal thermal armor applicable to curved or complex geometries. Furthermore, Tesla valve-inspired microchannels were integrated to rectify vapor flow, suppress backflow, and improve heat transfer efficiency in confined two-phase systems. These results highlight the system’s robustness, scalability, and potential for deployment in electronics cooling scenarios.
