11218321.label: Major findings and research outcome
11218321.value: 1.New Design Paradigm Developing a structured thermal armor that integrates heterogeneous thermal and geometric configurations to suppress the Leidenfrost phenomenon. This architecture introduces spatially resolved thermal conductivity pathways aligned with vapor flow, enabling high-temperature superwetting and rapid phase-change cooling. The design breaks the Leidenfrost barrier first reported in 1756 by maintaining stable liquid–solid contact and promoting directional vapor release at temperatures exceeding 1000 °C. It addresses a centuries-old scientific and engineering challenge in phase-change thermal regulation and establishes a broadly applicable strategy for managing interfacial heat transfer under extreme thermal conditions. 2.New Mechanisms Revealing a previously unrecognized flow–thermal field matching mechanism, which enables coordinated alignment between vapor transport and heat flux. By coupling vertically graded thermal conductivity with surface-guided capillarity, this mechanism actively regulates vapor escape and maintains persistent liquid–solid contact under extreme temperatures. The mechanism redefines interfacial boiling control by linking directional heat flux with vapor dynamics, offering a fundamental advance beyond conventional models of phase-change heat transfer. 3.New Applications Establishing a new framework for high-temperature thermal management through scalable structural strategies compatible with complex geometries and harsh environments. The hybrid architecture overcomes the long-standing limitation of effective heat dissipation above 1000 °C, far beyond the 600 °C threshold where conventional systems typically fail. By integrating heterogeneous thermal pathways with directional vapor transport, it enables continuous and stable cooling under dynamic two-phase conditions. For example, its integration with Tesla-valve-inspired microfluidic channels enhances localized heat removal in electronic devices. The design supports large-area manufacturing and industrial deployment, with ongoing applications in aerospace thermal protection and nuclear power plant cooling. This innovation has expanded the technological boundaries of structural heat regulation and was honored with the Nukiyama Memorial Award, the highest distinction in the field of heat transfer.

11218321.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11218321.value: Building on the demonstrated capability of heterogeneous thermal architectures to fundamentally suppress the Leidenfrost effect and sustain stable liquid–solid contact at temperatures exceeding 1000 °C, this research provides a solid foundation for advancing high-temperature thermal regulation. Future efforts will focus on systematically addressing the remaining scientific and engineering challenges in ultra-high-temperature phase-change heat transfer. In the next stage, we will further refine the flow–thermal field matching framework through multiphysics simulations and operando thermal diagnostics, aiming to elucidate the coupled dynamics between vapor transport and directional heat flux. Concurrently, we aim to expand current design principles toward adaptive thermal systems with real-time reconfigurable pathways, enabling intelligent heat routing under dynamically changing conditions. From an application perspective, the structured thermal armor will be integrated into industrial platforms such as high-power electronics, aerospace thermal shielding, and nuclear cooling systems, with particular emphasis on operational stability, scalability, and environmental resilience. These developments are anticipated to drive transformative progress in next-generation thermal management technologies and are currently being advanced through collaborations with partners in the aerospace and advanced energy sectors.

11218321.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11218321.value: Efficient cooling at extremely high temperatures is essential for aerospace, energy, and electronic systems. However, most existing materials fail beyond 600 °C, leaving a critical gap in thermal protection technologies. Our research solves this long-standing problem by developing a novel thermal armor with engineered heat pathways, liquid-wicking membranes, and directional vapor escape channels. This structured surface maintains stable liquid–solid contact even above 1150 °C, enabling continuous and efficient cooling where traditional materials break down. By decoupling heat flow and vapor movement, our design achieves robust thermal regulation under extreme conditions. This breakthrough opens new directions in thermal science and supports advanced applications such as nuclear reactor cooling, next-generation electronics, and aerospace heat shielding. Our work has been published in Nature, Science Advances, and Advanced Materials, and has received international recognition. Notably, it was honored with the 2024 Nukiyama Memorial Award and the 2023 Falling Walls Breakthrough Prize as one of the top ten advances in engineering and technology.

11218521.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11218521.value: Decentralized storage (DS) is emerging as an appealing alternative to commercial cloud storage. It envisions open storage marketplaces where anyone can join and monetize unused disk space to store and serve data for others. As commonly acknowledged by all DS proposals today, such openness mandates effective auditing mechanisms to assure owners of their remotely stored data integrity. Ideally, by employing certain auditing mechanisms to routinely check the data integrity, the DS can remunerate or fine individual storage providers accordingly, enforcing correct functioning and health for the ecosystem. For auditing transparency, a standard architecture here is on-chain auditing, where a general-purpose blockchain serves as an unbiased auditor to publicly verify storage proofs submitted by storage providers and fairly resolve potential disputes between parties. Despite the promises, the stringent requirements of this blockchain-reliant architecture make realizing on-chain auditing paradigm a daunting task: 1) The immutability and public accessibility of blockchain pose unique security threats towards the on-chain auditing trails; 2) Scalable on-chain auditing designs require the storage proofs to be as small and easy to verify as possible; 3) The ubiquitous data dynamics in real-world storage systems calls for efficient auditing of dynamic data; 4) Implementing a fully functional on-chain auditing system demands non-trivial systemization efforts. In this project, we plan to push forward the frontier of this under-explored area with secure, dynamic, and practical on-chain auditing for decentralized storage, with three research tasks: 1) Develop a secure and efficient on-chain storage auditing framework: a) enhancing security guarantees against unforeseen threats that exploit the on-chain auditing trails, such as unsolicited data recovery and storage freeriding; b) achieving new auditing schemes that are more affordable with much improved on-chain efficiency. 2) Devise a scalable on-chain auditing protocol to support dynamic data: a) designing a near-optimal indexing translation data structure, to efficiently turn an auditing scheme into a dynamic one with minimal changes; b) improving indexing data structure with performance trade-off, potentially making the design more scalable. 3) Establish a full-fledged working prototype for practical deployment: a) enabling a secure and trustworthy middleware service to alleviate the workload for data owners and storage providers respectively; b) building a data abstraction layer to enable the auditing support for diversified data applications. Our project will greatly advance the field of decentralized storage ecosystem, contributing new insights to the trending on-chain auditing paradigm. Our research outputs will also serve as solid grounds for future decentralized data applications. 去中心化存儲 (DS) 正在成為商業雲存儲的有競爭力的替代方案。它設想了一個開放的存儲市場，任何人都可以加入並利用未使用的磁盤空間為他人存儲和提供數據。正如當今所有 DS 提案所普遍承認的那樣，這種開放性市場要求有效的審計機制來確保所有者遠程存儲數據的完整性。理想情況下，通過採用特定審計機制來例行檢查數據完整性，DS 可以相應地向單個存儲服務提供商提供報酬或懲罰，從而保障存儲生態系統的健康發展。為了做到公開透明的審計，業界觀點普遍認為需要通過鏈上審計，即借用某通用區塊鏈作為無偏見的審計者，公開驗證存儲提供商提交的存儲證明，並公平解決各方之間的潛在爭議。 儘管有好的願景，這種依賴於區塊鏈的鏈上審計機制設計仍然存在諸多尚未完全解決的難題：1）區塊鏈的不可篡改和公共可訪問性使得鏈上審計紀錄存在被攻擊者濫用的潛在安全威脅； 2）可擴展的鏈上審計設計要求存儲證明必須盡可能空間開銷小且易於驗證； 3）不斷更新的動態數據擬對高效存儲審計的設計提出全新挑戰； 4) 打造功能齊全的鏈上審計的系統化工作紛繁複雜。 鑑於此，本項目中我們擬計劃通過安全、動態和實用的去中心化存儲鏈上審計來推動這一前沿領域，研究任務包括：1）開發安全高效的鏈上存儲審計框架: a) 加強針對鏈上審計紀錄的安全保障，預防其被攻擊者濫用造成的潛在數據恢復威脅，以及影響存儲審計安全機制的隱患； b) 設計新的審計方案，力求達到更高效的鏈上審計效率。 2)支持動態數據的鏈上審計： a) 設計一個高性能的索引轉換數據結構，有效的將靜態審計方案轉變支持動態數據更新的方案； b) 通過性能權衡改進索引數據結構，使設計可支持大規模數據。 3) 為實際部署建立成熟的工作原型： a) 啟用安全可靠的中間件服務，分別減輕數據所有者和存儲提供商的工作量； b) 構建數據抽象層，為多樣化的數據應用提供審計支持。 我們的項目將極大地推動去中心化存儲生態系統領域的發展，為去中心化存儲網絡的鏈上審計範式貢獻新的見解。我們的研究成果也將作為未來去中心化數據應用的堅實基礎。

11218521.label: Realisation of objectives
11218521.value: The mid-term progress has been reported before, with directly related major publications at IEEE TDSC, TPDS, IEEE ICDCS, ACM CCS, etc. Below, we briefly conclude major achievements of the project objectives, including research activities (with output at TIFS, TDSC, TNSE, ICDCS, etc.) curried out during this second 18-month reporting period. ## Realizations of objective 1, 3 and 4 #### DWare: Cost-Efficient Decentralized Storage With Adaptive Middleware We built DWare, a TEE-enabled middleware that makes on-chain auditing economical and adds secure deduplication—two missing pieces for practical decentralized storage. DWare standardizes tag generation (BLS+polynomial commitments), batches proofs, and minimizes auditor state, achieving 1.2 KB proofs and 0.25 MB on-chain state per 1 TB dataset—far below ADS baselines. Deduplication integrates client-side fingerprinting with enclave-gated proof-of-ownership and cross-user sharing, resisting probing via nonce-based PoW attestation. A data abstraction layer decouples backends; cache-aware oblivious updates and batching keep overhead small. Prototypes show DWare serves 30+ owners, cuts gas-equivalent costs by up to 50×, and maintains practical throughput. The preliminary findings are reported in IEEE TIFS 2024. ### PuffChain: A Dynamic Scaling Blockchain System With Optimal Effective Throughput PuffChain couples elastic capacity with auditable consensus via (i) role decoupling for parallel block assembly, (ii) duplication-free packing, and (iii) three-phase BFT with whitelist filters salvaging valid blocks. Auto-tuned throughput adjusts packers based on block size; VRF-based sortition ensures liveness. On EC2 (100 nodes), PuffChain reaches 6,061 tps—within 1% of network capacity—showing protocol-network co-design enables scalable, real-time auditing. The preliminary findings are reported in IEEE TNSE 2024. #### Powering Privacy and Performance for Lightweight Blockchain Clients via TEE The rapid growth of blockchain networks has led to a surge in lightweight client adoption. This shift introduces two critical challenges: 1) Lightweight clients must rely on external sources for transaction data, exposing users to potential privacy and security threats. 2) Existing privacy-preserving query systems struggle to handle the vast amounts of data in blockchain networks efficiently. To tackle the dual challenges of maintaining query privacy and managing extensive blockchain data efficiently, our framework seamlessly integrates state-of-the-art Private Information Retrieval (PIR) techniques with Trusted Execution Environment (TEE) hardware capabilities. Our solution also supports diverse query types, including keyword-based, predicate, and range queries, while enabling lightweight clients to verify the integrity and completeness of query results. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach reduces full-node storage overhead by nearly 50% and improves communication efficiency by 4x compared to state-of-the-art PIR-based solutions, with only a modest 4-11% increase in query time for integrity verification. The preliminary findings are reported in IEEE MSN 2024. #### Towards Public Verifiable and Forward-Privacy Encrypted Search by Using Blockchain We closed a long standing gap: achieving both forward privacy and public verifiability without placing heavy indexes on chain. Our design keeps indexes/files off chain for performance, but anchors per keyword “checklists” as compact multi set hash digests on a smart contract. Each update uses fresh tokens and masked labels to break linkability; each search verifies only the delta (newly added results) by checking digest differences against the off chain return, while the contract immutably records verified outcomes for future reuse. To address deletions—often ignored in forward private designs—we adopt a hybrid index (keyword chains for search, file chains for deletion) so deletions are processed directly without revocation lists or full re encryption. The result is a protocol that provides auditable correctness guarantees with forward private updates, sublinear search, and efficient deletion. Our Ethereum prototype demonstrates modest gas for digest operations, query throughput >35K entries/s off chain, and stable latency even under dynamic updates, indicating the practicality of verifiable encrypted search for on chain auditing contexts. The preliminary findings are reported in IEEE TDSC 2023. ## Realisations of objectives 1, 2, and 4 #### RangeQC: A Query Control Framework for Range Query Leakage Quantification and Mitigation We developed RangeQC to move privacy governance from “after the fact attack analysis” to “before release risk control.” The key idea is to translate all three primary leakage patterns in range schemes—access (which records retrieved identifiers), volume (which embeds inclusion chains), and search (which reveals token existence/frequency)—into compact, actionable metrics. Concretely, we use PQ tree cardinality to measure how much order information survives, a candidate volume graph to capture how close an attacker is to reconstructing base slot volumes, and relative entropy over token maps to quantify search frequency inference. These metrics enable a practical proxy enforcer to simulate “what would be leaked” per query and apply tunable rules (e.g., bounding per query information gain, halting when cumulative progress nears a threshold, suppressing repeated identical accesses, or disallowing fine grained/sparse ranges). This unified and light touch approach does not mandate ORAM or pervasive padding; instead, it gives operators a dial to trade utility for incremental privacy at run time. Across four real datasets and multiple state of the art attacks, RangeQC consistently raises reconstruction error (e.g., up to 12.8× nMAE increase) under realistic settings, showing that fine grained, rule driven control is a viable path to scalable, leakage aware auditing. The preliminary findings are reported in IEEE ICDCS 2023. #### Cross-User Leakage Mitigation for Authorized Multi-User Encrypted Data Sharing We addressed a subtle but damaging vector in multi user systems: cross user linkage, where colluding servers or malicious users correlate authorizations and shared results to infer identities or roles. Our two server scheme (honest but curious, non colluding) blinds trapdoors and authorization tokens, and transforms matching via zero sum garbled Bloom filters with oblivious transfer so that each server learns only partial, non linkable information. Result unlinkability is enforced by per query blinding and per user encryption of returned identifiers; a group based Bloom filter allows narrowing the obfuscation scope to improve efficiency while preserving unlinkability within groups. Formal simulation based proofs (under DDH) show that even with colluding malicious users, servers cannot correlate authorizations or results beyond benign leakage. A prototype confirms that these protections can be achieved with practical computation and communication, offering a deployable defense against an often overlooked leakage class in on chain, multi user auditing environments. The preliminary findings are reported in IEEE TIFS 2024. ### Toward Full Accounting for Leakage Exploitation and Mitigation in Dynamic Encrypted Databases We systematized dynamic leakage across search, updates, and file retrieval, and argued for “local indistinguishability” as a practical security target: queries should be indistinguishable within clusters rather than globally, composed over time. Our two‑layer hardening—cluster‑based index padding (to equalize result lengths within clusters) and cluster‑based file‑volume padding (to eliminate size fingerprints)—keeps the adversary’s advantage bounded while avoiding ORAM‑grade overheads. Batch padding with buffer/time triggers smooths costs; decryption‑on‑demand strips padded ciphertext to minimize client workload; and sequential‑composition bounds show how guarantees accumulate over updates. On real datasets, the scheme suppresses recovery below 0.5% with <1.2× total overhead, showing that judicious, continuous perturbation can neutralize dynamic leakage without sacrificing system usability—an attractive profile for long‑lived, on‑chain auditing tenants. The preliminary findings are reported in IEEE TDSC 2024.

11218521.label: Major findings and research outcome
11218521.value: Our project, Towards Secure, Dynamic, and Practical Auditing for Decentralized Storage Networks, has delivered significant advances that push the boundaries of secure and scalable auditing in decentralized ecosystems. The key outcomes are: 1. New Models and Frameworks for Secure On-Chain Auditing We developed novel auditing models and protocols that enable privacy-preserving and efficient verification of dynamic data in decentralized storage. These frameworks overcome limitations of traditional Proof-of-Storage schemes by introducing succinct index structures and adaptive designs, ensuring practical deployment without sacrificing security. This work enriches the theoretical and practical foundations of blockchain-based auditing and sets new directions for dynamic data integrity assurance. 2. Scalable and Elastic Auditing Architectures for Blockchain Systems To address performance bottlenecks, we designed new consensus and throughput optimization frameworks that integrate dynamic scaling with auditable guarantees. Our architecture introduces role-decoupled consensus and duplication-free transaction packing, coupled with adaptive control mechanisms for real-time elasticity. These designs advance the frontier of blockchain scalability while maintaining verifiable integrity, demonstrating how protocol and network co-design can achieve robust auditing under dynamic workloads. 3. Privacy-Hardened Middleware and Leakage-Aware Controls We proposed innovative middleware solutions and proactive privacy governance frameworks that move beyond reactive defenses. These include metadata-hiding analytic systems, leakage quantification models, and fine-grained query control mechanisms that mitigate cross-user linkage and dynamic leakage in multi-user environments. Collectively, these contributions establish new paradigms for privacy-preserving auditing, offering deployable solutions that balance security, usability, and efficiency. 4. Prototype Systems and Practical Integration for Diverse Applications Our research culminated in working prototypes that integrate advanced cryptographic primitives, Trusted Execution Environments, and data abstraction layers to support heterogeneous storage backends. These systems validate the feasibility of secure auditing in real-world decentralized networks and open pathways for broader adoption in applications such as encrypted search, lightweight blockchain clients, and multi-owner data sharing. This outcome bridges theoretical rigor with practical deployment, enriching the landscape of secure decentralized storage solutions. These findings collectively advance secure, dynamic, and practical auditing for decentralized storage networks, introducing new models, frameworks, and designs that significantly broaden the frontier understanding of privacy-preserving and scalable blockchain auditing. Results have been disseminated through leading venues, including IEEE TDSC, TIFS, TPDS, TNSE, ICDCS, ACM CCS, etc. (see Part-C for further details)

11218521.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11218521.value: Integrated Auditing Ecosystem with Adaptive Privacy Controls and Intelligent Interfaces Building on our current middleware and auditing frameworks, the next phase envisions a full-fledged decentralized auditing ecosystem that seamlessly integrates secure storage verification, privacy-preserving queries, and dynamic deduplication under a unified architecture. This ecosystem can be designed for Web3 environments, supporting interoperability across decentralized applications, smart contracts, and heterogeneous storage backends. One interesting direction will be the incorporation of Large Language Models as intelligent interfaces for auditing and governance. LLMs can provide natural language interaction for complex auditing tasks, generate adaptive compliance policies, and assist in interpreting cryptographic proofs for non-expert stakeholders. Combined with blockchain-based trust anchors, this approach will democratize access to secure auditing while maintaining rigorous guarantees. Furthermore, the system will feature adaptive privacy controls that allow operators to tune security-performance trade-offs dynamically, guided by workload characteristics and user-defined policies. By leveraging semantic reasoning from LLMs and decentralized identity frameworks, the ecosystem can enforce fine-grained, context-aware privacy rules across multi-owner and multi-user environments. This direction not only strengthens the technical foundation for secure decentralized storage but also aligns with the broader vision of Web3 governance, where transparency, automation, and user-centric control converge to create resilient, trustless ecosystems.

11218521.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11218521.value: Decentralized storage is an emerging alternative to traditional cloud services. Instead of relying on big providers, it creates open marketplaces where anyone can rent out unused disk space. This model promises transparency and resilience, but it raises a critical question: How can users trust that their data remains safe and intact without depending on a single company? Our research addresses this challenge by developing new ways to audit data securely and efficiently using blockchain technology. In simple terms, we design systems where a public blockchain logically functions (through codified actions) as an impartial referee, verifying that storage providers are doing their job correctly. This prevents cheating and ensures fairness in the ecosystem. Our research activities go further by tackling real-world complexities: data changes frequently, auditing must be fast and affordable, and privacy must be protected. Our solutions combine advanced cryptography, smart middleware, and adaptive designs to make auditing practical for diverse applications, from Web3 platforms to decentralized apps. This work lays the foundation for trustless, transparent, and privacy-aware storage networks, enabling safer digital services for businesses and individuals in the next generation of the internet.

11218621.label: Project Objectives
11218621.value: To predict tasks' execution time according to the surroundings. Our preliminary has shown that tasks' execution time could vary a lot according to the surroundings such as traffic scenarios, the types of obstacles, and the number of obstacles around the ego vehicle. Accurate prediction of tasks' execution time is important in deriving a responsive task scheduling. We plan to develop a real-time inception inspired model to predict tasks' execution time under a given surrounding where the loss functions will be designed empirically to optimize different parts of the model. To this end, we will conduct comprehensive experiments in Apollo CyberRT to collect and label data, and train the model to achieve fast and accurate online prediction. To evaluate the impact of time disparity on driving safety. Driving safety requires that data streams from multiple sensors stay synchronized in the pipeline. However, different sampling rates, improper task scheduling, and buffer management often make them out of synchronization. As a result, a task may take inputs with large time disparity from multiple precedent tasks, which may lead to accidents. To evaluate the impact of time disparity on driving safety, it is critical to identify the threshold where a time disparity above the threshold may lead to high collision rate. To this end, we will add different levels of time disparity on synchronized sensing datasets such as Waymo and KITTI. We then use the motion planning and Collison-Checker in CommonRoad, which consists of composable benchmarks for motion planning, to evaluate the impact of time disparity on driving safety. The impact will be measured by two performance metrics, namely the probability of finding a feasible trajectory and collision rate. To develop an AoI-centric task scheduling framework on multi-core processors. Taking age of information and time disparity into consideration, we have formulated an ILP problem to minimize the maximum age of information where the time disparity in any execution is no more than the threshold to be empirically obtained in objective 2. Considering that tasks' execution time cannot be predicted accurately in a long time period and it is time consuming to make a scheduling in a long time period, we will develop a rolling horizon based task scheduling. We will use the solutions obtained in rolling horizon to train a deep reinforcement learning model so that real-time task scheduling decisions can be made through fast and accurate online inference.

11218621.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11218621.value: An autonomous driving system consists of many inter-dependent software components to perform various tasks such as perception, motion planning, and control. In recent years, various models and algorithms have been developed for individual tasks to achieve shorter execution time and higher accuracy. When such tasks are put into a pipeline, driving safety depends on not only the performance of individual tasks, but also how they are scheduled on multi-core processors. Driving safety requires that 1) driving decisions are made according to the latest surroundings, and 2) sensing data stays synchronized in the pipeline to avoid making driving decisions based on distorted surroundings. In this project, we introduce two new performance metrics, namely, age of information (AoI) and time disparity, to capture the requirements of autonomous driving. AoI is defined as the time difference between the time when the control task generates control commands and the minimum raw data timestamp of the control task’s inputs. Our preliminary results have shown that minimizing the maximum AoI is equivalent to jointly maximizing the throughput and minimizing the responsive time, where throughput and responsive time are often separately considered in conventional task scheduling. For a task with multiple inputs, time disparity is defined as the maximum time difference of the raw data timestamps among its inputs. In this project, we aim to develop an AoI-centric task scheduling framework for autonomous driving, which takes the impact of time disparity on driving safety and tasks' execution time dynamics into consideration. In particular, we will use Apollo CyberRT as our simulator. We will develop learning models to dynamically predict tasks’ execution time according to the surroundings. We will also develop learning models to study the impact of time disparity on driving safety, i.e., to empirically derive the threshold where time disparity above that will cause serious driving safety issues. Given the predicted execution time of tasks, a rolling horizon based task scheduling will be developed to minimize the maximum AoI while ensuring that time disparity is less than the derived threshold. We will then use the solutions obtained to train a deep reinforcement learning model offline so that real-time task scheduling decisions can be made through fast and accurate online inference. In summary, this project will open a new landscape for task scheduling. We expect the proposed AoI-centric task scheduling framework will make contributions not only to autonomous driving, but also other applications demanding data freshness and synchronization. 自动驾驶系统由许多相互依赖的软件模块组成，用于执行各种任务，例如感知、运动规划和控制。近年来，针对单个任务开发了各种模型和算法，以实现更短的执行时间和更高的准确性。当这些模块集成到一起的时候，驾驶安全不仅取决于单个任务的性能，还取决于它们在多核处理器上的调度方式。 行车安全要求1）根据最新环境做出驾驶决策，2）传感数据在集成系统中保持同步，避免根据不实的环境做出驾驶决策。在这个项目中，我们引入了两个新的性能指标，即信息年龄 (AoI) 和所使用的传感器数据的时间差异，来刻画任务调度的性能。 AoI 定义为控制任务生成控制命令的时间与控制任务所用到输入的最小原始数据时间戳之间的时间差。我们的初步结果表明，最小化最大 AoI 等效于同时优化最大化吞吐量和最小化响应时间。传统任务调度通常分别考虑吞吐量和响应时间。对于具有多个输入的任务，时间差异定义为其输入之间原始数据时间戳的最大时间差。 在这个项目中，我们旨在为自动驾驶开发一个以 AoI 为中心的任务调度框架，该框架同时考虑了时间差异对驾驶安全及任务执行时间可变的情形。特别是，我们将使用 Apollo CyberRT 作为我们的模拟器。我们将开发机器学习模型，根据环境动态预测任务的执行时间。我们还将开发机器学习模型来研究时间差异对驾驶安全的影响，即根据历史数据推导出超过该时间差异将导致严重驾驶安全问题的阈值。给定任务的预测执行时间，我们将开发任务调度算法以最小化最大 AoI，同时确保时间差异小于安全阈值。然后我们将使用获得的解决方案离线训练深度强化学习模型，以便可以通过快速准确的在线推理做出实时任务调度决策。 综上所述，该项目将为任务调度开辟新的方向。所提出的以 AoI 为中心的任务调度框架不仅将为自动驾驶做出贡献，还将为其他需要数据新鲜度和同步的应用做出贡献。

11218621.label: Realisation of objectives
11218621.value: Objective 1 is to predict tasks' execution time according to the surroundings. For objective 1, we have conducted experiments to test the variable execution time of different tasks in Apollo CyberRT systems. We are also developing algorithms to predict the execution of tasks under different environment scenarios to complete objective 1. The results have been reported in IEEE INFOCOM 2022 (Part C 9-1). We further developed a model to predict the executive time of tasks in Autoware running on ROS2. In particular, we model each callback’s execution time as a time series and employ a Transformer-based prediction model to estimate the executive time for the upcoming round. We train a lightweight Transformer for each callback using data collected from a real vehicle running Autoware.Universe, and integrate the trained models into ROS 2 as independent model nodes. At runtime, each callback publishes its actual execution time to the corresponding model node, which in turn provides the predicted execution time back to the AoI-aware scheduler. Experiments on the Autoware DAG show that using the predicted execution time instead of conservative worst-case execution time reduces the maximum AoI by up to about 15%, while the additional inference and communication overhead of each prediction is only about 2.2 ms. The result demonstrates that the prediction framework is both effective and practical for time-sensitive ADS. The result is reported in Part C 8-2. Objective 2 is to evaluate the impact of time disparity on driving safety. In Part C 9-1, we have conducted obstacle avoidance experiments on CommonRoad, a collection of road motion planning benchmarks. The scenarios are either transformed from real traffic data or manually created based on real road networks. We have selected some typical scenarios to see the motion planning results under different levels of AoI. We deliberately let the ego vehicle plan its trajectory based on the environmental information collected 100, 200, and 300 ms ago, and then simulate driving according to the planned trajectories in the current environment. We can conclude that the deviation of the perception of the environment caused by the high AoI level can easily mislead the autonomous vehicle with an illusion that it is safe, which can cause serious safety hazards and even traffic accidents. Part C 9-3 and 8-2 show that, in ROS 2–based ADS, the default scheduling schemes focus mainly on latency and ignore the existence of using stale sensor data under low response latency scenarios, exposing the vehicle to delayed and potentially unsafe driving reactions. By translating AoI into the corresponding spatial deviation of moving obstacles, we reveal that low latency alone only indicates that the system reacts quickly, whereas high AoI means it reacts quickly to outdated information. This mismatch leads to significant errors in the perceived positions of obstacles and can easily create risky driving scenarios. Objective 3 is to develop an AoI-centric task scheduling framework on multi-core processors. In Part 3 8-1 and Part 3 9-1, we have shown that minimizing AoI is equivalent to jointly minimizing the response time and maximizing the throughput. We formally formulate the AoI-centric task scheduling problem as an ILP problem. We extend the formulation and formulate the optimal AoI-centric periodic scheduling problem with a given cycle to derive practical scheduling solutions. A deep reinforcement learning-based solution is designed accordingly. To better design deep reinforcement learning based scheduler, we have addressed a few challenges in deep reinforcement learning. The results are published in Part C 8-4, 8-5, 8-6. We also conducted research on task scheduling at the edge where co-task scheduling between the edge and the vehicle’s onboard computing resources will be critical in autonomous driving. Accuracy and deadline-guaranteed task scheduling at the edge. The work has been published in Part C 9-2. In Part C 9-3 and Part C 8-2, we further extend from CPU-level scheduling to ROS 2–level scheduling in realistic ADS frameworks. Specifically, we design CARSS and its enhanced variant ARPSS, which exploit the ADS DAG structure, ROS 2 executor semantics, and execution-time prediction to jointly assign callbacks to executors, set priorities, and select the freshest callback instances. Extensive experiments on several ADS DAGs demonstrate that our AoI-centric ROS 2 scheduling reduces the maximum AoI by approximately 20–30% compared to existing chain-aware and heuristic scheduling policies, while some of the observed AoI remain close to the theoretical bounds derived in our analysis. Information freshness, measured by the Age-of-Information (AoI) metric in autonomous driving systems. In the Artificial Intelligence of things, it is more meaningful to promptly capture events as they occur at the sources, we extend the metric of AoI to a novel information freshness metric called Age of Event (AoE). Subsequently, we thoroughly investigate the problem of AoE-minimizing transmission scheduling. Evaluations performed on a real traffic event dataset reveal that even in the absence of complete knowledge, our algorithms exhibit competitive performance when compared against the clairvoyant benchmark and markedly outperform AoI baselines. The result is published in Part C 8-3.

11218621.label: Major findings and research outcome
11218621.value: The major findings are: 1) For an autonomous driving system with streaming sensory data and interdependent tasks, considering age of information is critical in ensuring safety. This is confirmed on both Apollo CyberRT and Autoware on ROS2. 2)The task execution time varies under different scenarios and it makes a different in scheduling. Execution time prediction is feasible; 3) Scheduling taking age of information and variable execution time can improve the system performance in terms of safety. The details have been illustrated in Section 5.3 of this completion report. The above findings are validated in the research outcomes, which have been published in Top conferences and journals. Two Ph.D. students are trained, and one patent is filed.

11219321.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11219321.value: Wireless technologies enabled by photonic microwave devices have been of growing importance over the past decade. Mobile communications is now ubiquitous as an integral part of the modern society. The capability of ensuring different levels of security for these technologies is foreseeably an aspect to be addressed. In recent years, researchers have developed an interesting approach of secure communications based on high-speed random number generation for optical fiber systems, while extensions to photonic microwave wireless systems can be expected in the near future. For secure key distribution, the generation of correlated random bits at ultrahigh speeds has attracted much attention through the nonlinear chaotic dynamics of semiconductor lasers, where the security stemmed from the fast broadband dynamics. Such approaches relied on the recently developed principle of bounded observability, while chaos signals of broad bandwidths and high dimensions are desired. Different laser dynamics with compound and cascaded feedback were reported, though the signals generated were mainly developed without involving any microwave subcarriers for transmission. These approaches of distributing random bits focused on fiber-based systems. In this proposal, the external cavity dynamics of semiconductor lasers is considered in a new region for wireless key distribution on microwave subcarriers. Through investigating the external cavity dynamics of lasers, an on-off switching behavior on a single-tone microwave oscillation was recently found. The on-off switching corresponds to variations of the oscillation envelope. The envelope was found to bifurcate from being regular to chaotic, resulting in chaotic bursting of microwave oscillations as wireless subcarriers, which can be used for distributing random bits. For the photonic microwave key distribution, the project will first experiment on the external cavity dynamics for microwave chaos bursting, which will be compared with the Lang-Kobayashi model regarding the external cavity mode interactions. Moreover, distribution of correlated random bits will be developed using the microwave oscillations as the subcarriers over wireless channels, where the bit rate will be maximized and bit errors will be minimized by optimizing the dynamics and postprocessing parameters. Fundamentally, the entropy extracted by the scheme will also be quantified through theoretical and experimental investigations, where the trajectory in the high-dimensional dynamics for amplifying the effect of noise will complement the statistical randomness testing. Success of the project will contribute to secure wireless applications through harnessing the microwave dynamics in lasers. 過去十年中，基於光子微波器件的無線技術變得越來越重要。移動通信在現代社會中不可或缺。保障這些技術中各種程度的安全性將成為重要課題。近年來，科研人員們為光纖系統開發了一種基於高速隨機數生成的保密通信方法，其亦可在不久的將來推廣至光子微波無線系統。經由半導體激光器非線性混沌動力學所生成的超高速相關隨機數，已經在安全密鑰分發方面引起了廣泛關注，其安全性源於動力學的高速與寬帶。這些方法依賴於近期發展的受限可觀察原理，需要寬帶和高維數的混沌信號。目前已報道了多種複合與級聯反饋的激光器動力學，然而其產生的信號極少涉及用於傳輸的微波副載波。這些分發隨機比特的方法側重於光纖系統。 本項目計劃利用半導體激光器外腔動力學的一個新領域，來實現在微波副載波上分發無線密鑰。最近，在激光器外腔動力學的研究中發現了一種單一頻率微波振蕩的開關切換，其中開關切換對應於振盪包絡的變化。研究發現，振蕩包絡從規則分岔至混沌，導致了微波振蕩的混沌突發，其中微波振蕩作為無線副載波可用於分發隨機數。對於光子微波密鑰分發，本項目將首先進行外腔動力學產生微波混沌突發的實驗，並在外腔模相互作用方面將其與Lang-Kobayashi模型對比。此外，本項目將在無線信道上使用微波振蕩作為副載波分發相關隨機數，通過優化動力學和後處理參數使比特率最大化的同時，亦將誤碼降至最少。該方案也將通過理論與實驗，從根本上量化所提取的熵，其中放大噪聲影響的高維數動力學軌跡將對統計學隨機性測試加以補充。通過利用激光器的微波動力學，成功實現本項目將有助於保障無線應用的安全性。

11219621.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11219621.value: The large and increasing amount of solid waste generated each year in cities makes solid waste management one of modern society's most pressing issues. While the most efficient solution is to prevent waste generation in the first place, the biotransformation of food and other organic waste streams into value-added products ranging from compost to biomaterials and bioenergy is necessary to divert them away from saturated landfills. Microbial biosurfactants, surface-active molecules naturally produced by microorganisms, can be derived from the fermentation of organic waste streams. Biosurfactants, in particular sophorolipids (SL), hold promising opportunities for application in environmental remediation, cosmetics, personal care, detergents, pharmaceutical and agricultural industries. Sophorolipid production from the bioconversion of food and other organic waste is a promising solution, which is still an emerging valorisation technology. Thus, it is imperative to quantify and optimize the environmental impacts of this emerging technology very early in its design phase to guide its scale-up towards maximizing its sustainability. While LCA and TEA are widely applied for retrospective quantification of environmental impacts of technologies ready for implementation, the inherent lack of detailed datasets for emerging technologies contributes to significant uncertainties, making the adoption of traditional assessment approaches challenging. This project proposes taking a dynamic LCA (dLCA) approach to address these inherent uncertainties through iterative collaborative research with biotechnologists (Co-I) at the forefront of developing waste-derived sophorolipid production. The overarching goal is to apply the dynamic life cycle assessment (dLCA) framework to compare alternative pathways for bioconversion of organic waste to sophorolipids to guide its sustainable design. The project has three main objectives, 1) Model the life cycle of the waste valorisation technology to produce sophorolipid at the laboratory-scale, 2) Assess the economic and environmental impacts of alternative pathways for sophorolipid production at an industrial-scale, and 3) Prioritise future research questions to guide the sustainable design of emerging waste valorisation technology through repeated traversal of the dLCA framework. Successful application of dLCA will be transformative in its capacity to advance the understanding of the tradeoffs between systemic environmental costs and economic benefits for design decisions. Also, given the variation in the composition of waste streams for different regions, such a systematic evaluation of the environmental and economic implications will steer the selection of SL production pathways keeping location-specific sustainability in mind. This project's completion will provide new knowledge on potential unforeseen consequences associated with the eventual implementation of a full-scale waste-derived SL production plant. 日益增多的固體廢棄物是現今城市治理所面臨的一大難題。源頭減量、對廢棄資源再利用及再循環是應對該難題的基本思路。其中，運用生物方法將厨餘等有機廢棄物轉化為肥料、生物材料及燃料等高附加值產品是一個有發展前景的產業，亦可以有效降低垃圾填埋場的運行負荷。 在廢棄物加工轉化的衆多衍生品中，微生物表面活性劑是一個值得關注的產品。微生物表面活性劑是由微生物產生的一類具有表面活性的化合物，具有毒性低、易降解等特點。槐糖脂（Sophorolipids）便是微生物表面活性劑的一種，其在環境修復、個人護理化妝、洗滌、製藥和農業等行業都有著廣闊的應用前景。目前科學實驗已證明了對厨餘等有機廢棄物進行生物轉化以生產槐糖脂的可行性，但該技術方案仍需更多的評估及優化以實現規模化可持續生產。生命周期評價及技術經濟分析方法是用於評估新興技術環境影響、技術可行性、經濟回報的主流方法，但其使用亦受到了數據匱乏陳舊、技術快速迭代等因素限制。 本項目將采用動態生命周期評價的框架，通過評估專才與生物科技專才的緊密合作，高效地采集及模擬由有機廢棄物生產槐糖脂各個階段的相關數據，以比對選定最佳技術路綫。本項目具體包括以下目標：1）基於實驗室數據對有機廢棄物生產槐糖脂各個生命周期進行建模；2）評估規模化生產條件下有機廢棄物生產槐糖脂各技術路綫的環境影響和經濟效益；3）基於動態生命周期評價結果指導有機廢棄物生產槐糖脂的研究課題的選定，促進相關產品的可持續生產。 本項目聚焦全生命周期的有機廢棄物資源化利用，及時追蹤相關技術發展過程中效益與風險的變化，開展多維度的綜合評估，將為由有機廢棄物生產槐糖脂的研發及規模化生產提供可持續策略支持，提升相關生產的經濟效益、並有效規避潛在的環境風險。

11300021.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11300021.value: 这个项目的目的是关于欧拉流的正则激波反射-衍射问题发展严格的数学理论。特别是，它将主要关注二维可压缩欧拉方程控制的正则激波反射-衍射问题的解的全局存在性，以及其他相关问题。 欧拉流正则激波反射-衍射问题解的全局存在性是数学流体动力学中一个长期存在的公开问题。有严重的分析困难，如双曲-椭圆耦合混合型非线性偏微分方程，自由具有角奇异性的非线性退化偏微分方程的边界问题、低正则涡度输运方程的退化等。此外，激波反射-衍射问题是典型的二维黎曼问题之一，其解为多维双曲守恒定律的一般熵解的局部形态、局部结构和大时间渐近状态。在本项目中，我们将首先尝试建立楔角接近直角时正则激波反射-衍射解的全局存在性。接下来，我们将考虑解的几何结构，例如衍射跨音速激波的凸性，以及其他相关问题。为解决本项目中的问题而发展的任何技术和方法将有助于其他具有类似困难的问题以及高超声速守恒定律系统的数学理论。 关于自相似坐标下势流方程的全局解的存在性和几何结构，以及马赫反射解的局部结构的文献很多（参见 [1, 2, 4, 7{11, 14, 15, 17, 19, 21, 27、30、33、35、37、40]）。然而，目前还没有对等熵/全欧拉方程支配的全局激波反射-衍射解进行严格的分析结果。由于该主题在非线性分析和空气动力学中的重要性，我们基于为势流方程开发的技术，通过研究本项目中提出的目标来研究激波反射衍射问题是有价值的。我们多年来一直致力于解决相关问题。我们在[5]中证明了非线性波系统激波衍射问题解的全局存在性和最优规律性； [10]中势流方程的激波衍射问题解的规律性丧失； [11]中自相似坐标中跨音速激波的凸性； [12]中势流规则激波反射-衍射问题解的唯一性和结构稳定性。在这个项目中，我们将主要关注证明技术的进一步发展。获得的结果，研究上述目标。

11300421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11300421.value: Quantum technology, such as quantum computation, quantum cryptography, and quantum simulation, is likely to become one of the driving force for the development of human society in future. Such technologies have enormous potentials because they can achieve goals far beyond today's classical computer power. Recently, Google has announced that it has reached the first milestone towards such quantum supremacy. As a result, competitions on building infrastructures for future quantum technology has become increasingly important. One crucial step towards the realization of quantum simulation and quantum computation is the ability to store and coherently manipulate quantum information in an isolated quantum system. However, this is generally not an easy task. Conventionally it is believed that a generic quantum many-body system will eventually reach thermal equilibrium under its own dynamics. As a result, the initial state memory will quickly get lost to nonlocal degrees of freedom, and hence can no longer be recovered by a local measurement. What remains are the fluctuations of some conserved quantities, whose dynamics is purely classical. In fact, this notion is so widely accepted that many textbooks on statistical mechanics are built on the ergodicity hypothesis. Recently, however, people have realized that this classical fate is not inevitable. In particular, an isolated interacting many-body quantum system can escape thermalization if strong quenched disorders are present. This phenomenon, now known as many-body localization (MBL), has attracted enormous interest in the research community because all eigenstates in the energy spectrum break ergodicity. Thus, quantum information stored in a generic initial state may be retained for an extended period of time, which presents a great potential for quantum information storage and manipulation. In this work, we will study quantum information scrambling in a many-body localized system. Specifically, four main research tasks are outlined in this proposal: (1) Understanding quantum information scrambling in a many-body localized system; (2) Behavior of quantum information scrambling near MBL-thermal transitions; (3) The application of machine-learning techniques in quantum information scrambling; (4) Quantum information scrambling in generic out-of-equilibrium systems. This study aims at uncovering how the quantum information stored in the initial states spreads out in an MBL system, and the results will help us better understand how to utilize a generic many-body system for quantum information storage and manipulation purposes. 量子技術，如量子計算、量子密碼學和量子模擬，有可能成為未來人類社會發展的動力之一。 這類技術具有巨大的潛力，因為它們可以實現遠遠超出今天經典計算機能力的目標。 最近，谷歌宣佈，它已經達到了這種量子霸權的第一個里程碑。 因此，為未來的量子技術建立基礎設施的競爭已經變得越來越重要。 實現量子模擬和量子計算的一個關鍵步驟是能夠在一個孤立的量子系統中存儲和連續地操縱量子信息。 然而，這通常不是一個容易的任務。 之前人們認為一個通用的量子多體系統在其自身動力學的作用下最終會達到熱平衡狀態。 因此，初始狀態的記憶將很快消失，變成非局部的自由度，也就不能再通過局部測量恢復。 這樣的系統中剩下的只是一些守恆量的波動，其動力學是純經典的。 事實上，這一概念被廣泛接受，以至於統計力學的教科書普遍都是建立在各態歷經假說之上的。 然而，最近人們已經意識到，這種經典的命運並非不可避免。 特別是，如果存在較強的無序性，一個孤立但有相互作用的多體量子系統可以避免進入熱平衡態。 這種可能性引起了研究界的巨大興趣，因為能譜中的所有本征態都會打破遍歷性。 這種現象也被命名為多體局域化（MBL）現象。 在這樣的系統中，儲存在初始狀態下的量子信息可能會被保留很長一段時間。 這個特性也為量子信息的存儲和操作帶來了巨大的潛力。 在這項工作中，我們將研究多體局域化系統中的量子信息擾動過程。 具體來說，本項目中列出了四個主要的研究任務。 （1） 理解多體局域化系統中的量子信息擾動過程。 （2） 通過量子信息擾動過程來理解多體局域化與熱平衡態相變點附近的行為。 （3） 研究機器學習技術在量子信息擾動過程中的應用。 （4） 研究量子信息擾動過程在一般非平衡系統中的應用。 總之，本項目旨在揭示存儲在初始狀態下的量子信息如何在一個多體局域化的系統中擴散，其結果將幫助我們更好地理解如何利用一個多體系統來進行量子信息存儲和操縱的目的。

11300621.label: Project Objectives
11300621.value: To develop and analyse efficient, easy-to-implement, robust, competitive HDG methods for the biharmonic equation. We would like to provide discrete H2-stability of their numerical solutions on arbitrary Lipschitz polyhedra and obtain optimal convergences to the true solution and its Laplacian. To develop and analyse efficient, easy-to-implement, robust, competitive HDG methods for solving generalized eigenvalue problems of biharmonic operator and von Karman equations. 11300621.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11300621.value: 双调和算子是一个重要的模型问题. 它出现在诸如von K´arm´an 方程, Cahn–Hilliard 方程, 和the hydrodynamics coupled phase-field 模型. 所以，人们渴望拥有高效的，可靠的数值计算方法来逼近双调和算子. 大多数已有的求解双调和算在的数值方法属于以下这几类别：C1-协调元方法, Ciarlet Raviart (C-R) 方法, Hellan-Herrmann-Johnson (HHJ)方法, 非协调元和间断 (DG)方法. 这些计算方法有如下的缺点. C1-协调元方法的编程实现是不容易的. CR方法不能提供数值解的离散的H2稳定性, 而这种稳定性在数值求解一些非线性方程 (比如von K´arm´an 方程)时时非常重要的. HHJ方法有太多的全局自由度，这是因为它同时计算对解本身和解的所有二阶偏导数的数值逼近. 大部分非协调元和DG方法只对解进行数值逼近，以至于对解的拉普拉斯的逼近精度要低很多，而对解的拉普拉斯的高精度数值逼近在求解Cahn–Hilliard 方程, the hydrodynamics coupled phase-field 模型时是很重要的. P.I.的长期目标是从理论到计算层面，开发和研究高效的，可靠的求解双调和算子的数值计算方法，以此来避免上面提到的已有的数值计算方法种的缺点. 在这个研究计划种, P.I. 将主要关注研究和开发一种新型的数值计算格式 - 可杂交化的间断伽钌金(HDG)方法. 我们提出的数值求解双调和算子的HDG方法有可能避免上面提到的种种缺点. 在杂交化以后，我们的求解双调和算子的HDG方法的全局变量是对解和解的拉普拉斯在网格交界面上的数值逼近, 所以全局变量的数量不会过多. 对解和解的拉普拉斯的数值逼近也会被提供. 使用精心设计的数值解空间和数值流数, 我们的求解双调和算子的HDG方法可以在任意的Lipschitz多面体上对数值解提供标准的离散H2稳定性, 并且对解和解的拉普拉斯同时获得最优数值收敛. 这些特性使我们的HDG方法适用于数值求解 von K´arm´an 方程, Cahn–Hilliard 方程，the hydrodynamics coupled phase-field 模型和其他使用双调和算子做领导项的椭圆类和抛物类方程. P.I. 有兴趣研究开发高效的，容易编程实现的，可靠的HDG方法，来数值求解一类使用到双调和算子的椭圆类和抛物类方程.

11300621.label: Major findings and research outcome
11300621.value: The PI has given error analysis with polynomial dependence on the inverse of epsilon in SAV methods for the Cahn-Hilliard equation. Here epsilon is a parameter to describe the depth of the interface between two phases, which can be very close to zero. The discovery is important to analysis of SAV methods which preserve energy at discrete level. In addition, several important and related research outputs have been discovered. For example, error analysis of two-phase incompressible Navier-Stokes flow, pointwise stability of HDG methos for the heat equation.

11300721.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11300721.value: The proposed research project will develop computationally efficient algorithms with focus on their theoretical properties in a centralized or decentralized distributed computing environment. Unlike many existing studies on parametric models, the specific setting we investigate is nonparametric regression in the reproducing kernel Hilbert space. In such estimation problems, data are distributed on multiple machines for various reasons (for example for data privacy, or simply to utilize the computational power of multiple machines). First, for distributed estimation with a central machine that aggregates the local estimators obtained by multiple machines using local data, it is well-known that the number of machines that can be used in such a system is limited and thus the size of local data can still be large. We propose to use random projection on each machine to reduce computation. Theoretically, it is a nontrivial problem to establish that such a combination does not significantly degrade performances in the distributed setting. Second, we consider a decentralized system in which there is not a central machine that communicates with all others. Instead, each machine regularly communicates with its neighbors to exchange intermediate results. In such a setting, we propose a gradient method in the functional space combined with random projection. Again we will try to establish optimal convergence rates that depend on the network topology, the mini-batch size for the gradient method, the number of machines, and the approximation from random projection. Finally, we will consider extensions to general non-least-squares losses. We will also investigate the numerical efficiency through extensive simulation studies in large-scale estimation problems. 此研究項目將開發計算效率高的算法，研究在集中式或分散式分佈式計算環境中的算法理論性質。與許多現有的參數模型不同，我們研究的重點是再生核希爾伯特空間中的非參數回歸。在這樣的估計問題中，出於各種原因（例如為了數據隱私，或者只是為了利用多台機器的計算能力），數據分佈在多台機器上。首先，對於使用中央機器聚合多台機器使用本地數據獲得的局部估計量的分佈式估計，眾所周知，在這樣的系統中可以使用的機器數量是有限的，因此局部數據的樣本量很可能還是很大的。我們提出在每台機器上使用隨機投影的方法來減少計算。從理論上講，證明這種方法不會顯著降低分佈式設置中的性能是一個重要的問題。其次，我們考慮一個分散的系統，其中沒有與所有其他機器進行通信的中央機器。相反，每台機器定期與其鄰居通信以交換中間結果。在這種情況下，我們提出了一種結合隨機投影的函數空間中的梯度方法。我們將再次嘗試建立取決於網絡拓撲、梯度方法的小批量大小、機器數量和隨機投影近似值的最佳收斂率。最後，我們將考慮擴展到一般的非最小二乘損失。我們還將通過對大規模估計問題的模擬來研究數值計算效率。

11300721.label: Realisation of objectives
11300721.value: Distributed learning in an RKHS is an important topic in modern nonparametric modelling. In this project we mainly consider two distributed setups. In the first setup, using the server-worker model, there is a single server machine that aggregates the local estimator computed by all workers. In the second setup, all machines are peers and they iteratively carry our local computations and communicate with their neighbors to exchange information to achieve consensus. However, currently there is limited work in this area that provided practical (computational efficient) algorithm with theoretical guarantees in the RKHS. With the support of the GRF grant, we aim to consider these important problems. We have realized the proposed objectives, and for each objective we state how our published papers contribute towards the goal. 1. Establishment of the theoretical optimal convergence rate for distributed random projection in a centralized system "Properties of Standard and Sketched Kernel Fisher Discriminant" achieves the objective by first formulating the kernel Fisher discriminant problem using operator theory to define a clear population target. It then introduces a randomized sketching technique that projects the data into a lower-dimensional space to reduce computational cost. The core of the theoretical analysis shows that even with this significant dimensionality reduction, the resulting sketched estimator converges to the true solution at the same optimal rate as the standard, more computationally expensive, method. "Distributed Nystrom Approximation with Convex Lipschitz Loss" further demonstrated this result by establishing the optimal rate for distributed learning with Nystrom approximation. It provides a rigorous theoretical framework that incorporates both source and capacity conditions, proving that the one-shot distributed estimator with Nystrom projection achieves the same celebrated optimal rate as the central estimator. 2. Establishment of the theoretical optimal convergence rate for random projection with the gradient method in a decentralized system "Decentralized learning over a network with Nystrom approximation using SGD" directly accomplishes this objective. It provides a rigorous characterization of decentralized, gradient-based learning using Nystrom approximation. The paper establishes the optimal learning rate for stochastic gradient descent with mini-batches over a decentralized network, showing that the estimator on each node converges at the minimax optimal rate, subject to conditions on the network topology and algorithm parameters. 3. Execution of large-scale numerical studies for the proposed methods All three papers successfully include comprehensive numerical simulations to validate their theoretical findings. "Decentralized learning over a network with Nystrom approximation using SGD" performs simulations on decentralized networks, illustrating the method's performance with varying batch sizes, numbers of anchor points, and network structures (ring and random graphs). "Properties of Standard and Sketched Kernel Fisher Discriminant" carries out extensive simulations comparing sketched and non-sketched methods, demonstrating the computational advantages of sketching while maintaining accuracy. "Distributed Nystrom Approximation with Convex Lipschitz Loss" includes numerical studies for distributed quantile regression with Nystrom approximation, testing the method on both 1-dimensional and 3-dimensional problems with a large total sample size and various configurations of local machines and anchor points. 4. Extension of the proposed distributed estimation method to general loss functions "Distributed Nystrom Approximation with Convex Lipschitz Loss" makes a contribution in this area by extending the distributed Nystrom framework beyond least squares to a broad class of convex Lipschitz losses. This includes important examples such as quantile regression, logistic loss, and Huber's loss. The paper provides a general theoretical analysis and explicitly verifies the necessary conditions for the quantile loss, thereby establishing the optimal convergence rate for these general loss functions.

11300721.label: Major findings and research outcome
11300721.value: Our major findings and research outcomes are summarized in the following. 1) In a paper “Properties of Standard and Sketched Kernel Fisher Discriminant” accepted by IEEE TPAMI, we study learning of Fisher discriminant function using random projection. This is a more complicated situation than we originally planned, since we feel the least squares case is relatively simple. In this work, we provide an important theoretical understanding of kernel Fisher discriminant by first identifying its population target, which is not available in the literature despite the popularity of the methodology. Then, we established asymptotic properties of the finite sample estimator showing its statistical convergence rate. Due to the heavy computational burden of kernel-based method, we proposed the sketching (random projection) method that approximates the solution efficiently. Compared with other existing ad hoc approximation methods, our method comes with rigorous theoretical guarantee, showing the approximation is as accurate as the exact solution to the first order. 2) In “Decentralized Learning over a Network with Nystrom Approximation Using SGD” that appeared in Applied and Computational Harmonic Analysis, we carry out a study that is mainly related to the second objective of the GRF proposal. Here we consider the more complicated setup to decentralized supervised learning in the RKHS. In such a setting, an infinite-dimensional gradient descent algorithm is used by each machine and each alternatingly carry out a descent step and a communication step (to exchange the information about the current estimates). Again, we use Nystrom method (another specific instantiation of random projection) to make it possible to efficiently combine the information from the neighbors. We establish also the optimal convergence rate under suitable assumptions, that works for both batch gradient descent and for mini-batches based gradient descent (similar to stochastic gradient descent). 3) In ”Distributed Nyström Approximation with Convex Lipschitz Loss”, we develop a distributed learning method for nonparametric estimation in reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces, combining the divide-and-conquer strategy with Nystrom approximation. The key innovation lies in extending beyond least squares to general convex Lipschitz losses, including quantile regression and logistic regression. We establish that the distributed estimator achieves the minimax optimal convergence rate, matching what would be obtained using all data on a single machine. This optimal rate holds under standard regularity conditions, provided the number of partitions and Nystrom projection dimension are appropriately chosen.

11300721.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11300721.value: Based on the findings of these papers, several promising research directions emerge. A key next step is extending the decentralized gradient framework from "Decentralized learning over a network with Nystrom approximation using SGD" to general convex losses. This would create a unified, communication-efficient method for decentralized nonparametric learning beyond least squares. Further development should also focus on moving from synchronous to asynchronous decentralized algorithms, which are more robust in practical network environments. Additionally, investigating multi-round communication protocols, rather than one-shot averaging, could potentially relax current constraints on the number of partitions or improve convergence rates. A systematic study would involve first formulating the decentralized algorithm for a general loss, then establishing its theoretical convergence properties under asynchrony, and finally validating the approach with large-scale numerical studies on real-world distributed datasets.

11300721.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11300721.value: When data is too large for one computer, we split it across many machines. But combining results from these machines is challenging, especially for complex "kernel" models used in advanced AI. Our research tackles this problem. We developed new methods that let each machine work on a small part of the data. One method uses "sketches" to compress the local calculations, while another uses "anchor points" (the Nystrom method) to create a common, simplified model that all machines can use. This makes computation and communication between machines much faster. We proved our distributed methods are just as accurate as using one super-computer with all the data. Our work provides a scalable, theoretically sound blueprint for training powerful AI models on massive, distributed datasets without sacrificing performance, making big data analysis more efficient and practical.

11300821.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11300821.value: In this project, we aim to fully uncover and comprehensively study a peculiar spectral phenomenon of a global nature for the transmission eigenvalue problems, i.e. the surface localization of transmission eigenfunctions. Furthermore, we shall consider the corresponding applications of the surface-localized transmission eigenstates for problems of practical significance in inverse scattering theory and wave imaging associated with acoustics, electromagnetism and elasticity. The transmission eigenvalue problems are a type of non-elliptic, non-selfadjoint and nonlinear (in a certain sense) spectral problems that arise in the theory of wave scattering. They connect to the direct and inverse scattering problems in many aspects in delicate ways. The spectral properties of the transmission eigenvalues have received considerable attentions in the literature over the years due to their theoretical and practical importance. Recently, several studies reveal that the transmission eigenfunctions possess rich geometric structures. Nonetheless, most of the existing and ongoing studies are concerned with the local geometric properties of the transmission eigenfunctions, showing that they generically vanish around the corner or highly-curved parts of the underlying boundary. Meanwhile, a completely new and highly intriguing global pattern of the transmission eigenfunctions was discovered by chance in our recent study. It is found that the transmission eigenfunctions show a certain localization/concentration phenomenon (in terms of the $L^2$-energy) around the boundary of the underlying domain. That is, though vanishing around the corner or highly-curved parts of the boundary according to the local geometric property, ``many" transmission eigenfunctions tend to localize/concentrate around the boundary of the underlying domain. The corresponding finding, though still rather preliminary, has opened up an exciting direction of research for many potential developments. In this project, we aim to fully develop the corresponding study along this direction to completely uncover such a peculiar spectral phenomenon and gain a thorough mathematical understanding. We shall provide rigorous justifications and theoretical understandings of the surface-localized transmission eigenstates associated with the Helmholtz, Maxwell and Lame systems that respectively arise in acoustics, electromagnetism and elasticity. Then we shall study their qualitative and quantitative relationships to the underlying domains as well as the medium parameters. Furthermore, we shall consider the corresponding applications in super-resolution imaging, sensing and artificial mirage. The results achieved in this project shall not only enrich the geometric understanding of the spectral theory for transmission eigenfunctions in a global view, but also provide a new perspective on the wave localization, which is a central topic in mathematical physics. 在此項目中，我們主要針對一類獨特的全局譜幾何現象开展全面深入的探索和研究，即傳輸特徵函數的邊界能量聚集。进一步，我们将考虑其在反散射理论和波成像中的应用。我们的研究将包含声波、电磁波及弹性波。 傳輸特徵值問題是一類非橢圓、非自伴及某種意義上非線形的譜問題，其來源於波的散射理論，並在諸多方面有著深刻和精細的聯繫和關聯。文獻中有大量關於傳輸特徵值的研究，而最近的研究表明，傳輸特徵函數有著豐富的幾何結構，如其在角點或高曲率處消失。但此類關於特徵函數的研究均關注其局部幾何特性。此項目負責人同合作者最近發現了一類全新的全局性幾何結構，即傳輸特徵函數的邊界能量聚集現象。雖然此發現仍處於初期階段，卻開闢了一個全新的研究方向。我們將據此為研究的出發點，對此類獨特的譜現象進行全面深入的探究，在若干一般場景下，提供嚴格的理論論證及數學解釋。進一步，我們將考慮相關研究在超分辨成像及人工蜃景效應中的應用。此項目所產生的研究成果，不僅可以在一個全局觀點上豐富傳輸特徵函數譜幾何的研究，而且對數學物理中的中心課題之一，即波的聚集現象，提供了一個全新的視角。

11300821.label: Realisation of objectives
11300821.value: This project has successfully achieved all its stated objectives, establishing a comprehensive body of work that progresses from fundamental theoretical justification to the exploration of profound physical applications. The accomplishments against each objective are detailed below (please refer to Section 6.1 below as well as Section C for the related references). Objective 1: Rigorously justify and mathematically understand the surface localization of transmission eigenfunctions in generic scenarios for three types of transmission eigenvalue problems associated with the Helmholtz, Maxwell and Lame systems, respectively. Achievement: This objective has been fully accomplished and even extended. We have provided a rigorous mathematical justification for the phenomenon of surface localization across all three proposed physical systems through a series of high-impact publications. Helmholtz System (Acoustics): The surface localization of acoustic transmission eigenfunctions was rigorously established for generic scenarios in [1, 2, 7]. Maxwell System (Electromagnetism): The geometrical properties and surface localization of electromagnetic transmission eigenfunctions were justified in [6]. Lame System (Elasticity): The boundary localization and surface resonance of elastic transmission eigenfunctions were rigorously proven in [5]. Extension to Coupled Systems: Furthermore, we extended this foundational understanding to a coupled-physics setting, justifying novel geometric patterns of transmission eigenfunctions in [4,8]. Objective 2: Study the qualitative and quantitative properties of the surface-localized transmission eigenstates and characterize their relationships to the underlying domain as well as the medium parameters in different scenarios of mathematical and physical significance. Achievement: This objective has been comprehensively addressed. Our research delved beyond existence proofs to perform a deep qualitative and quantitative analysis of these eigenstates. Geometric Properties: In [6], we analyzed the geometric properties of the eigenfunctions in relation to the domain shape. Stratified Media: In [1], we provided a detailed characterization of boundary localization within the specific but physically significant context of spherically stratified media, directly linking eigenstate behavior to medium parameters. Spectral Patterns: In [5], we extensively studied the spectral patterns of elastic eigenfunctions, characterizing their relationships to boundary localization, surface resonance, and stress concentration, thereby connecting eigenstate properties to material parameters. Objective 3: Study the physical implications of the surface-localized transmission eigenstates and in particular apply them to problems in the inverse scattering theory and wave imaging associated with acoustics, electromagnetism and elasticity, including super-resolution imaging, sensing and artificial mirage. Achievement: This objective has been robustly achieved through the demonstration of several transformative applications, directly translating our theoretical discoveries into practical methodologies. Artificial Mirage: As a direct application in electromagnetism, we demonstrated in [6] how these eigenstates can be utilized to create an "artificial mirage" effect. Super-Resolution Imaging: We pioneered a novel inverse scattering scheme in [3], where the concept of invisibility, linked to eigenstates, is leveraged to achieve "super-visibility" and super-resolution imaging in electromagnetism. Sensing and Wave Manipulation: In the context of elasticity, we applied the surface-localized eigenstates in [4,5] to precisely generate and control "stress concentration," a critical phenomenon for material sensing and engineering.

11300821.label: Major findings and research outcome
11300821.value: This project established a unified theory for the universal phenomenon of surface-localized transmission eigenfunctions across wave systems, translating this fundamental discovery into innovative applications for wave manipulation and imaging. Major Findings: Universal Surface Localization: We rigorously proved that transmission eigenfunctions—waves that can exist inside an object without incoming fields—generically localize at the boundary. This was demonstrated across acoustics (Helmholtz) [1,2,7], electromagnetism (Maxwell) [6], elasticity (Lamé) [5], and coupled acoustic-elastic systems [4,8]. This universality reveals a profound spectral property linking object geometry to internal wave confinement. Quantitative Properties: Our analysis characterized how these eigenstates' behavior depends on the domain's shape and medium parameters. In stratified media [1], localization is precise. For elasticity [5], we linked these states to surface resonance and stress concentration, providing a mathematical tool for predicting field hotspots. Research Outcomes: Artificial Mirarage: We showed that materials tailored to support these eigenfunctions can create a "mirage," making a scatterer appear invisible or displaced [6]. Super-Resolution Imaging: We developed a paradigm-shifting scheme where "invisibility" (enabled by eigenstates) is used to achieve "super-visibility," breaking the diffraction limit for electromagnetic imaging [3]. Controlled Stress Concentration: We demonstrated that elastic eigenfunctions can be used to focus elastic energy with extreme precision, enabling targeted stress concentration for material testing and engineering [5,8]. 11300821.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11300821.value: This research establishes a foundational framework with significant potential for expansion. The immediate potential lies in extending the theory to more complex scenarios, including anisotropic metamaterials, time-evolving media, and stronger nonlinearities. Furthermore, the applications can be advanced from principle-to-proof to practical technology, particularly in designing meta-devices for super-resolution medical imaging and targeted ultrasound therapy. To that end, we will try to apply dedicated funding to develop a comprehensive computational framework for "eigenfunction-based inverse scattering," integrating data-driven methods. Moreover, we will foster interdisciplinary collaborations to translate these theoretical principles into functional prototypes for next-generation sensing and imaging technologies.

11300821.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11300821.value: Imagine you can make light or sound waves cluster perfectly at the surface of an object, like a skin-tight shell of energy. Our research discovered that this is a universal hidden property of waves, which we proved for sound, light, and even vibrations in solid materials. This discovery is significant because it gives us a new fundamental principle to control waves. We have already used it to create "artificial mirage" effects and design a new super-resolution imaging technique that can see incredibly fine details, much like a microscopic magnifying glass. It also allows us to focus stress inside materials, which can help in testing their strength and safety. In short, this work provides a new scientific toolset. Its value lies in paving the way for future innovations in non-invasive medical imaging, advanced sensing technologies, and new smart materials.
