11301121.value: 本項目研究通過解離生物正交反應調節無機和有機金屬過渡金屬配合物的發光特性和光細胞毒性，作為診斷和治療的應用。近二十年來，生物正交化學允許其在原生環境中研究生物過程和生物分子，從而促進了生命科學中各種新應用的誕生。雖然傳統的生物正交化學專注於生理條件下兩個反應基團之間的生物相容性連接反應，但人們對特定化學鍵可被生物正交反應裂解的解離生物正交反應或“點擊-釋放”反應迅速產生興趣。通過解籠鎖過程，生物正交裂解反應已成功應用於研究小分子和蛋白質的功能，設計基於創新反應的傳感和成像試劑，以及具有高度特異性和可控的載藥釋放。由於其有趣的光物理和單線態氧光敏行為、優異的膜穿透性和可控的細胞攝取特性，發光過渡金屬配合物在生物傳感、生物成像和光治療中的應用持續引起極大興趣。我們設想將過渡金屬配合物具吸引力的光物理和光敏特性與生物正交反應的特異性相結合將產生新一代的可激活生物試劑。在本項目中，我們將用具有優異發射猝滅能力的解離生物正交基團修飾過渡金屬配合物以調節其發光特性和單線態氧光敏活性。生物正交單元的裂解轉化不僅會使配合物呈現磷光開啟性質，而且會激活配合物的光敏特性，這將得到有趣的磷光開啟探針以用於可控的光細胞毒性、生物分子傳感和成像，以及研究蛋白質的活性和功能。儘管“點擊-釋放”策略已應用於不同領域，但我們相信探索具有解離生物正交反應性的光功能無機和有機金屬探針將大大拓寬生物正交化學的研究範圍，並進一步加強其在生物應用中的影響，這對化學生物學、生物化學和細胞生物學界將具有廣泛的吸引力。本項目將產生許多展示發光過渡金屬配合物在生物試劑開發中的獨特性質和作用的結果，這將大幅提升對活細胞和生命系統中的生物過程的理解，並為範圍廣泛的診斷和治療應用提供令人振奮的機遇。

11301121.label: Realisation of objectives
11301121.value: We have designed three rhenium(I) tetrazine complexes [Re(N^N)(CO)3(py-Tz-NHBoc)](CF3SO3) along with a PEGylated derivative. These complexes incorporate a dissociative carbamate linker, making them bioorthogonally activatable photosensitizers for the controlled induction of immunogenic cell death (ICD). Initially, these complexes exhibited weak emission and singlet oxygen (1O2) generation due to the efficient quenching effect of the tetrazine moiety. However, upon undergoing a bioorthogonal reaction with trans-cyclooctene (TCO-OH), the carbamate linkage was effectively cleaved, resulting in the detachment of the rhenium(I) polypyridine core. This transformation yielded rhenium(I) aminomethylpyridine complexes that demonstrated significantly higher emission intensities and 1O2 photosensitization efficiencies. Notably, the PEGylated complex showed minimal cytotoxicity in the absence of light. However, it exhibited significantly enhanced photocytotoxicity (IC50,light = 0.6 – 4.6 nM) against TCO-OH-pretreated cancer cells. Mechanistic studies revealed a cascade of cellular events, including lysosomal dysfunction, suppression of autophagy, and the induction of ICD. This study exemplifies the application of bioorthogonal dissociative reactions in the development of advanced therapeutic agents. In another study, we developed a comprehensive strategy that integrates enzyme-instructed self-assembly (EISA) with bioorthogonal chemistry to achieve the targeted accumulation and activation of ruthenium(II) tetrazine complexes, specifically [Ru(N^N)2(py-Tz-Ph)](Cl)2 in cancer cells. This approach employs a bicyclo[6.1.0]non-4-yne (BCN)-modified phosphopeptide, FFBCN, which features a phosphate group that is selectively recognized and cleaved by alkaline phosphatase (ALP), an enzyme that is notably overexpressed in various cancer cell types. The ALP-mediated dephosphorylation of FFBCN initiates a self-assembly process, resulting in the formation of large supramolecular assemblies. These assemblies significantly enhance the selective accumulation of BCN moieties within cancer cells, thereby providing a rich array of bioorthogonal handles. This is crucial for facilitating reactions with the ruthenium(II) tetrazine complexes, which in turn promotes the selective activation of their emission properties and the generation of 1O2 for applications in imaging and photodynamic therapy (PDT). A particularly noteworthy aspect is the incorporation of bioorthogonal dissociative reactions, which allow for the self-assembly process in response to specific biological stimuli. Our findings underscore the potential of combining EISA and bioorthogonal dissociative chemistry to create highly targeted and effective strategies for cancer therapy. We have designed three phosphorogenic iridium(III) bis-tetrazine complexes [Ir(dptz)2(N^N)](Cl) featuring two tetrazine moieties that serve as both bioorthogonal handles and emission quenchers. These complexes were non-emissive in fluid solutions but exhibited significant emission enhancement (I/Io = 561.6 – 3885.7) upon reaction with strained alkynes, such as BCN. The complexes were exploited for stapling peptides that bear two BCN moieties and for the fabrication of nanogels using a four-arm poly(ethylene glycol) (PEG) containing four BCN units. The resulting luminescent nanogel efficiently released encapsulated BODIPY dyes in lysosomes, confirming its potential for intracellular cargo delivery. In a separate study, we designed four mesoionic iridium(III) N^S complexes, [Ir(N^C)2(p-ttqt)], as PDT agents and ICD photoinducers. These complexes effectively generated ROS and oxidized NADH upon photoirradiation. They were essentially non-cytotoxic in the dark but exhibited extremely high and selective photocytotoxicity toward cancer cells. Mechanistic studies revealed that the complexes specifically accumulated in the endoplasmic reticulum (ER), where ROS generation triggered efficient ICD. We have also explored the use of specific dissociative reactions for various applications, including peptide and protein modifications, as well as enzyme activity studies. We developed three near-infrared (NIR)-emitting iridium(III) methylsulfone complexes [Ir(bpz)2(N^N)](PF6) as sulfhydryl-specific reagents. Upon reaction with cysteine, the methylsulfone group was cleaved, resulting in the formation of stable luminescent conjugates. One of these complexes was utilized to construct photofunctional peptide and protein conjugates. Notably, a conjugate incorporating an EGFR-targeting peptide selectively accumulated in the plasma membrane of EGFR-positive cancer cells and induced potent photocytotoxicity. In another study, we developed three iridium(III) 2-formylphenylboronic acid (2-FPBA) complexes [Ir(N^C)2(bpy-2-FPBA)](PF6) for the selective modification of N-terminal cysteine (N-Cys) in peptides and proteins. These complexes exhibited high reactivity, chemoselectivity, and regioselectivity toward N-Cys. One of the complexes was conjugated to various organelle-targeting peptides, resulting in conjugates that specifically localized to the mitochondria, ER, or Golgi apparatus in cancer cells, where they exhibited potent photocytotoxicity. Additionally, we designed a phosphorogenic peptide substrate for furin by conjugating a 2-FPBA complex with an emission quencher, QSY-7, to a furin-cleavable peptide. Specific enzymatic cleavage of the peptide spatially separated the luminophore from the quencher, leading to emission enhancement and the generation of 1O2. We have designed three iridium(III) 2-cyanobenzothiazole (CBT) complexes [Ir(N^C)2(bpy-CBT)](PF6) as site-specific labels for N-Cys and utilized bioorthogonal dissociative reactions for cancer targeting studies. All the complexes exhibited high reactivity and selectivity toward N-Cys, forming a luciferin-like linkage for bioconjugation. One of the complexes was employed to label a matrix metalloproteinase (MMP)-2/9-sensitive peptide modified with QSY-7. The resulting conjugate displayed emission turn-on and 1O2 generation in the presence of MMP-2/9, which cleaved the peptide and separated the iridium(III) complex from the quenching QSY-7 moiety. Additionally, the CBT complex was utilized to form two types of hydrogels, namely Gel-1 and Gel-2. Gel-1 was a non-biodegradable hydrogel that served as a 3D cell culture scaffold with integrated MMP-2/9 sensing for enzyme activity studies, while Gel-2 was a biodegradable hydrogel that functioned as an MMP-2/9-sensitive carrier for the targeted delivery of luminescent iridium(III) complexes into cancer cells for imaging and PDT. Recently, we developed an iridium(III) 3-chloro-6-thio-1,2,4,5-tetrazine complex [Ir(pqe)2(bpy-CONH-S-Tz-Cl)](PF6) and conjugated it with an integrin-targeting RGD peptide to yield a tumor-targeting conjugate featuring a photoresponsive S,S-tetrazine unit for cancer phototherapy. This conjugate exhibited weak emission and negligible 1O2 generation due to the presence of the tetrazine unit. Upon light irradiation, the S,S-tetrazine moiety underwent specific dissociation, yielding thiocyanate and amide products, which resulted in increased emission intensities and enhanced 1O2 generation efficiencies. Remarkably, the conjugate demonstrated higher cellular uptake in integrin-overexpressing U87-MG cells compared to MCF-7 and HEK293 cells, which have low integrin expression levels. This led to greater photocytotoxicity toward U87-MG cells due to effective integrin targeting, efficient release of the highly cytotoxic iridium(III) thiocyanate and amide complexes, and enhanced 1O2 photosensitization. Furthermore, we developed three dendritic iridium(III) guanidinium complexes [Ir(N^C)2(bpy-Gu9)](Cl)10 as molecular glues. Upon photoirradiation, all the complexes displayed intense emission and efficient 1O2 generation. These complexes were utilized to modify doxorubicin (DOX)-loaded, disulfide-crosslinked BSA nanoparticles, constructing a GSH-responsive nanoplatform for combined chemotherapy and PDT. Upon reaction with GSH, which is abundant in cancer cells, the disulfide bonds in the nanoparticles were selectively cleaved, leading to nanoparticle disassembly and the subsequent release of both DOX and the photoactive complexes to induce apoptosis. In summary, we have designed transition metal complexes, along with related bioconjugates and nanoplatforms, that dissociate upon reaction with specific bioorthogonal groups, enzymes, thiols, or light. These dissociative reactions can modulate the photophysical and photochemical properties of the complexes, as well as their (photo)cytotoxic activity. The complexes, bioconjugates, and nanoplatforms generated in this project have been successfully applied in various applications, including organelle staining, enzyme activity monitoring, cancer cell imaging, and cancer-targeted PDT. Our results demonstrate that these innovative reagents hold significant potential for theranostic applications, where they can be used not only for diagnosis but also for targeted treatment. By leveraging the unique properties of these transition metal complexes, we can enhance the specificity and efficacy of therapeutic interventions, paving the way for more effective cancer treatments and improved patient outcomes. The versatility of these systems highlights their importance in advancing the field of targeted therapy and personalized medicine.

11301121.label: Major findings and research outcome
11301121.value: We have developed rhenium(I) tetrazine complexes that incorporate a dissociative carbamate linker, serving as bioorthogonally activatable photosensitizers for ICD induction. The reaction with TCO-OH triggered carbamate cleavage, releasing highly photocytotoxic rhenium(I) aminomethylpyridine complexes that, upon photoirradiation, induced lysosomal dysfunction, autophagy suppression, and ICD. This work represents the first example of leveraging bioorthogonal dissociation reactions for controlled ICD induction. A novel concerted strategy combining EISA and bioorthogonal chemistry has been established to enable cancer-selective imaging and PDT using phosphorogenic ruthenium(II) tetrazine complexes. The ALP-catalyzed removal of the phosphate group on FFBCN triggered peptide self-assembly into large supramolecular structures, facilitating the selective accumulation of BCN units in ALP-overexpressing cancer cells. The enhanced photocytotoxicity observed for these assemblies in intracellular regions underscores the critical role of localization for effective PDT. We have also designed phosphorogenic iridium(III) bis-tetrazine complexes that serve as both a bioorthogonal handle and an emission quencher for peptide stapling and nanogel fabrication. These complexes exhibited high reactivity and selectivity toward bis-cyclooctynylated substrates, demonstrating significant emission enhancement following the reaction. One of the complexes was utilized to prepare a luminescent nanogel that released encapsulated BODIPY dyes in lysosomes, showcasing great potential for cargo delivery. Additionally, we explored other dissociative reactions for theranostic applications. We designed N-Cys-selective iridium(III) 2-FPBA and CBT complexes and utilized them to develop enzyme-responsive peptide-based phototheranostic agents. These peptide conjugates exhibited emission turn-on and 1O2 generation when their sequences were specifically recognized and cleaved by furin or MMP-2/9, which are overexpressed in cancer cells, enabling cancer-specific imaging and PDT. We also synthesized MMP-2/9-sensitive hydrogels that serve as either non-biodegradable scaffolds for evaluating enzyme activity in 3D cell cultures or biodegradable carriers for cancer-targeted delivery of photoactive iridium(III) complexes for imaging and PDT. Furthermore, we developed an iridium(III) 3-chloro-6-thio-1,2,4,5-tetrazine complex and conjugated it with an RGD peptide, resulting in a tumor-targeting conjugate featuring a photosensitive S,S-tetrazine unit for cancer phototherapy. The emission intensity and 1O2 generation efficiency of the conjugate significantly increased upon light irradiation due to the photodissociation of the quenching S,S-tetrazine moiety. Remarkably, the conjugate displayed higher cellular uptake and photocytotoxicity in integrin-overexpressing cancer cells. Finally, we designed decacationic dendritic iridium(III) guanidinium complexes as molecular glues and utilized them to modify GSH-responsive, DOX-loaded BSA nanoparticles, creating an innovative nanoplatform for combined chemotherapy and PDT. Reaction with GSH cleaved the disulfide bonds and dissociated the nanoparticles, releasing both DOX and the iridium(III) complexes to induce apoptosis.

11301121.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11301121.value: We have successfully developed transition metal complexes, bioconjugates, and nanoplatforms that dissociate upon specific reactions with bioorthogonal groups, thiols, enzymes, or light. Our research has revealed that the intriguing photophysical and photochemical properties of transition metal complexes can be modulated by these dissociative reactions, making them versatile for applications such as organelle staining, enzyme activity monitoring, cancer cell imaging, and cancer-targeted PDT. Our studies primarily focused on bioorthogonal reactions between tetrazine and BCN/TCO. To expand the scope of these investigations, we propose broadening the trigger molecules of the bioorthogonally dissociable transition metal tetrazine complexes to include vinyl ethers, benzonorbornadienes, and 3-isocyanopropyl derivatives, each exhibiting different dissociation reaction kinetics for a range of applications. Additionally, exploring dissociative reactions for constructing logic-gated complexes that display emission and ROS generation only upon two distinct bioorthogonal reactions may offer a promising strategy for precise imaging and therapy. Further development should also focus on enhancing the performance of metal complexes by improving their two-photon absorption and emission at longer wavelengths, which would be beneficial for in vivo studies in animal models. By advancing these areas, we aim to improve the application of transition metal complexes in biomedical research, ultimately enhancing their efficacy in theranostic contexts.

11301121.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11301121.value: Bioorthogonal chemistry has enabled the study of biological molecules in their native environments, facilitating a wide range of novel applications across the life sciences. While traditionally focused on ligation reactions, recent attention has shifted to dissociative bioorthogonal reactions, in which specific chemical bonds are cleaved in response to a bioorthogonal trigger. These highly specific cleavage reactions have been utilized for the uncaging of protein or drug molecules, reaction-based imaging, and payload release with excellent spatial and temporal precision. In this project, we have applied dissociative bioorthogonal chemistry for the first time to modulate the luminescence properties, photochemical behavior, and (photo)cytotoxic activity of transition metal complexes. We have developed bioorthogonally dissociable transition metal complexes that are initially non-emissive and non-(photo)cytotoxic but exhibit a significant increase in their emission intensity and (photo)cytotoxicity following bioorthogonal cleavage, enabling their use in imaging and controlled therapeutic delivery. This strategy harnesses the unique photophysical and photochemical properties of transition metal complexes while adding a level of control via bioorthogonal triggers. Our approach provides a novel platform for targeted imaging and photodynamic therapy. We firmly believe that our findings will not only expand the bioorthogonal toolbox for biomedical research but also provide new directions in theranostic design.

11301321.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11301321.value: 雜萜是部分結構來源於萜類生物合成途徑的天然產物。雜萜類化合物的雜合性質決定了該類化合物的化學多樣性和廣泛的生物活性。盡管雜萜類化合物在自然界中廣泛分布，但真菌來源的雜萜化學多樣性更為豐富。因此，近年來真菌雜萜類化合物的生物合成得到了廣泛的研究。盡管如此，仍有許多結構有趣的真菌雜萜類化合物的生物合成途徑尚未闡明，對這些化合物的生物合成研究將豐富參與有趣化學反應的酶庫。此外，特征生物合成基因數量的不斷增加和基因組序列的快速積累意味著，充分利用現有的遺傳信息可以有效地獲得新的有用的分子。本項目旨在：（1）從真菌雜萜的生物合成途徑中發現新的酶學；（2）通過激活沉默基因簇獲得新的雜萜類化合物；（3）構建人工生物合成途徑合成“人工”天然產物。 為了實現上述目標，首先將通過異源重組兩種類似的真菌天然產物 setosusin 和 brevione E的生物合成途徑進行初步研究，因為這兩種化合物都具有獨特的結構特征。負責構建這些有趣分子結構的酶將被生化表征，以概述可能的反應機製。接下來，將嚐試利用基因組挖掘和生物合成工程的方法獲得新的真菌雜萜。最後，將建立一種使真菌天然產物生物合成快速有效重建的新方法。使用這種方法，異源表達在公開基因組序列中發現的未表征的基因簇，從而發現新的真菌雜萜。該方法還將用於創建不同來源的生物合成基因的合成代謝途徑，這將拓寬真菌雜萜的化學空間。 綜上所述，該項目將揭示真菌雜萜生物合成途徑中新穎的酶反應機製，並將產生一些新的化合物分子，其中一些可能具有強大的生物活性。本項目將要開發的方法可廣泛應用於真菌天然產物的生物合成研究，從而進一步推動我們對真菌天然產物的生物合成的研究。

11301321.label: Realisation of objectives
11301321.value: Objective 1: Elucidation of the complete biosynthetic pathways of fungal meroterpenoids, setosusin and brevione E. This objective has been completely realized. Fortunately, the complete biosynthetic pathway of setosusin was elucidated before the initiation of the project. In this project, the biosynthetic gene cluster for brevione E was initially identified, and its biosynthesis was successfully reconstituted in the heterologous fungus Aspergillus oryzae. Further in vivo and in vitro characterization of biosynthetic enzymes led to the elucidation of the biosynthetic pathway. Additionally, the structure of brevione E was revised in this project. Objective 2: Mechanistic investigation of the enzymatic reactions responsible for the construction of the complex molecular architecture of the abovementioned molecules. This objective has been completely realized. First, the α-ketoglutarate-dependent dioxygenase BrvJ was characterized to be responsible for the formation of the cycloheptenone moiety in brevione E biosynthesis. Interestingly, SetK, a close homologue of BrvJ in setosusin biosynthesis, only performs simple hydroxylation on the same substrate. Protein structure modelling and subsequent mutational experiments identified the key amino acid residues that dictate the product selectivity. Additionally, our mechanistic investigation revealed the presence of an unusual SAM-dependent decarboxylase BrvO. Objective 3: Development of a methodology that facilitates genome mining and biosynthetic engineering of fungal natural products. This objective has been completely realized. One of the major problems with genome mining targeting fungal meroterpenoids was the inability to detect key biosynthetic enzymes for these molecules using the available bioinformatic tools. We have created a fungal biosynthetic gene cluster database, the FunBGCs database, which was then utilized as the foundation to develop a genome mining tool, FunBGCeX. FunBGCeX was successfully applied to identify several meroterpenoid gene clusters with unusual features. Additionally, synthetic biology and enzyme engineering approaches were successfully established to obtain new meroterpenoid species. Objective 4: Obtaining new fungal meroterpenoids by heterologously reconstituting unexploited gene clusters for fungal meroterpenoids. This objective has been completely realized. As mentioned above, by applying (global) genome mining strategy, several unexploited biosynthetic gene clusters were identified. Experimental characterization of these clusters resulted in the discovery of a number of previously undescribed meroterpenoid molecules. Objective 5: Synthesis of new fungal meroterpenoids by biosynthetic engineering approach. This objective has been completely realized. First, by coexpressing 5-methylorsellinic acid (5-MOA) synthase and genes for the biosynthesis of 3,5-dimethylorsellinic acid (DMOA)-derived meroterpenoids, a series of unnatural meroterpenoid species were obtained. In another study, by rationally introducing a mutation to a prenyltransferase, an unnatural metabolite with a different length of prenyl chain was created. Objective 6: Elucidation of the biosynthetic pathways of the new metabolites obtained above in case that they harbor a characteristic structure. This objective has been completely realized. The complete biosynthetic pathways leading to insuetolides, meroterpenoids discovered from Aspergillus insuetus by genome mining, have been established. This biosynthetic route involves an unusual terpene cyclase, InsA7, which folds its substrate into a pre-boat-chair conformation. Furthermore, a drimane–phthalide hybrid obtained by the heterologous expression of a biosynthetic gene cluster from Annulohypoxylon moriforme was found to be synthesized via a cyclization of the farnesyl group unusually installed by the dimethylallyltryptophan synthase-type prenyltransferase MfmD. Objective 7: Evaluation of the biological activities of the compounds obtained in this project. This objective has been partially realized. Regarding biological activities, only moderate or weak antimicrobial activity was observed for a few metabolites obtained in this study. To complement this, we worked on the biosynthesis of known bioactive natural products, which would contribute to the efficient production of these molecules.

11301321.label: Major findings and research outcome
11301321.value: This project elucidated, for the first time, the biosynthesis of the allelopathic agent brevione E by identifying its biosynthetic gene cluster and reconstructing the pathway both in vivo and in vitro. These efforts led to the complete elucidation of the biosynthetic pathway of brevione E and a structural revision of the molecule (Ref. 1). In addition, biosynthetic studies on several other meroterpenoids and related natural products were also performed (Ref. 8, 12). Another major component of this project was the genome mining–guided discovery of natural products. We first applied conventional genome mining to identify novel meroterpenoids, resulting in the isolation of previously unreported compounds (Ref. 2). Furthermore, we developed a genome mining tool, FunBGCeX, which was subsequently used to discover structurally unprecedented molecules and uncover unusual biosynthetic mechanisms (Ref. 6, 7). We also carried out in-depth biochemical and mechanistic characterization of enzymes involved in fungal meroterpenoid biosynthesis (Ref. 4, 5, 9). A representative example is the functional analysis of transmembrane terpene cyclases. By integrating AlphaFold2-generated structural models with targeted mutagenesis, we gained insights into their catalytic mechanisms and product selectivity (Ref. 4). Furthermore, engineered biosynthetic pathways for producing unnatural meroterpenoids were successfully established (Ref. 3, 10). For example, the biosynthetic pathways of 3,5-dimethylorsellinic acid (DMOA)-derived meroterpenoids were reprogrammed by replacing the native DMOA synthase with a 5-methylorsellinic acid (5-MOA) synthase, leading to the generation of several new meroterpenoid species. In summary, this project unveiled previously unknown biosynthetic mechanisms in fungal meroterpenoid pathways, expanded the structural diversity of meroterpenoid molecules, and established an efficient genome mining strategy. Collectively, these findings will facilitate future research in fungal natural product biosynthesis and biosynthetic engineering.

11301321.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11301321.value: With the rapid expansion of available fungal genomes, our genome-mining tool has the potential to uncover many additional, yet-unexplored biosynthetic gene clusters for meroterpenoid natural products. Systematic characterization of these clusters will likely reveal new structural scaffolds and further broaden the chemical diversity accessible from fungal meroterpenoids. In addition, this project has identified several enzymes exhibiting unusual or previously uncharacterized functions. Their detailed biochemical and mechanistic analyses remain to be carried out and will constitute a major focus of future work. Such studies are expected to deepen our understanding of meroterpenoid biosynthesis and provide a foundation for the rational engineering of biosynthetic pathways.

11301321.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11301321.value: This project set out to understand how fungi produce a group of natural chemicals called meroterpenoids, many of which have important biological activities. We also aimed to find new, previously unknown meroterpenoids by making use of the rapidly growing amount of fungal genome information. The project achieved several major outcomes. First, we clarified how fungi build some structurally complex meroterpenoids. Second, we developed a genome-based tool that can efficiently identify promising gene clusters for discovering new fungal compounds. Third, we analyzed the functions of key enzymes involved in making meroterpenoids. Finally, we engineered new biosynthetic pathways to create “unnatural” meroterpenoids that do not occur in nature, thereby expanding the variety of available compounds. Overall, this research has deepened our understanding of how fungi produce valuable natural products and has introduced a new strategy for discovering and creating meroterpenoids. These advances may contribute to the development of new useful molecules, including potential leads for medicines or other applications, in the future.

11301421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11301421.value: 光催化分解水是一種快速的製氫方式和有前途的可再生燃料，可減少我們對環境污染的化石燃料的依賴。整個反應涉及兩個基本的電化學過程：(i)光電陰極的析氫反應(HER)將H2O還原為H2；(ii)光電陽極的析氧反應(OER)將H2O氧化為O2。目前，使製氫經濟可行的主要挑戰是用作這些光化學電極的光催化半導體的高成本。此外，當今使用的最先進的水分解材料可以有效地用作光陽極或光陰極，但不能同時用作兩者！鎵硫屬化物(GaSe和GaS)正在成為適用於光氧化和光還原水的最佳替代材料，因為它們的電子特性可以通過化學摻雜和機械拉緊進行廣泛可調，以及它們靈活的二維 大表面積能夠最大限度地收集太陽能輻射。眾所周知，二維 GaSe 和 GaS 的表面實際上是惰性的，因此顯示出低的水分解活性。然而，人們鮮為人知的是，摻雜和拉緊究竟如何以及在多大程度上改變了它們的電子特性並改善它們的表面反應熱力學。該提案旨在基於密度泛函理論，對摻雜和拉緊對二維 GaSe 和 GaS 整體催化性能的影響的潛在分子原理建立理論理解。 HER和OER的光催化效率依賴於具有 (1) 合適電子特性的材料，通過它們的帶隙來描述最佳太陽光吸收，以及相對於H2和O2生成的各自氧化還原電位的導帶邊緣位置和(2)活性表面反應熱力學，由反應中間體的吸附自由能描述。一些選定的非金屬（例如 C、N、O、P 和 As）通常用作摻雜劑來改變二維材料的化學性質，將被考慮替代 GaSe 和 GaS 中的 Se 和 S 原子。改變摻雜劑和拉緊強度對上述表面特性的影響將在理論上進行示意性檢查並更好地理解。通過擬議的研究，我們預計了一些同時用於HER和OER的單一最佳集成GaSe/GaS 異質結構的理論發展。目前的理論設計對於未來光催化分解水生產氫燃料的高效材料的實驗製造具有重要意義。

11301421.label: Realisation of objectives
11301421.value: This project established a theoretical understanding of the structure–property relationship in oxygen doped gallium selenide (GaSe) and identify atomic configurations that enhance its catalytic performance for the hydrogen evolution (HER) and oxygen evolution reactions (OER). The objectives of this project have been fully realized through a rigorous and systematic density functional theory (DFT) calculations using Vienna ab initio Simulation Package (VASP) with the projector-augmented wave method and the Perdew–Burke–Ernzerhof generalized (PBE) functional. The Brillouin zone was sampled with a 5×5×1 k-point mesh, and a plane-wave cutoff energy of 500 eV was applied, with convergence thresholds set at 10−5 eV for energy and 0.001 eV/Å for forces. A monolayer GaSe constructed using a 3×3×1 hexagonal supercell. Oxygen doping was modelled by substituting one to four selenium atoms (GaSe1−xOx), corresponding to concentrations of (x = 6–22%), with multiple atomic configurations (e.g., lh, ld, L, O, Y) to understand how O substitution patterns control HER activity using adsorption free energy (ΔGH) as chemical descriptor, bandgap, and band-edge alignment using bonding analysis (PDOS, pCOHP, Bader charges). It showed that isolated O dopants (all separated by at least one Ga–Se–Ga unit, “ld-type” configurations) only weakly improve hydrogen adsorption and can even deactivate the surface as x increases, whereas adjacent O atoms around a common Ga center (“localized” O–Ga–O motifs such as 17% L, 17% O, 17% Y, 22% YO) weaken the Ga–O covalent bond, increase H binding at O, and reduce the bandgap into 2.09–2.21 eV window suitable for visible-light-driven HER. For these localized configurations the ΔGH becomes almost thermoneutral (ΔGH ≈ −0.13 to +0.06 eV), comparable to Pt and other benchmark HER catalysts, while conduction and valence band edges remain appropriately with respect to the H+/H2 and H2O/O2 redox levels. The study further demonstrated that modest in-plane tensile strain (up to ~1%) can be used as an additional knob to weaken Ga–O bonding, narrow the bandgap to ~1.95–2.05 eV, and fine-tune ΔGH within ±0.07 eV without losing proper band alignment, thus meeting the objective of jointly optimizing light absorption and HER kinetics via dopant configuration and strain. Projected crystal orbital Hamilton population (pCOHP) and integrated pCOHP (IpCOHP) analyses provide were carried out to an insight into bonding interactions. In GaSe₁₋ₓOₓ, the Ga–O bond is more ionic than the Ga–Se bond, with significant negative charge localized on oxygen atoms (Bader charge ~ −0.95 e). The covalent character of the Ga–O interaction, as measured by IpCOHP, inversely correlates with ΔGH. Configurations with adjacent oxygen atoms (e.g., 17% Y, 22% YO) exhibit less negative IpCOHP values, indicating a weakened Ga–O covalent interaction. This weakening of Ga–O covalent interaction enhances the affinity for H adsorption in HER. The IpCOHP reveal that oxygen atoms bonded to the same gallium centre (O–Ga–O), which reduces covalency and elongates the Ga–O bond and enhance the adsorption strength of H* in HER (Objectives 1, 3, & 4). Extending the GaSe1−xOx platform and dopant-geometry to the more demanding OER half-reaction, again using periodic DFT. Nørskov approach also used to compute adsorption Gibbs free energies of HO*, O*, and HOO* intermediates and the resulting OER overpotentials as a function of x and dopant arrangement. It confirmed that merely increasing O content or using a single, isolated O dopant enhances overall surface reactivity but does not by itself lower the OER overpotential, because all intermediates are stabilized similarly and O* often binds too strongly, making HOO* formation the potential-determining step with large overpotential. By systematically scanning configurations, the study showed that linearly separated ld-type dopants have little effect on the OER profile, while linearly adjacent lh-type dopants improve activity but still suffer from O* poisoning. Crucially, more localized three O motifs around one Ga centre (17% Y and 22 YO) alter the preferred O* adsorption site from a Ga–Se bridge to a Ga–O bridge and kinetically trap O* there, which weakens its effective binding and breaks the usual HO*/O*/HOO* scaling, yielding low overpotentials of ~0.58 V (17% Y) and ~0.38 V (22% YO) comparable to RuO2 and IrOx. These same configurations had previously been identified as near optimal for HER, so the combined results meet the project goal of identifying specific, experimentally realistic O dopant arrangements that simultaneously optimize HER and OER on the same GaSe1−xOx surface, providing a unified theoretical blueprint for bifunctional water-splitting catalysts based on O doped GaSe (Objectives 2, 3 & 4). We further studied a single ionic center solvated in water clusters as model systems to understand the formation of inserted [HMnIIIOH(H2O)n−1]+ intermediates from [MnI(H2O)n]+ via oxidative addition in the gas phase, which is a key process relevant to the HER (Objectives 1 & 4). The computational study, employing systematic DFT calculations, successfully elucidates how intracluster water activation converts highly reactive Mn(I) centres in hydrated manganese clusters into far less reactive Mn(III) hydride–hydroxide species. This transformation accounts for the experimentally observed inertness of larger clusters toward N2O. The investigation first established the size-dependent structures and spin states of [Mn(H2O)ₙ]⁺ clusters (n = 1–12), identifying septet three-coordinate Mn(I) structures as the ground state for all non-inserted forms, while low-lying quintet states become increasingly accessible with growing hydration (energy separation ≈20 kJ mol−1 for n ≥ 3). This proximity of spin manifolds facilitates intersystem crossing on experimental timescales and sets the electronic basis for water insertion. The point at which water insertion becomes favourable was pinpointed by comparing O–H oxidative addition barriers in quintet clusters against competing water evaporation. For n ≥ 8, the oxidative addition is both kinetically accessible and thermodynamically exergonic relative to evaporation, whereas the reverse reductive elimination from the resulting Mn(III) hydride–hydroxide is unfavourable. Consequently, the inserted Mn(III) form becomes energetically preferred and dominant in larger clusters, aligning with prior experimental estimates. The apparent lack of reactivity toward N2O was rationalized by contrasting the behaviour of Mn(I) and Mn(III) forms. Mn(I) clusters (both septet and quintet) form weakly bound linear N2O adducts initially, but electron transfer yields strongly exothermic bent N2O⁻ complexes (−55 to −220 kJ mol−1), indicating intrinsic high reactivity. In sharp contrast, the Mn(III) hydride–hydroxide species bind N2O only weakly (−30 to +7 kJ mol−1), stabilize no reduced N2O⁻ forms, and face high barriers (>90 kJ mol⁻¹) to insertion into Mn–H or Mn–OH bonds, rendering them effectively inert. Overall, the calculations reveal that under experimental clustering conditions, irreversible O–H insertion occurs early, followed by preferential water loss rather than reversion to Mn(I). The clusters that ultimately encounter N2O are therefore predominantly the inert Mn(III) hydride–hydroxide form, its weak N2O coordination masks the latent high reactivity of the underlying Mn(I) centre.

11301421.label: Major findings and research outcome
11301421.value: The rational design of advanced materials for energy conversion hinges on understanding reactivity at the atomic scale [1,2,4]. Atomic-scale control over defects, dopant configurations, and local environments tunes catalytic reactivity across 2D materials, molecular complexes, and ionic clusters for HER, OER, and related processes. We found that reactivity depends not only on composition alone, but also on the precise arrangement of active sites within their local environment [1,4,5]. For GaSe, DFT calculations show that replacing Se with O can either activate or passivate the basal plane depending on how O atoms are arranged around an Ga atom. Adjacent O atoms forming O–Ga–O units weaken Ga–O bonds (evidenced by increased IpCOHP values), yielding two key benefits: (1) it significantly improves hydrogen adsorption and brings the ΔGH close to the ideal thermoneutral value (ΔGH ≈ 0.02–0.13 eV); and (2) reduced bandgap (2.09–2.21 eV vs. 2.76 eV pristine), optimal for visible-light absorption. In contrast, isolated O atoms strengthen Ga–O bonding, raise ΔGH (to 0.75 eV), widen the bandgap (to 2.53 eV), and deactivate the surface [1]. A related OER study confirms that increasing dopant concentration alone fails to enhance activity and often worsens performance by over-stabilizing intermediates. Instead, a specific configuration—three O atoms bonded to one Ga atom—creates an optimal site that tunes binding energies of HO*, O*, and HOO* intermediates, particularly weakening the poisoning O* adsorption. This yields a predicted overpotential of 0.38 V [4], comparable to precious-metal catalysts like RuO2 and IrOx, and bifunctional HER/OER capability. Similar DFT simulations reveal that DMDS reduction by hydrated electrons is not a simple electron transfer, but a multi-step process controlled by the solvent's hydrogen-bonding network, with reactivity depending strongly on cluster size [5]. Likewise, anomalous HCl displacement from sea-salt aerosols by weaker acids stems from specific defect sites, not bulk thermodynamics, enabling a pathway unfavorable on perfect lattices via electrostatic induced stabilization [6]. Furthermore, hydrated manganese clusters demonstrate how solvent molecules mask intrinsic reactivity, with water pre-emptively oxidizing Mn(I) and rendering it inert to substrates like N₂O [3]. Therefore, the major contribution of this project is the establishment of a fundamental design principle: precise control over dopant arrangement or defect, rather than just concentration, is essential for developing high-performance, non-precious metal catalysts.

11301421.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11301421.value: Our DFT simulations have demonstrated that 17%-O, 17%- L, 17%-Y, and 22%-YO structures of O-doped GaSe are potential materials for water-splitting reactions. Among these structures, 22%-YO has excellent performance for both HER and OER. However, a single-material photocatalyst, such as 22%-YO, with a direct bandgap and suitable band-edge positions would often suffer a poor catalytic performance due to photoexcited electron-hole recombination. Heterostructures formed from two semiconductors are promising materials to overcome these drawbacks. Since overall water-splitting efficiency depends on the performance of individual materials respective for HER or OER, multiple-component materials often work better than conventional single catalysts. We expect that combinations of the best materials developed for HER and OER will offer basis components for constructing suitable heterostructure materials that provide efficient photocatalytic activity to generate hydrogen. Future works should examine the surface reaction kinetics, bandgaps, band-edge alignments, valence band offset (VBO), and conduction band offset (CBO) of these plausible heterostructures to identify the types of heterojunctions and overall surface activities.

11301421.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11301421.value: This project used advanced computer simulations to explore how clean hydrogen fuel more efficiently produced by splitting water using sunlight. The material used, called gallium selenide (GaSe), is not very good at this on its own. The key discovery is that adding oxygen atoms to GaSe in specific, clustered patterns makes the material highly effective for both producing hydrogen and oxygen. For the hydrogen-producing side, this tweak makes the material bind hydrogen "just right" and better absorb visible light. For the tougher oxygen-producing side, the right oxygen pattern creates a super-active site, making the reaction much easier. The big idea is that it is not just how much oxygen you add, but precisely how you arrange these atoms that unlocks high performance for both halves of the water-splitting reaction. The work provides a clear, practical guide for creating low-cost, earth-abundant catalysts that could enable efficient, clean hydrogen production through electrolysis or solar-driven water splitting.

11301721.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11301721.value: 金屬納米材料由於其獨特的物理化學性質和巨大的應用潛力，特別是在催化領域的應用，而引起廣泛的關注。近期，納米材料相工程（PEN）為金屬納米材料的功能調節與性能提升開闢了新的道路。除結晶相之外，無定形的金屬納米材料具有特殊的長程無序結構，從而展示出獨特的性質和優異的應用性能。特別是，無定形金屬納米材料具有大量懸空鍵、配位不飽和位點等缺陷結構，賦予它們明顯優於結晶相材料的催化性能。例如，本課題組已經證實鈀納米晶的無定形化可以顯著提高其在電化學析氫反應中的催化活性。 眾所周知，目前PEN主要專注於具有單一相的納米材料的研究，既結晶相或無定形。類似於由不同組分構建的異質結構，由結晶相和無定形複合而成的納米異相結構由於不同相之間的相互作用及無定形/結晶相界面的存在，可以在諸多應用中展示出優異的性能。近期，本課題組首次採用濕化學一鍋合成法成功製備了具有可控結晶度的無定形/結晶異相鈀納米片。重要的是，我們發現該鈀納米片的結晶度可以顯著影響其在4-硝基苯乙烯選擇性加氫反應中的催化活性與產物的選擇性。然而，受限於無定形金屬納米結構的熱力學不穩定性，通過濕化學法合成具有獨特性質和優異性能的無定形/結晶異相金屬納米材料目前仍十分具有挑戰性。 鑑於上述無定形/結晶異相鈀納米片優異的催化性能，我們進一步致力於開發有效的方法以合成多種無定形/結晶異相金屬納米材料，包括單組分金屬納米材料、金屬納米合金和異質結納米材料（如核殼結構、不對稱結構、分枝狀結構等）。在成功合成異相納米材料的基礎上，我們將系統研究它們的性質和催化應用，包括電催化（析氫反應、二氧化碳還原反應等）和非均相催化（如選擇性加氫反應）。此外，我們還將深入探究異相結構的形成機理及其結構-性能的構效關係。

11301721.label: Realisation of objectives
11301721.value: Briefly, the revised objectives have been achieved. A series of amorphous/crystalline heterophase metallic nanomaterials with well-defined compositions and architectures was prepared, their structural and phase-related properties were systematically investigated, their catalytic performances were demonstrated in representative electro- and heterogeneous catalytic reactions, and mechanistic insights into phase formation and phase-dependent catalysis were obtained. Several of the key publications explicitly acknowledge support from the Research Grants Council of Hong Kong (GRF), confirming that they are direct outputs of this project . 1. Preparation of amorphous/crystalline heterophase metallic nanomaterials The first objective was to develop synthetic strategies for amorphous/crystalline heterophase metallic nanomaterials with diverse compositions and structures (monometallic, bimetallic/multimetallic nanoalloys, and complex heterostructures). This has been comprehensively realized. A general one-pot wet-chemical method was established to synthesize three types of Cu@SnO₂ heterostructures (hemicapsule, yolk–shell, and core–shell), each comprising a crystalline, multiphase Cu core and an amorphous SnO₂ shell. The Cu core contains both thermodynamically stable fcc domains and unconventional 2H/4H/6H hcp domains with abundant planar defects, while the SnO₂ shell is fully amorphous, providing a clear crystalline/amorphous heterophase (Adv. Mater., 2022, 34, 2201114). A general seeded method was developed to synthesize hollow PdSn intermetallic nanoparticles with two distinct ordered phases (orthorhombic Pd₂Sn and monoclinic Pd₃Sn₂), providing a powerful example of phase-controlled multimetallic nanoalloys (Adv. Mater., 2023, 35, 2302233). Unconventional 2H-phase Pd-based alloys and 4H-phase Pd-based alloys were prepared on unconventional 2H or 4H Au templates, enabling the construction of core–shell and hierarchical heterostructures. These structures integrate multiple crystal phases within a single multimetallic nanostructure, consistent with the phase-engineered heterophase design in this proposal (Adv. Funct. Mater., 2025, 35, 2405073; J. Am. Chem. Soc., 2024, 146, 24141–24149; Nat. Sci., 2022, 2, e20220026). Using pre-formed heterophase Au nanostructures, a crystal-phase-selective oxidative etching strategy was developed to selectively remove 4H or 2H domains after coating with Pt-based alloys. This produced well-defined ladder-like Au@PtAg nanoframes and other hollow multimetallic heterostructures, again featuring coexisting crystal phases and complex architectures (Small Methods, 2024, 8, 2400430). A wet-chemical reduction strategy was developed for preparation of a family of amorphous multimetallic Pd-based nanomaterials (PdRu, PdRh, PdRuRh). These materials exhibit long-range disorder (amorphous phases) but well-defined nanostructures and compositions, providing a complementary amorphous platform to the crystalline and heterophase systems (Nano Res., 2023, 16, 4650–4655). 2. Study of properties of amorphous/crystalline heterophase metallic nanomaterials The second objective focuses on understanding the structural, phase, and stability properties of the heterophase nanomaterials. A key achievement is the in situ aberration-corrected HAADF-STEM study of ultrathin amorphous Ru, Rh and IrCo nanosheets doped with carbon, which revealed a three-stage nucleation pathway from amorphous precursors: (i) atomic aggregation, (ii) formation of lattice-expanded nanocrystals, and (iii) relaxation to final nanocrystals. The final products were unconventional phases (fcc Ru, hcp Rh and an intermetallic IrCo alloy), and in situ EELS and DFT showed that migrated surface carbon stabilizes these metastable phases (Adv. Mater., 2022, 34, 2206994). The crystal-phase-selective etching of heterophase Au nanostructures showed that unconventional 4H and 2H domains are more susceptible to oxidative leaching than the fcc domains, enabling controlled removal of specific phases and providing insight into their relative stability and surface reactivity. This not only generated new hollow structures but also clarified how phase energetics and reactivity can be exploited in post-synthetic transformations (Small Methods, 2024, 8, 2400430). 3. Exploration of catalytic applications The third objective focused on the usage of these heterophase nanomaterials as catalysts in electrochemical and heterogeneous reactions. This has been achieved across multiple representative reactions. The hemicapsule Cu@SnO₂ heterostructures were demonstrated as highly efficient CO₂RR catalysts, showing Faradaic efficiencies for C₁ products (CO and formate) above 90% over a wide potential window (-1.05 to -1.55 V vs RHE) and reaching 95.3% at -1.45 V vs RHE. This directly links architecture and heterophase structure to CO₂RR selectivity and efficiency (Adv. Mater., 2022, 34, 2201114). Hollow o-Pd₂Sn intermetallic nanoparticles delivered a mass activity of 12.9 A mg Pd⁻¹ for the glycerol oxidation reaction (GOR) in alkaline media, highlighting the importance of phase and morphology in tuning reaction pathways (Adv. Mater., 2023, 35, 2302233) Unconventional-phase multimetallic nanomaterials templated on 2H-Au nanosheets (e.g., Au@PdFe) were employed as efficient electrocatalysts for methanol oxidation, further supporting the phase-engineering strategy for alcohol oxidation reactions (Adv. Funct. Mater., 2025, 35, 2405073). Ladder-like Au@PtAg nanoframes exhibited HER activity in acidic media comparable to commercial Pt/C. In parallel, 2D/0D hierarchical Pd@Rh heterostructures grown on unconventional 2H-Pd seeds showed excellent HER performance, requiring only 21.3 mV overpotential to reach 10 mA cm⁻² and ranking among the best Rh-based HER electrocatalysts in acid. (Small Methods, 2024, 8, 2400430; Nat. Sci., 2022, 2, e20220026). 4. Mechanistic understanding of heterophase formation and phase-dependent applications The final objective aimed at understanding the mechanisms of heterophase formation and how phases govern catalytic behavior. This objective has been achieved. The in situ nucleation study on amorphous Ru, Rh, and IrCo nanosheets provides a mechanistic framework for how amorphous intermediates transform into metastable crystalline phases via multi-step nucleation and lattice-expansion/relaxation processes. This directly addresses the "formation of heterophases" aspect of the project by showing how unconventional phases can be deliberately accessed from amorphous starting materials (Adv. Mater., 2022, 34, 2206994). The PdSn intermetallic work showed mechanistically that the crystal phase of the Pd seed dictates whether the resulting intermetallic nanoparticles are hollow or solid, highlighting a phase-templating effect in alloy formation. The Cu@SnO₂ system revealed how subtle changes in synthetic conditions control the transition between hemicapsule, clarifying the structure-formation relationship in metal@semiconductor heterostructures. This offers a mechanistic route for post-synthetic phase and architecture engineering.

11301721.label: Major findings and research outcome
11301721.value: This project focuses on the Phase Engineering of Nanomaterials (PEN), specifically addressing the challenges in synthesizing and utilizing thermodynamically unstable amorphous/crystalline heterophase metal nanomaterials. The major findings and outcomes are summarized as follows: 1. Breakthroughs in Synthesis: We have successfully developed robust wet-chemical synthetic strategies (e.g., one-pot methods) to overcome the thermodynamic instability of amorphous metal phases. The controlled synthesis of various noble metal nanomaterials, such as Pd and PdCu nanosheets, with tunable amorphous/crystalline heterophase structures has been acheived. This allows for the precise engineering of the coexistence of long-range disordered (amorphous) and ordered (crystalline) domains within single nanocrystals. 2. Elucidation of Structure-Property Relationships: The project revealed that the abundant phase boundaries created between amorphous and crystalline domains are critical for modulating physicochemical properties. These heterophase interfaces, combined with the high concentration of unsaturated coordination sites and dangling bonds inherent to the amorphous regions, induce a unique synergistic effect. This structure effectively optimizes the electronic binding energy and adsorption properties of the catalyst surface, which is unattainable in single-phase counterparts. 3. Enhanced Catalytic Performance: The synthesized heterophase nanomaterials exhibited superior catalytic performance in key chemical transformations. o Selectivity: In the hydrogenation of 4-nitrostyrene, the heterophase catalysts demonstrated exceptional chemoselectivity, which could be fine-tuned by adjusting the crystallinity and aging of the materials. o Activity & Stability: For energy-related applications, such as the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) and electrochemical CO2 reduction, the synthesized nanomaterials showed significantly enhanced activity and stability compared to the commercial catalysts. In conclusion, this project established a general pathway for constructing amorphous/crystalline heterophases, offering a novel paradigm for designing high-efficiency catalysts for organic synthesis and renewable energy technologies.

11301721.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11301721.value: Although the catalytic reactions examined in this project span methanol oxidation, glycerol oxidation, hydrogen oxidation, hydrogen evolution, and CO2 reduction, the core strength and long-term potential of this work lie in the synthetic strategy for constructing amorphous/crystalline heterophase metal nanomaterials. Building on the current progress, further development will focus primarily on advancing the synthetic methodology. First, we will conduct operando and time-resolved characterization to directly capture key intermediates formed during the heterophase synthesis, thereby clarifying the mechanisms governing amorphization, crystallization, and interface formation. Second, we will develop new synthetic routes that enable more precise control over the phase composition, interface density, and metastable structures. Third, we will systematically establish correlations between crystalline/amorphous phase configurations and catalytic performance across representative reactions, providing a unifying framework for rational catalyst design. These efforts will consolidate the synthetic foundation of the project and open pathways toward more predictive and generalizable control of heterophase nanomaterials for catalysis.

11301721.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11301721.value: This project aims to develop new ways to make metal nanomaterials with specially designed structures that can speed up important chemical reactions. These reactions include producing clean hydrogen, converting waste carbon dioxide into useful products, and improving the efficiency of alcohol-based fuels. Although such reactions are essential for future energy and environmental technologies, today's catalysts often work poorly, are expensive, or break down too quickly. Our research focuses on creating metal materials that contain both ordered and disordered regions. This unique combination allows the material to behave differently from ordinary metals, making the reactions faster and more energy-efficient. By understanding how these structures form and how they influence performance, we hope to provide a new toolbox for designing better catalysts. The outcomes of this project may benefit society by supporting cleaner energy production, reducing carbon emissions, and enabling more efficient use of chemical resources. In the long term, the methods developed here could help industry create greener technologies and contribute to Hong Kong's efforts in sustainability and advanced materials research.

11301821.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11301821.value: The study of viruses' transmission is essential for understanding many diseases such as COVID-19, Ebola, AIDS, and SARS. Occasional mutations in the viral genomes may cause a major challenge in drug development. However, some mutations may help us create a new type of treatment by developing defective interfering particles (DIPs), which lack some viral genes essential for replication. In this project, we propose to buildld a mathematical model to study the virus spreading speed and a corresponding computational model with stochastic effects to study the spatial pattern generated by the interaction of viruses and DIPs. By comparing the simulations obtained from the model with different scenarios, we can understand the mechanisms for DIPs' effect. Our project aims to provide insight and framework tools to study the effect of DIPs in the virus spreading. Our results can inspire us to develop a new method to strengthen the effect of DIPs and give a potential answer for some biological questions related to virus transmission. The long-term aim of our study is to help medical scientists decide how to use DIPs to inhibit the transmission of viruses in a new treatment in the future. 病毒傳播的研究對於了解新型冠狀病毒、伊波拉、愛滋病和沙士等許多疾病十分重要。病毒基因組中的偶然突變可能會給藥物開發帶來重大挑戰。然而，一些突變中可能會發展出一些干擾缺損粒子而有助我們創造一些新型治療方法。 在這個項目中，我們建議使用數學模型來研究病毒傳播速度，並使用具有隨機效應的計算模型來研究病毒與干擾缺損粒子間相互作用產生的影響。通過將模型獲得的模擬與不同實驗結果進行比較，我們可以了解干擾缺損粒子的機制，從而提供框架工具來研究干擾缺損粒子在病毒傳播中的影響。這研究有助我們開發一此新方法來加強干擾缺損粒子的作用，並為一些與病毒傳播相關的生物學問題提供一些線索。研究的長期目標是幫助醫學家決定如何在新治療中使用干擾缺損粒子來抑制病毒的傳播。

11301821.label: Realisation of objectives
11301821.value: All the objectives were achieved under the proposed plan. We were working with Dr. Wai Tong (Louis) Fan (Mathematics, Indiana University) on a project. Our group had an online meeting with Dr. Fan biweekly. In the project, we built a mathematical model to study the effect of DIPs on the spread of viruses by applying stochastic models in a two-dimensional domain. Our work was verified by the data obtained by biologists.

11301821.label: Major findings and research outcome
11301821.value: In this project, we developed a model framework with a new hybrid method to study the spatial-temporal dynamics of viruses and DIPs co-infections within hosts. We presented two different scenarios of virus production and compared the results from deterministic and stochastic models to demonstrate how the stochastic effect is involved in the spatial dynamics of virus transmission. We compared the spread features of the virus in simulations and experiments, including the formation and the speed of virus spread and the emergence of stochastic patchy patterns of virus distribution. Our simulations simultaneously capture observed spatial spread features in the experimental data, including the spread rate of the virus and its patchiness. The results demonstrate that DIPs can slow down the growth of virus particles and make the spread of the virus more patchy.

11301821.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11301821.value: Our work can be extended to other biological systems of the dynamics of viruses. Also, our tool for studying the random effect of virus spread can be applied to study the role of stochastic effects in different types of biological models. One of our publications has applied the concept of our tool.

11301821.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11301821.value: The study of viruses' transmission is essential for understanding many diseases such as COVID-19, Ebola, AIDS, and SARS. Occasional mutations in the viral genomes may cause a major challenge in drug development. However, some mutations may help us create a new type of treatment by developing defective interfering particles (DIPs), which lack some viral genes essential for replication. In this project, we built a mathematical model to study the virus spreading speed and a corresponding computational model with stochastic effects to study the spatial pattern generated by the interaction of viruses and DIPs. Our results can inspire us to develop a new method to strengthen the effect of DIPs and give a potential answer to some biological questions related to virus transmission. The long-term aim of our study is to help medical scientists decide how to use DIPs to inhibit the transmission of viruses in a new treatment in the future.

11302121.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11302121.value: 具有交換偏壓耦合異質界面的材料在原子級別層面上的局部磁性、結構和化學信息對於預測和控製它們在邏輯和存儲設備中的物理特性和性能具有極其重要的意義。這亦能迎接對不斷增長的新節能信息和通信技術的需求的挑戰。 然而，由於目前可用的磁表征技術的空間分辨率的限製，直接獲得原子尺度的磁信息是非常具有挑戰性的。 為了打破這一瓶頸，我們最近開發了原子平面分辨電子磁圓二色性 (EMCD) 方法，該方法使我們能夠在原子水平上獲得定量的自旋和軌道磁矩，以及在透射電子顯微鏡 (TEM) 中進行納米級磁滯回線測量。 在這個提議中，基於我們在方法論上最新近的發展，我們的目標是直接可視化氧化物異質結中反鐵磁材料和鐵磁材料之間界面的原子級磁信息，並定量確定來自具有特定界面配置的納米級樣品區域的交換偏置場，目前沒有任何可應用的技術能夠達到這一目標。 除了磁信息，我們還可以通過將掃描透射電子顯微鏡與電子能量損失光譜和能量色散 X 射線光譜相結合，提供原子位置、元素組成和化學鍵的原子尺度信息。 結構、成分、鍵合和磁性信息可以從同一區域關聯起來，從而深入了解原子尺度上交換偏置耦合異質結的結構-性質關系。 該提議的方法論對於其它磁耦合接口也是一般且通用的解決方案。 此外，配備高相幹脈沖電子槍、雙像差校正器、電子能量損失光譜儀和超快速低劑量敏感相機的時間分辨像差校正環境（TRACE）透射電子顯微鏡已交付香港城市大學，並於 2020 年底完成安裝安裝。這一設備具有獨特的功能，它可顯著抑製數據采集過程中的輻射損傷和噪聲水平，這對於提高用於定量分析的實驗 EMCD 光譜的信噪比極為重要。 考慮到交換偏置耦合異質結在信息技術中的各種設備中的廣泛應用，該項目不僅能從根本上有助於理解原子級電荷、自旋、軌道和晶格自由度之間的協同相互作用，而且能夠為未來應用的磁性異質結構的新設計鋪平道路、改進設備性能。

11302121.label: Realisation of objectives
11302121.value: In relation to all three project objectives listed in Section 5.1, we have achieved them to 100%. How all three project objectives have been achieved to 100% are listed below, objective by objective. 1. In relation to the project objective 1 listed in section 5.1 1.1 High-spatial-resolution imaging of spin configuration, atomic positions, and chemical information of ferromagnetic oxides La0.7Sr0.3MnO3(published in Physical Review Letters, 129, 057201, 2022) We successfully conducted research on ferromagnetic (FM) oxides La0.7Sr0.3MnO3, which displays a Mn valence-modulated electrostatic shaping behavior. We obtained spatially resolved magnetization, composition, and Mn valence data. Our findings clearly demonstrate that the magnetic transition region is triggered by a subtle change in Mn composition, resulting in charge transfer at the interface due to carrier diffusion. 1.2 Atomic-scale visualization of atomic positions and chemical bonding of topotactically transformable antiphase boundaries of antiferromagnetic oxide Sr4Fe6O13-δ(published in Nature Communications 14, 7382,2023) The antiferromagnetic (AFM) oxide Sr4Fe6O13-δ exhibits a robust layered structure composed of SrO and FeO6/FeO4/FeO5 perovskite-type layers that alternate. Atomic-scale visualization of oxygen migration under oxidation-reduction conditions clearly reveals a reversible topotactic transformation between two configurations of antiphase boundaries (APBs). Our work unequivocally demonstrates that the antiphase boundaries of AFM Sr4Fe6O13-δ films are readily engineered through topotactic transformability, enabling precise manipulation of physical properties. 1.3 Theoretical optimization for detecting magnetism in two-dimensional ferromagnetic perovskite oxides by electron magnetic circular dichroism (EMCD) (published in Micron, 187, 103718, 2024) To achieve high-spatial-resolution EMCD imaging with a high signal-to-noise ratio, we performed comprehensive computational simulations to optimize the experimental conditions, such as sample thickness, accelerating voltage, Sr doping concentration, collection semi-angle and position, and sample orientation, in La₁₋ₓSrₓMnO₃ (LSMO). 1.4 Atomic-scale visualization of spin configuration, atomic positions, and chemical bonding of antiferromagnetic YFeO3(published in Miao Zhang’s PhD thesis “High spatial resolution electron magnetic circular dichroism of antiferromagnets”) We developed the beam-shift four-dimensional (4D) EMCD technique to determine three-dimensional (3D) magnetization vectors in the canted antiferromagnetic orthoferrite YFeO3, including the magnetic moment direction and relative strength, on an individual atomic plane basis, without prior knowledge of the directions of the Néel vectors. We achieved a lateral spatial resolution for the 3D magnetization vectors of the Fe atoms of better than 2.25Å. Spin canting and reorientation in YFeO3 can be directly correlated at the atomic scale with the corresponding atomic structure and elemental distribution. 2. In relation to the project objective 2 listed in section 5.2 2.1 Quantitative measurement of magnetization curve and exchange bias shift of individual ferrimagnetic NiFe2O4 nanograins coupled with antiferromagnetic BiFeO3 by using EMCD We have achieved the magnetization curve in a TEM on an individual single-crystal ferrimagnetic NiFe2O4 (NFO) grain in a NiFe2O4/BiFeO3 (BFO) nanocomposite thin film with exchange bias coupling by using magnetic-field-dependent EMCD. The experiments of NiFe2O4/BiFeO3 samples were carried out in a Lorentz mode with the out-of-plane external magnetic field perpendicular to the sample, varied from -0.4 T to 2.3 T by changing the excitation current of the objective lens in a TEM. By tilting the sample into the G = (004) two-beam condition, the Fe EELS signals of NiFe2O4 can be extracted by placing the objective aperture at “+” and “-” positions at the diffraction plane. The Fe EMCD spectra of NiFe2O4 can be acquired by subtracting two Fe EELS signals acquired at “+” and “-” positions from each other. The quantitative magnetic moments of Fe can be calculated according to the sum rule of EMCD spectra. The experiment EMCD spectra result of NiFe2O4 collected at the external magnetic fields of 674.71 mT and -298.47 mT, respectively show that the EMCD signals are negative at the Fe L3 peak and positive at the Fe L2 peak under the external magnetic fields of 674.71 mT, while the EMCD signals are positive at the Fe L3 peak and negative at the Fe L2 peak under the external magnetic fields of -298.47 mT. The reversed EMCD spectra at reversed external magnetic fields prove that the EMCD signals change significantly with the external field and therefore reflect the magnetization process. Following the sum rules of EMCD, the relative EMCD strength of Fe atoms can be determined quantitatively by integrating the corresponding EMCD spectra at Fe L3,2 edges at the various external magnetic fields, which is the magnetization curve based on magnetic-field-dependent Fe EMCD spectra. This magnetization curve possesses the vertical asymmetry in the saturation values, whose magnitude is about 20%-30% lower at negative fields. The exchange bias shift is about 0.1 T,which is contributed by the exchange bias coupling between ferrimagnetic NiFe2O4 and AFM BiFeO3. 3. In relation to the project objective 3 listed in section 5.1 3.1 Atomic-scale determination of cation and magnetic order in the antiferromagnetic triple perovskite Sr3Fe2ReO9 (published in Microscopy and Microanalysis 29, 326, 2023) We reported the investigation of the antiferromagnetic 1:2 B-site-ordered Sr3Fe2ReO9 triple perovskite using TEM experiments and first principles calculations. Atomic arrangement, cation order, and valence states were determined at the atomic scale for a nanosized region of this perovskite. High-resolution HAADF-STEM imaging with EDS confirmed the alternate stacking of Fe and Re cations without significant anti-site occupation at the three crystallographically equivalent sites. Additionally, first principles calculations predicted the magnetic ground state and exchange parameters of the cations, revealing antiferromagnetic coupling between nearest neighbor Fe and Re cations. 3.2 Atomic structure and magnetic order of exchange-bias-coupled interfaces between ferrimagnetic Sr2FeReO6 and antiferromagnetic Sr3Fe2ReO9 (published in REN Jie’s PhD thesis “Atomic structure and magnetic coupling of functional materials and their heterointerfaces”) We investigated the exchange-bias-coupled oxide interfaces between ferrimagnetic double perovskite Sr2FeReO6 and antiferromagnetic triple perovskite Sr3Fe2ReO9 with different B-site ordering periodicities. Atomic arrangement, cation order, valence states, and magnetic properties were determined at the interface by using HAADF-STEM imaging, EDS, EELS, and EMCD. First principles calculations on the superlattice model with the same modulation of B-site ordering periodicity observed experimentally show that magnetic coupling between Fe and Re atoms at the interface results in characteristics of ferromagnetism, in contrast to the antiferromagnetic nature of the parent phases. 3.3 Atomic structure and magnetic properties of the exchange-bias-coupled interfaces between ferrimagnetic NiFe2O4 and AFM NixFe1-xO We use an aberration-corrected atomic-sized electron probe to directly sculpt ferrimagnetic spinel NiFe2O4 bits within an antiferromagnetic (AFM) rock-salt NixFe1-xO spacer by beam-induced phase transition. The process is governed by a quantitative real-time feedback loop that translates atomic-resolution live imaging into deterministic control, enabling the on-demand fabrication of atomically sharp FM/AFM interfaces with the desired interface termination. Through in-situ nanobeam electron magnetic circular dichroism (EMCD), which probes the out-of-plane magnetization component, we perform single-bit magnetometry that demonstrates the detectable magnetic signals obtained from a ~4 nm size information bit surrounded by an AFM matrix with exchange bias coupling.

11302121.label: Major findings and research outcome
11302121.value: In this project, we have developed the high-spatial-resolution EMCD technique with nanoscale and even atomic-scale spatial resolution to characterize the ferromagnetic materials, e.g., La0.7Sr0.3MnO3, antiferromagnetic materials, e.g., Sr4Fe6O13-δ, YFeO3, LaMnO3, Sr3Fe2ReO9, and exchange-bias-coupled interfaces between antiferromagnetic materials and ferrimagnetic materials, such as Sr2FeReO6/Sr3Fe2ReO9, NiFe2O4/NixFe1-xO, and NiFe2O4/BiFeO3. The element-specific magnetic hysteresis loop measurements have been achieved, for the first time, in a TEM by using EMCD. The exchange bias shift of the NiFe2O4/BiFeO3 interface is determined as 0.1 T, in comparison to no obvious exchange bias shift in soft magnetic materials, NiFe2O4. Based on the relevant research results in this project, we have published ten journal articles (Items 1 to 10 in Part C-8). As the corresponding author or co-corresponding author, one article in Physical Review Letters (Item 3 in Part C-8), one article in Nature Communications (Item 9 in Part C-8), two articles in Microscopy & Microanalysis (No. 1 in the Microscopy Category, Items 1 and 7 in Part C-8)), one article in Chem (Item 10 in Part C-8), one article in Micron (Item 6 in Part C-8) were published. In addition, my students and I have delivered the 18 invited talks/oral talks/poster presentations at the international and regional conferences (Items 1 to 18 in Part C-9), such as the IEEE INTERMAG 2023 Conference, the 20th International Microscopy Congress, The 7th/8th Conference on Frontiers of Aberration Corrected Electron Microscopy, SCANDEM 2023 the 73rd Annual Meeting of Nordic Microscopy Society. To promote our research results, I co-organized the HKIAS Forum and the 5th Sino-German Symposium on Advanced Electron Microscopy and Instrumentation at the City University of Hong Kong in December 2025. All the outputs mentioned above have fulfilled the output dissemination plan in the original proposal. Five students are awarded the PhD degree. Their thesis titles, e.g., “Atomic structure and magnetic coupling of functional materials and their heterointerfaces”, “Spatially Resolved Electron Magnetic Circular Dichroism of Magnetically Coupled Interfaces and Antiphase Boundaries”, “High spatial resolution electron magnetic circular dichroism of antiferromagnets”, “Development of Spherical and Chromatic Aberration Correctors for a Compact Low-voltage Electron Microscope” are directly related to this project. (Items 1 to 5 in Part C-10) In addition, we also developed advanced electron optics components to better characterize magnetic materials and the FM/AFM interfaces. Five relevant patents were awarded. (Items 1 to 5 in Part C-11)

11302121.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11302121.value: The research platform established in this project offers substantial potential for further development along two closely related directions. First, we will build on atomic plane resolved EMCD and achromatic EELS to extend our studies to two dimensional perovskite oxides and van der Waals heterostructures, aiming to directly probe emergent interfacial magnetism, proximity effects, and possible topological magnetic states, and to identify structural descriptors that govern magnetic anisotropy and spin–charge coupling. Second, leveraging the quantified high frequency voltage attenuation and the stroboscopic TEM setup, we will investigate nanosecond–sub nanosecond magnetic and structural dynamics under electric, thermal, and optical stimuli, while optimizing pulsed electron sources, synchronization schemes, and data analysis pipelines for time resolved EMCD and EELS. The proposed course of action includes further upgrades of the electron source, correctors, and detectors, integration of advanced simulations and machine learning for quantitative interpretation of imaging and spectroscopy, and deepening collaborations with industry and international partners to translate the developed techniques and granted patents into specialized TEM platforms tailored for functional quantum and magnetic materials.

11302121.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11302121.value: This project set out to understand how magnetism behaves at the smallest possible scale—down to individual atomic layers—where different magnetic materials meet. These interfaces are crucial for modern technologies such as magnetic memory, sensors, and spin-based electronics, yet their behavior has long been difficult to observe directly. By developing and applying advanced electron microscopy techniques, we succeeded in visualizing atomic structures, chemical bonding, and magnetic configurations simultaneously and with unprecedented precision. For the first time, we were able to measure how magnetic properties change locally at interfaces between different magnetic materials, including the subtle “exchange bias” effect that stabilizes magnetic states in devices. We also demonstrated that atomic-scale structures at interfaces can be deliberately engineered and even written or modified using an electron beam, allowing precise control over magnetic behavior. The significance of this work lies in its ability to connect atomic structure directly with magnetic function. This provides a reliable experimental foundation for designing next-generation magnetic and spintronic materials. Beyond specific materials systems, the methods developed in this project establish a powerful toolkit for studying complex functional materials at the atomic scale, offering long-term value for both fundamental research and future technological innovation.

11302221.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11302221.value: Although small-molecule anticancer drugs such as platinum drugs are effective against a variety of tumor types, the adverse effects and drug resistance significantly limit their broader clinical applications. One promising solution is to develop novel Pt coordination compounds with controllable activation properties, which enable the drug to be activated in a spatially and temporally controlled fashion with minimized “off-target” effects. Along this line, photoactivatable Pt(IV) prodrugs, including diazido-Pt(IV) complexes and Pt(IV) compounds bearing axial photoactivators, have been extensively developed and explored. However, the light penetration depth remains a limiting factor, and photoactivatable Pt(IV) prodrugs may not be suitable for non-invasive therapy against tumors deep beneath the skin. In this proposal, we aim to address this problem by developing Pt(IV) anticancer prodrugs that can be controllably activated by ultrasound, which can penetrate deeply into the human body. Our preliminary study indicates that a carboplatin-based Pt(IV) prodrug bearing a sonosensitizer at the axial position can be activated by ultrasound, and this prodrug can also effectively kill cancer cells upon sono-activation. Based on this proof-of-concept, we plan to synthesize and characterize several types of ultrasound-activatable Pt(IV) complexes including those that are highly resistant to reducing agents. Stable prodrugs will be tested for their sono-activation properties under optimized ultrasound treatment conditions. The cellular accumulation levels, cytotoxicity, and cell death mechanism will be examined in vitro. Any lead compounds will be further evaluated to determine their in vivo antitumor activities. The success of the proposed project will lead to the discovery of Pt(IV) anticancer prodrugs that can be controllably activated by ultrasound and have strong antitumor activity both in vitro and in vivo. This discovery may also contribute significantly to the emerging field of sono-sensitized chemotherapy (SSCT). Such prodrugs represent a novel therapeutic modality independent of the penetration depth, and therefore may significantly expand the range of tumor types that can be treated, compared with those treatable by conventional photoactivatable anticancer drugs. 儘管以鉑類藥物為代表的多種小分子抗癌藥物已應用於對多種癌症的臨床治療中，其有效性及廣泛適用性仍受限於毒副作用以及腫瘤耐藥性等缺陷。通過開發新型外界刺激響應型的Pt(IV)前藥，可以對前藥進行時間、空間選擇性的有效激活，從而克服傳統藥物的“脫靶效應”。對新型光激活型Pt(IV)前藥包括diazido-Pt(IV)及其他軸向官能團為光敏基團的Pt(IV)前藥的探索、開發亦方興未艾。然而，受限於可見光對於生物組織的低穿透性，光激活Pt(IV)前藥難以支持對於深層腫瘤的非侵入性治療。在此項目中，鑒於超聲波對於人體組織的優越穿透性，我們擬開發一類可對超聲波刺激進行相應性激活的新型Pt(IV)前藥。經前期探索，我們得到一種基於卡鉑、且軸向基團由聲敏劑所修飾的超聲激活Pt(IV)抗癌前藥。該前藥能夠在超聲激活條件下對腫瘤細胞進行高效滅殺。基於該實驗結果，我們將設計合成多種超聲激活的Pt(IV)前藥並對其化學性質進行表征、測試，進而篩選出在細胞還原性環境中較為穩定的前藥分子，同時探索其最優化的超聲激活條件。此外，這些前藥分子的腫瘤細胞積累水平、細胞毒性以及細胞死亡機理將被詳細研究。具有優秀體外抗癌活性的前藥分子將進一步用於小鼠活體實驗，以評估其體內抗腫瘤活性。該項目的成果將引領一類全新的、具有卓越抗癌性能的超聲激活Pt(IV)抗癌前藥，並顯著地促進超聲敏化腫瘤化學療法這一新興領域的發展。該類超聲激活的Pt(IV)前藥將不受治療深度限制，相比光激活前藥，極大地拓展了腫瘤治療的適用範圍。

11302221.label: Realisation of objectives
11302221.value: Objective 1: Design, synthesis, and characterization of ultrasound-activatable Pt(IV) prodrugs Two clinically approved platinum-based anticancer drugs, carboplatin and oxaliplatin, were selected as parent compounds for the development of Pt(IV) prodrugs. To introduce sono-responsiveness, two classes of sono-sensitizers—heptamethine cyanine and porphyrins (in both metal-free and metallated forms with Mg, Mn, and Pd)—were conjugated to the axial positions of the Pt(IV) scaffolds. The resulting complexes, cyaninplatin, TPP-Pt(IV), PdTPP-Pt(IV), MnTPP-Pt(IV), and MgTPP-Pt(IV), were comprehensively characterized by ESI-HRMS, ¹H NMR, ¹³C NMR, ¹⁹⁵Pt NMR, and HPLC. All complexes exhibited efficient ultrasound-triggered reduction, confirming their sono-responsiveness. Notably, cyaninplatin and MgTPP-Pt(IV) demonstrated high stability in PBS and under reductive conditions, while being readily reduced upon ultrasound exposure, highlighting their potential as robust and controllable sono-activatable Pt(IV) prodrugs. Objective 2: In vitro evaluation and mechanistic study of the prodrugs Building on the excellent stability and the efficiency sono-responsivenes of cyaninplatin and MgTPP-Pt(IV), we next evaluated their anticancer activity using the MTT assay across multiple cancer cell lines. Carboplatin, oxaliplatin, and the corresponding sono-sensitizer ligands served as controls, while the lung fibroblast cell line MRC5 was included to assess the dark toxicity in normal tissues. Both cyaninplatin and MgTPP-Pt(IV) were non-toxic under dark conditions, exhibiting IC50 values exceeding their maximum solubility concentrations. Upon activation with focused ultrasound, their cytotoxicity increased dramatically, showing enhancements of up to more than 50-fold. Notably, the sonoactivated forms of cyaninplatin and MgTPP-Pt(IV) displayed up to a 250-fold enhancement in cytotoxicity relative to their corresponding Pt(II) counterparts. Moreover, cyaninplatin demonstrated superior tissue penetration compared to NIR laser irradiation, underscoring the potential of ultrasound activation to achieve deep-tissue tumor ablation and highlighting the clinical translational promise of sono-activatable Pt(IV) prodrugs. The mechanisms of action of cyaninplatin and MgTPP-Pt(IV) were further investigated. Cyaninplatin was efficiently internalized by cancer cells and selectively accumulated in the mitochondria. The resulting mitochondrial DNA platination and ROS generation upon ultrasound exposure caused severe mitochondrial dysfunction, disruption of redox homeostasis, and induction of endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress, ultimately leading to paraptotic cell death. The concurrent induction of immunogenic cell death (ICD) further indicates an immune-activating mode of cytotoxicity. In contrast, ultrasound activation of MgTPP-Pt(IV) significantly enhanced nuclear DNA platination, accompanied by lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) release and GSDME cleavage, characteristic of pyroptotic cell death. Collectively, these results unveil distinct mechanisms of action from conventional Pt(II) drugs, which primarily induce DNA-damage mediated apoptosis, thereby offering a strategy to overcome platinum resistance. Objective 3: In vivo evaluation of the prodrugs The in vivo therapeutic efficacy of cyaninplatin and MgTPP-Pt(IV) was evaluated in tumor-bearing mouse models. Both complexes exhibited significantly enhanced antitumor activity compared with their corresponding Pt(II) counterparts and the mixtures of Pt(II) drugs and sono-sensitizers, while inducing no observable body weight loss or histological damage to major organs. For instance, compared with the PBS-treated group, the tumor volume and weight in mice treated with cyaninplatin were reduced to 24.3% and 7.4%, respectively, demonstrating potent sono-therapeutic efficacy. Notably, Leveraging the inherent fluorescence and photoacoustic imaging capabilities of cyaninplatin, we non-invasively visualized its tumor accumulation and biodistribution across major organs (heart, liver, lungs, spleen, kidneys, and tumor) following intravenous administration. This multimodal imaging capability enabled real-time monitoring of drug delivery and optimization of ultrasound activation timing. In summary, we have successfully developed a new class of sono-activatable Pt(IV) prodrugs that combine high anticancer potency, immune activation, and multimodal imaging within a single molecular platform. By elucidating their distinct mechanisms of action and demonstrating their in vivo efficacy and biosafety, this work establishes a novel theranostic strategy to enhance the therapeutic performance and selectivity of platinum-based chemotherapy, paving the way for clinical translation of ultrasound-activated platinum therapeutics.
