11302221.label: Major findings and research outcome
11302221.value: Conventional platinum chemotherapy relies on apoptotic cell death via indiscriminate DNA damage, often leading to severe side effects and the emergence of drug resistance. To address these long-standing issues, we have created a new generation of sono-activatable Pt(IV) prodrugs that harness focused ultrasound for selective activation within tumors. Ultrasound offers deep tissue penetration, non-invasiveness, and precise spatial–temporal control, allowing treatment to be confined to diseased regions while sparing healthy tissues. Upon activation, these prodrugs initiate non-apoptotic cell death pathways—one disrupts mitochondrial integrity to induce paraptosis and immune activation, whereas another provokes pyroptosis through extensive nuclear DNA platination. Their multimodal imaging features further enable real-time tracking of drug distribution and activation timing, ensuring accurate therapeutic guidance. In animal models, both prodrugs achieved remarkable tumor suppression with minimal systemic toxicity, underscoring their biosafety, cost-effectiveness, and the clinical potential of ultrasound-driven platinum therapy. This strategy represents a paradigm shift toward precisely controllable and immune-activating platinum-based cancer treatments.

11302221.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11302221.value: Our research has demonstrated that sono-activatable Pt(IV) prodrugs offer a promising strategy for precise and controllable cancer therapy, overcoming drug resistance. However, several challenges remain to fully realize their potential: 1. Improving sonoactivation efficiency; 2. Enhancing tumor-targeting ability; 3. Combination with standard therapies. Our next steps include: 1. Developing prodrugs with higher sonoactivation efficiency to boost anticancer effectiveness; 2. Improving tumor-targeting capabilities to minimize side effects; 3. Exploring synergy with immunotherapy, chemotherapy, or radiation for rapid clinical adoption. Following these efforts, the most promising candidates will advance to preclinical evaluation to assess their efficacy, safety, and translational potential as next-generation, non-invasive platinum-based theranostic agents.

11302221.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11302221.value: Platinum-based cancer drugs are widely used but often limited by drug resistance and systemic toxicity. To address these challenges, we developed a new class of sono-activatable platinum(IV) prodrugs that can be non-invasively and precisely activated by focused ultrasound. Unlike conventional platinum drugs, which induce apoptotic cell death via DNA damage, these prodrugs exhibit distinct subcellular mechanisms—one targets the mitochondria to induce paraptotic and immunogenic cell death, while another triggers pyroptosis through enhanced nuclear DNA platination. By leveraging the deep tissue penetration and spatiotemporal precision of ultrasound, together with the prodrugs’ intrinsic multimodal imaging capabilities, tumor accumulation and activation can be monitored non-invasively, enabling precise, tumor-specific therapy while minimizing off-target toxicity. In animal models, they demonstrated potent tumor inhibition with excellent biosafety. Combined with the cost-effectiveness and clinical safety of ultrasound, this platform offers a highly translatable and next-generation strategy for precise platinum-based theranostic cancer therapy.

11302321.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11302321.value: 尋找低複雜度多項式系統的零點

11302321.label: Project Objectives
11302321.value: To design and analyze an algorithm computing approximate zeros of square polynomial systems which is well-adapted to systems whose polynomials have low evaluation complexity. The complexity analysis should show the algorithm is efficient through an average-case polynomial bound (as is common after the formulation of Smale's 17th problem). This imposes a restriction on the families of (low evaluation complexity) polynomials considered, namely, that the family is invariant under unitary transformations of its components.

11302321.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11302321.value: Smale's 17th problem asks for an algorithm to compute a zero of a complex polynomial system efficiently (that is, in average polynomial time). After several breakthroughs this problem was recently solved with a positive answer. The success of this endeavour (described in the entry `Smale's problems' in Wikipedia) has raised the question of whether a similar result can be obtained for low-complexity polynomials. A low-complexity polynomial is one that can be evaluated with few arithmetic operations (compared with the the number of coefficients needed to write down the polynomial). For instance, the polynomial (1+X) to the power 2^n can be evaluated with n+1 operations. But to write it down we need 2^n+1 coefficients. The goal of this project is to obtain an algorithm, similar in spirit to the ones developed to answer Smale's 17th problem that would compute zeros efficiently, where now the polynomial time bound is not on the number of coefficients of the polynomials in the system but in their evaluation complexity. It goes without saying, this goal will apply only to some families of low-complexity polynomials. As the complexity analysis we pursue is average-case, it will be convenient to select such families to be unitarily invariant. Smale 的第 17 個問題要求一種算法來有效地計算複雜多項式系統的零（即在平均多項式時間內）。經過幾次突破後，這個問題最近得到了肯定的回答。這項努力的成功（在維基百科條目“Smale 的問題”中有所描述）引發了一個問題，即是否可以為低複雜度多項式獲得類似的結果。 低複雜度多項式是一種可以用很少的算術運算來計算的多項式（與記下多項式所需的係數數量相比）。例如，多項式 (1+X) 的 2^n 次冪可以通過 n+1 次運算進行評估。但是要寫下來，我們需要 2^n+1 個係數。該項目的目標是獲得一種算法，在精神上類似於為回答 Smale 的第 17 個問題而開發的算法，該算法將有效地計算零點，現在多項式時間界限不是系統中多項式的係數數量，而是他們的評估複雜度。 不用說，這個目標只適用於一些低複雜度多項式。由於我們追求的複雜度分析是平均情況，因此選擇這樣的族是單一不變的會很方便。

11302321.label: Realisation of objectives
11302321.value: The only objective of this project has been fully achieved. We designed an algorithm that takes as input a family of n polynomials in (n+1) homogeneous variables and returns a zero of this system in n-dimensional projective space. We analysed the average complexity of the algorithm and showed that it is bounded by a low-degree polynomial in n, the maximum degree D of the input polynomials, the evaluation complexity L of them, and a measure of the geometric intricacy of their sets of zeros. There is no occurrence of the dense input size in this complexity bound. This result was published in one of the top current journals of mathematics. In addition, we included it in a survey paper and presented it in what is arguably the most important conference in a computational mathematics.

11302321.value: We designed an algorithm that takes as input a family of n polynomials in (n+1) homogeneous variables and returns a zero of this system in n-dimensional projective space. We analysed the average complexity of the algorithm and showed that it is bounded by a low-degree polynomial in n, the maximum degree D of the input polynomials, the evaluation complexity L of them, and a measure of the geometric intricacy of their sets of zeros. A major application of this result is in the context of polynomials given by algebraic branching programs, a family which is naturally unitarily invariant. For this family, we computed the geometric intricacy mentioned above thus obtaining very simple (and low!) average complexity bounds.

Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11302321.value: A central problem in mathematics is solving equations. This problem takes various forms depending on the kind of equations and the nature of the solutions sought (and, hence, the adjectives diophantine, differential, algebraic, ..., one currently finds attached to the word 'equations'). One common kind of equations are those given by polynomials (a simple example of them being the quadratic equation one studies in secondary school). The importance of efficiently solving this sort of equations is such, that mathematician Steve Smale proposed the problem of finding an algorithm to do in his list of 18 problems for the mathematicians of the 21st century (it is problem number 17). Our work fits within this problem as it gives a very satisfying solution for an important class of polynomial equations.

11302421.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11302421.value: 離子跨膜傳輸中的流體耦合

11302421.label: Project Objectives
11302421.value: We will develop a model that describes the conservation of mass, momentum, charged particles and electric field in two fluid regions separated by a long thin porous membrane, where the fluid regions are electrolyte solutions with charged ions. We will use separate models for the porous membrane and the two fluid regions that are separated by the membrane. Our general model will be for a membrane that has arbitrary shape with active ionic fluxes and for an arbitrary number of ionic species with arbitrary valences. However, we will start with the most basic case of a planar membrane with passive fluxes for ions and only two ionic species with equal and opposite valences. We will exploit the fact that the aspect ratio in such flows is typically large and use asymptotic techniques to develop a lubrication approximation for the system of equations. We will further exploit the fact that the Debye layers are typically significantly narrower than the width of the flow to derive equations that govern the mechanics in the Debye layers. We will then apply asymptotic matching techniques to couple the Debye layers and the bulk regions. These asymptotic techniques will reduce the extremely complicated full system into a system of partial differential equations (PDEs) with one spatial variable and one time variable and no narrow boundary layers. The system of PDEs will be coupled with two ordinary differential equations (ODEs) for the pressures in the two bulk regions and two nonlinear algebraic equations for the zeta potentials on either side of the membrane. We will begin by examining the steady state solutions of this system which will involve solving a system of ODEs coupled with algebraic constraints. In fact, for weak ionic effects, the nonlinear algebraic constraints can be linearised by using the Debye-Huckle approximation. This will allow us to reduce the system into a simple system of coupled ODEs. We will then numerically solve the Debye-Huckle system using a finite difference technique. This will allow us to start to understand the role of electrical effects in modifying filtration in the simplest possible setting. We will then consider the linear stability of the steady states by applying a finite difference approximation and solving the resulting eigenvalue problem. We will also consider the full numerical time-dependent solutions of the system. This will involve numerical techniques similar to those developed by the PI in the papers Mertz et al. (2019) and Lauriere et al (2019). Having understood the system with the Debye-Huckle approximation we will then return to the system with full nonlinear constraints on the zeta potentials and determine the importance of nonlinear effects on steady-state transport, stability and the time-dependent behaviour. In biological applications, it is often the case than more than one ionic species needs to be taken into account to appropriately model the system. This makes solving the ion transport equations and the electric field balance significantly more difficult. Nevertheless, techniques to deal with multiple ion species with arbitrary valences have been developed by the PI in the paper Wang et al. (2014). Moreover, most biological membranes contain nonlinear pumps that actively maintain homeostasis for the cell. This will modify the expressions for ionic fluxes across the membrane. We will therefore consider these two effects. We will also consider non-planar membranes and determine the role that membrane curvature plays in determining ion fluxes.

11302421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11302421.value: We propose to study ion transport between two flow regions separated by a porous membrane for arbitrary numbers of ions with arbitrary valences. This will serve as a model problem for numerous engineering and biological applications where cross-flow filtration is important. A major challenge in working on these types of problem is that there is a typically a huge discrepancy between the width of the bulk flow region and the width of the Debye layers. To avoid this problem we will use formal long-wavelength asymptotics to derive a one-dimensional system of equations that describe the flow and ionic concentrations in the bulk regions. We then plan to use matched asymptotic analysis to determine the solutions inside the porous membrane, and the Debye layers adjacent to the membrane. We thereby will obtain an effective macro-scale description of this challenging multi-scale problem. We expect that the macro-scale equations will be of mixed type, in which ion concentration, electric potential and fluid motions are fully-coupled. To examine the behaviour of these equations we will perform numerical simulations. In particular, we will determine the effects of the electric field on the ion transport between the two flow regions. Of particular interest to applications will be how an electric potential between two regions can enhance the cross-flow filtration. We will also determine how the effects of multiple ionic species, nonlinear active pumps across the membrane, and membrane curvature modify the dynamics. 我們建議研究由多孔膜隔開的兩個流動區域之間的離子傳輸，用於任意數量的任意價態離子。這將作為許多工程和生物學應用的模型問題，其中錯流過濾很重要。解決這些類型問題的一個主要挑戰是整體流動區域的寬度與德拜層的寬度之間通常存在巨大差異。為了避免這個問題，我們將使用正式的長波長漸近來推導出一維方程組，該方程組描述了體積區域中的流動和離子濃度。然後我們計劃使用匹配漸近分析來確定多孔膜內部的溶液，以及與膜相鄰的德拜層。因此，我們將獲得對這個具有挑戰性的多尺度問題的有效宏觀描述。我們預計宏觀方程將是混合型的，其中離子濃度、電勢和流體運動是完全耦合的。為了檢查這些方程的行為，我們將進行數值模擬。特別是，我們將確定電場對兩個流動區域之間的離子傳輸的影響。應用中特別感興趣的是兩個區域之間的電勢如何增強錯流過濾。我們還將確定多種離子種類、跨膜的非線性有源泵和膜曲率的影響如何改變動力學。

11303021.label: Project Objectives
11303021.value: Minimization of electron radiation damage for flexible metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) Because flexible MOFs are electron beam sensitive (soft) materials, it is difficult to observe MOFs by conventional TEM with continuous electron source. We will install state-of-the-art TEM, JEOL GRAND ARM II in November 2020. Using pulsed electron source and ultra-fast and ultra-high-sensitivity direct electron detection camera, we can precisely control dose rate and total dose during observation to reduce the radiation damages. Environmental in-situ TEM imaging of flexible MOFs in gas or liquid cells MOFs are coordinated meso porous materials which have huge specific surface areas. Thus, MOFs can absorb/desorb gas or liquid inside the pores. Moreover, the pore size can be precisely controlled by selection of specific size of organic ligands and metals. Selective adsorption/desorption to specific gas can be achieved. Therefore, MOFs are thought to be promising materials of selective adsorption/desorption for specific gas such as CO2 or H2 which is important for the applications to greenhouse gas storage/separation/purification or clean hydrogen energy cycles, respectively. In-situ TEM observation in environmental gas or liquid cells are necessary to solve the detailed mechanism of deformation and gas adsorption/desorption. Environmental observation in gas or liquid phase will be achieved using our new gas and liquid holder. Samples are sandwiched by tough and thin silicon nitride membranes. Gas or liquid can be kept inside of the nano channel of gas or liquid cells. High space/ time resolution imaging of flexible MOFs All the conventional methods, such as powder x-ray diffraction, atomic force microscope (AFM), or cryo electron microscopy (cryo-EM), can observe only the initial (closed narrow pore; gas desorbed) and final (open large pore: gas adsorbed) states of flexible MOFs transformation. Because deformation and gas adsorption/desorption of flexible MOFs is fast physical process. Using our new TEM system the intermediate states can be snapshot with ultra-fast Gatan K3-1S (C-MOS) camera. Also, atomic resolution will be achieved by our new TEM with double aberration corrected and highly coherent cold field emission gun. With the high time and space resolution, atomic resolution imaging of flexible MOFs at not only initial and final states but also intermediate state can be achieved. External laser stimuli or hearing in-situ experiments accompanied with deformation of flexible MOFs and gas adsorption/desorption MOFs can change structure between closed narrow pore (gas desorbed) and open large pore (gas adsorbed) according to temperature change. This is known as thermally triggered transformation. We can control temperature with heating chips in gas or liquid environmental cells. Also, the laser stimuli can be used to serve as a temperature source to trigger phase transformation of MOFs. Developing a new 3D structural analysis method Firstly, the 3D structure will be constructed before laser stimuli or heating from exit wave function (electron hologram) reconstructed from focal series images. Then, the structural evolution in 3D after laser stimuli or heating can be refined using molecular dynamics-simulation annealing (MDSA) method based on matching intensity of single image. MDSA method will be developed under the support of this project. Revealing detail mechanism of thermally triggered deformation of flexible MOFs accompanied with gas adsorption/desorption Using these advanced techniques as mentioned above, we are aiming to observe dynamics of flexible MOFs at high time resolution and atomic resolution in gas or liquid environmental cells. That reveals the detailed mechanism of deformation between closed narrow pore and opened large pore structures of flexible MOFs accompanied with gas adsorption/desorption. The information of the atomic resolution dynamics may offer a fundamental understanding of phase transformation mechanism of thermally triggered breathing or selective gas adsorption/desorption.

11303021.value: 通过适当调整冷场发射枪的电子束脉冲长度和脉冲速率，我们打算以微米秒时间分辨率记录三维原子分辨率动力学，并且在室温以上使用外部激光刺激对柔性金属有机框架（MOF）。原位动力学实验可以在 H2/CO2 环境中或没有 H2/CO2 环境中进行。原子分辨率动力学的信息可以提供对热触发呼吸和柔性 MOF 的选择性气体存储/分离器的相变机制的基本理解，这分别对药物释放和温室以及清洁氢能源技术非常重要。由于样品必须嵌入玻璃冰层内，目前的低温电子显微镜还没有达到室温以上原子分辨率动力学的时域，而当前的超快电子显微镜也没有实现空间分辨率不足（~20nm- 200 nm）虽然它的时间分辨率更高。

11303321.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11303321.value: 气溶胶污染对空气质量、气候变化和人类健康具有有害影响，是全球决策者关注的重要问题。有机气溶胶在亚微米气溶胶中占据相当重要的一部分，而二次有机气溶胶 (SOA) 有在有机气溶胶的总质量中占主导地位。大气水相（例如云层、雨雾、气溶胶液滴）中有机物的水相化学反应是 SOA 的形成和转化中的重要一环，但当前社会对该领域的了解知之甚少。无机硝酸盐广泛分布在大气气溶胶、云层和雨雾中，它在水相中光解会产生羟基自由基（·OH）和其他多种含氮活性基团，而这些活性物质可以参与水相中SOA的形成与转化。研究表明，气候变化和污染物的持续排放将进一步增加全球云层、雨雾与气溶胶中无机硝酸盐的质量浓度。因此，大气水相中由硝酸盐介导的有机物光氧化反应将会在未来SOA 形成和转化中发挥尤为重要的作用。 本研究计划的目标是为硝酸盐介导的水相有机物光氧化现象如何驱动 SOA 形成与转化这一问题提供新的见解。首先，该计划的第一部分将研究特定的人为源和生物源两类 SOA 前体物，各自在水相硝酸盐介导下光氧化形成的 SOA的过程。人为源 SOA 的前体物采用酚类化合物，已有研究表明，在人为污染源地区通常伴随较高浓度的酚类物质与无机硝酸盐排放。而萜酸被选为生物源 SOA的前体物，因为萜酸是典型的单萜氧化产物，也是全球生物源 SOA 的主要贡献者。研究计划的第二部分将研究水相硝酸盐介导的光氧化如何将气相 VOC 转化成水溶性的SOA 。在该部分中，选用甲苯和α-蒎烯作为气相VOC的代表物，并研究它们形成典型人为源和生物源SOA的反应过程。同时，该部分也会模拟在真实大气水相环境中，在硝酸盐介导下SOA的形成和转化的水相光氧化实验。我们将使用多种不同的分析与检测技术，包括使用液相色谱-质谱法对SOA 水溶液中的有机成分和氧化产物进行定性与定量、使用紫外-可见光谱法来测量反应过程中SOA 吸光特性的演变趋势，以及使用水溶性有机碳分析仪来量化水相SOA的产率。这项研究计划不仅有助于增强对硝酸盐介导的水相有机物光氧化机理的认识，填补该领域的知识空白，更为重要的是，该计划的研究成果可以为大气模型的完善提供有效信息，包括有机物的反应速率常数、反应动力学、生命周期和反应路径等，对预测硝酸盐高排放地区中大气云层、雨雾和气溶胶液滴中SOA的演变具有重要意义。

11303421.label: Project Objectives
11303421.value: Establish a general dimension reduction expression of state space (DRESS) modeling framework, in which a. High dimensional time series data are reduced to a minimum dimensional latent dynamic subspace and a complementary subspace with static factors only. b. The latent dynamic variables are modeled with a general, interacting, and compact state space model. c. The latent variables have a descending order of predictability. Develop a general objective function with meaningful constraints to extract latent variables with the best predictability in a descending order. Develop algorithms that perform dimension reduction and extract interacting dynamic latent variables simultaneously; develop consistency analysis for the latent subsystem with parsimonious state space parameters. Develop solution algorithms that are statistically efficient and numerically robust to collinearity. Develop a method that can adaptively determine the number of dynamic latent variables with effective prediction power. Develop algorithms to integrate existing first-principles models and known factors with the DRESS model.

11303421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11303421.value: Data from industrial operations are usually in time series forms. With the growing popularity of industrial internet of things (IIoT), time series data become massive, high-dimensional, dynamic, and collinear. These characteristics make the data contain both serially correlated and serially uncorrelated features. On the other hand, engineering fields have developed valuable first-principles models with many years of investment. This project aims to attack two challenges in developing time series data analytics for industrial systems: 1. How to extract low dimensional dynamic features in parsimonious forms for accurate prediction and interpretation, and 2. How to effectively incorporate first-principles models with latent variable analytics. This project serves to develop fundamental understanding and algorithms to make use of high-dimensional, dynamic data for predictive analytics and monitoring. The project begins with surveying methods in engineering, financial time series, and statistics. We then integrate them with dynamic system theory to form a new framework of dimension reduction expression of state space (DRESS). The problem of dimension reduction with non-dynamic data has been well studied in the literature. On the other hand, the problem of time series analysis without dimension reduction has also been well studied. However, the massive dynamic data from IIoT and Industry 4.0 calls for a new framework, in which dimension reduction and dynamics must be analyzed simultaneously. With such an approach, high-dimensional data can be effectively utilized for predictive analytics. Further, the reduced-dimensional latent variables can be visualized for monitoring and decision-making. In addition, this project develops a method to incorporate first-principles models and known factors into latent variable data analytics. Therefore, prior knowledge accumulated in the first-principles models can complement the power of big data analytics. The integrated approach will facilitate fast adoption of data science by industries and provide sustainable and interpretable solutions. The developed algorithms will be demonstrated on industrial case with a goal of environmental emission monitoring and predictions. The proposed multi-dimensional dynamic data analytics can be extended to many other applications. The proposed data processing and analytic techniques could inspire solutions to similar problems in other fields, such as financial time series, dynamic system identification, and machine learning for dynamic feature analysis. 來自工業系統運營的數據通常採用時間序列形式。隨著工業物聯網（IIoT）的日益普及，時間序列數據變得海量、高維、動態和共線性。這些特徵使得數據同時包含時間自相關和時間不相關的特徵。另一方面，工程領域已經通過多年的投入，開發了众多有價值的第一性原理模型。該項目旨在解決為工業系統時間序列數據分析的兩個挑戰： 1. 如何以簡約的形式提取低維動態特徵以進行準確的預測和解釋， 2. 如何有效地將第一性原理模型與潛變量分析相結合。 該項目旨在開發基本理論和算法，以利用高維動態數據進行預測分析和監控。 該項目從综述工程、金融時間序列和統計中的方法開始。然後我們將它們與動態系統理論相結合，形成一個新的狀態空間降維表達（DRESS）框架。文獻中已經很好地研究了非動態數據的降維問題。另一方面，非降維時間序列分析問題也得到了很好的研究。然而，來自工業物聯網和工業 4.0 的海量動態數據需要一個新的框架，必須同時做降維和動態分析。通過這種方法，可以有效地利用高維數據進行預測分析。此外，降維的潛變量可以可視化，以進行監控和決策。 該項目將研究一種將第一性原理模型納入潛在變量數據分析的方法。因此，在第一性原理模型中積累的先驗知識可以補充大數據分析的能力。集成的方法將促進行業快速採用數據科學，並提供可持續和可解釋的解決方案。開發的算法將在工業案例上進行演示，目標是環境排放監測和預測。 該項目所提出的多維動態數據分析可以擴展到許多其他應用領域。所提出的數據處理和分析技術可以激發其他領域類似問題的解決方案，例如金融時間序列、動態系統識別和用於動態特徵分析的機器學習。

11303521.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11303521.value: It is a classical problem in fluid dynamics about the stability and instability of different hydrodynamic patterns in various physical settings, in particular the inviscid limit of laminar flow and boundary layer. The study can be traced back to the early work by Lord Rayleigh and Heisenberg among many others. In fact, for inviscid flow, the classical criterion for stability was given by Rayleigh saying that a necessary condition for instability of shear flow profile is that the shear flow must have an inflection point, and it was later refined by Fjortoft. On the other hand, for viscous flow, except the case of the linear Couette flow, which is proved to be linearly stable for all Reynolds numbers by Romanov, all other profiles (including those which are inviscid stable) are shown to be linearly unstable for large Reynolds numbers. One of the powerful analytic tools initiated by Sommerfeld and Orr is the spectral analysis by studying the Fourier normal mode behavior through the famous Orr-Sommerfeld equation (denoted by OS equation) derived from the linearization of the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations. As for the stability and instability investigation, tremendous progress has been made since the pioneer work by Heisenberg, C.C. Lin, Tollmien, and Schlichting, motivated by the study of the boundary layer around a solid body. The related theories influenced by the wing design for airplanes have crucial impact on the developement of aerodynamics because of the importance in understanding on the transition from the laminar flow to turbulence that is also related to the separation of boundary layer. A large number of literatures have been devoted to the estimation of the critical Reynolds number for stability based on the Navier-Stokes equations for various shear flow pattens, such as Poiseuille flow, Blasius profile, exponential suction profile, etc. Without viscosity, the OS equation is the Rayleigh equation for inviscid flow. Hence, OS equation can be viewed as a singular perturbation of Rayleigh equation in high Reynolds number. This project aims to study the OS system of equations derived from the linearization of the MHD system around a shear flow profile. With our previous understanding on the stability mechanism of strong tangential magnetic field on the boundary layer system, we will investigate the instability mechanism of the weak tangential magnetic field even when velocity profile has the corresponding stable structure for the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations. 在不同的物理框架下研究不同的流體力學模式，特別是laminar流和邊界層的無粘性極限，的穩定性與不穩定性問題是流體力學中的一個經典問題。這項研究可以追溯到早期Rayleigh和Heisenberg等人的研究。事實上，對於無粘流，Rayleigh給出了經典的穩定性判據，認為剪切流失穩的一個必要條件是剪切流必須有一個拐點，它後來被Fjortoft改進。另一方面，對於粘性流，除了Romanov證明了線性Couette流對所有Reynolds數是線性穩定的之外，其他所有的 profiles (包括那些無粘穩定的)都是在大雷諾數下線性不穩定的。 由Sommerfeld和Orr提出的強大的分析工具之一是譜分析，它主要研究由不可壓縮Navier-Stokes方程通過線性化所得到的著名的Orr-Sommerfeld方程(下記OS方程)的Fourier模式的行為。至於穩定性和不穩定性的研究，自Heisenberg，C.C. Lin, Tollmien和Schlichting等人關於繞一個固體的邊界層研究的開創性工作以來，已經取得了巨大的進展。受到飛機機翼設計影響的相關理論由於在理解從層流到湍流的轉變以及和邊界層的分離的重要性對空氣動力學的發展有至關重要的影響。大量的文獻已經研究了保證Navier-Stokes方程包含Poiseuille流, Blasius流等在內的粘性剪切流穩定的臨界Reynolds數估計。對無粘情形，OS方程是無粘流的Rayleigh方程。因此，OS方程可以看作是在高Reynolds數情形下Rayleigh方程的一個奇異攝動。 本項目旨在研究由MHD方程組圍繞一個剪切流線性化所得到的OS方程組。根據我們之前關於強切向磁場對邊界層方程組的穩定機制的理解，我們將研究弱切向磁場的不穩定機制，即便是速度場在不可壓縮Navier-Stokes方程情形具有相應的穩定結構。

11303521.label: Realisation of objectives
11303521.value: Both objectives in the project have been fully addressed. The research results have been written in four papers. One of them has been published in Archive for Rational Mechanics and Analysis, and the other three have been submitted and are under review. A classical problem in fluid mechanics concerns the stability and instability of different hydrodynamic patterns in various physical settings, particularly in the high Reynolds number limit of laminar flows with boundary layers. Despite extensive studies when the fluid is governed by incompressible Navier-Stokes equations, there are very few mathematical results on the compressible fluid. The first paper aims to introduce a new approach to studying the compressible Navier–Stokes equations in the subsonic and high Reynolds number regime, where a subtle quasi-compressible and Stokes iteration is developed. As a byproduct, we show the spectral instability of subsonic boundary layers. In the second paper, we study the space-time analyticity of solutions to both the Prandtl and Navier-Stokes equations in the half-space. The analyticity estimates are local in time variable and global in space variable up to the boundary, with the lower bound of analyticity radii agreeing with that for the classical heat equation. The space-time analytic smoothing effect holds for the Navier-Stokes equations with finite Sobolev regular initial data, and for the Prandtl equations with real-analytic initial data in tangential direction. In the third paper, we concern with the spectral instability of strong boundary layers for compressible Navier-Stokes equations at the high Reynolds number. Although there were fruitful mathematical results on the stability problem for the compressible fluids with small bulk viscosity [29, 40], the related stability results with large bulk viscosity dependent on the Reynolds number is few. The purpose of this paper is to study the effect of the scale relationship between the shear viscosity and the bulk viscosity on instability for the Mach number m > 0 including both subsonic and supersonic cases, by taking the bulk viscosity in the form of λε = ε^{1+γ} with γ ∈ (−∞, +∞). Here ε denotes the reciprocal of Reynolds number. The proof is based on the modified quasi-compressible system which takes the divergence of velocity into account. Finally, the well-posedness of the three dimensional Prandtl equation is an outstanding open problem due to the appearance of the secondary flow even though there are studies on analytic and Gevrey function spaces. This problem is raised as the third open problem in the classical book by Oleinik and Samokhin. The fourth paper aims to address this open problem in the steady case by introducing a new approach to study the structural stability of background profile that includes the famous Blasius solutions. The key observations include the introduction of some intrinsic vector fields and new versions of maximum principle. In particular, we overcome the difficulties caused by symmetry breaking through the analysis on the curvature-type quantities generated by commutators of the vector fields. The new approaches and analysis techniques can be used to study the instability induced by the Tollmien-Schlichting wave governed by the incompressible MHD system in the Prandtl-Hartmann regime. The interaction of the inviscid mode and viscous mode that leads to the instability is analyzed by the introduction of a new decomposition of the Orr-Sommerfeld operator on the velocity and magnetic fields. The critical Gevrey index for the instability is justified by constructing the growing mode in the essential frequency and it is shown to be the same as the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations in the Prandtl regime. For example, we can rigorously justify the physical understanding that the transverse magnetic field to the boundary in the Prandtl-Hartmann regime has no extra stabilizing effect on the Tollmien-Schlichting wave.

11303521.label: Major findings and research outcome
11303521.value: We introduce some new approaches and analysis techniques to study the stability and instability mechanisms in fluid dynamcis governed by Navier-Stokes equations and MHD system. It is based on the study of Orr-Sommerfeld equations and systems in various physical situations. Precisely, a classical problem in fluid mechanics concerns the stability and instability of different hydrodynamic patterns in various physical settings, particularly in the high Reynolds number limit of laminar flows with boundary layers. Despite extensive studies when the fluid is governed by incompressible Navier Stokes equations, there are very few mathematical results on the compressible fluid. For this, we also introduce a new approach to studying the compressible Navier–Stokes equations in the subsonic and high Reynolds number regime. We also study the space-time analyticity of solutions to both the Prandtl and Navier Stokes equations in the half-space. The analyticity estimates are local in time variable and global in space variable up to the boundary, with the lower bound of analyticity radii agreeing with that for the classical heat equation. In addition, we investigate the spectral instability of strong boundary layers for compressible Navier-Stokes equations at the high Reynolds number. Although there were fruitful mathematical results on the stability problem for the compressible fluids with small bulk viscosity, the related stability results with large bulk viscosity dependent on the Reynolds number is few. Our study analyze the effect of the scale relationship between the shear viscosity and the bulk viscosity on instability for the Mach number including both subsonic and supersonic cases. Finally, we study the well-posedness of the three dimensional Prandtl equation is an outstanding open problem due to the appearance of the secondary flow even though there are studies on analytic and Gevrey function spaces. This problem is raised as the third open problem in the classical book by Oleinik and Samokhin. This work aims to address this open problem in the steady case by introducing a new approach to study the structural stability.

11303521.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11303521.value: We have investigated the instability of fluid dynamics by deriving a new Orr-Sommerfeld system and a decomposition for analysis. Moreover, we also derived the Orr-Sommerfeld equation for compressible Navier-Stokes equations and introduce the quasi-compressible-Stokes iteration for analysing the instability and stability of Prandtl boundary layers. We believe that these newly derived system and equations, together with the introduced analysis approaches can be used for future study on this kind of problems. For example, the high Reynolds number limit with strong boundary layer for compressible fluid, in particular with temperature effect is still an outstanding open problem in mathematics. We hope our analysis can shed some light on the future investigation on this topic.

11303521.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11303521.value: It is a classical problem in fluid dynamics about the stability and instability of different hydrodynamic patterns in various physical settings, in particular the inviscid limit of laminar flow and boundary layer. The study can be traced back to the early work by Lord Rayleigh and Heisenberg among many others. In fact, for inviscid flow, the classical criterion for stability was given by Rayleigh saying that a necessary condition for instability of shear flow profile is that the shear flow must have an inflection point, and it was later refined by Fjortoft. On the other hand, for viscous flow, except the case of the linear Couette flow, which is proved to be linearly stable for all Reynolds numbers by Romanov, all other profiles (including those which are inviscid stable) are shown to be linearly unstable for large Reynolds numbers. One of the powerful analytic tools initiated by Orr and Sommerfeld is the spectral analysis through the famous Orr-Sommerfeld equation derived from the linearization of the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations. This project aims to derive and analyse the Orr-Sommerfeld system of equations derived from other physical systems that include the MHD system in order to investigate their instability and stability mechanisms.

11303721.label: Project Objectives
11303721.value: Circuit analysis and experimental optimization of efficient spontaneous poling process of high performance electro-optic polymers by commercial pyroelectric elements: these studies will be very important to guide the further design and synthesis of highly efficient OEO materials, and to develop new EO device concepts that can be facilitated by pyroelectricity. Develop direct poling and patterning techniques to fabricate low loss EO polymer waveguides through pyroelectric effect: the study would provide a highly controllable and scalable process to produce a uniform array of OEO materials that are integrated onto nanophotonic structures. Design of new heterogeneous dielectric structures to create in-plane polarization: using pyroelectricity to introduce the in-plane polarization and self-assembly of OEO materials that are essential to various designs of hybrid photonic devices. Establish quantitative structure-property relationship analysis of molecular and material properties of new-generation OEO materials: the studies in concise synthesis and molecular design of these OEO materials will be guided by the tabulation of their linear and NLO properties in bulk materials, which is crucial to streamline future development of high performance OEO materials for photonic applications. Explore pyroelectric poling or pyroelectricity-enabled self-assembly of supramolecualr OEO materials on densely packed modulator arrays based on hybrid nano-photonic or plasmonic platforms: the small dimension (50 nm to 200 nm) of nanophotonic waveguides presents a great opportunity to assemble the NLO active molecules with the assist of pyroelectricity.

11303721.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11303721.value: The worldwide explosion in data transmittal and usage creates an ever-increasing demand for ultrafast, energy efficient, and integrated photonic/electronic devices for information processing. In emerging nanophotonic platforms, light-matter interactions are enhanced by orders of magnitude at the sub-wavelength dimensions, and a variety of nanoscale photonic structures have been implemented into high-speed, low-power and small-footprint optoelectronic devices with exceptional performance. Due to intrinsically large optical nonlinearity, organic electro-optic (OEO) materials have been identified as one of the most promising active materials to be incorporated into these nanophotonic devices to enable hybrid OEO nanophotonic systems. Despite recent progress, the performance achieved so far in these hybrid electro-optic (EO) devices is still far away from the theoretical limits. One major challenge is low in-device poling efficiency of OEO materials, which is mainly due to severe charge injection and transport in submicron scale waveguide structures. Proposed to address such problems is using “net” electric fields generated by conformal and detachable pyroelectric elements to achieve high degree of non-centrosymmetric order of new generation OEO materials for performance breakthrough. Pyroelectric elements provide several exceptional features that can used to generate high electric field by heating or cooling of pyroelectric materials such as high electric fields (up to 3 - 4 MV/cm) through modest change of temperatures, minimized free charge carriers generation, manipulatable surface charges, deployable as standalone source with diverse selection of materials, and versatile electrodeless design for applying electric field to the recipient materials. In this project, based on rational design and facile synthesis of new generation OEO materials, we will explore protocols of using electric field generated by pyroelectrics to direct self-assembly and poling of OEO materials. Through interface engineering, novel pyroelectric elements, such as pyroelectric crystals and ceramics, will be modified as conformal and detachable electric field source to study basic electrostatics and develop new device concepts for hybrid OEO nanophotonic platforms. New self-assembled OEO materials will be synthesized and processed at multiple length scales, and be used in complex densely packed structures of nano-photonic and plasmonic waveguides to enable ultra-compact, low-power, and high-speed electro-optic (EO) modulators for on-chip optical communications. The proposed study will provide an integrative platform to investigate the fundamentals of electric field assisted self-assembly processes and surface chemistry. It can potentially open up new processing strategies of functional dielectrics and their hybrid systems over multi-length scales and dimensions for a broad spectrum of electronic and photonic applications. 在全球範圍內，數據傳輸和使用的爆炸式增長對光子/電子設備信息處理的超快、節能和集成性能的需求不斷增長。在新興的納米光子平台中，光與物質的相互作用在亞波長尺度上增加了幾個數量級。多種納米光子結構已被高效地應用於高速、低能耗和小尺寸光電器件中。由於具有大的光學非線性特性，有機電光 (OEO) 材料被認為是最有希望應用於這些納米光子器件，以實現混合有機電光納米光子系統的活性材料之一。儘管最近取得了一些進展，但迄今為止在這些混合電光 (EO) 設備中，實現的性能仍遠低於理論極限。一個主要挑戰是 OEO 材料的器件內極化效率低，這主要歸於亞微米級波導結構中存在嚴重的電荷注入和傳輸。本課題解決此類問題的方法是使用保形、可拆卸的熱釋電元件產生“淨”電場，實現新一代OEO材料的高度非中心對稱極化，從而實現性能突破。 熱釋電元件具有多種特殊性能，可通過適當的溫度變化，減小自由電荷載流子的產生，可操作的表面電荷加熱或冷卻熱釋電材料產生高電場（高達 3 - 4 MV/cm）。可部署為供多種材料選擇的獨立源，以及用於將電場施加到受體材料的多功能無電極設計。在本項目中，基於新一代OEO材料的合理設計和簡便合成，我們將探索利用熱釋電產生的電場來指導OEO材料的自組裝和極化的協議。 通過界面工程，我們將新型熱釋電元件如熱釋電晶體和陶瓷修飾為保形和可分離的電場源，以研究基本靜電學，並開髮用於混合 OEO 納米光子平台的新器件概念。新的自組裝 OEO 材料將在多個長度尺度上合成和加工，並用於納米光子和等離子體波導的複雜密集結構，以實現可用於芯片光通信的超緊湊、低功率和高速電光 (EO) 調製器。本課題的設計研究將為研究電場輔助自組裝過程和表面化學的基本原理提供一個綜合平台，並可開闢新的多長度和尺寸的功能電介質及混合系統的加工策略，以廣泛用於電子和光子領域。

11303821.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11303821.value: 對深度卷積神經網絡在分類問題中的漸進分析

11303821.label: Project Objectives
11303821.value: The first objective is to establish error analysis of binary classification schemes. We shall first construct a family of deep convolutional neural networks and apply it to approximate functions in weighted L_p spaces on unit spheres. Then we shall establish the confidence-based excess misclassification error analysis by empirical process techniques and methods from approximation theory including local polynomial reproduction and integral discretization. A general loss function and various specific ones of interest will be considered. Last, we expect to derive faster convergence rates in the case of low noise: Tsybakov's assumption . The seconde objective is to establish error analysis of multi-class classification schemes. In the multi-class scenario, we shall first investigate a general quantitative relationship between the misclassification error and error assessed using a convex and Lipshitz loss function. Then the excess error analysis will be divided into a sample error term and an approximation error term. We shall establish more delicate estimation for the sample error by the idea of modulus of convexity of a norm. For the latter term, we shall construct a family of deep CNNs with the structure of multiple channels and dwonsamplings to approximate vector-valued functions. The third objective is to estimate the convergent rate of classification algorithm with gradient descent method. We shall study the global convergence and generalization abilities of the gradient descent method for deep CNNs on classification problem using general loss function. confidence-based rates of global convergence and loss convergence will be investigated in terms of the number of iterations and a learning rate. In addition, the generalization error of classification with gradient descent schemes will be estimated.

11303821.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11303821.value: Classification is a classic problem in learning theory. Nowadays various classification algorithms have been developed and widely applied in AI (artificial intelligence). As deep neural networks have achieved great success in science and technology that involve large amounts of data, such as speech analysis, image and video analysis, finance and bioinformatics, rigorous mathematical analysis on classification methods by deep neural networks is in urgent demand. A classification algorithm usually involves a minimization based on training data with respect to a potentially rich hypothesis function space and a loss function. It is well known that algorithms with misclassification error are typically unfeasible. Instead, various loss functions have been proposed and applied. Therefore, to analyze different loss functions and characterize their classification behavior will have a great impact for classification problems. Statistical investigation in this direction has been extensive, especially for the binary scenario, which provides us a theoretical framework of classification learning methods. However, to obtain better understanding, more sophisticated and quantitative error analysis is needed as well. In this project, we shall focus on classification methods based on deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs). Precisely, we aim at establishing rigorous approximation analysis on the error in using classification algorithms for binary and multi-class scenarios with various loss function and deep CNNs. Also we shall consider gradient descent methods for a minimum error entropy principle in the framework. Analysis will be carried out by means of approximation theory of local polynomial reproduction and integral discretization. The desired results will have impact both for the theoretical analysis community and for the real practitioners in industries. In addition, the analysis produced in this project may help to design new network algorithms that are more efficient and accurate. 分類問題是學習理論中的一個經典問題。現今各種分類算法已被開發並廣泛應用於AI（人工智能）。隨著深度神經網絡在涉及大數據的科學技術方面，如語音分析、圖像和視頻分析、金融和生物信息學，取得重大成功,對應用深度神經網絡的分類方法進行嚴格的數學分析有著需求迫切。 分類算法通常涉及基於訓練數據對潛在假設函數空間和某個損失函數的最小化。人們已經熟知應用錯分類損失函數的算法是不可行的。取而代之地，人們提出了其他各種損失並進行了成功應用。因此，分析不同的損失函數 並他們在分類問題中的表現將對會有重大意義。這方面的統計研究已經很豐富，特別是針對二分類情況，為我們提供了分類學習的理論框架。 然而，為了獲得對此問題的深入認識，更複雜和量化的分析也是必不可少的。 在本項目中，我們將會關注基於深度卷積神經網絡（CNN）的分類方法。確切地說，我們的目標是針對不同損失函數和CNN網絡下二元和多元分類算法建立嚴格的漸進分析。並且我們還將考慮在最小誤熵原理框架下的梯度下降方法。分析將會通過局部多項式再生和積分離散化理論進行展開。預期的結果將會對理論分析和實際應用產生影響。此外，本項目的分析結果還將助於設計更有效和準確的新網絡算法。

11303821.label: Realisation of objectives
11303821.value: The project's three core objectives are focused on binary classification error analysis, multi-class classification error analysis , and convergence rate estimation of gradient descent-based CNN classification algorithms, with explicit requirements for approximation rates, loss function specificity, error decomposition, and gradient descent generalization analysis. For Objective 1--Error Analysis of Binary Classification Schemes, it has been achieved, with quantitative bounds for L_p -approximation, minimax optimal convergence rates, and validation across loss functions. Precisely, the 2021 paper ( Generalization Analysis of CNNs for Classification on Spheres ) directly addressed binary classification on spheres, constructing deep CNNs to approximate functions in L_p spaces (1≤p≤∞) and providing explicit L_p -approximation rates for Sobolev space functions. It derived generalization bounds and learning rates for excess misclassification error, targeting convex loss functions (e.g., hinge loss) — addressing the core challenge of non-smooth/continuous target functions tied to such losses. This fulfilled the requirement for confidence-based excess misclassification error analysis using spherical analysis, cubature formulae, and approximation theory. In the 2025 paper ( On the Rates of Convergence for Learning with Convolutional Neural Networks ), we supplemented this by deriving minimax optimal convergence rates for binary classification with two specific loss functions (hinge loss, logistic loss) — fulfilling the "faster convergence rates" goal (minimax optimality denotes near-optimal speed under low-noise/Tsybakov-like conditions). It also proved a new approximation bound for CNNs with weight constraints, refining the L_p -approximation framework. For the objective 2--Error Analysis of Multi-Class Classification Schemes, it was achieved for hypergraph multi-classification analysis, and multi-channel CNN approximation and error decomposition. Two 2023 papers ( Generalization Analysis of Pairwise Learning for Ranking With Deep Neural Networks / Optimal Estimates for Pairwise Learning with Deep ReLU Neural Networks ) adapted the multi-class error decomposition framework to pairwise ranking (a multi-sample task analogous to multi-class classification). Firstly, we targeted convex loss functions (hinge loss \phi_h ), characterizing the \phi_h -risk minimizer (fulfilling the "quantitative relationship between misclassification error and convex loss error" requirement); then we derived approximation error convergence rates tied to function smoothness/noise conditions (sample error estimation via hypothesis space properties of deep neural networks, mirroring the "modulus of convexity of a norm" approach); Additionally, we established excess generalization error bounds for the algorithm. The 2024 paper ( Approximation analysis of CNNs from a feature extraction view ) constructed deep multi-channel CNNs for linear feature extraction, deriving function approximation rates for high-dimensional/vector-valued functions (directly fulfilling the "multi-channel/downsampling CNN for vector-valued approximation" requirement). It demonstrated superiority over traditional linear transformations (Fourier/wavelets) and bridged 1D/2D CNNs via matrix vectorization, expanding the applicability of multi-channel CNNs to high-dimensional multi-class tasks. As an extension, the 2025 papers ( High-Pass Matters: Theoretical Insights and Sheaflet-Based Design for Hypergraph Neural Networks/Deep Hypergraph Neural Networks with Tight Framelets) extended multi-class analysis to hypergraph node classification, proving that integrating low-pass/high-pass spectral components reduces generalization error in multi-class tasks. This validated the project’s core error analysis framework for multi-class scenarios beyond traditional CNNs. For the objective 3--Convergence Rate of Gradient Descent-Based Classification Algorithms, it was achieved for core convergence/generalization analysis validated, with gradient descent explicitly tied to GCNs/HGNNs; CNN-wide convergence rates derived. In the 2025 paper ( On the Rates of Convergence for Learning with Convolutional Neural Networks ), we derived minimax optimal convergence rates for CNN-based estimators (least squares for regression, hinge/logistic loss for binary classification), analyzing the covering number of feed-forward neural networks (CNNs as a subset) with weight size constraints — providing a theoretical foundation for convergence rate estimation (aligning with the "confidence-based global convergence rates" requirement). The 2025 paper ( Deeper Insights into Deep Graph Convolutional Networks: Stability and Generalization ) explicitly analyzed stochastic gradient descent (SGD) for deep graph CNNs (GCNs), characterizing upper bounds for stability/generalization influenced by two quantitative factors: the maximum absolute eigenvalue of graph filter operators and network depth. This directly addressed the "gradient descent generalization error" requirement, extending it to a broader class of convolutional models (GCNs). In addition, the 2025 paper ( High-Pass Matters: Theoretical Insights and Sheaflet-Based Design for Hypergraph Neural Networks ) analyzed generalization error in hypergraph node multi-classification, proving that high-pass spectral components (integrated into gradient descent-trained HGNNs) reduce misclassification error, validating the project's goal of estimating generalization error for gradient descent-based multi-class classification.

11303821.label: Major findings and research outcome
11303821.value: The project on deep convolutional neural network (CNN) classification approximation analysis yielded key theoretical and methodological outcomes across 8 papers. In paper[1], we established L_p -approximation rates (1≤p≤∞) for CNNs on spherical data, derived excess misclassification error bounds for hinge loss, and used spherical analysis/cubature formulae to address non-smooth target functions. Paper[5] supplemented this with minimax optimal convergence rates for hinge/logistic loss in binary classification, refining CNN approximation constraints. In paper[4], we constructed multi-channel CNNs for linear feature extraction, proving their superiority over Fourier/wavelets and deriving high-dimensional function approximation rates. It bridged 1D/2D CNNs via matrix vectorization, enabling vector-valued function approximation critical for multi-class tasks. Two papers[2,3] adapted multi-class error decomposition to pairwise ranking, deriving hinge loss risk minimizers and approximation error rates tied to smoothness/noise. The paper[6] analyzed SGD stability, linking generalization to graph filter eigenvalues/network depth. Hypergraph CNN papers [7,8] showed low-pass/high-pass spectral integration reduces multi-class generalization error.

11303821.value: Extend the analysis framework and techniques to other advanced models, such as transformers.

11303821.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11303821.value: This research focuses on making deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs)—the tech behind image recognition, speech apps, etc.—more reliable by understanding how they “learn” and avoid mistakes, and how well CNNs approximate real-world patterns, how to cut errors when classifying things (e.g., telling cats from dogs), and how to make training faster/steadier. CNNs often feel like "black boxes"—this research shines a light inside, so we can trust them more (e.g., in medical imaging or self-driving). It gives rules to build better CNNs: faster training, fewer mistakes, and even works for trickier data (like connected data in social networks). For tech developers, it's a guide to make smarter AI; for users, it means more reliable AI tools.

11304121.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11304121.value: 硫酸盐主要由二氧化硫 (SO2) 氧化产生，是大气颗粒物 (PM) 的关键组成部分。然而，传统的空气质量模型无法重现硫酸盐的产生在重度雾霾期间。解决了这种差异其他硫酸盐形成途径，主要是通过多相和非均相过程。可以对硫酸盐形成提供新见解的缺失过程的进一步研究是至关重要的。生物质燃烧 (BB) 颗粒中普遍存在的光敏剂具有对引发大气化学中的新反应越来越感兴趣。这光敏剂吸收太阳辐射会产生三重激发态 (3C*)引发各种在基态不会发生的化学反应。 在这个提议的项目中，我们将评估通过 BB 衍生的 SO2 氧化形成的硫酸盐水相和颗粒相中的光敏剂。不同班级代表BB 衍生的有机物和真实 BB 样品的（例如，芳香羰基）将用作 3C*前体。水相实验将在 3C* 前体浓度下进行预计受 BB 影响的区域的云或雾滴。。拟议的研究将提供有关 S(IV) 大气动力学的信息氧化成 SO42- 在云滴和 BB 衍生的 3C* 前体的存在下不同RH条件下的气溶胶。动力学参数将被输入到动力学模型中与其他已知机制在硫酸盐生产的重要性方面进行比较。

11304121.label: Realisation of objectives
11304121.value: We first conducted photooxidation SO2 by model photosensitizers from biomass burning, including 3,4-dimethoxybenzaldehyde (DMB), vanillin (VL), and syringaldehyde (SyrAld), utilizing an aerosol flow tube and single-particle aerosol mass spectrometry (SPAMS). This study presents insights into aerosol SO2 oxidation by photosensitizers derived from biomass burning using single-particle characterization. Sulfate formation in photosensitizer-coated particles, in terms of both number percentage and RPA of sulfate, was significantly higher under UV irradiation than under dark conditions. From dark conditions to UV irradiation, the average number percentages of sulfate-containing particles increased from less than 2 % to 43 %–99 %, and the sulfate RPA increased from almost 0 to 0.12–0.67 for SyrAld-, VL- and DMB-coated particles. Also, increased light intensity could further promote the sulfate formation. Further on this study, we investigated the sulfate formation in real biomass burning organic aerosols. Specifically, we reported a kinetic study on the multiphase reactivity involving 3BBOA* in submicron aerosol particles, using an aerosol flow reactor (AFT) coupled with multiple offline analytical tools. In this work, we referred to the water extract of the BB particles as BBOA. We focused on the water extract due to its better compatibility with analytical tools for deeper insights into our study. The potential effects of water-insoluble components were also discussed. We focused on sulfate formation from SO2 oxidation as an indicator of the multiphase reaction kinetics. This choice was driven by the atmospheric significance of sulfate and the relatively straightforward mechanism compared to that of organic oxidations. We used chemical probes and transient absorption spectroscopy (TA) to determine the oxidant concentrations and reaction rate constants in diluted solutions and then extrapolate to aerosol conditions, enabling modeling of the sulfate formation rate and comparisons with the measurement results. Mass spectrometry provides identification of the potential photosensitizers in BBOA. In addition, quantum chemical calculations and electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy (EPR) connect the reactivities of 3BBOA* to photochemical parameters such as redox potentials, broadening our mechanistic understanding of BBOA-driven reactions. The overall goal of this work is to provide quantitative insights into the photosensitizing capabilities of BBOA particles and facilitate future parameterization. In this study, we found that sulfate formation in BBOA particles under light is predominantly driven by photosensitization involving the triplet excited states (3BBOA*) instead of iron, nitrate, and S(IV) photochemistry. Rates in BBOA particles are three orders of magnitude higher than those observed in the bulk solution, primarily due to the fast interfacial reactions. Our results highlight that the chemistry of 3BBOA* in particles can greatly contribute to the formation of sulfate, as an example of the secondary pollutants. Photosensitization of BBOA will likely become increasingly crucial due to the intensified global wildfires. Furthermore, we extend our study to explore how the interaction between photosensitization and chlorine chemistry influences atmospheric oxidative capacity. Particulate chloride ions (Cl–) have traditionally been considered a significant component in the marine environment, contributing to the coarse mode particles. Biomass burning is an important source of particulate Cl–, particularly in the form of potassium chloride, which can account for up to 2% of sub-micrometer particle mass. A comprehensive global continental emission inventory of particulate chloride ions suggested that particulate chloride is mainly emitted from biofuel (29%) and open biomass burning processes (44%). Reactive radicals, such as chlorine radical (Cl•) and dichlorine radical anions (Cl2•–), can be generated through photochemical reactions of chlorine-containing compounds. The reactive uptake of SO2 by particles was performed using in situ Raman spectroscopy/Flow cell. In brief, the flow cell features two quartz windows, with the Raman laser passing through the top window for characterization and the bottom window for light irradiation. The photolysis experiments were initiated with a xenon lamp (model 6258, ozone-free xenon lamp, 300 W, Newport). In this study, we investigate the impact of the interaction of chlorine chemistry and photosensitization on the oxidative potential of aerosols by utilizing SO2 oxidation to form sulfate as an indicator. Mixed particles of chloride with glyoxal and its reaction products of ammonia of imidazole-2-carboxaldehyde (IC) were studied. Premixed NH4Cl + glyoxal particles have a 4–5 times higher sulfate formation rate than premixed NaCl + glyoxal, particularly at low relative humidity, suggesting the role of photosensitization. Furthermore, the addition of IC resulted in an ∼73-fold increase in sulfate production rate compared to NH4Cl alone. No noticeable sulfate formation was observed in the presence of IC alone, likely due to the high particle acidity in this study (i.e., pH = 2). The kinetic analysis of these particles results yields a reaction rate constant of chloride ions with the triplet state of IC, 3IC*, ∼3 orders of magnitude higher than previously reported values in bulk solution. These findings underscore the significance of the synergetic effect of chlorine chemistry and photosensitization in enhancing atmospheric oxidative capacity. Built on this model system, we further investigate the sulfate formation in particles containing NaCl and BBOA. In this study, we performed in situ droplet and bulk aqueous solution reaction experiments using BB extract–NaCl mixtures to explore the possible interplay between biomass burning and marine aerosols in coastal areas. BB was derived from the burning of rice straw (RS), wheat straw (WS), and corn straw (CS), as well as incense burning (IS). The aims of this study are to (i) compare the differences in sulfate formation among different kinds of BB–NaCl particles and BB extracts, (ii) examine the impacts of OH• aging on sulfate formation across different BB–NaCl particles and BB extracts, and (iii) investigate the role of NOCs and chloride ions in BB-extract-mediated sulfate formation. Note that BBF and BBA refer to the fresh BB and aged BB. This study provided laboratory evidence that the PSs in biomass burning extracts can enhance the sulfate formation in NaCl particles, primarily by triggering the formation of secondary oxidants under light and air conditions, with a lower contribution of direct photosensitization via triplets. The sulfate formation rates of BBF–NaCl particles were ∼ 10-fold higher than those of ISF–NaCl, following the trend of CSF–NaCl > RSF–NaCl > WSF–NaCl > ISF–NaCl. Upon UV exposure, the sulfate formation trend shifted to RSA–NaCl > CSA–NaCl > WSA–NaCl > ISA–NaCl, which might be explained by the effects of chloride (evidenced by aqueous reactions, Fig. 3 and Table 1). Interestingly, the incorporation of Cl− into bulk solutions increased the sulfate formation rate in RSA, while it decreased it in RSF. Note: Prof. CHAN Chak Keung was the original Principal Investigator (PI) of this project. Midway through the project, he accepted a position at King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST), and the PI role was formally transferred to Prof. Patrick Lee. Nevertheless, Prof. Chan remained actively involved as a Co-Investigator, continuing to supervise the research and contribute substantially to its successful delivery. As he took responsibility for communicating and coordinating the dissemination of research findings, he served as the corresponding author for most of the project’s publications.

11304121.label: Major findings and research outcome
11304121.value: 1. We find evident sulfate formation in the biomass-burning-derived photosensitizer particles under UV and SO2 exposure, attributable to photosensitized oxidation of S(IV). The efficiency of sulfate production by photosensitizer particles under UV irradiation, represented by the number percentage of sulfate-containing particles (99 %–43 %) and the relative peak area (RPA) of sulfate (0.67–0.12) in single-particle spectra, in descending order, were 3,4-dimethoxybenzaldehyde (DMB), vanillin (VL), and syringaldehyde (SyrAld). 2. Through further investigation of a realistic biomass burning system, we demonstrate the high reactivity of 3BBOA* in aerosol particles, indicated by the rapid sulfate formation via SO2 oxidation. Notably, the photosensitized sulfate formation in BBOA particles occurs much more rapidly than in diluted solutions, which is attributable to prominent interfacial reactions. 3. Furthermore, we observed that the interaction between photosensitization and chlorine chemistry enhances the generation of reactive chlorine species, such as Cl and Cl₂⁻, which subsequently promote sulfate formation. Mixed particles of chloride with glyoxal and its reaction products of ammonia of imidazole-2-carboxaldehyde (IC) were studied. Premixed NH4Cl + glyoxal particles have a 4–5 times higher sulfate formation rate than premixed NaCl + glyoxal, particularly at low relative humidity, suggesting the role of photosensitization. Furthermore, the addition of IC resulted in a ∼73-fold increase in sulfate production rate compared to NH4Cl alone. 4. By studying the SO2 uptake into laboratory-generated droplets containing incense smoke extracts and sodium chloride (IS–NaCl) under irradiation. We found enhanced sulfate production over pure NaCl droplets, attributable to photosensitization induced by constituents in IS. Low relative humidity and high light intensity facilitated sulfate formation and increased the SO2 uptake coefficient by IS–NaCl particles. Aging of the IS particles further enhanced sulfate production, attributable to the enhanced secondary oxidant production promoted by increased proportions of nitrogen-containing CHN and oxygen- and nitrogen-containing CHON species under light and air. 5. By mixing real biomass burning (BB) extracts and NaCl, mimicking internal mixtures of BB and sea-salt particles. BB–NaCl particles had a significantly higher sulfate formation rate than incense burning (IS)–NaCl particles. For fresh particles, the sulfate formation rate followed the trend of corn straw (CS)–NaCl > rice straw (RS)–NaCl > wheat straw (WS)–NaCl > IS–NaCl. The filter sample aging was achieved by exposure to OH• generated from UV irradiation. After aging, RS–NaCl particles exhibited the highest enhancement in sulfate formation rates among all the BB–NaCl particles due to interactions between RS and NaCl.

11304121.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11304121.value: In this proposal, we focused on the role of photosensitization in sulfate formation through the photooxidation of SO2 mediated by photosensitizing agents. In the real atmosphere, secondary organic aerosols (SOA) represent another significant component of PM2.5. The influence of photosensitization on the photooxidation of volatile organic compounds (VOCs) and the subsequent formation of secondary aerosols warrants further investigation. To examine this process, the same experimental setup, namely, an aerosol flow tube coupled with an aerosol mass spectrometer (AMS) and a proton-transfer-reaction mass spectrometer (PTR-MS), can be employed to study the uptake of VOCs into biomass burning organic aerosols and model photosensitizers, as well as the resulting SOA formation. We can also study the effect of different factors, including light intensity, oxidants/precursor concentrations, and relative humidity, on the SOA yields.

11304121.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11304121.value: Wildfires have become increasingly prevalent, impacting ecosystems, climate, and human health on a global scale. Organic aerosols resulting from wildfires and open biomass burning, collectively termed biomass-burning organic aerosol(s) (BBOA), represent the predominant source of global primary organic aerosols (POA). Annually, BBOA contributes about 60 to 85% of the total POA, with emissions estimated at approximately 31 to 36 Tg. These aerosols are rich in brown carbon (BrC) that can significantly absorb solar radiation, accelerating the warming of the Earth–atmosphere system. The findings of this project underscore the enhanced atmospheric oxidative capacity attributable to the presence of BBOA, which may facilitate the formation of particulate matter and contribute to deteriorating air quality. Therefore, preventing the occurrence of wildfires and reducing residential fuel combustion and agricultural biomass burning are critical measures for mitigating air pollution.

11304221.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11304221.value: Organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs) dominate the high-end market for flat-panel monitors. Their advantages include low power consumption, good color saturation, and versatile form factor, particularly in making displays for smartphones and various hand-held electronic devices. Since 2015, almost all major smartphone companies (i.e., Samsung, Apple, Sony, Huawei, etc.) have used OLED panels in their flagship products. Thus, with their high performance and power efficiency, OLED displays have gained a reputation as top-of-the-range products. Moreover, the materials, particularly the emitters, are undergoing continual development to improve performance. In contrast to the outstanding progress in long-wavelength emitters, however, there is an urgent demand for more efficient and durable blue-emitting materials, particularly those capable of harvesting both singlet and triplet excitons via thermally activated delay fluorescence (TADF) or phosphorescence, respectively. However, despite extensive studies, the color chromaticity, efficiency, and stability of blue-light emitters have failed to progress substantially. This opens up an opportunity for alternative materials to construct suitable blue emitters. To this end, we believe that Ir(III)-based emitters that bear carbene cyclometalate(s) are the best candidates for efficient and durable blue emitters, due to their more destabilized lowest unoccupied molecular orbitals (LUMOs) in comparison to other chelating designs. In turn, the greater Ir-C bond strength destabilizes the metal-centered (MC) dd excited states and reduces the unwanted quenching caused by thermal population of these MC dd states. As a result, this class of emitting materials should undergo fast intersystem crossing induced by both the iridium metal atom and intra-ligand charge transfer (CT) transition. They will also exhibit increased radiative decay and shortened lifetime to the sub-microsecond region and, ultimately, give rise to OLED devices with longer operational lifetimes. 有機發光二極體已逐漸成為高階智慧型手機的標準屏幕器件。他們的優點是可塑性高、低耗能、高色飽和度與解析度。然而就學理技術而言、高效且長壽命的藍光材料尚未開發完成、成為相關顯示技術的重大瓶頸、也成為現階段產業界與學術界的共同研發的重點。對此、有兩項發光材料有可能成為未來的商用藍光發光物、其一為熱活化延遲螢光 (TADF) 材料、其二則是傳統銥金屬磷光材料、但在現階段、這兩項材料的光物理特性暨安定性均未能達到產業化的最低要求。對此、我們相信銥金屬卡賓 (carbene )配合物、在經過適當的分子修飾、應是最有機會滿足產業應用的指標。因此、我們擬將不同型態的拉電子基團修飾到卡賓配體之上、以降低最低分子空軌域 (LUMO) 的能量、將原先落在紫色光區的磷光放光、紅移至藍光的區間。此外、卡賓配體因有較強的金屬–配體鍵結能、故能有效提升金屬中心 dd 激態能級、減少熱誘發的淬息現象、增加發光量子效率。最後、這系列的銥金屬卡賓配合物、由於重原子效應與配體間電荷轉移效應的雙重影響、亦預期會有較短的激態發光半生期、能夠間接的增加藍光 OLED 器件的操作壽命。

11304221.label: Realisation of objectives
11304221.value: As we stated in this proposal, the Ir(III) based metal complexes have been employed as red and green OLED phosphors in making various commercially viable OLED devices. However, up to current stage, virtually no true-blue Ir(III) phosphors were capable to afford both the high efficiency and stability in commercial OLED devices, imposing an unsurmountable obstacle to this technology. Hence, this deficiency encourages intensive investigation on the development of blue phosphors, particularly the carbene based Ir(III) complexes, as this class of emitters is expected to be more versatile in chemical designs and superiority in physical properties and efficiencies in comparison to those with other third-row transition-metal elements such as Pt(II), Au(I) and Au(III), respectively. For this reason, we launched this research project aimed at designing, preparation and testing new Ir(III) carbene emitters and fabrication of highly efficient blue OLED devices using these Ir(III) emitters, together with the boron-nitrogen based thermally activated delayed fluorescent (TADF) terminal emitters. Such a device configuration is important for its capability in inducing efficient Förster resonance energy transfer process from Ir(III) sensitizers to BN terminal emitters, giving blue hyperfluorescence or hyperphosphorescence, with very short exciton lifetime and excellent chromaticity. In line with our investigations, we have successfully obtained a series of brand-new designs of OLED blue phosphors with very high efficiencies, from which many OLED devices were also obtained with highly efficient narrowband blue electroluminescence. We hope RGC can agree with us that our project has proceeded satisfactorily. Moreover, we have completed all objectives stated in our proposal, which can be confirmed by the research outputs accumulated in Part-C of this report.

11304221.label: Major findings and research outcome
11304221.value: Our major findings are to confirm the potential of Ir(III) carbene emitters in serving as both the phosphors and sensitizers for durable and efficient blue OLED devices, which remained as a very important direction for current OLED technologies. Our findings also confirmed one class of OLED architecture, which involved utilization of our Ir(III) carbene emitters as sensitizer and boron-nitrogen (BN) based MR-TADF emitters as terminal emitters, to which efficient Förster resonance energy transfer from Ir(III) sensitizers to BN terminal emitters could give rise to narrowband blue electroluminescence. We then declared this narrowband emission (from associated OLED devices) as hyperphosphorescence. Moreover, the photophysical performance of our Ir(III) carbene emitters are improved by replacement of N-alkyl appendage on carbene chelates with more stable N-aryl counterpart and solved the problems on competitive cyclometalation for the carbene chelates featuring dual N-aryl appendages; namely: introduction of greatly asymmetrical design on N-aryl groups. Relevant approaches are of great importance to this community, and this is also the reason that we could publish many high impact papers as shown in Part-C of this project report, i.e., in the session of Research Outcome. However, we still believe that our design of Ir(III) carbene emitters has not yet reached their climax, implicating better designs are still waiting to be uncovered. Hence, this belief will give us a strong impetus in continuing the related research endeavors for another two-to-three years. Our goal is to invent blue phosphors that can be employed for further commercial applications.

11304221.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11304221.value: Our first target is to design and prepare durable and efficient blue OLED emitters. Moreover, our chelates should be equally suitable for preparation of other transition-metal complexes with unique opto-electronic, magnetic and photon-induced catalytic properties etc. It is notable that this project may not go beyond a period of five years, if there is no actual technological breakthrough. On the other hand, our proposed carbene offers possibility of making other compounds with distinctive properties mentioned earlier. Hence, even though we failed in getting wanted OLED emitters, our carbene chelates could be employed in synthesizing other materials based on earth abundant metal and lanthanide elements, which were also considered pivotal to future development of photochemistry and photo-physics of coordination compounds. We shall collaborate closely with our academic and industrial partners in continuing our current and future research plans.

11304221.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11304221.value: Emitters have been long considered a vital component for the organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs). Nowadays, albeit with inferior efficiency, blue fluorophores are still employed for fabrication of commercial OLED devices. To conquer this deficiency, scientists have invested considerable efforts in developing blue phosphors (or equivalents) for maximization of their efficiencies. After 20 years of development, only limited successes were obtained. Hence, at this moment, majority of people have considered the Pt(II) phosphors with tetradentate coordinated chelate should be the most probable candidates in serving as the blue phosphors needed for future commercial OLED devices. However, through our dedicated investigations, we have confirmed the high performances of Ir(III) carbene phosphors and revived their potential in future commercial applications. We intended to use the next two-to-three years of time to fully evaluate these Ir(III) carbene emitters, particularly on their durability and photophysical performances, and trying to push forward their actual applications in fabrication of commercially viable OLED devices.
