11304921.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11304921.value: 智慧手機、電動汽車和電網儲能站使用鋰離子電池 (LIB) 作為能量源。然而，LIB 技術並不理想，因為它依賴於易燃有機物電解質，帶來多種安全問題。 對於電池領域來說，解決這個問題的最直接和有效的策略是替代有機物電解質，例如，水系電解質就是其中一個重要選擇。安全電池市場具有巨大的商業重要性。例如，全球柔性電池市場預計到 2025 年將達到 2.96 億美元，年增長率為24.7%。 水性電池可以以更低的成本生產。製造成本和製造環境比 LIB 更寬鬆。雖然水系電池的安全性和成本效益是兩大內在優勢， 和 LIB 相比，它們的能量密度較低。這主要是由於它們的輸出電壓低。低輸出電壓通常歸因於具有窄電化學穩定性視窗的水性電解質的限制。反過來，可以通過增大輸出電壓和比容量來提高能量密度。我們深入研究了水性電池的優點和化學性質。相對於廣泛 使用過的金屬離子電荷載流子 (MCC)、基於非金屬電荷載流子 (NMCC) 的電池有提供改進性能的巨大潛力，特別是在能量密度和功率方面密度。在本項目中，我們建議使用非金屬鹵素離子碘化物（I）和溴化物(Br) 作為電荷載流子/陰極材料。我們將針對水性電池的挑戰以及可用於克服它們的策略將進行詳細研究。該項目的最終目標將是使用高性能和超安全電池用於儲能或者柔性電子設備。

11304921.label: Realisation of objectives
11304921.value: Supported by this project, we conducted a comprehensive investigation into host materials capable of effectively confining halogens and compatible electrolytes to enable reliable multiple-electron transfer processes. This research led to the development of batteries with improved capacity, higher discharge voltage, and enhanced energy density, with a high cathode loading mass and flexible applications, marking a significant advancement in the field. Design, fabrication, and redox reversibility of cathode materials: To address the challenges associated with zinc-halogen batteries, we explored two strategies to effectively host halogen elements while achieving high capacities. The first approach involves leveraging the physical adsorption between halogen elements and carbon-based hosts. By incorporating multiple halogen elements into a mesoporous carbon host, we not only enhanced the battery capacity but also evaluated the compatibility of the physical adsorption mechanism for different halogen species. For example, we employed a mixture of iodine monobromide (IBr) and mesoporous carbon host as cathode material, which effectively suppressed the cross-diffusion of Br2/Br3-. This suppression was achieved through the coordination between bromine and iodine and the efficient physical confinement provided by mesoporous carbon. The resulting Zn||IBr battery demonstrated two distinct voltage plateaus at 1.63 V (Br0/Br-) and 1.28 V (I0/I-) in a 2 M ZnSO4 electrolyte, delivering a high capacity of 267.3 mAh g-1 at a current density of 0.2 A g-1. The second strategy involves the utilization of chemical interactions between halogen species and protonated organic hosts. We designed suitable chemical host materials based on bis-ammonium host (ODA) to localize halogen species through intermolecular interactions, such as steric hindrance and hydrogen bonds like N-H…X (where X represents I, Br, or Cl). This approach mitigated capacity loss by synergistic steric hindrance and the interactions between the bis-ammonium groups and halide ions. Specifically, the bis-ammonium host confined halogen elements through steric hindrance and Van der Waals forces, which helped prevent cathode degradation and reduced the undesired crossover of halide and polyhalide ions. The resulting Zn||ODAI2 and Zn||ODABr2 batteries delivered high capacities of 235 mAh g-1 and 312 mAh g-1, respectively, at a current density of 0.2 A g-1. Tailored electrolytes for multiple-electron conversions and high-performance batteries: To fully unlock the potential of halogen cathodes for high-energy storage, it is crucial to activate more electrons from each electrochemical halogen element with high reversibility. Recognizing that halogen atoms with lower electronegativity in interhalogen compounds exhibit polarization, we introduced a trace amount of chloride ions (e.g., 0.1 M LiCl, KCl, or ZnCl2 additive) into the electrolyte. This addition stabilizes the high-valence I⁺ ion on the cathode electrode, which forms after the initial oxidation step from I- to I0 through the I…Cl interactions, enabling a two-electron transfer process based on the I+/I0/I- redox couple. Demonstrated batteries gave high discharge plateaus of 1.71 V vs. Zn2+/Zn and 3.41 V vs. Li+/Li and nearly doubled the capacity and energy density compared to the one-electron conversion of I0/I-. Given that the high activity of free water molecules inside the electrolytes can inevitably cause the decomposition and reduction of the I+ ion, the rate performance and cycling stability of such batteries are significantly limited. We designed a concentrated ZnCl2 electrolyte (30 m) and an activated carbon host to enable multiple-electron conversions involving high-valence halogen elements for reliable high-energy batteries. Generally, Zn(H2O)62+ represents the dominant solvation structure in diluted electrolytes, such as 1 M ZnCl2, indicating the presence of a large number of highly reactive water molecules. As the concentration of zinc chloride increases, Cl⁻ ions gradually replace solvated water molecules in the first solvation shell. At 10 M and 20 M ZnCl2, Zn(H2O)3Cl3- and Zn(H2O)4Cl2 become the predominant species, eventually giving way to a high number of ZnCl42- in 30 M ZnCl2. This increase in salt concentration is accompanied by a consistent disruption of the hydrogen bond network in the aqueous electrolyte. Specifically, each water molecule has an average hydrogen bond number of 1.21 in 1 M ZnCl2, which decreases to 0.53, 0.17, and 0.08 in 10 M, 20 M, and 30 M ZnCl2, respectively. This decline in hydrogen bonding reflects a reduction in the reactivity of water, which aligns with the observed broadening of the electrochemical stability window and the suppression of the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) to support reversible redox reactions of high-valence halogen elements. As such, the electrodeposited iodine at the positive electrode interacts with chloride ions from the electrolyte, enabling interhalogen coordination chemistry and forming ICl3- at high voltages without hydrolysis, as supported by in situ and ex situ spectroscopic analyses and theoretical calculations. This process not only facilitates a two-electron transfer based on the I+/I0/I- redox couple (with plateaus at 1.59 V and 1.13 V vs. Zn2+/Zn) but also promotes the stabilization of oxidized Cl0 by coordination with iodine elements. This coordination contributes to an additional one-electron transfer of Cl0/Cl- at a higher potential (1.84 V vs. Zn2+/Zn), further enhancing the maximum specific capacity (612 mAh gI-1 at 0.5 A gI-1) and energy density (905 Wh kgI2-1) while evaluating based on the net mass of electrodeposited iodine. The designed 30 m ZnCl2 electrolyte has also shown promise in suppressing the side reactions and simultaneously inhibits the dissolution of iodine elements to ensure good cycling stability (2000 cycles at 2 A g-1 for Swagelok cells, 300 cycles at 2.5 A cm-2 for the pouch cell). Functional batteries utilizing engineered halogen cathode materials: We also fabricated two-dimensional tin-based iodine-rich Dion-Jacobson (DJ) perovskite microcrystals, ODASnI4 (ODA: 1,8-octanediamine), as cathode materials. Density functional theory (DFT) analysis demonstrated that the electrochemical performance can probably be enhanced by the short-range ordered perovskite lattice and the presence of unbonded halogen species that are localized at the amorphous-aqueous electrolyte interface. The residual (002) crystallographic plane of ODASnI4 exhibited distinct adsorption energies of -0.70 eV and -1.58 eV for triiodide (I3-) and iodine (I2), respectively. These adsorptive interactions generated halogen-bonded structures with interatomic distances of 3.030 Å (Sn-I⋯I2) and 3.469 Å/3.381 Å (Sn-I⋯I3-). Theoretical calculations under vacuum conditions further quantified coordination energies and electrostatic forces between cationic ODA2⁺ and anionic I3⁻ (-6.21 eV), ODA2⁺ and neutral I2 (-1.07 eV), Sn2⁺ and I3- (-11.36 eV), and Sn2⁺ and I2 (-4.44 eV), disregarding the influence of aqueous environments. The significant adsorption energies for I3- and I2 confirm that integrating ODASnI4 perovskite microcrystals into cathodes mitigates the polysulfide-like shuttle mechanism, highlighting their potential for stabilizing halogen redox processes and durable zinc-ion batteries. The assembled Zn|2 M ZnSO₄ + 0.5 M LiCl|ODASnI4 rigid battery exhibited two distinct voltage plateaus at 1.71 V (I+/I0) and 1.18 V (I0/I-), contributing to a high specific capacity of 489 mAh g-1 at 0.5 A g-1. This capacity is double that of conventional one-electron iodine conversion. Even at higher current densities of 2 A g-1 and 2.5 A g-1, the battery maintained impressive capacities of 384 mAh g-1 and 372 mAh g-1, respectively. To enhance flexibility, a polymerized acrylamide matrix was prepared using N, N'-methylenebisacrylamide and potassium persulfate, replacing the traditional membrane and effectively holding the aqueous electrolyte. The flexible pouch battery, incorporating the ODASnI4 cathode and an optimized zinc anode, successfully powered a cold light panel, demonstrating its practical application potential.

11304921.label: Major findings and research outcome
11304921.value: We developed two strategies to effectively host halogen elements. The first approach lies in leveraging the physical adsorption between halogen species (halogen and halide anions) and carbon-based hosts. The second strategy utilizes chemical interactions between halogen elements and protonated organic hosts to restrain the loss of active species. We designed tailored chemical host materials to localize halogen species through intermolecular interactions, such as steric hindrance and hydrogen bonds, e.g., N-H…X (where X = I, Br, or Cl). Both strategies effectively restrained the dissolution of (poly)halide anions and mitigated the undesired shuttle effect, ultimately enhancing the electrochemical performance and cycling stability of the studied batteries. For example, a Zn||IBr battery fabricated using mesoporous carbon and iodine monobromide as cathode materials exhibited two distinct voltage plateaus at 1.63 V (from the Br0/Br- redox couple) and 1.28 V (from the I0/I- redox coupe) in a 2 M ZnSO4 electrolyte, delivering a high capacity of 267.3 mAh g-1 at a current density of 0.2 A g-1.[Ref. 10] Meanwhile, the chemical affinity of the bis-ammonium host toward iodide and bromide anions enabled capacities of 235 mAh g-1 for Zn||ODAI2 and 312 mAh g-1 for Zn||ODABr2, respectively, at the same current density.[Ref. 14] The assembled aqueous zinc batteries demonstrated excellent durability, achieving 10000 and 3000 cycles at 4.5 A g-1 for the ODAI2 and ODABr2 cathodes, with capacity retentions of 75% and 80%, respectively. Conventional halogen-based conversion reactions in aqueous batteries have a limited number of effectively transferred electrons during the whole electrochemical procedure. To tackle this, we introduced additional chloride salts into either ZnSO4 electrolyte or commercial electrolyte of lithium batteries to passivate high-valence iodine cations (I+) by interhalogen coordination. The exercises were verified valid and universal to enable a novel two-electron conversion (I+/I0/I-) in both aqueous and organic electrolytes, eventually achieving twice the capacity of the conventional one-electron I0/I- conversion.[Ref. 4, 5, 6] To further improve the battery durability subjected to the rich active water molecules in the electrolyte, we projected a concentrated ZnCl2 electrolyte (30 m) and an activated carbon host to confine halogen species and activate multiple-electron conversions. The increase in salt concentration is accompanied by the disruption of the hydrogen bond network and formation of high number of ZnCl42- in 30 M ZnCl2, generating reversible I+/I0/I- (1.59 V and 1.13 V) and Cl0/Cl- (1.84 V) redox couples. The assembled zinc-iodine batteries demonstrated a high capacity of 612 mAh gI-1 at 0.5 A gI-1 and 2000 cycles at 2 A g-1. The corresponding pouch cell (10 cm × 8 cm) was successfully assembled showing a high capacity of 124.7 mAh at 2.5 mA cm-2 and 73.8% capacity retention after 300 cycles. [Ref. 9] Moreover, a flexible membrane-free pouch battery based on a low-dimensional tin-iodide (ODASnI4) cathode was successfully fabricated by powering a cold light panel, showing its practical application potential.

11304921.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11304921.value: Multiple-electron conversion of halide-based cathode materials can provide at least three benefits: (1) Increase the specific capacity (and energy density) of the battery; (2) Enable batteries with multi-functionality and different application scenarios; (3) Greatly reduce the battery cost. My future research on non-metallic halogen cathode materials will be conducted in the following two directions: 1. High-voltage aqueous batteries can be theoretically achieved while enabling high-valence iodide/bromide cations (e.g., I+, IO3-, Br+) and stable Cl0/Cl- redox reactions in the electrolytes. However, oxidized bromine and chlorine are highly reactive and volatile. Supported by this project, we have demonstrated the effectiveness of physical and chemical adsorption for confining halogen species. Moving forward, we aim to develop advanced passivation strategies and/or adsorbents for elemental halogens, targeting aqueous batteries with a voltage exceeding 1.8 V and an energy density surpassing 200 Wh L-1. 2. We will investigate various electrolyte additives to initiate the redox reactions of high-valence halogens and analyze their critical relationships with the electrochemical windows of the electrolytes, ensuring the stable operation of high-voltage batteries.

11304921.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11304921.value: Multiple-electron conversions of non-metallic halogen elements in aqueous electrolytes offer a promising pathway for developing cost-effective, high-energy zinc batteries. By leveraging interhalogen coordination and physical/chemical adsorbents, reversible multiple-electron conversion reactions of halogens can be achieved with minimal side effects, such as the shuttle of halogen species in aqueous electrolytes. In this project, we developed conventional aqueous electrolytes enhanced by chloride salt additions, which provide abundant chloride ions to passivate high-valence iodide cations (I+) and enable two electron conversions of the iodine element (I+/I0/I-). Furthermore, a concentrated (30 m) zinc chloride electrolyte was designed to reduce the activity of water molecules, prevent the hydrolysis of high-valence halogen species (I+ and Cl0), and facilitate a three-electron transfer process based on I+/I0/I- and an additional Cl0/Cl-. The resulting aqueous zinc-iodine Swagelok cell demonstrated a high capacity of 612 mAh gI-1 at 0.5 A gI-1 and stable cycling over 2000 cycles at 2 A g-1. Meanwhile, the pouch cell (10 cm × 8 cm) achieved a capacity of 124.7 mAh at 2.5 mA cm-2 with 73.8% capacity retention after 300 cycles. The practicality of the flexible pouch battery was further demonstrated by successfully powering a cold light panel, underscoring its potential for real-world applications.

11305021.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11305021.value: Optical waveguides are structures that guide the propagation of light. Currently, there exist many different types of optical waveguides for different applications. In recent years, parity-time (PT) symmetric optical waveguides and waveguides supporting bound states in the continuum (BICs) have received significant research interest in the photonics community. PT-symmetric optical waveguides use a balanced gain and loss to realize non-Hermitian degeneracies, also called exceptional points (EPs), in their guided modes. Waveguides supporting BICs can produce arbitrarily strong resonant responses for waves impinging upon the waveguide core. These special optical waveguides have many interesting properties that can be explored in applications. The purpose of this project is to carry out a systematic mathematical study for PT-symmetric waveguides, waveguides with BICs, and waveguides with the so-called complex modes, through rigorous mathematical analysis, accurate numerical simulation, and improved mathematical modeling. We study some important theoretical properties such as existence and robustness, for EPs, BICs and complex modes in optical waveguides, and explore their applications. 光波導是用來引導光傳播的結構。許多不同的種類的光波導出現在不同的應用中。近年來，宇稱-時間（PT）對稱的光波導和帶連續譜中束縛態（BIC）的光波導受到了很多學者的關注。PT對稱的光波導利用平衡的增益和損耗來實現非Hermit的退化態，也稱為EP點。帶BIC的光波導可以產生理論上無窮大的共振效應。這些特殊的光波導具有很多有趣的性質和潛在的應用。本項研究的目的是對PT對稱光波導，帶BIC的光波導，以及帶複模的光波導進行一個系統的數學研究，包括數學建模，數值計算及數學分析。我們將研究光波導中的EP點，BIC和複模的各種性質（包括存在性和魯棒性），探索它們的各種應用。

11305221.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11305221.value: Lysine demethylases play critical roles in regulating many cellular events. Biological studies have shown that malfunction of lysine demethylases is associated with a number of important diseases such as cancers and neurological diseases. Consequently, it has aroused much interest to develop chemical tools for detecting lysine demethylase activity. A number of methods have been developed to detect lysine demethylase activity, including enzyme-coupled approach, antibody-based assays, and others. Nevertheless, few fluorescent probes are available that allow detection of endogenous lysine demethylase activity in native cellular environment. In this proposal, we seek to develop novel fluorogenic probes to detect lysine demethylase activity. In the first stage, we plan to design and synthesize high-performance fluorophores based on rhodamine. By fine tuning the substituents at the spirolactam nitrogen in rhodamine, we aim to develop new fluorophores with high fluorogenicity and cell permeability. After obtaining suitable fluorophores, a HaloTag ligand will be introduced to the fluorophores to examine their fluorescence turn on ability. Cell imaging study will be performed to examine whether the probe is able to image HaloTag protein in non-wash conditions. Furthermore, we will adopt similar approach to develop NIR based fluorophores with high fluorogenicity. NIR fluorophores have shown advantages in bioimaging such as reduced phototoxicity and increased tissue penetration. This will further expand the tool box of fluorogenic probes for live-cell imaging applications. Building on these results, we will move on to design LSD1 specific probes. Specifically we will introduce the optimum fluorophores to the known potent LSD1 inhibitor scaffolds. After verifying the probe’s chemical structure, we will first test the fluorescence response of the probes with recombinant LSD1 in concentration- and time- dependent manners. Subsequently the probes will be applied to imaging LSD1 activity in living cells. SiRNA and inhibition experiments will be performed to examine whether the probes detect LSD1 activity selectively. Furthermore, super-resolution imaging will be conducted to investigate the detailed cellular localization and the movement of LSD1 during DNA damage process. Through the proposed research, we hope to generate robust fluorogenic probes for elucidating the roles of LSD1 in biology. The current research team has extensive experience in fluorescent probe design and the bioimaging field. We are confident that the research will be completed successfully and contribute to the advancement of bioimaging and epigenetic research. 赖氨酸去甲基化酶在调节许多细胞事件中发挥了关键作用。生物学研究表明，赖氨酸去甲基化酶的功能障碍与许多重要疾病相关，如癌症和神经系统疾病，因此，开发用于检测赖氨酸去甲基化酶活性的化学工具吸引了研究人员的浓厚兴趣，迄今为止已开发出多种方法检测赖氨酸去甲基化酶活性，包括酶偶联法、基于抗体的测定法等。尽管如此，依然极少有荧光探针可用于检测天然细胞环境中的内源性赖氨酸去甲基化酶活性。在该计划书中，我们致力于开发新型荧光探针用于检测赖氨酸去甲基化酶活性。在第一阶段，我们计划设计并合成基于罗丹明的高性能荧光团。通过微调罗丹明中内酰胺位点的取代基，我们将开发出具有高荧光响应能力和细胞通透性的新荧光团。获得合适的荧光团后，HaloTag 配体将被引入以检查其荧光开启能力。随后我们将检验探针是否能够在非洗涤条件下对 HaloTag 蛋白进行生物成像。此外，我们将采用类似方法开发具有高荧光响应能力的近红外荧光团。近红外荧光团在生物成像方面展示了显著的优势，例如降低光毒性和增加组织穿透能力，这将进一步扩展用于活细胞成像应用的荧光探针工具。在获得高性能荧光团后，我们将已知的 LSD1 抑制剂引入荧光团来设计 LSD1 特异性探针。探针合成后，我们将首先开展时间梯度和浓度梯度实验来测试探针与 LSD1 的荧光响应能力。随后，探针将被应用于检测活细胞中 LSD1的活性，我们亦会开展siRNA和小分子抑制剂实验来研究探针是否能够特异性检测LSD1活性。在这些研究成果的基础上，我们将进一步开展细致超分辨率成像用于研究 DNA 损伤过程中 LSD1 的精细定位和动态迁移。通过该研究，我们希望产生性能优异的荧光探针以阐明 LSD1 的生物学功能。我们研究团队在荧光探针设计和生物成像领域拥有丰富的经验，我们坚信将成功完成该项研究，并为生物成像和表观遗传学研究的发展做出贡献。

11305321.label: Realisation of objectives
11305321.value: Realisation of objectives Objective #1: To investigate the neural activity from analyzing the nonlocal nonlinear integro-differential equations of neural field model with transmission delays. We had performed a thorough research on the recent development of nonlocal nonlinear integro-differential equations of neural field model with transmission delays. The main feature of these neural field models in mathematical neuroscience is to treat the cortical space as continuous medium. Since the brain involves a huge number of neurons and synapses even in a very small piece of cortex, this feature provides more realistic modelling for the large-scale neural activity of spatially extended networks of neurons as described in terms of nonlinear integro-differential equations. In these neural field models the associated integral kernels represent the spatial distribution of neuronal synaptic connections. Objective #2: To develop a meshless computational method which is efficient and effective for solving the nonlocal and nonlinear integro-differential equations for simulating neural activity. Based on the recently developed localized radial basis function collocation method (LRBFCM) and exponential time differencing (ETD) method, we derive in this paper an accurate and efficient numerical method for solving neural field models with space-dependent delays formulated as system of integro-differential equations. This combined LRBFCM-ETD method inherits the advantages of these two methods in space and time, thereby offering high accuracy and efficiency for both uniform and non-uniform discretizations, extending the applicability of the method to multi-dimensions easily, and maintaining a good behaviour in a large time-step and long-time integration. Some numerical experiments are presented and numerical results show that the obtained simulations via the LRBFCM-ETD method are reliable and effective for approximating the solution of the neural field models investigated in the current project.

11305521.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11305521.value: The boosting of nonlinear optical effects in nanostructured materials relies on the strong light–matter interaction, which is often associated with the optical near-field spatial confinement beyond the diffraction limit and resonant intensity enhancement. Localized surface plasmon resonances in metal nanostructures may enhance the nonlinear response of the metal and that of nearby nonlinear materials. However, the centrosymmetric crystal structure of many metals (such as gold and silver) forbids the bulk occurrence of certain nonlinear processes, such as second-harmonic generation (SHG), within the electric-dipole approximation. Beyond this approximation, SHG can be substantially enhanced in metal, dielectric, and metal–dielectric hybrid nanostructures with higher-order multipole moments (such as electric quadrupoles and magnetic dipoles), generating larger nonlinear conversion efficiencies that are crucial for potential applications in optical biosensing, nanoscale laser devices, and light sources. Although Mie-type magnetic resonances have recently been exploited to enhance the SHG of all-dielectric nanostructures comprising high-index semiconductors, there have been few studies on metallic nanostructures, probably due to the physical constraint of generating pronounced magnetic resonance in visible and near-infrared regions. This constraint can be alleviated by assembling individual metallic nanostructures into two- or three-dimensional resonant nanoclusters. For instance, we have recently achieved strong plasmon-induced in-plane magnetic dipolar resonance in an ultrasmall plasmonic nanocavity comprising a gold nanosphere dimer closely spaced from a gold thin film. Inspired by this preliminary observation, we propose to realize magnetic resonance-enhanced SHG in such plasmonic nanocavities and similar ones, and determine the physical mechanism of this effect. Theoretical analysis suggests that magnetic SHG results from the Lorentz force exerted on metal electrons, and that the nonlinear polarization is proportional to the cross-product of electric and magnetic near-fields, indicating that the nonlinearity is induced by magnetoelectric coupling. A microscopic hydrodynamic model has revealed that the overall SHG conversion efficiency is enhanced by collectively maximizing the Lorentz contribution, the nonlinear Coulomb term and the convective term. We propose to collaborate with Prof. Peter Nordlander at Rice University (USA) to perform stringent calculations to quantify the magnitude of the Lorentz force-induced SHG and other nonlinear sources as functions of cavity geometry and excitation conditions. We will then perform polarization-resolved, angle-dependent single-nanocavity-level SHG mapping and spectroscopy measurements to verify our theoretical predictions. This will delineate novel physical mechanisms for subwavelength control of nonlinear light scattering in metal nanostructures, thereby affording new physical guidelines for the design of efficient nonlinear nanoplasmonic metadevices. 納米結構材料中非線性光學效應的增強依賴於光與物質的強相互作用，這通常需要通過超越衍射極限的光學近場空間限域和共振強度增強來實現。金屬納米結構中的局域等離激元共振能夠增強金屬本身和其附近非線性材料的非線性響應。然而，很多金屬（例如金和銀）的中心對稱晶體結構在電偶極近似下不允許發生特定的非線性過程，例如二次諧波效應。與此同時，二次諧波現像在一些具有高階多極矩（例如電四極矩和磁偶極矩）的金屬、電介質和金屬-電介質混合納米結構中卻可以得到顯著增強，從而產生更大的非線性轉化效率，這在光學生物傳感、納米激光器和納米光源等領域應用具有重大意義。 盡管近年來米氏磁共振已經被用來增強高折射率全介質半導體納米結構的二次諧波效應，但對其在金屬納米結構中的研究較少，很可能是由於這種結構在可見和近紅外區域較難實現顯著的磁共振。將多個金屬納米結構組裝成二維或三維的金屬納米團簇有望突破這一限制。比如，我們最近在一個由金納米顆粒二聚體-金薄膜組成的超小型等離激元納米腔中實現了等離激元誘導的面內磁偶極共振。受這一初步實驗觀察的啟發，我們計劃在此等離激元納米腔內實現磁共振增強的二次諧波增強，並研究其內在物理機制。理論分析已經表明，磁致二次諧波是由施加在金屬電子上的洛倫茲力所引起的，而非線性極化與近場電場和磁場的向量積成正比，也進一步表明了非線性過程是由磁電耦合引起的。微觀流體動力學模型表明，通過對洛倫茲貢獻、非線性庫倫項和對流項集體最大化，整體的二次諧波轉化效率會得到大幅提升。我們計劃與美國萊斯大學的Peter Nordlander教授合作來進行嚴格的理論計算，以量化洛倫茲力引致的二次諧波等非線性過程的強度與腔體幾何結構和激發條件之間的關系。然後，我們將對單一納腔產生的二次諧波進行偏振和角度依賴的成像以及光譜測量，以驗證我們的理論預測。該項目的研究結果將實現對金屬納米結構中非線性光的亞波長調控進行全新的物理解釋，從而為進一步設計高效的非線性納米等離激元器件提供新的物理指導。

11305521.label: Realisation of objectives
11305521.value: We have achieved the proposed project objectives by undertaking the planned research activities, with details summarized as follows. Results achieved (1) We have successfully designed an ultra-compact plasmonic nanocavity consisting of a gold nanosphere dimer on a gold thin film, which supports a pronounced magnetic dipolar resonance. Importantly, upon excitation of this magnetic dipolar resonance under appropriate incidence conditions, a strong and well-defined spatial overlap between the enhanced magnetic and electric near fields is formed within the nanogap region. To achieve this project objective, we employed COMSOL Multiphysics to simulate the optical modes of a dimer-on-film nanocavity under various excitation conditions. By systematically tuning three key parameters, including the nanoparticle diameter (~ 100 nm), gap thickness (~ 2 nm), and the angle of incidence, we optimized the spectral response range and near-field confinement associated with the magnetic dipole resonance, as well as its spectral and spatial overlap with the cavity’s electric dipolar resonance. The simulation results reveal a strong localized magnetic field enhancement within the nanocavity gap, and the tight field confinement leads to a substantial spatial overlap between the enhanced electric and magnetic near-fields. Regarding experimental realization of the designed nanocavities, we synthesized silica-coated gold nanospheres using a modified wet-chemistry approach. The silica shell serves as a stable and well-defined dielectric spacer, forming a robust and reproducible nanogap when the nanoparticles are coupled to a gold thin film. This configuration effectively suppresses direct metal-metal contact, ensuring mode stability under optical excitation. Using our home-built oblique-incidence dark-field scattering micro-spectroscopy, we directly observed a pronounced magnetic dipolar resonance mode at around 950 nm under oblique incidence. The experimental results are in excellent agreement with the numerical simulations. Together, these findings establish a clear design principle for realizing cooperative electric-magnetic resonance enhancement in ultra-compact plasmonic nanocavities. These results have been published in Light: Science & Applications, 2025, 14, 305. (2) We have successfully developed a theoretical framework that enables both physical interpretation and quantitative determination of Lorentz-force-induced second-order optical nonlinearity in ultra-small plasmonic nanocavities. Within this framework, we can systematically engineer the nonlinear multipolar interference in the nanocavity, clearly distinguishing the relative contributions of different nonlinear mechanisms to the total SHG signal. This approach offers concrete and experimentally accessible guidelines for mode design, excitation configuration, and signal interpretation. First, in collaboration with Professor Fan Yang of Sichuan University, we investigated the linear and nonlinear optical properties of plasmonic nanoparticle-on-mirror (NPoM) cavities using transformation-optics-based theoretical methods. The introduction of transformation optics provides a simple method for obtaining analytical solutions, systematically analyzing the mode structure, near-field confinement, and nonlinear behavior in the NPoM cavity. Moreover, an effective medium theory has been proposed, characterized by effective surface conductivity and nonlinear surface susceptibility. These effective parameters can serve as a guideline for the nanocavity design in both the linear and nonlinear optical regimes. On this basis, we quantitatively describe Lorentz-force-induced SHG in an ultra-compact dimer-on-film nanocavity within a hydrodynamic model. Excitation of the magnetic dipolar resonance not only leads to strong local magnetic field enhancement (|H/H0|~25) but also produces a pronounced spatial overlap between the enhanced electric (|E/E0|~300) and magnetic fields within the nanogap. This overlap is essential for efficiently driving Lorentz-force-induced nonlinear currents and for achieving high SHG conversion efficiency in the far field. Consequently, in the designed ultra-compact dimer-on-film nanocavity, the contribution of the Lorentz term (P x H) to SHG is significantly amplified and becomes a dominant component of the overall nonlinear response. At the same time, we systematically analyzed the nonlinear sources and their far-field radiation properties. This method enables clear separation and quantitative comparison of different nonlinear mechanisms, including Lorentz term, Coulomb term, and electron convection terms, while simultaneously considering their interference during far-field radiation. Building upon earlier theoretical developments, we further advanced the investigation of Lorentz-force-induced SHG by introducing symmetry breaking in these plasmonic nanocavities. Reducing the structural symmetry activates additional nonlinear channels and further optimizes the spatial overlap between electric and magnetic fields. Within this symmetry-engineered platform, the characteristics and multipole interactions of different nonlinear sources were analyzed, further distinguishing the relative contributions of different mechanisms to the overall SHG signal. These results have been published in Physical Review B, 2023, 108, 205408, and Light: Science & Applications, 2025, 14, 305. (3) We successfully observed Lorentz-dominated SHG in the ultra-compact nanosphere-dimer-on-film cavity and experimentally verified the physical origin of the magnetic Lorentz-induced SHG at the single-particle level through polarization-resolved, wavelength- and power-dependent SHG spectroscopy measurements, achieving results highly consistent with the theoretical predictions. Using our home-built oblique-incidence dark-field scattering micro-spectroscopy, we were able to define the incident angle and polarization precisely to measure the scattering response of individual nanocavities. Under p-polarized excitation at an incident angle of 70°, a pronounced magnetic resonance mode was observed in the scattering spectrum at 950 nm. We conducted spectroscopic nonlinear-optical measurements near the magnetic resonance wavelength. The SHG intensity under the magnetic dipole resonance excitation is approximately ten times that without invoking this resonance. The SHG conversion efficiency dominated by the magnetic resonance mode is 6 × 10−8 W−1. The measured SHG intensity increases quadratically with the average power of the fundamental radiation in the used experimental range (0.3–0.9 mW within an illumination area of 1 um2), which not only reflects the intrinsic nonlinear nature of SHG but also indicates no structural modification in the cavities under fs laser illumination. Scanning the fundamental wavelength across the magnetic dipolar resonance mode, we observed strong variations in the SHG output. Without using any free-fitting parameters, we obtained an excellent qualitative agreement between the simulated and experimental SHG output. These results have been published in Light: Science & Applications, 2025, 14, 305. (4) Finally, beyond the original project objectives, we also observed an obvious difference in the size of two nanospheres within each dimer. This observation inspired us to investigate the influence of structural asymmetry in SHG of plasmonic dimer nanocavities. In a highly symmetric plasmonic nanostructure, even-order nonlinear optical processes, such as SHG, are often quenched in the near-field regime and hence forbidden the far-field nonlinear radiation (although the second-order surface nonlinearity of the metal can be improved by the enhanced plasmonic near-fields). Under this premise, the introduction of symmetry breaking is necessary for enhancing SHG. Therefore, we fabricated plasmonic dimer nanocavities composed of two gold nanospheres of different diameters and then investigated the influence of symmetry breaking in their SHG response. Our results show that SHG intensities of symmetry-broken gold nanosphere dimers can be significantly enhanced under off-resonance excitation, whereas plasmonic near-field enhancement mainly contributes to SHG under on-resonance excitation. The above-described research work inspired us to further break the symmetry in the plasmonic nanosphere-dimer-on-film nanocavity, which not only activates the contribution of electric dipole (often negligible in symmetric cavities), but also leads to a nearly three-fold increase in the spatial overlap of the local electric and magnetic fields. Both of these effects enhance the resultant SHG response. Through comprehensive polarization and symmetry analysis, we were able to achieve a quantitative description of the Lorentz-driven nonlinear behavior. These results have been published in Nanophotonics, 2024, 13 (18), 3337, and Light: Science & Applications, 2025, 14, 305.

11305521.label: Major findings and research outcome
11305521.value: Major findings and research outcomes of this GRF research project are summarized in the following six aspects. (1) Theoretically, we have investigated the linear and second-order nonlinear responses of a class of ultra-compact plasmonic NPoM cavities. The introduction of transformation optics provides an easy-to-implement approach for obtaining analytical solutions of such coupled plasmonic systems. (2) Experimentally, we have demonstrated modulation of the SHG intensity in gold nanosphere dimers through symmetry breaking. While the near-field enhancement still dominates the amplification of SHG under on-resonant excitation, we observe a significant symmetry-breaking modulation of SHG intensities under the off-resonant excitation conditions. (3) Numerically, we have designed an ultra-compact plasmonic nanosphere-dimer-on-film nanocavity supporting a pronounced magnetic dipole resonance at 950 nm, achieving strong magnetic field enhancement (|H/H₀| > 25) and spatial overlap with electric fields (|E/E₀| > 300) in the nanogap. (4) Numerically, we have employed the hydrodynamic model to quantify Lorentz-force-induced second-order nonlinearity in plasmonic nanocavities, decomposing the nonlinear source into Coulomb, Lorentz (proportional to P₁ × H₁), and convective contributions. Numerical analysis reveals that the Lorentz term dominates SHG, driven by pronounced spatial overlap between enhanced electric and magnetic fields in the nanogap—a key factor for efficient nonlinear current generation and high far-field SHG conversion efficiency. Additionally, we have systematically analyzed the nonlinear sources and their far-field radiation, enabling clear separation, quantitative comparison of mechanisms, and accounting for their mutual interference during radiation. (5) Experimentally, we have observed the Lorentz-force-induced magnetic SHG response at the single-particle level in the plasmonic nanosphere-dimer-on-film nanocavity. The magnetic dipole resonance increased the SHG output by an order of magnitude. The SHG conversion efficiency dominated by the magnetic resonance mode is 6 × 10−8 W−1. Our experimental results show excellent agreement with the calculations based on the hydrodynamic model. The strong field confinement in this ultra-compact nanocavity improves the spatial overlap between the enhanced electric and magnetic fields, facilitating Lorentz-dominated resonantly enhanced SHG. (6) Furthermore, by exploring symmetry breaking in the dimer, we enabled tunable contributions from electric and magnetic dipoles to the SHG response. Through comprehensive polarization and symmetry analyses, we quantitatively describe the Lorentz-driven nonlinear behavior. Notably, the magnetic SHG enhancement differs fundamentally from conventional nonlinear nanostructures—these traditionally focus on electric near-field enhancement. This distinction expands the design paradigm for nonlinear-optical systems. Beyond advancing understanding of nonlinear optics, these findings hold significant promise for nonlinear nanophotonics innovations and pave the way for advanced nanoscale nonlinear-optical systems.

11305521.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11305521.value: While carrying out this GRF research project, we discovered that stable insulating gaps are essential for supporting magnetic modes in plasmonic nanocavities, prompting us to consider whether quantum conductance might influence SHG in these structures. We realized that inserting conductive molecules into the gap could provide a controllable channel for quantum conductance, allowing us to study how electron tunneling affects the SHG response. Additionally, nonlinear chiroptics has garnered significant research interests from the nanophotonics community. Based on the light-induced circulating current characteristics of the studied magnetic resonance modes, we now have the opportunity to explore chiral SHG processes driven by these magnetic resonances.

11305521.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11305521.value: This research project focuses on investigating the second-harmonic generation (SHG) mechanism in an ultracompact plasmonic nanosphere-dimer-on-film cavity, with an emphasis on the magnetic Lorentz contribution that has long been overlooked. We designed a nanocavity structure supporting a pronounced magnetic dipole resonance at 950 nm, which achieves strong confinement and spatial overlap of enhanced electric and magnetic fields within the nanogap. Leveraging the hydrodynamic model, we quantitatively decomposed the nonlinear sources of SHG and confirmed that the Lorentz term (proportional to P₁ × H₁) becomes the dominant contribution under the magnetic dipole resonance excitation. Experimental results verified a ten-fold enhancement in SHG intensity, with a conversion efficiency of 6 × 10⁻⁸ W⁻¹ and excellent consistency with theoretical hydrodynamic simulations. By exploring symmetry breaking in the dimer, we further demonstrate tunable contributions from electric and magnetic dipole resonances to the cavity’s SHG response. This work breaks through the traditional reliance on electric near-field enhancement in nonlinear nanophotonics, establishing a novel design paradigm cantered on magnetic-Lorentz-driven SHG. The findings deepen the understanding of nonlinear optical responses in plasmonic nanostructures and provide critical technical support for the development of high-efficiency, miniaturized nonlinear nanophotonic devices, with broad application prospects in high-precision sensing, optical data processing, and nanoscale optoelectronic systems.

11305721.value: 自 1828 年 Wöhler 首次合成尿素以來，為了養活全球不斷增長的人口，根據統計2018 年已有超過 2 億噸尿素被用作氮基肥料。然而，越來越多的哺乳動物和工廠廢物排放的尿素已經使尿素污染成為一個主要的環境問題。尿素在水溶液中是一種非常穩定的分子，主要通過廢水進入生態系統；在海洋中，它會引發藻類大量繁殖並排泄威脅水生生物的軟骨藻酸。目前，工業廢水中尿素的去除依賴於高溫/高壓下的化學水解，大規模成本高。儘管從氨(NH3)工業合成尿素已經很成熟，但卻少有研究將尿素水解回“兩個氨分子”的反應以及相關催化劑的開發。在自然界中，這種反應是由許多土壤細菌中的脲酶催化的。然而，用天然酶解決這個環境問題是不可行的，因為它們很容易變性(denature)，在不論製備或是儲存方面都需要極高的成本。為了解決這些缺點，在過去十年中，開發具有生產成本低、儲存簡單和高pH/熱穩定性等優點的人工酶引起了廣泛的關注。 此研究計畫旨在設計和合成具有與天然脲酶相當活性的人工酶。正如文獻中所揭示的，脲酶催化尿素水解的機理為: (1) 在Ni-O(H)-Ni 活性中心吸附尿素並隨後(2) 在尿素上形成離去基團 (即 -NH3+)。這兩個關鍵步驟促進了水對尿素上碳的親核攻擊生成 NH3 和氨基甲酸。即使沒有脲酶的幫助，在水溶液中第二個 NH3 也可以很容易地被氨基甲酸釋放出來。我們的初步催化劑篩選顯示，此反應路徑需要路易斯酸 (Lewis acid, LA) 和布朗斯特酸 (Brönsted acid, BA)位點。然而，我們發現LA 強度不但影響了尿素的吸附(步驟1)也影響了步驟 2 BA位點催化的質子轉移。在初步研究中發現HNb3O8催化劑(並非NiO)可以提供最好的活性，此研究計畫首先將通過先進的表徵工具來揭示尿素的吸附/活化結構，建立結構-酸度-活性關係。然後，我們將在不同pH/溫度範圍下比較它們與天然脲酶的活性。除此之外，我們也將合成具有各種 LA/BA 強度的Nb層狀催化劑並測試它們的活性。此研究計畫的成功將可以為高活性人工脲酶的合理設計提供指導。

11306021.value: 可穿戴儲能設備對於集成了能量收集器供能電子器件的智慧服裝至關重要，因此在過去十年中不斷吸引研究者關注，並發表了大量高品質研究成果。柔性超級電容器、金屬離子和金屬空氣電池均作為候選儲能設備被研究過。其中鋅離子電池（ZIB）具有相對較高的能量密度，且鋅儲量豐富，因此極具前景。同時，ZIB中水基電解質的安全性滿足可穿戴應用的主要標準，此外還具有低成本和高導電性的優點。最近，ZIB中引入了水凝膠電解質，結合了作為隔膜的絕緣框架和離子導電的電解液，可防止液體洩漏並增強電池柔韌性。 由於鋅電極在強鹼性和酸性環境中腐蝕嚴重，因此在ZIB中首選中性和弱酸性電解液，如硫酸鋅和三氟甲磺酸鋅。後者可降低去溶劑化能，增強了鋅在陽極上沉積和嵌入陰極的反應動力學。然而，三氟甲磺酸鋅的高成本限制了其實際應用。因此，我們提出了一種低成本的替代品，甲磺酸鋅電解液，由於與三氟甲磺酸鹽相似的陰離子結構，預計該電解質對快速反應動力學的去溶劑化步驟擁有相同影響。此外，硫酸鹽和三氟甲磺酸鹽水凝膠的離子電導率不同，說明決定ZIB內阻的水凝膠中的鋅離子傳輸受陰離子的影響。因此，本課題將首次研究基於甲磺酸鋅的水凝膠中的反應動力學和離子傳輸。 此外，測得的水凝膠的離子電導率是由電荷載流子被靜電壓力驅動的運動和較小程度的擴散引起的。但是在充放電條件下，由陽極和陰極反應引起的濃度梯度引起的鋅離子擴散的作用更大。所以，研究不受電場影響的擴散率將有助理解離子傳輸過程，以及電荷載流子和水凝膠微結構的影響。因此，我們提議研究水凝膠電解液的擴散率和離子電導率，以揭示水凝膠微觀結構和陰離子對離子傳輸的影響。由於鋅離子和陰離子的分佈無法單獨通過實驗獲得，且製備不同微結構的水凝膠耗時較長，因此將結合數學建模與擴散率和離子電導率實驗進行研究。 固體電解液介面（SEI）和SEI層的演變顯著影響反應動力學和電極穩定性。對柔性ZIB的有限研究也證明瞭水凝膠電解液的准SEI或人工SEI層的重要意義。此外，最近類比研究結合聚合物骨架的應力和水溶液的高擴散性，揭示了混合電解質對抑制鋅枝晶生長的影響，強調了理解這種介面反應的重要性。然而，涉及水凝膠介面反應的反應機制和動力學還沒有得到充分的研究。因此，本課題將進行陽極水凝膠介面（AHI）上鋅枝晶的微觀可視化研究，以闡釋枝晶的形狀演變和生長。原位形成AHI層有望抑制枝晶形成。 水凝膠對通過陰極水凝膠介面的電荷轉移的影響也將通過阻抗譜進行研究。離子傳輸和介面反應的基礎知識將進一步闡述水凝膠電解液在ZIB中的作用，並助力可穿戴儲能系統的推廣和設計。

11306021.label: Realisation of objectives
11306021.value: Objective 1: The impact of hydrogel microstructure and counter ions on the ionic conductivity in hydrogels has been investigated via symmetric zinc cells using hydrogel electrolytes, which have different polymer (gelatin) concentrations [1]. The hydrogel electrolytes are denoted as GSx (x=0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3 g/ml), where G, S and x represent Gelatin, Solution, and the ratio, respectively. Through different gelatin concentrations, hydrogel electrolytes with different microstructure and pore size distribution were developed. The distinguished porous structure of the hydrogels shows the impact of the gelatin/solution ratio on both the pore size and the thickness of pore walls. As the ratio increases, the proportion of large pores decreases, and small pores dominate. Moreover, the thickness of the pore walls clearly increases with higher gelatin content in the hydrogel. The mercury intrusion porosimetry results shows that GS0.05 has the highest porosity (90.39%), whereas GS0.3 has the lowest porosity (71.73%). The ionic conductivities of GS0.05, GS0.1, GS0.2, and GS0.3 are 52.4, 23.5, 20.1, and 16.9 mS cm-1, respectively, which were calculated by electrochemical impedance spectroscopy. The conductivity decreases with increasing gelatin concentration, since hydrogels with higher gelatin/solution ratios have smaller pores and thicker walls, and thus lower water content, which leads to reduced ion transport. In addition, the hydrogel microstructure of bacteria cellulose (BC) has been investigated in our work [3]. The BC electrolyte possesses a highly porous 3D structure, which can allow a higher aqueous solution absorption, leading to higher ionic conductivity. EIS for the symmetric cell of Zn/BC hydrogel electrolyte/Zn was carried out. Then, the ionic conductivity of BC electrolyte was calculated (27.8 mS cm−1). Furthermore, the impact of counter ions on the ionic conductivity and reaction kinetics have been illustrated in our publication [2, 10]. Objective 2: The zinc dendrite formation on the anode hydrogel interface (AHI) was observed by operando optical microscopy (OOM). [1] The in-situ solid-electrolyte interphase (SEI) shell was formed at the electrode and hydrogel interface at the electroplating process because of the zinc dendrite formation on the AHI. The effect of the in-situ forming AHI layer on suppressing dendrite formation were demonstrated by CA test and SEM images. For instance, the current density of GS0.05 continues to increase over 100 s, which indicates that the zinc ions on the surface of the electrode tend to propagate laterally along the two-dimensional surface in long deposition expansion. Consequently, the current density reaches equilibrium, which indicates the surface area of the electrode remains constant. At lower porosity, the equilibrium current density is reached earlier, denoting improved inhibition of dendrite. SEM images of zinc deposition morphology in symmetric cells with GS0.1-0.3 electrolytes at early stage and long-term stage both show that hydrogel porosity decreases with increasing gelatin concentration, and the zinc is deposited more uniformly. As more dendrites are formed, the layer becomes thicker, which illustrates that the lower porosity leads to denser zinc plating. The effect of dendrite suppression using hydrogel electrolyte is also investigated in our work by Zn/BC hydrogel electrolyte in Zn symmetric cell. [3] Besides, the works on hydrogel-based zinc-ion batteries for overcoming dendrite growth and side reactions are summarized. [8] In addition, OOM was used to observe zinc dendrite formation on the anode in aqueous system. [5] To evaluate the efficacy of the MES additive in enhancing the uniformity of Zn plating while mitigating side reactions and disordered Zn dendrite formation, a detailed morphological analysis of Zn deposition was conducted. The real-time Zn plating processes were observed through in situ optical microscopy in Zn//Zn cell at 10 mA cm−2. The ZS electrolyte yields uneven Zn protrusions on the Zn surface within 24 min, progressively evolving into large Zn dendrites as plating proceeds. Furthermore, the emergence of bubbles on the Zn surface signifies the occurrence of H2O decomposition reactions. In comparison, the Zn deposition layer in ZS-0.05MES electrolyte maintains a relatively uniform and compact appearance, which lacks protrusions and bubbles throughout the Zn plating process. The zinc dendrite growth dynamics and the tin dendrite deposition on graphite felt in flow battery are also found untangled. [6, 9] Objective 3: The effect of the cathode hydrogel interface (CHI) on the charge transfer of the intercalation process was investigated on a CNFs@Mn3O4/BC hydrogel electrolyte/Zn cell. [3] To evaluate the redox potentials and reaction kinetics of the cathode materials, CV at scan rates ranging from 0.1 mV s−1 to 0.5 mV s−1 and EIS under open circuit voltage were performed. Two pairs of reduction and oxidation peaks are observed, where oxidation peaks at 1.59 and 1.65 V and reduction peaks at 1.24 and 1.35 V at a lower rate of 0.1 mV s−1. However, two pairs of redox peaks overlay when increasing the scan rates. At a higher rate of 0.5 mV s−1, the oxidation peak appears at 1.69 V, and reduction peaks emerge at 1.19 and 1.30 V. The electrochemical reaction is slightly dominated by the capacitive behavior, which is favorable for fast kinetic. According to the CV results, the electrochemical reaction is more dominated by capacitive control when the sweep rate increases from 0.1 to 5.0 mV s−1. In addition, the full cell exhibits a high ionic conductivity of 10.5 mS cm−1 according to the bulk resistance (Rb = 5.6 Ω) by the EIS presented, contributed by the 3D porous architecture of BC matrix providing more volumes for ion transportation. Charge/discharge rate performance of CNFs@ Mn3O4/BC hydrogel electrolyte/Zn cell were investigated under stepwise current densities from 0.1 to 4.0 A g−1 with five cycles. Impressively, the as-assembled cell delivered reversible capacities and CE of approximately 100%. Galvanostatic charge/discharge profiles at different current densities, where two discharge platforms are observed. The first and second discharge platforms during the discharge may be regarded as the insertions of H+ and Zn2+, respectively. Generally, due to volume expansion induced by zinc ion intercalation in Mn-based cathode leads to cathode dissolution. Nevertheless, the 3D scaffold not only provides rich active sites, but also its porous structure accommodates the volume expansion in the repeated charge/discharge process, which enhances the cycle stability. Besides, the CE maintains close to 100% throughout the cycling. High specific capacity of the cathode promises considerable energy density and power density of the battery. The CNFs@ Mn3O4 cathode delivers a maximum energy density of 560.6 Wh kg−1 and a maximum power density of 5.4 kW kg−1 based on the cathode mass. To probe the intrinsic storage mechanism, ex-situ XRD and SEM were employed to further study the composition and morphology of CNFs@Mn3O4 electrodes at different charge/discharge states. Ex-situ XRD pattern of the electrode in different states shows the characteristic diffraction peak of Mn3O4 became inconspicuous owing to the interference of the base carbon paper. After the first cycle, the two-stage discharge curve is more pronounced, because new electrodes typically require larger electrochemical forces (higher overpotentials) to drive the reaction. The charge transfer of the intercalation processes on cathode side in aqueous system is also investigated in our work. [5] Hydrogel-based electrolyte has been applied in our research on flexible zinc-air battery. [4] Furthermore, the works on cellulose-based hydrogels for sustainable, intelligent wearables are summarized. [7]

The distinguished porous structure of the hydrogels shows the impact of the gelatin/solution ratio on both the pore size and the thickness of pore walls. The conductivity decreased with increasing gelatin concentration, since hydrogels with higher gelatin/solution ratios had smaller pores and thicker walls, and thus, lower water content, which led to reduced ion transport. Hydrogels with lower porosity allowed for denser zinc plating during initial and long-term cycles since their high Young's modulus and the uniform distribution of micropores led to dendrite suppression by mechanical pressure and regulated ion transport, respectively. However, hydrogel electrolytes with higher porosity resulted in higher stability after long-term cycles because of enhanced mechanical recovery and because the voids generated between the hydrogel and electrode during electroplating and stripping were recovered. 11306021.value: The gained knowledge of ion transport and interfacial reactions will illustrate the role of hydrogel electrolyte zinc ion battery, guiding the promotion and design of wearable energy storage systems. Furthermore, the experience and gained knowledge of hydrogel electrolyte-based zinc ion battery will guide the preparation and design of polymer-based electrolyte, such as lean-water gel and all solid-state polymer electrolyte.

11306021.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11306021.value: This project aims to improve wearable batteries for smart clothing. We are studying a new, safe, flexible, and higher power density zinc ion battery that uses hydrogel-based electrolyte. This hydrogel is key because it prevents leaks and allows the battery to bend. Our research unveiled how the battery's ingredients behave, especially ions move transport through hydrogel, and elucidated the mechanisms of the chemical reactions where the hydrogel interacts with the battery's electrodes. By understanding how hydrogel behaves inside the battery, we provided a clear guide for designing better, more efficient, and longer-lasting power sources for future wearable applications.

11306521.label: Realisation of objectives
11306521.value: Over the course of the project, we translated the double‑protection concept into a reproducible, manufacturing‑compatible stack and exercised it under repeatable, device‑relevant stress protocols. The internal strand centered on an ALD‑deposited SnO2 interlayer with a deliberately tuned oxygen‑vacancy population. Drawing on prior lessons from inverted high‑efficiency device interfaces, we established process windows for substrate temperature, precursor pulse and exposure, and purge timing that yield ultrathin (few‑nm), highly conformal films across textured perovskite surfaces and electrode topographies. A moderate density of oxygen vacancies proved beneficial: it enhanced electron selectivity and reduced interfacial recombination, and it created coordination environments (Pb–O/Sn–O) that immobilize lead ions generated upon perovskite degradation. In static soaking and metered‑dripping protocols intended to emulate rainwater ingress and condensate exposure, the ALD‑SnO2 alone consistently delivered apparent sequestration in the 80–88% range. Variations traced back to film uniformity at edges/steps, perovskite composition, and the ionic strength/pH of the test medium. Early‑stage open‑circuit voltage penalties were largely mitigated through interfacial energetics alignment (work‑function tuning of adjacent layers) and mild post‑ALD treatments, allowing the layer to act simultaneously as an electron extraction/passivation film and a chemical “anchor” for lead. The external strand implemented a chemical barrier by dispersing a strongly acidic cation‑exchange resin (Na+ form) into a UV‑curable matrix (UVR‑C), applied on the back‑electrode side after metallization. We mapped a practical processing window that preserves ion‑exchange capacity post‑curing while ensuring uniform wetting over the electrode and perimeter features. Key levers were resin loading and rheology; an overly viscous ink compromised edge coverage, whereas an underloaded formulation reduced exchange capacity per area. In model solution tests, free‑standing resin films rapidly removed the majority of Pb2+. Integrated on devices, the UVR‑C reduced detected lead in simulated leakage by roughly an order of magnitude relative to unprotected controls, without measurable penalties to series resistance or fill factor at the cell scale when viscosity and cure profiles were controlled. During scale‑up to sub‑modules, we adopted simple perimeter controls (masking, edge bead removal) and in‑line viscosity checks to stabilize batch‑to‑batch consistency. We then validated the combined architecture—ALD‑SnO2 inside, UVR‑C outside—under stressors that bracket plausible field risks. In an acid‑rain mimic (pH≈4.2, controlled drip), protected samples yielded collected water with lead signals at low‑ppm levels in our setup, contrasting sharply with tens of ppm from unprotected references. Under high‑humidity exposure (≈85% RH, seven days), condensate from protected devices likewise exhibited strongly suppressed Pb signals. Hail‑impact simulations (steel‑ball drop) deliberately fractured glazing to probe worst‑case leakage paths; this introduced module‑to‑module variability due to crack networks that can bypass barriers. Two mitigations proved effective: increasing ALD cycle count and dwell near the perimeter to improve conformality at edges and steps, and refining resin particle‑size distribution and viscosity to promote percolation into microcracks and robust edge sealing. These adjustments narrowed the spread across batches without degrading photovoltaic metrics. From a device‑performance standpoint, small‑area inverted cells with ALD‑SnO2 retained high power conversion efficiency and minimal hysteresis. Any initial voltage loss associated with the new interface was largely recovered after interlayer energetics and deposition adjustments. The encapsulation step was neutral to J–V metrics at cell scale and transferable to sub‑module footprints with standard lamination practices and attention to perimeter shunt suppression. Importantly, the interface and stability strategies used here align with our broader advances in inverted perovskites that have surpassed the 25% efficiency threshold and passed international damp‑heat criteria, as well as with a “self‑encapsulation” path based on oxygen‑vacancy‑engineered ALD‑SnO2 enabling long‑term operation at elevated temperature and light. This continuity of design logic informed gatekeeping criteria (e.g., acceptable voltage loss windows, pass/fail ICP thresholds) and reduced iteration cycles. Overall, the objectives were realized in practical terms. The ALD‑SnO2 interlayer contributed substantial, reproducible lead immobilization while maintaining charge extraction. The UVR‑C barrier provided a low‑cost, scalable capture mechanism that is process‑compatible and resilient to routine handling. Their combination raised apparent sequestration into the high‑90% range under multiple, independent stress scenarios. The work also clarified the main levers for further improvement—crack bridging and edge sealing—which we have already begun to address within the established process envelope, setting a clear path for larger‑area demonstrations and third‑party verification.

11306521.label: Major findings and research outcome
11306521.value: We established a practical double‑protection scheme that integrates an ALD‑grown SnO2 interlayer with controlled oxygen vacancies and a low‑cost ion‑exchange encapsulation to curb lead release while preserving device performance. Ultrathin ALD‑SnO2 was tuned via process windows (temperature, precursor dose, purge time) to introduce a moderate oxygen‑vacancy density. This improved electron selectivity and suppressed interfacial recombination, while providing coordination environments that immobilize Pb2+ formed during perovskite degradation. In device‑relevant aqueous exposure (soaking and metered dripping), the ALD‑SnO2 layer alone reproducibly captured a substantial fraction of released lead, typically around the 80–88% range across representative formulations and test matrices. Film uniformity and band alignment were identified as key levers to balance capture efficacy with charge extraction. Complementing the internal layer, we formulated a UV‑curable ion‑exchange barrier (UVR‑C) by dispersing a sulfonic‑acid cation‑exchange resin (Na+ form). Processing maps were defined to retain exchange capacity after curing, and resin loading/rheology were tuned for uniform coverage over back electrodes and perimeter features. In model solution tests, free‑standing resin films rapidly removed most Pb2+; when integrated on devices, the encapsulant alone reduced detected lead in simulated leakage by roughly an order of magnitude versus unprotected controls, without measurable penalties to cell‑scale series resistance under controlled viscosity and cure profiles. Combining ALD‑SnO2 with UVR‑C consistently pushed apparent sequestration into the high‑90% regime under standardized acid‑rain mimic (pH≈4.2) and high‑humidity exposure (≈85% RH, seven days). Hail‑impact simulations introduced variability due to crack networks that can bypass barriers; this highlighted the need for conformal ALD coverage at edges/steps and improved resin percolation/edge sealing. Incremental refinements in ALD conformality and resin particle‑size/viscosity narrowed batch‑to‑batch spread without undermining photovoltaic metrics. Overall, the results indicate a robust, low‑cost, and fabrication‑compatible pathway to suppress lead release under realistic stress while maintaining functional performance.

11306521.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11306521.value: The ALD-SnO2 plus resin architecture is inherently compatible with inverted perovskite stacks and standard encapsulation lines. Next, we will strengthen crack tolerance by enhancing ALD conformality at edges and textured features and by co‑optimizing oxygen‑vacancy density to balance conductivity with chemical binding. On the encapsulation side, we will refine resin particle-size distribution, loading, and rheology to promote percolation into microcracks and robust edge sealing, and assess regenerability or end‑of‑life handling to limit waste. Scale-up efforts will translate the process to larger laminated-glass sub‑modules with in‑line monitoring of ALD thickness/uniformity and resin viscosity, and extend stress protocols to multi‑cycle damp‑heat and thermal cycling. Independent ICP verification will be sought to benchmark procedures. We will also explore broader ion‑exchange chemistries to address mixed Pb/halide species formed during degradation and evaluate field-relevant durability with industry collaborators.

11306521.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11306521.value: Perovskite solar cells are an emerging type of solar technology known for high efficiency and low manufacturing cost. A practical concern, however, is that many high‑performing perovskites contain lead, which could potentially leak into the environment if panels crack during storms or long exposure outdoors. In this project we developed a “double lock” to address that risk. Inside the device, we add a very thin functional layer that both helps electricity flow and chemically binds any lead released during degradation. Outside, we apply a low‑cost resin coating that captures lead ions before they can wash out with rainwater. In laboratory simulations of hail impact, acid rain, and humid weather, this combined protection greatly reduced the amount of lead detected in collected water compared with unprotected samples, while preserving good power output. The materials we use are inexpensive and compatible with current production methods, which means the approach can be scaled. Overall, our results point to a practical pathway for safer perovskite solar panels without sacrificing performance.

11306621.label: Project Objectives

For a free boundary problem of PDEs of the compressible hydrodynamical model for warm plasmas , when the initial data are perturbations of the equilibrium solution, characterize the long time behavior of solutions, towards the equilibrium solution, and determine the time decay rate of the perturbations. 11306621.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11306621.value: 本項目的目的為研究由帶自由邊界的可壓縮流體耦合Poisson偏微分方程描述的帶電粒子的流體模型長時間適定性和動力學行為。這一偏微分方程組用於描述由通過Coulomb力相互作用的帶電粒子組成的溫等離子體的運動。 流體， 等離子體及相關研究領域的自由邊界問題自然地出現在眾多物理，工程及醫學模型，其理論研究和數值模擬都具極大挑戰性。 對於無粘流體自由邊界問題， 現有關於長時間適定性和動力學行為結果主要關於在各種情形下描述水波的帶重力無旋不可壓縮Euler方程組。對於無粘可壓縮流體自由邊界問題， 除了可壓縮Euler方程組的一些擴張解外，少有關於長時間適定性和動力學行為結果。本項目中所提出研究的偏微分方程組具有可壓縮流體部分以及關於電勢的Poisson部分。 正是Poisson部分使得問題具有定態解。 這一定態解可期望為動態問題的漸近穩定狀態。這與文獻中已有的可壓縮Euler方程組的擴張解的長時間穩定性機制有極大區別。 對於本項目提出研究的偏微分方程組， 利用法形式變換及關於常狀態為背景解的線性系統（歸結爲Klein-Gordon 方程）的衰減性質， 文獻中已有在不帶邊界的二維及三位歐氏空間中初值問題時間整體解的構造。 與這些工作比較， 本項目中問題的挑戰性在於自由邊界演化幾何和內解的相互作用及對長時間如何追蹤這種相互作用。事實上， 對於帶自由邊界的可壓縮流體及相關問題， 這類關於長時間解的結果很少。 研究非線性雙曲問題的長時間正則性一直具挑戰性和困難。 關於這些問題，在波方程，Klein-Gordan及Einstein 方程的研究中 已發展了高階加權擬線型能量估計及法形式變換的思想方法。 這些思想方法將被用於解決本項目中的問題。為此，研究長時間自由邊界的演化及表面波和內解的相互作用， 理解內解和自由邊界演化的偏微分方程的非線性結構具有實質性。 可以期望在本項目中發展的分析和幾何方法將會對流體及相關自由邊界問題具有應用。

11306821.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11306821.value: 计算鲁棒博弈扩充及完美d-扩充合理均衡点的紧致可微路径跟踪方法

11306821.label: Project Objectives
11306821.value: A Logarithmic-Barrier Robust Game and an Interior-Point Smooth Path to an Extended or Perfect d-Extended Proper Equilibrium: With the introduction of an extra variable ranging between zero and one and a polytope of feasible mixed strategy profiles depending on the extra variable and a pair of parameters, we will formulate a perturbed robust game such that every Nash equilibrium is an epsilon-extended or epsilon-perfect d-extended proper equilibrium. As an application of logarithmic barrier terms and a differentiable function of the extra variable, we will constitute with the perturbed robust game a logarithmic-barrier robust game in which all players jointly solve against a given mixed strategy profile a linearly constrained convex optimization problem. Applying optimality conditions to the optimization problem together with a fixed point argument, we will create an equilibrium system, which has a trivial unique solution when the extra variable equals one and can be exploited to construct an interior-point smooth path to an extended or perfect d-extended proper equilibrium in robust games. As an alternative scheme, we will also form a square-root-barrier robust game and derive an interior-point smooth path that meets the demands. A Convex-Quadratic-Penalty Robust Game and an Exterior-Point Smooth Path to an Extended or Perfect d-Extended Proper Equilibrium: Incorporating convex-quadratic-penalty terms into payoff functions, we will make up with the perturbed robust game a convex-quadratic-penalty robust game in which all players jointly solve against a given mixed strategy profile a linearly constrained convex quadratic optimization problem. We will capitalize on this penalty robust game to ensure with variable transformations the existence of an exterior-point smooth path to an extended or perfect d-extended proper equilibrium in robust games. Another scheme we will study is to generalize the linear tracing procedure and gain an exterior-point smooth path that fulfills the requirements. An Entropy-Logarithmic-Barrier Robust Game and a Smooth Path to an Extended or Perfect d-Extended Proper Equilibrium: Inspired by the quantal response equilibrium in normal-form games, we will form with the perturbed robust game an entropy-logarithmic-barrier robust game in which all players jointly solve against a given mixed strategy profile a linearly constrained strictly convex optimization problem. We will utilize the entropy-logarithmic-barrier robust game together with exponential transformations of variables to acquire a smooth path to an extended or perfect d-extended proper equilibrium in robust games. As for the quantal response equilibrium, we will study how the smooth path behaves as the extra variable descends from one to zero. Another approach we will exploit is an entropy-barrier-convex-quadratic-penalty robust game. A Compact Formulation: To meet the requirements of the perturbed game, the polytope of feasible mixed strategy profiles will have an exponential number of inequalities in terms of the number of pure strategies, which can cause a severe numerical difficulty even when the number of pure strategies is moderate. To tackle this problem, we will exploit the sorting networks and formulate a polytope, which has a polynomial number of variables and a polynomial number of inequalities or equalities in terms of the number of pure strategies and whose direct projection on the strategy space will be the same as the polytope of feasible mixed strategy profiles. Numerical Implementations: When a smooth path is constructed, we will first parameterize each point on the path with the corresponding path length. A system of differential equations will then be established to characterize the path. We will adapt a predictor-corrector method for solving the system. The emphasis will be on the exploitation of special structures for numerical stability and efficiency. As in interior-point methods, scaling technique will be put to good use. Various alternative methods will be explored for efficiently following the path. When differentiable path-following methods are successfully developed in the research, we will code them in both MATLAB and C++. Extensive numerical experiments will be carried out in a systematic way. A software package of the methods will be made available in both MATLAB and C++ for applications.
rows: A Logarithmic-Barrier Robust Game and an Interior-Point Smooth Path to an Extended or Perfect d-Extended Proper Equilibrium: With the introduction of an extra variable ranging between zero and one and a polytope of feasible mixed strategy profiles depending on the extra variable and a pair of parameters, we will formulate a perturbed robust game such that every Nash equilibrium is an epsilon-extended or epsilon-perfect d-extended proper equilibrium. As an application of logarithmic barrier terms and a differentiable function of the extra variable, we will constitute with the perturbed robust game a logarithmic-barrier robust game in which all players jointly solve against a given mixed strategy profile a linearly constrained convex optimization problem. Applying optimality conditions to the optimization problem together with a fixed point argument, we will create an equilibrium system, which has a trivial unique solution when the extra variable equals one and can be exploited to construct an interior-point smooth path to an extended or perfect d-extended proper equilibrium in robust games. As an alternative scheme, we will also form a square-root-barrier robust game and derive an interior-point smooth path that meets the demands.

A Convex-Quadratic-Penalty Robust Game and an Exterior-Point Smooth Path to an Extended or Perfect d-Extended Proper Equilibrium: Incorporating convex-quadratic-penalty terms into payoff functions, we will make up with the perturbed robust game a convex-quadratic-penalty robust game in which all players jointly solve against a given mixed strategy profile a linearly constrained convex quadratic optimization problem. We will capitalize on this penalty robust game to ensure with variable transformations the existence of an exterior-point smooth path to an extended or perfect d-extended proper equilibrium in robust games. Another scheme we will study is to generalize the linear tracing procedure and gain an exterior-point smooth path that fulfills the requirements.

An Entropy-Logarithmic-Barrier Robust Game and a Smooth Path to an Extended or Perfect d-Extended Proper Equilibrium: Inspired by the quantal response equilibrium in normal-form games, we will form with the perturbed robust game an entropy-logarithmic-barrier robust game in which all players jointly solve against a given mixed strategy profile a linearly constrained strictly convex optimization problem. We will utilize the entropy-logarithmic-barrier robust game together with exponential transformations of variables to acquire a smooth path to an extended or perfect d-extended proper equilibrium in robust games. As for the quantal response equilibrium, we will study how the smooth path behaves as the extra variable descends from one to zero. Another approach we will exploit is an entropy-barrier-convex-quadratic-penalty robust game.

A Compact Formulation: To meet the requirements of the perturbed game, the polytope of feasible mixed strategy profiles will have an exponential number of inequalities in terms of the number of pure strategies, which can cause a severe numerical difficulty even when the number of pure strategies is moderate. To tackle this problem, we will exploit the sorting networks and formulate a polytope, which has a polynomial number of variables and a polynomial number of inequalities or equalities in terms of the number of pure strategies and whose direct projection on the strategy space will be the same as the polytope of feasible mixed strategy profiles.

Numerical Implementations: When a smooth path is constructed, we will first parameterize each point on the path with the corresponding path length. A system of differential equations will then be established to characterize the path. We will adapt a predictor-corrector method for solving the system. The emphasis will be on the exploitation of special structures for numerical stability and efficiency. As in interior-point methods, scaling technique will be put to good use. Various alternative methods will be explored for efficiently following the path. When differentiable path-following methods are successfully developed in the research, we will code them in both MATLAB and C++. Extensive numerical experiments will be carried out in a systematic way. A software package of the methods will be made available in both MATLAB and C++ for applications.

11306821.value: 博弈论作为一种冲突建模与分析工具，已经被成功应用于各个领域。在这些应用中，纳什均衡及其精炼的计算发挥着至关重要的作用。近来学者们将鲁棒优化引入正则形式的博弈中，并发展出鲁棒博弈理论。该理论能有效解决应用中常出现的收益不确定问题。当鲁棒博弈有限时，可以将纳什均衡及其精炼的概念自然地推广到该博弈。Milgrom and Mollner(2020)提出扩展适当均衡的概念，其是适当均衡的严格精炼。然而，扩展适当均衡存在固有的计算困难，即使博弈中纯策略的数量适中。为了缓解这种困难，我们提出完美d-扩展适当均衡的概念。本项目致力于提出有效且高效的可微路径跟踪算法来计算鲁棒博弈中的扩展适当均衡或完美d-扩展适当均衡，其中收益不确定性被刻画为有界的多面体。为了实现这一目标，我们引入了一个在0和1之间变动的额外变量，以及一个关于额外变量的可微递增函数，其函数值在0和1之间并且先于额外变量减少至0。随后我们构造一个摄动鲁棒博弈，其中所有参与者在面对给定的混合策略组合时求解一个线性规划，并确保摄动博弈的每个纳什均衡都是一个ε-扩展适当均衡或者ε-完美d-扩展适当均衡。利用这个摄动博弈和递增函数，我们构造障碍鲁棒博弈或惩罚鲁棒博弈，其可以用于建立一条通向鲁棒博弈中扩展适当均衡或完美d-扩展适当均衡的光滑路径。为了减少计算负担，特别是当纯策略的数量很多时，我们利用排序网络并获得上述线性规划问题的紧密公式化表达，其中变量数量、不等式或等式数量都是多项式的。通过运用博弈的特殊结构以及缩放比例技术，我们提出能在数值上跟踪上述光滑路径的高效程序，并为应用这些方法提供一个软件包。

11307121.label: Project Objectives
11307121.value: To examine the contamination situation of organotins (OTs) in the coastal marine environment of Hong Kong after the implementation of the AFS Convention (i.e., Cap. 413N) in January 2017, by determining imposex status in the marine gastropod Reishia clavigera, and quantifying the concentrations of various OTs in the gastropod, seawater and sediment samples, and by comparing the results with relevant historical data (i.e., we will test an overarching hypothesis that the management intervention and law enforcement can effectively reduce the OTs contamination and imposex incidence). To conduct both laboratory and field studies to test the hypothesis that OTs, especially triphenyltin (TPT), at environmentally relevant concentrations can significantly alter species compositions of the marine benthic community in sediments as depicted by the environmental DNA profile. Through laboratory-based microcosm studies, we will reveal the temporal changes of the eDNA diversity in sediment after spiking with environmentally relevant concentrations of TPT and OTs, respectively. Concomitantly, we will examine the diversity of eDNA in the coastal marine sediment samples collected along a pollution gradient, and establish the relationship between the eDNA diversity and the concentrations of OTs in the sediment. Based on the results, we will determine effect thresholds (i.e., predicted no effect concentrations) of TPT and OTs, at or below which the integrity of the benthic community remains unchanged, and will better understand the impact of these chemicals to the benthic ecosystem.
