11500421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11500421.value: Organizations have started to use artificial intelligence (AI) for recruitment because of its promise to handle large volumes of applicant data, standardize decision procedures, and improve performance through highly consistent and accurate decisions. However, many job applicants and human resources professionals (HRPs) remain skeptical about AI’s recommendations in the selection process. In part, job applicants are concerned with fairness, while HRPs are concerned with AI’s predictive accuracy. They may worry about the inherent biases of AI, which stem from skewed patterns in organizations’ past recruitment behaviors (e.g., only hiring males or graduates from certain colleges). This situation may practically explain why AI recruitment tools have experienced resistance from job applicants and HRPs. This research proposal with two studies aims to draw on the organizational justice perspective to clarify the psychological mechanisms underlying resistance to AI recruitment tools. Moreover, we aim to explain the boundary conditions in which AI-led recruitment is acceptable or may even be preferred over HRPs. Study 1 investigates if job applicants have different perceptions of recruitment decisions on the various dimensions of organizational justice (i.e., distributive, procedural, interpersonal, and informational) when they are made by an AI as opposed to HRPs. We also investigate how these differences in justice perception impact applicants’ attitudes and behaviors on AI-led recruitment processes (mediating effect). Furthermore, we explore how applicants’ perceived organizational justice AI-led recruitment decisions could be improved relative to those from HRPs. In particular, we test if the explanation level and anthropomorphism degree of the AI recruitment tool will alter applicants’ justice perceptions and responses to recruitment decisions. Lastly, we present a social power perspective to test if applicants’ actual and perceived social power impacts their justice perceptions and acceptance of AI-led recruitment processes. Study 2 explores the issues from HRPs’ perspective to determine the best combination of different types of AI explanations (i.e., input, process, and output) with AI bias forewarning to persuade HRP to use AI for confirmation, as hiring aid, or delegation. In addition, we examine whether HRPs’ various justice perceptions mediate the effects of explanations on their reliance on AI. Collectively, these studies seek to provide important contributions to the literature at the nexus of human-computer interactions (HCI), organizational justice, and human resource management. In particular, we aim to advance our understanding of the psychological mechanisms and boundary conditions that influence the acceptance of AI in the recruitment processes from the applicants and HRPs’ perspectives. 很多著名公司已開始使用人工智能 （AI） 進行招聘，因為AI能處理大量申請人的數據，有標準化決策程式，並通過高度準確的決策來提高效率。然而，許多求職者和人力資源專業人員 （HRP） 仍然對 AI 在甄選過程中提出的建議持懷疑態度。的確，求職者關心公平性，而人力資源部則關注人工智慧的預測準確性。他們可能擔心人工智慧的內在偏見。這些偏見可能源於企業過去招聘行為（例如，只僱用男性或某些學院的畢業生）的模式。這種情況實際上可以解釋為什麼人工智能招聘工具受到求職者和人力資源部的抵制。此外，我們旨在解釋用人工智能協助招聘是可以接受的，甚至可能優於人力資源部的邊界條件。研究一將調查求職者在由人工智能而不是人力資源部做出招聘決定時，是否對組織公正的各個方面（即分配、程式、人際關係和資訊）有不同的看法。此外，我們探討如何改善申請人認為由人工智能主導的招聘決策與人力資源部的招聘決策。特別是，我們測試人工智能招聘工具的解釋水準和擬人化程度是否會改變申請人的正義觀念和對招聘決定的反應。最後，我們提出一個社會權力視角，以測試申請人的實際和感知的社會權力是否影響他們的正義觀念和接受人工智能主導的招聘過程。研究二從 HRP 的角度探討這些問題，以確定不同類型的 AI 解釋（即輸入、流程和輸出）與 AI 偏見預警的最佳組合，以說服 HRP 使用 AI 進行確認，作為招聘協助或委託。總的來說，這些研究旨在為人機交互（HCI）、組織正義和人力資源管理等相關文獻提供重要貢獻。

11500421.label: Realisation of objectives
11500421.value: Thus far, we have submitted one paper to MIS Quarterly for review and published five international conference papers from this project, one in ICIS 2023, two in PACIS 2024, one in AMCIS 2024, and another in AMCIS 2025. We are also developing the conference papers for journal submission. Most of the seven objectives are completely achieved, except for the degree of anthropomorphism of an AI system stated in Objective 3. The reason for not examining the degree of anthropomorphism is that there is a fast-growing emerging literature on the topic of AI anthropomorphism, which makes the study of it less novel. Instead, we build on the findings of Objective 3 about outcome explanations by examining the impact of different types of outcome explanations (referent-based vs. rejection rate-based, newly developed idea) on applicants’ acceptance of AI-generated rejection letters. Outcome explanations emphasize either referent information or rejection rates. While both aim to enhance fairness perceptions, they may differ in the extent to which they address applicants’ concerns about the legitimacy of the rejection decision. We postulate that applicants prefer referent explanations (grounded in equity) over rejection rate explanations (grounded in equality), as referent explanations align more closely with merit-based fairness expectations—particularly in competitive hiring contexts. Currently, this newly added idea on deeper investigation of two types of outcome explanations, along with Objectives 1 and 2, is included in one paper currently under review in MIS Quarterly. Additionally, we extend the role of AI in sending rejection letters to AI interviews and publish a paper in PACIS 2024. As technology evolves, e-interviewing gains prominence for its efficiency and resource-saving benefits. Despite this, AI interviews consistently elicit negative candidate attitudes. To improve perceptions of this emerging method, we examine candidate responses to different AI interview designs. Specifically, we explore how interview style and monitoring alerts affect perceptions of organizational attractiveness and attitude to rejection. Our experiment reveals that alerts enhance both the positive relationship between a friendly interview style and organization attractiveness, as well as the negative relationship between a friendly style and attitude towards rejection, both mediated by perceived warmth and competence. These findings shed light on the impact of alerts on candidate perceptions, informing our understanding of AI interview design. They also offer practical insights for organizations employing such systems, illustrating the intricate dynamics between interview styles, alert cues, and candidate perceptions, ultimately shaping organizational attractiveness and response to rejection.

rows: The overarching objective of Study 1 is to examine how to increase job applicants’ acceptance of artificial intelligence (AI)-led recruitment systems’ decisions. The first of the five objectives of Study 1 is to examine whether applicants will report more positive attitudes toward the organization if recruitment decisions are made by human resources professionals (HRPs) compared with an AI.

Study 1’s second objective is to evaluate if applicants perceive recruitment decisions differently in terms of the various dimensions of organizational justice (i.e., distributive, procedural, informational, and interpersonal) when they are made by an AI as opposed to HRPs. We likewise aim to assess whether such perceived differences in organizational justice mediates the effects of hiring deciders on the attitudinal and behavioral responses of both decision-makers.

The third objective is to study if the design features of an AI recruitment tool will alter applicants’ informational justice perceptions and attitudinal and behavioral responses to recruitment decisions made by an AI (vs. HRPs). To this end, we propose the design features of explanations (i.e., input, process, outcome) and degree of anthropomorphism of an AI system.

The fourth objective is to examine if applicants’ actual and perceived social power impacts their justice perceptions and acceptance of AI-led recruitment tool (vs. HRPs). Lastly, Study 1 likewise aims to evaluate whether such perceptions vary depending on applicants’ belief on whether human decision-makers are likely to be biased for or against them.

Study 2 differs from Study 1 because the latter focuses on job applicants’ perspective in accepting AI-led recruitment systems’ decisions, whereas the former approaches the issue from HRPs’ perspective. Accordingly, the overarching objective of Study 2 is to examine how to persuade HRPs to use AI for confirmation, as a hiring aid, or delegation. In particular, Study 2’s first objective is to verify if HRPs’ procedural and distributive justice perceptions toward AI partially explain their resistance to AI usage.

Given that increased process and outcome transparency (explanations) may hamper HRPs’ ability to detect an AI’s mistake (Poursabzi-Sangdeh et al., 2018), the second objective is to evaluate whether a detailed input explanation can help address this issue and alert HRPs on the potential inequality of the data source for biased AI.

Study 2’s third objective is to examine the role of bias forewarning and explanation features (i.e., input, process, and outcome) on persuading HRPs to accept AI’s hiring decision. One reason for HRPs’ resistance to AI adoption is the potential bias, similar to Amazon’s automated recruitment system, which did not rate job applicants for technical posts in a gender-neutral manner (Dastin 2018). Therefore, Study 2 examines whether a forewarning to HRPs on various potential biases can help adjust their usage of AI and integrate AI with a different degree of reliance on the recruitment process.

11500421.label: Major findings and research outcome
11500421.value: Effectively communicating job rejections has substantial implications for organizations’ reputation and ability to attract future applicants. While human resource (HR) managers are traditionally responsible for delivering rejection letters, organizations are increasingly turning to artificial intelligence (AI) to automate rejection letter delivery. However, despite the growing adoption of AI in recruitment, little is known about how applicants respond to rejections from AI vs. HR, whether explainable AI rejections can outperform unexplained HR rejections, and how different types of AI explanations influence applicant perceptions and behavior. Drawing on organizational justice theory, we develop a typology of explanation types and propose competing hypotheses regarding the effects of HR, AI, and explainable AI on applicants’ justice perceptions and acceptance of rejection outcomes. Across two experiments, we find that in the absence of explanations, applicants perceive AI and HR rejections as equally just and acceptable. AI process explanations, which clarify how decisions were made, do not improve applicant reactions compared to unexplained HR rejections. Conversely, AI outcome explanations, which clarify why an applicant was rejected, enhance perceptions of justice and acceptance, particularly when framed in terms of referent comparisons (e.g., qualifications of selected candidates) rather than general rejection rates. As technology evolves, e-interviewing gains prominence for its efficiency and resource saving benefits. Despite this, AI interviews consistently elicit negative candidate attitudes. To improve perceptions of this emerging method, we examine candidate responses to different AI interview designs. Specifically, we explore how interview style and monitoring alerts affect perceptions of organizational attractiveness and attitude to rejection. Our experiment reveals that alerts enhance both the positive relationship between a friendly interview style and organization attractiveness, as well as the negative relationship between a friendly style and attitude towards rejection, both mediated by perceived warmth and competence. In addition, the negative effect of the AI interview method compared with HR on attitude towards firms is weakened when the applicants' social power level is low, and such effect is mediated by perceived justice and social anxiety. These findings shed light on the impact of alerts on candidate perceptions, informing our understanding of AI interview design. They also offer practical insights for organizations employing such systems, illustrating the intricate dynamics between interview styles, alert cues, and candidate perceptions, ultimately shaping organizational attractiveness and response to rejection. Our findings also contribute to the information systems literature, particularly at the intersection of AI and human interaction in hiring processes.

11500421.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11500421.value: This project presents opportunities for future research. First, we used a scenario-based experimental design to simulate rejection experiences. While this approach enhances internal validity, future studies could enhance the robustness of findings and increase generalizability by considering the incorporation of real-world data or conducting field experiments. Second, although the participants reflected the age range of young job seekers—the demographic most active in job search—the results may not generalize to older job applicants or those in different life or career stages. Future studies should test the model across diverse applicant populations, including varying age groups, educational backgrounds, and levels of job experience. Third, our study focused only on process and outcome explanations. Future studies could explore other types of explanations, such as counterfactuals. Finally, while our study shows that explanations enhance organizational justice perceptions and acceptance decisions, it is equally important to examine how recipients interpret and process these explanations. The interpretability of explanations depends not only on their content but also on the format, expertise, and technical literacy of the recipient. Future studies could evaluate how these factors affect recipients’ interpretability and subsequent attitudes and behaviors.

11500421.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11500421.value: This research explores how job applicants react to rejection letters sent by artificial intelligence (AI) versus humans (HR managers) and whether adding explanations to AI rejections makes a difference. It finds that, without explanations, AI and HR rejections are seen as equally fair. But when AI explains why someone was rejected—especially by comparing them to hired candidates—applicants find it fairer and more acceptable. Simply explaining how the AI decided doesn’t help. The study also looks at AI-driven video interviews, which many applicants dislike. It tests whether friendly interview styles and real-time feedback (like alerts) improve perceptions. Results show that alerts make friendly AI interviews seem warmer and more competent, boosting the company’s appeal. Additionally, compared to interviews conducted by HRs, AI interviews are less disliked by applicants who feel less socially powerful, as they perceive the process as fairer and feel less anxious. Overall, this work helps companies design better AI recruitment tools—making rejections less frustrating and interviews more engaging—while maintaining their reputation and attracting future talent. This improves candidate experience while making recruitment processes smoother and more transparent. It also advances research on how AI and humans interact in hiring.

11500721.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11500721.value: 求同还是存异？线上渠道中的产品信息差异及其影响

11500721.label: Co - Investigator(s)
11500721.value: Prof Li, Xiaoling Prof Palmatier, Robert W.

11500721.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11500721.value: 随着电子商务的激增，消费者网上购物时常面对多个商家售卖同一产品或服务。想象一下，您想购买戴森吹风机。您的在线搜索结果里有40 多家提供此产品的卖家：戴森、亚马逊、丝芙兰等。每个卖家的页面对戴森吹风机和相关服务的描述略有不同。这些对相同产品的描述差异是否会影响您对此产品的购买兴趣呢？这个问题不仅对网络卖家很重要，对该产品的制造商或品牌商也至关重要。 不同网络商家提供的关于同一产品的信息存在差异（简称: 信息差异），从这些商家的角度是可以理解的。正如传统的营销智慧所说，商家故意将他们的描述区分开来，便于与其他销售相同产品的商家竞争，导致消费者遇到的信息差异。但是，总的来说，信息差异是否有利于产品制造商的总体销售？ 电商采取的自主差异化策略可能是一把双刃剑。一方面，差异使消费者难以处理信息，并可能引起对产品质量和/或真实性的怀疑。另一方面，差异化信息使消费者能够比较各个卖家的服务，并因此可能会吸引购买。 因此，信息差异对产品总体销售的净影响仍然未知。为了回答这个问题，我们确定了两种类型的信息差异——产品描述和服务描述的差异——并检查它们对总体点击率 (CTR)的不同影响。借鉴信息处理理论，我们提出 a) 产品描述差异会降低点击率，因为它引起真实性/质量怀疑并增加信息处理难度，而 b)服务描述差异通过增加感知差异来提高点击率，即使也增加了信息处理的难度。此外，我们调查了三种调节因素：产品价格、产品复杂性和市场集中度。 我们计划进行两项实证来检验我们的假设。第一项实证将使用大规模的点击流数据，取自中国主要网络市场中电子产品的数据，以测试主效应和调节作用。第二项实证将提供中介效应的实验测试。研究结果不仅会丰富我们对在线渠道协调的理解，而且为制造商、电子卖家和电子平台提供优化指南。

11501121.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11501121.value: 貿易，人口流動和大流行：新型冠狀肺炎疾控政策的效果

11501121.label: Project Objectives
11501121.value: We extend classical epidemiological models to incorporate endogenous migration and interregional trade across multiple regions. Simultaneously, we also introduce heterogeneous agents to a dynamic model of economic geography. We study the interplay between migration, trade, and pandemics. We show that, on one hand, migration serves as a mechanism to spread the virus, on the other hand, an automatic social distancing measure to contain the virus. We evaluate the impact of containment policies on pandemics and social welfare, especially policies that restrict migration. We study optimal migration policies that maximize social welfare. We apply the theory to the US by calibrating our model to 50 US states. We conduct counterfactual simulations to assess the effect of observed policies and compare them to alternatives.

We study the interplay between migration, trade, and pandemics. We show that, on one hand, migration serves as a mechanism to spread the virus, on the other hand, an automatic social distancing measure to contain the virus.
We evaluate the impact of containment policies on pandemics and social welfare, especially policies that restrict migration. We study optimal migration policies that maximize social welfare.
We apply the theory to the US by calibrating our model to 50 US states. We conduct counterfactual simulations to assess the effect of observed policies and compare them to alternatives.

11501121.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11501121.value: The 2019 novel coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic has caused enormous loss of lives worldwide and brought the global economy into a deep recession. Due to the deepening of globalization and urbanization, infectious disease outbreaks have become more common in recent years, including SARS in 2003, H1N1 in 2009, MERS in 2012, Ebola in 2014, and Zika in 2015. How to cope with pandemics while reaping the benefits of globalization remains a long-term challenge for humanity. This project studies disease dynamics and the effect of containment policies in spatial economies with interregional trade and endogenous migration. We build a multi-region Susceptible-Infected-Recovered (SIR) model with production, trade, consumption, and migration. Agents weigh the risk of infection and economic opportunities across regions to choose an optimal location for work and life in each period. Hence, agents automatically practice social distancing by avoiding high-risk areas. Our model predicts that if migration cost is sufficiently low, then the global basic reproductive number R0 can be greater than one even if the local R0 is smaller than one. However, when global R0 coincides with local R0, further tightening of migration control becomes ineffective in reducing R0. Consequently, there is scope for optimal mobility control. We apply our theory to the US economy. We provide reduced-form evidence using smartphone user data, which suggests that the risk of infection at the destination reduces bilateral migration flows. We also show that US state policies to contain the pandemic effectively reduced the number of COVID-19 cases. Finally, we calibrate the model to 50 US states and run counterfactual simulations to evaluate the effect of observed as well as alternative containment policies on the pandemic and social welfare. 2019 年新型冠狀病毒 (COVID-19) 大流行在全世界造成了巨大的生命損失，並使全球經濟陷入深度衰退。由於全球化和城市化的深入，傳染病暴髮變得更加頻繁。 包括2003年的SARS、2009年的H1N1、2012年的MERS、2014年的埃博拉、2015年的寨卡病毒。如何在享受全球化的好處的同時應對流行病是人類面臨的長期挑戰。 該項目在具有區域間貿易和內源性遷移的空間經濟中研究流行病疾病動態以及疾控政策的影響。我們構建了一個包含生產、貿易、消費和遷移的多區域傳染病 (SIR) 模型。 模型中的個體會權衡跨地區的感染風險和經濟機會，以選擇每個時期的工作和生活的最佳地點。因此，個體會通過避開高風險區域來自動進行社交疏遠。我們的模型預測，如果遷移成本足夠低，那麼即使局部基本再生數 R0 小於 1，全局基本再生數 R0 也可以大於 1。然而，當全局 R0 與局部 R0 重合時，進一步加強遷移控制對降低 R0 無效。因此，存在最佳移動性控制的餘地。 我們將我們的理論應用於美國經濟。我們使用智能手機用戶數據提供簡化形式的證據，這表明目的地感染的風險減少了雙邊移民流動。我們還表明，美國遏制大流行的國家政策有效地減少了 COVID-19 病例的數量。最後，我們將模型校準到美國 50 個州並運行反事實模擬，以評估觀察到的以及替代的遏制政策對大流行和社會福利的影響。

11501721.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11501721.value: 近年來隨著數字技術的進步和移動設備的廣泛使用，信息和通信技術 (ICT) 的生態系統已轉向移動應用市場。然而，應用程式市場競爭異常激烈，通常僅由少數領先應用程式主導市場。應用程式開發人員不得不頻繁添加新功能或發布新應用程式以保持在市場上的活躍性。因此，數字創新生態系統中出現了創新擴散悖論，即創新技術的快速發展可能會阻礙應用程式的傳播。 本項目探討了開發人員如何解決創新擴散悖論，提高其創新表現的創新策略。應用程式不同於傳統的實體產品：開發人員可以通過技術升級，通過版本更新為現有的應用程式添加新功能，或者發布全新的應用程式。選擇合適的創新策略成為了開發者面臨的重要議題。 本項目利用品牌資產理論來研究開發者應用創新策略對基於用戶感知的品牌資產的影響，並研究後者對創新表現的影響。品牌資產可以“打動”潛在客戶，並使產品在激烈的競爭市場中脫穎而出。然而，很少有研究從應用開發者的角度來調查應用傳播和應用創新策略的影響。我們旨通過提高應用程式開發者的品牌資產來揭示應用程式創新策略對創新績效的影響程度。 本項目計劃採用多層次、多方法結合的設計。我們將從開發者角度收集開發者應用創新策略和創新績效的歸檔數據，從用戶的角度將通過調查問捲的方法收集開發者品牌資產的數據。通過將不同維度的數據相結合，為品牌資產理論視角提供實證證據。 本項目將是從應用程式開發人員的角度來解決應用程式創新擴散悖論的開創性研究之一。本項目旨對數字產品在新興數字生態系統中傳播和品牌資產文獻做出理論貢獻。從應用層面來說，本項目的研究結論將對從業者選擇合適的應用程式創新策略提供建議。

11502021.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11502021.value: 消費者恐慌性購買和囤積下的供應鏈管理

11502021.label: Project Objectives
11502021.value: To study the investment and inventory problems among suppliers and retailers facing panic buying and hoarding. Such panic buying and hoarding may be due to pandemic or other reasons. To develop a theoretical rationale to better understand how supply chain investments and contracting affect current and future prices and quantities, and hence consumer panic buying and hoarding behaviors. To examine the impacts of policies on panic buying, hoarding, supply chain investments and contracting, and gain insights into the role of public policy in regulating business conduct and appropriate allocations of products such as PPEs.

To develop a theoretical rationale to better understand how supply chain investments and contracting affect current and future prices and quantities, and hence consumer panic buying and hoarding behaviors.

To examine the impacts of policies on panic buying, hoarding, supply chain investments and contracting, and gain insights into the role of public policy in regulating business conduct and appropriate allocations of products such as PPEs.

11502021.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11502021.value: According to a news release by the World Health Organization in March 2020, panic buying and hoarding are two of the four main reasons causing severe disruption to the global supply chain of personal protective equipment (PPE), in addition to rising demand and misuse. Such disruption creates huge risks for doctors, nurses and frontline workers who may not be adequately equipped to care for COVID-19 patients during this pandemic. In this project, we consider the contracting and investment problems in the supply chain, and focus on the effects of panic buying and hoarding behavior on strategic inventories of retailers and the resulting suppliers' contracting strategy. We define the concept of "the social welfare during the pandemic" (SWP), and study the impact of policies on panic buying, hoarding and supply chain investments. Finally, we will provide suggestions for the choice of public policy to improve the SWP. The successful completion of the project will contribute to the new research area of incorporating customer behavior into supply chain management. In addition, it will improve our understading of how customer panic buying and hoarding behavior affects the optimal strategy of retailers and suppliers, and shed lights on possible policies to deal with panic buying and hoarding in pandemics such as the current one induced by COVID-19. 疫情來襲，不少消費者紛紛搶購。這種行為給供應鍊和醫療保健系統的安全帶來了很大壓力。在這種情況下，可能會鼓勵零售商扣留庫存，而可能會鼓勵供應商進行產能投資。然而，疫情大流行的未來是不確定的，這給零售商和供應商的決策帶來了巨大的挑戰。 在這個項目中，我們考慮了供應鍊合同和投資問題，重點研究了恐慌性購買行為對零售商戰略庫存的影響以及由此產生的供應商合同策略。我們將定義「大流行期間的社會福利（SWP）」的概念，並研究了恐慌性購買對 SWP 的影響。我們將關注公共政策，研究政策對恐慌性購買、供應鏈投資和合同的影響。最後，我們將對公共政策的選擇提出建議，以改善 SWP。該項目的成功完成將有助於將客戶行為納入供應鏈管理的新研究領域；特別是，如果全面了解零售商和供應商，它將提高我們對客戶恐慌性購買行為如何影響最佳策略的理解。

11502021.label: Realisation of objectives
11502021.value: The project objectives have been successfully achieved, with significant progress made in addressing all the intended goals. The first objective, which aimed to study the investment and inventory challenges faced by suppliers and retailers during episodes of panic buying and hoarding, has been comprehensively addressed. The research provides a detailed examination of how such behaviors disrupt supply chains, particularly during crises such as pandemics, and highlights the challenges of inventory shortages, excess demand, and inefficiencies in meeting consumer needs. Drawing on real-world examples like the COVID-19 pandemic, the study effectively employs theoretical models to analyze these disruptions and their implications on supply chain performance. The second objective, focused on developing a theoretical rationale to understand how supply chain investments and contracting influence prices, quantities, and consumer behaviors, has been fully achieved. The project developed a robust theoretical framework using dynamic models and queue-based systems to analyze the interplay between supply chain investments, contractual mechanisms, and consumer panic behaviors. The findings demonstrate how strategic investments, such as capacity expansion and inventory buffers, along with tools like downtime rebates and fee-for-service incentives, can stabilize prices and ensure product availability. These insights are crucial in explaining how supply chain resilience can mitigate panic buying and hoarding, addressing both current and future challenges effectively. The third objective, which sought to examine the impacts of public policies on panic buying, hoarding, supply chain investments, and contracting, has been successfully addressed. The study evaluates the effectiveness of various public policy approaches, including consumer vouchers and provider subsidies, in improving supply chain performance during crises. The research highlights the cost-effectiveness of mixed-subsidy policies, which tackle both affordability and capacity constraints, and offers valuable insights into how public policies can regulate business conduct and ensure equitable access to essential goods. While the findings are broadly applicable, they also provide a foundation for addressing the allocation of critical products such as PPEs, with opportunities for further exploration in product-specific contexts. In conclusion, the project has made significant strides in addressing the theoretical and practical aspects of supply chain management under conditions of panic buying and hoarding. The research has delivered substantial contributions to understanding supply chain investments, contracting, and public policy impacts. Moreover, it provides actionable insights for improving supply chain resilience and ensuring equitable access to essential goods during crises. These achievements underscore the success of the project in meeting its objectives and advancing knowledge in this critical area.

11502021.label: Major findings and research outcome
11502021.value: The project has produced significant findings and advanced understanding in the area of government subsidies and their role in enhancing accessibility and affordability for socially-beneficial services, such as healthcare and other essential public services. These findings have resulted in two scholarly papers, each contributing key insights into the design and impact of subsidy policies. The first paper, titled Improving Affordability and Accessibility for Socially-Beneficial Services via Government Incentives, develops a dynamic continuous-time Markov chain model to evaluate the cost-effectiveness of different government subsidy policies. The study finds that downtime-rebate subsidies consistently outperform fee-for-service subsidies in cost-effectiveness when incentivizing service providers. It also highlights that while consumer-voucher policies are effective in addressing affordability, they suffer diminishing returns due to unresolved supply-side bottlenecks. The paper’s most notable contribution is the introduction of a mixed-subsidy policy that combines consumer vouchers with provider-based incentives, achieving cost reductions of up to 25% compared to single-subsidy strategies. This approach proves effective in simultaneously improving affordability and access to services, offering valuable guidance for policymakers designing cost-efficient subsidy programs. The second paper, titled Competition and Complementarity Between Online Healthcare Platforms and Offline Hospitals, investigates the dynamic interplay between online healthcare platforms and traditional offline hospitals, with a focus on low-to-middle-income countries. The study reveals that the entry of online healthcare platforms can complement offline hospitals under specific conditions, leading to a win-win scenario where overall treatment rates increase and offline hospitals experience greater demand for their services. However, it also identifies a potential challenge, as the presence of online platforms may reduce treatment affordability for patients with serious needs when offline hospitals face high capacity costs. To address this, the research recommends a combination of government regulations, such as price ceilings for offline hospitals and quality assurance mechanisms for online platforms. These measures can improve overall treatment rates and maintain affordability for patients with serious needs without imposing additional financial burdens on the government. Together, the findings from these two papers provide theoretical and practical insights for policymakers, service providers, and researchers. They underscore the importance of targeted subsidy policies and regulatory frameworks in ensuring equitable access to essential services while optimizing government expenditures. The project’s contributions have the potential to influence public policy in critical sectors, including healthcare, education, and other socially-beneficial services, fostering more efficient and equitable systems.

11502021.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11502021.value: This research opens several avenues for further development to address challenges in making essential services more accessible and affordable. One promising direction is to explore the application of mixed-subsidy policies in diverse service sectors, such as education, childcare, and eldercare, to test their effectiveness in different contexts. Additionally, further work can investigate how subsidies can be optimized when service providers operate in competitive markets, where multiple providers and platforms compete for government funding and customer demand. A key area for future research is the integration of advanced technologies, such as artificial intelligence and blockchain, to improve the transparency and efficiency of subsidy distribution. For instance, blockchain could help prevent fraud in provider-based subsidies like downtime rebates, while AI could optimize subsidy allocation based on real-time data about citizen demand and provider capacity. From a policy perspective, pilot programs should be designed to test the mixed-subsidy approach in real-world settings, such as healthcare or public transportation, to evaluate its practical benefits and refine the framework for broader implementation. Finally, future studies could focus on the long-term social and economic impacts of these policies, ensuring they promote equity and sustainability while remaining cost-effective for governments.

11502021.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11502021.value: This research project focuses on making essential services, like healthcare, more affordable and accessible for everyone, especially when costs are high, or waiting times are long. It explores how governments can use financial support, such as subsidies, to help both citizens and service providers. For example, one approach involves giving vouchers to citizens to reduce the cost of services, while another provides financial incentives to service providers to increase their capacity and reduce delays. The research shows that combining these two approaches—helping citizens afford services while also encouraging providers to increase supply—can save governments up to 25% in costs compared to using just one type of subsidy. This "mixed-subsidy" method not only improves affordability but also ensures services are readily available. Another part of the project looks at how online healthcare platforms, like telemedicine, interact with traditional hospitals. It finds that online platforms can complement hospitals by directing patients with serious needs to the right care, but careful regulation is needed to keep treatments affordable. Overall, this project provides practical strategies for governments to improve public access to essential services in a cost-effective way, helping create fairer systems that benefit both citizens and service providers.

11502221.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11502221.value: 大数据时代，企业通常收集消费者的种种数据，并利用这些数据区分老客户和新客户，给予他们不同的价格。例如，电商，保险公司和手机应用经常给新客户折扣。这种行为被称作消费者行为定价，并受到学术界和业界的关注。 在数据科技发展下，企业给消费者的价格通常是秘密的：无论是其他消费者还是竞争对手都看不到企业和消费者之间的价格。基于这种现象，我们计划研究价格不透明条件下的消费者行为定价。我们考虑一个竞争模型：两个企业在两个时间点向客户销售产品或服务。企业可以根据客户第一个时间点的行为为他们做第二个时间点的定价。不同于以往研究，我们假设这个价格是其他客户和其他企业所看不到的。 我们的研究将帮助学者更好的理解消费者行为定价，并帮助企业做更好的定价决策，以及政府做更好的监管数据和保护消费者。

11502221.label: Realisation of objectives
11502221.value: All objectives have been achieved. The details are as follows: 1. I developed a model of behavior-based pricing under price nontransparency, solved the model, and obtained closed-form solutions. I also solved a related model of behavior-based pricing without transparency. This objective has been successfully completed. 2. I demonstrated that price transparency benefits firms at the expense of consumers and overall social welfare. In particular, price transparency softens market competition and drives down equilibrium prices. This objective has been successfully completed. 3. I showed that classical results in behavior-based pricing do not hold when prices are non-transparent and established that firms may have incentives to make prices transparent under behavior-based pricing. Moreover, I find that behavior-based pricing does not necessarily soften first-period competition. This objective has been successfully completed. 4. Additionally, I analyzed the effects of price nontransparency in distribution-channel settings. I find that price nontransparency can benefit firms when consumers do not know the firm’s costs. This objective has been successfully completed.

11502221.label: Major findings and research outcome
11502221.value: The key finding of this study is that price transparency is detrimental to consumers. When firms can endogenously decide whether to make their prices transparent, they are likely to do so, which reduces market competition and benefits firms at the expense of consumers. Therefore, policymakers should take a strong stance against the sharing of price information between firms.

11502221.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11502221.value: Past research has intensively investigated the effects of behavior-based pricing. However, the existing literature generally assumes that prices are transparent, which may not be the case in practice. Future research could relax this assumption to examine whether the classical results still hold when prices are non-transparent.

11502221.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11502221.value: Behavior-based pricing refers to the practice of firms offering discriminatory prices to new and existing consumers. In the digital age, firms can make customized price offers to individual consumers that are not observable by rival firms or other consumers, resulting in non-transparent pricing. Additionally, firms can voluntarily share their price information. This research demonstrates that price transparency improves firm profits at the expense of consumers and social welfare, urging public policymakers to take a stronger stance against data sharing between firms. This research enhances our understanding of the effects of data sharing between firms and provides regulatory guidance for policymakers.

11502621.label: Project Objectives
11502621.value: We will study the theoretical properties of adaptive Lasso in structural vector autoregressive (SVAR) models with both stationary and nonstationary variables. In particular, we will derive the convergence rate and the bound for the selection error. We will check the validity of the data driven penalty terms so that adaptive Lasso can be applied in SVAR models without requiring the knowledge about which series are stationary or nonstationary. The project will consider the possibility to let p grow at various rates as T goes to infinity. The restricted eigenvalue condition will be studied under nonstationarity. We will extend our previous pointwise inference results to a uniform sense. We will investigate the conditions under which the inference is valid for the whole parameter space. Other possible extensions for the inferential theory will be also considered. Monte Carlo simulations will be conducted to check the finite-sample properties of the proposed methods. We will compare the proposed method with existing alternatives in terms of estimation accuracy (measured by root mean square estimation errors) to illustrate the advantage of the new method. Simulations will be run to check whether the coverage probabilities of the confidence intervals are close to the nominal levels for various points in the parameter space. Empirical applications will be conducted to show the gain from the proposed method applied to well-known economic data sets.

11502621.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11502621.value: Structural vector autoregressive (SVAR) models are widely applied to estimate impulse response functions (IRFs), which describe the dynamic impacts of an economic shock on a system of variables. In recent years, SVARs with external instrumental variables (SVAR-IV) have become more popular to uncover the unobserved effects of economic shocks. Existing theory for SVAR-IVs is usually developed under a crucial assumption called stationarity. However, practitioners often include highly persistent time series into SVARs, so the stationarity assumption is likely to be violated in many empirical applications. Motivated by the gap between the theory and common practice, this project mainly concerns two theoretical problems when we allow for possible nonstationarity in SVAR-IV models. First, we will consider how to select useful (lagged) variables in SVAR-IV models via a shrinkage method called adaptive Lasso. This method has selection consistency, that is, it is able to keep relevant variables and eliminate irrelevant variables under the assumption of stationarity. In nonstationary cases, its properties are less explored in the literature. We plan to extend the theory of adaptive Lasso to nonstationary SVARs and design data dependent penalty terms so that adaptive Lasso can achieve selection consistency without requiring the knowledge about which variables are nonstationary. Second, this project plans to develop a statistical inference method that is uniformly valid over the parameter space. Our previous study develops a pointwise approximation for inference. Pointwise results may perform poorly when parameters take certain values in the parameter space. In contrast, the uniformity means that the inferential theory works for all values in the parameter space. That is, uniformly valid inference methods will work well when parameters take the least favorable values. We plan to find the conditions under which our previous pointwise result can achieve uniformity. 結構向量自回歸 (SVAR) 模型被廣泛應用於脈衝回應函數 (IRFs) 的估計，描述經濟衝擊對變數系統的動態影響。近年來，具有外部工具變數的 SVAR (SVAR-IV) 的應用越加普遍，以揭示經濟中不可觀測的衝擊的影響。 SVAR-IV 的現有理論通常是在平穩性假設下發展起來的。然而，從業者通常將高度持久的時間序列包含在SVARs中，因此許多實證應用可能違反了平穩性假設。基於理論與實踐之間差距，在考慮到SVAR-IV 模型中可能的非平穩性的前提下，該項目主要涉及兩個理論問題。 首先，我們將考慮如何在 SVAR-IV 模型中，通過自我調整Lasso的收縮方法來選擇模型的有用（滯後）變數。該方法具有選擇一致性，即能夠在平穩性假設下保留相關變數，剔除不相關變數。在非平穩情況下，文獻中並沒有其性質的深入研究。我們計畫將自我調整Lasso理論擴展到非平穩 SVAR 中，並設計資料依賴的懲罰函數，以便自我調整Lasso可以實現選擇一致性，而不需要知道哪些變數是非平穩的。 第二，本項目計畫開發一種在參數空間上一致有效的統計推斷方法。我們之前的研究開發了一種逐點近似的方法用於統計推斷。當參數採用某些值時，逐點結果可能表現不佳。相比之下，一致性意味著推斷理論適用於參數空間中的所有值。也就是說，當參數取最不利的數值時，一致有效的推斷方法仍將工作得很好。我們計畫找到我們之前逐點結果可以達到一致性的條件。

Based on the two core papers, "Can news predict firm bankruptcy?" (Paper 1 published) and "News Sentiment and Trading Volume in Equity and Corporate Bond Markets" (Paper 2 under reivew), the research project has achieved several key objectives beyond the primary goal of forecasting bankruptcy: 1. Validation of LLMs for Cross-Asset Financial Analysis: The research successfully demonstrated that Large Language Models (LLMs)—specifically ChatGPT in Paper 1 and DeepSeek in Paper 2—can be effectively prompted to extract asset-specific sentiment (equity vs. bond) from the same news articles. This validates the use of LLMs as a versatile tool for generating nuanced, market-specific information, moving beyond a single, generic sentiment score. 2. Identification of News as a Determinant of Trading Volume: Paper 2 established a novel and economically significant link between LLM-extracted news sentiment intensity (the absolute value of the sentiment score) and subsequent trading volume in both equity and corporate bond markets. This fills a gap in the literature by demonstrating that public, text-based information is a powerful and incremental driver of trading activity. 3. Discovery of Asymmetric Cross-Market Volume Spillovers: The project achieved the objective of mapping information flow across markets. Paper 2 documented that bond-specific sentiment strongly predicts equity trading volume, whereas equity-specific sentiment has a much weaker and less stable effect on bond volume. This finding of asymmetric spillovers provides new evidence on the interconnectedness of these markets, suggesting that credit-related news is highly salient for equity investors. 4. Formalization of a Microstructure Mechanism (Camouflage–Depth): Paper 2 did not just document empirical findings but also developed a theoretical framework—a multi-asset Kyle-type model—to rationalize the results. This model introduced the "camouflage–depth mechanism," which explains how stronger news shocks increase liquidity trading, leading market makers to offer deeper quotes, which, in turn, encourages more aggressive informed trading, ultimately increasing total volume. 5. Demonstration of the Superiority of Full-Text Analysis: Both papers independently confirmed that extracting information from the full body text of news articles is significantly more informative and predictive than relying on headlines alone, establishing a best practice for future textual analysis in finance.

This model introduced the "camouflage–depth mechanism," which explains how stronger news shocks increase liquidity trading, leading market makers to offer deeper quotes, which, in turn, encourages more aggressive informed trading, ultimately increasing total volume. 5. Demonstration of the Superiority of Full-Text Analysis: Both papers independently confirmed that extracting information from the full body text of news articles is significantly more informative and predictive than relying on headlines alone, establishing a best practice for future textual analysis in finance.

11502721.label: Major findings and research outcome
11502721.value: The major finding of this research is the superior capability of Large Language Models (LLMs), specifically ChatGPT, in forecasting corporate bankruptcy. The study rigorously demonstrated that the news-based variables generated by ChatGPT significantly enhance the accuracy of predictions compared to established methods. Crucially, the LLM approach outperformed both traditional dictionary-based methods (such as the Loughran and McDonald dictionary) and specialized financial language models, like FinBERT, in terms of out-of-sample performance. For instance, incorporating ChatGPT-generated variables yielded a remarkable 77.78% improvement in out-of-sample pseudo $ R^2$ for one-month-ahead predictions, far surpassing the gains from the benchmark models. Furthermore, the analysis revealed that processing the full body of news articles yields substantially more predictive power than merely analyzing headlines. This highlights the LLM's ability to capture subtle, long-form context and nuanced information that is often missed by simpler methods that focus only on titles. This rich context is crucial for generating accurate and superior bankruptcy forecasts. The study also established that these news-based signals are not substitutes for existing data but are powerful complements. When incorporated into standard prediction models, the ChatGPT variables provided substantial incremental predictive power beyond traditional financial ratios and market variables, confirming that news sentiment captures unique, timely information about a firm’s credit risk that is not yet reflected in its delayed financial statements. The predictive strength of these timely news variables diminishes over longer forecast horizons, emphasizing their role as crucial short-term warning indicators. Beyond statistical accuracy, the research investigated the economic mechanisms, demonstrating that ChatGPT-derived sentiment effectively captures real-time macroeconomic conditions—such as market volatility (VIX), GDP growth, and recession probability—which are critical drivers of corporate default but are often reported with significant delays. The predictive power of the ChatGPT-derived signals was also translated into profitable investment strategies, where long-short portfolios based on predicted bankruptcy probability generated substantial positive alpha. The primary research outcome and dissemination goal were fully achieved. The project successfully produced an impactful academic paper that was accepted for publication in the Journal of Financial Markets, a leading finance journal. This achievement validates the methodology and ensures the findings are disseminated to the broader academic and professional community.

11502721.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11502721.value: The project’s successful validation of LLM-derived sentiment for both credit risk (Paper 1) and trading volume/liquidity (a follow-up paper) sets the stage for the final, crucial step: linking these signals directly to corporate bond pricing. The proposed course of action is to complete the grant’s original Objective 2. We will analyze how the DeepSeek-derived bond sentiment, which strongly predicts trading volume, influences the liquidity premium embedded in corporate bond yield spreads. This involves augmenting existing pricing models with our proven news-based liquidity and credit risk factors. Furthermore, we will conduct a detailed empirical investigation of the "camouflage–depth mechanism" proposed in the second paper by examining the impact of news sentiment on market microstructure variables such as bid-ask spreads and market depth. This will provide a complete picture of information flow from news to trading activity and, ultimately, to bond valuation.

11502721.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11502721.value: This research utilizes powerful AI, such as ChatGPT, to predict when a company is likely to experience financial distress or bankruptcy. The Nature of the Research: The core idea is to solve the problem of outdated information. Currently, we rely on a company’s quarterly financial reports, which are often months old. Our AI tackles this by reading and understanding millions of daily business news articles in real-time. It doesn't just count keywords; it comprehends the full context of the text. Significance and Value: We found that the AI's analysis is much more accurate and faster at spotting a company's financial trouble than any traditional method. This real-time, AI-driven insight acts as a superior early warning system. For investors, it means avoiding sudden losses. For banks, it allows them to manage lending risk more effectively. For regulators, it provides a faster, more accurate "crystal ball" for monitoring the health of the entire financial system. Essentially, we’ve created a modern, powerful tool for managing corporate risk.

11503121.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11503121.value: 2002 年，美国公众公司会计监督委员会(PCAOB) 成立，以监督为美国上市公司提供审计服务的美国和外国会计师。先前的研究发现，对外国审计师的审查提高了其在美国上市客户的审计质量（Lamoreaux，2016；Krishnan 等，2017），而且这种积极影响外溢到非美国上市客户的审计质量（Fung 等，2017）。先前的研究进一步证明，PCAOB审查的积极影响扩展到全球审计和资本市场，这体现在被审查的外国审计师的市场份额不断增加（Aobdia 和 Shroff，2017 年）、被审查审计师的非美国上市客户的资本支出增加（Shroff，2019 年），以及提高了全球并购的交易质量（Kim 等，2020 年）。然而，关于PCAOB在产品市场中的作用的证据很少。因此，本研究试图调查 PCAOB 国际监管对非美国上市客户与其供应商之间贸易信贷的影响。 贸易信贷是非正规融资的必要渠道。 WTO 的报告（2018 年）显示，80% 的国际贸易由贸易信贷支持。我预测 PCAOB 国际监管会对贸易信用产生积极影响，原因如下。首先，之前的研究表明，财务报告有助于融资提供者评估贷款风险（Hui 等，2012；Penman，2013；García-Teruel 等，2014）。此外，供应商依赖信用评级机构进行信用风险评估（Love, 2015; Cassar 等, 2015; Sutherland, 2018），而这些机构会依据公司的财务信息进行评估（Kim 等, 2013; Ayers 等, 2010 年；Florou 等，2017 年）。最近的研究（Lamoreax，2016 年；Krishnan 等，2017 年；Fung 等，2017 年）表明 PCAOB 审查提高了财务报告质量，从而有助于供应商评估公司的信用风险。其次，最近的研究表明，PCAOB 审查减少了公司与各种利益相关者之间的信息不对称（Shroff，2019 年；Kim 等，2020 年；Lamoreaux 等，2020 年）。改善的企业信息环境有助于供应商监控企业的投资和经营决策，从而提高供应商向企业提供贸易信贷的意愿。第三，作为公共审计监管机构，PCAOB 可以通过证明审计过程符合审计标准来提升审计价值（Coates，2007）。一些研究发现，PCAOB 审查增强了投资者对审计工作的信心，增加了投资者对财务报告可靠性和可信度的评估（Aobdia 和 Shroff，2017；Krishnan 等，2017；Gipper 等，2020），因此增强供应商对企业财务报表的信任。

11503121.label: Major findings and research outcome
11503121.value: This paper demonstrates that enhanced auditing standards, driven by the oversight of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (PCAOB) on non-U.S. auditors, enable global exporting firms to improve their operations and engage more effectively in global value chains (GVCs). Analyzing a dataset of U.S. waterway imports from suppliers across 36 countries, we find that PCAOB international inspections significantly increase exports to U.S. buyers, especially for intermediate and capital goods. Furthermore, exporters enhance their product complexity, reflecting improved information quality and reduced informational frictions with downstream importers. Notably, the positive impacts of PCAOB inspections are more pronounced for exporters facing greater informational challenges—specifically, those with initially lower reporting quality, smaller market shares, or located in countries with weaker institutions or higher geopolitical risks relative to the U.S. Additionally, we observe that PCAOB inspections extend the duration of supply chain relationships and encourage relationship-specific investments by suppliers. Importantly, U.S. importers with a higher proportion of suppliers audited by PCAOB-inspected auditors show improved financial performance. Overall, our findings indicate that audit oversight plays a crucial role in facilitating the formation, upgrading, and success of GVCs.

11503121.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11503121.value: Based on the data collected, variable constructed, and the main findings obtains from this paper, there are some potential research areas worth of further exploration, such as (1) How PCAOB inspections on auditors of global exporting firms affect the importing activities from non-U.S. corporate buyers? (2) How PCAOB inspections on auditors of global exporting firms affect the buying decisions from foreign governments (foreign government procurement)? (3) How do consumers perceive the quality of product from exporters whose auditors are subject to PCAOB oversight, and does this perception impact purchasing decisions?

11503121.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11503121.value: This study explores how improved auditing standards, enforced by the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (PCAOB), help companies perform better in international markets. By analyzing data on U.S. imports from 36 countries, we found that PCAOB inspections lead to an increase in exports to the U.S. These inspections also encourage companies to make more complex and higher-quality products. Our findings suggest that better audits improve the quality of information shared between exporters and U.S. buyers, reducing misunderstandings. This effect is particularly strong for exporters who initially struggle with lower-quality reporting or come from countries with weaker institutions. Additionally, PCAOB inspections strengthen long-term relationships between suppliers and buyers, leading to more investment in these partnerships. Finally, U.S. companies that rely on suppliers audited by PCAOB-inspected firms tend to see better financial results. Overall, our research indicates that effective audit oversight plays a crucial role in helping companies improve, compete, and succeed in global markets. This study highlights how high-quality financial reporting improves participation in global value chains and shows the economic benefits of audit oversight. We suggest that allowing PCAOB inspections can help exporters to the U.S. by enhancing their credibility with U.S. buyers, benefiting both regulators and exporting countries.

11503321.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11503321.value: 人力資源投資對研發的長期影響：以醫藥行業為例

11503321.label: Project Objectives
11503321.value: We assess whether skilled labor shortages impede drug clinical trial success rates by employing two natural experiments: one based on random H-1B visa lotteries and the other based on a policy shock to the supply of high-skilled foreign labor. A drug must transition successfully through several phases of clinical trials to receive regulatory approval. Furthermore, sufficient human capital is required to evaluate drug market potential and/or to design, execute, and analyze subsequent drug trials. We hypothesize that skilled foreign labor shortages reduce the likelihood of successful phase transitioning. Our rationale for this stems from our premise that a pharmaceutical company's eagerness to commit further investments in new drug development is negatively influenced by its existing workers' deficiency of required skills (i.e., skills gap). Identifying a skilled labor channel in drug attrition rates contributes to the academic literature by establishing, for the first time to our knowledge, a causal relationship between skilled labor supply and the performance of long-term R&D. This is also valuable for managers in the pharmaceutical industry who are looking for ways to improve drug development success rates. We assess whether skilled labor shortages undermine novel drug discovery using the aforementioned two natural experiments. For each pair of drugs in a pharmaceutical company's development pipeline and portfolio, we calculate the Tanimoto coefficient, which is the most popular similarity measure of chemical structures used in chemoinformatics. Newly discovered drugs are considered more novel if they are less similar than those in a pharmaceutical company's drug portfolio. We hypothesize that shortages of skilled foreign labor reduce future drug novelty due to a larger skills gap. Identifying a skilled labor channel in drug novelty contributes to the academic literature by highlighting the importance of human capital in breakthrough innovation. This is valuable knowledge for managers in the pharmaceutical industry as it pertains to investment strategies that may lead to the discovery of blockbuster drugs. We assess whether skilled labor shortages reduce the breadth of diseases that pharmaceutical companies seek to treat, as implied by their drug development pipeline and portfolio, using the aforementioned two natural experiments. Treating different diseases or medical conditions require a broad range of expertise, which could be expanded through hiring a diversity of skilled workers. We hypothesize that shortages of skilled foreign labor inhibit such knowledge expansions in treating various diseases and medical conditions. To conduct this analysis, we categorize drugs according to two classification systems: (1) the Anatomical Therapeutic Chemical Classification System and (2) the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems. The former is based on the chemical structure of the drug and the latter is based on information provided in Investigational New Drug filings (FDA). Identifying a skilled labor channel in product diversity contributes to the academic literature by documenting the role of human capital in exploratory and exploitative (e.g., repurposing existing drugs) innovation. We assess whether skilled labor shortages cause pharmaceutical companies to adopt technologies in automation and digitization using the aforementioned natural experiments. Adopting these technologies can serve as an alternative investment strategy to compensate for the worker skills gap. We hypothesize that instead of pursuing workers specialized in scientific fields related clinical research, pharmaceutical companies may seek workers specialized in information technology, big data analytics, and artificial intelligence. The latter set of workers could complement existing clinical researchers in providing tools to enhance molecular modeling, simulations, or screening methods, for example. We measure the intention to adopt technologies in automation and digitization through the number job postings by pharmaceutical companies that require these skills. Identifying a skilled labor channel in technology adoption contributes to the academic literature by showing how automation, artificial intelligence, and other digital technologies complement and/or substitute for skilled workers. This is valuable to policymakers currently evaluating the causes and consequences of automation. We evaluate how drug quality is impacted by unmet skilled labor demand aggregated across years, as measured by patient ratings obtained by scraping online pharmaceutical review sites. We quantify overall patient satisfaction via patient drug ratings. We hypothesize that, in the long run, satisfying skilled labor demand leads to the fruition of more approved effective drugs with fewer adverse drug reactions. Identifying a skilled labor channel in drug quality contributes to the academic literature by documenting the product market impact of human capital investments. This analysis is valuable to policymakers interested in improving consumer welfare through the development of superior drugs. We intend to verify that satisfying skilled labor demand has a stronger positive impact on pharmaceutical firms that are financially constrained than those that are not. This analysis contributes to the academic literature on investment-cash flow sensitivity. This is also valuable for policymakers in gauging the financing frictions faced by pharmaceutical companies and informing them on possible solutions based on human capital investments. We write papers publishable in top tier finance journals.

11503321.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11503321.value: The negative economic effects of the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic have increased and thus highlighted the challenges of world-wide pharmaceutical drug development. Since 2008, institutional investments in the pharmaceutical sector have declined, stagnating the growth of long-term R&D expenditures globally. Recent studies point to costly external financing for the paucity of breakthrough drugs but fall short in identifying potential investment channels through which financing can facilitate novel drug discovery. Our project serves to fill this gap by exploring the human capital channel and determining whether investments in skilled labor are critical in the success of drug development for pharmaceutical companies. Long-term R&D is a risky endeavor as it often involves multiple stages of investments that not only span several years, but also have a high chance of failure. Corporate investments in long-term R&D typically necessitate the selective hiring and intensive training of high-skilled workers. Understanding how the employment of high-skilled workers affect the performance of long-term R&D informs policymakers of whether human capital investments are effective in creating breakthrough innovation. Drug development is a natural environment to study the performance of long-term R&D as the progress of each drug is observed through its clinical trial phase transitions, which in totality, may last over a decade before the drug reaches market. Unlike other studies which use firm investment aggregate data gathered from public financial statements, our study uses drug development data which allows us to look inside a "black box" of firm decision making at the product level. We seek to determine whether human capital investments play a role in (1) novel drug discovery, which we measure based on drug chemical structure similarity to other drugs in a firm's development pipeline, and (2) reducing drug attrition rates within clinical trials. We conduct two natural experiments: one based on random lotteries that the United States Citizenship and Immigration Services uses to allocate H-1B visas and the other based on a policy shock to the overall supply of skilled foreign labor through the H-1B program in our assessment process. We estimate the impact of shortages in high-skilled foreign labor (e.g., statisticians, biochemists, engineers, scientists, physicians, etc.) on drug development for U.S. pharmaceutical companies. 11503321.label: Realisation of objectives
11503321.value: We have successfully achieved the core research objectives of this project—specifically objectives 1 through 6. These objectives centered on examining how skilled foreign labor shortages affect various aspects of pharmaceutical innovation, using two quasi-experimental settings: the randomized H-1B visa lottery and an exogenous policy shock to visa supply. For objectives 1, 2, and 3, we analyzed whether skilled labor constraints influenced the likelihood of clinical trial progression, the novelty of drugs (measured by chemical similarity via the Tanimoto coefficient), and the breadth of diseases targeted in a firm's development portfolio. Our results support the hypothesis that skilled labor supply plays a critical role in the success and exploratory scope of long-term pharmaceutical R&D. For objective 4, we assessed whether firms responded to skilled labor shocks by shifting toward increased investment in automation and digital technologies. Specifically, we measured changes in job postings that emphasized skills related to information technology, data analytics, and artificial intelligence. In objective 5, we turned to the quality of drug outcomes. By scraping and analyzing patient drug reviews from WebMD, we assessed whether firms experiencing labor shortages produced drugs with lower patient satisfaction and more adverse side effects. This allowed us to quantify the downstream consumer welfare implications of skilled labor supply. For objective 6, we studied financial constraints as a moderating factor and found that the benefits of satisfying skilled labor demand were particularly pronounced for firms facing greater internal financing frictions—underscoring the interaction between human capital and capital constraints in driving innovation outcomes. However, objective 7—publishing in a top-tier finance journal—remains in progress. Our initial manuscript, while methodologically rigorous and empirically rich, was not well received by editors and reviewers at leading finance journals. Feedback consistently suggested that the topic, though important, was more closely aligned with innovation strategy and management than core finance. In response, we are actively revising and repositioning the manuscript for submission to top-tier strategy and management journals, where the paper’s focus on skilled labor, innovation pipelines, and strategic investment decisions is more likely to resonate. It is worth noting that progress on the project was delayed due to the unforeseen impact of the COVID-19 pandemic. In particular, we faced significant difficulties in recruiting and retaining qualified doctoral-level research assistants. This staffing shortage hindered timely progress in data collection, preprocessing, and coding—especially for web scraping, constructing firm-level innovation metrics, and implementing high-dimensional econometric analyses. While we ultimately overcame these challenges, the initial setbacks contributed to slower-than-expected progress, especially on manuscript preparation and submission. Nonetheless, the project has now generated a robust set of findings that meaningfully advance our understanding of how skilled labor shortages impact R&D productivity, innovation quality, and strategic firm behavior. With additional time to complete the repositioning and submission process, we are confident the work will result in impactful academic publications and offer valuable insights for both scholars and policymakers.

Treating different diseases or medical conditions require a broad range of expertise, which could be expanded through hiring a diversity of skilled workers. 11503321.label: Major findings and research outcome
11503321.value: This project provides compelling causal evidence that access to high-skilled foreign labor is a key driver of pharmaceutical innovation and, by extension, long-term public health outcomes. Leveraging two quasi-experimental research designs—a randomized H-1B visa lottery and an abrupt policy-induced reduction in visa availability in 2003—we examined how skilled immigration affects the pace and scope of drug development in the U.S. pharmaceutical industry. Our findings reveal that pharmaceutical companies with higher H-1B visa allotments exhibit significantly faster drug pipeline progression. These firms generate more patents for new drug compounds, file more drug applications targeting a broader range of diseases, and initiate more early-stage clinical trials (Phases 1 and 2). In contrast, firms heavily reliant on H-1B workers experienced a notable slowdown in drug development after the 2003 cap reduction. These firms pursued fewer new drug trials and showed diminished efforts in exploring treatments across a diverse set of medical conditions. These patterns indicate that high-skilled foreign professionals play a critical and non-substitutable role in enabling scientific progress within pharmaceutical firms. They support functions ranging from molecular modeling and trial design to data analysis and regulatory strategy. Restrictions on such talent not only hinder firm-level innovation but may also delay the development of life-saving or life-enhancing therapies. The policy implications are clear: immigration rules governing high-skilled labor can have unintended but significant consequences for national innovation capacity and health system advancement. Limiting access to global talent risks weakening the research infrastructure of one of the most R&D-intensive industries, with downstream effects on patient outcomes, drug availability, and international competitiveness. Our research contributes to a growing body of evidence that immigration policy must be understood not just through the lens of labor market balance, but also as a tool to support science, innovation, and consumer welfare. Crafting policy that ensures timely and adequate access to high-skilled talent—while preserving fair labor standards and national interests—is essential to fostering a robust and responsive pharmaceutical sector capable of addressing future health challenges.

11503321.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11503321.value: The findings from this project open multiple avenues for further development. In particular, the causal relationship we establish between skilled labor supply and pharmaceutical innovation invites deeper investigation into the mechanisms through which human capital drives firm strategy and long-term R&D performance. Future research can expand this framework by exploring cross-country comparisons, assessing how different immigration regimes shape national innovation outcomes in the life sciences. We also see strong potential to explore how firms adapt to skilled labor shortages through strategic shifts—such as increased investment in automation, outsourcing of R&D, or pivoting toward therapeutic areas with lower complexity. These behavioral responses merit further study, particularly in the context of digital transformation in healthcare. In the short term, our primary course of action is to repackage the main manuscript to align with the editorial focus of leading journals in strategy, management, and innovation. We are also exploring a companion paper emphasizing the public health and policy implications for publication in interdisciplinary outlets. With additional time and research assistance, we aim to produce high-impact publications that reach both academic and policy audiences, reinforcing the broader importance of human capital investments for science and society.

11503321.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11503321.value: This project explores how shortages of highly skilled workers—especially foreign scientists and engineers—affect the ability of pharmaceutical companies to develop new medicines. To study this, we used two real-world events: a visa lottery system that randomly allows some companies to hire foreign talent, and a major government policy in 2003 that suddenly reduced the number of skilled foreign workers allowed into the U.S. We found that companies with better access to skilled foreign workers were more successful in moving new drugs through clinical trials, discovering more innovative treatments, and developing drugs for a wider range of diseases. These findings matter because drug development is a long, costly, and uncertain process. Having the right talent in place makes it more likely that life-saving treatments will reach patients. Our research shows that policies affecting immigration don’t just influence jobs—they also impact scientific progress, public health, and patient well-being. This work helps policymakers understand how important it is to align immigration, labor, and innovation strategies to support medical advancement and global competitiveness.

11503421.label: Project Objectives
11503421.value: Replace the butterfly strategy with new and more rigorous analysis that will extrapolate from the volatility surface to calculate the daily price of the so-called “digital option”. This is a feasible but computationally intensive approach. The immediate result will be a new cross-sectional strategy. Develop a new measure, which I call BIRM, to determine the expected market return during a crash, which can be used for market timing. 11503421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11503421.value: 資產定價研究的聖杯是預測未來回報。在此項目中，我使用期權數據來推斷在市場崩盤狀態下單個股票的回報預期。例如，考慮蝴蝶策略：只有當股價跌入特定範圍時，蝴蝶策略才會獲得回報。當然，當投資者認為這個範圍更有可能時，溢價就會增加。另一方面，被稱為“恐懼指數”的 VIX 隨著市場崩盤的可能性增加而增加。對於每隻標準普爾 500 指數股票，我計算了 VIX 與不同行使價的蝶式溢價之間的相關性。與 VIX 聯動最積極的蝴蝶揭示了該股票在未來市場崩盤中的回報預期。我稱這種回報為蝴蝶隱含回報 (BIR)。我通過做空 BIR 低的脆弱股票並做空 BIR 高的有彈性的股票來構建一個新策略。在 1996 年至 2019 年的樣本期間，相對於各種因子模型，它獲得了統計上顯著的 alpha，範圍為每月 0.25% 至 0.36%。在 BIR 的基礎上，我構建了一個稱為市場蝴蝶隱含回報 (BIRM) 的價值加權平均值，它可以解釋 SVIX的26% 到 40% 的變化。在此項目中，首要任務是通過使用數字期權而不是蝴蝶期權來改進現有策略。這一步是可行的，但計算量很大。它將對個股的回報預期產生更清晰的衡量，然後可以將其匯總為投資者對崩盤期間市場回報預期的衡量。因此，擬議的項目將有助於有關總體可預測性的文獻和有關橫截面股票收益的文獻。

11503421.value: Interestingly, the work has practical applications beyond academia. HKAIFT, a lab funded by ITC, is collaborating with the MPFA to develop a passive, low-cost downside risk management system. The project focuses on identifying stocks that are resilient during market crashes. Leveraging the algorithm from this research, HKAIFT created and plans to publicly release the HKAIFT SafeSelect Index, which consists of the top 80% of stocks most likely to withstand a market downturn. MPF schemes can choose to track this index directly or use the accompanying 'risky list'—the bottom 20% of stocks—to exclude high-risk stocks from their portfolios. This dual approach provides MPF operators a practical method to optimize their investment strategies without incurring excessive costs or breaching regulatory requirements.

11503421.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11503421.value: This research helps investors and retirement fund managers minimize losses during market crashes. By analyzing extensive options data, the project’s main achievement is an algorithm that identifies stocks likely to perform well in severe downturns. Its value is twofold. First, it makes downside risk management more accessible and affordable, as fund managers can simply select safer stocks or remove riskier ones without resorting to complex or costly trading strategies. Second, it has tangible real-world impact: MPF operators can use it to optimize retirement funds and better protect individuals’ savings in turbulent markets. Ultimately, this project offers a practical, cost-effective way to bolster long-term financial security, demonstrating that advanced financial research can directly benefit both professional and individual investors.
