11509521.label: Major findings and research outcome
11509521.value: Motivated by the sales operation e-commerce platforms such as Amazon, this project makes original theoretical contributions to the operations management literature by developing a unified framework that integrates demand learning, advertising selection, and dynamic pricing under uncertainty. Departing from existing studies that treat these decisions in isolation, the project formulates the joint click-through and sell-through problem as a two-stage dynamic and stochastic optimization model, thereby capturing the endogenous interaction between advertising exposure, demand realization, and pricing decisions over time. This modeling approach is novel in explicitly linking upstream learning from advertising with downstream pricing control in a single analytical structure. A key theoretical contribution is the development of a Thompson-sampling-type learning algorithm tailored to this two-stage decision environment. Unlike standard bandit formulations, the proposed algorithm allows demand information learned from advertising performance to cascade into pricing decisions, generating a coupled learning–control process. The research establishes structural properties of the optimal policies, including monotonicity and neighborhood convergence, which provide rigorous characterization of how optimal decisions evolve as demand uncertainty is resolved. These results extend the theory of learning-based stochastic control by accommodating multi-dimensional state variables and interdependent decisions. The project further derives an optimal pricing strategy that adjusts sell-through rates to meet targeted sales objectives while accounting for heterogeneous customer responses. The analytical results characterize the functional form of optimal discounts as a function of updated demand beliefs, offering new theoretical insights into the relationship between learning speed, price adjustment, and revenue outcomes. This contributes to the pricing literature by moving beyond static or myopic discounting rules toward dynamically optimal, learning-aware policies. All theoretical findings are validated through extensive computer simulations, which confirm convergence properties and demonstrate consistent performance improvements relative to benchmark heuristics. Overall, the project advances the theoretical foundations of adaptive decision-making in digital retail and platform operations, providing novel models and analytical tools that can support future research on learning-driven operational strategies. Major outcomes of this project have been consolidated into a manuscript submitted to Production and Operations Management. Following three rounds of major revision and one minor revision, the paper has been resubmitted, and the review process is approaching completion.

11509521.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11509521.value: The theoretical framework developed in this project provides a solid basis for further, incremental extensions within the domain of learning-based operations management. One natural direction is to extend the current two-stage model to settings involving a larger number of products or longer planning horizons, which would allow examination of interaction effects while preserving the core analytical structure. In addition, the proposed learning and pricing framework can be adapted to consider more general demand environments, such as gradual demand shifts or limited competitive interactions, in order to assess the robustness of the theoretical insights derived in this study. These extensions would build directly on the existing results without requiring fundamental changes to the modeling approach. Finally, future research may explore the use of empirical data or numerical calibration to further illustrate the practical relevance of the proposed policies. Overall, the project establishes a well-defined theoretical foundation that can support continued investigation of adaptive decision-making under demand uncertainty in digital retail and platform-based operations.

11509521.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11509521.value: Online shopping platforms such as Amazon need to decide which products to promote and how to price them, even though customer preferences are uncertain and change over time. This project successfully developed a new way to help online retailers make better advertising and pricing decisions by learning from sales data as it becomes available. The main achievement of this research is the creation of a unified decision framework that links advertising choices, customer demand, and pricing decisions into a single learning process. The study also developed learning-based methods that allow decisions to improve gradually as more information is collected. Computer simulations show that these methods can consistently outperform commonly used approaches, leading to better sales outcomes and more effective use of promotional resources. Looking ahead, the results of this project have strong potential for future application. The proposed methods can be extended to settings with more products, longer planning periods, or changing market conditions. They can also be adapted to real-world data from online platforms to support data-driven decision-making. Overall, this research provides a practical foundation for improving how online retailers learn from customers and adjust their strategies over time, benefiting both businesses and consumers.

11600921.value: 項目標題： 倒退如何影響反擊？對比菲律賓與泰國的反獨裁化運動

11600921.label: Co - Investigator(s)
11600921.value: Prof Cheng, Edmund Dr Prajak, Kongkirati

11600921.label: Project Objectives
11600921.value: Connect the literature on autocratization – particularly about “executive aggrandizement” and “promissory coups” which both make claims to continued democratic legitimacy - to the emergent study of “pushback” against “backsliding,” i.e. opposition against autocratizing regimes. Conduct the first systematic paired comparison of the early phase of opposition in two recent and divergent backsliding cases in Southeast Asia – “executive aggrandizement” in the Philippines and a “promissory” military coup in Thailand – which allows a detailed and contextualized analysis of each case that large-N quantitative studies cannot capture while also producing potentially generalizable findings that go beyond what a single country study can yield. Assess an institutional explanation that explains pushback in terms of residual electoral, state institutional, and civil societal forms of democratic accountability despite autocratization by examining Philippine and Thai backsliding in detail: the relative (un)fairness of elections, the degree to which state institutions are manipulated and the extent of restrictions put on civil society. Demonstrate this institutional explanation does not adequately elucidate significant variations in pushback between the two cases as there appears to have been considerably more pushback in Thailand than in the Philippines despite more electoral bias, more overt control of state institutions as well as greater generalized repression of and restrictions imposed upon civil society in the former than in the latter country. Conduct detailed analysis of the 2019 midterm elections in the Philippines and parliamentary elections in Thailand, undertake protest event analysis (PEA) of major opposition demonstrations in both countries, and do social media analysis that examines the relative strength and particular character of the opposition activism. Develop an alternative explanation of why opposition has been stronger in Thailand despite greater generalized repression and institutional manipulation than in the Philippines by examining how the outcomes of “framing battles” over democratic legitimation claims by these regimes and opposition criticism of them have affected variations in pushback.

11600921.value: The autocratization literature has emphasized types and mechanisms of democratic “backsliding,” with some recent research focusing on resistance to this threat. Despite increasing interest in opposition, there has been little analysis of how different kinds of backsliding affect the extent of pushback, a research lacuna this project addresses. Specifically, the project asks why there been more pushback in elections and through protests against Thailand’s military-monarchical regime than by those opposing an aggrandizing president in the Philippines. An institutional explanation which accounts for pushback based on the degree of residual electoral, state institutional, and civil societal forms of democratic accountability despite autocratization does not explain the variation between these two countries because there has been more opposition in Thailand despite greater generalized repression and institutional manipulation there than in the Philippines. An alternative explanation is thus sought which explores how pushback is shaped by “framing battles” over regimes’ democratic legitimacy claims despite autocratizing. Thailand’s military-monarchical rulers’ have had limited success in portraying recent elections as restoring democracy, with legitimacy linked to the monarchy also eroding. This has catalyzed the formation of a broad civilian alliance which it is hypothesized has bridged a major class/regional cleavage by framing opposition as a struggle to restore democracy. By contrast, oppositionists in the Philippines, confronting an illiberal but popular president claiming democratic legitimacy, have largely been confined to a human rights frame with limited mobilization against the regime. The project thus aims to make an important contribution to an emergent “pushback” literature by offering the first paired comparison of opposition in these two Southeast Asian backsliding cases - “executive aggrandizement” in the Philippines (since 2016) and a “promissory” military coup in Thailand (in 2014). These country cases are appropriate because, despite important differences, they followed parallel political paths until autocratizing in distinct ways. Paired comparison allows for more detailed and contextualized analysis than large-N quantitative studies can capture while also producing potentially generalizable findings that go beyond what a single country case can yield. The PI, who has published extensively on Philippine politics, will work together with a Thai politics expert (co-I Dr. Prajak Kongkirati, Thammasat University) and a scholar with a track record of using quantitative methods to research contentious politics (co-I Dr. Edmund Cheng, City University of Hong Kong) employing mixed methods to study similarities and differences between these cases in terms of autocratization, election results, protest events, social media activism, and framing. 項目標題： 倒退如何影響反擊？對比菲律賓與泰國的反獨裁化運動 項目摘要： 現有研究獨裁化的文獻重點關注民主「倒退」的類型與機制，而近期的若干研究則側重於對此等威脅的抵抗。儘管對反對行動的關注在增加，卻幾乎沒有關於不同類型的倒退如何影響反擊的程度的分析，此乃本項目旨在解決的一個研究空白。具體而言，本項目提出這麼一個問題：為何泰國在選舉及抗議中對軍政府-君主制政權的反擊，比菲律賓反對總統擴權的人更多？ 嘗試從制度去解釋反擊取決於民主問責程度（儘管仍存在專制），包括剩餘投票、國家機構及公民社會等形式，仍無法解釋這兩個國家之間的差異，因為儘管泰國的廣泛鎮壓及制度操縱比菲律賓更甚，其出現的反對力量卻亦更多。 由此尋求另一種解釋 —— 探討在獨裁下仍圍繞政權民主合法性主張的「框架之爭」是如何形成反擊的。泰國的軍政府-君主制政權統治者試圖將近期的選舉描繪為恢復民主，但成果有限，而其君主制合法性亦受到削弱。這對形成廣泛的民間聯盟起到了催化作用，據推測，民間聯盟透過將反對行動框飾為恢復民主的鬥爭來彌合主要階級/地區之間的分歧。相較之下，面對著一位聲稱具有民主合法性、屬非自由派卻廣受歡迎的總統，菲律賓的反對派在很大程度上被局限在人權框架內，反對政權的動員有限。 因此本項目旨在透過對這兩個東南亞倒退案例 —— 菲律賓自 2016 年以來的「行政擴權」與泰國 2014 年「可預期的」軍事政變 —— 兩者當中的反對派進行首次比對，為新興的「反擊」主題文獻作出重要貢獻。此等國家案例是合適的，因為儘管兩國存在重大差異，均曾遵循平行的政治路徑，直至以不同的方式走向獨裁。相較於案例數量繁多的量性研究，配對比較可實現更詳細、更場景化的分析，同時亦能產生超越單個國家案例所能產生的具備推廣應用潛質的結果。 曾就菲律賓政局廣泛發表文章的項目首席研究者將與合作研究者包括泰國政治專家、泰國國立法政大學普拉賈克·孔吉拉提（Prajak Kongkirati）博士，以及曾致力於使用量性方法研究抗爭政治的香港城市大學鄭煒（Edmund Cheng）博士合作，採用混合方法研究此等案例在獨裁化、選舉結果、抗議事件、社交媒體行動主義以及框架方面的異同。

11602121.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11602121.value: The Festival d’Avignon, established in 1947, is one of the largest and most famous performing arts events in the world. Every year, plays are performed in, and translated from, many different languages. With this in mind, one might expect there to be research on translation at this event. However, this is not the case. The absence of such scholarship stands in stark contrast to the number of studies devoted to directors and playwrights who have produced work at the festival. This gap in the literature suggests that the contribution of translators to the creative process of developing a show for live performance goes unrecognised, particularly at this event. This lack of recognition is precisely what the project wishes to investigate, by studying translation at the Festival d’Avignon from the perspective of its (in)visibility. The project will survey the productions that have been staged at the festival from its inception to the present. It will determine which plays have been staged in translation and explore how translators have been credited. It will highlight instances in which plays have been translated using audio-visual means, and investigate any differences in how such practices are recognised in comparison with other forms of translation. By studying online and physical archives, the project will examine how the festival records and documents translation practices. It will also investigate the translator’s involvement in the creative process of developing shows for performance at the festival. It will consider whether translators’ presence in rehearsals has an effect on how they are credited in production materials. In doing so, the project will ask how the role of the translator fits into discussions about the authority of directors and playwrights, a key topic of research on European and global theatre. To achieve its aims, the project will use a combination of methods. The research team will use archival materials available both online and onsite in Avignon to classify productions staged at the festival from its inception to the present. The PI will also conduct semi-structured interviews with festival organisers and representatives of theatre companies performing there to document and appraise the creative processes involved, with a specific focus on the role of translators. The PI will use the findings of this case study to shed light on the (in)visibility of theatre translators more generally, and as a springboard to reflect on ways in which translators can be appropriately credited for their contributions. 11603521.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11603521.value: 國際研究表明，許多以英語為第二語言 (ESL) 的學生並沒有從他們英語的課堂提供的英語接觸中完全受益，部分原因是他們的英語熟練程度較低。在香港，雖然部分 ESL 學生通過了英語門檻水平並被英語作為授課語言（EMI）初中中學錄取，但他們在用英語作第二語言寫作科學抽象概念時仍面臨嚴峻挑戰。特別是 ESL 理科學生因其寫作能力有限而受到批評，這是科學領域知識傳播的主要手段。這些學生在達到國際科學成就標準的潛力與用英語交流科學知識的能力薄弱之間存在差距。這種差距對於在以中文作為授課語言小學學習並在中學轉為 英語授課 的 ESL 理科學生來說尤為明顯。 擬議的為期 3 年的項目將探索這些學生的科學寫作能力，並通過比較年級和 EMI中學類型來確定他們的 EMI 經驗程度是否對他們的科學寫作發展產生積極影響。為了獲得多方面的證據，該項目將有以下目標。 1) 評估理科學生的一般科學報告寫作能力和語言技能 2) 探索學生科學寫作的話語特徵。 3) 確定科學教師使用的教學工具和教學方法。 4) 了解教師對EMI教學的看法。至少招收240名初中生。將採用為期 1 年的縱向自然探索方法。每個學生參與者將被邀請在他們的初中學習一年後就同一主題製作一份科學報告。生成的報告將由訓練有素的標記進行標記，以評估文本的組織和有效科學寫作的詞彙語法特徵的使用（例如，分解密集信息、邏輯連接想法、跟踪參與者和主題）。此外，參與科學教師的教學活動將使用自然課堂觀察進行分析。教師對EMI教學的看法也將在訪談中探討。該項目將概述 EMI 經驗對香港背景下初中學生科學寫作的影響，並得出 1) ESL 科學學生寫作能力的概況，以及 2) 對科學教學的一系列影響在 EMI 初中環境。

11604121.label: Project Objectives
11604121.value: Identify various impacts that overseas work has had on migrant domestic workers’ home connection and relations, and their changing perceptions of self-family relationships. Examine factors affecting migrant domestic workers' life plans and the length of time they will stay overseas. Offer modalities of good practices among migrant domestic workers that enhance better life plans. Develop a new conceptual framework, “the precarity-transnationality” nexus, to make holistic analysis of the impacts that migration and overseas work have on foreign domestic helpers at different life stages and their different vulnerabilities. Make policy suggestions to reduce the precarities that foreign domestic helpers are facing. Publish journal papers and a book to fill the gap of knowledge in the existing migration literature and arouse new intellectual debates on labour and migration governance.

11604121.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11604121.value: 此項研究主要對象是香港的外籍傭工。香港自七十年代開始輸入海外傭工，大部份來東南亞國家如菲律賓、印尼、泰國等，近年傭工數目已達接近四十萬人。這些跨境工人離鄉別井去外地工作，主要是為家人帶來更好的物質生活。然而不少個案顯示多年的海外工作和生活，使她們和家人的關係發生很大的變化，其個人的想法和人生安排也因長年在外而起了變化。長期的合同工也讓他們難以計劃自己的將來。到底傭工們有否為自己作長遠的人生計劃?打算在海外工作多少年?何時回國與家人團聚?回家後又有如何繼續工作和生活，或重新融入回國後的村鎮生活? 這些都是本研究要探討的問題。此研究將合併跨境與不安穩性兩個概念，作為研究的分析架構，以探討跨境工作的不可預期性和外傭面對的種種困難。 Multiple methods: 1. Literature review 2. Survey A survey on foreign domestic workers in HK will be conducted to collect data on: 1) overseas work’s impacts on their familial relationships; 2) factors that they will consider to continue overseas work and return home; 3) changing familial relationships; 4) effective ways of connecting with home and handling home obligations; 5) long term life plans (in the coming 10 years and beyond). 3. Individual and focus group interview We will conduct both individual and focus group interview with FDW to enhance our understanding of the difficulties of both work life and personal life, and the structural limitations that obstruct workers from making better plans. Focus group interviews will enhance the data-collection process by invoking group dynamics and interactions during such sessions and will help us draw views that we may not be obtained from individual interviews. 4. Ethnographic research We intend to conduct ethnographic field work in the Philippines and Indonesia to collect data on FWD's daily interaction and changing relationships with their families when they return home. Due to the unforeseeable situation of COVID-19's development, we will make up emergency plans (such as hiring local researchers in the two countries) if field trips are made impossible.

11604121.label: Realisation of objectives
11604121.value: This project has explored the following issues: Migrant domestic workers’ working and living experiences in Hong Kong, their work-life plans and return trajectories. A survey was conducted among migrant workers (both Filipino and Indonesians). A total of 256 filled questionnaires were collected. The PI and her research team are analysing the final results for the use of publications. The project also examined factors that influenced migrant domestic workers’ overseas plan and how they prepared for a home-return, what kind of returns they anticipated, and what might push them to overseas places to work again (mobility pathways). The authors have published a paper on ‘home-bound precarity’ which analysed how home conditions and relations might work to coerce immobility of workers and also strengthen the desire for outgoing movements. We revised the previously crafted theoretical concept, “precarity-transnationality”, in order to highlight the problems workers encountered at home. We believe this is a more nuance conceptual framework for examining workers’ home relationships. The PI had worked together with different NGOs and consulates of the sending countries in organizing events and workshops. These workshops aim to discuss policy issues related to the recruitment of foreign domestic workers, placement charges, and regulation of agencies. We also identified good practices in Hong Kong and sending countries that could help improve the management of foreign domestic workers. The workshops also sought to achieve the followings: enhancement of workers’ knowledge on migration, and empowerment of workers. The PI and her research assistants made 4 different field trips to the Philippines and Indonesia, in which they met with the labour authorities in both countries. They had discussed with labour officials difficulties that migrant workers were facing and made suggestions to them about labour placement costs. Two policy papers (on management of FWD during a pandemic crisis, and on transnational manpower governance) were written by the PI, and sent to the Chief Executive Office of HKSAR. The PI believes the project had achieved most of the pre-designed tasks of the research project. It has resulted in the publication of 1 special issue in “Asian and Pacific Migration Journal”, and 3 articles in this special issue. In addition to that, another paper was co-authored by the PI and Co-I, published in the Journal of Ethnic and Migration Studies. There are 3 more pending papers: 1. The Returnscape: the labyrinthine imaginaries and trajectories of temporary migrant workers (under review by Current Sociology) 2. The ‘black hand’ and transnational ambiguity: Migration costs and cross-border labour governance (under review by International Migration) 3. From politics to poetics of migration: Migrant workers’ ‘life-in-migration’ during the COVID pandemic (under review by Migration Studies) Over 90% of the objectives and tasks of the project had been achieved. The PI is preparing a monograph with data collected in this project. This monograph will build on the results published in various journal articles and utilize those data not yet published.

11604121.label: Major findings and research outcome
11604121.value: This project has outstanding achievements, as the PI and Co-I have published their research results in one special issue, 2 journal articles and 1 more pending article. We have dealt with the following issues: Domestic workers’ precariousness in their work life and the transnational connections with home in the country of origin, as well as changing family relationships (objective 1, see paper 1, 2, 3 & 4). We discussed the peculiar “sporadic hyper-precarity” faced by overseas domestic workers during the COVID pandemic and how their experiences demonstrated the “sanitized divide” and “care divide” between local families and domestic workers that had in turn resulted in the unequal treatment of workers. We highlighted how home connections can be a source of stress and estrangement. The soft violence imposed on migrant women has led to the formation of ‘home-bound precarity’ which is one of the root causes of migrant workers’ protracted precarious experience (paper 4). We also discussed workers’ life plan and their return pathways in another article (objective 2, paper 5). We argue that returns are of diverse patterns and out of different reasons. Forming different spatiality and temporality, workers often conduct alternate home-bound and destination-bound returns, creating their own visions and meanings for a return. The PI and her assistants interrogated workers’ experiences during the placement process: how they were overcharged by recruitment agencies and what caused the high placement fees. They conducted field work in the villages in the Philippines and Indonesia where workers returned to. The workers told the research team their various stories of making work-life plans. Young workers still cherished for a chance to work overseas again, while others felt the dilemma between leaving the family and the lack of stable income if they stayed home (paper 5 & 6). The PI developed another concept – ‘poetics of migration’ in a life-in-migration. Previous literature of migration has mostly discussed the politics of migration, rarely was there serious discussion of the poetics of migration. She drew on E. Glissant’s idea of ‘poetics of relation’ to elaborate on what could be unexpected freedom and empowerment even under a time of crisis (paper 7). The PI will further organize the collected research data and put them in the monograph she is preparing. The PI has written 2 policy papers (on management of FWD during a pandemic crisis, and on transnational manpower governance) and sent them to the Chief Executive Office.

11604121.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11604121.value: We believe that based on what we have written, more work can be developed on the concept of ‘home-bound precarity’ and the form of soft violence created in transnational connection. We urge further scholarly effort in studying overseas domestic workers’ work-life plan and return pathways – which are diverse and entail different meanings from the perspectives of the workers. Currently, sending countries, such as Indonesia and the Philippines mainly focus on micro finance projects and entrepreneurship programmes to support the reintegration of return workers. Our findings show that many returns of workers entail different spatialities and temporalities, as well as reasons and outcomes. There is a need to conduct deeper studies of the diverse return patterns.

11604121.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11604121.value: This project examines migrant domestic workers’ living and work experiences in Hong Kong, and their transnational practices. It interrogates their work-life plan and return pathways. To date, most of the studies of overseas domestic workers focus on their distress and consider them victims of the global labour regime. This project has identified spaces of empowerment, growth, and resistance. Throughout their working life as overseas domestic workers, these migrant women have experienced both precariousness and empowerment. Many were able to use their acquired skills and experiences to enhance their future living at home. With better work-life plan and policy initiatives, overseas work would be benefiting both workers and their families. On the other hand, the labour governance regime should conduct more systematic research on workers’ real experiences to fill the gap in state-sponsored reintegration programmes.

11604221.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11604221.value: 中国刑辩维权律师法律动员的实证研究

11604221.label: Co - Investigator(s)
11604221.value: Dr Wu, Jun Dr Xiao, Huina

11604221.label: Project Objectives
11604221.value: To present empirical findings on the legal mobilization by criminal defence weiquan lawyers (rights-protection lawyers) in China and fill the gap in the weiquan lawyering literature. To ascertain how weiquan lawyers mobilize different actors in the criminal justice system to improve the rate of success, how weiquan lawyers influence the outcome of criminal lawsuits and what factors contribute to the success of a weiquan criminal lawsuit. To identify the factors (capacity, ideology, social relations, allies and legal opportunity) that influence the variation of mobilization by weiquan lawyers; to assess whether legal mobilization by criminal defence weiquan lawyers in China is effective, in terms of litigation successes and out-of-court mobilization effectiveness. To provide useful data that allows policy researchers (both governmental and non-governmental) to reflect on the current problems in China’s criminal justice system, e.g. data on the common violations (of procedural and substantive laws) by the police, procurators, courts and other actors in the criminal process and data on the judicial attitude towards weiquan lawyering in criminal cases. To provide useful data to guide weiquan lawyers on how to deal with different actors in a criminal case and to highlight those strategies that work well, both in terms of safeguarding the defendant’s procedural rights as well as ensuring the best possible substantive outcome. To facilitate positive legislative changes in the Chinese criminal justice system (such as reforming its rules on pre-trial detention), to inform the global cause lawyering movement of the Chinese criminal defence weiquan experience, and to help the international human rights community better understand the state of affairs of criminal justice in China. To contribute to comparative legal mobilization theory beyond criminal defence weiquan lawyering, benefiting the work of non-criminal public interest lawyers, NGOs, interest groups and activists in both authoritarian and democratic states.

11604221.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11604221.value: Weiquan lawyers (or “rights-protection lawyers”) are public-interest lawyers in China. Public-interest lawyers are lawyers who look beyond their immediate commercial interests to advocate for greater causes in society. Weiquan lawyers generally operate within the political framework of the party-state, but the more radical ones do sometimes challenge that framework. While much has been written about the nature and practice of weiquan lawyering in China, legal mobilization as a theory that explains weiquan lawyering in criminal lawsuits is under-researched. Legal mobilization refers to the strategic use of litigation and other law-related avenues to achieve a cause. This project seeks to fill this gap and offer an empirical assessment on how weiquan lawyers litigate strategically and critique its effectiveness. In measuring “effectiveness”, one needs to move away from the straightforward test of “cases won” and adopt a multifaceted approach to winning. As we look at many weiquan cases, while the defendant may not have been acquitted or received a reduction in sentence (unsuccessful litigation), the involvement of weiquan lawyers had brought about broader changes in the litigation environment that are conducive to rights-protection (overall successful in achieving the cause). For instance, the case may have raised public awareness of the issue to the extent that some form of legislative or policy change occurred due to public pressure. One specific aspect to watch out for in assessing effectiveness, apart from simply looking at courtroom successes, is the ability of weiquan lawyers in bringing about rule-changes. 维权律师（或“护权律师”）是中国的公益律师。公益律师是指超越其眼前的商业利益，为社会上更大的事业进行宣传的律师。维权律师通常在党政国家的政治框架内运作，但更激进的律师有时会挑战这一框架。虽然关于中国维权律师的性质和实践的文章很多，但关于解释刑事诉讼中维权律师的理论，法律动员的研究不足。法律动员是指战略性地利用诉讼和其他与法律有关的途径来实现一项事业。本项目试图填补这一空白，对维权律师如何进行战略性诉讼提供实证评估，并对其有效性进行批判性评价。在衡量“有效性”时，需要摆脱“胜诉”这一简单的测试，而应采取一种多面的方法来衡量是否取胜。纵观许多维权案件，虽然被告可能没有被无罪释放或获得减刑（诉讼不成功），但维权律师的参与给诉讼环境带来了更广泛的变化，更有利于维权（整体上成功实现了维权）。例如，该案例可能引起了公众对该问题的关注，以至于立法或政策在公众压力下发生了某种形式的变化。在评估有效性时，除了简单地看法庭上的成功之外，还需要注意的一个具体方面是，维权律师在促成规则改变方面的能力。

11604421.value: 西醫藥產品廣告的跨文化譯寫：以《華字日報》（1895-1940）為例

11604421.value: To examine the relationship between print media and the dissemination of scientific knowledge and Western medicine at the turn of the twentieth century. To compare Chinese advertisements for the same Western medicines appearing in Hong Kong and Shanghai newspapers from the 1910s to 1930s. 11604421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11604421.value: Few studies have explored the advertisements for Western medicine that were placed in Hong Kong Chinese newspapers at the turn of the twentieth century. This project will first briefly review the relationship between print media and the dissemination of scientific and medical knowledge. It will then examine the methodological aspects of research on advertisement translation and describe the archaeological work performed to tabulate the advertisements for Western medicine that were published in The Chinese Mail between 1895 and 1940. With the translation archaeology established, the project will work to answer a series of questions, such as: Which Western medicines were placed in the Hong Kong Chinese newspapers? Why were they chosen? What happened to the translation of the brand names? What kind of medical discourses were applied to introduce the symptoms of the related diseases, and what functions did they expect these Western medicines to serve? Did the Chinese advertisements merely follow their English counterparts, or were they tailored to local consumers? To what extent were they (re)framed? Did the act of (re)framing lead to the juxtaposition of two different medical discourses in one text? The adaptation of Western medicine advertisements for Hong Kong Chinese newspapers has been defined as transadvertising. Accordingly, the proposed project will discuss issues of further interest to the field of translation history. For example, what kind of impact did these advertisement translations have on the local readership? Did they challenge the local people’s thinking about diseases and treatments? Did they win acceptance among Chinese users? Did the local merchants follow suit and develop similar medical products in light of the lucrative nature of this health business? The above questions will be particularly important for a study of the years immediately following the outbreak of the bubonic plague in 1894. As the literature review will illustrate, Chinese advertisements for Western medicine in Shanghai newspapers from the 1920s to the 1930s have been well-covered in scholarly discourse. This project will make synchronic comparisons between Hong Kong and Shanghai in the 1920s and 1930s. Baker’s model of analysis will be applied to examine how Western medicines were placed on the Chinese market and will demonstrate how their brand names and descriptions were (re)framed to fit the discourse of traditional Chinese medicine. This study will enhance our understanding of pharmaceutical history and translation history in Hong Kong. 香港作為中西交匯之處，見證了早期華文報紙的濫觴。十九世紀中葉以降，西方科學技術的進步帶來醫藥業的繁榮。二十世紀之交，在香港的英文報紙也大量刊載西醫藥廣告，而香港的中文報紙也開始翻譯、推銷這些醫藥產品。我們不禁要問，這段時期報紙主要翻譯刊載了那些西藥產品的廣告呢？這些產品為何受到華人使用者的青睞呢？這些產品的英文廣告在翻譯製作成中文廣告的時候，是如何被改寫和編譯的呢？我們不得不承認，在十九世紀末，香港華人是社會人口的主要構成部分，而中醫更是華人普遍接受的診治方法。西醫藥產品主要基於西醫理論和病徵，廣告中的醫藥話語是否能直接被華人接受呢？本研究首先搜集1895至1910這十五年間，在香港最主要的中文報紙《香港華字日報》出現頻率最高的一系列西醫藥產品的廣告，並與同期香港的英文報紙刊載的相同產品的英文廣告進行對比研究，深度描寫這些西醫藥產品的英文廣告是如何被改寫成中文廣告，比如用中醫藥話語描述病症、添加用藥禁忌、採取圖文並茂等手段。其次，本研究將搜集二十世紀二十至四十年代香港華文報紙刊載的西醫藥廣告，並與同期上海華文報紙刊載的同類藥品廣告比較，呈現二者之間的異同，並解釋其背後的社會文化成因。

11604521.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11604521.value: 人工智能的應用與隱私關注：比較用戶對 AI 聊天機器人和人工代理的看法

11604521.value: To understand the applications of the AI chatbots and human agents in different sectors and enterprises in Hong Kong, Mainland China, and the U.S. To compare users’ perceived trust, privacy concerns and intention to use AI chatbots and human agents in Hong Kong, Mainland China, and the U.S. To generalize the challenges and problems faced by the public and private sectors and enterprises in the application of chatbots and human agents, and to offer them suggestions about how to alleviate chatbot users’ privacy concerns and protect their personal data. To promote cross-sector (public and private) and cross-regional collaboration, and provide practical suggestions for improving chatbot services and promoting innovative AI applications. To test the theories and models related to privacy concerns, perceived trust, and usage intention and build a comparative model for anthropomorphic virtual agents.

11604521.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11604521.value: The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI) has attracted wide attention and generated heated discussions about user privacy. As an AI application, a chatbot is a conversational agent with natural language processing ability to imitate human conversation. Since chatbots cannot replace humans in the performance of more complicated or personalized tasks, human agents still co-exist with chatbots in the business or other sectors. A chatbot can be embedded in different platforms or through different channels to implement particular tasks. It can also develop a long-term relationship with and even become an emotional companion to its users. In expanding the existing scholarship regarding human-robot interaction, this study will cross-culturally explore users’ privacy concerns with regard to two types of chatbots, namely, task-oriented and companion-oriented chatbots and their different impacts on people’s usage intentions. It will also examine users’ perceived trust in the expertise, reputation, or technology of chatbots and their intentions in using chatbots and human agents. Studies have shown that cultural or regional differences regarding users’ privacy concerns should not be ignored when conversational agents are involved. People in Mainland China are generally more receptive to new technologies. They are more willing to provide their personal data in exchange for the services and products they need. However, people in Hong Kong and the U.S. tend to be more cautious when using new smart devices or applications. Therefore, the focus of this study will be on Hong Kong, Mainland China, and the U.S. In the first year, in-depth interviews with chatbot designers and relevant enterprises will be conducted. Meanwhile, panel group studies that focus on the users will be conducted in Hong Kong and Mainland China in order to prepare for the online experiment. In the second year, the online experiment will be conducted in the three regions based on having 2 (chatbot vs. human) x 2 (task-oriented vs. companion-oriented) conditions to understand users’ perceived trust, privacy concerns and usage intention. After the online experiment, the panel group studies will be conducted again in order to supplement the above quantitative findings. This study will contribute to scholars’ and practitioners’ understanding of chatbots in cross-cultural digital communication environments by investigating users’ perceptions of the communication entity (chatbot) and their usage intention when interacting with them. In delineating the notions of perceived trust and privacy concerns, this study aims to extend research in the field of human-machine communication along with the societal implications. 人工智能（AI）的快速發展引起了廣泛關注，也引發了關於用戶隱私的熱烈討論。作為人工智能應用，聊天機器人是一種具有自然語言處理能力的對話代理，可以模仿人類對話。由於聊天機器人無法替代人類執行更複雜或個性化的任務，因此人工代理仍與商業或其他領域的聊天機器人共存。 聊天機器人可以嵌入不同的平台或通過不同的渠道來執行特定的任務，還可以與用戶建立長期關係，甚至成為其情感伴侶。在擴展現有的人機交互研究的同時，本研究將跨文化探討用戶對兩類聊天機器人（即任務導向和伴侶導向的聊天機器人）的隱私關注及其對人們使用意圖的不同影響，並將研究用戶對聊天機器人的專業知識、聲譽或技術的信任度以及他們使用聊天機器人和人工代理的意圖。 相關研究顯示，當涉及對話代理時，不應忽視有關用戶對隱私關注的文化或地區差異。中國人普遍更容易接受新技術。他們更願意提供他們的個人數據以換取他們需要的服務和產品。然而，香港人和美國人在使用新的智能設備或應用程序時往往更加謹慎。因此，本研究的範圍將專注於香港、中國大陸和美國。 本研究第一年將將對聊天機器人設計師和相關企業進行深度訪談。同時，將在香港和中國大陸進行以用戶為中心的焦點團體訪談，為在線實驗做準備。第二年，在線實驗將在三個地區進行，基於2（聊天機器人vs.人類）x 2（任務導向vs.同伴導向）條件，了解用戶感知信任、隱私關注和使用意圖。在線實驗結束後，將再次進行焦點團體訪談，以補充解釋上述定量研究結果。 本研究透過調查用戶對聊天機器人的感知以及與他們交互時的使用意圖，將有助於學界和業界對跨文化數字傳播環境中的聊天機器人的理解。在描述用戶感知信任和隱私關注的概念時，本研究亦期望擴展人機傳播領域的研究以及其社會影響意涵。

11604821.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11604821.value: 香港緊急情況下政府權力規制比較研究

11604821.label: Project Objectives
11604821.value: To examine and identify deficiencies in the legal framework on emergency powers in HK through a comparative study with regulatory models in other jurisdictions. To make concrete proposals on how the existing legal framework should be reformed with regard to model choice, and classification of emergency powers for better regulation. To examine and identify problems in the existing supervision of emergency powers in HK through a comparative and jurisprudential study of supervisory measures in other jurisdictions. To make specific suggestions on how to improve existing supervision of emergency powers in HK. To make a contribution to the comparative literature on emergency powers.
rows: To examine and identify deficiencies in the legal framework on emergency powers in HK through a comparative study with regulatory models in other jurisdictions.
To make concrete proposals on how the existing legal framework should be reformed with regard to model choice, and classification of emergency powers for better regulation.
To examine and identify problems in the existing supervision of emergency powers in HK through a comparative and jurisprudential study of supervisory measures in other jurisdictions.
To make specific suggestions on how to improve existing supervision of emergency powers in HK.
To make a contribution to the comparative literature on emergency powers.

11604821.label: Realisation of objectives
11604821.value: All five objectives have been achieved. The research has first identified essential elements of law on emergency power through comparative study. The first is whether it is de facto or de jure emergency power. The second is the nature of the framework on emergency power, i.e. whether emergency power is regulated by the Constitution, or by ordinary legislation, or a mixture of both, or simply by application of doctrine necessity. The third is scope, i.e. whether the emergency law is general emergency law or specialized emergency law. The fourth is the content and substantive function of emergency law. The fifth is tiering of emergency regulations. Such doctrinal and comparative research has laid down the foundation for detailed examination of the legal framework on emergency powers in HK. The second part of research is detailed study of legal regulation of emergency powers in HK. Hong Kong's framework on emergency power adopts the model of constitutional law plus ordinary local legislation on emergency power, but at the same time subject to regulation of certain international law as far as protection of fundamental rights is concerned. Through comparative study, this research has identified several specific deficiencies in the legal framework on emergency powers in HK through comparative research. The first is there exist legal ambiguity and also lack of direction restraint on the exercise of emergency power at both national and local level. HK's unique legal status has made its legal regulation of emergency powers different from many other jurisdictions under comparative study. It's because the Basic Law, which is HK's mini-constitution, grants authority to decide national state of emergency to the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress under Art. 18 subject to no supervision at local level in HK. The exercise of such national emergency power is not subject to international supervision because China is not a party to the ICCPR. Secondly, at local level, HK's legal framework on emergency power is a tiered one with two pieces of specific legislation. After careful analysis, this research has identified several issues: lack of self-limitation mechanisms and possible expansion of power by the executive branch; the Bill of Rights Ordinance may not provide adequate safeguards under existing local emergency regime. The research has also carefully examined several actual cases: the application of the Emergency Regulations Ordinance by the Chief Executive in Council to enact the Prohibition on Face Covering Regulation and its judicial review; the enactment of a series of publlic health emergency regulations under the Prevention and Control of Disease Ordinance, and the regulation made under the Emergency Regulations Ordinance to postpone the LegCo and the Chief Executive election and so on. The research has chosen two important issues to conduct in-depth study. The first is whether the legislature in HK is able to effectively supervise the executive in the scenario of a local emergency. The second is whether the judiciary in HK is able to effectively supervise the executive in the scenario of a local emergency. The research has come to the following conclusions.The legal regime per se does not directly promise how emergency power will be exercised within the course of legal operation. A well-structured democratic society that customarily constrains the emergency power of the executive may, in practice, refrain from exercising such power, or have established mechanism for democratic dialogue with a positive effect on preventing the generation of future terrorism and violence that would trigger emergency law. In another scenario, the laws may have established mechanisms for checks and balances, but one power branch may be reluctant to do so on another, leaving such a mechanism of no avail. For example, for the US, “while Congress may vote to terminate a presidentially declared state of emergency, it has done so only once in four decades.” And for that, “the Congress voted to end that emergency, but the president vetoed Congress’s resolution, and so the emergency remains in place.” The actual realization of emergency control may come into effect through non-legal operations. One example would be Japan, where there is a legal regime, but the real efficiency lies in extra-legal consequences deriving from legal measures, rather than legal measures per se. Japan does not have a constitutional emergency regime, and it declared a state of emergency according to an ordinary law on infectious disease without binding restrictive measures. It is a de jure state of emergency and requires declaration. However, it functions in an extra-legal way that can not be said to be the straightforward outcome of an application of the law, and is open to question under the rule of law. Another scenario would be the situation in mainland China, where no legal state of emergency has been triggered or invoked, yet non-government subjects have coercively restricted people’s fundamental rights in reaction to an emergency incident, with no legal basis. The most ideal combination is of mutually supporting rule of law and democracy, where laws are well made and democratic supervision on the exercise of power is effective. Where laws have potential risks, effective democratic supervision can prevent them from being exercised to the extreme, such potential risks in laws can only be taken as excusable as they can be stopped by well-functioning democracy from inducing great harm; while in societies with weak democracy, even formally well-made laws may be manipulated. In the latter case, check and balance mechanisms impose more barriers and inconveniences for such manipulation and hinder the abuse of power. The actual implementation of an emergency system in the earthly world may be beyond the scope of emergency law or law per se. Still, one should do the best in the design of institutions. This research has touched upon the weakness of the current emergency system regarding HK in terms of the prevention of abuse of power. The legal provisions of the emergency laws are majorly concerned with delegation of power, and lack the motivation to restrain it. As for carriers and executers of emergency power, the NPC and NPCSC have been placed at the supreme position within the PRC legal-political system, and there is nothing to constrain them effectively. In HK's political system, the executive enjoys a relatively dominant position. Checks from the local legislature and the judiciary on local ERO regulations are reluctant. This paper has proposed options to create more control on the emergency power, to reduce its possibility of abuse. Whichever suggestion is offered, it will need the lawmaker’s willingness to place the power in pen. On the level of Basic Law, self-restraint of the central authority is essential. At local level, changes regarding the ERO have to do with the functioning of HK's political structure in an emergency. The Government needs to be willing to impose self-restriction against abuse of power and to enhance the democratic legitimacy of the LegCo, to constrain the possibility of the executive clinging to emergency power in a future emergency and refusing to give it up and therefore rejecting LegCo check. Although the assumption of good faith is required, institutions are designed because humanity is unreliable. In instructional designs against abuse of power, the worst possibilities and outcomes should be taken into consideration.

11604821.label: Major findings and research outcome
11604821.value: The legal framework on emergency power for both national emergency and local emergency needs better checks and balances. At the level of Basic Law, self-restraint of the central authority is essential as the NPCSC is in reality subject to no checks and balances. At local level, ideally structural change should be made in order to increase the weight of legislative control in emergencies. Alternatively, a more prompt negative vetting process where the LegCo should be convened immediately for the submission of the regulation made under the ERO, and the negative vetting process should be scheduled speedier than that of ordinary subsidiary legislations. Also time limit should be set for emergency legislation. In addition, certain concepts in the Emergency Regulations Ordinance need to be clarified in order to reduce their vagueness. It's desirable to set up a legally prescribed proclamation mechanism targeting the public emergency under the Bill of Rights Ordinance. The most ideal combination is of mutually supporting rule of law and democracy, where las are well made and democratic supervision on the exercise of emergency power is effective.

11604821.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11604821.value: The PI will propose concrete proposals to amend relevant local legislations to the HK Government for its consideration.

11604821.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11604821.value: This research has studied the legal framework on regulation of emergency powers in HK through comparative study with other countries. It has identified some deficiencies in the existing legal framework such as lack of checks and balances for the exercise of national emergency power under Art. 18 of the Basic Law and weak legislative supervision over exercise of local emergency powers by the Executive. The research proposes options to create more control on the exercise of emergency power in order to reduce possibility of abuse. This research makes a unique contribution to comparative study literature on emergency powers because HK's unique constitutional status under the principle of one country two systems, which has made regulation of emergency in HK is shared between national and local legislation.

11604921.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11604921.value: 神聖之技：中日佛教寺院與工匠，960-1368 AD

11604921.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11604921.value: During the Song (960–1276) and Yuan (1271–1368) dynasties, Buddhist monasteries in southeastern China continuously increased in both scale and wealth. Their influence reached as far as Japan. Artisans, although scarcely mentioned in official records, played a significant role in this process. The proposed research will focus on Chinese artisans associated with monasteries or the production of Buddhist objects during this period. Much of their work survives due to the sacred nature of their products, providing an invaluable opportunity to study the history of this underrepresented Chinese group. The project will reevaluate the position of artisans in social, religious, and economic realms and reveal their contribution to China-Japan Buddhist exchange between 960 and 1368 by investigating their interaction with multiple social classes and their transborder mobility. The proposed project will examine inscriptions on Buddhist architecture and objects and monastic records to study two main groups of Chinese artisans during the above period: carpenters and masons who constructed buildings for monasteries, and sculptors who manufactured Buddhist statues. The artisans’ ability to construct awe-inspiring religious architecture or wish-fulfilling ritual objects earned them a certain authority and redefined their relationship with their patrons, who ranged from royalty and court officials to impoverished but devout villagers. Monasteries attracted more patronage by possessing powerful ritual objects, and artisans contributed to the monastic economy by providing precisely such objects. During this period, artisans played a significant role in the robust Buddhist exchange between China and Japan. In the late twelfth century, a group of Chinese masons from the coastal city of Ningbo migrated to Japan. They participated in the most important project then, reconstructing the prestigious Tōdaiji monastery in Nara. One of the masons later adopted a Japanese name. His descendants inherited his Japanese clan name and masonry as their family profession, and transplanted certain Chinese art styles to Japan via their works. Their expertise was highly recognized by the Japanese authorities. By exploring the image of Chinese artisans in a religious setting, the proposed project will demonstrate that artisans played a more important role in Buddhist communities, local societies, and cultural exchange than previously recognized. Moreover, this study will advance our understanding of the relationship between Buddhism and materiality by shedding light on the people who provided craftsmanship. Craftsmanship embodied the power of religion, and the artisan’s skill and knowledge sometimes determined how certain Buddhist concepts were presented to believers. 在宋元時期，中國東南地區的佛教寺院在規模上與掌握的財富上都保持著增長。它們的影響甚至遠及日本。雖然官方史料中很少提及工匠群體，但是他們實際上在這一過程中扮演了重要角色。本研究將聚焦於中國宋元時期為寺院工作、或者製造佛教相關用品的工匠們。鑒於他們所製造的物品多具有宗教的神聖性質，他們的作品中为数不少得以保存至今，為研究這一尚未得到足夠關注的群體提供了寶貴的材料。通過考察工匠們與不同社會階層的互動以及他們的跨境活動，本研究將重新審視工匠們在社會、宗教、以及經濟領域的地位，並揭示出他們在宋元時期的佛教交流方面的貢獻。 本研究將調查佛教建築與物品上的石刻或銘文、以及寺院記錄，以此考察宋元時期的兩類工匠，包括為寺院搭建建築物的木匠和石匠，以及雕刻佛像的佛師。工匠們建造令人敬畏的建築、或製作具有神力的宗教物品的能力，實際上也為他們贏得了一種權威，並且重新定義了他們與他們的主顧的關係。而工匠們的主顧涵蓋由皇親國戚、朝中重臣到貧窮卻虔信的村民等各個階層。當寺院擁有據稱十分靈驗的佛像等物品時，會吸引来更多的捐贈，而工匠們正是通過提供這類物品，對寺院經濟做出貢獻。 在宋元時期，工匠們在中日間活躍的佛教交流中也扮演了重要角色。在十二世紀末，一群石匠從中國的港口城市寧波遷移到了日本。他們參與了當時日本最為重要的建造項目—重建位於奈良的著名佛教寺院東大寺。其中一名石匠之後改用了日本名字，而他的後人不僅繼承了这一日本姓氏，並且以石匠為家族職業。他們通過自己的作品，把中國佛教藝術的一些特點帶入了日本，而他們的專業技能也得到了日本的統治階層的高度認可。 通過考察宗教環境中的中國工匠的形象，本研究力圖證明工匠們在佛教社群、地方社會、以及文化交流中均扮演著比既有認知更為重要的角色。同時，通過把工藝製作的實際执行者帶到臺前，本研究意圖加深現有對佛教與物質性之間關係的理解。工匠技藝可以體現出宗教的力量，而工匠們自有的技術與知識有時決定了佛教概念會被如何呈現給信眾。

11605121.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11605121.value: 在香港大學留學的亞洲國際學生的身份軌跡：縱向敘事的研究方法

11605121.label: Co - Investigator(s)
11605121.value: Prof BENSON, Philip Prof MONTGOMERY, Catherine

11605121.label: Project Objectives
11605121.value: To investigate Asian international students’ identity negotiation in their academic and social integration in the university To investigate Asian international students’ language experiences in their academic and social integration, especially the impact of their language experiences on their identity negotiation To examine Asian international students’ identity trajectories over time during their studies in the university To identify factors that may account for the similarities and differences in Asian international students’ identity trajectories

To investigate Asian international students’ language experiences in their academic and social integration, especially the impact of their language experiences on their identity negotiation
To examine Asian international students’ identity trajectories over time during their studies in the university
To identify factors that may account for the similarities and differences in Asian international students’ identity trajectories

11605121.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11605121.value: 這項研究將從身份的角度來調查在香港大學留學的亞洲國際學生的學術和社會融合經歷。這項研究特別會調查他們的身份和他們在學術和社會融合中的身份軌跡，以及他們的語言經歷對他們身份建構的影響。這項研究旨在了解亞洲國際學生如何建構他們作為大學學術和社會成員的身份，他們的語言經歷如何影響他們在學術和社會融合中的身份建構，他們如何駕馭他們在香港學習期間的經歷，以及哪些因素可能造成影響他們身份軌跡的異同。 這項研究項目將以關於身份的觀點，輔以一些相關理論，包括身份建構、身份軌跡、學術和社會融合，和語言社會化作為研究基礎。研究將採用縱向敘述方法，並結合多方法研究設計作為研究方法。數據收集將在三年內在三所香港大學進行。三所香港大學為一所一流的綜合性大學，一所二級綜合大學，及一所三級大學。 研究參與者為六十位在三所香港大學留學的亞洲國際本科生。在三年時間裡，研究項目將與參與者進行多輪個人半結構化訪談，當中會輔以視覺方法，以收集他們在大學的學術和社會融合經驗，包括他們的語言經驗。參與者還會完成書面活動日誌，其中報告會講述他們在大學的日常經歷。研究將會使用敘述式探究方法來分析收集到的數據，以了解參與者的身份建構和他們在學術和社會融合中的身份軌跡。

11605221.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11605221.value: 复杂制度环境下的监管中介：角色、政府联系和绩效

11605221.label: Co - Investigator(s)
11605221.value: Prof Levi-Faur, David Prof Lo, Carlos Wing-hung

11605221.label: Project Objectives
11605221.value: Extend the regulator–intermediary–target (RIT) model by distinguishing between a diverse set of intermediary types (i.e., who are the regulatory intermediaries) and identifying and classifying their roles, practices, and strategies in interacting with regulators and firm clients in environmental governance in China (i.e., what intermediary work has been done, and how). Explore the influence of the intermediaries’ connection to the government, including both institutional embeddedness and ascribed personal connections to the government, in shaping regulatory intermediaries’ market performance. Probe the institutional complexity that arises from regulatory changes, intermediary market competition, and public sector reform, which influences the impact of government connections in determining intermediary performance over time and across jurisdictions. Consider practical implications that can help policymakers and regulated business firms respond to the opportunities and challenges in the emerging RIT processes.

Explore the influence of the intermediaries’ connection to the government, including both institutional embeddedness and ascribed personal connections to the government, in shaping regulatory intermediaries’ market performance.

11605221.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11605221.value: Intermediaries are a significant component of market and economic institutions. Although their importance has manifested across social and economic domains (i.e., finance, innovation, health care, education), research on regulatory intermediaries has thus far been limited. A regulatory intermediary is a third party that connects regulators and the parties they regulate by providing information and expertise (e.g., audit, inspection, rating, and ranking) to facilitate regulatory enforcement and compliance. The emerging scholarship focuses largely on the demand side of intermediary services in studying either regulators’ engagement of intermediaries in enforcement and policy implementation or, more recently, firms’ choice of intermediary in response to regulation. Less is known about how the supply side of intermediaries competes in the flourishing and evolving intermediary service market. This issue is particularly worthy of investigation in China, where intermediary involvement is thriving due to regulatory decentralization in many policy fields. Without a careful understanding of how intermediaries function as influential actors, one can hardly understand their collective role in expanding the reach and effectiveness of regulation. The literature sheds little light on this issue, and further study is essential to uncover its complexity and dynamics. To fill these gaps, the proposed study will investigate how intermediaries operate at the business-government interface with regard to environmental governance in China. Based on the wider intermediary literature, we will seek to answer three important research questions. (1) What is the role of intermediaries in the regulator-intermediary-target triad in shaping the regulatory process and its effectiveness? (2) How do regulatory intermediaries rely on government connections when competing for firm clients? (3) How do regulatory changes, intermediary market expansion, and public sector reform shape the impact of government connections on an intermediary’s market performance? We will adopt a two-study multimethod design. Study 1 will seek to answer question 1 via policy archive analysis and in-depth interviews with intermediary entities, regulated firms, and regulatory officials in three selected cities (Guangzhou, Tianjin, and Chengdu). In Study 2, we will examine questions 2 and 3 by assembling a novel quantitative dataset of intermediaries that specialize in Environmental Impact Assessment in Guangdong province to test four hypotheses. This project will build on our previous research on firms’ choice of intermediary in response to environmental regulation in China, and it will provide significant insights into the theoretical development and practical implications of intermediation in effective regulatory governance. 中介机构是市场和经济体系的一个重要组成部分。尽管其重要性已体现在社会和经济活动的各个领域（如金融、创新、医疗保健、教育等），但迄今为止，对监管中介的研究还很有限。监管中介作为连接监管机构和被监管对象的桥梁，可以通过提供信息和专业知识（如审计、检查、评级和排名）来帮助监管机构实现监管目标。当前的学术研究主要侧重于中介服务的需求方，例如监管机构对中介机构及其行为的监督和管理，或者被监管对象如何为应对监管而挑选不同类型的中介服务机构。对于中介机构自身如何在蓬勃发展和不断变化的中介服务市场中进行竞争，我们仍然知之甚少。这个问题在中国尤其值得研究。随着监管权力的下放，中介机构在许多政策领域的参与程度正逐渐加深。如果缺乏对中介机构角色和行为的深入认识，我们将很难理解其在监管领域起到的实际作用。由于现有文献尚未对此进行详细阐述，通过进一步研究揭示该问题的复杂性和动态性至关重要。 本项目旨在研究监管中介机构在中国环境治理中的行为和角色。基于现有文献，我们将回答三个重要的研究问题。首先，在监管机构、中介机构、以及被监管对象三者之间，中介机构如何影响监管过程及其有效性？其次，中介机构在竞争过程中如何依赖政府关系？再次，中介机构的经营水平是否受到监管环境变化、中介市场扩张和公共部门改革的共同影响？我们将通过两项子研究回答这些问题。在研究（一）里，我们将在三个指定城市（广州、天津和成都）收集相关的环境政策以及环保中介机构监管数据，并与不同类型的中介机构、被监管企业、以及监管机构进行深入访谈。在研究（二）中，我们将收集在广东省从事环境影响评价的中介机构的经营数据来检验研究问题（二）和（三）下的四个假设。本项目将建立在我们之前关于企业如何选择中介机构以应对环境监管的研究基础上，并将为有效监管治理中的中介机构的理论发展和实践意义提供重要见解。

11605421.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11605421.value: 中、日文化交流考論──以十八世紀中葉至十九世紀末兩國之 《韓非子》為中心

11605421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11605421.value: 《韓非子》為先秦法家思想集大成之作，然而，此書自漢代以後便乏人問津，致簡篇不齊，文字錯亂，幾不可讀。清代中晚期，人才輩出，如盧文弨、顧廣圻、王念孫、俞樾、孫詒讓等優秀學者，整理《韓非子》，不遺餘力，成績斐然。與此同時，日本《韓非子》的研究亦蔚然成風，荻生徂徠、太田方、蒲坂圓等貢獻極大。比較之下，筆者發現兩地學者對《韓非子》的訓釋，頗有相同之處，這可反映十八世紀中葉至十九世紀末中、日兩國文化交流的狀況。本計劃將蒐羅不易得見的日人《韓非子》著作，全面比較兩地學者在《韓非子》的成就，追尋其中互為影響的痕跡，並提出已見，解決《韓非子》中的疑難問題。

11606221.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11606221.value: 共同對抗愛滋病：採用隨機對照試驗提升愛滋病母子的與健康相關的生活質素

11606221.label: Project Objectives
11606221.value: We will develop a randomized controlled trial to improve the HRQoL among Chinese HIV+ women and their children infected with HIV via mother-to-child transmission. There will be three arms, the resilience arm, the adherence arm, and the control arm (Figure 1). To examine the effectiveness of the interventions on individualistic outcomes, we will test the following hypotheses: (1) The resilience intervention will improve the mediators associated with the intervention sessions, such as positive coping and social support, the proximal outcome of resilience factors, and the distal outcome of HRQoL. (2) The adherence intervention will improve the mediators associated with intervention sessions, such as adherence information and behavioral skills, the proximal outcome of adherence, and the distal outcome of HRQoL. To examine the synergistic effects of the combined interventions at the dyadic and family levels, we will treat the HIV+ mother–child dyad as a whole and provide combined interventions through a resilience arm and an adherence arm. We will test a hypothesis that pairs who undergo the combined interventions (i.e., the resilience arm and the adherence arm) will show more improvements in dyadic coping, mother–child closeness, and family harmony (Figure 2) compared with the control mothers and children who receive routine individual-oriented services. To investigate the mediating mechanisms that the resilience intervention and adherence intervention improve individualistic outcomes, we will test the following hypotheses: (1) For the resilience arm, the enhanced mediators (e.g., positive coping and social support) associated with the resilience-intervention sessions at the end of the intervention will transmit the effect of the intervention on the increases in resilience factors during follow-ups (Figure 3a). (2) For the adherence arm, the improved mediators (e.g., adherence information and behavioral skills) associated with the adherence-intervention sessions at the completion of the intervention will transmit the effect of the intervention on the increases in adherence in follow-ups (Figure 3b).

11606221.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11606221.value: HIV陽性（HIV+）婦女與其經母嬰傳播感染HIV的孩子屬於高風險人群，他們與健康相關的生活質素（HRQoL）受到影響。對於那些生活在醫療資源有限地區的HIV+母子，HRQoL下降尤其嚴重。然而，該人群在研究和服務中並未受到關注。目前尚無任何干預研究將HIV+的母子視為一個整體，並將他們雙方作為同伴一起納入HIV疾病管理中。 本研究旨在開發簡短、具有文化適應性、以理論為指導的干預措施，以改善中國HIV+母子的HRQoL。本干預包括以下五個要素：1. 分別從心理與行為的角度，設計兩種不同的干預方案以提升HRQoL；2. 關注母子二元配對；3. 不僅考察個體層面的果效，還擴展到母子關係和家庭層面的果效；4. 考慮文化適應性；以及5. 提升可持續性。 在本研究的隨機對照試驗中，HIV+母子二人一組將被隨機分配到三種干預組中：1. 抗逆力干預組，即心理干預方法，包含污名管理、情緒管理、積極應對和社會聯繫四個部分；2. 藥物依從性干預組，即基於信息-動機-行為技能模型的行為干預方法，包含依從性信息、個人動機、社會動機和行為技能四個部分；3. 對照組，即常規治療。我們將在干預前及干預後1個月和3個月的隨訪中使用結構化測量手段進行定量評估。通過混合方法的評估設計，我們還將進行半結構化訪談，以闡明干預過程和實施中的情況。 為分別考察母親和兒童個體層面的干預果效，我們將檢驗干預措施是否改善了與干預內容相關的中介因素、抗逆力、自我報告的藥物依從性以及HRQoL。 為考察母子組合在二元和家庭層面的干預果效，我們將檢驗抗逆力干預和依從性干預（均採用母親和兒童的二人組合模式）是否會促進母子二元應對能力、母子親密度和家庭和睦。 為進行中介分析以闡明干預如何對個體結果起到果效，我們將考察與干預內容相關的中介變數是否會傳遞干預對提升抗逆力或依從性的果效。 這項干預試驗以公共衛生為要務，將推動更高水平的實踐科學研究。本研究的結果將有助於在資源有限地區開展HIV醫療健康的循證實踐，並促進制定適用於邊緣化人群且具有文化敏感的干預方案。

11606421.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11606421.value: 閱讀「淫詩」：朱熹「淫詩說」與明清《詩經》閱讀史

11606421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11606421.value: 朱熹認為，《詩經·國風》有很多「淫詩」。傳統的《詩經》詮釋，堅信這是詩人在諷刺淫奔之事，作者思想與詩歌主題都符合孔子所說的「思無邪」；相反，朱熹卻提出，這是淫奔者在自述醜行，作者就是淫奔者。自元代延祐年間以後，科舉考試以朱熹《詩集傳》為準，明清時代的讀者閱讀《詩經》，都要面對朱熹的「淫詩說」。 朱熹的「淫詩說」，不僅引發了經學的論爭，還提出了一種新的閱讀理論，對明清時代的閱讀史和《詩經》閱讀實踐產生了極大影響，這是學界長期以來所忽視的。 朱熹將關注重心從作者轉向了讀者。朱熹認為，《詩經》作者不需「思無邪」，但是，讀者必須「無邪」。只有在淫者自述醜行的「淫詩」中，讀者才能親身體驗人欲的危險，從而激發警省之心，完成養心功夫。因此，朱熹提出了一個「觀淫止淫」的閱讀理論，突出了讀者的道德自主能力。 然而，朱熹只是構想了一種理想讀者。在理想規範與閱讀實踐之間，還有很多不確定性與張力。現實情境中的讀者，是否能夠在閱讀實踐中實現「觀淫止淫」的理想目標？明清時代的讀者，對於朱熹指出的「淫詩」作品，又有哪些實際的閱讀反應？ 本計劃另闢蹊徑，不囿於經學史領域，而是轉向閱讀史，關注各類讀者閱讀「淫詩」的方式、體驗、反應及效果。本計劃將圍繞理想規範、閱讀實踐之間的落差與矛盾，以〈王風·丘中有麻〉、〈鄭風·山有扶蘇〉、〈鄭風·褰裳〉等具體「淫詩」詩篇為中心，梳理明清時代不同身份讀者的閱讀體驗和反應，並考察明清時代讀者閱讀《詩經》「淫詩」與閱讀戲曲小說之間的微妙關聯，反思閱讀「淫詩」的實際效果。 簡言之，朱熹的「淫詩說」，不僅與經學史相關，更與閱讀史、文化史密切相關。本計劃將綜合經學史、閱讀史、文學史、思想史、文化史等各種視角，深入研究朱熹「淫詩」説在明清時期閱讀實踐中的歷程。

11606621.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11606621.value: 在香港打擊基於圖像的濫用行为

11606621.label: Project Objectives
11606621.value: This project will investigate and provide evidence about how cases involving image based abuse could be, are being and should be dealt with in the criminal justice system in Hong Kong. The project will demonstrate that the currently available legal responses are not adequate to address the harms caused by image based abuse. This project will make recommendations for reform based on the evidence of how cases of image based abuse currently could and are being dealt with in Hong Kong The project aims to develop recommendations for reform that will improve legal response to image based abuse in Hong Kong to better protect victims and society from image based abuse. The project aims to benefit the international community by adding to public debate about how best to respond to image based abuse.

11606621.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11606621.value: New communication technologies have created opportunities to create, discover, gather and share information. This has enabled new forms of image based abuse that violate a person’s sexual autonomy, privacy and dignity. At present there has not been a comprehensive study of how cases involving image based abuse could be, are being and should be dealt with in the criminal justice system in Hong Kong. Available information suggests that the current responses in the criminal justice system are not appropriate to meet the harms presented by image based abuse. Hong Kong has no specific laws to address image based abuse. Until 2019 some of these behaviours were prosecuted under s. 161 of the Crimes Ordinance Cap. 200 (access to computer with criminal or dishonest intent). However, in Secretary for Justice v Cheng Ka Yee [2019] HKCFA 9 the Court of Final Appeal closed the door on using this offence in most cases. Immediately following this decision, the Law Reform Commission of Hong Kong published a report recommending new offences to criminalise voyeurism (using a device to view a person’s private parts or a person engaging in a private act) and upskirting (recording images of a person’s private parts). This report did not consider the need to criminalise other related image abuse behaviours, such as ‘revenge pornography’ (non-consensual distribution of intimate images). There is therefore a gap in existing law and in reform recommendations. This project will fill these gaps by investigating how image based abuse behaviours could, are and should be dealt with in the criminal justice system in Hong Kong. Research of legal databases will reveal what offences are available for responding to image based abuse and what evidence there is that the offences have been used. A quantitative survey will be conducted with stakeholders (solicitors, barristers, members of the magistracy and judiciary and victim support and advocacy groups) to find out whether and how these cases are dealt with in practice. Qualitative interviews with stakeholders will provide deeper and richer context to the survey responses. This research will reveal what types of behaviour have been subject to prosecution, for what offences and under what circumstances. Finally, based on these findings, a comparative review of legal responses in other jurisdictions and feedback from stakeholders, suggestions for reform in Hong Kong will be advanced to prevent such behaviours, better protect victims of image based abuse and benefit Hong Kong Society. 新的通信技術為創建、發現、收集和共享信息創造了機會。在利用這些機會的同時也催生了基於圖像的新形式濫用行為；這些濫用行為侵犯了一個人的性自主權、隱私和尊嚴。目前，並沒有針對涉及濫用圖像的案件在香港的刑事司法系統內部可以、正在和應該如何處理的全面研究。現有信息表明，目前刑事司法系統提供的應對措施與基於圖像濫用行為所帶來的危害並不相匹配。香港尚沒有專門的法律來處理基於圖像的濫用行為。直到 2019 年，其中一些濫用行為根據《刑事罪行條例 – 第200章》第 161 條（有犯罪或不誠實意圖而取用電腦）予以起訴。然而，在Secretary of Justice v Cheng Ka Yee [2019] HKCFA 9 一案中，終審法院關閉了在大多數情況下借用第161條發起控訴的大門。自該案件後，香港法律改革委員會隨即發布一項報告，建議將偷窺行為（使用設備查看某人的私處或查看從事私人行為的人）和掀裙行為（錄製某人私處的圖像）定為新的犯罪行為。但是，該報告並沒有考慮將其他相關的圖像濫用行為定義為刑事犯罪行為的必要性，譬如“色情報復行為”（未經同意分發私密圖像）。因此，現行法律和改革建議之間依然存在一段差距。該項目通過調查香港刑事司法系統可以、正在和應該如何處理基於圖像的濫用行為來填補上述提到的製度空白。對法律數據庫的研究可以揭示出哪些罪行可以適用於基於圖像的濫用行為，以及有何種證據表明這些罪行確實已經被應用。對利益相關者（事務律師、訴訟律師、裁判官和司法機構成員以及受害者支持和倡導團體）進行定量調查，可以查明此類濫用案件是否以及如何在實踐中獲得處理。對利益相關者進行的定性訪談可以為調研回復提供更加深入及豐富的背景資料。這項研究將揭示哪些類型的行為已經受到起訴，基於何種罪行以及在何種情況下受到起訴。最後，基於上述調查結果，以及對其他司法管轄區域的法律回應及利益相關者反饋的比較研究，本項目將提出立足於香港本地的改革建議以防止此類行為的再次發生，以求為遭受圖像濫用行為的受害者提供更強有力的保護和造福整個香港社會。

11607021.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11607021.value: 表演与场所：人类世的戏剧制作

11607021.label: Project Objectives
11607021.value: To critically analyze an emerging body of drama and performance that engages with ecological questions and contextualize it within political, social, scholarly and artistic conversations around issues such as climate-induced displacement, environmental justice, and urbanization. To highlight the extent to which ecological crises require a form of thinking that is interdisciplinary, transnational, and transcultural and foreground the role of performance in developing that form of thinking. To contribute new lines of research in ecocriticism relating to the role of intermedial, intercultural, and international collaborations in expanding ecological awareness and translating global issues, such as climate change, into meaningful, comprehensible narratives. To define a placed-based ecologically oriented pedagogy that connects the concepts and critical thinking of the seminar room with the aesthetic and technical experiments of performance and media design practices. To organize and present a public talk and symposium on ecological issues relevant to Hong Kong theatre artists and public.

To highlight the extent to which ecological crises require a form of thinking that is interdisciplinary, transnational, and transcultural and foreground the role of performance in developing that form of thinking.

To define a placed-based ecologically oriented pedagogy that connects the concepts and critical thinking of the seminar room with the aesthetic and technical experiments of performance and media design practices.
To organize and present a public talk and symposium on ecological issues relevant to Hong Kong theatre artists and public.

11607021.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11607021.value: Science studies scholar Bruno Latour and biologist Neil Everndon, among others, emphasize the role of the arts in translating environmental data into accessible narratives (Everndon 1978, 102; Latour 2016; see also Heise 2016). Artists can act as cultural mediators, using their skills of storytelling to cultivate sensitivity to the scope and implications of complex phenomena, such as climate change. The proposed project will examine an emerging body of drama and performance that engages with ecological issues through a focus on place. The project is unique in its focus on place as a dramatic element, its transnational scope, and its inclusion of both stage drama and site-specific performances, which are seldom examined together. The case studies chosen include theatre-makers from the US, Germany, Belgium, and Taiwan, whose works are produced through transnational collaborations and circulate internationally. They are: Frances Ya-Chu Cowhig; Idris Goodwin; Sarah Cameron Sunde; Rimini Protokoll; Kris Verdonck/A Two Dogs Company; Laurie Anderson and Hsin-Chien Huang; and U-Theatre’s Ecological Base. Place is presented by these artists not as inert backdrop to human action, but as a central actor, and theatre, as a medium, is expanded, with performances taking place on the stage, street, ocean, mountaintop, and a virtual moonscape. The analysis of these works will be organized around three spatial paradigms that have defined human-place relationships during the Anthropocene: landscape, environment, and network. Historically, these paradigms chart changing relationships between humans and place: from stable local scenes seen at a distance, to enveloping natural and cultural surroundings, to a meshwork of social and technological connections. This project builds on my research in contemporary drama and ecological performance to explore the various ways that drama can model more sustainable relationships between humans and the places they inhabit. Furthermore, it will examine how performance technologies sensitize audiences to the temporal scope and geographical scale of ecological issues. The methodology of the project will be aligned with current practices in theatre and performance studies, which includes a critical analysis of performances and their contexts, interdisciplinary research, and interviews with theatre-makers, which will provide valuable insights into the production of these works and the larger social and ethical issues at stake. The data collected from research will be published in two journal articles and culminate in a scholarly monograph. It will also be applied in my work as a teacher-scholar in Hong Kong through public talks, teacher workshops, and collaborations with local theatre artists. 科学研究学者 Bruno Latour 和生物学家 Neil Everndon 等人强调艺术在将环境数据转化为可访问的叙述方面的作用（Everndon 1978, 102；Latour 2016；另见 Heise 2016）。艺术家可以充当文化调解人，利用他们讲故事的技巧来培养对复杂现象（例如气候变化）的范围和影响的敏感性。 拟议的项目将研究一种新兴的戏剧和表演体系，这些戏剧和表演通过对地方的关注来处理生态问题。该项目的独特之处在于其将地方作为戏剧元素的关注点、跨国范围以及包含很少一起审查的舞台剧和特定地点的表演。选择的案例研究包括来自美国、德国、比利时和台湾的戏剧制作人，他们的作品通过跨国合作制作并在国际上流通。他们是：Frances Ya-Chu Cowhig；伊德里斯·古德温；莎拉·卡梅伦·孙德；里米尼协议； Kris Verdonck/A Two Dogs Company； Laurie Anderson 和 Hsin-Chien Huang；和U-Theatre的生态基地。这些艺术家所呈现的地方不是作为人类行为的惰性背景，而是作为一个核心演员，而作为一种媒介的剧院得到了扩展，在舞台、街道、海洋、山顶和虚拟的月球景观中进行表演。 这些作品的分析将围绕三个空间范式进行组织，这些范式定义了人类世期间的人与地关系：景观、环境和网络。从历史上看，这些范式描绘了人类与地方之间不断变化的关系：从远处看到的稳定的当地场景，到包围的自然和文化环境，再到社会和技术联系的网络。这个项目建立在我对当代戏剧和生态表演的研究的基础上，探索戏剧可以通过各种方式模拟人类与其居住地之间更可持续的关系。此外，它将研究表演技术如何使观众对生态问题的时间范围和地理范围敏感。 该项目的方法将与戏剧和表演研究的当前实践保持一致，其中包括对表演及其背景的批判性分析、跨学科研究以及对戏剧制作人的采访，这将为这些作品的制作提供宝贵的见解和更大的社会和道德问题处于危险之中。这项研究将产生两篇期刊文章和我的第二本专着。它也将通过公开演讲、中学教师工作坊以及与当地戏剧艺术家的合作，应用到我作为香港教师学者的工作中。

11607921.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11607921.value: 外籍家庭傭工與香港的量刑

11607921.label: Co - Investigator(s)
11607921.value: Dr MANIKIS, Marie Dr TOMASSETTI, Julia Louise

11607921.label: Project Objectives
11607921.value: To assess whether Foreign Domestic Helpers are sentenced more or less severely in the Hong Kong trial courts when compared with similarly situated offenders committing the same offences. To assess whether or not employers who commit offences against their Foreign Domestic Helpers are sentenced more leniently in the Hong Kong trial courts when compared with similarly situated offenders committing the same offences. To discover the most important determinants of sentencing quantum in the Hong Kong Magistrates Courts within major offence categories. To interrogate the language used by Hong Kong District Court and Court of First Instance judges when referring to crimes committed by Foreign Domestic Helpers, and crimes committed against Foreign Domestic Helpers by their employers. To propose novel policy solutions to the disadvantage experienced by Foreign Domestic Helpers within Hong Kong's institutional framework, including the criminal justice system. To pave the way methodologically and paradigmatically for further research on the treatment of ethnic minorities and migrant workers within Hong Kong's criminal justice system.

To assess whether or not employers who commit offences against their Foreign Domestic Helpers are sentenced more leniently in the Hong Kong trial courts when compared with similarly situated offenders committing the same offences.
To discover the most important determinants of sentencing quantum in the Hong Kong Magistrates Courts within major offence categories.

To interrogate the language used by Hong Kong District Court and Court of First Instance judges when referring to crimes committed by Foreign Domestic Helpers, and crimes committed against Foreign Domestic Helpers by their employers.
