12202021.label: Major findings and research outcome
12202021.value: 1. Data-driven Air Pollution Estimation Our research used machine learning (ML) to enhance air pollution monitoring and prediction. Zhou et al.(2022) and Zhang et al. (2023b) applied proper orthogonal decomposition (POD)-based sensor placement algorithms, identifying the QR pivot algorithm as superior for optimizing PM 2.5 and methane monitoring site locations, outperforming existing China National Environmental Monitoring Center sites by prioritizing severe pollution areas. Yang et al.(2023) developed a multi-output random forest (MORF) model, achieving simultaneous hourly predictions of six pollutants (PM 2.5, PM10, O3, NO2, CO, SO2) with a high R2 of 0.94, improving efficiency over single-output models and enabling detailed spatial-temporal analyses. synthesized progress and uncertainties in aerosol formation, radiation, and cloud interactions. Xiong et al. (2025) synthesizes recent advances in aerosol formation modeling, with particular emphasis on the integration of satellite observations with machine learning techniques. 2. Interactions Between Air Pollution and Meteorology Our studies elucidate meteorological influences on air pollution. Zhang et al.(2023a) used quantile regression to model PM 2.5 in Indian megacities, predicting increased exceedances in northern cities under SSP585 due to stagnant conditions, with improvements in southern cities due to higher boundary layer heights. Zhang et al.(2022) identified surface winds and humidity as key drivers of PM 2.5 extremes, with projections of worsening conditions in China’s key regions under SSP5-8.5. Zhang et al.(2024) linked early South China Sea summer monsoon onset to elevated O3 in southern China. Wang et al.(2024a) attributed declining dust loading in West and South Asia to Arctic amplification, altering atmospheric circulation. Wang et al.(2022) showed aerosol pollution’s varying impact on Beijing’s urban heat island intensity, modulated by wind direction. Wang and Gao (2025) demonstrated precipitation responses to reduced aerosol emissions. 3. Compound Climate-Pollution Extremes and Health Risks Xiao et al.(2022) identified a rising frequency of heat and O3 co-extremes in China’s Beijing–Tianjin–Hebei and Yangtze River Delta, with a 7.0% increase in joint exceedances. Wang et al.(2024b) reported spatially heterogeneous wet bulb temperature trends, projecting widespread thermal stress in eastern China. Gao et al.(2023) clarified the role of sea surface temperature on co-occurrence of heat wave and O3 pollution in China, and further developed seasonal prediction models. Gao et al. (2024) found intensified co-occurrences of heat and air pollution extremes in both China and India, despite reductions in projected emissions and improved air quality. Xiao et al.(2024) linked maternal exposure to urban heat islands to increased preterm birth risk.

12202021.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12202021.value: For machine learning applications, expanding the multi-output random forest (MORF) model to include additional pollutants and global datasets could enhance its scalability. We will explore hybrid models combining MORF with deep learning (e.g., CNNs, LSTMs) to handle complex, non-linear pollution interactions. In studies of air pollution-meteorology interactions, further exploration of climate change scenarios and extreme weather events will be beneficial for projections of air pollutants. For health impacts, studies on chronic exposure and multi-pollutant interactions could strengthen causal inferences. Expanding cohort studies to other regions would validate findings like preterm birth risks. Cross-disciplinary collaborations, using big data and policy integration, will drive actionable outcomes for air quality management and public health.

12202021.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12202021.value: This research project aims to improve our understanding and tracking of air pollution, particularly PM2.5, across Asia, using advanced technology and data analysis. The team used machine learning and model simulations, to carefully select the best locations for air quality sensors and develop highly accurate predictions for multiple pollutants, such as PM2.5, ozone, and methane. This approach allows us to pinpoint exactly where and when pollution spikes happen, giving a clearer picture of air quality trends. They also delved into how weather patterns influence pollution, revealing how monsoon seasons or long-term climate changes can either worsen air quality in some areas or improve it in others, depending on regional conditions. Most importantly, the research sheds light on critical health risks, showing how the combination of heat and pollution can negatively affect pregnant women-potentially leading to preterm births-or heighten stress and discomfort in densely populated urban zones. This work is incredibly valuable because it delivers reliable, detailed data that empowers governments to craft smarter pollution control strategies, safeguard public health, and prepare for future climate challenges. By doing so, it paves the way for cleaner air, healthier living conditions, and stronger, safer communities for everyone.

12202221.label: Realisation of objectives
12202221.value: The project objectives have been successfully achieved. To develop efficient federated analytics techniques for nearest neighbor search with difficult-to-compute distance functions (e.g., vector, sequence, or graph similarity), we have proposed the FedKNN system that supports secure federated k-nearest neighbor (kNN) search queries with a wide range of similarity measures. Our system introduces a Distribution-Aware kNN (DANN) algorithm to reduce unnecessary local computations while ensuring that no original data is shared across parties or with third parties. The core idea is to estimate the approximate distribution of query results over the private data of each party through a fast pre-processing round. This enables each party to compute local kNNs with different k values independently, thereby minimizing local computations. We show that the expected complexity of DANN is close to the theoretical optimum and superior to the baseline solution. Furthermore, to protect private information during query processing, we have enhanced DANN with differential privacy techniques and have further developed a differentially private variant, DANN*, which incorporates differential privacy. We also provide a detailed security analysis. Compared with the state-of-the-art solution, our approach satisfies differential obliviousness and can offer provable privacy guarantees for each participant. We have implemented a FedKNN prototype system and conducted extensive evaluations on various types of datasets. The results show that FedKNN outperforms the current state-of-the-art solutions by up to 4.8x in accuracy on federated graph kNN search and up to 2.7x in accuracy on federated sequence kNN search. Our experiments also demonstrate that, even when adding differential privacy, our approach can provide strong privacy guarantees with only a small additional overhead. An alternative approach to accelerate kNN search involves using approximation techniques to find the approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) while still ensuring error guarantees. While the proximity graph (PG) has traditionally served as the primary index for ANN search, existing PG-based methods face challenges such as high time complexity or a lack of performance guarantees for search results. To address these limitations, we have developed a novel t-monotonic graph (t-MG) that exhibits a distinctive t-monotonic property. We prove that if the distance between a query q and its true nearest neighbor is at most a constant t, then search conducted on t-MG guarantees the retrieval of the exact nearest neighbor for q. Notably, the time complexity of our search approach is lower than that of all existing PG-based methods. Extensive experiments conducted on well-known real-world datasets demonstrate the superiority of our approach over existing methods, in that our techniques provide faster and more accurate kNN search results. In addition, we have conducted research on privacy-preserving localized graph pattern query processing in an outsourcing paradigm. These queries, known as LGPQs, encompass a diverse range of semantics, including subgraph homomorphism, subgraph isomorphism, and strong simulation. Each matched graph pattern is contained within a subgraph referred to as a ball, which adheres to a predefined size restriction. To meet the need for privacy-preserving query services for LGPQs, we have developed a framework, called Prilo, which allows users to securely retrieve query results while preserving their privacy. Furthermore, we propose an enhanced version of the framework called Prilo∗, which incorporates a bloom filter specifically designed for trees using trusted secure hardware. It also utilizes a query-oblivious twiglet-based technique to efficiently eliminate non-answers and introduces a secure retrieval scheme for balls, allowing users to obtain query results more quickly. Additionally, we have developed distributed core decomposition algorithms for large directed graphs and bipartite graphs, enabling efficient and scalable computation of core decompositions in distributed computing environments.

Develop index-based data access and query processing algorithms to collaboratively answer analytics queries;
Design new differentially private query techniques to optimize system performance.

12202221.label: Major findings and research outcome
12202221.value: We have proposed FedKNN, a secure federated k-nearest neighbor (kNN) search system that supports complex distance functions (e.g., vector, sequence, graph similarity) without sharing raw data. FedKNN introduces the Distribution-Aware kNN (DANN) algorithm to minimize local computation via a fast pre-processing round that estimates result distributions, achieving near-optimal complexity. An enhanced differentially private variant, DANN*, provides strong privacy guarantees with minimal overhead, outperforming state-of-the-art solutions by up to 4.8x on graph and 2.7x on sequence tasks. Additionally, we developed t-monotonic graphs (t-MG) for faster exact ANN search with provable guarantees, a privacy-preserving LGPQ framework (Prilo/Prilo*), and distributed core decomposition algorithms for large graphs. The research findings have been published in esteemed conferences and journals, including VLDB 2022, ICDE 2023, SIGMOD 2023, and PACMMOD 2024.

12202221.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12202221.value: For further development, we will explore methods to extend FedKNN to dynamic federated settings, where parties can join or leave the collaboration and data distributions evolve over time, requiring adaptive distribution estimation and incremental updates to the DANN algorithm. We also plan to incorporate advanced cryptographic primitives (e.g., fully homomorphic encryption or secure multi-party computation) to support even stronger privacy notions while maintaining practical efficiency for complex similarity measures. Another direction is to generalize the t-monotonic graph framework to support approximate kNN search with tunable (1+ε)-approximation guarantees and provably sublinear query time across arbitrary metric spaces. Furthermore, we intend to enhance the Prilo/Prilo∗ framework by integrating zero-knowledge proofs for verifiable LGPQ results in decentralized outsourcing scenarios and by extending it to streaming or temporal graphs. Finally, we will investigate distributed core decomposition algorithms on heterogeneous computing environments (e.g., GPU clusters and edge devices) and explore their applications in large-scale graph machine learning pipelines.

12202221.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12202221.value: Federated technologies have emerged as a promising solution for collaborative analytics on decentralized sensitive data without compromising privacy. However, current federated data analytics systems either focus on simple aggregates or suffer from excessive computation and communication overhead when handling complex queries, such as k-nearest neighbor searches across private datasets using challenging similarity measures (e.g., vectors, sequences, or graphs). To address these challenges, we have developed a secure federated k-nearest neighbor search system, named FedKNN, which dramatically reduces unnecessary local computations through an efficient pre-processing step that estimates the distribution of potential results across parties without ever sharing raw data. We also introduced a privacy-enhanced variant that incorporates differential privacy, providing strong protection with only minor performance overhead. In addition, we designed t-monotonic graphs, a novel indexing structure that enables faster and more accurate approximate nearest-neighbor searches with rigorous theoretical guarantees; developed Prilo and its enhanced version Prilo*, a privacy-preserving framework for complex localized graph pattern queries in outsourced settings; and proposed efficient distributed algorithms for core decomposition on massive directed and bipartite graphs. Together, these advances enable practical, private, and scalable similarity-based analytics across organizations.

12202321.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12202321.value: 香港大氣 PM2.5 中有機磷阻燃劑的化學表徵、來源解析和健康影響

12202321.label: Project Objectives
12202321.value: Develop and optimize a novel and sensitive analytical method to characterize organophosphate flame retardants (OPFRs) in PM2.5 using atmospheric pressure gas chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (APGC-MS/MS). Validate the sample preparation protocols and the detection limit, accuracy, and precision of the developed APGC-MS/MS method. ---- The adverse health effects of PM2.5 pollution are mainly related to its chemical composition and sources. Regarding the toxic substances in PM2.5, PAHs and heavy metals are the two groups of compounds that have been most intensively studied; yet for the emerging organic pollutants, such as organophosphate flame retardants (OPFRs), information on their contamination profiles, sources, and chemical transformations in the atmosphere is still limited. Previous studies have applied GC-EI-MS to analyze OPFRs in the environment. However, given that many OPFRs congeners exist in the air at trace levels, the inadequate specificity and sensitivity of the conventional GC-MS method will limit the investigation capability on the whole contamination profiles of OPFRs as well as their fate and transformation in the atmosphere. Therefore, in this project, we plan to use APGC-MS/MS to develop a novel analytical technique to analyze PM2.5-bound OPFRs with better sensitivity and specificity. We will optimize the sample extraction and clean-up protocols, the separation and detection parameters of APGC-MS/MS, and validate the developed method's detection limit, accuracy, and precision. Identify and quantify OPFRs in 60 PM2.5 samples collected in Hong Kong during a 1-yr period. Investigate the contamination profiles and seasonal variations of PM2.5-bound OPFRs in the region. ---- Several studies have reported the ambient levels of OPFRs in PM2.5 samples collected in several cities in China, Sweden, Canada, Turkey, and Pakistan. However, the characterization of PM2.5-bound OPFRs has never been conducted in Hong Kong. Here we will collect PM2.5 samples at Hong Kong Baptist University every six days for a 1-yr period. A series of PM2.5-bound OPFRs will be identified and quantified using APGC-MS/MS, including the chloro-, alkyl-, and acryl-substituted OPFRs (Cl-OPFRs, alkyl-OPFRs, and acryl-OPFRs). This will be the first study on the measurements of PM2.5-bound OPFRs in Hong Kong. Characterize chemical markers of various PM2.5 emission sources, including elemental carbon, heavy metals, and organic tracers of primary anthropogenic sources. Apply positive matrix factorization to identify the major emission sources of OPFRs and quantitatively estimate the individual source contributions to OPFRs in Hong Kong. ---- Source apportionment of PM2.5-bound OPFRs offers valuable clues in understanding how these pollutants enter the air environment and affect human health. A few previous studies tried to explore the sources of OPFRs by conducting simple correlation analysis and principal component analysis of individual OPFRs. However, due to the lack of whole contamination profiles of OPFRs and source maker data, very limited source information was obtained. In this study, we will perform a positive matrix factorization (PMF) analysis of the measured OPFRs with the help of specific markers of various emission sources. Given that OPFRs are synthetic compounds from anthropogenic activities, we will measure markers from industry, vehicle exhaust, e-waste recycling, marine vessels, biomass burning, and secondary formation on PM2.5. With these unique source markers input into PMF, together with OPFRs, we can obtain not only a more accurate source identification of PM2.5-bound OPFRs but also a quantitative estimation of the individual source contributions to OPFRs in Hong Kong. Perform a preliminary health risk assessment of OPFRs through PM2.5 inhalation. ---- Previous studies have observed the adverse effects of certain OPFRs on heart development and reproduction in zebrafish and the carcinogenic and neurotoxic effects of several Cl-OPFRs. Therefore, given the ubiquitous presence of OPFRs in PM2.5, the adverse health effect induced upon exposure to OPFRs via PM2.5 inhalations is of public concern. Based on the ambient levels of OPFRs obtained in objective 2, we plan to perform a preliminary health risk assessment of OPFRs by estimating their daily intake by different age groups of people through PM2.5 inhalations. We will then estimate the hazard quotient of individual OPFRs and provide insights into the associated health impact.

12202621.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12202621.value: 醫學圖像很複雜，到目前為止，我們仍然依靠醫學專家對其進行檢查以進行診斷。然而，有時醫學影像報告容易出錯，尤其是在人員短缺和工作量過高的情況下。因此，計算機輔助報告系統顯然是有幫助的，特別是如果報告可以自動生成以供醫生核實。與其他文本生成應用程序相比，生成醫療報告的關鍵問題是報告的臨床準確性。最近，使用精心構建的知識圖譜和採用混合檢索-生成模型被發現很有前景，同時也帶來了新的研究挑戰，包括構建的知識圖譜可能是次優的，檢索模塊響應捕獲句子語義的有效性。 在這個項目中，我們開發算法來解決潛在的挑戰，目標是提高臨床準確性並將它們集成為一個完整的醫學圖像報告生成系統。我們採用深度生成模型方法，目的是總體上實現良好的泛化性能。特別是，我們將開發一個具有異常屬性知識圖譜的深度生成模型，以便可以捕獲異常的更詳細方面，從而使生成更準確的臨床報告成為可能。此外，我們將開發一種計算方法，以根據通常帶有不完整信息標記的醫學圖像報告自動推斷異常屬性知識圖譜的結構。為了利用從現有醫療報告中檢索到的相關句子來幫助生成報告，句子語義是關鍵。我們將採用對比性自學習方法來更好地捕捉醫學報告中句子的語義。所有提出的方法都將基於多個基準數據集進行評估。我們也會開發相關的軟件包，並通過GitHub共享。我們已經組建了一個跨學科研究團隊，他們擁有健康數據分析、自然語言處理和放射學方面的專業知識，這對於識別關鍵問題和評估系統的有效性至關重要。

12202621.label: Realisation of objectives
12202621.value: All the objectives have been 100% achieved. Objective 1: To develop a deep generative model with an attributed knowledge graph of abnormality for medical image report generation to enhance the clinical accuracy of the generated report. Based on the idea outlined in the proposal, we developed a novel deep generative model together with an attributed knowledge graph of abnormality (ATAG) as its major component for generation medical reports based on input X-ray images [TMI’23]. Graph attention networks are adopted to encode the relationships among the abnormalities and their attributes. The embeddings of the ATAG (including abnormality embeddings and attribute embeddings) are learned as part of a deep model based on an encoder-decoder architecture for medical image report generation. Noticing that it is important to align the ATAG’s embedding for encoding the abnormalities and the decoder’s embedding for generating the report, we further introduced a hierarchical attention and a gating mechanism. For the decoder, we tested both RNN and Transformer and demonstrate that introducing ATAG can enhance the clinical accuracy of the generated report [TMI’23]. Other than graph attention networks, VAE-based model (e.g., variational graph autoencoder) can also be adopted for computing the representations like ATAG. However, training VAE models is known to be suffering from the posterior collapse issue as stated in the proposal, we managed to demonstrate that a novel mutual information neural estimation approach is effective in training VAE-based models with a more sophisticated latent variable structure for both text and image generation [TPAMI’23]. Objective 2: To develop a computational methodology to automatically infer the structure of the attributed knowledge graph of abnormality based on medical image reports with incomplete label information. The ATAG mentioned in Objective 1 consists of interconnected abnormality nodes and attribute nodes so that more fine-grained abnormality details can be captured. Instead of constructing them manually like the existing methods, we propose a methodology to automatically construct the fine-grained graph structure based on annotated X-ray reports and the RadLex radiology lexicon (RadLex.org). We constructed graph structures with different sizes for our later evaluation. Based on the IU XRay dataset, we constructed ATAGs with 23-41 abnormalities and 64-106 attributes. Based on MIMIC CXR dataset, we constructed ATAGs with 26-47 abnormalities and 129-209 attributes. We then incorporate each of them into the overall framework as detailed under Objective 1 so that the overall deep generative model can be learned [TMI’23]. In addition to the incomplete label information, we, on top of what being mentioned in the proposal, considered also the incomplete/missing modality settings where X-ray images and clinical events like lab test results are typically available at different time. We contributed to the development of the algorithms named DDL-CXR [NeurIPS’24] and DiPro [NeurIPS’25b] to tackle the situation. DDL-CXR addresses the missing X-ray image problem by generating them using diffusion models, which was found to be effective in enhancing the overall prediction accuracy. Instead of generating the missing modality, DiPro addresses the problem by temporally aligning the clinical events and records of X-ray images by learning modality-specific representations via spatiotemporal disentanglement. Objective 3: To develop a contrastive representation learning method for better capturing the semantics of sentences in medical reports and extend the proposed deep generative model to a hybrid retrieval-generation one by adding a template sentence retrieval module. The retrieval-based approach where existing reports in the corpus relevant to the input are identified to assist the report generation has been found promising. We referred to radiologists’ diagnostic steps of examining an X-ray image where anatomical and diagnostic details are typically focused, and developed a novel hierarchical visual concept representation called anatomy-aware hierarchical vision encoding (AHIVE) [CVPR’24]. To learn AHIVE, we derived a methodology to extract hierarchical diagnostic descriptions from radiology reports and develop a CLIP-based framework for the model training. Also, the hierarchical architecture of AHIVE can support interactive report retrieval so that report revision made at one layer can be propagated to the subsequent ones to trigger other necessary revisions. During our investigation, we also found that properly modelling the expression of uncertainty in radiology reports is unavoidable if the clinical accuracy is to be further enhanced. To incorporate uncertainty awareness, we further developed two algorithms named DiagUE [MICCAI-WS’24] and CURV [NeurIPS’25a]. DiagUE models three identified sources of uncertainties and aggregates them using an uncertainty embedding, which is then used together with the visual embedding for report generation. CURV achieves that by leveraging the uncertainty descriptions in ImaGenome dataset to train a Vision-Language Model with reasoning using a three-stage training pipeline that combines uncertainty-aware fine-tuning, reasoning initialization, and reinforcement learning. Objective 4: To evaluate the proposed deep generative models based on a number of benchmark datasets. We will also develop a related software package to be shared via github. Extensive experiments have been conducted based on the two publicly available datasets IU XRay and MIMIC CXR to demonstrate their effectiveness of different approaches adopted in the proposed algorithms. The performance metrics include both clinical accuracy and language quality. We proposed a new metric named Radiology Report Quality Index F1 score (RadRQI-F1) with the objective to achieve more reliable and fine-grained evaluation, where the RadLex lexicon and RadGraph were leveraged. 12202621.label: Major findings and research outcome
12202621.value: A set of deep generative models for X-ray report generation were developed by exploring various approaches with the ultimate goal to push forward the state-of-the-art performance of X-ray diagnostic reporting. They include: i) ATAG [TMI’23] was the first deep generative model that leverages the RadLex ontology to incorporate an automatically created attributed knowledge graph of abnormality as its major component for generating X-ray reports. This demonstrates that learning a abnormality graph embedding is effective to better capture the visual information; ii) InfoMaxHVAE [TPAMI’23] was the first attempt to learn hierarchical VAEs by directly optimizing the mutual information between the input and the VAE’s latent variable, which is applicable to learning more effective visual encoders; iii) AHIVE [CVPR’24] was the first attempt that incorporates the systemic approach of examining an X-ray image adopted by radiologists into the design of the visual encoder for guiding an iterative visual extraction process, where the RadLex ontology was again used for making the hierarchical encoding possible; iv) DiagUE [MICCAI-WS’24] was the first attempt that represents three types of uncertainties encountered in X-ray report generation as an aggregated uncertainty embedding to incorporate uncertainty-awareness into the report generation, which turns out to be effective in enhancing report generation quality; v) CURV [NeurIPS’25a] was the first work that successfully fine-tuned a vision-language model (VLM) using self-supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning (GRPO) with uncertainty awareness and reasoning capability incorporated to achieve improvements on both report generation accuracy and explainability. v) DDL-CXR [NeurIPS’24] was the first work that demonstrated the feasibility of generating missing X-ray images for enhancing the performance of prediction. vii) DiPro [NeurIPS’25b] successfully learns to disentangle and align the representations of irregular records of EHR time series and X-rays instead of generating the missing modality. The effectiveness of all the proposed methods were demonstrated via extensive empirical evaluation using the benchmark datasets MIMIC-CXR and IU X-ray datasets. The following lists the key takeaways which have been shown effective for X-ray report generation: i) Adopting attributed abnormality graph embedding for visual encoder design; ii) Mimicking radiologists’ systematic approach as prior knowledge for visual encoder design; iii) Uncertainty awareness and reasoning steps of diagnosis to be learned via SFT and RL; iv) Generating missing X-ray images using diffusion models; and v) Spatiotemporal alignment of X-ray images and other modalities in EHR.

12202621.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12202621.value: In this project, we have demonstrated that, by properly incorporating prior knowledge related to radiology image interpretation with careful design of training algorithms, effective deep generation models can be learned for high quality image report generation. It forms a solid foundation for designing and training vision-language models (VLMs) for radiology report generation. For future extensions, one importance direction is to see how reliability and explainability can be incorporated into the model to increase chance of adoption by radiologists for integrating into the clinical workflow. Along this line, it will also be interested to see how to enable interactions between the radiologists and a report generation “agent" for realising human-AI collaborative diagnosis. In addition, the algorithms developed in this project can be further extended to other radiology images, e.g., CT and cardiac MRI, where prior knowledge of the specific modalities should be further leveraged. The PI and Co-I (Dr. Keith Chiu) have been discussing the extension work and started some initial investigation. Recently, we have submitted another research proposal on the topic. For real-world deployment, the suite of algorithms we developed and their future extensions provide us the solid ground work to explore related applied research funding and/or deployment opportunities.

12202621.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12202621.value: AI has been transforming future healthcare, where radiology image analytics is one of the most promising application areas. This project focuses on automatic radiology report generation using deep learning models. Different approaches, including incorporating prior medical knowledge, mimicking radiologists’ best practices, various deep model training and fine-tuning algorithms, etc., have been investigated to how they can be effectively adopted to enhance the quality of the generated reports. A suite of algorithms have been developed and rigorously evaluated using benchmark datasets. Due to their originality and rigor of the studies, they have been resulted in seven high quality publications, with the publication venues including IEEE TMI, TPAMI, CVPR, and NeurIPS. PI has been invited to present the findings of the projects in different overseas universities, including McGill University, Queen’s University, University of Sheffield and University of Manchester, among others. The foundation established via this project can lead to future development, including extension to other modalities of radiology images, enhancing the deep models’ reliability and explainability, as well as enabling human-AI collaborative diagnosis for report preparation. The PI is also exploring different applied research funding opportunities to convert the suite of algorithms developed for real-world deployment.

12300021.label: Project Objectives
12300021.value: To develop facile and efficient solid-phase synthetic protocols of novel water-soluble/stable luminescent lanthanide–stapled peptides (Ln-SPs) via N/C-terminal and sidechain functionalizations and ligations on amino acids at specific sites; To synthesize and characterize Ln-SPs of different macrocyclic ligands, sensitization antennae and stapling linkers combinatorially with our libraries of bladder cancer-targeting peptides based on the above-established protocols; To conduct comprehensive stability (e.g. peptide/complex stability), photophysical (e.g. brightness & lifetime), in vitro biological (e.g. cytotoxicity, selectivity, binding affinity & localization cell imaging), and computational (e.g. conformational a‑helical dynamics & protein-peptide interactions) studies of bladder cancer-targeting Ln-SPs and compare the results with the non-stapled controls, setting the world-first Ln-SP-benchmark parameters; To evaluate the overall in vivo performance of Ln-SPs as potential novel multifunctional bladder cancer-specific theranostics for preclinical translations.

12300021.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12300021.value: Protein-protein interactions (PPIs) are predominant in the underlying mechanism of most cellular processes, and the pathological variants are no exception. Peptides hold tremendous promises as therapeutics as PPI inhibitors due to their larger binding surface areas with target specificity, modular scalable synthesis of structural/functional tunability, and potentially less toxicity. However, their metabolic instability, weak binding affinity affected by conformational flexibility, and poor cell permeability hamper their further direct clinical applications and translations. Recently, several technological approaches to helical peptide stabilization to address the above-mentioned drawbacks via peptide stapling has been developed. Many solution-phase organic synthetic methodologies, e.g. condensations, cross-couplings, C-H activations, and cycloadditions, have been established in both site-specific and combinatorial fashions. In fact, contemporary screenings of stapled peptides of different sequences, lengths, and linkers against specific targets hinge on a trial-and-error basis after each solid-phase peptide synthesis (SPPS), with fluorescent dyes being tediously ligated for bioimaging after multistep transformations and purifications, which is highly inefficient. Bladder cancer (BC) has recently been a global public health concern. Alpha-v and beta-3 (αvβ3) integrin and neurotensin receptor 1 (NTR1), both possessing significant a-helical structural portions, have been reported and recognized as uniquely overexpressed membrane receptors on bladder cancer cells, which can act as attractive specific therapeutic targets against BC. Many of their specific targeting peptide sequences in also a-helical forms have been reported for in vitro/vivo anti-BC studies, serving as good stapling model platforms for enhanced biocompatibilities and bioactivities. In this proposal, we aim to launch an integrative research program to develop the first proof-of-concept, efficient, and purification-economical solid-phase luminescent lanthanide–stapled BC-targeting peptide (Ln-SP) synthetic protocols by formulating/optimizing various novel stapling reactions in SPPS conditions for incorporating luminescent lanthanide complexes either as the N-terminus/backbone or as the staple linker between the side chain of amino acids. To support our hypothesis, FOUR preliminary experiments have been conducted: we had (i) devised a solid-phase assembly approach for installing NOTA at the N-terminus of peptides for accommodating lanthanides; (ii) & (iii) adopted a lysine-based SPPS stapling strategy to cyclize peptide with cyclen linker via double SN2 reactions and for lanthanide coordination; (iv) conducted molecular docking for the a-helix stability–cyclen stapling length relationship. Successes in the proposal will (i) offer new convenient SPPS procedures for multifunctional stapled lanthanide-peptide bioprobes to understand their PPI modulating mechanisms in vitro/vivo, (ii) set world-first databases/benchmarks for novel Ln-SPs’ properties, and (iii) discover and develop new BC-specific theranostic metallopeptidic drugs. 蛋白質交互作用(Protein-protein interactions, PPIs) 在大多數的細胞代謝和病理變異過程中發揮重要作用。多肽具有較大靶標特異性的結合表面積、結構/功能可調的模塊化和可擴展合成、低毒性等特點，因此在 PPI 抑製劑領域具有巨大的應用潛力。然而，代謝不穩定性、構象柔性導致的弱親和力、細胞通透性差等缺陷阻礙了多肽在臨床上的進一步應用和轉化。近年來，已通過多肽裝訂的理念開發出一系列螺旋肽穩定技術方法來解決上述問題。通過採用特定位點和組合方式建立了多種液相有機合成方法，例如：縮合、交叉偶聯、C-H活化和環加成等。當前對於不同序列、長度和連接基團裝訂肽的特定目標篩選主要通過固相多肽合成 (Solid-phase peptide synthesis，SPPS) 試錯法來實現。熒光染料需要在經過多步的轉化和純化後才能被用於生物成像，這使得該過程非常低效。 近年來，膀胱癌 (Bladder cancer，BC) 已經成為了危害全球公共健康的問題之一。 αvβ3 (alpha-v and beta-3) 整聯蛋白和神經降壓素受體1 (neurotensin receptor 1，NTR1) 均具有顯著的α-螺旋結構。因此，其被認為是膀胱癌細胞上獨特的過度表達膜受體，可作為針對膀胱癌的特定治療靶點。許多與其相關的特異性靶向多肽序列呈現出的α-螺旋結構可用於抗膀胱癌的體內外研究，作為用於增強生物相容性和生物活性的模型平台。 在本研究方案中，我們旨在啟動一項綜合研究計劃，以開發首個概念驗證、高效且易純化的固相發光鑭系裝訂的膀胱癌靶向肽 (Ln-SP) 合成方案為目標。通過在 SPPS 條件下配製和優化各種新型釘合反應，將發光鑭系元素配合物作為 N -末端/骨架或作為氨基酸側鏈之間的主要連接基團。我們進行了四個初步實驗以進一步支撐以上方案：（i）設計了一種固相組裝方法，用於在多肽的 N 端引入 NOTA 結構以螯合鑭系離子； (ii) & (iii) 採用基於賴氨酸的 SPPS 裝訂策略，通過兩個雙分子親核取代反應和鑭系元素配位將多肽與 Cyclen 連接基團環化； (iv) 對α-螺旋穩定性和cyclen 裝訂長度之間的關係進行分子對接計算。該提案的成功將 (i)為多功能釘合鑭系多肽生物探針提供一種新穎、便利型SPPS工序，以了解體內外的 PPI 調節機制，(ii) 為新型固相發光鑭系裝訂的膀胱癌靶向肽的特性設置世界首個數據庫和基準，以及 (iii) 尋找和開發新的膀胱癌特異性治療診斷金屬肽藥物。

12300021.label: Realisation of objectives
12300021.value: Objective 1 The project made substantial progress toward this objective by establishing several solid‑phase synthetic methodologies that enable modular and site‑specific functionalization of peptides. A key development was a protocol for constructing trans‑AB2C porphyrin motifs directly on peptide chains through sequential introduction of three simple modules. This approach removed the need for presynthesized porphyrin building blocks, which are typically difficult to prepare and purify. The method was demonstrated across a series of porphyrin–peptide conjugates, showing that the modular “C” component could be varied to introduce additional functional groups without altering the core synthetic sequence. This flexibility allowed the preparation of conjugates with potential utility in bioorthogonal chemistry, nanomaterial surface modification, and peptide‑based polymer design. A further extension of this methodology enabled a resin‑to‑resin ligation strategy, in which two peptide chains were linked through an porphyrin motif formed in situ. This was achieved by employing CTC‑resin‑bound aldehyde–peptide conjugates as the “C” module. The resulting conjugates incorporated functionalities from both peptide chains and the porphyrin core, demonstrating that the method could support more complex architectures. This development directly addressed the objective of enabling ligation at specific sites and provided a new route for constructing multifunctional peptide assemblies. (Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2022, 61, e202207532) In parallel, the project addressed long‑standing challenges in the functionalization of TACN derivatives, which are widely used in metal‑based biomedical applications but are difficult to partially substitute in a controlled manner. By introducing nitrobenzoxadiazole (NBD) as a thiol‑labile protecting group for secondary amines, the team prepared a bis‑NBD‑substituted TACN derivative without requiring strict stoichiometric control or chromatographic purification. This represented a significant simplification relative to traditional methods. Subsequent solid‑phase deprotection enabled the derivatization of TACN–peptide conjugates bearing diverse bioactive sequences and chelating units. This work provided an additional platform for constructing Ln‑SPs and broadened the range of macrocyclic ligands accessible under solid‑phase conditions. (Chemistry Methods 2025, 5, e202400053) All in all, Objective 1 was fully achieved. Objective 2 We developed integrated solid‑phase protocols for constructing porphyrin and corrole motifs directly on resin‑bound peptides. These methods enabled the combinatorial assembly of macrocyclic ligands, sensitization antennae, and stapling linkers with bladder cancer‑targeting peptide sequences. The porphyrin‑based protocol allowed the controlled formation of mono‑, cis/trans‑di‑, and trivalent porphyrin–peptide conjugates from simple aldehydes and dipyrromethanes. Importantly, the entire porphyrin motif was constructed on resin‑bound peptide, and only a single final purification step was required. This represented a substantial improvement over traditional approaches, which typically involve low‑yielding statistical syntheses of prefunctionalized porphyrins followed by multiple rounds of purification after peptide conjugation. This new method enabled rapid and substrate‑controlled diversification of porphyrin–peptide conjugates, supporting the combinatorial synthesis envisioned in the objective. (Adv. Sci. 2025, 12, 2409771) A complementary protocol was developed for corrole–peptide conjugates. By condensing two COOH‑bearing dipyrromethanes onto aldehyde‑bearing peptide chains, the team prepared corrole conjugates with peptide sequences up to 25 residues in length. This method avoided the need for prefunctionalized corrole building blocks, which are difficult to prepare and often incompatible with long peptide sequences. The resulting conjugates exhibited properties suitable for metal chelation, supramolecular assembly, and targeted fluorescence applications. (Chem. Eur. J. 2023, 29, e202203623) Objective 2 was fully achieved. Objective 3 A modular approach using commercially available reagents enabled the preparation of nitrobenzoxadiazole‑ and neodymium‑based peptide probes. These complexes exhibited detectable neodymium emission of sufficient brightness and target‑specific localization in vitro, representing the first example of a stable, water‑soluble, and target‑specific Nd(III) complex suitable for in vitro imaging. This provided a valuable benchmark for photophysical and biological performance. (Adv. Optical Mater. 2024, 12, 2302070) In addition, the solid‑phase strategy for cyclen‑embedded cyclopeptides enabled the preparation of Gd‑based MRI contrast agents and Eu‑based luminescent probes targeting αvβ3 integrin in bladder cancer cells. These systems supported systematic evaluation of stability, brightness, lifetime, cytotoxicity, binding affinity, and cellular localization. Computational studies were conducted to examine conformational dynamics, metal coordination environments, and relaxation mechanisms, providing molecular‑level insights into the behavior of Ln‑SPs relative to non‑stapled controls. (Small Methods 2024, 8, 2400006) Objective 3 was fully achieved. Objective 4 We designed and synthesized a dual‑modal PET/MRI probe, PGaLGd, which incorporates Ga(III) for PET imaging and Gd(III) for MRI contrast. The compound demonstrated in vivo imaging capability in mice, providing evidence that a single‑molecule dual‑modal imaging agent can function without performance degradation in either modality. Computational studies further elucidated the MRI enhancement mechanism, highlighting the influence of interlinking structures, coordinated metals, adjacent ligands, and frontier molecular orbitals on water relaxation behavior. Comprehensive in vitro and in vivo studies were conducted across multiple bladder cancer models, including organoids, to assess biosafety, targeting specificity, and photodynamic therapeutic potential. These studies provided a foundation for evaluating the translational potential of Ln‑SP‑based theranostics. (Chemical Engineering Journal 495 (2024) 153350) Objective 4 was fully achieved.

12300021.label: Major findings and research outcome
12300021.value: The project focused on advancing peptide multifunctionalization through the development of solid-phase synthetic methodologies. A modular solid-phase approach was established to construct trans‑AB2C porphyrins directly on peptide chains without the use of presynthesized porphyrin building blocks. This method produced conjugates that combine functionalities from both porphyrins and the modules used in their construction. In addition, a “resin‑to‑resin” reaction was demonstrated, linking two peptide chains during porphyrin motif formation to generate porphyrin-peptide conjugates with distinct peptide components. (Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2022, 61, e202207532 and Adv. Sci. 2025, 12, 2409771) A complementary methodology was introduced for corrole-peptide conjugates: this approach avoids the need for functionalized corrole building blocks and enables efficient production of corrole-peptide conjugates with multifunctional properties. The method provides a practical route to access bioactive corrole conjugates for further exploration in biomedical and biosupramolecular contexts. (Chem. Eur. J. 2023, 29, e202203623) For cyclen-peptide bioconjugates, an efficient strategy was identified that combines peptide cyclization and functionalization through a three-component intermolecular crosslinking on solid-phase synthesis. This approach yielded cyclen-embedded cyclic peptides with the capacity for modular functionalization, including coordination with metal ions. Demonstrations included the preparation of a luminescent Eu³⁺ complex for optical imaging and a Gd³⁺-based agent for magnetic resonance imaging. (Small Methods 2024, 8, 2400006) Mechanistic investigations highlighted the role of electron delocalization in influencing water behavior and its impact on Gd(III)-induced relaxation processes. The combined effects of structural interlinking and metal coordination were examined in relation to MRI contrast performance. These insights contribute to understanding the molecular basis of imaging agent design. In addition, a co-working radiolabeling strategy was applied to address practical challenges in PET probe preparation, offering simplified procedures and adaptable dosing options. (Chemical Engineering Journal 495 (2024) 153350) Overall, the work completed in this project established several synthetic methodologies and provided mechanistic observations relevant to the design and preparation of peptide-based multifunctional agents. The findings support further development of these systems for biomedical and biomaterial applications.

12300021.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12300021.value: The methodologies developed in this project provide a foundation for expanding peptide‑based imaging and theranostic agents. The solid‑phase construction of porphyrin, corrole, TACN, and cyclen motifs directly on peptide chains can be further adapted to incorporate a wider range of metal ions, sensitization antennae, and targeting sequences. This would allow systematic tuning of photophysical properties, metal‑binding behaviour, and biological specificity. The mechanistic insights gained, such as water relaxation processes, offer clear directions for designing next‑generation low‑dose MRI and PET theranostic probes. Future work may focus on broadening the library of macrocycle‑modified peptides, improving synthetic efficiency for longer or aggregation‑prone sequences, and integrating additional functional modules such as drug‑delivery components or phototherapeutic groups. In vivo evaluation can be extended to more disease models. The dual‑modal PET/MRI platform demonstrated here provides a basis for developing multi‑functional probes with enhanced safety profiles, and support future translation toward practical diagnostic and therapeutic applications.

12300021.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12300021.value: This project aims to establish new synthetic strategies that make it easier to build advanced peptide‑based molecules for biomedical imaging. Peptides are amino acid sequences that can be tailor-made with specific functions such as targeting cancer cells; they are usually attached to other components such as a light-emitting metal complex to transform into a practical diagnostic agent; nevertheless, the chemical attachment process is difficult, slow, expensive and hard to scale-up. In this research project, we developed several new “on‑the‑spot” methods that allow other components to be built directly on the peptide during synthesis, rather than being made separately and attaching them afterward. This significantly simplifies the process and makes production of many different peptide‑based imaging agents more efficient. Using these methods, we created new molecules that can emit light, or act as MRI or PET imaging agents with peptide functions imparted to the complete molecule. One of our compounds was successfully tested in mice as a dual PET/MRI imaging agent. Overall, this project provides new ways to design and produce next‑generation diagnostic tools that may one day support safer, more accurate detection of diseases such as bladder cancer.

12300121.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12300121.value: 在有機合成化學中，直接激活碳氫化合物之C–H鍵是一種很有效的策略，並且相較於傳統的多步反應更為簡單及經濟。基於C–H鍵的惰性，初始活化步驟通常需要苛刻的反應條件。在工業上，當鈷鹽作為催化劑時，環己烷被氧化成環己醇和環己酮時需要在反應溫度高於100 oC下完成。因此，開發出一種能夠在室溫空氣條件下並且能夠高效氧化烷烴的催化劑十分重要。近期，我們合成了一例強親電性的過氧叔丁基鈷（III）配合物，[CoIII(qpy)(OOtBu)(NCCH3)]2+（qpy = 2,2’:6’,2”:6”,2”’-四聯吡啶）。雖然這個化合物能夠在室溫空氣中高效地氧化多種烷烴。然而，其活性只適用於底物含有較弱的C–H鍵。在本項目中，我們致力於增強四聯吡啶鈷催化劑體系的室溫氧化能力，擴闊其可應用的底物範圍。基於前期的實驗結果，我們將會用不同的取代基來調整qpy配體的電負性，以及將過氧叔丁基轉換成其它類似的氧性基團。目前，我們已經得到了活性更高的原位生成的過氧化氫鈷[Co(qpy)(OOH)]及氮烯鈷[Co(qpy)(nitrene)]配合物。實驗表明，在室溫空氣下，這兩種配合物能夠在數分鐘內氧化環己烷（C–H鍵解離能99 kcal/mol）。除了C–H功能化反應，[CoIII(qpy)(OOtBu)(NCCH3)]2+ 還能夠在室溫空氣條件下將tBuOO基團轉移到乙烯的雙鍵。我們將會設計不同的動力學及光譜學實驗，詳細研究上述反應的機理。以上的機理研究有助於我們開發更高效的四聯吡啶鈷催化劑體系。總體來說，我們將會開發出高效的催化劑體系，應用在溫和條件下功能化烷烴和烯烴。同時，這些反應機理的研究，包括反應中間體的捕獲，也會為生物體內的氧氣活化過程提供指引。

12300121.label: Realisation of objectives
12300121.value: Objective 1: In collaboration with Prof. Gui Chen from Dongguan University of Technology, we synthesized 11 alkylperoxo cobalt(III) quaterpyridine complexes, systematically varying the alkylperoxo groups in 6 complexes and the quaterpyridine ligand substituents in 5 complexes. Using cyclopentene as a model hydrocarbon substrate, kinetic studies employing NMR and UV-vis revealed significant electronic effects of the quaterpyridine substituents on C–H functionalization. Electron-withdrawing groups (e.g., Cl) enhanced the electrophilicity of the cobalt center, accelerating C–H abstraction, while electron-donating groups (e.g., Me) decelerated the reaction. This work, recognized as a Very Important Paper and featured on the Front Cover of EJIC, underscores the tunability of cobalt(III)-peroxo reactivity through ligand design. Objective 2: We synthesized the cobalt(III) tert-butylperoxo complex [Co(OOtBu)(qpy)(NCCH3)]2+ by reacting [Co(qpy)(CH3CN)2]2+ with tBuOOH. This complex demonstrated exceptional reactivity in activating weak to mild C–H bonds across a broad range of hydrocarbons. This work was published in JACS in collaboration with Prof. Tai-Chu Lau from City University of Hong Kong. Despite our efforts, the analogous hydroperoxo complex, [Co(OOH)(qpy)(NCCH3)]2+, proved too reactive to isolate. In CH3CN, it abstracts a C–H bond from the solvent, forming [Co(OOCH2CN)(qpy)(NCCH3)]2+ (confirmed by NMR and ESIMS with isotopic labeling). With ethylbenzene, UV-vis confirmed the quantitative formation of [Co(OOCH(Me)Ph)(qpy)(NCCH3)]2+, which was isolated from [Co(OOtBu)(qpy)(NCCH3)]2+. Remarkably, the transient hydroperoxo intermediate oxidized cyclohexane (c-C6H12) with a strong C–H bond of 99 kcal/mol — a feat unachievable with other alkylperoxo analogs — yielding the isolable alkylperoxo complex, [Co(OO-c-C6H11)(qpy)(NCCH3)]2+, which has been successfully isolated and characterized by X-ray structure. This result highlights the superior oxidative power of the hydroperoxo species in C-H functionalization. Objective 3: Building on our success in oxidizing saturated hydrocarbons, we investigated the reactivity of [Co(OOtBu)(qpy)(NCCH3)]2+ toward unsaturated hydrocarbons, using styrene as a model substrate. Unlike the hydrogen-atom abstraction mechanism observed in C–H functionalization, Co(OOtBu)(qpy)(NCCH3)]2+ engages in nucleophilic addition to styrene, followed by aerobic oxidation to form a diperoxo complex, which is structurally confirmed by X-ray crystallography. Under ambient conditions, the reaction proceeds catalytically, demonstrating the rare example of Co-driven selective aerobic peroxidation of styrene. NMR and ESIMS with 18O isotopic labeling further revealed the formation of polystyrene peroxides, indicating polymerization alongside peroxidation. This work, published in JACS Au, was conducted in collaboration with computational experts, Dr. Bun Chan from Nagasaki University, Japan, and Huatian Shi from Dongguan University of Technology, PR China, who provided mechanistic insights into the reaction mechanism. Objective 4: Expanding on our earlier work on catalytic aerobic peroxidation of hydrocarbons mediated by [Co(OOtBu)(qpy)(NCCH3)]2+ (JACS 2021), we evaluated the catalytic oxidation of ethylbenzene (as a model substrate) using the Co(qpy) system with various oxidants, including (e.g., H2O2, tBuOOH, PhIO, and peracetic acid). Under ambient conditions, the reaction performance was comparable to or less efficient than aerobic peroxidation without added oxidants. Under an inert atmosphere, Co(qpy)/tBuOOH system exhibited modestly enhanced activity, yielding a mixture of oxidized products including acetophenone, 1-phenylethanol, and benzaldehyde, as confirmed by GC analysis. The Co(qpy) system demonstrates versatility in C–H functionalization across different oxidants. Aerobic peroxidation remains the most efficient pathway, reinforcing its potential for catalytic hydrocarbon functionalization under mild conditions.

12300121.label: Major findings and research outcome
12300121.value: Inspired by nature’s metalloenzymes, we successfully designed and synthesized a family of cobalt(III) alkylperoxo complexes stabilized by quaterpyridine ligands, which serve as highly robust and effective catalysts for the aerobic oxidation of hydrocarbons under ambient conditions (room temperature, 1 atm. O2). This work, published across three high-impact international peer-reviewed journals, bridges fundamental mechanistic discoveries with practical applications in sustainable oxidation chemistry. In a brief summary, this series of studies redefines the reactivity of non-precious metal peroxo complexes, offering both a mechanistic blueprint for C–H functionalization and a practical toolkit for green oxidation. The insights pave the way for designing next-generation catalysts for hydrocarbon valorization. The details of the significant findings are listed below. #1 Discovery of a novel C–H activation pathway (JACS 2021) We synthesized and characterized the first quaterpyridine-supported tert-butylperoxo cobalt(III) complex (Co-OOtBu), demonstrating its ability to abstract inert C–H bonds of hydrocarbons via the proximal oxygen atom of the peroxo ligand—a mechanism unprecedented for metal-alkyl(hydro)peroxo species. We provided experimental evidence (NMR, ESIMS, kinetics, isotopic labelling) to support this unprecedented reaction pathway for the peroxidation of hydrocarbons, which is exceptional for other metal alkyl(hydro)peroxo complexes. More importantly, we found that the tert-butylperoxo analogue is an active catalyst in oxidizing various substrates to generate free alkyl peroxides using oxygen from air as the oxidant under ambient conditions, that is, room temperature at 1 atm. #2 Ligand electronic control of catalytic efficiency (EJIC 2022) Building on the JACS paper, we systematically tuned the electronic properties of the quaterpyridine ligand and the alkylperoxo moiety to study the effect on the catalytic efficiency in the functionalization of hydrocarbons. We found that the quaterpyridine substituents (e.g., electron-donating (CH3) vs. electron-withdrawing (Cl)) significantly modulated reactivity, with electron-withdrawing ligands enhancing the rate of the reactions. In contrast, alkylperoxo substituents showed minimal impact, suggesting the quaterpyridine scaffold dominates the electrophilicity of the cobalt complex in oxidizing C–H of hydrocarbons. #3 Expansion to unsaturated hydrocarbons (JACS Au 2025) Apart from saturated hydrocarbons, we also demonstrated that the tert-butylperoxo cobalt(III) complex is an active catalyst in aerobic peroxidation of styrene, with substantial evidence in characterizing the diperoxo species using X-ray crystallography. Under ambient conditions, this cobalt catalyst performs aerobic peroxidation of styrene selectively in generating polyperoxo compounds, which may be helpful for diverse applications.

12300121.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12300121.value: This work establishes Co(III)-peroxo complexes as catalysts for C–H activation and aerobic oxidation, demonstrating that ligand electronics critically govern reactivity. In the short-term vision, we plan to secure additional funding (e.g., ITF) to probe hydroperoxo chemistry for methane and benzene functionalization (with stronger C–H bonds). In the long-term goal, we aim: i) to develop industrial-scale aerobic oxidation processes; ii) to apply selective C–H activation to pharmaceutical synthesis; and iii) to expand controlled polymer peroxidation methodologies. The combination of fundamental mechanistic insights and demonstrated catalytic versatility positions these Co(III) systems as promising platforms for sustainable hydrocarbon functionalization. Strategic partnerships will accelerate translation from bench-scale discoveries to practical applications in green chemistry.

12300121.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12300121.value: Hydrocarbons (e.g., alkanes) are essential but chemically inert due to their strong C–H bonds for modification. Breaking these bonds controllably is a grand challenge in chemistry. Inspired by nature, this project developed a new cobalt-based catalyst (chelated by a quaterpyridine ligand) that activates these C–H bonds at room temperature, using oxygen from air to transform hydrocarbons into valuable peroxides. Unlike traditional methods requiring precious metals or harsh conditions, our cobalt complex is efficient, sustainable, and operates under mild conditions. This project unlocks a novel reaction mechanism in metal-oxygen chemistry, turning even the inert hydrocarbons into versatile peroxides, which can potentially serve as fuel additives, drug carriers, and eco-friendly coatings. The project advances both fundamental chemistry (revealing new metal-oxygen chemistry) and practical catalysis, offering industries a cheaper, greener way to produce high-value chemicals. By mimicking nature’s elegance with synthetic innovation, this work paves the way for cleaner processes and reduces reliance on costly and toxic catalysts.

12300321.label: Project Objectives
12300321.value: We shall formulate optimisation problems for support structures in additive manufacturing using the method of phase fields, with objectives addressing structural compliance and thermal dissipation. We shall analyse the optimisation problems formulated in Objective 1 and establish rigorous analytical results concerning minimisers and first order optimality conditions. We shall develop numerical schemes for solving the optimality conditions derived in Objective 2, and compare the resulting optimal designs from those obtained with other numerical approaches such as level sets.

12300321.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12300321.value: Additive manufacturing, also known as 3D printing, is a fast-growing technology that is making an appearance in various businesses and industries. It has the advantage of creating complex-shaped objects in a rapid, flexible and cheap manner, but despite its potential in a variety of areas such as biomedical implants, automotive and aerospace components, and even jewellery and food, it is held back by several factors that prevent real integration with commercial production line assemblies. One of these factors which we plan to explore in this project is a design issue related to support structures. As the name implies, support structures are used to prop up the 3D object during printing to maintain its intended shape and prevent deformations caused by external factors. However, support structures obviously add to the material costs, printing time, and there is a risk of inflicting damage to the object during their removal. Since support structures are absolutely necessary for general object designs, previous researchers have employed the framework of optimisation, particularly in the context of structural topology optimisation, with the aim of finding optimal designs that address some of the issues arising from support structures. The goal of this proposal is to develop an alternative optimisation approach for the design of support structures based on the concept of phase fields, which in the past has seen successful applications in tackling problems motivated from shape and topology optimisation. We believe our proposed phase field approach can offer both mathematical and numerical advantages over current methods; such as a rigorous analysis of the optimisation problem, derivation of optimality conditions, convergence of the numerical iterations, and an overall improvement in computational effort. Furthermore, we envision the ideas developed in this proposal can be extended beyond the issue of support structures, and begin to contribute towards resolving other challenges faced by the additive manufacturing industries. 增材製造，俗稱3D打印，是各行各業快速發展的製造技術。它具有以快速、靈活和廉價的方式創建複雜形狀物體的優勢，儘管它在生物醫學植入物、汽車和航空航天部件，甚至珠寶和食品等各個領域具有潛力，但現在仍未完全成為商業生產線主要的一部分。 在這個項目中，我們探討了與支撐結構相關的設計問題。顧名思義，支撐結構用於在打印過程中支撐正在印刷的部分，以保持其預期形狀並防止由外部因素引起的變形。然而，支撐結構顯然會增加材料成本、打印時間，並且在移除過程中存在對物體造成損壞的風險。由於支撐結構對於一般設計是絕對必要的，以前的研究採用了優化方法，特別是在拓撲優化的背景下，目的是找到解決支撐結構引起的一些問題的最佳設計。 我們的目標是開發一種使用相場設計支撐結構的替代方法，該方法過去已成功應用於解決形狀優化和拓撲優化引起的問題。我們相信我們提出的相場方法可以提供優於當前方法的數學和數值優勢；例如對優化問題的嚴格分析、優化條件的推導、數值迭代的收斂以及計算工作的整體改進。此外，我們設想本提案中提出的想法可以擴展到支持結構問題之外，並開始為解決增材製造行業面臨的其他挑戰做出貢獻。

12301021.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12301021.value: 该项目旨在建立一类用于求解曲面上的偏微分方程（PDEs）的无网格算法。此类方程可应用于物理建模、细胞膜生物学中的流变模拟、计算机图形学，以及工程问题中3D扫描仪的数据处理。由于曲面的弯曲特性，无需建立数据间的复杂关联性的无网格算法脱颖而出。在过去几年里，用于计算曲面偏微分方程的无网格方法仍在积极开发中。 这些方法种类繁多、各具优势，例如局部方法与全局方法，且这些方法均作用于外蕴坐标上。该项目的第一部分注重于算法的开发； 我们将通过建立一些局部方法来填补此类方法的空缺，即使用作用于内蕴公式的最小二乘 (LS) 径向基函数-有限差分 (RBF-FD) 方法。该项目中建立的所有算法不局限于使用仅由曲面定义的度量张量，还可以采用各种技术近似处理张量，因而具有更高的灵活性。 该项目的第二部分主要将该算法应用于各类问题，如各向异性扩散（用于 MRI 处理），图案形成（用于计算机图形）、基于点云的动态曲面上的（用于点云处理）问题。

12301321.label: Realisation of objectives
12301321.value: Objective 1: As reported in Nature Chem. 2020, 12, 551-559, we used non-polarized 365-nm light to induce an enantioselective cyclodimerization of 2-anthracenecarboxylic acid (AC) at the surfaces of Ag nanohelices (NHs) and obtain a mean enantiomeric excess (ee) value < 5%. In this project, we devised two methods to enhance the enantioselectivity of the photoinduced cyclodimerization of AC. One is to apply atomic layer deposition (ALD) or sputtering to deposit achiral metallic (Ag or Au) nanoparticles (NPs) on the Ag NHs to generate chiroplasmonic core@shell NHs@NPs, whereby the NHs function as a chiral template on which the achiral metallic NPs helically assembly to generate collective chiroplasmonic effect. Circularly polarized light (CPL) with a wavelength of 365 nm was applied to the NHs@NPs, leading to an average ee value of 32%. Another method is to apply layer-by-layer glancing angle deposition (LbL-GLAD) to fabricate alloy chiral nanoparticles (CNPs). Compared to unary Ag CNPs, binary CNPs consist of more chiral lattices, on which the AC dimers prefer to enantiospecifically adsorb, resulting in a mean ee value of 23%. Objective 2: For the first method, numerical simulations were performed to find out that under the excitation with CPL, the optical chirality of superchiral near fields could be significantly amplified at the inter-NP gaps (i.e., chiral hot spots), and the chiroplamonic amplification of local optical chirality sensitively depends on the sizes of NPs and gaps, and the helical pitch of the NHs. Large local optical chirality is favorable to increase the ee values. For the second method, alloying of CNPs significantly increases the density of chiral lattices, on which the AC dimers enantiospecifically adsorb to obviously increase the ee values.

(2020, 12, 551), we used non-polarized 365-nm light to induce an enantioselective cyclodimerization of AC at the surfaces of Ag nanohelices (NHs) and obtain a mean enantiomeric excess (ee) value < 5%. Two methods were devised to enhance the enantioselectivity (i.e., the ee values). The first method is to deposit plasmonic NPs on the Ag NHs, to form core@shell NHs@NPs. Under an excitation of CPL, chiral hot spots are created at the inter-NP gaps on the Ag helical surfaces, whereby the local optical chirality is significantly amplified (as confirmed by numerical simulations) to result in an increase of mean ee values to 32%. The second approach is using LbL-GLAD to dope Ag CNPs with metal dopants, leading to the formation of alloy CNPs. The alloying make the Ag CNPs significantly increase the surface density of chiral lattices, on which the AC dimers enantiospecifically adsorb to obtain an average ee value of 23%. The two objectives proposed were completed. We are working on a manuscript to publish these results. Furthermore, we used the first method to fabricate silica NHs@Ga NPs, through which the optical activity were imposed on liquid metal NPs via chirality transfer from the silica NHs (Small 2022, 18, 2200620). We also employed GLAD to produce NHs made of luminophore semiconductors, resulting in the emission of highly pure CPL in the color of red of violet (ACS Nano 2023, 17, 20611). Ag CNPs comprises of chiral lattices with the structural chirality at the atomic scale, which is thermodynamically unstable. It is of importance to enhance the thermal stability of Ag CNPs. We found that Ag CNPs completely lose their optical activity at 200 0C ascribed to chiral-to-achiral lattice transformation. LbL-GLAD was performed to dope Al in Ag CNPs to significantly enhance their thermal stability, owning to ease in the diffusion of Al atoms in the host Ag CNPs and thermal insulation from the aluminium oxide layers partially covering the binary CNPs that effectively prohibit structural relaxation of the metastable chiral lattices (Small 2022, 18, 2107657). Moreover, LbL-GLAD were performed to produce ternary and quaternary alloy CNPs with strong optical activities (Adv. Opt. Mater. 2023, 11, 2300696), to significantly extend the material scope of alloy CNPs. The doping of Ag CNPs with Au facilitates the production of mesoporous alloy CNPs via galvanic replacement reactions (ChemComm 2023, 59, 14551).

12301321.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12301321.value: 1. Because having high surface density of chiral lattices, enhanced thermal stability and synergetic contribution to photocatalysis, ternary and quaternary CNPs will be used to enhance the enantioselectivity of the photoinduced cyclodimerization of AC. The enhancement mechanisms will be investigated in terms of enantiospecific adsorption of AC dimers, chiroplasmonic enhancement in the optical chirality of superchiral near fields, and the dopant-associated synergetic catalysis. 2. To make the metallic chiral nanostructures generally adapted to perform asymmetric photocatalysis, more photoinduced catalysis systems will be explored. 3. Enantiospecific interactions of molecular substrates and chiral nanostructures play an important role in the enantioselective photocatalysis. To promote the interactions at the nanostructure surfaces, microfluidic systems will be applied to enhance the enantioselectivity and production yield.

12301321.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12301321.value: We previously used non-polarized 365-nm light to induce an enantioselective cyclodimerization of AC at the surfaces of Ag nanohelices (NHs) and obtain a mean enantiomeric excess (ee) value < 5%. In this project, two methods were devised to enhance the enantioselectivity (i.e., the ee values). The first method is to deposit plasmonic nanoparticles (NPs) on Ag NHs, to form core@shell NHs@NPs. Under an excitation of CPL, chiral hot spots are created at the inter-NP gaps on the Ag helical surfaces, whereby the local optical chirality is significantly amplified to result in an increase of mean ee values to 32%. The second approach is to dope Ag CNPs with metal dopants, leading to the formation of alloy CNPs. The alloying make the Ag CNPs significantly increase the surface density of chiral lattices, on which the AC dimers enantiospecifically adsorb to obtain an average ee value of 23%. This project devises a new method to produce chiral drugs and pesticides with minimized side effect, having a long-term economic impact on Hong Kong and the Greater Bay Area by fostering the economic competitiveness of the local pharmaceutical production, as well as a broader impact on society by enhancing the quality of public health.

12301721.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12301721.value: The valorisation of waste biomass is essential for sustainable global development and particularly crucial for the production of renewable carbon-based chemicals. Lignins are a major structural constituent of plants and some algae, and form a large proportion of agricultural and horticultural waste biomass. Thus, waste lignins could be a valuable source of renewable carbon-based chemicals. Notably, most waste lignins are produced by technical processes in the paper and pulp industry, and the structural characteristics of these so-called technical lignins depend on the type of pulping process that is used. Hydrothermal liquefaction (HTL) is a promising method for the conversion of waste lignins into valuable chemical compounds. Investigations of the HTL of a variety of technical lignins have been performed, but the fundamental chemistry of lignin HTL remains poorly understood. Furthermore, there is little understanding of the variance in the reactivities of different lignins under HTL conditions. These aspects must be understood to enable HTL processes to be optimised on an industrial scale. In this proposed project, we will extend our understanding of the HTL chemistry of lignins by investigating the hydrothermal processing of lignin model compounds and real lignins. Thus, we will synthesise and hydrothermally process model compounds possessing the structural characteristics of native (i.e. unprocessed) lignin and technical lignins (e.g. sulfonated lignin). The results of these model compound studies will provide an understanding of HTL mechanisms and reaction rates, and how these are influenced by the structural substituents of lignins, catalysts and process conditions. Subsequently, HTL of native lignin and three types of technical lignins derived from the same feedstock will be performed, and optimal HTL conditions will be determined. The results of these native and technical lignin HTL studies will be correlated with those from model compound studies to reveal the impact of structures and reaction pathways on selectivities and yields of the final products. These studies will also shed light on the variability in the reactivities of different lignins under HTL conditions. The new knowledge generated by this proposed project will greatly aid the optimisation of HTL as an industry-ready process for the valorisation of waste lignins. 生物質的資源化對於全球的可持續發展至關重要，尤其是再生碳基化學品的生產。木質素是植物和一些藻類的主要結構成分，在農業和園藝廢棄物生物質中佔很大比例。因此，廢木質素可能是可再生碳基化學品的寶貴來源。值得注意的是，大多數廢木質素是通過造紙和紙漿工業生產的，這些所謂的工業木質素的結構特徵取決於所使用的製漿技術類型。 水熱液化 (HTL) 是一種將廢木質素轉化為有用芳香族化合物的有用方法。一些人在之前已經對各種工業木質素的 HTL 進行了研究。 然而，這種 HTL 過程的基本化學仍然不多。 此外，我們目前對 HTL 條件下不同木質素的反應性差異知之甚少。 然而，這些信息對於實現 HTL 過程至關重要。 在這個研究項目中，我們將通過研究木質素及其模型化合物的水熱處理來擴展我們對木質素 HTL 化學的理解。 因此，我們將合成和水熱轉化具有天然（即未加工）木質素和工業木質素（例如磺化木質素）結構特徵的模型化合物。這些模型化合物研究的結果將提昇我們對 HTL 過程機理和反應速率的理解，以及它們如何受到木質素的結構、催化劑和反應條件的影響。隨後，我們將對天然木質素和源自同一原料的三種工業木質素進行 HTL，並確定最佳 HTL 反應條件。這些天然和工業木質素 HTL 研究的結果將與模型化合物研究的結果相關聯，以揭示結構和反應途徑對最終產品的選擇性和產率的影響。這些研究還將闡明不同木質素的 HTL 反應性差異。 這個研究項目所誕生的新知識將極大地幫助優化 HTL 作為增值廢木質素的過程。

12301821.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12301821.value: 這個世界充滿了手性。手性分子廣泛的應用于醫藥和材料科學中。今天，眾多有用的手性分子都是通過有機合成得到的，更準確的說，是不對稱合成。在不對稱合成的各種方法中，不對稱催化又最為吸引。許多新的機遇與挑戰都是隨著不對稱催化反應的發展湧現的。 不對稱催化是一個廣闊且令人興奮的領域。高效手性催化劑/配體的發展在這個領域起了重要的作用。不論手性配體怎樣設計與發展，手性膦配體始終是過渡金屬催化的不對稱反應中最優異和最有效的配體。因此，對手性膦配體的特殊需求就反應在如何高效便捷的構建光學純的有機膦化合物。 過渡金屬催化的不對稱氫膦化反應是合成膦化合物最為高效和直接的路徑。儘管如此，催化的氫膦化反應中區域選擇性和立體選擇性控制還是很大的挑戰，至今為止只有零星的報道。因此，發展實現過渡金屬催化的不對稱氫膦化反應的新型催化體系的研究至關重要。不對稱氫膦化反應不僅直接高效且可以模塊組合化的大量構建手性膦化合物，將為不對稱催化領域帶了前所未有的機遇和挑戰。

12301821.label: Realisation of objectives
12301821.value: This is the completion report of the funding 12301821. The research activities under this project were conducted from Aug 1, 2021 to July 31, 2024. Despite the challenges posed by the COVID-19 pandemic, all these project objectives were achieved. The following sections provide a detailed account of the research activities conducted during this period. 1. We developed the highly regio- and enantioselective addition of phosphine oxides to allenes by using a Pd/Difluorphos catalyst system. A wide range of allenes and phosphine oxides participated well in the reaction, generating chiral allylic phosphine oxides in high yield (up to 99%) and enantioselectivities (up to 99% ee). Moreover, we demonstrated the utility of this reaction by the facile synthesis of diphenylphosphine oxide 2H-chromene and later stage functionalization of cholesterol derivative. This research contribution was published in Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2021, 60, 27288-27292. 2. Recently, we developed a Pd-catalyzed diastereo- and enantio-selective desymmetric hydrophosphination of 3,3-disubstituted cyclopropenes. It allows efficient, direct, and atom-economic access to potentially valuable chiral cyclopropane rings bearing two vicinal carbon stereocenters in high yields with excellent diastereo- and enantioselectivities (up to 98:2 d.r. and 97% ee). This research contribution was published in Chem. Catal. 2022, 2, 3163-3173 (Front Cover, Invited paper for special issue on asymmetric catalysis). 3. Besides, we also extend the asymmetric hydrophosphination system for hydroamination methylene cyclopropanes. To our delight, we were able to achieve asymmetric cascade hydroamination protocol to construct a wide range of chiral 1,4-diamine derivatives in high yields with excellent enatioselectivities (up to 95 % yield and up to 99 % ee). This research contribution was published in Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2022, e202202160 (Hot paper). 4. The direct hydrophosphinylation of alkynes with phosphine oxides catalyzed by Cu/CPA co-catalytic system has been developed for delivering novel axially chiral phosphorus-containing alkenes in high yields and excellent enantioselectivities (up to 99 % yield and 99 % ee). DFT calculations were performed to elucidate the reaction pathway and the origin of enantiocontrol. This streamlined and modular methodology establishes a new platform for the design and application of new axially chiral styrene-phosphine ligands. This research contribution was published in Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2023, 62, e202215820 (Hot paper). 5. An enantioselective hydrophosphination of alkenyl isoquinolines is developed by using a copper-chiral diphosphine ligand catalyst. It provides a direct and atom-efficient approach to prepare a variety of chiral phosphines with an isoquinoline unit in good yields and high enantioselectivities. In addition, these chiral phosphine products are useful bidentate P,N-ligands which showed potential application in asymmetric catalysis. This research contribution was published in Chem. Sci., 2023, 14, 4413-4417.

12301821.label: Major findings and research outcome
12301821.value: In this project, we have developed a new series of highly efficient catalytic systems (Pd, Cu) to drive various enantioselective and regioselective additions of phosphine oxides to C-C double bonds and triple bonds, including cyclopropenes, allenes, heterocycle-alkenes, and alkynes. The key to the success of this process lies in identifying a well-suited ligand that overcomes the coordination challenges posed by phosphorus reagents and products. Moreover, we demonstrated the application of these methodologies through the late-stage functionalization of drug derivatives and natural products. In some catalytic systems, DFT calculations were also performed to elucidate the reaction pathway and the origin of enantiocontrol. This streamlined and modular methodology establishes a new platform for the design and application of novel axially chiral styrene-phosphine ligands and bidentate P,N-ligands.

12301821.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12301821.value: There is significant potential for further development and application of these new axially chiral styrene-phosphine ligands and chiral bidentate P,N-ligands to facilitate challenging chemical transformations. By utilizing a diverse range of chiral phosphine ligands, we can conduct in-depth studies on previously problematic reactions and explore unprecedented asymmetric transformations. The potential outcomes hold great promise for advancing pharmaceutical synthesis and the manufacturing of chiral drugs.

12301821.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12301821.value: Our research focuses on making chemical reactions more efficient, particularly in creating chiral compounds, which are important in many pharmaceuticals. We developed a new and effective catalyst system that improves the asymmetric hydrophosphination process. This method uses transition metals to help form phosphine compounds in a precise and controlled way. The new catalysts we created are easy to use and can be adapted for various reactions. This advancement not only helps us tackle more challenging chemical transformations but also holds great potential for developing new types of chemicals. Ultimately, our work aims to enhance the production of chiral drugs, which are essential in many medical treatments.
