12600521.label: Major findings and research outcome
12600521.value: This study’s findings showed that Chinese calligraphy exists as a rejuvenated form of public art with contemporary significance in Hong Kong in wider communities beyond the literati realm and reaches wider audiences in city life. All research outputs showed that Hong Kong as a unique place can be perceived through emplaced calligraphic works as they are manifested in its various spatial expressions and material forms. For instance, while some calligraphic works appear as inscribed wooden plaques that function as the markers of places or buildings such as schools and parks, others take the forms of integral decorative elements in architecture, such as calligraphic couplets etched in the lateral posts of stone gateways, halls and courtyards, also as motto plaques in schools, and as layout designs on moving vehicles, websites and social media posts. All research outputs highlighted the indispensable role of calligraphic materiality, spatiality and multimodality in enriching calligraphy’s textual meaning beyond the exclusive parameter of language. For instance, site-specific performances of calligraphy with elements— including the calligrapher’s body movements evoked by wielding a giant brush, interactive improvisation with the audience, calligraphic aesthetics, the literary meaning of the huge Chinese characters, and the on-site ambience of historical, social and cultural contexts of the historic sites— were effectively used to communicate richer, deeper and more incisive meanings pertaining to the functions, missions and visions of historic buildings in Hong Kong and the broader socio-cultural meanings of the historical and cultural heritage as well as the revitalization of historic buildings within the context of the history and development of the modern city of Hong Kong. Beyond on-site spaces, these live performances were documented and transformed as video broadcasted in different modes of mass media including TV programmes and online videos (YouTube) in cyberspace with multiple layers of meanings and multimodal perception experiences. Beyond empirical research on a wide spectrum of emplaced calligraphic works, 3 calligraphy performances, 1 solo exhibition and 3 calligraphic works in group exhibitions were inspiringly conducted by the PI as artworks-cum-research outputs, and were subsequently analyzed and interpreted as scholarly research outputs in 3 international conference papers, a book chapter and a fully illustrated book manuscript (see abovementioned 5.3 Realisation of objectives). Furthermore, a series of 5 research impact outputs and related activities (see abovementioned 5.3 Realisation of objectives) generated greater interest in and a richer understanding of the research findings.

12600521.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12600521.value: Through a new framework of collecting, analysing and interpreting emplaced works of calligraphy in Hong Kong, and disseminating new knowledge to recipients, the PI developed a new approach that yielded deeper insights into the new knowledge through the synergy between empirical research on the major calligraphic expressions of educational, park, festival and funerary cultures, and alternative modes of expression and cyberspace (with traditional text-based research outputs including conference paper, book chapter, monograph/ book manuscript) and creative works manifested in 3 calligraphy performances, 1solo exhibition and 3 calligraphic works in group exhibitions. On the other hand, the 6 research impact outputs and related activities— including a digital scholarship website that features an online exhibition of Chinese calligraphy, TV programmes that feature the PI’s research and artistic practice of Chinese calligraphy with calligraphy performances at historic and heritage sites of Hong Kong, gallery talks and a talk and panel discussion at calligraphy forum — effectively extended the research impact in the form of socially engaged activity that brought the research to wider recipients and communities, suggesting potential future development into interdisciplinary research that will integrate art-historical research with creative outputs.

12600521.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12600521.value: The sustaining Chinese tradition of inscribing calligraphic inscriptions in public spaces has been a unique cultural phenomenon in China. This research is original in terms of its new framework of collecting, analysing, interpreting and disseminating traits of this tradition that are distinctive to Hong Kong in its socio-cultural and historical contexts. Hence, the research outputs offered a significant and original contribution to knowledge. Findings showed that inspiring calligraphic expressions in sites such as parks, schools, festival venues, cemeteries, calligraphy performances, websites, mass media and social media platforms signify a wide spectrum of people’s aspirations, visions of society, and thoughts on life and death, thus shedding light on the people from different walks of life who make up Hong Kong society and on what has shaped their thoughts and values. Thus, the project offered a significant contribution to the reconstruction of identity embodied in calligraphic works in physical and cyber spaces. More importantly, this research yielded new and deeper insights into the contextual artistic expression of Hong Kong’s development as a city. In this way, the study will enhance Hong Kong residents’ sense of heritage, identity and belonging, particularly among future generations.

12600821.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12600821.value: With the rapid advancement in ubiquitous computing, mobile technologies such as smartphone has become an indispensable tool that penetrates deep into various aspects of our everyday life. As revealed in some studies, smartphone users can develop strong attachment to their device to an extent that they perceive smartphones as a part of their extended selves. It is likely that smartphone dependence will continue to exacerbate as smartphones are becoming increasingly appealing and versatile. In fact, excessive or problematic smartphone use (PSU) has been identified as emerging public health issues, posing new challenges to people’s mental health. Nonetheless, owing to embarrassment, social undesirability and privacy, some help-seekers are reluctant to seek help as reflected by the consistently low help-seeking rates for face-to-face pathological behavior treatments found across many countries. As such, digital interventions are seen as plausible solutions for circumventing the hurdles that might deter individuals from seeking face-to-face treatments. Recently, there has been a proliferation of mobile health apps, yet research on the efficacy and effectiveness of digital interventions for PSU is scarce. Despite the potential of the digital approaches to PSU, there remain issues concerning their empirical evidence, design and implementation to be tackled. These include (1) lacking empirical studies on mobile health interventions, (2) lacking evidence-based mobile interventions for PSU, (3) lacking adaptability in most of the mobile-app interventions to address the diverse needs of students with PSU, (4) lacking knowledge about the relationship between self-reported PSU and the actual patterns of smartphone use, and (5) lacking knowledge about the processes of behavioural change in PSU. To address the research gaps and methodological challenges mentioned in the previous section, we attempt to develop a novel mobile context-aware adaptive intervention for students with problematic smartphone use to regulate their usage and behaviours, and examine the effects of the mobile-app intervention implementation on students with PSU through a randomized controlled study. This study contributes to the research community and the general public in several ways. Firstly, the empirical analysis of smartphone usage patterns will deepen our understanding of the change processes of students’ smartphone behaviours during intervention. This will lead to developing more effective interventions and support for students’ with PSU. Secondly, the context-aware adaptive mobile-app intervention developed in this study with will provide a guiding framework for developing adaptive interventions for other problematic behaviours. 隨著普適計算的急速發展，智能手機等流動技術已成為不可或缺的工具，其應用深入到我們日常生活的不同層面。正如一些研究所揭示，智能手機用戶可以對他們的設備產生強烈的依戀，以至於他們將智能手機視為擴展自我的一部分。隨著智能手機變得越加有吸引力和多功能，對智能手機的依賴可能會繼續加劇。事實上，過度或問題性智能手機使用 (PSU) 已被視為新浮現的公共衛生問題，對人的心理健康構成了新的挑戰。儘管如此，由於尷尬、社會的不認受及隱私，一般問题使用者不願意尋求幫助，這正反映許多國家發現尋求面對面病理行為治療的求助率一直偏低。 因此，透過電子媒介提供介入方案被視為可排除問題性智能手機使用者尋求面對面治療時所面對的障礙。最近，流動健康應用程序激增，但有關PSU的數碼介入方案之功效及其有效性的研究甚少。儘管 PSU 數碼介入方案具備潛力，但仍存在有關其科學證據、設計及實施的問題有待解決。其中包括 (1) 缺乏關於流動健康介入方案的實證研究，(2) 缺乏以證據為本而設計的 PSU 的數碼介入方案，(3) 大多數流動應用介入方案缺乏適應性，無法滿足 PSU 學生的多樣化需求，(4) 缺乏就問題性使用者的PSU自我報告的與其實際智能手機使用模式之間關係的認知，以及 (5) 缺乏關於 PSU 行為變化過程的認知。為了解決上述的研究缺口及方法論挑戰，我們嘗試為問題性智能手機使用學生開發一種嶄新的情境感知自適應流動應用程式介入方案，以規範他們的使用和行為，並以隨機對照實驗方式，就實施情境感知自適應流動應用程式介入方案對PSU 學生的果效行研究。 本研究將為學術界和公眾作出多樣貢獻。首先，智能手機使用模式的實證分析將加深對實施流動應用程式介入方案期間學生智能手機行為變化的了解。研究所得的數據，將為 PSU 學生製定更有效的介入方案。其次，本研究所開發的自適應流動應用程式，將為開發針對其他行為問題提供指導框架。

12601121.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12601121.value: In May of 1942, Mao Zedong hosted three meetings of what was later famously called the Yenan Forum on Literature and Art. The published record of these meetings has remained the principal guidelines for artistic practice in the new China ever since. In October 2014, China’s leader Xi Jinping gave the “Speech at the Forum on Literature and Art” in Beijing, which echoed Mao’s agenda delivered at Yenan, but with his own appropriations and idealizations addressed to a stronger China. This proposed study would review the different emphases delivered by Mao and Xi regarding artistic practice, the strategies and policies developed, and the implications in terms of the relevant political and moral values. The originality of this study is to elucidate the references to traditional Confucian aesthetics in Mao’s view on the role of an artist, in contrast with that in the Soviet-style Marxism–Leninism, together with Xi’s talk of the “truth, goodness and beauty”, which is a different aesthetics appropriation of the Confucian aesthetics. This study is intended to reveal the Confucian thread in the aesthetics claims of Mao and Xi, including artistic practice, the functions of art, and the impacts of art and artists on society. It will also compare and contrast the three modalities, namely, the aesthetics of the Confucian tradition, the pragmatic aesthetics of Mao and Xi in addressing art and morality and the social well-being in China. This study of the common agenda of art and morality will shed light on the understanding of the social functions and values of art implied in the current authoritarian discourses in China. The linking of the traditional Confucian aesthetics with the foundational modes of thought in the speeches of Mao and Xi reveals the thread of social and aesthetic thoughts embedded in the hierarchical structure of Chinese Confucian society and the position of artists in society. The study will conclude with a review of the impacts of Xi’s policies on and the prospects for artistic practice in the current art spheres in China, with particular attention to the situation of the film industry, which is receiving huge number of audiences or mass. The study wishes to enhance the understanding and the sensitivity of film producers regarding the growing censorship and measures in cinematic creativity. The research will employ interdisciplinary methodologies including historical review, philosophical analysis, critical studies, China studies and comparative aesthetics, leading to academic presentations and publications. 摘要 1942年5月，毛澤東在延安召開三場會議，史稱延安文藝座談會。座談會上毛澤東發表重要講話，其內容自此成為中國文藝政策的金科玉律。2014年10月，中共中央總書記習近平在北京發表《在文藝工作座談會上的講話》，重申毛澤東文藝主旨的同時，以個人感悟及時代願景，提出建設文化強國的藍圖。 本研究將重新審視毛習兩人關於藝術實踐、文藝政策及其政治道德意涵上的不同側重點。本研究的創見在於闡明兩人理論背後的儒家影響：相較於蘇聯馬克思列寧主義的美學觀，毛澤東對於藝術家的定位有著傳統儒家美學的認知背景，而習近平講話中的“真善美”則可以被解讀為一種儒家美學的當代應用。 本研究意在揭示毛習講話中針對藝術實踐、文藝之地位與作用、藝術家及其作品對於社會之影響這三方面內容中的儒家脈絡，進而比較分析三種模式，即儒家傳統美學觀、實用主義美學觀下的藝德問題、藝術作品對於中國社會的福祉，研究文藝實踐如何對道德產生引導效用，幫助理解當代中國官方論述中藝術創作的社會作用及價值。將傳統儒家美學觀與毛習講話中的基本思維模式聯繫在一起，能進一步揭示在中國傳統儒家社會層級結構中的社會及美學觀念。本研究將以述評及展望習近平文藝政策對於當代中國藝術實踐的影響作為結論，並特別以市場的電影產業為例。 本研究意在提高電影製片人對於日趨收緊的電影審查及創作自由之理解及敏感度。本研究將採用跨學科研究法，包括歷史回顧、哲學分析、批判理論、中國研究及比較美學的方法。研究成果將進行學術報告及出版。

12601121.label: Major findings and research outcome
12601121.value: Major Findings: 1. The Gang of Four radicalized the Yenan Talks during the Cultural Revolution era in the 1960s, led to a new Party-sanctioned form of political art and revolutionary operas and the condemnation of the “bourgeois decadence” of the oppositional art camps. 2. Only after Deng Xiaoping’s condemnation of the Cultural Revolution in 1979 were the talks reassessed. The content of art and literature in China are still following the correct political morality and the guidance of the CCP. 3. Art must convey a “realistic” view of history, and any depiction of historical figures must emphasize their heroic qualities. Productions made for export must convey a positive sense of the Great China. 4. On October 15, 2014, Xi Jinping gave his “Speech at the Forum on Literature and Art” in Beijing, which echoed Mao’s agenda delivered at Yenan but was appropriated and idealized to emphasize the development of a strong China. His speech was regarded as putting less emphasis on the historical revolution and Communism, but as encouraging artists to celebrate Party-sanctioned morality, cultural heritage, and nationalist sentiment. 5. Xi said that art must combine “a realist spirit” with “romantic feelings,” “to shine light on real life, use the light to dispel darkness, use the beautiful and good to vanquish the ugly and the bad, let people see beauty, see hope, and see that their dreams are ahead”. He asked artists to put material returns aside and create works that embodied both artistic quality and political correctness. 6. This agenda deviated from Mao’s historic Yenan Talks, in which Mao said that creative ambitions must first serve the people and the revolutionary clause. In addition, Xi’s approach was informed by the “moral high ground,” which differed from Mao’s propaganda tactics in 1940s China. The moral high ground is undoubtedly a sign of patriotism. His priority was that art must contribute to the rejuvenation of the great Chinese nation. 7. Xi used the term meihao to describe a “better life” or meihao in China, meaning that life is aesthetically pleasing and morally ordered. The duty of an artist is to produce visions of a good life, and the responsibility of the CCP is to create the socioeconomic conditions for its realization. Through the meihao principle, art can promote a positive image of the nation and address any negative connotations with strong patriotism.

12601121.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12601121.value: Mao Zedong?s very influential speeches on Literature and Art at the Yenan Forum in 1942 lays the socialist direction of artistic expression in form and content in the new China. Mao promoted the important position of literature and art as basic revolutionary causes, and regarded them as tools and operation of ideological changes and political revolution. In 2014, China leader Xi Jinping regarded art and literature as important means of enhancing cultural confidence and realizing the China Dream of national rejuvenation. Art is important manifestation of comprehensive national strength. This study reviews the evolution of the agenda of art and literature in China between the two influential leaders, and how they have discussed art and moral concerns in artistic practice and their different emphasis. The study believes that there are influences of traditional Confucian aesthetics on the discourses of Mao and Xi regarding the social functions of art. The study wants to see the link and development, and the impacts of the dominant and powerful Confucian discourses with its beliefs in art and morality, and art?s impacts on social governance and political power. These form the guidelines for artistic expression and censorship.

12601821.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12601821.value: 抗爭影像：廿一世紀新媒體、數碼影像科技及演算思維在公共及虛擬領域如何重新定義攝影真相

12601821.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12601821.value: 本研究計劃藉建立、發展、概念化和理論化「抗爭影像」，書寫二十一世紀公共和虛擬領域中攝影及影像的技術發展。影像技術在現今人類日常生活中無所不用：人臉識別我們的快樂指數、熱成像和紅外線成像檢測人類的健康、人工智能生成的神經和網絡圖像（如深偽技術和逆對影像）建構新又或具誤導性的身份特徵甚至是虛假資訊。日新月異的影像技術已成全球公民抗命運動中文化生產及傳播工具。過往十年，公民影像媒體日漸興起、以手機作新聞直播、以地理標記影像數據、法證建築學中攝影技術的使用等已成公民抗命文化不可或缺的部份，同時虛擬實境和擴增實境技術以及網絡迷因等工具已成為公共發言和政治游說的手法。在審視和紀錄社會和政治現實的領域，現今影像技術的進步和普及對影像的本質如真實性、意義和誠信作解構，並徹底的重新定義真相、意義和視覺文化的語境及討論。身處二十一世紀，新媒體、數碼科技和演算思維帶動並改變人類和機器對攝影真相的看法，顛覆攝影歷史和理論中的經典思維，重塑攝影實踐，斷離二十世紀所奠定的基礎。這複雜的題目在藝術實踐及學術研究將對二十一世紀的攝影產生全新的定義，並在媒體研究、視覺傳媒和視覺及媒體藝術等領域發揮擴展知識的功能。本計劃以「抗爭影像」的概念出發，從當代視覺文化公民抗命的例子中作分析及理論，研究內容包括有新聞攝影、紀實攝影、網絡迷因、虛擬現實、擴增實境、操作影像及逆對影像等。計劃透過媒體民族誌及網絡田野研究等質性研究方法，把「抗爭影像」置於學術語境並進行理論分析，以產生對攝影及影像全新的意義、操作及功能，在後攝影的學術討論中作出頁獻。研究成果包括：學術論文、國際會議報告、公共及教育策展計劃和攝影、視覺文化或數碼人文學科教材。

12602721.label: Project Objectives
12602721.value: To provide a detailed account of Japanese intellectuals’ engagement in both European and Japanese Renaissance studies as a unique form of transcultural knowledge production. To illustrate how interdisciplinary interests were mobilised in Japan for the production of knowledge on the Renaissance. To elucidate the function of history writing for Japanese intellectuals working on Renaissance studies in relation to contemporaneous social and political developments. To identify commonalities and differences between various examinations of the Renaissance undertaken by Japanese intellectuals. To explore various prewar and postwar intellectual discourses on Japanese modernisation to clarify the unique characteristics of the study of the Japanese Renaissance.

12602721.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12602721.value: 1930年代初起，來自眾多領域之日本領頭左翼知識份子開始了對於文藝復興的相關研究，更甚者探索了「日式」文藝復興作為日本現代性的轉捩點之可能性（15至19世紀之間）。文藝復興通常被認為是歐洲步入現代性的轉折點，其文化亦被視為現代人文主義和個人主義的源泉。許多來自世界各地的現代學者亦的確受到文藝復興的啟發。然而鮮為人知的是，現代日本學者亦曾試圖探索文藝復興的思想在日本歷史上所具備的信息和意義。上世紀初學者為何以文藝復興作為研究主體？他們如何透過文藝復興探究日本歷史？他們的研究對於當代有關日本現代化的爭論究竟有何意義？這些核心問題啟發了是次研究，其重要性在於引入了日本知識份子對於日本歷史的獨特探究及對於跨文化知識上的批判及實踐。 為進一步鑽研這些問題，是次研究將會分析不同日本文藝復興學者所提出的論說。而在同時撰寫歐洲及日本歷史的學者之中，其中三位將會作為是次的主要研究對象，分別為：文化評論家——花田清輝（Hanada Kiyoteru，1909-1974）、馬克思主義理論家及活躍份子——福本和夫（Fukumoto Kazuo，1901-1983），以及歷史學家——羽仁五郎（Hani Gorō，1901-1983）。三位學者均有相同馬克思主義的知識背景，亦同樣在1930至1940年代初開始有關於文藝復興的獨立研究，以及在戰後時期持續進行相關研究。 是次研究中，筆者將會藉這些學者在文藝復興上的學術研究探討他們如何呈現各自的思想軌跡，以及他們在二戰前後對於日本現代化具代表性的討論。其中，有關於馬克思主義、日本民俗、現代主義、現代化理論以及人民的歷史的討論均為是次研究的重點。由此而生的出版物及報告將展示三位學者在研究文藝復興道路上的政治隱喻，並以此呈現對日本帝國主義、資本主義以及以歐洲中心主義為本的現代化敘事方式的批判。透過介紹這些日本學者如何從文藝復興吸取經驗及教訓這種獨特而未被重視的嘗試，是次研究將有助擴闊現代日本及國際在知識史上的視野。

12603721.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12603721.value: 香港的家務勞工：性別、空間與勞工的交錯關係

12603721.label: Project Objectives
12603721.value: To increase awareness of the social and economic value of domestic work in Hong Kong. Nearly 35% of Hong Kong’s workforce participate in elementary work and service industries. Domestic workers are a large portion of this statistic and unpaid domestic work is officially unaccounted for. Raising awareness of the contribution of paid and unpaid domestic work to society helps dismantle misconceptions of its undesirability and gendered responsibility as ‘women’s work’. To advance knowledge of the significant contribution of women in the domestic work sector in Hong Kong. In Hong Kong, the majority of domestic workers are women. Apart from citizens, there are 390,000 Foreign Domestic Helpers who make up 10% of the city’s workforce. Within this 10%, 98.5% are women. Sociologists have coined this phenomenon as the ‘feminisation of labour’, where a labour sector is dominated by women due to various factors. Hong Kong has a long history of women occupying the domestic work sector. Today, women still dominate due to societal traditions and gender norms. These past practices collide with contemporary society where gender equality is an important part of a society’s advancement. Enhancing knowledge of the significant contribution of women in domestic work in Hong Kong will facilitate discussions around women’s role and work in society. To supplement existing research on domestic work, adding a Hong Kong-focused perspective to international discourse. Existing research on local or migrant domestic labour are heavily focused on other countries. My proposed project will focus on what happens in Hong Kong, and its role and impact on the global market. It will also give a unique perspective from a design research and urban spatial viewpoint, which offers new knowledge and supplement existing research in other disciplines where domestic work features. To use design research strategies to establish a new approach in obtaining and visualising information, resulting in a visual database. Through my PhD at the School of Design at the University of Technology Sydney in 2018, using spatial design methodologies such as spatial mapping and diagramming, combined with ethnographic fieldwork strategies such as fieldwork observation and interviewing, I now have a database of over 500 photographs, diagrams and spatial mappings that demonstrate the spaces and activities that women migrant workers engage in public space. Further, this archive includes drawings of their homes and details of their living situations. In the proposed project, I intend to expand this archive by conducting research on other demographics of Foreign Domestic Helpers, and local women who partake in paid and unpaid domestic work. This database will offer powerful insights and provide a unique visualisation of the socio-spatial conditions that women experience in their daily lives in relation to domestic work. To use a new interdisciplinary approach that integrates gender, labour and space. As existing research are mostly discussed within singular disciplines, the proposed project has an intersectional approach that examines relevant factors such as the feminisation of labour, impact on local and global political economy, and the spaces that domestic work occur in. Understanding the workers’ everyday spaces allow for a micro exploration that can combine with the macro frameworks to provide a meaningful and holistic consideration of individual experiences and larger reflections of a labour condition. An intersectional lens of gender, labour and space is an important explorative framework as domestic work is bound by a combination of social, cultural, economic and spatial factors. To encourage the use of domestic labour as a socially-engaged context for teaching and learning. It is important for the creative arts sector to engage with community-based topics and social affairs to increase awareness and contribute to the multiple facets of society. As a topic within the design curriculum it will encourage students to engage with gendered labour in creative ways that can stimulate learning and provoke positive impact on social and cultural well-being. The proposed outcomes will also offer different types of engagement for teaching and learning. The scholarly monograph will be a great scholarly resource, while the visual archive and the podcast series will stimulate and engage students creatively in the multi-dimensions of the topic. To share knowledge with the scholarly community, local NGOs and other interested parties beyond academia through the digital database, the podcast series and two collaborative events. Due to the ongoing global pandemic and possible social unrest, the proposed collaborative events (an exhibition and a public seminar) may happen or could be limited to digital platforms. The dissemination of this project’s findings through a digital archive and podcast series will strengthen the events and allow interested parties easy access to engage with and share parts of the project with their community locally and internationally.

12603721.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12603721.value: Over the last century, the world has seen a progression towards gender equality and women’s empowerment. As stated in the United Nations’ Sustainable Development Goals, ‘gender equality is not only a fundamental human right, but a necessity for a peaceful, prosperous and sustainable world’. Equal access to education, financial independence, and opportunities at work are paramount in ensuring women become equal members of society. This project aims to address inequality starting in the home, where unpaid work is often the invisible labour that keeps households running. This research aims to highlight and explore domestic work in Hong Kong through the intersection of gender, labour, and space. The project will be the first study dedicated to Hong Kong’s domestic labour using design research methodologies, spatial design visualisations, and ethnographic fieldwork. Existing research on domestic labour is often disseminated within text-based scholarship in sociology, labour studies, and gender studies. However, the topic has yet to be explored and visualised in a three-dimensional way through spatial design and an intersected consideration of gender, labour and space. This research and its methodology will make original contributions to an invaluable sector in the city’s functioning and well-being of its people, through lived experiences and spaces. The scope of the research focuses on paid and unpaid domestic labour by local women and foreign domestic helpers, and it will be disseminated through a scholarly monograph, a digital database, a podcast series and two collaborative events with Hong Kong-based NGOs. This project will produce three strands of knowledge specific to the outputs. The first explores the domestic work sector in Hong Kong, and how it is connected to the global political economy and its local and global impacts, disseminated through a scholarly monograph. The second focuses on the spatial dimensions of the topic, interlinking urban space and domesticity through spatial visualisations, diagrams, and photographs that will be available on a website. This digital database aims to add a spatial aspect to existing knowledge that is often unseen and underexplored. The third will give poetic detail to the human dimension of this topic, featuring migrant domestic workers and local women who participate in domestic work, through a podcast series that gives a platform for their experiences and stories to be told and heard. Overall, the project offers powerful and interesting insights on the economic impact and the socio-spatial experience of women participating in paid and unpaid domestic work in Hong Kong. The scope of the research focuses on paid and unpaid domestic labour by local women and foreign domestic helpers, and it will be disseminated through a scholarly monograph, a digital database, a podcast series and two collaborative events with Hong Kong-based NGOs. This project will produce three strands of knowledge specific to the outputs. The first explores the domestic work sector in Hong Kong, and how it is connected to the global political economy and its local and global impacts, disseminated through a scholarly monograph. The second focuses on the spatial dimensions of the topic, interlinking urban space and domesticity through spatial visualisations, diagrams, and photographs that will be available on a website. This digital database aims to add a spatial aspect to existing knowledge that is often unseen and underexplored. The third will give poetic detail to the human dimension of this topic, featuring migrant domestic workers and local women who participate in domestic work, through a podcast series that gives a platform for their experiences and stories to be told and heard. Overall, the project offers powerful and interesting insights on the economic impact and the socio-spatial experience of women participating in paid and unpaid domestic work in Hong Kong. 在過去一世紀，性別平等與女性充權運動在全球均取得了莫大進展。一如聯合國可持續發展目標所述：「性別平等不僅是基本人權，更是邁向和平、繁榮及可持續世界的必要基石」。為確保女性在社會上受到公平對待，給予她們同等機會接受教育，讓她們在財務上獨立自主、在職場上擁有充裕的機遇，這些均是不可或缺的重要條件。由於家庭往往依賴隱形勞動者無償工作才得以維繫，許多不平等問題也緣自家庭內部。故此，本計劃將從家庭着手展開研究，從性別、勞工與空間的相交點切入，探索與香港家務工作相關的議題，並引起關注。 這項計劃將是首個運用設計研究方式、空間設計圖，以及民族誌式田野工作探討香港家務工的項目。現存有關家務勞動的研究通常在社會學、勞工研究和性別研究等圈子以學術論文形式傳播。然而，尚未有人考慮到性別、勞動力和空間之間的交差關係，並以空間設計方式探索此議題，繼而以圖像方式將其具體呈現。這項研究及其方法將透過各式生活體驗和空間，為城市運作和人民福祉等重要範疇作出原創貢獻。本研究側重於本地婦女和外籍家庭傭工的有償和無償家務勞動，並將透過專題學術論著、電子資料庫、Podcast 系列，還有與香港非政府組織的兩次合作活動進行傳播。 該項目將因應相關研究成果產生三大層面的知識。首先是探討香港的家務工作界別、它與全球政治經濟的關聯，以及其帶來的本地及全球影響，相關成果將透過專題學術論著發表。其次是專注研究與主題相關的空間維度，透過網站上可供瀏覽的空間圖像、圖表和照片，將城市空間和家庭生活連繫起來。由於現存學說鮮少提及空間角度，或者以之探索相關議題，此項目的電子資料庫正正旨在增加相關面向。第三是透過一系列Podcast節目增添人性化的感動情節。我們將以外籍家庭傭工以及參與家務工作的本地婦女為重點，讓她們透過Podcast這個平台講述相關經驗，令更多人能聆聽到她們的故事。總體而言，本計劃就女性在港從事有償或無償家務工作的社會空間經驗，還有其經濟影響提供了重大而有趣的見解。

To evaluate how Confucius and the Confucian classics were seen and used in Pre-Tang and early Tang times in court culture and literary creation. To investigate in what ways Wang Bo’s account of the Buddha’s life differs from the way this god was presented in Buddhist sutras before and contemporaneous with him, whereby evaluating his contribution to Chinese Buddhist history. To examine the idiosyncrasy of Wang Bo in his stele inscriptions for Confucian temples, which clearly differ from others by the injection of his own image and sentiments in the solemn settings, and discuss its contribution to the history of Chinese literature. From interdisciplinary perspectives, to bridge the study of Chinese literature and other fields such as Buddhology and Confucianism and to open up dialogues with the international research communities in the US, Japan, Taiwan, etc.

12604521.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12604521.value: 王勃（650–約676）是他生活年代即初唐時期最負盛名的作家。但學界對其傳世的文學作品的研究尚欠深入，以致於其地位並未受到應有的重視。近世湧現的關於王勃的研究著述大都以其詩歌為主要對象，較少注重其非韻體作品，而這些卻正是王勃在世時所賴以出名並獲得後代激賞的作品。本研究計劃旨在通過重新「發現」這些作品長期被忽略的重要貢獻，填補這個文學史和文化史上的欠缺。主要研究的作品所屬的「散文」體裁包括記、碑、序、書等。 本研究計劃的重點對象文本是〈益州夫子廟碑〉和〈釋迦如來成道記〉。王勃撰寫這兩篇作品的一個重要特色，是在這兩種文體規範下較為少見的個人抒情成份。這樣的研究必須依賴對前代同樣體裁和題材的作品的梳理、統計，據以考量並評價王勃的創新貢獻。本研究將從《文選》及王勃的前輩作品中選取約十篇碑文，又在佛經中選取較早期寫成或譯出的釋迦本生傳記，從比較中尋繹王勃如何跳出文體規範的內容的框架，以當時盛行的駢文形式，寫成一篇篇辭藻華麗而又風格獨特的聖人傳記，同時也為作者的自我抒情服務。 另一個研究重點是《論語》這部儒家經典在王勃作品中所見的地位。這部分研究先從王氏家族的儒學背景入手，其中最重要的是其祖父王通（584–618）所創立的儒學門派對於其門人和家族成員的影響。這些背景對於研究王勃編纂儒家經籍，以及其作品中常見的儒家思想元素，特別是《論語》的典故等方面的考察，尤具意義。

12606221.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12606221.value: 本項目旨在研究「眼」「語」關聯對兒童朗讀能力的影響。 朗讀訓練其中一項重要目的，是讓老師協助學生說話時能夠抑揚頓錯，說話動聽(如適當使用高低音去表達情感)。若干研究已表明 (一) 有效的朗讀並非純粹口部發聲，而是透過眼睛理解文字，再用口部發出悅耳的聲音；(二) 即使在默讀中，人仍能感受到自己說話，「聽到」自己的抑揚頓錯；以及(三) 眼和口在朗讀中緊密並用、環環相扣。正如若果我們默讀時沒有感受到語調(Intonation)，人就無法了解文字要表達的意思。正因為語調運用牽涉眼睛和口語，「眼」「語」關聯很有可能幫助我們理解為何某學生的朗讀能力比另一個好，某學生的朗讀能力比較弱。雖然很多學者都意識到「眼」和「語」的關聯，他們鮮有對這關聯深入研究。 最近，我們一項先導研究已初步顯示「眼」和「語」的關係。我們將在這基礎上進一步研究他們對朗讀能力的影響。研究人員將給予不同口才的兒童一系列的活動，找出是否口才了得者能夠善用眼睛觀察，而口才平庸者不能善用眼睛觀察，兩組人是否有明顯分別。透過不同的數據分析，我們找出「眼」和「語」的關聯。例如，我們會用眼動追踪器(EyeLink eye tracker)找出不同口才的人士的眼、語運用。我們採用先進技術 (如GLMMs)去找出不同組別以及不同測試之間的關係。 研究結果將會對實質教學，以及教學理論層面作出貢獻。一旦確定了「眼」「語」關聯以及了解他們如何關聯，教師便可以重新設計教學活動，例如教師可以先了解不同口才人士的分別，他們的眼睛注視甚麼，從而設計適合的朗讀活動。研究結果亦會提升我們在語調領域(English intonation)以及其他的領域，例如元思考(awareness)及意識(noticing)，的理解。

12606821.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12606821.value: 中國現代合唱音樂的跨文化性、歌詞和演出實踐

12606821.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12606821.value: 在過去一個世紀，獨特的跨文化創作及演奏實踐印證著中國合唱音樂的發展，協助塑造了中國的現代音樂景觀。然而，產生於現今中國族群之間的持續社會變遷，引起了有關語言、音樂及歌詞隨著合唱文化在新世紀不斷發展的一些關鍵問題：現代歷史情境如何把中國合唱音樂塑造成一個跨文化藝術形式？當中運用了甚麼作曲過程來揉合中國及西方音樂元素，以促成一種跨文化合唱曲目？怎樣的文字及語言系統能展示中國合唱的形式及其如何呈現出音樂感？中國的歌唱技巧及帶有聲調的口語如何被應用於一種混合的、以美聲唱法為本的演奏實踐？ 中國合唱音樂通過採納西方合唱音樂的主要組成部分而演變，包括和聲、織體、男女高低聲部分類，以及意大利式/古典的美聲唱法的聲樂美學。而目標明確地融合中華文化乃基要原則，亦同為重要。中國合唱音樂包含眾多地區的詞彙及語言，包括普通話、廣東話、台語，以及地區方言，代表了不同種族和地域，以及其對民謠和音樂元素的運用。因時制宜的中國聲樂樂種亦反映出形形色色的社會情境，而傳統歌唱風格的使用，可見於帶有民間色彩的作品之中。 本研究將探索中國合唱音樂中的跨文化、音樂及文字基礎，與構成了國際性媒介的現代歷史、國家語言，以及當代演奏實踐的關聯。本研究突顯理論預料之外的啟發—合唱音樂於（一） 中國境內地區之間，以及（二）國際之間中國與非華裔合唱社群的本質關係。本研究亦分析因時制宜的音樂元素，以及音樂和歌詞關係中的跨文化進程。研究的出版將更深入評估歷史、歌詞、語言、音樂傳統，以及社會潮流於現代中國合唱音樂界別中的互動。 通過聚焦於如此獨特的國內外文化潮流，本研究將於了解中國族群中香港的身份上呈現重大而急需的價值。因此，研究於關鍵的時代變遷中，對音樂學、民族音樂學、合唱表演實踐，以及當代中港研究的範疇上作出重大的貢獻。

12607721.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12607721.value: 關於《獅子山下》中地方感的建構，以及通過不同敘事方式重寫1970-1980年代香港地方感的實踐本位研究

12607721.label: Project Objectives
12607721.value: To interview the producers, directors, and screenwriters of Below the Lion Rock to find out how the episodes were conceptualized and filmed; the interviews will be followed by a Textual Analysis that investigates the themes and messages of Below the Lion Rock from the 1970-1980s, and explores the actual meaning of the “Hong Kong spirit” conveyed in the series. The research outcome will be used to inform the design of the Below the Lion Rock Cultural Tour as the social and cultural impact of the research. To examine why Hong Kong people consider Below the Lion Rock a mirror that reflects the life of old-time Hong Kong and manifests the “Hong Kong Spirit” through the THREE MAJOR FACTORS (Activity, Form, and Image) of the Sense of Place Theory (Montgomery, 1998) – the theory for studying the relationship between humans and places. 2a. Activity – The PI will examine the dramatized portrayal of social policies of the 1970s – 1980s (e.g. Ten-Year Housing Plan, the establishment of The Independent Commission Against Corruption (ICAC), the "Two is Enough" (「兩個夠哂數」) campaign promoted by The Family Planning Association of Hong Kong, etc.) in Below the Lion Rock to see how the docudrama re-imagined social reality, in order to analyze how Below the Lion Rock made use of the “Activity” factor (e.g. Streetlife, cultural events, etc.) to craft the sense of place of Hong Kong. 2b. Form – The PI will explore the relationship between the real-life cityscape of Hong Kong and the urban snapshots captured in Below the Lion Rock, based on the “Form” factor (e.g. landmarks, public realm, etc.) of the theory. 2c. Image- The PI will study the “Image” factor (e.g. sensory experiences evoked by things and products of 1970-1980s) adopted in Below the Lion Rock with those that appeared in governmental publicity campaigns, used by Tourist Association, textbooks, popular songs, caricatures, etc. To publish two critical papers in peer-reviewed academic journals such as Cultural Studies Quarterly and Journal of Creative Writing Studies 3a. One critical paper will be on the creative relationship between Below the Lion Rock, Hong Kong’s social development, and the “Hong Kong spirit” depicted in Below the Lion Rock; 3b. Another critical paper will be on the investigation of how Below the Lion Rock’s Grand Narrative was employed as a vehicle for incorporating the notions of “Activity”, “Form” and “Image” in the Sense of Place theory in constructing the urban identity of Hong Kong. To test the hypothesis that place-based research can be generative for creative writing through a Creative Writing workshop. To publish four creative works based on: 5a. The interviews of four Hong Kongers (who had lived in Hong Kong during the 1970s – 1980s but have backgrounds different from the characters epitomized in Below the Lion Rock, e.g. a British colonist residing in Hong Kong, a South Asian minority, an indigenous inhabitant of the New Territories, and a resident of an outlying island. 5b. The studies of four everyday objects (e.g. telephone sets, televisions, air conditioners, and MTR) which made a strong impact on the lifestyle, interpersonal distance, and community concepts of Hong Kong people. The four creative works will explore how different perspectives and images of Hong Kong during the 1970-1980s could be produced through Personal Narrative (A narrative relating to the mundane happenings of an ordinary day and extraordinary events that mark one’s lives) (Langellier, 1989) and Object-based Narrative (A narrative that focuses on the objects from a certain period and the nature of life, as illustrated by the objects) (Effros, 2011) and how practice-based research can feed into creative writing To enrich the public’s knowledge about Hong Kong’s social changes during the 1970-1980s through the publication of the four creative works, especially the impact from the popularization of telephones, televisions, and air-conditioning, and the commencement of MTR operation, which had changed the Interpersonal Relationship, Spatial Cognition of public and private spaces, and Self-Identity. The initiative will provide an opportunity to explore and fill the public’s gap of knowledge in the “Hong Kong image” and “collective memory” built by the mass media and publicity campaigns. To explore and compare the features, advantages, and limitations of the sense of place created with the Personal Narrative and Object-based Narrative approaches of the four creative works (in Point no.5) with that created in the Grand Narrative approach of Below the Lion Rock (in Point no. 4b). The research outcome will be presented in a public seminar and will inform the instructional design of the Community Creative Writing Workshop – another social and cultural impacts of this research project so that students can apply the skills in their writing.

12607921.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12607921.value: 背景： 讀寫障礙是一種學習障礙，影響一個人對單詞或字母的識別能力，因而降低閱讀和理解的準確性。 2016 年至 2019 年間，香港有特殊學習需要的兒童人數增加8.3%（財務委員會，2019-20）。 預計這增幅將繼續上升，因為公眾意識到這種特定的學習障礙若沒有得到治療可能會成為終身問題。 父母缺乏能力幫助患有讀寫障礙的孩子產生負面的親子關係影響，從而導致更多的家庭危機。 目標： 本研究的第一個目標是測試簡短而有針對性的多元家庭敘事治療對華人家庭患有讀寫障礙的孩子之成效 (MFNT) ，主要針對減少香港家庭患有讀寫障礙的孩子之家長及孩子的心理困擾，改善親子關係和增強父母對社會支援的感知。第二目標是考究這些參與MFNT的家庭成員之間的態度和互動變化過程。 方法： 本研究假設MFNT將有助於減少家長及患有讀寫障礙的孩子之心理困擾，建立健康的親子關係，並促進使用社會支援。 隨機對照試驗 (RCT) 設計，輔以質性訪談將用於評估 MFNT 的整體有效性。 一開始在這個為期 24 個月的項目中，56 個家庭患有讀寫障礙的孩子 (FCD)，總數168 個參加者將從四所本地公立小學招募。 這些家庭將在每所學校被隨機分配到治療小組（MFNT干預）和對照小組（照常治療）。 通過重複測量，此 RCT 設計表示為： 治療小組：T0 x T1 T2 對照小組：T0 T1 T2 在這個設計中，除了從 T0 到 T2 的前測和後測數據收集之外，一系列的半結構性訪談將在每個研究地點進行，探討治療後自願處理其治療經驗的家庭成員彼此之間的態度和互動變化。 意義： 這項研究將增加關於 MFNT 有效性的經驗證據。 特別是，它會評估適合華人 FCD 文化的相關要素。 其長期影響將包括使用循證實踐手冊來培訓專業人員在校如何識別及解決 FCD 的需求，以便他們能夠更有效幫助患有讀寫障礙的孩子提高適應能力及提高學業和生活學習成就。

12607921.label: Realisation of objectives
12607921.value: Quantitative Research Objective 1 has been achieved. Multiple Family Narrative Therapy (MFNT) was delivered with 1 engagement meeting and 4 intervention sessions in a group format. A total of N=54 families of children with dyslexia were recruited and were randomly assigned by site to the treatment group (n=31) or the waitlist control group (n=23). All hypotheses were assessed, and the assessments were made at three timepoints: pre-intervention (T1), post-intervention (T2), and 3-month follow-up (T3). Data were analyzed by a series of mixed-design ANOVAs. H1: Parents’ psychological distress was measured using the Kessler Psychological Distress Scale (Kessler et al., 2003). Results showed that MFNT significantly reduced the psychological distress of parents in the treatment group (T1: M = 27.026, SD = 9.105; T2: M = 22.763, SD = 7.009, T3: M = 21.789, SD = 5.950), F(2, 18) = 10.54, p = .001, partial η2 = .528, and the post hoc analysis showed that significance took place between T1 and T2 (p = .001), T1 and T3 (p = .001). There was no significant time interaction among parents in the control group. H2: Parents’ parental stress was measured by the Parental Stress Scale (Leung, C., & Tsang, S. K., 2010). Results showed that MFNT significantly reduced the parental stress of parents in the treatment group (T1: M = 64.921, SD = 13.837, T2: M = 60.763, SD = 13.877, T3: M = 48.000, SD = 12.936), F(2, 18) = 19.828, p < .001, partial η2 = .688., and the post hoc analysis showed that significance took place between T1 and T3 (p < .001). Significance was also found in control group (T1: M = 66.000, SD = 2.828, T2: M = 49.000, SD = 18.385, T3: M = 49.000, SD = 8.485), F(2, 18) = 4.784, p = .022, partial η2 = .347, post hoc analysis showed that significance took place between T1 and T2 (p = .026). There was no significant difference between the treatment group and the control group. H3: Perceived social support was measured using Guilt and Shame Questionnaire (Bosch, A., van de Ven, M., & van Doesum, K., 2020) and Satisfaction with Family Life Scale (Zabriskie, R. B., & Ward, P. J., 2013). Results showed that MFNT reduced the guilt and shame of parents in the treatment group (T1: M = 22.316, SD = 8.863, T2: M = 19.39, SD = 5.775, T3: M = 18.237, SD = 4.979), F(2, 18) = 4.593, p = .024, partial η2 = .338, and the post hoc analysis showed that significance took place between T1 and T2 (p = .020), T1 and T3 (p = .022). A significant increase in guilt and shame was found in control group (T1: M = 13.000, SD = 0.000, T2: M = 11.000, SD = 1.414, T3: M = 16.000, SD = 4.243), F(2, 18) = 4.207, p = .032, partial η2 = .319. However, there was no significant difference between the treatment group and the control group. H4: Parent-perceived parent-child relationships were measured using the Parent-Child Relationship Scale (Fine et al., 1983). No significant results were found within the treatment group and the control group. H5: Child-perceived parent-child relationships were measured using the Parental Bonding Inventory with four dimensions: indifference, overprotection, autonomy, and care (Cavedo & Parker, 1994). For perceived parental indifference, the main effects of condition, F(1,40) = 0.08, p = .785, η2 = .002, and time, F(1,40) = 0.09, p = .763, η2 = .002, were non-significant. A significant interaction effect between condition and time was found in perceived parental indifference, F(1,40) = 9.56, p = .004, η2 = .193. Specifically, perceived parental indifference at T2 (Mtreatment = 1.69, SD = 0.47) was significantly lower than that at T1(Mtreatment = 2.03, SD = 0.55) in treatment group, t(30) = 3.81, p <.001, Cohen’s d = 0.68, while no significant change between T1 and T2 was observed in control condition, t(10) = -1.24, p = .245, Cohen’s d = 0.75. These results indicated that the intervention was effective in reducing child’s perceived parental indifference. For perceived parental overprotection, the main effects of condition, F(1,40) = 2.24, p = .142, η2 = .053, and time, F(1,40) = 0.00, p = .991, η2 = .000, were non-significant. A significant interaction effect between condition and time was found in perceived parental overprotection, F(1,40) = 21.03, p = .000, η2 = .345. In particular, perceived parental overprotection at T2(Mtreatment = 1.85, SD = 0.508) was significantly lower than that at T1(Mtreatment = 2.27, SD = 0.58) in treatment group, t(30) = 4.68, p <.001, Cohen’s d = 0.84. However, perceived parental overprotection at T2 (Mcontrol = 2.51, SD = 0.33) was significantly higher than that at T1 (Mcontrol = 2.08, SD = 0.49) in control condition, t(10) = -2.39, p = .038, Cohen’s d = 0.59. For perceived parental autonomy, the main effects of condition, F(1,40) = 0.08, p = .773, η2 = .002) and time, F(1,40) = 0.64, p = .429, η2 = .016, were non-significant. No significant interaction effect between condition and time was found for perceived parental autonomy, F(1,40) = 0.01, p = .927, η2 = .000. No significant results were found within the treatment group and the control group. For perceived parental care, the main effects of condition, F(1,40) = 0.18, p = .675, η2 = .004, and time, F(1,40) = 12.42, p =.001, η2 = .237, were non-significant. A significant interaction effect between condition and time was found for perceived parental care, F(1,40) = 9.82, p = .003, η2 = .197. Nevertheless, perceived parental care at T2 (Mcontrol = 2.73, SD = 0.47) was significantly lower than that at T1(Mcontrol = 3.32, SD = 0.34) in control group, t(10)= 3.15, p =.010, Cohen’s d = 0.95, while no significant change between T1 and T2 was observed in treatment condition. Qualitative Research Objective 2 aims to examine changes in attitudes and interactions among family members participating in MFNT and assess the project's objectives. The study occurred in three stages: Stage 1 involved providing four intervention sessions based on an integrated model for the consenting first group. Stage 2 focused on analyzing process and outcome data. Stage 3 included compiling publications and reports, and revising the practice manual. Qualitative research was completed at all sites in each stage. Post-intervention, two families from each of four schools were randomly invited for interviews to provide feedback on treatment experiences, parent-child relationships, and coping mechanisms. In total, eight families shared their experiences. Semi-structured questions focused on treatment experiences, changes in attitudes and interactions, observed changes in family members, and helpful aspects of the intervention. Participants discussed stress reduction, de-stigmatization, parental expectations, coping methods, and family relationships. Data collected before, during, and after the intervention showed that participants deepened their involvement in retelling their life stories, leading to new preferred family identities. Three themes emerged: intrafamilial re-authorship, interfamilial change and empowerment, and individual therapeutic evolution.

12607921.label: Major findings and research outcome
12607921.value: Results revealed that MFNT significantly reduced parents’ psychological distress, parental distress, guilt and shame, and child’s perceived indifference and overprotection. Parents experienced a significant reduction in psychological distress, while no significant improvement in their perception of parent-child relationship. Conversely, children reported no significant reduction in their psychological distress but rated a significant reduction in their perception of parental overprotection and indifference. These findings suggest that multiple family narrative therapy might have differential effects on parents and children at intrapersonal and interpersonal level respectively. It highlights the potential of multiple family narrative therapy in eliciting positive changes in not only parental psychological distress, but also in parental behaviour and attitudes towards their children. According to the qualitative results, three themes were identified. First, intrafamilial re-authorship was found, families’ preferred identity was shifted from being a passive victim to an active fighter. Parents experienced a shift in their attention from their child's academic accomplishments to their child's emotions and effort, leading to enhanced family harmony and increased mutual tolerance. Children also expressed that their parents have exhibited increased gentleness and reduced anger towards them while assisting with school assignments. Decreased stigma and increased opportunities for engagement allow parents to become more flexible and understanding towards their child, and less controlled by academic pressure from teachers or stigmatization from others. Second, interfamilial empowerment was found among the participants, parents reported that they experienced a sense of understanding from other parents, a unique connection that they couldn't find elsewhere. This suggests that shared experiences of mutual crisis create a sense of universality, and the act of sharing those experiences fosters a supportive environment. They also noticed the impact on their children and reported that their children have become more sociable with other children both in the group and outside the group. Third, individual evolution was found, According to parental narratives, the personification of dyslexia has facilitated a process of self-reflection regarding their attitudes towards dyslexia and their child. This opportunity for reflection is often unavailable in other contexts. Personifying dyslexia enabled parents to develop a greater acceptance of their child's dyslexia and facilitates a more manageable adjustment in their expectations.

12607921.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12607921.value: This study provides empirical evidence supporting the effectiveness of multiple family narrative therapy (MFNT). We recommend future studies to: (1) implement MFNT with larger samples in various settings (e.g., schools, charitable organizations), and (2) use a longitudinal research design to study long-term effects (6 months, 12 months, etc.). Further research on parent-child dyadic intervention among Chinese families is needed, as the focus has traditionally been on changing the child rather than improving the parent-child relationship. Parents' needs are often overlooked, with emphasis placed on children's academic performance. This study introduces a new therapeutic model addressing both parents' and children's needs, particularly those with learning disabilities. By combining MFT and NT with a shorter intervention duration, the program shifts focus to include parents, reducing stigma and fostering mutual support among participants with similar concerns. This participatory and collaborative approach has potential for further theoretical exploration in China's cultural context. Developing the MFNT model further can reduce social stigma associated with Families of Children with Dyslexia (FCDs) and those with Special Educational Needs (SEN), generating academic interest in these stigmatization issues. Future studies with different SEN types, larger samples, and longer follow-up periods will provide more knowledge on treatment efficacy and sustainability.

12607921.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12607921.value: The nature of this research is in its innovative approach of utilizing MFNT specifically cater to the Chinese cultural context. By involving multiple families in therapy sessions, the project recognizes the importance of collective support and shared experiences among parents dealing with similar challenges. This participatory and collaborative therapeutic model breaks the isolation often experienced by families of children with dyslexia and reduce the stigma associated with learning disabilities. The research project’s significance is twofold. Firstly, it expands the conceptual framework of therapeutic interventions by combining NT and a Multiple Family approach, providing a novel and culturally sensitive treatment option for Chinese families. Secondly, it addresses the unmet needs of parents by focusing not only on the academic improvement of their children but also on strengthening the parent-child relationship within the family as a treatment unit. The positive outcomes of this research brought great value to the evidence-based practice, producing guidelines that inform therapists, social workers, schools and policymakers about the implementation and effectiveness of MFNT. Moreover, by reducing the social stigma surrounding dyslexia and increasing academic interest in such issue, the research project promotes inclusivity, understanding, and support for families of children with dyslexia in Chinese society.

12608821.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12608821.value: Despite the normative and tactical merits of nonviolence, violent protests remain a ubiquitous phenomenon throughout history. Many popular protests around the world began with the use of violence, while some initially peaceful protests might turn violent along the course – often as a result of protesters’ tactical escalation or the state’s decision to repress dissent by force. The causes of violence are often complex and varied, and thus much scholarly attention has been drawn to this line of inquiry, seeking explanations as to why violent protests occur. In contrast, research has been lacking regarding the impact of protest-related violence on citizens after the protests. While we know that violence plays an important role in shaping immediate protest outcomes, we know much less about how violence leaves lasting imprints on participants and non-participants in the aftermath of protests. How do protest-related violence shape citizens’ post-protest socio-political attitudes and behaviour? This study aims to fill this research gap by focusing on the case of protest-ridden Hong Kong and the legacy of the 2019 Anti-Extradition Bill Protests. Using large-n population surveys, panel surveys and focus group interviews, it investigates how and why citizens’ exposure to state violence and their perception of protesters’ violence during the protests influence their trust, tolerance, civic participation, mental well-being and attitudes towards political violence. By combining various methodological approaches, this research will produce rich and original evidence to unveil the enduring significance of protest-related violence. It will also be, to the best of our knowledge, the first study in Hong Kong to examine the impact of experiencing a massive wave of protests on individuals. Our findings will advance the comparative study of modern-day protests, inform policymakers on public sentiments and provide insights to facilitate reconciliation after political upheavals. 暴力示威是歷史上常見的現象。雖然一直以來有不少研究聚焦暴力示威背後有各種成因，但是學界卻鮮有關注這類示威發生後對參與者、非參與者和普羅大眾的影響。此研究將以香港2019年反對逃犯條例修訂草案運動為案例，嘗試填補這個學術上的缺口。研究團隊將會利用人口問卷、追蹤調查和焦點小組等方法，調查香港市民如何看待反修例運動和當中出現的各種暴力，以及運動如何影響他們的社會信任、公共參與、精神健康和其他政治態度。研究結果將會貢獻政治社會學的理論發展，並有助政府了解大型社運後的民意和促進社會和解。

12609121.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12609121.value: This project aims to reconstruct the development of Hong Kong leftist films from the inception of the Second Sino-Japanese War to Hong Kong’s return to China, and to rewrite the history of the Chinese cinema of Hong Kong in this period. This important left-wing film culture has been little studied even in Chinese-language film history, not to mention the English-language literature. Its politics, aesthetics, and socio-political criticism remain unexplored. This historical study raises important issues. How can we redefine ‘leftist cinema’ not narrowly, in terms of political ideologies or institutions, but broadly by analysing its socio-political themes, artistic visions, filmic styles, and the effects of cinematic circulation and audience reception? How can we reassess the legacies of progressive film culture? Secondly, how did filmmakers and artists negotiate individual and group identity, social-ethical criticism and market realities as they crafted their works under political censorship and socioeconomic constraints? Finally, how can the recovery of cinematic pasts and cultural histories enhance mutual understanding and cultural exchange between Hong Kongers and mainlanders, especially the younger generation? To address the first question, the PI and researchers will scrutinize government documents, film studio materials, memoirs, popular journals and newspapers to reveal the cultural politics of Chinese-language film activities in colonial Hong Kong. The PI and one Singapore-based researcher will undertake archival research in Singapore and Malaysia, where leftist cinema had a popular following in the 1950s and 1960s. The research will go beyond Hong Kong to examine the legacies of leftist films and culture in their global connections. The second issue relates to how cultural politics affected the ethics and identity of individual films. Researchers will conduct oral interviews and examine studio histories to shed light on the politico-ethical practice of veteran workers and professionals. The project adopts a two-pronged analytical approach, integrating sociohistorical analysis of film culture and a microscopic study of human agency and creativity. It will participate in current debates in Sinophone studies, Cold War history, Chinese-language film historiography, and the cultural politics of Hong Kong cinema. The research outcomes will be several international conference presentations and refereed journal articles. The impacts of the study extend beyond academia to produce new knowledge and public understanding of Hong Kong cultural history and Hong Kong-China relationships. The team will conduct outreach programs through public exhibitions, lectures, and screenings to promote knowledge transfer to the wider public. 本研究項目旨在重構香港左翼電影文化從抗日戰爭爆發到香港回歸的發展歷程，重寫這一時期香港華語電影的歷史。香港的左翼電影文化在華語電影史上以至英語學界一向鮮有研究，對它的政治、美學和社會批評的認識更是付諸闕如。我們如何重新定義“左派電影”？我們如何重新評估進步電影的文化傳承？本研究計劃提出要廣泛地分析其社會政治主題、藝術視野、電影風格、電影發行以及觀眾的接受美學來衡量。這項目會在香港進行資料搜集，口述歷史訪問，及公眾電影放映與講座。除此以外，研究人員會在新加坡搜集有關左翼電影在東南亞華語電影市場的推銷及接受歷史，以考察左派電影和文化在海外的聯繫和傳播。研究採用雙管齊下的分析方法，對電影文本、電影人的工作經驗、及政治文化與社會脈落作綜合分析，對當前有關冷戰史、華語電影史學和香港電影文化的政治論述作出貢獻。

12609221.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12609221.value: 流動的臣民：帝國邊陲下的英國國民身份與領事保護制度（~1900-1950）

12609221.label: Project Objectives
12609221.value: To investigate how and why places on the colonial periphery, such as the Chinese treaty ports, were important sites for the implementation, negotiation, and contestation of British nationality laws. To combine the approaches of legal, social, and cultural history to explore the tangible personal consequences of gaining or losing British protection or nationality for putative Britons born overseas, particularly ‘Asia-born’ children and the dependent spouses of British male settlers. To explore the ways in which individuals and different communities ‘performed’ their Britishness in their petitions for British passports or protection and the varied, albeit increasing inflexible, ways in which consuls assessed the merits of these applications. To assess the ways in which consular and Foreign Office debates about the extent to which British subjects from other sites of the British empire who lived or sojourned in China were entitled to British protection – such as Indian communities or the Straits Chinese – shaped evolving ideas about an imperial citizenship that was at once incorporative and unequal. To centre the 1914 British Nationality and Status of Aliens Act and its subsequent addendums as a major, overlooked turning point in the genealogy of colonial-era nationality legislation, which had far-reaching consequences for many putative Britons overseas. To explore how the introduction of modern state technologies of identification, such as the passport, sought to establish and document individual, communal, national and imperial identities. To disentangle the contested categories of British subject and protected person in the Chinese treaty ports and to consider the ways in which these categories shifted in response to metropolitan directives/legislation and local political conditions.

12609221.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12609221.value: How was membership of a political community defined and what did it mean for individuals on the edges of empire, where the state was often remote and where multi-level forms of belonging existed? Focusing principally on the Chinese treaty ports with comparative material from, Japan, Siam (Thailand) and Egypt, this research will elucidate the importance of political and social contexts on the colonial periphery to the trial, interpretation, and contestation of British nationality legislation in the first half of the twentieth century. A major aim is to investigate how the specific political and social conditions of colonial sites beyond the boundaries of the territorial British empire, particularly the existence of extraterritorial legal regimes and cosmopolitan demographics, brought to the forefront the tension between inclusive ideals of universal imperial citizenship and a contradictory impulse to contain cross- colonial migration by narrowing the eligibility criteria for British nationality. In doing so, this study will demonstrate how analysis of Britishness overseas must be anchored in specific local legal, demographic, and political conditions rather than only sentiment and identity. This research will establish how individual, community, national, and imperial identities – and the tensions between them – were negotiated and established through technologies of control and identification, such as the passport. Examination of petitions for British passports or protected person status in extra-imperial sites demonstrate how settlers and expatriates performed their Britishness to consuls charged with enforcing nationality laws, often by asserting links to British institutions and people rather than bona fide legal credentials. Consular deliberations about these applications, on the other hand, bring to light subjective understandings of imperial loyalties, and the extent to which they were perceived to be dissipated by place, race, and gender. Above all, this project seeks to integrate humanity into legal history by elucidating the profound ways in which the enforcement of increasingly narrow definitions of British citizenship overseas impinged upon the lived experiences of liminal individuals and communities. The research will highlight the experiences of three groups of people whose national statuses were frequently contested: 1) children born to a British parent outside of British territory; 2) formerly British women married to Chinese subjects and women of other nationalities married to British subjects, and 3) British imperial subjects who sought to assert British national and legal identities in the course of cross-colonial travels to semicolonial sites, such as the Chinese treaty ports. 在遠離母國管治的帝國邊陲，英國臣民往往擁有多重身份歸屬。他們是怎樣被識別為英籍成員？英籍身份對他們又有何意義？本研究透過中國、日本、泰國與埃及等地的史料，分析中國條約港口的政治和社會狀況。由於享有治外法權和多元的人口結構，這些非英國屬土擁有特殊的政治社會形態。它們體現了20世紀上半葉英國國籍立法過程的內部張力，也反映了20世紀上半葉英國國籍立法過程的不同嘗試、詮釋與爭議：在接納普世臣民為英國國民的理想背後，同時也包含收緊國民識別方法、限制殖民地之間移民的現實考慮。本研究將指出，「海外英國性」的研究必須建基於海外特定的法制、人口、政治狀況，不能只限於族群情感和身份認同兩方面。 另外，本研究將透過包括護照在內的身份識別與管理科技，探討國民身份在個體、社群、國族、帝國四個層面之間所呈現的張力與調和。本研究將融合人文學科與法制史角度，深入探討三類英籍身份存疑人士。第一類是英籍父或母在非英國屬土所生子女；第二類是嫁給中國男性的英籍婦女、及嫁給英籍男性的其他國籍婦女；第三類是透過移民至中國條約港口等半殖民地城市，嘗試爭取英國國籍及法律認可的大英帝國臣民。這三類人的生活經歷，能夠反映英國逐漸收緊的國籍政策，對海外臣民所產生的深遠影響。

12609621.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12609621.value: The impact of the built environment on travel behavior has received extensive research attention around the world over the past decades. Different study designs and various sophisticated modeling approaches have been used to estimate the impact. However, most of the existing studies assume that the impact of the built environment on travel behavior is time-invariant, ignoring the fact that such impact may change over time especially over the course of urban expansion. Recognizing these long-term trends are crucial to accurately evaluate the influence of land use policies on transport demand. Further, there is a long-time debate on the existence of a stable time budget that people are willing to spend on daily travel. Urban expansion may lead to further apart of activity locations such as home and workplace and thus the need for longer travel time. On the other hand, the spatiotemporal constraints limit people’s time available for daily travel. Investigating the dynamics of the built environment and travel behavior will shed light on the constant travel time budget hypothesis. To fill these gaps in the literature, this research is proposed to utilize data from periodical travel surveys that are usually conducted in major cities to investigate the built environment-travel behavior connection from a long-term dynamic perspective. We will first explore the dynamic trends of both the built environment and travel behavior over the course of decades. Methods like propensity score matching (PSM) and hierarchical age-period-cohort (HAPC) model would be used to address the age, period, and cohort effect in travel behavioral changes. We shall pay special attention to the trends of daily travel time to shed light on the constant travel time budget hypothesis. Further, we shall apply latent class structural equation model (SEM) to examine the long-term dynamics of land use impacts on travel behavior. We propose to conduct the empirical study in Shenzhen, China for the urban expansion and transport developments that Shenzhen has experienced over the past decades and the availability of large scale household travel surveys in multiple years. Academically, this research will enrich the literature on the built environment-travel behavior connection with a dynamic perspective and provide evidence concerning the constant travel time budget hypothesis. Practically, the outcomes of this project will deliver useful policy information for future urban planning and land use-based mobility strategies, especially for cities in emerging economies. 在過去的幾十年裡，建築環境對出行行為的影響在世界範圍內受到了廣泛的研究關注。不同的研究設計和各種複雜的建模方法已被用於估計影響。然而， 大多數現有研究假設建成環境對出行行為的影響是不隨時間變化的，忽略了這種影響可能會隨著時間的推移而發生變化的事實，尤其是在城市擴張過程中。認識到這些長期趨勢是準確評估土地利用政策對交通需求的影響至關重要。 此外，關於人們願意在日常旅行中花費的穩定時間預算的存在存在長期爭論。城市擴張可能導致家庭和工作場所等活動地點的距離更遠，因此需要更長的旅行時間。另一方面，時空限制限制了人們可用於日常出行的時間。研究建築環境和出行行為的動態变化將有助于验证恆定出行時間預算的假設。 為了填補文獻中的這些空白，本研究擬利用通常在主要城市定期進行的出行調查的數據，從長期動態的角度調查建築環境與出行行為的聯繫。我們將首先探索幾十年來建築環境和旅行行為的動態趨勢。諸如傾向得分匹配 (PSM) 和分層年齡-時期-隊列 (HAPC) 模型等方法將用於解決年齡、時期、以及旅行行為變化的隊列效應。我們將特別關注每日旅行時間的趨勢，以闡明恆定旅行時間預算的假設。此外，我們將應用潛在類結構方程模型 (SEM) 來檢查土地利用對出行行為影響的長期動態。我們建議在中國深圳進行城市擴張和交通發展的實證研究。在學術上，這項研究將豐富關於建成環境-出行行為的動態聯繫的文獻觀點並提供有關恆定旅行時間預算假設的證據。實xiang際应用上，本课题的研究成果將為未來城市規劃和基於土地利用的交通策略提供重要参考。

12609821.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12609821.value: 評估專門技能對雙模態與單模態雙語優勢的影響：手語傳譯員與口語傳譯員之對比研究

12609821.label: Co - Investigator(s)
12609821.value: Dr Hunt, Danielle I. J. Prof Liu, Min-hua Dr Macnamara, Brooke

12609821.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12609821.value: Evidence from research on bilingualism has prompted the ‘bilingual advantage hypothesis’, positing that language control is needed when two languages are processed and such a control during bilingual processing enhances cognitive functioning. However, investigations have shown that, compared with bilinguals who are fluent in two spoken languages (unimodal bilinguals), those who use a signed language and a spoken language (sign-speech or bimodal bilinguals) do not seem to show a bilingual advantage (Emmorey, Luk, et al., 2008). It is assumed that the different language modalities (one signed and one spoken) in bimodal bilinguals allow simultaneous production of two languages and reduce the demands for language control because the two languages do not compete for the same articulatory output system (Emmorey, et al., 2016). Past studies often involve participants whose bilingual competency and experience are too diverse, making a comparison among studies difficult. Comparing bimodal and unimodal interpreters, highly advanced bilinguals who practice switching between two languages as a profession, can provide a window into whether bilingual advantage is modality specific. This study (the Bimodal Study) is an extension of an ongoing GRF supported study, “Assessing the scope of expertise-driven advantages in bilinguals: A comparison of interpreters and translators” (the Unimodal Study), where we gauge participants’ cognitive functioning in unimodal (speech-speech) interpreters, translators, interpreting students, and non-interpreter unimodal bilinguals to see if long-term engagement in an extreme bilingual activity such as simultaneous interpreting has significant consequences on cognitive abilities. The participants in this proposed Bimodal Study will be bimodal professional interpreters, students who receive interpreting training, and an age-matched control group composed of non-interpreter bimodal bilinguals, including students. The data from both groups of students will be collected three times throughout the two years when they receive their respective training. The data from professional interpreters and non-interpreter bilinguals will be collected one time and their performance in the various cognitive tests will be compared with students’ performance in the same tests. The same set of validated tests adopted for the Unimodal Study will be used in the Bimodal Study. We will compare the results from both studies to see if language modality is a differentiating factor for any observed effects, and if yes, how task demands associated with different modalities are manifested in the impacts on cognitive functions. Our unique approach to comparing two groups of bilinguals with different language modalities can shed light on the adaptive capacity of bilingual cognitive systems. 雙語研究依相關證據提出｢雙語優勢論｣，假設在處理雙語的過程中需要用到語言掌控機制，並預期使用這種掌控機制會強化認知功能。但另有研究顯示，與精通兩種口語的雙語者（單模雙語者）相比，使用手語和口語的雙語者（雙模雙語者）似乎並沒有雙語優勢 (Emmorey, Luk, et al., 2008)。假設指出，雙模雙語者因能利用不同語言模態（手語和口語）同時產生兩種語言，兩種語言不會用到相同的發音系統，因而減少對語言掌控之需求（Emmorey , et al., 2016)。參與前人研究之雙語者通常雙語能力和經驗相當不同，使得研究之間難以比較。傳譯員精通雙語，專業工作涉及兩種語言之轉換。欲了解雙語優勢是否與特定雙語模態有關，比較雙模和單模傳譯員是可行的作法。本「雙模研究」是我們「評估專門技能對雙語優勢的影響：口譯員與筆譯員之對比研究」（進行中的GRF「單模研究」）之延伸。在「單模研究」中，我們比較單模口譯員、筆譯員、口譯學生，以及一般單模雙語者之認知功能，以觀察長期從事高度挑戰之雙語活動（如同聲傳譯）是否對認知能力產生重大影響。本「雙模研究」之參與者是雙模專業傳譯員、接受傳譯培訓的學生，以及由一般雙模雙語者（包括學生）組成的年齡匹配對照組。兩組學生的數據將在他們接受各自培訓的兩年內分三次收集。專業傳譯員和一般雙語者的數據將一次收集。其在各種認知測試中的表現並將與學生在同樣認知測試之表現相互比較。在單模研究中採用的同一組認知測試將用於雙模研究。我們將比較兩項研究之結果，觀察語言模態是否能解釋可能看到的不同現象，並檢視不同模態的任務需求如何體現對認知功能之影響。我們比較兩組不同語言模式的雙語傳譯員，方法獨特，可能揭示雙語認知系統之可塑性。

12610221.label: Project Objectives
12610221.value: To extend the horizon of literary studies beyond the conventional discipline by crossing into the boundaries of medical humanities. To bridge the gap between the literary art and health science by infusing literature with medical methods and knowledge while broadening the vision of scientific research with humanistic concerns. To address the COVID-19 problems through literature, particularly in the form of online diary, the daily-based documentary literary genre that first appeared on social media through the internet. To compare and contrast the different situations and understandings of the pandemic as an international issue in both China and America. To reexamine women’s writings in the face of public crisis by analyzing COVID diaries as both a feministic form and a therapeutic method. To examine internet censorship, especially in mainland China, and investigate how it has affected the epidemic. To prepare for the post-pandemic world with concerns raised in the epidemic writings.

12610221.label: Realisation of objectives
12610221.value: All of the listed objectives have been realized. 1. An interdisciplinary study of health humanities has been achieved through an investigation of eleven epidemic writings. 2. The gap between literary art and health science has been bridged by reading the narratives from the medical perspective and broadening the horizon of scientific research with humanistic concerns. 3. The COVID-19 problems, including both physical and psychological, have been addressed through a study of online diaries posted on a variety of social media platforms. 4. The different situations and understandings of the pandemic as a global crisis have been compared and contrasted between the journals composed in China and America. 5. Women’s writings as "sedatives" in the face of the public health crisis have been analyzed in terms of feminine sensitivity and sensibilities. 6. The post-pandemic outlook has been discussed through an open online dialogue between Dr. Luk Che Chung, JP, in Hong Kong and Ms. Jiang Xue, a Chinese journalist in New York. 12610221.label: Major findings and research outcome
12610221.value: The project researched the role of journal keeping in the time of coronavirus from China to America, focusing on mainland and overseas Chinese women’s writings of this pandemic in the form of a diary. Amidst the COVID-19 pandemic and geopolitical tensions between the People’s Republic of China and the United States of America, this daily-based documentary genre appeared on the internet and provided nuanced individual perspectives in contrast to the grand official narrative and stimulated heated debates. From Ai Xiaoming’s “Wuhan Diary” to Zhang Lan’s “New Yorkers in the Epidemic,” Dou Wanru’s “Notes on New York’s Epidemic” and Wang Ruochong’s “New York Epidemic Diary,” then to Jiang Xue’s “Chang’an Decameron,” I explored how these literary logs have recorded everyday activities and emotional changes during the outbreak, what personal stories of the disadvantaged and marginalized told us about the human cost and social impacts of the disaster beyond the governments’ grand narratives, and why they have become so popular and controversial. Relating the genre to gender, I found eleven women writers’ diaries that provide their readers with feminine perspectives of the plight. The phenomenon demonstrates diary-writing as therapy against the trauma of the plague. The multifaceted mode of these writings is made possible by a prosaic style that not only contains a variety of contents but also embraces the voices from all walks of life in different tones, including those of the women writers themselves who negotiated their gender as well as ethnic identity in the difficult time of COVID-19.

12610221.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12610221.value: The research has the potential for further developments in different directions, including but not limited to: 1. Rhetorical study, such as the use of humor and satire in the women’s digital diaries, which I have attempted in the second paper that I have just produced. 2. Stylistic study, the genre of the diary can be further explored in its past and present forms, for example, Samuel Pepys’s (1633-1703) journal about the Great Plague of London from 1665 to 1666 and the emerging diary blogs; in fact, I have been giving public lectures about historical and fictional diaries and will continue to do so. 3. Thematic study, e.g., wartime diaries that record the epoch and reveal personal emotions and thoughts, which can be another GRF project.

12610221.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12610221.value: The research explores the role of literature during the time of the coronavirus from China to America, focusing on mainland and overseas Chinese women’s writings about this pandemic in the form of diaries, the daily-based documentary literary genre, first appearing on the internet. From Chinese city lockdown diaries to notes on the New York outbreak, the project examines how these literary records of everyday life and emotions are different from official figures and reports of the outbreak, what personal stories of the disadvantaged and marginalized tell us about the human cost and social impacts of the disaster beyond the governments’ grand narratives, and why they become so popular and controversial. These women diarists provide their readers with feminine perspectives of the pandemic and inspire them to write about their own lives during difficult times. In response to their diaries, there have appeared not only numerous comments but also follow-up diary entries. The phenomenon is important as it indicates common netizens’ need to carry on writing as therapy against the trauma of the plague.

12610921.label: Project Objectives
12610921.value: 探討明治年間日本學者翻譯歐美倫理文獻，主要包括《西國立志篇》(中村正直譯,1871)、《童蒙教草》(福澤諭吉譯,1872)、《訓蒙叢談》(海老名普譯,1873)、《泰西勸善訓蒙後篇》(箕作麟祥譯,1873)，分析日本小學教科書在學習西學過程中作出的轉變，並進一步闡釋它們對中國童蒙讀本轉型帶來的影響。 以康有為弟子陳子褒和盧湘父所編寫的蒙書為研究對象，探討晚清塾師上溯《爾雅》和《廣雅》，以及參照宋、元、明間中國通俗日用類書的知識門類；且在西學和日本小學教育改革的影響下，他們重構晚清童蒙讀本的知識體系，藉此勾勒中國在百日維新前至國民政府成立的20多年間小學教育現代化的過程。 以晚清中國維新時期中、日文化交流為視點，比較明治年間日本小學讀本與陳子褒自日本回國後所撰寫蒙書的異同，揭示晚清塾師遵照日本小學教育改革，在程度分級、讀本課題、讀本繪圖和史地教科書等各方面，改良中國傳統蒙書，促使中國小學教育走向現代化。 通過分析日本橫濱學校編寫的小學讀本，比較康門弟子陳子褒、盧湘父和林奎三人蒙書的異同，勾勒晚清塾師在傳統儒家教育與日本小學讀本之間的决擇取捨，包括傳統蒙書的表述方式、思想內涵和語言運用等。 在日本小學教育和蒙特梭利教學法的啟迪下，陳子褒認為兒童學習興趣是編寫蒙書的首要條件。在這方面，本文重新檢視中國傳統知識分子的幼學觀點，特別是王陽明學派倡議的教育法，剖析中國傳統幼學與西學和日學的異同，揭示它們與國民政府教育部倡議「以兒童為中心」為教育宗旨的傳承關係。 從晚清西方語言學的傳入，分析陳子褒根據《馬氏文通》的語法理論，闡釋蒙書內的字詞詞性，兼探討他通過語素構詞方式，增強兒童的聯想力，使蒙書知識能夠更有效地傳授。 分析陳子褒通過粵語的書寫特點，提高粵地婦孺閱讀蒙書的能力，且從中揭示晚清童蒙讀本在文言、白話和粵語三者共同使用中，所呈現出來的社會價值觀。
