14100021.label: Realisation of objectives
14100021.value: With reference to the objectives below, I would like to note that we revised the mechanistic gene target. The original therapeutic axis was YY1/OGT/SERCA2, however, we were unable to rescue the phenotype by overexpressing OGT or SERCA2 as originally planned. Instead, we identified a new target - insulin - that is directly regulated by YY1 in pancreatic β cells. We have published these findings, with a correspondingly updated title: “YY1 regulates glucose homeostasis by controlling insulin transcription in pancreatic β cells” (Liu D… Lui KO, Diabetes 2022; 71:961–977). Further details, mapped to the original objectives, are provided below. The results mentioned in below figures refer to those published figures in Liu et al., Diabetes, 2022. A detailed summary is available on the additional pages to this completion report. Aim 1. To examine expression pattern & requirement of beta cell YY1 during development Under this aim, we have investigated the expression pattern & requirement of beta cell YY1. We studied the YY1 expression profile during embryonic and neonatal development until adulthood, in both human and mouse. Our results showed that the expression level of YY1 has increased dramatically after birth in both human and mouse pancreatic beta cells. This might suggest that YY1 could be more important for β-cell function in the postnatal pancreas (Fig 1). We then attempted to study β-cell function in the neonatal and adult pancreas. We generated a conditional knockout mouse (cKO) line, Pdx1CreERT/+;Yy1fl/fl, by crossing Pdx1CreERT/+ with Yy1fl/fl (control). In cKO mice, Yy1 expression in mature β-cells can be temporally ablated because Cre recombinase is only activated in β-cells to remove the Yy1 cassette via loxP recognition at specific time points after Tamoxifen (Tam) induction. We investigated their body weight, fed blood glucose levels, fasting blood glucose levels, and performed intraperitoneal glucose tolerance testing on neonatal and adult cKO mice, compared with the respective control littermates. Our findings uncovered that β-cell loss of Yy1 resulted in an early onset of diabetes manifested as hyperglycemia, glucose intolerance, and progressive loss of β-cell mass in both neonates and adults (Fig 2-3). Aim 2: To examine how YY1 is downregulated in adult beta cells during diabetes We have cultured the MIN6 beta cell line in pro-inflammatory cytokines such as IL-6, TNFα or IFNγ for 1-3 days; and confirm that these cytokines did not alter the expression levels of YY1 by western blot (data not shown). Moreover, we cultured MIN6 cells with anti-inflammatory cytokines such as IL-10 and TGFβ and demonstrated that YY1 expression was also not changed compared to controls (data not shown). Our findings indicate that YY1 expression was not governed by the inflammatory state of diabetes. Aim 3 To examine the molecular mechanisms by which YY1 regulates glucose metabolism in adult beta cells In this aim, we proposed to identify the YY1 mediated O-GlcNAcylated targets in the adult beta cells; to determine if the YY1/OGT axis regulates insulin synthesis; and/or insulin secretion. Unexpectedly, we tried to rescue OGT expression in YY1 cKO mice. OGT overexpression did not rescue glucose homeostasis after beta cell-specific loss of Yy1. We therefore focused on identify new direct gene target(s) of YY1 in this aim with the following new findings: To evaluate the potential mechanisms by which YY1 regulates adult pancreatic β-cell function, we performed genome-wide bulk RNA-seq with islets purified from cKO and control mice. RNA-seq results has defined dysregulated insulin signalling and defective glucose responsiveness in beta cells devoid of YY1. To further determine the direct targets of YY1 that regulate pancreatic β-cell function, we performed ChIP-seq analysis of mouse islets. We identified 37 differentially expressed protein-coding genes from our RNA-seq data that showed binding peaks of YY1, 36 of which displayed the canonical core motif sequence as determined by ChIP-seq. Among these genes, 7 were upregulated and 30 were downregulated in cKO islets, indicating that YY1 could act as both a repressor and an activator for regulating gene expression. Next, we performed enrichment analyses with global histone modification profiling targeting H3K4me1 for primed enhancers, H3K27ac for active enhancers, and H3K27me3 for poised enhancers in pancreatic β-cells. By integrating data from RNA-seq, YY1 ChIP-seq and histone H3 ChIP-seq analyses of pancreatic islets, we found that the Ins1 and Ins2 genes were potentially regulated by YY1. Further analyses through luciferase reporter assays, loss- and gain-of-function experiments demonstrate that YY1 binds to the enhancer regions in exon 2 of Ins1 and Ins2, activating insulin transcription and, therefore, proinsulin and insulin production in pancreatic beta cells. We also showed that YY1 directly interacts with RNA polymerase II, potentially stabilising the enhancer-promoter interaction in the multiprotein-DNA complex during transcription initiation (Fig 4-5). Aim 4 To examine if overexpression of OGT/SERCA2 rescues diabetes in iβYY1-KO mice The original plan to demonstrate that YY1 regulates insulin synthesis, secretion and/or beta cell survival in vivo via the YY1/OGT/SERCA2 axis. Given that our rescue experiments failed to confirm that OGT/SERCA2 can functionally rescue the loss of YY1, we further investigate whether YY1 regulates beta cell survival or metabolic behavior: To determine if β-cell dysfunction after YY1 ablation resulted from increased cell death, we performed immunostaining for INS and cleaved caspase 3 (cCASP3) in frozen pancreatic sections collected at 2 weeks after Tam treatment. INS+cCASP3+ cells were hardly detected in cKO and control islets (Supplementary Fig. 3A), and the number of cCAPS3+ cells per cKO and control islet was not significantly different (Supplementary Fig. 3B). To determine if β-cell dysfunction resulted from increased DNA damage, we also performed immunostaining for INS and phospho(p)-γH2AX, which marks chromatin areas flanking double-stranded DNA breaks. Our results revealed no staining of p-γH2AX in INS+ β-cells in either cKO or control islets (Supplementary Fig. 3C). We then conducted a study to see if mitochondrial dysfunction is detected at 2 weeks after Tam treatment in Pdx1CreER;YY1fl/fl mice. Immunostaining for INS and MitoSOX Red did not reveal a significant difference in the accumulation of mitochondrial-specific reactive oxygen species in β-cells of cKO and control mice (Supplementary Fig. 4A). Tetramethylrhodamine, ethyl ester immunostaining (Supplementary Fig. 4B) or flow cytometry (Supplementary Fig. 4C), respectively, revealed no significant difference in the mitochondrial membrane potential of INS+ β-cells or isolated islets of cKO and control mice. RT-qPCR analyses also showed no significant difference in the expression levels of the mitochondrial gene cytochrome C (Cycs) in cKO and control islets (Supplementary Fig. 4D). Our data showed YY1 ablation does not directly contribute to β -cell death or mitochondrial dysfunction in β -cells. β-cells treated with Yy1 siRNA or lentivirus-mediated stable Yy1 knockdown had significantly downregulated gene expression of Ins1 and Ins2 and significantly reduced INS production, whereas β-cells treated with the Yy1 overexpression plasmid had significantly upregulated gene expression of Ins1 and Ins2 and significantly increased INS production. We further performed glucose-sensing INS secretion (GSIS) assays and INS tolerance test. Our results indicated that YY1 controlled the biosynthesis rather than secretion or sensitivity of INS by regulating the transcription of Ins1 and Ins2 in β-cells.

14100021.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14100021.value: The findings of this research uncovered a novel role for YY1 as a transcriptional activator of insulin gene expression, assisting β-cell maturation and function after birth. These results could advance our understanding of beta-cell biology and provide clinically relevant insights targeting disease-related INS biosynthesis, including diabetes or even cancer.

14100021.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14100021.value: We are able to figure out the mechanism by which YY1 regulates glucose homeostasis and beta cell function through a novel regulatory pathway: In this study, we found that YY1 was ubiquitously expressed in both human and mouse pancreatic β-cells after birth. Nevertheless, the physiological role of YY1 during β-cell development and the molecular mechanism by which YY1 regulates β-cell function remain largely unknown. By generating the Pdx1CreERT/+;Yy1fl/fl mice, we temporally deleted Yy1 in β-cells during neonatal and adult development. After Tam treatment, these mice developed hyperglycemia, impaired glucose tolerance, and reduced β-cell mass in both neonates and adults. Moreover, they also displayed hypoinsulinemia with normal INS sensitivity compared with the control mice, manifesting as a type 1 diabetic phenotype. Through integrative transcriptomic, genomic, and epigenomic data mining, we revealed an unappreciated role of YY1 as a transcriptional activator of the Ins gene in pancreatic β-cells. The results of this proposal are published in Liu et al., Diabetes, 2022 with RGC GRF grant 14100021 acknowledged in the paper.

14100121.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14100121.value: 肺動脈高壓 (PAH) 是一種危害人類健康的全球性公共衛生疾病，可發生於任何年齡人群，老年人發病率較高。持續性、不可逆的血管重塑是 PAH 的主要病理特徵。然而，大多數 PAH 靶向藥物（主要是血管舒張劑）僅對輕度至中度 PAH 患者（I-II 期）有效，而對血管重構嚴重的晚期（III-IV 期）PAH 患者效果不佳。深入理解肺血管重塑的發生機制，對於開發更有效的 PAH 治療靶點至關重要。 我們的預實驗結果表明，在人肺動脈內皮細胞（PAEC）中，轉化生長因子-β2（TGF-β2）誘導 Smad3 磷酸化和內皮間充質轉化（EndMT ）相關基因表達方面的能力比 TGF-β1 更強。基於上述結果，我們設想內皮 TGF-β2 可能通過誘導 EndMT 參與肺血管重塑和 PAH 的發生。 通過本項目研究，我們將首次闡明內皮 TGF-β2 在 PAH 發病中的作用；探索 TGF-β2 下游新的關鍵信號分子，以深入理解 TGF-β2 和 EndMT 之間的關聯；我們還將探討 TGF-β2小分子抑制劑是否具有治療PAH的潛力。

14100121.label: Major findings and research outcome
14100121.value: The present project reveals the critical role of endothelial TGF-β2 in the pathogenesis of pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH). We found that TGF-β2, but not TGF-β1 or TGF-β3, is significantly upregulated in the pulmonary arterial endothelial cells (PAECs) of both PAH patients and SuHx-induced PAH mice. TGF-β2 is more potent than TGF-β1 in inducing endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EndMT), a key process driving vascular remodeling in PAH. Mechanistically, hypoxia-induced dephosphorylation of 4E-BP1 suppresses the translation of Nrf2, thereby relieving its inhibitory effect on TGF-β2 transcription. Activation of Nrf2 via KEAP1 knockdown or dimethyl itaconate (DMI) treatment effectively suppresses TGF-β2 expression and attenuates EndMT. Furthermore, endothelial-specific knockout or knockdown of TGF-β2 mitigates SuHx-induced PAH, as evidenced by reduced right ventricular systolic pressure (RVSP), right ventricular hypertrophy index (RVHI), and vascular remodeling. Administration of a TGF-β2 neutralizing antibody also alleviates PAH progression in mice. These findings highlight TGF-β2 as a central mediator in PAH and identify the 4E-BP1/Nrf2/TGF-β2 axis as a promising therapeutic target. We are now preparing a manuscript for submission in January 2026.

14100121.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14100121.value: Our study opens several avenues for future research and therapeutic development: 1. Mechanistic Deepening: Further elucidate the downstream signaling pathways of TGF-β2 in EndMT and vascular remodeling, including non-Smad pathways and cross-talk with other PAH-related pathways such as BMPR2. 2. Therapeutic Optimization: Evaluate the efficacy and safety of long-term TGF-β2 neutralization or Nrf2 activation in larger animal models and eventually in clinical settings. 3. Combination Therapy: Explore the synergistic effects of TGF-β2 inhibitors with existing PAH therapies (e.g., prostacyclin analogues, endothelin receptor antagonists) to enhance treatment outcomes. 4. Biomarker Development: Investigate serum TGF-β2 levels as a potential diagnostic or prognostic biomarker for PAH in human cohorts. 5. Drug Delivery Systems: Develop targeted delivery systems for TGF-β2 neutralizing antibodies or Nrf2 activators to enhance pulmonary vascular specificity and minimize systemic side effects.

14100121.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14100121.value: Our research explores the role of TGF-β2 in pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH), a serious lung disease that leads to high blood pressure in the lungs and heart failure. We found that TGF-β2 is highly active in the blood vessels of PAH patients and drives harmful changes in blood vessel cells. By blocking TGF-β2, either through genetic methods or with a neutralizing antibody, we were able to reduce disease symptoms in mice. We also discovered that increased Nrf2 can suppress TGF-β2. This means that drugs activating Nrf2 could offer a new way to treat PAH. Our findings are significant because they reveal a new target for therapy and could lead to better treatment for patients suffering from this life-threatening disease.

14101121.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14101121.value: 腎臟是 SARS-CoV-2 病毒的靶器官，導致 1/3 的重症 COVID-19 患者出現急性腎損傷 (AKI)。糖尿病是 COVID-19 的危險因素，然而，糖尿病患者 SARS-CoV-2 相關 AKI 的機制不清，無特異有效療法。我們前期研究發現腎臟特異性過度表達 SARS-CoV-2核殼 (N) 蛋白會導致嚴重的AKI，伴有大量腎小管壞死、血清肌酐升高和高死亡率，尤其是那些老齡合併有糖尿病腎病 的db/db小鼠。機制研究發現，SARS-CoV-2 N蛋白可與糖基化終產物受體 (RAGE) 結合以激活 Smad3 而引起腎小管細胞死亡，併通過激活 Mincle-Syk-NF-kB 途徑引起腎臟細胞因子風暴，進一步加重 SARS-CoV-2 N 蛋白誘導的 AKI。最更要的是，应用Smad3 抑製劑 SIS3 可治療SARS-CoV-2 N 蛋白誘導的 AKI。基於這些初步但新的觀察結果，我們假設 SARS-CoV-2 N 蛋白可能通過 Smad3 依賴性機制誘發嚴重糖尿病AKI。靶向抑製Smad3 可能是治療 SARS-CoV-2 N 蛋白誘導的糖尿病 AKI 的一種新療法。所以，我們計劃通過：1) 確定 SARS-CoV-2 N是誘導糖尿病db/db小鼠 AKI的病毒蛋白； 2) 通过基因敲除技術，探討Smad3 在SARS-CoV-2 N蛋白誘導 AKI 的作用機制； 3) 使用 Smad3 抑製劑 SIS3 開發抗SARS-CoV-2 N 蛋白誘導 AKI 的新療法。我們預期： SARS-CoV-2 N 蛋白是誘導 AKI 的致病分子，可引起老齡db/db小鼠嚴重AKI；Smad3是SARS-CoV-2 N 蛋白誘導 AKI 的核心機制，SARS-CoV-2 N蛋白可以通過Smad3-p21G1細胞週期阻滯機制引起腎小管細胞死亡，觸發Mincle-Syk-NF-kB 炎症通路，M1巨噬細胞激活和“細胞因子風暴”；Smad3抑制劑SIS3可能是COVID-19糖尿病AKI患者 的一種新的有效療法。這項研究的結果將在科學上和臨床上對防治 COVID-19 AKI有生重大影響。

14101121.label: Major findings and research outcome
14101121.value: We have very successfully completed all 3 Specific Aims with several novel and important findings. We first identified a pathogenic role of SARS-CoV-2 N protein in AKI. By using the ultrasound-microbubble gene transfer technique, we are able to kidney-specifically overexpressing SARS-CoV-2 N protein in the mouse kidney to induce AKI with more severe clinical outcomes in those diabetic mice with older age and underlying kidney disease. These findings support the clinical notion that diabetes is a risk factor in COVID-19 AKI, particularly in those with older age and underlying diabetic kidney disease. We then uncovered that SARS-CoV-2 N protein induces AKI via the Smad3-p21/p16 and Ripk3/MLKL death pathways as SARS-oV-2 N can bind and activate Smad3 directly to induce tubular cell necrosis via activating p21/p16 and Ripk3/MLKL-dependent cell death pathways. We also identified that SARS-CoV-2 N can activate M1 macrophages to produce abundant cytokines via a HMGB1-Mincle-Syk-NF-kB dependent mechanism. This finding may well explain the “cytokine storm” in critical ill COVD-19 patients clinically. Finally, we uncovered the regulatory role and mechanisms of Smad3 in COVID-19 AKI as mice and cells lacking Smad3 are protected from SARS-CoV-2 N-induced tubular cell death and AKI in vivo and in vitro by inactivating the Smad3-dependent p21/p16 and Ripk3/MLKL-mediated cell death pathways. We have also developed a novel therapy for SARS-CoV-2 N protein-induced AKI in db/db mice with Smad3 inhibitors including SIS3 and quercetin, a Traditional Chinese herd compound. We found that treatment with SIS3 or quercetin can effectively inhibit Smad3 signaling and therefore attenuates SARS-CoV-2 N-induced AKI in both db/m and db/db mice by blocking p21/p16 and Ripk3/MLKL-mediated AKI. All these findings have been published in Adv Sci (2022 Jan;9(3): e2103248); Signal Transduct Target Ther (2023 Apr 7;8(1):147); Mol Ther (2023 Feb 1;31(2):344-361); and Frontiers in Immunology (2023 Nov 3; 14:1264447). By establishing a collaborative study with Guangdong Provincial People's Hospital, we successfully secured a Greater Bay Area Grant to establish a Guangdong-Hong Kong Joint Labs for Genetic and Immunological Kidney Disease. Through this collaboration, we have completed this grant with total of 6 joint publications and a joint Chinese Patent filed (See Part C: Research Output). In addition, a PhD student, Liying LIANG, and a Hong Kong Scholar, Dr Wang Wenbiao, have been trained successfully. Dr Liang has passed her thesis examination and Dr Wang has been promoted to Associate Professor in Guangdong Provincial People's Hospital.

14101121.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14101121.value: The identification of SARS-CoV-2-induced cell death in mouse models of AKI via the SARS-CoV-2 N -Smad3-dependent mechanism may lead to the development of novel and specific anti-COVID-19 therapies by directly suppressing the SARS-CoV-2 N RNA replication and inhibiting TGF-beta/Smad3 signaling with Smad3 inhibitors such as SIS3 and quercetin. In addition, the discovery of Smad3 mediates SARS-CoV-2N-induced AKI via the p21/p16 and Ripk3/MLKL necroptosis pathways may also promote the research into the development of a novel therapy for COVID-19 AKI by targeting these cell death pathways clinically.

14101121.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14101121.value: kidney is a major target organ of SAR-CoV-2 and SARS-CoV-2-induced acute kidney injury (AKI) is common in critically ill COVID-19 patients. In this study, we identified that AKI is induced by SARS-CoV-2 N protein in mice, which become much more severe in diabetic mice with older age and underlying kidney disease. We also found that SARS-CoV-2 N protein induces AKI via the Smad3-dependent mechanism. Furthermore, we uncovered that Smad3 mediates SARS-CoV-2 N-induced AKI by activating the p21/p16 and Ripk3/MLKL cell death pathways. We also identified that SARS-CoV-2 N-induced tubular cell death can release a damaged molecule called HMGB1, which can activate M1 macrophages to produce abundant cytokines via a HMGB1-Mincle-Syk-NF-kB dependent mechanism. This finding may well explain the “cytokine storm” in critical ill COVD-19 patients clinically. Thus, targeting Smad3 with Smad3 inhibitor such as SIS3 or quercetin, a Traditional Chinese herbal compound, may be a novel and specific treatment for COVID-19 AKI clinically.

14101321.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14101321.value: 結直腸癌是香港的頭號癌症。我們之前的研究報導了 SLC25A22為KRAS突變性結直腸癌的致癌因子。在前期工作中，我們發現SLC25A22敲除顯著下調細胞因子相關信號，預示SLC25A22可以調節抗腫瘤中的免疫微環境。通過小鼠同源腫瘤模型，我們對SLC25A22敲除的腫瘤進行了免疫細胞浸潤組成的分析，顯示MDSC浸潤程度下調，T細胞（CD4+/CD8+ T）浸潤程度上調，結果說明SLC25A22可通過調節結直腸癌中的免疫浸潤，進而降低抗腫瘤的免疫作用。結合RNA測序和抗體芯片的結果確定了CXCL1是SLC25A22的直接作用基因。CXCL1通過與其受體 CXCR2 的相互作用，誘導免疫抑制性的MDSC細胞，從而抑制抗腫瘤的T細胞（CD4+/CD8+ T）。有鑑於此，我們在小鼠模型中採用了SLC25A22 敲除與抗PD1的組合療法，並發現 SLC25A22 敲除可以協同anti-PD1抗體激活在腫瘤內的細胞毒性T細胞。因此，我們假設 SLC25A22 為KRAS突變性結直腸癌的新治療靶點。本課題的目標如下：1）評估 SLC25A22 在 KRAS 突變性結直腸癌中免疫抑制的作用；2）闡明SLC25A22介導的免疫抑制機制；3) 評估 SLC25A22 敲除與抗PD1治療在 KRAS 突變 CRC 中的協同作用。這些目標將說明 SLC25A22 在 KRAS 突變 CRC 中免疫抑制中的作用，並驗證其作為與免疫治療相結合的可行。

14101321.label: Realisation of objectives
14101321.value: Objective #1. To determine the role of SLC25A22 in immune suppression in KRAS-mutant colorectal cancer First, we explored the role of SLC25A22 in KRAS-induced immunosuppression. CRC organoids from APC-KRAS mutant and Apcmin/+KrasG12D/+Slc25a22fl/flVillin-Cre mice with colon-specific Slc25a22 knockout (APC-KRAS-SLC25A22KO) were implanted in immunocompetent mice. Flow cytometry showed that total MDSC and PMN-MDSC were reduced by Slc25a22 knockout; while total T-cell, and CD8+ T-cell were induced. Both immunofluorescence (IF) and immunohistochemistry (IHC) confirmed decrease of MDSC cells in Slc25a22 knockout tumors as exemplified by the reduced infiltration of Cd11b+Gr-1+ and S100a8+ cells, respectively. We validated these data in KRAS-mutant CT26 allografts. Slc25a22 knockout (Slc-KO) CT26 tumors showed lower tumor size together with reduced MDSC and PMN-MDSC, while total T cells and CD8+ T cells were increased. These results imply that SLC25A22 knockout reversed KRAS-induced immunosuppression. We also retrospectively analyzed spontaneous colon tumors from APC-KRAS and APC-KRAS-SLC25A22KO transgenic mice. MDSC was depleted in SLC25A22 knockout mice as shown by IF (Cd11b+Gr-1+) and IHC (S100a8), while CD8+ T cells were induced, thus validating our observations in allografts. Furthermore, we employed PBMC humanized mice model implanted with DLD1 cells with or without SLC25A22 knockout to assess the effect of this gene in modulating human immune response. As expected, SLC25A22 knockout (SLC-KO) impaired tumor growth and tumor weight. Analyses of tumor-infiltrating huCD45+ immune cells confirmed reduction of human MDSC (HLA-DR-CD11b+CD33+), together with increased infiltration of CD8+ T cells). This verified the effect of SLC25A22 on human CD45+ immune cells infiltration in KRAS-mutant CRC. Taken together, SLC25A22 consistently promotes immunosuppression in multiple animal models through recruitment of MDSCs and reduction of CD8+ T cell infiltration and activation. Objective #2. To elucidate the mechanism of SLC25A22-mediated immune suppression via a CXCL1-CXCR2 axis To probe the molecular mechanism of SLC25A22-mediated immunosuppression, we performed RNA-seq of SLC25A22 knockout DLD1 cells. Gene set enrichment analysis revealed 13 common dysregulated pathways in SLC25A22 knockout cells. Strikingly, top depleted pathway is Cytokine-Cytokine Receptor Interaction, implying involvement of SLC25A22 in cytokine signaling in addition to its metabolic function. Integrated profiling using PCR array and cytokine array revealed that SLC25A22 knockout in DLD1 and CT26 cells decreased cytokine expression. We identified that CXCL1 and CXCL3 were down-regulated by SLC25A22 knockout. qPCR validated down-regulated CXCL1/3 in KRAS-mutant CRC cells (DLD1, Colo26, and CT26) after SLC25A22 knockout. CXCL1 secretion was also suppressed in APC-KRAS-SLC25A22KO organoids compared to APC-KRAS organoids. Corroborating our findings, CXCL1/3 are top cytokines correlated with SLC25A22 mRNA expression in TCGA cohort. Collectively, SLC25A22 mediates CXCL1/3 in KRAS-mutant CRC. As CXCL1 is a chemoattractant of MDSCs, we hypothesized that SLC25A22 is required for tumor-induced MDSC chemotaxis through CXCL1/3. Indeed, while conditioned medium from control cells promoted MDSC migration, such an effect was blunted in SLC25A22 knockout cells, indicating that SLC25A22 loss impaired the ability of CRC cells to promote MDSC chemotaxis. CXCL1-siRNA, but not CXCL3-siRNA, suppressed migration of MDSC in DLD1-sgControl conditioned medium, suggesting that CXCL1 as the predominant cytokine that mediates MDSC migration. Confirming this, anti-CXCL1 antibody also abrogated MDSC migration in conditioned medium from sgControl cells, but not in Slc-KO cells. Reciprocally, addition of CXCL1 restored MDSC migration in CT26-Slc-KOand Colo26-Slc-KO cell conditioned medium. SLC25A22-mediated CXCL1 is thus critical for recruitment of MDSC. CXCR2 is the receptor for CXCL1 expressed on MDSCs. In line with this notion, CXCR2 inhibitors abolished MDSC migration and infiltration in control tumors, but had no effect on SLC-KO tumors. SLC25A22 thus promotes MDSC chemotaxis via a CXCL1-CXCR2 axis in KRAS-mutant CRC. Mechanistically, SLC25A22-mediated glutamine metabolism drives CXCL1 chemokine via asparagine biosynthesis. First, we incubated SLC-KO cells with downstream TCA cycle and amino acid metabolites, revealing that only asparagine rescued CXCL1 mRNA and protein levels in both DLD1 and CT26 cells with SLC25A22 knockout. Further, exogenous asparagine restored the ability of DLD1-SLC-KO and CT26-Slc-KO cells to promote MDSC migration. To test whether asparagine is the critical metabolite, we depleted asparagine by asparagine synthetase (ASNS) knockdown or Asparaginase (ASNase) treatment, showing that both impaired the capacity of KRAS-mutant CRC cells to induce MDSC migration. This support the a SLC25A22-asparagine-CXCL1 axis underlying MDSC recruitment in KRAS-mutant CRC. Objective #3. To evaluate the synergy between SLC25A22 knockout and immune checkpoint therapy in KRAS-mutant colorectal cancer As SLC25A22 knockout repressed MDSC, we hypothesize that targeting SLC25A22 may synergize with ICB therapy. We first explored the therapeutic effect of anti-PD1 in combination with SLC25A22 knockout in CT26 cells and MC38 cells overexpressing mutant Kras. In both models, anti-PD1 alone had no effect on tumor growth, in line with the immune resistance phenotype of KRAS-mutant CRC. Importantly, SLC25A22 knockout plus anti-PD1 exerted synergistic effects as compared to control and either single treatment, leading to tumor regression and reduction in tumor weight. Immunological analysis showed that SLC25A22 knockout plus anti-PD1 synergized to reduce MDSC and promote cytotoxic CD8+ T-cell infiltration and IFN-γ expression, implying the activation of antitumor immune response. To therapeutically target SLC25A22, we utilized nanoparticle (VNP) for siRNA delivery in vivo. We tested therapeutic efficacy of SLC25A22 siRNA in combination with anti-PD1 in MC38-KrasG12V allografts. When tumor volume reached ~100 mm3, mice were randomized to receive VNP-siControl, VNP-siSLC25A22 with or without anti-PD1. Combination of VNP-siSLC25A22 and anti-PD1 synergistically inhibited growth of MC38-KrasG12V allografts by activating cytotoxic IFN-γ+ CD8+ T-cell, in agreement with that SLC25A22 as a therapeutic target for overcoming immunotherapy resistance in KRAS-mutant CRC.

14101321.label: Major findings and research outcome
14101321.value: Mutations in the KRAS oncogene are highly prevalent in CRC and it drives CRC by promoting tumor cell proliferation. However, recent evidence also suggests a strong link of mutant KRAS with an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. Our previous studies have shown that SLC25A22 (Gastroenterology, 2016, 2020) as a functionally important gene in KRAS-mutant CRC. However, it is unclear whether SLC25A22 also participates in regulating the tumor immune microenvironment of KRAS-mutant CRC. In the continuation of our work, we have expanded by work by investigating the 1) role of SLC25A22 in modulating the tumor immune microenvironment of KRAS-mutant CRC; 2) the mechanism of actin of SLC25A22 in modulating tumor cell-immune cell crosstalk in KRAS-mutant CRC; and 3) the potential therapeutic value of targeting SLC25A22 for boosting immunotherapy efficacy in KRAS-mutant CRC. We defined a metabolic circuitry of SLC25A22-asparagine-SRC/ETS2/CXCL1 promoting an immunosuppressive microenvironment in KRAS-mutant CRC. SLC25A22-mediated CXCL1 recruits MDSC and inactivates cytotoxic T cells. Our work implies strategies targeting SLC25A22 to improve therapeutic response to immunotherapies in immune-cold KRAS-mutant CRC. This project has been fruitful and the primary paper been published in Nature Communications in 2023 [IF=15.7], with the PI as corresponding author. Apart from this work, we have also investigated the role oncogenes in CRC, including YTHDF1 (Cancer Research, 2024; corresponding author, IF=16.6) as well as the microbiome (Cell Host Microbe, 2024; 2025; corresponding author, IF=18.7). A total of 10 papers were published based on this funding.

14101321.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14101321.value: In this proposal, we revealed SLC25A22 as a key metabolic factor in modulating the tumor immune microenvironment, and is a promising target for boosting immunotherapy response in KRAS-mutant CRC. To further improve our understanding of SLC25A22 in KRAS-mutant CRC, we will investigate the function, mechanism and translational value of this gene using transgenic mouse models of colon-specific knockin and knockout. More indepth view of the onco-immunology of SLC25A22 will be gained by using single cell RNA-sequencing, imaging mass cytometry, and spatial technologies. We will collaborate with expertise in mass spectrometry and bioinformatics to unravel novel immunological mechanisms involved in SLC25A22-mediated immunosuppression in KRAS-mutant CRC. To target SLC25A22 in vivo, we will improve our nanoparticle formulation and/or screen small molecules to inhibit SLC25A22 therapeutically. The promising inhibitors will be further optimized through liaising with pharmaceutical firms.

14101321.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14101321.value: Nature of the project: Recent evidence suggests that mutant KRAS, a key oncogenic frequently mutated colorectal cancer. Our previous work has shown that solute carrier family 25 member 22 (SLC25A22), as an important tumor promoting gene in KRAS-mutant CRC. In this study, we additionally demonstrated that SLC25A22 critically regulate the tumor infiltrating immune cells. By promoting the secretion of a cytokine CXCL1, SLC25A22 promotes the infiltration of a highly tumor suppressive cell population, which in turn compromises immune surveillance, leading to increased tumor growth in vivo. This suggests that targeting SLC25A22 and its associated metabolites might be a strategy for reactivating antitumor immunity in KRAS-mutant CRC. Significance: Our work demonstrated that SLC25A22 as an actionable target in KRAS-mutant CRC. The combination of targeting SLC25A22 with a novel nanoparticle-siRNA formulation in conjunction with anti-PD1 synergized to inhibit the growth of KRAS-mutant CRC in vivo, thereby implying the potential role of SLC25A22 as an immunotherapy sensitizing target. Value of the project: Strategies to inhibit SLC25A22 might be developed as an adjuvant to improve the efficacy of anti-PD1 immune checkpoint therapy in the treatment of KRAS-mutant CRC, an immune cold tumor that typically responds poorly to anti-PD1 therapy.

14101621.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14101621.value: 二甲雙胍作為青光眼的神經保護療法—隨機對照試驗

14101621.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14101621.value: Dr Chan, Poemen Pui-man Dr KAM, KA WAI Prof Ma, Ronald Ching-wan Dr Wan, Ho-Nam Kelvin

14101621.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14101621.value: 青光眼，這種視神經慢性退化的疾病，是目前世界範圍內首位導致不可逆的眼盲原因。儘管降低眼壓被證實能有效的減緩視神經的退化，然而仍然有相當部分的病人的視覺在眼壓受控的情況下繼續進行性退化。因此發展有別於降低眼壓的神經保護性治療來防止視神經退化從而減輕青光眼盲性負荷就變成非常關鍵。截止到2020年有7600萬青光眼患者，研究對青光眼的神經性保護的需求變得十分迫切。 雖然二甲雙胍是一種廣泛採用於治療2型糖尿病 (DM)的口服降糖藥物，越來越多的臨床研究證明二甲雙胍可以減低許多隨著年齡增加而引致的相關疾病風險，包括神經退化性疾病。在早前一項對 150,016 名 糖尿病患者進行的回溯性研究中，與沒有服用二甲雙胍的患者相比，每天服用超過 1500 毫克二甲雙胍的患者，其患上開角型青光眼的風險降低25%。二甲雙胍具有很高的安全性。因此，我們此研究志在透過隨機對照試驗，調查二甲雙胍是否可以被轉用作為青光眼患者的神經保護治療。 我們會進行一項為期 24 個月、雙盲、安慰劑對照、平行組、多中心的試驗，將 240 名根據廣域光學相干斷層掃描基於趨勢的進展分析至少有一隻眼患有進展性視網膜神經纖維層神經節細胞層變薄的原發性開角型青光眼患者隨機分成兩組, 接受每天服食1500 毫克二甲雙胍或安慰劑。並每隔 2 個月對所有患者進行眼壓、視網膜神經纖維層神經節細胞層厚度和視野測量的隨訪。實驗的目標在於比較兩組中（1）平均網膜神經纖維層神經節細胞層厚度的變化速率，以及（2）視野檢查中的平均差的變化速率，我們猜想，在 24 個月的隨訪中，與使用安慰劑治療的患者相比，使用二甲雙胍治療的患者視網膜神經纖維層神經節細胞層變薄的速度和視野平均差下降速度都較慢。 是次研究極有可能證明在二甲雙胍的神經保護性能有效證實的情況下現有醫治青光眼病人的規範可能會被更改，從而減輕有正常眼壓青光眼患者盛行的中國和其他亞洲國家日趨增加的青光眼盲性負荷。此外，它將影響將來神經保護試驗的研究設計，從而加快開發青光眼神經保護治療。

14101721.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14101721.value: EBV 相關鼻咽癌 (NPC) 是一種缺乏角化並被歸類為未分化或低分化的獨特類型頭頸癌。鼻咽癌在華南和東南亞是一個嚴重的醫療保健問題，在中年勞動力人群中其發病率是特別高。不幸的是，大多數NPC 患者診斷時已經出現晚期疾病並且臨床治療效果不佳。我們通過全基因組測序揭示了 NPC 的綜合基因組景觀，並發現多個潛在的精準治療目標。在 32-34% 的原發性和復發性 NPC 中，我們發現甲基硫腺苷磷酸化酶MTAP 的純合缺失，導致其對MAT2A/PRMT5靶向治療的脆弱性。在 MTAP 缺失的腫瘤細胞中，MTAP 的缺失導致甲基硫腺苷 (MTA) 的積累，MTA 選擇性抑制精氨酸甲基轉移酶 PRMT5 的甲基化活性，從而增加它們對 PRMT5 消耗的敏感性。在我們的初步研究中，我們揭示抑制其下游酶 MAT2A (甲硫氨酸腺苷轉移酶 II α ) 顯著降低了 PRMT5 活性並抑制了 MTAP 缺陷型 NPC 細胞的細胞生長，但並不影響MTAP野生型 細胞。我們更發現PRMT5 抑制在EBV 相關癌症中的許多獨特特性，包括促進細胞分化、抑制幹細胞調節因子和誘導 EBV 裂解基因表達。基於這些新發現，我們假設 PRMT5 的精氨酸甲基化活性在維持 NPC 細胞的轉化特性和 EBV 潛伏期方面起著關鍵作用。在這項研究中，我們將全面剖析 MTAP 缺失的 NPC 中的合成致死靶標PRMT5 的獨特功能和治療潛力。因此，（1）我們將闡明 抑制PRMT5在減弱癌症相關特性和破壞 NPC 細胞中的 EBV 潛伏期方面的影響； (2) 我們將進行臨床前評估 MAT2A 抑製劑在NPC 模型中的PRMT5靶向治療功效。此外，通過 抑制PRMT5重新激活 EBV 裂解基因和減弱幹細胞調節因子引證 MAT2A 抑製劑與 GCV 或常規化療藥物聯合治療在 MTAP 缺失的 NPC 中的協同作用； (3) 我們將揭示 抑制PRMT5在促進 NPC 細胞分化和 EBV 裂解再激活中的作用機制。這項研究將為晚期和復發性 NPC患者開闢新的治療策略。

14101721.label: Realisation of objectives
14101721.value: We have conducted comprehensive investigations to address the proposed objectives: (1) To comprehensively elucidate the impacts of PRMT5 inhibition in attenuating cancer related properties and disrupting EBV latency in NPC cells To elucidate the effects of PRMT5/MAT2A inhibition on MTAP-deficient NPC cells, we have successfully established three pairs of isogenic MTAP-null EBV-positive NPC cells by CRISP-gene editing. The loss of MTAP expression and reduced PRMT5 activity (SDMA level) were confirmed in the three MTAP-null EBV-positive NPC cell lines (C666-1, NPC43 and C17). Compared with the paternal cell lines, significant growth inhibition was observed in these MTAP-null NPC cells while we knocked down the expression of PRMT5 or MAT2A by specific siRNAs and shRNAs. To efficiently explore the action mechanisms of targeting MTAP-PRMT5-MAT2A axis and specific antitumor effect of MAT2A inhibition, a panel of MAT2A inhibitors were selected for treatment of the paired MTAP null and parental NPC cell lines. In addition to the reported MAT2A inhibitors (FIDAS5, AGI-24512, AG-270), two newly developed MAT2A inhibitors (BT115386, BT115101) obtained from ScinnoHub Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. were used. Among these MAT2A inhibitors, we found that BT115386 and FIDAS-5 showed the highly selective growth inhibition and markedly reduced PRMT5 activity in all MTAP-null NPC cell lines, either with wild type (C666-1) or mutated TP53 (NPC43, C17). The potent growth inhibitory effects of BT115386 and FIDAS-5 were also demonstrated in a MTAP-del/TP53-del C666-1 cells line, indicating p53 is only one of the downstream targets of PRMT5-MAT2A inhibition. The IC50 of BT115386 in MTAP-deleted NPC cells are >10 folds lower that in their MTAP-wild type parental NPC cells. The findings suggested the usefulness of BT115386 in clinical management of NPC patients. Our study also concluded that MTAP-deletion, but not TP53 status, is a biomarker to select NPC patients for BT115386 treatment. To elucidate the actions of mechanism of MAT2A inhibitors, we have examined the effects of MAT2A inhibitors (BT115386, BT115101 and FIDAS-5) on PRMT5 activity and various cellular mechanisms in MTAP-null NPC cell lines. We confirmed that both three MAT2A inhibitors repressed the SDMA level and PRMT5 activity significantly in the MTAP-deficient NPC cells, but not in their parental cell lines. Similar findings were also observed in the MTAP-deleted and MTAP-WT NPC cells treated with shRNAs against MAT2A and PRMT5. In MTAP deficient NPC cells, we found the reduced expression of full-length MDM4 protein and increase of p53 after treatment with these MTA2A inhibitors. Obvious induction of downstream targets of p53, including p21 and pro-apoptotic protein BAX was detected after treatment. In these MAT2A inhibitor treated cells, increase of cleaved caspase-3 was also demonstrated. The results demonstrated that these compounds activated the p53 and apoptotic pathways in the MTAP deleted NPC cells with wild-type TP53. In contrast, no obvious changes of the expression of BAX and p21 in the MTAP-deleted NPC cells with p53 mutation, suggesting the sensitivity of these cancer cells to the growth inhibitory effects of the MAT2A inhibitors is due to p53-independent mechanisms. Aside from p53 pathway, targeting PRMT5 by the specific MAT2A inhibitors reduced the methylation and stability of a core transcriptional factor in lipogenesis, SREBP1 in the NPC cells, subsequently repressing the FASN expression. The BT115386 and FIDAS-5 treatment of selectively attenuated lipogenesis in MTAP-deleted NPC cells. As we reported previously, targeting lipid metabolism by SREBP1 and FASN repression is one of critical antitumor effects of PRMT5 inhibition in MTAP-deleted NPC cell lines, either with mutated or wild-type TP53. On the other hand, we also demonstrated the specific effect of the MAT2A inhibitors on inducing aberrant RNA splicing events in MTAP-deleted NPC through RNA sequencing. Furthermore, we have revealed that the targeted therapy against PRMT5 activity also induced terminal differentiation, and suppressed stemness and EMT markers including c-MYC, SOX2, KLF4, ID2 and N-cadherin in the MTAP-deficient NPC cells. Importantly, targeting the cancer stem cells properties by PRMT5 inhibition subsequently resulted in inducing EBV lytic reactivation in NPC cells. In EBV-positive NPC, we have demonstrated the EBV latent-lytic switch is regulated by multiple viral and cellular factors. Of note, the NPC cancer stem cells with high NTRK2/SOX2 expression is resistance to lytic induction agents. Here, MAT2A inhibitors suppressed PRMT5 activity to repress cancer stem cell properties, subsequently resulting in the induction of multiple EBV lytic proteins (BZLF1, BRLF1, EA-D, GP350) in MTAP-deleted NPC cells. (2) To preclinically assess the efficacy of synthetic lethal targeting PRMT5 by MAT2A inhibitors in a panel of in vivo patient-derived NPC models We have examined the in vivo anti-tumor effect of FIDAS-5 and BT-115386 on the isogenic pair of MTAP-deleted/paternal C666-1 CDX and two MTAP-deleted NPC PDXs (xeno-76, xeno113), as well as C15, a PDX with intact MTAP. The nude mice harboring the NPC xenografts were administered orally with vehicles or the MAT2A inhibitors daily. We revealed that the MAT2A inhibitor markedly inhibited the growth of MTAP-deleted NPC tumors (xeno-76, xeno-113, MTAP-deleted C666-1), but not in C15 and parental C666-1 tumors. Additionally, we demonstrated the effect of MAT2A inhibitor significantly prolonged the survival of mice bearing MTAP-deleted tumors in the long-term treatment experiments. In the residual tumors of the MTAP-deleted NPC, we detected a dramatic reduction of SDMA and c-MYC, as well as increase of p53 activity. The findings demonstrated a dramatic in vivo anti-tumor effect of MAT2A inhibitors in MTAP-deleted NPC preclinical models. (3) To define the action mechanisms of PRMT5 inhibition in promoting cellular differentiation and EBV lytic reactivation in NPC In the in vivo and in vitro experiments, we demonstrated that inhibition of PRMT5 activity by blockage of MAT2A resulted in repression of both Id2, c-MYC and expression of EBV lytic proteins in MTAP-deleted NPC models. By RNA sequencing, we revealed the common differentially expressed genes and the cellular mechanisms/pathways in the BT-115386-treated MTAP-deleted NPC cells. Notably, the BT-115386 treatment mainly suppressed MYC targets in these cell lines while c-MYC is commonly overexpressed in NPC, suggesting c-MYC is a key PRMT5 target. Furthermore, we have revealed the PRMT5 inhibition repressed Id2 in NPC cells via targeting its upstream c-MYC. Importantly, our findings also demonstrated knockdown c-MYC resulted in inactivation of lipogenesis, abrogation of stemness properties and induction of differentiation markers and reactivation of EBV lytic proteins. While c-MYC plays crucial role in NPC tumorigenesis, we unrevised a novel mechanism of PRMT5 inhibition for targeting c-MYC oncogenic properties in MTAP-deleted NPC cells in this study. By co-IP experiments, we demonstrated the c-MYC was bound to the PRMT5/WDR77 methylome complex while the interaction is dependent on the adaptor binding domain for its substrate in NPC cells. Using multiple deletion constructs of c-MYC, we identified the PRMT5 binding site in the a.a.168-272 region which contains the MB III domain. By co-immunoprecipitation, we revealed that the BT-115386 treatment inhibited arginine methylation of c-MYC protein in the MTAP-deleted NPC cells, resulting in the induction of ubiquitination and degradation of c-MYC protein. The c-MYC ubiquitination was shown in PRMT5-/MAT2A knockdown MTAP-deleted C666-1 cells. The findings implied that the MAT2 inhibitor target multiple oncogenic properties and EBV latency in the MTAP-deleted NPC cells through inducing c-MYC degradation. In conclusion, PRMT5/MAT2A inhibition by genetic ablation or pharmacological inhibition targets both p53 signaling and multiple oncogenic properties of c-MYC. The PRMT5 is a promising precision therapeutic target for NPC patients with MTAP homozygous deletion.

14101721.label: Major findings and research outcome
14101721.value: In this project, we successfully demonstrated that targeting PRMT5 by MAT2A inhibitor is an effective treatment strategy for MTAP-deleted NPC tumors and uncovered the underlying mechanisms of PRMT5 inhibition in targeting NPC oncogenic properties and EBV latency. The Major findings and research outcome include: (1) We detected up to 37.5% (75/200) NPC bearing clonal MTAP homozygous deletion, indicating NPC is the second most frequent MTAP-deleted human cancer. (Chan YY, 2025) (2) The specific antitumor effect of PRMT5 inhibition (via MAT2A/RTMT5 inhibitors and shRNA knockdown) was demonstrated in three MTAP-deleted NPC cell lines that were established by CRISPR-based gene editing. (Chan YY, 2025) (3) The effects of PRMT5 inhibition on suppressing cell proliferation, promoting cell death, inducing cellular differentiation, inhibition of stemness properties in MTAP-deletion NPC with either wild type or mutated TP53. (Chan YY, 2025) (4) We have unveiled multiple cellular and viral genes contribute to NPC tumorigenesis and maintenance of persistent latent infection (Tang WC, 2023; Lee SD, 2022; Wu et al, 2024; Wang B, 2025; Wang B, 2025). Importantly, we unveiled PRMT5 inhibition induce EBV lytic proteins through targeting CSC status and c-MYC activities in EBV-positive NPC cells (Wang X, 2025; Chan YY, 2025) (5) Among multiple MAT2A and PRMT5 inhibitors examined, we revealed the newly developed MAT2A inhibitor (BT -115386) exhibited potent in vivo growth inhibitory effect on multiple MTAP-deleted NPC xenografts, but not in the MTAP-intact tumors. (Chan YY, 2025) (6) As demonstrated in our study of combination with GCV in the lytic induction treatment, we revealed no significant effect on the involvement of GCV in enhancing the growth inhibitory effects on the MTAP-deleted tumor (Wu M, 2024). Furthermore, the combination treatment with chemotherapeutic agents did not further improve the in vivo treatment efficiency. (7) We delineated the mechanisms behind the pharmacological activities of PRMT5 inhibitions, mainly through altering RNA splicing, activating p53 activity and degrading c-MYC protein. The blockage of MAT2A and PRMT5 resulted in reduction of SDMe of c-MYC and its subsequent ubiquitination and degradation. We identified a novel binding site of c-MYC to PRMT5. C-MYC was severely degraded upon depletion of SDMe modification due to the loss of PRMT5 activity. (Chan YY, 2025) (8) Treatment of MAT2A inhibitor led to inhibition of stemness and lipogenesis, as well as induction of cellular differentiation and EBV lytic reactivation in NPC through its action on targeting c-MYC oncogenic properties in NPC. (Chan YY, 2025)

14101721.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14101721.value: Up till now, emerging clinical trials of MTA-cooperative PRMT5 inhibitors (MRTX1719, NCT05245500; TNG908, NCT05275478; AMG193, NCT05094336) and MAT2A inhibitors (e.g. AG270, NCT03435250; IDE397, NCT04794699;) are conducting in the patients with MTAP-deleted lymphoid malignancies and solid cancers. The last report of the phase I clinical trial of an MTA-cooperative PRMT5 inhibitor AMG193 revealed a favorable safety profile and antitumor activity across eight different MTAP-deleted solid tumor types. Nevertheless, being an endemic disease that rarely occurred in Western countries, no information about the clinical efficiency of these inhibitors in NPC. In conclusion, our preclinical study revealed the potent therapeutic efficacy of the MAT2A inhibitor (BT -115386) against MTAP-deletion NPC, provides strong evidence to support future clinical trials of BT-115386 and other MAT2A or PRMT5 inhibitors in this unique EBV-associated epithelial cancers. Currently, we are approaching multiple pharmaceutical companies for discussion of the potential critical trials of PRMT5 or MAT2A inhibitors in the patients with recurrent and metastatic NPC, as well as the patients with other head and neck cancers.

14101721.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14101721.value: Epstein-Barr virus (EBV)-associated nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC), an aggressive tumor with no target therapy options. By screening 200 NPC specimens, homozygous deletion of methylthioadenosine phosphorylase MTAP was clonally detected in 37.5% (75/200) cases of this cancer, the second most common MTAP-deleted cancer type. Importantly, we demonstrated that the MAT2A inhibitors significantly suppressed tumor growth and prolonged mice survival, for the synthetic lethal target methionine adenosyltransferase 2α (MAT2A) in this targetable vulnerability. Reduced protein arginine methyltransferase 5 (PRMT5) activity simultaneously enhanced p53 activity via aberrant splicing of MDM4-FL and led to abolishment of c-MYC arginine symmetric dimethylation and its subsequent proteasomal degradation. Loss of c-MYC thus reduced stemness and lipogenesis but induced cell differentiation and EBV lytic cycle, indicating that PRMT5 inhibition caused MTAP-deleted NPC cell death via multiple pathways. PRMT5/MAT2A inhibition by genetic ablation or pharmacological inhibition is therefore a promising precision therapy for NPC patients with MTAP homozygous deletion.

14102221.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14102221.value: Novel motor task training with one limb results in gain in performance in the untrained limb in humans, a phenomenon known as intermanual transfer or cross education, and believed to involve inter-hemispheric transfer of information. Despite the robustness of this phenomenon in various behavioral tests, the underlying neural mechanisms are still unclear. Due to the conserved neuroanatomy and functions of the motor system between rodents and human, the rodents have served as an excellent model for studying motor execution and motor learning by the mammalian brain. With recent advances in neuroscience research tools, especially multi-photon imaging and chemo/optogenetics applicable to the rodent models, this study exploits the power of these techniques to elucidate the brain mechanism of motor skill transfer from one hemisphere to the other. In our preliminary study, we adopted a novel mouse forelimb 2-dimension lever task to investigate the intermanual skill transfer phenomenon and also cellular activities in the primary motor cortex, a region highly involved in motor learning. Our study confirmed significant gain in performance for the untrained limb in testing sessions after long term practicing with the trained limb. Based on in vivo multiphoton recording from awake mice, cortical activities of two hemispheres were monitored in the whole process of unilateral training and following transfer tests. The results revealed emergent population activities of the untrained hemisphere suggesting remodelling of neural circuit driven by plasticity. Interruption of inter-hemispheric communication by severing the corpus callosum impaired the motor skill transfer and cortical activity reorganization. In this proposal, we will further characterise in detail different indices of motor performance of trained and untrained limbs, to gain a better understanding of what aspect and to what extent motor skill could be transferred. At the same time, we will scrutinise the significance of the emergent cortical activities in skill transfer and the role of the corpus callosum. Furthermore, the roles of different interneuron subtypes that are known to regulate activities of principal neurons while receive inputs from opposite hemisphere will be elucidated. Apart from addressing a basic scientific question that could shed light on the general mechanism of motor skill transfer and allocation of memory from one brain region to another, the results obtained will also have important clinical implications particularly in rehabilitation strategies for those motor impaired patients suffering from stroke and other trauma of the brain. 在人類中，用兩條肢體中的一個進行新的運動訓練會提高另一條肢體的表現，這種現象稱為大腦半球間轉移。這種現象的神經機制仍然是不清楚。囓齒動物已成為研究運動執行力和運動學習的極好模型 。隨著最近神經科學研究工具的進展，本研究利用這些技術闡明運動技能從一個半球轉移到另一個半球的大腦機制。 在我們的初步研究中，我們採用了一種新穎的小鼠前肢二維槓桿任務來 研究技能轉移現象。我們還研究初級運動皮層的細胞活動。我們的研究證實了單邊訓練顯著提高未經訓練的肢體的表現。 基於清醒小鼠體內多光子記錄，我們全程監測單邊訓練和轉移測試中兩大腦半球皮質活動。結果顯示神經元的重塑。 在這個項目中，我們將進一步詳細描述訓練和未訓練肢體的不同運動表現指標，以更好地了解什麼方面以及運動技能可以轉移到什麼程度。 同時，我們將仔細檢查皮層活動在技能轉移中的重要性和機制。

14102221.label: Realisation of objectives
14102221.value: Research was conducted largely according to the proposed timeline for objectives 1 to 3. These include, under objective 1, the study to confirm the transfer of kinematic skill from untrained limb to trained limb, addressed by detailed kinematic analysis of movement trajectories. The consolidation of transferred motor skill for extended period of time was also characterised. To better characterize motor skill transfer, we also conducted experiments to compare the two-phase movement task in our paradigm with a simpler one one-phase only movement, in terms of emergent motor cortical activities. Under objective 2, which is to decipher the roles of emergent activities in motor skill transfer, we studied in detail the population neuronal activities in the ipsilateral, untrained motor cortex during intermanual motor skill transfer, and to investigate their encoding properties. In addition, the essential role of the trans-callosal pathway was studied, indicating a key role of the transcallosal pathway which bridges both cortices from two hemispheres in achieving inter-limb skill transfer . For objective 3, we also conducted tests on transgenic mice to visualise the activities of PV and SST interneurons during motor training. However, in contrast to principal neurons, the activities of interneurons did not reflect a clear involvement in the transfer process itself via promoting the formation of emergent activities of principal neurons. On the whole, the three objectives are largely realized. The major results have been drafted a manuscript ready for submission within a few months’ time, after further statistical and modelling analyses of imaging data.

14102221.label: Major findings and research outcome
14102221.value: In this study, we introduced for the first time a mouse model to study inter-limb transfer mechanism and revealed the transfer phenomenon in mice when they were learning a complex 2-dimensional (2-D) forelimb task under longitudinal two-photon image recording. Compared with 1-dimensional (1-D) forelimb task, kinematic refinement of motor skills was observed during 2-D task learning, enabling precise quantification of transferred motor components across limbs. Adopting this paradigm, gain of performance in the untrained limb (UL) was discovered after unilateral training of the trained limb (TL). Through comparative study of 1-D vs 2-D tasks, we revealed more drastic functional adaptations and the emergence of a larger scale temporal evolving of cortical neurons in contralateral M1 (trained M1) after learning 2-D sequential movement. In ipsilateral M1 (untrained M1), population activity displayed evident reorganization and progressively evolved into a sequential responsive pattern associating TL movements, and this pattern was largely preserved in early testing sessions during UL movements, suggesting unilateral practicing induced plastic changes in untrained M1 and its potential role in facilitating inter-limb transfer, which directly supports the hypothesis in ‘cross-activation’ model. However, this capability inter-limb transfer was severely impaired following callosotomy while the unilateral skill acquisition itself appears to remain unaffected, indicating the integral role of transcallosal connection in inter-limb transfer but not unilateral learning. Also, cortical evolving in untrained M1 weakened in CC-bisected mice and their responsive features failed to persist in transfer tests after limb switching. Pair-wire correlation across successful trials also revealed a weakened relationship between population activity in untrained M1 and movement kinematics after CC-bisection. Moreover, the damage to CC additionally led to a reduction in the predictive accuracy from cortical activity to movement kinematics in UL at the early stage, further proving the necessity of transcallosal connections in facilitating associated cortical plasticity of the opposite hemisphere. Our study therefore demonstrated the neurobiological underpinning of motor skill transfer manifested as emergent neuronal activities in the ipsilateral motor cortex during the process of unilateral limb training, providing new compelling evidence for the ‘cross-activation’ hypothesis, critically dependent on the transcallosal projections. We also demonstrated the viability of employing mouse models to investigate neuronal mechanisms of inter-limb skill transfer.

14102221.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14102221.value: This study laid the foundation of using the rodent model to investigate intermanual motor skill transfer. Based on the findings, which will be submitted for publication in peer reviewed scientific journal, further work can be proposed to fully elucidate the nature of the plasticity that underlie the transfer phenomenon, that is, the action of transcortical projection. This question could form the foundation of future grant proposal. Fully understanding the mechanism has long-term implications not only in understanding the nature of motor skill (a type of memory) transfer, but has translational potential in motor rehabilitation programs to treat stroke and other motor impaired patients.

14102221.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14102221.value: The phenomenon of intermanual transfer of learned motor skill has been investigated experimentally for more than a century through various behavioral tests in humans. However, investigation into the underlying neuronal mechanisms has been constrained the lack of good animal models. This study for the first time employed advanced in vivo recording techniques to explore inter-limb transfer in the mouse model. Through a novel sequential motor task which enabled quantification of kinematic motor elements, we demonstrated the ability of the mouse to transfer unilaterally learned complex motor skills across limbs. Simultaneous populational recording by two-photon microscopy revealed that learning of sequential forelimb task induced more drastic contralateral cortical plasticity than that associated with ballistic movement learning. During the unilateral practice by the trained limb (TL), ipsilateral primary motor cortex (M1) underwent remarkable adaptations and exhibited comparable features during the test of untrained forelimb (UL). Notably, surgical bisection of mouse corpus callosum (CC) detrimentally affected their ability to inter-limb transfer without evident impact on unilateral learning. These results indicated that plasticity of the ipsilateral motor cortex encodes the transferred motor skill and demonstrated the indispensability of the transcallosal pathway in realizing inter-limb transfer.

14102321.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14102321.value: 假設：動脈粥樣硬化是一種炎症，它是在血管內層由動脈斑塊增生引致。血液內膽固醇過高是其中一個主要導致原因。人類膳食中包含膽固醇及氧化膽固醇 (Ox-C). 假設的理論是氧化膽固醇比膽固醇更容易會對腸道細菌群作出更多負面影響，從而更容易引起動脈粥樣硬化。我們的初步實驗數據亦支持上述假設。餵食含有氧化膽固醇飼料對腸道細菌群引起負面影響：會增加促炎細菌群的生長和減少產短鏈脂肪酸(SCFAs)細菌群。這些短鏈脂肪酸細菌群有助降低膽固醇及抗炎症。 目的：本研究對比氧化膽固醇和膽固醇對腸道細菌群的影響。腸道細菌主要集中厚壁菌門 (Firmicutes)、擬桿菌門(Bacteroidetes)、產短鏈脂肪酸細菌群和釋放脂多糖 (LPS)細菌群。改變腸道細菌群如何引致血液內膽固醇變化及動脈粥樣硬化的發生。 設計：本研究用雄性載脂蛋白E基因敲除小鼠作為實驗對象。小鼠隨機分為5組, 每組10隻 (n = 10) 餵食以下5 種飼料，為期16 週。5 種飼料包括對照飼料、對照飼料含有額外 0.1% 膽固醇、 0.2% 膽固醇、0.1% 氧化膽固醇及0.2%氧化膽固醇。每日記錄小鼠進食量，每週量度體重及收集糞便。當實驗完成，收集盲腸內容物以研究及分析腸道細菌群。 檢測參數： 研究氧化膽固醇和腸道細菌群怎樣影響與膽固醇代謝有關的基因信使核糖核酸表達。檢測參數包括：血液膽固醇、動脈斑塊形成、肝臟膽固醇、三酸甘油酯、糞便膽汁酸、糞便中性固醇、糞便短鏈脂肪酸、脂多糖和腸道細菌群。肝臟內羥甲基戊二酸單醯輔酶A還原酶、低密度脂蛋白受體、膽固醇7α-羥化酶、固醇調節元件結合蛋白 2、肝 X 受體和法尼醇 X 受體蛋白和信使核糖核酸。亦會研究體外無氧狀態下氧化膽固醇對盲腸內腸道細菌群的影響。 預期結果：初步實驗數據顯示，氧化膽固醇令厚壁菌門比擬桿菌門比例增加及抑壓產短鏈脂肪酸細菌群，這樣增加引起動脈粥樣硬化及患上心血管疾病的風險。

14102321.label: Realisation of objectives
14102321.value: We have achieved all the objectives as stipulated in the original proposal. Human diet contains both cholesterol and oxidized cholesterol (Ox-C). Cholesterol is susceptible to oxidation under various food processing conditions. The amount of ox-C can reach 11% total cholesterol in foods, particularly those foods from countries or regions where total fat intake is high and fried foods are popular. More than 30 Ox-C species have been identified and reported. Among them, five major ones dominate including 7α-keto, 7α-OH, 7β-OH, 5,6α-epoxy and 5,6β-epoxy cholesterol. Ox-C has been studied for its undesirable effects including cytotoxicity, and carcinogenesis. It is well known that high cholesterol consumption elevates plasma total cholesterol (TC) and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) levels and increases the risk of coronary heart diseases (CHD). Our previous study had found that Ox-C was more harmful by increasing plasma TC and LDL-C more than dietary cholesterol itself. Most concerned was that Ox-C could be more atherosclerotic and cause endothelial dysfunction in several animal models. In humans, Ox-C has been shown to be positively associated with the risk of cardiovascular diseases, most likely by promoting the recruitment of monocytes, and disturbing cholesterol homeostasis. The present project was to investigate the effect of Ox-C on gut microbiota related to atherosclerosis compared with dietary cholesterol itself. Objective 1 was to study the effect of oxidized cholesterol on gut microbiota. The present study clearly demonstrated that dietary oxidized cholesterol was able to significantly modulate the gut microbiota. Results showed that oxidized cholesterol caused a dramatic decrease in gut microbiota diversity. It increased the abundance of Escherichia-Shigella, which is regarded as a dysbiosis and inflammatory marker for IBDs in humans. In addition, dietary oxidized cholesterol promoted the relative abundance of Bacteroides and Romboutsia. Bacteroides are mucolytic bacteria with production of mucin-degrading enzymes. Mucin-degrading enzymes and bacteria can contribute to the damage of gut barrier in clinical colitis patients. We observed that dietary oxidized cholesterol increased the relative abundance of Enterococcus. In contrast, dietary oxidized cholesterol decreased the abundance of several beneficial bacteria, for example, Lachnospiraceae_NK4A136_group and Odoribacter. It was found that dietary oxidized cholesterol negatively modulated the gut microbiota composition by promoting the abundance of pro-inflammatory bacteria whereas inhibiting the SCFAs-producing bacteria in DSS-induced colitis mice. Objective 2 was to study the effect of oxidized cholesterol on short chain fatty acids (SCFAs) produced by gut microbiota compared with that of cholesterol itself. Addition of oxidized cholesterol into diet could increase the relative abundance of Escherichia-Shigella, Bacteroides, Romboutsia, Enterococcus, and Intestinimonas, whereas it decreased the relative abundance of Lachnospiraceae_NK4A136_group and Odoribacter. Dietary oxidized cholesterol significantly decreased acetic, propionic, and butyric acids in feces compared with cholesterol. However, it had no effect on aleric acid. Results clearly demonstrated that dietary oxidized cholesterol suppressed the production of total SCFAs. It was found that dietary oxidized cholesterol adversely caused gut dysbiosis by promoting the abundance of pro-inflammatory bacteria whereas inhibiting the SCFAs-producing bacteria in DSS-induced colitis mice. Objective 3 was to investigate the effect of oxidized cholesterol on lipopolysaccharide (LPS) compared with that of cholesterol itself. Over production of LPS and oxidative stress-related enzymes is usually associated with gut microbiota dysbiosis. The present study clearly demonstrated that dietary oxidized cholesterol promoted the production of LPS and intestinal inflammation. It was found that dietary oxidized cholesterol increased the amount of oxidative stress-related enzymes including NOX2, NOX4, iNOS, and MPO in DSS-induced colitis and promoted the production of MDA in the colon tissues. The present results showed that dietary oxidized cholesterol up-regulated the expression of iNOS, which was consistent finding in other IBDs models and may contribute to vascular permeability. Accompanied with an increase in bacteria infiltration and oxidative stress, the over expression of inflammatory cytokines can further aggravate the inflammation in colon tissues. The NF-B signaling is an inflammatory pathway involved in the progress of colitis. The present results clearly demonstrated that dietary oxidized cholesterol could activate the NF-B pathway, up-regulate the amount of pro-inflammatory cytokines, and cause oxidative stress in DSS-induced colitis. Objective 4 was to investigate the effect of oxidized cholesterol on atherosclerosis compared with that of cholesterol itself. Results showed that both the non-oxidized and oxidized cholesterol diets could increase deposition of cholesterol and atherosclerosis plaque in the aorta. Effect of dietary oxidized cholesterol were more potent than that of cholesterol itself. It was found that both non-oxidized and oxidized cholesterols significantly inhibited acetylcholine-induced relaxation of the aorta in hamsters. However, oxidized cholesterol was more potent in inhibition than cholesterol, suggesting that dietary oxidized cholesterol could cause greater endothelial damage because that dietary oxidized cholesterol could incorporate into lipoproteins and produce oxidized LDL, which accumulated on the endothelium to promote atherosclerotic plaque and impair endothelium-dependent vasorelaxation. Objective 5 was to study the oxidized cholesterol-induced changes in gut microbiota related to blood cholesterol and atherosclerosis. First, it was found that dietary oxidized cholesterol caused gut microbiota dysbiosis by decreasing SCFAs-producing bacteria and increasing the inflammatory bacteria, thus leading to lesser production of SCFAs. It is known that SCFAs could inhibit the HMG-CoA reductase and therefore oxidized cholesterol could increase blood cholesterol mediated by producing lesser SCFAs. Second, dietary oxidized cholesterol increased the production of LPS and thus it further increased plasma cholesterol as LPS activated HMG-CoA reductase.

14102321.label: Major findings and research outcome
14102321.value: We have conducted all experiments as planned in the original proposal. The results of the whole project have led to publish six SCI papers. The first outcome of this project was to examine the effect of oxidized cholesterol on gut microbiota. The results showed that oxidized cholesterol promoted colitis by exacerbating bleeding, body weight decrease, colon shortening, gut barrier damage, oxidative stress, and gut inflammation, whereas non-oxidized cholesterol had no effect. Meanwhile, oxidized cholesterol could adversely modulate the gut microbiota by increasing the relative abundance of pro-inflammatory bacteria (including Escherichia−Shigella and Bacteroides) and decreasing that of beneficial bacteria (Lachnospiraceae_NK4A136_group and Odoribacter). In addition, oxidized cholesterol significantly reduced the production of fecal short-chain fatty acids in colitis mice. The second major finding or outcome was to investigate the mechanism by which oxidized cholesterol promoted colitis using C57BL/6 mice as a model. Results showed that more severe colitis was developed in oxidized cholesterol-treated mice with the administration of dextran sulfate sodium (DSS) in water. Oxidized cholesterol-induced symptoms of colitis were eliminated when mice were administered with antibiotic cocktails, indicating the promoting effect of oxidized cholesterol on DSS-induced colitis was mediated by its effect on gut microbiota. Moreover, bacteria-depleted mice colonized with gut microbiome from oxidized cholesterol-DSS-exposed mice exhibited a severe colitis, further proving the gut dysbiosis caused by oxidized cholesterol exposure was the culprit in exacerbating the colitis. It was concluded that dietary oxidized cholesterol exposure increased the susceptibility of colitis in mice by causing gut microbiota dysbiosis. The third major finding/outcome was to evaluate the influence of dietary oxidized cholesterol on gut health and ecology. Results showed that the thickness of the mucus layer was significantly reduced in healthy mice treated with OXC. Short-term intake of oxidized cholesterol did not influence the expression of pro-inflammatory factors in healthy mice but it induced the decrease of Muc2 expression in the proximal colon, accompanied by an increase in the abundance of 2 mucus degrading bacteria, namely Akkermansia muciniphila and Bacteroides acidifaciens. The adverse effect of oxidized cholesterol on mucus layer disappeared in antibiotics-treated healthy mice, suggesting that the damaging effect of oxidized cholesterol on the gut mucus layer was not direct and instead was mediated by causing microbiota dysbiosis. Finally, the impact of oxidized cholesterol on the mucus layer and colitis was partly alleviated by green tea catechins. Last but not least, we found not only oxidized cholesterol but also frying fats and oil could cause the loss of species diversity and richness of gut microbiota. Oxidized corn oil and lard could adversely remodel gut composition and affect intestinal production of short-chain fatty acids, pro-inflammatory biomarkers (LPS and IL-6), anti-inflammatory biomarker IL-10, and atherosclerotic progression. It was concluded that frying oil could adversely modulate the gut microbiota and exacerbate the atherosclerosis.

14102321.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14102321.value: The present project was the first time to investigate effect of oxidized cholesterol on gut microbiota and colitis in mice. It was evident that dietary oxidized cholesterol exposure caused gut microbiota dysbiosis, increased the susceptibility of colitis, decreased the production of SCFAs while it increased the LPS. Even though the data are clear in animal experiments, it may not be directly extrapolated to what happens in human patients. The clinical trial is needed to validate the results obtained in the animal experiments.

14102321.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14102321.value: It is recommended that daily intake of cholesterol should not be more than 300 mg. Concerns about adverse effect of oxidized cholesterol as a food and environmental harmful substance are emerging. It is therefore necessary to identify the potential environment and health effects of this group of harmful compounds. Using murine colitis model, pseudo-germ-free mice, and fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) experiments, the adverse influence of OXC on gut health and microbiota was highlighted in this study. The findings demonstrated that OXC could be a risk factor for gut dysbiosis, most likely mediated by adversely modulating gut microbiota. The present research may suggest there is a need for the future safety evaluation of oxidized cholesterol.

14103121.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14103121.value: 杜興氏肌營養不良症(DMD)是由肌萎縮蛋白基因突變引起的，導致進行性肌肉萎縮無力以及早期死亡。針對肌萎縮蛋白基因的治療療效有限，而針對病理變化如纖維化的治療策略近期獲得了衆多關注。結締組織生長因子 (CTGF) 是纖維化的關鍵因子，在 DMD 肌肉中高度表達，是一個有應用前景的治療靶點。然而，目前靶向 CTGF 的藥物對 DMD 的治療效果仍有待確定。對於CTGF調節纖維化的分子機制需進一步深入研究。 CTGF有四個結構域，可與不同的下游蛋白相互作用以發揮各種生物學功能。N 端 CTGF(N-CTGF)和C端CTGF(C-CTGF)之間由鉸鏈肽連接。基質金屬蛋白酶(MMP)對CTGF鉸鏈肽的裂解可促進CTGF的促纖維化活性。生物信息學和體外實驗表明 N-CTGF 和 C-CTGF 中的活性結合位點在全長CTGF(FL-CTGF)中互相覆蓋隱藏，導致 FL-CTGF 的促纖維化活性較低。因此，鉸鏈區可能是抑制 FL-CTGF 裂解的潛在治療靶點。利用SELEX技術我們鑑定了靶向CTGF鉸鏈區的適配體(Apt-hinge)。 體外實驗表明Apt-hinge可抑制 FL-CTGF 的裂解，並抑制 CTGF 對成纖維細胞增殖和成肌細胞分化的影響。Apt-hinge進一步與PEG40K耦合以防止生物體內快速腎清除。全身給藥 Apt-hinge-PEG40K 耦合物 (Apc-CTGF) 可以抑制 mdx 小鼠中 FL-CTGF 的裂解。 因此，我們假設 Apc-CTGF 可以通過抑制 FL-CTGF 的裂解來抑制肌肉纖維化進程並改善 mdx 小鼠的肌肉功能。為了檢驗假設，本課題將完成四個目標。 1) 研究長期 Apc-CTGF 治療對 mdx 小鼠肌肉 FL-CTGF 裂解的影響。 2) 研究 Apc-CTGF 治療對 mdx 小鼠肌肉纖維化的影響。 3) 研究 Apc-CTGF 治療對 mdx 小鼠肌肉質量和功能的影響。 4）研究Apc-CTGF對mdx小鼠肝腎功能的影響。 本課題將有助於確定CTGF 鉸鏈區可能是抑制 CTGF 裂解和維持 CTGF 低促纖維化活性的潛在治療靶點，並將提供一種新的基於適配體的治療策略來抑制纖維化進程，從而改善DMD 中肌肉功能。

14103121.label: Realisation of objectives
14103121.value: All four specific aims have been successfully achieved, which confirms the hypothesis that Apc-CTGF can suppress fibrosis and improve muscle function in mdx mice by inhibiting the cleavage of full-length CTGF (FL-CTGF). For Aim 1, one hundred 3-month-old male mdx mice were recruited and assigned to four groups. 1) Baseline group (n=10): were sacrificed before the treatement; 2) Apc-CTGF group (n=30): were subcutaneously administered with Apc-CTGF at dose of 12mg/kg, twice a week; 3) Apc-RS group (n=30): were administered with random sequence aptamer-PEG40K conjugate using the same protocol as Apc-CTGF group; 4) Vehicle group (n=30): were subcutaneously administered with vehicle twice a week. Ten mice in Apc-CTGF, Apc-RS and vehicle group will be sacrificed at 2, 4 and 8 weeks after treatment start date, respectively. After sacrificing, the gastrocnemius (GA) and tibialis anterior (TA) muscle of each mice were collected. The mRNA level of CTGF in skeletal muscle will be assessed by quantitative PCR (qPCR). The expression levels of CTGF protein in different forms (FL-CTGF, N-CTGF and CCTGF) and MMP8 in skeletal muscles will be evaluated by western blotting. The MMP activity assays will be performed to evaluate the MMP activity in skeletal muscles. As hypothesised, 8-week treatment with Apc-CTGF significantly suppressed the cleavage of FL-CTGF in the gastrocnemius and tibialis anterior muscles of mdx mice. Western blot analysis showed a substantial and sustained reduction in the levels of the cleavage products, N-CTGF and C-CTGF, in the Apc-CTGF treatment group compared to both Apc-RS and vehicle control groups. Correspondingly, the activity of MMPs in muscle tissue was also significantly lower in the Apc-CTGF group. No technical problems were encountered, and the robust sample size ensured statistical power. For Aim 2, the skeletal muscle samples of baseline group, Apc-CTGF, Apc-RS and vehicle group that sacrificed at week 8 in Aim 1 were collected for this aim. The TA muscle was cryosectioned for Sirius Red staining for Collagen I/III and immunohistochemical staining for fibronectin. The GA muscle was used for total mRNA and protein extraction. The mRNA levels of TGFβ, Integrin αvβ3, Collagen I/III and fibronectin were assessed by qPCR. The protein levels of the above factors were assessed by western blotting. Histological analysis and immunohistochemistry revealed a significant reduction in collagen deposition and extracellular matrix (ECM) content in the skeletal muscles of Apc-CTGF-treated mice compared to controls. At the molecular level, qPCR and western blotting confirmed significant downregulation of key fibrotic markers, including TGFβ, Integrin αvβ3, Collagen I/III, and fibronectin. These findings provide direct evidence that inhibiting CTGF cleavage via Apc-CTGF effectively attenuates the fibrotic pathology in dystrophic muscle. For Aim 3, forty 3-month-old male mdx mice were randomly assigned into four groups as described in Aim 1. The mice were sacrificed after 8-week treatment. The function of GA muscle was evaluated by in situ muscle functional testing before sacrifice. After sacrificing, the GA and TA muscles were collected and weighted. Meanwhile, the blood was collected for creatine kinase (CK) activity assay, which was used to detect muscle damage. The TA muscle was cryosectioned for Hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) staining for mean muscle fiber cross-sectional area (CSA) calculation. The GA muscle was used for total mRNA and protein extraction. The mRNA level of myogenic markers (MyoD and myogenin) was assessed by qPCR. The protein levels of above markers were evaluated by western blotting Apc-CTGF treatment resulted in significant functional improvements in skeletal muscle. In situ muscle functional testing revealed enhanced peak isometric force in the gastrocnemius muscle. Treated mice exhibited greater muscle mass, larger mean muscle fiber CSA, and lower serum CK levels, indicating reduced muscle damage. Furthermore, molecular analysis showed upregulation of myogenic markers (MyoD and myogenin). These results confirm that suppressing fibrosis through this novel strategy leads to tangible improvements in muscle structure and function. For Aim 4: The blood of mice in Aim 1 was collected via cardiac puncture under anaesthesia before sacrifice. The collected blood was used for blood chemistry analyses which include aspartate aminotransferase (AST) and alanine aminotransferase (ALT) for assessment of liver function, and creatinine and blood urea nitrogen (BUN) for evaluation of kidney function. Blood chemistry analyses for liver function (ALT, AST) and kidney function (creatinine, BUN) showed no significant adverse changes in Apc-CTGF-treated mice compared to controls. These results indicate that the systemic administration of Apc-CTGF at the therapeutic dose (12 mg/kg, twice weekly) over 8 weeks has no detectable toxic effects on major clearance organs, supporting its potential safety profile for chronic use.

14103121.label: Major findings and research outcome
14103121.value: This project successfully validated a novel therapeutic strategy for Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD). We confirmed that the hinge region of CTGF is a viable therapeutic target. Our engineered aptamer-drug conjugate, Apc-CTGF, effectively inhibited the proteolytic cleavage of full-length CTGF by matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs) in the skeletal muscle of mdx mice, a model of DMD. This inhibition led to a significant reduction in fibrotic progression, as evidenced by decreased collagen deposition and expression of ECM proteins. Importantly, attenuating fibrosis translated directly into functional benefits. The treated mice exhibited improved muscle mass, enhanced muscle strength, and signs of better muscle regeneration. Importantly, the treatment showed no significant toxicity to the liver or kidneys. These findings provide in vivo proof-of-concept that targeting the CTGF hinge region with a nucleic acid aptamer is a promising anti-fibrotic strategy that can ameliorate pathology and improve outcomes in muscular dystrophy.

14103121.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14103121.value: The research holds strong potential for clinical translation. The next step is to assess the underlying mechanism of drug using genetically modified animal model. Concurrently, more efficient modification strategies (e.g. oleic acid) for in vivo long-lasting effect of the aptamer drug will be evaluated to refine its pharmacokinetic profile. Furthermore, exploring combination therapies—such as coupling Apc-CTGF with agents that address primary dystrophin deficiency or other secondary pathologies (e.g., inflammation)—could yield synergistic benefits. We propose to seek follow-up funding for translational development, engage with biotechnology partners for drug development, and initiate pre-IND (Investigational New Drug) enabling studies to advance this aptamer-based therapeutic towards clinical trials for DMD and potentially other fibrotic diseases.

14103121.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14103121.value: Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD) is a severe genetic disease causing progressive muscle weakness. A major pathological problem in DMD is "fibrosis"—the build-up of stiff scar tissue in muscles that worsens their function. Our research targeted a key protein called CTGF that drives this scarring. We developed a new type of drug, a "targeted aptamer" named Apc-CTGF, designed to block CTGF from cleavage, which keeps CTGF in low activity mode. In a mouse model of DMD, this drug successfully reduced scar tissue formation in muscles. As a result, the mice had stronger muscles and showed less muscle damage. The drug also appeared safe for the liver and kidneys. This work offers a promising new approach to treat DMD by focusing on stopping scar tissue, which could help improve quality of life for patients.

14103221.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14103221.value: 通過全基因組測序 (WGS) 繪製甲狀腺相關眼眶病 (TAO) 基因圖

14103221.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14103221.value: Prof Chen, Lijia Prof Choy, Richard Kwong-wai Dr Chu, Wai Kit Prof Kong, Alice Pik Shan Dr LEE, Alan Chun-hong Prof Pang, Chi Pui Dr Wei, Yingying Prof Yam, Cheuk Sing Jason

14103221.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14103221.value: 甲狀腺相關眼眶病 (TAO) 是大多數人群中最常見的眼眶疾病並且經常發生在甲狀腺疾病患者中，全世界每1,000 人中有多於一人患有此病。TAO的病理機制涉及內分泌和免疫功能障礙，導致代謝、眼科甚至神經系統併發症。TAO可以有效地通過手術、放射性療法、抗炎療法和免疫療法治療。但約一半患者的臨床結果和疾病管理仍然很困難，存在致盲的後果和生活質量下降。為了加強早期發現、適當的治療和強化疾病管理，有必要制定定量和客觀的疾病評估。分子標記被認為有助於疾病管理和制定治療策略。基於在患者和對照組的研究，以及從TAO患者獲得的細胞中的基因表達，已經發現了一些相關的多態性TAO候選基因，可是目前所掌握的TAO遺傳信息仍然有限，對TAO的病理認識不足，這些不足都會阻礙分子標記的建立。值得注意的是，雖然已經有利用全基因組方法研究其他主要甲狀腺疾病的如格雷夫斯病和甲狀腺毒性週期麻痺並找到高風險位點和潛在風險的等位基因，但目前還未有對TAO進行全基因組研究。為了繪製TAO基因圖，我們將使用全基因組測序 (WGS)。我們已建立了一個包含965名確診並已紀錄了詳細臨床和內分泌檢查的漢族TAO患者的隊列，其中10%以上的病人有家族病史。基於我們的在全外顯子組測序、全基因組關聯研究和家庭基因聯繫研究來分析複雜的眼部疾病如青光眼、老年相關性黃斑病變和近視的經驗，我們計劃在MGISEQ-2000平台上利用WGS技術和30倍配對末端測序，為20個TAO三人家庭組和10個TAO家族鑑定基因組單核苷酸變異、基因拷貝數量變異與基因結構變異，並研究這些變異是否TAO獨有或與TAO有關聯。利用WGS研究TAO三人家庭組和TAO家族的這種新方法將可發現與TAO有密切關係的基因位點或基因變異。這種新的遺傳信息將提供了解TAO的分子基礎，幫助制定治療策略並提供TAO致病和治療反應的分子標記。
