14104221.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14104221.value: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) is endemic in Hong Kong. It is a cancer that occurs at the back of the nose, close to the skull base and brain. Early-stage disease is curable and is associated with less long-term treatment induced complications than advanced-stage disease, but until recently many early cancers went undetected because they cause no symptoms. This has changed with the introduction of a blood test that measures Epstein Barr Virus (EBV) DNA which can detect early-stage cancers in asymptomatic subjects screened for NPC. However, these early-stage cancers can be difficult to find on subsequent investigation because they are hidden from view on the endoscopic examination. Our previous research established the role of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) for the detection of these hidden cancers. Through prospective studies using our proposed MRI protocol and grading system we have shown that up to 47% of early-stage NPCs are missed by endoscopic examination but can be detected by MRI. MRI therefore has an important role in the NPC screening programs for early detection of NPC leading to a decrease in mortality and morbidity. To expand the application of MRI in NPC screening, we have developed a new MRI grading system for use with a fast high-resolution T2-weighted MRI sequence, bringing down the cost of MRI and avoiding the need for an intravenous contrast agent. In this study we plan to take our research a step forward by using artificial intelligence (AI) to develop an algorithm that can be applied to the T2-weighted image to automatically detect NPC. Our initial AI research has adapted a convolutional neural network (CNN) to successfully segment NPC and distinguish NPC from benign causes of thickening in the nasopharynx using this MRI sequence. In this project the objectives are firstly, to refine our AI algorithm for automatic NPC detection; secondly, to prospectively perform a T2-weighted MRI in patients being investigated for suspected NPC and compare the results of our AI algorithm with the results of an expert using the current MRI grading system; thirdly, to develop a user-friendly interface to apply the AI algorithm to the MRI scan.

14104321.value: 闡明核仁RNA解旋酶DDX21在神經退化中的作用

14104321.label: Project Objectives
14104321.value: To elucidate the molecular mechanisms leading to loss of heterochromatin in ribosomal DNA (rDNA) through functional interactions between DDX21, nucleolar remodeling complex (NoRC), and heterochromatin proteins in the nucleolus; To genetically ablate Ddx21 in mouse dopaminergic (DA) neurons and study its biological relevance in causing Parkinson disease (PD) and neurodegeneration.

14104321.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14104321.value: Aim: To elucidate the biological and molecular functions of the RNA helicase DDX21 in neurodegeneration. Background: In yeast, chromatin instability of ribosomal DNA (rDNA) is a driver of aging. The mechanism of rDNA instability in higher eukaryotes as well as their role in aging are not clearly defined. A human diploid genome contains approximately 300–400 copies of rDNA repeats sequestered as clusters in five acrocentric chromosomes. rDNA is organized in the nucleolus, a membraneless subnuclear organelle where rDNA transcription, rRNA processing, and ribosome biogenesis occur. The nucleolus does not simply serve as a factory for ribosome assembly. Similar to centromeres and telomeres, rDNA is highly repetitive and enriched with heterochromatin, which contains repressive epigenetic marks (e.g., H3K9me3). Loss of constitutive heterochromatin is a cause of genomic instability, leading to growth arrest, cellular senescence, and aging. In the nucleolus, perinucleolar heterochromatin plays a role in rDNA silencing, and dysregulation of this process leads to nucleolar disorganization and rDNA instability, which may be attributed to increased nucleolar stress. rDNA instability in the brain may eventually lead to a loss or gain of rDNA copy numbers, a phenomenon first described by Johnson and Strehler (1972) after observing the selective loss of rDNA in the aging brains of beagles. In mice, nucleolar disruption in dopaminergic neurons leads to oxidative damage and Parkinsonism. In this project, we propose that the maintenance of rDNA stability is regulated by nucleolar helicases. Downregulation of such helicases with increasing age could lead to a loss of heterochromatin and rDNA instability, consequently resulting in neurodegeneration. Several recent noteworthy studies have indicated that the RNA helicase DDX21 directly regulates rDNA transcription, ribosome biogenesis, nucleolar organization, and resolution of R-loop to safeguard genome stability. We therefore plan to test our hypothesis by performing genetic perturbation of DDX21 in both human stem cells and transgenic mice. Objectives: 1) to elucidate the molecular mechanisms leading to loss of heterochromatin in rDNA through functional interactions between DDX21, nucleolar remodeling complex and heterochromatin proteins in the nucleolus; 2) to genetically ablate Ddx21 in mouse dopaminergic neurons and study its biological relevance in causing Parkinson disease and neurodegeneration. Significance: The current work under this grant suggests a novel mechanism through which rDNA instability and the associated nucleolar disorganization could be a driver of neurodegeneration, which is a major medical concern facing societies as a result of aging populations. 目的： 闡明 RNA 解旋酶 DDX21 在神經退行性疾​​病中的生物學和分子功能。 背景： 在酵母中，核醣體 DNA (rDNA) 的染色質不穩定性是驅動衰老的因素之一。高等真核生物中 rDNA 不穩定性的機制及其在衰老中的作用尚不清楚。人類二倍體基因組包含大約 300-400 個 rDNA 的重複基因，這些重複序列出現在五個近著絲粒染色體中。 rDNA 出現在核仁中，核仁是一種無膜的亞核細胞器，主要進行 rDNA 轉錄、rRNA 加工和核醣體合成。核仁不僅僅是作為核醣體組裝的工廠，與著絲粒和端粒相似，rDNA 有高度重複性並富含異染色質，其中包含抑制性表觀遺傳標記（例如 H3K9me3）。異染色質的缺失是基因組不穩定的一個原因，導致生長停滯、細胞老化和衰老。在核仁中，核仁週異染色質在 rDNA 中起沉默作用，該過程的失調導致核仁解體和 rDNA 不穩定，這可能歸因於核仁應激增加。大腦中 rDNA 的不穩定性可能最終導致 rDNA 的基因數量變化。Johnson 和 Strehler (1972) 首次觀察到在年老的比格犬大腦中 rDNA 的基因數量選擇性減少這種現象。在小鼠中，多巴胺能神經元的核仁破壞會導致氧化損傷和帕金森病。在本項目中，我們提出維持 rDNA 的穩定性是由核仁解旋酶調節的。隨著年齡的增長，這種解旋酶的下調可能導致異染色質的丟失和 rDNA 的不穩定性，從而導致神經變性。最近幾項重要的研究表明，RNA 解旋酶 DDX21 直接調節 rDNA 轉錄、核醣體合成、核仁組織和 R-loop 的解旋，以保護基因組穩定性。因此，我們計劃通過在人類幹細胞和轉基因小鼠中對 DDX21 進行遺傳擾動來測試我們的假設。 目標： 1) 闡明通過 DDX21蛋白、核仁重塑複合物和核仁中的異染色質蛋白之間的功能相互作用導致 rDNA 中異染色質丟失的分子機制； 2) 在小鼠多巴胺能神經元中敲除Ddx21基因，並研究其在引起帕金森病和神經退行性疾​​病中的生物學相關性。 意義： 本項目從當前的工作中提出了一種新機制，通過該機制，rDNA 不穩定性和相關的核仁解體可能是驅動神經退化的因素，這也是人口老齡化導致社會面臨的主要醫學問題。

14104521.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14104521.value: 擬南芥中一種非典型植物U盒類蛋白調節初生根生長的機理研究

14104521.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14104521.value: 本項目的目的是對模式植物擬南芥中一種非典型植物U盒類蛋白LPR調節初生根生長的機理進行研究。 植物根是植物體的地下器官，對植物的整體生長發育至關重要。根系提供植物在土壤中的錨定、水分和養分的吸收以及與土壤微生物群的相互作用。植物的根系由初生根和次生根（或側根）組成。初生根是在種子的胚中開始生長的根，是植物發現其土壤環境的原始根。高等植物的初生根來源於一組多能、自我更新的幹細胞，這些幹細胞分佈在根尖分生組織（RAM）中，產生不同的根組織，並確保根在植物生命週期中持續生長。初生根的生長由RAM的活性和伸長區中分化細胞的快速生長决定。所有這些過程都受到細緻的調節，而植物激素在每個過程中都起著關鍵作用。迄今為止，所有已鑒定的激素，包括生長素、細胞分裂素（CK）、赤黴素（GA）、油菜素甾體（BR）、脫落酸（ABA）、strigolactone（SL）、乙烯（ET）、茉莉酸（JA）和水楊酸（SA）均與植物根系生長發育的調控有關。最近的研究表明，這些激素相互作用，形成一個複雜的激素相互作用網絡。然而，這些不同的激素是如何通過訊號通路相互作用來調節植物根系的生長和發育的，人們對此知之甚少。 從最近的一項有關擬南芥磷酸化蛋白組學的研究中，我們鑒定到了一個新的植物蛋白LPR，這個蛋白在生物學功能上以前從未被描述過。與野生型植物相比，LPR的T-DNA插入突變體lpr的初生根更長，因此LPR意指長初生根（Long Primary Root）。在基因庫中，該蛋白被注釋為一種假定的含有U盒 (U-box) 的泛素E3連接酶，它與一些含有U盒的植物E3連接酶（PUB）具有序列相似性，例如那些含有Ser/Thr激酶（STK）結構域的PUB。然而，LPR在其N末端僅包含部分STK結構域，並且沒有任何U盒，這表明它不是典型的PUB型E3連接酶。與這一假設相一致，我們在初期研究中，沒有檢測到LPR有任何激酶或E3連接酶活性。有趣的是，LPR被發現與含有STK結構域的PUB33有直接相互作用，並且LPR能够增强PUB33的E3活性（自身泛素化）。此外，LPR基因的表達是由乙烯（ET）誘導的，且lpr突變體對ET抑制初生根生長的反應不敏感，表明LPR參與ET調控植物根系生長。此外，LPR和PUB33均可與三種ET受體ERS1、ERS2和EIN4相互作用。 基於上述初步實驗數據，我們假設LPR可能與PUB33形成异二聚體，從而增强PUB33對ET受體的E3連接酶活性，從而增强ET訊號輸出並抑制初生根生長。因此，本項目的主要目的是檢測LPR是否影響PUB33在其靶蛋白上的E3連接酶活性，以及它們如何影響ET調節的植物根系生長。我們預計LPR構成了ET訊號通路中一個新的組分，並且是植物根系生長的一個新的調節因子。

14104621.label: Project Objectives
14104621.value: Our preliminary results show that the GHRH-R antagonist MIA-602 could suppress degenerative retinal changes in experimental autoimmune uveoretinitis (EAU) mice based on the real-time measurements. Apart from these real-time measurements, we also need to define the possible sites of actions of GHRH-R antagonist, the changes in expression of GHRH, GHRH-R and related genes in posterior segments of the eye and the infiltrating cells during degenerative changes in the retina and in T cells. The first objective is to further investigate the anti-inflammatory outcomes, in terms of histology, cytokine profiling in serum and T cells, T cell antigen recall responses, retinal microglia, and retinal gene expression, of GHRH-R antagonist MIA-602 in EAU mice. Possible involvement of microglia will be studied. The drug toxicity in major organs of MIA-602 treated EAU mice will also be studied. Based on our preliminary results that the GHRH-R antagonist MIA-602 could suppress degenerative retinal changes in EAU mice, we hypothesize the GHRH-R knock out mice would develop no/lesser degenerative retinal changes and T cell responses upon experimental induction of autoimmune uveitis in mice. The second objective is to compare the retinal changes and T cell responses in wild type and GHRH-R knock out mice before and after EAU induction. As GHRH-R is an important protein to regulate the levels of downstream signaling molecules growth hormone (GH) and insulin-like growth factor-I (IGF1), we also want to study if supplementing GHRH-R downstream signaling molecules GH and IGF1 could restore the retinal changes and T cell responses in GHRH-R knock out mice after EAU induction. Recently, we have published a study on the GHRH-R signaling in another uveitis animal model, the lipopolysaccharide induced acute ocular inflammation model. Although this animal model is different from the EAU model, our findings suggest there is a direct interaction between GHRH-R and JAK2 kinase. Considering there are similarities between the lipopolysaccharide induced animal model and the EAU model, our preliminary work of treating EAU mice with JAK2 inhibitor ruxolitinib found that JAK inhibition is able to reduce ocular inflammation symptoms. This result suggests that JAK may involve in the GHRH-R signaling pathway in the EAU mice. The third objective will study the JAK-STAT family as important downstream signaling intermediates of GHRH-R in responses to EAU induction. Binding between GHRH-R and various JAK and STAT family members, and phosphorylation on various STAT family members, in non-induced and EAU animals treated with control treatment or MIA-602, as well as in wild type and Ghrhr-/- mice will be studied in proteins extracted from retina, iris and ciliary body.

14104621.label: Realisation of objectives
14104621.value: All the 3 objectives have been fully achieved. Objective 1: GHRH-R antagonist MIA-602 has been treated to the EAU mice. We found that MIA-602 could reduce EAU severity in terms of retinal-choroidal thickness, clinical scoring and retinal histology. Cytokine mRNA expression including Il17a, Il17f, Il22 and Csf2 in eye infiltrating CD4 positive T cells were significantly reduced by MIA-602 treatment. In the retina, the mRNA expression of Ghrh, Ghrhr and Ghrhr sv1 were significantly induced by EAU induction. We found GHRH-R was highly expressed in activated T cells. To evaluate the drug toxicity, as we wanted to focus more on the eyes, we measured the body weights of MIA-602 treated mice to evaluate the systemic drug toxicity. We did not detect any significant difference in the body weights between the solvent control treated and the MIA-602 treated mice. Objective 2: We found that EAU severity in terms of retinal-choroidal thickness, electroretinography, clinical scoring and retinal histology was significantly reduced in GHRH-R knock out mice after EAU induction. Cytokine mRNA expression including Il17a, Il17f, Il22 and Csf2 in eye infiltrating CD4 positive T cells were significantly reduced GHRH-R knock out mice after EAU induction. And we found that depletion of GH and IGF1 by antibodies did not reduce the abundance of T cells expressing the important cytokine IL-17A. Objective 3: We found that STAT3 phosphorylation on tyrosine 705 in T cells could be induced in wild type but not GHRH-R knock out T cells under differentiation. Ruxolitinib, a JAK2 inhibitor, could suppress STAT3 phosphorylation on tyrosine 705 in T cells. MR-409 could enhance the abundance of T cells expressing the important cytokine IL-17A, which this enhancement effect was suppressed by ruxolitinib treatment. Our results suggest JAK2 and STAT3 are important downstream signaling intermediates of GHRH-R in responses to EAU induction. As IL-17A is a hallmark cytokine of the T Helper 17 (Th17) cells, we further found that the abundance of Th17 cells were down-regulated in spleen, lymph nodes and eyeballs of MIA-602 treated mice and GHRH-R knock out mice after EAU induction. We also found the GHRH-R downstream proteins JAK2 and STAT3 are important to maintain the abundance of T Helper 17 cells.

14104621.label: Major findings and research outcome
14104621.value: We have found that GHRH-R inhibition, either by the treatment of MIA-602 or by knocking out GHRH-R, could alleviate experimental autoimmune uveitis in mice. We found the GHRH-R inhibition could suppress the downstream JAK2-STAT3 signaling pathway to suppress the abundance of T cells, in particular Th17 cells, in spleen, lymph nodes and eyeballs of EAU mice. These findings have been published as an original research article “Growth hormone releasing hormone signaling promotes Th17 cell differentiation and autoimmune inflammation” in the journal “Nature Communications”. Through this project, we have accumulated knowledge in the roles of GHRH-R pathway in eyes. Therefore, we summarized our EAU data, along with GHRH-R findings in other major eye diseases including glaucoma, diabetic retinopathy and retinoblastoma, to publish a review article “Growth hormone-releasing hormone receptor signaling in experimental ocular inflammation and neuroprotection” in the journal “Neural Regeneration Research”. Through this project, we have built international reputation in the field of uveitis. Therefore, I was invited to review a manuscript “The bromodomain and extra-terminal protein inhibitor OTX015 suppresses T helper cell proliferation and differentiation” in the journal “eBioMedicine”. And subsequently, I was invited to write a comment in eBioMedicine to guide the journal readers about how this new publication could enhance our understanding of autoimmune uveitis and its implications in the future development of a novel treatment. In addition, because of this project, we were able to learn more about the signaling pathways regulating the severity of ocular inflammation. We leant that there was a new cGAS-STING pathway detecting cytoplasmic DNA that could trigger immune responses and this pathway had been reported in multiple ocular inflammatory diseases. Therefore, we summarized the recent findings of the cGAS-STING pathway in various ocular inflammatory diseases and published a review article “Emerging Roles of cGAS-STING Signaling in Mediating Ocular Inflammation” in the journal “Journal of Innate Immunity”. Furthermore, this project allowed us to study the GHRH-R pathway in other eye diseases including macular degeneration, glaucoma and retinoblastoma, as well as other potential treatments of uveitis including green tea extracts and mineralocorticoid receptor agonist. These findings were reported in The Association for Research in Vision and Ophthalmology (ARVO) Annual Meeting in 2023 and 2024.

14104621.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14104621.value: In this project, we noticed the abundance of a specific subtype of T cells, the T Helper 17 cells, was suppressed in MIA-602 treated or GHRH-R knock out mice after EAU induction. In the future, we could study the precise cellular features including cell proliferation, cell death, and differentiation of naïve T cells into mature T cell subtypes regulated by GHRH-R. In addition, our existing results found GHRH-R inhibition could resolve retinal damages caused by EAU induction, as well as suppression of T cell abundance. In the future, we could study the specific target cells and tissues, for example T cells and/or retinal tissues, are the main target sites for GHRH-R inhibition in EAU mice.

14104621.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14104621.value: Autoimmune uveitis is a kind of intraocular inflammatory disorder that can lead to permanent blindness. Some patients fail to respond to the steroids that are the current standard treatment, while some develop serious side-effects. Lacking an effective treatment, autoimmune uveitis has become a chronic, recurrent eye disease. We conducted a study on autoimmune uveitis and has found its disease mechanism, which opens up a new direction for treatment. We identified a neuroendocrine growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH) pathway developing disease-causing T Helper 17 (Th17) cells that promote autoimmune uveitis. The team also discovered existing approved drugs that can suppress the GHRH pathway and could be developed as novel treatments.

14105321.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14105321.value: Background: Atherosclerosis is the chronic inflammation of vascular wall initiated by the interplay between disturbed blood flow and hyperlipidemia, leading to endothelial cell dysfunction, subsequent inflammatory responses and macrophage infiltration, eventually forming atherosclerotic plaques. Plaque formation causes narrowing, blockage of arteries often followed by plaque rupture and thrombosis, leading to serious consequences and it is the major cause of cardiovascular diseases (CVD) such as coronary artery disease and stroke. CVD remains among the top three causes of death with a mortality rate >13% and also one of the top causes of in-patient discharges in Hong Kong. Sox4 belongs to the sex-determining region Y(SRY)-box (Sox) family. It is considered as a highly conserved transcription factor. Sox4 is involved in many cellular processes such as cell proliferation, differentiation, and apoptosis. Previous studies showed an important role of Sox4 in tumor vascularization and metastasis. However, the role of Sox4 in vascular inflammation and atherosclerosis is unknown. Hypothesis: Based on our single cell RNA sequencing and preliminary result suggesting a pro-atherogenic role of endothelial-selective Sox4 overexpression in mice, we hypothesize that Sox4 upregulation exacerbates vascular inflammation leading to increased atherosclerotic plaque formation, while Sox4 inhibition reduces plaque formation. In endothelial cells, Sox4, which could be triggered by hypercholesterolemia, induces endothelin-1 production which impairs endothelial cell function and enhances vascular inflammatory responses. Project Description: To test the hypothesis, modulation of endothelial Sox4 expression will be achieved by adeno-associated virus to transduce either overexpression of Sox4 driven by endothelial-selective promoter in Apoe knockout mice fed with high cholesterol diet to induce atherosclerosis. Sox4 inhibition will be achieved by delivery of sgRNA of Sox4 in endothelial selective Cas9 knock-in mice. We will first examine whether endothelial overexpression of Sox4 accelerates while inhibition of Sox4 attenuates vascular inflammation and atherosclerosis under hypercholesterolemia in mice. We will then study whether the increased production of endothelin-1 is a key factor downstream of Sox4 to enhance endothelial dysfunction in endothelial cells by using functional, biochemical, and molecular assays, and whether antagonizing endothelin-1 pathway alleviates endothelial dysfunction and atherosclerosis related to Sox4 upregulation. We will also dissect the regulatory network and expression profile related to Sox4 in endothelial cells. Significance: This study shall provide insight into the complex transcriptional regulatory network governing endothelial cell behavior in the context of atherosclerosis. Results from this study will also explore the potential of targeting Sox4 and endothelin-1 related pathway in treating atherosclerotic vascular disease. 研究背景：動脈粥樣硬化是由血流紊亂和高脂血症相互作用引發的血管壁慢性炎症，導致內皮細胞功能障礙、炎症反應、和巨噬細胞浸潤，最終形成動脈粥樣硬化（AS）斑塊。斑塊形成導致動脈變窄、引起缺血，甚至斑塊破裂和血栓形成，是導致冠狀動脈疾病和中風等心血管疾病（CVD）的主要原因。Sox4 是一個高度保守的轉錄因子，參與許多細胞過程，如細胞增殖、分化和凋亡。以往的研究表明 Sox4 在腫瘤血管形成和轉移中的重要作用。然而，Sox4 在血管炎症和動脈粥樣硬化中是否有作用尚不清楚。 研究假設：前期實驗的單細胞 RNA 測序提示Sox4在AS的內皮細胞中高表達。在體小鼠內皮選擇性 Sox4 過表達增加AS 斑塊面積。現提出假設 內皮選擇性過表達Sox4加劇血管炎症，導致AS斑塊增加；同時抑制 內皮細胞表達的Sox4減少AS。高膽固醇血症可能是促使Sox4上調的誘因，引起下游內皮素-1生成，促使內皮細胞功能損害並加劇血管炎症反應。 研究計劃：我們將通過腺相關病毒上調由內皮選擇性啟動子驅動的Sox4，在高膽固醇飲食餵養的 Apoe 基因敲除小鼠中誘導AS。在體Sox4 的抑制將通過在內皮選擇性 Cas9 敲入小鼠中用腺相關病毒表達Sox4的sgRNA 來實現。我們將首先研究Sox4 的內皮過表達是否會加速，而 Sox4 的抑制是否會減輕小鼠高膽固醇血症下的血管炎症和動脈粥樣硬化。我們將進一步通過功能、生化和分子等多種方法檢測內皮素-1 的增加是否是 Sox4 下游增強內皮細胞功能障礙的關鍵因素。同時，用藥物拮抗內皮素-1 通路是否可以緩解與Sox4 上調相關的內皮功能障礙和動脈粥樣硬化。我們還將深入分析內皮細胞中與 Sox4 相關的調控網絡和表達譜。 研究意義：這項研究將深入了解在AS疾病發展中內皮細胞行為的轉錄調控網絡。這項研究的結果還將探索靶向 Sox4 和內皮素-1 相關通路在治療動脈粥樣硬化血管疾病中的潛在價值。

14106521.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14106521.value: Skeletal muscle has a remarkable ability to regenerate which relies on its resident muscle stem cells (also called satellite cells, SCs) normally residing quiescently beneath muscle fiber. SCs can quickly activate and proliferate following injury, then differentiate and fuse into myofiber; meanwhile a subset of SCs undergoes self-renewal and returns to quiescence to replenish SC pool. SC lineage progression is orchestrated by complex regulatory networks of intrinsic and extrinsic factors/mechanisms. Compared to the wealth of knowledge in the intrinsic regulation occurring in SCs, the extrinsic regulation mediated through SC crosstalk with other cell types within their niche environment is less explored. Emerging evidence demonstrates that disruption of the extrinsic regulations may render SC loss of ability to regenerate, contributing to muscle wasting conditions such as Duchene muscular dystrophy (DMD) which is characterized by repetitive cycle of degeneration/regeneration and eventual loss of regenerative ability, accumulation of inflammation and fibrosis. Here in this study we elucidate the complex niche environment in DMD. Findings from our pilot studies demonstrate that deletion of a key transcription factor, Yin Yang 1 (YY1) in SCs of dystrophic mdx mouse aggravates dystrophic pathology manifested by exacerbated fibrosis which is directly associated with increased number of fibro-adipogenic progenitors (FAPs). Further investigation shows that YY1 deletion leads to induction of CCL5 chemoattractant in SCs which increases the recruitment of macrophages (MPs); the MPs in turn promote FAP survival through elevated TGFβ signaling. Furthermore, we found CCL5 expression is regulated by YY1 at 3D genome level. Altogether, our preliminary findings promote us to hypothesize that intrinsic YY1 protein functions as a 3D structural protein to regulate CCL5 production by SCs which plays a role in orchestrating SC/MP/FAP crosstalk through CCL5/TGFβ signaling; loss of YY1 in SCs leads to skewed cellular niche environment and consequently severe fibrosis and dystrophic pathology. To test the hypothesis, three objectives are proposed (1) To further characterize how YY1 deletion in SCs aggravates dystrophic pathology and alters niche environment in mdx muscles. (2) To further investigate how intrinsic YY1 loss in SCs disrupts crosstalk of SC/MP/FAP via CCL5/ TGFβ signaling. (3) To elucidate how YY1 regulates CCL5 expression at 3D genome level in SCs. Once completed, this study will be the first to reveal the intricate connection between intrinsic and extrinsic regulations in DMD; it will thus enhance our knowledge foundation in the niche regulatory mechanisms underlying skeletal muscle regeneration and diseases for future therapeutic development. 骨骼肌在受到損傷後具有強大的修復和再生能力，得益於常駐在肌肉組織裡的肌肉幹細胞（也稱為衛星細胞）。 衛星細胞通常附著在肌肉纖維下方並保持靜息狀態，但是在肌肉受傷後可以迅速被激活，並進一步增殖、分化融合成肌纖維；同時，一部分衛星細胞返回靜息狀態以維持衛星細胞的數量。研究表明，衛星細胞的活性受到內在和外在機制網路的精細調節，相對而言，我們對內在調節機制的研究比較多，但是對外在的調控主要包括衛星細胞與其他細胞在其微環境中的相互作用的機制探索比較欠缺。大量新出現的證據表明，破壞外在調節可能會導致衛星細胞失去再生能力，導致肌肉萎縮，例如在杜氏肌營養不良症 (DMD)中，肌肉在初始階段進行重複性的退化/再生，但是最終由於外在調節的破壞導致喪失再生能力，並且伴隨著炎症積累和纖維化，肌肉功能被徹底摧毀。在這項研究中，我們將致力於闡明了DMD疾病中複雜的肌肉微環境調節。我們的初步研究結果表明，在DMD疾病模型小鼠（mdx 小鼠）的衛星細胞中，關鍵轉錄因數Yin Yang 1 (YY1) 的缺失會加劇肌營養不良病症，具體的表現為肌肉組織纖維化加劇，這與纖維脂肪前體細胞 (FAP) 的數量在肌肉微環境中激增直接相關。進一步研究表明，YY1 的缺失造成衛星細胞中 C-C 基序趨化因數配體 5（CCL5）的大量表達和分泌，從而募集更多的巨噬細胞 (Macrophage, MP) 浸潤肌肉組織； 巨噬細胞继而表達並分泌更多的轉化生長因數 β （TGFβ）來促進纖維脂肪前體細胞的存活。此外,我們發現 CCL5 的表達在 3D 基因組水平上受 YY1 調節。根據如上初步發現，我們提出如下假設：衛星細胞中的内源 YY1 蛋白能夠作為 3D 結構調節蛋白調控CCL5在衛星細胞中的表達，再通過 CCL5/ TGFβ 介導的衛星細胞/巨噬細胞/纖維脂肪前體細胞的相互作用來影響整個肌肉再生過程；衛星細胞中YY1 的缺失導致外在的肌肉微環境的改變，從而造成嚴重的纖維化和營養不良病症。為了進一步驗證該假設，我們提出了三個目標 (1) 進一步闡明衛星細胞中 YY1 缺失如何加重營養不良病症並改變肌肉的微環境。 (2) 進一步研究衛星細胞中YY1 缺失如何通過 CCL5/TGFβ 信號通路破壞衛星細胞/巨噬細胞/纖維脂肪前體細胞之間的相互作用。 (3) 闡明 YY1 如何在3D 基因組水平上調節 CCL5在衛星細胞中的表達。一旦這些目標被完成，這項研究將首次揭示在DMD疾病中肌肉修復的內在和外在調節的聯繫；它將加強我們在骨骼肌再生和疾病的調節機制方面的知識基礎，以促進未來肌萎縮疾病的治療發展。

14106521.label: Realisation of objectives
14106521.value: Aim1: To further characterize how YY1 deletion in SCs aggravates dystrophic pathology and alters niche environment in mdx muscles. This Aim has been 100% realized. Our study employed an inducible Yy1/mdx double knockout (dKO) mouse model to investigate the phenotypic and cellular consequences of YY1 deletion in muscle stem cells (MuSCs). Key findings include: 1. Aggravated dystrophic pathology: dKO mice exhibited severe muscle degeneration, increased fibrosis (confirmed by Masson's trichrome staining and fibrotic markers), enhanced inflammation (elevated inflammatory markers and macrophage infiltration), impaired regeneration (reduced centrally nucleated fibers and MuSC proliferation), and significant muscle weakness. 2. Altered niche composition: Single-cell RNA-seq analysis revealed skewed cellular heterogeneity in dKO muscles, with increased proportions of fibro-adipogenic progenitors (FAPs) and altered macrophage (MP) subpopulations, alongside a reduced MuSC pool. 3. Functional decline: dKO mice showed reduced exercise endurance, lower body weight, and decreased survival rates. Aim2: To further investigate how intrinsic YY1 loss in SCs disrupts crosstalk of SC/MP/FAP via CCL5/ TGFβ signaling This Aim has been 100% realized. Through integrated transcriptomic, proteomic, and functional assays, our study delineated a clear signaling axis: 1. YY1 loss induces CCL5 in MuSCs: Bulk RNA-seq and immunoassays showed upregulation of Ccl5 and other chemokines in dKO MuSCs. 2. CCL5/CCR5 axis mediates MP recruitment: Transwell assays confirmed enhanced macrophage migration toward dKO MuSCs, which was blocked by CCL5 or CCR5 neutralization. 3. MP-derived TGFβ1 promotes FAP accumulation: Increased TGFβ1 levels in dKO muscles were linked to MP infiltration. TGFβ1 inhibited FAP apoptosis, leading to FAP persistence and fibrosis. 4. Pharmacological validation: Treatment with the CCR5 antagonist Maraviroc (MVC) reduced MP and FAP numbers, lowered TGFβ1, and ameliorated dystrophic pathology. Aim3: To elucidate how YY1 regulates CCL5 expression at 3D genome level in SCs. This Aim has been 100% realized.The study employed advanced genomic and chromatin conformation techniques to uncover YY1’s role in 3D genome organization: 1. YY1 binding and enhancer identification: ChIP-seq revealed YY1 binding at a distal enhancer of the Ccl5 locus. 2. Altered chromatin looping: Hi-C and 3C-qPCR showed that YY1 deletion weakened enhancer-promoter (E-P) looping at the Ccl5 locus, leading to its derepression. 3. Functional validation: Artificial tethering of YY1 to the Ccl5 enhancer in C2C12 cells restored E-P interaction and suppressed Ccl5 expression. 4. Luciferase assays: Confirmed that the enhancer element represses Ccl5 transcription in a YY1-dependent manner. In summary, all three objectives have been fully achieved with robust experimental evidence spanning molecular, cellular, and organismal levels. This project has successfully elucidated a previously unrecognized role of MuSCs in actively shaping their niche via the YY1–CCL5–TGFβ1 axis in dystrophic muscle. The findings provide novel mechanistic insights and highlight the therapeutic potential of targeting the CCL5/CCR5 pathway in Duchenne muscular dystrophy.

14106521.label: Major findings and research outcome
14106521.value: Adult skeletal muscle stem cells (MuSCs) are indispensable for muscle regeneration and tightly regulated by macrophages (MPs) and fibro-adipogenic progenitors (FAPs) in their niche. Deregulated MuSC/MP/FAP interactions and the ensuing inflammation and fibrosis are hallmarks of dystrophic muscle. Here we demonstrate intrinsic deletion of transcription factor Yin Yang 1 (YY1) in MuSCs exacerbates dystrophic pathologies by altering composition and heterogeneity of MPs and FAPs. Further analysis reveals YY1 loss induces expression of immune genes in MuSCs, including C-C Motif Chemokine Ligand 5 (Ccl5). Augmented CCL5 secretion promotes MP recruitment via CCL5/C-C Chemokine Receptor 5 (CCR5) crosstalk, which subsequently hinders FAP clearance through elevated Transforming growth factor-β1 (TGFβ1). Maraviroc-mediated pharmacological blockade of the CCL5/CCR5 axis effectively mitigates muscle dystrophy and improves muscle performance. Lastly, we demonstrate YY1 represses Ccl5 transcription by binding to its enhancer thus facilitating promoter-enhancer looping. Altogether, our study demonstrates the critical role of MuSCs in actively shaping their niche and provides novel insight into the therapeutic intervention of muscle dystrophy. Our research outcomes are provided in Part C in details.

14106521.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14106521.value: Our Yy1/mdx dKO mice however display more severe dystrophic pathologies mimicking human DMD. Therefore, CCL5/CCR5 axis constitutes a potential target for DMD treatment. Although gene and molecular therapies targeting the primary defect of Dystrophin gene remain the most promising approach for DMD treatment, therapeutic strategies targeting the complex secondary mechanisms responsible for DMD pathogenesis are also being developed in parallel. Drugs aiming at reducing inflammation and fibrosis are proven to be effective in mitigating the disease progression. In our study, MVC treatment leads to notable amelioration of the dystrophy pathologies; both inflammation and fibrosis were reduced while muscle performance was improved, which encourages us to perform trials in human DMD patients in the future. In addition, our findings also reinforce the previously known pro-fibrotic role of TGFβ1 in dystrophic muscle highlighting it as a potential therapeutic target. Indeed, targeting TGFβ signaling by intramuscular injection of an inhibitor leads to reduced FAP accumulation and fibrosis in dystrophic mice.

14106521.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14106521.value: Our research explores how muscle stem cells, which are crucial for muscle repair, interact with their surrounding environment in Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD), a severe muscle-wasting disease. The scientists discovered that when a specific protein (YY1) is removed from these stem cells in mice with DMD, it makes the disease much worse. This happens because the stem cells start overproducing a signal (CCL5) that attracts too many inflammatory cells. These cells then create a harmful environment that blocks the natural cleanup of scar-tissue-producing cells, leading to increased scarring and inflammation. Importantly, the team found that using an existing drug (Maraviroc) to block this harmful signal chain reduced scarring, improved muscle function, and slowed disease progression in the mice. This work is significant because it reveals a previously unknown active role for muscle stem cells in shaping their own environment and identifies a promising new drug target for treating DMD.

14107321.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14107321.value: 結直腸癌 (CRC) 是香港第一大癌癥，其發生發展涉及一系列遺傳和表觀遺傳改變。RNA N6-甲基腺苷 (m6A)是人類中最豐富的RNA修飾形式，對RNA轉錄後調控中起著關鍵作用。最近研究表明了m6A調節蛋白在腫瘤發生過程中的重要性，其中就包括了我們團隊所報道的m6A甲基化酶METTL3。除了腫瘤細胞的內在因素，外部環境因素也可以通過調節腸道微生物群影響CRC的發生。腸道微生物群的擾動可能會破壞腸道細菌與宿主細胞之間的相互作用。我們團隊是最早揭示CRC患者糞便具有促腫瘤作用的團隊之一。然而，到目前為止，還沒有關於宿主RNA m6A修飾的改變是否會影響腸道微生物群的改變，以及這種改變是否會進一步推動CRC發展的相關研究。為了探究宿主m6A修飾對腸道微生物群變化的潛在作用，我們構建了Mettl3基因敲除小鼠模型。結果表明，Mettl3表達的沈默抑製了結直腸腫瘤的發生。通過16S rDNA測序分析，Mettl3減少了腸道微生物群的多樣性並極大改變了糞便中腸道微生物群的整體組成。我們發現，Mettl3增加了小鼠糞便中Anaerostipes、Clostridium、Parabacteroides以及Ruminococcus的豐度。相對應的，通過分析TCGA-COAD 樣本，在CRC中METTL3的表達水平與這些細菌的富集程度存在正相關。我們進一步探索了METTL3誘導腸道細菌變化的潛在機製。在功能上，Mettl3的異常表達可以損害腸道屏障的完整性，同時增加促炎細胞因子（如 CXCL1、IL-6 和 TNF-α）的表達和分泌。從機製上講，METTL3介導的m6A修飾異常可能會影響CRC中的 IFN-α、IFN-γ和 TNF等信號傳導。在本項研究中，我們旨在實現以下目標：（1）明確CRC中METTL3異常表達所影響的相關腸道細菌，並闡明METTL3介導的m6A修飾如何改變腸道微生物群落的機製；(2)證明 METTL3相關腸道細菌對CRC發生發展的作用和潛在機製；(3)評估CRC患者從癌前病變到癌變過程中METTL3相關腸道細菌的豐度，並評估其與METTL3表達水平的相關性；(4)研究METTL3相關微生物標誌物對結直腸癌診斷和預後的潛在價值。該項目的成果將增加我們對宿主-微生物群相互作用以及這種作用的異常變化與CRC發生發展的潛在關聯的理解。該項目將有助於我們開發CRC診斷和預後的新策略。

14107321.label: Realisation of objectives
14107321.value: (1) Mettl3 genetically engineered mouse models demonstrate its tumor-promoting role in colorectal cancer (CRC). We successfully generated colon-specific Mettl3 knock-in (Mettl3-cKI; Rosa26 LSL-Mettl3, CDX2-CreErt2) and knock-out (Mettl3-cKO; Mettl3 flox/flox, CDX2-CreErt2) mouse models. In AOM-DSS-induced CRC models, Mettl3-cKI mice developed a significantly higher tumor burden, characterized by both increased tumor number and size, compared to control mice. Conversely, Mettl3-cKO mice exhibited a protective phenotype with reduced tumorigenesis in both AOM-induced and Apc min/+ genetic models. Together, METTL3 promotes CRC development. (2) METTL3 expression reshapes the gut microbiome prior to tumorigenesis. To investigate whether METTL3 influences CRC via the gut microbiome, we conducted metagenomic sequencing on stool samples from tumor-free Mettl3-cKI mice and their WT littermates. METTL3 overexpression significantly altered the gut microbial composition prior to any tumor development. Alpha diversity analysis indicated a significant increase in both microbial richness (Observed species, ACE, Chao1) and overall diversity (Shannon index) in Mettl3-cKI mice. This restructuring was further confirmed by beta diversity analysis, where Principal Coordinates Analysis (PCoA) at the OTU level showed clear separation between the WT and Mettl3-cKI microbial communities. While several bacterial taxa, including Akkermansia muciniphila (A. muciniphila), Parabacteroides distasonis, Duncaniella dubosii, Muribaculum intestinale, and Muribaculum gordoncarteri, were highly enriched in both genotypes, LEfSe analysis identified 50 specific bacterial species with differential abundance in Mettl3-cKI mice (28 enriched, 22 depleted). Notably, the most significantly suppressed microbe was the mucin-degrading bacterium A. muciniphila, a common and beneficial resident of the healthy mammalian gut. Conversely, the abundance of A. muciniphila was significantly elevated after METTL3 knockout in Mettl3-cKO mice across both AOM-induced and Apc min/+ models. To directly test METTL3's regulatory role on A. muciniphila, we administered the bacterium via oral gavage to Mettl3-cKI and WT littermates following a prior course of antibiotics to deplete the endogenous microbiota. Strikingly, while A. muciniphila colonization levels increased in both groups from day 6 onwards, this increase was significantly attenuated in Mettl3-cKI mice compared to WT controls. Collectively, these data demonstrate that colon-specific METTL3 expression remodels the gut microbiome and directly impairs the colonization and abundance of A. muciniphila in the murine gut, independent of tumor presence. (3) METTL3 may regulate A. muciniphila abundance via the m6A-ETS1-phosphatidylcholine axis METTL3 is the principal methyltransferase responsible for mRNA m6A modification. To investigate the mechanistic consequences of its loss, we performed m6A sequencing in MC38 cells with and without METTL3 knockout (M3KO). We identified 9477 and 9092 high-confidence m6A peaks in control (MC38-NC) and M3KO cells, respectively. These peaks were predominantly enriched within coding sequences (CDS) and 3' untranslated regions, with a sharp density peak near the stop codon. Sequence motif analysis confirmed the canonical GGAC consensus motif. Comparative analysis revealed 316 significantly downregulated m6A peaks (adjusted p < 0.01, absolute fold change > 2) upon METTL3 knockout, corresponding to 289 transcripts. Among these, we validated five key downstream targets, including ETS1, whose m6A levels were directly regulated by METTL3. Intriguingly, ETS1 has been reported to promote phosphatidylcholine (PC) biosynthesis (DOI: 10.1016/j.celrep.2025.116530). In line with this, METTL3 overexpression significantly increased PC levels in stools of transgenic mice models and in cellular conditioned medium. We discovered that this conditioned medium directly suppressed the growth of A. muciniphila in vitro. This finding aligns with prior reports that a high-choline diet reduces Akkermansia abundance in vivo (DOI: 10.1038/s41387-021-00169-w). Collectively, METTL3-m6A-ETS1 axis may modulate host phosphatidylcholine production, thereby influencing the abundance of the gut commensal A. muciniphila. (4) A. muciniphila mediates the tumor-promoting role of METTL3 in CRC. To determine whether the suppression of A. muciniphila is functionally important for the tumor-promoting role of METTL3, we induced CRC with AOM in Mettl3-cKI mice and WT littermates. Following AOM treatment, mice received oral gavage of A. muciniphila (2 × 10⁸ CFU) or a vehicle control twice per week. Tumor progression was monitored by colonoscopy. Prior to harvest, colonoscopy imaging revealed that untreated Mettl3-cKI mice developed significantly more tumors than their WT counterparts. However, this difference was substantially diminished in mice that received A. muciniphila supplementation. Consistent with these observations, post-harvest quantification confirmed that Mettl3-cKI mice exhibited a significant increase in both tumor number and overall tumor load compared to WT controls. Again, A. muciniphila gavage effectively mitigated this difference, reducing tumor burden in Mettl3-cKI mice to levels comparable to those in WT mice. Successful colonization of A. muciniphila in the gut was verified by fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH), and METTL3 overexpression in the colonic epithelium was confirmed by immunohistochemistry (IHC). Given the established role of A. muciniphila in enhancing anti-tumor immunity (DOI: 10.1002/imo2.70010), we investigated the involvement of CD8⁺ T cells. In line with the observed tumor suppression, METTL3 depletion in Apc min/+ mice significantly increased the infiltration of CD8⁺ T cells, particularly the activated subset, as measured by flow cytometry and IHC. Notably, the growth-inhibitory effect of METTL3 knockout was completely abrogated upon CD8⁺ T cell depletion in CRC allograft model. Together, these data demonstrate that METTL3 could promote colorectal tumorigenesis by suppressing A. muciniphila, which may in turn dampens anti-tumor CD8⁺ T cell response. (5) METTL3 expression inversely correlates with A. muciniphila in human CRC. We explored the correlation between METTL3 expression and A. muciniphila abundance in human CRC tissues. Analysis of a CRC tissue microarray by METTL3 immunohistochemistry (IHC) and A. muciniphila-specific fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) revealed that tumors with low METTL3 expression (n=68) harbored significantly more A. muciniphila than those with high METTL3 expression (n=25) (p = 0.006). This finding corroborates the regulatory role of METTL3 in modulating A. muciniphila levels during CRC development. Importantly, this inverse relationship was maintained in both early-stage (I-II) and advanced-stage (III-IV) tumors. (6) Diagnostic and prognostic evaluation of METTL3 and A. muciniphila in CRC. METTL3 was significantly upregulated in CRC at both the mRNA and protein levels. Quantitative PCR revealed elevated METTL3 mRNA of tumors compared to paired normal tissue (P = 0.003), which was further confirmed by western blot analysis showing protein overexpression (P = 0.003). In a tissue microarray cohort of 197 CRC cases, high METTL3 protein expression correlated with poorer overall survival and was identified as an independent prognostic factor in multivariate analysis (P = 0.037), after adjusting for age, sex, tumor site, size, and TNM stage. Notably, METTL3 levels did not vary significantly across TNM stages but were already elevated in adenomas, suggesting that its dysregulation is an early event in colorectal tumorigenesis. These findings position METTL3 as a potential diagnostic and prognostic biomarker in CRC. In contrast, the abundance of A. muciniphila in stool samples from CRC patients did not show significant differences between healthy subjects and adenoma patients, or between adenoma and CRC patients, across two independent cohorts. Moreover, stratifying patients by high or low stool A. muciniphila abundance did not distinguish prognostic outcomes. This suggests that A. muciniphila abundance within the tumor microenvironment, rather than in stool, may represent a more relevant biomarker. Additionally, emerging evidence indicates that A. muciniphila abundance may correlate with patient response to immunotherapy, warranting further investigation to validate its potential clinical utility. (7) Achievement of Objectives. All proposed experiments for this project have been completed. The results are currently being compiled into a manuscript for publication.

14107321.label: Major findings and research outcome
14107321.value: (1) In this project, we demonstrate that the RNA m6A methyltransferase METTL3 promotes colorectal tumorigenesis. In mice, METTL3 overexpression increased tumor burden and depleted the beneficial gut bacterium A. muciniphila via an m6A-ETS1-phosphatidylcholine axis, while knockout had protective effects. Restoration of A. muciniphila mitigated METTL3-driven tumor growth, partly by enhancing anti-tumor CD8⁺ T cell immunity. In human CRC, METTL3 was upregulated, correlated with poor prognosis, and showed an inverse relationship with intratumoral A. muciniphila. These findings identify a METTL3-driven host-microbe axis as a key regulator of CRC progression. (2) The findings from this project have been extensively disseminated at a range of high-profile academic gatherings, including the Cross-Strait Digestive Disease Conference (2022, 2023), the International Digestive Disease Forum (2022), and UEG Week (2025). The work has also been featured through invited lectures, such as the AIC Distinguished Lectures (2025) and a seminar for Prof. Immo Prinz's group at the University Medical Center Hamburg-Eppendorf (2025). (3) METTL3 inhibits antitumor immunity by targeting m6A-BHLHE41-CXCL1/CXCR2 axis to promote colorectal cancer. (Gastroenterology. 2022 Oct;163(4):891-907. [IF= 25.1]) We demonstrate for the first time that METTL3 promotes the m6A-BHLHE41-CXCL1/CXCR2 axis, which recruits immunosuppressive myeloid-derived suppressor cells to inhibit CD8+ T cells, thereby promoting CRC. This was established through allograft and xenograft mouse tumor models, humanized mouse models, and transgenic mouse models, along with the use of RIP-seq, RNA-seq, and Ribo-seq platforms. We found that inhibiting METTL3 in combination with anti-PD1 treatment showed promising antitumor efficacy against both “hot” and “cold” CRC, highlighting METTL3 as a potential therapeutic target for CRC treatment. (4) Crosstalk between gut microbiota and RNA N6-methyladenosine modification in cancer (FEMS Microbiol Rev. 2023 Jul 5;47(4): fuad036. [IF= 12.3]) This review synthesizes evidence on how gut microbiota and m6A dysregulation, both established cancer players, may interact to drive oncogenesis. (5) RNA Modifications as a Therapeutic Target in Gastrointestinal Cancer: Exploring Emerging Opportunities (In: Interdisciplinary Cancer Research. Springer, Cham. https://doi.org/10.1007/16833_2024_298) This chapter details how the epitranscriptome controls oncogenesis. We also discuss the compelling potential of targeting these pathways for innovative therapeutic interventions. (6) Dr. Huarong Chen’s contributions have been recognized with an Emerging Leader in the field of Oncology award from Oncogene (2023), selection as a Top Reviewer for the same journal (2024), and a UEGW Basic Science Travel Grant (2025).

14107321.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14107321.value: Our research reveals a novel mechanism for CRC progression: the RNA m6A methyltransferase METTL3 depletes the beneficial gut bacterium A. muciniphila and suppresses anti-tumor immunity. We present a dual-path strategy to advance this discovery from insight to application. (1) Short-term: to publish a high-impact manuscript and present our findings at a premier international conference. (2) Medium/Long-term: Biomarker Development: to validate a combined METTL3 and A. muciniphila signature as a diagnostic and prognostic biomarker in multi-center cohorts. Therapeutic Targeting: to evaluate METTL3 inhibition and A. muciniphila supplementation to overcome immunotherapy resistance in preclinical CRC models.

14107321.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14107321.value: Our project uncovers a surprising connection between human protein, gut bacteria, and CRC. We found that high levels of RNA m6A methyltransferase METTL3 in the colon drive tumor growth. One of the keyways it does this is by altering the gut microbiome, specifically by reducing the levels of a beneficial bacteria called A. muciniphila. When we restored this bacterium in mice with high METTL3, it slowed cancer growth and boosted the body's immune defenses. In human patients, we saw the same relationship: tumors with high METTL3 had low levels of A. muciniphila, and patients with high METTL3 had worse outcomes. Crucially, measuring A. muciniphila in stool was not useful for diagnosis and prognosis. However, METTL3 itself is a promising new biomarker for detecting and predicting the course of CRC. This work reveals a new pathway where a human protein promotes cancer by disrupting the gut's microbial community.

14107821.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14107821.value: Adolescence is a vulnerable period for the emergence of insomnia, which affects more than 10% of the youths (approximately 40% if based on symptoms). Insomnia in youths tends to run a protracted course and is associated with numerous negative outcomes including poor quality of life, cognitive and academic impairment, and predisposing to development of depression and anxiety. The burden arising from insomnia has been increasingly recognized worldwide as a debilitating and costly public health concern. However, insomnia in youths is often ignored and under-treated, with only 10% of the local youths recognized their insomnia problem and none of them has received the recommended first-line treatment - cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia (CBT-I). Given the high prevalence, chronicity and long-lasting health-related consequences of insomnia, together with the delay and limited help-seeking behavior, it calls for the urgent need of early insomnia prevention in this vulnerable population. Thus, our team has initiated the first insomnia prevention trial by using brief cognitive behavioral approach targeting at-risk adolescents a few years ago. The study provided initial novel evidence that the cognitive behavioral preventive program is efficacious and feasible in reducing the risk of future development of insomnia. Adolescents who received prevention intervention reported lower incidence of insomnia disorder, fewer insomnia symptoms, less dysfunctional beliefs and cognition, improved daytime functioning and better sleep hygiene practice as compared to the non-active control. Although this initial study produced encouraging results, it was somehow limited by the lack of active control group to confirm the efficacy of the insomnia prevention program. The absence of active comparison might potentially undermine the inference of the study. It remains unclear whether the improvement was due to active component of the intervention or related to placebo or hawthorne effect (research participation effect) at which the two groups might have very different expectations for the outcomes. Based on our previous insomnia preventive trial, we aim to conduct a randomized controlled trial in comparing cognitive behavioral insomnia prevention program with the active control group in youths who are at risk of insomnia. The youth will be at 14-25 years old which will represent the most vulnerable period from middle adolescence to early adulthood for the emergence of insomnia. The results of this study will allow us to take this potential efficacious prevention program to scale and reduce the associated burden of insomnia in the future. 青少年踏入青春期後會有較大機會受到失眠問題的困擾。過往研究指出香港多於10%青少年（若以病徵計算，估計達四成青少年）存在失眠問題。青少年失眠問題有機會演變成慢性睡眠疾病，同時帶來負面影響，例如降低生活質素、影響認知能力和學業成績、甚至增加患上抑鬱症和焦慮症的風險。失眠問題帶來的財政負擔已逐漸被全球關注，並被視為嚴峻的公共衛生問題。然而，青少年失眠問題卻常常被輕視，在臨床上所提供的治療並不足夠。 例如，香港只有一成青少年意識到他們的失眠問題，當中沒有人接受過治療失眠的首選方案 「失眠認知行為療法 (CBT-I) 」。鑑於失眠的高患病率、長期性和對身體健康的長遠負面影響，再加上延遲治療和非常有限的求助行為， 「 預防失眠 」這個課題在青少年階段成為一個非常迫切的議題。 有見及此，團隊在數年前在高危青少年中開始探討簡短CBT-I對預防失眠的效果。該次試驗提供了初步新證據，表明CBT-I能有效降低青少年未來失眠的風險。與觀察對照組相比，實驗組青少年的失眠症患病率及症狀較低，存在較少的有關失眠的不合理信念和認知，日間功能及睡眠衛生習慣亦有所改善。儘管是次研究帶來了令人鼓舞的結果，其所採用的觀察對照組是研究設計的其中一個限制，此限制有機會削弱或影響是次研究的推論。因此，採用形式和時間相若的j健康課程對照組能夠進一步確認該失眠預防計劃的有效性。目前我們還未弄清，實驗組青少年所得到的改善是由認知行為治療引起，還是存在安慰劑效應，這些包括與治療師的接觸或參與者之間的支持，這些因素可能會帶來兩種截然不同的預期結果。 基於我們之前的失眠預防的有效證據，此研究目標是進行一項隨機對照試驗，將高危的青少年隨機分配到1) 認知行為治療失眠預防課程和2)形式和時間相若的對照組進行比較。計劃對象將會是14-25歲的青少年，這段時間是他們從青春期中期到成年階段較容易出現失眠的時期。 今次的研究結果將有助我們擴大這個潛在有效的預防計劃的規模，以減少將來失眠帶來的負擔。

14107921.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14107921.value: 背景 類風濕性關節炎 (RA) 是一種慢性疾病，其中一個特徵是滑膜持續發炎。滑膜持續發炎有機會導致關節破損，影響患者的活動能力。健康評估問卷(HAQ-DI)能反映患者的活動能力，HAQ-DI分數愈高，代表活動能力愈差。一般來說，發病時間愈長，HAQ-DI得分則愈高。常規X光是評估關節侵蝕的常用方法，可是其靈敏度較低。高解析度外周定量電腦斷層掃描 (HR-pQCT) 是一種評估關節侵蝕的新技術，其靈敏度較高。我們曾發表一個前瞻性研究，指出關節侵蝕的惡化速度或基線關節損傷程度有機會預測患者日後的活動能力。若更進一步追蹤這些患者，長期跟進他們的關節損傷程度，可以提供數據，使我們知道基線侵蝕程度或關節惡化/修復率會否與活動能力受損/恢復相關。此外，現時沒有明確數據指出關節侵蝕程度與活動能力損傷的關係是否受侵蝕位置(例如手腕與手指第二掌骨關節 [MCH2])影響。 項目描述 假設 MCH2 的侵蝕程度（基線和侵蝕惡化速度）與活動能力的減低（或恢復）率相關; 而 MCH2 和腕關節的侵蝕程度會導致 RA 患者的活動能力受損。 本研究的目的是 1) 使用來自兩個前瞻性 RA 隊列的長期隨訪數據，確定 MCH2 的基線或侵蝕程度的變化是否與功能的受損（或恢復）率相關，以及 2 ) 評估腕關節和 MCH2侵蝕程度對 RA 患者活動能力的影響。 我們將邀請所有曾進行過 HR-pQCT MCH2掃描的 RA 患者參與此後續研究。在2010 年至 2017 年間，我們招募了 247 名確診 RA 患者，而在2012 年至 2018 年間，我們招募了 148 名早期 RA 患者。在這 395 名患者中，371 名仍在本醫院跟進中。所有受試者將進行 1) 腕關節 及MCH2 HR-pQCT 評估，2) 活動能力評估，包括手握力檢查、HAQ-DI評分和關節炎影響健康評估問卷 (CAIMS)， 3) 臨床評估和抽血檢查 以及 4) 手和腳的 X 光片。 研究價值： 這項研究可能提供重要信息，確立HR-pQCT MCH2和腕關節檢查可用於評估RA患者的活動能力受損。

14107921.label: Major findings and research outcome
14107921.value: Data from 241 rheumatoid arthritis (RA) patients who underwent clinical and HR-pQCT assessment were available for MCH2 analysis (Supplementary figure 1). At baseline, RA patients had a symptom duration of 2.7 (0.8, 8.9) years, a disease duration of 1.7 (0.1, 7.1) years with moderate disease activity. After a follow-up interval of 8.3 (5.9, 10.9) years, disease activity significantly improved, with the majority of patients achieved simplified disease activity score (SDAI) low disease activity (40.2%) and remission (31.1%), accompanied by a significantly improved HAQ-DI scores. Primary outcome and secondary outcome 1. Over the 8-year period, erosion prevalence remained stable (78% vs. 83%, p = 0.168) (Table 2). New erosions at the MCH2 were detected in 43/241 (17.8%) patients. Meanwhile, the total number of erosions per person (p=0.01) and the total erosion volume per person (P=0.049) were significantly increased (Table 2). However, there was no correlation between baseline MCH2 erosion volume or changes in MCH2 erosion volume and changes in HAQ-DI. Secondary outcome 2. At the last visit, no relationship was observed between MCH2 erosion volume and HAQ-DI, low grip strength, or the dexterity component of the CAIMS. (Supplementary figure 2). Data from 232 patients with HR-pQCT assessment were available for wrist joint analysis (Supplementary figure 1). Erosions were present in 203 (88%) patients. The highest prevalence of erosions was observed in the lunate (186 patients, 80%), followed by the scaphoid (122 patients, 53%) and the radius (98 patients, 42%) (Table 2). Multivariate analysis revealed that the presence (at the radius and scaphoid), total number (at the lunate, scaphoid and the total number at the wrist joint), and the total volume (at the radius, lunate and total volume at the wrist joint) of erosions significantly correlated with HAQ-DI (ρ ranged from 0.14 to 0.22). The presence of erosion in the wrist bones was associated with low grip strength, while the total number of erosions (in the lunate and wrist bones) and the total volume of erosion in the lunate were significantly associated with impaired hand and finger function component of the CAIMS. Secondary outcome 3 The SvdH scores at all sites (metacarpophalangeal joints [MCPJ], wrist joint, and overall), as well as their components (erosion, joint space narrowing [JSN], and total score), showed a significant increased over the 8-year period. Multivariate general estimating equations analysis demonstrated a significant association between MCPJ JSN score, wrist erosion score and HAQ-DI.

14107921.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14107921.value: This study highlights the potential for further exploration into the relationship between joint erosions and physical disability in RA. While no significant association was found between HR-pQCT MCH2 erosion parameters and functional outcomes, wrist joint erosions were strongly linked to functional impairment. These findings suggest that wrist joint erosions may play a pivotal role in long-term physical disability in RA patients. To advance this research, future studies should focus on validating these findings in larger, more diverse cohorts and over longer periods to better understand the progression of functional disability in RA. Additionally, integrating advanced imaging techniques such as HR-pQCT with biomarkers of joint damage and inflammation could help identify early predictors of disability. Targeted interventions aimed at preventing or minimizing wrist joint erosions should also be investigated to reduce the burden of disability in RA. Proposed actions include the development of predictive models incorporating imaging and clinical data, the design of clinical trials to assess the efficacy of early and aggressive treatment strategies targeting wrist joint erosions, and the refinement of functional assessment tools to capture subtle changes in hand function. These efforts could significantly improve patient outcomes and quality of life.

14107921.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14107921.value: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a condition that can cause joint damage and affect physical function. This study aimed to understand whether damage at the second knuckle joint (MCH2) or wrist bones is linked to physical disability and changes in hand function over time. Researchers followed 241 participants with RA over 8 years. At the start and end of the study, participants underwent tests to measure joint damage using advanced imaging techniques at the MCH2, x-rays, and assessments of physical disability. In addition, advanced imaging technique of the wrist bones and hand function were assessed at the last visit. The study found no link between damage at the MCH2 joint and changes in physical function over the 8-year period. However, damage in the wrist bones was associated with weaker grip strength and poorer hand and finger function at the end of the study. Further analysis showed that wrist bone damage was independently linked to the presence of disability. In conclusion, while damage at the MCH2 joint did not predict functional changes, wrist bone damage was an important factor associated with disability in RA patients. Future studies are needed to confirm how wrist bone damage affects long-term function in people with RA.

14108021.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14108021.value: The prevalence of motion sickness (MS) in the general population is believed to be 1%–60%, although on long and intense enough journeys, almost everyone would be susceptible. The current drugs used to treat MS are poorly effective and associated with unpleasant and/or dangerous adverse effects. A clear need exists to develop more effective anti-MS drugs. Given that people with a history of MS also have a higher risk of developing nausea and emesis due to chemotherapy, surgery under anaesthesia and pregnancy, a new and safer anti-MS drug would have wide clinical utility. The most widely accepted mechanism of MS is described by the ‘sensory-mismatch theory’, which proposes that the response is generated by sensory conflict and neural mismatch between converging patterns of vestibular, visual and proprioceptive input. In line with this theory, we used a mouse model to show that MS may involve alpha-9 nicotinic acetylcholine receptors (α9 nAChRs) in the inner ear. Using Suncus murinus (SM), a laboratory animal commonly used in anti-emetic research, we identified that a low dose of an alpha-9 alpha-10 nicotinic acetylcholine receptor (α9α10 nAChR) antagonist, VC1.1, reduced motion-induced emesis. The anti-emetic action can be considered superior to that of the standard anti-MS drugs because it was not accompanied by sedation or negative effects on locomotor activity. However, VC1.1 also activates gamma-aminobutyric acid B (GABAB) receptors, so the precise anti-MS mechanism of action is unknown. We have developed novel recording techniques in SM to permit an assessment of drugs to prevent emesis and the physiological changes indicative of ‘nausea’ when used in conjunction with a c-fos immunohistochemical analysis of brain function. The proposed studies would re-evaluate the anti-MS potential of VC1.1 in comparison with the GABAB receptor agonist baclofen, and the highly selective α9α10 nAChR antagonist, RgIA4. The gold-standard anti-MS drug, diphenhydramine, will be used as a positive control. We expect to discover that selective α9α10 nAChR antagonists represent a novel class of anti-emetic agent to treat MS. These studies would form the basis of a drug discovery programme to develop compounds that target the inner ear to treat nausea and emesis in situations in which the pathways involved in MS may have been perturbed. Because the inner ear lies outside the blood–brain barrier, we anticipate that the adverse-effect profile of peripherally acting α9α10 nAChR antagonists would be superior to that of the standard drugs currently available for the treatment of MS. 暈動病 (Motion Sickness, MS) 在一般人群中的患病率據约為 1%–60%, 然而在足夠長且強度足夠的旅程中，幾乎每個人都會易感。目前用於治療 MS 的藥物效果不佳，並伴有令人不快和/或危險的副作用，因此需要開發更有效的抗 MS 藥物。鑑於有 MS 病史的人因化療、麻醉下手術和懷孕而出現噁心和嘔吐的風險也更高，因此一種新的更安全的抗 MS 藥物將具有廣泛的臨床應用價值。 感覺錯配理論是最為廣泛接受的 MS 機制, 此理論提出MS是由前庭、視覺和本體感覺輸入的收斂模式之間的感覺衝突和神經失配產生的。根據這一理論，我們使用小鼠模型來證明 MS 可能涉及內耳中的 α-9 菸鹼型乙酰膽鹼受體 (α9 nAChR)。使用常用於止吐研究的實驗室動物 Suncus murinus ，我們發現低劑量的 α-9 α-10 菸鹼乙酰膽鹼受體 (α9α10 nAChR) 拮抗劑 VC1.1 可減少運動誘發的嘔吐。因為VC1.1不伴有鎮靜或對運動活動的負面影響, 因此它的止吐作用可能優於標準抗 MS 藥物。然而，VC1.1 也會激活 γ-氨基丁酸 B (GABAB) 受體，因此確切的抗 MS 作用機制尚不清楚。 我們在 SM 中開發了新的記錄技術，當與腦功能的 c-fos 免疫組化分析結合使用時，可以評估藥物以防止嘔吐和指示噁心的生理變化。本研究將重新評估 VC1.1 與 GABAB 受體激動劑巴氯芬和高選擇性 α9α10 nAChR 拮抗劑 RgIA4 相比的抗 MS 潛力。金標準抗 MS 藥物苯海拉明將用作陽性對照。我們期望選擇性 α9α10 nAChR 拮抗劑能夠作為一類用於治療 MS 的新型止吐劑。這些研究將構成藥物發現計劃的基礎，以開發靶向內耳的化合物，以治療 MS 相關通路可能受到干擾的情況下的噁心和嘔吐。因為內耳位於血腦屏障之外，我們預計外周作用的 α9α10 nAChR 拮抗劑的副作用會優於目前可用於治療 MS 的標準藥物。

14108921.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14108921.value: Anaplastic thyroid cancer (ATC), an undifferentiated form of cancer, is with very poor prognosis due to the rapid progression of the disease and very limited therapeutic tools available. ATC usually loses the normal thyroid ability, thyroid differentiation markers and therapeutic molecules, which makes this malignancy resistant to current anti-tumor treatments. Therefore, uncovering the mechanism leading to the undifferentiated status of thyrocytes is crucial for not only the understanding the thyroid-tumorigenesis but also the development of new treatments aiming to reverse the undifferentiated status. Using various experimental tools including proteomic analysis, ChIPBase, ChiP-Seq, gene ontology analysis, immunoprecipitation coupled with LC-MS/MS and STRING, we have produced a rich data to support our proposal. We found the overexpression of hematological and neurological expressed 1(HN1) in ATC. Importantly we demonstrated that the knockdown of HN1 could significantly recover the expression of the thyroid-related differentiation molecules including sodium iodide symporter (NIS). Mechanically, HN1 is likely to bind to TRIM28 and epigenetically inhibit CTCF, the master transcription factor for the negative regulation of the thyroid-related differentiation molecules. Based on the above data, we hypothesize that the upregulation of HN1 inhibits CTCF to block the transcription of the thyroid-related differentiation molecules, which prevents the differentiation of thyrocytes and promotes the development and progression of ATC. To test the hypothesis, we proposed to perform a series of experiments to test below 4 aims. 1) to verify the positive role of HN1 in the promotion/ maintenance of tumor cell undifferentiated status in ATC by examining a large number of ATC samples, and analyzing the expression and functions of differentiation molecules in cancer cells (ATC and PTC) and normal thyrocytes. 2) to explore how HN1 inhibits CTCF in ATC. 3) to determine the impact of HN1 inhibition on the growth of ATC in vivo and on the efficacy of 131I or/and paclitaxel against ATC. We hope that the results generated by this translational study lead to develop a new therapeutic strategy against ATC by aiming to reverse the undifferentiated thyrocytes to differentiated ones. 甲狀腺未分化癌 (ATC) 是一種未分化的癌症，由於疾病進展迅速且可用的治療工具非常有限，因此預後非常差。 ATC通常會失去正常的甲狀腺能力、甲狀腺分化標誌物和治療反應分子，這使得這種惡性腫瘤對目前的抗腫瘤治療產生抗藥性。因此，揭示導致甲狀腺細胞未分化狀態的機制不僅對於理解甲狀腺腫瘤發生而且開發旨在逆轉未分化狀態的新療法至關重要。使用各種實驗工具，包括蛋白質組學分析、ChIPBase、ChiP-Seq、基因本體分析、免疫沉澱結合 LC-MS/MS 和 STRING，我們已經產生了豐富的數據來支持本研究。我們發現 ATC 過度表達血液學和神經學表達 1(HN1)。重要的是，我們證明了 抑制HN1可以顯著恢復包括碘化鈉同向轉運蛋白 (NIS) 在內的甲狀腺相關分化分子的表達。從機制上講，HN1 可能與 TRIM28 結合併在表觀遺傳上抑制 CTCF，CTCF 是負調節甲狀腺相關分化分子的主要轉錄因子。基於以上數據，我們假設 HN1 的上調抑制 CTCF 阻斷甲狀腺相關分化分子的轉錄，從而阻止甲狀腺細胞分化並促進 ATC 的發生和進展。為了驗證此假設，我們將進行一系列實驗來測試以下 3 個目標。 1）通過檢測大量ATC樣本，分析癌細胞（ATC和PTC）和正常甲狀腺細胞中分化分子的表達和功能，驗證HN1在ATC中促進/維持腫瘤細胞未分化狀態的積極作用. 2) 探索 HN1 如何抑制 ATC 中的 CTCF。 3) 確定 HN1 抑制對體內 ATC 生長的影響以及對 131I 或/和紫杉醇對抗 ATC 的功效的影響。我們希望這項轉化研究產生的結果能夠通過將未分化的甲狀腺細胞逆轉為分化的甲狀腺細胞，從而開發出一種針對 ATC 的新治療方案。

14109421.label: Realisation of objectives
14109421.value: Key finding 1: Mg enhanced distraction osteogenesis – Addressing Objective 1 Mg accelerated critical size bone defect repair by reducing 25% of the consolidation time as demonstrated by the X-rays and microcomputed tomography (micro-CT) results. A femoral segmental mid-shaft critical size bone defect rat model was developed to test the efficiency of Mg nail. Animals were divided into two groups: control group (distraction without implantation) and Mg group (in which pure Mg nail was implanted into the femoral marrow cavity, blue arrow). After a 5-day latency phase, bone lengthening was initiated at a rate of 0.25 mm/12 h for 10 days. At 8 weeks after distraction, X-ray images showed that the defect gap of the Mg group was filled with more mineralized bone with lamellar-like structure than the control group. Meanwhile, the defect gap of the Mg group at 6 weeks showed more bone formed than that of the control group at 8 weeks, indicating that Mg shortened 25% of consolidation time. 3D reconstructed CT images of the defect gap of the Mg group showed more bone tissue than that of the control group at 2 weeks. Mg group significantly increased newly formed bone volume (+392%) and tissue volume (+62%) compared with that of the control group at 2 weeks as demonstrated by the micro-CT results (P < 0.05). Mg facilitated bone formation and remodeling during DO process as indicated by the histology results Consistent with X-ray and micro-CT results, the control group showed predominant fibrous tissue formation and sparse bone tissue in the bone defect region, while more newly formed trabecular bone tissue was observed in the Mg group at 2 weeks after distraction. Meanwhile, the polarized light images showed that collagen fibers aligned better in the Mg group than that in the control group, indicating that Mg enhanced woven bone formation in the defect area. At 8 weeks after distraction, the Mg group showed more mature lamellar bone and connected bone marrow cavity in the middle of the regenerate zone. On the other hand, an inter fibrous tissue gap was observed in the regenerate zone of the control group. Polarized light images revealed more regularly arranged collagen fiber alignment of mature bone in the Mg group compared with the control group, indicating advanced remodeling with better lamellar alignment in the Mg group. Furthermore, calcein/xylenol fluorescence microscopic evaluation suggested increased new bone formation and advanced bone remodeling in the Mg group, as compared with the control group. At 8 weeks, the Mg group showed a significantly higher ratio of xylenol/calcein than that of the control group, indicating the increased mature lamellar bone remodeling rate. Moreover, the MAR of the Mg group was significantly higher than that of the control group in the mineralizing zone of defect region at 8 weeks (P < 0.05). The quality of the newly formed bone was further investigated by four-point bending tests. The Mg group showed 87% higher maximum load (P < 0.01) and 130% higher maximum strength (P < 0.05) compared with the control group at 8 weeks after distraction. These results demonstrated that the implantation of Mg nail was effective in accelerating critical size bone defect repair during DO process. Key finding 2: Sensory nerve played a crucial role in Mg-accelerated DO process –Addressing objective 2 The expression of sensory neuropeptide CGRP was increased in the defect gap of Mg group compared with the control group as displayed by the immunohistochemistry (IHC) results. At 2 weeks after distraction, in the Mg group, both periosteal region and vessel-like tissues expressed significantly higher CGRP (Red arrow) and Tubulin (Black arrow), which is an important sensory neuropeptide involved in bone defect healing, as compared with the control group. These results revealed that the increased CGRP expression might be involved in the Mg-accelerated bone defect repair during DO process. Quantitative Micro-CT results showed that the Mg group had significantly higher BV/TV and BMD compared with the control, capsaicin, and capsaicin + Mg group at 8 weeks after distraction. No significant difference in BV/TV and BMD of Mg was detected among the control, capsaicin, and capsaicin + Mg group, indicating that the Mg-enhanced bone defect repair was inhibited when sensory nerve was blocked. Mg-enhanced angiogenesis through local upregulation of CGRP CGRP-induced angiogenesis was the major mechanism responsible for Mg-enhanced angiogenesis as indicated by the micro-CT-based angiography results. The representative images revealed that more vascular structure was found in Mg group, in the defect gap at 2 weeks after distraction, as compared with the control group, BIBN + Mg group (in which CGRP receptor antagonist was injected into the defect gap for 20 days), Y15 + Mg group (in which FAK inhibitor was injected into the defect gap for 20 days), and SU5416 + Mg group (in which VEGFR-2 inhibitor was injected into the defect gap for 20 days). Quantitative Micro-CT-based angiography results showed that the newly formed vessel volume (P < 0.01) in the Mg group was significantly greater than that of other groups in the defect gap at 2 weeks after distraction. No significant difference in vessel volume was found in the Control, CGRP receptor antagonist + Mg, FAK inhibitor + Mg, and VEGFR-2 inhibitor + Mg groups, indicating the indispensable role of CGRP, FAK, and VEGFR-2 in the Mg-enhanced angiogenesis during DO process. Key finding 3: CGRP-FAK-VEGF signaling axis may be responsible for Mg-enhanced critical size bone defect repair during DO –Addressing objective 3 At 8 weeks, in consistency with X-ray data, the 3D images of newly formed bone in the defect gap in the Mg group showed more mineralized tissue than that of the inhibitor/antagonist + Mg groups at 2 and 8 weeks after distraction. Quantitative data from Micro-CT data demonstrated significantly higher BV/TV and BMD in the Mg group compared with the inhibitor/antagonist groups at 2 and 8 weeks after distraction. At 2 weeks, BV and TV was significantly higher in the Mg group compared with the inhibitor/antagonist groups. No significant difference in BV/TV and BMD was found in the Control, CGRP receptor antagonist + Mg, FAK inhibitor + Mg, and VEGFR-2 inhibitor + Mg groups at each time point, indicating that the Mg-enhanced critical size bone defect repair could be blocked by the CGRP receptor antagonist, FAK inhibitor, and VEGFR-2 inhibitor. CGRP-FAK-VEGF signaling could be the major mechanism underlying the Mg-accelerated critical size bone defect repair during DO process as indicated by the IHC results. Mg nail led to significantly higher expression of CGRP in Mg and inhibitor/antagonist + Mg groups as compared with the Control group. Furthermore, the Mg group showed significantly higher expression of CD31 in the newly formed vessel-like tissue in the defect region than the inhibitor/antagonist + Mg groups, which further confirmed the indispensable role of the CGRP, FAK, and VEGFR-2 in the Mg-increased angiogenesis. Mg group showed higher expression of VEGFA in the newly formed tissue in the defect region than the CGRP receptor antagonist + Mg, FAK inhibitor + Mg groups, and VEGFR-2 inhibitor + Mg group. Together, the above results indicated that the CGRP-FAK-VEGF signaling axis may be the main molecular mechanism underlying Mg-enhanced critical size bong defect repair during DO process.

14109421.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14109421.value: We demonstrated that magnesium (Mg) nail implantation into the marrow cavity degraded gradually accompanied with about 4-fold increase of new bone formation and over 5-fold of new vessel formation as compared with distraction osteogenesis (DO) alone group in the 5 mm femoral segmental defect rat model at 2 weeks after distraction. Mg nail upregulated the expression of calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) in the new bone as compared with the DO alone group. We further revealed that blockade of the sensory nerve by overdose capsaicin blunted Mg nail enhanced critical size bone defect repair during the DO process. CGRP concentration-dependently promoted endothelial cell migration and tube formation. Meanwhile, CGRP promoted the phosphorylation of focal adhesion kinase (FAK) at Y397 site and elevated the expression of vascular endothelial growth factor A (VEGFA). Moreover, inhibitor/antagonist of CGRP receptor, FAK, and VEGF receptor blocked the Mg nail stimulated vessel and bone formation. We revealed, for the first time, a CGRP-FAK-VEGF signaling axis linking sensory nerve and endothelial cells, which may be the main mechanism underlying Mg-enhanced critical size bone defect repair when combined with DO, suggesting a great potential of Mg implants in reducing DO treatment time for clinical applications.
