14109721.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14109721.value: 骨骼肌衛星細胞功能障礙使得其再生能力降低，從而促使肌肉萎縮。然而，由於缺乏衛星細胞選擇性，目前針對衛星細胞的藥物治療策略療效低下並易產生脫靶副作用。因此，急需可靠的靶向衛星細胞的靶頭以促進衛星細胞靶向藥物遞送策略。核酸適配體可以高親和力和特異性結合靶標，適合成爲藥物遞送系統的靶頭。利用基於細胞的指數富集適配體系統進化技術（cell-SELEX），我們確定了一個衛星細胞靶向適配體（SCApt），它對衛星細胞具有高親和力，而對肝細胞和外周血單核細胞的親和力低。 SCApt主要分佈在骨骼肌中，並在成年小鼠全身給藥後維持高濃度水平。在骨骼肌中，SCApt 主要分佈在衛星細胞中。隨年齡增長，肌肉内JAK/STAT 信號通路激活並抑制衛星細胞功能。局部肌內注射脂質納米顆粒（LNPs）包裹的JAK2 siRNA 可以促進老年小鼠局部肌肉的衛星細胞功能和肌肉再生，表明 JAK2 siRNA 可以作為模型藥物來評估 SCApt 是否可以促進衛星細胞靶向藥物遞送。我們將包裹了JAK2 siRNA的LNPs與SCApt偶聯（SCApt-LNPs-siRNA）。SCApt 可以促進體外衛星細胞JAK2 siRNA 的基因抑制效率和細胞內化。SCApt可以通過體外巨胞飲作用促進siRNA的細胞內吞。此外，與偶聯對照適配體的siRNA遞送系統相比，SCApt-LNPs-siRNA在骨骼肌中的分佈更多，在肝臟和腎臟中的清除速度更快。在骨骼肌中，SCApt-LNPs-siRNA主要分佈在SCs中。在 SCApt-LNPs-siRNA 注射之前給予小鼠游離SCApt可以抑制siRNA在組織和細胞水平的衛星細胞特異性分佈。同時，我們也已確定SCApt-LNPs-siRNA在小鼠的給藥方案。全身給藥 SCApt-LNPs-siRNA 可以抑制JAK2的表達水平，促進成年小鼠肌肉損傷後的衛星細胞增殖和肌肉再生能力。根據以上前期研究可得出以下假設：SCApt可以促進包裹了JAK2 siRNA的納米脂質顆粒針對骨骼肌衛星細胞的靶向遞送，並提高老年小鼠肌肉再生能力。為了檢驗假設，本課題將完成四個目標。 1) 研究 SCApt-LNPs-siRNA在有或無游離 SCApt 預處理的情況下，在老年小鼠組織水平（骨骼肌與非骨骼肌組織）和細胞水平（衛星細胞與其他細胞）的分佈。 2) 研究 SCApt-LNPs-siRNA在有或無游離 SCApt 預處理的情況下，對老年小鼠組織水平（骨骼肌與非骨骼肌組織）和細胞水平的 JAK/STAT 信號傳導的影響。 3) 研究 SCApt-LNPs-siRNA在有或無游離 SCApt 預處理的情況下，對老年小鼠肌肉損傷後肌肉再生能力的影響。 4) 研究SCApt-LNPs-siRNA對老年小鼠肝腎功能的影響。此課題將有助於確立SCApt為有應用前景的肌肉衛星細胞靶向遞送靶頭，並促進開發新型的以肌肉衛星細胞為靶標的治療策略。

14109721.label: Realisation of objectives
14109721.value: This project successfully achieved all four of specific aims, confirming the central hypothesis that the skeletal muscle satellite cell (SC)-targeted aptamer (SCApt) can facilitate the delivery of encapsulated JAK2 siRNA to SCs, thereby improving muscle regenerative capacity in aged mice. Specific Aim 1: To investigate the distribution of SCApt-LNPs-siRNA Eighty 18-month-old male C57BL/6 mice were randomly divided into the following four groups (n=20 for each group): LNPs-siRNA group, scrambled aptamer (sApt)-LNPssiRNA group, SCApt-LNPs-siRNA group and SCApt-LNPs-siRNA with SCApt pretreatment group. JAK2 siRNA was labelled with Cy3. The mice were intravenously administered once via tail vein with LNPs-siRNA, sApt-LNPs-siRNA and SCApt-LNPs-siRNA, respectively, at a siRNA dose of of 1.0 mg/kg. In SCApt pretreatment group. SCApt (1.0 mg/kg) was intravenously administered via tail vein 1 day before SCApt-LNPs-siRNA injection. Ten mice in each group were sacrificed 4 hours post-injection of siRNA. The rest of mice were sacrificed 12 hours post-injection of siRNA. After sacrificed, the gastrocnemius (GA) muscle, heart, lung, liver, spleen and kidney were collected and assessed by biophotonic imaging technology to examine the tissue distribution. The tibialis anterior (TA) muscles were cryosectioned and underwent immunostaining for Pax7, a satellite cell-specific marker. The cellular distribution of Cy3-siRNA was evaluated between satellite cells and muscle cells. In vivo biophotonic imaging in aged mice demonstrated that Cy3-labeled SCApt-LNPs-siRNA exhibited significantly higher fluorescence intensity in skeletal muscle (gastrocnemius and tibialis anterior) and significantly lower signals in non-muscle tissues (liver, kidney, heart, lung, spleen) compared to the scrambled aptamer control (sApt-LNPs-siRNA) at 4 and 12 hours post-injection. Immunohistochemical analysis of muscle sections confirmed that the SCApt-LNPs-siRNA specifically co-localized with Pax7+ satellite cells, while control formulations showed minimal SC association. The SCApt pretreatment could abolish the skeletal muscle-specific and skeletal muscle SC-specific distribution of the SCApt-LNPs-siRNA at tissue and cellular levels, respectively. These findings suggest that SCApt could target satellite cells and facilitate the skeletal muscle-specific drug delivery. Specific Aim 2: To investigate the effect on JAK/STAT signaling. Forty 18-month-old male C57BL/6 mice were recruited and assigned into groups as indicated in Aim 1. The mice were sacrificed 1 day after the administration of siRNA in different forms. After sacrificed, the skeletal muscles (GA muscle and TA muscle), heart, lung, liver, spleen and kidney were collected. The SCs and muscle cells in GA muscle were separated by magnetic-activated cell sorting (MACS). The JAK/STAT signaling, including the mRNA levels of JAK2 and STAT3, the protein levels of JAK2, STAT3 and phosphorylated STAT3, in TA muscle, skeletal muscle-independent tissues, GA muscle derived SCs and muscle cells were evaluated by qPCR and western blot, respectively. Quantitative analysis (qPCR and western blot) of tissues and magnetically sorted cells from aged mice showed that a single intravenous dose of SCApt-LNPs-siRNA significantly suppressed JAK2 and STAT3 mRNA and protein levels, as well as STAT3 phosphorylation, specifically in skeletal muscle tissue and, more pronouncedly, in isolated SCs. In contrast, non-muscle tissues and non-SC muscle cells showed no significant change. The sApt-LNPs-siRNA control had minimal effect. Pretreatment with free SCApt blocked this specific silencing effect in muscle and SCs, confirming the mechanism is SCApt-dependent delivery. Specific Aim 3: To investigate the effect on muscle regenerative capacity. One hundred 18-monthold mice were randomly assigned into the following five groups (n=20 for each group): Uninjured group, LNPs-siRNA group, sApt-LNPs-siRNA group, SCApt-LNPs-siRNA group and SCApt-LNPs-siRNA with SCApt pretreatment group. All mice except uninjured group were intramuscular injected with 50 μl CTX (10 μmol) at GA and TA muscle, respectively, to induce muscle injury. One day after CTX injection, the mice were intravenously injected via tail vein with LNPs-siRNA, sApt-LNPs-siRNA and SCApt-LNPs-siRNA, respectively, at a siRNA dose of of 1.0 mg/kg. The administration of JAK2 siRNA in different forms was performed once a week for 4 weeks. The mice in SCApt pretreatment group were intravenously injected via tail vein with SCApt one day prior SCApt-LNPs-siRNA administration. Ten mice in each group were sacrificed on Day 8 post-CTX injection, the rest mice were sacrificed on Day 29 post–CTX injection. The mice were injected intraperitoneally with 5-ethynyl-2’-deoxyuridine (EdU) (50mg/kg) 4 h before the sacrifice. The function of GA muscle was evaluated by in situ muscle functional testing before sacrifice on Day 29. The GA and TA muscles were collected and weighed. The TA muscles were cryosectioned for histological and immunohistochemical staining. The mean muscle fiber cross-sectional area (CSA) was determined by H&E staining. The satellite cells were determined by immunostaining for Pax7 and MyoD. Satellite cell proliferation was assessed by EdU staining and Ki67 immunostaining. The SCs in GA muscle were isolated by MACS. The JAK/STAT signaling, including the mRNA levels of JAK2 and STAT3, the protein levels of JAK2, STAT3 and phosphorylated STAT3, in GA muscle derived SCs will be evaluated by qPCR and western blot, respectively. In aged mice subjected to CTX-induced muscle injury, systemic administration of SCApt-LNPs-siRNA (1.0 mg/kg, weekly for 4 weeks) significantly enhanced muscle regeneration compared to all control groups. Key findings included: a significant increase in SC proliferation (EdU+/Pax7+ cells) at day 8 post-injury; a larger mean CSA of myofibers at day 28; and improved in situ gastrocnemius muscle force production. These benefits were accompanied by sustained knockdown of JAK/STAT signaling within SCs. The regenerative benefits were abolished by free SCApt pretreatment, confirming they resulted from targeted delivery. Specific Aim 4: To investigate the effect on liver and kidney function. The mice in uninjured group, LNPs-siRNA group, sApt-LNPs-siRNA group and SCApt-LNPs-siRNA group in Aim 3 underwent the blood collection on the day of CTX injection (Day 0), Day 8, Day15, Day 22 and Day 29, respectively. The collected blood was used for blood chemistry analyses which include aspartate aminotransferase (AST) and alanine aminotransferase (ALT) for assessment of liver function, and creatinine and blood urea nitrogen (BUN) for evaluation of kidney function. Serial blood chemistry analysis throughout the 4-week treatment period in injured aged mice showed that repeated administration of SCApt-LNPs-siRNA did not induce significant elevations in liver function markers (ALT, AST) or kidney function markers (creatinine, BUN). Levels remained within normal ranges and were comparable to those in vehicle-treated uninjured and injured control groups. This confirms the systemic safety of the SCApt-LNPs-siRNA formulation.

14109721.label: Major findings and research outcome
14109721.value: This project successfully validated SCApt as a highly effective targeting moiety for skeletal muscle satellite cells. The major findings are: (1) SCApt-functionalized lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) selectively deliver the bioeffective agent (siRNA) to SCs in vivo in aged mice, with minimal off-target accumulation. (2) This targeted delivery system enables efficient and specific knockdown of the JAK/STAT signaling pathway within SCs. (3) By silencing JAK2 specifically in SCs, the treatment potently enhanced SC proliferation and improved structural and functional muscle regeneration following acute injury in aged mice. (4) The therapeutic regimen demonstrated an excellent safety profile with no detectable harm to liver or kidney function. Collectively, these outcomes provide conclusive proof-of-concept for SCApt as a novel tool for SC-specific therapeutics and establish a promising strategy to combat age-related muscle regeneration deficits.

14109721.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14109721.value: The research has high translational potential. The immediate next step is to test the SCApt delivery platform with other therapeutic cargoes (e.g., genes promoting self-renewal like Notch, or other inhibitory siRNAs) for treating chronic muscle wasting conditions such as Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD) and sarcopenia. Further pharmacokinetic and long-term toxicology studies in relevant disease models (e.g., mdx mice) are warranted. Concurrently, efforts will focus on scaling up GMP-compliant synthesis of the SCApt-LNP formulation and initiating investigational new drug (IND)-enabling studies. Collaboration with biotech/pharma partners will be sought to advance this cell-targeted aptamer-drug conjugate strategy towards clinical development for muscular disorders.

14109721.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14109721.value: As we age, our muscles lose their ability to repair themselves after injury, largely because the special stem cells responsible for repair (satellite cells) become less active. This project developed a new, precise way to deliver medicine directly to these satellite cells. We identified a tiny "homing device" (an aptamer named SCApt) that attaches specifically to satellite cells. This homing device was attached to nanoparticles carrying a drug (JAK2 siRNA) that enhances the proliferation and regenerative capacity of stem cells. In older mice with muscle injury, we showed that this targeted system successfully delivers its drug cargo exclusively to the muscle stem cells. The treatment effectively activated the regeneration of these cells, leading to much better muscle repair and recovery of strength, without causing harm to other organs like the liver or kidneys. This work provides a promising new therapeutic strategy for developing highly targeted and effective treatments for age-related muscle weakness and severe muscle diseases that require muscle regeneration.

14111021.label: Major findings and research outcome
14111021.value: 1. Between January 03, 2022, and August 31, 2024, two hundred and thirty-eight old adults with co-occurring sleep disturbances and cognitive impairments were screened for eligibility, of which 31 patients who declined to participate or did not meet eligibility criteria (n=108) were excluded. A total of 99 participants meeting the inclusion criteria were enrolled, of whom 36 (36.4%) were male, and the median (IQR) age was 72.8 (61.7-87.3) years. 2. At the 24th week (end point), primary outcome data was missing for five patients (Dropout rate: 5.1%). Within each treatment group, prominent improvements in subjective sleep quality were observed over the follow-up periods. The 40 Hz HD-tACS group had the lowest PSQI total score than the HD-tDCS and sham HD-tCS groups at the 4th week, 8th week, 12th week and 24th week, with an average eta-squared (η2) effect size of 0.24. Further pairwise comparison demonstrated that the 40 Hz HD-tACS group had significantly decreased PSQI total score than either the HD-tDCS group or sham HD-tCS group at the 4th week, 8th week, 12th week and 24th week (p<0.001). At week 12, HD-tDCS group had a lower PSQI total score than HD-tDCS, and there was a significant difference in the PSQI total score between these two groups (p=0.41). 3. The 40 Hz HD-tACS group had the highest correct numbers of delayed recall of words than the HD-tDCS and sham HD-tCS groups at the 4th week, 8th week, 12th week and 24th week, with an average η2 effect size of 0.21. Further pairwise comparison demonstrated that the 40 Hz HD-tACS group had significantly increased score of the delayed recall test than the sham HD-tCS group at the 8th week (p=0.013), 12th week (p<0.001) and 24th week (p<0.001). HD-tDCS had a higher score of the delayed recall test than sham HD-tCS at the 12th week (p=0.045) and 24th week (p=0.002). 4. Enhancements in MoCA total scores were observed in 40 Hz HD-tACS and HD-tDCS groups. At week 4, the 40 Hz HD-tACS group had the highest MoCA total score than the sham HD-tCS group (p=0.031). At week 24, both 40 Hz HD-tACS and HD-tDCS groups showed significant higher MoCA total scores than sham HD-tCS group. At week 4, the 40 Hz HD-tACS group showed significant lower saliva Aβ42 and higher Aβ 42/40 ratio than sham HD-tCS group.

14111021.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14111021.value: The highly encouraging results from this clinical trial establish a robust foundation for several critical and high-impact pathways of further development. 1. Protocol optimization: There is significant potential to personalize and optimize the therapeutic protocol. This includes determining optimal stimulation parameters (e.g., intensity, treatment target), individualizing dosing based on morphometric features and simulation models, and exploring closed-loop systems that deliver stimulation in response to real-time sleep EEG signatures. 2. Clinical translation: The results provide a strong rationale for expanding research toward specific clinical populations with high unmet need, such as individuals with insomnia disorder, older females with sleep comorbidity, or patients with pain and sleep disturbances. This positions the technology (40 Hz HD-tACS) to address clear clinical gaps. 3. Mechanistic investigation: Our findings open the door to elucidating the precise neural mechanisms underlying the treatment effect of 40 Hz HD-tACS. Further development could employ wearable EEG or polysomnography (PSG) coupled with neuromodulation, to map the causal pathway from stimulation to sleep architecture improvement, particularly in older adults at high risk of developing Alzheimer's disease.

14111021.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14111021.value: Background: Sleep disturbances are highly prevalent in ageing population and patients with age-related neurodegenerative diseases, which severely affect cognition and even lead to accumulated amyloid-β (Aβ). At present, non-pharmacological interventions for sleep disturbances in dementia patients are accepted as first line of treatment, of which the evidence from clinical trials is very limited. High-definition transcranial alternating current stimulation (HD-tACS) enables the entrainment of neuronal activities with optimized focality through injecting small electric current with a specific frequency and has significant enhancement effects on slow wave activities. Significance and value: The findings of this study will provide a pathway and Class I evidence to promote sleep quality and cognitive function in individuals at early-stage Alzheimer’s disease. This study will also evaluate the safety and efficacy of HD-tACS, and further optimize the personalized brain-based intervention strategies, which may promote the effective non pharmacological treatments and evaluation protocols in clinical practice, as well as new procedures to improve sleep-related cognitive dysfunction in a general population. Information will be helpful for in-depth understanding the relationship of “sleep disturbances-amyloid deposition” and guiding the further studies of sleep medicine and neurodegenerative diseases.

14111621.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14111621.value: 結直腸癌（CRC）在香港已經是首發的癌症。近些年來，結直腸癌的發病率出現了令人擔憂的發病率，并帶來了巨大的社會和經濟負擔。在過去十年中，癌症基因組測序在很大程度上描繪了結直腸癌的基因突變。然而結直腸癌的發生發展的轉錄后機制仍不明確。RNA N6-甲基腺嘌呤（m6A）修飾是對人類信使RNA加工（剪接、翻譯和降解）起至關重要的作用。m6A位點的修飾受到了m6A調節酶的動態調控，其中包括編碼器、閱讀器和擦除器。RNA去甲基化酶AlkB同源蛋白5（ALKBH5）是一種去m6A修飾的擦除器。然而，該基因在結直腸腫瘤發生的作用仍然知之甚少。我們的前期研究發現，在結直腸癌細胞株中敲低ALKBH5顯著的降低了細胞的體外增殖能力和體內的致瘤性，並且在免疫系統完整的老鼠中致瘤性加強。對Alkbh5敲除的腫瘤進行了免疫細胞浸潤組成的分析，顯示MDSC浸潤程度下調，自然殺傷細胞（NK）和細胞毒性T細胞（CD8+ T）浸潤程度上調，結果說明Alkbh5可通過調節結直腸癌中的免疫浸潤，進而達到對抗抗腫瘤的免疫作用。機制上，結合RNA甲基化免疫共沉澱測序和RNA測序的結果確定了AXIN2是ALKBH5的直接作用基因，作為一個WNT的抑制基因。ALKBH5通過抑制AXIN2的表達激活WNT/β-catenin-DKK1信號通路，以達到在結直腸癌中發揮促腫瘤的作用。體外實驗中證明DKK1是MDSC的趨化劑，結果顯示ALKBH5-AXIN2-Wnt/DKK1軸是ALKBH5在結直腸癌中免疫抑制作用的基礎。本課題的目標如下：1）利用ALKBH5敲除小鼠證明ALKBH5在大腸癌的作用；2）研究ALKBH5在大腸癌的分子機制；3）研究ALKBH5在大腸癌免疫微環境的作用；4）分析ALKBH5的臨床意義。通過一系列的實驗，驗證ALKBH5可作為結直腸癌發生發展過程中的獨立生物標誌物，並且也可在結直腸癌的治療過程中作為潛在的治療靶點。

14111621.label: Realisation of objectives
14111621.value: Objective 1: To determine the pro-tumorigenic function of ALKBH5 via modulating immune microenvironment in CRC To ask if ALKBH5-mediated m6A modification regulates CRC immune microenvironment, we established murine CRC allografts (MC38, CT26) with ALKBH5 knockout in immunocompetent mice. We then analyzed the composition of immune cells using multicolor flow cytometry. In the MC38 syngeneic mouse model, tumor growth was markedly decreased by ALKBH5 knockout, concomitant with reduced MDSC infiltration, including monocytic MDSCs and granulocytic MDSCs, together with increased NK and CD8+ T cell population. In line with this, deletion of ALKBH5 strongly suppressed tumor growth and boosted antitumor immune response in a CT26 syngeneic model. Conversely, overexpression of ALKBH5 induced MDSC infiltration, but inhibited NK and CD8+ T cells in tumors, thereby promoting MC38 allografts growth. To determine if the effect of ALKBH5 depends on MDSCs, we depleted MDSCs by anti-Gr-1 antibody in MC38 allograft, showing that anti-Gr-1 abolished the tumor-promoting effect of ALKBH5. We thus established that ALKBH5 drives immunosuppression in CRC by modulating MDSC infiltration in CRC. To validate the immunosuppressive effects of ALKBH5 in human CRC, we next established CD34+ humanized mouse model to mimic the human immune system in mice. Consistently, ALKBH5 knockout in HCT116 tumors significantly inhibited tumor growth in humanized CD34+ mice, with decreased MDSCs but increased NK cells, CD4+T cells, and CD8+ T cells. Furthermore, we generated colon-specific Alkbh5 knockin (Alkbh5 KI) mice (Rosa26lsl-Alkbh5CDX2-CreERT2), and induced CRC in these mice by treatment with azoxymethane plus DSS. Alkbh5 knockin promoted colorectal tumorigenesis compared to wildtype littermates. Flow cytometry revealed increased MDSC infiltration in Alkbh5 KI mouse tumors compared with wildtype mice, concomitant with significant reductions in NK and CD8+ T cells. Taken together, our comprehensive analysis of ALKBH5-assoicated CRC immune microenvironment demonstrated that ALKBH5 recruits MDSCs into CRC, leading to the inactivation of antitumor CD8+ T cells. Objective 2: To elucidate the molecular mechanisms by which ALKBH5 modulates immune landscape in CRC via m6A modification To investigate how ALKBH5 promotes CRC growth and suppresses antitumor immunity, we performed a series of experiments to explore the molecular basis of its action. First, we conducted MeRIP-seq and RNA-seq in HCT116 cells with or without ALKBH5 knockdown. Overlap of the candidate genes identified from MeRIP-seq and RNA-seq uncovered 5 potential ALKBH5 downstream targets (AXIN2, RGMB, NGFR, C1orf116, and ARL4C). Among them, expression of AXIN2 was consistently induced upon knockdown of ALKBH5 in multiple CRC cell lines, suggesting that AXIN2 may be a direct target of ALKBH5 in CRC cells. We next used m6A-immunoprecipitation qPCR to demonstrate that depletion of ALKBH5 increased the m6A level of AXIN2 mRNA; whereas ALKBH5 overexpression elicited opposite effects. Pulldown assay further confirmed that ALKBH5 binds to AXIN2 mRNA to demethylate m6A marks. We next explored whether and how ALKBH5 affects AXIN2 expression in CRC. We found that both mRNA and protein expression of AXIN2 were profoundly increased in ALKBH5-depleted CRC cells, whereas its expression was suppressed by ALKBH5 overexpression. Given that m6A modifications have a significant impact on mRNA decay, we hypothesized that ALKBH5 could regulate AXIN2 mRNA stability. As expected, ALKBH5 depletion stabilized AXIN2 mRNA, whereas ALKBH5 overexpression exerted an opposite effect. Corroborating in vitro findings, we observed negative correlations between ALKBH5 and AXIN2 expression at the protein and mRNA levels in CRC patient cohorts. These studies established that ALKBH5 down-regulates AXIN2 in CRC. AXIN2 functions as a scaffold protein in the β-catenin destruction complex to promote β-catenin degradation. Thus, we hypothesized that ALKBH5 activates Wnt signaling in CRC via inhibiting AXIN2. Indeed, ALKBH5 knockdown in CRC cells reduced nuclear β-catenin, and expression of MYC and cyclin D1; whereas ALKBH5 overexpression exerted opposite effects. Re-expression of AXIN2 in ALKBH5 overexpressing cells abolished the effect of ALKBH5 on promoting β-catenin expression and CRC cell growth. Together, we revealed a novel CRC via the ALKBH5-m6A–AXIN2–β-catenin axis in promoting CRC. To further link ALKBH5 to the modulation of the tumor immune microenvironment, we identified Dickkopf-related protein 1 (DKK1) as a top candidate downstream of ALKBH5-regulated Wnt/β-catenin signaling. On ALKBH5 depletion, decreased expression of DKK1 at both mRNA and protein levels was observed in CRC cells, whereas ALKBH5 overexpression exerted the opposite effects. DKK1 has been reported to be associated with MDSCs accumulation. We thus asked if ALKBH5 may induce DKK1 secretion to recruit MDSCs in CRC. Supporting our hypothesis, conditioned medium from ALKBH5-knockout MC38 or CT26 showed reduced capacity to attract MDSC migration compared with controls, while the difference was eliminated by supplementation of recombinant DKK1 protein. Whereas anti-DKK1 neutralizing antibody abrogated the promoting effect of ALKBH5 on tumor growth and MDSC infiltration in vivo. Taken together, the ALKBH5-m6A–AXIN2–β-catenin axis induces DKK1 expression to recruit immunosuppressive MDSCs into CRC tumors, leading to increased tumor growth. Objective 3: To investigate the clinical significance of ALKBH5 in CRC and its correlation with immune cell infiltration in CRC patients To evaluate the clinical significance of ALKBH5, protein expression of ALKBH5 was examined tissue microarrays consisting of 205 patients with CRC. Kaplan-Meier curve showed that high protein expression of ALKBH5 was correlated with poor overall survival. Multivariate Cox regression incorporating other risk factors, including gender, age, tumor location, and TNM stage, showed that ALKBH5 protein expression was an independent poor prognostic factor. These findings were verified in The Cancer Genome Atlas dataset, showing that high mRNA expression of ALKBH5 predicted poor overall survival in CRC patients and was an independent poor prognostic factor. Supporting a role of ALKBH5 in immunosuppression, higher expression of ALKBH5 was correlated with lower CD8+ T cell infiltration in human primary CRC tissues by means of immunohistochemical staining.

14111621.label: Major findings and research outcome
14111621.value: Aberrant epitranscriptome regulation is highly prevalent in CRC and increasing evidence indicates that it drives colorectal cancer (CRC) by modulating tumorigenic pathways. RNA N6-Methyladenosine (m6A) is the most abundant RNA modification in the human and a determinant in posttranscriptional regulation of mRNA splicing, translation and degradation. In this study, we focused on studying the role of the m6A eraser ALKBH5 as an oncogenic factor in CRC through modulating the tumor immune microenvironment. The major outcomes of this study include: 1) functional validation of ALKBH5 as a protumorigenic factor in CRC in murine tumor allgrafts, human CRC xenografts in CD34+ humanized mice, and colon-specific ALKBH5 knockin mouse model, and was complemented by comprehensive immunological profiling to identify the impact of ALKBH5 on promoting myeloid-derived suppresser cells (MDSCs) and suppressing CD8+ T cells; 2) integrated m6A sequencing and RNA sequencing, revealed the mechanism of action of ALKBH5 in CRC via a m6A-AXIN2-WNT-DKK1 axis to recruit MDSCs, thereby promoting the inactivation of CD8+ T cells and subsequent immune escape; 3) inhibition of ALKBH5 potentiated the efficacy of anti-PD1 immunotherapy by boosting cytotoxic CD8+ T cell response; and 4) identified and validated METTL3 as a prognostic biomarker for CRC patients. This project has been fruitful and has been published in Gastroenterology in 2023 [IF=25.9], with the PI as corresponding author, and has been cited >100 times. Apart from this work, we have also investigated the role of different m6A regulators in CRC, such as METTL3 (Gastroenterology 2023, IF=25.9) and YTHDF1 (Gut 2023, IF=25.8), as well as the function of METTL3 in NAFLD-associated HCC (Cell Reports Medicine 2023, IF=10.6). Other related projects include the role of SQLE in NAFLD-associated HCC (Gut 2024, IF=25.8) and the function of probiotics in CRC (Cancer Cell 2023, IF=44.5). A total of 12 peer-reviewed papers and 2 conference abstracts have been published based on this funding. One PhD student was trained during the completion of this project.

14111621.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14111621.value: To further improve our understanding of ALKBH5 in CRC as well as other cancers and its impact with immunotherapy efficacy, we will open up collaborative research with other academic researchers to investigate whether modification of ALKBH5 activity might represent a viable approach as an adjuvant to boost immunotherapy efficacy in CRC. We will consider to perform high-content molecular screening in order to identify ALKBH5 inhibitors. Efficacy of candidate inhibitor(s) will be tested using our primary organoids and transgenic mouse models of ALKBH5. Moreover, we will evaluate the synergism of ALKBH5 inhibition plus immunotherapies (e.g. checkpoint inhibitors) for the treatment of CRC. We hope that our efforts will translate into an effective and safe therapeutic strategy for treatment of CRC in the future. Additionally, since ALKBH5 expression predicts poor prognosis of CRC patients in CRC, we proposed that ALKBH5 may be a potential prognostic biomarker for CRC. We will collaborate with our academic partners, who will provide CRC patient cohorts from different ethnic groups for extensive validation of the clinical significance of ALKBH5 in CRC. We will apply for local and international patents based on our results. Ultimately, we hope to develop a novel diagnostic kit for prognostication of CRC patients.

14111621.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14111621.value: Nature of the project: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is the number one cancer in Hong Kong. Although immunotherapy is a promising treatment option in CRC, most patients failed to respond. N6-methyladenosine (m6A) modification has recently emerged as a new regulatory mechanism critical in regulating the tumor immune microenvironment. In this study, we first identified that ALKBH5 is an m6A regulator involved in CRC development and immunotherapy response. Functionally, ALKBH5 promotes an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment in CRC by recruiting myeloid-derived suppressor through a m6A-AXIN2-WNT-DKK1 axis. Inhibition of ALKBH5 potentiates anti-PD1 immunotherapy towards CRC tumors. Significance: Our work demonstrated that ALKBH5 as an actionable immunotherapeutic target in CRC. The combination of targeting ALKBH5 in conjunction with anti-PD1 therapy synergized to inhibit the growth of CRC in vivo, thereby implying the potential role of targeting ALKBH5 as an adjuvant strategy to boost immunotherapy efficacy in CRC. Apart from experimental findings, we showed that ALKBH5 is a specific biomarker that predicts poor survival in CRC patients. Value of the project: ALKBH5 is a potential therapeutic target and biomarker for CRC patients.

14112121.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14112121.value: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is an important cause of morbidity and mortality in hospitalized patients, but there are no effective treatment strategies available. Therefore, there is a pressing need to enhance our understanding of the pathogenesis of AKI. It is well accepted that tubular epithelial cell death plays an active role in the development of AKI with acute tubular necrosis being a key feature of AKI. Necrosis can be a regulated or programmed process. RIPK1-mediated programmed necrosis, i.e., necroptosis, plays a critical role in the development of AKI. Necroptosis is carried out by mixed lineage kinase domain-like protein (MLKL). Phosphorylation of MLKL by receptor-interacting protein kinase (RIPK) 3 and RIPK1 induces MLKL oligomerization. MLKL oligomers are translocated to the plasma membrane to induce membrane rupture and necrosis. However, how the RIPK1/RIPK3/MLKL pathway is regulated during AKI is largely unknown. Repulsive guidance molecule (RGM)b belongs to the RGM family consisting of RGMa, RGMb and RGMc. We recently published a paper in PNAS (2018) showing that RGMb inhibited necroptosis in proximal tubular epithelial cells by decreasing MLKL accumulation on the plasma membrane. However, the detailed mechanisms of RGMb’s anti-necroptotic action has not been elucidated. We now found that RGMb interacted with the UNC5B receptor, and UNC5B interacted with DAPK1. Importantly, a recent study has demonstrated DAPK1 inhibits necroptosis by promoting the p38 MAPK/MK2/RIPK1(S321) cascade. Interestingly, our preliminary results demonstrated that RGMb also promoted the phosphorylation of p38 MAPK, MK2 and RIPK1(S321), and that RGMb’s anti-necroptotic activity was blocked by inhibition of UNC5B or DAPK1. Therefore, our central hypothesis is that RGMb, UNC5B and DAPK1 form a pathway to inhibit necroptosis. We propose to: 1) determine whether UNC5B and DAPK1 mediate RGMb’s anti-necroptotic activity in tubular epithelial cells; 2) study how UNC5B and DAPK1 mediate RGMb’s anti-necroptotic activity in tubular epithelial cells; 3) characterise the RGMb/UNC5B/DAPK1 pathway in the kidney during AKI. The results we obtain will advance our understanding of the mechanisms of tubular cell death during AKI, and will provide essential information on the identification of new targets for development of diagnostic and treatment strategies to ameliorate AKI. 急性腎損傷(AKI)在住院病人中發病率和死亡率很高，但面前尚無有效的防治手段，因此迫切需要研究AKI的病理機製。腎小管上皮細胞死亡在AKI中起重要作用，而腎小管上皮細胞壞死是AKI的典型病例特征之一。在一些病例條件下細胞壞死是可調控的，RIPK1介導的可調控的壞死稱為程序性壞死(necroptosis)。近期的研究表明necroptosis在AKI中起重要作用。Necroptosis由MLKL來執行，RIPK1和RIPK3使MLKL磷酸化，磷酸化的MLKL進而由單體聚合形成寡聚體，MLKL寡聚體轉運到細胞膜引發細胞膜破裂、細胞壞死，然而目前尚不清楚RIPK1/RIPK3/MLKL通路在AKI中是如何受調控的。RGMb是排斥導向分子家族(包括RGMa、RGMb和RGMc)中的一員， 我們之前發表在PNAS上的文章發現RGMb通過減少MLKL在細胞膜上的聚集來抑製近曲小管上皮細胞的necroptosis，但RGMb抗necroptosis的詳細機製尚待研究。我們現在發現RGMb可和UNC5B受體結合、UNC5B又可和DAPK1結合。重要的是最近有一個研究表明DAPK1 可通過促進p38 MAPK/MK2/RIPK1(S321) 通路來抑製necroptosis。有意思的是我們的初步研究發現RGMb也可促進p38 MAPK、MK2和RIPK1(S321)的磷酸化，而且抑製UNC5B或DAPK1可阻斷RGMb的抗necroptosis活性。因此我們的假設是RGMb、UNC5B和DAPK1形成一個通路來抑製necroptosis。為證明這一假設我們將1）查明UNC5B和DAPK1是否在腎小管上皮細胞中介導RGMb的抗necroptosis功能；2）研究UNC5B和DAPK1如何在腎小管上皮細胞中介導RGMb的抗necroptosis功能；3）分析AKI腎臟中RGMb/UNC5B/DAPK1通路。本項目的完成將有助於我們進一步理解AKI中腎小管上皮細胞的死亡機理，並為急性腎損傷的臨床診斷與處理提供新的思路。

14112121.label: Realisation of objectives
14112121.value: RGMb interacted with UNC5B and UNC5C: Netrin-1 was originally discovered as a chemotropic molecule that regulates neurite outgrowth and neuronal migration. Neutrin-1 signals through two families of type I immunoglobulin-like receptors, i.e., the DCC family consisting of DCC (deleted in colon cancer) and its homolog neogenin, and the UNC5 family comprising UNC5A, UNC5B, UNC5C and UNC5D. All the three RGM family members (i.e., RGMa, RGMb and RGMc) interact with neogenin . To explore whether RGMb interacts with other netrin-1 receptors, we performed immunoprecipitation assays. We found that RGMb interacted with UNC5B and UNC5C, as well as neogenin (Neo-1). Therefore, RGMb is likely a novel ligand for UNC5B and UNC5C. DAPK1 much more strongly interacts with UNC5B than with UNC5A and UNC5C: Our immunoprecipitation assay showed the interaction between UNC5B and DAPK1. Interestingly, neogenin failed to be co-precipitated with DAPK1. Therefore, UNC5B is the main receptor of the DCC and UNC5 families that interacts with DAPK1. Of note, RGMb did not interact with DAPK1. RGMb is released from renal tubular epithelial cells to promote macrophage migration: We further examined whether RGMb is released from renal tubular cells during kidney injury. We found that RGMb levels increased in the kidney and serum of both human patients and mice with kidney disease. Tubule-specific ablation of Rgmb ameliorated renal inflammation and fibrosis indued by two low doses of folic acid or UUO. Soluble RGMb promoted the migration of RAW264.7 macrophages and bone marrow-derived macrophages (BMDMs). RGMb in interstitial fluids increased in response to UUO and facilitated macrophage migration. Inhibition of the iron-sensing receptor HFE abolished the effects of RGMb on macrophage migration. Our results suggest that RGMb mediates the communications between injured tubular cells and macrophages to aggravate kidney inflammation and fibrosis.

14112121.label: Major findings and research outcome
14112121.value: Tubular epithelial cells play an active role in the development of kidney disease. Tubular injury induces immune cell accumulation, and one of the major cell types is the macrophage. Repulsive guidance molecule (RGM)-b is a member of the RGM family, which consists of RGMa, RGMb and RGMc. Our previous work demonstrated that global heterozygous Rgmb knockout mice were protected from tubular injury induced by unilateral ureteral obstruction (UUO). However, the specific role of renal tubular RGMb in kidney inflammation and fibrosis remained to be established. Here, we found that RGMb levels increased in the kidney and serum of both human patients and mice with kidney disease. Tubule-specific ablation of Rgmb ameliorated renal inflammation and fibrosis indued by two low doses of folic acid or UUO. Soluble RGMb promoted the migration of RAW264.7 macrophages and bone marrow-derived macrophages (BMDMs). RGMb in interstitial fluids increased in response to UUO and facilitated macrophage migration. Inhibition of the iron-sensing receptor HFE abolished the effects of RGMb on macrophage migration. Our results suggest that RGMb mediates the communications between injured tubular cells and macrophages to aggravate kidney inflammation and fibrosis. We did not observe significant effects of tubular Rgmb deletion on tubular cell apoptosis and necroptosis during UUO. This work provided results for our US Provisional Patent Application no. 63/583,035 filed on 15 September 2023 (Applicants: Yin XIA, Yonglun KONG and Xiaoyi ZHANG). It is now being turned into a formal patent application (Ref# 19/168,404).

14112121.value: We will continue to study the effects of targeting tubular RGMb by approaches such as AAV9 viruses carrying a Cdh16 promoter (Ksp)-driven shRNA for RGMb or antibody-mediated neutralisation of soluble RGMb on macrophage infiltration and kidney inflammation and fibrosis.

14112121.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14112121.value: RGMb is released from renal tubular epithelial cells to the interstitium in response to kidney injury, thereby promoting macrophage migration and infiltration and aggravating renal inflammation and fibrosis. RGMb levels were elevated in the serum of human patients and mice with kidney disease. Therefore, our results suggest that RGMb may be a target for development of diagnostic and treatment strategies to ameliorate kidney disease.

14112521.value: Le Bihan 等提出了體素內非相干運動 (IVIM) 理論，可以按該理論定量計算反映組織水分子彌散和組織血管灌注 的參數 (Dslow, PF 和 Dfast)。我們在這方面發表了一些開創性的工作。在三項獨立的小型臨床研究中，我們證明了通過改進的 IVIM 分析幾乎可以完全區分健康肝臟和早期纖維化肝臟。 隨著 掃描的b 值越來越高時，彌散磁共振成像肝臟信號的衰減並不完全遵循雙指數模型，而這種關係可以用三指數衰減模型更好地擬合。然而，三指數模型擬合對於單個人體肝臟可非常不穩定。因此我們提出肝臟 DWI 信號與 b值的關係可以分割為兩個部分：第一段是 b=0 s/mm2 圖像和第一個非常低 b值的 圖像（例如 b= 2 s/mm2圖像）；其餘部分是第二段，可以更好地用雙指數衰減模型擬合。在肝臟彌散磁共振成像，當沒有擴散梯度磁場 (b = 0 s/mm2) 時，血管顯示高信號；然而即使應用了非常低的 b 值，血管也會顯示低信號。因此，對於第 一 段，沒有彌散梯度磁場時圖像和彌散梯度磁場開啟時圖像之間的信號差反映了組織血管密度（diffusion-derived vessel density，DDVD。對於第二段 ，從非零的低 b 值開始，彌散磁共振成像信號和 b 值之間的關係遵循雙指數衰減。我們的結果表明，DDVD 與 IVIM 灌注參數 PF 和 Dfast 有中等程度相關而且統計學呈現顯著性，DDVD是對於區分肝臟有無纖維化的有意義的生物學標誌。 隨年齡增加肝臟血流灌注減少已在生理學上得到充分證明，最近我們證明了隨年齡增加肝臟 DDVD值下降。此外，我們的結果顯示，隨著年齡的增長，健康受試者呈現Dslow降低的趨勢。但矛盾的是，PF和Dfast卻有隨著年齡的增長的趨勢。即使應用全擬合計算， Dslow的下降也有可能導致PF 和 Dfast的假性增高。 除其他研究目的外，我們的研究核心是通過一系列肝臟動物模型回答兩個關鍵問題：（1）能否證明磁共振 成像DDVD 較高或較低的測量 與組織學上較高或較低的微血管密度相關？ (2) 即使生理上的 PF 和 Dfast 沒有發生變化，Dslow 的下降是否會導致假性 IVIM 測量到的 PF 和 Dfast升高？

14112521.label: Realisation of objectives
14112521.value: The research objectives have been all achieved. With this GRF funding, we systematically investigated biophysical phenomena of IVIM and DDVD. We have shown that a higher liver iron level can lead to a lower IVIM-Dslow measure, and artificially high perfusion measure (IVIM perfusion fraction and IVIM-Fast) by IVIM. In the liver, IVIM perfusion fraction and IVIM-Fast are contributed more by T2-related signal decay rather than by true tissue perfusion, these two parameters cannot reliably reflect perfusion fraction or flow speed. While our study does not lend IVIM to be unusable, our results do suggest the reading of IVIM metrics should be viewed with great caution. We also proposed improved data fitting method for IVIM. Importantly, we have shown DDVD, as a biomarker reflecting perfusion, is highly correlated with vasculature. Liver studies show DDVD measures both vasculature of both arteries and veins. Liver DDVD can reflect hepatocellular carcinoma perfusion and neo-angiogenesis, and can potentially predict aggressiveness of hepatocellular carcinoma. In some cases, when human patients were available, we used human patient studies to replace preclinical animal study (which will be relevant in clinical practice). Using DDVD, rather than IVIM, can reliably diagnose liver hemangioma. A combination of DDVD and SDC can be considered as an abbreviated yet more reliable version of IVIM. We have shown that, by non-invasively using diffusion and diffusion and without the need for contrast agent injection, we can diagnosis liver focal nodular hyperplasia (FNH) (>70% of the cases), mass-forming intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (ICC, 60% of the cases), and about 1/3 of the liver metastasis. In diagnostic MRI, contrast injections are commonly administered. The most commonly used compounds for contrast enhancement are gadolinium-based contrast agents (GBCAs). The first gadolinium-based contrast agent (GBCA), gadopentetate dimeglumine (Magnevist) was approved in the late 1980's. Over 450 million doses have been administered worldwide from 1988 to 2017. If DDVD and SDC are integrated into clinical routines, we expect that globally >50% of the contrast agent enhanced MRI scan be saved. Our work will have a major impact.

14112521.label: Major findings and research outcome
14112521.value: With this GRF funding, we systematically investigated biophysical phenomena of IVIM and DDVD. We have shown that a higher liver iron level can lead to a lower IVIM-Dslow measure, and artificially high perfusion measure (IVIM perfusion fraction and IVIM-Fast) by IVIM. In the liver, IVIM perfusion fraction and IVIM-Fast are contributed more by T2-related signal decay rather than by true tissue perfusion, these two parameters cannot reliably reflect perfusion fraction or flow speed. While our study does not lend IVIM to be unusable, our results do suggest the reading of IVIM metrics should be viewed with great caution. We also proposed improved data fitting method for IVIM. Importantly, we have shown DDVD, as a biomarker reflecting perfusion, is highly correlated with vasculature. Liver studies show DDVD measures both vasculature of both arteries and veins. Liver DDVD can reflect hepatocellular carcinoma perfusion and neo-angiogenesis, and can potentially predict aggressiveness of hepatocellular carcinoma. Moreover, during the course of this GRF funded study, we proposed an additional metric: slow diffusion coefficient (SDC). We expanded the application scope for DDVD. We have shown promising results in that: 1) Liver hemangioma can be reliably diagnosed by DDVD/SDC; 2) liver focal nodular hyperplasia (FNH) can be mostly (> 70% of the cases) confirmed by DDVD/SDC without the need for a contrast agent injection; 3) a novel combination of diffusion metric including DDVD/SDC can predict aggressiveness of hepatocellular carcinoma; 4) a novel combination of diffusion metric including DDVD/SDC can predict aggressiveness and survival of intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma; 5) DDVD can be used to assess acute ischemic brain stroke; 6) DDVD can be used to assess diagnose breast cancer and evaluate breast cancer treatment response; 7) DDVD can be used to predict rectal carcinoma treatment response. Additionally, we have shown DDVD can be used to assess acute ischemic brain stroke, brain tumor IDH (isocitrate dehydrogenase) mutation status, parotid gland tumor perfusion, endometrial carcinoma neo-angiogenesis.

14112521.value: With this GRF funding, we systematically investigated biophysical phenomenon of IVIM (intravoxel incoherent motion) and DDVD (diffusion-derived vessel density). 14112921.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14112921.value: The emergence of antibiotic resistance (AR) and the lack of novel antibiotics have posed significant global medical challenges [1]. Alternatives, like antimicrobial antibodies, peptides, probiotics, metal chelation, are promising, but they are also limited by resistance development. Recently, depolymerases targeting the polysaccharide components of the bacterial capsule and biofilm matrix have been considered as promising antibacterial agents [2-5]. Importantly, they do not directly kill bacteria. Rather, they sensitize bacteria to serum killing or antibiotics. This suggests depolymerases barely promote resistant mutations, being a valuable asset in this AR battle. While the efficacy of depolymerase controlling systemic infections is well demonstrated, its efficacy against lung infections has not yet been studied. This provides the impetus for the present study, predicated on the potential of depolymerases in disrupting biofilms [6-9], thereby facilitating the entry of antimicrobials [10-12] to control lung infections. Particularly, we will focus on Acinetobacter baumannii due to its high incidence of AR. Indeed, our pilot data (Fig. 2e-g) show that the combination of Dpo71 and colistin had stronger bacterial suppression and antibiofilm ability. In this project, we will follow up on this promising data by screening additional combinations for their potency in lowering the antibiotic’s minimum bactericidal concentration (MBC) and minimum biofilm eliminating concentration (MBEC) both by > 2-fold. In addition, the refractory to resistance development of these combinations will be studied. We hypothesize that co-delivering the combination via inhalation would allow the two agents to achieve maximum concentrations in lungs. Currently, 75% of the developing inhaled protein therapeutics are liquids for nebulization [13]. We, therefore, will optimize the liquid formulations and nebulizers for pulmonary delivery of identified combinations. Our pilot data (Fig. 2h) show that a mesh nebulizer caused negligible deactivation of Dpo71, suggesting its robustness to withstand nebulization stresses. The selection criteria will be those offering an inhalable fraction ≥ 50%, a deactivation rate of depolymerase ≤ 10% and prolonged storage of 12 months. The impacts of delivery routes in the biodistribution of a selected formulation will first be assessed. Then, its efficacy in controlling bacterial lung infection will be evaluated using a mouse pneumonia model with the dose designed based on the pharmacokinetic results. This project will develop novel therapeutics using depolymerase and antibiotic combinations to address clinical problems associated with multidrug-resistant A. baumannii. The knowledge and protocols to be developed will also be applicable to other ‘superbugs’, like Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Klebsiella pneumonia, to be tested next. 抗生素耐藥性的出現和新型抗生素的缺乏給全球醫學帶來了重大挑戰 [1]。一些很有前景抗生素的替代品（如抗菌的抗體，抗菌肽、益生菌、金屬螯合）都受到耐藥性的限制。近年，靶向細菌莢膜的多醣成分的解聚酶被認為是一種有前途的抗菌劑 [2-5]。解聚酶雖然不能直接殺死細菌，但它們降低細菌的毒力，讓血清或抗生素有效清除細菌。這個特性，讓解聚酶幾乎不會促進抗性突變，使其變成這場抗生素耐藥性戰爭中的寶貴資產。 雖然解聚酶控制全身感染的功效已得到充分證明，但尚未研究其對肺部感染的功效。解聚酶能有效破壞生物膜 [6-9]，從而促進抗菌素的功效 [10-12]。因此，我們相信解聚酶在控制肺部感染方面會有很大的潛力。本研究，我們將重點關注鮑曼不動桿菌，因為它的耐藥性發生率很高。我們前期的試驗數據（圖 2e、2f）表明解聚酶 Dpo71 和粘菌素的組合具有更強的細菌抑制和生物膜抑制。在本項目中，我們將通過篩選更多組合，（挑選條件是能將抗生素的最低殺菌濃度 (MBC) 和最低生物膜消除濃度 (MBEC) 均降低 > 2 倍的效力的組合）來跟進這一有前景的數據。此外，我們還將研究這些組合對耐藥性發展的抵抗力。 我們假設通過吸入遞送可以使這兩種藥物的組合在肺部達到最大濃度。目前，75% 正在開發的吸入性蛋白質都是用霧化遞送。因此，我們也將優化液體配方和霧化器，用來遞送已確定組合到肺部。我們的前期試驗數據（圖 2g）顯示網狀霧化器導致 Dpo71 的失活率可忽略不計。組合的挑選條件為：可吸入分數≥ 50%、解聚酶失活率≤ 10% 和能長期儲存 12 個月的標準。選定組合後，我們將進行體內評價實。驗首先評估遞送途徑對選定製劑的生物分佈的影響。然後，我們會用小鼠肺炎模型評估其在控制肺部感染方面的功效。 本項目將使用解聚酶和抗生素組合開發新療法，以解決與多重耐藥鮑曼不動桿菌相關的臨床問題。將要開發的知識也有可能適用於其他革蘭氏陰性“超級細菌”，如銅綠假單胞菌和肺炎克雷伯菌，接下來將進行測試。

14113521.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14113521.value: 顱面畸形是常見的先天性疾病，這不單影響了病人的臉型外觀，更會對進食和語言發音等日常生活構成障礙。IRX5 基因突變會引致哈馬邁綜合症 (Hamamy syndrome)，病人會出現多項顱面畸形，包括顎部異常。然而，其病因和當中的發病機理並未解構，Irx基因於顱面及咽部發育的功能亦未清晰。 Irx3 和 Irx5 是同源蛋白質區段轉錄因子，它們屬連鎖基因組，位於 IrxB 基因簇上。在很多發育過程中，它們有各自特定的功能，也會有功能冗餘。胚胎成長時，上下顎主要由第一對咽弓的上下頜發育而成。我們發現，在第一對咽弓發育時，Irx3 和 Irx5 基因表達於神經嵴細胞和外胚層上皮細胞。而在突變小鼠和轉錄組分析中，我們初步實驗結果顯示，第一對咽弓的近端結構之發育需要 Irx3/5，失去 Irx3 和 Irx5 會令部份上頜變質成下頜。Irx3/5 可透過細胞自主形式控制神經嵴細胞發育；也在口部上皮和基板上皮細胞中有着關鍵作用，並以非細胞自主形式的分子信號控制咽弓內的其他細胞。 這研究計劃的目標，在於了解顱面和顎部發育時，Irx3 和 Irx5 基因在咽上皮及神經嵴細胞中的功能。首先，我們會研究一系列 Irx3、Irx5 及複合的小鼠突變體中，上下頜弓的異常表型。當中會包括神經嵴細胞特定及上皮特定條件式敲除小鼠。然後，透過單細胞 RNA 測序轉錄組分析，我們會探究 Irx3/5 突變小鼠中的細胞及分子改變，並鑒定 Irx3/5 在咽弓中的潛在轉錄目標和分子信號目標。接着，於第一蒐對咽弓的結構，我們將研究 Irx3/5 在外胚層上皮的功能，包括基板上皮和口部上皮。我們亦會通過類器官培育及突變小鼠，以證實 Irx3/5 在促成外胚層與神經嵴細胞之間的互動之作用。在這研究中，我們將建構出機理模型，以解釋 Irx3/5 促成的咽外胚層上皮與四周神經嵴細胞之間的互動，並解構解構 Irx3/5 在顱面和顎部發育的功能。

14113521.label: Realisation of objectives
14113521.value: Objective 1. To characterize the pharyngeal arch patterning as well as neural crest and epithelial defects of Irx3-/-, Irx5-/-, Irx3/5-/- and conditional Irx3/5-/- knockout mutants We first investigated the patterning defects of the Irx3/5-/- DKO PA1 at E10.5 using proximal marker genes Emx2 and Pou3f3 and found that both genes were absent, suggesting a loss of proximal PA1 in the DKO. To investigate the maxillo-mandibular identity of the mutant, the expression patterns of Dlx1, Dlx3 and Dlx5 were examined. We found that the mandibular gene Dlx5 was expanded to the proximal maxillary arch, Dlx1 domain in the proximal region was reduced, while no observable changes could be detected for the distal mandibular marker Dlx3. Gsc which marks the distal aboral mandibular arch was also unaffected. We concluded that Irx3/5 are required for the patterning of the proximal PA1, and for maintaining the maxillary identity. To gain insight into cellular functions of Irx3 and Irx5, we examined the expression profiles of Irx3 and Irx5 from E9.0 to E10.5. Irx3/5 are expressed in the proximal PA1 epithelium, including the rostral 1st pharyngeal cleft and proximal oral epithelium; but not in the distal PA1 epithelium. Expression could be detected in the PA1mesenchymal core at E9.25 and E9.5. In the neural crest lineages, Irx3/5 were not expressed at E9.5, but could be detected at E10.5 at the aboral region of maxillary and mandibular ectomesenchyme. To delineate the cell type-specific roles of Irx3/5, we generated neural crest-specific Wnt1-CKO (Wnt1-Cre;Irx3f/fIrx5-/-) and epithelium-specific Foxg1-CKO mutants. We found that the Wnt1-CKO displayed mild skeletal phenotype only. The expression of PA1 patterning genes were unaffected, though a mild reduction of Foxl2 and Rarb expression in the maxillary aboral domain could be detected in the Wnt1-CKO at E10.5. Together with the absence of jugal bone in E16.5 Wnt1-CKO, our results suggest that Irx3/5 are required only in a specific subset of neural crest cells. The severe phenotypes observed in the neural crest derivatives of the DKO are not due to the neural crest-specific functions of Irx3/5. On the other hand, we characterized the Foxg1-CKO and found that the mutants displayed partial maxillo-to-mandibular transformation of skeletal structures at E16.5. There was an ectopic expansion of Dlx5 domain to the maxillary process, and a distal-to-proximal expansion of the maxillary Bmp4 expression at E10.5. We concluded that Irx3/5 in the pharyngeal epithelium is essential for PA1 patterning and jaw development. We have fully achieved Objective 1. Objective 2. To investigate the functions of Irx3/5 in PA1 development by single-cell transcriptome analysis To understand the functions of Irx3/5 in specific cell populations of PA1, scRNA-seq experiments were performed. Irx3/5 DKO and wildtype PA1 samples were prepared by dissecting two pairs of PA1 from E10.5 embryos. After sequencing and filtering for high-quality reads, 6,322 wildtype and 5,159 mutant cells were recovered. Using UMAP and Seurat, cell clusters were analysed and annotated using specific marker genes, neural crest cells (8,205 cells) accounted for about 71%, other clusters of epithelial (3,340 cells), endothelial (265 cells) and mesodermal (451 cells) were also identified. The neural crest cells were extracted and further resolved by subclustering. Dlx5 and Dlx6 were used as markers to annotate the maxillary and mandibular subgroups, Pou3f3 and Emx2 for proximal cells, Msx1 and Msx2 for distal cells, Lhx8 and Gsc for oro-aboral cells. We observed a significant reduction of the proximal populations, a large proportion of the maxillary population was absent in the DKO. Importantly, an extra cluster of cells expressing mostly mandibular patterning genes was observed in the DKO. The reduced population of maxillary cells found in the scRNA profiles is consistent with the maxillo-to-mandibular transformation observed in the E16.5 DKO skeletal phenotype. We further analyzed the PA1 epithelial cells in the scRNA-seq dataset. Unbiased subclustering of wildtype cells resulted in subgroups with specific expression of signaling ligands Bmp4, Fgf8, Shh, Aldh1a3, and Sostdc1. We observed a mild increase in proportion of Bmp4 population and a reduction of Sostdc1 population in the DKO, consistent with the Bmp4 domain expansion observed in vivo. This result suggested that elevated Bmp4 in the oral epithelium could be caused by the changes in the proportion of different epithelial populations in the PA1. To understand the gene regulatory network mediated by Irx3/5 in the placodal epithelial cells, we examined the placodal cells (782 WT cells, 830 DKO cells) using SCENIC to predict potential Irx3/5 targets and visualized the gene regulatory network using Cytoscape. Among the predicted targets, we identified Pitx2 and Id2 as the top candidates. However, these two genes did not display differential gene expression in the mutant cells. Given the small number of placodal epithelial cells in our scRNA datasets, there are limitations in the GRN prediction. Nevertheless, Pitx2 is known to be a regulator in craniofacial development by maintaining Fgf8 and repressing Bmp4 expression. We have indeed confirmed the reduction of Fgf8 and expansion of Bmp4 in our in vivo mutant platform as described below. Our Objective on transcriptome analysis has been fully completed. Objective 3. To investigate the functions of Irx3/5 in the oral epithelium, epibranchial placode epithelium, and in mediating ectoderm-neural crest interaction To address the cellular and signaling functions of Irx3 and Irx5 in neural crest and placodal cells, we proposed to use organoid and in vivo mutant platforms. We established placode organoid culture model using human ES cells. We characterized the hESC derived organoids, the induced ectodermal cells were arranged in rings of specific domains containing SOX9+ neural crest cells, SIX1+ placodal cells, GATA3+ non-neural ectodermal cells. However, we considered this organoid model with mixed distributions of different cell types unsuitable for further genetic manipulation for specific gene function analysis. Therefore, we continued with our functional analysis using in vivo mutant model. We investigated the dynamic expression profiles of epithelial signaling ligands in PA1 epithelium. At E9.0, there are two distinct domains of Fgf8: the oral epithelium which persists to E10.5, and the first pharyngeal cleft which is transient and remarkably downregulated from E9.25. In the DKO, the Fgf8 domain in the oral epithelium was comparable to the control. However, Fgf8 at the rostral first cleft could not be detected in the DKO at E9.0, indicating that the local source of Fgf8 at the cleft region was reduced in the absence of Irx3/5. The PA1 epithelium contains two Bmp4 expression domains at the distal maxillary and distal mandibular regions. In the DKO, the maxillary Bmp4 domain was extended proximally at E9.25. The ectopic Bmp4 expression persisted in the maxillo-mandibular junction, while the mandibular Bmp4 domain remained unchanged in E10.5 DKO. We further investigated if the elevated Bmp4 would contribute to PA1 neural crest patterning. In the DKO, the expression of neural crest genes Msx1 and Msx2, the downstream BMP signaling targets were also expanded proximally at E10.5. Moreover, the expression of Sostdc1, a modulator of BMP and WNT signaling, was reduced in E9.5 DKO. Taken together, Irx3/5 in the PA1 epithelium is required to regulate the expression of signaling ligands, which is essential for interacting with the underlying PA1 neural crest cells. We have addressed Objective 3 of this project.

14113521.label: Major findings and research outcome
14113521.value: Irx3/5-/- double knockouts (DKO) displayed facial and jaw malformations. The mutants exhibited the loss of squamous and jugal bones which were derived from the proximal maxillary arch. The maxilla bone was severely affected, with an absence of frontal process but instead acquired the mandibular alveolar ridge and condylar process. The mandible was shortened with defective proximal region, fusion of upper and lower jaw (syngnathia) was observed. These abnormal phenotypes suggest a partial maxilla-to-mandible transformation in the Irx3/5-/- DKO mutant. The results indicate that Irx3/5 are required for neural crest functions in the developing PA1. (Andy Wong, MPhil thesis, 2022) Based on our analysis of neural crest genes by scRNA transcriptome and gene expression patterns, we concluded that Irx3/5 are required for the patterning of the proximal PA1, and for maintaining the maxillary identity. On the contrary, Irx3/5 are not required for the distal maxillary and mandibular arches. The patterning defects in E10.5 PA1 were consistent with the neural crest derived skeletal phenotypes observed in the developing upper and lower jaw of the E16.5 DKO. Using the neural crest-specific Wnt1-CKO, we found that Irx3/5 are required in the neural crest for jaw formation, particularly the maxilla and jugal. From the epithelial-specific Foxg1-CKO, we found that Irx3/5 are required in the pharyngeal epithelium, especially for the maxillary identity. These results support that Irx3/5 in the pharyngeal epithelium are required for PA1 development. (Tong et al, poster presentation in GRC and poster award, 2023) In this project, we show that the PA1 epithelium are regionalized and displayed temporal- and spatial-specific expression of signaling ligands. In PA1 epithelium, Fgf8 domains were reduced in DKO at E9.0, but Bmp4 expression was elevated and expanded to proximal region at E9.5. The Bmp4 downstream targets in the neural crest cells, Msx1 and Msx2, were also expanded in E10.5 DKO. Therefore, Irx3/5 in the PA1 epithelium is required to regulate the expression of signaling ligands, which is essential for interacting with the underlying PA1 neural crest cells. By integrating the data obtained from mouse mutants and scRNA transcriptomes, we have successfully elucidated the roles of Irx3 and Irx5 in proximal maxillary identity and pharyngeal development. The results this study have been summarized as a manuscript for submission to Nature Communications (Tong et al, 2026).

14113521.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14113521.value: 1. We have uncovered that the mammalian pharyngeal epithelium is regionalized into specific domains with characteristic signaling molecule profiles, which is important for positional information and patterning of the underlying neural crest in the developing pharyngeal arch. It remains unclear how the epithelial regionalization is achieved in the developing PA1. We will develop spatial transcriptome and scATAC-seq experiments to help resolve the regulation and function of regional-specific pharyngeal epithelial cells. 2. The Irx genes are evolutionary conserved and have been described as pre-patterning genes, but their roles in the evolution of jaw structures have not been systematically studied. One interesting observation from this study is that the abnormal jaw joint phenotype of the Irx3/5 DKO resembles some jawless vertebrates. The expression of IrxB cluster genes in the pharyngeal epithelium appeared to be associated with the development of jaw structures. We propose that comparative genomics studies with different species could be performed to correlate IrxB gene expression with the development of the jaw, which will shed light on the evolutionary origin of articulated jaw structures.

14113521.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14113521.value: Craniofacial malformation affects not only facial appearance of the patient, but also daily activities such as eating and speech. IRX5 mutation has been identified as the causative gene for Hamamy syndrome, the patients displayed multiple craniofacial defects including small mandible. During embryonic development, the upper and lower jaws are derived from the maxillary and mandibular branches of the first pharyngeal arch (PA1). We have found that Irx3 and Irx5 genes are expressed in the neural crest cells and ectodermal epithelial cells of the developing PA1. By mouse mutant analysis, we show that Irx3/5 genes are required for the development of the proximal PA1 structures, deficiency of both Irx3 and Irx5 led to partial transformation of the maxilla to mandible. Using tissue-specific conditional mouse mutants and single cell transcriptome technologies, we show that Irx3 and Irx5 are essential for pharyngeal epithelial cell functions. Irx3/5 are required to maintain the expression of key signaling factors Bmp4 and Fgf8, which in turn interact with the underlying neural crest cells for proper development of the upper and lower jaws. In this study, we have uncovered the importance of the pharyngeal epithelium and deciphered the developmental mechanism for a human congenital defect.

14113921.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14113921.value: Mitochondria are the primary power generator in eukaryotic cells producing ATP. The oxidative environment within the mitochondria makes them suspectable to oxidative damage. To maintain a healthy mitochondrial pool, eukaryotic cells have evolved multi-layered quality control systems. If the oxidative damage is beyond remedy, the impaired mitochondria are selectively recycled by an autophagic process termed mitophagy. From studies of yeast and metazoan cells, critical players in mitophagy have been identified; however, little is known about mitophagy in plant cells. We do not understand how damaged mitochondria are recognized and sequestered, and the molecular players involved in the process have not been identified. We have established an Arabidopsis system in which we can trigger selective autophagic recycling of mitochondria using uncouplers that dissipate the mitochondrial proton gradient. We confirmed that depolarized mitochondria became associated with autophagy markers, including ATG8 and that the recycling required Arabidopsis Autophagy related genes (ATGs). In electron micrographs, uncoupler-treated root cells have aberrant mitochondria enclosed by autophagosomes. The uncoupler-induced mitophagy led to the ubiquitination of mitochondrial surface and lipidation of ATG8 preceding phagophore assembly in metazoan cells. We have identified a cytosolic protein, Friendly, recruited to mitochondria and colocalized with ATG8 after inducing mitophagy. A family of mitochondrial membrane proteins was polyubiquitinated and became associated with ATG8 upon depolarization stress. In this proposal, we aim to characterize the functions of these proteins in selective mitochondria recycling using correlative light and electron microscopy and molecular biological tools. Mitochondria and chloroplast activities are co-regulated because they are crucial for energy homeostasis in plant cells. We observed that mitochondria in greening cotyledon cells of Arabidopsis were recycled by mitophagy. We hypothesize that mitophagy contributes to the modulation of the mitochondrial pool for the metabolic switch from the heterotrophic to autotrophic phase. We will investigate the developmentally programmed mitochondria recycling in plant cells and compare them with drug-induced mitophagy. My lab has studied mitophagy in C. elegans using combined molecular and structural biology approaches and has identified CPS-6 as a suicide factor that accelerates mitophagy. The PI lab extensive experience with the advanced microscopy techniques necessary for characterizing subcellular processes in plant cells. 14114221.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14114221.value: Trinucleotide repeat disorders are a set of genetic disorders caused by trinucleotide repeat expansion, a kind of mutation where trinucleotide repeats in certain genes or introns exceed the normal threshold. An expansion in the 5ʹ untranslated region of the fragile X mental retardation 1 gene consisting of 55–200 CGG repeats is associated with many disease phenotypes. Fragile X-associated Tremor/Ataxia Syndrome (FXTAS) is a late-onset condition in carriers of premutations in the FMR1 gene. The clinical phenotype of FXTAS includes intention tremor, cerebellar ataxia, memory and/or executive function deficits, psychological disorders, and parkinsonian features. Currently, there is no targeted therapeutic intervention that can arrest or reverse the pathogenesis of FXTAS. Recently, piperine, a bioactive alkaloid obtained from black pepper, demonstrated its strongly interaction with expanded-CGG RNA and can neutralize the cellular toxicity by improving the expanded-CGG RNA associated splicing defects and RAN translation in a FXTAS cell model system. Based on such identified novel effect and efficient brain uptake of piperine and our established treatment strategy for CAG toxicity with CAG expanded RHA inhibitors in R/62 mice since 2011, we hypothesized that the piperine preparations could serve as a potent expanded-CGG RNA inhibitor for the treatment of FXTAS. Since limited solubility of piperine remains to be the main obstacle for exerting its pharmacological action after oral administrations in mice or rats, further optimized piperine formulations with higher drug loading are needed to achieve greater dose ranges for evaluations on its relevant efficacies and toxicities. The current project is proposed aiming to evaluate and validate the therapeutic effect of a further optimized piperine nanoparticle formulation on FXTAS using selected Drosophila and mouse disease models. To achieve such objective, two parts of the experiments are designed including 1) further optimization of the nanoparticle formulation of piperine using flash nanoprecipitation technique; and 2) in-vivo evaluations of the optimized piperine nanoparticle on CGG repeats in transgenic Drosophila model expressing CGG repeats and CGG repeat knock-in mouse model. Our findings are expected to enrich the current drug development for RNA toxicity in repeat expansion disorders to address barriers to the treatment of rare diseases in Hong Kong and beyond. As the member of a recently formed alliance named Nexus of Rare Neurodegenerative Diseases (NRND), our team shall gain access to a global network of top-notch clinicians and biomedical researchers in various related disciplines, as well as patient groups to achieve our common goal of helping patients with rare diseases. 三核苷酸重複異常是由三核苷酸重複擴增引起的一系列遺傳異常，是由某些基因或內含子中的三核苷酸重複超過正常閾值而引起的一種突變。由 55-200 個 CGG 重複組成的脆性 X 精神發育遲滯 1 基因 5ʹ 非翻譯區的擴增與許多疾病表型有關。脆性 X 相關震顫/共濟失調綜合徵 (FXTAS) 是 FMR1 基因前突變攜帶者的遲發性疾病。FXTAS 的臨床表型包括意向性震顫、小腦共濟失調、記憶和/或執行功能缺陷、心理障礙和帕金森病特徵。目前，沒有可以阻止或逆轉 FXTAS 發病機制的靶向治療干預。胡椒鹼是一種從黑胡椒中提取的活性生物鹼，它近來被證明與擴增的 CGG RNA 有很強的相互作用，並且可以通過改善 FXTAS 細胞模型系統中擴增的 CGG RNA 相關的剪接缺陷和 RAN 翻譯來中和細胞毒性。基於此新活性和其有效腦攝取以及我們研究小組自 2011 年以來在 R/62 小鼠中使用 CAG 擴增 RHA 抑製劑建立的CAG毒性治療策略，我們認為胡椒鹼製劑可作為有效的擴增 CGG RNA 抑製劑用於FXTAS的治療。由於胡椒鹼有限的溶解度仍然是其在小鼠或大鼠口服後發揮藥理作用的主要障礙，因此我們需要進一步優化具有更高載藥量的胡椒鹼製劑以實現其更大的劑量範圍，以評估其相關功效和毒性。該項目旨在使用果蠅和小鼠疾病模型評估和驗證進一步優化的胡椒鹼納米顆粒製劑對FXTAS的治療效果。為了實現這一目標，設計了兩部分實驗，包括1）使用快速納米沉澱技術進一步優化胡椒鹼的納米顆粒劑型； 2) 在表達 CGG 重複序列的轉基因果蠅模型和 CGG 重複序列敲入小鼠模型中對優化的胡椒鹼納米顆粒進行進一步的體內評價。我們的研究結果有望豐富當前針對重複擴增障礙中 RNA 毒性的藥物開發，以克服香港及其他地區治療罕見疾病的障礙。作為最近成立的罕見神經退行性疾病（NRND）聯盟的成員，我們的團隊將接觸到各個相關學科的頂尖臨床醫生和生物醫學研究人員以及患者群體的全球網絡，以實現我們的共同目標幫助罕見病患者。

14114621.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14114621.value: 人類活動導致全球氣候變化, 頻發的極端天氣（如熱害）嚴重影響了農作物的產量和質量。目前對植物耐熱性研究主要集中在被認為起主導作用的註釋基因的初級轉錄本。然而，越來越多的證據表明植物在熱脅迫條件下可以發生大量的可變剪切，進而形成不同功能的蛋白。因此，為了進一步了解可變剪切的調控過程，本研究擬利用模式植物擬南芥研究mRNA前體加工蛋白激酶基因 (PRP4Ks) 不同mRNA異構體的功能差異。 PRP4Ks磷酸化剪切體蛋白對組裝剪切體 B 複合物和剪切依賴 PRP4K 的剪切位點至關重要。擬南芥基因組編碼兩個 PRP4K 同源基因, PRP4KA 和 PRP4KB，且突變PRP4K 可以導致植株生長和mRNA 前體剪切的缺陷。本實驗室數據表明，熱脅迫能引起PRP4KA 和 PRP4KB 不同mRNA異構體的差異表達。同時，通過納米孔RNA測序分析，我們也鑑定到PRP4KA 和 PRP4KB註釋外的可能編碼新功能蛋白的mRNA異構體。在此項目中，我們將PRP4KA 和 PRP4KB的mRNA 異構體與天然啟動子或誘導表達系統構建的重組載體分別在已有的擬南芥PRP4KA 和 PRP4KB突變體中表達，以研究其功能差異。本項目將研究PRP4KA 和PRP4KB不同mRNA異構體在熱脅迫過程中對mRNA前體剪切、蛋白組磷酸化和生理響應的作用，以進一步加深我們在轉錄後水平對植物熱脅迫響應的理解。

14114721.label: Co - Investigator(s)

14114721.label: Project Objectives
14114721.value: To evaluate whether behavioral upper-limb muscle synergies factorized from multi-channel electromyographic signals (EMGs) can be independently retrieved by direct electrical stimulation (DES) of specific motor cortical loci, applied during motor mapping for defining the functional motor areas in human patients undergoing awake brain surgery for tumor resection. This evaluation will be achieved by comparing the behavioral and DES-derived muscle synergies. For every DES-derived muscle synergy identified, we will obtain the spatial anatomical distribution of the motor cortical loci whose stimulations would activate the synergy, and examine whether these loci distribute themselves uniformly across a specific motor cortical region. We will compare the distributions of the different synergies to see whether they are organized with a topography that is consistent across subjects. To compare whether the behavioral muscle synergies observed before and after the operation are similar or not, assuming that with intraoperative motor mapping, the extent of resection is defined to minimize loss of motor functions post-op.

14114721.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14114721.value: 我們試圖通過直接刺激正接受清醒腫瘤切除手術病人的大腦闡明人類中樞神經系統如何產生隨意運動。我們將獲得有價值的數據來測試長期存在，但備受爭議的一個科學命題：隨意運動的基本組成部分是人類中樞神經系統中已編碼的肌肉協同。 了解人類中樞神經系統如何控制隨意運動仍然是一個基礎神經科學中的難題。多位研究人員曾建議，為規避運動控制的複雜性，中樞神經系統可能通過預先組織的神經運動模塊組合 （稱為肌肉協同）來激活作為獨立激活單位的特定肌肉群，已協調肌肉命令。這個假設很受歡迎（最近的相關文章發表在 PNAS、Nature Communications 等雜誌上），但其有效性一直被爭論不休。部分原因是迄今為止，我們還沒有令人信服的神經生理學數據可以直接展現編碼在人類中樞神經系統中的肌肉協同。 近期在動物通過刺激中樞神經獲得的數據展示了肌肉協同的神經基礎。受這些實驗的啟發，我們的目標是用類似的策略測試人類的肌肉協同假設。我們問，在運動行為期間觀察到的上肢肌肉協同是否可以通過直接刺激人腦的運動皮層區域來獨立展現。直接的大腦皮層電刺激可以在接受腦腫瘤切除外科手術的病人中實現。在此手術中，神經外科醫生系統地刺激暴露的大腦；清醒的病人於刺激同時從事運動，外科醫生即可確定哪些大腦區域與運動功能相關，並在手術中避免切除哪些區域，病人因此可在術後保留運動功能。這個神經外科手術為解決我們的科學問題提供了一個獨特但高度可行的平台。 在招募的腦癌患者（N=22）中，我們將在清醒腦部手術刺激大腦期間，以及在術前/術後進行的運動期間記錄多肌肉肌電活動。我們將比較隨意運動和大腦刺激誘發的肌肉協同，以評估是否可以通過腦刺激來獨立展現隨意運動中觀察得到協同作用，從而確立它們的神經基礎。對於每個協同，我們也會分析其被激活的皮層位點的空間分佈，已評估它在大腦表面的分佈。我們的數據不僅會解決一個重要的神經科學問題並產生學術影響，也對神經康復，神經外科，以及未來腦機接口的設計有影響。我們還希望通過這研究促進神經科學、神經外科和工程介的交流合作。

14114721.label: Realisation of objectives
14114721.value: We have completely and successfully realized all three objectives stated in the original grant application. OBJECTIVE 1: Comparison of Behavioral and DES-Evoked Muscle Synergies Patients diagnosed with gliomas with no clinically apparent motor functional impairment were recruited (n = 20). All subjects underwent, as part of their treatment plan, an awake tumor resection surgery that necessitated the exposure of at least part of the upper limb region of the primary motor cortex (M1). They also participated in three data recording sessions. In the pre- and post-operative (pre- and post-op) sessions, surface electromyographic signals (EMGs; 12-15 muscles of contralateral arm) were recorded during 10-11 upper limb tasks related to activities of daily living. In the intraoperative session after the brain was exposed, the patient was awakened and asked to stay at rest or perform specific motor tasks as direct electrical stimulation (DES; 2-5 mA, 60 Hz, 1-3 s per trial) was sequentially delivered to multiple cortical loci. This motor mapping procedure, performed under neuro-navigation, permitted the identification of the loci whose stimulations would elicit involuntary muscle responses (“positive” loci), and would be preserved during tumor resection. Surface upper limb EMGs were collected during intraoperative motor mapping. Non-negative matrix factorization (NMF) was then conducted to extract behavioral muscle synergies from the pre- and post-op EMGs, and DES-evoked muscle synergies from the intraoperative EMGs elicited from positive stimulation loci. Of the 20 glioma patients who underwent the above procedure, we identified positive M1 loci in 13 of them, and thus, 7 subjects did not yield any usable intraoperative EMG data. But we found that the data of these 13 subjects were sufficient for us to arrive at statistically significant scientific conclusions. OBJECTIVE 2 - Derivations of the Motor Cortical Map of Activity for Each Muscle Synergy For this objective, for all 13 subjects with usable intraoperative data, we successfully characterized the spatial distribution of the motor cortical loci that activated each muscle synergy, and examined whether these loci followed a specific or consistent topographical organization. A sine qua non for achieving these goals is to obtain the precise anatomical location of each motor cortical locus and reconstruct a standardized brain template that incorporates all stimulation sites across subjects. We developed a multi-platform reconstruction pipeline to systematically map each subject’s stimulated motor cortical loci. Subsequently, a group brain template was generated by co-registering all stimulation loci of all subjects embedded within the reconstructed cortical surfaces to the left hemisphere. With this group brain template, we then reconstructed the synergy activation map for each DES-evoked muscle synergy cluster by assigning each time- and trial-averaged normalized coefficient of each synergy in the cluster to the location of the trial’s corresponding stimulation locus on the template. OBJECTIVE 3 - Comparison of Pre- and Post-operative Behavioral Muscle Synergies Among the 13 subjects with intraoperative EMG data, 4 subjects unfortunately had a very aggressive form of glioma which did not allow them to have a long enough survival time to completely recover from the surgery for the post-operative recordings. We therefore only have pre- and post-operative EMGs from 9 subjects, which was fortunately still sufficient for a meaningful data analysis. We evaluated of the robustness of the extracted behavioral muscle synergies by comparing the pre- and post-operative synergies. Since in all subjects the tissues in the vicinity of the positive loci were spared during tumor resection, none of the subjects reported any noticeable post-operative long term motor functional impairment. We therefore anticipated the pre- and post-operative muscle synergies to be similar. From all subjects, we identified 64 pre-operative and 50 post-operative muscle synergies, categorizable by k-means into 5 pre-operative and 10 post-operative synergy clusters, respectively. Similarity between the pre- and post-operative synergies was then systematically assessed (see below).

14114721.label: Major findings and research outcome
14114721.value: Muscle synergies extracted from multi-muscle electromyographic (EMG) signals are widely interpreted as fundamental building blocks of motor control. Whether EMG-derived muscle synergies represent genuine neurally encoded modules or motor regularities arising from task constraints has been hotly debated. We seek to validate the potential neural origin of upper limb muscle synergies by exploiting direct electrical stimulation (DES) of the primary motor cortex (M1) routinely delivered by neurosurgeons during awake craniotomy surgery for glioma excision (Objective 1). We also analyzed the synergies’ cortical activity maps to reveal their cortical representations (Objective 2). Lastly, we compared the behavioral muscle synergies obtained before and after surgery to validate that the existing neurosurgical routine for glioma excision preserves motor control (Objective 3). OBJECTIVE 1 OUTCOME Across 13 subjects, most pre- and post-op behavioral synergies (59%) could be described well by DES-evoked synergies at both the subject group and individual levels, and some behavioral synergies (10%) could be reconstructed even better by merging multiple paired and/or unpaired DES-evoked synergies. Overall, the DES-evoked synergies could reproduce the behavioral synergies decomposed by NMF successfully, supporting the neural origin of the observed behavioral muscle synergies in human motor behaviors. OBJECTIVE 2 OUTCOME We reconstructed each synergy’s topographical representation over the M1 as an activation map. We observed that the maps of the synergies exhibited intermingling representations across their cortical access points. In addition, we revealed that applying DES to the anterior M1 activates sparser muscle synergies that are distributed more uniformly over the cortex; applying DES to the posterior M1 activates non-sparse muscle synergies that are more localized in their cortical representations. Thus, our findings demonstrate that the human M1 is composed of two functionally distinct subdivisions, each exhibiting a unique pattern of synergy organization. OBJECTIVE 3 OUTCOME From all subjects, we identified 64 pre-op and 50 post-op muscle synergies, categorizable by k-means into 5 pre-op and 10 post-op synergy clusters, respectively. All pre-op clusters could be matched to a post-op cluster with high scalar product (SP) between their cluster centroids (0.94 ± 0.07, mean ± SD), with SP values higher than those from matching the centroids of clusters of shuffled pre- and post-op synergies (0.72 ± 0.11). Thus, we validate that the existing neurosurgical routine for glioma resection is effective in preserving neuromotor control strategies. All results above are described in Xie et al. (2025), currently under review for potential publication in a high-impact journal.

14114721.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14114721.value: Our findings imply that behavioral muscle synergies of the upper limb could be accessed by focal stimulation of the primary motor cortex (M1). This result suggests the following two lines of future research: (1) Here, we used the classic Penfield-type bipolar electrodes to elicit the muscle synergies. This technique has enabled us to obtain a rough topographical activity map of each synergy over M1. It would be even more insightful in a follow-up study to use a finer electrode (e.g., smaller separation distance between the two stimulation ball tips) to produce a map for each synergy with even finer spatial resolution, so that the relationship between the maps of the different synergies can be investigated in more detail. (2) Our result implies that neuronal recordings from human M1 may be deployed to control specific muscle synergies. It would be instructive to record M1 neuronal population activities (from patients during operation, or from animal models) together with multi-muscle EMGs to examine the relationship between M1 neuronal activities and muscle synergy recruitment. Such a study would set the stage for the future development of a brain-controlled robotic arm that generates movement by M1-driven implementation of biomechanical functions associated with specific muscle synergies.

14114721.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14114721.value: Muscle synergies are muscle coordination patterns that are widely interpreted as fundamental building blocks of motor control utilized by the brain to coordinate groups of muscles during movement. But whether muscle synergies represent genuine modules of movement or motor regularities arising from other experimental sources has been hotly debated, because neurophysiological data that definitively demonstrate the neural basis of muscle synergies in humans has been lacking. Here, we seek to validate the potential neural origin of upper limb muscle synergies by exploiting direct electrical stimulation (DES) of the primary motor cortex (M1) routinely delivered by neurosurgeons during awake craniotomy surgery for glioma excision. Across 13 patients, 69% of the muscle synergies observed during pre-operative voluntary behaviors could be matched to DES-evoked muscle synergies or their combination. Analysis of the synergies’ cortical activity maps further revealed that the each muscle synergy had a distinct representation over M1. Our results not only provide direct causal evidence arguing for the neural origin of most behavioral muscle synergies in humans, but also demonstrate the existence of two M1 subdivisions with distinct patterns of muscle synergy organization.
