14115021.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14115021.value: Background: Bipolar affective disorder (BD) is a highly debilitating illness with significant personal distress, suicidality and socioeconomic burden. Depressive symptoms are causing greater disability than mixed/manic symptoms due to their predominance in the course of illness. Circadian disruptions, such as sleep disturbances, change in rest-activity pattern and neuroendocrine functions were often observed in patients with BD. In particular, patients with eveningness, i.e. the circadian preference for a late timing for rest and activity (often described as “night owls”), was associated with a higher depression severity, suicidal risk, and suboptimal efficacy with antidepressant treatment in bipolar depression. Recent meta-analysis reported bright light therapy (BLT) could be an effective adjunctive treatment for non-seasonal bipolar depression with an effect size of around 0.5 when compared to placebo condition. Nonetheless, the small number of controlled trials and the study heterogeneity precluded a solid conclusion on its effectiveness. In addition, the use of BLT has not been tested in the BD patients with eveningness, a supposed worst subtype of patients who might further benefit from circadian-focused treatment. Thus, there is a need to conduct a clinical trial to evaluate the use of adjunctive BLT for bipolar depression patients with eveningness for its treatment efficacy and safety. Aims: We aim to evaluate the efficacy of adjunctive BLT in addition to their maintenance treatment in reducing depressive symptoms. The second aim of the study is to explore the effects of BLT on sleep-wake changes and the sleep disturbances. Method: This is a randomized placebo-controlled trial. Each eligible participant will be randomized to either i) bright light therapy (BLT) or ii) inactive negative ion generator (placebo) treatment for 30-minutes daily at their habitual wake time for a total of six weeks. Subjects will be evaluated at baseline, 2nd, 4th and 6th week. The primary outcome is the change in the 17-item Hamilton Rating Scale of Depression (17-HRSD) from baseline to 6th week. The secondary outcomes included i) the rate and time to achieve response (defined as greater than 50% reduction of 17-HRSD from baseline) and remission (defined as 17-HRSD score of 7 or less) of depression; ii) the change of sleep parameters (from sleep diary and actigraphy) and the change of insomnia score from baseline to 6th week. 輔助光治療對夜晚型躁鬱症患者的隨機對照計劃 背景：躁鬱症不單令病人困擾，增加自殺風險，亦構成一定的社會經濟負擔。因抑鬱症狀在躁鬱症病情中佔更多的時間，所引起的影響也比混合或躁狂症狀更多。晝夜節律紊亂的情況，例如睡眠問題，作息和活動模式以及神經內分泌功能的轉變，在躁鬱症患者身上可以觀察到。特別是「夜晚型」的患者，（即一些喜歡晚睡晚起的「貓頭鷹」），他們有更嚴重的抑鬱症狀和自殺風險，對抗抑鬱藥的治療反應也較差。有研究顯示，對非季節性躁鬱症的抑鬱，強光治療可能是一種有效的輔助治療。儘管如此，現時只有少量研究，數據並未能完全証實光治療的有效性。同時，光治療亦未被應用在患有躁鬱症同時又屬於「夜晚型」的抑鬱患者，他們的病情較差但卻有機會受益於針對生理時鐘的治療。因此，現時有需要透過臨床研究，去詳細評估輔助光治療對「夜晚型」躁鬱症抑鬱的治療效果。 目的：第一是評估輔助光治療對減少抑鬱症狀的效果。第二是探討光治療對睡眠作息規律和睡眠障礙的影響。 方法：這是一項隨機對照計劃。合適的參加者會被隨機分派到光治療組或對照組。光治療組和對照組的參加者每天均會在慣常醒來的時間在家中進行三十分鐘的治療，為期六星期。所有參加者都會在基線、第二、第四和第六星期接受臨床評估。主要量度的治療效果為抑鬱症狀的改善程度，以及達到臨床治癒所需的時間。其次也會評估睡眠時間和失眠症狀的轉變。

14115021.label: Realisation of objectives
14115021.value: The current study aimed to conduct a randomized placebo-controlled trial (RCT) to evaluate the efficacy and safety of adjunctive bright light therapy (BLT) for patients with bipolar depression and eveningness. Adult patients with bipolar disorder who were in a major depressive episode were recruited for 6 weeks of adjunctive BLT with assessments conducted at the pre-treatment baseline, week 2, week 4 and week 6 (end of treatment). The project was impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic when it began in 2022. At that time, subject recruitment and assessment were hampered by social distancing measures. We enhanced recruitment by expanding the study sites to include all three major psychiatric clinics in the New Territories East Cluster. We also conducted proactive pre-screening of the potential cases in the adult psychiatric clinics and had dedicated research staff to station in the clinic for recruitment. We completed recruitment of the planned sample size (N=66). Subjects were randomized to BLT intervention group (N=33), and the sham negative ion generator (NIG) control group (N=33). BLT group received 30mins of BLT via a light box (light box sized 15.7’ H×11’ W× 7.25’D which emits 10 000 lux white light (SunTouch Plus; Nature Bright Company, CA, USA) at the midday. The placebo control group were prescribed exposure to a sham negative ion generator for 30 minutes at the midday. After randomization, 4 subjects (Spontaneous remission =1, Refused to participate further = 3) and 1 subject (Spontaneous remission =1) did not start treatment in the BLT and NIG group, respectively. Thus, 29 and 32 subjects had received the BLT and NIG treatments, respectively. We have anticipated at 30% attrition rate for this study based on our previous BLT RCT among patients with unipolar depression and eveningness. The drop-out rate in this study during the 6-week treatment was low at 7% (2/29) in the BLT and 3% (1/32) in the placebo group, respectively. The completion rate of the 6-week treatment is 93% (57/61), while the completion rate from the time of recruitment is 86% (57/66). Sleep-wake changes measured by the actigraphy and insomnia severity index (ISI) were the secondary outcomes. At baseline, 93% (26/28) and 97% (29/30) subjects in the BLT and NIG group completed the one-week actigraphy. At week 6, 82% (23/28) and 73% (22/30) subjects in the BLT and NIG group completed the one-week actigraphy.

14115021.label: Major findings and research outcome
14115021.value: Thirty-three patients were randomized to the active intervention of BLT group and 33 were randomized to the sham negative ion generator (NIG) control group. Using a modified intention to treat approach by including participants with at least one follow-up assessment, 29 and 32 participants from BLT and NIG groups were analyzed according to the original randomization. The primary outcome is the change of depressive symptoms measured by the 17-item Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (17-HDS). The mean change of 17-HDS scores from baseline to week 6 were -8.5 ± 5.0 and -4.6 ± 7.1 in the BLT and NIG group, respectively. Linear mixed models demonstrated a significant treatment × time interaction effect on the 17-HDS, indicating that the BLT group had a greater reduction in the 17-HDS scores over time compared to the NIG group (F(3, 177)=2.99, p =0.03), adjusted for age, gender and baseline 17-HDS scores. The between-group effect size (Cohen’s d) was 0.74, representing a medium effect. The cumulative remission rate (defined as a 17-HDS score of 7 or below) was 83% and 56% in the BLT and control group, respectively. A survival analysis using the Kaplan–Meier method showed that participants in the BLT group achieved remission earlier (log-rank χ²(1) = 5.0, p = 0.025). The Cox proportional hazard analysis showed a significant higher probability in achieving remission in the BLT group (Exp(B)=1.91, 95% CI: 1.02 – 3.58, p=0.043), adjusted for age, gender, duration of bipolar illness, and baseline 17-HDS scores. The secondary outcomes included the changes of insomnia severity index (ISI) scores and actigraphy sleep parameters. The respective changes of ISI scores were -4.0 ± 4.0 and -1.4± 5.3 in the BLT and control group, respectively. LLM demonstrated a trend towards a significant treatment x time interaction effect on ISI (F(3, 168) = 2.3, p=0.08). There was no significant change in the actigraphic sleep timings, wake after sleep onset (WASO), time in bed (TIB), and sleep efficiency. One participant in the BLT group developed hypomania, which was resolved after reducing BLT to 15 minutes daily. Another control group participant also developed hypomania and dropped out of the study. BLT was otherwise well tolerated with no severe treatment-emergent adverse events as measured by the adverse event checklist. In summary, adjunctive BLT demonstrated superior effects in reducing depressive symptoms with a quicker and higher cumulative remission rate compared to the control group among patients with bipolar depression and eveningness.

14115021.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14115021.value: To our knowledge, this study was the first RCT to provide evidence that adjunctive BLT is efficacious in reducing depressive symptoms and improving remission among patients with bipolar depression and eveningness. Participants in the BLT group were about twice as likely to experience remission during the trial compared with the control group, after accounting for demographic and clinical differences. BLT is well tolerated. With careful monitoring and dose titration, symptoms of hypomanic spontaneously resolved. This study supports that adjunctive BLT can be a useful add-on treatment to improve outcomes in this high-risk population. However, one limitation in this study is the lack of longer term follow up. It would be worthwhile examining the long-term clinical outcomes in future studies, i.e. at post-treatment 1-month and 6-month, to evaluate the sustainability of improvement or relapse upon cessation of treatment. In addition, the use of chronotherapeutic treatment should move towards precision medicine with tailored treatment according to individual characteristics. Based on the sleep, circadian and clinical profiles, further study should also investigate the predictors and clinical phenotypes that would predict a favorable response to BLT. Lastly, a dose-finding study is needed to identify the optimal duration and timings of BLT for each individual.

14115021.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14115021.value: Patients with bipolar depression and an evening chronotype are associated with higher depression severity, suicidal risk, and suboptimal response to antidepressant treatment. This study examined the effects of bright light therapy (BLT) as an add-on treatment to usual psychiatric care in patients with bipolar depression and eveningness (i.e. a tendency for a later timing for activity and rest, the so-called ‘night owls’). The key findings from this study are that BLT of 30 minutes a day for six weeks led to greater reduction of depressive symptoms, quick and higher remission rate than the control group. Participants in the BLT group have a two times higher chances to achieve a remission (minimal symptoms of depression) during the six-week treatment. The completion rate for the six-week treatment is high, and the treatment is well-tolerated. Like other antidepressants, hypomanic symptoms have occurred but had resolve quickly with a dose reduction of BLT. Light therapy is free from drug-drug interaction and has very few contraindications for its use. Given the efficacy and tolerability shown in this study, it supports the integration of BLT into clinical practice to enhance treatment outcomes in patients with bipolar depression and eveningness.

14115321.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14115321.value: Background The traditional standard of systematic 12-core transrectal(TR) biopsy was shown to be inferior to MRI-targeted biopsy in detection of clinically significant prostate cancer (csPCa). Transperineal(TP) systematic prostate biopsy has gained popularity in recent years due to the feasibility of taking more biopsy cores (up to 24 or more cores under local anaesthesia) with better csPCa detection. TP systematic biopsies are simpler and cheaper to perform compared with MRI approach, and a major proportion of biopsies are still performed without MRI guidance. It is unknown whether MRI-guided biopsy approach is superior to extended TP systematic biopsies. Aims and Hypothesis In this proposed study, we aim to compare csPCa diagnosis between MRI-guided biopsy pathway (MRI arm) versus 24-core TP systematic biopsies (TP arm). We hypothesize that MRI-pathway is superior to 24-core TP systematic biopsies. Methods This is a multicentre randomized controlled trial randomizing men with elevated serum Prostate-specific antigen (PSA) 4-20 ng/mL in 1:1 manner to MRI arm or TP arm. In the MRI arm, MRI prostate is performed, and MRI-targeted and 12-core systematic biopsy is performed only if MRI is suspicious. In the TP arm, all men will receive 24-core systematic transperineal prostate biopsy under local anaesthesia without MRI. Primary outcome is proportion of men with clinically significant Prostate cancer, defined as diagnosis of Gleason grade group ≥2 cancer in at least 1 biopsy core. Sample size calculation Pilot study on prospective cohort data was generated from 2 Urology centres involved in this study. The csPCa rates were 32% (MRI arm with 80% abnormal MRI) and 20% (TP arm). Using a superiority design with MRI arm being superior to TP arm, 500 men (250 per group) are required to achieve 80% power, with 5% two-sided Type 1 error and 10% drop-out rate. Timeline and feasibility Facilities for TP and MRI-guided biopsy are available in all 3 centres. Based on local biopsy data in the past 2 years, a total of 20 men can be recruited per month, and the study can be completed in 3 years. Practice-changing potential If MRI approach is found to be superior to extended 24-core systematic biopsy in csPCa detection, the current clinical practice should be changed: MRI approach should replace extended systematic biopsy approach to improve csPCa detection and reduce unnecessary biopsies. 背景 系統性12針經直腸活檢的傳統標準被證明在檢測有臨床意義的前列腺癌方面不如磁共振(MRI)靶向活檢。 由於可安全地抽取更多活檢及具有更好的前列腺癌檢測，在局部麻醉下的經會陰(TP)系統性前列腺活檢近年來越來越受歡迎。與磁共振方法相比，經會陰系統性前列腺活檢更簡單，執行成本更低。如今大部分活檢仍然在沒有 MRI 指導的情況下進行。 MRI 引導活檢是否優於系統活檢尚不清楚。 目標和假設 在這項擬議的研究中，我們旨在比較磁共振引導活檢(MRI 組)與 24針 經會陰系統性前列腺活檢 (TP 組) 之間的有臨床意義的前列腺癌的診斷。 我們假設MRI 組優於 24 針 TP組系統活檢。 方法 這是一項多中心隨機對照試驗，隨機分組前列腺特異性抗原 (PSA) 4-20 ng/mL的男性 以 1:1 的方式到MRI 組或 TP 組。 在MRI 組，將進行 MRI 前列腺掃描，而 MRI 靶向和 12 針系統活檢僅當 MRI掃描有可疑時才進行。 在 TP 組中，所有男性將進行 24針局部麻醉下系統經會陰前列腺活檢。這項研究的主要結果是具有臨床意義的前列腺癌的比例 。 樣本計算 前瞻性數據的試點研究來自參與其中的 2 個泌尿科中心。具有臨床意義的前列腺癌的發生率為 32%（MRI 組，MRI 異常率為 80%）和 20%（TP組）。 採用MRI組優於TP組的優勢設計，這項研究需要500人（每組250人）以達到 80% 的力量，5% 的兩側第一類型錯誤和 估計10%退出率。 時間表和可行性 三個泌尿科中心都提供 TP組 和 MRI組的活檢設施。 基於本地近2年的活檢數據，每月總共可以招募20名男性，這項研究可以在3年內完成。 改變現狀的潛力 如果這項研究發現 MRI 方法優於24 針系統活檢以檢測具有臨床意義的前列腺癌，目前的臨床臨床管理應該改變：應該使用MRI方法以取代系統活檢方法以提高前列腺癌檢測並減少不必要的活檢。

14115821.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14115821.value: It is very common in daily life to perform a physical (or motor) task and a cognitive task at the same time, such as talking while walking or driving, or driving in an unfamiliar area. However, reduced performance in the individual tasks, known as cognitive-motor interference, are almost inevitable when we engage in this kind of multitasking activities. Many brain disorders, including neurodegenerative diseases, multiple sclerosis, stroke and traumatic brain injury are characterized by both motor and cognitive impairments, exposing the patients to a much higher risk when dual cognitive-motor acts are attempted. However, the neurobiological basis underlying cognitive-motor dual-task ability and its weakening in disease conditions are unclear. Despite that valuable information has been obtained from human studies utilizing imaging techniques like fMRI and PET scans, due to the limited spatial and temporal resolution of these techniques in resolving neuronal activities at cellular levels, a clear picture is still unavailable. This project attempts to address this question based on a novel animal model of dual-task behavioral training which allows application of cutting-edge neuroscience research techniques, including 2-photon imaging and optogenetic manipulation. Our preliminary data have convincingly demonstrated the ability of the mouse to perform a motor task and a cognitive task at the same time, and demonstrated the existence of dual-task interference. Based on accumulated knowledge about dual-tasking and our data, we hypothesise that the medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) and the premotor cortex (M2) are critical for this ability. In this proposal, we will 1) optimise and characterise this mouse dual-task model, 2 )explore the active participation of mPFC and M2, and 3) investigate the mechanism and plasticity of cognitive-motor dual-task interference. The results would be useful not only in advancing our understanding of multi-task capability and its limitation, but could also advance the diagnosis and treatment of various neurological conditions. 在日常生活中同時運動任務和認知任務是很常見，例如邊走邊開車邊說話，或者在不熟悉的地方開車。然而，當我們從事這種多任務處理時，單個任務的表現降低，稱為認知運動干擾不可避免。許多腦部疾病，包括神經退行性疾​​病、多發性硬化症、中風和創傷性腦損傷的特點是運動和認知 損傷，當雙重認知運動時使患者面臨更高的風險行為。然而，認知-運動雙重任務背後的神經生物學基礎能力及其在疾病條件下的減弱尚不清楚。儘管利用成像技術從人類研究中獲得信息，例如fMRI 和 PET 掃描，由於它們的空間和時間分辨率有限,在細胞水平上解決神經元活動的技術，清晰的畫面仍然是不可用。這個項目試圖基於一種新的雙任務行為訓練動物模型應用前沿的神經科學研究技術，包括2光子成像和光遺傳學操縱來解決這個問題。我們的初步數據令人信服地證明了小同時執行運動任務和認知任務，並證明雙任務干擾的存在。基於對雙重任務的積累知識和我們的數據，我們假設內側前額葉皮層 (mPFC) 和運動前皮層 (M2) 對這種能力至關重要。在這個提議中，我們將 1) 優化和表徵這種小鼠雙任務模型，2）探索 mPFC 的積極參與和 M2，以及 3) 研究認知運動雙任務的機制和可塑性干涉。結果不僅有助於我們加深對多任務能力及其局限性，但也可以促進診斷治療各種神經系統疾病。

14115821.label: Realisation of objectives
14115821.value: All the three objectives have been realized in full. For objective 1, the team had optimized the cognitive-motor dual-task in the mouse model and characterized in detail the single-task performance as well as dual-task performance, revealing task interference reminiscent to those observed in human. For objective 2, to streamline the work without compromising the objective, we conducted our experiments focusing on an area representing both the mPFC and M2. Detailed long-term tracking of L2/3 neurons by multi-photon imaging was successfully conducted allowing interrogation into their roles in dual-task learning and execution. For objective 3, by a combination of multi-photon imaging, optogenetic manipulation, statistical analysis of population activities and neural network modeling, we investigated the neuronal circuit mechanism and its plasticity in the dual-tasking paradigm, providing insight into the cause of dual-task interference and the computing principle to resolve the challenge.

14115821.label: Major findings and research outcome
14115821.value: Dual-tasking, or the ability to execute multiple activities simultaneously, is crucial for survival in a complex environment. Despite the remarkable adaptability of the human brain and nervous system, our performance often deteriorates when faced with the demands of multiple inputs or outputs, a phenomenon known as dual-task interference. The underlying neural mechanisms of dual-task interference remain largely unknown due to a lack of neurophysiological investigations using neuronal recording and manipulation techniques with high spatiotemporal resolution. To address these questions, we devised a novel dual-task behavioral paradigm in rodent models, where a cognitive go/no-go task was inserted to the middle to a lever manipulation motor task. We found that 1) mice encountered significant interference in the dual-task paradigm; however, this interference was partially alleviated through training. Using two-photon calcium imaging, we tracked neuronal activity throughout the dual-task learning process. Specifically, we focused on the secondary motor cortex (M2) as a representative area in the prefrontal cortex, given its critical role in orchestrating a wide range of cognitive and motor functions. Through this approach, we reveal that 2) M2 corroborated earlier findings of mixed selectivity and overloaded activation in the prefrontal cortex. 3) Moreover, our findings provide direct evidence of resource competition and neural interference between tasks. We observed that the concurrently executed tasks recruited an overlapping group of neurons, which were allocated on a ‘first come, first serve’ basis, that is task-priority, 4) Meanwhile, neural interference also arose from the selective suppression of neurons activated by one task but deemed inappropriate for the other. This neural interference closely mirrored the behavioral interference observed. 5) We found evidence of local circuit reorganization and resource reallocation following training, which together contributed to more distinct task representations in M2 and improved dual-task performance. 6) By modelling learning via a recurrent neural network, we reproduced the behavioral interference and its amelioration via training, which is accelerated by the coordination and segregation strategies revealed by biological data. Collectively, our results provide a compelling example of how parallel information competes for and shares neural resources in the brain and how training resolves conflicts between task representations, leading to a more synergized and organized state for dual-task processing. The principle could be generalized across biological and artificial neural network systems.

14115821.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14115821.value: This project provided insight into the neurobiological basis of why the brain is severely capacity-limited in spite of its impressive complexity and processing power, by revealing fundamental aspects of brain functional architecture and the mechanisms of concurrent information processing. The results represent a significant step towards a deeper understanding of higher-order cognitive control. Moreover, the approach of this study in identifying pivotal areas and examining the effect of training-induced improvement in cognitive-motor dual-task performance is also expected to benefit the normal population as well as patients with cognitive deficits by designing early screening and intervention schemes, hence improves their overall quality of life and lessens the socioeconomic burden on the public health sector. Further research proposals focusing on the translational aspect of the project will be targeted.

14115821.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14115821.value: Navigating dynamic environments often requires the brain to process information from multiple tasks in parallel. Yet, the strategies for resource allocation and their adaptation with practice remain unclear. Here, we combine an original dual-task paradigm in mice with chronic two-photon imaging, optogenetic manipulations, and recurrent neural network models to dissect the underlying cortical mechanisms. We show that interference between tasks arises not only from processing bottlenecks among task-shared neurons but also from active suppression of non-shared populations. Intriguingly, this suppression supports a rapid coordination strategy that enables early dual-task success. With training, performance is optimized by a multi-level reorganization, including the recruitment of specialized neurons and progressive segregation of task representations. Network models implementing these coordination and segregation strategies accelerate dual-task learning, revealing a shared computational principle across biological and artificial neural networks. Together, these findings demonstrate how cortical circuits dynamically redistribute and restructure resources to support parallel task processing.

14116421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14116421.value: Ageing is associated with a decline in physiological reserve, systemic immune derangement and cardiac dysfunction. Based on estimates by the United Nations, the number of people aged 60 years or above is projected to increase by 56% from 2015 to 2030. Due to comorbidities (e.g. frailty, cardiac dysfunction) and recurrent health expenditure (e.g. hospitalisation for heart failure) associated with cardiovascular disease in ageing populations, there is an urgent need to better understand and develop strategies to manage ageing from a novel yet fundamentally solid perspective. Frailty, ageing-related inflammation ('inflammageing'), and cardiovascular complications are common in the older adult population. However, chronological age often does not reflect the biological state of an individual (biological or physiological age). While chronological age remains one of the most powerful determinants and predictors of morbidity and mortality in studies of cardiovascular ageing and frailty, there exists a wide variability in age-related decline in physiological functions, and in the rates and propensity of disease development. Using publicly available DNA methylation data sets from over 8,000 samples and multiple tissue sources, Horvath and colleagues were first to report the use of machine learning algorithms to develop an accurate biological age estimator. This age estimator, or Horvath's epigenetic clock, comprises 353 sets of cytosine and guanosine dinucleotides (CpGs) distributed across the genome, and is estimated to have a median error of only 3.6 years. There exists other epigenetic clocks (e.g. Hannum, Levine) with varying degrees in strength of association with disease phenotypes and chronological age. A number of clock and non-clock CpGs are also associated with chronic diseases. This study aims to 1) compare Horvath's and other epigenetic clocks with chronological age in classifying and predicting frailty, chronic inflammation and cardiac dysfunction (preclinical heart failure), and 2) determine their ability to predict future worsening of cardiac function, increase in frailty, and mortality. 生理儲備下降、免疫系統抗炎功能退化和心臟功能障礙與衰老相關。根據聯合國的推算，60 歲或以上的人口將由2015 年至 2030 年增加 56%。虛弱與衰老相關的炎症（inflammageing）和心血管晚期併發症甚為常見。當我們能夠比實際年齡及一般風險指標評估更準確地預測衰老和併發症風險，我們便可提供更優質的健康和醫療服務。實際年齡（chronological age）往往不能反映人體生理狀態或生理年齡（biological age）。雖然實際年齡仍然是心血管衰老和虛弱研究中發病率和死亡率的最重要預測因素之一，但它與年老相關的生理功能下降以及疾病發展的速率和傾向之間卻存在很大的差異。 DNA 甲基化（methylation）已被證實為相對可靠的生理年齡預測標記，Horvath的表觀遺傳時鐘（epigenetic clock）則為當中最著名和有用的生理年齡估算程式。在這項研究中，我們將以實際年齡、Horvath’s和其他表觀遺傳時鐘於分類和預測虛弱、衰老相關炎症和心臟功能障礙（初期或前心衰竭）方面進行比較，並鑑定它們在預測未來心臟功能惡化、虛弱加劇和死亡率的能力。

14116721.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14116721.value: SRPK2 是磷酸化富含絲氨酸/精氨酸 (SR) 的蛋白質家族並調節前體 mRNA 剪接的主要激酶之一。越來越多的證據表明 SRPK2 還參與其他細胞內的活動，包括細胞週期調節、細胞繁殖和細胞凋亡。 SRPK2 的表達在許多類形的癌症中被錯誤調節，並且與腫瘤遷移有關。為了闡明 SRPK2 在這些事件中的功能，我們 使用CRISPR-Cas9 介導的 SRPK2 基因敲除技術來研究其在 HEK293 和 HeLa 細胞中的影響。我們發現，與 正常表達SRPK2的細胞相比，這些敲除SRPK2的細胞表現出上皮間質轉化 (EMT) 的特徵並增加了細胞運動性。我們還確定了可能調節這些細胞活動的 SRPK2-acinusS-cyclin A1-WT1 通路。然而，我們 發現SRPK2 在上皮間質轉化和細胞遷移中的作用與先前的結果相反，即 敲低SRPK2 抑制了幾種癌症的發展和轉移。因此，我們假設 SRPK2 在癌症轉移中的功能可能具有細胞類型和/或組織特異性。 在本提案中，我們將首先嘗試確認 SRPK2-acinusS-cyclin A1-WT1 通路是否直接調節 HeLa 和 HEK293 細胞的 上皮間充質轉化、細胞遷移和潛在侵襲性。 然後，我們將通過 CRISPR-Cas9 系統構建各種 SRPK2基因敲除的細胞系，分別比較 SRPK2 在宮頸和結腸癌的不同類型細胞中的作用，以確定 SRPK2 在癌症轉移中的功能是否具有細胞類型和 /或組織特異性。 最後，我們將嘗試解析SRPK2 與 acinusS 複合物的結構。 獲得的結構信息將大大增強我們對 SRPK 結合和磷酸化非 SR 底物的機制的理解。 在 SRPK2 被證明在不同形式癌症的轉移中發揮相反作用的情況下，其結構可以為開發對抗某些轉移性癌症的療法提供結構基礎。

14117221.label: Project Objectives
14117221.value: Investigate the roles of circHomer1 in dendritic spine maintenance and synapse composition. This will characterize the expression profile and subcellular localization of circHomer1, and examine the effects of circHomer1 knockdown on dendritic spine morphology and synaptic proteins expression. Examine the roles of circHomer1 in neuronal functions in vivo in the context of a hippocampus-dependent spatial learning task. This will involve the use of specific molecular probes to track the trafficking and expression of different target proteins in vivo using two-photon imaging. Magnified analysis of proteome (MAP), a novel tissue expansion technology, will also be used to visualize synaptic proteins at super-resolution level. This will also involve the use of mini-endoscope to image calcium transients of GCamp6-expressing hippocampal neurons in awake freely behaving mice.

14117221.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14117221.value: 神經元回路受到經驗驅動的變化的影響，導致神經元調整其功能連接和反應。每個神經元接收並綜合來自眾多來源的輸入，並生成相關輸出。樹突棘是興奮性突觸的位置。位於樹突棘上的突觸可以根據經驗經歷動態變化，從而支持包括學習和記憶在內的基本大腦功能。重要的是，突觸缺陷是引起各種神經發育障礙和神經退行性疾病的公認原因。在這項提案中，我們將研究環狀RNA（CircRNA）的潜在作用，這是一類通過前體mRNA的反分裂在樹突棘維持和突觸功能中產生的新興調控性非編碼RNA。最近的研究强烈表明，腦組織中存在大量的環狀RNA。然而，對於CircRNA在樹突棘和突觸功能中的作用知之甚少。我們將關注circHomer1，一種源自Homer1基因的突觸circRNA。我們假設circHomer1通過調節突觸蛋白和表面受體表達在突觸信號傳導中發揮關鍵作用。該項目將利用體外和體內範例的優勢進行結構和功能分析。通過採用包括活體微型內窺鏡成像方法、雙光子成像和組織擴張科技在內的尖端科技，我們將：1）研究circHomer1在動物神經元樹突棘維持中的作用，2）研究circHomer1如何調節突觸蛋白和表面受體的表達，3）確定circHomer1在依賴性空間學習任務中在體內神經元功能中的作用。該提案的總體目標是為理解突觸調節的新機制提供關鍵資訊，並最終為治療神經系統疾病的治療策略提供見解。

14117321.value: 脲酶含鎳，是幽門螺桿菌感染人類，導致消化性潰瘍和胃癌的毒力因子。該病菌在胃中的存活依賴脲酶水解尿素成氨以中和胃酸。活性脲酶的產生須將鎳離子傳遞到活性位點的氨基甲酰賴氨酸殘基上。由於鎳是屬Irvine-Williams 系列頂部具競爭性的離子，能取代較弱的離子（如鎂離子）以抑制細胞內的酶，因此其游離濃度受到嚴格調控以避免毒害細胞。細胞須通過蛋白質之間特定的相互作用，將鎳離子從一個蛋白質轉移到另一個蛋白質，以防止將游離有毒的鎳離子釋放到細胞中。脲酶成熟途徑中有四種脲酶輔助蛋白 （或金屬伴侶蛋白）即 UreD、UreE、UreF 和 UreG — 鎳離子從 UreE 傳遞到 UreG， 在UreF/UreD 的幫助下，再從 UreG 傳遞到脲酶。 UreG 通過形成 UreE2G2 複合物從UreE接收其鎳離子。該複合物僅在 UreG 的 GTP 結合狀態下形成，而不在 GDP 結合狀態下形成。 UreE 如何識別 UreG 的 GTP 結合狀態以及 UreE2G2複合物的形成如何促進鎳轉移目前尚不清楚。 (1) 為了理解這個過程，我們首先建議測定 UreE2G2 複合物的晶體結構。為了證明其可行性，我們已經獲得了 UreE2G2 複合物的晶體。我們已收集到 3.8 Å 分辨率的衍射數據集，並解決了鎳結合的 UreE2G2 複合物的初步結構。我們將進一步優化結晶體，以獲得含鎳和不含鎳的高分辨率UreE2G2 複合物結構。 (2) 從結構所推測的結論將通過誘變和功能測定進行驗證。基於UreE2G2 複合物的初步結構，我們已發現了幾個保守的殘基可能對 UreE2G2 複合物的形成和尿素酶成熟中的鎳傳遞重要。我們將通過定點誘變創測試它們在 UreE-UreG 相互作用和脲酶成熟中的作用。 (3) UreE從上游的氫化酶成熟因子 HypA 接收鎳。對UreE 如何與 HypA 相互作用形成 HypA/UreE2 複合物以促進鎳的輸送，我們知之甚少。我們假設 UreE 的保守鹼性殘基與 HypA 的保守酸性殘基相互作用。針對這一假設，我們將創建 UreE 和 UreA 的電荷逆轉突變體，並測試它們在 HypA-UreE 相互作用和脲酶成熟中的作用。

14117421.label: Project Objectives
14117421.value: We propose to conduct a prospective, international, multi-centre, registry study on the use of ERBT for patients with bladder tumours. We aim to investigate the safety, technical feasibility, oncological outcomes, and hence the generalisability of ERBT in a real world setting. The primary outcomes are the complete tumour resection rate and recurrence-free survival for NMIBC. Secondary outcomes include the proper staging rate for NMIBC and MIBC, complete tumour resection rate for MIBC, successful ERBT rate, circumferential resection margin, deep resection margin, presence of detrusor muscle in the specimen, pathological findings on second look TURBT, occurrence of obturator reflex, operative time, rate of immediate post-operative intravesical chemotherapy instillation, need of bladder irrigation, hospital stay, 30-day complications and progression-free survival for NMIBC following ERBT. Based on the robust results from our on-going randomised controlled trial, together with this registry study providing data in real world setting, we believe we will be able to establish ERBT as the new standard in treating bladder cancer.

14117421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14117421.value: 背景 經尿道膀胱腫瘤整塊切除術 (ERBT) 已被提議為一種簡單但優於傳統逐塊切除術的技術。這技術能把膀胱腫瘤標本保持完整以進行適當的組織學評估及確定陰性切緣。我們針對小於三厘米膀胱腫瘤的 ERBT 多中心隨機對照試驗初步結果非常理想。在這個項目中，我們建議對 ERBT 進行全球數據庫研究，以提供ERBT在現實世界中的數據。 目標和假設 本研究旨在調查 ERBT 在現實世界中的安全性、技術可行性、腫瘤學結果以及其普遍性。我們假設 ERBT 是一種安全且技術上可行的手術，可以在現實世界中達到理想的腫瘤學結果。 方法 這是一項有關 ERBT 治療膀胱腫瘤患者的前瞻性、國際性、多中心全球數據庫研究。這項研究會納入被診斷患有膀胱腫瘤並計劃接受 ERBT 的患者。主要結果是非肌肉浸潤性膀胱癌 (NMIBC) 的完全腫瘤切除率和無復發生存期。次要結果包括 NMIBC 和肌層浸潤性膀胱癌 (MIBC) 的正確分期率、MIBC 的完全腫瘤切除率、 ERBT的技術成功率、環週切除邊緣、深部切除邊緣、逼尿肌抽取率、二次經尿道膀胱腫瘤切除術 (TURBT) 的病理結果、閉孔反射發生率、手術時間、術後膀胱內化療灌注率、膀胱沖洗的需要、住院時間、30 天內的並發症和 NMIBC的無進展生存期。 研究對象數目、時間表和可行性 在這項研究中，我們計劃招募 2,000 名研究對象。我們預計至少有 50 個中心加入這項研究，而每個中心需要納入 40 個研究對象。我們預計會在 20 個月內完成招募，即每個中心每月需要納入兩個研究對象。到三年資助期結束時，我們將能夠提供 有關ERBT 後一年復發率和一年進展率的結果。 未來的研究 基於我們正在進行的隨機對照試驗的穩健結果，再加上這項提供現實世界數據的全球數據庫研究，我們相信能夠把ERBT 確立為治療膀胱癌的新標準。

14117421.label: Realisation of objectives
14117421.value: Objective 1: We propose to conduct a prospective, international, multi-centre, registry study on the use of ERBT for patients with bladder tumours. This objective is fulfilled. In this prospective ERBT registry, initially we planned to recruit 2000 patients in total, but in the end, we recruited 2630 patients globally. The results we achieved are far exceeding what we have originally planned for. Objective 2: We aim to investigate the safety, technical feasibility, oncological outcomes, and hence the generalisability of ERBT in a real world setting. This objective is fulfilled. Initially we planned to recruit 2000 patients in total, but in the end, we recruited 2630 patients globally proving that this procedure is highly generalisable. The overall any-grade complication rate was 8.6% and grade 3 or above complication rate was 1.8%, demonstrating that ERBT has an excellent safety profile. Objective 3: The primary outcomes are the complete tumour resection rate and recurrence-free survival for NMIBC. This objective is fulfilled. Among the 2630 patients being included, the recurrence-free survival was 84% at one year which is very high compared to conventional transurethral resection of bladder tumour (TURBT). The complete tumour resection rate as evidenced by a negative second-look TURBT pathology was 67%. Objective 4: Secondary outcomes include the proper staging rate for NMIBC and MIBC, complete tumour resection rate for MIBC, successful ERBT rate, circumferential resection margin, deep resection margin, presence of detrusor muscle in the specimen, pathological findings on second look TURBT, occurrence of obturator reflex, operative time, rate of immediate post-operative intravesical chemotherapy instillation, need of bladder irrigation, hospital stay, 30-day complications and progression-free survival for NMIBC following ERBT. This objective is fulfilled. The proper staging rates were 97% for NMIBC and 82% for MIBC. The complete tumour resection rate for MIBC was 23%. The successful ERBT rate was 97%. The clear resection margin rate was 85%. Presence of detrusor muscle was achieved in 77% of the cases. Upon second-look TURBT, urothelial tumour was found in 34% of the cases. 5.6% of the patients experienced obturator reflex during ERBT. The rate of immediate post-operative intravesical chemotherapy instillation was 40%. 63% of the patients had bladder irrigation following ERBT. The median hospital stay was 2 days. The overall any-grade complication rate was 8.6% and grade 3 or above complication rate was 1.8%. The progression-free survival was 1.3% at one year. Objective 5: Based on the robust results from our on-going randomised controlled trial, together with this registry study providing data in real world setting, we believe we will be able to establish ERBT as the new standard in treating bladder cancer. This objective is fulfilled. Our study showed that ERBT is safe, technically feasible and generalisability in a multi-centre, real-world setting. The recurrence-free survival was 84% at one year which is very high compared to conventional TURBT. With our years of hard work, ERBT has been adopted in the European Association of Urology guidelines recommending that ERBT should be considered as the first-line treatment for patients with bladder tumours.

14117421.label: Major findings and research outcome
14117421.value: The Global ERBT Registry was contributed by 74 institutions from 27 countries. The primary outcomes were the complete tumour resection rate and recurrence-free survival for NMIBC. Secondary outcomes included the proper staging rate for NMIBC and MIBC, complete tumour resection rate for MIBC, successful ERBT rate, clear resection margin rate, presence of detrusor muscle, pathological findings on second look TURBT, occurrence of obturator reflex, operative time, rate of immediate post-operative intravesical chemotherapy, need of bladder irrigation, hospital stay, 30-day complications and progression-free survival for NMIBC. A total of 2630 patients were recruited The median age was 69 years. The median tumour size was 1.7 cm. The median number of tumour was 1. 80% were primary tumours, and 65% had single tumour. The majority of the patients had right lateral wall (31%), left lateral wall (31%) and posterior wall (19%) tumours. The technical success rate of ERBT was 97%. The median operative time was 30 min. 5.6% of the patients experienced obturator reflex during ERBT. Single-dose intravesical chemotherapy was instilled in 40% of the patients. 63% of the patients had bladder irrigation following ERBT. The median hospital stay was 2 days. The overall any-grade complication rate was 8.6% and grade 3 or above complication rate was 1.8%. The most common grade 3 or above complications were haematuria and bladder perforation. 91% of the patients had urothelial carcinoma, and among them, 96% were non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC). Among those with NMIBC, clear resection margin was achieved in 85% of them. The detrusor muscle sampling rate was 77%. Upon second-look TURBT, urothelial tumour was found in 34% of the cases. The complete tumour resection rate as evidenced by a negative second-look TURBT pathology was 67%. The proper staging rates were 97% for NMIBC and 82% for MIBC. The complete tumour resection rate for MIBC was 23%. The progression-free survival was 1.3% at one year. Upon multivariable analyses, recurrent (HR 2.12, 95% 1.52-2.94), multiple (HR 1.39, 95% 1.03-1.89), and high-grade tumours (HR 1.44, 95% 1.03-2.02) were associated with disease recurrence; T1 disease (HR 11.1, 95% 1.35-90.3), and presence of CIS (HR 3.99, 95% 1.31-12.1) were associated with disease progression. In conclusion, the Global ERBT registry demonstrated that ERBT was safe, technically feasible and highly generalisable, supporting its wider adoption globally. ERBT could achieve excellent oncological outcomes in NMIBC patients. We also identified the factors that were associated with disease recurrence and progression following ERBT.

14117421.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14117421.value: With the large dataset from the global ERBT registry, we will be able to perform propensity-score matching and comparative analyses to define the management alongside ERBT. We have prioritised 10 research questions to be answered: 1. To define the optimal case selection for ERBT. 2. To investigate the best energy modality for ERBT. 3. To define the value of enhanced imaging in addition to ERBT. 4. To define whether routine biopsy of tumour base and tumour edge is needed after ERBT. 5. To define the indication and efficacy of single-dose intravesical instillation of chemotherapy after ERBT. 6. To determine the indication of second-look TURBT after ERBT. 7. To define the indication and optimal regimen of intravesical maintenance chemotherapy after ERBT. 8. To define the indication and optimal regimen of intravesical BCG therapy after ERBT. 9. To determine the optimal surveillance protocol after ERBT. 10. To develop new prognostic scoring models for patients who underwent ERBT. The study results will be extremely valuable paving the management pathway of bladder cancer patients undergoing ERBT. We look forward to producing more important publications in the future.

14117421.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14117421.value: En bloc resection of bladder tumour (ERBT), i.e. removal of bladder tumour in one piece, is a potentially superior technique in treating patients with bladder cancer. In this project, we launched the Global ERBT Registry and collected data from 2630 patients who underwent ERBT globally. The peri-operative outcomes were promising and comparable to conventional transurethral resection of bladder tumour. The overall complication rate was 8.6%, and the rate of major complications was only 1.8%, demonstrating that ERBT has an excellent safety profile. Among the patients with non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer, the recurrence-free survival at one year was 84%, and the progression-free survival rate at one year was 1.3%. These oncological results were very promising compared to conventional transurethral resection of bladder tumour. In summary, we found that the ERBT was safe, technically feasible and generalisable in a real-world setting. In addition, oncological outcomes including disease recurrence and progression were promising following ERBT. The Global ERBT Registry also formed a strong foundation for conducting further ERBT-related research work in the future.

14119721.value: 增強青少年特發性脊柱側彎支架治療效果之混合支架治療方案：一個隨機對照研究項目

14119721.label: Co - Investigator(s)

14119721.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14119721.value: This is a prospective randomized controlled trial investigating the therapeutic effect of the Hybrid Bracing Protocol(HyBP) over the Conventional Brace in enhancing In-brace Correction(IBC) for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis(AIS). Scoliosis is a complex three-dimensional spinal deformity and AIS is the commonest with a high prevalence of 2-4%. If left untreated, AIS can progress resulting in significant health problems including back degeneration and negative body images. Bracing, such as Underarm Brace(UAB) used in our center, is indicated for skeletally immature patients with Cobb angle>20°. Another bracing system is a nighttime Lateral Bending Brace(LBB) designed in a bending position opposite to the convexity of the curve thus resulting in its overcorrection. If AIS becomes severe despite bracing, ultra-major surgery is indicated aiming at bony fusion of the deformed segment with instrumentation. It is therefore important to maximize treatment effectiveness with bracing to control curve progression and to avoid the need for surgery. In-brace Correction(IBC) is the percentage reduction in Cobb angle with bracing. Studies have reported IBC is an important determinant of brace effectiveness. For enhancement of IBC, we put forward the Hybrid Bracing Protocol(HyBP) combining the use of daytime UAB and nighttime LBB. To be best of our knowledge, HyBP has never been reported in the literature. Our pilot study on 8 patients treated with HyBP and 8 Cobb-matched historical controls treated with fulltime UAB showed very promising results with IBC of 42.1±22.0% and 22.1±14.9% in the HyBP and control group respectively. We therefore propose a formal prospective rater-blinded randomized controlled trial on 120 skeletally immature AIS female subjects with single thoracolumbar or lumbar curve newly prescribed with bracing. They are randomly allocated to the HyBP Group or the Conventional Brace Group (CB Group). The primary objective is to determine if the HyBP Group has better treatment effect in terms of In-brace Correction (IBC) when compared with the CB group at 3-month and 18-month after bracing. This is a 3-year study proposal representing the first phase of a project, to be followed by the second phase of the project when all subjects of the entire cohort will be assessed on curve outcome at time of completion of bracing and at 2 years post-bracing. This study will carry significant clinical impacts in that, if proven useful, the HyBP can be used for enhancement of treatment outcomes with bracing, thus preventing the scoliotic spine from deterioration and to avoid the need for surgery. 這是一項前瞻性隨機對照研究，旨在分析混合支架治療方案 (HyBP) 相對於傳統支架治療在增強青少年特發性脊柱側彎 (AIS) 的支架矯正率(IBC) 方面的治療效果。脊柱側彎是一種複雜之三維脊柱畸形，AIS最為常見，患病率高達 2 至 4%。如不及時治療，AIS 可會惡化，導致嚴重健康問題，包括背部退化和負面身體形象。支架治療如我們中心慣常使用之傳統矯形支架（UAB），適用於 Cobb角度 > 20° 之骨骼未成熟患者。另一種支架治療系統是獨立之夜用侧屈矯形支架（LBB），其設計特色在與脊柱側彎曲線凸度相反之彎曲型態，從而強化支架矯正率。若接受支架治療而脊柱側彎仍持續惡化，患者需要接受複雜及高風險之超大型手術，手術目的是利用器械及植入物將畸形脊柱節段融合。有見及此，有效之支架治療十分重要，以便控制側彎惡化並避免高風險手術。支架矯正率 (IBC) 是矯形支架治療期間患者Cobb角度減少的度數佔接受矯形支架治療前Cobb角度的百分比。研究顯示 IBC 是矯形支架療效之重要決定因素。為了增強IBC，我們提出結合使用白天UAB和夜用LBB的混合支架治療方案（HyBP）。文獻顯示從未有研究HyBP或相關之報告。我們為八 名接受 HyBP 治療之患者和八名接受全日UAB 治療Cobb角度-匹配之历史对照组患者作前导對照之研究顯示效果十分良好，HyBP 和對照組之 IBC 分別為 42.1±22.0% 和 22.1±14.9%。我們因此建議對 120 名骨骼未成熟並患有胸腰彎型或腰彎型脊柱側彎及即將開始接受矯形支架治療之 AIS 女性患者進行一項正式的前瞻性評價者盲法隨機對照研究。患者會被隨機分配到 HyBP 治療組或傳統矯形支架治療組（CB 組）。研究目的在確定配帶矯形支架後3 個月和後 18 個月，與 CB 組相比，HyBP 組在支架矯正率 (IBC) 方面是否有更好之療效。這是一項為期 3 年之研究提案，代表整項研究計劃之第一階段，隨後之第二階段將在完成矯形支架治療和兩年後評估所有受試者脊柱側彎嚴重程度。這項研究有重要臨床意義,若證明HyBP有更好療效，則可廣泛應用以防止脊柱側彎惡化並避免高風險之手術。

14120621.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14120621.value: 免疫檢查點阻滯劑療法（ICB）改變了包括肝細胞癌（HCC）在内的實體惡性腫瘤的治療格局，肝細胞癌位列致命癌症的排名前三位，也是全球第六常見癌症。雖然ICB對HCC的治療在近期臨床試驗中已取得了前所未有的成功， 但是在非炎症性腫瘤中，抗程序性細胞死亡蛋白1（anti-PD-1）的治療效果受到了細胞毒性T淋巴細胞浸潤不足的限制，其有效性僅在少數肝細胞癌患者中體現(15-23%). 最新的研究表明腫瘤微環境（TME）中特定骨髓系來源的亞群細胞是關鍵阻礙， 所以與標靶藥物合并用藥是提高免疫檢查點阻滯劑療法療效的一個方向。我們最近的研究發現，在肝細胞癌臨床前研究模型中，靶向髓源性抑制细胞 (MDSC)的扩增可以逆轉免疫抑制性的腫瘤微環境，進而加强anti-PD-L1介導的抗腫瘤T細胞反應（Nat Commun 2018；Gut 2018；2020）。儘管MDSCs在腫瘤相關免疫細胞間網絡調節的作用已經明確， 但由於缺乏對髓源性抑制细胞在PD-L1/PD-1阻滯劑療法中的抑制性作用及機制的清晰認識，完全剋服免疫檢查點阻滯劑療法的原發性耐藥問題仍然具有挑戰性。 爲了探索ICB治療后的免疫細胞藍圖，我們對來自23名HCC患者的39份腫瘤活檢組織進行了單細胞RNA測序。這些患者來自正在進行中的II 期临床研究 (NCT03419481)，他們接受了PD-1阻滯劑療法。我們對超過150,000個免疫細胞譜的初步分析表明，細胞和分子適應性可以指導臨床治療效果，其中CD14+MDSC樣細胞簇的積纍與CD8+T細胞呈負相關，并且在所有對PD-1治療無反應的患者中持續存在。我們已經確定了該髓系亞群細胞的已知和新的特徵基因，而且我們用離體的人類CD14+單核細胞分化來源的MDSC模型進行了驗證，這些特徵基因的擴增可能受到增强子激活的調節。此外，我們通過使用PD-L1/PD-1阻滯劑在原位移植的HCC細胞小鼠腫瘤模型中進行重複篩選，重現了ICB原發性耐藥的臨床情況。與人類HCC一致，ICB耐藥性的小鼠的腫瘤浸潤細胞中展現出與緻瘤性呈正相關的MDSC持續上調。基於這些初步發現，我們提出假設，增强子重塑可能會消除髓源性抑制细胞屏障，從而恢復抗腫瘤T細胞應答以剋服原發性ICB耐藥。這些發現將揭示新的腫瘤免疫逃逸的表觀遺傳機制。我們還將使用ICB耐藥小鼠模型探究正在進行臨床試驗的溴結構域抑制劑的治療效果。我們的這項研究將有潛力為HCC患者提供新的表觀遺傳聯合免疫療法。

14120621.label: Realisation of objectives
14120621.value: For Aim 1, we have delineated several epigenetic mechanisms regulating immunosuppressive myeloid cells in tumor immune evasion of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) based on the following findings: 1) Massive expansion of immature and suppressive myeloid cells is a common feature of malignant solid tumors. Using both orthotopic and transgenic mouse models, we showed that cell cycle-related kinase (CCRK) activates STAT3/E4BP4 signaling in polymorphonuclear myeloid-derived suppressor cells (PMN-MDSCs) to acquire immunosuppressive activity through transcriptional IL-10 induction and IL-12 suppression. Since CCRK can transactivate the expression of the histone H3 lysine 27 methyltransferase EZH2, which in turn may phosphorylate STAT3, this epigenetic pathway plays a key role in MDSC immunosuppression while inhibiting the matured myeloid phenotype. 2) scRNA-seq analysis of immune-checkpoint blockade (ICB)-resistant HCC tumors revealed significant gene enrichments in lipid metabolism and peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma (PPARγ) signaling pathway, which transactivates VEGF-A to promote MDSC immunosuppression. Palmitic acid could dose-dependently increase PPARγ mRNA expression in the ICB-resistant tumor cells, which exhibited lower PPARγ methylation level, thus indicating DNA hypomethylation-driven PPARγ up-regulation. This study suggested that lipid exposure may epigenetically up-regulate PPARγ transcription in the development of anti-PD-L1 resistance. For Aim 2, we have elucidated the functional role of immunosuppressive myeloid cells in multiple ICB-resistant HCC mouse models: 1) Our cross-species analysis has identified protein phosphatase 1 regulatory subunit 15A (PPP1R15A) as a therapeutic target governing the anti-T-cell activities of fibrosis-associated monocytic MDSCs (M-MDSCs). Knockdown of PPP1R15A suppresses M-MDSC functionality to restrict HCC growth and enhance ICB efficacy in an established clinically-relevant ICB-resistant HCC mouse model induced by carbon tetrachloride. Notably, suppression of PPP1R15A also reduces the immunosuppressive potential of fibrotic HCC patient-derived M-MDSCs. Moreover, a PPP1R15A+M-MDSC signature correlates with poor prognosis and immunotherapy unresponsiveness in patients with cancer. 2) scRNA-seq analysis in anti-PD-1-treated patients revealed that the proportion of macrovascular-like endothelial cells (MaVEC) highly expressing disorganization signatures was significantly higher in non-responders when compared to responders. Bromodomain-containing protein 4 (BRD4) was significantly highly expressed in MaVEC compared to liver-sinusoidal endothelial cell (LEC) in both patients and the orthotopic ICB-resistant mouse model. Notably, a clinically-trialed BRD4 specific inhibitor AZD5153 synergized with PD-L1 antibody to suppress tumor growth and ameliorated immunosuppressive microenvironment, which was accompanied by significant reduction and increase in MaVEC and LEC densities, respectively.

14120621.label: Major findings and research outcome
14120621.value: Although ICB has yielded impressive results in cancer patients, resistance to ICB therapies has increasingly been observed (Cheng, Gut 2022). Taking HCC as an example, accumulating evidence has demonstrated that MDSC accumulation in peripheral blood or tumor tissues is associated with poor prognosis and immunotherapy resistance in patients. Therapies that target MDSC to relieve immune suppression therefore represent promising strategies to better control HCC. The findings of this project underline the importance of the newly identified epigenetic and transcriptional drivers of PMN-MDSCs and M-MDSCs, respectively, in HCC tumor microenvironment (TME). Beyond tumor-intrinsic oncogenicity, we demonstrated that CCRK is upregulated in myeloid cells in tumor-bearing mice and in patients with HCC. Intratumoral injection of Ccrk-knockdown PMN-MDSCs increased tumor-infiltrating CD8+T cells and suppressed HCC tumorigenicity. Using an indel mutant transgenic model, we showed that Ccrk inactivation in myeloid cells may epigenetically confer a mature phenotype via STAT3/E4BP4 signaling, driving Th1 responses and CD8+T cell cytotoxicity to reduce orthotopic tumor growth and prolong survival. Our findings unravel mechanistic insights into MDSC-mediated immunosuppression and offer a therapeutic kinase-target for cancer immunotherapy (Zhou et al., iScience 2023). On the other hand, we uncovered over-expression of PPP1R15A, a myeloid cell-enriched endoplasmic reticulum stress modulator, in human M-MDSCs that correlated with poor prognosis and ICB non-responsiveness in patients with HCC. Blocking TGF-β signaling reduced PPP1R15A expression in M-MDSCs, whereas treatment of monocytes by TGF-β upregulated PPP1R15A, which in turn promoted ARG1 and S100A8/9 expression in M-MDSCs and reduced T-cell proliferation. Consistently, lentiviral-mediated knockdown of Ppp1r15a in vivo significantly reduced ARG1+S100A8/9+M-MDSCs in fibrotic liver, leading to elevated intratumoral IFN-γ+GZMB+CD8+T cells and enhanced anti-tumor efficacy of ICB. Notably, pharmacological inhibition of PPP1R15A by Sephin1 reduced the immunosuppressive potential but increased the maturation status of fibrotic HCC patient-derived M-MDSCs, representing a novel potential target for therapies (Liu et al., JHEP Reports 2024). To achieve the objectives of this project, we have generated ICB-resistant hepatoma through repeated in vivo selection using anti-PD-(L)1 antibody in orthotopic-grafted murine model or chemical-induced fibrosis-associated model and analyzed the expression levels of related genes in patients with HCC (Liu et al., Molecular Therapy 2023; Xiong et al., Gut 2023). By integrating both tumor cell biology and immunology, our results demonstrated that the epigenetic drivers such as BRD4 and histone deacetylases are exploitable druggable targets to overcome immunotherapy resistance in HCC (Chen et al., Gut 2023 abstract; Tu et al., Gut 2024).

14120621.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14120621.value: Our cross-species analyses using ICB-resistant mouse models and patient specimens from clinical trials have emphasized the crucial roles of CCRK+PMN-MDSCs and PPP1R15A+M-MDSCs in immunosuppressive TME and ICB resistance of HCC. The results from the preclinical models showed that specific inhibition of CCRK or PPP1R15A can break the immunosuppressive barrier to restrict HCC growth and enhance the efficacy of ICB therapies. PPP1R15A may also function as a prognostic and/or predictive biomarker in patients with HCC. A PPP1R15A+M-MDSC signature may be developed to predict immunotherapy unresponsiveness in patients with cancer. Furthermore, the deep understanding of CCRK oncogenicity and therapeutic potential in HCC as well as the unique preclinical models that recapitulate the molecular and cellular phenotypes of patients’ tumors have led to a strategic collaboration with Insilico Medicine for AI-powered CCRK drug discovery. Insilico Medicine's cutting-edge AI-powered drug discovery capabilities and pipelines, international standing in the industry, and connections with the commercial sectors will definitely accelerate development of our therapeutic target. This synergistic collaboration will not only expedite the development of effective and safe combination immunotherapy for patients suffering from HCC but also hold the potential for significant financial impact through intellectual property and knowledge transfer opportunities.

14120621.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14120621.value: The field of immuno-oncology has revolutionized cancer therapy, particularly with the development of immune-checkpoint blockade (ICB) antibodies that have become standard-of-care for many human cancers including hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). However, around 70% of HCC patients still do not respond to ICB therapies due to de novo or acquired resistance. In addition to T cell immuno-modulators, recent innovative therapeutic development has focused on strategies against the immunosuppressive myeloid cells present in the tumor microenvironment. Myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs) are pathologically activated neutrophils and monocytes with potent immunosuppressive activity. There are two major groups of MDSCs in humans and mice, namely polymorphonuclear MDSCs (PMN-MDSCs) and monocytic MDSCs (M-MDSCs), classified according to their origin. Through an integrative cross-species analysis involving scRNA-seq and preclinical models of HCC, we have identified the epigenetic and transcriptional drivers of PMN-MDSCs and M-MDSCs, whose specific inhibitions have abrogated the immunosuppressive myeloid barrier, thus reinstating antitumor T cell responses to overcome de novo ICB resistance. Our findings have delineated new epigenetic mechanisms underlying tumor immune evasion. As we have also determined the therapeutic effects of a clinically-testing bromodomain inhibitor using the ICB-resistant mouse models, this study would offer immediate translational potential of new combination epigenetic immunotherapy for HCC patients.

14121721.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14121721.value: The current global prevalence of diabetes is about 6.3% and still raising. Diabetic foot ulcers (DFU), is one of the common complications associated with diabetes. DFU is typically chronic skin ulcers in the foot with deep tissue destruction with varying degrees vasculopathy and neuropathy, and it is difficult to heal by traditional wound management treatment. Currently, 90% of patients suffered from severe DFU will eventually lead to an amputation. New treatments are urgently needed to promote DFU healing and improve the limb salvage rate. The tibial cortex transverse transport (TTT) surgery was first used in China to treat severe DFU and promote wound healing. A recent 3-year retrospective study confirmed that the TTT surgery significantly improved the wound healing and limb salvage rate for severe DFU patients. During and after the TTT treatment, patients reported pain relief, warmth feeling and angiography confirmed the formation of rich neo-vascular networks in the ischemic areas. Despite the outstanding clinical outcome, the mechanistic studies of TTT surgery for DFU treatment are still lacking. We hypothesize that TTT surgery may benefit tissue repair through the followings mechanisms: (1) Corticotomy in the tibia shaft reduces intramedullary pressure, improves the microcirculation and oxygen level of the distal limb tissues. (2) The mechanical stimuli during the controlled cortical bone flap movement promote formation of neo-vasculature in the distal limb tissues. (3) TTT surgery may mobilize mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) systemically, recruit MSCs to the wounds, and mediate the local inflammatory responses that facilitate tissue repair. The planned investigations are: (1) To perform the TTT surgery in the diabetic rats and measure the blood flow and transcutaneous oxygen level in the soft tissues of the distal limb before, after the corticotomy and during the TTT treatment. (2) To study the effects of TTT surgery on neo-vasculature formation in the cortical bone, bone marrow and surrounding soft tissues in the treated limb during wound healing in the normal and diabetic rats. (3) To study the effect of TTT surgery on MSCs mobilization and homing to the foot wound sites in the normal and diabetic rats. (4) To study the effect of TTT surgery on inflammatory responses at the wound sites in the diabetic rats. The current study will verify the possible biological mechanisms of TTT surgery in promoting DFU healing. Understanding the biological mechanisms will help to promote TTT surgery as an alternative novel treatment for severe DFU, and benefit DFU patients worldwide. 脛骨皮質橫向轉運（TTT）手術在中國首次用於治療嚴重糖尿病足潰瘍（DFU）並促進傷口癒合。 我們假設 TTT 手術可能通過以下機制有益於組織修復：（1）脛骨乾皮質切開術降低髓內壓，改善遠端肢體組織的微循環和氧氣水平。 (2) 受控制的皮質骨瓣運動過程中的機械刺激促進遠端肢體組織新血管的形成。 (3) TTT手術可以全身動員間充質乾細胞 (MSCs)，將MSCs募集到傷口，並介導促進組織修復的局部炎症反應。計劃的研究是（1）對糖尿病大鼠進行TTT手術，並在皮質切除術之前、之後和TTT治療期間測量遠端肢體軟組織的血流量和經皮氧水平。 (2) 研究TTT手術對正常和糖尿病大鼠傷口癒合過程中被治療肢體的皮質骨、骨髓和周圍軟組織中新血管形成的影響。 (3) 研究TTT手術對正常大鼠和糖尿病大鼠足部創面部位間充質乾細胞動員和歸巢的影響。 (4) 研究TTT手術對糖尿病大鼠創面炎症反應的影響。 目前的研究將驗證 TTT 手術促進 DFU 癒合的可能生物學機制。了解生物學機制將有助於促進 TTT 手術作為嚴重 DFU 的替代新療法，並使全球 DFU 患者受益。

14121721.label: Realisation of objectives
14121721.value: The research team has successfully addressed the core objectives outlined in the original proposal. Significant progress has been made, with several objectives not only met but exceeded, providing deeper mechanistic insights than initially anticipated. The following sections detail the extent to which each objective has been fulfilled. Objective 1: To perform the TTT surgery in the diabetic rats and measure the blood flow and transcutaneous oxygen level in the soft tissues of the distal limb before, after the corticotomy and during the TTT treatment. Achievement Status: Substantially Achieved. The project successfully established a diabetic rat model for TTT surgery. Initially, the standard Streptozotocin (STZ) dosage of 45 mg/kg resulted in unacceptably high mortality rates. To overcome this challenge, the protocol was optimized by administering STZ intraperitoneally at a dose of 35 mg/kg weekly for two weeks. Diabetes was confirmed five days after the second injection by a fasting blood glucose level >16 mmol/L. This optimized model was then used for all subsequent TTT procedures. Upon conducting a pilot study of TTT surgery, we observed that a transport and latency duration of 5 days resulted in the undesirable outcome of infection (10%, 1 of 10), with a potential mechanism involving the long-term opening of the marrow cavity. To better align our experimental model with clinical practice and mitigate the adverse effects associated with TTT surgery, we implemented modifications to the duration of cortical flap transport and latency, reducing them from 5 days to 3 days. According to the results of the Wound Healing Index (WHI), H&E and Masson staining, we found that the TTT treatment not only accelerated the wound closure, but also improved the wound healing quality. This also marked the successful establishment of TTT-DFU treatment rat model. Additionally, we used a pulse oximeter to measure the oxygen partial pressure at the ulcer site wound. Following TTT treatment, transcutaneous oxygen pressure measurements at the rat foot demonstrated a significant improvement in local blood flow and tissue oxygenation. This successfully confirms the primary hypothesis that TTT enhances peripheral perfusion in the distal limb. In addition, we also used rubber perfusion imaging and Laser Speckle perfusion imaging to contrast the blood vessels, and the results showed that after TTT treatment, the blood vessels dilated significantly, indicating enhanced blood flow. Objective 2: To study the effects of TTT surgery on neo-vasculature formation in the cortical bone, bone marrow and surrounding soft tissues in the treated limb during wound healing in the normal and diabetic rats. Achievement Status: Exceeded. The project comprehensively investigated neovascularization. Angiogenesis was assessed via angiography after blood vessel perfusion, which visually and quantitatively revealed a significantly higher number and volume of blood vessels in the newly formed skin of the TTT group compared to sham and fixation control groups. Moreover, immunofluorescence staining (by CD31 and alpha-SMA) was also indicated that more active vessel regeneration after TTT treatment. Furthermore, to gain deeper insights into tissue regeneration, collagen formation was evaluated. Masson's trichrome and Sirius Red staining, along with quantitative analysis, demonstrated a higher presence of collagen type III in the TTT group, indicating active and high-quality tissue formation. Moreover, we also performed another therapy method which developed from TTT called Cranial Bone Transport Technique (CBT). The result indicated that the lymphatic drainage system was enhanced, this also prompt us the bone transport technique enhance not only the neovascularization, but also the lymphatic system. Objective 3: To study the effect of TTT surgery on MSCs mobilization and homing to the foot wound sites in the normal and diabetic rats. Achievement Status: Fully Achieved with Mechanistic Insight. This objective was rigorously investigated and conclusively demonstrated. The mobilization of Mesenchymal Stem Cells (MSCs) was tracked using two complementary methods: Flow Cytometry: Peripheral blood samples were collected at multiple time points. Flow cytometry analysis using MSC-specific surface markers (CD90+, CD29+, CD45- and CD34-) revealed a significant increase in the proportion of MSCs in the peripheral blood and ulcer tissues on days 5 and 6 post-TTT treatment. Cell Tracking: GFP-labeled MSCs were administered intraperitoneally. The subsequent observation of these GFP-labeled cells in both the peripheral blood and ulcer tissues on days 5 and 6 provided direct visual confirmation of the mobilization and homing of MSCs to the wound site as a direct result of TTT treatment. These results provide robust and multi-faceted evidence fulfilling Objective 3. Objective 4: To study the effect of TTT surgery on inflammatory responses at the wound sites in the diabetic rats. Achievement Status: Exceeded. The project went beyond a general study of inflammation and delved into specific immunomodulatory mechanisms. A comprehensive assessment of macrophage and monocyte populations at the wound site was conducted at multiple time points. The project successfully surpassed the original goal of a general inflammation study by conducting an in-depth investigation into specific immunomodulatory mechanisms. A comprehensive, time-course analysis of innate immune cell populations at the wound site was performed. To precisely quantify and localize macrophage subsets, we utilized flow cytometry and immunofluorescence techniques targeting specific phenotypic markers. Analysis using CD68 (pan-macrophage), iNOS (M1), and CD206 (M2) markers revealed a significant immunomodulatory shift induced by TTT. The results demonstrated a clear differentiation shift towards the M2 macrophage subset which facilitating wound healing. Furthermore, to trace the origin of this polarization, we investigated macrophage precursors by analyzing classical and non-classical monocytes using CD43 and CD174a markers. This analysis revealed a significant increase in non-classical monocytes in the peripheral blood following TTT treatment. This systemic change provides a mechanistic explanation for the observed local increase in M2 macrophages at the wound site, indicating that TTT promotes a pro-healing immune bias from the precursor stage. Most critically, to establish a causal link between these cells and the healing outcome, we performed a functional inhibition experiment. Depletion of monocytes and macrophages via Clodroliposome administration resulted in a marked delay in tissue healing. This finding provides direct functional evidence that monocytes and macrophages, particularly the M2 subset, play an indispensable role in mediating the therapeutic effects of TTT for DFU. While this study provides robust evidence for the pivotal role of macrophage reprogramming, it does not fully elucidate the involvement of other critical immune cells, such as T lymphocytes (T cells), in the TTT-mediated healing process. The potential contributions of various T cell subsets (e.g., CD4+ helper T cells, CD8+ cytotoxic T cells, or regulatory T cells - Tregs) to immunomodulation and tissue repair remain an open and important question. Furthermore, this research has not yet explored the dynamic interactions between the mobilized Mesenchymal Stem Cells (MSCs) and the modulated immune cells. Investigating whether MSCs directly mediate the observed macrophage polarization via paracrine signaling, or conversely, whether the altered immune microenvironment influences MSC differentiation and function, represents a crucial next step for understanding the integrated regenerative circuit activated by TTT. In summary, TTT treatment significantly modulates the immune response by reprogramming the myeloid cell lineage: it systemically increases anti-inflammatory monocyte precursors, which subsequently differentiate locally into pro-regenerative M2 macrophages at the wound site. This deliberate shift from a pro-inflammatory to a pro-healing immune phenotype is a fundamental mechanistic discovery that explains, in significant part, the enhanced tissue regeneration observed with TTT.

14121721.label: Major findings and research outcome
14121721.value: We comprehensively investigated the mechanisms of TTT surgery for treating diabetic foot ulcers (DFU). The work successfully validated the clinical efficacy of TTT and provided novel, mechanistic insights into its mode of action. The key findings are summarized below: 6.1.1 Functional Improvement in Perfusion and Healing[1]: TTT surgery was conclusively shown to be a potent stimulus for improving lower limb circulation in a diabetic rat model. The procedure significantly enhanced blood flow and transcutaneous oxygen pressure at the distal foot, creating a critical pro-healing environment. 6.1.2 Robust Angiogenesis and Tissue Remodeling[1,3]: The research provided direct visual and quantitative evidence that TTT promotes extensive neo-vasculature formation in the soft tissues surrounding the wound. Furthermore, analysis of collagen deposition demonstrated that TTT enhances the quality of tissue regeneration, favoring the formation of collagen type III, which is associated with active and early-stage healing. 6.1.3 Systemic Mobilization and Homing of Stem Cells (unpublished): We demonstrated that the procedure mobilizes Mesenchymal Stem Cells (MSCs) from the bone marrow into the peripheral circulation. Using advanced cell-tracking techniques, we confirmed that these MSCs actively home to the ulcer site, providing a cellular reservoir for tissue regeneration. This mobilization was mechanistically linked to the activation of the SDF-1/CXCR4 signaling pathway, a key axis governing stem cell trafficking. 6.1.4 Beneficial Immunomodulation of the Wound Environment (unpublished): Moving beyond vascular effects, the research revealed that TTT profoundly modulates the local immune response. At the wound site, TTT treatment reduced the population of pro-inflammatory M1 macrophages; increased the population of pro-healing M2 macrophages and anti-inflammatory non-classical monocytes, creating a conducive microenvironment for healing in chronic diabetic wounds. 6.1.5 Synthesis of Mechanism[3]: The integrated outcomes support a powerful, multi-faceted mechanism for TTT: The controlled mechanical stimulus of the surgery acts as a "biological switch" simultaneously improving macro- and micro-circulation; recruiting systemic repair stem cells to the wound; and reprogramming local inflammation towards a healing state. These three pillars work synergistically to overcome the pathological barriers to healing in DFU. 6.1.6 Conclusion and Future Direction[2,4,5]: The findings not only explain its clinical success but also open direct pathways for future development, including protocol optimization, combination with adjuvant therapies, and the creation of innovative medical devices, ultimately aiming to improve standards of care for diabetic wound patients globally. Moreover, to detect the potential mechanism underlying the bone transport, small animals bone transport model has been established and will utilized in future researches.

14121721.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14121721.value: The promising results from this foundational research open several impactful pathways for further development. Firstly, we may investigate the upstream molecular triggers activated by the mechanical stimulus of TTT. This includes studying specific mechanosensitive pathways (e.g., YAP/TAZ, Piezo1 channels) and their role in initiating the observed cascade of angiogenesis, immunomodulation, and stem cell mobilization. Moreover, research may move towards personalizing TTT or to create a receptive pro-healing environment makes it an ideal platform for combination with advanced therapies, such as optimal transport technique, MSCs, bioactive scaffolds, growth factors and so on. Lastly, Beyond diabetic foot ulcers, the principle of using controlled mechanical stimulation to systemically enhance perfusion and regeneration could be explored for other ischemic conditions, such as peripheral arterial disease or refractory wound healing in non-diabetic patients. For the proposed course of action, we may investigate its advanced mechanism by targeted molecular biology experiments on wound tissue from the established rat model to identify key upstream signaling pathways activated by TTT. Concurrently, we may work with engineers in designing a next-generation, smart TTT device or combined therapy methods.

14121721.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14121721.value: Diabetic foot ulcers are serious wounds that can be very difficult to heal, sometimes leading to amputation. This research tested a promising surgical technique called Tibial Cortex Transverse Transport (TTT). Imagine a tiny section of shinbone being gently pulled outward and then moved back into place. We discovered that this simple mechanical action acts as a powerful biological signal to the body. In studies with diabetic rats, the TTT procedure significantly improved blood flow to the injured foot, kick-started the growth of new blood vessels in the wound, and attracted the body's own repair stem cells to the site. Crucially, the surgery also helped "reprogram" the wound environment. It reduced harmful inflammation and boosted the types of immune cells that support healing and tissue regeneration. Together, these effects created the perfect conditions for the ulcer to close and heal properly. In short, TTT doesn't just treat the wound locally; it activates the body's entire repair system. This research provides strong scientific evidence for why this innovative surgery is an effective new option for treating chronic diabetic wounds and preventing amputations.

14122021.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14122021.value: Miscarriage is pregnancy loss, a common complication in early pregnancy. The risk of repeating miscarriage increases after the ﬁrst loss of pregnancy. Recurrent miscarriage is defined as the loss of two, three or more consecutive pregnancies before the 24th week of gestation. Apart from genetic disorders, structural uterine abnormalities, hormonal abnormalities and prothrombotic conditions, many cases of recurrent miscarriage are unexplained, no underlying causes could be identiﬁed and no prediction biomarkers and effective treatment are available. The frequency of normal embryonic karyotypes increases with the number of previous miscarriages, suggesting endometrium factors are important in recurrent miscarriage. In order to explore potential candidate genes for the repeated pregnancy loss, we carried out whole genome transcriptome profiling by RNA sequencing of endometrium in women with recurrent miscarriage. We identified Caveolins and associated calcium signaling pathway are significantly enriched and up-regulated in the endometrium of women with recurrent miscarriage. Caveolins are scaffolding proteins constituting main component of caveolae plasma membranes for cell signal transduction, mechanosensation and endocytosis. We hypothesize that Caveolins play a role in the development of miscarriage. In this study, we aim to characterize the endometrium expression and to dissect the underlying mechanism of Caveolins and its calcium signaling molecules in miscarriage. To explore potential treatment for recurrent miscarriage, we also aim to use specific Caveolins inhibitors to prevent miscarriage. Results of the study can provide the first-hand data in the scientific field of reproductive biology and medicine on the expression levels and cellular localization of Caveolins and associated calcium signaling molecules in endometrium of women with recurrent miscarriage. Detailed studies of endometrium Caveolins and its calcium signaling pathway in early pregnancy can also provide mechanistic insights in the cellular and molecular functions of Caveolins in the endometrium for implantation and decidualization in early pregnancy. 14122021.value: For objective 1, To characterize expression and localization of Caveolins (CAV) and its calcium signaling pathway in endometrium of women with recurrent miscarriage, expression and localization of CAV and its calcium signaling pathway in endometrium of women with recurrent miscarriage (RM) during the window of implantation had been characterized by various methods, including real-time quantitative PCR, immunohistochemistry and immunofluorescent staining and immunolabeling transmission electron microscopy (reported in last report). 14122021.label: Major findings and research outcome
14122021.value: Objective 1: To characterize expression and localization of Caveolins and its calcium signaling pathway in endometrium of women with recurrent miscarriage, as reported in last report, proteomic analysis and real-time quantitative PCR showed all RNA transcripts CAV1, CAV2, CAV3 and some of its alternative spliced transcript CAV1α and CAV1β, but not CAV2α, CAV2β, CAV2c, are upregulated in the endometrium of women with RM. Section immunohistochemistry showed the increased mRNA expression of CAV1, CAV2, CAV3 and protein expression of CAV1, CAV2, CAV3 and associated calcium signaling molecules especially RYR and CAMK in the luminal epithelial cells. Immunolabeling transmission electron microscopy confirmed the localisation of protein CAV1, CAV2, CAV3 in the luminal epithelial secretory cells and developed pinopodes, but not in the ciliated cells, of the endometrium. The results confirm CAV1, CAV2 and CAV3 expressions in the endometrium and suggest their potential role of Caveolins in endometrium epithelial cells in miscarriage. Objective 2: To study the functions of Caveolins and its calcium signaling pathway in early pregnancy and its roles in the development of miscarriage, force expression of CAV1, but not CAV2 and CAV3, in endometrium in pregnancy mice in vivo experiments resulted in lower uterine weight and number of implanted embryos, high rate of pregnancy loss and early resorption of embryos in the implantation sites. Similarly force expression of CAV1, but not CAV2 and CAV3, in endometrial epithelial and stromal cell culture also showed lower cell growth, proliferation and decasualization characteristics. Proteomic and metabolomic profiles showed significant opposite level of immunoglobulins and progesterone and correlated with microvessel density and CAV1 expression with predictive value for the RM outcomes. Density of various immune cells including uNK cell subsets and local angiotensin II and its type 1 and 2 receptors in the endometrium were not dysregulated in peri-implantation endometrium and also not associated with abnormal angiogenesis and caveolin signaling in RM and pregnancy outcomes, suggesting renin-angiotensin system is not, but immune and hormonal level are a underlying mediator of endometrium caveolin and calcium hemostasis in RM. Objective 3: To examine the therapeutic effects by targeting Caveolins on the prevention of miscarriage, Caveolins specific inhibitors in pregnancy mice in vivo experiments resulted in higher uterine weight and number of implanted embryos, reduced rate of pregnancy loss and early resorption of embryos in the implantation sites. Caveolins specific inhibitors in endometrial epithelial and stromal cell culture also showed increased cell growth, proliferation and decasualization characteristics, suggesting therapeutic potential of Caveolins specific inhibitors in RM. For the PD-1 and PD-L1 in endometrium, we found PD-L1 was mainly expressed in the outer layer of chorionic villi, which is in line with previous observations that PD-L1was enriched in placental and decidual syncytiotrophoblasts. Gene expression levels of all three isoforms of PD-L1, ADAM17, and ADAM10 were significantly reduced in women with miscarriage, suggesting maternal-fetal interface is a potential contributor to the immunosuppression by PD-L1 signaling during the early pregnancy period and potential therapeutic targets for miscarriage prevention.
