14200021.label: Project Objectives
14200021.value: Minimum structural redundancy DNN architecture compression When designing low-footprint ASR systems on a given amount of speech data and limited computational resources, it is crucial to optimize the trade-off between model foot-print and accuracy performance. In this process, a range of neural network structure design decisions over the network topology, number of hidden nodes, connectivity and the choice of hidden activations need to be made. These choices can be substantially different from those suitable for non-resource constrained settings. In the machine learning community, this DNN structural compression problem remains under active research to date. To this end, the proposed automatic neural architecture compression methods not only allow a wide range of neural structural configurations to be considered, but also jointly models the uncertainty over both the network architectures and their parameters consistently under a Bayesian deep learning framework. This allows the performance ranking over a large number of compressed neural architectures to be accurately predicted given limited training data, while alleviating the need of training and evaluating many compressed systems individually. The combination of Bayesian deep learning and neural architecture compression facilitates the incorporation of expert knowledge over hand-crafted architecture designs as neural structural priors. This is particularly useful in rapid neural architecture compression scenarios, for example, adapting neural structural configurations from unlimited resource conditions to low-footprint settings. This research will be the first to apply Bayesian DNN architecture compression methods to resource constrained speech recognition tasks. Efficient parameter optimization of mixed precision quantised DNNs Existing methods of training quantized DNN models predominantly use the standard back-propagation algorithm and its modified variants. When the weight parameters are restricted to discrete values, using gradient descent methods to either directly train quantized DNN systems from scratch, or apply post quantization fine-tuning, is problematic. The current solution to this problem is to use low precision quantized parameters in the forward pass to compute the error loss before full precision parameters are used in the backward pass to propagate the gradients for model update before quantization is applied again. However, in practice these methods often lead to very slow convergence in quantized model training, while the performance gap against full precision models remains large. In this project, we reformulate a mixed precision quantization approach as an optimization problem. This problem will be solved using efficient alternating direction methods of multipliers (ADMM) based learning of mixed precision quantized DNN parameters. This algorithm draws strength from both the decomposability of dual ascent schemes and the stable convergence of multiplier methods. Both the recognition accuracy loss and quantization error objective functions are efficiently minimized. This research will be the first to apply ADMM based optimization methods to resource constrained speech recognition tasks. Learning optimal local bit-widths for high-performance mixed precision quantized DNNs Uniform precision based DNN quantization methods fail to account for the locally varying sensitivity measured on different parts of an ASR system to quantization error. This often leads to large performance degradation against the full precision systems. A natural solution to this problem is to use mixed precision DNN quantization methods. A fundamental issue when developing mixed precision quantized ASR systems is how to determine the suitable local bit-widths to be used, for example, at individual hidden layers. In existing research on low-bit DNN quantization techniques for low-footprint ASR system development, such choices are either uniformly made across the entire system, or manually set using expert knowledge of the underlying task application. The proposed mixed precision quantization systems will use optimal local bit-widths that are automatically learned using either a minimum performance sensitivity measure based approach, or a mixed precision neural architecture search based method. Both methods are expected to provide improved trade-off between compression ratio and accuracy performance. This research will be the first to exploit auto-configured mixed precision DNN quantization for resource constrained speech recognition tasks. Developing exemplar systems and recipes for low-footprint speech recognition Exemplar systems and recipes developed on publicly available speech data sets provide rapid pathways to disseminate our research outputs and deliver impact within the speech technology community and beyond. Such efforts can provide insights on how to design ultra-compact low-footprint ASR systems for easier edge deployment, as well as significantly enhanced training and evaluation efficiency when used on cloud. Current ASR system development recipes reprehended by, for example, those provided under the Kaldi and PyTorch speech recognition toolkits are mainly designed for the construction of conventional, full precision DNN based ASR systems. The exemplar mixed prevision ASR systems and associated recipes to be developed under this project will facilitate the rapid dissemination of low-footprint speech recognition technologies, and their further application to a wide range of speech technology applications. These efforts can help bring computationally efficient and environmentally accountable speech based AI technologies to users around the world.

14200021.value: 近年來，基於深度神經網絡 (DNN) 的人工智能技術，例如自動語音識別 (ASR)，需要越來越多的計算和能源消耗。這不僅增加了當前在雲上運行的商業產品的成本，而且在將這些系統部署到移動設備上以增強隱私和減少延遲時也造成了困難。這個問題的一個強大解決方案是使用低位 DNN 量化技術。通過使用低精度值（例如二進制數）替換浮點精度的模型參數，可以顯著減小模型大小。當前的量化方法使用統一精度。這無法處理 DNN 不同部分對量化誤差的不同性能敏感性，並且通常會導致性能大幅下降。本項目提出了新穎的混合精度 DNN 量化方法，以生產緊湊、輕量化的ASR 系統。由此產生的靈活性可以在模型壓縮率和精度性能之間提供更好的權衡。在本項目中，我們將首先在當前最先進的基於神經網絡隱馬爾科夫混合架構和Transformer端到端技術ASR 系統上研究這些技術。它們的通用性還允許它們在未來的研究工作中擴展其他形式的端到端方架構。我們最初專注於面向英語、普通話和粵語混合精度量化 ASR 系統研發。我們設想我們的低精度輕量化 ASR 技術可以擴展到其他語言以及其他相關語音技術如語音增強、語音合成和對話系統。

14200021.label: Major findings and research outcome
14200021.value: Deep neural networks (DNNs) based AI technologies such as automatic speech recognition (ASR) require increasingly more computation and energy consumption in recent years. In a broader context, this heavy reliance on the scaling of computing resources and training data quantity is in line with the underpinnings of today’s AI technology development. However, such trends not only increase the costs of current speech AI systems operating on cloud, but also creates difficulty when deploying these systems on mobile devices to enhance privacy-preservation and reduce latency. To this end, in this project we have developed a range of technology solutions addressing these challenges: 1) minimum structural redundancy neural architecture compression and inference speedup; 2) efficient parameter optimization of mixed precision model quantisation; 3) learning optimal local bit-widths for high-performance mixed precision model quantization; and 4) development of exemplar systems and recipes for low-footprint speech recognition systems and recipes on publicly available speech corpora. A particular focus when developing these technologies is to ensure the final low-footprint speech processing systems not only benefit from a very large “lossless” model compression ratio, e.g., over 16 times, to be commensurate with the target computational resource constraints, but equally importantly incur no statistically significant accuracy performance degradation. The effectiveness and efficiency of our approaches are extensively demonstrated across generations of speech technologies represented by, e.g., hybrid TDNN, E2E Conformer, speech foundation models such as wav2vec and HuBERT, and the recently emerging LLM-based ASR systems. The research efforts under this project have led to a total of 22 publications. These include 6 journal articles and 16 conference papers, all of which are published at top tier speech technology venues such as IEEE/ACM TASLP (as IEEE TASLPRO from 2025), IEEE ICASSP and ISCA Interspeech.

14200021.value: Deep neural networks (DNNs) based AI technologies such as automatic speech recognition (ASR) require increasingly more computation and energy consumption in recent years. In a broader context, this heavy reliance on the scaling of computing resources and training data quantity is in line with the underpinnings of today’s AI technology development. However, such trends not only increase the costs of current speech AI systems operating on cloud, but also creates difficulty when deploying these systems on mobile devices to enhance privacy-preservation and reduce latency. To this end, in this project we have developed a range of technology solutions addressing these challenges. The outcome of this research will enhance the computational efficiency of current speech-based AI systems. The effectiveness and efficiency of our approaches are extensively demonstrated across generations of speech technologies including recent LLM-based ones, on multiple languages including English, Mandarin and Cantonese, as well as both typical and medical speech domains.

14200221.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14200221.value: 面向信息新鮮度的調度：一種 “信息的不確定性”框架

14200221.label: Project Objectives
14200221.value: Our first objective is to develop Uncertainty of Information (UoI)-based scheduling algorithms that minimize the sum of the uncertainties about the states of remote processes. Our preliminary work shows that this problem can be formulated as a Restless Multi-Armed Bandit problem (RMAB) [1] by modeling the remote processes as Markov processes. For simple Markov processes in which the state transition probabilities are symmetric, we can use the well-known classical Whittle index to determine which remote process should update its state information next, greatly simplifying the scheduling algorithm. However, for non-trivial Markov processes in which the state transition probabilities are asymmetric, our problem is an RMAB that is tough to solve. It is not clear that the Whittle index approach still works. As part of objective 1, we aim to settle this issue. Our second objective is to develop UoI-based scheduling algorithms that minimize the uncertainties about the remote processes with fairness in mind. When there is a need to ensure the uncertainty about any of the remote processes does not grow too large, it is not appropriate to minimize the sum of the uncertainties of the processes. For example, we might want to minimize the maximum uncertainty among the processes. It turns out that this problem cannot be formulated strictly as a classical RMAB anymore. Objective 2 of this project will explore algorithms that can effectively balance the minimizations of uncertainties among the processes. Our third objective is to develop UoI-based scheduling algorithms when the communication medium is not 100% reliable. An update may be lost in transit on its way to the server. This adds to the challenge of the algorithms in Objectives 1 and 2. In particular, we will investigate whether only incremental changes to the algorithms are needed, or an entirely new set of algorithms are called for. Together, objectives 1, 2, and 3 will cover the main issues faced by communication systems that aim to minimize the UoI associated with remote processes at a central server.

14200321.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14200321.value: 偏好合作博弈論：理論、計算算法和應用

14200321.label: Project Objectives
14200321.value: Generalize the classical Shapley value (CSV), which is one of the cornerstone results in cooperative game theory, into a generalized preference aware Shapley value (PSV). In fact, one can view CSV is simply a special case of the PSV when each agent has equal preference to cooperate with any other agents in a coalition group. In real life, we know that people may have different preferences to cooperate with different people, e.g., a company may only be willing to cooperate with another company which has ``complimentary interests'' rather than ``competitive interests''. Therefore, PSV allows one to study a much broader class of collaborative strategy. More importantly, it allows one to apply the theory to more realistic emerging networking applications. Because the computational complexity of the CSV is exponential and NP-hard, computing the PSV will be more difficult in general. Instead of exact computation, we aim to develop computational efficient algorithms to compute the tight bounds of PSVs. These computational efficient algorithms may use different ``sampling'' approaches so as to cover the whole design space of PSV, i.e., it may be based on Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling, or the epsilon-based oracle sampling algorithms, or importance sampling methods, etc. So that we can cover all possible scenarios in finding the values for PSVs. Apply our theory of PSV and computational algorithms into emerging applications, such as large scale 5G edge computing networks, or large scale crowdsourcing systems. In particular, we plan to collaborate with our industrial collaborators. Specifically, we will collaborate with Tencent Inc. to investigate how one can incentivize a group of end-users to collaboratively perform network tomography so that WeChat or QQ system can discover a better routing path in the Internet, and this will significantly improve many real-time video/audio streaming applications. We will also collaborate with another industrial collaborator, Huawei Inc, to develop the right payoffs to incentivize different regional Internet service providers (ISPs) or mobile phone operators to collaboratively support and deploy new network protocols or new network architectures. This will bring better QoS and diverse services to users.

14200321.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14200321.value: 博弈論是一種數學理論，可以預測代理交互的結果。博弈論在網絡和通信社區有著悠久的歷史。博弈論可以大致分為兩類：（a）競爭博弈論，和（b）合作博弈論。本研究的目的有三個：（1）首先，我們旨在擴展和概括經典的 Shapley 值（CSV。(2) 其次，我們的目標是設計計算效率高的算法來計算這些廣義的 Shapley 值。(3) 鑑於此廣義 Shapley 值及其計算算法，我們計劃通過將這一新理論和範式應用於許多新興網絡應用程序來展示其效用。本研究考慮為“偏好沙普利值”開發基礎數學理論和計算算法設計，以確定誘導許多代理之間協作的相對重要性或收益。

14200721.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14200721.value: 運用基於多參數磁共振成像的自動化分割與放射組學預測甲狀腺眼疾進展

14200721.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14200721.value: Dr Chong, Kam Lung Kelvin Prof Dou, Qi Prof Shi, Lin

14200721.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14200721.value: 研究目的 研發適用於多參數磁共振成像的深度學習算法，從而實現對眶部解剖結構的穩健、準確、有效的自動化分割；並基於此算法構建放射組學模型用於預測甲狀腺眼疾進展。 研究背景 甲狀腺眼疾（TAO）是一種自身免疫性炎症，侵犯眶部及眶周組織，諸如眼外肌肉、脂肪等；其影像評估主要依賴於磁力共振成像。甲狀腺眼疾的進展會對病人日常生活造成相當負面的影響。對處於進展晚期的嚴重患者，手術治療不可避免。然而，預測甲狀腺眼疾是否會進展/加重依然是一個極具挑戰性的臨床難題；主要原因在於進展型與非進展型甲狀腺眼疾二者之間，基線磁力共振圖像上眼外肌等組織的信號和紋理特征不易鑒別或者不能目測。 放射組學既可融合多參數磁力共振圖像的定量特徵，又可獲取那些人類視覺難以識別、甚至無法識別的特徵， 從而實現對眶部結構及組織損傷特徵的綜合性分析。近來，深度學習驅動的自動化分割技術顯著提高了放射組學的分析質量，使其在臨床結局預測任務中表現優異。 因此，基於深度學習的放射組學具有極大潛能去發現獨特的影像學特征，用於在基線階段鑒別進展型和非進展型甲狀腺眼疾。 研究方法 本研究計劃前瞻性招募甲狀腺眼疾患者。患者將接受多參數眶部磁共振成像與詳細的眼科臨床檢查, 從而評估甲狀腺眼疾的臨床活動度，嚴重度和疾病進展等情況。時間點分別為基線，隨訪6個月及12個月。第一階段：在全卷积網絡基础上構建深度學習模型，進而在三维T1加權圖像上對眶部結構及組織（諸如眼外肌、脂肪、泪腺等）進行自動化分割。第二階段：將分割出的眼外肌或其他結構的標記疊加至不同磁共振序列配準後的圖像，進而提取標記範圍内各序列的放射組學特徵（包括形態學、信號、紋理特徵等）。第三階段：使用特徵選擇工具，對所提取的放射組學特徵進行篩選。第四階段：將篩選後的病人放射組學特徵輸入一種機器學習分類器（即預測模型），輸出結果為預測的疾病進展類別：進展型和非進展型甲状腺眼疾。 研究意義 本研究的顯著影響在於首次構建深度學習模型，用於在磁力共振圖像上精準分割甲狀腺眼疾所侵犯的眶部結構及組織。該項技術將成為針對甲狀腺眼疾的最先進的自動分割技術，同時促進深度學習技術在眶部磁力共振圖像處理中的廣泛應用。研發的基於放射組學的疾病預測模型可促成更為個性化的治療方案，有助於免除甲狀腺眼疾病人的無效或不必要治療。

14201321.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14201321.value: 用於陰影檢測、去除和生成的數據高效深度學習技術

14201321.label: Project Objectives
14201321.value: To develop a weakly- and semi-supervised instance shadow detection framework by exploring the knowledge from multiple existing datasets prepared for different image processing tasks, thus improving the performance for detecting the shadow instances, object instances, and shadow-object associations. To develop an unsupervised framework for video shadow removal by exploring the temporal correspondence and cycle consistency in videos. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first deep-learning-based algorithm for video shadow removal. To develop an end-to-end deep neural network architecture by exploring the image completion self-supervised subtask and domain adversarial learning for boosting the generalization capability of deep models for shadow detection and removal in real-world scenarios. To develop a low-cost light direction estimation algorithm by training a lightweight deep network architecture on the synthetic images and adopting a domain adaptation algorithm to predict light directions in real images, which helps to render the shadows of virtual objects in AR scenes.

14201321.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14201321.value: Shadows are common in the natural images, which are the light-deficient regions caused by occluded objects. This project aims to explore multiple aspects of shadows, including shadow detection, removal, and generation. First, shadow provides visual cues for perceiving lighting conditions and scene geometry, and this project on shadow detection, removal, and generation helps to analyze and create fascinating photos, thus improving the intelligence of photo editing. Second, the presence of shadows could degrade the performance of object detection and tracking, and shadow removal in adverse illumination benefits AI applications on outdoor systems. Third, shadow generation helps to create more realistic shadows of virtual objects in the AR environment, thus improving the sense of immersion for AR applications. Recently, deep convolutional neural networks have shown remarkable performance for shadow detection, removal, and generation on the benchmark datasets by training the networks with the paired shadow images, shadow masks, and shadow-free images in a supervised manner, resulting in several limitations. First, the labeling process of shadow masks is expensive, and it is hard or even impossible to obtain the paired shadow and shadow-free images in complex scenarios. Second, these supervised methods trained on limited data have limited generalization capability to detect shadows in general real-world situations. Third, these deep-learning-based algorithms are trained on single shadow images and fail to produce temporal-consistent shadow-free images for videos. Fourth, the shadow generation methods trained on the limited real shadow images are hard to produce shadow details of complex virtual objects for AR applications. To solve the above issues, this project shall develop a series of data-efficient deep learning algorithms that explore the knowledge from various existing data, unlabeled data, and synthetic data to improve the performance of shadow detection, removal, and generation in real-world environments. First, we shall develop an instance shadow detection framework to find shadow instances paired with object instances by exploring the knowledge from multiple existing datasets prepared for different image processing tasks. Second, we shall develop an unsupervised framework for video shadow removal by exploring the temporal correspondence and cycle consistency in videos. Third, we shall improve the generalization capability of deep networks for shadow detection and removal via image completion and domain adversarial learning. Last, we shall develop a low-cost light direction estimation algorithm via synthetic images and domain adaptation learning to predict the light directions in real images, which helps to render the shadows of virtual objects in AR scenes. 陰影是自然圖像常見的現象，它是由被遮擋物體引起光線不足的區域。該項目旨在探索陰影的多個方面，包括陰影檢測、去除和生成。首先，陰影為感知光照條件和場景幾何信息提供了視覺線索，該項目通過探索陰影檢測、去除和生成有助於分析和創建可觀的照片，從而提高照片編輯的智能水平。其次，陰影的存在可能會降低物體檢測和跟踪的性能，而在不利照明條件下的陰影去除算法有助於提升用於戶外系統的 AI 應用算法性能。第三，陰影的生成有助於在 AR 環境中創建更逼真的虛擬物體的陰影，從而提升 AR 應用的沉浸感。 最近，深度卷積神經網絡通過以有監督的方式使用成對的陰影圖像、陰影掩模和無陰影圖像訓練網絡，在基準數據集上顯示出較好的陰影檢測、去除和生成的性能，但是這些算法仍然存在一些局限性。首先，陰影掩模的標註過程成本十分昂貴，在復雜場景下很難甚至不可能獲得到成對的陰影和無陰影圖像。其次，這些在有限數據集上訓練的監督方法在一般真實世界中檢測陰影的泛化能力有限。第三，這些基於深度學習的算法通常在單張陰影圖像上進行訓練，無法在視頻中生成時間一致的無陰影視頻序列。第四，在有限的真實陰影圖像上訓練的陰影生成方法難以為 AR 應用生成複雜虛擬對象的陰影細節。 為解決上述問題，本項目將開發一系列高效利用數據的深度學習算法，從各種現有數據、未標記數據和合成數據中挖掘知識，以提高現實世界中陰影檢測、去除和生成算法的性能。首先，我們將開發一個實例陰影檢測框架，通過探索為不同圖像處理任務準備的多個現有數據集中的知識，找到與對象實例配對的陰影實例。其次，我們將通過探索視頻中的時間對應性和循環一致性來開髮用於視頻陰影去除的無監督框架。第三，我們將通過圖像補全和域對抗學習來提高深度神經網絡對陰影檢測和去除的泛化能力。最後，我們將通過合成圖像和域自適應學習，開發一種低成本的光照方向估計算法來預測真實圖像中的光照方向，從而提升渲染 AR 場景中虛擬物體陰影的性能。

14201321.label: Realisation of objectives
14201321.value: This project aims to develop data-efficient deep learning algorithms to enhance shadow detection, removal, and generation in real-world environments. The key research and development objectives include improving the performance of deep models for image/video recognition, analysis, and restoration, with a particular focus on shadow images. To achieve these objectives, we have developed various deep learning frameworks for shadow perception and understanding, achieving state-of-the-art performance in both effectiveness and efficiency. We proposed instance shadow detection models and extended them to video-level frameworks capable of tracking shadow–object pairs over time, while also exploring instance-level and dichotomous segmentation to improve structural completeness. Additionally, we built large-scale datasets for shadow analysis, refined noisy annotations, and advanced 3D hand–shadow reconstruction for realistic shadow understanding. The project has yielded 4 journal paper and 12 conference papers. The major findings are summarized below: Summary of Major Findings [J1][TPAMI-23] introduces a new problem called instance shadow detection, which involves detecting both shadow instances and their associated object instances in an input image. To tackle this task, a new dataset is compiled, including masks for shadow instances, object instances, and shadow-object associations. An evaluation metric is designed for quantitative assessment of instance shadow detection performance. Furthermore, a single-stage detector is devised to perform instance shadow detection in an end-to-end manner. The applicability of this method is demonstrated in light direction estimation and photo editing. [J2][TIP-24] addresses the challenge of unreliable depth cues in RGB-D instance segmentation, where depth maps often contain noise and structural inconsistencies. To overcome this limitation, a dual-branch cross-modal calibration framework is proposed to jointly refine RGB and depth representations through dynamic interaction, multiscale feature fusion, and depth-guided noise filtering. [J3][TIP-24] proposes a semi-supervised framework for video instance shadow detection, enabling the detection and tracking of paired shadow-object instances across frames. The framework leverages labeled images and unlabeled videos through a two-stage training process, incorporating an association cycle consistency loss for temporal coherence and a bidirectional retrieval mechanism to recover occluded instances. A new benchmark, SOBA-VID, and metric, SOAP-VID, are introduced for evaluation. [J4][TOG-25] tackles the challenging problem of reconstructing 3D bimanual hand poses from target shadow shapes by modeling complex hand–shadow geometry and lighting constraints. It proposes a learning-based approach that infers plausible hand configurations capable of casting the target silhouette. A benchmark is constructed for evaluation, accompanied by shadow-specific metrics for quantitative assessment. [C4][MM-23] tackles the challenge of achieving high-accuracy Dichotomous Image Segmentation (DIS) that captures both global object regions and fine structural details. The proposed framework restructures and bipartitely arranges complementary features to simultaneously boost the effectiveness of trunk and structure identification. [C5][ICRA-23] enhances the boundary quality of instance masks for robust and precise instance segmentation in challenging scenarios. It proposes an IoU-based Boundary-aware Mask head (IBM head) for predicting instance-level masks, boundaries, and their corresponding IoU scores to generate sharper and cleaner boundaries. [C7][ICCV-23] presents a framework for shadow detection with noisy labels, explicitly addressing label noise through an iterative self-training process. The method uses shadow counterfeiting to distinguish shadows from dark regions and refines labels via global-local fusion and shadow-aware filtering and progressively corrects inaccurate annotations and mitigates overfitting. Development of Fundamental Deep-Learning Techniques In addition to the main tasks, we developed fundamental deep-learning techniques for video dehazing, optimization and generalization, model calibration, uncertainty learning, multi-agent reinforcement learning, multi-modal representation learning, and 3D information analysis: [C1][CVPR-23] develops a two-stage sharpness-aware optimization approach based on the decoupling paradigm in DLTR (Deep Learning with Tangent Prop). In the first stage, the feature extractor and classifier are trained under parameter perturbations at a class-conditioned scale. In the second stage, adversarial features are generated using class balanced sampling to further enhance the robustness. [C2][CVPR-23] systematically investigates the calibration performance of mixup, with a specific focus on the interaction between mixup and post-calibration. By incorporating mixup inference, models can be trained using the original one-hot labels, avoiding the negative impact of confidence penalty. [C3][CVPR-23] presents a video dehazing framework based on a multirange temporal alignment network with physical priors. The construction of a large-scale benchmark dataset for outdoor video dehazing enables evaluation of dehazing performance across various application scenarios and downstream tasks. [C6][MM-23] highlights that classical Evidential Deep Learning trained with mean square error can hinder the learning of evidence. To address this issue, it proposes the I-EDL method to alleviate the over-penalization of mislabeled classes by considering importance weights with different classes for each sample. [C8][ICML-24] explores the challenge of low sample efficiency in multi-agent reinforcement learning. A new framework is designed to enable stable high-replay training through a Shrink-and-Perturb mechanism that maintains network plasticity and a Random Amplitude Scale (RAS) augmentation that improves data diversity. [C9][AAMSA-25] focuses on the problem of overestimation in multiagent reinforcement learning. To address this issue, it introduces a dual ensemble mechanism that applies random ensembles to both individual and global Q-values to mitigate overestimated targets, and a hypernet regularizer that constrains hypernetwork parameters to suppress accumulated bias. [C10][AAAI-25] presents a two-stage multi-modal framework for 3D representation learning that enhances cross-modal consistency and diversity by combining feature-level and input-level mixing of text, image, and point cloud data. The method improves zero-shot and linear-probing 3D classification as well as cross-modal retrieval, showing strong generalization and compatibility. [C11][NeurIPS-25] underscores the significant role of reinforcement learning (RL) in enhancing the Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning capabilities of large language models. It introduces a framework that integrates RL-based optimization into the CoT generation process, enabling models to iteratively refine reasoning trajectories through reward-guided feedback. [C12][NeurIPS-25] presents a reinforcement learning–based text-to-image generation model with a bi-level Chain-of-Thought (CoT) mechanism. It combines semantic-level reasoning for prompt planning and token-level reasoning for detailed image synthesis, optimized jointly through the proposed BiCoT-GRPO strategy to enhance visual generation quality. These advancements collectively enhance our understanding and capability in shadow detection, removal, and generation, significantly advancing the field of computer vision and deep learning.

14201321.label: Major findings and research outcome
14201321.value: In this project, we developed a suite of deep-learning-based algorithms to address shadow detection, removal, and generation. Our research focused on enhancing shadow perception and understanding through tasks such as instance-level and dichotomous segmentation, image- and video-level shadow detection, and hand shadow reconstruction, thereby improving the performance of intelligent vision systems such as low-altitude drones and robotic platforms operating under dynamic lighting conditions. Key findings and outcomes include: Image Instance Shadow Detection: A novel task was proposed to detect shadows along with their corresponding objects. An end-to-end one-stage detector was formulated, and a new dataset with labels indicating shadows and their objects was collected. This work was published in the prestigious TPAMI journal [J1]. Instance Segmentation: A dual-branch cross-modal calibration framework is proposed to jointly refine RGB and depth representations through dynamic interaction, multiscale feature fusion, and depth-guided noise filtering [J2]. Video Instance Shadow Detection: A semi-supervised framework for video instance shadow detection is proposed, enabling the detection and tracking of paired shadow-object instances across frames. A new benchmark, SOBA-VID, and metric, SOAP-VID, are introduced for evaluation [J3]. Hand Shadow Reconstruction: This framework reconstructs 3D bimanual hand poses from target shadow shapes by modeling complex hand–shadow geometry and lighting constraints. A benchmark is constructed for evaluation, accompanied by shadow-specific metrics for quantitative assessment [J4]. Dichotomous Segmentation: The proposed framework restructures and bipartitely arranges complementary features to simultaneously boost the effectiveness of trunk and structure identification [C4]. Shadow Detection: This deep framework addresses noise in shadow labels by training deep models in a self-training manner, significantly improving the accuracy of shadow masks and enhancing shadow detection performance [C7]. Additionally, we developed fundamental deep-learning techniques, including video dehazing [C3], optimization and generalization [C1], model calibration [C2], uncertainty learning [C6], multi-agent reinforcement learning [C8], and multi-modal representation learning [C10], [C11], [C12]. These advancements collectively enhance our understanding and capability in shadow detection, removal, and generation, contributing to the field of computer vision and deep learning. Our research resulted in five top-tier journal papers and twelve top-tier conference papers, demonstrating strong contributions and innovations across both application-driven and fundamental studies.

14201321.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14201321.value: Our research can be further extended to support emerging applications in the low-altitude economy and intelligent robotics. The developed shadow analysis and restoration algorithms can enhance environmental perception and visual reliability for aerial platforms such as drones and unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), enabling robust operation under highly variable lighting and atmospheric conditions. Additionally, these techniques can be integrated into robotic vision systems to improve depth perception, object recognition, and interaction safety in dynamic and unstructured environments. To support these developments, we will continue expanding and refining annotated datasets while advancing algorithms for comprehensive shadow perception and understanding. Collaboration with academic institutions, technology companies, and industry partners will promote the joint development and validation of real-world applications. We will also disseminate our findings through publications and workshops to foster continued innovation and collaboration in this field.

14201321.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14201321.value: Our project focuses on improving how machines perceive and understand shadows under complex lighting and real-world conditions. Imagine a drone flying at low altitudes over a city with changing sunlight, or a robot operating in environments with strong light and reflections; shadows can greatly interfere with their visual perception. We developed advanced deep learning algorithms that allow machines to accurately detect objects and their shadows, separate shadowed regions, and reconstruct obscured details, resulting in clearer and more reliable visual understanding. The significance of this research lies in enhancing the safety and reliability of outdoor intelligent systems. For instance, drones equipped with our algorithms can navigate more stably under dynamic lighting for urban inspection, logistics, and environmental monitoring. Robots can also perform safer and more precise operations in complex indoor and outdoor environments. Overall, our work aims to make machines more adaptable and intelligent in visual perception, ensuring they can operate safely and effectively in complex real-world conditions.

14201421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14201421.value: Langevin diffusion is a class of continuous-time stochastic process which has been shown to be a powerful method for global non-convex optimization. It can be viewed as a variant of continuous-time gradient descent where a properly scaled Gaussian noise is added to the gradient to steer the trajectory of the diffusion towards global minima of the objective. Due to the simplicity and tractability, Langevin diffusion, its time-discretization, and their variants are frequently used in machine learning in a broad range of applications from Bayesian learning to solving non-convex optimization problems. A critical question for using the Langevin diffusion for global non-convex optimization is the design of the temperature schedule that controls the amount of Gaussian noise injected over time. In this project, we will design endogenous state-dependent temperature schedule for Langevin diffusion in the context of non-convex optimization. Our approach is based on a novel formulation using stochastic control with entropy regularization. The proposed research will advance our understanding and lead to the development of new Langevin dynamics based algorithms for non-convex optimization. 朗之萬擴散過程是一類可用於全局非凸優化的連續時間隨機過程. 它可以被視為梯度下降法的變體，而其中加入的高斯噪聲允許軌蹟有更多機會逃離局部最小值. 朗之萬擴散方程及其變體已被廣泛用於機器學習，包括貝葉斯學習以及解決非凸優化問題. 使用朗之萬擴散過程進行全局非凸優化的一個關鍵問題是溫度參數的設計. 在這個項目中，我們將從控制的角度出發設計內生的狀態相關的溫度參數. 我們的方法是基於帶有熵正則化的隨機控制. 擬議的研究將推進基於朗之萬動力學的新算法的開發並用於非凸優化.

14201421.label: Realisation of objectives
14201421.value: We have successfully accomplished all our objectives. Specifically, we achieved Objective 1 by leveraging tools from stochastic relaxed control and continuous-time reinforcement learning to introduce temperature randomization and entropy regularization. By solving the resulting control problem, we derived a state-dependent, truncated exponential distribution that can be used to sample temperatures in a Langevin algorithm, expressed in terms of the solution to a Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman partial differential equation. This enabled us to achieve Objective 2. To validate our approach, we conducted a numerical experiment on a one-dimensional baseline example, where the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation can be easily solved. Our results compared favorably with other available algorithms in searching for a global optimum, thereby achieving Objective 3. Finally, we explored various extensions, including applying convergence analysis ideas from Langevin dynamics to study error bounds for generative diffusion models, as well as using continuous-time reinforcement learning to investigate regret bounds for episodic continuous-time Markov decision processes. This investigation allowed us to achieve Objective 4.

14201421.label: Major findings and research outcome
14201421.value: With the support of the grant, we have successfully published four papers in top journals, including Mathematics of Operations Research, Journal of Machine Learning Research, Operations Research and SIAM Journal on Control and Optimization (SICON). In the following, we summarize the major contributions and research findings from each paper. Paper 1 in Part C: We use the continuous-time reinforcement learning approach to develop an efficient learning algorithm for continuous-time Markov decision processes with unknown parameters in the finite-horizon episodic setting. We derive bounds on the worst case expected regret for the proposed algorithm and show that both upper and lower are bounds are of the order of square root on the number of episodes. Paper 2 in Part C: Inspired by the convergence analysis of Langevin algorithms, we establish convergence guarantees for a general class of score-based generative models in the 2-Wasserstein distance, assuming accurate score estimates and smooth log-concave data distribution. Paper 3 in Part C: Motived by the stochastic optimal control approach, we analyze the joint admission and scheduling control of a queueing system with two classes of customers: online and walk-in. Unlike walk-in customers, online customers are given a target time for pick up upon placing an order. We develop a novel analysis for this problem and design a policy that is asymptotically optimal. Paper 4 in Part C: We develop an endogenous temperature control scheme for applying Langevin diffusions to find non-convex global minima, using an entropy-regularized stochastic relaxed control approach. We derive a state-dependent distributional control, which can be used to sample temperatures in a Langevin algorithm. Numerical analysis shows that our algorithm perform alternative ones. We remark that although an initial version of Paper 4 was submitted to the journal SICON around one month prior to the project's start date of August 15, 2021, it went under a significant revision process (with the help of a PHD student) before it was accepted for publication on December 15, 2021 and published electronically May 2022. The revision process was supported by this grant and it was an integral part of the project's progression. We also remark that our preliminary research such as the control formulation of the problem, and other related studies, have been clearly stated and declared in our proposal submission/update. No duplicate funding was sought or received for this research project and there is no any substantially similar research.

14201621.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14201621.value: 複雜多智能體系統協作式輸出調節的綜合方法

14201621.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14201621.value: The output regulation problem (ORP) has been one of the fundamental control problems and it arises from many practical control problems such as the vertical take-off and landing of airplanes on the carriers, high performance robot manipulation, and vibration attenuation of highspeed train. It aims to design a feedback control law to achieve asymptotic tracking and disturbance rejection in an uncertain plant. Here both the reference inputs and disturbances are generated by an exosystem. The problem can be handled by two methods, namely, feedforward control design and internal model design. The cooperative output regulation problem (CORP) is a generalization of the ORP to a networked multi-agent system, and includes such problems as consensus, synchronization, formation, and flocking as special cases. The group of networked systems together with the exosystem can be viewed as a multi-agent system with the exosystem as the leader system and the networked systems as the follower system. The cooperative output regulation problem was first formulated by PI in 2012. Since then, the PI has developed two approaches, namely, the distributed observer design and the distributed internal model design to deal with the CORP. These two approaches can be viewed as the distributed counterpart of the feedforward control design and the internal model design, respectively. The distributed observer design is effective in dealing with the CORP for linear multi-agent systems over jointly connected switching graphs, which can be disconnected at all time. Nevertheless, since this approach makes us of the solution of the regulator equations, it cannot handle the uncertainty of the plant by itself. In contrast, like the conventional internal model design, the distributed internal model approach converts the CORP to a distributed stabilization problem of a distributed augmented system and is thus capable of handling uncertain nonlinear multi-agent systems. However, since this approach requires the communication graph to be connected at all time, it cannot handle jointly connected switching graphs. In practice, due to the change of the environment or the failures of the sensors and actuators of a multi-agent system, the communication networks are often switching and can be disconnected from time to time. The jointly connected switching graph is the least restrictive way for modelling practical communication networks. Thus, in this project, we will combine the distributed observer and the distributed internal model to obtain an integrated approach that is able to deal with uncertain nonlinear multi-agent systems over jointly connected switching graphs. 輸出調節問題（ORP）是基礎的控制問題之一，它源於諸如載具上飛機的垂直起降，高性能機器人的操縱，和高速列車的震動衰減等實際控制問題。該問題旨在設計一種反饋控制律，以實現不確定系統的漸進跟蹤和干擾抑制。此問題中，參考輸入及外部擾動信號皆由外部系統產生。該問題可通過兩個方法解決，即前饋控制方法與內模方法。協作式輸出調節問題（CORP）是ORP向網絡化多智能體系統的推廣，它包含一致性、同步、編隊、集群這些特殊情況。網絡化系統連同外部系統可以視為一個多智能體系統，其中外部系統視為領導者，網絡化系統視為跟隨者。協作式輸出調節問題最先於2012年首次提出。目前有兩個方法來解決CORP，分別是分佈式觀測器方法與分佈式內模方法。這兩個方法可以分別視為前饋控制方法與內模方法在分佈式系統下的對應。分佈式觀測器方法能夠有效處理在可以時刻不聯通的聯合聯通網絡下的線性多智能體系統的CORP。儘管如此，由於此方法利用了調節器方程的解，它本身無法處理模型的不確定性。相比之下，與傳統的內模方法類似，分佈式內模方法可以將CORP轉化成對分佈式增廣系統的分佈式鎮定問題，從而能夠處理不確定的非線性多智能體系統。然而，由於此方法要求通信網絡時刻聯通，它不能夠處理聯合聯通的切換通信網絡。在實際應用中，由於環境的變化或多智能體系統傳感器和執行器的故障，通信網絡會經常發生切換且會時常斷開。聯合聯通的切換網絡是對實際通信網絡的限制最少的建模方法。因此，在此項目中，我們將分佈式觀測器和分佈式內模結合起來搭建一個能夠處理聯合聯通切換網絡下不確定的非線性多智能體系統的綜合方法。

14201721.label: Realisation of objectives
14201721.value: The project objectives regarding technical validation and clinical evaluation have been fully realized. We have successfully achieved the primary target of developing a fast, robust, and non-invasive MRI technology to measure Macromolecular Proton Fraction (MPF) in human tissues. While prior MPF research has predominantly focused on the brain, extending this modality to the liver presented significant challenges, primarily due to respiratory motion and the inherently low signal-to-noise ratio of endogenous contrast mechanisms. We optimized our technology to achieve robust MPF quantification of the liver within brief breath-holds, requiring neither contrast agents nor additional hardware. In addition to MPF, we investigated and developed fast T1rho mapping technology for liver applications. Both technologies share the same spin-lock MRI acquisitions. Recognizing that providing a confidence level is crucial for quantitative Magnetic Resonance Imaging (qMRI), we successfully developed methodologies to measure the uncertainty of these quantitative metrics when imaging the liver. Furthermore, we conducted an in-depth investigation into the NMR physics underlying our spin-lock technology. A major finding was that our spin-lock-based MPF quantification is orientation-independent. This stands in contrast to conventional saturation-pulse-based MPF imaging, where quantification can be confounded by the orientation of ordered tissue structures, ensuring our measurements remain reliable regardless of scan geometry. We successfully recruited a cohort of 61 patients with biopsy-proven fibrosis and 81 healthy controls. Technical objectives were met by confirming the high repeatability and reproducibility of our quantitative MRI sequence. Notably, despite a significant reduction in the allocated budget compared to the original funding request, we successfully mitigated this resource constraint and expanded our evaluation scope. We managed to secure access to commercial MR Elastography (MRE) for comparative analysis and conducted histological analysis (H&E) to measure collagen content. The comparison of our MPF approach against MRE and histology yielded promising results. The project has successfully bridged the gap between academic research and clinical application. We have established close collaborations with MRI vendors and clinical partners, with vendors expressing strong interest in the commercial potential of this work. With their support, we are currently coordinating with our clinical collaborators to initiate further clinical studies. While the development of reliable, non-invasive imaging for liver fibrosis remains a challenging endeavor given the global burden of chronic liver disease, this project has made significant strides toward that goal. We remain committed to further refining this technology to fully address current clinical limitations.

14201721.label: Major findings and research outcome
14201721.value: This grant has successfully advanced the field of quantitative magnetic resonance imaging with a specific focus on liver fibrosis. We investigated and optimized two primary imaging modalities, Macromolecular Proton Fraction (MPF) mapping and T1rho mapping, both developed using spin-lock techniques. A primary accomplishment of this project was the development of "trustworthy" quantitative imaging technologies. Specifically, the ability to estimate the confidence and reliability of quantitative measurements. Given the liver's susceptibility to respiratory motion, rapid acquisition is critical to prevent motion artifacts. We established a robust pipeline for accelerating quantitative mapping using self-supervised deep learning. By incorporating relaxation constraints, we demonstrated that accurate maps can be generated from a significantly reduced number of weighted images, facilitating faster clinical scans. Crucially, we integrated uncertainty estimation into these networks. We developed an uncertainty-aided framework that not only predicts biochemical values but also provides a confidence level for each pixel. This allows for the automatic identification and removal of unreliable data points, reducing relative mapping error to below 3%. Furthermore, we expanded this methodology to a multi-tasking framework capable of simultaneous multiparametric mapping, utilizing uncertainty weighting to adaptively balance the learning process between different parameters. In the domain of pulse sequence development, we addressed the challenge of orientation dependence in ordered tissues. We validated that our spin-lock technique, which probes macromolecular content (e.g., collagen), effectively suppresses residual dipolar coupling (RDC) via strong effective spin-lock fields. This renders the quantification independent of tissue orientation, offering a significant advantage over traditional magnetization transfer methods, which are often confounded by the "magic angle" effect. To ensure the robustness of our quantitative metrics, we conducted rigorous testing on a cohort of 81 healthy controls. Statistical analysis confirmed the repeatability and reproducibility of our technology. Furthermore, we assessed the impact of scan geometry, establishing that MPF measurements remain stable regardless of slice orientation, a vital feature for clinical workflow flexibility. We also recruited 61 patients with biopsy-proven liver fibrosis. In this cohort, we acquired data using both our quantitative imaging technologies and commercial MR Elastography. The final analysis demonstrated a positive correlation between our MPF metrics and fibrosis stages. MRE demonstrated good performance in identifying advanced stages of fibrosis. Our MPF method showed promising sensitivity. We conclude that further large-scale studies are necessary to fully transition this technology into clinical use worldwide.

14201721.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14201721.value: The efficacy of our spin-lock technology relies on robust RF power delivery. However, abdominal imaging demands significantly higher RF power than neuroimaging. This challenge is exacerbated by the industry shift toward 70cm wide-bore MRI systems, which have reduced RF transmit efficiency compared to conventional 60cm systems. To overcome these hardware limitations, we are developing innovative, "RF-friendly" pulse sequences. These engineering solutions aim to maintain the fidelity of spin-lock contrast while operating effectively within the stricter RF constraints of modern wide-bore scanners. While our initial results are promising, large-scale validation is required to transition this technology into clinical use worldwide. We propose establishing multi-center partnerships with hospitals and manufacturers to substantially increase our patient cohort. A critical objective of this expansion is to validate the utility of MPF for early-stage fibrosis detection. Unlike stiffness-based methods which assess fibrosis indirectly via mechanical properties, our technology directly probes macromolecular collagen content. We hypothesize that this direct detection mechanism will offer superior sensitivity in early-stage disease. Validating this advantage will be instrumental in establishing our technology as a standard, non-invasive biomarker for liver fibrosis assessment.

14201721.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14201721.value: Chronic liver disease is a major global health issue, affecting over 1.5 billion people. A key indicator of liver damage is fibrosis, or scarring of the liver tissue. Traditionally, doctors diagnose this using a liver biopsy which is a painful procedure that involves inserting a needle to remove a small tissue sample. Because biopsies are invasive and only test a tiny spot on the liver, there is an urgent need for a safer, more comfortable way to detect liver damage, especially in the early stages when it can still be reversed. Our research introduces a new MRI technology to solve this problem. Unlike a painful biopsy, our method scans the whole liver without using any needles. Our studies show this technology has the potential to directly detect liver fibrosis using the standard MRI machines already found in most hospitals, so no expensive new equipment is needed. By partnering with hospitals and manufacturers, we are working to make this fast, affordable tool widely available. This will help patients get diagnosed early and treated sooner through a safe, simple scan.

14201921.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14201921.value: 計算多關節組裝結構的結構剛度是一項具挑戰性的任務。通常，現有方法依賴於模擬結構在特定外部載荷下的情況。但這樣做需要費力的手動設置步驟，例如仔細指定外部負載。此外，所涉及的計算是耗時的。在這個研究項目，我們的目標是製定一個新的計算框架來自動分析組裝結構的整體剛度，而不需要用戶提供指定的載荷，這樣，我們就可以自動找到使組裝結構最大變形的外部載荷。我們的計算框架是通用的，它能支持由多個部件和不同類型的關節而組成的組裝結構。此外，我們提出的方法能有效向用戶提供實時反饋。另一方面，我們所設計的框架是可微分的，因此，我們可以有效地利用梯度計算進行自動結構優化。 綜上所述，我們將在研究項目中探索以下任務： (i) 為建模部件和關節制定統一的表示方法，並設計新的度量標準來量化組裝結構的剛度； (ii) 推導出一個新的計算模型來自動地尋找組裝結構中的可移動的部件或部件群，並進一步推斷相關部件的相應和協同運動； (iii) 擴展至非剛性部件，並有效預測組裝結構的最壞剛度情況；和 (iv) 設計新的基於梯度計算的自動結構優化方法，通過修改其部件的三維形狀或調整相關關節的參數以自動增強該組件。 在這個項目的過程中，我們將通過模擬生成各種類型的虛擬三維組裝結構，製造和組裝各種類型的結構，並通過各種實驗以評估各組裝結構。該項目將補充並擴展研究團隊之前的兩個項目，旨在提高其自動生成結構的完整性。此外，通過此項目，團隊將推進在計算組裝結構方面的研究工作，並將繼續努力發展能夠獲得頂級研究期刊和會議的高質量結果。

14201921.label: Realisation of objectives
14201921.value: This project aims to develop cutting-edge computational methods for analyzing and creating 3D assembly structures. We started this project by developing optimization-based techniques for analyzing and optimizing 3D assembly structures in the early project stage, then focusing on innovating new techniques on 3D representation/generation/manipulation. The published papers are all in top-tier international research journals/conferences. Also, we started our collaboration with Adobe and Autodesk with joint publications in top-tier international computer graphics and machine learning conferences: SIGGRAPH and ICML. At the beginning of this project, we studied structural rigidity for assemblies with mechanical joints. Importantly, we addressed the limitation of existing works in quantifying how rigid an assembly is, by developing a new measure, worst-case rigidity, i.e., formulated as the largest possible deformation that an assembly undergoes for arbitrary external loads of fixed magnitude. Computing the worst-case rigidity is non-trivial, due to non-rigid parts and different joint types. We thus formulated a new computational approach by encoding parts and their connections into a stiffness matrix, in which we modeled parts as deformable objects and joints as soft constraints. Based on this, we formulated worst-case rigidity analysis as an optimization that seeks the worst-case deformation of an assembly for arbitrary external loads and solved the optimization problem via an eigenanalysis. Furthermore, we presented methods to optimize the geometry and topology of various assemblies to enhance their rigidity, as guided by our rigidity measure. In the end, we also validated our method on a variety of assembly structures with physical experiments and demonstrate its effectiveness by designing and fabricating several structurally rigid assemblies. Then, we started to study 3D representations, including a disentangled hybrid explicit-implicit 3D shape representation that decouples the topology and local 3D geometry. Also, we formulated the first neural wavelets representation for compactly encoding 3D shapes and structures, enabling direct 3D generative modeling of a continuous implicit representation. This is a cornerstone work, by which we further extend it by considering 3D inversion beyond 3D generation and manipulation. Beyond these works, we studied the encoding redundancy in the representation and developed a compact wavelet-tree representation with subband coefficient encoding in the latent wavelet space, allowing us for the first time to train a large 3D generative model on a very large-scale extensive dataset of over 10 million 3D shapes. This is a collaborative work with Autodesk Inc. and the PhD student involved eventually joined Autodesk Inc. after his graduation. On the other hand, we developed novel learning-based techniques for generating 3D assemblies. These are novel deep generative methods. Overall, this includes a three-stage pipeline for creating 3D figurine assembly from human photos, with a novel coarse-to-fine pipeline design and a decal generative pipeline, enabling us to effectively reproduce both prominent and detailed features on 3D figurines based on the input photos. Later, we designed a novel learning-based approach that can effectively generate intricate LEGO assemblies in the form of 3D micro buildings: we first proposed the new idea of a 3D semantic volume representation to encode part assemblies and further developed a 3D diffusion-based generative model that can unconditionally generate 3D assembly models. Lastly, we also innovated a new approach for articulated objects, in which our trained neural network model can enable us to understand and manipulate articulated objects via human commands, leveraging structure prediction and command encoding for motion control. Further, we innovate various novel methods for 3D reconstruction, generation, and manipulation, including a new neural approach for point-set self embedding, with which we can sparsely encode structural information from dense point sets, achieving compact storage and accurate 3D reconstruction. We also developed a 3D shape reconstruction and generative framework that disentangles topology and shape, a new text-guided 3D shape generation framework that decouples shape-color in the 3D generation, and a novel approach that formulates 3D generation as a 3D shape space exploration with the help of the large vision-language model CLIP. Lastly, we innovated a new three-stage 3D hand-mesh reconstruction pipeline from images with task decoupling, designed the PACO self-supervised framework for object-level scene deocclusion, utilizing a parallel variational autoencoder and a visible-to-complete latent generator to predict full-view feature maps from partial inputs, and developed a novel coupled representation and a neural volume optimization for latent-space 3D shape editing. Please refer to the major findings and research publications for the details.

14201921.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14201921.value: In this project, a series of cutting-edge techniques have been developed by the research team for analyzing, optimizing, and generating 3D assembly structures, enabling a systematic analysis of assembly structures and also AI-based 3D generation and editing. Technical-wise, we derived a new mathematical model to efficiently quantify the rigidity of assembly structures. Besides, we designed several AI-based approaches, including a compact neural wavelet-tree representation with subband coefficient encoding that enables us to train a very large 3D generative model on an extensive dataset of over 10 million 3D shapes (it is a collaborative work with Autodesk Inc.), a neural volume optimization approach with a coupled representation for delivering latent-space 3D shape editing, and the first diffusion-based approach that can generate a rich variety of intricate LEGO micro buildings via our semantic volume representation, enabling us to handle different brick types beyond the basic rectangular bricks. Overall, more than ten research publications have been produced in this project and they were published in world-leading international journals/conferences, such as SIGGRAPH, CVPR, and ICML, in computer graphics, vision, or machine learning research.

14202121.value: 摩擦表面電荷機理研究與材料工程

14202121.label: Project Objectives
14202121.value: To establish a macroscale method for investigating the triboelectric charge transfer mechanism through thermionic or field emission of electrons, focusing on the dominant charge transfer carriers (electrons/ions/materials); to determine the charge transfer mechanism in various material pairs, particularly in polymer/polymer pairs; to compare mechanisms and charge generation between contact and sliding triboelectrification methods; to study the impact of material strain and surface treatments on the surface charge. To study the triboelectric charge transfer mechanism using a microscale method such as atomic force microscopy, and to verify the results and conclusions obtained in the macroscale study. To develop methods to promote triboelectric charge generation; to develop methods to adjust the surface charge through electrostatic discharge; to summarize the standardized charge tailoring methods (targeted to be adjustable between 10-200 μC/m2). To identify and demonstrate the wide range of potential applications by either enhancing or suppressing the triboelectric surface charge.

14202121.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14202121.value: The focus of this proposed project is to identify the mechanism involved in the triboelectric effect using macroscale and microscale methods, develop technologies to tailor the triboelectric surface charge, and explore applications in energy harvesting, electrostatic discharge protection, among others. Triboelectric effect universally exists between surfaces of two materials in contact and is the origin of static charges, which was discovered thousands of years ago but is still poorly understood. Over the years, scientists have struggled to determine how to prevent the triboelectric effect as can cause the failure of electronic components and integrated circuits. However, in recent years, interest in the triboelectric effect changed its focus as it can enable mechanical energy harvesting through the triboelectric nanogenerator, which has a multitude of applications particularly in self-powered systems. However, the mechanism that creates the triboelectric effect is still not clear, especially the dominant carrier of the charge transfer. Without a clear understanding of the mechanism involved in the triboelectric effect, researchers are unable to optimize or modulate the surface charge which is essential for practical applications. The proposed studies are therefore imperative in both fundamental and practical contexts to encourage further development. Through experimental and theoretical studies, this project will investigate the mechanism that creates the triboelectric effect, and summarize technologies that can successfully control the surface charge. The triboelectric charge transfer mechanism will be revealed through the surface potential barrier, which can be extracted from thermionic or field emission of electrons. The experiments will be conducted in both the macroscale method through a designed vacuum chamber, and the microscale method using atomic force microscopy. Different material pairs will be evaluated and compared using two different triboelectrification methods. Methods by which the triboelectric surface charge can be optimized will be investigated. Ultimately, novel applications focused on tailoring surface charge to the requirements of various applications will be explored. The findings of this study will promote the advancement of this field in both the fundamental understanding of the triboelectric effect and its potential applications. This research will serve as a systematic study of the triboelectric mechanism through the newly proposed multi-scale methods using carefully designed experimental setups, which will shed light on the unknown mechanism of the triboelectric effect. The study may also supply the paradigm-shift strategies to tailor the surface charge, and will serve the interests of researchers worldwide in multi-disciplinary fields such as energy harvesting, electrostatic discharge protection, and high-voltage applications. 本項目的重點是利用宏觀尺度和微觀尺度的方法確定摩擦電效應的機理，開發調控摩擦表面電荷的技術，並探索其在能量收集、靜電放電保護等方面的應用。 摩擦電效應普遍存在於兩種接觸材料的表面之間，是靜電的起源。人們在幾千年前就發現了摩擦電效應，但至今仍知之甚少。多年來，科學家們一直在努力研究如何防止可能導致電子元件和集成電路失效的摩擦電效應。然而，近年來，人們對摩擦電效應的研究改變了方向，因為摩擦電納米發電機可以基於摩擦電效應收集機械能，並在自供電系統中有廣泛的應用前景。然而，產生摩擦電效應的機理尚不清楚，尤其是電荷轉移的主要載體尚不明確。如果不清楚摩擦電效應的機理，研究人員就無法優化或調控表面電荷，而這對實際應用至關重要。因此，進一步的研究對於基礎研究和應用都具有重要意義。 本項目將通過實驗和理論研究，研究產生摩擦電效應的機理，發展成功控制表面電荷的技術。從電子的熱離子或場發射過程中所提取的表面勢壘可以反映摩擦電荷轉移機制。相關實驗將通過自行設計的真空室進行宏觀尺度的測量，以及使用原子力顯微鏡進行微觀尺度的測量。不同的材料組合通過兩種不同的方法進行的摩擦起電將被評估和比較，並對摩擦表面電荷的優化方法進行研究。最終，本項目將實現對表面電荷的裁剪，以滿足各種應用的要求。 本研究的結果將促進這一領域的發展，無論是對摩擦電效應的基本認識還是對其潛在的應用。本研究將通過新提出的多尺度方法和精心設計的實驗裝置對摩擦電機理進行系統研究，這將有助於揭示摩擦電效應機理。該研究還可能提供範式轉換的策略用以調控表面電荷，並將服務於多學科領域的研究，如能量收集、靜電放電保護和高電壓應用等。

14202121.label: Major findings and research outcome
14202121.value: (1) Outcome 1: established a macroscale method for investigating the triboelectric charge transfer mechanism Through the thermionic emission of electrons, a quantified model was proposed to investigate the triboelectrification of macroscale materials, with the contribution ratios from different charge transfer mechanisms identified for different polymers. Interestingly, these contribution ratios were usually larger than 1, indicating that the total generated charge in triboelectrification is actually much larger than the net surface charge, which is also consistent with the previous studies. (SmartMat 3 (4), 619-631) We also discovered heat-excitation effect to promote the triboelectric charge generation, and compared the difference between contact and sliding triboelectrification methods. Charge promotion and charge durability was demonstrated in sliding based triboelectrification, where 3-time energy promotion was obtained. (Advanced Science, 11 (41)) We discovered that if the metal side of the triboelectric pair was placed by metallic glass, the triboelectrification efficiency can be enhanced by 3.4 times (Nature Communications 14 (1), 1023), and surface treated by insulation oils can further promote the surface charge generation by avoiding discharge in voids. (Energy Environ. Sci., 17, 5283-5294) Material strain can also positively contribute to the charge generation (manuscript in preparation). (2) Outcome 2: developed a microscale method for investigating the triboelectric charge transfer mechanism By using the atomic force microscopy platform in HKUST-Guangzhou, we are able to develop the microscale method combined with theoretical simulations to investigate the triboelectrification mechanism. We confirmed the mosaic bi-polar charge pattern observed in macroscale experiments, and concluded that effective contact until the repulsive van der Waals force is required for triboelectric charge generation by electron transfer (manuscript in preparation). (3) Outcome 3: developed methods to adjust triboelectric charge in a large range We developed the method of using external electrical field to tune the surface charge. For a CS-TENG with polymer/Cu contact, we can easily achieve the charge density in range of about 0-2300 μC/m^2, which is far beyond our original target of 10-200 μC/m^2. (ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces 14 (4), 5355-5362 and Energy Environ. Sci., 17, 5283-5294) Other methods such as heat-excitation (Advanced Science, 11 (41)), strain engineering and minimization (manuscript in preparation) can also adjust triboelectric charge. (4) Outcome 4: demonstrated the wide range of potential applications We have developed the wide applications of surface with tunable triboelectric charge including tribo-induced electroluminescence, self-powered wireless sensing, water desalination, etc (multiple papers in the list).

14202121.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14202121.value: In terms of fundamental studies, triboelectric charge generation in macroscale is greatly limited by surface roughness and contact intimacy, and thus it is very important to study that in microscale, with instrument of atomic force microscopy and other microscale characterization platforms, to reveal the mystery triboelectric mechanism which puzzled people for over 2000 years. However, currently these studies are still very limited. Our team has conducted microscale studies for almost one year, thanks to instrument supported by HKUST-Guangzhou. We will continue working on that to understand fundamental physics behand the triboelectric effects. In terms of applied studies, with the electric-field-excitation method and other charge manipulation methods, we may potentially use triboelectric charge for applications with promoted performance. We have demonstrated applications including tribo-induced electroluminescence, self-powered wireless sensing, water desalination, etc, with enhanced performance. We wish we can expand applications of triboelectricity as a self-powered method for other applications.

14202121.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14202121.value: This project aims to understand how the triboelectric effect works by studying it at both large and small scales. We have concluded that the triboelectric charge can be generated through mixed ways by electron transfer and material transfer. We have created ways to control the triboelectric charge generation that builds up on surfaces when they rub together, through external electric field and other methods. This knowledge could be useful in areas like capturing energy from movement or preventing damage from static electricity. By carefully designing experiments, we have uncovered new insights into how this effect works. The research could change how scientists think about managing surface charges and will be valuable for experts in various fields, including those focused on energy and preventing electrical mishaps. The future study can go to very tiny scales such as 1/1000000 of 1 meter to understand how the triboelectric effect works in such tiny scales and explore the triboelectric charge as a power source for more applications.

14202421.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14202421.value: 大規模智能反射面輔助移動聯邦學習

14202421.label: Project Objectives
14202421.value: To conduct a theoretic and algorithmic study of reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) optimization in over-the-air federated learning systems. In particular, we will first analyze the joint impact of RIS configuration, device scheduling, and transmitter/receiver schemes on the accuracy and convergence federated learning processes. We will then design effective algorithms to jointly optimize the RIS operation with other control variables for over-the-air federated learning. To design a RIS-enabled blind transmission scheme for over-the-air model aggregation. To enable coherent signal aggregation at the receiver, most over-the-air model aggregation schemes require the transmitters to pre-equalize the transmitted signals according to the instantaneous channel state information (CSI). The transmitter-side CSI acquisition, however, incurs high feedback overhead. In this project, we will design a novel RIS-enabled blind transmission scheme, where the signal alignment at the receiver is achieved by RIS configuration instead of transmitter-side pre-equalization. To design a RIS-enabled privacy-preserving federated learning scheme. Preserving data privacy is one of the main motivations behind federated learning. Recent studies show that model parameter exchange during the training process is still vulnerable to privacy attacks. Differential privacy has been recently applied to protect data privacy by randomly perturbing the transmitted model parameters. Nonetheless, random perturbation on model parameters inevitably hurts the convergence of federated learning. In this project, we plan to investigate the use of RIS to enhance the data privacy preservation in over-the-air federated learning systems.

14202421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14202421.value: The availability of massive amounts of data at mobile edge devices has led to a surge of interest in developing artificial intelligence (AI) services at the edge of next-generation wireless systems. To facilitate distributed machine learning while preserving data privacy, federated learning has emerged as a new paradigm where distributed devices collaboratively train a shared AI model based on their local data. In practice, unreliable wireless propagation environment is the main bottleneck that limits the convergence and accuracy of wireless federated learning. In particular, the channel heterogeneity across mobile devices causes severe straggler issues that inevitably complicates the learning system design. Reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) is envisioned as a key enabler for future 6G mobile networks. By reflecting the incident signals with reconfigurable phase shifts, RIS is capable of manipulating the wireless propagation environment to achieve unprecedented energy focusing at the receivers. To render RIS a viable solution for relieving the communication bottleneck in wireless federated learning systems, it is of paramount importance to design RIS mechanisms that greatly enhance the learning accuracy and convergence, address the channel and data heterogeneity across devices, and ensure data privacy. Existing RIS designs have focused on the communication aspects that aim to increase data transmission rates. In contrast, both the communication and computation aspects play an important role in wireless federated learning. To address the challenge, we plan to focus on the following important tasks in this project: (1) to analytically characterize the impact of RIS on the convergence of federated learning; (2) to jointly optimize the device selection, RIS phase shifts, and receiver beamforming to enhance the federated learning accuracy and convergence; (3) to greatly reduce the transmitter-side complexity and downlink signaling overhead by investigating RIS-enabled blind adaptive federated learning; and (4) to design privacy-preserving RIS schemes, so that data privacy is guaranteed without compromising the convergence of federated learning. RIS and mobile edge intelligence are both key building blocks of future wireless systems. This project addresses an important and timely issue, namely, to exploit the PHY-layer advantages of RIS to greatly enhance the federated learning performance. The work, if successful, paves the way for massive integration of edge intelligence service in future wireless systems. With the PI’s solid expertise in wireless system optimization, RIS signal processing, and mobile edge intelligence, this proposal is deemed very feasible. 無線網絡中的數據的海量增加，以及人工智能應用的飛速發展，促使無線邊緣智能化成為未來無線網絡的重要研究課題。作為一種利用分布於移動用戶端的大數據來進行分布式機器學習的算法機制，聯邦學習是未來無線邊緣學習算法的重要選項之一。在實際系統中，隨機不可靠的無線傳輸環境是限制聯邦學習收斂性和準確性的主要瓶頸，而不同用戶的信道差異也造成嚴重的straggler問題，大大增加系統設計的複雜性。 大規模智能反射面是未來第六代無線通信系統的主要的使能技術之一。通過調節反射元的反射角度，智能反射面可以大幅提高無線信號在接受端的強度。當反射面被應用於聯邦學習機制中，我們需要結合聯邦學習需求，重新設計反射單元機制，以求獲得最優的有效性和收斂性。 現有的反射面設計主要針對系統的通信需求，而在無線聯邦學習中，通信和計算是兩個同等重要的需求，需要在系統優化中被聯合考慮。本項目旨在（1）分析大規模智能反射面對聯邦學習收斂性的影響、（2）聯合優化用戶調度、反射角度、以及接受端波束成型、（3）開發發送端盲傳輸算法，以降低發送端複雜度、（4）研究反射面輔助的聯邦學習中隱私保護機制。 智能反射面與移動網絡邊緣智能是未來無線通信系統的兩大基石。本項目旨在研究兩者融合，以智能反射面大幅提升聯邦學習系統性能。

14203421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14203421.value: Subgraph queries are variants of conjunctive/first-order-logic queries on binary relations and aim to extract information about a pattern graph's occurrences in a massive data graph. Some representative examples are: "count the number of 3-cycles in the friendship graph of Facebook", "in the relationship graph of Taobao, how much percentage of the 5-cliques contain a shop suspicious of cheating?", "how do the previous two statistics change over time?", and so on. These queries are essential in numerous areas, including social networks, data mining, e-commerce, communication, software engineering, transportation, bioinformatics, etc. Computing the query result from scratch incurs intolerable response time, especially for complex pattern graphs. The phenomenon calls for data structures that can reduce the query cost dramatically by consulting pre-computed information. This project plans to investigate how to maintain such data structures when the underlying data graph goes through frequent updates. The research will respond to the industry's intense demands for innovative algorithms to continuously monitor subgraph patterns' occurrence statistics. The project will cover subgraph counting, complex aggregation, and sampling, all of which are critical operations for building graph analytics systems. Besides algorithms processing those operations precisely, our study will strive to understand the inherent tradeoff between running time and approximation precision. The motivation stems from the fact that end-users can often tolerate bounded accuracy, provided that this can substantially reduce the processing cost. We expect that the project's findings will advance the theory on conjunctive queries, improve graph systems' efficiency, enhance end-users' experience, strengthen companies' competitiveness, and contribute to the open-sourced development of relevant applications. 子圖查詢在許多應用（如社交網絡、數據挖掘、電子商務、通信、軟件工程、交通、生物信息學等等）中都是不可或缺的一種操作。衆所周知，子圖查詢的時間代價是非常高昂的。若不對原數據圖進行預處理，一個算法常常會慢得讓用戶無法忍受，尤其當被查詢的子圖相對複雜時更是如此。正由於這樣的原因，爲子圖查詢設計專門的數據結構（即對原圖進行適當的預處理）以降低查詢時間一直是計算機科學裏重要的課題。 本項目旨在研究動態環境下能有效支持子圖查詢的數據結構。這裏"動態”是指原圖因為結點或邊的插入和刪除的關係發生了變化，而這種變化導致數據結構也須進行修改。現實中，用戶常常能夠接受有限度的誤差。我們發現哪怕是微小的誤差都可以讓子圖查詢的時間顯著地縮減。項目研究的重點就是去探索誤差與時間之間的數學關系，爲現實中的進行取舍提供可靠的依據。我們期望本項目的成果能對改善用戶體驗，加強公司競爭力，及設計開源代碼能做出貢獻。
