14203521.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14203521.value: Deep learning has become one of the foundation techniques in many safety-critical systems, such as autonomous vehicles and medical diagnosis systems. There is no doubt that these systems need to be resilient to both adversarial examples (AEs) that are maliciously perturbed variants of the training or test data and out-of-distribution (OOD) samples drawn from a different distribution than the training data. There has been a vast body of research to defend against such abnormal inputs. However, to the best of our knowledge, they all suffer from certain weaknesses, e.g., being able to defend against only a subset of abnormal inputs or causing accuracy loss for normal samples. Moreover, most of the existing solutions cannot defend against adaptive attacks, wherein attackers are knowledgeable about the defense mechanisms and craft adversarial examples accordingly. In this project, we plan to investigate a defense-in-depth strategy to detect AEs and OOD samples. To be specific, we categorize abnormal inputs into three types: OOD samples, AEs with small perturbation, and AEs with large perturbation. Then, we propose to defend against them in a layer-by-layer manner by combining multiple attack-agnostic defense techniques. The first layer of defense is for those AEs with large perturbation. We plan to leverage the 'noise' features extracted from the input to discover the difference between natural images and tampered ones. The last layer of defense is for those AEs with small perturbations and OOD samples. Under such circumstances, the inference result of the abnormal input would largely deviate from its semantic information. We propose a novel learning-based solution to model such contradictions for abnormal input detection. We could also resort to some existing AE detection techniques as intermediate defense layers if some AEs are more suitable for them to detect. Then, how to combine these layers of defense effectively and efficiently to achieve a high abnormal input detection rate with minimum cost is formulated as a design exploration problem and solved accordingly. The expected research output of this project is a one-off abnormal input defense solution for deep learning systems. Compared to existing techniques, it would have the following benefits: (i) a high detection rate for all kinds of abnormal inputs; (ii) little impact on the accuracy for normal samples; (iii) robust against adaptive attacks. Therefore, we expect this project's success would have a transformative impact on how future deep learning systems are designed to operate safely in the open-world environment. 深度學習已經成為許多安全關鍵系統（如自動駕駛汽車和醫療診斷系統）的基礎技術之一。毫無疑問，這些系統需要能夠抵禦惡意對抗性樣本（Adversarial Examples: AE）以及檢測與訓練數據不同的分佈外（Out-of-distribution: OOD）樣本。 儘管近年來已經有針對異常輸入的大量研究，據我們所知，現有方法都存在某些弱點。例如，只能夠抵禦異常輸入的一個子集，或者導致正常樣本的準確率大幅下降。此外，大多數現有的解決方案不能抵禦適應性攻擊，即，攻擊者對防禦機制針對性的製作對抗樣本。 在本項目中，我們計劃研究一種檢測AEs和OOD樣本深度的深度防禦策略。具體來說，我們將異常輸入分為三種類型：OOD 樣本、小擾動的AE、以及大擾動的AE。我們建議通過結合多種與攻擊無關的防禦技術，以分層的方式對它們進行逐步防禦。第一層防禦是針對那些具有較大擾動的惡意樣本。我們計劃利用從輸入中提取的 "噪聲 "特徵來發現自然圖像和被篡改圖像之間的區別。最後一層防禦是針對那些具有小擾動的AEs和OOD樣本。在這種情況下，異常輸入的推理結果會在很大程度上偏離其語義信息。我們提出了一個新穎的基於學習的解決方案，對異常輸入檢測的這種矛盾進行建模。此外，我們還可以藉助一些現有的AE檢測技術作為中間防禦層。如何將這些防禦層有效地結合起來，以最小的成本實現足夠高的異常輸入檢測率，是本項目要解決的關鍵問題。 本項目的預期研究成果是一個針對深度學習中異常輸入的一次性防禦解決方案。與現有技術相比，它將具有以下優點： (i) 對各種異常輸入有較高的檢測率；(ii) 對正常樣本的準確性影響不大；(iii) 對適應性攻擊具有魯棒性。我們預計這個項目的成功將對未來的深度學習系統如何在開放世界環境中安全運行產生較大影響。

14203521.label: Realisation of objectives
14203521.value: We have successfully realized all project objectives (100%). Our research into a "Defense-in-Depth" framework has resulted in a comprehensive suite of detection and repair mechanisms that protect deep learning systems against both Adversarial Examples (AEs) and Out-of-Distribution (OOD) samples. 1. Investigation of the Defense-in-Depth Framework (Objective 1 - 100% Achieved): We successfully investigated and validated a defense-in-depth framework. Rather than relying on a single defense layer, we developed multiple complementary techniques that target different aspects of model vulnerability. This includes: Detection Layers: We developed mechanisms based on semantic contradiction and neighborhood relations in self-supervised learning to filter out malicious inputs at inference time. Model Hardening/Repair Layers: We proposed "HybridRepair" and "HiBug", which serve as foundational layers to ensure the deployed model itself is robust and bug-free before attacks even occur. Generative Verification Layers: We integrated advanced generative models (Diffusion models) to act as verifiers for input validity. 2. Detection of AEs with Large Perturbations (Objective 2 - 100% Achieved): We addressed the detection of large perturbations through our semantic-aware detection frameworks. While our initial proposal focused on statistical "noise" features, our research evolved to leverage semantic contradiction, which is highly effective against large perturbations where the input's visual content significantly deviates from the model's classification. Our work presented at NDSS 2022 ("What You See is Not What the Network Infers") demonstrates that large perturbations invariably break the semantic consistency between the input and its reconstruction, allowing for near-perfect detection rates for this category of attacks. 3. Contradiction-Based Detection for Small Perturbations & OOD (Objective 3 - 100% Achieved): This objective resulted in our most significant breakthroughs. We successfully developed novel learning-based techniques that model the "contradiction" between inference results and semantic information: Semantic Mismatch for OOD: In our ECCV 2022 work, we introduced a detection method based on semantic mismatch under masking. This effectively identifies OOD samples by verifying if the model can consistently reconstruct masked portions of an image based on its predicted class. Diffusion-Based Guards: We advanced this concept further in ICCV 2023 with "DiffGuard," which utilizes pre-trained diffusion models to guide OOD detection. Self-Supervised Neighborhoods: For small perturbations (AEs), our ICML 2024 paper ("Be Your Own Neighborhood") utilizes neighborhood relations built on self-supervised learning to detect subtle adversarial manipulations that traditional methods miss.

14203521.label: Major findings and research outcome
14203521.value: This project has yielded 8 top-tier conference publications, establishing a robust "Defense-in-Depth" strategy for Deep Learning (DL) systems. 1. Semantic Contradiction is a Robust Indicator: Our work published in NDSS 2022 and ECCV 2022 established that comparing a model's "interpretation" of an input (via reconstruction or masking) against the raw input is a highly effective defense. We found that AEs and OOD samples exhibit a high "semantic gap" that cannot be easily hidden by attackers, providing a generic detection metric superior to traditional statistical methods. 2. Generative Models as Security Guards: With the rise of diffusion models, we validated their utility in security at ICCV 2023 (DiffGuard). We discovered that pre-trained diffusion models can act as independent verifiers, effectively "purifying" or flagging inputs that deviate from the training manifold. 3. Robustness via Repair and Interpretability: Beyond detection, we found that model repair is critical for defense-in-depth. HybridRepair (ISSTA 2022) and HiBug (NeurIPS 2023) demonstrated that annotation-efficient repair and human-interpretable debugging can significantly reduce the attack surface of DL models by fixing logic bugs and distribution shifts before deployment. 4. Advanced Attack Analysis: To ensure our defenses are robust, we also explored new attack vectors. MMA-Diffusion (CVPR 2024) analyzed multimodal attacks, while MagicDrive (ICLR 2024) explored 3D geometry control, providing insights into how future defensive systems must account for diverse, synthesized testing environments. Please note that, while the original dissemination plan specified two journal publications, we have pivoted to focus on top-tier conferences. This shift ensures our findings are shared more rapidly, keeping pace with the high velocity of development in the AI field.

14203521.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14203521.value: Multi-Modal Defense: Our work on "MMA-Diffusion" highlights the need to extend our semantic contradiction framework to multi-modal models (e.g., Vision-Language Models). We plan to adapt our detection layers to verify consistency between text and image modalities. Self-Supervised Defense Deployment: The success of our "Be Your Own Neighborhood" (ICML 2024) approach indicates that self-supervised signals are computationally efficient for real-time defense. We plan to optimize this method for deployment on edge devices (e.g., autonomous vehicles) where latency is critical.

14203521.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14203521.value: Deep Learning AI is increasingly used in safety-critical roles, such as driving cars or diagnosing diseases. However, these systems can make catastrophic errors when facing "Adversarial Examples" (images with hidden tricks designed to fool the AI) or "Out-of-Distribution" objects (things the AI has never seen before). This project successfully built a "Defense-in-Depth" security system to solve this. Think of it as a multi-layered security checkpoint. First, we use a "semantic check" where the AI must prove it understands the object—if the AI claims an image is a "Stop Sign" but cannot accurately draw one based on the image, our system flags it as an attack (Semantic Contradiction). Second, we use advanced "Repair" tools to fix bugs in the AI's logic before it is even used. Our results, published in top international venues, show this multi-layered approach acts as a robust safety net, accurately catching dangerous errors and attacks that standard systems miss, ensuring AI can operate safely in the real world.

14203721.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14203721.value: 非負矩陣分解的概率框架：從可識別模型到隨機變分推斷與多層分解

14203721.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14203721.value: 非負矩陣分解是挖掘數據中典型特征的強大工具。它已被運用到包括機器學習、計算機視覺、圖像處理、信號處理和數據科學等諸多領域，也在許多包含數據分析（生物、藥學、金融、遙感等）的科研領域發揮重要作用。非負矩陣分解在應用中的成功引起了理論科學家對探索非負矩陣分解工作原理的熱潮，並催生了一系列理論可證實的非負矩陣分解研究。理論可證實的非負矩陣分解保證了特征要素可識別性，這一點區別於傳統的非負矩陣分解。特征要素可識別性在很多應用中具備重要性，例如在醫學影像學中，確保器官的不同部分能夠被正確識別是必要的。 迄今，大量的理論可證實的非負矩陣分解研究基於幾何學框架。此項目提出一個概率學非負矩陣分解分析框架（PINNACLE）。此項目有兩方面必要的動機。其一，依據統計推斷產生的框架可更好地抵禦噪聲，然而傳統的幾何學框架在抵抗噪聲方面具有局限性。其二，可識別性在現有基於統計推斷的非負矩陣分解中鮮有研究。在PI最近的科研中發現PINNACLE具備強大的理論可識別性，其關鍵點在於大數據。同時，在變分推斷框架下，PINNACLE可被視為傳統非負矩陣分解的一個正則化變形，此結果創新性地建立了傳統非負矩陣分解與統計推斷的聯繫。從結果展示了難得的科研契機。此項目旨在研究高斯噪聲下包涵一大類統計數據模型的PINNACLE模型，分析其識別性，並且為其設計推斷算法。解決此類推斷問題具有很高的挑戰性。我們將結合統計推斷（尤其是變分推斷）和運籌學（例如結構化矩陣分解和大數據中的非凸優化）來量身設計推斷算法，而現有研究少有此類設計。另外，近來多層非負矩陣分解（又稱為深度矩陣分解）因為其更強的模型可解釋性引起越來越多的科研關注。此項目也將研究PINNACLE處理多層非負矩陣分解及其應用。 此項目在本質上屬於基礎科研，是匯集大數據估計、統計推斷、運籌學和結構化矩陣分解的交叉科研。此項目旨在豐富非負矩陣分解理論與方法，具有基礎科研的重要性，對實際應用產生長遠影響。此項研究深度挖掘大數據大樣本的良好結構特性，並非常適合運用於機器學習與數據科學中的大數據問題。

14203821.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14203821.value: 術中HRCT引導下的µ-EBOCT肺泡成像用於量化病理組織的研究

14203821.label: Project Objectives
14203821.value: Aim 1: Design and fabricate a portable µ-EBOCT engine, an ultrathin 3D-printed endoscope that corrects for aberrations and compensates for dispersion mismatch, and a fast and compact rotary joint. Expected outcome/impact: Our system will operate at 800 nm with a super-broad spectral bandwidth of approximately 250 nm. We will develop an ultrathin monolithic OCT endoscope with a small form factor of ~500 µm in diameter (including the plastic sheath) using two-photon polymerization to 3D print the 125-µm-diameter freeform micro-optics directly onto the single-mode fiber. A novel triplet micro-optics design that combines a spot size reducer and two freeform surfaces will overcome spherical and chromatic aberrations and astigmatism, provide an optimal numerical aperture. In addition, we will use a common-path distal optics configuration to automatically cancel the dispersion mismatch between the reference and sample beams. This new endoscope will feature an ultrahigh axial resolution (<2 µm in air), an optimal transversal resolution (~7 µm), and an appropriate depth of focus. With a self-made high-speed and compact rotary joint (not commercially available for an 800-nm broadband source), the endoscope of the portable µ-EBOCT system will perform a circumferential scan at ≥20 frames/sec, thereby enabling real-time volumetric imaging of alveoli in the clinical setting and a short µ-EBOCT intervention during bronchoscopy procedures (i.e., ~10 minutes). Aim 2: Develop a few-shot learning graph neural network (GNN) to automatedly quantify alveolar microstructures and integrate the algorithm into the µ-EBOCT system for real-time pathology assessment. Expected outcome/impact: Conventionally, OCT images cannot be directly interpreted by clinicians without special training. More importantly, high-speed OCT generates a large amount of volumetric imaging data (up to tens of GBs). Therefore, an automated image assessment tool with an accuracy comparable to that of an expert reviewer is highly desirable to cope with the increasing volume of diagnostic images and the shortage of available human expertise to interpret them. To reduce the reliance on annotated data and utilize 3D sequential features, we will develop a new few-shot learning GNN that combines an augmentation method with a self-supervised mechanism and a sequential model. This GNN-assisted quantitative pathology approach will further enhance the clinical viability of µ-EBOCT in performing objective pathology assessments at patients’ bedsides. Aim 3: Validate the performances of µ-EBOCT and intraoperative-HRCT guided alveolar imaging in a clinical setting and conduct a prospective trial on 20 patients with a variety of alveolar diseases and disease severities. Expected outcome/impact: The feasibility of accurately deploying the ultrathin endoscope to targeted sites in the lungs and imaging alveolar pathology with the intraoperative guidance of HRCT in the clinical setting will be demonstrated. This study will provide new information about the structural changes in the alveoli of humans with alveolar diseases for a broad spectrum of disease severity. The ability to automatedly quantify such changes in vivo will have great significance in understanding these diseases. This work will provide the opportunity to correlate the structural properties of alveoli identified by both HRCT and µ-EBOCT with the types and severities of alveolar diseases in humans. The work will also enable future development of novel treatment evaluations by noninvasively quantifying the effects of treatment on alveoli.

14203821.value: 肺泡是呼吸系統的核心。影響肺泡的疾病，例如急性呼吸窘迫綜合徵 (ARDS)，會損害關鍵的氣體交換功能，導致危及生命的呼吸系統衰竭。比如近年的 COVID-19 大流行，冠狀病毒會入侵並損傷肺泡，在全球範圍內導致入住重症監護病房的 ARDS 患者數目激增。儘管肺泡至關重要，能夠對其進行在體的組織病理學成像和量化的技術手段仍然非常有限。由於對肺泡進行活檢存在困難，目前研究肺泡病理的方法仍然依賴於間接的肺功能測試、屍檢獲得的組織病理圖像、或常規的放射成像檢查。 最近開發的支氣管光學相干斷層掃描 (EBOCT) 技術能夠以微米級的分辨率對體內氣道進行三維成像。目前該技術仍然無法用於準確檢測和量化肺泡的微結構和相關的細微病理變化。這主要是由於（1）傳統 EBOCT 的分辨率 (~10 µm) 仍然不夠，(2) 沒有可進入末端支氣管對肺泡進行在體成像的微型內窺鏡，(3) 沒有可行的術中引導技術將內窺鏡精確部署到肺深部的可疑部位，以及 (4) 沒有可靠的方法用以實現 三維OCT 圖像的實時自動定量分析。 在本項目中，我們提議 (1) 開發便攜高分辨率的µ-EBOCT 技術和超微型的內窺鏡，用以實現對末端支氣管和肺泡的快速在體三維成像； (2) 開發新的神經網絡技術用以實現自動化定量組織病理分析，並將其集成到 µ-EBOCT 系統中； (3)招募20 名患有各種肺部疾病的患者，進行前瞻性的肺泡成像試驗，以驗證 μ-EBOCT技術和術中 HRCT 引導的性能。這項創新的技術將為在體肺泡病理學的成像和量化提供新的手段，期望可以促進對相關疾病的病理和治療的研究，並最終幫助優化患者的治療效果。

14203821.label: Realisation of objectives
14203821.value: Aim 1: Design and fabricate a portable µ-EBOCT engine, an ultrathin 3D-printed endoscope that corrects for aberrations and compensates for dispersion mismatch, and a fast and compact rotary joint. Part of the related results were reported in journal publications No. 2, 5, 6 and 8-11 and conference papers No. 1-2 (please refer to Part C), two patents (US 63/538,716; CN 202410901042.6) are related to Aim 1.2. Aim 1.1: the development of portable µ-EBOCT engine and compact rotary joint. For the portable µ-EBOCT engine, we developed a compact 800-nm spectral-domain OCT system featuring a custom broad-spectrum (~250 nm) superluminescent diode (Superlum) and a high-speed spectrometer with an A-scan rate of 250 kHz (Cobra-S, Wasatch). Regarding the rotary joint, we engineered a compact, high-speed fiber-optic rotary joint designed for proximal scanning endoscopy. This rotary joint corrects chromatic aberration, achieves one-way throughput exceeding 70%, maintains optical coupling variation within ±5% during continuous rotation, and exhibits back-reflection below -60 dB. With this rotary joint, imaging speeds of up to 20 frames per second are attainable. Aim 1.2: the development of ultrathin 3D-printed endoscope with diameter of ~500 µm. We have developed a novel endoscope utilizing in-house liquid-shaping 3D printing technology to achieve a compact, monolithic probe with high-resolution imaging capabilities. Semi-spherical micro-lenses of various sizes and shapes are fabricated using a 3D printer. The ultrathin OCT fiber probe consists of a single-mode fiber (SMF), a non-core fiber (NCF), and a custom micro-lens. The NCF is first spliced to the SMF and then coupled to the micro-lens at an incident angle θ using optical glue (NOA81). The distal optics are protected by a hypodermic tube, while the remaining fiber probe is enclosed in a torque coil. The entire assembly is housed in a 500-µm diameter plastic sheath, allowing free rotation of the endoscope within the sheath. The performance of the endoscope was characterized using the 800-nm µ-EBOCT system. The OCT laser beam diameter was measured in both x and y directions with an optical beam profiler (BladeCam2-XHR, DataRay Inc.). At approximately 240 µm from the sheath’s outer surface, the focused beam spot achieved a transverse resolution of ~4.5 µm. The estimated depth of focus is about 200 µm, determined by polynomial fitting of mean beam diameters within the range where the beam size was less than twice the focused spot size. Achromaticity was confirmed by less than 5% variation in axial resolution (~2.4 µm) along a 1-mm imaging depth and by stable back-reflected spectra with mirror translation, demonstrating the endoscope’s ultrahigh resolving capability. Aim 2: Develop a few-shot learning graph neural network to automatedly quantify alveolar microstructures and integrate the algorithm into the µ-EBOCT system for real-time pathology assessment. Part of the related results were reported in journal publications No. 1, 3, 4, 7 and conference papers No. 3 and 4 (please refer to Part C). Aim 2.1: the development of few-shot learning graph neural network algorithm for automated quantification of airway and alveolar microstructures. We developed a Transformer-based neural network for automated quantification of airway and alveolar microstructures in OCT images, utilizing sheep and dog airway datasets. The model leverages tissue continuity in 3D datasets and efficiently utilizes limited annotated data by incorporating unannotated samples. This approach (1) reduces dependence on large annotated datasets and (2) effectively captures long-range spatial features, enhancing semantic segmentation of sequential data. Model performance was validated on a test dataset, showing high concordance with expert manual annotations informed by histology. The automated detection achieved over 0.8 IoU for each airway microstructure, including alveoli, with a mean IoU of approximately 0.92. Aim 2.2: implementation and validation of the automated quantification model in µ-EBOCT system. To enable real-time processing, we applied model compression techniques—including channel pruning, head pruning, and quantization—to optimize and accelerate inference for airway quantification. Experimental results demonstrate that our method segments OCT airway images at over 20 frames per second, exceeding the acquisition speed of our imaging system (which is normally 20 frames per second). Aim 3: Validate the performances of µ-EBOCT and intraoperative-HRCT guided alveolar imaging in a clinical setting and conduct a prospective trial on 20 patients with a variety of alveolar diseases and disease severities. Part of the related results were reported in journal publications No. 9 and 10 (please refer to Part C). Aim 3.1: the performance validation of µ-EBOCT and intraoperative-HRCT guided airway/alveolar imaging in pre-clinical pig models. The in vivo pig lung imaging protocol was approved by the Animal Experimentation Ethics Committee of CUHK. Three pigs were anesthetized according to the approved guidelines, and µ-EBOCT airway imaging was conducted under bronchoscopy and HRCT guidance. The imaging endoscope was introduced into the small airway through the 2.2-mm working channel of a bronchoscope (Ambu aScope 4 Broncho) and positioned at the target lung section using bronchoscopic visualization and real-time HRCT imaging. High-quality OCT images were successfully obtained in all cases, clearly delineating airway microstructures including epithelium, glands, cartilage, and alveoli. Aim 3.2: the performance validation of µ-EBOCT for airway/alveolar imaging in patient specimens. We obtained ethical approval from the 301 Hospital in Beijing and transported our µ-EBOCT system to the facility for collaborative research. In a prospective study, we imaged specimens from over 20 patients who underwent lobectomy or segmentectomy for various lung diseases, including lung cancer, asthma, and COPD. Our primary focus was on alveolar imaging and the assessment of related pathologies, particularly in asthma and COPD patients. Preliminary findings revealed marked pathological features such as enlarged and ruptured alveolar sacs in COPD patients, and significant airway wall remodeling in asthma patients. Although this project ended, our OCT lung imaging study is ongoing. Following comprehensive safety and performance validation, we intend to extend µ-EBOCT imaging to in vivo human lung applications in the future.

14203821.label: Major findings and research outcome
14203821.value: The major research outcome includes 11 published journal papers, 4 conference papers, and 2 patents (please refer to Part C). The major findings include: 1. Developed a novel 800 nm µ-EBOCT imaging system achieving ultrahigh axial resolution of 2.4 µm (in air) and fast A-scan speeds up to 250 kHz, surpassing the conventional 100 kHz rate. 2. Engineered a compact, high-speed rotary joint enabling µ-EBOCT imaging at up to 20 frames per second—a critical advancement for in vivo lung imaging. 3. Fabricated 3D-printed OCT endoscopes with a diameter of approximately 500 µm using an in-house liquid shaping technology. 4. Developed a Transformer-based automated quantification method for detection, segmentation, and analysis of airway microstructures, achieving a mean IoU of 0.92—comparable to experienced OCT reviewers. 5. Integrated the automated quantification algorithm into the µ-EBOCT system, enabling real-time segmentation and quantification of airway microstructures at over 20 frames per second—faster than the image acquisition rate and suitable for real-time clinical applications. 6. Validated the µ-EBOCT system for high-resolution imaging of airways and alveoli in vivo in pigs, with the guidance of HRCT. 7. Demonstrated the capability of µ-EBOCT to identify characteristic alveolar pathologies in patient specimens, including distinct features of COPD and asthma.

14203821.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14203821.value: For the next phase of the project: 1. We will further enhance the automated quantification method for real-time integration with the µ-EBOCT system, improving model performance and reliability using a newly curated airway image dataset. 2. We plan to develop an AI-assisted copilot to automate endoscope navigation within the lungs under intraoperative CT guidance, optimizing the clinical utility of the µ-EBOCT system and reducing radiation exposure for physicians. 3. Although the µ-EBOCT system has met key technological milestones, further clinical validation is necessary. We will conduct in vivo studies in patients to assess its performance for high-resolution imaging of airway and alveolar pathologies.

14203821.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14203821.value: Alveoli are tiny air sacs in our lungs that are vital for breathing, but diseases like COVID-19, asthma, and COPD can severely damage them and lead to life-threatening complications. Unfortunately, it is difficult for doctors to see and measure changes in these tiny structures using current imaging techniques, which lack the detail needed to guide treatment. Our research team is developing a cutting-edge imaging system that combines an ultra-thin, high-resolution microscope and advanced artificial intelligence. With this portable tool, doctors can see detailed, real-time images of the alveoli inside the living lung, something never before possible. The built-in AI quickly analyzes these images, helping doctors detect early signs of disease, understand how conditions progress, and monitor how well treatments are working. By making the invisible visible, our technology could revolutionize how lung diseases are diagnosed and treated. It holds promise for better patient care, safer and more effective therapies, and a deeper understanding of diseases that threaten millions worldwide.

14203921.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14203921.value: Spatial cable-driven parallel robots (S-CDPRs) have meaningful applications for various industries, such as building construction, large-scale manufacturing, structure inspection and maintenance of utilities, due to its simplicity and ability to manoeuvre in large spaces. However, one inherent drawback of this type of robot is its ability to perform dexterous motion and operate in tight spaces. One novel solution to this problem is to mount hyper-redundant snake-like cable-driven robots (HR-CDPR) on the spatial CDPR platform. In this hybrid arrangement (SHR-CDPR), the spatial CDPR can translate over a large (from 10 to 100m) workspace zone, while the hyper-redundant component can perform dexterous motion and navigate into tight spaces and cavities. Existing hyper-redundant CDPRs and rigid robot arm hybrid CDPRs both have a limited payload capability in order to keep the actuators lightweight. The proposed SHR-CDPR resolves this issue as all actuating motors are situated at the base platform, and route all cables to the hyper-redundant robot through the base platform. The goal of the system is to be able to operate within spaces between 10m to 100m, while carrying a payload of 30kg at 2m span of the hyper-redundant arm. For the novel SHR-CDPR, several significant challenges will be studied to achieve the following breakthroughs: 1) the incorporation of internal cable-routing with reconfiguration to significantly increase the hyper-redundant robot’s workspace and payload capabilities; 2) the study of the workspace for the SHR-CDPR possessing a high number of degrees-of-freedom in order to optimally design suitable cable-routing and attachments; and 3) the development of a learning iterative-learning control framework that can combine the advantages of model-based and model-free approaches, where the learning component will provide a rich insight to the importance of the different robot model parameters. Furthermore, the design and control of SHR-CDPRs will be used in the prototype development of a 22 degrees-of-freedom SHR-CDPR. The potential applications for the proposed robot include cleaning of sewage sedimentation tanks, inspection of aircraft hangers and operations within deep underground building foundation bored-piles. 基於空間繩索驅動並聯機器人 (S-CDPR)簡單的構造和其宏大的工作空間特性，使它們在建築施工、重工業、結構檢查和公用設施的維護與檢修等各個行業中具有實際的用途。然而，其中一個固有缺點是在狹窄的空間中，它們缺乏靈巧性去執行較為複雜的任務。其中一種創新的解決方法是在S-CDPR 平台上安裝超冗餘蛇形繩索驅動機器人 (HR-CDPR)。在這種混合排列 (SHR-CDPR) 中，S-CDPR 可以在一個宏大的工作空間（從 10 到 100米）中進行平移，而蛇形機器人可以進入到狹窄的空間，執行各種複雜的任務。為了減輕驅動器的重量，現有的HR-CDPR 和剛性機械臂混合 CDPR的載荷能力都因此而受限。我們所提議的 SHR-CDPR 足以解決這個問題，因為所有驅動電機都位於外置框架上，並通過工作平台將所有繩索佈線到超冗餘機器人。該系統的目標是能夠在 10米 到 100米 的空間內有效運行，同時在超冗餘機器臂的 2米 跨度上有 30公斤 的有效載荷。 對於此新型 SHR-CDPR，研究將有以下幾個重大挑戰：1）研究內部繩索佈線和其可重構的機制，以增加超冗餘機器臂的工作空間和有效載荷能力； 2) 研究多自由度SHR-CDPR 的工作空間，以優化其繩索佈線和連接位的設計； 3) 開發迭代學習控制算法，綜合模型控制和無模型控制的優點，以求得不同模型參數的重要性。此外，SHR-CDPR 的設計和控制算法亦可延伸於高自由度 SHR-CDPR 的開發。此機器人的潛在應用包括：清潔污水沉澱池、檢查飛機吊架、以及鑽孔式深樁地基內的各種任務。

14203921.label: Major findings and research outcome
14203921.value: Overall, this project and its objectives were successfully completed. The major findings could be summarised as follows: - The development of a generalised model for SHR-CDPRs, where the model encapsulates traditional spatial CDPRs, multiple rigid body cable-driven robots, and even continuum (flexible) cable-driven robots. By utilising the Frenet frame along the support connecting rod, the proposed method establishes CDR models with arbitrary cable routing schemes in a unified mathematical form. This then allows an entire class of CDPRs, and their hybrid permutations to be studied. - The optimisation-based design framework for the design of SHR-CDPRs, including both the kinematic design of the backbone using an RRT approach, and the location of cable attachments using a divide-and-conquer optimisation approach that designs the cable one-by-one. It was shown that as a result of this approach, each cable attachment design results in a convex optimisation problem that can be conveniently solved. - The development of a control framework for SHR-CDPRs through a hybrid reactive and iterative learning control approach. The primary challenge to overcome was the high redundancy, and hence the possibility to not satisfy the dynamics constraints of CDPRs. To achieve this, the reactive approach resolves the high actuation redundancy to ensure feasibility but may not achieve good performance over a prescribed trajectory. Additionally, the iterative controller then optimises the kinematic redundancy null space over repetition of the entire trajectory. Results in simulation and hardware show the performance and applicability of the controller. - To tackle the complex geometry of the end-effector of SHR-CDPRs, a generalised wrapping model was developed. - In addition to fundamental research, practical prototypes, including a large-scale real-world robot for bored-pile construction, were developed in this project. Through this project, two graduate students were trained, Dr. Grace Yaoxin Guo who focused on the modelling, design and analysis for the generalised class of SHR-CDPRs, and Mr. Thomas Hing Cheung Chan who focused on developing an application for the SHR-CDPR within building construction of bored piles. This work has resulted in a U.S. Non-Provisional Patent being granted. Regarding academic publications, this project has resulted in three journal publications (1 within the journal Mechanisms and Machine Theory, 1 within the ASME Journal of Mechanical Design and 1 within IEEE Transactions on Control and Systems Technology) and one conference publication. Moreover, two publications are in preparation with submission expected in early 2026.

14203921.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14203921.value: This project has led to further development to other types of flexible CDPRs, such as soft robotic surface end-effectors for CDPRs, and large-scale inflatable backbone cable-driven robot with origami joints. The successes of these developments can be combined with this project, where long reach inflatable cable robots can be mounted on top of the spatial CDPR end-effector. The modelling and analysis developed through this project are used for these further developments. Practically, different applications related to building construction are being and will be further explored. The proposed course of action to execute these works include further grant applications with the RGC GRF, RGC RIF and ITF funding.

14203921.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14203921.value: This project aims to develop a novel class of hybrid cable-driven parallel robots that combine traditional parallel cable-driven robots (CDPR) with a hyper-redundant cable-driven robot that is mounted on the CDPR's end-effector platform, named SHR-CDPR. The SHR-CDPR aims to combine the advantages of CDPRs, such as large workspace and simple to set up robot, and enhances it further to increase its dexterity and orientation workspace. Through the project, several important aspects were considered, including: 1) the development of a generalised model for SHR-CDPRs; 2) the design of the kinematic structure and optimisation of cable attachment locations; 3) the development of a hybrid reactive and iterative learning controller for SHR-CDPRs; and 4) analysis for SHR-CDPRs such as workspace analysis and cable wrapping models. In addition to the fundamental developments on the modelling, analysis and control, the project explored the practical development and real-world applications. This includes lab prototypes on 1m - 2m scale systems, and a larger robot for the application of cleaning building bored-piles during construction (BORED robot). The BORED robot consists of a vertical cable-driven platform with a secondary continuum hose cable-driven robot. These examples show the practical relevancy for this class of robot.

14204021.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14204021.value: The objective of this project is to study a novel research problem on transferring knowledge from multiple source domains to a target domain in a privacy-preserving manner. Only the source-domain models without their data are publicly accessible for training the target-domain model with target data. The source and target domains do not need to have any common samples or class labels. Online communications between distributed servers are forbidden. This is a more challenging but realistic problem setup for real-world scenarios. Existing deep learning techniques, including federated learning, continual learning, transfer learning, data-free knowledge distillation, private knowledge transfer, cannot be readily extended to solve the new problem. Federated learning requires constant communications between the computational nodes. Continual learning aims to match the performance of multi-task learning. Transfer learning without specific designs has difficulties in avoiding the catastrophic forgetting phenomenon. Data-free knowledge distillation compresses a large model into a smaller one only in a single domain. Existing private knowledge distillation techniques generally assume that the source and target domains share the same class labels. To solve the novel problem, we propose to first build a strong baseline framework to validate the feasibility of using only pre-trained source-domain models without their data to guide the learning of a model in the target domain. The cross-domain knowledge transfer will be conducted via knowledge distillation. However, we observe that the knowledge gaps between different domains are generally large and imbalanced. We will investigate two novel multi-domain co-adaption strategies to mitigate the knowledge gaps for achieving effective private knowledge transfer. The first strategy adopts meta-learning for tuning the source-domain networks to determine what knowledge should be encoded by the source-domain models and how to balance the multiple source domains, such that the target-domain model can maximize its performance via knowledge transfer. The second strategy aims to learn a series of proxy networks of the multi-domain models. The multi-domain proxies are trained to mutually adapt each other to gradually close the knowledge gaps between the domains. Private knowledge transfer between the proxies would be much efficient. For unsupervised learning models, we propose to adopt pseudo labels and contrastive learning for encoding their knowledge and generalize the proposed algorithms to transfer private knowledge for unsupervised learning. The successful implementation of this project would develop novel privacy-preserving deep learning algorithms that are more suitable for real-world scenarios. The privacy issues and concerns on training modern AI models can be significantly mitigated. 本項目旨在研究一個新的機器學習問題，以一種保持隱私的方式將多個源域的知識轉移至目標域。該問題假設在訓練中僅有基於源域數據訓練的模型是可獲得的，而源域的數據在訓練目標域的目標模型時不可獲得，源域和目標域也可以沒有任何共同的樣本和類別，且分散式訓練服務器之間的在綫通訊也是被禁止的。這是一個更加富有挑戰性和真實的問題定義。已有的深度學習技術，包括聯邦學習、持續學習、遷移學習、無數據自蒸餾等，不能夠直接的被用於解決這個新的研究問題。爲了解決這個問題，本項目首先提出一個強而有效的基綫模型來驗證該問題的可行性：將跨領域的知識通過使用蒸餾技術遷移。我們觀察到不同域之間的知識鴻溝過大且不均衡。本項目計劃研究面嚮多數據域聯合適應的策略來減弱數據域之間的知識鴻溝從而實現隱私知識的有效遷移，我們提出使用一系列跨數據域代理模型的方案。這些跨數據域代理被訓練為同時互相適應而逐漸縮小不同模型之間的數據域鴻溝，這些代理模型之間的隱私知識遷移因而可以實現高效化。針對無監督學習模型，我們提出使用偽標簽和對比學習來編碼它們的知識并將本項目的維持隱私性的知識遷移方法擴展至無監督學習模型的知識遷移。該項目的成功實施可以研發富有創新性的維持隱私的深度學習模型，且更適用於真實世界的應用場景，針對當代人工智能模型訓練的所需訓練數據的隱私性擔憂也可以被大大降低。

14204321.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14204321.value: The ankle joint is the second most common site vulnerable to osteochondral defects (OCD), which ranks second only behind the knee joint. Osteochondral defects of the talus (OCDT) are often caused by traumatic events such as ankle sprains or fractures. In due time these OCDT can progress to ankle joint osteoarthritis (OA) with prolonged pain and joint dysfunction. Articular cartilage repair remains clinical challenges. Accurate and reliable assessment tools for evaluating outcomes of cartilage repair are critical for both improvement of existing procedures and development of new methods. Histological evaluation based on biopsies is the golden standard for articular cartilage assessment; however, biopsies are not still widely used in intra-operative assessment or studies of the cartilage repair due to their invasiveness nature. The spatial resolutions of conventional clinical imaging (X-ray, CT, MRI and ultrasound) are insufficient to assess early OA changes in a small joint like the ankle. One possible solution would be to use Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT) to enable in situ microscopic imaging of the osteochondral tissues to guide the cartilage repair surgeries. However, navigating within ankle joint for OCT endomicroscopy is difficult for the ankle is a constricted and curved joint and the risk of damaging cartilage or ligaments is higher than most other arthroscopic surgeries. Hence, our objective of this project is to improve access to the OCDT by designing and developing an image-guided hand-held concentric tube robotic endomicroscopy instrumented with position/shape sensors and fiber optic OCT probe for in situ cartilage quality assessment to facilitate cartilage repair surgeries. Hence, the proposed specific aims are: Aim 1 : Develop a hand-held concentric tube robotic (CTR) endomicroscopy incorporated with an OCT imaging probe and Fiber Bragg Grating (FBG) sensors to aid in navigating within the ankle joint for delivery of the OCT probe to the leision sites. Aim 2 : Develop a surgical navigation system that fuses the pre-operative MRI, intra-operative arthroscopic and OCT imaging for enhanced perception of the CTR endomicroscopy and neighboring osteochondral anatomy. Both FBG sensors and macroscopic MRI/arthroscopic imaging provide spatial guidance to the targeted osteochondral lesion and thereafter OCT enables in situ volumetric microscopic assessment. Aim 3 : Validate the CTR endomicroscopic device assisted by surgical navigation system in cadaveric ankles. Aim 4 : Establish OCT quantitative criteria and evaluate the preclinical feasibility and accuracy of CTR endomicroscopy with integrated OCT in identifying healthy cartilage vs. cartilage leasions due to injury and degeneration in cadaveric ankles. 踝關節已成為易引發軟骨損傷的第二大關節（僅次於膝關節）。距骨軟骨損傷常由踝關節創傷所致（扭傷或骨折），隨時間進展可演變為踝骨關節炎（OA），並伴隨長期疼痛與運動障礙。基於活檢的組織學評估是關節軟骨評估的金標準，但由於其有創性，未被廣泛用於評估軟骨損傷與術中修復狀況；對於踝關節等小關節，臨床常用成像（X射線、CT、MRI和超聲）的有限空間解析度無法精確檢測OA早期徵兆。因此，研發高解析度原位軟骨評估工具，對於準確評估關節軟骨損傷至關重要。光學相幹斷層掃描（OCT），作為一種有效解決方案，可實現關節軟骨原位顯微成像，引導術中軟骨修復。然而，由於踝關節複雜的解剖結構，在其狹窄彎曲關節腔內進行OCT顯微內鏡檢查極具挑戰性，其損傷軟骨或韌帶的風險高於其他關節鏡手術。因此，該專案總體目標是通過研發一個宏觀-微觀跨尺度影像引導下的手持同心管機器人輔助顯微內鏡工具（集成位置/形狀傳感器和光纖OCT探頭），通過柔性機器人輔助遞送OCT探頭至踝關節軟骨損傷部位，進行基於顯微內窺成像的原位軟骨質量評估與術中軟骨修復引導。 該項目可分為4個子任務： 任務1：開發手持同心管柔性機器人(CTR)輔助顯微內鏡工具，集成OCT成像探頭和光纖布拉格光柵(FBG)傳感器，精確安全遞送OCT內鏡至軟骨損傷微小病灶處； 任務2：開發“宏觀-微觀”跨尺度手術導航系統，融合術前MRI、術中關節鏡和內窺OCT成像多源資訊，提升對柔性機器人輔助顯微內鏡工具和毗鄰軟骨組織的智能感知。FBG形狀感知和宏觀尺度的MRI/關節鏡影像提供空間引導資訊，微小病灶處的三維OCT成像提供軟骨微觀尺度原位量化評估； 任務3：通過屍體驗證試驗，開展跨尺度影像引導柔性機器人輔助顯微內窺系統的性能評估； 任務4：建立基於三維OCT的軟骨質量量化評估標準，通過採用該新型顯微內鏡工具辨識健康軟骨與損傷軟骨，開展臨床前可行性評估。

14204321.label: Major findings and research outcome
14204321.value: This pioneering research has established a transformative paradigm in musculoskeletal diagnostics through the development of the world's first image-guided robotic endomicroscopy platform for microscopic joint assessment. By synergizing cutting-edge robotics, advanced optical imaging, and intelligent navigation technologies, our system represents a leap forward in minimally invasive joint evaluation. The project's groundbreaking contributions across its four key research objectives are detailed below: Aim 1: Hand-Held CTR Endomicroscopy Development We conceived an innovative approach to joint imaging by integrating concentric tube robotics with advanced optical technologies. The system combines steerable tubular architecture with Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT), overcoming traditional limitations in accessing constrained joint spaces. Our computational design methodology, incorporating statistical shape modeling, enabled optimal navigation through complex anatomical geometries while maintaining clinical practicality. The incorporation of fiber optic sensing represents a significant advance in real-time device tracking for endoscopic procedures. Aim 2: Multi-Modal Surgical Navigation System The research developed a groundbreaking surgical navigation framework that bridges multiple imaging scales. Our technical innovation lies in the seamless fusion of pre-operative volumetric imaging with intraoperative microscopic visualization, creating a unified surgical workspace. The platform's novel registration approach and hybrid tracking architecture establish new capabilities for transitioning between tissue-level and cellular-resolution assessment during arthroscopic procedures. Aim 3: System Validation Through comprehensive anatomical testing, we demonstrated the system's clinical viability in realistic surgical conditions. The validation protocol confirmed the technology's ability to safely access and assess challenging joint regions while preserving surrounding tissues, establishing a foundation for future clinical translation. Aim 4: OCT Quantitative Criteria The research established new standards for optical diagnostics in joint pathology by correlating advanced OCT parameters with histological findings. Our analytical framework enables non-invasive characterization of tissue degeneration at previously unattainable resolutions, creating an alternative to invasive biopsy procedures for disease monitoring. Overall Significance This work represents a fundamental advancement in minimally invasive joint diagnostics, introducing the first navigation-integrated robotic OCT platform capable of microscopic assessment in complex anatomies. The system's modular architecture and innovative technological integration create new possibilities for both small and large joint applications. The project has generated multiple intellectual property developments and is currently progressing toward clinical translation through industrial partnerships.

14204321.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14204321.value: This research lays the foundation for several promising future directions: 1. Clinical Translation & Expanded Validation: The next phase involves clinical trials to evaluate real-world performance in diagnostic and therapeutic applications. Long-term studies could assess the system’s role in early osteoarthritis detection and guided interventions. 2. Enhanced AI Integration: Machine learning could refine OCT image interpretation, automating biomarker detection and improving diagnostic accuracy. Federated learning approaches may enable multi-center data aggregation while preserving patient privacy. 3. Miniaturization & Multi-Joint Adaptation: Further optimization could reduce device size for pediatric or tighter joint spaces (e.g., wrist, TMJ). Modular redesign may facilitate compatibility with existing surgical robots. 4. Therapeutic Extensions: Combining diagnostics with targeted micro-interventions (e.g., laser ablation, localized drug delivery) could transition the platform from assessment to treatment. Proposed Implementation Pathway: 1. Short-term (0-2 yrs): Finalize regulatory approvals through industry partnerships (e.g., arthroscopy device manufacturers) 2. Mid-term (2-5 yrs): Conduct multi-center trials while refining AI-assisted analytics 3. Long-term (5+ yrs): Develop next-generation systems with closed-loop therapy capabilities This roadmap positions the technology to evolve from a diagnostic tool into an intelligent surgical assistant for precision joint preservation.

14204321.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14204321.value: This research has created a breakthrough medical technology—a tiny, intelligent camera system that helps doctors examine joints with incredible detail during minimally invasive procedures. Unlike current methods that either provide broad views or require tissue removal, our system combines robotic precision with advanced imaging to see microscopic damage while navigating tight joint spaces safely. The key innovation is a flexible, pencil-sized robotic scope that can: 1. Move like a snake through complex joint anatomy 2. Take ultra-high-resolution 3D images of cartilage and bone 3. Work seamlessly with existing surgical tools This means doctors could potentially detect early arthritis or sports injuries at the cellular level without cutting tissue, allowing for earlier and more precise treatments. The technology has been successfully tested in ex vivo studies and is being developed for real-world use through medical industry partnerships. By replacing invasive biopsies and improving diagnostic accuracy, this system could transform how joint disorders are managed—helping patients recover faster with less pain. Future versions may even guide microscopic repairs during the same procedure. The project has already generated some technologies that may benefit various medical specialties beyond orthopedics.

14204521.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14204521.value: Visual scene understanding is one of the holy grail problems in computer vision. There is a wide range of scene understanding tasks such as scene categorization, scene parsing, layout detection, and scene graph generation. Previous deep learning methods consider the scene understanding as supervised image recognition, thus rely heavily on training with the human annotations. Meanwhile, various scene understanding tasks are studied separately through ad-hoc annotated data and designed models, ignoring the potential synergy among the tasks. We propose a novel generative approach for scene understanding. Rather than following the standard pipeline of annotating data and training classifiers, the proposed generative approach learns a hierarchy of visual concepts from synthesizing images. The generative approach brings a new paradigm to the conventional classification-based scene understanding, unifying separately studied scene recognition tasks and scene editing into a single framework. This framework will develop several technical innovations: (1) a novel generative model is designed to incorporate the scene layout and the scene graph as priors. The scene layout describes the overall 3D scene structure while the scene graph indicate the representative objects and their spatial relations, providing the crucial structural knowledge in the generation. (2) To disentangle and identify the visual concepts in the learned representation, we propose to embed invertible mappings in the generative model's latent space. This invertible mapping will align the latent space with visual concepts to steer the image generation process, such as adding or removing some visual concepts in the output image. (3) To enable taking a real image as input, we will further propose a multi-task encoder network. The encoder is trained from the image reconstruction by considering the trained generator as a loss; thus, it can distill the disentangled and semantically aligned features in the generative representation. This encoder will predict multiple visual concepts such as scene graph and scene attributes from the input while allows users to edit the concepts then reconstruct the edited result from the generator. This proposed generative approach will solve both the discriminative tasks such as scene categorization and scene parsing, and the generative tasks such as scene manipulation and view synthesis, under a single framework. We will benchmark the proposed approach with other ad-hoc methods on each task separately. We will conduct ablation studies to evaluate the synergies of the learned representation brought by combining different tasks. We will open-source the proposed methods for benefiting the computer vision community. 視覺場景理解是計算機視覺中的關鍵問題之一，包含諸多應用方向，如場景分類，場景分割，場景圖生成等。過去的深度學習方法通常把場景理解問題當做監督學習任務，通過人為標定大量數據來進行。與此同時，不同的場景理解應用都分別標定自己特有的數據以及設計特定的模型，而忽略了數據和模型之間的通用性。 本研究項目會提出一個新的生成式場景理解框架。跟之前分別標定數據然後進行監督學習的場景理解框架不同之處在於，我們是以圖片生成作為監督信號，來學習具有泛化性的場景理解表征。本研究課題會探索新的方法，嘗試把場景生成和場景理解統一到一個框架之中。學習出來的表征可以既用到生成任務之中，也可以用到分類任務之中，實現一個統一的深度學習表征學習方法。

14204621.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14204621.value: 從癌癥到傳染性疾病，如當前全球SARS- CoV-2的擴散等，低成本的快速核酸檢測設備對於疾病的控製和檢測發揮著關鍵作用。低成本的核酸快速檢測設備在許多疾病的控製和評估中發揮著關鍵作用，從癌癥到感染，如當前全球SARS- CoV-2大流行。雖然聚合酶鏈反應(PCR)是目前檢測和定量目標DNA/RNA的金標準，但數字PCR (dPCR)作為一種新興的、通過對高度稀釋的液滴型PCR反應腔群體進行泊松統計來獲得準確的測量手段，對樣品製備的要求要寬松得多。到目前為止，所有PCR方案，包括適用於dPCR的方案，都使用熒光探針作為檢測手段。與樣品相關的抑製會導致熒光猝滅，有時還會出現假陽性，這使得 PCR 混合物中可用組分的選擇受到限製。因此，PCR 試劑通常是受限且昂貴的。 在本項目中，我們提出通過利用表面等離子體共振 (SPR) 傳感器的亞 fM 分辨率來開發一種新的無標記 dPCR 方法，該分辨率是由於原子薄的二維材料(如石墨烯或硫系化合物)的相位奇異性帶來的巨大古斯-漢欣位移（Goos-Hänchen (G-H) shift）而導致的。在此被提議的方案中，SPR 通過監測由擴增子與其共軛物之間的特異性結合引起的傳感器表面的折射率來檢測擴增子的存在。 dPCR 是在被打印在傳感器表面上的 2D 微孔陣列內進行的。隨著 SPR 傳感器芯片經歷熱循環，由於目標核酸的存在，擴增子將反過來擾亂 G-H 位移。一個成像檢測器監測每個微孔的 s 和 p 偏振之間的橫向分離，即 G-H 偏移，提供無標記的 dPCR 信號。由於我們只關心正/負微孔的數字計數，而不是絕對 G-H 偏移，只要靈敏度足夠大，信噪比就不再是問題。這使得檢測巨大的 G-H 偏移（本質上是一種差分測量方案）成為相對於其他 SPR 方案的有利選擇，盡管由於熱循環可能導致基線信號漂移。 本項目所提出的 dPCR 裝置將為香港社會帶來重大利益。雖然我們的高人口密度使我們不可避免地容易爆發傳染病，但為了將風險降到最低，政府經常采取嚴厲措施，實行保持社交距離或全面屠宰牲畜。其經濟代價是巨大的。與此同時，低成本的 DNA/RNA 篩查也促進了個性化精準醫療的發展，其中患者的基因圖譜可被用來提高治療的準確性和療效。

14204621.label: Major findings and research outcome
14204621.value: Through this project we have developed a high-throughput ultra-sensitive label-free biosensor platform for detecting disease-related biomolecules and nucleic acid strands. For delivering ultra-sensitive performance, we have adopted a new scheme based on the detection of Goos-Hänchen (GH) shift between the p- and s-polarisation components. The demonstrated experimental detection limit of cytokine cancer biomarkers (TNF-alpha and IL-6) was in the sub-femto molar regime (1x10E−16M). We have found that the major parameter for achieving ultra-high sensitivity is the control of the sensor layer thickness and composition. Our experiments revealed that a usable sensor surface can only be delivered with very tight control of thin film deposition conditions. For the high-throughput functionality, we have incorporated several solid-state digital micro-mirror devices (DMD) to generate programmable illumination patterns for arrayed GH shift interrogation. While detection sensitivity will be compromised when we use the system in an arrayed sensing mode, the best experimental detection limit from a single sensor element was also in the sub-femto molar regime. For digital PCR, we have conducted experiments to explore the possibility droplet generation and temperature cycling in a novel pump-free platform through the actuation of centrifugal force. The effort has yielded a single-use disposable microfluidic device and its peripheral hardware for the execution of mechanical and electronic operations, which has a capability of detection approximately 20 copies per microlitre of disease-related nucleotides including influenza A virus (IAV), respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), varicella zoster virus (VZV), Zika virus (ZIKV), and adenovirus (ADV). While we encountered significant signal disturbance in the GH shift when the microfluidic device underwent temperature cycling, we had to rely on the use of fluorescence for reading digital PCR signals. For this reason, we have only achieved 80% of Objective#1 of this project. During the course of this project, experimental efforts in microfluidic device fabrication, nano-material processing and image data analysis have led to considerable R&D advancement in rapid prototyping of microfluidic components with the use of Parafilm, solid-state nanopore single molecule characterisation, sequencing of single nucleotides and peptides, deep-learning of digital PCR droplet images for highly efficient estimation of nucleic acid concentration levels.

14204621.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14204621.value: While this project has successfully demonstrated ultra-sensitive label-free detection of disease-related nucleotides in sub-femto molar regime with plasmonics and the possibility of single molecule analysis with a solid-state nanopore, there exists a research gap for conducting single molecule vibrational studies through the utilisation of surface enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) as a target molecule gets immobilised in the vicinity of a pre-functionalised nanopore when it undergoes translocation through the nanopore. The presence of an immobilisation event can be identified through monitoring the current blockade signal of the nanopore device. As soon as the single target molecule is anchored at the "plasmonic nanopore", one can perform SERS according. We believe this follow-up project idea carries significant scientific impact since currently no true single-molecule SERS platform has been reported yet. At present, we are conducting preliminary experiments within our team for proof-of-concept demonstration. We are continuing our effort on explore potential commercialisation of DMD-enabled GH biosensors given its ultra-sensitive label-free detection performance and the possibility of low-cost operations.

14204621.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14204621.value: This project has delivered an ultra-sensitive biosensor capable of detecting disease-related molecules such as DNAs or proteins with minimal sample preparation. Within this project, we have demonstrated detection of clinically relevant target molecules include cytokine cancer biomarkers (TNF-alpha and IL-6), DNAs of influenza A virus (IAV), respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), varicella zoster virus (VZV), Zika virus (ZIKV), and adenovirus (ADV). The limit of detection in the sub-femo molar and 10's DNA copies per microlitre regime. This biosensing platform aims to address point-of-care testing applications. Another achievement of this project is the establishment of a single-molecule analysis platform based on the use of a silicon nanopore. We have successfully achieved discrimination a panel of common proteins, DNAs and peptides through analysing the signal characteristics associated individual single molecule translocation events. This technique will lead to highly accurate assessment of molecular interactions at a single-molecule level, which is critically important for many branches of science and engineering.

14204821.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14204821.value: Decision making under uncertainty is ubiquitous, stochastic optimization and game theoretic models have been powerful mathematical approaches for identifying decision maker's optimal decision making and their interactions. Stochastic generalized equations (SGE) provide a unified framework for characterizing the first order optimality and equilibrium conditions of these decision making problems, which means solving these stochastic optimization and equilibrium problems are mathematically equivalent to solving a system of SGEs. In data-driven problems where the true probability distribution of the underlying random variables is unknown, one often uses samples such as empirical or computer simulated data to construct an approximation of the SGEs and then solve the latter to obtain an approximate solution. The existing research of SGE focuses on asymptotic convergence of the solutions obtained from solving the sample average approximated SGE (SAA solution in short) to the true solution of the SGE and uses the former to construct a confidence region of the latter. A key assumption of the research is that sample data are generated by the true probability distribution which means that they do not contain noise. In data-driven problems which are more common than ever nowadays, such assumption may not be satisfied. Indeed, data from real-world experiments are often corrupted with outliers and/or exhibiting heavy tails. For instance, heavy-tailed processes are routinely used in finance and in biology or medical experiments datasets are regularly subject to some level of corruption by outliers. Under these circumstances, the SAA solutions may not converge to the solution of the true SGE problem. In this project, we aim to address the issue by developing a new theory and method which builds upon robust statistics for analyzing SAA solutions in a data-driven environment. We start by investigating impact of the outliers of the underlying uncertainty data on the SAA solutions and then moving on to consider a situation where all data are potentially corrupted. In the latter case, we investigate how topological structure of the data may affect the quality of the SAA solution. As a motivation and an application, we examine how the new analytical approaches work in practical stochastic optimization and equilibrium problems including machine learning problems. The outcomes of this project will provide a unified theoretical grounding for analyzing quality of SAA solutions in stochastic optimization and game theoretic models and including stochastic variational inequalities and stochastic complementarity problems 不確定性在決策過程中普遍存在，隨機優化和博弈論模型是幫助決策者確定最優決策及其相互作用的有效數學方法。隨機廣義方程(SGE)為描述這些決策問題的一階最優性條件和均衡條件提供了一個統一的框架，這意味著求解這些隨機優化和均衡問題在數學上等價於求解SGE。在數據驅動的問題中，隨機變量的真實概率分布往往是未知的。人們經常使用樣本，如經驗或計算機模擬數據，來構建SGE的逼近問題，然後通過求解後者來獲得一個近似解。目前關於SGE的研究主要集中在樣本均值近似SGE的解(以下簡稱SAA解)到SGE真解的漸近收斂性分析，以及利用SAA解構造SGE真解的置信域。該研究的一個關鍵假設是，樣本數據是由真實概率分布產生的，這意味著它們不包含噪聲。在數據驅動的問題中，這種假設可能不被滿足，而這一問題在大數據時代更為常見。事實上，實驗的真實數據經常會被異常值所破壞，或者顯示出厚尾特征。例如，在金融、生物學或醫學實驗中經常使用厚尾分布，數據集經常受到異常值的某種程度的破壞。本項目首先研究不確定性數據中的異常值對SAA解的影響，然後考慮所有數據都可能被破壞的情況。在後一種情況下，我們研究數據的拓撲結構如何影響SAA解的性質。作為一個動機和應用，本項目還將研究如何把新的分析方法應用到實際的隨機優化、均衡問題以及機器學習中。項目的成果將為分析隨機優化和博弈論模型，包括隨機變分不等式和隨機互補問題中SAA解的性質提供統一的理論基礎。

14204921.label: Project Objectives
14204921.value: To understand and model the single-camera- and multi-camera-based OCC system, aiming to develop theoretical frameworks and identify the fundamental limitations of its communication performance. Simulations based on the model will be implemented to gain insights on the optimization of digital signal processing (DSP) algorithms for signal combinations. Model refinement will be conducted based on experimental verification. Firstly, the single-camera-based OCC system model will be developed based on rolling-shutter camera models and camera signal processing. We will derive the data rate limitation by considering camera-specific characteristics, including video frame gap time and memory readout time, that are not user adjustable. The effects of camera settings like shutter speed, ISO, and f-number will then be investigated. Additional information from sensor specifications, such as dark current, thermal noise, sensitivity, fill factor, dynamic range, and optical crosstalk, will be used to systematically derive the overall signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), bit-error-rate (BER), and the transmission capacity. Secondly, the bandwidth of the multi-camera module as an optical receiver, with multiple detectors working at interleaved sampling times, will be studied in the temporal and spatial domain. Given the distinct characteristics of each camera in the module, we will investigate the limit of the aggregated data rate for multi-camera OCC. The theoretical model established will lay the foundation for developing effective DSP algorithms to combine the captured images from different camera sensors. The experiments conducted later in this project will help provide useful information to refine the channel model. To develop and optimize the signal processing algorithms for multi-camera and multi-user OCC systems. We will design and optimize the throughput with emphases on (1) capacity enhancement by advanced DSP algorithms to combine received signals from multi-camera and (2) robust signal detection for multi-user vehicle networks. For this objective, we will study the capacity enhancement in multi-camera-based OCC systems and explore multiple access schemes based on the results derived in Objective 1. Firstly, efficient image processing algorithms and advanced DSP algorithms for communication will be investigated to process the signals received by multiple cameras to maximize the transmission data rate. For the vehicle network, to decode signals from multiple vehicles simultaneously, we will explore effective signal processing schemes to assist spatial division multiple access. The main challenges that will be tackled are (1) signal source detection and segmentation and (2) camera setting optimization to detect signals of different optical powers. To develop advanced signal processing algorithms for data rate and robustness enhancement. Two schemes will be investigated, a blurring-assisted communication technique aided by vibration and an ambient light-resistant communication system. For this objective, issues for practical implementation will be considered. The first is the camera vibration that may be induced by the movement of smartphone users or moving vehicles. Actually, we will leverage the vibration-induced blurring effect to elongate the received light pattern on the image sensor, thus increasing the area that the rolling shutter effect can be used to increase the data rate. The vibration effect is further magnified when the telephoto camera is used. We will examine different camera settings and the vibration control strategy to optimize communication performance. To achieve robust data transfer under high ambient light conditions, we will first characterize the effect of ambient light on the OCC system to fully understand this interference issue. Next, we will investigate different background cancellation schemes and advanced signal detection algorithms to mitigate the effect of ambient light.

14204921.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14204921.value: Smartphones, arguably the most indispensable personal device nowadays, play a crucial role as a gateway to the Internet. The image sensor on each smartphone’s camera is ready to serve as an optical receiver for communication purposes. The communication that utilizes image sensors as the detector is termed optical camera communication (OCC). Various real-life applications can be supported by employing OCC techniques, including mobile payment and indoor positioning. Multi-camera is now a standard configuration on smartphones. Albeit some multi-camera OCC systems have been developed, the fundamental limit of data rate is yet to be found. On the vehicle communication side, information exchange can be achieved by employing existing headlights and taillights as transmitters and in-car cameras as receivers. It presents great potential to support autonomous vehicles without delving into the development of new hardware. The formation of network connections is automatic when one car enters into (or leave) the sight of another car’s camera, a self-forming ad-hoc peering. A cluster of close-by cars automatically forms a network using OCC. It provides great advantages on the network latency, interference resistance, and cost, compared to radio-frequency (RF)-based vehicle communication. However, the study of OCC’s multi-access and networking issues is minimal, impeding the realization of its full capacity. Besides, innovative techniques to combat ambient light interference or camera shaking are necessary for practical considerations. In summary, this proposal will focus on the investigation and optimization of the OCC-based smartphone system and vehicle network. We will research: (1) the theoretical modeling of single-camera and multi-camera systems, aiming to explore the fundamental limit on the transmission capacity; (2) the advanced signal processing for multi-camera receivers and multi-access schemes to maximize the transmission rate and total throughput; (3) blurring-assisted OCC system and robust communication for practical implementation; (4) the real-time demonstration for OCC-based smartphone system and vehicle network. This project is strategically vital to Hong Kong, a city with a high retail shop density. The smartphone OCC system will provide versatile location-based services for customers. Hong Kong is also a metropolitan city with many carriageways. The highly congested traffic imposes a great challenge for autonomous vehicles. By intelligently exploiting in-car cameras and car’s headlight/taillight, a vehicle OCC network can be established to transfer timely information for collision avoidance and smart routing decision. In short, precise location-specific information provision and road safety can be significantly improved via the proposed OCC-based smartphone system and vehicle networks, respectively. 智能手機可以說是當今最不可或缺的個人設備，它作為通往互聯網的門戶發揮著至關重要的作用。每部智能手機相機上的圖像傳感器都可以用作通信的光接收器。使用圖像傳感器作為檢測器的通信稱為光學相機通信 (OCC)。採用OCC技術可以支持各種現實生活應用，包括移動支付和室內定位。多攝像頭現在是智能手機的標準配置。儘管一些基於多相機的OCC 系統已經開發成功，了一些基於多相機 的OCC 系統，但傳輸速率的根本極限制尚未被發現。在車載通信方面，可以通過使用現有的前大燈和尾燈作為發射器，使用車載攝像頭作為接收器來實現信息交換。它具有支持自動駕駛汽車的巨大潛力，而無需深入研究新硬件的開發。當一輛車進入（或離開）另一輛車攝像頭的視線時，網絡連接便自動形成的。附近的汽車集群使用 OCC 自動形成網絡。與基於射頻 (RF) 的車輛通信相比，它在連接延遲、低延遲、抗干擾和成本方面提供了出色的性能。然而，對 OCC 的多路訪問和網絡問題的研究很少，限制了OCC實現其全部的傳輸容量。此外，出於實際考慮，還需要新的技術來對抗環境光干擾或相機抖動。綜上所述，本提案將重點研究和優化基於OCC的智能手機系統和車載網絡。我們將研究： (1) 單攝像頭和多攝像頭系統的理論建模，旨在探索傳輸容量的根本限制； (2) 多相機接收器和多路訪問方案的先進信號處理，以最大化傳輸速率和總吞吐量； (3) 基于模糊輔助的 OCC 系統和用於實際应用的稳定通信； (4) 基於OCC的智能手機系統和車載網絡的實時演示。 該項目對香港這個零售店密度高的城市具有戰略意義。智能手機OCC系統將為客戶提供多種基於位置的服務。香港也是一個多車道的大都市，高度擁堵的交通對自動駕駛汽車提出了巨大的挑戰。通過智能地利用車載攝像頭和汽車前燈/尾燈，可以建立車輛OCC網絡以及時傳遞信息，避免碰撞和进行智能路線決策。簡而言之，通過提議的基於 OCC 的智能手機和車輛網絡，可以顯著提升基於位置的信息傳輸服務和道路安全狀況。

14204921.label: Realisation of objectives
14204921.value: Objective 1: To understand and model the single-camera- and multi-camera-based OCC. In [1], we investigated the fundamental limits of optical camera communication (OCC) systems and developed a theoretical model, applicable for both single-camera and multi-camera OCC. The time-domain and frequency-domain response are derived for a given exposure time and readout time. Based on the model, we conducted a simulation considering exposure time, readout time, gap time, and additive white gaussian noise. Through the simulation, we can derive the bit-error rate (BER) for On-off keying (OOK) and four-level pulse amplitude modulation (PAM4) under different data rates. We have derived an SNR model for the OCC system. Lambertian emission pattern was employed to derive the optical power of the LED light source. Multiple noise sources are considered, including photon shot noise, dark current shot noise, read noise, dark signal non-uniformity, and photon response non-uniformity. As CMOS sensors and solar panels are all fundamentally bandlimited devices (rolling shutter limitation and diffusion capacitance limitation), it will be desirable to combine these two devices to achieve a self-powered simultaneous image sensing and high data rate communication receiver with a lower system and signal processing complexity. Therefore, we also investigated the nonlinearity of photovoltaic visible light communications. The study is beneficial to OCC as image sensors also exhibit the fundamental nonlinear response that limits its dynamic range. In [4], we proposed and experimentally demonstrated a simple passive post-distortion compensation circuit without complex DSP and achieved a one-order of magnitude reduction in BER. In [5], a programmable anti-logarithm linearization circuit (PALC) for linearizing photovoltaic modules was proposed and implemented. With the investigation of an optimal number of diodes required in PALC under different scenarios, a BER reduction from 1.4×10-1 to 8.2×10-3 is achieved under 1000 lux with self-adaptation. Objective 2: To develop and optimize the signal processing algorithms for multi-camera and multi-user OCC systems. [multi-camera OCC systems] We investigated signal processing algorithms for multi-camera systems and verified the effectiveness in a visible light communication system, since smartphone operating systems and camera APIs may not be designed to handle multiple cameras simultaneously, limiting the ability to control and synchronize them effectively. In [6], we employed advanced DSP techniques, such as orthogonal circulant matrix transform (OCT) precoding and a simplified third-order Volterra equalizer, to mitigate inter-symbol interference (ISI) and nonlinear distortions, which can be adapted to process signals from multiple cameras, enhancing throughput and reliability. Wavelength division multiplexing (WDM) was demonstrated with narrow channel spacing (4 nm), enabling parallel data transmission across multiple channels. This approach can be applied to multi-camera OCC systems, where each camera operates on a different wavelength, significantly increasing system capacity. Additionally, the use of an optical phased array (OPA) for beam steering ensures precise alignment of communication beams, which is essential for multi-camera setups with varying angles and distances. These advancements in DSP, WDM, beam steering, and high-speed communication directly address the challenges of multi-camera OCC systems, such as signal interference, alignment, and real-time data transmission, making this work highly relevant for optimizing multi-camera OCC systems. [multi-user OCC systems] We investigated signal processing algorithms for signal detection from multiple light sources. We assembled plastic fibers into a fiber display so that multiple light strips can be captured on the image sensor to realize spatial multiplexing. Nine LED transmitters are coupled to nine plastic fibers and form a 6 cm × 7 cm light-emitting area for parallel transmission. The effectiveness of our proposed scheme is experimentally verified. It is demonstrated that a data rate > 150 kbit/s can be achieved for the spatially multiplexed system, suitable for text messages or audio narration in an Art gallery [3]. The system's robust signal detection techniques, such as timing recovery and equalization, provide insights for decoding signals from multiple users simultaneously, which is crucial for multi-user networks. The optimization of camera settings (e.g., exposure time and ISO) ensures reliable detection of signals with varying optical powers, addressing challenges in multi-user environments Objective 3: To develop advanced signal processing algorithms for data rate and robustness enhancement. Two schemes will be investigated, a blurring-assisted communication technique aided by vibration and an ambient light-resistant communication system. [Data rate enhancement] To enrich the application scenario of the OCC system. OOC for underwater communication were investigated [2]. We focused on enhancing water-air optical wireless communication (WA-OWC) systems through real-time beam tracking to mitigate the vibration effects of dynamic waves and mobile receivers by analyzing the blurred images. We proposed image-based beam tracking and developed a system using a camera and MEMS mirror to track and compensate for beam offsets, achieving a zero-packet-loss 600 Mbit/s transmission and reducing packet loss rates from over 85% to below 7% [9]. We extended this by optimizing the tracking system for faster response times and higher receiver velocities (up to 150 cm/s), reducing packet loss rates by 70% and increasing throughput from 50 Mbit/s to 850 Mbit/s [11]. We further demonstrated the potential of machine learning for robust WA-OWC systems, by introducing a ResNet-based neural network model for real-time beam tracking using wave-distorted images [10]. The model estimates beam positions with high accuracy, reducing packet loss rates from 18% to 4% under high wave dynamics. The system achieves a 600 Mbit/s transmission with minimal packet loss. [Robustness enhancement] To enhance robustness of OCC system, we investigated signal processing algorithms for challenging environment with not limited to ambient light, but also hand shaking, signal distortion, and bandwidth limitation. In [1], we have developed a real-time anti-shaking algorithm for a non-line-of-sight (NLOS) OCC system. In practical scenarios, the mobile phone user’s shaking hand and interference from ambient light will cause misalignment between images. After scaling, the residual amplitude fluctuation will still degrade the BER performance. We have proposed a simple yet efficient image registration algorithm to calculate the transformation matrix between images corrupted by the white and black stripes. With the anti-shaking algorithm, around one order of BER improvement can be realized when using hand-held smartphone as the receiver.

14204921.label: Major findings and research outcome
14204921.value: Objective 1: Modeling and Analysis of OCC Systems The theoretical framework developed for OCC systems reveals the fundamental limitations of communication performance [1]. A signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) model was established considering light power and various noise sources. Combined with the bandwidth limit derived from experiment characterization, the fundamental limits of system capacity can be evaluated using the Shannon limit. The study of the nonlinearity of photovoltaic visible light communications is beneficial to OCC as image sensors also exhibit the fundamental nonlinear response that limits its dynamic range and communication performance [C2][C3]. The characterization in real-time image-based beam tracking is also beneficial to OCC, as both systems need to optimize settings to capture images of rapidly changing objects [C6][C7]. Objective 2: Multi-camera OCC system and multi-user OCC system The project explored multi-camera and multi-user OCC systems, yielding notable throughput improvements. Using the iPhone 11 Pro, a nested barcode design enhanced throughput by 20.5% over standard barcodes, achieving 122.9 kb/s. For LED-to-multi-camera communication with the OnePlus 5T, dual cameras were combined to reach a data rate of 84 kbit/s, significantly surpassing single-camera performance. In multi-user scenarios, optical companding techniques and color multiplexing led to peak goodput rates exceeding 80 kbit/s [1]. A parallel transmission system utilizing nine LED transmitters coupled to plastic fibers achieved data rates over 150 kbit/s, underlining the effectiveness of robust signal detection techniques [C1]. The low-complexity nonlinear equalizer developed for passive optical networks is applicable for enhancing multi-user OCC [C8]. Objective 3: Data rate and robustness enhancement In an NLOS OCC system, a lightweight image registration algorithm demonstrated a substantial reduction in BER using a hand-held smartphone as the receiver [1]. The image processing techniques developed for underwater scenarios are useful for creating processing algorithms tailored for OCC [J1][J3]. Additionally, the simplified Volterra equalizer designed for bandwidth-limited systems helps mitigate inter-symbol interference and nonlinear distortion in OCC [C4]. The precoding algorithms can reduce the processing overhead on smartphones used in OCC [C8]. Furthermore, an ambient light-resistant communication system was developed, which mitigated visual flicker and enhanced signal modulation. A four-level flicker coding scheme for LED transmitters achieved a 65% improvement in data rates [1]. The frequency tunable technique is also valuable for designing LED transmitters that operate below the low-frequency range that causes visual flicker [J2]. An automatic color correction algorithm for barcode decoding maintained a decoding success rate exceeding 95% under varying indoor lighting conditions.

14204921.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14204921.value: User mobility presents a challenge in practical applications, but recent advancements in image stabilization have improved the ability to maintain the light source's position on the sensor. Signal processing algorithms must be adapted to account for user movement, particularly by updating scaling factors based on signal intensity in newly captured images. Additionally, the upstream link of OCC systems has not been thoroughly explored, which limits the technique's application. Utilizing the smartphone's flashlight as a transmitter presents a natural solution for establishing an upstream link. Future research will focus on developing a bidirectional OCC system that employs the flashlight for upstream communication, enhancing the overall functionality and potential use cases of OCC technology. Establishing industry standards for OCC is vital for ensuring compatibility and interoperability across devices, facilitating broader adoption in consumer electronics and public infrastructure. Future research will focus on providing a stable framework for developers, enabling seamless communication in smart cities and IoT environments.

14204921.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14204921.value: This research project focused on enhancing communication using light, specifically for OCC systems. It explored the challenges and opportunities in using smartphone cameras to capture data via light, which is vital for applications like smart homes, automotive networks, and augmented reality. The project began by modeling OCC systems and identifying key limitations in their communication performance. Key innovations include employing multi-transmitter/multi-camera setups, developing advanced image processing techniques, and robust signal detection methods, which aim to enhance system throughput and reliability. Addressing practical issues, such as receiver vibrations and ambient light interference, the project explores creative solutions like leveraging image registration and color correction algorithms to improve communication performance. These advancements enable devices to communicate more effectively, even in challenging environments, which pave the way for more efficient and reliable OCC systems, opening new possibilities for applications in data sharing, vehicle networks, and advertising.
