14205421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14205421.value: 群同步問題的目標，是從屬於某群的原信號的帶噪聲相對變換測量中把該信號恢復。群同步問題有著很廣泛的應用，包括計算機圖形、網絡分析、機器人技術和結構生物學等。這些問題的優化模型一般都是非凸的，但它們通常都具有良好結構。本項目的目標是要研究如何利用這些結構來為一類群同步問題設計快速高效算法，並分析它們的統計性能和收斂率。本項目的成果將為群同步問題提供新的計算理論，並為這類問題提供更快更好的算法。

14206321.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14206321.value: 約束編程是人工智能 (AI) 的經典支柱之一，是一種通用方法以解決許多工業應用中出現的組合搜索問題，例如規劃、調度、裝箱等。 解決一般約束滿足和優化問題是NP難的。 這些問題的解空間複雜，難以分析。 對這些約束問題的數十年的研究工作證實，搜索，無論是系統的還是隨機的，仍然是解決這些問題的唯一有效的通用技術。 許多研究都在尋找通過向問題模型靜態地添加約束來或通過在搜索期間生成修剪信息來動態地修剪搜索空間的方法。 支配關係是在約束優化問題 (COP) 的變量賦值上定義的傳遞和非自反關係，通過它我們可以推導出有效的打破支配約束，以防止搜索訪問搜索空間中被支配的區域，從而有效地加快求解過程.然而，直到今天，必須手動發現支配關係，這通常需要人類的洞察力和獨創性。這限制了該方法的適用性。我們最近在 IJCAI-PRICAI'20（人工智能領域的頂級會議）上報告的工作激發了這一提議，其中我們展示瞭如何在沒有人工干預的情況下僅通過機械地檢查問題模型來自動有效地產生破壞無益的優勢。結果表明，我們可以在解決某一類COP時有幾個數量級的效率提升。該技術是通過利用我們的工作提出的支配關係的重要新理論特徵來實現的。基於這一成功，我們建議進一步研究支配關係的理論特性、自動識別支配關係的方法以及為此類任務開發有效算法。 約束優化問題是極其困難的問題，在實踐中以各種形式出現。 如今，現實世界的問題變得越來越大、越來越複雜，解決這些問題的難度呈指數級增長。 我們希望擬議的研究能夠產生關於支配關係的深入知識，並由此無需人類建模者考慮如何識別這種關係以及如何加快求解過程。 人類洞察力應該專注於給出問題的正確模型。 這將使我們更接近計算機科學的最高目標：用戶提出問題，機器解決問題。

14206521.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14206521.value: 傳輸控制協議 (TCP) 可以說是互聯網的引擎，為大多數互聯網應用程序承載數據。鑑於其重要性，研究人員在過去幾十年進行了廣泛的研究，開發了許多創新的 TCP 設計以提高其性能。然而現有的大部分研究都集中於 TCP 的長期（即幾十秒）性能上。雖然這是一個有效且重要的指標，但我們認為 TCP 的短期性能（幾秒或更短）同樣重要。因為我們觀察到，隨著帶寬的增加，互聯網中大多數數據傳輸的持續時間越來越短。這項目通過開發一種稱為 Stateful-TCP 的創新方法來解決這一挑戰，以繞過短期 TCP 性能的關鍵障礙—TCP 的慢啟動 (SS) 機制。儘管過去幾十年TCP 設計有許多創新，但 SS 在當今部署的 TCP 中一直保持不變。它的目標很簡單：以保守的傳輸速率開始數據傳輸，然後隨著數據包的成功傳送逐漸增加傳輸速率。這是一個合理的設計，因為每個TCP流獨立運行，並且在未知底層網絡路徑的情況下開始。然而，由此產生的低初始傳輸速率可能會嚴重限制 TCP 的效率，因為大多數TCP流在它們有足夠的時間來提高傳輸速率之前就會結束。Stateful-TCP 通過重用先前TCP流中已測量的網絡度量（有狀態度量）傳送到後續TCP流（到同一用戶）來解決此瓶頸，以便後者可以一開始就有效地利用可用路徑帶寬。由於大多數互聯網應用程序會生成許多 TCP 流，這意味著除了第一個流之外的所有TCP流都將繞過 TCP 的 SS。 Stateful-TCP 是對當前 TCP 擁塞控制設計的補充，因此可以應用到近年來開發的許多新TCP設計。為了展示其潛力，我們將 Stateful-TCP 應用於 Cubic（Linux 中的默認 TCP），在中國進行的 1,000 多個客戶端的大規模獨立基準測試中，1 MB 傳輸速度成功提高了 50% 以上。這 GRF 將使我們能夠充分開發 Stateful-TCP 的潛力，包括研究新的狀態指標、於其他現代 TCP 設計的應用、與騰訊合作進行大規模實驗等，並將成果通過 RFC 和開源軟件貢獻到互聯網業界。

14206721.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14206721.value: 新型二維鐵電憶阻器及其作為神經形態陣列的人工突觸

14206721.label: Project Objectives
14206721.value: The fabrication of α-In2Se3 memristor array relies on the large-scale fabrication of high-quality single crystalline α-In2Se3 thin film. The first objective of this proposal is to develop a facile PVD method for large-area growth of monocrystalline α-In2Se3 ultrathin films by introducing multilayer h-BN as growth substrate. To fabricate the memristor array, the size of the PVD-grown monocrystalline α-In2Se3 sheets should try to exceed 500 µm. In case the large-area monocrystalline α-In2Se3 ultrathin films cannot be finished in time, an alternative plan ‘B’ is also proposed. The alternative solution is to artificially control the position and orientation of the fabricated α-In2Se3 thin flakes or other ferroelectric thin flakes via PDMS stamping with the prepared ink. The second objective of this project is to fabricate the α-In2Se3/other ferroelectric memristor and to optimize its dynamic range. Various devices with different material composition will be fabricated and studied to achieve the optimized performance. As an explorative device structure, the target dynamic range is proposed to be10 with a small on-current (~10^-5 A) to minimize heating and power consumption. With defect passivation and encapsulation, the stability of the device will be improved and a retention over 10,000 s will be realized. While the device areas of the recently reported 2D memristors typically range from 4 to 500 µm^2, the target channel length of the proposed device will be 40 ~ 800 nm. The forth objective is to fabricate a 8 × 8 on-chip α-In2Se3/other ferroelectric memristor array. The proposed bottom-up fabrication method has much lower demand of equipment compared to that by the conventional crossbar array. The coefficient of variation (standard deviation over mean) will be calculated to evaluate the dispersion of the distribution and the device-to-device variation. A yield over 90 % is expected in this proposal. To verify the functionality of the memristor array, an all-connected artificial neural network will be constructed with the memristor array. The software simulation of the all-connected neural network will be constructed with Python. The weight of each synapse will be trained to obtain optimal recognition accuracy. The recognition accuracy of the memristor network will be compared with the software neuron network to demonstrate its computation ability.

14206721.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14206721.value: With the tremendous progress of big-data technology and data size, the von Neumann bottleneck impedes the further development of modern computation technology, where enormous power and time are consumed when a large amount of data is transmitted back and forth between the processing unit and storage unit. To surpass the von Neumann architecture, extensive studies on artificial neuron network have been conducted. By mimicking mammalian neuromorphic system where data storage and process are integrated in a synapse, artificial neuron network is expected to have much faster processing speed and lower power consumption. The hardware implementation of artificial neuron network relies on the fabrication of high performance memristors, which is a direct imitation of mammalian synapse. Conventional memristors are based on the electrically driven motion of metal ions in dielectric layer and the formation of conductive filament. Thanks to the randomness of ion motion, the memristors typically undergo the poor stability and reproducibility. Moreover, the integration density is also limited by the three-dimensional device configuration. In this proposal, we propose an alternative pathway to implement a memristor in all two-dimensional material platform by utilizing the unique intercorrelated in-plane and out-of-plane ferroelectricity in α-In2Se3 ultrathin film. Different from conventional ferroelectric material where the polarization switching is induced by a parallel electric field, the intercorrelated ferroelectricity in α-In2Se3 allows the polarization modulation with a perpendicular electric field and is therefore promising to construct two-terminal memristor with simpler device structure and smaller device size. Compared to the conventional memristor composed of conductive filament, the ferroelectric memristor is anticipated to have smaller operation current, lower power consumption, higher endurance, longer retention, higher reproducibility, high repeatability, and smaller device area, which is of technical importance in computation systems. The goal of this proposal is to design and fabricate a high-density two-dimensional ferroelectric memristor array. And we formulate a technically feasible three-step plan. Firstly, we will focus on developing a large-area fabrication technique for monocrystalline α-In2Se3 ultrathin films. Secondly, we will optimize the memristic performance of the devised memristor with device engineering. Finally, we will fabricate a high-density 2D ferroelectric memristor array and demonstrate its computing capability by performing Iris recognition. We believe that the design and fabrication of this high-performance and high-density memristor array are of technical significance in transcending the von Neumann bottleneck and development of high-density in-memory artificial neural networks. 隨著大數據技術和數據規模的巨大發展，現代計算技術的進一步發展受到馮諾依曼瓶頸的限制，即大量數據在計算機的處理單元和存儲單元之間來回傳輸而消耗巨大的功率和時間。為了超越馮諾依曼架構，人們已經對人工神經元網絡進行了廣泛的研究。通過模仿哺乳動物神經形態系統，其數據存儲和處理集成在突觸處，人工神經元網絡有望具有更快的處理速度和更低的功耗。根據對哺乳動物突觸的直接模仿，人工神經元網絡的硬體實現依賴於高性能憶阻器的製造。 傳統的憶阻器由基於電介質層中金屬離子的電驅動運動和導電細絲的形成而實現。由於離子運動的隨機性，憶阻器的穩定性和再現性通常較差。此外，集成密度還受到三維器件配置的限制。在該研究項目中，我們尋求另一種途徑，通過利用 In2Se3 超薄膜中獨特的相互關聯的面內和面外鐵電性，在In2Se3和其他二維材料平臺中實現憶阻器。與傳統鐵電材料的極化轉換是由平行電場引起的不同，In2Se3中的相關鐵電性允許使用垂直電場進行極化調製，因此有望構建具有更簡單器件結構，以及具有更小器件尺寸的兩端憶阻器。與傳統的由導電絲組成的憶阻器相比，鐵電憶阻器有望具有更小的工作電流、更低的功耗、更高的耐久性、更長的保持時間、更高的再現性、更高的重複性和更小的器件面積，這在計算系統中具有重要的技術意義。 該研究項目的終級目標是設計和製造高密度片上二維鐵電憶阻器陣列。我們制定了一個技術上可行的三步走計劃。首先，我們將專注於開發單晶 In2Se3及其他鐵電超薄膜的大面積製備技術。其次，我們將通過器件優化工程，實現憶阻器的高憶阻性能。最後，我們將製作一個高密度的二維鐵電憶阻器陣列，並通過執行虹膜識別來展示其計算能力。我們認為，這種高性能、高密度憶阻器陣列的設計和製造對於突破馮諾依曼瓶頸和發展高密度內存人工網絡具有重要意義。

14206821.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14206821.value: 多智能體系統協同的先進運動規劃技術

14206821.label: Project Objectives
14206821.value: For the motion planning of a single unmanned aerial vehicle in complicated and cluttered environments, we first generate motion primitives through dynamic programming. The motion primitive will satisfy all the boundary, state, and input constraints of the physical system. Save the motion primitives as a lookup table. For the primitives generated in the step above, we design an appropriate neural network (using a deep learning approach if necessary) as a function approximator to estimate the mapping relation between the boundary conditions and the resulting trajectory. For the cooperative motion planning of multiple vehicles, the first objective of the proposed research is to define the objective function (cost function) for the whole group of vehicle in accordance to specific missions (such as fulfill the tasks in the shortest time or find the shortest path) to be completed. Decouple the optimization problem of the whole group into several sub-problems, with each of them is assigned to an individual vehicle and work out the coupling variables between them. For each sub-problem, the constraints include input, boundary, inter-vehicle collision avoidance constraint. For the non-convex optimization sub-problem, use the particle swarm optimization (PSO) to optimize the model predictive control (MPC) problem. The PSO is a derivative-free optimization method, and each particle can be implemented in parallel due to the parallelism of the NVIDIA Graphics Processing Unit, which greatly reduces the computation time. Lastly, the above overall motion planning framework are to be implemented and tested through some real applications, such as good delivery. To link our research with the currently funded Hong Kong Centre for Logistics Robotics by Innovation and Technology Commission - InnoHK, we will definitely adopt the proposed solutions to tackle the problems initiated by the Centre.

14206821.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14206821.value: Over the last decade, the research of cooperative control of multi-agent systems has blossomed due to their successful applications in solving real-life problems, such as the attitude synchronization of robot manipulators and spacecrafts, and the formation control of unmanned vehicles. The superiority of multi-agent systems over single ones for the control and coordination of unmanned vehicles, as such as unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), unmanned ground vehicles (UGVs), unmanned surface vehicles (USVs) and unmanned underwater vehicles (UUVs), is obvious and has been frequently reported in the literature. The high scalability of multi-agent systems can achieve tasks that could not be performed by single agent systems. Various cooperative control problems of multi-agent systems have been extensively investigated, which include consensus, synchronization and formation control. In cooperative control of multi-agent systems, a critical problem is to design appropriate controllers such that the group of agents can reach an agreement on certain quantities of interest. Most of the available results for the cooperative control of multi-agent systems assume that the group of agents are operating in obstacle-free environments, such as open spaces. Only very few of them have attempted to tackle the navigation problem of multi-agent unmanned systems in cluttered environments to avoid obstacles. In practical applications, collision avoidance among individual agents (such as UAVs) within the group (i.e., the inter-vehicle collision avoidance) is extremely important. Unfortunately, such an issue has not been clearly addressed in the open literature. Traditionally, motion planning is the task of guiding an unmanned vehicle from one place to another while avoiding obstacles. It is to compute a dynamically feasible and collision-free trajectory that starts from an initial state and ends at a specified target. In this project, we propose to develop advanced motion planning techniques that enable multiple unmanned systems, specifically UAVs or drones, to autonomously navigate and fly in cluttered environments without inter-vehicle collisions. It aims to provide a standard motion planning framework for general multi-agent unmanned systems. The proposed research, once realized, is expected to play an instrumental role for unmanned aerial systems in numerous industrial applications, such as reconnaissance for search and rescue, environment monitoring, security surveillance, powerline and pipeline inspection, and geographical mapping. More importantly, the proposed system can be easily adopted for multiple UAVs to carry out fully autonomous flight missions in GPS-denied environments, such as for high-rise building inspection, traffic monitoring, logistic checking and goods delivery, which are key components forming a smart city. 近十多年來，多智能體系統協同控制的研究因其在解決現實生活問題中的成功應用而發展迅速，例如機器人協同操縱和航天器的姿態同步以及無人系統的編隊控制。在無人飛行器、無人地面車輛、無人水面船只和無人水下航行器等無人系統的控制和協調方面，多智能體系統優於單智能體系統，是顯而易見的，多智能體系統可以完成單智能體無法完成的任務。多智能體系統的各種協同控制問題已被廣泛研究，包括協同、同步和編隊控制。在多智能體系統的協同控制中，一個關鍵問題是設計適當的控制器，使得一組智能體可以就某些感興趣的變量或任務達成一致。多智能體系統協同控制的大多數結果都假設智能體在無障礙環境中運行，如開放空間。只有極少數的文獻嘗試解決多智能體無人系統在雜亂環境中的導航以及避障問題。在實際應用中，如何避免集群內各個智能體之間的碰撞是個極為重要。遺憾的是，這樣的問題在公開文獻中並沒有得到很好的解決。在本研究項目中，我們提出開發先進的運動規劃技術，使多個無人系統能夠在雜亂的環境中自主導航和飛行，而不會發生相互碰撞。它旨在為一般多智能體無人系統提供標準的運動規劃框架。我們預計這項研究將對無人系統在眾多工業實際應用中發揮重要作用。

14206821.label: Realisation of objectives
14206821.value: Foundational Single UAV Planning The project successfully addressed the fundamental challenge of motion planning for single Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) operating in complex, cluttered environments. We utilized dynamic programming to generate a comprehensive set of motion primitives, rigorously designing them to satisfy all boundary, state, and input constraints inherent to the physical systems. Once validated, these motion primitives were systematically organized into a lookup table. This robust database served as the bedrock for subsequent, advanced planning stages. Neural Network Integration Building upon the generation of these primitives, we designed and implemented a sophisticated neural network function approximator, integrating deep learning techniques to manage system complexity. This network was engineered to estimate the mapping relationship between various boundary conditions and resulting flight trajectories. By leveraging data from the established primitives, this objective enabled significantly more efficient and intelligent flight path prediction, effectively automating real-time decision-making processes during navigation. Multi-Agent Cooperation Strategy To facilitate cooperative motion planning for multiple agents, a core goal of the study, we defined a precise global objective function tailored to specific mission requirements. This function optimized critical parameters, such as minimizing total mission time, reducing energy consumption, or identifying the shortest group path. We successfully decoupled the complex fleet-wide optimization problem into individual sub-problems assigned to specific vehicles. In solving these, the system effectively managed coupling variables while strictly enforcing constraints regarding input, boundaries, and, most critically, inter-vehicle collision avoidance to ensure safe simultaneous operation. Computational Optimization The project also overcame significant computational hurdles related to non-convex optimization by employing Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) to solve Model Predictive Control (MPC) problems. By harnessing the parallel processing capabilities of NVIDIA Graphics Processing Units (GPUs), we achieved a dramatic reduction in computation times for this derivative-free method. This technological breakthrough allowed for the rapid calculations necessary for real-time autonomous flight. Real-World Validation Finally, the complete motion planning framework was implemented and validated through diverse real-world applications. The framework has been successfully adapted for critical industrial tasks, including autonomous infrastructure inspection and maritime protection using unmanned surface vehicles. These deployments demonstrated the system’s versatility and effectiveness in GPS-denied and obstacle-rich environments. Specifically, we utilized our techniques in the following applications: 1. Autonomous Indoor Inspection System: Traditional indoor facility inspections on pipelines and boilers are often manual, making them logistically challenging, labor-intensive, costly, and hazardous. While UAVs offer a promising alternative, the lack of indoor GPS signals poses a significant localization challenge for fully autonomous inspection. Furthermore, narrow and complex indoor environments make flight safety difficult to guarantee. Leveraging our foundational work, we developed a UAV-based "explore-then-exploit" system to tackle these problems for autonomous data collection and scene reconstruction. The proposed system integrates two UAVs and features a two-step Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) method for localization and 3D mapping, a safety-guaranteed coverage path planning algorithm, and an obstacle-aware trajectory generation method. Validated in GPS-denied, cluttered indoor environments, the system successfully conducted 3D scene reconstruction. Performance analysis confirmed the system's robustness and feasibility for high-efficiency, low-cost facility management. 2. Hierarchical Multi-UAV Framework While UAVs are powerful tools for inspecting large-scale, unstructured 3D infrastructures, current approaches often suffer from extended completion times. To improve time efficiency in these cluster environments, we developed a hierarchical multi-UAV cooperative framework designed to balance workload and reduce overall task duration. The framework operates in two sequential stages: exploration and exploitation. In the exploration stage, a density map updates global and local information to dynamically partition areas based on reconstructability and relative UAV positions, while a Voronoi-based planner guides UAVs to optimal regions. Once the global map is obtained, the exploitation stage generates and divides viewpoints, accounting for the battery capacity of each agent. Finally, a shortest-path planning method minimizes travel costs to ensure high-quality reconstruction. Experiments in both simulated and real-world environments demonstrated the time efficiency, robustness, and effectiveness of this approach.

For the cooperative motion planning of multiple vehicles, the first objective of the proposed research is to define the objective function (cost function) for the whole group of vehicle in accordance to specific missions (such as fulfill the tasks in the shortest time or find the shortest path) to be completed.

Decouple the optimization problem of the whole group into several sub-problems, with each of them is assigned to an individual vehicle and work out the coupling variables between them. For each sub-problem, the constraints include input, boundary, inter-vehicle collision avoidance constraint.

For the non-convex optimization sub-problem, use the particle swarm optimization (PSO) to optimize the model predictive control (MPC) problem. 14206821.label: Major findings and research outcome
14206821.value: The research successfully established a comprehensive motion planning framework for Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) capable of operating in complex, cluttered, and GPS-denied environments. By utilizing dynamic programming to create a database of motion primitives and integrating a neural network function approximator, the project achieved highly efficient, real-time trajectory prediction. Furthermore, the team overcame significant computational hurdles in non-convex optimization by employing Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) on NVIDIA GPUs, allowing for the rapid solving of Model Predictive Control (MPC) problems necessary for autonomous flight. Building on this foundation, the study demonstrated effective multi-agent cooperation through a hierarchical framework that optimizes global objectives such as mission time and energy consumption. This was validated in real-world applications, including an "explore-then-exploit" system for indoor facility inspection that achieved centimeter-level accuracy without GPS, and a workload-balancing system for large-scale infrastructure inspection. These deployments proved that the proposed methods can safely decouple complex fleet optimization problems, strictly enforce collision avoidance, and significantly reduce task completion times compared to traditional manual or single-agent approaches.

14206821.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14206821.value: The research holds significant potential for Smart City applications, where the system's ability to navigate cluttered, GPS-denied environments could enable autonomous delivery swarms and search-and-rescue units in dense urban areas. To achieve this, future development should focus on optimizing algorithms for onboard edge computing and upgrading the neural network to handle dynamic, moving obstacles like traffic. In maritime and environmental protection, the framework can be expanded to coordinate heterogeneous fleets of aerial and surface vehicles. This "air-sea" collaboration would revolutionize port security, offshore inspection, and large-scale environmental monitoring, such as tracking forest fires. The proposed course of action involves adapting the control laws for diverse vehicle types and rigorously testing collision avoidance protocols to meet commercial safety standards.

14206821.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14206821.value: This research teaches drones how to fly safely and intelligently by themselves, even in difficult places where GPS doesn't work, such as inside narrow pipelines or around complex city infrastructure. Instead of relying on a human pilot to control every movement, we created a digital "brain" for these machines using advanced mathematics and artificial intelligence. This system allows a single drone to "see" its surroundings and dodge obstacles instantly. Furthermore, it enables groups of drones to communicate and work together like a coordinated team. The value of this work is that it transforms dangerous and expensive industrial tasks into safe, automated routines. Currently, inspecting a crumbling bridge or a high-pressure boiler is risky for human workers and costly. Our technology allows drones to take over these hazardous jobs. Beyond industrial inspections, this research lays the essential groundwork for the future of smart cities.

14206921.label: Project Objectives
14206921.value: Online Anomaly Detection in Cloud Systems with Concept-drift Adaption Log analysis is an important means of anomaly detection in cloud systems. However, most existing log anomaly detection models have a closed-world perception, which assumes that the set of distinct log events generated by a system is known and stable over time. Models formed under such assumptions fail to perform well in production environments because logs are continuously evolving. Therefore, we propose an online anomaly detection model which consists of two parts. The first is an online learning algorithm to quickly learn unseen log patterns. The second is a model rollback mechanism, which enables the model to adapt to concept drift issue by allowing it to return to the previous version. Such model is tailored for the complex and ever-changing nature of cloud services. Adaptive Failure Diagnosis via Human-in-the-loop Maintainers generally assign different importance of system performance to different KPIs in the cloud. Some essential KPIs should be closely monitored because anomalies of these KPIs could indicate serious failures in the cloud. However, such failures do not happen often. Hence, it is not practical to train a supervised learning model to detect the failures. To solve this problem, we propose an adaptive failure diagnosis mechanism based on human-in-the-loop. With this method, we could train a more accurate model from both historical data and human knowledge. More specifically, maintainers could interact with a serving model with minimal efforts. When false alarms and misses happen, the model is expected to adaptively learn from them with the help of the human interaction. As a result, the model could be more accurate over time by systematically accumulating the human knowledge. Fault Localization via Dependency-aware Root Cause Recommendation Recently, the microservice architecture has become increasingly popular and the needs for its reliable operation arise naturally. However, due to the massive, complex, and ever-changing dependency between microservices, it is difficult and time-consuming to manually pinpoint the system failures and locate the root cause of faults. Therefore, we propose a comprehensive fault localization mechanism for the microservice architecture. Specifically, the mechanism consists of a method for vectorizing and clustering microservices according to logs and KPIs, which infers the dependency between microservices, and a dependency-aware collaborative filtering algorithm that recommends the possible root cause of faults from historical mitigation records. Our mechanism features the vectorization and clustering of microservices to reduce computation complexity, as well as the recommendation of possible root causes that consider the dependency as well as the inherent similarity between microservices.

14206921.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14206921.value: 近年來，IT 企業開始將其應用程序和服務部署在雲計算平台上，例如 Microsoft Azure。隨著雲系統在復雜性和容量方面的不斷增長，雲故障變得不可避免，這可能導致服務中斷或性能下降。能否妥善管理雲故障將極大地影響公司收入和客戶信任度。因此，我們確定了工業雲系統中常見的三個關鍵挑戰。首先，由於雲系統正在積極進行不斷的功能升級和系統演進，系統監控數據的統計屬性可能會不時發生變化。其次，目前缺乏將人類專家知識融入模型訓練的手段。在診斷大型系統的故障時，此類知識必不可少。第三，雖然雲服務/資源的依賴關係可以為跟踪雲故障的級聯效應提供豐富的信息，但在現有的根本原因分析方法中並未明確考慮它們。 我們建議通過開發 AIOps（智能化運維）框架來實現彈性雲系統並解決這三個挑戰。我們的目標是全面提升雲系統和服務的可靠性。特別是，該框架由軟件可靠性工程的端到端管道組成，即異常檢測、故障診斷和故障定位。異常檢測尋找系統不符合正常行為的異常模式，例如高 CPU 使用率和低吞吐量。我們提出了一種基於日誌的異常檢測模型，該模型可以在線方式快速學習前所未有的日誌模式，並動態適應系統演化引起的概念漂移。故障診斷試圖找出由故障直接引起的最重要的問題；例如，異常的關鍵性能指標（KPI）。我們引入了一種具有人在環策略的自適應故障診斷算法，用於有效的模型訓練。最後，故障定位定位故障的根本原因，例如出現故障的微服務或設備。我們使用依賴感知協同過濾為微服務架構開發了一種新的故障定位技術。此外，我們將開發一個工具包，其中包含在該項目中獲得的 AIOps 模型和技術供公眾訪問。

With this method, we could train a more accurate model from both historical data and human knowledge. More specifically, maintainers could interact with a serving model with minimal efforts. When false alarms and misses happen, the model is expected to adaptively learn from them with the help of the human interaction. As a result, the model could be more accurate over time by systematically accumulating the human knowledge.

Fault Localization via Dependency-aware Root Cause Recommendation Recently, the microservice architecture has become increasingly popular and the needs for its reliable operation arise naturally. However, due to the massive, complex, and ever-changing dependency between microservices, it is difficult and time-consuming to manually pinpoint the system failures and locate the root cause of faults. Therefore, we propose a comprehensive fault localization mechanism for the microservice architecture. Specifically, the mechanism consists of a method for vectorizing and clustering microservices according to logs and KPIs, which infers the dependency between microservices, and a dependency-aware collaborative filtering algorithm that recommends the possible root cause of faults from historical mitigation records. Our mechanism features the vectorization and clustering of microservices to reduce computation complexity, as well as the recommendation of possible root causes that consider the dependency as well as the inherent similarity between microservices.

14206921.label: Major findings and research outcome
14206921.value: In total, one journal papers and nine conference papers were published, addressing the project's objectives from various perspectives. All of these publications acknowledge the support of this grant. The key outcomes are summarized below. (We use [C1] to denote conference publications [1], and [J1] to denote journal publications [1], etc.) To improve log understanding, we develop SemParser [C3], the first semantic-based log parser that extracts explicit and implicit semantics using an end-to-end semantic miner and a joint parsing mechanism. SemParser enhances downstream tasks by recovering richer event information beyond syntax-based methods. Recognizing that anomalies manifest collaboratively across heterogeneous data, we conduct a large-scale study on logs and metrics and propose HADES [C1], a semi-supervised end-to-end framework that fuses log semantics and metric patterns using hierarchical modeling and cross-modal attention. HADES effectively captures global system states for accurate anomaly detection. For microservice troubleshooting, we propose Eadro [C2], the first framework integrating anomaly detection and root-cause localization by jointly modeling traces, logs, and KPIs. Through multi-task learning, Eadro improves both detection accuracy and localization robustness. Beyond cloud data, we build advanced industrial-grade diagnosis systems. ADAMAS [C6] is an AutoML-based anomaly detection framework that uses Bayesian optimization and a novel NFMK metric, supported by lightweight human-in-the-loop feedback and continuous reconfiguration. It outperforms existing models and is deployed in Huawei Cloud. To detect correlation-violating anomalies, we design ISOLATE [J1], combining graph attention networks with temporal modeling and a label-conditional VAE under positive-unlabeled learning. ISOLATE achieves state-of-the-art performance in anomaly localization. Issue reports often contain incomplete information, so we propose COCA [C4], the first LLM-based root-cause analysis framework enhanced with source-code knowledge. Through static log-source retrieval, execution-path reconstruction, and code knowledge profiling, COCA boosts localization accuracy by over 28% on real distributed systems. At the hardware level, we study failures in large-scale HBM deployments and propose Cordial [C7], a cross-row error prediction model leveraging bank-level spatial locality, greatly improving failure prediction accuracy for AI training clusters. Finally, we introduce SBLLM [C5], a search-based LLM framework for code optimization, combining evolutionary search and pattern retrieval to achieve up to 209% performance improvement across Python and C++ programs. Collectively, these contributions advance cloud reliability from hardware to application layers and demonstrate strong real-world impact.

14206921.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14206921.value: Although our work has produced strong outcomes including eleven papers and multiple systems deployed in production, further improvements remain possible. Current anomaly detection frameworks (e.g., ADAMAS, ISOLATE) achieve high accuracy but are reactive and still constrained by real-time detection efficiency. Future research should shift toward proactive, lightweight, and predictive resilience techniques. A first direction is faster-than-real-time anomaly detection by extending ADAMAS with forecasting models to predict metric trends and preempt failures before they manifest. A second direction is automated and adaptive resilience testing for dynamic microservice architectures. Using insights from ISOLATE and COCA, we aim to build an intelligent fault-injection and evaluation system that autonomously adapts to evolving service topologies. Third, we will pursue integrated code and runtime-level optimization, linking runtime anomaly detection with COCA’s code knowledge extraction and SBLLM’s search-based optimization to form a closed-loop remediation pipeline. Fourth, we will extend hardware-level prediction from Cordial to additional components and build cross-layer models connecting hardware signals with application-level impact. To execute these directions, we plan to create the AutoResilience testing framework, build a unified optimization platform, expand hardware-to-application prediction, and validate all innovations with industrial partners.

14206921.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14206921.value: Modern cloud computing systems, which power everything from online shopping to AI training, are incredibly complex and prone to failures that can disrupt services and cause significant financial losses. Our research focuses on making these systems more reliable and resilient. We developed intelligent tools that automatically detect when cloud systems are experiencing problems, much like a health monitoring system for computers. Our frameworks can identify performance issues before they cause major outages by analyzing system behavior patterns and understanding how different components interact with each other. When problems do occur, our system acts like a detective, automatically investigating issue reports and examining the underlying computer code to pinpoint root causes, dramatically reducing the time engineers need to diagnose failures from hours to seconds. We also developed methods to predict memory failures in high-performance computing systems used for AI training and tools to automatically optimize code for better performance. These innovations have been successfully deployed in production cloud systems serving millions of users, demonstrably improving system reliability, reducing downtime, and saving valuable engineering time. Our work makes cloud services more dependable and cost-effective for both providers and users.

14207021.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14207021.value: Millions of silicon photonics optical transceivers, mostly 100GbE today but migrating to 400GbE over the next five years, are being deployed in data centers which serve more than 90% of the global internet traffic. Waveguide grating couplers (WGC) are widely used in silicon photonics for coupling light between optical fibers and silicon waveguides. WGC have the advantages of not being limited in placement to the edge of the silicon chip, compatibility with wafer scale testing for selecting dies before the expensive process of photonic packaging, do not require (potentially low yield) facet polishing, have lower alignment precision requirement than edge couplers and, in the future, they may be used with spatial division multiplexing using multicore or multimode fibers. Current WGC are unsuited for use with wideband wavelength division multiplexing (WDM) because their optical bandwidth is insufficient, with only about 29nm 1dB optical bandwidth being typically offered by foundries. Edge couplers have over 100nm optical bandwidth, but being limited to the one dimensional edge of a planar waveguide, are unsuited for direct interface with the multicore fibers which can enable future increases in bandwidth density. 100GbE transceivers today can use four wavelengths in the Local Area Network (LAN) WDM grid (channel spacing of about 4.5nm) which are supported by current WGC technology. But more wavelengths, or the use of the ITU-defined 20nm CWDM channel spacings, will require WGC to have larger optical bandwidths. CWDM distributed feedback (DFB) lasers do not need precise temperature control nor precise wavelength registration, and therefore are low-cost and more suitable than the dense WDM DFB lasers developed for telecommunications. Low cost is essential for massive deployments in short reach intra-datacenter interconnects. For example, for 400GbE, eight WDM channels (instead of 4 WDM channels in 100GbE) is needed in one variant of the 400GbE standard. Further advances towards future 1.6Tb/s ethernet transceivers may need even more wavelength channels. In this proposal we aim to develop a new type of WGC which offers 1dB optical bandwidths of over 110nm. Such unprecedented wide optical bandwidths WGC will find applications in future wideband optical transceivers. In this project we propose the novel concept of Resonance-enhanced Waveguide Grating Coupler (REWGC) which we shall study in detail theoretically and experimentally. The REWGC will offer unprecedented optical bandwidth for use with wideband CWDM optical transceivers for future ultrahigh capacity data transmission. 數以百萬計的矽光收發器（目前主要是 100GbE，但在未來五年內將遷移到400GbE）正在數據中心部署，這些數據中心為全球 90%以上的互聯網流量提供服務。波導光柵耦合器 (WGC) 廣泛用於矽光子學中，用於在光纖和矽波導之間進行耦合。與邊緣耦合器相比，WGC 的優點是不受耦合位置的限制，與晶圓級測試兼容，可以在昂貴的光子封裝工藝之前，用於選擇芯片，不需要端面拋光（潛在的低良率），對耦合對準精度要求比較低，並且在未來，WGC可與多芯或多模光纖一起使用，進行空分複用。由於帶寬不足，當前的WGC不適合用來寬帶波分複用 (WDM)，代工廠通常只提供1dB帶寬大約為29nm的WGC。邊緣耦合器具有超過100nm的帶寬，但僅限用於平面波導的邊緣，不適合與實現帶寬密度提升的多芯光纖直接耦合。現在的 100GbE 收發器可以在局域網 (LAN) WDM 中使用四種波長（大約 4.5nm 的信道間隔），當前 WGC 支持這些波長。但是更多的波長，或使用 ITU 定義的 20nm CWDM 信道間隔，將需要 WGC 具有更大的帶寬。與為電信開發的密集 WDM 分佈式反饋 (DFB) 激光器相比， CWDM DFB激光器不需要精確的溫度控制和精確的波長配準，因此成本更低。低成本對於短距離數據中心內部互連的大規模部署至關重要。例如，在 400GbE 標準的一種版本中400GbE需要 8 個 WDM 通道（而不是 100GbE 中的 4 個 WDM 通道）。未來 1.6Tb/s 以太網收發器的進一步發展可能需要更多波長通道。在這個項目中，我們的目標是開發一種新型寬帶WGC，可以提供超過 110nm 的 1dB 帶寬。這種前所未有的寬帶 WGC 將在未來的寬帶光收發器中發揮重要應用。我們提出了共振增強波導光柵耦合器 (REWGC) 的新概念，我們將在理論上和實驗上詳細進行研究。REWGC 將提供前所未有的帶寬，用於未來超高容量數據傳輸的寬帶CWDM 光收發器。

14207021.label: Realisation of objectives
14207021.value: In this project we introduced several innovations which advanced the technology of wideband waveguide grating couplers. In the first of two different approaches , following the idea in the provisional patent that we filed at the time of writing the grant proposal, we were successful in increasing the 1dB bandwidth of waveguide grating couplers to 110nm. Later in the project we introduced a new second approach developed and we were able to increase the 1dB bandwidth to beyond 200nm. The first technique we introduced [1] and validated was based on the concept of reducing the grating length to increase its bandwidth and we engineered the mode matching by forming optical cavities centered at the middle of the grating with a mirror symmetric grating structure. We exploited the intensity enhancement by the cavities and the out of plane scattering at each discontinuity produced by the grating teeth. By running genetic numerical optimization algorithm we were able to achieve a reasonably uniform spectral response for a wide range of wavelengths, we were able to match spatial variation of the diffracted field along the grating with fiber mode pattern to achieve high coupling efficiency. The mirror symmetric grating structure naturally forms a peak in diffracted intensity a the center of the grating as is needed to match the peak in the mode field of the fiber at the center. The devices were fabricated initially in our own clean room and later in commercial foundries. We were able to measure 108nm 1dB bandwidths in the devices designed for off-normal out of plane coupling and fabricated by a IMEC [1] and 121nm 1dB fabricated devices in the devices designed for perfectly normal out of plane coupling [2]. Thus we fully successfully completed objective 1 of the project proposal in with the 121 experimentally achieved 1dB bandwidth surpassing the 110nm target set in objective 1. Furthermore the high efficiency broadband grating coupler fabricated by IMEC [2] also fully met the requirements for objective 2 of the project proposal. In the course of implementing the plan as set out in the original proposal we explored the novel idea of including the use of shifted polysilicon overlay for dual band granting couplers [3], polarization splitting grating couplers [4], and to use a vertical slot waveguide as means to tune the grating strength for wideband grating couplers [5]. With the latter approach we were able to demonstrate over 200nm 1dB bandwidths [5] and we also achieved ultralow back reflection, of less than -35dB [6]. These results far surpassed our original expectations. One of the difficulties we had in this project was insufficient funding, limiting our capability to buy the expensive custom multicore fibers, RF probes and RF amplifiers. Nonetheless we did carry out the silicon photonics development needed for the objective 3 and objective 4 demonstration of high speed data interconnects by integrating innovative (original designed developed by our group) high-speed modulators [7], novel fabrication-tolerant CWDM filters based n an innovative bent and angled multimode interferometer [8] and high-efficiency perfectly vertical grating couplers for use with multicore fiber [9], novel improved coupling efficiency polarization diversity grating couplers [10], and wide bandwidth with high coupling efficiency wideband gratings [11]. We implemented many of the device designs on a silicon chip and tested their performances individually. Individual modulators with over 300Gb/s data modulation were demonstrated and we demonstrated CWDM multiplexers and demultiplexers with four wavelength channels. Integrated together these devices can enable silicon photonics to drive data interconnects to scale well beyond 1Tb/s data rates [12, 13] but unfortunately we did not have four sets of Arbitrary waveform generators, 67GHz RF amplifiers and RF probes to drive all channels simultaneously, so we were unable to test the simultaneous operations of all wavelength channels. The fabricated silicon waveguides together with the ring resonators and the wide bandwidth grating couplers fabricated in this project also enabled us to carry out an energy-time quantum entanglement over 40km single mode fiber [14]. However without the resources to buy the many parallel data sources, modulator drivers and the multicore fibers, CWDM laser array and high speed detectors we could not demonstrate the aggregate >1Tbs CWDM data transmission and hence the objectives in 3 and 4 were only 95% complete, despite our having completed all the device design and their individual optical tests which were published in the papers listed below [7-13]. 14207021.label: Major findings and research outcome
14207021.value: The major findings include: 1. silicon photonic grating couplers can be designed and fabricated for >120nm bandwidth with high coupling efficiency of about 2dB. 2. Silicon photonics grating couplers could be designed for polarization spliting or polarization diversity operation. 3. We can implement a robust high efficiency design with 0.6dB coupling loss only at the expense of reducing the operational bandwidth to about 40nm 1dB bandwidth. 4 Silicon photonics modulators can have 3dB bandwidths of over 90GHz and enable over 100Gbaud data transmission. 5. Silicon photonics is a promising technology for high capacity data interconnects.

14207021.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14207021.value: There is excellent potential to use silicon photonics in future co-packaged optics for the scale-up and scale out networks needed in the large computing networks used to train large languague models. there remains many challenges for further research, such as whether it is possible to achieve robust fabrication tolerances to enable large arrays of grating couplers to couple to large arrays of multicore fiber for the high bandwidth density I/O needed in data centers, Another challenge is how to maintain high signal fidelity without the use of the digital signal processors (which cannot easily scale to hte >100Gbaud data rates and still maintain the low power consumption and low latency needed in the scale up networks of data centers.

14207021.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14207021.value: The results of this project advanced the state of the art in silicon photonics and addresses the critical problems of how to achieve low coupling loss over a wide spectral range of over 110nm nd coupling losses as low as 0.6dB. The silicon photonics technologies will underpin the future development of power efficient training of large AI models in data centers.

14207121.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14207121.value: Foodborne diseases, which mainly result from the contamination of food or water by harmful bacteria and viruses, are responsible for 600 million cases of foodborne illnesses and 42,000 deaths globally every year. The aggravated burden of these diseases has increased the demand for rapid laboratory food pathogen tests. However, traditional microbiological culture-based methods are time-consuming, and thus, cannot provide an effective screening of samples to prevent the spread of contaminated pathogens. Although strategies that rely on nucleic acid-based methods, immunological methods, or other biosensors have shown potential, the time-consuming step of bacterial cultivation remains necessary given the need to pre-enrich the bacteria and validate the live pathogens. The proposed project aims to develop a new diagnostic method based on a novel biomarker based on the activities of essential enzymes in the target foodborne pathogens. Currently, there are no competitive technologies in the market that possess the combined capacities of sensitivity, specificity, and time-to-readout. Once this new diagnostic approach is successfully validated, the improvement in pathogen monitoring is expected to enable the rapid pathogen-based testing of all suspected cases. This will allow competent authorities and food companies to better contain and mitigate epidemics by detecting hazardous contamination before products are marketed, thereby reducing the economic impact of outbreaks, facilitating international trade, and enhancing food-chain sustainability and security. Along with the technical development, we have teamed up with an industrial partner to validate the diagnostic method in the food sector and to formulate a business plan and marketing strategy. It is expected that this combined effort will increase the speed at which the technology will reach the identified beneficiaries, both locally and globally. The success of the proposed study will represent an important opportunity to translate Hong Kong’s scientific excellence into societal impacts in the near future, thus helping transform the Greater Bay Area into an international powerhouse for combating foodborne outbreaks. 食源性疾病主要由有害細菌和病毒污染食物或水引起，每年在全球造成6億食源性疾病病例及4.2萬死亡病例。逐漸加劇的食源性疾病，增加了快速檢測食物病原體污染的需求。然而，基於微生物培養的傳統方法耗時較長，無法有效篩選樣本，並進一步防止受污染病原體的傳播。儘管現有基於核酸檢測、免疫學或其他生物傳感器檢測的策略顯示快速檢測的潛力，但考慮到需要預先富集細菌及驗證活病原體，耗時的細菌培養仍然是必要的。擬議的項目旨在開發一種基於新型生物標誌物的診斷方法，該生物標誌物乃是基於目標食源病原體內的必需酶活性。目前市場上還沒有同時兼顧靈敏度、特異性和實時讀取等性能的競爭性技術，因此，一旦這種新的診斷方法得到成功驗證，主管部門和食品公司能在產品上市前提早檢測到可能致病的污染，並更好地控制和減少食源性致病菌的傳播，從而減少因食源污染對經濟的影響，加強食物鏈的可持續性和安全性。隨著技術的發展，我們將與工業夥伴合作，以在食品相關行業驗證提出的診斷方法，並制定商業計畫和營銷策略。預計這種聯合策略將加快此技術在香港當地和全球惠及受益者的速度。我們期望，本擬議研究的成功，可以在不久的將來，將香港的科學成果轉化為社會影響，使得大灣區能成為抗擊食源性疾病爆發的國際領先群。

14207121.label: Realisation of objectives
14207121.value: The aim of this project is to to develop and validate a new biomarker for identifying ‘live’ foodborne pathogens with high specificity, high sensitivity and short time-to-result. During the project period, we have realized the proposed objectives as the following: Objective 1. Develop the Mag-Hydro-Drops for Enzyme Extraction from Single Bacterium and Subsequent Reactions: We have developed the hydrogel-based microreactors, which retain the benefits of a confined reaction but eliminate the problems associated with the water–oil interface, thus ensuring that microbial enzymes may be effectively extracted and that the subsequent aqueous reactions may be easily integrated. Polyacrylamide (PAA)-based hydrogel beads were produced by a standard droplet microfluidic device fabricated by conventional soft lithography. Briefly, a polydimethylsiloxane prepolymer was cast and cured on the SU-8 master following a standard protocol. Our results demonstrated that the droplet size and generation frequency can be modulated through flow competition between the oil phase (Qo: fluorocarbon oil HFE-7500 with 0.5% PicoSurf and 0.5% v/v tetramethylethylenediamine [TEMED]) and aqueous phase (Qa, Reagent 1: hydrogel precursor (10% v/v acrylamide, 1% w/v ammonium persulfate and magnetic particles). The designed device can produce thousands of uniform PAA beads (50  0.5 μm). Furthermore, the acrydite-modified RCA primers were facilely incorporated into the PAA beads during polymerisation through an overnight incubation. The bacteriophages specifically targeting E. coli (E. coli bacteriophage T4, ATCC) have shown effective to break non-pathogenic E. coli expressing EcoRI in a bulk manner. The Bradford assay is validated for the evaluation of enzyme extraction by measuring the extracted total enzymes/proteins through a colorimetric assay based on an absorbance shift of the dye bound to the proteins. Additionally, we have validated that the targets may be amplified through Rolling Circle Amplification (RCA) in the gel beads. Briefly, PAA beads were pre-functionalized with acrydite-modified RCA primers. Polymerase Phi-29 was able to produce DNA tandem repeats in the presence of pre-formed circles, as a mimic of enzyme targets, and the fluorescent probes can hybridize with the identification regions on the tandem, which differs distinctly from the case without the pre-formed circles. Pre-formed circles modified by purified human topoisomerase 1 (human TOP1) were applied to validate the amplification reaction in the PAA beads. Hybridisation duration and limit of detection using titrated amounts of pre-formed TOP1 circles have been explored to optimise the reaction on PAA beads. EcoRI specific DNA substrates have also been applied as the circular template for the on-beads rolling circle amplification and has proven successful. Buffers as well as DNA substrate concentration for the EcoRI cleavage reaction have been investigated and optimised prior to RCA on PAA beads. Objective 2. Develop a Set of DNA Nanosensors for the Detection of Targeted Bacterial Endonuclease: Our patented assay can specifically detect the targeted activities of either purified enzymes or enzymes extracted from E. coli. To exploit the technology to specifically detect E. coli O157:H7, a bioinformatic approach was introduced to identify EcoRI expressed by E. coli O157:H7. The process of identifying specific DNA substrates for different pathogen-specific enzymes follows a bioinformatics approach that involves determining the targeted bacteria’s genetic fabric in all available databases to ensure that only the best enzymes are selected, based on the specificity of identifying the targeted pathogens. The ‘percent identity’ of a set of three randomly selected enzymes expressed by the E. coli O157:H7 was briefly compared with the enzymes expressed by other organisms, as predicted in the REBASE database (http://rebase.neb.com) and NCBI blast (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/). When a similar set of enzymes is found in another organism, a new set of enzymes from the E. coli O157:H7 was evaluated. The final sets of the selected enzymes were verified using bioinformatics and/or genome sequencing, as appropriate. Such procedure has been validated by our AU collaborator for E. coli, wherein a putative set of enzymes was found to be isoschizomers of the commercially available endonucleases, EcoRI, XhoI and PstI. The DNA nanosensor targeting EcoRI was designed as per the previously validated strategy in our patented assay, a pair of linear DNA substrates containing a specific cleavage site for EcoRI, together with ‘ligation blocks’, essentially an amine functional group at both 3’ and 5’ ends of the DNA nanosensor (T4 EcoRI PA substrate: 5’- /AmC6/ ATTCACTgaattcAGCGCTTAGGAGTGCATATACGATGCACTGTGAAGATCGCTTATGCATCGTATATGCACTCCTAAGCGCTgaattcAGTGAAT /AmC6/-3’, T4 EcoRI ID substrate: 5′- /AmC6/ ATTTGACgaattcGTCGTATAGGAACTTCGAACGACTCGCCTCAA TGCACATGTGGCTCCCGAGTCGTTCGAAGTTCCTATACGACgaattcGTCAAAT/AmC6/ -3′). In the absence of EcoRI, the DNA nanosensor remained uncleaved, and thus, the two pieces of DNA would not be fused. In the presence of EcoRI, the pair of DNA nanosensors was cleaved with the amines removed, allowing the DNA ligase to fuse the two pieces of DNA. The covalently closed DNA circle was then amplified by polymerase-assisted isothermal RCA, following our previously published protocol. Objective 3. Develop and Characterize an Analytical Platform for the Detection of Single Cell Activities: The proposed project primarily aims to specifically identify the presence of E. coli O157:H7 in low concentration. We have therefore developed a customised detection platform for analysing enzyme activities in single drops. We have developed a customised fluorescence spectroscopy that can analyse fluorescent emissions in each mag-hydro-drop. The excitation from a 488-nm laser will be focused through an oil immersion 20× objective lens (NA = 0.95, Nikon) to excite the observation volume within the microfluidic channel. The emission was then collected through the same objective, passed through a pinhole and separated by appropriate dichroic mirrors and bandpass filters before being detected by independent photomultiplier modules (PMM02-1, Thorlabs). Customised Labview programs was used to control the motorised translation stage and communicate with a digital counter (National Instruments) for data acquisition and analysis. The integrated platform, termed hydrogel Bead-based Isothermal Detection (BEAD-ID) was subsequently used to evaluate the activity of DNA-modifying enzymes on-bead. We validate BEAD-ID’s effectiveness through the quantification of two DNA-modifying enzymes, human TOP1 and restriction endonuclease EcoRI. Our results indicate a direct correlation between enzyme concentration and fluorescence intensity on the oligo-PAA beads, demonstrating the platform’s sensitivity (6.25 nM TOP1, 6.25 U/L EcoRI) and reliability in food matrix (25 U/L EcoRI in milk matrix). Furthermore, we introduce a customized flow cytometry-mimicking setup for high-throughput detection and quantification of fluorescence of up to 352 Hz, providing rapid and objective assessment of enzyme activities. Compared to conventional methods, BEAD-ID offers enhanced flexibility and scalability in enzyme activity assessment, positioning it as a promising tool for diagnosis and analyses to further our understanding of DNA-modifying enzymes. Traditional quantification methods for the study of DNA-modifying enzymes often neglect enzymatic activities, prompting the need for innovative approaches to ensure accurate assessments. This project has developed BEAD-ID, employing hydrogel beads as a micro-incubator and micro-carrier of reporting products. This beads-based setup offers a facile solution for enzyme detection and quantification via commonly used detection schemes, fluorescence microscopy and a flow cytometry mimicking setup. Derived from the surface-based REEAD setup, BEAD-ID advances by providing a high-throughput and objective assessment scheme. Moreover, customisable properties of hydrogel beads may extend the utility of BEAD-ID for a wide range of biochemical applications.

14207121.label: Major findings and research outcome
14207121.value: The proposed BEAD-ID was shown promising for a quantitative assessment of enzymatic activities. As a characterization of the system, reporter probes were observed via the corrected total bead fluorescence (CTBF) based quantification. The signal to noise ratio (S/N) was characterized at 157, indicating robust fluorescence signal with low noise. Moreover, the limit-of-detection (LOD) was determined using the 3 approach, where the LOD is defined as the blank mean + three times the standard deviation of the blank sample. The LOD was estimated to be 0.99 amol/bead. As a model enzyme, the activity of TOP1 on-bead was assessed by the microfluidic flow setup. Fluorescence signal and enzyme concentration was observed well correlated. The quantification of TOP1 activity yielded a S/N of 23 and a LOD of 2.44 nM TOP1, suggesting a reliable fluorescence-based detection of the enzyme activity in the customized optical flow system. Noted that up to 7,000 beads were assessed in the flow system per experiment, ensuring the statistical power and thereby providing an objective analysis compared to CTBF quantification. We have published the developed platform and findings in two journal articles: Biosensors (Impact Factor: 5.6, top 15% in the field of Instruments & Instrumentation, Peer-Reviewed Publications #1) and iScience (Impact Factor: 4.1, top 25% in the field of Multidisciplinary Sciences, Peer-Reviewed Publications #4). We have presented the results in three international conferences presentations (Recognized international conference #2-4). Beyond the described tasks in the proposal, we have also collaborated with Prof. Aaron Ho Pui Ho in the Chinese University of Hong Kong to develop a workflow that may simply the fabrication step and reduce the fabrication cost. The results are presented in a flagship conference in the field of lab on a chip (Peer-reviewed Conference Paper #1). We have also initiated a collaboration with Prof. Shuwen Zeng to develop novel sensing mechanisms for the detection of molecular activities. The results have been published as a peer-reviewed journal article in Analyst (Impact Factor: 3.3, top 40% in the field of Analytical Chemistry, Peer-Reviewed Publications #3). We have also co-authored a review article to discuss the technical needs in the field, published in Advanced Optical Materials (Impact Factor: 7.2, top 15% in the field of Optics, Peer-Reviewed Publications #2). Additionally, a PhD student trained by this project was awarded 1st runner up in the Research Poster Exhibition hosted by the Chinese University of Hong Kong in 2022 (Other Impact #2).

14207121.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14207121.value: Beyond this project, we have furthered the study to different applications, particularly under the scope of droplet-based polymerase chain reaction (ddPCR) and single cell analysis. A project in collaboration with Dr. Meng Yan at the State Key Laboratory of Marine Pollution (now renamed as the State Key Laboratory of Marine Environmental Health, SKLMEH), focusing on the application of ddPCR for biodiversity studies is funded by the Hong Kong Offshore LNG Terminal Project, under the scheme of Marine Conservation Enhancement Fund (Other Impact #3). Further, a patent relevant to the sequencing of single bacteria has also be filed (Other Impact #1).

14207221.label: Project Objectives
14207221.value: This project aims to provide a coherent guideline on the design and processing of ion-blocking interfaces for achieving stable and bright metal halide perovskite light-emitting diodes (PeLEDs). The detailed technical objectives include: To understand how the composition and configuration of the interface organic molecules affect their (1) binding strength and electronic interactions with the perovskite lattice and (2) steric hindrance against ion migration and charge transport. To develop well-controlled fabrication processes for creating perovskite/charge-transporting layer interfaces with low defect density, high ion-blocking capability and sufficient charge injection capacity; To extend the findings from Objectives 2 and 3 to color-tunable perovskite systems and understand how the interface molecular designs should be modified to accommodate the lattice variation induced by mixed halide (e.g., I and Br) and mixed cation (e.g., Cs and bulky organic cation) compositions. To systematically describe the interface modification effects through combined chemical, morphological, structural, optical and electrical characterizations and theoretical modelling; Through optimizing the processing conditions and device structures, to demonstrate PeLEDs with excellent stability and high brightness, e.g., PeLEDs with > 22% peak external quantum efficiency, >5000 cd/m^2 brightness, and a T50 (at 200cd/m^2) of > 1000 hours.

14207221.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14207221.value: This project aims to provide a coherent guideline on the design and processing of ion-blocking interfaces for achieving stable and bright metal halide perovskite light-emitting diodes (PeLEDs). A systematic theoretical and experimental investigation will be carried out to understand how the molecular configuration, chemical bonding, defect and lattice structure of the perovskite surfaces concertedly affect the operation stability and efficiency of PeLEDs. PeLEDs have shown great potential in low-cost and energy-efficient lighting and display applications because of their low-temperature processability, high electroluminescence efficiency and color purity. However, the poor operational stability of PeLEDs remains as a main bottleneck for commercialization. Many PeLEDs exhibit significantly degraded radiance or shifted emission wavelength within hours of operation. Recently reported passivation and ligand engineering methods, while substantially enhanced PeLED efficiency, are not yet able to address the stability issue. Also, the commonly used material recipes for stability improvement of perovskite solar cells cannot be applied directly to solve the PeLED degradation problems due to the large differences of the two types of devices in film thickness and morphology, internal electric field and material composition. Very recently, we found that the stability of PeLEDs can be greatly enhanced by suppressing ion migration across the perovskite/charge-transport layer interface with a molecular passivation layer. Yet, there lacks a guideline on how such molecular ion-blocking interfaces should be designed and processed to enable stable, bright and wavelength-tunable PeLEDs. In this project we will focus on the following four research tasks to develop a systematic approach for building ion-blocking interfaces. Firstly, we will carry out a comparative study to investigate how the configuration (e.g., linear vs branched) and composition (e.g., anchoring groups) of the passivation molecules affect their interactions with the perovskite lattice and their steric hindrance against ion migration. Secondly we will develop fabrication methods to optimize the efficacy of top and bottom interface modification. The first two tasks will be performed on three-dimensional perovskite systems (e.g., CsPbBr3) so that the modification effects at the interfaces can be decoupled from those in the bulk emissive layer. Thirdly, to extend the findings to multi-color PeLEDs, we will vary the perovskite composition to explore how the interface design should be modified to accommodate the lattice variation induced by mixed halide (or mixed cation) compositions. Finally, we will study the device physics associated with the interface modification and establish physical models to describe the operation and degradation mechanisms of the PeLEDs. 該項目旨在為實現穩定、高亮度的金屬鹵化物鈣鈦礦發光二極管 (PeLED)設計離子阻擋界面。通過進行系統的理論和實驗研究，以揭示鈣鈦礦表面的分子構型、化學鍵、缺陷和晶格結構如何協同影響 PeLED 的運行穩定性和效率。 PeLED 因其低溫加工性、高電致發光效率和色純度，在低成本和節能的照明和顯示應用中顯示出巨大的潛力。然而，PeLED 運行穩定性差仍然是其走向商業化的主要瓶頸。許多 PeLED 在運行數小時內表現出顯著降低的輻射或改變的發射波長。最近報導的鈍化和配體工程等材料處理方法雖然顯著提高了 PeLED 效率，但還不能解決其穩定性問題。此外，而用於提高鈣鈦礦太陽能電池穩定性的常用材料配方也由於兩種類型器件在薄膜厚度、形態、內部電場和材料成分等方面的差異，不能直接應用於解決 PeLED 的問題。最近，我們發現通過使用分子鈍化層抑制離子在鈣鈦礦/電荷傳輸層界面的遷移，可大大增強 PeLED 的穩定性。然而，關於如何系統設計和處理離子阻擋界面仍缺乏理論指導和實驗方法。 在本項目中，我們將專注於以下四項研究任務，最終建立構建離子阻擋界面的系統方案。首先，我們將通過比較研究，闡述鈍化分子的空間架構和成份組成如何影響它們與鈣鈦礦晶格的相互作用以及它們對離子遷移的空間位阻。其次，我們將研發材料處理方法以支持鈣鈦礦頂部和底部界面修飾與優化。前兩項任務將在三維鈣鈦礦系統（例如 CsPbBr3）上執行，以便界面處的改性效果可以與體發光層中的改性效果分離。第三，為了將研究結果擴展到多色 PeLED，我們將改變鈣鈦礦成份，探索如何修改界面設計以適應混合鹵化物（或混合陽離子）成分引起的晶格變化。最後，我們將研究與界面修改相關的器件物理特性，並建立物理模型來描述 PeLED 的運行和退化機制。

14207221.label: Realisation of objectives
14207221.value: For Objectives 1 and 2, we systematically investigated how the composition, configuration, and functionalization of interface organic molecules influence their binding strength, electronic interaction, and steric blocking effects at metal halide perovskite interfaces. Through a series of experimental studies employing diammonium cations, bulky branched ammonium cations, and functionalized aromatic ammonium cations, we established clear structure–property relationships governing organic–perovskite interfacial interactions. We demonstrated that interface molecules can exhibit selective binding preferences toward specific lattice components (e.g., Pb–Br versus Pb–I octahedra), leading to controlled crystallization pathways and surface reconstruction. The steric size and molecular geometry of the organic cations were shown to play a decisive role in suppressing ion migration and leakage current pathways while maintaining effective electronic coupling with the perovskite lattice. These findings provide a mechanistic understanding of how interface molecular design balances defect passivation, ion blocking, and charge transport. For Objective 3, we developed well controlled interface modification and post deposition treatment processes compatible with solution processed 3D perovskite films. Instead of relying on thick reduced dimensional interlayers that often impede charge injection, we focused on mild, surface localized interface regulation strategies that preserve bulk crystallinity. These include controlled incorporation of diammonium species to form thin quasi 2D surface shells, organic cation mediated halide exchange treatments to regulate halide redistribution, and surface anion engineering to reduce defect formation during solvent processing. These approaches consistently yielded perovskite/charge transport layer interfaces with reduced defect density, enhanced ion blocking capability, and sufficient charge injection efficiency, thereby achieving the intended balance between stability and performance. For Objective 4, we successfully extended the interface design principles developed in earlier objectives to color tunable mixed halide perovskite systems spanning red, blue, and deep blue emission. The project revealed that mixed halide and mixed cation compositions introduce additional lattice strain, halide heterogeneity, and ion migration challenges, which necessitate adaptive interface molecular designs. We demonstrated that selective molecular binding, steric hindrance, and functional group engineering can be tuned to accommodate lattice variation induced by different halide ratios while maintaining structural integrity and spectral stability. These results confirm that the importance of interface engineering is broadly applicable across multiple emission colors and mixed composition perovskite systems. For Objective 5, we systematically characterized the effects of interface modification using a comprehensive combination of chemical, morphological, structural, optical, and electrical analyses. Correlative studies linking interface molecular structure to film morphology, photoluminescence behavior, charge transport characteristics, leakage current suppression, and operational stability enabled a coherent description of interface driven performance enhancement. These experimental observations were further interpreted through theoretical models of crystallization behavior, defect passivation, and ion migration pathways, providing an integrated understanding of interface modification effects. For Objective 6, we demonstrated PeLEDs with high brightness, high efficiency, and significantly improved operational stability through optimized interface design and processing conditions. For example, red PeLEDs developed under this project achieved a record luminance of 10,745 cd m⁻² and a half lifetime exceeding 15 hours under a high current density of 20 mA cm⁻², representing state of the art performance among 3D perovskite based red LEDs. In addition, blue mixed halide 3D PeLEDs realized under this project delivered a record external quantum efficiency of 19.28%, highlighting the effectiveness of the interface engineering strategies developed. Building upon the scientific foundations established in this project, more recent work on solid state ligand exchange of CsPbI₃ nanocrystals using halide containing inorganic ligands has further pushed the external quantum efficiency of red PeLEDs to above 23% (unpublished). While the ambitious targets of simultaneously achieving a peak external quantum efficiency exceeding 22% and a T50 longer than 1000 hours at 200 cd m⁻² within a single device architecture were not fully realized during the project period, this outcome reflects a widely recognized and ongoing challenge in the field of visible light PeLEDs. In particular, the intrinsic trade offs among ion blocking, charge injection, spectral stability, and operational lifetime—especially in wide bandgap mixed halide perovskites—remain a major bottleneck at the international research frontier. To address these fundamental limitations, the project strategically prioritized the development of transferable interface design guidelines and mechanistic understanding, which have established a solid foundation for continued device optimization and long term stability improvements beyond the project timeframe. 14207221.label: Major findings and research outcome
14207221.value: 1. We demonstrated that diammonium halides can be employed to regulate the crystallization of mixed bromide–iodide perovskite films by selectively interacting with Pb–Br octahedra. This selective binding promotes the formation of thin quasi 2D surface layers during film growth, leading to efficiently passivated perovskite grains with reduced lattice strain. As a result, 3D perovskite based red PeLEDs exhibited record luminance and improved operational stability, highlighting the effectiveness of diammonium induced ion blocking interfaces (Publication #2). 2. We established that the organic cations used in post deposition halide exchange processes play a decisive role in determining current transport and leakage behavior in deep blue PeLEDs. By comparing linear and bulky branched ammonium cations, we showed that branch structured cations can effectively fill inter grain voids without disrupting the 3D perovskite lattice, thereby suppressing leakage currents and enabling record efficiency deep blue PeLEDs (Publication #3). 3. We revealed that subtle chemical functionalization of interface cations critically influences their surface binding strength and resistance to solvent induced lattice damage during halide post treatment. Fluorinated aromatic ammonium cations were shown to preserve the 3D perovskite structure while effectively passivating surface defects, leading to mixed halide blue PeLEDs with high efficiency, excellent color purity, and improved spectral stability (Publication #4). 4. We introduced surface anion engineering using acetate rich interfaces to address halide heterogeneity induced by conventional post treatment processes. Strong acetate–lead interactions were found to suppress halide vacancy formation and slow halide infiltration, enabling uniform halide redistribution and record efficiency blue mixed halide 3D PeLEDs with narrowband emission (Publication #5). Together, these outcomes provide a coherent mechanistic framework and practical toolbox for interface engineering in PeLEDs, significantly advancing the field toward stable, high performance perovskite optoelectronic devices.

14207221.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14207221.value: The research outcomes of this project reveal substantial potential for further development toward simultaneously achieving ultra high efficiency and long term operational stability in visible light perovskite LEDs. While significant progress has been made in interface molecular design and processing control, the intrinsic trade offs among ion blocking, charge injection, and spectral stability—particularly in wide bandgap mixed halide perovskites—remain a key challenge across the field. Future work will focus on extending the interface design guidelines established in this project to more robust material systems and device architectures. Specifically, rational co design of interface molecules and charge transport layers will be pursued to further decouple ion migration suppression from charge injection efficiency. Advanced surface and interface characterization, combined with in situ and operando measurements, will be employed to directly probe ion dynamics and interfacial degradation mechanisms under electrical bias.

14207221.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14207221.value: Metal halide perovskites are emerging as highly attractive materials for next generation light emitting diodes (LEDs) due to their excellent optoelectronic properties and solution processability. Despite rapid progress in device efficiency, the operational stability of perovskite LEDs (PeLEDs) remains a major obstacle to practical implementation. A key origin of this instability is ion migration and defect formation at perovskite interfaces under electrical bias. This project focused on the rational design and processing of ion blocking interfaces to address these challenges. By systematically investigating the role of organic cations and anions at perovskite surfaces and grain boundaries, the research established clear structure–property relationships linking interfacial chemistry to film formation, defect passivation, charge transport, and device stability. The outcomes include controlled interface modification strategies applicable to mixed halide perovskites across red, blue, and deep blue emission regimes. The project delivered several state of the art PeLED demonstrations with record luminance or efficiency and, more importantly, developed transferable interface design guidelines that clarify fundamental trade offs between ion blocking and charge injection. These insights provide a solid foundation for further optimization of high performance, stable perovskite optoelectronic devices.
