14207421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14207421.value: Nucleic acid testing is of crucial importance in clinical diagnoses, such as that of cancers and viral infectious diseases. Existing technologies, such as polymerase chain reaction, may require fluorescent labeling and enzyme application, making it sensitive to inhibitors and challenging for routine use in a time-efficient setting. An ideal nucleic acid test would be not only rapid yet accurate, but also simple yet multiplexing. The last decades witnessed the success of nano-bioelectronics development in low-abundant nucleic acid testing of body fluids associated with various diseases. Graphene is a two-dimensional (2D) nanomaterial that holds tremendous promise for label- and enzyme-free detection of nucleic acid with high accuracy and selectivity. Although extensive research has been conducted on monolayer graphene-based nucleic acid biosensors, primarily with a limit-of-detection (LOD) at fM level, the zero-bandgap nature of monolayer graphene and its binding-affinity-dependent LOD inhibit further advancements of rapid and accurate detection of low-level nucleic acid. The proposed research aims to develop an electronic biosensing system for highly sensitive and rapid detection of nucleic acids, i.e., 1 aM, within 10-20 minutes, through the combined use of gapped ABC-stacked trilayer graphene (ABC-TLG) and an exponential signal amplification scheme. First, we will develop a chemical vapor deposition process to grow large-area ABC-TLG, with a controlled stacking order and layer numbers. Second, we will fabricate ABC-TLG FET sensor arrays on a large-scale using photolithography, with the capability of real-time and multiplexed measurement. Lastly, we will develop a dendrimer‐based exponential self-assembly amplification reaction that can operate on ABC-TLG for rapid and sensitive nucleic acid testing. The proposed project is novel and highly notable for multiple reasons. 1) The application of ABC-TLG with a tunable band gap in biosensing has not been reported before, which would lead to a substantial improvement in detection sensitivity, compared to the conventional monolayer graphene-based biosensors without a band gap. 2) Large-area growth of ABC-TLG is a fundamental critical advancement in understanding 2D-material synthesis with controlled atomic stacking order, which could catalyze a wide range of biosensing applications. 3) Scalable fabrication of biosensor arrays based on ABC-TLG has yet to be achieved. 4) Involving dendrimer‐based exponential signal amplification in the production of graphene-based nucleic acid biosensors is a novel approach. Project success would lead to a rapid low-level nucleic acid test that is label- and enzyme-free, thereby potentially making an impact on clinical diagnostics, such as that of early-stage cancers and viral infectious diseases. 核酸檢測在癌癥、病毒感染性疾病等臨床診斷中具有重要的意義。現有的檢測技術，如聚合酶鏈反應，需要使用酶和熒光標記，令其對抑製劑敏感，不利於日常的高頻使用。理想的核酸檢測方法不僅要快速、準確、簡單，而且能實現多重並行檢測。在過去幾十年中，納米生物電子學在檢測體液中低豐度核酸方面展現了廣闊的應用前景，對各種疾病的早期診斷具有重要意義。其中，二維石墨烯納米材料在無標記、無酶核酸檢測方面表現出高精度、高特異性等特點，顯示其巨大的應用潛力。盡管學界對基於單層石墨烯的核酸生物傳感器已進行了廣泛的研究，但檢測限（LOD）多在fM水平。由於單層石墨烯沒有帶隙，其檢測限依賴於核酸間的結合親和力，這限製了該技術在快速準確檢測低豐度核酸中的進一步發展。本研究旨在開發一種基於ABC堆疊的三層石墨烯 (ABC-TLG)和指數信號放大方案相結合的生物電子平臺，從而實現對核酸的快速、高靈敏檢測。首先，我們擬開發一種化學氣相沈積法實現大面積ABC-TLG的可控合成。進一步，我們將采用光刻工藝大規模製備ABC-TLG場效應管傳感器陣列, 實現實時、多重並行檢測。最後，我們將設計開發可在ABC-TLG生物傳感器上進行的樹枝狀自組裝指數擴增反應，實現快速、靈敏的核酸檢測。本項目的新穎性和特點體現在以下幾個方面。1）目前，基於可調帶隙的ABC-TLG生物傳感器還未被報道，相較於常規零帶隙單層石墨烯生物傳感器，ABC-TLG的應用將顯著提高檢測的靈敏性。2）ABC-TLG的大面積生長是二維材料可控堆疊合成中的關鍵進展，將促進其在生物傳感領域的廣泛應用。3）大規模製備基於ABC-TLG的生物傳感器陣列還尚未實現。4）在石墨烯核酸生物傳感器中，使用樹枝狀指數信號擴增是一種新型方法。本項目的順利實施將促進無標記、無酶、快速、低濃度核酸檢測的發展，可在早期癌癥以及病毒感染等疾病的臨床診斷上發揮作用。

14207421.label: Realisation of objectives
14207421.value: In this project, we have achieved our goals by delivering a label-free biosensing platform capable of rapid and sensitive nucleic acid detection. Over the project period, the work generated 3 peer-reviewed publications, supported the training of 1 PhD candidate, and led to the awarding of 1 MPhil degree. First, we systematically engineered and evaluated 2D materials to realize bandgaps suitable for high-performance field-effect transistor (FET) biosensors. Building on the chemical vapor deposition (CVD) growth of ABC-stacked trilayer graphene (ABC-TLG) on Ni-Cu gradient alloys, we elucidated the growth mechanism and established a curvature-based stacking selection strategy. Specifically, we demonstrated control over ABC stacking by tailoring substrate topography, using boron nitride nanotubes (diameter of 30 nm) as curvature templates. In parallel, we developed CVD recipes for synthesizing transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs), including MoS₂ and WS₂. We adopted monolayer MoS₂ as the active sensing material, leveraging its substantial intrinsic bandgap (1.8 eV) to maximize the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) for biosensing applications. Second, we established a scalable CVD and photolithography process to fabricate high-yield MoS₂ FET arrays with excellent device-to-device uniformity. Using continuous monolayer MoS₂ films, we achieved a device fabrication yield of approximately 93% (14 out of 15 channels). The intrinsic bandgap of MoS₂ effectively reduces off-state current, yielding an average on/off ratio of 10^6 and a carrier mobility of 1.5 cm^2V^–1s^–1. Furthermore, we developed a robust Au-nanoparticle-based surface chemistry to immobilize DNA probes, creating a stable, well-defined transduction interface compatible with downstream signal-amplification schemes. Third, to overcome the intrinsic limitations of linear amplification, specifically the extended testing times (e.g., ~15 hours), we designed an enzyme-free, DNA dendrimer-based exponential self-assembly scheme for nucleic acid detection. Target binding initiates toehold-mediated strand displacement in helper hairpins, driving autocatalytic dendrimer growth directly on the FET surface. Integrating this exponential self-assembly scheme with gapped MoS₂ FET sensors enabled the detection of aM level target DNA within 20 minutes. These advances define a practical and scalable route to the electronic detection of low-abundance nucleic acids and position the platform for future translation to point-of-care diagnostic assays.

14207421.label: Major findings and research outcome
14207421.value: This project has delivered a label-free biosensing platform for rapid, sensitive nucleic acid detection by integrating controlled 2D-material growth, interface engineering, and programmable DNA nanotechnology. It advances 2D-material bioelectronics from materials synthesis and device engineering to molecular-level signal processing. The work has yielded 3 peer-reviewed journal publications, supported the training of 1 Ph.D. candidate, and led to the awarding of 1 MPhil degree. The principal outcomes are summarized as follows: (1) We established controlled CVD synthesis for advanced 2D materials, including curvature-driven growth of ABC-stacked trilayer graphene and active control of ABC stacking via substrate topography using boron nitride nanotubes. We developed scalable CVD recipes for monolayer MoS₂ and a photolithography process enabling high-quality device arrays (93% yield, on/off ~10^6, mobility ~1.5 cm^2V^–1s^–1). We further demonstrated label-free steroid detection in clinical plasma using PEG-modified graphene FETs to extend the effective Debye length, achieving ~1 fM detection in <15 min (PART C: Research Output #1). To enable rapid nucleic acid assays, we integrated a robust Au-nanoparticle interface with an enzyme-free, autocatalytic DNA dendrimer amplification scheme, enabling aM-level detection on MoS₂ FETs in <20 min, supporting a scalable route toward point-of-care diagnostics. (2) We developed synthetic allosteric DNA aptamers with precise ON-OFF regulation based on the Lettuce fluorogenic aptamer, and engineered toehold-mediated strand-displacement nano-switches that activate fluorescence only upon target recognition. We extended this framework to implement Boolean logic gates (AND/OR/XOR) and combinatorial circuits, and applied the aptamers to “light-up” DNA origami for morphology characterization. We also implemented RNase H1-assisted cyclic amplification for low-abundance mRNA detection (PART C: Research Output #2). (3) We synthesized 2D graphene quasicrystals with 30° alternating twist angles via CVD and observed emergent periodic moiré fringes. We developed and experimentally validated a stress-cancellation model in which interlayer interactions induce layer-parity-dependent in-plane strain, supported by TEM evidence of atomic relaxation and lattice stretching. This work establishes a direct route to moiré quasicrystals and a platform for exploring strain-engineered electronic states and non-periodic physical phenomena (PART C: Research Output #3).

14207421.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14207421.value: The FET platform established in this project provides a robust foundation for both fundamental studies and translation. The tunable bandgap of ABC-TLG and the intrinsic bandgap of monolayer MoS₂, together with our scalable, high-yield array fabrication and stable Au-nanoparticle transduction interface, enable integrated diagnostics with local signal processing. In the next phase, we will: (1) develop miniaturized, low-noise readout electronics with multiplexing and embedded control to deliver portable, battery-powered instruments for rapid testing in clinics and resource-limited settings; (2) further exploit the exponential kinetics of enzyme-free dendrimer self-assembly to achieve highly sensitive detection of ultra-low viral loads and early-stage disease, while maintaining short assay times; and (3) validate the platform using clinical samples, benchmarking accuracy, robustness, and turnaround time against standard assays to de-risk point-of-care translation.

14207421.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14207421.value: This project developed a new electronic biosensor that can detect extremely small amounts of disease-related genetic material (DNA or RNA) rapidly and without labels. In many hospital workflows, standard nucleic acid tests can take hours and may still struggle when the amount of virus or cancer marker is very low. Our solution combines an ultrathin semiconductor transistor with a programmable DNA “reaction network” placed on the sensor surface. When a target molecule is present, it triggers a chain reaction in which designed DNA strands self-assemble into a large, branched structure (a dendrimer). Because this growth is exponential, a single target can be converted into a much larger electrical signal that is easy to measure on the chip. Using this strategy, we achieved detection down to aM levels within 20 minutes, compared with the ~15 hours typically required by earlier linear amplification approaches. This platform provides a practical route toward fast, affordable, and accurate point-of-care testing in clinics and resource-limited settings.

14207721.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14207721.value: The long-expected arrival of quantum computational devices in the near future will create unprecedented challenges for cryptography. While existing proposals for post-quantum cryptosystems will probably mitigate the worst dangers, the development of a secure infrastructure against robust but realistic models of quantum adversaries is likely to take center stage in the coming decade. In addition to the use of powerful primitives, modern cryptography relies on an elaborate web of reductions to achieve complex secure functionalities. The aim of this project is to develop and analyze post-quantum variants of common cryptographic reductions. As realistic quantum adversaries in the near to medium future are unlikely to have universal quantum computing power, a key component is the study of bounded quantum devices in the cryptographic context. As a starting point we plan to investigate the following three questions: (1) the classical simulation of quantum distinguishers of bounded query complexity; (2) the power of non-adaptive quantum distinguishers for distributions arising in the analysis of pseudorandom functions; and (3) the pseudorandomness of small-biased distributions against bounded quantum adversaries. 量子計算設備的面世長久以來備受期待，而其可能在不久將來的出現則將為密碼學帶來前所未有的挑戰。雖然現有後量子加密系統的方案相信能減輕在最壞情況下的危險，但針對穩健而現實的量子對手模型的安全基礎建設將很可能成為未來十年內的中心研發目標。 除了使用強大的密碼學原語之外，現代密碼學還依賴一連串精密的歸約法來達成複雜的安全功能。這個研究項目之目的為開發和分析常見密碼歸約法的後量子變體。由於在短至中期的未來中，現實的量子對手不太可能擁有通用的量子計算能力，此項目一個關鍵部分正是有關密碼學環境中有界量子設備的研究。 作為起點，我們計劃研究以下三個問題：（1）有界查詢複雜度的量子判別器的經典模擬； (2) 非自適應量子判別器應對偽隨機函數分析中所出現之分佈的能力； (3) 針對有界量子對手的小偏置分佈的偽隨機性。

14208021.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14208021.value: Continuous scaling of the VLSI system leaves a great challenge on manufacturing, thus optical proximity correction (OPC) is widely applied in conventional design flow for manufacturability optimization. A traditional way to conduct OPC is by leveraging a lithography model but this method may suffer from heavy computational burden. Worse more, most of these methods focus on optimizing a single clip locally instead of addressing the full-chip scale optimization problems. To mitigate these difficulties, we propose DeepMO, a deep learning-enabled OPC framework with high performance and scalability for full-chip scale. DeepMO is an end-to-end mask optimization framework, where the key components are a deep lithography simulator (DLS) focusing on lithography modeling and a deep mask generator (DMG) to perform mask generation. We will particularly research on three major challenges that include (1) handling large scale design; (2) reliability improvement; and (3) layout representation enhancement. We will partner with several overseas semiconductor companies (nVIDIA, Cadence) and mainland leading EDA and circuit design companies (Huawei HiSilicon, UMEC, SMIT) on this topic. The academia-industry collaboration promises innovative and high-risk academic research coupled with realistic industry data/benchmarks, and timely technology transfer through the companies can benefit the 300 billion semiconductors and equipment industry. The project will also contribute to the education plan, including curriculum development, undergraduate/graduate student training, and research mentoring. VLSI系統的連續縮放給製造帶來了巨大挑戰，因此光學鄰近校正（OPC）被廣泛應用於傳統設計流程中以優化可製造性。進行 OPC 的傳統方法是利用光刻模型，但這種方法可能會承受沉重的計算負擔。更糟糕的是，這些方法中的大多數都專注於在本地優化單個剪輯，而不是解決全芯片規模的優化問題。 為了緩解這些困難，我們提出了 DeepMO，這是一種支持深度學習的 OPC 框架，具有高性能和全芯片規模的可擴展性。 DeepMO 是一個端到端的掩膜版優化框架，其中的關鍵組件是一個專注於光刻建模的深度光刻模擬器 (DLS) 和一個執行生成的深度掩膜版生成器 (DMG)。我們將特別研究三大挑戰，包括（1）處理大規模設計； (2)可靠性改進； (3) 佈局表示增強。

14208021.label: Realisation of objectives
14208021.value: This document outlines how and to what extent the project objectives have been achieved through our comprehensive research and analysis work on mask optimization techniques in electronic design automation (EDA). Through our research work, we have thoroughly investigated deep learning integration into high-performance mask optimization, developed strategies for ensuring high-quality massive mask optimization, identified approaches to addressing major challenges in current solutions, and studied systematic CAD algorithms and tools for next-generation chip design. Through our research work, we have achieved the first objective of studying how deep learning can be integrated into high-performance mask optimization problems in EDA. We completed comprehensive analysis revealing multiple successful integration strategies. We investigated neural network-based methods employing transformer-based multibranch neural networks to replace discrete pixel-based masks with implicit level set representations, enabling end-to-end mask optimization with GPU acceleration achieving runtime performance around one second. We studied reinforcement learning approaches directly applicable to mask optimization without relying on differentiable proxies, addressing fundamental limitations of discriminative and generative learning models. We analyzed learning-to-optimize frameworks where iterative ILT optimization algorithms are unrolled into learnable neural networks with high interpretability, generating high-quality initial masks for fast refinement. We explored physics-informed machine learning approaches where optical kernel regression disassembles rigorous lithographic models into non-parametric mask operations and learned optical kernels. These approaches demonstrate remarkable efficiency, using only 31% of parameters while achieving 69 times smaller mean squared error compared to conventional methods with superior generalization capability. We investigated generative model integrations enabling co-evolution of layout pattern generation and learning-based OPC methods, achieving significant enhancements in OPC performance and pattern legalization. In open-source platforms, we studied modular frameworks integrating various ILT components with PyTorch interfaces, supporting rapid development and evaluation of GPU-accelerated and AI-driven ILT methods. We examined differentiable lithography frameworks built on differentiable programming toolkits with GPU acceleration, enabling large-scale layout simulation while supporting both Abbe and Hopkins imaging models. Through this research, we established understanding that deep learning can significantly enhance mask optimization through neural network initialization, physics-informed constraints, reinforcement learning, and differentiable simulation frameworks, showing substantial improvements in solution quality and computational efficiency. For the second objective, we completed work on learning how to ensure high-quality massive mask optimization using dedicated deep learning flows and algorithms. We conducted comprehensive analysis of strategies addressing challenges of scaling mask optimization to full-chip designs. We investigated full-chip scale optimization approaches employing multi-level partitioning strategies with divide-and-conquer methodologies, workload distribution frameworks with scalable multi-GPU parallelism, and gradient-fusion techniques with multi-level healing strategies to fix boundary errors. We studied multigrid-Schwarz methods overcoming challenges in tile assembly for large-scale layouts, achieving comparable performance to full-chip ILT while offering increased parallelizability and alleviating tile stitching discontinuities. We identified computational efficiency strategies including multi-level resolution methods employing downsampling strategies, achieving significant reductions in L2 loss and PVBand compared to state-of-the-art methods. We analyzed GPU-accelerated frameworks using level-set methods with momentum-based evolution techniques and self-adaptive conjugate gradient methods, achieving high optimization quality and fast convergence. We completed study of quality assurance mechanisms including process window-aware optimization employing cost functions suppressing disturbance from condition fluctuations, ensuring robust mask quality under process variations. We investigated adaptive optimization frameworks leveraging pattern distribution and repetition properties, adaptively selecting suitable OPC solvers and enabling reuse of optimized masks through graph-based dynamic pattern libraries. We analyzed manufacturing-aware optimization methods integrating circular E-beam mask writer constraints directly into the optimization process, ensuring optimized masks remain manufacturable. Through this work, we established understanding that high-quality massive mask optimization requires hierarchical approaches combining full-chip partitioning, GPU acceleration, adaptive solver selection, and manufacturing-aware constraints, addressing scalability, quality, and manufacturability simultaneously. The third objective focused on studying how to tackle major challenges of state-of-the-art mask optimization solutions. We achieved this objective through detailed analysis identifying solutions to seven major challenges. We investigated computational overhead and runtime efficiency challenges, analyzing acceleration strategies including GPU-accelerated lithography simulators, multi-level simulation frameworks, and learning-to-optimize methods. Discrete diffusion models for source mask optimization demonstrate over 200 times higher throughput compared to traditional methods. We studied boundary errors in partitioned designs, analyzing gradient-fusion techniques and multi-level healing strategies addressing tile stitching discontinuities. We investigated poor generalization capability challenges through physics-informed approaches incorporating domain knowledge into neural networks, demonstrating superior generalization using small-scale training datasets. We completed analysis of manufacturing constraints integration challenges, studying methods integrating circular E-beam mask writer constraints directly into ILT processes. We investigated manual parameter tuning challenges through transformer-based neural networks with parameter selectors and rule learning systems automatically extracting and optimizing rule parameters. We studied limited scalability challenges through multi-level partitioning strategies, workload distribution frameworks, and multigrid-Schwarz methods enabling full-chip optimization. We completed investigation of source-mask co-optimization complexity challenges through GPU-accelerated simulators based on Abbe's theory enabling concurrent source and mask optimization. Through this work, we established understanding of solutions addressing computational efficiency, scalability, manufacturability, generalization, and automation challenges. For the fourth objective, we completed work on developing understanding of systematic CAD algorithms and tools for next-generation chip design under advanced technology nodes. We conducted comprehensive research into systematic frameworks, open-source tools, and industrial application methods. We studied systematic algorithm frameworks analyzing mask optimization systems for SRAF generation and model-based OPC learning from information-augmented ILT engines, demonstrating systematic rule learning applicable across different complex design patterns. We completed analysis of adaptive OPC frameworks adaptively selecting solvers based on pattern complexity while leveraging pattern distribution and repetition properties, and graph-based dynamic pattern libraries enabling systematic reuse of optimized solutions. We analyzed modular frameworks integrating lithography simulation, objective functions, and evaluation metrics, offering PyTorch interfaces for systematic development of GPU-accelerated and AI-driven methods. We studied differentiable lithography simulation engines with comprehensive APIs, systematically designed for large-scale layout simulation supporting both Abbe and Hopkins models. We investigated algorithm design principles including level-set based methods with process window-aware cost functions and self-adaptive conjugate gradient methods, multigrid methods addressing tile assembly challenges, and diffusion-based optimization enabling concurrent source and mask optimization. We studied practical full-chip ILT flows addressing industrial bottlenecks with multi-level partitioning, workload distribution, and boundary healing, validated on real design layers. We completed analysis of manufacturing-aware algorithms systematically integrating manufacturing constraints into optimization algorithms, ensuring practical applicability. Through this research, we established understanding of systematic algorithms and tools integrating deep learning, GPU acceleration, manufacturing constraints, and scalability considerations into unified frameworks suitable for advanced technology nodes. In summary, we have fully achieved all four objectives through our comprehensive research and analysis work. Our research demonstrates successful understanding of how deep learning can be integrated into EDA mask optimization, providing scalable, high-quality solutions addressing real industrial challenges while maintaining manufacturing feasibility. We have gained knowledge of multiple integration strategies including neural networks, reinforcement learning, physics-informed methods, and generative models. We have completed comprehensive study of full-chip optimization strategies, computational efficiency methods, and quality assurance mechanisms. We have identified and analyzed solutions to major challenges including computational overhead, boundary errors, generalization, manufacturability, scalability, and automation. We have completed thorough investigation of systematic algorithm frameworks, open-source tools, and industrial application methods for next-generation chip design. No underachievements were encountered, as all objectives were fully met through our comprehensive literature analysis and systematic study work, establishing a solid foundation for understanding and advancing mask optimization techniques in advanced semiconductor manufacturing.

14208021.label: Major findings and research outcome
14208021.value: Through our comprehensive research work on mask optimization techniques in electronic design automation, we have identified several key findings and achieved significant research outcomes. First, we discovered that deep learning integration can significantly enhance mask optimization performance through multiple approaches. Physics-informed machine learning methods (DAC23-Nitho) achieve remarkable efficiency using only 31% of parameters while achieving 69 times smaller mean squared error with superior generalization capability compared to conventional approaches. Reinforcement learning models (TCAD24-RL-OPC) enable direct optimization of preferred objectives without relying on differentiable proxies, addressing fundamental limitations of traditional methods. Neural network-based approaches employing transformer architectures (TCAD23-DevelSet) can achieve runtime performance around one second while outperforming state-of-the-art methods in printability. Second, we found that full-chip scale optimization requires hierarchical approaches combining multiple strategies. Multi-level partitioning with divide-and-conquer methodologies and gradient-fusion techniques (ISPD24-FuILT) effectively address boundary errors in partitioned designs. Multigrid-Schwarz methods (DAC24-MS-ILT) overcome tile assembly challenges, achieving comparable performance to full-chip ILT while offering increased parallelizability. Multi-level resolution methods (DAC23-Efficient ILT) achieve at least 33.8% reduction in L2 loss and 15.5% reduction in PVBand compared to state-of-the-art methods. Third, we identified that manufacturing constraints must be integrated directly into optimization processes. Circular fracturing-aware ILT methods (DAC24-CircleOPC) integrate E-beam mask writer constraints into the optimization process, ensuring optimized masks remain manufacturable while maintaining quality. Adaptive optimization frameworks (DAC24-EMOGen, TCAD24-AdaOPC2.0) leveraging pattern distribution enable reuse of optimized masks through dynamic pattern libraries, achieving up to 39% enhancement in OPC performance. Fourth, we established that systematic CAD tools and open-source platforms are essential for advancing the field. Open-source platforms (ASICON23-OpenILT, ASICON25-TorchLitho 2.0) provide modular frameworks with PyTorch interfaces supporting rapid development of GPU-accelerated and AI-driven ILT methods. Differentiable lithography frameworks enable large-scale layout simulation while supporting both Abbe and Hopkins imaging models. Rule learning systems (TCAD25-RuleLearner) automatically extract and optimize rule parameters, eliminating manual parameter tuning requirements. Our research outcomes demonstrate that integrating deep learning, GPU acceleration, manufacturing constraints, and scalability considerations into unified frameworks can provide comprehensive solutions to next-generation chip design challenges, successfully addressing computational efficiency, scalability, manufacturability, generalization, and automation simultaneously.

14208021.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14208021.value: First, we can extend the integration of advanced machine learning techniques, particularly exploring transformer-based architectures for complex pattern recognition and optimization. Second, there is significant potential to enhance full-chip scalability by developing sophisticated distributed computing frameworks that can handle increasingly large designs efficiently. Third, we should investigate the integration of emerging manufacturing technologies, such as EUV lithography constraints and novel mask writing techniques, to ensure our optimization methods remain aligned with industry capabilities. Fourth, developing robust physics-informed models that incorporate real-world process variations and uncertainty quantification would significantly improve practical applicability. The proposed course of action includes: (1) implementing and validating optimization strategies in real industrial design flows; (2) developing standardized benchmarking frameworks to evaluate different approaches objectively; (3) establishing collaborative partnerships with industry to ensure research outcomes address practical needs; (4) creating comprehensive open-source toolchains that integrate multiple optimization techniques; and (5) conducting systematic studies on trade-offs between optimization quality, computational cost, and manufacturing feasibility. These actions will help bridge the gap between academic research and industrial deployment, advancing the state-of-the-art in mask optimization for next-generation chip design.

14208021.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14208021.value: When making computer chips, engineers create tiny patterns on silicon wafers using light. However, these patterns often become distorted during manufacturing, like a blurred photo. Engineers use masks similar to stencils to create correct patterns. Our research improves how these masks are designed using artificial intelligence and advanced computer algorithms. Instead of manually adjusting mask designs through trial and error, we use intelligent computer systems that automatically find the best mask pattern. These systems use techniques similar to image recognition, applied specifically to chip manufacturing. This project can make chip manufacturing faster, more accurate, and less expensive. As chips become smaller and more complex, traditional methods struggle. Our research shows that artificial intelligence can solve these challenges efficiently, reducing mask design time while improving chip quality. Better chip manufacturing means more powerful computers, smartphones, and devices we use daily. It helps semiconductor companies reduce costs and improve production, making advanced technology more accessible to everyone.

14208221.label: Project Objectives
14208221.value: To study theoretically and experimentally the cavity-enhanced stimulated Raman scattering (SRS) effect with sensitive photoacoustic detection of hydrogen gas. We propose to design a high-finesse (> 6000) Fabry-Perot cavity for the power build-up of the pump laser at 1581 nm. The Stokes laser at 1742 nm is made collinear with the pump laser and transmitted through the optical cavity with a high transmission (> 95%). A longitudinal resonant photoacoustic cell (8 cm long) is designed and placed inside the optical cavity for acoustic detection. We will investigate the linear response, dynamic range, minimum detection limit, and long-term stability for hydrogen detection. We will also exploit the influence of gas pressure and polarization of the Stokes light on the photoacoustic Raman signal. To develop a compact photoacoustic SRS hydrogen sensor using a miniaturized cavity and a quartz tuning fork (QTF). We propose to implement a custom-made QTF with a resonant frequency of 7.2 kHz for acoustic detection. Such a tiny QTF is placed at the center of the miniaturized optical cavity of 2 cm in length. 14208421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14208421.value: This proposal aims to develop an anti-PT-symmetric system on an integrated photonic platform for investigation of anti-PT-symmetric optics at the nanoscale. The development of quantum mechanics is one of the most significant achievements in the 20th century. A fundamental assumption in quantum mechanics states that a system’s Hamiltonian must be Hermitian to obtain a real energy spectrum and ensure the probability conservation. This condition, however, is sufficient but not necessary. Actually, Bender and Boettcher discovered in 1998 that a class of non-Hermitian Hamiltonians can also have real energy spectra under certain conditions, as long as they possess the so-called “parity‒time (PT) symmetry.” This remarkable finding not only has extended quantum mechanics from the real into the complex domain, but also has revolutionized many other branches of classical physics. Experimental and theoretical advancement in PT-symmetric optics has enabled novel methods of manipulation and confinement of optical waves. However, building a PT-symmetric optical system is sometimes challenging due to the difficulty in local control of the optical gain. Therefore, another type of non-Hermitian systems, the anti-PT symmetric systems, have been proposed. To date, experimental studies on anti-PT symmetry have progressed slowly. Due to its versatile applications in communication and signal processing, an anti-PT symmetric system on the integrated photonic platform is highly desirable and remains to be developed. We will study anti-PT symmetric optics at the nanoscale on an integrated photonic platform. We will fabricate an optical cavity consisting of suspended waveguides on a silicon chip. We will first explore the cavity-enhanced four-wave mixing effect in the optical cavity. With the aid of Brillouin scattering, we will harness the four-wave mixing effect to control the dissipative coupling between two Stokes light signals at different frequencies. By varying the ratio between the coupling strength and the frequency difference, we expect to observe the anti-PT-symmetry-related phenomena in such an optical system. By exploring interesting physics in a completely new domain, this proposal has far-reaching significance for both fundamental research and engineering applications. Fundamentally, the experimental results of this proposal will be used to test and verify the anti-PT theories. New experimental results that are not supported by the existing theories may stimulate further theoretical development. Technology-wise, better understanding of the physics of anti-PT symmetry on an integrated photonic platform will lead to unprecedented engineering applications on a chip, such as ultrahigh-sensitivity sensors, mode switchers, and highly efficient Brillouin lasers and amplifiers. 該提案旨在開發一個集成光子學平台上的反PT對稱系統，用於研究納米尺度的反PT對稱光學。 量子力學的發展是二十世紀最重要的成就之一。量子力學裏的一個基本假設指出，系統的哈密頓量必須是厄米的才能獲得實能譜並確保概率守恆。然而，該條件是充分但非必要的。事實上，Bender和Boettcher在1998年發現了一類非厄米哈密頓量，只要它們具備所謂的奇偶時間（PT）對稱性，在一定條件下也可以有實能譜。這一非凡的發現不僅將量子力學從實領域拓展到復領域，而且還徹底改變了經典物理學的許多其它分支。 PT對稱光學的實驗和理論進展開闢了操縱和限制光波的新方法。然而，由於局部控制光學增益非常困難，構建PT對稱光學系統有時仍具挑戰性。因此，人們提出了另一種類型的非厄米系統，即反PT對稱系統。迄今為止，關於反PT對稱性的實驗研究進展緩慢。由於其在通信和信號處理中的多功能應用，集成光子學平台上的反PT對稱系統受到高度需求並有待開發。 我們將在集成光子學平台上研究納米尺度的反PT對稱光學。我們將在硅芯片上製作一個由懸空波導構建的光學腔，探索光腔中的腔增強四波混頻效應。藉助Brillouin散射，我們將利用四波混頻效應來控制兩個不同頻率的Stokes光信號之間的耗散耦合。通過改變耦合強度和頻率差的比值，我們期待在此光學系統中觀察到與反PT對稱相關的現象。 通過在一個全新的領域探索有趣的物理學，該提議對基礎研究和工程應用都具有深遠的意義。對於基礎研究，該提案的實驗結果將用於測試和驗證反PT理論。現有理論不支持的新實驗結果可能會促進理論的進一步發展。在技術方面，更好地理解集成光子學平台上反PT對稱物理學將導致芯片上前所未有的工程應用，例如超高靈敏度傳感器、模式切換器和高效Brillouin激光器和放大器。

14208521.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14208521.value: In this information age, graph processing plays a critical role to analyse and extract valuable information from massive datasets for a wide range of applications. As graphs continue to grow to have billions of vertices and hundreds of billions of edges, external graph processing serves as a low-cost and scalable option for processing large-scale graphs on a single machine by offloading the huge graph data from main memory into external storage. On the other hand, the emerging flash-memory based solid-state drives (SSDs) have begun to offer several promising features, such as extreme-high bandwidth, ultra-low latency, and memory-like byte-accessibility, so as to satisfy different performance requirements of various applications. Thus, not surprisingly, SSDs have become the most widely employed data storage for high-performance and data-intensive applications, including external graph processing. Nevertheless, as graph algorithms are exploring the irregularly-structured vertices and edges, intensive random accesses to graph data are often introduced and largely deteriorate the efficiency of external graph processing, since most external storage, including SSD, commonly suffers poor performance of random I/O. More seriously, these random accesses to external graph data are usually small (in the granularity of few bytes), whereas the conventional block I/O only allows transferring data in the unit of block (which is usually of 512 bytes). Based on our investigation, such a huge mismatch between the granularities of graph data access and block I/O not only leads to the problem of low I/O efficiency but even makes the superior performance of emerging SSDs underutilized. Thus, this research aims to build an I/O-efficient external graph processing framework by making the best use of emerging SSDs. Specifically, this research will, for the first time, leverage the dual block-accessibility and byte-accessibility of emerging SSDs to improve the I/O efficiency and performance of graph data accesses. This research will also exploit the observed power-law edge distribution behind large-scale graphs to effectively absorb a large portion of random vertex updates in a small area of the application-visible SSD-internal DRAM for performance and endurance enhancements. To realize and evaluate the proposed designs, this research will develop a cross-layer framework that can facilitate the uses of dual I/O data paths and application-visible SSD-internal DRAM for graph algorithm/system developers. This project is particularly important for Hong Kong, since the success of this research will benefit all possible service users/providers (ranging from end-user, enterprises, to government units) by presenting an I/O-efficient external graph processing framework. 隨著資訊爆炸的時代來臨，圖處理對於分析大量數據的眾多應用與系統而言，已成為了不可或缺的角色。傳統的圖處理需要將整個圖數據載入記憶體內以進行高效率運算。然而，隨著圖持續成長至數十億個節點和數千億條邊，容納整個圖數據將需要巨量的記憶體。相較之下，外部圖處理將整個圖數據留在外部存儲，並只載入需要的數據到記憶體中進行運算。換言之，外部圖處理成為了一個不僅低成本且具可擴展性的解決方案。另一方面，新興的固態硬碟已開始提供更佳的功能以滿足各式各樣的應用需求，比如超高頻寬、超低延遲、字節可訪問性等等。由於這些優勢，固態硬碟已被廣泛地使用在各類高效數據存儲應用，而外部圖處理便是其中一種應用。 然而，因為現實中的圖數據大多具有不規則結構，圖算法在探索的過程中經常造成了大量的隨機訪問。一般來說，外部存儲（包括固態硬碟）多半無法有效率地處理隨機訪問。對於圖處理所造成的隨機訪問，情況將更為嚴重，因為這些訪問的大小通常只有數個字節；反觀，傳統外部存儲所支持的塊I/O卻只允許以塊為最小單位（通常為512個字節）的傳輸數據。基於我們的觀察，如此巨大的差異不僅導致了過低的I/O效率，甚至連新興固態硬碟的優勢都無法充分發揮。因此，此研究致力於充分利用新興固態硬碟來架構I/O高效率的外部圖處理框架。為了達成此目的，本研究將首次利用新興固態硬碟之雙重可訪問性（塊可訪問性和字節可訪問性）來提升圖處理的I/O效率和性能。為了更進一步提高效能與固態硬碟的壽命，此研究基於現實中圖的冪律分布特性，將固態硬碟內部少量的記憶體用來吸收大部分的節點更新。為了實現與評估所提出的設計，本研究將開發一個跨層框架，讓圖算法/系統之開發人員能更簡易地使用雙重I/O路徑以存取新興固態硬碟內部的存儲區與記憶體區。 此研究將能實現一個I/O高效率的外部圖處理框架，並有益於所有潛在的服務提供者與使用者（個人、企業至政府部門）。因此，此研究對香港的資訊科技發展極為重要。

14208521.label: Realisation of objectives
14208521.value: This project has been going very well. All the objectives stated in this project have been either completely achieved or exceedingly achieved. For Objective 1, we have introduced several new designs that take into account the characteristics of modern SSDs to improve the I/O efficiency and performance of graph data accesses. First, we propose a new graph ordering called I/O-Efficient Graph Ordering (IOE-Order), designed to enhance I/O efficiency and boost the processing performance of graph algorithms based on the Breadth-First Search (BFS) algorithm through the preprocessing of graph data. IOE-Order comprises two major pre-processing steps: the first exploits both graph traversal pattern and degree information to closely store the vertices and edges which are most likely to be accessed together for I/O efficiency improvement, and the second splits the BFDS-ordered graph into multiple sorted bins based on out-degrees of vertices to further increase I/O efficiency and deliver high flexibility in pre-caching vertices. Second, we present Seraph, a fully-external graph computation system that achieves optimal scalability while toward satisfactory efficiency improvement. Inspired by the comparable sequential and random access performance offered by modern storage, Seraph adopts the principle of on-demand processing to access only the necessary graph data for saving I/O and employs a series of practical optimizations, including hybrid format, vertex passing, and selective pre-computation, to achieve further performance improvement. Third, we present Grafu, an external graph system that unleashes the full potential of future value computation while providing synchronous semantics. Grafu incorporates: 1) an elevator execution order to significantly increase the number of future-computed vertices for considerable IO reduction; 2) the conditional barrier to adaptively remove the computational-costly barriers while guaranteeing dependency; and 3) the greedy coloring ordering that re-distributes the edge data to reduce extra memory consumption required by future value computation to a nearly-negligible level. For Objective 2, since there are no publicly available products of dual-interfaced SSD, we have built an SSD prototype that supports not only conventional block I/Os but also byte I/Os through exposing the SSD-internal DRAM as Controller Memory Buffer (CMB). Our SSD prototype is based on Cosmos+ OpenSSD, an open-sourced PCIe-based SSD development platform based on the Xilinx Zynq-7000 SoC. To realize CMB, we 1) added an additional PCIe BAR channel to enable CMB access; 2) directed PCIe commands specified by CMB to the memory access controller; 3) enabled access to DDR memory from the processing system via AXI, and 4) populated the Controller Register in accordance with the NVMe specification. Based on the developed prototype, we have also conducted empirical evaluations to understand the latency and bandwidth of both block I/O and byte I/O as well as their trade-off. The results indicate that the average latency of CMB access is proportional to the request size. For example, an 8 B CMB access has an average latency of around 1 us, while a 16 B access has twice the latency of an 8 B access, at around 2 us. The same trend applies to requests of other sizes. Furthermore, recognizing that in practice, the CMB could be made of non-volatile memory (NVM) instead of volatile memory like DRAM, we have also investigated RaceTrack Memory (RTM), one of the latest, most promising types of NVM. Particularly, we devise a novel mechanism called SMART, which addresses the mismatch between the granularity of RTM access/shift commands and the row-level access patterns to enhance access performance. Its core idea is to simultaneously and proactively march all domain block clusters (DBCs) within a subarray, allowing subsequent accesses to other DBCs to be served without the need for additional shift commands. For Objective 3, we have developed new techniques that can leverage either host-attached or application-visible SSD-internal memory to address the notorious random vertex updates. Particularly, we introduce the out-degree binning technique, which reorders the graph into multiple sorted bins based on the sizes of edge lists (i.e., out-degrees of vertices) and further stores all the bins sequentially as the edge data according to their average out-degrees. This technique not only facilitates the vertex pre-caching (or pinning) but also has the potential to enhance the I/O efficiency for runtime graph processing. This is because the vertices of small out-degree can be physically separated and then efficiently pre-cached, while loading data from other bins can achieve significantly higher I/O efficiency. Moreover, this technique provides high flexibility in pre-caching (or pinning) vertices based on varying memory availability, as edge data can be easily pre-cached starting from the bin with the smallest average out-degree, depending on the available memory in different machines. On the other hand, we further put forward the vertex passing technique, which associates each vertex partition with an in-memory passing buffer to delay and aggregate the vertex updates to the same subgraph. When a vertex attribute is updated but remains in storage, this technique delays the update and transfers the update information to the corresponding passing buffer; once the attributes of the vertex to be updated are loaded into memory, it merges the updates from the passing buffer back into the attributes. For Objective 4, we have utilized the developed SSD prototype to investigate various addressing mapping design in the flash translation layer (FTL), focusing on access performance and SSD-internal DRAM consumption. Our findings confirm that the conventional page-based address mapping delivers the best access performance in nearly all scenarios, but it demands approximately 1/1000 of the DRAM capacity compared to flash memory. In contrast, the emerging zone-based address mapping presents an opportunity to reduce SSD-internal DRAM consumption without sacrificing performance, where a zone can be considered a superblock comprising physical flash blocks from different flash dies; however, it imposes strict sequential access constraints when writing to zones, requiring upper-layer applications to adapt to this interface change. For Objective 5, we have created a cross-layer framework, based on the developed, dual-interfaced SSD prototype, to facilitate the use of dual I/O data paths by various applications or systems. To enable byte-level I/Os, applications need only to map the CMB through Memory-Mapped I/O (MMIO), where each MMIO access can be issued in the unit of 8 bytes, rather than the standard block size, to reduce the read/write amplification, resulting in improved performance. For Objective 6, we have explored a diverse range of graph algorithms and large-scale graph datasets to investigate the trade-off among I/O efficiency, graph processing time, and performance scalability. Specifically, we have studied various types of BFS-like algorithms (including All-Pair Shortest Path, Breadth-First Search, and Weakly Connected Components), centrality and ranking algorithms (including Pagerank and Weighted Pagerank), community detection algorithms (including Label Propagation and K-core), and probabilistic inference algorithms (including Belief Propagation and Dispersion). In addition to these classical algorithms in graph theory domain, we have also examined the advanced graph neural networks (GNN) as well as estimators for All-Distances Sketch (ADS) based graph neighborhood sketching. Furthermore, considering that the open-source graph datasets are generally limited in size, we have generated an ultra-large-scale graph called RMAT, which contains 8.6 billion of vertices and 112 billion of edges, to evaluate the performance scalability of the proposed framework.

Additionally, recognizing that in practice, the exposed Controller Memory Buffer (CMB) could be made of non-volatile memory (NVM) instead of volatile memory like DRAM, we have also investigated RaceTrack Memory (RTM), one of the latest, most promising types of NVM [C2]. For Objective 3, we have developed new techniques that can leverage either host-attached or application-visible SSD-internal memory to address the notorious random vertex updates. Particularly, the out-degree binning technique is introduced to reorder the graph into multiple sorted bins based on the sizes of edge lists (i.e., out-degrees of vertices) and further stores all the bins sequentially as the edge data according to their average out-degrees [C1]. On the other hand, the vertex passing technique is put forward to associate each vertex partition with an in-memory passing buffer to delay and aggregate the vertex updates to the same subgraph [C3]. For Objectives 4 and 5, we have utilized the developed SSD prototype to investigate various addressing mapping design in the flash translation layer (FTL) and create a cross-layer framework to facilitate the use of dual I/O data paths by various applications or systems. For Objective 6, we have explored a diverse range of graph algorithms and large-scale graph datasets to investigate the trade-off among I/O efficiency, graph processing time, and performance scalability. Our investigation includes classical graph algorithms, such as BFS-like algorithms, community detection algorithms, and probabilistic inference algorithms [C1], [C3], [C5], as well as advanced graph neural networks (GNN) [C4] and All-Distances Sketch (ADS) based graph neighborhood sketching [C6].

14208521.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14208521.value: This research project aims to build an I/O-efficient external graph processing framework utilizing modern solid-state drives. While numerous advanced techniques have been introduced, the inherent performance limitations of external graph processing still prevent us from matching the performance of shared-memory graph processing. Recently, with the rise of many AI and/or machine learning (ML) applications, obtaining exact answers through graph analytics is no longer always essential. In light of this, approximate graph processing presents a new avenue for further exploration, allowing a trade-off between accuracy and substantial reductions in execution time. Among the available approximate techniques, graph sketching stands out as a compelling approach. This technique creates compact summaries (i.e., sketches) while preserving key properties of graph datasets so that computations can be efficiently approximated via sketches at runtime, with provable accuracy guarantees. It trades inexpensive storage space for significant computational savings, making it an ideal fit to leverage the advantages while mitigating the disadvantages of external graph processing. Consequently, figuring out how to translate and implement the theoretically sound graph sketching approach within real-world AI/ML system pipelines poses a challenging yet promising opportunity to enhance the scalability and efficiency of external graph processing for further investigation.

14208521.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14208521.value: In this information age, graph processing plays a crucial role to analyse and extract valuable information from massive datasets. As graphs grow to billions of vertices and edges, external graph processing emerges as a low-cost and scalable option for processing large-scale graphs on a single machine by offloading extensive graph data from main memory into external storage. This research identifies a potential mismatch between the granularities of graph data access and block I/O, which can lead to low I/O efficiency and seriously underutilize the superior performance of modern solid-state drives (SSDs). It then develops an I/O-efficient external graph processing framework that leverages the dual block-accessibility and byte-accessibility of modern SSDs, as well as the power-law edge distribution observed in large-scale graphs, to enhance I/O efficiency of graph data accesses for performance and endurance enhancements. Furthermore, extensive evaluations using diverse graph algorithms and large-scale datasets validate the effectiveness of the developed cross-layer framework. The success of this research holds particular significance for Hong Kong, offering substantial commercial value and benefits for service users and providers through the presenting of an I/O-efficient external graph processing framework.

14209421.label: Project Objectives
14209421.value: Develop a digital micromirror device (DMD)-based two-photon lithography (TPL) system integrated with a new dual-comb spectroscopy (DCS) module that allows for multi-focus parallel fabrication and time-resolved in situ spectroscopic study of the photopolymerization process. The DMD-TPL systems can apply up to 10,000 laser foci to perform parallel nanofabrication with a target build rate of 1,000,000 voxel/sec. Synchronize the femtosecond laser amplifier (pump/fabrication beam) with the DCS module, consisting of two passive mutually coherent fiber lasers (probe and local beams), to realize tri-comb spectroscopy for fast time-resolved transient absorption measurements. Investigate the photopolymerization process, e.g., combined two-photon absorption and multi-photon ionization, induced by ultrahigh peak power laser pulses (10 – 100 TW/cm2) and femtosecond oscillators based on the DCS module and custom-designed photoresins. Study different two-photon initiator molecules and based on the findings, generate guidelines for optimization of the photoresin composition to fully exploit the advantages of the ultrahigh peak power lasers (i.e., high printing speed and low laser dosage). Theoretically and experimentally investigate the performance limit of multi-focus writing based on the DMD and binary holography for up to 10,000 foci. Establish a quantitative relationship among the focus quality, number of laser foci, and photoresin compositions. Develop methods and algorithms to optimize the design and generation of binary holograms to improve the positioning accuracy and intensity uniformity for up to 10,000 laser foci. Optimize and fabricate large-scale aspherical lens and optical and mechanical metamaterial structures using 1,000 – 10,000 foci to demonstrate the capability of the DMD-TPL system.

14209421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14209421.value: This proposal aims to realize high-throughput two-photon lithography by generating thousands of programmable laser foci via binary holograms; and to investigate the new photopolymerization kinetics induced by the ultrahigh-peak-power laser system. To achieve the goal, a regenerative laser amplifier will seed a custom-built two-photon fabrication system to perform 3-D nanofabrication; and a new dual-comb spectroscopy (DCS) system will be designed and constructed around the two-photon fabrication system to study the photopolymerization process in situ with high temporal resolution. Two-photon polymerization is an important additive manufacturing method that is typically performed via raster-scanning the focus of a high-repetition rate femtosecond laser in photoresins, thereby inducing a nonlinear absorption process to polymerize submicron features. Although it enables submicron structures to be additively created, the processing rate is limited by the serial scanning procedure. To achieve parallel processing, e.g., multi-focus or light sheet writing, a femtosecond laser amplifier is often adopted; however, the different photopolymerization kinetics involving ultrafast absorption peaks on the scale of hundreds of femtoseconds to picoseconds induced by ultrahigh-peak-power laser pulses has yet to be fully understood, resulting in suboptimal photoresin formulation, laser processing parameters, and fabrication results. To realize and investigate high-throughput two-photon fabrication, we will use a digital micromirror device (DMD), i.e., a programmable binary mask, to generate thousands of individually programmable laser foci to perform 3-D nanofabrication based on binary holography and custom-developed photoresins. During printing, a compact and passive mutually coherent DCS system will be developed to in-situ investigate the kinetics of two-photon absorption (TPA) processes on different classes of photoresins to understand the interplay between TPA and multi-photon ionization during radical generation. In parallel, we will develop models and algorithms to guide the hologram design and to study the discrete sampling errors and intrinsic noises from the DMD. Fabrication experiments based on the DMD-scanner and DCS system will be designed and performed to validate the predicted results, identify the optimal processing parameters, and establish deterministic relationships among the fabrication resolution, number of laser foci, fabrication rate, and photoresin composition. The result of this work will enhance the fundamental understanding of the kinetics of two-photon polymerization as well as the rate and resolution of two-photon lithography via multi-focus fabrication. Specifically, the DMD-scanner presents tremendous advantages for fabricating large-scale complex structures, which will generate impact in the nanomanufacturing industry; the DCS system may find important applications in studying functional materials and structures with ultrahigh resolution and sensitivity. 本項目旨在通過二進制全息圖產生數千個可編程激光焦點來實現高通量雙光子光刻；並研究由超高峰值功率激光系統引起的新光聚合動力學。為實現這一目標，將用再生激光放大器作為定制雙光子製造系統的光源，以執行 3D 納米製造；並且將圍繞雙光子製造系統設計和構建新的雙梳光譜（DCS）系統，以高時間分辨率原位研究光聚合過程。 雙光子聚合是一種重要的增材製造方法，通常通過在光樹脂中逐點掃描高重複頻率飛秒激光的焦點，從而誘導非線性吸收過程以達到亞微米的製造精度。雖然它可以實現亞微米結構的增材製造，但其製造率卻嚴重的受到串行掃描過程的限制。為了實現並行處理，例如利用多焦點或光片寫入，飛秒激光放大器是一個常用的方案；然而，涉及由超高峰值功率激光脈衝引起的數百飛秒到皮秒範圍內超快吸收峰的不同光聚合動力學尚未完全被了解，導致光樹脂配方、激光加工參數和製造結果欠佳。 為了實現和研究高通量雙光子製造，我們將使用數字微鏡器件 (DMD)，即可編程二進制掩模，生成數千個單獨可編程的激光焦點，並基於定制的光樹脂及二進制全息原理來執行3D 納米製造。 在印刷過程中，我們將開發一種緊湊且被動的相互相干 DCS 系統，以原位研究不同類別光樹脂上雙光子吸收 (TPA) 過程的動力學，了解 TPA 與自由基生成過程中多光子電離之間的相互作用。同時，我們將開發模型和算法來指導全息圖設計並研究來自 DMD 的離散採樣誤差和固有噪聲。最後，我們將設計和執行基於 DMD 掃描儀和 DCS 系統的製造實驗，以驗證預測結果，確定最佳加工參數，並建立製造分辨率、激光焦點數量、製造速率和光樹脂組成之間的確定性關係。 這項工作的結果將增強對雙光子聚合動力學以及通過多焦點製造的雙光子光刻的速率和分辨率的基本理解。具體而言，DMD 掃描儀在製造大規模複雜結構方面具有巨大優勢，這將對納米製造行業產生影響； DCS 系統可能會在研究具有超高分辨率和靈敏度的功能材料和結構中找到重要應用。

14209421.label: Major findings and research outcome
14209421.value: In this project, we have successfully developed a multi-focus two-photon lithography (TPL) based on a digital micromirror device (DMD) and binary holography; by quickly switching the designed holograms displayed on the DMD, we can simultaneously control up to 10,000 laser foci, where each laser focus’ position and amplitude can be individually programmed. The holograms containing 1 – 10,000 laser foci are synthesized by superposition, followed by an interactive optimization process, i.e., weighted Gerchberg-Saxton algorithm, to ensure the uniformity and quality of each laser focus and minimize discrete sampling processes. The TPL system is integrated with a dual-comb spectroscopy (DCS) module to monitor the fabrication process in situ as well as to investigate the photopolymerization kinetics. Based on the findings from the DCS module, new photo-initiators and two-photon resins have been selected, developed, and characterized uniquely for the regen laser amplifier that possesses ultrahigh pulse energy (4 mJ). This high energy pulses accordingly enables 10,000 voxels to be simultaneously written with a single laser exposure in 1 ms. We have fabricated an array of different optical components, including large-scale optical gratings, 3D metastructures and aspherical lenses to demonstrate the precision and speed of the new TPL system. (Details of these works can be found in journal papers #1, #2, #5 and conference paper #1 attached in Part C: Research Output.) This project also supports the development of other related laser nanofabrication processes (journal papers #6, #7 and conference paper #2), advanced imaging and spectroscopy methods (journal #4, #8) and pulsed laser systems (journal #3).

14209421.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14209421.value: In this study, a multi-focus TPL system is integrated with a DCS system for investigating the photopolymerization processes; and enhance the quality and resolution of TPL. These results provide a solid foundation to design and engineer new two-photon resins with improved resolution and robustness; new research has been going in this direction. In the meantime, in our new design, instead of using two laser systems; we use a single DCS module, i.e., a single-cavity dual-comb laser system, to perform simultaneous TPL and spectroscopy study, where the first comb performs two-photon printing and the second comb performs real-time spectroscopic study. The measured interferograms are used to monitor the photopolymerization status and part dimension which greatly reduces the equipment cost and improves the reproducibility of TPL. A manuscript based on this result is currently under review in Nature Communications.

14209421.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14209421.value: In this project, we have successfully developed a parallel laser two-photon lithography (TPL) 3D printing system to write complex nanostructures with 90 nm precision. To investigate the photopolymerization process, we developed a dual-comb spectroscopy (DCS) system integrated with the TPL to monitor and study the fabrication process in situ. The findings in the DCS system provide insights and guidance to develop new two-photon resins to improve the printing quality and robustness. To verify the results, we have printed and characterized an array of different optical components, including large-scale optical gratings, 3D metastructures and aspherical lenses. The results confirm the validity of our theory and methods of parallel TPL. The substantially improved printing rate (2M voxels/sec) makes TPL an attractive technology for industrial application instead of an obscure laboratory research tool, generating great impact to the nanotechnology, biotechnology, and advanced manufacturing community.

14209521.label: Project Objectives
14209521.value: Objective 1: Develop a digital micro-mirror device (DMD)-based angle scanning TPM system. The DMD-based TPM system is the basis for further throughput enhancement development. Two imaging configurations in this TPM system will be developed and pushed to achieve their hardware-limited performance, i.e., (i) large FOV configuration: > 300 μm x 300 μm FOV with 1.5 tomograms/second speed (from the high pixel count camera port; camera operated at 72 fps); and (ii) high speed imaging configuration: > 200 tomograms/second speed with > 60 μm x 60 μm FOV (from the high speed camera port; camera operated at 10k fps). The 3D imaging speed is limited by the camera speed as DMDs are much faster (49 illumination angles are used for 3D imaging speed estimation). Objective 2: Explore angle-multiplexing for imaging throughput enhancement. With the patterning flexibilities provided by the DMDs in the designed TPM system, three illumination angle-multiplexing schemes will be explored to further improve the imaging throughput, i.e., (i) simultaneous multiple illumination angle (Sim-MIA) scheme; (ii) sequential multiple illumination angle (Seq-MIA) scheme; and (iii) Seq-MIA + reference modulation (Seq-MIA+Ref-Mod) scheme. The expected throughput enhancement factor from scheme (i) and (ii) is around 4 times (i.e., > 800 tomograms/second in the high speed configuration) and 8 times in scheme (iii), as estimated by the maximum number of angles that can be packed in the Fourier space. Objective 3: Develop comprehensive imaging protocol, evaluate imaging performance, and explore biomedical imaging applications. To enable efficient and optimal imaging operation, we will first develop a comprehensive imaging protocol that mainly includes: (i) optimized illumination pattern designs for each angle multiplexing scheme; (ii) standardized phase retrieval algorithms for processing interferograms from each illumination scheme; and (iii) optimized 3D RI map reconstruction models. Additional efforts will be dedicated to improving computational efficiency and data management. For each imaging mode, we will characterize the spatial and temporal resolution as well as explore the imaging RI contrast using calibration and testing samples. After characterization, we will perform imaging tests on various cell lines and validate them with fluorescence imaging. Throughout the project period, we will work with our collaborators to explore potential biomedical applications.

14209521.value: 在這個項目中，我們將探索在角度掃描斷層掃描相位顯微術(TPM) 中提高成像通量的方法，以期實現其無標記3D成像的性能極限。 顯微鏡技術的進步促進了許多突破性的科學發現。 TPM 作為光學顯微鏡領域的一項最新發明，通過測量3D 折射率 (RI) 分佈圖，能夠以高分辨率和靈敏度對未標記的樣品進行 3D 觀察。它為無標記 3D 成像開闢了新的途徑，例如細胞動力學的長期監測、細胞生長的精確量化和生殖細胞的無創可視化。然而，由成像視場（FOV）和採集時間共同決定的成像通量在當前的 TPM 方法中受到限制（一般FOV 小於 100 μm x 100 μm，而圖像採集時間超過 0.1 秒），從而阻礙了它被用於許多新興的高內涵細胞篩选和成像應用。 為了提高 TPM 成像通量，我們將首先設計並實現多功能照明角度掃描 TPM 系統，其中角度掃描將通過在數字微鏡設備 (DMD) 上顯示全息圖和濾光圖案來實現。借助兩款高性能相機，該 TPM 系統將實現兩種不同的成像模式：(i) 大 FOV 模式：超過 300 μm x 300 μm FOV（1-2 斷層圖像每秒成像速度）； (ii) 高成像速度模式：超過 200 張斷層圖每秒的成像速度（~ 60 μm x 60 μm FOV）。然後，我們將探索在 TPM 系統中照明角度復用和參考光束調製的方法，更有效地利用傅立葉空間，進一步將成像通量提高近一個數量級。實現角度復用後，我們將開發全面的圖像採集、處理和 RI 重建協議，以期實現高效和優化的 3D 成像操作。我們將表徵所開發的TPM 系統的空間分辨率和時間分辨率以及RI的測量靈敏度，同時將通過熒光成像模塊驗證觀察到的生物結構。成像系統開發完成後，我們將開展活細胞成像，並與合作者共同探索生物醫學上的應用。 利用非侵入性、無標記和高通量 3D 成像的優點，我們計劃將推動這種顯微技術在諸多生物醫學研究上的應用，包括(i) 細胞生理學研究（例如神經元網絡動力學和功能）； (ii) 細胞力學特性的測量（例如紅細胞機械參數）； (iii) 癌症診斷（例如無標記/虛擬染色組織病理學）。

14209521.label: Realisation of objectives
14209521.value: Objective 1: Develop a digital micro-mirror device (DMD)-based angle scanning tomographic phase microscopy (TPM) system. To improve the imaging throughput, we worked on designing and building a two DMD-based angle scanning TPM system that can be configured to offer either high imaging speed or a field-of-view (FOV), developing a series of physical models for both 2D and 3D high-resolution object reconstruction, i.e., the 3D refractive index (RI) map, and experimentally demonstrating high-throughput volumetric imaging [J1-3, C1, C2]. By synchronizing a high-speed camera (Fastcam SA-X2, Photron) and high-speed DMDs (DLPLCR65EVM, Texas Instruments), the TPM system achieved volumetric imaging at a speed exceeding 200 tomograms/second with a FOV of ~ 56 × 56 μm^2 and a lateral resolution of ~ 209 nm as experimentally verified on various testing samples, including USAF resolution target, 3D printed cell phantoms, and so on [J3]. To achieve a large FOV, a high pixel count camera (MV-CH210-90YM-M58S-NN, HIKROBOTICS; 222 fps at the full field; 5120 x 4096 pixels) was implemented, which allowed the TPM system to experimentally achieve a FOV > 310 × 248 μm^2 [J10]. Objective 2: Explore angle-multiplexing for imaging throughput enhancement. To further enhance the imaging throughput of the TPM system, we proposed and implemented three illumination angle multiplexing schemes, including: (i) simultaneous multiple illumination angle (Sim-MIA) scheme [J5, C5]; (ii) sequential multiple illumination angle (Seq-MIA) scheme; and (iii) Seq-MIA + reference modulation (Seq-MIA+Ref-Mod) scheme [J6, J9, J10, C1]. To achieve the Sim-MIA scheme, multiplexed Lee hologram patterns were generated and displayed on the first DMD, which provided four oblique illumination beams simultaneously. Four phase maps were retrieved from one interferogram, thus directly enhancing the system’s throughput by a factor of four. The system reached a volumetric imaging speed of > 600 tomograms/second [J6, C1], which is at least one order of magnitude higher than current TPM systems. To achieve the Seq-MIA scheme, four Lee holograms were sequentially displayed within one camera exposure, which enabled retrieving four phase maps from one interferogram. To fully use the spectral domain and address the information overlap issue, we further implemented the reference modulation to Seq-MIA, i.e., the Seq-MIA+Ref-Mod scheme, under the large FOV configuration by adding a second pair of DMDs to the reference arm to shift the locations of the passbands. The realization of simultaneous imaging of interferograms from six illumination angles within a single camera exposure directly increased the imaging speed by 6 times without affecting the FOV, thus greatly improving the imaging throughput of TPM [J10]. In addition, we developed dynamic speckle illumination for a reflection-mode TPM system, similar to simultaneously adding many random illumination angles, which allowed us to achieve spatial gating to realize imaging thick biological specimens, e.g., quantifying the optical properties of cornea inside an ex vivo rat eye [J5, C5]. Moreover, to further enhance the volumetric imaging speed, we developed a deep learning-based 3D RI reconstruction method using a single multiplexed interferogram, which allowed us to achieve an unprecedented volumetric imaging speed of 12,500 tomograms/second with the same high-speed camera [J9]. Objective 3: Develop comprehensive imaging protocol, evaluate imaging performance, and explore biomedical imaging applications. For developing comprehensive imaging protocols and evaluating the imaging performance, we proposed a set of metrics, including contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR), SNR, and structural distinguishability (SD), to quantitatively evaluate the 3D RI tomograms. These metrics allowed us to quantitatively study how experimental conditions inﬂuence the image quality, such as the number of illumination angles (N), RI contrast (∆n) between sample and background, and sample feature size [J3]. We further standardized the TPM reconstruction process and analyzed the relationship between SNR and the number of illumination angles [J4]. Moreover, we optimized the illumination angle to make full use of the camera throughput and interferogram bandwidth [J5, J6, C6]. Finally, with our TPM system we explored a variety of biomedical applications as summarized in the following: (i) Cell classification: By segmenting the cells and extracting a set of 3D morphological and biophysical parameters, i.e., volume, surface area, dry mass, and mean RI, we showed that TPM can distinguish unlabeled cell species of large-scale populations [J7, J8]; (ii) Cell mechanics: We applied TPM for characterizing transient 3D deformations of red blood cells induced by the shearing force in a microfluidic channel on the sub-millisecond scale, which showcased its potential for quantifying cell mechanical properties and monitoring ultra-fast cellular dynamics; (iii) Neuronal-network imaging: We used the large FOV configuration to achieve 3D imaging of nerve cells and axon-like structures, such as refraction fibers related to the formation of migrasome [C2]; (iv) Characterization of chondrocytes: The response of chondrocytes to inflammatory cytokines was characterized by investigating the changes in cell size, production of matrix protein, and motility before and after interleukin1β (IL-1β) treatment [C3]; and (v) Cornea imaging: Collaborating with the Hong Kong Eye Hospital, we performed volumetric imaging of cornea inside an ex vivo rat eye and quantified its optical properties, including the mapping of nanoscale topographic features of Dua’s and Descemet’s membranes [J5]. Additionally, for additive manufacturing applications, we demonstrated our high-speed TPM system can be used for in situ characterization of 3D printed micro-nano structured from two-photon lithography [C7].

14209521.label: Major findings and research outcome
14209521.value: Under the project support, we wrote 10 journal papers with 8 already published in high-profile journals, including Light: Science & Applications (2023), Laser Photonics Reviews (2024), and ACS Photonics (2023), as well as published 7 conference proceedings. Our major findings and research outcome are summarized as follows: (i) We developed a DMD-based TPM system for high-throughput live-cell imaging applications [J2, C2, C4, C7]. Two imaging configurations were developed and optimized to achieve their hardware performance limit; (ii) The angle-multiplexed scheme in combination with a 3D U-Net based reconstruction enabled our TPM system to achieve an unprecedented volumetric imaging throughput of over 12,500 tomograms/second, while providing sufficient morphological information to distinguish different cellular species [J9]. It also allowed for characterization of transient 3D deformations of red blood cells induced by the shearing force in a microfluidic channel on the sub-millisecond scale, thus showcasing its potential for quantifying cell mechanical properties and monitoring ultra-fast cellular dynamics; (iii) we demonstrated the sequential multiple illumination angle with reference modulation (Seq-MIA+Ref-Mod) scheme, which can shift the position of the passbands by the reference beam modulation. This allowed us to increase the imaging speed by 6 times or so while maintaining a large field-of-view and high spatial resolution [J10]; and (iv) we explored many promising applications of our high throughout TPM system, including cell classification, characterizing cell mechanics, neural imaging, characterization of chondrocytes, in situ characterization of 3D printed micro-nano structures, etc. [J5, J7, J8, C2, C3, C7]

14209521.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14209521.value: 1. By introducing wavelength and polarization scanning and multiplexing to the TPM system, it may allow for realizing molecular specificity of certain molecules, which may provide a clear correlation between observed morphological contrast and molecular compositions. 2. Our TPM system could be further combined with advanced fluorescence microscopy modalities to achieve multimodal imaging, thus offering a more comprehensive analysis of living cells. Furthermore, with machine learning we may endow super-resolution imaging capabilities to label-free imaging, including TPM. 3. By further exploring second near-infrared illuminations and coherence-gating in TPM, we may achieve imaging of thick structures for applications in both biomedical imaging and nanometrology in advanced manufacturing as we proposed in a newly approved GRF project (Ref. No. 14202825).

14209521.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14209521.value: As a newly developed 3D optical imaging modality, tomographic phase microscopy (TPM) opens new avenues for label-free 3D imaging of living cells with many important potentially applications, such as long-term monitoring of cell dynamics, quantification of cell growth, classification of subtle cell types, quality control for stem-cell based therapies, etc. However, the imaging throughput of TPM, joined determined by the imaging field of view (FOV) and speed, is limited that has hindered its use in many cutting-edge biomedical imaging applications targeting high-content screening. With the support of this project, we achieved a reconfigurable angle-scanning TPM system that can offer both large imaging FOV of > 310 x 310 μm^2 (one order of magnitude higher than the current state-of-the-art) and a high volumetric imaging speed of 12,500 tomograms/second through both illumination multiplexing and deep learning (3 orders of magnitude higher than the current state-of-the-art). Therefore, this work paves the way for TPM to be widely used for high-content live-cell analysis. To demonstrate such potential, we explored classification of unlabeled cells, characterization of cell mechanics, long-term imaging of chondrocytes, imaging of neuronal networks, etc.

14209621.label: Project Objectives
14209621.value: The first objective of this project is to develop a digital foreground calibration technique to compensate for the path mismatch and clock skew in a passive-N-path-filter (PNPF) based bandpass (BP) Delta Sigma modulators (DSMs). We will also explore applications of the proposed calibration technique in other N-path circuits. The second objective of this project is to develop two new architectures of PNPF-based BP DSMs with time-interleaving. The time-interleaved architectures will enable a high-speed operation of the BP DSMs, and the extra path mismatches and clock skews they bring in can be compensated by the digital calibration technique stated in Objective 1. Analysis and synthesis of the two BP DSM architectures will be conducted. A noise-shaping order higher than two (i.e., a loop filter’s order higher than four) will be constructed for the PNPF-based BP DSMs. The third objective of this project is to design and realize a high-speed PNPF-based BP DSM in a CMOS process. One of the time-interleaved PNPF-based BP DSM architectures will be adopted, depending on the result of the second work. For applications in reconfigurable wireless receivers with direct-IF digitization, the BP DSM will be designed with the following targeted specifications: a bandwidth of up to 20 MHz, a dynamic range over 60 dB, and a tunable intermediate frequency (IF) up to 800 MHz (a system sampling frequency up to 3.2 GHz). This design will expand the bandwidth and the IF of the PNPF-based BP DSM (through the proposed time-interleaving and calibration approaches), and achieve a power efficiency significantly better than state-of-the-art wideband BP DSMs.

14209621.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14209621.value: 帶通 (BP) Delta-Sigma 調製器 (DSM) 是 DSM 家族的重要成員，廣泛用於無線接收器，用於中頻 (IF)信號 的直接數字化。使用 BP DSM，與使用基帶模數轉換器 (ADC) 的傳統方法相比，接收器中的數字化位置更靠近天線，能降低接收器的複雜度，並且容許更多的接收器功能由數字電路來執行，這在先進的CMOS工藝上更有優勢。 過去的三十年來，人們對 BP DSM 進行了大量研究。BP DSM 中的核心模塊諧振器已有各種電路實現，包括有源開關電容器 (SC)電路、有源偽 N 路徑 SC 電路、有源 N 路徑 SC 電路、連續時間 (CT)有源 RC 電路和 CT Gm-LC 電路。儘管近年取得了重大進展，但 BP DSM 的能效仍然是一個需要解決的關鍵問題，因為以上各電路實現方法中的大多數都需要高速閉環放大器，而這些放大器是極耗電的。本團隊最近發表了一種使用無源 N 路徑濾波器 (PNPF) 後接開環放大器來實現諧振器的新方法，展示了基於 2MHz 帶寬基於 PNPF 的 BP DSM，揭示了新方法的可行性、卓越的能效、小面積和可重構性。但是，它有性能瓶頸：時鐘偏差和路徑不匹配。此外，演示的BP DSM帶寬較窄。 本項目旨在：（1）克服基於 PNPF 的 BP DSM 中的時鐘偏差和路徑不匹配挑戰； (2) 開發基於時間交織 PNPF 的寬帶寬 BP DSM 架構； (3)在CMOS技術中實現寬帶低功耗基於PNPF的BP DSM。本項目將研究基於最小均方算法的數字校準方法以校正由時鐘偏移和路徑不匹配引起的失真。校準方法能使我們能夠實現（2）和（3）中的目標，而無需擔心時間交織電路帶來的不匹配和時鐘偏差。 本項目的結果將： (1) 幫助電路設計人員克服其他 N 路徑電路中的時鐘擺幅和路徑不匹配問題； (2) 幫助 ADC 設計人員在 BP DSM 中節省功耗； (3) 為無線接收器設計人員提供新的 IF ADC 選項； (4) 啟發其他研究人員對基於 PNPF 的 BP DSM 進行研究。

14210621.value: 保護多種在開放的互聯網上之關鍵服務，或一般來說，樹立信息傳播之可信度，是一道重要且頻繁出現的研究課題。其共通點在於建立信任。當前的公鑰基礎建設由少數數碼證書機構控制，僅能提供寡頭信任模型。再者，人們只能根據傳播者的身份而不是其他人所擔保的屬性／聲譽決定信息可信度。要求每個人申請並傳播關於他們屬性／聲譽的證書既侵犯私隱，亦難以大規模擴展。 此提案旨在提供在四個典範場景中建立信任的方案，對多個密碼學領域作出貢獻。 1）去中心化的信任網絡：權威機構（受信任的網站／朋友）可以向其他人（其用戶／朋友）發佈基於屬性的密鑰。任何人都可以逐案創建不同解密政策的密文，只有足夠多權威機構均獨立認證為滿足屬性的人才能解密（傳統概念只考慮不相交的屬性域）。為此我們提出去中心化謂語加密及其去中心化謂語隱寫系統的擴展，讓人們秘密地自行拓展他們的信任圈。挑戰包括構建基於配對的短密文密碼系統以配合嚴峻的隱寫容量。 2）匿名聲譽：驗證要求用戶的匿名聲譽憑證具有「良好」分數。在每次通過驗證的對談之後，伺服器可以回溯地增加／減少分數。除「壞」用戶會被列入黑名單外，所有用戶均保持匿名。現有工作採用順序判斷：單個（具爭議／惡意注入的）未經判斷分數的對談會阻止所有用戶進行驗證，從而被阻斷服務(DoS)。我們的目標是無DoS問題及去中心化的設計，即不依賴於任何受信初始設置的密鑰。核心創新點包括具有新驗證語義及分數兌換語義的新憑證設計。 3）保密電子現金：為了去中心化我們的匿名聲譽系統，我們將貨幣視為聲譽並設計一種新型基於賬戶的保密電子現金（它包含了持久的聲譽，而不是基於單次轉賬所餘資金）。針對現時最先進的方案，我們發現能阻礙誠實用戶花費／收款的DoS攻擊。我們提出了一個可持續的謂語交易系統，該系統支持零元空賬的空間回收及高表達力的付費語義的謂語，使其兼容於不同的共識機制。此外，我們加入交易費用機制以作為DoS對策。除了密碼學，安全性還得到理性論證的支持。 4）去中心化匿名聲譽：它建基於2）和3）之上，並有額外的貢獻。通過不同的密碼學技術解決這些看似不同領域中的挑戰，我們的最終目標是去中心化匿名聲譽的「聖杯」概念，將信任從個體的聲譽保持私隱地擴展到他們所擔保的信息。
