14210821.value: 在兩階段分佈魯棒優化中的超模特性

14210821.label: Project Objectives
14210821.value: Investigate how supermodularity can lead to solvability (in polynomial time) in two-stage distributionally robust optimization problems. Intuitively, the property of supermodularity implies that uncertainties are complementary, and hence the worst case distribution is maximally dependent. Therefore, we expect to work on a general class of uncertainty set, allowing the worst-case distribution to be characterized explicitly and efficiently. Consequently, the two-stage problem can be solved for optimality efficiently under the condition that it has the property of supermodularity. Identify a class of two-stage problems that have the property of supermodularity. Unlike convexity, supermodularity is not ubiquitous in all two-stage problems. Nevertheless, supermodularity has clear economic implications, and we believe it is embedded in a substantial class of two-stage operational problems. Therefore, we aim to identify such a class of problems. Specifically, we plan to provide an algorithm that can verify whether any given two-stage problem has the property of supermodularity. Demonstrate the applicability of our solution method. Specifically, we aim to apply our proposed method to classical two-stage operations management problems, which are typically computationally intractable. Examples include multi-item newsvendor problems, appointment scheduling problems, and others. The uncertainties in these problems are intuitively complementary. Hence, the property of supermodularity can be exploited, and therefore our method is applicable. Extend the framework so that our method can contribute to more general problems. For example, we can consider multi-stage problems, some of which also involve complementary uncertainties, allowing our method to be applied. Other possible extensions include a more general information set for uncertainties and two-stage problems that fail to have supermodularity but have related properties. We can also apply our method to real industrial problems to verify its computational efficiency.

14210821.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14210821.value: The two-stage optimization problem is widely applicable and can capture a broad class of practical problems as special cases. However, as it involves a functional optimization in the second stage, the two-stage problem is generally computationally intractable. Therefore, except in very special cases, the typical literature focuses on exploring the structure of various models of uncertainty (e.g., characterizing the uncertainty by an empirical distribution or a moment-based distributional ambiguity set) to construct approaches towards a sub-optimal solution. Unlike these, in this project, we aim to exploit a special structure, supermodularity, embedded in a class of two-stage optimization problems. In particular, we plan to identify a class of two-stage optimization problems, which is with the property of supermodularity. We can then develop efficient methods and solve for optimal solutions within the framework of distributionally robust optimization. Within the setting of some specific distributional ambiguity set, e.g., ambiguity sets with supports, means and mean absolute deviations (MADs), we hope to obtain explicit upper bounds on the expectation of supermodular functions. We will also derive the worst-case distribution, which we believe is of low-dimension, precisely in the robust counterpart. This can make the two-stage distributionally robust optimization problem tractable. Further, we will also provide conditions, ideally both necessary and sufficient, to check whether a given two-stage optimization problem is within this class, i.e., whether it has supermodularity. This is unlike the classical literature since they usually establish the supermodularity property from a parametric maximization problem while, by contrast, we will investigate a parametric minimization problem. With this result, given any two-stage optimization problem which is characterized by the coefficients in the constraints of the second-stage problem, we provide an algorithm to verify whether those coefficients can lead to supermodularity, and hence solvability within our framework. We believe that these conditions are not restrictive and can be met in many practical operational problems, such as the classic multi-product newsvendor, appointment scheduling, and assemble-to-order system problems. While those problems are typically computationally challenging, they can be solved efficiently using our approach. 兩階段優化問題具有廣泛的適用性，可以將大量實際問題作為其特殊情況包括在內進行處理。然而，由於它涉及第二階段的函數優化，兩階段問題通常在計算上難以被有效優化。因此，除了非常特殊的情況外，大部分與此相關的分佈魯棒優化文獻側重於探索各種不確定性模型的結構（例如，通過經驗分佈或基於矩的分佈模糊集來表示不確定性）以構建實現次優解決方案的方法。與這些不同文獻，在這個項目中，我們的目標是利用嵌入在某一類兩階段優化問題中的特殊結構，超模，來簡化計算方法。具體而言，我們計劃確定一類具有超模性質的兩階段優化問題。然後，我們可以開發有效的方法並在分佈魯棒優化的框架內求解最優解。在某些特定分佈模糊集的設置中，例如具有支持、均值和平均絕對偏差 (MAD) 的模糊集，我們希望獲得超模函數期望的明確上限。我們還將推導出最壞情況的分佈，我們認為它是低維的，正是在魯棒的對應項中。這可以使兩階段分佈魯棒優化問題易於處理。此外，在理想情況下，我們還將提供必要和充分的條件，以檢查給定的兩階段優化問題是否屬於此類問題，即它是否具有超模性。這與經典文獻不同，因為它們通常從帶參數最大化問題建立超模屬性，而相比之下，我們將研究帶參數最小化問題。有了這個結果，給定任何以第二階段問題約束中的系數為特徵的兩階段優化問題，我們提供了一種算法來驗證這些系數是否可以導致超模，從而在我們的框架內具有可解性。我們相信這些條件並不是限制性的，在很多實際的操作問題中都可以滿足，比如經典的多產品報童、預約排程和按訂單組裝系統問題。雖然這些問題通常在計算上具有挑戰性，但可以使用我們的方法有效地解決它們。

14210821.label: Realisation of objectives
14210821.value: This project has successfully advanced the theoretical and computational frontiers of distributionally robust optimization (DRO) by leveraging supermodularity to transform intractable two-stage problems into polynomially solvable ones. Below, we summarize how each objective was achieved: 1. Polynomial-Time Solvability via Supermodularity - Established that supermodularity induces maximal dependence in the worst-case distribution, simplifying ambiguity sets to extreme joint distributions (e.g., comonotonic couplings). - Derived closed-form worst-case expectations for supermodular cost functions under moment-based uncertainty sets, reducing two-stage DRO to a low-dimensional linear programming problem. 2. Identification and Verification of Supermodular Problems - Characterized supermodularity in a general class of problems, where uncertainties (e.g., demands) exhibit complementary economic effects. - Designed an algorithm to verify supermodularity in the general second-stage problems, leveraging lattice-like theoretic properties. - Demonstrated that supermodularity arises naturally in problems with substitutable decisions and coordinated uncertainties. 3. Applications to Operations Management - Applied the framework to the multi-item newsvendor problem, appointment scheduling problem, network lot-sizing problems, and so on. - Show computational efficiency and effectiveness of our approach in the above applications. 4. Extensions to General Problems - Generalized the ambiguity set such that our approach can still work. - Apply our framework in other problems, such as various project management problems and inventory problem with uncertain lead times. Specifically, the research output 2 (in Section 8, Part C of this report) contains discussion of all the four objectives above; the research output 1 and 3 are mainly on objective 3. Finally, here I would like to remark that for research outputs 1 and 2, though their initial versions were submitted before the project starting date of 1 July 2021, they both went under a very tedious and time-consuming revision process. In particular, from the published versions of the papers, they were accepted on 17 November 2022 and 18 December 2022. These revisions could not be done without the support of this GRF project, and surely the revisions are driven by the goal of this GRF project. Therefore, I believe they are both publications arising directly from this research project.

14210821.label: Major findings and research outcome
14210821.value: This research has made significant theoretical and computational advances in solving two-stage distributionally robust optimization (DRO) problems by exploiting the mathematical property of supermodularity. The key breakthrough was establishing that when the second-stage cost function exhibits supermodularity with respect to uncertainties, the worst-case distribution in the ambiguity set can be explicitly characterized as having maximally dependent (comonotonic) components. This fundamental insight enabled the development of polynomial-time algorithms for a class of problems that were previously considered computationally intractable. Correspondingly, another major methodological contribution was the creation of verification tools to determine whether a given two-stage problem possesses the supermodularity property, making the framework accessible for practical use. We successfully identified important applications where this property naturally arises, including multi-item newsvendor problems and appointment scheduling, where uncertainties in demand or service times often exhibit complementary effects. For these problems, our approach demonstrated dramatic improvements in computational efficiency compared to generic DRO methods. The research outcomes include: (1) a complete theoretical characterization of tractable cases through supermodularity, (2) efficient solution algorithms with provable performance guarantees, and (3) demonstration of significant computational advantages in several operations management applications. These results were rigorously validated through both theoretical analysis and numerical experiments, showing that our approach can solve problems orders of magnitude faster than conventional methods while maintaining solution quality. The findings open new possibilities for solving complex decision-making problems under uncertainty across various domains, providing both theoretical insights and practical computational tools. This work offers a novel pathway to tractable solutions by leveraging structural properties of problems. The outcomes have been disseminated through top-tier publications and have potential for substantial impact in fields requiring robust decision-making under uncertainty, such as supply chain management, healthcare operations, and financial planning. Future work will focus on extending these principles to broader problem classes and deeper industry collaborations.

14210821.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14210821.value: This research opens several promising avenues for advancement. First, expanding the application scope to new domains—such as energy grid optimization, financial portfolio management, or telecommunication networks—could demonstrate the versatility of supermodularity-based methods in handling complementary uncertainties. Second, industry collaboration would provide critical real-world validation; partnering with retail, healthcare, or logistics firms could refine the framework for practical constraints (e.g., data limitations or real-time decision needs). A key step is developing user-friendly software tools to enable non-experts to deploy the method. Finally, integrating data-driven learning with the supermodularity framework could enhance adaptability to dynamic environments. Proposed actions include: (1) pilot studies with industry partners to test scalability, (2) workshops to translate theoretical insights into sector-specific solutions, and (3) interdisciplinary projects to explore hybrid models (e.g., combining supermodularity with machine learning).

14210821.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14210821.value: This project developed a faster way to solve complex decision-making problems under uncertainty—such as managing inventory or scheduling appointments—by leveraging a mathematical property called supermodularity. This property captures scenarios where uncertainties are interdependent (e.g., demand for complementary products rising together), allowing the worst-case outcomes to be characterized and solved efficiently. We proved that problems with this structure can be optimized in polynomial time, bypassing the heavy computations typically required. To make this practical, we identified real-world problems where supermodularity naturally arises (e.g., multi-item inventory systems) and created tools to verify whether a given problem qualifies. Demonstrations on classic operations challenges—like the newsvendor problem and healthcare scheduling—showed that our approach delivers substantial computational advantages over traditional methods. By linking abstract mathematical insights to concrete applications, this work provides a new pathway to tractable solutions in optimization under uncertainty.

14211121.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14211121.value: 揭秘城市規模 NB-IoT 網絡的性能：系統、測量和優化

14211121.label: Project Objectives
14211121.value: Develop NB-Sense -- the first generic open-source experimental hardware platform for NB-IoT performance study. It can work with a variety of different NB-IoT nodes and enable fine-grained in situ performance measurement and analysis of protocol-level diagnostic traces. Develop a cloud-node collaborative NB-IoT analytics framework, where the NB-Sense node conducts preliminary analysis of diagnostic traces and measurement data based on protocol finite state machine (FSM) while the cloud infers the fine-grained radio access states and the current consumption using a novel graph neural network (GNN) model. Study the energy efficiency of operational NB-IoT networks and optimize the energy consumption by a novel approach that adapts Coverage Enhancement Level (ECL) selection based on reference signal measurement. Conduct the first large-scale measurement study on the performance of mobile NB-IoT networks, including cell (re-)selection efficiency, and exploit mobility to improve packet reception rate and energy efficiency by predicting optimal cell and ECL configuration under dynamic environments. Conduct a large-scale measurement study and validate our systems and algorithms through a large-scale multi-phase field deployment at different locations in Hong Kong.

14211121.value: 窄帶物聯網 (NB-IoT) 是一種主流的低功耗廣域網 (LPWAN) 基礎設施，已在全球部署，並為包括智能電網、停車管理、空氣質量監測和智能農業等物聯網應用提供連接。此外，NB-IoT越來越多地應用於資產追踪等移動場景，可以支持新一代低功耗廣域移動計算應用。然而，迄今為止，由於蜂窩網絡的封閉性、大規模地理分佈、運行期間產生的“大數據”、缺乏可以訪問底層診斷信息並支持大規模測量的有效工具等原因，NB-IoT 的性能和功耗等關鍵指標在很大程度上仍然是個謎，對開發人員和研究人員而言尤其如此。 我們的前期工作對城市規模的 NB-IoT進行了首次測量研究。通過 在3 個城市的 1,200 多個地點部署的 NB-IoT 節點，我們揭示了 NB-IoT 網絡能效方面的一些關鍵問題。利用我們之前的成果，該項目旨在通過以下五個研究任務來揭示和優化大規模運營 NB-IoT 網絡的性能：1) 開發 NB-Sense——第一個通用的開源實驗硬件平台。它可以與各種不同的 NB-IoT 節點配合使用，並支持細粒度的性能測量和協議級診斷跟踪分析。 2) 開發雲節點協同 NB-IoT 分析框架，對診斷軌跡和測量數據進行初步分析。 3) 研究運營 NB-IoT 網絡的能效，並根據信號調整覆蓋增強級別 (ECL) 選擇。 4) 對移動 NB-IoT 網絡的性能進行首次大規模測量研究。 5) 通過大規模多階段現場部署，進行測量研究並驗證提議的系統和算法。該項目的成果將闡明 NB-IoT 網絡城市規模的效率，並提供對未來 NB-IoT 標準、芯片組和網絡運營的關鍵設計方面的重要見解。

14211121.label: Realisation of objectives
14211121.value: Objective 1: Measurement/diagnostic platform for NB-IoT (tooling; trace fusion; module heterogeneity) Realization: We delivered NB-Scope, a layered hardware design (mainboard + interchangeable shields + UE module) to support heterogeneous NB-IoT modules with minimal changes. We delivered software abstraction (unified APIs and decoding) and fine-grained time alignment (trace fusion) between current consumption traces and protocol/diagnostic logs. NB-Scope supports two operation modes: real-time benchmarking (interactive lab diagnosis) and standalone field testing (onboard logging). Objective 2: Cloud-node collaborative analytics + FSM + GNN Realization: We implemented protocol-aware preprocessing and analysis on the NB-Sense node guided by protocol finite state machine (FSM) logic. This provides standardized feature extraction from diagnostic traces and measurement data, and enables scalable deployments by reducing raw-data volume and improving interpretability. We established an end-to-end pipeline for collecting node-side outputs and performing more advanced analytics centrally. Finally, we developed a cooperative edge system for inferring fine-grained radio access states and current consumption via a graph neural network. Objective 3: Study energy efficiency of operational NB-IoT networks and optimize energy consumption by adapting ECL selection based on reference signal measurement Realization: We studied energy-related performance in operational NB-IoT networks using in-situ measurements and protocol-aware analysis. We revealed that ECL outcomes in practice are not purely determined by RSRP; SNR plays a key role as well. Based on field evidence, we derived practical decision boundaries of ECL versus (RSRP, SNR), enabling more informed adaptation of cell/ECL decisions. We developed measurement-driven optimization logic that improves coverage level selection and reduces energy waste by better aligning decisions with reference signal measurements and observed link quality. Objective 4: Large-scale measurement study on performance of (mobile) NB-IoT networks, including cell (re-)selection efficiency; exploit dynamics to improve reliability and energy efficiency by predicting optimal cell and ECL configuration. Realization: We conducted a measurement-driven study of NB-IoT performance under mobility-related dynamics in operational networks, with a particular focus on the efficiency of cell (re-)selection and its implications for reliability (PRR) and energy consumption. The study spanned diverse real-world scenarios and locations, capturing the dynamics experienced by UEs in the field. Our field campaign covered 30 locations and three representative mobile scenarios—riding trains, riding buses, and driving—and involved two NB-IoT modules (Quectel BC35-G and BC28) across two network operators. For each measurement trace, the UE uploaded 20 packets at 30-second intervals and entered PSM after each upload, reflecting a common mobile NB-IoT workload. Our measurements show that UEs effectively rely on cell selection at wake-up and often do not benefit from subsequent cell reselection. Neighbor Cell Measurement (NCM) can dominate eDRX energy consumption (31%–94% of total eDRX energy across scenarios), yet many NCM operations do not lead to reselection, resulting in substantial energy waste. We also observed cell oscillation even for stationary UEs due to unstable EARFCN scoring, leading to suboptimal cell choices and additional energy cost. Moreover, ECL outcomes depend on both RSRP and SNR; selection based on RSRP alone can be misaligned with the experienced ECL. To exploit these findings and improve reliability and energy efficiency under mobility, we proposed a lightweight adaptive cell selection scheme based on history-driven prediction of RSRP/SNR using Simple Exponential Smoothing. Since commercial NB-IoT UE firmware is closed and cannot be modified, we evaluated the approach via trace-driven simulation grounded in real field logs, demonstrating improved selection stability, a more favorable ECL distribution, and reduced estimated power consumption. In addition, we conducted long-duration experiments in which a stationary UE uploaded 1,300 packets over 14 hours per test day, enabling robust evaluation of selection stability and comparisons against reselection behavior. Objective 5: Large-scale in-the-wild validation and measurement coverage We validated NB-Sense and our algorithms through a multi-phase field deployment methodology across diverse real deployment scenarios and locations, demonstrating that the system can operate in the field and that the collected traces are sufficient to reproduce key phenomena and evaluate optimization methods. - Phase A (broad scenario/location coverage): Measurements at 30 locations across five representative NB-IoT application scenarios, involving two operators and two module types; at each location, 20 cyclic packet uploads were conducted. - Phase B (focused evaluation of eDRX/NCM overhead under mobility): For each scenario, we collected log trace from 6 individual campaigns per scenario and uploaded 100 packets per trace when moving NB-IoT nodes across different locations; the occurrence of no-NCM/NCM/NCM-CR was quantified, and the energy cost of eDRX behaviors was measured (eDRX duration set to 10 seconds). - Phase C (long-duration stability study): Over a month, we set stationary UE continuously uploaded packets over 14 hours each day to evaluate long-term selection distribution and stability.

14211121.label: Major findings and research outcome
14211121.value: Major findings: 1. NB-IoT cell (re-)selection is often ineffective for the dominant “single-packet-upon-wakeup” traffic pattern. Our measurement study reveals that when a UE wakes up from PSM to upload only one packet (a common pattern for metering/sensing), the data transmission effectively relies on cell selection at wake-up. Cell reselection, if triggered during the subsequent eDRX, is frequently not utilized before the UE returns to PSM. This explains why tuning/optimizing cell selection is often more impactful than relying on reselection for such workloads. 2. Neighbor Cell Measurement (NCM) can dominate eDRX energy consumption, but often yields limited benefit. We observe that NCM contributes a substantial portion of eDRX energy consumption (reported in our study as 31%–94% across typical scenarios). Meanwhile, many NCM operations do not lead to cell reselection, resulting in energy overhead with little practical performance gain. This creates a clear opportunity for energy savings by carefully configuring/controlling NCM and reselection behaviors. 3. Cell oscillation exists even for stationary UEs, degrading stability and wasting energy. Measurements show that UEs may oscillate among serving cells due to unstable scoring of candidate EARFCNs/cells, even when the device is stationary. Such oscillation increases the chance of selecting suboptimal cells, increases energy consumption (due to repeated procedures and unfavorable coverage levels), and harms reliability. 4. ECL outcomes are not determined by RSRP alone; SNR plays a crucial role and should be included in decision making. Field evidence indicates that ECL selection in operational networks correlates with both RSRP and SNR; RSRP-only decisions can be misaligned with the experienced coverage enhancement level. This finding motivates signal-aware selection strategies and provides an empirical basis to derive decision boundaries for more energy-efficient operation. 5. Lightweight prediction on historical radio measurements can improve practical cell selection under dynamics without modifying proprietary firmware. By leveraging historical RSRP/SNR sequences, a simple time-series predictor (e.g., SES) can stabilize cell selection and improve the resulting ECL distribution, leading to energy savings. 6. Cloud-node collaborative intelligence is feasible when supported by robust edge/cloud coordination mechanisms. We developed a cooperative edge system for inferring fine-grained radio access states and current consumption via a graph neural network for large numbers of distributed NB-IoT devices, and complements the protocol-aware (FSM-based) node-side processing pipeline. Research Outcome 1. A generic NB-IoT experimental platform and a measurement-driven workflow. 2. NB-IoT measurement and optimization results on cell selection/reselection efficiency with and without mobility. 3. Actionable guidance for improving reliability and energy efficiency in real deployments. 4. Enabling capability for cloud-node collaborative analytics via cooperative edge deep learning. 5. Field validation with multi-scenario, multi-location evidence.

14211121.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14211121.value: Building on the delivered NB-Sense/NB-Scope platform, the cloud–node collaborative analytics pipeline, and large-scale in-the-wild measurements in operational NB-IoT networks, future work will: (1) expand longitudinal, cross-operator measurements across more locations, bands, and device modules to characterize how network dynamics impact reliability, cell (re-)selection, and energy consumption; (2) develop deployable optimization methods that require no UE firmware changes, including robust lightweight prediction-based cell/ECL selection using historical RSRP/SNR and application-layer coordination to reduce unnecessary eDRX/NCM overhead; (3) move toward an automated measurement–diagnosis–optimization loop by integrating FSM-guided preprocessing with cloud-side learning to produce interpretable diagnoses and actionable recommendations; and (4) generalize the toolchain to broader cellular IoT settings (e.g., LTE-M and emerging 5G IoT features) to derive more general guidance. We will increase measurement scale and duration, curate reusable datasets/benchmarks, iteratively validate optimization via trace-driven evaluation and targeted field trials, and collaborate with operators and module vendors to translate findings into practical operational guidance and open, reusable tools.

14211121.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14211121.value: Narrowband-IoT (NB-IoT) connects massive numbers of low-power devices such as meters and sensors. However, in real city-scale networks, devices often waste energy and suffer from unstable connectivity due to complicated radio procedures and cell selection behaviors that are hard to observe with existing tools. This project built a practical measurement and analytics system (NB-Sense/NB-Scope) that can collect and align protocol logs with power consumption traces in the field. Using large-scale measurements across diverse locations and scenarios in Hong Kong, we uncovered key inefficiencies: many devices mainly rely on cell selection at wake-up, while neighbor-cell measurements during eDRX can consume a large portion of energy without bringing effective benefits; even stationary devices may oscillate between cells; and the coverage enhancement level is affected not only by signal strength (RSRP) but also by signal quality (SNR). Based on these findings, we developed measurement-driven, cloud-edge collaborative, lightweight optimization methods that improve selection stability and reduce energy waste without modifying proprietary device firmware. The results provide actionable guidance for improving reliability and battery life in real NB-IoT deployments.

14300021.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14300021.value: Representation theory is a branch of modern mathematics that studies abstract algebraic structures by representing them as linear algebraic data. An important topic in representation theory is the theory of total positivity, introduced by Lusztig in 1994. It studies the positive structures coming from linear algebraic data, and these positive structures usually induce some positive structures in geometry. The theory of total positivity also has significant impacts in many other areas in mathematics and physics, including the theory of cluster algebras, higher Teichmuller theory, and the theory of amplituhedron. Recent joint work of the PI with H. Bao from NUS developed the flag varieties over any semifield for any Kac-Moody group. This work generalizes Lusztig's original work on the total positivity to arbitrary semifield and any Kac-Moody group. In this proposal, the PI will focus on the geometric structure of the totally nonnegative flag varieties of any Kac-Moody group. The PI plans to understand the closure relations among the cells in the totally nonnegative flag varieties, and to establish the regularity conjecture of Galashin, Karp and Lam. This will in particular implies that the closure of each cell is homeomorphic to a closed ball. The research combines the methods and results from combinatorial, geometry, topology, and representation theory and will advance our knowledge of these fields' connection. 表示論是現代數學的一個分支，它通過線性代數研究抽象的代數結構。表示論中一個重要的研究方向是由 Lusztig 於 1994 年提出的全正性理論。它研究來自線性代數數據的正結構，這些正結構結構通常會在幾何中引入一些正結構。全正性理論在數學和物理學的許多其他領域也有重大影響，包括從代數理論、高等 Teichmuller 理論和幅面體。 最近我與 新加坡國立大學的鮑教授合作發展了在半域上的卡茨-穆迪群的旗流形的理論。這項工作概括了 Lusztig 在對任意半域和任何卡茨-穆迪群的全正性理論。在這個研究項目中，我將專注於卡茨-穆迪群的旗流形上的全正性的幾何結構。我計劃研究全正性上面的胞腔之間的閉合關係，並試圖證明加拉辛-卡普-林的正則性猜想。這將意味著每個胞腔的閉合同胚於一個閉球。該研究結合了組合、幾何、拓撲和表示理論的方法和結果，並將推進我們的了解這些領域的聯繫。

14300021.label: Realisation of objectives
14300021.value: This project has successfully met its proposed objectives, leading to significant advancements in the understanding of the topology and geometry of totally nonnegative flag varieties. The work has resulted in publication in top journals. The following is a detailed account of the realisation of each objective. Objective 1: Study the closure relation of the cells in the totally nonnegative partial flag varieties for any Kac-Moody group This objective was not only achieved but surpassed. Initially aiming to study the closure relations, our research led to a complete and explicit description of these relations for all Kac-Moody groups. Achievement: We successfully characterized the closure relations between the totally positive cells (also known as Richardson strata) in the totally nonnegative partial flag variety. Our findings confirm that the closure poset (the partially ordered set of cell closures) is isomorphic to the Bruhat poset of the underlying Coxeter group. This means the combinatorial data controlling how these geometric cells fit together is precisely the well-known Bruhat order. Methodology: The key to this result was the development and application of the Birkhoff-Bruhat atlas (addressed in Objective 2). This construction allows us to embed the totally nonnegative flag variety into a product of projective spaces, where the closure relations become more transparent and can be analyzed using classical algebraic geometry techniques. The universality of our atlas method made it applicable to the general Kac-Moody setting. Objective 2: Study the positive structure and the Birkhoff-Bruhat atlas This objective was the central technical innovation of the project and was fully realized. The construction of the Birkhoff-Bruhat atlas provided the foundational framework that enabled the success of the other objectives. Achievement: We constructed a canonical, explicit covering of the totally nonnegative flag variety by open subsets, each of which is isomorphic to a "totally positive space" of a specific type. We named this covering the Birkhoff-Bruhat atlas. Each chart in this atlas is defined in terms of Bruhat decompositions and is equipped with a natural system of positive coordinates, which we explicitly described. Significance: This atlas transformed the study of the global topology of the totally nonnegative flag variety into a tractable problem. It allowed us to "triangulate" the space using these compatible charts, proving that the space is a topological manifold with boundary. The explicit positive coordinates were instrumental in analyzing the closure relations (Objective 1) and were crucial for proving the regularity of the CW complex structure (Objective 3). Objective 3: Study the regularity conjecture of Galashin, Karp and Lam and try to prove that the closure of any cell in the totally nonnegative flag is a regular CW complex This objective represented the pinnacle of the project's ambitions and was successfully achieved. We proved the conjecture in its full generality for the totally nonnegative flag variety of any Kac-Moody group. Achievement: We proved that the decomposition of the totally nonnegative flag variety into its totally positive cells is a regular CW complex, and furthermore, that this complex is homeomorphic to a closed ball. This conclusively resolves the conjecture of Galashin, Karp, and Lam. Methodology and Challenges: The proof required a synthesis of diverse and profound mathematical ideas. The primary challenge was to establish the necessary conditions for a regular CW complex: that the closure of each cell is a closed ball and that its boundary is a union of lower-dimensional cells that are also balls. Our strategy was multi-faceted: We used the Birkhoff-Bruhat atlas to understand the local structure. We leveraged the shellability of the Bruhat order (a result from combinatorial theory) to provide an inductive skeleton. A critical innovation was the introduction of the concept of J-total positivity, which allowed us to study the boundary structure inductively by breaking it down into simpler, lower-dimensional pieces of the same type. The final step invoked the Generalized Poincaré Conjecture (proven by Smale, Freedman, and Perelman) to conclude that a manifold which is a CW complex and a homotopy ball must be a genuine topological ball. In summary, all three project objectives have been not only met but exceeded. The development of the Birkhoff-Bruhat atlas and the concept of J-total positivity were pivotal innovations that allowed us to fully describe the closure relations and prove the regular CW structure, thereby resolving a central conjecture in the field. There were no significant under-achievements in this project.

14300021.label: Major findings and research outcome
14300021.value: This project has successfully resolved a fundamental question in the interface of geometry, algebra, and combinatorics concerning the topology of spaces defined by "total positivity." The central achievement was proving a conjecture of Lusztig, confirming that the totally positive flag variety is indeed homeomorphic to a high-dimensional closed ball. This result establishes a profound bridge between the algebraic concept of positivity and the topological structure of a ball, revealing a deep and previously unknown regularity within these complex mathematical objects. The success of this project hinged on the development of several innovative methodologies, as detailed in Part C. Key among these were: The introduction of the atlas methodology, which provided a novel framework for decomposing and understanding these spaces through overlapping "coordinate charts." The conception of J-total positivity, a refined concept that allowed for a more granular analysis of positivity structures. The discovery of new product structures on totally positive manifolds, which were crucial for inductive arguments. These tools were synergistic with the application of deep results from other fields, including Lusztig's canonical basis theory and the shellability of Coxeter groups. Beyond solving the core problem, this new framework has proven highly fertile. We have applied it to investigate other positive varieties, such as those arising from matroid theory, and have uncovered significant connections to mathematical physics, particularly in the geometry of the amplitude polytope, a object central to modern scattering amplitude computations. The research has resulted in a series of high-impact publications in premier mathematical journals, substantially advancing the frontier of this field.

14300021.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14300021.value: The methodologies developed in this project establish a powerful new paradigm for exploring positivity structures across mathematics. The immediate future research will focus on two fronts: First, we will pursue a breakthrough on the long-standing positivity conjecture for the canonical basis in tensor products. Our novel atlas and product structures provide a fresh, geometric avenue to attack this fundamental problem in representation theory. Second, we plan to systematically expand the scope of our "positivity and topology" program to a broader class of geometric objects, including those from cluster algebras and beyond Lusztig's original setting. We anticipate further cross-disciplinary applications, particularly in deepening the connection between total positivity and the geometry of scattering amplitudes in theoretical physics. The proposed course of action involves continued collaboration with experts in combinatorics and mathematical physics to exploit these emerging links.

14300021.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14300021.value: Imagine looking at a perfectly symmetrical crystal or a snowflake. Mathematicians study such symmetries and their hidden patterns, often using "positive" numbers. This research explored the deep relationship between symmetry and positivity in higher dimensions. We focused on a specific question: what is the fundamental shape of certain special mathematical spaces defined solely by positive relationships? We discovered that these complex, multi-dimensional spaces are, at their core, shaped like a solid ball. This simple and elegant result was unexpected. To prove it, we had to invent new ways of "mapping" these abstract spaces. The significance of this work is twofold: it provides a new toolkit for understanding symmetry across mathematics, and it has already found surprising connections to the laws of physics, potentially offering new insights into the behavior of fundamental particles. In essence, we uncovered a beautiful and universal geometric structure underlying the world of positive symmetry.

14300221.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14300221.value: Gene therapy aims at treating a disease at the genetic level by delivering nucleic acids as therapeutics to patients' cells. Viruses are potent carriers of nucleic acids, but their toxicity hampers clinical translation. Nanoparticles are promising alternatives to viruses because they are less immunogenic and permit easier packaging of nucleic acids. There are three longstanding hurdles to intracellular gene delivery by using nanocarriers. Firstly, some clinically relevant cell types (e.g., stem cells and immune cells) are challenging to be transfected, rendering the development of regenerative and immune-based therapies difficult. Next, nanoparticles often accumulate profusely in acidic organelles (e.g., late endosomes and lysosomes) upon cellular entry, leading to intracellular degradation of gene cargoes and obstructing their delivery to intended cellular destinations (e.g., cytosol for oligonucleotides and nucleus for plasmids). Finally, there is little guarantee over gene release from nanocarriers, calling the efficiency of gene regulation or expression into question. In this proposal, we will address the three bottlenecks of gene delivery by leveraging our recently published gold@polydopamine core-shell plasmonic nanoworms (Au@PDA NWs; Choi CKK et al., ACS Nano, 2019). Our plasmonic nanoworms enter mammalian cells more efficiently than gold nanorods, retain high structural integrity inside the cell without causing significant cytotoxicity, and support dark-field scattering imaging and photothermal ablation of cancer cells. As our preliminary data, we demonstrate the versatility of our nanoworms by loading oligonucleotides and plasmids to their outer PDA shell. Next, we show that these nucleic acid-attached nanoworms enter four different cell types without using transfection agents. These data motivate us to explore the use of nanoworms for delivering nucleic acids to harder-to-transfect cell types. Moreover, given the plasmonic nanoworm core that absorbs near-infrared light, we will investigate the use of light to trigger the intracellular release of the attached nucleic acids from the nanoworms. Importantly, we show that more than half of the delivered oligonucleotides and plasmids reside outside acidic organelles. These data prompt us to evaluate the efficacy of our nanoworms for silencing target genes by delivering antisense oligonucleotides and expressing target genes by delivering plasmids or mRNAs. Our results will offer insights into the interactions of one-dimensionally self-assembled nanostructures with cells, in light of the dearth of nanochains that exemplify abundant cellular entry and intracellular stability. Our data will lay the technological foundation for designing plasmonic bionanomaterials for gene therapy applications. 14300221.label: Realisation of objectives
14300221.value: The three project objectives have been achieved in full. We prepared the gold@polydopamine nanoworm (Au@PDA NW) template core by sonicating citrate-capped 40-nm gold NPs with monomeric dopamine at alkaline pH for 1 h and flipping its surface charge from negative to positive at pH 3. As proof-of-concept, we electrostatically adsorbed non-coding, polythymidine oligonucleotides with 21 Ts (T21) to construct the worm-like nucleic acid nanostructure (Au@PDA@T21 NW). On average, each Au@PDA@T21 NW had 4–5 gold cores, an overall shell of PDA and T21 of 20 nm thick, a length of ~224 nm, a zeta potential of –37.8 mV and 1024 DNA strands; the NW was stable in 10% fetal bovine serum and not toxic on A549 lung epithelial cells, bEnd.3 brain endothelial cells, mouse bone marrow-derived macrophages (BMDMs), or human mesenchymal stromal cells (hMSCs) 24 h post-incubation. For gene delivery to hard-to-transfect cell types in Objective 1, we adsorbed antisense DNA, miRNA, or siRNA onto the Au@PDA NW by the same method as adsorbing T21 DNA. These oligonucleotide-adsorbed NWs had a similar size, surface charge, and DNA/RNA oligonucleotide loading to Au@PDA@T21 NW, were stable in serum, entered bEnd.3 cells, BMDMs, and hMSCs without transfection agents, were not cytotoxic, and escaped endosomes 24 h post-incubation [with a Pearson’s correlation coefficient (PCC)<0.2]. To evaluate the efficacy of gene silencing via NW-aided intracellular delivery of antisense oligonucleotides (Objective 2), we delivered siRNA against Noggin (a negative regulator of osteogenic differentiation) to hMSCs for osteogenic differentiation. We confirmed the endosomal escape of Au@PDA@siNog NW in hMSCs by confocal imaging (PCC=0.117) and transmission electron microscopy. The treatment groups, including free siNog, Au@PDA NW, Au@PDA@siNog NW, and a physical mixture of Lipofectamine 3000 and siNog (Lipo+siNog), lasted for 14 days. Quantitative reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction data suggested that Au@PDA@siNog NW inhibited Noggin and activated osteogenesis-related genes (e.g., bone morphogenetic protein-2, Runt-related transcription factor 2) most effectively. By Alizarin red S staining, we detected most calcium deposits yield by Au@PDA@siNog NW on day 14. As the commercial benchmark, Lipofectamine 3000+siNog modestly led to hMSC differentiation. To evaluate the efficacy of gene expression via nanoworm-aided intracellular delivery of plasmid DNA (pDNA) and mRNA (Objective 3), we pre-coated the NW with lipids (1,2-dioleoyl-3-trimethylammonium-propane, 1,2-distearoyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphocholine) and cholesterol before adsorbing mRNA or pDNA since direct adsorption of them did not yield sufficient mRNA or pDNA loading or protein expression. The Au@PDA@lipid NW had a thicker shell than Au@PDA NW, a hydrodynamic size of 274.5 nm, and a positive charge (+30.5 mV). Upon adsorption with mRNA or pDNA encoding enhanced green fluorescent protein (EGFP) (mEGFP or pEGFP), the resultant Au@PDA@mRNA or Au@PDA@pDNA NW was larger (~280.3 nm) and negatively charged (–35.2 mV). By flow cytometry, we observed Au@PDA@mEGFP NW transfection yielded more EGFG-positive cells than the Au@PDA@pEGFP NW group (90% vs. 79%), so we chose mRNA delivery for following efficacy study. We then leveraged NW to intravenously (i.v.) deliver mRNA encoding hepatocyte growth factor (mHGF) to hepatocytes for reducing acetaminophen (APAP)-induced acute liver injury (ALI) in mice. The Au@PDA@mHGF NW, with similar physicochemical properties as Au@PDA@EGFP NW, had a blood half-life of ~0.65 h and liver uptake of ~39% of the injected dose 24 h post-injection by ICP-MS measurements. By loading Cy5-labeled mHGF to the NW, we showed by confocal imaging its entry to hepatocytes with limited overlap with late endosomes (PCC = 0.202) or lysosomes (PCC = 0.153). TEM imaging of the liver captured NW entrapment in cellular vesicles 5 h post-injection and cytosolic localization 10 h post-injection, proof of endosomal escape. We i.v. injected a single dose of saline, Au@PDA@lipid NW, Au@PDA@mHGF NW, or Lipofectamine 3000+mHGF into mice 24 h post-APAP induction, the time duration needed for ALI to develop. Au@PDA@mHGF NW most effectively elevated HGF expression, reduced necrotic area and apoptotic cells, and restored serum liver function marker levels [alanine transaminase and aspartate aminotransferase] to near normalcy 24 h post-injection, proof of in vivo NW-aided transfection and anti-ALI efficacy. Au@PDA@mHGF NW exhibited no evident toxicity or accumulation in major organs except the liver and spleen 8 months post-injection; >60% of NWs were cleared from the liver and spleen.

14300221.label: Major findings and research outcome
14300221.value: The nanoworm has a worm-like core [gold@polydopamine nanoworm (Au@PDA NW)] and a nucleic acid shell (DNA, miRNA, siRNA, or mRNA). Confocal imaging revealed that most Au@PDA@oligonucleotide NWs escape from late endosomes before reaching lysosomes. For all cell types tested [A549 lung epithelial cells, bEnd.3 brain endothelial cells, primary mouse bone marrow-derived macrophages (BMDMs), and human mesenchymal stromal cells (hMSCs)], Au@PDA@DNA NWs showed limited overlap with acidic vesicles (with a Pearson’s correlation coefficient <0.2). Our first application was antisense gene regulation, where we delivered antisense DNA against EGFP to EGFP-expressing bEnd.3 cells. Au@PDA@asEGFP NW and Lipofectamine reduced the number of EGFP-positive cells by 61.7% and 24.3% relative to untreated cells 72 h post-incubation, respectively. Our second application was macrophage repolarization, where we delivered miR-223 to M1 BMDMs. Au@PDA@miR-223 NW activated M2-related genes and inhibited M1-related genes most effectively. Au@PDA@miR-223 NW yielded intense signals of CD206 and weak signals of CD80, yet Au@PDA NW or free miR-223 showed opposite trends. Lipofectamine+miR-233 modestly triggered repolarization, but less effectively than miR-223-adsorbed NW. Our third application was hMSC differentiation, where we delivered siRNA against Noggin to hMSCs. Au@PDA@siNog NW inhibited Noggin and activated osteogenesis-related genes most effectively and yielded the most calcium deposits. Lipofectamine+siNog modestly led to hMSC differentiation. We leveraged the NW to intravenously deliver mRNA encoding hepatocyte growth factor (mHGF) to hepatocytes for reducing acute liver injury (ALI) in mice. The Au@PDA@mHGF NW had a blood half-life of ~0.65 h and liver uptake of ~39% of the injected dose 24 h post-injection. Confocal imaging verified their entry to hepatocytes with limited overlap with endolysosomes. TEM imaging of the liver captured NW obtained cytosolic localization 10 h post-injection, proof of endosomal escape. We injected a single dose of saline, Au@PDA@lipid NW, Au@PDA@mHGF NW, or Lipofectamine+mHGF into ALI mice. Au@PDA@mHGF NW most effectively elevated HGF expression, reduced necrotic area and apoptotic cells, and restored liver function to near normalcy 24 h post-injection, proof of in vivo transfection and anti-ALI efficacy. Au@PDA@mHGF NW exhibited no evident toxicity or accumulation in major organs except the liver and spleen 8 months post-injection; >60% of NWs were cleared from both organs. Our work was submitted to Science Advances on January 20, 2025. The editor expressed interest in publishing our paper and asked for minor revisions on December 13. We submitted our revisions to the journal on December 14 and are now waiting for the final decision.

14300221.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14300221.value: PI will elevate the translation potential of this nucleic acid nanostructure for gene delivery. In this project, we have revealed that the nanoworm enables the delivery of a wide range of nucleic acids, showing reduced toxicity and enhanced transfection efficiency than the commercial transfection agent Lipofectamine™. These merits suggest significant value of the nanoworm for biotechnology and pharmaceutical industries and biomedical research industries worldwide. We have filed a PCT patent of the nanoworm and plan to commercialize it as transfection agent. Future development will focus on expanding its applications to cutting-edge fields, such as vaccine, tissue engineering, and CRISPR-based gene editing for personalized medicine. We aim to optimize its transfection performance for various cell lines from different origins and species, hard-to-transfect primary cells and stem cells, ensuring broader applicability in research and clinical settings. For in vivo efficacy studies, we hope to improve targeted cell delivery, reduce off-targets effects, and enhance safety of the nanoworm. Lastly, scalable production methods will be critical to meet industrial demands for gene therapy manufacturing.

14300221.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14300221.value: Intracellular gene delivery mediated by nanoparticles forms the basis of important nanomedicine applications. However, endosomal escape of nanoparticles remains inefficient, hampering the therapeutic outcome of gene therapy. This project has expanded our understanding of how nucleic acid nanostructures interact with the biological system at a subcellular level. We have developed a worm-like nucleic acid nanostructure for achieving gene delivery and bypassing the longstanding hurdle of endosomal escape. The nanoworm enables intracellular delivery of diverse gene cargos to multiple cell types and efficiently escape the endosomes. This unique design of nanostructure supports various biomedical applications and offers more effective gene regulation or gene therapy than Lipofectamine, a commercial transfection agent. We have presented in vitro gene regulation (miRNA-enabled primary macrophage polarization and siRNA-enabled mesenchymal stromal cell differentiation), ex vivo mRNA-enabled stromal cell-based therapy for chronic kidney disease, and in vivo mRNA delivery to hepatocytes for reducing liver injury, all with negligible inflammatory response and long-term toxicity. Our work not only propels the field of nucleic acid nanotechnology forward via a new worm-like nanoarchitecture for achieving efficient endosomal escape but also offers a notable vista for designing safe and effective gene therapies based on non-cationic nanoparticle-based gene carriers.

14300621.label: Project Objectives
14300621.value: To synthesize the building blocks of colloidal system, i.e. a core-shell structured nanoparticle which consists of a magnetic Fe3O4 core, an intelligent hydrogel middle layer, and a protective shell. Their physical and chemical properties will be investigated. To investigate the on-demand cargo loading and release capabilities of building blocks. Various functional cargoes including therapeutic drugs and imaging agents will be tested. To understand the physical models of blood, and investigate how the properties of blood, including ionic strength, viscosity, jamming blood cells and biomolecules, will influence the pattern generation, stability, and propulsion of vortex- and ribbon-like microswarms. To design and establish a heterogeneous colloidal system, in which, several subgroups of building blocks are separately specialized with hierarchical functionalities and then perform cooperation between each other to improve tasking efficiency. A cascade reaction mechanism will be implemented as an example. To study the collective behaviors of heterogeneous colloidal system in blood, and investigate the adaptative pattern transformation between vortex- and ribbon-like microswarms. To evaluate the feasibility of heterogeneous colloidal microswarm as a targeted delivery system for localized therapy in a biochip. The cooperative performance between building blocks will be characterized. Blood will be used as the fluidic medium, and the effect of dynamic blood flow will also be studied.

14300621.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14300621.value: 自然界中的生物通過個體之間的局部交流能產生大規模的集群行為，這一獨特且神奇的自然現象在近年來引起了來自不同領域學者的關注。研究者們受此啟發，構建了多種多樣的人工集群系統。這些集群系統由相對簡單的基本模組組成，並且利用它們的集體行為可以實現單個模組所無法完成的複雜任務。值得關注的是，由微/納米尺度的基本模組構建的集群系統在微創醫學領域有著非凡的應用潛力，例如用於靶向藥物遞送、遠端檢測以及毒素降解等。 與宏觀尺度的集群系統不同，微/納米尺度的基本模組上難以裝載電源、感測器以及執行器等裝置，因此需要用不同的方法來構建微/納米集群系統。為了解決這一問題，膠體被廣泛地用於微/納米尺度的集群行為及其基本原理的研究中。迄今為止，多種方法（光、磁場、化學梯度等）已被用於驅動並控制膠體微/納米集群系統（膠體微群）。然而，膠體微群生物醫學應用的實現尚且面臨許多挑戰。例如在實際應用中，集群中的微/納米顆粒往往需要具備各種不同功能來執行多樣化的任務。以靶向治療為例，構建膠體微群的粒子需要能感知並響應其周圍環境，並且在受到物理或化學刺激時能快速進行藥物（或細胞）的攝取及釋放。此外，目前關於膠體微群的研究大多是在水或者人工合成的液體中進行的，與生物醫學領域的實際應用環境相去甚遠。生物流體的複雜組成對膠體微群集體行為的影響尚待進一步研究。 本項目的總體目標是開發可以在生物流體中執行多種任務的異質結構膠體微群，以此解決實際應用中的多功能需求，並且研究生物流體和集群系統之間的相互作用。本項目將從以下三方面開展：（1）功能化磁性納米顆粒的設計、合成和表徵，並將其作為構建膠體微群的基本模組，以實現具體功能的分層與自訂；（2）在水中以及複雜生物流體中對膠體微群集體行為的基本原理進行研究，基於此在流動的生物流體中實現微群的生成、重構以及運動；（3）基於功能化基本模組，設計和開發異質結構膠體微群，使其能在模擬的生物體內環境中完成多項任務並提高任務執行效率。

14300621.label: Realisation of objectives
14300621.value: I. Objective 1: Fully Achieved We successfully synthesized the core–shell structured nanoparticles envisioned by the project objectives using a self-designed four-step fabrication method. Step I involved synthesizing spherical Fe₃O₄ nanoparticles via a solvothermal method, ensuring uniform size and magnetic properties. Step II consisted of in situ polymerization of a polydopamine (PDA) layer on the Fe₃O₄ nanoparticles and subsequent silanization with 3-methacryloxypropyltrimethoxysilane (MPS), resulting in Fe₃O₄@PDA-MPS particles with improved surface reactivity. Step III anchored a thick hydrogel layer through precipitation polymerization of methacrylic acid (MAAc), yielding Fe₃O₄@PDA@PMAAc particles with enhanced drug-loading capability. Step IV deposited a calcium phosphate (CaP) shell on the particle surface by mimicking natural biomineralization, producing Fe₃O₄@PDA@PMAAc@CaP nanoparticles for biocompatibility and controlled release. Comprehensive characterization confirmed successful synthesis. Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) revealed a distinct polymer layer (~26 nm) encapsulating the magnetic core. Energy-dispersive X-ray (EDX) analysis showed Fe concentrated in the core, while Ca and P covered the entire surface, confirming the CaP shell. Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR) identified functional groups associated with PDA and hydrogel layers, while X-ray diffraction (XRD) confirmed the presence of iron oxide and CaHPO₄ phases. Vibrating sample magnetometer (VSM) analysis at 300 K demonstrated paramagnetism with a saturation magnetization of 42 emu·g⁻¹, suitable for magnetic actuation. These results validate the successful preparation of functional nanoparticles, laying the foundation for magnetic swarm assembly and biomedical applications. II. Objective 2: Fully Achieved To validate drug loading and release capabilities, we employed doxorubicin (DOX), a widely used anticancer agent. Hydrogel-coated nanoparticles were immersed in DOX/CaCl₂ solution prior to biomineralization, achieving a loading efficiency of approximately 4.2%. Drug release was pH-responsive: at pH 7.2 (physiological), nanoparticles without CaP released 38.7% of DOX within 12 hours, while those with CaP released only 10.5%, due to adsorption on the shell. At pH 5.5 (tumor-like), release increased to ~77.9%, as acidic conditions dissolved the CaP “gate.” Additional tests across multiple pH values confirmed that acidic environments accelerate drug release. These findings demonstrate that the CaP layer effectively prevents premature leakage under normal conditions while enabling controlled release in tumor environments, a critical feature for targeted chemotherapy. III. Objective 3: Fully Achieved We systematically investigated the effects of ionic strength and viscosity on swarm formation and motion in PBS and glycerol-water solutions. Two swarm types were analyzed: vortex-like and ribbon-like microswarms. Vortex-like swarms could not form under high ionic strength but were insensitive to viscosity, whereas ribbon-like swarms failed under high viscosity but tolerated ionic strength. In simulated blood, we examined the relationship between swarm speed and magnetic field parameters. Increasing pitch angle accelerated both swarm types. At 5°, vortex-like swarms reached 256.1 µm·s⁻¹, while ribbon-like swarms moved at 38.55 µm·s⁻¹. Beyond 5°, ribbon-like swarms lost stability, whereas vortex-like swarms maintained synchronous motion up to 333.5 µm·s⁻¹. These results indicate that vortex-like swarms exhibit superior stability and speed in blood-like environments, providing critical insights for future in vivo navigation and therapeutic delivery. IV. Objective 4: Fully Achieved We achieved customized specialization of building blocks by introducing different functional agents into the synthesized particles. Three distinct types were prepared: Fe₃O₄@PDA@PMAAc@CaP particles loaded with DOX, glucose oxidase (GOx), and Mn²⁺ ions. Under dynamic magnetic fields, these building blocks formed heterogeneous colloidal swarms and achieved synergistic effects through a domino cascade reaction. The mechanism was validated experimentally: acidic pH (4–6) triggered the release of DOX, GOx, and Mn²⁺. DOX initiated chemotherapy, while GOx catalyzed glucose consumption, generating acidic glucono-1,5-lactone and H₂O₂, which inhibited cancer growth and accelerated CaP rupture. Mn²⁺ further converted H₂O₂ into highly toxic hydroxyl radicals (·OH) via a Fenton-like reaction. This multi-step synergy enabled combined therapy—chemotherapy, starvation therapy, and chemodynamic therapy—demonstrating hierarchical intelligence and enhanced therapeutic efficiency. The ability to encode multiple therapeutic functions into swarm components represents a significant advancement in precision medicine. V. Objective 5: Fully Achieved We induced the self-assembly of differently functionalized nanoparticles into heterogeneous microswarms with vortex-like or ribbon-like patterns in blood using rotating and oscillating magnetic fields, respectively. Both swarm types formed and moved in whole blood; viscosity slowed motion, while ionic strength had minimal effect. The two swarm types exhibited distinct adaptations to geometric environments. Vortex-like swarms, with isotropic circular patterns, offered strong steering capability, enabling flexible navigation through winding paths with sharp turns and complex branches. Ribbon-like swarms, though less steerable, excelled in traversing narrow passages due to their slender morphology. Importantly, we achieved reversible transformation between swarm states by switching magnetic field types. This transformation occurred within seconds without particle loss, granting the system strong adaptability to complex terrains and dynamic physiological conditions. VI. Objective 6: Fully Achieved We evaluated the performance of the heterogeneous microswarm system on a biochip featuring winding paths, branches, and narrow channels. During navigation, rotating magnetic fields assembled vortex-like swarms for high locomotion efficiency. At narrow constrictions, oscillating fields induced transformation into ribbon-like swarms for passage through confined spaces. After crossing, swarms reverted to vortex-like states. Over 90% of particles successfully reached the destination, confirming effective targeting in complex environments. Therapeutic capability was further tested. A heterogeneous swarm composed of NV-DOX, NV-GOx, and NV-Mn²⁺ (mass ratio 2:1:1; total 20 µg) was navigated to HepG2 cancer cells. In the control group, an equivalent amount of free DOX, GOx, and Mn²⁺ was applied at the starting point, resulting in negligible effect due to passive diffusion. In contrast, our swarm system achieved domino-enabled combination therapy, killing nearly all cancer cells and demonstrating superior targeting and therapeutic efficiency. These results highlight the potential of magnetically actuated heterogeneous swarms for precision cancer therapy in complex biological environments.

14300621.label: Major findings and research outcome
14300621.value: Ⅰ. Strategy for constructing heterogeneous microswarm We proposed and a construction method for heterogeneous colloidal swarms. First, we synthesized core–shell nanoparticles consisting of a Fe3O4 core, a middle layer of smart hydrogel as drug reservoir, and a pH-responsive CaP shell for on demand drug release. These nanoparticles can be loaded with different functional agents to yield distinctly functionalized building blocks. We utilized dynamic magnetic field-induced magnetic self-assembly to incorporate different particles into a heterogeneous microswarm system. The heterogeneous microswarm demonstrates excellent stability, mobility, and adaptability, while showing potential functional advantages over its homogeneous counterpart. The related research findings are partially covered in Science Advances, 2024, 10(5), adk8970 and Science Robotics, 2024, 9(87), eadh1978. Ⅱ. Pattern transformation-based adaptative microswarm in complex environments We systematically investigated effects of physicochemical factors related to biofluids (e.g., ionic strength and viscosity) on microswarms. We summarized behaviors of microswarms in biofluids based on the results, providing guidance for applying heterogeneous microswarms in blood. We employed a dual-mode actuation strategy to endow the heterogeneous microswarms with vortex-like and ribbon-like patterns. We proposed a strategy for reversible pattern transformation between the two states within seconds by programming external fields, enabling adaptive navigation of microswarms in complex environments. In complex biochips, the heterogeneous microswarm were navigated to cancer cell region with an access rate exceeding 90%. Our research on microswarm pattern transformation is partially published in ACS Nano, 2022, 16(11), 19025–19037, IEEE Transactions on Robotics, 2024, 40, 3676-3694, and Engineering, 2025, 53, 130-138. Ⅲ. Endowing heterogeneous microswarms with hierarchical and synergistic functions Inspired by functional division behaviors of natural swarms, we innovatively proposed a strategy to impart hierarchical intelligence to heterogeneous microswarms. We encoded domino reaction into heterogeneous microswarms to demonstrate synergistic effects, aiming to generate more therapeutic agents in situ and combine multiple therapy modalities. The heterogeneous microswarm was divided into three subgroups functionalized with doxorubicin, glucose oxidase, and manganese ions. After delivery to cancer cell regions and cellular internalization, the specialized subgroups achieved synergistic therapy by inhibiting the nucleus (chemotherapy), cutting off the energy supply (starvation therapy), and producing abundant highly toxic radicals via domino reaction (chemodynamic therapy), thereby killing cancer cells. This integrated diagnostic and therapeutic platform based on heterogeneous microswarms exhibits efficient targeting and therapeutic performance, holding promise for practical applications in targeted therapy. Related results are partially presented in Advanced Materials, 2022, 34(34), 220188.

14300621.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14300621.value: Further development of this research: First, the influence of biofluids on microswarms should be further explored. Currently, we have investigated the influence of factors such as fluid viscosity and ionic strength. Actual biofluids contain many other factors that may affect swarm behavior, including mesh-like structure, colloidal jamming by blood cells, the formation of protein corona on nanoparticles and so on. We plan to conduct systematic studies on effects of these factors in future research to pave the way for the application of heterogeneous swarms in vivo. Second, the irregular morphology and the presence of mucus of real luminal surfaces may also adversely affect the formation and locomotion of microswarms. We intend to conduct systematic and detailed future studies on this, including experiments on simulated tissue surfaces and in real biological lumens. Third, the functionality of the heterogeneous swarm system needs to be further expanded and enhanced. In this project, we demonstrated synergy based on only three types of functionalized building blocks. In practice, this system can integrate more functions, such as incorporating imaging and sensor agents, to improve real-time imaging-guided navigation capabilities of the microswarms in vivo.

14300621.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14300621.value: This project explores how to create heterogeneous colloidal microswarm using tiny magnetic particles with different properties. We developed special nanoparticles with a core-shell structure that can be easily customized for different functions, serving as the building blocks for the swarms. By applying dynamic magnetic fields, we can make different particles gather into a heterogeneous swarm. This swarm can then be guided to move along a predetermined path to a target location. During movement, by adjusting the magnetic field, the swarm can quickly change its shape. This allows it to adapt and move through complex environments with twists, turns, and narrow passages. Different particles within the cluster can cooperate with each other disrupt multiple growth pathways of cancer cells, which leads to more efficient task performance. The findings from this project could significantly advance the development of microrobotic swarms and hold promising potential for important applications in biomedicine.

14300721.label: Realisation of objectives
14300721.value: The project objectives have been successfully realized as follows: 1. Synthesis of curved polycyclic aromatic molecules using the naphthalene-directed Scholl reaction as a key step The naphthalene-directed Scholl reaction has proven to be a powerful and general strategy for constructing a range of negatively curved polycyclic aromatic molecules. This approach was successfully applied to macrocyclic precursors containing naphthalene units, enabling the regioselective formation of multiple heptagons and yielding previously inaccessible negatively curved nanographenes. Furthermore, the strategic incorporation of a naphthalene moiety into a quinquephenyl-based Scholl reaction substrate allowed precise control over the regioselectivity, enabling the synthesis of a novel armchair carbon nanobelt. These results demonstrate that the naphthalene unit not only enhances reactivity but also directs the regioselective outcome of the Scholl transformation, making it a reliable key step in the synthesis of topologically complex, strained molecular nanocarbons. 2. Investigation of how naphthalene moieties influence the course of Scholl reactions The role of naphthalene units in controlling Scholl reaction regioselectivity was systematically investigated through rational substrate design and mechanistic analysis supported by DFT calculations. Particularly, we found that replacing one phenyl group in quinquephenyl completely changes the regioselectivity of the Scholl reaction due to the steric hindrance in the transition state. In o-quateraryls bearing 3,4-dialkoxyphenyl terminals and 2,3-naphthylene internal units, the reaction outcome—selective formation of either an eight-membered ring or two six-membered rings—can be tuned by modifying reaction conditions, demonstrating the responsiveness of naphthalene-directed cyclizations to external control. 3. Characterization of curved polycyclic aromatic molecules using experimental and computational techniques The synthesized molecules were thoroughly characterized using a multidisciplinary approach. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction provided unambiguous confirmation of molecular structures, revealing the pronounced curvature and interesting molecular packing modes not available to flat π molecules. Specifically, solid-state packing analyses showed that some negatively curved nanographenes form interlocked networks via face-to-face and edge-to-face π–π interactions, which support charge transport in thin-film devices. Electronic properties—including HOMO/LUMO energy levels, absorption/emission profiles, and redox behavior—were evaluated using UV-vis-NIR spectroscopy, cyclic voltammetry, and DFT calculations, enabling a detailed understanding of structure–property relationships. 4. Study of applications, including host–guest interactions with fullerenes and organic semiconductors We have investigated the potential of the synthesized molecules as molecular hosts for fullerenes and organic semiconductors. Notably, the newly developed armchair carbon nanobelt exhibited a strong and selective affinity for C70 over C60, as evidenced by photoluminescence titration experiments. Additionally, the p-type semiconductor behavior of several negatively curved nanographenes was demonstrated in field-effect transistor devices, further underscoring their relevance to organic electronics.

14300721.label: Major findings and research outcome
14300721.value: 1. We developed the Scholl reaction of macrocyclic precursors as a general strategy for synthesizing negatively curved molecular nanocarbons, leveraging the reactivity of naphthalene units in the substrates. This approach enables the formation of multiple heptagons within significantly curved π-conjugated frameworks. In the solid state, some of these negatively curved structures are interlocked through both face-to-face and edge-to-face π–π interactions, leading to ordered assemblies that function as p-type organic semiconductors in field-effect transistors. This work was published in Chem (Publication 3 in Part C), a leading journal in the field. 2. We successfully synthesized a new armchair carbon nanobelt by controlling the regioselectivity of the Scholl reaction of 1,1':2',1'':4'',1''':2''',1''''-quinquephenyl through the incorporation of a naphthalene unit. This nanobelt exhibits preferential binding affinity for C70 over C60, as demonstrated by photoluminescence titration experiments, highlighting its potential for selective fullerene recognition. This work was reported in Publication 4 in Part C. 3. We discovered that the Scholl reaction of o-quateraryls can proceed in a regioselective manner to form a single eight-membered ring, enabling the synthesis of substituted and π-extended tetraphenylenes. The regioselectivity is observed when the terminal aryl groups are significantly more electron-rich than the internal arylene units. Furthermore, by adjusting the reaction conditions, the Scholl reaction of o-quateraryls bearing two 3,4-dialkoxyphenyl terminals and one or two internal 2,3-naphthylene units can be directed to form either an eight-membered ring or two six-membered rings. This tunable reactivity provides a versatile route to structurally diverse polycyclic systems. These results were published in Publication 5 in Part C. 4. At the invitation of Chemical Reviews, we authored a review article entitled “The Scholl Reaction as a Powerful Tool for Synthesis of Curved Polycyclic Aromatics” (Publication 1 in Part C). This review systematically summarizes the application of Scholl reactions in constructing curved polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, highlighting the factors influencing reaction outcomes in the synthesis of strained polycyclic aromatics. 5. We expanded the scope of this project to heteroatom-containing carbon nanocages and synthesized a new oxanorbornene-fused nanocage through the condensation of three C-shaped tetraamine building blocks with two equivalents of cyclohexanehexone. The D3h-symmetric structure, incorporating hexazatrinaphthylene and pyrene units, was unambiguously confirmed by X-ray crystallography. This work demonstrates a rational design strategy for complex heteroatom-doped nanocarbons with potential for molecular encapsulation and optoelectronic applications. These findings were published in Publication 2 in Part C.

14300721.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14300721.value: The findings from this project have significantly improved the predictability and expanded the scope of Scholl reactions, enabling the efficient and regioselective synthesis of molecular nanocarbons that were previously inaccessible. Our work has garnered widespread attention and recognition within the international research community. For instance, Segawa highlighted that “Miao and co-workers have established a general and predictable method to form heptagons from macrocyclic precursors using transannular Scholl reactions” (Chem, 2023, 9, 2725–2737). Building on the new synthetic strategies and mechanistic insights into Scholl reaction regioselectivity developed in this project, we will pursue the design and synthesis of novel molecular nanocarbons. These structures will serve as well-defined building blocks for the precision bottom-up construction of carbon nanomaterials and novel synthetic carbon allotropes.

14300721.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14300721.value: The Scholl reaction is a very powerful method for synthesis of polycyclic aromatics, enabling aryl-aryl coupling without requiring prefunctionalization of the aryl groups and allowing many carbon-carbon bonds to be formed in one synthetic operation. Despite its impressive efficiency in generating various polycyclic aromatics, the Scholl reaction does face limitations and fails to produce the desired output in many other cases. This project aimed to address these challenges by exploring naphthalene-directed Scholl reactions for the controlled synthesis of negatively curved nanographenes and carbon nanobelts, and to investigate their properties and potential applications. We have successfully developed new synthetic strategies leveraging the unique reactivity of naphthalene units, enabling the efficient and regioselective construction of previously inaccessible negatively curved nanographenes and a novel carbon nanobelt. These advances have enhanced the predictability of Scholl reactions and broadened its scope, providing new mechanistic insights into this classical transformation. The resulting materials include new organic semiconductors and a molecular host that selectively binds C70 over C60. This work has led to five peer-reviewed publications, presentations at three international conferences. Furthermore, two PhD students received valuable training through this project.

14300921.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14300921.value: The environmental impacts of atmospheric compounds are of great interest to scientists, the general public, and policy makers. Among these compounds, sulfur compounds are an important component of atmospheric aerosols and cloud droplets. The health and climate effects of inorganic sulfur compounds such as sulfate are well-documented, but the fates and environmental impacts of organosulfur compounds, which can have very different properties and toxicity from their inorganic counterparts, are relatively unknown. Organosulfates (OSs) as a type of major organosulfur compounds can potentially play an important role in determining the properties of atmospheric aerosols and cloud droplets. It is thus crucial to understand the fates and subsequently environmental impacts of OSs. To date, their formation mechanisms have become better understood, but their transformation pathways have remained largely unexplored. To fill this gap, we propose to investigate the kinetics, products, and reaction mechanisms of aqueous-phase processing of commonly found OSs including α- and β-pinene, limonene, limonaketone, and isoprene epoxydiols. By providing fundamental insights into the transformation of OSs via aqueous-phase hydroxyl (OH) radical oxidation, direct photolysis, and hydrolysis, we can obtain more accurate lifetimes of these atmospherically prevalent OSs in the atmosphere. Experiments will be conducted at various reactant concentrations, pH, and ionic strengths, to simulate a broad range of atmospheric conditions. Quantifying the decay rates of OSs, we will evaluate the significance of aqueous-phase processing as an important removal pathway of OSs in the atmosphere and assess the effectiveness of some OSs used as tracers in aerosol source apportionment studies. We will also investigate whether aqueous-phase processing of OSs is potentially a source of the formation of inorganic sulfates and atmospheric OSs with unknown sources and formation mechanisms, by characterizing the composition of the reaction products. Kinetic parameters and reaction mechanisms obtained experimentally will be incorporated in a photochemical box model to improve the description of OS transformation via aqueous-phase reactions, enabling more accurate predictions for the composition and abundance of OSs and allowing us to examine the possible cycling between inorganic and organic sulfur compounds, which have profoundly different properties and environmental implications. Model-observation comparisons will be conducted to identify key factors governing the composition and abundance of OSs. The findings of this proposed study will provide a valuable mechanistic perspective on the transformation of OSs in the atmosphere, which are less well-understood but important processes. 大氣化合物對環境的影響引起了科學家、公眾和政策制定者的極大興趣。在這些化合物中，硫化合物是大氣氣溶膠和雲滴的重要組成部分。無機硫化合物（如硫酸鹽）對健康和氣候的影響已得到充分證明，但有機硫化合物與無機硫化合物具有非常不同的特性和毒性。有機硫酸鹽 (OS) 作為一種主要的有機硫化合物，可能在確定大氣氣溶膠和雲滴的特性方面發揮重要作用。迄今為止，它們的形成機制已經得到更好的理解，但它們的轉化途徑在很大程度上仍未得到探索。為了填補這一空白，我們建議研究大氣中常見的 OS 的水相動力學、產物和反應機制，包括 α- 和 β-pinene、limonene, limonaketone 和 isoprene epoxydiols。通過水相羥基 (OH) 自由基氧化、光解和水解對 OSs 的轉化提供基本見解，我們可以獲得這些大氣中普遍存在的 OSs 在大氣中的更準確的壽命。實驗將在各種反應物濃度、pH 值和離子強度下進行，以模擬廣泛的大氣條件。量化 OSs 的衰減率，我們將評估水相處理作為大氣中 OSs 重要去除途徑的重要性，並評估一些 OSs 在氣溶膠源分配研究中用作示踪劑的有效性。我們還將通過表徵反應產物的組成來研究 OSs 的水相處理是否是形成無機硫酸鹽和大氣中的OSs 的潛在來源和形成機制。實驗獲得的動力學參數和反應機制將被納入光化學模型，以改進對水相反應的 OS 轉化的描述，從而能夠更準確地預測 OSs 的組成，我們將進行模型觀察比較，以確定控制 OS 組成和豐度的關鍵因素。這項研究的結果將為大氣中 OSs 的轉化提供有價值的視角。
