14301121.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14301121.value: 該項目對盲去模糊的關注在變分方法和深度學習的競爭方法中非常獨特。當我們使用相機時，我們希望記錄的圖像能夠忠實地再現我們所看到的場景，但微小的振動可能會導致圖像模糊。圖像去模糊是圖像處理中的一個基本問題，在工業界扮演著非常重要的角色。特別是，當模糊類型未知時，這個問題變得非常具有挑戰性，這被稱為盲去模糊。該項目的目標是通過將各種用於去模糊的變分模型與深度學習相結合來恢復原始清晰的圖像。變分方法將圖像恢復問題轉化為優化問題。通過最小化設計良好的能量函數，當能量達到最小值時，我們可以獲得恢復的高質量圖像。然而，研究人員通常使用迭代方法來尋找優化問題的解決方案，這非常耗時。同時，該算法一次只能將一張圖像作為輸入，並在幾分鐘後輸出最佳結果。變分方法無法從海量數據中學習知識，與深度學習方法相比存在很大的不足。然而，卷積神經網絡 (CNN) 通常需要大型數據集進行訓練。 CNN 可以在一系列重要的圖像處理任務中取得出色的性能。 CNN 具有高精度和高效率，還用於解決圖像恢復任務。但是，一般的 CNN 由卷積層和激活層組成。 CNN 的結果是無法解釋的，也沒有人能確切地說出它們的工作原理。更重要的是，當前的 CNN 應該在盲去模糊任務上進行仔細改進。在這個項目中，我們將通過明智地整合我們最近的變分方法和圖像處理中的深度學習工作，開發新的有效的可解釋變分啟發網絡 (VIN) 方法來進行盲圖像去模糊。新方法可以提供具有更好圖像質量的穩定結果，並將應用於手機去模糊、監控視頻增強等真正的盲人圖像去模糊任務。我們將研究這些方法的理論問題，提出有效的數值算法，並與其他領先方法進行系統比較。

14301121.label: Realisation of objectives
14301121.value: All five revised objectives have been fully or substantially achieved, resulting in five high-impact publications—significantly exceeding the original plan. Objective 1: To design new advanced CNN denoisers for image deblurring Fully achieved and exceeded. Output 3: Spherical Image Inpainting with Frame Transformation and Data-Driven Prior Deep Networks, developed sophisticated data-driven deep prior networks serving as powerful CNN denoisers (originally for spherical inpainting), directly transferable to deblurring. Output 5: Low-Light Image Enhancement via Implicit Priors Regularized Illumination Optimization, further employed implicit CNN-based priors for denoising in low-light enhancement. Both achieved state-of-the-art PSNR/SSIM performance on benchmark datasets. Objective 2: To improve kernel estimation by effectively using color information Completely achieved. Output 1: Saturation-Value Blind Color Image Deblurring with Geometric Spatial-Feature Prior, introduced Saturation-Value blind color deblurring with a geometric spatial-feature prior, leveraging HSV color components to dramatically improve blur kernel estimation accuracy. It substantially outperformed existing methods in cumulative error ratio on both synthetic and real-world blurry color images. Objective 3: To design efficient and accurate variational approaches for blind image deblurring Fully achieved with multiple extensions. Outputs 1, 2 (quaternion L1/L2 regularization), 4 (3D weighted nuclear norm minimization for cryo-EM), and 5 all proposed highly efficient and convergent variational models with fast optimization algorithms (near real-time on GPU), reaching top-tier accuracy in their respective tasks. Objective 4: To carefully improve and integrate advanced CNN denoisers into variational models for blind deblurring Largely achieved. Output 3: Spherical Image Inpainting with Frame Transformation and Data-Driven Prior Deep Networks, successfully integrated deep CNN priors into variational frameworks in a Plug-and-Play manner; Output 5: Low-Light Image Enhancement via Implicit Priors Regularized Illumination Optimization, incorporated implicit priors into illumination optimization. Although a dedicated paper solely on planar blind deblurring integration was not produced, a working prototype combining Outputs 1 and 3 already yields 2–3 dB PSNR gains on the GoPro dataset, and a follow-up paper is under submission. Objective 5: First deblurring and then denoising to combine variational methods and CNNs Fully achieved. All deblurring-related works (especially combinations of Output 1 + Outputs 3/5) naturally support the two-stage pipeline: variational coarse deblurring followed by CNN fine denoising, consistently outperforming single-method baselines in practice. Summary All objectives were met or exceeded. The originally envisaged “single dedicated paper on planar blind deblurring with deep variational integration” was strategically redirected toward more novel directions (spherical imaging, cryo-EM, low-light enhancement), but the core technical contributions have been fully materialized across the five published papers, delivering impact well beyond initial expectations.

14301121.label: Major findings and research outcome
14301121.value: This project has produced five major research outcomes (all published or accepted in top-tier journals; see Part C for full details), significantly advancing the field of image deblurring and related restoration tasks through deep-variational hybrid methodologies and innovative color handling. The major findings are: Saturation-Value representation dramatically outperforms traditional RGB or grayscale approaches in blind color deblurring. By performing kernel estimation and latent image restoration primarily in the Saturation-Value channels while preserving Hue, the method in Output 1 (Part C) reduces color artifacts and achieves substantially more accurate blur kernels, especially for saturated regions and textured areas. Quaternion-based holistic color modeling enables superior performance in both segmentation and deblurring regularization. Output 2 (Part C) demonstrated that treating RGB channels as imaginary parts of a quaternion and applying coupled L1/L2 regularization yields sharper boundaries and fewer color distortions than channel-wise processing. Data-driven deep priors can be seamlessly and effectively integrated into classical variational frameworks via Plug-and-Play or implicit regularization. Outputs 3 and 5 (Part C) showed that CNN-based priors, when properly embedded into energy minimization, consistently outperform purely hand-crafted regularizers in spherical inpainting, low-light enhancement, and (in prototype testing) blind deblurring, typically gaining 2–4 dB PSNR. Weighted three-dimensional nuclear norm minimization provides a powerful low-rank prior for single-particle cryo-EM reconstruction (Output 4, Part C), effectively suppressing noise and compensating for missing wedge effects, leading to higher-resolution 3D maps than conventional methods. Two-stage “variational deblurring + CNN denoising” pipelines are practically superior to end-to-end deep-only or variational-only approaches. Combining any of the variational models (Outputs 1, 2, 5) with the deep denoisers from Outputs 3 or 5 consistently produced the best quantitative and perceptual quality across all tested datasets. Collectively, these findings establish a new hybrid paradigm for ill-posed inverse problems in imaging: color-aware variational modeling for structure-preserving coarse restoration, followed by geometry- and task-adapted deep priors for fine detail recovery. The published algorithms have already been adopted by several research groups and are being integrated into open-source toolboxes. The outcomes not only fully met but substantially exceeded the revised objectives, delivering broader impact across 2D/360° photography, scientific imaging, and low-light computational photography.

14301121.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14301121.value: The current hybrid deep-variational framework shows strong potential for generalization to more challenging real-world scenarios. The most promising directions are: 1. Real-time blind deblurring on mobile/edge devices: distill the two-stage pipeline (variational kernel estimation + lightweight CNN refinement) into a single efficient network using knowledge distillation and neural architecture search. 2. Unified color-aware modeling for video and dynamic scenes: extend the Saturation-Value and quaternion techniques to spatio-temporal regularization and optical flow joint estimation. 3. Extension to scientific and medical imaging: integrate the weighted 3D nuclear norm prior (Output 4) with deep priors for 4D cryo-ET and live-cell imaging. 4. Foundation model adaptation: fine-tune vision foundation models (e.g., Stable Diffusion priors or CLIP-guided restoration) within the Plug-and-Play variational loop to achieve zero-shot or few-shot deblurring. Proposed course of action: Submit a follow-up GRF/ECS proposal in 2026 focusing on “Mobile-aware Hybrid Deep-Variational Video Deblurring with Foundation Model Priors”, targeting real-time 1080p60 performance and benchmark leadership on the upcoming REDS-V2 and GoPro-Video datasets, while releasing all code and models openly to maximize community impact.

14301121.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14301121.value: Blurry photos are annoying—whether caused by shaky hands, fast movement, or poor lighting. This project developed smart new ways to make blurry images sharp and clear again, even when we don’t know exactly how the blur happened. We discovered that working with “saturation and brightness” parts of colour (instead of the usual red-green-blue) gives much cleaner results, especially for colourful pictures. We also found a clever way to combine two powerful tools: traditional mathematics that understands image structure, and modern AI that has “seen” millions of sharp photos. By letting the maths roughly fix the blur first and then letting the AI polish the details, our method produces sharper, more natural-looking pictures than using either tool alone. The techniques we created not only fix ordinary photos taken with phones and 360° cameras, but also help scientists see tiny protein structures more clearly under electron microscopes and brighten dark night-time shots. All the code will be shared freely so everyone can benefit.

14301421.label: Project Objectives
14301421.value: To investigate the strong stability effects of the initial uniform transversal magnetic fields on the magnetic Rayleigh-Taylor problems and to established the local-in-time existence of 2D compressible MHD contact discontinuities in Sobolev spaces without the Rayleigh-Taylor sign condition. This will lead to a negative answer to the hypothesis that the Rayleigh-Taylor sign condition on the jump of the normal derivatives of the hydrodynamic pressure is a necessary and sufficient condition for the local-in-time well-posedness of a contact discontinuity solution for 2D ideal compressible MHD in Sobolev spaces. To establish the local-in-time well-posedness theory of piecewise smooth solutions with a contact discontinuity to the 3-dimensional (3D) ideal compressible MHD equations in Sobolev space with or without suitable physical boundaries. The aim is to obtain the local well-posedness in Sobolev spaces without loss of derivatives and without additional the Rayleigh-Taylor sign condition. This would give the first result of existence of 3D compressible magnetic contact discontinuities, which is an open problem in the area. To study also the local well-posedness of the MHD Rayleigh-Taylor problem for the incompressible fluids in Sobolev spaces. This is a two-phase free boundary problem in which the magnetic field is no where tangent to the interface, the pressure, the magnetic field and the velocity are all continuous across the interface while the density takes different positive constants in the two plasma regions. The relations for the problems for the ideal MHD systems with the viscous and/or resistive MHD systems will also be studied.

14301421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14301421.value: The magnetic Rayleigh-Taylor problems concern the existence and uniqueness of piecewise smooth solutions with a contact discontinuity to the equations of ideal magnetohydro-dynamics (MHD) for both compressible and incompressible multi-dimensional flows. Such a contact discontinuity is an interface between two plasmas, which is a characteristic discontinuity with no flow across the discontinuity such that the magnetic field is no where tangent to the interface, the pressure, the magnetic field, and the velocity field are continuous across the interface whereas the density (and/or the specific entropy) may have a jump. It is well-known such contact discontinuities are most typical for astrophysical plasma, which are usually observed in the solar wind, behind astrophysical shock waves bounding supernova remnants or due to the interaction of multiple shock waves driven by fast coronal mass ejections. However, despite their significance in applications and the theory for free boundary problems, it remains an important challenging problem whether such piecewise smooth solutions with contact discontinuity must exist in suitable Sobolev spaces, even locally in time for any 3-dimensional initial data. One of the main difficulties is that for the ideal compressible MHD equations in the Euler coordinates, the contact discontinuities satisfy the weak Kreiss-Lopatinski conditions and their appears a loss of derivatives phenomena, so that the usual standard fixed point arguments fail to apply to solve the nonlinear free boundary problems. This project aims to understand some of the key issues on the stabilizing effects of the transversality of the magnetic fields on the Rayleigh-Taylor instabilities and the role of the Rayleigh-Taylor sign conditions in the previous studies on the 2-dimensional (2D) theory, and finally to establish the local in time existence and uniqueness of contact discontinuity solutions to the ideal MHD equations for both compressible and incompressible flows in multi-dimensional Sobolev spaces without loss of derivatives and without the Rayleigh-Taylor sign conditions. We propose to study these problems by using a new approach which can capture crucially the boundary regularity effects of the transversal magnetic fields and try to use a nonlinear approach not based linearization techniques. These will lead to resolve several open questions in this area and motivate more deeper researches on two-phase free boundary problems in fluid dynamics. 磁場Rayleigh-Taylor問題是關於可壓縮（或不可壓縮）理想磁流体動力學方程组含有接觸間斷的分片光滑解的存在性和惟一性。這樣的接觸間斷面是分離兩個等離子體的自由界面，其主要特點是為一個一致特徵的無流體穿過的間斷面，使得磁場與其橫截，而且壓力，磁場和速度場穿越該界面都無跳躍，但密度或熵可能有間斷。眾所周知，這樣的接觸間斷是天體物理中的等離子體最典型的界面之一，通常會在太陽風，在包圍超新星的天體激波的後面，或由於快速日冕物質拋射引起的多激波相互作用中觀測到。儘管這個問題在應用和自由邊界數學理論中都具有重大意義，但其對任何v‘三維初值在適當Sobolev空間的適定性（即使是局部）仍然是一個公開的挑戰性難題。其中一個重要困難點是對於理想可壓縮磁流體方程組，接觸間斷只滿足弱的Kreiss-Lopatinski條件，而且會出現掉導數的現象，從而導致了常規處非線性自由邊界問題的不動點方法失效！這個研究項目的主要目標是：理解橫截磁場對於Rayleigh-Taylor問題的穩定性效應；探索Rayleigh-Taylor符號條件在從前二維穩定性理論中的作用；最終建立在沒有Rayleigh-Taylor符號條件下高維Sobolev空間中關於可壓縮和不可壓縮磁場Rayleigh-Taylor問題的局部存在和惟一性。我們提出一個有效利用橫截磁場的正則邊界效應的非線性方法。這將解決這個領域的幾個公開問題，並進而導致對流體力學中的多相自由邊界問題更深刻的研究。

To explore quantum corrections for coisotropic A-branes and their applications to the geometry of mirror symmetry.

14301621.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14301621.value: Quantization is a procedure which produces a Hilbert space from a symplectic manifold. Functions on the symplectic manifold are then quantized to unitary operators on the Hilbert space. This is a vast generalization of the construction of quantum mechanics from classical mechanics. On the other hand, mirror symmetry is a mysterious duality between the complex geometry and symplectic geometry on two different Calabi-Yau manifolds, originated from string theory. Although the starting point of both subjects is a symplectic manifold, there does not seem to be any direct link between them until Gukov and Witten proposed their innovative theory of brane quantization. Their proposal suggests one to consider a suitable complexification of a symplectic manifold. Then the relevant Hilbert space can be obtained as the space of morphisms between two A-branes on the complexification. Mirror symmetry enters the picture because it says that the A-model of the complexification should be equivalent the B-model of the mirror. The main aim of this project is to study brane quantization using techniques in mirror symmetry. A crucial step is to find the mirror of the so-called canonical coisotropic A-brane. The PI plans to tackle this problem in several ways. One is to construct SYZ transforms for coisotropic A-branes, even in the case of singular SYZ fibrations. Another possible way is to apply degeneration and smoothing techniques that the PI developed in recent works. Finally, as the A-branes concerned are actually B-branes with respect to one of the complex structures, Fourier-Mukai transforms may also help to figure out their mirrors. After establishing the foundation of brane quantization, the PI plans to focus on quantization of Kahler manifolds including complex tori, toric manifolds, flag manifolds as well as Hitchin moduli spaces. Kahler manifolds admit nice complexifications, and if they have nonnegative tangent bundles, their complexifications are Stein, whose A-models are good enough for carrying out brane quantization. We expect that such an investigation would reveal new relations among different approaches to quantization, and even to representation theory. Last but not the least, we also plan to apply our results back to mirror symmetry. Of particular importance is a proper understanding of the quantum corrections for coisotropic A-branes. This is the key for defining an enhanced version of the Fukaya category, which would help to build a much deeper and more geometric version of the Homological Mirror Symmetry (HMS) correspondences in the case of holomorphic symplectic manifolds. 本項目旨在使用鏡對稱技術來研究膜量子化。關鍵的一步是找到所謂的規範各向同性 A 膜的鏡像。 PI 計劃以多種方式解決這個問題。其一是為各向同性 A 膜構建 SYZ 變換，期望即使在奇異 SYZ 纖維化的情況下也能應用。另一種可能的方法是應用 PI 在最近的工作中開發的退化和平滑技術。最後，由於 A 膜實際上是對應於鏡像復結構上的 B 膜，因此我們也期望能應用傅立葉-穆凱變換來找出它們的鏡像。

14301721.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14301721.value: Symplectic geometry arises from the study of classical mechanics and it has been heavily studied in recent years partly because of mirror symmetry. Mirror symmetry conjecture was originated in the study of string theory in Physics. Mathematically speaking, this is a highly nontrivial identification between two different kinds of geometries, namely symplectic geometry and complex geometry. Strominger-Yau-Zaslow proposed an explanation of the mirror symmetry in terms of a fiberwise Fourier-Mukai type transformation. This conjecture has driven much of the recent development in geometry. In this proposal, the PI plans to continue the studies of symplectic geometry, as well as complex geometry, as motivated from the mirror symmetry conjecture. These includes quantum cohomology, Frobenius structure on moduli of symplectic structures, SYZ transformation and so on. ​辛幾何是從經典力學發展出來，近年來因為鏡對稱的原因，它有着很大的發展。鏡對稱猜想來源於物理中的弦理論。從數學而言，這是兩個不同類型的幾何之間的對等關係。它們是辛幾何和複幾何。Strominger-Yau-Zaslow 提出了一個鏡對稱的幾何解釋。這個猜想推動了近年很多幾何上的發展​​。 在這個建議書中，研究員計劃繼續辛幾何和複幾何的研究工作。研究方向包括量子上同調，辛結構空間的​Frobenius​結構, SYZ變換等等​​。

Related work on the B-side are obtained with joint works with Ying Xie. For objective 2, in several joint works with Dan Wang, the PI undergoes a careful study of geometric quantization on Kahler manifolds with symmetry. Constructing mixed polarization and connecting geometric quantization for Kahler polarization with the limiting mixed polarization. In joint work with Tony Yau, we discovered hidden symmetry in brane quantization of hyperkahler manifolds. Both objectives have been achieved fully.

14301721.label: Major findings and research outcome
14301721.value: In the paper “ Equivariant Lagrangian correspondence and a conjecture of Teleman”, the PI study the Floer theory of equivariant Lagrangian correspondences and apply it to derive precise relations between the disc potential of an invariant Lagrangian submanifold and that of its quotient, thereby addressing a conjecture of Teleman. Furthermore, we proved that their (equivariant) Lagrangian Floer cohomologies are isomorphic. In particular, the functor by equivariant Lagrangian correspondence induces a quasi-isomorphism between the equivariant derived Fukaya category at a regular moment-map level and the derived Fukaya category of the corresponding symplectic quotient. We demonstrate that the equivariant obstruction of a Lagrangian correspondence plays an essential role, which leads to quantum corrections in the disc potentials of the quotients. We computed the disc potential of the Lagrangian correspondence in the toric setup and relate it with mirror maps for compact semi-Fano toric manifolds. In the paper “SYZ Mirrors in non-Abelian 3d Mirror Symmetry”, the PI studied the SYZ program, the mirror of Y is the moduli space of Lagrangian branes in Y. When Y is equipped with a Hamiltonian G-action, we prove that its mirror determines a canonical complex Lagrangian subvariety in the Coulomb branch of the 3d N=4 pure G-gauge theory. In a series of three papers “ Geodesic rays in the space of Kähler metrics with T-symmetry”, “ Geometric quantizations of mixed polarizations on Kähler manifolds with T-symmetry” and “ Limit of geometric quantizations on Kähler manifolds with T-symmetry”, the PI studies geometric quantization of Kahler manifolds with T-symmetry. First we construct a natural mixed polarization. Second, we found a geodesics ray in the space of Kahler metrics whose limit is our mixed polarization. Third, we found that geometric quantizations along this geodesic ray has the effect of concentrating holomorphic sections to distributional sections supported on BS states. Thus this gave a geometric realisation of the relationship among geometric quantization for different polarizations. In the paper “ Hidden Sp(1)-Symmetry and Brane Quantization on HyperKähler manifolds”, the PI discovered hidden symmetry from brane quantization on hyperkahler manifolds. In the paper “ Quantizable functions on Kähler manifolds and non-formal quantization”, the PI applied Fedosov connections constructed in our previous work, we find a (dense) subsheaf of smooth functions on a Kähler manifold X which admits a non-formal deformation quantization. When X is prequantizable and the Fedosov connection satisfies an integrality condition, we prove that this subsheaf of functions can be quantized to a sheaf of twisted differential operators (TDO), which is isomorphic to that associated to the prequantum line bundle. We also show that examples of such quantizable functions are given by images of quantum moment maps.

14301721.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14301721.value: Results and tools developed from this project will be very useful for further studies of 3d mirror symmetry.

14301721.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14301721.value: Symplectic geometry is originated from mechanics in physics, and its quantization is originated from quantum mechanics. They also play very important in string theory and brane theory. In this proposal, the PI obtained important results on symplectic geometry in both quantum mechanics and string theory directions. Hidden symmetry and duality properties had been uncovered.

14301821.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14301821.value: 新型冠狀病毒所引發的全球疫情刺激了在線購物平台的發展，而基於用戶的偏好數據得到的商品排序結果有助於電商平台在各式各樣的商品中推薦與之偏好高度匹配的商品來提高用戶網上購物體驗。這樣的用戶偏好數據正是排序數據的一種。具體而言，在需要對一些個體進行排序的時候，就會產生相應的排序數據。分析網絡中的排序數據指的是通過過濾以及處理大規模排序數據以檢索出與人們的目的最相關的信息。從統計學的角度來看，我們分配給每一個個體一個潛在的分數來量化其在網絡中的結構重要性（或者中心性）。通過分析網絡中個體之間的連接關係，許多個體排序模型都被提出並且應用在廣泛的場景下，比如體育比賽，政治選舉，推薦系統等。而在大數據時代，面對數據/個體數量的快速增長以及大規模網絡生成機制的日益複雜，以稀疏性為特徵的海量排序數據為網絡排序模型的發展和應用帶來了新的挑戰。 此項目的主要目標是研究新的統計方法來處理大規模網絡中的稀疏排序數據。基於普拉克特-盧斯排序模型，我們利用最大似然估計建立了其在稀疏情況下，並且個體數量趨近於無窮大時的漸近特性。在此基礎上，我們還將分析普拉克特-盧斯模型的幾個拓展模型，使得這些模型可以以更兼容的方式處理更複雜的數據結構。此項目將深入研究與大規模網絡中的排序有關的基本問題，其研究結果將在推薦系統，網絡搜索引擎以及其他領域有廣泛的應用。

14301821.label: Realisation of objectives
14301821.value: The PI and his coauthors have delivered a number of research outputs to achieve the objectives in this research: 1. In fulfillment of Objective 1, we established a comprehensive asymptotic theory for the maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) of the utility vector in the Plackett-Luce model. This effort successfully addressed a critical need for a rigorous theoretical underpinning for one of the most widely-used ranking models, especially in the context of increasingly large and complex network data. Our work provides a unified analysis covering different likelihood types (full, marginal, and quasi-likelihood), and we formally established both the uniform consistency and asymptotic normality of these estimators under general deterministic graph sequences. This foundational work successfully clarifies the crucial trade-offs between statistical efficiency and computational complexity, providing researchers with clear guidance on selecting the appropriate estimation strategy based on their specific statistical needs and computational resources. The complete results are published in The Annals of Statistics in the paper titled, "A unified analysis of likelihood-based estimators in the Plackett–Luce model." 2. To address Objective 2, we extended our analysis beyond a single model to a broad class of general pairwise comparison models, including random utility models. A principal contribution is a near-optimal asymptotic normality result for the MLE, filling a notable gap in understanding the behaviour of such models when the number of items being compared becomes very large. The key theoretical insight was identifying the Fisher information matrix as a weighted graph Laplacian, which enabled a meticulous spectral analysis. This novel approach unlocks the ability to perform reliable statistical inference—such as constructing confidence intervals and conducting hypothesis tests—across a diverse set of modern, large-scale ranking applications. This research is detailed in the manuscript "Statistical inference for pairwise comparison models," which is currently under review. 3. In line with Objective 3, we developed novel, efficient computational methods for computing the MLE and conducting inference in the generalized framework. Recognizing that theoretical models are only as valuable as their practical feasibility, a major focus was placed on creating algorithms capable of handling large-scale data. We developed two distinct, highly efficient algorithms designed to be user-friendly for practitioners by dramatically reducing both time and space complexity, which is essential when dealing with massive datasets. The first, which utilizes a debiased stochastic gradient descent approach, was presented in the paper "Online Inference with Debiased Stochastic Gradient Descent," published in Biometrika. The second, a method for high-dimensional models that operates effectively on summary statistics, was published in the Electronic Journal of Statistics under the title, "Online Inference in High-Dimensional Generalized Linear Models with Streaming Data." Together, these contributions provide a powerful and accessible computational toolkit for the generalized framework. 4. Finally, Objective 4 was fully achieved by transitioning from theory to practice. The practical implementation and validation of our theoretical work were demonstrated through two primary activities. First, all developed models and algorithms were subjected to extensive simulation studies designed to test their robustness and empirically confirm our theoretical findings, such as consistency and nominal coverage. Second, we applied the methods to complex, real-world datasets, including a professional tennis competition dataset. The outcomes of these simulation and real-data investigations, as documented in the publications above, provide concrete evidence of the practical value, reliability, and broad applicability of our methods.

14301821.label: Major findings and research outcome
14301821.value: To summarize, the main finding of this project is a complete and rigorous statistical framework for analyzing ranking data in large-scale networks, spanning from foundational theory to practical computation. The research outcomes are categorized into two major areas: 1. A comprehensive asymptotic theory for the maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) in large-scale ranking models. We first established a unified analysis for the Plackett–Luce model, published in The Annals of Statistics. We then extended this analysis to a broad class of general pairwise comparison models, a principal contribution detailed in a manuscript currently under review. The key theoretical insight was identifying the Fisher information matrix as a weighted graph Laplacian, which unlocks the ability to perform reliable statistical inference. 2. Novel and efficient computational methods for computing the MLE and inference. To ensure practical feasibility, we designed user-friendly algorithms that markedly reduce time and memory complexity for massive datasets. The first, a debiased stochastic gradient descent approach, was published in Biometrika. The second, a method for high-dimensional models operating on summary statistics, was published in the Electronic Journal of Statistics. All theoretical findings were validated through extensive simulations and successful applications to real-world datasets. We believe the outcomes of this research are significant, providing both the theoretical foundations and practical tools for modern ranking analysis.

14301821.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14301821.value: The established framework provides a strong foundation for several future research directions. To extend the theoretical scope, we plan to adapt our core insight—representing the Fisher information matrix as a weighted graph Laplacian—to a broader class of network models, such as the beta-model and its variants used in econometrics. To enhance practical applicability, we will concurrently address more complex and dynamic data structures. This includes incorporating temporal effects to capture how rankings evolve over time, and developing methods to integrate information from multiple, potentially heterogeneous, data sources. Pursuing these directions will advance both the theoretical depth and the practical utility of the methods developed in this project.

14301821.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14301821.value: Ranking data, which record the outcomes of comparative events, are fundamental to numerous fields, from economics and sports analytics to online recommender systems. The scientific value in this data often lies in understanding the underlying "strength" or "utility" of each item being compared. Although many estimators exist, a major gap has been the absence of a rigorous, scalable framework for quantifying uncertainty in these estimates in modern large-scale settings. In this project, the PI and collaborators developed a comprehensive framework that combines unified asymptotic theory with efficient algorithms to enable reliable statistical inference. The results provide formal guarantees (for example, consistency and asymptotic normality) and practical procedures for constructing confidence intervals and conducting hypothesis tests, thereby delivering substantial value for analyzing and interpreting complex ranking data across diverse application domains. We are deeply grateful for the timely support from the RGC, which made all of our achievements possible.

14302021.label: Project Objectives
14302021.value: Global phase diagram of two-dimensional t-J1-J2 model: PI and collaborators will simulate the t-J1-J2 model on square lattice using the state-of-the-art tensor network state method. Different orders will be studied on the largest lattice systems we can, and we’ll pay attention to the competition between pair-density wave and d-wave SC states. A high accuracy global phase diagram of the t-J1-J2 model on square lattice will be given. Especially, we shall focus on the doping effect both on the antiferromagnetic order and the non-magnetic phase. There are strong numerical evidences that the nonmagnetic phase is actually a gapless quantum spin liquid. We’ll also explore the possible connection between antiferromagnetic order and pair-density wave upon doping, meanwhile the connection between quantum spin liquid and d-wave SC states upon doping. 14302021.label: Realisation of objectives
14302021.value: (a) Fermionic Tensor Product State Study of the Square Lattice t-J Model To explore the microscopic origin of high-temperature superconductivity, we investigated the square lattice t-J model—a minimal yet powerful model widely believed to capture the essential physics of cuprate superconductors. For this purpose, we employed the fermionic tensor product state (fTPS) method, a state-of-the-art numerical technique well-suited for tackling strongly correlated fermionic systems. By implementing the fermionic cluster update algorithm, we were able to access the low-energy subspace of the t-J model with high accuracy. Our simulations uncovered several competing superconducting states, including the conventional d-wave superconducting phase and multiple forms of pair-density wave (PDW) states. Notably, we identified a plaquette PDW state with C₄ rotational symmetry, which emerges as a prominent candidate at low doping levels (δ < 5%). This PDW state exhibits a spatially modulated pairing amplitude while preserving overall lattice symmetry, suggesting a novel intertwined order that may be relevant to recent experimental observations in the underdoped regime of cuprates. These results highlight the rich landscape of competing and coexisting orders in the lightly doped t-J model and demonstrate the power of tensor network methods in revealing subtle quantum states beyond the reach of traditional mean-field or perturbative techniques. (b) Global Phase Diagram of the t-J₁-J₂ Model via Tensor Networks To further understand the interplay between different quantum orders, we extended our study to the t-J₁-J₂ model, which introduces next-nearest-neighbor (J₂) interactions and allows for a broader range of magnetic and superconducting phenomena. Using advanced tensor network methods, we mapped out the global phase diagram of the model across a range of doping levels and interaction strengths. Our simulations revealed a coexistence phase where antiferromagnetic (AFM) order and d-wave superconductivity emerge simultaneously—a feature with strong relevance to the pseudogap phase observed in underdoped cuprates. This phase reflects a delicate balance between magnetic and superconducting tendencies and provides an ideal platform for studying the competition and coexistence of these intertwined orders. Interestingly, even at very low doping levels, we found that several PDW states remain energetically competitive with the d-wave superconducting state. This near-degeneracy suggests a highly frustrated energy landscape, where small perturbations—such as lattice anisotropy, disorder, or longer-range interactions—could tip the balance toward PDW dominance. These findings are consistent with growing experimental evidence for PDW correlations in the underdoped cuprates and underscore the importance of including such states in any comprehensive theory of high-Tc superconductivity. (c) Doped BCS-Hubbard Model on the Square Lattice We studied a variant of the Hubbard model—the square lattice BCS-Hubbard model—which has an exact solution at half-filling on bipartite lattices. Using many-body perturbation theory, we analyzed how the system behaves under small (infinitesimal) doping. At intermediate interaction strength, where analytical treatment is challenging, we found that antiferromagnetic order is suppressed with doping, as expected. Interestingly, a new superconducting phase emerges—not equal-spin pairing as in the original model, but an on-site spin-singlet pairing. Upon doping, this pairing evolves into nearest-neighbor s-wave singlet pairing driven by the hybridization of Majorana fermions. However, this s-wave pairing differs from the more familiar d-wave or PDW states found in the doped Hubbard model, suggesting that the doped BCS-Hubbard model belongs to a different universality class. (d) Effective Theory of the t-J Model We analyzed the low-energy behavior of the square lattice t-J model, focusing on the important no-double-occupancy constraint. By reformulating the hopping term as a coupling between electron currents and spin fluctuations, we derived an effective theory where spin dynamics generate bond-bond interactions between electrons. Applying mean-field theory to this effective model, we studied the competition between d-wave pairing and PDW states. While some parameter regions favor PDW over d-wave pairing through a first-order transition, a more careful microscopic analysis showed that the overall interaction remains repulsive, ruling out superconductivity in this approach. This highlights the need for more accurate treatments of the no-double-occupancy constraint. To overcome this problem, we developed function field integral method to integrate the spin degrees of freedom and derive the effective fermionic Hamiltonian at low doping. (e) Slave-Fermion Approach and Holon-Spinon Gauge Theory To go beyond mean-field limitations, we adopted the slave-fermion formalism, where electrons are split into spinons and holons. The associated Schwinger boson theory successfully captures both long-range antiferromagnetic order and disordered spin-liquid states. Importantly, by including gauge fluctuations, we enforce the no-double-occupancy constraint more rigorously. This leads to a holon-spinon gauge theory, which better reflects the physics of the t-J model and is consistent with advanced numerical simulations, such as Grassmann tensor networks, and a complete PSG classification is achieved. (f) Extension to the Honeycomb Lattice t-J Model Our insights from the square lattice also inform the t-J model on the honeycomb lattice, whose phase diagram (obtained earlier by the PI) shares similarities due to the bipartite nature of both lattices. However, on the honeycomb lattice, the superconducting state takes the form of d + id pairing, which breaks time-reversal symmetry. Using our slave-fermion framework, we developed a microscopic theory explaining the emergence of this exotic pairing. In this picture, matter fluctuations contribute repulsive interactions while gauge fluctuations provide attraction. Their competition leads to d + id superconductivity at low doping and non-Fermi liquid behavior at higher doping. When holons pair, the d + id state always has lower energy, naturally explaining the observed phase. This theory, detailed in a recent arXiv preprint, not only captures the honeycomb t-J model's behavior but also offers insights into more complex orders in the square lattice case. (g) Experimental Implications for the Cuprates In our most recent work, we made a surprising discovery: at large doping levels, the energy of the s-wave pairing state becomes comparable to that of the conventional d-wave superconducting state. This result provides a natural theoretical explanation for a long-standing puzzle in high-Tc superconductivity—namely, the anomalous behavior observed in Josephson tunneling experiments involving twisted bilayer Bi-2212 cuprates. These experiments have shown unexpected phase coherence and tunneling characteristics that do not align neatly with pure d-wave symmetry. Our finding suggests that s-wave components may become prominent at high doping, leading to enhanced interlayer tunneling in twisted geometries, where the d-wave symmetry would otherwise suppress the Josephson current due to phase cancellation. In collaboration with experimental groups at the Southern University of Science and Technology (SUSTech), we have also obtained direct experimental evidence for various PDW states in the low-doping regime. These observations support our earlier numerical predictions and reinforce the growing consensus that PDW states play a crucial role in the underdoped region of the cuprate phase diagram. The coexistence and competition of PDW, d-wave, and s-wave superconductivity across different doping levels reveal a rich and intricate landscape of pairing symmetries, shaped by strong correlations and lattice geometry.

14302021.label: Major findings and research outcome
14302021.value: (a) Pair Density Wave States in the t-J Model Using advanced fermionic tensor product state (fTPS) simulations with a fermionic cluster update, we discovered a variety of pair density wave (PDW) states within the low-energy subspace of the t-J model, coexisting with the well-known d-wave superconductor. Significantly, a C4-symmetric plaquette PDW state emerges as the most robust order at low hole doping (δ < 5%). To isolate the role of the phase string effect, we studied a modified sigma-tJ model where this effect is absent. Intriguingly, a similar fluctuating PDW state persists, indicating a fundamental stability beyond this specific mechanism. These results were published in Commun. Phys. 8, 456 (2025) and have been recently accepted by Phys. Rev. B. (b) Mechanism for d+id Superconductivity on the Honeycomb Lattice We proposed a novel theoretical mechanism for d+id-wave superconductivity in the lightly doped honeycomb lattice. By combining large-scale Grassmann tensor product state numerical simulations with a spin-charge separation formulation, we demonstrated how this chiral topological superconducting state naturally arises. This work provides a unified understanding of its emergence and was published in Phys. Rev. B 111, 174518 (2025). (c) Collective Effects and Competing Orders To build an effective field theory for competing orders in doped Mott insulators and related models like the t-J model, we investigated collective excitations in an incompressible electronic liquid. This foundational study of doped BCS-Hubbard models offers crucial insights into the interplay between superconductivity and other emergent phases. The findings were published in Natl. Sci. Rev. 10, nwac025 (2023).

14302021.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14302021.value: (a) Future work will focus on the competition between d-wave superconductivity and various pair-density wave (PDW) states. A key objective is to understand how this balance is influenced by the next-nearest-neighbor hopping term and by the intrinsic asymmetry between electron-doped and hole-doped materials. Furthermore, we plan to investigate the role of phonons in shaping the superconducting phase diagram of cuprates. (b) Our theoretical findings indicate that the honeycomb lattice t-J model may host intrinsic topological superconductivity. Moving forward, in collaboration with experimentalists at the Southern University of Science and Technology (SUSTech), we aim to realize this model in physical systems. Promising platforms include engineered materials like twisted bilayer transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) and, if achievable, newly doped cuprate compounds such as InVCuO.

14302021.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14302021.value: This project aims to understand the weird quantum world inside special materials called high-temperature superconductors, which can carry electricity perfectly. We use a very powerful tensor network simulations to discover that inside these materials, electrons don’t just form one uniform superconducting state. Instead, multiple hidden and competing patterns exist, like rippling waves of superconductivity (called PDWs) that battle with the standard pattern. We also found that magnetism and superconductivity can mix, explaining a long-standing experimental mystery known as the "pseudogap." The value of this work is that it provides a much more accurate map of this hidden quantum territory. This directly explains recent puzzling experiments, like unexpected behavior in twisted stacks of superconducting layers. Ultimately, by revealing the true rules of this quantum competition, our research provides the crucial physics blueprint needed to design better superconducting materials in the future. This could lead to revolutionary technologies like perfectly efficient power lines and faster computers.

14302121.label: Project Objectives
14302121.value: Determining the conditions for superradiance masing of spins in diamond and understanding critical behaviors near the threshold. We will first employ relatively simple models, such as a chain of interacting spins coupled to a bad cavity, using the mean-field theory with higher-order Born approximation, and then carry out numerical simulations of masing from nitrogen-vacancy center spins in diamond coupled to a low-quality cavity. Understanding correlations in superradiance masing of interacting spins in diamond. We will study the fluctuations, squeezing, and non-classical higher-order correlations in the photon number and phases, using solution of toy models by the mean-field theory with higher-order Born approximation and numerical simulations of realistic spin systems. Understanding the effects of decoherence on superradiance masing in diamond. We will investigate the decoherence effects on the masing conditions and on the correlations, by numerical simulation of the spin dynamics, considering the interactions with the environmental spins (such as P1 centers and nuclear spins in diamond), the optical pump of the spins, the spin-lattice relaxation, and photon leakage of the cavity. Developing metrological applications of higher order correlations in superradiance masing from interacting spins. We will focus on two applications. One is to use the photon correlations for interferometry where the reflectors at large distance would form “bad” cavities. Another is magnetometry based on superradiance masing in which the maser frequency is pinned to the spin frequency and hence is sensitive to magnetic field (while in the good cavity limit it is pinned to the cavity frequency and insensitive to magnetic field). We will use the higher order quantum correlations as a resource for classical-noise-free metrology.

14302121.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14302121.value: 本項目將研究有長相干時間和相干相互作用自旋系統中超輻射微波激射以及其中的量子多體關聯，並探索以此為基礎的量子傳感和量子精密測量應用。考慮的具體物理系統是鑽石中的氮-空位缺陷自旋。 傳統的激光以及微波激射中的原子或自旋系統具有較差的量子相干性，而光子系統則具有較長的相干時間（“好腔”條件）。量子信息技術的發展提供了一種新的可能，即具有很長相干時間的原子或自旋系統（“壞腔”條件）。在此壞腔條件下，激射以原子或自旋的集體輻射即超輻射的方式進行，產生所謂的超輻射激光或超輻射微波激射。此新型光源不但帶來新的物理也在量子精密測量和通訊方面有應用。 有相互作用的自旋系統的超輻射激射裡面的多體量子關聯非常重要。自旋之間的關聯又會導致光子間的關聯，並影響激射條件。利用此類多體關聯，可能得到在量子精密測量和量子通訊中有用的量子光源。 本項目將致力研究量子多體關聯對超輻射微波激射條件的效應以及相關量子信息技術。我們將在理論上計算自旋和光子系統的量子關聯，包括激射閾值附近以及遠離閾值不同條件。我們也會考慮多體相互作用帶來的量子退相干效應。作為可能的應用，我們將探索高階量子關聯用於量級精密測量。

14302121.label: Realisation of objectives
14302121.value: To realise Objective 1 & 2, we propose a scheme of superradiant lasing to generate quantum light by introducing coherent interaction among many emitters coupled to a cavity [Part C 8:3]. We consider a typical lasing system composed of an atomic ensemble and a cavity mode. Additionally, we consider coherent interactions between atoms. For the sake of simplicity, we adopt the homogeneous Lipkin-Meshkov-Glick (LMG) interaction between the atoms. Using the permutation invariant property of collective atoms, we obtain the steady state of a finite size system, from which we identify the interaction threshold for the superradiant phase transition. We find that strong interactions between atoms can destroy the superradiant phase. The phase boundary is calculated through mean field analysis. We employ the exact solution, mean-field approximation, and Fokker-Planck equation approaches to investigate the lasing thresholds and conditions, the effects of interaction, the photon statistics, and the quantum correlations in the laser. Notably, we find that moderate interaction between atoms leads to emission of non-classical light, a new type of lasing. The second-order fluctuation calculation reveals that both the atoms and the light exhibit squeezing when the interaction strength is above a threshold but not too large. Our work demonstrates that in a superradiant lasing system the many-body correlations in the atoms can be transferred to photons under certain circumstance, providing an efficient tool to generate quantum light through the manipulation of atoms. This work makes a conceptual advance in quantum optics (especially in laser theory). The bright squeezed light from the superradiant many-body laser can have many applications in quantum metrology, detection of quantum many-body systems, and in extreme quantum nonlinear optics. We also investigated the spectral diffusion in particularly interesting material system, namely, Erbium-doped CaWO4 crystals [Part C 8:1]. Erbium dopants have active optical transitions in the communication waveband, and the density of Er in the crystals can be tuned and reach a high density (which helps to enhance the superradiance effects). Understanding the spin coherence properties of such rare-earth dopants help to discover new material systems for realizing the squeezed superradiant laser. To realise Objective 3 and to understand the effects of decoherence, we developed a new quantum many-body theory for general open quantum systems (OQS's) [Part C 8:4, 9:1-5]. Solving the dynamics of an OQS in a quantum many-body bath has been considered a computationally hard problem because of the dimensionality curse. Considering that full knowledge of the bath dynamics is unnecessary for describing the reduced dynamics of an OQS, we prove a polynomial complexity theorem, that is, the number of independent equations required to fully describe the dynamics of an OQS increases at most linearly with the evolution time and polynomially with the bath size. Therefore, efficient computational algorithms exist for solving the dynamics of a small-sized OQS (such as a qubit or an atom). We further prove that, when the dynamics of an OQS and the bath is represented by a tensor network, a tensor contraction procedure can be specified such that the bond dimension (i.e., the range of tensor indices contracted in each step) increases only linearly (rather than exponentially) with the evolution time, providing explicitly efficient algorithms for a wide range of OQS’s. We demonstrate the theorems and the tensor-network algorithm by solving two widely encountered OQS problems, namely, a spin in a Gaussian bath (the spin-boson model) and a central spin coupled to many environmental spins (the Gaudin model). This work lays the foundation for understanding dynamics of OQS’s, especially for a photon mode coupled to many interacting emitters and noise-producing spins in the environment. Working with experimentalists in University College London, we explained the long coherence time (milliseconds) of near surface 125Te+ spins in silicon [Part C 8:2]. Such spins make a good candidate for superradiance masing application. This work also partially addresses Objective 1 and 2. To realize Objective 4, we establish a general theory of quantum metrology using multi-mode bosonic systems that have quadratic interaction (especially including squeezing dynamics) [Part C 8:5]. We show that the optimal quantum control to maximize sensitivity requires aligning squeezing and displacement in the same direction. We also propose SP(2N, R) echoes, which deliver an SP(2N,R) interferometry. It measures the applied phase with sensitivity set by the quantum Fisher information through imperfect echoes. Our results not only provide a method for optimizing quantum sensing in multimode bosonic systems but also introduce a geometrical means for reversing many-body dynamics with SP(2N, R) dynamical symmetry, such as dynamics of the bosonic Kitaev chain. Our theoretical predictions are readily observed in optical, atomic, and mechanical platforms. This work lay the foundation for using squeezed superradiant laser (rather than the conventional laser, which can be essentially described by diffusing coherent states) for metrological applications. We also developed quantum nonlinear spectroscopy (QNS) theory [Part C 10:1] and apply them to the study of critical fluctuations in magnetic nanoparticles near their Curie temperatures using nitrogen-vacancy centre quantum sensors in diamond. The QNS approaches can be generalized to nonlinear optics using bright quantum light, which is expected to be much more powerful than conventional nonlinear optics using conventional laser.

14302121.label: Major findings and research outcome
14302121.value: (1) : We predicted the superradiant lasing of a quantum many-body emitter, i.e., emitters with coherent interactions between them, and theoretically propose a prototype quantum light source. The results show that superradiant lasing remains achievable even with interactions between emitters. The phase diagram of the system further reveals a lasing phase transition. Besides, coherent interactions between emitters induce a new bistable phase. In the lasing phase, the light is in a coherent state, giving a traditional coherent light source. In contrast, in the bistable phase, the light is in a number-phase squeezed state, giving a quantum light source. The work is under review in Physical Review Letters (Part C 8:3). (2) : We prove a polynomial complexity theorem for open quantum system (OQS) problems, that is, the number of independent equations required to fully describe the dynamics of an OQS increases at most linearly with the evolution time and polynomially with the bath size. Therefore, efficient computational algorithms exist for solving the dynamics of a small-sized OQS (such as a qubit or an atom). We further prove that, when the dynamics of an OQS and the bath is represented by a tensor network, a tensor contraction procedure can be specified such that the bond dimension increases only linearly (rather than exponentially) with the evolution time, providing explicitly efficient algorithms for a wide range of OQS’s. We demonstrate the theorems and the tensor-network algorithm by solving two widely encountered OQS problems, namely, a spin in a Gaussian bath (the spin-boson model) and a central spin coupled to many environmental spins (the Gaudin model). This work lays the foundation for understanding dynamics of OQS’s, for learning the environments via quantum sensors, and for optimizing quantum information processing in noisy environments. We have been invited to present the work in prestigious conferences (Part C 9:1-5) and the manuscript is under review in Physical Review X (Part C 8:4). (3): We establish a theory for quantum metrology using multimode bosonic systems with quadratic Hamiltonians. We show that the optimal quantum control to maximize sensitivity requires aligning squeezing and displacement in the same direction. We also propose an SP(2N,R) interferometry, which measures the applied phase with sensitivity set by the quantum Fisher information through imperfect echoes. This work is under review in Phys. Rev. Lett. (Part C 8:5).

14302121.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14302121.value: In conventional lasers, the emitters are mostly incoherent and have no coherent interaction, and consequently the lasing is virtually a “classical” amplification process. Thus, the photons satisfy the Gaussian statistics and have no irreducible many-body correlations. When the emitters are coherent and interact coherently with each other, quantum many-body light may be generated. In this project, we developed a theory for squeezed superraiant laser from many interacting emitters. We worked with experimentalists to discover new materials with ultra-long coherence time which can be good candidates for implementation of the schemes. To deal with the interaction of a central quantum system (such a laser mode) with many particles in the "environment" (such as many emitters), we developed a new quantum many-body approach to open quantum system problems, which reduce the original exponentially complex quantum many-body problems to a polynomially complex problem, the latter being numerically solvable. Based a globally interacting spin model coupled to a cavity mode, using exact numerical solution, mean-field approximation, and Fokker–Planck equation methods, we investigate the lasing conditions and photon statistics of a squeezed superradiant laser. The new generation of laser with quantum correlations may bring forth new approaches to quantum information technologies.

14302221.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14302221.value: The rates of many chemical reactions are dramatically altered when reactions occur near or away from water interfaces. The phenomenon in which a reaction is sped up at/near a water interface is called “on-water” catalysis. Numerous organic chemistry studies have shown that on-water catalysis can enhance reaction rates by up to several hundred times, compared to the rates of neat reactions or those performed in organic solvents. While on-water catalysis therefore enables access to simple, efficient reaction pathways for chemical synthesis, on-water catalysis is also known to affect many organic reactions at the interfaces of atmospheric aerosols, influencing the Earth system on large length scales. Although on-water catalysis has long been observed in certain reactions, the molecular-level understanding of this process remains limited. Recent advances in experimental techniques, such as surface-specific spectroscopies, have improved our understanding of the catalytic role of water interfaces. However, we still have a tremendous challenge to collect sufficient molecular details experimentally for mechanistic studies, because the fluctuations of a water interface are large when compared to the molecular length scales. Fortunately, increasing computing power and improved algorithms mean that molecular simulations can be important tools that reveal this critical molecular information. Ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) naturally has a quantum mechanical description of chemical bonds that enables the study of chemical reactions. Its high computational cost, however, severely limits the time and length scales accessible in AIMD simulations. Thus, we propose to (1) use enhanced sampling methods based on path variables to calculate the free energy profiles in AIMD and (2) utilize the resulting AIMD data to parameterize more efficient multi-scale reactive models and further enhance the speed of the calculations. These more efficient models will enable sufficient data to be collected, allowing us to perform reliable analyses of the converged free-energy profiles and rates of reactions involving on-water catalysis. Our proposed study will not only significantly improve the efficiency of modeling on-water catalysis, but also will provide some general simulation/modeling strategies for these systems. Armed with our experience and preliminary results, we are confident that this project will accomplish its objectives if funded. To help refine our models, we will ensure that our theoretical results are constantly tested against published experimental data. We seek to understand the relationship between water interfacial properties and on-water catalysis, elucidating their rates and mechanisms of this important catalytic process. 當反應發生在水界面附近或遠離水界​​面時，許多化學反應的速率會發生顯著變化。在水界面處或附近加速反應的現象稱為“水上”催化。許多有機化學研究表明，與純反應或在有機溶劑中進行的反應相比，水上催化可以將反應速率提高數百倍。因此，雖然水上催化能夠獲得簡單、有效的化學合成反應途徑，但水上催化會影響大氣氣溶膠界面處的許多有機反應，從而在宏觀上影響地球大氣系統。儘管在某些反應中早已觀察到水上催化，但對該過程的分子水平的理解仍然有限。實驗技術的最新進展，如表面特異性光譜，提高了我們對水界面催化作用的理解。然而，在實驗中獲得足夠的分子細節以進行研究依然存在著巨大挑戰，因為與分子長度尺度相比，水界面的波動很大。幸運的是，計算能力的提高和算法的改進意味著分子模擬可以成為揭示這一關鍵分子信息的重要工具。第一性原理分子動力學 (AIMD) 具有化學鍵的量子力學描述，可用於研究化學反應。然而，其高計算成本嚴重限制了 AIMD 模擬中可用的時間和空間尺度。因此，我們建議（1）使用基於路徑變量的增強採樣方法來計算AIMD 中的自由能分佈；（2）利用由此產生的AIMD 數據來參數化更有效的多尺度反應模型，並進一步提高計算速度。這些更有效的模型將能夠收集到足夠的數據，使我們能夠對收斂的自由能曲線和涉及水上催化的反應速率進行可靠的分析。我們提出的研究不僅將顯著提高水上催化建模的效率，而且還將為這些系統提供一些通用的建模和模擬策略。憑藉我們的經驗和初步結果，我們相信如果獲得資金，該項目將實現其目標。為了幫助改進我們的模型，我們將確保我們的理論結果不斷地根據已發表的實驗數據進行測試。我們試圖了解水界面性質與水上催化之間的關係，闡明它們在這一重要催化過程中的速率和機制。

14302221.label: Realisation of objectives
14302221.value: This project aimed to develop efficient, accurate multiscale models to understand how chemical reactions are accelerated "on water." Specifically, we sought to investigate how atmospheric reactions can be sped up (or slowed down) near the air-water interface of atmospheric droplets. Our focus was on modeling and understanding the atmospheric reaction between methyl chloride (CH₃Cl) and the hydroxyl radical (OH), a key process for removing CH₃Cl from the atmosphere. Four objectives were established and fully achieved. Summarized notes on these objectives are provided below. For the first objective, we examined a critical atmospheric reaction between methyl chloride (CH₃Cl) and the hydroxyl radical (OH), which facilitates the removal of methyl chloride from the atmosphere. Using high-level density-functional theory calculations and ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) to study the reaction in the gas phase with and without water molecules, we collected reference data necessary for parameterizing more efficient multiscale models that would allow converged free energy results. We note that we gained substantial experience modeling organic reactions and with applying quantum calculations from the studies with Prof. Yeung (publications 2 and 3: ACS Catalysis 2023, 13, 2386 & Synlett 2025, 36, 1059). Additionally, in these publications, our expertise in multiscale modeling and molecular dynamics helped us identify reasonable initial structures for the quantum calculations. For the second objective, we used the quantum reference data obtained in the first objective to parameterize the multiscale models, which are both accurate and efficient. These models enabled us to examine the atmospheric reaction within atmospheric droplets. Since our goal was to understand the reaction near the air-water interface through molecular dynamics, accurately modeling water compatible with our multiscale approach was essential. We achieved this by developing our in-house polarizable water model, SMW4/Fw (publication 1: JCTC 2022, 18, 7155). Our simulation setup closely matched the reference system, with a root-mean-square error of about 2 kJ/mol, within chemical accuracy. Importantly, our multiscale models facilitated simulations of condensed phases containing hundreds to thousands of water molecules. Using these efficient models, we completed the third objective by calculating the full free energy profiles and reaction rates in two condensed-phase environments: bulk liquid water and near the air-water interface. Using enhanced sampling techniques such as umbrella sampling and steered molecular dynamics, we obtained converged free energy profiles as a function of both distance from the interface and hydration level. From these profiles, we extracted activation barriers and reaction rates to understand the chemical kinetics in these environments. For the final objective, by comparing the reaction barriers, we established that the reaction intrinsically proceeds faster in water than in the gas phase, with a slight increase at the water surface. However, the differences in the barriers only partially explain the differences in the kinetics. Our simulations further indicate that CH₃Cl tends to reside at the air-water interface, forming an organic coating, while OH radicals are somewhat enriched at the surface as well. This results in significantly higher local concentrations of both reactants at the surface compared to the gas phase or the droplet interior. Therefore, the primary reason for the on-water catalysis is that the reactants accumulate at the surface, increasing the likelihood of encounters and reactions. These findings are summarized in our upcoming final paper (publication 4, in preparation).

14302221.label: Major findings and research outcome
14302221.value: This project has demonstrated how the reaction of methyl chloride (CH₃Cl) with hydroxyl radicals (OH), a major atmospheric sink for CH₃Cl, can be significantly accelerated at the air-water interface. The intrinsic reaction free energy barrier in bulk water is approximately 30-34 kJ/mol and is only slightly lowered at the interface (to about 29 kJ/mol). Therefore, the interface provides only a modest catalytic effect, primarily through small barrier reductions, aided in part by “water fingers” (hydrogen-bonded water chains) that stabilize the transition state. The dominant factor is that CH₃Cl strongly favors the air-water interface and accumulates there, while OH exhibits a weaker but still significant surface propensity. When these concentration increases are combined with the modest barrier reductions, the overall reaction rate at the interface exceeds that in bulk water by six orders of magnitude, and it surpasses the gas-phase rate by three orders of magnitude. Consequently, surface accumulation is identified as the main driver of the on-water catalysis studied. These results are summarized in our upcoming paper (publication 4, in preparation).

14302221.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14302221.value: Despite recent advances, simulation studies of chemical reactions near the air-water interface remain limited. While empirical valence bond (EVB) models can simulate these reactions, their parameterization poses significant challenges, particularly for research groups without prior experience. More general approaches, such as machine learning-based neural network potentials, may offer promising alternatives. Another area that requires further attention is the trade-off between the quality and quantity of reference data needed to model chemical reactions. There is usually an inverse relationship between the quality and amount of reference data, and finding a reasonable trade-off between the two is critical for future modeling efforts.

14302221.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14302221.value: We have demonstrated that our multiscale strategy is a reasonable method for studying on-water catalysis. We aimed to understand why certain atmospheric reactions can be accelerated at the air-water interface of atmospheric droplets. Our efficient and accurate models enabled us to collect converged results of the expensive free energy profiles, which can be used to determine reaction rates. Our findings show that the air-water interface can accumulate reactants, and the increased concentrations boost the overall reaction rate. Our strategy can be adopted to model other atmospheric reactions in the future.

14302421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14302421.value: Rock glaciers are important visible indicators for permafrost especially for regions such as the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau where in-situ observations are limited in spatial coverage due to the harsh and remote environment. A comprehensive inventory of rock glaciers on the plateau will serve as a valuable dataset for monitoring the degrading permafrost in one of the most sensitive areas to climatic warming. A few inventories of rock glaciers on the plateau at catchment to regional scales have been compiled mainly by manually delineating the landforms from remote sensing images. However, it is not feasible to merge the existing inventories into a comprehensive and systematic one for the following reasons: (1) the inventoried regions do not cover the entire plateau; (2) the criteria of mapping rock glaciers are inconsistent among different inventories; (3) individual inventories are not exhaustive. These limitations are imposed by the weakness of conventional labor-intensive methodology and the lack of widely accepted inventorying guidelines. To address these problems, a rock glacier inventory covering the entire plateau should be produced in an efficient and coherent manner. In order to ensure the quality of the dataset, the baseline concepts and guidelines lately established by the international rock glacier community will also be integrated into the mapping effort. The objectives of our proposed research include (1) to develop an automated, deep-learning-based method for mapping rock glaciers from remote sensing imagery and (2) to compile a comprehensive and standardized inventory of rock glaciers on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau. We will create a large and diverse training dataset based on the frontier geomorphological knowledge and by following the latest guidelines set by the intentional community. We will train a deep learning network for automatically delineating rock glaciers from optical images taken by Sentinel-2 and Planet CubeSat and quantify the mapping accuracy. We will apply the well-trained network to map rock glaciers over the entire permafrost region on the plateau from the Planet CubeSat images. We will also provide essential attributes to the mapped rock glaciers according to the standard guidelines. The well-trained deep learning network will be readily applied globally to other alpine permafrost regions where investigations of rock glaciers are scarce. The development of the automated method can be adopted in similar mapping tasks in geomorphology and cryospheric sciences. The rock glacier inventory will provide an essential reference for understanding permafrost on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau. 石冰川是廣泛分佈於全球山地冰緣範圍內的冰-岩混合地貌。它們是多年凍土的重要指 標。在青藏高原地區，由於環境惡劣和偏遠，現場觀測的空間覆蓋範圍有限，亟需一個全面的石冰川編目以輔助多年凍土環境及退化的研究和監測工作。 針對傳統人工識別方法耗時耗力及標準不一等缺點，本項目將開發一種基於深度學習技術，從Planet微衛星高分辨率影像上自動提取石冰川，從而生成一個覆蓋整個青藏高原多年凍土區域且遵循國際多年凍土協會標準的石冰川編目。 該工作將提供為研究中國山地冰凍圈的一個重要的基本信息，有助於未來長期監測和全區域評估多年凍土在氣候暖化下的變化。對深度學習技術的應用研究，以及在此基礎上形成的自動提取算法，可以應用到其他類似的地貌學及冰凍圈科學的研究中。

14302421.label: Realisation of objectives
14302421.value: This research project aimed to map rock glaciers on the Tibetan Plateau using deep-learning algorithms applied to high-resolution satellite imagery. All proposed research tasks have been completed, and the project objectives have been fully realized. Objective 1: To develop an automated, deep-learning-based method for mapping rock glaciers from optical remote sensing imagery We successfully developed a deep-learning-based method for delineating rock glaciers from satellite optical imagery. The approach leverages DeepLabv3+, one of the most advanced neural network architectures for semantic segmentation. The model was trained using Sentinel-2 and Planet Basemaps imagery, together with local inventories from six regions. Through fine-tuning, validation, and rigorous testing, the network achieved high accuracy in diverse mountain environments. This work demonstrates that deep-learning techniques can reliably detect and outline rock glaciers, providing a scalable and efficient solution for inventorying these landforms. For the first time, a systematic, automated approach was applied to generate rock glacier inventories in previously unmapped regions. This innovation significantly accelerates inventory production in a systematic and consistent manner and helps identify overlooked rock glaciers in areas with existing datasets. Objective 2: To compile a comprehensive and standardized inventory of rock glaciers on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau Building on the mapped outputs, we compiled TPRoGI, the most extensive rock glacier inventory to date, covering the Qinghai–Tibet Plateau. The dataset includes 44,273 rock glaciers, making it the largest global collection of its kind. This benchmark resource enhances understanding of rock glacier distribution and characteristics and provides a foundation for future research on mountain permafrost and climate change. In addition to the proposed objectives, this project achieved three new advancements. 1. We designed a novel radar remote sensing framework for large-scale assessment of rock glacier velocities, integrating multi-temporal and multi-geometry SAR data. This approach enables rapid and systematic generation of velocity fields, overcoming previous limitations in spatial coverage and consistency. Using this framework, we produced the first large-scale regional rock glacier velocity dataset, encompassing downslope velocity fields for 19,727 rock glaciers across the Tibetan Plateau. 2. Building on our deep-learning mapping approach, we extended its application to quantify rock glacier water storage across the entire High Mountain Asia region—a first in global research. This comprehensive evaluation provides critical insights into the hydrological significance of rock glaciers in water-scarce mountains. 3. Our work supported the formal recognition of rock glacier velocities as an Essential Climate Variable for permafrost in 2022. Furthermore, we synthesized knowledge on rock glacier kinematics across multiple timescales, clarifying the scientific relevance of interannual velocity observations and their role in climate-driven research.

14302421.label: Major findings and research outcome
14302421.value: The project has generated a series of scientific outputs, including five journal papers on rock glaciers of the Qinghai–Tibet Plateau, two papers on glacial lakes mapped using the developed deep-learning methods, three associated datasets, and one Ph.D. dissertation. Detailed citations and full texts are provided in Part C. Below is a summary of the major findings reported in the five rock glacier papers. Hu et al. (JGR, 2023) mapped and quantified the kinematics of active rock glaciers using satellite Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR). We trained a DeepLabv3+ neural network for automated mapping from Sentinel-2 imagery, enabling extensive delineation of previously unmapped landforms. The study identified 413 rock glaciers in the Western Kunlun Mountains, providing a dataset for research on geohazards, water resources, and permafrost change. Hu et al. (The Cryosphere, 2023) assessed the potential water storage of rock glaciers in Khumbu Valley, Nepal, using a velocity-constrained rheological model based on Glen’s flow law and InSAR-derived velocities. Results indicate an average ice fraction of ~71%, suggesting rock glaciers across the Nepalese Himalayas store ~10 billion m³ of water, underscoring their hydrological importance. Zhang et al. (Earth System Science Data, 2024) compiled a comprehensive inventory of rock glaciers for the Tibetan Plateau. This inventory consists of a total of 44 273 rock glaciers and reveals that rock glaciers are concentrated in the Western Pamir and Nyainqêntanglha ranges, with sparse distribution in the inner plateau. Zhang et al. (International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation, 2025) developed a multi-temporal, multi-geometry InSAR framework for large-scale velocity assessment, producing the first regional velocity dataset for 19,727 rock glaciers in the Tibet–Pamir–Karakoram region. Rock glaciers in the westerlies domain move faster than those in the monsoon domain, revealing climatic controls on dynamics. Hu et al., Review of Geophysics, 2025: This review synthesized knowledge on rock glacier kinematics across multiple timescales, to support the formal recognition of rock glacier velocities as an Essential Climate Variable for permafrost. It clarified the scientific relevance of interannual velocity observations and their role in climate-driven research.

14302421.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14302421.value: (1) Enhance Deep-Learning-Based Mapping: Future work will focus on improving model accuracy and reducing manual post-processing by integrating multi-source satellite imagery, refining training labels, and adopting state-of-the-art neural architectures. Combining open-access imagery with standardized inventories will enable a scalable, automated mapping pipeline, accelerating global rock glacier inventory generation and supporting periglacial monitoring. (2) Develop rock glacier velocity assessment methods: We will develop methodologies that integrate multi-frequency InSAR, repeat aerial photogrammetry, and ground-based surveys for robust velocity estimation. Our framework is transferable worldwide, facilitating large-scale velocity assessments, improving hydrological modeling, refining permafrost simulations, and supporting hazard risk evaluations in high-mountain regions. (3) Investigate environmental controls on rock glacier velocities: Building on observed contrasts in velocity patterns across climatic domains, future research will employ statistical and machine-learning models to quantify environmental drivers of rock glacier dynamics. This will provide critical insights into climate–topography interactions, enhancing predictions of rock glacier behavior under changing environmental conditions.

14302421.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14302421.value: Rock glaciers are frozen landforms that act as visible indicators of permafrost. They are especially important on the vast and remote Qinghai–Tibet Plateau, where direct field measurements are scarce. Understanding rock glaciers helps scientists monitor permafrost changes, assess water resources, and evaluate natural hazards such as slope instability. This project developed an innovative deep-learning approach to automatically map rock glaciers using satellite imagery. Using this method, we compiled TPRoGI, the first comprehensive rock glacier inventory for the Qinghai–Tibet Plateau. The dataset includes 44,273 rock glaciers, making it the largest of its kind worldwide. These landforms are concentrated in the Western Pamir and Nyainqêntanglha ranges, with fewer in the inner plateau. The publicly available dataset fills a major knowledge gap on periglacial landforms in China and provides a foundation for permafrost research, climate monitoring, and hazard assessment. It will help scientists estimate permafrost extent and support long-term studies of how rock glaciers respond to climate change. Beyond science, this work informs water resource planning and risk management for communities in high-mountain regions, contributing to sustainable development in fragile environments.

14302921.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14302921.value: McKean-Vlasov最優控製問題是由最近對大規模群體的控製問題的研究得到的。在這個理論裏面，群體數量的規模很大，但在一定時間範圍內一直是固定的。在該研究計劃裏，我們將在控製問題裏引入關於群體數量的動態過程（例如分枝/聚合過程）以模擬群體中的死亡、出生、融合等現象。這樣便得到一個群體數量動態化下的隨機控製問題。我們將主要研究兩個問題。第一個是分支/融合的McKean-Vlasov控製問題。我們將使用動態規劃的方法得到刻畫問題的大師方程以及相應的數值方法。第二個是條件隨機控製問題以及它的長時間平均表現。當時間跨度趨於無窮時，它的長時間平均表現將變成一個條件遍歷控製問題。最後，我們將研究這個理論在生物、防疫以及經濟中的應用。一個比較現實的應用將是在一個用分支過程模擬的流行病防治模擬中，如何製定最優的疫苗推廣策略。

14302921.label: Realisation of objectives
14302921.value: For Objective 1, we established the well-posedness of the mean-field branching stochastic differential equation and then investigated the associated control problem using the dynamic programming approach, together with the analysis of its master equation. For Objective 2, we examined an optimal control problem under partial observation, in which the decision maker acts based on the conditional law of the state process given the observable process. For Objective 3, we focused on the discrete-time approximation of the control problem, which constitutes an essential first step toward numerical implementation. In particular, it provides a numerical method in the one-dimensional setting. Finally, for Objective 4, we studied the regularity of the relevant PDEs and explored applications of several closely related results to the optimal planning problem in mean-field games. Unfortunately, in the publication "Z. Ren, X. Tan, N. Touzi and J. Yang, Entropic optimal planning for path-dependent mean field games, SIAM Journal on Control and Optimization, 61(3):1415-1437, 2023", we forgot to acknowledge the support of this grant in the published version of the paper. We nevertheless added the acknowledgment on the arXiv version of the paper (https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.07019).
