14302921.label: Major findings and research outcome
14302921.value: 1. We rigorously proved that the mean-field branching diffusion SDEs (stochastic differential equations) have a unique solution under some technical conditions. 2. We introduced an optimal control problem of the branching diffusion processes, characterized the value function as solution to the HJB master equation and then provided a verification theorem. 3. We studied the discrete-time approximation of some optimal control problem, which leads to some first numerical approximation algorithms.

14302921.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14302921.value: The controlled branching processes problem has potential applications in the unbalanced optimal transport problem, which is motivated by applications in modern machine learning algorithms. We will try to develop these applications in our future research projects.

14302921.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14302921.value: This project lies in the field of applied mathematics and aims to provide a rigorous mathematical analysis of optimal control problems of the particle systems with dynamically evolving population sizes. It introduces a novel class of control problems and establishes several fundamental properties, including the well-posedness of the branching SDE, the dynamic programming principle, the associated HJB equations, and discrete-time numerical approximations. These results lay a solid mathematical foundation for the model and support its potential future applications.

14303021.label: Project Objectives
14303021.value: It is proposed to study the local geometric structure of self-affine sets. We aim to investigate the geometric properties of tangent sets and micro-sets of general self-affine sets, and apply them to analyze the arithmetic sums and embedding properties of self-affine fractals. 14303021.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14303021.value: Self-affine sets and measures are among the most interesting fractal objects. They are generated from a finite set of contracting affine transformations. By repeatedly iterating these transformations, we obtain a fractal set, which is called a self-affine set. When we assign a probability measure in the iteration, we get a self-affine measure. Although their generating schemes are quite simple, this class of sets and measures have a highly irregular geometric structure. So far, self-affine sets and measures have been broadly used by scientists and engineers to describe the irregularity, complexity and distributions of various geometric shapes in the nature. In the last three decades, they have also attracted great interest from many branches of mathematics, such as geometric measure theory, dynamical systems, number theory and probability. In this project, we aim to study the local geometry and multifractal structure of self-affine sets and measures. In one direction, we plan to investigate the geometric structure of limiting sets generated from the ``zooming-in'' dynamics on self-affine sets, and try to apply it to the study of arithmetic sums and embedding properties of self-affine sets. In the other direction, we will conduct the multifractal analysis of self-affine measures, in which we will study the fine geometry and scaling laws of these measures. The proposed problems are only well or partially understood in some special cases (e.g. Bedford-McMullen self-affine carpets). We will focus on the study for more general self-affine sets and measures. This research will deepen our understanding of the fine geometry and dimensional theory of non-conformal fractal objects. 自仿射集合與測度是最有趣的分形對象之一。它們由一組有限的收縮仿射變換所生成。通過反复迭代這些變換，我們得到一個分形集合，稱為自仿射集。當我們在迭代中分配相應的概率時，我們得到一個自仿射測度。雖然其生成方案很簡單，但這類集合與測度通常具有高度不規則的幾何結構。目前自仿射集合與測度已經被科學家和工程師廣泛用於描述自然界中諸多複雜而不規則的幾何形狀。在過去的三十多年裡，它們也引起了許多數學分支的極大興趣，例如幾何測度論、動力系統、數論和概率。在這個項目中，我們的目標是研究自仿射集合與測度的局部幾何和多重分形結構。一方面，我們計劃研究自仿射集合上的“局部放大”動態系統及所生成的極限集的幾何結構，並嘗試將其應用於自仿射集的算術和及嵌入特性等問題的研究。另一方面，我們將研究一般自仿射測度的重分形結構。這項研究將加深我們對非共形分形對象局部幾何與維數的理解。

14303021.label: Realisation of objectives
14303021.value: It is a fundamental and challenging problem in fractal geometry and dynamical systems to study the local geometry and dimensional properties of self-affine sets and measures. These family of fractal objects are very different from self-similar fractals, since they have different contraction ratios along different directions. In this project, we determine the various dimensions of a large class of Borel subsets of typical self-affine sets, corresponding to the projections of all Borel subsets of the symbolic space under the coding map associated with the self-affine systems. Moreover, we establish the dimensions of the pushforward of Borel measures on the symbolic space under the coding map. In particular, we provide a necessary and sufficient condition for these pushforward measures to be exact dimensional. These results significantly extend the important work on the dimension theory of typical self-affine sets and invariant measures developed by Falconer and Jordan–Pollicott–Simon. In addition to adopting and extending the transversality methods used for orthogonal projections and self-affine fractals, we also develop new techniques to analyze the covering properties of the projections of sets and measures under the coding maps. We also conduct a multifractal analysis of typical diagonal self-affine measures in the plane and in higher dimensions. In particular, we determine the Lq-spectrum of these measures for q∈(0,1) for almost all translation vectors. Moreover, we verify the validity of the multifractal formalism for these measures on the same range of q. Our approach combines tools from convex analysis and dynamical systems. In addition, we obtain an interesting relationship between the two commonly used separation conditions—namely, the strong separation condition and the open set condition—for self-similar iterated function systems, which partially answers an open question raised by Urbański nearly 20 years ago.

14303021.label: Major findings and research outcome
14303021.value: In [1], we investigate various dimensions of projected sets and measures on typical self-affine sets under the coding maps. For a translational family of affine iterated function systems, under mild assumptions on the norms of the linear part of the IFSs, we show that, for every given Borel subset of the coding space, the various dimensions (Hausdorr, packing, upper and lower dimensions) of its projection under the coding map are constant for almost all translation parameters. Similarly, for a Borel probability measure on the coding space, we show that the Hausdorff and packing dimensions of its projection under the coding map are constant for almost all translation parameters. This work extends widely the previous results of Falconer (1988) and Jordan-Pollicott-Simon (2007) on the projections of invariant sets and invariant measures on typical self-affine sets under the coding maps. In [2], we investigate the relationship between two commonly used separation conditions—namely, the strong separation condition and the open set condition—for iterated function systems. Let E be a self-similar set generated by a homogeneous iterated function system of similitudes in Rn. Suppose this IFS satisfies the open set condition but not the strong separation condition. We show that E cannot be generated by any other iterated function system that satisfies the strong separation condition. This result partially answers a longstanding folklore question concerning the separation conditions for generating iterated function systems of self-similar sets. In [3], we conduct the multifractal analysis of typical diagonal self-affine measures in the plane and higher dimensions. We determine explicitly the L^q-spactrum of these measures for the range of q in (0,1) for almost all translation vectors. Moreover, we verify the validity of the multifractal formalism in this range of q.

14303321.label: Project Objectives
14303321.value: To study different issues of the spatially homogeneous Boltzmann equation for uniform shear flow, particularly including: (a) to explore the negative power law of the large velocity tail of solutions; (b) to prove the existence and large time asymptotics of infinite energy solutions in the case of Maxwell molecules without angular cutoff; (c) to discuss the existence and large time behavior of solutions for other collision models. To study the stability/instability of kinetic shear flow in the perturbation framework for the spatially inhomogeneous Boltzmann equation with a small shear rate in a two-dimensional channel domain either infinite or finite, and further establish the hydrodynamic or free molecule limit in the incompressible setting.

14303321.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14303321.value: This project is concerned with quantitative and qualitative properties of a spatially homogeneous non-Maxwellian state that is governed by the Boltzmann equation for the Maxwell molecule gas under the effect of a linear shearing force. Such state is also called a homoenergetic solution introduced independently by Truesdell and Galkin. In fact, there exist many kinds of homoenergetic solutions when the translation of velocity is a time-dependent affine transformation of space variables. The discovery of those formally exact solutions is significantly important in the numerical and theoretical study of nonequilibrium phenomena in kinetic theory. We mainly focus on the uniform or simple shear flow in the two dimensional setting corresponding to a macroscopic shearing velocity whose horizontal component is linear along the vertical direction. An important feature of the uniform shear flow is that the velocity distribution function behaves self-similar in large time with an exponentially growing temperature, and the self-similar profile is far from equilibrium with a polynomial tail in large velocity for any non-zero shear rate. The specific goal of this project is to study the global existence, shear-rate-dependence and large time stability of uniform shear flow solutions in the spatially homogeneous framework for situations where the initial energy is infinite, the angular part of the collision kernel is singular, the intermolecular interaction changes to hard potentials, or other collisional kinetic models are used to replace the Boltzmann operator. More importantly, we expect to further study the asymptotic stability of uniform shear flow over a two-dimensional channel domain in the spatially inhomogeneous setting. Quite few such results are known in kinetic theory so far, even though there have been extensive mathematical works on the same research topic for the Couette flow in the field of fluid dynamical equations. A more challenging task is to construct the approximation solution uniform in shear rate in the fluid limit or in the weakly collisional limit. Since many kinetic simple flows with the effect of boundaries are fundamental physical problems describing the nonequilibrium motion of a rarefied gas, we expect the current project to develop and enhance basic mathematical understandings of existence and stability in the context of uniform shear flow. 該項目是關於在線性剪切力作用下由麥克斯韋分子氣體的玻爾茲曼方程控制的空間均勻的非麥克斯韋狀態的定量和定性的性質。這種狀態也稱為同能解，由 Truesdell 和 Galkin 獨立引入。事實上，當速度的平移是空間變量的時間依賴的仿射變換時，存在多種同能解。這些形式上的精確解的發現對於動力學理論中非平衡現象的數值和理論研究非常重要。我們主要關註二維情形下的均勻或簡單剪切流，對應於宏觀剪切速度的水平分量沿垂直方向是線性的。均勻剪切流的一個重要特徵是速度分佈函數隨著溫度呈指數增長而在長時間內表現出自相似性，並且對於任何非零剪切力，自相似分佈遠離平衡態，在大速度下呈現出多項式衰減。 該項目的具體目標是在初始能量無窮大，碰撞核有角奇異，分子間相互作用變為硬勢或其他碰撞動力學模型代替玻爾茲曼算子等情況下研究空間均勻框架中均勻剪切流解的全局存在性、剪切速率依賴性和大時間穩定性。更重要的是，我們希望進一步研究空間非均勻環境中二維通道域上均勻剪切流的漸近穩定性。儘管在流體動力學方程領域中對於Couette流的同一研究課題已經有大量的數學工作，然而迄今為止，在動力學理論中很少有這樣的結果。一個更具挑戰性的任務是在流體極限或弱碰撞極限下構造均勻剪切分佈的近似解。由於許多具有邊界效應的動力學簡單流動是描述稀薄氣體非平衡運動的基本物理問題，我們希望當前的項目能夠發展和加強對均勻剪切流背景下存在性和穩定性的基本數學理解。

14303321.label: Realisation of objectives
14303321.value: In the project we have made extensive studies of kinetic shear flow governed by the nonlinear Boltzmann equation and provided essential results in understanding the subject in connection with the objectives of the current project. The project produces 8 research outputs among which two are under review and one is under preparation. In what follows, we present our main achievements. The problems proposed in the first objective have been fully resolved with our research outputs Papers 1, 2, 4, 7 and 8: (Paper 1) With Shuangqian Liu: Uniform shear flow via the Boltzmann equation with hard potentials, Discrete and Continuous Dynamical Systems, 45 (2025), no. 10, 4071-4118. (Paper 2) With Zongguang Li and Shuangqian Liu: Global mild solution with polynomial tail for the Boltzmann equation in the whole space, arXiv.2212.04676. (Paper 4) With Chuqi Cao and Zongguang Li: Time-velocity decay of solutions to the non-cutoff Boltzmann equation in the whole space, Communications in Mathematical Analysis and Applications, 3 (2024), no. 1, 61-120. (Paper 7) With Jose A. Carrillo, Kam Fai Chan and Zongguang Li: Inelastic Boltzmann equation under shear heating, to appear in Kinetic and Related Models. (Paper 8) With Shuaikun Wang: Infinite energy solutions to the non-cutoff Boltzmann equation with deformations, in progress. We further explain how those objectives have been resolved. First of all, in order to treat (a), we have developed the Hilbert method in Paper 1 for studying the sheared Boltzmann equation in case of hard potentials. In our previous work (ARMA 2021) that originally motivated the current project, we solved the problem for the Maxwell molecule model. In that case, the solution tends self-similarly toward the non-Maxwellian profile which decays polynomially in large velocities. For the hard potentials indicating that the Boltzmann collisions are more dominated, the self-similar asymptotic profile has to be Maxwellian and thus decay exponentially in large velocities. The problem (b) has been treated in the recent work Paper 8 that has been still under preparation. In this work, we study the spatially homogeneous Boltzmann equation for Maxwell molecule interactions without angular cutoff in the presence of a linear deformation force described by a matrix. We prove that there exists a unique global-in-time measure-valued solution to the Cauchy problem for initial data allowing infinite energy and further that the solution is smooth at any positive time if initially it is not a single Dirac measure. Moreover, we obtain the self-similar asymptotic behavior of those infinite energy solutions under a suitable scaling. In particular, we establish the existence of a self-similar profile with infinite energy and also justify both weak and strong convergence to the self-similar profile with an exponential rate. For the problem (c) on other types of collisions, we mainly focus on the inelastic Boltzmann model, confirming the competition between shear heating and inelastic cooling that governs the large time behavior of temperature. Specifically, temperature increases to infinity if shear heating dominates, decreases to zero if inelastic cooling prevails, and converges to a positive constant if the two effects are balanced. In the balanced scenario, the corresponding self-similar profile aligns with the steady solution. Our studies in Paper 2 and Paper 4 play an important role in understanding the stability analysis of solutions with polynomial tails in large velocities in the framework of spatially inhomogeneous domain, in particular, the whole space without any boundary. With these two works, we expect to further study the asymptotic stability of homoenergetic solutions in the spatially inhomogeneous setting where the temperature of the system may grow to infinity at infinite time. This direction certainly would be able to create a completely new research project. The problems proposed in the second objective have been fully resolved with our research work Papers 3, 5 and 6: (Paper 3) With Shuangqian Liu, Robert M. Strain, and Anita Yang: The 3D kinetic Couette flow via the Boltzmann equation in the diffusive limit, arXiv.2409.00311. (Paper 5) With Hongxu Chen and Junhao Zhang: Global dynamics of isothermal rarefied gas flows in an infinite layer, Mathematische Annalen, 393 (2025), no. 1, 831-922. (Paper 6) With Hongxu Chen: Boltzmann equation with mixed boundary condition, SIAM Journal on Mathematical Analysis, 57 (2025), no. 3, 3297-3334. In Paper 3, we completely solved our problem. Precisely, we concern a Boltzmann theory for the 3D kinetic Couette flow describing the motion of a rarefied gas confined by two parallel infinite plates moving tangentially relative to each other with opposite velocities. We focus on the Boltzmann equation in the diffusive limit in a 3D periodic channel domain with the diffusive reflection boundary condition imposed on the plates and an external force present. Using a perturbation approach, we establish existence of the stationary solution to the steady problem and further obtain the exponential asymptotic stability for the time-dependent problem near the obtained stationary 3D kinetic Couette flow. The result implies that the first order approximation of the Boltzmann solutions for small Knudsen numbers is determined by the perturbed incompressible Navier-Stokes-Fourier system with the external force around the Couette flow in fluid dynamics. A key feature of our approach is to construct solutions in the Lagrangian frame with the bulk velocity for the fluid Couette flow connecting the same velocities of two moving plates and as such a shearing force appears to make solutions have only the polynomial tail in large velocities. In contrast to the finite channel domain, the problem in case of the infinite layer domain is much more difficult because the non-compactness of the domain implies that the solution admits the diffusive behavior in large time and thus decays polynomially in large time as the same rate of solutions to the heat equation along the tangent direction. In Papers 5 and 6, we mainly study such problem when the shearing effect is absent. Extension of those results to the case of including an additional boundary shearing effect is expected to be further justified and being under our preparation as a completely new project.

14303321.label: Major findings and research outcome
14303321.value: In Paper 1, we study the uniform shear flow via the Boltzmann equation in case of hard potentials. We prove the global existence and large time behavior of solutions provided that the shear strength is small enough. In Paper 2, we study the Cauchy problem on the Boltzmann equation in the whole space. The goal is to construct global-in-time bounded mild solutions near Maxwellians with the perturbation admitting a polynomial tail in large velocities. The full range of both hard and soft potentials with cutoff can be covered. This provides the first result on the construction of slow-decaying solutions when the spatial domain is unbounded. In Paper 3, we study the Boltzmann equation in the diffusive limit in a finite channel for the 3D kinetic Couette flow. Our results demonstrate that the first-order approximation of the solution is governed by the perturbed incompressible Navier-Stokes-Fourier system around the fluid Couette flow. Moreover, in the absence of external forces, the 3D kinetic Couette flow asymptotically converges over time to the 1D steady planar kinetic Couette flow. In Paper 4, we consider the perturbed solutions with polynomial tail in large velocities for the non-cutoff Boltzmann equation near global Maxwellians in the whole space. The global in time existence is proved in the weighted Sobolev spaces and the almost optimal time decay is obtained in Fourier transform based low-regularity spaces. The result shows a time-velocity decay structure of solutions. In Paper 5, we study the Boltzmann equation in an infinite layer with diffusely reflecting boundaries that are isothermal and non-moving. We establish the global-in-time dynamics of such rarefied gas flows near global Maxwellians. This is the first result on the Boltzmann equation with non-compact and diffuse boundaries. In Paper 6, we study the Boltzmann equation in a smooth bounded domain featuring a mixed boundary condition, that's partially specular and partially diffuse reflective. Our main focus is on constructing global-in-time small-amplitude solutions around global Maxwellians for the corresponding initial-boundary value problem. In Paper 7, we study the spatially homogeneous inelastic Boltzmann equation for Maxwell molecules with linear deformation. We establish existence and stability of non-Maxwellian self-similar profiles with small deformation in the nearly elastic regime, and also obtain weak convergence to these self-similar profiles. This confirms the competition between shear heating and inelastic cooling. In Paper 8, we construct the infinite-energy self-similar solutions to the non-cutoff Boltzmann equation and establish their asymptotic stability.

14303321.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14303321.value: The current project has motivated several completely new directions that the PI would keep working on in the future. First of all, the homoenergetic solutions have been well understood in the spatially homogeneous setting. It remains open to treat their asymptotic stability in the spatially inhomogeneous framework. The main trouble arises from the divergence of temperature at infinite time. Second, inspired by series of works by Kagei at the fluid level, it is very interesting to develop an analogous stability theory for the Boltzmann equation in an infinite layer with the boundary shear moving effect. Third, regarding the kinetic shear flow, all the current results are based on an essential assumption that the shear strength is small enough. However, for the classical fluid equations such as Euler or Navier-Stokes, the shear strength is of order one. Indeed, the shear of order one is able to provide an enhanced dissipation. Therefore, it is quite interesting to develop the kinetic shear flow for a general shear which does not need to be small.

14303421.label: Project Objectives
14303421.value: SPECIFIC AIM 1: Engineering Cry3Aa crystals to improve their use for the delivery of non-covalently bound AMPs to treat intromacrophage infections. Previous studies by our laboratory have shown that Cry3Aa crystals are effective vehicles for the delivery of antimicrobial peptides to leishmania-infected macrophages as evidenced by the dramatically improved therapeutic index. In this aim, we would like to improve this technology by exploiting one of its key features, the ability to use molecular biology to produce engineered Cry3Aa crystals with enhanced functional properties. In this case, we will characterize the AMP binding and release properties of two highly negatively charged Cry3Aa crystals, Neg3Aa and Neg26C, that have been designed to exhibit tighter AMP binding. The most promising construct with then be used to produce the corresponding AMP-loaded crystal which will then be delivered leishmania infected macrophages to evaluate its anti-amastigote activity. If this is successful, we will also explore the coexpression of Cry3Aa and AMPs to see if it is possible to directly produce AMP-loaded Cry3Aa crystals in Bacillus thuringiensis. If successful, it would greatly reduce the cost of the therapeutic and open up other avenues of study. SPECIFIC AIM 2: Exploring Cry3Aa-AMP fusion crystals as anti-leishmanial agents. This aim will focus on exploring the delivery of crystals comprised of Cry3Aa genetically-fused to an AMP. It capitalizes on one of the major strengths of the Cry3Aa crystal framework – the ability to directly generate the AMP as part of the Cry3Aa crystal delivery system, with the AMP's fusion to Cry3Aa protein abrogating its natural antimicrobial activity. It also avoids the possible undesired release of the AMP from the crystal following intravenous injection. The key challenge, however, is how to elicit release of the AMP once the Cry3Aa-AMP fusion crystals are inside the macrophage. Two strategies will be explored to test this. In the first intein-based strategy, intein linkers will be incorporated between the Cry3Aa and AMP polypeptides that can be activated by thiols or low pH. In the second prodrug approach, the cleavage sequence the essential lysosomal protease cathepsin D will be added to the linker between Cry3Aa and AMP. The therapeutic effectiveness of the resulting Cry3Aa-AMP fusion crystals will be tested in cell culture. Solubilizing Cry3Aa mutants and the addition of multiple AMP repeats can be explored to further improve the anti-leishmanial activity of the most promising constructs. SPECIFIC AIM 3: Evaluating the effectiveness of engineered Cry3Aa-AMP constructs for the treatment of leishmaniasis in vivo. Once the best constructs from Specific Aims 1 & 2 have been identified from cell culture, we plan to test them in mice. Two leishmania mouse-infection models will be utilized. A mouse footpad model for cutaneous leishmaniasis will be used to evaluate the effectiveness of the Cry3Aa-AMP constructs against L. amazonesis, while a visceral leishmaniasis mouse model will be used for the treatment of infections by L. donovani. The outcome of these studies will provide insight into the potential of these therapeutics for the treatment of leishmanial infections in higher animals such as dogs and humans.

14303421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14303421.value: Most pathogens in the human body are engulfed and killed by phagocytes (i.e. macrophages and neutrophils). Intracellular pathogens, such as Leishmania, however, can survive and replicate within macrophages (their natural niche). Killing such intracellular pathogens is challenging due to multiple physiological barriers that hinder the ability of traditional drugs to reach the target site. Antimicrobial peptides currently attract high interest due to their diverse potential applications, rapid action and low likelihood of resistance, but their instability and nonspecific activity limit their clinical application. We have recently reported a novel protein delivery system based on Cry protein crystals that are readily taken up by macrophages, and demonstrated their use as delivery agents to improve the therapeutic effectiveness of antimicrobial peptides known to kill leishmania. In this proposal, we exploit the fact that Cry3Aa crystals are comprised of a genetically-encoded protein to engineer specific properties such increased charge, explore the genetic fusion of the antimicrobial peptide to the Cry3Aa protein, and genetically-encode sites of specific protease cleavage sites. We hope to demonstrate that the delivery of antimicrobial peptides using these engineered Cry3Aa crystals will lead to dramatic improvements in their therapeutic effectiveness against leishmaniasis. 人體內的大多數病原體會被吞噬細胞（如巨噬細胞和中性粒細胞）吞噬並殺死。然而，細胞內病原體，如利什曼原蟲，可以在它們天然的寄生部位巨噬細胞內存活和復制。由於多層生理上的屏障阻礙了傳統藥物到達目的部位的能力，殺死此類細胞內病原體具​​有相當的挑戰性。抗菌肽目前因其潛在的多樣化應用、快速作用和低耐藥性而引起高度關注，但它們的不穩定性和非特異性活性限制了它們的臨床應用。最近我們報導了一種基於 Cry 蛋白晶體的新型蛋白質遞送系統，該系統能很容易地被巨噬細胞吞噬。我們證明了用它們作為藥物載體可以提高具有抗利什曼原蟲活性的抗菌肽的治療效果。在此研究計畫中，我們利用Cry3Aa 晶體是完全由基因編碼的蛋白質組成這一優勢來設計特定的性質，例如增強帶電性，探索抗菌肽與 Cry3Aa 的融合蛋白，以及引入特定的蛋白酶切割位點。 我們希望證明使用這些工程化的 Cry3Aa 晶體遞送抗菌肽將顯著提高它們對利什曼病的治療效果。

14303421.label: Realisation of objectives
14303421.value: All of the objectives have been performed, and in the end we have achieved our ultimate goal - the generation of a functional construct based on Cry-mediated delivery of an AMP that can be used to treat visceral leishmaniasis in a mouse model. Specific Aim 1: For this aim, we explored the ability of new Cry3Aa constructs, two more negatively charged variants Neg3Aa, and Neg26C, and a pH-responsive construct Cry3AD2His, to bind to three AMPs - (1) melittin, the main component of bee venom; (2) MM-2, a less hemolytic variant of melittin, and (3) RI-1018, an anti-leishmanial peptide with low hemolytic activity that had been reported in the literature. Each of the different Cry constructs was prepared, purified and characterized by TEM to confirm their size and morphology. Once their proper formation was confirmed, their ability to be taken up by RAW264.7 cells was evaluated, and their cytotoxicity determined. Cry3Aa, Neg3Aa, and Neg26C crystals showed good uptake into macrophages, but surprisingly, Cry3AD2His crystals did not. The IC50 of Cry3Aa, Neg3Aa, Neg26c and Cry3AD2His were 0.6 uM, 0.8 uM, 0.7 uM and 0.5 uM respectively. The affinity of the different AMPs to crystals of Cry3Aa, Neg3Aa, and Neg26C was evaluated by gel electrophoresis of the pellet and supernatant. As expected, the positively charged melittin and MM-2 peptides were found to bind to each of the crystals, with binding to Neg26C being observed to be the tightest. The RI-1018 peptide, however, showed only modest affinity to the Neg26C crystal. The cytotoxicity and hemolytic activity of the soluble peptides, and peptides bound to crystal were then determined. IC50 of Melittin, MM-2, and RI-1018 peptide were 1.17, 16, and >20uM respectively. Melittin exhibited high RBC hemolytic activity, while MM-2 showed no hemolytic activity at the concentrations tested, and RI-1018 only at 50 uM. We then tested the ability of the peptide-loaded crystal constructs to treat Leishmania infected macrophages. The melittin-loaded constructs were ineffective, mainly because they were too toxic to the macrophages. Both MM-2-loaded Neg3Aa and Neg26C crystals, as well as RI-1018 loaded Neg26C crystals were shown to effective at treating Leishmania infected macrophages at 8 uM concentration, but this concentration is fairly high and so we focused on our further efforts on developing Cry3Aa-melittin fusion constructs capable of the targeted delivery of the AMP to the macrophage (Specific Aim 2) - hoping that Cry3Aa-entrapment could mitigate its toxicity. Specific Aim 2: This aim focused on the production and delivery of Cry3Aa to the target AMP. The advantage of this approach was that the AMP is directly produced as part of the construct greatly reducing the cost of the AMP. For these studies, we chose to genetically fuse melittin as well as its naturally inactive precursor promelittin (PMLT). The direct fusions were prepared, purified and characterized, but when the constructs were tested against Leishmania infected macrophages, they were found to be inactive. Then following the proposed plan, we tested different linkers to see if they could be used to alter the release of the AMP in the macrophage and thereby enhance its effectiveness. In one design we incorporated an LPXTG site within the Cry3Aa-PMLT crystal with the idea of co-delivering sortase to mediate the release of melittin from the crystal. Unexpectedly, we found that crystals of this modified Cry3Aa-mPMLT construct were also effective at treating Leishmania-infected macrophages in cell culture without further addition of sortase. We hypothesized that incorporation of the LPETG sequence provided a preferential cleavage site for cathepsin D/E, promoting its cleavage and release of the melittin within the lysosome - the site where intracellular leishmanial amastagotes reside. This was confirmed by co-delivering pepstatin A, a general inhibitor of lysosomal aspartic proteases, such as cathepsin D/E, resulting in loss of the ability of the modified Cry3Aa-mPMLT crystals to kill the amastigotes in the Leishmania infected amastagotes. We also tested the toxicity of the Cry3Aa-mPMLT crystals, and showed that Cry3Aa-fusion abrogated both the cellular toxicity against macrophages as well as the hemolysis of RBCs suggesting that had potential as a therapeutic for in vivo studies. Given its excellent properties, we thus selected this construct for further in vivo studies (Specific Aim 3). Specific Aim 3: We performed in vivo studies of Leishmania infected mice using Cry3Aa-mPMLT crystal using both the footpad and visceral mouse models. Treatment of mice infected with Leishmania amazonensis with Cry3Aa-mPMLT crystal in the mouse footpad model showed reduction in the levels of leishmania infection. We subsequently tested this construct using a visceral model of leishmaniasis using mice whose had been infected with Leishmania donovani. Here too we showed that mice treated by tail vein injections with Cry3Aa-PMLT* crystals showed reduced infection levels. In vivo acute toxicity studies of Cry3Aa-mPMLT were also performed and showed no evidence of toxicity based on body weight, organ index, or serum ALT/AST activity or creatine levels. These data suggest that Cry3Aa-mPMLT crystals have potential as a therapeutic for the treatment of leishmanial diseases.

14303421.label: Major findings and research outcome
14303421.value: The major findings of this study have been published in the journal article Habib et al. ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces, 2004. One key breakthrough was the demonstration that we could produce Cry3Aa-melittin fusions in bacteria without killing the cell. This means that fusion of melittin to Cry3A abrogates its extreme toxicity of melittin. Moreover, this loss of toxicity is sufficient to allow for Cry3Aa-melittin crystals to be intravenously delivered to mice making it suitable for in vivo applications. We also showed that Cry3Aa could also be fused to pro-melittin (PMLT) for even further reduction of the marginal toxicity. The second major breakthrough was the demonstration that the release sequence LPET could be placed in theCry3Aa-PMLT construct to provide a trigger for release of the melittin from the crystals. Finally, we demonstrate the effective application of this technology to the treatment of visceral leishmaniasis in a mouse model - a disease that can lead to death in humans if left untreated.

14303421.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14303421.value: The general strategy of fusing highly toxic AMPs to Cry3Aa and the targeted release of these crystals in macrophages provides a general approach for the treatment of multiple intramacrophage infections. Moreover by altering the cargo, this approach could be modified for use to deliver therapeutic proteins to macrophages, or alternatively, by altering the targeting and release mechanism, the treatment of other cellular diseases such as cancer.

14303421.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14303421.value: Macrophages are a general class of immune cells that kill bacteria and other microrganism by engulfing and digesting them. One class of parasite called Leishmania have developed a novel way to survive in the macrophages where they grow and multiply. While antimicrobial peptides can kill Leishmania, getting these peptides into the macrophages can be difficult particularly in vivo. Here we demonstrate that by fusing an antimicrobial peptide derived from bee venom called melitin to a protein Cry3Aa that forms micrometer sized crystals, we can deliver this antimicrobial peptide to macrophages both in cell culture and in mice. By adding a sequence that is targeted by proteases within macrophages, we can promote the release of melittin within the leishmania-infected macrophage and thereby allowing the melittin to promote the killing of the leishmania in the macrophage. This technology could ultimately lead to a new approach for the treatment of leishmaniasis as well as other related diseases.

14303621.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14303621.value: 本課題的研究目的是合成含定域硼-硼單鍵的碳硼烷並雜環化合物，並且研究它們同小分子化合物以及不飽和底物的反應活性。含有定域硼-硼單鍵的雙硼化合物是非常具有研究價值的分子。由於硼原子中2p空軌道的存在，定域硼-硼單鍵呈現出一些獨特的電子性質。空氣穩定的雙硼化合物，例如B2pin2，在過去的幾十年裡受到了深入的研究並且在有機合成中有著重要的應用。更為活潑的雙硼化合物可以在無過渡金屬幫助的情況下實現小分子以及不飽和化合物的活化。基於此，我們設想通過將定域硼-硼單鍵引入到雜環化合物中來合成新的有機硼化合物，這樣的研究思路在文獻中鮮有報導，然而由於環張力的存在有可能進一步增強定域硼-硼單鍵的反應活性。初步結果表明含定域硼-硼單鍵的碳硼烷並四元雜環化合物能夠同不飽和底物作用發生擴環反應。在這份研究計劃中，我們計劃通過利用碳硼烷獨特的3D立體骨架，來合成碳硼烷並四元，五元以及六元雜環化合物，其中分別包含一個，兩個以及三個定域硼-硼單鍵，以此來研究這類化合物的反應活性。我們希望這項研究可以為定域硼-硼單鍵的官能團化提供新的合成方法，同時提高我們對含定域硼-硼單鍵的多硼化合物反應活性的理解，從而進一步發掘這類化合物在有機合成中的應用。

14303621.label: Realisation of objectives
14303621.value: Boron-boron bonded compounds play a significant role in various chemical processes, including organic synthesis, catalysis, and materials science. Their unique bonding characteristics enable the formation of stable frameworks that enhance reactivity and selectivity in chemical reactions. This project focuses on developing new boron-boron bonded compounds and organoboron reagents, exploring their applications in organic synthesis. We synthesized a carborane-fused four-membered boracycle featuring an electron-precise boron-boron bond, 1,2-[BBrSMe2]2-o-C2B10H10, through the reaction of 1,2-Li2-o-carborane with B2Br4(SMe2)2. This novel boracycle serves as a "strain-release" compound for the diboration of alkenes and alkynes, leading to the generation of ring-expansion products. Notably, when bis(trimethylsilyl)acetylene was employed, an allene-functionalized six-membered boracycle was obtained. Moreover, density functional theory calculations indicate that the reaction of this boracycle with ethylene follows a stepwise mechanism. We prepared a tetra(o-tolyl)(hydrido)diborane(4) anion, an analogue of the [B2H5]⁻ species, by reacting tetra(o-tolyl)diborane(4) with sodium hydride. Unlike common sp²–sp³ diborane species, this compound demonstrated nucleophilicity of the σ-boron-boron bond towards N-heterocyclic carbene-coordinated transition metal halides (Cu, Ag, and Au), resulting in the formation of η²–B–B bonded complexes, as confirmed by single-crystal X-ray analyses. Compared to the sodium complex, structural data of these transition metal complexes reveal significant elongation of the boron-boron bonds, following the order Au > Cu > Ag. Density functional theory studies indicate that the diboron ligand interacts with the coinage metal through a three-center-two-electron B–M–B bonding mode. The prolonged boron-boron bond in the gold complex compared to the copper and silver compounds may be attributed to the superior electrophilicity of the gold atom. We demonstrated a catalyst-free 1,2-diborylation of aryllithium using tetra(o-tolyl)diborane(4), yielding a series of 1,2-diborylaryl lithium species in excellent yields under mild conditions, which produce 1,2-di(tolyl)borylarenes in 60–91% yields upon treatment with a hydride-abstracting reagent. In these transformations, one sp² C–H bond of the arene is activated, utilizing both boryl units to form two new (sp²)C–B bonds. This represents a novel strategy for selective diborylation of arenes. Density functional theory calculations suggest that an aromatic nucleophilic substitution is a key step in product formation. We synthesized a hexaaryl-substituted diboron(6) dianion via the reductive boron-boron coupling of 9-borafluorene. Intriguingly, it exhibits the ability to undergo homolytic boron-boron bond cleavage, generating boryl radical anions, as confirmed by electron paramagnetic resonance studies in the presence of 2.2.2-cryptand at room temperature. Additionally, it reacts directly with diphenylacetylene, producing an unprecedented 1,6-diborylated allene species with a dearomatized phenyl ring. Density functional theory computational studies suggest that homolytic boron-boron bond cleavage is favored in the reaction pathway, and the formation of the boryl radical anion is crucial for dearomatization. Furthermore, it achieves dearomative diborylation of anthracene and activates elemental sulfur/selenium under mild conditions. The borylation products have been successfully characterized by nuclear magnetic resonance spectra, high-resolution mass spectrometry, and X-ray single-crystal diffraction. By employing simple yet versatile bipyridines as ligands, we synthesized a series of redox-active borate anions characterized by nuclear magnetic resonance and X-ray single-crystal diffraction. Notably, the borate anion can reduce lithium ions, generating elemental lithium metal and boron radicals, thereby demonstrating its potent reducing ability. Furthermore, it can serve as a powerful two-electron reducing agent and be readily applied in various reductive homo-coupling reactions and the Birch reduction of acridine. Additionally, this borate anion demonstrates its catalytic ability in the selective two-electron reduction of carbon dioxide to carbon monoxide. In summary, we reported a series of boron-boron bonded diboron reagents, exploring their applications in organic synthesis, small molecule activation, and catalysis.

14303621.label: Major findings and research outcome
14303621.value: 1. Development of a carborane-fused four-membered boracycle featuring an electron-precise boron-boron bond. Its reactivity towards small molecules and unsaturated compounds has been explored. Additionally, this four-membered boracycle can be further transformed into o-carborane-fused six-membered boracycles. 2. Development of a tetra(o-tolyl)(hydrido)diborane(4) anion. This compound demonstrates the nucleophilicity of the σ-boron-boron bond towards N-heterocyclic carbene-coordinated transition metal halides (Cu, Ag, and Au), resulting in the formation of η²–B–B bonded complexes. 3. Development of a catalyst-free 1,2-diborylation of aryllithium using tetra(o-tolyl)diborane(4). This method enables the synthesis of a series of 1,2-diborylaryl lithium species in excellent yields under mild conditions, producing 1,2-di(tolyl)borylarenes in 60–91% yields upon treatment with a hydride-abstracting reagent. 4. Development of a hexaaryl-substituted diboron(6) dianion. This compound exhibits the ability to undergo homolytic boron-boron bond cleavage, generating boryl radical anions that facilitate challenging borylation reactions. 5. Development of a strong reducing boron anion. This anion can serve as a powerful two-electron reducing agent and can be readily applied in various reductive homo-coupling reactions and the Birch reduction of acridine. 6. Reaction mechanisms were investigated in detail to understand the reactivity of the B-B bond, integrating experimental results with DFT studies. Based on these findings, proposed mechanisms were developed to account for the experimental observations. This mechanistic understanding offers valuable insights for the design of new catalytic reactions. In summary, this original work has resulted in 8 peer-reviewed articles published in international chemistry journals, including Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. (x 1), J. Am. Chem. Soc. (x1), Chem. Sci. (x1), Nature Communications (x 1), Chemical Records (x 1), J. Mater. Chem. C (x1), Dalton (x1), and Journal of Organometallic Chemistry (x 1). PI was invited to give three invited lectures at international conferences. Three PhD students were trained.

14303621.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14303621.value: The research on B-B bonded diboron compounds presents significant potential for further development, particularly in expanding their applications in organic synthesis and catalysis. Future efforts could focus on exploring additional reaction pathways and mechanisms involving these compounds, as well as synthesizing new derivatives with enhanced reactivity and selectivity. Our further research will be to investigate further modifications of existing diboron compounds to create new structures with diverse functional groups, aiming to enhance their versatility in various reactions. Additionally, we will explore the use of B-B bonded compounds as catalysts or catalyst precursors in important organic transformations, such as C-H borylation processes. By pursuing these avenues, we aim to maximize the utility of B-B bonded diboron compounds and contribute to advancements in synthetic chemistry and related fields.

14303621.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14303621.value: Boron-boron bonded compounds are important in chemistry because they help create stable structures that enhance reactions. This project provides chemists with a powerful new toolbox of boron-boron bonded reagents. These reagents enable simpler, more efficient, and highly selective ways to build complex organic molecules and materials. They unlock new reaction pathways (like catalyst-free diborylation and radical dearomatization) and can perform challenging tasks like activating small molecules (CO₂, H2) or acting as potent reductants. Overall, these findings highlight the versatility and significance of boron-boron compounds in advancing chemical reactions and developing new materials.

14303721.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14303721.value: In the past decade, significant efforts have been made in developing new energy resources to meet the globally growing demand. However, the anthropogenic processes associated with new energy development may cause earthquakes, termed induced earthquakes. One scenario is related to shale gas development, which was boomed in late 1990s because hydraulic fracturing (fracking), an innovative technique to inject high-pressure fluids and stimulate fracture growth in the low-permeability shale reservoir, had been extensively used in various countries. Consequently, numerous fracking-induced earthquakes have been reported at a wide range of geological settings. More recently, fracking-induced earthquakes become damaging and some of them lead to fatalities in the Sichuan Basin, raising significant concerns regarding assessment of the hazards and risks of these earthquakes. In this proposal, I plan to conduct a detailed investigation on earthquakes at the Weiyuan Shale Gas Field (WSGF), Sichuan, China. Shale gas industry in China has not been quickly developed until 2009, when the first vertical well was drilled in the WSGF that had been established as a national demonstration base. Before 2015, very few earthquakes occurred in the WSGF. But the number of earthquakes increased drastically from 2018, with a few damaging and deadly events in 2019. Some earthquakes led to suspension of fracking and even abandoned fracking wells. Assessment of relevant seismic risks is not only critical for production security and local population, but also plays a significant role in developing shale gas industry in China. Despite the urgent need, investigations on the seismicity in the WSGF are quite few. One of the challenges to investigate induced seismicity is the paucity of seismic network with sufficiently good coverage. Fortunately, permanent seismic network in the WSGF has been significantly improved after the 2019 February Mw 4.3 earthquake, which ruptured an extremely shallow fault (<1.5 km in depth). It remains enigmatic why the shallow fault generated the destructive earthquake. I plan to deploy a dense temporary network with 300 portable instruments, conduct machine learning based earthquake detection and location, and derive precise spatial and temporary evolution of the local earthquakes, as well as high-resolution fault zone structure. By integrating fracking well data and subsurface structure constrained by seismic reflection profiles, we anticipate identifying mechanisms of how fracking activities in the WSGF induce earthquakes so as to provide necessary foundation to formulate appropriate societal responses for reducing earthquake risks. 為了滿足全球日益增長的能源需求，新能源的開發在過去的十年蓬勃發展。但是，一些伴隨的人類活動會誘發地震，比如自九十年代末興起的水壓致裂技術在頁岩氣發展中的應用，全球已經不同地區都有壓裂導致的地震。近期，四川盆地的水力壓裂誘發地震更具破壞性，對評估和減輕地震災害帶來了挑戰。這裏，我計劃針對四川盆地中的威遠頁岩氣田進行研究。中國的頁岩氣工業自2009年迅速發展，第一口頁岩氣井就在威遠。2015年之前，當地的地震數目不多，但隨著頁岩氣產量的增高，地震急遽增加，尤其是2018年之後，發生過多次破壞性地震。儘管對於工業生產和人民生命財產安全都很重要，但針對威遠地區開展的地震研究卻很稀缺。而進行誘發地震研究的一個挑戰就是地震台網覆蓋。自2019年2月之後，威遠地區的觀測台網已經大大提高。我計劃開展基於機器學習的地震檢測，分析地震的時空變化，並探索墨林斷層的高精度內部結構。通過整合多種信息，我們希望可以釐定威遠地區的誘發地震機制，為該地區的地震減災服務。

14303721.label: Realisation of objectives
14303721.value: The project aims to advance the understanding of hydraulic-fracturing (HF)–induced seismicity in the Weiyuan Shale Gas Field (WSGF), Sichuan Basin, through the development of dense-array observations, machine-learning based earthquake detection and relocation, structural imaging, source parameter determination, and mechanisms of induced seismicity. With support from the project, 13 peer-reviewed publications have been published and two PhD students graduated. Collectively, these outputs demonstrate that the objectives have been not only achieved but, in several respects, exceeded. Below we outline the main achievements. Objectives 1& 2: Detailed catalogues of induced seismicity in WSGF The first two objectives—creating detailed catalogues of HF-induced seismicity in WSGF—were fully achieved. Using PhaseNet and waveform cross-correlation, detection rates increased nearly 60-fold over China Earthquake Network Centre (CENC) records. A dense 245-station nodal array captured ~29,700 events (ML –1.35 to 3.42), revealing distinct spatial patterns: southern seismicity clustered around HF pads (pore-pressure diffusion), while northern events aligned with pre-existing faults (Yang et al., 2025, Tectonophysics). To constrain fault kinematics, ~4,400 focal mechanisms were derived via deep-learning models (Song et al., 2025, TSR), showing dominant reverse faulting on north–south structures and stress heterogeneity among smaller events. These catalogues offer critical insights into fault orientations and regional stress regimes. Objectives 3: High-resolution structure of the Molin fault and WSGF We clarified how geological structures shape the spatial and temporal patterns of induced seismicity using body-wave tomography. Earthquakes were found to cluster along the Weiyuan anticline and basement rift, with larger events (ML ≥ 3.0) occurring in low-velocity zones (Zi et al., 2023, Tectonophysics). The September 2019 Mw 5.0 event ruptured a northeast-striking basement fault, linked to a fault relay ramp between thrust faults (Chen et al., 2025, JGE). With the developed workflow to inspect and fix timing problems from temporary network, we were able to constrain accurate timing of waveform records by the dense array (Abbas, et al., 2023, ERA). We also developed a dense-array-based method of deriving subsurface structure from earthquake coda waves and noise interferometry (She et al., 2022, Tectonophysics).Waveform analyses revealed low-frequency anomalies near the Molin fault and preserved reservoirs, indicating fluid retention and structural heterogeneity (Abbas et al., 2024, GJI). InSAR-based slip models showed shallow, high-dip reverse ruptures driven by pore-pressure diffusion and poroelastic stress (Zhang et al., 2024, SRL). Together, these results highlight the key role of tectonic structures, damage zones, and reservoirs in controlling seismic productivity. Objectives 4: Mechanisms of induced earthquakes in WSGF The project surpassed expectations in identifying triggering mechanisms. Near-fault monitoring revealed an ~11-month phase of precursory activation before the September 2019 ML 5.6 earthquake—one of the first detailed observations of long-term preparation for an HF-triggered event (Zi et al., 2025, Commun. Earth Environ.). Continuous seismicity mapped the fault plane ahead of rupture, and modelling confirmed that post-injection aseismic slip contributed to delayed failure. Additional studies showed that stress transfer by aseismic slip can outpace aseismic slip, promoting cascades of activation and acting as a new mechanism of induced seismicity (Yang et al., 2023, Sci. Rep.). These findings offer a unified view of interacting processes—pore-pressure diffusion, poroelastic loading, aseismic slip, and stress transfer—in HF-induced earthquake triggering. New insights In addition to fully achieving the original objectives, the project yielded new insights of intellectual significance and methodological innovation. Methodological innovations include short-segment ambient-noise cross-correlation corrected clock drift, ensuring stable timing and accurate event locations (Abbas et al., 2023, ERA). Curvelet-transform denoising significantly improved signal-to-noise ratios, outperforming traditional methods and preserving waveform fidelity (Zhang et al., 2024, BSSA). Instrument heterogeneity was resolved through systematic calibration, enabling consistent amplitude and robust magnitude estimates (Yang et al., 2025, Tectonophysics). Furthermore, we developed a new method of enhanced spectral decomposition to compute earthquake stress drop. ~11,800 induced events were analysed, yielding an average stress drop of ~2.3 MPa with clear spatial and depth variability (Zhang et al., 2024, GJI). Together, these advances ensured high-quality, internally consistent data for detection, relocation, and source analysis. New insights in the source properties of HF-induced earthquakes indicated that HF-proximal microseismicity showed lower stress drops (0.6–1.3 MPa), while larger on-fault events reached 3–6 MPa, highlighting the role of pore-pressure–assisted rupture and aseismic slip (Zi et al., 2025, Nat. Commun. Earth Environ.). Such contrast of on- and off-fault seismicity offered an opportunity to develop an effective real-time warning system. Variability in focal mechanisms, documented through a dense-array catalogue of ~4,400 events, further confirmed the presence of small-scale stress heterogeneity and fault-geometry complexity (Song et al., 2025, TSR). At the regional scale, spectral and inversion techniques improved stress-drop and attenuation estimates, providing vital context for Weiyuan studies and advancing hazard assessment frameworks (Dang et al., 2023, SDEE; 2024, SDEE; 2025, GJI).

14303721.label: Major findings and research outcome
14303721.value: Research outcome includes 13 peer-reviewed publications and two PhD completions, as well as a number of conference projects and a few postdocs that were trained during the project. Major findings include new insights on mechanisms that can trigger earthquakes (Yang et al., 2023), long precursory activation of seismogenic faults (Zi et al., 2025), structural control on earthquake magnitude (Zi et al., 2023). These findings are made based on the generation of new comprehensive catalogues of earthquakes in the WSGF (Yang et al., 2025, Tectonophysics; Song et al., 2025, TSR; Zhang et al., 2024) by deployment of dense array, application of the state-of-arts machine-learning tools, and integration with geodetic observations and models (Zhang et al., 2024, SRL; Chen et al., 2025, JGE). Furthermore, we find low-frequency waveforms from earthquakes near the Molin fault and develop a new approach to identify small-spatial-scale subsurface fluids, a long-term challenge in Earth sciences (Abbas et al., 2024, GJI). In addition, we develop new methods to correct clock drift by short-window ambient noise, enhance waveform quality by curvelet-transform denoising, as well as to compute earthquake stress drop by a new spectral decomposition workflow (Zhang et al., 2024, GJI). With newly constructed high-resolution catalogues, we are able to identify the different stress drops from on- and off-fault earthquakes, allowing us to propose a new framework for real-time warning system to regulate hydraulic fracturing in Sichuan. In sum, the project delivered high-resolution seismic catalogues, clarified structural controls, identified triggering mechanisms, and introduced methodological advances with broad scientific and societal impact.

14303721.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14303721.value: Despite overall success, several challenges remained. Instrument failures and battery limitations shortened recording durations, though staggered redeployments mitigated gaps (Yang et al., 2025, Tectonophysics). Rupture geometries of large events remain debated, reflecting limits of even advanced tomography in complex media (Zi et al., 2023, Tectonophysics). Instrument-response differences initially biased magnitude and spectral estimates, but calibration and denoising methods substantially improved consistency (Abbas et al., 2023, ERA; Zhang et al., 2024, BSSA). Future work is demanded to overcome these problems. Moreover, translating our findings into real-world industrial practice is inherently challenging, as operational priorities often differ from scientific objectives. Effective knowledge transfer requires substantial effort, dedicated resources, and strategic engagement to ensure meaningful and wide-reaching societal impact.

14303721.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14303721.value: This project aimed to better understand how hydraulic fracturing (HF)—a method used to extract shale gas—can trigger earthquakes in the Weiyuan Shale Gas Field, China. Using a dense network of sensors and advanced machine-learning tools, researchers detected nearly 30,000 small earthquakes, far more than previously recorded. These findings helped map out seismic activity and revealed strong links between fracking operations and nearby fault zones. Remarkably, the team discovered that some large earthquakes were preceded by nearly a year of subtle underground activity, offering new clues about how stress builds up before a major event. They also found that certain faults and underground structures influence the size and location of earthquakes, and identified a new mechanism behind induced seismicity. Low-frequency signals near the Molin fault pointed to hidden fluid zones, which may help forecast future risks. To improve data quality, the team developed new methods to correct timing errors, reduce noise, and measure stress released during each quake. These innovations led to a new framework for real-time warning systems that could help manage fracking operations and reduce seismic hazards. Overall, the project blends cutting-edge science with practical tools to improve safety and awareness in shale gas regions.

14303921.label: Project Objectives
14303921.value: SNoS - the Sky Noise Simulator This is an optical module to convert any submillimetre source in a laboratory into a combination of two components: (1) signal - a weakly linearly polarised radiation; (2) noise - a linearly unpolarised radiation with fast fluctuation and a slow drifting of the intensity. The intensities of the two components are adjustable and should vary inversely to simulate Kirchhoff’s law. Use SNoS to test existing polarimeter, APol (GRF14307118), and develop new observation strategies.

14303921.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14303921.value: This project has two main aims: (1) to build a sky noise simulator (SNoS) in the laboratory to enable polarimeters for submillimetre observations to be tested in situ rather than in remote observatories; and (2) to construct a Martin–Puplett interferometer polarimeter (MPIP) which can remove sky noise more effectively than existing techniques, thereby improving the accuracy of astronomical observations. Observational astronomy involves a constant battle against atmospheric conditions. The situation is particularly severe for submillimetre observations, as water vapour is a very efficient absorber and emitter of submillimetre radiation. As a result, submillimetre observatories are all built in particularly dry places: a dead volcano in Hawaii [1], a high desert in Chile [2], and a remote site in Antarctica [3]. Even in desirable sites like these, sky emissions can easily be hundreds of times larger than celestial signals. It takes sophisticated strategies to “find the needle in the haystack”. Inconveniently, new instruments can only be tested and new strategies tried out in these remote observatories, which inevitably makes for slow progress. For example, the current polarimeter running in Hawaii still uses the same strategy it used in the 1990s. On top of the low signal-to-noise ratio, the submillimetre thermal emission from molecular clouds is polarised at a very low degree (therefore extremely difficult to detect) yet is extremely important for understanding the mechanisms of star formation [12, 13, 14, 15]. Parallel with SNoS, we propose a new idea for submillimetre polarimeter, the Martin–Puplett interferometer polarimeter (MPIP), to be tested immediately after SNoS is built. The state-of-the-art submillimetre polarimeters take the difference between the two orthogonal polarisations (in order to remove the unpolarised sky noise) either detected by different detectors (e.g., SHARP [4]) or detected at different time (e.g., SCUPol2 [5]). MPIP can take this difference between orthogonal polarisations detected at the same time by the same detector and thus remove sky noise much more effectively. This project has considerable practical significance. By simulating sky noise in our laboratory, we will be able to test our polarimeter (APol, GRF14307118) in situ, before it is delivered to the observatory. More importantly, we will also be able to conveniently explore new ideas for next-generation polarimeters. The results of this project will remove existing obstacles to the development of improved polarimeters. 14303921.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14303921.value: The submillimeter band represents the final frontier of astronomical observation. At these wavelengths, atmospheric noise—primarily emitted by water vapor—can be hundreds of times more intense than the faint signals from celestial objects. Consequently, telescopes are forced to operate in the driest locations on Earth, such as the Antarctic plateau or the Greenland summit. This remoteness makes on-site instrument testing profoundly challenging, as any troubleshooting or modification often requires transporting equipment back to distant laboratories. These formidable logistical barriers have historically constrained the pace of technological advancement in the field. The Sky Noise Simulator (SNoS) we have developed directly addresses this bottleneck by enabling precise replication of sky noise in a controlled laboratory setting, thereby revolutionizing the development cycle for submillimeter instrumentation.

14304021.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14304021.value: Flow and transport processes in heterogenous porous media are highly coupled mechanisms. In particular, the transport equation gives the material balance law for the transport of constituents, which is driven by a flow velocity satisfying the flow equation. Due to the heterogeneous nature of the media, the velocity field contains multiscale features, which drive a multiscale transport phenomenon. Solving these equations computationally is a challenging task due to disparity of scales, high variations in the velocity fields and nonlinear coupling between flow and transport. Therefore, developing robust, accurate and efficient multiscale methods is a challenging task in many applications including material sciences, filtration, membrane applications, groundwater hydrology, petroleum engineering and so on. There are in literature some computational multiscale techniques including numerical homogenization, numerical upscaling, multiscale finite element method, and so on. These methods typically give instability in the regime of high Peclet number for transport, and are based on linear ideas that do not take the nonlinear coupling of flow and transport systematically. As a result, they typically give inaccurate solutions for realistic situations where the media contain highly heterogeneous porous materials. In this project, our focus is to develop accurate and robust multiscale methods for coupled flow and transport problems in heterogeneous porous media. The novelties of our proposed work are multifold. We will design multiscale basis functions for flows and transport that have a provable localization property. Thus the basis functions can be computed efficiently on local domains. We will also design a hybrid technique, which allows one to construct diffusion basis functions and transport basis functions separately in order to take into account important properties of the respective operators, and allows a robust and accurate coupling of these two types of basis functions. Moreover, we will design fast adaptive computational techniques that can control the error of each time step so that the overall performance of the method is high. The proposed research provides a novel multiscale method for coupled flow and transport problems arising from many realistic applications. Our novel techniques avoid idealized scale concepts and linear multiscale techniques. We expect that our methodology will provide an accurate, efficient and robust tool for many applications involving flow and transport in heterogeneous porous media, and help engineers, domain scientists and industrial leaders to design practical solutions. 非均質多孔介質中的流動和傳輸過程是高度耦合的機制。特別是，輸運方程給出了成分輸運的物質平衡規律，它由滿足流動方程的流速驅動。由於介質的異質性，速度場包含多尺度特徵，從而驅動多尺度傳輸現象。由於尺度的差異、速度場的高度變化以及流動和運輸之間的非線性耦合，以計算方式求解這些方程是一項具有挑戰性的任務。因此，在包括材料科學、過濾、膜應用、地下水水文學、石油工程等在內的許多應用中，開發穩健、準確和高效的多尺度方法是一項具有挑戰性的任務。文獻中有一些計算多尺度技術，包括數值均勻化、數值放大、多尺度有限元方法等。這些方法通常會在傳輸的高 Peclet 數狀態下產生不穩定性，並且基於線性思想，沒有系統地處理流動和傳輸的非線性耦合。因此，對於介質包含高度異質多孔材料的實際情況，它們通常會給出不准確的解決方案。 在這個項目中，我們的重點是為非均質多孔介質中的耦合流動和輸運問題開發準確而穩健的多尺度方法。 我們提出的工作的新穎性是多方面的。 我們將為具有可證明定位屬性的流動和運輸設計多尺度基函數。 因此，可以在局部域上有效地計算基函數。 我們還將設計一種混合技術，它允許一個人分別構建擴散基函數和傳輸基函數，以考慮各自算子的重要屬性，並允許這兩種類型的基函數穩健而準確地耦合。 此外，我們將設計快速自適應計算技術，可以控制每個時間步的誤差，從而使該方法的整體性能較高。 擬議的研究為許多實際應用中產生的耦合流動和運輸問題提供了一種新的多尺度方法。 我們的新技術避免了理想化的尺度概念和線性多尺度技術。 我們希望我們的方法能夠為涉及非均質多孔介質中的流動和傳輸的許多應用提供準確、高效和強大的工具，並幫助工程師、領域科學家和工業領導者設計實用的解決方案。

14304121.value: 極小曲面理論中的奇異點分析

14304121.label: Project Objectives

14304121.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14304121.value: Most physical laws in nature are described mathematically by differential equations, e.g. Einstein's equation in General Relativity and Navier-Stokes' equation in fluid dynamics. The non-linearity of such equations often leads to formation of singularities. The study of singularities, e.g. black holes in relativity and turbulence in fluid dynamics, is therefore essential to our understanding of the underlying physical phenomena. There have been a lot of studies on the singularities arising in certain geometric variational problems which provide mathematical models for soap-films and soap-bubbles. Mathematically, Plateau's Problem is to show the existence of a minimal surface with given boundary. Many different mathematical models have been proposed to approach this problem and it is of fundamental importance to understand the singularities that can arise in each model. Earlier works mostly focus on minimal surfaces without singularities and more recently an effective min-max theory has been developed. A satisfactory existence theory for singular minimal surfaces is still lacking. In this project, the PI proposes to develop a mathematical theory for minimal surfaces with soap-film singularities. Geometric methods, as well as advanced techniques in geometric measure theory and partial differential equations, will be employed to study the fundamental existence and regularity questions for singular minimal surfaces. Our goal is to construct singular minimal surfaces in a wide range of settings, including higher dimensions and curved background spaces. The PI will investigate the geometric and analytic properties of singular minimal surfaces and their relationship with the ambient geometry. A more long-term objective is to explore their applications in other physical problems encountered, for example, in grain boundary motions and general relativity. 自然界中的大多數物理定律都是通過數學上的微分方程來描述，例如廣義相對論中的愛因斯坦方程和流體力學中的納維-斯托克斯方程。這種方程的非線性常常導致奇點點的形成。正因如此，奇異點的研究對於我們理解潛在的物理現象例如相對論中的黑洞和流體力學中的湍流至關重要。 目前已有大量關於某些幾何變分問題例如肥皂膜和肥皂泡的數學模型中出現的奇點點研究。在數學上，Plateau 問題是要證明給定邊界的極小曲面的存在。對於這個問題我們已經有許多不同的數學模型來解決，因此了解每個模型中可能出現的奇點尤其重要。早期的工作主要集中在沒有奇異點的極小曲面上，包括最近發展迅速的最小-最大理論。可是我們仍然缺乏一套帶有奇異點的極小曲面的理論。 在這個項目中，我們提出為具有肥皂膜奇異點的極小曲面開發一套新的數學理論。我們將會運用幾何方法，包括幾何測量理論和偏微分方程的先進技巧，來研究帶奇異點的極小曲面的基本存在性和規律性問題。我們的目標是在廣泛的情形下，包括更高的維度和彎曲的背景空間等，構造帶奇異點的極小曲面。 我們將進一步研究帶奇異點的極小曲面的幾何和分析性質及其與背景空間幾何的關聯。作為更長期的目標，我們將探索這套理論在其他物理問題中的應用，例如晶粒邊界運動和廣義相對論中。

14304121.label: Realisation of objectives
14304121.value: Regarding Objective 1, the PI and his collaborators have initiated a systematic study of singular minimal surfaces arising as the limit-interface for natural functionals in phase transition theory, which yields a very powerful methodology to construct singular minimal surfaces inside bounded domains of Euclidean spaces. In particular, we use sophisticated techniques from geometric measure theory to study the geometric and analytic properties of such singular minimal surfaces. Our work paves the way to the far-reaching program of developing a general min-max theory for free boundary minimal hypersurfaces via the Allen-Cahn approach. On the other hand, the PI and his PhD student Yizi Wang has discovered a novel strong maximum principle for singular minimal surfaces in higher codimensions. Maximum principle is an essential tool in studying analytic and geometric properties of solutions to geometric variational problems. While such maximum principles are known to be true mostly in codimension one, our work established a surprising result that it also holds in higher codimensions even in the singular context of viscosity solutions. Finally, Albert Wood, a postdoc of the PI, and his collaborator has successfully constructed new families of low cohomogeneity Lagrangian translating solitons and special Lagrangian submanifolds in complex Euclidean spaces. These novel examples serve as singularity models for Lagrangian mean curvature flow and provide interesting calibrated minimal submanifolds in higher codimensions. Altogether, the results described above have fully achieve Objective 1, in fact to a much further extent including situations in higher dimensional and in the complex analytic settings. Regarding Objective 2, the PI and his collaborators have developed the general existence theory of singular minimal surfaces inside Riemannian manifolds with boundary. More precisely, we proved the existence of free boundary minimal hypersurfaces in the context of varifolds which allows soap-film type singularities. Moreover, our work combined state-of-the-art techniques from nonlinear partial differential equations and geometric measure theory to obtain the optimal integer rectifiability of the limit-interface, hence extending the foundational work of Hutchinson-Tonegawa up to the boundary. On the other hand, Gongping Niu, a postdoc of the PI, and his collaborators have studied the isoperimetric problem in closed 8-dimensional Riemannian manifolds and proved generic regularity results for these isoperimetric regions. While the singular set of such isoperimetric regions are relatively small (of codimension at least seven), the singular sets are expected to be much bigger in the multi-bubble partitioning problem. Their work will be fundamental to the study of existence and regularity of such soap bubble cluster-like constant mean curvature surfaces (a close cousin of minimal surfaces) in Riemannian manifolds of arbitrary dimensions. As a result, Objective 2 has been fully addressed to great satisfaction and many new directions have been discovered. For Objective 3, there are also major progress in finding new applications of singular minimal surfaces in various geometric and physical problems. Motivated by the conjectural spacetime Penrose inequality, the PI and his PhD student Yizi Wang have started a thorough investigation of the inverse spacetime mean curvature flow for free boundary minimal surfaces in initial data sets for initial-boundary value problems of the Einstein equation in mathematical general relativity. We apply the elliptic regularization technique to construct weak solutions to this non-variational geometric flow. The work of the PI’s postdoc Albert Wood and his collaborator mentioned above also offered key insights into the singularity formation of geometric flows that are closely related to special Lagrangians, a central object of study in Calabi-Yau geometry and Mirror Symmetry in physics. Finally, the work of the PI’s another postdoc Gongping Niu and his collaborators provide the key mathematical analysis of singularity structure for isoperimetric regions which have profound applications in the study of scalar curvature in geometry as well as natural geometric variational problems such as multi-bubble clusters and grain boundary motion in material science. In summary, all the three objectives set out in this project has been successfully completed. Moreover, the research findings have opened up several new directions for further investigations and applications to mathematics and other related scientific disciplines.

14304121.label: Major findings and research outcome
14304121.value: Research Output 1 by the PI and his collaborators is the major findings coming out of this project. Under a natural uniform bound on the Allen-Cahn energy, we established the up-to-the-boundary rectifiability of any limit interface varifolds arising from a sequence of general critical points to the Allen-Cahn energy functional in any bounded domain of a Riemannian manifold of arbitrary dimension. Our results are valid without any assumptions on the geometry (such as convexity) of the ambient manifold nor the minimizing property or stability of the critical points. Our new techniques also resolved a mysterious boundary concentration phenomenon as observed by earlier results in the literature. This important work is tied to all three objectives of this project and has been published in the prestigious journal Archive for Rational Mechanics and Analysis. The PI has also trained his PhD student Yizi Wang to work on some parts of this project. In Research Output 2, we proved a strong maximum principle for certain weak solutions (e.g. in the viscosity sense) to the minimal surface system. Since maximum principles are in general not valid for systems of equations, it is surprising that one can still establish such a result in this higher codimension setting. In Research Output 3, we carried out the analysis of the inverse spacetime mean curvature flow with a free boundary condition, which is expected to shed light on the spacetime Penrose inequality for initial data sets with non-compact boundary. Since Yizi did not continue in academic, it is still taking some time for us to polish the two manuscripts to be submitted soon (within the next few months) for publication in reputed journals. Finally, the PI has proposed to his postdocs to work on some parts of this project. In Research Output 4, Albert Wood and his collaborator considered an ansatz generalizing the construction of Castro-Lerma in the complex Euclidean plane and succeeded in proving the existence of a novel family of low-cohomogeneity Lagrangian translating solitons and special Lagrangian submanifolds inside complex Euclidean space of higher dimensions. In Research Output 5, Gongping Niu and his collaborators have established a generic regularity result for isoperimetric regions inside Riemannian manifolds of dimension eight, a critical dimension where singularity starts to form. These works have expanded the scope and application of this project and they have been submitted to well-regarded international journals for publication.

14304121.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14304121.value: With the foundational analytic work accomplished in Research Output 1, we will further develop the regularity theory for limit interface arising from stable or finite Morse index solutions to the Allen-Cahn equation on bounded domains. This will be part of a substantial program of the PDE-based Allen-Cahn approach to the min-max theory of free boundary minimal hypersurfaces. Based on the research findings in this project, we shall continue to investigate the geometric and analytic properties of singular minimal surfaces in the higher codimensional setting, and explore further geometric and physical applications of such objects and their relation to singularity formation in evolution problems such as grain boundary motion.

14304121.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14304121.value: This project has studied the geometric and analytic nature of singularities arising naturally in geometric variational problems such as the mathematical models for soap films. The mathematical study of such singularities requires sophisticated techniques from differential geometry, partial differential equations and geometric measure theory. Together with his students, postdocs and collaborators, the PI has discovered new tools to analyze the fine structure of singularities in a wide range of situations. These have opened up possibilities to study their physical applications in the mathematical theory of general relativity, phase transition and grain boundary motion.

14304221.value: 本計劃的目標是開發函數時間序列門檻模型。 由於數據收集和存儲技術的進步，高頻數據在工程、環境計量學、金融計量經濟學和遺傳學等各個科學領域變得越來越流行。 研究高頻數據的一種流行方法是將數據轉換為函數來作出分析。 例如，高頻數據的觀測可以劃分為自然連續的時間間隔，例如天、週或月，其中典型的例子包括金融指數的日內記錄和城市的每日溫度。 函數時間序列建模在分析高頻數據集的序列相關性方面特別有用，它減輕了傳統多元時間序列建模中大規模參數估計的低效率和數值運算的問題。最近，許多研究為函數自回歸和函數 GARCH 模型的理論和實踐發展做出了貢獻。另一方面，門檻模型是一類重要的非線性時間序列模型，它允許對跨制度的不同潛在依賴結構進行建模，但尚未在函數時間序列的背景下進行探索。 因此，現有的方法不能模擬以下的有趣機制: 根據先前觀察的最大值（或其他泛函）是否高於門檻值，函數表現出不同的自回歸結構。 為了將門檻模型的框架擴展到函數時間序列，本計劃旨在 通過靈活建模各種場景下的不同結構，為函數時間序列開發門檻模型。 我們將研討與這新模型相關的三個重要問題。首先，我們根據所提出的模型為過程的平穩性和遍歷性建立條件。其次，我們為每個門檻值和模型參數開發了有效的估計和模型選擇程序。最後，我們研究門檻值和模型參數推斷的漸近理論。模型的擴展以包含外生變量或結構性變化也將被探索。 成功執行本計劃將會產生函數時間序列門檻建模工具。 隨著高頻數據問題對函數時間序列分析的需求不斷增加，本研究 將函數時間序列的靈活門檻建模，這是現有方法無法實現的。 這將促進廣泛的科學研究領域取得重大進展，例如計量經濟學、電氣和環境工程、金融和遺傳學。

14304221.label: Major findings and research outcome
14304221.value: We successfully developed a functional threshold autoregressive model for flexible functional time series modeling. In particular, the behavior of a function at a given time point can be described by different autoregressive mechanisms according to different values of a threshold variable at a past time point. Sufficient conditions for strict stationarity and ergodicity of the functional threshold autoregressive process are established. A novel criterion based method is develop to simultaneously conduct dimension reduction and estimation of thresholds, autoregressive orders, and model parameters. The consistency and asymptotic distributions of the estimators of both thresholds and underlying autoregressive models are established. Simulation studies and a real application of U.S. Treasury zero-coupon yield rates are provided to illustrate the effectiveness and usefulness of the proposed methodology.

14304221.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14304221.value: The current results assume some moment and homoscedasticity conditions of the noise terms. Extension to heavy-tailed or heteroscedastic noises are interesting and important future research directions.

14304221.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14304221.value: Functional time series refers to data observed regularly in time with each observation being a function. This type of data arises naturally in the big data era since everyday we observe huge amount of data, and some data may be dense and evolve continuous enough to be treated as a function. For example, stock price movement or temperature in a day. This project develops a threshold model for functional time series data, so that the behavior of the function in each time point is allow to be governed by a few different rules according to different behaviors of a threshold variable. This feature greatly enhances the flexibility of modeling functional time series.
