14304421.label: Realisation of objectives
14304421.value: We have successfully realized all objectives listed in Section 5.2 1. A series of highly stereoselective transition metal-catalyzed C-F bond functionalizations of fluoroalkenes have been developed. (1) The palladium-catalyzed defluoroborylation of tetrasubstituted gem-difluoroalkenes with unsymmetrical diboron reagent (pin)B−B(dan) was achieved to access novel boronamides containing the monofluorinated vinyl−B(dan) functionality. (2) The palladium-catalyzed defluorosilylation of gem-difluoroalkenes was achieved to access tetrasubstituted vinylsilanes containing the monofluoroalkene motif in excellent diastereoselectivities. (3) The palladium-catalyzed Hiyama cross-coupling reaction of gem-difluoroalkenes demonstrated excellent functional group tolerability for the synthesis of monofluoroalkenes. (4) The palladium-catalyzed Mizoroki−Heck reaction of gem-difluoroalkenes was achieved to synthesize monofluorinated 1,3-diene products with control of the geometry of each double bond. (5) The rhodium-catalyzed C−F bond functionalization of gem-difluoroalkenes with arylboronic acids enabled C−F bond arylation of both trisubstituted β,β-difluorostyrenes and tetrasubstituted β,β-difluoroacrylates toward the synthesis of valuable monofluoroalkenes. 2. The synthetic utility of monofluoroalkenes as building blocks was demonstrated. (1) The reaction between monofluoroalkenes and Grignard reagents without catalysts was achieved to synthesize trisubstituted alkenes with excellent diastereoselectivity. (2) The rhodium-catalyzed defluorinative coupling of boronic acids with (E)-monofluoroalkenes was achieved to access (Z)-alkene products with an inversion of double bond geometry. (3) The borylated monofluoroalkenes can undergo cross-couple directly with gem-difluoroalkenes without reactivation in Suzuki−Miyaura reactions to afford vincinal difluoro 1,3-dienes with modular control of the substituents. (4) Various transformations of the double bond of monofluoroalkenes were demonstrated to access novel monofluorinated compounds.

14304421.label: Major findings and research outcome
14304421.value: In this project, we have investigated transition metal-catalyzed C-F bond functionalization of fluoroalkenes which led to the following important findings. (1) Four new reactions of palladium(0)-catalyzed stereoselective C-F bond functionalization of gem-difluoroalkenes were developed including defluorosilylation (Org. Lett. 2023, 25, 2333), defluoroborylation (Org. Lett. 2023, 25, 4406), Mizoroki-Heck reaction (Org. Lett. 2023, 25, 6217) and Hiyama cross-coupling reaction (Org. Lett. 2024, 26, 376). These transformations enabled carbon-carbon, carbon-silicon and carbon-boron bond formations in the synthesis of pharmaceutically relevant monofluoroalkenes with excellent diastereoselectivity. (2) Besides palladium, rhodium(I) catalysts were also shown to be effective in the C-F bond arylation of gem-difluoroalkenes (Org. Lett. 2023, 25, 877) and monofluoroalkenes (Org. Lett. 2022, 24, 6380) with boronic acids. These transformations demonstrated excellent diastereoselectivity and broad substrate scope. Using Grignard reagents without the catalyst was also viable for defluoroalkylation of fluoroalkenes through completely different mechanisms (Org. Lett. 2022, 24, 4087). A photocatalytic acylmonofluoromethylation of alkenes was also developed (Org. Chem. Front. 2023, 10, 6124). (3) The monofluoroalkene products from the C-F bond functionalizations were amenable to further transformations as synthetic building blocks for structurally diverse monofluorinated compounds. The outcome of this project has led to the publication of 8 original research articles in international peer-reviewed journals. The findings of this project were disseminated in 10 international and national conferences and meetings. Two Ph.D. students have received training from this project and successfully graduated.

14304421.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14304421.value: For the transition metal-catalyzed C-F bond functionalization, other metals besides palladium and rhodium can be utilized. We plan to use earth-abundant transition metals such as iron, cobalt and nickel to develop novel C-F bond transformations of difluoroalkenes. Detailed studies including reactivity, stereoselectivity and mechanisms will be carried out to find new reaction pathways and applications. These studies will be both fundamentally important and practically useful for synthesizing monofluorinated compounds. For the utility of fluoroalkenes as building blocks, we will continue investigating the asymmetric transformations of monofluoroalkenes including enantioselective hydrogenation, cycloaddition and difunctionalization. The products will contain stereogenic centres with a carbon-fluorine bond, which are challenging to construct and important to drug discovery.

14304421.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14304421.value: Monofluorinated compounds have important applications in disease treatment and cancer diagnosis. However, the synthesis of monofluorinated building blocks is challenging due to the control of both reactivity and selectivity. In this project, we have developed a series of highly stereoselective transition metal-catalyzed C-F bond functionalization of difluoroalkenes to access monofluoroalkenes, which can be further transformed into various monofluorinated compounds. The use of palladium and rhodium catalysts can effectively activate the robust carbon-fluorine bond with concomitant construction of carbon-carbon and carbon-heteroatom bonds. This defluorinative functionalization strategy allows the synthesis of novel monofluorinated motifs with high efficiency and selectivity, which will eventually find applications in drug discovery. The outcome of this project has led to 8 publications, 10 conference presentations and the graduation of 2 Ph.D. students.

14304521.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14304521.value: 本項目旨在開發用於分析多族裔全基因組關聯研究的統計方法。以英國生物樣本庫為典型的大規模生物樣本庫的出現為我們破譯複雜疾病的遺傳結構提供了前所未有的機會。大型生物樣本庫往往具有豐富的族裔多樣性。儘管這些大規模生物樣本庫使得我們可以研究少數族裔的疾病遺傳結構，我們在數據分析方面面臨著新的挑戰。 長期以來，研究人員一直意識到人口異質性對關聯分析造成的混淆。避免混淆的一種方法是先對各個族裔的數據分別做關聯分析然後進行薈萃分析。然而，生物樣本庫通常由基因組起源于多個祖先的混合個體組成。對於混合群體的關聯分析，經典方法試圖在確定遺傳變異是否與特定表型相關時矯正人口異質性。然而，這些方法無法識別在某些但不是全部族裔中與表型相關的變異，而且這些方法忽視了那些所有族裔共有的變異在不同族裔中的效應大小的差異。因此，儘管迫切需要，但分析生物樣本庫規模的多族裔全基因組關聯研究的統計方法仍十分匱乏。 在本項目中，我們將為多族裔全基因組關聯研究開發計算高效的統計方法。特別是，我們將開發一種嚴格的假設檢驗方法來推斷族裔特異的關聯。我們提出的計算技術將大大降低時間複雜度並把內存消耗從TB降到MB尺度。通過結合使用隨機更新和並行計算的進一步加速，我們開發的算法將能夠分析由數十萬個體組成的生物樣本庫規模的多族裔全基因組關聯研究。我們將把開發的方法應用於公共的和我們自己的全基因組關聯研究數據，重點關注眼部疾病。 通過解決遺傳學中的前沿科學和計算問題，該項目將對統計遺傳學、統計計算和並行計算產生深遠影響。由此產生的科學發現將加深我們對疾病的遺傳機制的理解，促進香港和其他地方的個性化醫療的發展。

14304821.value: Landau-de Gennes 理論已成功的被應用到液晶材料的向錯研究。對物理學家、化學家和數學家來說最重要的是圍繞向錯的方向場結構。在一個常數極限中，三個基本結構已被數值證實。它們是徑向解，半度環解和分裂核解。最近，在低溫極限下，這三種結構的存在都得到了嚴格的證明。然而，對於具有有限溫度的 Landau-de Gennes 理論，這三種結構的存在任然未得到嚴格證實。在這個項目中，我們計劃研究三個主要問題 。第一個問題是向錯的三種基本結構的存在。我們還想研究這個問題中带有 Ball-Majumdar 位勢的模型。 數值上已經表明，當域集的拓撲結構複雜時，我們可以得到更複雜的向錯結構。在我們的第二個問題中，我們計劃研究一些向錯的紐結問題。一般來說，液晶材料可以用Landau-de Gennes 理論裡不同的參數來描述。我們的第三個問題是擴展我們的研究到具有變參數的一般 Landau-de Gennes 理論。成功解決這些問題需要深入分析橢圓偏微分方程。此外，許多以前的同一參數的工作應該能夠擴展到各向異性情況。我們這個項目可能會開拓幾何分析的一些新研究方向。我們相信我們的研究會引起物理學家，化學家和數學家的關注。 我們希望這些研究工作能夠為我們未來對向錯動力學的研究提供了一些啟示。

14304921.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14304921.value: 自然界中的酶往往以組裝體或者複合物存在。酶的組裝拉進了活性位點、防止酶反應的中間體的洩漏、並且提高了產物合成的效率。我們和其他組開發了多種多酶複合物。雖然如此，精準、動態調控多酶複合物的形成是個難點。 相分離形成的蛋白質凝聚體是由液體-液體相分離形成的一類無膜細胞器。有些代謝酶在細胞內形成蛋白質凝聚體，從而曹文一類動態多酶組裝體。這些精妙的組裝體啓發我們猜測蛋白質凝聚體可以用來富集酶，另外小分子原料以及產物能夠有效跨過蛋白質聚集體的邊界從而實現聚集體內外的物質交流。我們的前期實驗也證實了組裝生物合成酶在蛋白質聚集體中可以有效提高酶的催化活性。 仍然有兩個問題沒有解決：1. 蛋白質相分離能否區格兩個不同的通路，2. 是否可以在細胞內實現。在這個申請書里，我們計劃開發可控多酶相分離體系，並且研究相分離如何提升amorphadiene的生物合成。使用倍半萜烯合成途徑作為模型，我們的研究計劃旨在1. 獲得控制蛋白質相分離的技術能力，2. 瞭解蛋白質相分離如何影響級聯催化，3. 開發一種調控生物合成的新方案，4. 獲得工程化的高效合成菌株。

14304921.label: Realisation of objectives
14304921.value: In this project, we proposed to develop a new type of multienzyme complexes through liquid-liquid phase separation and the formation of protein condensates. Enzymes in their native conditions in cells often form metabolons, or multienzyme complexes, in order to realize the maximal catalytic efficiency. Clustering enzymes into complexes, rather than having all enzymes in discrete, stand-alone forms scattered in the cytosol, facilitates intermediate transfer, insulates against intermediate leakage, reduces the side effects of toxic intermediates, and streamlines metabolic flux towards the desired products. In the area of synthetic biology, researchers express enzymes in heterologous hosts, such as the bacterium E. coli, to acquire a more efficient production of valuable chemicals or biologics. These multienzyme complexes were often constructed using a scaffold or encapsulation in a protein shell. These strategies confine enzymes in metabolons but limit the exchange of substrates and products. Here, we developed a novel strategy by constructing protein condensates through liquid-liquid phase separation of an RGGRGG protein, and then encapsulating sequential enzymes for sesquiterpene biosynthesis within the droplets. We verified this strategy first in vitro using recombinant proteins and demonstrated a marked increase in the product FPP. Then we constructed RGGRGG protein condensates inside E. coli cells, which supported the biosynthesis in vivo. Taken together, we developed a new type of multienzyme compartmentation strategy both in vitro and in vivo inside E. coli cells via liquid-liquid phase-separated protein condensates, and showed that clustering enzymes enhances the biosynthesis of terpene products. This finding may be implemented in the fermentation industry to streamline metabolic flux and increase biosynthetic yield.

14304921.label: Major findings and research outcome
14304921.value: A new strategy for forming multienzyme complexes is reported. By constructing protein condensates inside E coli cells, we can enrich biosynthetic enzymes within protein droplets for the first time. We showed that this simple operation led to a significant increase in product yield in E. coli. Several papers have been published to report the results above. The key paper has been highlighted in Matter 2022, 3, 2397–2561. The students won first Prize in the 8th Hong Kong University Student Innovation & Entrepreneurship Competition, a Silver Medal in "Internet +" National University Student Innovation & Entrepreneurship Competition, and a Bronze Medal in "Challenge Cup" National University Student Innovation & Entrepreneurship Competition. This work was also reported at international conferences as invited or keynote talks. Several Ph.D. students received training under this project, and graduated with a Ph.D. degree during the period.

14304921.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14304921.value: Here, we report a novel strategy for increasing the biosynthetic yield of valuable chemicals. The engineering strategy is relatively easy and has potential for industrial application. The protein condensates we have developed may also inspire other applications in soft matter and biomedicine, other than synthetic biology.

14304921.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14304921.value: Bacteria can be engineered to produce valuable chemicals for us. Biosynthesis helps save the environment from our overreliance on petroleum chemistry, which is both unsustainable and polluting. To realize this, we need to engineer enzymes and put them into bacterial cells so that they can perform the synthetic task. Here, we invented a new strategy of enzyme engineering by assembling them within protein droplets inside bacterial cells. This simple operation significantly increases the amount of chemicals we can produce from bacterial cells, thereby making it commercially competitive and environmentally friendly.

14305121.label: Project Objectives
14305121.value: Verify ion-binding-induced enzyme conformational changes and identify the true calcium binding site. Our preliminary work suggests that calcium activates PcncAAAD, at least in part, by anchoring a 17-amino acid (aa) N-terminal loop that caps and stabilizes residues lining the substrate binding pocket. Between the two metal-binding sites revealed by the X-ray crystal structure, site A plays the dominating role in this process. However, although we employed the latest NBFIX terms in our molecular dynamics simulations, they were still limited in accuracy due to the lack of explicit treatment of polarization. As the first step to fully elucidate PcncAAAD calcium activation mechanism, we plan to employ a polarizable force field based on the Drude oscillator model to verify ion-binding-induced enzyme conformational changes observed in our preliminary work. Along with these calculations, enzyme kinetics assays will be performed by our collaborators on mutants targeting either site A or B, in order to unambiguously identify the true calcium binding site in PcncAAAD. Examine the impact of PcncAAAD structural elements on its activity. We plan to develop a scoring scheme that estimates the contributions from its structural elements to pcncAAAD's activation. This scheme will be employed to evaluate in silico mutations designed to either activate or de-activate the enzyme. Along with experimental verification, it will enable us to pinpoint the key structural elements regulating the activity of PcncAAAD. Disentangle the roles of C-terminus appendage domain. Experimental results from our collaborators indicate that truncated (without the C-terminus) PcncAAAD shows little to zero activity, even though it contains the entire catalytic core domain with the co-factor PLP. Whether such a loss of activity is solely due to the lack of calcium binding sites in the C-terminus, however, remains elusive. Indeed, apart from accommodating the divalent cation, the C-terminus has two additional interfaces with the catalytic core domain. These two interfaces may act as "glues'' to help prevent the full-length PcncAAAD from undergoing deteriorating conformational changes seen in our simulations of the truncated enzyme. Building upon results from work proposed under objectives 1 and 2, we will explore various mutations that target the aforementioned interfaces, in order to fully disentangle the roles played by the C-terminus appendage domain.

14305121.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14305121.value: The aromatic amino acid decarboxylase from Psilocybe cubensis (PcncAAAD) catalyzes the first step in the biosynthesis of psilocybin, a psychoactive alkaloid with potential applications in treating a series of severe psychiatric disorders. Unlike its counterparts in mammals and plants, PcncAAAD is activated by calcium, which brings an up to 500-fold increase in catalytic efficiency of the fungal enzyme. Recent work from our experimental collaborators indicates that calcium binding to PcncAAAD is mediated by a unique, 300-amino acid C-terminus appendage domain. However, the exact mechanism of activation by the divalent cation remains unknown. Here, we plan to combine computer modeling with our collaborators' enzyme kinetics experiments, in order to fully elucidate the mechanism of calcium activation in PcncAAAD. Our preliminary 14-microsecond molecular dynamics (MD) simulations already revealed key conformational transitions governing such activation. Building upon these results, we will first employ a polarizable force field based on the classical Drude oscillator model to further examine ion-binding-induced conformational changes of the enzyme. Next, we plan to conduct and analyze microsecond MD simulations on various mutants designed to verify the proposed calcium activation mechanism. Incorporating feedbacks from our collaborators' experiments, a scoring scheme that quantifies the contributions of PcncAAAD structural elements to its activity will be developed. Finally, through mutating key interface residues, first computationally and then experimentally, we plan to fully disentangle the roles played by the unique C-terminus appendage domain in regulating the activity of the fungal enzyme. Apart from a thorough understanding of the structure-function relationship in PcncAAAD, our results may create new bioengineering opportunities for the synthesis of psilocybin and its analogs. In addition, strategies to manipulate PcncAAAD activity may shed light onto future design and engineering efforts targeting other PLP-dependent or ion-activatable enzymes. 來自裸蓋菇的芳香氨基酸脱羧酶（PcncAAAD）負責催化裸蓋菇素生物合成的第一步。裸蓋菇素是一種精神藥物，在治療一系列嚴重的精神疾病上有潛在應用。不同於哺乳動物和植物中的脱羧酶，PcncAAAD可被鈣離子激活，進而帶來高至500倍的催化效率。近期，我們的實驗合作者發現PcncAAAD的鈣離子激活是由一個獨特的，300個氨基酸的C端附屬區域提供的。然而，這一激活的具體原理仍然未知。結合電腦模擬與合作者的實驗工作，我們計劃詳盡闡明PcncAAAD的鈣離子激活原理。我們初步的14-微秒模擬計算已揭示了這一激活過程中的重要構象變化。基於這些結果，我們將採用基於Drude振盪模型的可極化力場進一步研究離子結合帶來的酶構象變化，並量化各結構對這一激活過程的貢獻。最後，採用微秒MD模擬，我們將研究為闡明鈣離子激活原理而構建的各類突變體。除了詳細理解PcncAAAD的結構-功能關係，我們的結果可能為裸蓋菇素及其衍生物的合成帶以及其他基於PLP的或可被離子激活的酶帶來新的生物工程設計機會。

14305121.label: Realisation of objectives
14305121.value: Towards the proposed study on the calcium activation mechanism in PcncAAAD, we have conducted extensive molecular dynamics (MD) simulations with both the classical CHARMM force field and the polarizable Drude model. Along with our collaborator's mutagenesis and enzymatic studies, these simulations and experiments have fully addressed all three objectives: Objective 1: Verify ion-binding-induced enzyme conformational changes and identify the true calcium binding site. We have conducted six replicas of microsecond MD simulations of the wild type (WT) PcncAAAD in a calcium or a sodium solution. A differential contact map computed from these simulations pinpoints regions experiencing the greatest structural differences between these two ionic environments. Along with simulations of a truncated version of PcncAAAD lacking any enzymatic activity, we identified three core structural elements, namely, the N-terminal domain (NTD), the active site, and a "lid-rim" structure, that characterized the ion-binding induced conformational changes of the enzyme. Next, to further probe the role of a "lid" loop capping a short alpha-helix at the "rim" of the active site, we designed and simulated four mutants targeting this lid-rim structure. After verifying their destabilizing effect on the enzymatic structure through extensive MD simulations, our experimental collaborator measured the mutants' activity and showed that all four mutants were indeed deactivated. Collectively, these results validate that the aforementioned structural elements underlie the calcium-mediated activation of PcncAAAD. Finally, to differentiate the role played by the two metal-binding sites (A and B) of PcncAAAD, we designed and simulated a series of mutants, including two that destroyed either site A or B, as well as one that destroyed both sites. Through their comparison with WT simulations and the corresponding experimental verification, we conclude that both sites A and B are true calcium binding sites. Nonetheless, while site A is crucial for maintaining a functional lid-rim structure and enabling the enzyme's activation, site B only plays a supportive role by stabilizing the CTD structure. In summary, Objective 1 has been realized. Objective 2: Examine the impact of PcncAAAD structural elements on its activity. Based on the key structural elements identified in objective 1, we designed a relative conformational variation (RCV) scoring scheme. Specifically, we took WT PcncAAAD in a calcium buffer as the native conformation, with its median root mean square deviation (RMSD) mapped to 0; we then took the truncated PcncAAAD in a sodium solution as the completely inactive conformation with its median RMSD mapped to 1. The thus established RCV scoring scheme allowed us to design and predict loss-of-function mutations to validate the calcium activation mechanism of PcncAAAD. In addition to developing the RCV scoring scheme as proposed, we further differentiated the role of calcium in PcncAAAD activation through additional holo-enzyme simulations. Specifically, we modelled the holo-PcncAAAD in complex with its reaction intermediate, in order to investigate whether calcium may directly impact substrate and co-factor binding. The simulations clearly revealed calcium being excluded from the well-sealed active site when the loop adopted a closed-state conformation, precluding direct interactions between the divalent cation and the substrate. In summary, Objective 2 has also been realized. Objective 3: Disentangle the roles of C-terminus appendage domain. To disentangle the role of the C-terminus appendage domain (CTD), in addition to the full-length PcncAAAD simulations conducted using the classical CHARMM force field, we performed replicas of microsecond Drude simulations of the CTD alone in either calcium or sodium solution. Comparative analysis of these simulations revealed a “splitting” deformation of the CTD upon calcium unbinding at site B, which was located at the interface between its double β-barrels. Our analysis shows that a stable double-β-barrel-fold conformation of CTD provides the necessary structural stability and suitable interacting geometry for two binding interfacial regions between the CTD and NTD, i.e. the intra- and inter-monomer NTD-CTD contact regions. These results clearly pinpointed the role of the CTD --- its two β-barrels each contributed to an NTD-CTD interface and only when both interfaces are stabilized, through calcium binding at sites A and B, respectively, the enzyme achieves its maximum activity. Destabilization of either interface reduces structural stability and enzymatic activity, although the effect is more severe upon destabilization of the intra-monomer NTD-CTD interface near site A, since this site is located right above the active pocket. Through binding to site B, calcium stabilizes the CTD’s own structural integrity, thereby, contributing to the stability of the inter-monomer NTD-CTD interface. Therefore, in addition to contributing three residues to site A, the CTD plays the additional role of stabilizing the inter-monomer NTD-CTD interface for maintaining the overall structural integrity of PcncAAAD. Overall, the hierarchical stabilization revealed by our simulations highlights a sophisticated regulatory architecture that enables a distal, non-catalytic domain, i.e., the CTD, to deliver a substantial impact on the activity of PcncAAAD. In summary, Objective 3 has been realized.

14305121.label: Major findings and research outcome
14305121.value: In this project, we have employed molecular dynamics simulations using both classical and polarizable force fields, validated by experimental mutagenesis and in vitro enzyme assays, to decipher PcncAAAD's calcium activation mechanism. We show that between its two metal-binding sites, the site at the intra-monomer NTD-CTD interface (site A) plays a primary role in the calcium activation of PcncAAAD, whereas the secondary site within the unique CTD (site B) contributes to the calcium-mediated stabilization of enzyme structure. We further demonstrate that binding of calcium, but not sodium, exerts a profound influence on PcncAAAD activity by stabilizing a "lid-rim" structure underlying site A, which in turn maintains the integrity of the substrate-binding environment. In silico mutations disrupting site A or the lid-rim structure reveal severe structural distortion of the active site, leading to reduced or even eliminated activity as confirmed by in vitro enzymatic assays. Albeit distant from the active site, calcium binding at site B stabilizes the CTD, promoting the integrity of the NTD-CTD interface, thus playing a supportive role in PcncAAAD activation. The above structure-related calcium activation mechanism is further supported by holo-enzyme simulations, where a closed catalytic loop can seal the active site against direct ion participation in the catalytic process. Overall, the computational and experimental studies conducted in this project pinpoint the molecular mechanism underlying the noncanonical activation of PcncAAAD by calcium. These findings deepen our understanding of metal-activatable enzymes and hold promise for the rational design of engineered enzymes for the synthesis of aromatic amino acid derivatives. The above results have been summarized in our manuscript titled "Calcium Activation Mechanism of a Noncanonical Aromatic L-Amino Acid Decarboxylase from Psilocybin Mushroom", which was submitted to Communications Biology in Mar, 2025. After receiving the review in May, 2025, the PI and collaborator conducted new simulations and experiments to address reviewers' questions. The revised manuscript was re-submitted in Dec, 2025 and is attached to this report. The PI has presented findings from this project in two international conferences, namely, the 11th Congress of the International Society for Theoretical Chemical Physics (ISTCP-2024) at Qingdao, Shandong, China, in October, 2024, and the APS Joint March and April Meeting Global Physics Summit 2025 at Anaheim, CA, USA, in March, 2025. A PhD student has been trained and defended in 2023 with a thesis title "Molecular Dynamics Simulations of PcncAAAD, AtEPS1 and Perovskite Quantum Dots and Modeling of ZnC-finger Analog".

14305121.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14305121.value: The work conducted in this project has laid the foundation of further computational investigation of other members of the AAAD family and, more broadly, other enzymes with structure-dependent activities and functions. The RCV scoring scheme developed here can be adapted to design in sillico mutants and predict their stability and structure-induced functional changes. Building upon the work conducted in this project, we plan to join forces again with our experimental collaborator to investigate a number of other enzyme systems, examining their conformational changes during substrate binding, product unbinding as well as their interactions with partner proteins, e.g., membrane transporters.

14305121.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14305121.value: Unlike other members of the aromatic amino acid decarboxylase (AAAD) family, the fungal PcncAAAD contains a unique C-terminal appendage domain (CTD) and two metal-binding sites. Our work has provided mechanistic insights into the calcium activation of this enzyme. Employing a tailored scoring scheme, we assess a series of carefully designed mutants in molecular dynamics simulations, followed by experimental validation. Our findings reveal that the metal-binding site A, located at the intra-monomer interface between the N-terminal domain (NTD) and the CTD, is crucial for maintaining a functional lid-rim structure and enabling PcncAAAD's activation, while the metal-binding site B plays a supportive role by stabilizing its CTD structure. Through simulating the holo-enzyme in complex with a reaction intermediate, we further show that calcium is unlikely to participate in direct interactions with the substrate. Overall, our findings provide new insights into the intricate structure-function relationship underlying the calcium activation of PcncAAAD, while also uncovering generalizable principles for the design and engineering of metal-activatable enzymes for diverse applications.

14305621.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14305621.value: 這項擬議研究的目的，是開發一種高效的芳香族陽離子的有機 π-酸催化體系，應用於各種化學反應。 “π-酸”是具有酸性表面的缺電子芳族化合物。典型的例子是帶有吸電子取代基的苯衍生物（例如六氟苯）。與路易斯酸或布朗斯台德酸不同，π-酸不具有布朗斯台德酸性，並且對水分不敏感。π-酸可以很容易地與電子供體（例如，氮、羰基氧、陰離子）發生非共價相互作用。 非共價相互作用在催化化學轉化中的應用引起了科學界越來越多的關注，因為其催化效果能夠引發有趣的反應性。一個新興的研究領域涉及使用π-酸作為有機催化劑（也稱為陰離子-π-催化）。π-酸催化劑具有高方向性相互作用和可擴展的 π-表面性質。非布朗斯台德酸性性質增加了π-酸催化劑在化學轉化中官能團的兼容性。有機催化劑也被認為是金屬催化劑的更環保替代品。π-酸強度和空間位阻易於調節。然而，許多π-酸因其整體電荷中性結構而呈弱酸性，導致其催化效率不理想。芳族化合物陽離子（例如咪唑鎓）是更強的π-酸，但它們的酸度通常會因其對應的陰離子（例如咪唑氯化物中的氯離子）與π-酸表面的作用而顯著地削弱它的催化效果。 我們的研究組近年來從事基於非共價相互作用的有機催化的發展（例如Yeung, Y.-Y. et al. Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2018, 57, 3485; Angew. Chem. Int Ed. 2018, 57, 12869; ACS Catal. 2019, 9, 8083). 根據以往的經驗，我們擬議開發強π-酸催化劑，以拓寬非共價催化反應的應用。 最近，在一項未發表的工作中，我們發現衍生自咪唑鎓二溴化硒化合物的π-酸可以有效地活化喹啉、亞胺和 N-溴代琥珀酰亞胺，並分別催化轉移氫化、Friedel-Crafts 反應和親電鹵化反應。咪唑鎓硫屬元素化物與分子鹵素反應能夠輕易地製備π-酸催化劑。環丙烯陽離子衍生的π-酸也可以通過類似的方法製備。它們的強π-酸性質可歸因於其對應陰離子的有效隔離。我們發現這些π-酸的催化性能優於許多其他酸性有機催化劑。基於這些初步發現，在本研究中，我們計劃進一步開發和探索π-酸催化劑在各種轉化中的應用。我們預計新的π-酸催化體系將成為有機合成的有用工具。

14305621.label: Realisation of objectives
14305621.value: 1. Prepare a series of pi-acid organocatalysts At the initial stage of the project, we prepared a series of cyclopropenium chalcogen dihalide salt catalysts. A representative catalyst synthesis began with amination of the tetrachlorocyclopropene to give the NCy2 substituted cyclopropene. Selenylation of the cyclopropene with sodium hydrogen selenide gave the corresponding cyclopropenium selenide. Subsequently, treatment of the selenide with molecular bromine gave cyclopropenium selenium dibromide as an orange solid in 90% yield. Under similar reaction conditions by using sodium sulfide instead of sodium hydrogen selenide, cyclopropenium sulfur dibromide was obtained as a reddish brown solid smoothly (92%). These compounds could be prepared in gram-scale and were found to be benchtop-stable at least for months. Using this approach, we also prepared the imidazolium chalcogen dihalide salt catalysts. Single crystal samples of these chalcogen dihalide salts were obtained and studied using X-ray diffractometry. The results suggest that the structures were in favor of the zwitterionic resonance forms bearing stable and unoccupied cationic moieties. 2. Examine the performance of the pi-acid organocatalysts in various transformations that involve the activation of imines, carbonyls, epoxides and anions These catalysts were then subjected to the investigation. Transfer hydrogenation of quinoline with Hantzsch ester was used in the benchmarking study. To our delight, excellent yields of the desired hydrogenated products were achieved when the reactions were carried out with just 1 mol% of the cyclopropenium chalcogen dihalide salt catalysts for 5 min. The catalytic performance of the cyclopropenium catalysts was even better than that of the typical phosphoric acids, halogen bond, anion-pi, and urea catalysts. The scope was then studied. It was found that the catalytic protocol was generally applicable to a range of imine substrates with electron-withdrawing and electron-donating substituents. Imine that is derived from acetophenone was also compatible with the system. Moreover, the catalytic protocol was found to be applicable to the transfer hydrogenation of quinolines to tetrahydroquinolines. A number of quinolines bearing methyl, phenyl, methoxy, and fluorine groups gave the corresponding products in good yields. Next, Friedel-Crafts reaction between imine and indole was performed in another benchmarking study. This approach is highly useful in the preparation of bis-indole products that exist in numerous marine and terrestrial natural compounds having interesting biological activities. However, this type of reaction usually requires strongly acidic catalysts that are moisture sensitive. Some common organocatalysts were found to be unable to promote the reaction. In contrast, the cyclopropenium chalcogen dihalide catalysts were able to promote the reaction in excellent yield. The scope was then studied and the catalytic protocol was applicable to various imines bearing electron-withdrawing and donating substituents to give the bis-indole products in good yields. Other than N-methyl indole, a range of unprotected N-H indoles with bromide, methyl and methoxy substituents were also compatible with the catalytic protocol, furnishing the desired products smoothly. The bis-indole products could also be obtained by the reaction between the mono-indole substrates and one equivalent of alkyl amides under the optimized conditions. The same catalytic protocol could also be used in the preparation of unsymmetrical bis-indoles that are also valuable pharmaceutical building blocks. We also studied the imidazolium chalcogen dihalide salts in catalytic halogenation of arenes. In general, the catalytic protocol could be applied to various arene substrates and excellent yields and regioselectivity were obtained by using very low catalyst loading (down to 0.01 mol%). For instance, alkoxy (methoxy, isopropoxy, benzyloxy) arenes were brominated to give the corresponding brominated arenes smoothly. The less reactive substrates bearing alkyl or electron-withdrawing groups were examined and they could be halogenated using a relatively higher loading of catalyst. Less hindered alkyl substrates typically suffer from difficulty in controlling the regioselectivity. Nonetheless, good regioselectivity was obtained using the imidazolium chalcogen dihalide catalyst and N-bromosuccinimide as the halogen source. Alkyl substrates, including s-butylbenzene, xylenes, and mestylene were examined, and their corresponding mono-brominated products were obtained with excellent regioselectivity. Other than ether, nitrogen-substituted substrates, including anilines, indolines, and phenyl acetamides were also compatible to give the desired products in excellent yield. Aldehyde was susceptible to oxidation with halogen sources. Nonetheless, the substrates bearing aldehyde functional group remained intact. Moreover, alkyl naphthalenes, naphthyl ethers, and naphthanols could be brominated with excellent yields and regioselectivity. Polyaromatic compounds, including anthracenes and binaphthalenes were also studied. It is typically non-trivial to control the bromination because there are multiple bromination sites. Nonetheless, the corresponding monobrominated products were obtained in satisfying conversions. Heteroaromatic compounds such as pyrazole and quinoline were also compatible. Other than bromination, we also examined the catalytic protocol in selected substrates using other halogen sources, including N-chlorosuccinimide (NCS) and N-iodosuccinimide (NIS), and the corresponding chlorinated and iodinated products were obtained smoothly. Brominated compounds have emerged as promising tools in medicine, leveraging bromine’s distinct advantages for diagnostic imaging and radiotherapy. Compared to fluorine and iodine, bromine isotopes offer a good balance; they have longer half-lives than fluorine and greater in vivo stability than iodine, making them particularly suitable for PET imaging. Thus, we have utilized the newly developed catalytic protocol to perform late-stage bromination of several valuable drug molecules and bioactive compounds, including Ipriflavone, Naproxen, Sulfachloropyridazine, Pyriproxyfen, Tocopherol, Xanthotoxin, Bifendate, Cloquintocet, Napropamide, Estrone, and tyrosine derivatives. These drug molecules contain multiple functional groups that are sensitive to base, acid, and oxidant. Nonetheless, all these compounds were successfully mono-brominated with good regioselectivity. After demonstrating that the imidazolium chalcogen dibromides could be potent catalysts to activate N-haloamide reagents, we envisioned that the catalysts could catalyze other halogenations and mechanistically unrelated reactions. Thus, they were used to promote the electrophilic bromolactonization of carboxylic acid to give the corresponding bromolactone quantitatively. The catalysts were also applied to activate quinoline in the Hantzsch ester reduction to give dihydroquinoline in 97% yield. The catalysts were also applied to the Mannich reactions for the synthesis of amines. During the research endeavor, we also developed some methods based on chalcogen catalysis. In addition, during the study of transfer hydrogenation, it was unexpected to realize that Hantzsch ester itself could promote ipso-hydroxylation of boronic acids in the absence of external catalyst. 3. Evaluate the performance of the chiral pi-acid organocatalysts in the asymmetric transformations We also prepared a series of chiral chalcogen dihalide catalysts to investigate their applications in asymmetric transformations. First, chiral amines were reacted with formaldehyde and glyoxal in the presence of HCl gave chiral imidazolium salts. Chalcogenation of the imidazolium salts using elemental chalcogen furnished chalcoureas. Oxidation of the chalcogen in chalcoureas by molecular halogens provided the chiral catalysts. The performance of these catalysts were examined using the reactions stated in the abovementioned objective 2. Moderate-to-good ees were obtained in different entries and further optimizations are underway. For example, synthesis of various bis-indoles were achieved in moderate ees. These results are pending publications. 4. Publish the results in world-class peer-reviewed international journals Under this project, publications including Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2025, e202511770; ACS Catal. 2024, 14, 3018-3027; ACS Catal. 2024, 14, 9198-9206; ACS Catal. 2023, 13, 2386-2395; Org. Chem. Front. 2022, 9, 4091; New J. Chem. 2022, 46, 21047. The detail appears in Part C. Overall, all objectives have been fully realized and a summary of the major research outcomes are shown below.

14305621.label: Major findings and research outcome
14305621.value: 1. Noncovalent interactions originated from C(sp3)−H···X hydrogen bonds frequently appear in different areas but employing those interactions in catalysis is less common, attributed to the insufficient catalytic performance due to their relatively weak interaction strength. In this study, we have developed cyclopropenium chalcogen dihalides as catalysts, in which effective site isolation of the counteranion significantly enhances the availability of the noncovalent interaction donor. Their catalytic performance in various reactions are comparable to those of typical Lewis acids and much better than those of many common catalysts based on noncovalent interactions. 2. In this study, we found that Lewis basic selenourea derived from imidazole can be oxidized by the halogen source to give a benchtop stable and non-hygroscopic imidazolium hypervalent selenium dibromide catalyst. The negative charge in the hypervalent selenium compound is stabilized by the electronegative bromide, leading to the site-isolated and unoccupied imidazolium cationic moiety for the activation of reagents. The catalytic protocol was found to be applicable to late-stage halogenation of drug molecules with low catalyst loading. Further study revealed that hypervalent imidazolium selenium dibromide can generally be applied to other mechanistically unrelated hydrogen bond-catalyzed reactions. 3. Soft Lewis basic sulfides are frequently employed as catalysts in the electrophilic functionalization of unsaturated compounds because the reactions can be operated under mild conditions. Among these reactions, electrophilic selenylation reactions are less reported, partly due to the lack of sufficiently strong Lewis base catalysts. We have developed cyclopropenium sulfides as strong and soft Lewis base catalysts for electrophilic selenylation of phenols. The catalytic protocol was also found to be useful for the late-stage modification of tyrosine peptides. Mechanistic studies indicate that the catalyst can activate the amide-type electrophilic reagents by effective site isolation of the counteranion via nonclassical hydrogen bonds. 4. Electrophilic halogenation reactions are highly useful in various areas. N-Haloamides are commonly used as halogen sources because of high stability and commercial availability. In order to activate N-haloamides, Lewis basic chalcogens are commonly used as catalysts to site-isolate the strongly coordinating amide moieties. However, the corresponding trisubstituted chalcogenonium−halogen cationic intermediate is sensitive to moisture and nucleophiles, leading to poor compatibility in some reactions. In this study, we have developed an efficient catalytic halogenation protocol using phenyl selenium with ortho-substituted carboxylic acid as the catalyst. The catalytic system is applicable to a wide range of electrophilic functionalization reactions including haloamidation, haloesterification, halocycloetherification, halolactonization, aromatic halogenation, and halopolyene cyclization reactions.

14305621.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14305621.value: Acid catalysts are very useful in various chemical transformations. While acid catalysis is well established, some acid catalysts involve toxic metals. In addition, many acids are moisture sensitive and tedious reaction setup is needed. In some other cases, substrates containing acid-sensitive functional groups or Lewis basic substituents are incompatible. In this research project, aromatic cationic catalysts are used to activate electron-donor substrates such as carbonyl and imine compounds. The steric and electronic demands of the catalysts can be altered easily by changing the substituents. These catalysts are insensitive to moisture and the catalytic reactions can be operated under ambient conditions. In addition, the catalytic performance of the newly developed acid catalysts is superior to some commonly used Lewis acid catalysts due to minimized poisoning effect. Moreover, highly regio and chemoselective reactions can be achieved. In future, we will further explore the applications of aromatic cationic catalysts in other chemo and/or stereoselective reactions that can be operated under ambient conditions and has high functional group compatibility.

14305621.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14305621.value: Many chemical manufacturing processes are energy- and atom-inefficient, leading to the generation of significant amounts of wastes and emissions. To meet the growing demand on energy for the global economy, it becomes more important than ever to look for green alternatives of energy-efficient processes. However, the current state of technology lags behind the schedule to meet the international targets. Small molecule catalysts are considered as nanoscale molecular machines that can provide control in various transformations at molecular level. Catalysis underpins many industries as over 90% of chemicals produced rely on the use of catalysts to certain extent. It is obvious that catalytic processes play a key role in improving air and water quality, reduce energy consumption and emission, and offer solutions to long-term sustainable energy and environmental protection. In the current project, we have developed a number of useful catalytic protocols using aromatic cationic catalysts. Our work on the novel catalysis provides a very useful tool for various transformations. In addition, organocatalysis is mild and metal-free, which are attractive features to the manufacturing sectors. The research endeavor results in the synthesis of a wide range of useful building blocks for various medicinal and chemical applications.

14305721.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14305721.value: This proposal aims to carry out state-of-art in operando structural characterization on all-inorganic perovskite solar cells (PSCs). We will design and construct a home-made in operando grazing-incidence wide-angle X-ray scattering (GIWAXS) chamber to monitor the structural and phase evolution of all-inorganic PSCs under various work conditions. Organic-inorganic hybrid PSCs have realized power conversion efficiencies over 25% recently, approaching the benchmark achieved by the market-dominating polycrystalline silicon solar cells. However, the incorporation of organic A-site cations imposes intrinsic drawbacks in thermal and light stability, being inevitable obstacles on the road of the commercialization of PSCs. Consequently, extensive research efforts have been devoted to developing all-inorganic PSCs, mainly by employing Cesium (Cs) ions to replace organic A-site cations. The relatively too small Cs ion, however, challenges the formation of a stable photoactive black phase with corner-sharing PbX6 octahedra. Consequently, the operational stability, namely the stability of working all-organic PSCs, is one of major research focuses. Phase segregation and decomposition, irreversible ion migration, and interface degradation are often reported due to its intrinsic phase instability. On the other hand, our preliminary results indicated that positive outcomes such as self-defect passivation can occur with light illumination and external bias. Therefore, an in-depth investigation of the structural and phase evolution of operating all-organic PSCs is highly demanded to understand the underlying mechanism of the abovementioned phenomena, and will ultimately lead to strategies of suppressing degradation and curing defects for high-performance all-inorganic PSCs with promising operational stability. Herein, the proposed in operando GIWAXS characterization will allow a direct correlation between the operational device characteristics and structural and phase evolution. the structural and phase dynamics acquired can reveal vital aspects of all-inorganic PSCs, such as the phase stability, intrinsic strain and lattice distortion, which will be correlated with their device performance measured simultaneously. We plan to interrogate fundamental properties of all-inorganic PSCs, for instance, defect tolerance, ion migration, ionic and electric conduction, and interfacial properties that correlate with the structural change. We believe the successful implementation of the proposed work will provide a profound understanding of the working and degradation mechanism of all-inorganic PSCs. It will offer insightful guidelines to identify new high-performance and stable all-inorganic perovskite materials and to develop novel fabrication recipes. In addition, the in operando characterization chamber to be constructed in this project can potentially be utilized to study the operational mechanism of other photovoltaic/optoelectrical devices, making broader contributions to the field. 該提案旨在對全無機钙钛矿太陽能電池（PSC）進行最先進的原位工作結構表徵研究。我們將設計並建造掠入射廣角 X 射線散射（GIWAXS）原位工作表徵腔体，以監測各種工作條件下全無機PSC的結構和相位演變。 有機-無機雜化PSC最近實現了超過 25% 的光电轉換效率，接近主導市場的多晶硅太陽能電池的性能。然而，有機陽離子在熱和光穩定性方面存在缺陷，成為PSC商業化進程中不可避免的障礙。因此，廣泛的研究工作致力於開發全無機PSC，使用銫離子代替有機陽離子。然而，相對太小的銫離子對形成具有穩定的具有共頂點的 PbX6 八面體的光活性黑色相構成挑戰。因此，其工作穩定性是研究重點之一。全無機PSC相分解、不可逆離子遷移和界面退化等缺點經常被報導。另一方面，我們的初步結果表明，在光照和外部偏壓下會產生積極的自我缺陷鈍化，迫切需要對全無機PSC的結構和相演變進行深入研究來了解上述現象的潛在機制，並最終為高性能全無機PSC提供抑制退化和修復缺陷的策略。 原位工作 GIWAXS 表徵可以直接關聯全無機PSC的工作性能與結構相變，理解相穩定性、固有應變和晶格畸變等性質的原理。我們計劃研究全無機PSC缺陷耐受性、離子遷移、離子和電子傳導等基本特性，以及與結構變化相關的界面特性。 我們相信，本提案的成功實施將深入理解全無機 PSC 的工作和退化機制，提供有見地的指導方針，以助尋找新的高性能和穩定的全無機PSC材料，開發新的製造配方。此外，該項目開發的原位工作表徵方法也可用於研究其他光電器件的運行機制，為該領域做出更廣泛的貢獻。

14305721.label: Realisation of objectives
14305721.value: We have designed and constructed an in-operando chamber for grazing-incidence wide-angle X-ray scattering (GIWAXS) (Objective 1). The chamber is airtight and equipped with two stomata for gas in and out so that the measurement can be conducted in various kinds of atmosphere. The chamber has a quartz window on top for stimulated sunlight shining through on the sample and Kapton windows on sides for X-ray in and out. We optimized the thickness of the Kapton film (25 μm) to balance the background scattering and mechanical load. Inside the chamber, there are patterned electrode contacts, providing the condition for I-V measurement and bias control when the external source meter is connected. Besides the production of the designed chamber, we have designed a program for biasing, I-V measurement and data saving. To systematically investigate the correlation between device characteristics and operational stability with crystal structures in terms of crystallinity, lattice constants, orientation and lattice strain (Objective 2), we applied perovskite quantum dots (PQDs) to regulate the growth of tin-based perovskite films. With the assistance of PQDs, we have realized an epitaxial-like growth of highly oriented tin-based perovskite films. The synchrotron-based in situ GIWAXS has found PQDs can act as nucleation centers to promote the growth of highly oriented perovskite crystals for both FASnI3 and MASnI3 systems. By tuning the lattice mismatch between the PQDs and the tin-based perovskite, the degree of lattice strain has been regulated, leading to reduced defect density and improved efficiency and stability. This work has been published in ACS Energy letters (ACS Energy letters, 2022, 7, 10, 3251–3259). We also utilized in situ GIWAXS to investigate the distinct phase behaviors of CsPbI3 PQDs under two different temperature profiles–instant heating-up (IHU) and slow heating-up (SHU). IHU induced a phase transition from black to yellow phase, while SHU stabilizes the majority in the black phase. Structural refinement analyses revealed that the removal of surface ligands triggered the phase transition and switched the energy landscape. The extended relaxation time afforded by the SHU process fostered more ordered PQD packing, which maintained the lattice symmetry and enhanced the stability of the black phase. This work was published in Small 2023, 19, 47, 2303885. To further correlate the packing behaviour of CsPbI3 PQDs in thin films and its impact on the device performance, we performed GISAXS and multi-length-scale all-atom and coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations to elucidate the PQD packing density and the influence of organic surface ligands on it. We found mixing of CsPbI3 PQDs with two different sizes promoted closer face-to-face contact, which exhibited largely suppressed trap-assisted recombination, much longer carrier lifetime, and thereby improved power conversion efficiency. This work was published in ACS Nano 2023, 17, 20, 20634−20642. To understand the fundamental degradation pathways of all-inorganic perovskite solar cells and to elucidate the influence of intrinsic properties (e.g., defect tolerance and ion migration) on their phase, light, and humidity stability (Objective 3), we precisely engineered the crystallization of all-inorganic CsPb(I₁₋ₓBrₓ)₃ perovskite during high-temperature annealing. We revealed the formation of a black γ-phase at low temperature (LT-γ-phase), which was temporarily stabilized by the dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) solvent. It transformed to δ-phase when DMSO evaporated and restored to γ-phase at high temperature (HT-γ-phase). Notably, we found that an additional methylammonium chloride (MACl) treatment further stabilizes the LT-γ-phase, allowing a direct transition from LT-γ-phase to HT-γ-phase while bypassing the δ-phase, resulting in a uniform and pinhole-free film with reduced defects and released strain. We achieved an efficiency as high as 20.1 % and improved the device stability under illumination and humidity (Objective 4). This work was published in Nano Energy, 2023, 117, 108907. We also performed operando GIWAXS measurements with the designed chamber to investigate the structural stability of tin-based perovskite solar cells under operating conditions (Objective 3). We designed an ultra-thin (≈3 nm) dual-functional lead sulfide (PbS) capping layer onto the perovskite surface to serve a critical dual role: protecting the underlying tin-based perovskite from oxidation and moisture and thereby mitigating its degradation; improving the interfacial electronic properties to enable efficient charge extraction. We conducted operando GIWAXS measurements under constant AM1.5G illumination and a constant voltage near the maximum power point (0.6 V) in ambient air to simulate real-world operating conditions and capture potential structural changes. Without the PbS layer, the control device exhibited significant degradation under the combined stress of voltage and illumination. The intensity of the (100) peak initially increased slightly within the first 20 min, likely due to light-induced lattice expansion that relaxed local strain and improved lattice order. However, this was followed by a progressive decrease over the next 40 minutes, culminating in a net reduction of 7.4% after 60 minutes. In contrast, the device with PbS cap maintained much greater structural stability. The (100) peak intensity of the device with the PbS layer remained relatively stable and even increased 3.6% over the same operation period, signifying the robust structural stability of the perovskite film under operational stresses when protected by the PbS layer. This work was recently published in Small 2025, e06340. To provide guidelines to develop high-performance and stable all-inorganic perovskites (objective 4), we have investigated the interfacial layer of all-inorganic CsPb(I1-xBrx)3 solar cells. We modified the commonly used ZnO electron transporting layer by introducing appropriate amount of PbX2 (X = I−, Cl−, and CH3COO−) into the ZnO precursor solution. The modified PbX2:ZnO substrate promoted the growth of all-inorganic perovskite layer with improved morphology and orientational order. Besides, the PbX2 resulted in increased oxygen vacancies in ZnO, forming a favorable energy level alignment with the perovskite layer thus facilitating charge extraction and suppressing charge recombination. Consequently, the CsPb(I1−xBrx)3 PSCs based on PbX2:ZnO exhibited enhanced stability and performance. The efficiency was boosted from 17.64% to 20.04% with an improved fill factor of 84.14% and a VOC of 1.28 V. This work has been published in EcoMat, 2022, 4, 4, e12192. Furthermore, we also utilized synchrotron based in situ GIWAXS to investigate the branched iso-butylammonium (iso-BA+) and the linear-shaped n-butylammonium (n-BA+) on the crystallization of 2D perovskite. It was found due to the lower aggregation enthalpies of iso-BA+, tends to form large-size clusters in the precursor solution, which can act as pre-nucleation sites to expedite the crystallization of vertically oriented 2D perovskite (Small, 2023, 2206787). We also carried out collaboration studies on developing efficient hole transporting layers for perovskite solar cells (Advanced Materials, 2022, 34, 49, 2110587) and oriented growth of perovskite through an in-plane directional crystallization technique (Adv. Energy Mater. 2024, 14, 2303988).

14305721.label: Major findings and research outcome
14305721.value: Through this project, we published 9 publications in peer-reviewed journals and presented our results times in local and international conferences (part C). Overall, our results provide fundamental insights and practical strategies for the correlation of crystal structure, device performance, and operational stabilitie of perovskite photovoltaic materials towards high-efficiency and stable solar cells. Major finding 1: We designed and constructed a novel in operando GIWAXS chamber capable of simulating real-world photovoltaic working conditions, including controlled atmosphere, light illumination, and electrical biasing. The chamber features optimized Kapton windows and integrated electrodes, enabling high-resolution X-ray scattering simultaneous with device performance tracking. Major finding 2: We systematically monitored the structural and phase evolution of all-inorganic and tin-based perovskite films and devices. Using in situ and operando GIWAXS, we correlated device performance with structural parameters such as phase purity, crystallinity, lattice strain, and crystal orientation. Major finding 3: We uncovered fundamental degradation pathways in perovskite materials, highlighting the roles of surface ligands, lattice strain, and environmental factors. We demonstrated that tailored annealing profiles and chemical treatments (e.g., MACl, PbS) can suppress detrimental phase transitions and significantly enhance humidity, light, and operational stability. Major finding 4: We developed multiple effective strategies for achieving high-performance and stable devices, including: mixed-size quantum dot packing, PbS capping layers, PQD-assisted epitaxial growth, and modified transport layers. These approaches yielded devices with remarkable efficiencies and improved durability, providing clear guidelines for future material and process design.

14305721.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14305721.value: 1. Broader application of the in operando chamber to other optoelectronic devices. The successfully developed in operando GIWAXS chamber represents a versatile and powerful diagnostic platform beyond perovskite solar cells. Its capability to simultaneously provide structural and electronic information under working conditions makes it highly applicable to a wide range of optoelectronic devices, such as light-emitting diodes (LEDs) and photodetectors. 2. Building on the success of our GIWAXS studies, a potential research direction is the integration of spectroscopic methods, such as photoluminescence, with X-ray scattering within the same chamber. This would allow us to simultaneously capture charge carrier dynamics under operating conditions, providing a comprehensive view of the device degradation mechanisms.

14305721.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14305721.value: This project aimed to improve a new type of solar cell technology made from materials called perovskites, which are efficient at converting sunlight to electricity but tend to degrade quickly under real-world conditions. We built a special lab chamber to study these solar cells while in operation—exposed to light, air, and electric current—to understand how they change at the atomic level. We discovered key reasons why they break down and developed several methods to make them more stable and efficient, such as adding protective layers and improving how the materials are formed. As a result, we created solar cells that not only perform better but also last longer. Our findings provide insightful guidelines for making perovskite solar cells a practical and reliable source of clean energy in the future.

14305821.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14305821.value: When it is not possible to compute the probability distribution of a random variable exactly, it is necessary to use a probability approximation. For example, the central limit theorem states that the distribution of a sum of a large number of independent random variables can be approximated by a Gaussian distribution. In practice, however, such simple first-order approximations may not be sufficiently accurate. To overcome this shortcoming, scholars have studied asymptotic expansions containing additional correction terms. Such expansions are often referred to as Edgeworth expansions, in particular in the context of the central limit theorem. Edgeworth expansions have been derived and justified in various settings using characteristic functions. However, they can suffer from several issues: (1) They may approximate the distribution function of interest by a quantity which is not a proper distribution function (e.g., approximate probabilities can be negative); (2) They may not provide sufficiently accurate approximations to small probabilities. In this project, we will use Stein's method to derive and analyze new asymptotic expansions using invariant measures of suitable diffusions with state-dependent diffusion coefficients. Our new expansion will have the following advantages: (i) It will be given by probability distributions, offering easy interpretability via classical probability concepts such as moments; (ii) It will achieve better accuracy in approximating small probabilities; (iii) It will be able to handle general dependent random variables; and (iv) It can be used for multivariate approximations. More specifically, we will (a) obtain new asymptotic expansions in the one- and multi-dimensional central limit theorems using invariant measures of diffusions whose diffusion coefficient depends on the cumulants of the random variable/vector of interest; (b) use Stein's exchangeable pair approach to obtain asymptotic expansions in non-central limit theorems; (c) investigate possible improvements of the dependence on dimension in the large-dimensional setting using the asymptotic expansion; and (d) explore applications of the new asymptotic expansions to problems in statistics, machine learning, finance and stochastic systems. The outcome of this project will be of interest to both the theoretical and the applied probability community. 當無法準確計算隨機變量的概率分佈時，需要使用概率近似。例如，中心極限定理指出，大量獨立隨機變量之和的分佈可以近似為高斯分佈。然而，在實踐中，這種簡單的一階近似可能不夠準確。為了克服這個缺點，學者們研究了包含附加校正項的漸近展開式。這種擴展通常被稱為埃奇沃斯擴展，特別是在中心極限定理的範疇中。 埃奇沃斯展開式已經使用特徵函數在各種情形中推導出並證明其合理性。然而，它們可能會遇到幾個問題：（1）它們可能通過一個不是適當分佈函數的數量來近似感興趣的分佈函數（例如，近似概率可能為負）； (2) 它們可能無法為小概率提供足夠準確的近似值。 在這個項目中，我們將使用斯坦因方法，使用具有狀態相關擴散係數的擴散過程的不變測度來推導和分析新的漸近展開。我們的新擴展將具有以下優勢： (i) 它將由概率分佈給出，通過經典概率概念（例如矩）提供易於解釋性； (ii) 它將在逼近小概率時獲得更好的準確度； (iii) 將能夠處理一般的相依隨機變量； (iv) 它可用於多元近似。 更具體地說，我們將 (a) 使用擴散過程的不變測度獲得一維和多維中心極限定理中新的漸近擴展，其擴散係數取決於感興趣的隨機變量/向量的矩； (b) 使用斯坦因的可交換對方法在非中心極限定理中獲得漸近展開； (c) 使用漸近展開研究高維問題中維數依賴性的可能改進； (d) 探索新的漸近擴展在統計、機器學習、金融和隨機系統中的問題的應用。 該項目的結果將引起理論和應用概率社區的興趣。

In Ding and Fang (2025, Science China Mathematics), we applied a new asymptotic expansion to the exponential random graph model, which is widely used in statistics and machine learning. In Fang, Liu, Su and Wang (under review), we studied the asymptotic expansion of large stochastic systems conditioning on their first-order observables. This addressed Objective 4.

Explore applications of the new asymptotic expansions to problems in statistics, machine learning, finance and stochastic systems.

14305821.label: Major findings and research outcome
14305821.value: It is of wide interest to obtain asymptotic expansions in probability approximations and this is the main topic of this project. Our main tool is Stein’s method. In Fang, Liu and Shao (2023, Bernoulli), we studied a two-term Edgeworth expansion for a changed measure in the multi-dimensional central limit theorem. We used the two-term Edgeworth expansion to improve the dependence on dimension in the large-dimensional central limit theorem. In Ding and Fang (2025, Science China Mathematics), we proposed a new asymptotic expansion using the Hoeffding decomposition in a non-central limit theorem setting. We applied the new asymptotic expansion to the exponential random graph model, which is widely used in statistics and machine learning. In Fang and Liu (2025, Bernoulli), we used Stein coupling to analyze asymptotic expansions. In Fang, Liu, Su and Wang (under review), we studied the asymptotic expansion of large stochastic systems conditioning on their first-order observables. Other related work includes: (i) From p-Wasserstein bounds to moderate deviations (Fang and Koike (2023)), (ii) Sharp high-dimensional central limit theorems for log-concave distributions (Fang and Koike (2024)), (iii) Normal approximation for exponential random graphs (Fang, Liu, Shao and Zhao (2025)), (iv) High-dimensional central limit theorems by Stein’s method in the degenerate case (Fang, Koike, Liu and Zhao (under review)).

14305821.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14305821.value: Several problems are left open by this project. (i) Skewness correction in high-dimensional central limit theorems. High- dimensional CLT is a relatively new topic, but has already attracted researchers from the fields of probability, statistics, and econometrics. One open problem in high- dimensional CLT is whether skewness correction brings any benefit to the approximation accuracy. We believe this is the case and we are currently working in this direction. (ii) Asymptotic expansions in functional approximations. Gaussian process approximations have been well studied in the literature. However, the asymptotic expansion in Gaussian process approximations is less developed. We believe it is an interesting potential direction to work on.

14305821.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14305821.value: A central theme in probability theory is approximating the distribution of a random variable of interest by a suitable limiting distribution. In practice, however, such simple first-order approximations may not be sufficiently accurate. It is of significant interest to obtain more accurate approximations using asymptotic expansions. In this project, we have studied a two-term Edgeworth expansion for a changed measure in the multi-dimensional central limit theorem. We used the two-term Edgeworth expansion to improve the dependence on dimension in the large-dimensional central limit theorem. Moreover, we have proposed a new asymptotic expansion using the Hoeffding decomposition in a non-central limit theorem setting. We applied the new asymptotic expansion to the exponential random graph model, which is widely used in statistics and machine learning. We used Stein’s method to analyze asymptotic expansions. Finally, we have studied the asymptotic expansion of large stochastic systems conditioning on their first-order observables. We expect these new theoretical developments as well as applications will enrich the asymptotic theory in probability and large sample theory in statistics and many other areas.

14306321.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14306321.value: One crucial aspect of the standard model of particle physics (SM) is the generation of the mass of electroweak gauge bosons, which is attributed to electroweak symmetry breaking through the Brout-Englert-Higgs mechanism; in turn, this mechanism requires the existence of a particle, which was discovered in 2012 by the ATLAS and CMS experimental collaborations using data from the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) of the European Organization for Nuclear Physics (CERN). The SM describes the Higgs boson as even under charge-parity inversion (CP); hence, the detailed study of the CP structure of the Higgs couplings, which could unveil deviations from a purely scalar interaction, constitutes an important probe for new physics. After the discovery, the LHC went over an extended shut-down period for maintenance and upgrades, and restarted operations with a collision energy of 13 TeV, in what is called the “Run 2” data-taking period, which ended in December 2018. After another extended shut-down, LHC collisions will resume in early 2021; “Run 3” will then increase the total integrated luminosity up to around 300 fb-1, which will have a significant impact on the sensitivity of several searches for new physics, as well as on the precision reached in the measurement of related SM processes. The Run 3 dataset will allow stringent constraints on potential non-SM contributions to the CP structure of the Higgs boson couplings. Hong Kong institutions, working jointly as the Joint Consortium for Fundamental Physics in Hong Kong (JCFP), were accepted in June of 2014 as members of the ATLAS Experimental Collaboration. Since then, Hong Kong researchers and students have made strong contributions to the analysis32 of LHC data and have adopted a number of responsibilities within ATLAS. The goal of this project is to further strengthen the participation of Hong Kong at CERN through work on the following areas: 1. Probe the CP structure of the coupling between the Higgs boson and tau leptons. 2. Study the performance of tau lepton reconstruction and identification algorithms in ATLAS in the phase space relevant for the CP study. 3. Train Hong Kong students and postdocs for research in the forefront of fundamental physics. These areas are designed to avoid overlap with the objectives of the JCFP proposal and, to the maximum extent possible, to complement them to build a complete and solid physics program from Hong Kong institutions, with a significant impact and a long-term contribution to LHC Physics.

14306321.label: Realisation of objectives
14306321.value: Objective 1. Probe the CP structure of the coupling between the Higgs boson and tau leptons. Ten years after the discovery of the Higgs boson [ATL12, CMS12], the study of its properties and its use as a possible tool in the search for physics beyond the Standard Model (BSM) remains among the most important and active areas of research at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) at CERN. In the Standard Model (SM), the Higgs boson is a purely even state under charge-parity inversion, and both ATLAS and CMS have excluded pure odd couplings between the Higgs boson and gauge vector bosons; however, the potential non-zero CP-odd contributions to these couplings are suppressed [Zha11] (or they enter via non-renormalizable terms [Har13, Gho19]); Higgs couplings to fermions may be more suitable to unveil potential BSM contributions because they could contribute at the tree level, which render both the tau and the top Yukawa couplings as observables of paramount interest. Our team has made major contributions to the first measurement at ATLAS of the CP properties of the Higgs boson interaction with tau leptons. We have been involved in most areas of the analysis, including likelihood fit studies, the development of fitting code, the study and evaluation of systematic uncertainties, fake backgrounds and trigger biases, and transverse spin correlation studies in the Drell-Yan background that helped validate the modelling of the dominant background in the measurement. Correspondingly, one of our group members was appointed to give the paper presentation on behalf of the analysis team in the ATLAS collaboration weekly meeting, and another group member was appointed as co-analysis contact. The results were published as an ATLAS conference note and in the journal EPJC [ATL23]. In the context of this analysis, we have also trained a few senior undergraduate students to study the use of a machine-learning approach to extract the CP information of the Higgs boson interaction with tau leptons targeting Run-3 measurements at ATLAS. This encompassed preparing the machine learning package and data samples for the students and studying the input feature importance and the impact of the missing neutrino information. We have gradually incorporated more detailed experimental settings as we move towards the analysis of the full ATLAS Run-3 data where detector and reconstruction effects and the corresponding uncertainties are expected to have a large impact on the classification performance. Objective 2. Study the performance of tau lepton reconstruction and identification algorithms in ATLAS in the phase space relevant for the CP study. Our group has maintained a continuous involvement in the study of the performance of tau identification algorithms used in the analysis of final states that involve tau leptons, both in direct collaboration with the ATLAS tau working group and within the ATLAS group in charge of the study of Higgs decays involving tau leptons. In earlier studies, we have studied and characterized the performance of the algorithms used in ATLAS to identify tau leptons using both a cut-based approach and scores based on machine learning techniques to select the events of interest in the search for a high-mass resonance able to decay into lepton flavor violating final states, and in the search for lepton-flavor violation in the decay of the Higgs boson. In this project, our focus has been on aspects of tau reconstruction directly relevant to the measurement of the parameters of interest for the CP measurement, like efficiencies and fake rates. Due to the physics environment that will be provided by the LHC during the run 3 data taking period, we extended our studies of the performance of tau leptons under a larger pileup (i.e., the number of proton-proton interactions per bunch crossing) and at the slightly larger center of mass energy attained in run 3 (13.6 TeV). We also studied how the classification of the decay modes of the tau leptons increases the sensitivity of the search. Objective 3. Train Hong Kong students and postdocs for research in the forefront of fundamental physics. One PhD student and three undergraduate students worked on the project. This has allowed them to benefit from the close interaction with colleagues from other ATLAS institutions (located both in Hong Kong and overseas), to work with recent machine learning and multivariate analysis techniques, to learn several of the tools used for research in High Energy Physics, and to work with recent proton-proton collision and Monte Carlo simulation data from the Large Hadron Collider on searches and measurements at the energy frontier. 14306321.label: Major findings and research outcome
14306321.value: A study of the charge conjugation and parity (CP) properties of the interaction between the Higgs boson and τ-leptons is presented. The study is based on a measurement of CP-sensitive angular observables defined by the visible decay products of τ-leptons produced in Higgs boson decays. The analysis uses 139 fb−1 of proton–proton collision data recorded at a centre-of-mass energy of √s =13 TeV with the ATLAS detector at the Large Hadron Collider. Contributions from CP-violating interactions between the Higgs boson and τ-leptons are described by a single mixing angle parameter φτ in the generalised Yukawa interaction. Without constraining the H → ττ signal strength to its expected value under the Standard Model hypothesis, the mixing angle φτ is measured to be 9◦ ±16◦, with an expected value of 0◦ ± 28◦ at the 68% confidence level. The pure CP-odd hypothesis is disfavoured at a level of 3.4 standard deviations. The results are compatible with the predictions for the Higgs boson in the Standard Model.

14306321.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14306321.value: There are several avenues to extend and/or refine the work done in this project. The methods and results used in the EPJC publication are optimised for the total integrated luminosity and physics environment corresponding to Run 2, while the Run 3 dataset will, by itself, more than double the amount of data available for a subsequent study. The center of mass energy for Run 3 will also be slightly larger, and a number of detector enhancements will allow for some improvements in lepton reconstruction performance. There is also ample room to explore further refinements of the classification of the tau-lepton reconstruction.

14306321.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14306321.value: This research project contributes to our understanding of the fundamental processes of Nature on two fronts: (a) searching for phenomena that is not expected in our current theories, and (b) improve the particle reconstruction tools used to study high-energy particle collisions. These objectives are pursued through the analysis of proton-proton collisions at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) at CERN in Geneva, Switzerland. There, protons travel almost at the speed of light; when they collide, they can transform into any particle allowed by the laws of Nature. Our current description of these laws (the "Standard Model", or SM) provides very precise predictions for the possible outcomes of these collisions, but we know that the SM is incomplete, so we are making a systematic search for phenomena not contained in it. We aim specifically to (a) measure the geometric properties of the way in which the Higgs boson, discovered in 2012, decays into tau leptons, to determine any possible discrepancies with the SM, and (b) improve the methods used to identify and reconstruct the particles that are produced in high-energy particle collisions at the Large Hadron Collider.

14306421.label: Project Objectives
14306421.value: (Generality) We study TAVC estimation via a general framework. We plan to (a) define a wide class of estimators in a neat and elegant way; (b) prove that many well-known existing estimators are special cases under our proposed framework; (c) show that both recursive and non-recursive estimators can be defined under our framework. (Principle) The TAVC estimators are derived from principles. We plan to (a) formulate the belief and philosophy that we usually wish to have as five concrete guiding principles; (b) use these five principles to guide us to define good estimators; and (c) demonstrate that the resulting estimators are more statistically sensible and have good properties. (Theory) The detailed theoretical properties of the estimators will be investigated. We plan to (a) derive a set of very general sufficient conditions for L2 consistent; (b) provide easily verifiable conditions for achieving algorithms that have O(1) time and space complexity; (c) compute the optimal convergence rate and optimal mean squared error of the estimators; (d) compare it with existing estimators in terms of both computational and statistical criteria. (Implementation) The implementation issues and related properties will be clearly presented for a better understanding of the estimators. We plan to (a) show that the estimator is always non-negative; (b) provide practical algorithms for different users’ specific situations; (c) demonstrate how to implement it with optimal parameters; and (d) apply it to a more general setting, e.g., multi-dimensional problems. (Application). We would like to apply our proposed estimators to various problems. We plan to (a) apply the recursive estimators to other related fields that could potentially be benefited; (b) connect different fields that fundamentally require the same techniques; (c) verify the advantages of using our proposed estimators in some real problems.
