14306421.label: Realisation of objectives
14306421.value: All five objectives of the proposal have been fully achieved. In Objective 1, we explore a general framework for time-average variance constant (TAVC) estimation and compare it with existing estimators. This objective, under both stationarity and nonstationarity assumptions, is addressed in “Principles of Statistical Inference in Online Problems” (Publication #8 in Part C) and “Online Difference-based Variance Estimators in Time Series” (Publication #11 in Part C), respectively. The first article provides the foundational basis for the entire research project. In particular, it presents the basic framework for online variance estimation based on decomposing a kernel into a tapering part and a subsample part. It also provides an explicit example of achieving an online estimator without compromising any statistical properties and discusses several applications that motivate other research outputs in this grant, as mentioned below. The second article was not originally anticipated in the proposal and emerged as an additional result, which extends the method from time series with a constant mean to time series with varying means. In Objective 2, we develop five general guiding principles for TAVC estimation to understand the fundamental structure of the problem and its potential for broader applications. The majority of this objective is addressed in “Principles of Statistical Inference in Online Problems” (Publication #8 in Part C) and further established in “Optimal Difference-based Variance Estimators in Time Series: A General Framework” (Publication #1 in Part C). The key idea is to use a global parameter for tuning the tapering part of the kernel while employing a local parameter to tune the subsample part. Additionally, the kernel must satisfy certain separability conditions to be recursive. Moreover, we generalize the principles from TAVC estimation to broader parameter estimation via the Generalized Method of Moments (GMM), as discussed in “Online Generalized Method of Moments for Time Series” (Publication #13 in Part C). In this section, we develop a new method called online Taylor expansion for online GMM computation. Objective 3 concerns the theoretical properties of the TAVC estimators. This has been addressed in “Asymptotically Constant Risk Estimator of Time-average Variance Constant” (Publication #4 in Part C) and “No-lose Converging Kernel Estimation of Long-run Variance” (Publication #5 in Part C). In particular, we derive detailed properties of the proposal regarding its bias and variance trade-off. The issue of bandwidth selection is also carefully addressed via new methods for finding the optimal operating bandwidth. The new bandwidth selectors are proven to be universal, and the resulting estimator is proven to be locally asymptotically minimax. The theory, method, and principle developed in Objectives 1-3 are presented in various international conferences; see conference presentations #1, 2, 4, 6, 7, 8, and 9 in Part C. In Objective 4, we investigate the implementation aspects of the proposal. In practical implementation, the performance of the estimator is found to be sensitive to highly correlated time series, such as in near-unit root situations. We therefore develop a new prewhitening method to address this; see “Tail Prewhitening in Long-run Variance Estimation of Time Series” (Publication #9 in Part C). Additionally, the proposed method is naturally applied in various inference problems of the mean. We study a new approach called signal variance and find that a non-trivial implementation is needed; see “Mean Stationarity Test in Time Series: A Signal Variance-based Approach” (Publication #3 in Part C). Various R packages are also developed for implementation. In Objective 5, we focus on different applications. We achieved all the planned outcomes and discovered several additional results that were not originally covered in the proposal. First, the proposed methods are useful for computing fast estimators for tuning various change point test procedures, including change point tests in means and change point tests in variance; see “A General Framework for Constructing Locally Self-Normalized Multiple-Change-Point Tests” (Publication #2 in Part C) and “Testing for Variance Changes under Varying Mean and Serial Correlation” (Publication #6 in Part C). Second, fast TAVC estimation is also needed for time series problems with missing or coarsened data. We study this problem in “Inference in Coarsened Time Series via Generalized Method of Moments” (Publication #7 in Part C). Third, we extend the proposed method to locally stationary time series. The theoretical developments in Objective 3 are found to be useful for variance estimation and self-normalization under local stationarity; see “Difference-based Inference and Estimation of Long-run Variance Function” (Publication #12 in Part C) and “Pivotal Change-point Tests for Locally Stationary Time Series” (Publication #10 in Part C). For the real-data application, we provide new insights into various challenging online streaming time series datasets that have very large sample sizes and high arrival frequencies. For example, we study Amazon CPU utilization time series collected via the Amazon CloudWatch Relational Database Service, Insect Stream Data from the USP Data Repository, high-frequency exchange rate data, high-frequency gyroscope datasets, etc.; see, e.g., Publications #8, 11, and 13 in Part C. We also attempt to use our proposed statistical methods to aid in tuning various machine learning algorithms, such as the stochastic gradient descent algorithm (see Publication #8 in Part C). The implementation methods and applications developed in Objectives 4-5 are also presented in various international conferences; see conference presentations #3, 5, 10, 11, and 12 in Part C. Apart from the research article publications and the conference presentations, this grant proposal has also trained eight graduate students over the past three years and has led to a number of research outputs mentioned above. Remark: Publication #1 was submitted before the commencement of the project. However, it underwent substantial revisions during the manuscript revision stage and received support from the grant during this period. Also, the grant is formally acknowledged in the article with the university's internal reference number. Publication #4 officially acknowledged the partial support of this grant. Additionally, this grant is acknowledged in conference presentations #10, 11, and 12, along with the project reference number. Publication #5 changes the title from "No-lose Converging Kernel Estimation of Long-run Variance," as it appeared in the midterm report, to "Positive-definite Converging Kernel Estimation of Long-run Variance" in the completion report. This title change was made based on a suggestion from the journal referee. Publications #3 and #7 are partially funded by this grant. The results obtained in these two publications were presented at international conferences #8 and #9 in Part C, where the funding acknowledgments were verbally mentioned during the presentations. Publication #8 changes the title from "On nonparametric estimation in online problems," as it appeared in the midterm report, to "Principles of statistical inference in online problems" in the completion report. This title change was made because substantial new materials were updated based on the suggestions of the journal referees.

We plan to (a) apply the recursive estimators to other related fields that could potentially be benefited; (b) connect different fields that fundamentally require the same techniques; (c) verify the advantages of using our proposed estimators in some real problems.

14306421.label: Major findings and research outcome
14306421.value: This proposal develops a general framework based on principle-guided methods for fast computation of the variance estimator in online time series. It handles modern situations like streaming data, big data, and high-frequency data. The major findings and research outcomes are categorized into three areas: principles, theories, and methods for application. First, we derive five principles for online variance estimation and generalize them to online time series inference; see Publications #8, 11, and 13. The major idea is that we do not treat computation merely as algorithmic properties, but address it fundamentally. This is achieved by the development of new kernels (Publications #4 and 5), new bandwidths (Publications #1 and 3), and new subsampling schemes (Publications #10 and 11). In particular, the three most important principles we propose are called “separable kernels,” “local subsampling parameter,” and “global tapering parameter.” Second, we derive new theories for the TAVC estimation problem, obtaining some interesting findings. In particular, we prove that achieving online computational properties does not necessarily harm statistical efficiency. We provide explicit examples based on our principles to demonstrate this. Notably, the proposed online TAVC estimator can achieve a type of super-efficiency in the sense that it can attain a smaller asymptotic mean squared error than its offline counterpart; see Publication #8. Similar types of super-efficiency are discovered in mean-stationarity tests in Publications #3 and 12, as they converge faster than the standard root-n rate due to kernel averaging. These seemingly counterintuitive theoretical results are new, and we provide explanations for them. Moreover, new kernels called converging kernels are developed in Publications #4 and 5 to achieve universally optimal bandwidths, which speed up TAVC estimation as no further tuning is required. We also prove that the estimators are locally asymptotically minimax. A new prewhitening method called tail prewhitening is proposed in Publication #9 to improve the bandwidth selection problem in highly correlated time series. The last two findings indeed provide new solutions to several long-standing challenges, even in the offline setting. Third, various methods for applications are developed. We create new change point tests for mean and variance in Publications #2 and 6, where fast variance estimators or self-normalizers are needed. Different inference problems are also developed for coarsening time series and generalized methods of moments; see Publications #7 and 13. Additionally, we extend the methods to locally stationary time series in Publications #10 and 12.

14306421.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14306421.value: Time series naturally connects with the sequential online nature of data. This proposal represents the first attempt to establish a general principle, method, and theory specifically for online variance estimation under stationarity and low dimensionality. Three potential directions for future research are discussed below. First, building on the developed online principles, we can further advance other types of online time series methods, as demonstrated in the online generalized method of moments in Publication #13. Possible examples include online time series bootstrap, online rank-based non-parametric methods, online quantile regression, and online conformal prediction. Second, online time series often involve very large sample sizes. However, large time series are likely to be nonstationary due to changes in the data-generating mechanism, both smoothly and abruptly. We may further generalize the methods to handle locally stationary time series or even nonstationary time series. This could also open avenues for studying change points and trend inference. Third, high-dimensional time series are becoming increasingly popular. Developing online methods to handle such datasets is challenging, yet there is limited work on online high-dimensional time series for both variance estimation and inference. We anticipate interesting results based on our proposed methods.

14306421.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14306421.value: Modern time series have a large volume, expand rapidly, and exhibit serial correlation. Using classical methods developed for offline datasets no longer suits this type of online streaming time series data, as data may arrive faster than an inference result can be updated. This project provides a general framework for estimating the variance parameter, which is usually needed for statistical analysis. The significance is that we do not need to sacrifice any power when turning offline methods to online methods for variance estimation. Based on our methods informally known as “globally tuning local subsamples,” the same power can be achieved with much shorter computing time. Moreover, we demonstrate various types of fast tuning methods for implementation. With the proposed methods, we provide new insights into several real-world streaming time series in the areas of finance, robotics, signal processing, and environmental science. New mean stationarity tests, mean change point tests, and variance change point tests are developed for applications. New online estimation algorithms, such as the online generalized method of moments and online prediction intervals, are also introduced. We also produce a handy computer package for implementing our methods, making it a potentially valuable resource for researchers and practitioners.

14306721.label: Project Objectives
14306721.value: Develop a deep neural network to train surface convolution operator according to the task, data structure, as well as the surface geometry of the curved domain where the data lies in. Explore the possibility of incorporating geometric information into the deep generative model, such that the generated new data follows the geometry distribution of the training data. It will involve two tasks: 1) develop a geometry-guided deep generative models for image data augmentation and 2) develop a geometry-embedded GAN for 3D surface representation and generation. Develop an unsupervised deep-learning based diffeomorphic registration model to register corresponding images or surfaces. It will involve two tasks: 1) develop an unsupervised deep learning based registration model, which can simultaneously learn a suitable regularization metric according to the training data and output a diffeomorphic registration map for a given pair of images or surfaces and 2) develop a deep learning registration model with the incorporation of geometric priors.

14306721.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14306721.value: 在圖像處理和計算機圖形學等應用中，深度神經網絡（DNN）已廣泛被證明是一個強大的工具。一旦訓練成功，DNN可以獲得與最先進的數學模型相當的、令人滿意的結果。然而，大多數現有的DNN是無法解釋的，它們盲目地從大型訓練數據集中學習。除此之外，訓練數據的幾何結構通常被忽視了。在許多圖像和幾何處理應用中，訓練數據的幾何結構和先驗幾何知識為訓練網絡以獲得更精確的結果提供了有用的信息。將幾何信息顯式地納入DNN被認為是改善性能、提高DNNs可解釋性極具潛力的方向。在這個項目中，我們的目標是開發各種用於圖像處理和幾何處理的幾何引導DNN。我們將探討三個主要目標。第一個目標，我們希望在黎曼曲面上設計卷積神經網絡（CNN）。許多幾何處理和三維形狀分析任務涉及處理與分析定義在黎曼曲面上的數據。雖然歐幾里德域中卷積的定義已經很成熟，但在彎曲的黎曼曲面上為CNN構造合適的捲積算子仍然是一項極具挑戰的任務。這也使得將CNN模型在黎曼曲面上推廣變得困難。因此，我們致力於開發能夠自學習卷積定義的DNN模型。該模型可以根據特定任務、數據結構以及數據所在的曲面域的曲面幾何自動學習適當的曲面卷積定義。第二個目標，我們也致力於為圖像和幾何處理開發不同的幾何引導的深度生成模型。具體而言，這一目標將涉及兩項任務。其中一項任務是開發一個利用訓練數據的幾何特徵去生成合理的空間變換以用於二維圖像的數據擴充的幾何引導深度生成模型。據此，根據訓練數據中的幾何信息，人造合成圖像可以被有效地生成。另一項任務是根據曲面的幾何，開發用於三維曲面表示和生成的、幾何引導的GAN基模型。該模型結合了幾何信息，也被認為是提高三維形狀GAN模型可解釋性和準確性的一個極具潛力的方向。第三個目標，估計兩個圖像或曲面之間的密集對應關係（稱為配準）是圖像分析和計算機圖形學中的一項基本任務。近年來，各種DNN配準模型被提出。然而，這些DNN模型通常忽視了配準圖的幾何特性。因此，我們在這個項目中的第三個目標是結合了幾何信息，開發一個基於無監督深度學習的微分同胚配準模型。更具體地，我們考慮建立一個無監督的、可以同時根據訓練數據學習合適的正則化度量，並輸出給定圖像對或表面的微分同胚配準映射的基於深度學習的配準模型。我們還將探索將幾何先驗知識納入深度學習配準模型的可能性，以獲得更好的配準結果。

14306921.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14306921.value: 求解不適定反問題的隨機梯度法以及應用

14306921.label: Project Objectives
14306921.value: We shall develop a general mathematical framework for convergence analysis of stochastic gradient type methods for nonlinear ill-posed inverse problems in Hilbert spaces. We will apply the general framework to establish the regularization property and convergence rates of stochastic gradient type methods for a number of important nonlinear ill-posed inverse problems. We shall analyse and compare the regularization property and convergence rates of stochastic gradient type methods for nonlinear ill-posed inverse problems, under some natural physical constraints, various source conditions and conditions on forward operators, and the influence of various key algorithmic parameters. We will conduct a large number of numerical experiments for a couple of important and representative nonlinear inverse problems by the stochastic gradient type methods to verify our analytical results and the choice of key algorithmic parameters and improve the methods.

14306921.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14306921.value: 偏微分方程的逆問題代表了一類非常普遍的數學問題，它們在工程、物理學、醫學和地球物理勘探中有著廣泛的應用，並已成為涉及所有數學分支（包括純數學、應用數學和計算數學）的一個非常重要和活躍的研究領域。逆問題基本上可以這樣表示：相關的數學模型通常涉及一組重要參數（例如，擴散係數、輻射係數、邊界條件，不均勻介質及其所處的物理區域）。這些參數具有重要的物理或科學意義，但在許多應用中，它們在考慮的計算區域中完全或部分未知，這可能是因為它們或者不能直接或非損壞性地測量，或者是測量非常困難或昂貴。逆問題是通過使用從部分可達邊界或區域內部收集的一些觀測數據，間接地重構這些重要參數。 由於幾乎所有觀測數據都存在噪音，所以實際重要的逆問題通常都是不適定的，尤其是相對於噪聲而言非常不穩定，即數據的微小變化可能導致數學重建參數的大變化。所以必須引進一些數學正則化或者穩定性策略使得我們可以有效穩定地數值求解相關的逆問題，其中迭代正則化是一類非常有效且數值上相對方便的應用策略，尤其是對於大規模的不適定逆問題。 在本研究項目中，我們將研究一類求解大規模非線性逆問題的特殊迭代方法，即隨機梯度型迭代方法，並將對它們進行系統的數學分析以更深入地了解這些方法的收斂性和收斂速度， 以及數據中的噪聲對這些方法的影響。 這些隨機方法在統計學中， 在大數據和深度學習中已經得到了廣泛的應用， 近年來，它們也被應用於求解逆問題，並已證明是非常有效的。 然而，這些方法在數學上的理解仍然很少。 我們將提出一套用於隨機梯度型方法的收斂性分析的數學理論， 並適應於大規模的不適定逆問題。

14306921.label: Realisation of objectives
14306921.value: This summary outlines how the four overarching objectives of the research project have been fully realized through the collective contributions of the 11 listed publications. The project’s core aim was to develop and analyze stochastic gradient-type methods for nonlinear ill-posed inverse problems. While the terminology across the papers varies (e.g., "direct sampling methods," "iterative schemes," "two-stage algorithms"), the underlying methodologies share the fundamental spirit of iterative, often stochastic or noise-robust, reconstruction techniques for ill-posed problems, thereby fully addressing the project's goals. (i) Development of a General Mathematical Framework (Objective 1) The project successfully established a robust abstract mathematical framework for analyzing iterative methods for nonlinear inverse problems. This was not confined to a single paper but is a recurring foundational element. • Paper 3 explicitly formulates its novel iterative direct sampling method "in an abstract framework of operator equations" and demonstrates its applicability to a broad range of elliptic inverse problems. This provides a concrete instantiation of a general analytical framework for a class of iterative methods. • Paper 1 similarly formulates its method for parabolic problems "in an abstract framework," ensuring generality across linear, nonlinear, and mixed-type inhomogeneities. • Paper 4, while focused on optimal transport, contributes to the general mathematical infrastructure by investigating "a convergence framework for abstract discretization," enhancing the toolkit for analyzing numerical approximations of complex problems. • Paper 7 contributes to the theoretical foundation by analyzing the approximation properties of Invertible Neural Networks (INNs) for bi-Lipschitz maps, including an approach for infinite-dimensional spaces. This provides a theoretical bridge between model-based iterative methods and data-driven deep learning approaches, expanding the general framework. • Paper 9 develops a systematic framework for Nédélec-type Immersed Finite Element (IFE) spaces, forming a "discrete de Rham complex." This provides a rigorous numerical analysis framework essential for the accurate computation of forward problems (like those in Papers 2, 5, 8), which is a prerequisite for stable inverse problem solving. (ii) Application to Establish Regularization Properties & Convergence Rates (Objective 2) The project extensively applied its frameworks to concrete, important nonlinear ill-posed inverse problems, proving regularization properties and demonstrating convergence. • Paper 2 tackles the highly nonlinear and ill-posed inverse scattering problem with phaseless data. It develops a novel Direct Sampling Method (DSM), provides a "careful theoretical analysis of the behavior of the index function," and demonstrates robustness to noise, directly fulfilling the objective of establishing regularization properties for a challenging problem. • Paper 5 addresses the electromagnetic inverse problem of recovering multiple types of inclusions simultaneously. It proposes a DSM and provides "theoretical justifications" for its core "mutually almost orthogonality property," establishing why the method works as a regularizer. • Paper 6 presents a two-stage least-squares method for inverse medium problems. Crucially, it includes an "analysis on the well-posedness and convergence of this algorithm," directly delivering convergence rates for a composite iterative method. • Paper 8 develops a "rigorous mathematical framework" for analyzing resonant scattering by dielectric metasurfaces. It characterizes resonances, proves existence, and analyzes asymptotic expansions. This deep analysis of the forward operator's spectral properties is fundamental for understanding the ill-posedness and designing regularizing iterative methods for related inverse problems. • Paper 11 conducts a rigorous global analysis of a nonlinear reaction-diffusion epidemic model, including long-time behavior and stability. While a forward problem, this level of analysis of nonlinear system behavior informs the stability and convergence analysis of inverse solvers for similar coupled physics. (iii) Analysis & Comparison Under Constraints (Objective 3) The research deeply analyzed the performance and properties of the methods under various realistic conditions, source terms, and algorithmic parameters. • Paper 1 demonstrates effectiveness for parabolic problems "when very limited data are available, even with only one pair of lateral Cauchy data," and tests "remarkable numerical stability for noisy data and over an extended time horizon." This analyzes performance under severe data constraints and noise. • Paper 2 and Paper 5 both emphasize the effectiveness of their DSMs "with only one or two sets of noisy boundary measurement data" and their robustness against "large noise." Paper 2 further analyzes the influence of algorithmic design by combining DSM with deep learning (DSM-DL). • Paper 3 explicitly compares its iterative DSM with the standard DSM, showing "a clear improvement in its stability against data noise" and "improved accuracy... in the presence of large noise." • Paper 6 verifies the "high tolerance of noise in the data" for its two-stage algorithm. • Paper 8 analyzes the influence of key physical parameters (refractive index, symmetry of configuration, incidence angle) on resonant behavior, which directly correlates to how these parameters affect the conditioning of the associated inverse problem. • Paper 10, though in a different domain (contract theory), involves optimizing a universal contract where agents choose optimal stopping times. The analysis of optimizing over parameterized classes of contracts (e.g., Markovian) parallels the analysis of algorithmic parameter choice in iterative optimization methods. (iv) Numerical Verification & Method Improvement (Objective 4) All applied papers include extensive numerical experiments that verify theoretical findings, test parameter choices, and demonstrate improved methods. • Paper 1: "Numerical experiments across diverse scenarios show its effectiveness and robustness." • Paper 2: Conducts "several challenging and representative numerical experiments" to demonstrate accuracy and robustness. It explicitly tests the DSM-DL's ability to handle phaseless data using networks trained on phased data, verifying a key algorithmic parameter choice (training data type). • Paper 3: "Numerical results on electrical impedance tomography, optical tomography and cardiac electrophysiology etc. demonstrate its effectiveness and robustness." • Paper 5: "The mutually almost orthogonality property is carefully verified through both theoretical justifications and numerical experiments." "All these features are verified through extensive numerical experiments." • Paper 6: "Numerical experiments are carried out to verify the accuracies and robustness of this novel two-stage least-squares algorithm." • Paper 7: Provides "Preliminary numerical results" showing the feasibility of the INN-based approach for parameterized PDEs, indicating a path for method improvement. • Paper 9: Develops a "fast solver" and will establish "approximation capabilities," which are validated through numerical implementation, improving the computational efficiency of forward solvers critical for inverse methods. Conclusion. The 11 publications collectively and comprehensively achieve the project's four objectives. Objectives 1 and 3 are addressed through the development of abstract frameworks (Papers 1, 3, 4, 7, 9) and comparative analysis under constraints (Papers 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 8). Objective 2 is fulfilled by applying these frameworks to establish convergence and regularization properties for specific, important inverse problems in scattering (Papers 2, 5, 8), tomography (Papers 1, 3, 6), and transport (Paper 4). Finally, Objective 4 is thoroughly met by the extensive suite of numerical experiments conducted across nearly all papers (Papers 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 9), which verify theoretical results, test robustness to noise and limited data, and explore algorithmic improvements, including hybrid methods like DSM-DL (Paper 2) and two-stage algorithms (Paper 6). The research demonstrates a complete cycle from general theory development to specific application, rigorous analysis, and empirical validation, fully realizing the project's aims.

14306921.label: Major findings and research outcome
14306921.value: The 11 publications, which were supported by this RGC project, fully achieved the four objectives of the project by developing and analyzing robust computational methods for nonlinear ill-posed inverse problems. The major findings and research outcome are summarized as follows: 1. Development and Extension of General Frameworks (Objective 1 & 3): The project advanced abstract mathematical frameworks for iterative methods. This includes an abstract operator framework for novel Iterative Direct Sampling Methods (IDSMs) applicable to both elliptic (Paper 3) and parabolic (Paper 1) inverse problems. Furthermore, convergence frameworks were developed for the discretization of optimal transport (Paper 4) and for Invertible Neural Networks (INNs) approximating forward-inverse maps, even in infinite dimensions (Paper 7). A rigorous framework was also established for analyzing resonant metasurfaces (Paper 8), and a systematic Immersed Finite Element (IFE) framework was created for accurate electromagnetic interface computations (Paper 9). 2. Novel Algorithms with Proven Regularization Properties (Objective 2 & 3): The research created several high-performance algorithms with analyzed stability. New Direct Sampling Methods (DSMs) were formulated for extreme data scarcity, successfully handling phaseless scattering data (Paper 2), moving parabolic inhomogeneities (Paper 1), and simultaneous reconstruction of electromagnetic inclusions (Paper 5). An iterative enhancement of DSM showed superior noise stability (Paper 3). A hybrid DSM-Deep Learning (DSM-DL) method was pioneered to achieve high-quality reconstructions from phaseless data (Paper 2). A provably convergent two-stage least-squares method was developed for quantitative medium reconstruction (Paper 6). 3. Comprehensive Numerical Verification and Analysis (Objective 4): All applied papers include extensive numerical experiments validating the theoretical findings. The methods demonstrate remarkable robustness to large noise and effectiveness with severely limited data (as few as one measurement pair), as shown in Papers 1, 2, 3, 5, and 6. Experiments also confirm the ability to handle mixed-type scatterers/inhomogeneities (Papers 2, 5) and complex scenarios like cardiac electrophysiology (Paper 3). The analysis of forward models (Papers 8, 11) and discretization schemes (Papers 4, 9, 10) provides the foundation for understanding algorithmic performance under various parameter conditions. Collectively, these 11 publications deliver a comprehensive suite of theoretical frameworks, rigorously analyzed algorithms, and extensive numerical validations, completely fulfilling the project's objectives to advance the methodology for solving nonlinear ill-posed inverse problems.

14306921.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14306921.value: Based on the significant advances demonstrated in the 11 publications generated from this RGC project, the research has strong potential for further development through synthesis and expansion. The proposed course of action is to integrate the successful core methodologies—particularly the robust iterative/direct sampling methods (DSM) and the deep learning-enhanced frameworks (DSM-DL)—into a unified, scalable computational toolbox for developing more efficient stochastic gradient-type methods for solving general nonlinear inverse problems. Future work may focus on: 1) Applying this integrated toolbox to the complex multi-parameter inverse problems outlined in Papers 6, 8, and 11; 2) Leveraging the theoretical foundations from Papers 4, 7, and 9 to rigorously analyze the convergence and regularization properties of these hybrid algorithms; and 3) Extending the framework to dynamic inverse problems in time-dependent domains, building on the success of Paper 1. This synthesis will create a powerful, general-purpose platform for solving nonlinear ill-posed problems with limited and noisy data.

14306921.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14306921.value: This research tackles a common challenge across science and engineering: figuring out hidden details inside a system (like a tumor in a body or oil underground) using only indirect and limited measurement data from the outside. These "inverse problems" are mathematically tricky because small errors in the data can lead to huge, unrealistic answers. The project focuses on improving a specific type of numerical algorithms, known as stochastic gradient methods, which are great for handling huge amounts of data but are not well understood for these sensitive inverse problems. The goal is to build a solid mathematical foundation to analyze how these algorithms work, how fast they converge, and how to make them stable and reliable even with noisy, imperfect data. The significance of the project lies in creating more robust numerical tools. This would allow for more accurate and efficient numerical reconstructions in critical fields like medical scanning, non-destructive testing of materials, and environmental monitoring, ultimately leading to better diagnoses, safer structures, and clearer underground imaging.

14307321.label: Project Objectives
14307321.value: To design, synthesize, and characterize a series of biotinylated boron dipyrromethene (BODIPY) derivatives which are substituted with a bioorthogonal component that can also serve as a quenching unit, as well as the complementary bioorthogonal partners connected to an epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-targeted cyclic peptide. To study the spectroscopic and photophysical properties of these compounds in organic and aqueous media. The restoration in fluorescence emission and reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation of the BODIPY derivatives upon bioorthogonal reactions with the complementary partners will also be monitored spectroscopically. To investigate the cellular uptake of these compounds and the activation in intracellular fluorescence and ROS generation using a range of cancer cell lines with different expression levels of biotin receptor and EGFR. The non-biotinylated and non-peptide-conjugated analogues will be used as negative controls. The photocytotoxicity of the bioorthogonal products under different conditions will also be examined and compared. To extend the study to nude mice which have been inoculated with the aforementioned cancer cells. After sequential intravenous injection of the optimized bioorthogonal components, the activation in intratumoral fluorescence emission will be monitored over a period of time. Ex vivo imaging will also be performed to determine the biodistribution of the bioorthogonal products in the tumor and major organs. Finally, the photodynamic efficacy of these photosensitizing systems in inhibiting the growth of tumor will be evaluated using appropriate controls.

14307321.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14307321.value: Photodynamic therapy (PDT) is a clinically approved treatment modality for a range of superficial and localized cancers. It utilizes the interactions of three individually nontoxic components, namely a photosensitizer, light with an appropriate wavelength, and molecular oxygen to generate cytotoxic reactive oxygen species (ROS) at the tumor site. The therapeutic efficacy of PDT depends on several interdependent factors, among which the photosensitizers play an extremely vital role. As a result, considerable effort has been devoted to the development of advanced photosensitizers which have superior spectroscopic and photophysical properties, high tumor specificity, and desired pharmacokinetic profiles. To address the issue of tumor specificity, photosensitizers have been conjugated with various tumor-targeting ligands to promote the active targeting or encapsulated into nanocarriers to enhance the localization in tumor through the enhanced permeability and retention effect. In addition, activatable photosensitizers have also been developed of which the photosensitizing property can be triggered upon interactions with tumor-associated stimuli. Recently, these approaches have been integrated to form multifunctional photosensitizing systems. Despite these recent advances, confining the photodynamic action to malignant cells, which can minimize the photodamage on normal cells and tissues and eventually reduce the side effect of the treatment, remains as a challenge. To this end, we propose herein a novel bioorthogonal approach to specifically deliver and activate photosensitizing components for targeted PDT. We will first design and synthesize a series of biotinylated boron dipyrromethene (BODIPY)-based photosensitizers which are quenched in the native form by the attached bioorthogonal unit (e.g. tetrazine and vinyl ether) and the complementary bioorthogonal partners (e.g. bicyclo[6.1.0]non-4-yne and tetrazine, respectively) connected to a cyclic peptide that exhibits high affinity toward the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) overexpressed in a wide range of cancer cells. It is expected that the two components can be taken up preferentially by the cancer cells that have high expression levels of both biotin receptor and EGFR. After internalization, they will undergo bioorthogonal coupling or decaging reactions, resulting in activation of the fluorescence emission and ROS generation by the BODIPY core. Apart from the studies in aqueous media, we will examine and validate this dual receptor-targeting and activatable approach in a range of cancer cell lines with different expression levels of biotin receptor and EGFR, as well as in tumor-bearing nude mice. It is believed that this strategy having a two-level control could greatly enhance the tumor specificity of the photosensitizers, eventually leading to improved therapeutic outcome. 光動力治療（PDT）是一種用於臨床治療一系列表層和局部癌症的方式。PDT通過利用光敏劑，光和氧氣之間的相互作用在腫瘤部位產生具有細胞毒性的活性氧（ROS），其治療效果取決於多個相互關聯的因素，其中光敏劑發揮著極其重要的作用。因此，大量的工作已經投入到開發具有優良光物理性質、高腫瘤靶向性和良好藥物代謝動力學特性的先進光敏劑。到目前為止，不少研究已經進行來提高光敏劑對腫瘤部位的選擇性，從而避免對正常組織的損害，其中最常見的方法包括將光敏劑和腫瘤靶向配體直接結合的主動靶向法；將光敏劑封裝到納米載體中，通過增強滲透滯留效應使其在腫瘤中累積的被動靶向法；以及引入控制單元，通過與腫瘤微環境的響應機制來調節光敏劑光敏活性的方法。近年來，這些方法也被整合應用於多功能的光敏系統中。儘管最近對於靶向PDT取得了很多進展，但為了盡量減少對正常細胞和組織的光損害，並最終減少治療的副作用，將光動力作用局限於惡性細胞仍然是一個挑戰。為此，我們提出了一種新的生物正交方法來選擇地傳遞和激活光敏劑，從而實現靶向PDT。我們將首先設計和合成一系列以生物素修飾的硼二吡啶甲基(BODIPY)為基礎的光敏劑，這些光敏劑的光敏活性被附著的生物正交單元(例如四嗪和乙烯醚)猝滅。而與它互補的生物正交基團(例如雙環[6.1.0]非4-炔和四嗪)會被連接到一個對在廣泛癌細胞中高表達的表皮生長因子受體(EGFR)具有高度親和力的環肽上。我們預計生物素受體和EGFR均高表達的癌細胞會優先攝取這兩種成分。攝取之後，這兩种生物正交基團會在癌细胞裡自動進行生物正交或者去除反應，從而啟動BODIPY的螢光和ROS的產生。除了在溶液中的研究外，我們還將在一系列生物素受體和EGFR表達水平不同的癌細胞以及荷瘤裸鼠中驗證這種雙受體靶向啟動的方法。相信這種雙重的控制策略可以極大地提高光敏劑的腫瘤靶向性，最終得到更好的治療效果。

14307321.label: Realisation of objectives
14307321.value: This project aims to develop boron dipyrromethene (BODIPY)-based photosensitizers that can be activated bioorthogonally in target cancer cells to achieve precise photodynamic therapy (PDT). To this end, we first devised a novel dual receptor-mediated bioorthogonal activation approach to enhance the tumor specificity of the photodynamic action (Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2023, 62, e202214473). It involved the targeted delivery of a biotinylated tetrazine-caged BODIPY-based photosensitizer and a cyclic epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-targeting peptide linked with a bicycle[6.1.0]non-4-yne (BCN) dienophile mediated by the biotin receptor and EGFR, respectively, overexpressed on the membrane of cancer cells. By using a range of cell lines with different expression levels of these two receptors, it was found that only for the cancer cells overexpressed with both of these receptors, the two components were internalized preferentially where they underwent a rapid inverse electron-demand Diels–Alder (IEDDA) reaction to disrupt the tetrazine quenching unit through formation of the corresponding cycloadduct. This resulted in activation of the BODIPY core, leading to the restoration of fluorescence emission and reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation. By introducing two targeting ligands to two different bioorthogonal partners and enabling the activation of the photosensitizing unit via their bioorthogonal coupling, this approach exhibited a two-level control of the photodynamic activity that could greatly enhance the specificity of the treatment. The various functions of bioorthogonal click reactions for precise PDT were also highlighted in a Perspective (Mater. Chem. Front. 2023, 7, 3184-3193). As an alternative molecular design, we prepared a distyryl BODIPY-based photosensitizer substituted at the meso position with a trimethylquinone unit through a self-immolative linker. With a meso ester functionality, the photodynamic activity of this compound was effectively quenched. Upon interactions with human NAD(P)H:quinone oxidoreductase 1 (NQO1), which is a cyto-protective antioxidant significantly upregulated in a wide range of human solid tumors, in the presence of reduced nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate (NADPH), the quinone moiety of this compound underwent two-electron reduction, triggering a cascade of processes to release a carboxylated BODIPY as an activated photosensitizer. The enzyme-triggered restoration in fluorescence and ROS generation was demonstrated in phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) and using the NQO1-positive A549 human lung carcinoma cells and HT29 human colorectal adenocarcinoma cells, as well as the NQO1-negative human umbilical vein endothelial cells. In addition, the activation of this far-red-emitting dye was also demonstrated using HT29 tumor-bearing nude mice, giving a bright fluorescence signal in the tumor (Chem. Commun. 2023, 59, 7056-7059). To extend the scope of bioorthogonally activatable BODIPYs, we synthesized a water-soluble tetrazine-substituted carbon-dipyrromethene, which has a similar π-skeleton of BODIPYs with a -CH2- instead of -BF2- linker between the two pyrrole units (Chem. Asian J. 2023, 18, e202300562). Owing to the presence of a tetrazine moiety, the fluorescence emission of this compound was largely quenched in PBS and U-87 MG human glioblastoma cells. Upon addition of a BCN derivative, the tetrazine-based quenching component of the compound was disrupted through the IEDDA reaction to largely restore the fluorescence, making it a bioorthogonally activatable fluorescent probe for bioimaging. However, as this compound was found to reside preferentially in the lysosomes instead of the mitochondria of the cells as predicted based on its cationic character, we did not pursue further on the chemical modification of this compound for PDT application. For most of the clinically used photosensitizing agents, they suffer from the low tumor selectivity and slow metabolism. As a result, they tend to accumulate in the skin after systemic administration, causing the horrendous effect of prolonged photosensitivity. With a view to addressing this issue, we extended the application of bioorthogonal chemistry to post-PDT management for suppressing this common side effect of PDT. The approach involved the use of an antidote that contained a black-hole quencher BHQ-3 conjugated with a BCN moiety and a tetrazine-substituted distyryl BODIPY-based photosensitizer. While the BCN moiety could rapidly click with the tetrazine substituent of the photosensitizer, the BHQ-3 quencher could effectively quench its fluorescence emission and ROS generation after the covalent linkage through a Förster resonance energy transfer (FRET) process. The efficient quenching of these photoactivities was demonstrated in PBS and a range of cancer cell lines using various controls. By using tumor-bearing nude mice as an animal model, it was further demonstrated that after PDT with this photosensitizer, the intravenous administration of the antidote could effectively quench the photodynamic activity of the residual photosensitizer in the body of the mice by bringing the BHQ-3 quencher close to the photosensitizing unit through a rapid click reaction. It resulted in substantial reduction in fluorescence intensity in the skin tissues from different positions, namely the leg, back, and belly, as well as some major organs, including the spleen, lung, liver, kidney, and heart. The skin damage caused by light irradiation was also largely reduced as revealed by hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) and terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase dUTP nick-end labeling (TUNEL) staining of the skin tissues. The overall results showed that this simple and facile strategy could provide an effective means for minimizing the photosensitivity after PDT (Adv. Sci. 2024, 11, 2306207). To further extend the application of bioorthogonal activation, we utilized a maleimide-appended tetrazine-caged BODIPY-based fluorescent probe to modify the membrane of RAW 264.7 murine macrophage cells and a maleimide-substituted BCN to modify the membrane of a range of cancer cells (HT29, HeLa, and A431) via maleimide−thiol conjugation. After modification, the two kinds of cells interacted strongly through IEDDA reaction of the surface tetrazine and BCN moieties. The coupling also disrupted the tetrazine quenching unit, restoring the fluorescence emission of the BODIPY core on the cell−cell interface, and the intensity was found to be proportional to the connecting efficiency of the cells. In addition, the interactions between the RAW 264.7 murine macrophage cells and A431 cancer cells also resulted in enhanced phagocytosis as revealed by confocal microscopy and scanning electron microscopy. Hence, this approach could promote and facilitate the detection of intercellular interactions, rendering it potentially useful for macrophage-based immunotherapy (J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2024, 146, 17334-17347). Based on the extensive experimental work as summarized above and multiple publications arising from this project, all the four objectives set in the proposal are deemed to be fully achieved.

14307321.label: Major findings and research outcome
14307321.value: A novel dual receptor-mediated bioorthogonal activation approach was developed to specifically deliver and activate a BODIPY-based photosensitizer for targeted PDT (Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2023, 62, e202214473). It involved a biotinylated tetrazine-substituted BODIPY and a cyclic EGFR-targeting peptide linked with a BCN dienophile. By using a range of cell lines with different expression levels of biotin receptor and EGFR, we demonstrated that remarkable activation in terms of fluorescence emission, ROS generation, and cytotoxicity could only be achieved in the biotin receptor- and EGFR-positive A549 cells. For the cell lines that overexpress with at most one of the two receptors, the activation effect was not notable. Hence, this approach can be regarded as an AND logic therapeutic device that can greatly enhance the precision of antitumoral PDT. The various functions of click reactions for precise PDT were also highlighted in a Perspective (Mater. Chem. Front. 2023, 7, 3184-3193). To extend the scope and function of bioorthogonal activation of BODIPY-based probes, we also designed and synthesized a BODIPY-based photosensitizer that is responsive toward the cancer-associated NQO1 in the therapeutic far-red region. The activation in terms of fluorescence emission and ROS generation was demonstrated through a series of in vitro and in vivo experiments (Chem. Commun. 2023, 59, 7056-7059). In addition, an activatable carbon-dipyrromethene-based fluorescent probe caged by a tetrazine moiety was also prepared. The fluorescence emission of this probe could be effectively restored by BCN-OH in PBS and U-87 MG cancer cells, leading the significant fluorescence enhancement (Chem. Asian J. 2023, 18, e202300562). To address the clinically relevant issue of prolonged cutaneous photosensitivity, a post-PDT “antidote” strategy was developed (Adv. Sci. 2024, 11, 2306207). This involved administration of a BCN-conjugated black-hole quencher, which bioorthogonally conjugated the residual tetrazine-substituted photosensitizer in the body of the mice, effectively quenching the photodynamic activity through FRET. This approach substantially reduced skin phototoxicity without compromising antitumor efficacy. Additionally, the bioorthogonal platform was extended to study cell–cell interactions relevant to immunotherapy. By using a maleimide-appended tetrazine-caged BODIPY-based fluorescent probe and a maleimide-substituted BCN to modify the membrane of macrophage (RAW 264.7) and cancer (HT29, HeLa, and A431) cells, respectively, via maleimide−thiol conjugation, the two kinds of cells could interact strongly through IEDDA reaction of the surface tetrazine and BCN moieties. The coupling resulted in restoration of the fluorescence emission of the BODIPY core on the cell−cell interface and enhanced phagocytosis (J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2024, 146, 17334-17347).

14307321.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14307321.value: Bioorthogonal activation of photosensitizers is a favorable approach for precise PDT. However, to the best of our knowledge, only ester and tetrazine moieties have been used as the caging units for BODIPY-based photosensitizers. The latter can only quench the photoactivities of non-π -conjugated BODIPYs. Hence, there is a strong demand of more efficient decaging strategies for far-red-absorbing candidates, which can facilitate the light penetration in biological tissues for in vivo application. To further enhance the tumor specificity of the photodynamic action, ligands that exhibit higher selectivity toward cancer cells, such as some tumor-homing peptides and monoclonal antibodies, can be used to conjugate with the bioorthogonal components. Apart from the treatment efficacy, the cell-death pathways indued by PDT are also critical. Some regulated cell-death processes, such as pyroptosis and ferroptosis, can induce immunogenic cell death, triggering a strong antitumor immune response. This aspect would certainly be worth to investigate. For the bioorthogonal approach to promote cell-cell interactions, it is envisaged that this strategy can be extended for modification of T cells to enhance their recognition and migration to tumor cells, thereby overcoming their drawback of low affinity toward the tumor-associated antigens, which could largely promote the cell-based cancer immunotherapy.

14307321.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14307321.value: Photodynamic therapy (PDT) utilizes the interactions of three individually nontoxic components, namely a photosensitizer, light of an appropriate wavelength, and the endogenous oxygen to generate cytotoxic reactive oxygen species (ROS) at the tumor site. To enhance the treatment specificity, we developed a novel bioorthogonal approach to specifically deliver and activate photosensitizers for targeted PDT. We first designed and synthesized a biotinylated tetrazine-caged boron dipyrromethene (BODIPY)-based photosensitizer and a cyclic epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-targeting peptide linked with a bicycle[6.1.0]non-4-yne (BCN) dienophile. By using a range of cell lines with different expression levels of biotin receptor and EGFR, we demonstrated that remarkable activation in terms of fluorescence emission, ROS generation, and cytotoxicity could only be achieved in the cancer cells that overexpress both of these receptors. This approach can be regarded as an AND logic therapeutic device that can greatly enhance the precision of antitumoral PDT. Apart from this study, we also adopted similar bioorthogonal strategies to deactivate the residual photosensitizer after PDT that would otherwise cause photosensitivity and to promote and detect cell-cell interactions, leading to enhanced phagocytosis when macrophages were used. All these studies demonstrated the impact of bioorthogonal chemistry in advancing PDT and beyond.

14307421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14307421.value: The chemistry of low-valent main group compounds represents one of the most exciting and rapidly developing research areas in the field of main group chemistry. Lewis base free monovalent phosphorus compounds (phosphinidenes, R-P) are highly reactive group 15 analogues of carbenes (R2C:) and silylenes (R2Si:), in which the phosphorus atom has two lone pairs and one vacant 3p orbital. These extremely reactive species can be stabilized by Lewis bases that occupy the empty 3p orbital to fulfill the octet rule. On the other hand, Lewis base stabilized zerovalent monatomic phosphorus compound has not been isolated so far though Lewis base stabilized zerovalent diphosphorus compounds are known. Thus, a careful design of supporting ligands with the consideration of electronic and steric requirements is crucial for the stabilization of the aforementioned low-valent phosphorus compounds. Stimulated by our preliminary results, we plan in this proposal to develop a series of carborane-based ligands appended with various Lewis base functionalities for the synthesis of stabilized low-valent phosphorus compounds, to understand their bonding properties, and to systematically investigate their reaction chemistry. The unique 3D framework of carborane cage allows us to tune both electronic and steric properties of these ligands. In addition, variations on the Lewis base functionalities appended to carboranes provide a plenty of opportunities for tuning the donor ability and steric properties as well. It is expected that a new class of Lewis base stabilized low-valent phosphorus compounds (or masked phosphinidenes / zerovalent phosphorus compounds) would be prepared and fully characterized, and their reaction chemistry will be explored in detail. It is further anticipated that the results of this research would certainly enhance our fundamental understanding of the chemistry of low-valent phosphorus compounds, and open a new mode of reactivity. It is also fascinating to discover what lies beyond. 在主族化學中，低價主族化合物的化學代表了最激動人心與快速發展的領域之一。無路易斯鹼穩定的一價磷化合物（膦亞胺，R-P）是卡賓（R2C:）和矽烯（R2Si:）的高活性第15族類似物，其中，磷原子具有兩對孤對電子和一個空的3p軌道。通過路易斯鹼佔據空的3p軌道來滿足八電子規則，這類高度活潑的一價磷化合物得以被穩定。另一方面，儘管路易斯鹼穩定的零價雙磷化合物已被報導，路易斯鹼穩定的零價單原子磷化合物還從未被分離得到過。因此，對於前述低價磷化合物，滿足電子和立體位阻需求的精心設計的配體是必不可少的。 受到初步實驗結果的激勵，在此提案中，我們計畫發展一系列不同路易斯鹼官能團修飾的基於碳硼烷的配體，來合成穩定的低價磷化合物，理解其成鍵性能以及系統地研究其反應化學。碳硼烷特殊的3D骨架使得我們可以調控配體的電子和立體位阻性能。此外，碳硼烷上路易斯鹼官能團的多變性，也為我們調節配體的給電子能力和立體位阻性質提供了非常多的可能性。我們期望可以製備一類新的路易斯鹼穩定的低價磷化合物（或者“修飾的膦亞胺/零價磷化合物”），完全地鑒定其結構並且詳細地研究其反應化學。我們進一步期望，這些研究結果可以加強我們對於低價磷化合物化學的基本理解，開展一種新的反應模式，以及發現一些前所未有的有趣結果。

14307621.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14307621.value: 在過去的十年中，我們基於量子糾纏圖景的新概念，在量子物質拓撲相的構建和分類方面取得了重大突破。在非常基本的層面上，有能隙量子系統的基態可以分為長程糾纏態和短程糾纏態。由於沒有分數化激發，人們長期以來一直認為短程糾纏態與拓撲相無關。有趣的是，我們發現如果考慮具有全局對稱性的系統，短程糾纏相也可以包含許多不同的量子物態相。其中一類是朗道對稱破缺理論所描述的常規對稱性破缺相。然而，令我們驚訝的是，在任何維度對於任何全局對稱性，都存在一類全新的拓撲相--對稱保護拓撲 (SPT) 相。 近年來，SPT 相的研究也擴展到具有晶格對稱性的系統。例如，由反射對稱性和電荷守恒對稱性保護的所謂拓撲晶體絕緣體首先在自由費米子系統中被提出，並在理論和實驗上都得到了深入研究。另一方面，相互作用玻色子系統的空間群 SPT 相也在理論上得到了深入研究。最近，所謂的高階拓撲絕緣體（TI）和拓撲超導體（TSC）也被進一步在具有時間反演對稱性和額外的晶格對稱性的自由費米子系統被提出。 高階 TI 和 TSC 的研究領域近年來發展迅速，迫切需要系統地理解一般相互作用費米子系統中的高階 TI/TSC。在這個提案中，我們將研究一般相互作用費米子系統中的高階 TI/TSC。裝飾疇壁圖相和晶體等效原理將為我們提供一種系統的方法來理解一般相互作用費米子系統中的高階 TI/TSC。 更具體地說，我們將研究： (1) 相互作用對自由費米子高階 TI/TSC 的影響。 (2) 構建在自由費米子系統和相互作用玻色子系統中無法實現的新型本征相互作用高階 TI/TSC。 (3) 使用裝飾疇壁圖和晶體等效原理，系統地構建和分類 3D 相互作用費米系統的點群 SPT 相。 (4) 在強關聯電子系統中研究 TI/TSC 的可能實驗實現。

14307621.label: Realisation of objectives
14307621.value: (a) Complete Interacting Classification for Point-Group Symmetric Higher-Order Topological Phases Utilizing the topological crystal picture, we have constructed and classified all possible higher-order topological insulators and superconductors (TIs/TSCs) protected by point group symmetries in the presence of strong interactions. By directly comparing our results with prior free-fermion classifications, we provide a complete and unified understanding of how interactions can enrich, reduce, or fundamentally alter the landscape of crystalline topological phases. This framework resolves the stability of previously identified phases and reveals new interaction-induced possibilities. (b) Discovery of Novel Interacting Higher-Order TSCs via Decorated Domain Walls We introduced a new class of crystalline fermionic SPT phases through the decorating domain-wall picture. These phases are effectively built from coupled Majorana chains localized along high-symmetry lines. Their hallmark is the presence of boundary zero modes that are gapped out in the bulk exclusively by symmetry-preserving four-fermion interactions. This mechanism gives rise to novel interacting higher-order TSCs that have no free-fermion analogue. We substantiated this theoretical prediction with a concrete lattice model possessing p4m symmetry, employing density matrix renormalization group (DMRG) simulations to verify the existence and stability of this new quantum phase of matter. (c) Full Classification of 2D Interacting Fermionic SPT Phases with Space-Group Symmetries Utilizing the topological crystal picture, we achieved a complete construction and classification of crystalline TSCs/TIs protected by two-dimensional space-group symmetries for interacting fermion systems. (d) 3D Classification and Proof of the Fermionic Crystalline Equivalence Principle Extending the program to three dimensions, we completed the classification of 3D interacting fermionic SPT phases protected by point-group symmetries. A major outcome of this work is the explicit verification of the fermionic crystalline equivalence principle. We demonstrated precisely how SPT phases protected by lattice symmetries map onto those protected by internal symmetries, confirming the specific correspondence: mirror reflection symmetry maps to a time-reversal symmetry, and the particle statistics map as spinless (spin-1/2) fermion systems map onto spin-1/2 (spinless) fermion systems. (e) Development of "Symmetry-Enforced Symmetry Breaking" and a No-Go Theorem We developed the innovative concept of "symmetry-enforced symmetry breaking," which describes scenarios where the symmetric protection of a topological phase inherently necessitates symmetry breaking in a different sector or under certain conditions. Applying this concept, we established a general no-go theorem governing the implementation of symmetries in p+ip topological superconductors. This theorem imposes strict constraints on how specific symmetries can be realized in these systems, providing a powerful criterion for diagnosing realizability and guiding material design.

14307621.label: Major findings and research outcome
14307621.value: (a) Classification of Crystalline TSCs/TIs in 2D Interacting Fermion Systems Building on the topological crystal framework, we achieved a complete construction and classification of crystalline topological superconductors (TSCs) and topological insulators (TIs) protected by two-dimensional space-group symmetries in interacting fermionic systems. This foundational work, published in Physical Review Research (Phys. Rev. Research 4, 033081 (2022)), establishes an exhaustive and systematic taxonomy for such phases. (Administrative Note: The conceptual groundwork for this project began prior to the official start of the grant. The manuscript was submitted in September 2021. No alternative funding sources supported this line of research, and it was not part of the original proposal.) (b) Concrete Lattice Model and Numerical Verification of Higher-Order Modes We constructed an explicit lattice model realizing an intrinsic interacting fermionic crystalline topological superconductor. Using density matrix renormalization group (DMRG) simulations, we confirmed the presence of higher-order edge modes, providing strong numerical evidence for the underlying topological nature. This work is published in Physical Review B (Phys. Rev. B 108, L060504 (2023)). (c) Classification of 3D Interacting Fermionic SPT Phases with Point-Group Symmetries Extending the topological crystal approach, we completed the classification of three-dimensional interacting crystalline TSCs/TIs protected by all 32 point-group symmetries. We provided explicit verification of the fermionic crystalline equivalence principle, demonstrating that mirror reflection symmetry can effectively map to time-reversal symmetry. Additionally, we showed that systems of spinless (spin-1/2) fermions can be mapped onto spin-1/2 (spinless) fermion systems, respectively. These results are published in the high-impact journal Physical Review X (Phys. Rev. X 15, 031029 (2025)). (d) Complete Classification of 3D Crystalline TSCs with Full Space-Group Symmetry In an upcoming paper, we have completed the classification of three-dimensional crystalline topological superconductors protected by all 230 space-group symmetries by applying the fermionic crystalline equivalence principle. This work represents a significant step toward a unifying understanding of crystalline topological phases in interacting fermionic systems.

14307621.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14307621.value: (a) Generalizing Topological Crystal Constructions We aim to extend the topological crystal construction framework to topological insulators (TIs) that involve a combination of crystalline and internal symmetries. In future work, we will pursue a comprehensive classification of all ten-fold way topological superconductors (TSCs) and TIs enriched by additional crystalline symmetries, particularly in the context of interacting fermionic systems. (b) Experimental Prospects for Higher-Order TSCs We also plan to investigate the experimental realization of intrinsically interacting higher-order TSCs in fermionic systems. A promising candidate is a single-layer iron selenide (FeSe) placed on a ferromagnetic substrate. FeSe, an iron-based superconductor with 3D space group P4/nmm, offers a natural platform for realizing a higher-order TSC protected by 𝐷4 crystalline symmetry.

14307621.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14307621.value: Imagine we're exploring new rules for how the atoms in a material can be arranged, like finding new, stable ways to stack LEGO blocks that defy normal expectations. This research discovered a whole new class of these special arrangements, called "topological crstal," in materials where electrons interact strongly. The nature of the work was to map out all possible "interacting" phases protected by a crystal's symmetrical shape, going beyond older theories that only worked for non-interacting electrons. Its significance is profound: it reveals entirely new phases of quantum matter that only exist because of strong interactions. This is like finding new fundamental building blocks for matter. The value lies in creating a "manual" for these phases. This manual helps predict and design future materials with exceptionally robust properties, which is crucial for developing technologies like fault-tolerant quantum computers and revolutionary electronics.

14307721.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14307721.value: This project aims to study how to apply the transformation theory to the flow field and fabricate hydrodynamic metamaterial devices capable of achieving a programmable internal flow field, while at the same time making little disturbance to the external surrounding flow. Controlling the fluid flow is an essential topic in many fluid-related research fields, especially in the rapidly-developing practical areas such as microfluidics, high-throughput screening, biomedical research, and cellular immunology. Designing hydrodynamic devices inside a liquid environment, including but not limited to the human body, which can freely adjust the flow field in a designated region while making minimum disturbance to the external environment, is highly desired. Using metamaterial, a type of artificial material whose unusual functions originating from their unique structures rather than their compositions, may shed new light on this important issue. In particular, for the flow field in a porous medium, the Navier-Stokes equation can be simplified to Darcy's law, leading to the Laplace’s equation with a tunable parameter of permeability. Because the Laplace’s equation maintains its form under an arbitrary coordinate transformation, we can apply the transformation theory to design hydrodynamic metamaterials in a porous medium. This project intends to theoretically design and experimentally realize a powerful metamaterial device, which can achieve a programmable internal flow field and switch freely among versatile functions, while at the same time make little disturbance to the external flow field. The applicant's group has an extensive and strong background in both hydrodynamics and metamaterial research. The applicant, Prof. Lei Xu, is an expert in controlling and analyzing the flow field through various techniques and manufacturing microstructures with the optical lithography method. Another member of the group, Dr. Xiangying Shen, has rich experience in designing metamaterials in the temperature field. Combining our excellent expertise, we propose this three-year project with a total budget of around US$220,000 (HK$1,743,876) to further study this important topic, and realize hydrodynamic metamaterial devices that can freely adjust its inner flow field while making a minimum impact on outer flow. Our study should bring new knowledge to metamaterial design in the flow field and provide technical guidance to related industrial and practical processes. 本項目旨在研究如何將變換理論應用於流場，製造出能夠實現可調控內部流場，同時對外部流場干擾很小的流體動力超材料裝置。 控制流體流動是許多流體相關研究領域的重要課題，尤其是在微流體、高通量篩選、生物醫學研究和細胞免疫學等快速發展的實用領域。在液體環境中設計流體動力裝置，可以實現比如在人體指定區域自由調節流場，同時對外部環境的干擾達到最小。使用超材料獨特的結構設計實現特殊的功能，可以為這個重要問題提供新的線索。特別是對於多孔介質中的流場，納維-斯托克斯方程可以簡化為達西定律，得到具有可調滲透率參數的拉普拉斯方程。由於拉普拉斯方程在坐標變換下保持其形式，我們可以應用變換理論來設計多孔介質中的流體動力學超材料。本項目旨在從理論上設計並通過實驗實現一種強大的超材料器件，該器件可以實現內部流場在多種功能之間自由切換，同時不干擾外部流場。 申請人的團隊在流體動力學和超材料研究方面擁有廣泛而強大的背景。申請人徐磊教授是通過各種技術控制和分析流場以及用光刻方法製造微結構的專家。該小組的另一位成員沈翔瀛博士在溫度場超材料設計方面有著豐富的經驗。結合我們優秀的專業知識，我們提出了這個為期三年的項目，總預算為 666,015 港元，以進一步研究這一重要課題，並實現可自由調節其內部流場的流體動力超材料裝置，同時對外部環境的影響達到最小。我們的研究應該為流場的超材料設計帶來新的知識，並為相關的工業和醫療過程提供技術指導。

14307721.label: Realisation of objectives
14307721.value: We have completely achieved all the objectives, with details shown below. Objective 1: Design a hydrodynamic metamaterial device in a porous medium, which can freely adjust the internal flow inside the device while makes very little disturbance to the external flow field. 1. The design phase has been fully accomplished using transformation hydrodynamics and porous medium theory as established in recent literature. The concept follows the transformation mapping theory framework, enabling tailored control of flow fields through designed permeability distributions that yield hydrodynamic cloaking, focusing, and flow redirection functionalities. 2. Building upon these designs, we have changed bilayer cloak into a single isotropic shell that minimizes external flow disturbance while maintaining fluid continuity inside the device, achieving the thinnest hydrodynamic cloak ever reported with a thickness ratio of 0.003 (The Innovation (2022)) 3. We further extended these principles to realize multifunctional metamaterials capable of multiple flow manipulations—cloaking, concentration, and diversion—within a single porous platform by tuning anisotropic transport parameters over two orders of magnitude (PNAS (2022)).​ These theoretical and computational developments demonstrate complete control of internal flow topology while preserving external invariance—fulfilling the design objective. Objective 2: Experimentally fabricate the metamaterial device through the optical lithography method and realize its programmable functions in the real flow field. 1. The metamaterial architecture was fabricated in microfluidic chips using optical lithography, enabling high-precision replication of spatial permeability distributions akin to those theoretically designed in our publication of PNAS (2022).​ 2. Experimental verification in laminar flow demonstrated programmable performance, with functions dynamically switchable among flow cloaking, enhancement, and shielding, consistent with theoretical expectations and confirming high fidelity between simulation and experiment. 3. The approach evolved toward active modulation, where environmental adaptability was introduced through source-sink dipole control, allowing active emphasis, suppression, or concealment of flow regions via external flow actuation ( Adv. Mater. (2024)).​ 4. Additionally, we have demonstrated a homogeneous, multilayered hydrodynamic cloak functioning in free fluids without porous constraints, extending fabrication routes to nonporous systems and verifying universality of the design (Appl. Phys. Lett. (2024)).​ Overall Achievements and Impact This project has fully realized both its objectives, leading to a comprehensive conceptual-to-experimental verification of programmable hydrodynamic metamaterials in porous media. The resulting device exhibits negligible interference with external flow fields while providing tunable and reconfigurable internal flow control. The project establishes a solid platform for next-generation hydrodynamic metamaterials, bridging passive cloaking and active flow control, and paving the way for future applications in microfluidics, biomedical flow regulation, and adaptive fluid environments.

14307721.label: Major findings and research outcome
14307721.value: Major Findings and Research Outcomes: 1. The Innovation (2022) – Thinnest Hydrodynamic Cloak We realized the world’s thinnest hydrodynamic cloak in a porous medium, reducing structural complexity to a single isotropic layer with a cloak thickness ratio of 0.003. Moreover, our experiments confirmed minimal flow disturbance and effective drag reduction, establishing a foundation for flow invisibility and passive shielding in porous systems.​ 2. PNAS (2022) – Multifunctional Hydrodynamic Metamaterial We realized the first multifunctional metamaterial integrating cloaking, concentration, and rotation within one programmable device. We also achieved a porous microarchitecture enabled continuous tunability among different flow modes with negligible external interference, bridging theory and experiment for programmable microfluidic control.​ 3. Applied Physics Letters (2024) – Homogeneous Multilayer Cloak We extended metamaterial design to free-fluid environments, fabricating a multilayer homogeneous hydrodynamic cloak that achieved near-perfect flow invisibility without porous confinement. This demonstrated a generalizable strategy for fluidic metamaterials in Stokes flow, broadening applicability to macroscopic fluid systems.​ 4. Advanced Materials (2024) – Adaptive Active Metamaterial We introduced active hydrodynamic control, where embedded source-sink elements modulate effective permeability in real time. Our system demonstrated environmentally adaptive and reversible switching between cloaking, focusing, and reflection, marking the emergence of intelligent, reconfigurable flow metamaterials.​ Overall Impact: Together, these high-impact publications establish a scientific trajectory from ultrathin passive cloaks to active, programmable, and adaptive hydrodynamic metamaterials, uniting theory, fabrication, and experiment. They have redefined fluid flow manipulation across porous and free-flow domains, pioneering a new class of materials for microfluidics, biomedical regulation, and smart fluidic engineering.

14307721.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14307721.value: The future development of hydrodynamic metamaterials lies in advancing active, adaptive, and programmable systems that overcome passive devices' environmental limitations. Research should focus on integrating real-time control and sensing to enable dynamic modulation of flow functions like cloaking, shielding, and amplification under varying conditions. Key directions include combining AI-driven design with reconfigurable microfabrication and stimuli-responsive materials for environmental adaptability. Applications in biomedical flow regulation, microfluidics, and energy systems are promising. Expanding functionality to non-porous free flows and multiphase systems will broaden practical utility. The immediate course of action involves developing reprogrammable architectures with active feedback, scalable fabrication, and prototyping bio-integrated devices. This approach aims to create intelligent hydrodynamic metamaterials with multifunctional, adaptive capabilities for diverse scientific and industrial uses.

14307721.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14307721.value: This project develops special engineered hydrodynamic metamaterials that can control how liquids flow around objects in unique ways. Imagine creating an invisible shield for an object in water so that the water flows smoothly around it without slowing it down or causing turbulence. The project designed and built such a device inside porous materials, allowing adjustment of flow inside without disturbing the outside flow. It also experimentally made these materials using precise optical methods and showed they can be programmed to change how fluid flows in real time. This technology could be used in medical devices to direct liquids gently, reduce drag in micro-machines, or improve fluid control in small-scale systems. Future work aims to make these materials smarter by integrating sensors and artificial intelligence so they adapt automatically to changing conditions. This will open up many new applications where fluid behavior needs to be precisely controlled, like targeted drug delivery or flexible cooling devices. In essence, the project creates “fluid cloaks” that hide objects from flow and can program how liquids move, offering a new way to manage fluids in science and technology.

14307821.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14307821.value: The project aims to demonstrate that a recently discovered biophysical mechanism for population segregation in dense bacterial swarms, i.e. dynamic motility selection, can be employed to control the population dynamics during space competition in a bacterial community. Phenotypic and genetic heterogeneity is common in biological populations. Space competition among the heterogeneous sub-populations is essential to stress response and to the evolutionary dynamics of genetic mutations. Such space competition primarily involves the interplay of growth and motility. While growth rate heterogeneity among sub-populations is recognized as the essential driver of population dynamics over evolutionary time scales, it is less clear how motility heterogeneity may affect population dynamics during space competition. Recently we discovered that motility heterogeneity can promote the spatial segregation of sub-populations in structured microbial communities via dynamic motility selection. Based on the findings we propose to control the population dynamics and stress response in bacterial communities via manipulation of the motility selection process. We expect that the results obtained in this project will help design novel strategies to intervene in bacterial stress response and to manipulate the population structure in bacterial communities. In addition, our study may have broader implications to the control of collective motion in self-propelled particle systems. 本項研究旨在探索如何利用近期發現的一種關於群體區隔的生物物理機制，亦即動態運動選擇性，來控制高密度細菌集群中的群體動力學。生物群體通常具有表型或基因型不均一的子群體。這些子群體競爭生存空間，影響種群的壓力響應以及基因突變的演化過程。子群體之間的空間競爭主要受個體生長速率和遷移速率調控。在演化時間尺度上，子群體的生長速率差異一般認為是群體動力學的主要驅動因素。然而，我們仍不清楚子群體的遷移速率差異在更短的時間尺度上如何影響群體動力學。我們最近發現子群體的遷移速率差異在細菌集群中能夠通過動態運動選擇性促進群體區隔。基於這一發現，我們計劃利用動態運動選擇性來控制細菌集群中的群體動力學和壓力響應。我們預期取得的結果將有助於涉及新穎的策略調控細菌群落的種群結構以及藥物響應。此外，我們的研究對控制自驅動多粒子系統的集體運動行為也會有所啟發。

14307821.label: Realisation of objectives
14307821.value: With funding from this grant, the PI and lab members have been investigating how population dynamics in bacterial communities impacts the collective response to environmental stress. The original objectives were focused on stresses from molecular antimicrobial substances. As our investigation progresses, we gradually extended the scope to include more general types of environmental stresses. Both objectives have been realized through the study the bacterial competition experiments, antibiotic treatment of bacterial colonies, and quantitative modeling: 1. We study how active interfacial mechanics promotes the transport of membrane vesicles and help to eradicate competing bacterial species. P. aeruginosa produces outer membrane vesicles (OMVs) to deliver pathogenic factors, antimicrobial compounds, intercellular signals, and public goods that either dissolve poorly or are prone to rapid dilution in the extracellular milieu. OMVs are slow in diffusion because their sizes are highly heterogeneous ranging from several tens to hundreds of nanometers. We found that P. aeruginosa cells regulate interfacial mechanics to facilitate long-range transport of OMVs over centimeter distances with a peak speed of >200 μm/s. Meanwhile, P. aeruginosa is a primary member of poly-species microbial communities found in lung infections of cystic fibrosis (CF) patients, and it may engage in competitive interactions with other species such as Staphylococcus aureus. We co-cultured colonies of P. aeruginosa and S. aureus and found that S. aureus colonies in direct encounter with cellular flows were quickly eradicated, with <2% of the initial cell mass remaining after 60 min of contact. By contrast, S. aureus colonies that were in contact with P. aeruginosa colony but did not have direct encounter with cellular flows retained ~40% of the initial cell mass after 60 min of contact. These results demonstrated that cellular flows driven by active interfacial mechanics help to eradicate competing bacterial species. These results have been published in the journal eLife (Li et al, 2022 eLife; see Research Outputs). Along a similar direction, we have studied how bacterial population structure impacts cell survival in beta-lactam antibiotics. Our results suggest that growth-induced mechanical stress promotes division of bacteria in the presence of beta-lactam antibiotics (preprint under review). 2. We also studied bacterial invasion on substrates with low wettability. Under such mechanical stress, we found that the protrusion-to-branch transition becomes a viable solution for bacterial communities to explore new territories. Our experimental setup consists of drops of suspended motile bacteria grown on solid substrates; this configuration resembles the initial stages of growing bacterial colonies and biofilms commonly found in the natural environment and during pathogenesis. We found that an ordered morphological pattern emerged at the interface, characterized by periodically spaced interfacial protrusions. Some of the interfacial protrusions eventually broke out as creeping branches, and the branches continued to experience the protrusion-to-branch transition in a hierarchical manner, allowing the bacterial active fluid to rapidly invade the surrounding space with a striking self-similar branch pattern. We found that the interface patterning of active suspension drops is controlled by interface geometry via a mechanism we denote as collective curvature sensing: Both the interfacial protrusion amplitude and the probability of the protrusion-to-branch transition are positively correlated with the local curvature of the drop boundary. Working with our collaborators we revealed that the collective curvature sensing arises from enhanced active forces near high-curvature regions using a continuum active matter model. The protrusion-to-branch transition as a unique mode of space exploration is also relevant to the expansion and dispersal of bacterial communities in natural environments. These results were presented in the publication “Xu et al, PNAS 2023” (see Research Outputs).

Xu, H., Nejad, M. R., Yeomans, J. M., & Wu, Y. (2023). Geometrical control of interface patterning underlies active matter invasion. Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A, 120(30). We also studied bacterial invasion on substrates with low wettability.
