The protrusion-to-branch transition as a unique mode of space exploration is also relevant to the expansion and dispersal of bacterial communities in natural environments. 3. Yisen Li & Yilin Wu, “Mechanical interaction enables a collective mode of bacterial proliferation”, manuscript under review. We have studied how bacterial population structure impacts cell survival in beta-lactam antibiotics. We discovered that cells under the treatment of wall-targeting beta-lactam antibiotics proliferated robustly in aggregates, while isolated cells failed to divide and eventually experienced membrane rupture. Combining results from quantitative imaging and computational modeling, we attributed this unexpected finding to mechanical shearing between densely packed cells driven by their growth activities; such mechanical shearing enhances cell deformation, thereby enabling cell division and sustaining population growth in a colony.

14307821.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14307821.value: Our finding that cellular flows driven by active interfacial mechanics help to eradicate competing bacterial species suggest that physical mechanisms can be exploited to transport and deliver cell-produced antimicrobial substances, such as quinolines encapsulated in OMVs with antibacterial activities against Gram-positive bacteria and toxic compounds carried by rhamnolipid micelles, thereby enhancing the efficiency of inhibiting competing bacterial species. The finding of a protrusion-to-branch transition as a unique mode of active matter invasion provides a novel strategy to engineer pattern formation of active materials. Our finding of the collective mode of bacterial proliferation enabled by self-generated mechanical stresses may help to understand bacterial survival from wall-targeting antibiotic treatment and phage infection. Research along these directions will be worth pursuing.

14307821.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14307821.value: In this project we studied how population dynamics in bacterial communities impacts the collective response to environmental stresses, including stress from antimicrobial substances, from competitors, and from the mechanical environment. We demonstrated that cellular flows driven by active interfacial mechanics help to eradicate competing bacterial species. We found that growth-induced mechanical stress promotes division of bacteria in the presence of beta-lactam antibiotics. We also found that bacterial colonies grown on substrates with low wettability overcomes the difficulty in range expansion via a protrusion-to-branch transition mechanism, which allows the bacterial community to explore new territories.

14307921.label: Project Objectives
14307921.value: The main objective of the proposed study is to identify a family of statistical models for network data. The proposed family of network models would be able to encompass many of the major network features such as average path length, clustering coefficient, degree-degree correlations and size indexes. An equally important objective is to develop a statistical inference methodology for estimating the model parameters. Special emphasis will be placed on large networks. Furthermore, when node or edge information are instantly available, another objective of the proposed study is to incorporate the additional information to aid the estimation process. Since the asymptotic distribution of the estimators provides rich information about the estimators, it would be important to develop theoretically the asymptotic distribution. Using the asymptotic results established in the proposed study, efficient numerical procedures for statistical inference that can be applied empirically will be developed. By building mixtures of multiple network models, this project will lead to a deeper understanding of these statistical methods and will enhance the applicability of the proposed family of statistical network models to social networks and real networks from other disciplines. Applications to real-life network analysis will also be conducted.

14308121.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14308121.value: Palladium-catalyzed cross-coupling process has emerged as one of the most well-received and modern protocols allowing chemists to assemble structurally diversified arene-containing molecules, in which they are materially attractive and pharmaceutically useful compounds. These convergent methods have revolutionized the way of scientists to perform complex organic synthesis from readily available electrophilic and nucleophilic components. At the center of these synthetic technologies, catalyst development which enables challenging and/or problematic bond construction process to be proceeded smoothly would be highly attractive. Thus, catalyst exploration and development is particularly central to contemporary catalysis research for innovative organic synthesis. The new development of aromatic bond-construction methodology would advance the existing coupling processes and put forward of catalysis sciences. The purposes of this project are (1) to rationally design and explore a new family of highly tunable indole-imidazole-hybrid phosphine ligands fit for transient proximal-chelation framework; (2) to carry out in-depth investigation towards the fundamental aspect, scope and limitation of the new palladium-catalyzed aryl carboxylate cross-coupling and related arylation processes; (3) to carry out relevant mechanistic investigation using both experimental and theoretical approaches, for acquiring more elementary knowledge in this catalysis science. This project is expected to explore a new field in cross-coupling reactions. The fundamental knowledge attained during the course of catalyst development and manipulation, and the rationale of proximal ligand coordination towards the new cross coupling partners (i.e. aryl acetate) would be of significant value for academic interest and potential applications. The proposed study is based on our solid proof-of-concept initial results, as well as previous success in the ligand and catalyst design and synthesis, as well as our extensive experiences in aromatic bond-construction research. These new areas are anticipated to offer us an excellent opportunity in making a substantial advancement to the frontier of catalysis research and put forward of establishing a favorable foundation for fine-chemical industry in Hong Kong. 芳香鍵構建方法的新發展將推進現有的偶聯過程並提出催化科學。該項目的目的是（1）合理設計和探索適合瞬態近端螯合框架的高度可調的吲哚-咪唑-雜化膦配體的新家族； (2) 對鈀催化的醋酸芳基酯交叉偶聯及相關芳基化新工藝的基本方面、範圍和局限性進行深入研究； (3) 使用實驗和理論方法進行相關的機理研究，以獲得更多催化科學的基礎知識 擬議的研究基於我們堅實的概念驗證初步結果，以及之前在配體和催化劑設計與合成方面的成功，以及我們在芳香鍵構建研究方面的豐富經驗。這些新領域有望為我們在催化研究前沿取得實質性進展提供絕佳機會，並為香港的精細化工產業奠定良好基礎

14308121.label: Realisation of objectives
14308121.value: This is the completion report of the project GRF14308121, for the period of 01-01-2022 to 31-12-2024. The proposed studies commenced on 1st Jan, 2022. The first 15 months coincided with severe waves of the COVID-19 pandemic in Hong Kong, which caused significant delays in chemical deliveries and disrupted the initial research momentum. To mitigate these delays, the research team diligently worked to recover progress by proactively preparing key starting materials in-house and exploring alternative synthetic pathways. The scientific workdone toward achieving the project's objectives is detailed below. The research team had conducted the investigation of a new family phosphine ligands which are capable for activating aromatic C-O bond under palladium catalysis. We established a series of phosphines having unique alkoxy units. The ligand bearing -P(alkyl)2 moiety located at the C3 position of the indole core was found highly efficient in facilitating the coupling reaction between alkenyl tosylates with perfluoroarenes. The X-ray crystallographic analysis of new ligand geometry and the resulting Pd complex were performed. Interestingly, this ligand features a fitting balance of the P electron-richness and proximal steric bulkiness, leading to the success of this process. These research outcomes were published in Eur. J. Inorg. Chem. in mid-2022 (Eur. J. Inorg. Chem. 2022, e202200288). Moreover during the COVID-19 period, we also contributed an account for illustrating the background and rationale of the ligand design for tackling particular C-O cross-coupling reactions. This contribution was published in Dec-2022 (Acc. Chem. Res. 2022, 55, 3688). Furthermore, we comprehensively overviewed the Sonogashira coupling process using phenolic electrophiles under palladium catalysis. This review article was published in early 2023 (Chin. J. Chem. 2023, 41, 1099). In the context of aromatic C–O bond cleavage and functionalization, we prepared an array of sterically hindered biaryl aryl sulfonates. These studies revealed that the resulting substrates were capable to undergo a novel redox-neutral benzylic C–O cyclization. This unprecedented protocol provided efficient access to diverse semi-helical and bihelical chromene frameworks, as reported in "Organic Letters, 2022, 23, 6805". Subsequently, while investigating C–O bond formation in the flavonoid-type molecules, we developed an expeditious conjugate addition/annulation/1,5-hydride shift cascade. This modular strategy enables the synthesis of chromenes bearing all-pyrano substituents, in which they are scaffolds previously inaccessible by classical methods. This work was published in "Chemical Science 2022, 13, 13617". In order to tackle the existing challenge of steric-hindered cross-coupling process using difficult electrophiles, the aryl tosylates and mesylates, we explored a new series of N-substituted indolyl phosphine ligands. Indeed, there has no successful example reported so far for tri-ortho-substituted biaryl synthesis using ArOTs. In our finding using the newly developed phosphine ligands, we were able to achieve the first examples of ArOTs steric-hindered cross-coupling. These findings have been complied and are ready for submission to Angewandte Chemie International Edition (manuscript attached). Concerning the aryl carboxylate electrophile cross-coupling reaction, we have developed a unique N-cyclopentyl indolyl phosphine ligand for this study. We have achieved the first successful examples of aryl pivalate (ArOPiv) coupling under palladium catalysis. With the DFT calculation study, we found that this new cross-coupling proceeds with unconventional concerted pathway rather than the traditional oxidative addition/transmetallation steps. These research findings have been complied and are ready for submission to Nature Communications (manuscript attached).

14308121.label: Major findings and research outcome
14308121.value: The major findings and research outcomes of the proposed study are the development of the tailor-made phosphine ligands for tackling challenging or unexplored phenolic electrophiles, for instance, the aryl tosylates, mesylates, and the undisclosed aryl pivalates cross-coupling under palladium catalysis. We have successfully achieved the first examples of cross-coupling for sterically hindered aryl tosylates. A manuscript detailing this work has been prepared and is ready for submission to Angewandte Chemie International Edition (manuscript attached). Furthermore, we have also accomplished the first successful examples of aryl pivalate cross-coupling. A non-traditional concerted mechanistic model was found to be key to enabling this Ar-OPiv coupling under palladium catalysis. These results will be submitted for publication in Nature Communications (manuscript attached). Our research on aromatic C–O bond functionalization initially targeted sterically hindered biaryl aryl sulfonates, leading to the discovery of an interesting redox-neutral benzylic C–O cyclization. This unprecedented method efficiently constructs diverse semi-helical and bihelical chromene frameworks. This outcome has been published in Org. Lett. 2022, 23, 6805. Extending this work to flavonoid systems, we developed an expeditious cascade involving conjugate addition, annulation, and 1,5-hydride shift. This modular approach provides direct access to fully pyrano-substituted chromenes, a class of scaffolds lacking viable prior synthetic routes. This outcome has been disclosed in Chem. Sci. 2022, 13, 13617. Our extensive research has established a platform of highly tunable and easily modifiable ligands. In recognition of this success, we were invited by the editors of Accounts of Chemical Research and the Chinese Journal of Chemistry to contribute an Account and a Review article, respectively. These articles detailed our expedition of this ligand class and provide comprehensive synthetic protocols for assembling new catalytic systems for tackling challenging coupling reactions. These outcomes are: Acc. Chem. Res. 2022, 55, 3688 and Chin. J. Chem. 2023, 41, 1099.

14308121.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14308121.value: There remains significant potential for developing new catalyst systems to facilitate challenging chemical transformations. By leveraging a diverse catalyst portfolio, we can conduct detailed mechanistic studies on problematic reactions and pioneer unprecedented cross-coupling methodologies. The outcomes of this work hold great promise for advancing pharmaceutical synthesis and the manufacturing of complex aromatic materials.

14308121.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14308121.value: Centered on the design and development of next-generation catalyst systems, this proposal aims to enable versatile and previously inaccessible chemical transformations. Our foundational work has successfully introduced a novel series of highly efficient catalysts, which have accomplished sterically congested cross-coupling processes of significant challenge. This discovery provides a robust and impactful platform for researchers engaged in innovative catalyst design and the synthesis of complex, imaginative molecular structures.

14308321.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14308321.value: 揭示基於沉積-溶解的Zn-Mn2+/MnO2水系電池的衰退機制及改進策略

14308321.label: Project Objectives
14308321.value: We aim to unravel the degradation mechanisms of the aqueous Zn-Mn2+/MnO2 battery by decoupling the combinatory effects of the cathode and anode, investigate key factors controlling MnO2 deposition morphology and dissolution kinetics, and develop strategies to mitigate Zn corrosion and MnO2 accumulation. The technical objectives subordinate to our overall objective are as follows: We will investigate three hypotheses on cathode degradation mechanisms: (i) the exfoliation of thick MnO2 layer leads to active material loss; (ii) the poor conductivity of MnO2 limits dissolution process and the residual MnO2 passivates the electrode surface; (iii) insufficient H+ concentration to support MnO2 dissolution due to H+-consumption by Zn anode corrosion. We will investigate two hypotheses on anode degradation mechanisms: (i) H+ crossovers to anode and attacks Zn metal to produce H2 gas; (ii) Zn dendrite formation. We will employ comprehensive spectroscopic and microscopic techniques to decouple processes responsible for combinatory effects at the electrode-electrolyte interfaces. The presence of H+ is beneficial for cathode MnO2 dissolution but problematic for Zn anode due to Zn corrosion/HER side reactions. We propose to apply proton blockage anion exchange membrane (AEM) to reduce proton-crossover to Zn anode. The morphology of MnO2 deposition is critical as it determines the practical deposition capacity and dissolution efficacy during discharge. We will examine nucleation and growth kinetics of MnO2 and investigate key factors controlling MnO2 deposition morphology/dissolution kinetics including (i) the role of electrolyte pH and buffer electrolyte pKa; and (ii) the role of charging patterns and overpotential. To break the trade-off of H+ in cathode (helps MnO2 dissolution) and anode (Zn corrosion/HER), we propose to apply redox mediators to facilitate MnO2 reduction without adding acids. We will apply redox mediators with high stability and fast kinetics to convert the accumulated MnO2. Redox mediators not only can reduce the MnO2 deposited on carbon electrode, but also can reduce resistive MnO2 or exfoliated MnO2 suspended in the electrolyte.

14308321.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14308321.value: 本項目旨在通過解耦正極和負極的組合效應來揭示基於沉積-溶解的Zn-Mn2+/MnO2水系電池的衰退機制，研究調控MnO2沉積形貌和溶解動力學的關鍵因素，同時提出可以有效減緩鋅腐蝕和MnO2累計的策略。 開發基於安全、低成本、環保的水溶液電解液的水系可充電電池是未來儲能發展的重要方向。水系鋅錳液電池由於其低成本、高元素豐度、高安全性和生態友好性的特點，已作為便攜式電子產品的一次電池發展了數十年。然而，錳基主體材料中的鋅離子(Zn2+)或質子(H+)嵌入反應受限於低容量(150-305 mAh/g)和較低的電壓(1.2 – 1.4 V)。近期，一種基Mn2+/MnO2在弱酸中沉積溶解反應的新型正極反應被報道，其理論電壓（1.95V）和容量（570 mAh/g）均高於基於（Zn2+或H+)嵌入反應的傳統Zn-MnO2電池。然而，該電池性能也受到面積容量低、效率低和循環壽命差的限制。 在本項目中，我們將研究關於正極衰退機制的三個假設：(i) 厚MnO2層的剝落導致正極活性材料的損失； (ii) 具有不良導電性MnO2限制了溶解過程且殘留的MnO2鈍化電極表面； (iii) 由於鋅負極腐蝕消耗H+導致H+濃度不足以支持 MnO2溶解。我們將研究關於負極衰退機制的兩個假設：(i) H+交叉到負極並攻擊Zn金屬產生H2氣體； (ii) 鋅枝晶的生成。我們將採用全面的光譜和顯微技術來解耦電極-電解質界面組合效應的各個過程。此外，由於MnO2沉積的形貌決定了實際的沉積容量和放電過程中的溶解效率，我們將研究調控MnO2沉積形貌和溶解動力學的關鍵因素，包括 (i) 電解質pH 值和緩衝電解質的作用； (ii) 充電模式和過電勢的作用。為了減輕Zn腐蝕/析氫反應的副反應，我們計劃採用離子交換膜以保護負極。為了打破正極（有助於MnO2溶解）和負極（Zn腐蝕 / 析氫反應）中H+的權衡，我們計劃採用氧化還原介質來促進MnO2的還原而無需添加酸溶液。 該項目將深入瞭解 Zn-Mn2+/MnO2電池的衰退機制並提出減緩策略，實現用於安全儲能應用的穩定電池設計。

14308321.label: Realisation of objectives
14308321.value: Objective 1: We decoupled the degradation mechanisms of aqueous Zn–Mn batteries by systematically investigating the interplay between cathode and anode. Using a combination of in situ and ex situ characterization techniques, including scanning electron microscopy (SEM), X-ray diffraction (XRD), X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), and online electrochemical mass spectrometry (OEMS), we investigated key factors and developed strategies to mitigate Zn corrosion. We developed a nuclei-rich strategy for Zn anodes, which fundamentally modifies the Zn plating mechanism from instantaneous nucleation to progressive nucleation, inhibiting dendrite formation. We introduced the strategy by fabricating a hydroxyapatite-based nuclei-incubating interface. This interface promoted progressive nucleation over instantaneous nucleation, as confirmed by chronoamperometry and the Scharifker–Hills model. The resulting Zn electrode achieved dendrite-free cycling for over 1200 h at 15 mA cm–2 and 10 mAh cm–2, with a coulombic efficiency of 99.7%. The Zn–MnO₂ full cell with a low N/P ratio of 1.9 demonstrated a long cycle life of 3000 cycles. We investigated the role of electrolyte concentration and solvation structure using hydrotropic solubilization, which suppresses HER and improves Zn reversibility. We designed ion-regulating membranes to study proton crossover and its impact on Zn corrosion and MnO2 accumulation. The membrane increased the proton transport barrier from 0.065 eV to 0.104 eV, as measured by transmembrane activation energy, and reduced H+ permeation rate by ~50%. This effectively suppressed Zn corrosion and improved MnO2 reversibility. Objective 2: We investigated hypotheses on cathode degradation (e.g., exfoliation of MnO2, poor conductivity, insufficient H+) and anode degradation (e.g., H+ crossover, Zn dendrite formation). We validated several hypotheses regarding cathode and anode degradation mechanisms using advanced spectroscopic and electrochemical methods. We confirmed that Zn dendrite formation is a key issue, and we addressed it through nucleation promotion and electrolyte engineering. We developed new electrolytes (HSE-10m) to improve Zn stripping and deposition uniformity. In addition, the mild viscosity (199.7 mPa s) of HSE-10m could help to achieve a more uniform Zn deposition by suppressing dendrite growth and limiting anion convection. Hence, the Zn//Cu asymmetric cell cycled in HSE-10 m showed an average CE of 99.4% for the first 100 cycles and reached 99.6% at 150 cycles. We confirmed that H+ crossover from the posolyte to the negolyte exacerbates Zn corrosion and leads to irreversible MnO2 accumulation. The results showed that the DcoPZ membrane retained H+ in the posolyte, reducing “dead” MnO2 formation. For anode degradation, we identified Zn dendrite growth and HER as primary failure modes. We used SEM and EIS to show that the nuclei-incubating interface reduced the nucleation overpotential by 50% and increased the exchange current density from 10.19 to 17.04 mA cm–2. We applied FTIR, XANES, and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to reveal that hydrotropic agents (e.g., KAc, urea) transformed Zn2+ solvation structure from bidentate to monodentate acetate coordination, which suppressed HER and enabled a high Zn transference number of 0.42. Objective 3: We designed and fabricated an innovative ion-regulating membrane (designated as DcoPZ) featuring a surface-enriched positively charged network. This functional layer was constructed through the coordination between Zn2+ ions and the nitrile groups (C≡N) of polyacrylonitrile (PAN), forming a stable crosslinked structure on a robust porous substrate. The formation mechanism and chemical composition were thoroughly confirmed by X-ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy (XPS). The membrane surface charge properties were quantitatively analyzed via zeta potential and surface charge density measurements, revealing an increase of approximately +6.3 mV and 0.81 mC m–2 compared to the unmodified substrate. The positive surface charge was pivotal for ion selectivity. The membrane exhibited high selectivity for K+ over H+, as evidenced by ion transference number measurements (tH+ decreased from 0.82 to 0.65). Using a customized H-type diffusion cell, we measured the proton permeation rate, which was significantly reduced by ~50% (from 2.553 mol m–2 h–1 for the pristine substrate to 1.269 mol m–2 h–1 for DcoPZ). The membrane's effectiveness was demonstrated in practical zinc-manganese flow batteries (ZMFBs). It enabled a near-neutral battery system to achieve a record accumulated capacity of 6510 mAh cm–2 over 200 cycles at a high current density of 30 mA cm–2 with an areal capacity of 30 mAh cm–2 This represents a monumental improvement in lifespan and stability for ZMFBs, directly attributable to the suppressed H⁺ crossover and consequent mitigation of Zn corrosion and dead MnO₂ formation. Objective 4: We examined the nucleation and growth of MnO2 and the role of electrolyte composition and operating conditions. We studied the interrelated MnO2 deposition/dissolution behavior in the context of proton management. A key finding was that the local H+ concentration, governed by the membrane ability to retain protons in the posolyte, critically determined the efficacy of MnO2 dissolution during discharge. We employed UV-Vis spectroscopy to semi-quantitatively track the concentration of dissolved Mn2+ and the formation of soluble intermediates. By effectively reducing H+ crossover, the DcoPZ membrane ensured a sufficient proton concentration for the MnO2 reduction reaction, thereby enhancing its reversibility of the Mn2+/MnO2 couple. The synergistic strategy provides favorable conditions for ZMFBs to work at a high current density amounting to 100 mA cm-2 at 30 mAh cm-2. Furthermore, by altering the operational mode to simulate fluctuating renewable sources, the flow batteries show a high charge capacity of 90 mAh cm–2 (111.7 mWh cm–2) over 420 hours, with plating for nearly 8 hours per cycle. A higher charge capacity of 100 mAh cm–2 (130.1 mWh cm–2) was achieved for nearly two weeks with a plating time of 6.4 hours, representing one of the best stabilities reported for zinc-manganese flow batteries. Objective 5: We implemented a redox-mediated strategy to enhance the reversibility of the Mn2+/MnO2 couple. Potassium Iodide (KI) was introduced into the posolyte at concentrations of 0.1 M to 0.15 M. The I⁻/ I3⁻ redox couple acted as an mediator to facilitate the reduction of deposited MnO2. During charge, I⁻ is oxidized to I₃⁻ at the carbon electrode. The generated I3⁻ then chemically oxidizes Mn2+ to MnO2. More importantly, during discharge, I3⁻ can diffuse to and chemically reduce the solid MnO2 deposits (even those that are electronically disconnected or physically exfoliated) back to Mn²⁺, thereby recovering active material. The effectiveness of this mediator was confirmed by the superior battery performance. The full cell achieved stable cycling over 200 cycles, demonstrating the effectiveness of the mediator strategy in improving cathode reversibility. This mediator strategy was instrumental in achieving high areal capacities. For instance, in ZMFBs equipped with the DcoPZ membrane and the KI mediator, we demonstrated stable cycling at an ultra-high areal capacity of 100 mAh cm⁻² (130.1 mWh cm⁻²) for over 321 hours (~13.4 days), with a plating time of nearly 6.4 hours per cycle, enabling a highly reversible and high-energy-density near-neutral Zn-Mn battery system. Overall, the project has achieved its objectives through a multidisciplinary approach combining in situ characterization, electrolyte engineering, interfacial design, and membrane science.

14308321.label: Major findings and research outcome
14308321.value: We developed innovative strategies to address critical challenges in aqueous Zn-based batteries, including dendrite formation, hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), and proton crossover. Key findings include: We proposed and demonstrated a novel nuclei-rich plating strategy to fundamentally alter the Zn deposition behavior. By constructing a hydroxyapatite-based nuclei-incubating interface on the Zn surface, we successfully transitioned the Zn plating mechanism from instantaneous nucleation to high-rate progressive nucleation. This approach enabled unprecedented cycling stability: over 1200 hours in symmetric cells under harsh conditions (15 mA cm–2, 10 mAh cm–2) with a coulombic efficiency of 99.7%. When integrated into a Zn–MnO2 full cell with a low N/P ratio of 1.9, the cell delivered a long cycle life of 3000 cycles, highlighting the profound impact of nucleation control on battery performance. We broke the solubility limit of eco-friendly and low-cost zinc acetate (Zn(Ac)2) from 1.6 m to 23 m by introducing hydrotropic agents (potassium acetate, urea, and acetamide). This change exposed hydrophilic carbonyl groups, enhancing interaction with water and suppressing free water activity. The resulting Zn-rich electrolyte (e.g., 10 m Zn(Ac)2 + 15 m KAc) exhibited a high Zn-ion transference number (0.42), expanded electrochemical window (~2.5 V), and significantly suppressed HER, as confirmed by OEMS. In practical applications, the Zn//PTO full cell retained 70% of its initial capacity after 4000 cycles at 10 C, demonstrating exceptional reversibility and rate capability. We designed a novel ion-regulating membrane (DcoPZ) featuring a surface-enriched positively charged network constructed via Zn2+ crosslinking with polyacrylonitrile. The membrane increased the proton transport barrier from 0.065 eV to 0.104 eV and reduced the H+ permeation rate by ~50%. Simultaneously, the surface charges guided uniform Zn2+ distribution at the electrode interface, promoting oriented Zn deposition along the (002) plane and suppressing dendrite formation. The DcoPZ-enabled Zn–Mn flow battery achieved a record accumulated capacity of 6510 mAh cm–2 over 200 cycles at 30 mA cm–2 and a high areal capacity of 100 mAh cm–2 (130.1 mWh cm–2) at 20 mA cm–2, representing one of the most stable and high-energy-density aqueous flow batteries reported. These findings provide comprehensive insights into electrolyte design, interfacial engineering, and membrane technology for low-cost, high-performance aqueous batteries.

14308321.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14308321.value: The developed near-neutral battery systems are particularly attractive for applications in wider temperature operation and sensitive environments due to their low toxicity and environmental friendliness. Further optimization of the electrolyte composition and membrane structure can lead to enhanced ionic conductivity, wider temperature operation, and improved durability. Future work can focus on the large-scale synthesis and production of hydrotrope-enabled concentrated electrolytes and ion-regulating membranes. This involves optimizing reaction conditions (e.g., solvent selection, crosslinking time) for membrane fabrication and developing continuous processes for electrolyte preparation. Extensive testing under real-world conditions—including varying temperatures, humidity, and load cycles—would be considered to evaluate long-term performance, safety, and reliability. Comprehensive life-cycle assessment (LCA) and techno-economic analysis (TEA) could be performed to quantify environmental benefits and cost competitiveness.

14308321.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14308321.value: To address the demand for safe, affordable, and sustainable energy storage is rapidly growing, we have developed aqueous battery technologies that overcome the key limitations of traditional lithium-ion batteries, which are known for their flammability, high cost, and resource scarcity. We developed safer, affordable, and long-lasting water-based zinc batteries to overcome key issues in traditional batteries. Our innovations include: a special layer that prevents harmful zinc spikes, enabling over 1200 hours of stable operation; a highly concentrated, eco-friendly electrolyte that retains 70% capacity after 4000 cycles; and a smart membrane that blocks damaging particles while maintaining high energy storage. These advances create efficient, non-flammable batteries using abundant materials. Next, we will scale up production with industry partners for real-world uses like storing solar and wind energy, powering electric vehicles, and supporting the grid. Ultimately, this project paves the way for a new generation of sustainable, high-performance energy storage systems that are crucial for a clean energy future.

14500121.label: Project Objectives

14500121.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14500121.value: Multi-dimensional panel data models have been widely used in empirical research and received much attention in the econometrics literature recently. The traditional multi-dimensional models often assume homogeneous slope coefficients, which can be violated easily in practice. It is well known that estimators based on misspecified models are often inconsistent and subsequent inferences are invalid. This project provides systematic studies on how to model slope heterogeneity in multi-dimensional panel data models. First, we consider a set of candidate models which allow heterogeneity across different dimensions, and provide an easy-to-implement OLS-type estimation method for the models. Second, we propose a model selection procedure based on cross-validation to determine the correct model. Third, we adopt adaptive group Lasso (least absolute shrinkage and selection operator) method to combine model selection and estimation. We will study the asymptotic properties of our new methods. Monte Carlo simulations will be used to demonstrate the finite sample performance of our methods. Empirical applications to international trade will be provided to show the importance of allowing heterogeneous effects and demonstrate the usefulness of our new methods. 多維面板數據模型已廣泛應用於實證研究，並且在最近計量經濟學文獻中也備受關注。傳統的多維度模型通常假設同樣的斜率係數，這在實踐中很容易被違反。眾所周知，基於錯誤模型的估計量是通常是不一致的，隨後的推論是無效的。該項目提供多維面板數據異質性建模的系統研究。首先，我們考慮一組允許異質性的候選模型並提供易於實現的OLS估計方法。其次，我們提出了一套模型選擇的方法。第三，我們採用Lasso的方法來結合模型選擇和估計。我們將研究新方法的漸近性質。蒙特卡洛模擬將用於驗證我們方法的有限樣本性質。新的方法會應用到國際貿易的實證研究，以此來顯示允許異質性的重要性並證明我們新方法的有用性。

14500121.label: Realisation of objectives

The paper is expected to be accepted after some minor revisions. Objective 1 is achieved. I propose a new estimation method to estimate those factors and their associated loadings. Objective 2 is achieved. In this paper, I systematically study the asymptotic properties of new estimators and develop the distribution theory. It turns out the theoretical development is challenging. The supplement to this paper contains about 100 pages of theoretical derivation. Objective 3 is achieved. 14500121.label: Major findings and research outcome
14500121.value: In the paper, entitled "Three-Dimensional Factor Models with Global and Local Factors", conditionally accepted at Econometric Theory, I explore a novel panel data model that integrates both latent global factors, which impact all individuals, and latent local factors, which affect specific groups of individuals. I propose a new multi-step estimation procedure based on principal component analysis. I first show that the numbers of global and local factors can be estimated uniformly consistently. Given the number of global and local factors, I propose new estimators for the factors and their associated factor loadings. I study the asymptotic properties of the new estimators and show that the new estimators are asymptotically normally distributed. Building on this result, we develop a new inference method for both global and local factors. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed methods, I conduct extensive Monte Carlo simulations to demonstrate that the new methods perform well in finite samples. I provide an application to the dataset of international trade that reveals the relative importance of different types of factors. I find that the global factor, source country factor, and destination country factor contribute to 14.4%, 21.0%, and 28.1% of the total sample variance, respectively.

14500121.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14500121.value: For the econometric theory, there are many interesting directions for future development. For example, so far, I have only considered stationary and strong factors in my model. It will be valuable to consider nonstationary factors with unit-root-type behavior, weak factors, or structural changes. Incorporating weak factors or accounting for non-stationarity within the model could provide deeper insights and enhance its robustness. Another example is to allow interaction between the unobservable factors and observable variables. By integrating these interactions, the model can offer a more comprehensive understanding of the underlying processes. Given the generality of the proposed model and estimation methods, it is imperative to conduct more empirical applications in the future. These applications will not only validate the theoretical advancements but also demonstrate the practical usefulness of the model in various empirical studies.

14500121.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14500121.value: I propose a novel three-dimensional panel data model that incorporates different types of unobservable factors. Specifically, the model includes global factors that affect all individuals and local factors that impact only certain groups of individuals. This type of model has numerous potential applications. The paper discusses three examples in the contexts of economic growth, trade, and macroeconomics, and provides a detailed empirical application in international trade. The model can be used for many different purposes. First, it provides an effective way of reducing the dimensionality and summarizing information for large data sets. Second, it provides useful variance decomposition in the spirit of ANOVA (analysis of variance). Third, the underlying unobservable factors may contain useful economic information. Fourth, the estimated factors can be thought of as diffusion indices and used to improve forecasting accuracy. Fifth, this model provides foundations for the more general model with observable exogenous regressors.

14500421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14500421.value: Companies are actively collecting data on consumers’ activities to infer their interests and preferences. The ability to store and move personal data electronically independent of physical presence has given rise to data-driven markets, which makes consumers’ privacy concerns salient. Policy makers around the globe are actively legislating or amending regulations that aim to protect consumers' privacy rights in online data-driven markets. Examples include Hong Kong’s PDPO passed in 1995 and amended in 2012, EU’s GDPR enacted in 2016, California’s CCPA enacted in 2018. While common wisdom and arguments about how these privacy regulations will help or hurt the online advertising industry prevail, it remains unclear how they will impact the long-run equilibrium market outcomes. We aim to answer the following research questions in this project: (1) Given that consumers' control of their data has been one of the capstones for privacy protection adopted by policy-makers across jurisdictions around the globe, what are the market implications of consumers' control? Do consumers always benefit from control of their data? If so, what types of consumers benefit most? (2) How does consumers' control affect the online advertising industry? Can advertising firms and platforms also benefit from consumers' control? Is there a win-win situation? (3) Besides granting consumer control, are there other effective privacy regulation policies? What is the optimal mechanism for privacy regulation from a social welfare point of view that balances privacy needs and the value of sharing? Is the optimal mechanism in a relatively simple form that allows for easy implementation in practice? Is it robust to consumers' inattention and miscalculation? In answering these research questions, we aim to provide a unified economic analysis of privacy regulations in data-driven market. Our research will provide insights into the underlying economic tradeoffs as well as practical guidelines for policy-makers in Hong Kong and elsewhere, when revising the current privacy laws to cope with new privacy challenges and address public concerns for data-driven economy. 很多公司正在積極收集有關消費者活動的數據用來推斷他們的興趣和偏好。這種以電子方式存儲和移動個人數據的能力催生了數據驅動的市場，這使得消費者的隱私問題變得突出。全球的政策制定者正在積極立法或修訂法規，旨在保護數據驅動市場中消費者隱私權。例如： 1995 年通過並於 2012 年修訂的香港 PDPO、2016 年頒布的歐盟 GDPR、2018 年頒布的加利福尼亞州 CCPA。雖然關於這些隱私法規將如何幫助或損害在線廣告業的普遍智慧和爭論盛行，但尚不清楚它們如何將影響市場的長期均衡。我們旨在本項目中回答的以下研究問題：(1) 賦予消費者對其數據的控制權一直是全球各個司法管轄區政策制定者採用的隱私保護的主要原則，尚不清楚的這會對市場帶來什麼樣的影響？消費者是否總是受益於對其數據的控制權？如果是這樣，哪些類型的消費者受益最大？ (2) 消費者對數據的控制如何影響網絡廣告行業？廣告公司和平台能否也從中獲益？是否存在雙贏的局面？ (3) 除了賦予消費者對數據的控制權，還有其他有效的隱私監管政策嗎？從社會福利的角度來看，平衡隱私需求和共享價值的最佳隱私監管機制是什麼？最優機制是否具有相對簡單的形式以在實踐中易於實施？如果消費者存在疏忽和誤判，它是否仍然有效？通過回答這些研究問題，我們旨在對數據驅動市場中的隱私法規進行一個統一的經濟分析。我們的研究將為香港和其他地方的政策制定者在修訂現行隱私法規以應對公眾對數據驅動型經濟的擔憂時提供指導。

14500421.label: Major findings and research outcome
14500421.value: General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR)—the European Union’s data protection regulation—has two key principles. It recognizes that individuals own and control their personal (but not contractual) data in perpetuity, leading to three critical privacy rights, namely, the rights to (i) explicit consent (data opt-in), (ii) to be forgotten (data erasure), and (iii) portability (data transfer). It also includes data security mandates against privacy breaches through unauthorized access. We study GDPR’s equilibrium impact by including these features in a dynamic two-period model of forward-looking firms and consumers. Firms collect consumer data for personalization and price discrimination. Consumers trade off gains from personalization relative to potential losses from privacy breaches and price discrimination in their purchase, data opt-in, erasure, and transfer decisions. Though data security mandates impose fines on firms for privacy breaches, firms can benefit from higher opt-in given lower breach risk. Surprisingly, data security mandates can hurt consumers. The effect of privacy rights is nuanced. Since the right to opt in separates goods exchange from the provision of personal data, it prevents market failure under high breach risk. But it also reduces consumer opt-in and personal data availability. Erasure and portability rights reduce consumers’ hold-up concerns by disciplining firms to provide ongoing value by limiting price discrimination and not slacking off on data security; but they also reduce the incentive to offer lower initial prices that encourages opt-in. Overall, privacy rights always benefit consumers in competitive markets, but they can surprisingly hurt consumers under monopoly, as monopolists have less incentives to subsidize consumer opt-in. They raise (reduce) firm profit and social welfare when breach risk is high (low). Finally, privacy rights increase firm profit most at moderate levels of data transferability. 14500421.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14500421.value: The digital economy increasingly relies on data collected across websites and platforms. While individual disclosures may seem harmless, aggregated data can re-identify consumers and expose them to privacy risks. We propose a theoretical framework that explains why consumer behavior often follows an "few or all'' pattern: some people disclose selectively to a handful of websites, while others fully abandon privacy protections and opt in everywhere. This finding sheds light on the paradox of privacy, offers a new mechanism for understanding heterogeneity in consumer behavior online, and has direct implications for the design of privacy regulation and platform policy. One working paper: Nonlinear Identification Risk from Data Aggregation Leads to Privacy Choice Polarization. Co-authored with Zikun Liu and K. Sudhir.

14500521.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14500521.value: 隨著信息技術的快速發展，社交媒體開始在個人投資者的決策過程中發揮越來越重要的作用。 Seeking Alpha 和雅虎財經等在線投資社區 (OIC) 已成為投資者與他人分享投資意見的熱門場所。發現從 OIC 中提取的投資者意見對股市有重大影響。 OIC 生成的內容對個人投資者的價值已經得到證實，但沒有研究調查影響內容受歡迎程度的因素。具體而言，活躍在OIC的個人投資者是否明智地將注意力主要集中在文章受歡迎程度、文章的有用信息上，或者只是被文章的表麵線索所吸引，目前還不得而知。 為了填補這一研究空白，我們的研究將根據在 OIC 上發表的預測股票趨勢的文章來研究以下研究問題： OIC 讀者是否主要基於文章的有用性而喜歡它？如果不是，這種非理性行為將如何進一步影響 OIC 文章貢獻者的行為？ 為了回答上述研究問題，我們將使用從 Seeking Alpha 獲得的 OIC 文章數據進行一系列文章、讀者和作者級別的分析。首先，我們將進行文章級別的分析，以確定文章特徵與文章有用性對文章流行度的相對重要性。其次，從消費的角度，進行讀者層面的分析，考察讀者偏好文章的特徵隨著他/她的經驗增加而發生的變化。最後，從供給側的角度，我們也將進行作者層面的分析，以檢驗作者寫作風格隨經驗增加的演變。 PI 和 Co-Is 在相關主題上進行了合作，並成功地完成了關於 OIC 的工作論文，這些論文將在即將舉行的幾個會議上提交。我們希望我們提出的研究能夠通過在在線社區中找到一種新的注意力偏差形式，對學術文獻和管理實踐做出重大貢獻。

14500521.label: Realisation of objectives
14500521.value: We have successfully achieved the objectives outlined in this study through a comprehensive data collection, analysis, and empirical investigation process. 1. Data Collection and Cleaning We have collected, assembled, and cleaned OIC data from Seeking Alpha and financial market data from CRSP. The data was preprocessed to remove inconsistencies, missing values, and duplicates, ensuring a high-quality dataset for analysis. 2. Theoretical Proposition and Empirical Identification of Attention Bias We have developed a theoretical framework defining attention bias in Online Investment Communities (OICs). Through empirical identification using Seeking Alpha data, we have tested and confirmed the presence of attention bias, where investors tend to focus more on superficial article characteristics rather than the actual helpfulness of the content. 3. Empirical Identification of Mechanisms Underlying Attention Bias We have identified key mechanisms contributing to attention bias through both reader-level and author-level analyses. Our empirical findings reveal that both readers and authors exhibit behavioral trends that further reinforce attention bias in OICs. 4. Reader-Level Analysis (Consumption Perspective) We have analyzed how readers’ article preferences evolve with experience. The results demonstrate that as readers gain more experience, their focus slightly shifts toward more substantive content, but superficial cues still play a dominant role in article selection. 5. Author-Level Analysis (Provision Perspective) We have examined how authors adjust their writing styles over time. Our findings suggest that experienced authors tend to refine their article structures and adopt strategies that maximize engagement, often prioritizing readability and sentiment over in-depth analysis to attract more attention. 6. Managerial Implications Our study provides critical insights for OIC platform managers, authors, and investors. The results highlight the existence of attention bias, where online investors disproportionately focus on superficial cues rather than helpfulness. We offer recommendations to improve content ranking algorithms, enhance investor awareness, and guide authors toward more balanced content strategies. These insights contribute to better decision-making and improved content consumption in OICs. Through these efforts, we have successfully met our research objectives, providing a robust theoretical and empirical understanding of attention bias in Online Investment Communities.

14500521.label: Major findings and research outcome
14500521.value: This research examines how investors on social media react to firms’ ESG (Environmental, Social, and Governance) performance. Using investor-generated content from Seeking Alpha and ESG scores from Sustainalytics, the study finds that: • ESG performance predicts social media attention: Firms with higher ESG scores receive more discussions and articles on Seeking Alpha. • ESG performance does not predict social media sentiment: Investors’ opinions (positive or negative) about firms are not significantly influenced by ESG ratings. • Environmental and social factors drive attention: Investors are particularly responsive to environmental and social aspects of ESG but less so to corporate governance. • ESG downgrades reduce attention, while upgrades increase it: Negative ESG events lead to a drop in investor discussions, while positive ESG changes attract more attention. • Robustness checks confirm findings: The results hold across different methodologies, event studies, and statistical tests. These findings highlight that ESG affects investors primarily by increasing visibility (attention) rather than changing their opinions (sentiment).

14500521.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14500521.value: Future research can extend this study by: • Expanding the sample beyond S&P 500 firms: Investigating smaller or international firms could provide deeper insights. • Exploring other social media platforms: Studying Twitter, Reddit, or Yahoo! Finance could reveal different investor reactions to ESG. • Analyzing real-time ESG news events: Examining how specific ESG-related news influences investor behavior could provide more actionable insights. • Investigating long-term financial impacts: Assessing whether ESG-driven attention translates to stock performance over time. • Enhancing sentiment analysis: Using advanced AI techniques to analyze investor sentiment more accurately. The proposed course of action includes developing a broader dataset, refining sentiment analysis methodologies, and exploring additional investor behavior patterns.

14500521.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14500521.value: This research explores how investors react to companies’ ESG (Environmental, Social, and Governance) performance on social media. ESG is an important factor in sustainable investing, influencing business decisions and financial markets. However, it remains unclear how much investors actually care about ESG when discussing stocks online. The study analyzes investor discussions on Seeking Alpha, a popular online investment community, and compares them with ESG scores from professional rating agencies. The findings reveal that companies with higher ESG scores receive more attention online, meaning they are talked about more frequently. However, investors' opinions (positive or negative sentiment) do not change significantly based on ESG scores. In other words, ESG influences visibility but not investor perception. Interestingly, investors are more responsive to environmental and social aspects of ESG than corporate governance. Additionally, when a company’s ESG rating improves, discussions increase, and when it declines, discussions decrease. These insights are valuable for businesses, investors, and policymakers. Companies can use ESG strategies to attract investor attention, while regulators can focus on improving investor awareness of governance issues. Understanding these dynamics helps create more informed and responsible investment decisions in the digital era.

14500621.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14500621.value: Investors are increasingly concerned with corporate environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance and actively manage ESG risks, related to poor ESG performance, to enhance investment value. The COVID-19 crisis once again highlights that ESG can have significant implications for the economy and for society (JP Morgan, 2020). We study the interactions between firm ESG performance and the equity option market. Specifically, we examine how ESG performance affects investors’ perceived risk, and, therefore, the pricing of ESG risk in option market. We establish causality by investigating multiple ESG risk shocks and the effects of Paris Agreement. We explore the time-series and cross-sectional features of the interactions between ESG performance and option market. The U.S. equity option market has experienced tremendous growth accompanied by liquidity improvement in the past 20 years. Combined with low transaction costs and high leverage (Biais and Hillion (1994)), option market is a primary outlet for informed trading as option prices are very sensitive to and informative about risk and uncertainty. For example, options whose lives span political events tend to be more expensive, reflecting that political uncertainty is priced (Kelly et al. (2016)). Ilhan et al. (2020) find that climate policy uncertainty is priced in the option market. Bloom (2009) shows that option implied volatility negatively predicts employment and output. Yet, it is unknown whether option market participants care about the underlying firm’s ESG performance and related risks. Our study provides the first empirical evidence for this question. Besides filling the void in literature about how firm ESG performance affects option market, our proposed study is of use in at least three practical situations. First, option market may be the best outlet to study the price of ESG risk, as the market consensus option price can be regarded as representing the perceived level of risk for the underlying firm. Given that ESG risk can be related to future rare events like climate changes and litigations, the forward-looking information embedded in option prices better quantifies the compensation for the ESG related risks in higher moments. Second, the ESG risk information from option market is important for asset managers given the growing importance of managing risks like climate change in risk management process (Pastor et al. (2020)). Third, the perceived ESG risk measures constructed from option data can serve as indicators for corporate managers to adjust firm behaviors. 投資者越來越關注企業環境、社會和治理 (ESG) 表現，並積極管理控制與 ESG相關的風險，以提升投資價值和回报率。去年来势汹汹的新冠疫情危機再次凸顯 了ESG對經濟和社會的潛在重要性。在这样的大环境下，我們的項目研究了公司 ESG 績效與股票期權市場之間的相互作用。具體而言，我們分析了公司ESG 的表現如何影響投資者的感知風險，進而影響期權市場中與ESG相關的風險的定價。我們通過調查多個 ESG 風險衝擊和巴黎協定來確定因果關係， 並且進一步探討了 ESG 表現與期權市場之間相互作用的時間序列和橫截面特徵。 在過去的 20 年裡，美國股票期權市場經歷了空前絕後的增長，伴隨著流動性的巨大改善。受益於低交易成本和高槓桿率（Biais 和 Hillion（1994）），同時又由於期權價格對風險和不確定性異常敏感， 期權市場便成為了知情交易的主要平台。例如，政治事件發生時期的期權往往更昂貴，反映出政治不確定性是會影響證券價格的（Kelly 等人（2016 年））。Ilhan等人在他們 2020的文章中發現氣候政策的不確定性在期權市場中也同樣會影響資產價格。 Bloom (2009) 發現期權隱含波動率與未來的就業率以及產出呈現負相關。然而，期權市場參與者是否關心標的公司的 ESG 表現和相關風險尚不清楚。我們的研究為這個問題提供了第一個實證證據。 除了填補有關公司 ESG 績效如何影響期權市場的文獻中的空白外，我們提出的研究在實際情況中至少有三方面的指導意義。首先，期權市場可能是研究 ESG 風險價格的最佳渠道，因為期權價格能反應出投資者對標的公司的感知風險。鑑於 ESG 風險可能與氣候變化法規和公司訴訟等稀有事件相關，期權價格中嵌入的前瞻性信息能更好地量化 ESG 相關風險的補償。其次，來自期權市場的 ESG 風險信息對資產管理公司十分重要（Pastor 等人（2020）），因為在風險管理過程中氣候變化等相關風險的重要性日益增加。第三，由期權價格所構建的ESG感知風險數據，可以作為企業管理者調整企業行為的一個全新指標。

14500721.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14500721.value: As the outbreak of COVID- 19 surged around the world, affecting millions of people, the hospitality sector experienced a sharp decline in consumer spending. Due to lockdown measures, bars, restaurants, and hotels were forced to close (Hall et al., in press). When the COVID-19 curve flattened, some governments slowly started to re-open businesses, including restaurants and hotels. With reopening came many changes in service encounters to keep people safe (both service providers and customers) in the face of the ongoing pathogen threat. In particular, service robots are becoming a significant part of service delivery tasks in the hospitality industry, including cleaning facilities, taking orders at restaurants, and handling check-in processes at a hotel. It is unclear how consumers are responding to this “new normal” in service delivery, namely contactless services, in which advanced technologies (e.g., artificial intelligence and robots) replace human service providers to minimize direct contact with consumers during service interactions (Henkel et al., in press). How do consumers evaluate contactless service delivery by service robots at a re-opened restaurant or café? More specifically, during/after the COVID-19, how do they perceive service interactions with different types of service robots? And what underlies their reactions? To address these questions, the current research theorizes that contactless service provision during the coronavirus pandemic triggers consumers’ basic need to be connected with others (e.g., friends and family), which consequently influences their evaluation of humanlike features of service robots. Specifically, we propose that, when the contagion threat (operationalized as the COVID-19 in the current project context) is salient, consumers will evaluate more positively contactless service by humanoid (vs. non-humanoid) service robots because the robots’ humanlike-ness may at least partially satisfy consumers’ need to feel connected with others. We will also explore if this relationship holds (i) with consumers from different cultural backgrounds, and (ii) under different social situations. In sum, this research will provide important insights into consumer reactions to service robots during/after the coronavirus pandemic, as well as consumer, robot, and contextual factors that affect these reactions. Both lab and field experiments will be conducted to test our theorizing. 新冠肺炎全球肆虐，各國的封關及社交距離措施，影響着數以百萬計人的生活及對各國經濟造成嚴重打擊。其中對酒店，餐飲服務業的影響尤其嚴峻。 儘管疫情逐漸緩和，顧客仍然面對持續的新冠肺炎感染風險，因此酒店及餐飲服務業的營運需要強調顧客安全的重要性。而服務機械人在這方面可以擔當着一個重要的角色，例如在酒店及餐廳進行無人消毒清潔，負責食物下單以及在酒店裏接待旅客入住。 面對着這種非接觸式服務(人工智能及服務機械人代替人與人接觸)普及化，顧客會怎樣評價這種新的服務？他們又怎樣評價不同類型的服務機械人？其背後的原因會是什麼？ 在探討這些問題，本研究推測當人們面對這些非接觸式服務的時候，會激發他們的社交需要(例如渴望與家人及朋友見面)。所以當他們接觸人形化的機械人時，會對他們產生較正面的評價(相比於非人形的機械人)，因為人形化的機械人外型符合了人類追求社交的原始需要。我們亦會探討不同文化背景以及不同社交情況下，人們對機械人的評價會有什麼不同。 總括而言，本研究將會對新冠肺炎疫情下，服務機械人如何影響消費者評價有重要的啟示。本研究將會採取實驗方法來測試以上的推測。

14500721.label: Realisation of objectives
14500721.value: Regarding the first objective, we have accomplished 100% of it by examining consumer behavior in the context of contactless service delivery by service robots. We have successfully conducted a field study and multiple online experimental studies to test the consumer responses to robotic services in various contexts (e.g., hotel and restaurant). We were also able to test various manifestation of consumer responses to service delivery by robots, including service evaluation, attitude towards robots, and purchase behavior. Regarding the second objective, we have accomplished 100% of it by demonstrating the mediating role of a social motive in explaining consumer behavior in the context of contactless service delivery by service robots. Through multiple rounds of online experiments, we had measured the social motives in various forms and found these psychological mechanism can at least partly explain how consumers respond to the service delivery by service robots. Regarding the third objective, we also have accomplished 100% of it by testing an individual level factor (i.e., nationality) and a contextual factor (i.e., group composition) that moderates consumer behavior in the context of contactless service delivery by service robots. For the individual-level factor, we have collected data from different countries, including U.S., U.K., and Hong Kong. For the contextual factor, we relied on a scenario-based manipulation of group composition to test its effect. Using a field experiment and online experiments, we were able to draft a decent package of studies and submit it to Annals of Tourism Research, which is one of the top journals in the hospitality and tourism fields, in September 2023. After multiple rounds of revision and resubmission, the manuscript was accepted for publication in March 2024.

14500721.label: Major findings and research outcome
14500721.value: In three field and online experimental studies, we demonstrate that consumers are more likely to make indulgent choices in a robotic (vs. interpersonal) service encounter. However, these effects are muted when consumers interact with a humanoid (vs. non-humanoid) service robot because humanlike robots can generate a stronger automated social presence. We found such impact of service encounter type with samples from different nationalities: U.S. and Hong Kong. Moreover, this robotic effect on consumer indulgence is diminished in group consumption (vs. solo) settings where consumers have a lower level of desire for social connections. Our research advances the literature on service robotics by examining a novel unintended consequence of consumer–robot interactions: the likelihood of indulgent choices. Moreover, our work identifies a new underlying mechanism, namely, consumers' situational need to belong (i.e., social affiliation motive). This mechanism explains how robotic service encounters influence consumers' indulgent choices. Finally, our research reveals a boundary condition for the effect of robotic service encounters on solo versus group consumption. Understanding how group composition (solo vs. group) influences a focal consumer's behavior is important because solo consumption is a global tourism trend. While previous investigations have explored diverse factors that influence solo consumers' behavioral intentions, we identify a novel factor: the role of robotic service encounters in solo consumers' preferences for indulgent choices. Together, our findings add to the growing body of literature on indulgence and solo dining. From a managerial lens, understanding the unintended consequences of robotic service encounters will benefit tourism and hospitality firms by providing tailored product offerings. Additionally, our findings call for attention from policymakers and practitioners by showing that the rise of robotic service encounters may result in unintended unhealthy behaviors among consumers. Given the global trend of healthy eating and well-being, we suggest that practitioners may want to leverage humanlike features to service robots to help consumers regulate such unintended acts of indulgence.

14500721.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14500721.value: The current research focuses on how the service agent type (humanoid vs. non-humanoid vs. human) influences consumers' indulgent choices. However, special circumstances may present important boundary conditions for this effect. For example, in an extremely crowded restaurant, consumers' social withdrawal tendencies may override the need to belong, and consequently, the agent effect on indulgence may be diminished. Moreover, some individuals might prefer solo dining and thus feel less lonely and have a weaker situational need to belong, thereby demonstrating a pattern opposite to our findings in Study 3.1 More boundary conditions should be explored to ensure the robustness of the service agent's effects on indulgence. We regarded the need to belong as the key underlying mechanism of the agent-type effect on indulgent consumption. However, there may be alternative explanations for this effect. For example, prior research has suggested that food consumption plays a role in impression management. That is, people are motivated to make healthy food choices to achieve a socially desirable image. Given that people tend to experience fewer social concerns about their actions during human–robot interactions due to low levels of mind perceptions, exploring the role of impression management in people's decision-making in robotic service encounters is worthwhile. Culture plays a pivotal role in shaping consumer behaviors, and cross-cultural studies have consistently indicated that Asians exhibit greater sensitivity to social relationships and interactions than Westerners. It is conceivable that Asian tourists and consumers might possess a stronger need for social belonging and engage more extensively in indulgent consumption when encountering robotic services. Further research could examine this intriguing cultural distinction.

14500721.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14500721.value: This research shows that people are more likely to make indulgent choices, like splurging on treats, when they interact with robots instead of humans. However, this tendency is lessened when the robot looks human-like because these robots create a stronger sense of social connection. Additionally, when people are in groups, they tend to indulge less compared to when they are alone, as they feel less need for social interaction. For businesses in tourism and hospitality, understanding how robotic service can influence consumer choices is important for creating better products. Our findings also highlight a potential concern for policymakers: the increasing use of robots in service roles might lead to unhealthy eating habits among consumers. Given the growing focus on healthy living, we suggest that making robots appear more human-like could help encourage better choices among consumers.

14500921.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14500921.value: Remanufacturing industry is an integral part of circular economy and is expanding rapidly attributed to recent technical advances like additive manufacturing, data analytics, and internet of things (IoT). There is a wide range of industry sectors that have successfully applied remanufacturing, including electrical and electronic equipment, automotive, medical devices, and aerospace. For example, the market size of auto parts remanufacturing is 6.8 billion USD in the US while around 7.4 billion Euro in Europe. A remanufacturing firm usually collects product returns (or called {it cores}) from either end users or third-party brokers and then remanufacture them into serviceable products to fill customer demand. Remanufacturing involves taking products or components to like-new conditions, via a variety of processes and new technologies. By remanufacturing, the firm can save costs and energy of manufacturing from new materials, extend the life cycle of products, generate sales and revenue, and establish ``environmental-friendly" image to the public. The uncertainties of returned product quantities and customer demand and their dependence over time impose great operational challenges on remanufacturing firms, which affect their efficiency, profitability, and quality of customer service. In this project, we study infinite-horizon, periodic-review remanufacturing inventory systems with random product returns and customer demands. Distinct from most of the prior studies, the quantity of returned products in a period depends on demands occur in the previous periods. The firm decides remanufacturing and manufacturing quantities and uses on-hand serviceable inventory to fill customer demand with an aim to minimize the expected long-run average cost per period. Due to the well-known ``curse of dimensionality'' of the resulting dynamic program of optimal analysis, we focus on developing and analyzing simple, easily implementable policies, such as simple base-stock policy, forecast-adjusted base stock policy with or without disposal. Via the stationary analysis of the underline stochastic processes of inventory dynamics, we develop simple approximations for the optimal policy parameters. These approximations improve the implementability of the policies and enable us to unveil some insights of managing such inventory systems. We demonstrate and compare the effectiveness of the approximations and the simple policies numerically over both simulated and real data. Moreover, we study the impact of mis-specifying the return forecasting models. Several important extensions will be studied, including disposal of cores, multiple types of cores, joint management of new and remanufactured products. 產品再製造行業作爲循環經濟不可或缺的一部分近來迅速發展，主要歸因與技術的進步，如3D打印，數據分析，和物聯網。有許多不同的工業行業已經成功的運用再製造，包括電子與電氣設備，汽車，機械，及航空航天。例如，汽車部件再製造的市場規模在美國和歐洲分別達到了68億美金和74億歐元。再製造企業通常從產品使用者或者第三方中間商回收使用過的舊產品，然後對其進行再製造，從而變成可以用來滿足客戶需求的產品（再製造產品）。再製造通過一系列的步驟和技術，將舊產品轉變成接近或達到新產品質量標準的產品。通過再製造，企業可以節約生產成本和原材料及能源成本，延長產品的生命周期，產生新的銷售和收益，同時建立崇尚環保的品牌形象。 回收產品的數量和再製造產品需求的不確定性及之間的相關性給再製造企業的運作帶來挑戰，影響其效率，盈利，及顧客服務質量。在本項目中，我們研究無限階段，離散時間的再製造庫存系統。該系統面臨隨機的產品回收和顧客需求。和之前的研究不同，我們考慮每一期回收產品的數量和之前產品的需求（銷售）相關。企業需要決定再製造和製造（使用新的部件）產品的數量並使用再製造產品的庫存來滿足每階段的顧客的需求。 企業的目標是最小化每期的平均成本。 由於用來求解最優策略的動態規劃問題狀態空間的維度太大，我們主要關注簡單易行的控制策略，如簡單的基準庫存策略和基於預測調整的基準庫存策略。通過對這些策略下庫存動態所對應的隨機過程的穩態分析，我們開發出對於最優控制參數的簡單的近似。這些近似能夠使得這些策略的實用性更强同時揭露管理該類庫存系統的一些洞察。我們在實際和仿真數據上展示及比較這些近似的有效性。同時，我們還研究了如果使用錯誤的產品回收預測模型帶來的影響。我們還會討論幾個重要的拓展，包含舊產品的丟棄，多種可回收的舊產品，及共同管理新舊產品的庫存。

14500921.label: Realisation of objectives
14500921.value: All the project objectives have been achieved successfully. In the paper titled “Remanufacturing Inventory System with Demand-Dependent Returns: Optimality Analysis and Approximations,” we have conducted a thorough literature review on the product return models that consider historical demand/sales and other features. This realizes Project Objective 1. We develop remanufacturing inventory models with demand-dependent product return. In particular, we study an infinite-horizon periodic-review remanufacturing inventory system with random demand and product returns. The quantity of returned products each period depends on the historical demands following a distributed lag model. A firm operating the system remanufactures product returns into a serviceable product to fulfil customer demand. When needed, the serviceable product can also be manufactured/ordered. Manufacturing and remanufacturing have different lead times. The firm decides manufacturing quantity each period in order to minimize the expected long-run average cost of inventory holding, demand backlogging, and manufacturing. The problem is formulated as a Markov Decision Process (MDP). This realizes Project Objective 2. We analyze the model to establish the existence of stationary optimal policy under the long-run average cost criterion using the vanishing discount factor approach together with a coupling argument. Via state space reduction, we further prove that the optimal policy is a so-called forecast-adjusted base-stock (FABS) policy when the maximum return lag is shorter than the manufacturing lead time. When the maximum return lag is longer than the manufacturing lead time, the optimal policy becomes state-dependent base-stock type. Due to the challenge of the computation of optimal solution and its implementation of the latter case, we adopt the FABS policy in general, provide an exact evaluation procedure via stationary analysis, and develop easily computable approximations for the optimal base-stock level. These realize Project Objectives 3 and 4. In a numerical study, we show that the FABS policy and the approximations are very effective. This realizes Objective 5. Moreover, we numerically demonstrate that the FABS policy performs much better than a simple base-stock policy that does not incorporate forecast of product return, which demonstrate the value of return forecast. This realizes Objective 6. This paper is currently under first-round Major revision with Operations Research.

14500921.label: Major findings and research outcome
14500921.value: There are two major outputs (papers) from this project. The first paper mentioned earlier entitled “Remanufacturing Inventory System with Demand-Dependent Returns: Optimality Analysis and Approximations” is currently under first-round Major Revision with Operations Research. The second paper entitled “Sampling-Based Approximation for Series Inventory Systems” is forthcoming at Management Science. I will next provide a short summary of the major findings in each of the two papers. In the first paper, we study an infinite-horizon periodic-review remanufacturing inventory system with random demand and product returns. A firm operating the system remanufactures product returns into a serviceable product to fulfil random customer demand. When needed, the serviceable product can also be manufactured/ordered. The firm decides manufacturing quantity each period to minimize the expected long-run average cost of inventory holding, demand backlogging, and manufacturing. We first establish the existence of stationary optimal policy under the long-run average cost criterion. Due to the challenge of the computation of optimal solution and its implementation, we adopt a so-called forecast-adjusted base-stock (FABS) policy, provide an exact evaluation procedure via stationary analysis, and develop easily computable approximations for the optimal base-stock level. In a numerical study, we show that the FABS policy and the approximations are very effective. In the second paper, we study inventory management of an infinite-horizon, series system with multiple stages. Each stage incurs inventory holding cost while the most downstream stage also incurs demand backlogging cost when it experiences inventory shortage. The objective is to minimize the expected total discounted cost over the planning horizon. We apply the sample average approximation (SAA) method to obtain a heuristic policy (SAA policy) using the empirical distribution function constructed from a demand sample (of the underlying demand distribution). We derive an upper bound of sample size (viz., distribution-free bound) that guarantees that the performance of the SAA policy be close (i.e., with arbitrarily small relative error) to the optimal policy under known demand distribution with high probability. We also provide a lower bound of sample size that matches the upper bound (in the order of relative error). Furthermore, when the demand distribution is continuous and has an increasing failure rate (IFR), we derive a tighter sample size upper bound (viz., distribution-dependent bound). In addition, we show that both bounds increase polynomially as the number of stages increases. Finally, we extend the results to finite-horizon series systems.

14500921.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14500921.value: The PI will first conduct the revision of the first paper and resubmit it to Operations Research. We will try to get the paper published soon. Meanwhile, there are several possible extensions relevant to the project that are worth pursuing, such as allowing the firm to keep inventories of returned products and decide when to remanufacture/dispose and considering more general product return modes. Moreover, we may incorporate demand and return learning when their distributions are unknown to the firm and need to be learned.

14500921.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14500921.value: The remanufacturing industry plays a key role in sustainability by reducing waste and saving resources. An operational challenge faced by many remanufacturing firms is to manage inventory efficiently facing uncertain product return and demand. This project examines a company that remanufactures used products (returns) to meet demand, while also ordering new products if needed. Random returns depend on past sales. We characterize the optimal policy that minimizes the cost of such system and further develop a simple and easy-to-implement heuristic that incorporates forecast of product return. Numerical tests show forecasting returns cuts costs significantly, and the heuristic performs well. Another output of the project looks at managing inventory in a multi-stage, serial supply chain, where each stage orders from the one before it, and the first stage orders from an outside supplier. Customer demand at the final stage is random. The goal is to minimize total inventory-related costs over time. The study uses past demand data to create a smart ordering strategy (SAA policy) and calculates how much data is needed for this strategy to work almost as well as the best possible when assuming demand distribution is known. Results show the needed data size grows steadily with more stages.

14501321.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14501321.value: Many markets are characterized by the purchase of assortments with multiple units/varieties. There are two underlying mechanisms in assortment shopping, namely state dependence (i.e., utility reinforcement or satiation) and consumption flexibility. Previous studies have not sufficiently investigated how these two factors may interactively influence optimal assortment shopping and subsequent consumptions. We plan to meet this challenge by examining three related issues in the proposed project. First, we will fully solve the general dynamic programing problem for any assortment. We will consider a random-utility framework in which a forward-looking shopper decides on the optimal assortment and subsequent consumptions. We will derive closed-form solution for optimal consumption policy and maximum expected value of selecting any assortment. We will also investigate how the optimal assortment may vary with the decision parameters and evolve dynamically over time. Second, we will develop a structure model of grocery shopping for assortments and estimate it on panel data. This will allow us to demonstrate how our model can be embedded into a larger framework to construct structural models of assortment choice, which may yield distinctive advantages over extant reduced-form models. Third, we will develop algorithms to identify the optimal assortment by examining and exploiting its structural properties. This will allow us to efficiently simulate optimal assortment choices and conduct policy analysis to evaluate potential impacts of marketing decisions. The algorithms can also be used to recommend assortments to individual consumers. 許多市場的特徵之一是消費者可能會同時購買多個不同的產品（assortment choice）。這樣的現象有可能是由兩個原因導致的：路徑依賴（也就是說對於某個產品的效用會隨著以前的消費量的增加而增加或減少），以及爲了保持將來消費靈活性的動機。對於這兩個因素怎麽共同作用以影響消費者的最優購買以及隨後的消費策略，以前的文獻還沒有深入的研究過。爲了應對這個具有挑戰性的問題，我們計劃從三方面來進行研究。 首先，我們會尋求完整的解決關於如何選擇assortment的動態規劃問題。在我們考慮的隨機效用框架下，消費者會前瞻性的考慮最優assortment選擇以及之後的最優消費策略。我們會完整的刻畫消費者的最優消費策略，並推導出選擇任意一個assortment所帶來的期望價值。我們也會研究，當決策問題的參數發生變化時，或者隨著時間的推移，最優的assortment選擇會怎麽發生改變。第二，我們會構建一個結構性模型，並基於消費者日常購買assortment的面板數據來估計模型的參數。這方面的研究可以幫助我們展示如何把我們的模型嵌入更大的框架下，以構建結構性的模型來研究關於assortment的選擇，並展示我們的模型相比較之前文獻裏的模型有更爲顯著的優勢。第三，我們會基於最優assortment的結構性性質，來提出關於如何確立最優assortment的算法。這些算法可以幫我們更有效的預測消費者的最優assortment選擇行爲，以對各種營銷策略或決策的可能效果進行評估。我們的算法也可以用來對消費者的選擇進行推薦。

14501421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14501421.value: 眾所周知，創新是經濟增長最重要的驅動力之一（Spence，1984；Jaffe，1986；Aghion 和 Howitt，1992）。在過去的二十年裡，關於什麼因素可以推動創新的學術研究激增。創新產生的一個重要渠道是上游企業（通常是投入品供應商）進行創新以提高下游企業的生產力。供應商創新變得越來越重要，例如，Henke 和 Zhang (2010) 提供的證據表明，許多製造行業的公司依賴於他們自己的零件或材料供應商的創新來改進他們自己的產品或生產過程。研究已證明供應商的創新通常會導致供應商引用客戶現有的專利，反之亦然（Dasgupta、Zhang 和 Zhou，2020；Chen、Dasgupta、Huynh 和Xia，2020；Banerjee、Dasgupta 和 Shi，2020），这些研究結論发现了特定於供應商和客戶之間的研发与創新。 本研究使用囊括了全球專利申請和引用記錄的知識產權綜合數據庫，對知識產權保護如何影響國際供應鏈中的創新和技術合作進行分析。具體而言，我們通過專利制度強度和專利執法機制強度在不同國家和相同國家不同地區的差異，研究如果供應商所在國家和地區擁有更強的知識產權保護是否会引导美國客戶在該國從事更多的專利活動,并积极促进供應商與其美國客戶之間搭建更多技術合作。我們通過現有的數據庫創建不同的變量來衡量公司之间的技術合作。其中的一種變量是供應商及其客戶公司對彼此專利的交叉引用。此變量可以通過該知識產權數據庫實現, 因為這個數據庫不僅記錄了一個知識產權部門所管轄地區的所有專利，而且提供了關於這些專利是否引用了其它地區的專利的信息。如前所述，這種交叉引用現在廣泛用於供應鏈文獻中，以衡量技術合作和特定關係的投資。本研究還將通過引用客戶在該國提交的專利來探索對供應商所在國的其他公司可能產生的溢出效應，以及這些與美國客戶公司研發人員建立的關係是否會導致供應商國家的研發人員遷移到美國。總體而言，這項研究將提供證據來證明更強有力的知識產權保護製度是否會鼓勵貿易夥伴之間更多的技術合作，並促进更多供應鏈環節的形成，從而創造更多的就業和增長。

14501421.label: Realisation of objectives
14501421.value: All project objectives have been met. 1. One of the project’s most important contributions is to highlight the incentives of US customer firms to share knowledge with their foreign suppliers and facilitate the latter’s innovation. For this, cross-border patenting is important so that imitators cannot gain by stealing their intellectual property. 2. Our findings show that cross-border patenting by customers is associated with positive market reactions of suppliers and more innovation by suppliers when the economic value of these patents is higher. Since customers are unlikely to file patents and disclose knowledge in another country when the risk of their IP being usurped is high, our findings can be considered as prima facie evidence of the importance of IPRP at the country level. 3. The analysis includes both developed and developing countries. Separate attention has been provided to member countries of the European Patent Convention. One advantage of examining these countries separately is that patents filed with the European Patent Office automatically apply to all member countries, so that decision to file a patent is less endogenous to a specific country. 4. This is one of the key findings of the paper. We document significant spillovers that extend to the rival firms in the same supplier industry in the same country. The patenting activity of a supplier is positively related to the economic value of patents filed by customers of its rival firms in the same industry, and it cites more of these rival’s customers’ patents when generating its own patents. It also succeeds in attracting new customers (but distinct for rivals’ customers). 5. We found a paper by Kerr and Kerr (2018, cited in our working paper) which finds that US and foreign firms collaborate on patents (“global collaborative patents” with inventors from both sides involved) and migration to the US by foreign inventors tracks the ethnic connections of the inventors of US firms. While the study does not focus specifically on supply chain relationships, it does to some extent preempt this objective of our paper. We find similar results (we have created a comprehensive database on international inventor movements) but we did not include that in the current working paper. We may pursue it to study entrepreneurial activities of these inventors (not included in the current research objectives) in follow-up research.
