14504721.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14504721.value: Abstract (If results turn out as predicted) We find evidence that firms pay media outlets with high credibility to help improve their informational transparency. Contrary to the conventional belief that bought news service is mainly for achieving slanted coverage, we find that news reporting by connected media is associated with lower information asymmetry and lower earnings response coefficients than reporting by unconnected media. Connected media provide more of both positive coverages (i.e., coverages with positive tones) and negative ones, albeit proportionately more the former than the latter. Positive news articles from connected media are more informative to stock prices and associated with a greater reduction in information asymmetry than positive articles from unconnected media. Negative coverage of connected media is as informative as that of unconnected media. News articles by connected media are more original and more influential, and accompanied with a larger reduction in the daily bid-ask spread. Journalists from connected media also conduct more visits to the firms. In additional analysis, we find that firms with greater need for transparency are more likely to build business connections with the newspapers. 我們研究公司向高可信度的媒體支付費用，以幫助提高其信息透明度。與購買新聞服務主要是為了實現有偏報道的傳統觀點相反，我們發現，與無關聯媒體相比，有關聯媒體的新聞報道具有較低的信息不對稱性和較低的盈余反應系數（ERC）。有關聯的媒體提供了更多的正面報道（即帶有正面語氣的報道）和負面報道，盡管前者的比例高於後者。來自有關聯媒體的正面新聞文章比來自無關聯媒體的正面新聞文章對股價的信息量更大，並且與信息不對稱的減少程度更相關。有關聯媒體的負面報道與無關聯媒體的負面報道一樣信息豐富。有關聯媒體的新聞文章更具原創性和影響力，並伴隨著每日買賣價差的大幅下降。來自有關聯媒體的記者也對這些公司進行了更多的訪問。額外分析中，我們發現對透明度有更大需求的公司更有可能與報紙建立業務聯系.

14504721.label: Realisation of objectives
14504721.value: Obj 1: When a firm pays these media outlets for news service, how severe would be the coverage slanting? Consistent with prior research on media’s bias resulting from conflict of interest, news outlets indeed publish more positive news articles on their affiliated firms than on unaffiliated firms. When we estimate the same regression by replacing the dependent variable with the number of articles with negative tones, the indicator for the presence of business affiliation Affiliated is also significantly positive, though with a much smaller coefficient. Taken together, the results indicate that news outlets publish more of both positive and negative news reports for their affiliated firms, although the increase of positive news outpaces that of negative news. Additional analyses of news coverage around the revelation of accounting frauds provide a consistent message: there is no evidence that affiliated outlets, relative to their unaffiliated counterparts, positively bias their coverage either before or after the fraud catches public attention. In fact, affiliated outlets reduce positive and increase negative reporting of fraud firms more than unaffiliated outlets before the revelation of the frauds, consistent with affiliated outlets leveraging their information advantage and increasing the informativeness of their reports. Next, we examine good- and bad-performance years separately to explore whether coverage by affiliated media helps reduce information asymmetry in bad times. If affiliated newspapers are biased, firms are more likely to pressure them in bad times and their coverage can be uninformative or even misleading, increasing information asymmetry. Our analysis indicates that, when firms have a bad year, namely, when their annual stock returns or annual earnings are negative, coverage by affiliated media continues to exhibit a negative association with the bid-ask spread. Yet, the impact of coverage by affiliated news outlets on information asymmetry is stronger when the hiring firms have a good year than when they have a bad year. Using large shareholders and executives reducing their shareholdings as an alternative indicator of bad news, we also find that coverage by affiliated media reduces information asymmetry, although the effect is not as strong as in normal years. These results suggest that media’s favorable slanting does not necessarily conflict with informativeness. Obj 2: What would be the net effect to investors and the firm’s information environment? We begin our analysis by examining whether affiliated media outlets help reduce information asymmetry as measured by the bid-ask spread. Focusing on the four CSRC-designated media outlets and using annual data, we find that news reporting, excluding mandated disclosures, by affiliated media outlets is negatively associated with the firm’s bid-ask spread. Meanwhile, news reporting by unaffiliated media outlets is not significantly associated with the firm’s bid-ask spread, considered alone or jointly with affiliated coverages in the same model. Using a DiD design, we confirm that a firm’s bid-ask spread decreases after it adds an outlet to its official disclosure channel as compared to its industry and size-matched control peers. In addition, we reach a similar conclusion using the price reaction to earnings announcements as an alternative measure for firms’ informational transparency: More affiliated news coverage during the year is associated with a lower price reaction to firms’ earnings announcements. We do not observe such an effect for news coverage by unaffiliated news outlets, considered alone or jointly with affiliated news coverage. Obj 3: Do the media outlets’ journalists put in more efforts in producing their reports? To understand the mechanisms through which affiliated news outlets improve firms’ transparency, we examine whether news outlets invest more efforts in covering their affiliated firms. Analyses indicate that journalists conduct more site visits to their affiliated firms, suggesting that these journalists pay more attention and have greater access to affiliated firms. Excluding mandated disclosures on affiliated newspapers, we find that these outlets publish more news articles, both with positive and negative tones, about the hiring firms. Relatively, they publish a greater number of positive reports. DiD analyses reveal an increase in site visits and news coverage by a news outlet after it is added by the firm as one of its official disclosure platforms. Obj 4: Would their reports be more or less original and influential? We find that reports published by affiliated outlets tend to be more comprehensive than those by unaffiliated outlets. These reports are also more original compared to reports preceding them as reflected by how much the concerned news article is similar to news reports published in the previous seven days. Further, news reports from affiliated outlets are associated with a stronger market reaction than reports from unaffiliated outlets. Publication of the affiliated news reports is also associated with a lower bid-ask spread on the publication day measured relative to the average spread in the previous three days. While the superior informativeness of affiliated coverage is concentrated in news reports with positive tones, we find no evidence that news reports with negative tones issued by affiliated newspapers are less informative than those issued by unaffiliated outlets. Obj 5: What type of firms are incentivized to hire the news service of these media outlets? Further analyses show that the impact of affiliated media on information asymmetry is more pronounced when there is a greater demand for credible disclosure channels, for example, when hiring firms have more related-party transactions, when their local legal systems are weak, and when they have a large number of shareholders which indicates the presence of many retail investors. These findings are consistent with affiliated media coverage helping reduce information asymmetry by lowering investors’ information processing costs and firms proactively seeking this benefit when they have the need. Overall, our results demonstrate that firms in weak institutional environments can enhance transparency through establishing business connections with highly influential media outlets. Such enhancement effect materializes because affiliated news outlets invest more effort, provide more coverage, and publish more informative reports. Reputation concerns constrain these outlets from unduly biasing their reporting. While affiliated news outlets help firms reduce information asymmetry in both good and bad times, they tend to produce more reports with a positive tone than unaffiliated news outlets and their impact on information asymmetry is more pronounced in good times. Favorably slanted reporting can be still highly informative to investors. Our paper is the first to document that firms proactively collaborate with influential media to enhance their informational transparency. The prevalence of relationship-based transactions in emerging economies result in high information opacity among firms. Nonetheless, we find evidence consistent with firms having incentives to improve transparency. The findings further our understanding of alternative disclosure channels through which emerging-market firms reduce information asymmetry.

These reports are also more original compared to reports preceding them as reflected by how much the concerned news article is similar to news reports published in the previous seven days. Further, news reports from affiliated outlets are associated with a stronger market reaction than reports from unaffiliated outlets. Publication of the affiliated news reports is also associated with a lower bid-ask spread on the publication day measured relative to the average spread in the previous three days. While the superior informativeness of affiliated coverage is concentrated in news reports with positive tones, we find no evidence that news reports with negative tones issued by affiliated newspapers are less informative than those issued by unaffiliated outlets. Additional analyses of news coverage around the revelation of accounting frauds provide a consistent message: there is no evidence that affiliated outlets, relative to their unaffiliated counterparts, positively bias their coverage either before or after the fraud catches public attention.

14504721.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14504721.value: We examine in a weak legal environment whether and how purchased news coverage from media outlets with high influence affects firms’ information transparency by exploiting a unique setting where Chinese public firms purchase news coverage de facto through paying news outlets designated by the market regulator as mandatory disclosure platforms. We find that news coverage by the fee-affiliated newspapers – compared to unaffiliated news outlets – helps reduce information asymmetry. Evidence suggests that firms’ incentives to enhance transparency play a role in rendering the results. Affiliated media reduces information asymmetry in both good and bad times, although the effect is stronger when firms have good performance. We find no evidence of affiliated media significantly biasing their reports relative to unaffiliated outlets when there is bad news. Overall, we provide evidence on emerging-market firms proactively collaborating with influential media to enhance their informational transparency.

14505021.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14505021.value: 可比性減退以致暫時迷失？ - 會計變更、數據中介和散戶投資者

14505021.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14505021.value: Although the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) is quite forthcoming in protecting retail investors, accounting standard setters appear to be more lukewarm on retail investors. For example, retail investors are not explicitly listed on the Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB) website as the types of investors it wants to hear from, perhaps because retail investors are not regarded as the primary financial statement users. However, the recent emergence of low-cost online stock brokers has drawn more retail investors into direct stock investments. How retail investors utilize the financial statement information in their investing process is still not clear, especially when firms are transitioning to new accounting standard. Two recent pronounced accounting standard changes on revenue recognition and leases could have a significant impact on firms’ financial statements. Because the adoption of these new standards may require significant work by firms, standard setters provide practical expedients to reduce firms’ transition effort. These include the option for firms to adopt the modified retrospective approach for the transition. Under this approach, firms do not need to restate the comparative financial figures in prior years using the new standard. Consequently, their financial statements may present financial figures derived using two different standards: historical figures using the old standard and current figures using the new standard. During the initial application of new standard, the potential loss in intertemporal comparability in the presented financial figures may have differing impacts on different types of investors. While firms are required to state the impact of adopting the new standard in the notes to financial statements, retail investors may not have the necessary resources and sophistication to read through the detailed disclosures. Compared to institutional investors, retail investors could be more susceptible to using incomparable figures presented in financial statements to make their investment decisions during the transition. Using the recent transitions to IFRS 15 and IFRS 16 as the setting, the proposed project aims to utilize the unique data available in Hong Kong (HK) to examine whether intertemporal financial statement comparability matters for retail investors. Additionally, retail investors are likely to rely more on the summary financial figures provided by data intermediaries. High-quality data intermediaries may moderate the adverse impact on retail investors during the transition. The project thus will also examine the role of data intermediaries, an area largely unexplored in prior literature, in influencing the trading decisions of retail investors. 可能因為散戶投資者不被視為主要的財務報表使用者，財務會計準則委員會網站上並沒有明確列出散戶投資者是其希望聽取的投資者類型。然而，最近低成本在線股票經紀行的出現吸引了更多散戶投資者進行直接股票投資。現時尚不清楚散戶投資者究竟在投資過程中有多大程度上利用財務報表信息，尤其是公司在向新會計準則過渡時。 最近關於收入確認和租賃的兩項明顯的會計準則變化對公司的財務報表有潛在重大影響。由於採用這些新標準可能需要公司進行大量工作，因此會計準則制定者提供了實用的權宜之計，以減少公司的過渡工作。其中包括公司可以選擇採用修改後的追溯方法進行過渡。在這種方法下，公司無需使用新準則重述前幾年的比較財務數據。因此，他們的財務報表可能會同時列報兩種不同標準得出的財務數據：歷史數據使用舊標準，而當前數據使用新標準。 在新準則初始應用過程中，所列財務數據的跨期可比性潛在損失可能對不同類型的投資者產生不同的影響。雖然公司需要在財務報表附註中說明採用新準則的影響，但散戶投資者可能沒有資源和相關經驗來閱讀詳細的披露。與機構投資者相比，散戶投資者可能更容易在過渡期間使用財務報表中呈現的跨期無可比性的數字來做出投資決策。 以最近向 IFRS 15 和 IFRS 16 的過渡為背景，項目旨在利用香港可獲得的獨特數據來研究跨期財務報表可比性對散戶投資者是否重要。此外，散戶投資者可能更多地依賴數據中介機構提供的匯總財務數據。高質量的數據中介機構可能會在過渡期間緩和對散戶投資者的不利影響。因此，該項目還將研究數據中介在影響散戶投資者交易決策方面的作用，這一領域在先前的文獻中基本上沒有探索過。

14505121.label: Project Objectives
14505121.value: Re-evaluate the price informativeness measure proposed in the literature in the Chinese A-share market and the US stock market. This test will also shed light on how this reform improves price informativeness in China.

14505121.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14505121.value: 在本研究中，我們將探究投資者如何通過學習提升金融素養。具體而言，我們計畫研究（1）投資者如何從自己的交易經歷中學習，（2）金融教育的作用有多大，以及（3）從交易中學習的有效性如何可以被提高？我們將使用深圳股票交易所的帳戶級別交易數據以及通過深交所的投資者教育項目進行隨機試驗來研究這些問題。 本項目分為兩步。首先， 我们将利用深交所的交易數據，基於投資者的交易紀錄來構建投资者的金融素养指標。利用這些指標，我們可以研究新投資的投資素養如何隨者投資經驗的增加而提升。同時我們也關心，如果金融素養確有提升，會對投資者的投資表現和市場參與決策產生怎樣的影響。 第二步是進行一個隨機試驗來檢驗金融教育的效果。該試驗有兩個實驗組。一組會收到關於購買漲停板或是高送轉的股票高風險提示；另外一組除了相同的提示之外，還會收到投資者之前購買漲停板或是高送轉的股票的交易紀錄。這個額外的提醒在於加強過去投資經歷的對現在投資行為的影響。我們會觀察之後6個月這兩組投資者相對於對照組投資行為的變化。 本項目可以貢獻於投資者行為和投資者教育的研究文獻。還可以對市場監管提供指導，以提升投資者教育項目的效果。這對於像中國一樣的新興市場的投資者尤為有意義，因為新興市場的投資者多數由於缺乏投資經驗而表現欠佳。

14505121.label: Realisation of objectives
14505121.value: We have completed all five research objectives. The main results of the project are included in academic paper, Earnings Management and Price Informativeness, which has been presented at several conferences (e.g., CFRC and CICF) and research seminars and won the best paper in asset pricing award from the CRFC conference. We are now revising the paper and plan to submit to top journals in the field for publication. In the paper, we summarize the main findings from realisation of all five research objectives. First, we re-evaluate the price informativeness measure proposed in the literature in the Chinese A-share market and the US stock market. We find that the Chinese stock market seems to be informative with the standard measure. Second, we verify the price informativeness measure using dividend payout instead of earnings in the Chinese A-share market and the US stock market. But here we find evidence that suggests low level of price informativeness of the A-share market. Third, we propose a new measure of earnings management using non-recurring gain and loss, and examine Chinese firms' motive for earnings management, and how it impact stock prices and subsequent returns. Fourth, we propose a manipulate-to-cater mechanism, which features a corporate manager who wants to maintain high share prices caters to investors’ expectation on performance by manipulating future reported earnings. We show that such mechanism can reconcile all empirical findings. Fifth, we use the delisting rule reform in 2019 in China as an event, which effectively prevent earnings management behavior of firms, to test our predictions. The results are consistent with our conjecture.

14505121.label: Major findings and research outcome
14505121.value: How to measure the informativeness of asset prices is a key question in finance. Bai, Philippon, and Savov (2016) propose a method using current market capitalisation and future earnings to assess the predictive power of stock prices for future profits. Carpenter, Lu, and Whitelaw (2021) apply this method to China’s A-share market and find that A-share stock prices are as informative as those in the US. This finding is surprising, given the A-share market exhibits high volatility, speculative trading, governance issues, and evidence of strategic earnings management that lowers financial reporting quality. To address this puzzle, we revisit the evidence and propose an alternative explanation. We argue that the methodology used in prior studies may not fully apply to the A-share market due to its reliance on the assumption that reported earnings reflect actual profits. In the A-share market, however, corporate managers strategically manage future reported earnings to align with investor expectations and support high share prices. This earnings management mechanism implies that high market capitalisation predicts high reported earnings but not necessarily payouts. Eventually, the managed component of earnings reverses, leading to lower stock returns as investors recognize the distortion. We test these predictions and find supportive evidence. First, we replicate Carpenter et al. (2021) and confirm that A-share stock valuations predict future earnings as effectively as US stocks. However, when we replace earnings with total payouts (dividends and share repurchases), A-share stock valuations show little predictive power, unlike SP500 stocks, which predict both earnings and payouts. Next, we examine earnings management using Non-Recurring Gain and Loss (NRGL) as a proxy. Firms with high shell value (low profits/assets but maintained for reverse mergers) often report high NRGL. Stocks with high NRGL are overvalued, exhibit low future returns, and experience long-term earnings reversals as NRGL is unsustainable. Finally, we analyze the 2019-2020 delisting rule reform, which restricted NRGL use. Post-reform, NRGL usage declined, high-NRGL stock prices dropped, and the correlation between firm valuation and future earnings weakened. This suggests that reduced earnings management improved the informativeness of A-share prices. Our findings highlight the importance of considering market-specific factors like earnings management when evaluating stock price informativeness.

14505121.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14505121.value: The A-share market (combining both Shanghai and Shenzhen exchanges) is the second largest market in the world and the largest in the region in terms of market capitalisation. Understanding the price informativeness is important and valuable for market participants and regulators. Our study provides a comprehensive review of earnings quality, pricing efficiency, and long-term performance of the A-share market. Furthermore, because of Mainland China’s capital control policy, direct access to the A-share market is still limited, with the Hong Kong-Mainland connect program serving as the primary channel. Studying the recent developments of the A-share market can potentially encourage more non-domestic investors to invest into the mainland stock market, thereby promoting financial connectivity between Hong Kong and Mainland China.

14505121.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14505121.value: Understanding how well stock prices reflect a company's value is crucial in finance. Bai, Philippon, and Savov (2016) developed a method to assess this by comparing current stock prices to future earnings. Carpenter, Lu, and Whitelaw (2021) applied this to China’s A-share market and found its stock prices as predictive of future earnings as U.S. stocks. This result is surprising given the A-share market’s volatility, speculative trading, and evidence of earnings manipulation. Our study revisits this finding and suggests an alternative explanation. Prior methods assume reported earnings reflect actual profits, but in the A-share market, managers often inflate earnings to meet investor expectations. This creates the illusion of informativeness in stock prices while misrepresenting financial health. Over time, these manipulated earnings reverse, leading to lower stock returns. We confirm that A-share prices predict reported earnings but not actual payouts like dividends. Using Non-Recurring Gain and Loss (NRGL) as a measure, we find firms with inflated earnings have overvalued stocks and poor long-term returns. After the 2019-2020 reforms restricting NRGL use, earnings manipulation declined, reducing A-share price informativeness. Our findings highlight the need to account for market-specific factors when evaluating stock price efficiency.

14505621.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14505621.value: The rising consumer income often accompanies the increasing preference for high quality brand-name products. With China’s fast-growing income per capita in the past few decades, it is not surprising that domestic Chinese producers and retailers adjusted their product design and retail format to meet these changes. We label the reconfiguration of retail format, which centers on the quality and brand-name of the product, as “modern retail”. Traditionally, brand-name chain stores, a key part of modern retail, played a pivotal role in the dramatic expansion of consumer choices in the early 2000s. It boosts consumption upgrade, facilitates structural transformation and bolsters economic growth. However, chain-store based retail is costly to develop. Apple stores, for instance, have an average size of about 8,000 square feet in the US. Using 2004 and 2013 China’s economic census data, we have found that modern retail growth is negatively correlated with land price change across cities. E-Commerce can break this bottleneck. As a space-free sales technology, E-Commerce provides a cheaper and more efficient way to reach customers. Unlimited virtual retail space is particularly important for the development of modern retail. If online store were not available, Apple would probably have to maintain more offline stores and scale back its overall size. Analogously, China’s “modern retail” consumption goods would probably be much less developed without Taobao, T-Mall and JD. The counterfactual could be even worse in economies like China where land prices are severely distorted. This project, we would like to investigate the effect of E-Commerce on retail transformation and its welfare implications. To this end, we plan to do the following three exercises. (1) Using transaction-level data from Alibaba to establish some stylized facts about the rise of E-Commerce and modern retail. (2) Test the two hypotheses: (i) Modern retail grows faster in the cities with larger share of E-Commerce; (ii) E-Commerce grows faster in the cities with more expensive commercial land or more distorted commercial land price. (3) Structurally estimate a model to evaluate quantitatively welfare gains of the rise of E-Commerce. 本項課題旨在研究電子商務對零售業轉型的作用及其福利影響。我們將從一下三個方面進行研究。首先，我們將使用來自於阿裏集團的交易數據構建關於電子商務和現代零售業興起的特征事實。其次，我們將檢驗兩個基本假說：（1）在電子商務市場份額較大的城市中，現代零售業的增長速度會更快；（2）在物業地產價格或其扭曲程度較高的城市中，現代零售業的增長速度也會更快。最後，我們將構建結構模型並通過量化分析來估算電子商務的福利影響。

14505621.label: Realisation of objectives
14505621.value: The main objectives listed in the proposal have been achieved by two closely related research projects: 'The Origin of Growth in the Digital Economy' (referred to as Paper 1) and 'Logistical Efficiency and Rural E-Commerce' (Paper 2). Our studies on E-Commerce and logistical efficiency also led to three related researches in the COVID period: 'Evaluating Hong Kong Consumption Voucher Scheme' (Paper 3), 'The Economic Cost of Locking down like China: Evidence from City-to-City Truck Flows' (Paper 4), and 'On (Un)Congested Roads: A Quantitative Analysis of Infrastructure Investment Efficiency using Truck GPS Data' (Paper 5). Paper 3 and 4 generated large social impacts, receiving lots of media attentions and follow-up discussions in the policy circle (see Appendix). Paper 4 was just published by Journal of Urban Economics. The rest of the report will focus on Paper 1-2. Paper 1 presents the following sets of stylized facts (Object 1): (1) Growth in Product Varieties: The number of product varieties purchased by consumers grew at an annual rate of 9.8%. This reflects the increasing diversity of products available on e-commerce platforms. New varieties tend to be niche products, characterized by higher prices and smaller market shares, aligning with specialized consumer preferences. (2) Market Expansion for Niche Products: E-commerce platforms enable niche products to reach geographically dispersed markets, overcoming traditional barriers of scale. By connecting rural or specialized producers with urban and distant consumers, platforms provide sufficient market size for niche products to be commercially viable. (3) Online and Traditional Retail Pricing Dynamics: The price of new goods is higher than that of existing or exiting goods, indicating that new varieties often cater to higher-quality or specialized markets. Despite the higher prices of new products, the Digital Price Index (DPI), which tracks the price of existing online goods, decreased significantly (from 100 in 2013 to 75 in 2018). This trend is in contrast to the Consumer Price Index (CPI) for offline goods, which increased over the same period. The price decline in the DPI highlights the unique pricing dynamics of e-commerce, where competition and innovation keep prices low for existing products. (4) Quality and Market Share of New Varieties: New product varieties tend to have higher quality compared to exiting goods, as evidenced by their higher prices and greater market share. Over time, new varieties consistently capture a larger portion of the market than exiting varieties, illustrating their ability to meet evolving consumer demands. (5) Spatial Dynamics of Demand and Supply: Demand for new products: Buyers of new varieties first appear in high-income, urban regions in eastern China. Over time, demand spreads westward to less affluent and rural areas as incomes rise and e-commerce becomes more accessible. Supply of new products: Sellers of new varieties remain concentrated in the east, leveraging established infrastructure, economies of scale, and market networks. This geographic stability underscores the importance of urban hubs as production and distribution centers. (6) Long-Distance Trade: E-commerce significantly reduces geographical barriers, enabling long-distance trade. Products that may not find strong local demand can reach consumers in distant regions, ensuring sufficient market size for profitability. This is particularly relevant for niche products, which thrive on access to geographically dispersed demand. Paper 1 accomplishes the following empirical analysis (Object 2): (1) Data: The study uses transaction-level data from Taobao and TMall (2013-2020), covering tens of millions of online sellers. Product categories are defined at the most granular level within Alibaba's taxonomy system, allowing precise tracking of variety creation and expansion. (2) Empirical Strategy: We then employ a Bartik instrument (shift-share instrument) to establish a causal relationship between the growth of the digital economy and the creation of new product varieties. (3) Results: The regression model shows that regions with higher growth in online sales experience a greater number of new product categories. Even when excluding 'superstar cities' (Beijing, Shanghai, Shenzhen, Hangzhou, Guangzhou), the results remain consistent, proving that e-commerce impacts variety creation across diverse regions. The results highlight: (1) Online sales are positively and significantly correlated with the emergence of new product categories. (2) Excluding superstar cities reduces the effect slightly but does not eliminate it, showing that the findings are generalizable. Paper 1 also conducts the following theoretical analysis (Object 3): (1) Model: We then develop a dynamic model to capture how e-commerce promotes innovation and economic growth through the creation of new product varieties. In the model, households maximize utility by consuming a diverse set of products. The consumption of niche products depends on income levels and product rankings. Firms innovate to create new varieties. They face fixed costs but benefit from access to larger markets via e-commerce platforms. (2) Mechanism: Innovation and growth are formalized by (2a) The creation of new varieties depends on the number of researchers and R&D investments. (2b) E-commerce platforms lower fixed costs, incentivizing more research into niche products. (2c) As more niche products enter the market, they contribute to long-term economic growth. (3) Findings: The model shows that E-commerce amplifies the role of niche products in driving growth. By reducing fixed costs, platforms attract more researchers and investments into innovation. The geographic concentration of sellers in established hubs, combined with the diffusion of demand to remote regions, creates a balanced growth dynamic. Main findings in Paper 2 The study analyzes a unique data from over 20,000 villages between 2015 and 2020. Unlike the standard E-commerce data that only reveals the linkages between online sellers and buyers, this dataset is based on village E-commerce, in which village producers directly sell their products to buys. Therefore, a major advantage of the data is the establishment of trade linkages that connect producers and consumers. Using city-to-city truck flow and speed data (developed by Paper 4 and 5), we construct city-to-city logistics efficiency index, which is unlikely to be affected by the development of rural E-commerce. This minimizes endogeneity concerns. We find that even a small improvement in transportation speed had a significant impact on (1) the number of E-commerce sellers, (2) transactions per seller, and (3) revenue per seller. We explore the following mechanisms. (1) Platform Support: Alibaba has played a major role in supporting Taobao Villages through: (a) Credit programs to help sellers invest in their businesses. (b) Training programs that teach online selling skills. (c) Promotional campaigns to attract more customers to rural sellers. Villages receiving these supports benefited even more from faster logistics. (2) Digital Infrastructure: The Broadband China Program helped improve internet access in rural areas, enabling more people to participate in online commerce. Villages with better internet connectivity saw greater benefits from improved transportation. (3) Entrepreneurship: Innovative and business-savvy individuals drive e-commerce success in rural areas. Villages with higher levels of entrepreneurship were better able to take advantage of faster logistics to grow their businesses. Appendix: Impacts Paper 3 was highly appreciated by Hong Kong government. Our work was cited by the Financial Secretary and often quoted as key evidence for launching the second-round fiscal stimulus. Paper 4 was extensively reviewed by Caixin and widely cited by many reports. Our approach of using high-frequency private-sector data for nowcast is also appreciated by Hong Kong government.

14505621.label: Major findings and research outcome
14505621.value: In the paper 'The Origin of Growth in the Digital Economy', we use transaction-level data from Alibaba's platforms (2013-2020) to analyze the trajectory of growth in the digital economy. We present a set of stylized facts on (1) product variety expansion; (2) niche product viability; (3) Spatial dynamics; (4) innovation and growth. We conduct empirical analyses. The regression model shows that regions with higher growth in online sales experience a greater number of new product categories. Finally, we develop a model, which shows that E-commerce amplifies the role of niche products in driving growth. By reducing fixed costs, platforms attract more researchers and investments into innovation. The geographic concentration of sellers in established hubs, combined with the diffusion of demand to remote regions, creates a balanced growth dynamic. In addition to the rapid growth of e-commerce in the urban areas, rural e-commerce has emerged as a powerful driver of economic development in China. A key contributor to this transformation is the rise of the so-called 'Taobao Villages' - rural communities where residents actively engage in online commerce, primarily through Taobao and Tmall platforms. In the paper 'Logistical Efficiency and Rural E-Commerce', we explore how improving logistics efficiency, particularly transportation speed, has helped these villages thrive. We analyzed data from over 20,000 villages between 2015 and 2020 and found that even a small improvement in transportation speed, which is constructed to minimize endogeneity concerns, had significant impacts on various indicators of E-commerce growth. In conclusion, E-commerce platforms like Alibaba's Taobao and TMall are central to this transformation. They create ecosystems where sellers benefit from aggregated demand, and buyers enjoy a wider variety of goods at competitive prices. These platforms also enable niche products to find geographically dispersed demand, which traditional retail channels cannot reach. The digital economy, as facilitated by e-commerce platforms, represents a fundamental shift in consumption and production dynamics. Its ability to foster innovation, expand market access, and support the rise of niche products ensures inclusive and dynamic growth across regions.

We plan to improve the quantitative analysis in the future research and release the price index data to the public.

14505621.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14505621.value: This project has two main findings. First, we show the transformative impact of the digital economy on market dynamics, focusing on how e-commerce platforms drive innovation, expand product varieties, and create opportunities for long-term economic growth. Key mechanisms of growth in the digital economy include: (1) Innovation: The development of new technologies and products to meet specialized consumer demands, which drives productivity and market expansion. (2) Externalities: Lower production costs as volumes grow through economies of scale and Products or services become more valuable as more people use them through network effects. Second, we also show how improving logistics efficiency, particularly transportation speed, has helped E-commerce thrive. Using a unique dataset with linkages between producers and buyers, we find that faster transportation enables rural producers and sellers to sell more products, earn higher revenues, and attract more entrepreneurs to join the e-commerce ecosystem. Improving transportation speed has proven to be a game-changer for rural e-commerce in China. This finding also shed lights on the underlying mechanism for the rapid growth of e-commerce in the urban areas.

14505721.value: 創新、技術和最佳貿易和產業政策

14505721.label: Project Objectives
14505721.value: Theoretically, we build up the analysis in sequence : (a) First we consider the case where technology in each country and sector are taken as given. In this case, what are the optimal trade policies (import tariff and export tax)? How do optimal trade policies vary with the degree of openness? What are the optimal industrial policies? Should a country tax or subsidize its comparative advantage sectors using domestic policies? (b) We then consider the case in which there is endogenous technology accumulation through innovation activities. In this scenario, what are the optimal innovation policies in a closed economy and in an open economy? Should a country tax or subsidize innovation in its comparative advantage sectors using domestic policies? How do the optimal innovation policies vary with the degree of openness? (c) Lastly, considering both trade and innovation policies combined with endogenous technology accumulation, how do trade and innovation policies interact and shape technology and welfare? The initial theoretical analysis that we have conducted so far (explicated below) yields several important insights: the first is that in an economy, when technology is fixed, the government does not want to tax/subsidize any sectors as it is distortionary. However, they would want to employ trade policies to manipulate the terms of trade and raise welfare, assuming they face no retaliation from foreign countries. But when technology is endogenous in an open economy, the government will want to conduct both domestic (innovation and industrial) and trade policies. What do they look like? Initial findings suggest that it may want to discard the sectors in which it cannot compete at all, subsidize the sectors that are comparable to the foreign counterparts, with the possibility of surpassing them in certain sectors, and tax those in which they are good at and specialized. The full extent of results is rich and merits a thorough analysis. All of the above results take place in a baseline framework that abstracts from any kind of externality or distortions. Even in this scenario there is room for policy in a multi-sector open economy framework. This baseline model makes transparent the underlying mechanisms that drive our results and illustrate why they depart from conventional mechanisms. We then go one step further and take into account a more realistic set of industry characteristics and facets related to openness. As previous growth theories have demonstrated, optimal policies will depend on the assumptions made by each theory: imperfect competition pricing, knowledge spillovers, congestion externalities, or creative destruction. Different assumptions generate different gaps between private choice and social choice of innovation efforts. In an open economy, the answers to these questions depend on the industrial characteristics, but also additionally on comparative advantage, and domestic resource misallocations. Our research develops a framework with a multi-country, multi-sector, dynamic open economy model with endogenous technology accumulation through R&D and innovation, to yield general theoretical results. In turn, we establish the conditions under which intervention improves welfare. Lastly we conduct quantitative analysis using data on trade and policy data along with R&D and other innovation spending statistics, to prescribe the optimal domestic and trade policies. We estimate our model using firm-level, trade, R&D and policies data. This strategy helps identify the key parameters and industry characteristics by considering the interaction of trade, innovation, and existing policies.

14505721.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14505721.value: One of the most important questions in the current international arena is the competition between the two largest economies, China and the United States, about trade and cutting-edge technologies such as semiconductors, artificial intelligence, 5G networks. This competition has recently spurred nations to engage in active governmental actions or plans to support domestic firms and industries. Many are endeavouring to understand the nature of this competition and the optimal policy of nations in such an environment. So far, the debates about the optimal policy rest on an abstract level amongst policymakers and firms. Should China rely on domestic innovation policies rather than on trade for technological catch-up? Should it devise innovation incentives in certain industries over others? Should the U.S. respond to such policies? And how do these policies and the resulting U.S. response ultimately shape trade patterns, technology accumulation, and feedback onto the Chinese optimal policy? It calls for an international trade and technology framework to provide answers to these core issues at hand. Most existing frameworks in trade or in technological innovation are not suited to analyze these questions. In the trade literature, technology is typically taken to be exogenous. In theories of technological innovation, there is usually little room for trade policies to play a role. A comprehensive framework is one that integrates trade, the endogenous accumulation of technology, and a reactive foreign policy. Such framework helps us provide clear theoretical insights along with quantitative analysis. Most importantly, the dynamic implications in this framework shape the optimal policy. The project makes significant contributions theoretically and quantitatively. We derive optimal policy, which includes trade and innovation policies, in an open economy framework with endogenous technology accumulation. The technology process nests industry features, which lead to different implications on optimal policies across industries. We first consider the domestic government's problem, taking foreign government policies as given, and solve the optimal trade and domestic policies. We then consider the scenario in which there is strategic competition between governments---a case that is particularly relevant in the context of US-China dynamics. Quantitatively, we estimate our model using firm-level, trade, innovation input (including R&D and investments) and policy data. This strategy helps identify the key parameters and industry characteristics by considering the interaction of trade and various domestic policies. Lastly, we characterize the optimal domestic and trade policies. The baseline analysis can be extended with dynamic comparative advantage or domestic misallocations. 當前國際舞台上最重要的問題之一是中美兩個最大經濟體之間在貿易和半導體、人工智能、5G網絡等尖端技術方面的競爭。這種競爭最近促使各國採取積極的政府行動或計劃來支持國內公司和行業。許多人正在努力了解這種競爭的性質以及國家在這種環境下的最佳政策。到目前為止，政策制定者和企業之間關於最優政策的爭論停留在抽象層面。中國應該依靠國內創新政策而不是貿易來實現技術追趕嗎？它是否應該在某些行業製定創新激勵措施而不是其他行業？美國應該回應這些政策嗎？這些政策以及由此產生的美國反應最終如何影響貿易模式、技術積累以及對中國最優政策的反饋？它呼籲建立一個國際貿易和技術框架，為手頭的這些核心問題提供答案。 大多數現有的貿易或技術創新框架不適合分析這些問題。在貿易文獻中，技術通常被認為是外生的。在技​​術創新理論中，貿易政策通常幾乎沒有發揮作用的空間。綜合框架是將貿易、內生技術積累和被動外交政策相結合的框架。這樣的框架有助於我們提供清晰的理論見解和定量分析。最重要的是，該框架中的動態影響塑造了最佳政策。 該項目在理論和實證上都做出了重大貢獻。我們在具有內生技術積累的開放經濟框架中推導出最優政策，包括貿易和創新政策。技術過程嵌套了行業特徵，從而導致對跨行業最優政策的不同影響。我們首先考慮國內政府的問題，以國外政府的政策為前提，解決最優的貿易和國內政策。然後我們考慮政府之間存在戰略競爭的情景——這個案例在美中動態的背景下特別相關。從實證上講，我們使用公司層面、貿易、創新投入（包括研發和投資）和政策數據來估計我們的模型。通過考慮貿易和各種國內政策的相互作用來幫助確定關鍵參數和行業特徵。最後，我們描述了最優的國內和貿易政策。基線分析可以擴展考慮動態比較優勢或國內錯配。

14505921.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14505921.value: 穩定均衡的存在，逼近，和比較靜態分析

14505921.label: Project Objectives
14505921.value: 1. To enhance our understanding on dynamic economic environments. The standard equilibrium solution concept in dynamic games often requires agents be fully rational; that is, they need to be sufficiently sophisticated to understand the strategic environments. In real-life applications, an individual agent may not be able to optimize her payoff, or she simply does not have the precise knowledge of the complicated dynamic interactions. To study how agents may play in such scenarios, we shall provide an equilibrium notion to capture this kind of behavioral features. 2. To show that the equilibrium notion is applicable, useful, and sensible. Specifically, we shall show that an equilibrium exists in general stochastic games in this project. In addition, we shall also provide the comparative statics results based on the equilibrium notion to be proposed. The aim is to demonstrate that the analysis of the equilibrium notion is not vacuous, and could provide sharp predictions in applications of interest. Importantly, as our focus is on stochastic games with a large number of agents, we shall argue the behavioral features we impose are indeed mild in the sense that they tend to disappear when the number of agents increases to infinity. 3. To establish a foundation for a variety of economic applications. A key consideration in economic applications is the computability and complexity of the equilibrium. This concern is particularly relevant for games with a large number of agents, as we shall consider in this project. If the computational burden is exponential, then computing equilibrium would become infeasible in many practical examples. We shall discuss the simplicity and computational issue based on the equilibrium notion to be proposed, and argue that the curse of dimensionality can be avoided. As a result, our results can help address the equilibrium computation concern in relevant applications.

14505921.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14505921.value: 隨機博弈模型是描述動態環境的標準博弈論理論框架。針對隨機博弈的分析，核心的均衡概念是穩定馬爾科夫完美均衡。之前的文獻通過構建一系列反例揭示，這一類均衡並不一定存在。為了解決這一問題，大量文獻通過研究具有各種特殊結構的狀態轉化空間，論述了穩定均衡在隨機博弈中的存在性。這一研究方法的不足之處在於其不能處理很多重要的不滿足這些特殊結構的隨機博弈。此外，在實證研究中，計算複雜度會隨著人數增多而指數級增長。在有大量參與者的隨機博弈中，這些問題的存在限制了穩定馬爾科夫完美均衡的可適用性。 本項目旨在引入一類新的易於處理並且可適用的均衡概念，並針對這一均衡進行全面的分析。計劃研究的均衡概念的關鍵思想是假設每個參與者認定市場上有無窮競爭者，從而該參與者的個體行為對於市場總量沒有影響。這一假設在有海量參與者的博弈中廣泛滿足。建立在這一假設下，一方面，我們旨在證明在一般環境下的均衡存在性；另一方面，則將用實際的經濟學應用展示這一均衡概念可以幫助經濟學研究避免計算過於複雜的問題。從這個意義上說，本項目為各類動態場景下的經濟應用提供了初步的理論基礎。由於隨機博弈模型被包括進化生物學、計算機科學、交通問題等各類學科廣泛採用，目前的研究也將產生一定的跨學科的影響。

14505921.label: Realisation of objectives
14505921.value: The primary goal of this project was to enhance our understanding of dynamic environments by proposing a novel concept and demonstrating its applicability, usefulness, and computational feasibility. We achieved this objective by introducing the no-mixing property and analyzing its implications in dynamic games (Objective 1). This property eliminates the need for randomization in equilibrium strategies, capturing behavioral features observed in practical settings. Specifically, it reflects how agents behave when they lack the sophistication to optimize their payoffs or have incomplete knowledge of complex strategic interactions, while still preserving tractable and analytically meaningful results. These findings are documented in the paper Does Randomization Matter in Board Games?, which was supported by this project. In this paper, we rigorously analyze the role of behavioral strategies in dynamic economic environments. The proposed equilibrium concept is examined within the framework of multi-player sequential games, where we established that an equilibrium always exists. A key focus of the project was the computational feasibility of the concept. We demonstrated that the use of conceptually complicated behavioral strategies is unnecessary, which challenges the wides use of randomization in recent artificial intelligence advancements, such as AlphaGo and other reinforcement learning algorithms. These results suggest that simpler, non-randomized strategies can be equally effective, offering appealing implications for solving board games and addressing the second objective of this project (Objective 2). Overall, this project contributes to both theoretical and practical advancements in the study of stochastic games and dynamic environments. The findings substantiate the practicality and predictive power of the proposed concept and highlight its relevance to real-world applications. In particular, the results enhance our understanding of dynamic economic environments by introducing a behaviorally grounded framework, with implications for board games, artificial intelligence, and broader economic applications (Objective 3).

Importantly, as our focus is on stochastic games with a large number of agents, we shall argue the behavioral features we impose are indeed mild in the sense that they tend to disappear when the number of agents increases to infinity.

To establish a foundation for a variety of economic applications. A key consideration in economic applications is the computability and complexity of the equilibrium. This concern is particularly relevant for games with a large number of agents, as we shall consider in this project. If the computational burden is exponential, then computing equilibrium would become infeasible in many practical examples. We shall discuss the simplicity and computational issue based on the equilibrium notion to be proposed, and argue that the curse of dimensionality can be avoided. As a result, our results can help address the equilibrium computation concern in relevant applications.

14505921.label: Major findings and research outcome
14505921.value: This research contributes to the understanding of dynamic economic environments and mathematical frameworks for decision-making in complex settings. The paper, Does Randomization Matter in Board Games?, investigates the necessity of randomization in equilibrium strategies for sequential games. By introducing the no-mixing property, we demonstrate that randomization in equilibrium strategies is often unnecessary, aligning with observed behaviors in practical settings like board games. This property simplifies the analysis of subgame perfect equilibria (SPEs) by reducing the reliance on conceptually complicated behavioral strategies. In particular, we prove that the no-mixing property holds universally in two-player zero-sum games, including those with infinite action spaces, stochastic elements, and infinitely many stages. These results suggest that the wide use of mixed strategies in artificial intelligence applications, such as AlphaGo, suggesting that simpler equilibrium strategies may be unnecessary. The findings offer both theoretical insights into stochastic games and practical implications for solving board games and designing decision-making algorithms.

14505921.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14505921.value: The findings from this research open several promising avenues for further exploration. The results on the no-mixing property suggest a need to revisit the role of mixed strategies in broader classes of games, such as multi-player or non-zero-sum settings, where randomization may still be relevant. Future work could explore whether other sufficient conditions, beyond the single payoff condition, can ensure the no-mixing property in broader classes of games, potentially including games with simultaneous moves. Another is to investigate the computational implications of the no-mixing property, particularly in complex multi-player or stochastic settings where mixed strategies are traditionally thought to be necessary. Additionally, extending the results to dynamic games with incomplete or asymmetric information may provide deeper insights into strategic interactions under uncertainty.

14505921.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14505921.value: This research aims to better understand how people and systems make decisions in complex, uncertain situations, such as in games, markets, or other strategic environments. In real life, decision-makers often face challenges like incomplete information or limited ability to evaluate all possible outcomes. This project develops new mathematical tools to study such scenarios and provides insights into how individuals or groups can make optimal choices, even under these constraints. It examines strategies in games, such as board games like chess or Go. It challenges the idea that players always need to use random strategies to succeed and shows that simpler strategies can often achieve the same results. This has practical implications for artificial intelligence and game design. Overall, this research advances both theory and practice, offering tools to address real-world problems in economics, artificial intelligence, and strategic decision-making.

14506021.label: Realisation of objectives
14506021.value: 1. The project successfully constructed a novel dataset covering over 1,800 vehicle recall events in China from 2004 to 2020, matched at the model-month level to domestic car sales data for selected years (2017-2020). The recall data were collected from announcements by China's State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) and include detailed information on defect descriptions, affected models, recall dates, and manufacturer origin. One key challenge was determining the severity of the reported defects, which is critical for downstream empirical analysis. Unlike in the U.S., Chinese recall announcements rarely include standardized severity ratings, and the textual descriptions of defects vary widely in structure and terminology. To address this, the project used text analytic methods that combined rule-based information retrieval techniques and machine learning as a robustness check. This allowed us to infer whether a defect was likely to be "serious" (e.g., related to braking, steering, or fire risks) based on its language patterns. These data efforts produced a foundation for subsequent empirical and theoretical work, enabling a set of stylized facts that reveal delayed recall behavior by multinational firms, heterogeneous patterns by ownership type, and evolving responses post-regulatory reform. 2. The original aim of this project was to evaluate how Chinese consumers respond to vehicle recalls and to measure spillover effects on related but non-involved car models. However, empirical findings revealed that Chinese consumers generally show limited sensitivity to recall announcements (which is nonetheless consistent with prior study of consumer responses to vehicle recalls in the U.S.) unless three conditions are met: the recall (i) was first issued in the U.S., (ii) involved a serious safety defect, and (iii) was covered by major domestic news outlets. In most cases, recalls in China without U.S. precedents or media attention had no significant effect on consumer demand. The unforeseen results prompted a substantial and productive pivot in the research focus. Instead of continuing to analyze muted demand responses, the study shifted to investigating why multinational firms recall vehicles more slowly or selectively in China, and how information opacity influences firm behavior. Nonetheless, empirical evidence still identifies statistically significant sales drops for high-salience recalls and mild spillovers to other models in the same brand family under certain conditions. These patterns confirm the conditional nature of recall salience in China and justify the shift in research direction. This pivot led directly to a richer exploration of firm strategies and policy effects, as addressed in the structural and policy components of the study. While the original consumer-centered hypothesis was only partially supported, the revised focus significantly enhanced the project's empirical and policy value. 3. In light of the earlier empirical finding that recall announcements in China generally do not influence consumer behavior--except when linked to serious U.S. recalls and covered by official media--the focus of our research shifted accordingly. The revised goal of this step became twofold. First, through a structural demand estimation, the project aimed to assess whether the lack of firm-initiated recalls in China can be understood in relation to limited consumer responsiveness. Second, through a separate stylized theoretical model, the project aimed to evaluate the welfare consequences of improving information transparency for consumers. The structural analysis uses a standard discrete-choice framework to estimate vehicle-level demand based on monthly sales data. The estimates confirm that only a narrow subset of recalls—those with cross-national relevance and media coverage—lead to reductions in demand, highlighting the limited role of recall announcements in influencing consumer decisions in most cases. These results suggest that firms may have little to lose from delaying or avoiding recalls when consumer awareness is low. To complement the empirical work, a simple theoretical model was developed to illustrate the incentives firms face in deciding whether to initiate recalls in such an environment. The model shows how limited consumer awareness can weaken the pressure on firms to disclose problems. Counterfactual simulations based on the model indicate that even modest improvements in information availability—such as making foreign recall records more accessible—could lead to substantial consumer welfare gains. Together, the structural and theoretical components provide a coherent framework for understanding the consequences of weak information environments and the potential benefits of policy intervention. 4. This part of the project has evolved to become the new central focus of the research paper. Building on the empirical finding that consumer responses to recalls in China are limited, the study shifts to thoroughly examining how and why multinational car manufacturers are often reluctant to initiate recalls in the Chinese market, especially compared to their practices in the U.S. Using detailed recall and sales data, the research documents selective recall behavior by these firms. The working paper version emphasizes empirical detection of these patterns and explores their implications. It carefully analyzes how limited public information and weak enforcement create incentives for firms to avoid recalls, which in turn negatively affects consumer welfare. The study further discusses policy reforms aimed at increasing transparency, such as China's 2012 disclosure regulations, and demonstrates that these reforms have helped reduce recall delays and improve market outcomes. By focusing on this supply-side perspective, the paper delivers important insights for policymakers on the need to strengthen recall enforcement and expand public access to recall information. The research thus provides actionable evidence supporting regulatory efforts to enhance consumer protection and improve firm accountability in China's automotive sector. This component is fully achieved and now represents the core contribution of the project.

14506021.label: Major findings and research outcome
14506021.value: This study provides a comprehensive analysis of automobile product recalls in China over the past two decades, uncovering important insights into recall practices, consumer responses, and firm incentives in a rapidly growing but uniquely challenging regulatory environment. One key empirical finding is the limited responsiveness of Chinese consumers to recall announcements. In general, recall events in China have little to no measurable impact on consumer demand. Our analysis shows that only recalls linked to severe defects previously announced in the U.S. and extensively covered by official Chinese media result in significant demand reductions, with sales declines reaching up to 10–15% in affected models. Moreover, the likelihood that a vehicle model will be recalled in China also increases when it had a severe defect recall previously announced in the U.S., highlighting the crucial role of cross-national information and media coverage in shaping recall activity. In response to this consumer insensitivity, our study documents a striking reluctance by multinational car manufacturers to initiate recalls in China unless compelled by highly visible, cross-national incidents. Before regulatory reforms in 2012, foreign firms routinely delayed or limited recalls in China compared to their U.S. practices, exploiting weaker enforcement and lower consumer pressure. The findings underscore how gaps in information transparency and oversight create incentives for firms to withhold safety actions, raising serious concerns about consumer protection. After the 2012 reforms, recall rates for severe defects improved by roughly 30%, indicating regulatory progress. To better understand the underlying mechanisms, we combine a structural demand estimation with a stylized theoretical model. The demand model confirms that only salient recall events depress sales, consistent with limited consumer attention. The theoretical framework illustrates how this weak consumer responsiveness reduces firms' incentives to recall defect vehicles voluntarily. Our welfare analysis shows that improved information disclosure could increase consumer welfare by an estimated 4.5% (a conservative estimate) by enabling better-informed purchasing decisions. Finally, we provide detailed empirical evidence that China's 2012 recall policy reforms have had measurable effects in increasing the frequency of recalls, especially for severe defects. These reforms help close the information gap and create stronger incentives for multinational firms to comply with recall requirements. Our findings emphasize the critical role of transparent information and effective regulation in ensuring product safety and protecting consumers in emerging markets.

14506021.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14506021.value: Building on the current findings, future research can further explore the dynamic interactions between firms and regulators in China's evolving recall system. Incorporating richer firm-level data and developing models that capture dynamic decision-making would deepen understanding of how recall incentives adjust over time under changing regulatory pressures. Additionally, extending the analysis to include consumer heterogeneity--such as differences in awareness and trust across regions and income groups--can inform more targeted policy designs. On the policy front, future work should simulate the impact of alternative disclosure regulations, enforcement intensities, and information campaigns to identify cost-effective measures that enhance consumer welfare. We aim to continue to refine the empirical framework with new data sources, expanding theoretical models to incorporate dynamic strategic considerations, and collaborating with policymakers to translate research insights into practical regulatory reforms that enhance safety and market efficiency in China's auto industry.

14506021.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14506021.value: This research examines how automobile safety recalls function in China and why they have often been less effective in influencing consumer behavior. In many countries, such as the U.S., vehicle recalls typically lead to reduced sales for affected models, as consumers become aware of safety concerns. However, our study finds that in China, recalls generally do not impact buyers unless the defects have already been publicly reported in the U.S. and covered by official media. We identify that many multinational car manufacturers have avoided recalls in China, partly because consumer responses to recall information have been limited and regulatory enforcement was comparatively weak, especially before 2012. Since regulatory reforms in 2012, recall transparency and enforcement have improved, leading to better outcomes. Our findings suggest that providing consumers with more complete and accessible information--particularly about serious defects identified abroad--could encourage safer purchasing decisions and motivate firms to act more responsibly. Overall, this research sheds light on the challenges facing China's vehicle recall system and offers practical policy recommendations to enhance consumer protection and automotive safety.

14506221.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14506221.value: Global awareness of environmental and social sustainability has given financial incentives, in forms of government support and consumer preference, for business organizations to set and achieve sustainability goals. In recent years, a growing number of companies around the world have utilized a new supply chain financing instrument known as sustainability-linked loan (SLL) to meet their financing needs while advancing the companies’ environmental and social responsibility objectives. Different from conventional loan with a simple interest-rate-only contract, interest rates in an SLL are typically linked to preset sustainability targets such as reduced carbon emissions or diversification in a company’s governance structure, etc. Despite its great success in the past years since its interception in 2017 and even greater potential in future years, SLL is a relatively new financial instrument. In this proposed research, we will study the effectiveness of SLL in the context of supply chain financing and supply chain sustainability. We will develop an analytical framework with a lender (a bank or a supply chain buyer) who offers an SLL contract to a borrower (a supplier), both of whom have financial incentives to improve the supplier’s sustainability performance. Through in-depth analysis of the supplier’s optimal borrowing and sustainability investment decisions under an SLL, and the lender’s optimal design of SLL contract structure, we aim to provide managerial insights on the effectiveness of SLL as a supply chain financing instrument to promote supply chain sustainability. Our proposed study will contribute to the supply chain management literature significantly. One of the novel features in our research project is to study the impacts of a new financial instrument, the SLL, on supply chain sustainability performance. To our knowledge, this proposed project is among the first to consider SLL in supply chain management. By studying a financing instrument that incorporates financial incentives for improved sustainability performance directly into its financing covenant, our research is expected to make new and significant contributions to both supply chain financing and supply chain sustainability literature. Our proposed research also has the potential to help business organizations to better understand how to address some of the challenges they might face when deploying SLL in a supply chain to achieve their financial and sustainability objectives. 近年來，越來越多的世界各地的公司使用了一種新的被稱為可持續發展表現掛鈎貸款 (SLL) 的供應鏈融資工具以滿足他們的融資需求，同時推進公司的環境和社會責任目標。不同於從具有簡單的僅利率合同的傳統貸款，SLL 的利率通常與預設的可持續性目標相關，例如減少碳排放或公司治理結構的多元化等。SLL 是一種相對較新的金融工具。自 2017 年以來的過去幾年中，SLL取得了成功，並且在未來幾年將具有更大的潛力。在這項擬議的研究中，我們將研究 SLL 在供應鏈融資和供應鏈可持續性背景下的有效性。我們將構建一個分析框架來研究 SLL 合同的借方的借款和可持續性投資決策，以及貸方的SLL 合同結構的優化設計。本研究旨在提供有關SLL作為供應鏈融資工具促進供應鏈可持續性的有效性。

14600021.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14600021.value: The ability to accurately read others’ minds is crucial for building interpersonal relationships and effective communication. Research shows that even adults face challenges in empathic accuracy—the ability to read the specific moment-to-moment mental states of others in everyday interactions. While young children possess some forms of empathic understanding, the extent of their empathic accuracy is uncharted. This proposed research will fill a gap in the study of empathic accuracy by focusing on childhood. Its contributions will include a communication quality that may be used in contexts such as educational and clinical settings in which objectively accurate mind reading is crucial. It will also pave the way for the development of interventions to support desirable developmental outcomes associated with empathic accuracy. Given that adults often overestimate their empathic abilities, it is important to investigate the extent to which children and their carers have accurate insights into children’s ability to understand others. Identifying fallacies about empathic accuracy will facilitate the development of interventions to improve this ability. In the proposed research, a new standard stimulus paradigm will be used to assess the ability of 380 children aged 5–6 and 9–10 years to infer the mental states of adults and children engaging in dynamic parent–child interactions. Eight empathic accuracy stimulus videos of parent–child dyads naturally engaging in common daily activities will be created. The videotaped parent and child targets will record their mental states at specific moments. These mental states will then be compared with participants’ inferences to provide an objective and ecologically valid score of mind-reading accuracy. Additionally, both child participants’ self-estimated performance and parents’ estimates of their child’s performance and the average performance of boys and girls will be assessed. These estimates will be compared with actual performance data. The study will provide pioneering data to address the following questions: What is the level of children’s empathic accuracy toward children and adults in dynamic parent–child interactions? Does the empathic accuracy of boys and girls differ, and does this ability change during middle childhood? How do children and adults perceive the empathic accuracy of children? If perceptions are inaccurate, are they overestimated, underestimated, or random? Finally, do perceptions reflect gendered expectations, and if so, are these expectations supported by performance data? 準確讀懂他人思想的能力對於建立人際關係和有效溝通至關重要。研究表明，即使是成年人也不是有很高的移情準確性——在日常互動中解讀他人特定時刻心理狀態的能力。雖然幼兒擁有某些形式的移情理解，但他們移情的準確性的程度是未知的。這項研究將通過關注童年來填補移情準確性研究的空白。它的貢獻將包括發展一套溝通質量的評估工具，可用於教育和臨床等需求客觀準確的讀心術的環境中。它還將幫助發展干預措施，以支持移情準確性會帶來的良性發展成果。鑑於成年人經常高估他們的共情能力，調查兒童及其照顧者對兒童理解他人的能力的準確洞察程度很重要。識別關於移情準確性的謬誤將促進干預措施的發展，以提高這種能力。 此研究將使用一種新的標準刺激範式來評估 380 名 5-6 歲和 9-10 歲兒童推斷參與動態親子互動的成人和兒童心理狀態的能力。研究將創建八個參與日常活動的親子共情視頻。被錄像的父母和孩子目標人物會記錄他們在特定時刻的心理狀態。這些心理狀態將會與參與者的推論進行比較，以提供客觀和生態有效的讀心準確性評分。此外，研究會收集兒童參與者的自我表現評估、父母對孩子表現的評估、以及父母對男孩和女孩的平均表現的評估。這些估計值將與實際表現數據進行比較。此研究將為解決以下問題提供開創性數據：在動態的親子互動中，兒童對兒童和成人的移情準確度如何？男孩和女孩的移情準確度是否不同？這種能力在童年中期是否會發生變化？兒童和成人如何看待兒童的移情準確性？如果評估的觀感不准確，它們是高估、低估還是隨機的？最後，觀感是否反映了性別期望，如果是，這些期望是否與實際表現數據一致？

14600921.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14600921.value: 誰家土地？中華帝國晚期城市內的房屋擁有、買賣和出租--以清朝廣州府為例

14600921.label: Project Objectives
14600921.value: • Policies on land and houses in the Qing dynasty: In my view, there were broadly three major types of land in Guangzhou prefecture during the Qing dynasty: (1) wasteland: land unregistered by anyone; (2) government land: land registered by the government; and (3) civilian land: land registered by individuals. This project will investigate whether the Qing government imposed any restrictions on the building and transfer of houses on these three different types of land. In my sample study of the Kowloon Walled City I found that Qing officials decided where houses could be built within the government city. The project will gather more empirical data in order to explore housing policy more fully. • The source(s) of laws and customs concerning land ownership and housing construction: The Great Qing Code and customary land law governed who could own and occupy land and houses. This project will attempt to discover what happened when law and custom were in conflict. I assume that Qing officials adjusted the Code in lawsuit disputes over land and houses by accepting some customary practices, but only as long as they did not violate the Code. Qing officials, no matter what level they occupied in the bureaucracy, were not allowed to deviate from the Great Qing Code in their legal judgments. If any official had a good reason to side-step the Code, he needed to petition the Emperor for an endorsement. This is my assumption, and this project will look for actual cases to support it. • Restrictions on the categories of persons (particularly women) who could acquire land: Qing China was a lineage society, with succession through the male. In many villages dominated by lineages, the villagers reserved land for fields or houses for their male lines only. On the other hand, the Qing Code allowed every person, no matter how young or what gender, to build a house on the land that person owned. There was no law that only males could own land or houses. Women did own land, usually buying it with money from their dowries. These dowries often comprised jewels and cash, but women could sell the jewels and use the cash to make investments in land and become landlords. In most families married women kept their own savings and spent them at their discretion. Although after they died, such properties, including cash and assets, might fall into the hands of their sons or adoptive sons, which meant their husband’s families, the fact remains that women owned land and houses and this was allowed by the state. The Qing state did give women a low priority in the law of succession, but never stipulated that they could not own land and houses in villages. In the literature so far we have too few examples of how Chinese women controlled and transferred their land and house properties. This project will try to fill in this academic gap. • Role of community leaders in acquiring land or houses: The Qing government never allowed any civilian, including ancestral and communal trust members, to usurp its authority; but in reality were individuals, even landlords, required to get their community leader’s approval before they built houses on their land? This project will investigate the role, if any, played by community leaders regarding housing construction. I shall study lawsuit cases and conduct oral history interviews to explore what happened to people if they did not follow a community leader’s instructions. • House ownership: In my preliminary research there were two major types of houses in Guangzhou prefecture – residences and shop-houses – and either could be owned by more than one person. The real owner of a house, no matter whether he/she also owned the land where the house was built, might rent out his/her house to another person under a perpetual lease. This divided ownership of houses created difficulties when the Republican Guangzhou government attempted to re-develop Guangzhou city. Using textual analysis and oral history, this project will investigate how these houses were managed in the Qing.
rows: • Policies on land and houses in the Qing dynasty: In my view, there were broadly three major types of land in Guangzhou prefecture during the Qing dynasty: (1) wasteland: land unregistered by anyone; (2) government land: land registered by the government; and (3) civilian land: land registered by individuals. This project will investigate whether the Qing government imposed any restrictions on the building and transfer of houses on these three different types of land. In my sample study of the Kowloon Walled City I found that Qing officials decided where houses could be built within the government city. The project will gather more empirical data in order to explore housing policy more fully.

• The source(s) of laws and customs concerning land ownership and housing construction: The Great Qing Code and customary land law governed who could own and occupy land and houses. This project will attempt to discover what happened when law and custom were in conflict. I assume that Qing officials adjusted the Code in lawsuit disputes over land and houses by accepting some customary practices, but only as long as they did not violate the Code. Qing officials, no matter what level they occupied in the bureaucracy, were not allowed to deviate from the Great Qing Code in their legal judgments. If any official had a good reason to side-step the Code, he needed to petition the Emperor for an endorsement. This is my assumption, and this project will look for actual cases to support it.

• Restrictions on the categories of persons (particularly women) who could acquire land: Qing China was a lineage society, with succession through the male. In many villages dominated by lineages, the villagers reserved land for fields or houses for their male lines only. On the other hand, the Qing Code allowed every person, no matter how young or what gender, to build a house on the land that person owned. There was no law that only males could own land or houses. Women did own land, usually buying it with money from their dowries. These dowries often comprised jewels and cash, but women could sell the jewels and use the cash to make investments in land and become landlords. In most families married women kept their own savings and spent them at their discretion. Although after they died, such properties, including cash and assets, might fall into the hands of their sons or adoptive sons, which meant their husband’s families, the fact remains that women owned land and houses and this was allowed by the state. The Qing state did give women a low priority in the law of succession, but never stipulated that they could not own land and houses in villages. In the literature so far we have too few examples of how Chinese women controlled and transferred their land and house properties. This project will try to fill in this academic gap.

• Role of community leaders in acquiring land or houses: The Qing government never allowed any civilian, including ancestral and communal trust members, to usurp its authority; but in reality were individuals, even landlords, required to get their community leader’s approval before they built houses on their land? This project will investigate the role, if any, played by community leaders regarding housing construction. I shall study lawsuit cases and conduct oral history interviews to explore what happened to people if they did not follow a community leader’s instructions.

The real owner of a house, no matter whether he/she also owned the land where the house was built, might rent out his/her house to another person under a perpetual lease. This divided ownership of houses created difficulties when the Republican Guangzhou government attempted to re-develop Guangzhou city. Using textual analysis and oral history, this project will investigate how these houses were managed in the Qing.
