14601021.label: Project Objectives
14601021.value: This proposed work aims to examine the effects of a multicomponent, integrative lifestyle intervention comprising lifestyle elements with sound evidentiary support (exercise, diet, sleep, and stress management) in the context of depression in a Chinese adult population. Depression is a debilitating mental health condition that is primarily characterized by a persistently depressed mood and a loss of interest or pleasure in usual activities [1]. Despite effective treatments for depression, there is still an unmet need for mental health treatment [2]. Previous reviews have suggested that the increased prevalence of depression may be influenced partly by changes in lifestyle related to modernity [3]. However, the therapeutic approach adopted by modern clinicians places more emphasis on biomedical markers. Looking beyond these immediate causes (e.g., biomedical markers), there is a hierarchy of determinants from all levels of causality (i.e., proximal, medial, and distal) in diseases of modernity [4]. Unequivocally, first-line treatments such as pharmacological agents have important clinical value. However, they do not always yield the complete remission of symptoms. For this reason, clinicians should not consider them as a sole and complete solution to all diseases, especially those with a lifestyle etiology [5]. Modernization, in tandem with technological advancements, has remarkable public health implications in different lifestyle behavior domains. Major shifts in lifestyle behaviors include physical inactivity, unhealthy eating patterns, and irregular sleep-wake patterns. For example, the increased time constraints and urge to increase productivity and efficiency have increased the consumption of ready-to-eat and pre-packaged foods and decreased the duration and quality of sleep. Technological advancements have promoted physical inactivity and sedentary behaviors [6,7]. Recently, a cross-sectional and longitudinal analysis of the UK Biobank with 84,860 participants suggested that several lifestyle factors are associated with depression, including physical activity, dietary pattern, and sleep quality [8]. Likewise, a local survey study of 271 respondents demonstrated that a poor lifestyle, such as a low level of physical activity, unhealthy diet, and poor sleep, is predictive of a higher prevalence of depression, anxiety, and stress [9]. Previous evidence demonstrated that the pathogenesis and progression of depression may depend on the multiplicative interactions between different lifestyle determinants related to depression [4]. Therefore, a modern perspective calls for an integrated approach by considering all of the modifiable underlying risk factors instead of placing narrow attention on single risk factors to manage depression [10]. Lifestyle medicine (LM) is the adoption of an evidence-based lifestyle therapeutic approach that involves combinations of nutrition, exercise, sleep, and stress management as therapeutic modalities [11]. It is ideally applied as a comprehensive, multifaceted approach that considers several levels of causality of a given disease and focuses on both prevention and therapeutic management [4]. It empowers individuals with self-management skills to make healthy lifestyle changes that address the underlying causes of physical and mental health problems. There are several credible reasons for advocating a multicomponent lifestyle intervention alongside conventional treatment approaches. First, promoting positive mental health through lifestyle changes has been proven effective in both clinical and normal populations [10]. Second, lifestyle changes provide an ideal modality to tackle the perceived stigma surrounding conventional treatments, as suggested by previous studies demonstrating that the acceptability of lifestyle changes is high and that these are sometimes preferred due to their low cost and fewer side effects when compared with psychotherapy and pharmacotherapy [12]. Third, in addition to their potentially safe and cost-effective nature, lifestyle changes provide secondary health benefits, such as improvements in physical health, psychological well-being, quality of life, and cognitive function [10,13]. Research integrating multiple evidence-based lifestyle elements for the treatment of depression is limited, and relevant studies in the Chinese adult population are scarce or non-existent. The proposed study will be the first large-scale randomized controlled trial (RCT) to provide rigorous scientific evidence on the effectiveness of a group-based, multicomponent lifestyle intervention for depression. If proven effective, LM can be considered as an alternative or adjunctive treatment option to conventional therapies and an entry-level community intervention for wider dissemination, like the Act-Belong-Commit campaign, which provides a lifestyle framework for promoting mental health at the population level [12]. Furthermore, a process evaluation will be conducted to identify culture-specific facilitators of and barriers to integrated lifestyle intervention. To pave the way for future studies, a pilot case-control study will be nested in the proposed trial to elucidate the potential role of the gut microbiome in depression and how the modern lifestyle is associated with the microbiome. This proposed high-quality, large-scale RCT aims (1) to determine the effects of group-based multicomponent LM intervention, (2) to evaluate the effects of digital health technologies on LM adherence; (2) to identify the processes that facilitate or hinder the implementation of LM; and (3) to collect pilot evidence on the potential role of the gut microbiome in depression.

14601021.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14601021.value: Depression is a global public health issue associated with substantial socio-economic costs. An existing hypothesis suggests that modernization has contributed to the increasing prevalence of depression over the last few decades, and that modifying lifestyle elements may improve depressive symptoms and physical and mental wellbeing in depressed individuals. However, adherence to recommended lifestyle changes remains challenging. In this proposed randomized controlled trial with an embedded process evaluation, the aims are to (1) examine the effects of a group-based multicomponent lifestyle medicine (LM) intervention with/without the support of digital health technologies to promote adherence (LM-S/LM alone) relative to care-as-usual (CAU) for depression; (2) to identify processes that facilitate or hinder the implementation of LM and contribute to the outcomes; and (3) to collect pilot evidence on the potential role of the gut microbiome in depression using a nested pilot study. The proposal comprises two studies. In Study I, 141 eligible participants will be randomly assigned to receive LM-S, LM alone, and CAU in a 1:1:1 allocation ratio. The LM-S and LM alone groups will receive a 6-week, group-based, multicomponent lifestyle intervention (i.e., exercise, diet, stress, and sleep management). Digital health technologies (i.e., a self-tracking app and wearables) will be used in the LM-S group to promote adherence. Study II will be a nested pilot case-control study exploring the potential role of the gut microbiome in depression and its associations with lifestyle choices. Thirty depressed individuals will be selected from Study I, and 30 healthy individuals will be recruited from the community at baseline. The major assessments will be at baseline (Week 0), 1 week (Week 7), and 3 months post-intervention (Week 18). The primary outcome measure will be the Patient Health Questionnaire-9 to evaluate depression severity. Secondary outcomes will include both subjective measures (i.e., psychological health symptoms, sleep quality, lifestyle profile, and quality of life) and objective measures (i.e., daily physical and sleep activities). Stool samples for gut microbiome analyses will be collected in Study II. The process evaluation will cover processes related to recruitment, treatment delivery, and barriers to implementation. The treatment effects will be compared using linear mixed-effects models, and the gut microbiome will be analyzed using non-parametric tests. This proposed study will be the first large-scale randomized controlled trial to provide rigorous scientific evidence about the effectiveness of group-based, multicomponent lifestyle intervention for depression. If proven effective, the intervention will be a potentially safe and low-cost option for augmenting depression management. 抑鬱症是一個全球公共衛生問題，且與龐大的社會經濟成本有關。在過去數十年，現代化的生活模式被假定為促成抑鬱症患病率上升的因素之一。因此，改變不良的生活方式有可能是一個有效的介入治療，以改善抑鬱症患者的抑鬱症狀和身心健康。然而，如何使參加者持續依從健康生活方式仍是一個挑戰。 這項包含治療過程評估的隨機對照實驗，旨在(1)透過與恆常對照組的比較，探討生活方式介入治療小組在配合/不配合醫療健康科技的情況下，對於提高依從性以及抑鬱症的治療效果；(2) 識別促進或阻礙實施生活方式介入治療的過程； (3) 進行病例對照研究，以收集腸道微生物群對於抑鬱症潛在作用的先導證據。 是項計劃書包含兩個研究。在研究一，141名符合資格的參加者將會以1:1:1 的比例隨機分配到有/不配合醫療健康科技的生活方式介入治療小組（LM-S/LM）和恆常對照組 （CAU）。LM-S 和 LM小組將會接受為期六週的多元生活方式介入治療（即運動、飲食、壓力和睡眠管理）。此外， LM-S小組將會使用醫療健康科技（即自我追蹤手提電話應用程式和腕動計）來促進依從性。研究二將會進行病例對照研究，以探討腸道微生物群對於抑鬱症的潛在作用以及其與生活方式的關聯。其中，30名患有抑鬱症的參加者將會從研究一中選出，而30名健康人士則會在小組開始前從社區招募。 主要評估將會在小組開始前（第零週）、六週小組完結後（第七週）和小組完成後十二週追蹤期（第十八週）進行。主要的療效指標是以病人健康問卷來量度。而次要的療效指標則包括主觀測量部分（即心理健康症狀、睡眠質素、生活方式和生活質量）和客觀測量部分（即日常和睡眠活動）。另外，用於腸道微生物組分析的糞便樣本將在研究二中收集。而過程評估將涵蓋與招募、治療傳達和阻礙實施生活方式介入治療的過程。小組的治療效果將會以線性混合效應模型來比較，而腸道微生物群對於抑鬱症的潛在作用將以無母數統計進行分析。 這項研究以嚴謹科學證據探討生活方式介入治療小組對於處理抑鬱症的效果，是該研究領域中第一個大規模的隨機對照實驗。若研究效果理想，生活方式介入治療小組將有潛力成為處理抑鬱症的一個既安全且低成本的選擇。

14601421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14601421.value: 在人類世時代，我們目睹了雨林、冰川等地理景觀的消逝，以及大量野生動植物的滅絕。然而在數碼技術的幫助下，這些消失中的風景與動植物，連同奇異世界、奇幻生物和非人類角色，越來越多地出現在大大小小的屏幕上。在這波全球性的奇觀浪潮中，奇幻類影視作品於過去的二十年收穫了大量人氣，在中國內地和香港形成了極具特色的產業類型。本研究將分析中國當代電影、電視和動畫中與日俱增的非人類角色與他們生活的環境，並將這些角色與空間置於人類世的審美視野之中，藉此為奇幻研究提供新的解讀。 首先，該研究將擴展人類世與電影的研究，通過華語奇幻影視中人類以外的維度來反觀人類與人文的意義。過去華語生態電影研究往往側重真實環境佈景的紀錄片和寫實主義的劇情片，而本研究則將數碼虛擬場景的分析引入這一研究圖景。其次，該研究關注當代華語奇幻作品中的超自然現象與非人類角色，與歐美語境下的奇幻研究形成補充和對照。人類世的概念指由西方式現代化導致的地球分期，而本研究在中國語境中探索奇幻想像，這將豐富我們對人類世的理解。同時，本研究將奇幻影視置於華語電影具體的歷史脈絡之中。一個多世紀以來，以現代化、科學進步為名對銀幕上的超自然現象的審查從未休止。第三，數位技術不僅僅是一種技術工具，本研究將探討它如何影響大眾對人類世環境的想象，以及這一技術如何形塑人類世背景下數位視覺效果及動畫作品的文化意義。 人類世作為一種媒介化的建構，其美學原則是由數碼電影技術塑造的。本研究將利用影視產業研究數據和資料，通過對影視媒體製作人、視覺效果設計師、動畫藝術家的採訪，結合影視作品的文本分析，探討人類世的媒體理論框架。

14601421.label: Realisation of objectives
14601421.value: The understanding of the digital non-human in Chinese fantasy media has primarily been presented in two peer-reviewed journal articles. The objectives are mainly realized through the following three aspects: journal articles, conference presentations, and a bilingual website. First, PI published “Platformized Seriality: Chinese Time Travel Fantasy from Prime-time Television to Online Streaming” (Tan, 2022) in Global Storytelling: Journal of Digital and Moving Images, published by Michigan Publishing. In this article, PI examines time-travel serials—now immensely popular in the context of China’s growing video-streaming industry, convergence culture, and the financial boom of digital platforms. Analyzing the trope of the female time traveler in historical romance, this essay examines how chuanyue, or the Chinese time-travel genre, subtly unsettles contemporary gender-related anxiety and the dominant discourse on development and progress, partly explaining the pleasure it generates. The genre of chuanyue benefited from the rise of platform infrastructure designs such as bullet screens and pay-on-demand-in-advance services that direct new forms of audience engagement and new practices of binge-watching. Focusing on the fantasy genre and the mutability of the time traveler’s gender, sexuality, and class, I explore how the trope of traveling backward marks a reconfiguration of conceptions of time, space, and history, thus opening a space to negotiate with the neoliberal narratives of linear and progressivist temporality. This study also raises the idea of “platformized seriality” to address the changing formation of narrative forms in the era of digital streaming. This article addresses Objectives 1 and 2, which is to analyze the proliferating fantastical representations in contemporary Chinese films, television, and animations. Second, addressing Objectives 1, 2, and primarily 3 and 4, PI published “Materializing the Digital Landscape: The Cinema-ecology Complex and Chinese fantasy media” in the International Journal of Asian Studies by Cambridge University Press (Tan, 2023). This article expands on the important scholarship of “materialist” media studies as well as existing ecocinema scholarship by stressing the materiality of digital landscapes in contemporary Chinese fantasy (or qihuan and xuanhuan) film and television works that have gained significant popularity in China and Hong Kong. Specifically, this article examines the animist landscape in film and television adaptations of Eternal Love, a fantasy romance television serial that loosely draws on Daoist mythology. Focusing on the material aspects of digital landscapes of Chinese fantasy cinema, the article develops the notion of the “cinema–ecology complex” to address the materiality of digital landscapes, the cinematic footprint of digitally enhanced landscapes through location shooting and the consumption of landscapes as scenic spots, including daka practices, in film studio cities and related film-induced tourism. I examine the cinema–ecology complex from three angles: firstly, as sporadic cinematic imprints on ecology through location shooting, particularly in remote areas with minimal human presence; secondly, in terms of the cinematic portrayal of landscapes that perpetuates them on screen; and thirdly, through the emergence of the spectator-tourist engaging emotionally with landscapes facilitated by film studio cities and associated film-induced tourism. Thus, the cinema–ecology complex elucidates the ecological impact of the film production process and its tourist endeavors. Ultimately, this article calls for a textual–infrastructural approach in cinema and media studies, which tends to reorient to the infrastructural aspects of media production, distribution, and consumption (Please see 6.1 for details). Third, PI also presented and disseminated the findings in two international conferences (responding to Objective 5), including the Society for Cinema and Media Studies Conference in Denver, the leading conference in the field of cinema and media studies in 2023, as well as Visible Evidence conference, a leading conference in documentary studies in the same year (please see Part C for details). Through attending international conferences, PI disseminates the research findings to an international scholarly community. Fourth, addressing Objectives 1, 2, and 4, and primarily 6, a bilingual (Chinese and English) website for categorizing various kinds of non-human representation in Chinese fantasy media is now available at https://nonhumanchinesemedia.wordpress.com. This website provides detailed information about four major non-human characters in Chinese fantasy films and media and is divided into four sections according to these non-humans: white snake, ghost, fox, and goeng si. Each section starts by introducing these non-human characters’ varied roles in traditional Chinese culture, especially literature and opera, which constitutes a historical background for introducing how early Chinese-language cinema and contemporary film reshaped the non-human characters by adapting traditional literature and opera differently. This website also highlights the important film works, filmmakers, and production companies that are crucial to present non-human characters on screen. At the end of each section, a list of representative films and a selected bibliography are laid out for reference. The website provides rich materials, references, and historical background for different kinds of non-humans in Chinese fantasy media. It not only includes fiction-films, but also television and online series, as well as animation. The website is structured in four major areas. First, the first section introduces “White Snake in Chinese Fantasy Film and Media”. It starts with explaining how the stories of white snakes evolved in ancient China. In “Early Film Adaptations of White Snake Legend”, the influence of Japanese filmmakers is emphasized to showcase the transnational context. The part “Green Snake in White Snake Films” intends to point out Hong Kong writer Lilian Lee and filmmaker Tsui Hark’s influential breakthrough in making the green snake more significant in the white snake films. Second, “Ghosts in Chinese Fantasy Film and Media” highlights ghosts’ highly allegorical roles in Chinese-language films. This section introduces a less-mentioned ghost filmmaker, Yao Feng-pan of Taiwan to show his ambitions in making ghost films as social critique. Besides, by setting A Chinese Ghost Story (1987) as an example, this section points out the ghost’s potential for transgressing social norms. Finally, the ghost’s position as a subject of censorship is introduced in outlining their (dis)appearances in contemporary mainland Chinese films. Third, “Fox in Chinese Fantasy Film and Media” begins with introducing Fox’s varied images in Chinese culture. They can be depicted as loyal friends of humans while they can also be appointed as the villains of literature and films. “Early Chinese-language Cinema Related to Fox” introduces how the foxes are represented in films with different Chinese topolects. “Fox in Contemporary Chinese-language Media” shows fox’s appearance in different media, such as film, television, animation, and digital media platforms. The fourth section gives insights into one of the most prominent generic innovations brought by Hong Kong filmmakers: “Hong Kong Goeng Si Film”. Two perspectives of goeng si film are emphasized. First, the relationship between the goeng si films and Hong Kong people’s anxiety about the 1997 handover. The second perspective is on goeng si films as transcultural products, especially how goeng si films both appropriate religious rituals from Xiangxi and learn from Western Vampire films. In summary, through the aforementioned journal articles, international conference presentations, as well as the bilingual website, the objectives of the project have been fully achieved.

14601421.label: Major findings and research outcome
14601421.value: The significant findings of this GRF project are condensed in the cited journal articles. Most importantly, I introduce the concept of the cinema–ecology complex to comprehend the digital non-human within the Anthropocene epoch. This concept, rooted in the materialist turn and environmental media studies, illuminates cinema’s often overlooked interdependence with, exploitation of, and imaginative engagement with ecology. Particularly, I stress the material aspects of cinematic art to explore the cinema–ecology complex, revealing how cinematic media and ecology, notably natural landscapes, intertwine across various dimensions. The landscape emerges as a pivotal non-human element within this complex, forming a textual-infrastructure system. I examine the cinema–ecology complex from three angles: firstly, as sporadic cinematic imprints on ecology through location shooting, particularly in remote areas with minimal human presence; secondly, in terms of the cinematic portrayal of landscapes that perpetuates them on screen; and thirdly, through the emergence of the spectator-tourist engaging emotionally with landscapes facilitated by film studio cities and associated film-induced tourism. Thus, the cinema–ecology complex elucidates the ecological impact of the film production process and its tourist endeavors. Simultaneously, the research introduces the concept of platformized seriality, denoting the amalgamation of online platform infrastructure design, content regulation, generic conventions, and experimental approaches for representing the fantastic in the digital age. Methodologically, an innovative textual–infrastructural approach to media studies is developed to engage with the examination of the non-human at both textual and infrastructural levels. This approach intersects the "materialist turn" in contemporary cinema and media studies, influenced by post-humanism, new materialism, object-oriented ontologies, and speculative realism, with the exploration of material elements within texts, including objects, non-human life forms, environments, and settings on screen (including ecocinema), as well as animals and non-humans in film and media. By integrating the cinema–ecology complex and examining the infrastructures supporting audiovisual entertainment production and consumption, such as green screens, location shooting, and film studio cities, this article aims to bridge the gap between the considerable scholarly focus on screened entertainment and the limited attention devoted to understanding infrastructural dynamics in humanistic media studies (For details, see Part C.) Additionally, the website provides empirical details of the history of different categories of non-human on screen in the Chinese context.

14601421.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14601421.value: My conceptualization of non-human Chinese fantasy media engages in dialogue with various theories in ecocriticism, including new materialism and media infrastructure studies. As demonstrated with the concept of the cinema-ecology complex, I strive to combine textual analysis with a materialist reading. Another area of study is the imagination of the underwater. In recent decades, the Asia Pacific region has seen an increase in underwater scenes in film and video works, thanks to advancements in underwater cinematography and sound recording. This trend connects to earlier imaginings of the ocean in mythology and folklore, as well as the recent development of aquariums and underwater tourism in Asia. While science fiction and fantasy media depict both fantastical and dystopian visions of the underwater world, other films and eco-documentaries explore the ocean's significance for coastal communities, as well as the biodiversity and challenges of marine ecosystems. Expanding on the focus of cinema and environmental humanities, I have already submitted another GRF grant (result pending) to delve into submerged aesthetics in light of recent scholarship in critical ocean studies.

14601421.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14601421.value: The project delves into the portrayal of digital non-humans in Chinese fantasy media within the context of the Anthropocene era. Beyond mere exploration, this endeavor aims to elevate public consciousness and deepen understanding of both non-human entities and environmental concerns. The insights and data gleaned from this research will prove invaluable across diverse academic domains, including environmental humanities, film and media studies, and China studies. Moreover, the outcomes of this investigation, particularly those disseminated through a bilingual website dedicated to the theme of non-human entities in Chinese cinema, hold significant promise for scholars, environmental advocates, and NGO practitioners not only within China but also in broader international spheres. Additionally, these findings are poised to enrich the curricula of undergraduate and postgraduate programs in environmental humanities, film and media studies, and China studies. By illuminating the interplay between cinema and the environment, this study, along with its accompanying website, offers a fresh perspective on contemporary China, serving as invaluable educational resources for understanding media in the ear of the Anthropocene.

14601921.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14601921.value: It is well known that dyslexia runs in families. Recent family studies in alphabetic languages suggest that the risk of a child to become dyslexic can be estimated based on parents’ reading abilities. This offers a new way for early recognition of dyslexia that facilitates early intervention. It remains unknown whether such intergenerational transmission of dyslexia is present in Chinese with its unique writing system. Moreover, reading in Chinese draws on multiple cognitive-linguistic abilities different from reading in alphabetic languages, which may result in distinct dyslexia subtypes. It also remains unknown whether different cognitive subtypes show different patterns of intergenerational transmission. Predicting subtypes in dyslexia could help to provide tailored intervention programs at the earliest stage. The proposed project has two objectives, 1) to predict children’s dyslexia using parents’ reading abilities and home literacy environment; 2) to predict children’s subtype of dyslexia using parents’ cognitive abilities. Four hundred children with dyslexia and both their parents (n = 800) will be recruited. One hundred and twenty child and adult controls will also be recruited. Children will be assessed on word reading skills and cognitive-linguistic abilities covering domains of rapid naming, morphological processing, phonological processing, orthographic processing, and visual working memory. Parents will complete tasks assessing their reading and cognitive skills in the same domains as their children but with age-appropriate measures. In addition, they will fill in questionnaires on their history of reading difficulties, home literacy environment and social economic status. The assessment will be administered online in the form of video conferencing to ensure a large and representative sample. The dichotomous status and the severity of dyslexia in children will be predicted using parents’ reading and cognitive abilities and home literacy environment variables. Children with dyslexia and their parents will be compared with the control groups to identify the cognitive deficits shared between generations. Furthermore, we will classify the dyslexic children into cognitive subtypes based on several theory-informed models, and examine whether the dyslexia subtypes can be predicted by parental variables. The study is significant because family studies investigating intergenerational transmission of dyslexia are rare in Chinese societies. The study may have a long-term impact on early identification of children at risk of dyslexia based on parental cognitive-behavioural profiles. In addition, understanding cognitive subtypes and the intergenerational transmission helps to provide risk assessment that map on a specific subtype of dyslexia, which will inform early tailored intervention. 大量證據支持閱讀障礙是家族性的。最新的家庭研究表明父母的閱讀水準可以預測兒童患有閱讀障礙的概率，為早期識別閱讀障礙提供新方向。中文書寫系統尤其特殊，中文閱讀障礙在家庭中的代際傳播尚未清楚。中文閱讀需要的語言認知能力與閱讀拼音文字非常不同，導致中文閱讀障礙中獨特的亞類型。閱讀障礙亞類型是否能夠代際傳播，猶未可知。預測閱讀障礙亞類型可以幫助儘早設計個人化的干預方案。 此專案有兩個目標，第一，通過父母閱讀水準和家庭讀寫環境預測學童是否有閱讀障礙及其嚴重程度。第二，通過父母語言認知能力特點預測學童閱讀障礙亞類型。此專案以本實驗室現有的資料庫為基礎進行，其中包括84名有閱讀障礙的兒童（平均年齡為103個月），以及50名年齡相當的及健康控制組兒童。我們會額外招募138個年紀相當的閱讀障礙兒童，來擴大樣本量，目的是建立複雜先進的統計模型。閱讀障礙兒童的父母也會參與研究（數量=444【222*2】）。同時，100個孩子未患有閱讀障礙的父母也會作為控制組參與。家長和孩子會完成一系列任務，測量各種認知語言技能，其中包括字詞認讀、語音技能、字型技能、語素技能以及流利度。測試將會以網路會議的方式進行，來保證樣本具有代表性。閱讀障礙兒童和父母會與正常兒童和成人比較，以發現父母和孩子共有的認知障礙。進一步，我們會將閱讀障礙兒童分型，研究父母變數對閱讀障礙類型的預測。 此項研究意義重大，因為閱讀障礙代際傳播的研究在中文社會中尚屬少見。從長遠來看，研究結果可以指導閱讀障礙的早期發現，即根據父母的行為認知特點來判斷孩子的閱讀障礙風險。另外，瞭解閱讀障礙的亞類型及其代際傳播可以幫助建立更細緻的風險篩查，對應到具體的認知亞類型，具體的預測對設計早期個人化干預方案尤為重要。 關鍵字：中文閱讀障礙，代際傳播，認知亞類型，早期發現

14602021.label: Project Objectives
14602021.value: To provide a new, global comparative perspective on mostly isolated national debates regarding the integration of climate change mitigation in EIA procedures. Climate change mitigation has been integrated in EIA procedures, or such steps have been contemplated, in multiple jurisdictions across the world (developments have been identified in at least 30 jurisdictions). At present, the debates take place in these various jurisdictions mostly in isolation from one another. As most EIA instruments have important commonalities, global comparative perspectives could significantly enrich these various debates. To identify critical issues relating to the integration of climate change mitigation in EIA procedures and to document how they are being approached in various jurisdictions. Tentatively, the project identifies five critical issues relating to the integration of climate change mitigation in EIA procedures, with regard to (a) the methodologies and scope of the assessment; (b) the principles guiding the determination that a project’s impact on climate change is “significant”; (c) the adaptation of deliberative processes, which lie at the core of the EIA procedure, in the absence of directly affected populations and in a global context; (d) the relation with other policies on climate change mitigation, in particular cap-and-trade mechanisms; and (e) the difficulty of ensuring that the documentation of the impact of a project on climate change are fairly taken into account by national or local decision-makers, even though the latter may be inclined to favour local economic development over global environmental protection. To assess various approaches to critical issues in integrating climate change mitigation in EIA procedures and to identify effective ways to integrate climate change mitigation in EIA procedures. The five critical issues presented above have led certain jurisdictions to adopt innovative approaches to EIA. Some approaches are perhaps specific to a particular legal or socio-political context, but others could be relevant elsewhere. A comprehensive review followed by case studies and consultations with relevant stakeholders will help to identify legal developments through which critical issues were addressed, leading to an effective integration of climate change mitigation in EIA procedures. To foster a better academic understanding and knowledge of how EIA may help to mitigate climate change. The project will lead to the publication of a monograph or other publications presenting a global comparative perspective on the integration of climate change mitigation in EIA procedures. To inform policymakers, decision makers, judges and other relevant stakeholders in various jurisdictions about the various possible approaches and best practices in integrating climate change mitigation in EIA procedures, thus contributing to reinforcing the effectiveness of EIA procedures as well as the effectiveness of national efforts on climate change mitigation. A report for policymakers will be broadly circulated to relevant stakeholders. This will help policymakers, in Hong Kong and elsewhere, and other stakeholders, in devising effective ways to integrate climate change mitigation in EIA procedures.

14602021.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14602021.value: This project explores how climate change mitigation is integrated in Environmental Impact Assessments (EIA) procedures conducted around the world in order to identify issues and potential solutions. EIA seeks to ensure that the administrative decisions approving projects likely to affect the environment are well informed. While EIAs typically focus on local environmental impacts, they have increasingly been viewed as an opportunity for considering climate change mitigation in decisions on greenhouse-gas-intensive projects. In various jurisdictions (e.g. Canada, EU Member States, USA, Australia and South Africa), new precedents, statutes, regulations and technical guidance have led to the integration of climate change mitigation in certain EIA procedures. Yet, these debates, arising in a distinct national context, almost systematically unfold in isolation from developments taking place elsewhere. The premise of this research project is that much could be gained if each of these national debates could be informed by developments in other jurisdictions. In particular, his project could inform forthcoming developments in China (where authorities have alluded to the need to integrate climate change mitigation in EIA, but haven't adopted a systematic approach) and in Hong Kong (where such developments are yet to take place). The integration of climate change mitigation in EIA procedures raises five critical questions: 1. Defining the impacts of a project on climate change: a project can impact the climate system in indirect ways, for instance when fossil fuels are produced for off-site combustion, and debates have taken place on what emissions are to be documented as part of a project’s EIA. 2. Assessing significance: the impact of some projects on climate change have been discarded as an “insignificant” contribution to global greenhouse gas emissions, but alternative approaches are being developed to assess significance in context. 3. Organising deliberations: the deliberative process, central to the EIA procedure, may need to take particular forms in the absence of specifically “affected populations”. 4. Relation with other measures on climate change mitigation: EIA as a tool for climate change mitigation may appear redundant with other measures on climate change mitigation, in particular cap-and-trade mechanisms, but in many ways it appears rather complementary. 5. Ensuring effective influence on projects: EIA might be a purely formalist requirement if decision-makers favour local economic activity over global environmental protection. The project documents how various jurisdictions have approached these issues and draws lessons that could inform further developments. Thus, it seeks to promote more effective ways to integrated climate change mitigation in EIA procedures. 本項目探究了如何將減緩氣候變化納入到在世界範圍內實行的環境影響評估（環評）程序，以確定問題和可能的解決辦法。 環評旨在確保那些批准可能影響環境的項目的行政決定對其影響是充分知情的。雖然環評通常關注當地的環境影響，但它們越來越被視為在溫室氣體密集型項目決策中考慮減緩氣候變化的機會。在不同的司法管轄區（如加拿大、歐盟成員國、美國、澳大利亞和南非），新的判例、法規、條例和技術指南都已經將減緩氣候變化納入特定的環評程序中。然而，這些在獨特的國家背景下產生的爭論幾乎是系統地脫離其他地方的事態發展而展開的。本研究項目的前提是，如果這些國家的爭論可以從其他司法管轄區的發展中獲得信息，那麼就會有很多收穫。特別是，本項目可以為中國（當局已暗示將減緩氣候變化納入環評，但尚未採取系統的方法）和香港（尚未開展此類發展）未來的發展提供信息。 將減緩氣候變化納入環評程序提出了五個關鍵性問題： 1. 定義項目對氣候變化的影響：項目可以間接影響氣候系統，例如，當化石燃料生產用於場外燃燒時，會產生關於項目的環境影響評估應記錄何種排放的爭論。 2. 評估重要性：一些項目對氣候變化的影響因對全球溫室氣體的排放只有“微不足道”的貢獻而被廢棄，但是正在發展其他方法來評估重要性。 3. 組織審議：在沒有具體“受影響人群”的情況下，作為環評程序核心的審議過程可能需要採取特定形式。 4. 與減緩氣候變化的其他措施的關係：環評作為減緩氣候變化的工具，與減緩氣候變化的其他措施，特別是與總量管制和交易制度相比，可能顯得多餘，但在許多方面又相當互補。 5. 確保對項目的有效影響：如果決策者更傾向於地方經濟活動而非全球環境保護，那麼環評可能只是一種純粹的形式主義的要求。 本項目記錄了不同司法管轄區如何處理這些問題，並從中汲取經驗教訓，為進一步的發展提供信息。因此，它試圖促進將減緩氣候變化納入環評程序中的更有效的方式。

14602321.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14602321.value: 心靈因果性的當代交互主義進路

14602321.label: Project Objectives
14602321.value: To offer a contemporary interactionist approach to mental causation that is physicalistically acceptable. To argue that the causal closure of physics is neither justified by scientific evidence nor required by physicalist metaphysics. To critically examine several leading difference-making accounts of causation and to explore their theoretical relevance to the problem of mental causation. To elaborate the theoretical advantages of the interactionist approach over competing approaches. To complete two articles publishable in leading philosophy journals.

To argue that the causal closure of physics is neither justified by scientific evidence nor required by physicalist metaphysics.
To critically examine several leading difference-making accounts of causation and to explore their theoretical relevance to the problem of mental causation.
To elaborate the theoretical advantages of the interactionist approach over competing approaches.
To complete two articles publishable in leading philosophy journals.

14602321.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14602321.value: 根據心靈哲學中的主流觀點，心理屬性不能還原為或等同於物理屬性。然而，此非還原主義的立場似乎難以容納心靈因果性這一重要的現象。大部分的哲學家都接受「物理的因果閉合性」原則；根據這個原則，每一物理結果都有一個充足的物理原因。如果物理領域是因果閉合的，並且心理屬性又不同於物理屬性，那麽我們會得出一個令人不安的結論：心理狀態不能因果地導致任何物理狀態——人類的能動性也就無從談起。在有關心靈因果性的文獻中，幾乎所有的進路都預設了「物理的因果閉合性」原則。但這些理論捉襟見肘、問題重重。本研究計劃力圖發展一個心靈因果性的交互主義進路。根據這一理論，心理狀態是某些物理狀態的不可或缺的原因。如果交互主義為真，那麽物理領域則不是因果閉合的。我將會論證，對於非還原主義而言，交互主義是最為可行的心靈因果理論。在當今的心靈哲學中，人們普遍認為，「物理的因果閉合性」原則不僅得到了經驗科學的充分支持，而且是物理主義世界觀的應有之義。在本研究計劃中，我試圖挑戰這一共識，提出一個物理主義版本的當代交互主義理論。具體來說，我將論證，交互主義與物理規律（例如「能量動量守恆定律」）是相容的。並且，交互主義也不會違背物理主義的世界圖景——對於物理主義而言，本體論意義上而非因果性意義上的依存關繫才至關重要。此外，心靈因果性的問題與因果關係本身的哲學探究密不可分。本計劃也將批判性地考察幾個主要的因果理論，並嘗試發展一種操控主義的因果觀。我將表明，操控主義比其他因果理論更為優勝，而且能夠為心靈因果的交互主義進路提供有力的支持。

14602321.label: Realisation of objectives
14602321.value: The objectives have been completely realized. 1) In the article “Downward Causation in a Physicalist World” (under review in Canadian Journal of Philosophy), I develop a sophisticated interactionalist approach to mental causation. I argue that this version of interactionalism is consistent with both physical sciences and the physicalist metaphysics. Moreover, I contrast my interactionist approach with an alternative, compatibilist model of mental causation. I argue that the interactionist account is no less physicalistically acceptable than compatibilism but immune from various serious problems with the latter. 2) In the article “Causality and Realization-Sensitivity” (under review in Australasian Journal of Philosophy), I develop a promising account of higher-level causality that explores the idea of realization-sensitivity and -insensitivity. I argue that this causal account is more plausible than competing difference-making accounts of causation because it provides a unifying and suitable understanding of causality. The article also attempts to show that a sensitivity-based approach can shed new light on the topic of mental causation. 3) In the article “A Causal Argument for Physicalism” (the lead contribution for an article symposium in Asian Journal of Philosophy), I develop a novel causal argument for physicalism understood broadly, inspired by the causal argument for reductive physicalism. I aim to show that, while the old causal argument for reductive physicalism is controversial, the new causal argument for physicalism simpliciter is promising. More specifically, I argue that whereas Closure, a crucial premise of the old argument, is false, Closure*, a significant premise of the new argument, is plausible. Eventually, we should accept an interactionist version of physicalism. [Please note that this GRF grant, which consists solely of a teaching relief grant, has not been spent at all, because I have been using another teaching relief grant I concurrently hold (under the RGC Research Fellow Scheme).]

14602321.label: Major findings and research outcome
14602321.value: There are three significant research findings. First, I develop a sophisticated interactionalist approach to mental causation that is physicalistically acceptable. Second, I put forward a novel causal argument for physicalism without lending support to reductionism. Third, I develop a promising account of higher-level causality (and mental causation in particular) that appeals to the notion of realization-sensitivity. The research project directly results in a number of high-quality journal articles and conference papers. Some of them (such as the articles “Downward Causation in a Physicalist World” and “A Causal Argument for Physicalism”) have already stimulated various responses and discussion from other reputable philosophers.

14602321.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14602321.value: Whether an interactionist approach to mental causation is credible depends essentially on whether it can be supported by respectable theories of causation. The dominant tradition in contemporary metaphysics of causation seeks to characterize causality in a broad counterfactual framework. There are two influential counterfactual approaches to causation, the Lewisian classical counterfactual approach and the interventionist counterfactual approach. In this current project, I focus on the first approach. But in the future, I plan to compare this approach with the interventionist approach and find out which approach is more plausible and which approach can offer better support for a non-reductionist view of mental causation. This research is expected to make significant contributions to philosophy of mind and higher-level causation.

14602321.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14602321.value: It is widely agreed in the philosophy of mind that mental phenomena are non-identical to physical phenomena. However, this anti-reductionist view has been accused of failing to accommodate mental causation, the precondition of human cognition and agency. If the physical domain is causally closed, and if the mental is distinct from the physical, it seems to follow that mental states can never cause any physical states. This research project has developed a contemporary version of interactionism that promises to offer the most plausible account of mental causation available to non-reductive physicalists. It is worth noting that this interactionist account rejects the causal closure of physics. Although many philosophers assume that denying physical causal closure is incompatible with the physicalist worldview, this project defends a sophisticated interactionist approach that is physicalistically acceptable.

14602921.label: Project Objectives

14602921.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14602921.value: Aim: This is a comparative study of the reception and localization of the Yijing (Classic of Changes) on China’s ethnic frontiers and peripheries including non-Sinic ethnic groups (such as the Tibetans and the Mongols) and the Sinosphere (such as Japan and Korea). Project Background: The Yijing was one of the most globalized Chinese classics that had been studied and used in different parts of the world. It was localized outside China to fit different cultural traditions. The history and impact of the Yijing in China and the West have been extensively researched, whereas its reception and localization in Asia remain little studied. This project will be a pioneering study of the Yijing in pre-modern Asia from a comparative perspective. Brief Project Description: Through a textual analysis of primary sources, this proposed project will be a comparative study of the historical reception of the Yijing in China’s neighboring states located within and beyond the Sinosphere. From Tang to Qing, a Yijing cultural sphere was formed in Asia. With China as the place of origin and the center, the sphere consists of two layers. The Sinic nations (Japan, Korea, Vietnam and the Ryukyu Kingdom) are in the inner layer, whereas non-Sinic ethnic groups (the Tibetans, the Tanguts, the Mongols, the Manchu, the Hui, the Miao) are in the outer layer. In the Sinosphere, the text, images and divination of the Yijing were seriously studied and some very original and influential commentaries were written. In non-Sinic China’s peripheral tribal states, people were primarily interested in the Yijing divination and the translation of the text. The symbols, concepts and oracles of the Yijing were assimilated into their indigenous religions and cultures. This study compares the reception of the Yijing in the Sinosphere and non-Sinic ethnic groups in pre-modern Asia by examining its translations, interpretations and applications. Project Significance: This study will break new ground in Yijing studies, East Asian studies and Asian religions in the following aspects: (1) to construct a new notion of the “Yijing cultural sphere” as an analytical framework to study the Yijing from a global perspective; (2) to provide the first academic investigation of the Yijing on China’s ethnic frontiers and peripheries; (3) to be the first comparative study of the Yijing in the Sinosphere and non-Sinic cultures in pre-modern Asia; and (4) to be developed into a monograph that will shape a new direction of Yijing studies. 易學在中國非漢族及週邊地區的比較研究 本研究旨在比較易學在中國境內非漢族（如藏族、蒙古族）及週邊地區（如日本、韓國）的傳播與在地化。《易經》是最全球化的中國經典之一，在全球各地供人學習與使用。雖然中國及西方的易學史已被廣泛研究，易學在亞洲的接受及在地化的相關研究卻不多。本研究對開拓現代以前的亞洲易學史具高度價值。 透過對原始史料的文獻分析，此研究比較中國境內非漢族及週邊國家的易學史。徙唐至清的期間，亞洲出現易學文化圈。中國是此文化圈的根源及中心。中心以外分內外兩層。內層是漢字文化圈成員（如日本、韓國、越南、琉球）。外層是漢字文化圈以外的非漢族群（如藏族、党項族、蒙古族、滿族、回族、苗族）。在漢字文化圈之內，《易經》的義理、象數及占卜被認真研究，出現一些具創意的重要易學著作。在漢字文化圈以外的非漢族群在易學上的主要興趣在占卜及翻譯。易學的符號、概念及占卜與當地宗教及文化融合。此研究比較漢字文化圈及非漢族群在易學的翻譯、解釋及應用。 本研究對易學、東亞研究及亞洲宗教均有突破性貢獻。第一，構建具全球易學視野的「易學文化圈」概念。第二，開創中國境內及週邊非漢族群的嶄新研究領域。第三，提供首個漢字文化圈及非漢字文化圈的比較易學研究。第四，撰寫學術專書，對全球易學提供新方向。

14602921.label: Realisation of objectives
14602921.value: The four academic objectives have been fully achieved during this two and a half year project. (1) Outline the historical reception of the Yijing in pre-modern Asia based on primary sources: For the first time in the academia, the whole picture of the history of the Yijing was drawn. I have outlined the historical reception of the Yijing in Japan, Korea, Vietnam, the Ryukyu Kingdom and non-Han ethnic groups in Asia based on primary sources. (2) Create a new concept called the Yijing cultural sphere as an interpretive framework to study the globalization and localization of the Yijing in a global perspective: I have created a new concept of Yijing cultural sphere in Asia in my academic book published in 2023 from the Taiwan University Press. It shows different levels of popularization and localization of the Yijing in Asia from a comparative perspective . This concept has drawn academic attention form experts of the Yijing. The book was nominated for the best philosophy book published in Taiwan in 2023. (3) Identify and compare the characteristics of Yijing studies in the Sinosphere and non-Sinic cultures in premodern Asia: I have identified the he characteristics of Yijing studies on China's ethnic frontiers and peripheries and explained why different Asian regions demonstrate different levels of localization. I have created the concept of cultural habitable zone within the Sinosphere to explain why Japan could create more original interpretations and applications of the Yijing than Korea and Vietnam that were culturally closer to China. (4) Examine the role of the Yijing in the making of Asian religion and culture. Special attention will be paid to the process of the assimilation of its ideas, images and divination practices in various Asian beliefs and customs: This is the part on which I published and presented most. It shows that the Yijing played a significant role in the making Asian religions and cultures. Element of the Yijing have been absorbed into Asian religions and cultures from Tibetan Buddhism, Japanese Shinto, Hui Islam to Japanese literature, Tibetan paintings and Korean mythology.

14602921.value: Major Findings: (1) I have constructed the concepts of Yijing Cultural Sphere in Asia and cultural habitable zone that explain the popularization and localization of the Yijing in Sinosphere. I plan to write an article to enhance and promote this concept. (2) Examine the role of Yijing in East Asian literature, art and popular culture. 14603121.label: Project Objectives
14603121.value: This project aims at developing a framework on the psychological attributes of arts that could elucidate preferences and responses to artworks of different genres. psychological framework on arts. Research on arts have been segregated by art genres because different art genres are like apples and oranges that they cannot be compared with each other. The overall objective of this project is to develop a Psychological Attributes of Arts (PAA) framework to map out the psychological attributes of arts that different art forms could be examined under a coherent set of attributes. One research goal is to develop a measurement inventory to operationalize the PAA framework that each artwork could be quantitatively described along a set of well-defined attributes. Measurements on this set of common psychological attributes shall then allow artworks of different genres to be compared. Theoretical and research findings developed upon one art genre could then be evaluated and extended to works of different art genres depending on the similarities and differences along these art attributes. 14603121.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14603121.value: Research on motivations and responses towards arts have been segregated by art genres. The segregation has impeded accumulation and generalization of research findings on one art genre to another. The major barrier is not having a common framework to map out attributes of arts from a psychological perspective that similarities and differences among artworks could be described and theorized. The current project aims at developing a psychological attributes of arts (PAA) that identifies a set of attributes to describe artworks of different genres. This project is an extension of our pilot work on a theoretical taxonomy proposing four attributes (narrative/non-narrative, static/dynamic, representational/abstract, and authenticity/make-believe) across art forms and a pilot empirical study on drama identifying four attributes (comprehensibility, relevance, epical, and sensational). Study 1 is a qualitative study to identify attributes within each of eight art genres (literary arts, film / media arts, visual arts, drama, music, dance, opera/xiqu and multi-arts). Study 2 is a qualitative study to identify further attributes by contrasting pairs of the eight genres. Study 3 is a quantitative study to develop the framework of PAA through exploratory factor analysis. Study 4a and 4b are quantitative studies to validate the PAA framework with local and non-local respondents through confirmatory factor analysis. Study 5 is a quantitative study to evaluate the construct and criterion validity of PAA framework by examining how PAA could predict preferences towards different art genres and how PAA could serve as mediators to explain the relation between personality and art preferences. The validated PAA framework shall serve as an important language to describe psychological attributes of art that allow theorization and generalization of research across art forms. 有關於對藝術的動機和反應的研究可按藝術流派分類，而這種分類方式阻礙了研究成果從一種藝術流派橫跨至另一種藝術流派的累積和概括化。其中，最主要的障礙是缺乏一個通用的架構去制定理論並找出不同形式的藝術在心理上引發相似或相異的特性。目前的研究旨在建構一個藝術心理屬性 (PAA)框架 來辨別一套描述不同流派的藝術作品。該研究是我們先導性項目的延伸，而該先導性項目以理論分類法提出四個跨藝術形式的屬性（敘事/非敘事、靜態/動態、代表/抽象、真實/虛構）和試點，另一戲劇先導計劃識別了四個屬性（可理解性、相關性、莊嚴程度和感動程度）。研究 一是一項定性研究，用於確定八種藝術流派（文學藝術、電影/媒體藝術、視覺藝術、戲劇、音樂、舞蹈、戲曲和多元藝術）中的特性。研究二是另一項定性研究，通過一對對地比較八種藝術流派去進一步確定屬性。研究三是一項定量研究，旨在通過探索性因素分析開發 PAA 框架。研究四a 和四b 是透過驗證性因素分析與本地和非本地受訪者一起驗證 PAA 框架的定量研究。研究五是一項定量研究，通過檢查 PAA 如何預測對不同藝術類型的偏好以及 PAA 如何作為中介來解釋個性和藝術偏好之間的關係，從而評估 PAA 框架的結構和標準有效性。經驗證的 PAA 框架應作為一種重要的語言來描述藝術的心理屬性，允許研究能跨藝術形式進行理論化和概括。

14603221.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14603221.value: 創造空間：以臨時城市戰略來重新連接香港公共開放空間和社區

14603221.label: Project Objectives
14603221.value: To develop a participatory process in order to actively engage the local community in the transformation of their urban environment through a series of focus groups and workshops in which critical issues and challenges can be identified, with priority given to specific actions in the public space. To implement three temporary urban design interventions in underused public spaces by soliciting the input of the community, and to create/reclaim new places for social activities where residents can be adequately represented so as to generate a more inclusive and sustainable urban environment. To examine the three urban design interventions by evaluating their impact on the use of the space as well as people's behaviours through an iterative and incremental process of feedback and assessment with the community. To formulate a macro-strategy for how the city can adopt temporary urban design interventions as a planning tool for re-activating unused public spaces and transforming these community-driven initiatives into permanent projects, addressing the tension between bottom-up and top-down processes by creating an enhanced and more inclusive urban environment.

14603221.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14603221.value: The aim of this research is to explore how the use of temporary urban design interventions can be a valuable strategy in transforming lifeless public spaces into vibrant components of the urban environment. Hong Kong is a world-class metropolis, but regrettably, most of the open public spaces in old urban areas were created adopting a rigid, top-down approach and by applying generalised, cookie-cutter solutions to a variety of different sites and urban conditions. These valuable but often underused open spaces do little to serve residents’ needs, as they neither facilitate social interaction nor encourage community activity. In Hong Kong, the existing ordinances and other planning strategies have not addressed the problematic conditions of public spaces in old urban areas. Furthermore, socioeconomic and political factors dictate the planning process by and large, relegating participatory mechanisms to the sidelines. Although the inadequacy of Hong Kong’s public spaces has been well documented (Xue and Manuel 2001; Tang and Wong 2008; Lai, 2017), few studies have examined how to upgrade and re-socialise these important resources in such a high-density environment. Given this context, this project was inspired by ‘assemblage thinking’: a bottom-up framework for understanding the complexity of urban problems by emphasising sociospatial relations at different scales (Kamalipour, 2015). As such, it offers a stimulating lens with which to re-view Hong Kong’s underused and/or marginal public spaces, whilst encouraging an inclusive approach to urban planning and design. Having already identified three categories of underused public spaces during prior investigation in the field - Detached, Static and Dysfunctional - this research takes a step forward, in both theory and practice by: a) developing a participatory strategy to engage the local community in the active transformation of their urban environment; b) implementing three tactical urban design interventions to be tested in selected public open spaces; c) evaluating what impact these placemaking projects may have on people’s behaviour; and finally, d) formulating a macro-strategy for adopting these tactical urban actions as a way of re-activating underused public spaces and transforming these temporary initiatives into permanent projects. The findings of this research will inform the current Hong Kong Government’s planning efforts, ‘HK2030+’, in order to create a more sustainable and liveable environment. The results will also be a useful reference for public space policymakers in Hong Kong’s Planning Department, facilitating the adoption of placemaking interventions as an important bridge between municipal authorities and the community. 本研究的目的是探索如何使用臨時城市設計干預措施的寶貴策略將毫無生氣的公共空間轉變為城市環境中充滿活力的組成部分。 香港是一個國際大都會，但遺憾的是，舊城區的大部分開放公共空間的創立都是採用死板的、自上而下的、通用的、千篇一律的解決方案以處理各種不同的地點和城市條件。這些有價值但經常未被充分利用的開放空間對滿足居民的需求幾乎沒有作用，因為它們既不促進社交互動，也不鼓勵社區活動。在香港，現有的條例和其他規劃策略並沒有解決舊城區公共空間的問題。此外，社會經濟和政治因素總體上決定了規劃過程，忽略了參與機制。 儘管香港公共空間的不足的事實已有充分的文件記錄（Xue 和 Manuel 2001；Tang 和 Wong 2008；Lai，2017），但很少有研究探討如何在如此高密度的環境中升級和重新社會化這些重要資源。 鑒於以上背景，這個項目的靈感來自「組合思維」：通過強調不同尺度的社會空間關係，以自下而上的框架來理解城市問題的複雜性（Kamalipour，2015）。因此，它提供了一個令人振奮的視角，可以用來重新審視香港未充分利用和/或邊緣的公共空間，同時鼓勵採用包容性的城市規劃和設計方法。 在先前的實地調查中已經確定了三種未充分利用的公共空間——獨立的、靜態的和功能失調的——這項研究在理論和實踐上都向前邁進了一步：a) 制定參與式戰略，讓當地社區積極參與改變他們的城市環境； b) 在選定的公共開放空間中實施三項戰術城市設計干預措施； c) 評估這些空間營造項目可能對人們的行為產生什麼影響；最後，d) 制定宏觀戰略，採用這些戰術性城市行動，作為重新激活未充分利用的公共空間並將這些臨時舉措轉變為永久性項目的一種方式。 這項研究的結果將為現屆香港政府的規劃工作「HK2030+」提供信息，以創造一個更加可持續和宜居的環境。研究結果也將為香港規劃署的公共空間決策者提供有用的參考，促進空間營造干預措施的採用，作為市政當局與社區之間的重要橋樑。

14603521.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14603521.value: 利用動態數學環境科技支援少數族裔學生的數學思維和教師相應的教學研究

14603521.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14603521.value: Dr Baccaglini-Frank, Anna Prof Jackson, Liz Prof Leung, Allen Yuk-lun Dr Sum, Emily Mr Wong, Ka Lok

14603521.label: Project Objectives
14603521.value: Examine what Hong Kong primary school mathematics teachers attend to when engaging EM students in DME-enhanced learning activities and how they interpret and respond to EM students’ mathematical thinking. Observe the process of developing mathematics teachers’ responsive teaching practices for EM students through in-moment and video-based retrospective analysis of their teaching. Investigate linguistic (i.e. language) and non-linguistic (i.e. gestures with or without touchscreen-based DMEs) resources in EM students’ mathematical communication in touchscreen-based DMEs. Characterise EM students’ mathematical discourse using a commognitive and non-deficit view of communication and identify their mathematical competences in multimodal, technological contexts.

14603521.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14603521.value: Recently, education reforms have taken place worldwide in response to the diverse linguistic and cultural backgrounds of student populations, as facilitated by international mobility. In Hong Kong, the local mathematics curriculum stresses the need to address mathematics learning for ethnic minority (EM) students who, in addition to the mathematical content, are simultaneously learning the language of instruction and the language specific to the mathematics register. As communication is an essential process for learning mathematics, teaching EM students mathematics poses instructional challenges. Equity concerns have grown as a result of EM students’ low academic achievements, especially in mathematics. With their limited vocabulary, EM students use multiple resources (e.g. home language, gestures, and visual representations) to communicate mathematically. Thus, teachers must be able to recognise and support this multimodal communication. However, little is known about how multimodal forms of communication can be effectively leveraged in mathematics classrooms. Although technological resources for multimodal mathematics learning are available in Hong Kong schools in the form of touchscreen-based dynamic and multi-representational environments (DMEs), teachers are not equipped to utilise them in their practice, especially in supporting EM students. This study’s dual aims are: (1) to develop Hong Kong teachers’ expertise in supporting EM students’ mathematical learning in multimodal, technological learning environments, (2) to uncover EM students’ competences in mathematical activities in DMEs through examining their multimodal discourse (e.g. words, gestures, and touchscreen dragging). Using the theoretical framing of commognition (i.e. thinking-as-communicating), this study collects qualitative data comprising the videotaped teaching sessions of six primary school mathematics teachers and 24 EM students from grades 1 to 6. In both research cycles, each teacher participant will engage in five co-planning, teaching, and post-teaching reflection sessions. The analysis will be twofold. First, it will focus on teachers’ practices in response to the EM students’ mathematical thinking during DME-enhanced learning activities. Second, it will examine the EM students’ communication as supported by touchscreen-based DMEs using the PI’s previously developed multimodal discourse analysis. This study underscores the importance of considering EM students’ non-linguistic forms of communication to facilitate mathematical learning in Hong Kong schools and beyond. It presents implications for teacher professional development regarding the use of dynamic and multi-representational technology in today’s multilingual mathematics classrooms. It advances a non-deficit, multimodal view of communication and informs future studies on capturing students’ mathematical competences through their gestures and touchscreen-dragging actions in DMEs, particularly in the case of language learners from non-dominant communities. 近年來，在國際流動的推動下，世界範圍內的教育改革都在關注學生的多元語言和文化背景。在香港，本地的數學課程也在強調關注少數族裔（EM）學生的數學學習，因為他們除了學習數學內容以外，還要同時掌握教師的教學語言和數學專用語言。由於交流是數學學習過程必不可少的環節，這為EM學生的數學教學帶來了額外的挑戰，而EM學生數學成績不理想的現狀亦令教育公平問題日益顯著。由於他們詞彙量有限，EM學生通常會借助不同的方式進行數學交流，例如母語，手勢和視覺表徵等。因此，數學老師必須能夠識別和支持這些多模式的交流活動。然而，我們對於如何在數學課堂中運用和支持多模態交流知之甚少。雖然香港的中小學已經運用科技資源，包括觸屏式的動態、多表徵數學環境（DMEs）去支持教學，教師仍然缺乏使用這些資源方面的訓練，尤其是結合這些資源去輔助EM學生的數學學習。 本研究項目的兩個目標為:（一）提高香港教師支持EM學生在多模態環境科技中學習數學的技能，（二） 通過分析EM學生在DME數學活動中的多模態語意（如言語、手勢觸屏拖動動作）去揭示他們的數學學習。本研究將採用交流認知理論的框架收集質性研究數據，包括對6名小學數學教師以及24名一至六年級EM學生的數學課堂進行錄像。在每一輪數據收集中，每位教師將參與5次合作設計、教學和課後反思。數據分析將圍繞兩方面進行。第一，關注教師如何基於EM學生在DME環境中的數學學習活動和思維作出相應的教學行為。第二，通過多模態語意分析去了解觸屏式的DME學習環境如何支持EM學生的數學交流。 本研究旨在強調香港（及其他） EM學生的非語言交流形式在數學學習中的重要性。相關的研究成果將會對如何促進教師在多語種數學課堂中使用動態、多表徵信息技術提供啟示。同時，該研究提倡一種非負面的、多模態的交流觀念，並且對於未來相關的研究有所啟示，即通過學生在DME中的手勢和触摸屏拖動動作來揭示他們的數學能力，尤其是非母語學生。

14604221.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14604221.value: 為愛，或為何？來自不承認同性婚姻地區的同性伴侶到海外結婚的悖論

14604221.label: Project Objectives
14604221.value: To address a central question of sociological concern, which is: how social minorities, in this case, sexual minorities, exercise their agency and resist when they are excluded from the current local legal system, in this case, legal marriage recognition. This theoretical question is particularly interesting and pertinent as the global development of sexual rights is highly uneven – while same-sex marriage is recognized in 28 countries, homosexuality is still explicitly criminalized in 68 countries. This research aims to understand a rather new phenomenon: same-sex couples living in places where same-sex marriage is not legally recognized going overseas to get married. To understand the social meanings of marriage, in particular, same-sex marriage, in contemporary society, through ethnographic research with same-sex couples living in places where same-sex marriage is not legally recognized who go overseas to get married. In an era when an increasing number of heterosexual people are delaying or even refraining from getting married, why would such same-sex couples make great efforts to go overseas to get married? The same-sex couples in question travel thousands of miles and often spend hundreds of thousands of dollars on a marriage that would in effect not be legally recognized in the places where they live. This research aims to provide a theoretically interesting case to understand the meanings of marriage as an institution for them, the challenges they face in accessing the institution, and the social meanings of their action of accessing the institution. To contribute to the theoretical understanding of globalization and sexual rights through understanding the socioeconomic background of same-sex couples living in places where same-sex marriage is not legally recognized who go overseas to get married: where they go to get married; how they do it; and what challenges they face, thereby analyzing the facilitators and barriers of the same-sex couples’ access to the marriage institution. To examine the ways in which same-sex couples adopt and resist the same-sex marriage rituals that have been developed in other parts of the world when they make great efforts to go overseas to get married. When they return home to where they live, how do they make sense of their marriage in a society that does not recognize their marriage? Do they open up about their marriage to their family, friends and colleagues? What challenges do they face and what social change do they bring?

14604221.value: 此研究關注有關婚姻制度的問題在現代社會中，婚姻（特別是同性婚姻）的意義為何？此研究為「婚姻制度的未來」 及「婚姻是否一個過時、快要消逝的制度」等學術討論作出貢獻。此研究為這討論帶入有趣的角度： 如果婚姻是不重要或是一個過時的制度，為甚麼有些同性伴侶會遠赴幾千哩及花費數以萬計的金錢到海外結婚，即使他們的婚姻並不被其居住地承認？ 透過田野式調查，研究來自不承認同性婚姻地區， 而到海外結婚的同性伴侶，研究問題為： 當越來越多異性戀者延遲或拒絕結婚，為甚麼這些同性伴侶如此重視這個制度，即使排除萬難都要結婚？ 他們的社經背景是甚麼？他們選擇在哪裡結婚，過程是如何的？他們遇到甚麼困難？他們自身、家人朋友，以及社會是如何理解婚姻？ 這個研究同時回應社會學的核心問題： 當被排除在現行的法律政策制度，社會小眾 （在此為性小眾）如何實踐其能動性去回應？放在全球性權利發展不平等的情況下(現時在28個國家承認同性婚姻，同時在68個國家將同性戀定為刑事罪行)，這個理論問題特別有趣及相關。 這研究同時亦回應全球化及性權的討論： 同性伴侶如何採用及抗衡在其他國家發展的同性婚姻儀式 ？當他們回到自己的居住地，他們如何理解其婚姻不被當地承認？他們會否告訴其家人、朋友及同事？他們會面對甚麼挑戰，以及能為社會帶來甚麼改變？ 我會與最少20對到海外結婚的同性伴侶進行深入訪問，他們來自不承認同性婚姻的地方，例如香港、中國內地及新加坡。同時，我亦計劃訪問這些同性伴侶的家人及朋友，以及為他們籌備婚禮的公司及服務提供者，例如攝影師、婚禮場地的提供者及職員。如果有同性伴侶正在計劃到海外結婚，我會尋求他們的準許，出席他們的婚禮，以作田野式考察。 在受訪同性伴侶的同意之下，我將會製作一套紀錄片（包括影像及相片）。 這紀錄片將會與推動及反對同性婚姻的非政府組織合作進行放映，並舉行研討會，讓參與者對同性婚姻這個議題作出討論。

14604321.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14604321.value: 簡介 即使已有臨床實證證明面對面及網路心理治療的成效，於抑鬱症治療中推廣及應用這些心理治療仍然是個挑戰。利用離散選擇試驗 (discrete choice experiment) 研究有抑鬱症人士對治療的偏好，能了解服務使用者如何權衡各種治療相關的特質。這種方法對比傳統利用李克特量表的調查，更能就服務使用者的治療偏好提供啟發。透過有關服務使用者對治療偏好的知識，資源更能被妥善分配，從而促進服務的實施。然而，對有抑鬱症的人士如何考量不同心理治療服務至今仍然了解不多。 研究目的 為加強有關服務使用者對心理治療服務偏好的實證基礎，本研究之目的是 (1) 探究各種心理治療服務的特質 (例如︰實行模式、等候時間、自付服務費用、匿名程度及轉介方式) 對選擇服務的重要性; (2) 於有抑鬱症的人士中，識別其對治療服務的偏好異質性; 以及 (3) 模擬面對面及網路心理治療的使用數據，以提供有關精神健康服務政策的建議。 研究及數據分析方法 於三百名超過臨床臨界值 (PHQ9 ≥10) 有抑鬱症症狀的人士中，採用離散選擇試驗的高效設計 (D-efficient design)。參加者需於假設性的治療情景作出選擇，這些情景的性質和級別會有系統地改變。 為引領整個研究的設計，形成性階段將在實驗階段前進行，以將有抑鬱症人士認為重要及相關的治療服務性質包括在研究中。研究中所使用的治療服務性質，將會由現有文獻及有抑鬱症的人士組成之焦點團體訪談所支持。 混合羅吉特模型 (mixed logit models) 將用作分析各種治療服務性質的偏好考量，而潛在類別模型 (latent class models) 則用作探究有相似偏好的類別。根據效用最大原則(maximum utility principle)，隨機模擬第一偏好方式 (ﬁrst-choice) 將會用作分析在每個偏好類別中，使用不同面對面及網路心理治療的有抑鬱症人士之百分比。 重要性 據我們所知，本研究是第一個採用離散選擇試驗去探討三個主要的抑鬱症心理治療服務性質 (結果、治療實行模式及費用) 的研究。在理論上，本研究提供的知識有助了解對心理治療服務最重要的各種考量。而實際上，本研究亦有助制定提供最佳心理服務的社會決策。

14605121.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14605121.value: 研究旨在評估虛擬現實 (VR) 和信息和通信技術 (ICT) 對聽障遊人 (HI) 在戶外環境中體驗的影響，以鹽田梓為個案。鹽田梓代表了香港受遊人和旅遊業發展歡迎的鄉村和島嶼景點。本研究將調查到訪前VR體驗和 到訪期間使用智能設備如何影響聽障遊人的感官體驗創建過程。 理論和知識的缺口有三個方面。第一，現存研究對感官障礙的遊人的感官體驗創造過程知識不足；第二，虛擬沉浸式技術和移動應用程式對感官障礙的遊人的體驗和影響尚未有充份研究；第三，對聽障人士在香港鄉郊環境所面對的障礙缺乏透徹的了解。 這些研究將協助創造感官增強的環境，亦幫助改善可達性社會和社會可持續性。 本研究通過一系列實驗式和行動式方法，調查障礙參與者在以下情況如何描繪島上的感官體驗創造過程：（1）有或沒有到訪前虛擬現實體驗 (2) 到訪期間有或沒有智能設備和移動應用程式。本研究將闡明參與者的自我報告體驗和其感官體驗創造過程。主要研究方法包括體驗原型地圖、問卷調查和焦點小組討論，樣本包括四組規定實驗條件共 160 名（一般和聽障）參與者。 本研究的理論意義有兩大方面。第一，通過整合無障礙旅遊、遊人體驗和體驗景觀創新的研究成果，將結合各個知識層面，了解虛擬和移動技術對感官障礙的遊人的影響。第二，研究結果強化感官障礙的知識，提高遊人在社會中的可達性和享受體驗。 在政策、地方管理和實踐方面，為政府、管理人員和殘疾人士提供策略建議，通過利用虛擬沉浸式技術和智能設備來增強和創新體驗，以實現更通用的設計和無障礙環境。

14605421.label: Realisation of objectives
14605421.value: Of the 196 survivors who fulfilled the inclusion criteria and were invited to participate in the study, 187 survivors provided informed consent. Of these, 185 survivors have completed the assessments and were included in the analysis (response rate: 94.4%). The mean age of the participants was 28.9 years (SD = 6.7 years), and 48.1% of the participants were female. The average age at diagnosis was 8.6 years (SD = 5.3 years), and the mean time since diagnosis was 20.3 years (SD = 7.4 years). The cancer diagnoses were hematological cancers (n = 118, 63.8%), CNS solid tumors (n = 8, 4.3%), and non-CNS solid tumors (n = 59, 31.9%). The research procedure included a prospective assessment of frailty status, neurocognitive assessment and behavioral assessment through a set of patient-reported questionnaires, as well as collection of 5 cc of blood for telomere length analysis. The study procedures also included a retrospective review of the participants’ previous cancer treatment/clinical data from the Clinical Management System (CMS). In summary, all research objectives have been met during the study period. Problems encountered and solutions. Note: there were no deviations from the original plan. 1. Recruitment No patients were recruited at the beginning of the study from January to May 2022 due to the 5th pandemic wave. As the pandemic gradually resolved, we managed to achieve the targeted sample size during the study period. 2. Telomere length assay Our proposed plan was to ride on the biological samples that were collected from 2 previous GRF grants (Ref 24614818 and 14601919). We assumed that 75% of survivors (n=188) will provide analyzable biological samples and complete frailty assessments. We had successfully utilized the above plasma samples to evaluate cytokine levels for the previous GRF grant. However, we had not tried processing or analyzing the DNA from the whole blood samples. With the support of Co-I Prof Kenneth To, we analyzed the first 50 set of blood samples in Dec 2022 (in preparation for the progress report), which include both “old” and “new” samples. The results were encouraging as the whole blood samples provided a high yield of DNA (i.e. the samples were free from impurity and had not degraded from storage). The intra coefficient of variation among the triplicate samples were low, indicating high reproducibility of the measurements. We were then more confident in the sample processing, storage and analytical methods for this study.

14605421.label: Major findings and research outcome
14605421.value: Objective 1a: To evaluate the association between physiologic marker of aging (frailty phenotype) and cognitive/ behavioral outcomes in survivors of childhood cancer Based on the Fried frailty criteria, the proportions of participants with frailty and pre-frailty were 22.7% and 27.0%, respectively. For cognitive outcomes, the multivariable model showed that “frail” survivors exhibited more severe impairments in attention and executive function, specifically in terms of inattentiveness (Estimate [Est]=4.57, P=0.007), sustained attention (Est=3.68, P=0.001) and cognitive flexibility (Est=8.08, P=0.009), than “non-frail/pre-frail” survivors. For behavioral outcomes, pre-frail/frail survivors demonstrated more neurobehavioral problems than non-frail survivors, especially anxiety/depression (Est=2.99, P=0.007), withdrawal (Est=2.93, P=0.005) and attention problems (Est=3.29, P<0.001). Objective 1b: To evaluate the association between biological marker of aging (telomere length) and cognitive/ behavioral outcomes in survivors of childhood cancer No significant associations were observed between telomere length and cognitive/behavioral outcomes in the overall cohort. However, significant association between telomere length and cognitive/behavioral outcomes were found in analyses stratified by age at cancer diagnosis, sex, and the presence of sarcopenia. Exploratory objective: Survivors who had been diagnosed with cancer at a younger age were more likely to have frailty (odds ratio [OR] = 0.93, 95% confidence interval [95% CI]: 0.87–0.99, P = 0.041). In the analysis stratified by median age at diagnosis (<8.5 years), significant association among frailty, telomere length and cognitive/behavioral outcomes were found only among those with a younger age at diagnosis (< 8.5 years), but not in the older diagnosis group. Survivors with chronic health conditions had 4.63 times higher odds of being frail than those without chronic health conditions (95% CI: 1.68–12.80, P = 0.003). Survivors who were employed (OR = 0.43, 95% CI: 0.20–0.92, P = 0.030) and had a higher monthly income level (≥ 20,000 HKD) (OR = 0.30, 95% CI: 0.13–0.70, P = 0.005) had a lower risk of frailty than those who were unemployed and had lower monthly income level, respectively. There were no significant between-group differences in telomere length, sex, age at diagnosis, cancer type, or cancer-related treatments. In the exploratory network analysis, fatigue had direct connections with multiple behavioral symptoms and was also associated with weak handgrip strength, slow walking speed, and low muscle mass.

14605421.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14605421.value: 1. Our results revealed associations between frailty and impaired attention and executive function. Taken together, frailty may be a physiological aging marker of cognitive impairment in survivors of childhood cancer. Our findings support the development of supportive interventions to slow premature aging and mitigate the adverse impact of aging on neurocognitive and behavioral outcomes in long-term cancer survivors. 2. A shorter telomere length was associated with internalizing symptoms, including anxiety/depression and withdrawal symptoms, in survivors diagnosed with cancer at a younger age. Our results suggest that physiological frailty is a more perceptible marker for monitoring aging and its complications. However, cellular markers of aging may provide a biological basis behind the vulnerability of certain subgroups of cancer patients to late effects. 3. Our network analysis identified fatigue as the leading component linking neurobehavioral outcomes and frailty, suggesting that interventions targeting fatigue may broadly improve physical and psychological health in this population. Our results provide the underlying basis to support physical activity as an effective intervention to prevent or delay the onset of frailty and improve the overall neuropsychological well-being of cancer survivors.

14605421.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14605421.value: At more than 10 years after cancer diagnosis, our study found that more than one fifth of young survivors of childhood cancer in Hong Kong were classified as “frail”, which is an aging-related syndrome of physiological decline. Being “frail” was associated with worse performance in the cognitive domains of attention and executive function, as well as symptoms of anxiety/depression and withdrawal problems. Survivors who were diagnosed with cancer at a young age were more likely to be “frail” and were associated with a shorter telomere length, which is a hallmark of biological aging. This may imply that early-onset cancer and treatment-induced DNA damage may reduce the cellular repair capacity, making younger survivors more susceptible to psychosocial and biological pathways to aging. Taken together, our findings may guide the development of interventions (e.g., exercise and dietary interventions) that can modify the aging pathway early in the cancer continuum. Early interventions may mitigate the adverse effects of frailty and aging, and potentially improve the survivors’ cognitive and behavioral functioning.

14606221.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14606221.value: 雙邊交易網絡中的配對和議價

14606221.label: Project Objectives
14606221.value: In this project, I will develop a game-theoretic model of decentralized matching and bargaining in buyer-seller networks. The model shall capture the key features of relevant real-life situations such as markets for firm mergers, patent acquisitions, land sales etc. In particular, I will incorporate in the model an innovative and tractable fully endogenous matching protocol that determines who bargains with whom, at what time. The first analytical task is to establish the existence of a Markov perfect equilibrium of the dynamic game using a standard fixed-point approach. Then, I will provide a complete characterization of the equilibrium outcome and identify its key properties such as efficiency and uniqueness. I aim to obtain a deep understanding of the strategic roles of the fully endogenous matching protocol in decentralized trading and identify the key differences between this protocol and the random matching protocol as well as the partially endogenous matching protocol in the existing literature. Another important goal of this study is to investigate whether the Walrasian price of a buyer-seller network, as defined in classic economic theory, can be sustained in a Markov perfect equilibrium of the dynamic game. Along this line, I will also investigate the validity of two related properties of the equilibrium outcome, namely, the equal treatment property and the path-independence property. An important research question in the study of social and economic networks is how network structure impacts the allocation of economic resources. In the context of buyer-seller networks, I will investigate via what channels and to what extent the network structure determines the trading prices. Finally, I hope that my theoretical study can produce some readily testable predictions so that in future research we can further investigate, through properly designed laboratory experiments, to what extent the game theoretic predictions are consistent with observable human behaviors.
