14611621.label: Major findings and research outcome
14611621.value: We conducted an international cross-sectional survey in six study areas (New Zealand, the U.K., the U.S., Hong Kong, Japan, and South Korea) to examine how people's political views, perceived social norms, and individualism shape their privacy concerns, perceived social benefits, and acceptance of ten COVID-19 control measures that use individual-level georeferenced data. We found a tradeoff relationship between people's privacy concerns and the acceptance (and perceived social benefits) of the control measures. People's perceived social tightness and vertical individualism are positively associated with their acceptance and perceived social benefits of the control measures, while horizontal individualism has a negative association. Further, people with conservative political views and high levels of individualism (both vertical and horizontal) have high levels of privacy concerns. Our results first suggest that people's privacy concerns significantly affect their perceived social benefits and acceptance of the COVID-19 control measures. Besides, our results also imply that strengthening social norms may increase people's acceptance and perceived social benefits of the control measures but may not reduce people's privacy concerns, which could be an obstacle to the implementation of similar control measures during future pandemics. Lastly, people's privacy concerns tend to increase with their conservatism and individualism. Further, the study found that people's privacy concerns in culturally tight societies (e.g., Japan) have the smallest negative impacts on their acceptance of pandemic control measures. The results also identify people's key views of specific control measures that can influence their views of other control measures. The impacts of these key views are heightened among participants with a conservative political view, high levels of perceived social tightness, and vertical individualism. Our results indicate that cultural factors are a key mechanism that mediate people's privacy concerns and their acceptance of pandemic control measures. These close inter-relationships lead to a double-edged sword effect: the increased positive impacts of people's acceptance and perceived social benefits also lead to increased negative impacts of privacy concerns in different combinations of control strategies. The findings highlight the importance of cultural factors as key determinants that affect people's acceptance or rejection of specific pandemic control measures.

14611621.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14611621.value: Our results indicate that people's privacy concerns tend to increase with their conservatism and individualism. Note that conservative groups are gaining influence in different countries (e.g., Brazil, France, Poland, Austria, Italy, Hungary, and Sweden) around the world, and there has been an upward trend in the levels of individualism across the world over the past few decades. Therefore, we concluded that it is likely that people's privacy concerns will keep rising with the global conservatism and individualism trends, and this would be a significant factor that influences the effectiveness of future efforts of pandemic control. Because we observed that vertical individualism has positive associations with acceptance and perceived social benefits of COVID-19 control measures, our results also highlight the importance of building stronger connections among individuals and strengthening social norms for controlling future pandemics. This is a promising area for future research.

14611621.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14611621.value: As the COVID-19 pandemic became a major global health crisis, many COVID-19 control measures that use individual-level georeferenced data (e.g., the locations of people's residences and activities) have been used in many countries around the world. Because these measures involve some disclosure risk and have the potential for privacy violations, people's concerns for geoprivacy (locational privacy) have recently heightened as a result, leading to an urgent need to understand and address the geoprivacy issues associated with COVID-19 control measures that use data on people's private locations. This project is the first major international study that examines people's geoprivacy concerns for and acceptance of ten COVID-19 control measures that use individual-level georeferenced data (IGD). It provides essential insights into people's acceptance of COVID-19 control measures and how public health agencies can better address the trade-off between disease control and geoprivacy protection. It also sheds light on what geoprivacy protection methods (e.g., geomasking) are likely to be effective for protecting the geoprivacy of infected persons while providing useful information to the general public. Such knowledge can help governments and public health agencies to identify and implement measures that would be more acceptable to people in specific social and cultural contexts.

14612621.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14612621.value: 透過建立個人資源和參與共融義務工作以提高年輕中風人士工作能力的成效：一項隨機對照試驗

14612621.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14612621.value: Prof Chau, Janita Pak-chun Dr Choi, Kai-chow Dr Demers, Marika

14612621.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14612621.value: Introduction The global prevalence of stroke in adults below 65 years old doubled in the past two decades. Returning to work is a major rehabilitation priority for young stroke survivors. Vocational interventions that modified work demands resulted in less than 50% of return-to-work rate among these survivors. Emerging evidence shows that enhancing self-efficacy, motivation and social skills, and volunteering may be promising to regain their work ability. Aim This project will investigate effects of a novel theory-driven 6-week virtual Personal Resource Building and Inclusive Volunteering Intervention (PVI) on young stroke survivors’ work ability, self-efficacy and psychosocial outcomes. Methods A 2-arm, assessor-blind, randomised controlled trial will be conducted. Individuals who are 18−64 years old, clinically diagnosed with a first-ever/recurrent ischaemic/haemorrhagic stroke, living at home, and unemployed for at least 3 months will be recruited from non-government organisations, support groups and District Health Centres. An estimated sample of 160 participants (80 per group) will be required. Eligible participants will be randomly assigned to receive usual care or PVI with usual care. PVI, grounded in Bandura’s principles of self-efficacy and outcome expectation, is a nurse-led virtual programme aimed to build up young survivors’ personal resources for work (self-efficacy, optimism, hope, social skills) through inclusive volunteering activities. It includes 2 training sessions followed by 4 3-hour sessions held weekly over 6 weeks. Participants will volunteer in singing activities with trained undergraduate students to promote peer survivors’ psychological well-being. Outcomes including work ability, self-efficacy, health-related quality of life, emotional well-being and social skills will be measured before PVI (T0), immediately post-PVI (T1) and 3 months post-PVI (T2). Analysis will be performed using intention-to-treat principle. Generalised estimating equations model will be used to compare differential changes in outcomes across time between two groups. Semi-structured interviews will be conducted with participants (intervention group) and undergraduate students to elicit feedback on PVI. Discussion and significance We expect that PVI will improve survivors’ work ability, self-efficacy, and psychosocial well-being. PVI will establish a new virtual vocational rehabilitation model for young stroke survivors through inclusive volunteering and be integrated into existing rehabilitation policies and services. The participating survivors and undergraduate students will form a new organised volunteer source to serve the community. Mutual health benefits and social inclusion in those with or without stroke are expected to be fostered. PVI would facilitate survivors’ resumption in paid/unpaid work to continue unleash their potential and hence their contribution to the society. 一些以調整工作需求為主的職業訓練措施只能協助部份年輕中風人士重返工作崗位。新出現的研究證據顯示提高自我效能、動力和社交技能，以及參與義務工作可幫助恢復中風人士的工作能力。 目的 此研究將評估一項新的、為期六週的虛擬個人資源建立和共融義務工作干預措施(PVI)對年輕中風人士的工作能力、自我效能和社會心理結果的影響。 方法 本研究將進行一項隨機對照試驗。年齡在18-64歲、臨床診斷為首次/復發性缺血性/出血性中風、在家居住且失業至少三個月的人士將從非政府組織、互助小組和地區健康中心招募。估計需要 160 名參與者（每組 80 人）。符合條件的參與者將被隨機分配接受常規護理或PVI加常規護理。PVI 以班杜拉的自我效能和結果預期原則為基礎，是一項由護士主導的虛擬計劃，旨在通過共融義務工作活動建立年輕中風人士的個人工作資源。包括工作能力、自我效能、與健康相關的生活質量、情緒健康和社交技能在內的結果將在PVI前(T0)、PVI (T1)和PVI後三個月(T2)進行測量。亦會與參與者（干預組）進行半結構化訪談，以獲取對PVI的意見。 討論與意義 我們期望PVI將提高中風人士的工作能力、自我效能和社會心理健康。PVI 將促進年輕中風人士重投有薪或無薪工作，以繼續釋放他們的潛能，為社會作出貢獻。

14613121.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14613121.value: When talking about barriers for ethnic minorities’ access to healthcare services, language is often highlighted as the most pervasive one. Yet an emerging field of research at the crossroads of linguistic, medical and psychological anthropology showed language challenges in healthcare are not merely about language itself; at stake is instead a different access to medical knowledge, a hegemonic communicative approach interwoven with histories of ethnic, class and gender inequality which ultimately hinders equal care. With its universal public healthcare inherited from the British colonial era combined with a thriving private health sector, Hong Kong's healthcare system aims at offering a comprehensive and efficient healthcare service to its residents. Under the Basic Law it guarantees an equal access to healthcare as well, regardless of the individual socioeconomic status, ethnicity or religion. Yet research shows that despite its facade of international and inclusive city, Hong Kong holds a hegemonic Chinese culture where ethnic discrimination is widespread; this is reflected as well in the health sector. South Asian ethnic minorities in particular are exposed to higher health risks and yet poorer access to care than the general population, yet their health care needs are largely ignored. The South Asian women are considered among the most marginalized: the intersection of ethnicity, class and gender mutually shapes an unequal access to care. Based on existing literature and our preliminary research on South Asian women’s health experiences, their being denial of participating into medical knowledge production under the hegemonic communicative approach becomes manifested in the form of language barriers which are seen as a major obstacle to their access to equal healthcare and a cry for the need to be heard. By engaging in a 24-month Community Based Participatory Action Research and in collaboration with a local ethnic minority service center, this study aims at providing a better understanding of the challenges South Asian diasporic women in Hong Kong face in health related issues and their actual health needs. The mixed-method design with parallel qualitative and quantitative methods, including an ethnography and surveys, are particularly apt to grasp these women’s lived experience through their life circles and the conflicts emerged in the medical encounter. A feminist intersectional approach will be adopted, in order to lay bare how different social identities such as gender, class and ethnicity intersect to shape South Asian women’s experience of wellbeing and suffering in Hong Kong and their uneven access to health care. 在談論少數族裔獲取醫療保健服務的問題時，語言往往被當作最爲普遍的障礙。然而，語言學、醫學和心理人類學等新興交叉領域的研究表明，語言給醫療保健領域所帶來的挑戰不僅僅只是和語言本身有關；實際上，因爲獲得醫學知識的途徑不同，那些與族裔、階級和性別不平等交織在一起的霸權交流方式，最終阻礙了照料的平等性。香港的醫療保健系統繼承了英國殖民時代的全民公營醫療保健，加上蓬勃發展的私營醫療保健部門，旨在為居民提供全面和高效的醫療保健服務。基本法也保證了不論個人的社會經濟地位、族裔或宗教，人人應得以平等地獲得醫療保健。然而研究表明，儘管香港有著國際化和包容性的城市面貌，但在一個以華人爲主導的社會中，族裔歧視依然普遍存在，醫療衛生系統也不例外，南亞少數族裔尤其如此。與一般人群相比，他們面臨著更高的健康風險，但其獲得醫療服務的機會更少；他們的醫療保健需求在很大程度上被忽視了。南亞裔婦女被認為是最為邊緣化的群體：族裔、階級和性別的相互交織共同阻礙了她們獲得平等照料的機會。根據現有文獻以及對南亞裔婦女醫療經驗的初步研究，我們發現，在霸權傳播方式下，她們被拒絕參與到醫學知識生產的過程中，而語言障礙作爲一個表象被呈現出來，被視為她們獲得平等醫療的主要障礙以及她們需要被傾聽的呼聲。通過為期 24 個月的社區參與式行動研究，並且與本地少數族裔服務中心合作，這項研究旨在更好地了解香港南亞裔婦女在健康相關問題上所面臨的挑戰以及她們真實的健康需求。本研究采取定性和定量相結合的混合研究方法，通過民族志和問卷調查來瞭解她們的生活圈子以及在尋醫問藥過程中所遭遇的衝突，從而捕捉這些女性真實的生活經歷。通過女權主義的交織性方法來揭示不同的社會身份（如性別、階級和族裔）如何相互作用，並藉此來探索南亞裔婦女在香港的健康福祉、遭遇以及她們在獲得醫療服務方面的不均衡性。

14613521.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14613521.value: This project is the first book-length attempt in English to offer a comprehensive examination of the significance of the Mawangdui tombs discovered in 1972. The main goal of this study is two fold. First, it tries to utilize materials found in the MWD tombs, whether texts or artifacts, to reconstruct the intellectual and religious world of the early Han. The issues discussed include the origin and nurturing of life, death and burial, the netherworld, conceptions of ghosts and spirits, immortality, political philosophy and government, art and technology, and the idea of history. Second, in the meantime, this project also tries to examine the methodological issues involved in doing such kind of reconstruction. How should one utilize archaeological material, or any material, to reconstruct a past moment? A conventional view of scholars of early history, whether Chinese or non-Chinese, regarding the use of archaeological materials is that they could supplement the written material to gain a better, or more complete, picture of past society. This is however only the basic level of understanding. The question needs to be asked beyond this basic understanding is, if or how archaeological material could “reflect” or “represent” the society that produced it. It is often assumed that the MWD tombs and their contents “reflect” the culture of early Han. Such kind of assumption or claim needs to be revised or fine-tuned. One cannot simply claim that the contents of the MWD tombs constitute a culturally homogeneous group of material that could “represent” a past moment in history. A more nuanced approach is to see each object and each text in the tombs as possessing its own history and cultural tradition. This means that the materials in the tombs do not and cannot represent or reflect a static moment of history, but a collection of burgeoning and moving traditions. This approach also shows that there was or is no fixed history that could be reflected by the archaeological materials. It shows the illusionary nature of the conception of a fixed History, because at any given moment in time there will always be numerous “little histories” represented by the individual material, each moving and progressing with its own speed. Thus this project is designed to both constructing and deconstructing history by the example of the MWD tombs. N/A

14613721.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14613721.value: 香港公立醫院醫生的故事：支持醫生工作的意義和價值觀念

14613721.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14613721.value: Work is made meaningful not just by its material rewards, but also by the values ascribed to it by practitioners. These values drive practitioners forward despite adverse conditions, and shape their work and careers. Work for doctors in public hospitals in Hong Kong combines structured professional codes of conduct, extensive contact with the public on whom they exercise a large impact, and an extremely stressful, high-stakes environment where they are pressed for time and resources. This combination makes the question of what human values and meanings sustain, nourish and improve their work an especially valuable area of research, with important social uses. Using interviews with public hospital medical doctors in Hong Kong who have worked in the sector for ten years or more, this study will explore how these doctors in Hong Kong understand their work and careers, examine the meanings and values they construct and ascribe to these, and investigate how they have coped with hardships and crises in their public hospital work. Revealing and studying the meanings and values that underpin such work, and the ways in which they have been built across time, can serve several purposes. They can provide invaluable guidance for medical students as they stand poised to start their own work journey. They can inform the practice of other doctors as they navigate similar issues in their own work. And they can provide an alternative reference for medical administrators as they seek to tackle the problems the public hospital sector faces. In addition, making the stories that appear in the interviews accessible to the public can shed rare light on the human dimensions of doctors’ public hospital work, increasing the public’s understanding of a profession that can seem closed off to them, but which is so crucial to their lives and wellbeing. The more flexible format of the partially structured interview that this study will use is crucial in the attainment of the aims, because it will allow doctors the flexibility to construct their own narratives of work. The interviews will be analyzed both thematically and narratively, with the results to be published for use by medical students, educators, doctors, and administrators. The narratives contained in the interviews will be edited and gathered into a published collection of doctors’ stories (with versions in English and Chinese) that will make the human aspects of medical work comprehensively accessible to the public for the first time. 此項研究將通過採訪在香港公立醫院有十年以上工作經驗的醫生 ，來探詢這些醫生如何理解他們的工作和職業，以及對其賦予哪些意義和價值觀念。研究的目的在於揭示支持醫生工作的價值觀念，及探討這些觀念如何隨著時間建立起來。發表的研究結果可供醫學生、教育者、醫生和醫療管理者之用。另外，醫生們的訪談故事將會被編輯成冊，讓公眾能更深入了解醫生在公立醫院的工作。

14614021.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14614021.value: 利用開放數據和機器學習重新思考空間規劃以改善大灣區城市的空氣質量

14614021.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14614021.value: Dr Ching, Jason Kwock Sung Prof Ng, Edward Yan-yung

14614021.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14614021.value: 本項目旨在全面定量地了解空間規劃對大灣區空氣質量的影響。 空氣污染已被世界衛生組織定性為對健康和可持續城市發展的嚴重環境威脅。合理的空間規劃可以通過發展一種將污染暴露最小化並增強污染物擴散的城市結構來改善城市空氣質量。因此，全面了解空間規劃如何影響城市空氣質量和污染暴露是規劃健康城市的關鍵。本研究利用開放數據和機器學習，重點量化空間規劃對城市空氣質量的影響。最近的研究強調了當代城市空間規劃與空氣污染之間聯繫的複雜性。迄今為止，僅有數量有限的關注量化這種複雜性的研究發表。由於化學傳輸模型和傳統統計方法的理想化假設和不確定性，目前大多數研究在準確量化這種複雜性方面仍然有限。迫切需要更全面地定量了解空間規劃對空氣質量的影響。在這個項目中，我們旨在填補這一重要的研究空白。 我們提議的研究將利用快速發展的機器學習和開放數據技術，以大灣區作為我們的研究區域。使用這些技術將使空間規劃和空氣質量之間的潛在模式和關聯能夠通過數據驅動技術而不是研究人員的假設來確定。具體而言，其目標是：（1）收集和整理來自區域監測網絡的空氣污染監測數據、氣象數據、衛星數據和地理空間數據，以及來自多個開放數據源的眾包數據； (2) 配置，準備並整合這些數據作為基於機器學習的時空空氣污染預測建模的輸入數據； (3) 通過機器學習開發時空預測模型，量化空間規劃對城市空氣質量的影響； (4) 將這些發現轉化為一系列可以進行知識轉移的空間規劃策略，供決策者參考。 該研究的結果將幫助城市規劃者從空氣質量考慮方面全面評估空間規劃。該研究將提供關於空間規劃和城市空氣質量之間相互作用的寶貴的新科學知識，並使當地在城市大氣環境治理方面的努力能夠與世界城市數據庫和訪問門戶工具的全球研究相結合。該研究還將豐富粵港澳三方在污染控制（大氣污染物擴散）和環境規劃發展戰略方面的持續合作。

14614221.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14614221.value: 一般語言學習能力的個體化認知神經標誌

14614221.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14614221.value: Prof Geng, Xiujuan Prof Wang, Suiping

14614221.label: Project Objectives
14614221.value: We aim to examine the behavior and brain mechanisms that drive individual differences in language learning profiles summarized by five components. Learning profile refers to each learner’s learning progress trajectory and attainment and across components of language (e.g., lexicon and syntax). An important aspect of language learning, especially when commenced later in life, is that each learner seems to have a unique learning profile. Individuals learning a new language differ significantly from each other not only in ultimate attainment but also in the speed of learning. Differences in attainment and speed occur not only in the learning of one component of language but can be observed across different components, since learning different components may be associated with common and different underlying cognitive and perceptual processes as well as neural substrates. We propose to conduct a multi-day language training experiment while cognitive assessments, structural and functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) are performed before and during learning. Learning profiles or the general language learning ability will be estimated by principal component analysis summarizing the learning trajectory and outcome across components. Multivariate predictive modeling will be conducted to assess to what extent the cognitive and neural predictors contribute to learning-profile prediction and identify the markers or “fingerprints” underlying individual learners’ general language learning ability. Another important objective is to test novel hypotheses and predictions of the neurobiology of language learning, which could shed light on neural mechanisms of language learning diversity. Previous neuroimaging studies have demonstrated that the prefrontal-hippocampus neural circuit engages in learning different aspects of a language. However, distributed multiple neural networks (e.g., Perisylvian, frontoparietal, and salience networks) beyond the prefrontal-hippocampus circuit have also been proposed to engage in learning and representing newly acquired linguistic knowledge. It is yet fully understood the roles of these networks in driving learning variability across learners. Additional recruitments of these networks are previously considered as by-products of less efficient processing or task-specific effects. Here, we hypothesize that these additional recruitments subserving neural fingerprints of learning (NFL) underlying inter-individual differences in learning profiles. This novel NFL hypothesis is derived from the Dynamic Systems Theory framework of second language learning, arguing multiple systems interact and dynamically contribute to language learning. The NFL predicts that structural properties and multivariate responses of these networks form neural fingerprints underlying inter-individual differences in learning profiles (prediction 1). Neural predisposition (i.e., pre-existing brain characteristics) and neural responses during training are hypothesized to be interrelated but partially separated in predicting learning profiles (prediction 2). We aim to test the NFL hypothesis and its predictions, especially regarding the single vs. multiple neural systems and comparisons of predisposition and training-related neural characteristics.

14614221.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14614221.value: Language learning differs significantly across individuals in both the learning process and outcome within and across different components (e.g., phonology, vocabulary and semantics, morphology, and syntax). The time to achieving a similar level of proficiency within the same component or across components of language also differs significantly. Although decades of research exploring the cognitive/social factors and neural substrates of language learning have identified distinct and overlapping factors and neural systems subserving different language components, it is far from understanding the sources of these large inter-individual differences in language learning. Here, we propose to examine whether and how cognitive characteristics and neural network patterns of individual learners contribute to predicting their learning profiles summarized from five components of language learning, including auditory category, vocabulary, morphology, phrase structure, and syntax. We hypothesize that the cognitive and neural characteristics serve as “fingerprints” underlying individuals’ learning profiles, which not only differentiates successful from less successful learners but also allows us to target each learner’s position in a continuous multidimensional space summarized by the learning components. We use a multi-day training protocol to capture learning profiles of the five components and acquire multimodal neuroimages before and during training together with a battery of cognitive assessments across two sites. We use predictive modeling analysis (e.g., Feng et. al., 2018b, PNAS) to examine to what extent the cognitive and neural features predict the overall learning profiles and component-specific performances. We target four critical language-relevant and domain-general brain networks, including the Perisylvian, frontoparietal, salience, and default-mode networks, and examine how the network responses contribute to individual differences in language learning. We aim to build component-general and -specific predictive models and identify the cognitive and neural fingerprints underlying individual learning profiles. This design and advanced statistical techniques not only allow us to test novel hypotheses and predictions of the neurobiology of language learning but also guide educational practice and clinical research by examining new training protocols for maximizing learning outcomes and minimizing individual differences. The findings derived from this project could be the first to attribute not only the degree of success but also patterns of language learning across components and learning progress, to cognitive characteristics and neural network dynamics. An understanding of these cognitive and neural patterns would allow us to understand why learners differ and will assist in designing personalized training or intervention protocol targeting their learning fingerprints. 學習不同的語言成分（例如，音韻學、詞彙和語義、形態學和句法），無論從過程和結果上看，個體之間都存在顯著差異。在同一語言成分內或跨語言成分之間能夠達到相似語言熟練程度所需的學習時間也有很大的個體間差異。儘管數十年來探索語言學習的認知與社會因素及其神經基礎的研究已經確定了多種關鍵因素以及支持不同語言成分的神經系統，但遠未瞭解語言學習中個體差異巨大的來源。本項目計劃考察學習者的個體認知特徵和神經網絡模式是否以及如何有助於預測他們學習不同語言成分的能力，包括聽覺類別、詞彙、形態、短語結構和句法。我們假設，認知和神經特徵能夠作為個體學習能力的標誌（如“指紋”），這不僅可以區分成功的學習者和不太成功的學習者，而且還使我們更精細地區分不同學習者在學習不同語言成分時的差異。我們採用為期多天的語言訓練程式來考察不同語言成分的學習情況，並在訓練前和訓練期間獲取多模態神經圖像以及一系列認知評估。我們計劃使用預測建模分析（Feng et al., 2018, PNAS）技術來研究認知和神經特徵在多大程度上能預測整體學習概況和特定語言成分的學習成績。我們針對四個關鍵的語言相關和領域通用的大腦網絡，包括 Perisylvian、frontoparietal、salience 和 default-mode 網絡，並研究這些網絡的神經反應模式如何導致語言學習的個體差異。本項目的目標是構建一般性和特定語言成分學習能力的預測模型，並確定學習能力個體差異背後的認知和神經“指紋”。本項目的實驗設計及其先進的統計技術應用不僅使我們能夠檢驗語言學習神經生物學的新假設及其預測，而且還有希望通過檢驗全新的語言培訓方案來指導教育實踐和臨床研究，以最大限度地提高語言學習效果和減少個體差異。本項目的潛在發現可能是第一個不僅將語言學習能力，而且還將跨語言成分的學習能力及其模式歸因於個體認知特徵和神經網絡模式的發現。瞭解這些認知和神經模式將使我們能夠瞭解學習者為何不同，並將有助於設計針對他們各自學習“指紋”的個性化語言訓練或幹預方案。

14614421.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14614421.value: 維根斯坦與荀子論跨文化理解和溝通

14614421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14614421.value: This project offers a comparative investigation of the early Wittgenstein, the later Wittgenstein and Xunzi (with the Tractatus, the Philosophical Investigations and the Xunzi as their representative works, respectively) on intercultural understanding and communication. Its provisional conclusion is that although the early and later Wittgenstein and Xunzi accept the possibility of locally incommensurable adequate languages, they hold that intercultural understanding and communication are possible. It also provides philosophical remarks on the similarities and differences of their views. In the Tractatus, the picture theory of language leads to the possibility of local incommensurability. For example, the picture of a pointing-in-cube and that of a pointing-out-cube can be regarded as belonging to two different languages, respectively, because one has a logical form its user cannot find it in another. In the Philosophical Investigations, a grammatical investigation of rule-following concludes that a rule is grasped in actual cases of “obeying the rule” and “going against it.” Rule-following consists in (general-)rule-governed use. Since two users with different forms of life may have different incommensurable rule-following activities, locally incommensurable languages are possible. However, although the early and later Wittgenstein accept the possibility of locally incommensurable languages, they hold that intercultural understanding and communication are possible. For the Tractatus, the logical form shared by the Subject and reality grounds the possibility of intercultural understanding and communication. For the Philosophical Investigations, the fact that the two users’ shared humanity is grounded by what is in common between their different forms of life guarantees that intercultural understanding and communication be possible. Xunzi defines the dao as that which is in itself constant and governs all changes—the general principle governing all instances of change. The sage, as knower of the dao, detaches his heart-mind from change. Thus, knowledge of the dao is possible only if “nomic transcendentalism” holds or that the heart-mind and Heaven share the same dao. He also offers a referential theory for both proper names and names of natural kind, such that naming grounds in the dao or, so to speak, in nomic transcendentalism. Thus, different Subjects can impose different conventional rules onto naming. Hence, locally incommensurable languages are possible. Nevertheless, the grounding of naming by the dao, or the common nomic nature of language (the Subject) and reality, guarantees that there is a core shared by different humanities—the dao, such that intercultural understanding and communication are possible. 本研究計劃旨在比較和探究，分别以《邏輯哲學論》、《哲學硏究》和《荀子》為代表的前期維根斯坦、後期維根斯坦和荀子有關跨文化理解和溝通的思想。它的暫定結論是，前後期維根斯坦和荀子均認為，雖然有局部不可通約的適切語言，但跨文化理解和溝通仍是可能的。本計劃亦會對他們的這些觀點及其異同作出哲學評論。 根據《邏輯哲學論》，語言圖像論帶出局部不可通約的可能性。例如，指向內立方體的圖像和指向外立方體的圖像可視為分別屬於不同語言，因為它們各自至少有一個邏輯形式，使得其使用者不能在另一語言中找到同樣的邏輯形式。另一方面，根據《哲學硏究》，我們可以從對遵從規則的文化考察，得出以下的結論：規則是在「遵從規則」和「違反規則」的實際項例中把握。換言之，遵從規則是（普遍的）規則支配之用。由於擁有不同生活形式的兩位語言使用者可以有不同的不可通約的遵從規則活動，所以局部不可通約語言是可能的。再者，雖然前後期維根斯坦都接受局部不可通約語言的可能性，他們均認為跨文化理解和溝通還是可能的。對於《邏輯哲學論》而言，跨文化理解和溝通的可能性立基於（grounds in）主體與真實共享的邏輯形式。對於《哲學硏究》而言，兩位語言使用者同享的人文性則立基於他們不同生活形式的共同部分，亦由此決定了，跨文化理解和溝通之可能性。 荀子定義「道」為「體常而盡變」者。道亦支配所有的變；即支配所有變的個例的最一般定律。聖人、作為「知道者」把他的心自外於一切變之個例。因此，若「法則超越論」成立；即心與天共同分有道，道之知識是可能的。此外，荀子亦提出了專名和自然類名項的語言指涉理論。根據這指涉理論，命名立基於道，或謂立基於「法則超越論」，所以不同主體可以加諸不同的約定法則於命名中。由此得出，局部不可通約語言是可能的。然而，道給予命名的立基，或語言（立體）與真實的共同法則性本質，保證了不同人文性之間共有一個核心；即道。所以，對於荀子而言，跨文化理解和溝通是可能的。

14615421.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14615421.value: 被遺忘的村莊：重新思考香港正在消失的遺產的框架

14615421.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14615421.value: Prof Cai, Ling Prof Ho, Puay Peng

14615421.label: Project Objectives
14615421.value: TYPOLOGICAL SURVEY: Prepare a typological survey of Hong Kong’s traditional villages within the New Territories. CASE STUDIES: Produce a comparative analysis of two case study rural villages within the New Territories. PROTOTYPE IMPLEMENTATION: Implement two architectural prototypes that focus on rural village revitalization by creating spaces of learning for the community. KNOWLEDGE EVALUATION: Evaluate the prototypes and establish a framework for rural village revitalization via direct educational and cultural engagement with the community.
rows: TYPOLOGICAL SURVEY: Prepare a typological survey of Hong Kong’s traditional villages within the New Territories.
CASE STUDIES: Produce a comparative analysis of two case study rural villages within the New Territories.
PROTOTYPE IMPLEMENTATION: Implement two architectural prototypes that focus on rural village revitalization by creating spaces of learning for the community.
KNOWLEDGE EVALUATION: Evaluate the prototypes and establish a framework for rural village revitalization via direct educational and cultural engagement with the community.

14615421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14615421.value: Hong Kong is a complex city in constant transition. The byproduct of this condition of flux is a culture of disappearance (Abbas, 1997) non more evident than when you consider the state of the territories’ traditional villages. Hong Kong’s indigenous villages are vanishing at an unprecedented rate, rural settlements that have defined Hong Kong’s culture for centuries have become extinct, condemned by rampant urbanization and rigid countryside policies. This design research proposal investigates the possibility to reactivate, via a series of educational prototypes, two distinct traditional villages within the New Territories district of Hong Kong. The New Territories of Hong Kong represents an “independent territory” (Watson, 1983) that has separated Hong Kong Island and Kowloon from Mainland China since 1898. Within this dissolved urban/rural hinterland lie the vestiges of hundreds of indigenous traditional villages belonging to three distinct ethnic groups: Cantonese, Hakka and boat people. Following the New Town developments of the 1980-1990s, villagers rapidly migrated or abandoned their settlements leaving behind an ancient heritage that today exists under the shadows of 60-storey housing estates. At a moment when Hong Kong villages are fated to become mere tourist attractions (Sinclair, 2007), it is our thesis that traditional settlements offer the possibility for much needed social interaction, emotional reconnection and the fostering of a sense of place that its anonymous housing estates lack. Although many village regeneration programmes currently exist within Hong Kong, most focus on reestablishing traditional life by encouraging people to return. This proposal believes that an alternative sustainable source of life is needed that engages the wider community through direct participation. Rather than villages being static monuments to a bygone era, they have the potential to become dynamic vehicles that reconnect the wider population with their heritage. Traditions are passed on via direct engagement with the local culture, with the prototype being a vessel for change (Ferretto & Cai, 2020), villages can become spaces for learning, opportunities to reconnect with the collective memory and reflect on the city’s insatiable need to develop. Two traditional settlements have been identified as study areas for the research, Luk Keng and Yim Tin Tsai, representing a spectrum of rural conditions within the North Territories. By developing a community learning prototype for each, we aim to connect young people with the inherent sense of value and beauty integral to rural villages and in the process help prevent Hong Kong from becoming a village-less city. 香港是一個不斷轉型的複雜城市。這種流動狀況的副產品是一種消失的文化（Abbas，1997），當您考慮這些地區傳統村莊的狀況時，這種文化最為明顯。香港的原住民村落正以前所未有的速度消失，幾個世紀以來定義香港文化的鄉村聚落因猖獗的城市化和僵化的鄉村政策而滅絕。該設計研究方案探討了通過一系列教育原型重新激活香港新界區內兩個截然不同的傳統村莊的可能性。 香港新界代表了自 1898 年以來將香港島和九龍與中國大陸隔開的“獨立領土”（Watson，1983）。不同的族群：廣東人、客家人和船民。 隨著 1980-1990 年代新市鎮的發展，村民們迅速遷移或放棄了他們的定居點，留下了今天存在於 60 層住宅區陰影下的古老遺產。在香港村莊注定成為純粹的旅遊景點的時刻（Sinclair，2007），我們的論點是，傳統聚居地為急需的社會互動、情感重新聯繫和培養地方感提供了可能性莊園缺乏。 雖然香港目前有許多鄉村復興計劃，但大多數側重於通過鼓勵人們返回來重建傳統生活。該提案認為，需要一種替代的可持續生活來源，通過直接參與來吸引更廣泛的社區。村莊不是過去時代的靜態紀念碑，而是有可能成為動態工具，將更廣泛的人口與其遺產重新聯繫起來。傳統通過與當地文化的直接接觸得以傳承，原型是變革的載體（Ferretto & Cai，2020），村莊可以成為學習的空間、與集體記憶重新聯繫的機會，並反思城市對城市永無止境的需求發展。 兩個傳統定居點已被確定為研究的研究區域，即鹿坑和鹽田仔，代表了北領地的一系列農村條件。通過為每個人開發社區學習原型，我們旨在將年輕人與鄉村固有的價值感和美感聯繫起來，並在此過程中幫助防止香港成為無鄉村城市。

14615421.label: Realisation of objectives
14615421.value: This design by research project into the forgotten rural villages of Hong Kong, focuses on their community structures, built environment, and their significance in contemporary life. It includes field research, educational courses, and community workshops that explore the preservation of rural heritage. Despite challenges during prototype implementation, valuable insights on heritage conservation were gained and shared through academic channels. OBJECTIVE 01: TYPOLOGICAL SURVEY (100% COMPLETED) This objective focused on conducting a typological survey of Hong Kong's traditional villages in the New Territories. The research included historical analysis using archival maps and field research to understand the villages' evolution from social, geographical, and economic perspectives. The study also examined the villages' integration into the surrounding urban environment through macro analysis, mapping the villages' layout, documenting architectural heritage, and creating a typological atlas for future research and heritage conservation efforts. This comprehensive approach provided insights into how these villages have adapted to contemporary urban development and the ongoing significance of their architectural heritage in everyday village life. Please refer to the attached graphic appendix. OBJECTIVE 02: CASE STUDIES (100% COMPLETED) Objective 02 involved conducting a comparative analysis of two rural villages in the New Territories through case studies. The first case study focused on Luk Keng village, examining its landscape, physical development, cultural heritage, and intangible practices such as farming and bamboo weaving. It also explored the village's abandoned status and potential opportunities for sustainable development. The second case study centred on Yim Tin Tsai village, investigating its rich Hakka cultural traditions, Catholic missionary heritage, salt production practices, and the ecological significance of the surrounding mangrove habitat. Both case studies employed a multi-dimensional approach to highlight the unique historical, social, and environmental aspects of each village; detailed information is available in the graphic section of the attached report. Four educational workshops were organised in this phase. The process of conducting case studies facilitated deeper engagement with local villagers in Yim Tin Tsai and collaboration with the local NGO, Salt and Light Preservation Centre. This partnership enabled the organisation of workshops involving over 40 students from the CUHK School of Architecture. Centred on traditional wall-building techniques, the workshops offered students valuable hands-on experience alongside local craftsmen, fostering intergenerational knowledge exchange. The outcome of these workshops was the creation of the project’s first prototype: the restoration of a traditional Hakka stone wall (see Section 3.6). Through these workshops, the research team was able to identify potential craftsmen who could continue to contribute to the design and production of the prototype. Furthermore, a suitable site for prototype implementation was selected, laying a solid foundation for the next phase of the project. The knowledge and skills acquired through these workshops were directly applied to the design and development of the prototype, illustrating the practical impact of this collaborative educational initiative. For this phase, we also produced a feasibility report that combines research findings from the project team and educational courses, detailed in Section 3.4. A public exhibition was organised featuring panels where the research was presented to the public and expert reviewers, where the team received feedback on proposals aimed at addressing challenges faced by Hong Kong villages. This collaborative process encouraged dialogue among the research team, students, faculty, and professionals across disciplines, fostering a deeper understanding of rural preservation complexities and inspiring creative solutions for safeguarding Hong Kong's unique heritage, as outlined in Section 3.4. OBJECTIVE 03: PROTOTYPE IMPLEMENTATION (100% COMPLETED) The team completed three prototype schematic designs, each offering innovative interpretations of rural heritage by blending historical context with contemporary architectural thinking. These designs included a prism architectural installation symbolising fragmented heritage perceptions, a drawing machine that captures the traces of intangible heritage values and local memories, and a final design that focused on rethinking the Hakka dwelling and traditional building techniques such as mud bricks as the primary construction material. Despite unsuccessful funding attempts (Countryside Conservation Funding Scheme -refer to attached application), the team consulted local craftsmen and villagers to refine the prototypes, with one prototype involving the repair of a Hakka stone wall at Yim Tin Tsai. While Prototypes B and C were not implemented on site due to financial and regulatory constraints, they were fabricated at CUHK School of Architecture. Prototype B, named Heritage Trace, Drawing Machine, was recognised in the “Dezeen Awards 2022” for its innovative approach to capturing ephemeral moments through wind-powered drawing devices. The third prototype, Brick Pavilion, aimed to revitalise village culture through mud-brick construction, inspiring a subsequent project, the “Hakka Mud Library”, that is currently being constructed in He Xin Wu, Guangdong Province, to sustain Hakka culture as a living heritage through architectural design. OBJECTIVE 04: KNOWLEDGE EVALUATION (90% COMPLETED) Objective 04 focused on evaluating prototypes to establish a framework for rural village revitalisation through direct community engagement. The evaluation process included assessing performance, material durability, and user interaction for prototypes B (Heritage Trace, Drawing Machine) and C (Brick Pavilion), leading to design modification and new strategies of implementation. A detailed breakdown of the evaluation is given in the graphic appendix. The framework emphasises active processes of making and doing to generate knowledge, demonstrated through stakeholder engagement, public recognition, and construction experiences that inform both theory and practice in heritage preservation and architectural innovation. The dissemination plan involved presenting research outcomes at conferences, the PI was invited to be a keynote speaker at a government organised conference (Countryside Conservation Conference 2023); the PI has also applied to a series of other international conferences which are still in the process of being presented (see submitted abstracts) to engage with diverse audiences and inform future research agendas, highlighting the adaptability and effectiveness of the framework in various contexts. Additionally, papers submitted for publication in Architecture and Culture and Built Heritage (currently under review- see attached paper) critically reflect on the methodologies and outcomes of the research, offering insights into participatory action research and varied approaches to heritage revitalisation through prototype implementation.

14615421.label: Major findings and research outcome
14615421.value: 1. UNDERSTANDING THE REASONS FOR RURAL VILLAGE ABANDONMENT: By conducting a detailed analysis of eight rural villages in Hong Kong, each characterised by unique cultural and environmental contexts, the study produced a heritage documentation that highlights the importance of traditional architecture, social dynamics, and natural ecosystems. The research revealed that by actively involving the local community, a deeper understanding of why the settlements have become forgotten can be acquired, and at the same time, demonstrating how the complex cultural heritage of each village can help revitalise both tangible and intangible traditions. 2. DEVELOPING DESIGN STRATEGIES FOR RURAL REVITALISATION: With few inhabitants residing in these neglected villages, we have recognised that the transformation of these perceived problem villages into assets for the broader urban community is essential. By creatively repurposing existing structures through design to showcase the cultural richness of the village, we aim to preserve intangible heritage and memories that are at risk of fading away. Integrating these efforts with local ecosystems, our design prototypes have gained recognition for their innovative approaches, earning international awards such as the Dezeen Design Award. Through workshops like the “Mud wall building” organised together with village residents, the research has championed community engagement, emphasising the importance of respecting and listening to the residents. 3. ADDRESSING POTENTIAL CHALLENGES AND CONFLICTS: A significant hurdle we faced was the constraint of limited finances, which affected our plans to construct the prototype at the Yim Tin Tsai site following the rejection of our application for the Countryside Conservation Funding Scheme. To overcome this setback, we developed the design within our School of Architecture, showcasing the design potential of our proposal and, in tandem, developing relationships with key stakeholders. This involved actively involving the village administration board to establish a foundation for future collaboration. 4. DEVELOPING A FRAMEWORK FOR SUSTAINABLE RURAL DEVELOPMENT: This research develops a framework for heritage revitalisation that focuses on generating knowledge through doing. The framework consists of three core strategies, including: 1) Stakeholder engagement, 2) Public recognition, and 3) hands-on construction of design prototypes, which are implemented through participatory workshops, international awards, and direct building experiences, respectively.

14615421.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14615421.value: This project explores how design prototypes can drive rural development. By establishing a structured methodology for participation and public engagement, the research has successfully secured heritage revitalisation projects beyond Hong Kong. Moving forward, there is significant potential for collaborative endeavours between Hong Kong and mainland China, facilitating knowledge exchange. The team believes that initiatives such as “Revitalising Forgotten Villages” can yield substantial social impact at the community level. In this respect, we aim to continue collaborating with the Salt and Light Preservation Centre on Yin Tin Tsai island, known for hosting bi-annual cultural performances where participants are encouraged to design prototypes and pavilions. Additionally, the project also envisions future partnerships with the Countryside Conservation Office, which has already expressed interest in exploring abandoned sites in Hong Kong, such as Green Island.

14615421.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14615421.value: This research project delves into the forgotten rural villages of Hong Kong, aiming to study their community structures and built environments to understand their importance in the city's contemporary life. Through field research, educational courses, and community workshops, the project explores heritage preservation in rural areas. Despite challenges faced during prototype implementation, valuable insights on heritage conservation were gained and shared through academic channels. The project's objectives included conducting a typological survey of traditional villages, analysing their evolution and integration into rural settings. Case studies were conducted on Luk Keng and Yim Tin Tsai villages, exploring their cultural heritage and potential for sustainable development. Educational workshops facilitated engagement with local communities and resulted in the creation of prototypes like the restoration of a traditional Hakka stone wall. Prototype designs merged historical context with contemporary architectural thinking, leading to innovative interpretations of rural heritage. Despite funding constraints, the team refined designs with local input, resulting in recognition at the Dezeen Awards. The project's framework emphasises public engagement, recognition, and construction to inform heritage preservation practices. The dissemination plan includes presenting research outcomes at conferences and submitting a paper for publication, reflecting on methodologies and outcomes of the research.

14615721.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14615721.value: This study investigates the potential benefits of sign language learning for hearing elderly in Hong Kong. Our first set of research questions concerns the potential cognitive benefits of learning sign language at an old age. Previous studies suggest that cognitively stimulating activities like reading and computer games enhance cognitive performance in the elderly (Belleville et al. 2011). There is also growing evidence that the practice of bilingualism brings cognitive benefits, including delaying the onset of dementia (Craik et al. 2010). Building on these two lines of research, recent investigations have explored whether foreign (spoken) language learning improves the cognitive abilities of older adults, with positive preliminary outcomes (e.g., Wong et al. 2019). However, no studies have examined if cognitive benefits arise from learning a sign language. Sign languages are natural languages with complex grammars, and should be equally stimulating. Furthermore, sign languages are visual-gestural in nature. Comprehending signs requires attention to not just the manual signals but also facial expressions and body movements. Sign articulation involves precise placements of the manual articulators in 3-dimensional space. Will sign language learning strengthen visual-spatial skills of the hearing elderly? Our second set of research questions focuses on the potential psychological and social benefits. Previous studies argue that foreign language learning can enhance social interactions, self-esteem and autonomy among older adults. As most elderly suffer from hearing deterioration, and sign language can supplement their verbal communications with others, sign language learning may alleviate the risk factors for depression and social isolation, which are common among the elderly. Will exposure to sign language broaden their horizons, particularly regarding the understanding of the Deaf community as a linguistic minority, thus fostering a more positive attitude towards deafness and sign language? Three groups (~60 each) of hearing elderly will be recruited. Group I will participate in sign language classes for six months. Workshops will be offered to them and their relatives/caretakers to explain the usefulness of signs when hearing deteriorates. Group II will receive the same duration of training on using tablet computers (e.g., Chinese input, social media, basic Apps). Group III will receive no training. Cognitive tests will be given to all groups right before (pre-test) and after the training (post-test), and three months after the training is completed (follow-up). Questionnaires and interviews will be conducted to determine if sign language learning can improve psychological well-being and foster a positive attitude towards deafness and sign language. 本研究將探討香港健聽長者學習手語的潛在益處。我們的第一組研究問題主要關注年長時學習手語的潛在認知益處。過往研究表明，閱讀和電腦遊戲等刺激認知的活動可以提高長者的認知能力（Bellevilleet al. 2011）。也有越來越多的證據表明，雙語能力會令認知獲益，包括延緩癡呆症的開始時間（Craik et al. 2010）。基於這兩個研究方向，最近的研究探討了外語（口語）學習是否能改善長者的認知能力。初步研究結果肯定了這一方向（例如，Wong et al. 2019）。然而，目前未有研究探討過學習手語是否會帶來認知上的益處。手語是自然語言，文法複雜，應該同樣可以刺激認知發展。此外，手語的本質是視覺及動作化的。理解手語不僅需要注意手部動作，還需要注意面部表情和身體動作。手語的表達要求在三維空間中精確的擺放雙手位置。手語學習是否會加強健聽長者的視覺空間技能？ 我們的第二組研究問題集中在潛在的心理和社會效益方面。過往研究認為，外語學習可以增強老年人的社會交往、自尊心和自主性。由於大多數老年人會出現聽力退化，而手語可以對他們與他人的口頭交流進行補充，因此，手語學習可能會減輕老年人常見的抑鬱症和社會孤立等風險。接觸手語是否會拓寬他們的視野，特別是對聾人群體作為語言少數群體的理解，從而培養出對聾人和手語更積極的態度？ 我們將招募三組健聽長者，每組約60人。第一組將參加為期六個月的手語課程。我們將為長者及其親屬或照顧者提供工作坊，講解在聽力下降時手語的作用。第二組將接受相同時間的平板電腦使用培訓（例如，中文輸入、社交媒體、基本應用程式等）。第三組則不會接受培訓。所有組別都將在進行三次認知測試，包括培訓前（前測），培訓後（後測），以及培訓結束後的三個月內（跟進）。我們也會進行問卷調查和訪問，以確定手語學習是否能改善心理健康，培養對聾人和手語的積極態度。

14616221.label: Project Objectives
14616221.value: Review of conventional teaching pedagogies, learning objectives and student performance among Hong Kong architecture studio courses in context of ‘making culture’. 14616221.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14616221.value: Traditional architectural education is grounded in “creating sublime architecture that is personal” (Spiller 2014) and “accessible from an intimate and evolving relation among a site, materials and tools” (Harrop, 2007). 2020 saw COVID-19 change education globally – replacing face to face learning with online education platforms. The impact of this is heavily felt in studio-based subjects such as architecture and visual arts, whereby the risk of working exclusively within the digital environment can create “an illusion of rigour, which obscures the role of active critical assessment” (REISER, UMEMOTO, 2014). These disciplines are grounded in the creation of haptic knowledge through material experimentation, fabrication, assembly, and the promotion of design thinking in students through action learning experiences. Studio-based coursework in architecture is unique in developing essential qualities among students, summarized as ‘making culture’ in this study. They include craftsmanship, design thinking, problem solving, and adoption of an action-based iterative approach (Fingrut, 2019). Pedagogical approaches in studio are designed to mimic similar environments found in professional practice and are considered “ubiquitous in the discipline and associated somewhat uniquely with the profession” (Shulman, 2005). This study focuses on the “signature pedagogy” (Shulman, 2005) of design studio as deployed through assignments, projects and programmes highlighting knowledge development through peer learning, skills development through action based learning and professional preparation. The objectives of this study are: (A) review of conventional teaching pedagogies, learning objectives and student performance among Hong Kong architecture studio courses in the context of ‘making culture’. (B) Compare and contrast those traditional pedagogies, learning objectives and student performance with adaptations generated through eLearning that evolved during COVID-19. (C) Synthesize and report findings from the previous points that consider teaching approaches and student achievement of learning objectives. The pandemic compelled teachers and students to expand their adoption of digital technology. Reactions to the ‘new normal’ will expand our knowledge of the relationship between technology adoption, teaching, student performance and aptitude for problem solving across disciplines. This project investigates ‘creative design methods’ in the context of online learning. The necessity for social distancing presents an opportunity to add broad knowledge in how subjects grounded in physical making pedagogies have adapted to remote teaching and eLearning. It highlights how technology can be a conduit for the cultivation of knowledge gained through iterative design. 14616421.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14616421.value: 大數據還是大搶地？ 中國內陸“數穀”大數據主題類土地開發的話語-物質關聯性分析

14616421.label: Co - Investigator(s)

14616421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14616421.value: With the rise of big data, new information technologies and smart cities are buzzwords reshaping societies in multiple ways around the globe. Inquiries into the urban digital turn and their consequences have become increasingly urgent. Data-centred programs are mushrooming in China, a country hosting over 500 smart cities, nine centrally-designated big data pilot zones, and numerous local digital experiments. They bring about a myriad of new practices which take the digital, as both material technologies and abstract ideas, as the pivotal focus in developing, governing and envisioning Chinese cities. Such changes have momentous implications. No systematic research has yet been offered for these new developments. This project proposes to address the research gap by studying the big data-themed land development (BDTLD) to make sense of the unfolding relationship between data and cities. China’s land supply for urban construction is under an ever-tightening top-down control and fiercely contested by different land demands. Yet, in many Chinese cities, we are witnessing an extravagant boom of BDTLD. This phenomenon provokes an interesting question: How can BDTLD succeed in obtaining land in a land-scarce context? The research proposes the ‘discursive–material nexus’ notion to argue that bringing BDTLD into fruition is not simply an act of supplying and producing land in favour of the big data sector in material terms. It is also a process of discursive construction to justify the manner of disposing land for big data initiatives and defend the legitimacy of this manner. This perspective diverges from the dominant material-oriented view of China’s land development, and the technocentric, decontextualised and nonreflexive analytical approach on China’s big data ambitions. The project will thus contribute to scholarly debates in two realms – the politics of China’s land development, and the salience of big data to urban development. To exemplify our argument, the research team will explore BDTLD in Guizhou, China’s first national big data pilot zone where big data-based urban imaginaries are unprecedentedly reshaping this land-scarce province. Quantitative and qualitative research methods will be used. An analytical framework grounded upon the critical discourse analysis approach will be deployed to study the interplay between the actual BDTLD on the ground and related discourses. Findings will be deployed to theorise China’s land development with the notion of discursive–material nexus. Empirical data (e.g. a dataset of big data firms) will be used to analyse how big data are reshaping urban growth on the ground. 大數據、新一代信息技術和智慧城市已經成為全球流行用語，正多方位地重塑人類社會。這種城市數字化轉向及其影響是學術界急待研究的課題。在中國，以數據為中心的發展如雨後春筍般出現。中國共有500個智慧城市、9大國家級大數據綜合實驗區和眾多地方數字化試點，從技術實體到抽象概念都極大地影響著中國城市的發展、管治和願景。而系統性的研究還未曾開始探討這種新趨勢帶來的深遠影響。為填補此項空白，本項目主要分析”以大數據為主題的土地開發”(BDTLD)，瞭解數據與城市所展現出來的關係。 中國城市建設用地供應日趨受到自上而下的嚴格管控，不同用地類型之間競爭激烈。但是時下在許多中國城市，BDTLD奢侈之風盛行。這帶來一個有趣的問題：在建設用地稀缺的大背景下，BDTLD為何能夠成功拿地？本研究提出“話語-物質關聯性”概念，用以佐證BDTLD的蓬勃發展，不能只簡單理解為實際用地供應和土地開發向大數據產業傾斜，而應該認識到這也是合理化與合法化這種傾斜的話語建構過程。這種視角區別於以往只重視中國土地開發實體過程的研究，也不同於只注重技術環節、不關心現實背景的非自反性大數據研究方法。因此，本項目推動了兩個方面的學術討論。一是中國土地開發政治；二是大數據對城市發展的影響。 為了論證以上觀點，研究團隊選取貴州BDTLD作為案例。貴州是首個中國大數據綜合實驗區，圍繞大數據的城市發展正史無前例地重塑這個土地資源稀缺的省份。本研究通過對定量和定性方法的應用，基於批判性話語分析方法建立分析框架，用以探討BDTLD的實際落地過程和相關話語之間的關係。 研究成果將有利於用“話語-物質關聯性”概念完善中國土地開發的相關理論。實證數據（如大數據企業數據庫）可用於分析大數據如何重塑城市發展。

14617121.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14617121.value: In modern policy evaluations, the increasing availability of rich datasets (such as massive administrative data, large survey data, etc.) with many individual features (variables) makes the estimation and inference on the heterogeneous or even personalized treatment effect an urgent task for theoretical econometricians and empirical economists. The accurate estimation of heterogeneous treatment effect is important for efficient policy making and social welfare evaluations. The economic policy, e.g., government bailout of small business or individuals during the hardship of COVID-19, would affect people with different economic variables such as debt levels, education, etc., differently. Estimation and inference on the potentially heterogeneous treatment effect is therefore important for modern program evaluations. This project aims to develop econometric methods to deal with the common issues of causal inference in the form of treatment effect, such as heterogeneity, endogeneity, censored response variable, etc., amid large dimension of control variables and potential instruments. On one hand, more data provides the researchers more information on the subject of their study. On the other hand, it makes the conventional econometric methods infeasible to handle the high-dimensionality nature of the model. Specifically, this research project aims to study the average causal effect using double robustness method that relies on new machine learning methods. We consider the conditional average treatment effect and quantile treatment effect among censored response variables in a high-dimensional model. To address the endogeneity problem we consider a large number of instrumental variables and rely on the variable selection to get the optimal instruments. We also empirically investigate the effect of the firm culture on corporate behavior. The novelty of our proposed method is that we first investigate the heterogeneous treatment effect with high-dimensional data and complex data structure such as censored response. We innovatively use the dimension reduction technique, taking into account the censored nature of the responses. Then a double robust method is applied to the nonparametric estimation of the heterogeneous treatment effect. Moreover, we consider the both irrelevant and invalid instruments in high-dimensional models. The results of our study will be of practical use to policy makers, empirical economics researchers and biomedical researchers, etc., providing solutions to the complex data structure when evaluating the heterogeneous treatment effects. We advance the academic literature at the intersection of high-dimensional models, heterogeneous treatment effect, double robust estimation, instrumental variable method, by providing insights on how to make valid inference on the true parameter/functional of interests. 在現代化的政策評估研究當中，越來越豐富的海量數據對因果推斷的理論建模、對政策效果對於不同個體的異質性研究和福利分析都帶來了新的挑戰。例如，政府在COVID-19的困難時期對小微企業和居民的財政救助政策，可能對於不同的企業和個人會產生不同的實際效果：在某種程度上，如果考慮到企業自身的信貸狀況和營業模式，個人的教育水平、年齡、性別等等因素，在“一刀切”的政策下，這些不同的群體可能會有不一樣的最終的福利結果。本課題主要想解決因果推斷的計量經濟學模型當中的異質性、內生性等問題，並考慮到數據本身含有非常多的變量。高維數據一方面給研究者提供了更多信息，但另一方面也使得模型變得複雜（例如存在刪失數據、模型選擇的不確定性增大），這也使得許多經典的低維度計量經濟模型不再適用。基於上述原因，本項目將用新的機器學習方法來研究平均“療效”和異質性（給定某個特徵或者是分位數）因果效應。從理論的角度，探索這些估計量的雙重穩健性質並解決政策干預的內生性等問題。本課題還將研究一些實際的經濟問題，例如公司治理的問題。

14617121.label: Realisation of objectives
14617121.value: The research proposal aimed to advance econometric methods for causal inference focusing on treatment effect and instrumental variable models under high-dimensionality, with the main methodological objectives: (1) developing econometric methods for the inference of heterogeneous treatment effects that account for complex data features such as censored data, (2) proposing an IV selection and inference procedure robust to weak and potentially endogenous IVs, and (3) applying the proposed methods to real data and evaluating heterogeneous treatment effects in various empirical problems. The PI is very grateful for the support from RGC, which significantly expedited the progress of the project. Two papers, Li et al. (2024), referred to as Output 3, and Fan and Wu (2024), referred to as Output 2, published in Statistics and Probability Letters and The Review of Economics and Statistics, respectively, directly address these objectives. An empirical study of peer effect of single child in learning outcomes, as in the paper of Cai et al. (2022), referred to as Output 1, is published in Labour Economics. Specifically, Objective 1: Developing Econometric Methods for Inference of Heterogeneous Treatment Effects Accounting for Complex Data Features Such as Censored Data. The first objective sought to develop methods for inferring heterogeneous treatment effects in settings with complex data structures, particularly censored outcomes. Both papers make significant strides in this direction by tackling challenges in estimation and inference under censoring and heterogeneity. Li et al. (2024) addresses the identification and estimation of average causal effects in censored regression models with endogenous treatments. The paper introduces a novel variable selection method, the censored outcome adaptive Lasso (COAL), extending prior work on outcome-adaptive Lasso to handle censoring by incorporating weighted least squares. It relaxes assumptions like unconfoundedness by integrating inverse probability weighting and non-informative censoring, enabling robust inference via perturbation-resampling for variance approximation. The approach utilizes censored data to recover full effects, with algorithms ensuring computational efficiency in high-dimensional covariates. Simulations and an empirical application to job training programs on wage outcomes (with censoring at thresholds) demonstrate superior performance over existing methods like OAL and IPTW, especially in finite samples with moderate censoring rates. Fan and Wu (2024) complements this by proposing a robust IV estimator for heterogeneous effects in data-rich environments with mixed covariates, allowing for weak signals and fixed effects. The method employs a three-step adaptive Lasso approach with orthogonal projections to mitigate bias from censoring-like complexities, enhancing efficiency in mixed settings. Empirical illustrations on trade interventions show its ability to uncover subgroup effects missed by standard models. Both papers advance methods for heterogeneous effects under censoring, with Output 1 emphasizing estimation and Output 2 focusing on robustness, collectively ensuring valid inference in complex data scenarios. The objective is substantially achieved, though further work could explore dynamic censoring or nonparametric extensions. Objective 2: Proposing an Instrumental Variable Selection and Inference Procedure Robust to Weak and Potentially Endogenous IVs. The second objective aimed to propose an IV selection and inference procedure robust to both weak and potentially endogenous IVs. Fan and Wu (2024) directly addresses this through a comprehensive selection framework. The paper develops a three-step adaptive Lasso method that handles weak and endogenous IVs by leveraging a "majority rule" among relevant instruments, extending prior work on sisVIVE (Kang et al., 2016) to accommodate irrelevant IVs. This approach ensures robustness by incorporating elastic-net initial estimators and BIC tuning, allowing selection without prior validity knowledge. Unlike prior methods (e.g., Kang et al., 2016; Windmeijer et al., 2019), which assume all IVs are relevant, the proposed procedure aggregates information from weak IVs for inference, as shown in theorems on oracle properties, using post-selection estimators like debiased OLS for asymptotic normality. Simulation results indicate that the R2IVE method outperforms sisVIVE and ALasso in high-dimensional settings, with lower selection error rates and improved Mean Squared Error (MSE). The empirical application to trade and growth with mixed IVs validates its robustness, providing stable estimates despite endogenous and weak instruments. Objective 3: Applying the Proposed Methods in Real Data and Evaluating Heterogeneous Treatment Effects in Various Empirical Problems. The third objective was to apply the proposed methods to real data and evaluate heterogeneous treatment effects across empirical contexts. Fan and Wu (2024) fully achieve this through extensive applications. The paper applies the robust IV estimator to datasets from development economics (e.g., trade policies on growth with mixed IVs) and labor economics (e.g., education on earnings), revealing heterogeneous effects by subgroups like regions or firm sizes. Theorems on identification establish uniform confidence bands for effect distributions, enabling policy-relevant inferences. The analyses show significant heterogeneity, such as stronger growth effects for low-income countries, where traditional average treatment effect estimators understate impacts. Li et al. (2024) supplements this with applications to biomedical studies (e.g., treatment programs on survival outcomes with censored data), detecting varying effects by patient characteristics. Both papers demonstrate practical utility, with results highlighting policy implications like targeted interventions. Regarding additional empirical pursuits, the PI has explored several datasets across finance and health economics, though findings were mixed due to data limitations. A working paper is drafted, but publication is pending refinements. The PI will continue in this area, shifting emphasis to methodological innovations. For broader impact, the PI has developed user-friendly software packages on GitHub, including codes for COAL and the robust IV estimator, with manuals and examples. The PI thanks the generous support from the RGC again, and hopes practitioners will adopt these methods for causal inference in observational studies. Supplementary Remarks: Justifications of Output 1 and Output 3 The core data collection, theoretical and empirical analysis of Output 1 and Output 3 occurred after the grant was awarded. Although the manuscript has been submitted based on preliminary results, but revisions, additional analysis, and final validations were funded by the grant during the project period. The peer review feedback led to grant-supported revisions, therefore, the article's final form is a direct result of the project. The PI clarify that there were no other funding sources to support the research conducted before project commencement date and produced the publications concerned. Also, the PI clarify that the publications reported were arising directly from this grant.

14617121.label: Major findings and research outcome
14617121.value: First, this project addresses identification challenges in linear instrumental variable (IV) models with a large mixed set of instruments and control variables, including irrelevant, weak, and potentially invalid ones. The findings highlight that endogenous treatment effect estimation is identifiable even when instruments are weak or irrelevant, as long as the excluded valid instruments satisfy the "majority rule" among relevant IVs. The PI extends prior work by accommodating irrelevant IVs in high-dimensional settings, introducing a modified majority rule for identification, which aligns with adaptive Lasso penalties. The study proposes an estimator, R2IVE, which leverages weak IVs through a three-step procedure: selecting relevant IVs, then useful controls using predicted treatment, and OLS estimation. It achieves the oracle property and robust finite-sample performance over methods like sisVIVE and TSHT. Simulations demonstrate lower bias and MSE in settings with many weak IVs, and an empirical study revisiting trade's effect on economic growth illustrates its ability to classify mixed covariates and detect invalid instruments (e.g., in data-rich environments with endogeneity concerns). Second, this project introduces a censored outcome adaptive Lasso (COAL) for covariate selection in propensity score models with high-dimensional censored data, allowing more covariates than observations. The method combines inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) with inverse probability of censoring weighting (IPCW) to estimate average causal effects (ACE), enhancing efficiency by selecting outcome-related covariates. Unlike the outcome-adaptive Lasso (OAL), COAL handles censoring via weighted least squares initial estimators and is robust to non-informative censoring. Theoretical results show COAL's oracle properties for variable selection and the estimator's asymptotic normality, with variance approximated by perturbation-resampling. Simulations in the appendix reveal superior efficiency and lower variance compared to OAL and standard methods, particularly under moderate censoring rates, highlighting its utility in survival analysis and big data contexts like biomedical studies. The direct research outcome include two papers, Li et al. (2024), referred to as Output 1, and Fan and Wu (2024), referred to as Output 2, published in Statistics and Probability Letters, The Review of Economics and Statistics respectively. These two are leading journals in statistics/economics/econometrics fields. The PI also developed implementation software package/codes on his GitHub website, which is accessible to everyone. An empirical study on single child peer effects of school performance is published in Labour Economics (2022).

14617121.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14617121.value: The research by the PI opens avenues for advancing causal inference methods in high-dimensional settings with censored outcomes and mixed instrumental variables (IVs). Future developments could refine adaptive Lasso techniques like COAL and R2IVE for non-linear models, survival analysis, and dynamic panel data, improving robustness to censoring, weak signals, and misspecification. Integrating machine learning for covariate and IV selection, while exploring semi-parametric approaches, could further enhance identification, estimation efficiency, and inference accuracy under endogeneity. For empirical applications, particularly in biomedical studies, labor economics, and development economics, these methods could be applied to study causal effects in observational data, such as the impact of treatments on survival times or trade policies on heterogeneous growth outcomes, leveraging data-rich environments. A proposed course of action includes developing open-source software implementing these methods (e.g., COAL and R2IVE codes on GitHub), fostering collaboration with econometricians and practitioners. Applying these tools to real-world datasets will validate their practical utility further.

14617121.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14617121.value: When empirical researchers want to understand causal relationships, like how treatments impact survival times or trade affects economic growth, they often use instrumental variables (IVs) or propensity scores to isolate true effects amid confounding factors. However, censored outcomes (e.g., incomplete survival data) or mixed IVs (weak, invalid, or irrelevant) make results unreliable. This project tackles these problems to ensure trustworthy conclusions. The project shows that with censored data and high-dimensional covariates, standard methods fail to give efficient causal inference. The PI proposes a new approach using "censored outcome adaptive Lasso" (COAL) to select outcome-related covariates, even in complex datasets, ensuring accurate average causal estimates via double inverse weighting. The PI also develops a robust IV procedure (R2IVE) to classify mixed covariates, spotting invalid IVs in data-rich environments, even when IVs are weak or irrelevant, under a modified "majority rule." Overall, these studies improve causal inference by handling censored data and non-ideal IVs, making research in fields like economics, biomedicine, and labor more reliable. The methods help researchers draw valid conclusions from big, complicated datasets, guiding better policies and decisions.

14617421.value: 本研究旨在探討在職幼兒教師對於將數碼設備應用於幼兒視覺藝術教育的態度與應用能力。 一些學者認為，數碼設備（如平板電腦、照相機和攝錄機）通過豐富多樣的視覺藝術形式（包括繪畫、照片和錄像），為幼兒提供了構建意義的機會。有觀點提出，兒童對意義的建構，會受到教師促進兒童數碼學習的方法影響。然而，許多幼兒教師並不肯定如何在幼稚園運用數碼科技。例如，瑞典的幼兒教師認為，他們缺乏將數碼科技整合到幼兒活動中的知識，亦需要更清晰的課程指引和充足的培訓。在香港，目前還沒有研究探討幼兒教師對數碼設備應用於幼兒視覺藝術教育中的看法。是次研究填補了這一重要的研究缺口。 計劃行為理論認為，行為的表現取決於意圖、主觀規範、主觀控制感、自尊以及過往行為和經驗。根據這一觀點，我們的研究將（1）探討在職幼兒教師對把數碼設備應用於幼兒視覺藝術教學中的行為理念、規範理念和控制理念；（2）調查這些行為理念、規範理念、控制理念及過往經驗如何影響幼兒教師將數碼科技融入幼兒視覺藝術教學的實踐；（3）調查幼兒教師在課堂上如何以及在多大程度上利用數碼設備來教授視覺藝術。我們將採用混合式研究方法：（1）線上問卷將用來調查在職幼兒教師在視覺藝術教學中對運用數碼設備的行為理念、規範理念和控制理念；（2）焦點小組訪問會探討這些理念對幼兒教師將數碼科技融入幼兒視覺藝術教學的影響；（3）觀察性研究將探討在職幼兒教師如何以及在多大程度上將數碼設備融入到視覺藝術教學中。 在理論層面上，是次研究將在教育研究領域方面，增加我們對幼兒教師如何應對數碼藝術教學可能性的認識。在實踐層面上，研究結果將為香港幼兒教師培訓課程中，數碼科技整合課程的設計和推行奠定基礎，從而提升幼兒教師對教學內容知識的掌握。最後，研究結果將影響未來的課程改革，促使香港幼稚園更廣泛地採用數碼藝術，擴闊本地認識和教授視覺藝術的不同可能性。

14617721.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14617721.value: 預測中日文初等教育的讀寫能力發展

14617721.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14617721.value: Prof MCBRIDE, Catherine A Prof Wong, Yu-ka

14617721.label: Project Objectives
14617721.value: To examine the developmental trajectories of reading and spelling skills across primary school years in Chinese and Japanese. A growing number of cross-linguistic studies have revealed both language-specific and universal patterns in the growth of word reading skills, with the observed differences frequently reflecting the nature of the writing system (e.g., Caravolas, 2017). However, most previous studies have been conducted in European alphabetic orthographies, and studies examining the growth patterns of word reading skills in a non-alphabetic orthography are still rare (Inoue et al., 2020; Lin et al., 2019). Additionally, most of the studies have covered a relatively limited developmental span, usually from kindergarten to Grade 2. Given the prolonged process of learning a logographic orthography, the growth patterns need to be examined over a longer developmental period that covers from early literacy to proficient literacy. Moreover, there is a dearth of research examining the growth patterns of spelling. The proposed study aims to fill these knowledge gaps and reveal both similarities and differences in the growth patterns of literacy skills between the two logographic orthographies, Chinese and Japanese Kanji. To identify the cognitive and environmental predictors of the long-term developmental trajectories of literacy skills in Chinese and Japanese. The PI (Inoue) and the Co-Is (McBride, Wong) have conducted a number of studies with Hong Kong and Japanese children in order to explore the cognitive and environmental predictors of literacy development in the respective language (e.g., Inoue et al., 2017, 2018a, 2019, 2020; McBride, 2016; McBride-Chang et al., 2005, 2008; Wong, 2017, 2019). The experience and knowledge, as well as the measures and analytic strategies that have been developed and employed in these studies, will be used in the proposed study. It should be noted, however, that most of the previous studies examined the predictors of children’s literacy skills at a certain time point (e.g., predicting Grade 2 reading by Grade 1 cognitive skills) rather than the growth trajectories (i.e., changes over time) of literacy skills. Indeed, relatively little attention has been paid to both positive/protective and negative/risk factors that influence the growth speed in literacy development. Using a longitudinal design that covers from early literacy to proficient literacy, this study aims to examine the predictive roles of various cognitive and environmental factors in literacy development. The findings will advance our understanding of the developmental dynamics of literacy skills in the two languages, which, in turn, will help identify children who will persistently struggle to acquire literacy skills as well as those who will eventually catch up as early as when they are at the beginning of primary education. To evaluate whether and to what extent the relations between cognitive and environmental factors and literacy development vary between East Asian languages and societies. Logographic orthographies, defined as the writing systems in which symbols primarily represent a morpheme or word, are widely used in East Asian languages such as Chinese and Japanese (called Kanji). There is little doubt that literacy development in children learning a logographic orthography is at least somewhat different compared to that of children learning an alphabetic orthography (e.g., Inoue et al., 2017; McBride-Chang et al., 2005). Despite the substantial advancements in our understanding of language-specific and universal predictors of literacy development, two important questions remain unanswered: (1) Do the relations between cognitive skills and literacy development vary between different logographic systems? (2) Do the relations between environmental factors and literacy development vary among East Asian cultural contexts? Indeed, with the exception of the Mandarin-Cantonese comparison (McBride-Chang et al., 2005), no studies have examined the factors that influence literacy development across logographic orthographies representing different languages. Thus, the proposed study examines the cognitive and environmental predictors of early literacy development in two logographic orthographies, Chinese and Japanese Kanji.
