14617721.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14617721.value: 本研究調查 (a) 小學生漢語和日語讀寫技能 (單詞閱讀，閱讀理解和拼寫) 的成長軌跡，以及 (b) 這一發展時期讀寫技能成長軌蹟的認知和環境預測因素。通過在三年內同時追踪 2 年級和 4 年級的兒童，該研究將涵蓋長達從早期識字到熟練識字的發展時期。該研究的結果將促進我們理解跨語言及社會文化背景的讀寫能力發展，這將有利於未來設計和實行讀寫技能教學，以及對東亞日益多樣化的兒童和家庭人口的社會支持。 對於學習漢語和日語等語標書寫系統的兒童來說，掌握讀寫能力尤其具有挑戰性。事實上，在這些語言中學習數千個視覺複雜的字符是一個艱鉅而漫長的過程，遠遠超出了小學教育，大量東亞社會的兒童在學習閱讀和拼寫方面遇到了很大的困難。儘管如此，現有研究對於小學不同年級讀寫技能成長軌蹟的個體差異，尤其是在語標書寫系統中的個體差異知之甚少。因此，早期識別那些將持續努力獲得讀寫技能的孩子以及那些最終會趕上的孩子仍然是極其困難的，甚至是不可能的。 為了填補這一知識空白，擬議的研究將評估香港和日本約 480 名小學生的識字發展及其潛在因素（即兒童的認知技能和家庭學習環境）之間的互動發展。本研究將採用三年三波縱向設計，以捕捉長期發展關係。根據我們最近對香港和日本的 1 年級和 2 年級兒童進行的跨語言研究的結果，我們假設 (a) 識字技能的增長速度將是漢語比日語更快，(b) 兩種語言的識字發展的認知預測因子會有部分不同，反映每種語言的特點，(c) 父母的閱讀和拼寫教學會預測早期識字，而父母與兒童的理解能力活動將預測孩子日後對兩種語言的閱讀理解能力。 該研究的結果將為兒童讀書能力發展診斷措施的選擇、設計和解釋提供信息，這對於包括香港和日本在內的東亞社會小學生的識字困難進行適當的、基於證據的早期識別和介入至關重要。早期識別和介入對於防止成績、動機和自尊下降的螺旋式下降以及實現未來的個人滿意度和職業成功至關重要。

14618221.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14618221.value: 關於父母如何促進兒童早期算術能力、數學語言及詞彙知識的一項干預研究

14618221.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14618221.value: Prof MCBRIDE, Catherine A Prof PURPURA, David Dr YANG, Xiujie

14618221.label: Project Objectives
14618221.value: Although previous research has established the importance of the home learning environment for children’s early numeracy development (Lefevre et al., 2010; Son & Morrison, 2010), the exact activities from daily routines that contribute best to improving children’s early numeracy skills remain unclear. Moreover, little research has focused on enhancing children’s home numeracy experiences prior to formal schooling. One strong rationale for the proposed project is that the home learning environment, particularly parental engagement, can be an important resource for young children’s early numeracy development before formal schooling (Cheung & McBride-Chang, 2015; Cheung, Yang, Dulay, & McBride, 2017; Gunderson & Levine, 2011; Huang, Zhang, Liu, Yang, & Song, 2017). However, the extent to which parental engagement can have a clear effect on children’s numeracy knowledge acquisition is unclear. The key issues to be addressed in this project center on how to promote Hong Kong children’s early numeracy, mathematical language, and vocabulary knowledge through parental coaching. Based on existing parent-child coaching programs from McBride and Cheung in mathematics (e.g., Cheung & McBride-Chang, 2015; Dulay, Cheung, & McBride, 2018) and vocabulary development via dialogic reading (Chow, McBride-Chang, Cheung, & Chow, 2008), as well as Purpura for early mathematics (Purpura et al., in preparation), we plan to investigate the intervention effects of dialogic storybook reading, number card game play, and vocabulary-building card game play on Hong Kong children’s early numeracy and vocabulary knowledge. Our proposed study has the following objectives: Objective 1: To translate and revise existing English dialogic reading mathematics storybooks in order to test their usefulness in a Chinese family setting. Our subsequent results can be compared to existing findings from American families on the feasibility of using dialogic reading to promote mathematics concepts in young Chinese children. We expect that dialogic mathematics storybook reading will be helpful for promoting early mathematics learning and vocabulary knowledge in Hong Kong. Objective 2: To focus on the needs of Chinese-speaking families in promoting mathematics learning. Compared to the English system, the Chinese number naming system is more linguistically transparent, and this might in turn affect the utility of mathematics interventions in Chinese-speaking children. The present study affords us an opportunity to explore various mathematics concepts in Chinese in order to understand potential advantages and disadvantages of everyday language in promoting children’s development of number sense and subsequent mathematics learning /problem solving. Objective 3: To examine and compare the effects of various parental training programs on Hong Kong kindergartners’ mathematical language, numeracy skills, and general vocabulary knowledge. These training programs include: 1) dialogic storybook reading using mathematical concepts, 2) number card games, 3) a combination of dialogic storybook reading and number card games, 4) a vocabulary-building card game, and 5) a (passive) control group. Children’s mathematics and general vocabulary knowledge, as well as their wide-ranging knowledge of mathematics skills, will all be pre- and post-tested in this intervention study. We predict that children in the intervention groups will significantly outperform their counterparts in the vocabulary control group and the passive control group on both mathematical language skills and early numeracy skills. The vocabulary group is expected to outperform the number cards group in general vocabulary knowledge, whereas the three intervention groups are all expected to improve relative to the control groups on mathematical language knowledge. Objective 4: To determine which training programs yield the strongest effects for promoting children’s mathematical language, early numeracy, and general vocabulary knowledge at home. We expect to find that the group that receives parental training highlighting a combination of dialogic storybook reading and game playing centered on mathematics concepts will demonstrate the strongest achievements in mathematics skills across all groups. This study will allow a more in-depth exploration of ways in which families can promote early mathematics and vocabulary development at home. Theoretically, this study will permit us to demonstrate a causal association of both dialogic storybook reading focused on mathematics and game play involving number cards with children’s numeracy development; it may also demonstrate the utility of games for promoting vocabulary knowledge. Collectively, these results will underscore the role of home numeracy in children’s early mathematics achievement. Practically, through the use of storybooks and games, this study can ensure that parents have two useful tools for making early mathematics learning meaningful and interesting to children. These approaches will provide important guidelines on critical mathematics content to be taught in early childhood and will enhance early numeracy in young children, including those at-risk for mathematics learning difficulties.

14618221.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14618221.value: 兒童早期的算術技能對以後的成功很重要。然而，現有的研究很少關注如何通過在家裡進行親子活動提高兒童早期的算術能力。對於年幼兒童而言，親子數學活動是一種潛在的重要家庭體驗。儘管許多研究著重於通過教師培訓提高學校整體的數學水平，很少研究會關注父母在家中如何可以提升兒童的數學語言和早期算術技能。因此，本研究旨在評估不同親子活動對幼稚園兒童的數學語言和早期算術技能的干預效果。 本干預研究擬招募五個親子組： 第 1 組父母將收到專門為促進兒童數學語言發展而編寫的對話故事書；此故事書主要側重於定量語言的使用。第 2 組家長將收到一套用於玩各種數學遊戲的數學遊戲卡，包括計數，數字識別、物件識別、數量比較等。在第 3 組裡，父母和兒童將進行對話故事書閱讀和使用數學遊戲卡，以評估這兩種干預方法一起進行時是否會產生比第 1 組或第 2 組更好的結果。第 4 組的父母將被要求進行詞彙構建遊戲，鼓勵孩子的複合詞構建能力；這是一個活性對照組。最後，第 5 組是被動控制組；他們按照年齡和性別與其他組進行匹配，將不會進行任何特殊培訓。 通過比較五個親子組，我們會評估不同親子活動對於促進兒童數學語言、早期算術發展、和詞彙知識的效果。我們預測第1至3組的兒童相關技能的表現會明顯地比對照和控制組裡的兒童較好；相關技能包括數學語言技能和早期算術技能。具體來説，第3組，即故事書閲讀和數字游戲卡混合組，分別對應非正式和正式的數學訓練，相比於第1組和第2組，他們預計會進步最多。第1至4組的兒童會接受關於一般詞彙知識和專門數學詞彙的測試。第4組兒童預期在一般詞彙知識上的表現會好於其他組，而第1至3組的兒童會在數學詞彙知識上進步最多。 從理論角度出發，我們希望證明對話故事書閱讀和數字卡片遊戲等親子活動與香港幼稚園兒童的數學語言和早期算術知識之間的因果關係。這些結果將表明早期家庭算術活動對於兒童數學學習的重要性。從實際應用角度出發，我們的研究會提供更有效的方法， 讓香港兒童可以與父母一起學習早期數學概念。這些干預研究的結果會催生新想法，為有數學障礙風險的兒童提供最佳的早期訓練方案。

14618721.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14618721.value: The persisting associations between parents’ educational attainment and children’s educational outcomes have been well documented in the developed world, although until recently the literature was primarily focused on such persistence form fathers to children. The role played by mothers in their children’s education has been increasingly recognized in the study of intergenerational social mobility studies. However, there is still too little research on intergenerational education mobility in Hong Kong, and thus, we also have limited knowledge about the prospects for girls to raise their socio-economic status through education.. In addition, existing studies did not provide consistent evidence that educational expansion policies have reduced the association between parents’ and children’s schooling, nor have studies examined the impact of Hong Kong’s education expansion reforms on intergenerational educational mobility. Further, of special importance for mobility researcher in Hong Kong are second-generation Mainlander immigrants constitute a large proportion of Hong Kong’s population, little is known on their intergenerational social mobility and the impact of educational expansion reforms on their mobility. Using Census data from 1991 to 2021, this proposal would allow the investigators to provide a comprehensive analysis of intergenerational education mobility in Hong Kong over a period of three decades, investigate the heterogeneity in intergenerational transmission of human capital in gender and immigration background, and assess the impact of educational reforms on intergenerational mobility. Our study builds on existing literature and makes several novel contributions. First, our findings will be the first to provide a comprehensive profile of intergenerational transmission of education of Hong Kong over three decades. Secondly, we intend to study the intergenerational education persistence between fathers (mothers) and daughters, a subject that has not been widely discussed in previous literature in Hong Kong (Lam & Liu, 2019) as well as international literature on intergenerational transmission for women (Azam, 2016). This information should be especially helpful to policy makers in societies with strong gender roles. More importantly, taking advantage of Census data for three decades, we will analyze the potential policy decisions that might have driven differences in the evolution of intergenerational education mobility in Hong Kong. Lastly, because low intergenerational educational mobility can lead to greater inequality and low economic efficiency in the long term, understanding of the intergenerational mobility of second-generation immigrants can shed light on the long-term integration of immigrant families. 父母的教育程度和孩子的教育成果之間持續存在的關聯在發達國家已有詳細記載，儘管直到最近，文獻還主要關注從父親到孩子的這種持續性。母親在子女教育中的作用在代際社會流動研究中越來越得到認可。然而，香港對代際教育流動的研究仍然太少，因此我們對女孩通過教育提高社會經濟地位的前景也知之甚少。 此外，現有研究並沒有提供一致的證據表明教育擴張政策減少了父母與子女教育之間的聯繫，也沒有研究考察香港教育擴張改革對代際教育流動的影響。此外，對於香港流動性研究人員而言，特別重要的是第二代內地移民佔香港人口的很大一部分，他們的代際社會流動性以及教育擴張改革對其流動性的影響知之甚少。本研究將利用 1991 年至 2021 年的人口普查數據，對過去三十年間香港的代際教育流動進行詳盡的描述，調查性別和移民背景下人力資本代際傳遞的異質性，並評估教育改革對代際流動的影響。 我們的研究建立在現有文獻的基礎上，並做出了一些新的貢獻。首先，我們的研究結果將是第一個提供香港教育在過去三十年間代際傳遞的全面概況。其次，我們打算研究父親（母親）和女兒之間的代際教育持續性，這個主題在香港以前的相關主題文獻以及關於女性代際傳遞的國際文獻中都沒有被廣泛討論。這些信息對具有強烈性別角色的社會中的決策者尤其有用。更重要的是，我們將利用三十年來的人口普查數據，分析可能導致香港代際教育流動演變差異的潛在政策決定。最後，由於長期低代際教育流動性會導致更大的不平等和低經濟效率，因此了解二代移民的代際流動性可以為移民家庭的長期融合提供線索。

14619121.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14619121.value: 在亞熱帶地區的高密度城市，街道網絡（包含道路及與其連接的行人空間）通常充當主要通風廊道。譬如在香港，審慎的街道網絡設計對城市通風環境極其重要，理由如下：首先，由於建築物的高地積比率和高容積比率，及樓宇間的建築通透度低，市區內部的空气流通非常依賴街道網絡。其次，街道作為戶外活動的主要空間，需要充足的空氣流通才能讓行人在炎熱潮濕的夏季達至舒適狀態。再者，由於街道網絡通常先於建築的規劃佈局，後期對街道網絡進行調整將變得極其困難。 儘管現時許多通風環境研究已經對規則形態的街道網絡（即正交的街道網絡）進行了深入分析，但只有少數研究涉及街道網絡的不規則形態特徵（即非正交的街道網絡）。事實上，不規則的街道網絡在亞熱帶地區的高密度城市相當普遍。然而，由於缺乏相關研究數據，規劃部門現時仍未能對市區中的不規則街道設計作有效指引。為了更全面地了解在複雜的城市建築環境下的空氣流通狀況，相關研究應當充分考慮不規則的街道網絡形態特徵對城市通風環境構成的影響，以更合理地指引道路和行人空間設計，從而為城市居民提供更舒適的居住環境。 本擬議研究旨在達成以下目標。首先，本研究將對香港數個典型高密度街區中的街道網絡形態特徵進行分類統計及分析，得出香港街道網絡形態特徵指標的一般取值範圍。其次，本研究將使用香港規劃部門現有的風洞實驗數據，對香港街道網絡形態特徵指標及行人水平風速率建立線性回歸模型。基於該回歸模型，本研究將進一步為香港的典型高密度街區繪製高精度的通風環境地圖。再者，基於上述研究成果，本研究將進行數個全新的風洞參數化實驗，用以量化說明不同的城市街道設計策略如何影響行人水平通風環境。最後，本研究將為規劃師和政府決策者提出建議，用以指導新區的街道網絡規劃及舊區的街道網絡活化。 本研究的預期成果包括：其一，開發一套數學統計模型/通風環境地圖，用以量化/可視化不規則高密度城市形態特徵對行人水平通風環境的影響。其二，為香港規劃部門提供決策依據，用以修訂及補充現時對市區道路和行人空間的設計指引。這些指引對於其他熱帶地區的高密度城市的規劃師和政府決策者亦具參考價值。

14619721.label: Project Objectives
14619721.value: To address the puzzle of how leaders avoid erosion to their domestic standing after backing down from a threat in an international conflict. To produce policy recommendations for leaders involved in an international conflict, particularly on how to manage public sentiment and morale at home and understand the intentions of an adversary abroad. To develop in-depth knowledge on three cases of international conflict in modern history: the Fashoda Crisis (1898) between Britain and France; 2) the Suez Crisis between Egypt, and Britain and France (1956); and 3) the standoff between China and India at Doklam (2017). 14619721.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14619721.value: In the study of international politics, audience costs theory posits that during a conflict, a leader who is willing to risk punishment by his citizens by declaring a threat in public must be – from the adversary’s perspective – more likely to be serious than bluffing. Because retreating from a high-profile threat is costly to the leader politically, it is credible. Recently, however, scholars have called into question the relevance of audience costs. The literature has remained largely theoretical, they argue, and empirical evidence for audience costs has been scant. Audience costs have always been premised on the assumption that citizens care less about assessing the merit of a leader’s decision to back down than holding him accountable for their country’s concomitant “loss of credibility, face or honor”. Simply put, to retreat is humiliating. But if harm to the collective self-esteem of a country is what causes a leader to lose support, then vice versa, he may seek to avoid punishment by manipulating his citizens’ understanding of a retreat in ways that mitigate – if not counteract – its deleterious effect. Social psychologists have postulated a number of cognitive strategies through which collective self-esteem may be bolstered in the event of a loss. Metaphorically, I label these strategies altogether the “Ah Q” theory of retreat management, based on the title character in Lu Xun’s satirical novella. I content that after a retreat, a country’s leader and his domestic allies – such as government and military officials, the media, and fellow partisans – are often motivated to engineer a sense of psychological victory among their domestic “audience”. Based on the germane works in psychology, I have identified eleven of such cognitive strategies. Empirically, I subject my theory to test through the complementary use of two methods: case studies and randomized survey experiments. The cases I examine in detail include the Fashoda Crisis (1898) between Britain and France; 2) the Suez Crisis between Egypt, and Britain and France (1956); and 3) the standoff between China and India at Doklam (2017). To better ascertain the causal relationship between the hypothesized variables, I conduct two vignette-based survey experiments in China and the US. With this research, I intend to produce a book manuscript (or several article manuscripts) for publication. 根據國際關係學內廣泛接受的「Audience Cost Theory」，領導人但凡在衝突中正式公開宣佈國家威脅的存在，比起虛張聲勢，敵方更應視它為認真有力的宣言。如果領導人在國家威脅面前臨陣退縮，他將會受到國家公民政治上的懲罰－－因此，要是領導人肯冒這個險而選擇高調發出聲言，這將構成有力的威脅。然而，最近學者對「Audience Cost Theory」的內容提出質疑；他們認為相關的文獻過分依賴理論，大致上缺乏根據現實經驗的證據。 「Audience Costs」的前提是，國家公民比較看重國家因領導人失策而失去的「信譽，面子或尊嚴」，而不評估領導人做出「退縮」決定的原因或價值。簡單而言，去撤退是一種恥辱的行為。 但是，如果損害國家的集體自尊是導致領導人失去支持的原因之一，反之亦然；領導人可能會通過操縱公民對撤退的理解以減輕或是抵消其有害的影響。社會心理學家提出了許多能夠在損失後彌補／增強集體自尊的策略。社會心理學家提出了許多能夠在損失後彌補／增強集體自尊的策略。我以「阿Q正傳」的標題人物為基礎，將這些策略統稱為「阿Q」撤退管理法。我推論在撤退之後，領導人和他的國內盟友－－例如政府官員、軍方、媒體和其他支持者－－經常會為國內的「觀眾」營造一種心理勝利的感覺，並且從心理學的文獻中識別了11 種相關策略。 我通過兩種互補的方法測試我的理論：案例研究和隨機調查實驗。詳細研究的案例包括：1）英國和法國之間的法紹達危機（1898 年）； 2）埃及、英國和法國之間的蘇伊士運河危機（1956年）；和 3）中國和印度在洞朗的對峙（2017年）。為了確定提出的變量之間的因果關係，我在中國（已完成）和美國（將使用當前贈款執行）進行了兩個使用史實片段的調查實驗。通過這項研究，我打算寫本書稿（或幾篇文章手稿）以供出版。

14619721.label: Realisation of objectives
14619721.value: I have conducted several activities that, in tandem, realized the objectives set forth in my grant proposal. First, as I have stated in the proposal and subsequently in my request for project revision, because most of my case studies concern the foreign policies of Western countries (the UK, France, etc.), many of the materials I need cannot be found in the academic libraries in Hong Kong. They are instead available at major academic libraries in the West, or at the national archives of the countries in question. To offer just one example, the Documents on British Foreign Policy 1919-1939 is a collection of the most important British documents on foreign policy published by the British government. It has 64 volumes. However, across all academic libraries in Hong Kong, only a handful of them are available, and they are mostly volumes related to British foreign policy towards East Asia (particularly China) and therefore of limited use for my research. As such, I have conducted research trips to the library of the University of Toronto, the third largest academic library in North America and has all of the materials I need (including the aforementioned example of the Documents on British Foreign Policy 1919-1939). In the summer of 2024, I also undertook a research trip to the National Archives of France in Paris and the UK National Archives in London. These activities have allowed me to consult the necessary primary (diplomatic memos and demarches, diaries and memories, diplomatic meeting minutes, etc.) and secondary documents to complete my case studies, especially on the Fashoda Crisis (1898) between Britain and France and the Suez Crisis between Egypt, and Britain and France (1956) (Project Objective #3). Second, in late-2023/early-2024, I have commissioned the survey company, Qualtrics, to administer a survey in mainland China (with n = ~3,000) to put to test some of my research hypotheses (for detailed research design, please see the original grant application) (Project Objective #5). Beyond the case studies and the survey experiment, I have also made the best use of my time throughout the duration of this grant to read up on the relevant literature in social and cognitive psychology (Project Objective #4). This exercise has been crucial to coming up with the proper theoretical framework to make sense of how leaders avoid erosion to their domestic standing after backing down from a threat in an international conflict, and to structure and guide my case studies and in the design of the survey experiment (Project Objective #1). Moving forward, the insights developed from this research will also have direct bearing on policymaking; they inform leaders on how to manage public opinion in times of international crises (Project Objective #2).

14619721.label: Major findings and research outcome
14619721.value: The major findings are that, as I have hypothesized, governments indeed resort to a number of social creativity strategies to ameliorate citizens’ sense of humiliation after they have backed down in an international conflict. These findings are present in the case study on China, which has been published in 2024 in the European Journal of International Relations. They are also demonstrated in the survey experiment I conducted in China, which I have written up in a draft manuscript soon to be submitted to a top-tier academic journal in International Relations for publication. They are also present (to various extents) in the other case studies I have conducted. Once completed, I plan to include these case studies in a book manuscript on the subject for publication with a major university press.

14619721.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14619721.value: As explained above, I currently have one draft manuscript that I intend to submit to a top-tier academic journal in International Relations for publication. I shall continue to work on the case studies using the materials collected during this research. Once completed, they will be included in a book manuscript on the subject for publication with a major university press. This research has also loosely inspired me to study more broadly the psychology of propaganda. I have submitted an application in the current round of GRF on this topic.

14619721.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14619721.value: This research interrogates how leaders can avoid erosion to their domestic standing after backing down from a threat in an international conflict. I argue that leaders may resort to a range of what scholars of Social Identity Theory in psychology call “social creativity strategies” in their propaganda to alleviate their citizens’ sense of humiliation. I have put this theory to test through the use of two methods: case studies on several international crises that involved such countries as China, India, UK and France; and a survey experiment that seeks to understand how individuals respond psychologically to the use of such strategies in their government’s propaganda. The findings have been largely positive. This is, however, not a “purely” academic exercise whose audience is limited to the scholarly inclined. Understanding the sociopsychological dynamics of humiliation alleviation would also be of practical interest to leaders and policymakers. This research would inform them on how to manage public opinion in times of international crises.

14620021.label: Project Objectives
14620021.value: 1 Using a nationally representative sample of 40 municipalities and prefectures, we will document the frequency and magnitude of local administrative redistricting and reclassification since 1949. Since we seek to understand the dynamics at all levels of government, we resort to a sampling approach in order to ensure that the workload is sustainable. We will document annual changes at the township, county, and prefecture/municipal levels since 1949. 2 Identify the underlying logic(s) behind local administrative redistricting in China. Building on the existing literature on leadership career incentives, we develop the argument that redistricting changes in China are driven by two distinct strands of strategies. One follows a top-down approach, by which high-level officials empowered to alter municipal and county-level boundaries and administrative structures try to reorganize lower level governments in order to maximize resource extraction and appoint loyal supporters to newly restructured localities. The second (bottom-up) approach applies to promotion-seeking county officials who strategically manipulate rounds of township and village reorganization in order to achieve the reclassification of their locality to a higher-level form (e.g. from ordinary county to county-level city). They do so by appealing to central and provincial authorities who tend to reward officials who promote local urbanization and development. We intend to demonstrate empirically how each of these strategies has been playing out in practice, specify the conditions under which one occurs from frequently than the other, and specify when and where they have been deployed jointly. (4) Structure and present the GIS data for public use in an open and easily accessible format. We suspect that the lack of attention to redistricting and reclassification is due to the absence of an easily usable data repository that analysts, administrators as well as the wider public can access while conducting research, oversight or policy analysis. We will therefore make our data publicly available. Finally, we will make our raw datasets available to specialized researchers interested in using this information for their own purposes (in STATA and equivalent format).

14620021.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14620021.value: We seek to explain the puzzle of persistent and widespread redistricting and reclassification of Chinese local governments since the foundation of the PRC. While the existing global literature in political science and public administration emphasizes “gerrymandering” for electoral motives as the key driver of redistricting, we still observe large scale rounds of redistricting and administrative reclassifications at all levels of Chinese government in the absence of constituency-based elections. This project investigates the political logic behind such initiatives and assesses their long-term impacts on the quality of local governance in China. In a sequence of three related articles, we will test the hypothesis that frequent changes in local administrative divisions are the product of political competition over the distribution of scarce resources, which affects both the career prospects of local officials and the developmental trajectory of the territories that they govern, with long-term impacts on governance, urbanization and development. Local redistricting is driven by both top-down and bottom-up approaches. High-level officials alter municipal and county-level boundaries and administrative structure in order to maximize resource extraction and consolidate their patron-client networks, while county leaders reshape subordinate township-level units in order to signal their competence to their principals and advance their careers. Furthermore, we show that the cumulative impact of recurrent restructuring on a given locality has important consequences for the quality of local governance in the long run. We draw upon a nationally representative sample of 39 prefectures/municipalities to document the details of redistricting and reclassifications among over 3500 townships and 350 counties since 1949. We combine this micro-data with measures of political mobility of key local leaders, as well as indicators of socio-economic and governance performance at each level of government into a unified geographical information system (GIS) . Finally, our analytical research will help produce analytical and data tools for analysts and researchers of local development in China who rarely take redistricting and reclassification into account due to the paucity of extant research on the topic. 我們試圖解釋持續和廣泛的重新劃分和新中國成立以來中國地方政府的重新分類。雖然現有的全球政治學和公共管理文獻強調出於選舉動機的“選區劃分”是重新劃分選區的關鍵驅動因素，我們仍然觀察到在各級進行大規模的重新劃分和行政重新分類中國政府在沒有基於選區的選舉的情況下。這個項目調查此類舉措背後的政治邏輯並評估其長期對中國地方治理質量的影響在三篇相關文章的序列中，我們將檢驗頻繁變化的假設地方行政區劃是政治競爭的產物稀缺資源的分配，既影響地方官員的職業前景以及他們管轄的領土的長期發展軌跡對治理、城市化和發展的影響。本地重新劃分是由自頂向下和自底向上兩種方法。高級官員改變市政和縣級邊界和行政結構，以最大限度地利用資源提取和鞏固他們的顧客-客戶網絡，而縣領導則重塑下屬鄉鎮單位，以便向他們的校長表明他們的能力並推進他們的職業生涯。此外，我們表明，累積影響特定地點的經常性重組對質量有重要影響從長遠來看，地方治理。 我們利用具有全國代表性的 39 個地/市樣本記錄3500多個鄉鎮的重新劃分和重新分類的細節和 1949 年以來的 350 個縣。我們將這些微觀數據與政治 主要地方領導人的流動性，以及社會經濟和治理指標將各級政府績效納入統一的地理信息系統（地理信息系統）。 最後，我們的分析研究將有助於為分析師提供分析和數據工具和中國地方發展研究人員很少採取重新劃分和由於對該主題的現有研究很少，因此重新分類。

15100821.value: 高血壓是骨關節炎潛在的危險因子，然而其分子機制尚不清楚。我們前期工作發現血管收縮因子內皮素-1可以導致關節軟骨細胞老化、促進創傷後骨關節炎的發生。而且，我們在自發性或藥物誘導性的高血壓大鼠模型中，進一步證實激活血管收縮因子包括腎素-血管緊張素系統和/或內皮素系統，可以導致軟骨細胞老化和骨關節炎退化的表現，這可能和內皮缺乏sirtuin家族中最近被廣泛關注的sirtuin 7 (Sirt7)有關。在我們培育出的血管老化小鼠模型中，我們通過單細胞測序確認Sirt7減少可導致內皮素-1及其B型受體顯著上調。因此，我們認為內皮Sirt7/內皮素信號軸功能異常導致關節老化及骨關節炎的發生。我們將利用高血壓大鼠模型驗證這一研究假說。首先，我們將比較內皮Sirt7/內皮素信號軸在自發性高血壓鼠和正常血壓鼠表達的異同。其次，我們將進一步檢測內皮素信號通路在這兩種大鼠關節軟骨中的表達。最後，我們將利用內皮細胞靶向補充sirt7，探討對關節老化及骨關節炎進展的影響。本課題將為開發新型抗骨關節炎藥物開闢一條新的思路。

15101221.label: Realisation of objectives
15101221.value: Objective 1: To investigate whether PPM1K deficiency induces mitochondrial dysfunction during M1 macrophage polarization. 1. PPM1K deficiency impaired both basal and maximal mitochondrial respiration rate, while only modestly increased glycolytic rate in M1-activated bone marrow-derived macrophages (BMDM) after LPS and IFNγ treatment. 2. Ablation of PPM1K increased mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (ROS) production in both M0 (resting) and M1 (pro-inflammatory) macrophages. 3. Deletion of PPM1K induced mitochondrial damage in both M0 and M1 macrophages. 4. TCA cycle-related metabolites were quantified with LC-MS/MS, demonstrating the accumulation of citrate, fumarate, iso-citrate and malate in PPM1K-null M1 macrophages when compared to the wild-type (WT) controls. 5. To investigate whether the effect of PPM1K deficiency on M1 macrophage polarization and mitochondrial dysfunction depends on BCAA metabolism, PPM1K deficient BMDM and their wild-type controls were pre-treated with low BCAA DMEM and the normal complete DMEM as control before M1 activation using LPS and IFNγ. Subsequent, qPCR analysis and immunoassay showed that reduction in BCAA abolished PPM1K deficiency-induced M1-associated genes expression and pro-inflammatory cytokines secretion. Similarly, induction of mitochondrial ROS production and damage by PPM1K deletion were also reversed by BCAA depleted medium Together, these findings showed that the impact of PPM1K deficiency on M1 activation and mitochondrial functions are BCAA dependent. 6. Pharmacological inhibition of BDK and activation of BCKDHA by BT2 nullified M1-associated gene expression, pro-inflammatory cytokines secretion, along with mitochondrial ROS production and damage induced by PPM1K knockout. 7. Treatment with mitochondria-targeted antioxidant MitoTEMPO reversed the heightened mitochondrial ROS, pro-inflammatory cytokines MCP-1 and IL-1β secretion and mRNA expression of M1-associated genes including Nos2, Tnfa and Il6 in PPM1K deficient M1 BMDM. At the same time, transcriptional expression of NRF1 and its downstream targets were also upregulated after MitoTEMPO treatment. Objective 2: To investigate the underlying mechanism by which PPM1K controls M1 macrophage polarization and metabolic reprogramming via NRF1 or other factors. 1. RNA sequencing analysis in PPM1K deficient M1 BMDM revealed that M1 pro-inflammatory genes, along with genes related to mitochondrial functions including ATP synthesis, mitochondrial membrane permeability, and mitochondrial membrane potential were downregulated by PPM1K knockout. Differentially expressed genes coupled with TRRUST analysis pinpointed NRF1 as one of the top enriched transcriptional factors. 2. Deletion of PPM1K in M1-activated BMDM diminished NRF1 protein level and transcriptionally inactivated NRF1 downstream target genes including Cycs (Cytochrome C), Tfam, Tfb1m and Tfb2m, whereas Nrf1 gene expression remained unchanged when compared to the WT controls. 3. In silico analysis of PPM1K protein sequence identified the monopartite nuclear localization sequence in its PPM-type phosphatase domain. Subcellular fractionation and immunocytochemistry imaging further confirmed that macrophage PPM1K translocates to the nucleus and co-localize with NRF1 in response to LPS+IFNγ treatment. 4. Co-immunoprecipitation experiment demonstrated the interaction between PPM1K and NRF1 in macrophages and HEK293T cells, and such interaction was regulated by LPS+IFN-γ stimulation and the DNA binding & dimerization domain of NRF1 was proven to be indispensable for PPM1K-NRF1 interaction. 5. Docking of 3D protein structure simulation predicted 8 potential sites for PPM1K and NRF1 interactions, 2 of which lie in the DNA binding & dimerization domain of NRF1. Co-immunoprecipitation of PPM1K and NRF1 binding site mutants illustrated that Gly241 on PPM1K and Tyr122 on NRF1 are required for PPM1K-NRF1 interaction. 6. Pharmacological activation of BCAA catabolism by BT2 impeded transcriptional expression of NRF1 downstream targets including Nqo1, Tfam, Tfb1m and Tfb2m in PPM1K deficient macrophages, without altering Nrf1 expression. 7. PPM1K null macrophages were infected with adenovirus encoding NRF1 to replenish NRF1 expression, leading to restored expression of Nqo1, Hmox1, Tfb1m. This reversal of NRF1 downstream targets expression was accompanied by the suppression of M1 related genes Nos2 and Mcp1 and the secretion of pro-inflammatory cytokines MCP-1 and IL-1β. 8. Adenovirus-mediated replenishment of NRF1 prevents impaired mitochondrial respiratory rate, excessive mitochondrial ROS production and mitochondrial damage caused by PPM1K deficiency. Objective 3: To determine whether myeloid-specific deletion of PPM1K promotes obesity-induced adipose tissue inflammation and systemic insulin resistance in mice. 1. We successfully generated homozygous myeloid-specific PPM1K (Myeloid-PPM1K-KO) knockout mice by crossing the PPM1Kfloxed/floxed mice with the transgenic mice expressing Cre recombinase. The transcriptional expression of PPM1K in BMDM from Mye-PPM1K-KO mice was drastically reduced when compared to the WT controls, without affecting the expression of PPM1K in metabolically active organs including the bulk adipose tissues. 2. BMDM from Mye-PPM1K-KO mice exhibited upregulated Mcp1 and Il1b, oversecretion of IL-1β and total nitrate & nitrite when compared to the WT controls. This exaggeration in M1 activation was concurrent with the downregulation of NRF1 downstream genes including Nqo1, Cycs, Tfam, Tfb1m and Tfb2m without altering Nrf1 transcriptional expression. 3. Metabolic phenotyping of male Mye-PPM1K-KO mice revealed that genetic deletion of PPM1K in myeloid lineage exaggerated the obesity, glucose intolerance and insulin resistance, along with elevating circulating BCAA/BCKA and pro-inflammatory cytokines after feeding with standard chow (STC) and high-fat-high-cholesterol (HFHC) diet. On the other hand, myeloid inactivation of PPM1K exerted minimal effects on energy metabolism. 4. Epididymal white adipose tissue (eWAT) from Mye-PPM1K-KO mice promoted mRNA expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines Mcp1 and Tnfa. Similarly, KEGG/GSEA analysis of RNA sequencing has shown that pathways related to insulin resistance, inflammation and BCAA/BCKA metabolism were enriched in eWAT of Mye-PPM1K KO mice when compared to the WT controls. Flow cytometry analysis of stromal vascular fraction of eWAT demonstrated heightened tissue resident M1 macrophages and decreased M2 macrophages, respectively. This is further validated by H&E staining, which confirmed the increased number of crown-like structure and immune cell infiltration in the eWAT of the Mye-PPM1K KO mice when compared to their WT littermates.

15101221.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15101221.value: 1. We demonstrated that genetic deletion of PPM1K in myeloid cells aggravates obesity-induced adipose tissue inflammation and systemic metabolic dysregulation. The BDK inhibitor/BCKDHA activator BT2 abolished hyperinflammatory response and the mitochondrial dysfunctions caused by the loss of PPM1K in macrophages. Of note, BT2 has not been approved for clinical use, but sodium phenylbutyrate (NaPB) is an FDA-approved drug for urea cycle disorder that also suppresses BDK. Further studies will validate whether NaPB protects against inflammation, mitochondrial integrity and metabolic dysregulations in rodents and eventually translate the findings to human subjects. 2. We observed that PPM1K deletion impaired mitochondrial respiration and TCA cycle, evidenced by the accumulation of TCA-related metabolites, but the fate of these BCAA remains elusive. To chart how defective BCAA catabolism feeds the TCA cycle and contribute to flawed mitochondrial functions, 13C-labelled leucine/isoleucine/valine will be traced in macrophages with/without PPM1K under their resting and M1 states. 3. We demonstrated that BCAA and their downstream catabolites BCKA are increased in M1 macrophages. However, the increase might be due to increase of BCAA uptake or defective BCAA catabolism. We will employ the metabolic flux techniques to further elucidate why BCAA/BCKA are accumulated in M1 macrophages

15101221.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15101221.value: Our study shows that PPM1K helps macrophages safeguards mitochondrial health and prevents excessive inflammation. Loss of PPM1K in macrophages impairs their mitochondrial energy production, generates more damaging reactive oxygen species, and switches the macrophage into a pro-inflammatory state. This functional defect is tightly linked to how macrophages metabolize branched-chain amino acids (BCAAs), nutrients commonly found in protein-rich foods. We also discovered that PPM1K cooperates with NRF1, a regulatory protein that turns on genes required for maintaining mitochondrial health and homeostasis. Without PPM1K, NRF1 transcriptional activity is weakened and mitochondrial functions decline. In mice lacking PPM1K only in the myeloid lineage, inflammation in adipose tissue worsens, weight gain and glucose intolerance increase, accompanied by elevated levels of BCAAs in the circulation. Promoting BCAAs catabolism reduces inflammation and improves mitochondrial health in macrophages, therefore represents a feasible to treat obesity-related chronic inflammation insulin resistance. Key findings: (1) Loss of PPM1K impairs macrophage mitochondria, raises oxidative stress, and drives stronger pro-inflammatory responses. (2) PPM1K controls inflammation and mitochondrial function in macrophages via BCAA dependent manners. (3) PPM1K partners with NRF1 to activate mitochondrial genes; restoring NRF1 rescues energy production, mitochondrial health and lowers inflammatory cytokines.

15101621.label: Realisation of objectives
15101621.value: 1. Functional characterization of STK39/PARP1 signaling in the regulation of liver T-ICs and drug resistance (100%) i. To investigate the effects of STK39/PARP1 modulation on the T-IC phenotypes To determine if STK39 drives self-renewal and tumor formation, we manipulated its expression in HCC cells using lentiviral knockdown and overexpression. Western blot analysis showed high STK39 levels in MHCC-97L and Hep3B cells, which were selected for knockdown, while Huh7 cells were used for overexpression. In vitro limiting dilution assays demonstrated that silencing STK39 significantly reduced stem cell frequencies in MHCC-97L and Hep3B cells. In vivo tumorigenicity assays indicated that STK39 knockdown decreased tumor size and number, along with lower liver CSC markers like CD24 and CD47. cDNA array analyses revealed higher STK39 mRNA levels in the CD133+ subpopulation compared to CD133- from Huh7 and PLC-8024 cells. In contrast, STK39 overexpression enhanced stem cell frequencies, tumorigenicity, and the expression of liver CSC markers. ii. To determine the effects of STK39/PARP1 modulation on HCC metastasis and drug resistance We investigated whether STK39 suppression sensitizes HCC cells to lenvatinib or sorafenib. Apoptosis assays showed increased rates in Huh7 cells after STK39 knockdown with either drug. Knockdown also reduced migration and invasion, while overexpression enhanced them. In an orthotopic liver model with MHCC-97L cells, the shSTK39 clone had lower tumor incidence and lung metastasis than controls. Additionally, using a STK39-targeting PROTAC degrader with lenvatinib in STK39-high MHCC-97L and Hep3B cells, colony formation assays indicated inhibited growth in STK39-high Huh7 cells and suppressed growth in lenvatinib-resistant HCC cells. iii. To assess the therapeutic potential of rAAV-8-shSTK39 in combination with lenvatinib/ rucaparib in a transgenic mouse model Instead of using rAAV8 to target STK39, we developed a specific inhibitor (H2) from Triazolyl-Sulonamides. H2, at a low dose of 15 µM, effectively reduced stem cell frequencies and enhanced the effects of sorafenib or lenvatinib. We evaluated H2's therapeutic effects, alone and with lenvatinib, in vivo using the lenvatinib-resistant patient-derived tumor xenograft PY003 and an immunocompetent C57BL/6J mouse HCC model. This included overexpressing activated c-myc-luc with PX330-sg-p53 and sleeping beauty transposase (Trp53KOMYCOE) via hydrodynamic injection. Results showed that the H2 and lenvatinib combination maximally suppressed tumor growth in both models, with no significant body weight loss in mice. 2. Elucidation of the molecular mechanism by which STK39 functionally contributes to tumor initiation, self-renewal, and drug resistance (100%) i. To investigate the binding activity between STK39 and PARP1 We established stable clones of S protein-FLAG-Streptavidin binding peptide (SFB)-STK39 in HEK293 cells and identified PARP1 as a potential binding partner. Overexpression of SFB-STK39 in Huh7 cells confirmed the interaction with PARP1 following pulldown of DDK-tagged STK39. This interaction was further validated in STK39-high expressing MHCC-97L and Hep3B cells via coimmunoprecipitation. Immunofluorescent staining also demonstrated co-localization of STK39 and PARP1 in HCC cell lines and patient samples with elevated STK39 expression. ii. To determine the effects of STK39 on PARP1 activity Alterations in STK39 expression significantly influenced PARP1 enzymatic activity, likely through phosphorylation at threonine 368 (T368) in both STK39 knockdown and overexpressing cells. In STK39 knockdown clones of MHCC-97L, PARylation—a key post-translational modification for chromatin remodeling—was suppressed, evidenced by reduced PAR polymer levels after PARP1 pulldown. Conversely, Huh7 cells with STK39 overexpression and PLC/PRF/5 lenvatinib-resistant cells exhibited increased sensitivity to lenvatinib when combined with rucaparib. To explore the STK39-PARP1 interaction in mediating lenvatinib resistance, we used a peptide blocking approach. Treatment with PeptiS_13, designed to disrupt this interaction, weakened the connection in STK39-high expressing Hep3B and MHCC-97L cells, as confirmed by coimmunoprecipitation. iii &iv. To investigate the effects of STK39 on PARP1-mediated SOX2/OCT4 regulation We investigated how the STK39/PARP1 interaction regulates SOX2 and OCT4 transcription in HCC. DNA fragments near the promoter regions of SOX2 and OCT4 in STK39-overexpressing cells, treated with and without rucaparib, were analyzed using micrococcal nuclease (MNase) and quantified by qPCR. The results showed increased uncut DNA fragments for SOX2 and OCT4 in STK39-overexpressing cells, indicating that STK39-driven PARP1 activity maintains an open chromatin structure, facilitating transcription and enhancing stem cell-like properties. Silencing STK39 reduced OCT4 and SOX2 expression, while overexpression restored them. Furthermore, PARP1 inhibition with rucaparib increased nucleosome occupancy and decreased SOX2 and OCT4 levels in STK39-overexpressing lenvatinib-resistant Huh7 and PLC/PRF/5 cells. 3. 15101621.label: Major findings and research outcome
15101621.value: Growing evidence shows that tumor cells evade targeted therapies by adopting states driven by phenotypic plasticity, often acquiring stem-like properties that enable them to bypass treatment mechanisms. Targeting the mechanisms that maintain these traits may improve outcomes. Since kinases are druggable targets, we aim to identify relevant kinases that drive this cellular state in our lenvatinib-resistant (LenR) patient-derived tumor xenograft mouse model of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Single-cell RNA sequencing showed that LenR tumors transition to alternative states, unlike sensitive tumors. RNA velocity and lineage analyses identified clusters enriched in cancer stemness, with Serine/threonine kinase 39 (STK39) significantly elevated in these clusters, facilitating state transitions in LenR HCC cells. Functional analyses showed that STK39 is crucial in regulation of cancer stemness and drug resistance and bears clinical significance. We identified a novel non-canonical pathway of STK39 in which it binds and regulates the activity of PARP1 via phosphorylation of PARP1 at site T368. In turn, this leads to PARP1-driven chromatin remodeling of the pluripotent factors including SOX2 and OCT4. To enable therapeutic targeting of STK39 in HCC, we developed a new inhibitor, H2, from a focused library of seven triazolyl-sulfonamide derivatives. We demonstrated that STK39 inhibitor H2 synergizes with lenvatinib in both in vitro and in vivo lenvatinib-resistant mouse HCC models. This combination suppressed tumor proliferation and angiogenesis while remodeling exhausted T cell content, promoting immune suppression against HCC. We identified the STK39 and PARP1 relationship as a key pathway driving cancer stemness and TKI resistance. Our findings support a novel combinatorial strategy using conventional HCC therapies to target the STK39/PARP1/SOX2/OCT4 signaling axis. Our research findings are scientifically and clinically significant, appealing to the readership of stem cell and cancer research. Key messages include: (1) We identified STK39 as a critical regulator of cellular state transitions in lenvatinib-resistant HCC tumors using single-cell RNA sequencing; (2) STK39 is overexpressed in lenvatinib-resistant HCC cells, correlating with poorer overall and disease-free survival; (3) STK39 plays a key role in regulating cancer stemness and drug resistance; (4) We discovered a novel non-canonical pathway where STK39 binds and phosphorylates PARP1 at T368, leading to chromatin remodeling and increased expression of stemness-related transcription factors SOX2 and OCT4; (5) We developed STK39 inhibitor H2, which demonstrates potent suppression of STK39 in vitro and in vivo; and (6) Combination therapy with lenvatinib and STK39 inhibitor H2 efficiently suppresses the growth of lenvatinib-resistant HCC and enhances T cell function.

15101621.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15101621.value: Tumor cells can evade targeted therapies by transitioning to alternative cellular states. We investigated the kinases involved in this process using a lenvatinib-resistant (LenR) model of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Single-cell RNA sequencing revealed that LenR tumors undergo these transitions, whereas sensitive tumors do not. Notably, Serine/threonine kinase 39 (STK39) was found to be enriched in cancer stemness clusters and plays a vital role in regulating stemness, drug resistance, and metastasis in LenR HCC cells. STK39 interacts with and activates PARP1, promoting chromatin remodeling and the expression of stemness factors such as SOX2 and OCT4. Our findings identify STK39 as a critical regulator of cellular states and drug resistance. In this study, we developed a novel, potent, and specific inhibitor (H2) targeting STK39 through a structure-guided approach using Triazolyl-Sulonamides. When combined with lenvatinib, the inhibitor H2 effectively suppresses tumor growth while maintaining manageable side effects, offering a new strategy for treating advanced HCC. We have developed this H2 compound in-house and plan to patent it as a new therapeutic agent for HCC treatment.

15101621.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15101621.value: Research shows that cancer cells can escape treatments by changing into different types of cells. Since certain proteins called kinases can be targeted by drugs, we are looking for those that help this process in a mouse model of liver cancer that doesn't respond to the drug lenvatinib. Our analysis revealed that these resistant tumors switch to these alternative cell types, unlike those that respond well to treatment. We found that a specific kinase, STK39, plays a big role in this switching, which is linked to cancer stem cells. STK39 helps these cells become more resistant to drugs and grow more aggressively. We discovered that STK39 works with another protein, PARP1, to change the way genes are expressed, promoting features associated with cancer stem cells. By developing a new inhibitor for STK39, we observed significant tumor growth reduction in resistant liver cancer models while improving the immune environment around the tumors. In summary, targeting STK39 may improve the effectiveness of lenvatinib, providing a new approach to treat liver cancer.

15104721.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15104721.value: Older adults with chronic diseases are prone to depressive symptoms and are at significant risk of developing depression. Prior research has consistently supported qigong as a promising approach to alleviate older adults’ depressive symptoms. However, its neurobiological mechanisms remain unclear. We propose that qigong exerts antidepressant effects through two pathways, given its focus on training the “mind” and “body”. With respect to its “mind” component, we hypothesize that qigong regulates activity of the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis to reduce cortisol levels, producing effects similar to the effects of mindfulness-based interventions. With respect to its “body” component, we hypothesize that qigong increases peripheral adiponectin levels, producing effects similar to the effects of low-intensity physical exercise. The down-regulation of cortisol and up-regulation of adiponectin enhance trophic factor signaling and up-regulate brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF), and BDNF level is related to neuroplasticity in brain regions and networks related to depressive symptoms. The aim of the current project is to test these pathways. To address this aim, we propose a multicenter, four-arm, randomized, single-blinded trial. We will randomly assign 300 depressed older adults with chronic diseases to one of the four groups: (a) qigong group, (b) mindfulness group, (c) low-intensity physical exercise group, and (d) wait-list control group. The active treatment groups will receive a 12-week training course in qigong (Eight-Section Brocades), mindfulness-based intervention, or low-intensity physical exercise, respectively. The primary clinical outcome is depressive symptoms, and the primary mechanism outcomes are salivary cortisol, plasma adiponectin, and serum BDNF. Secondary clinical outcomes include handgrip strength, positive and negative affect, cognitive function, and patterns of mood and attention captured by electroencephalogram (EEG). The changes in the primary clinical and mechanism outcomes from baseline to post-intervention (12 weeks after baseline) will be compared among the four groups. Mediation analyses will be performed to test whether the effects of qigong, mindfulness, and low-intensity physical exercise on depressive symptoms are mediated via their effects on cortisol, adiponectin, or BDNF levels. Support for the “mind” and “body” pathways would further increase scientific understanding of the antidepressant effect of qigong and inform its application as a treatment for depressive symptoms. 老年長期病患容易有抑鬱症狀，也容易發展成為抑鬱症。過往研究已顯示氣功可有效減少長者的抑鬱症狀，但是，這一療效的作用機制尚未確定。我們提出了兩條作用路徑，即「心靈」與「身體」作用路徑。「心靈」路徑是指氣功通過調節HPA軸（即下丘腦-垂體-腎上腺軸）來降低皮質醇水平，這一作用機制與靜觀干預類似。而「身體」路徑則是指氣功提高脂聯素水平，這一效果與低強度的運動鍛煉相似。此外，這兩條路徑還會提高神經滋養因子（BDNF）水平，促進大腦神經網絡的神經可塑性，以控制抑鬱症狀。 我們將進行招募300位老年長期病患隨機對照試驗，他們將被隨機分成四組，分別是（1）氣功組（八段錦），（2）靜觀干預組，（3）低強度運動組，（4）等候對照組。前三組將進行12周的干預。本次隨機對照試驗將進行干預前後的兩次評估，主要評估老年長期病患的抑鬱症狀，以及皮質醇、脂聯素和神經滋養因子水平。另外也會在干預前後測試老年長期病患的握力，並通過量表和腦電圖（EEG）檢查情緒和認知能力。我們將通過統計計算來檢驗氣功抗抑鬱的作用機制和各方面的療效。此項研究將加深對氣功的認識，幫助我們使用氣功造福長者。

15105621.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15105621.value: Major depression is a significant health problem with substantial costs to both individuals and society. The most commonly provided treatment for depression is antidepressant medication, which have only modest efficacy, are prone to causing side effects, have delayed action and do not benefit all patients. New treatments are needed that have minimal side effects and that will benefit patients who are resistant to antidepressants. Photobiomodulation, carried out by exposing the brain to low-energy laser irradiation (LLI), has shown therapeutic potentials on neurological disorders like stroke. Preclinical studies suggest that LLI effectively reduces depression-like behaviors in animals. Together, these findings suggest the non-invasive LLI treatment could be extended to alleviate major depression. One hypothesis for the development of depression is that due to a reduction in the generation of new neurons. While neurogenesis in humans remains controversial, there are animal models that can be used to evaluate this “neurogenic hypothesis” of depression. The proposed study will assess the efficacy of LLI in ameliorating or preventing depressive behaviors and whether any reduction in depressive behaviors is accompanied by the normalization of neurogenesis. Two rat models of depression will be used: the hypercortisolemia and chronic mild stress models. After two weeks of LLI treatment, the induction of depression-like behaviors will be evaluated. The animals will then be sacrificed for post-mortem brain analysis, which will include the assessment of neurogenesis, apoptosis and glial cell biology, and neurotrophic signaling in the hippocampus. The contributions of neurogenesis to the beneficial effects of LLI will be tested by ablating neurogenesis by the infusion of a cytostatic drug. To determine the molecular mechanisms involved in LLI-facilitated neurogenesis, the activation of the PI-3 kinase/Akt and Ras/Raf/MEK/Erk pathways will be examined both in vivo and in vitro. The proposed work will also assess the LLI treatment for side effects. The scientific premise of this proposal is that photobiomodulation is therapeutic for neurological disorders, such as major depression, as suggested by the neurogenic hypothesis of depression. Preliminary data from our laboratory support this central hypothesis. We have shown that two weeks of LLI prevents depression-like behavior induced by hypercortisolemia. This antidepressant effect was accompanied by increased hippocampal neurogenesis and dendritic maturation of new neurons. The proposed experiments will: (1) provide evidence in support of the neurogenic hypothesis of depression, (2) assess therapeutic mechanisms of LLI and (3) assess whether LLI has the potential to be an effective and non-invasive treatment for depression. 重度抑鬱症是一個嚴重的健康問題，對個人和社會都構成巨大負擔。抑鬱症最常用的治療方法是抗抑鬱藥，但其療效對患者不一，遲起效，亦容易引起副作用，並且不會使所有患者獲益。故此，治療重度抑鬱症需要新的其他治療方法，以達至減少副作用，並能幫助對抗抑鬱藥有抵抗力的患者。 光生物調節通過將大腦暴露在低能量下進行激光照射 (Low level laser therapy, LLI) 帶來療效，已顯示出對神經系統疾病的治療潛力，例如中風等神經疾患。基礎研究表明 LLI 可在動物實驗中有效減少抑鬱樣行為。總合而言，這些發現表明非侵入性 LLI 治療可能是緩解重度抑鬱症的治療方案之一。 抑鬱症發展的一種假設是：由於新的神經元產生減少，抑鬱症的病徵與病狀隨之出現 (此即’’ 神經元新生假設’’)。雖然人類的神經元新生仍然存在爭議，但是可用於評估這種“神經元新生假設”的動物模型卻提供了可研究的方向。此研究將評估 LLI 在改善或預防抑鬱行為及抑鬱行為是否伴隨著神經元新生而消減。 是項研究將使用兩種抑鬱症大鼠模型：高皮質醇血症和慢性輕度應激模型。伴隨著兩週的LLI治療後，將評估抑鬱樣行為的發生。實驗動物的大腦會被分析，其中將包括評估海馬體的神經元新生、細胞凋亡和神經膠質細胞生物學，以及神經營養信號傳遞。神經元新生對 LLI 治療效用的必需性將會通過注入細胞分裂抑製藥物來抵消神經元新生來測試。為了確定 LLI 促進的分子生物學機制， PI-3 激酶/Akt 和 Ras/Raf/MEK/Erk 信號通路將會以動物組織和細胞培養實驗測試。 是項研究的工作還將評估 LLI 治療的副作用。此提案的科學假說是光生物調節對能透過刺激神經元新生，從而治療重度抑鬱症和其他神經系統疾病。我們實驗室的初步數據支持這一中心假設。我們已經證明，兩週的 LLI 可以防止由高皮質醇血症引起的類似抑鬱行為。這種抗抑鬱作用伴隨著增加海馬神經元新生和新神經元的樹突成熟而出視。擬議的實驗將：（1）提供證據支持神經元新生假設，(2) 評估 LLI 的治療機制和 (3) 評估 LLI 是否可能成為一種有效且非侵入性的抑鬱症治療方法。

15105621.label: Realisation of objectives
15105621.value: All project objectives as outlined in the original application have been fully addressed and achieved to date, with no significant under-achievements encountered. The study employed two well-established animal models of depression: chronic corticosterone (CORT) administration and chronic mild stress (CMS) in rats. Low-level laser irradiation (LLI), delivered transcranially using near-infrared parameters of 820 nm wavelength, was applied as co-treatment. Objective 1: Fully achieved. Both CORT and CMS models successfully induced depression-like behaviors, as evidenced by increased the duration of immobility in the forced swim test (FST), reduced sucrose preference (anhedonia), and decreased time spent in centre zone in open-field test (OFT). Co-treatment with LLI significantly prevented these behavioral changes, reducing immobility times and restoring exploratory activity, supporting hypotheses 1a and 1b. Objective 2: Fully achieved. CORT and CMS treatments suppressed hippocampal neurogenesis, measured by reduced BrdU-positive cells and doublecortin staining in the dentate gyrus. LLI co-treatment effectively prevented this suppression, increasing neuroprogenitor cell proliferation and maturation, confirming hypotheses 2a and 2b. Objective 3: Fully achieved. Ablation of neurogenesis (using neurogenesis blockers such as AraC) vitiated the antidepressant-like effects of LLI in behavioral tests, demonstrating that intact neurogenesis is necessary for LLI's therapeutic benefits. Objective 4: Fully achieved. LLI activated the BDNF signaling pathway, with increased BDNF protein levels and downstream markers (e.g., phosphorylated TrkB, ERK/CREB activation) in the hippocampus. To further explore molecular mechanisms, transcriptomic analysis was conducted on fresh hippocampal tissue from selected groups. Results revealed differential expression of genes related to neuroplasticity, inflammation, and mitochondrial function, with BDNF and related pathways among the top enriched networks. In exploratory analyses, serum BDNF levels were measured as a potential peripheral biomarker; while no statistically significant difference was detected between groups, a positive trend toward elevation in LLI-treated animals was noted. Overall, these tissue-based and transcriptomic findings robustly confirm the hypothesis that BDNF signaling is activated by LLI and mediates its therapeutic effects Objective 5: Fully achieved. Unlike conventional antidepressants (which often cause weight gain or reduced libido), LLI did not induce significant changes in body weight, food intake, or sexual behavior metrics (e.g., mount latency in mating tests), indicating a favorable side-effect profile. No major problems were encountered that impacted achievement. Minor technical adjustments to laser parameters (e.g., optimizing fluence for penetration) were made early based on pilot data, ensuring consistent delivery without delays. All experiments were completed as planned, with adequate sample sizes and statistical significance (p < 0.05 in key outcomes).

15105621.label: Major findings and research outcome
15105621.value: This project investigated the antidepressant potential of low-level laser irradiation (LLI) in rat models of depression induced by chronic corticosterone (CORT) administration and chronic mild stress (CMS). The findings demonstrate that transcranial LLI exerts robust antidepressant-like effects through mechanisms involving enhanced neurogenesis and activation of the BDNF signaling pathway, without the side effects commonly associated with pharmacological antidepressants. In both models, LLI co-treatment significantly ameliorated depression-like behaviors. Rats exposed to stress and treated with LLI showed reduced immobility in the forced swim test (FST), increased sucrose preference, and improved exploration in the open-field test (OFT), compared to stress-only groups (CORT or CMS). LLI prevented the suppression of hippocampal neurogenesis induced by CORT and CMS, as evidenced by increased BrdU incorporation and a higher number of doublecortin-positive immature neurons in the dentate gyrus. Critically, ablation of neurogenesis abolished LLI’s behavioral benefits, establishing neurogenesis as a necessary mediator of its therapeutic effects. Molecular analyses revealed that LLI upregulated brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) expression and activated downstream signaling pathways (TrkB phosphorylation, ERK/CREB activation) in the hippocampus. Transcriptomic profiling of fresh hippocampal tissue identified broader gene expression changes, including enrichment in pathways related to neuroplasticity, mitochondrial function, and anti-inflammatory responses, further supporting BDNF-centric mechanisms. Importantly, LLI did not induce adverse effects such as changes in body weight or reduced libido, unlike conventional antidepressants. These outcomes support LLI as a novel, non-pharmacological antidepressant modality with mechanisms distinct from monoamine-based drugs. By stimulating mitochondrial function, reducing oxidative stress, and promoting neuroplasticity, LLI offers a safe alternative for depression treatment. Results have been published in one peer-reviewed article, are under review in another, are in preparation for a third, and have been presented at international conferences.

15105621.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15105621.value: The findings establish LLI as a promising, non-invasive antidepressant therapy, particularly for chronic stress-induced depression, given its neurogenesis-dependent mechanism, activation of BDNF signaling, broader transcriptomic effects, and minimal side effects. Further development could optimize treatment parameters for human translation and deepen mechanistic understanding at the molecular level. Proposed actions: - Conduct in vitro studies using primary neuronal or hippocampal cell cultures to dissect LLI’s direct effects on specific signaling pathways (e.g., BDNF/TrkB, mitochondrial bioenergetics, and anti-inflammatory cascades identified in transcriptomic analyses). - Perform follow-up preclinical studies in additional models to validate novel targets. - Initiate pilot human trials using transcranial near-infrared devices, incorporating peripheral biomarkers informed by current data. - Seek collaborative funding for mechanistic and multicenter clinical studies. Together, these steps could accelerate the development of LLI as an adjunct or alternative therapy for depression.

15105621.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15105621.value: Depression is a common mental health condition that affects mood, function and daily life of the affected individuals, which is often linked to reduction in new neurons growth and neurotransmitter imbalance. This research explored the potential therapeutic effect of a novel, non-invasive light therapy called low-level laser irradiation (LLI) as a new method to treat depression in animal models of depression. Using rats with induced depression-like behavior (which mimicks daily stress or surge in stress hormone), we found that LLI significantly reduced depression-like symptoms and lack of interest in rewards. It is likely to work by boosting the birth of new brain neurons (neurogenesis) in regions like the hippocampus and activating a trophic factors like brain-derived neurotrophic factor. Unlike other current antidepressants, which can cause weight gain or sexual side effects, LLI treatment showed none of these issues. The benefits is likely to be induced via increase of new neurons' birth, which highlights a mechanism for treating depression. This non-pharmacological and non-invasive approach could lead to new treatments for people with depression, especially those not responsive current options.

15106421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15106421.value: 活化 T 細胞核因子 5 (NFAT5) 是哺乳動物唯一的張力調節轉錄因子。在高滲压环境下，NFAT5 可以通过激活一系列轉錄程序来快速恢復細胞內滲透壓。一直以来，NFAT5被认为僅對暴露於顯著高滲壓环境的細胞至關重要。但是最近的研究发现NFAT5对诸多分子靶標都有调制作用。 張力驅動的核输入被認為是 NFAT5 調節细胞渗透压的主要途徑。在等滲條件下，NFAT5均匀分布於細胞質和細胞核中。滲压的增高导致NFAT5 在细胞核中高度富集，该现象极大可能与增强的核输入有关。然而負責 NFAT5 核輸入的分子机器尚未確定，高滲压如何促进這一過程的机理也知之甚少。 蛋白從細胞質到細胞核的輸入过程依賴於兩種類型的分子机器。如果被输入的蛋白包含經典核定位信號 (cNLS)，則由importin-α/β 異二聚體担任核輸入的分子机器： importin-α作為直接結合输入分子的cNLS的適配器，importin -β 作為受體將輸入蛋白-α/β-貨物複合物拉过细胞核上的核孔。如果貨物分子包含非經典NLS (ncNLS)，則由importin-β单独担任结合ncNLS的適配器和穿过核孔的受體。 NFAT5包含一個类似cNLS的多肽序列，它對於張力驅動的核輸入是必需的，但却不足以完全调控该过程。我們推测NFAT5 N端無結構的泛AED-NLS區域可能包含一個ncNLS，它可以招募特定的importin-β用於核輸入。此外，我們认为高滲压环境可能促進 NFAT5 ncNLS與其对应importin-β的結合，以促进其核輸入，從而激活 NFAT5 介導的滲透適應反應。 為了證實我們的假設，我們計劃首先使用siRNA篩選來識別NFAT5核輸入所需的特定importin-α/β 分子。我們還將通過对pan-AED-NLS區域進行突變掃描，以确认NFAT5的ncNLS的完整范围。我們將使用生化分析來表徵NFAT5 ncNLS與其对应importin-β之間的直接相互作用，並分析高滲压环境如何影響這種相互作用。我们還计划進行結構研究，以确认介導 NFAT5-ncNLS-importin-β相互作用的关键残基以及此相互作用如何受高滲压环境調節。我们已經獲得了大量的初步數據來證明我們研究計劃的可行性。我們相信這項研究將有助我们深入了解NFAT5如何在与生理和疾病相关的張力調節过程中发挥作用。

15200021.label: Project Objectives
15200021.value: To design and develop, through user profile generation, a generalized attacking framework for recommender systems (RecSys), based on which safe and reliable intelligent systems can be built for personalized recommendation. In view that performing white-box attacks with full knowledge of a target RecSys (i.e., model architecture and parameters) is unrealistic and inapplicable, we shall investigate possible means of generating fake user profiles for black-box attacks in RecSys, by employing reinforcement learning (RL) techniques with queries. To address the problem of inefficient and ineffective generation of user profiles through directly using RL techniques, which is brought about by a huge number of items (i.e., a large-scale discrete action space), we will develop a Hierarchical-structure Policy Gradient (HPG) framework for generating user profiles to attack black-box RecSys. In particular, the proposed HPG framework shall learn efficiently and effectively the strategy of selecting items and generating fake user profiles in large-scale discrete action space, with an aim to maximize long-run rewards. To devise, from the perspective of social relations, attacking strategies against black-box RecSys by incorporating the available social relations into user profiles generation, thereby testing the effectiveness of the proposed HPG framework for attacking black-box social recommendations. Particularly, in addition to generating user profiles from item perspective in item domain, the attackers can also build fake social connections with real existing users, and perform attacks from social perspective in social domain. Therefore, we shall consider exploiting the social relations in attacking black-box social RecSys. More specifically, to generate user profiles under the HPG framework, we plan to perform item selection from item perspective and social friend selection from social perspective. To craft strong attack strategies from the perspective of realistic user profiles through copying cross-domain user profiles directly, so as to evade fake user profiles detection from the target RecSys as well as test the effectiveness of the proposed HPG framework for attacking black-box recommender systems cross domains. In particular, instead of directly generating users with fake profiles, we shall embrace the proposed attacking HPG framework to learn the effective strategy of copying cross-domain user profiles. To develop an experimental prototype system with large-scaled real-world data to be collected from major social media sites and e-commerce sites, so as to test adequately the effectiveness of the theory and techniques proposed by this project.

15200021.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15200021.value: Recommender systems (RecSys) have become increasingly important in our daily lives since they play an important role in mitigating the information overload problem, especially in many user-oriented online services. The aim of RecSys is to identify a set of objects (i.e., items) that best match users’ explicit or implicit preferences, by utilizing the user and item interactions so as to improve the matching accuracy. With the fast advancement of deep neural networks (DNNs) in recent years, recommendation techniques become able to achieve promising performance toward accuracy (e.g., ranking metrics). However, recent studies have shown that existing deep neural networks are highly vulnerable to adversarial attacks, which has posed significant concerns for employing DNNs into RecSys. More specifically, adversaries intend to perform "data poison attacks" with well-designed user profiles to promote/demote a carefully chosen subset of items, so as to influence users’ beliefs towards items as much as possible. However, the majority of existing attacking methods in RecSys have been designed under white-box setting, where the attacker needs to have full knowledge of the target model (i.e., model architecture and parameters) and dataset. With privacy and security measures in RecSys, it is nevertheless unrealistic to access these kinds of knowledge assumed under white-box setting. In this project, we propose to develop a generalized framework to attack black-box RecSys. In particular, we propose to generate user profiles via a reinforcement learning (RL) based attacking method with queries. Due to real-world large-scale discrete action space in RecSys, we advocate a Hierarchical-structure Policy Gradient (HPG) framework to efficiently and effectively learn the strategy of user profiles generation. To demonstrate the generality and versatility of the proposed attacking framework via HPG, we'll further investigate its applications in two diverse yet representative real-life RecSys with readily available side information: 1) by considering the social based information platforms like Facebook, Instagram and Quora, we shall incorporate the available social relations information into user profile generation for attacking black-box social RecSys; 2) to take advantage of cross-domain platforms (such as Taobao vs JD.com, or Amazon vs eBay), we will devise a novel strategy to obtain real user profiles by copying cross-domain user profiles to attack black-box RecSys, to evade fake user profiles detection of defense strategies. Finally, an experimental prototype system will be developed to manifest the process of our proposed frameworks, and extensive testing will be conducted by using real-world data to evaluate our proposed research. 近年来，万维网日益普及并呈爆炸式增长，产生了大量数据，导致信息过载问题日益严重。因此，如何在适当的时间和地点提取满足用户信息需求的信息（产品或服务）已成为一个日益重要的问题。这推动了推荐系统的开发，其目的是通过利用用户和项目交互来识别最符合用户显性或隐性偏好的一组对象（即项目），从而提高匹配精度。 近年来，随着深度神经网络（DNN）的快速发展，推荐技术能够在准确性方面取得令人满意的性能（例如，排名指标）。然而，最近的研究表明，现有的深层神经网络具有高度的灵活性但也容易受敌方攻击，这对将DNN应用于推荐系统提出了重大挑战。更具体地说，对手打算使用精心设计的用户配置文件执行数据毒药攻击，以提升（或降级）精心选择的项目子集，从而尽可能影响用户对项目的信念。然而，推荐系统中现有的大多数攻击方法都是在白盒设置下设计的，攻击者需要完全了解目标模型（即模型架构和参数）和数据集。但由于推荐系统中的隐私和安全问题，在白盒设置下访问这些知识是不可能和不现实的。因此，我们在本项目中建议开发一个通用框架来攻击黑盒推荐系统。要做到这一点, 我们提出一种基于强化学习的攻击方法，通过查询学习生成用户配置文件。同时，针对大规模离散行为空间，提出一种分层结构的策略梯度框架，以有效地处理大规模离散行为空间以了解用户配置文件生成的策略。此外，我们还将进一步探讨如何将所提出的基于层次结构策略梯度的攻击框架应用到两个具有可用边信息的推荐场景中：1）通过基于如Facebook、Instagram和Quora等考虑了社交因素的信息平台，我们进一步将可用的社交关系信息整合到用户档案生成中，以攻击黑盒社交推荐系统；2） 利用跨域平台（例如淘宝vs.京东，亚马逊vs.易趣），我们引入一种新的策略，通过复制跨域用户配置文件来攻击黑盒推荐系统，从而获取真实用户配置文件，并达到对防御策略中的虚假用户配置文件检测的规避。

15200021.label: Realisation of objectives
15200021.value: For the first objective, we propose introducing a novel strategy to generate "fake" user profiles by copying cross-domain user profiles. Specifically, we develop CopyAttack+, a reinforcement learning (RL)-based black-box attacking framework [Fan et al. 2023], to effectively and efficiently select cross-domain user profiles from the source domain for attacking the target system. Additionally, we train a local surrogate system to mimic adversarial black-box attacks in the source domain, aiming to provide transferable signals that enhance the attacking strategy against the target black-box recommender system. Notably, traditional gradient-based techniques are impractical for black-box recommender system attacks, as they rely on the unrealistic assumption of full access to the target system and its dataset. In contrast, RL offers a natural paradigm for interacting with black-box systems: it enables the framework to receive feedback (rewards) and iteratively optimize the attack strategy [Zhao et al. 2019]—a key advantage that motivates our design of the RL-based CopyAttack+. Furthermore, drawing on the property of "transferability" [Liu et al. 2017], our local surrogate system is trained to simulate adversarial attacks in the source domain (Domain B), with the explicit goal of boosting the generalization of the attack strategy to the target black-box recommender system. For the second objective, we design a user profile selection approach based on the Hierarchical-structure Policy Gradient (HPG) framework [Fan et al. 2023]. The core goal of this selection task is to learn a strategy for identifying cross-domain user profiles—specifically, discovering a subset of source-domain users whose profiles can be injected into the target recommender system (System A) to achieve the objective of promoting a designated set of items. Two key challenges arise in this scenario: first, handling the large-scale discrete action space (i.e., the full set of available cross-domain user profiles); second, achieving satisfactory attack performance under the constraint of limited interaction resources with the target black-box recommender system. Most existing reinforcement learning (RL) techniques struggle to address such large discrete action spaces [Arulkumaran et al. 2017], as their decision-making time complexity scales linearly with the size of the action space—making them computationally infeasible here. To tackle these challenges, we propose a hierarchical-structure policy gradient network integrated with a masking mechanism, which models and optimizes the user profile selection process. For the third objective, we devise a novel Disentangled Contrastive Learning framework for Social Recommendations (DcRec) [Wu et al. 2022], which learns disentangled user representations from the item (collaborative) and social domains, and integrates disentangled contrastive learning to facilitate knowledge transfer between these disentangled representations for enhanced social recommendation performance. Social recommendation models typically leverage social relations to augment user representation learning. However, most existing approaches unify user representations for two distinct domains: user-item interactions (collaborative domain) and social connections (social domain). This unified paradigm fails to capture the heterogeneous behavioral patterns of users across the two domains, thereby limiting the expressiveness and discriminative power of the learned user representations. During the reporting period, we developed DcRec, which adheres to the general paradigm of self-supervised contrastive learning. Its core mechanism involves maximizing the representation consistency between different views of the same user instance, enabling effective disentanglement and knowledge transfer across the collaborative and social domains. For the fourth objective, we propose a novel strategy that leverages publicly accessible item attribute information (i.e., items’ knowledge graph, KG), which provides rich auxiliary knowledge to enhance the generation of fake user profiles. Specifically, we develop KGAttack [Chen et al. 2022], a knowledge graph-enhanced black-box attacking framework that employs deep reinforcement learning (DRL) to effectively learn attack policies. In this framework, the knowledge graph is seamlessly integrated into hierarchical policy networks, enabling the generation of high-quality fake user profiles for adversarial black-box attacks. For untargeted attacks on social recommender systems, attackers often construct malicious social relationships for fake users to boost attack efficacy. To address the limitations of existing methods, we first conduct preliminary studies that validate the effectiveness of two key factors—cross-community connections and cold-start items—in degrading recommendation performance. Building on these findings, we propose MultiAttack [Wang et al. 2024], a novel framework based on multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) that coordinates the generation of cold-start item profiles and cross-community social relations, enabling effective untargeted attacks on black-box social recommenders. For the fifth objective, we propose an experimental prototype system and conducting comprehensive validation of the theories and techniques presented in this project. To ensure the realism and scalability of our evaluations, we utilize large-scale real-world cross-domain datasets collected from major social media platforms and e-commerce sites. Specifically, our experiments employ three cross-domain datasets: MovieLen10M&Flixster (ML10M-FX) [Fan et al. 2021], MovieLen20M&Netflix (ML20M-NF), and Book-Crossing&Amazon-Book. We evaluate attack performance across two representative black-box recommender systems as target models: KGCN (a knowledge graph-enhanced model) and NeuMF (a hybrid collaborative filtering model). Results show that KG-incorporated attack methods (e.g., TargetAttack-KG, PoisonRec-KG) achieve significant performance gains on KGCN, demonstrating that the seamless integration of knowledge graphs (KG) with hierarchical policy networks facilitates the generation of high-quality fake user profiles—key to enhancing attack efficacy on black-box systems. Additionally, our proposed KGAttack outperforms existing baselines on NeuMF under the black-box setting and nearly surpasses all comparison methods across both target models. This validates the effectiveness of knowledge-enhanced hierarchical policy networks for fake user profile generation and confirms the model’s adaptability to diverse recommender system architectures. To further verify attack effectiveness on social recommender systems, we extend evaluations to traditional collaborative filtering-based methods (e.g., SBPR) and state-of-the-art graph neural network (GNN)-based methods (e.g., SocialLGN). The MultiAttack framework significantly degrades the recommendation performance of both model categories, highlighting its strong effectiveness and generalization capability for untargeted black-box attacks on social recommendation systems.
