rows: To design and develop, through user profile generation, a generalized attacking framework for recommender systems (RecSys), based on which safe and reliable intelligent systems can be built for personalized recommendation. In view that performing white-box attacks with full knowledge of a target RecSys (i.e., model architecture and parameters) is unrealistic and inapplicable, we shall investigate possible means of generating fake user profiles for black-box attacks in RecSys, by employing reinforcement learning (RL) techniques with queries.

To address the problem of inefficient and ineffective generation of user profiles through directly using RL techniques, which is brought about by a huge number of items (i.e., a large-scale discrete action space), we will develop a Hierarchical-structure Policy Gradient (HPG) framework for generating user profiles to attack black-box RecSys. In particular, the proposed HPG framework shall learn efficiently and effectively the strategy of selecting items and generating fake user profiles in large-scale discrete action space, with an aim to maximize long-run rewards.

To devise, from the perspective of social relations, attacking strategies against black-box RecSys by incorporating the available social relations into user profiles generation, thereby testing the effectiveness of the proposed HPG framework for attacking black-box social recommendations. Particularly, in addition to generating user profiles from item perspective in item domain, the attackers can also build fake social connections with real existing users, and perform attacks from social perspective in social domain. Therefore, we shall consider exploiting the social relations in attacking black-box social RecSys. More specifically, to generate user profiles under the HPG framework, we plan to perform item selection from item perspective and social friend selection from social perspective.

To craft strong attack strategies from the perspective of realistic user profiles through copying cross-domain user profiles directly, so as to evade fake user profiles detection from the target RecSys as well as test the effectiveness of the proposed HPG framework for attacking black-box recommender systems cross domains. In particular, instead of directly generating users with fake profiles, we shall embrace the proposed attacking HPG framework to learn the effective strategy of copying cross-domain user profiles.

To develop an experimental prototype system with large-scaled real-world data to be collected from major social media sites and e-commerce sites, so as to test adequately the effectiveness of the theory and techniques proposed by this project.

15200021.label: Major findings and research outcome
15200021.value: To address adversarial attack challenges for black-box recommender systems (no access to internal data/architecture), we propose KGAttack—a knowledge-enhanced framework. Under black-box constraints, KGAttack uses knowledge graphs (KGs) to improve fake user profile generation from massive items, with deep reinforcement learning (DRL) optimizing realism and adversarial intent. KGAttack integrates advanced components: a state representation module encoding sparse interaction/KG data into low-dimensional vectors, and a hierarchical policy network (high-level: global objectives like attack success; low-level: local actions like item selection). This design outperforms flat networks in attack effectiveness and profile quality. We validate KGAttack on three real datasets (MovieLens, Amazon Beauty, Yelp) under strict black-box settings (only top-K recommendations observed). Cross-model tests cover NeuMF (deep), Pinsage (GNN), and KGCN (KG-enhanced GNN). An ablation study confirms each component’s indispensable role. In complementary work, CopyAttack+ targets black-box systems via cross-domain profile transfer. Unlike KGAttack’s scratch generation, it copies source-domain profiles (via RL-based policy gradient networks) in three steps: select transferable users, refine profiles to match target domain, inject into target. Inspired by adversarial transferability, we train a local surrogate system (source data, mainstream architecture) to simulate target behavior. This captures transferable signals without extensive target interactions, cutting cost and boosting adaptability. CopyAttack+ is tested on the same three datasets (split into source/target). It outperforms baselines (single-domain RL, rule-based cross-domain, transferable attacks) in success rate, transferability, and efficiency. In-depth analysis reveals how user selection, refinement, and surrogate design impact performance.

15200021.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15200021.value: Our future work on recommender system adversarial attacks will focus on targeted strategies for source-domain-absent items (solving existing frameworks’ cross-domain item overlap reliance) and item demotion, plus integrating side information (user demographics, item content) to boost adversarial profile realism; we also propose MultiAttack, a social recommender attack framework that uses multi-agent collaboration to generate cold-start item profiles (for systems prioritizing new items) and fake cross-community social connections—disrupting social recommendation logic, with experiments on CiaoDVD/Epinions showing it outperforms baselines. While more cold-start recommendations raise exploration/diversity (valuable for dynamic preferences), over-exploration by well-trained models causes unnecessary costs (computational overhead, lower engagement), leading to missed opportunities and financial losses in practice (e.g., e-commerce); moreover, cold-start items include new, niche, and restricted ones, so attacks can push mismatched content (e.g., documentaries to action fans) or harmful content to minors, causing platform financial losses (fines, reputation damage) and social harm, making robust, attack-resistant recommenders academically and practically urgent.

15200021.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15200021.value: This research project focuses on strengthening the security and reliability of recommender systems—widely used in e-commerce and social media—by developing innovative AI-driven tools to simulate realistic "fake user" attacks. Leveraging techniques like reinforcement learning, knowledge graphs, and disentangled contrastive learning, it creates targeted fake user profiles, coordinates cross-domain/social attacks, and tests these methods on large real-world datasets against popular recommender system models. Its core significance lies in uncovering hidden vulnerabilities in black-box recommender systems that traditional methods overlook, addressing critical gaps in understanding how such systems can be manipulated. The practical value is substantial: it provides platforms with scalable testing frameworks to proactively fortify defenses, shields users from biased or manipulated recommendations, and ultimately fosters fairer, more trustworthy digital services that users can rely on.

15200321.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15200321.value: 實時數據流的網絡協議適配：架構、算法和實現

15200321.label: Project Objectives
15200321.value: To develop a protocol adaptation architecture for real-time streaming. Recently, new UDP mechanisms have been developed to fit the increasingly diverse scenarios of real-time streaming systems. Each UDP mechanism manages *some* application layer QoE metrics given different network layer conditions. Here, *QoE metrics* refer to the application layer perceived loss, delay, and throughput; and *network conditions* refer to the network layer bandwidth, network layer delay, transmission loss (in-network packet loss), and transmission error (bit error). The emerging UDP mechanisms introduce a unique challenge: How to organize different UDP mechanisms under one umbrella to holistically support the overall QoE (as a function of the QoE metrics)? In this project, we propose ReCon, a new architecture that can configure the UDP mechanisms in runtime to adapt to network condition changes and maximize the overall QoE. We specifically study three UDP mechanisms, which we list below. To model the behaviors of joint UDP configurations and develop a protocol adaptation algorithm using an MPC framework. The ultimate goal is to develop an algorithm that, given a changed network condition, finds a (re)configuration strategy of the UDP mechanism(s), so that the QoE is maximized. There are three challenges: 1) How to characterize the joint behaviors of the UDP mechanisms, i.e., what are their conflicts and what are the overhead of runtime adaptation? 2) How to design the algorithm to maximize the accumulative QoE? 3) How to address the practical issues such as online computation complexity? We first analyze the interplay of the UDP mechanisms and develop models for the joint performance of the UDP mechanisms. As the problem intrinsically has a feedback-control structure, we develop the algorithm using an MPC framework. We innovatively observe that our problem has a longest K-steps structure and we plan to develop algorithms accordingly. Finally, we develop schemes to make our algorithm practical. To develop a protocol adaptation algorithm through reinforcement learning. There are scenarios that is difficult to characterize and an MPC based algorithm can perform sub-optimally. We thus seek a reinforcement learning (RL) based approach since our problem requires control decisions. There are two challenges: With diverse network conditions, protocol configurations, and video features, the RL can have a large number of state-action pairs, thus how to reduce the number of adjustable parameters in the RL? and 2) How to train this RL, i.e., the policy of the RL, with high accuracy? We will develop a deep reinforcement learning (DRL) based algorithm, where a neural network (NN) model will be used to reduce the parameters. To train this RL, we will use a novel imitation learning approach to generate the training data and train the RL. To develop a reference implementation of ReCon. We will develop a reference implementation of ReCon based on WebRTC. We design ReCon to be application-agnostic. To ensure that a real-time streaming application can use ReCon without knowing the internal details, we will develop a module-on-demand-loading (MODL) system. The MODL system can flexibly generate a ReCon image with a minimum resource footprint given the functional requirements of the application. MODL will make our research to be easily deployable to support a wide range of applications.

15200321.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15200321.value: 隨著 COVID-19 的爆發，課堂、商務會議、學術會議和其他 面對面的會議變成了在線進行。以此帶來的對交互式實時流媒體的需求前所未有。 Zoom、Microsoft Teams等平臺可以提供基本支持， 然而，他們的用戶體驗(QoE) 都有很大的提升空間。例如，來自手機的呼入手機不穩定，仍然難以令人滿意。為了支持嚴格的延遲要求，實時流媒體系統采用 UDP 作為底層傳輸協議。遺憾的是默認的 UDP協議無法適應日益多樣化的網絡場景和應用層 QoE。最近，UDP 開發了一些改進，如新的UDP 校驗和的機制，新的包級別轉發糾錯和新的接收緩沖區大小調整策略。一個具體例子為新的 UDP-Lite 協議，定義了部分校驗，可以使得具有少量誤碼的數據包不被丟棄。此功能可以減少易錯環境中的丟包率，對有一定容錯能力的上次應用程序提高用戶體驗。UDP-Lite提供了可以配置不同的校驗和長度的手段，可以在校驗處理延遲和丟包率之間進行權衡，提高整體應用層用戶體驗QoE。 這些UDP機制是獨立開發的。它們如何聯合應用和他們的集體行為還不清楚。另外配置需要在當前的UDP 在流會話開始時進行，並在生命周期內保持不變。如何在運行時即時調整，以適應網絡變化尚不清楚。這些新的 UDP 機制引入了有趣的問題：如何組織不同的 UDP 機制在一起形成聚合優勢？哪些UDP 機制會產生沖突以及如何表征它們？什麽是適當的算法來管理 不同網絡場景下的不同UDP機制？ 本項目旨在系統地回答這些問題。在這個項目中，我們提出了一個新的架構，ReCon，可以整體調整 UDP 機制以適應網絡狀況的變化並支持 QoE。首先，我們分析 UDP 機制的行為並開發新模型以表征它們的聯合性能。有了這些模型，我們開發了一種新的實時算法，這個算法使用模型預測控制 (MPC) 框架，進而進行自適應調整。其次，我們發現在一些網絡場景中的UDP機制難以表征，因此我們開發一種新的強化學習算法。最後，我們開發ReCon 的參考實現，並部署於一個由谷歌支持的用於實時通信的開源框架WebRTC。 我們的項目在協議適配提案和我們計劃使用的算法方面都是新穎的進展。我們還將通過開發教育材料和合作來擴大項目的影響，與行業（例如，華為）一起試驗 ReCon 架構和算法。

15200321.label: Realisation of objectives
15200321.value: I. Overview: The primary objective of this project is to study lossy network to support new applications in video. In the first half of the project, we studied how to handle the network dynamics with QoE quality assurance. This part is related to the realizatino of Objective 1, 2, and 3. With the fast development of new video representation, in the second half of the project, we studied new volumetric videos and 3D Gaussian splatting videos, where 3D Gaussian videos further improved volumetric video representation with Gaussian ellipsoid, where the video can have smaller data and more realistic to human visual percentation. This part is related to the realizatino of Objective 1, 3, 4. We specifically describe our achievement in (1) loss and bitrate adapation, (2) volumetric video streaming, and (3) 3D gaussian splatting streaming. Before going to the details, we summarize the deliverables: Knowledge creation: 11 papers 1. Two were published in the first half and Nine were published in the second half of the project 2. Six conference papers: one IEEE INFOCOM (CCF A), two ACM Multimedia (CCF A), one IEEE Virtual Reality (CCF A), one AAAI (CCF A), one ICME. 3. Five journal papers: one IEEE TMC, one ACM TOSN, three IEEE IoTJ. Education: 1. Two Ph.D. graduated. 2. Two undergraduates trained. Broader impact: 1. Part of our work was adopted by Huawei through a collaboration project. II. Detailed progress report: 1. Loss and bitrate adaptation: We conducted a study on joint loss and bitrate adaptation in real-time video streaming. Our insight is to slightly sacrifice the bitrate and video quality to trade for the most significant delay to maximize the overall QoE. We propose Oppugno, an integrated framework that achieves joint loss adaptation and bitrate adaptation towards maximized QoE in realtime streaming services. Oppugno leverages existing UDP mechanisms and employs an advanced deep reinforcement learning algorithm Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), to adaptively select optimal actions based on network conditions. Trace-driven experiments demonstrate the superiority of our framework, which outperforms the SOTA work by 3.9% ∼ 11.6%. This work titled “Towards Joint Loss and Bitrate Adaptation in Realtime Video Streaming” was published in IEEE ICME 2022. We conducted a study on server-driven joint adaptation of loss and bitrate for multi-party real-time video streaming. In this paper, we propose the SJA framework, which is, to our best knowledge, the first server-driven joint loss and bitrate adaptation framework in multi-party realtime video streaming services towards maximized QoE. We comprehensively design an appropriate QoE model for MRVS services to capture the interplay among perceptual quality, variations, bitrate mismatch, loss damage, and streaming delay. We mathematically formulate the QoE maximization problem in MRVS services. A Lyapunov based relaxation and the SJA algorithm are further designed to address the optimization problem with close-to-optimal performance. Evaluations show that our framework can outperform the SOTA solutions by 18.4% ∼ 46.5%. This work titled “SJA: Server-driven Joint Adaptation of Loss and Bitrate for Multi-Party Realtime Video Streaming” was published in IEEE INFOCOM 2023. 2. Volumetric video streaming: In “P2VS: Progressive Partition-Based Volumetric Video Streaming under Network Dynamics”, ACM Multimedia, we studied how to handle volumetric videos with Quality of Experiences under network dynamics. We developed a progressive partition-based technique. In “Cell Configuration for QoE-Aware Volumetric Video Streaming via Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning”, ACM Transactions on Sensor Networks, we developed a cell configuration technique, and we adjust it through a hierarchical reinforcement learning approach. 15200321.label: Major findings and research outcome
15200321.value: The progress of the field is fast. With the development of underlying network software framework, e.g., new UDP sub-protocols, we developed loss and bitrate adaptation mechanisms that can marry upper layer QoE for real-time video streaming. Our insight is to slightly sacrifice the bitrate and video quality to trade for the most significant delay to maximize the overall QoE. We propose Oppugno (ICME22), an integrated framework that achieves joint loss adaptation and bitrate adaptation towards maximized QoE in realtime streaming services. Oppugno leverages existing UDP mechanisms and employs an advanced deep reinforcement learning algorithm Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), to adaptively select optimal actions based on network conditions. We also conducted a study on server-driven joint adaptation of loss and bitrate for multi-party real-time video streaming (INFOCOM23). In this paper, we propose the SJA framework, which is, to our best knowledge, the first server-driven joint loss and bitrate adaptation framework in multi-party realtime video streaming services towards maximized QoE. We comprehensively design an appropriate QoE model for MRVS services to capture the interplay among perceptual quality, variations, bitrate mismatch, loss damage, and streaming delay. We mathematically formulate the QoE maximization problem in MRVS services. A Lyapunov based relaxation and the SJA algorithm are further designed to address the optimization problem with close-to-optimal performance. The QoE has to connect with video characteristics and there are fast development in the video community. We studied streaming of volumetric videos and gaussian splatting. Specifically, we studied how to handle volumetric videos with Quality of Experiences under network dynamics (Multimedia25) where we developed a progressive partition-based technique. We developed a cell configuration technique, and we adjust it through a hierarchical reinforcement learning approach (TOSN25). We further study on-demand volumetric video streaming and we developed passive frame dropping techniques for video transmission (IoTJ24a). We studied volumetric video streaming in more interactive scenarios and we studied prompt engineering. We studied bitrate adaptation under prompted online adaptation (IoTJ24b) and prompt with inference (TMC24). We studied privacy issues in volumetric videos with a new reconstruction attack on volumetric videos (AAAI25). 3D Gaussian Splatting is one most recent advance in 3D scene representation. We were one of the first to study how to stream 3D Gaussian videos (VR25) as well as compression and streaming of 3D Gaussian videos while taking spatial heterogeneity into consideration.

15200321.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15200321.value: First of all, video quality of experience is an important topic. Streaming videos, under bandwidth constraints and software constraints (e.g., UDP and TCP) is an important topic. The development of network layer software stack is important yet a slow and gradual process. As a comparison, the developoment of is videos is much faster (as shown by volumetric video and 3D gaussian splatting). Therefore, there are potential to explore the video characteristics and adapt to these. This is an approach that this project took during the study.

15200321.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15200321.value: In the past years, the demand for interactive real-time video streaming is unprecedented. There are challenges amid opportunities. On the one hand, the applications have stringent delay requirements and on the other hand, lossy transmissions are tolerated to certain extent for video related applications. To improve the overall quality of experience (QoE) of real-time streaming, in this project we visited two important aspects: the underlying network support and the application characteristics. On the network support side, we studied new characteristics of UDPs, e.g., error correction, buffer size, etc., which provide opportunities to trade-off delay, loss, and errors. On the application side, we studied new advances in volumetric videos and 3D Gaussian splatting, which provide opportunities to trade-off QoE and loss. Overall, we advanced understanding of real-time streaming with contrasting objectives of QoE, bandwidth restrictions, and software restrictions. Our project results have contributed to the development of industry, and we have trained both postgraduate and undergraduate students.

15200421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15200421.value: Development of wearable electronics that can be truly worn on human body with desired functional performance, uncompromised safety and good wearing comfort is a common goal of scholars and professionals worldwide from a broad range of disciplines. One key challenge is to develop a kind of flexible materials that can integrate both advanced functions and common cloth advantages (i.e. conformable, breathable, stretchable, etc.) with a general strategy. Existed materials for wearable electronics usually possess excellent desired functions and/or some good mechanical properties based on some unique technical routes or materials. Inspired by human skin that is multifunctional, soft, breathable and highly stretchable via the generation of surface buckling, this project aims to design and study a new kind of hierarchically buckled porous microstructured textiles (HBPMTs) by rational surface design and engineering of stretchable textile substrates (such as elastic fibers and fabrics) with hierarchically buckled and porous microarchitectures using common brick materials (such as frequently-used polymers and functional nanomaterials). Based on previous work done by the applicant, a general physicochemical strategy consisted of mechanical control, selective swelling, interfacial self-assembly, thermal annealing and controllable releasing will be developed. The influential factors such as pre-stretched ratio, swelling degree, polymer concentration, annealing temperature and releasing rate on the formation of HBPMTs with controllable components and architectures will be investigated systematically. Through controllable design and construction of brick materials as buckled porous architectures along the surface of textile substrates, the resultant HBPMTs are expected to introduce the advanced functions of brick materials and meanwhile maintain the inherent advantages of textile substrates such as flexibility, air-permeability and stretchability. Moreover, the porous structures hierarchically contouring to the textile surface at the microscale also establish a micro-bridge connecting macroscopic fibers and functional nanomaterials, which possesses flexible and versatile designability for rational incorporation of functional materials with more exposed surface area for higher performance. The obtained HBPMTs are expected to maintain high interfacial activities of incorporated functional materials for a kind of stretchable smart wearables with high performance. Besides the experimental study, system modeling will also be carried out to quantitatively analyze various influential factors in order for the improvement and optimization of constructed HBPMTs. This study will lead to a new kind of modified textile materials that can achieve both advanced functions with controllable high performance and indispensable wearable comfort requirements for a kind of truly wearable systems with customized advanced functions. 開發可真正穿戴在人體上並具有所需功能性、安全性和良好舒適性的可穿戴電子設備是全球廣泛學科的學者和專業人員的共同目標。一個關鍵的挑戰是開發一種柔性材料，可以將先進的功能和常見的布料優勢（即貼合性、透氣性、可拉伸性等）相結合。基於一些獨特的技術路線或材料，現有的可穿戴電子材料通常具有出色的功能和/或一些良好的機械性能。受人體皮膚多功能、柔軟、透氣和表面高度拉伸性的啟發，該項目旨在通過結合可拉伸紡織基材的表面工程設計（例如彈性纖維和織物）與普通磚材料（例如常用的聚合物和功能性納米材料），研究一種新型分層屈曲多孔微結構紡織品（HBPMTs）。在申請人之前工作的基礎上，將開發包括機械控制、選擇性溶脹、界面自組裝、熱退火和可控釋放的策略。將系統地研究預拉伸比、溶脹度、聚合物濃度、退火溫度和釋放速率等對HBPMTs的影響。通過紡織基材表面設計和構建磚塊材料作為屈曲多孔結構，所得到的 HBPMT 有望引入磚塊材料的先進功能，同時保持紡織基材的固有優勢，如柔韌性、透氣性和拉伸性。此外，在微觀尺度上紡織品表面的多孔結構還建立了連接宏觀纖維和功能納米材料的微橋，具有靈活和通用的設計能力，可以增大表面積以獲得更高的性能。HBPMT 有望保持摻入功能材料的高界面活性，用於一種高性能的可拉伸智能可穿戴設備。除了實驗研究外，還將進行系統建模，定量分析各種影響因素，以改進和優化構建的 HBPMT。這項研究將制備一種新型的改性紡織材料，它既具有可控高性能，又具有定制功能為可穿戴系統提供穿戴舒適性。

15201121.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15201121.value: As the shipping industry transports more than 80% of the goods traded worldwide, the safety of ships is vital for society. In 2019, there were 2,815 shipping accidents, up 5% from 2018 and resulting in losses of at least US$2 billion. To improve maritime safety, the International Maritime Organization (IMO) has established international resolutions on the proper maintenance and operations of ships, and has empowered maritime authorities to inspect visiting foreign ships, namely port state control (PSC), to verify that all ships comply with international regulations. Due to the high cost of ship inspections and the limited number of inspectors, less than 5% of ships are inspected. Selecting potential substandard ships in advance to improve inspection efficiency and reduce inspection costs is essential for effective PSC. Current ship selection schemes rely on the sum of the scores of various factors, such as ship age and type, in which the scores are determined based on expert knowledge. However, the subjective value of these scores can be biased, compromising the effectiveness of these schemes. According to ship inspection and ship accident databases, in 2018, approximately 10% of the ships selected for inspection had no deficiencies, whereas 60% of the ships involved in serious accidents were not selected for inspection up to three months prior to these accidents. Concerns about accidents caused by substandard ships and limited inspection resources call for a more effective ship selection method to effectively enforce PSC. With the increased PSC inspection data accumulated in recent years, it is now feasible to make informed ship inspection decisions based on data. By leveraging publicly available PSC inspection data and recent development in data analytics, the proposed project aims to design a prediction-informed optimization method that can effectively identify substandard ships for inspection and efficiently direct inspectors to inspect the selected ships. Case studies using inspection data from the Port of Hong Kong will be conducted to validate the proposed method and formulate operational guidelines for maritime authorities. This study will contribute to both theory and practice. The proposed method will address transportation problems that are seemingly different yet share fundamental similarities, such as traffic signal control based on predicted traffic flows. The results of this project will be invaluable in preventing substandard shipping and protecting maritime transportation, thereby supporting the IMO’s goal of ensuring “the safety, security and environmental performance of international shipping.” 由於全球80%以上的貨物運輸由航運業完成，船舶安全對社會至關重要。2019年全球共發生2815起航運事故，較2018年增長5%，造成了至少20億美元的經濟損失。為提升海上航行安全，國際海事組織（International Maritime Organization, IMO）制定了關於船舶維護和安全操作的國際條例，並授權各海事管理部門檢查到訪港口的外籍船舶是否符合這些條例。該檢查被稱為港口國監督檢查（port state control, PSC）。 由於船舶檢查成本高、檢查人員數量有限，只有不到5%的外籍船舶能被所到訪的港口檢查。提前識別潛在的不合格船舶是提高檢查效率、降低檢查成本的有效手段，因此對於有效實施港口國監督檢查至關重要。現有的選船方案依賴于專家經驗，考慮船齡、船型等因素從而得到船舶綜合風險分數。然而，這些基於主觀經驗的分數可能會有偏差，進而降低該選船方案的有效性。船舶檢查資料庫和事故資料庫顯示，在2018年被檢查的船舶中約10%沒有發現缺陷，而60%發生嚴重事故的船舶在事故發生前的三個月內都沒有被所到訪的國外港口選中進行港口國監督檢查。因此，採用更有效的選船方法，從而減少不合格船舶和有限港口國監督檢查資源造成的船舶事故非常有必要。 近年來，港口國監督檢查資料的不斷積累使得基於實際檢查資料做出明智的船舶檢查決策變得可行。通過利用公開獲取的港口國監督檢查資料和最新的高效資料分析方法，本項目旨在設計一套基於預測的優化方法以高效識別需要檢查的不合格船舶並實現檢查員的高效分配。本項目將使用香港港的港口國監督檢查資料進行案例研究以驗證所提出的方法，並根據模型結果制定海事管理部門的操作指南。 該專案將有助於理論和實踐研究。其所提出的方法可以進一步用於解決看似不同、但本質上相似的交通問題，例如基於預測交通流的交通信號控制。該專案的研究成果將有助於防止低標準航運並促進航運業健康發展，從而助力國際海事組織確保“國際航運的安全、安保和環保”的目標。

15201121.label: Realisation of objectives
15201121.value: The three objectives of this project have been realized on time through the joint effort of all participants. Port state control (PSC) is the safeguard of maritime transport achieved by inspecting foreign visiting ships and supervising them to rectify the non-compliances detected. Ship risk profile (SRP) is currently the most common method of quantifying ship risk. To achieve Objective 1, we propose a data-driven bi-objective nonlinear programming model, referred to as the SRP+ model, to optimize the thresholds in the original SRP framework. To solve the model, we first linearize the nonlinear optimization model using the big-M method, and then develop an augmented epsilon-constraint method to transform the bi-objective model to a single-objective model and obtain all Pareto optimal solutions. In addition to proposing the SRP+ model, we modify the structure of the traditional decision tree (DT) to integrate the prediction and the decision parts of the problem, which we call integrated DT. Moreover, we innovatively propose the concept of “similar sets” and use the similar sets to select the hyperparameter tuple leading to the best decision optimization problem in the integrated decision tree. We further propose an innovative optimization framework for high-risk vessel selection. The essence of the optimization framework is to accurately rank all ships with respect to their risk levels predicted by machine learning (ML) models. The loss functions of the tailored ML models follow a "smart predict then optimize" criterion named cumulative detected deficiency number (CDDN), which is motivated by the characteristics of the decision problem. This inventive metric transforms the assessment of ranking accuracy to the area of the segmented histogram of the recognized deficiency number, which bypasses the computationally intensive training step of rankings and is easy to compute. Following this, three types of decision tree models are developed, which differ from each other in the varying integration levels of CDDN. Particularly, we rigorously prove that one integration method yields a tree structure identical to that of traditional DT models. Moreover, we develop two data-driven ship risk prediction frameworks using features the same as or derived from the current ship selection scheme. Like existing ship risk prediction models, the proposed frameworks are of black-box nature whose working mechanism is opaque. To improve model explainability, local explanation of the prediction of individual ships by the Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) is provided. Furthermore, we innovatively extend the local SHAP model to a near linear-form global surrogate model which is fully explainable. We further use PSC inspection data to design ship maintenance plans for ship operators to minimize overall operational costs. To this end, we use a smart predict-then-optimize (SPO) method to design an ensemble of SPO trees (SPOTs). Each SPOT uses an SPO loss function that measures the sub-optimality of the decisions derived from the predicted parameters. By exploiting the structural properties of the optimization problem analyzed in this study, we demonstrate that training an SPOT for this problem can be simplified tremendously by using the relative class frequency of true labels within a leaf node to yield a minimum SPO loss. The port state control officer (PSCO) routing problem involves selecting ships for inspection and determining the inspection sequence for available PSCOs, aiming to identify the highest number of deficiencies. In Objective 2, we adopt a decision-focused learning framework, integrating the PSCO routing problem into the ML models’ training process. However, as the PSCO routing problem is NP-hard and plugging it into the training process of ML models requires that it be solved numerous times, computational complexity and scalability present significant challenges. To address these issues, we first convert the PSCO routing problem into a compact model using undominated inspection templates, enhancing the model’s solution efficiency. Next, we employ a family of surrogate loss functions based on noise-contrastive estimation (NCE) for the ML model, requiring a solution pool treating suboptimal solutions as noise samples. This pool represents a convex hull of feasible solutions, avoiding frequent reoptimizations during the ML model’s training process. In the last phase, to validate the models, algorithms, and analyses obtained in our studies, case studies using the PSC data from the Port of Hong Kong were performed. Our findings suggest that accurate predictions do not guarantee good decisions; the decision-focused learning framework’s performance may depend on the optimization problem size and the training dataset size; and using a solution pool containing noise samples strikes a balance between training efficiency and decision performance. Numerical experiments show that the proposed models can save at least millions to tens of millions of inspection cost in Hong Kong dollars for the Hong Kong port each year, and up to 837 million inspection cost in Hong Kong dollars all over the world per year. In terms of managerial insights, case study results suggest that the threshold of the total weighting points to classify a ship as high-risk ship should be slightly increased, the thresholds of ship age should be significantly increased, the threshold of historical deficiency number should be increased, while the threshold of historical ship detention times should be decreased.

15201121.label: Major findings and research outcome
15201121.value: Theoretically, we have proposed a number of methods that integrate prediction with optimization, prescribing high-quality decisions for transportation and logistics problems. We propose an integrated decision tree to better leverage the decision problem to train the model and use the concept of “similar set” in data sets for hyperparameter tuning. We design a new loss function named cumulative detected deficiency number, which transforms the assessment of ranking accuracy to the area of the segmented histogram of the recognized deficiency number, thus bypassing the computationally intensive training step of rankings. We fully integrate the decision problem into the design of decision trees to form smart predict-then-optimize trees. We further prove that the training of these smart predict-then-optimize trees for the ship inspection problem can be simplified tremendously by using the relative class frequency of true labels within a leaf node. To address the NP-hard port state control officer routing problem, we adopt a decision-focused learning framework, integrating the routing problem into the machine learning models’ training process. We further apply scalable approaches for this integrated learning framework. Finally, we improve model explainability by the Shapley additive explanations and extend them to a near linear-form global surrogate model which is fully-explainable. Practically, we have proposed an SRP+ model, which maintains the same structure as the current decision practice but achieves significantly higher effectiveness in targeting substandard ships. The numerical experiments have demonstrated the potential of the proposed methods in identifying deficiencies and saving inspection costs.

15201121.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15201121.value: To address the practical problems arising from the project, we have identified two major theoretical problems that are worth future efforts. The first one is “fundamental challenge of data analytics,” i.e., it is hard, if not impossible, to conduct a rigorous comparison of an artificial intelligence method and the current practice, for some problems, such as the port state control problem. We have proposed some ways of partially addressing this challenge; however, future work is needed to gain deeper insights into it. The second one is to incorporate domain knowledge into the design of machine learning models, e.g., an older ship is expected to have more deficiencies than a new one, when all the other conditions of the two ships are identical. This type of domain knowledge can be incorporated into some machine learning models; however, whether they can be incorporated into other commonly used machine learning models is an interesting theoretical question. We will try to tackle these two questions in the future.

15201121.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15201121.value: To improve maritime safety, the International Maritime Organization (IMO) has established international resolutions on the proper maintenance and operations of ships, and has empowered maritime authorities to inspect visiting foreign ships, namely port state control (PSC), to verify that all ships comply with international regulations. Current ship selection schemes rely on the sum of the scores of various factors, such as ship age and type, in which the scores are determined based on expert knowledge. However, the subjective value of these scores can be biased, compromising the effectiveness of these schemes. Concerns about accidents caused by substandard ships and limited inspection resources call for a more effective ship selection method to effectively enforce PSC. We leveraged publicly available PSC inspection data and designed a prediction-informed optimization method that effectively identifies substandard ships for inspection and efficiently directs inspectors to inspect the selected ships. Case studies using inspection data from the Port of Hong Kong validated the performance of the proposed method. The results of this project contribute to preventing substandard shipping and protecting maritime transportation, thereby supporting the IMO’s goal of ensuring “the safety, security and environmental performance of international shipping.”

15201321.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15201321.value: Structural Health Monitoring (SHM) is an emerging technology, aiming at the on-line diagnosis of material/structural damage. Successful SHM allows for the safety enhancement of structures, evaluation of their residual lifetime, thus avoiding exorbitant maintenance costs. Exhibiting high sensitivities to damage, Nonlinear Guided Waves (NGWs) show great promise to the early detection of damage or even its precursors. However, NGWs are also vulnerable to other non-damage-related nonlinear sources that inevitably exist in an SHM system, which might put the general SHM methodology in jeopardy. The issue becomes even more alarming for the wave-mixing-based techniques, which have been recently developed in our laboratories. This proposal addresses some of these bottlenecking problems, which hamper the implementation of the NGW-based SHM, so as to formulate a comprehensive and feasible SHM strategy through the detection and localization of incipient damage inside structures. More specifically, a comprehensive two-stage NGW-SHM-specific plan is proposed: one via the best possible tuning of the system parameters; and the other via the manipulation of the NGW generation/propagation alongside the simultaneous mitigation of non-damage related sources. The former is achieved based on the thorough understanding of the wave properties of different NGW components, to be acquired through combined theoretical, numerical and experimental efforts. The latter is materialized through the deployment of customized meta-devices/patches, a kind of artificial functional structures, to be surface-mounted on the structure under inspection. These meta-devices are inversely designed to deliver customized functionalities such as wave filtering, steering and conversion, thus creating favorable working conditions for the NGW-SHM. Altogether, a comprehensive NGW-SHM solution will be established, implemented and experimentally validated, as finally showcased by the monitoring of two representative types of incipient damage in a plate. 結構健康監測具有十分重要的工程意義。以非線性導播為基礎的監測方法，受到多重非線性源的干擾，使得其實行遇到很大困難。本課題通過拓撲超材料優化的方式，設計外加的導波操作器件，淨化及調劑探測導波的性能，大大提高結構健康監測的可能行，為工程實現提出了新的可行方法。

15201621.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15201621.value: 監控和管理長時間坐著的建築設備操作員的疲勞

15201621.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15201621.value: Prof Tao, Xiaoming Dr Umer, Waleed Prof WONG, Arnold

15201621.label: Project Objectives
15201621.value: TO STUDY THE RELATIONSHIPS BETWEEN POTENTIAL CHEMICAL BIOMARKERS AND MENTAL AND PASSIVE PHYSICAL FATIGUE DEVELOPMENT AMONG CONSTRUCTION PLANT & EQUIPMENT OPERATORS. Chemical biomarkers are considered the gold standard for fatigue monitoring because of their accuracy and objectivity. However, unlike other construction workers whose work entails physically demanding and labor-intensive activities, construction plant & equipment operators are exposed to unique work settings (always responsible and sometimes hazardous) which often necessitate prolonged periods of sitting, and the significant mental effort which accompanies the continuous concentration required. As such, underlying biochemical changes may be quite drastic. The relationship between biomarkers produced in the body and fatigue development for construction plant & equipment operators will be investigated. Although there are numerous chemical biomarkers which could be studied in relation to fatigue development, blood lactate, cortisol, pH, potassium, sodium, and blood glucose concentrations in saliva are chosen for this project. Lactate has been chosen because studies indicate that prolonged sitting is accompanied by an increase in lactic acid concentration in the body, which may lead to feelings of fatigue. Similarly, mental fatigue has been found to be closely related to salivary cortisol levels. Potassium, pH, sodium, and glucose concentrations are also linked to an increase in lactic acid, hyper/hypokalemia, loss of energy, drowsiness, irritability, and muscle cramps. Machine learning techniques will be used to model and predict the Rating-of-Fatigue (ROF) scale based on the biomarkers identified. TO DEVELOP NON-INVASIVE WRIST-SWEAT-BASED WEARABLE SENSORS FOR THE SELECTED CHEMICAL BIOMARKERS. Once those biochemicals which allow accurate fatigue monitoring of construction plant & equipment operators are identified, we will develop wearable sensors to measure those biomarkers. Depending upon the results, we will monitor either all six pre-identified biomarkers or only some of them. The monitoring of biomarkers will be conducted in an integrated electrochemical chip that contains multiple sensing electrodes. The chip can transduce biological ion-based signals from human sweat into electrical signals with high gain and low current. Since some plan & equipment operators may work in air-conditioned cabins and do not sweat enough for accurate measurement of biomarker levels using the integrated sweat sensor, carbachol agarose gels and iontophoresis will be used to stimulate sweat generation when making measurements. The concentration of biomarkers in sweat is interpreted from a detected ‘change in sensor current’. To convert a current change to a biomarker concentration, a prior calibration model is required for that sensor. Calibration for each sensor will be achieved using a series of simulated sweat solutions with different biomarker concentrations as standards. Linear and polynomial regressions will be used to create calibration models for each sensor developed. TO VALIDATE THE WRIST-SWEAT-BASED SENSORS FOR FATIGUE MONITORING OF CONSTRUCTION PLANT & EQUIPMENT OPERATORS. To validate the novel wrist-sweat-based sensors for fatigue monitoring, wrist sensor measurements will be compared with (1) portable monitors from Horiba Inc. (field tests); and (2) EEG-based fatigue monitoring technology (lab tests). TO QUANTIFY THE EFFECTIVENESS OFTHE PROPOSED STRETCHING EXERCISES IN MITIGATING PLANT OPERATOR FATIGUE EFFECTS In this study, a randomized crossover study design will be used to examine the impact of stretching exercises on construction plant operator fatigue reduction. Participants will be randomly allocated to either: (1) a group which will perform stretching exercises only on the first two days of the experiments, or (2) a group which will perform stretching exercises only on the last two days of the experiments. Half of the participants will perform exercises designed for operators who cannot leave their cabins and the other half for operators who can leave. After four hours of plant operating simulation, participants will perform stretching exercises every 30 minutes based on the group they have been assigned to. Both subjective and objective measurements of fatigue will be taken every 30 minutes to ascertain subject fatigue changes and the impact of stretching exercises on fatigue. In summary, the research team will validate the feasibility of wrist-sweat-based-sensors to detect the fatigue levels of construction plant operators and evaluate the effectiveness of stretching exercises in mitigating fatigue. The results of this project will be a comprehensive solution to both monitoring and mitigating construction plant operator levels of fatigue.

15201621.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15201621.value: Accidents involving equipment contribute to a substantial proportion of total accidents on construction sites. Many studies have identified operators’ fatigue as a primary cause of these accidents. Owing to the nature of construction work, plant & equipment operators have to attentively perform their tasks while sitting in their control-cabins for prolonged periods. Mental fatigue caused by the sustained attention required and the passive physical fatigue arising from prolonged sitting have been identified as principal risk factors. Recent studies have proposed EEG (electroencephalography) and eye-tracking based solutions to detect mental fatigue. While studies have found them promising, there are certain limitations. EEG requires the tying of several sensors around the heads of operators throughout their working duration, and eye-tracking requires workers to wear heavy glasses equipped with cameras and other associated components. Such equipment could be very irritating when worn for extended periods of time. To overcome these limitations, this study proposes the development of non-invasive wrist-sweat-based wearable sensors that can monitor chemical biomarkers of mental and passive physical fatigue. To achieve this objective, firstly, consenting operators engaged in their daily work will be administered questionnaires, while saliva and blood samples will be collected from them to study the relationships between potential chemical biomarkers with mental and passive physical fatigue. Secondly, wrist-sweat-based wearable sensors, used to measure the most promising biomarkers, will be developed to non-invasively monitor the fatigue levels of operators. Thirdly, to prevent fatigue and its ill-effects, operators will be advised to stay hydrated, maintain a proper diet and a healthy lifestyle, which includes sufficient sleep. These measures can delay the onset of fatigue, they do not constitute a full intervention. To fully combat fatigue, this study proposes two eight-minute stretching exercises: one is designed for cases where operators can leave their control-cabins; the second exercise is designed for operators who are required to stay within their control-cabins (e.g. tower-crane operators). The subjective and objective effectiveness of these stretching exercises in alleviating fatigue will be assessed, leading to solutions for the problems described. In summary, this study will first develop and validate the feasibility of wrist-sweat based sensors in detecting the fatigue level of operators. Secondly, it will evaluate the effectiveness of stretching exercises in mitigating fatigue. Taken together, the results of this project will provide a comprehensive solution to monitoring and mitigating fatigue of plant operators (or any workers) exposed to prolonged sitting in seemingly harsh environments. 涉及设备的事故占建筑工地事故总数的很大一部分。许多研究已经确定操作员的疲劳是这些事故的主要原因。由于建筑工作的性质，设备操作员必须长时间坐在控制室中专心地执行任务。需要持续关注引起的精神疲劳和久坐引起的被动身体疲劳已被确定为主要风险因素。最近的研究提出了基于 EEG（脑电图）和眼动追踪的解决方案来检测精神疲劳。虽然研究发现它们很有前景，但也存在一定的局限性。 EEG 需要在整个工作期间将多个传感器绑在操作员的头部周围，而眼动追踪需要工作人员佩戴配备有摄像头和其他相关组件的厚重眼镜。长时间佩戴此类设备可能会非常刺激。为了克服这些限制，本研究建议开发基于无创手腕汗水的可穿戴传感器，可以监测精神和被动身体疲劳的化学生物标志物。为实现这一目标，首先对参与日常工作的操作人员进行问卷调查，同时收集他们的唾液和血液样本，以研究潜在的化学生物标志物与精神和被动身体疲劳之间的关系。其次，将开发用于测量最有希望的生物标志物的基于手腕汗液的可穿戴传感器，以无创监测操作员的疲劳程度。第三，为防止疲劳及其不良影响，将建议操作员保持水分，保持适当的饮食和健康的生活方式，包括充足的睡眠。这些措施可以延缓疲劳的发作，它们并不构成完全干预。为了充分对抗疲劳，这项研究提出了两种 8 分钟的伸展运动：一种是为操作员可以离开控制室的情况而设计的；第二个练习是为需要留在控制舱内的操作员设计的（例如塔式起重机操作员）。将评估这些伸展运动在缓解疲劳方面的主观和客观有效性，从而为所描述的问题提供解决方案。总之，本研究将首先开发和验证基于手腕汗液的传感器在检测操作员疲劳水平方面的可行性。其次，它将评估伸展运动在减轻疲劳方面的有效性。综上所述，该项目的结果将为监测和减轻长期坐在看似恶劣的环境中的操作员（或任何工人）的疲劳提供全面的解决方案。

15202221.value: 室內環境中的空氣傳播傳染病傳播已成為公共衛生的一個重要議題。當易感個體距離感染源 1.5 米以內時，空氣傳播的鄰近效應可導致在最初的短時間段內產生強烈的直接暴露。因此，表徵封閉環境中人員之間短距離污染物傳播對預防和降低呼吸道感染風險至關重要。 為了研究室內環境中傳染病的空氣傳播途徑，六氟化硫 (SF6) 示踪氣體通常用作飛沫核的替代物。對於短距離的人員之間污染物傳播，為了進行風險評估準確獲取總暴露量，捕獲直接接觸初期短時間的峰值濃度至關重要。然而，現有的商用 SF6 傳感器響應時間長達 45 秒，可能無法捕捉到短距離直接暴露的峰值濃度。在擬議的項目中，我們將開發一種超靈敏的 SF6 氣體傳感器，以顯著縮短響應時間。然後，開發的傳感器將用於測量環境艙中的人員之間短距離污染物傳播。 該項目將首先開發基於石英增強光聲光譜 (QEPAS) 的超靈敏 SF6 氣體傳感器，以實現 0.4 秒的短響應時間。 QEPAS SF6 氣體傳感器隨後將經過仔細校準和驗證，以確保儀器的準確性和靈敏度。然後，我們將使用開發的超靈敏 SF6 傳感器對環境艙中的人員之間短距離污染物傳播進行實驗測量。我們將測量靠近源的時間平均SF6 濃度分佈和被傳播個體呼吸區內的高時間分辨率瞬態 SF6 濃度。最後，準確的 SF6 測量數據將用於驗證和評估湍流模型和污染物傳輸模型。 本研究將通過提供高質量的實驗數據，增強我們對封閉環境中人員之間短距離污染物傳播的理解。開發的超靈敏 SF6 氣體傳感器將通過顯著縮短響應時間來推進室內污染物傳輸測量的實驗技術。該項目的成果將促進封閉環境中空氣傳播傳染病的控制。我們希望該項目能夠通過增強對短距離人員之間污染物傳輸的理解，降低呼出污染物的暴露量，降低呼吸道感染風險，從而造福廣大民眾。

15202421.label: Project Objectives
15202421.value: Most portfolio selection models in the literature assume that the tradings of traders do not affect the asset price evolutions. In practice, however, asset price evolutions are often significantly affected by large volume or famous traders. This project aims to narrow this gap by investigating portfolio selection problems for a large trader whose actions affect the asset price evolutions in a nonlinear way, in the setting of regime switching with random coefficients and trading constraint. Two inter-related problems will be investigated. The first one is the classical mean-variance portfolio selection problem and the other one is the lifetime target-tracking problem. They reduce to stochastic nonlinear quadratic optimal control problems under regime switching with random coefficients. We hope to establish the existence and uniqueness results for the corresponding stochastic Riccati equations so as to solve these portfolio selection problems completely.

15202421.label: Realisation of objectives
15202421.value: This project set out to investigate portfolio selection problems within the framework of regime-switching models, incorporating random coefficients, nonlinear wealth processes, and trading constraints. This represents a relatively new and important class of investment problems, characterized by significant mathematical and practical challenges due to their stochastic and nonlinear nature, high dimensionality, and the presence of control constraints. Achievement of Objectives All the objectives proposed at the outset of the project have been successfully addressed. We developed and analyzed advanced mathematical models that capture the complexities of financial markets where conditions can change unpredictably, and investors face realistic trading limitations. These models extend traditional approaches by considering random fluctuations in market parameters and nonlinear dynamics in wealth evolution, making them highly relevant for modern portfolio management. To tackle these challenging problems, we employed a combination of established and newly developed mathematical techniques. Notably, we utilized the multidimensional comparison theorem, truncation function techniques, log transformation, and the John-Nirenberg inequality. These methods enabled us to rigorously analyze the associated backward stochastic differential equations (BSDEs) and Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) equations, which are central to optimal portfolio selection under uncertainty. Throughout the project, we obtained many valuable results from both theoretical and practical perspectives. Our findings provide new insights into optimal investment strategies in complex market environments and offer practical guidelines for portfolio managers facing regime shifts and trading constraints. The successful realization of our objectives is evidenced by the numerous publications resulting from this work, including papers in top-tier journals and presentations at major international conferences. Challenges and Solutions The main challenges encountered during the project stemmed from the high complexity and dimensionality of the models, as well as the difficulty in solving the associated stochastic control problems. To overcome these obstacles, we developed new analytical techniques and collaborated with experts in related fields. Future Directions Given the significance and potential of this research area, we plan to continue our investigations in future projects. Our next steps will involve extending the models to even more realistic market settings, incorporating additional features such as transaction costs and liquidity constraints, and exploring data-driven approaches for parameter estimation and regime identification. We also aim to collaborate with industry partners to validate and apply our findings in real-world investment scenarios. In summary, the project has fully realized its objectives, making substantial contributions to the field of mathematical finance and laying a strong foundation for future research and practical applications.

15202421.label: Major findings and research outcome
15202421.value: This project has progressed exceptionally well, achieving all the objectives initially proposed. Our primary aim was to investigate portfolio selection problems within the framework of regime-switching models, incorporating random coefficients and trading constraints. In pursuit of this goal, we developed a range of advanced financial models that capture various market features and complexities. These models were rigorously analyzed using sophisticated mathematical tools, including the solution of stochastic Riccati equations and Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) equations. Please refer to the publication list for reference. A key outcome of our research is the establishment of new theoretical results that enhance the understanding of optimal portfolio strategies under regime-switching dynamics and uncertainty. Our findings provide valuable insights into how investors can adapt their strategies in response to changing market regimes and random fluctuations in model parameters, all while adhering to practical trading constraints. The impact of our work is evidenced by the publication of 13 research papers, several of which have appeared in leading journals such as the SIAM Journal on Control and Optimization, IEEE Transactions on Automatic Control, Applied Mathematics and Optimization, Finance and Stochastics, Journal of Optimization Theory and Applications, and the SIAM Journal on Financial Mathematics. Additional manuscripts are currently under review. Furthermore, we have actively disseminated our results through presentations at numerous prestigious international conferences and workshops, further establishing the significance and relevance of our contributions to the field. In summary, this project has made substantial advances in the mathematical modeling and analysis of portfolio selection under complex market conditions. The theoretical developments and practical implications derived from our research not only address the original objectives but also open new avenues for future investigation in mathematical finance.

15202421.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15202421.value: Building on the achievements of this project, several promising directions for further research are identified. First, extending the current models to high-dimensional markets will allow for more realistic and comprehensive portfolio analysis. Incorporating additional market features, such as transaction costs and liquidity constraints, can further enhance the practical applicability of the models. Integrating machine learning and data-driven techniques offers the potential to improve regime identification and parameter estimation, leading to more adaptive and robust portfolio strategies. Additionally, empirical validation using historical financial data and case studies will help demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approaches in real-world scenarios. To pursue these directions, we propose a phased course of action: (1) extend the theoretical framework to more complex market settings; (2) collaborate with data scientists to integrate advanced computational and machine learning methods; and (3) conduct empirical studies and engage with industry partners for practical validation and refinement. This approach will ensure the continued advancement and real-world relevance of the research in mathematical finance.

15202421.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15202421.value: This research project explores how investors can make smarter decisions when choosing investments in unpredictable and changing financial markets. We developed new mathematical models that help understand how market conditions can suddenly shift—like during economic booms or downturns—and how these changes affect investment choices. Our work also considers real-life limitations, such as rules about how often you can trade or how much you can invest. The significance of this research lies in its ability to guide investors and financial professionals in managing risk and maximizing returns, even when markets are uncertain or volatile. By using advanced mathematics, we provide tools that can adapt to changing market environments and help investors make better decisions. The value of this project is demonstrated by our publications in leading scientific journals and presentations at major international conferences, showing that our findings are recognized by experts in the field. Ultimately, our research contributes to safer and more effective investment strategies, which can benefit individuals, financial institutions, and the broader economy.

15203121.label: Project Objectives
15203121.value: To investigate the irregular steel sections used in contemporary structures to better understand the development trend of using them in an innovative structural system. To identify the structural failure and buckling modes of the steel members with irregular cross-sections and to clarify the major considerations in the design of such members. To propose an efficient numerical method by deriving a new line element, based on the asymmetric section assumption and high-order shape functions, for executing a second-order direct analysis for the practical design of steel members with irregular cross-sections. To formulate design provisions for steel members with irregular cross-sections that meet the codified design requirements to materialise the practical application of the proposed method. To validate the proposed analysis method via the available experimental results or the refined the sophisticated shell or solid finite element analysis to confirm its applicability for practical use. To implement the proposed method into existing structural analysis and design for promoting its application in the local construction industry for cost-saving measures and efficient design.

15203121.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15203121.value: 與眾多特大城市類似，人口老齡化問題及年輕一代對建築現場工作的興趣缺乏，造成了香港建築業勞動力長期短缺。為提高建造效率，低勞動力密度結構體系的使用需求日益增長，如組裝合成建築法（MiC）結構。然而，低效的鋼結構設計與施工仍不可避免地造成了鋼結構建造成本遠高於鋼筋混凝土結構。因此，具有顯著安裝便利性及成本優勢的異形截面鋼構件應得到更普遍的使用，以實現建造效率的提升。對於任意截面形式的異形截面鋼構件，自動化機器人焊接技術也已使其擺脫了製造加工的束縛。 常見的異形截面，如卷邊角鋼及Z型鋼，其自身具有非對稱性。直接採用傳統方法進行設計可能並不合適，因為傳統方法的設計公式基本上是由具有對稱截面的普通熱軋型鋼所推導的。因此，對於具有異形截面高結構效率的新型體系，合理設計方法的缺乏將成為制約其發展的關鍵因素。 鑒於此，本項目將解決異形截面鋼構件的設計問題，進一步完善現代結構設計方法—二階直接分析法。而穩健的電腦分析方法是實現該法的關鍵所在。針對鋼構件的二階直接分析，此前申請人提出了先進的新型數值算法，並在電腦程式NIDA中實現。該程式已在香港及周邊城市的一些標志性結構中被廣汎應用，例如香港中央政府總部大樓。但以往鋼結構設計多採用設計簡單的對稱截面。本項目將通過研發符合異形截面結構特徵的數值算法，並將現行二階直接分析法擴展至異形截面鋼構件設計中，以更好應對不同方向下不同強度的載荷，如重力荷載主導的情況。 該項目有望顯著改善結構工程的設計實踐，提高工程建造效率和經濟效益，降低人力需求，並有利於建造更經濟、更安全的結構。

15203121.label: Realisation of objectives
15203121.value: This research project successfully established a comprehensive second-order direct analysis method for steel members with irregular cross-sections, thereby fully accomplishing all six stated objectives. All peer-reviewed journal papers (22 papers) cited below were produced with support from this research project and explicitly acknowledged the project funding. Objective 1: To investigate irregular steel sections used in contemporary structures (100% completed) This research delivered a structured investigation of irregular steel cross-sections increasingly adopted in modern structural systems, including non-symmetric, non-prismatic, deteriorated, and heterogeneous/anisotropic members. Targets included open singly-symmetric sections (channels and angles) and their coupled second-order response (Chen et al., 2022), and tapered/non-prismatic members enabled by advanced fabrication (Abdelrahman et al., 2022). In-service irregularity was quantified for corrosion-driven random non-uniform section loss and offshore sheet piles with time-evolving properties (Zhang et al., 2022; Yang et al., 2022). Fire-driven irregularity was examined under elevated/non-uniform temperatures, showing stiffness degradation and amplified warping/twisting (Chen et al., 2023; Li et al., 2025). Emerging heterogeneous and anisotropic members were covered, including functionally graded (FG) sandwich/graded profiles (Li et al., 2024), metal 3D-printed members with direction-dependent anisotropy (Zhang et al., 2025), and cylindrical orthotropic members governed by ring orientation (Xue et al., 2025). Objective 2: To identify failure/buckling modes and clarify key design considerations (100% completed) This research identified governing instability and failure mechanisms of irregular-section members and clarified design-critical modelling considerations. Dominant global modes included flexural buckling, lateral–torsional buckling (LTB), axial–torsional buckling (ATB), and flexural–torsional coupled instability driven by non-coincident centroid and shear center, warping, and Wagner effects (Chen et al., 2022; Abdelrahman et al., 2022; Chen et al., 2023). For LTB, torsion/warping end-restraint sensitivity was quantified, confirming that semi-rigid restraints can substantially alter resistance and must be represented in stability assessment (Zhang et al., 2025). Under fire, non-uniform temperature fields and stiffness degradation amplified twisting/warping and shifted governing stability mechanisms (Chen et al., 2023; Li et al., 2025). Beyond superstructures, refined pile formulations captured coupled responses under complex loading, supporting consistent treatment of coupling in pile-supported systems (Ouyang et al., 2024). Objective 3: To propose efficient numerical methods/line elements for second-order direct analysis (100% completed) This research developed an integrated, efficient line-element framework for second-order direct analysis of irregular-section and non-prismatic members, with rigorous warping/torsion coupling. For nonsymmetric members, a geometric–material nonlinear formulation with explicit warping DOF and section-property coupling was established, together with yield-surface generation to support plasticity modelling without symmetry assumptions (Chen et al., 2022). For tapered/non-prismatic members, refined Timoshenko and generalized line-element formulations incorporated shear deformation, warping, and Wagner effects while maintaining robustness for spatially varying properties (Abdelrahman et al., 2022). For thick-walled nonsymmetric sections, an efficient second-order line-element method was formulated, supported by FE-based evaluation of warping, shear and torsion properties (Chen et al., 2024). For heterogeneous and advanced materials, FG section/member formulations captured twisting induced by graded properties via FE-based section discretisation and coupling (Li et al., 2024), while WAAM anisotropy and cylindrical orthotropy were embedded through FE-based section analysis and corresponding member formulations (Zhang et al., 2025; Xue et al., 2025). In parallel, physics-informed ML enhancements were delivered: PINN-based second-order analysis for beam-columns and non-prismatic members (Chen et al., 2023; Chen et al., 2025), and extensions to large-deflection piles and hybrid NN–FEM elements for soil–structure interaction (Ouyang et al., 2024). Objective 4: To formulate design provisions meeting codified requirements (100% completed) Validated analysis advances were translated into practical, code-consistent modelling recommendations and design provisions for irregular-section members. The developed second-order method supports stability assessment of asymmetric members where twisting effects must be considered, providing a rational basis for code-compliant design beyond simplified symmetric assumptions (Chen et al., 2024; Li et al., 2025). For LTB, quantified restraint effects were converted into modelling guidance suitable for semi-rigid conditions encountered in practice (Zhang et al., 2025). For fire design, parametric analyses supported simplified evaluation relationships for stability reduction of irregular members (Li et al., 2025; Chen et al., 2023). For deterioration, quantified sensitivity of torsion-involved instabilities to corrosion non-uniformity provided guidance for conservative stability assessment and prioritisation of ATB or combined-mode stability checks (Zhang et al., 2022; Yang et al., 2022). Objective 5: To validate the proposed methods via experiments and refined FE analyses (100% completed) Validation was conducted against refined shell and solid FE benchmarks and reported experimental evidence. The nonsymmetric geometric–material nonlinear formulation with yield-surface-based plasticity was verified through benchmark groups covering elastic and inelastic responses and coupled buckling behaviours (Chen et al., 2022). The thick-walled formulation was validated through benchmarks demonstrating robust capture of warping/twisting and transverse shear effects using FE-derived section properties (Chen et al., 2024). For thin-walled members with residual stresses, the improved shell-finite strip method was validated against experimental and refined numerical benchmarks for inelastic buckling prediction (Gao et al., 2025). Fire-related formulations were validated via thermal–structural benchmarking and extensive parametric analyses under elevated and non-uniform temperatures (Chen et al., 2023; Li et al., 2025). Objective 6: To implement the methods into software for practical use (100% completed) The developed analysis and design capabilities were implemented in software, notably MSASect2, enabling integrated cross-section analysis and second-order direct analysis for irregular members. MSASect2 incorporates FE-based cross-section analysis and line-element coupling for graded/heterogeneous members with twisting effects (Li et al., 2024), supports fire-related stability checks for IFC-protected and non-uniform fire cases with twisting effects (Li et al., 2025), and supports LTB assessment with torsion/warping restraint representation (Zhang et al., 2025). Conclusion: All six objectives were fully achieved. The project delivered a validated and software-implemented second-order direct analysis framework for steel members with irregular cross-sections, supported by 22 peer-reviewed journal publications spanning investigating irregular cross-sections, identifying instability mechanisms, developing advanced numerical analysis methods, formulating code-consistent guidance, conducting validation and practical implementation.

15203121.label: Major findings and research outcome
15203121.value: This project successfully refined the second-order direct analysis method for steel members with irregular (non-symmetric) cross-sections, achieving all major objectives. The research encompasses theoretical development in advanced numerical analysis methods, understanding of complex buckling behaviors, extension to machine learning techniques, and implementation into a practical software platform. These achievements are documented in 22 high-quality journal publications, with two PhD students trained and one software platform (MSASect2) developed. (1) Theoretical Development in Numerical Analysis Methods: Advanced line-element formulations were developed for geometric and material nonlinear analysis of nonsymmetric sections with rigorous yield surface analysis. Generalized formulations for tapered members with warping and Wagner effects were established, along with refined Timoshenko elements for tapered I-sections. Methods for thick-walled sections with warping degrees of freedom and twisting effects were developed. Extensions to functionally graded members and orthotropic sections were achieved, with improved shell-finite strip methods for inelastic buckling analysis. (2) Understanding of Buckling and Failure Behaviors: Steel members become nonsymmetric under various scenarios including non-uniform corrosion, elevated temperatures, and marine environments. Using the newly proposed analysis methods, flexural, lateral-torsional, and axial-torsional buckling strengths were systematically studied. For corroded members, axial-torsional buckling was most adversely affected. Fire-resistant design methods were developed for nonsymmetric sections under elevated temperatures using co-rotational formulations. Three-dimensional pile element formulations for steel piles with irregular cross-sections captured complex soil-structure interaction and coupled responses in pile-supported structures during soil liquefaction. (3) Extended Research to Emerging Machine Learning Techniques: Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINN) were successfully applied to second-order analysis of beam-columns, creating self-supervised learning procedures requiring minimal datasets. PINN methods were extended to large deflection analysis of slender piles with nonlinear soil-structure interaction. Neural networks-based spring elements and line elements synergized machine learning with finite element methods. PINN frameworks were implemented for geometrically nonlinear analysis of members with irregular cross-sections. (4) Implementation into Software Platform for Practical Application: The developed algorithms for analyzing nonsymmetric sections were implemented into MSASect2 (www.msasect.com), a freely available software providing comprehensive cross-section analysis and second-order design capabilities for steel members with irregular cross-sections. These achievements directly address the project's goal to improve design practices, enhance construction efficiency, reduce manpower demands, and enable adoption of innovative steel structural systems with irregular cross-sections essential for Hong Kong's construction industry towards more efficient and sustainable structures.

15203121.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15203121.value: Building on the validated second-order direct analysis method for irregular cross-sections and non-prismatic members, the next stage is to extend the methodology to constructional 3D-printed steel members, such as Wire Arc Additive Manufacturing (WAAM) members, where irregularity arises simultaneously from (i) anisotropic material behaviour, (ii) printing-induced geometric deviations and free-form or non-prismatic geometry, and (iii) significant residual stresses. Pilot projects such as the WAAM “Waving Love” pavilion in Hong Kong have demonstrated the feasibility and potential material efficiency of 3D-printed steel structures, yet current codified design approaches remain insufficient to quantify capacity reliably without extensive physical testing. The proposed course of action is therefore to: (1) characterise WAAM constitutive anisotropy, residual-stress patterns, and geometric imperfection descriptors through targeted coupon tests and representative component tests; (2) integrate these WAAM-specific parameters into the established line-element and cross-section analysis pipeline, including refined FE-based section property evaluation and anisotropic material modelling; (3) conduct reliability-oriented calibration against benchmark experiments and refined shell or solid FE simulations for representative WAAM members and subassemblies; (4) translate validated findings into design-oriented provisions consistent with direct analysis principles; and (5) implement the resulting methods into the developed software platform, i.e. MSASect2, for practical application.

15203121.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15203121.value: This project addressed an emerging design challenge in modern construction: steel members with irregular cross-sections are increasingly fabricated to improve structural efficiency, or they may develop uneven cross-sectional geometry in service due to corrosion or fire exposure. Such members can bend and twist simultaneously and may fail through coupled buckling modes that are difficult to assess using traditional methods developed for regular, symmetric cross-sections. The project developed and validated a second-order analysis method that explicitly accounts for twisting and warping effects for steel members irregular cross-sections, especially when the load path does not pass through the member’s shear centre. The method captures key mechanisms, including large deformations and yielding, and provides reliable predictions of strength and stability for steel members with irregular cross-sections. Its accuracy was demonstrated through extensive benchmarking against laboratory test results and detailed three-dimensional finite-element simulations, covering non-symmetric shapes, corrosion-loss patterns, and fire-induced temperature effects. Overall, the project delivers a validated analytical method for evaluating the structural stability of steel members with irregular cross-sections and supporting future innovation as advanced fabrication and construction methods continue to expand their use in modern steel construction.

15203421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15203421.value: Hand feel, or handle, is one of the very important attributes of apparel textiles. It is a complex matter involving both human sensation and perception, which has been problematic in communication by verbal or digital methods even among trained professionals. The subjective terms used to describe handle are vague, the low-stress mechanical and surface properties of fabrics, measured by objective methods, are subject to significant variations of interpretation due to the different perceptions of people. This communication difficulty prevents the entrance of the immersive experience of handle in virtual and augmented reality (VR/AR) systems and hinders the progress of online education, online shopping, online design, online healthcare, and entertainment when involving soft goods like textiles and apparel. This project proposes a new concept of actuating fabrics, named as fabric handle simulator (FHS), which can mimic the handle of textile fabrics by adjusting the fabric low-stress mechanical and surface properties with remote electronic control. The FHS may be used as a core component of future VR/AR technology, together with the other key component of a tactile sensing unit. In the handle communication, the sensing unit at a caller’s place collects the tactile signals of a fabric, then the signals are transmitted wirelessly to a receiver. The FHS at the receiver’s end will be activated under control of the signals sent by the caller. The receiver will feel an imitated handle when touching the activated FHS. Based on previously tested hypotheses of fabric handle evaluation, the project is aimed at creating the first-generation FHS, whose characteristic markers of low-stress mechanical and surface properties are quantitatively tuned by electronic means and implemented remotely. Theoretical models with multi-physics coupled structural mechanics will be proposed for guiding the design of the FHS. Interactive soft materials will be investigated to develop fine fibers tuned with electro-chemical, electro-thermo-mechanical and electro-adhesive mechanisms. The novel features of the fibers include the adjustability of fiber length, diameters, friction and curvature by electronic control with low power. A FHS prototype will be designed and fabricated with selected actuating fibers, fabric structural parameters and control mechanisms. Its performance will be evaluated both subjectively and objectively, then its functional characteristics will be determined together with the limitations. The project is expected to generate high-impact journal papers, new theoretical tools and new FHS technologies, paving the way to introduce handle in the future VR/AR online applications beyond the current visual and auditory experiences. 手感是服用紡織品最重要的屬性之一，是一個涉及人類感覺和知覺的複雜命題。即使在受過培訓的專業人士中，通過口頭或數位方法進行交流也有困難。用於描述手感的主觀術語含糊不清，通過客觀方法測量的織物低應力機械和表面性能經過不同人解釋，存在的顯著差異。這個困難阻礙了手感沉浸式體驗進入虛擬和增強現實 系統，從而限制了涉及紡織品和服裝等軟性商品線上互動技術在網上教育、網上購物、網上設計、網上醫療保健和網上娛樂等的順利應用。 該專案提出了一種新的電驅動織物概念，命名為織物手感模擬器。它具有遠端電子控制的低應力機械和表面特性，可以通過調整面料來模擬紡織面料的手感。可作為未來 VR/AR 技術的核心元件，成為其他觸覺傳感單元的關鍵部件之一。在手感通信中，傳感單元在發送者端收集織物的觸覺信號，然後無線傳輸信號到另一端的接收器。接收端的織物手感模擬器將用發送端的信號，控制實現相應的織物低應力機械和表面特性。接收者在觸摸織物時會感覺到一個仿製的手感。 該專案基於先前織物手感評估技術的研究，旨在創建第一代織物手感模擬器。 其低應力機械和表面性能特性可通過電子手段進行定量調整，和遠端實施。將提出具有多物理場耦合紡織結構力學的理論模型來指導織物手感模擬器 的設計。將研究開發用電化學、電熱機械調節的細纖維和電粘附機制。互動軟纖維材料的創新點是通過低功耗電子控制，實現對纖維長度、直徑、摩擦和曲率進行定量調節。 第一代 織物手感模擬器原型將使用研發的驅動纖維進行設計和製造。理論和實驗研究電驅互動性纖維、紗線、織物結構參數和控制機制。經主觀和客觀評價，確定它的功能特徵和局限性。 該項目有望產生高影響力的期刊論文、新的理論工具、和第一代織物手感模擬器技術。超越當前視覺和聽覺體驗，為未來虛擬和增強現實領域引入手感互動鋪平道路。 。

15203421.label: Realisation of objectives
15203421.value: We have fully addressed all five objectives set up in the original proposal. Two major categories of fiber-based actuators were identified, magnetorheological (MR) fiber assemblies for deformation of mm-scale and fluidic fabrics for deformation of cm-scale. Due to the limited budget, this project has focused on the MR fiber assemblies while other funding being sought for the second fluidic fabrics. Soft magnetic particles of a few microns have been selected as the filler and polymers of polyethylene and polyamide as the matrix. By mixing them in a thermal extrusion spinning machine followed by drawing process, composite fibers of various blending ratios were made and characterized for magnetic, thermal and mechanical properties as well as the microstructure. By using the new fine and robust MR fiber, we made twisted yarns following the ideal yarn structure where the fibers were concentrically placed. A lab-made device was fabricated and attached to the twisting machine. Woven fabric samples were made on the hand loom with plain , twill and satin weave of selected density, respectively. Their magnetic and mechanical properties as well as structure were characterized. We have used MR rods as the building block for building a multi-physics coupled structural mechanics model to describe the working mechanisms and actuating operation of the actuating MR fibers, concentric twisted yarns and woven fabrics. The calculated properties were compared with the measured ones to verify the model. A finger glove device was designed and fabricated with the novel yarn and fabric actuators that can be controlled by low electric power, to realize controllable changes in fabric surface texture and hairiness according to the model. A first-generation fabric handle simulator (FHS) prototype has been demonstrated.
