15203421.label: Major findings and research outcome
15203421.value: For the first time, we developed coupled magneto-structural mechanics models for magnetorheological (MR) yarns to describe the working mechanisms and actuating operation of the actuating MR fibers, yarns and fabrics, in order to guide the engineering design. We designed, fabricated, and characterized soft-magnetic composite fibers by melt-spinning route, then 7-fiber singles yarn actuators that tune the fiber cross-sectional shapes, size, and friction according to AC electric signals for the controlling external electro-magnetic field below 300 mT, safe to human applications. Woven fabrics were made by the MR yarns so that change rigidity and hysteresis of bending, shear, and lateral compression were achieved under control by electrical signals. MR yarn and fabric actuators were developed to realize controllable changes in fabric surface texture and hairiness. Finally, the above mentioned actuating units were used to demonstrate a first-generation FHS finger prototype. Most of the results were published in a Nature paper in the main text, supplementary information and videos.

15203421.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15203421.value: This work opens doors towards new direction for programmable fiber-based tactile emulation methods and devices. I proposed to put them in two scales for human-centred applications, that is, cm- and mm-scale actuators, which corresponding to human sensation mechanisms. The MR textiles are aimed at the mm-scale applications. Then we applied for two major research projects and obtained funding from TRS of RGC in 2024 as well as SSTF of ITC/Jocky Club in 2023 for these two aspects, respectively. The work is continuing.

15203421.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15203421.value: We have successfully completed the exploratory investigation on the mechanisms of low-stress handle emulation by textile structures and identified programmable MR fiber, yarn and fabric as the suitable candidates for detailed study. The theory and technologies established as well as the boundary would be strong scientific framework and engineering design guide for this kind of soft actuators. This study shed new lights to the direction and charted the routes for future development for tactile sensation emulation technology to be used in AR/XR, online commence, education and entertainments etc.

15204121.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15204121.value: 最近的技术进步见证了人类活动从物理空间到虚拟空间的转变。在个体层面，虚拟空间中的在线人类行为（例如电话和网页浏览）与地理空间中的现实（离线）行为在时间维度重叠。在群体层面，人们在物理空间和虚拟（在线）空间中在时间空间维度同时共位、共存。在线人类行为中不存在对移动的空间和经济限制。然而，物理-虚拟人类活动和交互的混合（例如重叠、协同定位和共存）增加了日常活动的碎片化，并影响了个人和群体层面的人类行为。现有方法通常分别处理物理和虚拟空间中的人类行为和交互，由于无法同时考虑多个人的流动和关系，这可能会导致推理性错误。多层网络可以使用多个链接更好地表示和量化现实中的多种人类交互。随着在线交流的快速增长，迫切需要开发一套空间分析解决方案，以提高我们对地理环境中物理-虚拟人类行为和交互的理解。 为了研究在线人类行为及其影响，本项目旨在使用移动大数据和先进的地理空间分析（例如最先进的多层网络和地理计算）更全面地模拟物理-虚拟人类行为和交互。数百万用户的大量移动大数据，包括移动信号数据、通话记录和网页浏览数据，都是从移动系统中获取的。将使用时空模型推断用户的家庭社区、身体活动位置和物理-虚拟交互。网站的域名被视为“数字”位置，连续的“数字”位置被表示为虚拟空间中的“数字”轨迹。通过同时考虑物理和虚拟的人类活动，拟议的项目将生成以人为中心和基于地点的多层网络，以建模和开发描述人类互动模式的指标，并进一步探索内部和内部规模的社会经济因素的关系。 本项目将利用越来越多的移动大数据来执行和推动地理和社会系统的多维数据密集型和计算研究。项目的结果将提供对物理-虚拟人类行为和交互模式的全面理解，这将有助于重新定义社会群体并确定他们与建筑环境的关系。因此，项目的结果将使城市设计师和人类福祉政策制定者能够提高城市生活质量，尤其是在香港等人口稠密的城市。

15204921.label: Project Objectives
15204921.value: Investigate the new requirements and identify the challenges of decentralized model training in large scale edge computing systems for data generated on the edge nodes. In this project, we target at developing new methods, algorithms and mechanisms to solve the challenges in Edge AI, more specifically in AI model training. The challenging issues arise mainly due to the inadequateness of the existing work in handling the data generated on the edge nodes, including the NonIID data, unlabeled data, and streaming data. We will investigate these new issues and their impact on Edge AI. Design a framework and solutions for the identified challenging issues, including learning task partition and cooperation, distributed semi-supervised learning and model training for streaming data. The solutions include methods, algorithms and mechanisms. Due to the NonIID data across the edge nodes, the data used for jointly training a general model may be greatly different from the data generated on a particular node, thus the general model has large inference error for the node. Considering this problem, we will develop a multi-task learning based approach, which spatially partition the edge nodes into several groups where each group learns a common task. We will further study the task partition and assignment problem and the model sharing/transfer mechanisms among the tasks. Within each task, we will investigate the federated incremental learning framework for dealing with the streaming data. To solve catastrophic forgetting in model training with newly arrived data on every edge node, we will develop solutions to achieve optimal trade-off between model inference and model sharing across multiple edge nodes. In order to exploit massive unlabeled data, we will study how to incorporate the semi-supervised learning mechanisms into the federated incremental learning framework. We will conduct both theoretical analyses and/or simulations to evaluate the performance of the proposed solutions. We will also implement a system prototype with representative applications to experiment and validate the effectiveness of our proposed algorithms and mechanisms.

15204921.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15204921.value: AI 模型傳統上是在中央雲上使用從終端設備收集的數據進行訓練。 對於邊緣計算，這會導致高通信成本、長回應時間和隱私問題。 最近研究者們提出邊緣智慧技術，支持在更靠近數據來源的網路邊緣訓練和部署機器學習模型。 邊緣智慧的一個重要問題是使用邊緣節點上的本地數據訓練具有快速收斂性的準確模型。 聯邦學習 (FL) 通過利用雲中的集中式伺服器來聚合從單個邊緣節點學習的模型來解決此問題。此外，存在其他分散式模型學習方法，例如分層 FL、Gossip 學習和 E-Tree 學習，以支援在大規模系統中的可擴展和快速模型訓練。 邊緣智慧相關研究仍有一些挑戰有待解決。第一個問題是邊緣設備上生成的 NonIID 數據導致的模型不準確。 現有的邊緣AI方法旨在學習適合所有邊緣節點的通用模型。 在實踐中，用於訓練廣義模型的數據與在邊緣節點上生成的 NonIID 數據有很大不同，導致模型在節點上進行推理不準確。 第二個問題是關於數據標記。 由於標記成本高，邊緣節點上生成的數據大多未標記。 現有方法假設良好標記的數據樣本無法有效工作，需要開發新的模型訓練方法來利用大量未標記的數據。 第三個問題是物聯網數據的特性，它們通常是不斷到達邊緣節點的流數據。 假設在啟動時數據樣本可用的現有方法不適合邊緣智慧場景。 為了解決這些具有挑戰性的問題，在本提案中，我們建議開發用於在大規模邊緣計算系統中使用未標記流數據進行模型訓練的方法和解決方案。為了解決 NonIID 數據問題，考慮到訓練和測試數據之間的領域差異，我們將開發一種有效的多工學習方法，並設計演算法來優化任務數量和任務到邊緣節點的分配；同時，將開發跨任務的知識共用和轉移的有效合作機制。為了解決數據標記問題，我們將開發一種新的分散式半監督學習方法來利用學習任務中的未標記數據。為了支援流數據的冷開機和終身（增量）學習，我們將開發方法來確定觸發終身學習的時間，提出演算法來選擇歷史數據樣本進行緩存，利用以前的知識和緩存樣本更新當前模型。將基於我們之前提出的 E-Tree 學習框架來實現和評估所提出的方法、演算法和機制。 該專案意義重大且具有創新性。將解決重要且具有挑戰性的研究問題，開發有助於推進邊緣計算和邊緣人工智慧技術和應用的創新性解決方案。本項目具有很高的學術價值，同時兼具較大的實際應用價值。

15204921.label: Realisation of objectives
15204921.value: We have achieved all the objectives as stated in the proposal. The first objective is to investigate the requirements and the challenges of decentralized model learning for data generated at the edge nodes. We have systematically investigated and identified the challenging issues. The first key issue is the non-IID data. Existing edge AI approaches target at learning a generalized model fit for all the edge nodes. In practice, data used in existing works for training a generalized model differs a lot from the NonIID data generated on an edge node, causing the model inaccuracy for inference on the node. The second key issue is data labeling. The data generated on the edge nodes are mostly unlabeled due to high labeling cost. Existing approaches assuming well-labeled data samples cannot work effectively, and new model training methods need to be developed to exploit massive unlabeled data. The third key issue is the nature of IoT data, which is usually streaming data continuously arriving at the edge nodes. Existing approaches assuming that data samples are available at the start-up time are not suitable for Edge AI. The second objective is to develop algorithms and mechanisms to address the identified challenging issues, and conduct theoretical analyses and/or simulations to evaluate the performance of the proposed algorithms and mechanisms. We have developed solutions to three specific problems. The first problem is the non-IID among edge devices. The second problem is the massive unlabeled data on edge devices [J6]. The third problem is the distributed model training framework for streaming data [J1, J5]. For the first problem, we studied the personalization of ML models in distributed model training to address the non-IID issue. One popular technique is personalized federated learning, which aims to train each participant with a customized model that can fit them well. In existing literature, meta-learning has been regarded as an important technique to achieve personalized federated learning, due to its fast adaptation capability. It first obtains a single global model, and each client achieves a personalized model by fine-tuning the global one with its local data. However, existing meta-learning-based approaches implicitly assume that the data distribution among different clients is similar, which may not be applicable due to the property of data heterogeneity in federated learning. We proposed a group-based federated Meta-learning framework, called G-FML, which adaptively divides the clients into groups based on the similarity of their data distribution, and obtains the personalized models with meta-learning within each group. Specifically, we developed a simple yet effective grouping mechanism to adaptively cluster the clients into multiple groups. The mechanism ensures that each group is formed by the clients with similar data distribution, such that the group-wise meta-model can achieve “personalization” at large. By doing so, our framework can be generalized to a highly heterogeneous environment. The experimental results show that our framework improves the model accuracy by up to 13.15% in comparison to the state-of-the-art federated meta-learning. For the second problem, we studied the unlabeled data issue. In existing works of distributed machine learning in edge computing, data are kept on each device without transferring across the network, and the model is optimized with global data information. However, these methods assume data generated on edge devices is labeled, which is unrealistic. In practice, due to the labor-intensive and time-consuming nature of data labeling in edge computing, only a small portion of data is labeled. We studied a new practical approach, Distributed Semi-Supervised Learning (DSSL), to learn models collaboratively with mixed private labeled and unlabeled data on each device. We also proposed a novel method, DistMatch, which exploits private unlabeled data using self-training on each device with the help of models from neighboring devices. DistMatch generates pseudo-labels for unlabeled data by properly averaging the predictions of these received models. Furthermore, to avoid self-training with wrong pseudo-labels, DistMatch proposes a consensus consistency loss to filter pseudo-labels with high consensus and force the output of the trained model to be consistent with these pseudo-labels. Extensive evaluation results via our self-developed testbed indicate the proposed method outperforms all baselines on commonly used image classification benchmark datasets. For the third problem, we studied the data heterogeneity challenge of streaming data in edge computing. Data is continuously generated on edge devices with inherent heterogeneity, which encompasses variations in dataset size, complexity, and similarity. This heterogeneity presents unique challenges, especially in training accuracy models. Continuous learning is a promising approach, but conventional continual learning methods are typically task-agnostic and depend on either rehearsal or regularization techniques, and they have limitations when dealing with such heterogeneous data. We proposed a novel adaptive continual learning (AdaptCL) method [J1] to tackle the issue of heterogeneity in sequential datasets. AdaptCL employs fine-grained data-driven pruning to adapt to variations in data complexity and dataset size. It also utilizes task-agnostic parameter isolation to mitigate the impact of varying degrees of catastrophic forgetting caused by differences in data similarity. Through a two-pronged case study approach, we evaluate AdaptCL on both datasets of MNIST variants and DomainNet, as well as datasets from different domains. Across all these scenarios, AdaptCL consistently exhibits robust performance, demonstrating its flexibility and general applicability. The third objective is to develop representative applications. We target the edge video analytics application with streaming videos. First, we proposed a scalable online video analytics scheme, called Novas [J5], which automatically makes precise service configuration adjustments upon constant video content changes to guarantee the QoS. Novas leverages the filtered confidence sum and a two-window t-test to online detect accuracy fluctuations without ground truth. In such cases, Novas efficiently estimates the performance of all potential service configurations through a singular value decomposition (SVD)-based collaborative filtering method. Finally, given the NP-hardness of the optimal scheduling problem, a heuristic scheduling strategy that maximizes the minimum remaining resources is devised to schedule the most suitable configurations to servers for execution. Results show that Novas can achieve a substantial over 27× improvement in satisfying the accuracy requirements and improve the goodput of the system by an average of 37.86%. Moreover, we proposed a blockchain-based collaborative edge intelligence (BCEI) approach to support trustworthy and real-time video surveillance. BCEI establishes a peer-to-peer network of edge devices that maintain a permissioned blockchain to authenticate video analytics results. By leveraging a permissioned blockchain, which has relatively low resource demands compared to public blockchains, the cameras stream videos to nearby edge devices, enabling the sharing of computation resources and data. Moreover, we have formulated and solved a joint stream mapping and task scheduling problem to schedule video streams and machine learning models among edge devices. This approach enables us to effectively manage the high volume and velocity of streaming data and to train models in a distributed manner across multiple edge devices. To evaluate the practicality and efficiency of BCEI, we deployed a real-world prototype for pedestrian reidentification. Seven Internet Protocol (IP) cameras were deployed in an indoor environment, streaming videos to a cluster of geo-distributed edge devices. Results demonstrated nearly real-time performance, outperforming state-of-the-art solutions in terms of system throughput and latency.

15204921.label: Major findings and research outcome
15204921.value: We conducted pioneering research to enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of decentralized model learning in edge computing. By designing and developing innovative methods and algorithms that address critical challenges in the field, our work has substantially advanced the state of the art. These contributions have resulted in 10 publications in top-tier journals and conferences and have been further translated into practical impact through the development of a distributed edge AI platform. This platform, which has yielded two patents, currently provides low-latency, privacy-preserving video analytics services across two university campuses. Our research findings and outcomes cover four major aspects. First, we have developed a personalized federated learning solution to address the non-IID issues in distributed model training in edge computing. We have designed and developed G-FML, a group-based federated Meta-learning framework to solve the problem, which adaptively divides the clients into groups based on the similarity of their data distribution. Specifically, we developed a simple yet effective grouping mechanism to adaptively partition the clients into multiple groups, ensuring that each group is formed by the clients with similar data distribution such that the group-wise meta-model can achieve “personalization” at large. The experimental results show that our framework improves the model accuracy by up to 13.15% relative to the state-of-the-art federated meta-learning. Second, we proposed Distributed Semi-Supervised Learning (DSSL) to learn models collaboratively with mixed private labeled and unlabeled data on each device. We also proposed a novel method, DistMatch, that exploits private unlabeled data by self-training on each device with the help of models from neighboring devices. Extensive evaluation results via our self-developed testbed indicate the proposed method outperforms all baselines on commonly used image classification benchmark datasets. Third, we proposed a novel adaptive continual learning (AdaptCL) method to tackle heterogeneity in sequential datasets. AdaptCL employs fine-grained data-driven pruning to adapt to variations in data complexity and dataset size. It also utilizes task-agnostic parameter isolation to mitigate the impact of varying degrees of catastrophic forgetting caused by differences in data similarity. Based on AdaptCL, we developed a food freshness detection system, which can effectively detect food freshness over time. The system demonstration attracts great interest from both academia and industry, with over 100+ visits, showing its societal impact. Fourth, based on BCEI, we developed a distributed edge intelligence system to support collaborative real-time video surveillance across multiple cameras. The proposed solution enables multiple cameras to stream the videos to different edge devices, which collaborate with each other to share computation resources and data. Experiments show that our proposed system can achieve near real-time pedestrian tracking and re-identification through efficient task scheduling. This platform has been deployed in PolyU and Beijing Normal University (Zhuhai) for pedestrian counting and safety monitoring, helping improve operational efficiency.

15204921.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15204921.value: In this project, we have conducted research to solve the non-IID, unlabeled, and streaming data challenge in distributed edge learning. We envision that further research can be done in two ways to extend the impact. One direction is developing practical applications for knowledge transfer. Edge AI has wide applications in industrial quality inspection, video surveillance, robotics, and smart manufacturing. This project studies non-IID, unlabeled, and streaming data challenges in edge AI, all of which are common challenges encountered in practical implementations. We have developed a system for edge video analytics to handle video streams covering large areas. Future applications will explore broader scenarios such as industrial applications and intelligent decision-making and control of robots. Another direction is to support large model fine-tuning in edge computing. With the explosive growth of large AI models (e.g., LLaMA, GPT variants) and the increasing demand for domain-specific adaptation, fine-tuning large models directly on or near edge devices is becoming critical. This reduces latency, preserves data privacy, and customizes models for local contexts. Edge-based fine-tuning supports injecting private enterprise knowledge, improving instruction-following capabilities, and reducing hallucination in large models, which is vital for vertical AIoT applications.

15204921.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15204921.value: Research conducted in this project makes a significant contribution to the distributed model training in edge computing. In particular, this research proposes novel methods and algorithms to address the key challenging issues, with the objective of accelerating the distributed model training and improving model accuracy. We investigated important problems, including distributed model training over non-IID, unlabeled, and streaming data, and proposed novel solutions and demonstrated their effectiveness and efficiency by developing a prototype that enables large-scale testing for distributed machine learning solutions in an edge computing environment. Based on that, we also developed a low-latency and privacy-preserving video analytics platform, which has been deployed in PolyU and Beijing Normal University (Zhuhai) for pedestrian counting and safety monitoring. Our research not only leads to advances in distributed model learning in edge computing but also generates significant impacts by enabling emerging advanced applications, including autonomous vehicles, video analytics, and smart cities.

15205221.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15205221.value: Wicking fabrics that facilitate controllable movement of liquid sweat from the skin surface to the environment are highly desirable to human comfort and performance. However, based on passive wicking and evaporation, excessive moisture absorbed and trapped inside conventional wicking fabrics cannot always be transmitted and dissipated directionally and quickly, making clothes uncomfortably heavy, sticky, and unbreathable. As well, wicking fabrics are generally non-repellent and non-resistant to external liquids such as rain. In this project, we propose an electricity-regulated wicking (E-Wicking) fabric that achieves efficient, directional liquid transport and dissipation under low voltage, making the skin dry and keeping moisture comfort. The design of the E-Wicking fabric is inspired by active sweat secretion of skin surface in the form of droplets and detachment of water droplets from alternating water-attractive and water-repellent regions of beetle’s back. The fabric will accelerate liquid transfer and block undesired external liquids by the combined effects of active electroosmotic action and passive capillary drainage. We will develop the E-Wicking fabric by sandwiching a nanofibrous membrane with thin fabric layers of electrically conductive materials as electrodes. On the skin side, the fast-wicking fabric will be utilized for quick liquid transfer towards the nanofibrous membrane with greater capillary pressure. The outer layer will be treated with super-hydrophobicity predominantly and moderate-hydrophobicity locally to repel external liquids, while allowing dissipation of liquid droplets through the local regions with smaller capillary resistance under low voltage. We will validate the design concept and theoretically and experientially investigate the mechanisms of E-Wicking process driven by the coupled electroosmotic and capillary flows, improving understanding of how significant factors, including patterned wettability, pore radius, and applied voltage, affect the liquid transport properties. Preliminary results have provided a potential basis for this project: when the E-Wicking fabric contacts a water source or generated steam, approximately corresponding to sensible and insensible perspiration, respectively, the absorbed liquid water can move directionally to the outer face and release as water droplets under a low voltage. However, external liquids are repelled and resisted on the outer surface with high breakthrough pressure. The scalable fabric exhibits high durability and the flow rate is found to exceed the individual's high sweating rate. From application-oriented implementation to fundamental research, the success of this project will advance knowledge and understanding of controllable liquid transport in porous media. The guidelines developed from this project will contribute to engineering high-performance wicking fabrics for many applications. 導水織物在個性化水分管理、微流控、油水分離和傷口敷料等領域具有廣泛重要的應用。然而，常規導水織物受到液體輸運調控能力的高度限製。例如，當導水織物吸收大量水分而不能快速轉移，衣服將變得沈重和粘稠，使穿著者不舒服。雖然親水織物有利於加速吸水，但吸收的水分往往不易排放轉移，實現完全的單向水分輸運。此外，導水過程還受限於復雜微結構織物產生的流阻，難以滿足不同應用中對快速可控液體輸運的迫切要求。 為此，本項目將研發一種電控排水（E-Wicking）織物，以實現程式調控液體輸運。E-Wicking織物將類似一個柔性開關，可以加速或阻止織物內的液體流動，並釋放或阻擋織物外表面的液體。我們將納米纖維膜夾在塗有導電聚合物的薄纖維層電極中間來構建 E-Wicking 織物，通過有機協調低壓電滲作用和毛細驅動來實現精確可控的液體輸運。此外，我們將使用環保等離子體技術處理織物表面，構築超疏水和中等疏水圖案分布，使內部液體通過中等疏水區域排除釋放，同時隔絕外部液體進入。將進行深入的基礎研究，包括在電滲和毛細作用耦合效應驅動下的 E-Wicking 過程理論建模、微觀結構和施加電壓對動態流體輸運控製影響的量化及優化。此外，初步探索提供了可行性依據：E-Wicking織物內的液體受可控低壓電驅動，輸運速度隨電壓增大而增加，並在外表面以液滴形式排放；同時外部液體難以侵入織物。 本項目是面向應用的基礎研究，將提升多孔介質中液體輸運機理的認識和理解，促進新型液體調控理論框架的發展。本項目還將推進設計具有多種應用的高性能排水織物，無需笨重且昂貴的硬質水泵。

15205221.label: Realisation of objectives
15205221.value: Objective 1 – Electricity regulated E Wicking concept This objective has been achieved. We have proposed and experimentally demonstrated an Electro textile based on electroosmosis and wettability patterning that provides unidirectional, electricity regulated liquid transport. Using a 0.2 μm PC membrane, the fabric reaches and exceeds the maximum human sweating rate (~1710 g·h⁻¹·m⁻²) at only 2.5 V, and achieves up to 23.6 times this rate at 7 V. Inclined and hydrostatic tests further show that, under reverse bias, the Electro textile can actively repel and block external liquids, withstanding >20 cm water column. Thus, the E Wicking concept and its targeted performance have been fulfilled. Objective 2 – Processing methods, dissipation rate, breakthrough pressure and durability This objective has been achieved in terms of processing and tunable performance. We have established a complete fabrication route combining hydrophilic/hydrophobic finishing of carbon fabrics, selective plasma patterning of “sweat pores”, and hot press lamination with porous membranes. By selecting different membranes (PC 0.1/0.2/0.4 μm and PTFE) and adjusting the applied voltage (2–7 V), we can tune both sweat dissipation rate and hydrostatic breakthrough pressure in a controlled manner. Mechanical (tensile and abrasion) tests indicate acceptable baseline robustness of the textile electrodes. Systematic long term durability (repeated cycling, washing, and electrochemical ageing) will be further studied in the commercialization stage, but the core processing and performance targets have been met. Objective 3 – Theoretical modelling and coupled electroosmotic–capillary effects This objective has been achieved at the level required for the current stage. We have established an EOF model for the porous membrane based on electric double layer theory and the Helmholtz–Smoluchowski equation, extended to porous media by including porosity and effective area. Single pore numerical simulations provide velocity, potential and charge distributions consistent with experiments. At the textile scale, the roles of electroosmosis in the membrane and capillary spreading/absorption in the carbon fabrics have been clearly identified and linked to the observed E Wicking behaviour. The theoretical framework and its connection to experiments are basically in place. Objective 4 – Experimental validation and parametric influence This objective has been achieved. The Electro textile design and mechanisms have been validated through systematic experiments under horizontal and inclined configurations and on a sweating manikin. We have quantified how pore size (PC 0.1/0.2/0.4 μm vs PTFE), wettability pattern (single vs double sided plasma, pore vs non pore regions), and applied voltage (2–7 V, with identification of electrolysis limits) affect flow rate, unidirectionality, and breakthrough pressure. The measured trends agree well with the proposed electroosmotic and capillarity based mechanisms, and a garment scale demo (sports T shirt) confirms practical feasibility. Therefore, the experimental validation and parametric understanding required by Objective 4 have been fulfilled.

15205221.label: Major findings and research outcome
15205221.value: Electricity‑regulated E‑Wicking textiles were demonstrated using carbon‑fabric electrodes and porous membranes to achieve low‑voltage, unidirectional sweat transport far beyond maximal human sweating rates, while actively repelling external water. A scalable fabrication route (hydrophilic/hydrophobic finishing, patterned plasma “sweat pores”, lamination) enables tunable dissipation rate and hydrostatic resistance via membrane choice and voltage. Electroosmotic flow in pores, coupled with capillary absorption/spreading in fabrics, was modelled and confirmed by single‑pore simulations. Systematic experiments clarified the roles of pore size, wettability pattern and voltage, and a sports T‑shirt prototype on a sweating manikin verified practical, garment‑scale applicability. Research Outcomes: 5 papers as corresponding author, including publications in leading journals such as Science, Advanced Materials, and Advanced Functional Materials, 2 additional papers in preparation / to be submitted, 2 PhD students and 1 undergraduate student successfully trained, International recognition, including a Gold Medal at the Geneva Inventions Exhibition, 1 Chinese patent granted and 1 US patent filed.

15205221.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15205221.value: The present work provides a solid electro‑textile platform with clear potential for further development. Next, we will systematically study durability under repeated wetting–drying, mechanical deformation, washing and long‑term low‑voltage operation, and optimize materials and encapsulation for real‑world garments. The current electroosmotic–capillary framework will be extended to a fully coupled, predictive design tool to determine optimal pore size, membrane thickness and wettability patterns for different climates and body locations. We will also pursue system‑level integration with wearable electronics (sensors, power management) for autonomous microclimate control. In parallel, we plan scale‑up and field tests with industrial partners in sportswear, protective and medical textiles.

15205221.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15205221.value: This project creates a new generation of bio‑inspired, electricity‑regulated wicking fabrics, called E‑Wicking fabrics, that work like artificial sweat glands in human skin. Unlike ordinary breathable or waterproof textiles, E‑Wicking fabrics can actively pump sweat out using only a very low voltage, while still blocking rain and external water. This provides major benefits for high‑performance sportswear, protective gear (e.g. firefighters, soldiers) and medical wearables, where overheating and sweat build‑up are serious problems. Mimicking natural sweat glands, E‑Wicking fabrics use a “sandwich” structure: two carbon‑fabric layers and a thin porous film in between. When a small voltage is applied, sweat is drawn from the skin side through microscopic “sweat pores” and released outside, even against gravity. The fabrics handle sweat rates far above the human maximum, remain thin and flexible, can be manufactured using scalable textile processes, and have already been demonstrated in sportwear, supported by patents and international awards.

15205321.label: Project Objectives
15205321.value: Develop predictive models that are applicable for commercial BMS considering multiple aspects. The main subtasks or challenges to be addressed include: i. selection of candidate model structures; ii. quantification of model applicability through the aspects of accuracy, robustness, computational load, and programmability in commercial BMS; iii. normalization of model applicability through different aspects for comparison; iv. selection of the models based on the quantified and normalized model applicability. Develop a mechanism to enable models to adapt to system change (e.g. equipment degradation, overhaul, sensor calibration) without risking control system stability. A matrix of model prediction error is proposed in this study to avoid periodic online training of models in commercial BMS that has high computational load and may cause controllers or network stations to restart. The main challenges to be addressed include: i. construction of the model error matrix with proper resolution over the input space, ii. development of an algorithm for real time and online adjustment of the model error matrix according to new measurements, iii. continuous evaluation of the model accuracy and alert to update the model parameters in case they are outdated. Develop a mechanism to cooperate supply and demand side controls for higher energy efficiency. The main challenges include: i. establishment of a proper means to identify the tolerance of indoor thermal environment. ii. establishment of a proper means to predict indoor thermal environment when a certain amount of cooling is supplied. iii. establishment of a negotiation scheme for cooperation between cooling supply and demand side controls. Develop novel adaptive predictive optimal chiller control strategies that are applicable for commercial BMS, including optimal chiller sequencing control, optimal supply chilled water temperature reset, and optimal chiller loading control. Validate the model selection method considering applicability in commercial BMS. All candidate models associated with the control of chiller plants will be built and compared. The validation will be based on a real HVAC system for a high-rise commercial building. Validate the proposed method for real time and online adjustment of the model error matrix. The validation will be conducted based on the operational data of a large and complex HVAC system in a high-rise commercial building in Hong Kong. Validate the proposed negotiation scheme for demand side and supply side control, as well as the novel adaptive predictive optimal chiller control strategies. A dynamic simulation platform, representing a large and complex HVAC system in a high-rise commercial building, will be built to test and validate the proposed control strategies. The control strategies will also be programmed into the commercial BMS onsite to validate their applicability. The control strategies will be activated to control the real system upon confirmation of their effectiveness.

15205321.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15205321.value: In Hong Kong, a hot and humid region, air-conditioning systems consume about 31% of total electricity. Energy efficiency enhancement for chiller plants in buildings has always been in high demand. Challenges in this regard include discovering and implementing effective control strategies and dealing with uncertainties. Many effective advanced optimal control strategies exist in literature, and almost all of them utilize complex predictive models and/or advanced optimization algorithms. The validation/implementation of these developed strategies are mostly conducted on simulation platforms or through advanced programming software that can handle complex models and advanced optimization algorithms. However, the control strategies widely applied in real systems are still rule-based (reactive rather than predictive) empirical near optimal methods. The limited capability of commercially available building management systems (hereinafter referred to as commercial BMS) is rarely considered during the development of these control strategies. In this proposed project, novel adaptive predictive optimal control strategies will be developed and validated to address the challenges of enhancing chiller plant efficiency considering the limitations of commercial BMSs. By taking the advantages of modern technologies in sensing and communication that are increasingly applied in buildings, the optimal control strategies should have similar or even higher performance than the strategies using complex predictive models and/or advanced optimization algorithms. The proposed control strategies involve a multi-aspect evaluation method to discover models with balanced applicability. Model applicability will be quantified in four aspects: accuracy, robustness, computational load, and programmability in commercial BMSs. The quantified model applicability will be normalized for easier selection. To be adaptive to system changes, a matrix of model error will be built for further online correction of model predictions, rather than periodically updating the models online. This model error matrix will be continuously adjusted online with new measurements. In this way, the model training process can be avoided in BMS, and the risk of restart of controllers/network stations due to high computational load can be eliminated. The proposed control strategies will also involve a scheme applicable to commercial BMS for cooperating between cooling supply and demand sides. Room conditions will be controlled to vary around the desired thermal comfort level. This will allow further increases in system efficiency. 15205721.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15205721.value: Loess is widely distributed in the world, including the Loess Plateau of China (LPC) with an area of 640,000 square kilometers. In the LPC, landslide is one of the most serious geohazards, particularly for places with clayey/silty loess wherein the number of landslides per unit area is about five times of the average value of China. Loess slopes are usually unsaturated due to the low water table and rainfall is the most important triggering factor of relevant landslides. To mitigate landslide hazard effectively, it is extremely important to fully understand the engineering properties of unsaturated loess, which are more complicated than those of many other soils. At unsaturated condition, loess is able to sustain a metastable structure because suction stabilizes soil skeleton. The structure is often accompanied by anisotropy (i.e. direction-dependent). Under excessive hydro-mechanical loads, structured loess would collapse and affect its anisotropic responses significantly. The importance of structure and anisotropy in the slope analysis has been well recognized. So far, previous studies of structure and anisotropy effects mainly focus on saturated loess. There is an urgent need to enhance the fundamental understanding and modelling capability of unsaturated loess, with a consideration of structure and anisotropy. The proposed project will address these challenges through laboratory testing and theoretical modelling. In the laboratory part, intact and reconstituted specimens of two loess soils (i.e. silty and clayey) will be tested using suction-controlled triaxial apparatuses. Their behaviour will be compared to reveal the influence of structure and anisotropy. Mechanical properties, particularly the critical state, dilatancy and wetting-induced collapse, will be determined for slope stability analysis. Hydraulic properties, including the water retention curve and water permeability function, will be obtained for seepage analysis. To assist data interpretations, soil microstructures will be determined. Based on these unique experimental results, a novel constitutive model will be developed for unsaturated loess. The newly developed model will be able to predict the evolution of structure and plastic anisotropy and its influence on the coupled hydro-mechanical behaviour of unsaturated loess. Furthermore, this model will be implemented into a finite element code and verified using physical model tests in the literature. Parametric studies will be conducted to investigate the hydraulic and mechanical responses of unsaturated loess slopes subjected to rainfall. The success of this project will improve our fundamental understanding and theoretical modelling of loess. The new results will enable engineers to improve the analysis and design of loess slopes. 黃土在世界範圍內分佈廣泛，其中我國的黃土高原面積達64萬平方公里。在黃土高原，滑坡是最嚴重的地質災害之一，特別是在黏質和粉質黃土覆蓋的區域，單位面積內滑坡數量約為全國平均值的5倍。主要原因在於，黃土比其它土體的工程性質更為複雜，具有明顯的結構性和各向異性，在非飽和條件下能夠維持亞穩定性結構，但在水-力荷載耦合作用下容易發生濕陷和失穩。為有效治理黃土地區的滑坡災害，充分認識黃土的工程性質具有重要意義。迄今為止，對黃土結構性和各向異性的研究主要集中在飽和狀態。因此，需要研究非飽和黃土的結構性和各項異性，並提出先進的理論模型。本項目將通過室內試驗和理論建模來解決這些問題。在室內試驗部分，將採用吸力控制的三軸儀對兩種黃土（即粉質和粘質）的原狀和重塑樣進行測試。基於試驗結果揭示原狀黃土的結構性和各向異性規律、黃土的力學性質（臨界狀態、剪脹和濕陷）以及水力學特性（持水特徵曲線和滲透係數方程）。基於試驗結果，將提出新的非飽和黃土本構模型，以預測非飽和黃土結構性和各向異性的演變規律及其對水-力學耦合特性的影響，並通過數值模擬對黃土邊坡進行參數分析。本項目的成功將提高對黃土工程特性的基本認識，建立完善的理論模型，幫助工程人員改進黃土邊坡的分析和設計。

15205821.label: Realisation of objectives
15205821.value: (1) Realisation of Objective 1 We have successfully developed a GNSS water vapor estimation tool based on the Precise Point Positioning (PPP) technique. The GNSS PPP tool has been used to process water vapor data from ground-based GNSS stations as well as from 5th Generation communication stations (“5G” stations). A large amount of water vapor data have been obtained. Multiple-year water vapor from nearly 300 GNSS stations in the South China region have been obtained. In addition to that, water vapor data from more than 1500 “5G” stations in the Province of Guangdong have been obtained. These water vapor datasets have been utilized in this project’s research work and publications/presentations. A number of machine learning-based models, including Back Propagation Neural Network (BPNN), Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM), gradient boosting decision tree (GBDT), generalized regression neural network (GRNN), K-nearest neighbor (KNN), multilayer perceptron neural network (MLPNN), and extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), have been developed to calibrate satellite water vapor data. The accuracy of the new retrievals using the machine learning models has been improved by more than 50%, taking MODIS near-infrared water vapor products as an example. Moreover, the new calibration model has considered the “cloud” effect and the water vapor under cloud conditions has been generated. The generation of accurate water vapor data under cloudy condition (“all weather” condition) is a significant advancement. This implies that much more water vapor data can be obtained under “cloudy” condition (i.e. all weather condition). This has significant advantage compared to raw satellite water vapor data, as many more water vapor data can be produced. In addition, this project has also generated a lot of microwave satellite water vapor data over land. Traditionally, microwave water vapor data are not available over land area due to the low accuracy of water vapor retrieval. In this project, we developed Machine Learning-based model to retrieve water vapor over land. The Global Precipitation Measurement (GPM) Microwave Imager (GMI) dataset has been used. 2017-2020 global GMI water vapor data over land have been obtained. The model was trained on 2017 data from 4,471 GNSS stations and validated globally with independent data from 4,341 GNSS stations (2018-2020) and 605 radiosonde stations (2017-2020). The accuracy is 5.82 mm to 6.02 mm, depending on the reference water vapor datasets. In addition, ocean-based satellite water vapor data over the South China region have been used. They have been assimilated into Numerical Weather Prediction (NWP) model to improve weather prediction performance during TC and other extreme weather conditions. In this study, BPNN model has been used to calibrate water vapor from altimetry satellite Jason-3 over coastal areas. Jason-3 water vapor data during the period February 2016 to June 2023 have been obtained. Our results showed that we can reduce the root mean square error (RMSE) of Jason-3 PWV in the coastal areas from 4.2 to 2.7 kg/m2 (35.7% of RMSE reduction). (2) Realisation of Objective 2 The multi-source water vapor datasets capture moisture distribution from land and ocean and supports continuous monitoring of water vapor evolution throughout the entire TC lifecycle and other extreme weather conditions. Taking the May 20, 2020 South China TC-induced heavy rainfall case as an example, using the raw water vapor data from the Chinese FY-4A satellite, the spatial and temporal structures of moisture were not present. After the calibration of the FY-4A satellite water vapor data, the calibrated FY-4A data revealed spatial and temporal structures of moisture. The raw PWV systematically underestimated moisture, especially in high-PWV regimes, whereas the calibrated dataset captured sharper gradients and more coherent mesoscale features. Assimilation diagnostics further indicated that the Numerical Weather Prediction (e.g. We used the Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) model) background tended to overestimate moisture in key convective regions, and assimilating the calibrated FY-4A water vapor data effectively corrected these biases by reducing excessive moisture and improving the thermodynamic fields linked to precipitation development. For the TC Haikui, the multi-source water vapor dataset from GNSS, satellite sensor AMSR2 (Advanced Microwave Scanning Radiometer 2), and conventional observations enabled continuous depiction of moisture transport, boundary-layer inflow, and moisture convergence along the eyewall and rainbands. When assimilated into NWP model (i.e. WRF model), these observations substantially improved the initial atmospheric state by correcting vertical humidity structure, enhancing low-level cyclonic inflow, and refining mid-tropospheric moistening associated with the typhoon circulation. The improved initial fields provided more realistic representation of rainband evolution, coastal convergence zones, and moisture pathways during different stages of the typhoon and at varying distances from land. (3) Realisation of Objective 3 To examine how the newly generated water vapor datasets may benefit a forecasting framework similar to that used by the HKO, a series of numerical experiments were carried out using the WRF 3DVAR system. For instance, for the TC Haikui (2023), the assimilation of GNSS-retrieved water vapor alone and AMSR2 ocean-based PWV alone both led to noticeable improvements in the initial moisture distribution and subsequent precipitation forecasts, particularly for light-to-moderate rainfall. These results demonstrate the value of incorporating additional water vapor information from land and ocean observations into the model initialization process. For the extreme rainfall threshold of 100 mm, the improvement was dramatic. The assimilation of AMSR2 data increased the Critical Success Index (CSI) by over 227% and the Equitable Threat Score (ETS) by over 257% compared to the result without water vapor data assimilation. In the 30 mm rainfall threshold, the Ocean-based AMSR2 water vapor can improve CSI by 80.66% and ETS by 94.89%. This indicates that capturing moisture structures over the open ocean (where ground stations are absent) is critical for correctly simulating the rainbands before they make landfall. The additional experiments conducted for April–June 2024 further supported the findings from the Haikui case. Assimilating PWV generally improved the representation of moisture fields and rainfall patterns over South China, especially in coastal regions where moisture convergence strongly affects precipitation. Our recent publication showed that for TC-induced intense-precipitation days (precipitation larger than 150 mm within 24-h) in South China, assimilating ocean-based microwave satellite water vapor data could improve the equitable threat score (ETS) by up to 26.3%), while assimilating ground-based GNSS water vapor data could improve ETS by up to 27.6%. When both ocean-based microwave satellite and GNSS water vapor data were assimilated, the ETS score increased by up to 39.5%. Overall, the experiments evaluated how the new water vapor datasets interact with a high-resolution forecasting system and offer practical guidance for refining moisture assimilation strategies in support of HKO rainfall prediction. To the best of our information, the HKO so far has NOT assimilated water vapor data from GNSS or water vapor data from remote sensing satellite yet. At the point of completing this report, the PI Prof. Liu’s team is working with HKO scientists to assimilate multi-source water vapor data into HKO’s operational NWP system. It took a longer than expected time to overcome various difficulties and achieve this stage. The preliminary test showed promising result but needs more extensive validation of historical datasets. More historical datasets need to be recovered or even re-calculated from HKO’s database, which takes a long time.

15205821.label: Major findings and research outcome
15205821.value: This project has achieved a series of outcomes and the major findings are summarized below. The project demonstrates the effectiveness of multi-sensor land-based and ocean-based water vapor observations, particularly their contribution to tropical cyclone and extreme weather forecasting. We have developed GNSS (Global Navigation Satellite System) precise point positioning (PPP) method and software tool to retrieve water vapor data from a large number of ground-based GNSS stations as well as 5G communication stations over land (through collaboration with Huawei Technologies and China Mobile Group Guangdong Co. Ltd). We have also developed methods to assimilate land-based and ocean-based water vapor data into Numerical Weather Prediction (NWP) model for extreme weather events like tropical cyclones (TC). Based on ocean-based satellite data, we have also developed methods to determine TC eye position. We have established a high-precision PPP-Ambiguity Resolution (AR) processing pipeline capable of generating water vapor datasets with millimeter-level accuracy. Water vapor from both ground-based GNSS data and 5G communication stations have been retrieved based on PPP solutions. We have established a high-resolution water vapor dataset by integrating ground-based GNSS and ocean-based satellite observations. Our analysis quantified the temporal and spatial variation rates of water vapor. A key finding is the identification of intense moisture corridors (Atmospheric Rivers) as a dominant mechanism for water vapor transport in the region. We found that these moisture plumes often create a background environment conducive to extreme precipitation. The spatial gradient of water vapor was found to be a reliable indicator of precipitation intensity, a characteristic shared by both tropical cyclones and extratropical systems. The research demonstrated that rapid temporal surges in GNSS-derived water vapor serve as effective precursors for approaching extreme weather systems. This finding supports the project's goal of enhancing forecasting reliability, suggesting that monitoring moisture transport intensity (IVT) is as critical as monitoring pressure systems for predicting severe weather impacts. Our analysis of TC Ragasa revealed a distinct temporal signature: a significant "V-shape" subsidence anomaly in the GNSS zenith total delay time series approximately 24 hours prior to the closest approach. This finding confirms that ground-based GNSS can effectively detect the moisture divergence associated with the outer subsidence area of a tropical cyclone, serving as a potential early indicator for TC track forecasting. Back Propagation Neural Network (BPNN)-based Machine Learning (ML) calibration model has been developed to calibrate satellite water vapor observations and improve satellite water vapor accuracy. For instance, calibration reduced RMSE (root-mean-squares error) of Chinese satellite FY-4A water vapor data by nearly 47% and effectively corrected long-standing dry biases. In NWP data assimilation, both raw and calibrated satellite water vapor data can improve the spatial pattern of precipitation forecasts, while the calibrated satellite water vapor data achieved notably higher forecasting scores (e.g. Equitable Threat Score, Probability of Detection, Critical Success Index) across multiple rainfall categories. Ground-based GNSS water vapor and ocean-based satellite water vapor each improved the rainfall forecast when assimilated independently in extreme rainfall cases (e.g. 150 mm/24 hours). The joint assimilation of the two datasets can further improve the forecasting performance. An investigation of typhoon eye positioning was carried out using multi-source geostationary satellite observations from FY-4A, FY-4B, and Himawari-9. The three satellites provide a broadly consistent depiction of storm-scale cloud-top structures, which effectively characterizes cloud-top temperature gradients and eyewall morphology. Extensive experiments conducted with multiple TCs demonstrate that among the three platforms, Himawari-9 consistently shows the highest positioning stability and accuracy, with FY-4A yielding comparable performance in most cases. Multi-satellite averaged results exhibit substantially higher robustness than any single-satellite input, achieving an MAE of 17.50 km and an RMSE of 22.71 km.

15205821.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15205821.value: This meaningful project will not stop upon its completion. Instead, future work will be continued in order to achieve more significant outcomes in this direction. Multiple areas can be explored. (1) Further enhancing the quality and applicability of multi-source water vapor datasets for high-impact weather forecasting. A key direction is to improve water vapor calibration under cloudy and deep-convection conditions, where infrared retrievals remain challenged. Additional efforts will be devoted to refining quality-control procedures and developing more robust calibration models that can adapt to seasonal, regional, and sensor-dependent variations. (2) With the large dataset generated, Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Deep Learning techniques can be introduced in order to enhance the accuracy of the water vapor data. AI models can be trained on the historical water vapor data to correct systematic biases in numerical weather prediction models, potentially outperforming traditional physical parameterization schemes. (3) Direct observation of the locations of tropical cyclone eyes using remote sensing satellite data can be explored. After that the TC data can be assimilated into Numerical Weather Prediction (NWP) models to enhance track forecasting and extreme rainfall forecasting. We are working on the identification of Atmospheric Rivers (ARs) based on a large amount of spatially and temporally continuous water vapor data. The identified AR is expected to be incorporated into Hong Kong Observatory’s NWP system and assist extreme rainfall forecasting during TC events in Hong Kong. Collectively, these developments aim to establish a more reliable, operational water vapor assimilation system that can support improved TC monitoring and prediction of extreme rainfall in South China and the Greater Bay Area. With the continued intensification of climate change, the impact of this work will become increasingly meaningful.

15205821.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15205821.value: Tropical cyclones (TCs) usually bring a significant amount of heavy rainfall and cause a series of disasters and damages. Hong Kong’s record-breaking flood event in September 2023 was a typical example due to TC Haikui. Rainfall forecasting can be enhanced by enhancing the measurement of atmospheric water vapor, the critical "fuel" for these extreme weather events. It overcomes limitations in traditional satellite data—especially over the South China Sea—by developing machine learning methods to correct satellite observations and by innovatively repurposing existing infrastructure. Specifically, ground-based 5G communication stations and GNSS/GPS station networks are used to create precise, continuous atmospheric water vapor data. Multiple remote sensing satellites have been calibrated and the water vapor observation accuracy has been significantly. All these data collectively make a dense, accurate measurement of atmospheric water vapor during tropical cyclones and other extreme weather events. The ocean-based microwave satellite water vapor data are particularly useful in enhancing weather forecasting during TC period. It provides valuable measurements over the vast area of ocean, which is not possible with other observation techniques. For example, for intense-precipitation days (precipitation larger than 150 mm within 24-h) in South China, assimilating ocean-based microwave satellite water vapor data could improve the equitable threat score (ETS) by up to 26.3%), while assimilating ground-based GNSS water vapor data could improve ETS by up to 27.6%. When both ocean-based microwave satellite and GNSS water vapor data were assimilated, the ETS score increased by up to 39.5%. Overall, the work provides meteorologists with new scientific tools and insights to issue more reliable early warnings, directly supporting disaster preparedness and public safety in coastal regions like South China and the Greater Bay Area.

15206221.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15206221.value: ROS（機器人操作系統）是最廣泛實驗的機器人軟件開發框架。其被數十萬開發者使用於各種類型機器人系統的開發。機器人系統的軟件通常受到實時性約束，從而使系統的運行與外部環境或物理對象內在的運行規律相匹配。實時性能現在已經成為ROS演進路徑上一個重要的考慮因素。第二代機器人操作系統ROS2為了達到更好的實時性能對其原有的結構進行了重大調整。ROS開發社區中的實時工作組目前也在積極地討論，實驗以及驗證ROS中的各種針對提高實時性能的各種新特性。ROS開發社區的各種努力是使ROS支持實時軟件的必要但是非充分條件。構建實時系統不但需要系統層面的支持，更需要對時間約束的滿足提高保障。此類保障需要構建在一個堅實的理論基礎之上：我們需要嚴格的模型來準確地描述系統的行為，並需要數學方法來形式化地證明所關心的性質。理論層面的深入認識還對ROS的演進起到指導作用。ROS中的許多微妙的設計選擇和實現細節不但是對它的分析變得很困難，並且首先已經使其時間可預測性變得很差。如果有了理論層面的深入認識，我們可以看穿這些微妙的設計選擇和實現細節背後我們所面臨的根本矛盾和實時ROS所能具備的最基本屬性。本項目的目標是為ROS構建這個理論基礎。更確切地說，項目的目標是開發相關理論來針對ROS上開發的機器人應用來證明及實施有關實時性能的重要性質。ROS在有不同實時性要求的各類應用中都得到使用。為了使ROS能滿足不用種類應用的各類需求，本項目將考慮以下幾方面：確定性，可預測性和魯棒性。這三方面各自都帶來了一些重要的挑戰。首先，時間確定性需要限製性極高的執行範式（例如時間觸發執行）並嚴重浪費資源。作為一個通用的機器人軟件框架，ROS難以采用過於嚴格的執行範式，因此需要設計一個既能覆蓋ROS基本特征又能提供證明的確定性屬性的更加靈活的執行範式。其次，現有的實時調度理論無非應對ROS的復雜性，因此需要大幅度地對現有的技術進行擴展來開發一個適用於ROS的分析框架。第三，為了使ROS能夠對各種幹擾具有魯棒性，需要開發新的理論來高效地在運行時進行資源的重新分配以穩定關鍵性任務的實時性能。通過與ROS開發社區的緊密交流，本項目的研究成果不但將用於構建對現有ROS上軟件的實時性能分析工具，而且將對ROS面向更強實時性能的長期演進起指導作用。

15206221.label: Realisation of objectives
15206221.value: This project has successfully achieved its core objectives, with significant theoretical advancements and prototype implementations. Objective 1: The project developed novel and sophisticated models to capture ROS timing behavior. Key publications introduced a DAG-based model for ROS 2 computational graphs and a timed automata model to formally describe the internal execution semantics of ROS 2 nodes. These models precisely capture the interaction between callback scheduling and inter-process communication, forming the foundation for all subsequent theoretical research. Objective 2: The project proposed a novel execution paradigm named Time-sensitive ROS (TSROS), which integrates real-time scheduling theory directly into the ROS executor. This paradigm provides a formal framework for assigning priorities and ensuring schedulability. While a full runtime system is a long-term goal, the theoretical foundation has been firmly established, demonstrating a clear path toward a less-restrictive, deterministic ROS. Objective 3: This objective saw the most direct output. The project developed the first comprehensive Response Time Analysis (RTA) for ROS 2 systems. This technique calculates the worst-case response time for every callback in a ROS node, considering complex factors like callback scheduling policies, communication chains, and different executor types (single-threaded, multi-threaded). This provides a vital method for off-line certification of real-time performance. Objective 4: The project extended its core analysis to be robust against disturbances. This was addressed by modeling and incorporating the effects of unpredictable events, such as buffer overflows or timing variations in sensing, into the worst-case timing analysis framework. The developed RTA inherently considers the worst-case interference scenarios, providing a bound on system behavior even in the presence of such disturbances. Objective 5: The theoretical outcomes were implemented into a practical analysis tool prototype. Furthermore, the research was evaluated using both synthetic benchmarks and real-world case studies, including an autonomous racing car (F1TENTH) platform. The experiments demonstrated the accuracy of the timing predictions and the performance benefits of the proposed TSROS scheduling approach, validating the theoretical work against realistic applications.

15206221.label: Major findings and research outcome
15206221.value: This project has produced several groundbreaking findings that fill a critical gap in real-time robotics research. The key outcome is the establishment of the first holistic theoretical and practical framework for timing analysis of ROS 2. The research conclusively showed that the default, non-real-time executor in ROS 2 introduces significant and unbounded timing unpredictability due to its FIFO-based callback scheduling. In response, the project developed a novel worst-case response time analysis that accurately bounds the execution time of callback chains, accounting for complex intra-node scheduling and inter-node communication. A major finding was the formalization of the ROS 2 execution model using timed automata, which enabled the application of formal verification methods. This model revealed previously overlooked blocking and priority inversion scenarios. Furthermore, the proposed TSROS paradigm demonstrated that by replacing the default scheduler with a priority-driven one, it is possible to achieve provable timing guarantees without sacrificing the flexibility of the ROS framework. These outcomes were encapsulated in a suite of analysis tools and validated on real robotic platforms, showing that the theoretical worst-case bounds are safe and tight, and that the proposed scheduling schemes can dramatically improve timing predictability and system performance. This work provides a foundational step towards making ROS a viable platform for safety-critical real-time applications.

15206221.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15206221.value: The potential for further development is substantial. The immediate course of action is to mature the TSROS runtime system into a fully functional, upstreamable fork of ROS 2, making deterministic execution directly available to developers. Theoretical work will focus on expanding the analysis to more complex scenarios, including: Distributed Systems: Extending the timing analysis framework to cover multi-node, distributed ROS systems across networks with uncertain delays. Mixed-Criticality Systems: Developing scheduling and analysis techniques for ROS applications where tasks have different levels of criticality, allowing for better resource utilization. Machine Learning Integration: Investigating the timing implications of integrating learned components (e.g., neural network controllers) and developing methods to bound their execution times. The long-term goal is to integrate these advancements into the mainline ROS distribution, establishing a de facto standard for building certifiably safe and real-time robotic systems.

15206221.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15206221.value: This research project tackles a fundamental challenge in modern robotics: making complex robot software both smart and reliably timely. Think of a self-driving car; it's not enough for it to eventually detect an obstacle—it must do so within a split second, every time. The project focused on the Robot Operating System (ROS), the "Windows" for most research robots. We discovered that the standard way ROS runs its programs leads to unpredictable timing, making it unsuitable for safety-critical tasks. To solve this, we created new mathematical methods to precisely predict the worst-case time any task in the robot's brain could take. We also designed a new "conductor" for the ROS brain that ensures the most critical tasks always run first, guaranteeing they meet their deadlines. In short, this work provides the essential tools and blueprints to build robot software that is not only functional but also provably safe and reliable, paving the way for their use in our homes, hospitals, and public spaces.

15206421.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15206421.value: 增強現實系統產生虛擬顏色刺激的色貌研究

15206421.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15206421.value: Prof Luo, Ming Ronnier Dr XIAO, Kaida

15206421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15206421.value: Accurate characterizations of perceived colour appearance are critically important to various communities, motivating researchers to make great efforts to understand how human beings perceive colour stimuli under different conditions. These investigations resulted in the developments of chromatic adaptation transforms (CATs) and colour appearance models (CAMs), which are widely used for colour reproductions and specifications in different industries, such as lighting, display, printing, and painting, involving either reflective surface colours or self-luminous displays or lights. Augmented Reality (AR), as an emerging technology, allows users to simultaneously see virtual and physical stimuli by superimposing virtual stimuli onto a real environment. As it provides a more realistic and immersive viewing experience, various communities are exploring the potential of making use of it. For example, lighting designers received inquiries to visualize design solutions using AR instead of computer displays. The type of virtual stimuli produced by AR, however, was never considered when developing the existing CATs and CAMs, as they appear neither completely reflective as typical surface colours nor completely emissive as typical self-luminous displays or lights. Recent studies, including the PI’s studies, and the experiences of a world’s leading manufacturer of AR—Facebook—clearly suggested that the existing CATs and CAMs cannot be used for AR graphics. This project aims to comprehensively investigate the colour appearance of virtual stimuli produced by AR through psychophysical experiments. Human observers will perform a series of colour matching experiments and evaluate the colour attributes of colour stimuli using magnitude estimation methods under various viewing conditions. The physical stimuli will be produced using real objects, realistic replicas, or 3D printed objects; the virtual stimuli will be produced using smart glasses. Numerical modelling will be performed to develop a two-step CAT, which overcomes the weaknesses of the existing one-step CATs, and a CAM for accurately characterizing the colour appearance of virtual stimuli produced by AR. This project is timely and will make great contributions to the development and adoption of AR technology. It will help manufacturers of AR hardware and software to develop better solutions to achieve high quality rendering and reproduction, allowing wider applications in different communities, such as lighting design, architecture and interior designs, education, and entertainment. This project will also further our knowledge on how the human visual system responds to colour stimuli under different conditions, which is a key topic in the International Commission on Illumination (CIE) Research Strategy. 准确表征与描述颜色刺激的色貌对于不同行业来说都至关重要，因而研究人员都致力于研究不同环境下的颜色刺激如何对人类视觉系统产生刺激。这些研究的结果帮助建立了不同的模型（色适应变换及色貌模型），用来帮助颜色复制和表征，并在不同行业得到广泛使用，例如照明、显示、打印、印刷。但是这些应用都是针对物体表面色、自发光显示器和光源。 近几年来，增强现实AR逐步发展，这一技术让用户可以同时看到现实环境和投影在现实环境上的虚拟刺激。相比于虚拟现实VR，AR可以提供更为真实和沉浸式的视觉体验，因而不同的行业都致力于将AR技术应用到实际，例如照明设计师希望采用AR技术取代电脑显示器来更好地呈现设计方案。但是，因为由AR技术所产生的虚拟刺激既非反射式的物体表面色也非自发光的颜色刺激，过去的色貌模型与色适应变换模型都没有针对性的研究。最近的几项研究（包括本项目申请人的研究）和Facebook的研究都发现现行的色貌模型和色适应变换都不能用于AR技术。 本项目旨在通过心里物理实验针对由AR技术产生的虚拟刺激的颜色色貌。观察者在不同的观察环境下将完成一系列的颜色匹配实验和颜色刺激色貌属性的评价。其中真实的颜色刺激将通过实际物体和3D打印来产生；虚拟颜色刺激将通过AR眼镜来产生。在心里物理实验结果的基础上我们将通过数学建模来提出一个新的两步色适应变换模型及一个针对AR虚拟刺激的色貌模型。 本项目将对AR技术的发展和应用起到重要作用。它将帮助AR硬件和软件的开发商提供实现高品质AR技术渲染和复制的工具，以帮助推广AR技术在各个不同领域的应用。此外，它还将帮助我们更深入了解人类视觉系统对于颜色刺激的反应。

15206821.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15206821.value: 温度变化是大跨斜拉桥梁的一种主要荷载；同时桥梁也承受其它荷载，比如风荷载。为了研究不同荷载对桥梁的作用，需要将温度荷载与其它荷载分离。另外，温度变化也会引起结构响应的变化，后者常常被用来探测结构可能出现的损伤，因此，为了可靠地准确地探测桥梁的损伤，也必须考虑温度的变化。 尽管人们已经对桥梁的温度作用作了大量的实测和分析研究，常用方法只是建立桥梁的温度和响应之间的相关性，而定量分析大跨斜拉桥梁的温度作用还未见到，其主要难点在于：1、大跨斜拉桥梁包含一定数量的斜拉索并呈现高静不定特性，桥梁的不均匀温度变化会造成复杂的结构内力。2、桥梁的传感器数量总是有限的，传感器测量得到的温度很可能不是对桥梁最不利的温度分布，因而实测数据需要与有限元模拟结合在一起；但是，一般的热传导分析与桥梁受力分析是分开进行的，即将桥梁的各个构件（比如桥塔、桥面）分别简化为一个二维或三维有限元模型，然后分别进行热传导计算，各构件得到的温度场综合起来输入到结构的整体三维有限元模型中，从而计算桥梁结构在温度荷载作用下的响应。这种方法需要大量的人工干预，计算效率低；同时，桥梁各构件的温度分别不是均匀分布，采用局部的二维或三维有限元模型不能准确地描述整座桥梁的温度分布，造成计算结果不够准确。 本项目将通过现场监测和先进的数值计算方法高效地、准确地研究大跨斜拉桥的温度作用。我们将以港珠澳大桥的三座安装有健康监测系统的斜拉桥为例，开展如下方面的研究： 1. 建立详细的桥梁三维整体有限元模型，该模型包括桥塔、主梁和斜拉索等所有构件，该有限元模型可以进行热传导分析和结构力学分析并使用相同的网格划分。 2. 将实测的太阳辐射值和环境空气温度作为边界条件，对桥梁整体结构进行三维热传导分析，得到桥梁的温度分布。将现场实时监测的温度结果对模拟结果进行验证和微调。 3. 将得到的温度分布自动输入到桥梁的同一个整体有限元模型中进行结构力学分析，计算桥梁结构在温度荷载作用下的响应（比如位移和应变）。 4. 根据桥梁最大响应，建立桥梁最不利温度模型，并对桥梁设计中的温度荷载提出建议。 上述步骤可以实时连续地完成，长期监测的数据将用来不断更新桥梁的温度荷载模拟。因此，本项目将使得大跨斜拉桥的温度作用研究得越来越准确，并可以实现温度荷载与其它荷载的分离，为桥梁设计提供准确的温度荷载模型。

15206821.label: Realisation of objectives
15206821.value: 1) Objective 1: This study comprehensively and accurately investigates the global 3D temperature distribution of long-span cable-stayed bridges by integrating the heat-transfer analysis and field monitoring data. A navigation channel bridge (Qingzhou Bridge) of the Hong Kong‒Zhuhai‒Macao Bridge is used as the testbed. A global 3D refined finite element model of the entire bridge is established. The external thermal boundary conditions of the outer surfaces of the structure are carefully determined based on the real-time ambient temperature, wind, and solar radiation, which are tailored for each surface to reflect the influence of the geometric configuration. The internal thermal boundary conditions of the inner surfaces of the box girder and tower are dependent on the measured ambient temperature, considering the vertical temperature difference of the girder and the uniform temperature inside the tower. Then, the numerical heat-transfer analysis and field monitoring data are integrated to calculate the detailed temperature distribution of the entire bridge in different seasons. Results show that ambient temperature, wind, and solar radiation significantly affect the temperature distribution. For the girder, the vertical temperature difference is significant throughout the year, and the transverse temperature difference is nonnegligible in winter and summer, while the longitudinal temperature difference is trivial. The internal temperature of the tower remains stable owing to the insulation of the concrete. The temperatures of the cables vary from each other, which may cause stress redistribution within the structure. The calculated temperatures are in good agreement with their measured counterparts. 2) Objective 2: This study develops a unified approach to the investigation of thermal behaviors of cable-stayed bridges by integrating the heat-transfer analysis and structural analysis based on the same refined global 3D finite element model. This novel approach is more efficient than the conventional “divide-and-conquer” approach, that is, bridge components, such as the deck and towers, are separately modeled with a two-dimensional (2D) or local three-dimensional (3D) model by ignoring the temperature variation in the longitudinal direction of the component. With the new unified approach, the temperature distribution data obtained in the first Objective is automatically converted to thermal loads, and thermal elements are changed to structural elements to calculate the temperature-induced responses of the bridge. Results show that the effect of the temperature variation of cables is nonnegligible and should be taken into account during the structural analysis. The longitudinal displacement of the girder and the longitudinal displacement of the tower top are mainly influenced by the average girder temperature, the mid-span deflection and the cable stress are dominated by the cable temperature and average girder temperature, and the stress of the girder is controlled by the vertical temperature difference. The ratio of the thermal stress of the girder to the dead load can reach 96%. The calculated displacement and stress of the bridge agree well with the corresponding measurements, consequently verifying the effectiveness of the proposed unified approach to calculating temperature-induced responses. 3) Objective 3: To facilitate efficient and practical investigation of the temperature effect on long-span cable-stayed bridges, a series of simplified temperature load models have been developed by integrating the advantage of accuracy of a refined model with the immediacy of field monitoring data. The Qingzhou Bridge, one navigation channel bridge of the Hong Kong‒Zhuhai‒Macao Bridge, is taken as the testbed. The simplified temperature load models are categorized by bridge components and constituted by temperature characteristics, including average temperature and temperature differences. These temperature characteristics are linear combinations of field thermometer measurements, which are verified by the detailed temperature results of the refined model. The simplified temperature load models are then incorporated into a finite beam element model of the bridge to calculate temperature-induced responses. This approach has shown to be as effective as structural analysis using the refined model, with much less computational cost. This simplification strategy can be extended to other cable-stayed bridges.

15206821.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15206821.value: Temperature is a major load of long-span cable-stayed bridges. Most current studies focus on simple regression analyses of the relation between the temperature and bridge responses. Quantitative studies on temperature behavior of long-span cable-stayed bridges are limited. This study has investigated the temperature behavior of long-span cable-stayed bridges efficiently and accurately by integrating field monitoring data and advanced computational techniques. N particular, A unified framework for heat-transfer analysis and structural analysis has been developed to obtain the 3D global temperature distribution and temperature-induced responses of cable-stayed bridges efficiently and accurately. A simplified temperature load model is also developed. The developed framework and models are verified through applications to the cable-stayed bridges in the Hong Kong–Zhuhai–Macau Bridge, equipped with real-time structural monitoring systems. The project will lead to an accurate quantitative analysis of temperature behavior of long-span cable-stayed bridges and facilitate cost-effective maintenance strategies. The proposed technique can also be applied to high-rise buildings and other types of infrastructure.

15207221.value: 用於氣動噪聲抑制的緊湊型超材料吸波器的建模與設計

15207221.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15207221.value: 在低縱橫比的涵道風扇系統中衰減寬帶噪聲仍然是一項技術挑戰，例如國內產品中的換氣扇、吹風機和冷卻風扇。與笨重的傳統被動措施（例如管道襯裡）相比，已經努力開發具有緊湊幾何形狀的降噪裝置，但它們在低頻區域的噪聲性能通常受到窄帶的限制。為了加寬吸聲帶，提出了一組具有不同鋸齒形管結構的平行微穿孔板吸聲器陣列，每根管子在不同位置依次插入多個穿孔板，即在鋸齒形通道腔中插入穿孔板。這種為聲波傳播形成更長路徑的多結構背腔可以提供緊湊尺寸的消音功能。當多孔吸收器陣列安裝在管道內風扇附近時，氣流穿過微孔板或穿孔板的孔口。渦流在孔口的邊緣產生，導致孔口之間強烈的空氣動力學-聲學相互作用，包括共享相同淺背腔的孔口以及由不同幾何形狀的相鄰腔體背襯的孔口。在許多先前的研究中，在掠流下穿孔板表面的聲學行為的不均勻性已被忽略。這促使我們在開髮用於精確預測這種用於空氣動力噪聲抑制的元穿孔結構陣列的綜合模型方面向前邁進了一大步。該模型包括同一淺腔內和相鄰腔內排列的孔口之間的空氣動力學-聲學相互作用； 微穿孔面板、內部穿孔面板、背襯聲學腔、管道和外部空間中的聲場之間的振動聲耦合。該模型使我們能夠了解具有不同淺腔幾何形狀和平行排列的穿孔特性的多個諧振器孔口的空氣動力學-聲學相互作用背後的吸聲機制和物理學。將進行參數研究，以系統地評估關鍵設計參數的影響。這有助於設計適當數量和尺寸的微穿孔超材料陣列，在空腔內部具有不同的內部結構，以有效抑制管道風扇系統中的噪聲，尤其是在低頻下。其噪聲性能將在開腔和短風管中進行理論和實驗驗證。一個成功的結果將為設計用於風扇噪聲控制的寬帶超材料提供有用的信息，例如吹風機和空調系統。

15207421.value: To determine the composition of the reactive bromine species (RBS) in the effluents of coal burning; To elucidate the mechanism of photo-assisted production of RBS from coal burning; To investigate the spatial extent of the RBS and products of halogen chemistry, and their impact on radical production in heavily polluted northern China.
