15210321.label: Project Objectives
15210321.value: Evaluate the effects of individual loading waveforms on the fatigue endurance limits (FELs) and fatigue lives of asphalt mixtures of different aging states. Currently, continuous haversine or sinusoidal waveforms are commonly used in fatigue tests. Traffic load-induced waveforms in field asphalt pavements, however, exhibit compressive-tensile or multi compressive-tensile-compressive patterns different than laboratory ones (Please refer to attached Figure 1). Recently, our research team applied actual loading waveforms recorded from instrumented roads to laboratory fatigue tests. We found that different loading waveforms of the same peak strain lead to dramatically different fatigue lives (Please refer to attached Figure 2 and Figure 3), likely due to differences in induced micro damage and healing in the samples. This observation motivates us to systematically examine the effects of loading waveforms (haversine, actual waveforms corresponding to single, tandem, tridem axles) on FELs and fatigue lives with consideration of other factors such as mixture type, strain magnitude, aging state, temperature, rest period, and loading pulse time. Evaluate the effects of composite loading waveforms on the FELs and fatigue lives of asphalt mixtures of different aging states. Unlike objective 1, this research component will study the loading waveforms delivered by entire representative vehicles. For instance, a composite loading waveform may be generated by a vehicle with one single axle, one tandem axle, and one tridem axle. The use of composite loading waveforms has the advantages of realistic consideration of the rest periods of axle load groups within a vehicle and realistic consideration of the interactions of axle load groups within a vehicle. The research tasks are similar to those in Objective 1, except for composite waveforms being used. Validate and calibrate FELs and estimated fatigue lives from pavements of long service lives, including two major expressways in Hong Kong (one served for 36 years and another one will reach 39 years at the end of the study period) and others in the Long-Term Pavement Performance (LTPP) program in the United States. With detailed data available for mechanistic analysis, the two roads in Hong Kong can not only provide useful information to validate the laboratory-determined FELs and fatigue models but also serve as valuable cases for long-life pavement design in the world. The Principle Investigator (PI) was the first place winner of the LTPP data competition [1]. Rich and rigorously monitored LTPP data helps further validate the identified FELs based on actual loading waveforms. To synthesize the research findings and develop a FEL-based long-life pavement design method for Hong Kong. Currently, even though Hong Kong requests all highway pavements to be designed to reach “long life” (a minimum of 40 years of structural life). The design method is still mainly empirical, replying on estimated equivalent standard axles. The current design practice suffers from over-design or under-design problems. Based on the three objectives above, this research component will develop a simple yet reliable method for long-life pavement design in Hong Kong. The general design procedure may be also applied to other regions.

15210321.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15210321.value: The majority of the 2,000 kilometers of roads in Hong Kong (HK) are paved with flexible pavements. Due to adverse social and economic impacts of road closures, a long-life pavement design strategy has been adopted, aiming to make pavements survive over 40 years without structural failure. The key idea underpinning long-life flexible pavements is the endurance limits. If load-induced horizontal tensile strains at asphalt layer bottom are below a fatigue endurance limit (FEL) and vertical compressive strains at subgrade top are below a endurance limit for permanent deformation, bottom-up fatigue cracking and deep-layer rutting will not occur. An early proposed FEL for asphalt mixtures is 70 µε, but different values were suggested later. Analysis of highway pavements in HK reveals that a proportion of traffic-induced critical tensile strains exceed the proposed FELs even for very conservative designs (total asphalt layer thickness>500 mm). Conversely, a major expressway in HK (total asphalt layer thickness of 400 mm) with many critical tensile strains above the reported FELs has served for 35 years without any fatigue cracking. Therefore, it is necessary to find a proper FEL to guide long-life pavement design in HK. This proposed study is also motivated by two of our preliminary findings. We recently developed a procedure to use actual loading waveforms induced by traffic axles to perform fatigue tests on asphalt mixtures. Under a same controlled peak strain, different actual loading waveforms lead to dramatically different fatigue lives. In addition, same asphalt mixtures of different aging states exhibit different fatigue lives. We suspect that discrepancies in loading waveforms between laboratory tests and field pavements and the evolving ageing states of field pavements contribute to differences in laboratory-determined FELs and the true FEL in the field. This study aims to investigate these issues. We will use loading waveforms corresponding to both individual axle groups and multiple axle groups in heavy vehicles to perform fatigue tests on asphalt mixtures of different aging states. Other compounding factors will also be examined in the tests. FELs and fatigue life estimation curves will be determined from the tests and be validated and calibrated from two major expressways in HK and selected experimental sections in the Long-Term Pavement Performance program. A simplified procedure for long-life pavement design will also be developed for HK. This research is anticipated to advance our understanding of the fatigue behaviors of asphalt pavements and help build long-life pavements more reliably and economically. 香港 2,000 公里的道路中，大部分都鋪設了柔性路面。由於道路封閉對社會和經濟的不利影響， 香港已採用長壽命路面設計策略，旨在使路面能夠使用 40 多年而不會出現結構破壞。支撐長壽命柔性路面的關鍵思想是疲勞耐久極限。如果瀝青層底部由荷載引起的水平拉應變低於疲勞耐久極限（FEL），路基頂部的垂直壓應變低於永久變形的耐久極限，則不會發生自下而上的疲勞開裂和深層車轍破壞。 早期提議的瀝青混合料 FEL 為 70 με，但後來不同學者提出了不同的閾值。對香港公路路面的分析表明，即使對於非常保守的設計（總瀝青層厚度 > 500 毫米），交通荷載引起的臨界拉伸應變的比例也超過了提議的 FEL。相反，香港的一條主要高速公路（瀝青層總厚度為 400 毫米）的許多臨界拉伸應變高於所提議的 FEL。而且，這條道路已經服務了 35 年，並沒有出現任何疲勞開裂。因此，有必要找到一個合適的 FEL 來指導香港的長壽命路面設計。 這項擬議的研究也受到我們的兩個初步發現的啟發。我們最近開發了一個測試方法，使用由交通車軸引起的真實載荷波形對瀝青混合料進行疲勞測試。在相同的受控峰值應變下，不同的真實加載波形會導致明顯不同的疲勞壽命。此外，不同老化狀態的相同瀝青混合料也表現出不同的疲勞壽命。因此，我們懷疑實驗室測試和現場路面之間加載波形的差異以及現場路面不斷變化的老化狀態導致實驗室確定的 FEL 和現場真實 FEL 有明顯的差異。 本研究旨在調查這些問題。我們將使用重型車輛中單個軸組和多個軸組對應的加載波形對不同老化狀態的瀝青混合料進行疲勞試驗，並考慮其他影響因素。 FEL 和疲勞壽命估計曲線將根據測試確定，並在香港的兩條主要高速公路和美國長期路面性能計劃（LTPP）的選定試驗路段進行驗證和校準。該研究還將為香港開髮長壽命路面設計的簡化程序。預計這項研究將增進我們對瀝青路面疲勞行為的理解，並有助於更可靠、更經濟地建造長壽命路面。

15211221.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15211221.value: During the development of new drugs for cardiovascular or heart diseases, human/animal models established from their tissues are important for investigating effectiveness and safety of the drugs. Although mechanical stimuli methods like surface topography and cyclic straining can be used for enhancing cell alignment and elongation respectively, the force generation from artificial cardiac muscle tissue models without highly aligned cultured tissues are still substantially inferior to that of a real human heart. Restricted by conventional fabrication techniques, surface topography based cell training platforms without micro-and-nano-structured substrates is limited to 2D cell culture rather than 3D tissue culture. Moreover, the mechanisms behind cell alignment and elongation under cyclic straining, especially 3D tissue culture, are not clear yet. Hence, it is crucial to study hybrid effects of cyclic straining and micro-nano-structures for substantial tissue force enhancement scientifically. With expertise of the team, this is a pioneering attempt to develop a novel method combining nano-lithography, light responsive collagen modified biocompatible LCE nanocomposite, finite element (FE) structural analysis for designing and fabricating a light actuatable upconversion nanophosphors (UCNPs)/azobenzene-containing LCE nanocomposite based micro-nano-structured dynamic cell training platform for enhancing force generation capability of grown cardiac muscle tissues in 3D cell culture micro-environment. Based on a theoretical model of free energy change for cell-substrate interaction and FE structural analysis, a robust 3D platform structure with a series of micro-nano-structured LCE fibers and supporting architecture is designed. The cell and tissue alignments are achieved by guiding cell growth along each pair of micro-nano-structured LCE fibers, while 3D tissue formation is generated through interaction of micro-tissues (multiple layers of grown cells) between different layers of adjacent fibers. Moreover, under low power near-infrared light actuation at a controlled switching frequency, UCNPs incorporated in the azobenzene-containing LCE will be fully used to convert the supplied photon energy into green light for causing a trans-to-cis photoisomerization of the azobenzene units so as to induce photo-mechanical cyclic elongation/retraction of the UCNPs/LCE structure for enabling in-situ 3D cell training process. With preliminary experience in fabricating light actuatable LCE woodpile structure and two-photon polymerization (TPP) compatible nanocomposite photoresists, a facile and repeatable manufacturing scheme is devised for fabricating the precise micro-nano-structured platform via TPP and enabling grown tissue force measurement. The proposed work will unfold underlying mechanisms governing interaction between the cardiac muscle cells and 3D dynamic micro-nano-structured cell training platform for further development of highly aligned artificial cardiovascular models for heart disease research. 在開發治療心血管或心臟病的新藥期間，從其組織建立的人類/動物模型對於研究藥物的有效性和安全性是很重要的。雖然機械刺激方法如改變表面形態和循環應變可用於增強細胞排列和伸長，但沒有高度細胞對齊排列的人造心肌組織模型所產生的力仍遠不如真人心。受傳統製造技術的限制，基於沒有微納結構的訓練平台僅限於二維細胞培養而不是三維組織培養。此外，細胞排列背後的機制和循環應變下的伸長率，尤其是三維組織培養，尚不清楚。因此，研究循環應變和微納米結構的混合效應對顯著增強組織所產生的力至關重要。 憑藉團隊的專業知識，這是開發新方法的開創性嘗試， 結合納米光刻、光響應膠原改性生物相容性液晶彈性體及有限元結構分析， 設計和製造納米複合材料的光驅動上轉換納米磷光體/含偶氮苯液晶彈性體納米複合材料的微納米結構動態細胞訓練平台，從而增強在細胞培養微環境中生長的心肌組織所產生的力。基於細胞基質相互作用自由能變化的理論模型和有限元結構分析，將設計出一個強大的三維細胞訓練平台包含了一系列液晶彈性體微納米結構和支撐架構。 細胞和組織的排列是通過引導細胞沿著每一對微納米結構的液晶彈性體纖維的生長來實現的。而三維組織形成是通過不同層間微組織的相互作用。此外，在受控的低功率近紅外光驅動下，包含在偶氮苯液晶彈性體中的上轉換納米磷光體將完全用於提供光子能量以轉換為綠光，以引起偶氮苯單元的光異構化以誘導光機械循環 用於原位三維細胞訓練平台的伸長/收縮過程。具有製造輕型可驅動液晶彈性體木樁結構和雙光子聚合兼容的納米複合光刻膠的初步經驗， 將設計出一種簡單且可重複的雙光子聚合製造方案來精確建構微納米結構細胞訓練平台。 擬議的工作將揭示心肌細胞和三維動態微納結構細胞訓練平台之間相互作用的潛在機制，以用於進一步開發高度細胞排列的人工心血管模型的心臟疾病研究。

15211421.label: Project Objectives
15211421.value: The objective of this study is to examine the LWB strength and behaviour of coped beams under combined bending, shear, and axial loading. Both single- and double-coped beams will be included, and efficient retrofitting strategies for these beams will also be explored. The study will benefit both academia and industry by revealing the interaction mechanism at the coped region, and by developing a comprehensive set of design/retrofitting rules for newly built and existing coped beams subject to possible large axial forces. Specifically, the objectives of this research project will be accomplished by completing the following tasks: Task I Experimental investigation A series of full-scale tests will be conducted, with varied cope and beam geometries (e.g., d/tw, dc/D and c/D), axial load levels, and reinforcing strategies. In particular, the effects of both tensile and compressive axial forces on the strength and behaviour of the coped beam specimens will be revealed by the experimental program. The stress-strain behaviour of the materials used for the specimens will be determined by tension coupon testing. Task II Numerical investigation The finite element (FE) method will be employed to trace the nonlinear behaviour of coped beams under complex loading conditions. The FE models will be validated through comparisons with the test results, and subsequently, a parametric study will be carried out to explore the effects of a broadened range of parameters. The nonlinear FE analysis results will provide a better understanding of the structural behaviour of the test specimens and will facilitate the development of design recommendations. Task III Examination of current design practices and the development of design recommendations The current design methodology for evaluating the LWB resistance of coped beams, when there is no axial force, will be critically reviewed against the test and numerical results obtained during this proposed study. A unified practical design approach that takes account of different loading conditions will be developed, and efficient reinforcing/retrofitting strategies will be proposed.

15211421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15211421.value: In steel structures, spatial interference is often inevitable at locations where different members meet. A typical case is the connection between secondary beams (stringers) and primary beams (girders), where the same flange elevation is required of both types of member to cater for architectural and construction purposes. To ensure sufficient clearance, the secondary beams are usually coped at one or both flanges. The presence of the coped region leads to substantially compromised load carrying capacity. Local web buckling (LWB) is the most found failure mode for a coped beam. The LWB behaviour of coped beams has received significant attention over the past decades, and relevant studies have led to the current design set out in the Steel Construction Manual (AISC). However, the research and design approaches have mainly focused on the behaviour of coped beams subject to bending and shear loading only and the influence of axial force, or loading, has never been properly considered. The presence of a substantial axial force is not uncommon for coped beams in steel buildings and bridges, which are subjected to wind, thermal expansion, braking, other loads in service and even earthquakes. These factors can result in a pronounced interaction of bending, shear, and axial forces at the coped region, and hence rather more complex LWB behaviour. The PI has conducted extensive experimental, numerical, and analytical studies on coped beams with various geometric configurations. A recent preliminarily study has indeed indicated that the LWB capacity of steel coped beams is sensitive to an axial force, and the current design method can be unsafe under certain circumstances if this effect is neglected. The aim of this study, therefore, is to experimentally and analytically investigate the fundamental mechanisms and the appropriate design of coped beams subjected to combined bending, shear, and axial loading. Both single- and double-coped beams will be included, and retrofitting strategies for these beams will be explored if necessary. The study will finally lead to a comprehensive set of design/retrofitting rules for both newly built and existing coped beams which are subject to possible large levels of axial loading during their service life.

15212021.label: Project Objectives
15212021.value: To design and fabricate composite electrode fibers in different structures with triboelectric and electrochemical functionalities in an additive functionalization manner and characterize properties of the as-prepared composite electrode fibers. To integrate composite electrode fibers with triboelectric/electrochemical properties into triboelectric nanogenerator (TENG)-/electrochemical power storage (EC)-based self-powered electronic textiles (SPET) devices on textiles via additive embroidery, and then characterize the triboelectric/electrochemical performance and mechanical properties of the designed devices. To engineer the electrode architecture and device arrangement, study the underlying mechanisms and relationships between structural parameters and performance of SPET devices, optimize the fabrication technologies and system performance. To integrate TENG and EC devices with rational designs a piece of fabrics to form SPETs, and then evaluate the properties including self-powered sensing ability, energy harvesting storage capability, and wearability. Applications of the as-developed SPET prototypes coupled with circuit designs as an integrated system will be demonstrated in particular application scenarios for self-powered charging and tactile pressure sensing.

15212021.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15212021.value: 自供電型電子織物（SPET）是一類集能量收集、能源存儲和傳感等多種功能性器件於一體的電子紡織品，可為日常衣物和紡織產品提供不間斷且穩定的電源供應，同時具有持續監測身體信號和與環境互動的能力。這類新興的、具有電源集成的無線織物系統在人類活動學習、個性化醫療和人機交互等多個領域顯示了巨大的應用可能性。目前對於SPET的研究已經在提高器件性能等方面做了巨大的努力，但在平衡各器件元件的功能性、設計美學、可穿戴性及易生產性等方面仍然面臨著嚴峻的挑戰。將SPET無縫集成於日常衣物中仍較困難，在可穿戴場景應用中的因此受到一定的限制。所以，開發一種有效的策略來實現具有特定功能和型態的各類電子織物元件在SPET系統內的可擴展化製造和無縫集成，具有很重要的意義。 本項目旨在利用紡織技術進行功能纖維的連續性製備，然後基於增材製造的原理實現功能纖維和器件於織物中的無縫集成。首先，將提出一種增材功能化和刺繡製造（AFEM）的方法，適用於SPET器件和系統的製備和集成。然後基於項目申請人的前期研究，將設計和評估織物器件的結構，通過實驗和建模研究分析各種器件單元結構和器件性能之間的關係。通過研究分析提出一種基於AFEM方法開發SPET的通用的結構模型。最後作為應用展示，將開發和優化一套集成有摩擦納米發電機和電化學存儲器件的SPET系統，展示其於能量收集和存儲、壓力傳感的應用潛力。 本項目針對AFEM的研究將為SPET的設計、製造和集成提供可定制、易集成和易生產的製備新思路。由於AFEM原則上適用於各種電機材料，因為本項目的研究成果可以進一步擴展到其他功能性器件，以設計製備出具有更高集成度、更多功能的新型智能電子紡織系統，例如化學傳感、驅動、無線充電等等。從長遠來看，這將有助於增強電子織物在可穿戴電子產品和人工智能等方面的實際適用性。

15212021.label: Realisation of objectives
15212021.value: Throughout the execution of the project, research activities were conducted to achieve the proposed objectives, including fabrication and characterization of composite textile electrodes, integration into self-powered electronic textile devices (SPET), investigation of structural-performance relationship, and demonstration of proof-of-concept applications. 1. Design and fabrication of composite electrode fibers with different functionalities. In this research task, the design and fabrication of these fibers are based on an additive functionalization approach, where functional components are incorporated to achieve desired performance enhancements. We firstly fabricated composite electrode fibers using continuous electrospinning techniques. A conductive thread served as the core electrode, while the outer sheath was formed by electrospinning thermoplastic polymers (e.g., thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU), styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene (SEBS)). Functional fillers, such as barium titanate (BaTiO₃) dielectric nanoparticles, liquid metal conductive nanoparticles, and electrochemically active materials (e.g., carbon nanotubes (CNTs)), were incorporated to impact triboelectric, conductive, and/or electrochemical properties. Similar practices have been demonstrated in fabric-shaped fibrous composite electrodes. Structure-gradient fiber mats (SGFM) were developed via template-assisted, layer-by-layer electrospinning, mimicking human skin’s modulus transitions and rough morphology. By varying BaTiO₃ and CNTs concentrations in each layer, a vertical gradient in composition and microstructure was achieved. By using a metal mesh collector, an array of bumps on SGFM was formed to stimulate the surface ridges of human skin. Such a gradient design and bump structure impacted dielectric properties, compressibility, and sensitivity to pressure. SGFM exhibited excellent moisture permeability of 528 g/m2/day and air permeability of 74 mm/s, comparable to that of conventional textiles. Liquid metal (LM) nanoparticles were also additively incorporated, forming highly permeable fiber mats with well-dispersed LM conductive networks. LM-embedded fiber mats showed tensile stress of ~2 MPa with breaking stress of ~90%, high air permeability (up to 24 mm s⁻¹) and moisture permeability (up to 780 g m⁻² day⁻¹). These composite fibers provide a versatile platform for multifunctional textiles in wearable electronics. 2. Integration via additive embroidery and performance characterization. Additive embroidery technology, combining digital design and precise processing, can be used to integrate composite electrode fibers into textile-based triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) or power supply devices. This task mainly focused on the integration of fabric triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) based on additive embroidery technology. High-elastic double-sided Dralon fabric served as the substrate for device integration. Fiber electrodes were embroidered in various different shapes to form fabric electrodes, which power output performance were the investigated. Embroidery stitches regulated electrode surface microstructure, affecting effective contact area and triboelectric charge density. The results showed that the triboelectric charge density increases with the increase of the height difference of the electrodes, and this law is consistent with the variation trend of the effective contact area. The design of the electrode structure also plays a crucial role in determining both the electrical output and the comfort of the triboelectric devices. Thus, electrode design involves a trade-off between electrical performance and comfort, tailored to application needs. One undergraduate student contributed to the systematic study on how stitch type and density affect electrode conductivity, mechanical strength, and air/moisture permeability, providing valuable data for optimizing wearable device performance. 3. Engineer electrode architecture and device arrangement. This task systematically investigated the mechanisms and relationships between structural parameters and the SPET device performance, focusing on electrode architecture and device arrangement. Theoretical modelling and experimental validation were combined to optimize fabrication technologies and system performance. High dielectric permittivity and low dielectric loss were found to enhance SPET sensitivity to pressure. Finite element simulations showed that materials with low Young’s modulus are easily compressed, improving sensing capability, while gradient transitions in mechanical properties allow appropriate strain changes across a wide pressure range. Experimental results demonstrated that electrode arrangement and SGFM structure significantly influence triboelectric output and sensing performance. Optimizing CNT concentration and film thickness balanced compressibility and robustness, with optimal SGFM thickness (300 μm) yielding the highest electrical output. SGFM-based SPET devices achieved sensitivity of 0.068 kPa⁻¹ (0–53 kPa), 0.013 kPa⁻¹ (53–660 kPa), and a broad sensing range up to 660 kPa, outperforming homogeneous fiber mats and other triboelectric textiles. Devices exhibited excellent moisture and air permeability, mechanical stability under cyclic compression, and durability after repeated washing and abrasion. This task also proposed an asymmetrical bending strategy for efficient characterization of cracking behavior in thin-film coatings on flexible substrates, applicable to evaluating mechanical and electrical stability of conductive electrodes. 4. System-level integration and application demonstration Electrode and device integrations were rationally designed into single fabric pieces to form SPETs, further advanced by combining with waterproof fabrics and wearable clothing formats. The all-fiber configuration of conductive and dielectric layers ensured outstanding air and moisture permeability. System-level integration of TENG-based SPETs with circuit modules enabled practical applications. SGFM-based triboelectric textiles were evaluated for self-powered sensing ability, wearability, and incorporated into a functional rehabilitation monitoring system for real-time physiological signal monitoring (pulse, muscle contraction, plantar pressure) without external power sources. This task also demonstrated the feasibility and advantages of combining TENG and energy management modules for wearable, comfortable, fully integrated self-powered systems in healthcare and motion monitoring. A fully integrated system was realized by coupling the TENG-based SPET with an energy management module and power storage components. The permeable TENG, constructed from a liquid-metal nanoparticle-embedded PVDF-TrFE fiber mat, achieved a high voltage output exceeding 35 V cm⁻² and a peak power of 2.8 mW. Paired with a specially designed energy management module, the system efficiently harvested biomechanical energy from human motion, rapidly charged a 0.68 mF storage capacitor to 3.1 V in 300 s (ten-fold faster than conventional rectifier designs), and provided a stable DC output suitable for powering wearable electronics. As a proof-of-concept, a smart garment was developed integrating the pTENG, energy management module, temperature sensor, and wireless transmitter, forming a self-powered wireless temperature sensing system. This system enabled real-time wireless health monitoring and data transmission, with sufficient energy (4.45 mJ per cycle, ≈22.5 mW power consumption) to support continuous sensing and transmission without reliance on external batteries. Expense Management Approximately 11% of the project funding remained unspent, primarily due to reduced opportunities to hire undergraduate assistants (COVID-19 impact), lower-than-expected equipment maintenance costs, and resource optimization in consumables procurement. The underspending resulted from prudent and responsible financial management, not shortcomings in project execution. All major objectives and milestones were achieved, and research quality was maintained throughout. Undergraduate student involvement In this research task, one undergraduate student was involved in investigating how different embroidery stitch types and stitch densities affect the properties of textile electrodes. Her work focused on systematically studying the impact of embroidery parameters on electrode conductivity, mechanical strength, and air/moisture permeability. By assisting in the design and fabrication of embroidered electrodes, the students contributed valuable data and insights into how stitch patterns and densities can be optimized to balance electrical performance with durability and comfort in wearable applications. Such participation not only supported the experimental progress of the project, but also provided them with hands-on research experience in advanced textile engineering and functional material characterization.

15212021.label: Major findings and research outcome
15212021.value: This project successfully developed a new class of composite electrode fibers and fibrous matrix through additive functionalization manners, enabling the integration of various electronic functionalities within highly permeable fibrous structures. By incorporating functional fillers such as BaTiO₃ nanoparticles, CNTs, and liquid metal nanoparticles, the fibers achieved enhanced dielectric, conductive, and electrochemical properties while maintaining textile-like breathability and mechanical robustness. Notably, the structure-gradient fiber mats (SGFM) mimicked human skin’s modulus transitions and surface morphology, resulting in improved compressibility, sensitivity, and excellent air/moisture permeability comparable to conventional textiles. Additive embroidery technology was then explored to precisely integrate electronic fibers into textile-based triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) and self-powered electronic textile (SPET) devices. Systematic studies revealed that embroidery stitch type and density significantly affect electrode conductivity, mechanical strength, and breathability. The choice of electrode structure and working modes allowed for balancing electrical output and wearing comfort, tailored to specific wearable scenarios. Theoretical modeling and experimental validation established the relationships between structural parameters and device performance. For example, optimized SGFM-based SPETs demonstrated high sensitivity (0.068 kPa⁻¹ in 0–53 kPa), broad sensing range (up to 660 kPa), and outstanding durability, outperforming homogeneous fiber mats and other triboelectric textiles. The devices maintained excellent performance after repeated washing and abrasion, confirming their robustness for wearable use. The research also achieved system-level integration by coupling TENG-based SPETs with energy management modules and storage components. Permeable TENG enabled efficient biomechanical energy harvesting, rapid capacitor charging, and stable DC output for powering wearable electronics. Proof-of-concept smart garments were demonstrated, integrating TENG-based SPETs, energy management, sensors, and wireless transmission for real-time, self-powered health monitoring and rehabilitation applications. This work establishes a versatile platform for next-generation smart textiles in healthcare, rehabilitation, and wearable electronics. Based on the research outcomes, a total of 8 related papers have been published, covering topics ranging from electrode fabrication to system integration. During the project period, one PhD student was trained and three conference presentations were delivered.

15212021.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15212021.value: The research outcomes have laid a strong foundation for the advancement of multifunctional self-powered textile electronics. Future development can be focused on exploring and integrating additional functionalities, particularly in tactile sensing and energy storage. Efforts will be directed toward enhancing the precision and sensitivity of tactile sensing, enabling more accurate detection of pressure, touch, and movement for advanced healthcare and human–machine interface applications. This can be achieved by leveraging the high spatial resolution provided by embroidery techniques, as well as the intrinsic multifunctionality of the composite fibers themselves. In parallel, improvements in energy storage capacity and power management will be pursued to support longer operation times and higher power demands for wearable devices. Further studies on long-term wearability, washability, and biocompatibility will ensure suitability for daily use. Collaboration with industrial partners will facilitate real-world validation and accelerate the translation of these innovations into practical products. Overall, the proposed course of action aims to deliver scalable, customizable, and high-performance smart textile solutions for personalized healthcare, rehabilitation, and next-generation wearable electronics.

15212021.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15212021.value: This project developed a new generation of self-powered electronic textiles that can sense, harvest, and store energy while maintaining the breathability and comfort of traditional fabrics. By incorporating advanced functional materials such as nanoparticles and liquid metals into fibers or fibrous matrix through additive functionalization techniques, these textiles are capable of generating electricity from movement. Especially, inspired by the structure of human skin, the resulting materials are both highly sensitive and durable, retaining their performance even after repeated washing and use. Precision embroidery methods were used to integrate electronic fibers into fabrics, enabling the creation of wearable devices tailored for various sensing and energy harvesting applications. The research demonstrated that the stitching pattern and density significantly influence the performance and comfort of these smart textiles. Fully integrated wearable systems were also developed, including smart garments that can monitor health signals (e.g., pulses, plantar pressure detection, rehabilitation postures) and transmit data wirelessly, powered solely by energy harvested from the wearer’s own movements. This work paves the way for next-generation smart clothing with practical applications in healthcare, rehabilitation, and daily life, making wearable technology more accessible, reliable, and user-friendly.

15212421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15212421.value: The most economically vibrant and densely populated large city clusters are usually connected to the marine environments, such as the Bohai Bay (BHB) in North China, Hangzhou bay (HZB) in East China and Pearl River Estuary (PRE) in South China. As important ecotones between mainland cities and marine environments, the three bays not only encounter polluted plumes from mainland cities with offshore winds, but also receive aged air masses recirculated from ocean by onshore winds, often resulting in severe secondary air pollution over the bay areas, which in turn affects the air quality in coastal cities and downwind areas. Although many studies on ozone (O3) pollution have been carried out in mainland cities adjacent to the bays, a dearth of studies focus on these bay areas, where the complete atmospheric processes especially the photochemical processes, are still unknown. To understand the atmospheric dynamics and chemistry that cause O3 pollution over these three bays and their adjacent areas, for the first time a comprehensive chemical database will be collected and an elaborate analysis of the data with both interpretative and numerical tools will be performed. Combining extensive observation data with computer modeling, this project aims to provide a thorough assessment of the major chemical processes responsible for photochemical O3 formation and the impact of speciated volatile organic compounds (VOCs) on O3 and other photochemical oxidant’s formation in each bay, interpret the influences of synoptic winds and mesoscale circulations on O3 pollution over the three bays and downwind and surrounding areas, and explore the interaction of O3 pollution among the three bays and summarize the relevance and uniqueness of O3 pollution over the three bays. The study results will have direct policy implications for reducing O3 pollution in the bay areas of China. The scientific findings will also contribute to our overall knowledge of the O3 science and have practical implications for other similar ecotones around the world. 經濟最活躍、人口最稠密的大城市群通常與海洋環境相連，例如華北的渤海灣、華東的杭州灣和華南的珠江口。三個海灣作為大陸城市與海洋環境之間的重要交錯帶，不僅遭遇內陸城市的污染氣團，還收到從海洋中回流的老化氣團，往往造成灣區二次空氣嚴重污染，這反過來又會影響沿海城市和下風向地區的空氣質量。儘管在毗鄰海灣的內陸城市開展了許多關於臭氧 (O3) 污染的研究，但缺乏關注這些灣區，其中完整的大氣過程，特別是光化學過程，仍然未知。為了了解導致這三個海灣及其鄰近地區 O3 污染的大氣動力學和化學，本项目將首次收集完善的化學數據，並使用解釋性和數值性工具對數據進行詳細分析。結合大量觀測數據以及模型模拟，該項目旨在全面評估負責光化學 O3 形成的主要化學過程以及特定揮發性有機化合物 (VOC) 對每個海灣中 O3 和其他光化學氧化劑形成的影響，解釋這些天氣風和中尺度環流對三灣及下風向及周邊地區O3污染的影響，探討三灣之間O3污染的相互作用，總結三灣O3污染的相關性和獨特性。研究結果將對減少中國灣區的 O3 污染產生直接的政策影響。科學發現還將有助於我們全面了解 O3 科學，並對世界上其他類似的交錯帶具有實際意義。

15212721.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15212721.value: Robot thermal servoing is currently an open problem in robotics that deals with the automatic regulation of the temperature profile of a surface through active motions of a robot. This advanced feedback control capability is needed to improve the performance in many economically-important applications, e.g. by servo-positioning heaters in a heat treatment process or by evenly distributing heat in robotic skin rejuvenation. Despite its practical benefits, state-of-the-art methods typically address this problem in an open-loop fashion (i.e. with no thermal feedback) and with static source-surface configurations (i.e. no robot controls). The main complication to the development of these types of methods lies in the lack of appropriate thermal-motor models for robotic systems that can facilitate the controller design; Yet, this approach has not been sufficiently studied in the literature. Capitalising on our previous work on sensor-based control, this new project sets the objective of establishing a complete, formal and general methodology that enables to conduct thermals servoing tasks with robots. Our proposed idea is to exploit the geometric-thermal-motor relations between the heat source and the surface for automatically planning and computing motion controls; The originality of the method lies in its capability to compute these relations in real-time, thus, improving its implementability in practical situations. The outcome of this project is expected to guide the modelling and synthesis of a new class of feedback controls. The addressed problem is fundamental in nature with clear practical applications, therefore, it has significant value to advance the state-of-the-art in robotics. 機器人熱伺服是機器人領域一個新的開放性問題，它通過機器人的主動運動來實現物體表面溫度分佈的自動調節。許多具有重要經濟價值的應用都需要這種先進的反饋控制以實現均勻加熱，例如在工業熱處理中實時反饋控制多個加熱器的位置，或在機器人光子嫩膚中實時規劃末端執行器的運動。針對這些實際應用，現有的解決方案通常是開環控制（即沒有熱反饋），熱源和目標表面的相對位置也是固定的（即沒有機器人控制）。開發機器人熱伺服控制器的主要難點在於目前並沒有適用於機器人系統的 “熱-關節運動模型”；這個問題在現有文獻中還未得到充分的研究。 基於我們之前在傳感器反饋控制方面的工作，這個新項目的目標是建立一個完整、正式和通用的方法，使機器人能夠執行各種熱伺服任務。我們提出利用熱源和目標表面之間的“幾何-熱-關節運動”關係進行規劃和計算控制；該方法的獨創性在於能夠實時計算這些關係，從而提高其實用性和魯棒性。該項目的成果有望為一種新型反饋控制提供建模與設計指導。我們所解決的問題具有明確的應用基礎，這對於推進機器人技術的最新發展具有重要價值。

15212721.label: Realisation of objectives
15212721.value: Objective 1: Radiation-Based Thermal Control We developed a comprehensive methodology for robots to perform radiation-based thermal control tasks using two distinct approaches. In our first approach, we created an innovative system that precisely controls heat transfer between a static radiation source and a robot-controlled object. This system uses surface-mounted temperature sensors to provide continuous feedback, enabling accurate servo-control of the heat transfer process. Our second approach represents a significant advancement in solar energy manipulation, where we developed a system using specialized lenses to concentrate and direct solar energy onto specific surface areas. This system employs thermal cameras for real-time feedback, enabling automated Heliography - a process that creates precisely controlled burn patterns using concentrated sunlight. Both approaches demonstrate novel ways to achieve accurate thermal control in robotic applications. Objective 2: Diffusion-Based Thermal Control We developed sophisticated laser-tissue simulations and predictive control strategies to regulate surface temperatures of skin tissue using pulsing heat sources. Our innovative method carefully accounts for how thermal energy from lasers accumulates and diffuses through various types of skin tissue at different rates, depending on specific bio-mechanical properties. This understanding enabled us to develop advanced thermal control methodologies that generate optimal irradiation plans, creating precise spatio-temporal thermal patterns across the skin surface. The system continuously adjusts its parameters based on real-time tissue response, ensuring safe and effective treatment delivery. Objective 3: Implementation Technologies We developed several cutting-edge technologies to implement our control theory. Our real-time thermal mapping system represents a significant advancement, combining infrared measurements with three-dimensional surface data to create accurate thermal profiles of complex surfaces. We also created sophisticated algorithms that enable optimal coverage of irregular surfaces by moving heat sources, ensuring uniform and precise heat application. Furthermore, we implemented advanced motion planning systems that maintain safe operating distances from heat sources while performing complex thermal tasks. These systems work together seamlessly to ensure precise thermal control while maintaining safety parameters. Objective 4: Experimental Validation We conducted extensive experimental validation of our theories using a wide range of sophisticated apparatus. For radiation-based thermal control, we employed robot manipulators equipped with high-precision thermistors, mobile Fresnel lenses for solar energy concentration, and mobile robots guided by advanced top-view camera systems. Our diffusion-based methods underwent rigorous testing using robotic systems that precisely controlled pulsing lasers over skin tissues, with temperature monitoring provided by state-of-the-art 3D infrared camera systems. The effectiveness and safety of our laser-based methods were thoroughly validated through comprehensive experimental studies involving human subjects and tissues, demonstrating the practical applicability of our theoretical frameworks in real-world scenarios.

15212721.label: Major findings and research outcome
15212721.value: We can classify the major findings and outcomes of this project into two categories: (1) Formalising Thermal Servoing, and (2) Systems and Technologies for Thermal Control. 1. Thermal Servoing Formulation. Before we started this research project, the robotics research community didn't have control theoretic formulation to model, analyse, plan, and perform automatic thermal control tasks with robotic systems. Through our investigations, we have produced a series of original papers that have formalised this challenging problem from a robotics research perspective. In contrast with traditional ad-hoc approaches, our new methodology enables to achieve complex thermal profiles in a variety of setups and systems, such as closed-loop thermal servo-control by radiative sources, infrared-based robotic Heliography, thermal stimulation of skin tissues, safe robot navigation in thermal environments, etc (refer to Part C, journal papers [1], [2], [7], [8], [10]). 2. Systems and Technologies for Thermal Control. This project has led to various important contributions in thermal servoing, including: systems design, planning algorithms, sensing technologies, and novel experimental systems. Our results have demonstrated how multimodal sensing (RGB-D + thermal) can be integrated with robotically controlled heat sources to, e.g., automatically concentrate solar energy onto surfaces, automate thermal dose delivery in skin rejuvenation, and perform robotic welding/scanning tasks (see [1], [2], [5], [9], [11]). The project also led the development of other related thermal planning, sensing, and control technologies for robotic systems (see e.g., [3], [4], [6], [7]). This project has enabled us to extensively publish in the best journals in robotics, automation, and sensing: - 11 published journal papers (11 Q1 papers) - 3 conference papers

15212721.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15212721.value: Our future research will focus on controlling multiple heat sources simultaneously during thermal procedures. This advancement would expand the system's capabilities, allowing us to generate more complex thermal patterns that are otherwise difficult to achieve with a single heat source. Such capability would significantly improve temperature-critical applications in fields like dermatology and advanced manufacturing. We also plan to extend our research from 2D surface heating to 3D volumetric thermal control. This advancement is crucial for processes like soft tissue ablation, where precise thermal control throughout a three-dimensional volume is required, rather than just on the surface. Additionally, we aim to incorporate data-driven approaches and machine learning methods, which weren't extensively explored in this project. These modern techniques could enhance our simulation and control capabilities, leading to more efficient and accurate thermal control systems.

15212721.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15212721.value: We developed an innovative methodology for robots to automatically control heat application on different surfaces. Our research created solutions to regulate heat transfer from radiation sources (like the sun or hot bodies) onto target surfaces, using temperature feedback for automatic control. We built a robotic system that precisely concentrates sunlight through special lenses to create specific burn patterns. Additionally, we developed techniques for robots to control pulsing lasers on surfaces like human skin, considering how heat spreads through different materials to create complex thermal stimulation plans. Our work included creating real-time thermal mapping systems and safety algorithms for moving heat sources. We validated our research through extensive testing with various setups: robot arms equipped with temperature sensors, mobile sun-focusing lenses, and laser systems, including clinical trials with human subjects. This pioneering research established the first formal framework for robotic thermal control, enabling applications in manufacturing, medical treatments, and solar energy.

15213621.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15213621.value: Continuum robots have been developing at an enormous speed owing to its advantages of large design freedom with easy implementation. Together with high flexibility and soft interaction, their applications have been extended from delicate tasks in operating rooms, to general tasks in industry and household. Although various robot prototypes have been developed, several challenges have yet been resolved. For instance, their performance on executing force-related tasks are not considered nor optimized. The soft body does not equip with any sensor for force measurement. Also, the motion induced through body deformation can lead to simultaneous change in the position and the orientation at the end-effector. In view of this, we propose an innovative soft robot design with a parallel mechanism to facilitate precise control at the end-effector through visual images. In order to carry out the proposed research, three important research issues will be addressed. First, we will design a continuum robot with the capability to decouple the motions of the end-effector. Based on the requirements from the task, the orientation of the parallel platform with the end-effector will be adjusted through relative motions between the actuators. New constraints will be introduced within the deformable body so that the orientation variations on the end-effector can be minimized while adjusting the body to reach different points along the surface of the task. Second, we will develop the mechanism to estimate the contact force using multi-view images, which can overcome the problem of occlusion. Augmented Reality markers will be added to the end-effector and monitored at different views. A ConvLSTM network will be constructed to estimate the local contact force based on the spatial and temporal changes on different markers, and the force vectors be fused to evaluate the global contact force. Third, we will develop the control algorithms to facilitate accurate end-effector manipulation. Camera images will be used to reconstruct into 3D surface, and 3D point cloud will be analyzed to generate the trajectory on a contourless surface. An impedance control method will be employed to guarantee a contact between the end-effector and the surface, and the position as well as the interaction force will be regulated to reach their desired values. Experiments will be conducted to examine the robot in performing different force-related tasks. Our proposed research will offer a new approach for a soft robot to execute the task precisely, providing new insights into innovative soft robots for various applications. 連續體機器人由於自由度大、易於實施等優點，一直以驚人的速度發展。連同高靈活性和柔軟接觸，它們的應用已經從手術室的精細任務擴展到工業和家庭中的一般任務。儘管各種機器人原型已經開發，但還有一些挑戰尚未解決。例如，它們在執行與力相關的任務時的性能沒有被考慮或優化。機器人自體不配備任何用於測力的傳感器。此外，機器人身體通過變形引起的動作執行導致末端的位置和方向同時發生變化。有鑑於此，我們提出了一種具有並聯機構的創新連續體機器人設計，以通過視覺圖像促進末端的精確控制。為了開展擬議的研究，將解決三個重要的研究問題。 首先，我們將設計一個能夠分開末端運動的連續體機器人。根據任務要求，通過執行器之間互相協調來調整末端所需的方向。將引入新的約束，以便在調整連續體機器人以到達任務表面的不同位置時，可大限度地減少末端執行器上的角度變化。 其次，我們將開發使用多視圖圖像作接觸力估計，這可以克服遮擋問題。擴增實境標記將被添加到末端並在不同的視圖中進行監控。將構建 ConvLSTM 網絡以根據不同標記的空間和時間變化來估計不同位置所受的接觸力，並融合力向量以評估真正接觸力。 第三，我們將開發控制算法以促進精確的末端操作。將使用相機圖像重建為 3D 表面，並分析 3D 點雲以在無輪廓表面上生成軌跡。將採用阻抗控制方法來保證末端執行器和表面之間的接觸，並且將調節位置以保證接觸力達到所需的值。實驗將會進行以檢查機器人執行不同的與力相關的任務。 我們的研究為連續體機器人提供一種新方法作精確任務執行，將機器人應用在不同的領域。

15214221.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15214221.value: Autonomous ships have evolved rapidly in recent years as a result of the advancement of artificial intelligence technologies. Because the advent of autonomous ships will change traffic activities, especially in the busiest ports, we should consider how to manage autonomous ship traffic in the presence of manned ship traffic. Although many studies have investigated autonomous shipping, integrated approaches examining port traffic remain largely unexplored. The key questions for autonomous ships in a port are associated with the interaction of autonomous ship traffic with manned ship traffic (i.e., driven/controlled by on-board personnel). If autonomous ships become a major traffic in ports, they must be able to account for various behaviours and patterns of movements of manned ships. Here, we propose an integrated system for modelling autonomous and manned ship behaviours with particular respect to the fact that heterogeneous decision-making processes co-exist in one system. Firstly, the proposed research project investigates the background marine traffic inside a port through an automatic identification system (AIS) survey and on-site observations. Behaviour-based indicators are observed during this initial stage in order to predict the human navigation behaviours. Secondly, we propose to develop a multiple-criteria decision-making model to study the mutual impacts of the heterogeneous traffic. Fuzziness will be used to handle potentially inaccurate information, while selfish and cooperative traffic also have various behaviours. Thirdly, risk-based analysis will enable port safety to be enhanced by accounting for the heterogeneous traffic. The interaction between heterogeneous traffic can be described using the game model. The project will establish a knowledge bridge between marine traffic science and future maritime policies. In addition, it will strengthen cooperation with other maritime research groups that are leading international efforts in autonomous ship traffic-based monitoring in ports. Autonomous ships will inevitably lead to a major paradigm shift in relation to port traffic. In order to fully ensure the safety and efficiency of autonomous ships, we need to know how autonomous and manned ships best navigate together. 近年來，隨著人工智能技術的進步，智能船舶迅速的發展，將影響到海上的交通活動。特別是在繁忙的港口，我們應該考慮如何在現有船舶航行的情況下，做好管理智能船舶航行。儘管有許多研究探討智能船舶的航行，但顯少有相關的研究從整合的觀點來分析港口的交通。智能船舶在港口內最主要的的問題是在於會與現有有人駕駛的船舶產生干擾，如果智能船舶未來成為港口主要的交通，更必須要瞭解各種等級智能船舶的行為與航行模式。在這裡，我們提出了一個整體的系統，用於對智能和有人駕駛船舶的行為進行模型預測，特別是考慮到混合決策過程共存於一個單一系統。首先，本研究項目通過自動識別系統調查和現場觀察來調查港口內的背景海上交通。此初始階段在於建立舶舶航行行為的指標，以預測船舶航行行為。其次，我們將發展一個多評準決策模型來研究混合交通的相互影響，模糊性的處理潛在的不準確信息與不同混合船舶的行為。第三，應用風險的分析與考慮混合交通模式來增強港口安全，應用博弈模型來描述混合船舶之間的交互行為，本研究項目將在海上交通科學與未來海事政策之間提供重要理論的基礎。此外，本研究項目將與其他海事研究小組的合作，這些研究小組在港口智能船舶交通監測方面處於國際領先地位。當智能船舶將不可避免地會導致港口交通主要範式的轉變，為了充分確保智能船舶的安全和效率，我們需要了解智能船舶與現有有人駕駛船舶共同航行的最好方式。

15214221.label: Major findings and research outcome
15214221.value: This project represents one of the pioneering efforts to model the behaviour of manned ships in addressing marine traffic problems. Leveraging the recent advancements in the Automatic Identification System (AIS), a substantial volume of marine traffic data has been collected and analyzed. Ship navigation behaviours have been systematically quantified using AIS data, focusing on key variables such as relative distance, relative velocity, and relative bearing (angle). These quantified behaviours have been incorporated into a Multi-Criteria Decision-Making (MCDM) model to better understand and predict ship interactions (Zhao, Yip, Wu, Lyu, 2022; Zhao, Wu, Yip, Lyu, 2023). A general decision-making model for ship operators has been developed, enabling the prediction of ship interactions under heterogeneous navigation behaviours (Zhao, Wu, Yip, Lu, Li, 2024). This model provides a robust framework for understanding the complex dynamics of marine traffic involving diverse vessel types and navigational strategies. The MCDM model has been further enhanced through the integration of game theoretic approaches, explicitly considering heterogeneous ship operators. This advancement contributes to the theoretical analysis of ship interactions and enables the prediction of multi-ship encounters based on varying ship particulars and behavioural patterns (Li, Yip, Zhao, Li, 2024; Zhao, Li, Yip, Wu, 2025). The marine traffic flow model has been applied as a hypothetical framework to investigate various real-world scenarios associated with marine traffic. A collision-risk-assessment system has been proposed for port environments where collision risk is elevated (Zhao, Li, Yip, Wu, 2025). Additionally, the project addresses the associated problem of ship fuel selection (Zhao, Yip, Li, Zhu, 2024; Zhao, Yip, Yang, Lu, 2025). Numerical experiments utilizing actual AIS data have been conducted to assess collision risks in marine traffic. As a result of this project, five journal papers have been produced, with two already published and three currently under review. The research findings have been disseminated at two international conferences, and two PhD students are being trained as part of the project. These outcomes collectively advance the theoretical and practical understanding of marine traffic behaviour, providing valuable tools for vessel traffic management and risk assessment in complex maritime environments.

15214221.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15214221.value: This research can be further developed in several impactful ways. Integrating real-time data with artificial intelligence (AI) will enable adaptive models for dynamic traffic prediction and risk assessment. The models can also be extended to include intelligent vessels, ensuring safe interactions in increasingly intelligent waterways. Future work should focus on creating user-friendly decision support tools for ship operators and port authorities, offering real-time collision warnings and optimal routing based on predictive behavioral analytics. Linking traffic models with ship behavioral data will support safer navigation and regulatory compliance. To maximize impact, trail implementations should be conducted in collaboration with ports and maritime authorities, with feedback used to refine the Vessel Traffic Control (VTC) systems. Partnerships with technology providers can help integrate these models into existing Vessel Traffic Control (VTC) platforms. Training programmes for maritime professionals and students will promote adoption and best practices. Securing additional funding will support large-scale trials and continuous model improvement, using real-world data to enhance accuracy. International collaboration can help standardize these tools, facilitating global adoption and improving maritime safety, efficiency, and sustainability.

15214221.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15214221.value: This project is one of the first to study how manned ships behave and interact in busy marine traffic, using new technology that tracks ships’ movements. We now have a large amount of real-world data about where encountering ships interact one another. Using these findings, we have developed game theoretic models to help predict how ships will interact, especially when they have different ship particulars. We have also used advanced Multi-Criteria Decision-Making tools to better understand situations where many ships are encountering, which helps us see how risks like collisions might develop. Our models have been tested with real data to study the risk of ship collisions in busy ports, and we have proposed new systems to help control ship traffic in these high-risk areas. Our research has led to several scientific papers and has been shared at international conferences. Two PhD students are also being trained as part of this work. Overall, our project helps make ship traffic safer and more efficient by using real data and new modeling techniques.

15214621.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15214621.value: The dyeing of cotton fibers with reactive dye in reverse micelles uses extremely low amounts of water and is promisingly environmentally friendly. This proposed dyeing process should strongly reduce the effluent treatment time and materials loading. However, the dyeing thermodynamics, mechanisms and adsorption phenomenon, in nanoscale, of the reverse micellar dyeing system has not yet been explored. Therefore, this project will explore the effect of different dyeing parameters of such a system in cotton fiber in order to better understanding the reverse micellar dyeing system. Nonionic surfactant is essential for assembling the micelles while organic solvent is used as a dyeing medium in reverse micellar dyeing system. However, petroleum-derived products of nonionic surface and solvent have negative effects on the environment and health effects to human beings. Thus, in this project, reverse micellar dyeing system will be developed using a “green” solvent, such as decamethylcyclopentasiloxane (D5), as the dyeing medium and a bio-degradable saccharide-based surfactant (alkyl glycosides) for assembling the reverse micelles. Reactive dyes with planar and non-planar molecular structure will be used for studying their interaction with cotton fiber surfaces during reverse micellar dyeing in order to elucidate the fixation mechanism. AFM phase imaging will be used to identify the dye aggregation behavior under the effect of various reverse micellar parameters on single cotton fiber surfaces. Surface chemical analysis with X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) will provide data on how single dye molecules interacts with the hydrophilic surface of cotton fiber and determine how the stability of reverse micelle influences the dye adsorption mechanism at the surface of cotton fiber. The XPS data will also provide strong evidence for possible dye-uptake mechanisms at molecular or atomic level. Using the absorbance data from UV-visible spectroscopy, the level of chemisorbed and physiosorbed dyes could be directly attributed after dyeing. We will observe how reverse micellar dyeing parameters influencing the reactive dye-cellulose interaction in both chemisorbed and physiosorbed states. The results obtained from these studies will help to select suitable reactive dye structures for quality maintenance with minimum hydrolysis and the factors affects the dyeing process for cotton fiber. After completion of this project, the outcomes could benefit the coloration industry, and society, by offering a highly-effective green dyeing process of cotton fiber. 15215421.label: Project Objectives
15215421.value: [Theory] Objective 1 - The underlying rationale behind the substitutability is the fundamental problem of sparse arrays. Answering this question facilitates to design more reasonable sparse arrays. So, our first objective is to study the rationality of sparse antenna arrays. Previous works studied this problem from the perspective of multi-antenna coverage. Instead, we present comprehensive theoretical analysis in the resolution redundancy of an antenna array and point out that an array essentially is a multi-resolution AoA estimator full of redundancy. To the best of our knowledge, this proposal is the first to quantify the redundancy of a conventional uniform array from the view of supportive resolution. [Design] Objective 2 – Our second objective is to take advantage of the proposed redundancy theory to present typical designs of the sparse linear or planar arrays in different scales. These sparse arrays are optimized to contain the minimally redundant but full-coverage resolutions. Meanwhile, they can be scaled down or up to equip with any number of antennas to meet diverse IoT demands. Particularly, we propose to design the log-spiral antenna belt (LSAB), which is a scalable planar antenna array. LSAB is advantageous to traditional uniform planar array in two aspects. First, it greatly increases the aperture size by using a few numbers of antennas over a large area. Second, it allows the whole tracking system to acquire sufficient segments from the smallest-sized IoT packet in a time-sharing fashion without the need for retransmissions. [Benchmark] Objective 3 – The successful implementation of the prototype provides the research community and the industry a novel method and proven experience in practice. Our third research is to fabricate and evaluate the performance of the designed sparse arrays through our existing 8x8 uniform planar array, compared with the common baselines. The proposed benchmark would quantify the outperformance of the designed sparse linear or planar arrays. [Filed Study] Objective 4 – Finally, we plan to implement LSAB prototypes over today's RFIDs. Our final objective is to use the developed prototypes to conduct a field study. To this end, we propose a novel reference RFID tags-based tracking system, which employs the spatial spectrums generated by LSAB as location signatures. We also plan to release the corresponding signal data and labels to the community for building an open and free benchmark library.

15215421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15215421.value: High-precision tracking of IoT devices inside buildings where GPS is unavailable has become a growing business interest. To this end, recent years have witnessed a major interest in developing accurate tracking systems with the help of an array of many antennas. An antenna array is a group of antennas placed in some way, resulting that the signals transmitted or received by each individual antenna sums up to provide better gain, directivity and performance over using a single antenna. Due to these benefits, antenna arrays have been widely used in many conventional wireless system (such as 5G, Wi-Fi). However, they are still not adopted in the IoT yet nowadays despite their attractive advantages because of the unfordable manufacture cost and high-power consumption caused by the antenna array. In this proposal, we propose the time-sharing sparse antenna arrays with minimal resolution redundancy, which aims to estimate the angle of arrival (AoA) of an IoT device in 3D space by using a few antennas connected to a time-shared channel. Our preliminary results demonstrate that one of our sparse arrays equipped with 9 antennas can perform as well as a traditional 9 x 13 uniform planar array consisting of 117 antennas. This proposal advances new hypotheses on the design of sparse arrays, which state that (1) a uniform antenna array is a multi-resolution AoA estimator with redundant resolutions; (2) a sparse antenna array can be constructed by eliminating such redundancy. Following the hypotheses, we design a serial of linear sparse arrays and a log-spiral planar antenna array to meet the special demands of IoT. Finally, we propose a key application for the field study. In total, this proposal initiates a new paradigm of AoA tracking systems enabled by sparse arrays. It presents a research effort to bring the advances of traditional antenna array into IoT, with solid preliminary studies we have made previously. It opens an avenue to study indoor localization and tracking from a new perspective and will motivate various researches over sparse arrays. 針對物聯網設備的室內追踪已經變成一個商業熱點。為此，最近幾年學術界掀起了利用天線陣列進行精準追踪系統研究的浪潮。天線陣列是由若干個獨立天線按照一定的規則排列而成的系統。這些天線可以相互補益從而具有比單根天線更高的增益、方向性和性能等特點。得益於這些好處，天線陣列被廣泛的用在諸如5G，Wi-Fi等傳統的無線電系統中。然而，至今很少天線陣列被物聯網設備所採用，因為天線陣列所增加的製造成本和耗能是一般的廉價物聯網設備無法承擔的。這個項目提出一種分時地最小分辨率冗餘的稀疏天線陣列。這種天線陣列通過分時方式連接幾根天線就能估計出物聯網設備在三維空間中的到達角。例如，我們的初步實驗結果顯示9根稀疏天線陣列就能達到傳統117根天線的均勻天線陣列的估計精度。我們稀疏天線的設計基於以下兩個簡單且基本的假設：（1）傳統的均勻天線陣實際上是一個存在冗餘的多分辨的到達角估計器；（2）可以通過消除均勻天線陣的分辨率冗餘來構造稀疏陣列。根據這樣的假設，我們設計了一系列的線性稀疏陣列和一個基於螺旋線的平面陣列。為了驗證這樣的假設和設計，我們提出一個關鍵的應用假設。總體來說，本項目旨在提出一種新的基於稀疏陣列的到達角估計系統範式，能夠為室內定位系統的設計提出一個新的研究，並能促進基於室內定位的相關研究。

15215621.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15215621.value: 航空業應對疫情的定量模型分析 - 信息模糊性和旅客健康報告的影響

15215621.label: Project Objectives
15215621.value: This study aims to contribute to decision-making related to pandemic control in the aviation industry. This is achieved by modelling the industry’s best response strategy, with alternative public policies evaluated and various stakeholders’ response actions analyzed. This is achieved with an analytical research Module 1 and an empirical research Module 2. Module 1 models the decision-making of stakeholders (airlines and regulators in different countries), in which profit-maximizing airlines make operation decisions under government health/operation regulations. The model is then extended for the analysis of the formation of a travel bubble. Both dynamic and static specifications are examined. Module 2 conducts behavior experiments and stated preference analysis on alternative health reporting/tracing requirements. The effects of travelers’ concerns over safety and privacy are jointly estimated. The effectiveness of alternative enforcements on health declaration is investigated. This study aims to contribute to the academic literature with major improvements addressing existing research gaps, notably the modelling of information ambiguity related to the spread of the infectious disease; trade-off between pandemic control and economic considerations; endogenous responses by airlines and governments in different countries; and air traveler behavior and attitude, notably those related to privacy, safety concern, health reporting and the associated enforcement policy. This is achieved by modelling airlines’ decision under government regulation. Pandemic control state is influenced by airlines’ decisions. Information ambiguity of the spread of the infectious disease is specified with a Knightian uncertainty model. Travelers’ behaviors are identified with Stated Preference experiments considering latent class and preference heterogeneity. This study aims to give practical recommendations on government policy and airline strategy for specific markets. This is achieved by linking results of the two complementary research modules. The two research modules are complementary. Empirical estimation results related to travel demand, health risk reporting/identification in Module 2 help calibrate analytical models in Module 1, thus that practical guidance on policy formulation and business strategy can be obtained for specific aviation market. Analytical results and insight obtained in Module 1 contribute to airline operation and strategy choice under alternative regulations, which in turn influence passenger utility and travel demand. Jointly the proposed study contributes to the literature with advanced and realistic modelling, and provides practical solutions in views of both public health and industrial needs.

15215621.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15215621.value: 航空運輸業在疫情中扮演的角色比較特殊。一方面，如果沒有良好的健康控制，航空業可能成為病毒在國際乃至大陸間傳播的渠道。因此，需要嚴格的限制措施以維護公共健康安全。另一方面，航空業是貿易和經濟發展的重要推動力量，在疫情造成經濟萎縮的情況下更具重要性。此外航空業對包括個人防護用品在內的醫療設備生產流通也至關重要。所以，疫情相關決策必須考慮到航空業的利益，確保其商業運行的可持續性。總而言之，航空業在應對疫情時必須同時考慮在健康控制和經濟發展方面的挑戰。如果關於傳染性疾病的相關信息和理解不充分（即在有信息模糊性的情況下），這樣的決策會更加困難。旅行健康申報可以減少信息不足的問題，但旅客對於個人隱私的顧慮往往嚴重限制其應用。國際旅行的情況更加複雜，因為政府在製定管制政策時需要考慮本國、中轉地和目的地國家的疫情狀況、旅客和航空企業的反應。也就是說，在決策制定時需要提前考慮到在信息模糊性條件下不同類型決策者的相關應對。 本研究致力於分析航空業應對疫情的最佳決策，在對不同的政策進行評估時提前考慮持份者的應對。以上所述的複雜決策會通過兩個研究模塊予以分析： 研究模塊一：對不同持份者的決策建模分析。研究任務1.1利用一個綜合模型分析以下持份者的決策：尋求利潤最大化的航空公司；尋求社會福利和公共健康的政府。研究任務1.2將以上模型擴展到兩個國家在建立旅行氣泡時的協商決策。研究任務1.3進一步分析市場均衡的條件和結果（如分析疫苗有效控制疫情的條件和結果）。這個研究模塊得到的解析結論會對公共政策和航空企業的商務決策提供有效支持。 研究模塊二：通過行為實驗分析旅行者的偏好。研究任務2.1分析旅行者安全方面的顧慮對於出行需求的影響。研究任務2.2量化旅客隱私顧慮對於健康申報的影響。研究任務2.3分析不同健康申報執行方法的效用。本模塊獲得的實證結果會幫助制定與旅行者動機相符的申報和監測應用，更有效地確定旅行者健康風險，減少信息模糊性。 兩個研究模塊互相補充。通過研究模塊二獲得的關於出行需求、健康風險申報的實證結果可以用於模塊一模型的定量分析 ，協助制定特定市場條件下公共政策和航空企業的商務決策。研究模塊一獲得的結論可以用於分析不同管制條件下航空企業的運營和決策，從而影響旅行者的利益和出行需求。同時研究這兩個模塊不僅對現實複雜條件下的建模分析有所貢獻，更可以在平衡健康控制和行業發展的條件下提供現實解決方案。

15216221.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15216221.value: 地下災害的不同規模和多陣列的探地雷達 (GPR) 診斷

15216221.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15216221.value: Dr Goodman, Dean Prof ZHU, Xiaolin

15216221.label: Project Objectives
15216221.value: Study the effects of different instrumentations (V-V/H-H polarizations, scan sampling and antenna frequency) on 3D sliced images obtained by the two tiers of data capture modes (a) GPR patrol and (b) GPR detail imaging in the training ground and two site of interests (SOIs). Establish a pixel-based pattern recognition classification model for change detection of potential pipe leak and voids by tier 1 data capture mode: GPR patrol in multi-array highway speed. Establish a supervised machine learning (SML) classification model for classifying severity of pipe leak and voids by tier 2 data capture mode: GPR detail imaging, based on the change-detection results in objective 2. 15216221.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15216221.value: Due to increasing city population requiring increasing demand of water supplies, sewer discharge, energy and telecommunication, city’s underground is getting more complex because of the very high density. For example in Hong Kong, 47km utilities occupy 1km road on average. Utilities are unavoidably aging and create problems, like ground subsidence caused by pipe leak and void. Locating these problems for rehabilitation or replacement requires a scientific approach of diagnosis. This process is best conducted by Ground Penetrating Radar (GPR) because of (1) its sliced image unfolding the underground spaces, (2) efficiency of data capture in highway speed, and (3) cm-scale fine resolution. While GPR slicing of the city underground is getting popular in both research and commercial work, its application is in small scale, and interpretation is highly subjective due to different non-standard data collection, processing and imaging methods. A first objective, systematic and bias-free workflow for GPR slice/C-scans has been established by PI’s research team and the Co-I Dean Goodman (Luo et al., 2019). This work paves for the proposed GPR change detection for imaging hazards growth. The far-reaching goal requires ‘track-changes’. This proposed project will make use of two tiers of multi-scale and multi-array methods: (1) GPR patrol via fast-moving multi-array for recognizing the most hazardous area without traffic disruption, and (2) GPR detail imaging via a small GPR single array involving partial road closure. This project will first study the instrumentation limitations of antenna polarizations, scan sampling and antenna frequencies on tier 1 and 2 methods. Secondly, an image-based approach will locate problematic water mains. The first means is tier 1’s change-detection diagnosis (Luo & Lai, 2020b). The second means is tier 2’s supervised machine learning for classification of two major underground hazards: pipe leak and void. The above development will involve lab/field experiments and numerical simulation in a 1900sq.m training ground designed by the PI. Finally, two real site of interests (SOIs) will be used to study the feasibility for establishing the underground medical record. This contributes to an objective, systematic and bias-free decision-making process while the most skilled analyst would fall short of handling huge volume of data. Together with Dr. Dean Goodman, a geophysicist from the USA, and PI’s colleague Dr. Xiaolin Zhu, a specialist in remote sensing, this research will develop a solution for urban underground health imaging and diagnosis. This project will trigger the establishment of fully covered underground health-record for hazard diagnosis in cities. 由於城市人口的增加，對供水、下水道排放、能源和電信的需求不斷增加，城市的地下由於密度非常高而變得越來越複雜。例如在香港，47 公里的公用事業平均佔用 1 公里的道路。公用事業不可避免地會老化並產生問題，例如管道洩漏和空隙引起的地面下沉。定位這些問題以進行康復或更換需要科學的診斷方法。該過程最好由探地雷達 (GPR) 進行，因為 (1) 其切片圖像可展開地下空間，(2) 以高速公路速度捕獲數據的效率，以及 (3) 厘米級高分辨率。雖然城市地下探地雷達切片在研究和商業工作中越來越受歡迎，但其應用規模較小，由於數據採集、處理和成像方法不同，解釋主觀性很強。 PI 的研究團隊和 Co-I Dean Goodman (Luo 等人，2019 年）建立了第一個客觀、系統和無偏差的 GPR 切片/C 掃描工作流程。這項工作為擬議的 GPR 變化檢測成像危險增長鋪平了道路。 深遠的目標需要“跟踪變革”。此項目將使用兩層方法: 不同規模和多陣列：（1）通過快速移動的多陣列進行 GPR 巡邏，以識別最危險的區域，而不會堵塞交通，以及（2）通過 GPR 詳細成像的小型 GPR 單陣列(涉及部分道路封閉)。此項目將首先研究天線極化、掃描採樣和天線頻率對第 1 層和第 2 層方法的儀器限制。其次，基於圖像的方法將定位有問題的水管。第一種方法是第 1 層的變化檢測診斷（Luo & Lai，2020b）。第二種方法是 Tier 2 的監督機器學習，用於對兩種主要地下危險進行分類：管道洩漏和空洞。上述開發將涉及在 PI 設計的 1900 平方米訓練場中進行實驗室/現場實驗和數值模擬。最後，將使用兩個真實的興趣點（SOI）來研究建立地下病歷的可行性。這有助於客觀、系統和無偏見的決策過程，以處理最熟練的分析師也無法處理的大量數據。 這項研究將與來自美國的地球物理學家 Dean Goodman 博士和 PI 的同事遙感專家朱孝林博士一起，為城市地下健康成像和診斷開發解決方案。該項目將觸發建立全覆蓋的地下健康檔案，用於城市災害診斷。

15216521.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15216521.value: 基於掃描至建築信息模擬及插件技術的室内空間綠建環評自動化

15216521.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15216521.value: Dr DARKO, Amos Dr Jalaei, Farzad

15216521.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15216521.value: 面對建築環境對可持續發展帶來的問題，我們需要一個更好的評估手段以提升既有建築物的可持續性表現。雖然目前存在各類綠建環評系統，但環評的過程非常複雜、耗時、昂貴，需要耗費相當資源及精力來搜集大量數據、提交文件以作評估。而這些人工數據搜集及歸檔可能會出錯、不準確，以致不可靠。 因此，自動化建築環評能夠提高評估過程的有效性及準確性，但相關研究卻很少，個別研究亦存在一些局限性，比如它們僅僅涵蓋一小部分的建築環評指標。而開發一個全面的自動化的建築環評流程有助於加强我們對環評各項指標的理解，並且自動化技術能夠提升綠建環評過程的精確度，這對促進全球建築環境的可持續性發展意義重大。過去的研究主要集中於新建建築，但由於既有建築對可持續性的影響頗大，提升既有建築綠建環評的有效性不僅能夠指引翻新工程，更能促進既有建築的可持續性。 此項研究目的包括兩個方面。首先，基於香港建築環境評估方法，該項目將建立一個一體化的方式以實現室内空間綠建環評自動化。我們通常會花費90%的時間在室内空間，因此提升室内空間的可持續性能夠增强人們的健康、生活質素及生產力。該研究將會基於一個高精準度、高速的三維激光掃描，用以掃描建築物内部空間的數據將其轉化成建築信息模擬，再通過一個創新性的插件在建築信息模擬環境内評估室内空間的可持續性。其二，該研究將測試這個系統，以證實室内空間綠建環評自動化的可行性，其表現將會與人工評估進行比較。總體來説，此項目將會開發及驗證“掃描至建築信息模擬及插件”的方式實現室内空間綠建環評自動化。通過利用三維激光掃描及建築信息模擬技術，有助於明確可持續目標，提升建築環評的有效性，減少人工數據搜集，提供更準確的信息。此項目的創新性在於：這將是首個嘗試實現室内空間綠建環評自動化的研究。值得注意的是，現今建築信息模擬的應用在建造業愈來愈普遍，香港政府規定合同造價高於3000萬港幣的公共工程項目需采用建築信息模擬。

15216621.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15216621.value: 高超聲速邊界層轉捩中多模態機理及其控制策略研究

15216621.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15216621.value: Prof HAO, Jiaao Dr Zhao, Rui

15216621.label: Project Objectives
15216621.value: To investigate the stabilization effects of different surface acoustic characteristics on the Mack second mode in high-speed BL flows and design the metasurface microstructures to realize the desired acoustic impedance. To compare and interpret the stabilization mechanisms of different acoustic metasurfaces by decomposing the instabilities into vortical, acoustic, and thermal components according to the momentum potential theory in terms of disturbance energy production, dissipation, and transport. To extend the application of different acoustic metasurfaces to the 3-D first-mode and crossflow instabilities and improve the stabilization effectiveness of acoustic metasurfaces for broadband disturbances. To verify the transition control performance of acoustic metasurfaces via high-speed wind tunnel experiments.

To compare and interpret the stabilization mechanisms of different acoustic metasurfaces by decomposing the instabilities into vortical, acoustic, and thermal components according to the momentum potential theory in terms of disturbance energy production, dissipation, and transport.

15216621.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15216621.value: The aeronautical technologies have exerted significant and far-reaching influence on the progress of human civilization. Currently, the United States Department of Defense has listed eleven cutting-edge technologies, with high-speed flight ranking third. The term high-speed indicates “flying at a speed greatly in excess of the speed of sound, usually greater than Mach 4”. With the fight speed increasing to Mach 6, the travel time between Hong Kong and New York can be reduced from 16 hours to only 3 hours, which may pave a life-changing way towards a faster worldwide communication in the foreseeable future. However, the high-speed fight poses a series of challenges to the vehicle design. A typical example is high-speed boundary-layer (BL) transition from laminar flow to turbulence, which causes a significant increase in heat transfer and skin friction. This translates to upraised cost and weight of highspeed vehicles due to increased thermal protection system (TPS) weight. Therefore, the interest in the technological development to increase the laminar BL region on the high-speed vehicle surface has increased rapidly over the past few decades in the aeronautical engineering community. One of the promising techniques is to use a thin porous coating (an absorptive type of acoustic metasurfaces with uniform microstructures) installed on the vehicle surface to dissipate the most unstable acoustic disturbances in the BL and increase its laminar run. However, recent studies reveal this uniform design is inherently disturbance frequency-dependent. It can excite other unstable modes with lower frequencies which may alternatively lead to transition. This project will focus on exploring the control mechanisms and design methods of acoustic metasurfaces for damping the broadband disturbances inside the high-speed BL to delay its transition. With an interdisciplinary research including aerodynamics, acoustics, and materials, this project will address two specific goals: (1) to verify and interpret the stabilization effects of different acoustic characteristics of metasurfaces on the two-dimensional (2-D) Mack second mode and (2) to widen the effective acting frequencies of metasurfaces by considering the three-dimensional (3-D) first and crossflow modes. Wind tunnel experiments, acoustic measurements, numerical simulations, and theoretical analysis will be combined to characterize the stabilization effect of acoustic metasurfaces. It is envisaged that the knowledge gained from this project will broaden the scope of applications of this passive control on the high-speed BL transition and explore the latent capability of acoustic metasurfaces as a novel TPS of high-speed vehicles. 航空技術對人類文明的發展已經產生了重大和深遠的影響。在美國國防部最近列舉的11項前沿尖端科技中，高速飛行技術位列第三。高速飛行概念是指“飛行器飛行速度遠超聲速（馬赫數≥4）”。當飛行器速度達到馬赫數6時，從香港到紐約的飛行時間將從普通航班的16小時降低到3小時，在可預見的未來，如此快速便捷的全球交流將會直接改變人們的生活。然而，設計適用於高速飛行的飛行器依然面臨著重重挑戰。其中之一便是高超聲速邊界層中湍流轉捩會導致飛行器表面的熱傳導系數和氣動阻力系數急劇上升。高速飛行器表面過度的氣動加熱要求設計高性能的熱防護系統（TPS），這也就意味著飛行器造價和重量的提升。因此，航空工程領域在過去的幾十年裏越來越關注發展在高速飛行器表面延遲轉捩從而延長層流區域的工程技術。其中，通過在高速飛行器表面安裝一層薄的多孔介質塗層（由規則微結構組成的吸聲型聲學超材料）來耗散邊界層中最不穩定的擾動波是最有希望實現層流控製的技術之一。近期以來的研究表明，這種具有一致規則微結構設計的聲學超材料的性能與擾動波的頻率息息相關。在耗散特定頻率的擾動波的同時也有可能激發其他頻率的擾動波從而導致轉捩。這個項目將集中於探索研究在高超聲速邊界層內具有廣譜耗散功能以延遲轉捩的聲學超材料的控制機理及其設計方法。基於包括氣體動力學，聲學，材料學等在內的跨學科交叉研究，這個項目將解決兩個特定的目標：（1）驗證和解釋不同聲學特性的超材料對二維Mack第二模態的穩定效果；（2）考慮三維Mack第一模態和crossflow模態的影響以擴展聲學超材料的有效頻率範圍。風洞試驗，聲學測量，數值模擬和理論分析方法將會被結合起來研究聲學超材料的穩定效果。這個項目的研究成果將會拓展聲學超材料作為一種被動控制技術在高超聲速邊界層轉捩中的應用範圍，挖掘出聲學超材料在高速飛行器新型熱防護材料方面的潛能。
