15216621.label: Major findings and research outcome
15216621.value: 1. Stabilization of Mack mode and metasurface design: We established an impedance‑driven design framework for hypersonic acoustic metasurfaces and demonstrated broadband suppression of the Mack second mode. A double‑layer perforated metasurface, combining a transmissive micro‑hole upper layer and a chambered lower layer to jointly tune resistive/inductive/capacitive components, achieved efficient second‑mode attenuation across a relatively broad frequency range (Paper 3). Frequency-domain and Time‑domain impedance boundary conditions (TDIBC) were developed/validated in Mach 6 DNS, reproducing amplitude/phase responses for single‑frequency and broadband inputs, thus enabling rapid impedance exploration and design iteration (Paper 2; Paper 8). We also demonstrated effective control with porous coatings even under thermochemical nonequilibrium (Paper 17). 2. Mechanistic comparison via momentum potential theory (MPT): An energy‑based decomposition clarified how vortical, acoustic, and thermal components contribute to instability growth and metasurface stabilization. We found the thermal-acoustic source peaks near synchronization and is the principal driver of second‑mode amplification across different wall‑temperature conditions; dissipative thermal-acoustic source destabilizes the second mode near the wall (Paper 1). A more unified theoretical framework combining MPT, relative phase analysis and inviscid Lagrangian method is established (Paper 7; Paper 9). Comparative MPT showed that absorptive, impedance‑near‑zero, and reflection‑controlled metasurfaces share similar vortical/acoustic/thermal source distributions, while stabilization differences arise from the diffusion source term Pdiff: absorptive designs restrain negative Pdiff near the surface; the other two strengthen positive Pdiff near/under the critical layer (Paper 13). 3. Extension to 3‑D first‑mode and crossflow instabilities: We clarified acoustic–vortical evolution mechanisms of the supersonic first Mack mode (Paper 16), established receptivity of first and crossflow modes in sharp‑wing hypersonic flows (Paper 14), and revealed stabilization mechanisms of traveling crossflow modes in swept wings (Paper 15). For broadband metasurface strategies, the impact mechanism on multi‑disturbance interactions was quantified (JFM, under 2nd-round review; Paper 7). 4. Verification pathway toward wind‑tunnel transition control TDIBC‑validated DNS provides a surrogate for experimental impedance characterization and guides test planning (Paper 8; JFM, under review). The established mechanism‑driven design guidelines, frequency‑targeted impedance maps, and identified mechanism for 3‑D first‑mode and crossflow instabilities form the basis for high‑speed wind‑tunnel verification of transition control performance in the next phase.

15216621.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15216621.value: 1. Robust metasurface design: Transition from idealized impedance to manufacturable designs using high‑temperature materials; mitigate microslit recirculation/edge‑wave “roughness” via geometry tuning; Multi‑objective optimization to balance suppression of second mode, minimal first‑mode excitation, structural/thermal constraints. 2. Modeling and uncertainty: Refine TDIBC with frequency‑dependent, temperature‑aware impedance models; perform uncertainty quantification on impedance retrieval and stability predictions. Build LES/RANS closures informed by DNS budgets (pressure–dilatation, thermal diffusion, Prt(y,k)), enabling rapid design screening. 3. Mechanism‑driven extensions: Use DNS-SPOD and/or resolvent analysis to identify amplification ridges (vortical/acoustic branches) and tailor impedance to the dominant triads at different Mach numbers or wall temperatures. 4. Experimental verification pathway: Calibrate impedance via coupon tests; conduct Mach 4–6 wind‑tunnel runs with instrumented panels (p′, u′, heat flux, transition location). Iterate the design with TDIBC‑DNS and SPOD guidance. Deliverables: validated wind‑tunnel suppression of second mode, quantified broadband gains, enhanced design rules for manufacturable metasurfaces, and deployable modeling tools for practical transition control.

15216621.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15216621.value: This project aims to make future hypersonic vehicles (flying at over five times the sound speed) safer and more efficient. At such speeds, a thin layer of air close to the vehicle’s surface can quickly turn turbulent, greatly increasing heat and drag. We studied how to “quiet” this layer by using specially designed, sound‑absorbing surfaces with micro-holes that act like a smart muffler for harmful waves in the airflow. Using advanced computer simulations and theory, we identified which types of waves and energy pathways most strongly trigger the dangerous “second‑mode” instability and how surface designs can stop it. We created new broadband and double‑layer metasurfaces that suppress these waves across a wide range of frequencies, and we built a fast modeling tool to design and test such surfaces virtually. We also discovered practical laminar-turbulent transition and the impact of sound‑absorbing surfaces, and we proposed fixes for the identified negative impact. The results provide clear design rules to delay turbulence onset, reduce heat load and drag and improve reliability of hypersonic vehicles. The wind‑tunnel test is employed to prove these benefits under realistic conditions.

15216721.value: To propose new technical tools for ZKP in lattice settings, including compacted vector compression, scalable binary proof, and efficient rejection sampling. Furthermore, the binary proof works as a bridge to make the vector compression suitable for more complicated ZKPs such as range proofs and one-out-of-many proofs. Finally, we convert the new proofs into range proof protocols and ring signature schemes for RingCT protocols. To carry out formal security analyses to prove that our proofs are secure under lattice assumptions, and conduct theocratical analyses and experiments to show our approaches are practical for real-world applications.

15216721.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15216721.value: Cryptocurrencies enable peer-to-peer transactions based on the blockchain technique. In June 2020, China's ministry of education published the plan for blockchain technology innovation. To allow anyone can verify all transactions on the blockchain, Bitcoin requires all details of a transaction are public. Such requirement leaks users' private information and makes Bitcoin unsuitable for confidential scenarios. To deal with the privacy issue, ring confidential transactions (RingCT) are applied in anonymous cryptocurrencies. By encapsulating transactions in zero-knowledge proofs (ZKP), users can prove useful statements without leaking private information, i.e., range proofs to hide the amount and ring signatures (one-out-of-many proofs) to hide their identities. However, existing ZKPs either require a trusted setup or cost significant time and space. Besides, current implementations are not secure against attacks from quantum computers. This project will study confidential transactions in today's private cryptocurrencies and propose novel efficient and quantum-secure RingCT protocols. The project will first propose several novel technical tools to improve the ZKPs in lattice-based post-quantum RingCT protocols without a trusted setup, i.e., compression technique, binary proofs, and rejection sampling. The new compression technique compresses a vector to reduce the proof size. Furthermore, we provide a binary proof for the range proof and one-out-of-many proof which is compatible with our compression technique. Finally, in lattice settings, we reduce the overhead of current rejection sampling with a new approach, which neither requires Gaussian sampling nor secrets with a fixed Hamming weight. Furthermore, we show how to adopt our techniques in range proofs and ring signatures. With the new techniques, it is practical to design post-quantum and communication efficient range proofs and ring signatures to enhance security and reduce communication costs. Comparing with existing approaches, the efficiency is greatly improved and the proof size is significantly reduced, which makes our approaches practical for private cryptocurrencies. The project has many technical merits. Privacy has become a major requirement for cryptocurrencies in many confidential applications. Proposing novel efficient confidential transaction protocols to provide anonymity and confidentiality is in the urgent need of private cryptocurrencies. We plan to conduct theoretical analysis and experiments to show the novel protocols are efficient and post-quantum secure to hide the amount and identities. Furthermore, all proposed approaches will be verified in formal secure analyses to show they have perfect completeness, perfect honest verifier zero-knowledge, and computational soundness. Besides RingCT protocols, we also discuss further applications of our techniques such as multi-party computing. 密码货币的发展让点对点交易得到广泛应用，如在2020年6月，中国教育部发布区块链技术创新计划。比特币作为第一种密码货币，通过公开交易细节的方式，允许任何人验证所有交易信息。但是这种公开方式泄露了用户的私人信息，也导致了比特币不适用于机密场景。 为了解决隐私问题，匿名密码货币采用环保密交易（RingCT）方式，通过将交易封装到零知识证明（ZKP）中，来保护用户隐私信息。其中包括通过区间证明技术隐藏交易金额，以及通过环签名（一对多证明）技术隐藏身份。但是，现有的ZKP方案需要一个消耗极高的可信初始化过程，并且目前方案无法抵抗量子攻击。 本项目首先针对基于格密码的零知识证明方案提出了多种优化技术，包括压缩技术、二进制证明、拒绝采样证明。其中，新的压缩技术可以大大缩小目前方案的证明体积。进一步，我们针对区间证明和一对多证明提出了二进制证明方案，同时兼容压缩技术。最后，在格密码中，我们使用既不需要高斯采样也不需要固定汉明重量的方案，以降低了拒绝采样的开销。 我们进一步设计区间证明和环签名方案。新提出的技术大大增强了设计并实现基于格密码的抗量子攻击的区间证明和环签名的可行性。与现有方案相比，我们方案具有更高的效率和更小的证明体积，并可以广泛应用于匿名密码货币中。 本项目具有许多技术优点。在许多匿名场景中，许多数字货币需要通过保密交易来保护隐私。因此，提出高效保密交易来提高匿名性和机密性是匿名数字货币的迫切需求。本项目所设计的协议的效率和安全性都会通过理论分析和安全性证明来进行验证。

15216721.label: Realisation of objectives
15216721.value: The project aimed to advance the state of post-quantum cryptographic protocols, specifically focusing on RingCT in lattice settings for private cryptocurrencies. The project successfully achieved its three primary objectives, which are detailed below. Objective 1: New Technical Tools for Zero-Knowledge Proofs (ZKPs) in Lattice Settings - Vector Compression Technique: One of the significant breakthroughs of this project was the development of a novel vector compression method. This technique was designed to reduce the size of proofs, which is a critical factor in enhancing the efficiency of cryptographic protocols. By batching monomials and leveraging quadratic residue challenges, the method effectively halved the communication complexity compared to existing approaches like Bulletproofs. This reduction in complexity is particularly beneficial in blockchain environments, where minimizing data size can lead to faster processing times and lower storage requirements. Moreover, the technique is versatile, as it can be applied in both lattice and discrete logarithm settings, thereby broadening its potential applications. Importantly, this method does not require trusted setups, which aligns with the decentralized ethos of blockchain systems, ensuring that the protocols remain secure and trustless. - Scalable Binary Proofs: Another key achievement was the development of a new binary proof framework. This framework allows for the partial amortization of multiple relations, making it compatible with vector compression techniques for complex zero-knowledge proofs, such as range proofs and one-out-of-many proofs. The framework generalizes existing amortization techniques to handle quadratic relations, which are often encountered in cryptographic applications. By doing so, it enhances the scalability and efficiency of zero-knowledge proofs, making them more practical for real-world use. - Efficient Cycle Masking and Rejection Sampling: The project also introduced a novel cycle masking scheme that efficiently generates small norm masking values satisfying inner-product constraints. This scheme is crucial for maintaining the security and efficiency of cryptographic protocols, as it ensures that masking values are generated in a way that prevents unauthorized access or manipulation. Additionally, the approach incorporates rejection sampling to reduce the proving time of existing designs. This improvement is significant, as it allows for faster and more efficient proof generation, which is essential for applications that require real-time processing. Furthermore, the new cycle masking approach mitigates side-channel attacks by ensuring that all masking vectors are computed within the same expected time, thereby enhancing the overall security of the system. Objective 2: Efficient Range Proof Protocols and Ring Signature Schemes - Range Proof Protocol: The project successfully designed range proof protocols using the new compression and binary proof tools in both discrete logarithm and lattice settings. In discrete logarithm settings, the team achieved a logarithmic proof size, reducing Bulletproofs from 2log(n) to log(n). This reduction is significant, as it decreases the computational resources required for proof generation and verification, making the protocols more efficient and scalable. In lattice settings, the use of inner-product based proofs eliminated the need for corrector values, further simplifying the proof generation process. Both solutions are practical for blockchain transactions, as they enhance the efficiency and security of the underlying cryptographic protocols. - Ring Signature Scheme: The project introduced two innovative approaches for achieving ring signatures. The first approach, a linear sum proof based on one-out-of-many proofs, improves efficiency without the need for binary proofs in lattice settings. This approach reduces the complexity and computational overhead associated with traditional ring signature schemes, making them more suitable for large-scale applications. The second approach, an any-out-many proof based on inner-product arguments, enhances anonymity by allowing to prove multiple secrets instead of a fixed one. This flexibility is crucial for maintaining privacy in blockchain transactions, as it ensures that sensitive information remains confidential. Both approaches reduce the signature size to logarithmic complexity and eliminate the linear growth limitations seen in previous work like Raptor. Additionally, they support batched verification, which ensures better efficiency in RingCT settings by allowing multiple transactions to be verified simultaneously. - Compatibility with Blockchain Systems: Both protocols were integrated into a simulated RingCT framework, demonstrating their compatibility with blockchain operations such as Mint and Spend. This integration is crucial for ensuring that the protocols can be seamlessly adopted in real-world blockchain environments. Objective 3: Formal Security Analyses and Experimental Validation - Security Proofs: The project included formal analyses of the proposed protocols, proving their perfect completeness, computational soundness, and honest-verifier zero-knowledge properties. These properties are essential for ensuring that the protocols are secure and reliable, as they guarantee that the proofs are both accurate and resistant to manipulation. Additionally, the team addressed potential side-channel attacks through timing analyses, demonstrating that there is no leakage during the proving process. This analysis is crucial for maintaining the security and integrity of the protocols, as it ensures that they are resistant to various forms of attack. - Experimental Implementation: The project involved the implementation of two prototypes: one under discrete logarithm settings and another under lattice settings. In discrete logarithm settings, the team developed a new secure elliptic curve and implemented the range proof system. This implementation demonstrated the practicality and efficiency of the proposed protocols in real-world applications. In lattice settings, the team introduced a new RingCT system, which showed a 15% improvement in efficiency compared to existing designs. This improvement highlights the potential of the proposed protocols to enhance the performance and scalability of blockchain systems.

15216721.label: Major findings and research outcome
15216721.value: 1. Novel Technical Tools for Zero-Knowledge Proofs - Vector Compression Technique (published in TDSC22): We have developed a novel compression technique specifically for vectors, which significantly reduces the communication overhead in zero-knowledge proofs. This method does not require a trusted setup, making it particularly suitable for decentralized blockchain systems. - Binary Proofs (published in PKC25): We introduced a scalable binary proof that acts as a bridge between vector compression and more complex zero-knowledge proofs, such as range proofs and one-out-of-many proofs. This binary proof is compatible with the compression technique, enabling more efficient proofs in lattice-based settings. - Efficient Cycle Masking (published in PKC25): A new cycle masking approach was proposed to minimize the overhead of masking vectors in lattice-based zero-knowledge proofs. This ensures that the norm of the masking vectors remains small, making it well-suited for inner-product based proof systems. 2. Efficient RingCT Protocol - Efficient Range Proof Protocols (published in TDSC22, ePrint24, PKC25, TIFS25): We designed and implemented new range proof protocols that leverage novel compression and binary proof techniques. These protocols, which include discrete-logarithm based methods (TDSC22, ePrint24, TIFS25) and lattice-based methods (PKC25), effectively address the limitations of existing range proofs. - Ring Signature Schemes (published in SP23 and PKC25): We introduced two new ring signature schemes. One is based on one-out-of-many proofs in lattice settings (PKC25), which efficiently eliminates the need for binary proofs to enhance efficiency. The other is based on a new any-out-of-many proof in discrete logarithm settings (SP23), which improves the anonymity of existing designs. 3. Applications Beyond Confidential Transactions - We have extended the applications of our proposed techniques to other privacy-preserving protocols, including compressed Sigma protocols (published in ePrint24), arithmetic circuit satisfiability (published in ePrint24), and e-health applications (TIFS24). These new zero-knowledge proof techniques have been shown to enhance the efficiency of these protocols and applications, particularly in lattice-based settings.

15216721.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15216721.value: 1. Lattice-Based Proof System with Standard Soundness During the project, Chen and Boneh developed a lattice proof system with standard soundness [LatticeFold in ePrint24]. This advancement provides a novel approach to achieving Bulletproofs-like compression without compromising soundness. Inspired by this, we designed a lattice-based proof system (published in ePrint25) that facilitates multi-round protocols in lattice settings. We believe that our new techniques in any-out-of-many proofs [SP23] can be effectively applied to lattice settings using these methods. 2. Private Multi-Party Transactions Current anonymous cryptocurrencies only allow a single spender with multiple accounts to conduct multi-account transactions. They do not support genuine multi-party transactions involving multiple spenders. The main challenge is that the spender must know the secret key for each account to generate the transaction, a requirement that existing ZKP systems cannot circumvent. During the project, we discovered that incrementally verifiable computation can efficiently address this issue, as demonstrated by [KiloNova in ePrint23 and SnarkFold in ePrint23]. We plan to leverage this concept to propose a private multi-party transaction system within RingCT.

15216721.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15216721.value: This project represents a significant advancement in the research of post-quantum RingCT protocols, specifically within lattice settings, aimed at enhancing the privacy features of cryptocurrencies. Traditional designs often involve costly operations and complex setups that can hinder efficiency and scalability, especially in blockchain environments. By streamlining these processes, our project significantly boosts the efficiency of RingCT protocols, making them more practical and adaptable for real-world blockchain applications. One of the key innovations of this project is its ability to extend these improvements beyond lattice settings. The concepts developed here can also be applied to discrete logarithm settings, which are commonly used in cryptographic systems. This adaptability not only enhances the efficiency of these systems but also improves their anonymity features, thereby broadening the scope and application of zero-knowledge proofs. Furthermore, the implications of this research extend beyond the realm of cryptocurrencies. The techniques and methodologies developed can be applied to other real-world applications, such as e-health systems, where privacy and data security are of paramount importance. Overall, this project not only advances the field of cryptography but also opens up new possibilities for secure applications in various industries.

15217221.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15217221.value: 浴室環境的熱感偏好及耗能優化模型

15217221.label: Project Objectives
15217221.value: Firstly, based on a simulation framework that incorporates the thermal preference variable, a new computational model will be developed providing thermal energy consumption for a range of showering facilities in the built environment. Secondly, the parameters needed in Objective (1), including heat transfer coefficients and other subject-related showering parameters, will be determined experimentally and statistically. Thirdly, a model test run, using the newly developed model, on a specific shower environment will be conducted and compared with measured results for validation purposes. Implications for the thermal comfort environmental control parameters as affected by thermal energy consumption will be determined, to demonstrate the practical application of the proposed model. Using Bayesian techniques, updating algorithms will be derived for both parameter estimates and occupant responses. Finally, the validated model will be used to generate the design data leading to optimal showering facilities, suitable for the Green Building Assessment process to demonstrate a further use of the model. A cost-benefit analysis comparing energy consumption against shower thermal preference and health effects will be performed.

15217221.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15217221.value: Smart energy applications are ‘core’ to the achievement of sustainable cities. Hong Kong, a key developed city in the Greater Bay Area (GBA) and characterized by its high-density built environment, consumes 60% more energy per capita for hot showers than its nearby cities due to user’s preference on shower frequency, water temperature and showering time. Although energy consumption in washrooms accounts for only about 20% of the total energy consumed in the residential sector, the energy consumption density (i.e. energy per unit area and time) in residential bathrooms (especially those in modern apartment buildings) is Bathroom design and bathing practice are the major energy consumption influencing factors in the bathroom environment. Even though various energy conservation and efficiency measures (e.g. water efficiency labelling schemes, conservation education programmes, and pricing strategies) have been implemented to reduce water heating electricity use, energy consumption models that enable the study of optimal bathroom environments are still lacking. To achieve thermal comfort before, during, as well as after showering, through sustainable design, thermal preference models which take consumer needs and expectations into account, are essential tools for climbing the rungs of sustainable development ladders and must be addressed in future practical building energy efficiency codes. This proposed project is innovative, and pioneering, in being the first to aim at understanding how shower design and control parameters (and building parameters) interact in meeting the thermal comfort aims of the individual. This is a step forward from knowing how the various parameters combine to meet a particular skin temperature requirement or a particular energy consumption. This study aims to establish thermal energy-efficient designs for high-rise urban residential shower and bathroom environments. It consists of the following core aspects: (1) to understand energy consumption in terms of human thermal comfort in the whole process of taking a shower, including before and after showering; (2) to formulate mathematical expressions that predict thermal energy requirements in various domestic thermal environments for showering, taking end-user thermal comfort levels, facility usage patterns, appliance characteristics, ventilation system designs, and various energy efficiency measures into account; and (3) to recommend sustainable thermal comfort practices in the bathroom environment to meet high performance and sustainable building requirements. 能源應用的智能化是實現城市可持續發展的核心技術之一。香港是大灣區（GBA）的一個重點發達城市，擁有高密度的建築環境。由於香港居民對淋浴頻率、淋浴時間、水溫和室溫的偏好，其熱水淋浴的人均能源消耗比鄰近城市高出60%。雖然衛生間的能耗僅佔住宅總能耗的20%左右，但住宅衛生間（尤其是現代公寓樓）的耗能密度（即每單位面積時間的能源消耗）卻非常高，因此耗能密度是浴室環境設計和淋浴操作中主要的能耗考慮因素。儘管政府已經實施了各種節能和效率改善措施（例如水效標籤計劃、節約教育計劃和定價策略）以減少加熱淋浴熱水所需的能源消耗，但目前仍缺少最佳浴室環境的耗能模型以供優化設計之用。為了確保用戶在淋浴前、淋浴中和淋浴後能夠達至熱舒適，需要將使用者需求和期望的熱偏好模型考慮在可持續設計中，以致實現住宅浴室的可持續發展。因此浴室的可持續發展應該包含在未來的建築能源效率法規中。本研究項目旨在了解淋浴設計和控制參數（包括建築參數）之間如何相互作用以滿足個人熱舒適目標，即了解各種參數如何組合以滿足特定皮膚溫度要求或特定能量消耗，從而建立城市住宅浴室環境的熱能效表達式。本研究主要包括以下幾個核心方面： (1) 從人體熱舒適度的角度了解整個淋浴過程中的能源消耗，包括淋浴前後； (2) 考慮用戶的最終熱舒適度、設施使用模式、器具特性、通風系統設計和各種能效措施，建立數學表達式來預測各種家庭淋浴熱環境中的熱能需求； (3) 推薦浴室環境中的可持續熱舒適實踐機制，以滿足高性能和可持續建築要求。

15217221.label: Realisation of objectives
15217221.value: 1. Objective 1: development of three computational models to predict thermal sensation and thermal energy consumption for a range of showering facilities. Initially, a thermal energy consumption model was developed to calculate energy use under varying shower conditions. Using this model, a database of showering energy consumption was established by evaluating energy use across different environmental parameters. The analysis identified water flow rate as the most influential variable and ventilation rate as the least influential for energy savings. The model employed an equation originally developed for fire engineering, which may not accurately represent shower scenarios. Consequently, further experiments were conducted to refine the relevant parameters. A thermal sensation model was also established using data from a series of showering experiments. Thermal sensation responses from 31 volunteers were collected under three shower conditions: control, colder, and warmer. The results demonstrated a non-linear relationship between participants’ thermal sensation votes (TSV) and air temperature. Furthermore, a dynamic thermal sensation (DTS) prediction model was developed using Python. The model accurately predicted occupants’ mean skin temperatures (MST) during showering; however, its prediction of dynamic thermal sensation was less satisfactory, as the underlying formula was originally designed for air exposure scenarios. Integration of these models enables the identification of an optimal showering environment that is both thermally comfortable and energy-efficient. Results indicated that water temperature had a 2.7-fold greater impact on total energy consumption compared to air temperature, and a 1.8-fold greater effect on occupants’ thermal comfort. Therefore, it is recommended to set the water temperature lower while increasing the air temperature to maintain thermal comfort and reduce energy consumption. 2. Objective 2: determination of parameters required for the energy consumption model. Several experiments were conducted to identify parameters necessary for the energy consumption model. Initially, a skin model, composed of a Styrofoam board and a thin aluminum board representing human skin, was developed and tested under 14 different showering conditions to determine the heat transfer coefficient between skin and water flow. The average heat transfer coefficient was found to be 96 W/(m2×℃), although this value varied significantly with different water flow rates and showerhead patterns. An additional experiment was performed in a controlled chamber to determine the relationship between air temperature changes and energy consumption rates. An updated equation, more suitable for showering conditions, was derived. This model demonstrated the effects of heat sources and ventilation on air temperature changes in a bathroom setting and assessed the feasibility of using collected temperature data to establish relationships between air temperature changes and energy consumption rates. 3. Objective 3: validation and improvement of the models The DTS model developed for Objective 1 was tested under three environmental conditions, and its predictions were compared with experimental results from a previous study. The comparison confirmed the validity of the DTS model, particularly for predicting MST. Additionally, a series of experiments were conducted in a typical residential bathroom to improve the model’s performance in predicting DTS, specifically to identify the relationship between MST and DTS during showering. Six environmental conditions were tested with 18 participants. Based on the collected data, a new DTS-MST model was developed. These findings have been published and presented at a conference. Incorporating the DTS-MST relationship into the DTS prediction model developed for Objective 1 will enhance its suitability for showering conditions and improve its accuracy in predicting DTS. 4. Objective 4: optimization of showering facilities. An experiment was conducted to evaluate the heat transfer performance of five showerheads with 18 spray patterns, using the skin model developed for Objective 2. Key metrics, including resistance factor, water supply pressure, and nozzle area ratio, were measured to assess shower performance. Results suggested that future showerheads should be designed with a greater number of smaller holes, and the nozzle area ratio should be maintained between 0.0075 and 0.015 kPa·min2/L2 to ensure thermal comfort while conserving energy during showering. A field study was also conducted to investigate water flow patterns in showering facilities at a swimming pool, with the aim of optimizing energy consumption. Based on the findings, installation of a water storage tank with appropriate volume was recommended to improve hot water energy efficiency. A focus group discussion was organized to explore occupants’ showering behaviors and preferences for the ideal showering environment. Results indicated that most participants preferred natural greenery and landscape elements in bathroom decor. Additionally, the inclusion of fruit scents and background music was found to enhance relaxation and occupant satisfaction during showering. These findings inform the design of showering environments by incorporating indoor environmental factors to improve comfort and well-being.

15217221.label: Major findings and research outcome
15217221.value: The principal outcomes of this research comprise two models for predicting showering thermal sensation, a model for forecasting showering energy consumption, and recommendations for optimizing showering facilities and bathroom design. Showering thermal sensation and dynamic thermal sensation prediction models: An initial literature review established foundational knowledge, including the selection of parameters and methods for developing prediction models [1]. Subsequently, a thermal sensation model was constructed using experimental data from volunteers, which demonstrated a non-linear relationship between thermal sensation votes and air temperature during showering [4]. Furthermore, a Python-based program was implemented to predict occupants’ mean skin temperatures and dynamic thermal sensation (DTS) during showering, utilizing environmental variables and personal characteristics [7]. Thermal energy consumption model: A comprehensive model was developed to estimate thermal energy consumption under various showering conditions. This model enables calculation of energy consumption based on four environmental variables—air temperature, water temperature, ventilation rate, and water flow rate—as well as showering duration [5]. Optimization of showering facilities: Experimental results on showerhead performance identified optimal design features, specifically recommending a greater number of smaller nozzles to improve both thermal comfort and energy efficiency [8]. Additionally, a field study of water flow patterns in showering facilities recommended the installation of appropriately sized water storage tanks to enhance hot water energy efficiency [6]. Suggestions on bathroom design: Focus group discussions generated recommendations for future bathroom design, such as incorporating natural greenery and landscape elements into bathroom decor. Additionally, the inclusion of floral or fruit scents and background music was suggested to enhance relaxation during showering [9]. Based on these research findings, nine journal articles and ten conference papers have been published (see Part C).

15217221.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15217221.value: The outcomes demonstrate significant progress in understanding showering thermal sensations and energy consumption, thereby facilitating further advancements. The developed thermal sensation prediction models, which integrate personal characteristics and environmental variables, may be further improved through additional experimental studies. As some experiments were constrained by small sample sizes, future research should incorporate a wider range of participants and environmental conditions to increase the accuracy and generalizability of these models. Furthermore, the application of machine learning techniques is recommended to generate deeper insights, particularly to optimise showerhead design and enhance comfort and energy efficiency. To translate these findings into practical applications, the project proposes the following actions. First, collaboration with designers and manufacturers of showering facilities is recommended to facilitate the integration of optimal design features identified in the research. Second, the implementation of bathroom design strategies that emphasize aesthetics and sensory enhancements should be encouraged in residential settings to evaluate their effects on occupants' showering comfort and satisfaction. Finally, educational initiatives targeting consumers will be undertaken to raise awareness of energy-efficient showering practices and promote the adoption of the proposed models. Collectively, these actions are expected to yield substantial improvements in both user experience and energy conservation during showering.

15217221.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15217221.value: Showering uses a lot of energy and water, but there is room to save both. This research looks for ways to make showers more comfortable and energy efficient. The study used lab and home experiments, surveys, focus groups, statistical analysis, and model building. Key results include a thermal sensation model, an energy-use model, and recommendations for showerhead and bathroom design. These findings can help create showers that are more comfortable and use less energy. Knowing what affects comfort and energy use can help designers build better showers that are good for both the environment and people's well-being.

15217321.label: Project Objectives
15217321.value: To design a novel framework with the hybrid storage of cloud and blockchain to support authenticated graph data query. The framework allows the outsource graph data on the cloud with dynamic data updates. The cloud hosts query services. The blockchain maintains the authenticated data structure using a smart contract and provides the trusted digest. To propose privacy-preserving authenticated query processing algorithms on graph data. The authenticated query algorithms can enable query users to efficiently verify the soundness and completeness of query results. To design a verifiable cloud query service by implementing a database fingerprint verification function in the blockchain. 15217321.value: 當前流行的雲服務可能不可靠也不值得信賴。不受信任的雲可能有意或無意中執行不正確的計算以響應來自客戶端用戶的查詢。因此，在這個項目中，我們利用區塊鏈技術，專注於認證查詢問題，以確保返回結果的可驗證性。 我們將首先解決圖數據存儲在雲上時的查詢問題。由於許多基於圖形的新興應用程序，圖數據引起了極大的關注。圖數據模型來自社交網絡、生物網絡和知識圖譜等。提供經過認證的圖查詢，以前的方法通常會洩露隱私敏感數據（例如，商業秘密或個人信息）。它們在處理數據時也效率低下。與目前的設計不同，我們將提出一個新穎的基於 RSA 累加器和完整性集的認證數據結構 (ADS)。我們的查詢設計是隱私保護的，因為它可以防止原始數據通過區塊鍊或不相關的查詢而洩露。我們方法中，經過驗證的數據結構，可以有效地通過智能合約支持數據動態更新。在這個項目中，我們將進一步優化經過驗證的圖數據查詢，以提高通信和計算能力。 然後，我們將解決可驗證的 kNN（k-最近鄰）查詢問題。關鍵字（STK）數據，廣泛用於基於區塊鏈的應用程序。現有工作僅支持帶有可驗證證明的簡單關鍵值查詢和布爾範圍查詢，忽略了靈活性和驗證方案的效率。為了克服這些限制，我們將提出兩種方法支持多維數據的kNN查詢。第一種方法是根據區塊鏈數據構建一個可驗證的、一致的雲數據庫。第二種方法是構建一個新穎的區塊鏈系統，命名為 STK-Chain，它設計了一種名為 Merkle RK-Tree 的新型數據結構。 STK-Chain能減少驗證時間，支持多維範圍的可認證查詢。

15217321.label: Realisation of objectives
15217321.value: We have fully achieved the six objectives listed above in this project. Objective 1: To design a novel framework with the hybrid storage of cloud and blockchain to support authenticated graph data query. We have fully achieved this objective by designing and implementing a secure hybrid framework that integrates cloud storage efficiency with blockchain integrity, underpinned by our proposed PAGB protocol and SolSaviour framework. To enable efficient and privacy-preserving authenticated graph queries, we developed PAGB [1], which utilizes accumulators and completeness sets to outsource large-scale dynamic graph data to the cloud while maintaining small-sized metadata on the blockchain for verifying result correctness and completeness without compromising privacy. Simultaneously, to guarantee the security and reliability of the smart contracts maintaining these data structures, we developed SolSaviour [4], which introduces a distributed Trusted Execution Environment (TEE) cluster to defend against vulnerabilities and attacks through decentralized contract repair and state migration, thereby providing a robust foundation for the authenticated query services. Objective 2: To propose privacy-preserving authenticated query processing algorithms on graph data. We have fully achieved this objective by developing advanced authenticated query processing algorithms within the PAGB framework [1], which simultaneously guarantee result soundness, completeness, and strict privacy preservation. To prevent privacy leakage, we utilized prime representatives to construct the accumulator, ensuring that the verification process validates query results without revealing sensitive topological information or attributes to the public blockchain. Furthermore, to address the challenge of completeness (ensuring no valid answers are missing), we introduced a novel "completeness set" mechanism that enables the generation of cryptographic witnesses for both the existence (membership) and non-existence (non-membership) of data across various graph operations, such as node/edge property queries and connectivity searches. Objective 3: To design a verifiable cloud query service by implementing a database fingerprint verification function in the blockchain. We have fully achieved this objective by developing the VQL middleware and the MRK-Tree framework [2]. To establish a verifiable cloud service, VQL reorganizes blockchain data into databases and calculates cryptographic fingerprints that are verified by miners and stored on-chain, enabling lightweight result verification via Merkle Patricia Trees. Furthermore, to support efficient kNN and range queries for multi-dimensional data, we designed the MRK-Tree and an Improved Block Header (featuring Bloom filter vectors and MRK Hashes). These structures, combined with our proposed Efficient Block Pruning (EBP) and Authenticated kNN/Range Query (AKQ/ARQ) algorithms, ensure that complex queries are executed with high efficiency while strictly guaranteeing the soundness and completeness of the results. Objective 4: To devise a blockchain system whose block has an improved block header structure and novel authenticated data structure in the body to store spatial-temporal-keyword data. We have fully achieved this objective by devising advanced blockchain architectures for both multi-dimensional data querying and trusted identity management. To enable authenticated queries on Spatial-Temporal-Keyword (STK) data, we designed the MRK-Tree as a novel block body structure and an Improved Block Header incorporating Bloom filter vectors, which, combined with our Efficient Block Pruning (EBP) algorithm, support highly efficient Authenticated kNN and Range Queries for light nodes [2]. Furthermore, to establish a trusted infrastructure for these services, we developed Pistis [6], a framework that leverages Merkle Patricia Trees (MPT) and Trusted Execution Environments (TEE) to issue and store authorized certificates, ensuring that the communication and identity verification among blockchain nodes are secure, tamper-proof, and verifiable by light-node users. Objective 5: To conduct a theoretical security analysis on the proposed designs, including the privacy of graph data, the soundness and completeness of query results. We have fully achieved this objective by conducting rigorous theoretical security analyses across our proposed frameworks to ensure data integrity and privacy. In [1], we formally defined the security properties for graph queries, proving via Theorem 1 and Theorem 2 that our PAGB scheme guarantees both soundness and completeness of query results based on the security of accumulators, while strictly preserving data privacy. For multi-dimensional data queries, we provided a comprehensive security analysis in [2], proving the unforgeability and reliability of the MRK-Tree and Improved Block Header mechanisms through formal lemmas, thereby ensuring that authenticated kNN and range query results cannot be tampered with or forged. Additionally, we analyzed the data authenticity of the VQL framework, demonstrating how cryptographic database fingerprints and Merkle Patricia Tree proofs effectively guarantee the consistency and verifiability of query results between the cloud middleware and the underlying blockchain ledger. Objective 6: To build a platform prototype for authenticated graph and kNN query services, and evaluate the performance of our proposed schemes in the constructed cloud and blockchain platform. We have fully achieved this objective by implementing platform prototypes for all proposed schemes and conducting extensive performance evaluations to verify their effectiveness and efficiency. For authenticated graph queries, we implemented the PAGB framework [1] and verified its low communication overhead using real-world knowledge graph datasets , while for multi-dimensional STK data [2], we built a blockchain prototype integrating the MRK-Tree that demonstrated up to 36.45x improvement in query time efficiency for authenticated kNN and range queries. To support verifiable cloud services, we developed the VQL middleware prototype on the Ethereum testnet, proving its high throughput capabilities compared to native clients. Furthermore, we extended our experimental evaluation to application-level security systems, implementing prototypes for the SolSaviour smart contract defense framework [4], the Pistis trusted certificate issuance system [6] using Intel SGX , the ZKDET [5] privacy-preserving data exchange scheme , and the DBE-voting system [3] on Hyperledger Fabric , all of which demonstrated feasible overhead and superior performance in practical scenarios. 15217321.label: Major findings and research outcome
15217321.value: The major findings of this project have significantly advanced the field of blockchain data management, specifically in enabling efficient, verifiable, and privacy-preserving query services. For Efficient and Authenticated Query Frameworks, we addressed the inefficiency of querying blockchain data. First, when handling STK Data, we discovered that traditional Merkle Trees are inefficient for multi-dimensional queries. We proposed MRK-Tree [2], a novel block body structure, and an Improved Block Header with Bloom filters. This finding enables authenticated kNN and range queries for Spatial-Temporal-Keyword transactions with up to 36x speedup. Then, for handling general data, we developed VQL, a cloud middleware that uses "database fingerprints" to bridge the gap between cloud efficiency and blockchain trust, allowing users to verify query results without running a full node. For Privacy-Preserving Graph Queries, we tackled the challenge of querying complex graph data on-chain. We proposed PAGB [1], finding that by combining accumulators with a "completeness set," we can support dynamic authenticated graph queries while strictly preserving data privacy. Beyond queries, we extended our findings to system-level security. We considered Smart Contract Security and proposed SolSaviour [4] and Pistis [6] to leverage Trusted Execution Environments (TEE) to protect deployed smart contracts and issue trusted certificates, mitigating the risk of software vulnerabilities. We also developed some applications to apply our verifiable mechanisms to data exchange (zkDET [5]) and electronic voting (DBE-voting [3]), proving that our architectures can support high-stakes applications requiring strict auditability and privacy. Research Outputs: The project has yielded fruitful outcomes, publishing 6 papers in top-tier venues, including 4 Top Journal Papers: • IEEE Transactions on Computers (TC): [2] (STK Queries). • IEEE Transactions on Knowledge and Data Engineering (TKDE): [1] (Graph Queries). • IEEE Transactions on Parallel and Distributed Systems (TPDS): [4] (SolSaviour), [6] (Pistis). • Top Conference Papers: IEEE ICDCS [5] and IEEE ICC [3].

15217321.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15217321.value: The technologies developed in this project have strong potential for further expansion in three key areas: 1. Cross-Chain Interoperability: The authenticated query structures (like MRK-Tree) can be extended to support cross-chain queries, allowing users to verify data across different blockchains (e.g., Ethereum and Hyperledger) seamlessly. 2. Privacy-Preserving Computing: Integrating our Zero-Knowledge (ZK) and TEE-based schemes (zkDET, SolSaviour) with Federated Learning. This would allow multiple parties to train AI models on blockchain-stored data without revealing the raw sensitive data. 3. Real-world Governance: The DBE-voting system and Pistis framework can be piloted in real-world scenarios, such as decentralized autonomous organization (DAO) governance or IoT device authentication, to replace centralized authorities with code-based trust.

15217321.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15217321.value: Blockchain is like a secure digital ledger, but searching through it is notoriously slow and expensive—like trying to find a specific sentence in a library where books are piled up randomly, not organized on shelves. Furthermore, asking a third party (like a cloud provider) to search for you is risky because they might provide fake or incomplete results. This project solved these problems by building a "smart index" and a "digital notary" system. We created new data structures (like MRK-Tree and VQL) that organize blockchain data (including complex location and graph data) efficiently, making searches lightning-fast. We developed mathematical proofs (authentication) that allow users to verify if the search results are 100% correct and complete, even when the data comes from an untrusted cloud server. We ensured that while the data is verifiable, sensitive details remain private. Our work makes blockchain systems practical for complex real-world applications like supply chain tracking, secure voting, and data exchange. The results have been published in top academic journals like IEEE TC, TKDE and TPDS. The project also supports the training of 2 PhD students in the topics of blockchain and security.

15217621.value: Aim 1: Synthesis and functionalization of small-sized multicolor fluorescent graphene quantum dots (GQDs) and gold nanoparticles (AuNPs). Multicolor GQDs will be synthesized via a bottom-up hydrothermal approach. The photo-stability, quantum yield and fluorescence lifetime of synthesized GQDs will be characterized. Small-sized AuNPs will be synthesized by a reduction approach with an optimal ratio of reducing agent/stabilizing agent. Aim 2: Design and establishment of hybridization chain reaction (HCR) enhanced multiplexed FRET nanoprobes for simultaneous detection of multiple miRNAs. Multiplexed FRET molecular beacon (MB) probes with hairpin structures will be synthesized with multicolor GQDs as donor molecules and AuNPs as acceptors for detection of multiple miRNAs. Hybridization chain reaction (HCR) approach will be combined with FRET probes for fluorescence signal amplification. The HCR enhanced FRET nanoprobes will be tested for detection of multiple miRNAs in buffer solution. The sensitivity, specificity, limit of detection (LOD) and linear detection range of FRET nanoprobes will be tested. Aim 3: In-situ multiplexed detection of miRNAs in exosomes derived from cultured cell samples and clinical samples with HCR enhanced multiplexed FRET nanoprobes. The effects of surface charge and concentration of AuNP-GQDs FRET nanoprobes on the nanoprobe uptake rate by exosomes will be studied. Exosomal miRNAs detection will then be tested with the HCR enhanced FRET nanoprobes. The correlation between detected the fluorescence signals detected at various emission channels and the contents of multiple miRNAs in exosomes measured by qRT-PCR will be established. Confocal fluorescence imaging will be performed for in-situ analysis of multiple exosomal miRNAs. Aim 4: High-throughput single exosome analysis in an integrated droplet optofluidic chip. A polymeric integrated microfluidic device will be fabricated with functions of prostate tumor exosome isolation with immunomagnetic bead, mixing of HCR enhanced multiplexed FRET nanoprobes and single exosomes in droplets, and droplet array generation for fluorescence detection and analysis. Subpopulation analysis of miRNAs profiles of single exosomes will be used for prostate tumor heterogeneity study.

15217621.value: 基於檢測體液中癌症生物標誌物的非侵入性和靈敏的液體活檢方法是侵入性組織活檢的有前途的替代方案。最近，由於與原始腫瘤細胞的結構和含量相似，以及它們在體液中的含量豐富，從腫瘤細胞分泌的循環腫瘤外泌體正在成為新的腫瘤生物標誌物。然而，目前的外泌體分析方法主要基於批量分析，無法揭示單個外泌體之間的差異。單外泌體分析（SEA）技術的發展對於腫瘤精準診斷具有重要意義。但目前的 SEA 技術主要集中在檢測腫瘤異質性信息有限的表面蛋白生物標誌物，缺乏對內部外泌體 miRNA 的原位多重檢測能力。儘管最近有一些關於外泌體 miRNA 檢測的報導，但由於低通量和缺乏多重檢測能力，尚未被廣泛採用。因此，開髮用於外泌體 miRNA 多重檢測的原位高通量和靈敏的 SEA 技術對腫瘤內異質性分析有很高的需求。 在該項目中，將在液滴光流控平台上開發一種通過雜交鏈反應 (HCR) 增強 FRET 納米探針的高通量、低成本的 SEA 技術，用於前列腺腫瘤外泌體中 miRNA 的原位多重檢測。這種 SEA 技術保留了前列腺腫瘤外泌體分離、高靈敏度和特異性、同時原位檢測多個 miRNA 以及基於液滴微流控芯片的高通量 SEA 分析的功能。為此，將首先建立小尺寸的核心-衛星 FRET 探針，以金納米顆粒 (AuNP) 作為受體，多色石墨烯量子點 (GQD) 作為供體，通過特定 miRNA 的適體連接。雜交鏈反應 (HCR) 方法將結合 FRET 探針進行熒光信號放大。然後將測試 HCR 增強的多重 FRET 納米探針的 miRNA 檢測和原位單外泌體分析。最後，SEA 分析將在集成液滴微流控芯片中進行測試，該芯片具有通過免疫磁珠純化前列腺腫瘤外泌體、液滴中單個外泌體封裝、樣品與納米探針混合和高通量信號數字計數的功能。將讀取和分析具有 3 種顏色強度編碼（藍-綠-紅）的單個外泌體的彩色條形碼，以進行深入的腫瘤外泌體異質性研究。所提出的原位 SEA 技術可以成為深入研究腫瘤內異質性的有力工具，可用於精確的癌症診斷、預後和治療效果評估。

15217721.value: 反射式多模光纖波前整形及其在生物組織深層的微創高分辨率光學刺激和成像的體外應用初探

15217721.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15217721.value: Prof Li, Haohong Prof Wei, Jin

15217721.label: Project Objectives
15217721.value: A method that is able to calibrate the multimode fiber, such as extracting the transmission matrix (TM), by merely processing the reflected signals obtained at the proximal portal of the fiber based on propagating invariant modes will be developed. In application, there is no need to interrupt the distal port of the fiber which is kept inside tissue in experiment. The obtained fiber information, such as TM, allows for online optical focusing and scanning within a full field of view that is certain distance away from the distal fiber end. Fast processing module based on field programmable gate array (FPGA) will be integrated and digital micromirror device (DMD) functioning at full speed (~23 kHz) will be used as the SLM to accelerate the calibration of the fiber (e.g., the reflection matrix and the transmission matrix) as well as its updates in experiment to overcome medium changes. An adaptive method based on dynamic mutation will be developed, which can adapt to multimode fiber perturbations, such as bending, twisting, and physiological motions, and maintain satisfactory focusing and imaging regardless of instability. The execution speed of focusing optimization and recovery will be expedited with self-customized interface via FPGA. A MMF-based wavefront shaping platform that is suitable for minimally invasive selected neuron stimulation and imaging at depths in tissue will be built and demonstrated for in vitro applications. A working depth of up to 1-2 mm into tissue, a lateral resolution of ~1 micrometer (sub-cellular), a field of view of 200 micrometers (in diameter), and a frame rate of over 10 Hz are expected. Note that the optical imaging and stimulation will be implemented simultaneously with one single multimode fiber in reflection mode. In the next phase (after this project), millisecond-order optical focusing and recovery as well as their in vivo applications in neuroscience will be sought for.

15217721.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15217721.value: Light has seen more and more applications in biomedicine. The intervention of light provides feasibility to probe or treat biological tissues at sub-cellular levels, enabling single-cell stimulation and imaging. That meets the demand of exploring brain and studying how neurons function. Current implementations of neuron stimulation and imaging, however, are limited as light is strongly scattered in tissue, resulting in trade-off between penetration depth and resolution. Existing solutions induce major trauma due to their bulky probe and are often too costly for wide applications. Therefore, developing a non-invasive or minimally invasive single neuron stimulation and imaging tool is of great significance that may significantly impact the community. Optical fiber-based platform appears attractive. With minimal invasion, optical fibers can be inserted deep into biological tissue, delivering light to regions that are otherwise optically inaccessible or spatially diffusive. Among various types of fiber, single-mode fiber needs a matching scanning module to form planar or circular imaging, graded-index fiber and fiber bundle usually have millimeter-order diameters, inducing larger invasive damages to brain tissues and probably their functions. Multimode fiber, on this aspect, is promising due to its low cost and small diameter (~100 µm), which effectively avoids interaction with major brain vessels and minimizes damage to the brain during implantation. Especially, when it is combined with wavefront shaping, single-cell resolution optical delivery and hence stimulation and imaging of selected sites within a relatively large field of view are possible. However, in operation, the distal end of the fiber is inserted in the tissue, and it is inaccessible for fiber calibration and recalibration, resulting in limited applications in biomedicine. All these have inspired this research proposal, in which we aim to develop a minimally invasive high-resolution optical stimulation and imaging platform based on reflected light from a single multimode fiber. There is no need to probe or interrupt the distal end of the fiber; the transmission matrix of the fiber is computed from the reflected optical fields from the proximal side of the fiber. Combined with adaptive wavefront shaping, online optical focusing and scanning at the inaccessible distal end of the fiber become feasible even when the fiber is perturbed. The feasibility for minimally invasive single or selective neuron stimulation and imaging at depths in tissue will be demonstrated in vitro. Whilst a lot need to be further developed, the proposed platform may open a new venue to explore deep brain. 近年來，光在生物醫學中得到了越來越廣泛的應用。光與組織之間的相互作用提供了在亞細胞水平探測或治療生物組織的可行性，從而實現單細胞光學刺激和成像，滿足探索大腦和研究神經元功能的需求。然而，這些研究的實施當前受到技術限制，源於光在生物組織中強烈散射，導致光學穿透深度和分辨率之間“魚和熊掌不可兼得”。現有的一些解決方案由於其龐大的探頭對生物組織引入額外的創傷，並且對於廣泛的應用來說通常成本太高。因此，開發一種無創或微創的單神經元光學刺激和成像工具具有重要意義，可能會對整個學科和應用領域產生重大影響。 就這方面而言，基於微米級別直徑的光纖平台顯得很有吸引力。收益於微小的侵入，光纖可以微創深入生物組織，將光傳送到自由空間光學無法進入或空間漫射的區域。在各類光纖中，單模光纖需要匹配的掃描模塊才能形成平面或圓形成像，漸變折射率光纖和光纖束的直徑通常為毫米級，對腦組織及其功能的侵入性損傷較大。相比之下，多模光纖因其低成本和小直徑（~100 µm）而很有前景，可有效避免與主要腦血管的相互作用，並最大限度地減少植入過程中對大腦的損傷。特別是當它與波前整形相結合時，單細胞分辨率的光學傳遞以及因此在相對大的視野內對選定部位的刺激和成像已經證明可行。然而，在操作時光纖的遠端插入組織中，無法進行光纖校準和重新校準，導致在生物醫學中的應用受到限制。 所有的這些都激發了此項研究計劃，其目標是開發一種基於單根多模光纖的反射式微創高分辨率光學刺激和成像平台。此項技術中，我們無需探查或干擾光纖的遠端，光纖的傳輸矩陣是從光纖近端獲得的反射光場計算出來。與自適應波前整形相結合，即使在光纖受到擾動的情況下，光纖難以接近遠端的在線光學聚焦和掃描也變得可行。我們還將在體外證明微創的精準或選擇性神經元刺激和組織深度成像的可行性。雖然很多細節需要進一步開發，擬議的研究有望開闢光學探索大腦深處的全新視角。

15217721.label: Realisation of objectives
15217721.value: The project aims to develop a reflective multimode fiber (MMF)-based wavefront shaping platform, which entails methods for reconstructing the transmission matrix (TM) for online calibration of the fiber, an adaptive MMF focusing optimization algorithm based on dynamic mutation, as well as exploring the in-vitro applications for high-resolution neuronn stimulation and imaging in deep tissues. The three major objectives of the project have been almost attained up to now, which will be elaborated as follows. For the first objective, we have approached the highly desired yet insufficiently addressed problem of MMF online calibration from multiple perspectives. In the scenario of reflection imaging, we fully exploited the propagation invariant modes (PIMs) of MMF as the physical prior, which allow the TM transformation between the real space and the mode space. The PIM representation also greatly facilitates the reconstruction of TM from the measurements of round-trip reflection matrices (RMs). The process of RM measurement was accelerated by using a digital micromirror device (DMD), which modulated the incident light to scan rapidly at the proximal facet of the fiber, with the reflective images being acquired by a camera correspondingly. Although DMD could achieve a maximum refresh rate of ~23 kHz, it maintained ~300 Hz to synchronize with the CMOS camera. By utilizing different realizations of distal reflector at the fiber end, such as a MMF segment of three different bending angles, it was possible to reconstruct the TM from three RM measurements. We proposed to solve the TM recovery problem efficiently by using a proximal gradient descent method implemented by a PC equipped with GPU and demonstrated wide-field reflection imaging through MMF based on matrix operation. Besides the explicit TM calibration, which usually takes several minutes that couldn’t meet the need of real-time application, we also propose a data-driven method for reflection-mode single-shot MMF imaging. One paper (Publication 5 in Part 8) has been published to describe the principle of training a network to learn the backward RM that matches the acquired speckle pattern at the proximal side of a MMF to the object at the distal fiber end. The trained RM could recover an image from the speckle pattern in a single shot, used for endoscopic reflection imaging for dynamic scenes with a large field of view (~540 μm in diameter). In the scenario of fluorescence imaging, a novel scheme of MMF online calibration is further developed based on the epi-detected fluorescence speckles at the proximal side of MMF. The results of fluorescence speckle demixing provided the information of speckle intensities at the positions of fluorescence targets, which were used to construct an intensity TM. Hence, selective focusing on the targets and object reconstruction could be feasible. One manuscript reporting the principle and proof-of-concept results of the fluorescence-based intensity TM is currently in preparation (Shengfu Cheng, Weibin Cai, Tianting Zhong, Haoran Li, Chi Moo Woo and Puxiang Lai, “Online focusing and endomicroscopy through a multimode fiber with fluorescence-based intensity TM”). With continuous efforts for experimental optimization and validation, this work may open new venues for robust MMF fluorescence endomicroscopy in deep tissues. For the second objective, we have developed adaptative wavefront optimization algorithms guided by dynamic mutation strategy and beyond. We previously found that in binary amplitude modulation, the error rate, which was directly related to the focusing quality, could gauge the deviation of the instant wavefront from the optimum one. A dynamic mutation algorithm based on the error rate was thus developed for adaptative focusing under disturbance. In this project, we have applied the idea of dynamic mutation to boost the performances of conventional optimization algorithms, thus developing parameter-free algorithm (PFA) and dynamic mutation-enhanced particle swam optimization, for adaptative wavefront control and focusing. Beyond that, we demonstrated the probability map-guided genetic algorithm (GA-ACO) can approach the optimal focusing efficiency through scattering media (Publication 17). We have shown that iterative wavefront shaping could be expedited by employing a customized FPGA circuit for on-board streaming data transfer and processing, with the focusing result being achieved within seconds. In the scenario of phase-only modulation, we also utilized a natural gradient ascent-based parameter optimization method for focusing light into a pattern through a 15-m-long unstable MMF, showing improved robustness and focusing contrast (Publication 1). Apart from focusing, scattered light suppression through a MMF was also achieved by the proposed alternating projection-based phase optimization method (Publication 4). For the last objective, we have built a wavefront shaping-enabled MMF endoscopy system for precise optogenetics and high-resolution imaging in deep tissues. The fiber was pre-calibrated by a four-phase-shifting coaxial holography method before being inserted into tissues. What’s more, the fiber could be re-calibrated from reflective signals once it was perturbed that caused imaging degradation. We have reported selective photoactivation to ChR2-expressing primary neurons with a minimally invasive MMF (core diameter of ~100 μm), which was confirmed by calcium imaging results using a wide-field fluorescence microscope, as shown in Publication 19 in Part 8 and the 2nd, the 3rd patents in Part 12. Besides, by equipping the system with a fluorescence epi-detection module, we also demonstrated MMF-based fluorescence imaging for various tissue samples such as 2 μm microspheres, mouse brain slice and green fluorescent 293T cells. It was characterized that the penetration depth of MMF could be centimeters, the imaging resolution was ~1.6 μm, and the field of view (FOV) was scalable to the working distance with a maximum of 500 μm in diameter. The working distance of MMF is adjustable with only a single TM calibration by complementing the TM with a defocus propagator. Still, the limited FOV of MMF makes it challenging to guide the positioning of the fiber into target neuron regions. Hence, efforts are undertaken to fabricate a side-viewing MMF which will provide an increased FOV up to millimeters towards an integrated optogenetics and imaging platform. With further engineering, our system will offer a novel solution for conducting precise optogenetics with real-time image guidance in deep brain to unravel the functions of inaccessible yet critically important neural circuits. Similarly, by equipping a photoacoustic signal detection module, MMF-based photoacoustic microscopy (Fiber-PAM) is also actively under development for high-resolution deep-tissue applications. A manuscript reporting the method and configuration of Fiber-PAM and its in-vitro tissue imaging results is in preparation (Chi Man Woo, Tianting Zhong, Chuqi Yuan, Xiaoqian Lian, Haoran Li, Shengfu Cheng, Long Jin and Puxiang Lai, "High-fidelity imaging at depths with lensless multimode fiber-based photoacoustic endomicroscopy (MMF-PAEM)". Also, a related US patent (4th item in Part 12) was most recently submitted (Puxiang Lai, Tianting Zhong, Shengfu Cheng, and Chi Man Woo, “Method and apparatus for high-fidelity lensless multimode fiber-based photoacoustic endomicroscopy”, US patent, under application). The development of MMF wavefront shaping platform have also fueled applications in speckle imaging and optical encryption (Publication 2, 6, 13, 15), MMF-based optical computing (Publication 12) and light field modulation (Publication 16), and other related deep-tissue imaging application (Publication 10, 14, 18).

15217721.label: Major findings and research outcome
15217721.value: First, we have developed reflection-mode MMF calibration methods by exploring both explicit and implicit schemes. For explicit calibration, reconstructing TM from three acquired RMs was demonstrated in the PIM representation, with reflection imaging being achieved via matrix operation. Also, deep learning was utilized to train a backward RM implicitly, capable of reflection-mode MMF endoscopic imaging in a single shot (Publication 5 in Part C). Second, we proposed a fluorescence intensity TM scheme that recovers a sub-TM by fluorescence speckle demixing, allowing selective focusing on the targets and object reconstruction. The work is confirmed by proof-of-concept results, which may offer a novel solution for MMF-based online focusing and fluorescence endoscopy. Third, we presented a non-interferometric method for retrieving the TM of a MMF merely from intensity measurements (Publication 9). Our TM retrieval method offers optimum efficiency with less running time or sampling ratio required, together with a robust setup and fast execution, which will benefit many MMF-based deep-tissue applications where interferometry is inaccessible. Fourth, we have introduced several adaptative, high-efficiency wavefront optimization algorithms. For example, the proposed GA-ACO achieved optimal focusing efficiency in experiment (Publication 17), our natural gradient ascent-based wavefront shaping achieved long-distance pattern projection through an unstable MMF (Publication 1), our alternating projection-based phase optimization realized fast and arbitrary glare suppression through MMF (Publication 4). Fifth, we have built a MMF-based wavefront shaping platform, which has demonstrated in-vitro biomedical application to precise optogenetics with minimal invasiveness (Publication 19) and high-resolution fluorescence imaging on various tissue samples. Besides that, the platform also shows non-biomedical applications to optical computing (Publication 12) and light field modulation (Publication 16). Sixth, the project has also fueled several related studies on complex photonics, including scattered imaging mechanism (Publication 7, 8), speckle imaging (Publication 6, 15) and speckle-based optical encryption (Publication 2, 13), as well as some deep-tissue imaging applications (Publication 10, 14, 18). The above findings have led to the development of several online MMF calibration and wavefront control methods for various imaging scenarios and pushed the boundary of MMF-based deep-tissue optical applications towards greater robustness and higher quality. These research outcomes, based on the MMF wavefront shaping platform, demonstrate our R & D strength and highlight its significant potential for deep-tissue optics, optical computing, communication and more.

15217721.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15217721.value: Further development of the reflective MMF wavefront shaping platform could be performed from the following aspects. First, although the proposed TM reconstruction from RM measurements in the PIM representation is feasible in principle, it is inevitably computation-intensive and challenging in engineering fabrication of the distal reflector for real application. A more practicable scheme for reflection-mode MMF re-calibration is online updating of the TM from a pre-acquired TM library based on the reflective signals and a look-up table. In the next phase, we will explore and optimize such method for millisecond-order recovery of optical focusing and imaging by online updating of the TM. Second, the proposed fluorescence-based intensity TM scheme requires experimental validation and optimization, which could be acquiring the fluorescence speckles more efficiently and optimizing the object reconstruction method in the absence of speckle correlation. Last but not least, we will fabricate a side-viewing MMF by fiber-optic micro-machining technique, which allows a much larger FOV to guide the position of the fiber into target regions for integrated neuron stimulation and imaging. In-vivo neuroimaging application in deep brain of small animals will be further explored for dynamic visualization of neurons and hemodynamics.

15217721.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15217721.value: The research project is about developing new ways of using light to see and interact with in-vitro samples and even neurons inside deep brain tissue, without causing much harm. Imagine a very thin fiber, thinner than a hair strand, that can be inserted deep into biological tissues. This fiber can carry light to places that are hard to reach. With the help of some smart technology, we can control the light so that it focuses on specific spots. This can help us see inside tissues with great detail and even stimulate neurons precisely in the brain to understand how they work. This could be very valuable for biomedical research and treatment, especially for brain-related diseases. The project aims to make this technology more precise, faster, and able to work even if the fiber is perturbed inside the biological tissues due to physiological motions. It's like developing a tiny, flexible magnifying glass that can go inside the tissues and help us learn more about how it works. To date, the project has fueled about 20 journal papers published or pending publications and 4 patents granted or pending grant. Additionally, it has successfully trained two PhD students for graduation.

15218421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15218421.value: Active flow control (AFC) has long been a hot topic due to its rich dynamics and great potential in various engineering applications. It utilizes actuators to manipulate the flow and hence has a much wider effective operation range than passive flow control. AFC can be more adaptive and efficient if sensor measurements are deployed to form closed-loop control. Classical closed-loop AFC is model-based, requiring sufficient knowledge of the dynamics of flow system. However, for complex AFC problems such as turbulence control, there are serious challenges, including high dimensionality, strong nonlinearity and multi temporal-spatial scales, which limit real-time control efforts. To address these challenges, data-driven model-free control may be a vital solution, since fluid dynamics is intrinsically a data-rich field. Hence, the fluid mechanics community believes that the booming machine-learning (ML) techniques can play an important role in AFC. Among various ML tools, reinforcement learning (RL), often referred to as deep reinforcement learning (DRL) when it adopts deep neural networks (DNNs) as function approximators, offers intriguing opportunities for tackling complex AFC problems. It optimizes decision making in interactive problems for which no solution is known a priori. Although very successful in achieving superhuman performance in games and robotics, only very limited RL applications in AFC have been reported, focusing on very simple settings. Hence, there are growing interests in pushing RL-guided AFC studies into more complex settings, i.e., three-dimensional turbulent flows that may require a large number of actuators. There are also needs in realizing RL-guided AFC in experimental environments where possible hardware delays and measurement/actuation noise should be properly handled. In this proposed research, we aim to push the existing boundaries through investigating an interesting but complex AFC problem: to mitigate or even eliminate the hydrodynamic traces of a blunt-based axisymmetric body using an array of jets. This mimics the scenario where an aquatic animal or an underwater robot is trying to hide from its predators. We will tackle this AFC problem using a state-of-the-art DRL algorithm, in both computational and experimental environments and under more challenging conditions, i.e., the flow is three-dimensional and can be turbulent, and the control is multi-input-multi-output (MIMO) and possibly with measurement/actuation noise. The success of this research will not only pave the way to efficient, robust and practical implementations of DRL guided AFC in real-world applications, but also shed some lights on the design and operation of underwater robotics to achieve hydrodynamic stealth. 主動流動控制因其具有重要的學術和工程應用價值一直以來都是研究熱點。通過激勵器改變流場，它比被動流動控制有更廣的操作範圍。如果進一步通過傳感器獲取的流場信息來進行閉環控制，它可以根據實際需要調整控制從而獲得更高的控制效率。傳統的閉環流動控制主要是基於模型實現的，需要事先對所控制流動系統動力學響應特性有足夠了解。對於高維度、強非線性及多時空尺度的複雜流動問題，例如湍流控制，基於模型的流動控制效果非常差。由於流動的流體能產生海量的速度與壓力數據，基於數據驅動的無模型控制可能是個有效解決辦法，因此學界相信正重新蓬勃發展的機器學習可以在流動控制領域發揮重要作用。在眾多的機器學習方法中，強化學習因其能在交互式問題裡快速提供最優決策可用來處理複雜流動控制問題。雖然在遊戲和機器人等領域的表現已遠超人類，目前強化學習在流動控制方面的應用非常有限且非常簡單，學界希望能在更複雜流動系統中實現基於強化學習的流動控制，並希望能在伴隨著硬件延遲和測量/激勵誤差的實驗環境中實現控制。因此，在本項目中我們致力於通過研究一有趣且複雜的流動控制問題來拓展現有的研究邊界：模擬水生動物或水下機器人獲得水動力隱身的場景，用射流陣列來減輕甚至消除一個平底回轉體尾跡里的水動力特征。對於這种可能發展為湍流的流動，我們將在數值模擬和水洞實驗兩種環境中實現基於強化學習的流動控制。本項目的成功將不僅能推動發展在真實世界中實現高效魯棒的基於強化學習的流動控制，而且能為水下機器人實現水動力隱身提供有效的設計與操作指引。

15218521.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15218521.value: Bladder cancer is one of the most common malignant tumors in the urinary system. While cystectomy is the gold standard treatment for invasive and recurred superficial high-grade bladder tumors, traditional open cystectomy remains one of the most invasive surgical procedures in urology. Clinical evidence has shown that laparoscopic cystectomy (LC) and robotic-assisted laparoscopic cystectomy (RALC) are feasible and reliable minimally invasive alternatives to open cystectomy. However, it is still a challenging task for surgeons to perform a successful LC/RALC mainly due to (1) the complicated (and patient-specific) surgical anatomy and (2) a loss of direct vision caused by the limited view of laparoscopic scenes. While some LC/RALC planning and intraoperative guidance systems have been developed, they are still incapable of sufficiently fulfilling the demanding clinical requirements. The main shortcomings include inaccurate segmentation under limited training data, imperfect visualization for comprehensive planning, and imprecise intraoperative and preoperative image registration under large deformations. More importantly, existing systems failed to seamlessly and naturally integrate human interactions into planning and intraoperative guidance procedures, resulting in that surgeons’ knowledge and experience cannot be efficiently combined with machine wisdom to enhance the preciseness and efficiency of computer-assisted LC/RALC. In this project, we shall develop a set of innovative yet efficient human-in-the-loop image segmentation, visualization, and registration algorithms to sufficiently leverage human-computer collaboration to tackle the aforementioned shortcomings. First, we shall propose a novel interactive deep learning architecture equipped with an unsupervised model to precisely segment bladder, tumor, prostate, and other relevant organs from CT volumes without using any pixel-level annotations. We shall further propose a new human-in-the-loop model tailored for vessel segmentation considering their unique yet complicated topological characteristics. Second, we shall propose a novel human-in-the-loop volume rendering algorithm via a generative adversarial network (GAN), allowing surgeons to conveniently select viewpoints and modify transfer functions to extract more useful visual information for precise planning. Third, we shall propose a new real-time registration algorithm to register preoperative models and intraoperative laparoscopic scenes for interactive intraoperative guidance. Finally, we shall integrate these techniques into a system and extensively evaluate it with our clinical collaborators. In summary, this is a joint project with a strong interdisciplinary team including experts in medical image computing, virtual/augmented reality, and LC/RALC. The proposed innovative techniques can not only strengthen LC/RALC planning and intraoperative guidance but provide insights on how to integrate human interactions into a computer-assisted surgery system to improve its preciseness and efficiency. 膀胱癌是泌尿系統最常見的惡性腫瘤之一。雖然膀胱切除術是治療侵入性和復發性淺表高級別膀胱腫瘤的金標準，傳統的開放式膀胱切除術仍然是最具侵入性的泌尿外科手術之一。臨床證據表明，腹腔鏡膀胱切除術（LC）和機器人輔助腹腔鏡膀胱切除術（RALC）是開放性膀胱切除術可行而可靠的微創替代方案。然而，迄今為止，外科醫生成功執行LC/RALC 仍是一項極具挑戰的任務。 主要原因包括（1）複雜的（和患者特異的）手術解剖結構和（2）由於腹腔鏡場景的有限視野導致的視覺信息損失。 雖然已有一些LC/RALC計劃和術中引導系統開發出來，它們仍然不能充分滿足嚴苛的臨床需求。 主要缺點包括有限訓練數據條件下不準確的分割，不完善的可視化導致不能進行全面的規劃，以及大變形下術中和術前圖像配准不精準。更重要的，現有系統未能將人機交互無縫、自然地整合到計劃和術中引導中，導致外科醫生的知識和經驗無法與機器智慧有效結合，從而提高計算機輔助 LC/RALC 的精確性和效率。 本專案中，我們將開發一套創新且高效的人機閉環互助圖像分割、可視化和配準演算法，以充分利用人機協作解決上述缺點。首先，我們將提出一個配備無監督模型的新型互動式深度學習架構，以在不使用任何圖元級標註的情況下從 CT 體數據中精確分割膀胱、腫瘤、前列腺和其他相關器官。考慮到血管獨特而複雜的拓撲特徵，我們將進一步提出一種為血管分割量身定製的人機閉環互助模型。 其次，我們將通過生成對抗網路 （GAN） 提出一種新穎的人機閉環互助體繪製演算法，使外科醫生能夠方便地選擇觀測點及修改傳遞函數，從而提取更多有用的視覺信息以進行精確規劃。 第三，我們將提出一種新的實時配準演算法來對術前模型和術中腹腔鏡場景進行配準，從而實現互動式術中指導。最後，我們會將這些技術集成到一個系統中，並與臨床醫生合作對其進行全面嚴格的評估。 總之，這是一個由強大的跨學科團隊合作的聯合專案，其中包括醫學圖像計算、虛擬/增強現實和 LC/RALC 方面的專家。 專案所提出的創新技術不僅可以加強 LC/RALC 計劃和術中指導，還可以提供關於如何將人機交互整合到計算機輔助手術系統中以提高其精確性和效率的新見解和新思路。
