15221621.label: Major findings and research outcome
15221621.value: This project is to deal with stochastic control problems with time-delay and constraints in many fields such as science, engineering, economics, management, communication networks, and especially financial investment. We mainly revisited some challenging, yet practically important wealth management models over a finite/infinite time investment horizon, reformulated them as stochastic control problems with time-delay and constraints, and derived their optimal analytical strategies. Also, we investigated the problems of when a family of stochastic nonlinear systems with large input/state delays is asymptotically stabilizable in mean square by memoryless state and/or output feedback. Although we did not project expenses for graduate student training in the original GRF proposal submitted to RGC in October 2020, our university appointed Mr. Zeng Yijie as a Research Assistant to work with us on this GRF-sponsored project GRF-sponsored 1 September 2022 – 28 February 2023. In August 2023, he become a PhD student at our university. In particular, our university committed Mr. Luo Sheng to be a PhD Student in 2022. This GRF-sponsored project supported him from September 2023 to August 2024. He will graduate from our university in August 2026. In the future, I will pay more attention to the training of research postgraduate students. During this project period, I presented an invited talk at Bridging Theory and Practice in Finance from 17 to 22 August 2025 in Hangzhou. I attended at the 9th Asian Quantitative Finance from 26 to 27 April 2025 in Shen Zhen. I participated in the 1st INFORMS Conference on Financial Engineering and FinTech from 19 to 21 August 2024 in Hong Kong. I attended at the 10th International Congress on Industrial and Applied Mathematics from 20 to 25 August 2023 in Tokyo. I presented an invited talk at Recent Advances on Quantitative Finance from 27 to 30 August 2023 in Hong Kong. I participated in SIAM Conference on Financial Mathematics and Engineering and introduced our research works in Philadelphia, USA from 6 to 9 June 2023. Also, I attended the 9th International Colloquium on BSDEs and Mean Field in Annecy, France from 26 June to 1 July 2022. Also, I served on the organizing committee of the 11th World Congress of Bachelier Finance Society and gave a talk in Hong Kong from 13 to 17 June 2022. In addition, we obtained Award in Natural Science for the Chinese Association of Automation (First Prize) on November 24, 2022.

15221621.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15221621.value: Although the research in this direction has been well developed for constrained control problems under time-delay stochastic systems, it lacks progress in both theoretical investigation and applications for standard and non-standard stochastic problems within the more general time-delay stochastic system framework, such as delayed and partially-observed stochastic differential equations. [1] Our methodologies and techniques on portfolio selection can be adopted to analyze behavioral portfolio selection, while one encounters investment problem with memory (delay) with reference to the historical consumption maximum over his/her investment time horizon. We will further develop those results established in papers 3, 9 and 14 of Part C in the future. [2] The results of Markovian regime-switching system in this project can be further developed to regime-switching LQ controls with time-delay over a finite/infinite time horizon (papers 2 and 12 in Part C). We will present the results in another project report after we complete it. [3] Reinforcement and data-driven approaches proposed in this project (papers 4, 6, 8, 11 and 15 in Part C) can be further employed to study more general stochastic control problems over a finite/infinite time horizon. We will present the results in another project report after we complete it.

15221621.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15221621.value: As for the theoretical contributions, this study will contribute to the literature on various topics such as consumption cost in portfolio selection (papers 3, 9 and 12 in Part C), mean-variance portfolio selection, fund management and agency theory (paper 9 and 13 in Part C) within the continuous-time framework. In addition, the methods adopted in the current research program will also improve optimal controls and the implementations developed in the field of stochastic control with time-delay and constraints (paper 16 in Part C) and under the regime-switching system (papers 2 and 12 in Part C). In particular, one of our findings provides a fundamental tool (paper 16 in Part C) to study a class of delayed stochastic control problems with random coefficients in the future. We also studied LQ stochastic differential games using open-loop and closed-loop Nash equilibria (paper 1 in Part C). Besides these, introducing reinforcement learning method paves the avenue for analyzing a class of optimal stochastic control problems (papers 4, 6, 8, 11 and 15 in Part C). Therefore, this project is believed to be of value and of practical importance with long-term significance, and it helps provide risk-management advice for policy makers and institutional investors.

15221821.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15221821.value: Advances in autonomous and connected vehicle technology will reshape future freight transport services. With billions of tons of goods and commodities shipped annually all over the world, a wide group of players, including large industrials, startups, and local governments, etc. are rushing to develop and deploy the autonomous transport of goods. Particularly, how to manage a fleet of autonomous trucks effectively will be one of the most pressing challenges faced by autonomous freight transport service providers. Other than labor cost reductions, the truck fleets will be revolutionized by ‘vehicle platooning’ technology that enables multiple autonomous trucks to travel close together to achieve significant fuel savings. However, these benefits will not be fully realized without careful planning. Motivated by this, we propose to develop both a static and a dynamic algorithmic framework to support the offline and real-time decision making of service providers regarding vehicle scheduling and vehicle platooning, in pursuit of cost minimization. Within each framework, optimization models and customized efficient algorithms will be developed to ensure that autonomous trucks are properly scheduled to successively fulfill multiple delivery requests within their service time windows, platoons are carefully formed to reap fuel-saving benefits, and new request information is responded to promptly. Extensive numerical experiments and case studies will be conducted to evaluate the proposed decision-making tools and to explore the impact of the platoon configuration, delivery request patterns, and other influential factors on the performance of the autonomous freight transport services. Suggestions for guidelines and measures of improvement will be provided to relevant stakeholders. This project will contribute to both theory and practice, and the achievements will be of tremendous value in promoting innovative industrial mobility. 自動駕駛和聯網車輛技術的進步將重塑未來的貨運服務。每年有數十億噸的貨物和商品運往世界各地，包括大型工業企業、初創企業和地方政府等在內的眾多參與者都在爭先恐後地開發和部署貨物的自動化運輸。如何有效管理自動駕駛卡車車隊，將是自動駕駛貨運服務提供商面臨的最緊迫挑戰之一。除了降低勞動力成本外，自動卡車車隊還將通過“車輛編隊”技術對貨運產生革命性的影響。該技術使多輛自動駕駛卡車之間保持很小的間距在一起行駛，從而顯著節省燃油。然而，如果缺乏細緻的規劃，這些效益將無法完全實現。受此啟發，我們建議開發靜態和動態算法框架，以支持服務提供商在車輛調度和車輛排隊方面的離線和實時決策，以追求成本最小化。在每個框架內，將開發優化模型和定制的高效算法，以確保自動駕駛卡車在其服務時間窗口內正確調度以連續完成多個派送需求，精心編隊以獲取節油收益，並及時響應新的需求信息。同時，我們將進行廣泛的數值實驗和案例研究，以評估提議的決策工具，並探索車排配置、派送需求模式和其他影響因素對自主貨運服務性能的影響。最后，我们將向相關利益相關者提供指導方針和改進措施的建議。該項目具有理論和實踐价值，其成果將對极大地促進創新工業運輸。

15221821.label: Realisation of objectives
15221821.value: Truck platooning has been touted as one of the most promising technologies to improve fuel efficiency thanks to the reduced air drag of the digitally connected truck’s slipstream in a trainlike convoy. The benefits of truck platooning lie in the reduced fuel consumption and labor cost, and the enhanced driving experience. However, these benefits cannot be realized without an appropriate routing, scheduling, and platooning plan of trucks subject to practical constraints. The project objectives of developing viable models and effective algorithms for autonomous-truck-based freight transport services, including both the offline and online vehicle scheduling and vehicle platooning, have been satisfactorily achieved across several journal publications and conference presentations. Specifically, following the research plan of the project, we achieve the first objective by proposing mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) models and advanced algorithms to optimize truck routing, platooning, and scheduling while considering practical constraints such as the state-and-position-dependent fuel-saving rates of platooning, trucks’ designated intermediate relays, platoon size limit, driver breaks, etc. We also develop customized algorithms including partial-MILP approach, iterated neighborhood search with tailored search operators, simulated annealing, edge set covering algorithm, etc. to handle the complexities of joint platooning and scheduling in two different contexts: the freight transportation on highway networks and the local container drayage problems. For the second objective, we further addresses the complexities of real-time vehicle scheduling and vehicle platooning problem for autonomous-truck-based freight transport service providers in a dynamic environment. Given the dynamic transportation requests, the fleet operators should dynamically schedule ATs with platooning and the speed of ATs can be adjusted to enable the dynamic formation and dissolution of platoons. We model this problem as a decentralized partially observable Markov decision process to minimize the total operation cost and introduce a notion of collaborative reward to facilitate platooning. To effectively solve the problem, we develop a fully decentralized multi-agent reinforcement learning framework, in which all individual agents learn the network with Double Deep Q-network method to improve computational efficiency. The performance of the proposed models and algorithms is thoroughly evaluated through numerical experiments using various networks and scenarios, which highlight their effectiveness compared to benchmark approaches. The study also explores the impact of many factors, such as platoon configuration, fuel-saving rates and driver schedule, on system performance, providing valuable managerial insights into the operation and management of autonomous-truck-based freight transport services. These achievements indicate a comprehensive fulfillment of the proposed project objectives.

15221821.label: Major findings and research outcome
15221821.value: Based on the provided information, the major research findings confirm the successful development of robust and efficient models and algorithms for optimizing autonomous-truck-based freight transport, achieving the project objectives. The collective outcome includes the development of viable mixed-integer linear programming models and intelligent algorithms, such as partial-MILP approach, iterated neighborhood search with tailored search operators, simulated annealing and edge set covering algorithm, which effectively solve complex vehicle scheduling and platooning problems. These models incorporate critical real-world constraints, including driver breaks, fuel savings from platooning, trucks’ intermediate relays, etc., leading to significant improvements in operational efficiency and cost reduction. Furthermore, the research has been extended to dynamic environments through a novel decentralized framework using a multi-agent reinforcement learning approach, specifically a Double Deep Q-network, which enables real-time, adaptive decision-making for scheduling and platoon formation in response to fluctuating cargo demand and traffic conditions. Comprehensive numerical experiments and sensitivity analyses have validated the superior performance of these solutions against benchmarks, providing valuable managerial insights into the impact of key factors, thereby offering practical strategies for optimizing autonomous truck fleet management in both planned and real-time operational settings.

15221821.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15221821.value: Building on our current research, there is good potential for further development in several key areas. The proposed course of action involves a multi-phase plan. A primary course of action is enhancing the realism of the models and the scalability of the algorithms. This includes integrating a broader mix of vehicle types (e.g., human-driven and autonomous trucks), incorporating more dynamic elements like real-time traffic and weather data, developing more efficient algorithms to solve large-scale problems in shorter time, and conduct pilot tests using simulation platforms that mimic real-world highway networks and even small-scale real-world trials for validation. Furthermore, the research can be expanded to broader logistics setting and problems, such as incorporating cargo consolidation and transfer shipment, synchronizing platooning and scheduling with warehouse and terminal operations for an integrated supply chain solution.

15221821.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15221821.value: Advances in autonomous and connected vehicle technology will reshape future freight transport services. This research project makes contribution to the field of autonomous freight transport by developing advanced algorithmic frameworks for the important operational challenges of vehicle scheduling and platooning with the objective to minimize costs. The project’s nature is both theoretical and applied. For theoretical impacts, the project systematically extends decision-making tools from offline planning to the challenging real-time ad-hoc environments to handle dynamic transport requests. From the practical point of view, the proposed decision-making tools will benefit the autonomous freight transport service providers, their customers, clients and the whole society. In addition, through extensive numerical experiments and case studies, it will generate actionable managerial insights and guidelines for practitioners to effectively deploy autonomous freight services. In summary, this project contributes to both theory and practice, and the achievements will be of tremendous value in promoting innovative industrial mobility in the era of autonomous vehicles.

15221921.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15221921.value: Porous asphalt (PA) with open-graded structure and large air void content is a functional pavement material, which offers various attractive benefits, such as reducing tire-pavement noise, decreasing water splashing and hydroplaning on rainy days, improving pavement surface friction, and alleviating urban heat island effects. However, as the pore structures of PA are often exposed to the moist environment, PA pavement usually has relatively short service life because of early-age moisture damage, which is mainly caused by the weakening effect of moisture diffusion on the asphalt mastic and aggregate-mastic interface, and the excessive pore-water pressure due to the coupling action of moisture and traffic load. To improve the resistance of PA to moisture damage, modification of the asphalt binder by a thermoset material, polyurethane (PU), has been found effective without compromising its functional properties. However, as a novel modification method, the fundamental interaction mechanism of PU and asphalt binder in moist environment has not been fully understood yet. To fill this gap and potentially apply PU modified porous asphalt (PUMPA) as a durable pavement material in Hong Kong, this study aims to investigate the interaction mechanism between PU and asphalt binder inside PUMPA under the combined effects of loading and water through a series of laboratory experiments and numerical simulations. A multiscale approach, which involves the investigation from the binder, to mastic and to mixture scale, will be adopted. The PU modification effect and mechanism at the binder scale will first be investigated through microscopic characterization of the physical and chemical interactions between PU and asphalt, and laboratory tests on the mechanical properties of PUMPA binder (PUMAB). Based on the enhanced understanding of the PU modification mechanism, an optimum PUMAB will be selected for characterizing the moisture-induced deterioration at both the mastic and mixture scales. Coupled chemo(binder)-physico(mastic)-mechanical(mixture) analysis will be conducted to understand the mechanism of PU modification comprehensively. Finite element models will be developed to simulate PUMPA’s performance under various loading and environmental conditions. Finally, the optimum conditions for applying PU as an asphalt modifier to produce durable PUMPA will be recommended, and guidance on the practical application of PUMPA will be developed. The outcomes of this study are expected to significantly enhance the fundamental understanding of the working mechanism of PUMPA and promote its wide application as a novel durable pavement material with multiple attractive functions, thus improving the sustainability of road networks both locally and worldwide. 具有開級配結構和大孔隙率的多孔瀝青混合料（PA）是一種功能性路面材料，具有降低輪胎路面噪音、減少雨天積水和輪胎打滑、改善路面摩擦，以及缓解城市熱島效應等多種優點。然而，由於PA的孔隙結構經常暴露在潮濕的環境中，PA路面容易發生早期水損壞，因此使用壽命通常較短。研究發現通過熱固性材料聚氨酯 (PU) 對瀝青粘合劑進行改性，可有效提高 PA 的抗水損害能力。然而，作為一種新型改性方法，聚氨酯與瀝青結合料在潮濕環境中的相互作用機制尚未完全了解。為了填補這一空白，並將 PU 改性多孔瀝青 (PUMPA) 作為一種耐久的環保型路面材料在香港應用，本研究旨在通過一系列實驗和數值模擬研究，表徵在荷載和水的共同作用下，PU 與瀝青結合料之間的相互作用機制。本研究將採用多尺度的表徵方法，首先通過PU與瀝青之間物理和化學相互作用的微觀表徵，以及PUMPA粘合劑（PUMAB）力學性能的實驗室測試，研究PU在粘合劑尺度上的改性效果和機理。基於對 PU 改性機制的深入理解，將選擇最佳 PUMAB 来表徵膠粘劑和混合物尺度上的水損害規律。基於化學（粘合劑尺度）-物理（砂漿尺度）-力學（混合物尺度）的耦合分析，以全面理解 PU 的改性機理， 並利用有限元模型来模擬 PUMPA 在各種負載和環境條件下的工程性能。最後，基於PU的改性機理，推薦應用 PU 作為瀝青改性劑生產 PUMPA 的最佳條件，並為 PUMPA 的實際應用提供指導。本研究的成果有望顯著提高對 PUMPA 工作機制的基本認識，並促進其作為兼具多種功能性及耐久性的新型路面材料的廣泛應用，從而提高本地和全球道路的可持續性發展。

15221921.label: Realisation of objectives
15221921.value: 5.3 Realisation of Objectives The project successfully achieved all five research objectives through a comprehensive multiscale approach, which involved investigation from the binder, to mastic and to mixture scale. Below is a detailed account of the realization of each objective. 1.Investigation of material modification mechanism (binder scale) The efficiency of using the developed PU-precursor based reactive modifier (PUM) in the preparation of polymer modified asphalt (PA) has been assessed, and the modification mechanism has been revealed. Petroleum asphalts of 60/70 pen grade have been modified by PUM at weight percentages of 0%, 5%, 10%, and 20%. To investigate the modification effect on asphalt material properties, including rheological properties, high - and low - temperature performance, and fatigue resistance, samples of the base asphalt and PUM - modified asphalt binders (PUMAB) have been characterized. Rotational Viscosity, Multiple Stress Creep Recovery (MSCR), Time Sweep fatigue, Bending Beam Rheometer (BBR), and Bitumen Bonding Strength tests have been conducted for the characterization. As the usage of PUM is treated as a chemical modification method, Bitumen - PUM interactions have been verified through fraction analysis, and the PUM modification mechanism has been demonstrated by Fourier - transform Infrared Spectroscopy (FTIR), Differential Scanning Calorimeter (DSC), Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM), and Fluorescence Microscope (FM). Based on these tests, the microstructure of PUMAB has been evaluated, and the chemical reactions between PUM and neat bitumen have been verified. With the enhanced understanding of the modification mechanism, the optimum composition of PUMAB has been identified, and a prototype PUMAB has been selected for the subsequent studies. 2.Investigation of material modification mechanism (binder scale) Cohesive and adhesive failures are the two major failure patterns of raveling in PA. Investigation has been conducted at mastic scale by focusing on the deterioration in bonding between aggregate and mastic (adhesion) by moisture infiltration and deterioration of mastic (cohesion) by moisture diffusion. The mastic (mixture of binder and filler) acts as a critical element in bonding the aggregates of PA, and the bonding efficiency generally determines the aggregates retention and durability. Therefore, Focusing on the two primary ravelling failure patterns in PA — cohesive and adhesive failures, the study examined the degradation of bond between aggregate and mastic (adhesion) due to moisture infiltration and the deterioration of mastic itself (cohesion) caused by moisture diffusion. 2.1 Experimental characterization: ·Characterization of Mastic - Aggregate Bonding (Adhesion) The surface energy approach was implemented to quantify the interaction at the aggregate - mastic interface. The surface energies of three types of aggregates (limestone, basalt, and granite) were measured using the universal sorption device (USD), while the surface energy of PU - modified asphalt mastic (PUMAM) was determined via the Wilhelmy Plate method. Based on the spreading pressure and specific surface area data, the surface energy components of both aggregates and PUMAM were calculated. Then, the adhesive bond energies between aggregates and mastic, as well as the cohesive bond energies of mastic in wet and dry conditions, were derived. The influence of PU modification on the free energies of aggregate - mastic adhesion was analyzed and evaluated. These results served as critical inputs and validation data for subsequent simulations. ·Characterization of Moisture Diffusion (Cohesion) Moisture sorption tests were performed using the Gravimetric Sorption Analyzer (GSA) to accelerate the characterization of moisture diffusion in asphalt mastics. The diffusion coefficients of PUMAM and unmodified mastic were obtained across two temperatures (20 °C and 60 °C) and five levels of vapor pressure. The impact of sample thickness (1, 2, and 5 mm) on moisture diffusivity was investigated, providing insights into the thickness - dependent diffusion behavior. The desorption process, which contributes to mastic erosion, was characterized through a custom - designed test setup with continuous water flow. The weight loss of moisture - conditioned mastic samples was recorded over time, quantifying the desorption - induced erosion effect. 2.2 Diffusion-mechanical modelling: ·Evaluation of Mechanical Properties and Model Development The cohesive strength of PUMAM was evaluated via direct tensile tests on dog - bone - shaped samples under both monotonic and cyclic loading. The effects of moisture conditioning on key mechanical properties (tensile strength, fracture energy, ductility, and fatigue life) were systematically assessed. A constitutive model for PUMAM was established, incorporating the experimental data on adhesion, cohesion, moisture diffusion, and mechanical performance. This model explicitly accounts for moisture diffusion - induced deterioration, enabling the prediction of mastic - scale degradation under moisture exposure. In summary, all planned experimental investigations and model developments have been completed, providing a comprehensive understanding of moisture - induced deterioration mechanisms at the mastic scale. 3.Pore-water pressure induced deterioration (mixture scale) Based on the conservation of energy and momentum, the material constitutive models and unsaturated flow models developed were fully coupled by leveraging the existing research experience. The constitutive law of PUMPA mixtures was investigated through the dynamic modulus test, which acted as a key component of the hydro - mechanical modelling. To characterise the development of pore - water pressure during the loading process, a laboratory tensiometer (with a diameter of 5 mm and length of 3.5 cm, produced by Kyowa) was employed in the mixtures. The pore - air pressure was measured using a sealed pipe connected to the PUMPA specimens; this setup drove the air from the specimens into a sensitive air pressure sensor. The schematic graph of the UCT experiment is presented in Figure 5b, and the experimental results confirmed the effectiveness of the proposed hydro - mechanical model. 4.Coupled chemo-physico-mechanical (CPM) moisture-induced damage analysis The weak form Partial Differential Equation (WPDE) based multiphysics numerical modelling method was successfully adopted to incorporate all individual models from previous research into the finite element software, Comsol Multiphysics. A 3D geometry of the PUMPA mixture was established with the aid of image processing software and then imported into Comsol for numerical analysis. Leveraging the foundations of prior research, parts of the models, including the coupling of chemo - mechanical (PU modification), physico - mechanical (moisture diffusion), and hydro - mechanical (pore - water) interactions, were successfully implemented into the WPDE - Finite Element Method (FEM) by the co - investigators (Zhang and Leng 2017, Zhang et al. 2017, 2018a, 2018b). The coupling effects and circular dependencies were efficiently resolved and evaluated through coupled WPDE simulations of moisture - induced damage multiphysics, which proved to be a breakthrough in the research of PUMPA. Based on these numerical simulations and the support from co - investigators, a coupled chemo - physico - mechanical (CPM) analysis framework was established. This framework is capable of predicting the engineering performance and service life of PUMPA in road structures under various moist environments and loading conditions. 5.Interaction mechanism analysis and application guidance development This study established a comprehensive and fundamental understanding of the durability enhancement mechanism of PUMPA. This understanding integrated factors including PU - aggregate interaction, moist diffusion characteristics, and hydro - mechanical interactions. The optimum conditions for utilizing PU as a sustainable and durable additive for PA road surfaces were identified and recommended via targeted material selection and mix design. Additionally, practical application guidance for incorporating this material into PA construction was developed, providing a valuable reference resource for highway agencies in Hong Kong and on a global scale.

15221921.label: Major findings and research outcome
15221921.value: This project successfully achieved its primary objective of understanding the multiscale chemo-physico-mechanical characteristics of polyurethane (PU) modified porous asphalt (PUMPA) for enhanced moisture damage resistance. The study employed a comprehensive multiscale approach, examining the PU modification effect from the binder scale through mastic to mixture scale. This methodology directly addressed the research gap identified in the proposal regarding the limited understanding of PU-asphalt interactions in moist environments. Through microscopic characterization of physical and chemical interactions between PU and asphalt, along with laboratory tests on mechanical properties, the research established the fundamental modification mechanisms of PU in asphalt. Based on these findings, the study characterized moisture-induced deterioration at mastic and mixture scales, and conducted coupled chemo(binder)-physico(mastic)-mechanical(mixture) analysis to comprehensively understand PU modification. The research successfully developed finite element models to simulate PUMPA's performance under various loading and environmental conditions. These findings led to the recommendation of optimum conditions for applying PU as an asphalt modifier to produce durable PUMPA, and provided guidance for the practical application of PUMPA. All research outputs directly addressed the proposal's primary objective of enhancing the fundamental understanding of PUMPA working mechanisms to promote its application as a durable pavement material with multiple functional benefits, thereby improving the sustainability of road networks. The project's key findings were published in nine peer-reviewed articles, with representative examples including "Performance characterisation..." (2022) and "Experiment and multiscale..." (2023). The former work was recognized with the Best Paper Award for "Performance and Adhesive Mechanism Characterization of Polyurethane Modified Asphalt Mixture" at an international conference, directly reflecting the project's successful achievement of its primary research objectives as outlined in the proposal. All publications acknowledged support from the RGC General Research Fund (GRF) 2021.

15221921.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15221921.value: The research has successfully developed finite element models to simulate PUMPA's performance under various loading and environmental conditions. Future development will focus on validating these models through pilot field trials in Hong Kong and refining the application guidelines for practical implementation. The project has established a strong foundation for PU-modified porous asphalt technology, which will be further developed to enhance pavement durability while maintaining the functional benefits of porous asphalt. Additionally, the research will explore the potential for expanding PU modification to other pavement types, building on the multiscale understanding achieved in this project.

15221921.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15221921.value: Porous asphalt is a special type of road surface that reduces tire noise, prevents water splashing during rain, improves road safety, and helps reduce urban heat. However, these roads often have short lifespans because water gets into their pores and damages the road structure. This research found that adding a special material called polyurethane (PU) can make porous asphalt more durable without losing its beneficial properties. The study used a detailed approach to understand how PU works with asphalt at different levels, from tiny particles to the whole road surface. By making porous asphalt last longer while maintaining its environmental and safety benefits, this research will help create more sustainable and cost-effective road surfaces for Hong Kong and beyond.

15222021.label: Project Title(Chinese)

15222021.label: Project Objectives
15222021.value: To conduct long-term monitoring of bending and hoop strains developed in diaphragm wall panels of a twin-circular 'peanut-shaped' cofferdam. The ground and structure response adjacent to the excavation will also be monitored, and a dataset will be established with these construction data, as well as the locations of soil samples and results of in situ and laboratory tests. To extend the Bayesian updating approach to assimilate multi-source measurement data, which allows subsequent refinement of prediction for the cofferdam system response. The three-dimensional cofferdam response can be represented through surrogate models established using machine learning techniques. To utilize the field data of system response and the data analytics approach to establish geotechnical correlations between soil test results and the most appropriate design parameters. The correlations will be developed with probabilistic characterisations and will be verified with data from other projects in the region.

15222021.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15222021.value: 雙環支護結構利用地下連續牆牆體之間的環作用力與彎曲剛度為基坑提供支撐，在一些工程條件下比傳統多支撐圍堰更有效率。由於此類結構所需內支撐的數量較少，在提高基坑的開挖速度的同時也會為現場機械的組裝提供更充足的操作空間。因此雙環結構被普遍應用於隧道鑽掘機 (盾構機) 工作井與接收井的施工設計中。然而此類支護結構的各項性能仍存有大量的不確定性。這其中包括在不同施工階段環變形與彎曲變形的變化，開挖引起的地面及週邊結構的位移，以及支護結構與盾構機井形狀和土體特性之間的相互作用。部分支護結構亦會在施工結束後被用作永久結構，因此有必要對其支護性能進行更為深入的研究。 本研究項目以香港的一項雙環圍堰工程為基礎，在採用傳統傳感器（如沉降儀）的同時，利用分佈式光纖傳感器來監測牆體的彎曲變形和環變形。光纖傳感器不僅能夠對盾構機工作井的全壽命週期（包括基坑的開挖、盾構機的掘進、地下結構的施工、支護的拆卸、回填）進行長期監測，也能對週邊永久牆體結構進行監測。根據不同施工階段的監測數據和岩土勘察信息，本研究將採用貝葉斯理論與機械學習方法來建立預測系統反應或預警的實時調整模型，以求用先進的現場監測技術降低岩土工程不確定性所帶來的工程風險。根據該模型所得的反饋數據及基於土工試驗的概率特徵分析，亦可對現行的設計規範和工程實踐進行對比與客觀的評價。通過全新的數據分析方法及現場監測數據， 本研究的結果將提升工程業界對多環支護結構支護性能的了解， 也有助於完善現行深基坑設計規範。

15222221.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15222221.value: 考慮雙重不確定性的逐日交通分配模型及其在交通網絡韌性分析中的應用

15222221.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15222221.value: Dr Kitthamkesorn, Songyot Prof XU, Xiangdong

15222221.label: Project Objectives
15222221.value: To develop a doubly stochastic day-to-day traffic assignment (DSD-TA) model that explicitly considers both objective and subjective uncertainty in the travelers’ dynamic route choice adjustment process by making use of recent advances in traffic equilibrium models under network uncertainty and Weibit-based route choice models without the identically distributed assumption. To extend the DSD-TA model to consider more realistic choice mechanisms by incorporating multiple user classes (e.g., risk-taking behaviors, trip purposes, and perceptions to emerging transport modes) and multiple travel choice dimensions (e.g., departure time, destination, and mode choice dimensions in addition to the route choice adjustment dimension). To develop a transportation network resilience analysis framework by encapsulating the DSD-TA model and its extensions to measure system performance throughout the lifecycle of perturbations as well as to identify vulnerable components in the transportation system to support the planning and design of resilient transportation networks. To develop solution algorithms and procedures for implementing the DSD-TA model in Objective 1, extensions of the DSD-TA model in Objective 2, and the transportation network resilience analysis framework in Objective 3 with realistic case studies in Hong Kong to demonstrate proof of concept.

15222221.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15222221.value: Transportation system is one of the important lifelines that is not only vital in providing mobility and accessibility to the efficient movement of people and goods but is also central to the functioning of modern societies. Hong Kong, as a small and densely populated city which houses 7.5 million people and 65 million visitors annually, is no exception. The transportation system in Hong Kong serves 16 million trips daily. Disruptions, particularly to the critical infrastructures, can severely damage the economic competitiveness of the city and make peoples’ daily lives difficult. Recent man-made and natural disasters, such as the two super typhoons Hato and Mangkhut in 2017, the severe signal failures of the Hong Kong metro system in 2018, and the social movement in Hong Kong in 2019, have challenged the normal functioning of the Hong Kong society. To guarantee the smooth operations of the transportation system under perturbations, resilience is being increasingly recognized as an important goal in the planning process by various government agencies. This project aims to develop a transportation network resilience analysis framework by encapsulating a doubly stochastic day-to-day traffic assignment (DSD-TA) model and its extensions to measure system performance throughout the entire lifecycle of perturbations. The potentially transformative aspect of this research lies in: (1) the development of DSD-TA model that explicitly considers two types of uncertainties in a day-to-day dynamics model: objective uncertainty due to travel time variability and subjective uncertainty due to travelers’ imperfect knowledge about the network state, and (2) the transportation network resilience analysis framework using the DSD-TA model to explicitly consider the evolution of network performance throughout the perturbation period. The proposed framework aims to provide a more comprehensive approach for planners in assessing the consequences of disruptions, identifying the critical components, and determining the recovery schedules after disruptions for the transportation system. The proposed research has the potential to gain a better understanding of the day-to-day network dynamics under both objective and subjective uncertainties and the dynamic transportation network resilience assessment with an explicit consideration of the entire lifecycle of perturbations. This new understanding of dynamic transportation network resilience will have broader impacts on improving the transportation network planning, design, and operations, and possibly help to create more robust and resilient transportation networks that are less disruptive to the society and peoples’ daily lives and its role in highly dense megacities such as Hong Kong. 交通系统为高效的客流和货物运输提供了流动性和可达性，是现代社会正常运转的生命线系统，香港也不例外。香港面积虽小，但作为一个高密度城市，容纳了高达750万人口和每年6500万访客。香港的交通系统每日需服务1600万次出行。然而，灾害事件，尤其是其对重要交通基础设施的破坏，将严重损害城市经济竞争力，并严重影响市民的日常生活。近年来，香港社会的正常运行已经受到了人为灾害和自然灾害的影响，例如2017年的超强台风天鸽和山竹，2018年的香港地铁严重信号故障和2019年的香港社会运动等。为保障交通系统在灾害干扰下的顺利运行，各政府机构已越来越多地将韧性作为一个重要的规划目标。 本项目旨在构建一个交通网络韧性分析框架，通过双重不确定性下的逐日交通分配（DSD-TA）模型及其扩展模型，度量灾害事件对交通网络性能的全周期影响。本研究的预期成果为：（1）建立一个DSD-TA模型以在逐日动态模型中显性考虑两种不确定性，即由出行时间波动带来的客观不确定性和由出行信息不完备造成的主观不确定性；（2）将DSD-TA模型应用于交通网络韧性分析，在灾害干扰的各个阶段分析交通网络性能的演化过程。本项目所提出的框架旨在为规划者提供一个更全面系统的分析工具，可用于评估灾害事件的后果，辨识交通网络中的关键组成部分，以及为灾后交通系统制定恢复计划等。 本研究有助于更好地理解交通网络在客观和主观双重不确定性下的逐日动态演变，并在动态交通网络韧性评估中明确考虑灾害全生命周期中造成的影响。对动态交通网络韧性的新理解将对交通网络规划、设计、运营的提升产生广泛影响，并有助于构建更强韧的交通网络，以减少灾害事件对社会和日常生活的影响，保障交通网络在诸如香港的高密度大城市中的生命线作用。 关键词：交通系统；平均超额出行时间；Weibit；逐日动态；网络韧性

15222321.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15222321.value: 高延性複材-鋼-混凝土組合連梁

15222321.label: Project Objectives
15222321.value: To develop a rational and accurate cyclic stress-strain model for the concrete in the proposed FRP-steel-concrete coupling beams (FSC-CBs); To investigate the hysteretic flexural and shear properties of FSC-CBs; To develop theoretical models and a design procedure for FSC-CBs under reversed cyclic loadings.

To investigate the hysteretic flexural and shear properties of FSC-CBs;
To develop theoretical models and a design procedure for FSC-CBs under reversed cyclic loadings.

15222321.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15222321.value: Coupled shear walls are a common type of lateral force-resisting systems for high-rise buildings. The coupling beams in a coupled shear wall should have sufficiently large flexural stiffness and shear strength to ensure effective coupling action between the wall piers, while have sufficient ductility for dissipation of seismic energy during an earthquake. This project is proposed to develop a novel form of ductile coupling beams consisting of a fibre-reinforced polymer (FRP) confining tube and a concrete-encased steel I-section, which are termed herein FRP-steel-concrete coupling beams (FSC-CBs). FSC-CBs are proposed to have an innovative truncated elliptical cross-section, which leads to not only effective confinement to the concrete, but also sufficiently large flexural stiffness and shear strength. FSC-CBs can be made using a prefabricated FRP tube as the form for casting concrete, while the FRP tube with a truncated elliptical shape can be manufactured via a filament-winding process. Due to the presence of the FRP confining tube with fibres close to the transverse direction, the common failure modes of existing forms of coupling beams, including concrete spalling, steel buckling and shear failure, can be largely suppressed in FSC-CBs, leading to highly ductile structural performance. Furthermore, as the FRP tube is not used as longitudinal reinforcement, it can be relatively thin with a minimal material cost, and does not need to be anchored into the wall piers. As a result, existing forms of beam-wall connections of steel-concrete composite beams can be applied, with little change to the construction practice. This project aims to develop a reliable design procedure for the FSC-CBs by addressing the following fundamental issues: (1) the confinement mechanism of the concrete in FSC-CBs; (2) the effect of shear-flexure interaction on the flexural and shear properties of FSC-CBs; (3) the reversed cyclic behaviour of FSC-CBs. The success of this project will pave the way towards wide applications of the ductile, durable and economical novel coupling beams, and will significantly advance the theory of hybrid FRP-steel-concrete structural members in general. The knowledge to be developed in this project will also allow the section form of FSC-CBs to be used for other structural applications especially where the ductility and/or durability demands are high (e.g. for high seismicity region and/or coastal environments). The project will thus meet a very important socio-economic need in Hong Kong, the rest of China and beyond for development of safe and sustainable civil infrastructure. 聯肢剪力牆是高層建築中一種常見的抗側力結構體系。在聯肢剪力牆中，連梁需要具有足夠的抗彎剛度和抗剪強度以保證牆肢間的耦合作用，且需要具有足夠的延性以在地震發生時發揮耗能作用。本項目旨在研發一種新型的高延性複材-鋼-混凝土組合連梁（簡稱FSC-CB）。該新型連梁的截面形狀為截頂橢圓形，由複材約束外管以及內填的工字型鋼增強混凝土組成。FSC-CB可通過在一個截頂橢圓形复材管中澆築型鋼混凝土建造，而截頂橢圓形复材管可通過纖維纏繞的方式製作。复材外管中主要包含接近環向的纖維，為內部的型鋼混凝土提供約束並增強連梁的抗剪能力，可有效避免傳統連梁中混凝土剝落、鋼材屈曲等常見的破壞模態。在FSC-CB中，由於復材外管並不作為縱向增強材料使用，故其厚度可以較薄而成本較低。同理，FSC-CB中的複材外管不需要在牆肢中錨固，故採用該新型連梁時，可以套用現有鋼-混凝土組合連梁的梁-牆節點形式而不增加施工難度。本項目將重點研究以下基本問題以建立針對FSC-CB的可靠設計方法：（1）FSC-CB中約束混凝土的機理；（2）彎-剪耦合作用對FSC-CB抗彎和抗剪性能的影響；（3）循環往復荷載下FSC-CB的力學性能。本項目不僅將為該新型高延性組合連梁的工程應用打下基礎，也將進一步發展複材-鋼-混凝土結構的設計理論，從而推進可持續土木工程結構在香港及更大範圍的應用。

15222421.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15222421.value: 拉格朗日-歐拉框架下噴霧模擬中的液滴碰撞理論和模型研究

15222421.label: Project Objectives
15222421.value: Theory: deriving a spray equation by using the Liouville approach, with focus on modelling droplet collision source term based on the two-droplet statistics. Specifically, (1) A general phase space will be considered to derive the proposed spray equation, (2) Bogolyubov’s multiple-scale analysis will be modified to deal with scale interaction, (3) “Molecular chaos” assumption will be examined to derive a correction function, (4) “Homogeneity” assumption will be examined to derive a correction function. Experiment: improving and parametrizing the regime nomogram in the We-B-Δ-Oh space for modelling the droplet collision transition probability function. Specifically, (1) to complement the literature data for a comprehensive We-B-∆-Oh regime nomogram, and to focus on enhancing the accuracy of regime boundaries. The ranges of collisional parameters are We=O(1-100), 0≤B≤1, 1≤∆≤7, and Oh=O(0.001-0.01), (2) to obtain accurate time scales from the high-speed imaging, and to develop multiple time-scale relaxation models to account for the “non-instantaneous” collision outcomes, (3) to parameterize the We-B-∆-Oh regime nomogram by physics-based fitting of the transition boundaries of regimes in We-B subspace according to tabulated ∆ and Oh. Computation: establishing a computational algorithm of the derived spray equation in the form of discrete DDF and implementing it in KIVA. Specifically, (1) to establish a conditional-expectation-based computational algorithm for droplet collision models by mainly following the approach of Hylkema and Villedieu, (2) to establish a grid-independent Lagrangian simulation in KIVA by following Subramaniam’s suggestions, (3) to test the proposed computation framework by simulating some simple sprays, for which experimental data are available in the literature.

15222621.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15222621.value: 面向车联网的机会式联邦学习

15222621.label: Project Objectives
15222621.value: Establish a novel opportunistic federated learning (OFL) architecture in vehicular environment that comprised of vehicle workers, RSEs and AS, who work together toward efficient model training with secure aggregation and straggler tolerance over opportunistic IoV communication; Develop an adaptive split learning method that can dynamically select part of the neural network layers and offload the gradients computing tasks to neighboring vehicles via the opportunistic V2V contacts; Design robust link connectivity management scheme that can improve the opportunistic channel access performance to support efficient FL data exchange, and propose a coded caching scheme that utilize RSEs to broadcast the aggregated model to vehicles to boost the FL training process; Develop a proof-of-concept prototype to systematically evaluate the proposed theories and algorithms.

15222621.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15222621.value: Federated learning (FL) can help vehicular users to collaboratively train machine learning models without transmitting private user data to the central server, which is essential to apply artificial intelligence (AI) techniques in emerging automotive applications, e.g., intelligent transportation, autonomous vehicles, etc. In this proposal, we construct a brand-new opportunistic FL (OFL) framework that extend current FL paradigm over Internet of vehicles (IoV) where the distributed workers are of high mobility and have inherent opportunistic vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) and vehicle-to-roadside (V2R) interactions. To enable effective and secure model training by large-scale vehicular users, there comes the following challenges for state-of-the-art FL frameworks. First, the highly dynamic nature of IoV introduce the limited availability of vehicular workers, which may have heterogeneous and varying bandwidth and computing resources, making the training process difficult to converge. And secondly, vehicles are willing to offload the transmission loads from cellular networks to cost-effective V2R communication for gradients uploading and aggregated model downloading. Such that the collection of gradients from large-scale vehicle workers entails high risks of privacy leakage, e.g., reconstruction user data from neural network parameters, as they may communicate with multiple parties during the training phase. In addition, current IoV protocols are inefficient in transmitting FL data, especially for the opportunistic network access via V2V and V2R contacts. To deal with the above challenges, we design a hierarchical architecture and refine the distributed learning process among vehicles, roadside edges (RSE) and the aggregation server (AS) over the IoV with enhanced connectivity management. We first design a hierarchical gradient coding scheme for secure aggregation and straggler tolerance utilizing the opportunistic V2V and V2R communication. Then we design optimization algorithms to split the training process of FL rounds into separated parts and offload the gradient computation tasks to opportunistic idle neighbors via the V2V communication. After that, we will design enhanced IoV connectivity management dedicating for the gradients collection and aggregated model dissemination via the opportunistic V2V and V2R channel access in vehicular conditions, which is compatible with most state-of-the-art IoV platforms. Finally, we will conduct systematic study on a proof-of-concept prototype to demonstrate the feasibility and validity of the proposed theoretical analysis. The proposal contributes to an effective FL framework over Internet of vehicles that is necessary to enable AI techniques in a variety of smart vehicular applications, which can greatly improve the road safety and efficiency, and thus bring great welfare to our society. 车辆用户可以通过联邦学习模式进行合作训练机器学习模型且无需传输敏感的用户数据，因而能够有效促进人工智能在车载环境中的应用。本项目研究一种新型的机会式联邦学习框架，能够挖掘移动车辆间以及车、路间的机会式通信资源，优化参数聚合和模型分发，提高模型训练性能。 当前的联邦学习模式依赖于传统稳定的通信模式，在面向大规模车辆用户时会面临以下挑战。首先，受其高速移动的特性，车联网用户的可连接性有限，且异构分布的带宽和算力容量会导致模型收敛困难。其次，当车辆用户将联邦学习数据传输任务从蜂窝网卸载到车路通信通道时，模型参数的传递须经由分布广泛的路边节点，从而容易导致隐私泄露问题，如攻击者可以通过泄露的梯度信息重建用户数据等。此外，目前的车联网通信协议没有针对联邦学习任务优化，尤其是在机会式网络接入条件下会降低参数交换成功率，从而影响联邦学习训练效率。 为克服以上挑战，本项目设计一种层级式的学习架构，能够优化包含车、路、云三级体系的分布式训练进程，提高模型训练效率和安全性。我们首先设计了一种分级梯度编码方式，能够加密聚合过程中的梯度信息并有效克服车辆用户可连接性受限的缺陷。其次，我们设计了一种基于分割学习的计算任务卸载机制，能够将部分梯度计算通过机会式数据通道分流到邻近的空闲用户，从而优化本地训练进程。此外，本项目还设计面向联邦学习传输任务的专用链路管理机制，能够有效利用机会式通信带宽资源并进一步加速模型训练进程。最后，我们还将设计一个原型验证系统，评估所提框架的可行性和算法性能。 本项目能够为人工智能在车联网环境下落地提供坚实的基础，能够满足未来智能车载应用的需求，从而提高道路安全和交通效率，促进智能化社会发展。

15223221.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15223221.value: Inorganic sulfate plays a key role in the formation and growth of aerosol particles and cloud droplets in the lower atmosphere, and is closely related to environmental issues such as climate change, air pollution, and acid rain. Production of sulfate could take place through a variety of pathways, contributing to the difficulties of making climate and air pollution policy. Previous modeling studies have proposed hypohalous acids, especially HOBr, to contribute significantly to sulfate production in the marine boundary layer, and recently supported by sulfate oxygen isotopic composition measurements made by the PI and co-workers. Further, based on model simulations, the PI and co-workers found this sulfate production mechanism in turn represents a large sink of tropospheric reactive bromine. Reactive bromine is critical for the removal of ozone, an important greenhouse gas and oxidant in the troposphere, and oxidation of mercury, a harmful chemical species for the ecosystem and human health. Thus, understanding sulfate production via the HOBr pathway has implications for many aspects of tropospheric chemistry, air quality, and climate. The importance of sulfate production via the HOBr pathway is poorly constrained, largely due to the difficulties in making HOBr observations and the fact that rate constant of the HOBr + HSO3− reaction has not been measured. The primary objective of this research proposal is to quantify the contribution of HOBr to sulfate formation and the impacts of this mechanism on the reactive bromine budget in the marine boundary layer. To accomplish this, we propose a coupled laboratory and modeling approach. The rate constant of the HOBr + HSO3− reaction will be determined in laboratory experiments. Then, this measured reaction rate constant will be used in the GEOS-Chem global chemical transport model to investigate the impacts of the HOBr + HSO3− reaction on tropospheric sulfate and reactive bromine budgets. Finally, we will make laboratory measurements of oxygen isotopic composition of sulfate collected in a recent field campaign at coastal Hong Kong. In combination of the observed reactive bromine and other oxidants in that field campaign as well as modeling, we will investigate the atmospheric implications of sulfate production via HOBr oxidation in a comprehensive manner. 硫酸盐在气溶胶颗粒物和云滴的生成与增长过程中扮演十分关键的角色，且与气候变化、空气污染和酸雨等环境问题密切相关。而大气中硫酸盐的生成涉及到许多反应途径，从而给制定气候变化与空气污染政策增加了难度。过去的数值模拟研究提出次溴酸(HOBr)对海洋大气边界层的硫酸盐生成有显著的贡献。项目主持人及同行最近发表的气溶胶硫酸盐氧同位素数据也支持这一观点。此外，项目主持人及同行通过模拟发现该硫酸盐产生机制可能会大量消耗对流层中的活性溴。活性溴对对流层臭氧的去除以及汞的氧化至关重要。其中，对流层臭氧是重要的温室气体和大气氧化剂，而汞是影响生态系统和人类健康的有害化学物质。因此，研究HOBr生成硫酸盐这一反应途径对了解对流层化学、空气质量和气候都有重要意义。我们对HOBr生成硫酸盐这一反应途径的了解依然十分有限。大气中HOBr浓度的观察数据十分稀缺，其与亚硫酸氢根离子的反应速率常数尚未在实验室中测量。本项目将结合实验与模拟的方法探讨HOBr生成硫酸盐这一反应途径对海洋大气边界层硫酸盐生成及活性溴消耗的贡献。我们将通过实验测量HOBr与亚硫酸氢根离子反应的速率常数。然后把该反应速率常数应用到 GEOS-Chem全球大气化学传输模型中，用于研究该反应对对流层化学的影响。同时，我们将测量真实大气气溶胶中硫酸盐的氧同位素组分，结合活性溴的外场观测数据，探讨HOBr 对硫酸盐生成的贡献。

15223421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15223421.value: This project is to study the effects of optical-phase-modulation (OPM) amplification associated with a high-finesse hollow-core-fibre (HCF) Fabry-Perot cavity and use them to enhance the sensitivity of HCF gas sensors based on photothermal interferometry (PTI). HCF gas sensors based on PTI in the near infrared (IR) have demonstrated remarkable performance. For strong absorbers in the near-IR such as acetylene, limit of detection (LOD) down to parts-per-billion (ppb) or lower has been achieved. However, for weaker absorbers in the near-IR such as CO, the LOD is on the level of 10 parts-per-million (ppm). Such a level of performance is insufficient for precision applications such as exhaled gas analysis for medical diagnosis, which requires LOD down to ppb or sub-ppb. Fabry-Perot cavities have been widely used in laser spectroscopy to enhance the effective absorption pathlength. Here we are interested in the OPM amplification effects of a high-finesse Fabry-Perot cavity. If a single-frequency laser is locked to the center of a cavity resonance, due to resonant light recirculation, a small modulation of the cavity length (baseline OPM) is transformed to a greater (amplified) OPM in the transmitted laser beam. The amplification factor is proportional to the cavity finesse. The reflected laser beam from the Fabry-Perot also experiences OPM amplification due to a combination of two effects: light recirculation and dark fringe (destructive interference) effects. If the intensities of interference beams are made approximately equal, then the amplification due to dark fringe effect can be very large. These amplification effects were favorably exploited in the LIGO interferometers for detecting gravitational waves. They could in principle be exploited to improve the sensitivity of phase-modulation-based fibre-optic sensors, in which the employment of fibre-based technologies enables more flexible systems with lower cost. However, there is no report on this to the best of our knowledge. We propose here to study the effects of OPM amplification in the context of HCF gas sensors based on PTI. Pump absorption of gas molecules in a gas-filled HCF generates OPM for a probe beam propagating through the HCF (photothermal effect), which results in an amplified OPM in the transmitted/reflected probe beam of the Fabry-Perot cavity made with the HCF. By detecting the amplified OPM interferometrically, more sensitive gas sensors can be developed. We plan to model the OPM amplification, design and fabricate high-finesse HCF Fabry-Perot gas cells, conduct gas detection experiments and evaluate sensitivity enhancement over conventional HCF-PTI gas sensors. 該專案旨在研究與高精密空心芯纖維（HCF）法布里-佩羅腔相關的光學相調製（OPM）放大效果，並利用它們提高基於光熱干涉測量（PTI）的HCF氣體感測器的靈敏度。 基於近紅外（IR）PTI的HCF氣體感測器已顯示出出色的性能。對於近 IR 波段吸较强的氣體（如乙烯），已實現了十億分之一 （ppb） 或更低的檢測下限（LOD）。然而，對於近 IR吸收較弱的氣體（如 CO），LOD 處於百萬分之 10（ppm）的水準。這種性能水準不足以用於精確應用，例如用於醫療診斷的呼出氣體分析，這需要LOD下降到ppb或更小。 法布里-佩羅特腔已廣泛應用於雷射光譜學，以提高有效吸收路徑長。在這裡，我們感興趣的是高精細法布里-佩羅腔的OPM放大效果。如果單頻激光鎖定在腔共振的中心，由於共振光的再迴圈，空腔長度（基線 OPM）的小調製在傳輸的鐳射束中轉換為更大的（放大的）OPM。放大因數與腔的銳度成正比。來自法布里-佩羅特腔的反射鐳射束也經歷了 OPM 放大，因為兩種效應的組合：光再迴圈和暗條紋（破壞性干擾）效應。如果干擾束的強度大致相等，則由於暗條紋效應而放大的程度可能非常大。這些放大效應在LIGO干涉儀中得到了有利的利用，用於探測引力波。原則上，可以利用它們來改進基於相位調製的光纖感測器的靈敏度，在這種感測器中，採用基於光纖的技術可以以更低的成本提供更靈活的系統。然而，據我們所知，目前還沒有關於此事的報告。 我們在這裡提出研究基於 PTI 的 HCF 氣體感測器背景下 OPM 放大的影響。充滿氣體的HCF中氣體分子的泵吸收產生OPM，用於通過HCF（光熱效應）傳播的探針光束，從而在用HCF製造的法布里-佩羅特腔的傳輸/反射探針光束中產生放大的OPM。通過以干涉方式檢測放大的 OPM，可以開發更靈敏的氣體感測器。 我們計劃對 OPM 放大、設計和製造高精細 HCF法布里-佩羅特腔氣體池進行建模，進行氣體檢測實驗，並評估對傳統 HCF-PTI 氣體感測器的靈敏度增強。

15224121.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15224121.value: 由於蓬勃發展的加密貨幣產業（例如分布式金融），區塊鏈分布式應用在越來越多支持智能合約的區塊鏈上普及。現有大約20種公共區塊鏈支持各種各樣的分布式應用。另外，分布式金融在區塊鏈上包含了113.1億美元的資產並導致了區塊鏈上的海量交易。 分布式應用的後端是運行在區塊鏈上的智能合約，其前端通過遠程方法調用來讓用戶調用後端的智能合約。因此，分布式應用有更大的攻擊面，包括鏈下的客戶端和鏈上的後端。這幾年發生了許多針對在不同區塊鏈平台的分布式應用的攻擊，導致了嚴重的經濟損失。然後，尚未有系統化的對運行在主流區塊鏈平台上的分布式應用的安全研究。現在的研究主要集中於以太坊智能合約安全，沒有考慮鏈下的客戶端和遠程方法調用服務。此外，現有的針對以太坊的研究無法直接用於其他區塊鏈平台因為它們具有不同的智能合約運行環境和二進制編碼方法。 在這個項目中，我們將首次對跨平台的分布式應用的安全進行系統性的研究。我們的研究是基於如下兩點觀察：（1）越來越多區塊鏈平台採用WASM運行環境來取代現有的智能合約運行環境（2）因為鏈下前端通過遠程方法調用來連接區塊鏈平台，鏈下前端的開發是獨立於區塊鏈平台。我們將提出新的方法來研究分布式應用的前端，包括鏈下的客戶端，遠程方法調用服務以及它們的網絡流量。我們將研發統一的方法來研究跨平台分布式應用的後端，包括它們的智能合約和交易。最後，我們將利用研發的技術來分析分布式應用詐騙並尋找分布式金融應用的漏洞，因為它們在主流區塊鏈平台上大量存在卻沒有自動分析方法來研究它們。

15224421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15224421.value: 該項目將在資源受限的邊緣設備上開發一種新穎的基於拆分學習的協作訓練框架。我們提出生成相互學習的概念，使用知識遷移設計了一種新穎的協作訓練策略，目標是在邊緣設備端和邊緣服務器之間實現高通信效率並避免隱私洩漏。為了解決動態環境中的有效推理，我們引入了一種靈活的局部推理-全局驗證機制，該機制可以實現局部模型快速推理和全局模型準確推理的權衡。為了適應異構邊緣環境，我們進一步研究為每個客戶定制模型拆分策略以優化推理質量（即準確性和延遲）。最後，我們將開發一個原型系統來評估該協作學習框架。我們提出的研究將使眾多邊緣設備能夠以高效通信和保護隱私的方式協同訓練模型，將展現巨大的技術優勢最終實現無處不在的邊緣智能，比如智慧城市、工業4.0和自動駕駛汽車等眾多領域。

15224421.label: Realisation of objectives
15224421.value: The overall objectives of this project have been successfully achieved through the design, theoretical development, and practical implementation of innovative collaborative learning, edge intelligence, and decentralized network frameworks. The project addressed key challenges in communication efficiency, privacy preservation, collaborative inference acceleration, adaptive computation layer design, and real-world system deployment. Four major research outputs were produced, each corresponding to one project objective, and all have been published in top-tier IEEE/ACM journals. The following summarizes how each objective has been realized and to what extent the goals have been accomplished. Objective 1: Design a novel communication-efficient and privacy-preserving collaborative learning framework with generative mutual knowledge transfer. We proposed an optimized sparse response mechanism that significantly improves communication efficiency and privacy preservation in federated learning environments. By introducing a differential privacy–based sparse update strategy and a noise optimization algorithm, the method reduces redundant gradient transmission and maintains high model accuracy. This framework enables secure and efficient mutual knowledge transfer among distributed clients, effectively achieving the dual goals of communication efficiency and privacy protection in collaborative learning. Objective 2: Design a flexible local inference method that can significantly enhance the speed of collaborative inference while retaining the accuracy with global verification. We developed a hierarchical tree-structured coordination model that organizes multiple clients into a communication-efficient topology for parallel training and local inference. Through adaptive aggregation and dynamic synchronization, the method achieves substantial acceleration in distributed training and inference while preserving global accuracy. The approach supports flexible local decision-making with centralized global verification, providing both scalability and consistency across collaborative edge networks. Objective 3: Develop a splitting-layer customization method by solving a complex optimization problem on straggler tolerance in training and quality of inference in terms of accuracy and latency. We formulated a novel optimization model jointly considering data freshness (Age of Information) and service delay in digital-twin-enabled mobile edge networks. By designing approximation and heuristic algorithms for update scheduling and application placement, the framework dynamically customizes computation-splitting layers between IoT devices and edge servers. This method achieves optimal trade-offs between inference accuracy and latency while maintaining robustness against straggler nodes, thereby improving the quality and responsiveness of edge-intelligence services. Objective 4: Implement the proposed framework and deploy it in a prototype edge network, over which we shall verify and evaluate our proposed theory, mechanism, and algorithms. A prototype system was built and deployed on a blockchain-based edge network. The system integrates distributed key generation, multi-committee verification, and chameleon-hash-based identity revocation to ensure decentralization, security, and efficiency. Experimental evaluations demonstrated that FutureDID achieves strong resistance to single points of failure and at least a 60× improvement in identity revocation efficiency compared to existing schemes. These results validate the theoretical models and confirm the effectiveness and practicality of the proposed mechanisms in real-world environments.

15224421.label: Major findings and research outcome
15224421.value: The project has produced a series of significant theoretical and practical contributions to the fields of federated learning, collaborative inference, mobile edge intelligence, and decentralized identity management. Through the systematic completion of all four objectives, the project has advanced the state of the art in communication-efficient privacy-preserving learning, adaptive computation strategies, and real-world prototype implementation. The major findings and outcomes are summarized as follows: 1. Enhanced Communication Efficiency and Privacy in Federated Learning. A novel Optimized Sparse Response Mechanism was developed to achieve differential privacy in federated learning while reducing communication overhead. The mechanism balances privacy protection and model utility through adaptive noise calibration and sparse gradient updates, enabling efficient and privacy-preserving knowledge sharing among distributed clients. 2. Accelerated Multi-Client Collaborative Inference with Global Consistency. The project introduced Tree Learning, a scalable coordination framework that organizes distributed clients in a hierarchical topology. This approach accelerates training and inference through local computation and selective synchronization, achieving up to several-fold speed improvements without compromising global model accuracy or consistency. 3. Optimization of Edge Intelligence through Digital Twin–Empowered MEC Systems. A new Age of Information (AoI)-aware optimization model was formulated to enhance real-time responsiveness in mobile edge computing. The developed approximation and heuristic algorithms jointly optimize update scheduling and resource allocation, achieving superior balance between inference accuracy, latency, and system robustness against straggler nodes. 4. Deployment and Validation of a Fully Decentralized Identity System. The project successfully implemented FutureDID, a blockchain-based decentralized identity framework featuring multi-party credential issuance, mutual verification, and efficient revocation via chameleon hash functions. Experimental evaluation demonstrated at least a 60× improvement in revocation efficiency and strong resilience against single points of failure, validating the feasibility and scalability of the proposed theories and algorithms. Finally, we have produced several high-quality publications based on these findings. One focuses on an optimized sparse response mechanism that enhances privacy and communication efficiency in federated learning, while another introduces a hierarchical coordination framework that accelerates collaborative inference with global consistency. A third contribution develops an AoI-aware optimization model for digital twin–empowered edge intelligence, and the final work implements a fully decentralized identity system with multi-party verification and efficient revocation. Together, these studies demonstrate consistent performance improvements across diverse distributed learning and edge computing environments, laying a solid foundation for building more secure, scalable, and deployable collaborative intelligence systems.

15224421.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15224421.value: The research outcomes of this project open several promising directions for future development. Building upon the theoretical foundations and prototype implementations achieved, the next phase of work will aim to extend the developed frameworks toward large-scale, real-world deployments and cross-domain generalization. First, in federated and collaborative learning, future research will explore adaptive model compression and communication scheduling strategies guided by reinforcement learning, enabling dynamic resource allocation and better scalability in heterogeneous networks. Integrating generative AI techniques can further enhance mutual knowledge transfer and privacy-preserving synthetic data generation. Second, in edge intelligence and digital twin systems, the proposed AoI-aware optimization framework will be expanded to support multi-modal sensing data, decentralized orchestration, and self-evolving digital twins for complex IoT environments. This can significantly improve real-time decision-making and reliability in smart cities, industrial IoT, and autonomous systems. Third, for decentralized identity management, future work will integrate the FutureDID framework with federated learning environments to build trustworthy federated identity systems, ensuring secure authentication and verifiable model provenance. Research will also investigate lightweight cryptographic primitives and interoperability across different blockchain infrastructures to enhance deployment efficiency. Finally, collaborations with industry partners will be pursued to translate the research outcomes into practical applications, such as secure edge-cloud collaboration platforms, privacy-preserving data marketplaces, and large-scale IoT service infrastructures. These developments will further consolidate the project’s impact and lay the groundwork for next-generation trustworthy, decentralized, and intelligent computing ecosystems.

15224421.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15224421.value: This project focuses on developing smarter and safer ways for computers and devices to learn and work together without exposing private data. In today’s world, where phones, sensors, and smart machines constantly collect information, sending all this data to a central server can cause privacy risks and delays. Our research created new methods that allow these devices to learn collaboratively while keeping their data private and reducing communication costs. We also designed techniques that help them make faster and more accurate decisions by sharing only essential information. In addition, we built a digital twin system, which creates virtual models of real-world devices to improve the freshness and reliability of information in Internet-of-Things networks. Finally, we implemented a fully decentralized identity system that ensures trust, fairness, and security using blockchain technology. Together, these innovations make intelligent systems more efficient, privacy-preserving, and trustworthy. The outcomes will benefit future applications such as smart cities, healthcare, and edge computing, where secure and efficient collaboration among many connected devices is essential.

15224521.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15224521.value: Distributed Optical Fiber Sensing(DOFS) are currently applied in numerous Scientific and Engineering disciplines ranging from civil engineering, biomedical devices, aerospace to railway and is playing an ever-increasing role. When light signals is transmitted along a fiber, minute mechanical and/or temperature disturbance somewhere along the fiber create significant changes in the forward and back-scattered light through Rayleigh, Brillouin and Raman scattering. Various DOFS techniques based on these effects demonstrated excellent capabilities in locating temperature/strain disturbances over a range of 100 km. The sensing range, spatial resolution, temperature/strain sensitivity and measurement time are fundamental metrics that depend on optical component hardware and associated signal processing techniques. In a parallel development, coherent detection and digital signal processing(DSP), or digital coherent systems, enable the arbitrary generation, detection and processing of polarization multiplexed optical signals and became the defining technology for current optical communications. Information are encoded in phase, amplitude, polarization, wavelength and spatial modes of an optical carrier to maximize spectral efficiencies. Over the past decade, the performance, cost and form factor have improved dramatically and this new framework of digital coherent systems become a set of powerful tools that have started to form a foothold in optical fiber sensing as well. Nonetheless, the applications of digital coherent systems to DOFS are still at its infancy stage and much remains to be investigated to elucidate the full potentials of DOFS using state-of-the-art optical transceivers and DSP and how such advanced DOFS can enable new sensing applications. The objectives of the proposed research are to characterize the theoretical limits of various DOFS with digital coherent systems and conduct state-of-the-art experiments to realize their potentials. In particular, we will 1)statistically characterize the performance limits of SBS-based and forward-transmission based DOFS with arbitrary waveform generation and DSP; 2)conduct improved OFDR, BOTDA and forward-transmission DOFS experiments with high bandwidth signaling and DSP 3)conduct proof-of-concept real-time traffic monitoring and diagnosis experiments using BOTDA and DSP on a deployed optical fiber loop that passes through densely populated areas around Hong Kong. The successful completion of the proposed research will clearly lay down the theoretical limits of DOFS with digital coherent systems and the proposed experiments will be record-breaking demonstrations that illustrate their potentials. The research outcomes will advance DOFS to a higher level of performance and open up new applications of optical sensing in various disciplines of Science and Engineering. 分布式光纤传感 (DOFS) 应用于众多科学和工程学科，从土木工程、生物医学设备、航空航天到铁路，并且发挥着越来越大的作用。当光信号沿光纤传输时，沿光纤某处的微小机械和/或温度扰动会通过光纤中的瑞利、布里渊和拉曼散射在前向和后向散射光中产生显着变化。基于这些效应的各种 DOFS 技术已经证明了在 100 公里范围内定位温度/应变扰动的出色能力。传感范围、空间分辨率、应变/温度灵敏度和测量时间是取决于光学组件硬件和相关信号处理技术的基本指标。同时，相干检测和数字信号处理（DSP）或数字相干系统使偏振复用光信号的任意生成、检测和处理成为可能，成为当前光通信的定义技术。信息以光载波的相位、幅度、偏振、波长和空间模式进行编码，以最大限度地提高光谱效率。在过去的十年中，性能、成本和外形尺寸都得到了显着改善，数字相干系统已经超越了传统的长距离通信，进入了数据中心短距离系统。这个新框架和一套强大的工具也开始在光纤传感领域立足。尽管如此，数字相干系统在 DOFS 中的应用仍处于起步阶段，还有很多需要研究以阐明使用最先进的光收发器和 DSP 的 DOFS 的全部潜力，以及这种先进的 DOFS 如何实现新的传感应用程序。 拟议研究的目标是用数字相干系统表征各种 DOFS 的理论极限，并进行最先进的实验以实现其潜力。我们将 1) 统计表征 BOTDA 和具有任意波形生成和 DSP 的前向传输 DOFS 的性能限制； 2) 使用高带宽信令和 DSP 进行改进的 OFDR、BOTDA 和前向传输 DOFS 实验 拟议研究的成功完成将明确规定 DOFS 与数字相干系统的理论限制，拟议的实验将是展示其潜力的破纪录演示。研究成果将把 DOFS 性能提升到一个新的水平，并开辟传感技术在科学和工程各个学科中的新应用。

15224921.label: Project Objectives
15224921.value: New optical encoding schemes are theoretically designed and systematically analyzed to generate optical carriers (i.e., computer-generated holograms) to represent data information, and a priori knowledge about complex transmission environments is not requested. Free-space optical data transmission setups in complex environments are designed by using single-pixel (bucket) detector as the receiver. Theoretical proof of the proposed methods and experimental work will be conducted in detail. Characteristics and performance of the proposed high-fidelity free-space optical data transmission in complex environments are systematically and experimentally studied. Multiplexing and demultiplexing technologies, e.g., orbital angular momentum multiplexing, are further investigated and integrated, and the achievable transmission capacity is analyzed. The related methods, e.g., look-up table and calibration approaches, are also studied for the proposed free-space optical data transmission in complex environments. Various application scenarios are studied to optimize the proposed high-fidelity free-space optical data transmission in complex environments, and the achievable transmission distance range (e.g., affected by the power of light source etc.), transmission capacity, security, mobility and system reliability are systematically investigated. In addition, the direct transmission of various types of signals (e.g., analog signals rather than just binary signals) will be tested and realized in various complex transmission environments. The significant challenges existing in free-space optical data transmission are overcome, and the competitive advantages compared to conventional methods are fully achieved.

15224921.label: Major findings and research outcome
15224921.value: The major findings of this GRF project are as follows: 1) We have found that high-fidelity optical ghost diffraction and information transmission through scattering media in free space can be realized by using a series of 2D arrays of random numbers as information carriers. A series of 2D arrays of random numbers can be directly generated to encode the ghosts, i.e., original signals or images. 2) We have found that zero-frequency modulation can be designed to generate a series of 2D random amplitude-only patterns (computer-generated holograms) for accurate optical information transmission through thick tissues at low light intensities. Light source modulated by the generated 2D patterns propagates through biological tissues, and a single-pixel bucket detector can be used to record light intensity with a differential detection technique. 3) We have found that a flexible combination of computer-generated magnification factors and physically-generated scaling factors can be applied as security keys to achieve high-security free-space optical transmission. Absorptive filters have been used to generate nonlinear scaling factors. A new research perspective for secured optical analog-signal transmission through scattering media in free space could be opened up by the physically-secured ghost diffraction. 4) We have found that a fixed reference pattern can be used before each illumination pattern to correct a series of recorded light intensities. It has been experimentally demonstrated that high-fidelity irregular analog signals can always be retrieved at the receiving end, and high robustness against highly dynamic and turbid water can be achieved. 5) We have found that high-capacity orbital angular momentum transmission can always be realized in complex and dynamic scattering environments using a single-pixel detector. The designed orbital angular momentum beam has a petal-like structure, and the total number of petals has been designed to be equivalent to the transmitted data. In this research project, research outcomes are as follows: (i) Supported by this GRF project, 12 journal papers have been published, and 2 international conference papers have been published and delivered. (ii) Supported by this GRF project, Ph.D. student Pan Zilan has been trained and Pan Zilan has been awarded Ph.D. degree in The Hong Kong Polytechnic University.

15224921.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15224921.value: In this GRF project, we have studied high-fidelity free-space optical data transmission in complex environments with computer-generated hologram and orbital angular momentum, and significant advantages, e.g., high capacity, high robustness and high system flexibility, have been demonstrated. It is expected that metasurfaces and single-photon detection technologies can also be applied to explore the wider applications using the approaches developed in this research project. In addition, other vortex beams can also be explored.

15224921.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15224921.value: Data transmission has played an important role in our modern society. Over the past decades, optical communication has dramatically revolutionized data transmission industry and our society in many different ways. With the ever-growing of heavy transmission in wireless communication, to address serious concerns wireless radio-frequency technologies have been facing for the next generation network (especially on the last mile and backbone), free-space optical communication for wireless transmission has been rapidly developed which becomes a strong complement. In this GRF project, we have successfully designed optical data encoding and decoding methods with single-pixel detection for high-fidelity data transmission in complex scenarios, and compared to conventional methods the higher transmission capacity, higher robustness and higher design flexibility have been achieved. We have illustrated how to retrieve high-fidelity data in complex environments. We have completed the analysis of the characteristics of the developed free-space optical communication systems in complex scenarios. It is believed that more application areas can be explored by using the approaches developed in this research project.

15225321.value: To develop an unrolling-based optimization framework that allows the plugin of the complex-valued DNN for solving the inverse problem defined in the complex field. To develop an effective and efficient complex-valued DNN scheme for signal denoising purpose. To apply the proposed complex-valued CNN denoising scheme to the problem of image phase retrieval.
rows: To develop an unrolling-based optimization framework that allows the plugin of the complex-valued DNN for solving the inverse problem defined in the complex field.
