To apply the proposed complex-valued CNN denoising scheme to the problem of image phase retrieval.

15225321.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15225321.value: Recently, the unrolling-based deep learning optimization methods have attracted much attention from researchers in different disciplines. It allows to plugin deep learning models to different optimization problems to achieve higher efficiency and more accurate estimation. However, most existing unrolling-based approaches are designed for real-valued data. In many optimization problems, we need to directly work with data defined in the complex field. One example is the Fourier spectrum. In this project, we propose to develop a complex-valued unrolling-based deep learning approach that we believe can further improve the efficiency when handling complex-valued data. Traditionally, there are two sub-processes in these unrolling-based approaches when applying to solve the inverse problems. They are inversion and denoising, and the denoising part is particularly important to the overall performance. Different deep neural networks are plugged in for its efficient implementation. For handling complex-valued data, we propose to develop a new complex-valued convolutional neural network (CNN) denoising method in this project. Although the study on the complex-valued neural network has been conducted for years, there are not many efficient complex-valued deep neural networks (DNN) reported in the literature. Besides, all of them are for classification but not denoising. The difficulty of developing efficient complex-valued DNN mainly comes from their training. It usually takes a long time and is difficult to converge. The need of evaluating the complex gradients in the backpropagation training process further increases the difficulty. To solve the problems, we propose to develop a new complex-valued CNN denoiser based on a feedforward approach without the need of using the backpropagation in training. When plugging into the unrolling-based approaches, the new complex-valued CNN denoiser can almost guarantee to give optimal results in each training. It also has a much simple network model that can be easily applied to the environment without sufficient computation resources (such as the edge computing environment). To demonstrate the efficiency of the proposed approach, we will apply it to the problem of image phase retrieval, which is a typical inverse problem defined in the complex field. We believe that the result of this project will lead to many new possibilities for the unrolling-based deep learning optimization methods and open a new research direction. 最近，展開性深度學習方法引起了廣泛關注。它允許將深度學習模型插入到不同的優化問題中，以實現更高效率和更準確的估計。然而，大多數現有的展開性深度學習方法都是為實值數據設計的。在許多優化問題中，我們需要直接處理複數值數據。一個例子是傅立葉頻譜。在這個項目中，我們建議開發一種複數值展開性深度學習方法，我們相信該方法可以進一步提高處理複數值數據時的效率。傳統上，這些展開性深度學習方法在應用於求解逆問題時有兩個子過程。它們是反演和去噪，去噪部分對整體表現尤為重要。為了處理複數值數據，我們建議在這個項目中開發一種新的複數值卷積神經網絡去噪方法。儘管對複數值神經網絡的研究已經進行了多年，但有效的複數值深度神經網絡並不多。此外，它們都是用於分類而不是去噪的。開發高效的複數值深度神經網絡的難點主要來自他們複雜的反向傳播訓練過程。通常需要很長時間，並且難以收斂。為了解決這些問題，我們建議基於前饋方法開發一種新的複數值卷積神經網絡降噪器，而無需在訓練中使用反向傳播。當插入展開性深度學習方法時，前饋複數值卷積神經網絡降噪器幾乎可以保證在每次訓練中給出最佳結果。它還具有非常簡單的網絡模型，可以輕鬆應用於沒有足夠計算資源的環境（例如邊緣計算環境）。為了證明所提出方法的效率，我們將其應用於圖像相位檢索問題，這是複數值領域中典型逆問題。我們相信，此項目的成果將為展開性深度學習優化方法帶來許多新的可能性，開闢新的研究方向。

15225321.label: Realisation of objectives
15225321.value: Following the objectives of this project, a complex-valued inverse problem called Fourier phase retrieval (PR) was investigated. For the first part of the project, we designed a novel deep neural network (DNN) structure named SiSPRNet for phase retrieval based on a single Fourier intensity measurement. We proposed a new feature extraction unit using the Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) as the front end. It allows all pixels of the input intensity image to be considered together for exploring their global representation. The size of the MLP was carefully designed to facilitate the extraction of the representative features while reducing noises and outliers. A dropout layer was also equipped to mitigate the possible overfitting problem in training the MLP. To promote the global correlation in the reconstructed images, a self-attention mechanism was introduced to the Up-sampling and Reconstruction (UR) blocks of the proposed SiSPRNet. Extensive evaluations of the proposed model were performed using different testing datasets of phase-only images and images with linearly related magnitude and phase. Experiments were conducted on an optical experimentation platform (with defocusing to reduce the saturation problem) to understand the performance of different deep learning methods when working in a practical environment. The results demonstrated that the proposed approach consistently outperformed other deep learning methods in single-shot maskless Fourier phase retrieval. For the second part of this project, we investigated using physics-informed approaches to improve the phase retrieval performance. More specifically, we proposed a physics-driven multi-scale DNN structure dubbed PPRNet. Similar to other deep learning-based PR approaches, PPRNet requires only a single Fourier intensity measurement as its input and does not need an extra masking scheme for the PR system to constrain the measurement data. The main novelty of PPRNet is the introduction of physics information to the PR process. Unlike the traditional physics-driven PR methods that often end up in a time-consuming iterative procedure, we adopted an unrolling-based framework such that the proposed PPRNet has a non-iterative feedforward structure but can still effectively utilize the intensity measurement to guide the image reconstruction process. It is enabled by the novel Hybrid Unwinding Block (HUB) embedded in the network’s input and expanding path. It separately processes the global and local information of the feature maps with the aid of the intensity measurement and combines them with a channel attention method. It significantly improves the quality of the reconstructed images and reduces outliers such as noise. Our simulation and experiment results have verified the effectiveness of PPRNet. In particular, our experiment results were obtained from an optical platform. They demonstrate the performance of PPRNet when applied to practical phase retrieval systems. From the simulation and experiment results, it can be concluded that the proposed PPRNet consistently outperforms state-of-the-art deep learning-based PR methods, proving it a promising solution to practical PR applications. The study was also extended to coded aperture-based phase retrieval. To enhance accuracy in phase retrieval, researchers may introduce extra constraints to the measurement procedure by including a random aperture mask in the optical path that randomly modulates the light projected on the target object and gives the coded diffraction patterns (CDP). It is known that random masks are non-bandlimited and can lead to considerable high-frequency components in the Fourier intensity measurements. These high-frequency components can be beyond the Nyquist frequency of the optical system and are thus ignored by the phase retrieval optimization algorithms, resulting in degraded reconstruction performances. The traditional binary green noise masking scheme can reduce the high-frequency components in the measurement. However, the scheme cannot be extended to generate multiple-level aperture masks. In this project, we proposed a two-stage optimization algorithm to generate multi-level random masks named OptMask that can also significantly reduce high-frequency components in the measurements but achieve higher accuracy than the binary masking scheme. We have shown how we could optimally select the cut-off frequencies and quantization levels of OptMask to minimize its high-frequency content and maximize its randomness. We demonstrated the performance of OptMask by applying it to a practical CDP phase retrieval system. The results showed that the quality of the amplitude and phase images retrieved using the proposed OptMask significantly outperformed the traditional CDP masking schemes both qualitatively and quantitatively. Based on the abovementioned results, it is concluded that the objectives of the project are fully achieved.

A journal paper [2] and a conference paper [4] were published to report the details of the proposed method. 3. The study was also extended to coded aperture-based phase retrieval. In this project, we proposed a two-stage optimization algorithm to generate multi-level random masks named OptMask that can significantly reduce high-frequency components in the Fourier intensity measurements and achieve higher accuracy than the traditional binary masking scheme. The scheme allows us to optimally select the cut-off frequencies and quantization levels of the mask to minimize its high-frequency content and maximize its randomness. A journal paper [3] was accepted to be published to report the details of the proposed method. 4. A PhD student was trained by the project.

15225321.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15225321.value: Phase retrieval is a key process in applications such as crystallography, optical imaging, astronomy, X-ray, electronic imaging, surface plasmon microscopy, etc. Traditional phase retrieval methods are often extremely time-consuming due to the tedious optimization procedure for image reconstruction. The advent of deep learning-based methods allows the possibility of real-time phase retrieval. However, the quality of the reconstructed images is often very poor and the robustness of the methods also has much room to improve. The proposed PPRNet solves the robustness problem by introducing the Fourier intensity information into the network model to help the training and inference processes. Such information constrains the inferencing to ensure quality image reconstruction. The method was extensively tested on a real optical path, which demonstrates the practicality of the method. Due to its real-time nature, we believe the proposed PPRNet will strongly impact the existing optical applications based on phase retrieval.

15225321.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15225321.value: In this project, an important problem in optical engineering namely phase retrieval (PR) was studied. PR aims to reconstruct a complex-valued signal from its intensity-only measurements. It is a crucial process in many applications such as crystallography, optical imaging, astronomy, X-ray, electronic imaging, etc. In this project, we developed two efficient PR methods based on artificial intelligence. Compared with the traditional PR approaches which are often time-consuming, the proposed methods namely SiSPRNet and PPRNet making use of the deep neural networks (DNN) can run in real-time due to the massively parallel DNN structure. While SiSPRNet emphasizes low complexity, PPRNet has high robustness by introducing the physics information of the imaging process into the DNN computation. It significantly outperforms the traditional learning-based PR methods in reconstruction quality. To enhance PR accuracy, researchers may introduce extra constraints to the measurements by including random aperture masks in the optical path. However, traditional random masks contain much high-frequency information that cannot be taken care of in the PR process and degrades performance. In this project, we propose an optimization method for designing random masks with high-frequency information suppressed. It can also be applied to multi-level mask design which further improves the PR performance.

15225921.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15225921.value: 滿足拜占庭魯棒性的隱私保護數據收集技術研究

15225921.label: Project Objectives
15225921.value: To formalize the problem of Byzantine-robust data collection under local differential privacy model. This objective enables us to understand the security and privacy threats in distributed data collection as well as the challenges and limitations when integrating both privacy and integrity protective schemes. To analyze the impact of Byzantine users on LDP-based statistics estimation and derive critical points when these mechanisms become invalid. This is crucial for decision makers to approve or disapprove the adoption of LDP mechanisms in mission-critical tasks. To design Byzantine-robust LDP mechanisms for classic statistics estimation. Decision makers can turn to these alternative mechanisms when the data collection tasks cannot use conventional LDP mechanisms due to Byzantine users. To design LDP mechanisms for Byzantine-robust statistics estimation. Decision makers can adopt these alternative statistics when conventional LDP mechanisms fail due to Byzantine users. To design Byzantine-robust LDP mechanisms for continual data collection. Such mechanisms are essential for many real-world applications (e.g., Internet of Things) where data arrive in streams.

15225921.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15225921.value: 隨著大數據分析和人工智能技術的飛速發展，數據成為信息時代最重要的資產，而由於數據中蘊含諸多個人敏感信息，隱私保護成為一個亟待解決的問題。本地化差分隱私是一種新興的隱私保護技術，在數據收集和分析過程中具有數據本地化擾動的特征，由於不依賴於可信的數據收集者，該技術在學術界和工業界得到廣泛關註，目前已被成功部署於Google、Apple和Microsoft公司的落地產品中。 本地化差分隱私技術對用戶的隱私提供了強健的保護，然而，其始終基於可信用戶的假設。現有研究對該技術在拜占庭用戶環境下的隱私保護和數據可用性問題鮮少涉及，這主要是因為拜占庭用戶能夠利用擾動算法產生的噪聲來偽裝惡意數據，以防止被檢測出來。因此，這為本地化差分隱私技術的在諸多研究領域的實際應用帶來了極大的挑戰，例如人口和經濟指標的統計、智能家居和智慧城市，以及聯邦學習等。在拜占庭用戶環境下，如何保證本地化差分隱私保護下的算法魯棒性和數據可用性是一個亟待解決的研究問題。 本項目致力於研究滿足拜占庭魯棒性的本地化差分隱私數據采集和分析問題，具體包括拜占庭用戶對本地化差分隱私算法的影響分析、拜占庭用戶的檢測和判定問題、本地化差分隱私的優化算法等。本項目的開展能夠為隱私數據采集和分析研究提供安全理論基礎和實際保護方案。除此之外，本項目的研究成果也會為其他相關IT領域，例如物聯網和人工智能等，提供借鑒和參考。通過為拜占庭用戶環境下的上述三個本地化差分隱私技術的關鍵問題提供原型解決方案，我們相信工業界能從本項目的成果中提煉出實用技術。

15226221.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15226221.value: 隱私保護下的對抗機器學習技術

15226221.label: Project Objectives
15226221.value: To formalize the security challenges in privacy-preserving machine learning. This objective enables us to understand the real security threats in this field as well as the challenges and limitations when considering both privacy protection and adversarial attacks simultaneously. To study the impact of local differential privacy on local data poisoning and local model poisoning attacks. This study helps us to predict the trend of these poisoning attacks and design mitigation methods when data privacy becomes pervasively enforced in machine learning. To study the impact of local differential privacy on model extraction and membership inference attacks. This study helps us to predict the trend of these adversarial attacks on model confidentiality and design mitigation methods when data privacy becomes pervasively enforced in machine learning. To study the impact of local differential privacy on adversarial sample and model evasion attacks. This study helps us to predict the trend of these adversarial attacks on data integrity and design mitigation methods when data privacy becomes pervasively enforced in machine learning.

15226221.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15226221.value: 隨著各國和地區對數據隱私的立法和執法(例如歐盟的GDPR和美國加州的CCPA等）工作的深入，大量企業開始對用戶數據實踐各類隱私保護技術，例如差分隱私和同態加密等。與此同時，隨著人工智能和機器學習的火熱開展，這些企業也同時面臨著機器學習領域的各種安全威脅，例如惡意樣本，模型竊取和訓練數據投毒攻擊等。 目前這兩個領域的研究並未有交集，但隨著此兩類安全威脅層出不窮，企業將很快面對在對抗數據隱私風險的同時抵禦機器學習中的各種安全風險。我們認為這反倒給這兩個各自獨立的領域提供了新的研究機會。我們需要研究的一個核心問題是“受隱私技術保護的數據是否更容易抑或是更難抵禦機器學習中的安全攻擊”？ 作為在這兩個領域有豐富研究經驗的學者團隊，我們認為本項目的開展會給機器學習和大數據領域提供更可靠的安全保障，也為物聯網及邊緣計算等相關領域的隱私和安全機制提供了啟發，最終能為智慧城市落地香港做出理論和實踐方面的貢獻。

15226221.label: Realisation of objectives
15226221.value: After 36 months of research endeavors, all objectives set out in the original proposal have been thoroughly studied and resolved. As for the detailed progress, we have achieved objective 2 by the end of year 2022, and objectives 1 and 3 by the year 2023, and objective 4 by the year 2024. To address the objectives 1-2, we study the impact of local differential privacy (LDP) on local data poisoning and local model poisoning attacks, respectively. For local data poisoning, we adopt a general opportunistic-and-colluding threat model and propose a multigroup differential aggregation protocol (DAP) to improve the accuracy of mean estimation under LDP. Different from all existing works that detect poison values on individual basis, DAP mitigates the overall impact of poison values on the estimated mean, thanks to a new probing mechanism, i.e., Expectation-Maximization Filter, to estimate features of the attackers. This work has been published in ICDE '23. For local model poisoning attacks, we propose 3DFed, an adaptive, extensible, and multi-layered framework to launch backdoor model poisoning attacks in federated learning. 3DFed sports three evasion modules that camouflage backdoor models: backdoor training with constrained loss, noise mask, and decoy model. By implanting indicators into a backdoor model, 3DFed can obtain the attack feedback in the previous epoch from the global model and dynamically adjust the hyper-parameters of these backdoor poisoning modules. Through extensive experimental results, we show that when all its components work together, 3DFed can evade the detection of all state-of-the-art FL backdoor defenses. This work has been published in IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy (S&P) 2023. In graph data analysis, Local Differential Privacy (LDP) has been adopted to collect graph data or graph metrics (e.g., clustering coefficient). However, they have not considered the security issues of LDP for graphs. We demonstrate that an attacker can inject fake users into LDP protocols for graphs and design data poisoning attacks to degrade the quality of graph metrics. As such, we present three data poisoning attacks to LDP protocols for graphs, and further design two countermeasures for these data poisoning attacks. This work has been published in ICDE 2025. In the safety alignments of large language models (LLMs), we proopse "Intrinsically Supervised Alignments by Assessing Corpus", a primary and coarse-grained safety alignment strategy for LLMs against data poisoning. Our empirical evaluations on mainstream LLMs show that ISAAC achieves a safety score comparable to current SFT solutions. This work has been published in AAAI '25. To address the objective 3, we also study the impact of local differential privacy on model extraction and membership inference attacks. Existing literatures show their vulnerability under model extraction (ME) attacks, while their private training data is vulnerable to another type of attacks, namely, membership inference (MI). In a recent work, we show that ME and MI can reinforce each other under a privacy-preserving setting. Through a chained and iterative reaction, we can significantly boost ME attack accuracy and improve MI by saving the query cost. This work has been published in NeurIPS 2022. To theoretically evaluate the risk of data privacy leakage in model extraction attacks from an attack-agnostic perspective, we use the Neural Tangent Kernel theory and formulate the linearized MEA as a regularized kernel classification problem and then derive the fidelity gap and generalization error bounds of the attack performance. We therefore propose a new theoretical metric called Model Recovery Complexity, which measures the distance of weight changes between the victim and surrogate models to quantify risk. This work has been published in WWW '25. We also observe that current model extraction attacks focus on actively designing query samples to enhance model fidelity and imprudently adhere to the standard ML training approach. This causes a deviation from the true objective of learning a model over a task. As such, we shift our focus from query selection to training process optimization, aiming to boost the similarity of the copy model with the victim model from neuron to model level. We leverage neuron matching theory to attain this objective and develop a general training booster framework, MEBooster, to fully exploit this theory. This paper has been published in IEEE TDSC 2025. As for ME defense, we have proposed class-feature watermark, a resilient black-box watermark that leverages class-level artifacts. This work has been published in AAAI '26. As for membership inference attacks, recent studies show that privacy leakages may occur in vertical federated learning (VFL), where parties hold split features of the same samples. We explore property inference attacks (PIAs) in VFL, where an adversarial party seeks to deduce global distribution information about a target property in the victim party’s training set. Our key observation is that the Lp-norm distribution of intermediate results in VFL could reflect the fraction of the target property in a training set. Inspired by this, we present ProVFL, a novel PIA framework involving distribution comparison and correlation augmentation modules. To achieve property inference, we design a distribution comparison module by creating various intermediate-result populations with different proportions, aiming to learn the relationship between Lp-norm distributions and their fractions. This paper has been published in IEEE TIFS 2025. As for model inversion (MI) attacks, recent MI attacks have managed to reconstruct realistic label-level private data, such as the general appearance of a target person from all training images labeled on him. We then propose sample-level privacy, the private information of a single target sample, on top the of the conventional label-level privacy. In particular, we introduce a novel metric tailored for training-sample analysis, namely, the Diversity and Distance Composite Score (DDCS), which evaluates the reconstruction fidelity of each training sample by encompassing various MI attack attributes. Under DDCS, we observe that many training samples remain resilient against even the most advanced MI attack. This work has been published in AAAI '25. To address the objective 4, we first apply differential privacy to skipgram in graphs, which becomes highly challenging due to the complex link relationships, and potentially results in high sensitivity and necessitate substantial noise injection. To tackle this challenge, we present AdvSGM, a differentially private skip-gram for graphs via adversarial training. Our core idea is to leverage adversarial training to privatize skip-gram while improving its utility. Towards this end, we develop a novel adversarial training module by devising two optimizable noise terms that correspond to the parameters of a skip-gram. This work "AdvSGM: Differentially Private Graph Learning via Adversarial Skip-gram Model" has been published in ICDE 2025. As adversarial perturbations (AP) have become a great concern in image classification tasks, we also study universal adversarial perturbations (UAP), which are exploited to fool most of the unseen samples. Such one-to-all perturbations have the merit of transferability, which has strong practical significance. To address this, we first define the transferability gap and the algorithm stability of the UAP algorithm, and prove the relationship between them, and also show that the convergence domain of existing UAP algorithms with dynamic constraints is excessively small, which degrades the capacity of UAPs. Then we propose a Stochastic Universal Adversarial Perturbation (SUAP) that involves additive noise and the expected constraint. Experimental results show that SUAP outperforms existing UAP algorithms with better white-box transferability. This work has been accepted in AAAI '26.

15226221.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15226221.value: New privacy laws like the EU’s GDPR and California’s CCPA are pushing companies to protect customer data using advanced techniques such as differential privacy and homomorphic encryption. At the same time, researchers are working to defend machine learning systems against attacks like fake inputs (adversarial samples), model theft, and poisoned training data. So far, these two efforts—privacy protection and security against attacks—have mostly been studied separately. But we argue it’s now crucial to tackle them together, especially as real-world AI systems need both. A key question is whether making data private actually makes machine learning models easier or harder to attack. The team, experienced in both fields, believes combining these areas will lead to stronger, more secure AI systems. Their work could benefit not just researchers and tech companies, but also smart-city initiatives—like those in Hong Kong—where data privacy and model security are vital for technologies like IoT and edge computing.

To understand the effects of lamellar structure and phase properties on plastic deformation of the ultrastrong and ductile nano-lamellar HEAs.

15227121.label: Realisation of objectives
15227121.value: Objective 1: This project investigated the atomic-scale interface structure and formation mechanisms of ultrastrong and ductile nano-lamellar high-entropy alloys (HEAs) using high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HR-TEM), atom probe tomography (APT), and small-angle neutron scattering (SANS). The microstructural evolution of an fcc/L12 Co–Cr–Fe–Ni–Al–Ti nano-lamellar HEA was systematically studied under varying aging temperatures and durations. Results show that both aging temperature and time are critical in controlling the interplay between nano-lamellar precipitation and recrystallization, which determines the morphology and volume fraction of L12 precipitates. At lower aging temperatures, nano-lamellar precipitates preferentially nucleate and grow along grain boundaries, resulting in a fine and stable nano-lamellar microstructure. Higher aging temperatures accelerate both recrystallization and nano-lamellar precipitation, leading to rapid formation of nano-lamellae and fully recrystallized ultrafine grains. Prolonged aging causes significant coarsening, with increased thickness and length of the L12 nano-lamellae. Kinetic analysis reveals that these nano-lamellar HEAs exhibit low activation energies for both lamellar coarsening and recrystallization, attributed to rapid grain boundary diffusion and high interfacial energy, as well as enhanced grain boundary mobility induced by the nano-lamellar structure. Building on these insights, the project developed fcc/bcc/L1₂ nano-lamellar HEAs with lamellae as thin as 20 nm and spaced 50 nm apart. These structures form through complex structural transformations and chemical partitioning, initiated by a eutectoid reaction at grain boundaries that produces alternating fcc and bcc nano-lamellae. Solute redistribution occurs as Fe and Co partition into the bcc nano-lamellae, while Ni, Al, and Ti enrich the fcc nano-lamellae. The limited solubility of Al and Ti in the fcc phase leads to the formation of L12 precipitates via a two-stage process: spinodal decomposition followed by structural ordering. Similarly, bcc precipitates form from the L21 phase through spinodal decomposition and subsequent transformation to a disordered structure. The lattice misfit between precipitates and matrix increases with higher Cr content, as Cr amplifies compositional differences and accelerates coarsening, thereby reducing thermal stability. First-principles calculations further elucidate the mechanisms of nano-lamellar structure formation, showing that high interfacial and strain energy anisotropy, which is strongly influenced by Cr and Ti content, favors nano-lamellar morphologies, while low anisotropy leads to spherical precipitates. Electronic structure analysis reveals a strong Ti-Ni affinity, destabilizing the Ni/Ni3Ti interface. Magnetic analysis suggests that the magnetic orientation of Cr at the fcc/L12 interface may undergo unusual reversals due to complex interactions with Co, further increasing interfacial energy anisotropy. Objective 2: The mechanisms of dislocation-interface interactions in ultrastrong and ductile nano-lamellar HEAs were systematically investigated using TEM. By comparing dislocation behavior at both coherent and incoherent interfaces, the study clarified how these microstructural features influence the strength and ductility of HEAs. Nanoscale L12 precipitates with coherent interfaces strengthen the alloy through a dislocation shearing mechanism. Dislocations shear these precipitates via stacking faults (SFs), leading to the formation of hierarchical SF networks and immobile Lomer-Cottrell locks, which significantly enhance work hardening and plastic stability. In contrast, Laves phases with incoherent interfaces strengthen the alloy through the Orowan bypass mechanism. Dislocations pile up at incoherent interfaces, increasing work hardening in the early stages of deformation but also causing local stress concentrations. Extensive SF interactions can create localized strain regions that initiate micro-voids, ultimately leading to ductile fracture. Thus, achieving an optimal balance between dislocation shearing in coherent phases and bypassing in incoherent phases is essential for maximizing both strength and ductility. Further, dislocation interactions in hierarchically heterostructured HEAs were explored to understand their high strength and ductility at both room and elevated temperatures. Dislocations were observed to shear through both nanoscale L12 and bcc precipitates, indicating that the shearing mechanism is active for multiple phase types. Hetero-deformation-induced strengthening arises from strain partitioning between soft fcc and hard B2 phases, with strain gradients and geometrically necessary dislocations near phase boundaries accommodating the mismatch. The addition of Nb increases the dispersion of fcc and B2 phases and raises the density of heterophase interfaces, significantly enhancing this strengthening effect. At elevated temperatures, increased atomic mobility facilitates dislocation movement and promotes the transformation of dislocation entanglements into stable sub-grains, further contributing to strain hardening. Based on these insights, a strategy was developed to overcome the strength-ductility trade-off in refractory HEAs by engineering stepwise, controllable coherent nanoprecipitations. Dislocations shear through coherent δ nano-lamellar precipitates but are effectively pinned by γ'' nano-precipitates, promoting local shear and alleviating stress concentrations that typically lead to premature failure. The small size and homogeneous distribution of nanoscale precipitates reduce elastic interactions and prevent crack initiation at interfaces, ensuring that enhanced strength does not compromise ductility. Additionally, hierarchical alloys with multiple interface types were shown to hinder crack propagation and further improve fracture resistance. The soft phases can accommodate and sustain large plastic strains, improving work hardening, while the pile-ups induce localized shearing of the secondary phases. Objective 3: The influence of lamellar structure on the mechanical properties and plastic deformation behavior of ultrastrong and ductile nano-lamellar HEAs was systematically investigated through tensile testing. Alloys with short aging times exhibit nanoscale lamellar structures and high dislocation densities, which significantly increase yield strength. However, these features can also serve as sites for crack initiation, limiting plastic deformation. As aging time increases, lamellar structures coarsen and promote recrystallization, resulting in nano-lamellar structures within ultrafine grains and optimal mechanical properties. In contrast, excessively coarse lamellar structures lead to a marked reduction in yield strength. APT revealed that lamellar structure is highly sensitive to Ni and Al content. Increasing the Ni/Al ratio refines grain size and provides more nucleation sites for nano-lamellar precipitation. TEM showed that fine nano-lamellar structures are sheared by dislocations, forming intersecting slip bands and enabling high work hardening. Coarse nano-lamellar structures with larger spacing are bypassed by dislocations, resulting in lower dislocation storage and reduced work hardening. The impact of multicomponent alloying on phase properties and plastic deformation was further explored using first-principles calculations of planar-fault energies. Site-preference calculations indicate that Co and Ni preferentially occupy corner sites, while Al, Cr, and Fe favor body-center sites in Fe–Co–Ni–Cr–Al HEAs. This sublattice partitioning alters local bonding and fault energetics, affecting slip and twinning behavior. Notably, the antiphase boundary (APB) energies of the multicomponent B2 phase for <111>{110} and <111>{112} slip systems are only half those of the conventional binary phase. Lower APB energy promotes the formation of complete <111> Burgers vectors and their decomposition into two 1/2<111> superpartial dislocations, facilitating primary slip and enabling extensive dislocation activity, enhanced plastic deformation, and improved ductility and strain hardening. For the multicomponent L12 phase, plastic deformation is closely linked to elasticity and planar fault energy. Increasing Ni, Cr, Nb, Ta, and V concentrations enhances cross-slip feasibility, primarily due to reduced APB energy anisotropy. Ta and Nb additions in Ni–Co–Al–Ti-based alloys significantly raise both APB and complex SF energies, improving intermediate-temperature yield strength. Local lattice distortion around planar faults, especially in Nb- and Ta-containing alloys, correlates with higher APB and SF energies and superior yield strength. At elevated temperatures, slow coarsening of coherent precipitates facilitates planar dislocation glide, enhances uniform deformation, and delays necking. Grain boundary segregation further suppresses intergranular precipitation and improves cohesion, greatly enhancing ductility.

15227121.label: Major findings and research outcome
15227121.value: (1) Both aging temperature and time are crucial in controlling the dynamic formation of nano-lamellar structures within ultrafine-grained HEAs. At lower aging temperatures, nano-lamellar precipitates preferentially nucleate and grow along grain boundaries, resulting in a fine and stable nano-lamellar microstructure. HEAs exhibiting high interfacial and strain energy anisotropy are more likely to develop nano-lamellar structures, whereas those with low anisotropy tend to form spherical precipitates. (2) The nano-lamellar structure in HEAs emerges through complex structural transformations and chemical partitioning. Specifically, a eutectoid reaction initiates at grain boundaries, producing alternating fcc and bcc nano-lamellae. The limited solubility of Al and Ti in the fcc nano-lamellae leads to the formation of L12 precipitates via a two-stage process: first, spinodal decomposition generates fcc precipitates enriched in Ni, Ti, and Al; subsequently, as these nano-precipitates grow, structural ordering transforms them from the fcc to the L12 structure. (3) Nanoscale phases with coherent interfaces are sheared by stacking faults, resulting in the formation of hierarchical stacking fault networks and immobile Lomer-Cottrell locks, which significantly enhance work hardening and plastic stability. In contrast, dislocations accumulate at the incoherent interfaces of Laves phases, increasing work hardening during the early stages of deformation but also causing local stress concentrations. (4) The shearing of coherent nano-lamellar precipitates in HEAs facilitates dislocation transmission and promotes localized shear rather than crack formation, thereby mitigating local stress concentrations that typically lead to premature failure. The small size of the nanoscale phases reduces elastic interactions, preventing crack initiation at the nano-lamellar precipitate/matrix interface. Consequently, strengthening from nano-lamellar precipitates makes a substantial contribution to overall strength, while the coherent interfaces ensure that this strengthening does not compromise ductility. (5) Hetero-deformation-induced strengthening arises from strain partitioning between the soft and hard phases in HEAs, with strain gradients and geometrically necessary dislocations near phase boundaries accommodating the mismatch. The addition of Nb increases the dispersion of both soft and hard phases and raises the density of heterophase interfaces, significantly enhancing hetero-deformation strengthening. (6) Multicomponent alloying reduces the antiphase boundary energy of the B2 phase in HEAs, promoting the formation of complete <111> Burgers vectors and their decomposition into two 1/2<111> superpartial dislocations. This facilitates the operation of the primary slip system and enables <111> slip, resulting in extensive dislocation activity, enhanced plastic deformation, and improved ductility and strain hardening.

15227121.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15227121.value: This project has elucidated the mechanisms underlying the formation and plastic deformation of nano-lamellar structured HEAs. Building on these insights, future research can focus on advancing the thermal stability, high-temperature strength, and work hardening capabilities of these alloys. The thermal stability of nano-lamellar structures is highly sensitive to interfacial structure, chemistry, and solute diffusion. Future studies should systematically investigate the dynamic evolution of interfaces and elemental distributions at elevated temperatures, tracking atomic-scale solute redistribution and interface migration during high-temperature deformation. Such work will clarify how interface structure and solute chemistry influence the dynamic growth and coarsening of nano-lamellae under extreme conditions. Additionally, future efforts can aim to enhance work hardening by precisely tailoring the intrinsic properties of constituent phases. The findings of this project indicate that work hardening behavior is governed by the formation of specific crystal defects, which are strongly influenced by stacking fault energy and antiphase boundary energy. Optimizing these intrinsic parameters through compositional tuning could facilitate the activation of multiple slip systems and delay the onset of plastic instability. Collectively, these studies will provide a fundamental framework for designing next-generation HEAs with exceptional thermal and mechanical performance.

15227121.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15227121.value: High-entropy alloys (HEAs) have emerged as an exciting new class of metallic materials, distinguished by their unique microstructures and exceptional mechanical properties. In particular, nano-lamellar structured HEAs achieve an unprecedented synergy of strength and ductility, effectively overcoming the long-standing strength-ductility trade-off. Despite these advances, the mechanisms governing their formation and plastic deformation remain poorly understood. This project systematically investigated the formation mechanisms, mechanical properties, and plastic deformation behavior of nano-lamellar structured HEAs through an integrated approach combining theoretical modeling and experimental validation. Specifically, the roles of alloy composition, aging temperature, and aging time in the formation and evolution of nano-lamellar structures were clarified. The interactions between dislocations and interfaces, as well as the underlying plastic deformation mechanisms, were elucidated. Furthermore, the influence of microstructure and phase properties on mechanical performance and deformation behavior was thoroughly examined. Building on these insights, new nanostructured HEAs with gigapascal-level strength and excellent ductility were developed. These findings not only advance the fundamental understanding of nano-lamellar structures and their interactions with dislocations, but also provide valuable guidelines for designing advanced alloys with superior mechanical properties for technological applications.

15227321.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15227321.value: The capacity of the internet has increased significantly in recent years. To cope with this demand, there is a constant need to increase the capacity of optical communication networks. Although it is possible to achieve this through installing new optical fiber, this can be very costly. As a result, there is a need to maximize the capacity of existing installed optical fiber. A number of approaches can be adopted including maximizing the spectral efficiency by using high order modulation schemes or packing the wavelength channels closer to each other; expanding the wavelength range to beyond C band and maximizing the utilization of network resources by dynamic assigning wavelength and modulation schemes based on the traffic demand of a given light path. i.e. the available network resources will be optimized dynamically. Since for a dynamic optical network, the modulation scheme and hence the network capacity will be decided by the available optical signal to noise ratio(OSNR), it is important a simple and accurate OSNR monitoring scheme can be found. In addition, since the loss along each span is an important contribution to the OSNR at each span of an optical communication network, the ability to monitor loss along each fibre span using live communication data is necessary to ensure optimum network performance can be maintained. Since many wavelength selective switches(WSS) will be used in reconfigurable optical add/drop multiplexers (ROADMs) in the network and misalignment and bandwidth deviation of optical filters in the WSS may result in significant narrowing of the WDM channels and will affect the signal to noise ratio of the signal, it is also important to identify wavelength detune of the filters in WSS so that the central wavelength of the filters can be tuned to align them together with the central wavelength of the WDM channels. In this project, we will explore a new scheme of OSNR monitoring through exploring the Cyclostationary property of modulated signal spectrum. In particular, we will investigate the effect of fiber nonlinearity and frequency offset so that accurate OSNR monitoring can be obtained. We will explore the use of deep neural network(DNN) based digital backpropagation to obtain loss and wavelength dependent loss in each of the transmission span as well as the best approach for placing monitoring points. It is anticipated that the study shall enable the realization of dynamic optical network that can optimize the utilization of available optical fiber resources. 近年來，互聯網的容量顯著增加。為了滿足這種需求，不斷需要增加光通信網絡的容量。儘管可以通過安裝新光纖來實現這一點，但這可能非常昂貴。因此，需要最大限度地提高現有已安裝光纖的容量。可以採用多種方法，包括通過使用高階調製方案或將波長通道彼此靠近來最大化頻譜效率；通過基於給定光路的流量需求動態分配波長和調製方案，將波長范圍擴展到 C 波段以外，並最大限度地利用網絡資源。即可用的網絡資源將被動態優化。由於對於動態光網絡，調製方案以及網絡容量將由可用光信噪比 (OSNR) 決定，因此找到一種簡單而準確的 OSNR 監測方案非常重要。此外，由於每個跨段的損耗對光通信網絡每個跨段的 OSNR 都有重要貢獻，因此必須能夠使用實時通信數據監控每個光纖跨段的損耗，以確保可以保持最佳網絡性能。由於許多波長選擇開關 (WSS) 將用於網絡中的可重構光分插復用器 (ROADM)，並且 WSS 中光濾波器的未對準和帶寬偏差可能會導致 WDM 信道顯著變窄，並將影響信號信號的噪聲比，識別 WSS 中濾波器的波長失諧也很重要，以便可以調諧濾波器的中心波長以將它們與 WDM 信道的中心波長對齊。在這個項目中，我們將探索 OSNR 監測的新方案，並研究光纖非線性和系統實現的影響，以便獲得準確的 OSNR 監測。我們將探索使用基於深度神經網絡 (DNN) 的數字反向傳播來獲得每個傳輸跨度中的損耗和波長相關損耗。預計該研究將能夠實現動態光網絡，從而優化可用光纖資源的利用。

15227321.label: Realisation of objectives
15227321.value: With the rapid development of the internet and AI, optical communication system become an essential part of our society. As a result, the reliability of the communication network is very important. To improve the reliability of the network, monitoring of key parameters is essential. In this project, we have investigated and implemented simplified optical signal to noise ratio monitoring scheme as well as optical link path loss successfully. All the objectives of the project have been successfully realised. In addition, we have realised that to ensure the reliability of optical network, we not only need to monitor optical parameters of the link, but also variation of physical parameter since disruption of the network is often the result of unauthorised digging and other physical intrusions. This can be achieved through sensing of optical links. Some additional work in this aspect has also been carried out.

15227321.label: Major findings and research outcome
15227321.value: In this project, we have investigated and implemented simplified optical signal to noise ratio monitoring scheme and this can be realised as part of the DSP algorithm of the optical coherent receiver. In addition, nonlinear compensation is often implemented at the coherent receiver and this can be realised through the use of deep neural network(DNN) based digital backpropagation. Since coefficients of DNN at each layer is direct proportional to the optical power, this can be used to monitor link loss at different optical span. This has been implemented to complement the measurement using OTDR. In addition, we have realised that to ensure the reliability of optical network, we not only need to monitor optical parameters of the link, but also variation of physical parameters such as vibration. Disruption of the operation of the optical network is often the result of unauthorised digging and other physical intrusions. This can be achieved through sensing of optical links. We have investigated various schemes that can integrated sensing into optical communication systems. The information of monitoring parameters such as CD has also been utilised to improve the performance of transmission links. The research work has results in 7 journal publications, all in leading journals of the research area. Two PhD students have been trained. However, they have not submitted their thesis by the time the report is submitted. As a result, the information is not included in the report.

15227321.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15227321.value: With the repaid development of optical network, its reliability becomes more and more important. For example, in finance services, any disruption of communication link will result in significant financial loss. Optical parameter monitoring will help to improvement the performance of optical communication network as well as its reliability. We will use the results obtained through the project to discuss with industry players and hopefully the techniques developed can be used in their systems in the future.

15227321.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15227321.value: With the development of internet and AI, the reliable and intelligent operation of optical communication networks become more and more important. For example, financial services need significant amount of optical communication links for financial data transmission. Any disruption to the links will result in significant amount of financial loss; in data centres used for AI training, huge amount of optical fibre links are also utilised. If a link breaks, the training will be affected seriously. To ensure intelligent and reliable operation of the optical network, it is essential to monitor some of the key optical parameters such as optical signal to noise ratio and link loss. In addition, since the transmission is often affected by unauthorised intrusions, sensing of physical parameters is also important. In this projects, some simple techniques for optical parameter monitoring as well as physical parameter sensing have been developed. The results produced should serve as useful input to the development of this important area.

15228321.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15228321.value: Hybrid structural systems adopting composite steel-concrete frames have become increasingly popular in construction. This is particularly important for densely populated area, like Hong Kong where high-rise construction is normal practice. In composite structures, it is of great importance to ensure that the two dissimilar materials (steel and concrete) work together and develop ‘composite action’. To improve steel-concrete interfacial bond strength, shear connectors (normally headed shear studs) are commonly used to transfer longitudinal shear forces across the steel-concrete interface. Shear connectors, for example headed shear studs, may also have a significant influence on the behaviour of composite columns as the shear connectors can serve as anchors. The steel tubes are therefore anchored to the concrete infill; hence the local buckling of the steel tubes is delayed, and the composite action is enhanced. However, rare discussion could be found on the influence of shear connectors on local buckling and composite action in CFST columns. This proposed research project aims to investigate the influence of shear connectors on the behaviour of square concrete-filled steel tubular (CFST) columns. Both experimental and numerical investigations will be carried out to obtain a clear understanding on the steel-concrete interfacial bond behaviour, load transfer mechanism in CFSTs (steel to concrete and concrete to steel), local buckling of steel tube and composite action in CFSTs with/without shear connectors. Normal strength steel grade S355 will be used to fabricate the square hollow tubes. Headed shear studs will be welded onto the internal surface of the tube. CFST structures will then be formed by in-filling normal-weight grade concrete (C50/60 with a characteristic cylinder strength of 50 MPa). Finite element models will be established to replicate the test observations for validation. The validated finite element models will be used to carry out a parametric study to cover a wider range of parameters. Design recommendations will be proposed for the effective use of shear connectors in square CFST columns. The research output of this proposed project will add values to the research area of effective use of shear connectors in CFST structures and contribute to facilitating the applications of CFST in construction. 採用鋼混組合框架的混合結構體系在建築工程中越來越受到歡迎。對於像香港這種高層建築眾多的人口密集地區這種結構體系尤為重要。在組合結構中，確保兩種不同的材料（鋼材和混凝土）協同工作，發揮組合效應是非常重要的。為了提高鋼-混材料界面的粘結強度，抗剪連接件（通常是T形連接件）常用來傳遞鋼-混界面的縱向剪力。抗剪連接件，例如T形連接件，對鋼管有一定的錨固作用，會對組合柱的性能產生很大的影響。鋼管錨固在內填混凝土上，可以延緩鋼管的局部屈曲，組合效應增強。然而，抗剪連接件對鋼管混凝土局部屈曲和組合效應的影響卻鮮有討論。 本研究課題旨在研究抗剪連接件對方形鋼管混凝土的受力性能的影響。將通過試驗和數值研究來明確鋼-混界面粘結行為，鋼管混凝土中的荷載傳遞機制（鋼至混凝土和混凝土至鋼），鋼管的局部屈曲，以及有無抗剪連接件的鋼管混凝土中的組合效應。試件中的方形空鋼管將由普通強度S355鋼材加工。空鋼管內表面焊接T形連接件。然後在空心鋼管內填充C50/60混凝土（標準圓柱體抗壓強度50MPa）來構成鋼管混凝土試件。隨後將建立有限元模型對試驗結果進行模擬和驗證。驗證後的有限元模型將會用於開展參數分析，以涵蓋更廣泛的參數範圍。基於試驗和數值分析結果，將提出鋼管混凝土中有效使用抗剪連接件的設計建議。本課題的研究成果將有助於抗剪連接件在鋼管混凝土中的有效利用，並將有利於鋼管混凝土在建築工程領域中的推廣。

15228621.label: Project Objectives
15228621.value: Design and optimization of TPMS based lattice structures: TPMS based lattice structures (TPMS-LS) are topologically ordered and 3D open-celled structures consisting of one or more repeating unit cells, which are defined by the topology with the detailed connectivity information among different geometry entities, cell size scale and TPMS types. These are considered as key design factors in this proposal for the early design in TPMS-LS development. However, how to conduct design and come out with design solutions aided by an efficient design methodology is critical as the physical response and the functional performance of the designed TPMS-LS are closely associated with the generated design with the detailed value specification of the design factors. Among the various design solutions, design optimization will be conducted with the aided of finite element simulation based on the design evaluation criteria to be developed such that the generated optimal solutions are able to comprehensively meet the necessary design specifications. Development of optimal SLM processing window and process parameter configuration for realization of the optimized TPMS design. For different TPMS-LS designs made of different material powder conditions, the optimal SLM process route, processing window and process parameter configuration and the detailed realization are unknown and need to be extensively explored and studied. The co-relation between process route and process parameter configuration with the quality/property/performance of the SLMed TPMS-LS is a critical issue to be exhaustively investigated and determined for the efficient development of quality lattice structure. Therefore, they will be systematically explored and investigated with the aim at establishment of a systematic knowledge for the efficient TPMS-LS development via SLM realization. Exploration and study of multi-scaled deformation and fatigue behaviors and the corresponding mechanisms of the SLMed TPMS-LS. Size effect (SE) affected deformation and fatigue behaviors in micro-scale are different from those in macro-scaled domains and the established know-how and knowledge in macro-scale may not be the same or fully valid in micro-scale. The SE based deformation and fatigue behaviors and the corresponding mechanisms of the SLMed TPMS-LS in micro-scale have not yet been fully explored. They will be thoroughly and extensively studied and the corresponding mechanisms will be identified and comprehensively detailed. This will provide a basis for development of post-fabrication processing such as heat treatment and efficient methods for enhancing the deformation and fatigue performance of the SLMed TPMS-LS. Development of efficient methods to holistically enhance the quality/property/performance of the SLMed TPMS-LS. Design and development of TPMS-LS are significantly affected by the details of design, fabrication and post-processing. To increase the quality/property/performance of the SLMed TPMS-LS, the co-relation identified between design, fabrication, deformation and fatigue behaviors and the corresponding mechanisms developed in the previous tasks will facilitate the generation of the efficient methods for enhancement of the quality/property/performance of the SLMed structures. Through post-SLM heat treatment, evaluation of the quality/property/performance of SLMed and heat-treated structures, the performance enhancement of the SLMed structures via re-optimization of SLM process, tailoring of microstructure and grain size and the structure re-design, will eventually be realized.

15229421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15229421.value: The electric power transmission systems have been experiencing fast and drastic changes throughout the world mainly due to the energy policies, which promotes the renewables. Wind and solar are two prominent and promising renewable resources. With recent advances in wind turbine and photovoltaic cell technologies, the wind and solar power penetration levels increase as well as the sizes of wind parks and photovoltaic solar plants. These renewables are connected to electrical grids through power electronic converters, and called inverter-based resources (IBRs). The competitive wind and solar resources are far from load centers and HVDC technology based supergrid is seen as a viable solution for the massive integration of large-scale IBRs. The increasing number of HVDC installations confirms that the development of transmission grids will go in the direction of hybrid systems with integrated AC/DC interconnections and high IBR penetration levels. This transformation introduces several technical challenges in power system planning and operation including power system protection. Power system protection deals with the protection of electrical power systems from faults through the disconnection of faulted sections. Reliability, stability, selectivity, speed, simplicity and cost are the key factors while designing the protection principles and selecting the protective relays. The IBRs and HVDC converters have significantly different fault current signatures and dynamic behaviors compared to conventional synchronous generators (SGs). Thus, legacy protection elements designed based on the assumption of a SG-dominated power system may not function properly in modern transmission systems that accommodate HVDC links and IBRs at large scales. Such protective relaying problems have been recently reported, in the context of wind generation, for distance, negative sequence and power swing protections. On the other hand, the reported problems do not contain all configurations and fault scenarios of a modern transmission system that are susceptible to protective relaying problems. Moreover, research on elimination of identified problems is currently only at initial stage. This project will deliver necessary models, tools and methods to assess protection system performance in modern transmission systems; identify potential protective relaying problems; and propose solutions. Depending on the nature of the problem, the proposed solutions will include development of advanced controls for IBRs and HVDC converters or new fault identification techniques/algorithms for the protective relays. The proposed controls should not introduce significant additional stress on IBRs and/or HVDC converters. The identified problems and effectiveness of the proposed solutions will be validated through real-time hardware-in-the-loop testing using actual relays. 在提倡可再生能源政策的促進下，電力傳輸系統在世界範圍內正在發生劇烈的變化。風能和太陽能是兩種主要的有發展前景的可再生能源。隨著風力發電機和光伏電池技術的突破，風能和太陽能在電能中的滲透率隨著風電場和光伏太陽能發電廠規模的增大正在顯著提升。可再生能源發電主要通過電力電子變換器連接到電網，因此被稱為基於逆變器的能源 (inverter-based resources, IBR)。然而受自然條件的製約，絕大多數的風能發電場和太陽能發電場均遠離用電負荷中心，因此基於高壓直流輸電 (high voltage direct current, HVDC) 技術的超級電網被視為解決大規模IBR並網問題的可行解決方案。 HVDC 組網量的不斷上升證實了輸電網的發展將朝著具有集成 AC/DC 互連和高 IBR 滲透水平的混合系統方向發展。但這種轉變也給電力系統的規劃和運行帶來了很多技術挑戰，例如電力系統保護問題。電力系統保護通過及時清除故障來保護電力系統的安全和穩定運行。可靠性、穩定性、可選擇性、速度、簡單性和成本是設計保護機制和選擇保護繼電器的關鍵因素。與傳統同步發電機相比，IBR 和 HVDC 變換器具有明顯不同的故障電流特徵和動態特性。因此，過去以同步發電機為主導的電力系統背景下設計的傳統保護元件可能無法在大規模集成 HVDC 和 IBR 的現代電力傳輸系統中正常運行。這個問題已經在近年來的一些繼電保護事故中得以證實，比如近年來發生在風力發電系統中的負序保護和和功率擺動保護事故。然而在已有的事故報告中沒有包含現代輸電系統中所有易受繼電保護問題影響的系統結構和故障場景。並且對於已發現的繼電保護問題的抑制和消除的研究目前還僅處於起步階段。本項目將建立必要的模型、工具和方法來評估現代電力傳輸系統的保護系統的性能；辨識潛在的繼電保護問題；並提出相應地解決方案。基於所提出問題的性質，本項目中提出的解決方案將包括開發麵向 IBR 和 HVDC 變換器的先進控制方法或面向保護繼電器的新型故障識別技術/算法。並且所提出的控制方法以不給 IBR 和 HVDC 變換器帶來過多額外負荷為前提。本項目所提出的問題及其解決方案的有效性將通過基於實際繼電器的實時半實物仿真 (hardware-in-the-loop) 進行驗證。

15300021.value: We will derive innovative first order necessary conditions and sufficient conditions for local minimizers of some structured MPEC with cardinality penalties. We will explore relationship between MPEC with cardinality penalties and MPEC with capped piecewise linear penalties. 15300021.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15300021.value: Mathematical Programs with Equilibrium Constraints (MPEC) are constrained optimization problems in which the constraints include variational inequalities or complementarity conditions. MPEC have numerous applications in engineering, sciences and economics, and appear widely in the academic research literature. The subject of MPEC has become a well-established and fruitful discipline within optimization. However, little theoretical analysis of algorithms for finding sparse solutions of MPEC with cardinality penalties is known, even though many practical problems share the feature of seeking a sparse solution of MPEC. A solution is said to have sparsity structure if many of its components are zero. MPEC with cardinality penalties are difficult to solve because the feasible region is not necessarily convex or connected and the objective is discontinuous. Moreover, in the era of big data, MPEC with cardinality penalties have another difficulty of the high dimensionality. All of these difficulties urge us to develop efficient optimization algorithms with affirmative theoretical supports. This project aims to systematically investigate the special structure of MPEC with cardinality penalties and develop efficient optimization algorithms for some practical models with strong application backgrounds. We will establish the corresponding theoretical properties such as the convergence of these algorithms to first order stationary points, local minimizers and global minimizers. Simulation studies will be conducted to evaluate the developed algorithms and compare them with existing algorithms in terms of speed, accuracy and robustness. Real data from smart transportation research will be used to demonstrate the applicability of the new theory and methods. The outcomes of this project will have a long-term and significant impact, because MPEC with cardinality penalties arise naturally from many applications in engineering and economics and urgently need efficient algorithms for implementation. Our theory and algorithms will attract attention from the international scientific community through collaboration with distinguished researchers and publications in top journals and major international conferences. 具有均衡約束的數學規劃（簡記為MPEC）就是約束中含有變分不等式或者互補條件的約束優化問題。MPEC在工程，科學和經濟等眾多領域中具有大量的應用，並且廣泛出現在相關學術研究文獻當中。作為優化領域中建立已久的學科，MPEC目前成果豐碩。雖然許多實際問題中都有尋找到MPEC問題的稀疏解的訴求，但是對於如何尋找一個具有基數懲罰項的MPEC問題的稀疏解，其相關算法的理論分析近乎空白。如果一個解的許多組成分量都是零，則稱此解具有稀疏結構。具有基數罰的MPEC問題的可行集往往不是凸的，甚至連通性也很難保證，其目標函數也是不連續的，這些差的性質導致了其難以求解。此外，在大數據時代的當下，過高的維數是具基數罰的MPEC問題求解的另一個難點。所有這些困難敦促我們發展具有積極理論支撐的有效優化算法。本項目旨在系統地研究具有基數罰MPEC問題的結構特征，並針對一些具有較強應用背景的實際問題設計有效的優化算法。本項目擬建立相關的理論性質，比如所提出的算法如何收斂到一階穩定點，局部最優解甚至是全局最優解。我們將用大量的仿真實驗來評估提出的算法，並與已有算法就計算速度，精度和穩健性等算法關鍵指標進行比較。同時，我們將利用來自智能交通的實際數據來檢驗新的理論和方法。因為具有基數罰的MPEC問題大量地出現在工程和經濟等領域的實際問題中，並且迫切需要高效的算法予以解決，所以本項目的成果具有長期和重要的意義。通過與相關領域的傑出研究者合作、在頂級期刊和主要國際會議發表學術論文等途徑，本項目的理論和算法成果也將受到國際科學界的關註。

15300121.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15300121.value: Very recently, Google announced that their quantum computers solved a problem in 200 seconds that would take classical supercomputer 1000 years to solve. In principle, quantum computing and quantum information processing use quantum systems as computational resources to outperform their conventional counterparts. It is expected that a quantum computer can solve computationally challenging tasks for a classical computer in a reasonable time. One of the obstacles against the realization of a quantum computer/device is decoherence, which is caused by a coupling between a quantum system and its environment. Quantum Error Correcting Code (QECC) is one of the best solutions to fight against decoherence. Shor and Steane in the 1990s proposed examples of how data could be redundantly encoded in the states of a quantum system and how the redundancy could be used to protect the data. There are mainly two different Quantum Error Correction (QEC) schemes in the literature. One scheme employs extra ancilla qubits for error syndrome readout. Another scheme, called Operator Quantum Error Correction (OQEC), employs higher rank projection operators based on the Knill-Laflamme result. Researchers also developed correction schemes, called Hybrid Codes, which protect both quantum and classical information simultaneously. All these topics have aroused the interest of many researchers. Based on the Knill-Laflamme condition and its generalizations to other more general correction frameworks, theorists proposed a mathematical tool called higher rank numerical range. It has been proved to be useful and influential in the theoretical study of quantum error correction. In this project, the investigator will establish mathematical techniques, particularly in higher rank numerical range and generalizations, to establish new theoretical results or improve existing frameworks in quantum error correction. He will also develop quantum error correcting codes for different quantum channels, especially channels with Pauli noise or collective rotation noise. He will propose practical and effective implementation schemes with detailed encoding and decoding quantum circuits. For this purpose, numerical algorithms will be developed. The proposed schemes will also be implemented and examined by online quantum simulators or cloud quantum devices currently available in the field, such as IBM quantum cloud services and Google quantum Computing playground. In short, this project will lead to significant new theoretical results, novel proof techniques, and practical implementation schemes in quantum error correction. 谷歌 (Google) 最近宣布其設計的量子計算機（量子電腦）能在 200 秒內解決一個以傳統超級計算機需要 1000 年才能解決的問題。何為量子計算機？理論上，量子計算以量子力學理論為基礎，在量子系統中處理數據及運算。科學家預計量子計算機可以在合理的時間內解決許多傳統計算機（電腦）不能完成的運算任務。實現量子計算機的一個主要障礙是量子系統受其環境干擾而產生消相干現象。量子糾錯碼 (QECC) 是對抗消相干現象最佳解決方案之一。Shor 和 Steane 在 1990 年代首先提出在量子系統中對數據進行多重編碼，以保護數據的量子糾錯碼例子。現今文獻中，主要有兩種不同的量子糾錯方案。第一種方案為使用額外輔助量子位來讀取數據錯誤的徵狀。另一種採用基於 Knill-Laflamme 有關高階秩投影算子理論原理，稱為算子量子糾錯的方案 (OQEC)。近年，研究人員還開發了稱為混合糾錯碼的方案，可同時保護量子信息和傳統信息。這些研究方向都引起了許多研究人員的興趣。基於 Knill-Laflamme理論及其他相關理論推廣，學者提出了一種稱為高階秩數值範圍的數學工具，能應用在量子糾錯的理論研究中。在本研究項目中，研究人員將通過高階秩數值範圍及相關理論以建構新的量子糾錯理論結果或改進現有框架。研究員亦會開發不同量子糾錯碼及數值算法，以在線量子模擬器為實驗平台，構建可操作及實用的量子電路圖以應用於不同的量子通道。簡而言之，本項目冀望在量子糾錯方面帶來重要的理論成果、新的證明技術和實用的實行方案。

15300121.label: Realisation of objectives
15300121.value: This project was successfully completed by an excellent team, including the Principal Investigator, Professor Raymond Sze; Dr. Liang Xiong and Dr. Bui Ngoc Muoi, two postdoctoral fellows supported by the project; Dr. Run Zheng, the PhD student supervised by the PI; and other collaborators. Together they delivered theory to practice advances across all three objectives. First of all, Dr. Zheng and the PI considered classical coding parameters for BCH code [Paper 4 in Research Output]. This work provides exact formulas and constructive analyses for the dimensions and Bose distances of families of classical codes. Those results supply precise k and d parameters and coset structure insight that we used to instantiate the classical layer in hybrid [[n, k : m, d]] quantum–classical codes, ensuring provable minimum distance guarantees on the classical component that integrates with a quantum code. These parameters directly informed our hybrid encoder/decoder designs and underpinned simulation benchmarks for logical error rates. Also, Dr. Muoi and the PI considered the operator theoretic structure of strongly entanglement breaking channels [Paper 3]. By characterizing strongly entanglement breaking channels in infinite dimensional settings and clarifying their operator algebraic features (e.g., commutative ranges and measure and prepare forms), this paper gave us rigorous “worst case” noise models. These models informed our operator quantum error correction (OQEC) design criteria. They also guided the construction of channel aware recovery maps and adversarial noise testbeds used in our simulations. Dr. Xiong and the PI also considered spectral criteria for absolute PPT and related separability diagnostics [Paper 5]. This paper develops spectrum only tests that decide when states remain positive under partial transposition for all local unitaries (APPT), plus practical sufficient conditions depending on extremal eigenvalues. These spectral filters let us assess feasibility of target encodings and recoveries without tomography, and they served as efficient constraints during code space search and state preparation planning. We integrated these filters into encoder/decoder synthesis and into large scale simulations to reduce overhead while maintaining rigor. In another manuscript with Dr. Xiong on Schmidt number witnesses beyond low dimensions [Paper 6], by constructing and bounding witnesses for certifying higher dimensional entanglement (Schmidt number ≥ 3, 4, 5, etc.), this paper provided tools to certify that the logical subspaces and post recovery states produced by our encoders achieve the intended entanglement dimensionality—an essential ingredient for verifying the nontriviality and robustness of newly discovered code spaces. The PI also worked with Dr. Lau and Prof. Li on geometric analysis of numerical ranges and decomposable ranges of normal matrices [Paper 2]. The geometric structure and star shapedness results for decomposable numerical ranges gave us principled warm starts and benchmarks for projector search and subspace optimization tasks that arise in QECC discovery. These insights reduced nonconvex search pathologies and accelerated convergence during code construction guided by numerical range geometry. Also, together with Dr. Xiong and other collaborators, the team worked on multipartite strongly symmetric states, geometric entanglement, and classicality via tensor methods [Paper 1]. This paper’s analysis of strongly symmetric subspaces and completely positive tensor decompositions supplied fast separability/classicality checks and tighter entanglement bounds. Those tools helped us shape encoder targets and recovery maps compatible with the desired entanglement structure in multipartite logical encodings, and they enabled lightweight, tomography free screening within our simulation pipeline. Objective 3 is at about 80% because the final tranche of on‑device validations depends on collaboration with experimental partners, which is not yet in place. We have completed large‑scale simulations and limited spot checks on available hardware, but the planned, coordinated experiments cannot proceed until the experimental team and access are confirmed. Once that collaboration is established, we will complete the remaining validations.

15300121.label: Major findings and research outcome
15300121.value: The project delivered the following findings and outcomes. Exact formulas and constructive analyses for the dimension and Bose distance of broad families of BCH type codes. These results provide precise k and d and coset structure insights, enabling principled hybrid [[n, k : m, d]] quantum–classical designs with provable classical protection and reliable baselines for performance evaluation. [Paper 4] A characterization of strongly entanglement breaking (SEB) channels in infinite dimensions, clarifying commutative ranges and measure and prepare forms. SEB channels serve as rigorous adversarial noise models and sharpen operator quantum error correction (OQEC) constraints, informing channel aware recovery strategies and robust stress testing. [Paper 3] Spectrum only criteria for absolute PPT (APPT), given via low dimensional LMIs and extremal eigenvalue conditions. These lightweight diagnostics act as tomography free feasibility filters for encoders and recoveries, and integrate naturally into synthesis and simulation pipelines to reduce computational overhead without sacrificing rigor. [Paper 5] Construction and bounding of Schmidt number witnesses that certify high dimensional entanglement (Schmidt number ≥ 3, 4, 5, …). These witnesses serve as both design targets and post implementation certificates that logical subspaces and recovered states achieve intended entanglement dimensionality. [Paper 6] Geometric descriptions and star shapedness results for decomposable numerical ranges of normal matrices, including explicit star centers. These geometric anchors provide principled warm starts and benchmarks for projector/subspace optimization, mitigating nonconvex search pathologies and accelerating convergence in code discovery. [Paper 2] Definition and analysis of multipartite strongly symmetric subspaces, tighter bounds on geometric entanglement, and completely positive tensor–based separability/classicality criteria. These tools enable fast, scalable checks that guide encoder targets and recovery maps compatible with desired multipartite structures. [Paper 1] Collectively, these findings form a coherent, reusable pipeline: algebraic parameters for hybrid designs; rigorous adversarial noise models; spectrum only feasibility tests; high dimensional entanglement certification; geometry guided subspace search; and tensor based separability diagnostics.

15300121.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15300121.value: If additional resources become available, the research team proposes three coordinated thrusts. First, they will expand hybrid QECC families by generalizing BCH type constructions to larger [[n, k : m, d]] regimes, targeting improved distances and rate–distance trade offs; analytical bounds from the classical parameter results will be combined with numerical range geometry to guide code space search and subspace optimization. Second, they will pursue channel adapted operator quantum error correction by designing recoveries tailored to strongly entanglement breaking and related adversarial channels, extending beyond Pauli/Markovian models to non Markovian dynamics and to continuous variable (bosonic) encodings suggested by measure and prepare structures. Third, they will deliver scalable certification and benchmarking by embedding APPT spectral tests and high dimensional Schmidt number witnesses directly into online validation pipelines, enabling tomography light feasibility screening, entanglement dimensionality certification, and acceptance testing with strong statistical efficiency.

15300121.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15300121.value: This research delivers a practical, theory‑driven toolkit for making quantum systems more reliable and easier to verify. Scientifically, it advances several fronts. It gives exact formulas for the size and guaranteed error resistance of broad families of BCH error‑correcting codes, extending well beyond prior results. It introduces spectrum‑only (eigenvalue‑based) tests that decide when states are positive under partial transposition (PPT) for all local operations—a standard marker tied to separability—providing necessary‑and‑sufficient conditions in key cases. It develops scalable witnesses that certify genuinely high‑dimensional entanglement from operator spectra, avoiding heavy optimization. It defines a lean “strongly symmetric” class of many‑body states with tighter bounds on entanglement and fast tensor‑based checks for classicality. It maps geometric structure in matrix ranges that guides stable design. And it rigorously characterizes strongly entanglement‑breaking noise in infinite dimensions (including Gaussian channels), with exact constructions of channel null spaces and fixed points. The value is concrete: reduced experimental and computational overhead, faster code design and state certification, and realistic worst‑case testbeds to stress‑test protocols. These advances sharpen fundamental limits and shorten the path from mathematical insight to dependable quantum communication, sensing, and computing.
