15300221.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15300221.value: In this project, the PI and his collaborators will study novel solution methods for solving a class of split feasibility problems: this is to find a point in the intersection of a nonempty closed set and the linear pre-image of another nonempty closed set, with the projections onto the two closed sets being easy to compute. This kind of problems arises in various contemporary applications such as compressed sensing, system identification and sparse matrix factorizations. Our investigation on split feasibility problems will be based on studying pseudoprojections and exploiting the underlying difference-of-convex (DC) structure. Specifically, we will investigate efficient algorithms based on the notion of pseudoprojection recently defined and studied by the PI and one of the co-I's. This can allow one to use proxy of the projection onto the linear pre-image of the closed set instead of the actual projection: the latter can be extremely hard or even impossible to compute for nonconvex split feasibility problems that arise in applications such as system identification. In addition, in view of the recent work of the PI and his collaborators that interpreted the CQ algorithm as a DC algorithm, we will take advantage of this connection with the vast DC literature to design new efficient algorithms for split feasibility problems, especially in some nonconvex settings. Finally, the techniques developed will be further extended to tackle the companion best approximation problems. This project will lead to more efficient algorithms for a class of split feasibility problems and their companion best approximation problems, and will likely encourage new mathematical models based on split feasibility in contemporary applications. 本項目將研究分裂可行性問題的有效算法。分裂可行性問題為可行性問題的特例，當中涉及兩個閉集，其中一個易於投影，而另一集合則為一個易於投影的閉集之線性逆象。此類問題常見於壓縮感應，系統識別及稀疏矩陣分解等應用。分裂可行性問題的研究將循兩方面進行。首先，我們將利用偽投影的概念設計分裂可行性問題的算法。另外，我們亦會運用分裂可行性問題的凸差規劃表達發展新算法。最後，我們會利用這些新技術求解伴隨分裂可行性問題的最佳逼近問題。研究成果可望促進分裂可行性問題的研究與發展。

15300221.label: Realisation of objectives
15300221.value: One of the goals of this project is to design better algorithms for split feasibility problems by exploiting the underlying structure of the problem. In this regard, in the paper “generalized power cones: optimal error bounds and automorphisms”, we analyzed the error bound properties of the split feasibility problem that involves the intersection of an affine set and the generalized power cone: the generalized power cone is a recent addition to the commercial conic solver MOSEK, and has been advertised as one of the five constituent cones of the “conic wheel”. We completely characterized the error bound behaviors of this split feasibility problem. Based on these error bound properties, we also characterized the automorphism group of the generalized power cone, which has important implications on the design of interior point methods for split feasibility problems involving this cone. Next, in the paper “Convergence analysis for a variant of manifold proximal point algorithm based on Kurdyka-Łojasiewicz property”, we studied the problem of finding a sparse nonzero vector in a subspace, which is a nonconvex split feasibility problem that involves the kernel representation of the subspace and a sparsity inducing (but zero avoiding) constraint. We proposed a variant of the ManPPA for solving this problem. Moreover, we established some structural properties (known as the Kurdyka-Lojasiewicz (KL) exponent) of the extended objective that govern the local convergence rate of the proposed algorithm. Specifically, we showed that when the L1 norm is used for inducing sparsity, the KL exponent of the extended objective of the original problem is ½, and the sequence generated by ManPPA is locally linear convergent; while in general we showed that the convergence rate can be analyzed by studying the KL exponent of a suitably constructed potential function. Finally, in the paper “Break recovery in graphical networks with D-trace loss”, we explored a novel way of modeling the problem of identifying a time-varying sparse precision matrix that evolves in a piece-wise constant manner. Although the original problem is nonconvex, we derived new convex estimation problems and provided the conditions for the consistency of the estimated change-points and of the sparse estimators in each block. The alternating direction method of multipliers was then suitably adapted. In summary, we have analyzed the underlying structures of some split feasibility problems and established important properties for the design and study of the associated algorithms. The other goal of the project is to design new algorithms for the companion best approximation problems. In this regard, in the paper “Convergence rate analysis of a Dykstra-type projection algorithm”, we proposed and studied a variant of the Dykstra’s projection algorithm for the companion best approximation problem of a general split feasibility problem with closed convex constituent sets and nonzero linear maps. Our analysis was based on the KL exponent / error bound property of the dual objective function and a newly proposed structural property known as C-(1,alpha) cone reducibility, with alpha being positive and at most 1. The latter property is satisfied by a wide range of sets including spectrahedrons and p cones. We derived conditions for guaranteeing a linear convergence rate and presented examples to illustrate the necessity of these conditions. We also characterized the convergence rate based on the quantity alpha, a structural property of the underlying split feasibility problem. In the nonconvex setting, in the paper “Convergence analysis for a variant of manifold proximal point algorithm based on Kurdyka-Łojasiewicz property” in which we studied the problem of finding a sparse nonzero vector in a subspace, the formulation we looked at can be viewed as a projection problem (in L1 norm) of the origin onto the set of unit vectors in the subspace we are interested in. In view of this, the algorithm we developed is a best approximation algorithm (in L1 norm) for the split feasibility problem of finding unit vectors in a subspace. In summary, we have designed some new algorithms for some companion best approximation problems and analyzed their convergence properties.

15300221.label: Major findings and research outcome
15300221.value: Four papers were submitted, and three of them have already been published. The first paper is “generalized power cones: optimal error bounds and automorphisms”. It was reported in the midterm progress report as a preprint and is now published in SIAM Journal on Optimization. This paper completely characterizes the error bounds for the split feasibility problem that involves the generalized power cone and an affine set. The second paper is “Convergence rate analysis of a Dykstra-type projection algorithm”. It was reported in the midterm progress report as a preprint and is now published in SIAM Journal on Optimization. This paper analyzes the convergence rate of the Dykstra’s projection algorithm for a large class of closed convex sets that cover spectrahedrons as special cases. The third paper is “Convergence analysis for a variant of manifold proximal point algorithm based on Kurdyka-Łojasiewicz property”. It is now published in Pacific Journal of Optimization for the special issue that dedicated to Professor Terry Rockafellar on the occasion of his 90th birthday. It studies the problem of finding a sparse nonzero vector in a subspace, which is a nonconvex split feasibility problem that involves the kernel representation of the subspace and a sparsity inducing (but zero avoiding) constraint. The fourth paper is “Break recovery in graphical networks with D-trace loss”. It was first submitted in October 2024 to the Journal of Machine Learning Research but was rejected. It is currently under review for the Journal and Computational and Graphical Statistics. The paper studies the problem of estimating a time-varying sparse precision matrix that evolves in a piece-wise constant manner.

15300221.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15300221.value: There are several avenues for further development. First, it will be interesting to further study the properties of cones (other than the generalized power cone) and the structure of the corresponding split feasibility problems for designing better algorithms. In addition, it will be interesting to investigate the problem of finding lower rank nonzero matrices in a subspace as a natural generalization of the problem of identifying sparse nonzero vectors in a subspace. Finally, it will also be interesting to further extend the property of C-(1,alpha) cone reducibility to cover more general class of sets. These are possible avenues for future research.

15300221.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15300221.value: In this project, the PI and his coworkers studied algorithms for split feasibility problems. In details, we studied structural properties such as error bounds and developed and analyzed new algorithms for split feasibility problems based on these structural properties. We also developed new algorithms for some companion best approximation problems. The outcomes may lead to new and more efficient algorithms for split feasibility problems and their companion best approximation problems, and encourage the proposal of new models based on split feasibility in emerging applications.

15300521.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15300521.value: Soft robotic systems could potentially create the next generation of biocompatible, human-compatible, and safe robotic systems, to provide a link between living systems and artificial systems at multiple levels. One of the key challenges is to create fully controllable soft robotic systems that integrate responsiveness, dynamicity, complexity, biocompatibility, motions, and computation to enable robotic bodies to deliver the desired behavior. The intrinsic dynamicity, reversibility, and multiple stimuli-responsive of supramolecular polymers, render the supramolecular system as one of the best candidates to build the next-generation soft robotic systems and materials. Multi-controlled supramolecular systems in aqueous media have been successfully demonstrated at microscopic length-scale, however, due to the non-optimized intra- and inter-structural interactions of the above supramolecular structures, the higher length-scale multi-controlled supramolecular system remains unexplored. In this proposal, we plan to strengthen intra-structural interactions for stable, mechanically strong, and large-aspect ratio supramolecular nanostructures by substituting Feringa-type first-generation molecular motors with stiff stilbene motif, which provides improved Pi-Pi interaction of the supramolecular nanostructures generated. With the simpler synthetic pathways and excellent photoisomerization quantum yield of stiff stilbene, we plan to develop stiff stilbene amphiphiles and serve as basic supramolecular assembling units in aqueous media, controlled by multiple stimulations. We aim to apply photoswitching stiff stilbene amphiphiles (SA) for the proposed new macroscopic soft functional materials from multi-controlled supramolecular systems. We propose to develop SA derivatives in order to control (a) activation wavelength of photoisomerization, (b) structural symmetry, and (c) aqueous solubility and packing parameter of SAs. In addition, we will develop the SAs into novel multi-controlled supramolecular assembling systems with response to various external stimuli. Through systematic material studies, we plan to develop photo-controlled biotarget releasing systems and transportable soft functional scaffolds for potential location specific drug/biotarget releasing materials. The current proposed supramolecular systems and soft functional materials are one of the important outcomes of interdisciplinary research areas between Chemistry, Materials Science, and Biotechnology. The success of this project would have a great impact on the research areas of Supramolecular Chemistry, Soft Functional Materials, and Biomaterial Science. 軟機器人系統有潛力創造下一代生物相容、人類相容和安全的機器人系統，以在多個層面上提供生命系統和人工系統之間的聯繫。關鍵挑戰之一是創建完全可控的軟機器人系統，該系統集成了響應性、動態性、複雜性、生物相容性、運動和計算，以使機器人身體能夠提供所需的行為。超分子聚合物擁有動態性、可逆性和多重刺激響應性，使超分子系統成為構建下一代軟機器人系統和材料的最佳候選材料之一。水介質中的多控制超分子系統已在微觀長度尺度上成功證明，然而，由於上述超分子結構的非優化結構內和結構間相互作用，更宏觀的多控制超分子系統仍然存在未開發。 在這提案中，我們計劃通過用剛性二苯乙烯基序取代 Feringa 型第一代分子馬達來增強穩定、機械強度和超分子納米結構的結構內相互作用。憑藉硬二苯乙烯更簡單的合成途徑和優異的光異構化量子產率，我們計劃開發硬二苯乙烯兩親物，並作為水介質中由多重刺激控制的基本超分子組裝單元。我們的目標是將光開關剛性二苯乙烯兩親物 (SA) 應用於來自多控制超分子系統的新宏觀軟功能材料。我們建議開發 SA 衍生物以控制 (a) 光異構化的激活波長，(b) 結構對稱性和 (c) SA 的水溶性和堆積參數。此外，我們將把 SA 開發成對各種外部刺激做出響應的新型多控制超分子組裝系統。通過系統的材料研究，我們計劃開發光控生物靶標釋放系統和可運輸的軟功能支架，用於潛在的定位特定藥物/生物靶標釋放材料。目前提出的超分子系統和軟功能材料是化學、材料科學和生物技術跨學科研究領域的重要成果之一。該項目的成功將對超分子化學、軟功能材料和生物材料科學等研究領域產生重大影響。

15300521.label: Realisation of objectives
15300521.value: The General Research Fund supported the developments of multi-controlled supramolecular assemblies of stilbene amphiphile amphiphiles into functional macroscopic soft scaffolds for cell-material interface applications. This proposal has been completely fulfilled with fruitful research output for six publications with acknowledgement to this proposal, including, ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces, J. Colloid Interface Sci., Macromol. Rapid Commun., Dyes Pigm., Beilstein J. Org. Chem., and a book chapter in Elsevier. The main proposed work was fully summarized in the full article of ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces. Biocompatible synthetic supramolecular systems have shed light on biomedical and tissue-regenerative material applications. The intrinsic functional applicability, tunability, and stimuli-responsiveness of synthetic supramolecular systems allow one to develop various multicontrolled supramolecular assemblies in aqueous media. However, it remains highly challenging to use state-of-the-art supramolecular assemblies of photoresponsive amphiphiles controlled by multiple stimulations in fabricating macroscopic materials. In this work, we have demonstrated a stiff-stilbene amphiphile (SA) multicontrolled supramolecular assembling system that comprises two different charged end groups. The excellent photoswitchabilities of SA in both organic and aqueous media are demonstrated. Furthermore, multiple stimuli, i.e., light, pH, and counterions, are applied to control the supramolecular assembling behaviors, which are monitored by circular dichroism spectroscopy and electron microscopies. This multicontrolled supramolecular system can be systematically assembled into macroscopic soft functional scaffolds, whose structural parameters are investigated by electron microscopies and X-ray diffraction techniques, suggesting the large aspect ratio of SA nanostructures assembled into macroscopic soft scaffolds. The fabricated soft functional scaffold is highly biocompatible for photocontrolled biotarget encapsulation/release selectively, as well as a cell-material interface for diverse cells’ attachment, which was based on the collaboration with Prof. Vincent Keng (ABCT, PolyU). This new synthetic multicontrolled soft functional material provides a new strategy toward the development of next-generation controllable and biocompatible soft functional materials. With the successful demonstration of the multi-controlled supramolecular assemblies of stilbene amphiphile amphiphiles, we have attempted to further improve the biocompatibility of the amphiphilic systems driven by visible-light. In the work of J. Colloid Interface Sci., amphiphilic molecules functionalized with photoresponsive motifs have attractive prospects for applications in smart functional bio-material ranging from cell-material interfaces to drug delivery systems owing to the precisely controllable functionality of self-assembled hierarchical supramolecular structures in aqueous media by a non-invasive light stimulation with high temporal- and spatial-resolution. However, most of reported photoresponsive amphiphiles are triggered by bio-damaging UV-light, which greatly limits the potential in bio-related applications. Herein, we present newly designed red-light controlled N,N’-diaryl-substituted indigo amphiphiles (IA), exhibiting excellent photoswitchablity and photostability with dual red-/green-light in organic media. Meanwhile, aqueous solutions of IA assembled into supramolecular structures in both microscopic and macroscopic length-scale, though the photoresponsiveness of IA is slightly compromised in aqueous media. At macroscopic length-scale, morphological changes of IA macroscopic scaffold prepared by a shear-flow method can be fine adjusted upon red-light irradiation. Moreover, the preferential attachment of live h-MSCs to IA macroscopic scaffold surface also indicates a good biocompatibility of IA macroscopic scaffold. These results provide the potential for developing the next generation of red-light controlled soft functional materials with good biocompatibility. Furthermore, to investigate the structural modification of the indigo core into thioindigo motif as summarized in the Dyes And Pigments, biocompatible synthetic supramolecular systems have been proven success in fabricating regenerative biomedical materials with intrinsic functionality, tunability, and stimuli-responsiveness. However, it remains highly challenging to develop a supramolecular soft scaffold that allows transferring intrinsic microscopic aligned structural properties to cell attachments. In this work, we have reported a thioindigo bola-amphiphile (TIA) that is equipped with long alkyl-linker to connect the carboxylic acid end-group on the opposite side. Though photoresponsiveness of TIA is hindered in aqueous medium, it can be slightly improved by utilizing a co-solvent system or doping TIA with other amphiphiles. Electron microscopies and X-ray diffraction analysis suggest that a large aspect ratio of TIA nanostructures assembled into macroscopic soft scaffold with high degree of unidirectional alignment. The fabricated TIA macroscopic soft scaffold is further incubated with hMSCs, in revealing unidirectional aligned cell attachments. This work could provide an alternative strategy towards development of next-generation biocompatible soft functional materials. Besides, the alkyl-chain length effect of donor–acceptor Stenhouse adducts (DASAs) amphiphile controlled by white light was summarized in the Beilstein J. Org. Chem., which was the awarded paper for the Young Investigator Award of Beilstein Institute in 2024. We presented a series of DASA amphiphiles (DAs) with minor structural modifications on the alkyl linker chain length connecting the DASA motif with the hydrophilic moiety. The excellent photoswitchability in organic medium and the photoresponsiveness in aqueous medium, driven by visible light, were investigated by UV–vis absorption spectroscopy. The assembled supramolecular nanostructures were confirmed by electron microscopy, while the supramolecular packing was revealed by X-ray diffraction analysis. Upon visible-light irradiation, significant transformations of the DA geometry enabled transformations of the supramolecular assemblies on a microscopic scale, subsequently disassembling macroscopic soft scaffolds of DAs. The current work shows promising use for the fabrication of visible-light-controlled macroscopic scaffolds, offering the next generation of biomedical materials with visible-light-controlled microenvironments and future soft-robotic systems. Additionally, the importance of the amphiphilic design of the stiff-stilbene amphiphile inspired for developing the bola-amphiphilic molecular motor amphiphiles and reported as the Macromol. Rapid Commun. Molecular motor amphiphiles have already been widely attempted for dynamic nanosystems across multiple length-scale for developments of small functional materials, including controlling macroscopic foam properties, amplifying motion as artificial molecular muscles, and serving as extracellular matrix mimicking cell scaffolds. However, limiting examples of bola-type molecular motor amphiphiles are considered for constructing macroscopic biomaterials. This work presents the designed two second generation molecular motor amphiphiles, motor bola-amphiphiles (MBAs). Aside from the photoinduced motor rotation of MBAs achieved in both organic and aqueous media, the rate of recovering thermal helix inversion step can be controlled by the rotor part with different steric hindrances. Dynamic assembled structures of MBAs are observed under (cryo)-transmission electron microscopy (TEM). This dynamicity assists MBAs in further assembling as macroscopic soft scaffolds by applying a shear-flow method. Upon photoirradiation, the phototropic bending function of MBA scaffolds is observed, demonstrating the amplification of molecular motion into macroscopic phototropic bending functions at the macroscopic length-scale. Since MBAs are confirmed with low cytotoxicity, human bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells (hBM-MSCs) can grow on the surface of MBA scaffolds. These results clearly demonstrate the concept of designing MBAs for developing photoresponsive dynamic functional materials to create new-generation soft robotic systems and cell-material interfaces. In the book chapter, we were reviewing the latest development of Photothermal-chemotherapy: the emerging supramolecular photothermal molecules. Photothermal-chemotherapy (PTCT) is a combined antitumor therapy synergized by both photothermal therapy (PTT) and chemotherapy. Performance of conventional chemotherapy is often limited by the dose-dependent side effect. Besides, a deadlier phenotype of cancer cell, cancer stem cell (CSC), is often accompanied with higher drug resistance. Incomplete removal of cancer cells would cause tumor relapse. PTT relies on photothermal conversion of photothermal agent (PTA) for cancer cell killing. However, hyperthermia induces upregulation of heat shock protein, which provides cancer cell thermotolerance to hinder photothermal therapeutic outcome. Furthermore, the delivery and retention of PTA to deep tumor tissue are challenging.

15300521.label: Major findings and research outcome
15300521.value: This research advances the development of biocompatible, stimuli-responsive supramolecular materials for biomedical applications. We designed a stiff-stilbene amphiphile (SA) system with dual charged end groups, enabling multicontrolled assembly in aqueous media via light, pH, and counterion stimuli. The resulting macroscopic soft scaffolds exhibit excellent photoswitchability, high aspect ratios, and biocompatibility, supporting selective biotarget encapsulation/release and diverse cell attachment. To overcome the limitations of UV-responsive systems, we developed red-light-controlled indigo amphiphiles (IA) that assemble into tunable macroscopic scaffolds, promoting human stem cell attachment. Structural modification led to thioindigo bola-amphiphiles (TIA), which form highly aligned scaffolds that direct unidirectional cell growth. Donor–acceptor Stenhouse adduct (DASA) amphiphiles with tunable alkyl chains enable visible-light-controlled assembly and disassembly of macroscopic scaffolds, offering potential for light-responsive biomedical materials and soft robotics. Furthermore, molecular motor bola-amphiphiles (MBAs) amplify molecular motion into macroscopic phototropic bending, supporting stem cell growth and dynamic biomaterial applications. Our review of supramolecular photothermal-chemotherapy agents highlights strategies to synergize photothermal therapy and chemotherapy for improved cancer treatment. Collectively, these findings establish versatile platforms for next-generation, controllable, and biocompatible soft functional materials in tissue engineering, drug delivery, and advanced biomedical technologies. 15300821.value: 相场方程的基于指数积分因子的保持能量稳定与最大模上界原理的数值方法

15300821.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15300821.value: This project focuses on development and analysis of exponential integrator based numerical schemes for some phase field models given by a class of semilinear parabolic equations, such as the Allen-Cahn equation and the epitaxial growth models arising in material sciences. We are concerned about two types of features, i.e., the energy stability and the maximum bound principle (MBP), where the former one implies the decay of energy and the latter one means that the solution preserves for all time a uniform pointwise bound in absolute value under appropriate initial and boundary conditions. They are two important features of solutions to phase field equations and possess clear physical meanings in practical problems. Numerical methods preserving such two features can avoid nonphysical results in numerical simulations. There has been increasingly much literature on energy stable numerical methods and several excellent works devoted to MBP-preserving numerical schemes. However, few researches have focused on the algorithms preserving such two features simultaneously. Thus, it is highly desirable to develop a series of energy stable and MBP-preserving numerical methods for phase field equations. To fill the gap, in this project, we will design and analyze a class of energy stable and MBP-preserving numerical schemes with high-order accuracy for various phase field models given by a class of semilinear parabolic equations. We will combine the scalar auxiliary variable (SAV) method with the exponential time differencing (ETD) approach to establish the ETD-SAV schemes, not only inheriting the advantage of the SAV method, i.e., the energy stability could be proved in an easier manner, but also preserving the exponential behavior of the linear operator for highly stiff systems. Since the standard SAV schemes with stabilization may not preserve the MBP, we will propose a novel stabilization technique for SAV schemes and combine it with the ETD method to construct stabilized ETD-SAV schemes which are energy stable and unconditionally preserve the MBP under the general framework of the MBP established in our recent works. With the help of the discrete MBP, we will conduct the convergence analysis of the proposed numerical methods. In addition, we will also consider the applications to some practical phase field equations, in which certain some adaptive time-stepping strategies could be adopted to further accelerate the simulations. 本项目针对一些相场方程建立基于指数积分因子的数值格式，这些相场方程属于半线性抛物方程，比如Allen-Cahn方程以及材料科学中提出的外延生长模型。我们关心能量稳定性与最大模上界原理(MBP)这两个性质，其中能量稳定性意味着能量递减，MBP意味着在适当的初边值条件下，方程的解在任意时刻都逐点保持某个一致的上界。这是相场方程解的两个重要性质，在实际问题中具有明确的物理意义。保持这两个性质的数值方法能够在数值模拟过程中避免出现非物理解。目前已有非常多关于能量稳定数值方法的研究论文，也有一些关于保持MBP数值格式的出色研究工作，但是关于同时保持两种性质的算法的研究工作还很少，因此非常需要建立一系列同时保持能量稳定性与MBP的数值方法。 为了填补这片空白，我们将通过本项目针对半线性抛物型相场方程设计一类同时保持能量稳定性与MBP的高精度数值格式。我们将标量辅助变量(SAV)方法与指数时间差分(ETD)方法相结合，建立ETD-SAV格式，这种格式继承了SAV方法易于证明能量稳定性的优点，同时保持了高度刚性系统线性算子的指数性质。由于按标准方法添加稳定因子的SAV格式不能保持MBP，我们将对SAV格式给出一种新的添加稳定项的方式，并与ETD方法结合，得到稳定化ETD-SAV格式，并证明这个格式可以无条件保持能量稳定性与MBP。在得到离散的MBP后，我们进而给出收敛性分析。除此之外，我们的格式还可以应用于一些实际的相场方程，并采用适当的时间自适应方法来加速数值模拟过程。

To improve the stability and tune material's properties of the prepared BP ultrathin films through the strategy of substrate and interface engineering. To demonstrate wafer-scale BP-based arrays of electronic (e.g., field-effect transistor) and optoelectronic devices using various substrates and interface layers.

15301121.label: Realisation of objectives
15301121.value: 1. In order to achieve Objective 1, we developed a polymer-assisted transfer process to obtain wafer-scale few-layer black phosphorus (BP) ultrathin films on various substrates. After the direct in-situ PLD growth of the BP thin film on mica substrate, we spin-coated a solution of EVA (vinyl acetate 40 wt %, 10 wt % in xylene) onto the sample at 1500 rpm for 60 seconds and baked it at 80 °C for 60 minutes to cure the EVA layer. Then, the EVA/BP film was immersed in ethylene glycol (EG) solvent at 50 °C for 30 minutes to facilitate detachment from the growth substrate. The detached film was carefully transferred onto the target substrate and baked in a vacuum drying oven at 50 °C for 30 minutes to ensure adhesion. Finally, the EVA film was selectively removed by soaking the sample in tetrahydrofuran (THF) for 30 minutes, resulting in clean, continuous ultrathin BP films on the target substrates, maintaining wafer-scale uniformity and structural integrity. In addition to developing the polymer-assisted transfer process, we investigated the interfacial adhesion mechanisms that govern transfer efficiency. We compared the performance of two common thermoplastic polymers, EVA and PS, as transfer supports. The EVA-assisted transfer resulted in complete detachment and clean, uniform BP films on SiO2/Si substrates, whereas PS showed minimal transfer. This difference is attributed to adhesion strength: EVA exhibits stronger bonding to BP than BP does to mica, facilitating effective film release, while PS exhibits lower adhesion to BP, causing the film to remain on mica. The superior adhesion of EVA arises from its copolymer structure, combining polar vinyl acetate groups and rubber-like elasticity, which promote robust interface interactions. These mechanistic insights into adhesion balances are crucial for optimizing wet transfer techniques for wafer-scale BP films, ensuring high film quality and uniformity on target substrates. The relevant findings have been published in Nature communications (2024) (impact factor~15.7). 2. To achieve Objective 2, we employed substrate and interface engineering to enhance stability and tailor the properties of BP ultrathin films. Beginning with biaxial strain engineering using a piezoelectric actuator on BP transferred to oxide substrates, we observed anisotropic Raman peak shifts: tensile strain induced redshifts while compressive strain caused blueshifts, with B2g mode shifts reaching ±15 cm^-1/%. These shifts, related to bond angle and length changes, were quantitatively linked to phonon behavior via Grüneisen parameters, highlighting potential applications in polarized light detection. Building on this, we integrated BP with a flexible ferroelectric copolymer P(VDF-TrFE) to fabricate ferroelectric-tuned synaptic transistors. The devices demonstrated excellent electrical performance—including high mobility (~900 cm^2/Vs), large on/off ratios (~10^3), and ultra-low energy consumption (~40 fJ)—along with reliable synaptic functions and 93.6% accuracy in digit recognition, underscoring neuromorphic computing prospects. Moreover, recognizing the need for device stability, we applied polymer passivation to BP field-effect transistors. This passivation proved highly effective: after 24 hours' ambient exposure, passivated devices maintained ~75% of their original output current, whereas unpassivated ones degraded drastically to 0.01%. The relevant findings have been published in Appl. Phys. Lett. (2023) (impact factor~3.6), Nano Letters (2024) (impact factor~10.8), Nature communications (2024) (impact factor~15.7). 3. To achieve Objective 3, we established an experimental and computational framework to investigate the growth mechanism, crystalline structure, and properties of wafer-scale BP. Few-layer BP thin films were synthesized using PLD, where freshly cleaved mica substrates (1 cm × 1 cm) and BP crystal targets (SMART-ELEMENTS) were positioned face-to-face separation in a chamber evacuated to 1.6 × 10^-9 Torr. The substrate temperature was maintained at 300 °C while a KrF excimer laser (248 nm, 5 Hz, 1.2 J cm^-2) ablated the BP target, generating a plasma plume containing large BP clusters for deposition. To elucidate the growth mechanism, simulations were performed using VASP with a 4×4×6 supercell model featuring a 25 Å vacuum layer. The simulations employed PBE functional with GGA+U correction, 300 eV plane-wave cutoff, and convergence criteria of 1×10^-4 eV and 0.05 eV/Å for energy and force. Various laser parameters were systematically investigated to examine their influence on phase formation and homogeneity. The results revealed that laser-induced phosphorization occurs through substrate surface absorption, transient heating, and phosphorus incorporation via rapid cooling, resulting in atomic lattice strain and non-uniform expansion due to temporary high pressure. Results indicate that phosphorus cluster formation occurs preferentially within high-pressure regions generated by controlled low-fluence laser irradiation, facilitating uniform BP film growth and enabling systematic investigation of PLD growth conditions. The relevant findings have been published in Applied Physics Reviews (2022) (Impact Factor~19.2), Nature communications (2024) (Impact Factor ~14.9), and Nano Letters (2023) (impact factor~ 11.2). 4. To fulfill Objective 4, we fabricated wafer-scale BP FET arrays on silicon substrates using wet-transferred ultrathin BP films. The devices exhibited high carrier mobility of 293 cm^2/Vs and a drain current modulation of 3.6×10^3 under −0.1 V drain voltage, demonstrating efficient charge transport and reliable switching. Mobility and on/off ratio remained stable as channel length increased from 75 µm to 570 µm, confirming uniform film quality and integrity at large scale. Compared to our previous top-gate BP FETs on mica (5 nm BP, 213 cm^2/Vs mobility, 5×10^3 on/off), the transferred BP FETs showed improved mobility with comparable on/off ratio. Relative to mechanically exfoliated BP devices, our large-area films provide uniform thickness, larger lateral size, and similar or better electrical performance, except for a slightly reduced on/off ratio. Furthermore, when compared with wet-transferred MoS2 FETs, the BP devices exhibit much higher mobility and comparable on/off ratio, benefiting from BP’s exceptional material properties. Moreover, the BP FETs were also developed and implemented as a hardware platform for image-based pattern recognition using a three-layer neural network, where the 28 × 28 input neurons correspond to image pixels and the 10 output neurons represent digit classes. This architecture naturally supports optoelectronic operation, as optical information (such as pixel intensities from an infrared or visible imager) can be converted into electrical inputs to the BP FET network, enabling BP-based optoelectronic and neuromorphic vision functionalities within the same device framework. The relevant findings have been published in Nature communications (2024) (impact factor~15.7) and Nano Letters (2023) (impact factor~10.8). 5. In summary, all objectives of the RGC GRF project have been fully achieved. During the project period, one PhD postgraduate student, Yuqian Zhao, was financially supported by the GRF grant, received comprehensive research training, and successfully obtained a PhD degree. As the first author, the student published several international journal papers in high-impact venues such as Nat. Commun., Appl. Phys. Lett., and Appl. Phys. Rev., and co-authored additional papers. In total, seven good journal articles acknowledging this project have been published, including works in Nature Communications (IF ~15.7), Nano Letters (IF ~10.8), Applied Physics Reviews (IF~19.2), ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces (IF ~8.3), and Applied Physics Letters (IF ~3.6), with the PI serving as the sole or co-corresponding author. One US patent on the PLD grown wafer-scale BP was granted during the project period. The PI also delivered plenary and invited talks on BP-related research at various international conferences relevant to materials science, thin-film and condensed matter physics. All research outputs appropriately acknowledge the support from this GRF project.

15301121.label: Major findings and research outcome
15301121.value: 1. We developed a polymer-assisted transfer process to achieve wafer-scale few-layer BP ultrathin films on diverse substrates, yielding clean, continuous films with preserved structural integrity. In our representative work of the project, EVA was identified as an efficient transfer support that, owing to its strong interfacial adhesion to BP, enables complete release of PLD-grown BP thin films from mica and their uniform transfer onto other substrates. These outcomes establish a reliable wet-transfer route for high-quality wafer-scale BP films. (See: Part C Journal 6, Conference 5). 2. We found the key growth mechanism and structural features of wafer scale BP by PLD. We identified that laser induced phosphorization and pressure driven BP cluster formation govern film development, and we found that tuning PLD conditions strongly impacts crystallinity and uniformity. Our results revealed clear links between processing parameters, lattice strain, and final film properties, offering guidance for scalable fabrication of high quality wafer scale BP. (See: Part C Journal 1, 6, 7, Conference 1,2,3,4). 3. We found that the Raman shift of the B2g mode in transferred BP ultrathin films can be tuned by applying biaxial strain via a piezoelectric actuator, reaching values up to about ±15 cm^-1 and enabling control of phonon behavior for polarized light detection. Further, ferroelectric-tuned synaptic transistors combining BP with P(VDF-TrFE) achieved large on/off ratio and ultra-low energy consumption (~40 fJ), and reliable neuromorphic functions including 93.6% accuracy in digit recognition. Polymer passivation greatly enhanced BP FET stability, retaining ~75% current after 24 hours versus near-total degradation in unpassivated devices. These key findings demonstrate effective substrate/interface engineering and device design to modulate BP properties and elevate device performance. (See: Part C Journal 4, 5, 6, Conference 4,5). 4. We developed wafer-scale BP FET arrays on silicon substrates using wet-transferred ultrathin BP films, achieving high carrier mobility (293 cm^2/Vs) and drain current modulation (3.6×10^3) at −0.1 V, indicating efficient transport and reliable switching. It was found that the device performance remained stable over long channel lengths, demonstrating uniform film quality and scalability. Compared to earlier mica-based BP FETs, mobility improved while maintaining comparable switching ratios. These films offer larger lateral size and uniform thickness than mechanically exfoliated BP, with performance exceeding wet-transferred MoS2 FETs in mobility and matching on/off ratios. This confirms the feasibility of scalable, high-performance BP device arrays on silicon for electronic and optoelectronic applications. (See: Part C Journal 6, Conference 1,2,3,4,5)

15301121.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15301121.value: Future development of this research will focus on further improving the quality, scalability, and functionality of wafer-scale BP films and devices towards various applications. First, the PLD growth and polymer-assisted transfer processes will be refined to realize larger-area, thinner, and single-crystalline BP films on technologically relevant wafer-scale substrates and interface layers, enabling robust integration with conventional silicon and other semiconductor platforms for large-scale circuits and photonic systems. Second, the demonstrated strain engineering and ferroelectric-gated BP synaptic transistors will be extended to more complex functional device architectures, leveraging BP’s anisotropic band structure and strain-tunable bandgap for polarization-sensitive detection, in-memory computing, and low-power integrated circuits. Third, device stability remains a central challenge; therefore, advanced passivation and encapsulation strategies, including 2D capping layers, molecular coatings, and multilayer polymer/oxide barriers, will be systematically explored to ensure long-term air-stable operation suitable for real-world deployment. Finally, we will pursue heterogeneous integration of wafer-scale BP with other 2D materials, as well as ferroelectric and memristive layers, to construct multifunctional heterostructure arrays. This multi-pronged course of action aims to translate our fundamental materials innovations into scalable, robust BP-based technologies suitable for high-performance electronics, optoelectronics, and neuromorphic computing applications.

15301121.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15301121.value: This research project focuses on making and tuning ultrathin films of black phosphorus (BP), a promising nanomaterial for future electronics and photonics. We employed substrate and interface engineering to transfer wafer-scale thin layer of BP onto different surfaces and substrates, ensuring it remains clean and uniform. By studying how BP grows under specific laser conditions and substrate temperature, we investigated how to control its structure and quality for good performance. We also used functional substrate and interface to perform strain engineering, which could change physical properties of BP in controllable ways. Additionally, we combined BP with flexible and tunable materials to produce advanced devices. To protect and stabilize these devices, we used a polymer coating that keeps them working well, even after exposure to air. Finally, we successfully made large arrays of BP-based transistors on conventional semiconductor silicon substrate, showing excellent electrical performance and stability across different device sizes. Our findings pave the way for fast and scalable growth of high-performance BP-based materials and devices, which may lead to smart and low-power electronics with applications in computing, sensing, and communication. This work brings together materials science and device engineering to unlock the potential of BP for next-generation technology.

15301321.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15301321.value: 具有定长向量解的非线性抛物方程的线性化隐式重整化方法的误差分析

15301321.label: Project Objectives
15301321.value: For the nonlinear parabolic equations describing Landau-Lifshitz equation and heat flow of harmonic maps, we shall present rigorous error estimate for the numerical solution given by a renormalized finite element methods with linearly implicit backward Euler time-stepping scheme. The error analysis would be based on a new geometric observation and a superapproximation estimate of the renormalization process, and the properties of lumped mass finite element methods on rectangular mesh. We shall furthermore extend the analysis of renormalized finite element methods to triangular mesh and some higher-order linearly implicit time-stepping methods, such Crank–Nicolson, second-order backward differentiation formula, or Runge–Kutta methods. We shall establish error bounds of a renormalized evolving surface finite element method for approximating mean curvature flow of closed surfaces by combining a matrix-vector technique used in previous work for partial differential equations on evolving surfaces and the analysis of renormalization technique described in this project.

The error analysis would be based on a new geometric observation and a superapproximation estimate of the renormalization process, and the properties of lumped mass finite element methods on rectangular mesh.

15301321.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15301321.value: For many systems of nonlinear parabolic partial differential equations, the solution of the equations is a vector field taking values in a sphere, namely, the length of the vector field is fixed. However, the standard linearly implicit finite element methods for these problems generally cannot preserve the fixed length of the vector solution. In this case, users might add a normalization step at every time level to normalize the computed numerical solution to the fixed length, before proceeding to the computation of the numerical solution at the next level. This renormalization technique is one of the simplest and most widely used methods for nonlinear parabolic equations with vector-valued solutions of fixed length. It is especially simple to implement and flexible to be combined with commonly used linearly implicit time-stepping methods for nonlinear parabolic equations. However, rigorous analysis of the accuracy of numerical solutions given by such renormalization methods remains open for the problems mentioned above, including heat flow of harmonic maps, the Landau–Lifshitz equations, and the equation of normal vector in mean curvature flow of closed surfaces. In this project, we fill in the gap between rigorous error analysis and numerical computation by systematically study the effect of renormalization in commonly used linearly implicit finite element methods for several nonlinear parabolic equations from physics and engineering, including the equation of harmonic map heat flows, the Landau–Lifschitz equation, and the equation of normal vector in mean curvature flow of closed surfaces. We prove appropriate error bounds of several renormalized finite element methods for the three equations mentioned above, with some commonly used linearly implicit time-stepping methods, including backward Euler method, Crank–Nicolson method, the second-order backward differentiation formulae and Runge–Kutta methods. Our error analysis would be based on new geometric observations and superapproximation properties of the renormalization process. 对许多非线性抛物型偏微分方程组，方程的解是一个在球面上取值的向量场，即向量场的长度是固定的。然而，这些问题的标准线性隐式有限元方法一般不能保持向量解的固定长度。在这种情况下，人们可以在每个时间级别添加一个重整化的步骤，将计算的数值解重整为固定长度，然后在下一级别继续计算数值解。这种重整化方法是求解具有定长向量值解的非线性抛物型方程最简单、应用最广泛的方法之一。它与常用的非线性抛物型方程的线性隐式时间步方法相结合，具有实现简单、灵活等优点。然而，对于上述问题，包括调和映象的热流、Landau-Lifshitz方程和闭曲面平均曲率流的法向量方程，仍然需要对这些重整化方法给出的数值解的精度进行严格的分析。本课题通过系统地研究物理和工程中几种非线性抛物型方程常用的线性隐式有限元方法中的重整化效应，填补了严格的误差分析与数值计算之间的空白，包括调和映象热流方程，闭曲面平均曲率流的Landau-Lifschitz方程和法向量方程。本文用几种常用的线性隐式时间步方法，包括后向欧拉方法、Crank-Nicolson方法、二阶倒向差分公式和Runge-Kutta方法，对上述类型的方程证明几种重整化有限元方法的误差上界。本项目中的误差分析将基于新的几何观测和重整化过程的超逼近性质。

15301321.label: Realisation of objectives
15301321.value: We have presented rigorous error estimate for the numerical solution given by a renormalized finite element method for the Landau-Lifshitz equation, addressing objective 1 of this project. The paper has been published in ESAIM: M2AN. We have extended the analysis of renormalized finite element methods to triangular mesh and higher-order linearly implicit time-stepping methods using kth-order backward differentiation formula, fully addressing objective 2 of this project. The paper has been published in Numerische Mathematik. By formulating mean curvature flow in terms of the evolution equations of normal vector and mean curvature, the evolution equation of normal vector has exactly the same form as the harmonic map heat flow. Therefore, the error estimate for the linearly implicit time-stepping methods using kth-order backward differentiation formula, with renormalization at every time level, still holds for the evolution equations of normal vector in mean curvature flow. Therefore, objective 3 is also addressed together with objective 2.

The error analysis would be based on a new geometric observation and a superapproximation estimate of the renormalization process, and the properties of lumped mass finite element methods on rectangular mesh.

We shall furthermore extend the analysis of renormalized finite element methods to triangular mesh and some higher-order linearly implicit time-stepping methods, such Crank–Nicolson, second-order backward differentiation formula, or Runge–Kutta methods.

We shall establish error bounds of an evolving surface finite element method for approximating mean curvature flow of closed surfaces by combining a matrix-vector technique used in previous work for partial differential equations on evolving surfaces and the analysis of renormalization technique described in this project.

15301321.label: Major findings and research outcome
15301321.value: The studies deliver the first complete mathematical framework and optimal L²‑error estimates for renormalized, structure‑preserving, linearly implicit FEMs applied to nonlinear parabolic equations such as the Landau–Lifshitz and harmonic map heat flow equations. The papers produced in this project successfully extend the theory from first‑order backward Euler to Crank–Nicolson and higher‑order BDF methods, and outline extensions to triangular and curved meshes, accomplishing the second objective fully. The developed framework—combining geometric projection analysis, mass‑lumping, and stability via multiplier techniques—lays a rigorous mathematical foundation for constructing and analyzing structure‑preserving evolving‑surface FEMs for mean curvature flow and related problems.

15301421.label: Project Objectives
15301421.value: Fabrication and structural characterizations of freestanding oxide perovskites. To achieve single crystal freestanding oxide perovskites through epitaxial growth on perovskite substrates with a scarified layer. The structural characterization can be carried out by XRD and Cs-corrected STEM. From STEM high-angular annular dark field (HAADF) image, their crystal structures will be characterized with accurately determined atomic positions and displacement (for a polarization state) in the unit cells. Characterizations of electromechanical properties of the freestanding oxide perovskites. By transferring a freestanding oxide perovskite film (with top electrode coated) on a substrate such as mica, its electromechanical properties including flexoelectric and ferroelectric (also pyroelectric and piezoelectric) effects can be characterized. These characterizations can be performed using scanning probe microscopies with electrical and mechanical stimulations such as piezoelectric force microscopy (PFM) and conductive atomic force microscopy (C-AFM). Macroscopic electromechanical property characterizations of the freestanding films can be performed through bending test with the freestanding film on a flexible substrate. Demonstration and deep understanding of photo-flexoelectric effect in freestanding oxide perovskites. Argument in literatures and our preliminary results suggest that the so-called photo-flexoelectric effect remains fundamentally unveil and deserves further study. With the freestanding oxide perovskites as a platform, we will address issues existed in the photo-flexoelectric effect and prove our hypothesis about the impact of photocurrent to flexoelectricity. Demonstration of device applications of freestanding oxide perovskites. Compared to bulk and thin films, freestanding oxide perovskites may bring the opportunities of real applications of flexoelectric effect. We will demonstrate device applications of the freestanding oxide perovskites by fabricating highly sensitive acoustic sensors, ultrahigh-frequency ultrasound transducers etc. The success of device application of the freestanding film will bring this technology great impact to commercialization.

15301421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15301421.value: Analogous to the two-dimensional transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD), a recently developed technology enables the synthesis of monolayer freestanding metal oxide perovskite films and extends the 2D material family to transition metal oxides. This significant progress promotes a great deal of research interest to study 2D oxide materials. Our proposed work focuses on electromechanical properties of freestanding oxide perovskites and their applications in flexible electronic devices. A single crystalline oxide perovskite has never been so flexible in human history before being able to be removed from its fragile epitaxial substrate by dissolving the sacrificed layer; this results in its superior electromechanical properties which are usually very small when being clamped on a fragile substrate. Among the potential superior electromechanical properties, very large flexoelectric and piezoelectric effects are the most significantly beneficiated properties from almost unlimited strain and strain gradient induced by its flexibility. Flexoelectricity describes the generation of electric polarization under mechanical strain gradient which can break crystal space inversion symmetry; while piezoelectricity refers to the generation of electric polarization from lattice deformations in non-centrosymmetric crystals. In this proposed project, the study of enhanced electromechanical properties of freestanding thin oxide perovskite films will be carried out aiming to achieve deep understanding on the enhancement mechanism and demonstrate applications of freestanding oxide perovskites in flexible electronic devices. Freestanding oxide thin films such as SrTiO3, BaTiO3 and Pb(Zr1-xTix)O3 are very good templates for study of large strain gradient induced flexoelectricity and coupling with piezoelectricity. Based on these freestanding oxide thin films, electromechanical devices will be fabricated utilizing their large strain and strain gradient characteristics. In order to make flexible devices, the oxide films will be transferred to flexible and conductive substrates. Potential applications of these devices include highly sensitive acoustic, infrared and strain/strain gradient sensors, ultrahigh-frequency ultrasound transducers, and miniaturized power generators etc. The success of this project will open-up a new research area of oxide perovskite freestanding films as a new class of 2D functional materials and enrich the understanding of physics behind toward applications of this new form of materials. 类似于二维过渡金属二硫属化物 (TMD)，最近开发的一项技术能够合成单层独立金属氧化物钙钛矿薄膜，并将二维材料系列扩展到过渡金属氧化物。这一重大进展促进了研究二维氧化物材料的大量研究兴趣。我们提出的工作重点是独立式氧化物钙钛矿的机电性能及其在柔性电子设备中的应用。单晶氧化物钙钛矿在能够通过溶解牺牲层从其脆弱的外延基板上移除之前，在人类历史上从未如此灵活。这导致其优异的机电性能，当被夹在易碎的基板上时，该性能通常非常小。 在潜在的优越机电性能中，非常大的挠曲电和压电效应是最显着的受益特性，因为它的柔韧性引起了几乎无限的应变和应变梯度。柔性电描述了在机械应变梯度下产生的电极化，它可以打破晶体空间反转对称性；而压电性是指非中心对称晶体中的晶格变形产生电极化。在这个拟议的项目中，将开展对独立式薄氧化物钙钛矿薄膜的增强机电性能的研究，旨在深入了解增强机制并展示独立式氧化物钙钛矿在柔性电子设备中的应用。 独立的氧化物薄膜如 SrTiO3、BaTiO3 和 Pb(Zr1-xTix)O3 是研究大应变梯度诱导的挠曲电和与压电耦合的非常好的模板。基于这些独立的氧化物薄膜，将利用它们的大应变和应变梯度特性制造机电设备。为了制造柔性器件，氧化膜将转移到柔性导电基板上。这些器件的潜在应用包括高灵敏度声学、红外和应变/应变梯度传感器、超高频超声换能器和小型化发电机等。该项目的成功将开辟氧化物钙钛矿独立薄膜的新研究领域。新型二维功能材料，并丰富了对这种新型材料应用背后的物理学的理解。

15301521.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15301521.value: 在納米粒子和單個原子之間架起橋樑的支持多核物質正引起越來越多的關注。除了來自位點隔離的優異原子經濟性之外，許多催化反應需要在活性位點有一個以上的金屬中心才能獲得化學和區域特異性。由於基於核數（原子數）和配位環境的廣泛可調的電子和幾何特性，多核物種通常表現出獨特的催化特性。然而，由於材料合成和表徵的複雜性，支撐型多核物種的應用和機理研究受到很大阻礙。我們研究的目的是建立一個可靠的研究平台，可以指導支撐型多核納米團簇的精確合成，從而在催化科學中得到更廣泛的應用。 微孔材料（例如沸石）的納米空間可以被用于構建納米團簇。在我們的初步研究中，我們開發了一種創新的模塊化方法，通過利用陽離子金屬物質和基於咪唑酯的配體的分子特異性，可以將兩個銅核連接在一起以在 ZSM-5 沸石中實現雙核 Cu2 結構。在此，我們的目標是系統地研究這些物種的電子和幾何特性，並製造四種關鍵的銅基雙金屬雙核物種（即 Cu-Fe、Cu-Co、Cu-Ni 和 Cu-Zn）負載在沸石上。 通過改變 HOMO-LUMO 功函數和對反應底物的結合偏好，以及改變金屬種類和配體分子可以影響電子特性。同時，改變連接分子的體積和沸石載體的骨架類型可以改變影響吸附質相互作用的幾何特性。將就 Huisgen 疊氮化物-炔烴環加成 (AAC) 研究負載雙核物種的催化化學，因為 AAC 的反應機制需要協同使用兩個活性 Cu 位點（或其他金屬陽離子) 。令人興奮的是，我們的 Cu2-ZSM-5 樣品可以比 Cu1 類似物更快地催化 AAC（1.4 h-1 的轉換頻率）12 倍。它也比大多數具有固有雙核 Cu2 位點的相關“單位點”多相催化劑更優越，例如 Corma 等人的 HKUST-1（三甲基銅，周轉頻率為 0.7 h-1），由于其電子學中的交替和幾何特性。 該研究項目具有創新性和重要意義。這項工作將首先建立一個可靠的平台，將無機化學中的模塊化概念轉移到固態材料。我們期待這工作能激勵其他學者設計新穎的功能材料，以應對長期存在的挑戰。

15301521.label: Realisation of objectives
15301521.value: This project was designed to establish a reliable research platform for the modular synthesis of supported multinuclear species on microporous materials, specifically bridging the gap between single-atom catalysts and nanoparticles by precisely engineering binuclear active sites. We are pleased to report that all project objectives have been fully realized. The success is demonstrated through a series of high-impact publications in top-tier journals, including Journal of the American Chemical Society, Angewandte Chemie International Edition, Chem Catalysis, and Cell Reports Physical Science. These works confirm our ability to control metal nuclearity, elucidate structural descriptors via synchrotron radiation, and apply these materials to challenging catalytic reactions. Realization of objective #1: Synthesis and characterization of supported binuclear Cu2 species. Our initial objective focused on synthesizing and characterizing supported binuclear Cu2 species with varied electronic and geometric properties. We developed a highly controlled modular approach, which allowed us to systematically classify the structural descriptors of atomically dispersed 3d metal bimetallic dual-atom catalysts, as detailed in our publication in Chem Catalysis (2022). This work provided a structural "genome" for rational catalyst design by identifying how the geometric configuration of the dual-atom sites influences their electronic properties. Furthermore, we successfully exceeded the scope of the original objective by pushing the boundary of nuclearity control to tri-atom clusters. In our recent breakthrough published in the Journal of the American Chemical Society (2025), we reported on the unprecedented control and unraveling of the nuclearity effect of atomically choreographed triatom Cu3 clusters supported on zeolites. This study definitively proved our ability to precisely control the number of metal atoms, or 'n' in Mn clusters, which was a core aspiration of the proposal. Realization of objective #2: Precise preparation and characterization of bimetallic binuclear systems We successfully fabricated and characterized various heterometallic ensembles, utilizing the advanced synchrotron techniques (RXRD and EXAFS) integral to the proposal. We demonstrated the precise preparation of bimetallic binuclear systems through the controlled synthesis of Cu-Fe dual-atom catalysts restrained on metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), which we reported in the Journal of Materials Chemistry A (2023). This achievement validates our synthetic strategy for installing specific, non-identical metal combinations within a porous host environment, allowing for the fine-tuning of catalytic performance through tailored metal-support and metal-metal interactions. Realization of objective #3: Investigation of catalytic chemistry This objective, which proposed the use of the Huisgen azide-alkyne cycloaddition (AAC) as a model reaction to investigate catalytic chemistry, has been fully realized and significantly expanded upon. We successfully demonstrated the predicted synergistic effects in the original model reaction: our work in Cell Reports Physical Science (2022), titled "Atomically precise bimetallic metal ensembles with tailorable synergistic effects," explicitly showed how varying the secondary metal species alters the electronic structure and binding preferences, leading to superior catalytic performance in the AAC reaction compared to monometallic analogues. Beyond this benchmark, we applied our precise deposition techniques to address more challenging and industrially relevant energy conversion reactions. For instance, our study in Angewandte Chemie International Edition (2025) reported exceptional CO2 hydrogenation to ethanol via precise single-atom Ir deposition, and our Cu-Fe dual-atom catalyst work demonstrated highly efficient O2 activation. These high-impact results validate the fundamental hypothesis of the proposal: that atomically precise multinuclear sites enable cooperative activation of small molecules and complex reaction pathways, extending the utility of the developed catalyst platform well beyond the initial model reaction. In conclusion, the research conducted under this grant has established a robust, modular synthesis platform for designing and characterizing atomically precise multinuclear catalysts. The successful realization of all three objectives, coupled with high-impact dissemination, confirms the novelty and significance of our approach in advancing the field of heterogeneous catalysis.

15301521.label: Major findings and research outcome
15301521.value: The research conducted under RGC Ref No. 15301521 yielded several significant scientific and technological advances, proving that atomic cluster precision is the key to engineering next-generation heterogeneous catalysts. Our major findings moved the field beyond conventional single-atom catalysis (SAC) to the realm of multinuclear clusters, resulting in high-impact publications. 1. Fundamental discovery of the nuclearity effect The most critical scientific finding was the precise unraveling of the nuclearity effect of supported metal clusters. We pioneered a modular synthetic platform capable of installing not just single atoms, but atomically choreographed binuclear M2 and triatom M3 clusters within zeolite channels. Our work in the Journal of the American Chemical Society (2025) demonstrated that systematically increasing the cluster size from n=1 to n=3 drastically alters the electronic and geometric properties, leading to a profound change in adsorption behavior, enhanced reactivity, and suppressed unwanted side reactions. This discovery provides the fundamental scientific basis for designing active sites based on the specific number of atoms required for a given reaction. 2. Modular engineering of synergistic bimetallic sites We successfully established a methodology for the precise engineering of heterometallic dual-atom catalysts, as reported in Journal of Materials Chemistry A (2023) and Chem Catalysis (2022). By combining two different metal species, such as Cu and Fe, within the confined space of MOFs or zeolites, we achieved a powerful synergistic effect. Advanced synchrotron characterization confirmed that the geometric pairing dictates the electronic interaction between the metals and the support, creating highly specific active motifs. This achievement validated our hypothesis that the deliberate pairing of metals is essential for achieving optimal catalytic function. 3. Expanded catalytic scope for sustainability The designed atomic clusters delivered superior performance across various reaction types. We successfully validated the initial objective by demonstrating the tailorable synergistic effects of bimetallic ensembles in the Cu-catalyzed Huisgen azide-alkyne cycloaddition (AAC) (Cell Reports Physical Science, 2022). Crucially, the platform was extended to high-impact energy challenges, achieving exceptional CO2 hydrogenation to ethanol (Angewandte Chemie International Edition, 2025) and highly efficient O2 activation. These outcomes confirm the versatility and value of our modular platform for developing robust, highly selective, and sustainable catalytic processes.

15301521.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15301521.value: The successful fabrication and mechanistic understanding of dual- and triatom clusters open up high-impact avenues for future research. The potential for further development lies in scaling the complexity and scope of the designed active sites. We will focus on two major areas: (i) We aim to move beyond triatom clusters to synthesize and stabilize larger, atomically precise metal ensembles (e.g., M4 or M5 sites). This is essential for unlocking challenging reactions that require large ensembles for multi-electron transfer or complex C-C bond formation pathways. (ii) We will apply these multi-site catalysts to complex, tandem catalytic reactions (e.g., one site activates H2 while the adjacent site performs C-H bond activation), providing new, highly efficient routes for C1 chemistry and alkane functionalization. The proposed course of action is to apply for a follow-up grant focused on ‘Atomic Cluster Engineering for Cascade Catalysis’. We will continue to leverage our established international partnerships, particularly access to advanced synchrotron facilities, to conduct in-situ/operando spectroscopy to track reaction intermediates in real-time. This will allow us to validate computational models and rationally design highly stable, scalable catalysts for industrial applications.

15301521.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15301521.value: This research project successfully engineered atomically precise metal clusters, specifically dual-atom M2 and triatom M3 active sites, supported on high-surface-area porous materials like zeolites and metal-organic frameworks (MOFs). The core significance of the work lies in overcoming the limitations of conventional single-atom catalysis by developing a modular synthetic methodology to control the nuclearity (the number of atoms) and heterogeneity (the combination of different elements) of the active site. The primary value demonstrated is the dramatic enhancement of catalytic function. By tailoring the electronic and geometric environment of these sites, we achieved superior performance in key sustainable chemical transformations, including the activation of oxygen, the reduction of carbon dioxide to ethanol, and the C-C coupling required for the Huisgen cycloaddition reaction. This precise control over atomic structure is essential for designing highly efficient, stable, and resource-saving catalysts for industrial applications.

15301621.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15301621.value: 傳統的場效應晶體管依賴於半導體中的電荷傳輸，這不可避免地導致由散射載流子引起的散熱，並導致集成電路的功耗不斷增加。通過采用具有無耗散特性的載流子傳輸機製，例如基於非電荷的信息載體（自旋、谷等），開發低功耗器件勢在必行。類似於半導體中的谷自由度，無質量的外爾費米子具有不尋常的輸運特性，這是由手性特性和對外部擾動的奇異軌跡造成的。理論上預測外爾半金屬/半導體中的手性反常電流在長距離內幾乎是無耗散的，但仍然缺乏有效控製其傳輸的實驗方法。 手性反常電流首先在拓撲半金屬中被發現。然而，三維拓撲半金屬中手性反常電流的操縱仍然是一個挑戰，因為它缺乏有效的方法來調節半金屬中的手性反常電流並抑製背景電導率。最近，單質碲半導體（Te）被揭示為一種外爾半導體，它具有抑製背景電導和處理信息的潛力，同時散熱更少。探索外爾半導體中手性反常電流的物理和器件應用是一個基礎研究興趣。 在這個項目中，我們計劃研究基於外爾半導體的場效應手性反常器件，其中手性反常電流在導通狀態下占主導地位，而由於在導通狀態中存在帶隙，截止狀態電流非常低。首先，我們將研究控製 Te 厚度的生長方法。適當厚度的 Te 能夠保留拓撲特征並抑製背景電導率。我們還將研究缺陷對費米能級位置的影響。其次，我們將對 Te 的手性異常特征進行磁輸運研究。我們還將準備可以通過離子液體進行靜電調製的 Te 器件結構，類似於傳統 場效應晶體管的操作。手征反常將通過非局域谷輸運測量得到進一步證實，這也可以通過外部場進行有效調製。最後，我們將利用手征反常電流由電場和磁場決定的特性，構建手征反常器件來執行基本的邏輯功能。

15301621.label: Realisation of objectives
15301621.value: 1. To perform studies on the growth methods of Te for controlling the thickness, and investigate the effects of defects on the properties of Te; Group-VI elemental two-dimensional (2D) materials (e.g., tellurene) have unique crystalline structures and extraordinarily physical properties. However, it still remains a great challenge to controllably grow 2D tellurene (Te) with good repeatability, uniformity and highly aligned orientation using vapor growth method. We design a Cu foil-assisted alloy-buffer-controlled growth method to epitaxially grow aligned single-crystalline 2D Te on an insulating mica substrate. The in-situ formation of Cu-Te alloy plays a key role on 2D Te growth, alleviating the spatial and temporal non-uniformity of precursor in conventional vapor deposition process. Through transmission electron microscopy analysis combined with theoretical calculations, we unveil that the alignment growth of Tellurene in the [110] direction is along the [600] direction of mica, owing to the small lattice mismatch (0.15%) and strong binding strength. The as-grown Te exhibits different morphologies under different growth pressures, which is kinetically controlled by the confined space formed under compression. With high pressure, the confined space completely seals the Te precursor between two substrates. The melting Te at high temperature is squeezed and recrystallize followed the shape of the confined space, which usually is amorphous. The attained Te flakes have thick center part and thin edge. When the compression is reduced, the low pressure cannot seal the powder, which allows the Te vapor at high temperature to escape from the small gap between two substrates. The left Te precursor will recrystallize in the preferred orientation, forming a rod-like shape. The attained Te products are single crystal with uniform thickness. 2. To study chiral anomaly characteristics in elemental semiconducting Te, and electrostatically modulate the chiral anomaly current in semiconducting Te. To corroborate the physics of chiral anomaly current by nonlocal valley transport with width-dependent and length-dependent structures; Modern electronics demand transistors with extremely high performance and energy efficiency. Charge-based transistors with conventional semiconductors experience substantial heat dissipation because of carrier scattering. Here we demonstrate low-loss topological phase change transistors (TPCTs) based on the chiral anomaly characteristics of tellurium (Te), a Weyl semiconductor. By modulating the energy separation between the Fermi level and the Weyl point of Te through electrostatic gate modulation, the device exhibits topological phase change between Weyl (Chern number ≠ 0) and conventional (Chern number = 0) semiconductors. In the Weyl ON-state, the device possesses low-loss transport characteristics due to the global topology of gauge fields against external perturbations; the OFF-state exhibits trivial charge transport in the conventional phase by moving the Fermi level into the band gap. The TPCTs show a high ON/OFF ratio (108) at low operation voltage (≤2 V) and high ON-state conductance/width (39 mS/μm). Our studies provide alternative strategies for realizing ultra-low power electronics. Non-local valley transport is also considered as the strong evidence of chiral anomaly. Chiral anomaly current is compensated by the inter-valley scattering, which involves large momentum transfer and long relaxation length. Our length-dependent valley transport results show that the Ohmic transport decays much faster than the chiral anomaly-based valley transport, which supports the low-loss transport characteristics (relaxation length of 3.5 μm) of chiral anomaly. This transport behavior is distinctly different form conventional charge transport with small mean free path (described by the Drude-Boltzmann theory), which is highly sensitive to low-energy/momentum scattering events. Our experimental results of the angle-dependent negative MR, planar Hall effect and non-local valley transport behaviors unambiguously suggest the existence of chiral anomaly current in our Te samples. 3. To design and construct device structures that can perform basic logic functions by using chiral anomaly current with both magnetic and electrical fields as input signals. The output conductance of TPCTs is dependent on the gating voltage, magnetic field and the relative angle between magnetic and electrical fields, which allows to process multiple input signals. By utilizing Vg and B as input signals and ΔG as the output signal, we can realize “AND” and “OR” logic functions based on Te TPCTs. Furthermore, we can switch “AND” and “OR” logic functions in a single TPCT by changing the angle between magnetic and electrical fields. Two-input OR logic functions. For the input1 (Vg), logic “0” and “1” are defined as -2V≤Vg <0 and 0≤ Vg ≤ 2V, respectively. For the input2 (B), logic “0” and “1” are defined as -8 T≤B <-4 T and -4 T≤B≤ 0, respectively. The output “0” corresponds to MR< -14%, and “1” corresponds to MR ≥ -14%. When input1 or input2 is logic “1”, the output is “1”. Three-input logic functions. We define θ as input1 with 0° as “0” and 10° as “1”. Vg is defined as input2 with Vg= 0 as “0”, and Vg= -2 V as logic “1”. Input3 is B with 1 T as logic “0”, and 2 T as logic “1”. The output is defined as “0” corresponding to |MR|< 1%, and “1” for |MR|≥ 1%. The logic functions (OR, AND) can be switched in one TPCT by changing the angle. Input1 is defined as “0” for Vg= 0 and “1” for Vg=-1 V. Input2 is “0” for B=1 T and “1” for B= 2 T. When Δσ is lower than the critical value (such as10 μS/μm), the output is “0”; otherwise, the output is “1”. For the thick sample under B//E (θ= 0), when either one of the input1 and input2 is “1”, the output is “1”, corresponding to OR logic. After switching the angle by 10° (θ= 10°), this device shows AND logic because when both input1 and input2 is “1”, the output is “1”. So, this “angle-switching” strategy can efficiently change the logic functions from OR to AND due to the high sensitivity of chiral anomaly current to the rotation angle.

15301621.label: Major findings and research outcome
15301621.value: This research successfully addressed three key objectives regarding two-dimensional tellurium (Te). First, a novel Cu foil-assisted alloy-buffer-controlled growth method was developed to epitaxially grow aligned, single-crystalline 2D Te on mica substrates. This method overcomes previous challenges in vapor growth by using an in-situ formed Cu-Te alloy to ensure uniformity and alignment, driven by a minimal lattice mismatch (0.15%) with the substrate. Growth kinetics were controlled by pressure, yielding either amorphous thick flakes (high pressure) or uniform, rod-like single crystals (low pressure). Second, the study demonstrated chiral anomaly characteristics in semiconducting Te, enabling the creation of a topological phase change transistor (TPCT). By electrostatically gating Te to shift the Fermi level relative to its Weyl point, the device switches between a low-loss "Weyl ON-state" (with chiral anomaly transport) and a trivial "OFF-state." This TPCT achieves a high ON/OFF ratio of 10⁸ at low voltage (≤2 V) and exhibits a long chiral anomaly relaxation length (~3.5 μm), confirmed by non-local valley transport measurements, angle-dependent negative magnetoresistance, and the planar Hall effect. Third, leveraging the chiral anomaly current's dependence on gate voltage, magnetic field strength, and their relative angle, the researchers designed reconfigurable logic devices. A single TPCT can perform basic "AND" and "OR" logic functions by using voltage and magnetic field as inputs. Crucially, the logic operation (AND vs. OR) can be switched dynamically simply by changing the angle between the electric and magnetic fields, demonstrating multi-functional programmability. In summary, the work provides a controlled growth method for 2D Te, unveils its chiral anomaly for low-loss topological transistors. We published 3 high-impact papers, including Nature Communications, Science Advances, and trained 3 PhD students.

15301621.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15301621.value: This research presents a strong foundation for future development in two main directions: device integration and material optimization. For device development, the immediate course is to scale and integrate the reconfigurable TPCT logic into more complex circuits, moving from single gates to functional units like adders or memory elements. Exploring three-terminal gate configurations could enhance control and simplify logic design. Concurrently, the unique angle-dependent response offers a direct pathway to develop novel vector and tensor sensors for magnetic field direction or strain. On the material front, the growth method should be optimized to produce wafer-scale, uniform monolayer or few-layer Te films, which are critical for industrial application. Exploring other elemental 2D materials (Se, S) or Te-based van der Waals heterostructures could unveil new topological phases or enhance device performance through engineered band structures. A systematic study correlating defect density (from the growth phase) with topological transport properties will be crucial for improving device yield and consistency. This combined approach aims to translate the fundamental discoveries into practical, high-performance electronic and sensing technologies.

15301621.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15301621.value: Today's chips waste a lot of energy as heat because electrons bounce around while moving. We aim to use a special material called "tellurium," which allows electrons to flow in a protected, highway-like state called the "chiral anomaly." This state dramatically reduces energy waste. Our plan has three steps: First, we will perfect a method to grow ultra-thin, high-quality tellurium crystals. Second, we will prove these crystals support the efficient chiral anomaly current and show we can control it with a simple electrical switch, like a transistor. Finally, and most innovatively, we will use both electricity and magnetism as inputs to create basic computing circuits. This allows a single device to be reprogrammed for different tasks, making future electronics far more powerful and energy-efficient.
