15301721.label: Project Objectives
15301721.value: We propose to develop a general protocol that we plan to combined a range of steady-state methods with our state-of-the-art ultrafast broadband time-resolved fluorescence (TRF) and transient absorption (TA) spectroscopy to enable a comprehensive and direct probe of thermal stability, electronic spectra and excitation dynamics for iMs modified differently with epigenetic methylation of C bases involved. The iMs examined are chosen from a series of genomic C-rich sequences in human telomeric and several oncogene promoter regions. The protocol is designed also to allow investigation of effects on properties of the iMs by microenvironment, e.g., buffer composition, the presence of cell-mimicking condition and, in particular, binding with fluorescence light-up ligands, including but not limited to DAPI and ThT. We propose to utilize the procedure in (1) to perform a comparative and systematic study for iMs with the varied methylation modifications from the different sequences to provide quantitative characterization for the hitherto unknown spectra, dynamics, and excited-state pathways through inter-base energy transfer, charge transfer, and proton transfer diagnostics to the respective iMs structures involved. The result will allow finding out the most favourable condition for stabilizing iMs, and to identify the interaction, dynamics, and positions of the modification that are most effective in altering the stability and properties of iMs, especially at the physiologically relevant neutral pH condition. The study proposed in (2) is designed also for the purpose to allow direct comparison between spectra and dynamic behaviors for the modified vs non-modified iMs formed by varied molecular assembling or with architectures that are different in both the iMs' core and the loop regions. This work will supply concrete evidences for addressing how the molecularity, structural rigidity, loop topology, and methylation of the bases in the core or the loop may affect the electronic nature and stability of iMs. We also propose to conduct comparative study using the procedure in (1) on interactions of DAPI and ThT with the modified and non-modified iMs formed from the same set of genomic sequences as for the studies in (2)-(3). The finding of this work will provide direct spectral and dynamic data that will enable to assess capacities of the ligands in binding with these iMs; it will also allow acquiring explicit evidence for resolving the mode and site(s) involved in the binding, for assessing how the epigenetic methylation of iMs may affect the binding properties. The study proposed in (4) is planned also to gain experimental observation for insight at the molecular level about requirement on electronic and structural property of ligand for effective interaction with iMs, as well as to supply information on specificity of these ligands in targeting iMs vs other secondary structures, e.g., GQs and ds DNAs. The result of this work should prove beneficial for further seeking and adding to the family of ligands for effective binding specific to iMs. The overall results of the proposed work will constitute a comprehensive set of data that will be the first in the areas of epigenetic modified iMs from genomic sequences and their interaction with the ligands selected. This will contribute importantly for understanding of the nature and photophysics of iMs in general, and for those with covalent and non-covalent modifications in particular. The research proposed is timely in view of the rapidly growing interest in iMs and the urgent current demand for information on their biological function and their applications in nano-biotechnology and as targets for chemical intervention of cell biology.

15301721.value: 胞嘧啶四鏈核酸具有獨特、可控的空間結構，在生物納米技術領域獲得廣泛的應用。該四鏈核酸是由富含胞嘧啶的序列經由相互嵌入半質子化胞嘧啶鹼基對而形成。儘管人們曾經認為它只是一種奇特的核酸二級結構，最近的研究發現該結構亦存在於人類細胞核並參與細胞週期的動態過程。此外，能夠形成該四鏈構型的富胞嘧啶序列在人類基因組中普遍存在，尤其集中於端粒及各種原癌基因的啟動子區域。因此，目前該結構的形成、穩定性及其生物學功能，備受關注。了解表觀遺傳修飾及配體相互作用對該四鏈結構的影響和效應是這方面極具挑戰性且相互關聯的重要課題。胞嘧啶甲基化是核酸中最常見的表觀遺傳修飾，在改變基因表達水平和各種遺傳疾病的發展中起關鍵作用。已報導的胞嘧啶四鏈核酸主要源自由常規鹼基組成的序列，對甲基化修飾的四鏈核酸研究甚少。另一方面，與大量已知的雙鏈及鳥嘌呤四鏈核酸配體相比，對與胞嘧啶四鏈核酸 結合配體的研究遠遠不足。為此，我們建議利用尖端超快時間分辨熒光及瞬態吸收光譜並結合穩態光譜方法對一系列由人類端粒及若干原癌基因啟動子序列富胞嘧啶核酸形成的四鏈結構進行系統而深入研究；並著重探討胞嘧啶甲基化表觀遺傳修飾及與配體結合等對該四鏈結構的影響和效應。該研究將實現對所選四鏈核酸電子激發態的首次直接探測和光譜表徵，並將獲得描述這些電子態的重要動力學及光譜特徵參數。這些數據包含有關這類核酸結構中鹼基間電子相互作用和相互耦合的信息，為闡明甲基化和配體結合對該結構的形成及性質的影響提供直接的實驗證據。此外，該研究亦將揭示如何調控胞嘧啶四鏈核酸的結構穩定性，對拓展其在抗癌藥物研發及生物傳感器等方面的應用具有重要意義。

15302121.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15302121.value: To reach the actuation level like biological muscles, has become one of the most challenging topics in the bionic field. This project is attempted to meet the challenge by study of new actuation materials at molecular level, aiming at creating some ground-breaking progress in muscle-like actuators and promoting the human-friendly interactive applications. Among various materials and approaches, ionic polymer actuator, as unique flexible electrochemical device, has attracted intensive attention due to its major advantage of safe working voltage (lower than 3V), showing great promising for the artificial muscles and user-friendly applications mentioned above. In principle, actuation in ionic polymer is attributed to dynamical accumulation (or depletion) of ions under electric field. Hence, ions adsorption (or desorption) and electrodes expansion (or contraction) are most crucial processes. Previously, ionic liquid based polymer actuators have been developed with great success in air-operability and durability. However, to meet practical use, several key issues in terms of low transducing efficiency, slow response and low force still need to be addressed. For instance, subject to nature of ions-driven motion, actuator usually needs tens of seconds or minute to achieve large strain due to slow ions mobility and long diffusion path. Moreover, our or others’ earlier work found that although energy storage density of porous nano-carbon electrodes (namely, carbon nanotube and graphene) is higher than that of traditional gold and platinum electrodes, the energy conversion efficiency of actuator still stays at a low level (<1.0%). Therefore, this project is attempted to improve the performances by study of new electrode materials and new device structures. Graphdiyne (GDY) as a new 2D carbon nanomaterials has unique sp and sp2 hybridized electronic structure, high theoretical conductivity, and high chemical activity. Different with pure sp2 carbon-based materials, GDY has numerous alkyne groups and unique alkene-alkyne-complex-transition activity. In this project, for the first time, porous and active GDY electrodes based ionic actuators will be fabricated and investigated in terms of actuation, energy storage and conversion. Characteristics of molecule-structure change and electronically tunable deformation of the GDY actuators will be demonstrated. In order to probe the dynamic process and actuation mechanism at molecular level, some highly sensitive in-situ characterization techniques, for example in-situ sum frequency generation spectroscopy, will be developed. Finally, GDY based ionic muscles in forms of yarns and fabrics, will be designed and explored, for purpose of scaling up actuation strain/stress and developing innovative wearable products with diverse bio-mechanical functions. 達到像生物肌肉一樣的驅動水平，已成為仿生領域最具挑戰性的課題之一。該項目試圖通過在分子水平上研究新的驅動材料來迎接挑戰，旨在在類肌肉驅動器方面取得一些突破性進展，促進人性化的智能交互應用。在各種材料和方法中，離子聚合物致動器作為一種獨特的柔性電化學裝置，因其工作電壓安全（低於3V）的主要優勢而受到廣泛關注，在人造肌肉和應用中顯示出巨大的前景。 原則上，離子聚合物的驅動歸因於電場下離子的動態積累（或消耗）。因此，離子吸附（或解吸）和電極膨脹（或收縮）是最關鍵的過程。以前，基於離子液體的聚合物致動器在空氣可操作性和耐用性方面取得了巨大成功。然而，為了滿足實際使用，轉換效率低、響應慢和力低等幾個關鍵問題仍然需要解決或改進。例如，受離子驅動運動的性質影響，由於離子遷移速度慢和擴散路徑長，執行器通常需要幾十秒或幾分鐘才能實現大應變。此外，我們或其他人的早期工作發現，雖然多孔納米碳電極（即碳納米管和石墨烯）的儲能密度高於傳統的金和鉑電極，但執行器的能量轉換效率仍然處於較低水平。因此，該項目試圖通過新的電極材料和新的器件結構來解決這些問題。石墨炔 (GDY) 是碳納米材料的新成員，由 sp 和 sp2 雜化碳原子層組裝而成。與純sp2碳基材料不同，GDY具有眾多的炔基和獨特的烯-炔轉化活性。在該項目中，將首次在驅動速度、能量存儲和轉換方面製造和研究基於多孔和活性 GDY 電極的離子致動器。將展示 GDY 致動器的分子結構變化和機電轉換特性。為了弄清動態過程和驅動機制，將開發一些高靈敏度的原位表徵技術，例如原位和頻發生光譜，以探測分子活性。

15302121.label: Realisation of objectives
15302121.value: 1. To achieve the cross-scale characterization for actuators, we employed in-situ probing techniques to closely examine molecule-level chemical bond rearrangements, actuation, and conformation changes. This approach provided detailed insights into the microscopic intermediate processes and their impact on macroscopic performances. Additionally, we systematically investigated the effects of voltage, current, and frequency of applied electric fields on the electromechanical properties of the actuators. By doing so, we established a comprehensive standard testing protocol that ensures consistent and reliable evaluation of actuator performance across various conditions, ultimately enhancing their efficiency and functionality. 2. To synthesize GDY materials, we will focus on evaluating their microstructure by analysing morphology, pore size, specific surface area, and graphitization degree using techniques such as SEM, HRTEM, XRD, XPS, RAMAN, and BET. These analyses provided a comprehensive understanding of the material's structural characteristics. Furthermore, the electrical and electrochemical properties of GDY when used as electrodes were assessed. This is achieved through scanning electrochemical microscopy, electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, and cyclic voltammetry, among other methods. These evaluations help determine the suitability and performance of GDY materials in various electrochemical applications. 3. To achieve electrochemical actuators based on GDY, we first synthesized and integrated GDY with selected polyelectrolytes to create innovative electrochemical devices. An experimental study was conducted to evaluate these devices, focusing on their electrochemical energy storage and actuation properties. Key performance metrics such as displacement, blocking force, cyclic stability, and transducing efficiency will be assessed using the methods established in Objective 1. Such comprehensive evaluation provided insights into the capabilities and potential applications of GDY-based electrochemical actuators, paving the way for advancements in smart materials and devices. 4. To establish a theoretical model for GDY-based electro-chemo-mechanical actuators, we developed a framework that captures the cooperative actuation of constitutive molecular machines. This model predicted charge/current-quantified actuation and electrostatic effects, providing insights into how molecular structure changes influence dimensional changes in the covalent bond network of GDY. We validated this model against experimental results, focusing on key parameters such as actuation efficiency and structural dynamics. Any discrepancies will guide modifications to the model, ensuring it accurately reflects the behavior of GDY actuators and enhances our understanding of their mechanisms.

15302121.label: Major findings and research outcome
15302121.value: The project yielded several significant findings in the development of GDY-based electrochemical actuators. Firstly, the synthesis of GDY materials revealed their exceptional structural properties, such as high surface area and unique pore structures, which contribute to enhanced electrochemical performance. The experimental studies demonstrated that GDY-based actuators exhibit impressive energy storage capabilities and mechanical actuation, with notable displacement and blocking force metrics. Secondly, the theoretical modeling provided insights into the cooperative actuation mechanisms at the molecular level, highlighting how changes in molecular structure influence the overall performance of the actuators. The model successfully predicted the charge/current-quantified actuation and electrostatic effects, aligning closely with experimental observations. Furthermore, the research identified the critical role of polyelectrolytes in optimizing the actuator's efficiency and cyclic stability, paving the way for improved material combinations. The findings also underscored the importance of precise control over the synthesis process to achieve consistent material quality and performance. Overall, the project advanced the understanding of GDY materials in electrochemical applications, demonstrating their potential for use in soft robotics, sensors, and other smart technologies. These findings lay the groundwork for future research and development, aiming to refine and commercialize GDY-based actuator technologies. Four journal paper have been published arising from the project.

15302121.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15302121.value: The potential for further development of research on GDY-based electrochemical actuators might be extended based on the unique properties and versatility of GDY materials. Future research could focus on several key areas: 1. Material Optimization: Explore the synthesis of GDY composites with other nanomaterials to enhance their mechanical, electrical, and electrochemical properties. This could lead to improved actuator performance and broader application possibilities. 2. Advanced Modeling: Refine theoretical models to incorporate more complex interactions and environmental factors, such as temperature and humidity, to better predict actuator behavior in real-world conditions. 3. Scalability and Fabrication: Develop scalable fabrication techniques for GDY-based actuators to facilitate their integration into commercial applications. This includes exploring cost-effective production methods and ensuring material consistency. 4. Application Exploration: Investigate new applications in fields such as soft robotics, wearable technology, and biomedical devices, where the unique properties of GDY actuators can offer significant advantages. 5. Long-term Stability and Durability: Conduct long-term studies to assess the durability and stability of GDY actuators under various operational conditions, ensuring their reliability for practical use. 6. Interdisciplinary Collaboration: Foster collaborations with experts in chemistry, materials science, and engineering to drive innovation and address complex challenges in actuator development.

15302121.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15302121.value: This project focuses on developing advanced materials called GDY (graphdiyne) to create innovative devices known as electrochemical actuators. These actuators can convert electrical energy into mechanical movement, making them useful for a variety of applications, such as soft robotics and smart devices. The research involves several key steps. First, we created GDY materials and study their structure using various scientific techniques to understand their properties. Next, we tested these materials as components in new electrochemical devices, examining how well they store energy and produce movement. We will measure important factors like how much they can move and how long they last. Additionally, we developed a theoretical model to explain how these GDY-based actuators work at a molecular level. This model will help us predict how changes in the material's structure affect its performance. We compare our model's predictions with experimental results to ensure accuracy and make improvements if needed. Overall, this project aims to harness the unique properties of GDY to create more efficient and versatile actuators, potentially leading to breakthroughs in technology and new applications in various fields.

15302221.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15302221.value: 基於球面上人工神經網絡的學習

15302221.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15302221.value: Artificial neural networks (ANN’s), especially those with multiple layers and special structures, are widely applied with the name of deep learning, in the past decade for data mining. Deep learning is empirically proved able to solve sophisticated and challenging prediction problems. Meanwhile, theoretical research is fast developing in recent years. In this project, we plan to develop a series of new methodologies for the mathematical analysis of deep ANN. First, we shall study a family of dot product kernels defined on spheres, and obtain the approximation theoretical properties of the associated reproducing kernel spaces. These kernel functions provide flexible protocols to connect the regularity properties of target functions to the error of ANN approximations for mathematical analysis. Then, we plan to study the approximation error of different deep ANN’s, in terms of L-2, L-infinity, and reproducing kernel space metrics. Finally, we plan to study ANN for pairwise learning, based on our existing work on the relations between pairwise kernel spaces and pointwise kernel spaces. 人工神經網絡(ANN)，特別是具有多層和特殊結構的神經網絡，在過去十年中被稱為深度學習並被廣泛應用於數據挖掘。應用實踐證明了深度學習能夠解決複雜且具有挑戰性的預測問題。同時，近年來理論方面的研究也在快速發展。在此項目中，我們計劃發展一系列用於深度人工神經網絡的數學分析新方法。首先，我們將研究定義在球面上的一系列點積核，並獲得相關再生核空間的逼近理論性質。這些核函數提供了靈活的刻畫方法，將目標函數的正則性與ANN的逼近誤差聯繫起來，以進行數學分析。然後，我們計劃在L-2、L-無窮大和再生核空間度量方面研究不同深度ANN的逼近誤差。最後，我們計劃基於我們現有的關於成對核空間和逐點核空間之間關係的工作，研究用於成對學習的ANN。

15302321.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15302321.value: In this project, we aim to better understand the spectral properties of sample covariance matrix under high-dimensional time-series models of volatility such as Dynamic Conditional Correlation (DCC) model. We will investigate the limiting properties of the spectral distribution of sample covariance matrix under high-dimensional volatility models and show that the limit deviates from the i.i.d. data that share the same unconditional covariance structure under various asymptotic conditions of the model coefficients. Based on the understanding of the limiting spectral properties of sample covariance matrix, we will further develop proper shrinkage estimator to recover the eigenvalues of the unconditional correlation/covariance matrix under the high-dimensional volatility models. 本项目旨在更好地理解樣本協方差矩陣在高維波動率時間序列模型（例如動態條件相關（DCC）模型）下的譜特性。 我們將研究高維波動率模型下樣本協方差矩陣譜分佈的極限特性， 并證明該極限將偏離于與獨立同分佈情況下具有相同無條件協方差的極限譜分佈。 基於對樣本協方差矩陣極限譜性質的理解，我們將進一步開發合適的收縮估計法來恢復高維波動率模型下無條件相關/協方差矩陣的特徵值分佈。

15302321.label: Realisation of objectives
15302321.value: All project objectives have been achieved, resulting in one publication (Annals of Statistics) and two manuscripts currently under revision for the Journal of Econometrics. We conducted an in-depth investigation into the asymptotic spectral distribution of the sample covariance matrix under scalar BEKK models. We discovered that the limiting spectral distribution (LSD) of the sample covariance matrix may not follow the Mar\v{c}enko-Pastur law, which is the standard limit under the i.i.d. assumption. This discovery has significant implications; in particular, it implies that the nonlinear shrinkage estimator proposed by Engle, Ledoit, and Wolf (2019) may not be valid in this context. We further identified the exact condition under which the LSD deviates from the Mar\v{c}enko-Pastur law, or equivalently, the condition under which the conventional nonlinear shrinkage estimator fails. To address this issue, we proposed a time-variation adjusted (TV-adj) sample covariance matrix and proved that its LSD always follows the Mar\v{c}enko-Pastur law. Based on this novel asymptotic result, we developed a new nonlinear shrinkage estimator and proved its asymptotic optimality. Furthermore, we studied the estimation of high-dimensional covariance matrices under elliptical factor models assuming only the existence of $(2 + \epsilon)$-th moments. By developing a novel approach to remove the effect of heavy-tailed scale parameters, we proposed a new estimator that achieves a faster convergence rate than the widely used POET estimator (Fan et al., 2018). Finally, we addressed the estimation of large mean-variance efficient portfolios when returns exhibit both heteroscedasticity and heavy tails. We developed a novel method that integrates robust regressions and a self-normalization technique with the MAXSER method established in our previous work (Ao, Li, and Zheng, 2019, RFS). We proved that this method produces portfolios that approach mean-variance efficiency as both the number of assets and sample size grow to infinity. Moreover, we developed a conditional method that utilizes time-variability in the underlying parameters to reach asymptotic conditional mean-variance efficiency.

15302321.label: Major findings and research outcome
15302321.value: 1. We derived the complete asymptotics of the sample covariance matrix under high-dimensional BEKK models. In particular, we highlighted the inapplicability of conventional shrinkage covariance matrix estimators in the presence of dynamic volatility. Furthermore, we developed a new optimal nonlinear shrinkage estimator for the covariance matrix. These results have been published in the Annals of Statistics. 2. We studied the estimation of high-dimensional covariance matrices under elliptical factor models assuming only the existence of $(2 + \epsilon)$-th moments. We introduced a novel strategy to remove the effect of heavy-tailed scale parameters and proposed a robust pilot estimator that achieves a sub-Gaussian convergence rate. We further developed a covariance matrix estimator and demonstrated that it achieves a faster convergence rate than the widely used POET estimator (Fan et al., 2018). This paper is currently under revision for the Journal of Econometrics. 3. We addressed the estimation of large mean-variance efficient portfolios when returns exhibit both heteroscedasticity and heavy tails. We proposed a novel method, MAXSER-H, that integrates robust regressions and a self-normalization technique with the MAXSER method developed in our previous work (Ao, Li, and Zheng, 2019, RFS). We proved that MAXSER-H yields portfolios that approach mean-variance efficiency as both the number of assets and sample size grow to infinity. This paper is currently under revision for the Journal of Econometrics.

15302321.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15302321.value: The covariance matrix, and cross-sectional dependence more generally, are fundamentally important across a wide range of applications. The results of this project provide a theoretically sound foundation for further research in areas such as portfolio optimization, risk management, and advanced machine learning approaches, including distributionally robust learning.

15302321.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15302321.value: The findings of this project offer significant value for large-scale portfolio optimization and risk management. Our discoveries under high-dimensional BEKK models reveal the significant impact of dynamic volatility, and we provide the correct solution under such a setting. Additionally, our study on estimating covariance matrices under heavy-tailed models offers a superior alternative to current state-of-the-art methods. Finally, we developed a new method for constructing efficient portfolios when asset returns exhibit both heteroscedasticity and heavy-tailedness; this method is both theoretically significant and practically valuable for investors.

15302821.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15302821.value: 過渡金屬催化交叉偶聯反應是一種常用的碳–碳鍵和碳–雜原子鍵生成方法，並提供了一種高度通用和具吸引力的手段去合成天然產物、新藥物和新材料。在交叉偶聯反應中，新型配體的重要性體現在其和過渡金屬絡合後，能使具挑戰性的底物得以轉化，以及解決當前成鍵過程中存在問題和探索更具創新性的成鍵反應。因此，開發和探索簡單，易於制備和高度可調的配體仍然是一個重要的課題。此外，當有機分子中存在多個不同或相同類型的官能團時，選擇性地控制交叉偶聯反應的反應位點是一個具有挑戰性的問題。而利用改變催化劑中的配體以控制反應的化學/位元點選擇性是一種極具吸引力的方法。該項目將會設計合成新型多樣化的膦配體，研究其在具有挑戰性的選擇性偶聯反應的可行性及配合理論化學計算探索反應機理，並在碳–雜原子鍵斷裂反應中對新的和通用的交叉偶合夥伴進行研究。此外亦將探索不對稱的膦配體用於不對稱偶聯反應中的可行性。

15302821.label: Realisation of objectives
15302821.value: This is the completion report for Project 15302821. The objectives outlined in the proposed work have been successfully achieved. We systematically constructed a comprehensive library of alkyl-heterocycle-based phosphine ligands. In particular, a new class of indolyl phosphine ligands was successfully synthesized, featuring an innovative alkyl substituent at the C2 position of the indole framework. The alkyl-indolyl ligand scaffold was efficiently prepared from readily available phenylhydrazine and alkyl methyl ketones through a straightforward Fischer indole synthesis, followed by sequential N-methylation, bromination, and phosphination. One representative ligand from this family, SelectPhos, bearing a C2-cyclohexyl substituent, exhibited outstanding catalytic activity across a range of chemoselective transformations, including Suzuki–Miyaura coupling, desulfination, deuterodehalogenation, and phosphorylation reactions. Notably, these reactions were accomplished using polyhalogenated aryl triflates, in which an inversion of the conventional reactivity order was observed, favoring C–Cl over C–OTf bonds. These results have been disseminated through multiple peer reviewed publications (Chin. J. Chem. 2023, 41, 909–914; Org. Lett. 2023, 25, 8429–8433; J. Organomet. Chem. 2024, 1005, 122983; J. Org. Chem. 2024, 89, 16262–16268). Density functional theory studies revealed distinct coordination and interaction modes between ligands bearing C2-alkyl and C2-aryl substituents. The Pd–SelectPhos complex was found to preferentially undergo oxidative addition at C–Cl bonds rather than C–OTf bonds. This unusual reactivity and chemoselectivity were attributed to a synergistic combination of preagostic C–H···Pd interaction and steric hindrance provided by the C2-alkyl group. In parallel, we were invited to contribute a comprehensive review article to Organic Chemistry Frontiers summarizing recent advances in palladium-catalyzed coupling reactions and highlighting the influence of ligand properties on the chemoselectivity of aryl (pseudo)halides (Org. Chem. Front. 2023, 10, 4408–4436). This review critically discusses catalyst design principles and their roles in controlling chemoselectivity. Additionally, we developed a novel series of alkyl-pyrazole-based phosphine ligands featuring cycloalkyl substituents of varying ring sizes at the C3 and C5 positions. Pyrazole was selected as the ligand scaffold because of its structural versatility and ease of functional modification. The synthetic route is efficient and cost effective. Knorr synthesis using 1,3 diketones and hydrazine hydrate afforded 3,5-dialkyl pyrazole cores, which were subsequently N-alkylated, selectively brominated at the 4-position, and transformed into the corresponding phosphine ligands through lithiation followed by reaction with ClPR2. These ligands demonstrated excellent performance in chemoselective C–H arylation and amination reactions (Adv. Synth. Catal. 2024, 366, 1565–1574; Adv. Sci. 2024, 11, 2309192). Combined experimental and computational mechanistic studies indicated that the optimized ring sizes of the pyrazole phosphine ligands play a key role in lowering energy barriers in both reaction pathways. We were also invited by the Editor of Chem Catalysis to contribute a preview article on palladium-catalyzed desymmetric hydrophosphination of 3,3 disubstituted cyclopropenes (Chem Catal. 2022, 2, 2805–2807). Furthermore, we successfully developed chiral phosphine ligands that do not require laborious resolution steps. By incorporating a chiral auxiliary into the ligand scaffold, diastereomeric complexes were obtained and their stereochemical configurations were unambiguously assigned by single crystal X-ray diffraction. These chiral ligands were subsequently applied to asymmetric Suzuki–Miyaura cross-coupling reactions. Overall, the outcomes of this project fully meet the proposed objectives and have generated significant methodological and mechanistic advances in ligand design and palladium-catalyzed chemoselective transformations.

15302821.label: Major findings and research outcome
15302821.value: During this project, we developed several new classes of phosphine ligands and demonstrated their effectiveness in highly chemoselective palladium catalysis. A key achievement was the design of indolyl phosphine ligands bearing a C2-cyclohexyl substituent. In combination with Pd(OAc)2, t-BuPhSelectPhos exhibited outstanding activity and chemoselectivity in Pd-catalyzed desulfinative cross-coupling reactions of polyhalogenated aryl triflates with aryl sulfinate salts. Notably, this system enabled an inversion of the conventional reactivity order (C–Br > C–Cl > C–OTf), providing a simple and efficient approach to functionalized biaryl scaffolds with broad substrate scope (Chin. J. Chem. 2023, 41, 909–914). This work was featured on the journal Front Cover. Using the same ligand platform, we further developed a Pd-catalyzed chemoselective deuterodehalogenation of halogenated aryl triflates, employing isopropanol-d8 as a convenient deuterium source (Org. Lett. 2023, 25, 8429–8433). In addition, we established highly chemoselective Suzuki–Miyaura cross-coupling reactions of polyhalogenated aryl triflates with (hetero)aryl boronic acids. Excellent reactivity and selectivity were achieved with palladium loadings as low as 0.02 mol%, and sequential double functionalization of bromochloroaryl triflates enabled efficient access to terphenyl derivatives (J. Organomet. Chem. 2024, 1005, 122983). We also advanced the synthesis of organophosphorus compounds through Pd-catalyzed chemoselective phosphorylation using SelectPhos ligands (J. Org. Chem. 2024, 89, 16262–16268). In parallel, we developed a new family of pyrazole-alkyl phosphine ligands featuring tunable cycloalkyl ring sizes at the C3 and C5 positions. These ligands showed exceptional performance in chemoselective C–H arylation and amination reactions. High regioselectivity was achieved across a wide range of heterocycles under additive-free conditions (Adv. Sci. 2024, 11, 2309192). In amination, the Pd/BirdPhos system enabled selective activation of C–Cl bonds over C–OTf bonds and was highlighted as a Very Important Publication with a Front Cover (Adv. Synth. Catal. 2024, 366, 1565–1574). Finally, we were invited to contribute a comprehensive review on recent advances in the application of ligands in Pd-catalyzed chemoselective coupling reactions, which was featured on the Front Cover (Org. Chem. Front. 2023, 10, 4408–4436).

15302821.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15302821.value: The outcomes of this research project offer significant opportunities to advance the fields of catalyst design and cross-coupling catalysis. These advances hold strong potential for further fundamental studies and practical applications, particularly in pharmaceuticals and functional materials. Moving forward, future efforts will focus on the continued development of phosphine ligands featuring alkyl substituents on the side ring and their application to expand reaction scope and address emerging challenges in new catalytic transformations.

15302821.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15302821.value: This research project focused on the development of new alkyl-heterocycle-based phosphine ligands, together with the exploration and establishment of novel and versatile cross-coupling partners. These studies demonstrate that rational ligand design can enable unconventional bond activation modes, thereby expanding the scope and synthetic utility of Pd-catalyzed chemoselective transformations. The methods provide efficient and practical approaches for constructing molecules that are important in pharmaceutical research and advanced materials development. We believe that the unique attributes derived from alkyl-heterocycle-based phosphine ligands will open new directions for future ligand design and facilitate the discovery of new catalytic reactions.

15303021.label: Project Objectives
15303021.value: Firstofall,weintendtostudythe(numerical)reconstructionofthediffusioncoefficientandpotential coefficient in the elliptic equation simultaneously from two internal measurements of solutions. The (stably) reconstruction of diffusion coefficient could be obtained by reformulating the problem and using an energy argument with novel test functions and some provable positivity conditions. Then with the recovered diffusion coefficient, the potential coefficient could be reconstructed by constructing a fix point iteration. The (linear) convergence of the iteration follows can be verified by emplying the strong maximum principle of the elliptic equation and contraction mapping theorem. Finally, we intend to propose (discrete) regularized scheme, and examine the convergence (for rough data) or derive error estimate (under some suitable assumptions of problem data). Second, we shall extend the argument to evolution problems, such as the parabolic equation. Analogous to the elliptic equation, we aim to show the uniqueness and some Hölder-type stability estimates of the reconstruction of diffusion and potential coefficients from two interior measurements, and to propose and analyze (discretized) numerical scheme with provable error estimates. When compared with the elliptic counterpart, the analysis is expected to rely on a new weighting in time direction and the maximal L^p regularity of parabolic equations. We shall also study this inverse problem of time-fractional evolution models, arising from the modeling of subdiffusion dynamics, whose mathematical and numerical analysis is more challenging compared with its parabolic counterpart, since the presence of fractional derivative may significantly change diffusive dynamics and solution regularity. Further, many powerful calculus tools such as chain rule and integration by parts formula are not applicable. We intend to propose a novel argument for the fractional models by employing (discrete) fractional maximal L^p regularity, fractional-type Grönwall’s inquality, and some non-standard error estimates in weighted Sobolev spaces. Third and last, we focus on the numerical analysis of fractional Calderón problem where the equation involves a fractional Laplacian, which often arises in the superdiffusion models. It is already known that the potential coefficient (or diffusion coefficient) can be uniquely determined by a single mea surement in the exterior domain. This contrasts sharply with the classical Calderón problem. In the procedure of reconstruction, we have to evaluate some actions of fractional Laplacian, which is a non- local operator. This requires to evaluate the multiplication between full-matrices and vectors (in the discrete system), whose computational complexity is O(N2) for nonuniform meshes, where N denotes the number of degrees of freedom. We shall propose a low-rank approximation by applying Hierarchical matrices, which potentially enables reducing the computational complexity to O(KN logN) (or O(KN) under some additional assumptions), where K denotes the parameter of low-rank approximation. Moreover, since the problem is severely ill-posed, we have to propose some regularization methods in order to control the condition number of the discrete system. Finally, we intend to analyze the proposed (regularized) numerical scheme and derive an error estimate which is expected to expressed in terms of noise level, regularization parameter, and disretization parameter. The analy- sis should employ some nonstandard energy argument as well as the (optimal) logarithmic stability estimate.

15303021.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15303021.value: Over the last few decades, inverse problems for PDEs have attracted substantial attention among mathematicians and engineers, due to their numerous important applications. These inverse problems are often mathematically and numerically more challenging that the corresponding direct problems, due to a lack of conventional well-posedness (existence, uniqueness, and continuous dependence on the data). In particular, inverse problems for elliptic and parabolic type PDEs have been extensively studied, and many important theoretical results, e.g., uniqueness and stability, have been established. Nonetheless, much work is still needed in develop efficient inversion algorithms with provable error bounds, when compared with more classical direct problems. In this project, we shall design and analyze numerical algorithms for approximately solving a class of nonlinear inverse problems for PDEs, i.e., to identify distributed parameters in PDEs from various observation data. The aim is to develop numerical schemes with provable error estimates, and also design fast algorithms. This project consists of three parts. First, we shall investigate the simultaneous (numerical) identification of two distributed parameters, diffusion and potential coefficients, in an elliptic problem from two internal observations of the solution. This is long standing challenge, due to the often dramatic difference in the sensitivity of the data with respect to the parameters of interest. The approach we shall pursue relies heavily on a weighted stability estimate and energy technique with special test functions, and a constructive algorithm based on fixed point iteration. Second, we shall extend the argument to evolution problems, including classical parabolic problems and time-fractional subdiffusion. The analysis also employs a new weighting in the time direction and the maximal L^p regularity of parabolic equations. Meanwhile, we shall discuss time-fractional subdiffusion models, for which the inverse problem is more challenging since many PDE tools such as chain rule and integration by parts formula are not applicable. Third and finally, we shall study the numerical treatment and error analysis of the so-called fractional Calderón problem, where the equation involves a fractional Laplacian. We shall develop regularized numerical schemes (with provable error estimate) to recover the potential term from single measurement, A fast algorithm using low-rank approximation will be proposed to efficiently solve the discrete system. 在过去几十年间反问题在数学界和工程界都受到了广泛的关注。相比于正问题，反问题具有很强的不适定性，因此通常都更具挑战性。一类重要的反问题是椭圆方程和抛物方程中的分布式参数的反演问题，也已经有了许多深入的理论研究。然而，相关数值方法的研究依然很缺乏。在这个项目中，我们将为一些典型的分布式参数的反演问题，构造并分析有效地数值方法。本项目分为三个部分。首先，我们将研究如何通过两次内部观测，同时反演椭圆方程中两个参数，即扩散系数和反应系数。这个问题的理论分析主要依赖于加权的稳定性估计、使用特殊测试函数的能量方法、以及一个构造性的不动点迭代。此外，我们将把以上的理论和方法推广到抛物型方程以及分数阶亚扩散方程中。 最后，我们将为分数阶非局部Calderon问题构造高效稳定的数值方法，通过单次非局部边界观测，反演非局部方程中的扩散系数或势参数。

15303021.label: Realisation of objectives
15303021.value: We have made significant progress and successfully achieved the objectives of this project. Objective 1: Reconstruction of the diffusion and potential coefficients in an elliptic equation We accomplished the objective, which involved studying the numerical reconstruction of the diffusion and potential coefficients in an elliptic equation simultaneously from two internal measurements of the solutions. A decoupled algorithm was developed to sequentially recover these two parameters. In the first step, we implemented a straightforward reformulation that reduced the problem to the standard task of identifying the diffusion coefficient. This coefficient was then numerically reconstructed, without requiring prior knowledge of the potential, by employing an output least-squares method combined with finite element discretization. In the second step, the previously recovered diffusion coefficient was utilized to reconstruct the potential coefficient using a method similar to the first step. Our approach was motivated by a constructive conditional stability result, and we provided rigorous a priori error estimates in L^2 norm for both the recovered diffusion and potential coefficients. Our analysis also extends to the unsupervised learning approaches with neural network approximations. Objective 2: Reconstruction of the diffusion and potential coefficients in parabolic equations We extended the argument to the parabolic equation and investigated the conditional stability of the reconstruction, developed a decoupled numerical algorithm to sequentially identify the two parameters, and proposed a fully discrete scheme with provable error bounds. The approach employed several technical methods, including decoupling the original problem into two single-parameter identification problems, deriving weighted L^2 stability estimates using an energy argument with specially designed test functions, and applying numerical analysis techniques for solving the direct problems. The argument also works for time-fractional subdiffusion models. Objective 3: Parameter identification problem for space-fractional models We have made significant progress in the numerical analysis of inverse problems for space-fractional models. For example, we studied the recovery of a spatially dependent source in a one-dimensional space-time fractional wave equation using boundary measurement data collected at a single endpoint. We introduced a bi-orthogonal basis for the Mittag-Leffler functions, which allowed us to establish uniqueness and Hölder-type stability estimates. To numerically solve the inverse source problem, we employed a Tikhonov regularization method and conduct extensive numerical experiments to demonstrate the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed method and to validate our theoretical findings.

These findings have been published in the IMA Journal of Numerical Analysis [5] and the SIAM Journal on Imaging Sciences [2]. 2. We conducted a numerical analysis of the inverse coefficient problem in parabolic equations. Our work focused on investigating the conditional stability of the reconstruction, developing a decoupled numerical algorithm to sequentially identify the two unknown parameters, and proposing a fully discrete scheme with provable error bounds. The approach utilized several advanced techniques, including decoupling the original problem into two simpler single-parameter identification problems, deriving weighted L^2 stability estimates through an energy argument with carefully designed test functions, and employing numerical analysis methods to solve the associated direct problems. This research has been published in the SIAM Journal on Numerical Analysis ([6]) and Numerische Mathematik [11]. 3. We investigated the recovery of a spatially dependent source in a one-dimensional space-time fractional wave equation using boundary measurement data collected at a single endpoint. To address this problem, we introduced a bi-orthogonal basis for the Mittag-Leffler functions, which enabled us to establish both uniqueness and Hölder-type stability estimates. For the numerical solution of the inverse source problem, we employed a Tikhonov regularization method and conducted extensive numerical experiments to demonstrate the accuracy, efficiency, and robustness of the proposed approach. A paper detailing this work has been submitted to Inverse Problems and is currently under review [14].

15303021.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15303021.value: The findings of this project open several avenues for further development and applications. Building on the progress made in reconstructing the diffusion and potential coefficients in elliptic and parabolic equations, future research could focus on extending these methodologies to more complex systems, such as coupled multi-physics models. The decoupled algorithms developed in this project could be further optimized for computational efficiency, particularly for large-scale problems, by applying advanced numerical techniques such as adaptive mesh refinement or parallel computing. Additionally, the extension of the argument to time-fractional and space-fractional models highlights significant potential for addressing inverse problems in anomalous diffusion and other nonlocal processes. Future work could explore these models in multi-dimensional settings or under noisy and incomplete measurement data, with the aim of improving robustness and practical applicability. Furthermore, integrating machine learning techniques, such as physics-informed neural networks, could enhance the efficiency of parameter reconstruction and provide a powerful hybrid approach to solving inverse problems. The proposed course of action includes extending the theoretical framework, improving computational methods, and applying the developed techniques to real-world problems, such as geophysical imaging, biomedical diagnostics, and industrial process monitoring. These efforts will broaden the impact and utility of the research outcomes.

15303021.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15303021.value: Inverse problems for PDEs are inherently challenging, both mathematically and numerically, due to the lack of conventional well-posedness, which includes existence, uniqueness, and continuous dependence on the data. While significant theoretical progress has been achieved, particularly in establishing key results on uniqueness and stability, there remains a pressing need to develop efficient inversion algorithms with provable error bounds, especially when compared to the more mature methods available for direct problems. This project aims to build a solid foundation in the numerical analysis of PDE-related inverse problems. Specifically, it focuses on designing and analyzing numerical algorithms to approximate solutions for a class of nonlinear inverse problems for PDEs. The primary objective is to identify distributed parameters in PDEs using various forms of observational data, with the overarching goal of bridging the gap between theoretical advancements and practical computational methods. We have made significant progress and successfully achieved the objectives of this project. First of all, we developed and analyzed a decoupled scheme for numerical reconstruction of the diffusion and potential coefficients in an elliptic equation simultaneously from two internal measurements of the solutions. Our approach was motivated by a constructive conditional stability result, and we provided rigorous a priori error estimates for the numerical reconstruction. Moreover, we extended the argument to parabolic equations. Specifically, we demonstrated the uniqueness and Hölder-type stability estimates that inspired proposed a numerical scheme with provable error estimates. Lastly, we addressed the analysis and numerical treatment of the inverse source problem for space-time nonlocal models, which are widely used to model anomalous diffusion in various applications, such as geophysics, biology, and finance.

15303121.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15303121.value: This project focuses on convergence and stability analysis of energy stable and bound-preserving numerical schemes for binary fluid-surfactant phase-field equations. Phase-field methods have been extensively used to explore the interfacial dynamics with surfactants in various fields. We will consider a binary fluid-surfactant phase-field system, which admits two intrinsic properties: nonlinear energy stability and the uniform bound of the surfactant concentration. Computationally, it is highly desirable to develop efficient and accurate numerical methods that preserve the intrinsic properties of differential equations as much as possible. There have been numerous works on energy stable numerical methods for binary fluid-surfactant phase field equations, while theoretical investigations on bound-preserving of the surfactant concentration are very limited, even though many requirements have been raised in numerical simulations. In this project, we will develop efficient first- and second-order linear energy stable and bound-preserving numerical schemes for binary fluid-surfactant phase field equations, based on the decoupling of the system and a stabilization technique. A first-order exponential time differencing (ETD) method and a second-order ETD Runge-Kutta method will be explored for time integration of both the fluid density equation and the surfactant equation. In the energy stability analysis, a strong assumption on the L-infinity bound of numerical solutions is usually needed due to the fourth-order dissipation nature of fluid densities. We will perform convergence analysis with a high-order consistency analysis for the fluid density equation such that this assumption could be removed in the energy stability analysis. For the bound-preserving investigation of the surfactant concentration, we will employ the maximum bound principle preserving numerical analysis method developed in our recent work. The main contribution of this project is the systematic analysis of efficient numerical schemes for binary fluid-surfactant phase field equations, which preserve energy stability and the uniform bound of the surfactant concentration simultaneously. 本項目主要研究含表面活性劑兩相流體相場方程的能量穩定和保界數值算法的收斂性和穩定性。 相場方法已經被廣泛地用於探索許多領域中與表面活性劑有關的界面動力學。 我們將考慮一個含表面活性劑兩相流體的相場系統，它有兩個內在屬性：非線性能量穩定性和表面活性劑濃度的一致有界性。在計算上設計有效且精確的，能盡可能保證微分方程這兩個內在屬性的數值方法是十分必要的。目前有許多針對含表面活性劑兩相流體相場方程能量穩定性方法的數值工作，但在表面活性劑濃度的保界上，盡管在數值模擬的時候提出了很多要求，相關的理論研究卻十分有限。 在本項目中，我們基於系統解耦和穩定性技巧，為含表面活性劑兩相流體相場方程設計有效的一階和二階線性保結構數值格式。一階指數時間差分方法和二階指數時間差分龍格-庫塔方法將會被用於流體密度方程和表面活性劑方程的時間積分。在能量穩定性分析上，由於流體密度的四階耗散性質，通常要對數值解的L無窮有界性給一個很強的假設。我們將在對流體密度方程進行收斂性分析時引入高階相容性分析技巧，以便在能量穩定性分析中消除這一假設。對於表面活性劑濃度的保界研究，我們將采用我們最近工作中發展起來的保最大界性質的數值分析方法。本項目的主要貢獻是將系統地分析含表面活性劑兩相流體相場方程的有效數值格式，該格式既保持能量穩定性，又同時保持表面活性劑濃度的一致有界性。

15303121.label: Major findings and research outcome
15303121.value: In this project, we have developed efficient numerical schemes for binary fluid-surfactant phase-field equations.The major findings are as follows: 1. In Dong-Li-Qiao-Zhang, 2023, we proposed the first-order ETD scheme for the binary fluid-surfactant system. We first apply the convex splitting method to the two-dimensional energy functional, and divide each equation in the system into the linear and nonlinear parts. This work addresses the Objectives 1-2. 2. In Duan-Ju-Li-Qiao, 2024, we constructed the first- and second-order numerical schemes for the Cahn–Hilliard type of binary fluid-surfactant model. We introduce three stabilization terms to apply the linear convex splitting of the energy functional. Then we adopt the central difference spatial method combined with ETD methods for spatial and temporal approximations. We conduct the convergence analysis and demonstrate the bound-preserving property for the numerical schemes, applying the high-order consistency analysis specially to the first-order case. Furthermore, we establish the energy stability. This work addresses Objectives 1-3. 3. In Duan-Ju-Li-Qiao, 2026, we studied the binary fluid-surfactant phase-field model which consists of two Cahn-Hilliard type equations. By the introduction of three stabilization terms, we adopt a linear convex splitting of the energy functional. Then the third-order ETD method and the Fourier spectral method are applied for temporal and spatial approximations. The developed scheme is proved to be energy stable, and the convergence and bound-preserving property are proved. This work addresses Objectives 1-2. 4. In Ma-Qiao, 2023, we proposed a decoupled numerical scheme for the time-dependent Ginzburg--Landau equations within the temporal gauge framework. The spatial discretization employs the second type Nedelec elements for the magnetic potential and the linear element for the order parameter, and we apply a linearized backward Euler method and the first-order ETD method for time discretization. We prove the maximum bound principle for the order parameter. This strategy can be used for binary fluid-surfactant phase-field equations. This work addresses Objective 2-3. 5. In Duan-Ju-Li-Qiao, In Preparation, we developed an exponential time differencing method for the hydrodynamics-coupled binary fluid-surfactant phase-field model. To facilitate the time integration, a gauge variable and an auxiliary field are introduced to reformulate the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations into a gauge system. The exponential time differencing method is then applied to the whole system with some stabilization terms added to ensure the stability of the schemes. This work addresses the Objectives 1-2.

15303121.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15303121.value: In the future research, we will further investigate the high-order stable numerical schemes for the hydrodynamics-coupled binary fluid-surfactant phase-field model. The logarithmic Flory–Huggins potential will be carefully treated based on the convex-splitting method. We will develop a tailored variable splitting strategy within the alternating direction method of multipliers framework, which can efficiently decouples the challenging logarithmic nonlinearity and enable effective handling of singularities.

15303121.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15303121.value: This project aims to improve the numerical methods used to simulate how two types of liquids (like oil and water) mixed with surfactants (like soap) interact with each other. Simulating these mixtures accurately is important for applications ranging from materials science to medicine. Current numerical methods can sometimes give results that are not physically realistic—for example, the amount of surfactant might go outside believable ranges, or the system might become unstable over time. To address this, our project develops new computational methods that make sure these kinds of problems do not happen. We focus on making sure our simulation results stay within reasonable and reliable bounds, and that they remain stable over time, even for complex mixtures. We use advanced mathematical techniques to analyze and prove that our new methods work as intended for the studied binary fluid-surfactant phase-field system. We expect to provide powerful tools for researchers and engineers, so they can more reliably and efficiently simulate mixtures of fluids and surfactants for a variety of scientific and engineering purposes.

15303321.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15303321.value: Bispecific antibodies have been a promising next-generation cancer treatment with enhanced clinical efficacy and safety. The bispecific antibody fuses two different kinds of antibodies into one entity that allows enhanced target recognition and opens up a wide range of applications. Generally, there are 60 different constructs of bispecific antibodies, mainly grouped into the IgG-like and non-IgG-like structures. Among them, two bispecific antibodies gain approval from the FDA, and over 85 bispecific antibodies are at different stages of clinical trials. Despite the fascinating applications of bispecific antibodies, designing and producing bispecific antibodies remain tedious and challenging, leading to the high production cost and hindering further research and development. In this proposal, a new and highly efficient chemical methodology will be described for the rapid development and generation of novel bispecific antibodies. The unprecedented strategy utilized our novel one-pot peptide cyclization and protein conjugation chemical reaction to join tumor-targeting cyclic peptides to a monoclonal antibody. This design combines the merits of monoclonal antibody and serum stable tumor-targeting cyclic peptides, which giving the monoclonal antibody an additional targeting ability to form a bispecific antibody. Our preliminary data showed that our bispecific antibody prototype could exhibit bispecific binding towards two target cells in vitro. With this simple, flexible, and robust one-pot reaction, a small library of novel immune cell-engaging bispecific antibodies will be designed and constructed. Lastly, the bispecific antibodies will be characterized against a panel of in vitro assays and in vivo models. The success of using such chemical approach to produce bispecific antibodies will give rise to new type of bispecific antibodies and a new platform for the rapid generation of new bispecific antibodies for research and therapeutic uses. 雙特異性抗體是具有增強的臨床療效和安全性的下一代癌症治療。雙特異性抗體將兩種不同類型的抗體融入一個實體中，允許增強目標識別，並打開各種應用。現在有大約60種不同的雙特異性抗體構建體，主要分組成IgG樣和非IgG樣結構。其中，兩個雙特異性抗體來自FDA的批准，超過85個雙特異性抗體是臨床試驗的不同階段。儘管有雙特異性抗體的迷戀應用，但設計和生產雙特異性抗體仍然乏味和挑戰，導致高生產成本和妨礙進一步的研發。在這一提議中，將描述新的和高效的化學方法，用於快速發展和產生新的雙特異性抗體。前所未有的策略利用我們的新型單盆肽環化和蛋白質綴合化學反應，將腫瘤靶向環狀肽加入單克隆抗體。該設計結合了單克隆抗體和血清穩定腫瘤靶向環狀肽的優點，其給予單克隆抗體的另外的靶向能力以形成雙特異性抗體。我們的初步數據顯示，我們的雙特異性抗體原型可以在體外表現出對兩個靶細胞的雙特異性結合。通過這種簡單，靈活，穩健的單鍋反應，將設計和構建一個小型免疫細胞接合的雙特異性抗體的小型文庫。最後，雙特異性抗體將表徵在體外測定和體內模型中的表徵。使用這種化學方法產生雙特異性抗體的成功將引起新型的雙特異性抗體和新的新特異性抗體的新平台，用於研究和治療用途的新的雙特異性抗體。

15303321.label: Realisation of objectives
15303321.value: The project successfully achieved, and in several areas exceeded, the revised objectives through the development, optimization, and validation of two novel classes of chemically assembled bispecific antibodies. The work completed resulted in two full manuscripts, multiple technological advancements, and substantial external recognition through international competitions, demonstrating both scientific and translational impact. Objective 1: Design and synthesis of immune cell-engaging bispecific antibodies using one-pot peptide cyclization and conjugation This objective was fully achieved. We established a robust and efficient one-pot chemical methodology to conjugate tumor-targeting cyclic peptides onto monoclonal antibodies. The workflow comprised (1) peptide dimer or cyclic peptide generation via thiol-mediated cyclization using a bifunctional linker; and (2) rapid ortho-phthalaldehyde–based conjugation to antibodies under mild conditions. The reactions proceeded with high conversion (>90%) and were reproducibly optimized to obtain controlled peptide-to-antibody ratios. Two major bispecific platforms were successfully developed: 1. Peptidic Bispecific Antibody (pBsAb) — A cyclic EGFR-binding peptide was conjugated to anti–SIRP-α IgG to produce a bispecific molecule capable of macrophage engagement. 2. Dendritic Bispecific Antibody (dBsAb) — A multivalent GPC3-binding peptide dimer was conjugated to anti–SIRP-α IgG, generating a dendritic architecture with enhanced avidity and superior biological performance. Both molecules were fully characterized using SDS-PAGE, ESI-MS/MALDI-TOF, and chromatography. The dendritic variant displayed excellent stability and maintained Fc integrity. This objective was therefore not only met but expanded to include the demonstration of multi-valent architectures with enhanced functional capabilities. Objective 2: Investigation of target selectivity and binding affinity This objective was fully achieved. Through ELISA, flow cytometry, and confocal microscopy, we established that both pBsAb and dBsAb retained their native antigen binding (SIRP-α) while acquiring high-affinity binding to the tumor targets (EGFR or GPC3). The dBsAb, in particular, exhibited nanomolar affinity and clear avidity advantages over monomeric formats. Key achievements include: Dual specificity confirmed across multiple cell lines with differential target expression. Preserved SIRP-α binding despite extensive surface modification. Serum stability maintained over 48 hours. Enhanced avidity demonstrated in competitive binding assays for dBsAb. Although the original plan referenced SPR for affinity determination, we adopted ELISA-based affinity and competitive binding assays instead due to instrument availability constraints. These approaches successfully generated high-quality quantitative binding data that fulfilled the objective. Objective 3: Evaluation of cell–cell interactions and ADCC-related immune activation This objective was fully achieved and scientifically expanded. Using time-lapse confocal microscopy, fluorescence imaging, and flow cytometry, we demonstrated that both bispecific antibodies effectively mediated macrophage–cancer cell interactions. Notably: dBsAb induced up to a 9-fold increase in macrophage adhesion relative to parental antibodies. Significant enhancement of phagocytosis was observed, with >2-fold increases in double-positive macrophage populations. The bispecifics effectively blocked the CD47–SIRP-α checkpoint, enabling macrophage activation. Cytotoxicity assays confirmed the selective elimination of target-expressing cancer cells. These findings support the mechanistic hypothesis that chemical bispecific assembly can potentiate macrophage-mediated tumor clearance. Objective 4 (Original only): In vivo anticancer validation Although removed from the revised objectives due to reviewer feedback and resource considerations, this objective was nonetheless successfully completed for the dendritic bispecific candidate. In vivo studies in a murine hepatocellular carcinoma model demonstrated: 68% tumor reduction after three doses. Dense macrophage infiltration and M1-like activation. No observable systemic toxicity. These results significantly elevate the translational value of the platform and provide preclinical validation beyond what was required in the revised objectives. Overall Achievement and Impact All revised objectives have been fully realized, with several achievements going beyond the proposed scope: Two complete manuscripts were produced, establishing both conceptual and applied breakthroughs. A patent portfolio has been generated based on these technologies. The project directly contributed to PolyU’s success in the international iGEM competition, with teams earning Silver (2023) and Gold (2024) awards for bispecific antibody and nanobody designs inspired by this research direction. In summary, the project successfully delivered a scalable, rapid, and versatile chemical platform for constructing immune-engaging bispecific antibodies, demonstrated its biological efficacy, and produced significant academic and translational outcomes. The groundwork laid by this project will continue to support future therapeutic innovation and commercialization pathways.

15303321.label: Major findings and research outcome
15303321.value: With the support of the awarded funding, our team successfully generated two complementary manuscripts, each establishing a key component of a new chemical platform for rapid bispecific antibody construction. The first manuscript, Macrophage-Engaging Peptidic Bispecific Antibody (pBsAb) for Immunotherapy via Facile Bioconjugation Strategy, reports a peptidic bispecific antibody (pBsAb) constructed by chemically cyclising and conjugating EGFR-targeting cyclic peptides onto an anti–SIRP-α monoclonal antibody. This study demonstrated that our bioorthogonal cyclization–conjugation method could endow an existing IgG with a second, fully functional antigen-binding capability, resulting in enhanced macrophage–cancer cell interaction, blockade of the CD47–SIRP-α axis, and potent antibody-dependent cellular phagocytosis. This manuscript was published in Chemical Science in 2024. Building upon this foundation, the second manuscript, Chemical Assembling of Glypican-3 × SIRP-α Dendritic Bispecific Macrophage-Engager for Immunotherapy Against Liver Cancer, advances the methodology by introducing a dendritic bispecific antibody (dBsAb) featuring multivalent glypican-3 (GPC3) peptide dimers grafted onto anti–SIRP-α IgG. This dendritic geometry significantly boosted avidity, accelerated immune-synapse formation, and produced superior macrophage recruitment and phagocytic activity compared to monomeric formats. In mouse models of liver cancer, the dBsAb achieved 68% tumor reduction, intense macrophage infiltration, and strong M1 activation with no measurable toxicity, establishing a powerful proof-of-concept for macrophage-engaging bispecific therapeutics. This manuscript is currently under final revision in MedComm. Together, these two studies demonstrate a cohesive technological pipeline: from developing a robust, modular peptide-to-antibody conjugation chemistry to applying this chemistry toward next-generation immunotherapeutic bispecifics. The platform bypasses heavy- and light-chain mispairing issues inherent in recombinant bispecific antibody production and allows rapid (<4 h), scalable, and cost-effective generation of bispecific constructs with customizable valency and target combinations. Impact & Future Potential This chemically driven antibody-engineering strategy represents a paradigm shift in bispecific antibody development. Its plug-and-play versatility enables the rapid exploration of novel target pairs, creation of macrophage engagers tailored for solid tumors, and integration with peptides, small molecules, or even aptamers. Beyond liver cancer, the platform could be adapted to target pancreatic, colorectal, and lung cancers, or to engineer multi-specific immune-modulating biologics. The method also lays the groundwork for future preclinical development, manufacturing translation, and clinical candidate generation.

15303321.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15303321.value: Building on the strong foundation established through the two completed manuscripts, our bispecific antibody platform has already progressed toward commercial translation. We have filed patent applications covering the key chemical conjugation technologies and dendritic bispecific antibody designs. To further accelerate development, a university spin-off, Abismuno Scientific Limited, has been established to commercialize this platform. The company has already secured two competitive funding awards—PolyU MicroFund and the Technology Start-up Support Scheme for Universities (TSSSU) by ITF, demonstrating strong external validation of the technology’s potential. The next phase will focus on advancing the glypican-3 × SIRP-α macrophage-engaging bispecific antibody toward preclinical development, including pharmacokinetics, toxicity evaluation, and assessment in additional orthotopic and immunocompetent models. Parallel efforts will refine conjugation chemistry to enhance product homogeneity and scalability, supporting future GMP-compatible manufacturing. Strategically, the platform will also be extended to generate new antigen combinations and multi-specific constructs, enabling rapid tailoring of immune-engaging biologics for different solid tumors. Through Abismuno Scientific Limited, we aim to pursue industry partnerships, co-development opportunities, and long-term translation toward clinical candidate development.

15303321.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15303321.value: This grant developed two innovative chemical approaches to create next-generation cancer-fighting antibodies more efficiently and effectively. Conventional bispecific antibodies designed to target cancer cells while activating immune cells are powerful but extremely difficult and expensive to manufacture. Our research shows that chemical methods can produce these advanced therapeutics more rapidly, reliably, and at lower cost. The first study demonstrated a new peptidic bispecific antibody, created by chemically attaching a tumor-targeting peptide onto an existing antibody. This simple modification allowed a single antibody to both recognize cancer cells and activate macrophages, the immune cells responsible for engulfing harmful cells. The second study expanded this concept by developing a dendritic bispecific antibody, featuring multiple tumor-targeting peptides on one antibody to greatly enhance tumor recognition and immune engagement. This molecule showed anti-tumor activity in laboratory and animal models of liver cancer, significantly shrinking tumors with no detectable toxicity. Together, these two works highlight a flexible, fast, and scalable platform for generating potent bispecific antibodies. The chemical strategy reduces production complexity, avoids engineering challenges, and enables rapid exploration of target combinations. This platform has the potential to accelerate the development of precise, accessible, and effective treatments for liver cancer and other difficult-to-treat solid tumors.

15303521.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15303521.value: 鈮酸鋰具有寬頻透射、高折射率、非線性係數大的優點，是基本的非線性光學材料之一。目前，在許多重要的激光光源、集成光子電路和二次諧波產生中都應用到鈮酸鋰。Von Neumann 和 Wigner1929 年首次提出了連續體束縛態 (BIC)，該束縛態與連續光譜的輻射波共存，並且完全束縛，沒有任何向外輻射的輻射波，具有超高品質因子 (Q-factor) 是連續體束縛態的關鍵重要性質，近年來，Yuri Kivshar 等人，提出連續體束縛態可以顯著增強多階非線性諧振。在這個研究計畫中，我們將計算、設計、製造和表徵新型鈮酸鋰超表面納米結構用於發展超高品質因子連續體束縛態的超表面非線性倍頻元件。依據能帶理論，從理論上研究超表面連續體束縛態，並通過模擬計算鈮酸鋰元件界面處的超表面共振光譜，來分析研究連續體束縛態，發展基於超表面納米結構、連續體束縛態和二次諧振產生的高階計算和模擬工作，應用於設計新型超表面納米結構的佈局。基於在先進納米製造方面的成功經驗和能力，我們將製造和表徵新型超表面樣品，以實現鈮酸鋰連續體束縛態二次諧振產生。我們的測量和表徵結果將驗證基於鈮酸鋰的連續體束縛態增強二次諧振產生的新型元光學器件。我們的目標是了解連續體束縛態增強二次諧振產生效應的機制，並將這一發現應用於新型超表面光學非線性器件的研究開發，期許項目的實驗和理論研究成果，將成為下一代高效納米光子學科技創新，創造出重要的連續體束縛態增強二次諧振產生的光學超表面元件及其應用系統。

15303521.label: Realisation of objectives
15303521.value: 5.3.1. BICs physics in local to nonlocal transitions for high Q resonance (Objectives 1 and 5) In this research, we addressed the long-standing contradiction between the inherently high loss of metallic materials and the requirement for a high resonant quality factor. By introducing a geometric dimensionality reduction strategy, namely reducing the structural height of metallic nanoarrays while keeping lateral dimensions fixed, we demonstrated a clear transition of the resonant mode from localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) to non-localized surface plasmon polariton (SPP). This transition dramatically decreases material dissipation, as the electromagnetic energy gradually shifts from being confined at the high-loss metal–air interface to being distributed in the lossless surrounding medium. As a result, the quality factor of the resonance increases by nearly two orders of magnitude—from values below 20 in the LSPR regime to about 3800 in the trapped SPP regime. Furthermore, our analysis reveals that this effect is not specific to one geometry but represents a general physical law for metallic nanoarrays. As the height decreases, the resonant wavelength continuously approaches the array period (Rayleigh anomaly), the mode volume expands, and the resonance evolves from a bright radiative mode to a dark trapped SPP mode. Importantly, the results show a universal scaling behavior, indicating that reducing structural height not only flattens the geometry but also effectively reduces intrinsic metallic loss in an exponential manner. Overall, this work provides both a practical design strategy and a fundamental insight: the dimensionality reduction of metallic nanoarrays transforms high-loss localized resonances into low-loss collective SPP modes, thereby overcoming the intrinsic Q-factor limit of plasmonics and bridging the gap between LSPR and SPP regimes. This work primarily aligns with Objectives 1 and 5. Objective 1: "To develop the design principle and simulation for introducing the BIC with the nonlinear meta-optical device..." The ultra-high Q-factor of the BIC can be used to enhance the efficiency of the generated nonlinear signal." This work develops a geometric dimensionality reduction design principle to achieve high-Q resonances (trapped SPPs, a type of BIC-related phenomenon) on a metallic platform, directly addressing the enhancement of light-matter interaction efficiency, which is foundational for nonlinear enhancement. Objective 5: "To understand the mechanism of the BIC enhanced SHG effect..." This work elucidates the transition from LSPR to trapped SPP, the associated loss reduction, and the universal inverse square-root scaling between Q and detuning, providing a fundamental understanding critical for leveraging high-Q resonances in nonlinear processes like SHG. 5.3.2. BICs physics in nonlocal phase modulation (Objectives 1,2, and 5) In this research, based on bound states in the continuum (BICs) in dielectric materials, we successfully designed and verified a novel nonlocal Huygens metalens for narrowband selective imaging. By optimizing the asymmetry of dielectric nanostructures, we effectively excited quasi-bound states and, combined with the generalized Kerker effect, achieved a transmission efficiency of up to 55%, significantly exceeding the theoretical limit of 25%. This design, centered on all-dielectric integrated resonance units, achieved a quality factor as high as 10^4 through precise control of structural parameters, while ensuring robustness to rotation angles. Experimental results showed that the metalens exhibits superior wavelength selectivity and efficient focusing capability in narrowband imaging. This technology, based on dielectric BICs, lays an important foundation for the development of nonlocal wavefront control and high-quality factor optical devices, widely applicable in cutting-edge fields such as nonlinear optics, quantum light sources, and augmented reality displays. This work primarily aligns with Objective 1-2 and 5. Objective 1: "To develop the design principle and simulation for introducing the BIC..." This work involves the design and simulation of dielectric metasurfaces utilizing quasi-BICs and Huygens' principles to achieve high-Q resonances. Objective 2: "To calculate and design the meta-surface nanostructures..." The metasurface employs optimized dielectric nanostructures to achieve high-Q and high-efficiency optical responses. Objective 5: "To understand the mechanism of the BIC enhanced SHG effect..." Although SHG is not directly measured, this work establishes the high-Q quasi-BIC mechanism as a foundation for future nonlinear enhancements. 5.3.3. BICs physics in high-loss platform to achieve high Q resonance (Objectives 1,2, and 4) In this research, we designed and experimentally realized a nonlocal metallic metasurface based on BICs, demonstrating its application in dark-field edge emission. By combining nonlocal effects with an asymmetric split-ring (ASR) structure, we achieved synergistic excitation of local dipole and quasi-BIC modes. Optimizing the ASR geometry and array period produced a strong scattering contrast between center and edge units, giving rise to the unique edge emission phenomenon. Bright- and dark-field characterizations confirmed that the interplay of local and nonlocal effects enables efficient scattering control and pixel-level spatial modulation without additional defects or structures. This work provides new strategies for flexible nonlocal metasurfaces, advances understanding of light–matter interactions, and opens avenues for future optical technologies. This work primarily aligns with Objective 1-2 and 4. Objective 1-2: "To develop the design principle and simulation..." and "To calculate and design the meta-surface nanostructures..." This work involves the design, simulation, and calculation of a metallic metasurface (ASR units) based on BIC physics (nonlocal lattice resonances) to achieve a specific optical functionality (edge emission). Objective 4: "To measure and characterize optical meta-surface nanostructures..." This work includes the fabrication (likely via methods mentioned in Objective iii, though not detailed here) and experimental characterization (SEM, optical spectroscopy in bright/dark field) of the proposed metasurface, demonstrating its novel properties. 5.3.4. BICs physics in high-loss platform to achieve high Q resonance (Objectives 1-5) In this research, we developed a hybrid lithium niobate (LN) metasurface leveraging quasi-BICs to enhance nonlinear optical conversion. By integrating subwavelength amorphous silicon nanorods on an X-cut LN thin film, we realized high-Q quasi-BIC resonances with strong electromagnetic confinement, aligning the electric field with the LN z-axis to fully exploit the nonlinear coefficient d33 and maximize SHG. Both linear and nonlinear optical characterizations confirmed the performance of this metasurface. Sharp transmission resonances matched simulations, and femtosecond laser excitation produced significantly enhanced SHG compared to unpatterned LN thin film, directly demonstrating the role of quasi-BICs in boosting nonlinear efficiency.. This proposed metasurface offers a compact and efficient optical platform for harmonic generation. This research validates the concept of BIC-enhanced SHG and provides a practical fabrication strategy, establishing a foundation for the next generation of integrated nonlinear photonic devices. Such devices have strong potential for applications in quantum light generation, frequency combs, and advanced nanophotonic technologies. This work primarily aligns with Objective 1-5. Objective 1-2: "To develop the design principle and simulation..." and "To calculate and design the meta-surface nanostructures..." This work established the theoretical framework of BICs, carried out precise simulations, and experimentally realized high-Q quasi-BIC resonances in hybrid LN metasurfaces, achieving strong SHG enhancement. Objective 3: "To develop the layout for the fabrication of the BIC enhanced..." This work realized hybrid LN metasurfaces via advanced semiconductor processes, with SEM and optical characterization confirming fabrication reliability and objective fulfillment. Objective 4-5: "To measure and characterize optical meta-surface nanostructures..." and "To understand the mechanism of the BIC enhanced SHG effect..." This work demonstrated high-Q quasi-BIC resonances, experimentally verified SHG enhancement, and elucidated the underlying mechanism, thereby achieving the objectives and paving the way for applications in quantum light, frequency combs, and nanophotonic technologies.
