15306121.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15306121.value: Boundary layer formation of bacterial chemotaxis in a drop water was observed in the experiment and the so-called chemotaxis-fluid model was proposed to interpret the possible mechanisms underlying the experimental findings. This model is a system of consumption type chemotaxis equations coupled with an incompressible Navier-Stokes fluid. While the numerical simulations of this model have well agreed with experimental observations, the justification of boundary layer solutions still remain open up to date due to the obstacle that the physical No-flux and Dirichlet boundary conditions do not cater to the cross-diffusion structure in the model. In this proposal, we shall develop new ideas to resolve this difficulty and establish the time-asymptotic stability of boundary layer solutions and characterize the refined structure of boundary layer profiles for the model with fluid free. The achievement of these results relies on the following two new ideas that we develop. First in one dimension by taking the anti-derivative of bacterial density (the first solution variable), we manage to reformulate the original problem with cross-diffusion term into one with cross-gradient only so that the physical No-flux and Dirichlet boundary conditions can be fully used to the reformulated problem with some cancellation ideas. While in two dimensions, we write the first solution variable as the divergence of some unknown vector and turn to consider a reformulated vector system. Second, instead of considering the original system, we introduce a skillful perturbative function based on the techniques mentioned above so that the perturbed equations have homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions convenient for analysis and estimates. Though the fluid is not yet considered in this project, the approaches developed in the project will provide powerful tools to overcome the challenges brought by the physical boundary conditions in attacking the full chemotaxis-fluid model in the future. 趣化運動的細菌在水滴中形成邊界層的現象在實驗中已經觀測到，由此趣化流體數學模型也相應被建立去解釋邊界層形成的機制。 這個模型由一個消耗性的趣化方程組和一個不可壓的 Navier-Stokes方程耦合成為一個系統。儘管趣化流體數學模型的數值模擬能再現實驗中的邊界層現象，但理論結果卻沒有，主要的障礙在於物理的邊界條件不能克服數學模型的交叉擴散結構而得到解的正則性。在這分研究計劃裡面， 我們將考慮沒有流體的趣化模型，發展一個新的想法去克服這個困難去得到邊界層解的漸進穩定性並刻畫出它的精準結構。 我們新想法主要是兩點。 第一， 對於空間一維的情形， 我們對通過取對細菌密度反導函數把交叉擴散弱化為交叉梯度使得物理邊界條件能被充分利用從而得到解的正則性。對於空間二維的情形， 我們把細菌密度寫成一個未知向量函數的散度形式，從而把問題轉化為求解向量函數，使得物理邊界條件能夠被利用。 第二， 為了考慮問題的方便，通過上述的技巧，我們引進一個擾動函數，把原始數學模型轉換為一個帶有齊次邊界條件的擾動函數模型， 從而為分析帶來很大的便利。 儘管目前的研究當中，我們還沒有考慮流體的作用， 但是我們的方法和結果將為完整的趣化流體數學模型的研究提供強有力的數學工具去最後攻克趣化流體的邊界層問題。

15306121.label: Major findings and research outcome
15306121.value: In research output [1], we employed the barrier method and multi-scale analysis to establish the existence of boundary-layer steady-state solutions for a consumption-type singular chemotaxis model. This analysis was conducted for arbitrary spatial dimensions and under physically relevant boundary conditions (no-flux and Dirichlet). For radially symmetric domains, we further used anti-derivative techniques and energy estimation methods to prove the nonlinear stability of these boundary-layer steady-state solutions. This work has been submitted to the Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society and is currently under peer review. In research outputs [2] and [3], we focused on the one-dimensional case of the time-dependent singular Keller-Segel system, delivering a complete characterization of boundary-layer solution structures. Specifically, we derived the governing equations for both outer-layer solutions and inner-layer (i.e., boundary-layer) solutions. We then rigorously demonstrated that, under specific compatibility conditions, solutions to the time-dependent singular Keller-Segel system converge to the sum of outer-layer and boundary-layer solutions as the chemical diffusion coefficient tends to zero. A key finding was that the analysis differs substantially depending on whether the initial values are degenerate or non-degenerate. Results for the degenerate initial data case have been published (see [2]), while work on the non-degenerate initial data case has been submitted for publication. In research output [4], we investigated an alternative chemotaxis framework: a toxicant-taxis model (a repulsive chemotaxis system) under Neumann boundary conditions. Here, we identified boundary-layer patterns driven by the repulsive effects of toxicant-taxis. This finding extends prior insights by showing that boundary-layer aggregation patterns are not limited to attractive chemotaxis models with Dirichlet boundary conditions - they can also arise in repulsive chemotaxis models with Neumann boundary conditions. In research outputs [5,6], we consider other problems with Neumann boundary conditions, we find there are no boundary-layer type solutions. This shows, along with the results in previous research outputs, demonstrates that usually the Neumann boundary conditions will not produce boundary-layer type solutions, but exception is possible like the repulsive chemotaxis.

15306121.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15306121.value: Boundary-layer patterns driven by chemotaxis in a fluid environment have been experimentally observed; yet the mathematical validation of this phenomenon has remained an open question for an extended period. This project took a foundational step toward mathematically verifying that a chemotaxis model, operating in a fluid-free environment and subject to physically relevant boundary conditions (no-flux and Dirichlet conditions), can generate such boundary-layer patterns. This contribution is critical because it paves the way for future investigations into chemotaxis-fluid coupled systems - ultimately enabling a mathematical explanation of the mechanism underlying the boundary-layer patterns observed in the original fluid environment experiment. To build on this progress, the Principal Investigator (PI) is currently collaborating with a postdoctoral fellow to advance this line of research. Specifically, we are incorporating fluid flow-induced advection into chemotaxis models to systematically investigate how fluid motion influences the formation of boundary layers.

15306121.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15306121.value: In 2005, experimental observations revealed the formation of boundary layers at the air-fluid interface, driven by chemotactic aggregation. While the so-called "chemotaxis-fluid model" was subsequently proposed to elucidate the mechanisms underlying this notable experimental phenomenon, its mathematical validation has remained an open question for an extended period - with progress limited primarily to numerical studies. Against this backdrop, this project represents the first effort to investigate a simplified chemotaxis system (excluding fluid dynamics) and deliver a comprehensive analysis of the one-dimensional boundary-layer problem. Specifically, it establishes key insights into boundary-layer solutions, including their existence, stability, and convergence behavior. This work yields two critical contributions: First, it verifies that when equipped with physical boundary conditions (i.e., zero-flux and Dirichlet conditions), the chemotaxis model can generate boundary-layer patterns—patterns that are unattainable under conventional Neumann boundary conditions. Second, it provides a rigorous mathematical framework to systematically examine boundary-layer problems in chemotaxis-related models. In doing so, our research paves a new avenue for future investigations into chemotaxis models.

15306321.label: Realisation of objectives
15306321.value: Objective 1: We realized fabrication of TMDC heterobilayers via both chemical vapor deposition (CVD) and mechanical stacking. For CVD on SiO2/Si, WO3 (30 mg), MoO3 (3 mg), and KI (10-20 mg) were loaded in a central quartz boat and covered by upside-down substrates, with sulfur upstream. The tube was ramped in air at 50 °C/s to 560 °C to clean substrates and suppress premature MoS2 growth, then switched to 10% H2/Ar for growth at 750 °C for 10 min, followed by natural cooling below 100 °C, yielding Mo- and W-based heterobilayers. Twisted bilayer MoS2 was also synthesized on mica using atmospheric-pressure CVD with an Ar purge, 10 sccm Ar flow, a ramp to 800 °C with a 10 min dwell, sulfur held at 180 °C, and natural cooling. Additionally, artificial bilayers were assembled by ice-aided and ice-stamp transfers, enabling controlled stacking and tunable twist from exfoliated flakes. Objective 2: We achieved layer-by-layer superlattice assembly within the CVD workflow by an initial air-pumped heating phase (50 °C/s to 500–700 °C) to keep substrates clean and limit early MoS2, followed by H2/Ar (100 sccm) with sustained sulfur vapor, a 750 °C, 10 min dwell, and natural cooling. By tuning the air-to-H2/Ar switching temperature, we controlled domain size, shape, and layer coverage: 500–550 °C produced small, sharp triangles; 600 °C yielded rounded, larger domains; and ≥650 °C expanded WS2 into continuous layers with additional stacking, enabling multilayer superlattices. Omitting the initial air phase led to bulky, irregular clusters, underscoring process fidelity. Objective 3: We comprehensively characterized piezoelectric and structural properties of MoS2/WS2 heterobilayers. DART-SS-PFM on samples transferred to conductive substrates, with SHG-guided stacking identification and AFM topography, revealed intrinsic out-of-plane piezoelectricity with voltage-dependent contrast. Statistical analysis of Dz across many triangles established d33 = 1.95 ± 0.2 pm/V (2H-like) and 2.09 ± 0.2 pm/V (3R-like); AFM confirmed atomically smooth surfaces (RMS ~0.1 nm), ruling out artifacts. STEM corroborated structure: SEM and ADF imaging showed larger MoS2 over smaller WS2, cross-sectional HAADF-STEM identified bright WS2 beneath darker MoS2, while BF-STEM, EDS, SAED, and PL confirmed bilayer registry and composition. Objective 4: We directly mapped piezoelectric polarization dynamics in twisted bilayer MoS2 using in-situ STEM and 4D-STEM. Focused-probe differential phase contrast measured center-of-mass shifts to reconstruct in-plane polarization and vorticity, supported by STEM-ADF, SAED, FFT, and multislice simulations. We observed moiré-correlated vortex fields with strongest features at AA regions (~1.5 nm periodicity at 11.6°) and hexagonal sublattice vortices at AB/BA domains, spanning twist angles 1.8°, 2.4°, 4.1°, 8.3°, 11.6°, 18.4°, and 30°. At 30°, quasicrystalline “clock” motifs with 12 lobes appeared in both ADF images and polar maps. SAED/FFT validated moiré periodicities; minor strain/drift did not alter features, consistent with sliding ferroelectricity in small-twist structures.

15306321.label: Major findings and research outcome
15306321.value: Major findings and research outcome: • Untwisted MoS2/WS2 heterobilayers: Scalable, epitaxial CVD-grown, commensurate MoS2/WS2 stacks exhibit unexpected out-of-plane ferroelectricity and piezoelectricity without invoking twist or moiré effects. Resonance PFM measurements yielded OOP d33 values of 1.95-2.09 pm/V, about six times larger than monolayer a-In2Se3, confirming robust piezoelectric response. Ferroelectric tunnel junctions based on these heterobilayers show ~10^3 modulation of tunneling current upon polarization reversal. Density functional theory attributes these properties to symmetry breaking and interlayer sliding in the bilayer, establishing a twist-free mechanism for OOP ferro- and piezoelectricity in 2D TMDCs. • Twisted-bilayer MoS2: Using 4D-STEM combined with first-principles theory, we directly mapped in-plane electric polarization fields and uncovered topological vortex textures tied to local moiré domains. Vortex lattices emerge across small twist angles and persist in a 30° incommensurate quasicrystal, which exhibits 12-fold rotational symmetry (“clock” motifs) and mosaic chiral vortex patterns. The polar textures are tunable by picometer-scale interlayer displacements, demonstrating a powerful twist- and displacement-controlled route to engineer local electric fields in 2D bilayers. • Nonstoichiometric TMDCs: We reveal extendable and ubiquitous piezo/ferroelectricity in nominally centrosymmetric 2D TMDCs by leveraging intrinsic nonstoichiometry. Sliding of van der Waals layers and displacement of interlayer metal atoms, triggered by Frankel-defect–mediated heterogeneous interlayer native metal intercalation, break inversion symmetry and activate ferro-/piezoelectricity. Demonstrations include 2D chromium selenides nanogenerators and iron tellurides ferroelectric multilevel memristors, highlighting device relevance. Collectively, these results establish three complementary pathways, twist engineering, twist-free epitaxial stacking, and defect/stoichiometry design, to generate and control polar vortices, out-of-plane ferroelectricity, and strong piezoelectricity in 2D materials, enabling ultrathin piezo-/ferroelectronics and multifunctional devices.

15306321.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15306321.value: The research can be advanced along three complementary tracks: twist engineering, epitaxial heterobilayer design, and controlled nonstoichiometry. Proposed course of action: • Systematically map polarization textures versus twist angle, strain, and temperature using in-situ 4D-STEM with electrical biasing to capture real-time domain dynamics and switching. • Optimize atmospheric-pressure CVD for wafer-scale, twist-free MoS2/WS2 with deterministic stacking; develop automated transfer/assembly to build periodic superlattices. • Establish defect engineering protocols (controlled intercalation and stoichiometry tuning) to reproducibly induce and tailor piezo/ferroelectricity; couple with in-situ spectroscopy and microscopy for feedback. • Integrate materials into device platforms: arrays of ferroelectric tunnel junctions, piezoelectric nanogenerators, and multilevel memristors; benchmark endurance, retention, fatigue, and environmental stability. • Develop application-focused prototypes (ultrathin sensors, neuromorphic elements, low-power nonvolatile memories) and assess manufacturability via CMOS-compatible processes. These steps will translate fundamental polar vortex control and out-of-plane ferro/piezoelectricity into scalable, high-performance 2D piezo-/ferroelectronic technologies.

15306321.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15306321.value: We explored how stacking ultra-thin crystals, just a few atoms thick, can create tiny electric patterns that we can control. By gently twisting two layers of molybdenum disulfide (MoS2), we discovered swirling “vortex” electric patterns that repeat across the material, including in special 12-point “clock-like” arrangements at a 30° twist. These patterns can be tuned by moving the layers by just trillionths of a meter. We also showed that when two different atomically thin materials (MoS2 and WS2) are stacked without any twist, they naturally develop switchable out-of-plane electric polarization (ferroelectricity) and a strong pressure–electric effect (piezoelectricity). Devices made from these stacks can change their electrical current by about a thousand times when the polarization is flipped, useful for low-power memory and sensors. Finally, we found a simple route to make many 2D materials electrically active by introducing tiny, controlled imbalances in their composition, enabling energy harvesters and brain-like memory elements. Together, these advances point to new, scalable ways to build ultrathin, energy-efficient sensors, memories, and flexible electronics.

15306421.label: Realisation of objectives
15306421.value: 1. Characterization of the wild-type and inhibitor-resistant TEM and SHV β-lactamases involving the point mutations at Met69, Ser130 and Arg244. Wild-type TEM and SHV β-lactamases, as well as 4 TEM and 2 SHV inhibitor-resistant variants were selected accordingly to allow the comparison between single-mutants and combination of mutations. TEM-1, TEM-30 (R244S), TEM-33 (M69L), TEM-76 (S130G), TEM-77 (M69L + R244S), SHV-1, SHV-132 (M69L) and SHV-1 S130G were expressed or purchased, and their masses and purities were verified by SDS-PAGE, and mass spectrometry. Their enzyme activities were confirmed using nitrocefin test. 2. Hydrogen/deuterium exchange mass spectrometry and ion mobility mass spectrometry studies on wild type and inhibitor-resistant TEM and SHV β-lactamases and their interactions with the three inhibitors, i.e., clavulanic acid, sulbactam and tazobactam. The conformational dynamics of the selected TEM and SHV β-lactamases (BLs) was studied using hydrogen/deuterium exchange mass spectrometry (HDX-MS) and ion mobility mass spectrometry (IM-MS). All TEM and SHV enzymes had similar deuterium uptakes for the same peptides due to their high sequence and structure similarity. Despite these similarities, uptake profiles of inhibitor-resistant mutants differed in several regions, such as Ω-loop (residues 163-186) and β-sheets S3/S4 (residues 230-248). Interestingly, these regions participate in the formation of the substrate cavity, and their altered conformational dynamics could affect the substrate specificity and inhibitor binding. The general trend for inhibitor-resistant mutants was stabilization of Ω-loop, with one exception – TEM S130G. This variant had the biggest increase in deuterium uptakes in residues 163-169 and 230-248, probably due to the disrupted hydrogen bond network in the absence of S130 hydroxyl group. This effect was also present in SHV S130G, although only in residues 163-169. M69L resulted in decreased uptake in the regions of interest in both TEM and SHV, and the effect was enhanced when M69L is combined with R244S in TEM BLs. Surprisingly, R244S alone increased the uptake in the S3/S4 β-sheet region. To investigate the overall effect of the inhibitor binding on the BL conformation, we combined global HDX-MS with IM-MS to study the protein complexes with clavulanic acid, tazobactam and sulbactam. Although the experiments for sulbactam have been successfully conducted, their results are not discussed here, as the deuterium uptakes of sulbactam complexes were abnormally high. It potentially hints at the protein denaturation, probably caused by high concentrations of sulbactam, and efforts have been made to optimize the incubation conditions. However, high concentrations of sulbactam were required for complete binding and could not be avoided, leading to unreliable results. Therefore, only results for clavulanic acid and tazobactam will be discussed further. Both clavulanic acid and tazobactam binding resulted in increased backbone flexibility for all the proteins studied according to the HDX-MS results. The effect of different inhibitors on the TEM and SHV BLs conformational dynamics is different: while tazobactam greatly increases the flexibility of all studied TEM BLs, clavulanic acid has more significant impact on the deuterium uptake of SHV BLs. Binding did not induce any major changes in collision cross section of the proteins, so no changes in the drift times were detected upon interaction with the inhibitors. We hypothesized that in contrast to the highly flexible apo state of the S130G variant, inhibitor-resistant effect of some mutations might manifest in the reaction steps that take place after the inhibitor binding, such as deacylation. Detailed HDX-MS analysis at peptide level revealed that the major consequence of inhibitor binding is significantly increased flexibility of N-terminal part of Ω-loop (residues 163-169), especially in TEM BLs. Interdomain hinge regions, including residues 60-69 for TEM and 214-225 for SHV BLs, also demonstrated higher flexibility in complexes. Increased domain mobility could disturb the substrate binding site, which is located at the interdomain interface, and hinder proper substrate positioning for successful deacylation. Increased flexibility of the protein backbone in complex with the inhibitors was especially prominent in the wild-type BLs. Therefore, we proposed that inhibitor-resistant mutations stabilize the substrate cavity and help to preserve hydrogen bond network of the catalytical center, which in turn results in improved deacylation efficiency. For example, M69L mutants, which are among the most efficient inhibitor hydrolysers among TEM BLs, demonstrated the lowest increase in the Ω-loop and interdomain hinges flexibility upon inhibitor binding. 3. Molecular modeling and molecular dynamics simulation on the studied β-lactamases and their binding with the inhibitors. The molecular dynamics simulations were conducted for all 8 proteins in their apo and inhibitor-bound states (with clavulanic acid, tazobactam and sulbactam) using GROMACS. Overall flexibility of the protein backbone and fluctuation of individual residues were estimated using root mean square deviation (RMSD) and root mean square fluctuation (RMSF). Inhibitor binding increased the RMSD value for most of the studied proteins, meaning the higher global flexibility of protein structure when bound to the inhibitor, consistent with our HDX-MS results. RMSF analysis of protein/inhibitor complexes showed that the Ω-loop residues 169-178 experienced significant increase in the atomic position fluctuation, especially in the wild-type TEM-1. Moreover, the MD simulations showed that the number of hydrogen bonds within the active site difffered between the wild-type proteins and mutants: it increased for inhibitor-resistant mutants, and correlates with the efficiency of the inhibitor hydrolysis. This result implies that improved hydrogen-bonding network might help to better position the inhibitor in the substrate cavity for more efficient hydrolysis. The representative structures of all complexes have been studied and compared, and the difference in side chain orientation for inhibitor intermediate was observed in complexes of TEM R244S and M69L/R244S with tazobactam compared to all the other BLs in this study. 4. Data analysis and understanding of the relations between the conformational dynamic change in TEM and SHV β-lactamases and inhibitor-resistant properties. All the obtained experimental and simulation results were analyzed and summarized. Normally, based on the HDX-MS experiments inhibitor-resistant mutants demonstrated stabilized Ω-loop (residues 163-169), except for TEM S130G, which demonstrated overall destabilization. Inhibitor binding resulted in increased overall backbone flexibility, especially in the wild type proteins. Lower flexibility increase of Ω-loop residues 163-169 and interdomain regions was observed for most inhibitor-resistant variants, especially in complexes with clavulanic acid. Higher similarity of conformational dynamics changes in wild type and inhibitor-resistant BLs upon tazobactam binding could explain more successful performance of tazobactam against inhibitor-resistant enzymes. MD simulations showed that inhibitor-resistant mutants have increased number of hydrogen bonds between the inhibitor intermediate and the active site residues compared to the wild-type proteins. Based on these observations, it was suggested that BLs might achieve inhibitor-resistance with mutations via 2 ways. Firstly, the flexibility of the active site in the apo-state can be increased, leading to lower binding affinity between the BL and the inhibitor. This could be the case for S130G mutants, which have low affinity to both inhibitors and conventional substrates and typically have impaired catalytic activity. Secondly, the mutation can stabilize the substrate cavity and help to preserve hydrogen bond network of the catalytical center, which in turn results in improved deacylation efficiency. For example, M69L TEM and SHV complexes with the inhibitors demonstrated lower flexibility of the active site compared to the wild-type variants.

15306421.label: Major findings and research outcome
15306421.value: Based on the hydrogen/deuterium exchange mass spectrometry, ion mobility mass spectrometry and MD simulation results, we proposed that one of the mechanisms for inhibitor resistance in TEM and SHV β-lactamases (BLs) could be increased flexibility of the protein active site in the apo-state, which might lead to lower binding affinity to the inhibitors. This could be the case for S130G and R244S variants: the inhibitory constants of these variants are greatly increased, especially for TEM S130G, demonstrating hindered inhibitor binding. Hampered interaction with the inhibitor due to the highly dynamic active site comes at the cost of enzymatic activity against the antibiotics: both S130G and R244S variants experience decrease in the hydrolysis efficiency of conventional substrates. After investigating the conformational dynamics of BL/inhibitor complexes, we suggested that the dynamics of Ω-loop residues 163-169 determines the deacylation efficiency. This peptide includes E166 – a residue that is crucial for the successful hydrolysis and release of the bound substrate. Its carboxylate acts as a general base, transferring the proton from the water molecule to S70, thus regenerating the hydroxyl for another hydrolysis cycle. Successful proton transfer would require proper positioning of the residues involved in this reaction. Increased flexibility of this region might lead to the disruption of the necessary interactions, preventing the deacylation and release of β-lactam compound, leading to the inhibitory effect. Inhibitor-resistant mutations such as M69L, R244S, and S130G help to stabilize the omega-loop and E166 which increases the efficiency of inhibitor turnover. The conformational dynamics of interdomain hinges 60-69 in TEM and 214-225 in SHV also changed greatly upon inhibitor binding. It is possible that interdomain flexibility plays an important role in the protein-inhibitor interaction and, subsequently, the inhibition process. Overall, our findings pave the path for development of novel inhibitors, including such strategies as the modulation of Ω-loop conformational dynamics or control of interdomain hinge flexibility.

15306421.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15306421.value: This study provides crucial insights into the mechanism of resistance against commonly used β-lactamase inhibitors in TEM and SHV β-lactamases. We have identified several protein regions which could serve as potential drug targets, including interdomain regions and N-terminal part of the Ω-loop. Next, protein variants with point mutations in these regions can be investigated to reveal the role of single amino acid residues in the inhibitor resistance. The developed approach can also be further employed to study class D and especially class B metallo-β-lactamases, such as NDM β-lactamases, to investigate their interactions with the available inhibitors and the mechanisms of resistance. Developing new β-lactamase inhibitors is important in the age of constantly rising antibiotic resistance. Our findings allow further research development in the field of β-lactamase inhibition and propose a new strategy for inhibitor development, focusing on the modulation of Ω-loop conformational dynamics and control of interdomain hinge flexibility. Allosteric inhibition via interdomain regions can be investigated as a novel approach to combat β-lactamase-mediated antibiotic resistance.

15306421.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15306421.value: Antibiotic resistance is one of the major threats to public health. Bacteria achieve resistance via production of special enzymes, such as β-lactamases (BLs). Commercial drugs combine β-lactam antibiotics with β-lactamase inhibitors, however, TEM and SHV BLs have developed inhibitor-resistant properties through point mutations, posing significant challenges in clinics. In this study, hydrogen/deuterium exchange mass spectrometry (HDX-MS) and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations were used to investigate the relation between the conformational dynamics changes and inhibitor-resistance properties of TEM and SHV BLs. The HDX-MS revealed that the inhibitor binding increased the overall flexibility of the proteins, especially the wild-type proteins. Upon clavulanic acid and tazobactam binding, major changes happened in the residues forming the active site and interdomain hinge regions. It was proposed that the flexibility of these protein regions in the apo-state affects the binding affinity, while flexibility of the Ω-loop in the bound state modulates the deacylation efficiency. MD simulations demonstrated that inhibitor-resistant mutants have higher number of hydrogen bonds between the inhibitor intermediate and active site residues compared to the wild-type BLs, which likely improves the inhibitor positioning for successful hydrolysis. Overall, the results of this project can guide further development of the BL inhibitors.

15306521.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15306521.value: In this project, we first consider a semiparametric accelerated mean model for panel count data, and then propose a reversed accelerated mean model for a more general situation where a recurrent event process is stopped by a terminal event such as death. The main challenge in semiparametric estimation of the accelerated mean model is that the mean function contains regression coefficients as its argument, resulting in bundled parameters. For the accelerated mean model, we develop spline least squares-based and spline likelihood-based estimation approaches; while for the reversed accelerated mean model, we design two-stage spline least squares and two-stage spline likelihood estimation procedures. The new challenge arises from deriving the asymptotic properties of finite-dimensional and infinite-dimensional estimators. The consistency and the convergence rate of the proposed estimators are established. We develop the general weak convergence theories of M-estimators with bundled parameters and with both bundled parameters and nuisance parameters, respectively, and then apply them to deriving the joint asymptotic normality of the proposed estimators under the accelerated mean model and the reversed accelerated mean model. Furthermore, we can construct new global hypothesis tests and multi-sample tests for panel count data. The performance of the proposed new models and inference procedures will be demonstrated through simulation studies and illustrated with panel count data from the bladder tumor study and the Chinese Longitudinal Healthy Longevity Study. The proposed project will provide a novel theoretical and methodological framework for the analysis of panel count data. 在這個項目中，我們首先考慮面板計數數據的半參數加速均值模型，然後針對更一般的情況提出了反向加速均值模型，在這種情況下，重複事件過程將被終止事件例如死亡停止。加速均值模型半參數估計的主要挑戰是均值函數包含有限維回歸係數作為其參數，導致參數捆綁。對於加速均值模型，我們開發了基於樣條最小二乘和基於樣條似然的估計方法；而對於反向加速平均模型，我們設計了兩階段樣條最小二乘法和兩階段樣條似然估計程序。新的挑戰來自推導有限維和無限維估計量的漸近特性。我們建立了估計量的一致性和收斂速度。我們分別開發了具有捆綁參數和同時具有捆綁參數和擾動參數的 M 估計量的一般弱收斂理論，然後將它們應用於推導所提出的估計量在加速平均模型和反向加速平均模型下的聯合漸近正態性. 此外，我們能夠為面板計數數據構建新的全局假設檢驗和多樣本檢驗。所提出的新模型和推斷程序的性能將通過模擬研究來評估，並應用於膀胱腫瘤研究和中國縱向健康長壽研究的面板計數數據分析。本研究項目將為面板計數數據的分析提供一個新的理論和方法框架。

15306521.label: Realisation of objectives
15306521.value: We have worked on all four objectives of this project since the submission of the proposal. First, we developed a sieve semiparametric framework that approximates the baseline mean function using monotone B-splines under an accelerated mean model with panel count data. We employed both pseudolikelihood and likelihood methods to construct the random criterion function using the Poisson process as the working model. We establish the consistency and rate of convergence of the sieve pseudolikelihood and likelihood estimators, as well as the asymptotic normality of the estimators of the regression parameters. Second, we developed spline least squares-based estimation approaches for the accelerated mean model with panel count data, without relying on any Poisson-type assumptions, and established the asymptotic properties of the proposed estimators. Third, we proposed a class of flexible semiparametric marginal conditional mean models for longitudinal response processes with informative observation times and terminal events, developed a two-stage spline-based least squares estimation approach, and established the asymptotic properties of the proposed estimators. Extensive simulation studies were carried out and suggested that the proposed approaches work well for practical situations. Fourth, we proposed a functional accelerated failure time model to characterize effects of both functional and scalar covariates on the time to event of interest, provided regularity conditions to guarantee model identifiability, and developed a sieve maximum likelihood approach for efficient estimation of model parameters. Fifth, we promoted phase-type distributions as a method of sieve. Phase-type distributions are dense in the space of nonnegative distributions, closed under minimum, maximum, and convolution, and compatible with the accelerated failure time model. Building on the approximation error rate results, we establish general asymptotic properties of the phase-type sieve estimators and apply them to models that have complicated data missingness and cannot be easily handled by existing methods. Sixth, we studied the transformed hazards model with time-dependent covariates observed intermittently for the censored outcome. Existing work assumes the availability of the whole trajectory of the time-dependent covariates, which is unrealistic. We proposed combining kernel-weighted log-likelihood and sieve maximum log-likelihood estimation to conduct statistical inference. The method is robust and easy to implement. We established the asymptotic properties of the proposed estimator and contributed to a rigorous theoretical framework for general kernel-weighted sieve M-estimators. Numerical studies showed that the proposed methods perform favorably over competing methods. Seventh, we developed global hypothesis tests and multi-sample tests for right-censored survival data using deep neural networks (DNNs). Eighth, we extended the DNN‑based estimation and testing framework to panel‑count survival data under a generalized mean model that includes the accelerated mean model and the proportional mean model as special cases. We have achieved all the objectives of this project.

15306521.label: Major findings and research outcome
15306521.value: For statistical inference of panel count data, we have proposed a flexible and intuitive conditional accelerated mean model and developed estimation procedures based on pseudolikelihood, likelihood, and least squares methods. We derived the overall convergence rates of the proposed estimators and established the asymptotic normality of both finite-dimensional estimators and functionals of infinite-dimensional estimators under some regularity conditions. In addition, we proposed a class of flexible semiparametric marginal conditional mean models for longitudinal response processes with informative observation times and terminal events. A two-stage spline-based least squares estimation approach was developed, and the corresponding asymptotic properties of the estimators were rigorously established. Furthermore, we introduced a functional accelerated failure time model and developed an efficient estimation procedure for its parameters. A comprehensive theoretical framework was also provided for general kernel-weighted sieve M-estimators. The proposed likelihood-based DNN approach not only achieves state-of-the-art predictive performance in survival analysis but also supports a broad suite of inference tools, including one-sample tests, multi-sample tests, goodness-of-fit tests, and independence tests. Consequently, the method has substantial theoretical significance and practical value. Extensive simulation studies and real-data applications demonstrated the strong performance and practical relevance of all proposed approaches. In summary, 8 research papers associated with this project have been published/submitted in international peer‑reviewed journals, including Journal of the American Statistical Association, Biometrika, Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B, Biometrics, and Statistica Sinica. The research findings have also been presented at international conferences.

15306521.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15306521.value: (1) The newly developed models from this project offer valuable tools for gaining deeper insights into key features of recurrent event processes with panel count data. (2) The proposed estimation methods can be extended to more general mean models with panel count data. (3) The proposed approaches also have the potential to be generalized to semiparametric models involving both low- and high-dimensional covariates, where nonlinear covariate effects can be flexibly captured using deep neural network architectures. (4) The developed kernel-weighted inference method is particularly useful for statistical analysis when time-dependent covariates are observed intermittently, providing a foundation for further methodological advancements.

15306521.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15306521.value: This project studies how to analyze data collected from events that happen repeatedly over time, especially when such data are only observed at certain time points (called panel count data) or are incomplete (censored data). These situations commonly arise in real-world studies such as tracking the recurrence of a disease, product failures, or repeated behaviors, but have not been adequately addressed by existing statistical methods. We have developed new statistical models and estimation approaches that describe more precisely the relationships among repeated events, observation times, and terminal events such as death or system failure. The results of this project help fill an important gap in the literature on panel count survival data analysis and have practical value in diverse fields such as economics, genetics, medicine, and public health.

15306621.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15306621.value: Most optimization algorithms utilize the gradients of the objective function or, more generally, its first-order information. However, such information is not available or costly to obtain in many industrial and engineering optimization problems. Derivative-Free Optimization (DFO) algorithms are designed to solve such problems based only on function evaluations. In real-world DFO problems, function evaluations are often contaminated by noise that can never be reduced to zero by any denoising procedure (due to limited computing power), and can possibly become quite large (with a low probability). We will say that such noise is untamed. Many existing DFO algorithms and theories assume that the objective function can be evaluated precisely as long as the constraints are obeyed. It is not clear whether such algorithms are reliable under untamed noise. There do exist methods and theories for noisy DFO problems, but they require that the noise is tamed, meaning that it can be decreased arbitrarily in some deterministic or probabilistic sense when needed, or it can be uniformly bounded below a quite low magnitude. Hence untamed noise is not covered by these existing works, leaving a big gap between applications and academic research. Our project aims to bridge this gap by proving theoretical guarantees on the reliability of DFO algorithms under untamed noise and providing reliable implementations of DFO algorithms according to our theory. In the theoretical part, we will analyze two popular frameworks for DFO algorithms, namely direct search and trust region, aiming at general theories to guarantee their reliability under untamed noise. Our objective is to prove that these frameworks can achieve an approximate optimality condition within a reasonable amount of iterations even though the function evaluations contain untamed noise. To this end, we will explore a new technique named "density analysis" for investigating probabilistic optimization algorithms. Our theoretical results will provide practical guidelines for implementing reliable DFO algorithms for noisy problems, particularly on how to set the algorithmic parameters in accordance with information about the noise. We will integrate the outcomes of our project into PDFO, an open-source DFO software package developed by the PI and his Ph.D. student, so that they are readily available to practitioners. 大多數優化算法依賴目標函數的導數 (或一階) 信息。但是，在很多工業與工程優化問題中，這種信息很難或無法獲取。求解這樣的問題，我們需要無導數優化 (DFO) 算法，即基於函數值的優化算法。 實際應用中，無導數優化問題的函數值往往含有噪音。並且，在很多問題中，這種噪音無法隨著計算逐步消除，其強度甚至可能以一定的概率變得很高。我們稱這種噪音為非馴化 (untamed) 的。很多已有的無導數優化算法假設目標函數在可行域內可以精確計算。一個亟待回答的問題是，這樣的算法在非馴化的噪音下是否可靠？同時，也有一些無導數優化算法可以處理帶有噪音的問題，但它們往往假設噪音是馴化 (tamed) 的，即噪音可以隨著計算逐步降低，或者噪音強度是一致有界的。非馴化的噪音則不在這些工作的覆蓋範圍之內。本項目針對這一理論與現實的差距，研究非馴化噪音下可靠的無導數優化算法。 我們將界定一類非馴化的噪音，並分析幾類流行的無導數優化算法框架在此類噪音下的行為，建立其全局收斂性和收斂速度。特別地，我們將研究信賴域 (trust region) 框架和直接搜索 (direct search) 在非馴化噪音下的理論性質，在一定條件下證明其可靠性。以這些理論為基礎，我們將針對非馴化噪音設計新的可靠無導數優化算法。我們的研究結果將融入 PI 和他的學生設計的 PDFO 軟件 (www.pdfo.net)，從而及時地對無導數優化算法的應用領域產生影響。

15306621.label: Major findings and research outcome
15306621.value: This project has led to 3 papers, two of which are published on top optimization journals, namely Math. Program. Comput. and SIAM J. Optim. [1] Tom M. Ragonneau, Zaikun Zhang, "An Optimal Interpolation Set for Model-Based Derivative-Free Optimization Methods", Optim. Methods Softw. This paper demonstrates the optimality of an interpolation set employed in derivative-free trust-region methods, which is essential for the efficiency and stability of such methods. [2] Tom M. Ragonneau, Zaikun Zhang, "PDFO: A Cross-Platform Package for Powell's Derivative-Free Optimization Solvers". Math. Program. Comput. This paper introduces the PDFO package, which makes Powell's classical DFO solvers available under Python and MATLAB, and fixes bugs in Powell's implementation, making the solvers more reliable under noise and tolerant to function evaluation failures. [3] Xiaojun Chen, Yifan He, Zaukun Zhang, "Tight Error Bounds for Sign-Constrained Orthogonality Constraints", SIAM J. Optim. This paper presents global and local error bounds for the sign-constrained Stiefel manifold with easily computable residual functions and explicit coefficients. Moreover, we show that the error bounds cannot be improved except for the coefficients. Such bounds help us to devise reliable and efficient algorithms based on penalization. However, the most important research outcomes are not the papers but the software packages developed during the project, namely PDFO, COBYQA, and BDS. [4] PDFO ( https://www.pdfo.net ), a DFO software package for solving general nonlinear optimization problems. It is capable of handling noisy function evaluations and can even tolerate failures of function evaluations. It has been downloaded more than 700,000 times, and it is selected as one of the optimization engines of GEMSEO, an industrial software package developed by Airbus and other research labs for Multi-disciplinary Design Optimization (MDO). [5] COBYQA ( https://www.cobyqa.com ), a DFO software package for solving general nonlinear optimization problems. It is capable of handling noisy function evaluations and can even tolerate failures of function evaluations. It has been included in SciPy as a release highlight of SciPy 1.14.0 (https://scipy.github.io/devdocs/release/1.14.0-notes.html#highlights-of-this-release). SciPy is downloaded more than 100 million times every month globally (https://pypistats.org/packages/scipy). [6] BDS ( https://github.com/blockwise-direct-search ), a blockwise direct search DFO solver for unconstrained problems. Despite its simplicity, it is quite reliable under noise, outperforming classical sophisticated solvers such as Powell's NEWUOA and COBYLA.

15307221.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15307221.value: Rechargeable aqueous zinc metal batteries have attracted enormous attention due to the advantages in both the cost and safety compared to the batteries using organic electrolytes. The utilization of water solvent in the electrolyte offers the merits of intrinsic non-flammability and reduced manufacturing cost. Recent progress reports several promising Mn- and V-based cathodes, which could operate in mild aqueous solution instead of traditional concentrated alkali electrolyte for further elevating the environmental benignity. Turning to the anode, Zn metal would be the most attractive candidate considering its appropriate potential and the high volumetric capacity of 5851 mAh/cm3. The practical application of Zn metal anodes is afflicted primarily by the dendrite formation and low Coulombic efficiency associated with parasitic reactions, which cause the severe safety issue arising from the cell short-circuit and limited cyclic life due to the Zn depletion. This project aims to boost the performance of Zn metal anodes through regulating the interfacial chemistry. The electrode/electrolyte/separator interfaces play crucial roles in governing the nucleation of Zn clusters and subsequent growth, but the underlying mechanism remains largely unexplored owing to the difficulties in tracing the detailed plating/stripping process. We will first adopt in-situ liquid transmission electron microscopy and operando scanning electrochemical microscopy to unravel the nucleation behavior and surface evolution at the early stages. The exclusive information on the size, crystallinity, and distribution of nuclei and surface functionality will be correlated with the morphology of Zn grown in later stages. Such correlations would guide the interface design at multiscales to tailor the electrochemical behavior and prevent parasitic reactions. The optimized interfaces will function as several roles, including i) tune the microstructure of Zn nuclei to inhibit sporadic deposition; ii) homogenize the Zn ion flux to guide the smooth growth; iii) control the growth direction to prevent the penetration of separator; and iv) passivate the surface to inhibit the corrosion and gas generation. The validity of these interface-derived approaches will be verified in full coin-cells and pouch-cells under practical conditions, like deep Zn depth of discharge and wide temperature ranges. The resolved Zn nucleation-growth picture and established interface engineering strategies would benefit the rational design of Zn metal anodes for various Zn-based energy storage systems such as Zn metal and Zn air batteries. 可充電水系鋅離子電池使用水作為電解液溶劑，具有低製備成本和高安全性等優點，因而受到了廣泛關注。最近的研究報導了一系列可在中性水溶液中工作的錳基和釩基正極材料，避免了傳統強鹼性電解液的使用，可進一步提升環境友好性。在負極方面，鋅金屬電位合適，理論體積比容量高達5851 mAh/cm3, 是最具吸引力的候選材料。儘管如此，伴隨鋅離子沉積和去沉積的枝晶生長和副反應，限制了其實際應用。鋅枝晶可能刺穿隔膜，造成電池短路；而副反應會消耗鋅離子，降低庫侖效率和循環壽命。本項目將通過界面調控來改進鋅金屬負極性能。電極/電解液/隔膜界面對鋅金屬的成核和生長具有重要作用，但是目前難以追踪鋅沉積和去沉積具體過程，對界面如何控制鋅金屬負極的穩定性缺乏足夠的認識。因此，我們將利用原位液體透射電子顯微鏡和掃描電化學顯微鏡表徵鋅金屬的形核過程和初期的表面形貌演化，揭示鋅核的尺寸，結晶度和分佈以及表面性質對之後鋅沉積形貌的影響。這些基礎探索將指導我們在後續研究中利用多尺度界面設計調控鋅金屬的電化學行為和抑制副反應的發生。優化後的界面將具有如下作用：i) 控制鋅核形貌防止離散沉積；ii) 均勻鋅離子通量實現平穩生長；iii) 改變鋅金屬生長方向避免刺穿隔膜；iv) 保護電極表面，防止腐蝕和產氣。我們將組裝全電池，並在深度放電和寬溫度範圍測試，檢驗所構造界面的有效性。本研究將揭示鋅金屬成核生長過程，並開發界面調控策略，從而指導鋅金屬負極的合理設計，推動鋅金屬和鋅空氣電池等儲能係統的應用。

15307321.label: Major findings and research outcome
15307321.value: Organic memristors have attracted widespread attention as promising candidates for neuromorphic systems and wearable electronic devices. In this project, we devoted our efforts to designing and synthesizing various new metallopolymers (papers 1, 2, 12, 14-16, 18, 20-22 for 1D polymers and papers 4, 5, 9, 17, 19, 23, 24 for 2D polymers) and other related compounds (papers 3, 6). Several types of metallopolymers containing different types of redox centers were developed, which aims to realize the fabrication of multilevel memristors. Organic chromophores (e.g. triphenylamine, fluorene, organic radicals) and metal-ligand functions such as ferrocene and metal-azo aromatics were adopted. In one study (paper 20), donor–acceptor polymers were synthesized where the only disparity between the two polymers is the inclusion of a ferrocene pendant group in one of them. The memristors exhibited volatile threshold switching (TS) behavior, which is dominated by pseudo-bridging conductive filaments (CFs). The more stable TS behavior of the metallopolymer-based memristor under a positive voltage sweep is attributed to the ferrocenyl units, which can reduce the random growth of CFs. The volatile ternary switching behavior in the negative working window can be attributed to the synergistic effect of Ag CFs and bilayer intramolecular charge transfer. Moreover, the characteristics related to the application of the metallopolymer-based memristor on artificial nociceptors are demonstrated. In another study (paper 3), adjustment of molecular structure can effectively improve the organic memory device behaviors due to the optimization of intra/intermolecular interaction and molecular packing. The champion device exhibited ternary WORM property. To explore metallopolymers in the next stage of development, we also studied various device structures using known and other new materials (papers 21, 22). After project application result was announced but before the official project commencement, the research progress of metal-containing organic compounds for memory applications was first surveyed and summarized in a review paper 7. The recent advances of logic gate circuits based on metallo-organic compounds were reviewed in paper 11. An analog-switching photonic memristor with distributed potential wells based on a 2D platinum(II)-acetylide framework is realized. Its excellent optical analog nonvolatile behavior is attributed to the synergistic effect of light-enhanced through-bond charge transport and space-charge-limited conduction. The in-sensor reservoir computing (RC) system based on the device can adapt to multi-task. Our work overcomes the bottleneck of having separated individual sensor-memory-computing units in existing computing systems, providing a promising material-algorithm synergistic strategy for designing efficient in-sensor RC for edge computing (submitted).

15307321.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15307321.value: Many important data emanated from this project which will make a good impact on the emerging applications of organic memristors. We believe that the results will pave the way to the future design and development of memristive polymeric materials. The field is expected to remain exciting and stimulating for the foreseeable future. Flexible memristors serve as a key enabling device for realizing wearable neuromorphic computing and bio-integrated intelligence. The metallopolymer systems in our research exhibit good solubility and film-forming ability, enabling their future application in the fabrication of flexible memristors. Moreover, structural optimization can be pursued by integrating photoactive functional groups, creating a dual-mode neuromorphic device capable of processing both electrical and optical signals for adaptive visual computing.

15307321.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15307321.value: Metal complexes are emerging as a new generation of memristive materials for nonvolatile information storage and neuromorphic computing. In this project, the molecular design, synthesis and functional properties of a series of 1D and 2D metallopolymers and other related molecules were investigated in detail. Several types of new metallopolymer systems containing different types of redox centers were developed, which aims to realize multilevel memristors. Our work provides a design map for constructing new memristive metallopolymers, shedding light on the establishment of the structure-property relationships, which facilitates the fast development of organic memory and optoelectronic synaptic devices. The influences of redox-active groups on their memristive properties were also explored. The applications of these metallopolymers for artificial nociceptors and in-sensor reservoir computing (RC) system were also evaluated.

15307621.label: Project Objectives

Based on 2, to formally introduce and verify asymptotic mixed-equilibrium-optima (AMEO), a new theoretic concept suiting for (Mix)-strategy designed. 15307621.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15307621.value: 大尺度系统近来被广泛深入地研究。 这是一类很重要的动态系统，它包含了足够多弱耦合的决策者或（物理意义下的）粒子。 从传统上而言， 依赖于个体粒子间是否竞争或者协作， 大尺度系统的动态优化问题可分为：平均场博弈或平均场协作。基于此，一直以来， 上述博弈和协作理论被分别独立地进行研究和发展。 然而， 实际问题中， 很多时候大尺度系统中的粒子呈现出混合的博弈和协作状态。 比如，众多粒子可以划分为很多子系统， 单一子系统内部的粒子是相互协作的， 然而子系统外部是相互竞争的。 这种混合的协作-竞争大尺度系统以及相关的优化问题， 长期以来被理论研究忽略，虽然这类问题具有重要的理论研究和实际应用价值。 因此，本项目致力于全面地提出和开展大尺度优化的混合型的博弈与协作分析。

15307621.label: Realisation of objectives
15307621.value: All objectives have been completely realized and some interesting researches have been obtained. Specifically, we systematically investigate the decentralized decision of mean field team and game, the discuss the wellposedness of related consistency condition system. We also compare the decentralized strategy among all individual small agents when they are cooperative or competitive. Our consistency condition system can be modeled as an fully coupled forward-backward stochastic differential equation (FBSDE). Its wellposedness is an interesting and very challenging topic and we propose a series works to address it. Specifically, the Riccati decoupling in linenar-quadratic setup, and some reflected BSDE and FBSDE in nonlinear case, that can be viewed as some combination of mean-field control with stopping time.

15307621.label: Major findings and research outcome
15307621.value: We examine the decentralized equilibrium strategy of mean-field game and team and their mixture. Specially, the Nash asymptotic equilibrium in decentralized sense has been well developed and their related consistency condition system have been derived that can be of an asymmetric Hamiltonian system. In closed-loop representation, it is represented via an asymmetric Riccati equation (ARE). In terms of the mean-field team, the asymptotic team or social optima is characterized via a variation decomposition. The related Hamiltonian system and Riccati representation have also been derived. We also discuss the coalition structure in which some mixture between the team and game are formulated. The relevant consistency condition system together with its wellposedness is also discussed. We propose some wellposeness results using the determinant criteria. We also have an deep investigation of mean-field team in presence of heterogeneity and decision constraint. This leads to unified team analysis framework. Moreover, as some application, the robustness of mean field team and game are also discussed using soft constraint analysis.

15307621.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15307621.value: It is possible to extend the mixture of team and game by considering the related Paroto optima. The mean field Pareto is an interesting and well-applied research direction but no rich literature on it. Our mixed team and game can be further formulated into an general coalition structure with Pareto interaction. It is also possible to further investigate the implication of Pareto weight with the coalition degree. Another possible extension is to consider the mean-field team and game using weak formulation, and some related BSDE or FBSDE Hamiltonian system can be derived. We also discuss its uniqueness and existence using reflected BSDE, an natural extension of BSDE using barrier. We plan to discuss the mean-field game using weak formulation with optimal stopping decision. This will lead to some reflected BSDE consistency condition.

15307621.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15307621.value: The large population system involves considerable negligible decision makers or agents. All agents are minor since their behavior cannot change the feature of the whole system. however, their joint or overall characteristic plays an important role to determine the evolution of the large population system. All agents can be classified into cooperative teams and competitive games. This project introduce the mixed large population team and game via the so-called coalition structure. Based on it, we systematically discuss the related mean-field team and game strategies. It is found that the mixture degree plays an important role in the important consistency condition system.

15500021.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15500021.value: This proposal attempts to study the fund flow which is called ``heartbeats’’ among the exchange traded funds (ETFs). When an investor pumps large amount of assets into the ETF and then pull out a similar amount in stocks, we call this trade ``heartbeat,’’ since when you plot the fund flows in a graph, it looks similar to what one would see on an electrocardiogram when a heartbeats. This type of a trade benefits from the Tax Reform Act of 1969, which let funds hand over appreciated stocks to withdrawing investors defer the capital gains tax. According to Bloomberg Businessweek, U.S. stock ETFs deferred tax on more than $211 billion in gains 2018, which implies roughly $23 billion in taxes. We intend to examine how much these trades occur. We then analyze the underlying stocks that it gets withdrawn and the characteristics of these ETFs. We expect low-basis stock to be withdrawn in heartbeats to defer the capital gains tax. We also expect this activity to appear more frequently in events around changes in constituents in indices. In general, we expect ETFs that follow indices that are likely to remove shares that has appreciated, such as small cap and Russell 2000, or active managed ETFs to use heartbeat trades more often than others. For assets that prices have not appreciated but leaving the index, ETFs need not use heartbeats to remove the asset from the portfolio. We intend to check on the different trading behavior of ETFs related to this matter. Also, we will examine the difference of price pressure and liquidity change of stocks that gets removed from the ETF by heartbeats and non-heartbeats. Since removed assets are handled by authorized participants, we do not expect any difference of price pressure or liquidity changes among heartbeat and non-heartbeat removed assets. However, unlike flows from arbitrage trades, we do not expect that heartbeat trades would not close the price discrepancies between ETF's market price and net asset value. Finally, we propose to test whether investors prefer ETFs that frequently uses heartbeat trades. Compared with other funds following the same index, we expect that tax efficient ETFs enjoy more inflows than other funds with similar characteristics controlling for past returns. However, we expect the Vanguard mutual funds to be popular compared to other ETFs since Vanguard patented a way to avoid taxes on mutual funds using ETFs that is valid until 2023.

15500021.label: Realisation of objectives
15500021.value: 1. Summarize and Report the Size and Frequency of Heartbeat Trades Heartbeat trades are defined as coordinated creation-redemption sequences designed to eliminate embedded capital gains from ETF portfolios. The study identified 6,842 such events between 2010 and 2024, alongside 18,577 comparable non-heartbeat deletions. This indicates that approximately 11.41% of all stock terminations in the sample meet the heartbeat criteria, underscoring that this is a relatively frequent phenomenon, particularly among large equity ETFs. The size of heartbeat trades is substantial. Bloomberg estimated that in 2018 alone, 548 heartbeat transactions, valued at approximately $98 billion, occurred, enabling ETF investors to avoid taxes on roughly $203 billion of capital gains. This highlights the significant scale of these operations and their material impact on tax deferral. The study's findings consistently show that heartbeat trades are concentrated among large ETFs, with the average fund involved in a heartbeat event having a significantly higher asset under management (AUM) compared to those in non-heartbeat events (approximately 24% larger asset size). This concentration among major players like State Street, BlackRock, and Vanguard, who purified between $57-$64 billion in accumulated gains in 2018, suggests that the ability to orchestrate these large-scale in-kind transfers is a key competitive advantage for larger funds. 2. Examine the Characteristics of Stocks and ETFs that are Involved in Heartbeat Trades The analysis revealed distinct characteristics for both the stocks and ETFs involved in heartbeat trades, strongly supporting the hypothesis of a tax-motivated trading strategy. Characteristics of Stocks: Stocks removed via heartbeat redemptions systematically exhibit characteristics consistent with large embedded capital gains. They are: Larger and More Liquid: Heartbeat-deleted stocks are, on average, substantially larger in market capitalization (mean log market capitalization 1.764 vs. 1.44 for non-heartbeats, a significant difference of 0.324). Growth-Oriented: They tend to have lower book-to-market ratios (mean 0.463 vs. 0.553), indicating they are growth stocks that have experienced significant prior price appreciation. High Prior Returns: These stocks show markedly stronger past performance. For instance, over the 13-36 months prior to deletion, heartbeat stocks appreciated about 5.1 percentage points more than non-heartbeat stocks (40.8% vs. 35.7%). This confirms that ETFs target their most highly appreciated positions to maximize tax deferral. Characteristics of ETFs: ETFs that utilize heartbeat trades also exhibit specific attributes: Large AUM: They tend to be significantly larger, with higher assets under management, reinforcing that larger ETFs are the primary users of this strategy. Low Expense Ratios: These funds typically charge significantly lower expense ratios (0.376% vs. 0.468% annually), consistent with them being index-oriented or otherwise tax-sensitive funds that compete on low costs and tax efficiency. Lower Portfolio Turnover: Heartbeat-participating ETFs exhibit much lower average annual portfolio turnover (248% vs. 442% for non-heartbeat funds), suggesting they minimize regular trading and rely on occasional in-kind redemptions to adjust holdings and manage tax liabilities. Persistent Usage: Nearly 90% of heartbeat events occur in ETFs that have used a heartbeat before, indicating a high degree of persistence and a habitual tendency for certain ETF sponsors to employ this strategy. Not Driven by Outflows/Distress: Contrary to some assumptions, heartbeat trades are not primarily a reaction to investor redemptions or liquidity needs. Funds experiencing heavy outflows are, in fact, less likely to employ heartbeat trades, and the practice is heavily skewed toward stable, established, asset-rich ETFs. This reinforces that heartbeats are driven by tax motives rather than financial distress. 3. Analyze the Effects on Market Liquidity and Market Efficiency The study found that heartbeat trades do not eliminate price pressure but rather shift it and amplify subsequent reversals, raising concerns about market fairness and informational asymmetry. Short-Term Price Distortions: Stocks deleted via heartbeat redemptions experience abnormal negative returns in the days leading up to the event, which then reverse in the days immediately following. This "V-shaped" transient return pattern is consistent with anticipatory trading by market participants, likely Authorized Participants (APs), who foresee the impending redemption. Anticipatory Trading and Information Asymmetry: The propensity-score matched analysis revealed that during the pre-event window (Days -2 to 0), heartbeat targets underperform their matched counterparts by approximately 9 basis points. On the event date (Day 0), the return differential widens markedly to -0.131 basis points, reflecting the price concession when the in-kind block is delivered to the AP. In the post-event window (Days +1 to +2), this pattern reverses, with heartbeat stocks outperforming their controls by 0.144 percentage points. This sequence—price weakness prior to settlement coupled with an immediate post-event reversal—is precisely the footprint expected if APs or affiliated desks short the target stock in anticipation of receiving it in-kind and subsequently cover their positions. Concentration of Impact: The price effects are economically meaningful and are primarily concentrated in transactions initiated by the largest ETFs. For top-quintile ETFs, the net post-minus-pre return differential exceeds +1 percentage point, while for smaller funds, it is economically negligible. This heterogeneity confirms that large block transfers generate sufficiently sizable price effects to elicit anticipatory trading and a measurable subsequent correction. These findings imply that while the in-kind mechanism is tax-efficient for shareholders, it induces additional short-horizon volatility and raises concerns about informational asymmetry, as price pressure materializes before the trade becomes public and is promptly reversed once short positions are covered. This creates a tension between the tax benefits for ETF investors and the potential costs imposed on the broader market. 4. Examine the Behavior of Investors Towards Heartbeat Trades The report primarily focuses on the behavior of ETF managers and Authorized Participants (APs) in relation to heartbeat trades, rather than individual retail investor behavior. ETF Manager Behavior: ETF managers strategically employ heartbeat trades to enhance tax efficiency for their shareholders. They deliberately target highly appreciated securities for in-kind redemptions to maximize the reduction in future tax liabilities, thereby preserving the fund's tax efficiency and sparing long-term shareholders a taxable distribution. This behavior is a persistent, ingrained part of their management toolkit, especially for large, low-cost index funds. Authorized Participant (AP) Behavior: The study provides strong evidence that APs (or affiliated desks) exploit their privileged knowledge of forthcoming redemptions. The observed price patterns—pre-event underperformance followed by a sharp post-event rebound—are consistent with APs engaging in anticipatory short-selling of the target stock before receiving it in-kind, and then covering their positions once the redeemed shares circulate back into the market. This behavior highlights an informational asymmetry where APs gain a timing advantage not available to other market participants. While ETFs typically do not pay explicit fees to APs for facilitating heartbeat trades, APs may benefit through these less transparent trading opportunities. In conclusion, heartbeat trades are a sophisticated, tax-driven mechanism primarily utilized by large, low-cost ETFs to manage capital gains. While highly beneficial for ETF investors in terms of tax deferral, these trades create measurable, short-term price distortions and raise concerns about informational asymmetry and market fairness, particularly due to the anticipatory trading behavior of Authorized Participants.

15500021.label: Major findings and research outcome
15500021.value: This comprehensive study provides the first security-level empirical analysis of ETF "heartbeat trades," confirming their role as a strategic tax-management tool. We identified 6,842 heartbeat events between 2010 and 2024, representing approximately 11.41% of all stock terminations by ETFs. These trades are substantial in size, with Bloomberg estimating $203 billion in capital gains avoided in 2018 alone. Our findings robustly demonstrate that heartbeat trades are systematically employed by large, low-cost, and low-turnover ETFs with a history of using such tactics. They are not driven by fund distress or outflows, but rather by the deliberate selection of stocks with large unrealized capital gains (high prior returns, low book-to-market ratios) to maximize tax deferral for shareholders. Crucially, the research reveals that heartbeat trades induce significant short-term price distortions in the underlying stocks. These stocks exhibit a "V-shaped" return pattern: underperforming in the days leading up to the redemption and then sharply rebounding afterward. This pattern is consistent with anticipatory trading and information asymmetry, where Authorized Participants (APs) exploit their privileged knowledge of impending redemptions. The price impact is economically meaningful and concentrated in trades executed by the largest ETFs, suggesting that while heartbeat trades are tax-efficient for investors, they create market inefficiencies and potential unfairness for other market participants.

15500021.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15500021.value: Future research could expand on several key areas. Firstly, as ETFs continue to grow, examining whether increased heartbeat activity correlates with broader measures of market efficiency or liquidity would be valuable. Secondly, the concentration of heartbeat usage among large ETF sponsors raises questions about industry competition; exploring if this ability acts as a barrier to entry for smaller fund families is a promising avenue. Thirdly, with the rise of non-transparent ETFs, investigating how reduced holdings disclosure impacts the feasibility and market effects of heartbeat strategies is crucial. Finally, comparative studies across different regulatory jurisdictions could shed light on how variations in tax treatment influence global ETF trading behavior. The proposed course of action involves leveraging granular trading data and potentially incorporating qualitative insights from market participants to further quantify the costs and benefits of these complex transactions.

15500021.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15500021.value: There's a special trick that ETFs (Exchange-Traded Funds) use to help their investors avoid paying taxes on their profits. It's called a "heartbeat trade." Instead of selling stocks that have gone up a lot in value (which would trigger taxes), the ETF temporarily swaps these stocks with a special partner (an "Authorized Participant, AP"). This partner then sells the stocks, but because of a tax loophole, the ETF and its investors don't have to pay the capital gains tax. This study found that these "heartbeat trades" happen quite often and involve huge amounts of money, saving ETF investors billions in taxes each year. However, there's a catch: because the AP knows exactly which stocks are being swapped, they can sometimes make a quick profit by trading those stocks just before and after the swap, causing temporary ups and downs in the stock price. This means while ETF investors benefit from tax savings, other ordinary investors might unknowingly buy or sell at slightly worse prices during these "heartbeat" events. The research highlights a complex situation where tax benefits meet concerns about fair play in the stock market.

15500421.label: Project Objectives
15500421.value: First, we plan to overcome one key barrier in conducting in-depth investigations on CSR contracting (e.g., the examination of the determinates of and possible capital market consequences associated with the emerging practices of integrating explicitly non-financial CSR criteria into executive compensation) by conducting a large-scale hand-collection for detailed CSR contracting data at the firm- or executive-level. Second, this study aims to conduct a comprehensive examination to identify various firm-, industry- and country-level determinants of this new compensation practice. Through the identification of the determinants, it helps regulators and major capital market participants in better understanding of the heterogeneity of such practices, across firms, industries and countries. Third, our study would contribute to the literature by identifying and presenting evidence showing the potential role of the inclusion of CSR criteria in compensation schemes to various managerial behavior, such as firms' long-term investment. Forth, using an international setting to examine CSR contracting, we will be able to examine further whether and how the role of CSR contracting in capital markets varies across country-level institutional environment. Fifth, by conducting a comprehensive examination of such practice using detailed CSR contracting information, we aim to identify the practices with the potential to create the greatest effect on fostering managerial long-term orientation while at the same time maximize shareholders’ value. Last, the findings of this research would be able to offer an opportunity to identify the potential best practices in the real world for future knowledge transfer.
