15503421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15503421.value: Private equity (PE) has become a large investor in the healthcare sector in the US. In addition, healthcare spending in the U.S. ranks the highest among developed countries. PE investments in US healthcare thus have the potential to have a large impact on people’s lives. While PE’s growing role in US healthcare is beginning to draw attention from the public, regulators, and politicians, unfortunately empirical evidence is lacking. Ex ante, it is not clear how PE would affect healthcare costs. Previous studies suggest that PE can cut costs and improve firms’ operational efficiency, which suggests PE takeovers of medical facilities might reduce healthcare costs. Yet, managers of PE-owned medical facilities, whose incentives are strongly aligned with equity holders, plausibly have strong incentives to breach implicit contracts and extract rents from patients. Due to high information asymmetry in the need for care and the quality of care, patient insulation from direct costs through the dominance of third party payment schemes, and increased consolidation of hospital markets, economic theory suggests that the healthcare sector is particularly vulnerable to provider rent-seeking. This proposal attempts to study the pricing impact of private equity acquisitions in U.S. hospitals. We will take advantage of a private health insurance claims data covering 28% of individuals with employer sponsored health insurance. The claims data contain actual prices paid to hospitals, enabling us to correctly infer hospital price changes around PE acquisitions. Our analysis will first shed light on the determinants of PE buyouts in the hospital industry. Next, holding constant patient diagnosis, hospital quality and case complexity, we will investigate the impact of PE acquisitions on hospital prices, and on the incidence and magnitude of out-of-network billing. Finally, we will examine how the price effect of PE acquisition varies with local hospital market competition, and how it differs from other types of hospital mergers. The results of this project will contribute to the scholarly literature on the impacts of PE investment on firms’ stakeholders. It will provide a better understanding of the role of PE investors in the healthcare sector, a critical issue at a time when private equity funds have penetrated the healthcare industry and when healthcare sector has been facing pressure to cut costs and prices. As private equity investment in healthcare has accelerated around the world (including China), the findings should be also useful and important for regulators and governments in many other countries. 私募股權已成為美國醫療保健行業的一個大投資者。此外，美國的醫療保健支出在發達國家中位居首位。因此，針對美國醫療保健的私募投資可能對人們的生活產生重大影響。雖然私募股權在美國醫療行業中日益重要的地位已經開始引起公眾、監管機構和政界人士的註意，但目前仍舊缺乏經驗性的證據。 進行此計劃課題之前，我們尚不清楚私募將如何影響醫療保健的成本。先前的研究表明，私募可以降低成本並提高公司的運營效率，這說明私募對醫療企業的收購可能會降低醫療成本。然而，在私募持有的醫療企業中，管理者擁有與股東高度一致的動機，這些管理者會更可能去違反隱性合同從而從患者那裏榨取利益。在醫療保健領域，醫療需求和醫療質量信息高度不對稱，患者因第三方支付機製盛行而與醫療直接成本隔絕，醫院市場集中度提高。鑒於以上特質，經濟理論指出醫療行業特別容易受到供給端尋租行為的影響。 在本次研究中，我們將利用一份涵蓋了全美28%雇主提供醫療保險的雇員的私人醫療保險索賠數據，嘗試去研究私募收購對於美國醫院價格的影響。這份索賠數據包含了支付給醫院的實際價格，使得我們能夠從中正確推斷出私募收購前後醫院價格的變化。我們的分析將首先闡明私募在醫療行業進行收購的決定性因素。接下來，在保持患者診斷、醫院質量和病例復雜性不變的情況下，我們將研究私募收購對醫院價格以及保外計費發生率和量級的影響。最後，我們將研究私募收購對醫院價格的影響是如何隨著當地醫院市場的競爭而變化的，以及私募收購與其他類型的醫院並購有何不同。 這個研究課題的結論將為私募投資如何影響公司權益關系者的學術文獻做出重要貢獻。它將讓人們更好地了解私募投資者在醫療保健行業中的作用。在私募基金滲透到醫療行業且醫療行業面臨成本削減和價格壓力的時期，這是一個關鍵的課題。隨著醫療領域的私募投資在全球（包括中國）加速，這個課題的研究結果對許多其他國家的監管機構和政府來說都有重要益處。

15503421.label: Realisation of objectives
15503421.value: We have finished empirical tests of all the three revised objectives. For revised objective #1, we find little effect of corporate practice of medicine laws on hopsitals' quality of treatment, and medical technology adoption. We tried different identification strategies: including Instrumental variable approach and matched DID. Due to the bias of publishing significant results in Finance, accounting and other Social Science fields, we decided to save time and not to write a working paper on the no findings of this project. For revised objective #2, we've completed a working paper, which is titled "Healthcare Workers' Pay Transparency and Patient Satisfaction". In this paper, by utilizing the staggered, state-level implementation of pay transparency laws in the U.S., we find that patient satisfaction is higher for hospitals in states that enact a pay transparency law than it is in states with no such legislation, consistent with the fair wage-effort theory. Within the healthcare context, this theory predicts that fairer wages for healthcare workers will incentivize them, resulting in higher-quality patient care. The positive effect of pay transparency on patient satisfaction is more significant for hospitals in Democratic states and in states where the hospital industry has a larger gender-based pay gap. The positive effect is also more evident in less profit-driven hospitals and in those that exhibit a higher labor intensity. Overall, we offer novel evidence that workers' pay transparency has a positive transmission effect on customer satisfaction. For revised objective #3, we used flooding to proxy for climate risk faced by hospitals, but the results were quite mixed. Thus, we put the project in our backpocket until very recent (see 6.2 below).

15503421.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15503421.value: For Objective #3, thinking carefully, flooding does not only affect local people's demand for healthcare, but it also affects hospitals' fundamentals that in turns affects the supply side of healthcare. Thus, we went to collect data on extreme temperature and used this as an alternative climate risk proxy, which does not affect a hospital's fundamentals. Moreover, the data on hospital ownership from AHA has many errors. We have also been trying to clean the data, which required manual check on a facility's ownership over time and we have a long time series from 1980 to 2022. An accurate ownership dataset on hospitals will improve the power of our tests. We will follow up and keep working on it using this new proxy. We aim to run empirical tests and have a working paper by 2025.

15503421.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15503421.value: This study demonstrates that legally mandating pay transparency for hospital employees can have a positive impact on patient satisfaction. The impact of pay transparency is more significant in hospitals in Democratic-leaning states. We also document that the effect of pay transparency on patient satisfaction is more evident in hospitals with a wider pre-existing gender-based wage gap and a greater post-adoption reduction in that wage gap, as well as in non-profit hospitals, government-owned hospitals, and those not owned by physicians. These findings suggest that pay transparency enhances patient satisfaction primarily through wage equality and improved employee morale. The positive effect is stronger for more laborintensive hospitals, which confirms that the effect operates through the labor channel. Finally, we present evidence that pay transparency laws reduce gender-based and overall pay inequality for hospital employees and that the laws increase lower-paid hospital employees’ wages, which lends further support to the fair wage-effort mechanism. We also corroborate our main finding by demonstrating that pay transparency laws can reduce hospital readmissions. Given that laws that enhance pay transparency and equity for workers continue to be developed, our study has valuable insights for policymakers.

15503921.label: Major findings and research outcome
15503921.value: We have met the objectives of the project and come up with results in three journal papers. The details of the three journal papers are as follows. (1) In the paper “Optimization of after-sales services with spare parts consumption and repairman travel” published in International Journal of Production Economics, we studied the optimization of discretionary after-sales maintenance services with spare parts consumption and repairman travel. Discretionary service means that the service quality (which depends on the use of imperfect IoT technology or not, and the repairman) and spare parts consumption are determined by the service provider. For details, please refer to the paper. (2) In the paper “Optimal after-sales service offering strategy: Additive manufacturing, traditional manufacturing, or hybrid?” published in International Journal of Production Economics, we investigated the effects of additive manufacturing (also known as 3D printing; an IoT application) on the optimal after-sales maintenance service offering strategy. A service offering strategy should be selected on the basis of not only its characteristics but also customers’ decisions influenced by the associated costs of each strategy. Two supply chain structures are examined in this study: one in which the service provider is vertically integrated and the other in which an outside agent is involved to adopt additive manufacturing. For details, please refer to the paper. (3) In the paper “Maintenance services offering strategies with imperfect IoT-enabled diagnostics: Monopoly and duopoly scenarios” submitted to Production and Operations Management, we analyzed the optimal capacity allocation and pricing decisions of service providers by taking account the imperfect nature of IoT-enabled diagnostics. The optimal service offering strategies are presented. Monopoly and duopoly scenarios are discussed separately. For details, please refer to the paper.

15503921.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15503921.value: Internet of Things (IoT) provides firms with new levels of traceability, quick response, and adaptability to cope with various after-sales services challenges. However, the application of IoT in after-sales services suffers from data noise and security attacks. Data noise leads to inaccurate outcomes of product status, while security attacks lead to economic and business losses. We have developed advanced mathematical tools capable of deriving optimal operational strategies with dual IoT accuracy and security concerns.

15504421.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15504421.value: 鎖定國際供應商與買家的關係:來自中美貿易戰的證據

15504421.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15504421.value: Prof Cui, Lin Prof Yiu, Daphne

15504421.label: Project Objectives
15504421.value: • This project aims to examine the impact of the US–China trade war on the relationship between US buyers and Chinese suppliers. o Problem identification: The current literature has investigated the factors driving buyer–supplier relationships (BSRs) from firm and relational perspectives; however, the impacts of exogenous shocks (e.g., trade war) to BSRs have been largely overlooked. International events are a vital source of such shocks, given that supply chains are now highly globalized, and hence, increasingly vulnerable to events such as trade wars and global pandemics. Firms have made a great effort to develop international BSRs, but these are now being challenged by adverse events. o Problem elements: This project will adopt a quasi-experimental design to examine the impacts of the trade war. The treatment (independent variable) is the trade tariff increase, while the effect (dependent variable) is the relational value of the dyad between the US buyer and the Chinese supplier. o Expected outcomes: Using the dyadic transaction value (known as the relational value) as the proxy for the BSR, this project is expected to capture the abnormal relational value change in US buyer – Chinese supplier dyads during the trade war. o Significance: This project is the first academic research effort to investigate how the US–China trade war contributed to BSR dissolutions between US buyers and Chinese suppliers. This project will have significant implications for firms in terms of managing international BSRs. The outcomes of this project will serve as an important reference for both buyers and suppliers in the global supply chain for estimating the possible consequences of a new tariff. • This project aims to explore the factors that may mitigate international buyer–supplier dissolutions during the trade war, or, in other words, “lock-in” buyers. o Problem identification: The occurrence of exogenous events, such as trade wars, are not under the control of firms. Firms need to understand how to cope with the impacts of such events, but the literature provides limited implications for both buyers and suppliers in terms of how to maintain the affected BSR. o Problem elements: This project objective aims to identify the moderators for the first objective (impacts of trade war on international BSRs). o Expected outcomes: Drawing on the theoretical lenses of social exchange theory, transaction cost theory and resource dependence theory, this project is expected to illustrate that dependences (measured as prior relational value and vertical relatedness), buyer asset specificity (measured as relational-specific investments and asset redeployability) and supplier innovativeness (measured as patents over R&D expenditures) can mitigate international BSR dissolutions in the trade war. Both firm- and industry-level evidence will be generated to demonstrate these findings. o Significance: This research objective adds to the literature calling for the development of resilient global supply chains (Pettit et al., 2019). This project will advance the literature by improving our understanding of the factors driving international supply chain resilience given the dynamism of international relations. The expected outcome will provide guidance for buyers in developed countries and suppliers in developing countries to take precautionary measures to mitigate supply chain risks.

15504421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15504421.value: Over the last few decades, offshoring has been widely adopted by multinational corporations (MNCs), and production has been extensively outsourced to developing countries. In line with this, the global supply chain has developed substantially, which has helped to reduce production costs for MNCs. To sustain competitiveness, MNCs have also made great efforts to develop long-term international buyer–supplier relations. However, trade barriers are increasingly being used by governments to protect domestic industry, indicating the global supply chain is entering a “de-globalization” phase. Thus, a question arises as to how these emerging trade barriers affect the buyer–supplier relationship between MNCs and their offshored suppliers? To enter this discourse, this project will examine how the US–China trade war caused broad relationship dissolution between US buyers and Chinese suppliers. This project will adopt an experimental design and use the dyadic transaction value (known as relational value) as a proxy for the buyer–supplier relationship. This project aims to provide evidence of an abnormal relational value change in US buyer–Chinese supplier dyads during the trade war. This project will further explore the factors that may mitigate such dissolution, or “lock-in” buyers. Drawing from the theoretical lenses of social exchange theory, transaction cost theory and resource dependence theory, this project proposes that dependences (measured as prior relational value and vertical relatedness), buyer asset specificity (measured as relational-specific investments and asset redeployability) and supplier innovativeness (measured as patents over R&D expenditure) are essential to mitigate buyer–supplier relationship dissolution during the trade war. This project seeks to provide both significant theoretical contributions and practical implications. Supply chain management scholars have investigated the factors driving buyer–supplier relationships from firm and relational perspectives; however, shocks to trade policy have been largely overlooked. Firms have made significant efforts to develop international buyer–supplier relationships, but these are now being challenged by adverse events. This project will be the first academic research proposal to investigate how the US–China trade war may have triggered relational dissolutions between US buyers and Chinese suppliers. This advances the literature by increasing our understanding of how the buyer–supplier relationship may adapt to business environment changes. The project outcome will also provide fresh insights for industry practitioners, by improving our understanding of how buyers and suppliers can mitigate the negative impacts. Last, this project will provide evidence for policymakers to aid the evaluation of the policy effects of tariffs. This project outcome will serve as an important reference for future trade policy-making. 跨國公司在過去數十年裡廣泛採用離岸外包策略，產品製造被大量外包到發展中國家。全球供應鏈亦因此得到發展。跨國公司的製造成本也因此下降。由於維持競爭優勢的需要， 跨國公司已投入大量資源來建立長期的國際供應商關係。但是由於近來貿易壁壘被許多政府使用以保護本國產業，這些趨勢讓國際供應鏈進入一個“去全球化”的階段。 這些變化驅使我們提出一個問題：“這些貿易壁壘如何影響跨國公司與他們離岸供應商的關係？” 因此，此項目探究中美貿易戰是否會讓美國顧客與其中國供應商脫鉤。此項目會設計一項自然實驗並以與供應商的交易金額來測量顧客與供應商的關係。此項目將提供實證證據以捕捉供應商交易金額於中美貿易戰中的異常變動。 此項目將會進一步探究什麼因素能夠減輕中美貿易戰所引致的脫鉤。這些探究將建基於社會交換理論，交易成本理論以及資源依賴理論。此項目提出買賣雙方的依賴度， 顧客的資產專用性， 以及供應商的創新性為三個重要的因素。 此項目尋求提供有價值的理論貢獻以及現實意義。供應鏈管理學者過去常從公司和買賣雙方關係的角度探究供應商關係。然而外生貿易政策政策衝擊的影響常常被學者忽略。企業已投放大量精力以建立良好的供應商關係，然而這些關係正受到國際事件的挑戰。此項目將為第一項學術研究以探究中美貿易戰中的顧客-供應商脫鉤現象。這些研究將增加我們對供應商關係如何應對環境變化的理解。此項目的成果亦能為企業應對政策衝擊帶來有用的啟示。最後，此項目亦會為政策制定者提供證據以評估貿易政策所帶來的影響。這些項目成果可作為未來貿易政策制定的重要參考。

15504421.label: Realisation of objectives
15504421.value: This project was guided by two key objectives: (1) to understand how the U.S.-China trade war impacted cross-border buyer-supplier relationships and firm-level operational performance; and (2) to identify factors that mitigate these negative effects. Objective 1: Impact of the trade war on buyer-supplier relationships and firm performance This objective has been fully realized. Drawing on a quasi-experimental, difference-in-differences methodology, the research provides compelling evidence that the 2018 U.S.-China trade war exerted a pronounced negative influence on U.S.-China buyer-supplier dyads. Firms in the U.S. that sourced directly from China suffered elevated inventory levels (days of supply by 8.2 days) and reduced profitability (return-on-assets by 1.29%), reflecting a disruption in the smooth flow of goods and cost structures. Furthermore, dyadic transaction values declined by approximately 18.42%, signifying a substantial erosion in relational value. By documenting how global political events translate into measurable operational and relational strain, this project makes a vital theoretical contribution to the international operations and supply chain management literature. It extends resource dependence theory and transaction cost economics by showing that external political turbulence can reconfigure power dependencies and transaction costs in cross-border relationships. This contribution emphasizes that managers cannot treat global supply networks as static; rather, they must actively consider the geopolitical environment as a key operational contingency. Objective 2: Identifying factors that mitigate the negative effects The project also successfully accomplished its second objective by illuminating the conditions under which firms can preserve or restore buyer-supplier stability amid geopolitical disruption. The findings highlight that not all dyads were equally vulnerable. Chinese suppliers with robust innovation capabilities, stronger corporate social responsibility (CSR) performance, and fewer local political ties displayed greater resilience. Similarly, U.S. buyers who managed less complex and more strategically composed supply bases were better positioned to withstand these shocks. This adds substantive nuance to theoretical frameworks, illustrating that the interplay of supplier attributes and supply base strategies can counterbalance exogenous threats. Theoretically, this refines existing models by demonstrating that firm-level capabilities and network configurations serve as buffering mechanisms that align with resource dependence logic (i.e., the importance of reducing uncertainty) and transaction cost considerations (i.e., safeguarding against opportunistic behavior under stress). Practically, it advises managers to invest in innovation, CSR initiatives, and careful sourcing strategies to bolster supply chain resilience. It also informs policymakers that stable and predictable trade policies are not merely political or economic tools but also mechanisms to preserve healthy global supply networks. By meeting both objectives and integrating these theoretical and practical insights, this research enriches the broader discourse on global supply chain resilience. It underscores that geopolitical conflicts have tangible, quantifiable effects on firm operations and relational stability. At the same time, it provides a roadmap for countering these disruptions through targeted strategies, advancing scholarly understanding while offering managers and policymakers clear guidance for navigating an increasingly uncertain global trade environment.

15504421.label: Major findings and research outcome
15504421.value: Our research investigates the impacts of geopolitical uncertainty on firm using three complementary studies. Two of studies published in Journal of Operations Management (JOM) and one published in International Journal of Operations and Production Management (IJOPM). Please refer to Part C for the publication details of these three papers. The first study (Fan et al., 2022, JOM) employs a difference-in-differences analysis to assess the impact of tariffs on U.S. firms with direct supplier connections in China. Results indicate that firms with direct Chinese suppliers experienced worse performance than those without, particularly in terms of increased inventory levels (days of supply) and reduced profitability (return-on-assets). Furthermore, firms with greater outsourcing intensity and higher horizontal or spatial supply base complexity suffered more severe negative impacts, highlighting the vulnerabilities in complex supply chains during trade disruptions. The second study (Fan et al., 2024, JOM) examines the transactional relationships between Chinese suppliers and their U.S. buyers. Using a natural experiment, we find that the trade war led to a significant 18.42% decline in transaction values for affected dyads. However, this adverse impact was mitigated when Chinese suppliers exhibited superior innovation capabilities, higher corporate social responsibility (CSR) performance, or fewer local political ties, suggesting that these factors play critical roles in sustaining buyer–supplier relationships amid exogenous shocks. The third study (Fan et al., 2023, IJOPM) uses two-way fixed-effects regression on panel data to explore firms' responses to political risk. It finds that firms are more sensitive to political risk when facing income stream uncertainty or strategic risks, but not stock return uncertainty. Firm-specific political risk is positively associated with vertical integration and product diversification, though it does not drive geographical diversification. These findings suggest that political risk significantly shapes firms' strategic responses, particularly in uncertain environments. Lastly, we have also developed a partitioner paper to summarize the practical implications, which is currently under review at Harvard Business Review. Collectively, these studies underscore the disruptive effects of the trade war on international buyer–supplier relationships and firm performance while identifying mitigating factors and strategic responses that can enhance resilience in global supply chains.

15504421.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15504421.value: This research lays the groundwork for deepening our understanding of how global supply chains respond to exogenous shocks, including trade wars. Future research could investigate how multiple concurrent disruptions, ranging from geopolitical conflicts to pandemics or environmental crises, jointly shape firm strategies and performance outcomes. Additionally, longitudinal analyses could track how buyer–supplier relationships and supply chain reconfigurations evolve over time, shedding light on the lasting structural changes and adaptive capabilities firms develop. Methodologically, incorporating qualitative case studies or interviews could enrich the quantitative findings and reveal context-specific coping strategies, enabling a more comprehensive understanding of why certain mitigation efforts succeed. Extending this research to different industries and geographic regions would illuminate whether these insights hold broadly or require tailoring to unique market conditions. In terms of practical implications, the findings support the development of managerial frameworks and policy recommendations that emphasize innovation, social responsibility, and strategic diversification as tools for building resilience. By engaging industry stakeholders and policymakers, future work can foster balanced trade policies and industry guidelines, ultimately strengthening global supply networks against future disruptions.

15504421.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15504421.value: This research looks at how the U.S.-China trade war affected businesses that buy products from Chinese suppliers. When tariffs suddenly went up, many American companies that relied on these suppliers saw their costs rise and profits drop. But not all companies suffered equally. Some Chinese suppliers, especially those who were more innovative, had better social responsibility practices, or did not depend heavily on local political connections, managed to keep stronger ties with their U.S. buyers. On the American side, companies that spread out their supply chains and built more flexible strategies were less harmed. By understanding which factors helped firms stay resilient during the trade war, this research offers valuable lessons for business leaders and policymakers. It can guide them in making decisions that reduce the negative impacts of sudden international disputes. Ultimately, this knowledge can help companies become better prepared for future challenges, ensuring that global trade remains more stable and reliable.

15504921.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15504921.value: Public companies are characterised by dispersed ownership. Assuming that investors act individually, the dispersion of ownership will impede intervention and create a free-rider problem (Shleifer and Vishny, 1986). Recent evidence calls this assumption into question by showing that investors are, in fact, connected to one another. While there has been an overall decline in the concentration of institutional ownership, over the past few decades there has been a substantial increase in ownership by connected institutional investors (Crane, Koch, and Michenaud, 2019). Despite the growing importance of shareholder connection, little is known about its real effects on companies. For example, how does shareholder connection affect corporate risk-taking behaviour? What are the implications of shareholder connection for a company's costs of borrowing and financing policies? My proposed project will examine these issues to fill the gap in the literature. In this project, I will investigate the real effects of shareholder connection on companies. One means by which to boost shareholder value is to force leveraged firms to increase risk-taking (Jensen and Meckling, 1976). If shareholders are isolated from one another, the high cost of coordinating their activities may prevent them from acting on the risk-shifting incentives. Connections between shareholders, either through common portfolio holdings or through social interactions, can reduce the cost of coordination and can facilitate shareholders' intervention to extract rents from debtholders, which may result in higher levels of firm risk. Therefore, I will investigate the effects of shareholder connection on corporate risk-taking behaviour, especially for firms that are approaching financial distress. I will also investigate the effects of shareholder connection on firms' costs of borrowing and financing policies. If shareholder connection intensifies the conflicts between debtholders and shareholders due to an increase in risk-taking, firms may face higher costs of borrowing and thus will have no choice but to increase their reliance on other sources of financing. To provide causal evidence on these effects, I will explore the 2003 mutual fund scandal and mergers between financial institutions as exogenous shocks to shareholder connection. The proposed project will provide a comprehensive analysis of how the connections between shareholders affect corporate risk-taking behaviour, costs of borrowing, and financing policies. The study's findings will contribute to the academic literature by demonstrating the real effects of investor connection on portfolio companies. More importantly, the findings will provide valuable guidance to the policymakers who wish to draft new regulations on shareholder coordination. 股權分散是上市公司的一個重要特徵。假設投資者獨立行動，股權分散會妨礙股東對公司進行干預，造成“搭便車”問題（Shleifer and Vishny，1986）。然而，這個假設受到了質疑，最近的證據表明投資者實際上是相互關聯的。在過去幾十年裡，伴隨著機構投資者股權集中度的整體下降，由相互關聯的機構投資者持有的股份比例大幅增長（Crane，Koch，and Michenaud，2019）。儘管股東關聯的重要性越來越高，但是我們關於其對公司的實際效應知之甚少。例如，股東關聯如何影響企業的風險承擔行為？股東關聯對於公司的借款成本和融資政策有什麼影響？本項目將會研究這些問題，以填補文獻中的空缺。 在本項目中，我將會研究股東關聯對公司的實際效應。提高股東價值的其中一種方式是迫使負債企業增加風險承擔，即進行風險轉移（Jensen and Meckling，1976）。在孤立的股東之間協調行動的高成本可能會抑制股東出於風險轉移動機而對公司進行的干預。通過共同持股或者社交互動形成的關聯，可以降低股東之間協調行動的成本，從而促進股東為攫取債權人利益而進行的干預，導致更高的公司風險水平。因此，我將會研究股東關聯對公司風險承擔行為的效應，尤其是處於財務困境中的公司。我也會研究股東關聯對公司借款成本和融資政策的效應。如果股東關聯通過提高公司風險進而加劇債權人與股東之間的衝突，公司可能會面臨更高的借款成本，因而不得不依賴於其他的融資來源。為了提供證據證明上述效應中的因果關係，我將會探索對股東關聯的外生衝擊，包括2003年美國基金醜聞以及金融機構之間的並購。 本項目將會詳盡分析股東關聯如何影響公司的風險承擔行為、借款成本、以及融資政策。本項目的研究成果將會闡明投資者關聯對被投資公司的實際效應，對已有文獻做出有益補充。更重要的是，本項目的研究成果將會為股權投資方面的政策制定者提供有價值的指引。

15504921.label: Realisation of objectives
15504921.value: The project objectives have been fully achieved. Details are provided below. (1) The first objective is to examine the effects of shareholder connection on corporate risk-taking behaviour. To achieve this objective, I have conducted empirical analysis using a comprehensive sample of US public companies over the period from 1980 to 2020. I construct a firm-level measure of shareholders’ portfolio overlap, defined as the ownership-weighted average of pair-wise portfolio overlap across all institutional investors in a given firm. Using stock volatility as the main measure of risk-taking, I estimate OLS regressions that control for various firm characteristics as well as firm and industry-year fixed effects. I find that managers take on more risk when the firm’s shareholders have a higher degree of portfolio overlap. The evidence lends support to the hypothesis that higher connectedness among shareholders through the network of common holdings is conducive to increased managerial risk-taking. I have conducted a number of additional analyses to support the interpretation of the main finding. To help establish a causal link between shareholders’ portfolio overlap and managerial risk-taking, I exploit mergers between financial institutions as a source of plausibly exogenous variation in shareholders’ portfolio overlap. Using an instrumental variable approach, I find robust results corroborating those obtained from the main analysis. In addition, I perform cross-sectional analyses to strengthen the causal inference that shareholders’ portfolio overlap affects managerial risk-taking. Specifically, I find that the baseline effect is concentrated in firms where risk-taking is personally costlier for managers (i.e., managers have larger ownership stakes, shorter tenure, or lower job mobility), where stakeholder relationships intensify shareholders’ risk preference (i.e., firms have higher distress risk or no major customer relationships), where managers have weaker risk-taking incentives from compensation (i.e., managers receive lower option-based pay), and where shareholder coordination is more important (i.e., firms have a more dispersed ownership structure). These heterogeneous effects support the idea that the increased risk-taking is driven by shareholders mitigating the risk-related agency conflicts. (2) The second objective is to examine the effects of shareholder connection on the costs of borrowing for firms. To achieve this objective, I have gathered data on firms’ bank loans. I estimate panel regressions that control for various firm- and loan-level characteristics as well as firm, year, and loan-type fixed effects. The results indicate that neither loan spreads nor the number of financial covenants in the loan package is significantly affected by shareholders’ portfolio overlap. Overall, I find no evidence that shareholders’ portfolio overlap has a significant effect on firms’ costs of borrowing. (3) The third objective is to examine the effects of shareholder connection on firms' financing policies. To achieve this objective, I have estimated panel regressions using firms’ financial policies as the dependent variables. Specifically, I find that when the degree of shareholders’ portfolio overlap is higher, managers reduce cash holdings, increase financial leverage, and make larger payout. These findings bolster the notion that shareholders with greater portfolio overlap induce managers to adopt riskier financial policies.

15504921.label: Major findings and research outcome
15504921.value: This project explores the implications of shareholders’ portfolio overlap for the risk-related agency problem. The major findings are summarized as follows. I find that managerial risk-taking increases with the degree of portfolio overlap among a firm’s institutional shareholders. An instrumental variable analysis supports a causal interpretation of the baseline finding. Consistent with the hypothesis that shareholders’ portfolio overlap facilitates intervention in managers’ risk choices, I find that the effect is more pronounced when risk-taking is personally costlier for managers, when shareholders’ risk preference is intensified by stakeholder considerations, when managers receive lower risk-taking incentives from compensation, and when firms’ ownership is less concentrated. I also find that the increased risk-taking is in alignment with shareholder value maximization. This project has resulted in a working paper, which has been accepted for presentation at international academic conferences, including The 2025 International Risk Management Conference (IRMC) and The 2025 International Conference of the French Finance Association (AFFI).

15504921.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15504921.value: I will continue to circulate the working paper and seek comments through presentation at various conferences and workshops. After further polishing the paper, I will submit the paper to academic journals for publication.

15504921.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15504921.value: This project explores the implications of shareholders’ portfolio overlap for the risk-related agency problem. The baseline analysis suggests that managerial risk-taking increases with the degree of portfolio overlap among a firm’s institutional shareholders. An instrumental variable analysis supports a causal interpretation. Consistent with the hypothesis that shareholders’ portfolio overlap facilitates intervention in managers’ risk choices, the effect is more pronounced when risk-taking is personally costlier for managers, when shareholders’ risk preference is intensified by stakeholder considerations, when managers receive lower risk-taking incentives from compensation, and when firms’ ownership is less concentrated. Further analysis reveals that the increased risk-taking is in alignment with shareholder value maximization. Overall, this project highlights that portfolio overlap constitutes a governance mechanism through which shareholders can coordinate to counteract ownership dispersion and maintain effective oversight of managerial behavior. Importantly, the findings provide valuable guidance to policymakers regarding regulations on investor interaction and coordination.

15505221.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15505221.value: Structured equity products are investment products, issued by financial institutions, and their payoffs depend on the value of certain underlying equity or equity index. Structured equity products are traded around the world, and their popularity has been increasing over the years. It is documented in the literature that the structured equity products are overpriced relative to what the standard asset pricing models suggest. Although various explanations of the overpricing have been proposed in the literature, it is still not well understood why issuers are able to sell and investors are willing to buy the overpriced securities. This project proposes to understand the overpricing of the structured equity products in Hong Kong, an important market for the structured products. The data contain detailed information about the trading activities and positions of issuers from which the risk and profit of the structured products from the issuers' perspective can be examined. I study whether issuers make excessive profits and whether their profits compensate the risks they take. The analysis of the project helps better understand the overpricing of the structured products as well as the roles that the issuers play in the structured products markets. 結構性股票產品是金融機構發行的投資產品， 他們的收益取決於某些標的股票或股票指數的價值。 結構性股票產品在全球範圍內交易，其受歡迎程度逐年增加。研究表明結構性股票產品定價相對於標準資產定價模型過高。 儘管文獻中對定價過高提出了各種解釋，但仍未完全理解為什麼發行人能夠賣出而投資者願意買入定價過高的證券。該項目旨在了解香港，一個在全球重要的市場，其結構性股票產品價格過高的原因。數據包含有關交易活動的詳細信息和結構性產品發行商的頭寸，從而可以考察發行商的風險和利潤。我研究發行商是否賺取超額利潤和他們的利潤是否能補償他們承擔的風險。項目分析有助於更好地了解結構性產品定價過高以及發行商在結構性產品市場的作用。

15505221.label: Realisation of objectives
15505221.value: To achieve the first objective, we conduct the empirical analysis on the Hong Kong derivative warrants market from January 2008 to December 2022. We retrieve the data from the Hong Kong Stock Exchanges, including the daily closing bid and ask prices, trading volumes in shares and dollars, number of outstanding shares, and contract specifications, such as calls or puts, underlying asset, strike price and expiration date, of derivative warrants, and daily closing bid and ask prices of underlying assets, and dividends, as well as issuers' trading activities, such as daily buying and selling volumes, average buying and selling prices, for each issuer. We consider two profit measures, the unhedged profit and the hedged profit. The unhedged profit includes the profit from daily trading by issuers and the cost of settlement of derivative warrants at maturity. Hedged profit is unhedged profit minus the cost arising from delta hedging by trading the underlying asset. We assume that issuers delta hedge their derivative warrant positions by trading underlying assets at a daily frequency, and the underlying asset is bought at the closing ask price and sold at the closing bid price. We measure the risks of derivative warrants faced by issuers by the Black-Scholes gamma and vega. Gamma, the sensitivity of the derivative warrant delta to changes in the underlying asset price, measures the rebalancing risk of the derivative warrant. Vega, the sensitivity of the derivative warrant price to changes in the volatility of the underlying asset, measures the volatility risk of the derivative warrant. Both rebalancing risk and volatility risk are difficult to hedge by issuers, so we term these risks as unhedgeable risks. To achieve the second objective, we conduct regression analyses of profits and risks of derivative warrants in a pooled regression. We focus on the hedged profit because issuers do hedge so that the hedged profit measures the actual profit more closely. The demand-based option pricing theory suggests that the demand pressure from investors matters for derivatives pricing. We also include the demand pressure measure in the regression analyses, the relative open interest, defined as the number of shares of derivative warrants held by investors at the end of a trading day divided by the total number of shares of the derivative warrant issuance. We control for the possibility that the issuing size and maturity of derivative warrants may affect profits to issuers, and also include the issuers' fixed effects to account for unobserved factors related to issuers. According to the demand-based option pricing theory, when the amount of unhedgeable risk is higher, the pricing impact of investors' demand pressure is expected to be greater. We include the interaction terms between unchangeable risks and investors' demand in the regression to test this theory. We also test if the availability of additional hedging instruments, i.e., exchange-traded options, reduces the impacts of unhedgeable risks and investors' demand on the profits of derivative warrants. While our main analysis focuses on the cross-sectional relationship between profits and risks of derivative warrants, we also examine their time-series relationships. We aggregate the profit across warrants within each half year because newly issued warrants typically expire in 6 months. We examine the relationship between the aggregate hedged profit and market return and volatility, where the market portfolio is proxied by the Hang Seng index.

15505221.label: Major findings and research outcome
15505221.value: We find that issuers earn about 0.34 (0.19) million HKD unhedged (hedged) profit per derivative warrant issuance on average. The aggregate hedged profit across all derivative warrants in the sample period is 22.7 billion HKD. The hedged profit varies substantially in the cross section, indicating the significant risks involved in the issuance of derivative warrants. For about two-thirds of issuers, the average hedged profit is positive and statistically significant. The few issuers that make losses on average are small issuers. Both of the unhedgeable risk measures, gamma and vega, are positive because both call and put derivative warrants have convex payoff functions with respect to the underlying asset price. Both vega and gamma are positively skewed. From the pooled regression analysis, we find that for both call and put derivative warrants, vega, gamma, and investors' demand have strong and positive effects on issuers' profits. We also find that when investors' demand is high, unhedgeable risks have a stronger relationship with profits, and that the effects of unhedgeable risks and investors' demand are weaker when exchange-traded options on the same underlying asset as derivative warrants are available, consistent with the demand-based option pricing theory. From the time-series analysis, we find that the aggregate hedged profit varies substantially across time, and it tends to be higher when the market return is low and market volatility is high. The results indicate that issuers make more profits during the volatile period when the risks of hedging their inventory are high.

15505221.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15505221.value: Derivative warrants are not the only popular type of structured products traded in Hong Kong. The callable bull bear contracts are another type. It is interesting to examine whether the results found in this project hold for the callable bull bear contracts. This analysis not only serves as a robust check but also may yield new insights. First, the callable bull bear contracts have a knockout feature, which is absent from derivative warrants. This knockout feature may introduce additional risks to the issuers. Second, unhedgeable risks, such as gamma and vega, considered in this project, may not be important for the callable bull bear contracts, because these risk measures are close to zero for these contracts unless they are close to being knocked out. The analysis of the project focuses on the effects of issuers’ hedging of the structured products that appeal to individual investors. The investigation of the types of structured products with appealing features and not easily replicable by individual investors can also be important and interesting.

15505221.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15505221.value: Structured equity products are investment products issued by financial institutions and are traded around the world. Their popularity has been increasing over the years. Structured equity products are found to be overpriced with respect to traditional derivative pricing models. The overpricing is typically attributed to issuers' catering to investors' behavioral preferences or exploiting their informational disadvantages and irrationality. In this project, we offer a complementary view of the overpricing of structured products by examining the profits and risks of structured products from the issuers' perspective. We examine the derivative warrant market in Hong Kong. We find that profits earned by issuers are positive on average and they vary substantially in the cross section. We quantify unhedgeable risks faced by issuers and measure investors' demand, and show that the profits of derivative warrants are positively related to unhedgeable risks and investors' demand. The results in the project suggest that the profits earned by issuers from selling derivative warrants can be partially attributed to the compensation for their costs of hedging and bearing unhedgeable risk that cannot be alternatively mitigated. The results are generally consistent with the demand-based option pricing theory.

15505621.value: 消费者异质性和公平性偏好下的多渠道零售

15505621.label: Project Objectives
15505621.value: First, we start by solving the equilibrium pricing decisions of our base model via backward induction. Such analysis is helpful in revealing the fundamental effects brought by consumers' fairness concerns and how these effects interact in driving the firm's equilibrium pricing decisions. Second, building upon the equilibrium results captured above, we plan to investigate how both the strength of fairness aversion and the fraction of fair-minded consumers would affect the firm's pricing strategy, profit, and the corresponding consumer surplus. Such analysis aims to provide rich managerial insights on whether enlarging the fraction of fair-minded consumers or exhibiting stronger fairness concerns could lead to consistent channel prices and benefit the consumers by improving their surplus. Third, due to the wide-spread threat of COVID-19 pandemic, the attractiveness of physically visiting brick-and-mortar store is significantly hindered by the requirement of social-distancing, and consumers exhibit a trend that systematically favors online shopping. There are multiple ways to capture the aforementioned new trend by adjusting our base model. We would like to understand how this new shopping trend interacts with the consumers' fairness concerns, and affects the firm's selling strategy and the corresponding welfare implications. Fourth, the wide-spread threat of pandemic also imposes burdens on the offline channel and reshapes consumers' shopping habit to the more convenient online mode. However, in some region, like Hong Kong SAR, the current stage of development for the e-commerce may not be able to fully support the increased online shopping needs. As such, policy makers may provide initiatives to develop and promote e-commerce. Such initiatives include, but are not limited to, (1) helping brick-and-mortar store to build online channel; (2) enhancing a multi-channel firm's online operating efficiency, and (3) expanding the consumers' awareness and capability of online shopping. We would like to evaluate the effectiveness of those initiatives and their corresponding impacts on both the firm and the consumers.

15505621.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15505621.value: E-commence becomes booming all around the world in recent years. Online shopping provides consumers with convenience and flexibility in choosing their desired products from a wider range of sellers without time and geographical constraints. On the other hand, e-commence also provides sellers great opportunities to access to a larger pool of potential consumers. As such, sellers could further expand their business horizon beyond geographical limitations by selling their products both locally and through online channels. The recent wide-spread threat of pandemic COVID-19 further strengthens the attractiveness of online shopping, as the feasibility of offline shopping via visiting brick-and-mortar store is significantly hindered due to the social-distancing requirements. Such a new trend imposes significant challenges for the retail industry to struggle with the decline of shoppers and sales, but, at the same time, offers great opportunities and incentives for both firms and policy makers to develop, maintain, and enhance e-commence business. Operating multi-channel is appealing to firms, as it offers an opportunity of reaching additional customer segments. The rise of multi-channel retailing also brings new challenges, since the firm needs to carefully manage the product sold in both channels. Among others, a key decision faced by the firm is how to price the same items sold in different channels. In particular, whether to offer the same channel prices or not? The ease of access to price information compounds the complexity of this decision, as pricing transparency not only increases the price sensitivity of consumers, but may also induce their perceptions of fairness and inequity aversion from the discrepancy between online and offline prices. Multi-channel retailing firms, especially those higher-performing ones, have common concerns about the consumers demand for price consistency across channels. In practice, however, there is considerable heterogeneity in multi-channel firms’ pricing strategies. Different firms may have distinct pricing strategies in managing multi-channel retailing, especially when consumers exhibit heterogeneous fairness concerns regarding the inconsistent channel prices. Some firms may adopt uniform price in order to eliminate such negative concerns, whereas others may strategically adjust their channel prices so as to migrate the fair-minded consumers between channels. Motivated by these practices, we aim to investigate a multi-channel firm's optimal pricing strategy in the presence of consumers' heterogeneous fairness concerns, and uncover the fundamental effects on both the firm’s profitability and consumers’ surplus, with special focus given to an environment with booming e-commerce due to the wide-spread threat of pandemic. 近年来，电子商务在全球范围内蓬勃发展。网上购物, 因其不受时间和地域的限制, 为消费者提供了极大的便利性和灵活性。另一方面，电子商务也为卖家提供了接触更多潜在消费者的绝佳机会。因此，卖家可以通过在本地和在线渠道销售产品，从而超越地域的限制，扩大业务范围。 最近新冠疫情的大流行进一步增强了网上购物的吸引力。由于保持社交距离的要求，通过访问实体店进行线下购物的可行性受到严重阻碍。这种新趋势给零售业带来了重大挑战，但同时也为公司和政策制定者开展、维持和加强电子商务业务提供了巨大的机会和动力。 经营多渠道销售对公司很有吸引力，因为它提供了接触更多客户群的机会。多渠道零售的兴起也带来了新的挑战，因为公司需要谨慎地管理在两个渠道中销售的产品。其中，公司面临的一个关键决策是如何为不同渠道销售的相同商品定价，特别是不同渠道是否提供相同的价格？获取价格信息的便利性增加了这一决策的复杂性，因为定价信息的透明性不仅会增加消费者的价格敏感性，而且可能会导致他们对线上和线下不同价的公平性的担忧。 多渠道零售公司，尤其是那些业绩较好的零售公司，普遍担心消费者对跨渠道价格一致性的需求。然而，在实践中，多渠道公司的定价策略存在相当大的异质性。不同的公司在管理多渠道零售时可能有不同的定价策略，尤其是当消费者对不一致的渠道价格表现出不同程度的公平性担忧。一些企业可能会采用统一价格来消除这种负面担忧，而另一些企业可能会战略性地调整他们的渠道价格，以便在渠道之间转移那些对定价公平性有顾虑的消费者。 在这些实践的推动下，我们的目标是研究多渠道公司在存在消费者异质性和公平性偏好下的最优定价策略，并揭示其对公司盈利能力和消费者剩余的影响。

15505821.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15505821.value: 總體市場分歧和企業投資：國際證據

15505821.label: Project Objectives
15505821.value: To examine how aggregate analysts’ forecast disagreement affects corporate investments in the U.S. To investigate whether country-level institution factors affect the association between aggregate analysts’ forecast disagreement and corporate investments in an international setting.
rows: To examine how aggregate analysts’ forecast disagreement affects corporate investments in the U.S.
To investigate whether country-level institution factors affect the association between aggregate analysts’ forecast disagreement and corporate investments in an international setting.

15505821.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15505821.value: The objective of this proposal is to investigate how aggregate analysts’ long-term earnings growth forecast dispersion affects corporate investments in an international setting. There are two approaches to measure aggregate market disagreement based on analysts’ earnings forecasts. The top-down approach suggested by Park (2005) uses analysts’ forecast dispersion of Standard & Poor’s (S&P) 500 index annual earnings. The bottom-up approach of Yu (2011) uses the value-weighted average of individual-stock analyst earnings forecast dispersions. Yu (2011) finds that aggregate market disagreement based on analysts’ long-run earnings growth forecasts significantly and negatively predicts future market returns from one- to three-year horizons, while the return predictive power of the top-down measure of Park (2005) is much weaker. We therefore follow Yu (2011) to use the bottom-up approach to measure aggregate market disagreement and hypothesize that this measure of aggregate disagreement negatively affects future corporate investments. One may argue that this measure of aggregate disagreement might be correlated with some existing economic uncertainty measures. However, our preliminary result indicates that this aggregate market disagreement measure dominates and in some cases subsumes the existing economic uncertainty measures in predicting future GDP growth in the U.S. Macroeconomists and policy makers have devoted a great effort to forecast economic activities, such as GDP growth and unemployment. Most macro forecasters seldom use rich information imbedded in the reports of individual-stock analysts, who are highly paid sophisticated market participants. This proposal represents one of these under-explored channels that use the valuable information imbedded in individual-stock analyst forecasts to predict corporate investments. Moreover, compared to existing measures of economic uncertainty which sometimes involves labor intensive analysis of voluminous media news articles, this measure is simple and easy to implement and it can be easily and readily extended to the international setting. The potential contribution from the expected result of this project is to document that this novel measure of aggregate disagreement is an incrementally significant leading indicator of corporate investments. Macroeconomists and policy makers can also incorporate this aggregate disagreement measure to improve their forecast accuracy of economic activities not only in the U.S. but also in other countries or regions. 本提案的目的是調查總體分析師的長期盈利增長預測離散度如何影響國際環境中的企業投資。有兩種方法可以根據分析師的盈利預測來衡量總體市場分歧。 Park (2005) 建議的自上而下的方法使用分析師對標準普爾 (S&P) 500 指數年收益的預測離差。 Yu (2011) 的自下而上方法使用了個股分析師盈利預測離差的價值加權平均值。 Yu (2011) 發現基於分析師的長期盈利增長預測的總體市場分歧顯著且負面地預測了未來一到三年的市場回報，而 Park (2005) 自上而下的衡量指標的回報預測能力)要弱得多。因此，我們遵循 Yu (2011) 使用自下而上的方法來衡量總體市場分歧，並假設這種總體分歧的衡量對未來的公司投資產生負面影響。 有人可能會爭辯說，這種總體分歧的衡量標準可能與一些現有的經濟不確定性衡量標準有關。然而，我們的初步結果表明，在預測美國未來 GDP 增長時，這種總體市場分歧衡量指標占主導地位，並且在某些情況下包含了現有的經濟不確定性衡量指標。 宏觀經濟學家和政策制定者投入了大量精力來預測經濟活動，例如 GDP 增長和失業率。大多數宏觀預測者很少使用個人股票分析師報告中嵌入的豐富信息，他們是高薪老練的市場參與者。該提案代表了這些未充分探索的渠道之一，這些渠道使用嵌入在個股分析師預測中的寶貴信息來預測企業投資。此外，與有時需要對大量媒體新聞文章進行勞動密集型分析的現有經濟不確定性措施相比，該措施簡單易行，並且可以輕鬆、輕鬆地擴展到國際環境。 該項目預期結果的潛在貢獻是證明這種衡量總體分歧的新方法是企業投資的一個漸進重要的領先指標。宏觀經濟學家和政策制定者也可以納入這種總體分歧衡量標準，以提高他們對美國和其他國家或地區經濟活動的預測準確性。

15505821.label: Realisation of objectives
15505821.value: The major objectives of this project are (i) to examine aggregate analysts’ forecast disagreement affects corporate investments in the U.S.; and (ii) to extend the study to an international setting and to examine whether institution factors affect the effect of aggregate disagreement on corporate investment. Our results in general have clearly achieved the objectives of the proposal. First, we find that disagreement negatively predicts future corporate investment in the U.S. market, but positively predicts corporate investment in the global markets outside the U.S. Second, we attribute this asymmetry to the uncertainty and optimism channels that are associated with disagreement. The increase in disagreement is related to uncertainty and future economic downturns in the U.S. market, while it captures the optimism effects in the international market due to the limits to arbitrage. The positive effect in the international market is linked to the overall market optimism and inflated price signals in the international markets. We find that international market disagreement contains positive information on firm’s future earnings. The positive effect internationally is attenuated by greater market openness and amplified when market valuation is high. This paper has been presented at Birmingham University, Fudan University, Tongji University, the 2023 Conference on Pacific Basin Finance, Economics, Accounting, and Management (PBFEAM) and the 2023 Asian Financial Association Annual Conference. After writing polish, it is ready for submission to a top-tier finance journal. It is clearly that we have achieved both objective of the project. I have also completed another paper directly related to this GRF project, which examines the effect of aggregate market disagreement on the macroeconomy in the global markets and explore the role of the United States. We show that US aggregate disagreement is a strong predictor of macroeconomic conditions. In non-US global markets, increases in US aggregate disagreement are associated with long-lasting declines in economic activities, whereas non-US aggregate disagreement does not have predictability. Furthermore, US aggregate disagreement significantly predicts future stock market returns negatively in the US and non-US markets, whereas non-US aggregate disagreement displays limited predictability. This paper has been presented at Birmingham University, Fudan University, and Tongji University, Xiamen University, the 2024 Great Bay Area Finance Workshop, the 2023 Conference on Pacific Basin Finance, Economics, Accounting, and Management (PBFEAM) and the 2023 Asian Financial Association Annual Conference. The paper is currently under review at Review of Financial Studies. Furthermore, I have also completed a paper partially related to this GRF project, which is associated with corporate external financing used to support corporate investment. Corporate investment is funded by either internally generated cash flow or by externally financing. External financing can be either equity or debt. Debt can be corporate bonds or bank loans. In this paper, we focus on bank loans. In particular, we investigate the impact of firm-level political risk on loan contracting. We find that firm-level political risk is positively associated with bank loan cost and that this effect is stronger for firms experiencing increased operation uncertainty and higher default risks. Firm-level political risk also tightens non-pricing loan terms by increasing the likelihood of collateral requirements and covenant restrictions. This paper has been published in Contemporary Accounting Research (2024). Overall, the outcomes of the project have clearly demonstrated that the project objectives have been successfully achieved.

15505821.label: Major findings and research outcome
15505821.value: Our major findings are as follows: (1) Disagreement negatively predicts corporate investment in the U.S. market, but positively in ex-US global markets. We attribute this asymmetry to the uncertainty and optimism channels associated with disagreement. Increases in disagreement are related to uncertainty and future economic downturns in the U.S. market, while it captures the optimism effect in international markets due to limits to arbitrage. The positive effect in international markets is related to general market optimism and inflated price signals. International market disagreement contains positive information on firm’s future earnings and the positive effect is attenuated by greater market openness and amplified when market valuation is high. (2) Using Yu’s (2011) bottom-up approach, we show that US aggregate disagreement is a strong predictor of macroeconomic conditions. In non-US global markets, increases in US aggregate disagreement are associated with long-lasting declines in economic activities, whereas non-US aggregate disagreement does not have predictability. Furthermore, US aggregate disagreement significantly predicts future stock market returns negatively in the US and non-US markets, whereas non-US aggregate disagreement displays limited predictability. The results highlight a leading role of US aggregate disagreement in the global economy and financial markets. (3) We investigate the impact of firm-level political risk on loan contracting. Firm-level political risk is positively associated with bank loan cost and that this effect is stronger for firms experiencing increased operation uncertainty and higher default risks. Firm-level political risk also tightens non-pricing loan terms by increasing the likelihood of collateral requirements and covenant restrictions. We further find that political connections and relationship-based borrowing can attenuate the adverse effect of firm-level political risk on loan contracting. The above major findings are detailed in the following three papers (updated): 1. Te-Feng Chen, Nanqi Li, and K. C. John Wei,* 2025, “Aggregate market disagreement and corporate investment: U.S. and international evidence,” ready for submission to Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis. 2. Te-Feng Chen, Nanqi Li, and K.C. John Wei,* 2025, Aggregate market disagreement and the macroeconomy in the global markets: The role of the United States, under review at Review of Financial Studies. 3. Walid Saffar, Yang Wang,* and K.C. John Wei, 2024, Firm-level political risk and bank loan contracting, Contemporary Accounting Research 41, 1577-1607.

15505821.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15505821.value: We find that local market disagreement, based on dispersion in analyst forecasts of a firm long-term earnings growth rates, predicts firm-level corporate investment negatively in the U.S. market but positively in non-US global markets. Moreover, US market disagreement predicts country-level macroeconomic activities not only for the US but also for non-US global markets. In contrary, local non-US market disagreement does not predict their own macroeconomic outcomes, highlighting the leading role of US aggregate market disagreement in the global economy and financial markets. We also find that our measure of market disagreement is different from conventional measures of economic uncertainty such as economic policy uncertainty (EPU) or financial market uncertainty. We find that market disagreement has a long-lasting effect while economic or financial uncertainty has a relatively short-term effect on macroeconomic activities. The potential for further development of the research centers on whether this market disagreement is a pricing factor in the context of asset pricing. This is an important and interesting research topic that deserves a comprehensive examination in a future study.

15505821.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15505821.value: Since market disagreement is different from conventional measures of economic or financial market uncertainty, in this study we comprehensively examine whether aggregate market disagreement affects firm-level corporate investment and country-level macroeconomic outcomes. Moreover, we also examine the role of US market disagreement on country-level macroeconomic activities in the global market setting. We find that local market disagreement strongly predicts firm-level corporate investment negatively in the U.S. market but positively in non-US global markets. Moreover, US market disagreement predicts country-level macroeconomic outcomes negatively not only for the US but also for non-US global markets. Our findings can inform corporate managers about the important role of market disagreement on their investment decisions and policy makers about their economic outcomes.

15506721.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15506721.value: 在低利率環境下調整後的稅息折舊及攤銷前利潤的相關性

15506721.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15506721.value: The paper proposes to examine how stock prices are associated with adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) reported in firms' earnings announcements. Adjusted EBITDA is a supplementary measure not prepared under Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP), or a non-GAAP measure. In the post-crisis time period, interest rates in the U.S. decrease and the credit market has been booming. Many firms rely heavily on debt financing and incur a large amount of interest expense. At the same time, many managers start to voluntarily exclude interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (ITDA) expenses, along with other more discretionary items (usually expenses) from GAAP earnings, to arrive at adjusted EBITDA as a profitability measure for equity investors. Managers claim that non-GAAP measures better convey operating performance because they are not affected by nonrecurring and noncore events outside management's control. However, ITDA expenses are not only recurring but also large in magnitude in the low interest environment. Among all types of non-GAAP measures, adjusted EBITDA is usually the most favourable due to the large number of excluded items from GAAP earnings. Although prior literature finds that equity investors prefer adjusted earnings (a metric resulting from excluding some items but not ITDA expenses from GAAP earnings) over GAAP earnings in valuing stocks, it is unclear whether adjusted EBITDA that excludes unambiguously recurring and large expenses is also used or even preferred by equity investors over other non-GAAP measures and GAAP earnings. Also, there are signals indicating the quality and usefulness of adjusted EBITDA that can affect how equity investors use adjusted EBITDA to value stocks. I use whether firms also disclose adjusted earnings alongside adjusted EBITDA, whether adjusted EBITDA minus ITDA expenses is negative but firms do not report adjusted earnings, and whether analysts make EBITDA forecasts as signals of the quality of adjusted EBITDA. I use whether adjusted EBITDA in earnings announcements for equity investors is identically defined as adjusted EBITDA in debt covenants as a signal of the usefulness of the metric. I will examine the value relevance (the association between stock returns and financial measures) of adjusted EBITDA relative to other earnings metrics, and I expect the value relevance of adjusted EBITDA to vary with the quality and usefulness of the metric. 本篇文章提議研究公司在業績公告中提供的Adjusted EBITDA(調整後的稅息折舊及攤銷前利潤)與股價的關系。Adjusted EBITDA不是按照通用會計準則準備的財務指標，即非通用會計準則指標(non-GAAP measure)。在金融危機以後，美國匯率降至歷史新低，信用市場蓬勃發展，很多公司主要依靠債務獲得融資，進而造成高額的利息費用。與此同時，很多公司開始刨除利息費用，稅費，折舊攤銷費用以及其他公司個別的費用來得到adjusted EBITDA這個指標提供給投資者。經理人聲稱非通用會計準則指標能更好的反應不受非常規事件和非核心業務影響的經營情況。但是稅息折舊及攤銷費用是常規費用，而且在低利率環境下這些費用金額很大。在眾多非通用會計準則指標裏，adjusted EBITDA剔除了最大額度的費用，因此成為對公司最友好的指標。盡管之前文獻有發現，相比在通用會計準則下準備的利潤，公司股價與經公司調整後的利潤(adjusted earnings)更相關，股價與adjusted EBITDA的關系是沒有被研究過的。Adjusted EBITDA還有一些屬性是可以影響到投資者如何看待這個指標，比如公司是否同時也披露adjusted earnings,如果adjusted EBITDA不剔除稅息折舊及攤銷費用就是負值，但是公司並不披露adjusted earnings,財務分析師是否提供EBITDA的預測，業績公告中的adjusted EBITDA和債務契約中的adjusted EBITDA的定義是否一致。文章將檢驗股價與adjusted EBITDA之間的關系，以及這些屬性如何進一步影響這個關系。

15507221.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15507221.value: 智能機器時代：製造企業真的能通過人工智能投資提升運營效率嗎？

15507221.label: Project Objectives
15507221.value: By matching the recruitment information on AI talent in Burning Glass Technologies with Compustat's financial data and using the Dynamic Panel Data (DPD) models, we will examine longitudinally the impact of AI investment on operational efficiency in the US manufacturing industry. Applying the Generalized Method of Moments (GMM) techniques, we will further investigate how such an impact could potentially be moderated, or strengthened, by different contextual factors, including firms' operational complexity, technology stock, and industry dynamism. We seek to provide useful insights about the contextual factors that make the AI capability of firms a more crucial asset, and develop valuable guidelines for management scholars, industrial practitioner and policy-makers to make the best use of AI in the intelligent machines era.

15507421.label: Project Objectives
15507421.value: As the importance and vulnerability of supply chains increase, the impact that supply chain contracts have on firms' financial outcomes grows. Understanding how the characteristics of supply chain contracts affect business, client, and audit risk is an essential area of the audit, particularly with the implementation of ASC Section 606, which places additional burdens of contract examination on auditors. Prior studies (e.g., Pratt and Stice 1994) document that client characteristics impact audit firm decisions. For example, audit clients’ financial position, growth orientation, industry, and strategic business decisions affect client acceptance decisions, risk assessment, and fee schedules (Pratt and Stice 1994). However, one area that has not been examined in prior literature is the effect that clients’ supply chain contract characteristics have on auditor’s decisions and the corresponding impacts on audit outcomes. Supply chain contracting has grown in economic importance over the past several decades. Recent findings suggest that approximately 35 percent of Big N auditor clients report having major customer/supplier relationships (Hertzel, Li, Officer, and Rodgers 2008). The characteristics of supply chain contracts are generally unknown for commercial contracts, creating a black box regarding supply chain contracts and audit outcomes. Given the importance of supply chain relationships to the macro economy and to firms that have significant supply chain exposures, supply chain contracts are likely to have an important and significant impact on audits. How the unique risks that supply chain contract characteristics expose audit clients to affects the decision-making of their auditors is a black box. While much research exists in supply chains and on audit, business, and litigation risk for auditors, very few studies examine the relationship between supply chains and auditors. Further, no studies of which I am aware investigate the impact of contract characteristics on audit decisions, although supply chain contracts are economically important and subject to substantially risks, as evidenced by the attention devoted to supply chain risks in firms’ Item 1A disclosures. Thus, this study provides an opportunity to investigate both the impact of supply chain choices on audits and the effect of contract characteristics on audit outcomes. Supply chain contract characteristics may expose auditors and their clients to risk associated with contract characteristics; however, these associations are difficult to study because of data availability. While a small number of studies examine the effect of auditors on supplier-customer relationships (e.g., Dhaliwal et al. 2017), no studies investigate how supplier-customer contract characteristics impact clients’ audit decisions, although supplier-customer relationships have grown in economic importance over the last several decades (Li et al. 2006). Johnstone et al. (2014) investigates how knowledge of the supply chain revenue cycle helps auditors make more informed judgements about risk, but they do not examine how supply chain contract characteristics impact auditors' decisions related to the engagement. Contract and enforcement complexity, combined with additional audit requirements may increase audit risk. The financial risk that clients are exposed to through their supply chains may impact client business risk, and financial risk is expected to vary according to contract characteristics, political associations of the client, and client characteristics. Additionally, the existence of litigation for breach of contract may increase auditors’ litigation risk if auditors fail to detect reporting misconduct that culminates in their clients’ breaching their supply chain contracts. Finally, audit outcomes may be influenced by the economic importance of supply chain relationships to audit clients, the contract type, presence of contract enforcement clauses, contract length, owner characteristics, and political associations of the client firm. Contract complexity, specialized litigation, and potential contract termination are some of the unique risks that clients with supply chain risks are exposed to and may result in differences in audit effort, audit fees, propensity to issue a going concern opinion, and incidence of material weaknesses over internal control. Currently, how supply chain contract risks impact auditors is a black box because the contracts for most supply chain relationships are not publicly available. Therefore, I proposed to study the impact of supply chain contract characteristics on audit decisions and audit outcomes in the context of government contractors where detailed information is available relating to contract type, contract enforcement clauses, contract financing, contract length, business owner characteristics, political associations, and officer compensation. Ultimately, I expect my analysis to reveal how supply chain contract characteristics are associated with auditors’ decisions and audit outcomes. This study will also provide important insights for auditors, boards of directors, audit committees, and regulators. Auditors, newly exposed to greater audit risk as a result of ACS Section 606, need to understand how contract terms are associated with litigation and client business risk. This study helps boards of directors understand the business risks of their supply chain contracts and how those risks relate to audit outcomes. Finally, this study can aid regulators who are assessing new contract accounting regulations.

15507421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15507421.value: This study plans to investigate the impact of audit client supply chain contract characteristics on audit outcomes. Item 1A frequently contains risks associated with supply chains, including the risk of cyber-attack at a customer, manufacturing defects, customers’ financial condition, and dependence on a single customer. How supply chain risks impact audit outcomes is a black box because contract details for commercial supply chains are not publicly available. This is not the case for US government contractors. For government contractors, detailed public information relates to contract characteristics. Therefore, government contractors provide a useful context to study the impact of supply chain contract characteristics on audit outcomes. Because government contractors navigate complex bureaucracies and stringent accounting guidelines, they represent an institutionally interesting context in which to study the impact of supply chain contract characteristics on audit outcomes. Further, government contractors and their auditors are also subject to litigation and reputational risk associated with fraud in the government setting, similar to commercial supply chain relationships. Finally, auditors of government contracts are subject to requirements for continuing professional education training, governmental accounting standards, and peer reviews, so the quality of auditing is expected to be high. The government supply chain context is also economically important. In 2019, actual US government spending was $4.45 trillion, or 21 percent of US gross domestic product. Therefore, the US government is an essential market for the products and services of US firms, making it not only an interesting context to study the impact of supply chain contract characteristics on audit outcomes, but also one of the largest supply chain settings in the US. First, I propose to investigate how supply chain contract characteristics influence auditors’ decisions surrounding risk assessment, audit effort, and client acceptance by using the Federal Procurement Data System which contains detailed information on government contracts above $25,000. Additionally, I will investigate how different contract characteristics are associated with litigation risk for auditors by using a novel dataset of specialized government contracting lawsuits initiated by whistleblowers. Second, I intend to study how supply chain contract characteristics affect audit outcomes for audit clients who have contracts with the US government. It is known that risks associated with clients’ supply chains affect audit outcomes (Johnstone et al. 2014).
