15601621.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15601621.value: In Hong Kong, 7% of adolescents are diagnosed with anxiety disorders and one in every four secondary school students reports clinical-level anxiety symptoms. However, the vast majority (65%) of them do not access services. Long waitlists in public services, the high cost of private services, or the fear of being stigmatised in school can hinder access to services. The high prevalence of anxiety and low intervention uptake indicate that there is a need to develop timely, scalable, and potent interventions suitable for adolescents. Growth mindset single-session interventions (SSIs) have the potential to be scalable intervention for diagnosable or subclinical psychopathology in adolescents. The key mechanism of effective SSIs is to provide precise intervention on the key aspect to trigger sudden gains and symptom reduction. The PI’s Early Career Scheme project (2019-2020) found fixed mindset of negative emotion more closely related to anxiety than was fixed mindset of personality. The findings provide strong support that intervention targeted on fixed mindset of negative emotion can be a more precise intervention for adolescent anxiety than the existing SSI on growth mindset of personality (SSI-GP). The proposed study is to develop Single-session Intervention of Growth Mindset for Anxiety (SIGMA) to teach adolescents that negative emotions can change and to compare its effectiveness in reducing anxiety to SSI-GP and an active control group with a three-arm randomised control trial. Adolescents (N=549, ages 12-16) from secondary schools will be randomised to one of three intervention conditions: the SIGMA, SSI-GP, or active control. All programs are approximately 40 minutes in length and self-administered by youth. Adolescents will be assessed for their anxiety symptoms (primary outcome), perceived control, hopelessness, and attitude towards help-seeking at pre-intervention, and 2-week and 8-week follow-up. A pilot test has confirmed the feasibility and acceptability of SIGMA among adolescents. We hypothesised that SIGMA and SSI-GP will result in larger reduction in anxiety symptoms than the control intervention at the end of treatment and follow-up period. We also predict SIGMA will have a greater effect than SSI-GP. Intention-to-treat principle and linear regression-based maximum likelihood multi-level models will be used for data analysis. The project brings together experts in mindset research, local social work, web-based intervention, statistics, youth mental health studies, and psychiatry. This study will not only provide evidence on what matters in growth mindset interventions for adolescent anxiety, but also serve as a scalable and accessible intervention to improve the well-being of young people. 香港有7% 的青少年被診斷出患有焦慮癥，四分之一的中學生報告有焦慮癥狀。然而，他們之中絕大多數 (65%) 無獲得服務。公共醫療服務輪候時間長，私人輔導服務成本高，學生害怕在學校受到歧視，這些因素都會阻礙受焦慮困擾的青少年獲得服務。焦慮的高发率和低干預率表明很有必要制定適合青少年的及時、有效的和可以被廣泛推廣的干預措施。 成長心態單次干預 (SSI) 時間短，有可能成為可以廣泛推廣的干預措施，幫週有已診斷或亞臨床精神病理學的青少年。有效單次干預的關鍵機制是提供精準干預，以產生即使的效果，使癥狀減輕。 本研究的主要研究者在其ECS 項目（2019-2021）中發現，发現消極情緒的定型心態與焦慮的關系比人格的定型心態更密切。該研究結果為改良現有的成長心態單次干預提供了強有力的支持，即針對消極情緒固定心態的干預可能比現有的人格成長心態 SSI (SSI-GP) 更精確地干預青少年焦慮。本研究計劃是建立焦慮相關成長心態單次干預 (SIGMA) 以教導青少年負面情緒可以改變，並用三組隨機對照組研究，比較其與 SSI-GP和支持療法在減少焦慮方面的效過。 研究將邀請來549名中學生（12-16 歲），隨機隨機分配到三種干預條件之一：SIGMA、SSI-GP 或支持療法。所有干預的長度約為 40 分鐘，由青少年在輔助下自行操作此網絡干預計劃的其中一個方案。研究員將在干預前以及 2 周和 8 周的隨訪中評估青少年的焦慮癥狀（主要結果）、感知控制、絕望和對尋求幫助的態度，預實驗測試證實 SIGMA 在青少年中的可行性和可接受性。我們假設 SIGMA 和 SSI-GP 在治療結束和隨訪期間比對照干預更能減少焦慮癥狀。我們還預測 SIGMA 將比 SSI-GP 產生更大的影響。將采用意向性治療原則和基於線性回歸的最大擬合多層模型進行數據分析。

15601621.label: Realisation of objectives
15601621.value: To realise the objectives, the first step was to develop SIGMA and adapted SSIGP from an existing growth mindset intervention and an active control group, the support therapy. We collected feedback from social workers and counsellors based on the principle of patient and public involvement (PPI). We also used co-production design and invited the targeted populations to provide feedback and suggestions. As the users can opt out of the intervention at any time, the content should be very relevant to engage the participants. Thus, we formed a youth advisory group to ensure the content was relevant to the targeted users and that our design of SSIs was engaging and appropriate to the targeted participants. Moreover, we invited a professional design team, including an artist (painter), a designer, and a digital designer, to design the videos. We designed cartoon and animation videos for the intervention. The cartoon heroine ('Hong Dou', the Red Bean) and her friends were designed by artists and digital designers to make the animations and videos captivating. Thus, the intervention videos can catch the attention of participants. Lastly, the online web-based intervention should be interactive for active participation. We embedded the intervention in the Qualtrics survey tool and inserted some interactive exercises after each session. This design not only helped maintain attention but also provided timely review or feedback for participants. The feedback collected supported that the SSIs in our study suit the adolescents' needs and expectations for mental health care. The successful development of the interventions facilitated the later realization of the objectives of the study. Second, we implement the randomised controlled trial of single-session interventions with careful and rigorous methods. First, we expanded the three-arm and included a subgroup by providing booster reminders of SIGMA. When we collected feedback from the teachers and social workers, they suggested that boosters may help strengthen the effectiveness of brief interventions. So we designed booster reminders for SIGMA and examined if boosters of reminding intervention core messages would strengthen the effectiveness. This is different from the original proposal and the protocol published which proposed to use a three-arm intervention. Instead, we proposed this four-arm randomised controlled trial (RCT) to provide evidence on the effectiveness of SIMGA (including SIGMA and SIGMA-BOOSTER) and compared it against the existing growth mindset intervention (SSI-GP) and the support theory as active control. The four-arm RCT does not violate the original design but adds a more valuable comparison to the three-arm RCT with the additional institutional support. Following PPI and with the help of a co-production team and a professional design team, the interventions are well-developed and the research design included one more arm with boosters to enrich the design. Third, we invited seven schools to participate in the study. They cover schools from Hong Kong Island, Kowloon and New Territory and include schools with English, Chinese, and mixed English and Chinese as a teaching medium. We originally planned to recruit participants from Form 2 to 3 (Grades 8 to 9). As one school does not have four classes from Grades 8-9, one class from grade 10 and 11 were invited. Thus, some of the participants exceed the age of 16. We recruited one more school than the protocol planned to make sure we could recruit enough participants. Four classes in the same selected grade(s) of each school were randomly selected to join the study. Then the four selected classes were randomised to the SIGMA condition, SIGMA-BOOSTER condition, SSI-GP condition, and the active control condition by random numbers. All students in those classes were invited to participate, and final participation depended on parental consent and students’ assent. A final sample size of 584 (146 per arm) was required. With reference to the attrition rate of our previous studies in a school setting (less than 20%), there is a requirement to recruit 732 participants at the baseline (183 per arm). We finally recruited 731 participants. As the number of participants in each class was different, the final recruited numbers of participants in the four arms were different. Generally, we followed the requirements of a randomised controlled trial study and recruited enough participants to test the hypothesis. Specifically, we hypothesized that SIGMA (including SIGMA and SIGMA-BOOSTER) and SSI-GP are more effective than active control using support therapy (ST) in the primary outcome of (i) reducing general anxiety symptoms, and secondary outcomes of (ii) reducing depressive symptoms, (iii) reducing suicidal/self-hurting thoughts, (iv) reducing hopelessness, (v) enhancing perceived control, (vi) increasing positive attitude to help-seeking, and (vii) enhancing psychological well-being. We also further examined the moderation effect of motivation level, baseline anxiety level and fixed mindset at baseline. We also collected the semi-structured feedback. We successfully tested all the hypotheses. Regarding the primary outcomes, we found a significant main effect of time (P <.001) but an insignificant main effect of group (P = .88) and group-by-time interaction (P = .54). Participants of four intervention groups all recorded a significant improvement of anxiety symptoms in the two-week and eight-week follow-ups. The improvement was sustained at the eight-week follow-up and no significant differences were observed between the two- and eight-week follow-ups. When comparing the changes from baseline to follow-ups between each pair of groups, the SSIGP intervention seemed to be more effective than SIGMA (including SIGMA and SIGMA-Booster) in reducing general anxiety symptoms, though the effect sizes ranged from very small to small. For the secondary outcomes, all the main effects of time were also significant and the main effects of group and interaction effects of group and time were all insignificant as for the primary outcome. The sensitivity analysis conducted for the per-protocol population showed similar results as for the intention-to-treat population. We conducted moderation analyses based on the baseline anxiety (high/low), motivation to change (high/low), and mindset (growth mindset v.s. fixed mindset) respectively. It signified that baseline anxiety level and mindset had moderating effects for all outcome measures, and motivation level had moderating effects for all outcome measures except suicidal/self-hurting thoughts. Participants with higher baseline anxiety, higher motivation to change their situation, and higher baseline fixed mindset showed more improvement on the outcome measures. In terms of intervention feedback, around 70% of participants indicated that they understood and agreed with the intervention content. Around 60% found the intervention helpful and interesting, indicated they like this course, and would recommend it to others. 60% of the users indicated increased confidence in their ability to cope with emotions after taking the intervention. Meanwhi le, very few found this course to be burdensome (3.8%) and interfering (9.6%). Around 60% indicated they accept or highly accept the intervention. The design of the interventions and the implementation of the randomised controlled trial of single-session interventions provided valuable experiences and implications for local practice. Also, the test of the hypotheses and the feedback of the interventions help fully understand the feasibility, the acceptability and the efficacy of the interventions and the efficacy of booster messages. Giving punchy and convincing core messages is most important to ensure the potential efficacy of single-session intervention. More efforts and explorations are needed to promote this potentially effective and scalable intervention to address the increasing mental health needs.

15601621.label: Major findings and research outcome
15601621.value: This report outlines the achievements and findings of our pioneering study on single-session web-based interventions for youth anxiety in Hong Kong. Our research enhanced transparency and provided a foundation for future studies in this field. Research Protocol and Intervention Development The research team published the study protocol to promote transparency and share our developmental process, design, and implementation strategies with peer scholars. This protocol serves as a valuable resource for researchers interested in building upon our experiences. For detailed information, please refer to Part C: Research Output, Item 1. Randomized Controlled Trial (RCT) Findings Our four-armed RCT involved 731 adolescents from seven secondary schools. The intent-to-treat analysis revealed a significant reduction in anxiety symptoms across all groups at both two-week and eight-week follow-ups. The mean and 95% confidence intervals (CI) for anxiety scores at baseline were as follows: SIGMA-Booster: 6.8 [6.0, 7.6], SIGMA: 6.5 [5.8, 7.3], SSIGP: 7.0 [6.2, 7.7], and ST: 6.9 [6.1, 7.7]. At the two-week follow-up, the scores decreased to: SIGMA-Booster: 5.9 [5.1, 6.7], SIGMA: 5.7 [4.9, 6.5], SSIGP: 5.4 [4.6, 6.2], and ST: 5.7 [4.9, 6.4]. At the eight-week follow-up, the scores were: SIGMA-Booster: 5.9 [5.1, 6.7], SIGMA: 5.3 [4.5, 6.0], SSIGP: 5.6 [4.8, 6.4], and ST: 5.8 [5.1, 6.6]. Moderation analysis indicated that participants with higher motivation for change, higher baseline anxiety scores, and fixed mindsets experienced greater improvements in anxiety symptoms. Over 70% of participants reported positive feedback regarding the feasibility and acceptability of the single-session interventions (SSIs). These results have been submitted to a medical internet journal for review (see Research Output, Item 3). Expansion and Future Directions Building on our initial findings, we expanded the study to another study with the institutional support. We adapted the SIGMA intervention for university students, the U-SIGMA intervention. We have applied for additional research funding to evaluate its efficacy in promoting mental health among university students in the Greater Bay Area. The protocol for this expanded study has also been published to ensure research transparency (see Research Output, Item 2).

15601621.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15601621.value: The current study highlights several avenues for further development and research. Firstly, while this study focused on a community sample, future research could explore the effectiveness of these interventions on clinical samples, potentially serving as a motivational tuning intervention for treatment. Secondly, to strengthen the findings, a larger-scale randomized controlled trial in a natural setting is underway, in collaboration with a local NGO. This will provide more robust data on the intervention's effectiveness. Thirdly, the finding that additional booster sessions did not enhance outcomes suggests that the initial intervention's content must be impactful and persuasive. This insight emphasizes the importance of delivering strong, convincing information during the sessions. Fourthly, incorporating a waitlist control group in future studies could offer a clearer understanding of the intervention's effects by providing a comparison between those who receive the intervention immediately and those who receive it later. Lastly, adaptations of the intervention can be made for different participant groups. The research team has already adapted and applied the SIGMA intervention to university students, using a waitlist control randomized controlled trial to examine its effectiveness. These steps will help refine the intervention and expand its applicability in various settings.

15601621.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15601621.value: This project explored scalable ways to help teenagers manage anxiety, a common mental health issue that many do not seek help for. The project researchers developed and tested four different short, online interventions aimed at improving how young people cope with anxiety. These sessions were based on the idea that changing how we think about our emotions can lead to better mental health. The study involved 731 students from seven schools, who were randomly assigned to one of the four sessions. Each session lasted about 45 minutes and was conducted online. The students' anxiety levels were measured before the session, and again two and eight weeks later. The results showed that all four interventions helped reduce anxiety and depression symptoms over the eight weeks. Students who were more motivated to change and had higher anxiety levels at the start showed the most improvement. More than 70% of the participants found the sessions helpful and easy to use. In summary, this research suggests that short, online interventions can be an effective, affordable, and less stigmatizing way to support adolescent mental health in schools. These interventions could be a valuable addition to existing school-based programs.

15602321.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15602321.value: 「紅色」基督教信仰交匯1950年代中國──以惠利特‧約翰遜為例

15602321.label: Project Objectives
15602321.value: to ascertain, by homing in on the writings of the “Red” Dean of Canterbury Hewlett Johnson (1874–1966), the premises of Christian sympathy for communism and the Communist-led People's Republic of China in the 1950s. This project answers why some Christians not only tolerated communism—which most people understood as an atheistic ideology—but also celebrated its ascendancy in China. to critically evaluate Johnson’s vision of China, the Eastern bloc and communism as representative of one notable strand of leftist thought in not just the West but across the globe during the 1950s in light of a decolonizing world. to concretize, by assessing Johnson's writings and public statements, how a radical critique of capitalism and Western imperialism coalesced in Britain around themes such as anticolonialism, Third World nationalism and social uplift brought about by socialist states such as the People's Republic of China. to situate the radical critique described above within the context of the global 1950s whereby Britain—like its counterparts across the European continent, the United States and Japan—was dislodging its empires, when former colonial subjects assumed or fought vigorously for agency as nation-state builders, and when the capitalist colonial order was discredited. In light of the West's many putative failings, this project reconstructs how "New China" inspired sympathy among British opinion makers. to add new perspectives to existing scholarship on Christianity, communism, the early People's Republic of China, and the transmission of ideas between supposedly distinct or even hostile societies and cultures. to, in order to fulfill the objectives above, deliver two conference presentations, one journal article and one book chapter. One article will explore the bitter controversy Johnson's highly publicized charge that the United Stated conducted biological warfare against China during the Korean War, an allegation shared by the famed biochemist-cum-sinologist Joseph Needham, stirred in a Britain whose global power was rapidly diminishing. The book chapter will examine Johnson's travels in China and the textual and visual strategies in which he and his wife Nowell represented the society they encountered. to form the basis, along with outcomes of the Principal Investigator's two ongoing or recently completed projects, of a monograph on "New China" in the global 1950s.

In light of the West's many putative failings, this project reconstructs how "New China" inspired sympathy among British opinion makers.

to add new perspectives to existing scholarship on Christianity, communism, the early People's Republic of China, and the transmission of ideas between supposedly distinct or even hostile societies and cultures.

to, in order to fulfill the objectives above, deliver two conference presentations, one journal article and one book chapter. One article will explore the bitter controversy Johnson's highly publicized charge that the United Stated conducted biological warfare against China during the Korean War, an allegation shared by the famed biochemist-cum-sinologist Joseph Needham, stirred in a Britain whose global power was rapidly diminishing. The book chapter will examine Johnson's travels in China and the textual and visual strategies in which he and his wife Nowell represented the society they encountered.
to form the basis, along with outcomes of the Principal Investigator's two ongoing or recently completed projects, of a monograph on "New China" in the global 1950s.

15602521.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15602521.value: 追求愉快和/或成長？青少年早期幸福傾向的發展以及父母的社會化影響

15602521.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15602521.value: Dr Kwan, Lok Yin Joyce Prof Shek, Daniel, Tan Lei

15602521.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15602521.value: Hong Kong, a member of the high-income countries, is known as the world’s most stressed-out city (Brynes & Harrington, 2020). Surveys have suggested that many adolescents in Hong Kong feel unhappy and stressed about their lives. Across many parts of the world, young people are facing various stressors and uncertainties that threaten their daily happiness and flourishing as a whole. Thus, understanding how adolescents can achieve happiness has become an increasingly important concern not only for the adolescents themselves but also for scholars, parents, educators, practitioners, and policymakers in Hong Kong and other societies globally. Positive psychology theories suggest that people attain happiness by pursuing pleasure and comfort (i.e., hedonic orientation) and/or by seeking personal growth, meaning, and virtue (i.e., eudaimonic orientation). While the hedonic orientation often evokes short-term positive feelings, the eudaimonic orientation fosters long-term fulfillment in personal growth and contributes to others’ welfare. Despite numerous studies documenting various outcomes of happiness orientations, research aimed at uncovering how these orientations develop is surprisingly scarce. Adolescence is a critical life-transitionary period when happiness orientations form, and during this time, parents remain one of the major socialization agents. Therefore, this project aims to uncover what makes young adolescents endorse which happiness orientation from the perspectives of adolescent development and parental socialization. First, we will examine the developmental changes of the hedonic and eudaimonic orientations over early adolescence. Second, as suggested by multiple socialization theories (Bandura, 1977; Deci & Ryan, 2008; van Gelder et al., 2017), we will examine three pathways in which parents influence the development of adolescent happiness orientations: parental modeling, parental encouragement, and general parental control. Finally, to uncover the developmental origins of happiness orientation, we will further examine the process of how parents transmit their happiness orientations to their adolescents through the three pathways. This three-year project will adopt a three-wave longitudinal design. Three consecutive annual assessments will be conducted in a sample of 860 two-parent families of seventh-graders comprised of adolescents, fathers, and mothers. By integrating theories of adolescent development, parental socialization and positive psychology, this study will provide a new perspective to address the hedonia-eudaimonia distinction in well-being, explicate the mechanisms underlying the development of happiness orientations, and offer an innovative account (i.e., parental happiness orientations) to explain parenting behavior. Findings will contribute to developing evidence-based programs and campaigns for parents and adolescents that focus on happiness orientations, ultimately helping promote adolescents’ flourishing locally and globally.

15602621.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15602621.value: Corpus-based translation research has offered abundant evidence of the special status of translated language as a unique type of language, which is characterized overall by more simplified, explicit, and normalized language use. While some scholars have claimed that these features are translation-inherent, there have been more and more calls for considering translated language as one special form of constrained communication, which is similar to other forms of constrained language use such as non-native language production. The same way of thinking has also been extended to interpreting, a cognitively more challenging translational activity, although empirical studies on this topic are few and sparse. By investigating four corpora covering two broad registers (i.e. business discourse and public speeches), including the Parallel Learner Interpreting Corpus (PLIC, to be constructed), the Parallel Professional Interpreting Corpus (PPIC, to be constructed), the existing Hong Kong Corpus of Spoken English (HKCSE) and the spoken BNC2014 corpus from a corpus-based multidimensional approach, this project aims to examine interpreted discourse under the framework of constrained language, focusing on consecutively interpreted English (i.e., consecutive interpreting) by advanced learner interpreters, compared with that by professional interpreters, non-native English (i.e., Hong Kong English) and native British English. The goals are: 1) to investigate how and in what ways advanced learner interpreting share similarities with or demonstrate differences from other forms of bilingually constrained language production and native language variety; and 2) to reveal the extent to which the differences or similarities can be claimed as general patterns inherent in constrained language forms. The proposed research is expected to contribute to the study of constrained language production both theoretically and practically. Theoretically, by focusing on learners’ interpreted language and highlighting its specific properties in relation to other forms of bilingually constrained varieties, we can deepen our knowledge of the working mechanism of bilingually constrained language production, especially when shared features, or language contact universals are identified, thus shedding light on the general patterns of cognitive processing. Practically, the shared linguistic features and the divergent patterns found between learner interpreting and other constrained language forms can be used to design more tailor-made drills, modules, and curricula for interpreter training. 基於語料庫的翻譯研究為翻譯語言作為一種獨特的語言類型的特殊地位提供了豐富的證據，其總體特徵是語言使用更加簡化、明確和規範化。雖然一些學者聲稱這些特徵是翻譯固有的，但越來越多的人呼籲將翻譯語言視為一種特殊的受限交流形式，它與非母語語言等其他形式的受限語言相似。 同樣的，口譯作為一種認知上更具挑戰性的翻譯活動，也可視為一種受限語言。但關於這個主題的口譯實證研究非常有限。 本研究通過採用基於語料庫的多維方法，探究涵蓋公開演講領域的四個語料庫，包括平行學習口譯語料庫（PLIC，待建）、平行專業口譯語料庫（PPIC，待建）、現有的香港語料庫Spoken English (HKCSE) 和 BNC2014 口語語料庫，本項目旨在研究受限語言框架下的口譯話語，主要關注高階學習者的交替傳譯，與專業口譯員，非母語英語（即香港英語）和本族語英語進行對比。本項目的目標是： 1) 研究高階學習者口譯話語與其他形式的雙語受限語言及母語有何異同； 2) 揭示何種程度上的相同點及不同點可以被認為是的受限語言固有的一般規律。 本項目預期在理論和實踐方面對受限語言產出的研究做出貢獻。從理論上看，通過探究學習者的口譯語言，並著重研究其與其他形式的雙語受限語言的異同，可以加深我們對雙語受限語言產出的工作機制的認識，同時能夠識別出這些受限語言的共同特徵或語言共性，從而闡明認知處理的一般規律。 從實踐上說，學習者口譯語言和其他受限語言之間的共同語言特徵和不同模式可用於為口譯教學設計更多量身定制的練習、課程模組和課程大綱。

15602821.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15602821.value: 青光眼是一種由於視神經損傷令周邊視力逐漸喪失的眼部疾病，可能導致平衡和活動能力受損。尤其當青光眼患者跨過或避開障礙物、行走在不平坦的地面上或橫過馬路時，比較容易跌倒。跌倒是長者非常關心的問題，憂慮跌倒後引致的後遺症，需要更多個人和社區護理及復康訓練。一直以來，運動可有效預防視障長者跌倒。近年有研究顯示，電子遊戲訓練能提升長者的平衡力，減低跌倒風險，但這類訓練甚少應用於容易跌倒的視障患者。我們在是次研究中，將探討互動的電子遊戲訓練對提升青光眼患者視覺功能及平衡力的成效，進一步減少對跌倒的恐懼、並提高生活質量。 次研究將採用前瞻性、兩組、隨機、單盲、主動對照試驗方式招募五十六位中度至嚴重的青光眼患者。患者需俱有穩定的週邊視野缺損、良好的認知能力和未曾參加平衡相關的訓練。參與者將按 1:1 的比例隨機分配到以下其中的一組：1)互動的電子遊戲訓練 (AVG_PI)； 2) 常規體能訓練 (PT)。我們採用任天堂Switch 電子遊戲為AVG_PI的參予者進行20次肌肉伸展和強化練習的訓練（每次 45 分鐘，每週 2 次，共10週）。PT 的參與者將接受 20次常規體能訓練（每次 45 分鐘，每週 2 次，共10週）。所有參予者在訓練前、十次和廿次訓練後進行評估。主要評估指標是活動能力測試，次要指標包括動態及靜態平衡測試、視覺認知、以及患者報告的跌倒恐懼感和生活質量的問卷。 研究結果將反映互動的電子遊戲能否有效減低青光眼患者跌倒的機率。

15603621.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15603621.value: 香港媒體1997年至2020年對中國（內地）報道的變化：一項歷時語料庫研究

15603621.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15603621.value: Dr Huan, Changpeng Prof Lam, Phoenix Prof Su, Hang

15603621.label: Project Objectives
15603621.value: To compile the first set of large-scale diachronic corpora of China-related reports from Chinese-language newspapers in Hong Kong. The three most influential Chinese language newspapers, namely, Apple Daily, Ming Pao, and Oriental Daily News, which cover the political spectrum of anti-Beijing, liberal and pro-Beijing stances respectively will be selected. The compilation of diachronic corpora aims to provide a comprehensive understanding of the changing practices of Chinese-language newspapers in Hong Kong. We aim to make the corpora available online for researchers and students who can analyze the data from various perspectives. To investigate the variations in topics or issues of concern (i.e. the ‘aboutness’) in China-related reports among the three newspapers from 1997 to 2020 through corpus linguistic analysis. Using keyword analysis, we aim to provide quantifiable evidences about how different newspapers are concerned with similar/different issues about China according to their stances, and how the concerns have evolved during the past 23 years. To investigate the diachronic changes and cross-newspaper differences in the reports in terms of their attitudes towards China . Using corpus-based annotation of attitudes based on Martin and White’s (2005) framework, this study aims to provide empirical linguistic evidence about the complexity of media attitudes towards China beyond a general positive/negative distinction. Through statistical analysis of annotated attitudes, we will provide theoretical and empirical underpinnings for discussing the nuanced diachronic changes from 1997 to 2020 and divergence across different newspapers. To provide a critical analysis of the three newspapers’ differing and changing discursive strategies in coping with the changing socio-political context. Working broadly with Wodak’s (2001) Discourse Historical Approach, we aim to explicate how the representation of China is shaped by the complex socio-political contexts and media environment in Hong Kong on the one hand, and how different newspapers deploy various attitudinal resources to deal with political pressure and influence their readers on the other hand.

15603621.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15603621.value: 香港回歸二十三年來在迅速融入中國發展的同時，敵對情緒也在部分群體中加剧。中國內地與香港之間複雜變化的關係一方面影響媒體話語，另一方面也受媒體報導的影響。雖然香港不斷變化的政治經濟對媒體的影響廣受學界關注，但很少有研究為這種影響提供實證證據。 該專案旨在系統考察從1997年到2020年，即香港回歸後的二十三年來，香港的中文報紙對中國（內地）報導的變化。我們將分析在立場上分別是反中、相對中立與親中的三个最有影响力的中文報紙，即蘋果日報、明報、東方日報。結合語料庫分析與批評性話語分析，該專案首先通過關鍵字分析考察不同時期、不同報紙關注的關於中國內地的事件或話題。然後，我們將通過對態度的類型、來源、目標的手動標注與定量分析對不同時期、不同報紙的態度進行比較。從批評性視角來看，新聞報導中的態度是應對社會政治變化並實現特定傳意目的的話語策略。我們將結合語境分析態度的顯著特徵以期發現不同時期、不同報紙的不同話語策略。 作為首個基於歷時語料庫的關於中國的報導的研究，該專案對話語分析與傳媒研究有如下貢獻。第一，通過描述報紙關心的話題和態度的變化，該項目可以為討論社會政治因素對新聞實踐的影響提供實證依據。第二，國際歷時語料庫研究絕大部分關注英文報紙，而基於中文語料庫的歷時研究為香港的中文報紙的話語實踐提供新的認識。第三，我們關於不同報紙應對社會政治環境變化所採取的的不同話語策略的討論對新聞教育工作者和從業者具有重要意義。

15603621.label: Realisation of objectives
15603621.value: Compiling the First Large-Scale Diachronic Corpus of China-Related Reports in Hong Kong Chinese Newspapers This objective has been fully achieved. The research team selected data from three then leading Chinese newspapers in Hong Kong—Apple Daily (AD), Ming Pao (MP), and Oriental Daily News (ODN). The team utilised keywords such as “China”, “Mainland” (大陆), “Mainland” (内地) and “Beijing” to precisely retrieve relevant news articles in the Wisenews database, ensuring that the collected data closely revolves around the “China” theme. The data collection spans from July 1, 1997, the day Hong Kong returned to China, to December 31, 2020, comprehensively covering the 23 years after Hong Kong’s return, thereby fully guaranteeing the diachronic nature of the corpus. The corpus comprises 188,239 news articles with a total size of 159,872,724 tokens. In addition to the news content itself, the research team also meticulously extracted meta-information such as the title and publication date of each news article, providing detailed background data for subsequent analysis. To conduct in-depth diachronic analysis, the research team divided the corpus into four sub-corpora based on different stages of Hong Kong media development, with each sub-corpus corresponding to a specific time period. The compilation of the corpus not only provides researchers with vast data support but also facilitates subsequent analysis work through the extraction of meta-information and the division of sub-corpora, making the analysis more convenient and efficient. The corpus has been opened to the public via CQPweb for online access via the website of Research Centre for Professional Communication in English (http://rcpce.engl.polyu.edu.hk/), allowing researchers and students to conduct in-depth data analysis from multiple angles. Exploring the Differences and Evolution of Topics or Issues of concern in Reporting This objective has been fully achieved. To get a thorough understanding of the cross-newspaper variations and evolution of topics or issues of concern in reporting, the research team employed corpus linguistics methods to analyse China-related reports in AD, MP, and ODN. Firstly, using the LDA model, the team conducted theme fitting on these news articles and successfully identified 13 specific themes within five major thematic areas, encompassing national identity construction, common culture construction, the construction of shared political status and future, national institution construction, and the economic domain. Secondly, through keyword analysis, the research team quantitatively assessed the degree of attention given by different newspapers to China-related issues at different stages and revealed how they selected reporting content based on their stances. The quantitative evidence clearly demonstrates how different newspapers paid attention to similar or different issues related to China based on their stances and how the attention evolved over the past 23 years. Overall, ODN extensively utilised discourse on national identity, common culture, and shared political status and future in its reporting, promoting the construction of national identity. AD focused more on the implementation and impact of Chinese government policies. MP exhibited a more neutral stance, reporting on China’s achievements in economics and culture while also pointing out problems in social governance and other areas. Relevant findings have been reported in Papers 2, 3, and 4 listed in Section C. Studying the Diachronic Changes and Cross-Newspaper Differences in Attitudes towards China in Reporting This objective has been fully achieved. This study adopted the Appraisal system proposed by Martin and White (2005) as the analytical framework and conducted in-depth attitude analysis on China-related reports in three Hong Kong Chinese newspapers using corpus annotation techniques. This method aims to go beyond simple positive/negative evaluations and reveal the complexity and nuances of media attitudes towards China. The research team manually annotated the collected news expressions using the attitude framework of the Appraisal system, conducted detailed statistical analysis on the annotated attitude data, and quantitatively assessed the attitude tendencies and frequencies of different newspapers towards China-related issues at different stages. Through ANOVA testing, the team analysed whether there were significant differences in the number and types of attitudes among different newspapers; calculated the annual averages and overall polarity of different attitude types to examine the evolution trends of attitudes over time; and utilised KH Coder software to construct attitude-word co-occurrence networks, analysing the specific vocabulary and topic preferences used by each newspaper when expressing different attitudes and revealing the thematic patterns and discourse strategies in attitude expression. Findings in this regard have been reported in Paper 3 listed in Section C. The research findings provide a solid theoretical and empirical foundation for understanding the reporting attitudes of Hong Kong media towards China between 1997 and 2020, which is of great significance for further studying the relationship between media attitudes and public opinion. Critical Analysis of the Discursive Strategies Adopted by Newspapers in Response to the Changing Socio-Political Environment This objective has been fully achieved. To delve deeper into the discourse strategies employed by the three newspapers in response to the evolving socio-political landscape, the research team drew extensively from Discourse-Historical Analysis, conducting a critical analysis of the discourse strategies within the newspapers. The team discovered that the three newspapers adopted distinct de/legitimation strategies in their reporting on China to cope with changes in the socio-political environment. The findings further develop the “us” and “them” framework and the discursive shift model in critical discourse studies. Specifically, “us” and “them” may constitute a continuum rather than a dichotomy; “us”, “them”, and the states between them are multidimensional and can coexist within a region or even within a single newspaper, rather than being mutually exclusive. On the other hand, the boundaries between the three stages of discourse shift model are not always clear-cut; there exist overlapping or transitional zones. The findings related have been reported in Papers 1 and 3 listed in Section C. Through critical analysis of discursive strategies, we have clearly elucidated how the newspapers respond to Hong Kong’s complex socio-political and media environments using various attitudinal resources. These findings not only contribute to our deeper understanding of the complexity and diversity of Hong Kong media’s reporting on China, but also contributes to theories of critical discourse analysis. In summary, our research team has successfully achieved the four research objectives. By compiling a large-scale diachronic corpus, conducting keyword analysis and attitude analysis, as well as critically analysing discourse strategies, we have provided rich empirical linguistic evidence for understanding topical differences, attitudinal complexities, and discourse strategies of Hong Kong Chinese newspapers in their reporting on China. Beyond the above, we have also adapted our proposed methodologies to more effectively achieve our objectives, particularly in leveraging AI, Machine Learning, and Large Language Model technologies. These methodological innovations have been documented in Papers 1, 5, and 6 listed in Section C. They not only addressed the initial challenges encountered in the research, such as the substantial workload in data processing and attitude analysis, but also advanced the methodology of discourse research in the age of Generative AI. The LLM-based attitude analysis tools have been made accessible to researchers and students, thereby further contributing to the academic community.

rows: To compile the first set of large-scale diachronic corpora of China-related reports from Chinese-language newspapers in Hong Kong. The three most influential Chinese language newspapers, namely, Apple Daily, Ming Pao, and Oriental Daily News, which cover the political spectrum of anti-Beijing, liberal and pro-Beijing stances respectively will be selected. The compilation of diachronic corpora aims to provide a comprehensive understanding of the changing practices of Chinese-language newspapers in Hong Kong. We aim to make the corpora available online for researchers and students who can analyze the data from various perspectives.

To investigate the variations in topics or issues of concern (i.e. the ‘aboutness’) in China-related reports among the three newspapers from 1997 to 2020 through corpus linguistic analysis. Using keyword analysis, we aim to provide quantifiable evidences about how different newspapers are concerned with similar/different issues about China according to their stances, and how the concerns have evolved during the past 23 years.

To investigate the diachronic changes and cross-newspaper differences in the reports in terms of their attitudes towards China . Using corpus-based annotation of attitudes based on Martin and White’s (2005) framework, this study aims to provide empirical linguistic evidence about the complexity of media attitudes towards China beyond a general positive/negative distinction. Through statistical analysis of annotated attitudes, we will provide theoretical and empirical underpinnings for discussing the nuanced diachronic changes from 1997 to 2020 and divergence across different newspapers.

To provide a critical analysis of the three newspapers’ differing and changing discursive strategies in coping with the changing socio-political context. Working broadly with Wodak’s (2001) Discourse Historical Approach, we aim to explicate how the representation of China is shaped by the complex socio-political contexts and media environment in Hong Kong on the one hand, and how different newspapers deploy various attitudinal resources to deal with political pressure and influence their readers on the other hand.

15603621.label: Major findings and research outcome
15603621.value: The project has generated several major findings on the representation of China in the Hong Kong press. Firstly, the overall sentiment of Hong Kong's mainstream Chinese newspapers towards China has been generally positive but has become increasingly negative until the data collection year of 2020, with a notable polarisation of emotions. Specifically, AD exhibits the most negative attitude, while ODN holds the most positive view. MP maintains a consistent neutral stance but demonstrates a gradual increase in subjectivity. Regarding the One Country, Two Systems policy in particular, ODN legitimises it as the cornerstone of Hong Kong's political system. MP maintains neutrality, providing a platform for diverse viewpoints. AD argues that the policy has been abused in implementation. The evolution of newspaper sentiments and attitudes is explained in relation to Hong Kong's sociopolitical dynamics. Secondly, in terms of discursive strategies, ODN actively promotes national identity construction through discourse related to ethnic identity, shared culture, political status, national institutions, and economic development. MP's coverage of China-related issues has shifted from an outsider to an insider perspective, indicating an increasing alignment with China, though not completely. AD, on the other hand, adopts a more direct and radical discursive strategy, directly criticising Chinese government policies and actions, particularly on the implementation of the One Country, Two Systems policy. These discursive strategies reflect the dynamics and complexity of media representations of China, shaped by the joint forces of local market demands, political needs, and their own ideological stances. The findings further develops the "us" and "them" framework and the discursive shift model in critical discourse studies. Furthermore, this study provides innovative methods integrating corpus linguistics, critical discourse analysis, and cutting-edge AI techniques. By constructing a large-scale corpus and combining advanced techniques in text mining, Natural Language Processing, and Large Language Models, we were able to capture and quantify the subtle differences in newspaper representations of China in an effective and efficient manner. The project has provided powerful tools and methods for linguistic and social scientific research. The project has produced six high-quality papers and four international conference/symposium presentations in the fields of linguistics, journalism, and communication studies. The Hong Kong news corpus developed under this project, along with the LLM-based automatic attitude analysis tool, has been made publicly available online in the near future. These resources will further facilitate academic research and contribute to the broader understanding of media discourse and its impact on society.

15603621.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15603621.value: The potential for further development of this research is enormous. First, the compiled corpus and analytical methods can be expanded to include more newspapers, more issues, and a longer time span, providing a more comprehensive understanding of Hong Kong media's attitudes. Second, the use of Large Language Models (LLMs) for discourse analysis, though promising, still faces challenges in accurately capturing subtle and implicit attitudes. We have released our web-based attitude analysis platform, which leverages LLMs, to the public domain. We are committed to ongoing improvements to enhance the performance of the underlying models that drive this innovative tool. Further research could explore techniques to enhance LLMs' capabilities in this regard, such as fine-tuning on domain-specific datasets and optimising prompt engineering. Third, comparative studies with other regions’ media portrayals of China could offer insights into the global dynamics of media representations. Furthermore, the data was until 2020 and recent developments in media attitudes is worth further exploration. The proposed course of action therefore includes continuously refining the analytical methods, expanding the corpus, and exploring new techniques to improve the accuracy and robustness of LLM-based discourse analysis.

15603621.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15603621.value: The evolution of media attitudes in Hong Kong towards China during the last twenty odd years is a topic of great social and academic significance. The project provides a systematic discourse analysis of the nuances and complexities of the changing portrayal of China in the main Chinese language newspapers in Hong Kong, namely, Apple Daily, Ming Pao, and Oriental Daily News, from 1997 to 2020. Findings regarding topics of concern, sentiments, attitudes towards the One Country, Two Systems policy, national identification, etc. have been reported in six research papers and five conference/symposium presentations. The project provides empirical evidence of the nature and extent of attitude change, complementing general observations and theoretical discussions in journalism and communication studies. It also provides innovative methods combining cutting edge NLP/GenAI techniques and (critical) discourse/linguistic frameworks for automating the analysis of media sentiments and attitudes. The corpora and an LLM-based attitude analysis interface are available to the public, which will empower further scholarly inquiry into media attitudes and attitude analysis in general. Beyond academia, our findings about the different discursive strategies employed by different newspapers to respond to the contextual changes will be valuable for journalism educators and media practitioners.

15603721.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15603721.value: The bill of lading, as an important shipping and trade document, is traditionally in paper form. However, the drawbacks inherent in using a paper bill of lading, such as delay and security risks, have become increasingly problematic in practice. Therefore, the idea of replacing paper bills of lading with electronic alternatives has long been discussed, both in China and worldwide. These discussions have shown, from different perspectives, the complexity as well as importance of regulating the electronic bill of lading. In actual practice, the electronic bill of lading is not widely used. Apart from the technological barriers, there lacks an effective legal enablement in China—the present legal framework does not recognize electronic transport documents. Fortunately, progress is being made to change this situation. For instance, the “Chinese E-Commerce Law” came into force in 2019; and in the process of discussing reform of the “Chinese Maritime Code”, the necessity of including rules for the electronic bill of lading is now well recognized. While there is increasing research into the electronic bill of lading and its legal and regulatory issues, the study of Chinese law on this subject lacks a coherent analysis. As an integrated study focused on Chinese law, this proposed research will carry out a holistic study of the challenges and prospects facing use of the electronic bill of lading. Accordingly, it will evaluate the existing Chinese laws covering sales, carriage and trade finance that require the tender of bills of lading; it will examine the desired functions of electronic bills of lading; and it will discuss whether, under Chinese law, the desired functions would be adequately regulated, and whether the relevant legal issues would be amply addressed. In addition, the proposed research will develop recommendations as to what changes to the law may be required in order to achieve benign regulatory and legal support for the use of electronic bills of lading. This proposed research will be divided into three inter-related research stages and will employ various research methods over a 36-month period, the methods including legal case studies, a comparative law research and structured interviews. The research outcomes are expected to have profound impacts, not only by stimulating further studies in this area of research, but also by providing a legal reference work for the various stakeholders involved in the acceptance, regulation and use of electronic bills of lading. 提單作為重要的運輸和貿易檔，傳統上採用紙質形式。然而，使用紙質提單所固有的缺點，例如延遲和安全風險，在實踐中變得越來越成問題。因此，在中國和世界範圍內，長期以來一直在討論用電子方式替代紙質提單的想法。但是這些討論從不同的角度也表明了監管電子提單的複雜性和重要性。 在實際操作中，電子提單並未得到廣泛應用。除了技術障礙外，中國還缺乏有效的法律支援—目前的法律框架不承認電子運輸單證。幸運的是，正在取得進展以改變這種狀況。例如，《中國電子商務法》於2019年生效；而在討論《中國海商法典》改革的過程中，現在已經充分認識到納入電子提單規則的必要性。 雖然對電子提單及其法律和監管問題的研究越來越多，但對中國法律的研究缺乏整體的分析。作為一項專注於中國法律的綜合研究，這項擬議的研究將對電子提單的使用面臨的挑戰和前景進行全面研究。因此，它將評估要求提供提單的現行中國法律，包括銷售、運輸和貿易融資；它將檢查電子提單的所需功能；並將討論根據中國法律，預期的功能是否會得到充分監管，以及相關的法律問題是否會得到充分解決。此外，擬議的研究將就可能需要對法律進行哪些修改提出建議，以便為電子提單的使用獲得良好的監管和法律支援。 這項擬議的研究將分為三個相互關聯的研究階段，將在 36 個月的時間內採用各種研究方法，包括法律案例研究、比較法研究和結構化訪談。預計研究成果將產生深遠的影響，不僅會刺激該研究領域的進一步研究，而且還會為參與電子提單的接受、監管和使用的各個利益相關者提供法律參考工作。

15604721.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15604721.value: 擬議的研究將調查香港和澳洲的一組特定工作人員如何面對將與2019冠狀病毒病相關的特殊感染控制措施結合到日常工作中的需求。是項提案將側重於善終服務工作者，即在標誌著生命終結的兩個階段，即喪親前和喪親后，會涉及到的人。這些工作人員可能會參與提供臨床/醫療和舒緩治療，或宗教、公民及社區服務。是項研究並不劃分和關注特定的臨床護理情境，而是將著重研究有助於在廣泛的社會層面上標記死亡的文化、社會和工作實踐。是項研究的基本原理是基於這樣的理解，即除了標誌著個人生理狀態的變化之外，對死亡的反應還反映了社會、文化和公共衛生的視角。在發達地區和國家，善終服務已經變得愈發複雜。這些變化源於人口老齡化、能夠延長生命的醫療進步以及某些服務從醫院到社區的轉移（Wang, Chan, & Lou, 2020）。因此，塑造善終服務的護理實踐吸引了廣泛的醫療和社會心理干預措施以及為個人和家庭提供干預措施的工作人員。2019冠狀病毒病的爆發和2020年3月宣佈的全球大流行使提供善終服務變得更加複雜化。儘管健康危機的未來是未知的，但人們已經達成共識，認為這是一個歷史性變革的時期（Fouad, 2020），可能會對人們的工作方式和地點產生長遠的影響（Cho, 2020）。我們將會在香港和澳洲收集數據，因為它們在政府資助的公共衛生系統方面具有共同的結構特征。然而，在危機應對和善終服務方法方面也存在關鍵的歷史、地理、人口和文化差異，這使得跨地區以及跨文化研究特別富有成效和洞察力（Varnum & Grossman, 2017）。通過研究相似點和不同點，是項研究將提供豐富的、有理論依據的見解。擬議的研究使用混合方法序列型解釋的設計。第一階段將使用網上問卷來收集有關情緒勞動、工作壓力和復原力的定量數據。第二階段將通過兩次半結構式個人訪談以及與受訪者的電子郵件往來來開發數據的深度。這些干預措施旨在引出個人經歷，并檢驗工作人員如何適應特殊的感染控制要求。這個關注點將讓我們能夠確定促進工作人員復原力和壓力管理的做法。成果將為香港和澳洲的公共衛生及政策領域貢獻新的知識，并促進該行業持續的服務調整和創新。

15604921.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15604921.value: Reform-era China has witnessed revolutionary changes in the culture of work as it underwent a dramatic departure from the Maoist ideologies in the late 1970s. The Maoist discourse of work as “devotion to the public interest and serving the people wholeheartedly” that stipulated egalitarianism and collectivist ethics gave way to the Post-Socialist discourse of work that endorsed the pursuits of self-fulfillment, individual benefits, material comfort, and social distinction. While work as a universal subject of inquiry has been a focus of the studies in anthropology, history, and sociology, there has been a lack of scholarly attention to contemporary China’s cultural representations of work, which have powerfully shaped the conceptions, meanings, and values of work and simultaneously illustrated its inner ambiguous and contradictory features. This project examines a body of cultural representations centering around work, such as Reform literature, finance-themed fiction, workplace novels, films about Reform-era China’s social transformations, TV documentaries and online videos about craftsmen as well as the ensuing broad discussions and debates, great controversies and multiple media adaptations these representations have generated. These cultural texts present complicated social scenes of “China at work” in which reform-minded industrialists, entrepreneurs, new petty urbanites-cum-homo economicus, white-collar professionals, and high-skilled craftsmen deal with the tensions between efficiency and justice, between quantity and quality, between emancipation and discipline, and between patience and productivity in the work realm. This project starts with the new time-numerical disciplinary regime of “scientific management” staged in the Reform literature in the early phase of Reform and Opening and then moves to a discussion of the forms of entrepreneurial labor celebrated by the Chinese intelligentsia and seen in popular representations in the early 1990s when China entered a financial age. It then focuses on the popularity of workplace novels which paralleled China’s global rise and incorporated self-help culture, game mentality and middle-class identity. Lastly it turns to the emergence of new forms of craftsmanship alongside millennium China’s self-conscious transition to post-industrial culture and a creative Made-in-China economy. Drawing from discourses in management, entrepreneurship, professionalism and craftsmanship and engaging with a variety of materials including literary and cinematic texts, newspaper essays, popular and intellectual writings, this project understands the formation of the new work culture as a new regime that produced new types of knowledge and disciplines and legitimized new forms of hierarchies, authorities and power relations and simultaneously sought alternative ways to go beyond the Post-Socialist developmentalism. 本研究關注改革開始時期中國的工作文化。毛時代的工作觀念以“全心全意爲人民服務”的平等主義和集體倫理為特徵，而後毛時代的工作觀念則轉向肯定個人成就、利益以及物質的舒適。當今的人類學、歷史學以及社會學中對工作的研究屢見不鮮，但是在文學與文化領域對當代中國工作文化的呈現則鮮少有系統研究。這些文化表徵曾經有力地塑造了工作的觀念、意義以及價值，同時也展現出工作文化中的内在的衝突與含糊。本研究分析一系列關於“工作”的文化呈現，譬如改革文學，財經小説，職場小説以及關於改革開放時期社會轉型的電影、紀錄片以及網路上的視頻。通過分析這些作品，本研究志在呈現“工作文化”中包含的效率與公平、數量與質量、解放與規訓以及耐心與生產力之間的關係。

15605021.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15605021.value: 香港華人家庭之親職完美主義及過度管教

15605021.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15605021.value: Prof Scharf, Miri Prof Shek, Daniel, Tan Lei Dr To, Siu-ming Dr Yu, Nancy Xiaonan

15605021.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15605021.value: Overparenting refers to the phenomenon of parents intruding into their children’s lives and removing perceived obstacles so that children can win in the competitive “rug rat race”. While the phenomenon of overparenting has intensified in the past two decades, studies examining the antecedents of overparenting are sparse in both Western and Chinese contexts, with a majority focusing solely on the influence of parents’ personal traits on overparenting without considering how different facets of parenting perfectionism – self-oriented parenting perfectionism (i.e., excessively high parenting standards and critical self-evaluation about parenting), culturally inclined parenting perfectionism (i.e., high parenting standards to promote family pride) and socially prescribed parenting perfectionism (i.e., one’s belief about the societal demand for a perfect parent) – contribute to overparenting. This pioneering study will thus examine three research questions: 1) What are the relationships between the three facets of parenting perfectionism and overparenting among Chinese parents in Hong Kong? As fathers are more influential than mothers in Chinese families, a related question to be examined is whether paternal parenting perfectionism affects maternal overparenting. 2) What are the mediators of the relationship between parenting perfectionism and overparenting? According to role identity theory, parents with excessively high parenting standards (i.e., parenting perfectionism) would endorse ideal parental roles in order to build up a stronger identity of being a “perfect” parent. Furthermore, the anxious rearing model maintains that parents with high parenting perfectionism would feel more stressful and anxious about any imperfections and mistakes that might spoil their children’s future, resulting in more overparenting behaviour. These two mediators will be examined in the present study. 3) Does marital quality moderate the relationship between parenting perfectionism and overparenting through two mechanisms proposed by family systems theory: a) stress from the marital domain spilling over into the parental domain; and b) trying to compensate for the unsatisfactory marital relationship? Against this background, we propose a three-wave longitudinal study to examine: first, individual and inter-spousal influences of parenting perfectionism on overparenting; second, the mediating effects of parental stress and parents’ endorsement of parental roles in the relationship between parenting perfectionism and overparenting; and third, the moderating effect of marital satisfaction on the parenting perfectionism-overparenting relationship among 650 dyads of Chinese parents in Hong Kong. The study will shed new light on how different facets of parenting perfectionism, as well as the proposed mediating and moderating mechanisms, contribute to overparenting in Chinese families. 過度管教意指父母闖入孩子的生活領域並消除他們可預視的障礙，使孩子在激烈的競爭中獲得勝利。雖然過度管教的現象在過去十數年間愈演愈烈，但關於過度管教的成因研究卻十分匱乏，而大多數研究均著重父母的個人特質對過度管教的影響，而忽視不同面向的親職管教完美主義 —— 自我導向型的親職完美主義（即過高的親職管教標準和對親職管教的批判式自我評價）、具文化傾向的親職完美主義（即為了提高家族聲望而有較高的親職管教標準）和社會期許型的親職完美主義（即社會對完美父母的要求）—— 導致過度管教。 因此，這項創新性研究將探討三項研究問題： 1) 香港華人父母之過度管教和上述提及之三種面向的親職管教完美主義之間的關係是甚麼？由於在華人家庭中，父親的影響力大於母親，因此其中一個相關問題是探討父親之管教完美主義會否會影響母親之過度管教模式。 2) 親職管教完美主義與過度管教之間的中介變項是甚麼？根據角色認同理論，具有較高親職管教標準（即親職管教完美主義）的父母會認同「理想的父母」之準則，從而建立更強的「完美父母」身份認同。此外，在焦慮的管教模式中，如果父母有較高的親職管教完美主義，他們會對有可能阻礙孩子未來發展的事情上感到壓力和焦慮，從而導致更多的過度管教行為。在本研究中將探討這兩個變項。 3）婚姻滿意程度會否影響親職管教完美主義和過度管教之間的關係？家庭系統理論提出的兩種可行機制：一）來自婚姻關係的壓力會影響父母之管教； 二) 父母透過過度親職管教試圖彌補不健康的婚姻關係。 在此背景下，我們提出了一項為期三年之縱向研究，以探討：(1)個人和配偶之間的親職管教完美主義對彼此過度管教產生的影響；(2)父母壓力和父母對家長角色的理解在親職管教完美主義和過度管教關係中產生的中介作用；(3)婚姻滿意度對父母的親職管教完美主義及過度管教關係中的調節作用。是次研究會以問卷調查方式訪問650對香港華人家長，希望能夠知悉析不同面向之親職管教完美主義及過度管教之關係，並了解其中介和調節機制。

15605821.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15605821.value: 從音段排序到聲調變化技巧：診斷兒童言語失用症之新見

15605821.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15605821.value: Prof Velleman, Shelley Mr WONG, Eddy Chun-ho

15605821.label: Project Objectives
15605821.value: To show that Maximum Performance Tasks and Syllable Repetition Task can contribute to the diagnosis of childhood apraxia of speech in Cantonese-speaking children, To document differences in pitch-variation skills in Cantonese-speaking children with versus without childhood apraxia of speech, and To prove that Tone Sequencing Tasks are effective for diagnosing childhood apraxia of speech in Cantonese-speaking children.
rows: To show that Maximum Performance Tasks and Syllable Repetition Task can contribute to the diagnosis of childhood apraxia of speech in Cantonese-speaking children,
To document differences in pitch-variation skills in Cantonese-speaking children with versus without childhood apraxia of speech, and
To prove that Tone Sequencing Tasks are effective for diagnosing childhood apraxia of speech in Cantonese-speaking children.

15605821.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15605821.value: Childhood apraxia of speech (CAS) is a motor-based speech sound disorder with a core impairment in planning and/or programming of spatiotemporal parameters of speech movement sequences. CAS may cause deficits in both segmental and suprasegmental components of speech, and it can severely affect children’s ability to speak intelligibly and communicate effectively, and impact their quality of life. Assessment tasks, such as the Maximum Performance Tasks (MPT) and the Syllable Repetition Task (SRT), examine children’s segmental sequencing skills to assist with the diagnosis of CAS. Suprasegmentally, lexical stress errors have been reported as a core feature and aid diagnosis of CAS. However, there are challenges in diagnosing CAS in children who speak tonal languages like Cantonese. In Hong Kong, although MPT and SRT have been used clinically to diagnose CAS in Cantonese-speaking children, their validity in assessing segmental sequencing skills in Cantonese-speaking children with CAS has not been reported. There is an urgent need of such investigations. Suprasegmentally, even though lexical stress is not found in Cantonese, a recent study has reported lexical tone errors in Cantonese-speaking children with CAS. Furthermore, deficits in pitch-variation skills were found in Cantonese-speaking children with CAS using a tone sequencing task (TST). It is hypothesised that there is a universal deficit in pitch-variation skills among speakers with CAS of tonal and non-tonal languages. Pitch-variation skill presents in Cantonese lexical tones and English lexical stress patterns. Further investigations on pitch-variation skills using TST in Cantonese-speaking children with CAS may shed light on suprasegmental deficits in tonal languages, as well as contribute to development of a valid diagnostic tool for CAS in children who speak tonal languages, such as Vietnamese, Thai, and Mandarin. This study aims to examine the diagnostic potential of the MPT, SRT and TST in diagnosing Cantonese-speaking children with CAS, and to investigate pitch-variation skills in Cantonese-speaking children with and without CAS. Thirty children with CAS and three groups of age-and-gender-matched controls (speech sound disorders [SSD] group, non-CAS SSD co-occurring with language impairment [S&LI] group, and typical development [TD] group) will be recruited. All participants will perform MPT, SRT, and TST. Their performance on these measures will be perceptually judged and acoustically measured. It is anticipated that Cantonese-speaking children with CAS will have poorer pitch-variation skills than the control groups, while MPT, SRT and TST will be appropriate diagnostic tools for identifying CAS in Cantonese-speaking children.

15606321.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15606321.value: 用於產品設計及評估的頭部參數化生物力學模型研究

15606321.label: Project Objectives
15606321.value: Develop a method to parameterise the human head model together with the skull and brain structure. Analyse the anthropometric differences of head models among genders and ethnic groups. Analyse the variations in head models among ethnic groups. Develop a predictive model based on skin surface data and skin thickness at different head and face locations.
rows: Develop a method to parameterise the human head model together with the skull and brain structure.
Analyse the anthropometric differences of head models among genders and ethnic groups.
Analyse the variations in head models among ethnic groups.
Develop a predictive model based on skin surface data and skin thickness at different head and face locations.

15606321.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15606321.value: During an accident, the human head can experience severe trauma. Although the skull provides a certain degree of protection, the human brain and sense organs are very delicate and vulnerable to impact injuries. Therefore, wearable headgear must be carefully designed to minimise the impact of those injuries. The design of wearable products requires an understanding of the head and face anatomy, as well as the variations in shape and size. Although 3D head surface scanning can provide a useful reference for product design, it is essential to consider the anatomical and biomechanical models to reduce injuries. Most existing biomechanical models are based on a small number of data sets that do not fully represent a given population and the considerable variation between subjects. There is a need for accurate population-specific parametric biomechanical models that can aid in the design of head and face products that are either custom made, or mass produced. In addition, because Computed Tomography (CT) scans are expensive and time-consuming, a predictive model based on low cost 3D surface scans and easily obtained skin parameters could reduce costs and save time. This study proposes to develop an accurate parametric biomechanical model based on CT scans from three ethnic groups (Chinese, Indian and Malaysian). The biomechanical model will consist of an individual’s head surface model, skull model, mandible model and brain model. A study of shape variations will result in different sizes of biomechanical models to represent the selected groups. In addition, a predictive model is also proposed that uses skin thickness and head surface data to predict head bone shape and brain shape. The accurate parametric head models developed in this study could assist designers and manufacturers better understand the head anatomy, and design head and face wearable products for better fit and protection. Future improvements to the predictive model will eliminate the need for CT scans by using 3D scanning and skin thickness measurements. With some changes, the parametric biomechanical head model could be used for a wide range of simulations (e.g., injuries, head and face surgery and forensics). Those efforts will support the design and evaluation of wearable head and face products (e.g., glasses, goggles, face masks, face shields and helmets) without the need for expensive and unethical methods. 人的頭部在事故中可能遭受嚴重創傷。雖然顱骨可以提供一定程度的保護，但大腦和感覺器官還是容易受到撞擊傷害。因此，必須特別設計可穿戴頭部裝置以降低傷害。可穿戴產品的設計需要基於人體頭面部的解剖結構及形狀尺寸的變化。在相關產品設計中，盡管三維頭部表面掃描技術可提供有用的數據參考，但頭面部的解剖特征及生物力學模型也是非常重要的。 現有的生物力學模型大多基於少量樣本，這些數據無法完全代表特定的人口群體以及研究樣本間的差異。為特定人群建立的生物力學模型可以幫助設計定制或批量生產的頭面部產品。此外，由於計算機斷層掃描 (CT) 既昂貴又耗時，基於低成本三維表面掃描和皮膚參數的預測模型可以降低成本並節省時間。 本研究計劃開发基於CT掃描的參數化生物力學模型。數據集將會包括中國人、印度人和馬來西亞人。該生物力學模型包括頭部表面模型、顱骨模型、下頜骨模型和大腦模型。形狀差異研究將生成不同尺寸的生物力學模型以代表不同群體。此外，本研究還提出以皮膚厚度和頭部表面數據來預測頭部骨骼形狀和大腦形狀模型。本研究中開发的參數化頭部模型可以幫助設計師和制造商更精確地了解頭部解剖結構，並設計有更好的貼合和保護性的頭面部可穿戴產品。 未來對預測模型的改進將通過使用三維掃描和皮膚厚度測量消除對CT掃描的需要。通過調整，該參數化生物力學模型可用於廣泛的模擬實驗（例如，受傷、頭面部手術和法醫）。研究結果將用於支持可穿戴頭面部產品（例如眼鏡、護目鏡、口罩，面罩和頭盔）的設計和評估。

15606821.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15606821.value: 從社會語言學及心理學角度分析外傭敘事中的創傷經歷

15606821.label: Project Objectives
15606821.value: To collect evidence of the linguistic structures of trauma storytelling. It has been suggested that trauma narratives are ‘broken’ and characterised by voids in the narrative flow (Brockmeier, 2008) but this hypothesis is based on relatively little linguistic evidence. Scholars in the health professions argue that “trauma, by its nature, breaks the continuity and smooth flow of daily life” (Tuval-Mashiach et al., 2004, p. 281) but they pay little attention to how this is signified through language. The research will provide evidence what this discontinuity of daily life looks like in narrative, and the expected outcome includes a linguistically informed framework for trauma storytelling. To identify the contributions made by spoken discourse and contextual factors to the study of trauma narrative. Overwhelmingly, existing trauma narrative research draws on written accounts, such as clinical interview questionnaires or written narrative self-reports, Tuval-Mashiach et al., 2004). This means losing linguistic, paralinguistic and contextual cues that are available in spoken discourse, and which can provide important emotional and psychological information about the victim’s experiences. Because of its focus on experience and how it is expressed linguistically, discourse analysis allows us to study how meanings are attached to the narrator’s thoughts, emotions and actions (Galasinski & Ziólkowski, 2013). The research will study the group setting, including feedback from the audience, which impacts how the narrative develops (Ochs & Capps, 2001), and the expected outcome is an outline of how contextual factors contribute to the development of (trauma) narrative. To identify the cultural factors that are important in DMWs’ trauma narratives. ‘Culture’ as an analytical concept is difficult to define and attempts to analyse its impact on people’s behaviour have often turned out to be simplistic and stereotypical (Ladegaard, 2018b; Zhu Hua, 2014). By applying a discourse analytical approach, the research will identify ‘cultural words’, which allow us to make inferences about the storyteller’s cultural norms and how these norms may impact her experience of trauma. Notions of shame, guilt and cultural taboos are expected to be important (Chan, 2018), and the expected outcome is to identify links between ‘cultural words’ and experiences of trauma. To explore how codeswitching and emotion are aligned in trauma storytelling. Previous research suggests there is a link between codeswitching and emotional expression (Ladegaard, 2018a), and the research aims to explore this link further. There are at least two possible reasons behind this purported link: either that the switch to the less emotionally charged L2 provides the narrator with emotional distance to her story (Bond & Lai, 1986), or the switch to the narrator’s L2 makes the storytelling more emotionally charged because it is more closely associated with the experience of abuse (Tehrani & Vaughan, 2009). Through in-depth discourse analysis, the research will provide evidence for one of these possible hypotheses, and the expected outcome is a new model of codeswitching and emotion in (trauma) storytelling. To explore alternative approaches to achieving justice and healing. Storytelling is no instant cure, but in telling and retelling painful experiences, there is potential for healing. As Garro and Mattingly (2000, p. 1) argue: “Narrative is a fundamental way of giving meaning to experience. In both telling and interpreting experiences, narrative mediates between an inner world of thought-feeling and an outer world of observable actions.” The research will explore different meaning-making processes and alternative approaches to achieving justice and healing, such as narrative justice (Hung & Denborough, 2013) and narrative silence (Puvimanasinghe et al., 2014). The expected outcome is a new framework for alternative approaches to healing. To disseminate the research findings: first, in high impact international journals and books; and second, in talks and reports to migrant worker NGOs and via their social media platforms. It is important that DMWs are the real beneficiaries of this research. Trauma victims are often powerless and voiceless, and work with them must therefore have as its ultimate goal to facilitate empowerment. Knowledge can empower people by giving them arguments to conquer prevailing wisdom, even if only in their own minds (Cameron et al., 1993, p. 143). We argue that this project provides an ideal scenario for knowledge transfer and fostering a mutually beneficial relationship between migrant women, NGOs and scholars. Thus, the intended outcome is that the findings become truly translational and be used to address structural flaws in the immigration system, the power asymmetries that drive forced labour migration, and push for a social justice agenda for DMWs (Ladegaard & Phipps, 2020).

15606821.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15606821.value: Every year thousands of domestic migrant workers (DMWs) return to Indonesia after completing one or more 2-year contracts in Hong Kong or another Asian or Middle-Eastern destination. The research on DMWs has focused heavily of documenting their experiences in the diaspora, but little research has been done on their relocation to the home country. In PI’s previous research, which looked at DMWs’ narratives of return, an unexpected finding was that a large number of returnees showed signs of being traumatised and depressed even years after their return, but they were in a context where no counselling or medical support was available (Ladegaard, 2020a). Research on trauma storytelling is still in its infancy. We know relatively little about what a trauma narrative looks like linguistically, and we know even less about how we identify trauma in storytelling. It has been suggested that the victim’s emotional responses could be used as criteria for determining if s/he is traumatised (Ladegaard, 2015). However, for Indonesian domestic workers for whom resilience and avoidance of emotional outbursts are essential, it is not reliable to look only for emotional expressions of trauma. In health settings, trauma is typically identified through standardised questionnaires or interviews. An advantage of adopting the narrative/discourse analytic approach that is proposed in this project is that discourse may give access to traumatic experiences, which would not be discovered in a traditional interview or questionnaire. The aim of this project is to document the linguistic structures of trauma storytelling. Indonesian DMWs who have returned to their home country, and migrant women who have been deported from Hong Kong because they have overstayed, will be invited to share their experiences in small-group sharing sessions. We will work closely with migrant worker NGOs in Indonesia and Hong Kong to identify women who are suitable for the project and willing to participate. The project will also explore how codeswitching and emotion are aligned in trauma storytelling, and whether the switch to the narrator’s L2 is more likely to create emotional distance, or the switch to L2 will facilitate emotional recall because it is the language in which the trauma happened. The research will also explore which cultural factors (if any) are associated with the women’s experiences of trauma, and it will seek to enhance a social justice agenda for DMWs by making the women and migrant worker NGOs the real beneficiaries of the research. 每年有數以千計的外傭在完成兩年的僱傭合約後，就會從香港或其他亞洲、中東地區返回印尼。有關外傭的研究，主要集中記錄她們在僑居地的經歷，但對她們歸國生活的研究卻很少。首席研究員之前研究外傭對於歸國的敘述，有一個意想不到的發現：大量歸國人士在回鄉數年後，仍有顯露創傷及抑鬱的跡象，但她們身處的環境並沒有諮詢或醫療方面的支援。（Ladagaard, 2020a）。 關於創傷敘事的研究仍處於起步階段。就語言學而言，我們創傷敘述了解不多，對於如何在敘事中識別創傷，更是知之甚少。有人認為，可以用受害者的情緒反應，作為判斷其是否受到創傷的標準（Ladegaard，2015）。然而，印傭因工作需要而必須忍耐及避免情緒爆發，僅尋找創傷的情緒反應的做法並不可靠。在醫療範疇中，通常以劃一問卷或訪談判別創傷。採用本研究中提出的敘述/話語分析，則可能得出無法透過傳統訪談或問卷發現的創傷經歷。 本研究之目的，是記錄創傷敘事的語言結構。我們將邀請已歸國的印傭，以及因逾期居留而被驅逐離港的外藉婦女，在小組分享會上分享其經歷。我們將與印尼及香港的外傭非政府組織密切合作，尋找適合並願意參與本研究的婦女。本研究還會探討語碼轉換及情感在創傷敘事中如何配合；以及切換到敘述者的第二語言時，是否更有可能產生情緒距離，或是否可以輔助情緒回憶（因其為創傷發生時使用的語言）。另外，本研究亦會探索哪些文化因素（如有）與婦女的創傷經歷有關，以幫助婦女及外傭非政府組織改善有關外傭的社會公義進程。

15607021.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15607021.value: 老人虐待會對個人、家庭和社會造成重大傷害。據估計，15.7% 的老年人是虐待的倖存者。我們需要製定和測試適當的干預措施來解決老人虐待問題。證據顯示動機式訪談法 (Motivational Interviewing, MI) 有助於降低家庭暴力的嚴重程度，但在老年人的研究相對很少。我們建議測試一個以 MI 為基礎、以案主為中心和因人而異的干預措施，目的是降低對香港社區居住的老年人受虐的嚴重程度。干預將包括一個 90 分鐘的個人會議和三個 30 分鐘的個人電話會談，由經過培訓的 MI 協調員提供。過程將列出個人目標以改善已知風險因素（身體和心理健康狀況不佳、社會支持），應用四個MI基本過程，即參與、聚焦、喚起和計劃。該干預措施已在使用相同招募程序和干預方案招募的 11 名老年參與者中進行了測試。結果表明，該干預措施得到了好評，對其有用性給予了積極反饋。我們將採用雙臂前測 / 後測附等待名單雙盲隨機對照試驗 (RCT)測試干預的有效性，並以未接受過 MI 培訓的志願者的友好電話會談作對照。我們將在隨機社區調查中從篩選中招募 154 名中國老年人虐待受害者的樣本。我們將評估下列各項的改善水平 --- 主要結果：(1) 虐待嚴重程度；三個次要結果：（2）主觀身體健康，（3）心理健康，（4）社會支持；以及兩個 MI的過程結果：（5）自我效能和（6）改變的準備。由於個別情況及個人目標之間可能存在差異，（7）目標實現將被視為單獨的過程結果並進行相應評估。每個結果變量將在治療前、干預完成時和三個月後評估。將進行具有事後比較、效果大小和 95% 置信區間的二（組）乘三（時間段）方差分析，以檢查受試者和對照組的結果差異。將採用廣義估計方程模型估計兩組間的時間和組別差異，並通過路徑分析檢驗干預的操作機制對主要和次要結果的作用。

15607621.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15607621.value: 移民家庭兒童的健康與福祉一直是全球範圍內研究的焦點之一。儘管影響移民家庭兒童健康與福祉的人口學特徵、經濟、社會因素等已廣為所知，政策環境的影響卻鮮有研究關注。為彌補此不足，本研究旨在考察由移民政策所衍生的制度性福利邊界和由移民自身經驗所衍生的感知性福利邊界，以及移民及其子女所經歷的多維度的社會融合，包括結構性，社會文化性及身份認同上的融合，如何共同對移民家庭兒童的健康與福祉產生影響。鑒於中國境內廣泛的地域差異，及不同地區、不同層級的城市在政策實施上的差異，本研究將在三個流動人口聚居的城市開展： 東部的上海，北部的北京，和南部的廣州。這一多城市比較研究將深化我們對於移民家庭兒童在不同社會情境之下如何受到移民政策和福利邊界影響的理解。 本研究將採用混合研究方法分兩個階段完成。第一階段包括全面綜合的政策回顧，對政策制定者及政策專家的關鍵人物訪談，及對流動人口開展的焦點小組訪談，旨在發展和完善制度性福利邊界和感知性福利邊界這兩個理論概念的定義，操作化和測量。第二階段則將開展大規模的問卷調查，並運用結構方程模型，考察制度性與感知性福利邊界，社會融合與移民家庭兒童的健康與福祉之間的關係。 本研究預期在理論層面，實踐層面及政策層面都有顯著的長期影響。首先，研究將進一步發展福利邊界理論，豐富其概念化，操作化，及在不同情境之下的適用性。其次，研究結果將深化我們對影響移民家庭兒童健康與福祉的因素的認知，從而為設計和開展適切的服務提供借鑒。再次，研究也為政策制定者提供重要參考，厘清政策實踐的哪一部分存在不足，是制度設計本身，還是移民及其子女的感知體驗，並由此規劃未來福利政策改革與發展的方向，以促進移民家庭的社會融合，提升移民家庭兒童的健康與福祉。

15609121.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15609121.value: Dr Chan , Wai Chi Prof Han, Yvonne Ming Yee Dr LU, Yiqing Erin Prof Ng, Siu Man Prof Tang, Wai Kwong Prof Yau, Suk Yu Prof Yu, Chong Ho Alex

15609121.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15609121.value: Insomnia is a common problem among older people. Growing public health concerns have made it necessary to find ways to alleviate sleep disturbance in this population. Mindfulness-based interventions (MBIs) and Tai Chi Chuan (TCC), two kinds of mind-body intervention, have been found effective in improving sleep disturbance. However, the majority of studies have relied on self-report outcomes only resulting in bias or imprecision. MBIs and TCC may represent distinct approaches with different mechanisms and philosophical orientations but could potentially work additively or synergistically if provided together. In addition, the underlying neurobiological mechanisms of these interventions remain unknown. With regard to an etiological model of sleep disturbance, this proposal represents the first attempt internationally to evaluate the complementary effects and neurobiological mechanisms within MBIs and TCC that could help older people with their sleep problems. It is hypothesized that older adults experiencing sleep disturbance randomly assigned to an MBI or TCC program will report a greater reduction of insomnia than those assigned to a sleep hygiene education (SHE) control condition. In addition, it is also hypothesized that the beneficial effects of MBI on rumination will be mediated by a treatment-related reduction of salivary cortisol and increase of frontal midline theta, whereas the beneficial effects of TCC on arousal level and physiological activation will be mediated by a treatment-related increase of the brain-derived neurotrophic factor and reduction of brain arousal level. One hundred and fifty-six older adults with sleep disturbance will be recruited from community-based elderly centers for this research project, which will use a mixed methods design. A three-arm randomized controlled trial design will be conducted to compare an MBI group, a TCC group, and an SHE control group. Assessments will take place at baseline (T1), after the intervention (T2), at a six-month follow-up (T3), and at a 12-month follow-up (T4). In addition, qualitative focus group interviews will be employed to further understand the linkage between an individual’s lived experience and neurobiological findings pertaining to the improvement of sleep disturbance of respective interventions. If the hypotheses are supported, the findings from this research project will provide novel evidence and empirical support for an alternative treatment for sleep problems, verifying the complementary effects of MBI and TCC. Moreover, by identifying the neurobiological mechanisms of the beneficial effects of both interventions, the findings will highlight process variables that could be specifically targeted to make the mind-body interventions even more effective in this population.
