15609321.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15609321.value: 摘要 近年，中國本土及海外都關注中國在經濟持續增長下的全球角色以及其擴張政策。其中，中國鄰近國家的政府便特別留意中國對它們國家（尤其對國內支柱產業）日益巨大的影響。在越南，光是二零一九年一月到十一月期間，中國的對外直接投資（ODI）便高達22.8億美元，幾乎是上年同期的兩倍。這個數字足以令中國成為越南第二大投資者。柬埔寨則於二零一九年吸引約36億美元的ODI，其中43%來自中國。因此，中國目前為柬埔寨最大投資者，且投資額遠超其他國家。過往研究顯示，ODI有時是影響一個國家法律架構、勞資關係系統以及勞動標準的重要因素。可是，尚未有系統性的比較研究，檢視中國的經濟擴張政策、全球生產系統與鄰近國家勞資關係系統，三者之間的關係。此外，亦未有研究有系統地比較中國投資者於不同國家的管理行為，以至被投資國各行動者的回應。這些行動者包括政府官員、工會組織者、企業代表、工人、本地及國際NGO等等。本研究計劃集中於勞資關係系統，比較越南與柬埔寨的中資工廠之異同。無論是法律和制度、公民社會組織、或工會主義傳統，越南與柬埔寨兩國都呈現相當大的差異。我們預期，中資的管理階層會利用不同的管理邏輯，以對應兩國殊別的法律及勞資關係系統。我們亦重視市場、當地國家及公民社會的角色和作用，並將仔細檢視以上種種對勞工工作及生活條件的影響。 此一比較研究的主要田野，包括越南的胡志明市及柬埔寨的金邊。兩個城市各自為兩國主要接收海外投資的地方，亦存在最多外國企業。為了確保比較分析的對象一致，我們只集中研究紡織業，即現時柬埔寨最大以及越南第二大的出口產業。資料將取自檔案研究，以及大量的半正式訪談和觀察。我們計劃訪問約30名中華人民共和國的投資者，以及100名越南和柬埔寨的工人（即每國50人）。雖然研究主題為中資工廠，但我們亦會訪問30名來自本地工廠和其他外資工廠的工人，還有相關的政府官員。這是因為有些研究，認為中國投資者與別國投資者的商業行為有所不同（包括其管理方式、招聘政策以及與本地政府官員的關係）。我們會訪問兩國工廠裡的管理人員。我們亦會訪問本地工會員工、商業組織代表、以及本地和國際NGO員工，理解他們對中國投資者行徑的回應。 本研究將對全球生產鏈、勞資關係系統和勞動條件的辯論作出貢獻。研究亦將豐富我們對越南及柬埔寨的現況，以及中國海外產業投資的認識。研究結果將發表於勞工研究和發展研究的研討會，並刊登於學術期刊，亦有潛力發展為學術專著。

15609421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15609421.value: 二氧化氮 (NO2) 是一種主要源自化石燃料燃燒和生物質燃燒的人為污染物。它能導致硝酸沈積、夏季煙霧的形成，以及對流層臭氧水平增加。雖然現有的研究已經證明了建築形態和社會經濟環境對二氧化氮濃度有所影響，但仍欠缺研究不同程度的社會經濟活動對城市二氧化氮水平的影響機制。2019 年冠狀病毒病 (COVID-19) 的爆發所導致的全球性嚴格封城措施，帶來了前所未有的機會去估算在不同的社會經濟活動限制水平下的二氧化氮濃度和擴散。此研究將會比較香港和武漢兩個代表不同空間涵構和封城條件的城市，論述空間環境和二氧化氮之間的相關性。這項研究將支持政府監測二氧化氮的時空分布特徵，以改善城市空間設計與規劃。 研究團隊會基於各種社會經濟活動限制場景，旨在提出一個用於估計城市空間涵構對二氧化氮濃度影響的時空模型，項目將分四部分進行。第一部分會開發一套時間序列預測模型。新模型將綜合以下模型：具備外生因素的移動平均自回歸模型 (SARIMAX)，自回歸綜合移動平均與廣義自回歸條件異方差 (ARIMAGARCH)，長短期記憶網絡 (LSTM)，和三角季節性 Box-Cox 變換 ARMA 錯誤趨勢，和季節性組件 (TBATS)。新模型將包括五個評估二氧化氮變化的社會經濟活動限制場景，包括封城前、開始時部分封城、完全封城、後期部分封城和解除封城。第二部分會估算和量化城市空間結構因素和二氧化氮的關系，包括建築形態、道路網絡、交通和通風，以及在不同場景下，使用結構方程建模分析空間因素和二氧化氮濃度變化的關係。第三部分會通過增量模式檢測模型，整合交通數據和空氣流動情況和模擬二氧化氮在各種場景下的時空擴散。最後，第四部分為每個場景建立貝葉斯分層模型，識別不同濃度和擴散情况的二氧化氮水平，從而為城市規劃提出建議。

15610121.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15610121.value: 晚清年間隨著改良與革命風潮漸起，以戲劇為革命與改良之工具的呼聲，成為主流。啟蒙者紛紛提倡戲劇改良，希望讓戲劇變得有益於世道人心。但多數提倡者都停留在理想與論說的階段，無法徹底實踐。進入民國，由於政府成立了管理戲劇相關的機構，清末提倡的戲劇改良主張，陸續成為民國政府的政策。在改良戲劇的背景與理念之下，戲劇的角色與文化身份開始發生轉變。戲劇普遍被看成單純的娛樂活動的認識，隨著政府推行戲劇政策，從此有了實質性的轉變，戲劇成為社會教育、通俗教育的一環，給當時流行劇壇的京劇及梆子劇的發展帶來極大的影響。 本計畫將整理1911 至1937年間北洋政府及南京政府的戲劇政策資料，同時探討在政策之下京劇及梆子劇的創作者與演出者如何應對？是否因特殊政策而更動了表演方式、劇本內容以及劇場規範？隨後將討論戲劇政策之下所延伸而出的禁演及新編劇目問題。增刪的劇目蘊含著甚麼樣的主題與類型?對於戲劇的表演形式將帶來什麼樣的變化?以上諸多問題，目前學界均未曾詳細討論，急待釐清。

15610321.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15610321.value: Abnormal speech development and atypical speech processing are important features of autism spectrum disorders (ASD), yet the underlying mechanisms behind these atypicalities remain poorly understood. Previous research that documented superior pitch processing skills among individuals with ASD (such as autistic musical savants) was disproportionately drawn from non-tonal language speakers with ASD. Recent studies with ASD speakers of Chinese, a tonal language, showed enhanced pitch processing in non-linguistic domains (e.g., music and nonspeech domains), but atypical perception of lexical tones. Lexical tone perception is a complex process that involves an interface between pitch and meaning and incorporates both acoustic and phonological processing. Limited studies in this field have not clearly differentiated between acoustic and semantic processing during lexical tone perception in ASD. Moreover, existing research has only focused on isolated lexical tone perception in ASD without surrounding context. So far, our full understanding of the nature of lexical tone processing atypicalities in tone language speakers with ASD are still far from complete. More detailed research is needed to uncover the nature of such perceptual atypicalities in ASD. In this project, both behavioral and EEG experiments will be conducted to systematically explore the factors underlying lexical tone processing atypicalities in tone-language-speaking children with ASD: within-syllable factor (lexical/semantic context), beyond-syllable factor (phonetic context), and higher-level attention. In particular, we will first investigate the lexical effects on pitch identification in children with ASD, with implications for exploring top-down semantic access in ASD during lexical tone judgment. Then, the contextual factor will be analyzed, including the effects of preceding speech and nonspeech contexts on lexical tone normalization. Moreover, using the EEG technique, we aim to investigate how attention modulates lexical tone processing in ASD and examine the time course of such lexical perception atypicality, that is, whether it only happens at the earlier pre-attentive stage without focal attention and/or at the later stage with focal attention. The findings of this project will shed important light on the psychological and neural bases of lexical tone processing atypicalities in tone language speakers with ASD. This research topic will help clarify domain-specific and language-specific auditory pitch processing atypicalities in autistic children from a tonal language background. The research findings will also be theoretically interesting, as they will allow for a better understanding of the existing cognitive theories of atypical sensory processing in ASD. 異常的言語發育和非典型的言語處理是自閉症譜系障礙 (ASD) 的重要特徵，但這些非典型性言語處理的機制仍然知之甚少。以前的研究發現在ASD患者中有的具有卓越的音高處理技能（例如獨具音樂禀賦的自閉症患者），但這些研究中ASD患者主要來自非聲調語言使用者。最近對母語為漢語（一種聲調語言）的ASD患者的研究表明，非語言領域（例如音樂和非語音領域）的音高處理得到增強，但對詞彙聲調的感知卻表現異常。 詞彙聲調感知是一個複雜的過程，涉及音高和語義之間的界面，並結合了聲學和音係處理。該領域的有限研究尚未明確區分ASD患者在詞彙聲調感知過程中的聲學和語義處理。此外，現有研究僅關注ASD患者中孤立的詞彙聲調感知，而缺乏上下文語境。到目前為止，我們對母語為聲調語言的ASD患者的詞彙聲調處理的非典型性質的理解還遠未清楚。需要更多更詳細的研究來揭示ASD患者中這種非典型性感知的性質。 在本項目中，通過行為和腦電實驗來系統地探索導致以聲調語言為母語的ASD兒童詞彙聲調加工異常的因素：音節內因素（詞彙/語義語境）、音節外因素（上下文語音語境） )，以及高層次的注意力。特別是，我們將首先研究對ASD兒童音高加工的詞彙影響，這對探索ASD患者在詞彙聲調判斷過程中自上而下的語義提取有影響。然後，將分析語境因素，包括語音和非語音語境對詞彙聲調歸一化的影響。此外，採用 EEG 技術，我們旨在研究注意力如何調節 ASD患者的詞彙聲調處理，並考察這種詞彙聲調感知非典型性的時間進程，即它是否僅發生在沒有主動注意力的早期預注意階段和/或後期主動主意階段。 該項目的研究結果將為母語為聲調語言的ASD患者的詞彙聲調處理非典型性加工的心理和神經基礎提供重要啟示。該研究課題將有助於從聲調語言背景的角度闡明ASD兒童的領域特定和語言特定的聽覺音高處理的非典型性。研究結果具有很好的理論價值，因為此研究將有助於更好地理解ASD患者非典型感覺處理的現有認知理論。

15610621.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15610621.value: We experience and learn from the physical world through our five senses. The sensory lexicon as a collection of sensory words can hence be considered as basic units of conceptualization of our knowledge of the physical world. In fact, sensory words are among the most tangible and easily accessible shared concepts about the world used by speakers of a language. Thus, studying the sensory lexicon allows us to understand how we interact with the physical world. In addition, sensory words can represent meanings in one or more sensory modalities, including, but not limited to, synesthesia, which involves cross-sensory mappings. Understanding why and how meanings can cross these fundamental categories can shed light on the nature of sensory perception and conceptualization. Moreover, uncovering possible correlations among senses, their modality exclusivity, and their preferred grammatical categories is an innovative approach that may lead to breakthroughs in our understanding of language and cognition. The sensory lexicon, therefore, provides a window for the study of possible cognitive motivations of grammatical categories. Note that the five senses are typically classified according to their degree of embodiment; hence all the above issues can also be interpreted in terms of degrees of embodiment. There are no empirically tested norms on the degrees of embodiment of sensory words to the best of our knowledge. As such the correlation between degrees of embodiment and sensory modality has not been explored. We address this research gap through the Sensory Modality Exclusivity and Embodiment Correlation (SMEEC) database, which links the sensory lexicon to modality exclusivity and embodiment norms. Correlational studies will be carried out to resolve the issues of relation between embodiment and modality exclusivity, embodiment and possible tendencies of linguistic categories, as well as possible correlations between embodiment and orthography, in terms of the semantic concepts represented by the semantic radicals of the Chinese characters. In addition to applications in neuro-cognitive studies of brain and language, SMEEC can be referenced in norming and assessments of cognitive abilities, especially for clinical purposes in the context of cognitive developments and communication disorders. It can also inform the design industry in Hong Kong, an industry which accounts for 13% of Hong Kong’s total exports. A greater understanding of the degree of overlapping across senses, how senses are embodied, as well as their language specific differences could benefit game designers, those working in human-machine interaction, and those working in creating cross-modal learning environments.

15610821.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15610821.value: Dysphagia affects around 8% of the global population. It is a common condition resulted from neurological disorders, degenerative diseases and head and neck cancers etc. Dysphagia is associated with life-threatening complications like dehydration, malnutrition and aspiration pneumonia. Treatment for dysphagia can be compensatory (e.g. liquid thickening, mincing of food, modifying swallowing postures etc.) and rehabilitative (e.g. training on swallowing exercises and maneuvers) in nature. Acquisition of novel swallowing maneuvers may allow patients to swallow more safely with an altered and improved physiology, and is considered a kind of motor learning. Despite that individual motor learning principles are adopted clinically, empirical evidence is largely lacking except for the use of biofeedback to augment the learning of swallowing maneuvers. The present project will be the first to apply an overarching theory to the acquisition of a swallowing maneuver. The schema theory is a classic motor learning theory that had received great interest in fields like sport sciences and rehabilitative sciences. The Mendelsohn maneuver (MM) is selected as an exemplar of swallowing maneuvers as well as rehabilitative treatment for dypsphagia. When executed properly, the MM will result in safer swallows by maximizing airway protection and making the passage of bolus to the esophagus easier. The present project sets out to translate and test the application of the schema theory to the acquisition of the MM in healthy adults and neurologically impaired individuals. Healthy adults will be introduced to the MM and practice executing it using different learning paradigms (Study #1). The events occurred in the swallowing structures and muscles during the practices will be examined using ultrasound imaging. Level of acquisition will be measured by the accuracy of performing the MM in the transfer phase (i.e. swallowing unpracticed bolus types using the MM) and the retention phase (i.e. swallowing the practiced bolus types one week after the learning is completed). The study will be replicated in individuals who had suffered from stroke, an etiology that constitutes the largest population of dysphagic patients (Study #2). Upon completion of the present project, whether or not and how the schema theory can be applied to the acquisition of swallowing maneuvers in the healthy and neurologically impaired populations will be made understood. Further, the effectiveness of different learning paradigms will also be compared and thus shed lights on future rehabilitative treatment design for dysphagia. 吞嚥障礙影響全球約 8% 的人口。它是由神經系統疾病、退化性疾病和頭頸癌等引起的常見病症。吞嚥障礙與危及生命的併發症有關，如：脫水、營養不良和吸入性肺炎。吞嚥障礙的治療本質上可以是補償性的（例如：增稠液體、切碎食物、改變吞嚥姿勢等）和康復性的（例如：吞嚥練習和吞嚥法訓練）。學習新的吞嚥法可以讓患者透過改變和改善生理機能以更安全地吞嚥，吞嚥法並被視為是一種運動學習。儘管臨床上採用了個別運動學習原則，但除了使用生物反饋來增強吞嚥法的學習之外，這些學習原則很大程度上缺乏經驗證據支持。 本研究將是第一個將總體理論應用於學習吞嚥法的研究。基模理論是一種經典的運動學習理論，它在運動科學和康復科學等領域引起了極大的興趣。 孟德森吞嚥法被選為吞嚥法和吞嚥障礙康復治療的範例。如果執行得當，孟德森吞嚥法將透過最大程度地保護呼吸道並使食團更容易通過食道，從而使吞嚥更安全。 本研究著手轉化和測試基模理論在健康成人和神經受損人士中學習孟德森吞嚥法的應用。健康的成年人將學習孟德森吞嚥法並透過不同的範例練習執行它（研究＃1）。練習期間發生在吞嚥結構和肌肉中的事件將使用超音波進行檢查。學習水平將透過執行孟德森吞嚥法的準確性來評估。評估分為兩階段，第一階段為轉移階段（即使用孟德森吞嚥法吞嚥未實踐過的食團類型），第二階段為保留階段（即在學習完成後一周吞下實踐過的食團類型）。本研究將在患有中風的人士中進行數據收集，而中風是一種構成吞嚥障礙患者群體的最大病因（研究＃2）。在本研究完成後，將了解基模理論能否以及如何應用於健康和神經受損人士中吞嚥法的學習。此外，本研究將比較不同學習範例的有效性，從而為未來吞嚥障礙的康復治療設計提供啟示。

15611021.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15611021.value: Social media posts are the most popular and influential form of online discourse. These real-time—often unedited and uncensored—posts reach thousands and possibly millions of recipients, each with the potential for near-instantaneous reposts and responses. Thus the author’s expressed emotion and attitude can permeate far and wide, with strongly polarized content often being both the most influential and the most controversial. Irony, sarcasm, lying, and fake news have become among the most hotly pursued topics in social media analysis from computational, cognitive, and communication perspectives. In this context, it can be observed that these potent comments on social media posts typically involve emotion-reversing linguistic devices when expressing strong emotions. Yet, few previous studies have focused on understanding how these devices (including opposites, negation, and irony) are used. These devices and their effects, while fairly obvious to a human reader, are much harder to identify in automated processing. In this study, we aim to provide a linguistic account of different devices of reversal of emotions and their functions in the context of Chinese social media. Our analysis will take place on three linguistic levels: establishing conceptual opposition at lexical level, reversal of polarity by negation, and intentional incongruity by irony. We will compile an emotion lexicon based on opposite pairs as the foundation for analysis of emotion reversal. We will further investigate the effects of negation on emotion polarity. And finally, we will explore the nature of incongruity of irony involving emotion expressions and their effects. The functions of these three linguistic devices will then be studied in terms of the three types of reversal: contingent/contextual, frustration/rejection, and satiation. These linguistic findings will be used to develop an emotion detection system that accurately captures emotion-reversing devices—one that allows for both the possibility of a straightforward interpretation as well as the ironic one. The system will also be able to predict possible reversal types of the reader. This, we believe, will help to enable a push towards better recognition of emotion-reversing language features, improve the quality and accuracy of analytical tools such as public opinion polling, marketing and surveys, as well as lay the foundation for further studies on perspectives, opinion forming, and persuasion. 社交媒體發帖是最受歡迎和最具影響力的線上話語形式。這些即時（通常未經編輯和審查的）的發帖到達了數千甚至可能數百萬的接收者，每一個都有可能獲得近乎即時回覆和響應。因此，發帖者所表達的情緒和態度可以滲透到廣泛領域，而且這些具有強烈極化情緒的內容往往是最具影響力和爭議性。從計算、認知和傳播的角度來講，諷刺、謊言和假新聞已經成為社交媒體分析中最熱門的研究話題之一。在這種情況下，不難發現具有強烈情緒的社交媒體發帖通常涉及情緒逆轉的語言現象。然而，以前相關研究很少關注於理解這些情緒逆轉語言現象，例如：對立、否定和反諷等。雖然這些語言現象對於人類讀者來說很容易識別，但是電腦自動識別這些情緒逆轉語言現象非常困難。 在本專案研究中，我們的目的是在中文社交媒體語境中提供一個不同情緒逆轉手段及其功能的語言學描述。我們的分析將在三個語言層面上進行：在詞彙層面建立概念對立，通過否定逆轉情緒極性，以及通過反諷發現情緒不一致。具體而言，首先，我們將編輯一個基於對立的情緒詞典作為情緒逆轉分析的基礎；其次，我們將進一步研究否定對情緒極性的影響；最後，我們將探討反諷中情緒表達不一致的本質及其影響。這三種語言現象的功能將從三種類型的逆轉來研究：偶然/語境、挫折/拒絕和滿足。這些語言學研究結果將應用於開發一個情緒檢測系統，該系統能夠準確識別情緒逆轉現象，達到同時理解直接語言描述和諷刺語言描述的目的。此外，該系統還能夠預測其他情緒逆轉語言現象。因此，我們相信本項目研究將有助於推動更好理解情緒逆轉語言現象的語言特徵，提高分析情緒識別應用系統（例如民意調查、市場調查和調查系統）的品質和準確性。同時，本專案研究為進一步研究視角、意見形成和說服打下基礎。

16100921.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16100921.value: Melanogenesis is the process of melanin production in melanocytes, which is a physiological response that protects DNA in the skin from damage, caused by exposure to sunlight. Melanin, whose production is induced by α-melanocyte-stimulating hormone (α-MSH) when stimulated by sunlight, is synthesized within the melanocyte as a melanosome. The skin becomes colored by the transport of melanin from the deep layer (melanocyte), where it is synthesized, to the upper layer (keratinocyte) of the epidermis. The transport process, too, is triggered by sunlight. Cholinergic synapses play important roles in both the central and peripheral nervous systems. Cholinergic transmission has been shown to occur in several non-neuronal systems, including inflammation, stress, and bone development. Specifically, it has been proposed that cholinergic signaling is involved in the regulation of sunlight-mediated melanin turnover, viz., the synthesis, release, and uptake of melanin by different cell types in the skin. In supporting this hypothesis, molecular components of the cholinergic system have been identified in skin cells. Both melanocytes and keratinocytes express choline acetyltransferase (ChAT), acetylcholine receptors (AChRs) and acetylcholinesterase (AChE). The relationship between keratinocytes and melanocytes in skin may be homologous to that of a typical neuronal cholinergic synapse, with the former serving as the presynaptic cell, and the latter as the postsynaptic cell in a “skin synapse”. Thus, sunlight triggers release of acetylcholine (ACh) from the pre-synaptic keratinocyte, which binds to muscarinic AChRs on the post-synaptic melanocyte, with the signal being terminated by hydrolysis of ACh by AChE. This cholinergic signaling is thus involved in melanogenesis, specifically in regulating the effect of sunlight on skin color. Having this hypothesis, we aim to identify possible roles of cholinergic system in dermatological functions, which could regulate skin melanogenesis. In the current study, we aim to answer: (i) how does ACh signaling affect melanin synthesis; (ii) how does ACh signaling regulate release and uptake of melanin; (iii) which AChRs are involved in this process here; and (iv) are cholinergic molecules being regulated during melanogenesis. 黑色素細胞産生黑色素的過程被稱爲黑色素生成作用，是皮膚保護自身DNA 不受陽光照射損傷的一種生理反應。在光照的刺激下，α促黑激素會誘導黑色素在黑色素細胞中産生並以黑素小體的形式存在。黑色素從合成的深層(黑色素細胞)運輸到表皮的上層(角質細胞)，從而造成皮膚顔色的變化。這一過程同樣被光照影響。膽鹼能突觸在中樞及周圍神經系統中均發揮重要作用。膽鹼能的傳遞存在於在非神經元系統中，包括炎症反應，應激反應和骨發育過程。特別地，膽鹼能信號在光照介導的黑色素生成周期中的作用已經被提出，包括黑色素的合成，釋放以及被不同皮膚細胞的吸收過程。與此同時，在皮膚細胞中識別到了膽鹼能系統中的相關分子元素， 比如膽鹼乙醯轉移酶，乙醯膽鹼受體和乙醯膽鹼酯酶在黑色素細胞及角質細胞中均有表達。在皮膚中角質細胞和黑色素細胞的關係可能類似於神經元膽鹼能突觸，角質細胞作爲突觸前細胞而黑色素細胞作爲突觸後細胞從而形成一個“皮膚突觸”。因此，在光照刺激下，乙醯膽鹼從突觸前的角質細胞釋放，隨後結合到突觸後的黑色素細胞上毒蕈碱乙醯膽鹼受體，這一信號傳遞會被乙醯膽鹼酯酶催化的乙醯膽鹼水解而終止。膽鹼能信號因此參與到在黑色素生成過程中，尤其是在調控光照在皮膚上的影響中發揮作用。基於此假設，我們旨在揭示膽鹼能系統在皮膚功能中可能的角色。在本研究中，我們想要解答的問題有：(i) 乙醯膽鹼信號如何影響黑色素的合成；(ii)乙醯膽鹼信號如何調控黑色素的釋放和吸收；(iii)哪些乙醯膽鹼受體參與這些過程; 以及(iv)哪些乙醯膽鹼受體在黑色素形成過程中被調控。

16100921.label: Realisation of objectives
16100921.value: The project successfully achieved all three proposed objectives, providing novel mechanistic insights into how the cholinergic system regulates skin pigmentation through coordinated control of melanin synthesis, release, and uptake. Objective 1: To determine the expression profile of cholinergic molecules in skin cells. We comprehensively characterized the expression of key cholinergic components in skin keratinocytes, both in vitro and in vivo, confirming their capacity to synthesize, package, and degrade acetylcholine (ACh). During keratinocyte differentiation, the expression of choline acetyltransferase (ChAT) and synaptophysin (SYP) increased approximately 2-fold, vesicular acetylcholine transporter (VAChT) by 1.5-fold, and acetylcholinesterase (AChE) by 3-fold. Immunofluorescence and transmission electron microscopy revealed ~40 nm vesicles resembling neuronal synaptic vesicles. Besides, these cholinergic markers were identified in skin melanocytes, however, at different magnitude and profile. The receptors responsible for ACh activation, including mAChRs and nAChRs, were identified both in keratinocytes and melanocytes. These lines of evidence support the concept of a “skin synapse” having ACh as the mediator. The expression of ChAT was highly recognized in epidermal and follicular keratinocytes but absent in melanocytes, as confirmed by co-staining with tyrosinase. These findings establish a keratinocyte-specific cholinergic system capable of mediating local signalling within the skin. This work was published in FEBS J 290:724-744 (2023). In addition, we have determined the cholinergic markers and signalling in skin layer of hair follicles. Dermal papilla cells in hair layer expressed different cholinergic biomarkers. Inhibiting AChE or stimulating mAChR in dermal papilla cells, culture vibrissae and skin epidermis promoted the hair growth. The response was shown to be mediated by Wnt/β-catenin signalling, suggesting the cholinergic role in hair growth. The work was published in J of Ethnopharmacol 334:118585. Objective 2: To clarify the involvement of the cholinergic system in melanin synthesis in melanocytes. We identified a critical role of keratinocyte-derived cholinergic signalling in regulating the production of melanin. Melanin is contained within melanosome, as produced by epidermal melanocytes, subsequently being transported, and internalized by epidermal keratinocytes. ACh is released by keratinocyte under UV exposure, which, mediated by α7 nAChR, to regulate the uptake of melanosome by phagocytosis of keratinocytes. The UV-induced phagocytosis of melanocytes in keratinocyte was markedly increased by inhibitor of AChE, and agonist of α7 nAChR. Besides, this event was triggered by intracellular Ca++ mobilization of keratinocyte. The result suggested that α7 nAChR is playing a regulatory role in modulating melanosome uptake in keratinocytes being induced by exposure to UV. This work was published in FEBS J 290:724-744 (2023). In addition, the activation of α7 nAChR on keratinocytes enhanced the UV-induced proopiomelanocortin (POMC) expression and α-melanocyte-stimulating hormone (α-MSH) secretion through Ca++-dependent signalling. Inhibition of α7 nAChR or Ca++ chelation abolished these effects, and α7 nAChR knockdown suppressed the UV-induced POMC transcription. Conditioned medium from α7 nAChR-inhibited keratinocytes failed to stimulate melanogenesis in B16F10 melanocytes, confirming the necessity of α7 nAChR-mediated cholinergic signalling for paracrine control of melanin synthesis. These findings, which substantiate the “skin synapse” model in UV-induced pigmentation, have been published in FASEB Journal 39:e71131(2025). Objective 3: To clarify the involvement of the cholinergic system in the release and uptake of melanin in skin and, thereby, in regulating melanin levels. We discovered that distinct cholinergic receptors independently regulate the two major phases of melanin transfer: release from melanocytes and uptake by keratinocytes. Activation of M1/M3 muscarinic ACh receptors (mAChRs) in melanocytes enhanced UV-induced melanosome exocytosis via Ca++ mobilization, PKC phosphorylation, and recruitment of exocyst components (Sec8, Exo70, Rab11b) and synaptotagmin, while antagonists of M1/M3 inhibited this process. Conversely, activation of α7 nAChR in keratinocytes promoted UV-induced phagocytosis of melanosomes through calcium influx and actin-remodeling proteins (cofilin, RhoA). Together, these findings reveal a coordinated cholinergic control of melanin transfer between skin cells. The results have been published in FEBS Journal 290: 724–744 (2023) and Pigment Cell & Melanoma Research 38: e13201 (2025). The exposure of UV in skin suppressed the expression of AChE in keratinocytes, revealed in both in vivo and in vitro models. The decrease in the enzyme resulted from a declined transcription of ACHE gene was mediated by microRNAs, i.e. miR-132 and miR-212. The levels of miR-132 and miR-212 were markedly induced by exposure to UV, which subsequently suppressed the transcriptional rate of ACHE. In the presence of low level of AChE, the overflow ACh caused the pro-inflammatory responses in skin epidermis, including increased secretion of cytokines and COX-2. These findings suggest that UV exposure is one of the factors contributing to cholinergic urticaria, a dermatological disease characterized by the presence of large patches of red skin and transient hives. This piece of work was published in FASEB J 38:e23641 (2024).

16100921.label: Major findings and research outcome
16100921.value: The key findings and outcomes address the 3 primary objectives of the grant. Objective 1: We have characterized the expression of cholinergic molecules in keratinocytes and melanocytes, both in vitro and in vivo, as well as their ability to synthesize, package and degrade ACh, supporting the proposed concept of “skin synapse”. During keratinocyte differentiation, the expression of ChAT and SYP increased approximately 2-fold. The VAChT increased 1.5-fold, while AChE expression showed a dynamic pattern, ultimately increasing by 3-fold by day 5 of keratinocyte culture. Immunofluorescence and TEM confirmed the presence of ~40 nm vesicles in keratinocytes, closely resembling neuronal synaptic vesicles. SYP was localized intracellularly, while VAChT was found in a punctate pattern on the cell surface. In mouse dorsal skin, ChAT was highly expressed in epidermal and follicular keratinocytes, but not in melanocytes (confirmed by co-staining with tyrosinase). This keratinocyte-specific expression was validated in cultured keratinocytes, as well as its co-culture with melanocytes. Objective 2: We have elucidated a critical role for keratinocyte-derived cholinergic signaling in regulating the secretion of α-MSH. The cholinergic system, specifically via α7 nAChR on keratinocytes, positively regulates the UV-induced α-MSH production, thereby indirectly controlling melanin synthesis within melanocytes. In an ex vivo mouse skin model, ACh stimulation significantly inhibited solar light-induced melanin production, with the combination showing the strongest effect. In keratinocytes, UV radiation induces the expression of POMC, the precursor to α-MSH. This induction was dependent on α7 nAChR activation and Ca++ influx, as it was blocked by an α7 nAChR antagonist or a Ca++ chelator (BAPTA-AM). Conditioned medium from keratinocytes (where α7 nAChR was inhibited) failed to stimulate melanogenesis in cultured melanocytes, confirming that cholinergic signaling in keratinocytes is essential for producing the α-MSH signal that stimulates melanin synthesis in melanocytes. Objective 3: We have discovered that distinct cholinergic receptors independently regulate the two key phases of melanin transfer: release from melanocytes via M1/M3 muscarinic ACh receptors (mAChRs) and uptake by keratinocytes via α7 nAChR. The UV-induced phagocytosis of melanosomes by keratinocytes was markedly enhanced by ACh or an α7 nAChR agonist and fully blocked by an α7 nAChR antagonist. This process involved α7 nAChR-mediated Ca++ influx and subsequent activation of actin-remodeling proteins (cofilin, RhoA). The UV-induced exocytosis of melanosomes from melanocytes was enhanced by a mAChR agonist and inhibited by M1/M3 mAChR antagonists. This mechanism involves M1/M3-mediated Ca++ mobilization, PKC phosphorylation, and recruitment of the exocyst complex (Sec8, Exo70, Rab11b) and synaptotagmin. In addition, we have shown the UV exposure is one of the factors contributing to cholinergic urticaria, a dermatological disease characterized by the presence of large patches of red skin and transient hives. Peer-reviewed journal articles have been published: • FEBS J, 2023, 290(3):724-744. doi: 10.1111/febs.16613. • FASEB J, 2024, 38(9):e23641. doi: 10.1096/fj.202400146R. • Journal of Ethnopharmacol, 2024, 334:118585. doi: 10.1016/j.jep.2024.118585 • FASEB J, 2025, 39(20):e71131. doi: 10.1096/fj.202502535R. • Pigment Cell Melanoma Res, 2025, 38(1): e13201 The research findings have been reported at the conferences: • 14th International Meeting on Cholinesterases • 15th International Meeting on Cholinesterases

16100921.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16100921.value: As reported in this grant report, we have demonstrated increased cholinergic signaling (ACh stimulation or AChE inhibition) affects melanosome release and uptake, as well as melanin synthesis in epidermal cells. Currently, we are characterizing the skin phenotype of the novel transgenic mice with decreased AChE expression (WAChE mouse, a gift from Prof. Eric Krejci). We will validate the findings with the transgenic model and probe the cholinergic signaling in skin functions in pigmentation. The proposed course of action will be i. Performing UVB irradiation on wild type and WAChE mice; ii. Isolation of skin tissue from wild type and WAChE mice; and iii. Isolation of primary keratinocytes and melanocytes from wild type and WAChE mice, followed by - Charaterization of the AChE expression level: Western blotting, immunostaining, Ellman assay, sucrose density gradient to identify the AChE isoforms, and their expression following UVB irradiation; - Characterization of the expression level of related molecules following UVB irradiation, including skin markers including melaninogenesis-related markers (i.e. MITF, TYR, TRP-1, TRP-2 etc.), POMC/ α-MSH, and the key phagocytosis/exocytosis regulators RhoA. Moreover, with the mouse model, we could explore other skin functions regulated by cholinergic system beyond pigmentation, such as skin barrier function, inflammation responses and wound healing.

16100921.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16100921.value: This research explored how skin cells communicate to control pigmentation (skin color). We discovered that skin cells can be controlled by acetylcholine, a chemical traditionally known as a signal transmitter for nerve cells. First, we confirmed that the outer skin cells (keratinocytes) can produce, store, and release the chemical acetylcholine. Second, we found that when exposed to UV light (like sunlight), these skin cells use this system to send a signal to the pigment-making cells (melanocytes) to produce pigment. Finally, we showed that acetylcholine independently controls the movement of melanin in the skin: the release of melanin from melanocytes and their uptake by surrounding keratinocytes. As a conclusion, we have decoded a new mode that skin cells use to manage pigmentation in response to sun exposure. Understanding this opens up new possibilities for developing treatments for pigmentation disorders, such as dark spots or melasma.

16101021.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16101021.value: 瀰漫性膠質瘤及其復發的臨床治療目前非常困難。了解膠質瘤進化的遺傳和微環境決定因素將揭示疾病進展的機制，從而指導改進患者管理。最近研究表明，復發病例的不同亞組發生了不同的驅動改變，包括但不限於體細胞超突變、MGMT 基因組易位 (Nat Commun 2020) 和 MET 信號通路的激活 (Cell 2018)，揭示了膠質瘤進化的異質性對治療的反應。儘管已經確定了多種分子軌跡，但仍不清楚個性化進化路線是如何確定的，腫瘤微環境的作用是什麼，以及是否存在癌症進化的早期預測因子。 在這項研究中，我們假設遺傳改變和腫瘤微環境 (TME) 協同驅動對特定分子軌跡的易感性，這些分子突變軌跡導致膠質瘤治療後復發過程中的惡性轉化和耐藥性。為了確定引導膠質瘤進化的易感因素，我們將整合和分析膠質瘤中可用的縱向測序數據集，並開發一個計算平台來解開影響克隆進化過程的複雜內在和外在因素。具體地，我們將通過整合多個來源，匯總來自 500 多名患者的匹配初始和復發膠質瘤的測序數據，特別是來自北京天壇醫院的一組新收集的患者數據。利用這個大型縱向神經膠質瘤隊列，我們將使用基於信息論的方法來識別初始腫瘤中影響神經膠質瘤突變動力學的信息因素，並訓練機器學習模型來評估新診斷的瀰漫性神經膠質瘤的個性化進展風險。具體而言，我們將實現以下三個目標： 目標 1：識別和闡明引導膠質瘤進化軌跡以響應治療的早期遺傳因素； 目標2：探索腫瘤微環境（TME）和新抗原表達在調節膠質瘤進化中的作用； 目標3：訓練機器學習模型，使用初始診斷時收集的遺傳（目標1）和微環境（目標2）因素評估神經膠質瘤進展的風險。

16101021.label: Realisation of objectives
16101021.value: Aim 1: To identify and elucidate genetic factors that steer evolutionary trajectories of glioma in response to therapy. We analyzed sequencing data of 544 initial-recurrent adult diffuse glioma pairs to identify genomic and transcriptomic early predictors of tumor evolution in each molecular subtype. Among key features in the IDH wild type glioma, MYC gain and/or functional activation of MYC targets at diagnosis emerged as the top predictors of the development of hypermutation at tumor recurrence. We validated the association between c-MYC and hypermutagenesis by chronic temozolomide induction experiments in isogenic patient-derived glioma models. We demonstrated that, by binding to open chromatin and transcriptionally active genomic regions, c-MYC increases the vulnerability of key mismatch repair genes to treatment-induced mutagenesis, thus triggering hypermutation. We next applied the same strategies to identify the genomic early predictors of tumor evolution in IDH mutant subtype of glioma. Like the IDH wild type gliomas, most of the molecular features in the recurrent gliomas were predictable from their status at initial. Interestingly, we observed other unexpected associations, including that CDKN2A deletion at initial preceded the histological grade change at recurrence (p-value = 3.7e-5), and that MYC gain at initial was associated to HM at recurrence in IDHmut-noncodel glioma (p-value = 0.032). Specifically, we found that 27 of 33 histological grade II/III IDHmut-noncodel gliomas harboring CDKN2A deletion obtained necrosis and/or macrovascular proliferation at recurrence (i.e., developed into histological grade IV), underscoring CDKN2A deletion as an early predictor of tumor necrosis and/or macrovascular proliferation. This observation provided new evidence supporting the latest update of the WHO classification of central nervous system tumors to include CDKN2A deletion as a diagnostic marker of grade 4 glioma. The above findings have been published in Science Translational Medicine (2023). Moreover, the process of collecting data and developing methods in Aim 1 also led to other publications such as Cancer Biol Med. (2022), Nature Genetics (2023), and Cell Reports Medicine (2024). Aim 2: To explore the role of the tumor microenvironment (TME) and expression of neoantigens in regulating glioma evolution. To study the dynamic changes and transcriptional programs involved in TME, we developed single-cell sequencing analysis methods and performed further analysis on monocyte and MDM collected from PBMC and glioma. A large fraction of infiltrated monocytes was activated and differentiated into MDM, which can be further categorized into four clusters, namely NR4A3+ MDM, FN1+ MDM, INKA1+ MDM and MRC1+ MDM. Starting from the PBMC-monocytes, the four subsets of MDM also showed differences in the paths and locations on the inferred trajectories. Nevertheless, they shared common characteristics including over-expression of macrophage differentiation markers (FCGR3A, HLA-DQA1, C1QA, IGF1), TREM2 and CSF1R, suggesting they could be depleted by anti-TREM2 and anti-CSF1R therapy in GB. In contrast, the monocytes found in GB samples, hereafter termed tumor-associated monocytes (TAMo), were more similar to monocytes found in the blood and demonstrated lower level of expressions of TREM2, CSF1R and macrophage differentiation markers, which might explain the limited power of anti-CSF1R therapy in depleting monocyte-like populations in mouse glioma models. More importantly, TAMo followed a different trajectory from the MDM clusters, and they demonstrated a distinct transcriptional profile from MDM and PBMC-monocyte with elevated expression of EGFR ligands (EREG and AREG), pro-angiogenesis factors (LRG1 and VEGFA), chemokine CXCL2 and scavenger receptor MARCO. The expression of these TAMo-specific genes was also detected in bulk RNA sequencing data of glioma patients. In the IvyGBM dataset with various anatomical regions of glioma, we observed enrichment of TAMo near necrotic regions. In consistent with previous studies, we observed the enrichment of MG markers at tumor periphery, while monocyte and MDM were preferentially localized at the regions with microvascular formation. The enrichment of MHC-II-low monocytes at hypoxic areas, which tuned the expression of gene signatures related to angiogenesis and metastasis in these monocytes, were also reported in mouse models with lung and breast cancer. The unique necrosis-associated spatial distribution of TAMo suggested the hypoxia environment of necrotic areas may either be an inducer of TAMo marker expression, or involvement of TAMo in promoting necrosis in glioma, which is one of the histological hallmarks of grade IV tumor diagnosis. Of the list of TAMo signature genes, EREG and AREG were the top two most significantly upregulated genes in TAMo and both are known to be ligands of EGFR. As there has not been any in vivo evidence or characterization of this cell population in previous studies, multicolor staining of tumor sections from these GB patients was performed and the results validated the presence of a population of mononuclear phagocytes (CD45+CD14+) that co-expressed EREG and AREG proteins. Thus, our study defined TAMo as a new subgroup of mononuclear phagocyte specifically enriched in GB and with potential functions in promoting EGFR signaling in the tumor cells. The above findings have been published in Science Advances (2023) and Cell Reports Medicine (2023). Aim 3: To train machine learning models to evaluate the risk of glioma progression using genetic (aim 1) and microenvironmental (aim 2) factors collected at initial diagnosis. Using pharmacogenomic profiling of 69 patient-derived glioma stem-like cells (GSCs) from IDH wild-type glioblastoma (GBM) cases, we stratified tumors into temozolomide (TMZ)-resistant and -sensitive groups, revealing key genetic markers (e.g., elevated expression of EGR4, PAPPA, LRRC3, and ANXA3) and microenvironmental traits (e.g., mesenchymal/proneural subtypes, 5-ALA negativity, and hypermutation) associated with drug resistance and poor clinical outcomes. These features were incorporated into an ML model that successfully predicted treatment response and survival, with further validation using multi-sector tumor samples and external TCGA datasets. In another collaborative study, we identified the E3 ubiquitin ligase RAD18, a key regulator of translesion synthesis, as a critical player in mediating TMZ resistance. RAD18 is activated in a Mismatch Repair-dependent manner in TMZ-treated GBM cells, facilitating post-replicative gap-filling and enhancing cell survival. A genome-wide CRISPR screen mapped the DNA damage response pathways interacting with RAD18, revealing how GBM cells deploy these mechanisms to withstand TMZ-induced genotoxic stress. Mutation signature analysis further demonstrated that RAD18 enables both error-free bypass of O6-methylguanine lesions (the most toxic TMZ-induced damage) and error-prone bypass of other TMZ-induced lesions. Notably, analysis of recurrent GBM patient samples showed that low RAD18 expression correlates with hypermutation, linking RAD18 activity to tumor evolution under treatment pressure. Lastly, we designed a computational pipeline to model glioma progression over time. To address missing data challenges, we developed a novel data imputation algorithm—Iteratively Sequential Ensemble Machine (ISEM)—capable of handling both categorical and continuous variables, performing better than existing methods. We then applied this pipeline to predict histopathological grade progression in a cohort of 219 lower-grade gliomas (grade II/III). Two classification models were created: Model I using clinical variables alone, and Model II integrating genetic and molecular features. Model II significantly outperformed Model I in both training and test datasets, as measured by AUC and AUPRC. SHAP analysis identified CDKN2A/B deletion as a top predictor of grade progression, underscoring the model's interpretability and biological relevance. The above findings have been published in Science Translational Medicine (2023), Genome Medicine (2023), and Nature Communications (2024).

16101021.label: Major findings and research outcome
16101021.value: This research project aimed to elucidate the molecular and immune determinants of glioma evolution, therapeutic resistance, and treatment response, focusing particularly on the impact of early molecular features and tumor microenvironment on longitudinal cancer dynamics. Drawing upon integrative genomic, transcriptomic, single-cell, and machine learning analyses (see Part C), the study produced several key findings: 1. Early Molecular Predictors of Glioma Evolution Longitudinal analysis of 544 paired initial-recurrent adult diffuse glioma samples revealed subtype-specific early molecular features that predict cancer progression and therapy-induced hypermutation. CDKN2A deletion at diagnosis was found to precede necrosis and microvascular proliferation in IDH-mutant gliomas. In IDH–wild-type gliomas, high Ki67 expression was associated with later hypermutation. Across all subtypes, MYC gain or activation of its transcriptional targets at diagnosis predicted treatment-induced hypermutation and was linked to adverse prognosis (Part C - Sci Transl Med 2023). 2. Development of Predictive Machine Learning Tool (CELLO2) The CELLO2 model was developed to predict glioma evolution using diagnostic features. CELLO2 successfully stratified patients into distinct prognostic groups and identified MYC-driven high-risk subgroups. This predictive capacity was validated using retrospective cohort data and further supported with in vitro evidence showing that MYC promotes temozolomide (TMZ) resistance via hypermutation through mismatch repair vulnerability (Part C - Sci Transl Med 2023). 3. Immune Microenvironment and Mesenchymal Transformation Single-cell profiling of glioma tissue and peripheral blood identified a new population of tumor-associated monocytes (TAMo), expressing EGFR ligands EREG and AREG. TAMo infiltration was mutually exclusive with EGFR genomic alterations but strongly associated with the mesenchymal glioblastoma subtype and poorer prognosis. Functional experiments and longitudinal tumor analysis indicated that TAMo promotes glioma invasion and mesenchymal transformation via a FOSL2-driven EREG/AREG-EGFR signaling axis (Part C - Cell Rep Med 2023). 4. TMZ Sensitivity Prediction and Patient Stratification In vitro TMZ screening of patient-derived glioma stem cells (GSCs) revealed molecular signatures of intrinsic TMZ resistance, including EGR4, PAPPA, LRRC3, and ANXA3 overexpression, and specific expression subtypes. A machine learning model integrating these features accurately stratified IDH-wild-type glioblastoma patients into TMZ-sensitive and -resistant groups with significantly different progression-free and overall survival outcomes. This model was implemented as a publicly accessible webserver (http://www.wang-lab-hkust.com:3838/TMZEP) for clinical use (Part C - Genom Med 2023). Overall, the project uncovered novel early biomarkers and immune drivers of glioma evolution, developed robust predictive tools for treatment response, and contributed valuable resources for precision oncology targeting glioma dynamics.

16101021.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16101021.value: The findings from this research open multiple avenues for further development. First, the CELLO2 predictive model and the TMZEP webserver can be expanded by incorporating additional multi-omics data (e.g., epigenomics, proteomics) and prospective clinical validation in larger, multi-center cohorts. This will enhance their predictive accuracy and clinical applicability for precision oncology. Second, the identification of MYC-driven hypermutation and TAMo-mediated EGFR activation highlights novel therapeutic targets. Future work will focus on preclinical testing of MYC and FOSL2/EGFR axis inhibitors in patient-derived glioma models to evaluate their potential in overcoming treatment resistance and mitigating aggressive tumor progression. Third, serial liquid biopsy approaches using circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) and peripheral immune profiling will be explored to non-invasively monitor real-time tumor evolution, treatment response, and immune dynamics. A proposed course of action includes: 1. Launching prospective clinical studies to validate the models in real-time patient management. 2. Developing combination therapies targeting MYC and TAMo pathways. 3. Collaborating with clinical and industry partners to translate the predictive tools into regulatory-approved diagnostics. These steps aim to bridge the gap between bench and bedside, with the long-term goal of improving survival and treatment outcomes for glioma patients.

16101021.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16101021.value: Brain cancer, especially a type called glioma, is very hard to treat because it often comes back after therapy and becomes more aggressive. This research looked at how these tumors change over time and why some patients respond better to treatment than others. By studying hundreds of brain tumor samples before and after treatment, the researchers identified early warning signs in the tumor’s DNA that can predict how the cancer will evolve. For example, they found that a gene called MYC can make cancer cells resistant to a common chemotherapy drug called temozolomide by causing more mutations in the tumor. They also discovered a special type of immune cell, called TAMo, which enters the brain from the blood and helps tumors grow and spread by activating a specific pathway in cancer cells. Using this information, the team built computer tools to predict how a tumor will behave and whether a patient’s cancer will respond to treatment. One of these tools is now available online for doctors and researchers. This research brings us closer to personalized treatments for brain cancer, helping doctors choose the best therapy for each patient and improving the chances of survival.

16101121.label: Project Objectives
16101121.value: Structural determination of G-quadruplexes formed by DNA and RNA G4C2 repeats and their hybrids (a) Current studies have demonstrated that a typical ALS/FTD patient carries 800 to 4000 GGGGCC repeats, while a healthy individual carries no more than 30 repeats in the first intron of the c9orf72 gene. G4C2 DNA and RNA repeats can form G-quadruplex structures which represent promising targets for discovering and designing small inhibitory molecules to potentially treat these fatal and incurable neurodegenerative diseases. (b) In order to discover small lead compounds with high selectivity and affinity to these targets, high-resolution structures of these G-quadruplexes are required and will be determined by NMR and x-ray crystallography. However, we may apply cryo-EM for large numbers of G4C2 repeats instead . Currently, only three NMR structures of monomeric G-quadruplexes have been determined, two from our group and one from a group in Europe. There are many unknown G-quadruplexes formed by monomeric or dimeric DNA and RNA including hybrid DNA/RNA G-quadruplexes. High-order G-quadruplex structures are also unknown. In this proposal, we will determine several unknown G4C2 DNA and RNA structures and their hybrid G-quadruplexes with different numbers of repeat mixtures. (c) In the past five years, my group has published several papers in the field of G-quadruplex structural biology. , In particular, the paper by Zhou et al. ( (2015) Sci. Rep.) has been well cited in the ALS/FTD field. Our preliminary NMR and x-ray crystallography studies have rendered an x-ray diffractable crystal sample for r(G4C2)4 G-quadruplex and solved a novel high-order dimeric d(G4C2)2 crystal structure. Structural determination of G4C2 G-quadruplexes in complex with small-molecule inhibitors In the past two years, a surge of small-molecule inhibitors have been proposed to bind to G4C2 G-quadruplexes. However, the selectivity and binding affinity of these compounds are low and there are no reported structures of G4C2 G-quadruplexes in complex with these small-molecule inhibitors. Currently, we have identified a potent marine natural product, F10, and several small peptides that could selectively bind to the G4C2 monomeric G-quadruplex DNA and RNA in addition to several commercially available compounds that were reported to have high affinity (not high selectivity) to these G-quadruplexes. In this proposed study, we will determine structures of these complexes for the future development of new, highly specific and strong binding inhibitors. Screening and designing small-molecule inhibitors that target G4C2 G-quadruplexes (a) In collaboration with the marine biologist Prof. Peiyuan Qian, we have been testing bindings between his marine natural compounds and our G4C2 G-quadruplexes by NMR, ITC and SPR. (b) Since we have already identified small peptides (<20aa) from TRF2, Orc1, Cdc6, and EBNA1 that could bind to our G-quadruplexes, we will also determine the structures of these peptides/G-quadruplex complexes followed by structure-based peptide design to increase their selectivity and binding affinity. Validate the effects of these compounds/peptides in vitro and in a cell model system (a) DNA replication assay: Biological analysis on the interaction between small-molecule inhibitors and RET G4-DNA. The sequences of single-strand G4C2 DNA templates and primers will be used in the DNA polymerase stop assay. RET G4, which contains a wild-type G-quadruplex forming sequence, will be inserted in the RET promoter and the G to A mutation sequence disrupting G-quadruplex formation will be used as a control. (b) Cell viability assay. Lactate dehydrogenase (LDH)-Cytotoxicity Assay Kit will be used to measure the cytotoxicity through detecting the activity of LDH released from pAg3 (GGGGCC)2/66 transfected Hela or 293 T cells.

Rep.) has been well cited in the ALS/FTD field. Our preliminary NMR and x-ray crystallography studies have rendered an x-ray diffractable crystal sample for r(G4C2)4 G-quadruplex and solved a novel high-order dimeric d(G4C2)2 crystal structure.

Structural determination of G4C2 G-quadruplexes in complex with small-molecule inhibitors In the past two years, a surge of small-molecule inhibitors have been proposed to bind to G4C2 G-quadruplexes. However, the selectivity and binding affinity of these compounds are low and there are no reported structures of G4C2 G-quadruplexes in complex with these small-molecule inhibitors. Currently, we have identified a potent marine natural product, F10, and several small peptides that could selectively bind to the G4C2 monomeric G-quadruplex DNA and RNA in addition to several commercially available compounds that were reported to have high affinity (not high selectivity) to these G-quadruplexes. In this proposed study, we will determine structures of these complexes for the future development of new, highly specific and strong binding inhibitors.

(b) Since we have already identified small peptides (<20aa) from TRF2, Orc1, Cdc6, and EBNA1 that could bind to our G-quadruplexes, we will also determine the structures of these peptides/G-quadruplex complexes followed by structure-based peptide design to increase their selectivity and binding affinity.

16101221.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16101221.value: In all animals with two eyes, the visual system must either combine the inputs from the eyes, or suppress one of them, in order to avoid double vision and perceive the world as a singular whole. In primates, when the eyes have different views of the world, the neural activity from one eye is thought to inhibit that of the other. However, the location and mechanism for this process remain unknown. We propose to use zebrafish larvae as a model system to investigate binocular inhibition. These animals have a relatively simple visual system, which they use to hunt prey. In this model organism, we can take advantage of genetic tools to label and manipulate neurons. In addition, zebrafish larvae are transparent, which facilitates functional imaging in the intact organism. We will first look for evidence for inhibition based on how the visual response changes when the system receives input from one eye vs. two. We will then identify neurons that mediate this inhibition, based on their functional profile and anatomy. Finally, we will observe the effect of silencing these neurons on visual activity and behavior. These experiments will lay the groundwork for understanding how binocular inputs interact in a simple vertebrate brain. 在所有擁有一雙眼睛的動物中，視覺系統會把雙眼的視覺信息沿著視神經傳遞到大腦。為了避免雙重視野（複視），視覺系統會結合來自兩隻眼睛的信息，或抑制其中之一，從而把看到的圖像視為一個單一的整體。而當靈長類動物出現複視問題的時候，一隻眼睛的神經活動被認為會抑制另一隻眼睛的神經活動。然而，這個過程的在大腦位置和機制仍待探究。 我們會以斑馬魚幼魚作為動物模型，來研究這項雙眼抑制的神經機制，斑馬魚以視覺系統捕抓獵物，而它們有一個相對上簡單的視覺系統。作為模式生物，我們可以利用基因操作技術來標記和操縱斑馬魚的神經元。此外，斑馬魚幼魚透明的，這使我們可以進行無創性活體動物全腦神經活動成像。首先，我們會對比神經系統接收來自一隻眼睛和兩隻眼睛的輸入時，視覺反應的差別和變化去尋找神經元被抑制的證據。然後，我們將根據其功能特徵和生理結構來鑑定介導這種抑制的神經元。最後，我們將觀察抑制這些神經元對視覺活動和行為的影響。這些實驗將為理解雙目視覺系統如何在簡單的脊椎動物大腦中相互作用奠定基礎。

16101221.label: Realisation of objectives
16101221.value: All of the objectives have been achieved. For objective 1, to image the response to prey in monocular vs. binocular larvae, we designed and 3D-printed a device to block one or both eyes of a head-fixed larva selectively and reversibly by laterally moving its arms in front of the eyes. We then validated its effectiveness via functional imaging of retinal ganglion cells, and showed that the blocked eye did not activate retinal ganglion cell axons in the contralateral AF7 arborization field. To record the responses of all key visual areas in the brain during stimulation of each eye, we developed a method using an electrically tunable lens in conjunction with two photon imaging to image up to 14 planes at a rate of 2 Hz/volume. This allowed us to collect the first volumetric recordings from all visual areas within the brain of hunting larvae, and we found populations of neurons that responded when prey was presented to the contralateral eye only, as well as a population that could respond when the stimulus was presented to either the left or the right eye. These binocular prey responsive neurons were located in three visual areas; the thalamus, pretectum and nucleus isthmi. These neurons responded specifically to prey stimuli, and the left and right eye receptive fields were centered in different parts of visual space, separated by about 30°, due to the eyes being fixed in our preparation. This separation means that, in a larva with eyes fully converged, most bino-PRNs would be optimally activated by a prey stimulus at the typical striking distance, suggesting that these neurons combine binocular visual information with the degree of convergence to determine prey position before the strike. For Objective 2, to identify the source of the interhemispheric signal, we next searched for gal4 lines that label the binocular population. By doing the same type of functional imaging experiment within the Lhx9 line, we found that the majority of the neurons within this line were bino-PRNs, giving us a genetic handle on these neurons. For Objective 3, to manipulate interhemispheric neurons to determine their impact on behavior, we optogenetically activated the hunting command neurons to trigger hunting. One interesting functional property of the bino-PRNs is that they respond more robustly during hunting trials, indicating that they may be getting some excitatory eye convergence related signal. We hypothesized that the hunting motor command has a facilitating effect on these bino-PRNs, as the prey is expected to enter their binocular visual field after hunting initiation, and this excitatory input propagates bilaterally, which would account for the activation of neurons that are ipsilateral to the prey. Hunting activity is controlled by a population of neurons in the Accessory Pretectal Nucleus (APN), and we reasoned that by optogenetically activating these neurons, which are labelled by a gal4 line, we could ask whether artificial activation of the hunting motor command can activate bino-PRNs. For these combined holographic optogenectics and two photon imaging experiments, we collaborated with the lab of Jianan Qu in the Electronic and Computer Engineering Department of HKUST. Their setup uses a spatial light modulator to deliver precise patterns of light to neurons of interest while performing volumetric two photon imaging. We found that holographic optogenetic activation of APN neurons could trigger prey capture eye convergence and tail movements, and we used functional imaging to identify the downstream neurons. When artificial hunting was evoked, neurons in the Lhx9 line within the pretectum and Nucleus Isthmi were activated, and we further confirmed by prey stimulation that these were bino-PRNs. Our results support a model where binocular neurons receive an excitatory motor signal indicating that the eyes have converged, in addition to visual information from both eyes. This could allow them to triangulate the location of the prey, and accurately place it in the strike zone. Overall, this project has identified a novel population of binocular neurons, characterized their functional properties, and shed light on their possible function in prey capture. Furthermore, this is the first time binocular neurons have been linked to a specific vertebrate behavior, and we will be able to use this behavior to understand the function and evolution of binocular vision.

16101221.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16101221.value: Most animals with two eyes combine the inputs to achieve binocular vision, which can serve numerous functions, and is particularly useful in hunting prey. However, the mechanisms by which visual information from the two eyes are combined remain largely unknown. Here, we designed a device to reversibly occlude the eyes of a head-fixed zebrafish larva, and used large-scale volumetric two-photon imaging to identify binocular neurons that respond to prey stimuli. We found these binocular prey-responsive neurons (bino-PRNs) were primarily located in three areas, the pretectum, thalamus, and nucleus isthmi. We then characterized the bino-PRNs’ functional properties, and found that their left and right eye receptive fields are offset to varying degrees, which would correspond to objects at naturalistic hunting distances for a larva with converged eyes. We also found that bino-PRNs have a significantly greater response in hunting trials, which could be the result of an eye convergence-related corollary discharge. We then optogenetically induced prey capture eye and tail movements, and found that this hunting command activates prey responsive neurons in the pretectum, thalamus, and nucleus isthmi. These findings indicate that bino-PRNs receive visual and motor input that would allow them to encode prey position in three dimensions.

16101621.label: Realisation of objectives
16101621.value: 1. The Ontogeny of Metaphocytes in Adult Zebrafish To delineate the development and functions of metaphocytes, we analyzed the transcriptome data sets of macrophages and metaphocytes in different barrier tissues and identified spic, which encodes an ETS transcription factor, was highly expressed in metaphocytes but barely detected in macrophages. We then generated a spic-specific reporter line Tg(spic:eGFP), in which the expression of eGFP was under the control of the spic promoter. Further characterization revealed that the Tg(spic:eGFP) reporter line largely recapitulated the endogenous expression of spic in barrier tissues. Using the Tg(spic:eGFP) and Tg(mpeg1.1:DsRedex) reporter lines, we defined the ontogeny of metaphocyte lineage. The lineage begins with spic+mpeg1.1- progenitors, which are small and bean-shaped. These progenitors then give rise to spic+mpeg1.1low immature metaphocytes, which subsequently develop into large, ramified mature metaphocytes expressing high levels of both reporters (spic+mpeg1.1high). This developmental pathway of metaphocytes was also demonstrated by the pseudotime trajectory analysis. 2. The Cellular and Molecular Basis Underlying Metaphocyte-deficiency in spicΔ136 Mutants The specific expression of zebrafish spic prompted us to speculate that it might play an essential role in the regulation of metaphocyte development. To test this hypothesis, we employed CRISPR/Cas9 to generate spic mutant fish and obtained two mutant alleles, which harbored a 103 bp and 136 bp deletion in exon 5, respectively. Both mutant alleles led to the production of truncated Spic proteins lacking the functional ETS domain, indicating that they are loss-of-function alleles. To assess the role of spic in metaphocytes, we outcrossed spic-deficient mutant with the Tg(grn2:eGFP;mpeg1:DsRedx) reporter line, which labels metaphocytes (eGFP+DsRedx+) and macrophages (eGFP-DsRedx+) with different fluorescent proteins. In spic-deficient mutants, metaphocytes were entirely absent from the epidermis and gills, whereas macrophages were unaffected, indicating a specific requirement for spic in metaphocyte development. Further analysis showed that while metaphocyte progenitors were present, both immature and mature metaphocytes were missing. Thus, spic is dispensable for progenitor formation but essential for their differentiation into immature metaphocytes. 3. The Role of Metaphocytes in Soluble Antigen-Induced Immunity To have a better understanding of the roles of metaphocytes in barrier tissues, we reanalyzed the scRNA-seq data sets of spic:eGFP+ and other cells in the epidermis. Interestingly, we noticed that il22ra2, which encodes the IL-22 binding protein (IL-22BP), a negative regulator of IL-22 signaling, was expressed exclusively in metaphocytes. Given the known critical role of IL-22 in modulating the immune responses in barrier tissues in mammals, we speculated that metaphocytes are likely involved in the function of epithelial cells and immune cells in barrier tissues. To verify this speculation, we compared the whole-tissue transcriptome profiles of the epidermis and intestine of spic-deficient mutants and siblings Results showed a upregulated expression of a set of genes associated with pro-inflammation and enriched in the GO term "response to external biotic stimulus" and "regulation of defense response" in the mutant epidermis and intestine. These defects are similar to the phenotype in IL-22BP-deficiency mice. Taken together, these data demonstrate that metaphocytes are the major source of IL-22BP production in zebrafish, and the metaphocyte-deficiency leads to the alteration of mucosal immunity and gut microbiota composition in barrier tissues, presumably through dysregulating the IL-22 activity. Following the departure of the original Principal Investigator, Prof. Zilong Wen, from HKUST, Prof. Jiguang Wang has assumed responsibility for grant management. The publications listed herein were produced under the project's original direction, and as such, do not include Prof. Wang as an author.”

16101621.label: Major findings and research outcome
16101621.value: In vertebrates, barrier tissues are the first line of the self-defense system that prevents the invasion of external pathogens. Barrier tissues contain various immune cells, which act collaboratively to eliminate pathogens and maintain tissue homeostasis. It is well-known that tissue-resident macrophages (TRMs)/dendritic cells (DCs) play pivotal roles in regulating the barrier immunity either directly or by modulating the activity of other immune and tissue cells. Intriguingly, using zebrafish as a model system, we recently identified a TRM/DC-like immune cell type termed metaphocytes, which share the origin with epithelial cells and reside exclusively in barrier tissues. In this proposed study, we revealed that metaphocytes of different origins are regulated by a single master regulator, Spic, whose deficiency leads to the depletion of metaphocytes. We further found that metaphocytes are the major source of IL-22BP in zebrafish barrier tissues and the depletion of metaphocyte results in altered barrier immunity in zebrafish. This work has been published in Cell Reports (42: 112793, 2023). In addition, we have also identified another regulator, Spi2, as an essential regulator for definitive hematopoietic cell development and creates a TgBAC(spi2:P2a-GFP) reporter line for tracking HECs, HSPCs, myeloid cells and thrombocytes from early development to adulthood. This work has been published in Development (149: dev200881, 2022).

16101621.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16101621.value: Given the important role of metaphocytes in modulating barrier immune response via production of IL-22BP, it would be interesting to search for mammalian counterpart in barrier tissues.

16101621.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16101621.value: Think of your skin and gut as your body's front-line security system, keeping out germs. In this study, we discovered a new type of security guard cell in zebrafish, called a "metaphocyte." These cells actively produced a protein termed IL-22 binding protein (IL-22BP) and are essential for controlling the immune system's response in these barrier tissues. We found that without a specific gene called spic, these cells are completely absent. We further showed that without metaphocytes, the fish's defense system in barrier tissues is severely impaired. This finding helps us understand how our own bodies might fight infections.

16101821.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16101821.value: Plastic debris in the form of microplastics is overwhelmingly abundant in coastal waters and present in the oceans beyond. Microplastics are emerging particle pollutants that hardly degrade and are relevant to and accessible to many aquatic organisms, ranging from phytoplankton to fish. There is increasing concern about their bioaccumulation along marine food chains for aquatic organisms inevitably take up microplastics from the environment, which can ultimately result in microplastics meeting their makers - humans. The toxicity of microplastics to aquatic organisms has been extensively studied, and the reported negative impacts induced range from blocking digestive tracts, reducing reproductive potential, to shortened lifespans. However, there is controversy surrounding the use of pristine microplastics in experimental studies, as these results cannot represent environmental conditions. The Plastisphere, defined as the microbial community inhabiting plastic surfaces, is suggested to play an important role in determining the physicochemical properties of environmental microplastics, which are key factors differentiating pristine and environmental microplastics. The Plastisphere community has important implications on the transport and fate of microplastics and may facilitate the carrier role of microplastics for pollutants and pathogens. This is an understudied risk for aquatic populations that ingest microplastics unintentionally. The in vivo interactions between aquatic organisms and biofilm-coated microplastics are not well understood. As most of the ingested microplastics have been found to accumulate in the digestive tract of aquatic animals, it is speculated that microplastics, the Plastisphere community, and the surface-adsorbed pollutants are all relevant stressors for the gut, its microbiome, and host health. In particular, the gut microbiome is known as a symbiotic microbial ‘organ’ of the host, carrying out vital functions such as nutrient uptake regulation and acts as the first line of defense against harm such as might be caused by chemical pollutants and pathogens. Gut microbiome dysbiosis, defined as the disturbed balance of gut microbial communities, which may arise from exposure to biofilm-coated environmental microplastics, is therefore a topic of research interest. To address current gaps in knowledge, this study aims to characterize the Plastisphere community and adsorbed persistent pollutants on microplastics in coastal waters. The study will then investigate toxicological effects of Plastisphere-coated environmental microplastics, using the model fish marine medaka. Potential gastrointestinal dysbiosis effects and physiological responses to environmental microplastic exposure will also be studied. This study will provide insights for stakeholders to better understand and evaluate the impact of plastic particles pollution in coastal accumulation hotspots. 新興污染物微塑料在沿海水域和海洋中廣泛分佈，且難以降解。微塑料與從浮游植物到魚類的許多水生生物的健康密切相關。因為水生生物不可避免地會從環境中吸收微塑料，人們越來越關注它們在海洋食物鏈中的生物積累以及對人類的影響。 廣泛的微塑料毒性研究顯示微塑料暴露會對水生生物產生負面影響，包括阻塞水生生物的消化道、降低其生殖潛力，甚至縮短其壽命。環境微塑料表面棲息著微生物群落。環境微塑料與其表面棲息的微生物群落組成塑料圈，塑料圈對環境微塑料的理化特性發揮著重要作用。塑料圈群落對環境微塑料的運輸和歸宿具有重要意義，並可能促進微塑料對污染物和病原體的載體作用。原始純淨微塑料不能代表環境條件中真實的微塑料，因此現有的基於使用原始純淨微塑料開展的實驗暴露研究存在一定的爭議。對於無意中攝入環境微塑料的水生種群而言，環境微塑料對他們的風險尚未得到充分研究。 水生生物與生物膜包裹的微塑料之間的體內相互作用尚不清楚。由於大多數攝入的微塑料積聚在水生動物的消化道中，因此推測微塑料、塑料圈群落及其表面吸附的污染物都是腸道、其微生物群和宿主健康的相關壓力源。腸道微生物群被稱為宿主生物的共生微生物“器官” ，具有重要的如營養吸收調節等功能，是生物抵禦化學污染物和病原體的第一道防線。因此，生物膜包被的環境微塑料暴露而引起的生物腸道微生物群落的平衡紊亂和失調是一個研究熱點。 本研究旨在表徵塑料圈微生物群落，研究沿海水域微塑料上吸附的持久性污染物，探索塑料圈上的環境微塑料的毒理學影響，以及潛在的環境微塑料暴露引致的胃腸失調效應。這項研究將幫助相關持份者更好地認識和評估沿海地區環境微塑料污染的影響。

16101821.label: Realisation of objectives
16101821.value: Objective 1. To make a thorough characterization of plastisphere biofilms in coastal waters. We characterized the microbial community of plastisphere biofilms in coastal waters using a combination of field studies and laboratory microcosm experiments. Progress has been slightly delayed due to the COVID-19 pandemic, and hence we applied for a 6-month extension to the project duration. 1.1 In Lo et al. (2024), we conducted a 14-day microcosm incubation experiment using seawater from the Yung Shue O fish farm to study bacterial colonization and biofilm formation on polycarbonate (PC) plastic. Using scanning electron microscopy, we examined the development of plastisphere biofilms on PC surfaces and analyzed the bacterial compositions. By day 3, early biofilm establishment was characterized by a high relative abundance of Gammaproteobacteria, primarily from the families Alteromonadaceae and Saccharospirillaceae, enriched from the surrounding seawater. However, as biofilms matured by day 7, with denser cell clusters and individual microcolonies surrounded by thickened extracellular polymeric substances and filamentous attachment strands, the relative abundance of these families gradually decreased in favor of Alphaproteobacteria families, such as Thalassospiraceae and Sphingomonadaceae. By day 14, mature biofilms showed an increase in circular and platelet structures, indicating the presence of diatoms and microalgae. These findings shed light on the early colonizers in plastisphere biofilms adapted to relatively oligotrophic plastic environments, which were eventually outcompeted during the biofilm formation and succession processes. 1.2 In Lo et al. (2025), we conducted a field incubation experiment to investigate biofilm community formation and succession across different plastisphere development stages. Virgin polyethylene, polypropylene, and polyester styrofoam microplastics were deployed for up to 21 days at four coastal sites in Hong Kong.We collected samples to examine compositional differences in bacterial biofilms between the pioneering community (day 3) and the later-stage community (day 7 onward). Our findings revealed that early biofilm compositions were influenced by random attachment events related to polymer types and environmental contexts. However, by day 7, ecological succession became a stronger determinant in shaping community compositions, marking a critical turning point. This work highlights the stage-dependent compositional transitions shaped by site-specific environmental impacts, advancing our understanding of microplastic biofilms as microhabitats for bacterial transport. 1.3 In (Qiang et al., 2021), we conducted a microcosm experiment with the aim of developing an experimental framework using strain-level long-read MinION Nanopore sequencing of bacterial ribosomal operons to study biofilm communities developing on microplastics at significantly higher resolutions. Virgin microplastics of environmentally prevalent high-density polyethylene, polyethylene terephthalate, and polystyrene, were incubated in a series of microcosms over a period of 31 days using water collected along a freshwater-estuarine gradient. We found that both salinity level and microplastic type impacted biofilm formation and promoted colonization by microbial communities distinct from surrounding waters. Additionally, strain-level analysis of the Limnobacter thiooxidans population abundantly found on all types of studied microplastics revealed that only five long-read rRNA operon sequences out of 15 occurred across multiple study sites. This approach enabled distinguishing distinct L. thiooxidans strains and novel Limnobacter species colonizing different types of microplastics, which is not possible using the short-read rRNA gene approach. Objective 2. To analyze the adsorption of persistent or significant pollutants on the surface of biofilm-enriched microplastic. Building on our studies in Objective 1, we further developed a pathogen screening database and workflows to characterize the occurrence of bacterial pathogens and antibiotic resistance genes on plastisphere biofilms. 2.1 In Lo et al. (2023), we developed a pathogen database containing over 200 bacterial species from 65 genera known to infect aquatic animals, some of which have implications for human diseases. This database serves as an important screening criterion for identifying potential pathogens enriched on plastisphere biofilms. 2.2 In Lo et al. (2024), we screened for aquaculture pathogen occurrences in plastisphere biofilm to address the potential pathogen enrichment capacity of plastics, and their responses to environmental stress. In addition to characterizing the temporal succession of the plastisphere biofilm community, we found that Pseudomonas and Pseudoaltermonas were dominant contributors to the general higher relative abundance of potential pathogens observed in the polycarbonate plastisphere-biofilm than in surrounding water, hence confirming the pathogen enrichment capabilities of plastisphere. We additionally examined the plastisphere’s response to environmental stress by introducing antifoulant butenolide exposure and found that environmental stress can further promote the selection, enrichment and spread of pathogenic bacteria in the aquatic environment as early as day 3. These findings have implications for assessing the risks of plastic use in important coastal sites such as aquaculture zones for their ability to enrich biological pollutants, especially under chemical stress. 2.3 In Lo et al. (2025), we screened for pathogenic components in environmentally incubated microplastic biofilms to characterize pathogen profiles influenced by ecological succession. Typhoon shelters exhibited the highest pathogen abundance among coastal sites. The dominant pathogen identified was Corynebacterium variabile, primarily enriched on polystyrene biofilms. However, most pathogens were rare and showed fluctuating abundances without significant temporal trends. While pathogen taxa co-occurred with keystone taxa such as Aeromonas, no significant correlations were observed between pathogen abundances and antibiotic-resistant genes such as sul1 and tetW. These results underscore the complex factors affecting pathogen occurrence in the plastisphere. Objective 3. To study the potential dysbiosis effects of environmental microplastics From our studies in Objectives 1 and 2, we found that microplastics can quickly be colonized by microbes from surrounding waters. Consequently, we exposed fish to microplastics incubated in fish culture water to develop biofilms and investigate the potential dysbiosis effects of microplastics on fish. 3.1. To address the dysbiosis-related health impacts of microplastics, the accumulation patterns of microplastics and known associated toxicological effects in the field were first scoped and reviewed. In our scoping review (Qiang et al., 2023), we synthesized the biological and environmental effects of microplastics in coastal estuarine environments. Based on our previous work (Ma et al. 2023), we developed and refined a laboratory exposure experiment to investigate patterns of polyester microplastic residues in exposed zebrafish over time. We not only demonstrated that the intestine is the primary target organ for microplastic accumulation but also found that microplastic retention in fish intestines displays a diurnal rhythm that decreases during the dark period and varies with exposure time, ingestion, and depuration processes. This also provided an experimental foundation to ensure retention for the subsequent dysbiosis study. 3.2 In Lo et al. (submitted and under review), we investigate the potential health risks of acute microplastic exposure, focusing on microplastic-induced gut microbiota dysbiosis. Zebrafish were treated for 3 and 7 days under the same exposure conditions as described in Ma et al. (2023), with assessments of gut histopathological changes and transcriptomic stress responses. Our major findings include stress responses characterized by upregulated energy production and downregulated detoxification, as well as vitamin and hormone metabolism pathways on day 3. By day 7, we observed downregulation of gut epithelium structural maintenance, lipid metabolism, and anti-inflammatory pathways. Dysbiosis was evident, with increased abundances of potential pathogens and pathobionts, alongside reduced diversity and commensals in the gut; however, no significant histopathological changes were noted by the end of the exposure period. This work highlights the negative synergistic effects of microplastic retention on gut health, leading to combined dysbiosis and weakened gut barrier function.
