16103321.label: Project Objectives
16103321.value: Determine the architecture of TMEM63B at atomic resolution Different from OSCAs, which respond to hyper-osmolality, TMEM63B plays a critical role in hearing by acting as an osmosensor that is preferentially activated by hypo-osmolality. The mouse TMEM63B, 832 amino acids in size, is ideal for single particle cryo-EM studies. We are able to purify TMEM63B proteins to near homogeneity with a good yield and stability in solution from HEK293 cells (Fig.5a). Negative staining confirmed that our protein preparation was suitable for high-resolution cryo-EM structural studies. We have already collected several cryo-EM datasets for TMEM63B. 2D averages confirmed that the purified TMEM63B proteins were homogenous (Fig.5b-c). We are now optimizing conditions for cryo-grid preparation to collect data for atomic-resolution structures. Decipher the mechanistic function of TMEM63B A high-resolution structure of TMEM63B will allow us to identify key residues that participate in ion permeation and channel gating, two important aspects for understanding channel functions. Structure-guided mutagenesis and electrophysiological studies will further affirm the type of roles the individual residues play in ion selectivity and/or gating. In addition, to elucidate the mechanically triggered gating mechanism we are planning to capture TMEM63B structures in different conformations including open and closed states. Key residues identified through structural comparisons of TMEM63B in these different conformations will be evaluated by mutagenesis and electrophysiological experiments. Indeed, Dr. Shi has identified several TMEM63B mutants that affect the responding rate to hypo-osmolality (Fig.3c). With these high-resolution structures, we will map all of the functionally relevant key residues in the structure and link their locations in the structure with functions in ion permeation and channel gating. Most importantly, these newly identified TMEM63B mutants with different sensitivities will allow us to capture different conformations of TMEM63B that will be most informative for the dynamic actions of TMEM63B. Determine functions of the three TMEM63s through structural analysis Structure informs function. The TMEM63s share high sequence similarities (Fig.2b) but behave differently in response to osmolality (Fig.3b). Of the three, TMEM63A is the most sensitive with the strongest response rate to hypo-osmolality. In contrast, TMEM63C exhibits the weakest osmosensitivity with no obvious stretch-activated currents [2-3]. Structural comparisons of the TMEM63s, with a focus on the ion permeation region and mechanical sensor domain, will help identify their distinct functions that correlate with their unique structural features. Our preliminary results show that all three TMEM63s protein can be expressed and purified to a higher degree of homogeneity using the HEK293 mammalian expression system (Fig.5-7). We are now optimizing conditions for sample preparations for cryo-EM analysis.

16103321.label: Realisation of objectives
16103321.value: Realisation of Objective 1 We have successfully resolved the structure of TMEM63C at 3.6 angstroms using single-particle cryo-EM, constructing the protein model based on the cryo-EM density map. Structural analysis indicates that TMEM63C comprises 11 transmembrane helices (TMs), labeled TM0 to TM10. The N-terminus is positioned in the extracellular domain, while the C-terminus is directed toward the cytosol. A long cytosolic domain, primarily consisting of α-helices, spans between TM2 and TM3. TM3 and TM4 are inclined towards the membrane and located at the outer edge of the transmembrane region. Additionally, short α-helices connect to the intracellular aspects of TM6 and TM7, with TM7 and TM8 being shorter and not extending fully across the membrane. Realisation of Objective 2 We have identified key residues in TMEM63C that are crucial for channel activity. Notably, mutations of three bulky, pore-facing residues (F542, F543, and Y546 on TM6), which are highly conserved among TMEM63 family proteins, lead to a significant increase in channel activity. Based on our structural observations and functional assays, we propose that under normal conditions, these bulky hydrophobic residues at the ion-passing pore's entry site obstruct the access of hydrophilic calcium ions. When hypotonic conditions are achieved, these residues may rotate away from the pore as a result of TM6 movement. Realisation of Objective 3 In our high-resolution cryo-EM density map, we identified two non-protein densities, likely composed of lipids, which may play a role in modulating the gating of mechanosensitive ion channels. These lipid densities are surrounded by specific residues in TM5 and TM9, located near lipid interactions observed in the structures of hTMEM63A and hTMEM63B. Furthermore, through a combination of mutagenesis and functional assays, we confirmed that the interaction between TM0, which contacts the lipid bilayer, and TM6, the pore-forming transmembrane segment, is crucial for channel opening in response to hypotonic conditions. Our experiments demonstrate that mechanical forces causing membrane thinning can be sensed by TM0, whose tilting triggers conformational changes in TM6, thereby activating the channel for ion conduction. In summary, we have addressed all of our objectives utilizing cryo-EM, electrophysiological and biochemical approaches, which facilitated our understanding of how TMEM63 proteins sense and respond to mechanical forces.

16103321.label: Major findings and research outcome
16103321.value: 1. We have developed a method by applying MSBP in cryo-sample preparation to improve particle distribution and orientation. Our data shows MSBP protects a majority of particles from the air-water interface and mitigates preferred orientation, as confirmed by analyzing various sample proteins. The use of MSBP is a simple method to improve particle distribution for cryo-EM structure determination. 2. We have made significant achievements by determining protein machineries in DNA replication. We have captured the structure of the human pre-replication complex in an open state with melted DNA bound in the central channel. This work unravels an intrinsic mechanism that couples DH formation with initial DNA melting to license replication initiation. Additionally, we have revealed the dynamics of yeast replisome by determining structures at different states. Our study elucidates a mechanism inherent to the replisome that coordinates the activities of CMG and Polε to overcome obstacles such as DNA damage and epigenetic marks encountered during translocation along replication forks. 3. We have successfully determined the structure of TMEM63C, exhibiting structural differences compared to the plant orthologs OSCAs. We have also demonstrated the important roles of the coupling of TM0 and TM6 in channel activity. Furthermore, we have confirmed that TMEM63C primarily exists as a monomer under physiological conditions, while TMEM63B is a mix of monomer and dimer in cells, suggesting that oligomerization serves as a novel regulatory mechanism for TMEM63 proteins. 4. Amidst the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic, we have determined several structures of spike protein bound with various neutralizing antibodies, providing valuable information to understand the structural basis by which these antibodies can neutralize a broad range of SARS-CoV-2 variants of concern (VOCs). Our work contributes to the design and optimization of effective vaccines and therapeutics against SARS-CoV-2 VOC broadly. 5. We determined cryo-EM structure of the marine cyanophage P-SCSP1u, significantly advancing our understanding of T7-like virus assembly mechanisms. By elucidating the capsid architecture and portal-tail complex, we identify an additional valve and gate that enhance our understanding of infection and DNA injection processes. The structure-based comparison and classification of podoviruses offer fresh insights into cyanophage evolution. 6. We developed a vesicle-based method for studies of membrane protein in their native cellular context. This method bypasses the need for detergent purification, thereby maximizing the preservation of the native lipids. It can be used for in vivo structural studies of various membrane proteins across different species and cellular membrane structures.

16103321.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16103321.value: We have successfully achieved our aims in this project by elucidating the mechanisms of TMEM63 family proteins through a combination of structural biology and electrophysiological methods. Our research has provided significant insights into the structural characteristics and functional dynamics of these proteins, which play vital roles in cellular processes. Building on these findings, we are continuing our investigation to explore the regulatory mechanisms of TMEM63 family proteins in response to small molecules. We have identified several small molecules that show promise in modulating the activity of TMEM63 proteins, particularly those that significantly inhibit their function. This exploration presents an exciting opportunity to understand how external factors can influence channel activity and the overall physiological roles of these proteins. To further our research, we will determine the complex structures of TMEM63 family proteins bound to these identified small molecules. Further structural analyses will enhance our understanding of the regulatory mechanism involved and provide valuable insights for optimizing these small molecules as potential therapeutic agents of related diseases.

16103321.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16103321.value: This proposal focuses on a protein called TMEM63C, which is essential for how cells respond to environmental changes, particularly during stress from low water levels. Using cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM), an advanced imaging technique, we successfully reconstructed a detailed map of TMEM63C's structure, revealing that it operates as a single unit, or monomer, rather than forming pairs or dimer. This discovery is significant as it clarifies the protein's role in various physiological processes and its implications for health issues such as hearing loss and kidney dysfunction. By understanding TMEM63C's structure and function, we gain valuable insights into the molecular mechanisms that enable cells to detect and respond to mechanical changes in their environment. Our findings contribute to the broader field of research on mechanosensitive ion channels—proteins that are vital for sensing mechanical forces within cells. This enhanced understanding could guide future studies aimed at developing therapies for diseases linked to ion channel dysfunction. Overall, our research not only advances scientific knowledge but also has the potential to lead to significant medical breakthroughs in treating related health conditions.

16103421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16103421.value: Axon regeneration constitutes a long-standing challenge in the field of regenerative medicine. Given the slowness of regeneration processes and the complexity of the native microenvironment surrounding lesion sites, the delivery of a collection of durable axon-growth-promoting therapeutics in vivo in a controllable and sustainable manner might hold the key to overcoming these challenges. Protein topology engineering has recently emerged as a new branch of protein engineering that emphasizes the creation of nonlinear protein polymers, e.g., cycles, catenanes, multi-arm stars, and networks, through the integrated use of cellular synthesis and covalent self-assembly. These alternative protein topologies deliver functional benefits such as enhanced thermostability, resistance to proteolysis, superselectivity, and switch-like behavior, due to multimerization and multivalency. Therefore, protein topology engineering opens the door to the development of novel materials conducive to axon regeneration. Here we propose to leverage protein topology engineering to develop an entirely protein-based photoresponsive hydrogel capable of delivering a combination of engineered biomolecules in vivo in a sustained and optically controlled manner. The combination will include axon-growth-promoting factors such as leukemia inhibitory factor (LIF) and antagonists of axon growth inhibitors such as chondroitinase ABC (ChABC). LIF is known for promoting neuroprotection and axon growth, while ChABC attenuates growth inhibitory biochemical cues by degrading proteoglycans, a combination of which could synergistically promote axon regeneration. These molecules will be topologically reconfigured into nonlinear, multivalent forms for improved durability and enhanced binding to their cognate receptors/substrates. Using the mouse model of optic nerve injuries, we will examine the ability of these protein materials to sustainably deliver growth factors and support axon regeneration in vivo. By integrating protein topology engineering with materials science, the proposed study represents a unique synthetic biology approach to advanced biomedical materials. A further combination of our strength in chemistry/protein engineering and Dr. Kai Liu’s expertise in axon regeneration will provide new opportunities for neuroregeneration research. 軸突再生是再生醫學領域長期存在的挑戰。鑑於再生過程的緩慢和病變部位周圍天然微環境的複雜性，以可控和可持續的方式在體內提供一系列持久的促進軸突生長的療法提供了可能的解決方案。作為蛋白質工程的一個新分支，蛋白質拓撲工程強調綜合使用細胞合成和共價自組裝來構建非線性蛋白質分子，例如循環、鏈狀結構、多臂星形和網絡。由於多聚化和多價性，這些獨特的蛋白質拓撲結構提供了一些功能優勢，如增強的熱穩定性、抗蛋白水解、超選擇性和靈敏性。 在這裡，我們計劃利用蛋白質拓撲工程來開發一種完全基於蛋白質的光響應水凝膠，能夠以持續和光控的方式在體內提供多種工程生物分子，包括軸突生長促進因子，如白血病抑制因子 (LIF) 和軸突生長抑製劑的拮抗劑，如軟骨素酶 ABC (ChABC)等。 白血病抑制因子以促進神經保護和軸突生長而聞名，而 ChABC 通過降解多醣蛋白來減弱生長抑制生化信號，這兩種蛋白的組合可以協同促進軸突再生。這些分子將在拓撲上重新改造成非線性多價形式，以提高耐久性並增強與其同源受體/底物的結合。我們將利用視神經損傷的小鼠模型，來檢查這些蛋白質材料在體內可持續遞送生長因子和支持軸突再生的能力。 通過將蛋白質拓撲工程與材料科學相結合，我們擬議的研究代表了一種獨特的合成生物學手段來創造先進的生物醫學材料。我們在化學/蛋白質工程方面的優勢與合作者在軸突再生方面的專業知識的進一步結合將為神經再生研究提供新的機遇。

16103621.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16103621.value: Plants are able to sense external mechanical cues, for examples, strong winds, heavy rains, herbivore touches, pathogen attacks, or tapping of neighboring plants. In response to various forms of forces, the whole plants undergo mechanically induced developmental and morphological alterations, i.e. thigmomorphogenesis. Such force signal-induced morphological changes also occur at cell and tissue level. Some such changes are known to enhance plants’ resistance to pathogens. Furthermore, plant directional movement such as root growth is to some extent guided by touch. Root’s growth normally moves away from physical barriers via thigmotropism. However, in the case of thigmonasty, the force-induced organ movements, such as tendril curling and/or leaf movement, the touch response or the direction of organ movement is independent to the source of touch force. Although the expression of more than 2.5% of Arabidopsis gene is rapidly upregulated in response to a mechanical stimulation, little is known about the sensors, subunits of mechano-signalosomes and force-signaling components responsible for the force signaling and mechano-responses. To identify the early force signaling components, we have performed SILIA-based quantitative phosphoproteomic analysis on 40-sec force stimulated Arabidopsis previously. As a result, we have identified a total of 24 force-responsive phosphopeptide groups, many of which are indeed kinases, phosphatases, cytoskeleton proteins and transporters, which may constitute a sophisticated network of signaling components mediating force signal transduction (Figure 1). In this study, we propose to apply 4C quantitative interactomics, molecular genetics and cell biology to study the functions and interactors of touch-responsive MEKK1, the representative of force signaling components proposed from our previously phosphoproteomics. The molecular and cellular roles of this kinase and its upstream interactors in Arabidopsis’ force signaling will be elucidated and documented. We will aim at identifying the upstream kinases (possibly the members of mechano-signalosomes) or the activator or regulator of MEKK1. We also propose to perform molecular, cellular, and reverse genetic studies on these mass spectrometry-identified MEKK1’s interactor(s). The multidisciplinary approach should clarify some roles of force signaling components in the mechanical response of Arabidopsis. The molecular and cellular study of the important major component(s) of the mechanically responsive phosphoproteome will provide information on the molecular mechanisms, post-translational modification networks and protein-protein interactions underlying thigmotropism, thigmonasty and thigmomorphogenesis. We expect that these findings will contribute to our understanding of the complex molecular systems underlying mechanical responses and to the improvement of crop productivity for providing food security to billions of people around the world. 植物能夠感知外部機械信號，例如強風、大雨、食草動物的接觸、病原體攻擊或鄰近植物的敲擊。響應各種形式的力，整個植物經歷機械誘導的發育和形態改變，即觸感形成。這種力信號誘導的形態變化也發生在細胞和組織水平。已知一些此類變化可增強植物對病原體的抵抗力。此外，植物的定向運動（例如根系生長）在某種程度上是由觸摸引導的。 根的生長通常通過觸變性而遠離物理障礙。然而，在觸變性的情況下，力引起的器官運動，例如卷鬚捲曲和/或葉子運動，觸摸反應或器官運動的方向與觸摸力的來源無關。儘管超過 2.5% 的擬南芥基因的表達在響應機械刺激時迅速上調，但對負責力信號和機械反應的傳感器、機械信號體的亞基和力信號組件知之甚少。為了識別早期的力信號成分，我們之前對 40 秒力刺激的擬南芥進行了基於 SILIA 的定量磷酸化蛋白質組學分析。因此，我們共鑑定了 24 個力響應磷酸肽基團，其中許多確實是激酶、磷酸酶、細胞骨架蛋白和轉運蛋白，它們可能構成一個複雜的信號成分網絡，介導力信號轉導。在這項研究中，我們建議應用 4C 定量相互作用組學、分子遺傳學和細胞生物學來研究觸摸響應 MEKK1 的功能和相互作用，MEKK1 是我們之前磷酸蛋白質組學發現的力信號組件的代表。該激酶及其上游相互作用物在擬南芥力信號傳導中的分子和細胞作用將被闡明和記錄。我們的目標是鑑定上游激酶（可能是機械信號小體的成員）或 MEKK1 的激活劑或調節劑。我們還建議對這些質譜鑑定的 MEKK1 的相互作用物進行分子、細胞和反向遺傳研究。多學科方法應闡明力信號組件在擬南芥機械反應中的一些作用。對機械響應磷酸化蛋白質組的重要主要成分的分子和細胞研究將提供關於分子機制、翻譯後修飾網絡和蛋白質-蛋白質相互作用的信息，這些信息是觸變性和觸感形成的基礎。我們預計這些發現將有助於我們了解機械反應背後的複雜分子系統，並有助於提高作物生產力，為全球數十億人提供糧食安全。

16103721.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16103721.value: The placenta is a vital organ for human development. During pregnancy, the fetus relies on the placenta to deliver nutrients, key growth factors and exchange gases. It also functions as a barrier to the external environment. Pregnancy complications arise in cases of placenta dysfunction and/or if it does not properly develop. Preeclampsia is a common and severe condition, which affects 2-8% of all pregnancies and is the leading cause of morbidity and mortality to both the mother and fetus. While many studies have identified symptoms and risk factors for this disorder, the underlying molecular mechanism remains unclear. Moreover, due to the lack of an accurate model, regulation of the differentiation process that produces placenta cell types has not been fully elucidated. Here we focus on how epigenetic mechanisms regulate non-coding sequences including retrotransposons to affect transcription in placenta development and disease. By employing a newly developed Trophoblast Stem Cell (TSC) system, we are able to derive two main placenta cell types in vitro: the extravillous trophoblasts and syncytiotrophoblasts. With a combination of distinct epigenomic techniques, we will analyze the regulatory changes during this differentiation process. Our preliminary results revealed that some retrotransposons have features in TSCs that suggest their regulatory roles on important placental genes. Expanding upon this finding, we will profile molecular changes that occur in the differentiated cell types. Subsequently, we will apply genetic engineering methods to functionally validate our results. Taken together, this study aims to clearly define the involvement of non-coding DNA sequences in placenta cell differentiation and development. In the context of preeclampsia, we have generated transcriptomic datasets from a collection of control and preeclampsia patient placenta samples. We also discovered that some retrotransposons are dysregulated and behave as regulatory elements, whereby they drive neighboring expression. We aim to profile the epigenomic changes occurring at these sites to identify the perturbed pathways in patient samples. We will test the functional consequences of these changes using the TSCs system. 16103721.label: Realisation of objectives
16103721.value: Objective 1: Define the role of retrotransposons in human placenta development During this project, we established a robust trophoblast stem cell (TSC) differentiation system that enables efficient generation and analysis of major placental cell types, including extravillous trophoblasts (EVTs) and syncytiotrophoblasts (STs). Using this model, we generated extensive multi-omic datasets capturing chromatin accessibility, histone modifications, 3D chromatin structures, and transcriptomic profiles at key stages of trophoblast differentiation. Our integrative analyses revealed that specific families of retrotransposons have been evolutionarily co-opted to function as cis-regulatory elements controlling essential placental genes. Notably, we identified LTR8B elements that act as enhancers for the pregnancy-specific glycoprotein (PSG) gene cluster, a family of genes crucial for trophoblast function and maternal-fetal immune modulation. Reduced activity of these LTR8B-derived enhancers in disease states corresponded with diminished PSG expression in STs, suggesting a direct link between retrotransposon dysregulation and placental dysfunction. This work provided the first comprehensive demonstration of how retrotransposons contribute to the transcriptional circuitry of human trophoblasts and was published in Nature Cell Biology (Gao et al., 2023). Building on these findings, ongoing work is focused on determining how retrotransposons influence 3D genome architecture and long-range cis-regulatory interactions in specific trophoblast cell types. We are also exploring whether similar molecular alterations are observed in other pregnancy complications. Objective 2: Elucidate the molecular triggers leading to placental disorder To understand how placental function is perturbed under pathological conditions, we combined bulk and single-cell multi-omics to investigate the molecular impact of SARS-CoV-2 infection at the maternal–fetal interface. Our analyses uncovered profound immune activation and epigenomic remodeling in COVID-19 pregnancies. Specifically, we observed (1) activation of innate immune and interferon pathways; (2) dysregulation of angiogenesis-related networks; and (3) loss of chromatin accessibility and reduced expression of pregnancy-associated genes, including those controlled by retrotransposon-derived enhancers. These results revealed that viral infection triggers widespread epigenomic reprogramming in the placenta, impairing the function of key trophoblast lineages and potentially contributing to pregnancy complications. The findings were reported in Nature Cell Biology (Gao et al., 2023). Our preliminary analysis also suggests that similar changes are observed in preeclampsia patients. This will lay the foundation for future studies. In addition, the integrative epigenomic analyses performed in this study generated coincidental insights into the deregulation of retrotransposons and cis-regulatory elements in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), which were incorporated into a subsequent paper (Communications Biology, accepted, Cheng et al.). Together, these studies illustrate how the tools and analytical frameworks developed in this GRF project have broad translational relevance beyond placental biology.

16103721.label: Major findings and research outcome
16103721.value: This project sought to elucidate how epigenetic mechanisms regulate retrotransposons and their roles in human placenta development and disease. Through the establishment of an optimized trophoblast stem cell differentiation system, we successfully captured the molecular transitions underlying the formation of EVTs and STs and produced a comprehensive multi-omic resource for placental research. Our analyses revealed that retrotransposons are not merely genomic relics but serve as integral components of trophoblast gene regulatory networks. We demonstrated that specific LTR subfamilies, particularly LTR8B, have been exapted as enhancers driving the expression of key placental genes such as the PSG cluster. Loss of these retrotransposon-derived enhancers corresponded with reduced gene expression in pathological states, linking epigenomic dysregulation to impaired trophoblast function. These findings, published in Nature Cell Biology, redefine how repetitive elements contribute to lineage-specific transcriptional programs and provide a mechanistic framework for understanding placental gene regulation. In parallel, we applied bulk and single-cell epigenomic profiling to examine placental tissues from COVID-19 pregnancies. The results revealed extensive transcriptional and chromatin remodeling, characterized by immune activation, repression of pregnancy-related genes, and diminished retrotransposon enhancer activity. These observations offer novel insights into how infectious or inflammatory insults can reshape the placental epigenome, leading to altered cellular function at the maternal–fetal interface. Collectively, this GRF project produced multiple high-impact outcomes: 1. Scientific discovery: Defined how retrotransposons regulate placental gene expression and respond to environmental perturbations. 2. Methodological advances: Established high-quality TSC differentiation and low-input multi-omic pipelines now being adopted by collaborators. 3. Translation and extension: Analytical approaches from this project were adapted to study HCC, leading to an additional publication (Communications Biology, accepted). These achievements have positioned our group at the forefront of placental epigenomics and contributed valuable datasets and analytical resources for the wider research community.

16103721.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16103721.value: The current project has laid the groundwork for multiple future directions. Building on our discovery that retrotransposon-derived enhancers regulate essential placental genes, we are now investigating how these elements participate in 3D chromatin organization to coordinate long-range gene regulation during trophoblast differentiation. Using high-resolution Hi-C and CRISPR-based perturbations, we aim to delineate how individual retrotransposon families influence nuclear architecture and cell-type-specific regulatory hubs. Furthermore, our findings on epigenomic reprogramming in COVID-19 pregnancies highlight the broader relevance of environmental stressors on the placenta. We plan to extend these studies to other pregnancy disorders, including preeclampsia, to determine whether similar epigenetic mechanisms underlie their pathogenesis. Finally, the bioinformatic frameworks developed here for analyzing transposable elements and cis-regulatory elements have proven broadly applicable to cancer epigenomics. Through collaborations with clinical partners at CUHK and HKU, we are applying these tools to identify retrotransposon-derived biomarkers for early disease detection and therapeutic response prediction.

16103721.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16103721.value: The placenta is a vital organ that supports fetal growth by providing nutrients, oxygen, and immune protection. Its proper development depends on precise regulation of gene activity, which is controlled not only by genes themselves but also by epigenetic mechanisms. These are chemical modifications that turn genes on or off without changing the DNA sequence. Our research uncovered that ancient viral-like DNA sequences, called retrotransposons, have been repurposed during evolution to control important placental genes. We showed that these elements act as “switches” to activate genes needed for healthy placenta formation, but when they malfunction, placental function is impaired. We also found that infections such as COVID-19 can alter these epigenetic switches, leading to changes in gene expression and immune activation at the maternal-fetal interface. These findings provide new understanding of how environmental and viral factors can affect pregnancy health and open potential avenues for early diagnosis and prevention of placental disorders.

16104521.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16104521.value: DNA replication is fundamental to the proliferation of both normal and cancerous cells. Some DNA replication-initiation proteins (DRIPs) are overexpressed in cancer cells, while they are expressed only in a small percentage of normal cells that are proliferating. Inhibiting DRIPs induces apoptosis in cancerous cells, but not in normal cells having intact checkpoints. DRIPs are attractive targets for cancer detection and anticancer drugs. Elucidating the mechanism and regulation of DNA replication may improve cancer treatment. Initiation of DNA replication is regulated by a two-step mechanism: replication licensing, then origin activation. During licensing, several DRIPs are loaded onto replication origins to form pre-replicative complexes (pre-RCs) in late M phase. Origin recognition complex (ORC) is required for loading other pre-RC components onto origins. Single-hexameric Orc1p-6p is an asymmetric structure, which would not be ideal for loading symmetrical MCM (minichromosome maintenance) double-hexamers. More critically, DNA replication results in a doubling of replication origins. When and how ORC associates with newly-replicated origins to protect them from histone invasion remains unsettled. It’s also unknown whether loading ORC to nascent origins is a regulated process essential for DNA replication. We have discovered that ORC self-interacts and forms double-hexamers (dimerizes) at origins during pre-RC formation in budding yeast and human cells. We have also determined that Noc3p forms a dimer which mediates ORC dimerization. In S phase, each ORC double-hexamer separates into two single-hexamers which bind to each pair of nascent origins until late M phase, in which new ORC proteins associates with the chromatin-bound ORC single-hexamers to re-form double-hexamers for replication licensing. ORC dimerization and de-dimerization are coupled to ORC dephosphorylation and phosphorylation, respectively. Importantly, preventing ORC dimerization in yeast prevents pre-RC formation, DNA replication and cell proliferation. This proposed study will examine the cell cycle-dependent Noc3p dimerization and ORC dimerization cycles that regulate eukaryotic DNA replication. We propose to further investigate ORC dimerization and its regulatory mechanisms in yeast and human cells. We will determine whether other proteins, ATP metabolism and/or origin DNA control ORC dimerization. We will also examine whether the dimerization of human ORC (hORC) regulates human DNA replication and perform structural studies to further demonstrate and better understand ORC dimerization. The findings are expected to shed new light on mechanisms controlling genome duplication. And if hORC dimerization proves essential for human DNA replication, it may become a useful anti-cancer target, as its disruption would inhibit cell proliferation and induce cancer cell death. 16104521.label: Realisation of objectives
16104521.value: Overall Summary: 1. We used Saccharomyces cerevisiae separation-of-function NOC3 mutants to confirm the separable roles of Noc3p in DNA replication and ribosome biogenesis. 2. We show that an essential and cell cycle-dependent Noc3p dimerization cycle regulates the ORC dimerization cycle. Noc3p dimerizes at the M-to-G1 transition and de-dimerizes in S-phase. 3. We show that the Noc3p dimerization cycle coupled with the ORC dimerization cycle provides three critical function: (1) enables replication licensing, as only dimer ORC-Noc3p/ORC-Noc3p is able to recruit MCM dimer; (2) protects nascent sister replication origins after replication initiation, as dimer ORC-Noc3p/ORC-Noc3p de-dimerizes after replication initiation and each ORC-Noc3p binds one newly replicated origin; and (3) prevents re-replication, as monomer ORC-Noc3p is unable to recruit MCM. This study has revealed a new mechanism of replication licensing and elucidated the molecular mechanism of Noc3p as a mediator of ORC dimerization in pre-RC formation. The main part of these results have been published in Life Science Alliance in 2022. Background: Although many initiation proteins have been identified, the mechanisms of their actions and of pre-RC assembly remain unclear. Several cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) and single molecule studies using purified proteins have aimed to elucidate the structures of pre-RC components to discern the mechanisms of replication licensing. The “one-ORC” model, based primarily on in vitro studies, proposes that the architecture of ORC1-6p is asymmetrical, and a single ORC hexamer recruits a single Cdt1p-Mcm2-7p complex, which subsequently recruits a second Cdt1p-Mcm2-7p complex (Sun et al., 2012, 2013, 2014; Li et al., 2015; Ticau et al., 2015; Zhai et al., 2017; Coster and Diffley, 2017; Yuan et al., 2017; Miller et al., 2019). The “two-ORC” model states that two ORC single-hexamers, each bound to one origin, simultaneously and synergistically recruit Mcm2-7p at a >7-fold higher efficiency than an ORC single-hexamer (Coster and Diffley, 2017). A cryo-EM study reported that 70% of the ORC-bound origin DNA had one-ORC (Orc1-6p) at the ACS, 4% with one-ORC at the B2 element, and 26% with two-ORCs (one at the ACS and another at the B2 element) in either an inverted (18%) or tandem (8%) orientation, and that eight different patterns of ORC- and MCM-bound origins were found, with each origin having one or two MCMs together with one or two ORCs (Miller et al., 2019). It was proposed that two MCM rings are sequentially loaded in a similar way by one or two ORCs at the same origin (Miller et al., 2019). Although the biological significance of two ORCs at the same origin was not elaborated, it was suggested that two ORCs at one origin load two MCMs sequentially, making this model significantly different from both the one-ORC and two-ORC models. In addition to the reports of two ORCs occupying two different sites at one origin (Miller et al., 2019) or two origins (Coster and Diffley, 2017), ORC dimers (stated as 5-10% of the purified ORC) have also been observed, but not elaborated (Sun et al., 2012; Ticau et al., 2015). We reported in vivo data to support an “ORC dimerization cycle” model suggesting that non-chromatin-bound ORC interacts with chromatin-bound ORC to dimerize at origins of replication to enable pre-RC formation at the M-to-G1 transition, and de-dimerization occurs in S-phase upon origin firing (Amin et al., 2020). This model suggests that symmetrical ORC dimers provide symmetric platforms for the simultaneous and synergistic loading of symmetric pre-RCs at origins (Amin et al., 2020). A recent single-molecule study has also reported one and two ORCs binding to a single ARS, and the authors proposed that both one- and two-ORC mechanisms may be active in vivo (Gupta et al., 2021). Significantly, the ORC dimerization cycle model (Amin et al., 2020) proposes that as ORC is continuously bound to the chromatin throughout the cell cycle (Liang and Stillman, 1997; Weinreich et al., 1999) and de-dimerizes in S-phase without a net gain of ORC on chromatin (Amin et al., 2020), both the parental and newly replicated origins at each locus are protected by ORC single-hexamers from potential invasion and subsequent inactivation by histones which have a high affinity for DNA, particularly at A/T rich sequences at replication origins (Moyle-Heyrman et al., 2013). Of note, ORC binding sites that have conserved nucleosome depletion patterns are likely to be true origins, further suggesting that ORC association with origins is required for accurate nucleosome configuration and hence proper origin selection and function (Lipford and Bell, 2001; Eaton et al., 2010; Tsai et al., 2014). Noc3p is continuously bound to the chromatin throughout the cell cycle, probably through its interactions with the four ORC subunits (Orc2p, -3p, -5p and -6p) that form the lower two-thirds of the Orc1-6p hexamer structure (Zhang et al., 2002; Huo et al., 2012; Wu et al., 2019). Noc3p can self-interact (Wu et al., 2019), similar to Orc1-6p (Huo et al., 2012; Wu et al., 2019; Amin et al., 2020). This raises the posibility that Noc3p may mediate ORC dimerization. In this project, we show that different separation-of-function yeast mutants of NOC3 have varying proficiencies and deficiencies in ribosome biogenesis and DNA replication, that Noc3p is required for ORC dimerization and MCM loading at origins of replication, that Noc3p monomers self-interact and dimerize in a cell cycle-regulated manner, that free Noc3p and ORC proteins bind chromatin to form (Noc3p-ORC)2 dimers in late M-phase right before MCM loading, and that Noc3p de-dimerizes in S-phase. Our findings uncovered an essential, cell cycle-dependent, and likely semi-conservative ‘dimerization cycle’ of Noc3p that mediates and couples with ORC dimerization to regulate eukaryotic chromosomal DNA replication. This is the first time since the discovery of Noc3p as a novel replication-initiation protein (Zhang et al., 2002) that the molecular mechanism of Noc3p as a mediator of ORC dimerization in pre-RC formation has been elucidated. In addition to the molecular and cellular studies described above, in collaboration with Prof. Guang ZHU’s lab and Dr. Yuanliang ZHAI’s lab at HKUST, we have obtained purified MCM proteins and made progress in the purification of ORC and NOC3 proteins, for the visualization of the ORC/ORC and ORC-NOC3/ORC-NOC3 dimers and structural studies of these proteins. For further study, we will use the purified proteins to visualize the ORC/ORC and ORC-NOC3/ORC-NOC3 dimers and structural studies of these proteins using cryo-EM.

We show that the Noc3p dimerization cycle coupled with the ORC dimerization cycle provides three critical function: (1) enables replication licensing, as only the (ORC-Noc3p)-(ORC-Noc3p) dimer is able to recruit the MCM dimer; (2) protects nascent sister replication origins after replication initiation, as the (ORC-Noc3p)-(ORC-Noc3p) dimer de-dimerizes after replication initiation and each ORC-Noc3p monomer binds one newly replicated origin; and (3) prevents re-replication, as monomer ORC-Noc3p is unable to recruit MCM. 4. We also show that human ORC and NOC3 form ORC-ORC and NOC3-NOC3 dimers, respectively. This study has revealed a new mechanism of replication licensing and elucidated the molecular mechanism of Noc3p as a mediator of ORC dimerization in pre-RC formation. The main part of these results have been published in Life Science Alliance in 2022. Achievements: In this project, we show that different separation-of-function yeast mutants of NOC3 have varying proficiencies and deficiencies in ribosome biogenesis and DNA replication, that Noc3p is required for ORC dimerization and MCM loading at origins of replication, that Noc3p monomers self-interact and dimerize in a cell cycle-regulated manner, that free Noc3p and ORC proteins bind chromatin to form (Noc3p-ORC)- (Noc3p-ORC) dimers in late M-phase right before MCM loading, and that Noc3p de-dimerizes in S-phase. Our findings uncovered an essential, cell cycle-dependent, and likely semi-conservative ‘dimerization cycle’ of Noc3p that mediates and couples with ORC dimerization to regulate eukaryotic chromosomal DNA replication. This is the first time since the discovery of Noc3p as a novel replication-initiation protein (Zhang et al., 2002) that the molecular mechanism of Noc3p as a mediator of ORC dimerization in pre-RC formation has been elucidated. In addition to the molecular and cellular studies described above, in collaboration with Prof. Guang ZHU’s lab, Dr. Shangyu DANG, and Dr. Yuanliang ZHAI’s lab at HKUST, we have made progress in the purification of ORC and NOC3 proteins, for the visualization of the ORC-ORC and (Noc3p-ORC)-(Noc3p-ORC) dimers and structural studies of these proteins.

In the near future, we will use the purified proteins to visualize the ORC/ORC and ORC-NOC3/ORC-NOC3 dimers and structural studies of these proteins using cryo-EM.

16104521.value: Noc3p was identified as ribosome biogenesis protein by others in 2001, and we identified it also as a replication-initiation protein (Cell, 2022). Now we used budding yeast separation-of-function NOC3 mutants to confirm the separable roles of Noc3p in DNA replication and ribosome biogenesis (Life Science Alliance, 2023). We also show that an essential and cell cycle-dependent Noc3p dimerization cycle regulates the ORC dimerization cycle, which was discovered by us (Cell Reports, 2000). Noc3p dimerizes, forming a Noc3p-Noc3p complex, at the M-to-G1 transition and de-dimerizes in S-phase. This study has revealed a new mechanism of replication licensing and elucidated the molecular mechanism of Noc3p as a mediator of ORC dimerization in pre-RC formation. The main part of these results have been published in Life Science Alliance in 2023.

16104621.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16104621.value: 成体干细胞能够自我更新和同时不断产生有功能的后代细胞来维持组织的平衡稳态。它们在治疗退行性疾病，糖尿病和癌症等各种人类疾病中有很大的潜能。为了能够发挥干细胞最大临床应用潜能，我们需要对干细胞自我更新和分化的分子控制机制有更好的了解。虽然在干细胞自我更新和分化研究方面取得很大的进展，但是从自我更新到分化的转换过程（STDS）仍然知之甚少， 也是干细胞领域里最重要问题之一。果蝇卵巢生殖干细胞在组织中可以利用其位置和分子标记很容易与分化的后代细胞有效区分， 对研究干细胞的STDS是一个非常有利的系统。Rbp9蛋白是具有3个RNA结合膜体（RNA recognition motifs or RRMs）的高保守RNA结合蛋白Elavl家族成员。以前已发表工作显示，Rbp9蛋白能够调控果蝇卵巢生殖干细胞分化过程。我们前期研究结果发现：1) Rbp9 通过与分化的主要因子BAM蛋白相互作用来调控果蝇卵巢生殖干细胞的STDS；2) Rbp9 调控生殖干细胞的早期后代细胞中mRNA的翻译; 3) Rbp9 在培养果蝇卵巢生殖干细胞中与34个蛋白有特异性的结合（包括翻译调控蛋白，mRNA剪接调控蛋白，RNA结合蛋白以及其它蛋白）， 还与241个不同mRNAs有特异性结合; 4) 小鼠 Rbp9 同源蛋白Elavl2和 Elavl4也在小鼠的睾丸生殖干细胞的早期后代细胞中特异性表达, 更为惊喜的是能够成功替代Rbp9在果蝇中调控卵巢生殖干细胞的STDS。 该研究项目的长远目标是，在分子和细胞水平上能够更好地理解Elavl家族蛋白Rbp9如何控制果蝇卵巢生殖干细胞的STDS。它的两个具体的目标是研究Rbp9如何与不同RNA结合蛋白调控目的mRNA的翻译来控制生殖干细胞的STDS。小鼠的Elavl2/4 蛋白完全可以代替Rbp9的生殖干细胞后代细胞分化的功能，因此该项目研究发现会对果蝇卵巢和小鼠睾丸的生殖干细胞的STDS提供独到的见解。因为控制STDS的分子机制对不同组织干细胞都非常重要，该项目的发现对更好理解干细胞如何维持组织平衡态以及对干细胞治疗退行性疾病，糖尿病，癌症和不育症都是至关重要的。

16104621.label: Realisation of objectives
16104621.value: During the funded period, we have successfully realized all the major objectives, which are summarized as follows: Aim 1. To investigate the functions of Rbp9-associated mRNAs in controlling the GSC STDS in the Drosophila ovary. Aim 1a. To investigate if Rbp9 promotes the translation of differentiation regulator bam and Sxl in CBs/MCs via direct 3’UTR binding In this study, we have demonstrated that RBP9 directly controls BAM protein expression in cystoblasts (CBs) and mitotic cysts (MCs) by regulating translation through three RBP9 binding sites in the bam 3’UTR. First, the bam 3’UTR is sufficient to determine BAM protein expression in CBs/MCs using a GFP reporter. Second, the RBP9 site-deleted bam 3’UTR leads to the loss of BAM protein expression, but does not affect mRNA expression, in CBs/MCs, indicating that RBP9 controls BAM protein expression in CBs/MCs via translational regulation. Third, the bam 3’UTR with the RBP9 sites mutated also causes the loss of BAM protein expression in CBs/MCs, further demonstrating the importance of direct RBP9 binding in controlling BAM protein. These results demonstrate that RBP9 controls BAM protein expression via translational regulation. In addition, we have also investigated whether RBP9 also regulates the translation of Sxl and mei-P26, two known differentiation factors, in early GSC progeny. Sxl and mei-P26 have 34 and 19 RBP9 binding sites on their 3’UTRs, which are clustered together. Both the 3’UTRs of Sxl and mei-P26 can sufficiently recapitulate their protein expression in early GSC progeny using the GFP reporter, indicating that their protein expression is primarily controlled post-transcriptionally. Either the Sxl 3’UTR or the mei-P26 3’UTR, which deletes the region containing RBP9 binding sites, can no longer support the normal expression patterns of SXL or MEI-P26 protein in early GSC progeny, suggesting that RBP9 binding is critical for the proper protein expression of SXL and MEI-P26 in early GSC progeny. Interestingly, the deletion of RBP9 binding sites accordingly affects mRNA and protein expression patterns, indicating that RBP9 controls their protein expression via regulation of mRNA stability instead of translation. These results demonstrate that RBP9 controls the expression of its target genes in modulating STDS by regulating mRNA stability and translation. Aim 1b. To study the functions of Rbp9-associated mRNAs in regulating the GSC STDS. In this study, we have used RNA iCLIP to identify 415 mRNAs as direct RBP9 targets, including bam, Sxl, mei-P26, mad, dm, and Rbp9 itself. In addition, 15 other genes have also been studied previously required for GSC self-renewal or differentiation, such as aret and stet. Among all these previously studied genes, 8, 7, and 6 are required for GSC self-renewal, CB differentiation, and both, respectively. By screening the remaining 394 genes, we have identified 38, 5, and 2 genes for their requirements for controlling GSC self-renewal, CB differentiation, and both, respectively. These results indicate that RBP9 controls GSC progeny differentiation by repressing the expression of self-renewal factors and promoting the expression of differentiation factors. These findings have further enriched our current understanding of how stem cell self-renewal and differentiation. Aim 2. To investigate how Rbp9 regulates the translation of differentiation factors for promoting the GSC STDS in the Drosophila ovary Aim 2a. To investigate if Rbp9 controls the GSC STDS by recruiting RNA-binding differentiation factor Bam, Bgcn and Sxl Since BAM, BGCN, SXL, and RBP9 are all expressed in early GSC progeny and required for GSC progeny differentiation, we have been motivated to investigate whether RBP9 directly recruits BAM, BGCN, and SXL to control its target gene expression. In S2 cells, our co-IP results show that RBP9 can pull down SXL and weakly BAM and BGCN in the presence of RNA. However, RBP9 can no longer bring down SXL, BAM, and BGCN in the absence of RNA (cell extracts are treated with RNAse I before performing co-IP experiments), suggesting that RBP9 does not directly recruit SXL, BAM, or BGCN. However, our results do not exclude the possibility that RBP9 can bind to the same RNA targets with SXL, BAM or BGCN to regulate their expression collaboratively. Aim 2b. To investigate if Rbp9 promotes the translation of Bam and Sxl in CBs/MCs by directly recruiting translation initiation factors To study how RBP9 controls the translation of bam, we have investigated whether RBP9 directly recruits translation initiation factors. Our previous studies have shown that RNA-binding proteins BAM and AUB regulate the translation of their target mRNAs by directly recruiting translation initiation factors, eIF4 and pABP (polyA binding protein). The eIF4 complex is composed of eIF4G, eIF4A, and eIF4E. In S2 cells, our co-IP results show that RBP9 can pull down eIF4A, eIF4E1, and pABP, suggesting that RBP9 forms protein complexes with eIF4 and pABP. To further investigate if RBP9 directly interacts with eIF4 components or pABP, we have used purified bacterially expressed RBP9, eIF4A, eIF4E1, and pABP to show that RBP9 can directly bind to eIF4E1 and pABP, but not eIF4A. Our results indicate that RBP9 controls BAM protein expression via regulation of translation initiation by directly recruiting eIF4E1 and pABP. Aim 2c. To investigate the functions of Rbp9-associated proteins in regulating the GSC STDS Among the RBP9-associated proteins, 13 RNA-binding proteins, 3 splicing factors, and 9 other proteins have not previously been determined for their functions in the regulation of GSC self-renewal and differentiation. We have used RNAi to knock down their expression in GSCs and their progeny to show that 8 of them are required for controlling STDS, while one gene is required for GSC self-renewal. We will continue to investigate their detailed molecular mechanisms in the regulation of STDS. In addition to finishing all the planned objectives, we have gone beyond our initial plan to explore the function of individual RNA-binding domains, RRM1-3, in the control of STDS. By expressing different RRM domain deletions and individual RRM domains, we have demonstrated that RRM1 is critical for STDS control, whereas RRM3 functions as a dominant-negative. Interestingly, ELAVL2 and ELAVL4, two orthologs of Drosophila RBP9, are also expressed in early GSC progeny, but not in GSCs, of the mouse testis. Furthermore, we have also demonstrated that mouse ELAVL2 and ELAVL4 can functionally replace RBP9 in the Drosophila ovary to control STDS. These results demonstrate that RBP9 function in the control of GSC differentiation is conserved from Drosophila to mammals. In summary, this study has made important contributions to a better understanding of the molecular control of stem cell progeny differentiation, which could enhance our ability to use stem cells to treat devastating human diseases, such as Parkinson’s and Alzheimer’s diseases.

16104621.label: Major findings and research outcome
16104621.value: Adult stem cells can self-renew and continuously produce functional cells for maintaining tissue homeostasis. As an essential step of generating functional cells, stem cells must undergo the self-renewal-to-differentiation switch (STDS), which terminates self-renewal and initiates differentiation. However, the genetic control of the STDS remains poorly understood. In this study, we use germline stem cells (GSCs) in the Drosophila ovary as a model to show that ELAVL family member RBP9 is required intrinsically to control STDS partly by regulating translation. Our genetic results show that RBP9 is necessary and sufficient to drive STDS in BAM-dependent and -independent manners. Among RBP9’s three RRM domains, only the first two RRMs are critical for controlling the STDS. Our iCLIP results have identified 415 target mRNAs in cultured GSCs and immediate daughters, in which most binding sites are in 3’UTRs, including those encoding known differentiation factors. Interestingly, RBP9 binding to the 3’UTR is critical for translationally promoting the expression of BAM by directly interacting with eIF4E1 and PABP. RBP9 controls differentiation factor MEI-P26 expression, likely by regulating mRNA stability. Finally, its mammalian homologs, ELAVL2 and ELAVL4, can functionally replace RBP9 in Drosophila to drive the STDS. Therefore, this study has provided important insights into RBP9 function in controlling STDS. The knowledge gained from this study should be critical for treating degenerative diseases, diabetes, cancer, and infertility.

16104621.value: In the future, we will continue to investigate the functions of some of the identified RBP9 target mRNAs and RBP9-interacting proteins.

16104621.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16104621.value: Adult stem cells can self-renew and continuously produce functional cells for maintaining tissue homeostasis and for treating various human diseases. As an essential step of generating functional cells, stem cells must undergo the self-renewal-to-differentiation switch (STDS), which terminates self-renewal and initiates differentiation, and then proceed to gradually produce functional cells. However, the genetic and molecular control of the STDS remains poorly understood. In this study, we use germline stem cells (GSCs) in the Drosophila ovary as a model, in which over 80% of important human disease genes can be found, to show that ELAVL family member RBP9 is required intrinsically in stem cell progeny to control STDS partly by regulating translation. ELAVL2 and ELAVL4, the mammalian homologs of RBP9, can functionally replace RBP9 in Drosophila to drive the STDS. Therefore, this study has provided important insights into RBP9 function in controlling the generation of functional cells from stem cells. The knowledge gained from this study should be critical for treating degenerative diseases, diabetes, cancer, and infertility.

16200021.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16200021.value: The flurry of recent artificial intelligence (AI) research has made significant performance breakthroughs in diverse areas of science and engineering, and changed the landscape of industries from manufacturing all the way to healthcare. In particular, deep learning has powered the rise of AI to near human-level understanding of images, text, and speech. China has committed itself to becoming the world’s premier AI innovation center by the year 2030. Reaching this goal will create an enormous amount of economic value. China is already home to many of the world's top AI companies. However, reaching the status of the world’s premier AI innovation center will require more high-impact problems to be solved. The goal of the proposed project is to address key issues related to anomaly detection in time series data. This is crucial in industrial applications such as industrial internet of things, smart manufacturing and the energy sectors, as well as in web services, finance, e-commerce, and social media. Previous ground-breaking work in processing time series has been deployed to billions of smart phones around the world. Pushing the boundaries of AI understanding of time series data is without a doubt a high-impact problem. It is entirely possible that the proposed project could change the way time series data is processed across every industry. Historically, there has been a great amount of effort focused on anomaly detection in time series data. Unfortunately, even the latest anomaly detection research is plagued by a high false positive rate. Major challenges in anomaly detection with time series data can largely be described in three ways. (1) real-world time series data have highly nonlinear temporal dynamics. (2) anomalies are rare, and (3) anomalies are constantly changing. In this project, we will leverage state-of-the-art research from AI and machine learning to address issues in time series anomaly detection. Existing shortcomings stem from fundamental flaws which limit the amount of information these models can capture in time series data. We will (i) develop powerful new deep learning models, based on the recent transformer architecture that power most advanced deep models (including the phenomenal GPT-3 from OpenAI); (ii) use unsupervised learning to combat the problem of rarity; and (iii) incorporate online learning so that the model can be continually updated. We believe this combination will lead to breakthroughs in time series anomaly detection performance. 近年来，关于人工智能的研究在科学、工程等各个领域都取得了巨大的进展，并给许多行业（如制造业、医疗保健等）带来了重大改变。特别是以深度学习为代表的人工智能技术已经在图像视觉、文本理解以及语音分析等诸多领域接近人类的水平。发展先进的人工智能技术已经成为推动社会经济发展的新关键。在中国的最新发展规划中，中国将投入大量资金支持人工智能力技术的发展并且力争到2030年成为人工智能领域的世界领导者。现阶段的中国已经拥有了世界顶级人工智能公司。然而，要达到世界一流人工智能创新中心的伟大目标，还有许多具有挑战性、高影响力的难题要攻克。 本项目的目标在于解决面向时间序列数据的异常检测任务相关的技术难题。这对于工业物联网、智能制造和能源领域等工业应用以及网络服务、金融、电子商务和社交媒体的发展都是至关重要。之前在时间序列数据的开创性工作已经部署到了全球数十亿部智能手机上。如何利用前沿的人工智能技术进一步理解复杂的时间序列数据已经成为一个很有影响力的研究问题。 本项目的研究工作完全有可能会给每个行业处理时间序列数据的方式带来更准确、更高效的性能提升。 在过去几十年里，已经有了大量的研究侧重于时间序列的异常检测任务上。然而，即使是最新的异常检测技术也不可避免的存在高误报率的困扰。针对现实时间序列数据进行异常检测的主要挑战主要有三点： (1) 真实世界的时间序列数据往往具有高度非线性的动态变化；(2) 数据包含的异常点通常是稀少的； (3) 异常数据的模式规律也会随时间不断变化。 在本项目中，我们将利用人工智能和机器学习领域中的前沿技术来解决面向时间序列的异常检测难题。现有技术的局限性主要在于方法本身，这使得现有技术在时间序列数据中可以挖掘的信息量是有限的。不同于现有技术，我们将（1）基于人工智能领域中最新的 Transformer 架构提升模型对非线性时序数据的学习能力，从而开发出面向时间序列异常检测的强大新型深度学习模型。该架构会支持最先进的深度模型（包括来自 OpenAI 的最先进模型 GPT-3）；（2 ）使用无监督学习来解决异常数据不足的学习难题；（3）结合在线学习使得模型可以动态更 新，支持针对复杂异常模型的实时学习，提高实际的应用效率。 我们相信把上述三方面的技术结合将会很好地解决时间序列异常检测难题，带来技术性能上的重大突破。

16200221.label: Project Objectives
16200221.value: To investigate how to make federated learning workloads considerably more scalable by adopting a three-layer hierarchical architecture. To scale up to potentially millions of client devices in the era of Artificial Intelligence of Things (AIoT), we will conduct an in-depth study on how to utilize a three-layer architecture to improve scalability by two orders of magnitude compared to existing FL systems, and on the robustness of such a hierarchical structure in the presence of clients' dynamic behavior. To design optimized aggregation algorithms suitable for the proposed three-layer architecture. Although existing aggregation algorithms have been proposed to improve convergence behavior when using federated averaging for aggregation, these algorithms are no longer suitable with the introduction of edge servers in our proposed three-layer architecture. To design a new aggregation algorithm deployed across edge servers, we will propose a new adaptive optimization framework to adjust optimization parameters across edge servers in a coordinated manner during the progress of training, while considering observations made at the edge and origin servers. To design a new meta-learning framework for personalized FL. We will propose a new meta-learning framework called adaptive federated meta-learning, which is specifically designed for FL. The proposed framework maximizes state-of-the-art model-agnostic meta-learning and unsupervised meta-learning to achieve a balanced and customizable trade-off between the accuracy of the global model and its adaptability for local personalization. To design and implement a new open-source framework for scalable FL. To evaluate our three-layer architecture for personalized FL, we will design and implement a new open-source framework that maximizes the building blocks available in popular FL frameworks. To maximize the reproducibility of our research, we will release the source code of our new framework and benchmark datasets used to evaluate our algorithms.

16200221.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16200221.value: 在人工智能物联网（AIoT）时代， 大量智能设备 - 从相机、智能手机和传感设备 - 旨在相互自主协作。不久前还难以想象的任务 - 例如监控摄像头上的面部识别与零售店的显示器协作以显示更多相关内容 - 很快就会成为现实。 基于数据大多是私有的，因此联邦学习 (FL) 范式将以协作方式训练机器学习模型，而不会暴露原始私有数据。 尽管联邦学习最近受到了极大的关注，但其研究在 AIoT 背景下仍处于起步阶段。大多现有研究都集中在简单的客户端-服务器架构上，缺乏扩展性。更具有挑战的是，大多现有研究都假设训练一个共享的全局模型，没有考虑到设备的个性化需求。具体来说，每个设备都可能需要部署个性化模型，该模型针对其本地收集的数据集和个体需求进行定制。 在本项研究中，我们首先寻求通过在训练工作负载中利用大量参与客户的数据来提高联邦学习的可扩展性。受分布式内容分发网络 (CDN) 概念的启发，我们提出并设计了一个包含边缘服务器的三层分层架构，进一步研究如何在这样的分层结构中设计和优化新的聚合算法，以便训练工作能够尽快收敛到目标精度。我们将研究如何通过我们的三层架构在联邦学习环境中最有效地利用旨在生成通用学习模型的元学习框架。 为了证明我们提出的三层个性化 FL 架构的可行性和效率，我们计划基于现有 FL 框架（如 TENSORFLOW FEDERATED、FATE、FEDML 和 SHERPA.AI）的基本要素构建一个新的开源框架。我们将结合流行的机器学习基准数据集，如 CIFAR-10、CIFAR-100 和 WikiText，以及 Mini-Imagenet 和 CUB，用于小样本图像分类。该项目的技术和成果将带来更具可扩展性和个性化的联邦学习，非常适合在新兴的 AIoT 时代连接数十亿客户端从其用户和周围环境收集数据。

16200221.label: Realisation of objectives
16200221.value: Artificial Intelligence of Things or AIoT is rapidly becoming reality with artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) techniques being expected to be ubiquitously deployed in smart devices and sensors to process massive amount of data. The recent introduction of the Federated Learning (FL) framework has enabled such data to be utilized locally to train globally shared models without being transmitted to a centralized FL server. This overcomes the privacy and performance problem in typical machine learning paradigm. While FL has attracted significant attention, it has been routinely deployed using a relatively simple client-server architecture, in which locally generated data are processed at the client side, and the training results are transmitted to the server for aggregation and model updates. This design encounters two fundamental problems in AIoT environment, (1) it is not scalable with the presence of potentially enormous number of smart sensing devices, and (2) the shared global model fails to capture the unique requirement from each individual device. Moreover, each device sometimes demands a personalized model customized for its locally collected dataset and individual preference. This project improves the scalability of FL by utilizing localized data from numerous participating clients in training workloads. The realization builds upon a proposed novel three-layer hierarchical architecture with the addition of edge servers. The inclusion of edge servers brings three fundamental benefits, (1) it can substantially reduce the amount of model update traffic needed to be sent to a central FL server, (2) it improves the scalability of the overall FL system with the aggregation at the edge servers, and (3) it further mitigates the privacy leakage and security vulnerability by keeping the model updates within the boundary of an edge server, i.e., for instance within an institution. The three-layer hierarchical architecture we proposed consists of a central server, edge servers, often at the boundary of an institution, and a large number of smart devices under the jurisdiction of an edge server. Each smart device, upon receiving the global model from the corresponding edge server passed from the central server, the client conducts local training utilizing only its local dataset to update the model and sends its updated model to the edge server. Each edge server aggregates models from its clients and transfers the aggregated model to the central server. This substantially reduces the amount of model updated that need to be transmitted to the server FL server and also mitigates the security vulnerability without exposing the model parameters beyond the boundaries of institutions. The central server then generates an updated global model by aggregating all institutions’ aggregated models. There are several technical difficulties we have encountered. While the proposed three-layer FL architecture can effectively mitigate the model updates and potential privacy leakage, there still exists frequent exchanges of model weights during training process, which may lead to excessive communication overhead. We mathematically analyzed the impact of pruning technique on the training performance, and we showed that it can effectively compensate the performance degradation. We further devised an adaptive pruning algorithm, and the results showed considerable improvement in communication efficiency with negligible degradation in global model accuracy. FL utilizes proper functions to estimate the quality of each local update based on certain metrics; for instance, the values derived from the training loss or model parameters. These metrics are used to measure the quality of the corresponding client local training, and relative gaps between the local model and the global model. However, these metrics are often insufficient for the global model to converge towards high training quality, esp., under time-varying network conditions and heterogeneous computation capabilities. We proposed a new aggregation strategy that weights the local updates by quality. Specifically, we apply deep reinforcement learning (DRL) technique to dynamically evaluate the quality of model updates with accommodations for both data and device heterogeneity during training process. We formulate the model aggregation as a control problem and apply our quality evaluation on the weighting in the global aggregation process. The results demonstrated that our designed DRL technique can handle an arbitrary number of client updates and accommodates dynamically changing heterogeneity across a large number of clients. This significantly improves the FL system scalability and the performance in the dynamic and heterogeneous environment. FL is typically performed in a synchronous parallel manner, in which a slow client could prolong the entire training iteration. We proposed Pisces, an asynchronous FL system with intelligent participant selection and model aggregation for accelerated training. To avoid excessive resource costs and stale training computation, Pisces uses a novel scoring mechanism to identify suitable participants in each training iteration and enables model aggregation to dynamically bound the progress gap between participants and servers with a provable convergence guarantee in a non-convex setting. We implement Pisces on our developed open-source FL platform, Plato, and demonstrate its performance improvement in accelerating the time-to-accuracy. Communication is one of the major bottlenecks that prolongs the training process, especially under large model variances due to skewed data distributions. Existing approaches utilize either single momentum-based gradient descent, or random client selection for variance reduction, both of which often lead to poor model accuracy and system efficiency. We proposed FedMoS, a communication-efficient FL framework with coupled double momentum-based update and adaptive client selection to jointly mitigate the intrinsic variance. FedMoS designs an adaptive selection scheme to provide a proper client representation during aggregation. By optimally calibrating clients’ selection probabilities, it can effectively reduce the sampling variance while ensuring unbiased aggregation. FL offers a privacy-centric distributed learning framework, enabling model training on individual clients and centralized aggregation without data exchange. Yet, this implementation often suffers from non-IID. and long-tailed distributions across many applications, which leads to overfitting and convergence in sub-optimal state. We explored the impact of data heterogeneity on model bias and introduced an personalized FL framework, which integrates three innovative modules: (1) Biased Activation Value Dropout (BAVD) to mitigate overfitting and accelerate training; (2) Adaptive Cluster-based Model Update (ACMU) to refine local models for ensuring coherent global aggregation; and (3) Prior Knowledge-assisted Classifier Fine-tuning (PKCF) to enhance classification and personalized models in accord with skewed local data with shared knowledge. The effectiveness under even extreme non-IID situation is validated with experiments on a variety of real-world datasets for image classification and semantic segmentation. We design and implement an open-source federated learning (FL) platform – Plato (https://github.com/TL-System/plato) by incorporating our proposed techniques and innovations from this project including: (1) a new aggregation mechanisms enables the server to adjust its weights when aggregating client updates to produce a shared global model; (2) a client training customization mechanism used to calibrate local updates on the clients during local training for enhancing the global model; (3) a client selection mechanism for selecting clients with higher data quality in each round; (4) a novel personalized FL mechanism designed to train models that are personalized to produce high validation accuracies on the specific dataset at each client device, while still being able to benefit from collaborative training over a shared global model; (5) a communication-efficient FL mechanism to mitigate the communication overhead during the training process, by pruning, compressing, or quantizing the model at each client.

16200221.label: Major findings and research outcome
16200221.value: FL facilitates collaborative learning of global models among geographically spread devices. The proposed hierarchical FL framework presents a practically feasible solution to accommodate the scaling problem, while considerably reducing the model update communication that needs to be routed to the central server for aggregation. We start by implementing PLATO, an open-source framework for scalable federated learning and use that to conduct extensive investigation. The results suggest that even a simple pruning method, e.g., L1-norm unstructured pruning, can substantially mitigate the communication overhead with negligible degradation in model accuracy. We design a new pruning mechanism, which prunes local model updates instead of local model weights, and we demonstrate that the global model trained can converge to higher accuracy with fewer training iterations, especially when clients have highly skewed non-IID local datasets commonly exhibited in FL environments. We proceed to conduct mathematical analysis of the impact on the shared global model, and we find that the epoch numbers of clients’ local training can significantly affect the federated model performance. Based on the analysis, we propose a new framework to adaptively tune clients’ epoch numbers based on the differences between their institutions’ aggregated models and the current global model within our proposed three-layer hierarchical architecture. The evaluation under real network environments indicates this enhances the global model accuracy while reducing the number of required training iterations and the elapsed training time. Clients in federated learning systems are heterogeneous in computation, storage, and data distribution, which often require personalized models. One common strategy is for clients to collaborate among each other with similar data distributions to train a federated model with local pruning. We devise a personalized FL method based on BN (Batch Normalization) masks, in which each client adaptively adjusts its BN mask, enabling effective structured pruning with minimal performance loss. By only exchanging BN masks, it significantly improves personalized FL model performance while reducing computational and communication costs. We observe that model updates exhibit similarity across different training rounds and parameters often follow a linear updating pattern. We propose federated learning with speculative updating (FedSU) to attain larger sparsification ratio without compromising model accuracy. Specifically, we devise a regression-free mechanism and leverage the prediction error as a feedback signal to adjust the parameter update. We implement FedSU as a Python module, and large-scale experiments verify its effectiveness in improving the communication efficiency with significant convergence speedup.

16200221.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16200221.value: The proposed hierarchical architecture provides the potential towards the full realization of scalable and personalized federated learning (FL) systems. One of the major limitations in practice is the privacy leakage during aggregation. While FL learning system does not reveal the clients’ raw data, adversaries can still infer a client’s private information from its updates. Homomorphic encryption (HE) has been shown to be effective in providing strong privacy guarantees without compromising the learning accuracy. With HE, aggregation can be performed directly on ciphertexts, without decrypting them first. However, HE incurs significant computation and communication overheads as it performs computationally intensive cryptographic operations and generates ciphertexts that are much larger to transfer than plaintexts. It would be interesting to examine how parallel encryption/decryption operations on multiple plaintexts can help to reduce the encryption and communication overheads. Another issue is that it is difficult to collect trace data and performance measures in real world setting, which are largely unavailable publicly. The proposed open-source PLATO framework provides a reproducible FL framework, which can be used to conduct comprehensive investigation on the FL convergence performance, as existing methods are exclusively evaluated in simulation or emulation testbed, which are usually biased.

16200221.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16200221.value: Federated Learning (FL) enables clients to collaboratively train a machine learning model without exposing their individual data. In the context of AIoT, the existing FL framework encounters serious scaling problems as it relies on a centralized FL server for model aggregation while dealing with a potentially enormous number of smart sensing devices. Moreover, this framework fails to capture the unique requirements from individual clients, which often demand personalized learning results. The significance of this project and its outcomes are: (1) we introduce a hierarchical FL architecture with the inclusion of edge servers, which enhances the scalability by reducing the volume of model updates to the central FL server through new aggregation algorithms, while mitigating the privacy leakage issue; (2) we devise a meta-learning framework - adaptive federated meta-learning, which leverages the model-agnostic meta-learning to achieve a balanced trade-off between the global model accuracy and its adaptability for local model personalization; (3) we design and implement an open-source FL framework - PLATO, which is not only scalable to support large number of clients, but also extensible to accommodate different models, datasets and learning algorithms.

16200521.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16200521.value: 遵循社交距離的坐席安排

16200521.label: Project Objectives
16200521.value: Developing a framework for making a seating plan that considers social distancing measures. The proposed research is motivated by a general question, how to implement social distancing in an effective and efficient way. We will first develop a seating-plan model to cope with the concerned social distancing requirement, by introducing some concepts, such as risky region, marginally risky region, and target group portfolio. We will then set up an optimization problem to minimize the risk of infection among people, and study how to solve the optimization problem. In addition, we will investigate related managerial issues, such as the tradeoff between the risk level and the capacity utilization rate, and the impact of group visitors. Developing an approach for making a reservation-based seating plan that respects social distancing. For problems encountered in commercial applications, customers may arrive dynamically, and we need to make a seating plan immediately upon their arrival. The decision must be based on the consideration of the current request and the future request. We plan to develop an approach that is based on an important concept, target group portfolio, and aims directly for a set of ideal final seating plans. In this way, we can avoid the complexity of stochastic sequential optimization. Developing an approach for setting up a seat layout that respects social distancing. The first two objectives are concerned with making a seating plan over a given seat layout of which seats are densely installed. Facing the reality that social distancing needs to be practiced for a term, initiatives have been taken to redesign the seat layout of a venue, making it able to directly support social distancing. Based on the results obtained from the study of the first two objectives, we will develop an approach for seat layout design by considering different composition of people, social distancing measures, and the capacity utilization rates.
