16200521.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16200521.value: Social distancing, a non-pharmaceutical way to help contain the spread of an infectious disease, is broadly recognized and practiced. As a result, extensive research has emerged on social distancing with respect to its effectiveness and impact. What lags behind is operational guidance for implementation, especially when there are multiple ways to ensure social distancing, each with different tradeoff between risk and resource utilization rate. One typical example is how to make social distancing-ensured seating plans. We will start by considering a seating plan with a given set of seats. In a pandemic, the government may require a minimum physical distance between people. In addition, to reduce the risk of infection, the event organizer may want to operate seating distances beyond the government’s minimum standard. The problem is further complicated by the existence of groups of guests who will be seated together. To achieve such a goal, we develop a mechanism for seat planning, which includes a model to characterize the riskiness of a seating plan, and a solution approach to making a trade-off between seat utilization rate and the associated risk of infection. We will also introduce and investigate a concept, target group portfolio, to characterize some group compositions which lead to efficient tradeoff between risk and seat utilization rate. We also study a dynamic seating plan problem that is more suitable for commercial use. In this problem, customers arrive dynamically and the seating plan needs to be made without knowing the number and composition of future customers. This becomes a sequential stochastic optimization problem where conventional methods fall into the curse of dimensionality. To avoid this complexity, we develop an approach which is aimed directly at the final seating plans. Specifically, we make use of target group portfolio and design an approach to maintain the possibility of achieving one of the target seating plans. Finally, we study the seating layout design for multiple events with different customer compositions. This is motivated by the practice of some theaters that have removed a set of seats so as to create a suitable distance between remaining seats. We develop the models and solution schemes to optimize such removal decisions that consider different possible customer compositions. Our project will benefit multiple stakeholders, including the guests, event organizers, and space designers. In addition, it will also help the government to evaluate the impact of social distancing policies on both risk control and economic cost. 保持社交距離，作為一種遏制傳染病傳播的非醫藥措施，已得到廣泛的認可和實施。關於保持社交距離的研究，目前集中在其有效性和社會影響，很少研究涉及保持社交距離的實施細節。在某些場合下，存在多種方式來確保社交距離，各種方式具有其不同的風險和效益。一個典型的例子是如何制定確保社交距離的坐席安排。 我們將首先考慮如何為一個給定的群體活動進行坐席安排 。在疫情爆發後，政府可能要求公共場所人與人之間保持最小的物理距離。此外，為了降低感染風險，活動組織者可能希望安排超出政府最低標準的座位距離。問題的複雜之處在於，某些活動的參與者可以作為一個小組坐在一起，導致組別之間的社交距離問題。我們計劃開發一種坐席安排機制，包括一個表徵座席安排風險的模型，以及一個在座位利用率和相關感染風險之間進行權衡的解決方案。我們還將介紹和研究一個概念，即目標組別集合，而在風險和座位利用率之間進行有效權衡。 我們還計劃研究一個面向商業用途的動態坐席安排方案。在這類問題中，客戶動態到達，需要立即安排座位。這導致一個多階段隨機優化問題，傳統的方法將面臨維數爆炸。為了避免這個困境，我們提出一種直接針對最終坐席安排的方法。具體來說，我們利用目標組別集合的概念，設計一種方法來保持實現其中一個目標坐席計劃的可能性。 最後，我們將研究適用於不同客戶和活動的座位佈局設計。事實上，一些電影院已經移除了某些座位，以便在剩餘座位之間形成合適的距離。我們將開發模型和解決方案來優化考慮不同可能客戶組合的此類座位設計方案。 我們的研究項目將有益於多個相關方，包括活動參與者、活動組織者和場地經營者。此外，它還將幫助政府評估保持社交距離的政策，對風險控制和經濟成本的影響。

16200521.label: Realisation of objectives
16200521.value: Objective 1 is to develop a framework of seating management under the social distancing measures. To achieve this objective, we have proposed three optimization models, the Seat Planning with Deterministic Requests (SPDR) problem, the Seat Planning with Stochastic Requests (SPSR) problem, and the Seat Assignment with Dynamic Requests (SADR) problem. (1) In the SPDR problem, complete information about seating requests in groups is known. This applies to scenarios where participants and their groups are identifiable, such as family members attending a church gathering or staff from the same office at a company meeting. (2) In the SPSR problem, the requests are unknown but follow a probabilistic distribution. This problem is relevant in situations where a new seating layout must accommodate multiple events with varying seating requests. For example, during the COVID-19 outbreak, some theaters physically removed some seats and used the remaining ones to create a seating plan that accommodates stochastic requests. (3) In the SADR problem, groups of seating requests arrive dynamically. The problem is to decide, upon the arrival of each group of requests, whether to accept or reject the group, and then assign seats for each accepted group. Such seat assignment is applicable in commercial settings where requests arrive as a stochastic process, such as ticket sales in movie theaters. The above three models form an integrated framework for seating management under social distancing. Although each model represents a standalone problem tailored to specific situations, they are closely interconnected in terms of problem-solving methods and managerial insights. In the SPDR problem, we identify important concepts such as the full pattern and the largest pattern, which play a crucial role in developing solutions for the other two problems. Additionally, the SPDR problem serves as a useful offline benchmark for evaluating the performance of policies in the SADR problem. Furthermore, the solution to the SPSR problem can serve as a reference seat plan for dynamic seat assignment in the SADR problem. Objective 2 is to design a solution approach for dynamically allocating seats for arrived requests, which is essentially the SADR problem. We implement a two-stage seat-plan-based assignment approach. In the first decision phase, a relaxed dynamic programming evaluates each incoming request to determine its acceptance. The accepted requests then proceed to the second assignment phase, where the group-type control allocation is performed. Computational experiments show that this seat-plan-based assignment policy outperforms traditional bid-price and booking-limit policies. Objective 3 is to design a layout under the social distancing measures, based on which people can further investigate the impact of social distancing on the capacity utilization rate of a venue. This objective is achieved by studying the solution to SPSR together with extensive computational experiments. We utilize scenario-based optimization and develop solution approaches based on Benders decomposition. More importantly, we introduce the concept of the threshold of requests, representing the upper limit on the number of requests an event can accommodate without being affected by social distancing measures. Specifically, if an event receives fewer requests than this threshold, social distancing does not affect revenue. Our computational experiments demonstrate that the threshold of requests primarily depends on the average group size and is relatively insensitive to the specific distribution of group sizes. This finding provides a straightforward method for estimating the threshold of requests and evaluating the impact of social distancing.

16200521.label: Major findings and research outcome
16200521.value: The major achievement of this project can be summarized as follows. First, for the seating management problem under social distancing measures, this project offers a comprehensive framework covering different situations with deterministic request, stochastic request, and dynamic requests, respectively. For each situation, we develop models and solutions approaches. Such results will help event organizers or venue operators in achieving efficient operations under social distancing. Second, we reveal a series of managerial insights and guidance in terms of the impact of social distancing on the operations efficiency. For example, we introduce the concept of the threshold of requests, representing the upper limit on the number of requests an event can accommodate without being affected by social distancing measures. We find that the threshold of requests primarily depends on the average group size and is relatively insensitive to the specific distribution of group sizes. This finding provides a straightforward method for estimating the threshold of requests and evaluating the impact of social distancing. This will help both venue operators and governmental policy makers to make informed decisions. Last, we generalize the research from the specific seat management problem to a general theoretical model, multiple knapsack problems with items in limited types. While multiple knapsack problems are classic with extensive studies, the seating management problem suggests a meaningful special case in which items belong to a small number of types. This enabled us to develop special efficient policies. The generalization extends the scope of this project to many applications, such as social distancing related meeting room sharing and allocation, and storage management of dangerous goods in a space. The above first and second achievements are included in a PhD thesis (Part C, item 10 [1]), and the paper version has been submitted to a journal for review (Part C, item 8 [1]). They were also presented in conferences (Parc C, item 9 [1-4]). The third contribution is under the final stage preparation and will be submitted soon (Part C, item 8 [2]).

In addition, we will explore the new applications inspired by the general theoretical model (Part C, item 8[2]).

16200521.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16200521.value: This project focuses on social distancing, the practice of keeping space between people to prevent disease spreading. While crucial for public health, it comes at a cost, especially for service businesses like restaurants and theaters, as it reduces the number of customers they can serve in a limited space. Our goal is to find smarter ways to implement these social distancing rules so businesses can operate more safely and efficiently. We use seat planning as a key application. Instead of just closing every other seat, we investigate the most effective arrangements, like which specific seats to block, to maximize safety while still allowing a good number of customers. To test these ideas, we create computer simulations, like a digital model of a venue. This allows us to safely experiment with different layouts and see which ones work best. Ultimately, this research provides clear, practical guidance to both business owners and government officials, helping them make informed decisions that protect people’s health while also supporting the economy.

16200721.label: Project Objectives
16200721.value: We will develop cryptographic protocols for zero-knowledge accumulators with efficient membership/non-membership query evaluation, building upon recent work by the PI in the prime order setting (e.g., over elliptic curve groups) and other works in the hidden composite order setting (e.g., RSA) which, however, solve a similar problem without considering privacy. Our goal is to develop schemes that work in an offline/online mode: after running one costly pre-processing phase, zero-knowledge proofs can be computed on demand with minimal cost. This will entail proposing formal security definitions and proving the security properties of our constructions under these definitions. We will implement our cryptographic constructions from objective 1 and publish them as open-source cryptographic libraries, to be potentially used in other applications. From previous experience, there is a significant need for optimized cryptographic libraries as there are relatively few open-source options. Making our implementation available may help other researchers that wish to adopt, benchmark, or improve them. We will provide a prototype implementation of a zero-knowledge dictionary, using our above cryptographic constructions as building blocks, and make its code publicly available. We will use the techniques described in Section 2 of the proposal to optimize its implementation and then we plan to benchmark and evaluate its performance in the context of two applications: (a) transparent logs for key/certificate dictionaries, (b) privacy-preserving cryptocurrencies. We will explore research directions for building zero-knowledge systems with offline/online proving for more general applications. Combining the techniques used in objectives 1-3, we will provide cryptographic definitions for such schemes, propose constructions that achieve these definitions, and implement them for some test applications. As per our description in Section 2, we will use these cryptographic constructions to build efficient systems for modular proofs for database query evaluation (e.g., multi-dimensional range queries).

16200821.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16200821.value: In today’s competitive world, organizations compete in multiple markets and individuals including politicians, athletes, and sales representatives need to outperform opponents or peers in multiple roles, all of which require investment. Every competition has its attributes, some of which may be shared by other competitions as well. Thus, competitions in which an organization or an individual is engaged may be correlated, e.g., showmanship is a strength in certain roles but a weakness in others. Furthermore, even a well-prepared competitor can lose a competition to an overall weaker one as evidenced by surprises in sports, politics and marketplaces, making real life exciting and decision-making difficult. Both internal (e.g., mental and health) and external (e.g., weather, economic, and political) conditions during a competition can contribute to the actual success or failure of a competitor. Thus, resource allocation decisions need to take into consideration the random nature of the competitions. All of the existing literature along this line has ignored competition attributes by assuming that competitions differ only by their rewards. Under this assumption, competitors’ decisions are reduced to allocating resources (effort) to the competitions and a high level of effort in a competition implies a high probability of winning, hence a high expected reward from the competition. When competitions can be positively or negatively correlated, exerting more effort into an attribute may increase a competitor’s probability of winning in some competitions and decrease them in others. Thus, one needs to consider the attributes of the competitions explicitly and characterize a competition by its reward as well as the importance of each attribute in winning the competition. A competitor needs to strike the right balance among all the attributes when making his resource allocation decision in order to maximize his expected total reward from all competitions taking into consideration the correlations between competitions. In this proposed research, we will introduce competition attributes and correlations into the existing literature, and study competitors’ equilibrium resource allocation decisions. Such a problem has a wide range of applications in business, politics, and sports, etc., with a good understanding of the problem being critical to enhancing decision making in many organizations and people’s lives. The problem can be of high dimensionality, with multiple competitors and competitions, each with multiple attributes. Coupled with the fact that competitions can be correlated, it is technically challenging and may require the development of new methodologies. 當今世界競爭激烈，不僅公司組織需要同時在多個市場或領域中展開競爭，包括政治家、運動員、推銷員等等在內的個人也時常需要同時在多個職位或項目中超越對手、領先同行。任何競賽都需要參賽者某種形式的投入才能取勝，而每項競賽各有其考察的相關素質，同種素質也可能為多項競賽所共同考察。因此，組織或個人所同時參與的多項競賽之間存在相關性。例如，善於取悅他人對某些職位是優勢，對其他職位卻是劣勢。此外，競賽還具有不確定性。競賽進行期間的內部因素（比如心理和生理的狀態）和外部條件（比如天氣、經濟和政治氛圍）都將影響參賽者的最終成敗。正如在體育、政治和市場份額等領域裡時不時殺出的黑馬所證實的那樣，即便是一個準備充分的競爭者也可能輸給一個整體水準平平的對手。這讓世界更加精彩，也使為贏得競賽所做的各項決策變得更困難。 現有文獻在研究多項競賽共存時，競賽僅以其獎勵的不同作出區分，而忽略了其考察的各項素質的異同。在這一簡化下，參賽者僅需考慮如何將資源（精力、財力、時間等）分配到各項競賽上。在一項競賽中耗費的精力越多，則越有可能贏取該競賽，亦即該競賽的預期收益越高。而當我們考慮競賽間正向或負向的相關關係時，參賽者為某項素質所付出的努力可能會令其在某些比賽中更易取勝，卻在其他競賽中更難獲勝。因此，競賽還應就其所考察素質的種類和程度作出區分，而參賽者在分配其資源時，也需根據不同競賽間的相關性在各項素質之間求取適當的平衡，以期獲得盡可能高的競賽獎勵。 在本項擬議研究中，我們將在現有文獻基礎上引入素質及競賽間的相關性，並研究均衡下參賽者的資源分配決策。這一問題在商業、政治和體育等領域應用廣泛。對此問題的充分理解對提升組織決策水平和改善個人生活至關重要。由於存在多個參賽者、多項競賽、多類素質，該問題很可能是高維度的。再加上各項競賽間的相關性，該問題具有較大的技術挑戰且可能需要開發新的方法。

16202121.value: 數據流系統在雲計算中應用廣泛，涵蓋分布式機器學習、數據流處理和大數據分析，著名的系統包括 TensorFlow、Flink 和 Spark。它們提供了一系列預先實現的運算算子，開發者用算子構建出複雜的數據應用。每個應用表示為有向無環圖（DAG），其中節點代表算子，節點間的邊表示數據流向。數據流系統會根據 DAG 自動地部署和執行應用，甚至包括在複雜集群裏的並行執行。 數據流系統開發簡單，但執行中可能存在諸多問題，例如資源競爭、配置低效、規模受限等。而且由於執行過程複雜，開發者往往需要大量時間和精力才能解決這些問題。 我們在本項目中另辟蹊徑，將代碼分析與機器學習相結合來刻畫數據流應用的性能。性能刻畫的傳統方法需要修改系統代碼，或只能針對單個系統，而我們的方法無需改動，並且適配多數系統。新方法背後的核心觀察為：數據流系統的源代碼隱含著資源相關的語法和語義信息，例如數據壓縮（傳輸）通常是計算（網絡）密集型操作。我們據此構建了性能-資源模型，它根據每個數據應用的執行日志和源代碼，自動推測出應用花費在每種資源 （如 處理器、網絡、硬盤）上時間。基於時間信息，模型能估算應用在不同資源下的執行時長，或檢查執行中的異常問題。 該性能-資源模型的構建分兩個階段。在第一階段，我們從執行日誌中提取 DAG 信息，並在系統源代碼中定位每個節點涉及的函數。在第二階段，機器學習分類器根據函數代碼推測每個節點的資源使用情況。其中分類器的訓練數據來自於開源項目，多為有明顯資源調用的底層函數。由於資源調用的代碼特徵與具體數據流系統無關，所以分類器習得這些特徵後可以用於多種系統和編程語言。我們將以命令行工具的形式實現整套方法，並對主要的數據流系統（如 Spark、Flink 和 TensorFlow）提供支持。而後我們將進行實地的案例研究，展示新方法在性能優化及配置調試方面的有效性。

16202121.label: Realisation of objectives
16202121.value: In this project, we developed a novel, learning-based approach to characterize the performance of dataflow computations through code analysis. Our work culminated in a complete performance monitoring and reasoning system, achieving all five research objectives. This system, reported in [C1–C4, J1, J3], demonstrates that performance behavior can be inferred directly from program code and standard logs—without requiring intrusive instrumentation or framework modifications. - Realisation of Objective-1 We achieved the first objective by establishing a framework-independent methodology for performance characterization based solely on code and execution traces. Traditional profiling approaches rely heavily on instrumentation or repetitive controlled runs, but our system remains external to the framework. It learns the relationship between code structure and resource consumption without collecting low-level counters or modifying runtimes. The key insight is that a program’s source code implicitly encodes patterns that reveal how it uses CPU, disk, and network resources. Our system leverages this property to infer performance characteristics across different programming languages and dataflow frameworks. It requires only two inputs—execution traces and the corresponding source code of invoked functions—to construct accurate resource–behavior mappings. These findings confirm that performance characterization can indeed be learned directly from code, fulfilling Objective 1 [C1, C4]. - Realisation of Objective-2 Objective 2 was realized by building a comprehensive DAG-based job representation that captures both the structure and timing of dataflow execution. The system begins by collecting lightweight traces from existing logs or sampling profilers. For JVM-based frameworks such as Spark and Flink, it uses a sampling profiler that records stack traces and timestamps without interrupting normal execution; for TensorFlow and MXNet, it utilizes native profiling interfaces. From these traces, the system reconstructs a directed acyclic graph (DAG) where each node represents an operation and each edge encodes data or control dependencies. Each node is enriched with metadata—execution times, call stacks, and resource statistics—and linked to the corresponding source code and documentation. This automatic mapping transforms an abstract execution plan into a code-linked DAG profile, in which each operation is represented by its concrete implementation and computational semantics. This DAG representation serves as the analytical foundation for subsequent learning and modeling steps, enabling reasoning about performance bottlenecks in relation to specific code components. Objective 2 was fully realized and documented in [C4, J1, J3]. - Realisation of Objective-3 To meet Objective 3, we demonstrated empirically that source code contains distinct, learnable patterns that correlate with resource usage. We designed machine-learning models that learn from both code and textual documentation [C1, C4]. Code is transformed into abstract syntax trees (ASTs), then encoded using recursive autoencoders to capture lexical and syntactic features, while natural-language documentation is processed using contextual embeddings and recurrent networks to extract semantic signals about resource behavior. The resulting representations feed into neural classifiers that output a three-dimensional resource vector—the relative proportions of CPU, disk, and network utilization per function. The models were trained on a corpus of over 5,000 manually labeled functions and achieved an average accuracy of 81% with an F1-score of 0.9, demonstrating their reliability and generality across frameworks. A learnability analysis further revealed that the models associate keywords and constructs (e.g., “socket,” “send,” “stream,” “file”) with specific resource patterns, proving that resource behavior can be recognized directly from code structure and vocabulary. These findings verified our hypothesis that source code inherently encodes learnable performance patterns, thereby accomplishing Objective 3 [C1, C4, J1, J3]. - Realisation of Objective-4 The fourth objective was achieved by constructing a unified performance-resource model that integrates the code-derived resource vectors with the DAG execution profile. Each operation’s predicted resource usage—its CPU, disk, and network proportions—is aggregated across the DAG to model overall job performance. This model captures both individual operation characteristics and their interdependencies, allowing it to predict system-wide resource dynamics. The model supports two main applications. First, it enables performance debugging by identifying which code segments dominate specific resource usage. By tracing the DAG’s critical path and inspecting resource vectors, users can localize bottlenecks such as CPU-heavy transformations, disk-intensive serialization, or network-heavy data shuffles. Second, it provides performance prediction capabilities: given hypothetical changes to resource capacity (e.g., faster CPUs or higher bandwidth), the model estimates how overall runtime would vary. Experimental evaluations across six benchmark workloads on Spark, Flink, and TensorFlow showed that the model predicts runtime with an average error of 13.47%, comparable to state-of-the-art, instrumentation-heavy models like Monotasks. It also successfully detected real bottlenecks such as network imbalance in Spark and I/O contention in TensorFlow training. The model generalizes beyond analytics systems to serverless workflows and machine-learning training/inference pipelines, confirming its broad applicability. Thus, Objective 4 was fully realized through a scalable, accurate, and generalizable performance-resource model [C1, C3, C4, J1, J2, J3]. - Realisation of Objective-5 The fifth objective was met through the development of a working open-source toolchain that implements all proposed components across major dataflow frameworks. The tool operates as a command-line utility that interacts with Spark, Flink, and TensorFlow through standard logging and code inspection, requiring no modifications to the frameworks themselves. The architecture consists of four main modules: 1. Trace Collection – gathers execution data from existing logs and profilers. 2. Code and Documentation Analysis – employs the trained neural models to extract semantic and structural representations. 3. DAG Construction – integrates traces and code metadata into a unified job graph. 4. Performance Modeling and Visualization – computes predictions, identifies bottlenecks, and presents interpretable insights to users. Extensive evaluations across three frameworks and six benchmark workloads confirmed the tool’s scalability and efficiency. It maintained high predictive accuracy while introducing negligible runtime overhead. In multiple case studies, the system automatically uncovered subtle issues—such as unbalanced network transfers and hidden I/O contention—that previously required expert manual analysis. By releasing the tool as open source, we established a foundation for future research and industrial adoption. Its compatibility with mainstream dataflow ecosystems and non-intrusive operation make it especially suitable for large-scale production environments where traditional instrumentation is impractical. Moreover, it extends naturally to emerging computing paradigms such as serverless data processing and distributed machine-learning workloads. These achievements collectively fulfill Objective 5 and demonstrate the project’s practical impact [C1, C3, C4, J3].

16202121.label: Major findings and research outcome
16202121.value: This project studied the optimal container placement problem for long-running This project delivers a comprehensive realization of the research vision to learn and predict the performance of dataflow computations directly from source code. Its most significant finding is that program code itself contains rich, learnable patterns that correlate with how functions consume computational resources. By analyzing the syntactic and semantic structure of source code, the system developed in this project can infer whether a function is CPU-, disk-, or network-intensive without any instrumentation or framework-specific modification. This discovery establishes a new paradigm for performance characterization—one that depends on code intelligence rather than runtime profiling. Another key outcome is the successful construction of a DAG-based execution profile that connects runtime behavior with its corresponding source code. From ordinary framework logs and call traces, the system reconstructs the hierarchy of operations in a job and annotates each with its source code and resource-use predictions. This representation allows precise reasoning about performance bottlenecks in the context of actual code, bridging the gap between low-level profiling data and high-level program understanding. Through extensive experiments, we demonstrated that neural models can learn generalizable resource-usage patterns from thousands of open-source functions. Models trained on Scala and Java code accurately predict resource behavior across diverse frameworks such as Spark, Flink, and TensorFlow, achieving around 81 percent accuracy and a 0.9 F1-score. This confirms that the relationship between code structure and resource usage transcends programming language and framework boundaries. The project’s performance-resource model integrates code-derived resource vectors with DAG execution timing to predict job runtime and diagnose performance bottlenecks. In benchmark evaluations across multiple frameworks, our system achieves runtime prediction accuracy within 13.5 percent of observed performance, comparable to specialized systems that require intrusive instrumentation. It successfully identifies bottlenecks such as I/O contention and network imbalance in large-scale workloads. The project has led to fruitful results published in various top-tier conferences and journals (listed in the research output), including ATC, SoCC, INFOCOM, TPDS, and TNET. Among these publications, one paper titled “Golgi: Performance-Aware, Resource-Efficient Function Scheduling for Serverless Computing,” received the Best Paper Award at ACM SoCC 2023, the first time for Hong Kong researchers.

16202121.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16202121.value: Our current results demonstrate that learning-based code analysis can accurately capture the performance characteristics of dataflow computations, opening several promising directions for future research. One potential avenue is to extend the system’s learning capability beyond low-level function analysis to encompass higher-level program semantics and cross-stage optimization. By integrating static program analysis with runtime behavior modeling, future versions could reason about distributed coordination costs, data locality, and scheduling policies, enabling even finer-grained performance prediction. Another important direction involves integrating the state-of-the-art large language models and agentic technologies for new programming paradigms such as streaming analytics and serverless workflows. The proposed course of action focuses on developing a unified, self-evolving framework that continuously refines its models through incremental learning on real execution data. Incorporating feedback loops from deployed systems would allow the system to adapt to evolving frameworks and hardware configurations automatically. Additionally, coupling the system with optimization modules could transform it from a diagnostic tool into a prescriptive one--capable of not only identifying bottlenecks but also recommending code or configuration adjustments. These developments would move our system toward becoming a fully autonomous performance engineering assistant for modern dataflow systems.

16202121.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16202121.value: This project tackled the challenge of diagnosing and improving the performance of distributed dataflow computations used in frameworks such as Spark, Flink, and TensorFlow. These systems execute complex pipelines as directed acyclic graphs (DAGs) of parallel operations, often suffering from inefficiencies like resource contention and poor scalability that are difficult to diagnose manually. To address this, the project developed a learning-based system that characterized performance directly from program source code, without instrumentation or framework modification. The core idea was that source code contains recognizable patterns that indicate how operations use resources such as CPU, disk, and network. By combining static code analysis with machine learning, the system inferred each operation’s resource behaviour from past execution traces and code semantics. The system reconstructed DAG-based execution profiles, extracted the source code of operations, and used trained models to predict resource usage patterns. These insights were integrated into a performance-resource model that identified bottlenecks and predicted runtime under different configurations. Implemented as an open-source tool, the system worked across major dataflow frameworks and achieved high accuracy in real-world experiments. Overall, the project proved that code itself can reveal performance behaviour, offering a new, automated path for understanding and optimizing dataflow computation.

16203021.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16203021.value: 相變合金是生物醫藥，微電子和能量轉化應用中很重要的一類功能材料。隨著納米加工技術的日益成熟，人們已經可以在納米尺度製造很複雜的生物醫學器件，如血管和神經支架。與宏觀尺度相比，這些微納米器件要求更高的功能穩定性。近期關於晶體學相變相容性的理論指出，這些相變材料的疲勞問題與微觀組織界面處的相容性條件有關。在宏觀尺度上，通過很多實驗對其進行了驗證。但是對於納米力學尺度下的超彈性和疲勞，卻沒有得到系統的研究。儘管相變合金符合普適性的越小越強的力學尺度效應，但相變合金的疲勞問題更為複雜。馬氏體相變和塑性變形在力誘導相變過程中會耦合作用，變形機理比非相變材料複雜。到目前為止，還沒有建立一套針對相變納米力學的理性分析。 在這個項目中，我們將納米相容性的理論和實驗的問題羅列出來，並進行系統理性的研究。選取兩個相變合金系，即CuAlZn和CuAlMn進行納米力學的實驗和理論研究，特別針對晶界處的圍觀組織和織構的形成進行深入探討。理論上，我們將建立晶界相容性原理。實驗上，我們將合成(55-x)Cu - xAu - 45Zn (at%)，28 < x < 31和67Cu-xAl-yMn(at%)， 23 < x < 25，9 < y < 10。通過X光同步輻射表徵晶格常數和對稱性。通過StrucTrans算法計算晶體學相容性條件。在雙晶和三晶交界處通過FIB加工納米尺度結構進行原位納米力學表徵。我們將超彈性和超彈疲勞的實驗結果與理論結合，並推導出相變合金在微納米尺度下的力學尺度效應。

16203221.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16203221.value: Aerosols and droplets containing virus are among the main modes of transmission of infectious diseases including COVID-19. A three-dimensional (3D) optical imaging method that is capable of real-time monitoring of the size, morphology and phase structures of aerosols and droplets will offer a complementary tool to other existing aerosol detection and imaging methods towards controlling and monitoring of infectious diseases transmitted by aerosols and droplets, among other critical applications in atmospheric and environmental sciences for example. Optical coherence tomography (OCT), which is a mature, non-contact, real-time, 3D-imaging method applied typically to image biological cells and tissues could be adopted upon further research towards imaging transparent microparticles in air. Specifically, the swept-source OCT (SS-OCT) offers a high axial resolution accorded by the broad bandwidth of the wavelength-swept light source and a high-speed 3D image data acquisition by a high-speed photodiode detector. Conventional Fourier-domain mode-locking (FDML) lasers offer a swept source that allows each circulating lasing mode to transmit through a synchronized sweeping filter in cavity round-trips without building up from noise. This has enabled a fast axial scanning for OCT. In this proposal, we will demonstrate a frequency-comb FDML hybrid-integrated laser source emitting in the 1260 ~ 1360nm wavelengths. The laser will comprise (1) semiconductor optical amplifiers (SOAs), (2) a silicon photonic integrated circuit with a planar Echelle grating, electro-optically (EO) tunable microring Vernier filters and a microring frequency-comb filter and (3) a standard singlemode fiber delay line of only tens of meters long. We will use two external SOAs for initial system integration while aiming to heterogeneously integrate by wafer bonding an InAs/GaAs quantum-dot gain medium as an on-chip broadband gain on the silicon photonic chip. The free-carrier injection in a silicon PIN diode integrated in the silicon microrings will enable a fast ns-speed EO tuning. We will expand the microring free spectral range by a Vernier scheme and will adopt a discrete wavelength-sweep controlled by a field-programmable gate-array board. The result would be a fast, multi-megahertz sweep rate, and thus a short 10’s m-long fiber delay line that minimizes fiber dispersion and nonlinearity-induced laser frequency drifts and fluctuations. We will use a high-quality-factor silicon microring frequency-comb filter to narrow the instantaneous lasing linewidth to further improve the laser stability and to extend the imaging depth beyond 50 mm. We will incorporate the FDML laser in a fiber-based SS-OCT system towards 3D-imaging of 10~100 micrometer-size transparent microparticles, droplets and aerosols. 傳染病如新型冠狀病毒的主要傳播方式之一是靠含有病毒的氣溶膠和飛沫。一種能夠實時監測氣溶膠和液滴的尺寸、形態和相結構的三維 (3D) 光學成像方法可補足現有的氣溶膠檢測和成像方法，不僅能應用於大氣和環境科學中，並且可用於控制和監測通過氣溶膠和液滴傳播的傳染病。光學相干斷層掃描 (OCT) 是一種成熟的、非接觸式的、實時 3D 成像方法，通常應用於生物細胞和組織的成像，此成像方法可進一步用於研究空氣中透明微粒的成像。 具體而言，掃頻式OCT (SS-OCT) 可提供高縱向解析度，其取決於光源的頻寬與光電二極體陣列偵測器的3D 圖像數據採集速度。而傳統的傅立葉域鎖模 (FDML)掃頻激光光源通過諧振腔僅允許每個循環的激光模式通過同步掃頻濾波器，有效抑制噪聲的建立。這使得 OCT 的快速縱向掃描成為可能。 在此申請中，我們提議一種波長範圍在1260 ~ 1360nm 的混合集成頻率梳FDML激光源。此激光源將包括 (1) 半導體光放大器 (SOA)，(2) 帶有平面階梯光柵、電光 (EO) 可調微環游標濾波器和微環頻率梳濾波器的矽光子集成電路，(3) 只有幾十米長的標准單模光纖延遲線。我們將使用兩個外部 SOA 進行初步系統集成，最終實現矽光子芯片上通過異質整合直接用晶圓接合InAs/GaAs 量子點增益介質作為寬頻增益。以矽微環的矽 PIN二極管中的自由載流子注入實現納秒級速度 的EO 調諧。我們將通過游標方案擴展微環的自由光譜範圍，並將採用由現場可程式化邏輯閘陣列板控制的離散波長掃描。最終得到一個快速的、數兆赫茲的掃描速率，從而只需一條 10 米的短光纖延遲線就可大限度地減少光纖色散和非線性引起的激光頻率漂移和波動。我們將使用高品質因數的矽微環頻率梳濾波器來縮窄瞬時激光線寬，以此進一步提高激光穩定性並將成像深度擴展到 50 mm 以上。我們將結合FDML 激光與光纖的 SS-OCT 系統.，以對 10~100 微米大小的透明微粒、液滴和氣溶膠進行 3D 成像。

16203221.label: Realisation of objectives
16203221.value: Objective 1: Achievements: A fiber-based FDML laser We constructed a fiber-based FDML laser emitting in the O band wavelengths using a commercial ~110nm-bandwidth SOA and a commercial Fabry-Perot filter. The laser cavity comprised a ~3km-long single-mode fiber to synchronize the cavity round-trip time with the filter sweep frequency at 68 kHz. This achieved a stable laser output with a bandwidth of ~77.5 nm and a laser threshold of ~60 mA. The performance metrics are comparable to those reported in the literature. We designed and fabricated three key components, including (i) Echelle gratings, (ii) delay lines, and (iii) Vernier filters with electro-optic (EO) and thermo-optic (TO) tuning on SOI wafers with a thickness of 400 nm. (i) The fabricated grating dispersed a ~110 nm broadband source into two sub-bands centered at 1292 nm and at 1318 nm, consistent with our numerical simulations. (ii) Our delay lines with 1 µm-wide waveguides demonstrated a propagation loss of ~2.0 dB/cm at the O band wavelengths. (iii) Our Vernier filter comprises two cascaded microring resonators with two designed radii of 26 µm and 27 µm. Each microring is integrated vertically with a Molybdenum-based micro-heater and laterally with a p-i-n diode. The filter exhibited a Vernier expanded free spectral range (FSR) of ~70 nm. The TO tuning demonstrated an efficiency of 0.015 nm/mW up to an applied voltage of ~10 V. Under-achievements: (i) The Echelle grating did not achieve the targeted sub-band widths of ~60 nm for each passband. We target to increase the linear dispersion to approach the target performance in the upcoming fabrication. (ii) Vernier filter developments faced different challenges over three iterations. While our devices from the latest iteration successfully demonstrated the TO tuning over the target FSR, the side-lobe suppression ratio remained ~ -1 dB. To address these issues, we have revised our layout to prepare for the fourth iteration incorporating varied microring geometries, coupling lengths and gap spacing, and test structures for metal contacts and vias. Each iteration involved a cycle of designing, numerical modelling, fabrication, with exceeding ten number of masks for devices. Objective 2: Achievements: We designed and fabricated the originally proposed silicon microring frequency-comb filter. The measured FSR of ~9.3 GHz (~0.053 nm at 1310 nm) suggests that we can achieve the target FSR of 8.7 GHz upon a minor modification of the cavity round-trip length. The extracted silicon waveguide propagation loss was ~2.0 dB/cm through a successful electron-beam lithography. The comb filter reveals a measured cavity resonance linewidth of ~1.43 GHz, corresponds to a high Q-factor of ~1.6 × 10⁵. This is favorable to facilitate a narrow laser instantaneous linewidth upon linewidth narrowing below the cavity linewidth. Under-achievements: We have not integrated the frequency-comb filter with the PIC from Phase I, primarily due to ongoing unforeseen delays in completing the full PIC development cycles. Objective 3: Achievements: We successfully developed a heterogeneously integrated InGaAsP/InP multi-quantum-well (MQW) on silicon photonic platform. Our developed die-to-die atomic layer deposition-based molecular bonding technique can achieve a stable bonding yield of exceeding 95%. We developed an inductively coupled plasma reactive ion etching (ICP-RIE) process based on H2, Cl2, CH4, and Ar gases and achieved smooth III-V waveguide sidewalls. We achieved a low forward-bias resistance of 37~58 Ω, and a turn-on voltage of ~0.7 V in our fabricated InP p-i-n diodes. We characterized our fabricated 500-µm long MQW SOAs first for the C-band. Upon a bias voltage of 4 V, the SOA provides a maximum on-chip gain of 15.7 dB, with a 3-dB gain bandwidth of approximately 80 nm in the C-band (peak gain at 1537.3 nm). At room temperature, we achieved an on-chip gain of ~5 dB upon a power consumption of ~1 mW. Under-achievements: We did not pursue the originally proposed InAs/GaAs QD SOAs limited by commercial availability of the wafers. While fabrication of the O-band InGaAsP/InP MQW SOAs and heterogeneous integration onto the silicon PIC is in progress. The heterogeneous integration requires extensive process developments for at least 15 mask layers. We are developing further key process improvements, including more stable die-to-die bonding using a vacuum-oven, electron-beam evaporation for electrodes, sputtering for thick metal lift-off, and an optimized annealing for III-V surface passivation. Objective 4: Achievements: To build an OCT system completed with the signal acquisition and the post-processing from the ground up, we first constructed a free-space spectral-domain OCT (SD-OCT) setup using the O-band SOA as a broadband light source. This served as our testbed to demonstrate OCT capabilities, including interferometric signal generation, fringe detection, Fourier-domain signal processing, and axial/transverse resolution characterization. Building on this testbed, we constructed as originally proposed a swept-source OCT (SS-OCT) setup by integrating the fiber-based FDML laser from Objective 1 into a fiber-based SS-OCT testbed. The FDML laser's frequency-sweep filter produces upon a sinusoidal driving signal a nonlinear wavelength sweep in time and lacks a trigger signal that starts the sweep. To address this and to generate equidistant wavenumber sampling points, we applied a fiber-based Mach-Zehnder interferometer (MZI) with a fixed 2.7 mm path imbalance as a spectral ruler in time (a k-clock). We then simultaneously acquired the SS-OCT interference and the MZI clock signals using two balanced photodetectors for noise rejection and signal amplification. We worked together with a summer exchange undergraduate student to develop a MATLAB code for data acquisition using our SS-OCT system. The continuous data were segmented into individual wavelength sweeps while we employed the k-clock to resample the OCT interference signal onto a uniform k-space grid. Finally, we applied a discrete Fourier transform to generate the axial profile in real space. Our SS-OCT successfully reconstructed the depth profile of a 1 mm substrate glass. The measured axial OCT point-spread function resolution in air is ~44 µm (corresponding to ~33 µm in tissue, assuming a refractive index of 1.38). Under-achievements: Our measured axial resolution is worse than the theoretical ~9–10 µm Fourier-transform limit for the full 77.5 nm bandwidth due to inevitable spectral shape deviations, unoptimized filter profiles, and imperfections in the linearization in the k-space. We are investigating ways to further increase the axial resolution, including hardware and software co-optimizations. Demonstration using a frequency-comb FDML laser has not been achieved. The fixed 2.7 mm path difference with the existing fiber-based MZI (manufacturing constraint) limits the k-clock resampling. We are currently implementing an adjustable path imbalance to enable a longer coherence length and a larger axial range to image sub-mm-sized planar transparent dielectrics. Objective 5: Achievements: We imaged a sub-mm-sized transparent cover glass as a proof of concept using our fiber-based FDML laser with SS-OCT. We reconstructed the depth profile of the glass with the measured depth of 0.219 ± 0.004 mm. Under-achievements: We have not yet performed SS-OCT imaging of 10’s µm transparent dielectric particles or spray droplets/aerosols (Phase III). With the resolution improved from objective 4, we would be able to image few tens of transparent dielectric films. Current efforts focus on imaging water films on glass. We are developing an XY scanner for 3D imaging. Initial tests with an objective lens and XY scanner failed due to poor light reflection back into the fiber; we have purchased a dedicated scanning lens and are optimizing alignment.

16203221.label: Major findings and research outcome
16203221.value: 1. We demonstrated a fiber-based FDML laser using a commercial ~110 nm-bandwidth SOA and a Fabry-Perot filter in the O band. By extending the cavity with approximately a 3 km of single-mode fiber, we synchronized the cavity round-trip time to the 68 kHz sweep frequency driven by a sinusoidal signal, resulting in a swept bandwidth of ~77.5 nm and a threshold current of ~60 mA. We reported the related work in a contributed oral presentation at the SPIE Photonics West 2025. 2. We exploited this FDML source for a fiber-based SS-OCT testbed, where we applied a custom MATLAB code for data processing—including low-pass filtering for noise suppression, an MZI-based k-clock zero-crossing for resampling, and discrete Fourier transform for depth reconstruction. We demonstrated a depth profiling of a 1 mm glass slide and of a ~0.22 mm cover glass with an axial resolution of ~44 µm in air (estimated ~33 µm in biological fluids with a refractive index of 1.38). These results confirm the viability of the FDML approach for SS-OCT and establish a practical proof-of-concept imaging platform. 3. On the silicon PIC fabricated on a 400 nm SOI platform, we demonstrated four core components with key performance in the O- and/or C-bands as follows: (i) The planar Echelle grating dispersed a broadband light of ~ 120 nm into two sub-bands with bandwidth of ~13 nm in the O-band. We reported the related work at the SPIE Photonics West 2025 and at the SPIE-CLP conference on Advanced Photonics 2025 (awarded the Excellent Poster Award). (ii) The quasi-single-mode delay lines exhibited a propagation loss of ~2.0 dB/cm in the O-band and of 1.6 ~ 2 dB/cm in the C-band. (iii) The Vernier cascaded microring filters demonstrated an expanded free spectral range of ~70 nm in the O-band, with a thermo-optic tuning efficiency of 0.015 nm/mW up to a bias voltage of ~10 V. (iv) The microring frequency-comb filter demonstrated a free spectral range of ~9.3 GHz (~0.053 nm) and a resonance linewidth of ~1.43 GHz (Q ≈ 1.6 × 10⁵). 4. On the heterogeneously integrated III-V on silicon SOA, we designed and fabricated 500µm-long InGaAsP/InP quantum-well SOAs, demonstrating a ~90 nm gain bandwidth and a ~10 dB on-chip gain for the C-band at ~8 mA injection current, with a good die-to-die molecular bonding yield, providing a foundation for heterogeneously integrated SOA for realizing FDMLs.

16203221.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16203221.value: To demonstrate the hybrid-integrated FDML laser for the SS-OCT over the next months, we are currently addressing in the order of priority: 1. Design optimization and fabrication of the heterogeneously integrated InGaAsP/InP multi-quantum-well SOAs on the silicon PIC for the O-band. 2. Design optimization and fabrication of the cascaded microring Vernier filters with EO tuning, using an updated mask layout comprising additional test structures to resolve the contact reliability, and with various microring geometries, coupling lengths and gap spacing to address the target resonance filter linewidth and the side-lobe suppression ratio. 3. We will integrate either the on-chip SOA from 1) with an off-chip filter or the on-chip frequency sweep filter from 2) with an off-chip SOA, together with the fiber delay line to demonstrate the hybrid-integrated FDML laser. We will further implement the FDML SS-OCT testbed for imaging dielectric particles with an enhanced resolution by refining the hardware (including a free-space MZI) and the software (resampling algorithms).

16203221.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16203221.value: This project developed the design, fabrication and characterization of a silicon photonics chip with a heterogeneously integrated semiconductor optical amplifier and a hybrid integrated fiber delay line towards the realization of a compact, fast-wavelength-sweeping pulsed laser source emitting in the near-infrared wavelengths (1260 – 1360 nm) for optical coherence tomography applications. The primary research outcomes featured the demonstration of a myriad of low-loss, tunable silicon photonic components, including a tunable Vernier filter with a large spectral range, a planar grating that disperses over a wide spectral band, a frequency comb filter with a narrow resonance linewidth and an on-chip delay line. We further realized heterogeneously integrating a semiconductor optical amplifier on our silicon photonic chip. The team also successfully built a fiber-based wavelength-sweep pulsed laser testbed that demonstrated as a proof of concept the holographic imaging of a transparent sub-millimeter-thick glass slide with few tens of micrometer depth resolution. Our project demonstration paves the way for future real-time imaging of transparent dielectric microparticles and aerosols using hybrid-integrated wavelength-sweep laser sources for infection control, air-quality monitoring and environmental studies.

16203321.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16203321.value: Additive manufacturing is a key element in the advanced manufacturing revolution. Direct additive or deposition techniques afford complete freedom in controlling the geometric details and material composition in three-dimensional fabrication. They provide new routes for manufacturing cellular metamaterials with mechanical properties of high strength, lightweight, and other properties and with tremendous potential for aerospace, automotive, marine and offshore, and biomedical applications. Our project focuses on an outstanding challenge that must be overcome to exploit the full potential of cellular metallic structures manufactured through additive manufacturing. We focus on a new class of low-density mechanical metamaterials known as plate-lattices, which include recently discovered types, such as the “cubic+octet” type, that exhibit mechanical properties at the theoretical limit of stiffness and strength. These metamaterials can also be tailored with an isotropic response in stiffness and (nearly) in initial plastic yielding. However, the closed-cell modality of the plate lattices severely restricts their functionalities and fabrication, especially for powder-bed and resin-bath techniques. Meanwhile, open-cell modality is important for multi-functional applications, such as heat and mass transfers. We propose the development of open-cell cellular materials with the plate-lattice architecture and 3D fabrication of the cellular materials with substantial load-bearing and elastic buckling strength properties. If prominent cut-out features are created in plates of the primitive cell, the plate lattices would exhibit an open-cell modality in their fabrication with powder-bed and resin-bath techniques. We plan to use the most advanced 3D printing techniques, micro-SLM and Projection Micro Stereolithography (PμSL), for the fabrication and testing of the newly developed mechanical metamaterials. A major achievement of the project will be its demonstration of the superior mechanical properties that can be retained in the open-cell plate lattices at high porosity while providing open-cell modality. Such lightweight open-cell metamaterials will be highly valuable because of their lightweight and multi-functional potentials. The development of this project will support porosity-targeted high-performance applications and provide a quantum leap in the deployment of the additive manufacturing technologies to advance further the speed and quality of innovation. 增材製造是先進製造的關鍵要素。直接添加或沉積技術在控制三維製造中的幾何細節和材料成分方面提供了完全的自由。它們為製造具有高強度、輕質和其他特性的細胞超材料提供了新的途徑，在航空航天、汽車、海洋和近海以及生物醫學應用方面具有巨大潛力。 我們的項目專注於一個突出的挑戰，必須克服這一挑戰才能充分利用通過增材製造的製造蜂窩金屬結構的潛力。我們專注於一類新的低密度機械超材料，稱為板格，其中包括最近發現的類型，例如“立方+八位組”類型，其在剛度和強度的理論極限下表現出機械性能。這些超材料還可以根據剛度和（幾乎）初始塑性屈服的各向同性響應進行定制。然而，板格的閉孔模式嚴重限制了它們的功能和製造，特別是對於粉末床和樹脂浴技術。同時，開孔模式對於多功能應用很重要，例如傳熱和傳質。 我們建議開發具有板-晶格結構的開孔蜂窩材料，以及具有顯著承重和彈性屈曲強度特性的蜂窩材料的 3D 製造。如果在原始細胞的板中創建突出的切口特徵，則板格將在其使用粉末床和樹脂浴技術的製造中表現出開孔模式。我們計劃使用最先進的 3D 打印技術、微 SLM 和投影微立體光刻 (PμSL) 打印來製造和測試新開發的機械超材料。 該項目的一個主要成就將是它展示了可以在高孔隙率的開孔板晶格中保留的優異機械性能，同時提供開孔模態。這種輕量級的開孔超材料由於其輕質和多功能的潛力而具有很高的價值。該項目的開發將支持以孔隙率為目標的高性能應用，並為增材製造技術的部署提供巨大的飛躍，以進一步提高創新的速度和質量。

16203321.label: Realisation of objectives
16203321.value: For objective 1, we have fully achieved the design, analysis, and validation of open-cell cubic symmetric plate lattices (PLSs) through integrated theoretical modeling, numerical simulation, and performance verification. Designing open-cell 3D plate lattice structures (PLSs) involves two parts: failure analysis of PLS, and the determination of the optimal location and size of cutouts. Three typical PLSs with cubic symmetry, namely body-centered cubic (BCC), face-centered cubic (FCC), and simple cubic (SC), were studied. We have developed theoretical and finite element (FE) methods to investigate the failure modes, i.e., plastic yielding and elastic buckling, and the corresponding strength of PLSs. To determine the optimal locations and sizes of cutouts for each type of PLSs, we have developed linear statics and buckling analysis FE models of the unit cells for the PLSs with periodic boundary conditions. First, the optimal locations are identified using a combined theoretical and FE method based on Rayleigh-Ritz quotient of the first-order buckling mode. Surprisingly, we find that creating cutouts at proper locations can even increase the buckling eigenvalue of PLSs under certain compressive loads. Using the proposed method, we have determined the optimal cutout locations for the three types of PLSs. In contrast, the traditional method of designing open-cell PLSs with holes at the center of each plate can decrease the buckling eigenvalue. Second, the optimal sizes of cutouts are determined numerically. Starting with the minimum size that allows cleaning trapped materials which is determined according to the 3D printing system, buckling and static FEAs are carried out on perforated PLSs with a series of cutout sizes. We have found through extensive numerical analysis that the buckling eigenvalues of all PLSs first increase and then decrease with increasing cutout sizes. Therefore, the optimal sizes are determined at the peak of the buckling eigenvalue vs. cutout size curves. To further validate the designed open-cell PLSs, nonlinear FE analyses have been carried out to simulate the post-buckling behavior of those PLSs. The results show that PLSs at low relative densities could support stresses beyond the elastic buckling stress; PLSs at high relative densities would fail before elastic buckling stress due to the plastic yielding. In both situations above, open-cell PLSs using our design method outperform traditional perforation methods in terms of compressive strength, and approach the compressive strength of unperforated, i.e., closed-cell PLSs. Compared to traditional perforation methods, our open-cell PLSs achieve 20-30% higher compressive strength and approach the performance of closed-cell PLSs, while satisfying open-cell multifunctional requirements. For objective 2, to fabricate the open-cell metamaterials in controlled porosity with advanced micro-SLM fabrication technique to meet weight-targeted performance requirements. The optimal three PLSs with cutouts that maximize the compressive buckling strength designed in objective 1 have been fabricated using an in-house-built high-precision micro-SLM system and SS316L powders. The plate thickness is designed at 85 μm, approaching the highest resolution of this system and the lowest density of printable PLSs. For comparison, the minimum printable wall thicknesses of conventional SLM systems are usually 150-200 μm. The printing parameters including laser power, scan pattern, and scan speed have been optimized for thin-walled structures. The printing orientations have been optimized to avoid large overhanging plates. The fabrication results verify that all the proposed PLSs are successfully printed without significant distortions using the micro-SLM system and most remaining powders were easily removed. A low relative density of 5.51% is achieved for SC PLS, which is the lowest among the printed PLSs in existing literature. However, the plate thickness deviations from the design values are observed for as-printed PLSs. The plate thicknesses of PLSs and their relations with inclination angles are evaluated using an optical microscope. We find that the walls with a 45˚ inclination angle have a thickness of 108 μm, thicker than 88 μm for vertical walls. As a result, the as-printed relative densities of PLSs are all lager than the as-designed values. For objective 3, To fabricate open-cell plate lattices through the available Projection Micro Stereolithography (PμSL) fabrication processes and demonstrate its macro- and nanoscale capabilities. This objective has been fully achieved by leveraging PμSL-based two-photon polymerization (TPP) technology, successfully fabricating open-cell plate lattices with precise structural control and validating the process’s macroscale process feasibility and nanoscale feature fabrication capabilities. The core fabrication process adopted PμSL (Nanoscribe PPGT+ machine) with IP-Dip resin, combined with subsequent conformal coating and template etching, forming a complete workflow for open-cell plate lattice fabrication. This workflow integrates high-resolution 3D printing, ceramic film deposition, and template removal, enabling the realization of open-cell plate lattices from design to final product. We successfully fabricated lattice structures with macroscale and nanoscale overall dimensions composed of periodic open-cell plate lattice unit cells. The unit cell size was precisely controlled, and the lattice could be scaled to 5×5×5 or 6×6×6 unit cell arrays, verifying macroscale structural integrity and process repeatability. The fabricated plate lattices exhibited distinct open-cell properties, with interconnected internal pores and a porosity range of 94%–98.5%. Residual polymer templates were completely removed via oxygen plasma etching and FIB milling, ensuring unobstructed pore channels and validating the open-cell design’s successful realization. Objective 4 has been fully achieved through a comprehensive test program covering multi-dimensional evaluations of fabricated specimens. Key metrics including printing quality, material composition validity, and core mechanical properties (stiffness, load-bearing strength, buckling strength) have been systematically characterized and verified. For printing quality evaluation, scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and voxel-based 3D reconstruction to evaluate printing quality of PμSL-fabricated polymer templates and subsequent ceramic shells. Reconstructed surfaces were validated against SEM images, confirming geometric fidelity with deviation <5% for smooth surfaces. Comprehensive mechanical performance testing has been conducted. Measured effective Young’s modulus via uniaxial compression tests and RVE-based FEM simulation. For 5.5% relative density ceramic aerogels, the effective Young’s modulus was 1.2–1.8 GPa. Performed linear buckling analysis (periodic/anti-periodic boundary conditions) and nonlinear post-buckling tests. Experimental post-buckling behavior of 1.5% aerogels showed stable deformation without catastrophic collapse, validating buckling resistance. Extensive small-strain and large-strain compression tests have been conducted to study the mechanical properties and failure behavior of PLSs. Small-strain load-unload compression tests are designed and conducted to measure the Young’s modulus of the fabricated PLSs. The small-strain testing results show that the printed stainless steel PLSs exhibit superior specific Young’s modulus among the 3D printed lattice structures in literature. Large-strain compression tests have been conducted to test the strength and failure behavior of fabricated PLSs. Each sample is loaded quasi-statically to failure with a camera (Sony SLTA57) to capture the deformation behavior. The 0.2% offset strength is calculated from the stress-strain data. Results clearly show the layer-by-layer buckling failure mode for all three PLSs. Overall, the objective of extensive specimen testing and multi-dimensional performance evaluation was fully achieved. The test results not only validated the fabrication quality and material reliability but also provided critical data support for the design optimization of ultralight nanostructured ceramics.

16203321.label: Major findings and research outcome
16203321.value: The major findings for Open-Cell Plate-Lattice development mainly including three key aspects. First, we focus on nanoceramics and low-dimensional materials, which have significant applications in various engineering fields. Next, we employ advanced fabrication techniques, including cutting-edge additive manufacturing technologies. Finally, we incorporate the mechanical design aspect by exploring the architected design of nanostructured materials in three dimensions. Together, these elements represent a comprehensive approach to advancing the field of materials design. In this research, a continuous seamless shell-based configuration was utilized for nano-architected aerogels. It was demonstrated that this configuration results in stronger aerogels compared to the hollow tube design used in previous works. The results also showed that the strength of the nano-architected aerogels is significantly higher than that of conventionally synthesized aerogels, highlighting the importance of engineered design in the internal configuration of the aerogels. There are numerous TPMS geometries that can be employed for nano- architected aerogels. The results of this research can guide future re searchers on how to consider manufacturing imperfections and how to utilize the constant mean curvature of the shell as a design variable to enhance the performance of nano-architected aerogels. When comparing nano-architected aerogels to conventional aero gels, several important factors should be considered beyond just mechanical properties. One significant aspect is the surface area; conventional aerogels boast a much larger surface area, typically ranging from 350 to 700 m2 /g, while nano-architected aerogels have a surface area of only a few square meters per gram. This larger surface area is advantageous for applications such as sensors. However, nano- architected aerogels feature smaller-scale microstructures, which may help compensate for their lower surface area in specific uses. Additionally, the fabrication scale is a crucial consideration. Nano- architected aerogels cannot be produced on a macroscale, whereas conventional aerogels cannot be fabricated on a microscale. This limitation means that nano-architected aerogels are particularly well-suited for micro devices, where conventional aerogels may not be applicable. This work primarily focuses on the solid mechanics and materials science aspects of nano-architected aerogels. The same fabrication process can be applied to create aerogels with more functional materials, such as TiO2 , MXene, and transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs). Additionally, this technique can be utilized to fabricate composite and mixed oxide nanostructured ceramics, which have important applications in sensing technologies.

16203321.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16203321.value: This research focused on the solid mechanics and materials science aspects of 3D nanostructured ceramics, more functional nano-architected aerogels made from materials such as TiO2, MXene, and TMDs can also be fabricated. With advancements in microfabrication methods, techniques can be developed to integrate these nanostructured materials into real devices for applications like sensing. Additionally, there is promising potential for research on mixed oxide nanostructured ceramics, which can also be fabricated using this method and may have applications in gas sensing. Further research opportunities exist for ALD nanofilms, particularly in studying the strength of thinner films. This may require the exploration of alternative fabrication and experimental techniques.

16203321.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16203321.value: Traditionally synthesized ceramic aerogels possess a random internal configuration, which leads to poor mechanical properties. One effective strategy to address this issue is through architected design. This research explores a bottom-up synthesis approach to fabricate ceramic aerogels with an engineered internal configuration. The architected design specifically means creating periodic cellular structures with defined unit-cells. In this work, nano-architected ceramic aerogels composed of a 50–200nm Al2O3 film with a relative density of 1.5–6 % are fabricated. A seamless shell-based configuration is employed, diverging from previous works that utilized hollow-tube designs. Due to their slender nature, these nanostructured ceramics are prone to instability failure and are sensitive to manufacturing imperfections. The most critical imperfection in this fabrication process is the geometric deviation between the designed model and the final fabricated structure. This research studies the nature and extent of these geometric deviations and investigates their impact on mechanical performance. The results indicate that the strength of the nano-architected aerogels in this study is significantly higher than that of conventional aerogels and those with hollow-tube designs.

16203421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16203421.value: 服務機器人在我們的生活中扮演越來越重要的角色，輔助人們處理家務、工作和公共服務。在目前的全球公共衛生危機中，機器人的作用尤為突出。很多交給機器人的任務需要使用工具來完成，但專門的工具可能不是常常能獲得，因此需要機器人靈活的從動態環境中選擇具有相同功能的物品進行替換。這個過程叫功能示能。例如機器人找不到托盤來裝水果，可以嘗試用砧板替代。這樣的場景下幾乎不可能預先將所有可能性都預先編寫入機器人中。一個更可行的方法是讓機器人在實際使用中通過落地知識指導自我探索以及從人的展示中學習工具使用。 之前機器人領域關於物體示能研究主要側重對物體的物理操作。但神經科學和心理學提出對物體的操作可能不能提供充足的關於其功能的信息。目前只有極少數的工作在工具置換場景下研究物理示能，但因為數據集的限制僅覆蓋極少的物體和操作。 本項目汲取心理學理論中人通過經歷和展示學習示能關係的經驗，提出一個基於推理的可擴展的方法來教授機器人日常物品的功能示能知識。本項目在我們過去的人-機器人交互和自然語言處理研究的基礎上，將目標分成四個關聯任務：1）將機械知識落地於物理常識；2）基於推理進行物體選擇；3）交互式的通過人類用戶的展示來驗証推斷出的功能示能；以及4）構建拓展現實模擬系統進行測試實驗。

16203821.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16203821.value: Used products, e.g., electronics, have been generated at an ever faster rate since product life scan is getting shorter and shorter. Used products are not wastes but precious resource. How to collect used products becomes an important business problem for firms who pursue the substantial economic value of product remanufacturing and to comply with regulatory policies imposed by governments. This research proposal aims to design the optimal collection policy for used products when a manufacturer sells generation products to strategic customers. Depending on whether the manufacturer should impose conditions on the compensation for returned goods, we analyze both conditional (trade-in) and unconditional (buy-back) collection policies that take place in practice. Although two policies are studied separately in literature, the prior research did not jointly evaluate their performance when a secondary market exists for trading used products. With the rapid development of E-commerce, customers nowadays have easy access to a C2C platform to trade used products. This proposed research is among the first to investigate the implications of a secondary market on the design of the manufacturer’s used product collection policies. Our preliminary results show that the existence of a secondary market can significantly change the manufacturer’s preference between these two policies, and underscores the importance of taking the secondary market into account when the manufacturer designs its used product collection policy. Based on the preliminary results, we will develop a general model that considers more realistic situations including heterogenous beliefs of product valuations, dynamic market diffusion, and the option of purchasing used products from different channels. We will also extend the model to a supply chain system, and investigate how the used product collection policies provided by different partners affect purchasing behavior of customers, the profit of each partner and the entire supply chain. The proposed research will help to understand the impacts of strategic customer behavior and the secondary market on the choice of used product collection policy, and provide manufacturers with guidance on the design of the collection policy for used products. 随着产品生命周期的变短, 二手产品 (比如电子产品) 的产生速度越来越快。二手产品本身具有使用价值。对于追求资源回收产品再制造的潜在经济价值并且遵守政府施加的监管政策的公司来说, 如何收集旧产品是一个重要的业务问题。此课题旨在研究面对策略型顾客的制造商如何设计最优的旧产品回收政策。根据制造商对产品回收的限制条件, 我们研究了两种在实际中常见的有条件回收 (以旧换新) 和无条件回收 (回购) 政策。 尽管文献中分别研究了两种回收政策, 但是目前的研究并未在二手市场存在的情况下比较两种回收政策。随着电子商务的迅猛发展, 越来越多的消费者选择在客户对客户的平台上直接交易二手产品。我们的课题将是第一个研究二手市场对制造商旧产品回收政策设计的影响。我们的初步结果表明, 二手市场的存在对制造商选择回收政策 (以旧换新或者回购) 有本质的影响。这个结果进一步说明了制造商在制定旧产品回收政策时必须考虑二手市场存在的重要性。基于初步结果，我们将开发更加通用的模型，该模型考虑更现实的情况，比如消费者对产品有不同估值, 市场规模动态演化, 以及多渠道购买二手产品。我们还将模型扩展到一个供应链系统, 研究不同的旧产品回收政策如何影响客户的购买行为, 每个合作伙伴的利润以及整个供应链的利润。此课题的研究将有助于进一步加深策略型消费者和二手市场对旧产品回收政策选择的影响, 并为制造商提供有关旧产品政策设计的指导。

16204121.value: 蛋白質序列分析的尖峰隨機矩陣模型

16204121.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16204121.value: 數據科學是現代科學探索和發現的支柱。在生物應用中，測序技術的進步產生了大量關於各種生物體和病原體的數據。這種複雜的高維數據可用於產生對生物功能和結構的新發現，並可指導臨床治療的改進和疫苗的開發。 生物序列分析中的一項重要任務是從有限的高維數據樣本中推斷出可靠的相關模型。由於眾所周知的維數災難，經典的估計方法經常失效，因此開發更先進的技術是必要的。提議的項目就是在試圖解決這個問題。該項目的靈感來自於主要研究者(PI)最近的結果，其中來自生物數據集的經驗證據揭示了一種協方差結構，這種結構很容易讓人聯想到隨機矩陣理論(RMT)中所謂的尖峰模型(spiked models)。這種對應關係被用來提出了特別的“噪聲清除” 的協方差估計方法從而改進了關於丙型肝炎病毒和艾滋病毒的某些蛋白質的生物學推斷，並提出了新的疫苗設計方案。然而，之前所提出的方法應用範圍有限，尤其是對於較大的蛋白質或較小的數據集效果不佳。因此，一個可靠的研究方向是應用RMT來開發更具魯棒性的優化解決方案，這可以為未來一系列生物數據集進行有意義的生物學推斷。 最近的研究提出了一個能用於高維尖峰模型的協方差估計的優化框架。因此，提議的項目旨在應用這個框架解決之前的方法的局限性。該項目旨在放寬許多假設，研發出全新的一類從尖峰模型中得到的為生物序列分析量身定製的估計量。理論上本項目將開發最優的協方差和逆協方差估計方法，用於解釋生物序列數據的已知特徵，包括對生物序列數據的離散性、稀疏性、遺傳性和其他一系列性質的解釋。這個全新的方法將在模擬數據集上進行評估，並應用於生物遺傳序列數據相關性的研究，以解釋其生物學上的的功能和/或結構上的意義。這些方法還將用於擴展PI最近的工作，主要包括基於生物遺傳序列的相關性分析來找到傳染性疾病免疫靶點，從而指導疫苗的設計。

16204221.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16204221.value: High-efficient monolithic DC-DC converters are always in great demand in industry. Given the recent increase in the point of load converter applications, an ultra-low voltage-conversion-ratio DC-DC converter is needed. Currently this type of ultra-low voltage-conversion-ratio converter is implemented with multi-stage DC-DC converters, which have low power efficiency, or require very expensive GaN devices. To build an economical monolithic converter with an ultra-low voltage-conversion-ratio, a new type of DC-DC converter topology must be developed. In recent years, hybrid converters that combine the switched capacitor type converters and conventional switched inductor type converter have been developed, and they are a promising candidate for this application. In this project, a novel monolithic hybrid DC-DC converter topology will be developed to achieve an ultra-low conversion ratio and with improved power efficiency. Different control schemes will also be investigated to study the stability and response time of the hybrid converter. 16204221.label: Realisation of objectives
16204221.value: All three objectives have been completed successfully, as have been detailed in Hon-Piu Lam's PhD thesis [Lam 2023B]. Objective 1: To develop a hybrid converter topology that can provide a feasible ultra-low voltage-conversion-ratio with high power efficiency. A hybrid DC-DC converter has been proposed: it is an integration of a switched-capacitor converter (SCC) and a switched-inductor buck converter. We use VCR = 1/24X as an example. In Phase 1, CF is serially connected to C1, C2 and C3 that are connected in parallel; and in Phase 2, CF is connected in parallel to C1, C2 and C3 that are connected in series. This action gives a SCC with VCR = (1/4)X. When turn to the buck converter, in Phase 1, the input voltage is then (1/4)Vin = 6V for charging the inductor; and in Phase 2, the inductor gyrates the current from ground to the output voltage of Vo = 1V. Hence, the ideal duty ratio of the buck converter is D = 1/6 = 0.167. This duty ratio allows the buck converter to be more efficient. It is also clear that the duration of Phase 1 is DT, and that of Phase 2 is D'T = (1–D)T. More importantly, careful examination shows that the inductor current, which is also the load current and is thus the largest current, passes through only one switch for both the charging and discharging phases. The schematic of the power stage of the hybrid DC-DC converter can be found in [Lam 2023A] and [Lam 2023B]. Objective 2: To develop a control scheme for the proposed hybrid converter. The control scheme consists of many components: (1) Pre-charge circuit for flying capacitors (2) Soft-start controller: analog and digital speed control, soft-start open-loop compensator (3) Steady-state closed-loop compensator (4) Bootstrap gate drives for power transistors in different voltage domains The schematic of the complete controller of the hybrid DC-DC converter can be found in [Lam 2023A] and [Lam 2023B]. Objective 3: To build a prototype to demonstrate the performance of the proposed hybrid converter. A prototype of the hybrid DC-DC converter has been designed and fabricated in a 180nm BCD (bipolar-CMOS-DMOS) process. An ultra-low voltage conversion ratio of 48V-to-1V has been achieved by the hybrid converter, with control schemes working smoothly for both the switched-capacitor sub-converter and the switched-inductor sub-converter. The converter can self-start, and all the power supplies for the drivers switching at various voltage level domains were implemented (unlike many research designs from academia). Measurement results were reported in [Lam 2023A] and [Lam 2023B]. References: [Lam 2023A] H. P. Lam, W. H. Ki and P. K. T. Mok, "4C 3-level hybrid buck converter for 12~48V-to-1V point-of-load applications," IEEE Custom IC Conf. (CICC), San Antonio, TX, April 2023, 2 pages. [Lam 2023B] H. P. Lam, Monolithic Hybrid DC-DC Converter with Ultra-Low Voltage-Conversion-Ratio: An Evolution of 3-Level Hybrid Buck Converter, PhD Thesis, HKUST, Aug. 2023.

16204221.label: Major findings and research outcome
16204221.value: The goal of this research is to realize a hybrid converter (switched-inductor converter integrated with a switched capacitor converter (SCC)) that achieves a very low voltage conversion ratio (VCR). Our first work is a 2-phase four-capacitor (4C) 3-level hybrid buck converter [Conference Paper #1], by embedding a series-parallel SCC with VCR_SCC = (1/4)X, bootstrapped gate drivers, and controller all integrated on the same chip using 180nm BCD process, while CF and C1~3 are off-chip power capacitors. High power conversion efficiency (PCE) is attained by designing the inductor current (= load current) to pass through only one switch for both the charging and discharging phases. The measured peak PCE was 93% when the supply voltage was Vin = 12V, the output voltage Vo = 1V and the output current Io = 3A (VCR = (1/12)X). The converter also worked for the case of Vin = 54V and Vo = 1V (VCR = (1/54)X). In our second work, the hybrid converter achieves a VCR of D^2/2 [Conference Paper #2]. Therefore, 5V power transistors can be used in the main current path that significantly increases efficiency. An adaptive dead-time control and an anti-shoot-through buffer are proposed to further enhance efficiency. With VIN = 24V and VO = 1V, this converter achieves a simulated peak efficiency of 94.5% at 1A output. The third hybrid converter is a D^2 buck converter consisting of two buck converters in cascade, with the first handling high input voltage and low input current, and the second using low-voltage power switches to enhance efficiency [Conference Paper #3]. By implementing a sawtooth generator with well-defined thresholds, the undershoot detector realizes both delay-insensitive response and adaptive on-time extension during load transient. This work is designed in a 180nm BCD process. References: [Conference Paper #1] H. P. Lam, W. H. Ki and P. K. T. Mok, "4C 3-level hybrid buck converter for 12~48V-to-1V point-of-load applications," IEEE Custom IC Conf. (CICC), San Antonio, TX, April 2023, 2 pages. [Conference Paper #2] G. Chang, Y. Liu, W. H. Ki, "A 24V-to-1V hybrid converter with adaptive dead time control for point-of-load applications," IEEE Int. Symp. of Circ. and Syst. (ISCAS), Singapore, May 2024, 4 pages. [Conference Paper #3] L. Zhu, W. H. Ki, Y. Zhong, X. Ma, J. Jiang, "D^2 buck converter with delay-insensitive response and adaptive on-time extension during load transient," IEEE Int. Symp. of Circ. and Syst. (ISCAS), Singapore, May 2024, 4 pages.

16204221.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16204221.value: We realize that hard switching between capacitors causes charge redistribution and is the culprit for low efficiency. We are designing hybrid converters that only perform soft switching by always charging or discharging any capacitors through the inductor. Moreover, each additional capacitor needs at least three more power switches for connecting to the capacitor matrix, and hence, the number of capacitors should be minimized. We are exhausting all two-capacitor topologies to find the optimal one.

16204221.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16204221.value: There is high demand for power converters to have ultra-low voltage conversion ratios (VCRs) with wide input voltage (Vin) range (12V ~ 54V) that realize low output voltage (Vo) for Point-of-Load (PoL) applications. A simple buck converter has low power conversion efficiency (PCE) because the duty ratio D is too small, with D < Vo/Vin << 1. Using a hybrid power converter with a step-down switched-capacitor converter (SCC) could increase the duty ratio of the buck converter, but existing topologies require using two power switches in the main current path. Our proposed 4C 3-level hybrid buck converter attains high PCE by having only one power switch in the main current path that charges and discharges the inductor of the buck converter. While two power switches are needed in charging and discharging most of the flying capacitors, these power transistors can be smaller as the time available is longer, which is equal to D'T = (1–D)T ~ T, as D << 1. The 4C 3L converter was designed using 180nm BCD (bipolar-CMOS-DMOS) process, and measurement results showed that it attains the peak PCE of 93% when Vin = 12V, Vo = 1V, at an output current of Io = 3A.

16204421.value: To determine the bond-slip behaviour between the SHCC and steel rebar of various sizes, for different concrete cover thicknesses. To understand the bond behaviour of a carbon fiber-reinforced polymer (CFRP) strip encased inside SHCC, which governs its load-carrying capacity in the CFRP-SHCC repair system. Various parameters such as surface treatment, length, thickness and width of the strip will be studied. Effects of various parameters such as location of the strip end, strip width and strip thickness will be studied experimentally. Finite element analysis will then be performed to provide numerical results for comparing with test data and to provide better understanding of the failure mechanism. To design the appropriate repair, with the use of CFRP and SHCC, for beam members with a larger size (400mm x 200mm section) where either the flexural reinforcements have 50% of area loss, or some shear reinforcements are completely corroded away over part of its length.
