16204421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16204421.value: Infrastructure deterioration is a big problem in many countries around the world. For reinforced concrete structures, which make up a large proportion of civil infrastructure, steel corrosion is a major cause of deterioration. Under severe environments, such as coastal regions, where sea spray carries salt to the structure surface, or cold regions, where salt is employed for de-icing, corrosion can become very severe, leading to significant loss in the steel reinforcement area and reduction in load-carrying capacity that will affect structural safety. To renovate the structure, the conventional approach is to add a new piece of steel reinforcing bar to compensate for the steel area loss. However, a long lap length of 40 times the new rebar diameter is required for load transfer between the existing and new rebars, so a large amount of sound concrete has to be removed on both sides of the corroded region. This will lead to significant increase in repair time and cost. In an ongoing research project (RGC GRF 16211617), the PI and his team have shown that the reduced load capacity of high-yield steel rebars with 20–25% steel area loss (depending on the cover) can be fully compensated for with the use of high-strength strain-hardening cementitious composites (SHCC) as the repair mortar. With the high bond strength between SHCC and rebar, the required length for load transfer, and hence the time and cost associated with concrete removal, can also be significantly reduced. The present study aims at extending the idea to members with up to 50% loss of reinforcement area, by the incorporation of a carbon fiber reinforced polymer (CFRP) strip into the SHCC. For the proper design of this composite repair system, pioneering studies will be conducted on the interaction between SHCC and the embedded CFRP strip. Specifically, combined experimental/numerical approaches will be developed to (i) derive the shear stress vs displacement relation at the CFRP/SHCC interface which governs stress transfer and debonding failure, and (ii) understand and model the failure mechanism of cover separation which may occur at the end of the CFRP strip. Based on the findings, design will be carried out for the repair of beam members with severe area loss of steel reinforcements, and verified by the testing of corresponding members. Successful completion of the project will demonstrate the potential of a new and efficient repair technique for concrete structures showing severe steel corrosion. 基礎設施惡化是世界上許多國家面對的一個大問題，對於在民用基礎設施中佔很大比例的鋼筋混凝土結構來說，鋼筋鏽蝕是其劣化的主要原因。在沿海地區，海浪或海風會將鹽分帶到結構表面，在寒冷地區，鹽分常用於除冰，在此等惡劣環境下，腐蝕會變得非常嚴重，導致鋼筋面積的顯著減少，因而降低結構的承載能力，對安全產生影響。對結構進行修復，傳統的做法是增加一根新的鋼筋來彌補鋼筋面積的損失，然而，現有鋼筋和新鋼筋之間的荷載傳遞需要長達40倍新鋼筋直徑的搭接長度，因此必須在腐蝕區域的兩側清除大量的完好混凝土，這將導致維修時間和成本的顯著增加。在一個正在進行的研究項目 (RGC GRF 16211617) 中，PI 和他的團隊發現，面積損失達到 20-25%（取決於覆蓋層）的高強鋼筋，使用高強度應變硬化水泥基複合材料（SHCC）修補砂漿，可以完全恢復其降低了的承載能力。由於 SHCC 和鋼筋之間的高粘結強度，荷載傳遞所需的長度，以及與拆除混凝土相關的時間和成本，也可以大幅減少。本研究旨在通過將碳纖維增強聚合物 (CFRP) 條納入 SHCC，將這一修補方法擴展到鋼筋面積損失高達 50% 的構件。為了正確設計該複合修復系統，將對 SHCC 和嵌入式 CFRP 條帶之間的相互作用進行開創性研究。具體而言，將聯合使用實驗和數值方法以 (i) 推導出控制應力傳遞和脫粘破壞的 CFRP/SHCC 界面處的剪切應力與位移關係，以及 (ii) 理解和模擬可能發生在 CFRP 條末端的鋼筋保護層分離機制，根據研究結果，對鋼筋面積損失嚴重的梁構件進行修復設計，並通過相應構件的測試來作驗證。該項目的成功完成將展示一種新的、有效的修復技術在鋼筋嚴重腐蝕的混凝土結構中的應用潛力。

16204421.label: Realisation of objectives
16204421.value: This project aims at developing a novel repair technique for reinforced concrete members with significant loss of steel rebar area due to corrosion. Specifically, after removing the spalled concrete around the corroded rebar, the void will be filled with strain hardening cementitious composites (SHCC). In addition, carbon fiber reinforced polymer (CFRP) strip will be embedded inside the SHCC. With both the SHCC and CFRP providing tensile load carrying capacity, the addition of a new steel rebar, which requires time-intensive and costly concrete removal to provide sufficient lap length, is no longer necessary. For the repair, a high strength SHCC made with Portland cement (PC), silica fume (SF) and polypropylene fiber (PP) was employed. In parallel with the investigations on the repair method, more sustainable mixes were being developed with the use of fly ash, calcined clay and limestone. Several sustainable SHCCs with similar performance to the PC/SF mix but much lower carbon emissions have been identified for practical repair application in the future. For the CFRP, a standard method to prepare CFRP plates of various thicknesses was developed and the consistency of mechanical properties was verified with tensile testing following ASTM standard. All the objectives of the proposal have been fully achieved. For objective 1, bond tests were carried out on high yield steel rebar with different diameters (D = 20/25/32mm) and cover thickness (1D, 1.5D and 2D) placed at 4D embedment length in high strength SHCC. To analyse the bond-slip behaviour, a finite element model was developed, with nonlinear SHCC behaviour described by the continuous damage plasticity (CDP) model. In view of the strong mechanical interaction between the deformed steel surface and SHCC (which exhibits high resistance to local cracking), perfect bonding was assumed at the rebar/SHCC interface while the detailed surface geometry was not considered. This approach greatly simplifies the model development and enhances computational efficiency. The computed load vs displacement relations and failure mode for all the specimens were in good agreements with test results. The ‘simplified’ computational approach can hence be employed to analyse bond failure (resulted from SHCC damage and deformation at the mesoscale) under practical loading conditions, thus obtaining the proper bond length of the steel rebar to achieve sufficient load transfer to the patch to compensate for a specific steel area loss. For objective 2, a standard method was developed for applying sand particles on the CFRP surface to enhance CFRP-SHCC interaction. 5 different sand sizes have been employed. Using a pull-out set-up designed and fabricated in our laboratory, bond tests were performed on strips embedded in SHCC blocks. The highest bond capacity was obtained for 80-120 mesh sand, as smaller sand size would reduce surface roughness while larger sand particles would separate easily from the epoxy resin. Using strips with optimal surface condition, additional tests on CFRP strips were performed to study the effect of strip thickness, length and width on the pull-out behaviour. The pull-out load approaches an asymptotic value when the CFRP length is increased. With increasing thickness, the pull-out load increases but the CFRP stress (load/area) decreases. Such trends are consistent with predictions from shear lag theory and fracture mechanics. For objective 3, a finite element model of the test specimen was set up with interface elements placed between the CFRP and SHCC. The bond-slip relation at the interface was back calculated from the test results. With the bond-slip relation derived from one set of specimens, the load vs displacement behaviour for all other specimens can be properly derived. Such a relation can hence be taken as the interfacial property for determining the CFRP bond length in a repair. For objective 4, tensile test was performed on specimens simulating heavily corroded steel reinforcement strengthened with the CFRP-SHCC patch. Each specimen comprised a 20mm diameter high yield steel rebar with 50% area reduction over 50mm of its length, cast inside a SHCC block which also contained a pair of CFRP strips. The cross-sectional area of the SHCC block and CFRP strips are calculated to provide sufficient load carrying capacity for compensating the loss in steel area. In various specimens, the length of SHCC block and CFRP on both sides of the reduced area was from 6 to 12 times the rebar diameter. According to the bond-slip behaviour derived under objectives 1 to 3, the transfer length of 12D should be sufficient for activating close to 100% of the full bond capacities at both the steel-SHCC interface and the CFRP-SHCC interface. Test results showed that the load capacity of the 12D case reached 97.5% of the steel rebar with no area reduction. As the steel cover in the specimen (which is 30mm) is smaller than that in real concrete members under corrosive environments, the measured load capacity is believed to be a lower bound. With the high load recovery obtained in the tensile test, the repair approach was further studied in full beams, as described in objective 6 below. For objective 5, beams with CFRP-SHCC patch over part of the bottom side were designed to induce plate-end cover separation according to existing strength theory for CFRP in concrete, using corresponding material parameters for SHCC. Theoretically speaking, cover separation is caused by high splitting stresses at the steel rebar (induced by high tension in the CFRP) leading to the formation of a horizontal crack at the top of the cover. In all the tests, plate-end debonding failure was not observed even at loading far beyond the theoretically predicted value. Final failure was due to CFRP debonding near the middle of the beam, indicating that the CFRP plate reached its load capacity without inducing cover separation at the end. This is likely due to the high crack resistance of SHCC which controls the formation of splitting cracks around the rebar. Based on the test results and their analysis, it is concluded that plate end cover separation is not an important failure mode for this repair system under most practical situations. For objective 6, our calculations showed that the use of SHCC alone is sufficient to recover loss of steel stirrups equivalent to about 0.9% of shear steel ratio. Experiments were carried out on beams with 0.9% shear steel ratio, with 50% and 100% loss of stirrup area in the shear span, repaired using the SHCC patch alone. Compared to the control beam with full stirrups, the repaired beam reached 96% to 99% of the shear capacity. As the original shear capacity is always over-designed, the results indicate that use of SHCC can fully compensate for severe stirrup corrosion. For the flexural repair of beams, concrete beams with 50% reduction of steel area at the mid-span were repaired with CFRP-SHCC patch. The bond length on each side was 10 or 12 times the rebar diameter. The first set of tests showed failure at the interface between the SHCC patch and substrate concrete, at load levels corresponding to around 90% to 93% of the control beam with full steel section. By placing epoxy bonded steel anchors in holes drilled along the upper interfacial surface, 98%-99% of the original capacity can be recovered. The test results illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed repair method for beams with severe longitudinal rebar corrosion.

16204421.label: Major findings and research outcome
16204421.value: To enhance the sustainability of the proposed repair method, high strength SHCC mixes with up to 70% of Portland cement replaced by fly ash, calcined clay and limestone are being studied. A mix with cement: fly ash: calcined clay: limestone in the ratio of 0.3:0.5:0.133:0.067 reaches tensile strength of 10MPa at a strain of 5.8%, while maintaining average crack opening to below 0.08mm. This mix is suitable for the proposed repair system and many other applications of high strength SHCC. Details of the investigation are reported in journal paper No.1. To derive the bond-slip behaviour between deformed steel and SHCC, finite element analysis using continuum damage plasticity (CDM) model for SHCC and assuming no slip at the SHCC/steel interface was found to produce results in good agreement with experimental data. As this simplified modelling approach does not need to consider (i) the geometry of rebar surface, and (ii) interfacial sliding, model construction is simplified and computational efficiency is enhanced. The numerical modelling is presented together with experimental testing in journal paper No.2 and conference paper No.1. A coupled experimental-numerical approach was adopted to derive the bond-slip relation at the CFRP/SHCC interface, by tuning the interfacial parameters to achieve good agreement between numerical and experimental results of the CFRP pull-out test. While the derived interfacial relation is specific to the CFRP and SHCC mix adopted in this study, the methodology is generally applicable to other CFRP/SHCC combinations. The experimental and numerical studies on CFRP/SHCC bond are reported in journal paper No.4. This project has successfully demonstrated the feasibility of using SHCC alone to recover the load carrying capacity of reinforced concrete beams with severely corroded steel stirrups (up to 100% area loss) and the combined use of SHCC and CFRP strips to repair beams with up to 50% area loss of the longitudinal reinforcement. In the latter case, failure is often due to the debonding at the SHCC/concrete interface. The installation of epoxy bonded anchors along the interface was found to be an effective engineering approach to delay the debonding, enabling close to 100% recovery of load carrying capacity. The recover of shear and flexural capacity of beams with the proposed method are reported respectively in journal papers No.3 and No.5. In addition, results in conference paper No.2 show that plate end cover separation is greatly delayed and hence not a major failure mode of the repaired member.

16204421.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16204421.value: This project has demonstrated the feasibility and established the scientific basis of a new repair method for reinforced concrete structures with severe corrosion of steel reinforcements. A logical next step is to apply for the Innovation and Technology Fund to conduct a research and development project in collaboration with an industrial partner and the Hong Kong Development Bureau. In the completed study, the beam was turned upside down for the repair material to be applied from the top. For practical applications, viscosity modifying agents need to be added to the SHCC to avoid dripping when it is applied to the bottom of a beam. Also, to ensure proper curing under any field condition, self-curing SHCC can be developed by adding water-storing particles such as zeolite. In this project, finite element models are found to be effective in predicting the load recovery. Parametric studies should be carried out with additional experimental testing to verify the numerical results. Then, design charts should be developed for practical application. Together with the Development Bureau, old structures with severe steel corrosion (e.g., piers in outlying islands) can be identified for field trial of the repair technology, with construction carried out by the industrial partner.

16204421.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16204421.value: Localized steel corrosion is a severe problem for reinforced concrete structures in coastal cities or cold regions where salt is commonly employed for de-icing. To compensate for the loss in steel area, the conventional approach is to lap an additional rebar to the corroded bar. For proper transfer of loading to the new bar, a significant amount of sound concrete on both sides of the corroded region needs to be removed, leading to significant increases in repair time and cost. The current project develops a new repair approach using strain-hardening cementitious composites (SHCC) as the patching material with carbon fibre reinforced polymer (CFRP) strips embedded inside. Unlike conventional patching materials, SHCC can carry significant tension after cracking. Moreover, it exhibits strong bonding with both steel and CFRP, enabling sufficient loading transfer within a short distance. The patch size can hence be greatly reduced. Results in this study show that the CFRP-SHCC patch can effectively recover the load capacity of reinforced concrete members with very severe loss of steel area (up to almost 50% of the longitudinal steel and 100% of the stirrups). This new repair method has great potential for practical application in cities with chloride-induced steel reinforcement corrosion problem.

16204521.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16204521.value: 基于分布鲁棒的拍卖机制设计

16204521.label: Project Objectives
16204521.value: Formulate the robust auction problem when each bidder or the seller has either no or partial knowledge about the probability distributions of all bidders' valuation by using a distributionally robust optimization framework. Propose various distributional uncertainty sets to describe bidders' and sellers' knowledge and specify different formulations of incentive compatibility (IC) and individual rationality (IR) to capture bidders' preference. Study the closed-form solution in the particular case when only two objects and two bidders exist using the duality theorem to derive managerial insights. Investigate the theoretical properties, and develop efficient algorithms to solve the general problem. Test the effectiveness of new solutions with real auction data and demonstrate the benefits of the consideration of robustness.

16204521.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16204521.value: Auctions are widely used in real-world transactions. A well-designed auction is a fair and efficient mechanism as it provides equal opportunities for both sellers and bidders. Auctions are a common method of selling commodities, radio spectrum, used cars, paintings, antiques, and much else. Governments often auction off drilling rights, treasury bills and control of firms that are privatizing. The emergence of the Internet has made auctions more popular. Tens of thousands of online auction websites enable people to look for good deals anywhere, anytime. In this study, we propose to use the distributionally robust optimization framework to study the auction problem in economics. Although the multi-object auction has been studied in the economic literature, most researchers have assumed that the probability distributions of bidders' values are known exactly by all sellers and bidders. That assumption is not realistic in general since it is hard to obtain the exact joint probability distribution for multiple objects. Hence, we propose to consider the case where the underlying probability distributions of bidders' values are not fully known either to the seller or other bidders. Given bidders' reports about their values, sellers will decide their allocation rule and payment rule to maximize their worst-case expected revenue. We plan to explore this problem from the following directions. First, the seller and bidders may not have identical information about other bidders' valuation information. In some instances, the seller's information may be a subset of the bidders' information. Second, different distributional ambiguity sets may also affect the optimal auction. Third, with ambiguous information, bidders' incentive compatibility (IC) and individual rationality (IR) can also be defined in different formats. In the first step, we start with a simple case when only two objects and two bidders exist to derive the closed-form solution and collect managerial insights. We will then generalize the solution to the case with multiple objects and multiple bidders and develop efficient algorithms or heuristics to solve the problem. Finally, we will apply our framework to auctions in practice. If it is successful, this proposed study will enrich the existing auction theory and have a major impact on improving the effectiveness of real-world auctions. 拍卖在现实交易中得到了广泛的应用。良好的拍卖设计为卖方和投标人提供了平等的机会，因而成为一种公平、高效的机制。拍卖成为了出售商品、无线电频谱、二手车、绘画、古董等的常用方法。政府也经常通过拍卖设计出售钻井权、国库券和私有化企业的控制权。互联网的出现使得拍卖更加普及。成千上万的网上拍卖网站可以方便人们随时随地寻找好的交易。 在本研究中，我们提出使用分布鲁棒优化框架来研究经济学中的拍卖问题。尽管多物体拍卖在经济学文献中已有研究，但大多数研究都假设所有卖方和投标人完全了解所有竞买人对物件价值的概率分布。然后由于很难得到精确的多个物件的联合概率分布，这种假设在一般情况下是不现实的。因此，我们考虑的情况是卖方或其他投标人不完全知道投标人价值的基本概率分布。给定投标人关于其价值的报告，卖家将决定分配规则和付款规则，从而最大化最坏情况下的预期收益。我们计划从以下几个方向来探讨这个问题。首先，卖方和投标人对其他投标人的价值估计没有相同的信息。在某些情况下，卖方的信息可能是投标人信息的子集。第二，当我们用分布集合描述信息时，不同的分布集合的假设也可能影响最优的拍卖设计。第三，当不完全信息存在时，投标人的激励相容( IC )和个体理性( IR )也可以用不同的格式来定义。在第一步中，我们计划从一个简单的案例，只考虑两个物体和两个投标人存在时，得出闭式解。然后，我们将此解推广到具有多个物体和多个投标人的情况，并开发出高效的算法来解决问题。最后，我们将此框架应用于实际的拍卖案例中做分析。 如果成功，本文提出的研究将丰富现有拍卖理论，对提高现实世界拍卖的有效性产生影响。

16204721.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16204721.value: 基於尾緣鋸齒的氣動聲學降噪綜合研究

16204721.label: Project Objectives
16204721.value: To investigate the aerodynamic and aeroacoustic physics of trailing edge serrations on wings, propellers, and blades through anechoic wind tunnel experiments. The turbulent flow characteristics will be measured using time-resolved particle image velocimetry (PIV) and hot-wire anemometry (HWA), the sound sources will be identified by a phased microphone array, and far-field directivities by a microphone line array. The database will also be used to validate the numerical simulations in Objective 2. To conduct high-fidelity large-eddy simulations (LES) to quantify the two-point statistics of the turbulence on the serration surface. The simulations will be conducted for representative configurations. The constructed turbulence database will support the noise prediction model proposed in Objective 3. The LES and integral solutions of aeroacoustic governing equations also form an element of the project study. To develop a generalized physics-based noise prediction model for trailing edge serrations with input flow variables informed by numerical simulations. For a given type of serrations over a wide range of flow and geometry conditions, the mean flow and turbulent kinetic energy will be obtained by low-cost Reynolds-averaged Navier-Stokes (RANS) simulations. Together with turbulence models based on the LES database in Objective 2, the local turbulent characteristics can be computed and then employed for the noise computation. To investigate the effect of flexible trailing-edge serrations on the flow properties and noise generation characteristics. This study will provide an insight into the mechanism of the excess high-frequency noise reduction due to the flexibility. Numerical studies incorporating fluid-structure interaction will be performed as part of this study. Measurements of the structural deformation and the dynamic motion of flexible serrations will be conducted using a high-resolution laser profiler. To investigate the effect of surface treatment placed upstream of the serrations. The devices are expected to improve the flow quality around serrations, thereby improving the noise-reduction capacity of the serrations. An iterative process will be employed to design the devices according to the turbulence and acoustics characteristics. The success of this study can lead to a new type of noise control methodology to reduce noise emission from the trailing edge of a wing or an aerodynamic lifting surface.

16204721.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16204721.value: Noise generated by wings and lifting surfaces that can be found in aerospace and power industry has health and performance consequences. An important source of noise is turbulence scattering off the trailing edge of the device. This project aims at accurately predicting the aerodynamic noise reduction by trailing edge serrations and developing novel methods to enhance their noise reduction capacity. The motivation originates from the fact that there exist large discrepancies between noise measurements and predictions from available theories. The deviation can be attributed to an over-simplified assumption made of frozen turbulence and a lack of proper modelling of turbulence wall pressure spectrum. In addition, new turbulent structures can be generated due to the serration itself, impacting on the overall noise, the effect of which needs to be accounted for. To fill these gaps, a physics-based noise model, taking account of the complex turbulent flow, will be developed. Unlike existing methods, the proposed model will take account of the evolving turbulence structures over serrations. High-fidelity large-eddy simulations will be conducted for representative serration cases. The resulting database will be employed to estimate the required turbulence statistics, such as the wall pressure spectrum over serrations, for noise computation. The mean flow field and turbulent kinetic energy, that are needed for model input over a wide parameter range, will be provided by Reynolds-averaged Navier-Stokes simulations. All predictions and simulations will be compared with experiments conducted in an anechoic wind tunnel. Measurements include time-resolved particle image velocimetry and hot-wire anemometry for near-field flow and turbulence, phased microphone array for noise source, and line array for far-field directivities. To further enhance the noise reduction capacity, innovative approaches will be studied together with serrations. Flexible serrations, which can deform subject to pressure loadings, will be employed to improve the flow alignment. Proof-of-concept experiments showed that an additional noise reduction over rigid serrations can be achieved. In addition, low-profile vortex generators will be placed upstream of the serrations to produce vortex structures to counteract vortex pairs and crossflow generated at the serration roots. Proof-of-concept simulations suggested that the wake turbulent kinetic energy can be reduced through a representative device, proving its effectiveness to control the flow, and therefore the potential to improve the noise reduction performance. The outcome of this project will benefit low-noise designs of wings, propellers and blades which are widely found in industries such as aerospace, aviation, renewable energy, and urban air mobility. 在航空航天和風力發動等應用中常見的氣動升力面結構與空氣發生干擾會產生嚴重的噪聲問題。其中尾緣噪聲是寬帶噪聲的重要來源。本項目將通過使用尾緣鋸齒，對局部流動和噪聲產生進行精準控制，進一步提升尾緣降噪目的。本研究的一個背景是當前的理論預測結果與實際測量結果之間通常有著顯著差別。這主要是因為在建模過程中採用了凍結湍流的假設，同時湍流壁面壓力譜估計也通常不夠精確。另外，鋸齒結構本身也會造成新的湍流脈動，產生額外的噪聲。為此，我們將首先提出一個基於物理的複雜湍流噪聲產生模型，並一拼考慮鋸齒上具有空間變化的湍流結構。我們將開展高保真的大渦模擬研究，建立詳細的數據庫來對湍流空間結構進行建模。同時，我們還會開展大規模的雷諾平均納維-斯托克斯方程模擬，在一定的參數範圍內建立平均流場和湍動能數據庫，與建模得到的空間結構得到詳細的湍流變化情況。數值計算的結果將與靜音風洞實驗測量結果相互校驗。實驗測量手段包括熱線風速儀和粒子圖像測速法。同時，數值計算中的噪聲計算結果將於相控麥克風陣列以及用於遠場方向性的麥克風陣列測量結果相互比對。項目還將考慮不同的幾何構型，考慮升力面在具有一定攻角時，與可變形的柔性鋸齒相結合，進而改變流動方向。該設計的有效性也在預研結果中得到證實。另外，我們還將在鋸齒上遊安裝微結構渦流發生器，以抵銷鋸齒根部產生的渦流和橫向流動。在預研結果中，我們通過採用數值模擬，驗證了其流動控制的有效性，後期將在實驗測量中進行進一步測量。項目研究成果預期有助於優化空氣動力升力面，為低噪聲航空器、風力發電機等低噪聲設計提供新思路。

16204721.label: Realisation of objectives
16204721.value: The proposed objectives have been achieved by using theoretical, numerical, and experimental studies. The research findings from the project have been published in reputable journals, such as the Journal of Sound and Vibration, The Journal of Acoustical Society of America, and others. Two PhD students were supported by this fund, one of them got the Redbird PhD Award Program. The main accomplishment related to the stated objectives are summarized below. 1. We conducted extensive experiments in an anechoic wind tunnel to investigate the aerodynamic and aeroacoustic effects of trailing edge serrations on various aerodynamic surfaces, including wings and propellers. Time-resolved particle image velocimetry (PIV) and hot-wire anemometry (HWA) were employed to measure turbulent flow characteristics. A phased microphone array was used to identify sound sources, while a microphone line array provided far-field directivity measurements. The results show that the serration structures can suppress the trailing edge noise generation process. This comprehensive dataset has been established to validate the numerical simulations outlined in Objective 2. 2. High-fidelity LES were performed to quantify the two-point statistics of turbulence on serrated surfaces. Simulations were conducted for representative configurations, leading to the creation of a detailed turbulence database. This database supports the noise prediction model proposed in Objective 3 and enhances our understanding of the underlying turbulence dynamics. By using the high-fidelity simulation technique, the detailed flow field in the boundary layer can be obtained, assisting the understanding of the noise generation mechanisms. 3. We have developed a generalized physics-based noise prediction model for trailing edge serrations. This model utilizes input flow variables derived from numerical simulations. We obtained mean flow and turbulent kinetic energy data through low-cost Reynolds-averaged Navier-Stokes (RANS) simulations. The local turbulent characteristics computed from the LES database were integrated into the noise computation process, significantly improving noise prediction accuracy. This method has been used to predict the far-field noise from rotor blades at several inflow conditions. 4. Our investigation into flexible trailing-edge serrations revealed their impact on flow properties and noise generation. We conducted numerical studies incorporating fluid-structure interaction, which provided insights into the mechanisms behind high-frequency noise reduction due to serration flexibility. Structural deformation and dynamic motion of the flexible serrations were measured using a high-resolution laser profiler, confirming the beneficial effects of flexibility. 5. We explored the effects of upstream surface treatment on flow quality around serrations. The treatments were designed iteratively based on turbulence and acoustic characteristics, leading to improved noise-reduction capabilities of the serrations. This study paves the way for innovative noise control methodologies aimed at reducing noise emissions from aerodynamic surfaces.

The success of this study can lead to a new type of noise control methodology to reduce noise emission from the trailing edge of a wing or an aerodynamic lifting surface.

16204921.value: 我們提出了一種通過使用微電子機械系統技術製造的熱驅動相變微泵。這種新型微泵的核心原理是依靠在充滿液體的微通道中通過微加熱器使蒸汽氣泡產生相變生長和破裂的過程。與涉及運動部件的傳統泵不同，這種新型微泵的突出特點包括簡單、無移動部件、易於製造，以及能夠直接處理純液體和含有微粒的液體的能力。為了優化這種新型微泵的設計，我們需要了解微結構中微氣泡的形成、生長和破裂的過程。此外，我們還會闡明由微尺度快速加熱引起的新型熱流現象。這些目標將通過本項目中提出的創新實驗方法來實現。本項目的研究成果將加深我們對微結構中相變傳熱過程的理解，並為微機械矽微泵的設計提供必要的信息。隨著人們對微流體系統興趣的增加，在工業生產以及生物技術、環境測試和分析化學等領域的許多新應用中，都需要泵送和計量純液體和含微粒液體的技術。鑑於香港政府近年來一直在推動創新技術的發展，本項目所獲得的核心技術將直接惠及香港的經濟發展。

16204921.label: Realisation of objectives
16204921.value: The project has successfully achieved its initial objectives centered on the fundamental study of bubble nucleation, growth, and collapse in microchannels, as well as the fabrication and performance evaluation of thermally driven phase-change micropumps. Furthermore, the research was systematically extended, forming a coherent development chain from microscale thermal-fluid control to large-scale thermal management systems. Firstly, the mechanisms of bubble nucleation in microchannels were investigated both experimentally and theoretically. A specially designed microchannel test section equipped with uniformly spaced heating elements enabled controlled generation of vapor bubbles under localized heating conditions. This allowed the observation of heterogeneous and quasi-homogeneous nucleation behaviors under varying thermal loads. Theoretical modeling further provided insights into the thermal-fluid coupling dynamics governing nucleation in confined microscale environments. Secondly, the growth and collapse behavior of bubbles under pulsed heating loads were systematically explored. High-resolution experimental setups captured the dynamic evolution of vapor slugs, and transient pressure variations induced by bubble dynamics were quantitatively analyzed through the resulting fluid displacement and pressure head variations. These findings offered critical guidance for the subsequent design of thermally driven micropumps. Thirdly, based on these insights, prototype phase-change micropumps were fabricated, featuring precision-aligned embedded microheaters. Although the complete integration of microheaters and microsensors onto a single silicon chip remains a future goal, the prototypes successfully demonstrated non-mechanical, thermally actuated fluid pumping. Performance evaluation revealed a maximum pressure head of approximately 57–60 mm H₂O and a maximum volumetric flow rate of about 300 μL/min under optimal heating conditions (8.0–12.0 W and ~3 seconds heating duration). Building upon these achievements, the project research was further extended and validated through three major studies, all of which maintain intrinsic consistency with the project's original focus on multiphysics thermal-fluid coupling and thermal actuation control: (1) Development of a Multi-Path Decentralized RC Network Model Inspired by the microscale heat transfer modeling experience gained from bubble nucleation studies, a multi-path decentralized resistance-capacity (MDRC) network model was developed for prismatic lithium-ion batteries. By introducing refined heat flow path segmentation and decentralized mass distribution, the model significantly enhanced the accuracy of thermal response predictions, reducing the temperature prediction error from 4.24°C to 0.95°C. This work represents an extension of the microscale thermal modeling approach toward complex electrochemical thermal management applications. (2) Construction of a Reduced-Order Thermal Runaway Network (TRN) Model Leveraging the foundational modeling concepts of phase-change-induced thermal processes, a reduced-order TRN model was established for module- and pack-level thermal runaway propagation analysis. By redistributing heat source terms and correcting thermal runaway trigger criteria, the model achieved excellent agreement with experimental data, with trigger time prediction errors within 1 minute. This study validated the scalability and robustness of the project’s thermal-fluid modeling methodology, extending its applicability to large-scale energy storage systems. (3) Proposal of a Chessboard-Inspired Battery Pack Design for Thermal Runaway Prevention Extending the control strategies derived from localized heating and bubble growth dynamics, a novel chessboard-inspired battery pack architecture was proposed. By arranging cells into two interdigitated groups with staggered states of charge (SOC), the design effectively elevated the thermal runaway propagation threshold by 22°C at 75% pack SOC conditions. Additionally, specialized tab designs enabled approximately 10% of the thermal energy to be redirected to non-adjacent cells, significantly enhancing thermal safety. This work highlights the application of localized thermal control concepts at the system level, integrating structural and discharge strategies for enhanced energy storage safety. In conclusion, starting from the study of bubble nucleation and phase-change micropumping in microchannels, the project successfully expanded its theoretical and experimental frameworks to applications in large-scale battery thermal management and safety design. This coherent research progression not only validates the soundness of the established methodologies but also lays the groundwork for future integration of microscale thermal-fluid control and macroscale energy system safety technologies.

16204921.label: Major findings and research outcome
16204921.value: This project conducted a comprehensive investigation into a novel thermally driven, phase-change, nonmechanical micropump, integrating rigorous theoretical modeling with systematic experimental validation. A microchannel, fully filled with liquid and embedded with twelve uniformly distributed, sequentially activated microheaters, was fabricated to achieve precise control over vapor bubble nucleation, growth, and collapse. These processes enabled fluid transport without reliance on any mechanical moving components. Under optimal operational conditions—specifically, heating powers between 8.0 and 12.0 W and heating durations around 3 seconds—the micropump prototypes achieved a maximum pressure head of approximately 57–60 mm H₂O and a maximum volumetric flow rate of about 300 µL/min. A detailed theoretical model was developed to predict the dynamic response of the system, and the model’s predictions demonstrated strong agreement with experimental observations, validating the underlying physical mechanisms. Building upon the foundational understanding gained through this investigation, the research outcomes were further extended to address critical challenges in thermal management and energy system safety. Detailed experimental and numerical analyses were conducted on the design of liquid cooling plates for lithium-ion batteries, emphasizing the influence of non-uniform internal heat generation on thermal performance. These studies provided important design principles for enhancing the efficiency and reliability of battery thermal management systems. In addition, a reduced-order thermal runaway propagation model was developed for large-scale power systems, offering an efficient yet accurate tool for predicting catastrophic failure events in battery packs. Furthermore, inspired by the principles of localized thermal management, a chessboard-inspired design paradigm was proposed to mitigate thermal runaway propagation in lithium-ion battery systems. This innovative design approach demonstrated significant potential in enhancing the passive safety of high-energy-density battery packs. In conclusion, the project not only successfully fulfilled all originally proposed objectives but also catalyzed further advancements in the fields of microfluidic actuation, thermal management, and energy system safety enhancement. The major research outcomes have been disseminated through four peer-reviewed journal publications, contributing substantially to the body of knowledge and laying the groundwork for future technological developments in related disciplines.

16204921.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16204921.value: The research provides a strong foundation for further advancement in thermally driven, nonmechanical microfluidic systems. Future work could focus on optimizing heater design and microchannel architecture to enhance pumping efficiency, reduce energy consumption, and enable precise control of flow rates. Integration of advanced materials, such as phase-change composites or high thermal conductivity coatings, could significantly improve system responsiveness and durability. Additionally, scaling the concept to multi-channel arrays offers the potential for parallel fluidic control in lab-on-a-chip, cooling, and biomedical applications. Coupling the micropump with real-time feedback control systems, based on temperature or pressure sensors, could enable adaptive operation under dynamic conditions. Building on the broader thermal management insights, future research will also target the development of integrated thermal protection systems for energy storage devices. Specifically, applying localized phase-change strategies to design self-regulating cooling systems for lithium-ion battery packs holds substantial promise. The proposed course of action includes detailed modeling, microfabrication of next-generation prototypes, and experimental validation under practical operating conditions. Exploration of system reliability, long-term operation, and scalability will be prioritized to bridge the gap between laboratory demonstrations and real-world applications.

16204921.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16204921.value: This project developed a new kind of tiny pump that can move liquids without any mechanical parts like motors or gears. Instead, it uses heat to create small bubbles inside a narrow channel. By carefully controlling the bubbles, we can push the liquid forward simply and reliably. These micropumps are small, efficient, and have no moving parts that wear out, making them ideal for delicate systems like medical devices or electronics cooling. Beyond creating the pump itself, we also applied what we learned about heat and fluid movement to help cool lithium-ion batteries, which are widely used in electric vehicles and energy storage. We designed better battery cooling systems and new ways to prevent dangerous overheating events. Overall, this research not only created a new way to move liquids on a tiny scale but also contributed to making batteries safer and more reliable. The knowledge gained could lead to better cooling technologies for many different industries, helping improve the performance, safety, and lifespan of advanced electronic and energy systems.

16205021.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16205021.value: The manual visual inspection of civil infrastructure has long been considered as the standard practice. However, this conventional practice is time-consuming and labor-intensive, especially when the site is large and difficult to access. The results sometimes are also insufficient, inconsistent, and even inaccurate due to the subjective decisions of inspectors. All of these constraints could further hinder the in-time repairment on deteriorating infrastructure, which in turn might cause interruptions on the city’s daily operation and even arise public safety concerns. To align with the policy objectives of the HK Smart City Blueprint and the goals of Construction 2.0 as initiated by the HKSAR government. We, therefore, propose to dramatically transform the current visual inspection practice by establishing an innovative integrated inspection solution: AI-enabled detection, positioning and assessment of civil infrastructure defects using camera-LiDAR datasets, leveraging deep learning and other advanced algorithms for data processing. Once receiving camera-LiDAR visionary datasets, the first module proposed in this study—deep learning-based semantic segmentation algorithm— will performs pixel-wise defect identifications to generate high-resolution segmentation maps of defects (in the pixel level). Meanwhile, the second proposed module—dynamic relative pose estimation algorithm—will register coordinates of the datasets to generate a camera-LiDAR 3D map so as to position identified defects with an accurate dimension. Then, the outcomes from the first two modules will be integrated together for defect assessment in a quantitative and objective manner, where defect attributes, such as defect types, dimensions, absolute orientation and propagation paths, and the locations will be evaluated in a holistic view. Identified defects can also be ranked and grouped according to the designated damage grading system. Interface modules will also be established to integrate the actionable outputs with the existing digital databases and/or the design platforms to facilitate the planning of subsequent repair programs. Note that the established camera-LiDAR 3D maps are designed as an ever-evolving 3D mapping database. Images of newly discovered defects during routine checks can be simply captured with smartphone cameras and uploaded to servers for georeferencing and defect detection, thereby immediately updating the most recent site conditions. All the innovations developed from this study can be directly applied to advance other smart city infrastructural technologies that also involve intensive processing of multi-class data to help build an information-empowered digital city and keep Hong Kong in the race to become a truly smart and resilient hub in the Greater Bay Area. 於民用基礎設施的人工目視檢測長期以來被視為標準做法。然而，這種傳統做法費時費力，尤其是當場地較大且難以進入。由於檢測人員的主觀判斷，結果有時也不夠充分、不一致，甚至不準確。所有這些限制都可能進一步對及時修復日益惡化的基礎設施造成窒礙，進而可能導致城市日常運營中斷，甚至引發公共安全問題。 為配合香港特區政府發起的香港智慧城市藍圖政策和建設2.0的目標，我們建議通過建立創新的綜合檢測解決方案來顯著改變當前的視覺檢測做法：利用深度學習和其他高級算法進行數據處理，基於人工智能使用相機-激光雷達數據集對民用基礎設施缺陷檢測、定位和評估。一旦接收到相機-激光雷達視覺數據集，本研究中提出的第一個模塊——基於深度學習的語義分割算法——將執行像素級缺陷識別，以生成高分辨率的缺陷分割圖（在像素級別）。同時，第二個提出的模塊——動態相對姿態估計算法——將註冊數據集的坐標以生成相機-激光雷達三維地圖，從而以準確的尺寸定位識別出缺陷。然後，將前兩個模塊的結果整合在一起，以定量和客觀的方式進行缺陷評估，其中缺陷屬性，例如缺陷類型、尺寸、絕對方向和擴展路徑以及位置，將在整體觀點中進行評估。已識別的缺陷還可以根據指定的損壞分級系統進行排序和分組。接口模塊也被建立以將可操作的輸出與現有的數碼數據庫和/或設計平台結合，以促進後續維修計劃的規劃。請注意，已建立的相機-激光雷達三維地圖被設計為不斷發展的三維地圖數據庫。例行檢查期間新發現的缺陷圖像可以簡單地用智能手機攝像頭捕捉並上傳到服務器進行地理配準和缺陷檢測，從而立即更新現場狀況。 本研究的所有提案可直接應用於推進其他涉及多級數據的密集處理的智慧城市基礎設施技術，以幫助建設信息賦能的數碼城市，並使香港在競爭中成為在大灣區里真正智能和有彈性的中心。

16205321.label: Project Objectives
16205321.value: To develop perovskite quantum wires for different emission colors. Color purity is expected to be high with full width at half maximum (FWHM) of the emission peak less than 20nm. Color conversion efficiency is expected to be higher than 50%. To develop a large-scale (4-inch wafer size or above) growth process of perovskite quantum wires using a vapor method. Uniformity of deposition should be high (pixel yield >95%). The large-scale uniform deposition is critical for industrial mass production. To develop perovskite quantum wires-based color conversion film with long-term stability (> 3,000 hours) and continuous photoluminescent excitation, the perovskite quantum wires will be grown in a porous alumina membrane that can a) passivate the perovskite materials to avoid water/oxygen degradation; and b) work as an effective heat dissipater to overcome the critical overheating problem which is one of the key challenges for quantum dot color conversion competitors. With a porous alumina membrane replacing the packaging polymers normally used for quantum dots, the long-term stability of perovskite quantum wires will be significantly improved. To develop single red/green color conversion films with a 5 μm pattern pitch (corresponding to 5,000 ppi), and align them with commercially available micro-display panels for high-resolution image/video demonstration. These color conversion films are expected to demonstrate excellent stability in air and high color conversion efficiency of over 50% to ensure the brightness of the converted color and to reduce blue/ultra-violet (UV) leakage as much as possible. To develop full-color micro-displays with multiple-step photolithography and perovskite quantum wires growth steps to define red/green pixels and then precisely align them with the UV micro-display backlight for color down-conversion. The full-color micro-display is expected to have a color gamut covering at least 70% of the RGB color space in the CIE 1931 chromaticity diagram. 16205321.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16205321.value: Microdisplays are emerging display technologies offering the highest display pixel density to date and they are the most promising technology for virtual reality/augmented reality applications providing users virtual experience with a near-eye display goggle. The anticipated global microdisplay market by 2025 will be 3,609 million USD. However, full-color micro-displays are still a challenge owing to challenges on fabrication, especially when pixel density is high (e.g. 5,000 ppi). The most promising approach to realize a full-color micro-display with a high-pixel density is to use color down-conversion materials (the materials converting higher energy photon with shorter wavelengths to the lower energy photon with longer wavelengths), with the most common being CdSe/ZnS quantum dots mixed with a polymer matrix. However, quantum dots are usually deposited through a solution-based method, which creates a constraint on being scaled up for mass production. Moreover, mixing quantum dots with polymers brings in an issue of quantum dot heat dissipation, leading to a short operational lifetime. To address these two problems, here we propose to develop perovskite quantum wires for color conversion films for full-color 5,000 ppi micro-displays. It is know that halide perovskite materials possess high color purity (18 nm emission peak width) and close to unity high photoluminescence quantum efficiency. More importantly, our perovskite quantum wires have a diameter of less than 5nm, demonstrating a characteristic quantum confinement and emission color tunability, akin to quantum dots. The perovskite quantum wires will be deposited using a vapor growth method, which, in principle, means there is no limit on upscalability. Another important property is that these wires will be embedded in a porous alumina membrane. Such a membrane has much higher thermal conductivity than the perovskite materials themselves, serving as a dissipater to overcome overheating issue. Through multiple material growths and pixel patterning processes with precise alignment, we will fabricate full-color perovskite quantum wire-based color conversion film for 5,000 ppi micro-displays, with the lifetime of a film anticipated to be more than 5,000 hours. Such films will not only be useful for micro-displays but can also be used for other display technologies, such as liquid crystal displays (LCDs) and organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs). In addition, after delivering full-color conversion films, a micro-display based on electroluminescence from perovskite quantum wires can be explored, using active-matrix microelectrodes for high-efficiency and energy-saving micro-displays. 微顯示器是迄今為止提供最高顯示像素密度的新興顯示技術，它們是虛擬現實/增強現實應用中最有前途的技術，為用戶提供近眼顯示護目鏡的虛擬體驗。預計到 2025 年全球微顯示器市場將達到 36.09 億美元。然而，由於製造方面的挑戰，全彩微顯示器仍然是一個挑戰，尤其是在像素密度高（例如 5,000 ppi）的情況下。實現具有高像素密度的全彩微顯示器最有前途的方法是使用顏色下轉換材料（將波長較短的高能量光子轉換為波長較長的低能量光子的材料），其中最常見的是與聚合物基質混合的 CdSe/ZnS 量子點。然而，量子點通常是通過基於溶液的方法沉積的，這對大規模生產產生了限制。此外，將量子點與聚合物混合會帶來量子點散熱問題，導致使用壽命較短。為了解決這兩個問題，我們在這裡提出開發鈣鈦礦量子線，用於全彩色 5,000 ppi 微型顯示器的顏色轉換薄膜。眾所周知，鹵化物鈣鈦礦材料具有高色純度（18 nm 發射峰寬）和接近100%的高光致發光量子效率。更重要的是，我們的鈣鈦礦量子線的直徑小於 5nm，顯示出類似於量子點的特徵量子限制和發射顏色可調性。鈣鈦礦量子線將使用氣相生長方法沉積，原則上，這意味著對可擴展性沒有限制。另一個重要的特性是這些線將嵌入多孔氧化鋁膜中。這種膜具有比鈣鈦礦材料高得多的熱導率自己，作為消散器來克服過熱問題。通過多種材料生長和精確對準的像素圖案化工藝，我們將製造用於 5,000 ppi 微顯示器的全彩色鈣鈦礦量子線顏色轉換薄膜，薄膜的使用壽命預計超過 5,000 小時。此類薄膜不僅可用於微顯示器，還可用於其他顯示技術，例如液晶顯示器 (LCD) 和有機發光二極管 (OLED)。此外，在交付全色轉換膜後，可以探索基於鈣鈦礦量子線電致發光的微顯示器，使用有源矩陣微電極實現高效節能的微顯示器。

16205321.value: For objective 1, we have got color conversion films made by perovskite quantum wires with R/G/B three colors (Zhang et al., Sci. Adv. 11, eadu3840 (2025) ). The FWHM of the emission peak is 20nm and the PLQY for quantum wire color conversion film is as high as 92%. For objective 2, we have successfully fabricated the large-scale quantum wire film on a 4-inch wafer. The film uniformity is very high with a pixel yield of almost 100%. For objective 3, the color conversion film we fabricated show a PL lifetime of T50=5,644hr. For objective 4, we have fabricated the patterned color conversion film with the pixel density up to 63,500 ppi and mounted the color conversion films on commercialized UVA microdisplay panels (Zhang et al., Sci. Adv. 11, eadu3840 (2025) ). The UV/blue leakage is as low as 2.4% when the color conversion film thickness is increased to 8µm. For objective 5, the color gamut of the color conversion film is 87.7%. The film showed almost no degradation after 1 month (~720hr) test.

16205321.label: Major findings and research outcome
16205321.value: (1) High pixel-density color conversion film based on perovskite quantum wires(Zhang et al., Sci. Adv. 11, eadu3840 (2025) ) Halide perovskite materials have demonstrated exceptional potential in a wide range of optoelectronic applications, driving an urgent need for the development of perovskite-based integrated optoelectronic devices. However, the incompatibility of perovskite thin films with conventional wet lithography techniques has posed significant challenges, limiting their application in critical areas such as ultrahigh-density displays, high-resolution image sensors, high-density memristors, and integrated photonic circuits. To address this bottleneck, we have developed a self-aligned close-spaced sublimation growth method for perovskite quantum wires, enabling the fabrication of perovskite patterns with a feature size as small as 0.18 micrometers. This approach achieves an unprecedented pixel density of 63,500 pixels per inch, the highest reported for perovskites to date. Furthermore, we demonstrate the pixelation of perovskite quantum wires in combination with color conversion films, providing a viable solution for full-color microdisplays. Our method also extends to curved substrates, demonstrating its potential for near-eye microdisplay applications. Beyond microdisplays, the processes presented here hold promise for a range of other perovskite-based devices, including high-resolution displays, image sensors, and memristor arrays. (2) Large-scale perovskite LED based on quantum wire films Halide perovskite materials have emerged as highly promising candidates for efficient planar light-emitting diodes (LEDs) with great commercial potential in displays and lighting. However, conventional solution-based fabrication processes face significant challenges in producing large-scale or non-planar LEDs due to the non-uniformity of perovskite films and inherent material stability issues. This project successfully addressed these challenges by achieving the controlled growth of large-area, highly uniform arrays of crystalline perovskite quantum wires, with emission spectra spanning the entire visible range. Optimized MAPbBr3 quantum wires demonstrated an impressive photoluminescence quantum yield of up to 92% and a photoluminescence half-life of 5,644 hours under ambient conditions, showcasing excellent stability. LEDs based on these quantum wires were fabricated on both rigid and flexible planar substrates, achieving sizes up to four-inch wafers. Additionally, unique three-dimensional spherical LEDs with outstanding emission uniformity were demonstrated for the first time. The results of this study indicate that the developed approach is not only suitable for large-area planar perovskite LEDs but also provides a versatile strategy for the design and application of unconventional three-dimensional LEDs in the future, offering significant scientific and practical implications.

16205321.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16205321.value: In the future, we will continue our work on perovskite quantum wire based LEDs and displays. (1) Full color display based on peorvksite quantum wires: we have already realized the R/G/B colored color conversion films. In future, we will integrate three colors together and fabricated them on the driving circuit to make the electroluminiscent full color displays. (2) Holographic Imaging: With the achieved pixel density of up to 63,500 ppi, which far surpasses current display requirements, this technology holds great potential for applications in holographic imaging. (3) Semiconductor Chip Integration: Since the pixelation process we developed is perfectly compatible with photolithography, our perovskite quantum wire devices hold great promise for use in traditional semiconductor processes, enabling the integration of perovskite-based photonic chips.

16205321.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16205321.value: These studies present groundbreaking advancements in perovskite-based technologies for displays and lighting. (1) High Pixel-Density Color Conversion Film: Researchers achieved a world-record pixel density of 63,500 ppi using perovskite quantum wires, far exceeding current display requirements. This innovation enables ultra-high-resolution full-color displays and works on curved surfaces, making it ideal for applications like near-eye microdisplays (e.g., AR/VR). The technique also shows promise for high-resolution imaging and memory devices. (2) Large-Scale Perovskite LEDs: A new method for growing uniform perovskite quantum wires enables efficient and scalable LEDs with a 92% light emission efficiency and over 5,000 hours of stability. These LEDs were fabricated on flat and flexible substrates, including unique 3D spherical designs. Both studies address major challenges in perovskite technology, offering scalable solutions for ultra-high-resolution displays and unconventional LED designs, paving the way for next-generation optoelectronic devices.

16205421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16205421.value: Consensus, agreement, rendezvous, flocking, swarming, and synchronization problems for multi-agent systems have been extensively studied for over two decades. These problems can be unified, more or less, into an output synchronization problem where a network protocol interfacing the agents is to be designed so that the agents’ behaviors converge to a common trajectory. In most of the past studies, the agents involved are assumed to be identical, also said to be homogeneous. This assumption makes the problem rather easy to solve but severely limits the application scenarios. In recent years, more and more attention is shifted to the case when the agents are different, also said to be heterogeneous. In studying the heterogeneous case, most researchers up to now allow the use of different controllers in the network to achieve the synchronization, essentially and arguably turning the problem into an independent controller design problem for each agent. However, the use of different controllers in the network comes with the vastly increased cost in the design and the implementation. In this proposed research project we intend to study the synchronization problem when the diversity among the agents is big and the controllers are uniform and as simple as possible. There will be two major issues in our study. The first one is to characterize the solvability condition on the diversity of the agents. The second one is to give a design procedure which produces a simple uniform synchronizing controller. We will study several different cases and address several different considerations: (1) continuous-time LTI agents with uniform continuous-time LTI controllers; (2) discrete-time LTI agents with uniform discrete-time LTI controllers; (3) continuous-time LTI agents with uniform sampled-data controllers; (4) synchronization under time-varying network interaction, communication constraints among agents, and convergence speed requirements. In nature, we often see a flock of birds of different sizes and a swarm of animals of different species. In a smart society, we often envision to have formation flights of multiple UAVs of different shapes and sizes and the coordinated motion of a large number of autonomous vehicles of diverse forms. All these call for a powerful and effective controller design theory for synchronization. How much can we learn from nature? How much can deep control techniques offer in coordinating a collection of robots? What does collective intelligence really mean? This proposed project will shed new lights in answering these questions. 在近二十年里，多智能体系统的一致性问题、协同控制、编队、群集效应、蜂拥理论、同步控制等问题得到了广泛的研究。在一定程度上，这些问题都可以统一为一个输出同步问题，其中研究人员需要设计多智能体间的网络交互协议，使得多智能体的行为收敛到共同的轨迹。在早期的文献中，大部分工作只考虑了完全一样的多智能体，又称为同构多智能体。这个假设使得同步问题容易解决，却极大地限制了其应用场景。近几年来，不同多智能体，又称异构多智能体的同步问题受到了越来越多的关注。至今为止，大多数学者允许使用不同的控制器来实现异构多智能体的同步，本质上可以说将问题转化成为对每一个智能体单独设计控制器的问题。然而，在网络中使用不同的控制器极大地增大了设计和实施的成本。 本项目旨在研究设计尽可能简单的通用控制器来实现大差异异构多智能体的同步问题。本项目有两个关键问题：其一，针对智能体之间的差异刻画问题的可解性条件；其二，当可解性条件满足时，给出能实现同步的通用控制器的设计方法。我们将研究以下不同情形及考虑不同的侧重点：（1）连续时间线性时不变智能体及通用连续时间线性时不变控制器；（2）离散时间线性时不变智能体及通用离散时间线性时不变控制器；（3）连续时间线性时不变智能体及通用采样控制器；（4）在时变交互、具有通信约束、及对收敛速度有要求下的同步问题。 自然界中，我们经常观察到不同大小的鸟类集群和不同种类的动物蜂拥现象。在智能社会，我们经常期待看到不同形态和大小的无人机的编队飞行，及大量不同样式的无人车协同运动。这些目标的实现需要一个强大而有效的同步控制器设计理论。我们可以从自然界学到多少？深层的控制技术能为协调机器人提供什么？集群智能究竟代表什么？本项目将为回答这些问题指明方向。

16205421.label: Major findings and research outcome
16205421.value: Synchronization and consensus LTI controller design for heterogeneous continuous-time LTI agents was studied in [J1]. The weakest version of small phase theorem was studied in [J2]. A survey paper [J3] was written to review the whole phase theory in the past five years. 16205421.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16205421.value: This project is part of the effort in developing a phase theory for complex systems and networks. This is the third GRF project in this effort and it is following by another GRF project. The development is very fruitful and impactful. Several research teams in the world are carrying out follow up research in the phase theory and applying phase theory to practical problems in the field of communication, power systems, etc. We expect to see a boom of the phase theory in the coming years. The HKUST team, as the founder, will continue to make more contributions to the new scientific theory.

16205421.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16205421.value: The main purpose of this project is to understand how diverse agents can be synchronized using simple and uniform controllers. Synchronization algorithms foster collective behavior through local interactions, ensuring all agents asymptotically converge to a common trajectory through a synchronization protocol over a network topology. In most of the past studies, the agents are assumed to be homogeneous, which makes the problem rather easy to solve but severely limits the application scenarios. In recent years, more and more attention is shifted to the case when the agents are heterogeneous. A key consideration is scalability, which is ensured by designing a small number of distinguished controllers, significantly fewer than the number of agents, even when agent diversity is high. In nature, we often see a flock of birds of different sizes and a swarm of animals of different species. In a smart society, we often envision to have formation flights of multiple UAVs of different shapes and sizes and the coordinated motion of a large number of autonomous vehicles of diverse forms. All these call for a powerful and effective controller design theory for synchronization. In this proposed research project, we intend to study the synchronization problem when the diversity among the agents is big and the controllers are uniform and as simple as possible. We believe that the results from this research project will be impactful, not only scholarly but also to engineering applications.

16205721.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16205721.value: 鋅基液流電池具有高能量密度，低成本和高安全性等優勢，有望成為下一代大規模儲能技術。然而，在充電過程中，鋅的電沉積容易生成枝晶，不僅會導致電池容量的快速衰減且可能造成電池的短路，嚴重制約了這類電池的實際應用。一般認為，當沉積電流密度超過鋅離子的擴散極限時，鋅電極表面的離子濃度會持續降低，並在“桑德時間”時刻變為零，引發不穩定的鋅沉積造成枝晶。儘管過去有許多工作嘗試抑制鋅枝晶的生長，但對耦合熱/質傳遞、電化學反應及固-液相變的電沉積過程的機理認識還不夠充分，限制了高效鋅電極的開發。基於此，本項目的主要研究內容包括：1）借助原位光學觀測，系統研究電解液流動和溫度對鋅沉積特性的影響；2）構建相場-格子玻爾茲曼數值模型以揭示物質/離子傳輸、產熱和傳熱、電化學反應和動態形貌特性耦合的本征規律；3）基於這些認識，設計新型電極和流場來實現電解液和溫度的均布來實現鋅的均勻沉積。本項目不僅能夠加深對鋅沉積過程中傳質傳熱機理的理解，還有望解決制約鋅基液流電池的瓶頸問題，從而推動此類新型儲能技術的商業化應用。

16205721.label: Realisation of objectives
16205721.value: Through the project, we have realized all the proposed objectives by undertaking extensive research activities. Notably, we developed a dendrite-free, high-areal capacity zinc-bromine flow battery that can stably cycle for more than 2000 cycles. Details to realize the objective are as follows. For objective #1, we have developed a homemade in-situ optical microscope (OM) observation system, which allows us to monitor the real-time morphology evolution of Zn deposits during the plating process. By combining with other characterization techniques including 3D laser scanning microscope and scanning electron microscope, we investigated the impacts of flow rate, temperate, electrolyte composition, and operating current density on the Zn deposition behavior. Zn deposited on both the surface and cross-section of electrodes was observed to understand the distribution and growth rate of Zn dendrites. Results showed that all these design and operating parameters impose a significant effect on morphology of Zn electrodeposits. Particularly, it was concluded that achieving uniform initial Zn nucleation and regulating ion transport are essential to achieve uniform, dense, and dendrite-free Zn deposition, as severe dendrites were found to evolve from the initial randomly formed nuclei. The in-situ visualization characterization underpins our understanding and regulation of electrochemical Zn deposition. For objective #2, a phase-field model was developed to simulate Zn deposition and dendrite growth while lattice Boltzmann method as deployed in conjunction to simulate the fluid flow and heat/mass transfer. The simulations successfully revealed the complex morphology evolution at the electrode/electrolyte interface. It was found that the non-uniform distribution of fluid velocity leads to uneven ion concentration distribution, thereby resulting in non-uniform deposition rate. The inhomogeneous deposits further result in a non-uniform electric field distribution, which intensifies Zn2+ ions aggregation and eventually leads to severe Zn dendritic growth. Moreover, the non-uniformity of Zn deposits disrupts electrolyte flow on the surface, exacerbating the uneven Zn deposition. It was suspected that fast growth Zn deposits will penetrate the membrane and thus cause short circuits, thus hindering the increase of areal capacity. Additionally, for the first time, we revealed numerically that during stripping process, non-uniform Zn dissolution will induce the formation of “dead Zn”. During electrolyte circulation, the “dead Zn” may be flushed aways, significantly impairing the reversibility of Zn electrodes. These results provide fresh insights into the complex physical phenomena at a mesoscale. To further extend our understanding at a macro scale, we also developed a cell-scale model integrating fluid flow, mass transfer and electrochemical reactions, which unveiled the non-uniform distribution of the electrolyte over electrode/membrane interface. These numerical results generate essential knowledge on how the transport phenomena impact Zn deposition behavior. For objective #3, we have developed multiscale porous electrodes and novel flow field to promote uniform field distribution at the electrode/electrolyte interface. In the multiscale porous electrodes, the primary pores offer pathways for fast electrolyte flow while the secondary pores on the surface provide more active surface for Zn deposition and promote local convention due to the micro/nanostructures, leading to dense Zn deposition on the fiber surface. The newly engineered flow field ensured the uniform distribution of electrolyte cross the electrode, thus promoting the uniformity of Zn deposition. For the last objective, we have used the optimized electrodes and flow field to assemble lab-scale zinc-bromine flow batteries with 1 M ZnBr2+4 M NH4Cl as electrolytes. Remarkably, with the optimized flow field and multiscale porous electrodes, we were able to achieve a high area capacity of 200 mAh/cm2 without short circuits. More excitingly, the battery can be stably cycled for more than 2000 cycles without obvious degradation, representing the highest performance in zinc-bromine flow batteries. Overall, the project objectives have been fully addressed, with significant advancements in understanding of electrochemical Zn deposition coupling with heat and mass transfer, development of electrodes and flow fields, and improvement of battery performance. The research provides a comprehensive foundation for further development of high-energy, dendrite-free, and long-cycling zinc-based flow batteries.

16205721.label: Major findings and research outcome
16205721.value: Supported by the GRF project, our research has led to the following significant findings and outcomes. Zn deposition is complex physiochemical process coupling heat/mass transfer, electrochemical reaction and phase change. The morphology of Zn deposits plays a significant role in determining the areal capacity and cycle life of zinc-based batteries. It is the non-uniform Zn nucleation and unregulated ion/mass that leads to dendritic Zn deposition. Without fluid flow, it is possible to regulate mass transport at the electrode/electrolyte interface by electrolyte engineering including in-situ form solid-electrolyte interphase, cation and anion comodulated electrolyte, and kinesin-memetic ion director (No. 1, 5, and 6 in Section 8, Part C). The is because mass transport is mainly controlled by diffusion and migration under static conditions. However, in flow batteries, force convention becomes dominant in governing the mass transport process, and it is more crucial to promote the uniform electrolyte distribution. By combining Multiphysics simulation with experimental investigations, we revealed that it is the non-uniform distribution of the fluid flow that cause the uneven distribution of ion concentration, which leads to uneven Zn deposition that results in short-circuits. Accordingly, we have developed novel flow field and multiscale porous electrodes to promote the uniform electrolyte distribution and thus even Zn deposition. Remarkably, the optimal flow field and electrodes enabled the zinc-bromine flow battery to achieve an ultrahigh areal capacity of 200 mAh/cm2 and the battery can stably operate for over 2000 cycles without obvious degradation (manuscript under preparation). The temperate also plays a significant role in the performance of zinc-bromine flow batteries. On the one hand, it greatly increases the reaction kinetics and diffusion rate, which can improve energy efficiency. On the other hand, elevated temperatures will increase self-discharge and corrosion (No. 3 in Section 8, Part C). More importantly, in the presence of a bromine complex agent, we found that the impact of temperature is more complicated. Increasing temperature first more promote more uniform, textured Zn deposition and uniform mixing of oil-water two phases. Further elevating the temperate degrades the battery performance due to the severe side reactions and crossover (manuscript under preparation). A PhD student, Ang Li, is trained under the project and he is expected to graduate in August 2026. Five journal papers have been published based on the research results from this project, one manuscript has been submitted, and two manuscripts are under preparation.

16205721.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16205721.value: While our results show that enhancing mass transfer and promoting uniform distribution of ion and temperature at the electrode/electrolyte interface can effectively suppress zinc dendrite growth, it is found that zinc corrosion still exists in the long-term cycling test. This is due to the thermodynamic instability of zinc metal in aqueous solutions. Moreover, corrosion becomes more severe when the temperature increases. Therefore, future efforts should also be directed to minimize side reactions to achieve long-life zinc-based flow batteries. Electrolyte engineering such as co-solvent and additive are promising approaches due to their ease of preparation, low cost, and effectiveness. In addition, the imbalanced species crossover the separator/membrane is found to cause the electrolyte to accumulate in one side, leading to capacity decay. Understanding the transport phenomenon crosses the membrane and therefore developing highly selective membrane without sacrificing the conductivity and mechanical properties represent one of the most promising directions. The PI’s group will continue to improve the cycling stability of zinc-based flow batteries by addressing these critical challenges.

16205721.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16205721.value: Zinc-based flow batteries offer great promise for large-scale energy storage – a key enabling technology for widespread adoption of clean yet intermittent energy such as wind and solar. However, the practical application of this type of technology is severely hindered by zinc dendrite formation, which considerably reduces the areal capacity and shortens the cycle life. Temperature and mass transfer are the two key factors that affect the battery performance yet remain poorly understood. With the support of this project, we conducted extensive experimental and numerical investigations to elucidate the impact of fluid flow, heat and mass transport on the electrochemical deposition/dissolution behavior of zinc electrodes. Based on the fundamental understanding, we successfully developed strategies (i.e., engineering electrode and flow field) to promote the uniform distribution of ion concentration at the electrode/electrolyte interface. These efforts led to a dramatic boost in both areal capacity and cycle life of zinc-bromine flow batteries even operated at high current density. This project offers not only mechanistic insights into zinc electrodeposition, but effective strategies to regulate the electrochemical process, which are essential to the development of zinc-based flow batteries for safe and cost-effective energy storage.

16205821.value: 區塊鏈技術的進步催生了一種新的計算範式，使應用軟件能夠於沒有中央協調機制的情況下通過去中心化在網絡上運行。以太坊是第二大區塊鏈平台，提供智能合約的功能，使開發人員能夠實施利用分散系統的定制應用軟件。智能合約是自主程序，旨在合併託管在區塊鏈上的預定義合同或協議。開發人員經常會通過易用的去中心化應用程序 (DApps)使用智能合約。 DApps、智能合約及其底層區塊鏈相互交互，以分散的方式完成預定義的任務。現有的研究主要集中在智能合約本身的質量保證上，而沒有考慮由 DApps、智能合約及其底層區塊鏈組成的去中心化基礎設施中不同組件之間的交互。但是，如果交互處理不當，很容易出現問題。在去中心化的基礎設施中很難正確處理各種交互，因為（1）基礎設施中的組件是緊密耦合的，（2）區塊鏈上交易的執行是不確定的，以及（3）基礎設施可能很複雜。因此，錯誤通常來自基礎設施中的組件交互。 在這個研究項目中，我們的目標是了解去中心化基礎設施中複雜的交互機制，DApp中的錯誤表徵，並開發自動化技術來檢測和修復它們。我們將收集並發布第一個 DApp 中真實錯誤的大規模數據集，並提出模型來抽象基礎設施中的複雜交互機制。我們旨在通過系統地研究收集的數據集來總結 DApp 錯誤的常見原因、修復和後果。根據我們的經驗發現，我們將提出有效的技術，專門針對暴露 DApp 中的錯誤。我們將利用基於搜索的測試生成技術來自動生成測試用例來演練不同的交互場景，並在我們提議的交互模型之上定義測試目標。實證研究將使我們能夠推導出測試預言機，以促進 DApp 的錯誤檢測。我們計劃開發自動錯誤修復技術，可以快速及可靠地修復 DApp 中檢測到的錯誤。我們的技術可以幫助越來越多的智能合約和 DApp 開發人員有效地檢測和修復錯誤，並減輕他們繁重的手動測試任務，從而使他們受益。我們還將發布我們實施的技術和收集的數據集，以促進和激發未來的研究。該項目解決了工業中的一個重要問題。它得到了業界的大力支持，其中包括香港應用科技研究院（應科院）、華為、拉卡拉金融服務和騰訊。
