16206321.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16206321.value: The behavior of insect flight is of significant interest for designing human-engineered flapping-wing-based micro air vehicles (MAVs). MAVs have a broad range of applications, including environmental monitoring and surveillance and security. It has been found that wing flexibility is likely to have a significant influence on the resulting aerodynamics. Furthermore, insects can produce more force by increasing stroke amplitude and/or flapping frequency, but the kinematic response of a given species is thought to be consistent. Flapping flight with pitch regulation is a commonly used mode of thrust and lift generation in insects and has been widely emulated in flying vehicles because it allows for simple implementation of the complex kinematics associated with flapping wing systems. Compared to most other insects, dragonflies are of unusual characteristics due to its long wing aspect ratio and slender bodies. They are highly agile flyers, and can utilize wing phasing to control their forward, backward, gliding and maneuver flights. They also exhibit complex wing-air and wing-wing interactions; to date, some key aerodynamic mechanisms related to flexible tandem wing remain inadequately understood. In this proposed research, fluid–structure interaction on aerodynamic characteristics of flexible flapping wings will be investigated utilizing time-resolved particle image velocity, force sensors and advanced optical probing techniques. In order to probe the issues with sufficient control, both flexible artificial wings will be fabricated utilizing micro/nanofabrication techniques. The pitching and flexibility effects of membrane wing will be investigated under different flapping frequencies, stroke amplitudes. Engineered tandem flexible wings will be studied to understand the wing-wing and wing-vortex interaction along spanwise and chordwise and the flexibility effects will be elucidated. The spanwise aerodynamic behaviors associated with flapping wings’ phasing relationship, wing pitching and flexibility and wing spacing effects on wing-wing/wing-vortex interactions, wake capturing and lift enhancement will be investigated. A comprehensive study of the pitching effects on flexible flapping flights may help bio-inspired design of wing articulation systems for micro air vehicles. Numerical simulations will be conducted to analyze and optimize the wing kinematics control for flexible tandem wing design. Fluid–structure interaction through wing-wake captured by the hindwing will be measured by time-resolved particle image velocity and compared with numerical results. It is important to understand to what extent the wing pitching, spacing and phasing can affect the flight efficiency. An optimized model of flexible tandem flapping wing flights will be developed taking the wing pitching, phasing, frequency and stroke amplitude into consideration. 昆蟲飛行的行為對於設計微型撲翼飛行器 (MAV) 具有重要意義。 微型撲翼飛行器在環境監測、監視和安全等方面具有廣泛的應用。研究發現柔性機翼對微型撲翼飛行器的空氣動力學特性產生重大影響。此外，昆蟲可以通過增加撲翼幅度和改變撲翼頻率來產生更大的動力，但同一種類的昆蟲的撲翼運動學響應應該是一致的。昆蟲飛行中常用調節撲翼俯仰角的方法來產生推力和升力，這種方法已經在飛行器仿真模擬中得到了廣泛應用，因為它允許簡單地實現與撲翼系統相關的複雜運動學。與大多數其他昆蟲相比，蜻蜓因其翅膀的高展弦比和纖細的身體而具有不同尋常的特徵。它們是高度敏捷的飛行器，可以利用機翼相位控制它們的前進、後退、滑翔和機動飛行。它們還表現出複雜的翅膀空氣動力學參數和前後翅交互作用。迄今為止，與柔性串聯機翼相關的一些關鍵空氣動力學機制仍未得到充分了解。 在這項擬議的研究中，我們將利用高速粒子圖像速度儀、力傳感器和先進的光學探測技術研究流-固耦合相互作用對柔性撲翼氣動特性的影響。為了對問題有足夠的控制，我們將利用微/納米製造技術來製造兩個柔性翼。將在不同的撲動頻率、幅度下研究膜翼的俯仰和柔韌性影響。我們將研究設計的串聯柔性機翼，以了解沿展向和弦向的前後翅交互作用和翼-渦相互作用，並闡明柔性翼的影響。將研究前後翅的相位關係、撲翼俯仰和柔性以及翼間距對前後翅交互作用/翼-渦相互作用、尾流捕獲和升力增強相關的展向空氣動力學特性。對柔性撲翼飛行的俯仰效應的綜合研究可能有助於微型飛行器機翼鉸接系統的仿生設計。將進行數值模擬以分析和優化靈活串聯撲翼設計的撲翼運動學控制。通過後翼捕獲的翼尾流-結構相互作用將通過高速粒子圖像速度儀進行測量，並與數值結果進行比較。了解撲翼俯仰、間距和相位在多大程度上影響飛行效率是很重要的。我們將考慮撲翼俯仰、相位、頻率和撲拍幅度，開發柔性串聯撲翼飛行的優化模型。

16206321.label: Realisation of objectives
16206321.value: The primary purpose of Objective 1 is to develop different flexible wings with different stiffness and aspect ratios using micro/nanofabrication techniques. We have developed the flexible wings with different stiffness and aspect ratios using micro/nanofabrication techniques. Their performance meets the requirements outlined in the project proposal and ensures the successful completion of the following research. The primary purpose of Objective 2 is to investigate the effects of active/passive wing pitching, wing kinematics, and wing flexibility on aerodynamic performance. To understand the effects of active wing pitching and wing kinematics, flow fields and wing kinematics were measured on a live tethered dragonfly of the species wandering glider. The dragonfly was fixed by its thorax to a thin glass plate, and its right hindwing was surgically removed at the wing root, preserving the musculature and exoskeleton. Time-resolved PIV flow measurements were taken in a glass-walled flight chamber. A vertically aligned laser light sheet of about 1mm thickness illuminated the seeding particles in a spanwise cross section of the wings of the horizontally aligned dragonfly. To target the region of strongest expected flow structures, PIV measurements were taken at the wing midspan during mid-stroke. A high-speed camera recorded the flow in double-frame mode, and the data were subsequently processed using a multi-pass algorithm with stepwise decreasing interrogation windows to compute the vector fields. Then, the forewing of the dragonfly together with the adherent exoskeleton of the joint was removed and used for the experiments with passive pitch mechanism. Using the exact same wing and having only a short time to pass between the experiments ensured that wing flexibility and the resulting aeroelastic deformations (cambering and twisting) remained the same in both measurements. The wing temporal kinematics were measured from the high-speed camera recordings. The positional angle was calculated using the known distance between the laser plane and the wing root along with the projected distance between the laser-illuminated leading edge and the wing root inside the recorded PIV frames. The pitching angle was then measured as the angle between the line connecting a laser illuminated leading edge and trailing edge and the normal line of the stroke plane. To mimic passive wing pitching, a wing control mechanism that can realize wing flapping and passive rotation was developed utilizing micro-fabrication technology. The motions of the inner cylinder and outer tube were enough to realize both the wing flapping and rotation in sync similar to that of a real dragonfly in cruising flight with the use of only one motor. To further evaluate the dominance of inertial passive and active muscle-controlled pitch actuation in dragonfly flight, the flow fields and pitching angle variations of the naturally actuated wing of a tethered dragonfly were compared with those of the same wing artificially actuated via a proposed passive mechanism. The primary purpose of Objective 3 is to investigate the effects of wing-wing and wing-vortex interactions of flexible tandem wings under different wing kinematics, and to investigate the active and passive wing pitch reversal of artificial tandem wings. The effects of wing-wing and wing-vortex interactions of flexible tandem wings under different wing kinematics were investigated and active and passive wing pitch reversal of artificial tandem wings was studied. We found that passive rotation characterizes most of the forewing flapping cycle except the upstroke reversal where the dragonfly uses its muscle movement to accelerate its forewing rotation, and accelerated wing rotation at the upstroke reversal will result in a stronger leading-edge vortex (LEV) during the downstroke, the additional force from which is estimated to account for 4.3% of the total cycle averaged force generated. The effects of wing kinematics on both normal forward flight and escape flight of a dragonfly were further investigated. The wing aspect ratio, phasing, flexibility and kinematics for aerodynamics of tandem flapping wings were studied and optimized experimentally and numerically. The wing kinematics of tethered specimens and the prescribed wing morphology of a free-flying dragonfly were used in the simulation. By adopting a specific wing morphology and scaling it solely in time within the flapping cycle, the wing deformation pattern, including spanwise bending, twist, and camber, is maintained identically across all cases. The morphological model of the wings with prescribed deformations was constructed based on the measured dynamic deformation of the wings of a free-flying dragonfly in steady forward flight, which closely resembles the normal flight mode. We traced 3 flapping cycles and selected the cycle that provided the best continuity for the numerical model. A surface fitted to the traced markers was used to define the prescribed deformations of the wings in the numerical simulation. To shed light on the interplay between wing phasing, flapping amplitude, wing angles and aerodynamics, a parametric study of kinematics was conducted numerically. By investigating the effect of the individual kinematic parameters in isolation and in combination, we found that the phasing of the flapping positional angle does not affect the aerodynamics substantially by itself; however, in combination with the varied local angle of attack, it suppresses the variation in the total forces and slightly improves the efficiency. This part of the work was completed in collaboration with Professor Qiu's team. To address the challenges posed by complex geometries, moving boundaries, and large deformations in wing-wing and wing-vortex interactions, we established a comprehensive and advanced computational framework. Firstly, a novel Block-based Adaptive Particle Refinement (BAPR) method was developed, which is able to provide the necessary local refinement flexibly for any targeted characteristic. In addition, a new particle refinement strategy with the refinement scale ratio of 4 was employed for multi-level resolutions, and this significantly decreases the computational costs compared to the standard Adaptive Particle Refinement (APR) method. Secondly, particle distribution was optimized by a novel particle shifting technique (PST) leveraging Voronoi diagrams to ensure isotropy and exact volume conservation, even for violent flows. Thirdly, for solid mechanics, a semi-meshless Lagrangian finite-volume framework based on Voronoi diagrams was developed for general elastoplastic Reissner-Mindlin shells. The compensation terms are devised to suppress the zero-energy modes, ensuring high numerical robustness. Finally, these components were integrated into a novel three-dimensional meshless fluid–structure interaction (FSI) framework coupling smoothed particle hydrodynamics (SPH) with the semi-meshless shell solver. Within this framework, the boundary integral method is used to approximate operators at the interface instead of conventional multi-layer ghost boundary, while a velocity penalty term effectively eliminates the artificial slipping phenomenon by enforcing the no-slip condition. Furthermore, the versatility of this framework was demonstrated by a hybrid approach that enhances SPH for wall-bounded turbulence by coupling it with an unstructured finite-volume method near moving boundaries. Beyond the core meshless framework, an implicit Moving-Least-Squares Immersed Boundary Method (MLS-IBM) was developed as a key enhancement. It is designed to accurately enforce velocity boundary conditions by overcoming the asymmetry between interpolation and spreading operations. This approach ensures excellent conservation properties and achieves discretization errors at the level of machine precision, providing high accuracy in simulations of moving boundaries and large deformations. Collectively, these developments provide a highly efficient tool for studying wing-wing and wing-vortex interactions.

16206321.label: Major findings and research outcome
16206321.value: To achieve Objective 2, in [J1], fluid–structure interaction on aerodynamic characteristics of flapping wings has been investigated by utilizing time-resolved PIV, force sensors, and optical probing techniques. Both natural and artificial flapping wings were studied by utilizing micro/nanofabrication with controllable mechanisms that can provide active and passive wing pitching. The fluid-structure interaction under different wing pitchings, flapping frequencies, stroke amplitudes, and flexibility effects were investigated. Engineered tandem flexible wings were examined to understand spanwise and chordwise interactions and flexibility effects To achieve Objective 3, in [J1], the spanwise aerodynamic behaviors on wing-wing/wing-vortex interactions, wake capturing and lift enhancement were investigated. It was found that passive rotation characterizes most of the forewing flapping cycle except the upstroke reversal where the dragonfly uses its muscle movement to accelerate its forewing rotation. In [J5][J11], the effects of wing kinematics and fluid-structure interaction on both normal forward flight and escape flight of a dragonfly have been characterized. A Navier-Stokes-based numerical model has been adopted, and results have been substantiated by experimental data. The wing kinematics of tethered specimens and the prescribed wing morphology of a free-flying dragonfly were used in the simulation. To investigate kinematical-aerodynamic interplay, a parametric study found that escape flight boosts dragonfly lift but reduces thrust and efficiency. To address the challenges regarding simulation of flapping wings in Objective 3, we have developed a comprehensive numerical framework. Firstly, to reduce the computational cost, a BAPR strategy with a large refinement scale ratio was introduced [J2][J3]. A novel Voronoi-based PST was developed to improve numerical robustness by effectively maintaining isotropic particle distribution [J4]. Secondly, a high-order moving-least-squares targeted essentially non-oscillatory SPH (MLS-TENO-SPH) scheme was proposed for compressible flows [J6]. The MLS approximation is employed in smooth regions for high-order accuracy, while the TENO scheme is applied in non-smooth regions. Additionally, an implicit MLS-IBM was proposed to accurately enforce the velocity boundary condition [J9]. Computational fidelity for wall-bounded turbulence is significantly enhanced through a hybrid SPH–unstructured finite-volume framework that uses a reduced-order wall-modeled LES (WMLES) approach. [J10]. Thirdly, to further investigate the FSI mechanism, a semi-meshless thin shell model based on the Voronoi diagram [J7] was coupled with the fluid solver via a boundary integral method, enabling high-fidelity simulation of flexible structures [J8]. These outputs form an integrated framework capable of efficient, accurate simulation of complex FSI like wing-wing and wing-vortex interactions in flapping flight.

16206321.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16206321.value: Based on the findings, some aspects can be further explored for a fuller understanding of flapping wing aerodynamics. For the passive rotation structure, which used an inelastic string to bound the wing's pitching angle, oscillations were observed at the stroke reversal, which affect the wing’s aerodynamics. Thus, modifications to the passive rotation structure are needed to mitigate the oscillations. Furthermore, the tandem passive pitching flight can be explored with different phase lags and distances between the wing roots. The active pitching motor control system was built up, and an arbitrary combination of flapping and pitching motions could be achieved. Beyond the average wing-root rotational angle explored, other control parameters like the shape of the wing-root rotational angle can be further investigated. Regarding the artificial dragonfly wing, further attempts can focus on integrating corrugation into the wing structure, which can help enhance the spanwise stiffness without adding mass effects. With an appropriate combination of phase, active pitching, wing flexibility and angle of attack changes of the fore- and hindwings, the lift and thrust generation of the tandem winged system can be effectively controlled. The results can help develop flight control strategies for micro-scale air vehicle design.

16206321.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16206321.value: Insect flight is of significant interest for designing human-engineered flapping-wing-based micro air vehicles, which have a broad range of applications in environmental, surveillance, and security monitoring. We studied wing flexibility, pitching and fluid-structure interaction which have a significant influence on aerodynamic performance and energy efficiency. Flapping flight with pitch regulation is a commonly used mode of thrust and lift generation in insects and has been widely emulated in flying vehicles because it allows for simple implementation of the complex kinematics associated with flapping wing systems. In this study, we found that passive pitching can satisfy most of the forewing flapping cycle except the upstroke reversal where the dragonfly uses its muscle movement to accelerate its forewing rotation. This finding helps in the design of wing control mechanisms. We also found that in escape flight, the dragonfly generates additional lift while the thrust reduces and the overall efficiency drops in comparison with normal flight. Therefore, we can optimize the performance according to different applications. Together, progress on these fronts is reshaping the design paradigm of flapping wing air vehicles and other types of robots with shrinking physical dimensions and more versatile capabilities to meet wider ranges of missions.

16207221.value: Objective A: Multi-Tier Deep Neural Network Architecture for Federated Learning with Hybrid Data Partitioning: In the first task, we will design a multi-tier neural network (NN) architecture to incorporate multi-type features collected by clusters of heterogeneous IoT sensors in the network. Specifically, we partition the neural network into local type-specific NNs at each sensor and a global inter-type fusion NN at the cloud. The type-specific NNs are deployed at each local sensor to adapt to the type-specific features and structures, while the intertype fusion NN is implemented at the server to exploit the diversity from the multi-type features among the heterogeneous sensors. Such a partitioned design not only provides a flexible structure for joint feature fusion but also adapts to the incomplete data features at the local sensor side. Objective B: Hierarchical Federated Learning Algorithm to Embrace Sample and Feature Diversity: In the second task, we propose a hierarchical federated learning approach to exploit the sample and feature parallelisms in the hybrid data partitioning configuration. Specifically, the sample parallelism refers to the fact that the data held by each sensor may come from different samples of a dataset and hence, embracing these sensors in the federated learning ensures that sample diversity can be exploited. Similarly, feature parallelism refers to the fact that the data held by each sensor may also contribute to different feature space in the problem and hence, embracing these sensors in the federated learning ensures we have feature diversity as well. To achieve this, we will transform the original training problem into an equivalent primal-dual form such that the training problem can be separated at both the sample space and feature space.

16207221.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16207221.value: 未來 6G 無線網絡應設計為支持人工智能應用。其中，聯邦學習已被廣泛應用於在本地傳感器和中央服務器之間協作訓練一個公共的神經網絡。 對於傳統的聯邦學習應用，數據樣本分布在傳感器的本地數據集中。 在每次訓練迭代中，每個傳感器從中央服務器獲取最新的網絡模型參數值，然後利用其本地數據更新模型。 隨後，其計算的局部梯度或模型參數更新值被傳輸到中央服務器以進行模型聚合，如圖 1 所示。近年來，由於新興硬件技術的發展，大量具有不同感知能力的多類型傳感器被應用於數據收集和神經網絡的訓練。 例如，在分類任務中，一些傳感器被用於收集視頻或圖像數據，而其他傳感器可能會收集有關對象的重量或其他指標。 因此，各類型傳感器在特定類型的特徵空間上收集部分數據樣本，這導致跨本地數據集的混合數據分區，如圖 2 所示。這種跨多類型傳感器的混合數據分區為開發具有高效通信效率和可擴展的聯合學習算法帶來挑戰。首先，在傳統的聯邦學習中，每個傳感器都具有與雲中相同的神經網絡模型副本。然而，當網絡中存在異構傳感器時，這種同構神經網絡不再適用。其次，傳統的聯邦學習只利用了單一類型傳感器之間的樣本多樣性。對於混合數據分區的情況，聯邦學習方案應同時利用多類型傳感器之間的樣本和特徵的多樣性。第三，在傳統的聯邦學習方案實施中，空中梯度聚合或空中模型聚合可被用於提高無線網絡傳輸的頻譜效率。然而，由於網絡中存在異構傳感器，這種簡單的無線聚合方案無法被利用於具有混合數據分區的網絡系統。在這個項目中，我們將專注於解決這些挑戰，並設計一個具有高效頻譜傳輸效率的多層聯邦學習訓練方案，以利用異構類型傳感器本地數據集之間的樣本多樣性和特徵多樣性。具體來說，本項目的主要目標如下: (1) 適應於混合數據分區的多層深度神經網絡架構：在第一個任務中，我們將設計一個多層神經網絡架構，以適用於異構傳感器收集的多類型特徵數據。我們將神經網絡劃分為在本地傳感器處的局部特定類型神經網絡 以及在中央服務器處的全局類型融合神經網絡。 這種多層網絡結構設計不僅為多類型特徵數據的利用提供了靈活的架構，而且還適應於局部傳感器端的不完整數據特徵情況。 (2) 利用樣本和特徵多樣性的分層聯邦學習算法：在第二個任務中，我們提出一種分層聯邦學習訓練方案，以利用混合數據分區下的並行樣本和特徵多樣性。 通過優化問題理論分析，我們計劃將原始訓練問題轉換為等效的原始對偶形式，以便可以在樣本空間和特徵空間上分離訓練問題。 由於對未來無線通信系統中集成智能應用的訓練性能和頻譜效率的顯著提升，本項目所提出的分層聯邦學習訓練方案將對人工智能應用在6G通信系統中的實施產生巨大的影響。 這將有利於開闢潛在的基於人工智能的物聯網應用，並充分發掘下一代 6G 無線網絡的潛力，以推動一系列智慧城市應用進程。

16207521.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16207521.value: Internal erosion (including backward-erosion piping (herein called piping) and suffusion), water-overtopping surface erosion and shallow soil failure are three common failure modes of earth dams and slopes. Previous research has shown that plants and fungi, which have important ecological functions to the natural environment and earth infrastructure, can effectively improve the stability and erosion resistance of the surface soil downstream through plant root reinforcement and soil aggregation. However, study of the use of plant-fungus symbiosis as a bio-remediation technique to improve the internal erosion resistance is not available. The effects of plant roots and fungi on soil physiochemical properties and on the soil resistance to piping and suffusion under different soil stress states have not yet been investigated. Moreover, any detrimental effects on the internal erosion resistance due to the death of fungi and plants (hence root decay) are unknown. This project will, for the first time, develop new experimental evidence to the improvement of soil internal erosion resistance by deep-rooted plants and arbuscular mycorrhizal (AM) fungi. The focus will be studying the piping and suffusion resistances of both internally stable and unstable soils of different gap ratios. Modified triaxial erosion apparatus will be used to investigate both the piping and suffusion resistances of bio-remediated soils subjected to different isotropic and anisotropic stress paths (in both compression and extension spaces) relevant to the stress conditions in earth dams and slopes. In order to identify the underlying mechanisms by which plant roots and fungi improve the soil internal erosion resistance, changes in the root mechanical and chemical properties because of plant-fungus symbiosis will be investigated. The effects of plant roots and fungi on the soil aggregate stability, water repellence and shearing properties will also be explored. Special attention will be paid to any detrimental effects of root decay and the death of fungi on the internal erosion resistance. The project will be implemented by an inter-disciplinary team composed of engineers and biologist. Synergies among their expertise will help to unlock some key scientific research questions related to soil-plant-fungus interaction. The new understanding developed will provide engineers new insights into the use of plants and fungi as an alternative low-cost and environmentally-friendly bio-remediation technique to improving the engineering performance of earth dams and slopes. 內部侵蝕（包括管湧和潛蝕）、漫頂侵蝕和淺層土壤破壞是土壩和土坡破壞的三種常見模式。現存研究表明了植物和真菌對自然環境和土工結構有著重要生態功能，通過根系加固和土壤團聚作用能夠有效提高下游表層土壤的穩定性和抗侵蝕能力。然而，目前尚未有研究運用植物-真菌共生作為一種生物修復技術來提高內部抗侵蝕能力。而植物根系和真菌的土壤物理化學特性以及對處於不同應力狀態下土體抵抗管湧和潛蝕作用的影響也有待研究。此外，真菌和植物的死亡（根系腐爛）對土壤抗內部侵蝕能力的損害效應亦不可知。 本項目將首次開展創新性實驗研究深根植物和叢枝菌根真菌對土壤抗內部侵蝕的改善作用，並且將著重研究內部不穩定土壤的抗管湧和潛蝕能力。本項目將採用改進的三軸侵蝕裝置來探究生物修復土壤在承受與土壩和土坡的應力條件相似的不同各向同性或者各向異性應力路徑（包括壓縮路徑和張拉路徑）時的抗管湧和潛蝕能力。為了確定植物根系和真菌改善土壤抗內部侵蝕能力的內在機理，由植物-真菌共生導致的植物根系力學性質和化學性質的改變將被研究。植物根系和真菌對土壤團聚穩定性和剪切性質也將被探索。 本項目將由一支由工程師和生物學家構成的跨學科科研團隊承擔。他們各自專業的協同增效作用將有助於解開一些與土壤-植物-真菌相互作用相關的關鍵科研問題。由此得到的新認識將為工程師在採用植物和真菌這種相對低價環保的生物修復技術來提高土壩和邊坡的工程性能方面時有新的見解。

16207521.label: Realisation of objectives
16207521.value: Objective 1 has been achieved 100%. In this project, we inoculated AM fungi to Bermuda grass (Cynodon dactylon L.) and measured the biomass, the contents of cellulose and lignin, and the biomechanical properties, including tensile strength and Young’s modulus of the grass roots as they grew for 180 days and then decayed for 360 days after burning or for 60 days after the herbicide application. Results show that the AM fungi accelerated the accumulation of grass biomass and root cellulose content compared with non-mycorrhizal grass during the growth period. This effect of AM fungi made mycorrhizal grass generally maintained more biomass and cellulose content than non-mycorrhizal grass at every decaying stage. Inoculation of the AM fungi did not significantly change the root tensile strength or Young’s modulus, but it altered the correlations between tensile strength and root diameter, and Young’s modulus and root diameter. Mycorrhizal effects during the root decaying process appeared to diminish under herbicide treatment, compared with normal growth and burning treatments. Our study highlights the important role of AM fungi in maintaining in situ root biomass (a proxy for carbon content) from decaying or decomposing. In the project, we also investigated aggregate stabilisation and breakdown mechanisms in compacted dense mycorrhizal soils. Methods A pot-culture experiment with seven treatments (five replicates per treatment) was implemented. In a local decomposed granitic soil, we inoculated two grass species (Chrysopogon ziaanioides and Cynodon dactylon) with AM fungi. We used loose soil to grow C. dactylon to compare it with compacted dense soil, as well as pots without a plant and/or fungal inoculation for comparison. After 20 weeks of cultivation, we measured root and AM fungal characteristics, soil organic matter and aggregate properties by dry sieving, wet sieving and Le Bissonnais methods. Compaction led to the formation of macroaggregates (> 0.25 mm) but had a negative influence on the aggregate stability. The fungal inoculation increased polysaccharide production and aggregate stability in the compacted soil vegetated with C. dactylon. The inoculated C. ziaanioides showed a similar level of aggregate stability as the inoculated C. dactylon, but the uninoculated group demonstrated higher aggregate stability compared with the inoculated group owing to root decomposition. The aggregate stability against various breakdown mechanisms was related to the established aggregate hierarchy and qualitative organic matter inputs. Soil organic matter supplied by grass species together with the mediation of AM fungal hyphae played a crucial role in the systemic enhancement of aggregate stability in the compacted soil. Objective 2 has been achieved 100%. By using a newly developed triaxial permeameter, the internal erosion behaviour of bare soils were measured under different stress states and its consequences on the anisotropic mechanical behaviour of eroded soil. Evolutions of fabric anisotropy during erosion were evaluated by measuring the shear wave velocity at various wave propagation and polarisation directions under the isotropic loading condition. Soil samples with and without erosion were then sheared following a path of constant mean effective stress to determine the stiffness degradation curves. Results show that the losses of fines and the rearrangement of soil particles due to erosion increased the fabric anisotropy (i.e. increased horizontal alignments of soil particles) by 10% at all confining pressures. Such increase resulted in eroded specimens that were stronger than their intact counterparts upon triaxial compression, but the opposite trend was observed upon extension. The eroded specimens had a higher volumetric threshold shear strain than the intact ones, thereby suggesting that higher strains were required to substantially change the soil structure and reduce the small-strain shear stiffness. For the case of rooted soils, upon compression stress conditions (𝜂 >0), the presence of roots increases the i_cr is over four time higher of the bare samples from 0.25 to 0.96 at an effective confining pressure (p’) of 50 kPa and from 0.59 to 2.63 at p’ of 100 kPa and the amount of eroded fines was reduced from 12.9% to 4.9% and from 8.9% to 2.2% respectively. The roots alter the soil structure and form a more stable pore network. This is because the fibrous roots cross potential failure and flow paths, forming network that bridges pore spaces and binds soil particles, physically blocking fines migration. Additionally, upon extension stress conditions (𝜂<0), the i_cr increases similarly to compression cases, but the amount of eroded fines decreases far less. This divergence is attributed to stress-induced fabric anisotropy. During triaxial extension, the major principal stress acts radially, causing fibrous roots to reorient parallel to major principal stress (i.e., horizontally). This alignment creates low-tortuosity flow paths along the axis, reducing obstruction to migrating fines. In contrast, under triaxial compression, major principal stress is axial, aligning roots vertically. Importantly, the radially distributed fibrous root network (unlike a taproot system) provides mul-tidirectional reinforcement perpendicular to major principal stress. This enhances soil confine-ment, stabilizes force chains, and increases pore constriction—promoting self-filtration at the root-soil interface. As a result, despite similar increases in icr, the geometric hindrance under compression reduces fines transport by 60–75% compared to extension. Objective 3 has been achieved 100%. In this project, we measured the effects of root decomposition due to herbicide on the root biomechanical properties and root reinforcement provided by two vetiver species (Chrysopogon nemoralis and Chrysopogon zizanioides). We applied herbicide (i.e., propanil) to four treatments of each species, considering four different durations of decomposition (7-, 28-, 56- and 112-days since herbicide application). The biomechanical properties were measured by uniaxial tensile tests, whereas the root reinforcement to poorly graded sand was quantified by direct shear tests. Root decomposition significantly reduced mean root tensile strength, secant modulus and breakage strain of C. nemoralis and C. zizaniodes roots after 112 days since the herbicide application. Significant negative power correlations between root diameter and root strength (or root secant modulus) were identified. Root decomposition did not change the shape of these correlations, but they shifted downwards as roots decomposed. The root reinforcement also declined with the decomposition duration, in terms of root cohesion and maximum dilatancy within the study period. C. nemoralis displayed greater and quicker loss of both the root biomechanical properties and root reinforcement to soil than C. zizanioides. We also investigated the effects of root growth and decay on the changes in root biomechanical properties and the shearing behaviour of vegetated soils. Columns of compacted soils were grown with a grass species, Cynodon dactylon. The grass was grown for 6 months, followed by burning or herbicide applications to introduce root decay. The top part of each column was used for direct shear tests, whilst the roots collected from the bottom part were used for the measurements of root tensile and chemical properties. The vegetated soils displayed greater shear strength and larger dilatancy, which were attributable to the growth-induced increase in the root cellulose content, and thus the root tensile strength and modulus. Root decay caused declines in the root tensile properties, which translated to the reductions in soil dilatancy and soil shear strength lower than those of the fallow soil. Herbicide use introduced a much faster and significant loss of root reinforcement than burning because of the more severe decay and loss of root biomechanical properties.

16207521.label: Major findings and research outcome
16207521.value: With the arbuscular mycorrhizal (AM) fungal inoculation, the Vetiver showed a similar level of aggregate stability as the inoculated Bermuda. However, the uninoculated Vetiver exhibited high aggregate stability, which can be attributed to the distinctive organic carbon inputs through the decomposition of old roots. Compared with its loose counterpart, the dense soil imposed limitations on the root development of the Bermuda, soil organic matter inputs and soil aggregate stability. Nevertheless, the hyphae networks of the AM fungi effectively mitigated the adverse effects. Soil aggregate stability against various breakdown mechanisms was related to the hierarchical structure of the macro-aggregates, via the cooperation of grass roots and AM fungal hyphae and the qualitative organic matter inputs. Our study emphasised the systemic enhancement of aggregate stability in compacted soil through organic matter inputs and the mediation of AM fungi. Erosion took place when the hydraulic gradients of the soil specimens exceeded a critical value (i_start), and i_start increased along with the effective confinement. The fines loss triggered an initial increase in hydraulic conductivity, but this hydraulic property considerably decreased due to pore clogging by those fines that migrated and eventually accumulated at the bottom part of the eroded specimens. Erosion resulted in significant reductions in shear modulus at any confinement as the hydraulic gradient exceeded the i_start due to the increase in void ratio after fines loss. However, the fabric anisotropy of the initially isotropic specimens increased by up to 10% along with the hydraulic gradient, thereby implying that the particles were arranged with their long side orientated towards the horizontal direction and had stronger and stiffer horizontal contacts. After compression, the shear strength of the eroded specimens at the small-strain range was higher than that of the intact counterparts, with the former showing a less contractive behaviour. The changes in shearing behaviour were attributable to the erosion-induced increase in fabric anisotropy. However, the shear strength of these specimens became practically the same at a large strain range (i.e. >1%) due to the fabric evolution resulting from the straining process in which the soil particles may have aligned with the direction of the major principal stress. However, this observation was reversed following extension where the major principal stress was more aligned with the elongation of the majority of the particles of the more anisotropic eroded specimens.

16207521.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16207521.value: This project focuses on the soil behaviour under fully saturated condition. The next step will be to expand the scope to investigate the effects of degree of saturation or matric suction on the internal erosion resistance of unsaturated soils, which are often found in superficial depths of earthen dams. Indeed, with the presence of vegetation, plant transpiration dries soil further and hence changes the soil water regime. Thus, studying the internal erosion behaviour under unsaturated condition is relevant and vital. The new permeameter developed in this project could test saturated soils only, so it will need to be modified to allow matric suction to be monitored by a miniature high capacity tensiometer and/or to be controlled through state-of-the-art techniques such as axis-translation and hanging-column methods. Moreover, the pore-scale soil-root-water interaction during internal erosion is fundamental to understanding the element-scale engineering behaviour, but has not yet been explored in this project and the literature. Future efforts will be made to (1) develop new experimental systems that would allow in situ monitoring of soil-root kinematics under controlled hydraulic conditions; and (2) advanced numerical means such as coupled DEM-CFD, in an attempt to discover the exact mechanisms of root reinforcement to erosion-susceptible soils.

16207521.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16207521.value: In this project, a new and novel head- and flow-controllable triaxial permeameter has been designed, manufactured and patented to investigate the piping and suffusion resistances of bio-remediated soils subjected to different isotropic and anisotropic stress paths (in both compression and extension spaces) relevant to the stress conditions in earth dams and slopes. New experimental evidence about the improvement of internal erosion resistance of gap-graded soils made by deep-rooted plants and arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi is provided. We have advanced the understandings about the underlying mechanisms by which plant roots and fungi improve the soil internal erosion resistance and changes in the root mechanical and chemical properties because of plant-fungus symbiosis. The effects of plant roots and fungi on the aggregate stability, water repellence, permeability and shearing properties (including dilatancy) of the soil have been explored. Any detrimental effects of root decay and the death of fungi on the internal erosion resistance have also been explored. Based on the new data generated from this project and the discoveries, we are the first to provide new insights into the use of plants and fungi as an alternative low-cost and environmentally-friendly bio-remediation technique to improving the engineering performance of earth dams and slopes.

16207621.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16207621.value: The United Nations’ 2030 Agenda aims to promote sustainable industrialization, and foster innovation by making cities safe, resilient, and sustainable. Urban cities are characterized by dense populations with limited space, where the expansion of human settlements in cities have caused an increasing demand for utilities (water, electricity, and transportation system). The urgent need for underground tunnel infrastructures in congested urban cities necessitates the construction of closely spaced tunnels. Tunnel construction inevitably changes the distribution of stress in the surrounding ground, thereby inducing ground movements which could have an adversely impact on existing tunnels and underground services nearby. Previous studies have mostly focused on the responses of existing tunnels interacting with new perpendicularly crossing tunnels. However, there is an evidence that the stress redistribution and deformation induced by an adjacent new tunnel excavated at various skew angles can potentially cause larger deformation and bending moments than perpendicularly crossing tunnels. A systematic investigation of three-dimensional tunnel interactions with various skew angles is therefore necessary. Moreover, previous investigations focused on a single soil layer, which is often greatly simplified with respect to the actual ground conditions in the field. A study of two-layer soil systems is certainly more appropriate for many situations. This proposed project aims to investigate and understand the interaction between crossing tunnels with different skew angles in single and two-layer soil systems (sand and clay). Systematic three-dimensional centrifuge model tests will be carried out using the state-of-the-art geotechnical centrifuge at HKUST. To understand the complex tunnel-tunnel interactions, a recently developed excavation modelling technique by the PI will be used to simulate both volume and weight losses due to tunnelling in-flight. Moreover, three-dimensional numerical back-analyses of centrifuge model tests and parametric studies will be conducted using an advanced soil model, that can capture strain- and path-dependent soil stiffness, to investigate crossing tunnel interactions and to develop comprehensive design calculation charts. The findings from this study will promote safe and economical tunnelling design for congested underground spaces around the world. 聯合國2030年議程旨在建設安全、韌性和可持續的城市來促進創新和產業可持續化。人口密集、空間有限的城市中，人口增長導致對水、電和交通等基礎設施的需求持續增長。由於地下隧道基礎設施建設的迫切需求，在密集都市中難免要建設間隔很近的隧道。隧道施工不可避免地會改變周圍場地的應力分佈，從而引起場地變形，對附近現有的隧道和地下設施產生不利影響。以往的研究主要集中在現有隧道與新建的垂直交叉隧道的相互作用。然而，有證據表明，與垂直交叉隧道相比，以不同交叉角度開挖的相鄰新建隧道引起的應力重分佈和變形可能會導致更大的變形和彎矩。因此有必要對各種交叉角度的隧道的三維相互作用進行系統的研究。另外，以前的研究集中在單一土層中，這相比現場的實際工程條件往往過於簡化。對於兩層土分佈結構的研究適用於更多的工程條件。 本項目旨在研究單層土和雙層土(砂土及黏土)場地中不同夾角的隧道間的相互作用。計劃在香港科技大學採用先進的離心機技術進行系統的三維模型試驗。將採用本項目負責人最新研發的開挖模擬技術，在離心旋轉過程中模擬隧道挖掘造成的體積和質量損失，從而加深對複雜的隧道-隧道相互作用的理解。另外，將對離心機模型試驗結果進行三維數值反分析和參數研究，採用先進的岩土本構模型來反映土體剛度的應變相關性及應力路徑相關性，從而深入研究交叉隧道間的相互作用，並提出綜合的設計計算方法。本研究的成果將會促進世界各地的密集地下空間中進行隧道設計和開發的安全性和經濟性。

16207621.label: Major findings and research outcome
16207621.value: It is found that the maximum tunnel settlement is induced when two tunnels intercept at a skew angle 30 degrees. This is because the unsupported soil arching is wider and longer at 30 degrees than at 90 degrees during tunnelling interception. Tensile strains induced at an existing tunnel can be 2.3 times higher at 30 degrees interception than that at 90 degrees, prone to tunnel cracks. (Refer to Ng et al., 2022 in Part C). The existing tunnel elongates horizontally and vertically when a new tunnel intercepts at 90 degrees and 30 degrees, respectively. At 90 degrees, the hoop stress increases at the crown and decreases at the left springline of the existing tunnel, oppose to those of 30° tunnelling. The existing design approach of using tunnel interception at 90 degrees is found to be not conservative. To minimise tunnel settlement and deformation, a skew angle of 30 degrees or smaller should be paid more attention in design. (Refer to Ng et al., 2022 in Part C). When twin tunnelling in two layered soil strata with a loose layer overlies a dense layer, the most critical scenario is when the interface located at the new tunnel invert. In this case, soil arch is approximately 6% higher than that of a single low-density soil layer. Due to the wider soil arch formed, compared to that of a low-density uniform ground, the settlement of the existing tunnel and of the surface settlement trough is larger by 11.5% and 9.6%, respectively. (Refer to Ng et al., 2026 in Part C). When twin tunnelling in two layered soil strata with a dense layer overlies a loose layer, the most critical scenario is when the interface located at the existing tunnel invert. Induced tunnel deformation, bending moment and hoop stress are larger by 45%, 55%, and 34%, than those in a high-density uniform ground, respectively. (Refer to Ng et al., 2026 in Part C). The most critical situation is at the end of new tunnel excavation due to the largest stress reduction induced in the ground during the tunnelling process. The combination of induced bending moment and hoop stress can exceed the design M-N failure envelope of structure in layered soil after a new tunnel excavation. (Refer to Ng et al., 2026 in Part C).

16207621.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16207621.value: The research findings obtained from this project are based on circular-shaped tunnels. However, horseshoe-shaped existing tunnels are common in many urban cities such as London. Any new circular tunnelling will inevitably interact with existing horseshoe-shaped tunnels at different skew angles in multiple soil strata in congested cities. Based on previous research (Ng et al., 2016; 2018), existing horseshoe-shaped tunnels may be more vulnerable to damages due to new tunnel construction nearby. Further research to investigate circular tunnelling intersect with existing horseshoe-shaped tunnel at different skew angles in multiple soil strata. References Ng, C.W.W., Wang, R. & Boonyarak, T. (2016). A comparative study of different responses of circular and horseshoe-shaped tunnels to an advancing tunnel underneath. Géotechnique Letters 6, No.2, 168-175. Ng, C.W.W., Fong, K.Y. & Liu, H.L. (2018). The effects of existing horseshoe-shaped tunnel sizes on circular crossing tunnel interactions: three-dimensional numerical analyses. 16208021.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16208021.value: Gas dynamics equations are obtained at different modeling scales, such as kinetic and hydrodynamics scales. At the kinetic particle mean free path and particle collision time scales, particle transport and collision can be modeled separately, and the Boltzmann equation has been constructed for the particle free streaming and the particle collision processes. Many Boltzmann solvers and the direct simulation Monte Carlo (DSMC) method have been numerically constructed at the kinetic scale. At the hydrodynamic scale, macroscopic Navier-Stokes (NS) equations have been obtained to describe wave phenomena through the accumulation of the movement of a large amount of particles. The hydrodynamic scale is much larger than the kinetic particle mean free path scale. Theoretically, for the construction of gas dynamic equations, there exists continuously varying length and time scale between the hydrodynamic NS and kinetic Boltzmann equations. Practically, finding this modeling scale is difficult. In real-world engineering applications, such as high-speed vehicles in near-space flight, flow around the vehicle can range from highly compressible continuum flow at the leading edge to highly rarefied free molecular flow at the trailing edge. Therefore, multiscale modeling is necessary to accurately simulate such a flow covering different regimes. The past decade has seen the realization of a unified computational fluid dynamics framework covering the rarefied and continuum regimes. This framework is based on the direct modeling of flow physics in discretized space. In the construction of discretized governing equations, mesh size and time step are used as modeling scales. By the variation of cell’s Knudsen number (i.e., particle mean free path over cell size), discretized governing equations can be obtained at continuously varying scales. In this scenario, the Boltzmann and NS equations become the two limiting equations at large and small Knudsen numbers. The unified algorithms have gradually evolved, to include the discrete velocity method (DVM)-based unified gas-kinetic scheme (UGKS), the particle-based unified gas-kinetic particle (UGKP) method, and the wave-particle-based unified gas-kinetic wave-particle (UGKWP) method. In the proposed project, the UGKWP method will be extended to apply to polyatomic gas with translational, rotational, and vibrational modes in both continuum and rarefied flow simulations. 气体动力学方程是在不同尺度上建立起来的，比如介观动理学尺度和宏观运动学尺度。在分子平均自由程和平均碰撞时间的动理学尺度上，直接对粒子传输和碰撞进行建模，构造了玻尔兹曼方程。同时出现了求解玻尔兹曼方程的多种数值算法和直接利用粒子模拟的蒙特卡洛方法。在宏观尺度上，对于由于大量粒子集体运动形成的波运动的描述是宏观的纳维斯托克斯方程。宏观尺度要远远大于介观尺度的粒子平均自由程。理论上从宏观到介观应该是一个连续过渡的尺度变化，有其对应于不同尺度上的方程。但在实际上工作中，在中间找到一个适合的建模尺度十分困难。在实际工程应用中，比如围绕在近空间飞行的高速飞行器，由于在飞行器头部的气体被高度压缩，描述它们的可以是宏观意义上的连续流，即纳维斯托克斯方程。而在尾部的高速膨胀气体形成稀薄区，它们的描述要借助于动理学方程。所以为了同时给出在不同部位对应于不同流域的气体运动，多尺度建模和计算变得必不可少。在过去10年中，同时模拟稀薄和连续流的统一计算流体力学框架得以建立。这一框架是直接在离散空间中对物理运动过程建模实现的。在此空间中的网格大小和时间步长变成了物理上的建模尺度。随着网格努森数（平均自由程比上网格尺度）的变化，建立了对应的统一气体动理学格式。在此统一框架下，玻尔兹曼方程和纳维斯托克斯变成了统一气体动理学格式在很小和很大努森数下的极限方程。统一气体动理学格式也在不断的发展之中，从最初基于离散纵标法的方法，到后来的统一气体动理学粒子法，以及最新的统一气体动理学波粒方法。此研究计划将致力于把统一气体动理学波粒法延伸到多原子气体分子，同时考虑到平动、转动、和振动的非平衡效应对于连续流和稀薄流模拟的影响。

16208021.label: Realisation of objectives
16208021.value: The project focused on constructing a comprehensive modelling framework for multiscale and non-equilibrium gas dynamics, applicable from the continuum to the rarefied regimes, and on applying it to challenging high-speed and reactive flow problems relevant to aerospace and space applications. The publications listed demonstrate an integrated progression—from theoretical model development, algorithmic innovations, and physical model incorporation to high-fidelity validation using experiments and benchmark data. The following summarizes the achievements based on the four stated objectives. A central goal of this project was to incorporate internal molecular energy exchange (rotational and vibrational) and inelastic collision mechanisms into the UGKWP framework to extend its applicability to real gases in non-equilibrium thermodynamic states. Significant work has been completed in this area. The works by Wei, Long & Xu (Computer Physics Communications, 2024) and Wei, Zhu & Xu (JCP, 2024) mark key milestones. We developed adaptive unified gas-kinetic (AUGKS/UGKWP) models for diatomic gases that capture rotational and vibrational nonequilibrium by embedding internal degrees of freedom directly into the particle distribution function. This enables a more accurate description of non-equilibrium energy transfer and dissociation processes in high-enthalpy gas flows. Building upon these advances, the recent paper Wei, Cao & Xu (JCP, 2026) extends the unified gas-kinetic approach to reactive flows with inelastic particle collisions and multi-scale chemical nonequilibrium, coupling the chemical source terms with the wave-particle transport mechanism. This model successfully integrates reaction kinetics into the multi-regime framework without resorting to restrictive domain decomposition or empirical matching conditions. Further broadening the modeling scope, Pu & Xu (JCP, 2025) implemented the UGKWP framework to simulate partially ionized plasma, accounting for ion-neutral collisions and charge exchange processes—an important step toward coupling thermal nonequilibrium and electromagnetic field interactions. Similarly, Yang, Shyy & Xu (JFM, 2024) extended the wave–particle approach to polydisperse gas–solid multiphase flows, demonstrating that the UGKWP structure can unify kinetic descriptions across multiple interacting continua. Taken together, these developments demonstrate that the project has fully achieved its first objective by establishing a versatile UGKWP platform capable of handling internal energy exchange, inelastic collisions, and chemical reactions within a single consistent multi-scale kinetic framework. The second objective concerned the theoretical connection between microscopic kinetic formulations and macroscopic continuum equations—a foundation for validating the multiscale consistency of the UGKWP approach and understanding real-gas effects in its hydrodynamic limit. Through systematic asymptotic expansion, the UGKWP method has been shown to naturally recover the Navier–Stokes (NS) and Fourier’s heat conduction laws in the continuum limit. The study Wei, Cao, Ji & Xu (Advances in Aerodynamics, 2023) provided the first detailed analysis of the adaptive wave-particle decomposition mechanism, in which the relative weights of wave and particle components are controlled by both the cell and gradient-length Knudsen numbers. This adaptive criterion ensures that the method seamlessly transitions from rarefied kinetic transport to the hydrodynamic regime, without numerical stiffness constraints on grid size or time step. More importantly, the paper Guo, Zhu & Xu (Commun. Comput. Phys., 2024) provides a rigorous kinetic formulation of UGKWP, clarifying the wave–particle coupling and showing its natural recovery of Navier–Stokes limit from the Boltzmann equation. The paper Guo, Xu & Zhu (arXiv:2508.07189, 2025) extends UGKWP into a unified framework bridging Boltzmann and Navier–Stokes scales, defining the modeling scale and real gas corrections across regimes. This theoretical advancement directly clarifies how the macroscopic “wave” corresponds to the Chapman–Enskog expansion and how numerical dissipation in particle transport can be minimized in the near-continuum region. These analyses provide a rigorous theoretical foundation connecting the kinetic formulation to continuum physics, achieving Objective 2 by demonstrating accurate macroscopic recovery, preserving the correct transport coefficients, and revealing how real-gas effects emerge naturally within the UGKWP formalism. Validation is a critical aspect of assessing the accuracy and predictive capability of any kinetic solver. The UGKWP methodology has been validated against Direct Simulation Monte Carlo (DSMC) data and available experimental measurements in a broad range of canonical and practical flow problems. The Advances in Aerodynamics (2023) paper systematically compared the adaptive UGKWP method (AUGKWP) with DSMC and Unified Gas-Kinetic Scheme (UGKS) results across test cases such as Sod shock tubes, normal shock structures, hypersonic cylinder flows, re-entry capsule aerodynamics, and nozzle plume expansion. Nearly identical results confirmed the UGKWP’s ability to bridge continuum and rarefied regimes with substantially fewer particles—achieving the same accuracy as DSMC at a fraction of the computational cost. The works Long, Wei & Xu (Phys. Fluids, 2024) and Long, Wei & Xu (AIAAJ, 2024) extended this validation to laminar and transitional high-temperature flows exhibiting strong thermochemical nonequilibrium. Comparisons against DSMC data demonstrated excellent agreement in shock structure, surface pressure, and temperature distributions, confirming that the UGKWP correctly captures finite-rate energy relaxation. The models of Pu & Xu (JCP, 2025) confirmed its applicability to ionized plasma dynamics, ensuring the framework’s reliability for coupled thermal and electromagnetic non-equilibrium systems. These validations confirm that the UGKWP family of methods, developed under this project, is quantitatively consistent with DSMC and experimental benchmarks, achieving the third objective of reliable and efficient non-equilibrium flow prediction. The culmination of this project involved deploying the advanced UGKWP models for three-dimensional high-speed aerodynamic simulations under near-space conditions, where multiple physical regimes co-exist. The AUGKWP simulations reported in Advances in Aerodynamics (2023) included flow around a semi-circular cylinder, an Apollo-type re-entry capsule, and 3D nozzle plume expansions into vacuum, covering Mach numbers between 5 and 15 and Knudsen numbers from 10^(-5) to 10^(-1). These simulations demonstrated the method’s ability to handle large variations in local Knudsen number, capturing continuum flow near vehicle surfaces and rarefied flow in the outer field simultaneously. When compared with the original UGKWP and DSMC, the adaptive version achieved up to 60% reduction in computational cost and substantial memory savings by dynamically suppressing unnecessary particle tracking in equilibrium regions. Parallel computations on the Tianhe-2 supercomputer validated the method’s scalability for large 3D grids (> 300 000 cells). The simulations reproduced shock–boundary-layer interactions, wake structures, and nonequilibrium thermal layers characteristic of re-entry flows. These outcomes confirm the practicality of UGKWP-type solvers for near-space vehicle aerodynamics, meeting the final objective of the project. Through this series of coordinated studies, the project has met and, in many aspects, exceeded its stated objectives. It established a comprehensive kinetic modelling framework that integrates internal energy, inelastic collisions, and chemical/non-equilibrium processes into the UGKWP method. It provided theoretical clarity linking microscale kinetics to continuum macroscopic limits with explicit treatment of real-gas and turbulence effects. It validated the models against DSMC and experiments across a broad range of Knudsen numbers and Mach regimes. It demonstrated applied relevance through full-scale hypersonic and near-space flow simulations with substantial gains in computational efficiency. The body of work produced—spanning over ten high-impact journal papers in JCP, Phys. Fluids, JFM, AIAAJ, and Computers & Fluids—collectively advances the unified gas-kinetic modelling paradigm toward a general simulation tool for multiscale non-equilibrium flows in aerospace science.

16208021.label: Major findings and research outcome
16208021.value: The project on Non-equilibrium Flow Modeling and Simulation has successfully developed a unified and highly efficient computational framework capable of accurately resolving gas flows across all regimes—from continuum Navier–Stokes to rarefied gas dynamics. The core achievement is the creation of the Unified Gas-Kinetic Wave–Particle (UGKWP) method, which integrates macroscopic hydrodynamic waves and microscopic particle transport under the Unified Gas-Kinetic Scheme (UGKS) framework. By employing wave–particle decomposition, the UGKWP method naturally bridges the continuum and rarefied regimes, capturing multiscale transport physics without being restricted by numerical mesh size or time step relative to the molecular mean free path or relaxation time. To address the limitations of the original UGKWP, where the wave–particle weighting relied solely on the cell Knudsen number, an Adaptive UGKWP (AUGKWP) method was developed. The AUGKWP introduces a second Knudsen number based on local flow variable gradients, enabling the model to dynamically identify and capture non-equilibrium phenomena. This adaptive mechanism significantly improves computational efficiency and reduces memory consumption while maintaining accuracy. Consequently, the AUGKWP method achieves an optimal balance between physical fidelity and numerical performance, offering a versatile tool for multiscale flow simulations. Both UGKWP and AUGKWP have been validated through extensive benchmark tests, including the Sod shock tube, normal shock structures, and hypersonic flows around two-dimensional cylinders, three-dimensional spheres, and space vehicles. The methods have consistently demonstrated high accuracy and excellent computational scalability across all flow regimes. Comparisons with the Discrete Velocity Method (DVM) and Direct Simulation Monte Carlo (DSMC) show that UGKWP achieves substantial reductions in computational cost and memory usage while retaining accurate resolution of non-equilibrium effects. Furthermore, the method has been extended to capture energy exchanges among translational, rotational, and vibrational modes using a multi-temperature relaxation model, effectively incorporating real-gas effects for high-speed and high-temperature conditions. Large-scale three-dimensional simulations of space vehicle X-38 and the International Space Station further confirmed the method’s robustness and predictive capability. Throughout the project, more than ten peer-reviewed journal papers have been published, presenting methodological developments, theoretical analyses, and validation studies. These contributions have strengthened the theoretical foundation of multiscale gas dynamics and provided advanced simulation strategies for aerospace applications. In summary, this project has established a unified, adaptive, and physics-based computational platform for non-equilibrium flow simulation, marking a significant advancement in high-speed aerothermodynamics and rarefied gas dynamic modeling.

16208021.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16208021.value: The UGKWP and AUGKWP methods provide a powerful foundation for simulating multiscale, non-equilibrium gas dynamics, yet several opportunities remain for advancement. Future research will focus on extending the framework to chemically reactive and plasma flows, incorporating reaction kinetics, ionization, and radiation transport to capture thermo-chemical non-equilibrium in high-enthalpy environments such as hypersonic flight and spacecraft reentry. Another major direction is the integration of multiphysics coupling, including fluid–structure interaction, particulate flows, and magnetohydrodynamics (MHD), enabling realistic modeling of complex aerospace systems. From a computational perspective, the next step involves implementing high-performance parallel algorithms and GPU acceleration to achieve large-scale three-dimensional simulations with improved efficiency and scalability. In addition, introducing machine learning into the UGKWP framework will allow data-driven adaptation of model parameters, enhancing accuracy and convergence for diverse flow conditions. The proposed course of action includes: (1) extending the theoretical model to reactive and plasma regimes; (2) developing multiphysics coupling capabilities; (3) optimizing parallelization and GPU performance; and (4) implementing AI-assisted model adaptation. These efforts will evolve UGKWP into a comprehensive, intelligent, and scalable multiscale simulation platform for next-generation aerospace and high-speed flow research.

16208021.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16208021.value: This research project focuses on understanding and accurately predicting how gases behave when objects move through the air or space at very high speeds—such as spacecraft reentering Earth’s atmosphere or vehicles flying in hypersonic conditions. In these extreme situations, air no longer behaves like a smooth fluid; instead, it becomes a mixture of waves and fast-moving particles that collide and exchange energy in complex, non equilibrium ways. To study these phenomena, the project developed a new computer modeling approach called the Unified Gas-Kinetic Wave–Particle (UGKWP) method. Unlike traditional methods that work only for specific conditions, this new model can describe all types of gas flows—from smooth air motion to extremely rarefied conditions found in space—within one unified framework. It is also much more efficient and accurate, saving both computing time and memory. This research is valuable because it provides scientists and engineers with a powerful tool to design safer and more efficient spacecraft and high speed vehicles, predict heating and drag more precisely, and better understand gas behavior in extreme conditions. The method’s success strengthens the foundation for future aerospace technology and next generation flight systems.

16208921.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16208921.value: The past decade has witnessed a phenomenal development of wireless communications with profound social and economic impacts. The growth of wireless networks will continue and it is expected that by 2030 the overall mobile data traffic will reach an astonishing 60 zettabytes per year. This extraordinary growth coupled with many emerging data-intensive applications such as the Internet of Everything, cyber-physical systems, sustainable cities, and e-health, will need to leverage the power of machine learning (ML) and big data analytics. They will also continue to drive the demand for revolutionary technological advancements to meet more stringent performance requirements. In particular, ML approaches are needed that can take advantage of the massive amount data in future wireless networks where connected intelligence will be the dominant feature. Such approaches will also need to meet the requirements of the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), which restricts Internet companies to transmit or collect data from users directly. In addition, unlike traditional ML applications where data processing is centralized in the cloud, the raw data will be distributed across a massive number of devices. Large-scale distributed ML is therefore required for future mobile applications. Federated learning is a revolutionary collaborative ML paradigm, which enables deep learning model training over a large volume of decentralized data residing in mobile devices without accessing clients’ private data. It also results in ultra-low latency communications, a fundamental requirement for 5th generation (5G) and beyond wireless networks. In this proposed study, we endeavour to address some of the fundamental issues that need to be resolved before federated learning can be properly implemented in practice. Our focus will be on federated edge learning (FEL) which combines the emerging field of mobile edge computing and distributed learning. Of particular interest is the design of communication-efficient federated learning methods to strengthen data privacy and security while enabling low-latency global model aggregation for federated edge learning. The development of several resource allocation strategies for single-server wireless systems, hierarchical systems, and decentralized systems will also be a key objective. Specific challenges include non-identical data distribution, large model parameters, and heterogeneous computing and communication environments. Solutions require a delicate trade-off between computing and communications as well as the joint design of distributed learning and wireless networking techniques for the design of distributed paradigms for computing, communications, and learning under various constraints such as the stringent computation, bandwidth, storage, power, and privacy constraints of individual devices. 過去十年見證了無線通信系統的驚人發展及其在社會經濟方面帶來的深遠影響。無線網絡將繼續發展，預計到 2030 年，整體移動數據流量將達到驚人的每年 60 澤字節。這種非同尋常的數據增長加上許多新興的數據密集型應用，如萬物互聯、網絡物理系統、可持續城市和電子健康，需要機器學習算法和大數據分析的支持。為了滿足更嚴格的應用性能要求，這些數據和應用還將繼續推動對革命性的技術進步的需求。我們尤其需要機器學習方法來有效利用未來無線網絡中的海量數據，其中互聯智能將成為未來無線網絡的主要特征。此類機器學習方法還需要滿足通用數據保護條例 (GDPR) 的要求，該條例限制互聯網公司直接傳輸或收集用戶的數據。此外，與數據處理集中在雲端的傳統機器學習應用不同，在未來無線網絡中，原始數據將分布在大量本地設備上。因此，未來的移動應用需要大規模分布式機器學習的支持。 聯邦學習是一種革命性的協作分布式機器學習範式。它可以在不訪問客戶私人數據的情況下，對駐留在移動設備中的大量分布式數據進行深度學習的模型訓練。它還可以帶來超低延遲通信，以滿足第5 代 (5G) 及以後無線網絡的基本要求。在這項擬議的研究中，我們將解決聯邦學習在被部署之前需要解決的一些基本問題。我們的重點將放在聯邦邊緣學習上。它結合了移動邊緣計算和分布式學習這兩個新興領域。我們感興趣的是如何設計通信高效的聯邦學習算法，在加強數據隱私和安全性的同時為聯邦邊緣學習實現低延遲全局模型聚合。為單服務器無線系統、分層系統和分布式系統開發資源分配策略也將是我們的一個關鍵目標。具體的研究挑戰包括不同的本地數據分布、大規模深度學習模型參數以及不平均的計算資源和通信環境。解決方案需要在有限的計算、帶寬、存儲、單個設備的功率和隱私限制的限制下，聯合設計分布式學習和無線網絡技術，以在計算量和通信量之間達到微妙的平衡。

16209421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16209421.value: The unique topography and climate of the Tibetan Plateau make it a hot spot of mega geohazards, typically in the form of a large icy landslide-debris flow-landslide dam hazard chain. During the hazard propagation, the intact ice core is fragmented and mix with the entrained soil along the travel path, leading to a violent ice-soil mixture flow. Such a flow can block a river and form a large landslide dam. The landslide lake water will then cause the broken ice-soil mixture to dissolve, leading to a looser and unstable microstructure and eventually accelerated breaching of the dam. How the shear strength, deformation, hydraulic conductivity and erodibility of the ice-soil mixture deteriorate during dissolution is an open question. Numerous ice-soil-mixture landslide dams have formed in the past on the Tibetan Plateau, such as the 2000 Yigong landslide dam and the 2018 Gyalha landslide dam, and resulted in disastrous dam-breaching consequences. Climate change further increases the risk of ice-soil-mixture landslide dams, demanding a comprehensive understanding of the behaviour of ice-soil mixtures subject to dissolution. The primary objective of this research project is to investigate the deformation, shear strength and seepage erosion behaviour of ice-soil mixtures when a landslide at high altitude occurs and the broken ice-soil mixtures form a landslide dam and dissolve in the landslide lake water. To achieve this project goal, four closely related research tasks will be carried out. First, a stress- and temperature-controlled triaxial erosion apparatus will be developed for investigating the mechanical behaviour of ice-soil mixtures. Second, the deformation and shear strength characteristics of ice-soil mixtures during dissolution will be investigated using the developed triaxial erosion apparatus at various control conditions. Third, seepage erosion tests on dissolved ice-soil mixtures will be performed under both low and high hydraulic gradients. Forth, the performance of ice-soil-mixture landslide dams subjected to temperature change will be examined through advanced centrifuge model tests. A novel feature of this project is to understand the mechanical behaviour of ice-soil mixtures experiencing phase transformation due to dissolution at both the element level on the new temperature-controlled triaxial erosion apparatus and the full-scale level in two advanced geotechnical centrifuges. In addition to advancing soil mechanics and landslide science, this research project can provide a solid basis to develop engineering risk mitigation strategies for ice-soil-mixture landslide dams and to reduce the risks of the on-going Sichuan-Tibet high-speed railway and many other challenging projects on high-altitude mountain regions. 青藏高原獨特的地形和氣候使其成為地質災害頻發的熱點。這些災害常以大型冰磧滑坡-泥石流-堰塞壩災害鏈的形式出現。在災害傳播過程中，完整的冰芯逐漸解體破碎並沿途與夾帶的土壤混合，導致劇烈的冰土混合物流動，阻塞河道並形成大型堰塞湖。湖水會導致冰土混合物溶解，微觀結構更鬆散和不穩定，最終加速大壩潰決。冰土混合物的剪切強度、變形、滲透係數和沖蝕性在溶解過程中如何變化是一個懸而未決的理論問題。青藏高原最近發生了多次冰土混合物堰塞堵江事件，如2000年的易貢堰塞體、2018年的加拉堰塞體等，均造成了災難性的潰壩後果。氣候變化進一步增加了冰土混合物堰塞湖的風險，更有必要全面瞭解冰土混合物在溶解過程中的力學行為。 該研究專案的主要目的是研究高海拔滑坡形成堰塞湖後，冰土混合物在溶解過程中的變形、剪切強度和滲透侵蝕行為。 為實現該研究目標，本專案將開展四項密切相關的研究任務。 首先，開發一種基於應力和溫度控制的三軸滲透侵蝕實驗裝置，用於研究冰土混合物的力學行為。 其次，使用所開發的裝置在各種控制條件下研究溶蝕過程中冰土混合物的變形和剪切強度特性。 第三，在低水力梯度和高水力梯度下對溶解後的冰土混合物進行滲透侵蝕試驗。 第四，通過先進的離心模型試驗來檢驗冰土混合物滑坡壩在環境溫度增加情況下的性能。 該研究項目的一個創新點是同時基於溫控三軸侵蝕裝置上的單元試驗尺度和岩土離心機中的足尺試驗尺度研究冰土混合物溶解過程中的相變力學行為。除了推進土力學和滑坡科學的發展，該研究專案還可以為制定冰土混合物堰塞湖的減災策略提供依據，有助於降低正在興建的川藏鐵路和高海拔山區的許多其他具有挑戰性的重大工程風險。

16209421.label: Realisation of objectives
16209421.value: (1) Development of a stress- and temperature-controlled triaxial erosion apparatus for investigating the mechanical behaviour of ice-soil mixtures (Output #1, #2) The new apparatus was modified based on a stress-controlled triaxial apparatus. The experimental system consists of two components: a triaxial system with temperature control and a water collection system. To realize uniform temperature control, a spiral tube was connected to a thermostat and installed in the triaxial chamber. The spiral tube was arranged in such a way that the whole specimen can be imaged throughout the test for deformation analysis. During the tests, cooling anti-freezing fluid (glycol) was circulated through the spiral tube to adjust the temperature surrounding the sample. Glycol, instead of water, was also used as chamber fluid so that the system temperature can be maintained below 0 ◦C. Three thermocouples were attached to the top, middle, and bottom of the sample to monitor the change of temperature with time. A detachable container was attached to the bottom of the sample to collect and measure any melted ice that exited the soil matrix. (2) Deformation and shear strength of ice-soil mixtures during dissolution (Outputs #1, #2, #3) Triaxial compression tests have been carried out to investigate the deformation and shear strength of ice-soil mixtures during dissolution with various initial ice content (0%, 10%, 20%, 30%, 40%). When subjected to ice dissolution, the local strains along the specimen showed significant variations in both radial and axial directions, especially in specimens with higher initial ice contents. The stress condition turned to have significant influence on ice-dissolution-induced deformations. When the applied confining pressure is isotropic or compressive, the increase in initial ice content resulted in larger compressive radial and axial deformations. However, the extensive stress state deformed the specimen compressively in radial direction but extensively in axial direction. With the same initial ice content, the compressive stress state resulted in larger axial strain but smaller radial strain while the extensive stress state caused an opposite effect. Besides, the influence of stress conditions became more remarkable in ice-soil mixtures with higher initial ice content. Because the process of ice dissolution altered the particle arrangement and microstructure of the soil matrix, the stress-strain behavior of ice-soil mixture subjected to ice dissolution is expected to differ from that of bare soil. Compared with the benchmark stress-strain curve of bare soil, a clear reduction in drained shear strength was noted in all test ice-soil mixtures subject to ice dissolution under both triaxial compression and triaxial extension. With more ice content melting, the specimen became more shearing contractive, and its critical stress tended to decrease. The applied stress state during ice dissolution also had remarkable effect on the post-dissolution stress-strain behavior of ice-soil mixtures. The post-dissolution shear strength of the ice-soil mixtures that dissolved under non-isotropic stress states appeared to be slightly higher than those under isotropic stress states, and the shearing process was accompanied by smaller volumetric change. (3) Understand the internal erosion behavior of dissolved ice-soil mixtures (Output #2) Based on a triaxial internal erosion apparatus, a systematic experimental study was conducted to investigate the internal erosion behavior of ice-soil mixtures under controlled melting conditions. Three soil samples with distinct gradation characteristics (designated as Groups A, B, and C) were selected and classified according to their internal stability into unstable, transitional, and stable types. The specimens were prepared at predetermined ice contents, compacted, and subjected to a controlled temperature increase to induce ice melting. Internal erosion tests were subsequently performed under incrementally elevated hydraulic gradients to assess fine particle migration and associated structural alterations during seepage. To date, a comprehensive series of tests has been completed for Group B (transitional) and Group C (stable) soils at initial ice contents of 0% and 30%. The results demonstrate that specimens containing ice experience a marked decline in internal stability following melting—a phenomenon particularly evident in Group B soils, which initially exhibited lower stability. Furthermore, both radial and axial deformations resulting from the melting process were substantially more significant than those induced by subsequent seepage. The application of downward seepage forces only moderately amplified axial deformation and exerted a comparatively limited influence on overall specimen deformation. (4) Perform centrifuge tests of ice-soil-mixture landslide dams subject to temperature changes (Output #5) The stability of ice-soil mixture landslide dams under varying temperature conditions was investigated. A centrifuge testing scheme has been designed, and preliminary verification tests have been successfully conducted. The model dam, measuring 100 cm in length and 32 cm in height, was compacted to an initial void ratio of 0.55. Six layers of thermocouple sensors were embedded inside the model to monitor the internal temperature evolution during ice melting. Drainage holes were installed at the corners of the model container to replicate the drainage conditions typical of natural barrier dams. A high-speed camera system was used to continuously capture the dynamic morphological responses of the dam under temperature changes. Preliminary 1g tests indicate that ice melting considerably compromises dam stability, inducing significant global and local deformations, especially in near-surface regions. Analysis of image-derived displacement fields further elucidated the spatial distribution and evolutionary characteristics of deformation throughout the melting process, offering critical insights for the upcoming centrifuge tests.
