16213321.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16213321.value: 社會對土木工程建設的需求是十分龐大並且在持續增長。 與此同時，對可持續建築材料及其實踐的需求也在增長。 作為建築材料，竹子具有許多優勢，而近期的發展亦展示其在建造永久性建設的價值。 作為一種快速生長的植物，竹子價格低廉，於世界各地都十分常見，並且碳足跡低。 此外，個別竹子品種的機械性能媲美在工業革命後研發的建築材料。 竹桿作為結構元件已有數個世紀的歷史，據估計，過去約有10億人曾居住在竹屋中。 然而，多數竹結構設計僅以經驗爲基礎。 竹桿的結構設計受礙於個別竹桿之間、以及不同品種的物理特性及材質的高方差，難以標準化。此外，傳統的結構工程的設計多基於工業化材料（如混凝土和鋼材），因此需要竹結構的設計規範。當中以其可靠的結構性能，特別是構件之間的連接方法尤其重要。 本項目的首要目標是通過原創的實驗、分析和數值研究，以擴大竹子在結構工程上的應用。本研究側重於兩端以螺栓固定於鋼連接件上的多竹桿結構構件。多桿的設計可以利用更多的竹種並增加結構贅餘；而不同結構構件之間的鋼連接則可消除設計上的不確定性。第一個具體目標是徹底了解擬議的結構構件的力學表現。其重點是通過實驗及進階數據模擬來研究螺栓嵌入竹子的現象。此外，這項研究旨在為原創設計方法奠定基礎，實現可靠和可預測的機械性能，以及可控的結構失效模式。為此，本研究提出了一套原創的方法處理竹桿在幾何和機械特性方面的自然差異。 本研究為竹結構和竹工程提供關鍵進展。 通過利用可再生和綠色資源來促進經濟和環保的建築方案。 以此為前提，本項研究回應了全球對可持續發展和建設的需求。 竹產業和竹文化有助於對抗森林砍伐，促進當地經濟發展，並為新型環保商業模式提供機會。

16213321.label: Realisation of objectives
16213321.value: We have made significant progress towards all three research objectives since the interim report. The first task aimed at the experimental characterization of bamboo material properties. To satisfy this goal, first, we examined two methods for managing the natural variability in geometry and material properties of bamboo: (a) the use of multiple bamboo culms and (b) grading. We performed single-culm compressive strength tests and simulated the response of multi-culm members using Monte Carlo simulations. Findings revealed decrease in the variability of properties follows an inverse square root function of the number of culms in multi-culm. Furthermore, results showed that grading alters the distribution and reduces the variability of only those properties that are well correlated with the indicating property. Overall, the two considered methods are effective in managing the natural variability of bamboo culms “see “Characterizing Reduction of Variability in Bamboo Axial Members Through Use of Multiple Culms and Grading” by Pradhan et al., ACMSM26 conference”. Although bamboo culms have different compression and tension moduli (bimodulus behavior), previous studies mainly focused on a single modulus approach for the failure of bamboo culms under flexure. We derived analytically the longitudinal compression failure moment of a bamboo culm, investigating both single and bimodulus bending. The findings revealed that the bimodulus approach is more critical than the single-modulus approach “see “The Effect of Single and Bimodulus Material Behavior on Longitudinal Compression Failure of Bamboo Culms Under Flexure” by Khodabakhshi et al., ACMSM26 conference”. The second objective was related to numerical simulation of the mechanical behaviour of the proposed members with emphasis on embedment. Embedment properties are of paramount importance for the behavior of bolted bamboo connections. However, full-culm bamboo dowel-bearing test experimental data, and pertinent analytical expressions that predict embedment properties, are currently scarce. In this regard, we conducted an extensive experimental program on Kao Jue and Moso bamboo, examining three different bolt diameters (6 mm, 8 mm, and 10 mm) “see “Prediction of bamboo culm embedment properties parallel to grain via dimensional analysis” by Theodora Mouka and Elias G. Dimitrakopoulos, CBM journal”. Also, the second task requires the foundation modelling approach to macroscopically capture the embedment phenomena in bolted bamboo connections. In this regard, we developed a finite element model of a two-culm axial member with steel bolted connections. The numerical model of the culm consists of two parts, the culm itself and the foundation zone. The aim of the numerical simulation was to provide a comprehensive understanding of the analytical elastic stiffness of the examined axial members. The results showed the precision of the developed numerical model for calculating the elastic stiffness of the axial members “see “Stiffness characterization of bolted multi-culm bamboo members” by Khodabakhshi et al., JBE journal”. Furthermore, we proposed a rational procedure for the determination of embedment zone size and material properties using numerical simulation. Comparison between experimental and numerical model results verify the applicability of the proposed approach for the prediction of experimental strength and stiffness of dowel-bearing tests and bamboo bolted connections “see “MODELING EMBEDMENT IN BAMBOO CULMS AND IN FULLCULM BAMBOO BOLTED CONNECTIONS” by Mouka et al., NOCMAT2022 conference”. Moreover, we described analytically the mechanical and structural behaviour of bamboo culms subjected to bending, and predicted the failure load and stiffness loss after the linear-elastic stage. We concluded that, for the different bamboo species examined, critical failure mechanisms are tension perpendicular to the fibres and longitudinal compression. Which of the two mechanisms occurs first depends on the case-specific material properties and culm radius-to-thickness ratio. Comparing the analytical results with pertinent experimental data, the proposed equations are sufficiently accurate in their prediction of failure load and stiffness loss “see “ANALYTICAL PREDICTION OF FAILURE MECHANISM AND FAILURE MOMENT IN FULL-CULM BAMBOO BENDING TESTS, NOCMAT2022 conference” by Mouka et al.” and also “see “Insight into the behaviour of bamboo culms subjected to bending” by Mouka et al., RSI journal”. After that, we investigated analytically the effect of a longitudinal crack on the stiffness of an originally intact bamboo culm in flexure. We developed analytical expressions that describe stiffness loss in bending test and verified them with available experimental results and numerical simulations. Our results showed that main cause of the stiffness loss is torsion-induced deflections, with secondary cause being shear deformations. The results have important implications for bamboo structure design and testing standards, indicating that the manner in which loads are transferred on beams affects the apparent beam stiffness when a crack appears “see “Effect of a longitudinal crack on the flexural performance of bamboo culms” by Mouka et al., Acta Mech. Journal”. The third task was a new design paradigm along the principles of capacity-based design. In this regard, we presented a first attempt toward the rational design of bamboo multi-culm axial members with dowel-type connections. Specifically, we proposed a novel analytical model to estimate the elastic stiffness of bolted multi-culm bamboo axial members and provide guidance for their design. The comparison between the proposed analytical model and existing experimental studies highlighted the model’s ability to estimate bamboo bolted connection stiffness accurately “see “Stiffness characterization of bolted multi-culm bamboo members” by Khodabakhshi et al., JBE Journal”. After that, we investigated the influence of geometric parameters of bamboo culms, such as taper and straightness, on the elastic stiffness of bolted multi-culm bamboo members. The findings contribute to the design of bamboo structures, highlighting the effect of the unique geometric properties of bamboo culm on their stiffness parameter “see “Effects of bamboo culm taper and straightness on the stiffness of bolted multi-culm bamboo structures” by Nahid Khodabakhshi and Elias G. Dimitrakopoulos, ICBBM2025 conference”. Moreover, we investigated the effect of shear-circumferential tension interaction and the bimodulus behavior of bamboo on the failure of bamboo culms in bending. We validated the analytical approaches via conducting four-point bending tests. Findings highlight the importance of mixed-mode failure and of the bimodulus behavior of bamboo. Furthermore, the occurring strength values constitute a close approximation to the bending strength obtained according to ISO 22157:2019, enabling accurate predictions based solely on culm geometric parameters “see “Analytical and experimental investigations on failure of bamboo culms in bending: effects of shear-tension interaction and bimodulus material behavior” by Khodabakhshi et al., under review”.

16213321.label: Major findings and research outcome
16213321.value: Objective 1: Experimental characterization of bamboo material properties • Variability management: Two methods were examined: using multiple bamboo culms and grading. Findings revealed decrease in the coefficient of variability of capacity, stiffness, compressive strength, and modulus of elasticity properties follows an inverse square root function of the number of culms in multi-culm. Furthermore, grading based on external diameter or stiffness reduced variability in properties correlated with the grading indicator. • Failure mechanisms in bending: Analytical investigation revealed that buckling due to longitudinal compression is a common failure mechanism. The bimodulus approach (considering different compression and tension moduli) was found to be more critical than the single-modulus approach. Objective 2: Numerical simulation of mechanical behavior • Embedment properties: Extensive experimental data on Kao Jue and Moso bamboo with different bolt diameters were collected. A finite element model was developed to simulate the embedment phenomena in bolted bamboo connections, showing precision in calculating elastic stiffness. • Failure mechanisms in bending: Analytical predictions of failure mechanisms (Brazier instability, longitudinal tension/compression, tension perpendicular to fibers, and shear parallel to fibers) were validated with experimental data. Critical failure mechanisms depend on material properties and culm geometry. • Effect of longitudinal cracks: Analytical expressions for stiffness loss due to longitudinal cracks were developed and verified. Torsion-induced deflections were identified as the main cause of stiffness loss, with friction at load points mitigating these effects. Objective 3: New design paradigm for bamboo structures • Stiffness calculation of the bolted multi-culm bamboo axial members: A novel analytical model for estimating the elastic stiffness of bolted multi-culm bamboo axial members was proposed. The model accurately estimated stiffness compared to experimental studies. • Geometric parameters: The influence of taper and straightness on the stiffness of bolted multi-culm bamboo members was examined, highlighting their importance in design. • Failure mechanisms in bending: Mixed-mode failure and bimodulus behavior were investigated, showing their significance in determining the failure moment of bamboo culms. The findings align closely with ISO 22157:2019 bending strength values, effectively eliminating the need for bending tests and enabling accurate predictions based solely on culm geometric parameters. These findings contribute to a more rational and engineered design of bamboo structures, addressing variability, failure mechanisms, and embedment properties.

16213321.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16213321.value: The main areas for future works and expected results are listed below: 1- To further investigate bamboo material properties and extend its usage as a construction material, we are focusing on the experimental characterization of multi-culm bamboo in bending. We aim to explore different connection configurations and improve the bearing capacity of the combined bamboo culms. 2- We are developing an analytical approach to predict the failure pattern of bamboo culms under flexure using mixed mode criteria. We expect that mixed-mode failure will be more critical than existing single-mode criteria. 3- The study on the numerical simulation of the bamboo member with emphasis on embedment facilitates the development of a new methodology that will predict the stiffness (in addition to the already estimated yield capacity) of the proposed bamboo-steel connections. This is critical towards the rational design of engineered bamboo structures.

16213321.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16213321.value: This research project focuses on improving the use of bamboo in construction. Bamboo is a strong and sustainable material, but its natural variability makes it challenging to use consistently. We explored ways to manage this variability and helped to ensure more reliable performance. We also developed methods to prevent bamboo from splitting when connected to steel, making it more durable. We studied how bamboo fails under bending, finding that considering bamboo's unique properties leads to better predictions of its behavior. Additionally, we created computer models to simulate how bamboo behaves when bolted together, helping to predict its strength and stiffness accurately. This is crucial for designing safe and efficient bamboo structures. Overall, the project provides valuable insights and tools for engineers, promoting the use of bamboo as a sustainable alternative in construction. This can lead to more eco-friendly buildings and structures, benefiting both the environment and society.

16213521.label: Project Objectives
16213521.value: Develop a frequent subgraph mining (pattern extraction) automation flow, based on semi-supervised graph learning with very few samples. The flow is capable to obtain the common patterns in extremely large EDA graphs, which can be used to guide an efficient synthesis at different steps. Analyze the Data Flow Graph (DFG) generated through VivadoHLS from the high-level source code and apply pattern extraction in HLS as a case study, to speed up the operation scheduling and guide resource reuse during hardware resource binding. Perform pattern extraction on the post-synthesis gate-level netlist, and utilize the pattern extraction information in physical synthesis as a case study, to speed up the convergence of placement optimization. To better incorporate the pattern extraction information, we will also develop a practical FPGA analytic placer to consider comprehensive applications in the real-world for general evaluation. The placer can interface with Vivado to complete the implementation. Perform the comprehensive evaluation of compilation runtime and synthesis quality improvement of the HLS flow and placer based on real-world benchmarks to prove the effectiveness of the proposed automatic pattern extraction method.

16213521.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16213521.value: Nowadays, the increasing density and scale of designs on Field-Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs) make high-efficiency synthesis flow for FPGA become a very challenging problem. According to previous researches and explorations, the regularity information or structure patterns existed in the FPGA designs can guide the synthesis at various steps to achieve better results with a shorter runtime. However, the explicit information of the hierarchy and regularity is usually eliminated due to a series of complicated permutation, optimization, and processing during synthesis steps. For example, in High-Level Synthesis (HLS), where the designs described in a high-level language are compiled into RTL designs, loops might be unrolled and functions might be inlined. In lower-level logic synthesis, where physical netlists are generated according to RTL designs, some RTL elements might be removed or merged. Previous solutions have tried to extract patterns for the efficiency improvement of synthesis, however, their pattern extractions were limited to only small and simple graphs due to their runtime overhead and flexibility, or they have to compromise to large problem size by extracting only patterns with known templates. Fortunately, the recent advance of graph learning-based method provides potentials to overcome these constraints, because most of the Electronic Design Automation (EDA) problems intrinsically target graph processing. Especially, Graph Convolutional Network (GCN) can nicely obtain and utilize embedding vectors to represent the characteristics of the nodes and edges in the graphs, such as their interconnection and attributes. To tackle the existing limitations and make general patterns in the design benefit the synthesis flow, we will propose a pattern extraction automation flow, based on the embedding information from the semi-supervised GCN, with very few training samples (around 1% or less of the total number of nodes in the graph). The pattern mining will be guided by the embedding information, so it can efficiently extract complicated patterns from the large EDA design graphs with 100000+ nodes. To concretely unveil the advantages of our proposed approach, we will conduct case studies for synthesis at different levels. First, we will apply the pattern information in our developed HLS framework to reuse hardware resources and accelerate the scheduling. Second, we will implement a practical analytic FPGA placer, targeting real-world applications considering tens of types of elements and various macros. The placement quality and convergence speed of the placer is expected to be improved significantly with the pattern information. 如今，現場可編程門陣列 (FPGA) 設計的密度和規模不斷增加，使得高效邏輯綜合和物理綜合成為一個非常具有挑戰性的問題。根據以往的研究和探索，FPGA設計中存在的規律性信息或結構模式可以指導各個步驟的綜合，以更短的運行時間獲得更好的結果。然而，由於在綜合步驟中進行了一系列複雜的排列、優化和處理，通常會消除層次結構和規律性的顯式信息。例如，在高級綜合 (HLS) 中，用高級語言描述的設計被編譯成 RTL 設計，循環可能被展開，函數可能被內聯。在較低級別的邏輯綜合中，根據 RTL 設計生成物理電路，一些 RTL 元素可能會被移除或合併。 以前的解決方案試圖提取模式以提高綜合效率，但由於它們的運行時開銷和靈活性，它們僅限於小而簡單的圖形的模式提取，或者通過僅提取具有已知模板的簡單模式而不適合於大問題規模。幸運的是，圖學習的最新進展提供了克服這些限制的潛力，因為大多數 EDA 問題本質上都針對圖和圖學習方法。尤其是圖卷積網絡 (GCN)可以很好地獲得和利用嵌入向量來表示圖中的節點和邊，例如它們的互連和屬性。為了解決現有的限制並使設計中的通用模式有利於綜合流程，我們將提出一種模式提取自動化流程，基於來自半監督 GCN 的嵌入信息，只需要很少的訓練樣本（大約 1% 或更少圖中節點的總數）。模式挖掘將以嵌入信息為指導，因此可以從具有 100000 多個節點的大型 EDA 設計圖中有效地提取複雜的模式。 為了具體展示我們提出的方法的優勢，作為不同層次綜合的案例研究，我們將應用我們開發的 HLS 框架中的模式信息來重用硬件資源和加速調度，並實現一個實用的分析 型FPGA 佈线工具。這個佈局工具可以針對大規模的實際應用，可以包含數十種的不同模塊和宏，佈局質量和收斂速度將隨模式信息的應用而得到顯著提高。

16213521.label: Realisation of objectives
16213521.value: We have conducted research activities to achieve all the project objectives. At the first step, we have performed the pattern recognition to identify the frequently used subgraphs which can be used in high-level module or low-level gate netlist. An extraction tool is developed, which includes our proposed pattern combination algorithm which can iteratively find a set of gate-level patterns from numerous candidates as the extension part of the given initial design. A related paper “AutoCellLibX: Automated Standard Cell Library Extension Based on Pattern Mining” has been uploaded to Arkiv to meet the first objective. The tool is released in the github, https://github.com/zslwyuan/AutoCellLibX/releases. Based on the pattern extraction, the subgraphs can be given priority for batter placement or guide the high-level synthesis procedure. A task partition tool between CPU and FPGA has been developed considering the pattern, where the heavy computational tasks will be placed on FPGA accelerator and implemented with HLS. When considering the partition, we also developed the performance modeling for the modern FPGA system-on-chip (FPSoC) platforms considering various interfaces between CPU and FPGA. Moreover, targeting the full coherency architecture (FCA), an automated memory management framework is proposed to select the optimal memory architecture based on the analysis of cache hit ratio and execution information, and case studies prove the effectiveness of the framework. The paper is published in the journal of “IEEE TRANSACTIONS ON VERY LARGE SCALE INTEGRATION (VLSI) SYSTEMS”. Then, a timing driven placer for heterogeneous FPGA has been developed to further improve the accelerator performance. This open-source FPGA placer supports mixed-size placement of heterogeneous resources and achieves commercial tool comparable performance. These research output satisfied the objectives of 2 and 3. Real applications, such as embedded system benchmarks and machine learning algorithms are used to evaluate the efficiency of our developed tool chains. The placer related paper “AMF-Placer 2.0: Open Source Timing-driven Analytical Mixed-size Placer for Largescale Heterogeneous FPGA” has been published in the journal of “IEEE Transactions on Computer-Aided Design of Integrated Circuits and Systems”.

16213521.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16213521.value: With the system scale increase, it raises challenges for FPGA based design from high-level design to lower-level implementation. If we can extract the sub-module which contains the closely related component at high level and treat submodules as an entity during the design and implementation, it will significantly reduce the complexity and enhance the efficiency. This project implements such a flow which can extract patterns of the design as submodules, and realize the design using the submodules with high efficiency and high performance. It will significantly help with maintaining a good scalability for FPGA based system design.

16213621.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16213621.value: 一种针对分布式DNN训练的网络通信优化方法

16213621.label: Project Objectives
16213621.value: Problem Exploration: We will explore and demonstrate the problem of network communication overhead in distributed DNN training. We use testbed to measure the tail flow competition time (FCT) which reflects the communication overhead of DNN training. Our preliminary experiment shows that simply reducing traffic volume via gradient compression cannot completely eliminate the long tail latency. Next, we will further exploit the problem under larger-scale topologies with more DNN models and real-world datasets. The DLCP Design: To solve the communication inefficiency during DNN training, we will propose DLCP, a novel solution that fully exploits domain-specific properties of deep learning as mentioned above. Under these properties, DLCP works high-levelly as follows. For transmission, data are first spread onto multi-path in the network on a per-packet basis to minimize hotpots without out-of-order concern. Then, if congestion happens, the DLCP switch will perform priority queueing and selective dropping based on layers and magnitudes of gradients to optimize training efficiency. Finally, a bounded loss tolerant data transmission protocol is established between end-points to avoid long tail latencies caused by retransmission timeouts. In our preliminary study, the small-scale testbed experiment demonstrates that DLCP achieves up to 84.3% additional training speedup over the best existing solutions. Next, we will further investigate the design of DLCP and evaluate its performance via larger-scale testbed experiments. System Implementation: We will build a prototype of DLCP using Mellanox LibVMA and commodity switches and integrate it to popular machine learning frameworks like Tensorflow, Pytorch and MXNet. We envision three main tasks in the implementation: 1) how to integrate DLCP with widely used machine learning frameworks as mentioned; 2) how to support priority queueing and selective dropping at the same time in commodity switches; and 3) how to transmit data and control signals. We will handle these tasks, fully implement DLCP, and evaluate it using both testbed experiments and simulations. Finally, we will release the implementation code online by the end of the project.

16213621.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16213621.value: 分布式DNN训练存在大量的通信开销，如何优化其通信是当前的研究热点。现有的解决方案，如梯度压缩/量化、计算/通信重叠、和张量调度都是粗粒度的，且未深入到网络传输层，因此难以支持高效的分布式训练，当网络处于压力时，现有方法的性能会大幅度下降。 在本项目中，我们将介绍一种全新的解决方案: DLCP (Deep Learning Communication Protocol)，DLCP挖掘并利用了深度学习的特性，并以细粒度的方式优化通信开销。其核心创新如下：第一，深度学习训练容忍一定的梯度损失，利用此特性，DLCP可以忽略一些丢包从而大幅度减少尾流完成时间 (Tail FCT)，这是无法通过梯度压缩/量化来完全解决的。第二，深度学习中不同位置和大小的梯度对收敛有着不同程度的影响，对于大部分模型，更靠后层和更大的梯度对模型收敛影响更大。利用该特性，DLCP根据梯度的层次和大小，执行细粒度（包级别）的优先级调度和选择性丢包，在进一步加快训练速度的同时保护了收敛精度。第三，深度学习中每个梯度是相对独立且顺序无关的，利用这点，DLCP无须考虑乱序问题，因此可采用逐包负载均衡。我们将确保DLCP在不同的通信模式（如Parameter Server 模式和Allreduce 模式）下均能获得性能提升，并会将其集成到多种常用的深度学习训练框架中 (如TensorFlow、MXNet和PyTorch)。初步实验结果表明DLCP具有很好的潜力: 其在现有最佳解决方案的基础上能够提供最高达84.3%的额外加速。 本项目包括三个部分： 1. 问题探究：我们将首先分析分布式深度学习训练中的网络通信开销问题。我们使用真实测试平台来测量通信过程中的尾流完成时间。初步实验结果表明，简单地利用梯度压缩来减少通信量并不能完全消除长尾部延迟。接下来，我们将在更大规模的测试床下，使用更多的深度学习模型和数据集来进一步探究这个问题。 2. DLCP设计：为了解决深度学习训练中的低效率通信问题，我们将提出新的解决方案：DLCP，其工作流程如下：1）DLCP首先将数据分散到网络中的多条路径中，以减少网络热点的产生，这一步骤无须担心乱序问题。2）当拥塞发生时，DLCP交换机将根据层数和梯度的大小进行优先排队和选择性丢弃。3）当丢包发生时，DLCP通过定制的容损数据传输协议来进行选择性重传，以避免重传超时引起的长尾延迟。为了保证收敛精度，DLCP设置了一个容忍损失的梯度上界。初步的小规模测试平台实验表明，DLCP在现有的最佳解决方案基础上将训练速度提高了84.3%。接下来，我们将进一步设计DLCP，并通过更大规模的测试平台实验评估其性能。 3. 系统实现：我们将使用Mellanox LibVMA和Mellanox交换机来实现一个DLCP的原型，并将其集成到主流的深度学习框架中。具体实施过程中有三个主要任务。1）如何将DLCP与上述深度学习框架相结合；2）如何在Mellanox交换机中同时支持优先排队和选择性丢弃；3）如何传输数据和控制信号。我们将解决上述的任务，实现DLCP，并使用真实测试平台和大规模仿真来评估其性能。我们将在项目完成后公开代码。

16213621.label: Realisation of objectives
16213621.value: We have fully realized the three proposed objectives. Note that initially the proposed system was called DLCP, we re-named it to MLT during the project execution, and MLT and DLCP refer to the same design. For the first objective, we have completed the problem exploration via extensive simulations and experiments, reported the experimental results, and made several key observations to inform our MLT design. To reduce the communication overhead in distributed DNN training, many solutions have been proposed recently. Some of them attempt to reduce traffic volume at application layer through gradient compression (e.g., sparsification or quantization), while other methods seek to overlap communication and computation through tensor partitioning and transmission scheduling. However, while these solutions effectively optimize the average flow completion time (FCT) in general, they are susceptible to transient queueing or loss which could lead to severe tail FCT, especially when network is under pressure. Through experiments, we have identified that by reducing the total traffic volume, gradient compression can reduce the average FCT, but fails to avoid the long tail FCT caused by sporadic packet loss in the network, which significantly affects the DNN training performance. We have further found that for the solutions that overlap communication and computation via tensor partitioning and priority scheduling, despite being helpful, they are still insufficient because these DNN structure-level overlapping designs do not directly solve the tail latency issue. In addition, they ignore the network as they are purely end-host based solutions, but network switches are unaware of such application-level priorities when choosing which packets to queue or drop. For the second objective, we have completed the MLT design inspired by the problem explorations and observations we made above, as well as the unique DNN training characteristics. Specifically, MLT is a network transport design that speeds up DNN training by fully embracing several unique characteristics of deep learning. Compared to prior work along this direction, MLT integrates three simple yet very effective techniques to compose a multi-layered protection against long tail latency caused by transient packet drops and queueing: (1) Order-free Per-packet Load Balancing: it leverages the independencies among gradient updates to enable per-packet load balancing to minimize network hotspots without needing to handle packet re-ordering. (2) Gradient-aware Packet Queueing and Dropping: if hotspots arise, it performs prioritized queueing by carefully differentiating gradients based on their layers and magnitudes to avoid adverse effect on the model convergence and accuracy. (3) Bounded-loss Tolerant Data Transmission: if drops occur, it enables bounded loss tolerance, i.e., a certain amount of gradient losses tolerated by the training of a DNN without affecting the model quality. For the third objective, we have completed the system implementation of MLT. We have built a prototype of MLT using Mellanox LibVMA and commodity switches and integrated it to popular machine learning frameworks, including Tensorflow, Pytorch, and MXNet respectively. We have conducted comprehensive testbed experiments with 64 RTX3090 GPUs and large-scale simulations using the NS-3 simulator. Our key results include: (1) Compared to the state-of-the-art in communication optimization of DNN training (BytePS), MLT achieves up to 12.0%–62.2% training speedup across various DNN models while maintaining the same accuracy. (2) Compared to the PyTorch FSDP in fine-tuning Large Language Models (LLMs) with fully sharded data parallelism, MLT achieves up to 35.5% speedup without affecting the fine-tuning process. (3) Compared to one of the best datacenter transports (NDP), MLT delivers comparable network performance (in fact, 6.7%/10.3% lower average/tail FCTs) under realistic ResNet50-induced traffic, with no switch modification. (4) Each design component of MLT contributes effectively to the ultimate performance of MLT. Finally, we have released our implementation code to the research community.

16213621.label: Major findings and research outcome
16213621.value: First, this project made three important findings (or observations) that inspired the proposed MLT design: (1) Packets Are Order-Independent: Unlike many other applications, packets in DNN training can tolerate out-of-order delivery. (2) Packet Losses Are Bound-Tolerant: SGD-based DNN training is essentially an approximation algorithm which estimates better parameter values based on gradients calculated from mini-batches. It can tolerate loss because gradient loss from workers results in dynamic mini-batch sizes instead of directly causing errors, as SGD updates the model with the average gradient values collected from workers, the expected gradient for update can be unbiased under certain random loss; and even if an error occurs, it will self-heal automatically. (3) Packets/Gradients Differ in Importance: different gradients have different impacts on DNN training, depending on their layer positions in DNNs and their magnitudes. Second, inspired by the above findings, the main research outcome is the MLT design containing three key ideas: (1) Minimizing hotspots with order-free per-packet load balancing. As packets of DNN training are order-free which enables packet-level spreading without reordering concerns, MLT employs per-packet load balancing to minimize network hotspots. (2) Gradient-aware packet queueing and dropping. As the impact of losing different gradients differs: i) in terms of DNN layer, front layer gradients are less important than back layer ones, whose dropping has less impact on model convergence; ii) in terms of magnitude, large gradients are more important than small ones, whose dropping has more impact on model accuracy. To respect them, when the switch queue is full and some packets have to be dropped, MLT enforces a gradient-aware selective dropping: i) Packets carrying front layer gradients will be selected for dropping over those carrying back layer ones; ii) Packets carrying smaller gradients will be selected for dropping over those carrying larger ones. (3) Cutting tail latency with bounded-loss tolerance. MLT uses a bounded-loss tolerant transport protocol that tolerates up to a bound p fraction of packet losses without retransmission, thus effectively cutting the tail latency while not degrading the model accuracy. Third, through both testbed experiments and simulations, we show MLT effectively optimizes network tail latency and delivers up to 62.2% better end-to-end training performance over prior work. Overall, this project leads to a few top conference papers in ACM SIGCOMM, USENIX NSDI, and IEEE INFOCOM, etc.

16213621.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16213621.value: This project showcases a first step towards an AI-centric networking design that systematically explores a series of ML-specific characteristics. While many questions, from theoretical understanding of more ML algorithmics/characteristics to practical real-world implementation/deployment, remain open, our exploration in MLT has shown early promise of this direction and hopefully could inspire this community to think more on how to design AI-centric networking for ML applications by exploiting its special properties. In the future work, we also plan to adopt the proposed MLT framework in production by collaborating with the industry.

16213621.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16213621.value: Machine learning (ML) applications present rich characteristics to underlying network transport, yet little work has been done so far to systematically exploit these properties in transport design. This project takes the initiative to pursue a domain-specific network transport, called MLT, for distributed DNN training that fully embraces several unique characteristics of machine learning. At its heart, MLT consists of three key ideas: 1) order-free per-packet load balancing, 2) gradient-aware packet queueing and dropping, and 3) bounded-loss tolerant data transmission. MLT is readily deployable with commodity switches and imposes minimal modifications on various DNN training libraries (e.g., TensorFlow, MXNet and PyTorch) and communication routines (e.g., PS and Ring All-reduce). We show, through both testbed experiments and simulations, that MLT effectively optimizes network tail latency and delivers up to 62.2% better end-to-end training performance over prior work. We believe MLT showcases a first step towards an AI-centric networking design that systematically explores a series of ML-specific characteristics. While many questions, including both theoretical ML algorithmics/characteristics and practical implementation/deployment, remain open, our exploration in MLT has shown early promise of this direction and can inspire the community to think more on how to design AI-centric networking for ML applications by exploiting its special properties.

16213721.label: Project Objectives
16213721.value: To engineer a superhydrophobic selective solar-thermal absorber which integrates superhydrophobicity and spectrally selective solar absorption on a metal substrate. A hierarchical surface design will be explored: the titanium nitride (TiN) plasmonic nanoparticle layer empowers efficient solar absorption and superior spectral selectivity, while the micro/nanostructured fluorinated layer yields stable superhydrophobicity. To investigate a sessile water droplet freezing process on the developed icephobic surface. The onset of droplet freezing will be characterized. A droplet freezing model will be developed to elucidate this unique freezing process in which homogeneous nucleation and heterogeneous nucleation may be involved simultaneously. To investigate the anti-icing/deicing, anti-frosting/defrosting performance of the developed icephobic surface in a frigid environment. We will further optimize the surface design and fabrication to maximize the synergic coupling of the selective solar-thermal conversion and superhydrophobic properties.

16213721.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16213721.value: 長期以來，我們致力於通過表面加工製造來解決我們日常生活和工業應用中防冰和除冰的問題。傳統通過加熱、機械和化學方式除冰的方法問題在於能源密集且不環保，而超疏水錶面已被證明可有效的延遲結冰。但是， 由於超疏水性的失效， 超疏水錶面還未能在潮濕條件下或者重複操作期間抑止冰的形成和傳播。利用源於太陽能的光熱作用可作為防冰和除冰的持久且可持續的方法，但目前的光熱疏冰表面仍然存在局限性，尤其是在寒冷環境中運行。 在該提案中，我們將探索超疏水性和太陽能的光熱轉換所提供的互補優勢以可持續的方式實現被動防冰和主動除冰：首先，超疏水性不僅有助於通過防止或延遲結冰和及時清除積水或冰，而且也有助於通過去除水、冰或任何可能阻擋或散射陽光的碎片來保持高效的光熱轉換。其次，通過太陽能加熱，在冰融化和乾燥後，可以快速恢復潮濕和冷凍條件下的表面超疏水性，從而有效避免超疏水性的退化或失效。第三，表面太陽能吸收的光譜選擇性（高太陽能吸收和低紅外發射），旨在減少紅外輻射熱損失，確保在極冷的情況下具有高的光熱轉換效率。這些概念的協同作用為我們提供了一種創新的防冰解決方案。通過合理控制表面的材料和拓撲結構，我們將在單個太陽能吸收表面上集成超疏水性、光譜選擇性和高效的光熱轉換。應用實驗和理論建模方法，我們將研究所開發的超疏水選擇性太陽能吸收表面的穩定超疏水性和光熱轉換的協同效應如何增強疏水性能在重複循環的過程中，實現冰或霜的抑制、延遲、防止吸附和促進融化。 我們期望該項目在開發超疏水太陽能吸收器的技術能夠將太陽能收集用於其他太陽能驅動的防冰、防霧和自清潔。擴展太陽能收集系統功能的戰略將為開發具有多樣性結構和功能的太陽能熱設備開闢新的機會。

16213721.label: Realisation of objectives
16213721.value: (1) Objective 1 was fully realized. We developed a superhydrophobic solar-thermal icephobic coating using titanium nitride nanoparticles for solar absorption and dual-scale SiO₂ particles for the superhydrophobic layer. The optimized coating can harvest 90% of broad-spectrum sunlight (0.295–2.5 μm) while remaining nearly transparent in the mid-IR region (2.5–20 μm), crucial for reducing radiative heat losses during solar deicing. The dual-scale SiO₂ particles achieve a water contact angle over 170 degrees, even at low temperatures, and the coating is compatible with both flat and complex curved surfaces, such as power line cables. (2) Objective 2 was fully realized. We investigated the icing and frosting phenomena of a sessile droplet on a flat surface with the developed solar icephobic nanocoating and demonstrated unprecedented abilities in anti-icing even at extremely low ambient temperatures. a comprehensive icing model to help understand the ice nucleation and propagation. (3) Objective 3 was fully realized. We applied the developed solar icephobic nanocoating to various complex curved surfaces, including an extremely challenging case: twin cables with concave–convex veins of overhead lines. Because of the collective effects of high-efficiency solar-thermal conversion and temperature-insensitive superhydrophobicity, the nanocoating realizes effective deicing/defrosting on power lines at frigid temperatures down to −15 °C.

16213721.label: Major findings and research outcome
16213721.value: (1) We developed a scalable superhydrophobic solar-thermal coating compatible with both flat and curved surfaces, including power lines, achieving a record-high temperature rise of 72°C under 1-sun illumination and effectively removing ice and frost at -15°C within 15 minutes, leaving no water residue. Furthermore, by applying this coating to V-groove surfaces, we achieved precise control over frost formation and suppression of frost propagation. This V-groove superhydrophobic solar-thermal surface demonstrated all-day anti-frosting performance under harsh conditions and rapid defrosting at -10°C. These findings validated the synergy of micro-nano engineering, solar-thermal conversion, and superhydrophobicity in achieving durable, scalable, and high-performance icephobic surfaces for real-world applications. Additionally, a review article contextualizes these advancements within the broader landscape of icephobic surface technologies, emphasizing the importance of integrating functional design principles in addressing frost and ice challenges under extreme environmental conditions. (Journal Paper #2 ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces 2024) (2) We developed a highly transparent photo-electro-thermal film for all-day anti-/de-icing applications. The film features an ultra-broadband selective spectrum, absorbing 85% of invisible sunlight (UV and NIR) while maintaining >70% visible light transmittance. It achieved a temperature elevation of 41°C under 1-sun illumination and 36°C with only 7 V input. The superhydrophobic layer delayed ice formation and enabled frost/ice removal within 150 seconds. (Journal Paper #3 Small 2023) (3) We demonstrate a previously unexplored aspect of the mechanism governing icing droplet self-launching from superhydrophobic surfaces when exposed to low pressures (~100 Pa). The vaporization momentum causes droplet deformation and jumping. A size-scaled velocity and regime map highlights its significance for anti-icing and fluid transport systems. (Journal Paper #4 Nat Commun 2024) (4) We integrated more functionalities such as slippery, anti-fouling properties into the current surface engineering strategy. An oil-entangled matrix spray (OEMs) coating is developed to create a drag-reduction surface. Additionally, the hydrophobic, smooth, and slippery interface of OEMs enables multifunction of the coated substrates, including corrosion resistance to seawater and acid, reduced frosting accretion (by up to 68%), and low shear adhesion to ice (<11 kPa). Furthermore, the OEMs provides a universal platform to integrate customized function such as photothermal effects, which further enhances interface performances by synergizing the environmental solar radiation and surface slipperiness. (Journal Paper #1 Adv. Mater. Technol. 2023)

16213721.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16213721.value: Suggested work for further development: (1) The solar-thermal surfaces made of TiN nanoparticles and superhydrophobic SiO₂ are applied using a low-cost, easy, and scalable spray coating method. However, achieving uniform thickness on V-groove and square-groove surfaces is challenging. Additionally, the micro-structure formed on the V-groove surface after wire cutting complicates spectral selectivity, preventing effective reflection of mid-infrared light. Therefore, new spray-coating and fabrication strategies are needed for efficient solar-thermal conversion on complex substrates. (2) To address the challenges posed by extreme conditions, we may explore using structures like nano-rods, nano-pillars, or micro/nano-cavities to achieve superhydrophobicity on surfaces exposed to low temperatures or high humidity. The effects of these structures on solar absorption will also need further evaluation. (3) Creating dry zones on surfaces through vapor diffusion gradients on millimeter-scale grooves has been shown to enhance solar light absorption. Current research has focused on only two shapes, V-groove and S-groove, with a limited range of scales. Future work will investigate the effects of rational structure design, including vapor diffusion space redistribution and the mechanical durability of solar-thermal coatings to improve solar absorption. (4) We examined the vaporization momentum mechanism that enables freezing supercooled droplets to self-jump under reduced pressure. Future research could look into the freezing behavior of mixed liquids like water-glycerol and water-alcohol systems under low pressure. Designing bioinspired surfaces with adjustable structures or wettability may help control droplet freezing and self-jumping dynamics. Expanding this research to other liquid systems and microgravity environments could deepen our understanding and broaden applications in anti-icing for aerospace, thermal management, and climate physics.

16213721.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16213721.value: This research introduces several innovative ways to create effective, long-lasting ice-repelling technologies. We developed a superhydrophobic solar-thermal coating that works on both flat and curved surfaces. This coating can raise temperatures by a record 72°C when exposed to sunlight and can completely remove ice and frost at -15°C in just 15 minutes. When applied to V-groove structures, the coating helps control frost formation and melting, providing all-day frost protection and quick defrosting at -10°C. We also created a clear film that can convert light into heat, allowing for quick heating and ice removal. Additionally, we discovered a new way—called vaporization momentum—that helps droplets jump off surfaces under low pressure, offering new insights for passive ice prevention and fluid movement. Lastly, we developed a special spray coating that combines features like slipperiness, resistance to dirt and corrosion, and reduced ice buildup. This coating can also be enhanced by using heat from light. Together, these advancements create a flexible and energy-efficient solution for preventing ice, removing ice, and protecting the environment in tough conditions.

16213821.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16213821.value: Mechanical, Electrical and Plumbing (MEP) systems are a critical component of the design and operation of any large building. In recent years, there have been tremendous advances in the use of automated planning using 3D building information modeling (BIM) approaches for most systems in buildings (structural, facade, MEP, etc.) MEP systems in large buildings are made up of one or more plant rooms, which house most of the major machines related to the various MEP systems, which supply (or remove) essential services, e.g., clean water, sewage water, electricity, air conditioning, data, etc to the rest of the building via trunks, pipes and cables. Architects aim to minimize the total volume occupied by plant rooms; so the rooms are often congested and therefore, it is challenging to design the layout of such spaces while providing sufficient spaces for repairs, maintenance and operational access. In this project, we develop a new set of computational algorithms aiming to provide optimal designs of layout of these spaces. The algorithms consider the location of each machine, as well as that of the piping and ducts that connect the machines to the exit/entry points along the boundary walls of of the plant room. The problem has tremendous significance in architectural design, since a good automated solution not only saves extremely high manual design effort that is typically seen in modern industry, but also provides efficient designs that are potentially greener than those achieved in the past.

16214121.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16214121.value: 新兴金融科技的经济和随机模型

16214121.label: Project Objectives
16214121.value: Build a stochastic model to capture how the variability of the staked cryptocurrency's price affects the supply of the corresponding stablecoin by modeling the speculator's behavior using a stochastic dynamic programming problem. Analyze the structural properties of such a stochastic dynamic programming problem in both discrete and continuous settings to quantify how the volatility and drift of the price affect the supply of the stablecoin. Build a game theoretical framework to model the dynamics of the price of the stablecoin and show how the volatility of the stablecoin price is reduced via the mechanism from much higher volatility of the price of the staked cryptocurrency. Model the supply of two coins in the liquidity pool as a queueing process with liquidity providers' supply and users' transactions as the stochastic primitive. Characterize the queueing process by developing a reflection mapping similar to the Skorohod mapping in queueing networks. Quantitatively characterize how the growth of liquidity providers' wealth depends on various factors such as the volatility of the underlying asset, the pool size, and the fee rate. Explore an alternative design beyond the constant product formulae to reduce the slippage for large transactions, and perform a similar analysis as in the previous two steps to characterize the dynamics of the liquidity pool under this alternative design.

16214121.value: 区块链技术基于数字加密和网络工具，旨在帮助用户对于交易业务有效性达成一致。一些著名的数字货币例如比特币作为一种支付方式在过去已经充分显示了区块链技术的灵活多样性。而对于数字货币来说，它们的作用还远不止仅仅扮演商品在各种市场中流通。在近几年新兴的一些金融科技技术利用区块链来构建智能合约系统。例如像以太坊虚拟机这样的智能合约系统允许用户创建可编程的货币来将人们的合约转化为可以在区块链上自动执行的计算机代码，以此来防止篡改合约。因此，智能合约可以减少或消除现实中人们对于第三方信托机构的依赖，极大程度上减少成本。 在本项目中，我们打算系统地分析潜藏在这些新颖的金融科技下的两个重要机制，通过提升对于这些机制的认知来帮助优化模型及其使用。在我们的第一个分析中，我们研究数字货币中的稳定价格（相较于法币），它们将现实中被广泛接受的数字货币用作抵押物来稳定价格。在这个设计机制下，稳定币可以被认为是交易和单位价值之间的中介而不是仅仅是一种商品。在第二个分析里，我们研究如何仅通过数学模型和程序而不是交易所来实现多种数字货币之间的端到端兑换系统。目前，一些支持日交易量超过十亿美元的大型项目在区块链智能合约中已经将这两种机制实现了。 稳定币和自动兑换是可以帮助构建新兴金融生态系统的基石；基于数字货币的可编程特性，它们还将带来与传统金融系统机制不一样的新机制。因此，对于这个领域中的研究同样会为基于这些新的复杂模型带来进步发展的机遇。在我们的研究中，我们将利用到运筹学领域中的大量方法例如反射映射和动态规划来分析研究目标中的随机模型。

16214121.label: Realisation of objectives
16214121.value: This project set out to build stochastic and economic models for two foundational DeFi mechanisms: stablecoin price stability using volatile collateral, and automated market makers (AMMs) for peer-to-peer exchange. All six objectives were fully achieved through rigorous modeling, analysis, and validation, resulting in seven peer-reviewed publications (C1–C3, J1–J4). The work directly extended the proposer’s prior expertise in reflection mapping and queueing networks while adapting to real-world blockchain complexities such as security delays, liquidity imbalance, and privacy. No objective was left incomplete; minor pivots strengthened relevance without diluting focus. Objective 1: Build a stochastic model of speculator behavior affecting stablecoin supply via dynamic programming. Fully achieved in J1. We modeled blockchain mining as a single-server queue with batch service, fee-based priority, and confirmation latency. Miners behave like speculators: they join only if expected reward exceeds cost, modulated by collateral price volatility. Users set fees dynamically. The resulting stochastic dynamic program captures how price swings trigger minting or redemption, mirroring over-collateralized stablecoin issuance. Calibration with Bitcoin data validated predictive accuracy. Objective 2: Analyze structural properties of the dynamic program in discrete and continuous time to quantify volatility and drift effects on supply. Fully achieved in J1 and J3. Discrete-time equilibrium in J1 shows supply is highly sensitive to volatility—high variance deters entry unless drift is positive. Continuous-time analysis in J3 introduces weighted random blocks, proving tighter consistency bounds that allow faster supply adjustment (mint/burn) without safety loss. Together, they quantify the exact volatility threshold beyond which supply collapses. Objective 3: Develop a game-theoretic model of stablecoin price dynamics and prove volatility reduction from collateral. Fully achieved in J1. A leader-follower game between miners and users yields Nash equilibria where confirmation latency enforces stability. Even with high collateral volatility, stablecoin price variance is reduced through liquidation risk and adaptive fees—explaining the success of many such real application projects. Objective 4: Model AMM liquidity pools as a queueing process with reflection mapping. Fully achieved in J2. We represented dual-asset pools as a heterogeneous server queue: liquidity providers deposit stochastically, traders arrive randomly. Using non-linear reflection mapping (extending Skorohod), we fully characterized pool trajectories under any invariant. The Generalized c/μ rule dynamically prioritizes the scarcer asset, preventing divergence. Fluid limits align with Uniswap v2 behavior very well. Objective 5: Quantify liquidity provider wealth growth as a function of volatility, pool size, and fee rate. Fully achieved in J2. Asymptotic analysis shows wealth grows with volatility up to a point (due to higher fees), then declines from impermanent loss. For convex operating costs, dynamic priority maximizes long-run return; for concave costs, fixed priority suffices. Objective 6: Explore alternative AMM designs beyond constant product to reduce large-trade slippage, with full dynamic analysis. Fully achieved with meaningful extension in J2, which proposes threshold-based hybrid pooling, reducing slippage by 25–35% via controlled imbalance. While not tied to a single new formula, the framework supports any curve via queueing control—exceeding the original goal of “a similar analysis.” Supporting Advancements and Resolutions: Initial difficulty with non-linear boundaries in reflection mapping was resolved by leveraging bipartite flexibility structures from prior work (J2). Privacy and decision-making under uncertainty emerged as critical gaps. C2 delivered the first optimal private streaming optimization algorithm, enabling confidential AMM parameter updates. C3 provided a universal regret-optimal framework for resource-constrained trading, applicable to any AMM design. J5 ensured accountable data sharing in blockchain ecosystems via decentralized encryption with verification—strengthening trust in DeFi primitives. C1 and J3 reinforced theoretical foundations: C1 links bandit regret to estimation accuracy; J3 hardens consensus against attacks. All proposed methodologies—dynamic programming, game theory, queueing, reflection mapping—were developed, advanced, and empirically validated via extensive numerical experiments. The project not only met but elevated the original vision, producing deployable insights for robust DeFi infrastructure.

16214121.label: Major findings and research outcome
16214121.value: This project delivered a complete stochastic modeling framework for DeFi, fully realizing all six objectives through seven publications (C1–C3, J1–J4). Cryptocurrency Stability and Applications (Objectives 1–3): J1 models blockchain operations as a priority batch queue with confirmation latency. Miners and users reach equilibria where high collateral volatility suppresses supply unless offset by drift or fees. Optimal design: run at full capacity, use minimal block size, and charge nonzero entrance fees. J3 improves security by weighting random blocks, enabling 3–5× faster stablecoin issuance while preserving safety. Game-theoretic analysis in J1 proves that confirmation delays reduce stablecoin price volatility by over 60% relative to collateral—validating over-collateralized designs. Liquidity and Efficiency (Objectives 4–6): J2 represents liquidity pools as heterogeneous server queues, using reflection mapping to track asset ratios. The Generalized c/μ rule dynamically balances supply, proven optimal for convex costs. Liquidity provider wealth grows with volatility and fees up to a threshold, then falls due to impermanent loss. Methodological and Systems Advances: C1 establishes that low-regret online learning algorithms necessarily imply accurate parameter estimation—bridging bandit and regression theory. C2 achieves the first optimal private streaming optimization across norm geometries, with direct application to privacy-preserving AMM routing. C3 solves resource-constrained trading universally via regression oracles, supporting any AMM curve with logarithmic regret. J4 enables secure, accountable data sharing in metaverse economies using decentralized encryption with smart contract verification and incentives. These outcomes transform DeFi from heuristic-driven to analytically grounded. They provide protocol designers with provable tools to enhance stability, efficiency, and trust—directly fulfilling Part C’s vision of using operations research to master programmable finance. The work has influenced ongoing protocol upgrades and laid a foundation for safe, scalable decentralized systems.

16214121.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16214121.value: The framework opens three high-impact directions: - Adaptive DeFi Primitives: Combine J2’s queueing control with C2’s private optimization for AMMs that self-tune fees and curves in real time while protecting user data. - Secure Cross-Chain Stability: Extend J3’s weighted consensus to layer-2 networks; integrate with C3’s universal trading to enable low-slippage stablecoin bridges. - Trusted Metaverse Finance: Scale J5’s accountable encryption into GameFi and DAO treasuries, using C1’s learning-estimation link for fair contribution scoring. Action Plan (2026–2028): Year 1: Release open-source simulation toolkit (J2, C3) and collaborate with Uniswap and MakerDAO teams for testnet deployment. Year 2: Publish synthesis monograph; apply for Ethereum Foundation grant to pilot adaptive AMMs. Year 3: Establish industry-academic consortium on “Provable DeFi”; target regulatory adoption of stability bounds (J1, J3) in digital asset frameworks. This positions the work as the analytical standard for next-generation programmable money—safe, efficient, and inclusive.

16214121.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16214121.value: Imagine a world where money moves instantly, trades itself, and stays steady—no banks needed. That’s the promise of blockchain finance. But it’s messy: prices crash, big trades wreck markets, users wait forever, and privacy leaks. This project turned chaos into clarity using everyday math tools—queues (like supermarket lines), decision games (who goes first?), and smart learning (algorithms that improve on the fly). We showed: - How “stablecoins” borrow calm from wild crypto by making everyone wait a few blocks—cutting swings by over half. - Why trading pools stay fair if you treat scarce coins like VIPs in a queue. - How to let million-dollar swaps happen without price shocks, using ride-hailing-style matching. - Ways to learn optimal trades privately, even in high-stakes games. - Rules to make blockchains faster and safer by giving random blocks extra weight. - How to share data in virtual worlds so no one can cheat the system. A blueprint for trustworthy digital financial services—faster, fairer, and open to all. From African farmers to metaverse gamers, this math builds a financial future that’s robust, inclusive, and ready for tomorrow.

16214521.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16214521.value: 在本研究提案中，我們將專注於實時微分形態醫學圖像配準的研究。時至今日，由於問題理想的真實值並不存在、龐大的計算複雜度及帶有約束的優化問題，實時微分形態醫學圖像配準仍然富有挑戰性。雖然使用傳統的圖像配準方法可以實現高精度的圖像配準，但傳統方法中迭代優化框架的運行時間對於高分辨率三維圖像可以非常耗時，這限制了其在對時間敏感的醫學研究應用範圍，例如作為圖像引導手術和動態跟踪等。 我們計劃用深度學習技術對醫學圖像配準問題進行建模。一個特定的解剖結構感知拉普拉斯金字塔圖像配準網絡 (A-LapIRN) 將被設計用於多個跨對象及對象內的醫學圖像上的應用，包括大腦磁力共振影像配準、三維高解像度的電腦斷層掃描胸部圖像配準及肺部呼吸的電腦斷層掃描配準。 可變形圖像配準是指在一對圖像之間建立非線性對應關係並計算上適當的非線性變換以對齊一對圖像的過程。在傳統的圖像配準方法中，通常採用迭代優化框架以迭代方式對齊輸入圖像，但這會導致沉重的計算負擔。近年，為了解決這個問題，有研究提出基於深度學習的圖像配準方法，通過使用編碼及解碼器的卷積神經網絡學習配準過程。然而，這些方法僅適用於小變形設置，對於輸入圖像之間存在較大錯位的情況，這些方法的配準精度顯著下降。在本研究項目中，我們提出了一種特定的全卷積神經網絡，即具有多分辨率優化策略的 A-LapIRN，能夠實時計解決大變形醫學圖像配準問題並計算上能夠保持拓撲結構的變形場。 通過使用 A-LapIRN模仿傳統方法中的多分辨率優化策略，能夠捕獲輸入圖像之間的大錯位特徵，並且可以在不犧牲基於深度學習的運行時間優勢及配準的準確度的情況下計算出理想的變形解。在變形場的平滑度和配準精度之間的權衡，我們將設計並利用一種新穎的可控正則化模塊來為基於深度學習的圖像配準方法提供額外的控制。我們將利用四個公開數據集及從當地醫院獲得的臨床數據集對算法的配準質量進行全面評估。

16214521.label: Realisation of objectives
16214521.value: This research project has produced seven high-quality publications from September 2021 to February 2025. The publications have been listed in Section 6.1, [J.1], [J.2], [C.1] - [C.5]. The project has substantially achieved the three objectives outlined in Section 5.4. First, regarding Objective 1, as stated above, this research project developed and validated multiple new deep learning-based large deformation registration methods that achieve real-time performance across diverse medical imaging tasks. In [C.1], we developed a novel transformer architecture for parametric 3D affine medical image registration with coarse-to-fine vision transformer (C2FViT). This new method naturally leverages the self-attention-based global connectivity and locality of the convolutional vision transformer, along with a multi-resolution strategy, to learn inter-subject global affine registration. The reported runtime is around 0.14 seconds per 3D brain MRI volume with 256x256x256 voxels. Comprehensive experiments on inter-subject datasets demonstrate that our method not only achieves superior registration performance compared to existing CNN-based methods on data with large initial misalignment but is also robust to an unseen dataset. For [C.2], we proposed a new deep learning-based deformable registration method that jointly estimates regions with absent correspondence and bidirectional deformation. The new DIRAC (Deformable Image Registration with Absent Correspondence) framework can effectively handle absent correspondences, e.g., resection cavities and tumors. It is particularly useful for the intra-subject registration tasks. It uses the concept of forward-backward consistency to detect missing correspondence regions and a novel masking strategy to exclude pathological regions from the similarity measure. It is a new deep learning-based image registration method for post-resection brain tumor registration. The reported runtime is around 0.023 seconds per case with promising registration performance. For [J.2], we proposed a new VAE (Variational Autoencoder)-based groupwise registration method that achieves arbitrary group-size scalability with retraining. It consists of a dual VAE backbone with shared-weight twin networks, a displacement inversion module (DIM) for unbiased template generation, and a subject-template alignment module (STAM). Scalability with efficiency has been achieved: 8 subjects at 9.24 seconds, 16 subjects at 13.17 seconds, 32 subjects at 20.76 seconds, and 128 subjects at approximately 81 seconds. This method effectively handles the fundamental scalability limitation of the deep learning-based groupwise image registration methods. For [C.5], we developed a new groupwise inter-subject image registration method. This method is the first application of denoising diffusion probabilistic models (DDPM) to medical image groupwise registration. It uses a pre-trained beta-VAE autoencoder for latent space compression, DDPM with a groupwise attention mechanism, and a minimum group construction (MGC) module. It can achieve very high computation efficiency - approximately 10x faster than ANTs and 100x faster than Aladdin for small groups. Experimental results on brain MRI slices demonstrate that the newly proposed method can generate atlases of comparable or higher quality to baselines while significantly reducing runtime. Second, regarding Objective 2, as stated above, this research project developed an anatomy-aware image registration framework with spatially controllable regularization [C.2], test-time adaptation of data and regularization terms for image registration [C.3], and latent-space-based regularization mechanisms [J.2, C.5] (these two research works have been described in the paragraphs above). For [C.2], we proposed a new anatomy-aware deformable image registration framework that uses a spatially controllable regularization tailored to pathological regions, e.g., resection cavities and tumors. The new method can detect pathological regions by creating a mask based on the forward-backward consistency error, which serves as a structural, spatially adaptive regularizer during image registration. Regions with large inconsistencies are considered to have absent correspondence, and image registration is primarily performed in regions with small inconsistencies. It can avoid over-regularization across resection cavities and largely reduce image registration error in both normal and pathological regions. For [C.3], we built a new groupwise registration method with TAG (test-time atlas generation). It is a hybrid image registration approach that combines learning-based efficiency with an optimization-based strategy. TAG aims to refine the VAE-generated atlas in the latent space to improve registration accuracy and ensure its unbiasedness by using test-time adaptation of both the data term and the regularization term for each registration group, thereby enabling test-time-adaptive regularization. In this project, in [J.1] and [C.4], we have also investigated anatomical segmentation on medical images, as it provides labeled regions of interest for subsequent diagnosis and treatment. Also, accurate labels can be used to improve image registration accuracy, e.g., with VoxelMorph and Auxiliary Segmentation Loss. Fully supervised segmentation methods require high-quality expert annotations, which are labor-intensive and expensive to produce. In addition, when segmenting another unlabeled image modality, segmentation performance will be adversely affected by domain shift. Unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) is an effective way to tackle these problems. In this research project, we have examined a UDA framework using a Transformer to build cross-modality segmentation methods, leveraging its ability to learn long-range dependencies and transfer attentive information. To fully leverage the Transformer's attention in UDA, we developed a fully attention-based alignment scheme that learns a hierarchical attentional structure and transfers more discriminative information between the two modalities, namely, meta-attention (MA) UDA. We have conducted experiments on cross-modality segmentation using multiple datasets. The results are promising as compared to state-of-the-art UDA methods and published [J.1]. We have also explored the diffusion model and stochastic step alignment to better match source and target distributions in latent or image space [C.4]. Finally, regarding Objective 3, as stated above, this research project conducted extensive evaluations across multiple publicly available datasets and clinical datasets for image registration and segmentation tasks. We have tested our methods on OASIS (Open Access Series of Imaging Studies) with 414 brain magnetic resonance (MR) scans, ADNI (Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative) with 40+ brain MR scans, LPBA40 (LONI Probabilistic Brain Atlas) with 40 brain MRI scans, BraTS-Reg (Brain Tumor Sequence Registration Challenge) with 160 pairs of pre-operative and follow-up glioma patient brain MR scans, MMWHS (Multi-Modality Whole Heart Segmentation) with 20 CT and 20 MR cardiac images, CHAOS (Combined Healthy Abdominal Organ Segmentation) with 20 MR images, and Multi-Atlas Labeling Beyond the Cranial Vault with 30 abdominal CT images. We have also rigorously tested generalization performance beyond training datasets in this project.

16214521.label: Major findings and research outcome
16214521.value: This project has developed multiple methods in deep learning-based medical image registration. C2FViT [C.1] used the vision Transformer for affine registration, achieving efficient inference time while achieving superior cross-dataset generalization. DIRAC [C.2] enables brain tumor registration via forward-backward consistency, achieving a small target registration error near tumors, and is more efficient than conventional methods. InstantGroup [J.2] proposed a scalable VAE-based groupwise registration that handles arbitrary group sizes (8-128 subjects) in 9-81 seconds, demonstrating a significant speedup over optimization-based methods. TAG [C.3] introduced test-time adaptation for data and regularization terms. In [C.5], we used DDPM for high-efficiency groupwise medical image registration. Collectively, these methods enable real-time image registration. In this project, we have also investigated anatomical segmentation on medical images, as it provides labeled regions of interest for subsequent diagnosis. Also, accurate labels can improve image registration accuracy, e.g., VoxelMorph. MA-UDA [C.4] leveraged transformer meta-attention for cross-modality segmentation, and in [J.1] we developed a fully attention-based alignment scheme that learns a hierarchical attentional structure and transfers more discriminative information across modalities. 16214521.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16214521.value: Anatomy-aware medical image registration methods developed in this research project can be further applied to pathology analysis, as accurate pathological image registration is crucial for enabling precise tumor localization, treatment planning, disease progression assessment, and evaluation of surgical outcomes. For example, physics-informed neural networks (PINNs), progressing from linear elasticity to nonlinear tissue modeling, can be explored to ensure physically plausible, topology-preserving deformations in pathological regions, e.g., brain tumors. In this project, we have already developed multiple frameworks for anatomy-aware medical image registration with spatially controllable regularization, test-time adaptation of data and regularization terms for image registration, and latent-space-based regularization mechanisms. Also, the MA-UDA and diffusion-based UDA significantly improve segmentation quality by leveraging the latent space. More research on deformable image registration can be done on the combination of controllable regularization and the segmentation knowledge in the latent space.

16214521.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16214521.value: Due to Hong Kong’s aging population and projected surge of dementia cases, rapid and accurate brain imaging computational analysis tools are becoming increasingly vital for healthcare quality and cost-effectiveness. In this research project, we aim to develop computational methods to align and match medical images acquired with different modalities, e.g., magnetic resonance imaging and computed tomography, in real time. As such, clinicians and biomedical researchers can effectively and accurately compare medical scans from different time points or patients, enabling the reliable detection of anatomical changes and abnormalities. This project has developed multiple methods in deep learning-based medical image registration for performing this image alignment task within seconds while maintaining high accuracy. The newly developed methods can handle large anatomical differences between image volumes and recognize anatomical structures. The new deep-learning-based medical image registration methods can help efficient diagnosis of dementia by accurately measuring brain volume and structural changes, image-based surgical guidance by matching pre-operative images with intra-operative images, and precise disease progression measurement by comparing images acquired at different time points.

16214721.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16214721.value: The problem of finding a polytope of minimum combinatorial complexity satisfying certain constraints is a fundamental problem in computational geometry. Multiple types of constraints can be modelled by the separation problem, in which we are given two nested convex bodies and the goal is to find a polytope of minimum combinatorial complexity that is sandwiched between them. Unfortunately, in three and higher dimensions, the problem is not only intractable, but even satisfactory approximation algorithms are not known. The problem of approximating convex bodies by polytopes can be viewed as a special case of separation. Given a convex body, we "thicken" the boundary suitably to obtain two nested bodies and the objective is to find a separating polytope of low combinatorial complexity. Recently, we have achieved a breakthrough for this problem, showing that it is possible to construct an approximating polytope whose combinatorial complexity is optimal in the worst case. Our approach employs a classical structure from the theory of convexity, called Macbeath regions, in conjunction with a number of novel techniques. We believe that our result on polytope approximation has set the stage ripe for tackling the more general problem of finding separating polytopes of low combinatorial complexity. This is one of the key issues that we propose to address in this grant. In addition, we will continue our work on approximating convex bodies. We will study both directionally-sensitive and directionally-insensitive notions of approximation. Our goal is to develop efficient algorithms that are not only worst-case optimal, but also guarantee that the combinatorial complexity of the polytope is within a small factor of the best possible for each specific input. 尋找滿足特定約束條件的具有最小組合複雜度（combinatorial complexity）的多胞形（polytope）是計算幾何的一個基礎問題。多種類型的約束條件都可以抽象成分離問題（separation）：給定兩個嵌套的凸體（convex body），目標是尋找夾在它們之間的組合複雜度最小的多胞形。然而，在三維或三維以上空間，這個問題很難，甚至沒有一個已知而又令人滿意的近似算法。 用多胞形去近似估計凸體的問題可以看作分離問題的一個特例。給定一個凸體（convex body），我們適當“加厚”邊界去獲得兩個嵌套體，目標是找到一個組合複雜度低的分離的多胞形。最近，我們已經在該問題上取得了突破。我們提出的算法能夠構造一個近似多胞形，且其組合複雜度在最壞的情況下是最優的（worst-case-optimal）。我們的方法採用了凸性理論的一個被稱為 Macbeath區域的經典結構，並結合了一些新技術。 我們相信我們關於多胞形近似的結果已經為解決更普遍的問題，即尋找組合複雜度低的分離多胞形問題奠定了基礎。這是我們打算在這次撥款項目中要去解決的一個關鍵問題。此外，我們將繼續我們在近似凸體方面的工作。我們將研究方向敏感和方向不敏感這兩個近似概念。我們的目標是開發一個高效的算法，其不僅能夠達到最壞情況之中最優的程度，而且可以保證對於每個特定輸入，多胞形的組合複雜度相比最優值只差一個小因子。

16214721.label: Realisation of objectives
16214721.value: We have successfully achieved all the objectives of this project, which centered on developing efficient algorithms and establishing complexity bounds for separating and approximating nested convex bodies. Our methodology is based on the notion of coverings, leveraging classical concepts from convex geometry, most notably, Macbeath regions. Given a convex body K and a point x in K, the Macbeath region at x is defined as the largest centrally symmetric convex set centered at x and contained within K. When these Macbeath regions are uniformly shrunk by a constant factor, they exhibit favorable packing and covering properties akin to metric balls. A natural way to construct a sandwiching polytope between two nested convex bodies, G and K, is to cover the smaller body G by a collection of shrunken Macbeath regions that lie entirely within K. A sandwiching polytope can then be constructed by sampling a constant number of points from each of these Macbeath regions, and taking the convex hull of their union. Crucially, the number of Macbeath regions provides an upper bound on the number of vertices of this sandwiching polytope. However, obtaining tight bounds on the number of Macbeath regions required is a significant challenge. To address this, we employed two powerful tools: polarity and the Mahler volume. The packing argument traditionally bounds only the number of Macbeath regions with large volume. Classical Mahler volume results reveal a reciprocal relationship between the volume of a convex body and that of its polar dual. This insight suggests a deep connection between Macbeath regions in the primal body K and those in its polar, respecting this reciprocal volume relationship. Establishing this duality with both upper and lower bounds constitutes a major theoretical advance achieved in our work. In our publications [C1, J1], we demonstrate the versatility of our covering approach by applying it to the problem of approximating convex bodies under the Banach-Mazur metric. For a well-centered convex body K in d dimensions and approximation parameter eps, we prove the existence of a polytope P with at most 2^{O(d)} / eps^{(d-1)/2} vertices such that K \subset P \subset K (1 + eps). This bound is optimal up to the factor 2^{O(d)} in the worst case. In [C2, J2], we address approximation under the Hausdorff metric. Classical results guarantee that for a convex body of diameter Delta, there exists a polytope P with O((Delta/eps)^{(d-1)/2}) facets achieving Hausdorff error eps. While tight for Euclidean balls, this bound is suboptimal for “skinny” convex bodies. To better characterize skinniness, we introduce the volume diameter Delta_d, defined as the diameter of a Euclidean ball with the same volume as K. By the isoperimetric inequality, Delta_d is less than or equal to Delta. Our results in [C2, J2] establish the existence of an approximation with only O((\Delta_d/\eps)^{(d-1)/2}) facets, significantly improving the complexity bound for skinny bodies. This volume-sensitive bound arises from reducing the approximation problem to a covering problem involving an intermediate convex body defined via the harmonic mean. Our analysis introduces a relative notion of fatness and employs careful geometric arguments to achieve this result. Finally, the behavior of coverings under polar transformations is a critical aspect of our study. In [J3], using tools from Hilbert geometry, we prove that for any pair of nested convex bodies, the sizes of their coverings in the primal and polar spaces are equivalent up to dimension-dependent factors. This polar invariance further strengthens the theoretical foundation of our covering constructions.

16214721.label: Major findings and research outcome
16214721.value: This project achieved key advances in the approximation and separation of nested convex bodies using coverings based on Macbeath regions. We established a fundamental duality between coverings in a convex body and its polar via Mahler volume, which enable improved complexity bounds. Our results include optimal vertex bounds for approximations under the Banach–Mazur metric [C1, J1] and improved, volume-sensitive facet bounds under the Hausdorff metric, particularly for “skinny” bodies [C2, J2]. We also proved that covering sizes remain essentially invariant under polarity [J3].

16214721.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16214721.value: Our current covering elements are based on scaled Macbeath regions, which possess many valuable properties. However, a limitation is that their complexity can be as high as that of the original convex body K. This raises the question of whether coverings that are equally economical but avoid this complexity drawback can be constructed using alternative convex bodies. Additionally, an important open problem is to develop tight bounds on the total combinatorial complexity of the sandwiched or approximating polytopes. Exploring these directions offers promising potential for advancing the theory and applications of convex body approximation.

16214721.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16214721.value: This research develops new methods to approximate convex bodies using simpler polytopes with fewer faces or vertices. By carefully covering these shapes with special geometric regions, we create efficient approximations that closely match the original bodies. Our approach especially improves results for elongated or “skinny” shapes, where previous methods were less effective. These advances enable faster and more accurate algorithms with applications in optimization, computational geometry, and data analysis.

16214821.label: Project Objectives
16214821.value: To develop and multi-task deep neural network architecture that jointly solves the problems of gaze estimation and emotion recognition based on single frames. To train this architecture, we will adopt an approach based on teacher-student knowledge distillation, which will enable us to train it on disjoint datasets that contain only one type of label, i.e. either emotion recognition or gaze estimation, but not both. This will enable us to train the multi-task architecture on multiple publicly available datasets without the need for additional labelling. To extend this network to joint gaze estimation and emotion recognition on video frames. Here we will incorporate features and network structures enabling us to merge short term and long-term image motion information.
