16214821.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16214821.value: Gaze estimation and emotion recognition have important applications in human computer interfaces. Gaze estimation has been used in applications such as hands-free control for the disabled, virtual reality, social behavioral analysis, health care and human robot interaction. Emotion recognition has applications in affective computing, retail and education. Appearance based gaze estimation and emotion recognition share a common input: both rely upon the analysis of facial images. However, to date, they have been studied largely in isolation. Increasing amounts of evidence suggests that gaze and emotion are closely linked. For example, the “shared signal hypothesis” suggest that gaze direction and facial expression interact in the perception of emotion. Approach oriented emotions (joy and anger) are associated with direct gaze, whereas avoidance-oriented emotions (fear and sadness) are associated with averted gaze. This suggests that the there is much to be gained in developing an integrated multi-task approach to learning to estimate/recognize gaze/emotion jointly. The goal of the research proposed here is to develop such a system operating on both single images and video streams by exploiting multi-task learning and knowledge distillation in deep neural networks. We anticipate that this system will result in improved accuracy and better efficiency. We expect improved accuracy, because by treating both problems within a shared system will enable knowledge learned from gaze estimation to be exploited in emotion recognition, and vice versa. We expect better efficiency because the two tasks will share a common feature extraction stage: the convolutional layers of a deep neural network. Since these layers comprise the bulk of the parameters and impose the highest computation burden in a system, sharing them will significantly reduce both learning time and estimation/recognition time in comparison to treating the two problems in isolation. The better efficiency will enable wider adoption of the system, especially in environments where compute is limited, e.g. mobile devices. 視線估計和情感識別在人機交互系統中有重要的應用。視線估計已經在許多方面得到了廣泛的應用， 例如為殘疾人士設計的無需手持的操作系統，虛擬現實系統，社交行為分析，醫療以及人機交互系統。情感識別則在情感計算，零售和教育行業中應用廣泛。基於外觀的視線估計和情感識別技術都使用相同的輸入信號，即人臉數據。但是在目前的研究中，這兩項技術很大程度上是分開發展的。越來越多的證據表明，視線和情感是緊密聯繫在一起的。例如，「共享信號假設」學說認為，視線的方向和人臉表情在人類感知情感的過程中共同起作用。方法導向的情感（喜悅和憤怒）通常和直視的視線有關，而迴避導向的情感（害怕和悲傷）通常和迴避視線接觸有關。這說明，構建一個多任務系統來同時學習視線和情感的識別是相當有益的。這篇研究計劃的目標就是構建一個多任務學習和知識蒸餾的深度神經網絡系統，使其能夠處理單張圖片和視頻流數據。我們預期這個系統能夠在提高識別精準度的同時，改善識別的效率。前者是因為多任務系統可以使得其中一項任務利用另一項任務習得的知識，從而提升準確度。後者是因為這兩項任務共享同一個特徵提取系統，即多層的卷積神經網絡。因為多層卷積神經網絡有大量的參數，而且通常是一個系統中最耗費計算量的部分，與分開學習兩種的任務的系統相比，共享多層卷積神經網絡更能有效減少訓練和識別的時間。提升的效率可以拓展該系統在更多領域的應用，特別是計算力受限的場景下，例如在移動設備中。

16215521.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16215521.value: Amid global concerns over climate change, the electricity generation sector is decarbonizing. Gas turbines are vital to this process owing to their ability to switch flexibly between low-carbon fossil fuels and carbon-neutral alternative fuels, such as hydrogen and biofuels. Crucially, gas turbines can respond quickly to changes in electricity demand, stabilizing the power grid against intermittent production from renewable sources such as solar and wind. However, gas turbines emit pollutants such as nitrogen oxides (NOx), contributing to respiratory illness, acid rain, and global warming. NOx emissions can be reduced by adopting lean premixed combustion, but doing so increases the risk of thermoacoustic instability. This phenomenon, which arises from the coupling between unsteady combustion and sound, leads to high-amplitude self-excited flow oscillations in the combustor. If not detected early enough, such oscillations can cause thermal and mechanical damage, reducing the reliability and efficiency of gas turbines. Currently, two types of methods are available for early detection of thermoacoustic instability: (i) model-based methods, which can be accurate but require significant system knowledge and human expertise, and cannot easily generalize to new systems or conditions; and (ii) model-free data-driven methods, which are less affected by these limitations. A versatile tool for visualizing the topology of a high-dimensional phase space trajectory is the recurrence plot (RP). Recently, several researchers have extracted early warning signals from RPs using recurrence quantification analysis (RQA). However, their success has been limited to combustors exhibiting supercritical Hopf bifurcations. To date, little progress has been made towards developing early warning signals for combustors exhibiting subcritical Hopf bifurcations, even though these are widespread. We propose to combine the topological visualization capabilities of RPs and the data-driven classification capabilities of neural networks to develop a hybrid framework for real-time early detection of thermoacoustic instability. We will experimentally collect training and testing data on two existing combustors (one laminar and one turbulent), both exhibiting supercritical and subcritical Hopf bifurcations, and then convert the collected data into two-dimensional unbinarized RPs. We will use these RPs to train and validate convolutional neural networks, deploy the networks on both combustors, and then benchmark their performance (accuracy, robustness, response time, training cost) against established nonlinear dynamical indicators and machine learning algorithms, including RQA-based precursors. This project will lead to a new data-driven tool for real-time early detection of thermoacoustic instability in combustors with supercritical and/or subcritical Hopf bifurcations, improving the reliability and efficiency of low-NOx gas turbines. 在全球都對環境變化充滿顧慮的情況下，電力行業正逐步減少碳排放量。燃氣輪機對此環節至關重要，因為它能夠靈活地在低碳化石能源和碳中和替代能源（例如氫能和生物能）上切換。更重要的是，燃氣輪機能夠快速響應電力的需求。相比較於間歇性發電的可再生能源例如太陽能和風能等，它能夠穩定地輸出電能，從而保證電網穩定。然而，燃氣輪機會排放污染物（如氮氧化物），這些有害污染物會引起呼吸系統疾病，酸雨和全球變暖。氮氧化物排放可以通過採用貧油預混燃燒來降低，但是這樣做會增加熱聲不穩定性發生概率。熱聲不穩定源於燃燒室中不穩定燃燒和聲場之間的耦合，發生時會導致高振幅的自激流動振盪。如果沒有足夠早期地預測到，這種振盪能夠引起熱應力和力學結構性的破壞，降低燃氣輪機的可靠性和效率。目前，兩類方法可以被用於熱聲不穩定問題的早期預測：（i）模型法，該方法能夠準確地預測熱聲不穩定但是需要關於系統的重要信息和專業的人力資源，並且不能方便地被應用於其他新的系統或者工況下的預測工作。 （ii）無模型數據驅動法，該方法能夠較好的應對以上所述的限制。遞歸圖是一個被廣泛使用的方法，它能夠視覺上呈現系統在高維度相空間中的狀態。目前，許多研究人員通過對遞歸圖的幾何特徵進行定量分析，從而獲得能夠日早期預測熱聲不穩定的指標。然而，他們僅針對超臨界霍普夫分岔取得了不錯的結果。時至今日，對於亞臨界霍普夫分岔的預測工作還沒有取得很多的進展，儘管該類型的分岔廣泛存在於各類燃燒系統中。我們通過將遞歸圖獨特的拓撲形態展示能力和神經網絡強大的數據驅動分類能力相結合，提出一種新的混合型熱聲不穩定實時預測方法。我們會分別從兩個燃燒器中（一個層流燃燒器和一個湍流燃燒器）收集用於訓練和測試的實驗數據。這兩個燃燒器均能夠呈現亞臨界和超臨界霍普夫分岔。而後，我們將這些數據轉化成二維的遞歸圖。我們將使用這些遞歸圖來訓練和驗證神經網絡模型，並將訓練好的網絡部署於兩個燃燒系統中，檢測他們的性能。我們會與已知的非線性動力學指標和機器學習算法模型在準確性，魯棒性，響應時間和訓練成本上進行對比。該項目將著力研發一個新的數據驅動型熱聲不穩定預測工具，該工具可用於預測亞臨界和超臨界霍普夫分岔，並最終幫助低氮氧化物燃氣輪機提升可靠性和效率。

16215821.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16215821.value: Coastal cities such as Hong Kong and Shenzhen have been experiencing rapid development of their coastal fronts in recent years. However, extreme weather conditions, such as typhoons and storm surge, have caused severe damages to offshore structures in the surrounding area. Although large boulders are commonly used to protect coastal embankment from scouring and erosion, currently design guidelines are mainly based on empirical methods, derived from very limited small-scale experimental data. Extensive seawall collapse in recent typhoon events indicates the design may not be adequate. Facing depletion of quarry stones around the area, it is also an urgent need to develop more economical, efficient granular systems for coastal protection. Structuralized Cementing Technology, as recently invented by the research team, is a promising technique to structurally cement smaller-sized granular materials for wave erosion protection. Through collaboration with Tsinghua University, this proposal aims at providing a scientific basis and design guidelines of using the structurally cemented granular materials for coastal erosion protection through the state-of-the-art numerical modeling and centrifuge tests. Three inter-related tasks are planned. In Task 1, an advanced computational platform will be developed to better understand the fundamental mechanism of wave erosion process by coupling computational fluid dynamics (CFD) and discrete element method (DEM). The resolved CFD-DEM method can realistically simulate multiphase fluid (air and water) interaction with the structurally cemented, irregularly shaped granular system. It will be the first of its kind that enables direct quantification of fine-scale interactive forces between wave and the complex granular system without resorting to empirical functions. High-quality, scalable experimental tests are much needed to validate the numerical model. In task 2, a newly constructed drum centrifuge facility at HKUST will be used to study wave interaction with the structurally cemented granular systems. By exerting high gravity forces to the test model, the centrifuge tests can be reliably scaled to a large field scale (km). The centrifuge tests will provide unique sets of data to validate CFD-DEM modeling, and to examine the system performance under extreme weather conditions. Finally, design guidelines on using the cemented granular materials for wave erosion protection will be proposed (Task 3), including environmentally friendly construction measures and design optimization based on numerical and experimental study. 近年來，香港、深圳等沿海城市迅速發展。而颱風和風暴潮等極端天氣條件常常對周邊地區的近海結構造成嚴重破壞。雖然大塊石通常用於保護海岸堤防免受沖刷和侵蝕，目前的設計指南主要基於經驗方法和非常有限的小規模實驗數據。在最近的颱風事件中，海堤大面積倒塌，這表明現有的設計不夠適當。 面對地區性採石場的枯竭，迫切需要開發更經濟、更有效的海岸保護顆粒體系統。研究團隊最近發明的結構化膠結技術是一種很有前途的技術，可以結構化地膠結較小尺寸的顆粒材料以抵抗波浪侵蝕。通過與清華大學合作，本研究旨在通過最先進的數值模擬和離心機試驗，為使用結構膠結顆粒材料進行海岸侵蝕防護提供科學依據和設計指南。 本研究規劃了三項相互關聯的任務。任務 1將開發一個先進的數值計算平台，通過耦合計算流體動力學 (CFD) 和離散元方法 (DEM)，更好地理解波浪侵蝕過程的基本機理。 CFD-DEM的解析耦合方法可以真實地模擬多相流體（空氣和水）與結構膠結、形狀不規則的顆粒系統的相互作用。這將是第一個無需借助經驗函數即可直接量化波浪與復雜顆粒系統之間精細尺度相互作用的模型。其次，非常需要高質量、可擴展的實驗測試來驗證數值模型。任務 2將使用香港科技大學新建的鼓式離心機研究波浪與結構膠結顆粒系統的相互作用。通過對測試模型施加超重力，離心機測試可以可靠地擴展到大規模現場（公里）尺度。離心機測試將提供獨有的數據來驗證 CFD-DEM 模型，並檢驗極端天氣條件下的系統性能。最後，任務 3將提出使用膠結顆粒材料進行波浪侵蝕防護的設計指南，包括基於數值和試驗研究的環保施工措施和優化設計。

16215821.label: Realisation of objectives
16215821.value: Project objective 1 has been fully achieved. The PI and his coworkers have successfully developed advanced CFD-DEM method to understand the fundamental mechanism of dynamic interaction between wave-air-granular materials. (1) The study significantly advanced CFD-DEM simulations in the following aspects: a. We developed the-first-of-its-kind resolved CFD-DEM coupling method to simulate complex shaped solid materials with clumped Discrete Element Method (DEM) in two fluids (air and water), which is simulated by Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) method. The resolved CFD-DEM coupling simulation could provide sufficient details of interactive forces between solids and fluids, which are difficult to measure in experiments. b. In order to efficiently and accurately capture the entire flow regimes, from laminar to turbulent flow in densely packed granular media, in this research, we developed an innovative to modify fluid velocity at the fluid–solid and air-water interfaces, which can significantly improve the numerical accuracy of CFD-DEM simulation. c. To effectively simulate dynamic interactions between big-sized particles and fine-sized particles with two-phase fluids, we developed an innovative hybrid CFD-DEM model that combines the “fully-resolved” and the “extended un-resolved” methods. The CFD-DEM models were published in top journal Computers and Geotechnics [J4, J6]. (2) The developed CFD-DEM method was used to simulate the dynamic interaction between air-wave and rock armors. We simulated the stability of the armour layer under different wave loading conditions, by considering different armor unit shape and weight. The numerical simulation provided sufficient details of localized hydraulic variables such as the pore pressure, velocity, and vortex distributions, which are difficult to measure in experiments. The numerical simulation was validated through several experimental tests. We also studied the wave energy dissipation of complexly shaped rocks and to estimate the stability of rock armor layers under extreme wave loading. The results were published in top journals Coastal Engineering [J5] and Ocean Engineering [J7]. Success in objective 1 formed a solid basis for objective 2. Objective 2 has been fully achieved. We developed innovative numerical methods and laboratory experiments to study the mechanical behavior of structurally cemented granular materials, and developed design guidelines on using them for wave erosion protection. The following tasks were completed: (1) Experimental tests on cemented granular materials: In the reporting period, we conducted a series of laboratory tests on cemented granular materials. More than 40 samples were tested with different cement volume fractions. (2) Numerical models on cemented granular materials: In this research, we developed three innovative numerical methods to simulate cemented granular materials, namely, (a) a mesoscale bond model in Discrete Element Method to model complicated local morphology of the cement within irregular particles; (b) a periodynamic method with a newly developed “touch-aware” contact model to study the micro-mechanical behavior of cemented granular particles. (c) finite-discrete element method for simulating fracture and fragmentation in cementitious materials. (3) Experiments and numerical simulation were used to study the damage mechanism of cemented granular materials. The results indicated that strength of the material linearly increase with the cement ratio up to 80%. Beyond that, cement filling in the void greatly change the failure mechanism and increase the strength of the material, till it becomes a rock-filled concrete. The numerical simulation agreed well with experimental tests. (4) Centrifuge tests: two centrifuge tests were conducted out at HKUST Geotechnical Centrifuge Facility. The seawall stability with cemented granular systems were tested with different layout and configurations. (5) The study indicated that, cementation significantly increase strength and stiffness of granular materials, and the erosion resistance is greatly enhanced. Our advanced modeling tool can be used to scientifically design the cemented granular system for engineering applications, including optimized location and amount of cementation, and recommended size of boulders. These research results were published in Computers and Geotechnics [J1], International Journal of Numerical Method in Engineering [J2] and Acta Geotechnica [J3], and International Journal of Rock Mechanics and Mining Sciences [J8]. 16215821.label: Major findings and research outcome
16215821.value: 1. The project successfully developed advanced CFD-DEM numerical models to simulate dynamic interaction of multiphase fluid (air and water) interaction with granular systems, which is the first of its kind that can model complicated wave erosion phenomenon with irregularly shaped particles [J4, J5]. Various techniques have been developed to improve the efficiency and accuracy of the numerical model, including interface velocity correction [J4] and a hybrid method to handle particle systems with varying particle sizes [J6]; 2. Cemented granular materials were systematically studied by laboratory experiment and advanced numerical modelling [J1, J2, J3, J8]. Innovative mesoscale bond [J1] and contact algorithms [J2, J3] were developed to simulate the micromechanical behaviour and failure mechanisms of the cemented granular materials. The roles of different amount of cement filling on material strength and stiffness were clarified. 3. Wave erosion mechanisms have been systematically studied by the developed CFD-DEM models [J5, J7, C1, C2]. We studied key influential factors, such as the wave-current characteristics, turbulence development and energy dissipation mechanism, the sizes and shapes of riprap stones etc. Centrifuge tests were conducted to study the stability of seawall- cemented granular system [C3] with different design configurations. The developed CFD-DEM model provides a powerful computational tool for design and optimization of such a cemented granular system, and can greatly reduce the construction cost of the wave erosion protection structure. The research findings have been published as 8 SCI papers in top international journals, including Computers and Geotechnics [J1, J4, J6], International Journal of Numerical Method in Engineering [J2] and Acta Geotechnica [J3], Coastal Engineering [J5], Ocean Engineering [J7], and International Journal of Rock Mechanics and Mining Sciences [J8]. The research findings have been actively disseminated in various local, national and international conferences, including [C1] The 17th Asian Congress of Fluid Mechanics (ACFM), August 2023, Beijing, China; and [C2] [C3] in the 26th Annual Conference of The Hong Kong Society of Theoretical and Applied Mechanics, April 2023, Hong Kong, and [C4] International Conference DEM10 in Japan, July 2025, and various invited talks with industry and government agencies (See Part C.11) The resolved CFD-DEM solver was publicly released as open source at https://github.com/shenzhihao/CFDEMInterFoamIB. Many researchers have accessed the code and used it for research. Three Ph.D. students, Dr. Zhihao SHEN, Dr. Soheil MOHAJERANI, Dr. Yuntian ZHAO have been trained and graduated. One Ph.D. Student, Mr. Dongkai LI, is ongoing.

16215821.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16215821.value: This project successfully developed advanced numerical models to simulate complicated wave-erosion mechanism and demonstrated the advantage of using cemented granular system for coastal protection. Although small-scale laboratory tests were also conducted, real site performance of the cemented granular system need to be further validated. In the future, it is greatly needed to develop a real site testbed, in order to verify the performance of the cemented riprap system versus traditional system in extreme weather conditions. Such real-site experiment can provide valuable data to validate various hypotheses made in this study, and identify critical challenges for real-world application. This perspective can only be achieved by liaising with government agencies and industries to promote and improve such a cementing technology.

16215821.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16215821.value: Riprap, also known as rock armor or rubble, is commonly used to protect coastal structures from wave erosion. However, the current design practice is mainly based on empirical methods. Extensive riprap collapse in recent typhoon events indicates the design may not be adequate. Moreover, facing shortage of quarry stones, it is urgently needed to develop more economical, more efficient wave protection systems. This project proposes to use cemented granular materials to improve the coastal erosion protection. To fully understand the fundamental mechanism of wave erosion, first, advanced numerical models were developed to simulate the complicated dynamic interaction between the wave and the granular system. Extensive laboratory experiments were conducted to characterize the mechanical properties of cemented granular materials, and validated the developed numerical models. Finally, numerical and experimental study were carried out to develop design guidelines on using cemented granular materials for wave erosion protection. By using structurally cemented stone clusters instead of big stones as the erosion protection structure, the construction cost can be greatly reduced. It can generate significant impact for coastal development in Hong Kong, Pearl River Estuary and areas beyond.

16300021.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16300021.value: Boron-containing compounds have versatile potential applications in fields such as electronics (including organic light emitting diodes), pharmaceuticals and chemicals. They are extremely useful reagents and intermediates in the synthesis of organic compounds used for the production of pharmaceuticals, agrichemicals and organic materials. In the synthesis of boron-containing compounds, diboron compounds are powerful reagents that play extremely important roles in a large number of borylation reactions. Thus, in recent years, a diverse range of diboron compounds have been synthesized and characterized, and their reactions with various organic substrates have attracted considerable interest. Collaborating with experimentalists, we have theoretically studied many of the related reactions over the past few years. The collaborative work has placed us at the forefront of this research area of boron chemistry. This proposed project will build on our very recent work (jointly published in 2020 in the Journal of American Chemical Society by an experimental group and ourselves) on reactions of diboranes(4), a popularly used class of diboron compounds, with different organic azides. In that work, very interestingly, we found that the reaction outcomes varied considerably depending on the organic azides used and the different substituents on the diboranes(4). In light of those puzzling findings, we believe that further theoretical studies are required to systematically evaluate how different azides and substituents on diboranes(4) affect the reaction pathways. In this proposed project, we intend to perform density functional theory (DFT) calculations to explore the mechanisms underlying these and related reactions that lead to different outcomes. 16300121.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16300121.value: 關於低秩張量的穩健統計分析方法，理論及應用

16300121.label: Co - Investigator(s)
16300121.value: Prof Yuan, Ming Prof Zhang, Anru

16300121.label: Project Objectives
16300121.value: The PI and collaborators will develop computationally fast and statistically optimal methods for low-rank tensor estimation that are robust to heavy-tailed distributions. Most existing low-rank tensor methods impose sub-Gaussian assumptions on the noise or covariate tensors. Unfortunately, heavy-tailed distributions emerge in numerous applications, where existing methods become sub-optimal or completely ineffective. The PI and collaborators will investigate a shrinkage-based approach for robust tensor estimation under heavy-tailed distributions and for several fundamental low-rank tensor models. We shall propose data-driven thresholds, design fast algorithms, and demonstrate their statistical efficacy. The PI will investigate low-rank tensor estimation using robust loss functions, and study their capability of handling arbitrary corruptions and outliers. Outliers and arbitrary corruptions are common in tensorial datasets. Existing tensor methods are extremely sensitive to outliers or arbitrary corruptions. A small portion of corrupted entries can significantly deteriorate most low-rank tensor estimations. Robustifying the loss function is a well-known convention in robust statistics. The PI will investigate the applications of Huber loss and other robust loss functions to low-rank tensor estimation. We shall develop new algorithms to solve the associated optimization programs and study their statistical benefits for arbitrary corruptions and outliers. The PI and collaborators will propose a generalized framework for low-rank plus sparse tensor estimation to analyze mixed tensor data. Tensor data have mixed values if some entries are continuous variables, while others are categorical variables. Mixed tensor data often appear in sampling surveys or multi-relational networks. Existing tensor approaches fail to cope with mixed data while simultaneously recovering the low-rank and sparse components. We aim to analyze mixed tensor data using a family of heterogeneous exponential distributions. By allowing distinct link functions for individual entries, the proposed model will synchronously incorporate continuous, binary, and count data. The team shall devise effective algorithms, and showcase their statistical merits in application and in theory. The PI and collaborators will investigate tensor methods for analyzing multi-layer mixed networks. Recently, the PI and collaborators proposed a mixture multi-layer stochastic block model (MMSBM) for the investigation of community detections when multiple binary networks are available. However, multi-layer networks are often weighted, at least within some layers. We denote a multi-layer network as mixed if some or all layers are weighted. The PI’s previous work has only dealt with binary multi-layer networks. We will generalize MMSBM to multi-layer mixed networks, and propose efficient tensor methods for community detection and network classification. We shall investigate the statistical theory of these methods, and demonstrate their efficacy for processing real-world datasets.

16300121.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16300121.value: A tensor is a multi-dimensional array. Recent years have witnessed a burgeoning demand for collecting, processing, and analyzing tensor data, which routinely arises from diverse applications. Low-rank tensor estimation is the predominant method for tensor data analysis. However, existing low-rank tensor methods often require restrictive statistical conditions, and easily break down when these conditions are absent. To be more practically relevant, low-rank tensor methods should be statistically robust. The goal of this proposed project is to develop statistically efficient and computationally fast low-rank tensor methods that are robust to heavy-tailed distributions, arbitrary corruptions, heterogeneous noise, and mixed data. The PI and collaborators will investigate the following aspects: (1) a shrinkage-based approach for robust tensor estimation and its statistical robustness to heavy-tailed distributions and heterogeneous noise; (2) low-rank tensor estimation with robust loss functions, and their capability of handling arbitrary corruptions and outliers; (3) a generalized low-rank plus sparse tensor model for mixed data; and (4) tensor methods for analyzing multi-layer mixed networks. We will develop novel robust low-rank tensor methods, design fast algorithms, showcase their efficient application to real-world datasets, and develop relevant statistical theories. 多維矩陣，也稱張量，近些年在各種應用裡出現，同時也帶來巨大的處理這種類型數據的需求。低秩張量估計是一類常用的張量分析方法。但是現存的低秩張量方法需要非常嚴格的統計條件。為了更好的滿足現實需求，低秩張量方法需要統計的穩健性。 此項目的目標是發展快速的穩健的統計低秩張量分析方法，以應對重尾分佈，任意污染和異類噪聲。我們將研究以下問題：（1）基於收縮的穩健的低秩張量統計方法以應對重尾分佈和異類噪聲；（2）基於穩健損失函數的低秩張量方法以應對任意污染和離群值；（3）廣義的低秩加稀疏張量的模型以處理混合數據；（4）用於分析混合多層網絡的張量方法。我們將設計新的穩健低秩張量方法，快速的算法，在真實的數據集上顯示我們方法的有效性已經發展相應的統計理論。

16300221.label: Project Objectives
16300221.value: Develop a hydrodynamic model to study the spontaneous dynamics in viscoelastic active liquids. Specifically, I plan to develop a Maxwell-type model to computationally study the interplay of activity and viscoelasticity in polymer-based active liquids and compare the calculations to experimental observations. Develop a hydrodynamic model to understand viscoelastic tissues at the continuum level. Specifically, I propose to rely on a foam-based model and study how active stresses shape cell deformation and flow field, and modify the macroscopic rheological properties of the system. Develop a mesoscopic model, such as phase-field model, to understand viscoelastic tissues with details of individual cells. Specifically, I plan to develop a new model to simulate confluent tissues, in which the effects of activity and viscoelasticity of individual cells will be explicitly accounted for. The model will be compared to the previous model and the importance of cell-level details will be examined.

16300221.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16300221.value: Active matter, in which individual constituents undergo active processes by converting other forms of energy into mechanical work, can give rise to intriguing collective dynamics and novel material behaviors mimicking those of biomaterials systems. Examples of active matter include cytoskeleton polymer solutions, bacteria suspensions, tissues, animal flocks, and even vibrating rods. Developing a framework to understand these soft, non-equilibrium materials systems will help us elucidate how cells and tissues work and also benefit the rational design of synthetic materials for biomimetic applications. Recent successful paradigms of active-matter-based materials are active colloids and active liquid crystals, both of which have displayed tunable material properties and spontaneous dynamics that are promising as a new class of smart and autonomous materials. Active matter systems usually consist of multiple components and often-times exhibit both viscous and elastic properties. However, the viscoelastic property of active matter is poorly characterized and how it dictates the autonomous dynamics of the system remains elusive, limiting their further applications. A recent experiment suggests that flowing tissues can be regarded as Maxwell viscoelastic liquids. The role of activity in this system needs further studies. In another experiment, a dense suspension of bacteria is found to engender a large-scale spontaneous flow upon the addition of DNA polymers above a threshold concentration. How bacteria and polymers organize themselves and shape such flow needs more research. To elucidate the physics of viscoelasticity in active matter, I propose to develop continuum models to investigate the interplay of the microstructure and activity in viscoelastic active liquids. Specifically, a hydrodynamic equation accounting for the microstructure of the material will be examined. A similar approach has been proven successful in interpreting active liquid crystals. The new active matter model will be used to address several open questions in cell-based research. These questions include, for example, why certain cells with flexible shapes exhibit nematic phase, what determines the nature of the active stresses in dense cell colonies, and how different types of active stresses give rise to different active dynamics. To validate the model, simulation results will be compared to cell-based experiments performed by our collaborator. As such, the proposed research intends to deliver a quantitative framework to understand the viscoelastic properties of active matter systems and how they dictate the autonomous dynamics. It will help interpret the structure and rheology of complex biofluids and tissues, paving the way towards engineering them for biological and biomedical applications.

16300421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16300421.value: A hallmark of biological materials, such as living cells and tissues, is their emergent mechanical properties exhibiting a mixture of fluid- and solid-like behaviors across different spatial and temporal scales. The multiscale mechanics of such soft glassy materials have recently attracted much attention, given their important biological implications and immense practical applications in cell mechanics, material synthesis, and microfluidics. Despite their importance, our fundamental understanding of living materials remains limited. For example, how to accurately characterize the modulus of living materials at the cell and tissue levels with a well-defined measurement geometry and a precise mathematical modeling of viscoelastic relaxation is an ongoing challenge in biophysics and mechanobiology. In a recent experiment, we performed combined atomic-force-microscopy (AFM) measurements of stress relaxation and indentation force for 10 cell types ranging from epithelial and muscle cells to neuronal cells, from which we obtained a unified quantitative description of the compressive modulus of individual living cells. Our results show that the cell modulus contains three relaxation modes at different time scales that are closely linked to the hierarchical structure and active stress of living cells. This work provides a reliable experimental framework that can be used to characterize the mechanical state of living materials and investigate their physiological functions and disease states. This proposal aims to utilize the above experimental breakthroughs and investigate the emergent mechanical properties of living materials from single cells to epithelial monolayers. Our first project aims to study the mechanical properties of breast cancer cells. By changing the cancer cell line subtypes, treatments with biochemical markers/inhibitors, and substrate stiffness, we will map the landscape of the mechanical goals of breast cancer cells and pinpoint the physical causes that determine cellular desires. The second project aims to study the mechanics of the simplest tissue model comprising a spherical lumen-enclosing monolayer cyst cultured on a custom micro-patterned substrate. By combining the newly developed AFM force measurement and analysis methods with cell biological techniques, such as growth factors, inhibitors and different cell lines, we will study how epithelial cysts respond to the physical and biochemical cues that alter either single-cell dynamics or cell-cell junctions. By using an interdisciplinary approach that combines quantitative physical methods with biological and biomedical methods, we seek to advance our understanding of the multiscale mechanics of living matter, including cell and tissue homeostasis, in relation to their healthy and diseased states. 生命物質（例如活細胞和組織）的一個標誌性的新興力學特性是它們在不同的空間和時間尺度上展現了既像流體又像固體的複雜力學行為。考慮到這類軟玻璃態材料在細胞力學、材料合成、微流體學等多個領域的重要應用，近年來人們給予這類材料以廣泛的關注。儘管如此，我們在最基礎的層面上對生命物質仍然只有非常有限的瞭解。例如，在生物物理和力學生物學領域，如何在細胞和組織層次通過一個具有定義明確的測量幾何方法和精確的粘彈性弛豫模型來準確地表徵生命物質的粘彈性模量仍是一個長久的挑戰。在最近的實驗中我們利用原子力顯微鏡（AFM）對上皮細胞、肌肉細胞、神經細胞等10種不同種類的細胞進行了應力弛豫測量和壓痕實驗，並給出了一個能刻畫單個活細胞壓縮模量的統一定量描述。實驗結果表明細胞的粘彈性模量包含三個具有不同時間尺度的弛豫模式；這三個模式與細胞中的多層級結構和動應力密切相關。此工作提供了一個可靠的、可以用於表徵生命物質的力學狀態以及能研究它們生理功能及疾病狀態的實驗框架。 本研究計劃旨在利用以上實驗突破來研究包括單細胞和表皮單細胞層在內的生命物質的新興力學特徵。我們的第一個項目是研究乳腺癌細胞的力學特性。通過使用不同的癌細胞系亞型、引入生化標誌物或抑制劑以及改變基底的軟硬，我們得以描繪乳腺癌細胞的力學圖譜併發掘出可決定細胞慾望的物理因素。第二個項目是研究最簡單的組織模型—在慣用的微圖樣襯底上培養出的包含中空微腔的球形單層腺泡—的力學特徵。通過結合最新的AFM力學實驗和用於處理細胞的各種生化手段，例如使用生長因子、抑制劑和不同的細胞系，我們將研究上皮腺泡在引入多種可以改變單細胞力學或細胞間連接的物理和生化處理時會如何響應。通過結合定量物理實驗和生物化學處理的跨學科實驗方法，我們期望可以大大增進我們對生命物質多尺度力學以及與健康狀況相關的細胞和組織體內穩態的理解。

16300421.label: Realisation of objectives
16300421.value: Because Prof. Penger Tong’s contract as Chair Professor of Physics at HKUST expired in June 2022, Prof. Qin Xu in the same department temporarily took over the project as the PI for six months. In January 2023, Prof. Tong renewed his contract for an additional five years and was approved by the RGC to continue leading the project. He is fully responsible for completing the report. To fulfill the project’s two research objectives, we conducted many atomic force microscopy (AFM) measurements to study the mechanical properties of single cells and tissues, focusing on normal and cancerous breast cells and epithelial cysts. We found that the mechanical properties of these materials can be universally modeled using a relaxation modulus, E(t) =E_1exp(-t/τ_1)+E_2(1+t/τ_2)^(-α)+E_∞. (1) Equation (1) contains three distinct relaxation modes: an initial exponential decay, a long-time power-law decay, and a persistent modulus E∞ that does not vanish over a long time. The three distinct relaxation modes are related to the hierarchical structures of the living matter. In our comparative study of breast cancer cells (MDA-MB-231) and normal breast cells (MCF-10A), we found that although the measured E(t) for both cell types can be well fit by Eq. (1), the two cell types exhibit several differences. First, breast cancer cells have a lower initial stiffness E_0 (=E_1+E_2+E_∞ at time t=0) than normal breast cells. This finding is consistent with the reported softening of cancer cells. Second, breast cancer cells have a much higher E∞ value than normal breast cells. As the persistent modulus E∞ is believed to be linked to the active contractile stress generated by molecular motors, a larger E∞ indicates that breast cancer cells are better able to exert greater contractile stress on the cytoskeleton, facilitating their migration. To further explain these differences, we performed AFM measurements in simplified in vitro systems with known molecular compositions and densities. This approach allows us to correlate the mechanical parameters with molecular structures, enhancing our understanding of breast cancer cells and epithelial cysts. In one set of experiments, we systematically studied the emergent mechanics of a six-component protein condensate. The condensate consists of six reconstituted postsynaptic densities (6xPSD): PSD-95, GKAP, Shank3, Homer3, SynGAP, and NR2B. After mixing with a buffer, the six protein types form a phase-separated condensate via multivalent interactions and oligomerization. A previous study (Cell, vol. 174, 1 (2018)) demonstrated that the 6xPSD is a valuable platform that mimics PSD formation and functions in live neurons. Our study demonstrated that the 6xPSD is also a valuable platform for studying the mechanical properties of PSDs. Using combined AFM measurements and fluorescence recovery after photobleaching (FRAP), we obtained a quantitative description of the relaxation modulus E(t) of the 6xPSD condensate, like that of the cancer cells. The measured E(t) for the 6xPSD features an initial exponential decay and a long-time power-law decay, but its persistent modulus E∞ is close to zero, much smaller than that for the cancer cells. The FRAP measurements revealed that 80% of the 6xPSD proteins are mobile, diffusing in a dynamically crosslinked percolation network formed by the remaining 20% non-mobile scaffold proteins. Under applied stress, the mobile proteins in the 6xPSD condensate relax diffusively through local concentration rearrangements within the nanoscale porous network formed by the 20% scaffold proteins. The percolated protein network, on the other hand, exhibits slow power-law relaxation. Therefore, our experiments with the 6xPSD condensate lay the foundation for understanding the multiscale mechanics of cancer cells. Using the newly developed methodology, we investigated mechanical homeostasis and dysfunction in various cell types. In one study, we examined how the material properties of protein condensates are regulated to support cellular functions, a poorly understood topic. We studied the mechanical changes of the PSD condensates by introducing biologically relevant mutations and modifications that alter the protein interactions. For example, we introduced a mutation in the wild-type scaffold protein, Shank3, by replacing an amino acid that largely suppresses its oligomerization. Without the mutation, the 6xPSD condensate exhibits soft-glass-like behavior due to the formation of a percolated protein network. A single-point mutation in Shank3 oligomerization, which is critical for forming networked PSD condensates, softens the PSD, impairs synaptic transmission, and causes autism-like phenotypes in mice. Our studies thus demonstrated that the material properties of the PSD condensate play a crucial role in synaptic plasticity. This process is fundamental to learning and memory mediated by neuronal synapses. In the second set of experiments, we aimed to understand how the activity of molecular motors and other active processes influences the persistent modulus E∞ of normal and cancerous cells. In living cells, cargo transport by motor-driven vesicles must navigate a complex intracellular environment that is crowded, viscoelastic, sticky, and heterogeneous. In this study, we chose an in vitro system consisting of synthetic micromotors (also known as self-propelled particles) that can harvest energy from their surroundings and convert it into directed motion. They are developed as simplified model systems that exhibit dynamic behaviors like those of living systems, such as molecular motors, cells, and bacteria. These micro- and nanoscale “swimmers” also hold great promise for various biomedical applications, including directed cargo transport, drug delivery, and targeted cancer therapy. These applications require a better understanding of the motion of micromotors against the resistance of surrounding protein solutions and cytoskeletal networks, which can be modeled by imposing well-characterized external potential (or free energy) landscapes. Unlike passive particles at equilibrium, whose statistical distribution and escape dynamics over a potential landscape can be understood through Boltzmann statistics and Kramers' theory, active particles, such as micromotors, are intrinsically out of equilibrium. Their dynamics over complex potential landscapes can be understood only within the framework of non-equilibrium physics, which remains a grand challenge in statistical physics. Using a single-particle tracking algorithm, we collected a large volume of particle trajectories from a dilute monolayer of micromotors moving over various microgroove-patterned polydimethylsiloxane substrates fabricated by photolithography. The rugged surface of the microgroove-patterned substrate provides a one-dimensional periodic gravitational potential U_0(x) in the x-direction normal to the microgrooves. By varying the microgroove patterns on the substrate, we generated the potential U_0(x) with different functional forms. By analyzing the large amount of particle trajectories, we arrived at a unified statistical description of activity-assisted escape dynamics and the transport of micromotors across complex potential landscapes. We found that the escape dynamics of slow-rotating micromotors across a potential landscape can be described by an effective potential, U_eff(x;F_0), once the self-propulsion force, F_0, is included in the potential under the fixed-angle approximation. Our investigations into synthetic micromotors across different potential landscapes provided a quantitative understanding of the interplay between the self-propulsion force F_0, spatial confinement by the external potential U_0(x), and thermal noise, as well as their effects on activity-assisted escape dynamics and directed transport of micromotors across complex potential landscapes, such as those found in living cells. Due to the COVID-19 pandemic from 2021 to 2023, the PI’s group could not attend in-person international and regional conferences. The research activities reported here were primarily conducted using existing equipment. No major equipment purchases were made, and the funds were mainly allocated to support research staff.

16300421.label: Major findings and research outcome
16300421.value: Emergent Mechanics of a Networked Multivalent Protein Condensate. As protein interactions become more complex with increasing numbers of components (such as those in living cells), their condensates are expected to exhibit novel mechanical behaviors beyond those of simple one- or two-component protein condensates, which behave like Maxwell fluids. Here, we demonstrate the emergent mechanics of a functional multivalent condensate reconstituted with six postsynaptic density proteins. The measured relaxation modulus and protein mobility indicate that most proteins in the condensate (80%) are mobile and diffuse through a dynamically cross-linked network formed by the remaining (20%) non-mobile scaffold proteins. This percolating structure gives rise to two distinct relaxation modes at different timescales, comparable to those observed in cells. The long-time power-law rheology, with an exponent close to 0.5, is a hallmark of the binding/unbinding dynamics of weak bonds in multivalent protein networks. This work was recently published in Nature Communications (2025). Using the newly developed platform, we also investigated mechanical homeostasis and malfunctions across various cell types, resulting in two publications in Cell (2025) and Molecular Biology of the Cell (2025). Activity-assisted Barrier Crossing of Micromotors over Complex Potential Landscapes. With a thorough analysis of a large volume of micromotor trajectories over different potential landscapes, we found that an effective equilibrium approach can describe the nonequilibrium behavior of micromotors in the limit of long persistence time, once the self-propulsion force F0 of the micromotors is included properly into the activity-dependent potential, U±(x;F₀) = U_0(x) ± aF_0x, for the forward and backward moving particles with U_0(x) being the equilibrium potential and aF_0 the amplitude of the self-propulsion force projected along the x axis. This effective equilibrium approach has been successfully tested for several potential landscapes, including a spatially symmetric trapping potential without a net particle flux [Phys. Rev. E. (Lett.) (2023)], spatially asymmetric ratchet potential with directed particle transport [J. Chem. Phys. (2025)], the enhanced gravitational trapping of bottom-heavy micromotors in a symmetric confining potential [Soft Matter (2024)], and colloidal phase segregation of mixtures of light-powered and wavelength-selective micromotors [Nature (2023)]. Our work thus provided a robust statistical approach to describe non-equilibrium transport of micromotors across complex potential landscapes, such as those found in living cells.

16300421.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16300421.value: Our research activities have successfully addressed the project objectives by providing a unified description of the relaxation modulus for protein condensates, living cells, and monolayer cysts. The experimental framework developed from this study lays the groundwork for future investigations into more complex biological materials. Because the relaxation modulus of biomaterials contains six profiling parameters, characterizing the mechanical state of cells and tissues involves a large parameter space to explore. Up to now, we have studied only a few carefully selected systems. We aim to leverage our new analytical and experimental capabilities to systematically investigate the mechanical properties of a wide range of living systems, from cancer cells to tissues and organoids. We will identify the correlation between the viscoelasticity of living matter, as measured by AFM, and the corresponding microstructural evolution of the biomaterials, which can be visualized simultaneously using fluorescence confocal microscopy. This mechano-structural correlation is crucial for bridging the gap between the biochemical behavior of individual proteins and other biomolecules and the macroscopic mechanical laws governing living matter. We plan to seek additional funding to support this initiative.

16300421.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16300421.value: This research project investigated the emergent mechanics of living matters, including normal and cancerous breast cells, monolayer cysts, and protein condensates, and how the material properties affect health and disease. Using advanced techniques such as atomic force microscopy (AFM), we studied the common features and specific characteristics of these biomaterials. We found that the stiffness and flexibility of these materials can be described by a common relaxation modulus determined primarily by the response of mobile proteins and percolating networks to the applied forces over time. By comparing normal and cancerous breast cells, we discovered that cancer cells are softer but generate stronger internal stresses, aiding their movement and spread. Additionally, we investigated the mechanical response of a model protein condensate that mimics the structures found in brain cells. This system helped us understand how proteins interact to create unique mechanical properties. By providing a clearer understanding of the mechanical properties of proteins, cells, and tissues, our research not only advances scientific knowledge but also has potential applications in medicine and biotechnology. Our findings were published in high-impact journals, underscoring their significance within the growing fields of biological physics and mechanobiology.

16300521.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16300521.value: Concurrent up and down regulations of multiple mRNAs in an individual cell are the key events that determine many biological processes in cells, including cell differentiation and stimuli response. Synthetic tools that can mimic such regulation have great values for both basic and applied research, such as forming tissue chips with refined cell distribution for drug screening. Photoriboswitches can sense light to control mRNAs in a spatial-temporal manner, but the currently ones only allow either up or down mRNA regulation, unable to fulfill the need for bidirectional manipulation of mRNAs. To address this research gap, here we propose a new type of photoriboswitch that enables the use of a single light illumination to create mixed populations of up and down regulated mRNAs in mammalian cells. Natural mRNAs are regulated by RNA binding proteins (RBPs) that recruiting regulatory proteins to the mRNAs. In our previous work, we have used modified nucleotide to enable strong binding between RBPs and mRNAs. Rooted from this result, we found that RBP fusion with an activator protein can substantially up regulates mRNA, while the RBP alone or fusion with non-functional bulky motifs down regulate mRNA. On the other hand, we developed two independent light-controlled systems that utilize dimerization of light sensors to either bring two protein splicing motifs in place or dislocate them. As a result, light can induce or inhibit protein fusion formation. These preliminary results lead to our hypothesis that a photoriboswitch integrating both of the light controlled systems can inversely tune the fusion of two RBPs with activator protein to achieve bidirectional regulation of two sets of mRNAs under a single light illumination. In the proposed research, we will focus on screening light sensors and splicing motifs with low cross-reactivity to enable both light-controlled systems work independently in the same cell. We will then construct and optimize model bidirectional photoriboswitch. Importantly, the performance of the proposed photoriboswitch to bidirectionally regulate mRNAs and to perturb cellular process, such as programmed cell death, will be evaluated. The proposed advanced photoriboswitch enables bidirectional regulations of multiple mRNAs by a single light signal, substantially broaden the scope of mRNA manipulation. The novel bidirectional light-controlled machinery and the one-input two-output riboswitch design grant the proposed research high novelty. We believe the proposed research is significant for studying mRNA dynamics, for inspiring ribogenetic engineering, and for advanced cell manipulation for therapeutic and pharmaceutical purposes. 細胞在感應到生物信號時常會同時增強一些mRNA的蛋白質表達而抑制另一些mRNA的蛋白質表達。這種雙向調控機制決定著許多重要的細胞功能，包括細胞分化和刺激響應等。研發具有雙向調控機制的合成生物學工具從而精準操控細胞功能在醫藥研究領域有很重要的意義。感光mRNA控制迴路是一種通過感應外部光照調節細胞內目標蛋白質表達的合成生物學工具。因光照的可操作性強，這類迴路有廣泛的應用潛力。然而現有的感光mRNA控制迴路僅可以做到增強或抑制的單向蛋白質表達調控。我們在這裡提出一種新型感光mRNA控制迴路設計，可以在感應一種光照的條件下，同時增強和抑制不同的蛋白質表達。這種設計通過巧妙的序列設計使兩種調控蛋白質元件在感光的情況下發生不同的剪切。剪切後的兩個元件分別對兩組mRNA控制迴路產生反向調控作用。這種設計1）通過一個上游信號產生相反的兩個下游信號；2）拓寬了感光迴路的實用範圍；3）巧妙的將蛋白質剪切技術與mRNA控制迴路結合；4）展示了一種新的合成生物學工具設計。前期工作已分別證實了兩個元件在感光前後的剪切變化，以及初步驗證了mRNA控制迴路表達增強與抑制的調控機制。我們相信本項目將展現一種全新的mRNA控制迴路設計思路，拓寬這類合成生物學工具在實際應用中的前景。

16300621.label: Project Objectives
16300621.value: Construct a score-type test statistic for a change-point with a threshold simultaneously in a general class of time series models and study its limiting distribution under the null hypothesis and its local power under the local alternative. 16300621.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16300621.value: 本项目将发展同时检验一般类型时间序列模型中变点与门限的一般框架。为此目标，我们将构造一个一般的联合score-型检验统计量。在原假设下，此统计量应该依分布收敛于两参数的高斯过程的最大值，并且它的分布将不依赖于模型参数。在局部对立假设下，我们的统计量应该有非零的效力。在此基础上，我们将研究关于多变点与一个门限的统计量，并建立它的极限理论。我们将制作有关统计量的临界值表格。我们将进行大量的广泛的模拟实验以研究该统计量在有限样本下的可行性。我们将用本项目发展而来的理论与方法来分析各种经济与金融数据，特别是与香港有关的数据。我们期望本项目能为未来时间序列的变点与门限问题提供一个新的方向。

16300621.label: Realisation of objectives
16300621.value: We first investigated the supremum-type score test for the single-index model against a threshold single-index model. It is shown that the test weakly converges a maxima of a Gaussian process under the null hypothesis. The bootstrap method is used to tackle the bias problem and provide the p-values of our test statistic. In addition, we established a sufficient condition for the ergodicity of the general multiple threshold ARMA model. We then proposed a winsorized CUSUM approach for testing the change-point in the heavy-tailed univariate/multivariate time series. We begin by investigating the winsorized CUSUM process and deriving the limiting distributions of the Kolmogorov-Smirnov test and the Self-normalized test under the null hypothesis. Our tests are shown to exhibit a power approaching to one for both fixed and local alternatives. Furthermore, we studied the winsorized-mean-based least squares estimator (WLSE) for the change point and demonstrated that its limiting distribution is exactly the minimizer of a random walk. Additionally, the LSE of both means before and after change-point are shown to be asymptotically normal. Our framework is quite general and its assumption is very weak. This enables the application of our tests and estimation theory not only to linear time series but also to nonlinear time series, such as TAR and G-GARCH processes. To evaluate the performance of our procedures, we conducted simulation studies and provide two real examples from financial markets. The empirical evidence supports the effectiveness of our proposed procedures for testing and dating change-points in heavy-tailed time series. We finally developed a framework of testing for a change-point with threshold simultaneously in a general class of time series models. The proposed test is based on the sequential empirical process marked by certain scores. Under the null hypothesis of no change-point and threshold, it is established that the test statistic converges to the maximum of a two-parameter Gaussian process and the limiting distribution is model parameter-free. The test is shown to have nontrivial local power under local alternatives. Furthermore, two test statistics are constructed to test for no change-point against m change-points with threshold and for m change-points against (m + 1) change-points with threshold, respectively. Both tests are asymptotically free of model parameters. Simulation studies and real examples were given to illustrate the finite-sample performance and practical potential of the proposed tests To explore the possibility of extending our approach to the non-stationary time series, we carried out the following research: (1). We studied the full rank least squares estimator (FLSE) and reduced rank least squares estimator (RLSE) of the heavy-tailed and partially non-stationary ARMA model with the tail index in (0,2). It is shown that the rate of convergence of the FLSE related to the long-run parameters is n (sample size) and that related to the short-term parameters are n^{1/\alpha}\tilde{L}(n) and $n$, respectively, when $\alpha \in (1,2)$ and $\in (0,1)$. Its limiting distribution is a stochastic integral in terms of two stable random processes when $\alpha \in (0,2)$ for the long-run parameters and is a functional of some stable processes when $\alpha \in (1,2)$ for the short-run parameters. Based on FLSE, we derived the asymptotic properties of the RLSE. (2). We showed that he rate of convergence of the FLSE related to the long-run parameters in vector error correction (VEC) model is n (sample size) and its limiting distribution is a stochastic integral in terms of two stable random processes when the tail index α ∈ (0, 2). Furthermore, we showed that the rate of convergence of the FLSE related to the short-term parameters is n1/α ̃L(n) and its limiting distribution is a functional of two stable processes when α ∈ (1, 2). Simulation study is carried out to demonstrate the performance of both estimators. (3). We studied the unit root with the error following a short-memory linear process of GARCH noises which tail-index in (0, 2) and = 2, and (2, \infty) (corresponding to the heavy-tailed GARCH, IGARCH and the finite variance GARCH respectively). The limiting distribution of the Dickey-Fuller (DF) unit-root test is shown to be a functional of two stable processes when index in (0, 2) and a functional of a standard Brownian motion when index in [2, \infty). Since the limit distribution contains some nuisance parameters, it is difficult, if not impossible, to be estimated. This is especially the case when index in (1,2). To solve this problem, we propose an m-out-of-n centered residual-based block bootstrap (RBB), which is shown to have the same limit distribution as that of DF test and can be applied to both finite-variance and infinite-variance cases. Simulation studies and a real data analysis show that this RBB approach works well. To explore the possibility of extending our approach to the ARCH-type time series, we carried out the following research: (1).We studied the self-weighted least squares estimator (SWLSE) of the ARMA model with GARCH noises. It is shown that the SWLSE is consistent and asymptotically normal when the GARCH noise does not have a finite fourth moment. Using the residuals from the estimated ARMA model, it is shown that the residual-based quasi-maximum likelihood estimator (QMLE) for the GARCH model is consistent and asymptotically normal. Using the SWLSE and residual-based QMLE as the initial estimators, the local QMLE for ARMA-GARCH model is asymptotically normal via an one-step iteration. (2).We studied the autoregressive and moving average (ARMA) model with time-functional variance (TFV) noises, called the ARMA-TFV model. We first establish the consistency and asymptotic normality of its least squares estimator (LSE). The Wald tests and portmanteau tests are constructed based on the theory for variable selection and model checking. (3).We extended the noncausal autoregressive models by introducing noncausality into the variance component, allowing the volatility to depend on future prices as well, and refer to this model as the noncausal AR-ARCH model. We develop a quasi-maximum likelihood estimation method and establish its asymptotic properties. Building on this, we propose three hypothesis testing statistics to determine whether the data exhibits a noncausal AR structure and whether the innovation term follows a noncausal ARCH model. The simulation results demonstrate the consistency of the parameter estimation as well as the good size control and high power of the hypothesis tests in detecting noncausal structures. (4). We extended the double-well potential to a three-parameter model in order to capture the momentum and reversal effects in stock price dynamics. The proposed model is characterized by three parameters that control momentum, reversal, and volatility. By varying these parameters, the model can represent two distinct price patterns: (i) a mean-reverting pattern with a unimodal distribution, and (ii) a momentum pattern with abimodal distribution. We develop an estimation method and establish its asymptotic properties, along with a simulation study to evaluate its finite sample performance. An empirical application using high-frequency data is provided to demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed model in analyzing price.

16300621.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16300621.value: This project has developed a general framework for the simultaneous testing of a change-point with a threshold in a general class of time series models. A general joint score-type test have be constructed for this purpose. It was shown that the test statistic converges to the maxima of a two-parameter Gaussian process under the null hypothesis and its limiting distribution is model parameter-free. Our test has a nontrivial local power under local alternatives. Furthermore, we extended this type of test statistics for multiple change-points with a threshold in time series models and establish their limiting theory. The critical values of our test statistics have been tabulated. We have carried out an extensive simulation study to assess the performance of our test statistic in finite samples. This project has applied the new theory and approach to analyze various economic and financial data.

16300921.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16300921.value: The central theme of this proposed study will be to develop a new synthetic approach for the collective total syntheses of several sarpagine/macroline indole alkaloids, which are biologically active natural products that may have therapeutic utility (e.g. anti-cancer drug development). This family of secondary metabolites are structurally complex and pose a significant synthetic challenge. Although many synthetic methods have been documented for bioactive indole alkaloids, their highly potent bioactivity means that the development of new and efficient methodologies that facilitate or simplify the total synthesis remains of paramount importance. In this proposed project, we will develop a new sequential reaction that involves the aza-Achmatowicz rearrangement (AAR) and aza-Prins cyclization (APC) to generate synthetically useful 9-azabicyclo[3.3.1]nonanes (9-ABN), which are present in sarpagine/macroline indole alkaloids. Our preliminary study has verified that this new sequential reaction (AAR-APC) provides access to 9-ABN and we will comprehensively study the effects of various promoters (Lewis acids or Bronsted acids) and substitution effects of alkenes on its efficiency and relative stereochemistry. To showcase the synthetic utility of our AAR-APC-based approach, six representative bioactive 9-ABN-containing indole alkaloids: macroline, alstonerine, macrocarpine A, sarpagine, vellosimine, and pericyclivine are chosen as targets for collective total synthesis using our sequential AAR-APC approach. The synthetic route for these alkaloids is flexible and efficient, which will allow for rapid access to a library of sarpagine/macroline indole alkaloid natural products and analogues to evaluate their biological activities and therapeutic applicability. In summary, we will perform collective total syntheses of sarpagine/macroline indole alkaloids based on our newly-established sequential AAR-APC methodology. The findings from this study will have a significant impact on the chemistry and biology of indole alkaloids. 本擬議研究的中心主題是開發一種新的合成方法，用於合成若干sarpagine/macroline生物鹼的集體總合成。這些生物活性天然產品可能具有治療效用（例如抗癌藥物開發），但是這種二次代謝物家族結構複雜，構成重大的合成挑戰。雖然許多生物活性生物鹼的合成方法已經有文獻報到，然而它們非常有效的生物活性意味著開發或簡化總合成的新的高效方法仍然至關重要。在這個擬議的專案中，我們將開發一個新的連續反應體系:氮雜-Achmatowicz重新排列 （AAR） 和氮雜-Prins環化反應（APC），以產生在合成上非常有用的 9-azabicyclo[3.3.1] 非烷 （9-ABN），它們存在於Sarpagine/Macroline生物鹼中。我們的初步研究已經證實，這種新的連續反應 （AAR-APC） 可以快速的獲得 9-ABN骨架， 我們將全面研究各種促進劑 （路易斯酸或布朗斯特德酸） 的影響和烯烴取代基的作用、效率和相對立體化學問題。為了展示我們基於 AAR-APC 的方法的合成效用，我們選擇六種具有代表性的含 9-ABN 生物鹼：macroline, alstonerine, macrocarpine A, sarpagine, vellosimine, and pericyclivine，作為使用我們連續 AAR-APC 方法進行集體總合成的目標。這些生物鹼的合成路線是靈活和高效的，這將允許快速訪問Sarpagine/Macroline天然產物和類似物庫，以評估其生物活性和治療適用性。總之，我們將根據我們新建立的連續 AAR-APC 方法，對Sarpagine/Macroline生物鹼進行集體總合成。這項研究的結果將對鞋底生物鹼的化學和生物學產生重大影響。

16300921.label: Realisation of objectives
16300921.value: The three objectives have been fully achieved with publication of the work in Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2023, 62, e202311671. Objective 1: To develop the first sequential aza-Achmatowicz rearrangement/aza-Prins cyclization for the preparation of synthetically useful 9-azabicyclo[3.3.1]nonanes (9-ABN). To examine our hypothesis of the intramolecular aza-Prins cyclization (APC) of aza-Achmatowicz rearrangement (AAR) products, we first synthesized the model compound and carried out aza-Achmatowicz rearrangement on a gram scale using our Oxone-KBr green protocol to provide 3-piperidinone hemiaminal, which was subjected to various Lewis acids for identification of conditions that promoted the hypothetical intramolecular aza-Prins cyclization. We identified BiBr3 as the effective Lewis acid for the first sequential aza-Achmatowicz rearrangement/aza-Prins cyclization to provide 9-azabicyclo[3.3.1]nonanes (9-ABN) in 87% yield. The molecular structure was confirmed by X-ray diffraction analysis. Having optimized the reaction conditions, we examined the scope of the reaction by testing >20 substrates bearing different substituted alkenes or alkynes as the π-component in the aza-Prins cyclization, which delivered 9-ABN in 20-88% yields. Finally, we designed a substrate with a tethered phenyl group to intercept the carbocation generated in the APC reaction as an intermediate and achieved a cascade cyclization, which was similar to the well-established polyene cyclization. After initiation of aza-Prins reaction, subsequent Friedel–Crafts-type cyclization occurred to afford the tetracyclic compound in 54% yield. The relative structure was confirmed by X-ray diffraction analysis (CCDC: 2279074). A small set of substituents (Me, OMe, and phenyl) on the benzene ring were also explored and comparable good yields were observed. This preliminary cascade cyclization was encouraging and is expected to be extended to other substrates for the construction of complex polycyclic alkaloid compounds. Objective 2: To achieve a collective total synthesis of macroline-type indole alkaloids based on this novel aza-Achmatowicz rearrangement/aza-Prins cyclization. Having established the BiBr3-promoted intramolecular aza-Prins cyclization of AAR products for rapid construction of the 9-ABN core, we embarked on its application to the total synthesis of indole alkaloids through Fischer indolization of the 9-ABN under acidic conditions. We first concentrated our efforts on suaveoline Alkaloids: Suaveoline, norsuaveoline, and macrophylline. Our unified synthesis started with enantiomerically enriched 9-ABN, which was obtained in a decagram amount in 79% yield by our newly established AAR–APC method from enantiomerically pure furfuryl amide. The total syntheses of suaveoline and norsuaveoline were achieved in only 6 steps, while the total synthesis of macrophylline required additional three steps. the relative and absolute configurations of our synthetic(-)-macrophylline were further substantiated by single crystal X-ray diffraction analysis (CCDC: 2278457). Objective 3: To accomplish the collective total synthesis of sarpagine-type indole alkaloids based on this novel aza-Achmatowicz rearrangement/aza-Prins cyclization. We exploited the tetracyclic indole-fused 9-ABN intermediates for the unified synthesis of sarpagine alkaloids: (+)-Na-methyl-16-epipericyclivine (5 steps), (+)-affinisine (6 steps), and (+)-normacusine B (6 steps). All spectroscopic data of our synthetic natural products were consistent with those reported in the literature. Clarification of spending deviations on staffing. Research staff budget was $364,016 and the actual expenditure for research staff was $550,564. The primary driver of the variance in staffing expenses is a strategic re-allocation of personnel resources, undertaken to ensure the successful and timely delivery of the project's research objectives. These changes were necessary due to unforeseen scientific opportunities and challenges encountered during the project lifecycle. Research is inherently dynamic and our project yielded an unexpected challenge that required a specialized skilled chemist to pursue. Original Plan: The approved budget allocated funds for one research assistant (RPg) for 36 months]. Actual Implementation: During the project, we identified a need for a more diverse skill set and a different level of seniority. Instead of one RPg, we hired Postdoctoral Fellow (Dr. MA, Shiqiang) to accelerate the progress of the project, to elevate the level of research quality, and to accomplish the project timely (collective total synthesis of six indole alkaloid natural products). Justification: While the total cost may differ from the budget, this revised structure provided greater overall productivity and addressed the project's actual needs more effectively than the originally proposed model. In summary, the variances in staffing expenditures are a direct result of our adaptive management approach to a dynamic research environment. The changes were strategically implemented to overcome challenges, seize emergent opportunities, and ultimately maximize the scientific output and success of the project funded by the RGC.

16300921.label: Major findings and research outcome
16300921.value: a) Development of the Aza-Achmatowicz Rearrangement Followed by Aza-Prins Cyclization (AAR-APC Strategy). Core Innovation: this research project introduce the first intramolecular aza-Prins cyclization of unstable AAR products, overcoming their tendency to aromatize into pyridines under acidic conditions. BiBr3 serves a dual role as a Lewis acid (to activate the hemiaminal in AAR products) and a bromide nucleophile source (to trap the carbocation intermediate). This methodology expands the synthetic utility of AAR, previously limited to reductions or simple additions at the hemiaminal carbon. It provides a rapid, enantioselective route to highly functionalized 9-azabicyclo[3.3.1]nonanes (9-ABNs), a "privileged" core in alkaloids and drug molecules. The method tolerates functional groups (e.g., ketones, esters, sulfonamides) and enables gram-scale synthesis, making 9-ABNs accessible for further elaboration via substitutions, eliminations, or couplings. (Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2023, 62, e202311671) b) Application of this newly-established methodology to Total Syntheses of Indole Alkaloids. The 9-ABN core was advanced via Fischer indolization to a tetracyclic indole-fused intermediate (confirmed by X-ray, CCDC: 2263258). This common platform enabled divergent syntheses. Six enantioselective total syntheses demonstrate the method's power, positioning it as a valuable tool for natural product synthesis and drug discovery. (Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2023, 62, e202311671) c) Green chemistry (Oxone-halide) used for aza-Achmatowicz rearrangement in this project stimulated our group’s continuous interest in developing new green chemistry methods for organic reactions. We have discovered that Oxone-halide could be used as a green alternative method for (i) halogenative semipinacol rearrangement (J. Org. Chem. 2023, 88, 504-512), (ii) halogenation of indoles (J. Org. Chem. 2023, 88, 11497-11503), and (iii) ipso-bromination of arylboronic acids (Org. Lett. 2024, 26, 5151-5156). By merging our Fenton-bromide system (in water) with the Suzuki reaction (in water), this new formal oxidative Suzuki coupling reaction was demonstrated with 34 examples and tolerated with many common functional groups. In addition, we showcase the extension of this strategy to two cross-dehydrogenative couplings (oxidative Heck and oxidative Sonogashira), which further expands the utility of this green strategy in organic synthesis. (Green Chem. 2023, 25, 1345-1350).

16300921.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16300921.value: Biological Relevance: The synthesized alkaloids belong to families with >200 members, many showing cytotoxicity against cancer cells and potential to overcome multidrug resistance. The method facilitates access for biological evaluation. The AAR-APC strategy is modular and expected to apply to other macroline/sarpagine alkaloids. It mimics biosynthetic pathways (e.g., Pictet-Spengler) while offering synthetic flexibility. If further funding is available, a library of indole alkaloids will be synthesized and evaluated for their biological activity. In the meantime, further extension of this new synthetic strategy is made to other indole alkaloids.

16300921.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16300921.value: Tropical plants like Rauwolfia produce over 200 sarpagine and macroline indole alkaloids—potent compounds used in folk medicine for cancer, infections, and malaria. Their complex 9-azabicyclo[3.3.1]nonane (9-ABN) core has made lab synthesis slow and limited. This project (RGC Ref No. 16300921), led by Prof. Rongbiao Tong at HKUST, proposed a breakthrough: use eco-friendly furfural (from plant waste) and combine two reactions—aza-Achmatowicz rearrangement (AAR) and a brand-new intramolecular aza-Prins cyclization (APC)—to quickly build the 9-ABN. Early tests showed metal bromides (like BiBr₃) gave up to 87% yield of the core structure, confirmed by X-ray. The plan: 1. Phase I – Perfect the method across different building blocks. 2. Phase II – Use the 9-ABN to make multiple alkaloids via Fischer indolization, then test them for antibacterial and anticancer activity. By 2023, the team succeeded: they published the first AAR-APC method and completed six total syntheses (9–14 steps each), including suaveoline and normacusine B. This faster, flexible route now enables drug discovery from these rare natural medicines.

16301221.label: Project Objectives
16301221.value: To synthesize the major amino acid-conjugated metabolites of CS, the protein and DNA adducts of CS, and the corresponding stable isotope-labeled derivatives for use as reference standards and internal standards in liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometric (LC-MS/MS) analysis. To develop sample pretreatment and instrumental analysis methods for quantifying CS metabolites and CS adducts of DNA and proteins. Building on our significant experience in developing LC-MS/MS methods for bioanalysis, we propose to develop sensitive LC-MS/MS methods to rigorously discover and quantify CS metabolites and associated DNA and protein adducts and to investigate their potential use as biomarkers of exposure. To determine the exposure concentration- and duration-dependence of CS gas on the formation of protein adducts in vitro and in cultured human lung and liver cells. We propose to incubate cells and purified proteins with CS and its major metabolite, 2-chlorobenzaldehyde. After enzymatic digestion, CS-protein adducts in the purified proteins and in protein isolated from CS-exposed cells will then be quantitated using LC-MS/MS coupled with stable isotope-dilution methods. To identify and rigorously quantify the CS-related DNA adducts in purified DNA and cells exposed to CS and its major metabolites, with the goals of identifying the potential health effect associated with CS gas exposure.

16301221.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16301221.value: 2-Chlorobenzalmalononitrile (CS) is one of the main active components of tear gas used by many police forces worldwide for riot control. The extensive use of tear gas has raised serious concern about the health risks associated with CS gas exposure. However, the molecular toxicology of CS is poorly understood. The aims of the proposed research are to investigate the potential health effects associated with CS gas exposure and to develop biomarkers of CS exposure. This project addresses the development and application of ultra-high performance liquid chromatography- and gas chromatography-coupled mass spectrometry-based analytical methods of high sensitivity and selectivity to investigate the metabolism of CS and the ability of CS or its metabolites to form DNA and protein adducts, as well as to develop the identified metabolites and/or protein adducts as biomarkers of exposure. Through these analyses, it is anticipated that the potential health risk of CS gas exposure can be better understood, and biomarkers associated with the exposure can be identified and used to assess the exposure level. 催淚煙是各國警察部隊常用作控制暴亂的裝備，其主要活性成分包括2-氯苯亞甲基丙二腈 (CS)。廣泛使用催淚煙引起了大眾對接觸CS 氣體所帶來的健康風險的關注。然而，人們對CS的分子毒理學了解甚少。本研究旨在研究與 CS 氣體暴露相關的潛在健康影響並開發其暴露的生物標誌物。此項目致力於開發和應用基於超高效液相色譜-和氣相色譜-質譜聯用的高靈敏度和高選擇性的分析方法，以研究CS的代謝及CS或其代謝物與DNA或蛋白質形成加合物的能力，並開發已鑑定的代謝物及/或蛋白質加合物作為暴露的生物標誌物。通過這些分析，我們可以更好地了解 CS 氣體暴露的潛在健康風險，並可識別與暴露相關的生物標誌物，將其用於評估暴露水平。

16301221.label: Realisation of objectives
16301221.value: With strong support from the Research Grants Council (RGC) of Hong Kong, this project was successfully completed, achieving all objectives outlined in section 5.1. In brief, we synthesized major amino acid-conjugated metabolites of CS, specifically 2-(2-chlorophenyl)thiazolidine-4-carboxylic acid, along with its stable isotope-labeled derivatives to serve as reference and internal standards for liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometric (LC-MS/MS) analysis. Following this, we developed sample pretreatment and LC-MS/MS methods to measure CS metabolites, including 2-chlorobenzaldehyde (2-CBA), and to analyze CS adducts in DNA and proteins. Using these synthesized standards and methods, we determined the concentration- and duration-dependent effects of CS gas on the formation of 2-CBA and protein adducts in vitro, as well as in cultured human lung and liver cells. We also quantified CS-related DNA adducts in purified DNA and cells exposed to both CS and 2-CBA. For further details, please refer to the attached published research paper. Throughout the project, we trained one Ph.D. student and published three peer-reviewed papers related to the funded project (see Part C: Research Output for the published papers). Additionally, we are nearing completion of another research project focusing on CS-DNA adducts and are currently preparing a paper documenting our findings in DNA adduct analysis.
