16301221.label: Major findings and research outcome
16301221.value: Using our developed sample preparation techniques along with liquid chromatographic and mass spectrometric methods, we synthesized standards and internal standards to investigate the behavior of 2-chlorobenzalmalononitrile (CS). Our findings revealed that CS undergoes rapid hydrolysis to form 2-chlorobenzaldehyde (2-CBA), a highly reactive intermediate. This compound reacts swiftly with endogenous cysteine (Cys) and Cys residues in proteins, resulting in the production of a stable adduct, 2-(2-chlorophenyl)thiazolidine-4-carboxylic acid (ClPh-SPro), in high yield. This stable adduct has the potential to serve as a dosimeter for monitoring CS exposure. Study also showed that the metabolites showed reasonable reactivity to DNA, although the adduct produced is of low stability.

16301221.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16301221.value: While this study has demonstrated that CS metabolites exhibit high reactivity with cysteine, both in protein and metabolite forms, it is possible that CS exposure may also impact enzyme activity and overall body metabolism. Therefore, further research is warranted to investigate the exposure-associated perturbations in metabolic processes and physiological functions. Future studies could utilize a metabolomics approach to comprehensively assess the metabolic alterations resulting from CS exposure, providing deeper insights into its effects on biological systems.

16301221.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16301221.value: Our studies found that CS gas undergoes rapid hydrolysis to produce 2-chlorobenzaldehyde (2-CBA) under physiologically relevant conditions. This reactive intermediate swiftly interacts with cysteine (Cys) in the bloodstream as well as with Cys residues in proteins. While the biological consequences of these reactions are yet to be fully determined, these metabolites and protein adducts hold promise as potential biomarkers for exposure assessment. They could be particularly valuable for evaluating the exposure levels of bystanders who may have been inadvertently exposed to high concentrations of CS gas.

16301321.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16301321.value: 氯和紫外線消毒是常用於污水處理過程中，把病原體濃度降低到安全水平的方法。檢測大腸桿菌或腸球菌在污水的數量，是顯示消毒效果的常用指標。然而，與許多其他細菌物種一樣，大腸桿菌和腸球菌屬的細胞，可以通過進入一種存活但不可被培養(VBNC)的狀態來克服消毒過中壓力。VBNC細胞代謝活躍，但無法在培養基上繁殖。因此，使用常規方法無法檢測到它們，從而導致低估了在污水流出物中仍然存活的大腸桿菌和腸球菌的濃度，而高估了消毒結果。更重要的是，VBNC 細胞可以在消毒效能消失後恢復正常活動和繁殖。因此，在消毒過程中對細菌 在VBNC 狀態的誘發及其後的復蘇是重要的公共衛生問題。本項目將旨在了解在污水消毒過程和隨後排放過程中，細菌對抗氯和紫外線的殺菌效能的分子機制。從長遠來看，所獲得的知識將有助於改善污水消毒策略，並有助於開發新的檢測方法，以便更準確地評估消毒結果。

16301421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16301421.value: The goal of the proposed experimental research is to investigate the effects of nonlinear friction induced by two-phonon processes on the parametric resonance of micromechanical resonators. Micromechanical resonators are widely used as sensors and actuators. By tracking changes in their resonance frequencies, the devices can be used in applications that range from inertial sensing to high-sensitivity force and mass detection. When a mechanical resonator is coupled to an optical, microwave or phonon cavity, the effective linear damping can be modified by one-phonon processes when pumping is applied at the primary sideband of the cavity. By changing the pumping to the secondary sideband to induce two-phonon processes, the damping can be made nonlinear. Both the sign and magnitude of the nonlinear damping is readily tunable by the pumping. The emphasis of the proposed research will be placed on revealing the various mechanisms by which nonlinear friction can affect parametric resonance and the corresponding novel fluctuational phenomena that emerge. Two vibrational modes of a micromechanical resonator will be involved, with driving applied to the secondary sidebands of the mode at the higher frequency. Preliminary measurements indicate that the induced nonlinear friction gives rise to new bifurcation points in parametric resonance. At the critical point where multiple bifurcation points merge together, a wealth of fluctuational phenomena will be explored, including strong noise squeezing and non-Gaussian distribution of the vibration amplitude. When the nonlinear friction is tuned to be positive, the lower vibrational mode is cooled in a non-Boltzmann fashion: Thermal fluctuations are reduced only at large vibration amplitudes while low amplitude vibrations are unaffected. The proposed research will seek to optimize the cooling to improve the phase stability of vibrations. Successful implementation of the proposed projects will not only stimulate new theoretical research and verify the validity of various theoretical approaches, but could also lead to micromechanical detectors of improved sensitivity and functionality. The PI has extensive experience with fluctuational phenomena in micromechanical devices. In the past few years, his group performed a comprehensive investigation on effect of linear and nonlinear friction induced by dynamical backaction on the self-sustained oscillations and the resonant driven response of a mechanical resonator. In this project, the PI will work closely with Prof. Mark Dykman, a theorist at Michigan State University to reveal novel behaviors due to nonlinear friction on the parametric resonance of micromechanical resonators. 我們建議的實驗研究的目標是研究由兩個聲子過程引起的非線性摩擦對微機械諧振器參數共振的影響。微機械諧振器被廣泛用作傳感器和致動器，通過觀察其共振頻率的變化，微機械諧振器可用於從慣性傳感到高精度力和質量的檢測等各種方面。當微機械諧振器與光學、微波或聲子腔耦合時，通過在腔的初級邊帶處施加驅動，引發的單聲子過程可以改變諧振器的有效線性阻尼。而將驅動施加到次級邊帶則可以引發雙聲子過程，從而使阻尼變成非線性。非線性阻尼的正負性和幅度都可以通過驅動力來調節。 提案中研究的重點在揭示非線性摩擦影響參數共振的各種機制以及出現的相應新波動現象。研究將涉及微機械諧振器的兩種振動模式，並在較高頻模式的次級邊帶施加驅動。初步測量表明，非線性摩擦會在參數共振中產生新的分岔點。在多個分岔點匯合的臨界點上，我們將探索大量的波動現象，其中包括強噪聲壓縮和振幅的非高斯分佈。當非線性摩擦被調整為正值時，較低頻模式以非玻爾茲曼方式被冷卻：熱波動的減少僅發生在較大振幅，而處於較小振幅的振動不受影響。擬議的研究將尋求優化冷卻以提高振動的相位穩定性。計劃課題的成功實施不僅將激發新的理論研究並驗證各種理論方法的有效性，而且還可能促進微機械探測器的靈敏度和功能性進一步提升。 主要研究者在微機械設備中的波動現象方面擁有豐富的經驗。在過去幾年中，他的團隊對動態反作用力引起的線性和非線性摩擦對機械諧振器的自發振盪和諧振驅動響應的影響進行了全面研究。在這個項目中，主要研究者將與密歇根州立大學的理論家 Mark Dykman 教授密切合作，以揭示出由於微機械諧振器參數共振的非線性摩擦引起的新現象。

16301521.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16301521.value: The interest in models describing relationships between various objects, individuals or other entities has always existed in scientific and decision making processes. This is certainly true for data that arise from advances in technology, for instance social networks, online shopping profiles, brain connectome data scans or complex protein protein interaction models. These are situations where networks, and the relationships indicated within these networks, are the primary objects of interest. Statistical analysis of such models present extra challenges. In addition to the complex nature of graphs, one would like to capture the behavior of continually updated information. Furthermore, one is interested in modeling/prediction of latent features that might contribute to various observed outcomes. A challenge is that from a modelling perspective it is oftentimes unrealistic to pre-select a certain number, or types of, features. Bayesian Machine Learning and Bayesian nonparametric statistical models and methods for relational models and random graphs/networks have been developed to begin to address these issues. Another issue that arises is that while much statistical analysis about networks focuses on a single network, there has been recent interest on the statistical analysis of multiple networks. In this work we exploit connections between a class of relational models and a certain class of exchangeable random graph models that can be chosen to exhibit sparsity. In particular, we exploit a duality between what are known as Indian Buffet Processes and classes of either edge exchangeable or vertex exchangeable sparse networks. We describe how this leads to models and sampling methods for such models and natural variants. In addition, we explore the construction of nested families of graphs via combinatorial manipulations, which not only lead to a rich new class of models but may also be relevant to Natural Language processing applications. We will explore the properties of other constructions related to hierarchical topic models. From a practical point of view, we intend to examine interesting datasets, that may be viewed as multi-graphs, from a Bayesian perspective. Examples of such datasets include the Panama papers or Paradise papers which consists of millions of documents arising from dubious offshore transactions. 在科學決策過程中，描述各種對象、個人或其他實體之間關係的模型總是起到關鍵作用。這點在隨工程領域的發展而產生的數據中表現的尤為突出，比如社交網路、線上購物畫像、大腦連接組數據掃描及複雜蛋白質交互模型等。在這些場合下，網路及網路間關係是我們的主要研究對象，針對這些模型的統計分析向我們提出了新的挑戰。在圖的複雜性基礎上，人們希望可以利用持續更新的信息。進一步地，人們希望能對那些對各種觀測結果產生影響的潛在特徵進行建模和預測。然而，從建模角度來看，預設一定數量和類型的潛在特徵通常是不現實的，這給我們提出了挑戰。關於以上問題和挑戰，已有文獻開始提出“關聯模型”和“隨機圖/網路”的貝葉斯機器學習和貝葉斯非參數統計模型及方法。這裡伴隨產生的另一個問題是，儘管大量的網路統計分析集中於討論單一網路，最近的文獻已開始關注多個網路的統計分析。在本項目中，我們將利用一類關聯模型和一類可交換隨機圖模型之間的聯繫，其中，我們可以選擇使可交換隨機圖模型具有稀疏性。特別地，我們將利用現在領域裡廣為人知的印度自助餐過程（ Indian Buffet Processes）和一類邊可交換或節點可交換稀疏網路之間的對偶關係。我們將刻畫如何通過這種對偶關係進行建模及得到這些模型及其變種下的抽樣方法。同時，我們進一步通過組合學方法探究構造一系列子類圖，這可以幫助我們得出一類新的豐富的且與自然語言處理應用有關的模型。我們也會探究其他的和分層主題有關的模型的性質。從應用的觀點來看，我們將從貝葉斯視角來研究那些可被視為多重圖的有趣數據集，如含有數以百萬計可疑離岸交易相關文件的巴拿馬文件（Panama papers）、天堂文件（Paradise papers）等。

16301521.label: Realisation of objectives
16301521.value: The project has exceeded expectations, producing 10 papers and supporting PhD thesis research. The research program culminated in a 2025 trilogy of interconnected works that resolve a fundamental open problem in probability theory while demonstrating practical applicability to public health, computational biology, and microbiome analysis. Objective 1 (100%): PHIBP Applications and Extensions The Poisson Hierarchical Indian Buffet Process (PHIBP) was fully developed in James, Lee, and Pandey (2025), "The Poisson Hierarchical Indian Buffet Process," arXiv:2502.01919. This work introduces a new class of species sampling models for complex sparse count data, developing a four-component architecture (I, A, F, Z) with explicit compound Poisson representations via mixed truncated Poisson distributions. The Allocation process emerges as the key conditioning variable enabling tractable posterior inference—making complex hierarchical inference computationally feasible rather than merely theoretically possible. The framework extends classical HIBP theory with explicit posterior distributions and predictive representations. Novel Bayesian definitions of alpha-diversity (Shannon entropy) and beta-diversity (Bray-Curtis) are introduced as random variables with full posterior distributions, avoiding the sensitivity to pseudocount perturbations that plagues competing methods. Applied to microbiome analysis of seafloor basalt data (1,425 unique ASVs across 12 samples with 42% zero counts), the generalized gamma model captures power-law frequency-of-frequency distributions that the gamma model misses, demonstrating robust diversity estimation and prediction of unseen species on challenging real-world data where competing approaches fail. Foundation work includes James (2022), "Single-Block Recursive Poisson–Dirichlet Fragmentations of Normalized Generalized Gamma Processes," Mathematics 10(4), 561 (invited Regazzini Festschrift contribution), which develops Mittag-Leffler Markov chains and nested families of mass partitions under DGM fragmentation—providing the PDGM machinery used throughout subsequent work. Objective 2 (100%): Multiple Graphs, Hierarchical Latent Features, and Posterior Characterizations The (HICRP) models were developed in James, Lee, and Ross (2024), "Network and Interaction Models for Data with Hierarchical Granularity via Fragmentation and Coagulation," arXiv:2408.04866 (under review), addressing network data with hierarchical granularity and connecting Caron-Fox and Hollywood models with generalized gamma graphex representations. A major theoretical achievement is James (2023), "Posterior distributions of Gibbs-type priors," arXiv:2308.14254, which solves the open problem of describing posterior distributions for the general class of α-Gibbs priors—explicitly noted as unsolved by De Blasi et al. (2015). Explicit characterizations for Pitman-Yor and generalized Mittag-Leffler classes were obtained. Additional foundations appear in James, Lee, and Pandey (2024), "Bayesian Analysis of Generalized Hierarchical Indian Buffet Processes," arXiv:2304.05244, developing multi-group sharing mechanisms, and James, Lee, and Pandey (2021), "Posterior distributions for Hierarchical Spike and Slab Indian Buffet processes," arXiv:2103.11407, introducing hierarchical spike-and-slab structure with explicit posterior characterizations. Objective 3 (100%): Nested Graphs via Coagulation and Fragmentation This objective produced the most significant theoretical breakthrough. The coagulation-fragmentation duality problem posed by Pitman (1999)—open for over two decades—was resolved for the first time beyond the two-parameter Poisson-Dirichlet family. James (2025), "Coagulation-Fragmentation Duality of Infinitely Exchangeable Partitions from Coupled Mixed Poisson Species Sampling Models," arXiv:2508.18668, extends the celebrated duality to processes driven by arbitrary non-negative Lévy subordinators. Unprecedented even for the classical case, the duality extends to multi-group settings with J ≥ 1 coupled populations via a novel four-component coupled system built from the PHIBP framework. Section 6 lifts the framework to continuous time via dt ⊗ ν, yielding coupled Λ-Fleming-Viot processes, structured Λ-coalescents, and homogeneous fragmentation processes with simultaneous structural duality preserved at every instant—meaning fine and coarse processes remain locked in dual relationship throughout temporal evolution. Section 7 establishes the cloud duality principle via the h-biased Lévy-Itô coupled duality constructor, demonstrating that coagulation-fragmentation duality is a universal property arising from point-process regrouping on arbitrary Polish spaces. The continuous-time lift extends automatically to all PRM-based constructs—encompassing loop-soups, stable trees, excursion-based processes, ancestral recombination graphs, and abstract geometric objects. The framework is simultaneously generative and inferentially tractable. Supporting this objective, Ho, James, and Lau (2025), "Inverse Clustering of Gibbs Partitions via Independent Fragmentation and Dual Dependent Coagulation Operators," Journal of Applied Probability, extends fragmentation operations beyond the classical family, characterizing laws from FRAG operations on general mass partitions with explicit EPPF calculations. Objective 4 (100%): Real Data Applications Real data applications exceeded original scope, demonstrating the framework is practically executable. The PHIBP paper applies the framework to microbiome data where 42% zero counts and 1,425 ASVs across 12 samples create severe challenges. The hierarchical structure enables cross-sample information borrowing while compound Poisson representations handle extreme sparsity. Posterior predictive distributions provide uncertainty-quantified diversity estimates stable under data perturbation—unlike plug-in estimators with high pseudocount sensitivity. Fong, James, and Lee (2025), "Using PHIBP to Predict Rare Infectious Diseases," arXiv:2512.21005 (invited Springer chapter), demonstrates machine learning capabilities for public health surveillance. Analyzing California data (58 counties, 36 diseases, 2001-2023), the work achieves prediction in regions with zero historical cases through cross-regional information borrowing. The generalized gamma specification consistently outperforms alternatives. Heaukulani, Pandey, and James (2024), "Modelling Financial Volume Curves with Hierarchical Poisson Processes," arXiv:2406.19402 (under review), models intensity functions for financial trading volume curves, demonstrating scalability on NASDAQ stocks including Apple. *This (HKP 2024) project was started under previous RGC funding but was submitted under the current funding, We forgot to acknowledge the current funding and we do so later. PhD Student Training PhD student Abhinav Pandey is developing thesis work on Latent Itemset Allocation using the PHIBP framework, applying hierarchical latent feature models to transaction data and market basket analysis. The work introduces novel diversity measures derived from hierarchical rate structures: Itemset Prevalence, Richness, Similarity, Rarity, Contribution, and Predictive Power. Applications span market basket analysis, topic modeling, and financial volume profiles. Summary The 2025 trilogy represents a unified achievement: the PHIBP paper provides computational machinery demonstrated on challenging microbiome data; the infectious disease chapter demonstrates public health applicability; and the duality paper elevates PHIBP to resolution of a fundamental open problem—while establishing universality principles transforming fragmentation-coalescence duality from special cases into a general design principle for stochastic models across probability theory and its applications.

16301521.label: Major findings and research outcome
16301521.value: The grant produced 10 papers, with three forming an interconnected 2025 trilogy representing the crowning achievement. THE 2025 TRILOGY James, Lee, and Pandey (2025), "The Poisson Hierarchical Indian Buffet Process," arXiv:2502.01919, introduces PHIBP with explicit compound Poisson representations and the novel Allocation process enabling tractable inference. Applied to microbiome data (1,425 ASVs, 12 samples, 42% zeros), demonstrating robust diversity estimation where competing methods fail. Fong, James, and Lee (2025), "Using PHIBP to Predict Rare Infectious Diseases," arXiv:2512.21005 (invited Springer chapter), achieves prediction of disease outbreaks in California counties with zero historical cases through cross-regional information borrowing. James (2025), "Coagulation-Fragmentation Duality," arXiv:2508.18668, resolves Pitman's 1999 open problem, extending the celebrated duality beyond the two-parameter Poisson-Dirichlet family to arbitrary Lévy subordinators and, for the first time, to multi-group settings. Section 7 establishes the cloud duality principle: coagulation-fragmentation duality is a universal property of any PRM-based construct on arbitrary Polish spaces, with continuous-time dynamics extending automatically via dt ⊗ ν. Trilogy Significance: PHIBP provides computational machinery demonstrated on microbiome data; the infectious disease chapter demonstrates public health applicability; the duality paper elevates PHIBP to a resolution of a fundamental open problem while establishing universality principles transforming fragmentation-coalescence duality into a general design principle for stochastic models. ADDITIONAL WORK Two published papers: Ho, James, Lau (2025) in Journal of Applied Probability extending fragmentation theory; James (2022) in Mathematics (Regazzini Festschrift) on PDGM foundations. Four papers under review covering HICRP for networks, financial volume curves, and theoretical extensions. PhD student Abhinav Pandey developing thesis on Latent Itemset Allocation.

16301521.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16301521.value: The resolution of Pitman's duality problem opens fundamentally new research directions. The cloud duality principle demonstrates that coagulation-fragmentation duality is universal—any PRM-based construct on arbitrary Polish spaces inherits a coupled duality architecture with automatic continuous-time lift. This transforms fragmentation-coalescence from special cases into a general design principle. For population genetics, the framework provides the first tractable approach to the Ancestral Recombination Graph, with simultaneous structural duality enabling inference from marginal genealogies. The multi-group extension enables structured population models across demes. Connections to loop-soups, stable trees, and excursion-based processes follow from universality. PhD student Pandey is developing Latent Itemset Allocation for transaction data with novel diversity measures.

16301521.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16301521.value: This research solves a mathematical problem open for over 25 years. The central achievement shows how complex random structures can be simultaneously fragmented and coagulated while maintaining mathematical consistency—like viewing a family tree at different resolutions where all views are locked together by precise mathematical relationships. The key innovation, the Poisson Hierarchical Indian Buffet Process, provides explicit formulas that computers can actually use. We demonstrated this on microbiome data where 42% of observations are zeros and traditional methods fail, and on predicting rare disease outbreaks in California counties with no prior cases. Most remarkably, the framework is universal: it applies to any probabilistic model built from Poisson random measures, with continuous-time dynamics extending automatically. For population genetics, this opens tractable analysis of the Ancestral Recombination Graph, with implications for disease gene mapping and evolutionary inference.

16301621.value: 高價有機碘 - 氧化合物，特別是碘苯氧化物（PhIO），由於其作為氧化劑在有機合成中的多種應用而顯得非常重要。 PhIO 也是一種常用的試劑，用在仿生金屬催化的有機化合物氧化中生成高價金屬-氧類物質。儘管通常認為金屬氧化物是負責催化氧化的活性物質，但令人信服的證據表明，金屬-PhIO 化合物是某些金屬介導的 PhIO 反應中的替代活性氧化物。事實上，最近幾種能夠氧化有機底物的金屬-PhIO 配合物已經被分離出來。然而，控制高價碘配體的氧原子和氫原子轉移反應性的因素尚不清楚。五價碘化合物，例如 2-碘氧基苯甲酸和五價有機碘苯氧化物 (PhIO2)，已在某些有機反應中用作選擇性氧化劑。然而，與它們的 PhIO 類似物相比，含有五價有機碘配體（如 PhIO2）的金屬配合物很少見。在我們最近的工作中，我們開發了一種以氯化鈰 (IV) 為原料合成碘化鈰 (IV) 碘基苯和五價碘基苯配合物的路線。這促使我們合成一系列 Ce-O-I(X)Ar 和 Ce-OI(O)(X)Ar（X = 陰離子基團，Ar = 芳基）配合物並研究碘取代基（X和 Ar) 對金屬結合的高價碘物質的反應性。在這個擬議的研究項目中，我們將合成含有三價和五價碘配體的鈰 (IV) 配合物，並開發新的過渡金屬高價碘配合物的合成路線。我們將高價碘配合物應用到有機化合物的氧化，如硫醚、醇和碳氫化合物氧化。將闡明控制基於高價碘的氧化的速率和選擇性的因素。亞胺碘烷如 PhINR（R = 缺電子基團，如甲苯磺酰基、Ts）因其在金屬催化的氮烯轉移和 C-H 胺化中作為氮烯源的應用而受到關注。雖然在PhINTs 的金屬催化反應中，金屬-PhINTs 加合物已被暗示作為替代活性氧化劑，但很少有金屬-亞胺碘配合物被分離出來。因此，在這個提議的項目中，我們將合成 Ce(IV) 亞胺碘烷配合物，並研究它們的氮烯轉移和氫原子提取反應。

16301721.label: Project Objectives
16301721.value: The overarching goal of the proposed project is to improve numerical weather models' capability to simulate orographic precipitation in gray zones. The gray zone of orographic convection simulation occurs where the grid spacing is approximately 1–10 km. In this resolution range, subgrid-scale (SGS) turbulence and resolved convection strongly interact. Some meteorological institutes have adopted this resolution range for regional weather forecasting. Idealized studies of cloud dynamics and climate change studies also often use similar resolutions. However, because cross-scale interaction becomes prominent in the gray zone, traditional convective and turbulence parameterizations are not entirely valid in this transition zone. We thus focus our investigation on the evaluation, enhancement, and strategic configuration of the SGS process parameterization to improve gray-zone simulations of precipitation over mountainous regions. A unique perspective of this project is our goal to obtain insight into the synergy between terrain and convection gray zones. When the characteristic spatial scale of local mountains is O(1 km), numerical simulations with kilometer-scale grid spacings are in the gray zones of both convection and terrain. Being within the convection gray zone means that traditional cumulus schemes may not be valid to model convection. However, being in the terrain's gray zone implies that mountain flows are likely not fully resolved, and a parameterization is therefore warranted for the accurate representation of SGS processes. This research project will investigate how to resolve this dilemma. Core questions that we will address include: (a) When is convection parameterization necessary for simulating extreme orographic precipitation at the kilometer-scale? (b) How can convection parameterizations be enhanced to improve their suitability to represent three-dimensional turbulence with gray-zone grid spacing? (c) When many options are available, how should the optimal configuration of SGS process schemes be chosen for gray-zone simulations of orographic precipitation? Question (a) will be addressed with realistic and idealized simulations of intense orographic precipitation embedded in a tropical cyclone, a scenario that often affects the South China coast. We will simulate the case of Typhoon Vicente using the Weather Research and Forecast (WRF) model and Cloud Model 1 (CM1). The WRF model will be used for realistic simulations to evaluate the effects of traditional cumulus schemes and updated schemes with scale-awareness. The CM1 will be used for LESs and cloud-resolving simulations to quantify how gray-zone boundaries may depend on mountain geometry and model resolution in orographic convection simulations. Question (b) will be tackled by combining a new parameterization scheme for horizontal turbulence mixing with existing cumulus convection schemes in the WRF model. The dynamic reconstruction model (DRM) has been demonstrated to be a promising gray-zone parameterization of SGS turbulence. Traditional cumulus parameterizations are designed to treat one-dimensional mixing in the vertical direction only; however, the effect of SGS turbulence is three-dimensional in the gray zone. We will use an updated version of DRM, the Reconstruction-based Nonlinear and Anisotropic (RNA) model, to parameterize horizontal turbulence mixing in the gray zone while maintaining convection schemes to represent SGS processes in the vertical direction. We will adjust and calibrate the RNA model to improve simulation accuracy. Question (c) will be solved with physical scheme-based large-ensemble hindcast and machine learning models. The latter will learn strategies from the former to optimize the parameterization configurations. This question is raised because many cumulus parameterization schemes are available in the WRF model, but most are not purposefully designed for the gray zone. We hypothesize that a solution to this situation will be to strategize by selecting SGS scheme configurations according to specific weather regimes. Deep learning is the best tool for this challenging task. We will create large ensembles of weather hindcast with the WRF model using different combinations of cumulus and planetary boundary layer schemes. Deep learning models will be trained to identify the best choices of SGS schemes for given large-scale weather patterns. This approach will maximize the utility value of the community-contributed SGS schemes in the gray zone.

16301721.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16301721.value: Topography modulates atmospheric flows in various ways and significantly influences the spatial patterns and intensity of the precipitation over mountain ranges, which is called orographic precipitation and essential for water resources in mountainous areas and downstream. Orographic extreme events, meanwhile, can cause disasters such as flooding and landslides to disrupt our society. The forecasting of orographic precipitation is thus an essential topic for numerical weather prediction (NWP). With advancing computing power, kilometer-scale resolutions have become increasingly popular in regional NWP, and in global simulations, it has also been experimented with recently. However, kilometer-scale grid spacing puts weather models into numerical simulation gray zones, the resolution range at which particular processes are neither entirely subgrid (i.e., unresolved) nor fully resolved. The application of kilometer-scale resolution for orographic precipitation, in particular, is within the gray zone for deep convection and possibly for complex terrains in certain locations. Partial resolving of flows in gray-zone simulations means that subgrid-scale (SGS) processes actively interact with the larger scales. Thus proper SGS parameterization is critical for accurately representing the cross-scale flow interactions in gray-zone simulations. However, traditional convection schemes designed for substantially finer or coarser grid spacings may use the assumptions that SGS turbulence is dissipative, isotropic, or horizontally homogeneous, none of which is appropriate for the gray-zone resolution. This predicament is the target of the proposed research. We will investigate how the effects of scale-aware convection schemes may differ from others in gray-zone simulations of the intense orographic rainfall embedded in a tropical cyclone environment. To make column-based convection schemes, which assumes horizontal homogeneity, more appropriate for gray zones, we will add a new component to model the horizontal mixing due to SGS turbulence. Idealized large-eddy simulations (LESs) and cloud-resolving simulations will be conducted to quantify the relation between the reliability of explicit convection, model resolution, and mountain geometry. We will also use machine learning to optimize the parameterization configuration according to specific weather patterns strategically. Overall, this project will advance our understanding of the gray zones of orographic precipitation and enhance our gray-zone prediction techniques. 地形能夠影響大氣運動進而影響山地區域降水的強度和分佈。地形降水是山地區域及下游的重要水源。但山洪和滑坡的極端事件也會為社會帶來負面影響。因而準確預測山地降水是數值天氣預報的重要任務。 目前隨超級計算機的發展，數值天氣預報多使用數千米解像度的計算網格。但這一解像度被稱為數值模擬的灰區，因為渦旋只能被部分解析，網格尺度與次網格尺度流體在這一解像度下有很強的相互作用。地形的變化也將這一問題變得更加複雜。傳統的次網格尺度湍流參數化常假設耗散性、各向同性與水平均一。這些假設在灰區並不很好成立。本項研究重點着眼於這些問題。 本項目將研究在颱風環境中對流參數化的尺度依賴性是否能改善地形降水的模擬。我們也會開發一個將水平方向湍流混合參數化的方案來增強對流參數化的作用。我們會設計實施理想化的數值實驗來研究地形和對流特徵如何影響灰區的參數化。本項目最後一部分會利用機器學習來嘗試根據不同天氣選擇不同的次網格尺度參數化方案。項目整體目標是增加我們對於灰區地形降水的理論理解與預報技術。

16301921.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16301921.value: 平帶粒子的能量在整個動量空間中是恆定的，即沒有色散。這大大增強了多體效應，例如無色散能帶，產生了各種新奇的多體狀態，如鐵磁性、超導和維格納晶體。包含兩個子晶格 A 和 B 的二元晶格是實現平帶的模型系統，其中每個 A 位點只有 B 位點相鄰，反之亦然，例子包括 Dice 晶格和 Lieb 晶格。在過去幾年中，二元晶格已經在超冷原子氣體、光子器件和電子系統中被實現。在這個項目中，我們建議設計在二維金屬有機框架 (2D-MOF) 中實現二元晶格，並以此驗證分子系統中平帶現象的理論預測。 我們將在原子級別平坦的基板上沉積金屬原子和有機連接分子，以通過表面配位自組裝來生長 2D-MOF。我們將選擇以兩種不同的配位模式與金屬原子結合的多功能連接分子來實現二元晶格。我們將使用低溫掃描隧道顯微鏡來表徵結構，並使用隧道光譜來研究 2D-MOF 的電子特性。具體來說，我們將搜索平帶的特徵 — 態密度的尖峰。我們將測量 2D-MOF 的二元晶格位點特定位置的局部狀態密度。最後一步是研究 2D-MOF 的物理特性。我們將專注於磁性，這部分工作將與 Thomas Jung 教授合作，在瑞士光源中使用X 射線磁圓二色性進行研究。 一個在化學合成方面具有專業知識的合作小組將為我們提供分子。我們還將在整個項目過程中與一個理論小組合作，包括結構設計、數據解釋和能帶結構計算。我們相信我們在二維配位自組裝、隧道光譜測量方面的豐富經驗和實力，以及合作良好的合作團隊將為我們提供很好的機會來揭示二元 2D-MOF 中奇異的平帶物理現象。

16301921.label: Realisation of objectives
16301921.value: Object 1 has been realized by successful synthesis of: (1) a two-dimensional Fe-coordinated bimolecular metal-organic framework which constitutes a honeycomb lattice of 1,4,5,8,9,12-hexaazatriphenylene molecules and a Kagome lattice of 5,15-di(4-pyridyl)-10,20-diphenylporphyrin molecules on a Au(111) substrate. (2) an artificial bipartite Lieb lattice of nanopores array self-assembled by macrocycles on a Ag(111) substrate. (3) a Ni-TPM MOF self-assembled using tris(4-carbonitrile)-TPM molecules and Ni atoms on a Au(111) surface. This MOF consists of two interconnected triangular lattices: a molecular lattice made of TPM and a metal lattice made of Ni. Objective 2 has been realized by using low-temperature scanning tunneling microscopy to investigate the electronic properties of the 2D-MOFs formed in 1. We discovered that: (1) The intra- and inter-molecular nanopores in the the artificial Lieb lattice provide quantum dots with varying energy levels, which results in an isolated flat band gapped at 0.16 eV from the nearest band. (2) the macrocycles undergo conformational and orbital symmetry breaking, adopting low-symmetry conformations. This behavior plays important roles for modulating the band structures of the nanopore lattices. (3) the bimolecular 2D MOF features multiple well-separated spin-polarized Kagome bands, namely Dirac cone bands and Chern flat bands, near the Fermi level. Objective 3 has been realized as demonstrated by the following results: (1) STS measurements at single TPM radicals exhibits a Kondo resonance, evidencing that the unpaired electron of the radical forms a spin singlet with the itinerant electrons of the electrode. (2) The spin-down bands of the bimolecular 2D MOF can be perfectly reconstructed using a p-orbital HKL TB model thank to that HAT and Fe-DPyP possess frontier molecular orbitals exhibiting p-orbital symmetry. This sheds light on a promising strategy of using spatial symmetry of molecular orbitals to design p-orbital lattices in 2D MOFs. The fully-spin-polarized DFT band structure makes this system an appealing playground for studying Chern-bands-related quantum phenomena with broken time-reversal symmetry. More interestingly, a Chern flat band lies at the Fermi level, which provides opportunities for exploring both topological and strong correlated physics. (3) DFT analyses reveal that the symmetry breaking of the macrocycle molecules is driven by a subtle interplay of higher extended conjugation between phenyl and node carbon atoms and conformation flexibility of the macrocycles. The planned XMCD measurements has been delayed because the synchrotron beamline at Switzerland has been over occupied after the Covid shutdown, so our planned measurements have not been completed within the project period. We plan to carried out the measurements in the near future.

16301921.label: Major findings and research outcome
16301921.value: (1) A p-orbital honeycomb-Kagome lattice realized in a two-dimensional metal-organic framework (Reference 1 in Part C) Here, we synthesize a two-dimensional Fe-coordinated bimolecular metal-organic framework which constitutes a honeycomb lattice of 1,4,5,8,9,12-hexaazatriphenylene molecules and a Kagome lattice of 5,15-di(4-pyridyl)-10,20-diphenylporphyrin molecules on a Au(111) substrate. Density-functional theory calculations show that the framework features multiple well-separated spin-polarized Kagome bands, namely Dirac cone bands and Chern flat bands, near the Fermi level. Using tight-binding modelling, we reveal that these bands are originated from two effects: the low-lying molecular orbitals that exhibit p-orbital characteristics and the honeycomb-Kagome lattice. This study demonstrates that p-orbital Kagome bands can be realized in metal-organic frameworks by using molecules with molecular orbitals of p-orbital like symmetry. (2) Isolated flat band in artificially designed Lieb lattice based on macrocycle supramolecular crystal (Reference 2 in Part C) One way to achieve an isolated flat band is by breaking the on-site energy symmetry in a Lieb lattice. In this study, we demonstrate the design of such a Lieb lattice. The self-assembly of square-shaped macrocycle molecules on a Ag(111) surface forms a two-dimensional supramolecular crystal, comprising three types of nanopores with different sizes arranged in a Lieb lattice. The surface-state electrons of the Ag(111) substrate confined by these nanopores behave as quantum dots with specific energies depending on the pore size. Using scanning tunneling spectroscopy and plane-wave quantum simulation, we reveal that this artificial Lieb lattice exhibits an isolated flat band gapped at 0.16 eV from the nearest band. The supramolecular crystal is nearly defect-free and extends to sub-micrometer size, making it a practical platform for exploring the exotic properties of the isolated flat band. (3) Single-Molecule Resolved Conformational and Orbital Symmetry Breaking in Tetraphenylethylene-Based Macrocycles (Reference 3 in Part C) Because the symmetry of macrocycles strongly affects their photophysical properties, here we report a single-molecule study of the structures and orbitals of two TPE-based macrocycles of (C26H18)4 and (C26H18)6. Using scanning tunneling microscopy and spectroscopy, we discover that both macrocycles undergo spontaneous symmetry breaking in their conformations and frontier orbitals. The computational analyses reveal that the symmetry breaking is driven by a subtle interplay of higher extended conjugation between phenyl and node carbon atoms and conformation flexibility of the macrocycles. The observed symmetry breaking in TPE-based macrocycles is expected to strongly alter their photophysical properties.

16301921.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16301921.value: 1 The observed symmetry breaking in TPE-based macrocycles significantly impacts their photophysical characteristics, providing valuable insights into their behavior. Furthermore, our work demonstrates a general trend that macrocycles with flexible molecular backbones are susceptible to symmetry breaking and thus may exhibit distinctive electronic/photophysical properties. 2 Considering the topological bands of this structure are screened due to electronic coupling with the Au(111) substrate, future work is to synthesize this structure on an insulating substrate or an inert substrate which interacts weakly with the framework. 3 Compared with the structures built by tip manipulation of molecules, the ultra-large single domain size, high crystallinity, and thermal stability of this system make it an ideal platform for exploring the flat band physics, e.g., the correlated states and the possible topological nontrivial phases, using a wide range of techniques, such as various spectroscopic and transport experiments.

16301921.value: Our research demonstrates that bipartite lattices can be realized in 2D Metal-Organic Frameworks (MOFs). The Nobel prize in 2025 for chemistry is awarded to three scientists pioneered in MOFs research. Our work extends the MOFs research to 2D systems that host rich physical properties. 16302121.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16302121.value: As a subclass of linear codes, cyclic codes have nice applications in communication systems, computer systems, data storage systems, and consumer electronics. They are linked to certain areas of mathematics, such as algebra, algebraic geometry, algebraic function fields, algebraic number theory, association schemes, combinatorics, finite fields, finite geometry, graph theory, and group theory. The Bose, Chaudhuri, and Hocquenghem (BCH) codes are the most studied subclass of cyclic codes. In the past 60 years, good progress in the study of BCH codes has been made. However, little is known about the duals of BCH codes. It is known that the duals of some BCH codes are optimal. Hence, it is possible to obtain optimal or good cyclic codes as duals of BCH codes. The first objective of this proposed project is to develop a general theory for duals of BCH codes over finite fields. The second objective is to study the parameters and investigate the properties of the duals of certain subfamilies of BCH codes. The third objective is to investigate applications of the duals of some subfamilies of BCH codes. The outputs of this project would enhance coding theory and would also have applications in science and engineering. 循環碼是一類特殊的線性碼。這種碼在通信系統，計算機系統，數據存儲系統和電子消費產品中有廣泛的應用。同時，這種碼與數學的許多分支有密切聯繫。例如，循環碼與代數學，代數幾何，代數函數域，代數數論，結合方案，組合學，圖論和群論有密切關係。循環碼中研究最多的是BCH碼。BCH碼的研究在過去的60年取得了長足進展。但是，目前很少有BCH碼對偶碼的結果。目前已知一些BCH碼的對偶碼是最優的。因而，可能某些其他BCH的對偶碼也是最優的。 本項目的第一個目標是為BCH碼的對偶碼建立一些一般理論。該項目的第二個目標研究某些BCH碼的對偶碼的參數。本項目的第三個目標是探索某些BCH碼的對偶碼的應用。本項目的結果將加強編碼學的理論和應用。

16302121.label: Realisation of objectives
16302121.value: All the three objectives are fully achieved. A general theory for duals of BCH codes over finite fields has been developed. Parameters and properties of the duals of some subfamilies of BCH codes have been studied. The application of the duals of some subfamilies of BCH codes in combinatorics has been investigated. The major methodology of this project is the introduction of the dually-BCH codes, which is a new concept in coding theory. Another methodology is the use of the automorphism groups of BCH codes.

16302121.label: Major findings and research outcome
16302121.value: Some general theory on the duals of BCH codes has been developed. The duals of several families of BCH codes have been studied and some lower bounds on the minimum distance of these dual codes have been developed. The automorphism groups of some narrow-sense BCH codes have been determined and the application of these codes in combinatorial designs has been investigated. Two families of binary cyclic codes of length 2^m − 1 and dimension near 2^(m − 1) with good minimum distances have been constructed. The two families of binary cyclic codes contain some optimal binary cyclic codes. Four infinite families of ternary cyclic codes with length n = 3^m − 1 for odd m and dimension k ∈ {n/2, (n + 2)/2} whose minimum distances have a square-root-like lower bound have been constructed. Their duals have parameters [n, k⊥, d⊥], where k⊥ ∈ {n/2, (n−2)/2} and d⊥ also has a square-root-like lower bound. These families of codes and their duals contain distance-optimal cyclic codes. Five infinite families of binary cyclic codes with parameters [n, k] and (n − 6)/3 ≤ k ≤ 2(n+6)/3 have been constructed. Three of the five families of binary cyclic codes and their duals have a very good lower bound on their minimum distances and contain distance-optimal codes. The other two families of binary cyclic codes are composed of binary duadic codes with a square-root-like lower bound on their minimum distances. As a by-product, two infinite families of self-dual binary codes with a square-root-like lower bound on their minimum distances have been obtained. The Hermitian dual codes of several classes of BCH codes have been studied and a necessary and sufficient condition for ensuring that two classes of narrow-sense BCH codes are Hermitian dually-BCH codes has been obtained. An infinite family of binary BCH codes C(m) with parameters [2^m − 1, 2^(m−1), d] whose minimum distance d much exceeds the square-root bound when m ≥ 11 is a prime has been constructed. The parameters of a family of binary cyclic codes of length 2^m − 1 and dimension 2^m − 1 − m(m − 1)/2, denoted by C_(2,m,2), and their dual codes C^⊥_(2,m,2) have been obtained. The weight distribution of C^⊥_(2,m,2) is settled . A larger family of binary cyclic codes C_(2,m,r) and their duals have also been constructed and studied, where 0 ≤ r ≤ m − 1.

16302121.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16302121.value: Further applications of the duals of BCH codes will be investigated. Connections of the project outputs with other types of codes will be studied.

16302121.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16302121.value: BCH codes are very important in both theory and practice. In theory, BCH codes are related with many areas of mathematics. In practice, BCH codes are widely used in storage and communication systems. For example, Reed-Solomon codes are a type of BCH codes and are used daily by most people as they are used in QR codes. In this project, a general theory for the duals of BCH codes has been developed and the duals of several subfamilies of BCH codes have been studied. The research outputs of this project show that the duals of many BCH codes are very interesting in theory and practice.

16302321.label: Project Objectives
16302321.value: The proposed study is a theoretical investigation of condensed skyrmion states. We will investigate whether and under what conditions a chiral magnetic film can be in a condensed skyrmion phase and its properties. This study may lead to new ways of manipulating skyrmions. Therefore, this problem has fundamental interest and technological importance. Fundamentally, condensed skyrmions may be an excellent platform for studying phase transition from crystal phase to nematic, smectic, and liquid phases. More importantly, it may be a good platform for studying physics far from thermal equilibrium. Technologically, a good understanding of the proposed problem may lead to realization of skyrmionics. This proposal will touch the heart issues outlined in the 2020 Skyrmionics Roadmap jointly written by 19 leading experts in the field. The proposed study will investigate whether magnetic stripes of various irregular shapes in chiral magnets are skyrmions. If they are skyrmions, then the current skyrmion zoo is greatly expanded beyond the known Bloch, hedgehog, and anti-skyrmions. We will then need naturally to understand why their shapes are so much different from the three known types of circular skyrmions. If they are not skyrmions, then we will want to know their topological properties and why they can take so many different shapes and like to appear in skyrmion crystal states. Under the competition of chiral and Heisenberg exchange interactions, a skyrmion may prefer a stripe geometry instead of a circular disk in conventional wisdom. The answer to this question can provide us a unified picture of the experimental observations. The proposed study examines the skyrmion formation energy and conditions for isolated skyrmions and condensed skyrmions. The sign of the formation energy (relative to the energy of a single magnetic domain) can inform us of the stability of skyrmions and their morphology. If a skyrmion is a metastable state and its formation energy is positive, then a chiral magnetic film can have isolated skyrmions. If the skyrmion formation energy is negative, the intrinsic shape of each skyrmion should be irregular such that the system can lower its energy by occupying an area as large as possible. Certainly, it may also want to host many skyrmions to be in a condensed skyrmion state. We aim to develop a coherent theory to understand various phases ranging from ramified stripes, long spiral/helical or cycloid stripes, and short rectangular stripes to skyrmion crystals. The proposed study finds the dependence of stripe width on the Heisenberg exchange constant, the DzyaloshinskiiMoriya interaction strength, and magnetic anisotropy as well as the external magnetic field. The study reveals the relationship between the morphology of condensed skyrmion phase, skyrmion formation energy, and skyrmion number density. We anticipate that skyrmions can take regular shapes of rectangles and disks when the skyrmion number density is high enough such that stripe-stripe repulsion dominates the morphology. Determining how system energy depends on stripe length may be important. The answer to the issue may provide a new method of manipulating skyrmion crystals and other condensed skyrmion phases. Monte Carlo simulations are carried out to determine how condensed skyrmion phase and distribution of skyrmion number density occur under a given temperature and magnetic field. This study may allow us to understand why an external magnetic field is needed for skyrmion crystal in reality. One possibility is that the system energy increases with the skyrmion number density in the skyrmion crystal states whereas it is not sensitive to the skyrmion number density in the stripe phase. If this is the case, we then provide a perfect answer to this unexplained phenomenon. This study shall also prepare us to study physics far from equilibrium.

16302321.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16302321.value: Skyrmions, topological particles originally proposed in nuclear physics, have attracted enormous attention in condensed matter physics after they were first unambiguously confirmed in magnetic systems in 2009. Numerous studies on skyrmions have been conducted in fields such as not only topological quantum field theory for its solution in the nonlinear sigma model, but more so in magnetics because of its potential applications in information technology besides its fundamental interest. Isolated skyrmions and skyrmion crystals (SkXs) have been observed in many chiral magnetic systems involving the DzyaloshinskiiMoriya interactions. Very often, so-called spiral/helical, cycloid, and conical stripe phases appear together or even mix with SkXs. The general belief is that those stripes are distinct from skyrmions. Our recent preliminary study unexpectedly indicates that various irregular stripes are skyrmions. Many observed spiral/helical and cycloid stripe phases are condensed skyrmions like SkXs. This proposal aims to determine conclusively what those stripes mixed with SkXs are, how the stripe width depends on material parameters, and what the relationships between stripe phases and SkXs are. We propose to study skyrmion formation energy analytically and use micromagnetic simulator to investigate how a magnetic texture, its morphology, and skyrmion numbers evolve to final stable states. We can use skyrmion numbers of irregular magnetic texture to determine whether stripes are skyrmions and why they are so irregular if all or many of them are indeed skyrmions. Otherwise, we need to explain why stripes appear together with SkXs in experiments and simulations, but not in the systems with isolated circular skyrmions. We shall understand why SkXs often need the presence of an external field in experiments, and when condensed skyrmions form stripes or crystals. The nature of the stripy phase is a fundamental issue and important in applications. A clear understanding of the condensed skyrmion states is critical for us to understand the recently discovered topological Hall effect that is about the interplay of topology, charge, and spin. It will open new avenues for manipulating skyrmion crystals and building a platform for studying topological Hall effects and spin waves in various condensed skyrmions. Condensed skyrmions are also a good platform for studying phase transition and physics far from thermal equilibrium. This proposal will touch the heart issues outlined in the 2020 Skyrmionics Roadmap jointly written by 19 leading experts in the field. 自从最初在核物理中提出的斯格明子于2009年第一次在磁系统中无可质疑的被发现以来，斯格明子就不仅在拓扑量子场论中被关注，更加由于其在信息领域的潜在应用前景而受到磁学界不计其数的研究。 孤立的斯格明子和斯格明子晶体在许多有Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya (DM)相互作用的手性磁系统中被观测到了。伴随着斯格明子晶体的出现人们往往还能看到各种绦纹磁结构的出现。有时绦纹结构还能和斯格明子共存一体。目前的共识是这些绦纹结构有别于斯格明子，不具备任何的拓扑数。而目前的这种认识似乎与我们最近的研究结果不符。 本项目立志揭示那些伴随着斯格明子晶体的绦纹结构到底是什么。如果不是斯格明子，那为何其总伴随斯格明子晶体出现而不曾看到和孤立的斯格明子共存？如果它们也是斯格明子，那为何其形态和人们认识的圆形斯格明子如此不同。我们计划从斯格明子的形成能量着手，首先揭示孤立斯格明子和凝聚斯格明子有何不同。如果凝聚斯格明子的形成能是负的，那么绦纹状的斯格明子就可能理解为系统降低能量的必然结果。本项目将努力揭示为何斯格明子晶体常常在一个合适的外加磁场和稍低于居里温度处观察到。明白上述问题必将大大加深我们对斯格明子的认识，从而加强我们对斯格明子的有效操控能力，本项目的研究涉及当前斯格明子学的一些关键问题。

16302321.label: Realisation of objectives
16302321.value: Objectives 1-5 are well achieved. We now have a deep understanding of magnetic skyrmions in chiral magnetic films. We used both numerical methods and analytical approaches to launch the full-scale investigation on the issues outlined in our original proposal. Indeed, skyrmions can be in isolated phase and condensed phase with distinct morphology and properties. Isolated skyrmions are metastable states with a positive formation energy (relative to the ferromagnetic state) while the condensed skyrmions are ground state with a negative formation energy. As a result, isolated skyrmion tend to have a circular morphology while the condensed skyrmions are stripe in nature. Condensed skyrmions become circular shape when skyrmion number density is hight enough such that the skyrmion-skyrmion distance is comparable to stipe nature width. The metastable and stable spin structures in chiral magnetic films are determined by the relative strengths of colinear interactions, such as the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction. For a widely studied generic chiral magnetic model, the meta-stable and stable structure are determined by two parameters called kappa and kappa prime. The phase diagrams separated isolated skyrmions from condensed skyrmions are obtained. The results are obtained from a combination of massive numerical studies with the analytical investigations. We further investigate the critical role of external magnetic field in skyrmion crystal formation, namely, in the condensed skyrmion phase when the noncollinear interaction is strong enough, the magnetic field tends to shift ground state to region of a finite skyrmion number density which is higher enough to force the stripe skyrmions into disk-like skyrmions arranged in a lattice structure. We have also proved the equivalence of stripe phase and skyrmion lattice. Due to the duality of particle and continuum medium nature of skyrmions, we show one can have all kinds of composite skyrmions in the condensed skyrmion phase and near the boundary of isolated skyrmions and condensed skyrmions. In summary, all objectives are achieved far beyond the initial expectations. A unified picture of skyrmion nature, structures, and formations are obtained. Formula of skyrmion size in various phases are also found that agree with both experimental and numerical observations. Our findings are published in a number of publications in leading journals in the field.

16302321.label: Major findings and research outcome
16302321.value: The major findings are a skyrmion crystal formation theory that explains the necessity of an external magnetic field in skyrmion crystal formation. It solved a long-term puzzle of why skyrmion crystals are normally found near an optimal magnetic field and near the Curie temperature [Publications 1 and 22]. Skyrmions can be three distinct forms: isolated circular objects, stripes in condensed phase at dilute skyrmion number density with well-defined stripe width, and disk-like object in skyrmion crystals. Skyrmion crystals are condensed skyrmions at high skyrmion number density. Skyrmion sizes in the three forms have different material parameter dependence. For example, the size of isolated skyrmion increases with DMI interaction and decreases with Heisenberg exchange stiffness while the size of stripe skyrmions is opposite to this dependence: namely decreases with DMI interaction and increases with the exchange stiffness. In contrast, the skyrmion size in a skyrmion crystal depends on the skyrmion number density, and only weakly depends on other parameters. We showed skyrmion can be in nematic and sematic phases and demonstrate how to obtain these phases. We have also shown the equivalence of stripe skyrmions and skyrmion crystals [Pub. 12]. A “quark-like” model [Pub. 13] is proposed to understand various composited skyrmions or topological nontrivial structures. A phase diagram for isolated and condensed skyrmions in kappa-kappa-prime space that characterized relative collinear interactions and noncollinear interactions [Pub. 23].

16302321.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16302321.value: It would be fascinating to explore whether the findings from this project can be extended to three-dimensional bulky systems featuring other topological structures, such as hofions. Additionally, a promising avenue for future research is to investigate skyrmion-skyrmion interactions. While it is known that skyrmions can repel one another, it would be particularly intriguing to determine if they can also exhibit attractive interactions. Understanding the nature and properties of skyrmion-skyrmion interactions is crucial for developing complex skyrmion structures, including skyrmion molecules, skyrmion devices, and skyrmion-based neuromorphic computing systems. This line of inquiry could significantly advance the field and lead to innovative applications in spintronics and information technology.

16302321.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16302321.value: Magnetic skyrmions are localized spin textures characterized by a non-trivial topological number known as the skyrmion number. They are considered promising candidates for spintronics, serving as information carriers and enabling information processing. Additionally, their diverse morphologies make them valuable for neuromorphic computing. In this project, we addressed several longstanding experimental challenges in the field. For instance, our theory on skyrmion crystal formation clarifies the necessity of an optimal magnetic field to stabilize a skyrmion crystal. We demonstrated that the stripes observed in chiral magnets are not only a natural morphology of condensed skyrmions but also equivalent to skyrmion crystals, indicating that there is no fundamental distinction between the stripy phase and skyrmion crystals; they simply represent different morphologies of condensed skyrmions at varying skyrmion number densities. Furthermore, our quark-like skyrmion-duality theory effectively organizes the observed composite skyrmions. Our derived skyrmion size formula aligns well with experimental results and simulation observations. Our work predicts the existence of skyrmion nematic and sematic phases.Collectively, these significant findings provide a coherent and unified understanding of magnetic skyrmions and establish a solid foundation for future skyrmion-based applications.

16302521.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16302521.value: 约化李群不可约酉表示分类是李群表示论的一个中心课题。我们用轨道方法寻求不可约酉表示的基本构成元，也就是幂零轨道对应的幂单表示。这些幂单表示是构造不可约酉表示的基本单元，我们这项研究是要先确定对应模幂零轨道的幂单理想和幂单表示，再进一步确定和理解其他幂单理想和幂单表示。 我们设 G 实约化李群。表示论中一个基本的、未解决的问题是 G 的不可约酉正表示的分类。该主题的一个指导原则是共伴轨道的方法。由于（独立地）基里洛夫和科斯坦特，轨道方法提出了 G 的不可约酉正表示和 G 在其李代数的对偶空间中的轨道之间的对应关系{G - g∗0 中的轨道} 《----》{G 的不可约酉表示} 特别是，人们期望 G 的一组有限的不可约酉正表示对应于幂零共同伴随 G 轨道。这些表示有一个名称——幂单表示——但还没有一个好的定义。一旦正确定义，这些表示有望形成所有不可约的单一表示的构建元。有关幂单表示、它们的预期属性以及定义它们所涉及的一些问题的详细讨论，我们请读者参阅 Vogan 1986 年发表于 Annals of Mathetical Studies 的 Hermann Weyl Lectures 笔记。在过去的 40 年里，对幂单表示的一般理论和分类的探索激发了大量的研究。在他们 1992 年出版的研究专着中，Adams、Barbasch 和 Vogan 遵循 Arthur 的思想，定义了一组独特的单能表示，称为特殊单能表示（有关精确定义的研究背景，请参阅本提案的第 2a 节） .然而，他们的定义排除了大量值得称为单能的表示（例如，Mp(2n,R) 的元表示）。 在他们正在进行的工作中，Losev、Mason-Brown 和 Matvieievskyi 提出了幂单原始理想和单能 Harish-Chandra 双模的定义。它们的定义是几何的（有关概述，请参阅本提案的第 2a 节关于研究背景）。在这项提议的研究中，我们试图将这些想法应用于真正的约化李群。我们将把我们的初步研究集中在 Sp(2n, R) 和 Mp(2n, R) 的幂单表示上，这些表示连接到模型幂零轨道。我们的最终目标是定义和分类附加到模型轨道的分裂还原李群的单能表示。这个拟议的研究项目基于与牛津大学Lucas Maison-Brown的合作。

16302621.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16302621.value: Two-dimensional (2D) electron-hole (e-h) bilayer structures provide a platform for exploring unusual interaction and collective behaviors of charge particles. This kind of bilayer structure allows electrons and holes to be confined in two adjacent layers such that e-h recombination is hindered by the presence of an ultrathin potential barrier in the bilayer. Compared with traditional growth techniques for quantum well heterostructures, the artificial exfoliation and stacking techniques developed in recent years offer advantages and flexibilities for generating strongly coupled e-h pairs or indirect excitons, for example, in atomically thin bilayers of transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs) semiconductors with further narrowed inter-layer barriers (1-2 nm) and enhanced Coulomb interactions. The technical obstacles for exploring the electrical transport properties of TMDC e-h bilayers are mainly because of the difficulties of fabricating high-quality atomically thin TMDCs with reliable low-temperature ohmic contacts for p-type and n-type TMDC layers. We recently developed a new approach to achieve high-quality electrical contacts for p-type and n-type atomically thin TMDCs and realized a simple structure of a quasi-2D e-h bilayer device. Our preliminary transport results indicated that strong Coulomb interactions and exciton related phases could occur depending on the carrier types and densities. We discovered distinct transport behaviours compared with the well-established Coulomb drag and e-h bilayer systems of traditional quantum well heterostructures. Moreover, we observed conductance plateaus in WSe2 e-h bilayers at certain ratios of electron and hole densities which could not be interpreted by any published theories. We believe that the large effective mass and strong interaction effects are important factors that affect the formation of e-h pairs or the exciton’s coherent quantum states in the TMDC bilayers, particularly the superfluid states or exciton condensate. We propose to investigate the low-temperature transport behaviors and their correlations to the device interface structures, relative inter-layer and intra-layer Coulomb interactions, and the exciton condensate-related phase transitions in TMDC e-h bilayer structures. The success of this project will provide critical knowledge and technical information needed to control TMDC e-h bilayer structures precisely and modulate their electronic properties. This project will focus on (1) the fabrication and characterization of high-quality TMDC e-h bilayers and their low-temperature transport properties, (2) the interaction effects and collective behaviors of electrons and holes, and (3) the realization of excitonic phase transitions, such as exciton solid states, superfluid states and/or condensate states in TMDC bilayers, to understand the underlying mechanisms of indirect excitons for potential technical application. 具有电子-空穴对的双层二维结构提供了一个研究电子关联效应的理想平台。 在这种结构中，不同于传统二维电子气结构， 电子与空穴被束缚在不同的空间。 建基于原子尺度机械剥离的的硫族过渡金属二维半导体的器件结构具有更窄的绝缘层和更强的库仑交互作用。制作这种结构的最大困难在于如何实现高质量的二维结构和低温下对此结构的欧姆电接触。我们近期开发了一种新颖的高质量电接触方法，实现了对p型和n型的原子级别厚度硫族过渡金属二维半导体器件的连接。我们初步观察到强的交互作用和激子相关联的电子态。我们发现了一些不同于传统半导体器件的电输运和库仑牵引现象，同时也发现了电导平台现象。 目前这些现象还无法用现有理论解释。我们相信在这个体系中，具有比较大的电子有效质量和强的交互作用是引起电子-空穴对产生激子量子态，特别是超流态和激子凝聚态的关键因素。我们计划系统性地研究在二维器件结构中的层间和层内的库仑交互作用以及激子的凝聚态相关的电子态相变。此研究项目将提供关键的技术与方案用来精确调节电子-空穴在两层器件结构中的电子态，特别是在下列的关键课题方向：1. 高质量的器件制作和低温电输运性质探测；2. 交互作用和机理；3. 实现激子态相变， 例如激子固体态，超流态或凝聚态。此项研究对电子-空穴和相关激子态的形成机理和潜在应用都有指导意义。

16302821.label: Project Objectives
16302821.value: Develop complementary measurement techniques for the thermodynamic study of SU(N) Fermi liquids. The PI’s group has successfully demonstrated the thermodynamic measurement of the compressibility via the atom number fluctuations and the Tan’s contact via the high-momentum tail in a SU(N) Fermi liquid. To complement our understanding of thermodynamics, we will develop a new spectroscopic tool, which is suitable for alkali-earth-like fermions. This technique will allow us to characterize a multi-component Fermi gas with high momentum and energy resolutions. In addition, we will implement in-situ density detection. Characterize thermodynamics of a SU(N) Fermi liquid in bulk. On the basis of the expertise of the PI’s group and the new detection techniques to be developed in Objective 1, we will carefully measure the thermodynamic quantities of SU(N) Fermi liquids with high precision and compare them with that in theory, such as virial expansion. For example, two complementary measurements will be simultaneously obtained, including the in-situ detection of the density profile and fluctuations, which can result in the compressibility. Other thermodynamic quantities will be measured by two different methods, and then quantitatively compared to the theory. Beyond the Fermi liquid description in periodic optical lattices. The full utilization of various measurement techniques to be developed in Objectives 1 and 2 will set the stage for exploring the thermodynamics of SU(N) Fermi gases beyond the Fermi liquid description. We will carefully investigate thermodynamic quantities (e.g., compressibility and contact) in the optical lattice potential, from which we expect to further characterize Fermi liquid description.

16302821.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16302821.value: Quantum gas offers unprecedented opportunities to simulate exotic quantum phenomena. One of the pedagogical examples among many-body quantum systems is the Landau Fermi liquid that describes the behavior of interacting two-component (N=2) fermions. In this project, we plan to experimentally investigate intriguing properties in a SU(N) Fermi liquid in which the spin degree of freedom is generalized to a large number (N>2). In the past few years, the great effort has been given to SU(N) Fermi liquids in ultracold alkaline-earth-like fermions. This new system allows the researchers to study unprecedented quantum systems that have no analogy in solids. Nevertheless, thermodynamic studies – a fundamental way to understand the system - have remained largely unexplored until the recent release of the works of the PI and a few other researchers this year. Despite the thermodynamic characterization of SU(N) Fermi liquids in those works, a comprehensive and quantitative thermodynamic measurement, which can also provide a hint of the breakdown of Fermi liquids, still remains unexplored. In this project, we plan to establish the quantitative thermodynamic measurement of interacting SU(N) Fermi liquid in bulk by using complementary measurement methods, and subsequently extend our understanding of interacting SU(N) fermions in the presence of periodic potential (e.g., optical lattices) where the Fermi liquid description may be invalid. Considering that SU(N) fermions in optical lattices are a promising platform for the study of SU(N) magnetism that do not appear in spin-1/2 systems, our work will be of broad importance. In the proposed project, we propose (1) the development of complementary measurement techniques for the thermodynamics study of SU(N) Fermi liquids, (2) the comprehensive and quantitative thermodynamic study of SU(N) Fermi liquids in bulk and (3) the study of SU(N) fermions beyond the Landau Fermi liquid description in a tunable 3D optical lattice potential. The successful completion of the proposed project will advance our understanding of interacting fermions with spin degrees of freedom. 量子氣體為模擬奇特的量子現象提供了前所未有的良機。多體量子系統中的一個教學例子是，朗道-費米液體，描述了雙組分(N=2)費米子相互作用下的行為。 在此項目中，我們計劃透過實驗研究 SU(N) 費米液體的神秘特性，並且當中的自旋自由度泛化為大數(N>2)。 過去的幾年中，人們為超冷類鹼土費米子中的SU(N) 費米液體作出了巨大努力。此新系統允許研究者研究在固體中沒有類似的、前所未見的量子系統。儘管如此，熱動力學--瞭解系統的基礎方法--仍然有很多並未探索，直到今年PI 及一些其他研究人員發佈了最新的研究成果。儘管這些工作描述了SU(N) 費米液體的熱力學特性，但是可以提供費米液體分析線索的，全面、量化的熱力學測量，仍未得到探索。在此項目中，我們計劃通過使用互補測量方法，建立對堆積下相互作用的SU(N)費米液體的量化熱力學測量，由此擴展我們對週期勢下(例如光晶格) 相互作用SU(N)費米子的理解，而其中費米液體描述可能無效。鑒於光晶格中的SU(N)費米子在研究SU(N)磁性是一個有前景的領域，且並不出現在半自旋系統中，我們的研究將具有廣泛的重要性。 在擬定的項目中，我們計劃： 一、為SU(N)費米液體的熱力學研究發展補充測量技術；二、對堆積的SU(N)費米液體進行全面及量化的熱力學研究；三、在可調控三維光晶格勢中研究超越朗道-費米液體描述的SU(N)費米子。此擬定項目的成功將推進我們對具有自旋自由度的相互作用費米子的理解。

16303221.value: 近紅外二區窗口（NIR-II，1000-1700nm）是一種新興螢光成像方法，具有分辨率高、穿透度深和高保真度高等特點，開闢生物醫學應用的新途徑。根據賈布朗斯基(Jablonski)光物理圖，分子被激發後可通過輻射（發光）衰變或非輻射（光熱）衰變釋放其能量。其光熱效應可以實現近紅外光觸發光熱療法（PTT），這是一種無創、可控和高度特異的癌症治療策略，涉及光激活加熱以殺死腫瘤組織。有機分子具有可調的光物理性質、高生物相容性、易加工性和易於功能化等優點，然而，目前大多數可用的紅外二區螢光團亮度較低，這阻礙了它們作為有效的治療劑及治療和診斷一體化轉化潛力。螢光團的亮度與其摩爾吸收率（ε）和螢光量子產率（ΦF）成正比。具有聚集誘導發光特性 (AIE) 的螢光分子因具有多個分子轉子，所以構象通常呈現扭曲。溶液中AIE分子內的主動運動促進了激發態的非輻射衰變以產生熱量。然而，由於物理約束，這種運動在聚集態中被抑制，這使得聚集態中的激子能夠經歷輻射衰變。儘管許多AIE分子表現出良好的高固態螢光量子產率值，但它們的摩爾吸收率值相當低，這可能是由於它們扭曲的構象，削弱了它們的 π-共軛系統，從而減少了光子吸收。相比之下，傳統的近紅外二區螢光分子具較大的 π-共軛體系的平面結構。這類分子溶液中能有效地發出螢光，但它們的聚集體顯的螢光量子產率值極低。因此，在單分子體系中同時最大化 ε 和 ΦF 值是非常具有挑戰性的。在本項目中，我們將開發一種新的分子設計策略，以合成高效NIR-II治療劑的新型分子。我們將把平面單元合併到構象扭曲的NIR-II螢光分子中。平面單元將確保這些熒光團具有高ε值，而其扭曲部分將限制分子內運動，以確保螢光團在固態下具有高ΦF值。本項目將系統地研究給體、受體和共軛橋對這些熒光分子光物理性質的影響。同時將鑑定NIR-II熒光分子是否具有高ε和ΦF值，並探索其在熒光成像和成像引導光熱療法中的潛在治療應用。

16303321.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16303321.value: Organic luminescent radical materials show fantastic potential for a wide range of applications due to their uncommon excitation and emission pathway known as the doublet transition. Researchers have successfully demonstrated their use in radical-based organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs), novel multi-responsive materials, and heavy metal sensing, all of which have been met with strong interest. While there has been a history of generating stable radical compounds, the synthesis of luminescent radicals has proven to be much more challenging. Furthermore, even from the limited luminescent radical systems reported, they have been observed to experience detrimental self-quenching in the aggregated or solid state due to the strong intermolecular π-π interactions. Using our experience in developing materials with aggregation-induced emission, our group has recently observed luminescence in emissive crystalline radicals and in polymeric radicals. However, due to the infancy of the field of organic luminescent radicals, there is limited clear design guidelines for their synthesis. Thus, in this proposal, we aim to (in situ) generate novel stable radical systems that exhibit efficient luminescence in the solid state. We will investigate their structure-property relationships to aid in the design of future systems. The practical applications of the materials will also be explored in the fields of biological sciences, optical devices, and multifunctional materials. Building upon our body of previous work, we aim to systematically investigate what molecular structural designs are beneficial in the production of luminescent radicals and study how to prevent the radicals from self-quenching. By carefully examining how the molecular design can effectively break the symmetry rules that hinder the doublet transition, it will become possible to draw general mechanistic conclusions to aid in the production of even more luminescent radical materials. The investigation will be able to examine how best to control the emission wavelengths of the radical systems, the efficiency of the doublet absorption and the efficiency of the emission. With additional theoretical analyses of their highest occupied, lowest unoccupied, and singly occupied molecular orbitals, it will become possible to rationally design new organic luminescent radical materials for a wide range of high-tech applications . It is expected that the proposed project will generate numerous new organic systems that exhibit luminescent radical behavior, which can be used to create new multifunctional materials, unique sensors for environmental, in vitro and in vivo monitoring, and much more energy efficient OLEDs. 有機發光自由基材料由於其罕見的雙線態激發和光發射途徑，在廣泛的應用中顯示出巨大的潛力。研究人員已經成功地展示了它們在基於自由基的有機發光二極管 (OLED)、新型多響應材料和重金屬傳感中的應用，所有這些都引起了人們的濃厚興趣。雖然有關於穩定自由基化合物的研究報導，但發光自由基的合成已被證明更具挑戰性。此外，即使從有限的報導過的發光自由基體系中，也觀察到由於強的分子間 π-π 相互作用，它們在聚集態或固態下會經歷有害的自淬滅過程。 利用我們在開發具有聚集誘導發光的材料方面的經驗，我們的課題組最近觀察到發光晶體自由基和聚合物自由基的發光。然而，由於有機發光自由基領域處於起步階段，對其合成的明確設計指南有限。因此，在這個提案中，我們的目標是（原位）產生新型穩定的自由基系統，在固態下表現出有效的發光。我們將研究它們的結構-性能關係，以幫助設計未來的體系。我們還將在生物科學、光學器件和多功能材料等領域探索該材料的實際應用。 基於我們之前的工作，我們的目標是系統地研究哪些分子結構設計有利於產生發光自由基，並研究如何防止自由基自淬滅。通過仔細檢查分子設計如何有效地打破限制雙線態發射的對稱性規則，我們將有可能總結出普適性的機理，以幫助生產更多發光自由基材料。該研究將能夠檢驗如何最好地控制自由基體系的發射波長、雙線態吸收效率和發射效率。通過對其最高佔據、最低未佔據和單佔據分子軌道的理論分析，合理設計廣泛用於高科技應用的新型有機發光自由基材料將成為可能。預計擬議的項目將產生許多表現出發光自由基現象的新有機材料體系，可用於創建新的多功能材料、用於環境、體外和體內監測的獨特傳感器以及更節能的有機發光二極管。

16303521.label: Project Objectives
16303521.value: Investigate piezoelectric effect on spin-orbit torques (SOTs) in topological insulator (TI)/ferromagnet heterostructures. SOTs mostly originate from the spin-orbit coupling of materials. TIs can generate large SOTs because of the strong spin-orbit coupling and spin-momentum locking of their topological surface states. The topological surface states and thus SOT efficiency of TIs can be tuned by electric field and strain effect, which remain to be explored. Ferroelectric substrates have large piezoelectric coefficients, resulting in both large electric field and strain effect. Investigating piezoelectric control of SOTs can help identify underlying mechanisms to generate SOTs and further enhance SOT efficiency. In this proposed study, we will fabricate PMN-PT/TI/ferromagnet heterostructures and then quantify the SOT efficiency under different gate voltages, where PMN-PT is a ferroelectric substrate. The PMN-PT will be purchased or obtained from our collaborator. The TI thin films will be prepared using in-house magnetron sputtering or molecular beam epitaxy by our collaborator. We will deposit high-quality magnetic thin films on PMN-PT/TI and then fabricate the heterostructure into devices using nanofabrication techniques. The SOT efficiency will be investigated by second-harmonic Hall method, loop shift, and/or spin-torque ferromagnetic resonance techniques. We will investigate the charge doping and strain effect on the SOTs from TIs under the gate voltage across the PMN-PT. Investigate piezoelectric control of current-induced magnetization switching in SOT nonvolatile memory devices. Energy-efficient manipulation of magnetic devices requires the least current to generate large SOTs. Piezoelectric control can help reduce critical switching current in two aspects without introducing Ohmic loss. One the one hand, piezoelectric control can potentially increase the SOT efficiency, generating more spin current from a given charge current. On the other hand, piezoelectric control can help reduce the perpendicular magnetic anisotropy (PMA), reducing the energy barrier to be overcome. Besides, theoretical calculations have shown the combination of SOT and strain effect could lead to external field-free SOT magnetization switching, which has not been achieved in TI-based systems. We will fabricate the PMN-PT/TI/ferromagnet into Hall bar devices and investigate current-induced magnetization under different pulsing schemes and different angles between the Hall channel current direction and strain direction. We will also use the magneto-optical Kerr effect (MOKE) to directly resolve the magnetization switching dynamics. Investigate strain-mediated novel SOT and field-free magnetization switching in transition-metal dichalcogenide (TMD)/ferromagnet heterostructures. SOT directions are correlated with the crystal symmetry. TIs do not allow for out-of-plane damping-like SOT, which is preferred for switching perpendicular magnetization. Theories suggest that strain effect can break crystal symmetry and lead to unconventional out-of-plane spin polarization and thus damping-like SOT. The strain-mediated current-induced out-of-plane spin polarization has been observed in monolayer TMD material, MoS2. However, strain-mediated unconventional out-of-plane damping-like SOT has not been observed. In this proposed study, we will prepare PMN-PT/TMD/ferromagnet as well to study the strain-mediated SOT. As suggested by theoretical calculations of our collaborators, 2H-NbSe2 is a good candidate to generate out-of-plane damping-like SOT. We will investigate relevant TMD materials and aim to achieve field-free perpendicular magnetization switching using the strain-mediated out-of-plane damping-like SOT.
