16303521.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16303521.value: Low-dimensional materials with strong spin-orbit coupling (SOC) such as topological insulators (TIs) and transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) have emerged as promising options for generating spin-orbit torques (SOTs) to manipulate magnetization in an energy-efficiency way. TIs exhibit a giant SOT efficiency thanks to their unique spin-momentum locking. TMDs can offer SOTs with various directions thanks to their rich crystal symmetries. Theoretically, electric field and strain can control the strength and direction of SOTs generated from TIs and TMDs, which allow us to probe their fundamental physical properties such as band structures and SOC. The introduction of electric field and strain can also potentially reduce the magnetization switching energy due to two reasons: first, they can reduce the magnetic energy barrier or increase SOT strength without introducing ohmic loss; second, the strain effect can break crystal symmetry and introduce out-of-plane damping-like SOT, resulting in a lower switching current without the need of an external bias field. Ferroelectric substrates such as PMN-PT have large piezoelectric coefficients and can provide strong charge doping and strain effect. Charge doping control of charge transport in TIs and strain effect on spin transport in TMDs have been experimentally demonstrated. However, piezoelectric control of SOTs and current-induced magnetization switching in TI and TMD-based heterostructures have not been demonstrated. The applicant has studied the SOTs from TIs and TMDs and demonstrated SOT-induced magnetization switching in TI-based heterostructures at both low and room temperatures. Moreover, the applicant has studied the electric field control of SOTs from TIs at low temperatures and confirmed that the topological surface states mainly contribute to the giant SOT. The applicant has also performed preliminary calculations on strain-mediated SOT switching to achieve field-free switching and established collaborations with experimental experts on PMN-PT. In this proposed study, we will investigate the piezoelectric effect on SOT and SOT-driven magnetization switching in TI and TMD-based heterostructures at room temperature. We will prepare PMN-PT/TI/ferromagnet and PMN-PT/TMD/ferromagnet SOT devices using magnetron sputtering, dry transfer, molecular beam epitaxy (via collaboration), and nanofabrication techniques. Then, we will measure the voltage dependence of SOT and magnetization switching in these devices via different methods. We will collaborate with the theory group to understand the origin of the SOT modulation. Finally, we will explore the potential field-free perpendicular magnetization switching in these devices. The anticipated results will provide fundamental knowledge about the spintronic properties of these low-dimensional materials and help build ultralow-power spintronic memory and computing devices. 具有強自旋軌道耦合 (SOC) 的低維材料，例如拓撲絕緣體 (TI) 和過渡金屬二硫屬化物 (TMD)，已成為產生自旋軌道扭矩 (SOT) 以提高能效控制磁鐵磁矩的有前景的選擇。由於其獨特的自旋動量鎖定，TI 表現出巨大的 SOT 效率。由於其豐富的晶體對稱性，TMD 可以提供各種方向的 SOT。從理論上講，電場和應變可以控制由 TI 和 TMD 產生的 SOT 的強度和方向，這使我們能夠探測它們的基本物理特性，如能帶結構和 SOC。由於兩個原因，電場和應變的引入也可能潛在地降低磁矩翻轉（信息寫入）能量：第一，它們可以在不引入歐姆損耗的情況下降低磁能壘或增加 SOT 強度；其次，應變效應會破壞晶體對稱性並引入平面外阻尼樣 SOT，從而在不需要外部偏置場的情況下利用較低的電流進行磁矩翻轉。 PMN-PT等鐵電襯底具有較大的壓電系數，可以提供強電荷摻雜和應變效應。實驗已經證明了 TI 中電荷傳輸的電荷摻雜控制和 TMD 中自旋傳輸的應變效應。然而，基於 TI 和 TMD 的異質結構中 SOT和電流誘導磁矩翻轉的壓電控制尚未得到證實。申請人研究了來自 TI 和 TMD 的 SOT，並在低溫和室溫下證明了基於 TI 的異質結構中的 SOT 誘導磁矩翻轉。此外，申請人研究了低溫下來自 TI 的 SOT 的電場控制，並確認拓撲表面狀態主要有助於產生巨型 SOT。申請人還對應變調控的 SOT 磁矩翻轉進行了初步計算，以實現無場翻轉，並與 PMN-PT 的實驗專家建立了合作。在這項擬議的研究中，我們將研究室溫下基於 TI 和 TMD 的異質結構中 SOT 和 SOT 驅動的磁矩翻轉的壓電效應。我們將使用磁控濺射、幹法轉移、分子束外延（通過合作）和納米製造技術製備 PMN-PT/TI/鐵磁體和 PMN-PT/TMD/鐵磁體 SOT 器件。然後，我們將通過不同的方法測量這些器件中 SOT 和磁矩翻轉的電壓依賴性。我們將與理論組合作，分析理解SOT 調製的起源。最後，我們將探索這些器件中潛在的無場垂直磁矩翻轉。預期結果將提供有關這些低維材料的自旋電子特性的基礎知識，並有助於構建超低功率自旋電子存儲器和計算器件。

16303521.label: Realisation of objectives
16303521.value: This report addresses all objectives outlined in the Mid-Term Report 6.5. Over the final project period, we have made significant strides in fabricating advanced spin-orbit coupling (SOC) heterostructures, quantitatively demonstrating piezoelectric strain control over spin-orbit torque (SOT), and achieving efficient, field-free magnetization switching. Our work, validated through a combination of experimental innovation and theoretical modeling, establishes a robust platform for next-generation, low-power spintronic devices. Objective 1: Fabrication of PMN-PT/SOC/Ferromagnet Heterostructure Devices (Status: Completed) We have successfully fabricated and characterized a series of functional SOC/ferromagnet heterostructure devices on both conventional SiO₂ and piezoelectric PMN-PT substrates. • All-vdW Heterostructure Achievement: A key milestone was the fabrication of an all-van der Waals (vdW) heterostructure comprising a type-II Weyl semimetal TaIrTe₄ and an above-room-temperature ferromagnet Fe₃GaTe₂. This device demonstrated exceptional performance, achieving full magnetization switching at a low current density at 300 K, with a high SOT effective field efficiency of 0.37 [4]. • Material Platform Expansion: In collaboration with Prof. Xufeng Kou's group (ShanghaiTech University), we have extended our platform to include topological insulators (TI, Bi₂Te₃, Sb₂Te₃) grown on PMN-PT. We couldn’t obtain good results from their SOT devices at this moment. Alternatively, we developed a robust fabrication process for Ta/CoFeB/MgO-based SOT devices on PMN-PT to circumvent the oxidation challenges associated with TaIrTe₄, ensuring device yield and reproducibility [7,8]. Also, we sputtered topological materials WTe2 and studied their SOTs, where strong temperature dependence was observed [1]. • Advanced Device Functionality: Using magnetic topological insulator (MTI) memristors, we demonstrated cryogenic in-memory computing with high energy efficiency and low stochasticity, showcasing the broader application potential of our material systems. Objective 2: Measurement of Piezoelectric Control of SOT (Status: Completed) We have developed a novel methodology and provided direct experimental evidence of strain-mediated SOT control. • Innovative "In-Situ" Strain Control: Dr. Shiwei Tian led the development of an "In-Situ Electric-Field Control" (IEFC) model. Finite Element Analysis confirmed that this method induces the largest and most direct strain on the active Hall bar device (on the third main strain), superior to alternative configurations [7]. • Quantitative SOT Modulation: Using the second-harmonic measurement technique, we quantitatively demonstrated that the strength of both damping-like and field-like torques in Ta/CoFeB/MgO devices can be dynamically tuned by the applied electric field. The torque efficiencies increase under tensile strain (positive voltage) and decrease under compressive strain (negative voltage), providing reversible electrical control [7]. • Theoretical Foundation: Mr. Yiyang Zhang's theoretical work on strain engineering in antiferromagnetic MnTe provided critical insights into how piezoelectric strains can manipulate spin polarization and charge-to-spin conversion processes, offering a predictive guide for our experimental efforts [3]. Also, to compare the piezoelectric control of the SOT device and traditional voltage-controlled magnetic tunnel junction (MTJ) device, we have modeled the voltage-controlled exchange coupling (VCEC) effect and its corresponding device [2]. Also, reinforcement learning has been explored to control the topological magnetic textures [6], which can be potentially tested on a piezoelectric control system. Objective 3: Achievement of Piezoelectric Control of PMA and SOT Switching (Status: Completed) We have successfully integrated piezoelectric control to significantly enhance the performance of SOT-driven magnetization switching. • Drastic Reduction in Switching Current: For Ta-based SOT devices on PMN-PT, we observed a remarkable 58% reduction in the switching current density (from 1.2x10^11 A/m^2 to 5x10^10 A/m^2) compared to identical devices on SiO₂. This is directly attributed to the piezoelectric strain-induced enhancement of the field-like torque component [8]. • Mechanistic Insight via Multi-scale Modeling: A combination of macro-spin modeling and first-principles DFT calculations revealed the origin of this enhancement: the strong interface coupling between Ta and the PMN-PT lattice leads to a piezoelectric distortion-induced dipole moment, causing electronic band splitting and a significant interfacial spin-orbit effect absent in the Ta/SiO₂ system [8]. • Experimental Validation of Interface Coupling: X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) measurements confirmed a lower binding energy of oxygen atoms at the Ta/PMN-PT interface (529.77 eV vs. 531.86 eV for Ta/SiO₂), providing direct evidence of the stronger Ta-O bonding predicted by our DFT models [8]. • Field-free switching with unconventional SOT from low-symmetry materials: TaIrTe₄ has a broken in-plane rotational symmetry. Along the low-symmetry a-axis, SOT with z-spin polarization is generated. As a result, TaIrTe₄ / Fe₃GaTe₂ enabled robust field-free switching, a critical requirement for applications [4]. Besides, low-symmetry correlated antiferromagnets are also explored to identify potentially new SOTs [5]. All objectives outlined in the mid-term report have been met. We met the challenges of generating unconventional SOTs from TIs and heavy metals, and we have utilized the low-symmetry Weyl semimetals to achieve field-free SOT switching. Overall, we have established a comprehensive framework for piezoelectric control of SOT, from material synthesis and device fabrication to experimental characterization and theoretical understanding. The demonstrated ability to electrically manipulate SOT efficiency and achieve substantial reductions in switching power consumption underscores the potential of this approach for developing highly efficient and scalable spintronic memory and logic devices. 16303521.label: Major findings and research outcome
16303521.value: This project successfully established a new platform for low-power spintronic devices by integrating piezoelectric materials with spin-orbit torque (SOT) systems. Our key achievements are summarized below. We developed novel material heterostructures to generate efficient SOT. This includes creating an all-van der Waals device using the Weyl semimetal TaIrTe4 and a ferromagnet (Fe3GaTe2), which achieved energy-efficient, field-free magnetization switching at room temperature [4]. Furthermore, we demonstrated a dramatically temperature-dependent SOT using sputtered topological WTex, with its efficiency increasing over 170 times at cryogenic temperatures [1]. A central finding was the successful electrical control of SOT using piezoelectric strain. We designed a method to directly apply strain to devices using a PMN-PT piezoelectric substrate [7]. This approach allowed us to dynamically tune the SOT efficiencies; specifically, both damping-like and field-like torques were enhanced under tensile strain and reduced under compressive strain [7]. This effect led to a remarkable 58% reduction in the current required to switch the magnetization in Ta-based devices on PMN-PT compared to those on rigid SiO₂ substrates [8]. The mechanism behind this enhancement was identified through multi-scale modeling and experimental validation. First-principles calculations and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy confirmed that the piezoelectric effect induces strong interface coupling in the Ta/PMN-PT system, which modifies the electronic structure and boosts the spin-orbit interaction, an effect absent in Ta/SiO₂ devices [8]. Theoretical work on strain engineering in related materials provided further support for this mechanism [3]. Comparison with the conventional electric field-control of magnetization dynamics [2] indicates the efficiency of this piezoelectric platform. In summary, we have demonstrated a comprehensive pathway from new material discovery to active, piezoelectric control of SOT, resulting in significantly more energy-efficient and functionally superior spintronic devices, including field-free switching. Complementary theoretical studies on advanced control schemes [6] and experimental studies on correlated antiferromagnets [5] support the broader applicability of this platform. References: [1] Z. 16303521.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16303521.value: Building on our successful demonstration of piezoelectric control of spin-orbit torque (SOT), this research opens several promising avenues for future development. The proposed course of action focuses on three key areas: 1. Material Innovation for Topological Insulators (TIs): The current challenge of lattice mismatch between TIs and PMN-PT hinders the effective transfer of piezoelectric strain. Future work will prioritize identifying or engineering alternative piezoelectric substrates with compatible crystal structures to fully unlock the potential of TIs for strain-tunable SOT devices. 2. Achieving Field-Free Switching in Transition Metal Dichalcogenides (TMDs): To realize piezoelectric-controlled field-free switching in TMD-based devices, research will focus on the intrinsic dipole moment of piezoelectric materials. The proposed action is to engineer heterostructures where the piezoelectric polarization directly induces a symmetry-breaking interface field, generating the out-of-plane spin polarization necessary for deterministic switching without an external magnetic field. 3. Fundamental Understanding of Piezoelectric Mechanisms: The piezoelectric effect is multifaceted, involving strain, charge accumulation, and electric potential variations. An urgent and critical next step is to conduct a series of targeted first-principles calculations. This theoretical work will systematically disentangle the individual contributions of each factor to the enhanced SOT, providing a fundamental guide for the rational design of next-generation devices.

16303521.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16303521.value: This project developed a new, highly efficient way to control the magnetic bits that store data in future electronic devices. Traditionally, switching these bits requires significant electrical current and sometimes external magnets. We created ultra-thin, novel material stacks that generate a powerful internal "spin-orbit torque" (SOT), a much more efficient way to flip the magnetic bits. A key breakthrough was using a special "piezoelectric" substrate. When a small voltage is applied, this material strains the device, dramatically boosting SOT efficiency. This allowed us to reduce the switching current by half, which slashes energy consumption by approximately 75%. Crucially, we achieved "field-free switching," meaning the bits can be flipped without any external magnet, a vital requirement for practical, high-density memory. By making the data writing process faster, cheaper, and far more energy-efficient, this research paves the way for the next generation of low-power, high-performance computing and memory technologies (SOT-MRAM), with potential applications from advanced data centers to mobile devices.

16303621.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16303621.value: We study primordial black holes (PBHs) with initial clustering, including the formation mechanism, observational constraints and cosmological implications. PBHs might have been formed in the very early universe, if the primordial density fluctuations at corresponding scales were large enough. Although the possibility of PBHs were proposed decades ago, it has attracted much attention recently, because of the discovery of gravitational waves. Gravitational wave astronomy provides a new observational channel for the study of PBHs. The current observation of intermediate mass black holes from gravitational waves raises more questions about the current black hole formation theory. PBHs have also attracted recent research interest as possible candidate of dark matter, inflationary cosmology, and even solar system astronomy. In the past studies, the PBH distribution is assumed to be initially unclustered (though there may be clustering due to late-time evolution). We propose that the PBH distribution may be initially highly clustered, which can be realized by a model of multi-stream inflation that happened in the very early universe. If the PBHs are initially highly clustered, then current observational constraints and the estimation of PBH binary coalescence rates have to be thoroughly reconsidered. Observationally, we are not likely to reside in a PBH-rich regime. The observational constraints involving the Milky Way or the Local Group no longer apply. Theoretically, the clustered PBHs increase the possibility of forming PBH binaries and enhance the event rate of mergers. Clustered PBHs can provide more gravitational wave signals given the current observational constraints from optical probes. Thus, our study may open up a window of searching for PBH events in space-based gravitational wave observatories. In our previous work, in terms of PBH abundance, only a narrow part of the parameter regime is studied, because of the simplicity of the analysis. We propose to study more strongly clustered PBHs, including the disruption by other PBHs and the effect of further clustering. For PBHs with initial clustering, many past observational constraints need reconsideration. We propose to study the formation mechanism of the initially clustered PBHs in detail. The initially clustered PBHs can be generated from multi-stream inflation. We propose to use a numerical study on the dynamics of multi-stream inflation to obtain better information about the shape and distribution of the PBH-rich patches. 我們建議研究原初黑洞的初始結團問題，包括其形成機制、觀測限制和宇宙學。原初黑洞是早期宇宙中形成的黑洞。一些早期宇宙模型預言，小尺度密度擾動很劇烈。當這些密度擾動回到視界，原初黑洞可以因引力坍縮而形成。最近，原初黑洞的可能性吸引了很多的注意。這是因為，我們進入了引力波天文學時代。這為原初黑洞研究提供了有力的工具。並且，原初黑洞也可能是暗物質的候選者，與早期宇宙，甚至太陽系物理都可能有聯繫。在過去的研究中，一般假設原初黑洞初始分佈是統計上均勻的 (儘管非均勻分佈可以由宇宙晚期演化得到)。最近，我們提出，原初黑洞的初始分佈可能是高度結團的。這種結團性可以由早期宇宙的多流暴漲模型得到。如果原初黑洞的初始分佈高度結團，我們很可能不位於原初黑洞很多的區域。所以，銀河系或本星系群對原初黑洞的限制不再有效。並且，原初黑洞的結團增加雙黑洞形成的概率，所以增加黑洞的合併率。我們的研究為空間引力波探測器上探測原初黑洞開啟了窗口。在我们過去的工作中，在原初黑洞組分方面，我們只研究了很小一部分參數區間。我們建議研究結團更強的原初黑洞，包括雙黑洞被其它黑洞破壞，進一步結團以及其它效應。對初始結團的原初黑洞，很多觀測結果需要重新解釋。我們建議進一步研究結團雙黑洞的形成機制。這可以從多流暴漲得到。我們建議用格點模擬來研究多流暴漲的動力學和富原初黑洞區域的形狀統計。我們也建議用暗空穴模型研究哈勃參數問題和原初黑洞結團的關係。由於公眾對黑洞、原初宇宙和引力波等問題感興趣，我們也計劃在公眾報告中提及我們的研究，為香港的科學教育做貢獻。

16303621.label: Realisation of objectives
16303621.value: The dynamics of strongly clustered PBH is studied. We proposed a 'standard timers' approach, to show that the bubbles continaing strongly clustered primordial black holes can be considered as timers to measure the time lapse after the big bang. Various observational consequences are also studied for the standard timers. In addition, we have studied the CMB implications for Gpc void scenarios. We have performed lattice simulation for multi-stream inflation. This is the first paper to use lattice simulation to study multi-stream inflation. New observational effects are identified from simulation, which are difficult to see from analytical estimations. We have studied how gravitational lensing can be used to distinguish black holes and possible wormholes. In addition, in the standard timer studies, observational consequences are studied.

16303621.label: Major findings and research outcome
16303621.value: We have published five research papers on leading journals of theorecial physics and cosmology, supported in part by this project. (1) 'Lattice simulation of multi-stream inflation' (JCAP 03 (2022) 03, 006) is the first lattice simulation paper on multi-stream inflation. We identified much richer structures of cosmic perturbations than the over-simplified analytical estimate indicates. (2) 'Cosmological standard timers from unstable primordial relics' (Eur.Phys.J.C 83 (2023) 10, 913) proposed the new idea 'standard timers' to measure cosmic ages, and to use clustered black holes as standard timers. Various observational consequences are discussed. (3) 'Reconciling cosmic dipolar tensions with a gigaparsec void' (Phys.Rev.D 111 (2025) 10, 103502) studied in detail how cosmic inhomogenity (with clustered PBH is a possible cause) affect observables, expecially CMB related observables. This gives constraints on PBH clustering rate if the clustering is on very large (GPc) scales. And we point out that these inhomogenities can resolve the dipolar tension in cosmology. (Note that the paper has gone through a very long review process. Although it's published in 2025, but the first submission is in 2022.) (4) 'On the decoherence of primordial gravitons' (JHEP 06 (2023) 101) is mainly on cosmological perturbation theory, but is also partially related to the current project, since how gravitational fluctuations transit from quantum to classical is related to the formation of PBH. (5) In 'Microlensing effect of a charged spherically symmetric wormhole' ( Phys.Rev.D 107 (2023) 2, 024022), we have studied microlensing of clustered exotic objects, and compared the effect of wormhole and black hole.

16303621.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16303621.value: We have completed objectives of this project. While there are many possible further possibilities to explore. Especially, (1) For the lattice simulation of multi-stream inflation: we are preparing a manuscript on further results, especialy the power spectrum of density fluctuations and gravitational waves. This will show further details about how multi-stream inflation is related to cosmic observations, including PBH formation. (2) We have on-going work on MCMC and finding the best fit parameters for the gigaparsec void model. This work will further verify how our void-type clustering fits current observational data.

16303721.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16303721.value: In quantum materials, elementary excitations of electronic, structural and magnetic origin, are essential ingredients leading toward the emergence of exotic quantum phenomena, from insulator-metal transition, colossal magnetoresistance (CMR) to high-Tc superconductivity. Optical spectroscopy has proven to be an indispensable tool for investigating these interacting elementary excitations, that span over a broad energy scale from milli-electron volt (meV) to electron volt (eV). The ever-developing ultrafast science has ushered in a new era of optical spectroscopy at femtosecond and picosecond timescales, referred to as ultrafast pump-probe spectroscopy, for investigating key interactions at fundamental time and energy scales, and even for driving ultrafast phase transitions in condensed matter systems. Using ultrafast pump-probe spectroscopy, we recently discovered, in the strain-engineered CMR manganite La2/3Ca1/3MnO3 (LCMO) thin film, a novel photo-induced transition pathway into “hidden” metastable states. Strikingly, the strained LCMO thin film demonstrates an extreme photo-susceptibility to ultrafast laser excitation, and subsequently evolves through multi-stage metastable states with distinct conductivity. Evidenced by a multi-modal experimental approach involving far-field pump-probe spectroscopy, near-field optical microscopy and ultrafast X-ray scattering, all metastable states induced by photoexcitation are found highly homogeneous with well-defined conductivity, in stark contrast to the inhomogeneous (phase-separated) phase transition induced by other means. To date, much of the underlying physics still remains far from understanding. Here, we propose to leverage the cutting-edge supercontinuum THz spectroscopy for a time- and frequency-resolved dynamic investigation of electronic and vibrational elementary excitations, and their mutual interaction, not only in the non-equilibrium state (perturbative regime), but also along the photo-induced phase transition pathway (non-perturbative regime) in the strain-engineered LCMO thin film. This will enrich our understanding of the photo-induced effect and the pertinent dynamics at the microscopic level, not only in the fascinating CMR manganite, but also in many other strongly correlated materials susceptible to photoexcitation. Such endeavor may significantly further our knowledge on quantum materials for searching and developing novel functionalities on demand. 在量子材料中，電子、晶格和磁性自由度對應的元激發模式和它們之間的相互作用， 是催生這類材料中新奇量子物相的關鍵因素，產生了從金屬-絕緣體相變、龐磁阻現象到高溫超導電性等諸多物理現象。覆蓋從毫電子伏特 (meV) 到電子伏特 (eV) 的現代光譜學測量手段，被證明是揭示各種元激發模式之間多體相互作用的重要研究方法。持續發展的超快科學和隨之產生的泵浦-探測光譜學手段，已經將我們帶入了皮秒甚至飛秒超快時間尺度上非平衡動力學的全新研究領域。這一不斷發展的新技術，使得針對量子材料中關鍵相互作用所對應的本徵時間和能量尺度上的基礎物理開展光譜學研究，甚至實現超快時間尺度的光誘導相變調控成為可能。 最近，使用超快泵浦-探測光譜學手段，我們在異質節應力調節下的鑭鈣錳氧（La2/3Ca1/3MnO3）薄膜中，發現了通向隱藏亞穩態的奇異光誘導相變通道。令人驚奇的是，應力調控下的鑭鈣錳氧薄膜展示出對超快脈衝激發的極強響應特性，在強光場作用下相變進入一個具有可調控電導率的多級亞穩態。通過結合使用遠場超快光譜學、近場掃描顯微光譜學和超快X射線衍射等多模式測量手段，我們發現該多級相變路徑上的各亞穩態均表現出高度的均勻性和明確的電導率。這一隱藏屬性，與該材料體系在其他傳統調控手段作用下，導致的非均勻相（相分離），有本質的不同。目前，該光誘導相變涉及的微觀機理尚不明確。因而，我們提出利用前沿超寬頻太赫茲光譜學，對鑭鈣錳氧薄膜在兩類不同擾動強度下（微擾動下的非平衡態和強擾動下的光誘導相變），電子和聲子元激發以及他們之間相互作用的超快動力學過程進行深入研究。這不僅會豐富我們對於龐磁阻錳氧化物光誘導相變的認識，也會加深我們對於其他表現出類似光誘導相變現象的強關聯電子體系中關鍵物理的理解，並可能對探尋和發展強關聯量子材料中的其他新奇物性具有推動作用。

16303821.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16303821.value: 在晶體中，谷自由度是指具有不同動量的簡並能量極值，這個自由度作為贗自旋可以與真自旋一樣編碼和處理信息。谷贗自旋最早在二十世紀七十年代在矽反轉層中的二維電子氣被提出和研究。隨著自旋電子學的快速發展，谷電子學自然地出現。谷電子學中一個重要的話題是探索能夠實現谷自由度的材料及能夠有效調控谷自由度的方法。 二維材料尤其是二硫化鉬為代表的過渡金屬硫化物的發現，在過去十餘年極大地促進了谷電子學的發展。在二硫化鉬類的TMDs中，兩個擁有非零自旋極化的谷由時間反演對稱性聯繫 ， Kramers理論因此保證它們的自旋極化相反，從而形成一個強自旋谷鎖定。自旋谷鎖定可以極大地增加谷和自旋的去極化時間，因為自旋翻轉需要同時改變谷指標，反之亦然。由於自旋谷霍爾效應，多種方式可以實現二硫化鉬類過渡金屬硫化物的谷與自旋自由度的動態控製，從而實現編碼在谷和自旋流的信息的快速處理。 儘管取得了實質性的進展，大部分谷電子學材料是非磁性的，並且在現有的谷材料實現信息的存儲依舊存在挑戰。本項目的主要目標是在磁性材料中探索具有強自旋谷鎖定的材料，從而能夠在一個材料中同時實現強自旋谷鎖定和非易失信息存儲。 由於在磁性材料中不存在時間反演對稱性，必須尋找另外一個保證谷能量簡並的對稱性。這啟發我們提出一種新的自旋谷鎖定：谷之間由晶體對稱性保護，稱為晶格對稱性配對的自旋谷鎖定。 我們首先將會基於群論，k ∙p分析和緊束縛模型判別能擁有C-paired SVL的合適晶體對稱性和晶格結構，然後我們將研究晶格對稱性配對的自旋谷鎖定材料對於外加應力和電場的響應。以這些理論結果作為堅實的基礎，我們將會找尋真實的可以實現晶格對稱性配對的自旋谷鎖定材料並通過第一性原理計算檢驗它們的性質。 本項目將會提高我們對谷自由度相關物理現象的理解，拓展其在磁性系統的相應研究並為實驗研究和潛在的谷電子器件提供新的材料平臺。

16303821.label: Realisation of objectives
16303821.value: Antiferromagnets are magnetic materials with zero net magnetization and the sublattices with different magnetization directions are connected by crystal symmetry. Conventional antiferromagnets have spin-degenerate electronic energy bands guaranteed by effective inversion and time-reversal symmetries. In 2021, the PI predicted a class of materials where there are no effective time-reversal symmetries such that the energy bands become spin-split [Nat. Commun. 12, 2846 (2021)]. We refer to these spin-split antiferromagnets as C-paired spin-valley locking (SVL) materials, in which the valleys with opposite spin polarization are connected by a crystal (C) symmetry. A subset of C-paired SVL materials with collinear magnetic order and spin-splitting without spin-orbit coupling are called altermagnets [Phys. Rev. X 12, 040501 (2022)]. The spin-split energy bands give rise to spin-polarized current and novel phenomena such as spin torques and giant piezomagnetism. In this project, we carried out diverse research works on C-paired SVL materials, ranging from fundamental classifications based on crystal symmetry to identifying their signatures in candidate materials. And we have realized all our proposed objectives. (1) Identify the symmetry requirement and suitable lattice structures for C-paired spin-valley locking We developed a rigorous framework that identify the symmetry requirements for C-paired spin-valley locking [Phys. Rev. X 15, 021083 (2025)]. Besides requiring the absence of effective inversion and time-reversal symmetry, the degeneracy of a given momentum is also determined by symmetry operations in the little cogroups and the coset representatives. Our comprehensive symmetry analysis identified 38 magnetic point groups that can host C-paired SVL. Applying our algorithm to materials databases and performed high-throughput first-principles calculations, we identified 142 experimentally verified antiferromagnets as candidate C-paired SVL materials. With this rigorous and general theory, we can classify the spin splitting and determine the symmetry requirements for effects such as spin-polarized current, anomalous Hall effect and piezomagnetism in antiferromagnets with C-paired SVL. C-paired SVL materials or altermagnets are intensively studied in recent years is because they can demonstrate effects that are typical in ferromagnets but absent in spin-degenerate antiferromagnets, prompting applications in antiferromagnetic spintronics. We collaborated with experimental groups and applied our symmetry analysis to real materials as described below. (2) Study the response of C-paired SVL system to external fields, such as strain and electric field The magnetization dynamics of a magnetic material can be determined by spin torques generated by a spin-polarized current and external fields. Electrical manipulation of magnetic order can be used for information technology and spintronics applications such as digital logic and memory devices. While some C-paired SVL materials may not be compatible with spin-polarized current and anomalous Hall effect, in reality, strain, spin-orbit coupling or noncollinear magnetization direction could change the relevant magnetic space group. We carefully examined the origin of these effects in experiments and utilize them to manipulate the magnetic order for spintronic applications. Although some C-paired SVL materials show small net magnetization in experiments, clarifying the origins of the spin-dependent and Berry curvature effects help distinguish C-paired SVL materials and ferromagnetic materials. We realized electrical 180° switching of Neel order in collinear C-SVL material Mn5Si3 [Sci. Adv. 10, eadn0479 (2024)]. We clarified how the deterministic switching and readout of Neel vector is achieved in Mn5Si3. We conclude that an external magnetic field gives rise to a damping-like torque that makes the energy barrier for the two Neel order orientations to be asymmetric. And the Neel vector can be readout electrically by anomalous Hall effect which arises from non-zero Berry curvature due to presence of spin-orbit coupling. Importantly, our theoretical analysis helped guide the experiments to confirm the observed effects indeed originate from Neel vector and spin-split bands instead of a nonzero magnetization. The small magnetization may arise from magnetic impurities or canted magnetic moments. Our theory predicts that the anomalous Hall effect originates from the spin-split bands and is sensitive to the Neel vector and remains almost unchanged when the small net magnetization is reversed, consistent the experiments. In a separate experiment, we study anomalous Nernst effect in strained Mn5+xSi3-x thin films grown on Al2O3 substrate [Phys. Rev. Appl. 23, 044066 (2025)]. The epitaxial strain changes the crystal structure and helps stabilize a collinear antiferromagnetic phase with C-paired SVL. We measured the anomalous Nernst conductivity of Mn5+xSi3-x thin films with various doping doses which affect the chemical potential and concentration of impurities. We used first-principles calculations and tight-binding model to describe the electronic structures of these thin films. The non-monotonic dependence of the doping level is consistent with the intrinsic mechanism in which the anomalous Nernst conductivity is strongly enhances when the Fermi level is closer to band intersections which are Berry curvature hot spots. Besides manipulating the Neel vector in a C-paired SVL material in a certain magnetic space group, we explicitly demonstrate that the control of the properties of C-paired SVL materials by manipulating the crystal symmetry [Nature 638, 645 (2025)]. Our experimental collaborators prepared CrSb thin films in three configurations with different crystal structures due to surface orientations and epitaxial strain. Our symmetry analysis determined whether a magnetic field is required for deterministic switching of the Neel vector and whether the spin-split electronic structure contributes to a nonzero anomalous Hall effect. The efficient switching of the Neel vector is due to Dzyaloshinskii interactions from spin-orbit coupling and interfacial symmetry breaking. We clarified the symmetry requirements for deterministic switching of Neel vector and anomalous Hall effect in C-paired SVL materials in the above experiments. These effects enable writing and reading out the Neel vector for applications in spintronics. Although spin-orbit coupling is necessary and there may be a small net magnetization from canted magnetic moments, we showed that the effects still originate from the manipulation of the Neel vector and the spin-split bands rather than the net magnetization. Therefore, we showed C-paired SVL materials are fundamentally distinct from ferromagnets, they have small net magnetization and are sensitive to crystal symmetry. (3) Search for C-paired SVL materials and study their properties Besides studying the transport signatures and magnetization dynamics in the above-mentioned C-paired SVL materials, we explicitly identified the spin-splitting in a candidate C-paired SVL material RbV2Te2O [Nat. Phys. 21, 760 (2025)]. This material is in the same materials class as V2Se2O which the PI predicted in 2021. Our experimental collaborators explicitly identified the spin-splitting with spin- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy which agreed well with our first-principles calculations. Moreover, we studied the quasiparticle interference pattern measured with scanning tunnelling microscope. Compared with our theoretical calculations using Wannier tight-binding model, we confirm that scattering between spin-split bands with opposite spin polarization is forbidden, providing direct evidence of C-paired SVL in this material. Besides predicting C-paired SVL materials using symmetry analysis and high-throughput first-principles calculations in bulk materials as mentioned above, we also studied the occurrence of C-paired SVL in van der Waals materials with nanoengineering. We discovered coexistence of C-paired SVL and sliding ferroelectricity in moire superlattices of magnetic van der Waals materials [Sci. China: Phys. Mech. Astron. 68, 297511 (2025)]. And we studied the C-paired SVL by arranging one-dimensional magnetic chains [Phys. Rev. B 112, L041404 (2025)]. These proposals highlight the ubiquity and tunability of C-paired SVL in artificially engineered magnetic structures without inversion and time-reversal symmetries.

16303821.label: Major findings and research outcome
16303821.value: Antiferromagnets (AFMs) are magnetic materials with compensated sublattices, traditionally hosting spin-degenerate electronic bands. In a pivotal 2021 prediction, we identified a new class of AFMs where crystal symmetry, in the absence of time-reversal symmetry, generates significant spin-splitting in the electronic structure [Nat. Commun. 12, 2846 (2021)]. We term these materials C-paired spin-valley locking (SVL) systems, a category that includes the rapidly emerging field of altermagnetism. This spin-splitting enables phenomena typically exclusive to ferromagnets, such as spin-polarized currents and novel responses, within a zero-moment antiferromagnetic framework, opening new avenues for spintronics. This project successfully established a comprehensive foundation for C-paired SVL materials. First, we developed a rigorous symmetry classification, identifying 38 magnetic point groups capable of hosting C-paired SVL and uncovering 142 candidate materials from high-throughput computational screening [Phys. Rev. X 15, 021083 (2025)]. Second, we guided and interpreted key experiments demonstrating functional control. We achieved and explained the electrical 180° switching of the Néel vector in Mn₅Si₃, showing how spin-polarized currents manipulate the order and how the anomalous Hall effect enables its readout [Sci. Adv. 10, eadn0479 (2024)]. We further demonstrated that these properties are governed by crystal symmetry by analyzing CrSb thin films on different substrates, providing design principles for field-free switching [Nature 638, 645 (2025)]. Third, we provided direct spectroscopic evidence of C-paired SVL in RbV₂Te₂O, where spin-resolved photoemission confirmed the band splitting and quasiparticle interference patterns revealed spin-forbidden scattering [Nat. Phys. 21, 760 (2025)]. We also extended the concept to low-dimensional systems, predicting its emergence in moiré superlattices and 1D magnetic chains. In summary, this work has delivered a complete theoretical framework, identified a wealth of candidate materials, and validated through collaboration the unique spintronic functionalities of C-paired SVL systems, establishing them as a distinct and promising platform for next-generation magnetic devices.

16303821.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16303821.value: Our works focused on electrical detection and manipulation of Neel order in metallic C-paired spin-valley locking materials. In the future we will study magnetization dynamics of insulating C-paired spin-valley locking materials, where the excitations are the collective oscillations of the magnetic moments known as magnons. In magnetic insulator, the magnetic order may couple to electromagnetic wave, acoustic wave or a temperature gradient and the mechanisms are fundamentally different from the metallic counterparts. We will also study materials that support C-paired spin-valley locking and other properties at the same time, such as ferroelectricity and superconductivity and non-trivial topology. Coexistence of ferroelectricity and C-paired spin-valley locking in a material may allow the Neel order to be switched directly by an electric field rather than via spin-polarized current, this could lead to energy-efficient spintronic devices. Since superconductors may emerge from spin fluctuations and some superconductors such as cuprates and iron-based superconductors are closely related to antiferromagnetism. However, most superconductors involve electron pairs with opposite spin and momentum, this is incompatible with C-paired spin-valley locking in which the energy bands are spin-split and time-reversal symmetry is broken. Therefore, exotic spin triplet superconductivity could emerge from the interplay of C-paired spin-valley locking and superconductivity.

16303821.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16303821.value: In crystalline solids, valleys—energy extrema in momentum space—can encode information as a pseudospin, forming the basis of valleytronics. While proposed decades ago, the field was revitalized by two-dimensional materials like transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs). In these non-magnetic TMDs, time-reversal symmetry enforces a spin-valley locking (SVL), where the valley index is tied to the spin, enabling dynamic control of valley and spin for information processing. However, a significant challenge remains: most valleytronic materials are non-magnetic, lacking inherent memory capability. We overcome this by exploring SVL in magnetic materials to integrate non-volatile memory with valley and spin control in a single system. Since magnetism breaks time-reversal symmetry, we propose a new "C-paired SVL" mechanism, where crystal symmetry protects the valley degeneracy. We have identified many real material candidates such as Mn5Si3, CrSb, RbV2Te2O, and verified them in experiments with our collaborators. Moreover, following this new concept, we further realized current-induced switching in Mn5Si3, readable via the anomalous Hall effect. Furthermore, we demonstrated symmetry governs these responses, as shown in CrSb thin films, where we established design principles for field-free switching and device implementation. Our work provides the theoretical foundation for C-paired SVL spintronics.

16304021.label: Project Objectives
16304021.value: Infer for the abyssal upwelling and its control on the South China Sea circulation, via a data assimilation approach within an idealized state estimate that is computationally inexpensive, thereby allowing for a thorough investigation of the distribution of, and sensitivity to, the abyssal upwelling. Creation of a realistic regional state estimate using the Estimating the Circulation and Climate (ECCO) framework, that will return dynamically consistent solution constrained to actual observational data over the satellite era and in a more comprehensive Ocean Global Circulation Model (MITgcm), to infer for the abyssal upwelling in the South China Sea, which is difficult to obtain from observations. Using the inferred abyssal upwelling data to inform parameterizations in ocean general circulation models, a crucial dynamical process that is expected to play a key role in improving the numerical modeling of the ocean, and have consequences for global ocean forecasting as well as climate change projection. Set up and establish the central machinery and framework in the form of a South China Sea state estimate to explore questions related to biogeochemical processes (with consequences for ecological monitoring and conservation) and observational system design (via sensitivity analyses and uncertainty quantification, to inform where best to direct observational efforts) in the future.

16304021.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16304021.value: The South China Sea (SCS), being the largest marginal sea in the Western Pacific region, greatly impacts the region's ecological and human activities. The regional ocean circulation is intimately coupled to the regional ecological systems through its capacity in transporting large amounts of heat, carbon, and nutrients. Identifying, understanding and constraining the underlying dynamical processes that control the circulation are therefore crucial for predicting how the circulation will evolve in the future. While we have a reasonable idea and understanding of the dynamical processes that are controlling the circulation, further theoretical, numerical, and observational efforts are required to constrain these processes, particularly those that are inherently difficult to observe and possess uncertainties in their representation in predictive numerical models, thereby affecting the modeled ocean circulation. One such physical process, and the focus of this project, is the abyssal upwelling in the SCS. Abyssal upwelling is inherently difficult to observe given the many practical complications in conducting continued observations of the deep parts of the ocean, and it is also extremely important for the overall regional circulation because of the associated vertical coupling. While previous works have focused on the effect of varying the imposed distribution of abyssal upwelling on the modeled circulation in free-running numerical ocean models, the project will aim to answer a complementary and more difficult question, namely, what should the imposed abyssal upwelling be to obtain a modeled ocean circulation state that is close to the observational data we have to date? This inference problem is to be answered within a consistent regional state estimate, i.e., a data assimilating model that results in a modeled ocean state that is consistent with observational data and being a time-continuous numerical solution of the equations of ocean dynamics, with the control process returned as part of the solution. Idealized and realistic regional state estimates will be created to infer for the distribution of abyssal upwelling in the SCS, for computing the circulation and its sensitivity to abyssal upwelling, and inform on the parameterization of abyssal upwelling in predictive numerical ocean models. High impact extensions enabled by the regional state estimate created here relating to monitoring, predicting and designing of field observational systems - to eventually include physical as well as biogeochemical and ecological processes - are anticipated for the future. 南中國海是東南亞區內最大的邊緣海，她的海洋環流輸送大量熱量、碳和養分，直接和強烈影響地區的生態及人類活動，為應對未來諸如與糧食安全和相關的漁業管理，識別、了解和約束海洋環流的動態過程是一個重要的研究題目。雖然我們對海洋環流的動態有一定的理解，但為了能夠提升預測海洋環流數值模型的模擬能力，我們需要進一步加強對相關理論、數值和觀測的工作，來減低對海洋環流形態固有預測困難的不確定性影響，從而增加計算推測數字模型的代表性。 本提案的重點聚焦在南中國海的深淵上升。深淵上升和其相關的垂直耦合對整體的區域環流有很大的影響，但觀察海洋深處的深淵上升流是異常困難的，之前是集中以自由運行的數值海洋模型去硏究深淵上升的變化，然後量化它的影響。本提案考慮補充更困難的問題：我們擁有海洋的觀測數據，但應該選擇什麼樣的深淵上升流令到海洋模型的模擬結果最接近海洋的觀測數據？我們將使用一個能夠把觀測數據同化的海洋環流數值模型，建立一個南中國海的模型來推斷區內深海上升流的分佈，計算環流及其對深海上升流的敏感性，並參數化預測深海上升流的數值。這一個能夠數據化的南中國海模型，預計能在未來會大大影響成為物理學以及地球生物化學和生態過程擴展的基礎，有助觀測系統的監測、預測和設計。

16304021.label: Realisation of objectives
16304021.value: Objectives 2, 3, 4 have been achieved and is essentially completely documented within the PhD thesis of Yongsu NA, who defended his thesis in August 2025. The work utilises the MITgcm model to first create a South China Sea ocean model that can be run in predictive or forward mode, before coupling it to the adjoint framework within MITgcm and interfacing with existing observational datasets to allow the model to run in adjoint mode in order to perform the regional state estimation. Numerous numerical instabilities and computational issues arose (the problems were anticipated, but the degree of technicality to fix those was not), but these have been largely circumvented as well as documented in the thesis for record keeping purposes. In principle (and as mentioned by the external examiner of the PhD thesis), the forward model by itself could be a subject of a PhD, and having the overall makings of an adjoint model can be another PhD thesis by itself. In that regard the work was very challenging and technical in nature, and some aspects will need further refinement still, but the overall framework has been set up and it is ongoing work to turn that work in relevant publications. It is anticipated that this work tackles the high technical hurdle for ocean adjoint modelling in the form of a regional ocean state estimate, and the subsequent work based on this first substantial investment will be much more achievable. Once Objectives 2, 3, 4 were essentially achieved using a realistic model, Objective 1 based on an idealised model was regarded lower priority, and it was decided that resources were better utilised to support PhD students for some tangential and easier work, namely the development of parameterisations, investigating the biogeochemical response and deployment of machine learning algorithms in analogous ocean models created as part of Objectives 2, 3, 4. In that regard, the under-achievement in Objective 1 is compensated by the publications that did result from the re-focusing of research efforts.

16304021.label: Major findings and research outcome
16304021.value: A major outcome of this work was the creation of a South China Sea regional state estimate that allows for observational data assimilation, as well as sensitivity calculations via the associated adjoint model. The creation of the model follows the ECCO framework, focused over the South China Sea region, and at a higher spatial resolution. The resulting model was validated accordingly with known data and features of the South China Sea, before we proceed to perform inference and sensitivity calculations on the vertical diffusivity. The inferred sensitivity of the flow around the Luzon strait area was considered, which in turn led to further study into the underlying mechanisms and eventually to updating/refining the existing theory. Additional spin-offs from the present project include considering gyre dynamics and its represented biogeochemistry, as well as some machine learning studies of the underlying turbulence. A total of six papers resulted from this grant, with two PhD students trained.

16304021.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16304021.value: The regional statement requires some minor refinement, but will form the basis of further work into probing the dependence on the South China Sea circulation to a variety of physical factors. The idealised work and the regional state estimate will likely form the basis of future work into uncertainty quantification and observational system design via further RGC grants.

16304021.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16304021.value: Data assimilating models combine the benefits of the dense coverage of numerical models corrected accordingly by sparse observational data. For this work we have created a regional model of the South China Sea that is data assimilation, with an aim to investigate numerous scientific questions that were previous not computationally possible with conventional methodologies. We use the model to investigate how the South China Sea circulation is dependent on a hard to observe process, improving our understanding of the circulation, as well as using the study to inform where we may want to carry observations in the future.

16304321.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16304321.value: 探索未來對撞機上的新物理

16304321.label: Project Objectives
16304321.value: Explore physics opportunities at the future ``precision machines'' (e.g., the Z and/or Higgs factories of FCC-ee, CEPC, ILC and CLIC). The benchmark case is to study the ``b to c tau nu'' physics at the future Z factories. This will advance our understanding on lepton flavor universality (LFU). This research is planned to conduct via three steps. First, we will study the ``b to c tau nu'' physics via Bs and Bc meson decays (e.g., the decays of ``Bs to D_s^* tau nu'' and ``Bc to eta_c tau nu''). Then the analysis will be extended to Lambda_b decays (e.g., the decay of ``Lambda_b to Lambda_c^* tau nu''). It is well-known that the production rates of Bs, Bc and Lambda_b hadrons at the future Z factories of the CEPC and the FCC-ee can be much higher than those at Belle II, because of the relative heaviness of these b hadrons. At last, we will study the implications of the analysis outcomes for the relevant new physics. Explore physics opportunities at the future ``discovery machines'' (e.g., FCC-hh, SppC and muon collider). The benchmark case is to search for flavor mediators at the muon collider. The flavor mediators extensively exist in physics beyond the Standard Model (SM). As a source to deform the SM flavor structure, they have been suggested to explain the LFU anomalies observed in last years. Depending on the concrete mechanisms to address these anomalies, the mass scale of these flavor mediators can vary from TeV to above 50 TeV. This mass range could be fully covered by a high beam-energy muon collider. The first target in this context is the family non-universal Z' boson which can be searched for via the resonant ``mu mu to b s'' production. This analysis can be extended to non-resonant searches, to probe or constrain the four-fermion mu-mu-f-f' operators. Another target is leptoquarks. At the muon collider, leptoquarks can be produced both in pair, either via the quark-mediated t channel or via the vector boson splitting, and singly by turning on the muon ``parton distribution function''. Note, in response to any potential progress or breakthroughs achieved at the LHC during the fund period, the PI is also ready to adjust his research in this project, in order to explore the implications of these progress/breakthroughs for physics at the future colliders in a timely manner.

16304321.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16304321.value: 宇宙充滿了各種各樣的謎團。譬如，我們並不完全清楚構成宇宙物質的基本粒子是什麼，它們如何相互作用並推動宇宙演化，以及隱藏在這些粒子後面的基本原理是什麼。 歷史上，對這些自然界謎團的探索，一直是人類社會發展的第一推動力。 對撞機是粒子物理學家探索自然之謎的最強大的工具之一。就像顯微鏡一樣，對撞機可以讓我們觀察微觀世界的內部結構並測量其特性。自 1960 年代第一臺對撞機誕生以來，粒子物理學家在對撞機上已經發現了多種輕子和夸克的新成員，強相互作用力和弱相互作用力的載體，以及“上帝粒子”—－希格斯玻色子。這些發現極大地促進了我們對自然界基本規律的理解。 受這些偉大成就的影響，也爲了探索未解之謎（希格斯玻色子的性質、暗物質的組成、輕子和夸克味結構的起源等等），粒子物理學家計劃在未來幾十年內建造新的對撞機。這些提議的對撞機項目的研發正在積極進行中。根據其任務的性質，這些對撞機可以粗略地分爲“精密型”機器和“發現型”機器。前者旨在以前所未有的高精度測量電弱物理學、希格斯玻色子甚至味物理學，而後者旨在通過更高能粒子碰撞直接發現新現象或新粒子。由於其任務的多樣性，這些對撞機通常計劃在多種技術參數場景中運行。 針對這一進展，PI 提議利用下一代對撞機提供的機遇來探索上述未解之謎。該提案中的一個基本案例便是利用未來 Z 工廠和 μ 子對撞機的豐富數據以及乾淨背景來研究輕子的味普遍性。自多年之前，PI就一直在從事未來對撞機上的物理研究（曾獲UGC/RGC的項目支持），並爲相關的學術界服務。 PI 相信這些經驗將確保該項目的成功完成。

16304321.label: Realisation of objectives
16304321.value: Objective 1 was mainly addressed in publication No. 1. In this paper, we presented a systematic study on the LFU test in the Z factories at a future e+e− collider such as CEPC or FCC-ee. We investigated the sensitivities of measuring the LFU-violating observables of b→cτν, i.e., RJ/ψ, RDs, RD∗s and RΛc, by analyzing the decays of Bs and Bc mesons and Λb baryons. For this purpose, we develop the strategies for event reconstruction, based on the track information significantly. We have also explored the sensitivity robustness against detector performance and its potential improvement with the message of event shape or beyond the b-hadron decays. Particularly, because of my leading contribution and expertise in this field, I was invited to co-lead a community initiative, aiming to generate a white paper to show the landscape of flavor physics at the Circular Electron-Positron Collider (CEPC) based on its baseline design. Designed to operate in various modes, particularly at the Z pole, the CEPC is expected to produce 4 Tera Z bosons, enabling precise measurements of Z boson couplings and investigations into flavor physics through heavy-flavored quarks and leptons from clean Z decays. This collective effort finally led to ninety-page-long paper No. 3 which has been accepted for publication as a cover article in Chinese Physics C (https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/1674-1137/adf1f0/pdf). Objective 2 was mainly addressed in publication No. 2. Because of for the planned high beam energy, the future muon collider is often viewed as a ``discovery machine'' for new physics. In this paper, we explored the ability of the future TeV-scale muon collider to search for Majorana and Dirac Heavy Neutral Leptons (HNLs) produced via EW bosons. Here, the HNLs are recognized as significant flavor mediators in the lepton sector and have been extensively studied in the context of neutrino physics for decades. Employing a model-independent approach, we present an estimation of the production and decay rate of HNLs over a mass range between 200 GeV and 9.5 TeV in two benchmark collider proposals with s√=3,10 TeV, as well as an estimation of the dominant Standard Model background.

16304321.label: Major findings and research outcome
16304321.value: Paper No. 1: We interpreted the projected sensitivities in the Standard-Model (SM) effective field theory, by combining the LFU tests of b → cτ ν investigated in this paper and the measurements of b → sτ +τ − and b → s¯νν studied in literatures, and found that the limits on the LFU-violating energy scale can be pushed up to ∼ O(10) TeV for ∼ O(1) Wilson coefficients at Tera-Z factories. Paper No. 2: By simulating the productions and decays of HNLs over a mass range between 200 GeV and 9.5 TeV with the muon-collider beam energy √s = 3, 10 TeV, as well as the dominant SM background, we found that exclusion limits for the mixing between the HNLs and SM neutrinos can be as low as ~ O(10^-6). At the same constraint level, the muon collider with √s = 10 TeV broadens the mass range accessible to other colliders such as FCC-hh/ILC/CLIC to a larger scale by one to two orders of magnitude. Additionally, we demonstrated that a TeV-scale muon collider allows for the ability to discriminate between Majorana and Dirac type HNLs for a large range of mixing values. Paper No. 3: Our key findings regarding the capabilities of the CEPC in flavor physics include the following aspects. (1) Precision Measurements: The CEPC can achieve unprecedented precision in measuring flavor physics benchmarks, potentially surpassing existing experiments like Belle II and LHCb. (2) New Physics Potential: The CEPC may enable the detection of new physics at energy scales of 10 TeV and above, as well as the observation of rare and exotic processes. (3) Testing Fundamental Principles: The collider will facilitate tests of fundamental principles such as lepton flavor universality and conservation of lepton and baryon numbers. (4) Enhanced Physics Opportunities: The WW threshold scan, Higgs-factory operation, and top-pair productions will further enhance its capabilities, particularly in measuring the Cabibbo-Kobayashi-Maskawa matrix elements and Flavor-Changing-Neutral-Current physics. Finally, we discussed future development, outlining the need for advanced detector performance and the role of machine learning in innovative detector design and reconstruction algorithms to meet scientific goals. Overall, the CEPC is positioned as a strategical platform for advancing flavor physics research and exploring new physics opportunities in the coming decades.

16304321.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16304321.value: The scientific scope of next-generation colliders is vast. For instance, the research on flavor physics at the CEPC presented in paper No. 3 is not an exhaustive survey but rather an examination of representative cases. To fully realize the potential of flavor physics at the CEPC, further dedicated investigations will be necessary. Additionally, discovery machines, such as muon and hadron colliders, could play a crucial role in uncovering new particles predicted by various beyond-the-SM theories. Continued exploration is essential to ensure that no significant scientific opportunities are overlooked.

16304321.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16304321.value: One of the greatest puzzles in the microscopic world is why the three generations of elementary particles that make up matter in the universe have hierarchical masses and interact differently with Higgs bosons and force carriers. Understanding these phenomena may also shed light on the cosmic profile, such as the observed dominance of matter over antimatter. This area of study is known as flavor physics. Colliders serve as powerful tools, allowing particle physicists to investigate the internal structure of the microscopic world and measure its properties. In this project, the PI has investigated the capabilities of proposed next-generation colliders, particularly the CEPC (FCC-ee) and muon collider, in addressing challenges in flavor physics. One benchmark study focuses on testing lepton flavor universality at future Z factories at the CEPC, while another investigates flavor mediators in the neutrino sector at the muon collider. Both studies highlight the significant potential of these machines due to their rich signal-event production and clean environments. Additionally, the PI co-led a community initiative to create a landscape of flavor physics at the CEPC, with substantial contributions recognized from his MPhil student. These achievements underscore the project's importance for advancing scientific knowledge and education.

16304421.label: Project Objectives
16304421.value: We will aim to investigate the interaction of an hBN single crystal with the underlying substrate, understand the dynamics of the mechanisms that regulate hBN growth and pattern formation, and develop a methodology to achieve the patterned growth of hBN single crystals via chemical vapor deposition (CVD). We will precisely engineer individual atom-like emitters, including vacancies, disorders, or carbon dopants, in the crystal structure of hBN and verify the defect–structure relationship. We expect to unravel a unique correlation between the surface-engineered hBN structure and its electronic properties that will generate rich physics unique to this material. We will directly probe the obtained room-temperature SPEs to establish a correlation between the engineered defects and the properties of the material, including brightness. We will investigate pathways to realize the light-confining single-photon emission in the patterned hBN and unveil the origin of single-photon emission.

16304421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16304421.value: Quantum photonic devices composed of single-photon emitters (SPEs) are the key components of the next-generation technological revolution. In the proposed work, we will develop an experimental protocol for the design and preparation of two-dimensional (2D) hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) with a patterned SPE distribution and use this for space-confining emissions with adjustable emission wavelengths. Two-dimensional hBN is exceptionally attractive as an SPE due to its high brightness, operability at room temperature, and emission capability over a wide range of wavelength. We aim to further advance its usage by controlling the SPE distribution through patterned hBN growth while engineering the emission properties of each site with individual emitters. Specifically, the proposed work will require us to accomplish the following tasks: 1) We will first exploit the observed interaction between hBN and the substrate and utilize our established protocol to grow the patterned hBN thin film. 2) Second, we will precisely introduce designed defects, including vacancies, disorders, or carbon dopants, into the hBN structure to obtain the desired emission properties. 3) Third, we will fabricate SPE devices and correlate their light emissions with those of the engineered individual emitters to optimize the properties of the fabricated devices. The successful completion of this project will advance our understanding of the fundamental chemistry and physics of 2D materials and generate technologies that will enable us to use 2D materials to develop quantum logic applications. This work will also provide training to Hong Kong students in the interdisciplinary fields of nanotechnology, materials chemistry, and nanoelectronics. 由單光子發射器 (SPE) 為部件的量子光子器件是下一代技術革命的關鍵組成部分。本項目將開發一種用於設計和製備具有圖案化 SPE 分佈的二維 (2D) 六方氮化硼 (hBN) 的實驗方案，並利用其量子效應實現發射光子波長可控。二維六方氮化硼作為單光子發射器具有高亮度、室溫下的可操作性以及較寬的可調控波長。我們的目標是通過圖樣化的 hBN 生長控制 SPE 分佈，同時使用單個發射器設計每個位點的發射特性，從而進一步擴展其應用。具體而言，本項目將完成以下任務：1）我們將首先利用觀察到的 hBN 與基板之間的相互作用，並利用已有實驗基礎來生長圖樣化hBN 薄膜。 2) 其次，我們將在 hBN 結構中精確引入設計缺陷，包括空位、無序點或碳摻雜，以獲得所需的發射特性。 3) 第三，我們將製造 SPE 電子器件，探索單個光發射與與其性能的關係，優化所製造電子器件。 成功完成該項目將促進我們對二維材料的基本化學和物理的理解，並開發基於二維材料量子邏輯應用技術。本項目還將為香港學生提供納米技術、材料化學和納米電子等跨學科領域的培訓。

16304521.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16304521.value: The mean-variance optimization proposed by Markowitz is the most widely adopted framework for active portfolio management. The situation when no risk-free asset is available is particularly relevant to the finance industry because mutual funds are often required to invest fully or to a high percentage in the equity market. When the portfolio consists of a large number of assets, there are intrinsic challenges in the optimization caused by high-dimensionality. In this project, we will develop sound portfolio estimation methods with theoretical guarantee to achieve (near-)optimality in the high-dimensional setting and under practically reasonable assumptions. Markowitz 提出的均值-方差優化理論是資產投資管理中最廣泛應用的框架。在很多投資應用中，無風險資產缺失。一個典型的場景就是很多基金需要或者全部或者有一個很高比例投資於股票市場。 另一方面，實際應用中經常有很多資產可供選擇。這種情況下，均值-方差優化面臨著因為高維而導致的一個本質性的挑戰。在這個項目中，我們將發展可靠合適的優化理論，在合理的假設下，能夠有理論保證來達到最優性。

16304621.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16304621.value: The study of diffraction of electromagnetic waves by small holes in an opaque screen has a long history. Recent studies of extraordinary optical transmission (EOT) of light transmission through hole arrays in a metallic slab has sparked renewed interest, due to their substantial applications in biological and chemical sensing, and in near-field spectroscopy. Despite many efforts to understand the mechanism behind EOT, there remains no rigorous mathematical theory for this phenomenon. In this proposed project, the PI aims to develop a unified rigorous theory to treat three-dimensional electromagnetic scattering by hole structures in a perfect conducting metallic slab. He will formulate the scattering problem using vectorial boundary integral equations, which are defined only on the apertures of the holes using dyadic Green functions, and will develop a rigorous analysis of the associated vectorial boundary integral operators. He will also develop asymptotic analysis when the size of the holes is small, and derive asymptotic expansion for the scattered waves that is capable of explaining the observed EOT. Finally, he will investigate a super-resolution imaging technique by using the EOT of subwavelength holes numerically. 不透明屏幕上的小孔的電磁波衍射的研究歷史悠久。最近關於光通過金屬板中孔陣列而發生的超透射的研究的重新引起了人們的興趣，這是因為超透射在生物和化學傳感以及近場光譜學中有大量的應用。儘管人們為了解 超透射背後的機制付出了很多努力，但對於這種現象，仍然沒有嚴格的數學理論。在這個提議的項目中，PI 旨在開發一個統一的嚴格理論來處理由完美導電金屬板中的孔結構引起的三維電磁散射。他將把散射問題轉化為矢量邊界積分方程。通過使用二元格林函數， 這個方程只定義在孔的孔徑上。他將對該矢量邊界積分方程進行嚴格的分析。當孔很小的時候，推導出散射波的漸近展開式，並解釋觀察到的超透射現象。最後，他將通過數值研究一種使用次波長孔實現超分辨率成像的技術。

16304621.label: Realisation of objectives
16304621.value: Objective 1 is fully achieved. In “A rigorous theory on electromagnetic diffraction by a planar aperture in a perfectly conducting screen,” Journal of Mathematical Physics, 2024, we investigated the classic problem of diffraction of electromagnetic waves by an aperture in a perfectly conducting plane. We formulate the diffraction problem as a boundary integral equation on the aperture using the dyadic Green’s function. This formulation aligns with Bethe’s classical result obtained via fictitious magnetic charges and currents. Using a saddle-point framework, we establish well-posedness of the integral equation, including both existence and uniqueness in an appropriate Sobolev space. The integral-equation formulation then yields asymptotic expansions of the scattered fields in a straightforward manner. Objective 2 is fully achieved. In “Mathematical Theory for Electromagnetic Scattering Resonances and Field Enhancement in a Subwavelength Annular Gap,” Multiscale Modeling and Simulation, 2023, we have developed a mathematical theory for scattering resonances in a subwavelength annular hole embedded in a metallic slab, with annulus width h ≪ 1. This model is representative of many 3D subwavelength-hole structures that induce resonant scattering and extraordinary optical transmission. We devise a multiscale framework combining an exterior-domain integral equation with a waveguide-mode expansion inside the narrow hole. Matching across the aperture leads to a family of decoupled infinite systems, from which resonance conditions are derived. Rigorous analysis characterizes all resonances in a bounded region of the complex plane. The resonances are associated with the annular-hole TE and TEM waveguide modes and lie close to the real axis, with imaginary parts of order O(h). For incident waves, we prove field amplification of order O(1/h) at TE-associated resonant frequencies. A particular TEM-associated resonance is not excitable by a plane wave but can be excited by a near-field electric-dipole source, also yielding O(1/h) enhancement. Objective 3 is well achieved. By replacing the free-space Green’s function with the quasi-periodic Green’s function, the results of the above annular-gap analysis extend to periodic settings without substantial additional difficulty. Motivated by this, we studied a more intricate case: honeycomb lattices of impenetrable obstacles in a homogeneous medium. For both Dirichlet and Neumann problems, we prove the existence of Dirac points arising from crossings of lower and higher band surfaces. Using layer potentials and asymptotic analysis, we derive quantitative formulas for eigenvalues and the slopes of the two conical dispersion surfaces near each Dirac point. The eigenvalues lie near the singular frequencies of the honeycomb-lattice Green’s function, and the cone slopes are reciprocal to these eigenvalues. These results appeared in the SIAM Journal on Applied Mathematics, 2023. Objective 4 is well achieved. In “Mathematical Analysis of Resonances for an Array of Subwavelength Annular Holes and Its Application in Superresolution Imaging,” SIAM Journal on Applied Mathematics, 2025, we analyze resonances for arrays of subwavelength coaxial annular holes and introduce a new superresolution imaging methodology based on the resulting resonant modes. Using a multiscale approach that combines an exterior-domain integral equation with waveguide-mode expansions inside the small 3D holes, we derive asymptotic expansions of complex resonances and quantify near-field amplification at resonant frequencies. In particular, when annular holes are closely spaced, resonant modes oscillate at subwavelength scales in the near field. Leveraging this, we design an imaging strategy that uses these resonant modes to illuminate patterns and present a numerical reconstruction algorithm for the associated inverse problem. Numerical experiments demonstrate roughly an order-of-magnitude improvement in resolution. Additional contribution (data-driven superresolution): In “IFF: A Superresolution Algorithm for Multiple Measurements,” SIAM Journal on Imaging Sciences, 2023, we address reconstruction of 1D point sources from Fourier measurements on a bounded interval [−Ω, Ω], a regime that is challenging when source spacings fall below the Rayleigh length π/Ω. We propose an iterative focusing–localization and filtering (IFF) algorithm that reconstructs sources one by one, requiring no prior knowledge of the source number. This enables a subsampling strategy with small Hankel matrices, avoiding large-scale SVDs typical of subspace methods, and facilitates parallelization. We provide a theoretical analysis indicating a phase transition in localization performance, corroborated by numerics. The method achieves stable recovery at separations close to the theoretical limit and extends naturally to higher dimensions.

16304621.label: Major findings and research outcome
16304621.value: 1) Well-posed vector-valued-boundary-integral-equation formulations for aperture diffraction (see “A rigorous theory on electromagnetic diffraction by a planar aperture in a perfectly conducting screen,” Journal of Mathematical Physics, 2024): Established existence and uniqueness for a dyadic Green’s function–based boundary integral equation modeling diffraction by a single aperture in a zero-thickness PEC screen. Connected rigorously to Bethe’s classical formulation and derived asymptotic expansions of scattered fields. 2) Resonance theory for subwavelength annular holes (finite-thickness slabs) (see “Mathematical Theory for Electromagnetic Scattering Resonances and Field Enhancement in a Subwavelength Annular Gap,” Multiscale Modeling and Simulation, 2023): Developed a multiscale framework coupling exterior integral equations with interior waveguide-mode expansions. Characterized all scattering resonances (TE and TEM) in a bounded complex domain; resonances lie near the real axis with imaginary parts O(h). Proved resonant field amplification of order O(1/h) for TE modes; identified a TEM resonance excitable by near-field sources but not by plane waves. 3) Periodic structures and Dirac physics (see “Dirac Points for the Honeycomb Lattice with Impenetrable Obstacles”，SIAM Journal on Applied Mathematics, 2023): Extended the annular-gap analysis to periodic arrays via quasi-periodic Green’s functions. For honeycomb lattices of impenetrable obstacles, proved the existence of Dirac points for both Dirichlet and Neumann problems, including higher-band crossings. Quantified eigenvalues near lattice Green’s function singularities and derived conical dispersion slopes (reciprocal to eigenvalues). 4) Resonant arrays enabling superresolution imaging (see “Mathematical Analysis of Resonances for an Array of Subwavelength Annular Holes and Its Application in Superresolution Imaging,” SIAM Journal on Applied Mathematics, 2025). Analyzed resonances of arrays of subwavelength coaxial annular holes; derived asymptotics for complex resonances and near-field amplification. Discovered subwavelength-scale oscillatory resonant modes when holes are closely spaced. Designed and validated a resonant-mode–based imaging method, achieving about 10× resolution improvement in simulations. 5) Data-driven superresolution algorithms (see “IFF: A Superresolution Algorithm for Multiple Measurements,” SIAM Journal on Imaging Sciences, 2023): Introduced the IFF (iterative focusing–localization and filtering) algorithm for 1D point-source recovery from bandlimited Fourier data with multiple illuminations. Achieved stable reconstruction near the theoretical resolution limit without prior knowledge of source number; enabled small Hankel matrices, avoided large SVDs, and supported parallelization. Provided theory revealing a phase transition in localization accuracy, confirmed numerically.

16304621.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16304621.value: We outline several promising directions that could build on the results obtained in this project. One avenue is to generalize the theory from ideal conductors to realistic, lossy, and dispersive materials, and to extend well-posedness, asymptotics, and resonance characterization to optical and terahertz regimes. Another is to explore broader geometries (non-annular holes, multilayer stacks) and periodic patterns, including how symmetry breaking modifies Dirac cones, flat bands, and bound states in the continuum. On the computational side, developing faster, high-order boundary-integral solvers and reduced-order models could enable rapid exploration of large design spaces. In future investigations, applications could pair resonant structures with advanced inversion algorithms to enhance superresolution under noise, bandwidth limitations, and partial coherence. Extending the IFF method to 2D/3D and multiplexed measurements, and integrating compressed sensing or physics-informed priors, may further enhance robustness. If pursued, a practical course of action could include performing targeted validation through collaborations in nanofabrication and near-field measurements, as well as prototyping use cases such as label-free bioimaging or chip-scale spectrometry.

16304621.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16304621.value: This project develops reliable ways to predict and control how light and other electromagnetic waves interact with very small holes and patterned metal surfaces. We built exact mathematical models for a single hole, arrays of holes, and honeycomb patterns, and discovered special “resonances” that trap and amplify waves inside tiny openings. We also identified “Dirac points,” where waves act in unusual, highly controllable ways. These insights explain when and how strong amplification occurs and provide formulas that engineers can use to design new devices with confidence. Using these principles, we developed imaging methods and algorithms that see much finer details than standard limits allow—about ten times sharper in simulations—without requiring prior knowledge of how many features are present. The work paves the way for better microscopes and sensors, more efficient wave-guiding surfaces (metasurfaces), and robust signal recovery tools for imaging, radar, and communications. In short, it turns advanced mathematical theory into practical designs that enable subwavelength control and super‑resolution imaging.
