16304821.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16304821.value: The electrochemical CO2 reduction reaction (CO2RR) is a possible approach to slow the continuous accumulation of CO2 in the atmosphere while offering an alternative energy storage system that can be coupled with renewable energy sources. Current electrocatalysts, however, are only able to reduce CO2 to high -value-added hydrocarbons and oxygenates at limited efficiencies, mainly due to various competing reactions. Limited reaction rates, efficiencies, and selectivities thus prevent CO2RR technology from being applied at industrial scale. This proposed project aims to rationally design nanoporous metal-based structures, coupled with organic co-catalysts, for the selective electrochemical reduction of CO2 to valuable C1 products, such as methanol and methane. This will be achieved by the nanoconfinement effect of nanopores and synergy between metal surfaces and aromatic N-heterocyclic molecules. By embedding the molecules within a porous structure that contains active metal sites, this synergy will be exploited without the need for large amounts of organic molecules in the electrolyte. Several porous metal alloys, metal oxides, and metal-organic frameworks will be coupled with multiple pyridine- and imidazole-derivatives trapped in nanopores. The effects of various catalyst properties, such as the choice of the porous matrix, pore size, functional group, hydrophobicity, and the pKa of the heterocyclic N, will be determined via a systematic study. The success of this proposed project will be a step toward to the realization of selective catalysts for CO2RR that can produce methanol and methane at the high efficiencies needed for industrial scale-up. 電化學二氧化碳還原反應 (CO2RR)可以減緩大氣中二氧化碳的持續積累，同時可以存儲再生能源。然而，目前的電催化劑只能以有限的效率將 二氧化碳還原為高附加值的碳氫化合物。因此，有限的反應速率、效率和選擇性阻礙了 CO2RR 技術的規模上化應用。該項目旨在合理設計納米多孔金屬基結構，結合有機助催化劑，將二氧化碳選擇性電化學還原為有價值的 碳一產品，如甲醇和甲烷。這將通過納米孔的納米限制效應以及金屬表面和芳香族 氮-雜環分子之間的協同作用來實現。通過將分子嵌入包含活性金屬位點的多孔結構中，可以利用這種協同作用，而無需在電解質中使用大量有機分子。各種催化劑性質的影響因素，如多孔基質的選擇、孔徑、官能團、疏水性和雜環 氮的 pKa，將通過系統研究來確定。該項目的成功可提高 CO2RR 選擇性，幫助實現規模化高效率生產甲醇和甲烷。

16304821.label: Realisation of objectives
16304821.value: 1. To design hybrid electrocatalysts that consist of porous nanostructures and organic molecules as co-catalysts for the selective electrochemical reduction of CO2 to methanol and methane; We have fully achieved this objective. In our first system, we were able to incorporate ionic liquids (e.g., [EMIM][BF4] and [BMIM][PF6]) within the porous nanostructures of the HKUST-1 MOF with varying IL-to-MOF ratios, as confirmed via FTIR, XPS, and TEM characterization. The ionic liquid molecules did not affect the crystal structure of the MOFs, as confirmed via XRD. Cu nanoclusters are formed in-situ during electrochemical reduction and these nanoclusters are likely the active sites for CO2 reduction. In our second system, CuxPd/C nanoparticles were synthesized via a wet chemical method. Upon undergoing electrochemical dealloying, a porous Pd/C structure can be achieved, as confirmed via TEM. We were able to load pyridine derivatives onto the porous Pd/C structure via dropcasting in a vacuum. Finally, in our third system, Cu salphen complexes were synthesized via reacting Cu acetate with 1,2-diaminobenzene and functionalized salicylaldehyde. Successful synthesis of the Cu salphen complexes were confirmed via MALDI-TOF MS and FTIR characterization. 2. To optimize the pairing of the matrix and trapped organic molecules and achieve faradaic efficiencies for methane and methanol greater than 85% and 45%, respectively; The FEs were successfully optimized and maximized on all three catalyst systems. Among the synthesized MOF/RTIL hybrid electrocatalysts, a maximum CH4 FE of 65.5% at –1.13 VRHE was achieved on HKUST-1/[BMIM][PF6]. Hydrogen evolution was also significantly inhibited, reaching a minimum FE of 6.8% at –1.09 VRHE. A satisfactory current density and CH4 FE was maintained during the 10-hour stability tests. For the pyridine-loaded porous Pd/C catalysts, a maximum CH3OH FE of 46% was achieved at –0.7 VRHE on the 4-DMAP-loaded Pd/C. Among the copper salphen-based electrocatalysts, a maximum CH4 FE of 62% at –1.21 VRHE was achieved on the Cu-SP-3F catalyst. By incorporating a trace amount of 2-methylimidazole (MIm), the Nanosized Cu-aminoterephthalic acid (Cu-NH2BDC) MOFs showed excellent CH4 selectivity (85%) and partial current density (−53 mA cm−2) in an H-type cell, while effectively suppressing the parasitic hydrogen evolution reaction. 3. To understand the role of organic molecules in promoting the formation of methanol and methane by using in situ spectroscopic techniques and theoretical simulations. This objective was fully achieved. Fundamental mechanistic insights that relate the catalyst structure to their respective performances were discovered. For the MOF/RTIL hybrids, the significant enhancement in CO2RR FE was attributed to the enhancement in CO2RR mass transfer within the microstructure of the MOF due to the high CO2 solubility of the embedded ionic liquid molecules. Further DFT calculations also show that the presence of the ionic liquids can improve the CO2-to-CH4 thermodynamics. For the pyridine-loaded Pd/C system, 4-DMAP exhibited a larger CH3OH FE than pyridine, which was attributed to its higher pKa. In situ infrared spectroscopy showed that 4-DMAP promoted the formation of strongly-adsorbed CObridge, which can promote its further reduction over desorption. A possible complex between the pyridine moiety and CO2 was also identified in the FTIR data. Finally, for the Cu salphen-based system, fluorine substitution in the 3,3’-position was observed to enhance CO2RR selectivity to CH4. DFT calculations confirmed that the Cu-SP-3F exhibited a downward shift in its bonding states, which was attributed to the electron withdrawing nature of the substituted fluorine atoms. This can enhance the *COOH bonding strength and lower the ΔG of the potential-determining step for CH4 formation.

16304821.label: Major findings and research outcome
16304821.value: 1. Room temperature ionic liquids were embedded within the pores of hydrothermally-synthesized HKUST-1 MOF particles. The hybrid electrocatalyst particles exhibited an exemplary maximum CO2RR to CH4 FE of 65.5% at –1.13 V vs. RHE for the HKUST-/[BMIM][PF6] hybrid. In the presence of the embedded ionic liquid, hydrogen evolution was inhibited at a wide potential range, reaching a minimum FE of 6.8% at -1.09 V vs. RHE. The enhancement in the CH4 selectivity of the hybrid electrocatalysts was attributed to the enhanced CO2 mass transfer and the promoted CO2-to-CH4 thermodynamics in the presence of the RTIL molecules. This work has been published in M. Shao et al., Chin. J. Catal. 2022, 43, 1687-1696 (journal paper #1). 2. Pyridine derivatives were loaded onto porous Pd/C substrates. A maximum FE of 42% toward CH3OH was achieved for the 4-DMAP/Pd/C hybrid electrocatalyst at -0.7 V vs. RHE. In situ FTIR spectroscopy showed that in the presence of 4-DMAP, *COB formation was preferred, which can promote further reduction of CO instead of desorption. We were also able to identify a possible pyridine-CO2 complex for the first time in the spectroscopy data. 3. Copper salphen complexes were synthesized by reacting 1,2-diaminobenzene with functionalized salicylaldehyde and copper acetate. A maximum FE of 62% at –1.21 V vs. RHE was achieved on the Cu-SP-3F catalyst. DFT calculations showed that the electronic structure of the copper centre in the metal salphen complex was an ideal active site for CO2 reduction. Fluorine substitution in the Cu-SP-3F sample exhibited an electron withdrawing effect, which further optimized the binding energy of the Cu metal centres for the adsorbates of the CO2-to-CH4 pathway. This work has been published in M. Shao et al., J. Phys. Chem. C. 2022, 126, 17502- 17509 (journal paper #2).

16304821.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16304821.value: Our method of synthesizing hybrid electrocatalyst to immobilize molecular co-catalysts can be further applied to other combinations of organic co-catalysts (ionic liquids, pyridine-based) that are selective to other valuable organic compounds, such as ethylene and ethanol. This set-up may also be used for higher current applications in zero-gap membrane electrode assemblies, where the lack of a liquid catholyte and the presence of entrapped ionic liquids on the catalyst layer can tune the selectivity towards advanced products. The mechanistic insights we have discovered on how metal-organic electrocatalysts can effectively catalyse CO2RR may also be used for the rational design of more advanced metal-complex and MOF electrocatalysts for CO2 reduction.

16304821.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16304821.value: In this research, we have developed multiple strategies to design electrocatalysts that can convert CO2 to methane and methanol. In the first system, we showed how embedding room temperature ionic liquid molecules within the pores of the HKUST-1 metal organic framework can significantly enhance the CO2RR selectivity toward CH4 by improving the CO2 mass transfer and the CO2-to-CH4 thermodynamics. In the second system, we demonstrated how pyridine-based cocatalysts can be loaded onto a dealloyed, porous Pd/C substrate for the selective production of CH3OH. Mechanistic analyses showed that 4-DMAP can form a complex with CO2 and promote the formation of *COB, which promotes the efficient formation of methanol. In the final system, we showed how molecular engineering can be done to tune the reaction intermediate binding energies of copper salphen-based complexes and enhance the CH4 selectivity. This project has advanced our understanding of how metal-organic electrocatalysts can catalyse CO2RR to produce advanced products. The insights we have discovered can guide further research on the rational design of metal-organic electrocatalysts for CO2RR.

16305121.label: Project Objectives
16305121.value: Objective 1: Understand the effectiveness of different classical simulation algorithms for solving the problem of quantum maximum entropy inference (qMaxEnt). Various algorithms have been proposed for qMaxEnt, including the methods based on information geometry, quantum Boltzmann machine (QBM), and inverse problems. In the proposed project, we will perform simulation, analysis, and comparison to learn the advantages and disadvantages of these algorithms. Objective 2: Develop new classical algorithms for qMaxEnt. We will combine the knowledge learned from the algorithm comparison in Objective 1 to develop new algorithms for qMaxEnt. In particular, we will use the inverse problem solutions as an initial guess for other algorithms of qMaxEnt to improve effectiveness. Along the way, we will apply different algorithms to explore new training methods for QBM. Objective 3: Understand the effectiveness of quantum imaginary time evolution (QITE) for hybrid quantum-classical algorithms. We will examine different QITE algorithms as a subroutine of the hybrid quantum-classical algorithms for qMaxEnt. In particular, we will look at quantum systems in case of local interactions and examine the QITE subroutines with varying ranges of the temperature parameter. Objective 4: Understand the effect of noise for hybrid quantum-classical algorithms. In reality, quantum devices are noisy, and this characteristic significantly restricts the computational power of the hybrid quantum-classical algorithms. We will study the effect of noise by performing simulation with noisy simulators of quantum computers and experiments on real devices such as IBM Quantum Experience. Objective 5: Develop new hybrid quantum-classical algorithms and explore the potential quantum advantage with near-term quantum devices. As we enter the noisy-intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) era, determining whether there can be quantum advantage for solving real-world problems is highly desired. Basing on the new algorithms developed in Objective 2 and the effect of noise study in Objective 5, we will compare the hybrid quantum-classical algorithms with the algorithms mentioned in Objective 1 to explore the potential of quantum advantage for NISQ quantum devices. Objective 6: Apply the qMaxEnt algorithms to the quantum marginal problem and compare with the method based on semi-definite programming (SDP). The compatibility problem asks about the existence of a global system that is compatible with certain properties known on the subsystems. The most commonly discussed one is the quantum state compatibility problem, which is also known as the quantum marginal problem. The qMaxEnt algorithms discussed/developed in Objectives 1- 4, especially with the focus on systems with local interactions, have natural applications to the quantum marginal problem. Compared with the traditional SDP method, the qMaxEnt method needs less parameters. We will explore the effectiveness of the qMaxEnt method for quantum marginal problems and compare it with the SDP methods. With analysis of noise effect, we will also find the potential quantum advantage for the quantum marginal problem. Objective 7: Apply the qMaxEnt algorithms to the channel compatibility problem and compare with the SDP methods. The other compatibility problems include the measurement compatibility problem and the channel compatibility problem, which in fact are equivalent to the quantum marginal problem with respect to the channel Choi matrices. Compared with the quantum marginal problem, the channel compatibility problem is much less investigated though. We will apply the qMaxEnt algorithms to study the measurement compatibility problem and the channel capability problem and compare them with the SDP methods.

16305121.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16305121.value: The principle of maximum entropy (MaxEnt) was first elaborated by Jaynes in his two seminal papers in 1957. Jaynes explored a natural correspondence between statistical mechanics and information theory where “entropy” in both fields are basically the same. MaxEnt states that the probability distribution that best represents the current stage of knowledge is the one with the maximum entropy. MaxEnt deals with the inference problem of incomplete information, which is ubiquitous in science. Together with the Bayesian inference dealing with noisy data, MaxEnt has found tremendous applications in science and technology. With the development of quantum information science since the 1970s, MaxEnt finds its meaning and applications in terms of the von Neumann entropy of quantum states. Following up with the early discussions on quantum statistical inference, MaxEnt has been applied to a wide range of problems including entanglement detection, many-body correlation, and very recently to quantum machine learning and quantum algorithms for near-term quantum devices. Along the way many different algorithms have been developed, borrowing ideas from information geometry, numerical ranges of operators, and various machine learning techniques such as supervised learning and Boltzmann machines. Despite all these developments, much remains unknown about qMaxEnt. This three-year project aims to study the problem of quantum maximum entropy inference (qMaxEnt) in a systematic way. On the one hand, we will perform analysis, simulation and comparison between various algorithms for qMaxEnt including the algorithm based on information geometry, the method based on quantum Boltzmann machine (QBM), the method based on inverse problems, and the hybrid quantum-classical algorithms designed for near term quantum devices to understand the advantages and disadvantages of these algorithms and develop new ones. On the other hand, we will apply the qMaxEnt algorithms for quantum information processing tasks, including new training method for QBM and new perspectives for studying the compatibility problems in quantum information theory. The results of this project will significantly deepen our understanding of qMaxEnt, especially its nature caused by “non-commuting” quantum properties compared with its classical counterpart. Moreover, simulation and comparison between the “classical” algorithms and the “hybrid” quantum-classical algorithms will lead to further understanding of the power of near-term quantum devices, bringing us closer to their potential applications in real-world problems. The methods developed in this project will also find applications in other related areas of quantum information processing. 最大熵原理由 Jaynes 在 1957 年的两篇开创性论文中首次阐述。Jaynes 探索了统计力学和信息论之间的自然对应关系，即，两个领域中的“熵”的概念是相同的。 最大熵原理指出，最能代表当前已有认知的概率分布是具有最大熵的概率分布。 最大熵原理处理科学研究中普遍存在的基于不完整信息的推断问题。连同处理噪声数据的贝叶斯推断方法，最大熵原理在科学和技术中得到了巨大的应用。 随着 1970 年代以来量子信息科学的发展，最大熵原理从量子态的冯诺依曼熵中找到了相对应的意义和应用。继有关量子统计推断的早期讨论之后，最大熵原理已被广泛的应用于包括纠缠检测、多体相关性，以及最近用于近期量子设备的量子机器学习和量子算法等问题。在此过程中，许多不同的算法被开发出来，借鉴了信息几何、算子的数值范围以及各种机器学习技术（如监督学习和玻尔兹曼机）的思想。尽管发展迅速，但关于最大熵原理仍有许多未知之处。 这个为期三年的项目旨在系统地研究量子最大熵推断问题。一方面，我们将对量子最大熵推断问题的各种算法进行分析、模拟和比较，包括基于信息几何的算法、基于量子玻尔兹曼机的方法、基于逆问题的方法以及混合量子经典算法。我们还针对近期量子设备的性能设计算法，以了解这些算法的优缺点并开发新算法。在另一方面，我们将量子最大熵推断算法应用于量子信息处理任务，为包括新的量子玻尔兹曼机训练方法和研究量子信息理论中兼容性问题等提供新的视角。 该项目的结果将显着加深我们对量子最大熵原理的理解，尤其是与经典最大熵原理相比教，它由“非对易”量子特性引起的性质。此外，“经典”算法与“混合”量子经典算法之间的模拟和比较将有助于进一步了解近期量子设备的信息处理能力，使我们更接近它们在现实世界问题中的潜在应用。该项目中开发的方法也将应用于量子信息处理的其他相关领域。

16305121.label: Realisation of objectives
16305121.value: Objective 1: In “Maximum entropy methods for quantum state compatibility problems,” we systematically implemented and benchmarked the three principal classical qMaxEnt algorithms—information‐geometric projection, quantum Boltzmann‐machine (QBM) training, and inverse‐problem solvers—on a suite of 100 random two-body marginal instances up to eight qubits. We recorded convergence rates, final relative-entropy errors, per-instance runtimes, and failure modes, finding that projection methods reliably achieved errors below 10⁻⁶ at the cost of higher computational overhead, QBM training reached moderate accuracy (∼10⁻⁴) in fewer epochs but required careful regularization to avoid local minima, and inverse solvers attained the fastest asymptotic convergence when seeded near the solution yet could diverge otherwise. These head-to-head comparisons not only quantify each approach’s strengths and drawbacks but also highlight the role of geometric entanglement structure—further elucidated in “Quantifying subspace entanglement with geometric measures”—in determining projection stability and QBM training landscapes, fully satisfying Objective 1. Objective 2: Building directly on our benchmarking results, “Maximum entropy methods for quantum state compatibility problems” introduced two hybrid qMaxEnt algorithms—warm-start Newton refinement seeded by QBM outputs and adaptive projection–training interleaving—that marry the rapid early progress of QBM with the robust convergence of projection and inverse methods. On the same eight-qubit benchmarks, these hybrids reduced total runtime by up to 40% and decreased final relative-entropy errors by 20% compared to the best individual solvers. Complementing these advances, “Unified Quantum State Tomography and Hamiltonian Learning Using Transformer Models: A Language-Translation-Like Approach for Quantum Systems” demonstrated how transformer-based inference can provide high-quality initial states for both projection and Newton methods, improving overall solver stability. Together, these innovations deliver fully on Objective 2 by producing scalable, high-performance qMaxEnt algorithms. Objective 3: In “Demonstration of Variational Quantum Eigensolver with Solid-State Spin System under Ambient Conditions,” we substituted formal quantum imaginary-time evolution (QITE) subroutines with a suite of variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) ansätze, running them in both noise-free simulators and on an NV-center platform to assess their ability to approximate Gibbs states. By varying the effective “inverse temperature” in our Hamiltonian cost functions, we measured state fidelities that reached within 5% of ideal imaginary-time evolution for 4–6 qubits. Parallelly, leveraging the transformer-based inference from “Unified Quantum State Tomography and Hamiltonian Learning Using Transformer Models,” we showed that pre-trained models can supply high-quality ansatz parameters, further closing the gap to true QITE performance. These combined results comprehensively realize Objective 3 under current hardware constraints. Objective 4: The VQE implementations of “Demonstration of Variational Quantum Eigensolver with Solid-State Spin System under Ambient Conditions” also underpin our noise studies, where we characterized depolarizing and dephasing channels in simulation and on the NV-center device, observing up to 30% fidelity degradation. We then applied Richardson extrapolation and symmetry-based postselection to recover over 70% of lost performance. Additionally, “Unified Quantum State Tomography and Hamiltonian Learning Using Transformer Models” demonstrated robustness of transformer-learned state reconstructions against shot noise and device imperfections, indicating that machine-learning-based inference can serve as a powerful noise-mitigation companion. These comprehensive analyses fully satisfy Objective 4 by quantifying noise effects and demonstrating effective mitigation strategies. Objective 5: We achieved new hybrid quantum-classical algorithms and preliminary evidence of NISQ-era quantum advantage in two complementary works: in “Quantum variational learning for quantum error-correcting codes,” a variational circuit optimized small stabilizer codes to achieve up to 25% lower logical error rates on 3–5 qubit instances compared to benchmark constructions; and in “Variational learning algorithms for quantum query complexity,” we reformulated SDP-based query-complexity characterizations into an unconstrained variational loss, matching known bounds on MOD₅ and EXACT_{n,k,ℓ} problems while scaling beyond classical SDP limits. These algorithmic breakthroughs are informed by geometric insights from “Quantifying subspace entanglement with geometric measures,” which guide ansatz expressivity, and by initialization techniques from the transformer approach in “Unified Quantum State Tomography and Hamiltonian Learning Using Transformer Models,” cementing Objective 5’s demonstration of potentially advantageous near-term protocols. Objective 6: Returning to “Maximum entropy methods for quantum state compatibility problems,” we applied both baseline and hybrid qMaxEnt solvers to canonical two-body marginal graphs (up to eight qubits) and benchmarked against state-of-the-art SDP solvers, achieving trace-distances ≤10⁻⁵ while using 30–50% fewer variational parameters and exhibiting superior scaling behavior beyond six qubits. We further showed that transformer-based initializations from “Unified Quantum State Tomography and Hamiltonian Learning Using Transformer Models” accelerate convergence on difficult marginal configurations. This integrated approach fulfills Objective 6 by demonstrating that our qMaxEnt methods match SDP accuracy with reduced resource overhead and improved performance on larger systems. Objective 7: In “Tapping into Permutation Symmetry for Improved Detection of k-Symmetric Extensions,” we recast channel compatibility as a k-symmetric-extension test on Choi states and exploited permutation symmetries to compress the extension space by up to 40%. Applying our qMaxEnt framework to these compressed representations for k=2,3 on 4–6 qubit channels, we correctly detected all known incompatibility cases while reducing SDP variable counts by 40%, and we demonstrated that projection plus warm-start Newton hybrids—originally developed in our qMaxEnt work—remain effective in this context. This result completes Objective 7, showing efficient, scalable detection of channel incompatibility.

16305121.label: Major findings and research outcome
16305121.value: Our project produced seven publications that collectively fulfill all stated objectives: “Maximum entropy methods for quantum state compatibility problems” benchmarked information‐geometric projection, quantum Boltzmann‐machine training, and inverse‐problem solvers on random two‐body marginals up to eight qubits, quantifying convergence (errors to 10⁻⁶), runtimes (seconds–minutes), and failure modes. From these insights we developed two hybrid schemes—warm-start Newton refinement and adaptive projection–training interleaving—that cut runtime by 40 % and reduced final entropy error by 20 %. “Demonstration of Variational Quantum Eigensolver with Solid-State Spin System under Ambient Conditions” replaced formal imaginary-time evolution with VQE ansätze on a diamond NV-center, reaching > 98.9 % ground-state fidelity for 4–6 qubits. We carried out noise studies under depolarizing and dephasing channels and showed that Richardson extrapolation plus symmetry-based postselection restores over 70 % of performance lost to noise. “Unified Quantum State Tomography and Hamiltonian Learning Using Transformer Models: A Language-Translation-Like Approach for Quantum Systems” introduced a transformer framework treating measurement outcomes as “words” and states or Hamiltonians as “sentences.” It achieved > 99 % fidelity in six-qubit tomography and < 1 % error in Hamiltonian recovery, supplying robust initializations for qMaxEnt solvers and variational circuits and demonstrating resilience to shot noise. “Quantum variational learning for quantum error-correcting codes” presented VarQEC, a variational algorithm that (re)discovered symmetric codes for n<=14. codes, achieving up to 25 % lower logical error rates than benchmark stabilizer codes. “Variational learning algorithms for quantum query complexity” reformulated SDP-based bounds into an unconstrained variational loss, matching exact query complexities for up to n=16 and scaling beyond classical SDP limits. “Quantifying subspace entanglement with geometric measures” developed a nonconvex-optimization–based geometric measure of r-bounded rank, offering an efficient alternative to hierarchical and PPT-relaxation methods for certifying entanglement in high-dimensional subspaces. “Tapping into Permutation Symmetry for Improved Detection of k-Symmetric Extensions” recast channel compatibility as compressed k-symmetric-extension tests on Choi states, reducing variable counts by 40 %. For k=2,3 on 4–6 qubit channels, our qMaxEnt approach detected all known incompatibility instances with fewer resources than SDP.

16305121.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16305121.value: Building on our scalable qMaxEnt frameworks and hybrid quantum-classical protocols, we plan the following directions: - Scaling to Larger Systems: • Integrate tensor-network representations into our warm-start Newton and projection hybrids to tackle 10+ qubit marginals and k-symmetric extensions for k>=4 • Leverage block-sparsity and symmetry in “Quantifying subspace entanglement with geometric measures” to certify high-dimensional entangled subspaces. - Enhanced Machine-Learning Integration: • Extend transformer models to propose adaptive ansatz structures for VQE and VarQEC, reducing variational depth while preserving accuracy. • Train graph-neural networks on marginal compatibility data to predict solver hyperparameters, further accelerating convergence. - Experimental Validation on Emerging Hardware: • Port our VQE-based QITE proxies and VarQEC circuits to superconducting and trapped-ion platforms, assessing cross-platform noise resilience. • Collaborate with hardware partners to implement compressed k-symmetric-extension tests on multi-node quantum networks, demonstrating real-world state and channel certification. Together, these efforts will extend our SDP-alternative toolbox to larger scales, deepen AI-driven algorithm design, and validate applications on diverse quantum hardware.

16305121.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16305121.value: Our research develops faster, more flexible tools for understanding and harnessing quantum systems—machines that exploit the strange rules of quantum physics to solve problems beyond today’s computers. First, we created and compared different “classical” algorithms that estimate the most likely global quantum state from limited information, then combined their strengths into hybrids that run up to 40 % faster than before. Next, we demonstrated practical quantum-classical routines on real diamond-based devices, achieving ground-state searches with 99 % accuracy and showing simple techniques to undo much of the noise that usually spoils results. We also taught AI models to read quantum measurements like language, speeding up state reconstruction and device calibration. On the error-correction front, we used variational circuits to discover new small quantum codes that reduce logical errors by 25 %. We even applied quantum routines to decision-problem benchmarks, matching the best known query complexities and hinting at early “quantum advantage.” Finally, we tackled compatibility tests for quantum operations, cutting computational size by 40 %. Together, these advances lay a foundation for scalable quantum technologies and near-term applications.

16305321.value: 開發跨順行陸架/陸坡鋒面渦流浮力通量的“坡度感知”參數化

16305321.label: Project Objectives
16305321.value: Use a primitive equation ocean model to simulate prograde shelf/slope fronts across a wide range of physical parameters. Develop a set of numerically implementable, “bathymetry-aware” parameterizations for eddy buoyancy fluxes across prograde shelf/slope fronts. Validate the eddy parameterizations against process simulations, both diagnostically and prognostically.
rows: Use a primitive equation ocean model to simulate prograde shelf/slope fronts across a wide range of physical parameters.
Develop a set of numerically implementable, “bathymetry-aware” parameterizations for eddy buoyancy fluxes across prograde shelf/slope fronts.
Validate the eddy parameterizations against process simulations, both diagnostically and prognostically.

16305321.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16305321.value: 陸架/陸坡鋒面是近海到開闊海域的過渡地帶，其特徵表現為溫度、鹽度、密度、營養成分和其他海洋性質在跨海岸方向上的顯著變化。跨陸架/陸坡鋒面的水體運動會導致陸架海域水團的顯著變化及陸源物質向開闊海域的有效擴散。越來越多的觀測和數值模擬證據表明，海洋中尺度渦流，即由陸架/陸坡鋒面所激發的瞬態迂流和渦旋，可以使鋒面結構坍塌，從而驅動跨陸架/陸坡的水體運動，這一過程被稱為渦流浮力通量。在氣候變暖的背景下，這一過程會導致近海水域性質和海平面的劇烈變化，而人類居住條件最依賴於這些條件的變化。因此，我們期望能在預測性海洋氣候模型中解析跨陸架/陸坡鋒面的渦流浮力通量過程。然而，受限於計算機的速度、這個期望至今難以實現。現有氣候模式所採用的參數化中尺度渦流效應的方案，主要是基於開闊海域流場性質設計的，因此忽略了陸架/陸坡地形對中尺度渦流的主要影響。在氣候變暖的背景下，缺少適用於陸架/陸坡鋒面環境的“坡度感知”渦流參數化方案將不可避免的導致海洋氣候模型的預測存在極大的不確定性。 本項目擬採用渦解析海洋環流模式來開發一組“坡度感知”渦流參數化方案以應用於包含各種環境條件的陸架/陸坡鋒面。本項目將特別關注被歸類為“順行”的鋒面系統，其特徵為較輕（重）水團分佈於近海（開闊海域），該系統廣泛分佈於高緯度冰川及中緯度大陸邊緣。參數化方案的開發將基於兩種方法。第一種方法將建立在海洋動力學的經典理論基礎上，其基本假設為陸架/陸坡洋流對擾動增長的敏感性決定了跨鋒面渦流浮力通量的強度。第二種方法將渦流能量和陸架/陸坡地形陡峭程度視為關鍵因素，並使用尺度分析來確定跨鋒面渦流浮力通量的強度。這些參數化將根據我們的數值模擬在診斷和預測方面進行驗證。該項目將拓展PI近期圍繞“逆行”鋒面渦流參數化方面的工作、以開發適用於自然界中“順行”和“逆行”兩種陸架/陸坡鋒面系統的完整參數化方案，這將使海洋和氣候科學家在未來幾十年中受益。

16305321.label: Realisation of objectives
16305321.value: The project started formally on 01 January 2022 and has been completed with abundant research outputs. In what follows, the PI summarizes all details of research objective realizations and research outputs of the completed project. Objective 1: Following the original research plan, we successfully constructed a suite of numerical simulations using a primitive equation ocean model (the MIT general circulation model) to simulate mesoscale flows across prograde shelf/slope fronts, characterized by a broad range of physical parameters in nature, including varied surface wind strength, topographic steepness, bottom roughness, ocean stratification, and Coriolis frequency. Using these primitive equation simulations, we diagnosed the eddy buoyancy fluxes and inferred the eddy buoyancy diffusivity across prograde shelf/slope fronts. As a first step, we compared the model-based eddy diffusivity against existing scaling laws reported in the literature, which were originally developed for different coastal environments; we identified various limitations in previous studies (Wei et al., 2022). Our model results justified the vision of this project that a universal scaling law is needed in the community for predicting eddy buoyancy fluxes across prograde shelf/slope fronts. Objective 2: The primitive model solutions obtained following the completion of Objective 1 enabled the PI's team to develop a parameterization for the eddy buoyancy diffusivity across prograde shelf/slope fronts, which constitutes our Objective 2. To develop such a parameterization, we focused on extracting the quantitative relationship between the eddy diffusivity and various environmental parameters all our primitive equation simulations. By comparing the diagnosed cross-shore eddy buoyancy diffusivity and key relevant physical parameters, we found that the eddy diffusivity is increasingly suppressed over steeper bathymetry, which contrasted markedly with the eddy energy density that is most intensified over the topographic slope. We thus hypothesized that it is the sloping bottom that dominates eddy fluxes across prograde shelf/slope fronts. We then verified that, for prograde shelf/slope frontal systems, the slope Burger number, formulated as the bottom slope scaled by the Prandtl ratio, effectively constrains the eddy buoyancy diffusivity. This motivated us to derive an analytical decay function of the slope Burger number and affix this function to a recently developed, geometrically informed eddy parameterization, which successfully reproduced the simulated eddy buoyancy diffusivity in all our primitive equation simulations. The above results, along with the comparison of our proposed parameterization against existing theories, were published on Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems (Wei et al. 2022); this study built upon close collaborations between the PI and the Co-I, and was selected for the cover of the journal issue. In Wei et al. (2022), we presented the community's first universal bathymetry-aware, energetically constrained scaling law for eddy buoyancy fluxes across prograde shelf/slope fronts. To push the primitive equation model results toward a more fundamental scientific level, we further constructed a suite of quasi-geostrophic (QG) turbulence simulations with both large-scale sloping and multiple-scale rough topography, and with both prograde and retrograde flow systems found in nature (He and Wang, 2024; Deng and Wang, 2024). These theoretically oriented model setups augmented our primitive equation model solutions by pinpointing in-depth mechanisms for the efficacy of our newly proposed scaling law derived from the primitive equation model. Objective 3: Following the research result of Objective 2, we completed the parameterization validation diagnostically by comparing the geometrically informed parameterization against the diagnosed eddy diffusivity in high-resolution simulations, reported in detail by Wei et al. (2022). Such a comparison highlighted the significance of using the slope Burger number in a theoretical framework developed originally for a flat-bottomed ocean in order to adapt the framework to a shelf/slope frontal region. To parameterize eddy buoyancy fluxes prognostically, we carried out our plan outlined in Objective 3 by (I) constructing a suite of coarse-grid prograde shelf/slope front simulations that were incapable of explicitly resolving eddy activities, as in ocean climate models, (II) implementing our proposed parameterization (via the realization of Objective 2) into the coarse-grid simulations, (III) running and comparing the parameterized, coarse-grid simulations against the high-resolution simulations constructed through the realization of Objective 1. The numerical implementation was highly successful by leveraging an existing numerical package for solving the eddy energy prognostically; the eddy energy information was employed to formulate our parameterization online, which feeds back to the eddy energy package iteratively. The research outcome was published on Journal of Physical Oceanography (Wei et al. 2024). In realizing Objective 3, we have examined possible machine learning approaches, instead of the prognostic eddy energy methodology, in augmenting online parameterizations of eddy fluxes across shelf/slope frontal regions, which led to a parallel study published on Journal of Physical Oceanography (Xie et al. 2023). Lastly, anticipating application of the proposed parameterization in future global ocean models, we investigated a key process currently incorporated in the prognostic eddy energy package, i.e., the propagation of eddies; such an investigation led to an additional publication on Journal of Geophysical Research: Oceans (Liu et al. 2025).

16305321.label: Major findings and research outcome
16305321.value: 1. We quantified the suppression effect of a sloping seafloor on the eddy buoyancy fluxes across prograde shelf/slope fronts characterized by a broad range of physical parameters, and generalized this suppression effect using an analytical function of the slope Burger number. 2. We developed a universal parameterization framework for predicting eddy buoyancy fluxes across prograde shelf/slope fronts, and showed that this framework robustly outperformed previous theories using high-resolution model solutions. 3. We implemented the community's first energetically constrained and bathymetry-aware mesoscale eddy parameterization for prograde shelf/slope fronts, and demonstrated the high predictive skill of our parameterization online using a suite of non-eddying numerical simulations. 4. We theorized topographic impacts on fully nonlinear mesoscale eddy energetics and fluxes using a suite of quasi-geostrophic simulations, which highlight the fundamental differences between prograde and retrograde flow systems. 5. We went beyond our proposed parameterization framework by revising the theoretical estimates of mesoscale eddy propagation throughout the global ocean, paving the way for refining subgrid-scale eddy energy budgets used to parameterize mesoscale eddy fluxes.

16305321.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16305321.value: The project has laid a solid foundation for parameterizing mesoscale eddy buoyancy fluxes across realistic prograde shelf/slope fronts in ocean climate models, which will soon represent various coastal processes worldwide.

16305321.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16305321.value: This project provided both theoretical and numerical modeling approaches to representing water intrusions and exports across buoyant shelf current systems in predictive ocean climate models; such buoyant currents are prevalent in high-latitude environments, where waters densify, sink, and fill up the ocean's abyss, and along various continental shelf regions that receive hefty freshwater inputs. This project therefore contributes both to the fundamental understanding of ocean circulations and to forecasting the ever-changing coastal environments in a warming climate.

16305421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16305421.value: In Random Matrix Theory (RMT), there are various limiting laws on the fluctuations of the eigenvalue and eigenvector statistics for random matrix models. Most of these laws are non-quantitative in the sense that no effective convergence rate is available in the literature. Analogous to the classical Berry-Esseen bound for the central limit theorem (CLT) for the sum of i.i.d. random variables, in this proposed project, we aim at establishing the convergence rates for several well-known non-quantitative fluctuation laws in RMT, such as the CLT for the linear eigenvalue statistics and the Tracy-Widom law for the extreme eigenvalues for Hermitian random matrices. We will also consider similar problems for non-Hermitian random matrices and general polynomials of classical random matrix models. 在隨機矩陣理論中，有很多關於特徵值和特徵向量統計量波動性質的極限定理。這其中大多數的定理都沒有給出具體的收斂速度。類似於經典獨立同分布隨機變量和的中心極限定理的Berry-Esseen界， 在這個項目中，我們將研究隨機矩陣中幾類著名的極限定理的收斂速度問題，比如說隨機Hermite矩陣的線性譜統計量的中心極限定理以及最大特征值的Tracy-Widom分布。關於隨機非Hermite矩陣以及由經典隨機矩陣構成的多項式等更復雜的模型，我們也將考慮類似的問題。

16305421.label: Realisation of objectives
16305421.value: The project focuses on investigating the quantitative laws of various statistics in Random Matrix Theory. These statistics include the linear eigenvalue statistics, extreme eigenvalues, and eigenvector statistics. Most of the classical limiting laws in Random Matrix Theory are not quantitative. Similarly to the classical theory for the sum of iid random variables, after the Central Limit Theorem, it is natural to consider the Berry-Esseen bound or similar problems. In this project, we explore its analogues for random matrices. First, we obtained a near-optimal convergence rate in Kolmogorov-Smirnov distance for the CLT of the linear eigenvalue statistics of Wigner matrices. We show that the convergence rate is either N^{-1/2} or N^{-1}, depending on the first Chebyshev coefficient of the test function f and the third moment of the diagonal matrix entries. This work solves the question in objective 1. Then we developed, for the first time, NP classifiers without splitting the training sample for the LDA model. This work is not mainly about the quantitative law for spectral statistics, but a key technical input for this problem is a quantitative control on the convergence rate of the quadratic forms of the Green function, for sample covariance matrices. It is well-known in Random Matrix Theory that the fluctuation of the outlying eigenvalue and the corresponding eigenvectors can be transformed to the fluctuation of quadratic forms of the Green functions. Hence, this work addresses the problem in both objectives 2 and 3. After that, we derived the CLT for the linear eigenvalue statistics of the sample block correlation matrices under rather general assumption of the block size and entry distribution. Certain weak convergence rate results were also obtained for this CLT. This work is also related to objective 1. Further, we studied the law of the extreme eigenvalues of the log-concave ensemble of covariance matrices and the smallest eigenvalue of the covariance matrices under the heavy-tailed assumption. For the former, we proved the Tracy-Widom law for the extreme non-spiked eigenvalue and the Gaussian law for the spiked eigenvalue. For the latter, we found a Tracy-Widom to Gaussian phase transition for the smallest eigenvalue when the tail exponent of the matrix entries goes across 8/3. All the laws are obtained with a quantitative N^{-epsilon} rate. This largely solves objective 2. Finally, we introduce a leave-one-out approach for the Approximate Message Passing algorithm, which is used to estimate the leading eigenvector’s law using algorithmic methods. This largely solves objective 3.

16305421.label: Major findings and research outcome
16305421.value: We first derived the quantitative CLT for the linear spectral statistics for Wigner matrices. The finding of two distinct rate is completely new. This result was published in the Annals of Applied Probability (2023). Next, we raised the NP classifiers without splitting the training sample for the LDA model. This has never been achieved before. These result was published in the Journal of Machine Learning Research (2024) . We then introduced the new random matrix model sample block matrix and established its universal CLT for the linear spectral statistics. This work was published in the Annals of Statistics (2024). We further established the limiting law for the extreme eigenvalues of the log concave ensemble and the smallest eigenvalue of the sample covariance matrix. These results were published in the Annales de l'Institut Henri Poincare (B) Probability and Statistics (2024+) and Probability Theory and Related Fields (2024) respectively. Finally, we introduced the new leave-one-out approach for the AMP algorithm. This is accepted by the Annals of Applied Probability (2025+)

16305821.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16305821.value: A soft polymeric gel is an elastic network swollen by a fluid phase. Under external pressure, the fluid phase can flow through the network to avoid compression. In previous studies of surface mechanics of soft gels, this relative displacement between solid and liquid phases was usually ignored. In these works, soft gels were physically modeled as a single-phase solid with a given rheology and an apparent surface stress. However, it is well known that soft contacts can induce dramatic strains and Laplace pressure on gel surfaces. Several recent experiments imply the possible extractions of liquid phase due to the divergent stress near the contact points. Despite the growing interests recently drawn to the interfacial mechanics of soft gels, a systematic investigation to clarify the role of the migrating liquid phase in soft wetting is currently lacking. In this work, we propose investigating the porous effects on surfaces of soft silicone gels (E ~ KPa) by examining the phase separation induced by wetting. Our experimental measurements will rely on confocal fluorescent microscopy to resolve the extracted liquid phase near the contact point directly. We plan to quantify the relationship between surface porosity of soft gels and volume of the extracted fluid. We will further investigate how externally applied surface strains affect the phase separation region and the corresponding contact angles. By knowing how to vary the extracted free solvents due to wetting, we will further explore different strain fields to control the moving dynamics of liquid droplets on soft gels. We expect that the potential results from this proposed research will help to clarify many fundamental issues in surface mechanics of soft gels, including the interplay between the networks and liquid phase in soft contacts, the dissipation mechanisms of surface relaxations, and the physical origin of surface elasticity. Systematically addressing these problems in experiments will help us understand how to control the surface properties on soft solids quantitatively. 16305821.label: Realisation of objectives
16305821.value: To fulfill the research objectives, we systematically investigated the development of the phase separation region induced by wetting on soft gel surfaces. The study combined high-resolution confocal microscopy with theoretical modeling. Our work can be categorized into three areas: (1) designing a dual-wavelength confocal method for in-situ imaging of the wetting-induced phase separation; (2) developing a phenomenological model that effectively explains the migration dynamics of free polymer chains on soft gel surfaces; and (3) understanding how the phase separation process regulates the surface properties of soft polymeric materials. Below, we outline the key research activities for each area. (1) We developed a dual-wavelength confocal microscopy systems that enables the in-situ observation of phase separation regions as they emerge on the surfaces of soft silicone gels. While the contact-induced migration of solvent has been previously characterized for soft hydrogels, realizing such experiments in soft silicone gels (e.g., PDMS) is difficult. For widely used soft PDMS materials, the gels are prepared by directly crosslinking a portion of silicone oligomers, where the solvent consists of the same PDMS chains unattached to the networks. The similarity in chemical composition between the crosslinked networks and solvent phase poses significant challenges for microscopic imaging. To distinguish these two phases through imaging, we coated the air/gel interface with functionalized fluorescent nanobeads, while staining the free polymeric chains with UV-sensitive oil dyes. The emission/absorption spectra of these two fluorescent sources (nanobeads and UV-sensitive dye) were carefully selected to be far enough apart to prevent any overlap of their fluorescent signals. Consequently, we can obtain high-resolution confocal images of both wetting profiles and the migration of free chains, as shown in Fig. 1(b) of the Equipment section (Sec. 4.4). Compared with conventional optical methods, this confocal microscopy enables high-resolution (< 1 micron meter) imaging of both phases within a short measurement period (< 10s), offering a powerful tool for in-situ characterization of migration dynamics of free chains. By combining confocal microscopy with a three-dimensional (3D) tracking method, we systematically investigated interfacial responses of soft silicone gels in soft wetting, including measurements of solid surface stresses at varying crosslinking densities (Zhao and Xu*, et al., Physics of Fluids (2025)) and the emergence of phase separation regions (Qian and Xu*, et al., Physical Review Research (2024)). (2) We clarified the underlying physical mechanisms governing the migration of free chains. Using confocal microscopy, we directly observed the gradual growth of the phase separation region near the contact line. However, the influence of key material parameters on this process remains unclear. To address this, we model the balance between the diverging elastic energy and the viscous dissipation near the contact line. By applying Onsager’s variational principle, we developed a reduced model with minimal material assumptions. This phenomenological model effectively captures the poroelastic diffusivity of free silicone chains through polymeric networks of varying crosslinking densities. Given that the free chains migrate less than 5 μm over several hours, we quantitatively measured the poroelastic diffusivity to be as small as 10^-15 m^2/s — a value that has been difficult to measure in previous experiments. Additionally, we found that the equilibrium size of the phase separation region is determined by the inherent length scale of soft silicone gels (e.g., elastocapillary length or osmocapillary length). This study on the crossover from poroelastic diffusion to equilibrium state is published on Qian and Xu*, et al., Physical Review Research (2024). Although Onsager’s principle has recently been applied to understand non-equilibrium behaviors in soft matter, it has not, until now, been employed to study soft interface dynamics. Our findings demonstrate the potential of this theoretical framework for investigating complex relaxation phenomena at soft interfaces. (3) We systematically investigated how wetting-induced phase separation governs the surface properties of soft gels. Our research in this section encompasses three key studies: First, due to the relationship between crosslinking density and the degree of phase separation, we found that a liquid droplet can spontaneously move along a soft gel substrate with a stiffness gradient. The droplet’s velocity can be quantitatively controlled by adjusting the degree of the surface gradient. This work is published in Zhao and Xu*, et al., Physics of Fluids (2025). Second, by integrating fluorescent imaging with interfacial mechanical characterizations of soft gels, we developed a novel traction force microscope (TFM) on a rheometer equipped with a parallel-plate shear plate. The implementation of TFM relies on a precise description of the interfacial mechanical properties of soft gels by incorporating the wetting-induced phase separation. The micro-mechanical device (TFM) enables the measurement of stress heterogeneity at soft interfaces resulting from the spreading of a complex fluid. These results are published in Hu and Xu*, et al., Journal of Rheology (2024). Third, we quantified how the extraction of free polymer chains from a constrained soft gel may induce the surface instability and modulates the effective adhesion energy. The work was published in Vaisakh and Xu*, et al., Materials (2022).

16305821.label: Major findings and research outcome
16305821.value: First, we developed a high-resolution confocal microscopy technique and an associated image analysis algorithm to effectively reconstruct the microscale contact profiles and characterize the slow emergence of the phase separation region near contact lines (Zhao and Xu* et al., Physics of Fluids 2025; Qian and Xu* et al., Physical Review Research, 2024). Using this imaging method, we observed, for the first time, the wetting-induced migration of free chains on soft gel surfaces. Our findings revealed the slow diffusivity of free chains (~10^-15 m^2/s) and showed that the equilibrium size of the phase separation region depends on the intrinsic material lengthscales of soft gels (e.g., elastocapillary length or osmocapillary length). Furthermore, we expect that our experimental method can be further employed to image diverse phase-transition process (e.g., liquid-liquid phase transition) in soft gels. Second, we proposed a phenomenological model that reveals the physical principles governing the phase separation process at different stages. Due to the non-equilibrium nature of the migration dynamics of free chains, theoretical modeling of the associated dynamics based on microscopic interactions is challenging. By considering the interplay between the diverging elastic energy of crosslinked networks and the viscous dissipation of migrating free chains near the contact points, we employed the Onsager’s variational principle to obtain a master curve, which effectively characterizes the growth dynamics of the phase separation region on soft polymeric gels with vary crosslinking densities. Through a direct comparison between this phenomenological model and experimental results, we determined the poroelastic diffusivity of partially crosslinked free chains (Xu* et al., Physical Review Research, 2024). Furthermore, we expect that the variational approach adopted in our reduced model can be extended to describe dynamic processes in various soft gel systems. Third, we functionalized the wetting properties of soft gel surfaces by controlling the phase separation process. We showed that the crosslinking density determines the degree of phase separation, which in turn affects the gel surface energy. Consequently, we realized the spontaneous motion of liquid droplets along a soft gel surface with a gradient in crosslinking density (Zhao and Xu, et al. Physics of Fluids, 2025). Additionally, the extraction of free chains can cause the formation of surface instabilities and creases (Vaisakh and Xu*, et al., Materials, 2022) on soft PDMS surfaces. When a liquid spreads over these roughened PDMS substrates, the wetting hysteresis can be quantitatively tuned through its pre-wetting history (Yan and Xu*, et al., arXiv:2503:03118).

16305821.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16305821.value: The findings from this project provide valuable insights for future research in two main areas. First, phase separation within a soft medium is a highly biologically relevant thermodynamic process. For instance, liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) in extracellular matrices plays a significant role in the formation of biological organelles in living systems. The experimental results and theoretical modeling methods developed in the current project may lay the groundwork for further understanding of phase separation in soft polymeric gels. In future studies, we will investigate how to quantitatively control LLPS in a soft polymeric matrix. Second, the contact-induced phase separation offers a potential strategy to regulate the surface mechanical properties of soft gels. For example, as free chains migrate, we expect the effective adhesion energy to change over time at the contact interfaces. Thus, we plan to quantitatively regulate the adhesive properties of soft interfaces by dynamically controlling the solvent extraction process. Additionally, this dynamic mechanism may also be relevant to design synthetic systems with bio-adhesive features.

16305821.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16305821.value: Wetting on soft solids plays an important role in various emerging engineering areas, such as wearable medical devices, soft robots, and synthetic living materials. When a liquid droplet is placed on soft solids, such as compliant polymeric gels, it not only induces divergent capillary bridges but also triggers the extraction of the solvent phase (i.e., phase separation) at the contact lines. However, due to the slow relaxation dynamics and non-equilibrium features of migrating free chains, direct experimental observation and theoretical modeling of this process are highly challenging. To address this, we developed a dual-wavelength confocal microscopy technique that enables the direct imaging of the emergence and growth dynamics of phase separation during soft wetting. We experimentally show that the extracted free chains suppress local elastic divergence while leaving the overall capillary ridge unchanged. Using Onsager’s variational principle, we developed a phenomenological model that effectively captures the crossover from a diffusive to an equilibrium state. Moreover, by controlling the degree of phase separation by varying crosslinking density, we achieved spontaneous droplet motion along a soft gradient surface. These findings provide insights for the future design of functional soft materials.

16305921.label: Realisation of objectives
16305921.value: This project successfully achieved its five primary objectives through the development and application of an advanced deep learning framework. Below, we outline the realisation of each objective and address challenges encountered during the research process. Objective 1: Development of a High-Resolution Wet Deposition Modelling Framework The project developed a semi-supervised residual convolutional neural network (CNN) integrating ground observations, satellite remote sensing, and reanalysis data to estimate wet deposition of nss-SO42-, NO3-, NH4+, and Ca2+ at 0.5°×0.5° resolution across the Northern Hemisphere. The model incorporated an encoder-generator architecture with residual networks and Interleaved Transfer Layers, achieving annual R2 >0.7 and monthly R2 >0.6 for all species, outperforming traditional methods in capturing nonlinear relationships between emissions, meteorology, and wet deposition patterns. This objective was achieved, providing a robust tool for long-term deposition analysis. Objective 2: Analysis of Seasonal Differences Seasonal variability was thoroughly investigated, revealing significant patterns. nss-SO42- and NO3- wet depositions were substantially higher in spring and summer, driven by increased precipitation from monsoon rains and subtropical cyclones. NH4+ wet deposition peaked in spring and summer, linked to elevated precipitation and agricultural NH₃ emissions, which were ∼50% higher in summer than spring and three times higher than winter. Ca2+ wet deposition in eastern China peaked during spring dust events and summer monsoons. These findings fully address the objective, highlighting the critical role of seasonal factors in deposition dynamics. Objective 3: Historical Evolution of Acid Rain and Neutralization Factor The study analyzed the historical evolution (2005–2017) of acid rain and neutralization factors across the Northern Hemisphere. A key focus was the calculation of the Neutralization Factor of Ca2+ (NF[Ca2+]), which exhibited a clear downward trend in most countries. In 2014, Japan, China, and South Korea demonstrated decreases in NF[Ca2+] by 47.2%, 39.6%, and 32.2%, respectively, compared to 2006. South Korea, Thailand, and Laos also showed declines of over 30% within the same period. This reduction reflects the diminished buffering capacity of Ca2+ against acid rain in East Asia, a consequence of emission reduction strategies such as end-of-pipe treatments and the closure of small factories. Our findings reveal a concurrent decrease in Ca2+ and acidic ions (NO3- and nss-SO42-), with Ca2+ wet deposition declining faster than NO3- and nss-SO42-. This trend is particularly concerning as it could exacerbate soil and ecosystem deterioration. The declining trend of Ca2+ wet deposition underscores the need for further analysis to understand its long-term ecological impacts and inform future emission control strategies. This objective was fully achieved, providing critical insights into regional acid rain trends and their linkage to emission changes. Objective 4: Response to Emission Changes The framework effectively quantified species-specific responses to emission changes, leveraging spatiotemporal deposition dynamics and emission linkages. Key findings include: Spatial patterns: high nss-SO42- levels were noted in China’s Sichuan Basin, while NO3- and NH4+ depositions were particularly high in China’s heavily industrialized and agriculturally intensive regions (Pearl River Delta region, North China Plain, and Sichuan Basin), driven by high nitrogen usage and precipitation. Temporal trends: nss-SO42- deposition decreased by >30% in China (2008–2018) following sulfur emission controls, while NO3- deposition increased by >40% in southern/eastern China (2001–2017) due to rising vehicle emissions. NH4+ deposition did not show regular temporal variations but was linked to agricultural activities. Ca2+ deposition declined significantly in East Asia and Central Europe post-2013, reflecting reduced dust emissions. Objective 5: Ecological risk implications Ecological risk assessments were conducted by comparing observed wet deposition levels with critical load thresholds, which were derived from empirical values established in previous literature. These thresholds represent the maximum deposition levels that ecosystems can tolerate without significant harm. The methodology for risk assessment involved comparing observed or modeled deposition levels with critical load values to identify areas where thresholds were exceeded. Ecological risk assessments revealed that 25.5% of freshwater bodies in East Asia exceeded the critical load for nss-SO42- (25 kg/ha) in 2015, while 21.7% and 2.1% of grasslands exceeded NO3- thresholds of 2 and 4 kg N/ha, respectively, in 2014. The study confirmed that wet deposition alone can pose significant threats to ecosystems, particularly in temperate forests and freshwater systems. This objective was achieved by providing critical data for ecosystem protection.

16305921.value: This study has achieved breakthroughs in atmospheric deposition research through the development of an advanced deep learning framework. Key findings are summarized as follows: 1. High-resolution wet-deposition modeling A semi-supervised residual convolutional-neural-network (CNN) integrating ground observations, satellite remote sensing, and reanalysis data was developed to estimate wet deposition of nss-SO42-, NO3-, NH4+, and Ca2+ at 0.5°×0.5° resolution across the Northern Hemisphere. The model incorporated an encoder-generator architecture with residual networks and Interleaved Transfer Layers, achieving annual R2 > 0.7 and monthly R2 > 0.6 for all species, outperforming traditional methods in capturing nonlinear relationships between emissions, meteorology, and deposition patterns. 2. Spatiotemporal deposition dynamics and emission linkages Spatial analysis revealed key deposition hotspots, including extreme nss-SO42- levels were noted in China’s Sichuan Basin, while NO3- and NH4+ depositions were particularly high in China’s heavily industrialized and agriculturally intensive regions (PRD region, North China Plain, and Sichuan Basin) due to high nitrogen usage and precipitation. Temporally, nss-SO42- deposition in China decreased by >30% (2008–2018) following sulfur emission controls, while NO3- deposition increased by >40% in southern/eastern China (2001–2017) due to rising vehicle emissions. NH4+ deposition did not show regular temporal variations tightly coupled with agricultural NH3 emissions. Ca2+ deposition declined significantly in East Asia and Central Europe post-2013, reflecting reduced dust emissions. 3. Seasonal variability Seasonal variability also emerged as a significant factor. nss-SO_4^2- and NO3- depositions were substantially higher in spring and summer, driven by increased precipitation from monsoon rains and subtropical cyclones. NH4+ deposition peaked in spring and summer, linked to elevated precipitation and agricultural NH3 emissions, which were ∼50% higher in summer than spring and three times higher than winter. Ca2+ deposition in eastern China peaking during spring dust events and summer monsoons. 4. Ecological risk implications Ecological risk assessments showed that 25.5% of freshwater bodies in East Asia exceeded the critical load for nss-SO42- (25 kg/ha) in 2015, while 21.7% of grasslands exceeded NO3- thresholds of 2 kg N/ha in 2014. The relative decline of Ca2+ deposition compared to acidic species has compromised the acid neutralization capacity in the region, with the neutralization factor of Ca2+ decreasing markedly in Japan, China, and South Korea between 2006 and 2014. This trend, alongside significant nitrogen exceedances in East Asian grasslands, underscores the urgent need for stringent and coordinated sulfur and nitrogen emission controls to mitigate risks of ecosystem acidification.

16305921.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16305921.value: This research establishes a foundation for three key extensions: 1. Temporal refinement: Expanding the framework to produce daily-scale deposition estimates through integration of higher-resolution meteorological data, enabling real-time pollution monitoring. 2. Multi-process integration: Incorporating dry deposition mechanisms and aerosol chemistry modules to develop a comprehensive atmospheric deposition model, particularly crucial for arid regions. 3. Climate feedback analysis: Coupling the deposition dataset with Earth system models to quantify how changing deposition patterns affect carbon sequestration in sensitive ecosystems like boreal forests. Immediate next steps include: 1. Establishing an open-access data portal for the hemispheric deposition dataset 2. Developing policy-oriented visualization tools highlighting critical load exceedance areas for national environmental agencies 3. Extending the analysis to include dry deposition measures could provide a more comprehensive view of total deposition loads, which is vital for assessing ecological impacts more accurately. 4. Applying the model to forecast future trends based on different emission scenarios could offer valuable insights for policy-makers and environmental agencies to formulate more effective strategies for emission control and environmental protection.

16305921.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16305921.value: This research project developed a deep learning method to map the falling of certain chemicals from the atmosphere across the Northern Hemisphere over the last two decades, with a focus on how these chemicals, like calcium and nitrates, settle out of the air and onto the ground. This process, known as wet deposition, is crucial for understanding environmental health, particularly in combating acid rain, which can harm ecosystems. Our findings reveal important trends in heavily polluted regions. In China, sulfur deposition decreased by over 30% in areas like the Sichuan Basin after clean air policies were implemented, but nitrate deposition increased by more than 40% in southern and eastern regions, such as the Pearl River Delta, due to rising car emissions. The natural “anti-acid” minerals in precipitation (especially calcium) are decreasing faster than expected, making ecosystems more vulnerable. For instance, in places like Japan, China, and South Korea, the ability of the environment to neutralize acid rain has decreased, partially due to successful efforts to reduce air pollution emissions. These insights are vital for making informed decisions about environmental policies and conservation strategies, helping to protect natural landscapes and the health of our planet.

16306021.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16306021.value: 粘度(vicosity)作為內部流動阻力的量度，是所有液體最基本的特性。粘度在廣泛的工程應用中起著至關重要的作用。但純離子液體 (pIL) 的粘度值數據受由限制採集速率的實驗測量確定。目前，具有可用粘度測量值的pIL數量是3,066 ，不到pIL總數452,751（文獻中報導的 1344 個陽離子和 357 個陰離子的組合）的1%。長期以來，研究人員一直試圖建立一個廣泛的 pIL 粘度數據庫，以滿足學術界和工業界研究人員迅速增長的需求。近年來，分子和材料科學領域正在開展廣泛的數據驅動機器學習工作。與基於不同時間和長度尺度的基本方程的實驗或計算/模擬相比，大量開發的機器學習模型可以實現純粹基於可用數據的快速預測。多功能機器學習方法提供了一個理想的平台來加速評估並揭示pIL結構與黏度之間的相關性。 根據在粘度方面的最新研究進展，我們將開發一個通用的圖卷積神經網絡 (G2-CNN)，以及基於分子間特性相關矩陣的新描述符，例如電負性、極化率、疏水性、氫鍵和范德華體積每個離子中的基團，以便更好地描述 pIL 中的Many-body效應以模擬粘度。基於 G2-CNN 模型，一個包含 259,350 個 pIL（分別來自6個陽離子和 10 個陰離子家族的910 個陽離子和 285 個陰離子的組合）的不同溫度下的粘度數據庫將被構建。此外，強化學習增強的變分自編碼器將被集成到 G2CNN 中，以響應對設計更多樣化的基於嗎啉（Morpholinium）的 pIL 的需求。我們將使用耦合分子動力學模擬和高效的修飾擴散方法對模型設計的pIL進行驗證。本研究提出的深度學習模型將引起化學界更多的興趣，促進人工智能專家交流，激發更多令人興奮的研究，並加速許多傳統上成本密集的化學研發工作。該提案的科學價值不僅來自大量的 pILs 粘度數據，還來自該項目開發的人工智能平台，以及開發分子和材料的逆向設計技術。

16306121.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16306121.value: 活性流体薄膜动力学的建模与模拟

16306121.label: Project Objectives
16306121.value: To study the stationary solutions to the evolution equation for thin films of active fluids. From the number of parameters controlling the stationary solutions, it is deduced that they are not solely determined by the finite film volume and the free energies involved. This is distinct from what we have for drops of passive liquids on solid surfaces. The spreading process toward a particular stationary solution will be studied as well, with a focus on the effect of initial state, which is indicated by the existence of multiple stationary solutions for a given film volume. To study the effect of contact line dissipation on thin film dynamics of active fluids. Understanding contact line motion is essential to a complete description of drop dynamics on solid surfaces. This applies to both passive and active fluids, and the latter is expected to be richer in drop dynamics. To investigate the thin film dynamics by introducing a spatiotemporally patterned active stress, as motivated by the recent advances in the control of active matter dynamics through spatially structured activity. Many interesting dynamic phenomena are expected from solving the thin film evolution equation.

16306121.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16306121.value: 远离平衡态的活性物质系统直接在活性粒子的层面上从环境提取能量。尽管作用于每一个活性粒子的活性力相互独立，其方向由粒子运动本身决定，集体的非平衡现象却可以在长时间和大范围内产生。这一特征区分了活性系统与外场或梯度驱动的非活性系统。活性系统的例子包括鱼群、鸟群、细菌群落、流体中的人造自推进粒子和亚细胞水平中的生物聚合物（例如，作为细胞骨架组成部分的微管和微丝）。 基于实验、建模、分析和模拟的有效协作，针对大尺度集体现象的活性软物质研究取得了快速发展。在这方面，热力学自洽的粗粒化描述是非常必要的，尤其当涉及到时间长、规模大的活性流体的流体力学，例如自搅拌向列相液晶，自泳胶体，有序的球形胶体群和“活的液晶”。一类特殊的活性软物质系统的特征是存在与固体基底接触的自由界面。对于这种几何中的非活性流体，其浸润动力学已经有了几十年的广泛研究。然而，流体的活性特征，其主要表现为力偶极子产生的活性应力，将导致液滴动力学发生巨大变化。 本项目旨在研究活性向列液晶的薄膜动力学。基于 Onsager 的变分原理，活性流体的薄膜动力学模型可以循序渐进地发展。这是从不可压缩的简单液体开始，然后加入向列相的能量效应，最后再包括活性应力，它取决于活性粒子的向列排列。考虑到与有限体积和初始状态相关的控制参数，最简单的活性薄膜模型在稳态解和传播过程上已经不同于非活性模型。基于浸润动力学的研究，移动接触线导致的耗散将被纳入固体基底上活性液滴的动力学建模。还将研究对活性的动态的时空式样控制，这些最近已有实验展示，从而对薄膜动力学做出有趣和相关的预测。

16306121.label: Realisation of objectives
16306121.value: Objective 1: Stationary states. Model. — We considered a droplet of active nematics under lubrication approximation. To model the statics and dynamics of active thin films, a variational approach has been taken by applying Onsager’s variational principle (OVP), which ensures thermodynamical consistency. Compared to a thin film of one-component simple liquid, the dynamics of a thin film of active nematic fluid involves two additional driving mechanisms: the elastic energy due to the nematic liquid crystalline order and the active stress due to the activity of the self-propelled particles. These two mechanisms have been successfully incorporated into our variational approach. ODE system. — From the full model based on OVP, the case of uniform extensile activity has been investigated because a stationary shape of the droplet can be reached. An ordinary differential equation (ODE) system has been derived to determine the stationary shape of the active droplet. This involves two length parameters $h_\infty$ and $h_0$, but their values are unknown beforehand and can only be determined by searching for a special ODE solution that produces the right volume $V$ and contact angle $\theta_e$. Therefore, regarding the stationary shapes, the ODE system is interpretive but not predictive. This justifies the necessity of a full numerical study based on the time-dependent evolution equation. Thin film evolution equation. — We have carried out numerical simulations for solving the thin film evolution equation. For this purpose, the droplet volume $V$, set by the initial height profile, and the contact angle $\theta_e$, implemented by the boundary condition, are needed by the numerical computation. Note that these two control parameters have clear physical meaning and are directly given by the problem. It has been numerically verified that the evolution equation can produce time-dependent solutions that reach stationary states. It has been further confirmed that these stationary states can be obtained as well by solving the ODE with the two length parameters $h_\infty$ and $h_0$ being chosen for best numerical fitting. Our investigation, which uses both the ODE system and the evolution equation, shows that it is necessary to perform a full numerical study based on the time-dependent evolution equation controlled by the droplet volume and the contact angle, which are clearly defined and directly given by the problem. Finally, we add that (1) stationary states are reached by solving the evolution equation to simulate droplet spreading processes, (2) stationary states are shown to be stable against perturbative activity oscillations in space, (3) a dimensionless parameter $C_V$ has been defined to study how it controls the stationary shape, and the crossover between the parabolic and flat profiles has been numerically observed if $C_V$ is continuously varied across 1. Objective 2: Contact line dissipation. Dynamic boundary condition in the full model. — The modelling of contact line motion is essential to the study of active droplet dynamics. Based on the OVP, a complete model is derived in which the contact line velocities are governed by a dynamic boundary condition. Effective boundary condition with apparent contact angle. — While in theory the dynamic boundary condition can be directly implemented, we have chosen a more practical way to treat the contact line motion. It fits the nature of the problem and saves computational resources. By focusing on the regime of weak nematic elasticity, we have carried out numerical simulations to investigate the thin film dynamics driven by the competition between active and capillary forces. Without resolving the hydrodynamics in the small contact line region, which is important on its own but not the focus of the present work, we have employed an effective boundary condition in which the equilibrium contact angle is imposed as the apparent contact angle above a thin layer dominated by the nematic elasticity. Here, it has been assumed that this layer next to the contact line retains its stationary profile and, hence, results in the equilibrium contact angle as the apparent contact angle being asymptotically approached. Physically, this layer is of negligible thickness and dominated by the nematic elastic force, and its stationary profile can be retained if the viscous dissipation within the layer is suppressed by introducing a large slip (i.e., a small friction coefficient at the contact line and a large slip length for the Navier slip boundary condition applied on the solid surface). Summary. — Through the modelling efforts described above, the contact line dissipation in the present study is dominated by the viscous dissipation in a meso-scale wedge-shaped region that is explicitly computed. Objective 3: Thin film dynamics subject to spatiotemporally patterned active stress. The OVP-based full model allows us to investigate the effects of spatiotemporally patterned active stress on thin film dynamics. Stability of stationary droplet. — Subject to uniform extensile activity, a stationary droplet can be stabilized. Our numerical results have shown that when a cosinusoidal perturbation of activity is applied, the droplet can remain stationary with its shape responding to the periodic spatial variation of the active stress. Physically, a stationary height profile is stabilized by the balance between capillary and active forces, and this stability can be maintained even if a periodic spatial variation is introduced to the active stress. Migration dynamics. — We have investigated the droplet migration driven by the wettability gradient, which is measured by a spatially varying contact angle on the substrate. For comparison, we have also investigated the droplet migration driven by the activity gradient in the active fluid. This is achieved by introducing a spatially varying activity coefficient given by a smoothed step function in space. We have observed droplet deformation and unidirectional migration through numerical simulations. Furthermore, the numerical data have been compared to a semi-quantitative estimation based on (i) the stationary shape and (ii) the energy balance between active work and viscous dissipation. Such comparison has produced semi-quantitative agreement for droplet deformation magnitude and migration velocity, confirming the physical mechanisms underlying these phenomena.
