17108921.label: Realisation of objectives
17108921.value: This study aimed to investigate the effect of nucleos/tide analogue on HBV integration in both chronic hepatitis B (CHB) patients (Objectives 1 & 2); and in hepatoma cell lines (Objectives 3 & 4). In relation to Objectives 1 and 2, we studied the effect of nucleos/tide analogue therapy on HBV integration and hepatocyte clonal expansion in 35 CHB patients receiving nucleos/tide analogue therapy in the form of entecavir, telbivudine, or lamivudine. At baseline, HBV integration was detectable in all 35 patients. The extent of HBV integration was reduced after 1 year of treatment, with a median reduction of 0.22 log. After 10 years of treatment, HBV integration was still detectable, with a median of 0.93 log reduction in integration frequency. This finding showed that, although not a direct target of nucleos/tide analogue, integrated HBV DNA can be reduced by nucleos/tide analogue, and HBV integration and hepatocyte clone size are affected by antiviral therapy in CHB patients. As HBV integration is associated with the development of HCC in CHB patients. The result of this study pinpoints the importance of antiviral therapy in decreasing HCC risk and suggests an early antiviral treatment in CHB patients. In relation to Objectives 3 and 4, we made use of a hepatoma HepG2 cell line with integrated HBV DNA(named HepG2/SB/HBV) and studied the effect of entecavir on HBV integration, cell proliferation, and apoptosis. Entecavir administration did not affect the proliferation of the parental integrated HBV DNA-free HepG2 cells. Interestingly, entecavir specifically affected the survival of HepG2/SB/HBV. In HepG2/SB/HBV, the amount of phosphorylated histone H3 was reduced upon entecavir administration, resulting in cell-cycle arrest. Entecavir had no effect on the proliferation of HepG2 cells. However, it selectively inhibited the survival of HepG2/SB/HBV by reducing the abundance of phosphorylated histone H3, which led to cell cycle arrest . Consequently, the clone size of HepG2/SB/HBV after entecavir treatment was reduced. The results of this in vitro study suggested that, apart from its direct antiviral effect, entecavir targets hepatocytes with integrated HBV DNA, causing cell cycle arrest in these cells. Taken together, this study showed that nucleos/tide analogues could reduce the extent of HBV integration in CHB patients, with the possible mechanism being that they suppress the proliferation of hepatocytes carrying integrated HBV DNA.

17108921.label: Major findings and research outcome
17108921.value: This study contains 2 main parts :1) HBV integration in CHB patients; and 2) HBV integration in vitro. Part 1: We’ve demonstrated that NUC treatment can reduce HBV integration in CHB patients. The extent of reduction correlated positively with the duration of treatment. Before treatment, HBV integration was detectable in all CHB patients before treatment. and HBV integration could be reduced by antiviral therapy (0.22 log reduction in year 1 and 0.93 log reduction in year 10). HBV integration near HCC-associated genes such as FN1, TAX1BP1 and UGT1A1 were identified. This study demonstrated that, in addition to its suppression of on HBV reverse transcription, NUC can also reduce the extent of HBV integration. This finding is consistent with the reduced risk of HCC in CHB patients receiving NUC. The result of Part 1 has been published in Clinical Infectious Diseases, 2023, Vol.76 (3), p.e801-e809. Part 2: We’ve demonstrated that nucleos/tide analogue can reduce HBV integration in hepatoma cell lines. We demonstrated that entecavir selectively inhibit the proliferation of hepatoma cells with integrated HBV DNA, but not the parental integrated HBVDNA-free parental cells. A closer look of the cell characteristics showed that the abundance of phosphorylated histone H3, and hence cell proliferation, was reduced by entecavir treatment in the cells with integrated HBV DNA, but not in the parental integration-free cells. The in vitro study involving hepatoma cell lines has been published in Antiviral Research, 2025, vol.18, 237:106120. (doi: 10.1016/j.antiviral.2025.106120).

17109321.value: Prof Chan, Esther Wai Yin Dr Ho, Yuen Chi Prof Mak, Lung Yi Prof Seto, Wai Kay Walter Prof Yuen, Richard Man Fung

17109321.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17109321.value: 標題 恩格列淨對預防經核苷（酸）類似物治療的晚期肝纖維化或肝硬化慢性乙型肝炎患者的肝纖維化和肝硬化惡化的功效：一項隨機、雙盲安慰劑的對照試驗 摘要 慢性乙型肝炎影響全球 2.57 億人。 在2017 年，它導致約 3970 萬例的肝硬化和 40 萬例的肝硬化相關死亡。然而，目前尚無針對肝纖維化/肝硬化的治療方法。儘管核苷（酸）類似物能極大程度地抑制病毒複製，但經核苷（酸）類似物治療的患者仍可能發生肝纖維化/肝硬化惡化的情況。 第2型鈉-葡萄糖協同轉運蛋白(SGLT2) 抑製劑是一種抗糖尿病藥物，可通過減少肝臟脂肪變性/炎症、抑制腎素-血管緊張素醛固酮系統激活和減少體液瀦留來預防肝纖維化/肝硬化惡化，其效果與血糖控制無關。糖尿病患者的臨床研究表明，SGLT2抑製劑可減少肝脂肪變性/炎症、消退腹水（肝硬化併發症），並根據終末期肝病模型評分顯示改善肝功能參數和生存預後。我們經全港電子醫療數據庫的初步數據顯示，在患有糖尿病的慢性乙型肝炎患者（n=9,502）中，SGLT2抑製劑能降低三年內肝硬化發展風險達 58% 。目前沒有關於SGLT2抑製劑在預防慢性乙型肝炎患者肝纖維化/肝硬化惡化的隨機對照試驗。磁共振彈性成像和肝纖維化掃描是用於測量肝臟硬度的非侵入性技術，而前者比後者更為準確。 「老藥新用」概念的新穎性在於把原用於治療糖尿病患者的SGLT2抑制劑轉用於預防慢性乙型肝炎患者的肝纖維化/肝硬化惡化，此新概念值得进一步探索。我們以雙盲、隨機、安慰劑對照試驗來檢視恩格列淨（一種 SLGT2 抑製劑）對照安慰劑（比例為1:1）在降低糖尿病和非糖尿病並經核苷（酸）類似物治療的晚期肝纖維化/代償性肝硬化慢性乙型肝炎患者肝臟硬度的功效。我們將從現有的肝纖維化掃描數據庫中隨機抽取228 名患者作研究。療程組將被給予每日10毫克的恩格列淨。安慰劑藥丸會被製作成與恩格列淨藥丸外觀一致。受試者將被安排服用為期三年的恩格列淨或安慰劑，並接受臨床、體測和實驗室測試（基準日、第 8週、第16 周和此後每 4 個月）。他們將在基準日、第一年、第二年和第三年末接受肝纖維化掃描，並在基準日和第三年末接受磁共振彈性成像，以測量肝臟硬度。主要結果將會是兩組患者在第三年末相對於基準日的肝臟硬度的變化（通過磁共振彈性成像測量）。次要結果是緩解晚期肝纖維化/肝硬化、改善晚期肝纖維化惡化為肝硬化的進展、實驗室結果（肝轉氨酶、鐵蛋白、葡萄糖、血脂）和體測數據。 我們的研究成果將判斷SGLT2 抑製劑可否預防經核苷（酸）類似物治療的慢性乙型肝炎患者的肝纖維化/肝硬化惡化。

17109821.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17109821.value: The effect of sugars on health has been a controversial topic, as evidence from early experimental animal studies were fraught with limitations: 1) using fructose as the sole source of sugar in the diet; 2) replacing starch with sugars completely in the experimental diet; 3) using supraphysiological doses; and 4) short study period (a few weeks). This means their results are not directly translatable to human-relevant advice. Using intake levels closer to human consumption (10%kcal vs. 25%kcal), our preliminary data suggest that there is no dose-related effect of sucrose on body composition, food intake and glucose homeostasis in two generations of C57BL/6 mice, which is in stark contrast to the popular belief that “sugar causes obesity and diabetes”. With advances in our understanding of the potential intergenerational effects of paternal and maternal diets on the metabolic health of offspring, it is important to generate evidence to support or refute the hypothesis that high sugar consumption is detrimental not only to the current generation, but the generations to come. The proposed project is the first of its kind to examine the effect of lifelong high sucrose consumption on metabolic and endocrine health of not only 1, but 3 generations of mice. Specifically, we will test the following primary hypotheses: i) lifelong consumption of 25%kcal free sugars (in the form of sucrose) will NOT induce over-eating and impaired glucose metabolism, and increase adiposity compared with a 0%kcal or 10%kcal sucrose diet; ii) offspring (F1) of F0 mice fed a high sucrose diet will NOT have higher adiposity, and worse metabolic and endocrine health compared with offspring of F0 mice fed a low sucrose diet; iii) a high sucrose diet will NOT impair metabolic and endocrine health of F1 mice compared with a low added sucrose diet; iv) offspring (F2) of F1 female mice exposed to low/high sucrose diet in utero will NOT have different susceptibility to the effect of high sucrose diet on body composition, and metabolic and endocrine disturbances. Importantly, unlike previous studies, the levels of sucrose examined in the proposed study are in line with current recommended limits of free sugars intake for humans. Results from the proposed studies may provide new evidence to challenge the orthodox beliefs that “sugar causes obesity and diabetes” in the current/next generations, leading to a shift in research directions and clinical practice. 糖對健康的影響一直是一個有爭議的話題，因為早期實驗動物研究的證據充滿以下的局限性：1) 使用果糖作為飲食中糖的唯一來源； 2)在實驗食糧中用糖完全代替澱粉； 3) 使用超生理劑量的糖； 4）實驗週期短（一般只有數週）。這意味著這些實驗的結果不能直接轉化為與人類相關的建議。 通過使用更接近人類糖進食量的飲食（10%kcal 對 25%kcal），我們的初步數據表明於兩代 C57BL/6 小鼠中，蔗糖對身體成分、進食量和葡萄糖穩態都沒有劑量相關的影響，這與「糖會導致肥胖和糖尿病」這普遍看法形成鮮明對比。 隨著我們對父親和母親飲食對後代代謝健康的潛在代際影響的理解不斷進步，產生證據來支持或反駁高糖攝入不僅對當代人而且對後代有害的假設將變得重要。 擬議的研究項目是同類項目中第一個研究終生高蔗糖攝入對不僅是 1 代，而且是 3 代小鼠的代謝和內分泌健康的影響。 具體來說，我們將測試以下主要假設： i) 與 0%kcal 或 10%kcal 蔗糖飲食相比，終生攝入 25%kcal 游離糖（以蔗糖形式）不會導致暴飲暴食、葡萄糖代謝受損或並增加肥胖； ii) 與餵食低蔗糖飲食的 F0 小鼠的後代相比，餵食高蔗糖飲食的 F0 小鼠的後代 (F1) 不會有更高的肥胖以及更差的代謝和內分泌健康； iii) 與低蔗糖飲食相比，高蔗糖飲食不會損害 F1 小鼠的代謝和內分泌健康； iv) 在子宮內暴露於低/高蔗糖飲食的 F1 雌性小鼠的後代 (F2) 不會對高蔗糖飲食對身體成分、代謝和內分泌紊亂的影響具有不同的易感性。 重要的是，與之前的研究不同，擬議研究中測試的蔗糖水平符合目前推薦的人類游離糖攝入量限制。擬議研究的結果可能會提供新的證據來挑戰當前/下一代「糖可導致肥胖和糖尿病」的傳統觀念，從而導致研究方向和臨床實踐的轉變。

17110021.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17110021.value: Stilbenes are a rare group of natural products produced by a small number of unrelated plants. Several stilbenes such as pterostilbene and piceatannol are promising nutraceuticals due to their potent anti-oxidation and anti-cancer properties. As stilbenes are found in minuscule quantities from a few natural sources, their production cost as nutraceuticals are undesirably high. Stilbene synthases (STSs), which catalyze the key reaction step in stilbene biosynthesis, are sporadically present in isolated lineages within the plant kingdom. They are believed to have recruited from the ubiquitous chalcone synthase (CHS) independently during speciation in different taxonomic groups. Previously, we identified a pathogen-inducible STS gene (SbSTS1) in sorghum, a cereal crop well known for its ability to survive environmental extremes and its distinct natural products of agricultural and nutritional significance. Recently available genomes for a large number of grass species have allowed us to retrieve STS-like genes from sorghum-related grass species including sugarcane, switchgrass, and several millet species, suggesting the presence of stilbene biosynthesis pathway in a small phylogenetic group within the grass family. In this study, we will characterize the catalytic properties of the different grass STS-like enzymes and analyze the stilbene profiles in the respective species. In addition, site-directed mutagenesis will be performed to elucidate the molecular events potentially leading to successful acquisition of STS activities by CHS enzymes during speciation of stilbene-producing lineages in grasses. Moreover, we recently identified pterostilbene as a potentially efficacious defense metabolite in sorghum against its major pathogen Colletotrichum sublineolum. Pterostilbene biosynthesis requires the sequential activities of SbSTS1 and an O-methyltransferase (OMT). Two novel stilbene OMT genes (SbSOMT1 and SbSOMT2) which are pathogen-inducible and phylogenetically unique in sorghum have been identified. Their biochemical functions in relation to pterostilbene formation will be thoroughly examined . Furthermore, to understand the biological functions of stilbenes in sorghum, transgenic over-expression lines and gene-editing mutants will be generated for evaluation of metabolite profile, infection phenotypes, and agronomic properties. Overall, this proposed study will provide insights into how distinct stilbene biosynthesis pathways are recruited in a specific group of grass species but not in other related cereals. It will also establish whether pterostilbene is an essential defense component in sorghum for disease resistance. Furthermore, the proposed generation of transgenic sorghum plants that constitutively accumulate stilbenes represents a proof-of-concept investigation at laboratory scale to produce stilbenes in grains as functional food or in biomass as bio-factories for possible industrial implementation in the future. 二苯乙烯類物質是一種罕見並且僅有一小部分種類植物可以產生的天然產物。一些二苯乙烯類化合物，如紫檀芪和白皮衫醇，由於其強大的抗氧化和抗癌特，均性被視為很有前景的保健品。但天然產生的二苯乙烯類物質的含量十分稀少，其作為保健品的生產成本因此十分高昂。 二苯乙烯合成酶（STS）對二苯乙烯類物質生物合成中的關鍵反應步驟起到催化作用，其零星存在於植物界一部分獨立的譜系。它們被認為是在不同分類群的物種形成的過程中，從植物中普遍存在的查爾酮合酶（CHS）獨立進化而來的。高粱是一種穀類作物，因其抗逆性強和含具有重要農業和營養價值的天然產物而聞名，早前，我們已經在高粱中找到了一種病原體誘導型的STS基因（SbSTS1）。最近，通過大量可獲得的禾本科植物基因組資料，我們從與高粱相關的禾本科植物中找到了類似STS的基因，這些植物包括甘蔗，柳枝稷和一些穀類品種，這表明二苯乙烯類物質的生物合成途徑存在於禾本科植物一個小的種系發生群組中。在這項研究裡，我們將表徵不同禾本科類植物STS酶的催化特性，分析各個物種中二苯乙烯類物質的特性。除此之外，我們將對它們進行定點突變，以在分子層面闡明在可產生二苯乙烯類物質的禾本科植物物種形成中，可能導致CHS酶成功獲取STS相關功能活性的因素。 不僅如此，我們最近還發現紫檀芪是高粱中一種潛在有效的抗逆代謝產物，可以對抗高粱主要的病原體炭疽菌。紫檀芪的生物合成需要SbSTS1和O-甲基轉移酶（OMT）的連續催化。目前已經在高粱中鑒定出兩個新的病原體誘導型且具有系統發生上特異性的二苯乙烯OMT基因（SbSOMT1和SbSOMT2），我們將全面探究它們與紫檀芪形成相關的生化功能。同時，為了瞭解二苯乙烯在高粱中的生物學功能，我們將會培育轉基因的過表達植株系和基因編輯突變體，以評估其代謝產物特徵，侵染表型和農藝性狀。 總體而言，這項計畫的研究將深入探究不同的二苯乙烯類物質的生物合成途徑是如何在一些特定的禾本科植物中形成，卻不見於其他穀類植物。在本研究中我們還會通過試驗驗證紫檀芪是否是高粱抗病性的重要成分。此外，上文所述培育可持續積累二苯乙烯的轉基因高粱植株，可作為一種實驗室規模的概念驗證研究，以探求在未來工業生產應用領域用作為功能性食品的穀物，或是生物工廠的生物質生產二苯乙烯的可能性。

17110221.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17110221.value: Background: The emerging infectious disease COVID-19 has caused considerable impact in Hong Kong and across the world. By September 2020, vaccines are still under development and hence non-pharmaceutical interventions remain the most important control measures to control the disease. Therefore, monitoring the transmissibility of the virus to guide control policy is of critical importance. This could be done by estimating the time-varying effective reproductive number (Rt) in real-time. Purpose: We propose to develop a novel approach for the estimation of Rt and effectiveness of control measures by accounting for the substantial pre-symptomatic transmission of COVID-19. Furthermore, due to the pre-symptomatic transmission, large-scale testing for early identification of cases and isolation is one of the most important control strategies. Therefore the test capacity is expanding and needs to be accounted for. Finally, we propose to determine the sample size requirement to allow for real-time estimation. Methods: We will develop a data-augmented Bayesian approach to jointly estimate Rt and the number of unidentified cases that informed by number of tests of COVID-19. In this approach, the Rt for local cases and imported cases will be estimated separately since they are unlikely to have the same infectiousness. Then we will extend the approach by considering the control measures as covariates in the models. This model allows for joint estimation of multiple control measures, to account for their potential synergistic or interfering effects. Finally, we will conduct extensive simulations to determine the number of cases that would allow for real-time estimation of Rt, and the impact of censoring of most recent cases. Potential implications: This study proposes a novel methodology to estimate the Rt in real-time accounting for unidentified cases, which fill an important gap on COVID-19 epidemiology and control. Accurately monitoring the transmissibility of COVID-19 would allow for timely implementation of control measures. This framework can be used to estimate the effectiveness of control measures jointly to account for the potential correlations in effectiveness. Therefore, we can optimize the implementation of control measures to avoid unnecessary negative impact. This framework can also be extended to monitor other disease such as influenza. 背景：新出現的傳染病2019冠狀病毒在香港和世界各地造成了相當大的影響。到 2020 年 9 月，疫苗仍在開發中，因此非藥物干預仍然是控制疾病的最重要的控制措施。因此，監測病毒的傳播能力以指導控制政策至關重要。這可以通過實時估計即時有效繁殖率 (Rt) 來完成。 目的：我們建議建立新方法，通過考慮2019冠狀病毒的大量出現症狀前傳播來估計 Rt 和控制措施的有效性。此外，由於出現症狀前的傳播，大規模檢測以及時識別病例和隔離是最重要的控制策略之一。因此，進行實時估計時需考慮測試能力的擴大。最後，我們建議確定樣本大小要求以進行實時估計。 方法：我們將開發一種新的貝葉斯方法，以聯合估計 Rt 和根據2019冠狀病毒測試數目得出的未識別病例數。在這種方法中，本地病例和輸入病例的 Rt 將分別估計，因為本地病例和輸入病例可能具有不相同的傳染性。然後我們將通過將控制措施視為模型中的變量來擴展該方法。該模型允許對多個控制措施進行聯合估計，以說明它們潛在的協同或擾擾效應。最後，我們將進行廣泛的模擬，以確定允許實時估計 Rt 的案例數量。 潛在影響：本研究提出了一種新方法來估計未識別病例的實時 Rt，填補了 2019冠狀病毒流行病學和控制方面的重要空白。準確監測2019冠狀病毒的傳播性將有助於及時實施控制措施。該框架可用於聯合估計控制措施的有效性，以說明有效性的潛在相關性。因此，我們可以優化控制措施的實施，避免不必要的負面影響。該框架還可以擴展到監測其他疾病，例如流感。

17110221.label: Realisation of objectives
17110221.value: All three objectives were realized. The estimation of time-varying effective reproductive number (Rt) in real-time is central to monitoring the dynamics of an epidemic and guiding policy decisions. To achieve 1, we addressed the key challenges of underreporting and reporting delays by implementing novel methodologies. We first tested using alternative data streams for reliable Rt estimation. Severe health outcomes, including ICU admissions, severe cases, and mortality, were used as alternative data streams for Rt estimation. These indicators were more consistent than confirmed case counts, which were subject to substantial underreporting during the peak of the pandemic. For example, during the fifth wave, Rt derived from severe outcomes was 4.7, compared to 2.6 based on confirmed cases. This discrepancy highlighted the impact of underreporting on traditional Rt calculations. The robustness of these estimates was validated through comparisons with multiple epidemic phases. Moreover, during the early stages of the sixth wave, the use of severe outcomes allowed for accurate Rt estimation even when routine case reporting mechanisms were strained, providing critical insights for policy adjustments. Methodology, we developed bayesian deconvolution for temporal accuracy. A Bayesian framework was applied to deconvolve severe outcomes into infection incidence estimates. This technique corrected for reporting delays and aligned the timing of severe outcomes with likely infection dates, enabling real-time Rt calculations. The gamma-distributed priors smoothed out noisy datasets, ensuring stable Rt estimates under fluctuating data conditions. This approach was particularly effective during the chaotic early period of the Omicron BA.2 wave. For example, deconvolved data provided a clear signal of when Rt crossed critical thresholds, helping policymakers anticipate surges in healthcare demand. We also tested another approach that using the age-structured SEIR transmission model that accounted for the reporting changes, to estimate Rt for two Omicron subvariants, BA.2 and BA.5, during Hong Kong's fifth and sixth waves of COVID-19. These estimates considered differences in variant transmissibility, public health and social measures (PHSMs), and population immunity. We found that 1) during the peak of the fifth wave in March 2022, Rt for Omicron BA.2 initially reached 3.3 but declined to below 1.5 following the implementation of stringent PHSMs. 2) The emergence of BA.5 with higher transmissibility and the relaxation of PHSMs in April 2022 caused Rt to rebound, peaking at 3.5 in late May 2022. The model estimated variant-specific transmission dynamics and estimated revealed that BA.5 exhibited a 17% transmissibility advantage over BA.2, consistent with global observations of increased immune evasion in BA.5. This was evident as Rt during the BA.5 wave peaked at levels similar to the early BA.2 wave, despite higher vaccination and infection-induced immunity in the population. The model also highlighted the role of population immunity. Prior to the fifth wave, Hong Kong's population had only 19% effective immunity against infection. This rose to 60% within two months due to a combination of cumulative infections and increased vaccine uptake. Despite these gains, the effective reproductive number remained influenced by waning immunity and BA.5's immune escape properties. For example, population immunity against BA.5 was 15–17% lower than for BA.2 at the start of the sixth wave. To achieve Aim 2, we assessed the real-time effectiveness of interventions, providing insights into how different measures influenced transmission and severe outcomes. This aim was realized through a combination of retrospective modeling and real-time analysis. In brief, early waves demonstrated the effectiveness of stringent NPIs in reducing Rt below 1. However, the fifth wave, driven by the highly transmissible Omicron BA.2 variant, maintained an Rt above 1 despite similarly stringent measures. This finding underscored the limitations of traditional containment strategies and the need for supplemental interventions like increased vaccination coverage. We evaluated NPIs through Rt analysis. NPIs, such as mask mandates, social distancing, and travel restrictions, were grouped into packages and assessed for their impact on Rt. The hierarchical clustering model quantified the combined effect of these measures during different epidemic phases. For example, during the second wave, Rt decreased from 2.6 to below 1 following the implementation of moderate NPIs, effectively controlling transmission. However, during the fifth wave, Rt remained above 1 despite highly stringent NPIs, reflecting the challenge of controlling a highly transmissible variant like Omicron BA.2. We also evaluated impact of vaccination campaigns. The effectiveness of vaccination campaigns was assessed using dynamic models and real-world data. Key findings include: 1) Increasing vaccine coverage among seniors aged 80+ could have averted nearly 30% of deaths during the fifth wave. 2) Advancing booster rollouts by two weeks was estimated to prevent 4,000 hospitalizations and nearly 500 deaths. 3) These results highlighted the critical role of targeting vaccination efforts toward high-risk populations and the importance of early campaign initiation. We also included behavioural insights from surveys. Cross-sectional surveys revealed high adherence to NPIs, such as mask mandates (over 98%), and significant reductions in population mobility during peak transmission periods. These behavioral changes were integral to the effectiveness of NPIs, particularly in the early epidemic phases. These analyses enabled real-time evaluations of intervention effectiveness, guiding adaptive policy strategies. Achieving Aim 3 is important for accurate real-time estimation of Rt and intervention effectiveness required establishing methodological and practical benchmarks. We addressed Aim 3 through extensive sensitivity analyses and simulations. First, we determined the minimum sample size for reliable estimates. We determined that a minimum of 12 severe health events was required for robust Rt estimation. This threshold provided a practical guideline for low-incidence settings or the early stages of outbreaks, ensuring statistical reliability. We also conducted sensitivity analyses on parameter assumptions. Sensitivity analyses evaluated how variations in reporting completeness, delay distributions, and model parameters impacted Rt estimates. For instance: 1) Combining multiple data streams, such as ICU admissions and mortality, reduced biases by 20–30%, ensuring reliable estimates even under incomplete reporting conditions. 2) Delay corrections applied to severe outcomes had minimal impact on Rt estimates, demonstrating the robustness of the methodology. We also conducted Scenario-Based Simulations. Simulations were conducted to explore how different levels of vaccine coverage, intervention timing, and data completeness affected Rt estimates and policy outcomes. Key findings include: 1) In low-vaccine-coverage scenarios, Rt estimates were highly sensitive to the stringency of NPIs, highlighting the critical role of pharmaceutical measures. 2) In high-vaccine-coverage scenarios, moderate NPIs effectively reduced Rt below 1, supporting more sustainable public health responses. Finally, we tested real-time adjustments for data gaps. Dynamic models accounted for reporting delays and data gaps, ensuring that Rt estimates remained reliable even during high-transmission periods. This adaptability was critical during the chaotic fifth wave, allowing for accurate forecasting and timely policy interventions. These benchmarks provided a robust foundation for real-time epidemic management, ensuring accurate and timely decision-making across diverse conditions.

17110221.label: Major findings and research outcome
17110221.value: The grant successfully achieved all three objectives, advancing real-time epidemic monitoring, intervention evaluation, and public health decision-making. Regarding Aim 1, the estimation of Rt in real-time was central to monitoring epidemic dynamics and guiding interventions. Novel methodologies addressed challenges such as underreporting and reporting delays. Alternative data streams, including ICU admissions and mortality, were used for Rt estimation, providing more reliable insights than confirmed case counts. For instance, during the fifth wave, Rt based on severe outcomes was 4.7, compared to 2.6 from case data, highlighting the extent of underreporting. A Bayesian framework corrected reporting delays and aligned severe outcomes with infection dates, ensuring temporal accuracy and enabling stable Rt calculations even under data fluctuations. An age-structured SEIR model further revealed variant-specific dynamics. During the fifth wave, Rt for Omicron BA.2 peaked at 3.3 but dropped below 1.5 after stringent public health measures (PHSMs). However, the emergence of BA.5, with a 17% transmissibility advantage, and relaxed PHSMs caused Rt to rebound to 3.5. Despite higher population immunity, waning immunity and immune escape properties kept Rt elevated during BA.5's dominance. Regarding Aim 2, the real-time effectiveness of interventions was evaluated through dynamic modeling. Stringent NPIs effectively reduced Rt below 1 during early waves. However, the highly transmissible BA.2 variant maintained Rt above 1 despite similar measures, underscoring the need for complementary strategies. Vaccination campaigns played a critical role, with increased coverage among seniors aged 80+ potentially averting 30% of deaths during the fifth wave. Advancing booster rollouts by two weeks could have prevented 4,000 hospitalizations and 500 deaths. Behavioral surveys indicated high adherence to NPIs, which enhanced their overall effectiveness. Regarding Aim 3, the study established a minimum of 12 severe health events as necessary for robust Rt estimation, providing a benchmark for low-incidence settings. Combining multiple data streams reduced biases by up to 30%, ensuring reliable estimates even with incomplete data. Scenario-based simulations revealed the sensitivity of Rt to vaccination coverage and intervention timing, highlighting the importance of adaptive strategies. Real-time adjustments for data gaps ensured accurate estimates and timely policy decisions during high-transmission periods. Overall, these findings provided critical tools for adaptive public health strategies, improving Hong Kong’s epidemic preparedness and offering a global framework for managing future public health threats.

17110221.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17110221.value: The research conducted under this grant has laid a strong foundation for further advancements in real-time epidemic monitoring and intervention evaluation. Building on the methodologies developed, there is significant potential to enhance their applicability and expand their use to other infectious diseases and geographic regions. Future development could focus on refining the models to incorporate more granular data on immunity dynamics, such as individual-level vaccine effectiveness and the impact of waning immunity. Integrating genomic surveillance data could also improve the model’s ability to detect and predict the spread of new variants with immune-evasive properties. Additionally, the Bayesian framework for Rt estimation could be adapted to account for emerging data streams, such as wastewater surveillance or digital health indicators, to improve accuracy in settings with limited traditional data availability. The proposed action includes validating the models in diverse epidemiological settings, ensuring their adaptability to varying healthcare infrastructures and data quality. Collaborations with public health agencies could facilitate real-time implementation, providing decision-makers with actionable insights to guide vaccination campaigns and public health measures. Furthermore, the development of user-friendly software tools or dashboards based on these models could enhance their accessibility, supporting global efforts to improve pandemic preparedness and response.

17110221.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17110221.value: This research aimed to improve how we monitor and manage infectious disease outbreaks like COVID-19 in real-time. By focusing on Hong Kong’s experience during the COVID-19 pandemic, the study developed new ways to estimate how quickly the virus was spreading and evaluate the effectiveness of measures like vaccination and social distancing. One key finding was that using data on severe cases, hospitalizations, and deaths provided a much clearer picture of the virus’s spread, especially when many mild cases went unreported. For example, during the height of the pandemic, traditional data underestimated how quickly the virus was spreading. Our methods showed a much more accurate and alarming rate of transmission. The research also revealed that vaccinations and public health measures were essential in controlling the pandemic. For instance, vaccinating more elderly people earlier could have prevented a large number of hospitalizations and deaths. We found loosening restrictions too early caused the virus to spread faster, especially with new variants that were more contagious. This work has provided better tools for tracking outbreaks and making timely decisions to save lives. These tools can now help improve public health responses in future epidemics, ensuring better preparedness and faster action.

17110521.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17110521.value: Post-translational modifications (PTMs) discovered on histones provide another layer of gene transcription regulation. Emerging evidence shows that these PTMs, also collectively termed “histone codes”, function individually or in combinations to regulate biological processes. Lysine lactylation (Kla) has recently been discovered as a novel histone PTM and histone Kla can directly stimulate gene transcriptions. However, no “eraser” or “reader” that regulates the Kla dynamics has been reported. In our preliminary study, we found that SIRT3 can remove Kla modifications. In this proposal, we plan to investigate SIRT3 and other candidates for their potential Kla eraser/readout capabilities by using structural and biochemical approaches. Specifically, we propose (1) to develop an alkyne-functionalized chemical probe for further identification of SIRT3 as a Kla eraser and to seek other “reader/eraser” candidates for Kla; (2) to analyze the structural determinants of SIRT3 as a Kla eraser; and (3) to study SIRT3’s delactylation activity in vitro and in cells. As Kla has been shown to regulate gene expression to promote homeostasis, our findings will provide fundamental insights to understand its physiological functions and may contribute in drug design targeting relevant diseases. 組蛋白翻譯後修飾的發現為基因轉錄調控揭開了新的一章。更多的證據顯示這些翻譯後修飾，也被稱作“組蛋白密碼”，能單獨地或與其他蛋白共同去調節生理活動。賴氨酸乳酸化（Kla）是最近新發現的組蛋白翻譯後修飾，能直接刺激基因轉錄。然而，目前還未有調節Kla的“閱讀器”和“去除酶”報導。 我們初步發現，SIRT3具有去Kla的作用。因此我們決定利用結構生物學以及生物化學等方法來研究SIRT3以及其他可能的Kla“閱讀器”和“去除酶”。具體來說，我們將（1）建立一個炔基化學探針來更進一步鑑定SIRT3作為Kla“去除酶”以及尋找其他的Kla“閱讀器”和“去除酶”。（2）解析SIRT3作為Kla“去除酶”的結構生物學基礎。（3）研究SIRT3體外以及細胞內的去Kla活性。基於 Kla已經被證明能夠通過調節基因表達來促進內穩態，我們的研究發現將為更好理解這一生物學功提供基本的見解以及將為相關疾病的新藥研發提供思路。

17111221.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17111221.value: Spexin (SPX) 是一種由 GalR2/3 受體介導功能的神經肽，也是魚類新發現的飽腹因子。在金魚肝臟中，SPX表達可以被胰島素誘導，並涉及進食後的飽腹反應。在我們對金魚肝細胞的 RNA-Seq 研究中，脂聯素 (AdipoQ)作爲一種參與葡萄糖和脂質代謝並對糖尿病和肥胖症有緩解效果的脂肪因子，其轉錄表達可被 SPX上調。此外，在金魚肝臟中也可檢測到 SPX、AdipoQ 及其各自受體的信號，這意味著 SPX 和 AdipoQ 可能在魚類肝臟具有自分泌/旁分泌作用。在我們的前期研究中，我們發現: (i) 腹腔注射 AdipoQ 減少了金魚的覓食行為和食物攝入量，(ii) 餵食金魚會增加葡萄糖、胰島素、SPX 和 AdipoQ 血漿水平，以及肝臟SPX 與AdipoQ mRNA表達，(iii) 在金魚肝細胞中SPX 處理可以上調 SPX 和 AdipoQ mRNA 水平，這反應可被 SPX 血清免疫中和，(iv) 用 AdipoQ 進行類似處理可抑制基礎和 SPX 誘導的 SPX mRNA 信號， 反之AdipoQ 血清免疫中和卻可令SPX 基因表達上升，以及 (v) SPX 引發的 SPX 和 AdipoQ 表達是由 PLC/PKC 和 Ca2+/CaMK-II 信號通路耦聯的 GalR2 介導的，而 AdipoQ 抑制 的SPX 表達則涉及AMPK/PPARα/γ 信號傳導。這些結果意味著:（i）在餵食後由胰島素誘導的 SPX 信號可能在肝臟運作, 並觸發 SPX 自我調節以放大 SPX 輸出，同時亦刺激肝臟中 AdipoQ 表達，這反應可以作為引起飽腹反應的額外信號，與 (ii) 在肝臟中局部釋放的 AdipoQ 可通過抑制金魚肝細胞中基礎和 SPX 誘導的 SPX 表達, 進而構成對 SPX 信號的負反饋調控。為了驗證這些構想，我們將在金魚中進行全動物實驗和肝細胞培養的體外研究，以揭示 (i) 在魚類肝臟中與胰島素耦聯的SPX信號引發的SPX 和 AdipoQ反應及其功能作用與信號轉導，以及 (ii) 由肝臟中產生的 AdipoQ 在終止SPX 信號引發的餵食調控和受體耦聯所引起的中樞作用。我們的研究不僅展示了SPX 調節的新機理，同時亦首次闡明 SPX 和 AdipoQ 在脊椎動物中的自分泌/旁分泌相互作用。

17111521.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17111521.value: The vertebrate neuromuscular junction (NMJ) has been widely used as a model synapse for studying the formation, maintenance, and plasticity of chemical synapses. In the past few decades, extensive research progress has been made to understand how acetylcholine receptors (AChR) are spatially clustered at the postsynaptic membrane in response to nerve-secreted agrin at developing NMJs. As revealed by the ultrastructural studies using electron microscopy, and more recently using super-resolution microscopy, we now know that the postsynaptic junctional folds at mature NMJs exhibit spatially segregated distribution of different postsynaptic proteins throughout the crests and troughs regions. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying the formation of membrane specializations are largely unknown. Our preliminary data convincingly demonstrated that membrane infoldings are frequently observed in spontaneously formed aneural AChR clusters in Xenopus muscle cells cultured on extracellular matrix (ECM)-coated substratum, further suggesting that nerve-independent aneural AChR clusters exhibit the resemblance to synaptic AChR clusters in vivo. In this project, we will primarily use Xenopus tissue cultures in combination with different molecular manipulations and super-resolution imaging to answer a series of cell biology questions concerning the molecular and functional characterizations of membrane infoldings in association with aneural and synaptic AChR clusters. Since abnormalities of the junctional fold architecture are the most common phenotypes associated with several neuromuscular disorders, the results of this project will provide a better understanding of not only the molecular mechanisms underlying membrane infolding formation in NMJ development but also the pathogenic mechanisms underlying the structural changes of junctional folds in patients with muscular dystrophies. 脊椎動物的神經肌肉接合點(NMJ)已被廣泛用作研究化學突觸的形成、維持和可塑性。在過去的幾十年中，科學家已經取得了廣泛的研究進展，以了解乙醯膽鹼受體(AChR)如何在突觸後連會膜上聚集，以回應發育中的神經肌肉接合點中神經元所分泌的集聚蛋白。從電子顯微鏡和近期超分辨率顯微鏡下的超微結構可見，在成熟NMJ的突觸後連接褶皺的波峰和波谷區域中，不同的突觸後蛋白質表現出隔離的空間分佈。然而，膜特化形成的分子機制在很大程度上仍未被了解。我們的初步數據充份地證明，在細胞外基質塗層的基底上培養的非洲爪蟾肌肉細胞裏，自發形成的無神經AChR簇中經常呈現出膜內褶，進一步表明與神經元無關的AChR簇與體內突觸AChR簇的相似性。在這個項目中，我們將主要使用非洲爪蟾組織培養物結合不同的分子操作和超分辨率成像來回答一系列細胞生物學問題，這些問題涉及與無神經AChR 簇和突觸AChR簇相關的膜內褶的分子和功能特徵。由於接合點褶皺的異常是幾種神經肌肉疾病最常見的表型，因此這項目的結果不僅可以讓我們更明白NMJ發育時膜內褶形成的分子機制，還可以更好地了解肌肉萎縮症患者的接合點褶皺結構變化的致病機制。 脊椎動物的神經肌肉接合點已被廣泛用作研究化學突觸的形成、維持和可塑性。在過去的幾十年中，科學家已經取得了廣泛的研究進展，以了解乙醯膽鹼受體如何在突觸後連會膜上聚集，以回應發育中的神經肌肉接合點中神經元所分泌的集聚蛋白。從電子顯微鏡和近期超分辨率顯微鏡下的超微結構可見，在成熟神經肌肉接合點的突觸後連接褶皺的波峰和波谷區域中，不同的突觸後蛋白質表現出隔離的空間分佈。然而，膜特化形成的分子機制在很大程度上仍未被了解。我們的初步數據充份地證明，在細胞外基質塗層的基底上培養的非洲爪蟾肌肉細胞裏，自發形成的無神經乙醯膽鹼受體簇中經常呈現出膜內褶，進一步表明與神經元無關的乙醯膽鹼受體簇與體內突觸乙醯膽鹼受體簇的相似性。在這個項目中，我們將主要使用非洲爪蟾組織培養物結合不同的分子操作和超分辨率成像來回答一系列細胞生物學問題，這些問題涉及與無神經乙醯膽鹼受體簇和突觸乙醯膽鹼受體簇相關的膜內褶的分子和功能特徵。由於接合點褶皺的異常是幾種神經肌肉疾病最常見的表型，因此這項目的結果不僅可以讓我們更明白神經肌肉接合點發育時膜內褶形成的分子機制，還可以更好地了解肌肉萎縮症患者的接合點褶皺結構變化的致病機制。

17111721.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17111721.value: 疲勞是晚期肺癌患者最常見的症狀。運動是一種有潛在價值的治療方案。基於 零時間運動 (ZTEx)社區計劃的成功經驗及晚期肺癌患者需求評估結果, 及參照癌患者的意見及其先導測試的結果，我們設計了簡易智運動及聊天短訊支援計劃（智運動支援計劃, SES）， 即零時間運動的改良版本，加入飲食與症狀管理的建議，和提供心理支援以改善疲勞。我們的先導結果顯示良好的可用性及認受性。 SES旨在改善晚期肺癌患者疲勞（主要研究結果）、疾病的接納程度、運動自我效能感、焦慮及抑鬱的症狀、幸福感、疼痛及呼吸困難症狀、睡眠質素、身體活動水平、運動量、手握力、身體柔軟度和生活質素。 SES使用 (i) 接納為本的策略以接納與承諾療法增加個人的心理彈性以接納疾病；(ii) 小步的介入方法將簡單易行的智運動融入日常生活；(iii) 以智能手機技術 (WhatsApp/WeChat) 提供資訊和心理支援訊息，增強知識和動機，並提供抗惰性提示，以及 (iv) 個人化的聊天短訊支援，從而提升做運動和選擇健康飲食的自我效能及行動。 智運動支援計劃包括四個部分：甲部：為時 45 分鐘的 SMART個人運動練習環節；乙部：以理論為本的即時訊息（WhatsApp/微信）及以按時遞減的電話健康指導； 丙部：持續提供個人化聊天短訊、電話支援及熱線服務，丁部：以電子平台建立個人目標及自我監察。是項集群隨機對照研究將招募至少 120 名參與者，隨機分配到智運動支援 (SES組)或一般衛生信息組（GHI，控制組別），並於第 6 週和第 24週進行評估。兩個組別均收到相同日程和聯繫時間。我們會使用主觀及客觀的方式透過意向治療分析和敏感度分析檢視SES的成效，來評估計劃的認受性，可行性、遵從性、可信度和醫療服務的使用，並且會分析促進運動的因素和障礙， SES對身體活動、疲勞和相關結果帶來的影響。 是次為全球首個可能是最簡易及低成本並以理論及病人為本的智運動支援計劃改善晚期肺癌患者疲勞及其相關結果的隨機對照研究。研究的過程和成效評估及機理分析的結果將為臨床實踐方面帶來新的認識，有助建立簡單的行為改變模式，並進一步在其他病患者推行簡單運動及短訊介入研究。

17111721.label: Major findings and research outcome
17111721.value: A. Participants A total of 120 patients with advanced lung cancer (ALC) (52% male, mean age xx years) were recruited and were randomly allocated to the Smart Exercise Support (SES) group (n = 61) or the General Health Information (GHI) control group (n = 59). Both groups were similar in baseline characteristics. 115 and 105 ALC patients completed the 6-week and the 24-week follow-up. All 120 participants were included in the intention-to-treat analysis. B. Outcomes -Fatigue and Exercise Self-Efficacy: At 24 weeks, the SES group showed significantly greater reductions in fatigue [between-group difference: -3.2 (-6.12, -0.28), p < 0.05] and improvements in exercise self-efficacy [2.3 (0.99, 3.6), p < 0.001] compared to the control group. -Physical Activity Intensity: The SES group showed significantly greater increase in physical activity intensity (measured by MET scores) at both 6 weeks [650.63 (127.78, 1173.47), p < 0.05] and 24 weeks [872.39 (349.55, 1395.24), p < 0.001], compared to the control group. nt. -Physical Fitness: The SES group showed significant improvements in hand grip strength, flexibility, and exercise capacity at 6 and 24 weeks compared to the control group. Balance improved at 24 weeks in the SES group but did not differ significantly between groups. -Mood, sleep quality and acceptance of illness: The SES program significantly reduced depression at 6 and 24 weeks and improved happiness at 24 weeks. Acceptance of illness also improved, but these outcomes were not significantly different from the control group. No significant differences were found in sleep quality or anxiety symptoms. -Quality of Life: The SES group demonstrated greater increases in EORTC QLQ_C30 physical function subscale score at 6 and 24 weeks and fatigue subscale score at 24 weeks. C. Program acceptability and intervention credibility Participants found the SES program highly acceptable, noting its content was tailored to their age, health literacy, and expectations. The exercises were easy to follow, flexible, and allowed for autonomy in deciding what activities to perform. The online platform effectively motivated participants through goal setting and self-monitoring, though a slight decline in activity during the late phase was attributed to disease progression. D. Facilitators and Barriers of the SES program and Exercise adherence Facilitators included tailored content, flexibility, autonomy, simplicity, and positive health outcomes, which reinforced adherence. However, barriers such as disease progression and health fluctuations. E. Summary of findings The SES program significantly reduced fatigue increased physical activity, and improved physical fitness and quality of life in ALC patients. While mood and illness acceptance improved, these outcomes did not differ significantly from the control group. The program offers a scalable, low-cost smartphone-based model for reducing fatigue and improving physical activity, making it a novel intervention for ALC patients.

17111721.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17111721.value: The findings of this study highlight the potential for further development of digital interventions to support self-management in patients with advanced lung cancer (ALC) and other chronic or life-limiting diseases. The success of the SES program demonstrates that tailored, flexible, and low-cost digital tools can effectively empower patients to manage their physical activity, fatigue, and quality of life. This approach could be expanded to other conditions such as chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), where self-management of symptoms is critical for improving daily functioning and reducing healthcare utilization. Additionally, digital self-management tools could be integrated into perioperative care for lung cancer patients, helping them maintain or enhance physical fitness and mental resilience before and after surgery. Prehabilitation programs, delivered through smartphone-based platforms, could improve surgical outcomes and recovery while reducing complications. Future research should explore the scalability of digital self-management interventions across diverse populations and healthcare settings. Emphasis should be placed on refining content to ensure accessibility for patients with varying levels of health and technological literacy, as well as integrating advanced features like personalized feedback, artificial intelligence, and teleconsultation with healthcare providers. Moreover, cross-condition studies could assess the applicability of such programs for other cancers or chronic diseases, addressing shared challenges like fatigue, physical inactivity, and mental health. Overall, advancing digital self-management solutions offers a promising pathway for improving patient care and empowering individuals to take an active role in managing their health.

17111721.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17111721.value: This research focused on helping patients with advanced lung cancer (ALC) manage fatigue and improve physical activity using a smartphone-based program called Smart Exercise Support (SES). A total of 120 participants were randomly assigned to either the SES group, which provided tailored exercise guidance, or a control group, which received general health information. The study found that the SES program significantly reduced fatigue, increased physical activity, and improved physical fitness over 24 weeks compared to the control group. Participants in the SES group also showed better mental health, including reduced depression and improved happiness, though these differences were not significant compared to the control group. The program was highly valued by participants, who appreciated its flexibility, easy-to-follow exercises, and the ability to manage their own activities. The smartphone platform motivated users through goal setting and progress tracking. This research is significant as it demonstrates that a simple, low-cost digital program can empower patients with ALC to improve their quality of life. The SES program is scalable and could be used for other chronic conditions like COPD or in pre- and post-surgical care for lung cancer patients. It represents a promising step forward in digital self-management for cancer care.

17112021.label: Project Objectives
17112021.value: To investigate the clinical significance and prognostication of DGKH overexpression in HCC. We will perform a retrospective study to examine DGKH expression, alone or in combination with various liver cancer stem cell markers or pluripotency stemness genes, in a large cohort of tumor and adjacent non-tumor clinical tissue samples of different etiology driven HCC, including hepatitis B virus and non-alcoholic fatty liver disease. We will also examine the clinical significance of DGKH in predicting sorafenib treatment response. To investigate the metabolic and biological function of DGKH in the maintenance of HCC stemness. We will characterize the functional role of DGKH in vitro and in vivo using both HCC cell lines as well as hepatocyte and HCC patient-derived organoids. Additionally, we will explore the therapeutic potentials of targeting DGKH as a single and/or combined sorafenib treatment option for HCC, using HCC patient-derived organoids and a genetically engineered immunocompetent mouse model of HCC. To investigate if DGKH overexpression can promote cancer stemness in HCC through activation of phosphatidic acid-induced mTOR/p70S6K pathway. Rescue experiments involving phosphatidic acid and mTOR pathway inhibitors will be carried out on HCC cells with or without DGKH manipulated to examine the role of phosphatidic acid-induced mTOR/p70S6K pathway in DGKH-mediated cancer and stemness properties.

17112021.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17112021.value: 肝細胞癌 (HCC) 是世界上第五大最常見的癌症，也是東南亞和香港癌症死亡的第二大原因。儘管隨著檢測和治療的進步增加了這種疾病早期治癒的可能性，但由於遲發性、頻繁的腫瘤復發和對標準治療的抵抗，HCC的總體預後仍然不令人滿意。因此深入了解HCC背後的分子/細胞靶點顯得尤為重要，因為這可以為治療肝癌提供新的機會。目前研究普遍認為腫瘤幹細胞與腫瘤耐藥性、復發及HCC不良預後密切相關。事實上，現在有大量證據表明 HCC的發展受到腫瘤內稱為腫瘤幹細胞 (CSC) 的細胞推動，其作用非常類似於疾病的根源。肝臟是一個獨特的器官，因為它具有許多代謝功能，包括糖異生、糖原合成、脂質代謝及儲存以及血糖穩態。 在HCC發展過程中，這些代謝機制被廣泛重編程以支持HCC大量的營養需求。現在有新的證據表明脂質代謝改變與HCC的發展息息相關。最近的研究顯示，與HCC整體腫瘤相比，HCC內的腫瘤幹細胞具有不同的脂質代謝特徵(Qin et al. PNAS 2018)。然而，目前鮮有研究探討HCC中腫瘤乾性和脂質代謝之間的關係。通過對包含HCC臨床信息(The Cancer Genome Atlas, TCGA)以及乾性相關基因集(Yamashita and Cancer Stem Cell database)的各個公開數據庫的綜合分析，我們已經初步鑑定出可能與肝癌乾性相關的新代謝靶點。 我们发现了 174 个与 HCC 代谢、干性和晚期肿瘤分期相关的基因，其中的许多基因在甘油磷脂代谢通路中显著富集。在该通路中，DGKH被确定为热门候选基因。 DGKH 能够将甘油二酯转化为磷脂酸，因此参与磷脂酸的生成以及甘油三酯和甘油磷脂的全合成过程，可为正在恶性增殖的肿瘤细胞提供构建细胞质和细胞器膜的原材料。 我们的初步数据现表明，尽管DGKH 在正常肝脏中的表达水平非常低，但相比于TCGA HCC 数据集中的正常/非肿瘤肝脏组织，其在HCC患者癌组织中持续且显著上调，且DKGH高表达与总生存预后不良相关。与此一致的是，对配对的非肿瘤肝脏及HCC 癌旁组织的蛋白质组学分析发现，DKGH 在HCC组织中高表达；并且在蛋白质水平上，DKGH高表达也与无病生存不良预后以及未分化/低分化肿瘤相关。功能研究方面，在HCC 细胞中过表达DGKH增强了 HCC 细胞的肿瘤干细胞样特性，包括自我更新、侵袭迁移、和索拉非尼耐药；而在HCC 细胞中敲除 DGKH，则赋予与此相反的功能表型。 在進一步的分子機制中研究，隨著過表達DKGH 能夠引起p-mTOR (Ser2448) 、p-p70S6K (Thr389) 和 p-S6 (Ser235/236 和 Ser240/244) 的表達失調，我們發現DKGH可以激活 mTOR/p70S6K/S6 信號通路。隨後我們補救性地添加外源性磷脂酸，能夠提高由DKGH抑制導致mTOR信號減弱的HCC細胞的自我更新、侵襲轉移能力。基於上述數據，我們提出假說：DGKH 過表達可以通過激活磷脂酸誘導的 mTOR/p70S6K/S6 通路來促進 肝細胞癌乾性。 為了驗證這一假說，我們擬進行如下方面研究：(1) 探討DKGH 表達與HCC臨床指標及預後的關係；(2) 明確DKGH 在維持 HCC 乾性中的代謝和生物學功能；並為開展AAV8介導的DGKH靶向治療或聯合索拉非尼治療奠定理論基礎；(3) 系統闡明磷脂酸激活mTOR/p70S6K/S6 通路的分子機制 （其中DKGH過表達可以促進肝細胞癌乾性）。我們的上述研究是具有原創性的工作，將拓寬我們對肝細胞癌發病機制的了解，並為肝細胞癌的治療提供新策略與新思考。

Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17112021.value: This study explores how certain metabolic changes in liver cancer (HCC) help tumors grow, resist treatment, and recur. Researchers analyzed data from HCC patients, finding that a gene called DGKH plays a key role in these processes. DGKH was found to be more active in more aggressive and less treatable tumors. Experiments showed that increasing DGKH in cancer cells made them more stem-like, resistant to therapy, and able to spread. The team also discovered that a protein called EP300 boosts DGKH's activity, which then promotes a pathway called mTOR that supports tumor growth. In mouse models, reducing DGKH levels alongside standard treatment significantly decreased tumor size and spread. Overall, the findings suggest that DGKH is a critical regulator of liver cancer's ability to resist treatment and maintain its aggressive features. Targeting DGKH could be a promising strategy to improve outcomes for patients with HCC.

17112521.value: 肝细胞癌（HCC）是一种高度侵袭性的恶性肿瘤，临床致死率高。酪氨酸激酶抑制剂和免疫检查点抑制剂是唯一被FDA批准的用于晚期HCC治疗的药物。然而，酪氨酸激酶抑制剂治疗的生存获益有限，免疫检查点抑制剂治疗的客观反应率低。限制疗效的主要因素之一是由于HCC具有高度适应性，使肿瘤细胞能够克服各种类型的代谢压力，如高度氧化应激。由于HCC细胞代谢调控紊乱，其本身就面临高度的氧化应激压力。此外，标准治疗方案也会诱导氧化应激发生。氧化应激可以通过启动脂质过氧化反应，诱导铁依赖的程序调控性细胞死亡，该过程称为铁死亡。铁死亡主要通过氧化应激靶向细胞膜的多不饱和脂肪酸，产生脂质过氧化物，破坏细胞膜并导致细胞死亡。最近，两项重要的研究分别发现CoQ10/FSP1轴是一种新的保护细胞免于铁死亡的方式。这些研究表明，FSP1依赖NADPH将CoQ10转化成还原型, 还原型CoQ10清除自由基，阻止脂质过氧化，从而保护细胞。但是，CoQ10/FSP1轴在肿瘤尤其是HCC中的病理意义与临床意义尚待进一步探究。此外，由于死亡细胞具有招募抗原提呈细胞（如巨噬细胞和树突状细胞）到组织局部的功能，因此发生铁死亡的HCC细胞的免疫调节作用也亟待探究。有趣的是，我们发现HCC细胞主要依赖CoQ10/FSP1轴来克服铁死亡。我们的初步数据显示，FSP1在HCC患者组织中表达显著上调，并受到氧化应激反应通路KEAP1/NRF2的调控。值得注意的是，我们发现通过FSP1抑制剂诱导发生铁死亡的细胞可以被巨噬细胞吞噬。FSP1抑制剂不仅能有效地降低肿瘤负荷，还可以显著促进巨噬细胞、树突状细胞、T细胞等免疫细胞浸润。进一步实验表明，FSP1抑制剂单药可抑制HCC肿瘤的生长，同时其与PD1抑制剂具有协同作用。综合我们的前期研究，我们将进一步探究FSP1在HCC发展中的临床相关性、调控机制和病理作用，以及FSP1抑制剂单药和联合免疫治疗在HCC中的治疗效果。

17112521.label: Realisation of objectives
17112521.value: Objective 1: To study the clinical implication of FSP1 in human HCC Ferroptosis is a special mode of cell death triggered by iron dependent chain reaction of lipid peroxidation. Liver cancer cells survive and develop drug resistance through enhanced anti-ferroptosis systems. There are two major antioxidants, including glutathione and CoQ10, which have high propensity to neutralize reactive oxygen species (ROS). These two antioxidants are kept in chemically reduced forms so that they can perform their redox functions rapidly by GPX4 and FSP1 respectively. While GPX4 has been actively studied, the role of FSP1 in cancer, especially liver cancer, has remained elusive. We showed that FSP1 was upregulated in human HCC patients in two cohorts. We compared FSP1 mRNA expression levels in human HCC tissues to their corresponding non-tumor (NT) tissues in TCGA database. We also evaluated the FSP1 expression levels in HCC and NT tissues from patients of our QMH cohort by qPCR with Taqman probes. Moreover, we found that FSP1 overexpression was correlated to poor prognosis and clinical outcomes in HCC patients. Kaplan-Meier analysis revealed that FSP1 overexpression was associated with poorer overall and disease-free survival. We also evaluated the correlation of FSP1 expression with multiple clinicopathological features including Edmondson grading, direct liver invasion, tumor encapsulation, tumor microsatellite formation, tumor size, tumor (pTNM) stage, and venous invasion. We found that FSP1 overexpression was significantly correlated with larger tumor size. To rule out the contribution of anti-ferroptosis effect by GPX4 system in HCC, we also evaluated GPX4 expression in HCC patients and there was no alternation. Interestingly, transferrin, which is a pro-ferroptotic gene that mediates iron uptake in the cancer cell, was significantly downregulated. Altogether, these indicated that pro-ferroptotic pathway was dampened in HCC while HCC relied on FSP1 to protect themselves from ferroptosis. Objective 2: To delineate the regulatory mechanism driving FSP1 over-expression in human HCC As anti-ferroptosis pathway involves counteracting lipid ROS intracellularly, we wondered if NRF2, the master transcription factor mediating antioxidant responses, also regulated FSP1. We first found that there were positive correlations between FSP1 expression with multiple NRF2-regulating gene expressions in HCC patients, including TKT, ME1 and MTHFD1L, suggesting that potentially FSP1 was also regulated by NRF2. Chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP) assay revealed the binding of NRF2 to the antioxidant response element (ARE) we identified at FSP1 promoter region. We further validated the functionality of this binding site by dual luciferase reporter assay. We transfected HCC cell lines with wildtype or mutant ARE containing luciferase plasmids and then exposed the cells to oxidant treatment. We showed that oxidant treatment induced luciferase activity only in HCC cells with wildtype but not mutant ARE. Furthermore, this induction could be reversed by knocking down NRF2 or MAF, which dimerizes with NRF2 to drive antioxidant genes. We also demonstrated that activation of NRF2 induced FSP1 while NRF2 inhibition suppressed FSP1 on both mRNA and protein levels by genetic and chemical manipulation. We established stable NRF2 and KEAP1 (negative regulator of NRF2) knockdown clones in HCC cell lines and showed that NRF2 deficiency led to FSP1 suppression while KEAP1 knockdown upregulated FSP1. The usage of NRF2 chemical inducers (SFN and CDDO-Im) also consistently induced FSP1 in HCC cells at a dose dependent manner. All these converged to indicate that FSP1 was regulated by NRF2. Objective 3: To study the functional roles of FSP1 in human HCC FSP1 is an oxidoreductase, generating reduced CoQ10H2 from oxidized CoQ10 to protect cells from ferroptosis. We showed that FSP1 inhibition by both genetic manipulation or the use of FSP1 inhibitor (iFSP1) reduced intracellular CoQ10H2/CoQ10 ratio, and thus elevating intracellular lipid peroxidation levels, as revealed by BODIPY C11, 4-HNE and MDA staining. This induced ferroptotic cancer cell death, as measured by SYTOX Green staining or LDH release assay. FSP1 deficiency also suppressed proliferation, which can be abrogated using only ferroptosis inhibitor but not the inhibitors for other modes of cell death. We also demonstrated that in an orthotopic implantation tumor model in immunodeficient mice that FSP1 deficiency led to reduced tumor burden, as reflected by tumor volume and bioluminescent signals, and less lung metastasis. Interestingly, we demonstrated that FSP1 inhibition in cancer cells exhibited immunomodulatory effect. We performed a phagocytosis assay by co-culturing bone marrow-derived macrophages with CTV-labeled cancer cells with or without pre-treatment of iFSP1 to induce ferroptosis. We observed that ferroptotic cancer cells (induced by iFSP1 treatment) were more frequently phagocytosed by macrophages, suggesting the potential role of FSP1 in influencing the tumor immune microenvironment. To study the effect of iFSP1 on the tumor microenvironment (TME), we established a hydrodynamic tail vein injection (HDTVi)-induced HCC model with high fat diet to study the effects of iFSP1 in vivo. In this tumor model, NRF2 was activated by knocking out Keap1 using CRISPR-cas9 system. Together with the feeding of high fat diet, this elevated the lipid peroxidation levels in tumors, making it more susceptible to ferroptosis induction. We treated the tumor bearing mice with iFSP1 and studied the immune composition of tumors. We found that iFSP1 promoted immune cell infiltration into tumor, including macrophages, dendritic cells (DCs), and T cells. We further performed single cell RNA sequencing (scRNAseq) to delineate the immune landscape changes upon iFSP1 treatment on tumor-infiltrating immune cells. Consistently, we observed an increase of macrophages, DCs and T cells in tumors upon iFSP1 treatment. Sub-clustering analysis of myeloid cells showed that there was enrichment of antigen-presenting DCs and phagocytic macrophages. Furthermore, these phagocytic macrophages were also characterized by high expressions of MHC-II antigen presenting genes. We also studied T cell subpopulations. There were also induction of proliferating CD8+ T cells and exhausted CD8+ T cells. These T cells could be recruited by DCs and macrophages via CXCL9, which is a T cell chemoattractant induced by iFSP1. Objective 4: To evaluate the therapeutic values of FSP1 inhibitor (iFSP1) in HCC treatment We showed that iFSP1 as a single treatment significantly suppressed tumor growth in the aforementioned tumor model. Moreover, we found that immune cells expressed high levels of GPX4, the key player in the alternative anti-ferroptosis pathway, but low levels of FSP1, indicating that targeting FSP1 could specifically target cancer cells while minimize the effects on inducing immune cell death. This suggests that iFSP1 could be a better therapeutic option comparing to other ferroptosis inducers. We would like to further improve the treatment efficacy by combination treatment, so we explored our scRNAseq data and found that CD40 and PD-1 could be potential targets for combination treatment with iFSP1. We observed an upregulation of CD40, a co-stimulatory marker, on both DCs and macrophages and upregulation of PD-1 on exhausted CD8+ T cells upon iFSP1 treatment, pointing to potential combination treatment options. Therefore, we treated HCC tumor-bearing mice with iFSP1 in combination with CD40 agonist, anti-PD-1 or anti-PD-L1. CD40 agonist activates DCs and macrophages by enhancing antigen presentation ability of DCs and promoting macrophages to become more pro-inflammatory. Anti-PD-1 and anti-PD-L1 disrupted the interactions of PD-1 on T cells and PD-L1 on cancer cells so to unleash functions of T cells. While single treatment slightly improved the survival of tumor-bearing mice, all three combinations led to better survival outcomes in tumor-bearing mice as compared to single treatment groups.

17112521.label: Major findings and research outcome
17112521.value: We revealed that HCC cells depend on FSP1 to protect themselves from ferroptosis. We showed that FSP1 was overexpressed in human HCC and identified NRF2 as the regulator of FSP1. FSP1 inhibition led to reduction of CoQ10 and induction of lipid peroxidation in cancer cells, causing ferroptotic cell death. We further demonstrated that ferroptotic cancer cells were more susceptible to phagocytosis by macrophages. . Using single cell RNA sequencing, we delineated the tumor immune microenvironment upon FSP1 inhibitor treatment. We showed that there were enrichments of antigen-presenting dendritic cells, phagocytic macrophages and exhausted CD8+ T cells. We also explored the potential of combination treatment of FSP1 inhibitor and immunotherapies (CD40 agonist, anti-PD-1 and anti-PD-L1) and showed that they worked in synergy to suppress HCC progression. Together, we showed that FSP1 inhibition not only induced cancer ferroptotic cell death directly, but it also modulated the immune tumor microenvironment to suppress tumor growth. The findings in this project were published in a manuscript titled as “Ferroptosis Suppressor Protein 1 Inhibition Promotes Tumor Ferroptosis and Anti-tumor Immune Responses in Liver Cancer” in the journal of Cellular and Molecular Gastroenterology and Hepatology in 2023.

17112521.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17112521.value: The effects of different ferroptosis inducers on immune cells could be further explored. For example, multiple studies indicate that CD8+ T cells replied on GPX4 to protect themselves from ferroptosis, this suggested that GPX4 inhibitor may cause CD8+ T cell death. On the other hand, we observed an induction of CD8+ T cells upon FSP1 inhibitor treatment, this suggested that different ferroptosis inducers may exert different effects on immune cells. While different ferroptosis inducers were hotly pursued as potential anti-cancer drugs, whether they will induce ferroptotic cell death in immune cells worths further investigation because this may affect the treatment outcomes. Through multiple in in vitro culturing of immune cells and scRNAseq analysis on tumor-infiltrating immune cells, we can evaluate the influences of different ferroptosis inducers. We can also explore the potential of combining ferroptosis inducers targeting different anti-ferroptosis pathways.

17112521.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17112521.value: HCC is a lethal disease with limited treatment options. Ferroptosis is a form of immunogenic and regulated cell death and cancer cells have multiple mechanisms to protect themselves from ferroptosis. FSP1 is one of the key anti-ferroptosis players and we found that it was highly upregulated in HCC patients. We identified NRF2 as the regulator of FSP1. We demonstrated that FSP1 inhibition induced ferroptotic cell death and suppressed tumor growth. More importantly, we revealed the potential immunomodulatory role of FSP1 inhibition and explored the potential therapeutic values of combining FSP1 inhibitor and immunotherapies.

17112621.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17112621.value: 肝細胞癌（HCC）是原發性肝癌的主要類型。HCC 是全球最常見的癌症之一，在包括香港在內的華南地區發病率很高。HCC 的危險因素相對明確。乙型肝炎和 丙型肝炎是HCC的主要危險因素。在香港，超過 80% 的 HCC 患者與慢性乙肝有關。HCC 的發展是一個多步驟的過程，由遺傳和表觀遺傳失調的積累所驅動。最近的研究通過高通量測序揭示了 HCC 的突變情況。我們和其他科研人員之前也報導過表觀遺傳修飾的失調，例如 DNA 甲基化、RNA 修飾、組蛋白修飾和染色質重塑，經常與肝癌發生有關。然而，我們對 HCC 表觀遺傳失調的理解仍然非常有限。 核小體是真核染色質的基本單元，由 146bp DNA和核心組蛋白八聚體所組成。核小體動態重組決定染色質結構和基因表達。在細胞質中合成的組蛋白被組蛋白伴侶護送到染色質位點。染色質組裝因子 1 (CAF-1) 是一種異三聚體組蛋白伴侶複合物，負責真核細胞中的複制依賴性染色質組裝、異染色質形成和 DNA 損傷修復。我們的初步數據顯示，CAF-1 在人類 HCC 中經常上調，並與更具侵襲性的臨床病理特徵相關。在體外和體內實驗中，CAF-1 的敲除抑制了 HCC 的生長和轉移。從機制上講，CAF-1 的敲除誘導 H3.1 到 H3.3 組蛋白變體轉換。增加的 H3.3 摻入恢復了表觀遺傳沉默的腫瘤抑制基因的表達，誘導了 DNA 損傷，並導致 HCC 細胞凋亡。有趣的是，我們的初步數據還表明，CAF-1 的敲除導致內源性逆轉錄病毒的重新激活並促進微核形成，進而觸發 dsRNA 和胞質 DNA 傳感途徑並導致幹擾素介導的抗癌免疫反應的激活。在這項研究中，我們旨在徹底研究 CAF-1 在 HCC 中的病理作用。我們還將描述 CAF-1 在肝癌發生過程中調節染色質結構和基因表達的功能並揭示潛在的分子機制。我們還將探索靶向 CAF-1 作為 HCC 治療新策略的治療潛力。

17112621.label: Realisation of objectives
17112621.value: The first objective was to determine the expression and clinicopathological significance of the CAF-1 complex in human hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). This was thoroughly addressed through analyses of RNA sequencing data from both the researchers’ own HCC patient cohort and the TCGA database, which consistently demonstrated significant upregulation of the CAF-1 core subunits CHAF1A and CHAF1B in tumor tissues compared to non-tumor controls. Immunohistochemical staining further validated the elevated protein levels of these subunits in human HCC specimens. Notably, CHAF1B expression was already increased in cirrhotic liver and dysplastic nodules, indicating that CAF-1 upregulation may contribute to the early stages of liver carcinogenesis as well as tumor progression. Moreover, this upregulation was observed not only in HCC but also across various other solid tumors, suggesting a widespread oncogenic role. Clinically, high CAF-1 expression correlated with aggressive tumor features such as high histological grade and hypoxia scores, and was associated with poor patient prognosis including reduced overall and disease-free survival rates. Molecularly, CAF-1 expression positively correlated with the proliferation marker Ki67 and the pluripotency gene POU5F1, but not with other pluripotency genes NANOG and SOX2. Additionally, elevated CAF-1 levels were linked to TP53 mutations and inversely associated with CTNNB1 mutations, highlighting its relevance to specific molecular subtypes of HCC. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that CAF-1 is frequently overexpressed in HCC and serves as a significant biomarker with prognostic and clinicopathological implications. The second objective aimed to characterize the oncogenic roles of CAF-1 in human HCC. This was achieved through genetic knockout studies using CRISPR-Cas9 to delete the CHAF1B gene in HCC cell lines MHCC97L and Huh-7, which led to the concomitant degradation of both CHAF1B and CHAF1A subunits, effectively abolishing the CAF-1 complex. Functional assays revealed that loss of CAF-1 markedly inhibited HCC cell proliferation, colony formation, and migration, while inducing apoptosis. Cell cycle analyses showed that CAF-1 knockout cells accumulated in the S and G2 phases, indicating cell cycle arrest. In vivo experiments using orthotopic xenograft models further demonstrated that CAF-1 knockout suppressed tumor formation in the liver and reduced metastatic spread to the lungs. Importantly, in an immunocompetent mouse model of spontaneous HCC induced by Tp53 knockout and c-myc overexpression, simultaneous deletion of CAF-1 significantly decreased tumor incidence and burden, and prolonged survival. These results clearly establish that CAF-1 is essential for HCC tumor initiation, progression, and metastasis, underscoring its oncogenic role. The third objective focused on delineating the implications of CAF-1-mediated histone H3.1 incorporation on chromatin accessibility and gene expression in HCC. CAF-1 is known to mediate replication-dependent incorporation of histone variant H3.1 into chromatin. The study found that CAF-1 knockout caused a global reduction in H3.1 deposition in chromatin without affecting total cellular H3.1 protein levels, indicating impaired chromatin assembly rather than histone production. Interestingly, this loss was accompanied by compensatory enrichment of the histone variant H3.3, which is typically associated with euchromatin and open chromatin states, particularly at endogenous retrovirus (ERV) loci such as HERV9. ATAC-Seq analyses showed increased chromatin accessibility in CAF-1-deficient cells, predominantly at intronic, intergenic, and repetitive elements including ERVs, LINEs, and SINEs, while enhancer and promoter regions remained largely unchanged. RNA sequencing and RepEnrich2 analysis revealed significant upregulation of ERV transcripts, many exhibiting bidirectional transcription capable of forming double-stranded RNA (dsRNA). These findings demonstrate that CAF-1-mediated H3.1 incorporation plays a critical role in maintaining heterochromatin and silencing repetitive elements, and that its loss results in epigenetic reprogramming marked by heterochromatin opening, ERV de-repression, and accumulation of dsRNA. The fourth objective explored the potential of targeting CAF-1 to awaken anti-cancer immune responses. The accumulation of cytosolic dsRNA derived from ERVs and cytosolic DNA from micronuclei in CAF-1 knockout cells activated multiple innate immune sensing pathways. Specifically, the study observed activation of the STING pathway, which senses cytosolic DNA, and the MAVS and TRIF pathways, which detect cytosolic dsRNA. Downstream signaling events included increased expression and phosphorylation of STING, cGAS, IRF3/7, and nuclear translocation of NF-κB, leading to robust induction of interferon-stimulated genes, inflammatory cytokines, and senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) factors. Functional validation using siRNA knockdown of STING, MAVS, and TRIF attenuated immune gene upregulation, confirming the specificity of these pathways in mediating the immune response to CAF-1 loss. In vivo, knockdown of Chaf1b in a mouse HCC cell line reduced tumor growth and significantly increased infiltration of total T cells, especially cytotoxic CD8+ T cells expressing Perforin and Granzyme B, indicating enhanced anti-tumor immunity. Moreover, combining CAF-1 suppression with anti-PD1 immune checkpoint blockade synergistically inhibited tumor growth and further increased CD8+ T cell infiltration, demonstrating that CAF-1 inhibition sensitizes tumors to immunotherapy. These results establish that targeting CAF-1 induces a viral mimicry state and genome instability that activates intrinsic immune pathways, thereby promoting anti-cancer immune responses and improving the efficacy of immune checkpoint inhibitors. In conclusion, the study successfully achieved all four objectives, providing compelling evidence that the CAF-1 complex is a critical oncogenic factor frequently upregulated in human HCC with significant clinicopathological relevance. Functionally, CAF-1 supports tumor growth and metastasis by facilitating cell cycle progression and maintaining genome stability. Mechanistically, CAF-1 mediates replication-dependent histone H3.1 incorporation, which preserves heterochromatin integrity and silences endogenous retroviral elements, preventing accumulation of immunostimulatory nucleic acids. Loss of CAF-1 disrupts these processes, leading to replication stress, DNA damage, chromatin opening, ERV de-repression, and dsRNA formation, which collectively activate cytosolic nucleic acid sensing pathways and innate immune responses. Importantly, CAF-1 inhibition enhances T cell-mediated anti-tumor immunity and synergizes with immune checkpoint blockade, highlighting its potential as a therapeutic target to improve immunotherapy outcomes in HCC. This study thus lays a solid foundation for future translational research aimed at exploiting CAF-1 as a novel epigenetic immunomodulatory target in liver cancer.

17112621.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17112621.value: This research provides a proof of concept for combining epigenetic modulation with immunotherapy, demonstrating that targeting chromatin regulators like CAF-1 can activate anti-tumor immune responses. There is a critical need to develop specific inhibitors of CAF-1 to translate these findings into effective therapies, as no direct pharmacological agents currently exist to target this complex.

17112621.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17112621.value: This research discovered that the histone chaperone CAF-1 plays a crucial role in liver cancer growth by helping tumors avoid immune detection. CAF-1 normally helps package DNA tightly, keeping certain genomic regions silent. When CAF-1 is reduced, these regions, including endogenous retroviruses (ERVs), become active and mimic viral infection signals. This “viral mimicry” alerts the immune system, boosting its ability to recognize and attack cancer cells. As a result, tumors grew more slowly, and immune responses were stronger. Additionally, lowering CAF-1 levels enhanced the effectiveness of immunotherapy treatments like anti-PD1. These findings show that targeting the epigenetic regulation by CAF-1 can trigger viral mimicry, activating anti-tumor immunity and improving therapy outcomes in liver cancer.

17113221.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17113221.value: 该项目将阐明生物在极端热带海洋环境中功能适应的生态生理和调节机制。岩质海岸是地球上最极端的环境之一。在这些生境中，生命不断暴露在具有严酷梯度的非生物条件下，这可能超过许多海洋生物的致死极限。这些具有挑战性的环境促进了生存策略的进化，使潮间带生物寻找更适宜的微生境(迁徙)或者“稳坐原地”并发展应对极端条件的机制（斗争）。这些策略的成败取决于生理生态过程、生活史和分子适应之间精细协调的相互作用。这一点在高潮间带表现得最为明显，腹足动物的一个科，玉黍螺科（Littorinidae），统治着全球高潮间带。玉黍螺 （Littorinid）为极端环境中适应性进化的研究提供了一个极好的系统，因为它们生活在海洋对岩质海岸影响的最上部，持续的热应激加上干燥和缺氧，创造了一个很少物种能够生存的潮间带沙漠。作为在这种极端环境中长期选择的结果，littorinids进化出了一种有效的适应策略，通过进入一种对温度不敏感的低代谢状态来“斗争”。这种代谢模式是一种生理异常，因为它偏离了变温动物热演化的传统模式。在这里，通过结合进化原理与原位生态生理实验以及高通量转录组分析技术，本项目将探索一个创新的理论框架，旨在: (i)评估温度不敏感代谢抑制的能量限制(目标1);(ii)了解该适应性状的个体间差异是否可重复(目标2); (iii)建立潮间带变温动物适应性代谢阻滞的分子机制(目标3)。为了实现这些目标，我们将开发一种强大的实验设计，将高分辨率、全生物呼吸测量与最先进的分子和生物信息学方法相结合。该研究结果将为极端环境下生命的生存机制提供新的见解。这些信息也将为对生物保护遗传多样性管理有兴趣、协助适应气候变化(例如，基因救援)、生物工程和合成生物学(例如，改善人类/动物健康的遗传工具)以及农业/水产养殖生产(例如，抗胁迫生物的选择性育种)的有关部门提供有价值的重要的功能和遗传/基因组资源。

17113221.label: Major findings and research outcome
17113221.value: Our GRF project has elucidated the functional (whole-organism physiology) and molecular mechanisms underlying thermoregulation and phenotypic plasticity in marine ectotherms inhabiting tropical extreme environments. In these systems, natural selection has favoured physiological adaptations that deviate from traditional models of thermal evolution in ectotherms. Notably, these adaptations enable tropical intertidal ectotherms to mitigate thermal stress through metabolic arrest. Our research has clearly demonstrated how these animals regulate such physiological responses and how environmental factors influence their activation. Findings indicate that increased rates of environmental temperature significantly impair fitness-related traits. Additionally, we observed an upregulation of protein-folding genes at the expense of pro-survival pathways, suggesting a trade-off in molecular responses. However, mid- and slow rates of environmental change allow animals to gradually activate different strategies (e.g., behavioural, physiological, molecular), which maximise survival and reduce energetic costs. The capacity for these phenotypic and molecular adjustments varies along the vertical zonation of the intertidal zone, likely driven by natural selection (being more pronounced in high-shore populations compared to those lower in the intertidal). Importantly, higher-shore populations exhibit greater vulnerabilities to warming oceans and climate change, highlighting significant ecological and evolutionary trade-offs associated with their adaptation strategies.

17113221.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17113221.value: We have identified key molecular mechanisms that underpin hypometabolism and pro-survival strategies employed by organisms facing extreme environmental conditions. These mechanisms include specific gene regulation pathways that enable cells to enter a state of metabolic arrest, reducing energy expenditure and protecting vital functions during periods of thermal stress. Understanding these processes provides valuable insights into how organisms adapt and survive in harsh environments, such as tropical intertidal zones experiencing rapid temperature fluctuations. This knowledge has significant practical applications, particularly in the aquaculture sector. By leveraging these molecular insights, it may be possible to develop strategies to enhance the resilience, fitness, and overall performance of commercially valuable species.

17113221.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17113221.value: Temperature is one of the most important environmental factors that affect how animals live, grow, and evolve. In tropical regions, where temperatures don’t vary much throughout the year, many marine animals live close to their thermal limits. This makes them especially vulnerable to climate change, as even small temperature increases can cause harm. Interestingly, some of these animals have developed unique strategies to survive extreme conditions. They either move to cooler microhabitats (“Flight”) or stay put and activate special survival mechanisms (“Fight”). Some of these “Fight” strategies are unusual and differ from what’s typically expected in cold-blooded animals; they involve entering a state of metabolic arrest, where cellular activity is temporarily suppressed. This GRF project documents the functional and molecular mechanisms underpinning the adaptation of intertidal ectotherms to extreme environments. We found that the rate of environmental change highly conditions the capacity to regulate such adaptive responses. Moreover, these responses vary along the vertical zones of rocky shores, with higher-shore populations being more vulnerable to warming oceans, highlighting the risks climate change poses to these resilient yet delicate organisms.

17113721.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17113721.value: 基於單分子測序的體細胞突變檢測

17113721.label: Project Objectives
17113721.value: To devise an exome sequencing protocol for Single Molecule Sequencing and somatic variant calling The throughput of an Oxford Nanopore MinION sequencing flowcell is limited. To achieve somatic variant calling in a patient sample using a single flowcell, a workable exome sequencing wet lab protocol is needed. The protocol should be cost-effective and require low DNA input amount, and should consistently generate an average depth coverage of over 100-fold with an even distribution of depth coverage and covering most of the clinical targets in HGMD, OMIM, and Clinvar. Our aim is to develop a protocol for somatic variant calling with deep coverage and a high on-target rate. Our preliminary studies found a protocol that achieved sufficient depth coverage. We will perform 24 experiments to search for a protocol with even better performance with a higher on-target rate. To generate ample samples for training our deep learning model For any new algorithm development in bioinformatics that involves deep learning, having sufficient training samples is often the primary concern. However, only one referential tumor-normal pair with known somatic variants is publicly available, which is far from enough. To solve this problem, we have devised a new method to create synthetic samples from real data using the idea that a germline homozygous variant unique to one sample can be seen as a true somatic variant of another sample when the two samples are combined. The real data of two or more samples combined can simulate different depth coverage, allelic fraction, and contamination level of a normal sample. Using titration, we will mix two or more samples in different proportions to verify whether our synthetic data resembles real data. We will experiment with the mixture of two samples at different ratios, from 5%:95% to 45%:55%, in 5% steps. We will also experiment with a mixture of two, three, and four samples in equal proportions. Our goal is to generate ample samples for training our deep learning model for sensitive and accurate somatic variant calling. To implement a deep learning approach for somatic variant calling To distinguish true variant signals from sequencing errors in the Single Molecule Sequencing data, the PI has demonstrated that using deep learning is a viable approach. For somatic variant calling, which is one of the most challenging problems in variant calling, we propose a new model, called 21-genotype, to represent the complicated allelic composition of a somatic variant. We will upgrade our deep learning approach to use the new 21-genotype model to develop a viable method for somatic variant calling. We propose to implement a strategy for comparing a tumor-normal pair for accurate somatic variant calling. Our goal is to implement the first somatic variant caller for Single Molecule Sequencing data. Addressing confounding factors and benchmarking Somatic variant calling is difficult because of six known confounding factors: 1) low depth coverage, 2) low allelic fraction, 3) difficult genomic regions, 4) FFPE samples with DNA damage, 5) contaminated matched normal, and 6) long InDels. We will study the performance of our method with different settings, particularly in extreme cases. We will benchmark and demarcate our method using established standards for benchmarking somatic variant calling. Our methods and findings will be published, and our implemented somatic variant caller will be made open-source.

17113721.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17113721.value: 精準醫療指的是利用病人癌組織中的遺傳突變決定最佳治療方案。這需要用到精確的測試方法來將遺傳突變從測序的錯誤中分辨出來。要想將測序應用於提高病人生活品質，準確的區分突變和假信號是至關重要的。 此前，二代測序技術被用於癌症突變檢測，但其不能很好地識別結構性變異。最近幾年開發的單分子測序技術，體積小，簡單易用，樣品製備輕鬆，讀長長。利用這些優勢，單分子測序解決了結構性變異檢測的問題，使其成為了精準醫療應用中一個不可逆轉的趨勢。然而，單分子測序的單堿基錯誤率頗高（10%）使得小突變的檢測變得困難，讓其暫時無法徹底取代之前的技術。要克服這個困難，我們需要新的樣品製備方法和計算機算法。 本項目將開發切實可行的方法使得單分子測序適用於癌症的小突變檢測。我們將開發一個穩定、划算、低DNA輸入量以及易於操作的外顯子捕獲設計方案以達到使用單個測序流動池可以獲得關鍵癌症基因大於100層的覆蓋度。我們將開發一個基於深度學習的癌症突變檢測算法。基於以下認識“一個個體特有的純合生殖細胞突變若加入到另一個個體中，可視作另一個個體的體細胞突變”，我們將對多個個體的真實測序數據進行組合以產生大量的模擬癌症數據用於深度模型訓練。在數據中，我們將考慮到多個癌症突變檢測的難點，包括低等位基因比例、低測序深度、參考樣品污染和複雜基因組區域等問題。我們對項目進行了風險分析，並擬定了一個應對計劃。 我們的外顯子捕獲初始設計方案的結果令人滿意，使我們可以探索更高的測序深度和更低的DNA輸入量。我們利用深度神經網絡對生殖細胞突變檢測的理論和方法已經發表在Nature Communications (2019)和Nature Machine Intelligence (2020)。接下來我們將要攻克的癌症體細胞突變檢測難題，挑戰巨大。但我們相信是可以克服的，並在正文給出了方案和討論。我們先前的積累給這個項目打下了很好的基礎。讓我們使單分子測序成為精準醫療的標準方法。

17113721.label: Major findings and research outcome
17113721.value: The project has established the global standard of cancer mutation detection using single-molecule sequencing. The algorithm called Clair3 (Zheng et al., Nature Computational Science, 2022) that we have developed is now the go-to algorithm for cancer mutation detection using single-molecule sequencing. The theoretical performance limit of cancer mutation detection using single-molecule sequencing was demarcated (Luo et al., Nature Machine Intelligence, 2020). The cancer sample-only algorithm called ClairS-TO for sample availability-constrained usage environment was developed (Luo et al., Nature Communications, 2025) and is now being used by geneticists and oncologists worldwide for cancer diagnosis and targeted drug prescription on a regular basis.

17113721.value: The project has all objectives accomplished. Nevertheless, the PI of the project will seek opportunities in large genomics studies and project management with the fantastic track record of this project.
