17114021.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17114021.value: 目前肝細胞癌的治療選擇有限，手術切除與肝臟移植通常不適用於晚期肝癌患者。接受如化療或多種酪氨酸激酶抑製劑 (TKI) 靶向治療等舒緩治療的患者通常反應不佳並易產生耐藥性，導致腫瘤復發和不良預後。我們之前的研究中顯示，化療和 TKI 的耐藥性源自腫瘤內的癌症幹細胞。肝癌幹細胞能促進腫瘤的自我更新和存活，使腫瘤產生治療抗性 （Tong et al., Stem Cell Rep 2015; Tong et al., J Hepatol 2018; Leung & Tong et al., Hepatology 2020）。在研究肝癌幹性和耐藥性的分子靶點及通路的過程中獲得的相關知識將有助於合理並有效的設計治療方案。 蛋白激酶通過磷酸轉移的依賴性信號傳導級聯從而控制多種致癌功能，而針對其中的關鍵節點可以開發有效的選擇性抑制劑。然而，蛋白激酶在維持肝癌幹性和治療抗性中的作用尚未研究透徹。通過對兩個激酶組分析數據集的綜合分析，我們發現在人類肝細胞癌中檢測到活性 p38β 有更高的表達。p38β 是 p38 MAPK 的家族成員。在功能上，我們證明 p38β 能促進肝癌的腫瘤發生、癌症幹性和對化療藥物 5-氟尿嘧啶和順鉑的藥物抵抗性。為了鑑定 p38β 的新型結合底物，我們進行了串聯親和純化 - 質譜實驗並鑑定出 BiP 是p38β的潛在結合蛋白。BiP 是一種伴侶蛋白，可調節內質網應激和未折疊蛋白反應(UPR)。內質網應激和未折疊蛋白反應的持續激活與正常幹細胞和癌症幹細胞的幹細胞特性喪失有關。我們發現p38β過表達增加了 BiP 的磷酸化，從而抑制了未折疊蛋白反應的下游 PERK/eIF2α/ATF4 和 IRE1α 分支。 BiP 的抑制可以挽救和逆轉在 p38β過表達細胞中觀察到的致癌和幹性表型。 總而言之，我們假設p38β通過直接調節 BiP 介導的肝細胞癌中的未折疊蛋白反應信號的傳導來調節癌症幹性和耐藥性。我們提出的工作旨在通過在肝細胞癌中協調 BiP/UPR 信號來闡明p38β在促進癌症幹性和治療抗性方面的功能和調節作用。我們還將評估 p38β/BiP/UPR 通路在肝細胞癌中的臨床意義和治療價值。

17114021.label: Realisation of objectives
17114021.value: Objective 1: To characterize the functional roles of p38β in promoting cancer and stem cell-like properties in HCC. To investigate the functional significance of p38β upregulation in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), we knocked out the gene using CRISPR-Cas9 in PLC8024 cells, which have high endogenous p38β levels. p38β knockout significantly impaired oncogenic potential, as shown by reduced foci formation. Analysis of the CellMiner database revealed a strong positive correlation between p38β expression and resistance to chemotherapeutic agents like cisplatin (CDDP). Consistently, p38β-deficient cells showed a substantial increase in apoptosis after CDDP treatment, indicating enhanced drug sensitivity. p38β knockout also markedly reduced the frequency of tumorsphere-initiating cells, demonstrating impaired self-renewal capacity of HCC stem-like cells. To confirm the role of p38β’s kinase activity, we overexpressed wild-type (WT) or a kinase-dead mutant (Mut, T180A/Y182F) in MHCC97L cells, which have low endogenous p38β. p38β WT overexpression enhanced foci formation and tumorsphere initiation, whereas the Mut form had no effect. In vivo limiting dilution transplantation assays in NOD/SCID mice showed that p38β WT cells resulted in higher tumor incidence, larger tumor burden, and shorter tumor-free survival compared to EV and Mut controls. Serial transplantation confirmed sustained tumor-initiating capacity only in p38β WT-derived cells. These findings establish p38β as a key regulator of tumorigenicity, stemness, and chemoresistance in HCC, dependent on its kinase activity. Objective 2: To elucidate the molecular mechanism of p38β in regulating BiP/UPR pathway and thereby promoting cancer stemness and drug resistance. To identify how p38β drives stemness and chemoresistance, we performed tandem affinity purification and mass spectrometry (TAP-MS), which identified the ER chaperone BiP as a key interactor. Co-immunoprecipitation validated the p38β-BiP interaction in HCC cells and patient tissues, and this binding was dependent on p38β’s kinase activity. We next investigated if p38β acts through BiP. Knocking down BiP in p38β-overexpressing cells significantly reduced foci formation, tumorsphere initiation, and reversed CDDP resistance. Similarly, treating cells with HA15, a selective BiP inhibitor, phenocopied BiP knockdown, reducing oncogenicity and restoring chemosensitivity. BiP is a master regulator of the unfolded protein response (UPR), binding to and inhibiting stress sensors like IRE1-α and PERK under homeostasis. We found that p38β overexpression enhanced BiP’s interaction with IRE1-α and PERK and suppressed their phosphorylation, indicating attenuated UPR activation. Conversely, p38β knockout increased sensor phosphorylation. To assess ER proteostasis, we measured unfolded protein levels using a thiol-reactive dye (TPE-MI). p38β-overexpressing cells exhibited reduced unfolded protein accumulation after tunicamycin or CDDP treatment, while p38β knockout increased it. Crucially, BiP knockdown in p38β-overexpressing cells restored IRE1-α and PERK phosphorylation and increased unfolded protein levels, reversing the p38β-mediated suppression of the UPR. HA15 treatment similarly restored UPR sensor activation. These results demonstrate that p38β promotes stemness and chemoresistance by binding BiP in a kinase-dependent manner to suppress UPR signaling and unfolded protein accumulation. Objective 3: To explore the therapeutic potential of targeting p38β/BiP pathway as a single and/or combination therapy with existing HCC targeted therapy. To assess the therapeutic potential of targeting the p38β-BiP axis in a clinically relevant context, we established patient-derived xenograft (PDX) and patient-derived organoid (PDO) models from advanced HCC specimens exhibiting high p38β expression. In the PDX model, tumor-bearing mice were randomized into four treatment groups: vehicle (EV), HA15 (a selective BiP inhibitor), cisplatin (CDDP), and the HA15+CDDP combination. Tumor growth was monitored for 14 days. As expected, CDDP monotherapy moderately inhibited tumor growth, whereas the combination treatment led to a significantly greater reduction in both tumor volume and weight compared to CDDP alone. Consistently, limiting dilution tumorsphere formation assays using residual PDX-derived tumor cells showed that the combination treatment markedly decreased the frequency of tumorsphere-initiating cells, indicating impaired self-renewal capacity of HCC stem-like cells. Furthermore, IHC analysis revealed increased phosphorylation of IRE1-α in the combination group, consistent with enhanced activation of the UPR. In parallel, decreased PCNA staining and elevated TUNEL signals were observed, indicative of reduced proliferation and increased apoptosis in response to combination therapy. Consistently, combination treatment with HA15 and CDDP markedly suppressed PDO growth compared to either monotherapy, as visualized by bright-field imaging. To further confirm the synergistic effect of HA15 and CDDP in PDOs, we performed a drug combination assay using a dose-response matrix of both agents. Cell viability was assessed using CellTiter-Glo, and synergy analysis by SynergyFinder revealed a strong synergistic interaction, as indicated by a positive synergy score and a 3D synergy surface plot. Together, these findings support that pharmacological targeting of the p38β-BiP axis sensitizes HCC tumors to chemotherapy by restoring UPR signaling and disrupting tumor stemness. Objective 4: To investigate the clinical significance of p38β overexpression and the clinical correlation of p38β and BiP in HCC. To determine the clinical relevance of p38β, we performed immunohistochemical (IHC) analysis on a tissue microarray (TMA) comprising 136 paired HCC tumor (T) and adjacent non-tumor (N) liver samples. p38β expression was elevated in 53.68% of tumor tissues, compared to 28.68% of adjacent non-tumor tissues. Consistent with this, p38β protein levels were markedly increased in multiple HCC cell lines relative to the normal liver cell line MIHA. Kaplan–Meier survival analysis further revealed that high p38β expression correlated with poorer overall survival in HCC patients. Moreover, elevated p38β levels were strongly associated with advanced disease features, including higher TNM stage, late HCC staging, vascular invasion, and increased serum alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) levels. These findings establish p38β as a clinically relevant kinase that is upregulated in HCC and may contribute to both disease progression and therapeutic resistance. Differential gene expression profiling revealed that high p38β tumors exhibited elevated levels of hepatic progenitor markers (e.g., AFP, SOX9 and EpCAM) and reduced mature hepatocyte markers (e.g., ALB, G6PC), indicative of a less differentiated, stem-like cellular state. Moreover, gene set enrichment analysis revealed that genes upregulated in the high p38β group were significantly enriched in transcriptional programs associated with cancer stemness and poor differentiation, including the Rhodes undifferentiated cancer profile, the Engelmann cancer progenitor signature, and Yamashita liver cancer stem cell signature. Consistently, p38β expression positively correlated with elevated serum AFP levels in HCC patients. Kaplan–Meier survival analysis further demonstrated that patients with high tumor stemness scores (TSSHigh) and high p38β expression (p38βHigh) exhibited significantly poorer clinical outcomes compared to those with low levels of both markers (TSSLow; p38βLow). Moreover, Kaplan-Meier survival analysis further revealed that high p-BiP T648 expression correlated with poorer overall survival in HCC patients.

17114021.label: Major findings and research outcome
17114021.value: This study establishes p38β as a critical oncogenic driver in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) that promotes tumorigenicity, cancer stemness, and chemoresistance. Functional experiments demonstrated that p38β knockout impaired tumor growth and self-renewal, while its overexpression enhanced these properties. Crucially, this activity was dependent on p38β's kinase function, as a kinase-dead mutant was ineffective. The molecular mechanism was elucidated through the discovery that active p38β binds to the ER chaperone BiP, a master regulator of the unfolded protein response (UPR). This interaction suppresses UPR activation by enhancing BiP's inhibition of key stress sensors IRE1-α and PERK, thereby reducing unfolded protein accumulation and mitigating endoplasmic reticulum stress. This p38β-BiP axis is pivotal for its oncogenic role, as BiP knockdown or inhibition with HA15 reversed p38β-driven stemness and cisplatin resistance. The clinical significance of this pathway is underscored by the finding that p38β is upregulated in over half of HCC tumors, with high expression correlating with poor patient survival, advanced disease stage, and a dedifferentiated, stem-like cellular state. The therapeutic potential was confirmed in patient-derived models, where the BiP inhibitor HA15 synergized with cisplatin to suppress tumor growth, eliminate cancer stem cells, and reactivate the UPR. In conclusion, this research identifies the p38β-BiP axis as a novel signaling pathway that suppresses the UPR to foster an aggressive HCC phenotype, offering a promising therapeutic strategy to overcome chemoresistance by targeting this specific interaction.

17114021.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17114021.value: This research provides a robust foundation for translating the p38β-BiP axis into clinical application. The proposed course of action is the development and testing of a selective p38β inhibitor using a small molecule to inhibit the binding between p38β and BiP in HCC. Subsequently, the inhibitor will be rigorously tested for its efficacy and synergy with standard care (like sorafenib or cisplatin) in a broader panel of patient-derived organoids and xenografts.

17114021.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17114021.value: This research project aimed to mechanistically characterize the oncogenic functions of the kinase p38β in liver cancer, with a specific focus on its role in promoting cancer stemness and chemoresistance. We identified that p38β's tumor-promoting effects are mediated through a novel interaction with the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) chaperone BiP (GRP78). This p38β-BiP axis suppresses the unfolded protein response (UPR) by enhancing BiP's inhibition of the UPR stress sensors. This suppression of pro-apoptotic UPR signaling reduces stress, thereby fostering a chemoresistant and stem-like phenotype in liver cancer cells. The project validates the p38β-BiP interaction as a therapeutically targetable vulnerability. We demonstrated that pharmacological inhibition of BiP with HA15 synergizes with standard chemotherapeutics like cisplatin to re-activate the UPR, induce apoptosis, and eradicate tumor-initiating cells in patient-derived models. These findings provide a strong preclinical rationale for targeting this pathway to overcome therapy resistance in HCC patients with high p38β expression.

17114621.label: Realisation of objectives
17114621.value: All objectives have been achieved Objective 1: To examine if ALK oncogenic fusion and gain-of-function mutants are targets of arsenic trioxide in ALK-driven non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) and neuroblastoma (NB). Using 6 different EML4-ALK+ NSCLC lines (4 were TKI sensitive and 2 were TKI-resistant) and 2 other ALK-negative NSCLC lines as controls, we have demonstrated that all 6 EML4-ALK+ lines were highly sensitive to arsenic trioxide (ATO) induced growth inhibition and cell death, irrespective of their sensitivity to TKI. We further demonstrated that ATO down-regulated EML4-ALK oncogenic protein at the post-translational level with western immunoblot and semi-quantitative RT-PCR. Importantly, we showed that ATO downregulation of EML4-ALK inhibited the downstream signaling pathway. By using different constructs expressing motifs of the EML4-ALK in HEK293 cells, we showed that ATO specifically targeted the ALK domain of the fusion protein but not the EML4. Similarly in CLTC-ALK+ DLBCL, we have demonstrated ATO induced CLTC-downregulation at the protein level and that ATI specifically targeted the ALK domain of the fusion. (published in British Journal of Haematology) For NB, we also showed that ATO downregulated both ALK wild-type and ALK gain-of-function mutants at the protein level, and inhibited ALK downstream intracellular signalling in NB cells. 2. To examine the mechanisms of arsenic trioxide-induced degradation of these ALK fusion proteins and ALK gain-of-function mutants in respective cancer models. In EML4-ALK+ NSCLC, using co-immunoprecipitation experiments we showed that ATO degraded EML4-ALK by enhancing ubitquitination and thereby proteasomal degradation of the fusion protein. Importantly, restoration of EML4-ALK expression through forced expression abrogated ATO-induced cell death, supporting ATO acted through degradation of EML4-ALK in these ALK+ NSCLC. Similarly in CLTC-ALK DLBCL and ALK-mutated NB, ATO degraded CLTC-ALK (published in British Journal of Haematology) and ALK mutant through the proteasome pathway. Objective 3 To examine the effects of arsenic trioxide in NSCLC with TKI-resistant EML4-ALK mutants. Using a Ba/F3 cell model with different EML4-ALK mutants that were resistant to different generations of TKIs including crizotinib, ceritinib, and alectinib, we have shown that ATO degraded the EML4-ALK mutants and inhibited the growth of cells harbouring these mutants. The downstream signaling pathways (JAK-STAT, AKT) were inhibited by the use of ATO. Objective 4. To examine the effects of arsenic trioxide in xenograft murine models of these ALK-driven cancers. The in vitro activities of ATO were recapitulated in EML4-ALK-positive NSCLC xenografts in vivo. The growth of both TKI sensitive and resistant EML4-ALK NSCLCs xenografted in SCID mice were significantly suppressed by treating these mice with ATO at a clinically achievable dose. The explanted tumours showed increased in apoptosis and downregulation of JAK-STAT signaling pathway. Similarly, ATO inhibited the growth of CLTC-ALK DLBCL xenografted in SCID mice. (published in British Journal of Haeamtology) For NB, low-passage of ALK mutated/amplified NB cell lines (SH-SY5Y, Kelly, LAN-5 and NB-1) were subcutaneously injected into the right flank of 6-8 weeks old nude mice. 17114621.label: Major findings and research outcome
17114621.value: This project investigated the efficacy of arsenic trioxide (As₂O₃) against ALK-driven cancers, specifically non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL), and neuroblastoma (NB). As₂O₃ has shown significant dose-dependent inhibition of cell proliferation in NSCLC and DLBCL cell lines, with a GI50 within clinically achievable concentrations. It downregulates the EML4-ALK and CLTC-ALK fusion proteins post-translationally and reduces the phosphorylation of downstream signaling pathways, including AKT and STAT3. The compound degrades EML4-ALK and CLTC-ALK via the proteasomal pathway, as evidenced by increased ubiquitination, indicating its effectiveness against oncogenic fusion proteins. Notably, As₂O₃ also inhibits proliferation and degrades TKI-resistant EML4-ALK mutants, suggesting its therapeutic potential for TKI-resistant NSCLC. In vivo xenograft studies further confirm that As₂O₃ significantly suppresses tumor growth in models of ALK-driven NSCLC (including both EML4-ALK native and TKI-resistant mutants) and DLBCL. Overall, these findings position As₂O₃ as a promising therapeutic agent for ALK-driven malignancies, especially in TKI-resistant cases, by targeting and degrading oncogenic fusion proteins. A manuscript is being prepared for publication in international journal on the use of arsenic trioxide as a potential therapeutic agent for ALK-positive non-small cell lung cancers.

17114621.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17114621.value: 1. The detailed molecular mechanisms underlying arsenic trioxide As₂O₃ mediated degradation of oncogenic proteins (such as ALK-fusion proteins, BCL6 (previously studied in another GRF project)) have not been fully elucidated. We are currently looking at the binding of As₂O₃ to some of the chaperone proteins and its effect on those chaperone protein functions that leads to the degradation of the client proteins including those oncoproteins. Biophysical and biochemical analysis and structural studies are being planned. 2. A pilot clinical study on the use of As₂O₃ in TKI-resistant ALK-positive NSCLC is also being planned, in collaboration with oncologists.

17114621.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17114621.value: This study has provided evidence that arsenic trioxide is effective in killing cancer cells that are associated with anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK) aberrations. The most notable example is ALK-positive non-small cell lung cancer. Currently, this cancer is being treated with ALK inhibitors. However, resistance to these ALK inhibitors develops with prolonged treatment and the cancer will progress subsequently. Furthermore, the cost of these inhibitors is also very high. Our results demonstrated the use of arsenic trioxide as a potential therapy for ALK-positive lung cancer in animal model, including those that are resistant to ALK inhibitors. Oral formulation arsenic trioxide has been developed in Hong Kong and the cost is much lower than that of ALK inhibitors. This will potentially benefit our lung cancer patients in terms of drug efficacy and cost effectiveness.

17114921.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17114921.value: 背景/意義：自閉症譜系障礙 (autism spectrum disorder, ASD) 是一種早發性的神經發育障礙，可引致各種社交、溝通、行為等方面的困難。ASD亦有可能導致嚴重的終身殘疾及其他兼患的共病症。根據世界衛生組織估計，全球每160名兒童中就有1名患有ASD。ASD 的患病率亦在世界各地有上升的趨勢。由於目前尚無可根治ASD核心症狀的有效方法，減少與ASD及其共病症相關的可變風險因素是現時一個非常重要的研究領域。此外，及早發現ASD和進行干預治療對於促進兒童的最佳發育進程和改善功能也非常關鍵。基於電子健康記錄（electronic health records, EHRs）而建立的數據導向決策策略，可有效地識別患有ASD及其共病症的風險因素和高風險人士。這些策略對於制定 ASD 風險最小化和早期干預的措施尤其重要。目前有不同研究報告指出，某些孕婦風險因素和子代特徵可能會對子女ASD發病有影響。然而，目前研究只對這些風險因素進行了個別調查。各種孕婦風險因素和童年特徵（產前、圍產期和產後）與 ASD 及其共病症之間的關聯尚不明確。 此外，ASD 及其相關的共病症很有可能是由不同因素的相互作用所產生。因此，RIMA 團隊將評估多種因素對 ASD 和其共病症的綜合影響。 目的：RIMA團隊將評估與ASD及其共病症相關的風險因素，並使用機器學習技術（machine learning）來建立和驗證一套預測子代ASD的臨床算法。 研究策略/方法：當前研究的不足主要是因為樣本少以及每次只評估單一風險因素。我們假設機器學習方法將能夠檢測多個變數之間隱藏的趨勢和相互作用，並能夠揭示孕婦/子代風險因素與子代ASD 及其共病症之間的關聯。我們亦從現有具影響力的文獻中挑選孕婦危險因素和童年特徵。本項目將從香港、英國、台灣和韓國多個研究數據庫中檢索電子健康記錄 (EHR)。我們的 EHR 數據庫包含有關處方、藥房配藥、診斷以及實驗室測試結果的確切數據，而這些數據在以往的研究中經常缺乏。本研究的直接成果是對子代ASD 風險進行分類的臨床工具。該工具可協助制定母親風險最小化和兒童早期干預的策略。靈活的機器學習技術的應用亦有助於新假設的發展。該算法源自真實世界的數據，可以輕易地以自動化方式嵌入至當前的健康信息系統中。 團隊: RIMA 團隊由流行病學、統計學、兒科、兒童精神病學、產科、藥劑學、產科、計算機科學方面的國際專家組成。 所有團隊成員均曾與首席研究員合作並成功完成了先前的項目。 總結：RIMA團隊擁有適當的專業知識、數據使用權和項目管理技能以完成這項嶄新亦非常可行的研究。

17115121.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17115121.value: Marine heatwaves (MHW) are extreme climatic events that have recently been recognized as an emerging threat to marine ecosystems globally. Driven by climate change, heatwaves are already causing deleterious ecosystem and socio-economic impacts. South-east Asia is a climate change hotspot with the frequency and intensity of MHWs predicted to increase. However, the impact of MHWs on coastal organisms and ecosystems in SE Asia are largely unknown. Therefore, developing an understanding of the impacts that MHWs will have on the survival and adaptation of key species within marine communities has become an imperative. Here, we propose to use a broadly distributed subtidal sea urchin, Heliocidaris crassispina as a model species to test for changes to the physiological and molecular mechanisms which may provide resistance to MHWs. The extent to which ecosystems are impacted by heatwaves is determined by the biological responses of important species, the underlying physiological and molecular mechanisms, and whether these physiological changes impart increased thermal tolerance to the next generation. The process of “heat hardening” through plastic changes will be essential for the survival of individuals, although for populations to persist these tolerance mechanisms need to be passed to the next generation. Therefore, to understand the potential effects of MHWs, we need to unravel not only the physiological changes in the current generation but also whether these changes are heritable and confer thermal adaptation in subsequent generations. Here, we will experimentally assess the effects of consecutive MHWs and recovery periods on the physiological response of H. crassispina. Following this, we aim to elucidate the underlying effects of stress on the cellular functioning of this urchin by assessing changes to transcriptome expression following MHW exposure. We will then quantify any transcriptomic changes in the eggs to see whether adult responses are also expressed in the gametes as a form of maternal provisioning. Lastly, we will spawn the urchins and track the development from embryo to juveniles, to determine if any “heat stress memory” is evident in the physiological and molecular responses of the progeny of heat hardened parents. This will enable us to highlight the potential for thermal stress from heatwaves to be expressed in the physiology and molecular mechanisms of urchins that underpin phenotypic plasticity, and whether there is the potential for the inheritance of stress memory mediated by maternal priming in this ecologically important marine invertebrate. 海洋熱浪是一種極端氣候事件。近年，各界深知海洋熱浪會危害全球海洋生態，氣候變化帶來的熱浪已危及生態系統以及社會經濟。東南亞是氣候變化重災區，預期將面臨更頻繁及劇烈的熱浪，然而熱浪對海岸生物及生態系統的影響多仍屬未知之數。因此，我們有急切需要去了解海洋熱浪如何影響海洋族群中關鍵物種的生存與適應能力。 本研究以分佈廣泛的亞潮間帶海膽Heliocidaris crassispina作模式生物，測試其生理及分子機制的變化，以探討其中抵禦海洋熱浪的機制。生態系統受海洋熱浪影響的程度取決於重要物種的耐受性，當中牽涉的生理及分子機制，以及這些生理變化有否賦予下一代更高的耐熱能力。「耐熱強化」對個體生物來說性命攸關，但這些抵禦機制須流傳至後代才有助族群存續。因此，要掌握海洋熱浪的潛在影響，我們不但要拆解物種在單一世代的生理變化，更要研究這些變化是否可遺傳並賦予後續世代更強的耐熱可塑性。本研究先透過H. crassispina的生理反應來評估重複的熱浪和恢復週期對其之影響。然後，我們會測量H. crassispina在承受海洋熱浪時的轉錄組變化，以闡明熱力對海膽細胞功能的影響。我們亦會量度卵子中可能出現的轉錄組變化，從而探討母體對海洋熱浪的反應是否能在配子中出現。最後，我們會繁殖這些海膽並追蹤胚胎至幼體的發育情況，以判定經「耐熱強化」的親代，其後裔有否在生理及分子反應中顯示出「熱力記憶」。生理及分子機制是構成生物表型可塑性的關鍵，本研究有助指出海洋熱浪中的熱應力對這些機制可能帶來的影響，以及從海膽這種擁有重要生態價值的海洋無脊椎動物身上，探討透過母體遺傳熱力記憶的可能性。

17116521.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17116521.value: Sjögren’s syndrome (SS) is an autoimmune disease characterized by lymphocytic infiltration and tissue destruction of salivary and lachrymal glands, leading to severe dry eyes and dry mouth symptoms. SS is further complicated with systemic inflammations including lung and kidney injuries, while the development of B cell-malignancy in SS is highest among systemic autoimmune diseases. Due to the limited understanding of disease pathogenesis, SS patients have suffered from a lack of effective treatments in clinical management. Recent studies, including our findings, have indicated a pivotal role of T follicular helper (Tfh) cells in regulating humoral responses in autoimmune diseases. In collaboration with Peking University 3rd hospital, our pilot studies also validated the pathogenicity of Tfh cells in promoting autoantibodies and disease pathology. Emerging evidence suggests a close involvement of caveolin-1 (Cav-1) in T cell response. However, whether and how Cav-1 paly a role in SS pathogenesis remain unknown. We have recently established a mouse model for experimental SS (ESS) that recapitulates the hallmarks of human SS. In our pilot studies, we observed significantly exacerbated disease pathology and enhanced Tfh cell responses in Cav-1-/- mice. Using adoptive transfer technique, we identified that Cav-1 deficiency in CD4+ T cells promoted their follicular homing and autoreactive B cell response, which may attribute to elevated ICOS expression, a functional marker of Tfh cells and key factor in follicular recruitment. Consistently, Cav-1 inhibition also resulted enhanced Tfh differentiation in human CD4+ T cells. Mechanistic studies revealed that peroxisome proliferator-activated receptors (PPAR) was critically involved in Cav-1-mediated ICOS expression, while pioglitazone, an FDA approved PPAR agonist effective prevented ESS induction in mice. In this project, we will further investigate the mechanism underlying the Cav-1-mediated functional changes in Tfh cell responses. In collaboration Prof. Feng, we will extend our findings in humans and explore the novel therapeutic strategies by targeting PPAR in SS, a disease with high social relevance in Hong Kong. 原發性幹燥綜合征（primary Sjögren’s syndrome, pSS）是一種自身免疫性疾病，其主要特征為淋巴細胞浸潤及唾液腺、淚腺組織破壞，並導致嚴重的眼幹和口幹癥狀。此外，進一步合並包括肺臟和腎臟損傷在內的全身炎癥，且在系統性自身免疫性疾病中並發B細胞惡性腫瘤最多。由於對疾病發病機製的理解有限，臨床治療上我們還缺乏有效的方法。 近期研究（包括我們自己的發現）表明，T濾泡輔助（T follicular helper, Tfh）細胞在調節自身免疫性疾病的體液反應中起著關鍵作用。在與北京大學第三醫院合作中，我們初步證實了Tfh細胞在促進自身抗體產生和疾病病理過程中的致病作用。新的證據表明，小窩蛋白1（caveolin-1， Cav-1)與T細胞應答密切相關。然而，Cav-1是否以及如何在pSS發病機製中發揮作用尚未清楚。我們已經建立了實驗性幹燥綜合征（Experimental Sjögren’s syndrome, ESS）小鼠模型，其概括了人類pSS的特征。在初步研究中，我們觀察到Cav-1-/-小鼠的疾病病理顯著惡化，Tfh細胞應答增強。采用過繼轉移技術，發現 CD4+ T 細胞中的 Cav-1缺陷促進其濾泡歸巢和自體反應性B細胞反應，這可能歸因於誘導共刺激物（inducible co-stimulator , ICOS）表達升高，ICOS是Tfh細胞的功能標記物，也是濾泡募集的重要因素。與此相似的是，Cav-1的抑製也導致Tfh細胞在人類CD4+T細胞中的分化增強。機製研究揭示，過氧化物酶體增殖物激活受體 （peroxisome proliferator-activated receptors, PPAR）在Cav-1介導的ICOS表達中起關鍵作用，而FDA批準的PPAR激動劑吡格列酮能有效抑製ESS小鼠的發病。 在本項目中，我們將進一步探究Cav-1介導的Tfh細胞應答功能改變的機製。在與馮教授的合作中，我們將把把基礎研究成果拓展到臨床應用，並且探索靶向PPAR的pSS（一種在香港具有高度社會相關性的疾病）治療新策。

17116521.label: Realisation of objectives
17116521.value: The proposed experiments have been carried out and published in Cell Rep. 2025 Aug 26;44(8):116156. doi: 10.1016/j.celrep.2025.116156. 1. To identify the role of caveolin-1 (Cav-1) in Sjogren's syndrome (SS) pathogenesis 1.1 Cav-1 deficiency exacerbates ESS pathology Although previous studies have reported that Cav-1 deficiency ameliorated EAE pathology, we unexpectedly found that it considerably exacerbated experimental Sjögren's syndrome (ESS) in mice. Upon disease induction, Cav-1 knockout mice developed more severe salivary hypofunction, higher autoantibody titers, and enhanced IgG deposition on the salivary epithelium compared to wild-type controls. Long-term observation revealed accelerated tissue destruction in Cav-1 deficient mice, characterized by massive lymphocytic foci, increased apoptotic epithelial cells, and larger infiltrating areas in salivary and lacrimal glands. Furthermore, confocal imaging confirmed the presence of ectopic lymphoid structures and Bcl6+CD4+ T cells within B cell aggregates in the inflamed tissues. These collective findings demonstrate that Cav-1 deficiency promotes ESS development in mice. 1.2 Cav-1 constrains the expression of ICOS and follicular migration of Tfh cells While Th17 cells are established contributors to EAE and ESS pathogenesis, we found that Cav-1 deficiency did not alter Th17 cell frequencies in ESS. Instead, Cav-1 −⁄− mice exhibited a significant increase in Tfh cells in draining lymph nodes, alongside germinal center expansion and elevated GC B cell numbers. Cav-1 expression in CD4+ T cells rose transiently during ESS onset but declined as disease advanced. Using adoptive transfer models, we demonstrated that Cav-1 −⁄− CD4+ T cells—but not B cells—drove autoreactive humoral responses, enhancing IgG deposition in salivary tissues. This Tfh-promoting effect was confirmed in T cell–specific Cav-1 knockout mice and extended to the EAE model, where Cav-1 −⁄− MOG-reactive CD4+ T cells preferentially adopted a Tfh phenotype. Mechanistically, Cav-1 −⁄− Tfh cells showed elevated ICOS expression and enhanced migratory behavior, including pseudopod extension, cytoskeleton remodeling, and increased motility toward B cell follicles. ICOS blockade reversed these effects, normalizing Tfh accumulation, follicular homing, plasma cell generation, and autoantibody levels. Thus, Cav-1 constrains Tfh-driven autoimmunity not by altering central tolerance or T cell reactivity, but by limiting ICOS-mediated Tfh migration and follicular recruitment. 2. To investigate the molecular mechanism of Cav-1 in regulating T follicular helper cell response 2.1 Impaired PPARα expression in CD4+ T cells contributes to Cav-1-mediated Tfh cell response Cav-1 is primarily localized to the plasma membrane and cytoplasm of CD4+ T cells, but not the nucleus. RNA sequencing revealed that Cav-1 deficiency significantly altered the PPAR signaling pathway, with particularly reduced expression of PPARα at both transcriptional and protein levels in Cav-1−/− Tfh cells. Metabolomic analysis showed accumulated docosahexaenoic acid (DHA) and decreased linoleic acid in Cav-1−/− Tfh cells. Functionally, DHA suppressed while linoleic acid enhanced PPARα expression, suggesting a metabolite-mediated mechanism linking Cav-1 deficiency to PPARα downregulation. Genetic ablation of PPARα in CD4+ T cells enhanced Tfh cell differentiation, mimicking the Cav-1-deficient phenotype. Conversely, PPARα agonists, including the clinical drug fenofibrate, effectively suppressed Tfh cell differentiation in vitro. During ESS progression, PPARα expression dynamically changed in CD4+ T cells, transiently increasing at onset then declining as disease advanced. In vivo, PPARα antagonists promoted Tfh cell responses and elevated autoantibody production in ESS mice. These findings establish the Cav-1/PPARα axis as a key metabolic checkpoint restraining Tfh cell differentiation and humoral autoimmunity. 2.2 PPARα represses Icos transcription in Tfh cells Cav-1 deficiency leads to impaired lipid metabolism in CD4+ T cells, characterized by reduced lipid droplet accumulation and decreased fatty acid β-oxidation (FAO). This metabolic alteration was evidenced by lower mitochondrial respiratory capacity and reduced expression of key FAO enzymes in Cav-1−/− T cells during Tfh polarization. Notably, Icos transcription was upregulated in Cav-1−/− CD4+ T cells as early as 16 hours post-stimulation, preceding these metabolic changes. While PPARα target gene Cpt1a expression was decreased in Cav-1−/− T cells, restoring Cpt1a expression unexpectedly enhanced rather than suppressed ICOS expression. Similarly, fatty acid-free culture conditions did not diminish the elevated ICOS expression in Cav-1−/− cells. Mechanistic studies revealed that PPARα directly represses Icos transcription through binding to its promoter region as part of a PPARα/RXR heterodimer. This binding was detectable early during Tfh differentiation and could be modulated by PPARα and RXR agonists and antagonists. Disruption of PPARα nuclear translocation via COX-1 inhibition abolished its repressive effect on ICOS expression. These findings demonstrate that the Cav-1/PPARα axis regulates ICOS expression primarily through direct transcriptional repression rather than through modulation of lipid metabolism. 2.3 The Cav-1/PPARα axis critically regulates human Tfh cells We further validated the conserved role of the Cav-1/PPARα axis in human CD4+ T cells. Cav-1 deletion in human T cells enhanced their differentiation into ICOS+CXCR5+PD-1+ Tfh cells and increased ICOS and PD-1 expression, while reducing PPARα levels. Fenofibrate, a PPARα agonist, effectively suppressed human Tfh cell differentiation with an IC₅₀ of ∼7 μM and reduced Icos transcription early during polarization. Mechanistically, human PPARα directly bound to the Icos promoter during Tfh polarization, and this binding was disrupted by PPARα antagonism or inhibition of its nuclear translocation. Functionally, fenofibrate also inhibited ICOS-mediated T cell migration. In SjD patients, PPARα and Cav-1 expression were positively correlated in CD4+ T cells. Patients with higher circulating Tfh cell frequencies showed lower Cav-1 and PPARα levels, and Cav-1 expression negatively correlated with both ICOS expression and disease activity. These results confirm the Cav-1/PPARα axis as a conserved negative regulator of human Tfh cells and highlight PPARα targeting as a promising therapeutic strategy for Tfh-driven autoimmunity. 3. To develop novel therapeutic strategies for treating SS Fenofibrate, a pharmaceutical PPARα agonist with high affinity for both murine and human receptors, demonstrated therapeutic potential in experimental Sjögren's syndrome (ESS). When administered to ESS mice exhibiting acute inflammation meeting SjD diagnostic criteria, fenofibrate effectively ameliorated salivary hypofunction and reduced serum anti-SSA IgG levels, performing comparably to methotrexate (MTX), a first-line control treatment. Notably, fenofibrate specifically suppressed Tfh cell responses, particularly germinal center Tfh cells, and subsequently reduced GC areas, GC B cells, and plasma cells. In contrast, MTX primarily restrained B cell responses without affecting Tfh cell counts, consistent with clinical observations that MTX may even increase circulating Tfh cells in patients. In chronic ESS models, fenofibrate treatment significantly reduced salivary gland tissue damage, lymphocytic infiltration, and apoptotic epithelial cells, while preventing ectopic lymphoid structure formation. MTX failed to show similar efficacy at chronic disease stages. Crucially, in a humanized mouse model transplanted with SjD patient PBMCs, fenofibrate effectively suppressed human Tfh cells, confirming its cross-species therapeutic relevance. These findings collectively position PPARα agonism as a promising targeted approach for treating Tfh-driven autoimmune disorders like Sjögren's syndrome.

17116521.label: Major findings and research outcome
17116521.value: Tfh cells play a central role in humoral autoimmunity, including primary Sjogren disease (SjD). However, targeting Tfh cells in clinical management is challenging. Previous studies suggest that ICOS directs Tfh cell motility in engaging bystander B cells and promoting plasma cell differentiation. Herein, we took advantage of the mouse model of experimental Sjogren syndrome (ESS) and identified an unappreciated role of caveolin-1 (Cav-1) in suppressing ICOS expression in Tfh cells and SjD pathogenesis. PPARα), a transcription factor downstream of Cav-1, rapidly repressed Icos transcription upon Tfh polarization, independent of lipid metabolism. Both Cav-1 and PPARα were decreased in CD4+ T cells from patients with SjD and ESS mice. Notably, the pharmaceutical agonist of PPARα suppressed human and murine Tfh cell responses both in vitro and in vivo and effectively ameliorated the disease pathology of ESS mice with chronic inflammation. Other findings derived from this funding were listed in Part C.

17116521.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17116521.value: Although our present study has proposed a future approach of targeting PPARα in SjD, first-line medications are still essential for patients diagnosed with SjD. However, there is a lack of evidence-based studies using combined therapy of fenofibrate and disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs in patients with rheumatic diseases. Thus, safety and efficacy are both required to be tested, e.g., in humanized mouse model, and further verified in the clinical trial of fenofibrate treatment in SjD. Furthermore, it is not clear whether patient cohorts with normal PPARα expression levels would have different response to fenofibrate, highlighting the need for biomarker-driven patient stratification. Additionally, the broader immunomodulatory effects of PPARα activation on non-Tfh immune cell populations (e.g., B cells, macrophages) warrant further investigation to fully understand its clinical applicability.

17116521.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17116521.value: This research explores why the immune system sometimes attacks the body’s own moisture-producing glands, causing the autoimmune disorder Sjögren’s disease, which leads to severe dry eyes and mouth. We discovered a natural "braking system" inside our immune cells—a pair of proteins called Caveolin-1 and PPARα. This brake normally prevents a specific type of immune cell (T-follicular helper cell) from becoming overactive and driving the body to produce harmful antibodies. In Sjögren’s patients, this brake is weak. The study shows that strengthening it with a common, safe drug called fenofibrate can calm the overactive immune cells, reduce damaging antibodies, and alleviate disease symptoms in lab models. The significance is the discovery of a new internal checkpoint that, when faulty, leads to autoimmune disease. The value lies in identifying an existing, well-tolerated drug that could be rapidly repurposed as a targeted treatment for Sjögren's and similar conditions, offering new hope for patients.

17116621.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17116621.value: 神經病理性痛是一種由疾病或病變引起的軀體感覺異常，作為一種重要的臨床疾病，不僅對病人的生活質量造成了嚴重影響，同時對個人和社會都帶來沉重的經濟負擔。雖然現在已經存在大量的基於神經病理性痛分子機製作用的藥物被用於臨床，但其療效不盡如人意。硬膜外脊髓刺激(Epidural spinal cord stimulation, SCS)是一種新興的治療慢性疼痛的物理療法，可分為常規脊髓刺激(Conventional SCS, Con SCS)和1-10 kHz高頻脊髓刺激(High-frequency SCS, HF10 SCS)。 HF10 SCS比Con SCS表現出更有效和更持久的鎮痛效果。由於這種刺激方式剛剛被批准，HF10 SCS鎮痛作用的分子機制尚不清楚。因此，了解這些現有方法的作用機制十分重要，同時是為未來更好的神經調節治療奠定基礎。 我們為HF10 SCS建立了一種新的治療策略，優化了頻率和刺激時間，與Con SCS相比，新的治療策略能產生持久的鎮痛作用。為了研究Con SCS和HF10 SCS調節機制的不同，我們進行了轉錄組分析，並進行了功能驗證。 HF10 SCS顯著抑制炎症反應的發生和持續，促進M2型小膠質細胞極化。此外，我們發現，轉錄因子Kaiso被HF10 SCS特異性下調，而在HF10 SCS組中，Kaiso的過表達導致鎮痛效果的下降，並上調促炎細胞因子和P2X7R的表達，這些都是可以導致疼痛的因素並引起M1小膠質細胞極化。另一方面，P2X7R的下調在不影響Kaiso表達的情況下延長了Con SCS的鎮痛作用。基於這些數據，我們假設1)Kaiso-P2X7R- M1/M2小膠質細胞極化是驅動神經性疼痛炎症反應的關鍵調節軸，2)HF10 SCS通過特異性降低Kaiso-P2X7R- M1/M2小膠質細胞極化軸的作用，表現出比Con SCS更好的鎮痛效果。在本研究中，我們將通過以下方法來驗證這些假設:1)闡明Kaiso在疼痛發病機制中的作用，2)確認Kaiso和P2X7R在疼痛發病機制中的調節關係，3)理解SCS中的分子和細胞的改變。我們的研究將揭示HF10 SCS和Con SCS抑制傷害性信號傳遞的不同分子機制。本研究將為採用神經調節療法治療慢性疼痛患者提供臨床依據和指導。

17116621.label: Major findings and research outcome
17116621.value: Neuropathic pain poses a persistent challenge in clinical management. Neuromodulation has emerged as a last-resort therapy. Conventional spinal cord stimulation (Con SCS) often causes abnormal sensations and provides short analgesia, whereas high-frequency spinal cord stimulation (HF SCS) is a newer therapy that effectively alleviates pain without paresthesia. However, the modes of action of 10kHz HF SCS (HF10 SCS) in pain relief remain unclear. To bridge this knowledge gap, we employed preclinical models that mimic certain features of clinical SCS to explore the underlying mechanisms of HF10 SCS. Addressing these issues would provide the scientific basis for improving and evaluating the effectiveness, reliability, and practicality of different frequency SCS in clinical settings. We found that HF10 SCS significantly reduces immune responses in the SDH by inactivating the Kaiso-P2X7R pathological axis in microglia, promoting long-lasting pain relief. Targeting Kaiso-P2X7R in microglia dramatically improved efficacy of Con SCS treatment, leading to reduced neuroinflammation and long-lasting pain relief. HF10 SCS could improve the immunopathologic state in the SDH, extending its benefits beyond symptom relief. Targeting the Kaiso-P2X7R axis may enhance Con SCS therapy and offer a new strategy for pain management.

17117221.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17117221.value: Coral reefs are rapidly degrading as global warming drives more frequent and more severe mass bleaching events. These events result from the breakdown in the nutritional symbiosis between corals and diverse group of microalgae, the symbiodinians. Among the symbiodinians, the highly productive but thermally sensitive species which have underpinned the success of modern reefs are no longer ecologically favourable. Corals are under pressure to associate with the best partners in a warming world. Evolutionary theory suggests that while the emergence of new, stable host-symbiont combinations may be rare events, they result in rapid adaptations when they occur. The rarity of new stable associations may be explained by the complexity of ecological interactions involved in symbiont turnover. In the midst of ocean warming - the logical presumption is that coral survival will depend on associations with more thermally tolerant symbiodinians. Yet, thermal tolerance is just one of many physiological attributes inherent to the diversity of symbiodinians, a result of millions of years of competition and niche partitioning. In previous work (GRF RGC Ref No.e00700, 2013) we demonstrated that symbiodinian species grown in culture drastically altered their metabolism in response to competition, with thermally tolerant symbiodinians shown to be poor competitors. Therefore the ability of a coral to establish novel, and beneficial symbioses may depend on the hosts ability to regulate interactions among symbiodinians in hospite. Here we propose to use stable isotope tracing to examine the quantity and quality of nutrient cycling within the coral holobiont associated with either a thermally sensitive (C1), thermally tolerant (D), or mixed (C1+D) community of symbionts. We will trace nutrients through both “bottom-up” (inorganic nutrients taken up by symbionts and passed to host) and “top-down” (heterotrophic nutrients taken up by corals and passed to symbionts) processes to understand symbiont competition and host control, respectively. Our goal is to untangle the complex network of metabolic interactions among corals and their symbionts that may determine the fate of corals in the Anthropocene. If the rate of global change continues to outpace corals’ ability to adapt, “assisted evolution” strategies that promote symbiont turnover will require a thorough understanding of the ecological mechanisms that maintain functional symbioses. 全球暖化令大規模的珊瑚白化越發頻繁和嚴重，導致世界各地的珊瑚礁急速退化。珊瑚白化是珊瑚和多種微藻類（也就是珊瑚的共生體）的共生關係無法維持而造成的後果。在這些共生藻類中，有些物種的生產力很高，令珊瑚礁成為重要的生態系統。可是，它們亦對溫度轉變非常敏感，以致於在變暖的海裏，它們失去了生態上的優勢。珊瑚要維持與他們的共生關係，也要承受着巨大的壓力。而要在短時間內重新產生宿主與共生體的穩定組合，在進化論上來說是非常罕見的，因為物種需要快速的適應環境。 為何穩定的共生關係那樣罕見？其中一個解釋可能是共生體的轉換所牽涉到的複雜生態互動。因為海洋暖化，我們可以合理假設珊瑚與更耐熱的藻類共生會增加生存機率。但是，幾百萬年的生態競爭和生態位劃分令這些共生藻類的多樣性非常高，耐熱能力只是其中一項有利生存的條件。我們之前的研究（GRF RGC Ref No.e00700, 2013）以實驗室培養的共生藻證明，它們會因為競爭而急劇改變自身的新陳代謝。我們亦發現耐熱能力較高的共生藻為較弱的競爭者。因此，珊瑚要建立全新和有利的共生關係，有可能取決於宿主調節體內不同共生藻的互動的能力。 珊瑚共生總體內，有三種不同的共生體組合分類，分別為耐熱能力較低的C1分支，耐熱能力較高的D分支，或兩者混合的C1+D分支。我們建議使用穩定同位素分析來檢查這些分支的營養循環數量和質量，並以「由下而上」和「由上而下」的步驟來追蹤它們。前者以觀察共生藻吸收無機營養物並分享予宿主的過程去研究共生藻的競爭，後者則以觀察珊瑚吸收異養營養物並分享予共生藻的過程去研究宿主的控制。我們的目標是去理解珊瑚和共生體的複雜新陳代謝互動，因為這可能是決定珊瑚在人類世的命運的重要因素。如果全球改變的速度一直比珊瑚的適應能力轉變來得快， 我們便要更加透徹理解維持有效共生關係的生態機制，才能以「輔助進化」的策略去推動共生體的轉變。

17117221.label: Realisation of objectives
17117221.value: Objective 1 A large-scale experiment was undertaken at the Swire Institute of Marine Science. We sought to investigate how nutrient sharing differed between corals hosting different symbiont types, particulary for corals hosting a mixture of symbiont species. To achieve this, colonies of the hard coral Galaxea fascicularis were collected by scuba divers from Crescent Island, Hong Kong, and maintained in the aquarium facility at SWIMS. After acclimation to the aquarium conditions, the corals were “bleached” using an 8 day treatment with menthol solution to which causes dissociation with their original symbionts. We used visual confirmation by microscopy and imaging PAM analysis to confirm the absence of symbionts and their photosynthetic activity. The aposymbiotic coral were then split into two temperature treatments (ambient 26ºC and heat 29ºC) and among tanks each inoculated with one of three symbiont treatments: Durusdinium trenchii, Cladocopium goreaui or a combination of both symbiont species in a “mixed” treatment. These symbionts were obtained from the Australian Institute of Marine Science, and grown in culture, to ensure sufficient quantities. Literature and pilot studies had shown both of these symbionts to be taken up by Galaxea fascicularis, but our corals had an exceeding preference for Cladocopium sp. Symbionts. To attempt to overcome this host bias, the mixed species treatment included symbionts at a ratio of 90:10 D. trenchii: C. goreaui. Corals were inoculated with symbionts three times a week, for approximately seven weeks. During this time we also sampled corals for transcriptome analysis (n=4 corals per treatment at week 1, 3, 5, and 7). Weekly monitoring of symbiont ratios within the corals was conducted with species specific FISH labelling and analysis on the flow cytometer, to determine when a near even ratio of both species was present in the mixed treatment. This occurred relatively early in the experiment at ~ 5 weeks post bleaching. At this point symbionts were present at a 60:40 ratio, yet the corals were still visibly pale - a clear sign of low symbiont numbers which would not be sufficient for subsequent nutrient analyses (McIlroy et al., 2022). As such we extended inoculations for an additional two weeks. Unfortunately, the dynamics of symbiont communities are such that they can change very rapidly. During that two week period, the corals become completely dominated by Cladocopium sp. symbionts (~95% of total symbiont cells). Subsequent analysis by metabarcoding the ITS2 region of coral symbionts revealed that the Cladocopium sp. was not the cultured species we had been inoculating with (C. goreaui), but the native species of Cladocopium that is present with the majority of Hong Kong corals, including G. fasicularis sampled from Crescent Island. Furthermore, this transition to type C1a occurred in the D trenchii inoculated corals as well. This finding suggests that Hong Kong G. fasicularis show an extreme preference for their native symbiont type, even under different temperatures and laboratory conditions, despite the fact that many Galaxea populations are dominated by symbionts within the Durusdinium genus (Tong et al. 2017). In previous studies on symbiont uptake in coral larvae have shown that the host transcriptome is massively altered when corals are inoculated by treatment with non-native symbionts (Voolstra et al. 2009). Transcriptomic analysis of corals sampled throughout this experiment should provide more insight into the regulatory mechanisms of symbiont diversity. Currently, RNA from all samples has been extracted and sequences, with comparative analyses ongoing. Objective 2: Despite the symbiont communities being more homogenized to the native symbiont type than expected, we proceeded in carrying out the stable isotope tracer experiment once visible infection was present, i.e., 8 weeks after bleaching. Visible infection is required for obtaining the necessary biomass to measure nutrient assimilation (McIlroy et al. 2022). While not the initial objective of the proposed research, this experiment is unique in tracing nutrient exchange both from symbionts to corals as well as corals to symbionts during bleaching recovery and under different temperatures. For “bottom-up” nutrient transfer, corals were exposed to isotopically-enriched inorganic nutrients, sodium nitrate and sodium bicarbonate, that only the symbionts could utilize. For “top-down” nutrient transfer corals were fed isotopically-enriched brine shrimp (A. salina), that only the host could consume. Following 10 hour exposure to one of the nutrient sources, corals were sampled, rinse with DI water and frozen. Corals were thawed and their tissues removed from the skeleton and homogenized to release symbionts. A series of washing and centrifugation steps were used to separate host and symbiont tissues which were freeze dried and weighed for subsequent stable isotope analysis. Results indicate that recovery temperature had a strong effect on the assimilation of inorganic nutrients within the bottom-up tracer experiment but not in the assimilation of heterotrophic sources of nutrients in the top-down tracer experiment. This supports the theory that algal symbionts tend to be the more sensitive of the two partners to temperature stress (Putnam et al. 2017), but is somewhat counter to our expectation that increased coral feeding can potentially supplement the loss of symbiont derived nutrient sources during bleaching and recovery (Conti-Jerpe et al., 2020). It’s possible that, given both treatments were still in a bleaching recovery period, maximum feeding efficiency occurred in both treatments so that further increases within the heat treatment was not possible. The ratio of carbon to nitrogen can also be used to understand coral nutritional state (Fujii et al. 2020) and in this case revealed that both coral treatments were well below the expected C:N ratio of healthy corals (~7), which is not surprising during bleaching recovery. However, C:N ratios of the heat treatment were slightly lower for both corals and symbiont tissues suggesting that despite recovery, these corals were not recovering as well as those at lower temperatures. Further examination with compound specific stable isotope analysis, which is ongoing will provide further insight into how nutrient exchange within the symbiosis impacts bleaching recovery. Project Challenges and Under-Achievements The project faced significant challenges and delays due to the COVID-19 pandemic. During this time workflows were disrupted which impacted access, to aquarium facilities as well as the Flow Cytometer for sample analyses. There are some aspects of the project which are not yet completed including the compound specific stable isotope analysis and supplemental transcriptomic analysis. The PI and HKU Ph.D. student continue to pursue these results which will be included in a Ph.D. thesis submitted end of year 2024, and in at least one additional peer-reviewed publication submitted in 2025. The experimental conditions did not produce the expected treatments of variable symbiont communities. Despite positive results in initial trials and in collaborative work (McIlroy et al. 2022; Puntin et al. 2023) the corals collected in Hong Kong showed a strong preference over time to native strains. This greatly altered the outcomes and interpretations of our data. However, the pivot to understanding the role of nutrients in bleaching recovery provides are still novel and insightful. Furthermore, our supplemental transcriptomic analysis which was conducted throughout the infection period and covers the transition from non-native to native types is also a considerable contribution to understanding the mechanisms that corals may use to regulate the structure of coral symbiont communities.

17117221.label: Major findings and research outcome
17117221.value: Our research herein examined the process of bleaching recovery in the coral Galaxea fascicularis. We showed that these corals can be bleached using the menthol technique and reinfected with non-native cultures of Symbiodiniaceae (Puntin et al. 2023). This pilot work and an ongoing project on the coral Briareum asbestinum were used to establish methods and provide early insights into how the relative and absolute abundance of associated coral symbionts impact nutrient sharing (McIlroy et al. 2022). However, despite documented symbiont flexibility in G. fasicularis populations throughout the South China Sea, corals in this experiment demonstrated a strong affinity to eventually recover their native symbiont types. While not the initial focus of this study, we sampled through the reinfection process to examine the transcriptomic response of coral hosts and their symbionts during bleaching recovery. Ongoing analysis of those samples will help to understand host regulation of symbiont communities and identify genes may be responsible for symbiont turnover. Using a stable isotope tracer experiment we further explored the role of nutrient sharing among corals and their algal symbionts in the post bleaching recovery period. In this case, the recovery temperature had a strong effect on the ability of symbionts to assimilate both carbon and nitrogen which also resulted in less carbon and nitrogen passed to their hosts. On the other hand, the assimilation and sharing of heterotrophic nutrient sources was not sensitive to recovery temperature. This suggests that, for G. fascicularis, supplemental feeding by the host may not be sufficient to make up for the stress induced losses of nutrients provided by their symbionts. Subsequent compound-specific stable isotope analysis will further explore how the forms of nutrients assimilated and shared between corals and their symbionts varies during bleaching recovery at increased versus ambient temperatures.

17117221.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17117221.value: The biological and ecological factors that shape the coral microbiome will have critical influences on the fate of coral reefs under climate change. A growing area of research is focused on the experimental manipulation of the coral microbiome as a means of increasing heat tolerance. The regulatory mechanisms of host corals in controlling symbiont communities is an important factor to consider. Given the results of our study, there are many avenues for further development. For example, our coral samples were taken from a population of corals in Hong Kong, a habitat in which a single symbiont type dominates almost all coral species. To further our understanding of a coral's affinity for a specific symbiont, and flexibility in bleached adult corals, it would be helpful to repeat this experiment with Galaxea corals from other locations, where they are recorded to host multiple species across one habitat. Furthermore, the transcriptomics results of this study will give insight into signalling and immune responses of corals exposed to different types of symbionts. This will help us to understand whether the corals responded with hostility to the new symbiont types from the beginning, or if they were initially welcoming, to help "bridge the gap" of recovery before their initial symbionts regained a foothold. This information will be vital to structure future experiments.

17117221.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17117221.value: As our climate continues to change, coral reefs face unprecedented stress that causes the corals themselves to bleach, and die, wiping out important underwater habitats. In our research, we wanted to understand what we can do to help these corals adapt and survive this increasing environmental stress. Not unlike our human gut microbiome, corals host a diverse community of tiny organisms or "symbionts" that aid in their nutrition and health. Our goal was to provide foundational research for understanding what factors regulate the identity and abundance of different symbiont types. This is critical for conservation methods that seek to manipulate the coral symbiont community to include more climate-proof members. Our results suggest that initial flexibility in symbionts for our Hong Kong corals was short-lived and eventually corals re-associated with their native types. Conservation via symbiont manipulation remains a promising endeavour with many ways of overcoming this limitation.

17118421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17118421.value: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a disease featuring muscle weakness and atrophy due to the progressive degeneration of motor neurons. Advances in genome sequencing and data analysis have revealed the genetic variants associated with ALS. Besides causing a broad spectrum of neurotoxicity, it is well known that ALS-related mutations have common effects on not only the microtubule polymerization dynamics but also the cargo transport in motor neurons. In particular, pharmacological stabilization of microtubules delays the disease onset and extends the lifespan in ALS mouse models. The identification of ALS-related mutations in α4A-tubulin indicates that this microtubule component protein has properties critical for understanding how the cytoskeletal filaments become the convergence site of ALS pathogenesis. However, the mechanism by which ALS-related mutations in α4A-tubulin impact microtubule organization is currently unclear. The human genome encodes at least nine α- and ten β-tubulin families (i.e., isotypes) that show cell-type-specific protein expression profiles. In particular, the expression of α4A-tubulin increases from a neglectable level at the early stages of brain development to a significant amount in mature neurons. The expression profile of α4A-tubulin suggests that this α-tubulin isotype confers microtubules the essential properties for maintaining the cytoskeletal filaments’ functions and organization in mature neurons. However, due to the decades-long challenge of generating recombinant human tubulin, how α4A-tubulin regulates microtubule properties remains elusive. To overcome this challenge, we have developed a state-of-the-art strategy for generating a good quantity of recombinant tubulin with any isotype of interest. With preliminary data indicating that α4A-tubulin increases the microtubule stability, we are well-positioned to start dissecting the unique roles of α4A-tubulin on the microtubule intrinsic properties, which are critical in motor neurons and the adult-onset ALS pathogenesis. α4A-tubulin, which lacks the C-terminal tyrosine residue encoded in most α-tubulin isotypes, is highly conserved across different species, suggesting critical biological functions of ‘detyrosinated’ α4A-tubulin. In neurons, detyrosination is an α-tubulin post-translational modification (PTM) that marks the stabilized microtubules and guilds cargo transport. However, the roles of ‘detyrosinated’ α4A-tubulin regulating microtubule stability and microtubule-associated proteins’ binding remain unknown. With combinatorial approaches involving protein biochemistry, chemical biology, cell biology, and single-molecule fluorescence microscopy, we will dissect the effects of wild-type and mutant α4A-tubulin on microtubule polymerization dynamics and cargo transport. Our study will not only reveal the molecular mechanism by which α4A-tubulin regulates microtubule network, but also provide general guidelines for dissecting the integrated effects of PTMs and tubulin isotypes on microtubule properties. 肌萎缩性脊髓侧索硬化症(ALS)患者症狀為由運動神經元退化所引起的肌肉無力及萎縮。基因體定序及分析揭露了許多與ALS高度相關的遺傳變異。除了造成廣域的神經毒性之外，這些遺傳變異常見的影響包括導致運動神經元中的微管(microtubules)的聚合動態及細胞內運輸的缺陷。在小鼠模型中發現，以小分子藥物穩定微管有助於延遲ALS的疾病進程並延長個體的壽命。在α4A微管蛋白上發現與ALS相關的點突變不僅確認了微管在ALS疾病進程中扮演的重要角色，且為解析微管與ALS致病機轉的關係提供了新的研究方向。然而，目前仍不瞭解這些α4A微管蛋白上的點突變是如何影響微管的性質與架構。 α/β微管蛋白(α/β-tubulin)聚合形成中空圓柱絲狀的微管。在人類基因體中存在至少九種α微管蛋白及十種β微管蛋白同種型(isotype)，且各個微管蛋白同種型具有其特徵的蛋白質表達譜。相對於在腦部神經發育的早期階段α4A微管蛋白微乎其微的表達量，成熟神經細胞中具有顯著的α4A微管蛋白表達量。這個特徵的蛋白質表達譜暗示了α4A微管蛋白具有獨特的性質而能賦予維持成熟神經細胞功能及型態所需的微管架構。然而，由於取得重組人類微管蛋白上的困難所導致的生物物理及生物化學實驗上的限制，目前對於α4A微管蛋白的性質仍然缺乏瞭解。我們發展出了一個方法可以得到高度純化的任意微管蛋白同種型。藉由純化的重組人類α4A 微管蛋白，我們初步的結果顯示α4A微管蛋白可以增加微管的穩定度。以此為基礎，我們將解析α4A微管蛋白是如何藉由調控微管的性質並在成年發病的ALS致病機轉中扮演重要角色。 與其他α微管蛋白同種型相比，α4A 微管蛋白缺乏在羧基端的酪氨酸。 這個演化上高度保守的特徵暗示去酪氨酸的α4A 微管蛋白扮演關鍵的生物功能。在神經細胞中，α微管蛋白上的去酪氨酸轉譯後修飾不僅標記在細胞中穩定的微管並為指引胞內運輸提供了定位的訊號。然而，目前仍不清楚去酪氨酸的α4A 微管蛋白是如何調控微管的穩定度以及與其他微管作用蛋白(microtubule-associated proteins)的結合。藉由整合蛋白質生物化學、化學生物學、細胞生物學與單分子螢光顯微鏡，我們將研究α4A 微管蛋白上與ALS相關的點突變是如何影響微管聚合的動力學特性以及基於微管的胞器運輸。此研究計畫不僅會揭露α4A 微管蛋白調控微管架構的分子機制，亦為往後解析微管蛋白同種型與不同轉譯後修飾對微管性質的綜合效應提供了一個可依循的準則。

17118621.value: 人類冠狀病毒通過激活Notch信號通路以增強病毒複製

17118621.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17118621.value: Dr Chan, Jasper Fuk Woo Dr Shuai, Huiping Prof Yuen, Kwok Yung

17118621.label: Project Objectives
17118621.value: Objective 1: To characterize the basic biology of Notching signaling in the context of SARS-CoV-2 infection. Extending from our pilot studies on the identification of Notch signaling as a novel pathway for efficient SARS-CoV-2 replication, we aim to thoroughly dissect the role of Notch signaling on SARS-CoV-2 infection in this proposal. In Objective 1, we first seek to understand the fundamental biology of Notch signaling in the context of SARS-CoV-2 infection. (A) First, we will evaluate the expression of Notch signaling components in SARS-CoV-2 susceptible cells before and after SARS-CoV-2 infection. (B) Second, we will investigate the expression and distribution profile of Notch signaling components in human lung tissues. (C) Third, we will explore the expression of Notch signaling components in other SARS-CoV-2-relevant extrapulmonary tissues. Objective 2: To evaluate the physiological impact of inhibiting Notch signaling in in vitro, ex vivo, and in vivo models. Based on the knowledge obtained from Objective 1, we will have a more systemic grasp on the basic biology of Notch signaling relevant to SARS-CoV-2 infection. In Objective 2, we will thoroughly investigate the modulatory effect of Notch signaling on SARS-CoV-2 infection on multiple dimensions. (A) First, we will investigate the impact of inhibiting Notch signaling on SARS-CoV-2 replication in in vitro and ex vivo models. (B) Second, we will investigate the impact of Notch signaling inhibition on SARS-CoV-2 pathogenesis in golden hamster and hACE2 transgenic mouse models. (C) Third, we will evaluate the impact of Notch signaling inhibition on the pathogenesis of other highly pathogenic human coronaviruses including MERS-CoV and SARS-CoV. Objective 3: To investigate the mechanism of how Notch signaling potentiates SARS-CoV-2 replication. Extending from our findings from Objective 1 and 2, we next plan to investigate the mechanism of how Notch signaling potentiates SARS-CoV-2 replication in Objective 3. (A) First, we will investigate if FURIN is responsible for Notch signaling-mediated SARS-CoV-2 replication. (i) To evaluate this possibility, we will determine the expression level of FURIN in the presence of Notch inhibition. (ii) Next, we will evaluate if Notch inhibition will have an impact on SARS-CoV-2 spike cleavage. (iii) In addition, we will check if Notch inhibition will limit SARS-CoV-2 entry. (B) Second, we will investigate if other Notch effectors contribute to Notch signaling-mediated SARS-CoV-2 replication. (i) We will perform gain-of-function and loss-of-function assays on HES and HEY members on their capacity of modulating SARS-CoV-2. (ii) Upon identifying the specific HES and HEY members that could modulate SARS-CoV-2 replication, the underlying mechanism will be further explored.

17118621.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17118621.value: Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) was first reported from Wuhan, China in December 2019. The virus primarily infects the respiratory tract with clinical manifestations largely resemble those of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus (SARS-CoV) and Middle East respiratory syndrome coronavirus (MERS-CoV). However, SARS-CoV-2 has demonstrated an unusually high infectability and transmissibility among the human populations. As of October 2020, SARS-CoV-2 has resulted in over 40 million infections with more than 1 million deaths. The rapid spread of the pandemic triggered an unprecedented level of global research effort on SARS-CoV-2. Despite these extensive research efforts, currently an effective vaccine remains unavailable and treatment options are limited with suboptimal effectiveness in clinical trials. In this regard, understanding the basic biology of SARS-CoV-2 is urgently demanded to enable the design of more specific and effective antiviral strategy against the infection of this pandemic virus. In the preparation stage of this proposal, we performed RNAseq on SARS-CoV-2-infected human lung epithelial cells, Calu3. By analyzing the differentially expressed genes and the perturbed host pathways from the transcriptomic profile, our data revealed Notch signaling as a novel host pathway upregulated by SARS-CoV-2 infection. In subsequent pilot studies, we demonstrated that Notch signaling is essential for SARS-CoV-2 replication in vitro and ex vivo. At the same time, infection of SARS-CoV and MERS-CoV similarly upregulated Notch signaling in Calu3 cells and inhibition of Notch signaling with a specific small molecule inhibitor potently inhibited the replication of SARS-CoV and MERS-CoV in addition to SARS-CoV-2. These findings indicated that the Notch signaling pathway is essential for the replication of human pathogenic coronaviruses. In the current proposal, we aim to further investigate the mechanism of Notch-regulated SARS-CoV-2 replication and investigate the potential of Notch inhibition as a novel antiviral strategy against the infection of SARS-CoV-2 and other human pathogenic coronaviruses including SARS-CoV and MERS-CoV. Overall, our study will reveal novel mechanistic insight on the biology of SARS-CoV-2 pathogenesis and provide new targets for therapeutic intervention on SARS-CoV-2 as well as other human pathogenic coronaviruses. 嚴重急性呼吸系統綜合症冠狀病毒2(新冠病毒)於2019年12月被首次報導。該病毒主要感染呼吸道，臨床表現與嚴重急性呼吸系統綜合症冠狀病毒(SARS病毒)和中東呼吸綜合徵冠狀病毒 (MERS病毒)相類似。然而，新冠病毒在人群中表現出異常高的傳染性和傳播性。截至2020年10月，新冠病毒已導致超過4000萬人感染，超過100萬人死亡。新冠病毒的迅速蔓延引發了全球前所未有的針對新冠病毒的研究工作。儘管進行了廣泛的研究工作，目前仍然未有獲得有效的疫苗，並且藥物治療手段有限，臨床試驗效果欠佳。基於這些原因，我們迫切需要了解新冠病毒的基本生物學特性，以便設計出更具體、更有效的抗病毒策略來對抗這個病毒的感染及傳播。 在本提案的準備階段，我們對感染了新冠病毒的人肺上皮細胞Calu3進行了RNA測序（RNAseq）。通過分析轉錄組中的差異表達基因和受干擾的宿主信號通路，我們的數據揭示了Notch信號通路是一個受新冠病毒感染調控的宿主通路。在隨後的研究中，我們證明了Notch信號通路對於新冠病毒的體外和體外複製至關重要。同時，我們發現SARS病毒和MERS病毒感染同樣上調Calu3細胞中的Notch信號通路。並且，用特定的小分子抑製劑抑制Notch信號傳導可有效抑制 SARS病毒，MERS病毒，及新冠病毒的複制。這些發現表明Notch信號通路對於這些高致性病冠狀病毒的複制至關重要。在目前的提案中，我們旨在進一步研究Notch通路調節新冠病毒複製的機制，並研究抑製Notch作為一種新型抗冠狀病毒策略的潛力，以對抗新冠病毒和其他高致病性冠狀病毒的感染。總體而言，我們的研究將揭示新冠病毒發病的新機制，並為新冠病毒以及其他高致病性冠狀病毒的治療干預提供新的靶點。

17119021.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17119021.value: Schizotypy is a latent personality organization reflecting a putative liability for schizophrenia spectrum disorders. Schizotypy is a useful construct for investigating personality-psychopathy interaction, and a dynamic neurodevelopmental model for understanding the pathogenesis of psychosis. Although the majority is not expected to evolve into psychosis, schizotypal individuals exhibit a wide range of behavioral and cognitive impairments. The literature on schizotypy has several notable limitations. First, few previous studies have investigated the influence of psychopathology, stress, interpersonal and social support on the manifestations of schizotypal traits in epidemiological samples. Second, though empirical evidence supports the notion that schizotypy is a construct with both trait and state manifestations, previous studies seldom utilize epidemiological samples to track the naturistic fluctuations of schizotypal traits. Third, the cognitive trajectories of schizotypy remain unclear. This research aims to address these unresolved issues. In Phase I, we will apply network analysis to investigate the inter-relations between schizotypal traits, prodromal psychosis, psychopathology, stress, functioning and interpersonal and social support in 2000 “epidemiologically representative” local youth subjects. We will collect one-year longitudinal data on the fluctuations of schizotypal traits in the Phase I cohort, and delineate the latent subtypes of schizotypy, based on trajectories of schizotypal traits. In Phase II, we will identify 100 subjects in the original cohort who exhibit high levels of schizotypal traits and 100 subjects with low levels of schizotypal traits (based on the top tenth percentile and below-mean ratings on a schizotypy measure), and comprehensively assess their cognitive abilities (including motivation, empathy, attention, semantic and motor inhibition), using well-validated behavioral paradigms. We will compare the baseline cognitive performances of the 100 high- and 100 low-schizotypal groups with 50 patients with first-episode schizophrenia. We will collect one-year longitudinal data on the cognitive trajectories in the high- and low-schizotypal groups. This research presents a unique opportunity to explore risk and resilience factors for schizotypal traits and prodromal psychosis in a local epidemiological youth sample. Our results will also advance our understandings on cognitive impairments and its evolution in young people with high levels of schizotypy. Our findings are expected to have potential implications for early interventions and possible cognitive remediation to schizotypal youth with cognitive and functional impairments. 精神分裂型人格被構想為一個性格結構，反映演化成精神分裂譜系疾病的傾向及風險。精神分裂型人格有用於研究性格與精神疾病表徵的相互關係，也是研究腦神經發展模型一個典範。大多數帶有精神分裂型人格的人士都不會演化成為思覺失調，但此風險群組已知有着廣泛的行為與認知功能缺損。過去研究精神分裂型人格的文獻有幾項重要局限。首先 ，過去鮮有探討精神病徵，環境壓力，人際及社交支援等等對精神分裂型人格的影響。其次，精神分裂型人格已知帶有特徵及狀態兩種特質，但過往文獻鮮有使用流行病學代表性的樣本，以闡明此特徵的自然發展。再者，有關精神分裂型人格的認知功能發展軌跡之文獻尚未清晰。有見及此，本研究旨在化解以上問題。 本研究第一階段，我們採用網絡分析，研究精神分裂型人格，思覺過敏，早期思覺失調病徵，環境壓力，人際及社交支援，和功能之相互關係。我們將收集二千名有流行病學代表性的本地年青人為樣本。並對其觀察跟進一年，以了解精神分裂型人格的自然發展及演化。帶有不同高低程度的精神分裂型人格的樣本，其自然發展及演化，可反映精神分裂型人格的潛在種類。 本研究第二階段，我們由首階段之2000名樣本中，選出100名帶有高程度精神分裂型人格的被試，及另外100名帶有低程度精神分裂型人格的被試。我們詳細評估他們的認知功能，包括動機，心靈理論，專注力，及執行功能等等。此外我們也收集50名首發精神分裂症患者的認知功能，以作對比。我們會追蹤三組被試的一年數據，以了解其認知功能發展軌跡。 本研究借助一項年青人口普查樣本之便，提供一個解精神分裂型人格的機會。本研究有助了解精神分裂型人格及思覺失調的風險因子及保護因子。研究結果將加深我們對高程度精神分裂型人格此一高危群組之了解，並對思覺失調早期干預，預防醫療，認知功能訓練的各種治療手法有指導作用。

17119421.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17119421.value: GEN1处理复制和重组中间产物的调节机制如何确保基因组稳定性

17119421.label: Project Objectives
17119421.value: GEN1 belongs to a highly specialised group of endonucleases that is capable of cleaving Holliday junctions (HJs) into two disconnected DNA duplexes in a reaction known as HJ resolution. The N-terminus of GEN1 possesses enzymatic activity, while its C-terminus has not been studied to much detail. Our pilot data has shown that the C-terminus of GEN1 is essential for its resolution function in the cellular context. We hypothesise that the C-terminus of GEN1 serves as an acceptor for post-translational modifications that regulate the interaction between GEN1 and chromatin. Therefore, we will precisely map the critical region in the C-terminus that is essential for cellular functions of GEN1 by complementing GEN1-/- knockout cells with various GEN1 truncations. Furthermore, we will map the ubiquitin acceptor sites in the C-terminus of GEN1 and identify the ubiquitin E3 ligase. Our work will provide the first study of how post-translational modifications of GEN1 in its C-terminal tail regulate GEN1 functions in the chromatin context. GEN1 is capable of cleaving replication fork and flap structures in vitro, suggesting that it may also be able to process late replication intermediates in vivo. We hypothesise that GEN1 has a resolution-independent role in processing un-replicated DNA in common fragile sites (CFSs) to disconnect the sister chromatids. To test this hypothesis, we will investigate the phenotypes of GEN1-/- knockout cells in response to aphidicolin treatment that induces replication stress. We will measure the number of CFS-associated ultrafine anaphase bridges (UFBs) and mitotic DNA synthesis in GEN1-/- knockout and wild-type cells upon aphidicolin treatment. We will also investigate if the C-terminal tail of GEN1 is required for its recruitment to the un-replicated DNA regions in mitotic chromosomes. We hypothesise that GEN1 would preferentially bind to common fragile sites and other genomic loci that are prone to replication-induced DNA damage. To have a genome-wide understanding of the GEN1-DNA interaction upon replication stress, we will treat cells with aphidicolin followed by synchronisation in mitosis, and then identify the GEN1-associated genomic loci by chromatin immunoprecipitation of GEN1-GFP followed by sequencing (ChIP-Seq). We will compare the identified sites with the previously known fragile sites in published database. The identified sites will also be verified by ChIP-qPCR and FISH. Overall, we believe that the identification of GEN1-associated genomic loci under the condition of replication stress will reveal the precise mechanisms of genome instability induced by replication stress and the role of GEN1 in preventing such instability.

17119421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17119421.value: Sister chromatids can be covalently linked by Holliday junctions (HJs) formed as intermediates during the recombinational repair of DNA breaks, or by un-replicated DNA at common fragile sites (CFSs) upon replication stress, leading to the formation of DNA joint molecules (JMs). If not timely resolved, JMs can lead to chromosome segregation defects that are commonly observed in various cancer cells. Therefore, nucleolytic processing of JMs by structure-selective endonucleases (SSEs) is essential for promoting proper cell division. Human GEN1 belongs to a highly specialised group of SSEs that is capable of cleaving HJs into two disconnected DNA duplexes in a reaction known as HJ resolution. Although the biochemical activity of GEN1 is well-studied, how it is regulated during the cell cycle is unclear. Moreover, recombinant GEN1 protein cleaves replication fork-like substrates readily in vitro, but whether GEN1 plays a role in processing replication intermediates in vivo remains to be determined. Our pilot data has shown that although the N-terminal half of GEN1 displays the same biochemical activity as the full-length protein, the very C-terminus of GEN1 plays important regulatory roles in the cellular context. Meanwhile, we find out that GEN1 has a HJ resolution-independent role in processing replication intermediates induced by aphidicolin, an inhibitor of DNA polymerases. The aim of our project is to study the regulatory mechanisms of GEN1 and its functions in safeguarding DNA replication. Firstly, we will identify the critical region in the C-terminus of GEN1 that is essential for its resolution function in the cellular context, followed by the identification of post-translational modifications that are involved in the regulatory mechanism. Secondly, we hypothesise that GEN1 processes un-replicated DNA to allow mitotic DNA synthesis, thereby preventing chromosome missegregation. We will employ GEN1-/- knockout cell lines to study how they respond to aphidicolin treatment that induces replication stress. Finally, we plan to study the interaction between GEN1 and DNA by chromatin immunoprecipitation of GEN1-GFP followed by sequencing (ChIP-Seq). We hypothesise that GEN1 would preferentially bind to CFSs and other genomic loci that are prone to replication-induced DNA damage. Overall, our research will provide new mechanistic insights into how GEN1 promotes genome stability by processing various types of DNA intermediates to allow successful chromosome segregation. 姐妹染色單體可以通過Holliday連結體（Holliday junction, HJ）共價連接 （HJ是DNA斷裂重組修復過程中形成的中間產物），也可以在DNA 複製壓力下在公共脆性位點（CFSs）上形成連接，從而產生DNA連接分子（joint molecules, JMs）。如果不及時解決，JMs可能導致染色體分離缺陷，這在各種癌細胞中常見。因此，通過結構選擇內切酶（structure-selective endonucleases, SSEs）對JMs進行核溶解處理對於促進細胞正常分裂至關重要。人類GEN1屬於一個高度專業化的SSE蛋白，能夠將HJ分解為兩個斷開的DNA雙鏈體（又稱為HJ分解反應）。儘管GEN1的生物化學活性已經得到了很好的研究，但我們對於它在細胞週期中是如何被調節還不清楚。此外，重組GEN1蛋白在試管內很容易切割複製叉，但GEN1是否在細胞內處理複製中間體仍有待確定。我們的初步數據表明，儘管GEN1的N端半部分顯示出與全長蛋白質相同的生物化學活性，但GEN1的C端在細胞環境中起著重要的調節作用。同時，我們發現GEN1在處理DNA聚合酶抑製劑aphidicolin誘導的複制中間產物方面具有作用。我們項目的目的是研究GEN1的調節機制及其在保護DNA複製中的功能。首先，我們將找出GEN1 C端的關鍵區域，然後確定其調控機制。其次，我們假設GEN1處理未復制的DNA，從而防止染色體錯分。我們將利用GEN1敲除細胞係來研究它們如何處理由aphidicolin誘導的複制中間產物。最後，我們計劃通過GEN1-GFP染色質免疫沉澱和高通量測序（ChIP-Seq）研究GEN1和DNA之間的相互作用。我們假設GEN1優先與CFSs和其他易於產生DNA損傷的位點結合。總括來說，我們的研究將為GEN1如何通過處理各種類型的DNA中間產物來促進染色體分離提供新的機制性見解。
