17119621.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17119621.value: We and others have identified the anti-tumour effects of berberine, a natural alkaloid from Chinese herbal medicine Coptis, in human hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Berberine suppresses HCC cell proliferation and migration, and inhibits in vivo tumour growth and metastasis. While combination of berberine with anti-cancer drugs was studied on various types of cancers, our pilot screening found that berberine in HCC had specificity in potentiating sorafenib and its chemical analogue regorafenib, the approved multityrosine kinase inhibitors for advanced HCC. Sorafenib resistance was observed in many HCC patients. It is, therefore, of great importance to explore the mechanisms and to develop individualized therapeutic strategies for coping with these problems. A recent in vitro study showed that berberine could increase HCC response to sorafenib; however, in vivo evidence remains scarce. We have established an in vivo-generated sorafenib-resistant (IVSR) HCC cells by continuously treating HCC tumour-bearing mice with sorafenib, which could well mimic cell-autonomous and non-cell-autonomous resistance compared to those resistant cells generated from in vitro selection. Our preliminary study showed that berberine improved sorafenib treatment in IVSR-HCC cells, as well as in orthotopic HCC-implanted mice model derived from these cells. The effect of berberine in reversing sorafenib resistance in HCC deserves a systematic investigation. Metabolic profiling of berberine-treated IVSR-HCC cells revealed that berberine negatively regulated metabolites related to Warburg effect, which was acquired in sorafenib-resistant cells as a metabolic adaptation that favours aerobic glycolysis. Berberine suppressed expression of glycolytic genes, and repressed Warburg effect in sorafenib-resistant cells, while this effect was insignificant in sorafenib-sensitive cells. Transcriptomic analysis and phospho-kinase array showed that glycolysis inhibition by berberine was associated with its regulation on hypoxia, apoptotic pathways, Mapk cascade and NF-κB signalling. Hypoxia-inducible factor-1α (HIF-1α) was downregulated by berberine in sorafenib-resistant cells without changing multidrug resistance proteins. Hence, we hypothesize that inhibition of Warburg effect and its associated signalling pathways play a pivotal role in mediating the effect of berberine to overcome sorafenib resistance of HCC. We propose (a) comprehensively investigate effects of berberine in overcoming in vitro and in vivo resistance of HCC cells to sorafenib, (b) determine the role of glycolysis inhibition in mediating the effect of berberine on sorafenib resistance in HCC, and (c) elucidate the upstream signal and downstream response of glycolysis inhibition by berberine in sorafenib-resistant HCC. Successful demonstration of this project will contribute to the development of berberine as a novel adjuvant therapy to overcome sorafenib resistance in HCC. 我們和其他人的研究已經表明小蘗鹼（一種來自中草藥黃連的天然生物鹼）在肝細胞癌 (HCC) 中的抗腫瘤作用。小蘗鹼抑制 HCC 細胞增殖和遷移，並抑制體內腫瘤生長和轉移。雖然小蘗鹼與抗癌藥物的組合用藥在各種腫瘤中均有報導，但我們的初步篩選發現，小蘗鹼在增強HCC對索拉非尼及其化學類似物瑞戈非尼（已批准用於晚期 HCC 的多酪氨酸激酶抑製劑）的敏感性上具有特異性。索拉非尼耐藥在很多HCC患者中很常見。因此，探索機制並製定個體化的治療策略來應對這些問題非常重要。最近的一項體外研究表明，小蘗鹼可以增加 HCC 對索拉非尼的響應；然而，體內證據仍然很少。我們在預實驗中建立了體內產生的索拉非尼抗性 (IVSR) HCC 細胞，與體外選擇產生的抗性細胞相比，它可以很好地模擬細胞自主和非細胞自主抗性。我們的初步研究表明，小蘗鹼改善了 IVSR-HCC 細胞以及源自這些細胞的原位 HCC小鼠模型中的索拉非尼響應。因此，小蘗鹼逆轉 HCC 索拉非尼耐藥中的作用值得系統研究。小蘗鹼處理的 IVSR-HCC 細胞的代謝分析顯示，小蘗鹼能夠負調節與 Warburg 效應相關的代謝物。Warburg效應是一種在索拉非尼耐藥細胞中普遍存在的有利於有氧糖酵解的代謝適應。小蘗鹼抑製糖酵解基因的表達，並抑制索拉非尼耐藥細胞中的 Warburg 效應，而小蘗鹼的這種作用在索拉非尼敏感細胞中不顯著。轉錄組學和磷酸激酶陣列分析表明，小蘗鹼對糖酵解的抑制與其對缺氧、凋亡途徑、Mapk和 NF-κB 信號傳導的調節有關。另外，小蘗鹼下調索拉非尼耐藥細胞中低氧誘導因子-1α (HIF-1α) ，而不改變多藥耐藥蛋白。因此，我們假設抑制 Warburg 效應及其相關信號通路在介導小蘗鹼克服 HCC 索拉非尼耐藥性的作用中起關鍵作用。我們將 (a) 系統研究小蘗鹼在克服 HCC 細胞對索拉非尼的體外和體內耐藥性中的作用，(b) 確定糖酵解抑制介導小蘗鹼對 HCC 索拉非尼耐藥性的影響中的作用，以及 (c) 闡明小蘗鹼抑制索拉非尼 HCC 糖酵解的上游信號和下游反應。該項目的成功完成將有助於開發小蘗鹼作為克服 HCC 索拉非尼耐藥性的新型輔助療法。

17119621.label: Realisation of objectives
17119621.value: Specific Aim 1 has been fully accomplished as planned. We successfully established multiple sorafenib-resistant HCC cell lines and demonstrated that berberine effectively suppressed resistance across diverse cell types, confirming that its effects are not cell-line specific. In vivo studies in orthotopic HCC mouse models identified optimal dosing and administration routes, with berberine significantly enhancing sorafenib efficacy. Mechanistic analyses revealed reduced glycolytic activity, downregulation of resistance-associated proteins, and modulation of tumour-associated macrophage phenotypes. Pharmacokinetic profiling further validated berberine’s safety and bioavailability. These findings match the anticipated outcomes, confirming berberine’s potential in overcoming sorafenib resistance in HCC. Specific Aim 2 has been fully achieved. Through comprehensive in vitro and in vivo experiments, we demonstrated that inhibition of glycolysis is a key mechanism by which berberine overcomes sorafenib resistance in HCC. Genetic and pharmacological reactivation of the Warburg effect reversed berberine’s suppression of tumour growth, restored Mapk and NF-κB signalling, and increased anti-apoptotic protein expression, confirming glycolytic inhibition as a central mediator. In orthotopic mouse models, glycolysis reactivation attenuated the combined therapeutic effects of berberine and sorafenib, while glycolysis inhibition enhanced tumour suppression. These findings fully align with anticipated outcomes, providing direct mechanistic evidence for the role of glycolysis inhibition in reversing sorafenib resistance. Specific Aim 3 has been fully achieved. Our studies revealed that glycolysis inhibition by berberine in sorafenib-resistant HCC is mediated upstream by phosphorylation-dependent degradation of HIF1α, driven by AMPKα activation. Restoration of stabilized HIF1α reversed berberine’s suppression of glycolysis and its downstream effects, confirming its role as a key upstream regulator. Mechanistic analyses demonstrated that reduced glycolysis and lactate production led to suppression of NF-κB activation, decreased IκB phosphorylation, and diminished nuclear translocation of NF-κB subunits. This, in turn, downregulated anti-apoptotic proteins Bcl-2 and Bcl-xL, contributing to restored sorafenib sensitivity. These results align with anticipated outcomes, elucidating both upstream and downstream signalling pathways of berberine’s action. All the proposed experiments have been conducted and research questions have been elaborated.

17119621.label: Major findings and research outcome
17119621.value: This project comprehensively investigated the role of berberine in overcoming sorafenib resistance in HCC, elucidating its mechanistic basis and therapeutic potential through integrated in vitro and in vivo approaches. We focused on establishing multiple sorafenib-resistant HCC cell lines and orthotopic mouse models to evaluate the efficacy of berberine. We successfully generated resistant lines from diverse HCC cell origins, confirming that berberine effectively suppressed resistance irrespective of cell-line specificity. Optimal dosing and routes of administration were defined, with berberine significantly enhancing sorafenib’s anti-tumour effects in vivo. Mechanistic studies revealed decreased glycolytic activity, reduced expression of resistance-associated proteins, and modulation of tumour-associated macrophage phenotypes. Pharmacokinetic profiling demonstrated favourable bioavailability and safety parameters. Also, we examined the role of glycolysis inhibition in mediating berberine’s effects. Using genetic and pharmacological approaches to re-activate the Warburg effect, we demonstrated that restored glycolysis reversed berberine’s tumour-suppressive activity and reinstated Mapk and NF‑κB signalling, as well as anti-apoptotic protein expression. In orthotopic models, glycolysis reactivation attenuated the combined effects of sorafenib and berberine, while glycolysis inhibition amplified tumour suppression. These findings confirmed glycolytic inhibition as a central mechanism underlying berberine’s reversal of sorafenib resistance. Finally, we elucidated upstream signals and downstream responses associated with glycolysis inhibition. We identified phosphorylation-dependent degradation of HIF1α, mediated by AMPKα activation, as the key upstream event leading to suppression of glycolytic gene expression. Restoration of stabilized HIF1α abrogated berberine’s effects on glycolysis and sorafenib sensitivity. Downstream, lactate reduction and glycolysis inhibition suppressed NF‑κB activation, decreased nuclear translocation of NF‑κB subunits, and reduced expression of anti-apoptotic proteins Bcl‑2 and Bcl‑xL. This dual-level regulation—upstream via HIF1α degradation and downstream via NF‑κB pathway suppression—fully explains berberine’s capacity to overcome sorafenib resistance. Overall, the research outcomes provide robust preclinical evidence that berberine is a potent adjunct to sorafenib therapy in HCC, acting through targeted metabolic reprogramming and signalling modulation. These findings lay the groundwork for translational studies and potential clinical application of berberine as a resistance‑modifying agent in advanced HCC.

17119621.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17119621.value: This study has provided compelling mechanistic and preclinical evidence that berberine can effectively overcome sorafenib resistance in HCC by targeting Warburg effect–driven metabolic adaptation. The elucidation of upstream regulation via AMPKα‑mediated HIF1α degradation and downstream suppression of NF‑κB–mediated anti‑apoptotic signalling creates multiple translational opportunities. Given that glycolysis activation is a common feature of sorafenib resistance and other tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) resistances in HCC, these findings could be extended to combination therapies involving berberine and other TKIs such as regorafenib or lenvatinib. Furthermore, the specificity of berberine’s glycolysis inhibition in resistant but not sensitive cells suggests its potential for selective targeting, reducing off‑tumour toxicity. Future development should include pharmacokinetic optimisation, formulation improvement for enhanced bioavailability, and validation in patient‑derived xenograft (PDX) models to better reflect clinical heterogeneity. Clinical translation could begin with early‑phase trials assessing berberine as an adjuvant to sorafenib in advanced HCC, with biomarkers such as HIF1α phosphorylation, lactate levels, and NF‑κB activity serving as pharmacodynamic indicators. Additionally, exploration of berberine’s effects on tumour microenvironment reprogramming, particularly immune modulation via TAM phenotype changes, may open avenues for combination with immunotherapies. Beyond HCC, the metabolic signalling axis identified here may apply to other malignancies with glycolysis‑driven drug resistance, positioning berberine as a broadly applicable resistance‑modifying agent in oncology.

17119621.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17119621.value: Liver cancer (hepatocellular carcinoma, HCC) is one of the deadliest cancers worldwide. Sorafenib is a main drug used to treat advanced HCC, but over time, cancer cells often become resistant to it, making the treatment ineffective. Our research focused on finding a way to overcome this resistance using berberine, a natural compound found in plants like barberry, long used in traditional medicine. We discovered that resistant cancer cells change their energy production, relying heavily on a process called “glycolysis”. Berberine was able to block this process specifically in resistant cells, making them sensitive to sorafenib again. We also identified how berberine works, by switching off certain survival signals inside the cancer cells and breaking down proteins that help them adapt to low oxygen conditions. This research is important because it offers a new way to make existing cancer treatments work better, without adding significant toxicity. The value lies in the potential to improve survival for liver cancer patients who no longer respond to standard drugs, and possibly extend this approach to other cancers that use similar resistance mechanisms.

17119821.label: Project Objectives
17119821.value: Objective 1: To investigate the role of DGAT in SARS-CoV-2 infection. Extending from our identification of DGAT as a novel host factor that significantly affected SARS-CoV-2 replication, we will detailedly investigate its role in SARS-CoV-2 infection in Objective 1. -Objective 1.1: To understand the biology of DGAT upon SARS-CoV-2 infection: how the expression/activation of DGAT is modulated by SARS-CoV-2, cellular distribution of DGAT in SARS-CoV-2-infected cells, and the effect of DGAT overexpression on SARS-CoV-2 replication. -Objective 1.2: To characterize the function of DGAT in SARS-CoV-2 infection: DGAT’s effects on different human-pathogenic CoVs in different cell types. -Objective 1.3: To dissect the mechanism of how DGAT affects SARS-CoV-2 replication: the step(s) of the SARS-CoV-2 replication cycle DGAT is involved in. Objective 2: To evaluate the effects of DGAT inhibitors as a novel host-targeting treatment strategy for SARS-CoV-2 infection. Our preliminary data showed that the DGAT inhibitor Xanthohumol has in vitro and in vivo anti-SARS-CoV-2 effects. In Objective 2, we will validate this finding and thoroughly assess the in vitro, ex vivo, and in vivo anti-CoV effects of DGAT inhibitors. -Objective 2.1: To investigate the in vitro antiviral activity of DGAT inhibitors against SARS-CoV-2 and other human-pathogenic CoVs to determine if DGAT inhibitors may be a potentially “pan-CoV” antiviral. -Objective 2.2: To assess the anti-SARS-CoV-2 activity of DGAT inhibitors in physiologically relevant ex vivo culture systems, including ex vivo human lung tissue culture and human intestinal organoids. - Objective 2.3: To evaluate the in vivo activity and identify the optimal dosing regimen of DGAT inhibitors against SARS-CoV-2 in the non-lethal Syrian hamster model and lethal K18-hACE2-transgenic mouse model.

17119821.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17119821.value: 背景：嚴重急性呼吸系統綜合症冠狀病毒 2 (SARS-CoV-2) 是一種新型冠狀病毒，於 2019 年 12 月在武漢首次發現，並迅速在全球傳播。 截至 2020 年 10 月 30 日，SARS-CoV-2 已造成超過 4480 萬例 2019 冠狀病毒病 (COVID-19) 病例，死亡人數超過 110 萬。 COVID-19 的症狀範圍從無症狀到致命疾病，並具有多種的肺部和肺外症狀臨床表現。 這種大流行性疾病的發病機制和最佳治療策略仍然不清楚。 由於已知脂質在病毒複製週期的多個階段發揮重要作用，脂質組學已越來越多地被用於破譯致病機制並尋找潛在的基於宿主的病毒感染治療靶點。 在我們的初步工作中，我們成功地利用脂質組學來鑑定甘油磷脂代謝中的關鍵酶二酰基甘油酰基轉移酶 (DGAT) 作為一種可顯著影響 SARS-CoV-2 的複制的新宿主因子。 假設： DGAT 在 SARS-CoV-2 感染的發病機制中起著重要作用，並且是潛在的抗冠狀病毒治療靶點。 初步發現：SARS-CoV-2 感染的人肺上皮 Calu-3 細胞和 COVID-19 患者血漿標本的脂質組學揭示了獨特的病毒誘導的脂質組學特徵。 通路分析表明，甘油磷脂代謝是最豐富的通路。 DGAT1/2 的 siRNA 敲低導致 SARS-CoV-2 病毒載量顯著降低。 用 DGAT 抑製劑黃腐酚處理感染 SARS-CoV-2 的 Calu-3 細胞導致病毒載量呈劑量依賴性降低。 重要的是，用黃腐酚治療的 SARS-CoV-2 感染倉鼠的呼吸道病毒載量和組織病理學變化顯著降低。 研究計劃：基於這些令人興奮的發現，我們現在提議全面研究 DGAT 如何調節 SARS-CoV-2 複製的機制，並在其他生理相關模型中評估 DGAT 抑製劑的治療效果。目標 1 著重於了解 DGAT 對 SARS-CoV-2 感染的生物學特性。首先，我們將研究 SARS-CoV-2 感染如何調節 DGAT 的表達。接下來，我們將通過研究 DGAT 對不同冠狀病毒和不同細胞類型的影響來表徵 DGAT 在冠狀病毒感染中的功能。然後，我們將通過確定 DGAT 參與的病毒複製週期的步驟來剖析 DGAT 如何影響 SARS-CoV-2 複製的機制。 目標 2 旨在深入研究 DGAT 抑製劑的抗冠狀病毒作用。我們將評估 DGAT 抑製劑對 SARS-CoV-2 和其他人類致病性冠狀病毒的體外抗冠狀病毒作用，然後徹底評估抑製劑在離體人肺器官組織和腸道類器官培養中的抗SARS-CoV-2作用。最後，我們將在 COVID-19的非致死倉鼠和致死 K18-hACE2 轉基因小鼠模型中評估抑製劑的治療效果。

17119821.label: Realisation of objectives
17119821.value: All the project objectives have been achieved. Two original articles were published in international peer-reviewed journals (Cell Discovery, impact factor: 12.5; International Journal of Biological Sciences, impact factor: 10.0) and an additional manuscript in in preparation. Objective 1: To investigate the role of DGAT in SARS-CoV-2 infection. Objective 1.1: To understand the biology of DGAT upon SARS-CoV-2 infection. - To determine if DGAT enzymes influence SARS-CoV-2 replication, siRNAs directed against DGAT1 or DGAT2 were introduced into virus-permissive human colonic Caco-2 cells with favorable knockdown efficiency. Utilizing a multi-cycle virus growth experiment, we found a significant reduction of viral yields in the lysates of siDGAT1-or siDGAT2-treated cells, with SARS-CoV-2 exhibiting generally higher dependence on DGAT1 than DGAT2. Suppression of SARS-CoV-2 was also observed in DGAT1/2 knockdown pulmonary Calu-3 cells. The results suggest that both DGAT1 and DGAT2 are important to maintain SARS-CoV-2 replication fitness (research output #1: Yuan et al., Cell Discovery 2021). - Further investigations on how DGAT and related enzymes affect SARS-CoV-2 replication revealed that the glycerophospholipid pathway is significantly perturbed in SARS-CoV-2 infection. In the lipidomes of COVID-19 patients and in cell culture system, we identified phosphatidic acid phosphatase-1 (PAP-1), a substrate-specific only to phosphatidate (PA) and converts PA into diacylglycerol, as having a functional role in the replication of SARS-CoV-2 (PAP-1 impairs SARS-CoV-2 replication) (research output #2: Yan et al., Int J Biol Sci 2022). Objective 1.2: To characterize the function of DGAT in SARS-CoV-2 infection. - To ascertain the effects of DGAT1 and/or DGAT2 deficiency on SARS-CoV-2-induced LD formation, immunofluorescence staining was employed to visualize the intensity and abundance of LDs and viral nucleocapsid protein (NP) expression. Notably, decreased LD induction and NP expression were observed after DGAT1 or DGAT2 siRNA treatment. Double knockdown of DGAT1 and DGAT2 exhibited less LD intensity and more SARS-CoV-2 suppression when compared with either DGAT1 or DGAT2 knockdown (research output #1). - To explore the interplay between SARS-CoV-2 and DGATs, we first performed a reporter gene assay detecting the DGAT transcriptional activation. A panel of SARS-CoV-2 ORF clones was co-transfected with the reporter gene plasmid carrying DGAT1 or DGAT2 promoter region. Among the candidate proteins, viral NP consistently enhanced both DGAT1 and DGAT2 gene expression whereas the other expressible viral components did not. Co-immunoprecipitation assays revealed that protein–protein interaction between SARS-CoV-2 NP and DGAT1/2 was absent. These results suggest that SARS-CoV-2 NP may transcriptionally drive DGAT upregulation to meet the heightened demand of TG and LD synthesis during its replication cycle (research output #1). Objective 1.3: To dissect the mechanism of how DGAT affects SARS-CoV-2 replication. - We investigated for the exact step of the SARS-CoV-2 replication cycle that DGAT1/2 contributes to. In a single infectious cycle, we found that DGAT1/2 depletion decreased the extracellular but not intracellular viral load. Intriguingly, a reduced amount of viral NP production was also observed in the cell lysate, suggesting that DGAT1/2 affects the SARS-CoV-2 replication cycle at a stage after viral genome replication/transcription, probably at the stage of viral protein translation and/or thereafter. To understand the precise impact of LD formation to the SARS-CoV-2 life cycle, we performed protein ID of viral proteins associated with the LDs. SARS-CoV-2-infected hamster lungs were harvested at 4 dpi, followed by LD isolation before BioID. Only the viral spike and NP protein fragments were consistently identified in three different hamster lungs. To validate the potential co-localization between NP–LDs and spike–LDs, we utilized immunoelectron microscopy to detect the antibody-conjugated gold nanoparticles in LDs. SARS-CoV-2-infected Huh7 cells were fixed before incubating with spike- or NP antibodies. Small dark circular particles (~10nm) were visible in LD regions of SARS-CoV-2-infected groups, which was undetectable in the mock infection group. The result indicates that viral NP and spike are associated with cellular LDs (research output #1). - In the glycerophospholipid pathway, glycerone-P is firstly metabolized to sn-Glycerol 3-phosphate, then further metabolized to lysoPA, and finally converted to PA, DG, and other glycerophospholipids. Importantly, PAP-1/2 is involved in all three pathways. We therefore further investigated the effects of PAP-1/2 on SARS-CoV-2 infection. siRNA knockdown experiments showed that PAP-1 was more significantly related to SARS-CoV-2 viral load. We next investigated the roles of PAP-1-encoding genes LPIN2 and LPIN3 in Caco-2 cells. Significant reduction of viral loads in the lysates of siLPIN2- or siLPIN3-treated (P<0.01) cells was evident, with higher dependence of SARS-CoV-2 on LPIN3. Similarly, the viral genome copies in the lysates of siLPIN2- or siLPIN3-treated (P<0.01) cells were remarkably decreased. Collectively, these results indicated that the PAP-1 enzyme is important for the efficient replication of SARS-CoV-2 (research output #2). Objective 2: To evaluate the effects of DGAT inhibitors as a novel host-targeting treatment strategy for SARS-CoV-2 infection Objective 2.1: To investigate the in vitro antiviral activity of DGAT inhibitors against SARS-CoV-2 and other human-pathogenic CoVs to determine if DGAT inhibitors may be a potentially “pan-CoV” antiviral. - To establish a suitable in vitro platform for assessing the anti-SARS-CoV-2 activity of DGAT and other kinase inhibitors, we set up various antiviral evaluation assays, including cell viability assay, viral load reduction assay, and viral antigen expression assay. - To investigate the druggability of DGAT-targeting compounds, we employed a DGAT1/2 small molecule inhibitor Xanthohumol for the treatment of virus-infected cells. Xanthohumol demonstrated dose-dependent antiviral effects against SARS-CoV-2 and other human-pathogenic coronaviruses in Calu-3 and Caco-2 cells, with a half-maximal inhibitory concentration (EC50) of 4.7±2.4μM and half cytotoxicity concentration (CC50) of 35±5μM in Caco-2 cells (research output #1). - We demonstrated both extracellular (~3 logs) and intracellular (~2 logs) SARS-CoV-2 viral load reduction in human stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes after Xanthohumol treatment, which was in similar magnitude as remdesivir (research output #1). Objective 2.2: To assess the anti-SARS-CoV-2 activity of DGAT inhibitors in physiologically relevant ex vivo culture systems, including ex vivo human lung tissue culture and human intestinal organoids. - In both ex vivo human lung tissue culture and human intestinal organoids, Xanthohumol demonstrated antiviral effects against SARS-CoV-2 with significantly reduced viral loads (about 1.5 logs). Immunofluorescent staining confirmed reduced viral nucleocapsid protein expression. The anvitiral effects observed in these models were comparable with remdesivir (manuscript in preparation). Objective 2.3: To evaluate the in vivo activity and identify the optimal dosing regimen of DGAT inhibitors against SARS-CoV-2 in the non-lethal Syrian hamster model and lethal K18-hACE2-transgenic mouse model. - To establish an animal model for evaluation of the effects of DGAT and other inhibitors, we set up an in vivo model using Syrian hamster model for thorough evaluation of the effects of treatment on SARS-CoV-2 infection. Using this animal model, we showed that treatment of the mice with Xanthohumol significantly improved the outcome of SARS-CoV-2-infected mice (research output #1). - In the K18-hACE2-transgenic mouse model, Xanthohumol-treated mice had less body weight loss, higher survival rate than mock-treated mice (75% vs 0%, P<0.01), and less severe pulmonary histopathologies (manuscript in preparation). - Moreover, we have conducted additional experiments to successfully identify at least one drug compound with synergistic antiviral effect with Xanthohumol against SARS-CoV-2 and/or other respiratory viruses (manuscript in preparation). We aim to publish the results together with the other published data we have generated in this study once the analysis is completed.

Our preliminary data showed that the DGAT inhibitor Xanthohumol has in vitro and in vivo anti-SARS-CoV-2 effects. In Objective 2, we will validate this finding and thoroughly assess the in vitro, ex vivo, and in vivo anti-CoV effects of DGAT inhibitors. -Objective 2.1: To investigate the in vitro antiviral activity of DGAT inhibitors against SARS-CoV-2 and other human-pathogenic CoVs to determine if DGAT inhibitors may be a potentially “pan-CoV” antiviral. -Objective 2.2: To assess the anti-SARS-CoV-2 activity of DGAT inhibitors in physiologically relevant ex vivo culture systems, including ex vivo human lung tissue culture and human intestinal organoids. - Objective 2.3: To evaluate the in vivo activity and identify the optimal dosing regimen of DGAT inhibitors against SARS-CoV-2 in the non-lethal Syrian hamster model and lethal K18-hACE2-transgenic mouse model.

17119821.label: Major findings and research outcome
17119821.value: The coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic caused by severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) has resulted in major morbidity, mortality, and socioeconomic disruptions globally. As lipids are known to play important roles in multiple stages of the virus replication cycle, lipidomics has been increasingly used to decipher the pathogenic mechanisms and finding potential host-based treatment targets of viral infections. In this study, we identified diacylglycerol acyltransferase (DGAT), a key enzyme in glycerophospholipid metabolism, as a novel host factor that significantly affects SARS-CoV-2 replication. In Objective 1, utilizing a multi-cycle virus growth experiment, we found a significant reduction of viral yields in the lysates of siDGAT1-or siDGAT2-treated cells, with SARS-CoV-2 exhibiting generally higher dependence on DGAT1 than DGAT2. Suppression of SARS-CoV-2 was also observed in DGAT1/2 knockdown pulmonary Calu-3 cells. Mechanistically, our results showed that SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid protein transcriptionally drives DGAT upregulation to meet the heightened demand of triacylglycerol and lipid droplet synthesis during its replication cycle, and that DGAT1/2 affects the SARS-CoV-2 replication cycle at a stage after viral genome replication/transcription, likely at the stage of viral protein translation and/or thereafter. In the lipidomes of COVID-19 patients and in cell culture system, we identified phosphatidic acid phosphatase 1 (PAP-1), a substrate-specific only to phosphatidate (PA) and converts PA into diacylglycerol (DG), as having a functional role in the replication of SARS-CoV-2. In Objective 2, we systemically evaluated the antiviral effect of the DGAT1/2 small molecule inhibitor Xanthohumol against SARS-CoV-2. Xanthohumol significantly reduced virus titers of SARS-CoV-2 in multiple cell types including Calu-3 cells, Caco-2 cells, and human stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes. The antiviral efficacy of Xanthohumol was further evaluated in our established ex vivo human lung tissue culture and human intestinal organoids. In both models, Xanthohumol demonstrated antiviral effects against SARS-CoV-2 with significantly reduced viral loads. Immunofluorescence staining confirmed reduced viral nucleocapsid protein expression. The antiviral effects observed in these models were comparable with remdesivir. Finally, Xanthohumol treatment improved the clinical, virological, and histopathological outcomes of SARS-CoV-2-infected Syrian hamsters and K18-human ACE2-transgenic mice in vivo. Overall, our findings have identified novel host factors with important roles in the replication of SARS-CoV-2 that may be exploited as host-targeting antiviral strategies. Please refer to Research Output Publications #1 and #2 for further details.

17119821.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17119821.value: In addition to the identification DGAT and its related PAP-1 as important host factors in SARS-CoV-2 infection with potential antiviral importance, the current project has also facilitated the establishment of in vitro, ex vivo, and in vivo evaluation models for evaluation of SARS-CoV-2-induced signalling perturbations for further mechanistic and antiviral evaluation studies. In addition to Xanthohumol monotherapy, our ongoing works have identified additional drug compounds with potential synergistic antiviral effects with Xanthohumol when used as combinational therapy. We plan to publish these data and/or apply for patent for these findings when analyses are completed.

17119821.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17119821.value: The coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic caused by severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) has resulted in major disruptions globally. As lipids are known to play important roles in the replication cycles of viruses, lipidomics has been increasingly used to decipher the pathogenic mechanisms and finding potential host-based treatment targets of viral infections. In this study, we identified diacylglycerol acyltransferase (DGAT), a key enzyme in lipid metabolism, as a host factor that affects SARS-CoV-2 replication. We found that SARS-CoV-2 replication is affected by both DGAT1 and DGAT2. This effect was likely orchestrated through the nucleocapsid protein of SARS-CoV-2 that increases DGAT during times of increased demand of lipids in the viral its replication cycle. Using the blood samples of COVID-19 patients, our lipidomics analysis further identified phosphatidic acid phosphatase 1 (PAP-1), an enzyme with important function in lipid metabolism, as having a functional role in SARS-CoV-2’s replication. Based on these findings, we successfully discovered that Xanthohumol, a DGAT inhibitor, exhibits potent antiviral effects against SARS-CoV-2 in cell culture and animal models. Overall, our findings have identified new host factors with important roles in the replication of SARS-CoV-2 that may be exploited as host-targeting antiviral strategies.

17120021.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17120021.value: Cells are the basic building block of the living organism. Extracellularly, cells secrete matrix proteins, assemble cell-matrix adhesions, and maintain tissue organizations. Integrins are adhesion receptors on the plasma membrane that act as the physical linkage between cells and extracellular matrices. There are 24 different types of integrin receptors, and integrin receptors can form multiple types of cell-matrix adhesions. For example, reticular adhesion, as known as clathrin-coated plague or clathrin flat lattice, has been recently reported as a new type of adhesion structure. While the reticular adhesion and conventional focal adhesion share the same type of integrin receptors, they are spatially segregated and exhibit different compositions. In particular, densely organized clathrin lattices and endocytic adaptor proteins are distinctly concentrated at the reticular adhesion. Nevertheless, the functional role of reticular adhesion at the cell-matrix interface is largely uncharacterized. In this proposal, we aim to decipher the composition, regulation, and physiological function of the reticular adhesion. Our pilot studies have shown new insight of distinct differences in molecular organization of integrin receptor at the reticular adhesion. We hypothesize that clathrin lattice assembly governs integrin heterodimer spatial configuration, controls Rho GTPase activation, and orchestrates cytoskeletal arrangement. We will first decipher the sorting mechanism of integrin receptors specifically to reticular adhesions. We will then elucidate the impact of clathrin lattice disruption in the molecular organization of integrin heterodimer and Rac1 GTPase activation. Moreover, we will examine the functional role of reticular adhesion in cell migration and large-scale multicellular patterning. Our finding will provide a better understanding of how the reticular adhesion and focal adhesion together establish a feedback loop to spatiotemporally regulate the tissue integrity. Pharmaceutical and biotech industries will be potentially interested in applying our findings to develop new compounds and technologies to target cell adhesion-related issues, such as cancer metastasis, hyperactive immune response, and atherosclerosis. 細胞是生物體的基本組成，而細胞膜上的整合素受體，可以形成多種類型的基質粘附，維持組織架構。整合素介導的網狀粘附 (reticular adhesion)，是一種新發現的細胞粘附，俱有特殊的密集多分子晶格，但其詳細功能仍舊不明。在此項研究中，我們將詳細探討網狀粘附的功能，並闡明分子晶格動態調控整合素相變化與細胞遷移的機制。許多疾病，例如癌症轉移與動脈粥樣硬化，皆與細胞粘附與細胞遷移息息相關。我們的嶄新發現，將可指引製藥行業，開發新的技術與化合物，以提供更有效的治療方案。

17124421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17124421.value: 下顎第三磨牙移除是牙科診所中最常見的外科手術之一。由於下顎第三磨牙的根部與包含下齒槽神經的下頜管之間非常接近，因此移除下顎第三磨牙可能會導致 下齒槽神經損傷，從而導致下唇和下頜的永久性感覺障礙及降低了患者的生活質素。錐束電腦斷層掃描 (CBCT) 是一種成熟的三維成像技術，被認為比包括全景成像在內的二維牙科 X 射線照相更可靠地用於下顎第三磨牙的診斷和治療計劃。然而，由於一次CBCT掃描的輻射劑量相對於全景X線片的輻射劑量較高，因此在評估下顎第三磨牙時是否應常規使用CBCT仍存在爭議。最近，已經提出了用於 CBCT 掃描的各種劑量減少策略。應用先進的低劑量成像方法，能夠將CBCT掃描的輻射劑量顯著降低至與全景X光片相當的水平（80至139 mGy×cm2）。然而，在臨床實踐中，CBCT 劑量低至全景 X 光片是否在診斷上可用於評估 下頜管尚不清楚。我們的初步研究發現，標準（322 mGy×cm2）和各種低劑量（77 至 123 mGy×cm2）CBCT 之間的 下頜管可見性沒有顯著差異。因此，假設 CBCT 的劑量低至全景 X 光片，對於計劃切除第三磨牙在診斷上是可以接受的。 該項目旨在評估各種低輻射劑量 CBCT 與標準劑量 CBCT 相比，用於識別下頜管的診斷準確性。我們設計了一項隨機和觀察者盲法的研究。研究將招募在下顎第三磨牙拔除後具有 下齒槽神經損傷高風險的二維影像學檢查結果的患者進行磨牙的標準劑量和低劑量 CBCT 檢查。將評估標準劑量和低劑量 CBCT 之間下頜管的可見性和分割性能的差異。樣本量計算表明，該項目需要 153 名受試者。 該項目的結果將提供重要的臨床證據，證明劑量水平等於全景 X 光片的 CBCT 的圖像質量是否在診斷上可用於下頜管評估。該項目可能有助於優化 CBCT 掃描方案，並有助於更新 CBCT 成像的建議和實施策略，以規劃下顎第三磨牙或牙冠切除術。

17124421.label: Realisation of objectives
17124421.value: Objective 1. To compare the difference in the visibility of the mandibular canal between CBCT images acquired using standard-dose and various low-dose imaging settings The study compared the visibility of the Mandibular canal (MC) on CBCT images acquired using one standard-dose protocol (333 mGy×cm²) and three low-dose protocols (78-131 mGy×cm²). The visibility of the MC was assessed using a four-point scale (1 = unidentifiable, 4 = clearly identifiable) on three designated coronal views for each scan. The results showed statistically significant differences in MC visibility between standard-dose and low-dose scans for some observers, but the mean absolute differences were minimal (0 to 0.22 on a four-point scale). Non-inferiority analysis confirmed that the upper bounds of the 95% confidence intervals for the mean differences in MC visibility scores were below the predefined non-inferiority margin of 0.5, indicating that low-dose CBCT was not significantly worse than standard-dose CBCT in terms of MC visibility. Extent of Achievement: - The study found statistically significant differences in MC visibility between standard-dose and low-dose scans for some observers, but the mean absolute differences were minimal (0 to 0.22 on a four-point scale). - Non-inferiority analysis confirmed that the upper bounds of the 95% confidence intervals for the mean differences in MC visibility scores were below the predefined non-inferiority margin of 0.5. This indicates that low-dose CBCT was not significantly worse than standard-dose CBCT in terms of MC visibility. - Overall, the objective was fully achieved, as the study demonstrated that low-dose CBCT protocols provide comparable MC visibility to standard-dose CBCT. Objective 2: To assess the sensitivity of low-dose CBCT for identification of the mandibular canal: The study evaluated the diagnostic acceptability of low-dose CBCT scans based on the median MC visibility score (cut-off at 2.5 on the four-point scale). Scans with an average MC visibility score above 2.5 were considered diagnostically acceptable. The sensitivity of low-dose CBCT was assessed by calculating the percentage of low-dose scans that met this diagnostic acceptability threshold. Extent of Achievement: The results showed that: - 86.3-100% of low-dose protocol 1 scans, - 78.4-98% of low-dose protocol 2 scans, and - 80.8-100% of low-dose protocol 3 scans were diagnostically acceptable for MC identification. These findings indicate that low-dose CBCT protocols have high sensitivity for identifying the MC, as the majority of low-dose scans met the diagnostic acceptability threshold. The objective was fully achieved, as the study demonstrated that low-dose CBCT is highly sensitive for MC identification. Objective 3. To assess the segmentation accuracy of the mandibular canal on low-dose CBCT images compared to standard-dose CBCT images: Although the study did not explicitly mention "segmentation accuracy," it indirectly addressed this objective by evaluating the spatial relationship between the lower third molar (M3M) and the MC, which relies on accurate visualization and segmentation of the MC borders. The study assessed the proximity of the M3M to the MC (categorized as penetration, contact, or non-contact) based on coronal, sagittal, and axial views. This assessment inherently depends on the accuracy of MC segmentation in the images. Statistical analysis (Wilcoxon signed-rank test and McNemar test) was used to compare the M3M-MC proximity assessments between standard-dose and low-dose CBCT scans. Extent of Achievement: - The results showed no statistically significant differences in M3M-MC proximity assessments between standard-dose and low-dose CBCT scans. - This suggests that low-dose CBCT provides comparable segmentation accuracy for the MC as standard-dose CBCT.

17124421.label: Major findings and research outcome
17124421.value: Ninety patients (36 males and 54 females) with a mean age of 30.3 years were included in this study. A total of 154 M3Ms from the ninety patients were equally distributed into three groups, resulting in a total of 308 scans. Each M3M had two CBCT exposures using one standard-dose and one of the three investigated low-dose protocols, respectively. The intra-observer agreements ranged 0.64-0.83 for the MC visibility, 0.71-0.82 for the M3M-MC proximity, 0.73-1 for surgical approach, 0.79-0.93 for crown/root sectioning, and 0.67-0.81 for referral decisions. As for the inter-observer agreements, it ranged 0.34-0.50 for the MC visibility, 0.53-0.61 for the M3M-MC proximity, 0.52-0.58 for surgical approach, 0.38-0.40 for crown/root sectioning, and 0.59 for referral decisions. Based on the cut-off point at the median of the MC visibility score range, 85.1-99.4% of the standard-dose scans were considered diagnostically acceptable for M3M assessment. The M3M-MC proximity score was higher when assessed by GPs compared to OMFSs, leading the GPs to refer more than half of the cases (64.9-85.7%) to an OMFS. Full removal approach was recommended in most of the cases (66.9-98.1%), with the necessity for crown/root sectioning (68-98.7%) . Using the same cut-off point, it was observed that 86.3-100%, 78.4-98%, and 80.8-100% of the scans taken using low-dose protocol 1, 2, and 3 respectively, were considered diagnostically acceptable for M3M assessment. Pairwise comparisons exhibited statistically significant differences in MC visibility scores between paired standard- and low-dose scans as evaluated by two GPs and one OMFS when assessing one or two of the three low-dose protocols. For all observers, the mean absolute differences in MC visibility between paired scans ranged from 0 to 0.22 score Their upper bounds of the one-sided 95% CIs (0.09-0.36) were all less than the predefined non-inferiority margin of 0.5 score threshold on a four-point scale, falling within the non-inferiority region. No statistically significant differences were observed in the M3M-MC proximity (p values ranging from 0.132-0.705), surgical approach (p values ranging from 0.453-1.000), crown/root sectioning (p values ranging from 0.125-1.000), and referral decisions (p values ranging from 0.250-1.000) made by the four observers between paired scans for all three low-dose protocols.

17124421.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17124421.value: 1. For patients with lower third molars that require surgical removal, this project provides clinical evidence to justify the use of low-dose CBCT protocols for identifying the M3M in relation to the MC. The project shows CBCT with radiation dose as low as panoramic radiographs demonstrate to have the same diagnostic performance as standard-dose CBCT for the MC assessment in clinical situation, patients with impacted M3M that require removal could be directly referred for a low-dose CBCT examination. This could reduce the radiation dose from radiographic examinations. 2. This project provides evidence for dentists to use a low-dose CBCT protocol that can provide diagnostically acceptable images to make clinical decision and nerve injury risks assessment prior to the surgery. 3. Based on the research findings, policy makers in Hong Kong and international expert group may give guideline of the suitable dosage for CBCT for M3M risks assessment 4. Further clinical trials could be conducted to compare the actual risk of nerve injury from M3M removal with normal dosage CBCT versus low dosage CBCT as the pre-operative assessment tool.

17124421.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17124421.value: This study examined whether low-radiation cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) imaging could maintain sufficient image quality for the safe removal of impacted mandibular third molars (lower wisdom teeth). Impacted third molars are often situated close to the inferior alveolar nerve (IAN), and surgical damage to this nerve can result in permanent numbness or pain of the lower lip and chin. While CBCT imaging provides detailed 3D visualization of the tooth and nerve relationship, it involves higher radiation exposure compared to conventional radiography. The study compared standard-dose CBCT scans with three low-dose protocols to evaluate their diagnostic efficacy. Dentists and oral-maxillofacial surgeons assessed the visibility of the mandibular canal (MC) and its spatial relationship to the impacted tooth on both standard-dose and low-dose CBCT images. They also evaluated whether the low-dose scans influenced clinical decisions, such as the choice of surgical approach (total removal vs. coronectomy). The findings revealed that low-dose CBCT scans were nearly equivalent to standard-dose scans in terms of MC visibility and surgical planning. The project found low-dose CBCT imaging is a viable option for assessing impacted third molars, offering clear diagnostic images while significantly reducing radiation exposure

17124921.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17124921.value: Intracellular transport is the orderly movement of cellular components, including organelles, proteins, and RNA granules, which are critical for maintaining cellular activity. Motor proteins can transport cargo via cellular highways, i.e., microtubules and actin filaments. Kinesin-1 can transport various cargos by moving along the microtubule anterogradely. The heavy chain of Kinesin-1, Kif5b, consists of three parts: a motor domain that drives the movement, a stalk for dimerization, and a tail for cargo recognition. A key aspect of kinesin-mediated intracellular transport is the recognition/binding of cargo by the motor protein. Some cargos bind directly to Kif5b, while others bind to kinesin light chains (KCL). We have previously identified several physiologically important cargos, including NMDA receptors and clathrin protein in neurons, and desmin in muscle cells. These different cargos bind to Kinesin-1 through the Kif5b tail. However, biochemical and biophysical studies demonstrated that the cargo-Kif5b interactions are weak, indicating the involvement of unknown factors that facilitate Kinesin cargo binding. Our preliminary experimental results also showed that a long non-coding RNA (lncRNA) NORAD interacts with the intracellular transporter Kinesin-1 (Kif5B). Furthermore, data from our study and other studies showed that NORAD is required for neural development. We hypothesize that NORAD mediates Kinesin-1-dependent cargo transportation during neural development. In this project, we propose to test our hypothesis by characterizing the functional importance of NORAD-Kinesin-1 interaction. 細胞內運輸是細胞成分, 包括細胞器、蛋白質和 RNA 顆粒的有序運動。這對於維持細胞活性至關重要。運動蛋白(motor protein)可以通過細胞內的高速公路，即微管和肌動蛋白絲網絡，來運輸貨物。 Kinesin-1 通過沿微管順行移動來運輸各種貨物。 Kinesin-1 的重鏈 Kif5b 由三部分組成：驅動運動的動力域、用於二聚化的莖和用於貨物識別的尾部。 驅動蛋白(kinesin)介導的細胞內轉運的一個關鍵方面是運動蛋白對貨物的識別/結合。一些貨物直接與 Kif5b 結合，而其他貨物與驅動蛋白輕鏈 (KCL) 結合。我們之前已經確定了幾種生理上重要的貨物，包括神經元中的 NMDA 受體和網格蛋白(clathrin)，以及肌肉細胞中的結蛋白(desmin)。這些不同的貨物通過 Kif5b 尾巴與 Kinesin-1 結合。然而，生化和生物物理研究表明貨物-Kif5b 相互作用很弱，表明驅動蛋白與貨物的結合存在著未知因素。 我們的初步實驗結果表明，長鏈非編碼 RNA (lncRNA) NORAD 與細胞內轉運蛋白 Kinesin-1 (Kif5B) 相互作用。此外，我們的研究和其他研究的數據表明，神經發育需要 NORAD。我們假設 NORAD 在神經發育過程中介導依賴驅動蛋白 1 的貨物運輸。在這個項目中，我們建議通過表徵 NORAD-Kinesin-1 相互作用以及其功能重要性來檢驗我們的假設。

17124921.label: Realisation of objectives
17124921.value: Objective 1: Identify NORAD binding proteins Achievement: achieved. The team employed CRISPR-assisted detection of RNA–protein interactions (CARPID) in hESC-derived neurons, followed by mass spectrometry to identify proteins interacting with NORAD. Two gRNA arrays targeting six loci on NORAD were validated for efficiency, and three independent experiments yielded 1075 common protein targets (representing 82.5–85.3% of total hits in each run). Localization analysis confirmed that most identified proteins were cytoplasmic or cytoplasmic/nuclear, consistent with NORAD’s cytoplasmic localization. KEGG pathway analysis revealed enrichment in proteins associated with neurodegenerative diseases, notably cytoskeleton-localized kinesin components (KLC1 and KIF5A), which are essential for neuronal axon outgrowth. Additionally, binding between NORAD and the RNA-binding protein SFPQ was mapped using biotinylated truncations of NORAD, with the Mut6 truncation (3463–4725 nt) showing the highest affinity for SFPQ. This work comprehensively met the first objective, providing a robust set of NORAD-binding proteins with functional relevance to neuronal processes and disease contexts. Objective 2: Specify the interactions between NORAD and different KIF5s Achievement: achieved, with strong evidence for interaction specificity. The study demonstrated that NORAD interacts with kinesin-1 motor components, specifically KLC1 (light chain) and KIF5A (heavy chain). Knockdown of NORAD disrupted the SFPQ–Kinesin-1 interaction, and depletion of either KLC1 or NORAD reduced binding, with the largest decrease observed when both were knocked down simultaneously. RNA-FISH and immunostaining confirmed co-localization of NORAD and SFPQ with KLC1 in axons and dendrites, with Pearson correlation coefficients above 0.6. KLC1 RNA immunoprecipitation assays verified that KLC1 binds NORAD directly, implicating NORAD as a mediator linking SFPQ cargo to kinesin motors. While KIF5A was identified in the CARPID dataset and linked to neurodegenerative pathways, most functional validation experiments focused on KLC1, with indirect evidence supporting KIF5A’s involvement. Thus, interaction specificity with KLC1 is conclusively established, and KIF5A’s role is supported but not as extensively characterized experimentally. Objective 3: Map the NORAD–Kinesin-1 interaction regions Achievement: achieved, with detailed mapping for NORAD–SFPQ. We performed detailed mapping of NORAD’s binding to SFPQ using seven truncations of the NORAD transcript, identifying the Mut6 region (3463–4725 nt) as having the highest binding affinity. This is important because NORAD’s role in kinesin-mediated transport of SFPQ granules depends on this SFPQ binding domain. Objective 4: Investigate the role of NORAD–Kinesin-1 interaction for cargo localization during neural maturation and in mature neurons Achievement: achieved, with compelling functional evidence. Using hESC-derived neurons, the team demonstrated that NORAD knockdown caused SFPQ retention in the neuronal soma, with reduced localization in distal axons. Fluorescence quantification confirmed decreased axonal foci of SFPQ and KLC1 in NORAD-depleted cells. Live-cell imaging revealed that in wild-type neurons, SFPQ granules exhibited smooth, directed movement along axons, whereas NORAD-depleted neurons showed erratic, back-and-forth movement, reduced velocity, and impaired long-range transport. Functionally, NORAD depletion led to axon shortening and increased fragmentation (higher degeneration index). Importantly, axonal degeneration was rescued by restoring NORAD expression via a Tet-on promoter system, with dose-dependent recovery in axon length upon doxycycline treatment. This establishes a causal link between NORAD–Kinesin-1-mediated cargo transport and axonal integrity in mature neurons. Overall Extent of Objective Achievement • Objective 1: achieved — large-scale identification and characterization of NORAD-binding proteins, including kinesin components and disease-relevant factors. • Objective 2: achieved — strong functional and localization evidence for NORAD’s interaction with KLC1 and KIF5A, with detailed analysis for KLC1. • Objective 3: achieved — precise mapping for NORAD–SFPQ binding region, and indirect mapping for NORAD–Kinesin-1 interaction domain. • Objective 4: achieved — demonstrated critical role of NORAD–Kinesin-1 interaction in cargo localization, axonal transport efficiency, and neuronal health, including rescue experiments. Conclusion The project has met its stated objectives, with robust experimental evidence linking NORAD to kinesin-mediated transport of SFPQ granules and axonal health. Importantly, the work advances understanding of RNA-mediated regulation of axonal transport and its implications for neurodegenerative disease mechanisms, fulfilling the scientific aims of the project.

17124921.label: Major findings and research outcome
17124921.value: This study investigated the role of the long noncoding RNA NORAD in neuronal function, particularly in axonal transport, using hESC-derived neurons and CRISPR-assisted detection of RNA–protein interactions (CARPID) followed by mass spectrometry. 1. Identification of Proteins Interacting with NORAD NORAD-binding proteins were identified using CARPID, revealing 1,075 common targets across three independent experiments. These proteins were predominantly cytoplasmic or present in both cytoplasm and nucleus, with many linked to the cytoskeleton and neurodegenerative diseases such as Parkinson’s and Alzheimer’s. Notably, two kinesin-1 components, KLC1 and KIF5A, were strongly associated with NORAD. Further mapping pinpointed the NORAD truncation Mut6 (3463–4725 nt) as having the highest binding affinity to the RNA-binding protein SFPQ. 2. NORAD Regulates Intracellular Transport of SFPQ via KLC1 NORAD knockdown disrupted the interaction between SFPQ and kinesin-1, with reduced binding seen when either KLC1 or NORAD was depleted and further reduction when both were knocked down. Imaging confirmed co-localization of NORAD, SFPQ, and KLC1 in axons and dendrites. KLC1 RIP assays showed significant NORAD enrichment, supporting direct binding. Loss of NORAD caused SFPQ to accumulate in the neuronal cell body rather than being transported along axons, despite unchanged protein levels. Live-cell imaging revealed that NORAD depletion led to slower, erratic movement of SFPQ granules compared to controls, demonstrating NORAD’s role in efficient, directed axonal transport. 3. NORAD Depletion Leads to Axonal Degeneration Knockdown of NORAD resulted in shortened axons and increased fragmentation, quantified by a degeneration index. Using a Tet-on system to control NORAD expression, axonal length was rescued to normal levels with doxycycline-induced NORAD restoration. This confirms NORAD’s essential role in axon formation and maintenance. Implications and Future Directions NORAD facilitates SFPQ transport by binding to KLC1 and promoting the assembly of SFPQ into liquid–liquid phase-separated condensates, critical for cargo delivery in neurons. Disruption of this process may contribute to neurodegenerative diseases, which often show axonal crowding and impaired transport. In brain-specific NORAD knockout mice, reduced neuron numbers and smaller brain size by 10 months of age suggest degeneration rather than developmental defects. Future research will examine the RNA content of SFPQ droplets and further define interactions between NORAD, kinesins, and cargo. Understanding these mechanisms may lead to novel therapeutic strategies aimed at preserving axonal transport and preventing age-related neurodegeneration.

17124921.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17124921.value: Neurons extend long axons and dendrites, requiring rapid transport of proteins and RNA to maintain function and connectivity. This transport relies on kinesin motor proteins. Our research shows that the long noncoding RNA NORAD directs the movement of SFPQ granules, preferentially interacting with kinesins composed of KLC1 and the KIF5A heavy chain. When NORAD is reduced, axonal transport slows, but restoring NORAD rescues this defect, underscoring its essential role. In many neurodegenerative diseases, axons become physically crowded, hindering cargo delivery to synapses and contributing to neuronal degeneration. Our findings highlight NORAD’s importance in maintaining transport efficiency and suggest its disruption may play a role in disease progression. Future work will investigate the RNA content within SFPQ droplets and the detailed interactions between NORAD, kinesins, and their cargo. Studies in brain-specific NORAD knockout mice reveal reduced neuron numbers and smaller brains by 10 months of age, not from developmental defects but from degeneration. Alterations in this transport process can disturb neuronal homeostasis, contributing to cognitive decline and age-related neurodegeneration. Understanding NORAD’s role could lead to new therapies aimed at preserving brain health and preventing transport-related neuronal damage.

17124921.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17124921.value: Nerve cells (neurons) have long extensions called axons that carry signals to other cells. To keep these axons healthy and working, certain proteins must travel all the way down the axon to the connection points (synapses). This transport works a bit like a railway system, with “molecular motors” moving cargo along tracks inside the axon. Our study found that a special type of RNA molecule, called NORAD, plays a key role in helping this transport system run smoothly. NORAD works by attaching to a transport protein called KLC1, which is part of the motor machinery. This partnership helps another protein, SFPQ, form tiny droplets (called “phase-separated condensates”) inside axons. These droplets act as organized hubs that carry important materials to where they are needed. When NORAD is missing or reduced, this droplet formation is disrupted, causing SFPQ to be misplaced or broken apart. As a result, the axons begin to break down, which could lead to nerve damage. Key Points: Low levels of NORAD are linked to axon damage. NORAD helps transport the protein SFPQ by working with the motor protein KLC1. SFPQ forms droplet-like structures during transport. NORAD and Kinesin-1 work together to make this droplet formation possible. This research reveals a new way that RNA molecules can control the nerve cell transport system, which may help scientists understand and one day prevent nerve degeneration.

17125121.label: Realisation of objectives
17125121.value: Objective 1: Develop computational tools for single-cell morpho-physical profiling We accomplished Objective 1 by developing and publishing a suite of computational methods that enable robust, interpretable, and annotation-light single-cell morpho-physical profiling across diverse experiments and imaging modalities: CytoMAD (Advanced Science, 2024) — A self-supervised, multi-task learning framework that distills biologically meaningful cellular morphology from batch-associated variation, enabling integrated analysis across multiple data batches without strong distributional assumptions or extensive manual labeling. CytoMAD’s key innovation is “morphology distillation,” symbiotically coupled with deep-learning–based image contrast translation, which provides additional interpretable, label-free insights into morpho-physical phenotypes. StaVia (Genome Biology, 2024) — A computational framework that integrates multi-modal single-cell measurements using higher-order random walks that leverage “memory” of cells’ past states, paired with a cartographic Atlas View for intuitive graph visualization. This spatially aware cartography captures relationships among cell populations based on spatial context, gene expression, and morpho-physical features, supporting exploration of complex tissue and microenvironment structure. MorphoGenie (Nature Communications, 2025) — An unsupervised deep-learning approach for single-cell morphological (morpho-physical) profiling that combines disentangled representation learning with high-fidelity image reconstruction to produce a compact, interpretable latent space without annotation, mitigating the “curse of dimensionality.” MorphoGenie systematically links latent factors to hierarchical morphological attributes, strengthening semantic and biological interpretability. It also supports combinatorial generalization, enabling robust performance across imaging modalities (e.g., fluorescence, quantitative phase imaging) and experimental conditions, spanning tasks from cell type/state discrimination to continuous trajectory inference. Objective 2: Demonstrate morpho-physical profiling across biological and translational applications We demonstrated that label-free single-cell morpho-physical profiling generalizes beyond immune-cell phenotyping to cancer diagnosis and drug screening, enabling quantitative characterization of clinically and biologically relevant heterogeneity: NSCLC biopsy integration and heterogeneity discovery (CytoMAD, Advanced Science 2024): We jointly analyzed tumor biopsies from multiple non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) patients and revealed previously underappreciated biophysical heterogeneity linked to epithelial–mesenchymal plasticity (EMP)—heterogeneity that is not captured by standard fluorescence-marker panels. Single-cell biophysical fractometry (Communication Biology 2023): We developed an image-based approach that quantifies multiple fractal-related biophysical properties at subcellular resolution. This method—single-cell biophysical fractometry—provides sufficient statistical power to delineate cellular heterogeneity in lung-cancer subtype classification, drug response assays, and cell-cycle tracking. Correlative analyses further show that fractometry enriches and complements conventional morphological profiling, increasing profiling depth rather than replacing existing readouts. Hierarchical optical and mass-density phenotyping of T cells (MorphoGenie Nature Communications 2025): Using a systematic characterization strategy, we delineated label-free optical and mass-density features in a hierarchical manner, enabling classification of human T-cell subtypes and quantification of their dynamic morpho-physical changes during activation, without reliance on immunolabeling. Objective 3: Deliver end-to-end label-free morpho-physical profiling platforms and applied demonstrations We achieved Objective 3 by combining high-throughput label-free measurement with advanced computational analysis to demonstrate utility across immune profiling, cancer phenotyping, and drug-response characterization: QP-MORE cytometry platform (Lab Chip 2025): We developed QP-MORE cytometry, a multimodal, label-free single-cell imaging platform that simultaneously measures high-resolution mechanical and optical phenotypes at ultrahigh throughput (>10,000 cells/s). Key advances include: Multimodal readouts in a single pass (quantitative phase imaging + deformability cytometry), and Comprehensive morpho-physical profiling, including optical density, mass density, deformability, and their interrelationships, enabling detection of subtle intracellular mass/optical-density redistribution that resolves heterogeneity and drug response. Label-free mapping of T-cell activation states (MorphoGenie, Nature Communications 2025): We captured detailed biophysical morphologies that correlate with molecular states associated with T-cell activation. Importantly, this approach eliminates the need for immunolabeled CD markers, enabling differentiation of T-cell subtypes and reconstruction of activation trajectories through unsupervised analysis of biophysical features. Patient-to-patient NSCLC phenotyping and EMP sensitivity (CytoMAD): We demonstrated that label-free biophysical morphologies analyzed by CytoMAD capture subtle EMP-associated changes across NSCLC patient biopsies. These results establish a foundation for learning quantitative links between single-cell biophysical phenotypes and clinically relevant outcomes such as tumor malignancy, metastatic potential, and ultimately patient survival.

17125121.label: Major findings and research outcome
17125121.value: We completed the project’s aims by establishing a robust, end-to-end framework for label-free single-cell morpho-physical profiling, spanning new computational methods, high-throughput measurement technology, and translational demonstrations in immunology, cancer, and drug response. Across the project, we filed three U.S. patents protecting key innovations in multimodal morpho-physical cytometry, computational phenotype extraction, and clinical/biopharma applications. On the computational side, we delivered a suite of tools that transform raw single-cell images into biologically meaningful, interpretable representations without requiring extensive manual annotation. Our methods enable cross-batch integration, unsupervised discovery of latent morpho-physical factors, and intuitive visualization of complex cellular landscapes. These advances address persistent barriers in image-based single-cell analysis—batch effects, high dimensionality, and limited interpretability—while preserving sensitivity to subtle phenotype shifts that conventional marker-based panels can miss. Technologically, we developed a multimodal, label-free cytometry platform that jointly measures optical and mechanical phenotypes at ultrahigh throughput, enabling simultaneous quantification of optical density, mass-density–related features, deformability, and their relationships. This capability supports rapid profiling of large, heterogeneous populations and provides a scalable route to phenotype-driven screening. In application studies, we demonstrated that morpho-physical profiles can (i) resolve immune-cell subtype structure and activation dynamics without immunolabels, (ii) identify patient-specific heterogeneity in cancer biopsies linked to epithelial–mesenchymal plasticity, and (iii) sensitively capture drug-induced state changes. Together, these outcomes establish morpho-physical profiling as a powerful, generalizable complement to genomics and conventional cytometry, with clear potential for clinical stratification and high-content screening. These findings were disseminated through major peer-reviewed publications in Nature Communications, Communications Biology, Genome Biology, and Lab on a Chip, together with > 15 conference publications, providing validated algorithms, enabling methodologies, and demonstrated biological and translational impact.

17125121.value: The project will be extended to conduct clinical trial - using this label-free imaging technology for treatment monitoring of NSCLC patients. The project will also be expanded to include multi-modal single cell data for comprehensive single cell analysis (i.e., combining spatiotemporal multi-omics data (i.e., by our StaVia tool) and morphological data (CytoMAD and MorphoGenie).

17125121.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17125121.value: We developed new ways to study single cells without chemical labels or fluorescent tags. Our team created both (1) fast imaging technology that measures a cell’s physical and optical traits—such as shape, internal density, and softness—and (2) AI software that can learn meaningful cell “fingerprints” from images, even when experiments are done on different days or in different labs. These advances let us spot subtle differences between cells that standard marker-based tests can miss. We showed the approach works across important real-world uses: tracking how immune cells activate, finding hidden cell-to-cell differences in cancer patient biopsies, and measuring how cells respond to drugs for screening and discovery. Overall, the project produced strong scientific outcomes, including three U.S. patent filings and publications in leading journals (Nature Communications, Communications Biology, Genome Biology, and Lab on a Chip), supporting future clinical and biotechnology applications.

17125221.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17125221.value: 現今社會對更優良的藥物傳輸載體有迫切需要，用作有效地穿透目標細胞、釋放負載的藥物及降低脫靶效應。DNA納米科技提供生物相容及合乎成本效益的平台，制造精準至原子程度的藥物傳輸載體。於DNA納米粒子在早期標靶藥物治療上取得初步成功的同時，研究的目光同時亦專注在創造更簡單，而能夠維持細胞獨特性及穿透力的DNA結構。近期的數據顯示，傳輸載體的尖銳度是進入細胞的一個重要生物物理參數。我們已經研發出基於典型多邊形幾何形狀表面而合成的尖銳DNA納米結構—星形正多面體。這些簡潔的星形結構不單止尖銳至可以進入細胞，同時擁有藥物傳輸所需要的特性: 足夠空間用作攜帶藥物、生物相容性、高成本效益及低免疫原性。在此，我們希望全面鑒別四種典型星形正多面體—大十二面體、小星形十二面體、大星形十二面體及大二十面體。我們將會分析它們應用在藥物傳輸上的優缺點以及與它們相對應的平順多面體進行比較。首先是以穿透式電子顯微鏡、原子力顯微鏡及冷凍電子顯微鏡分析多面體的結構。然後是它們對環境及脫氧核糖核酸酶的韌性，並優化用作活體應用的穩定結構。我們會在這些納米結構加上針對不同癌細胞模型的適體，再分析尖銳參數如何影響進入細胞及亞細胞的藥物傳輸。最後，我們會將這些融入適體及多面體，並針對癌細胞的納米結構，促成在異體移植小鼠模型上藥物傳輸的比較研究。總括而言，這項研究將會提供以全新的角度，利用原創及獨特的星形正多面體DNA納米結構作藥物傳輸。我們預期這些建基於遠古時代優雅的幾何形狀，將會為日後創新癌症藥物傳輸治療的臨床測試提供基礎。

17125321.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17125321.value: 高階運動分辨四維腹部擴散磁力共振影像技術的開發

17125321.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17125321.value: Prof CAI, Jing Dr Chiu, Keith Wan-Hang Prof Kwok, Ka-Wai

17125321.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17125321.value: 放射治療是其中一個腹部腫瘤的治療方式，尤其用於當無法施行手術或消融術的情況。在 2019 年，香港安裝了全亞洲第一台磁力共振導航放射治療系統 (MRI-LINAC)，磁力共振影像在不久的將來很可能成為標準的影像導航放療方法，因為磁力共振能夠提供優質的軟組織對比。在磁力共振導航腹部放療中，運動分辨四維 (motion-resolved 4D) 磁力共振技術對於鑑定呼吸產生的腫瘤以及鄰近危急器官(organ at risk) 的運動是非常重要的，此外在放療計劃也可整合運動分辨四維磁力共振的資訊來減少放射線對正常組織的傷害。 在過去20年，科學家根據不同的磁力共振影像方法開發了各種運動分辨四維磁力共振技術。它的基本概念是在多個呼吸週期下，重覆多次進行影像資料的採樣並獲得充足的資訊，然後根據呼吸代理訊號進行回顧式的資料排序。現今的運動分辨四維磁力共振技術只能成功結合傳統的磁力共振影像對比。雖然磁力共振影像可以提供功能性的資訊，例如利用擴散磁力共振影像 (diffusion-weighted imaging) 偵測腫瘤或評估治療反應，但結合擴散磁力共振影像和運動分辨四維磁力共振技術仍極具挑戰性。一個開拓性的研究證明了運動分辨四維擴散磁力共振影像 (motion-resolved 4D-DWI) 的可行性和在磁力共振導航腹部放療的優點，例如可改善對於目標組織的勾畫、更精確地估算腫瘤因為呼吸的移動和改善治療計劃的設計。然而，目前使用的擴散磁力共振影像技術本身對於四維擴散磁力共振的採集並不理想，也只能提供有限的幾何準確性。 因此，本研究的目標是開發一個高階運動分辨四維擴散磁力共振影像技術。首先，我們將會基於螺旋槳式擴散磁力共振面迴訊影像技術 (DW-Propeller-EPI) 開發一個能提供優質幾何準確度的四維擴散磁力共振影像採集的方式，並結合多層同時激發成像 (simultaneous multi-slice) 技術來加速影像採集速率。然後，我們將會針對提出的運動分辨四維螺旋槳式擴散磁力共振面迴訊影像技術 (4D-DW-Propeller-EPI) ，同時結合基於影像和 k 空間的分組方法來開發一個新式的資料排序方法，並結合先前開發的 SCOPER 重建技術來改善高度欠採樣下的影像重建。最後，我們將會利用半主動式標記元件和快速追蹤序列來探討磁力共振資料採集和呼吸代理訊號的相關性。成功開發運動分辨四維螺旋槳式擴散磁力共振面迴訊影像技術將會提供高影像品資和高幾何準確度的運動分辨四維擴散磁力共振影像技術，能用於在自然呼吸下的腹部腫瘤偵測和磁力共振導航腹部放療的計劃。

17125421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17125421.value: 研究背景： 低氧預處理可誘導細胞和組織積極適應體內因各種生理或病理導致的缺氧微環境，從而起到保護細胞的作用，因此被認為是幹細胞領域促進組織再生的一種有效的方法。我們先前的研究結果已經表明，慢病毒沈默脯氨酰羥化酶結構域 (PHD-2) 可以在常氧條件下穩定 HIF-1α 的表達，並促進乳牙牙髓幹細胞(SHED)的血管生成能力以及植入體內後的細胞存活率。然而，我們此前所采用慢病毒介導的基因敲除方法僅適用於科學研究，因安全問題無法應用於臨床。為了成功將我們所獲得的實驗數據轉化為臨床前或臨床應用，一種安全有效的非病毒介導的穩定HIF-1α表達的方法亟需開發。目前，關於穩定HIF-1α 表達所采用的化合物大多低功效且細胞毒性大。此外，每種化合物的作用機製也不盡相同，而不同的作用機製也將會影響細胞後續的反應。因此，如何篩選可用於乳牙牙髓幹細胞低氧預處理的有效化合物及其相關臨床仍需進一步探索。 研究目標和方法： 目標1. 使用系統的生物信息學和相關實驗方法破譯在常氧條件下可以穩定 SHED 中 HIF-1α 的最優小分子 (SM)。此前，本課題組在生物信息學分析的基礎上已經初步鑒定了兩種 SM 化合物。隨後，我們將通過 HRE 熒光素酶檢查所篩化合物的 HIF-1α 激活能力（包括初步測定以劑量復測），通過免疫印跡檢測HIF-1α 的穩定性，免疫熒光檢測HIF-1α 的羥基化和核異位，qPCR 和 ELISA檢測 VEGF的表達及分泌水平。另外，小分子的生物安全性將通過檢測細胞的 DNA 損傷來進行評估。 目標2. 鑒定 SM 對SHED的存活、血管生成和血管內皮分化能力的影響。本課題將在體外和體內評估細胞活力（包括CCK-8細胞增殖檢測以及活/死細胞雙染色）、血管形成（包括Matrigel基質膠成管實驗和纖維蛋白磁珠實驗）、多向分化潛能（包括成牙本質分化誘導、成骨分化誘導和血管內皮細胞分化誘導）。 此外，SM刺激下的SHED的耗氧量、ROS 清除能力、糖酵解水平和ATP水平也將通過相應的分析進行評估。 目標3. 評估聯合應用選擇性 PHD 和 FIH 抑製劑是否可以更好地模擬 SHED 中缺氧所導致的轉錄因子表達水平的變化。 SMs 將與 FIH 抑製劑結合，一系列的HIF 靶基因的轉錄水平將通過 RNA 測序、微陣列分析和 qPCR 進行檢測和分析。 研究意義： 本項研究將首次使用基於 RNA 測序的生物信息學和相關實驗方法來識別、鑒定和優化可用於在常氧條件下誘導乳牙牙髓幹細胞穩定表達HIF-1α 的小分子化合物。本項研究的發現將開發可模擬缺氧環境的細胞支架結構並探究其在牙髓再生方面的應用。

17125921.value: 氧化鋯作為現代 CAD/CAM 牙科材料，由於其優異的機械強度、美觀性和生物相容性，是牙科修復體的絕佳選擇。為了模仿牙齒的顏色，通常需在白色氧化鋯中添加了著色劑。事實上，天然牙齒不僅包含一種顏色。因此，制備牙科氧化鋯時需要預染色和後燒瓷釉來模仿牙齒顏色。然而，對於上釉的氧化鋯牙來說，烤瓷邊碎裂是一個眾所周知的嚴重問題，它會導致瓷破裂並切割口腔粘膜。作為一種自 1774 年以來的牙科技術，瓷牙染色對技術高度敏感且容易磨損，即缺乏壽命。這些問題是不可修復的，並且，要去除氧化鋯假體時，在高水冷下還會產生火花，以及產生大量氣溶膠。所以，在患者口中要格外小心（例如緩慢地）處理。 為了解決這個問題，我們發現並發明了一種新「光子打印」技術。這技術利用特定範圍的紫外線波長和物理參數來改變氧化鋯的局部顏色。根據我們的初步研究，這不會改變氧化鋯的機械和結晶特性。通過改變紫外線照射的波長和時間，氧化鋯表面的顏色可以從暗白色變為多種牙齒顏色。我們假設這是由於吸收特定光子波長的紫外線導致 Zr-O 鍵的 LUMO-HOMO 處的帶隙 (Eg) 變化。 因此，這項目旨在使用最先進的計算和物理儀器來研究紫外線光子如何作用於氧化鋯的機制。因此，可以精確地預測顏色變化。此外，光子印刷氧化鋯將會在實驗室環境中受到挑戰，以證明氧化鋯具有生物相容性和穩定性。還將製造一個 3D 陣列設備，以在氧化鋯上打印多種顏色，作為概念驗證模型。最終，該項目可轉化為一種產品，它在改變當前氧化鋯染色和著色實踐、解決當前氧化鋯問題以及使真正數字牙科方面具有影響力。

17125921.label: Realisation of objectives
17125921.value: 5.3.1. Objective 1: While both 254nm and 222nm can change the colour of zirconia, the energy input for 254nm would be far insufficient than 222nm. Thus, we have investigated the fundamental interaction between high-energy photons and 3 mol% yttria-stabilized tetragonal zirconia polycrystal (3Y-TZP) was investigated to determine the mechanism of discolouration. Specimens were subjected to 222 nm UV-C irradiation (irradiance: 1.870 mW/cm2) for varying durations (15min to 24-hours). Five irradiation period (15min,30min,1- hour,4- hours, and 24-hours) and one with no treated were employed. Colour difference (DE*) and translucency parameter (TP) were tested using a colourimeter with the specimens before and after UV-C irradiation immediately, 1 day, 3 days, 7 days, and 14 days. Both irradiation time and testing points had significant effects (P<0.001) on colour change and TP change, and there was an interaction between the two factors (P<0.001). A longer irradiation period induced a higher degree of colour change, which was prone to recovery. With the irradiation is longer, the reduction of TP is higher. TP returned to baseline levels within 1 to 3 days across all groups, and the values remained stable thereafter (P>0.05). The crystalline structure were tested by XRD, which showed the same crystalline structure and no monoclinic (m) phase after 222 nm UV-C treatment. Surface roughness (Sa) tested by AFM showed insignificant difference between treated and untreated groups. The biaxial flexural strength (BFS) test showed no significant difference between the specimens before and after UV-C irradiation. Prolonged 222 nm UV-C treatment (>1 h) increased the hydrophilicity and SFE of zirconia surfaces, and those of 4-h and 24-h were higher than 1-h group both immediately and 14 days after irradiation. This fundamental study prove that the 222nm UV-C irradiation provided a simple, safe and promising approach to achieve satisfactory colours on 3Y-TZP in clinical practice. In terms of mechanism, we investigated the colour change when UV-C (222nm) light irradiates 3Y-TZP for 0,15 min,30 min,1-hour,4-hours, and 24-hours. The Band gap was calculated from the absorption spectra with the Tauc plot (UV-visible spectroscopy). The surface composition was evaluated through X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS). The location of the oxygen vacancy was tested through electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR). The computer calculation using Density Functional Theory was conducted with a 2x2x2 tetragonal zirconia supercell for baseline structure, one oxygen atom deleted for VO1 structure, two oxygen atoms deleted for VO2 structure and three oxygen atoms deleted for VO3 structure. The Density of States (DOS) were calculated with the Perdew-Burke-Ernzerhof (PBE) functional in Generalized Gradient Approximation (GGA) method. The Band gap reduced rapidly from the baseline group (3.184 eV) to the 30-min irradiated group (3.097 eV) and further to 3.067 eV after 24h irradiation. The XPS results showed that the electron density around O1s reduced and the electron density around Zr3d increased. The EPR signal (g=2.0037) increases progressively as the UV-C irradiation time is prolonged from 15 minutes to 24 hours. This result proved that UV-C irradiation can generate oxygen vacancies. The DOS showed that there was a Urbach tail formation in forbidden gap, leading the narrowed band gap, which was consistent with the band gap tested in lab experiment. This study confirmed the mechanism of UV-C-induced oxygen vacancies modifying the colour of 3Y-TZP. 5.3.2. Objective 2: To evaluate the biocompatibility of the specimens after UV-C irradiation, specimens were subjected to 222 nm UV-C irradiation (irradiance: 1.870 mW/cm2) under varying irradiation durations (from 15 min to 24 hours) and then used for the cell (MC3T3-E1) culture and biofilm (with bacteria Streptococcus mutans) formation. The cell adhesion and proliferation were conducted. The initial adhesion of cells was evaluated after 4-hour and 1-day incubation, and the proliferation of cells was evaluated after 3-day and 5-day incubation using Cell Counting Kit-8. The initial adhesion of MC3T3-E1 cells on the 24-group was slightly lower than that of the 15-min group and control group (P=0.012), while no difference was found at 1 day between groups (P=0.463). For cell proliferation, at the culture time of both 3 days and 5 days, there was no significant difference. The cell morphology after 4-h culture was observed through SEM. No significant difference was observed between the five UV-treated groups and the control group. The CFU was conducted, and the biofilm structure was captured by confocal laser scanning microscopy with Live/Dead bacterial viability kits. No significant difference in CFU of S.mutans was found among groups (P=0.985). There were differences in the thickness of the biofilms formed: 1-h(21.20±0.73 µm) and 4-h (21.00±1.76 µm) groups got significantly thinner biofilm than the control group (29.20±2.40 µm) (P=0.010). In the study of “Influences of environmental temperature on the UV-C colour printing performance”, we explored the effects of environmental temperature during 222 nm UV-C colour printing on the change of optical properties of 3Y-TZP. The specimens were treated by 222 nm UV-C irradiation as the above studies did. Environmental temperatures were controlled by a cold plate or a hot plate, forming four groups: heating group 1 (HG1, 360.15 K), HG2 (340.15 K), reference group (RG, 310.15 K), and cooling group (CG, 280.15 K). Colour changes were recorded before and at multiple time points (0, 1, 3, 7, 10, and 14 days) post-irradiation to calculate ΔE*, ΔE*00 and TP. Lower environmental temperatures enhanced immediate ΔE* and reduced TP, with quadratic relationships observed. For 24-hour group, immediate ΔE* ranked CG (15.30) >RG (9.43) >HG2 (6.94) >HG1 (5.75), and TP ranked HG1 (10.11) > HG2 (10.16) > RG (8.56) > CG (6.71). Except in HG1, ΔE* and TP showed logarithmic relationships with irradiation time. Lower temperatures accelerated recovery for both ΔE* (Recovery speeds were 3.520, 3.656, 5.694 and 12.308 for HG1, HG2, RG and CG, respectively) and TP. RG showed the highest stabilised ΔE* for t ≥4h, while TP recovery was incomplete in CG groups with longer irradiation times. ΔE*00 has similar trends with ΔE*. Thus, the colour was highly influenced by the environmental temperature. Lower environmental temperatures yield higher immediate ΔE*, greater TP reduction, and faster recovery. 5.3.3. Objective 3: Actual zirconia sample would be in rough and smooth in a same surface. This study investigated a dye-free colouring strategy for 3Y-TZP zirconia by combining surface roughness with 222 nm UV-C irradiation. Specimens with varying clinical roughness 0.142um, 0.056um and 0.003 um were subjected to UV-C exposure. Results indicated that extremely smooth surfaces (0.003um) exhibited the highest immediate colour change and translucency reduction. Smoother surfaces allowed faster colour recovery. Prolonged irradiation caused irreversible translucency loss. In conclusion, surface topography critically influences UV-C colour modulation, demonstrating the potential for photonic colouring and information storage applications in zirconia ceramics. We filed a patent “A Device to Control the Printing of Colours on Ceramics”, a new type of light-controlled printing device combines a light source control and colour control system to achieve colour control and printing at the same time on ceramics. The device can achieve precise customization of the ceramic colour by controlling factors such as light irradiation time and irradiation intensity. Further, in addition to the electronically controlled multi-array light source, the device may have an adjustable grating and a full-angle rotatable stage to customize the ceramic colour printing.

17125921.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17125921.value: The established relationship between the UV-C irradiation period and the colour change in 3Y-TZP lays the foundation for a novel, pigment-free direct-printing technology. Further development should focus on enhancing the colour stability and the precision. It should be investigated whether direct UV-C printing can be identified and improve precision by employing higher-energy light. Besides surface topography alternation and temperature modification during UV-C irradiation, adding dopants can also serve as an improvement method. The stability of the colour change in 3Y-TZP can be further investigated under irradiation in another atmosphere (e.g., Ar).

17125921.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17125921.value: Zirconia is widely used for dental crowns due to its outstanding mechanical properties. However, it takes significant manual work to paint zirconia crowns to match a patient’s native teeth. And the painting layer can chip and then break. This project develops a “photon-printing” technique that uses specific UV-C light (222 nm) to print the colour on ceramics surface directly. It is like how skin tans in the sun without using chemical dyes. The research demonstrates that this light treatment successfully converts white zirconia into natural, yellowish tooth shades without compromising mechanical properties. The project further refines the UV-C irradiation by adjusting the environmental temperature during UV-C irradiation to achieve further control of the light treatment. Consequently, conquering the recovery issue, the dentists could soon customize the colour of restorations in the dental chair, communicating more with patients and achieving the colour automatically.
