17126021.label: Project Objectives
17126021.value: 1. The overarching aim of this project is to determine whether Artificial Intelligence (AI) is better at predicting the occlusal morphology and 3D position of missing tooth/teeth based on the features of remaining dentition than conventional non-AI approaches. Dental prostheses should be designed to follow the natural teeth (biomimetric) when replacement of missing teeth. Occlusal morphology of dental prostheses are the most critical parameters when replacement of missing teeth. Based on our previous studies, we have developed virtual patient models (VPMs) to simulate individual patient’s jaw movements for designing the occlusal morphology of dental prostheses. Despite computer-assisted design (CAD) software are available for assisting the design of dental prostheses, considerable clinical time are still required to capture patient’s data to simulate jaw movement and significant human input are needed to optimize the occlusal morphology of dental prostheses. Teeth of an individual patients are genetically controlled and exposed to mostly identical oral environment, therefore the occlusal morphology and 3D position of teeth in a dental arch are inter-related. It is hypothesized that AI can automated designing the single-tooth dental prostheses from the features of remaining dentition. This is one of the pioneer studies of application of AI in Prosthodontics to determine the occlusal morphology and 3D position of natural teeth. This study use natural teeth as gold standard instead of use teeth generated by dental technicians. Considerable clinical time is usually required to adjust the occlusal surface of dental prostheses to fit into patient’s mouth (occlusion). Objective 1: To compare four deep learning methods/algorithms in interpreting and learning the features of 3D models Currently, it is uncertain which deep learning methods/algorithms is the best in interpreting and learning the features of 3D models. Following our experience in using the AI to detect the gingivitis on 2D photography, the method/algorithm used will affect the outcome of AI system. This project will compare four methods/algorithms in interpreting the 3D models in deep learning. We will first input 200 maxillary dentate training models into our AI system. Then the computer will learn the relationship between individual tooth and remaining dentition. We will collect 100 maxillary dentate teeth models specifically for the validation process. One natural tooth will serve as control and will be removed. We will determine the best deep learning algorithm by compare the geometric morphometric (occlusal morphology) and 3D position of teeth generated by different deep learning methods/algorithms to that of the original natural tooth. The null hypothesis is deep learning methods/algorithms in interpreting the 3D models do not affect the AI prediction of the occlusal morphology and 3D position of single-missing teeth. Objective 2: To compare the AI system with maxillary tooth model alone to maxillary and mandibular (antagonist) models We will determine if the maxillary arch alone or if both the maxillary and mandibular (antagonist) arch are needed for the prediction of single-missing tooth. In theory, the mandibular models provide additional information for the prediction of vertical height and 3D position of missing teeth in the maxillary models. The null hypothesis is deep learning with or without the antagonist (mandibular) teeth models do not result in any differences in the occlusal morphology and 3D position of single-missing tooth predicted by AI. Objective 3a: To compare the occlusal morphology and 3D position of the single-tooth dental prostheses designed by trained AI and by dental technicians Objective 3b: To compare the time required for designing dental prostheses for replacement of single missing tooth by AI and by dental professionals The final objective of this study is to compare 1) the occlusal morphology and 3D position and 2) time required for the AI-designed and human-designed (manual and computer-assisted) single-tooth dental prostheses. The occlusal morphology and 3D position of the dental prostheses will be compared to that of the natural teeth. We will also record and compare the time spent for these design processes. The null hypothesis is when comparing to natural teeth, the occlusal morphology and 3D position of dental prostheses for replacement of single missing tooth designed by AI do not different to that designed by dental professionals. Moreover, the time spend in designing of dental prostheses by AI do not different to that designed by human.

17126421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17126421.value: Human pluripotent stem cells can give rise to various types of functional cells in vitro, and hold great promise for medical applications such as cell-based therapies including cancer immunotherapies. However, current human pluripotent stem cells have scientific and technical limitations that hinder their wider applications, and more research advances are needed. Despite intensive research, it is still challenging to establish bona fide and robust pluripotent stem cells from most animals. Our laboratory has recently developed a technology that enables establishing a new type of stem cells, named expanded potential stem cells or EPSCs, from multiple animal species: mouse, human, pig, and cow. Unlike pluripotent stem cells, EPSCs can efficiently generate all cell types, including the extraembryonic tissues (trophoblasts in the placenta, for instance) and somatic cell types (cells in the liver, the blood, the heart, etc.). Trophoblasts in the placenta are the essential cells for developing embryos and pregnancy. Our published and unpublished research findings demonstrate that human EPSCs are more genetically stable, permits efficient and precise genome-editing, produce trophoblast stem cells, and have unbiased developmental potential to somatic cell lineages. EPSCs may thus provide a new stem cell source for fundamental and translational research, and demand further investigation. In this proposal, we aim to focus on studying BMP signalling, a developmentally important signalling pathway, using single-cell genomics and experimental approaches in EPSCs. Our preliminary results reveal that the evolutionarily conserved BMP signalling is essential in cell fate determination of human and porcine EPSC’s differentiation to the trophoblasts, and in the formation of blastoids from porcine EPSCs. We propose to identify key molecular events and determinants in the generation of trophoblasts and other cells from EPSCs. The research outcomes are expected to advance pluripotent stem cell applications such as production of clinical-grade cell products for therapies, and to facilitate the establishment of EPSCs from more animal species such as rabbit, which is an important model organism in biomedical research. Due to obvious ethical concerns and technical challenges, only limited knowledge is available about early human embryo development. Generation of extraembryonic such as trophoblasts and embryonic cell lineages from human EPSCs can provide a new in vitro model and system for better understanding of human embryonic development, which is directly relevant to the diagnosis and treatment of human disease including infertility and pregnancy associated complications. 人多能幹細胞可以在體外分化產生多種功能型細胞，在醫學上具有重大的應用前景，例如在腫瘤免疫領域的細胞治療。然而，由於人多能幹細胞在科學和技術上具有局限性，限制了它們的廣泛應用。所以，人多能幹細胞的研究亟待尋求科研進展。儘管目前存在廣泛的研究，但是從大部分物種建立真正意義上穩健的多能幹細胞系仍然極具挑戰。最近，我們實驗室開發了一種新的干細胞技術 - 擴展潛能幹細胞 （EPSC）。這種技術可以幫助我們從包括老鼠，人類，豬，牛在內的多個物種中建立全新的干細胞系。區別於多能幹細胞，擴展潛能幹細胞可以有效地產生目前所有的細胞類型，包括胚外組織 （例如來自胎盤的滋養層細胞）和體細胞系的所有細胞類型 （例如肝細胞，血細胞，以及心肌細胞等）。胎盤的滋養層細胞對於胚胎髮育和妊娠十分重要。我們發表的和未發表的研究結果均證明人擴展潛能幹細胞在遺傳上更穩定，在基因編輯上更加有效和準確，並且具有發育全能性，不僅可以產生滋養層幹細胞，同時在體細胞的各譜系分化上也沒有偏倚。擴展潛能幹細胞可以為基礎研究和轉化醫學提供全新的干細胞類型，所以也應當有更多的研究著力於此。在這個課題中，我們著重於研究對於發育至關重要的的骨形成蛋白通路 （BMP signalling）在擴展潛能幹細胞中的作用，主要通過單細胞基因組學和實驗驗證的手段進行研究。我們前期的實驗結果揭示了骨形成蛋白通路在發育和進化中的保守性：首先，BMP4在豬和人的擴展潛能幹細胞的命運決定，即往滋養層細胞的分化中發揮重要作用；其次，BMP4也參與了擴展潛能幹細胞往類囊胚發育的過程。我們在研究方案中提出研究在擴展潛能幹細胞向滋養層細胞及其他類型細胞分化過程中的關鍵分子事件和決定性因素。這項研究成果預期不但能促進多能幹細胞的轉化應用，例如產生用於治療的臨床級細胞類型；還可以促進從其他物種建立多能幹細胞系，例如兔擴展潛能幹細胞的建立，這也是生物醫學領域中重要的實驗動物模型。另外，由於倫理的限制和技術挑戰問題，目前關於人類早期胚胎髮育的知識非常有限。從人擴展潛能幹細胞中產生胚外組織例如滋養層細胞譜系和胚胎來源的細胞譜系，將為人類胚胎髮育提供嶄新的體外模型和研究思路，同時也將對人類不孕症及妊娠相關疾病的診斷和治療產生直接影響。

17126421.label: Realisation of objectives
17126421.value: We have achieved all Objectives listed in the proposal. We have found that BMP signaling is essential for generating both trophoblasts and amniotic ectoderm (AME) lineage cells from human pluripotent stem cells including human EPSCs. Importantly, trophoblast generation only transiently requires BMP4 whereas low and constitutive BMP4 promotes AME cells. Besides establishing human TSCs, we are in the process of developing a culture condition to maintain AME stem cells in long term culture. We have established rabbit EPSC cultures from preimplantation embryos. We will further modify the system for a more homogenous stem cell culture.

17126421.label: Major findings and research outcome
17126421.value: 1. We have used single cell RNAseq and probed the differentiation of human EPSCs toward TSCs. These analyses have revealed several key cellular and molecular events. a. Both TSCs and AME cells are efficiently generated from hEPSCs under the current standard TSC culture condition. For example, we have performed comprehensive and systemic single cell genomics analysis of the TSC lines derived from hEPSCs and demonstrated clearly that these TSCs are highly similar to the published TSC lines directly derived from human preimplantation embryos, placenta tissues and naïve stem cells. b. These EPSC-TSCs are used for studying coronavirus infection in human trophoblasts which were recently published(Ruan, Ye et al. 2022). We found that early syncytiotrophoblasts (eSTBs) generated from hTSCs have some enriched transcriptomic features of peri-implantation trophoblasts, express high levels of angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 (ACE2), and are productively infected by SARS-CoV-2 and its Delta and Omicron variants to produce virions. Antiviral drugs suppress SARS-CoV-2 replication in eSTBs and antagonize the virus-induced blockage of STB maturation. These findings implicate possible risk of COVID-19 infection in peri-implantation embryos, which may go unnoticed. Stem cell-derived human trophoblasts such as eSTBs can potentially provide unlimited amounts of normal and genome-edited cells and facilitate virus research and antiviral discovery. c. We have developed a computation tool, SpatialDM, for rapid identification of spatially co-expressed ligand–receptor and revealing cell–cell communication patterns 2. We have established a AME stem cell culture comdition. Single cell RNAseq analysis confirmed their identity when compared to their in vivo counterparts. We have also found that BMP signaling is required from both TSC and AME derived from hEPSCs. 3. We have successfully established rabbit expanded potential stem cells (rbEPSCs) from rabbit preimplantation embryos. These rbEPSCs exhibit uniform pluripotency, such as high expression of some pluripotency marker genes like Oct4 and Nanog. Additionally, we conducted EB formation experiments using these rbEPSCs, which demonstrated that these rbEPSCs can efficiently form cells of all three germ layers. It is worth noting that these cells can also efficiently form extraembryonic tissues, such as the trophoblast lineage. Furthermore, we have successfully generated blastocyst-like structures called blastoids in vitro using rbEPSCs. These rabbit cell-derived blastoids closely resemble the morphology of true rabbit blastocysts and express similar patterns of markers in ICM and TE regions. Therefore, our study provides a valuable platform for investigating disease models and some translational work, such as antibody production.

17126421.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17126421.value: 1. Further characterization of EPSC-derived TSCs and AME cells. Continued investigation into the cellular and molecular events underlying the differentiation of hEPSCs towards TSCs and AME cells is crucial. This will involve in conducting additional single-cell genomics analyses to explore the similarities and differences between EPSC-derived TSC lines and their in vivo counterparts. Additionally, in-depth studies on the role of BMP signaling in both TSCs and AME cells derived from hEPSCs can provide valuable insights into their functional properties and potential applications. The further development of AME stem cell technology is expected to advance not only fundamental knowledge of cell lineage development in human embryogenesis but also cell-based therapy. 2. Optimization of rbEPSCs culture and blastoid formation. Continued optimization of the culture conditions for rbEPSCs can enhance their utility as a model system for studying pluripotency, embryogenesis, and disease modeling. Further exploration of the differentiation potential of rbEPSCs into various cell lineages, including extraembryonic tissues like the trophoblast lineage, can provide valuable insights into early embryonic development and tissue regeneration. 3. The proposed course of action involves collaborative efforts among researchers, leveraging advanced technologies such as single-cell genomics and stem cell culture techniques, and funding opportunities to support the continuation of these research endeavors. By addressing the key research questions outlined above, the research team can contribute significantly to the fields of stem cell biology, developmental biology, and infectious disease research.

17126421.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17126421.value: We use state of the art genomic and other technologies to generate specific cell types from human stem cells. We focus on the BMP signaling pathway in generating the cells in extraembryonic tissues, such as the placenta, which are disposed after the birth. We find that BMP signaling pathway is essential in the generation of trophoblasts and amniotic ectoderm cells (AME). Our findings provide new knowledge about human embryo development and can be helpful for human fertility research, and for generating functional cells from human stem cells in culture dish. We have cultured out another type of stem cells, called, AME stem cells. These new cells are being tested to serve for cell-based therapy. We have used human trophoblasts generated in this study and discovered that they are good cells for virus infection, such as SARS-CoV-2 and Influenza, and for vaccine study and for antiviral discovery. The rabbit is an important model organism in biomedical research but bona fide stem cells from rabbit embryos are not available. We have developed culture conditions that allow derivation of stem cells from rabbit preimplantation embryos, which would be useful for downstream studies in modeling human disease and in drug evaluation and screens.

17127021.label: Major findings and research outcome
17127021.value: Our results demonstrate that thalamically-evoked spindle-like activities propagate to numerous sensorimotor and non-sensorimotor limbic regions in a frequency- and length-dependent manner. We show that these spindle-like activities promote cross-modal associative memory consolidation by potentiating and engaging a subset of key integrative regions brain-wide. Together, our findings reveal the cross-modal spatiotemporal targeting characteristics of thalamo-cortical spindle activities. We further discover their causal actions during memory consolidation at systems level. Our experimental findings provide direct evidence for the first time that the temporal specificity of neural activity pulse train patterns initiated in sensory thalamus can predetermine their subsequent long-range propagation pathways and targets. This knowledge provides fundamental insights into the brain long-range information transfer and processing. Critically, our results reveal that temporal coding underpins the whole brain functional architecture in presence of the vast and relatively static anatomical architecture.

17127021.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17127021.value: Our study demonstrates the initiation of low frequency oscillatory activities brain-wide as a potential intervention to enhance memory performance or rescue memory decline in future studies. Future studies would include the stimulation of different sensory thalamic nuclei or even brain regions that are critical for sensory processing to uncover similarities and differences across different brain circuits. Further, a more varied and complex temporal patterns of neural activity can be initiated to expand our present knowledge of long-range information transfer and processing.

17127021.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17127021.value: We interrogated the spatiotemporal targeting characteristics of thalamo-cortical spindle activities and their brain-wide actions on associative memory consolidation. Using whole-brain fMRI, optogenetic stimulation, and multisite electrophysiology recordings, we demonstrated the stimulation frequency- and length-dependent brain-wide cross-modal targeting of somatosensory thalamically-evoked spindle-like activities. Using parallel behavioral and visual fMRI experiments, we directly revealed that these evoked spindle-like activities supported visual-somatosensory associative fear memory consolidation by potentiating neural memory representation in key sensorimotor and limbic integrative regions brain-wide, especially superior colliculus, periaqueductal gray, insular, retrosplenial and frontal cortices. We investigate whether and how temporal pattern of neural activity determines large-scale neural activity propagation characteristics using the well-established somatosensory thalamo-cortical circuit and an integrative optogenetic neuroimaging approach. Combining brain-wide fMRI readout with optogenetics will permit perturbation of sensory thalamo-cortical circuits by arbitrarily initiating a range of neural activity pulse train patterns from the VPM thalamocortical excitatory neurons, simultaneous whole-brain monitoring of neural activities evoked by optogenetic perturbation and flexibility to elucidate how optogenetically-evoked neural activity trains can alter task-induced neural activities across the entire brain. This optogenetic fMRI approach is crucial to precisely initiating and characterizing the brain-wide downstream propagation to provide fundamental insights into the long-range sensory information transfer and processing.

17127121.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17127121.value: 海馬體能調節聽覺中樞處理？功能磁共振影像(fMRI)研究

17127121.label: Project Objectives
17127121.value: Design and implement an optogenetic auditory fMRI methodology that combines optogenetic manipulation of hippocampal excitatory neurons with auditory fMRI with high sensitivity, spatiotemporal resolution and experimental efficiency in rats using our 7 Tesla MRI. Delineate the modulatory effects of optogenetically-manipulated neural activity in multiple subregions of the hippocampus along the dorsal-ventral axis on brain-wide central auditory processing using optogenetic auditory fMRI, and examine the underlying neural events. Explore the behavioral effects of optogenetically-initiated hippocampal neural activity on auditory processing, and their associations with changes in auditory-evoked fMRI responses.

17127121.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17127121.value: 聽覺在日常溝通、學習及記憶處理是必不可少的。聽覺中樞功能失調及相對應的感官處理導致辨識及理解複雜的聲音，尤其辨識及理解言語變得困難。然而，現有對於聽覺系統如何準確地解碼、理解及察覺接收到的複雜聲音依然貧乏。尤其在除聽覺中樞以外的聽覺處理路徑（即中腦、丘腦及皮層）仍然未知。 在這個申請中，我們提出研究海馬體在聽覺中樞處理中的功能性角色。海馬體在學習及記憶處理中擔當完善的角色，對準確解讀及理解聲音尤其重要。雖然是間接關聯，但海馬體與聽覺及多感官處理仍然有關。另外，海馬體與皮層及皮層下擁有相互軸突投射，而皮層及皮層下的區域則與聽覺處理有關。由此可見，海馬體極有可能包括於聽覺處理網絡之內。我們假設海馬體於調節聽覺中樞處理扮演核心的角色。我們將會運用光遺傳和全腦fMRI 所結合的神經影像方法來研究海馬體的活動如何影響聽覺中樞處理。組合光遺傳及fMRI 可讓在海馬體引起指定細胞種類的特定神經元活動，同時亦可觀察全腦神經活動的傳播，及海馬體對聽覺有關的感官和認知功能的影響。 在初步的研究（包括已發表及未發表）中，我們發現以5赫茲刺激腹側海馬（ventral hippocampus, vHP）的興奮性神經元能引起猛烈的神經活動傳播到初級聽覺皮層。我們亦以兩組不同聲音（包括自然或人工/噪音聲效）配合5赫茲光遺傳技術來刺激vHP。vHP刺激調節了在聽覺中腦、丘腦及皮層中只對自然聲效的聽覺反應。其中，光遺傳刺激vHP在正或負活動有差不多的增強反應。可是對倒置聲效（即人造聲響）或寬頻帶噪音卻沒有類似的增強效果。我們初步的發現闡述了海馬體在全腦聽覺處理行為相關的聲響時擔當從上到下的調節角色。 為了驗證我們的假設，我們計劃首先改良光遺傳聽覺fMRI 技術，從而捕捉到有更好靈敏度的聽覺刺激引起全腦活動影像並作出分析。藉此技術，通過光遺傳刺激或抑壓海馬體中不同位置的興奮性神經元，並結合電生理記錄分析，我們可以有系統地研究海馬體在聽覺中樞處理中的功能角色。此外，我們會研究因光遺傳調節海馬體而導致的，以及與聽覺刺激引起fMRI 反應有關的功能和行為的結果。這個研究的成果可拓展我們對除傳統路徑以外大規模聽覺中樞處理的理解。再者，這個項目可以為研究全腦聽覺處理網絡打好基礎，有助日後研發聽覺功能失調的治療方案。

17127121.value: Project objectives were not fully completed due to the lack of sufficient funds to accomplish the more technically challenging and laborious research tasks that were outlined for each of the three objectives, particularly the examination of animal behavioral changes in optogenetically-initiated hippocampal neural activity on auditory processing in Objective 3. Although we were not able to accomplish 100% of said tasks, we were able to compromise to achieve a significant portion of it as shown in our journal publications listed in Section 8 and conference proceedings listed in Section 9 of the report.

17127121.label: Major findings and research outcome
17127121.value: We experimentally revealed that the hippocampus, a limbic region vital for learning and memory functions, modulates auditory responses to natural sound processing along the early ascending auditory pathway by monitoring auditory responses during optogenetic vHP stimulation or pharmacological inactivation using large-view fMRI. We discovered a robust hippocampal influence on BOLD responses to vocalizations, but not artificial/basic acoustic stimuli, in the auditory midbrain, thalamus, and cortex. However, due to the limited sensitivity of fMRI, we do not discount the weak neural activity changes in small neural populations in response to artificial/basic acoustic stimuli at IC, MGB and AC that can be caused by vHP outputs. Nevertheless, these fMRI results directly support the large-scale and faciliatory influence of the hippocampus on vocalization sound processing and shaping the corresponding response selectivity in early auditory centers within the ascending auditory pathway. We uncovered long-range hippocampal modulation of vocalizations within the ascending auditory pathway during 5 Hz optogenetic stimulation at vHP. However, we do not preclude the potential modulatory effects of other stimulation frequencies like 10 Hz. Even though BOLD activations evoked by 10 Hz optogenetic stimulation were not as widespread as 5 Hz, we still observed robust activations in subcortical regions (e.g., AMG, MS, LS, DBB) albeit with weaker activations in cortical regions (e.g., AC, Prh, Cg). Overall, our findings suggest that hippocampal top-down modulatory outputs, which may be triggered by behaviourally relevant auditory inputs, were augmented by optogenetic stimulation of vHP to enhance responses to vocalizations.

17127121.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17127121.value: The present fMRI study established a top-down and large-scale modulatory role for the hippocampus throughout the ascending auditory pathway, including the auditory midbrain, thalamus and cortex, to facilitate natural sound processing such as vocalizations. Our findings expand our present understanding of central auditory system beyond the traditional cortex centric views. Future studies should elucidate the precise hippocampal modulatory processes of natural sound that arise from the brain-wide auditory information processing networks.

17127121.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17127121.value: Despite its prominence in learning and memory, hippocampal influence in early auditory processing centers remains unknown. Here, we examined how hippocampal activity modulates sound-evoked responses in the auditory midbrain and thalamus using optogenetics and functional MRI (fMRI) in rodents. Ventral hippocampus (vHP) excitatory neuron stimulation at 5 Hz evoked robust hippocampal activity that propagates to the primary auditory cortex. We then tested 5 Hz vHP stimulation paired with either natural vocalizations or artificial/noise acoustic stimuli. vHP stimulation enhanced auditory responses to vocalizations (with a negative or positive valence) in the inferior colliculus, medial geniculate body, and auditory cortex, but not to their temporally reversed counterparts (artificial sounds) or broadband noise. Meanwhile, pharmacological vHP inactivation diminished response selectivity to vocalizations. These results directly reveal the large-scale hippocampal participation in natural sound processing at early centers of the ascending auditory pathway. They expand our present understanding of hippocampus in global auditory networks.

17200021.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17200021.value: 了解和優化鈣鈦礦太陽能電池的運行穩定性

17200021.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17200021.value: Prof NAZEERUDDIN, Mohammad Khaja Prof Yin, Wanjian

17200021.label: Project Objectives
17200021.value: Establishing the trap evolution and DTDD coupled model for the study of PSC degradation. We propose to establish an experimentally verified spatial and temporal trap evolution model coupled with DTDD model to address the degradation of PSCs beyond the limitation of typical solar cell (SC) models. As the interaction between the mobile ions/atoms and the trap state evolution has not been fully elucidated, we will study the trap effects on the diffusion of mobile ions/atoms in the whole device, which can be from the diffused particles in a PSC, as well as the decomposition and halide/cation segregation of a perovskite (all of which are widely considered as the dominant photo- and thermal- induced degradations). We will then introduce time- and space- dependent trap states and the corresponding trap-assisted recombination into DTDD model, and comprehensively study the effects of carriers (mobile ion, electron, hole) and trap states on the degradation of PSCs. The model will then be experimentally verified. Consequently, the coupled model will provide the fundamental and insightful device physics on the trap evolution and trap-assisted recombination loss in PSC degradation. Diagnosing the device flaws in PSCs. Under continuous operation, the PSC deterioration is dominantly caused by the device flaws, including surface recombination at two interfaces of perovskites, bulk recombination of perovskite and low conductivity of PSC layers. Meanwhile, the interaction between the mobile ion migration induced electric field and the device flaws will result in various features found in J-V hysteresis. We therefore introduce the J-V hysteresis with rich information on PSC electrical properties as an indicator for the device flaws. By re-visiting and understanding the different general J-V hysteresis features, we can qualitatively investigate each of the device flaws by theoretical study through the coupled model, and by experimental study through designing and characterizing specific PSCs. With these comprehensive studies, we will not only consolidate the physical understanding of the device flaws but also validate the coupled model study on the J-V hysteresis as an effective and quick diagnosis to identify device flaws of PSCs. . Identifying the origins of PSC operational degradation. Since identifying the origins of PSC degradation and efficiency losses during the device operation is very desirable for optimizing PSC performances, we will introduce the diagnostic method in Objective 2 for in-situ real-time study of the origins of PSC degradation during the long-term stability test which will shorten the time and cost of device optimization. Importantly, through optical correction of the coupled model using detailed balance theory, we will qualitatively and quantitatively evaluate the classified efficiency losses by the weighted contribution from each loss term, including the bulk recombination loss in perovskite, surface recombination loss at each interface of perovskite, optical loss, and loss from the low conductivity in the different layers. Meanwhile, we will investigate the electroabsorption spectroscopy of cross sections of PSCs at different degradation stages with the coupled model study to determine the degradation components/locations. Overall, the studies will offer the in-situ and effective diagnosis on the operational stability of PSCs, and allow as to determine and understand the degradation origins, qualitative and quantitative efficiency losses, and degraded locations. Optimization of the operational stability of PSCs. Based on the coupled model offering comprehensive PSCs degradation physics, we will experimentally and theoretically study various CTL materials, to realize highly performed and stable PSCs made from various perovskites.

17200021.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17200021.value: 鈣鈦礦太陽能電池 (PSC) 可實現 25.5% 的顯著功率轉換效率 (PCE)，已發展成為一種有前途的成本效益光伏技術。 同時，它們的壽命發展仍然落後於幾千小時。 因此，嚴重受限的長期 PSC 操作穩定性已成為實際應用的主要問題。 儘管使用仔細的封裝來消除水分/氧氣，但許多實驗研究證實了 PSC 降解。據報導，這種降解主要受移動離子/原子的擴散支配，包括鈣鈦礦離子、載流子傳輸層（CTL）離子和電極原子。效率衰減可歸因於擴散粒子產生的複合陷阱狀態。因此，了解降解研究中的動態陷阱演變和相應的重組損失至關重要。同時，典型的太陽能電池模型，包括傳統的漂移擴散模型、詳細平衡模型和電路模型，無法處理 PSC 退化過程中陷阱態的時間和空間演變。為了直觀地研究離子/原子擴散的影響，我們將考慮封裝良好的 PSC（即沒有水分/氧氣效應），並開發一個經過實驗驗證的陷阱演化和動態陷阱結合漂移擴散耦合模型，以提供基本的和有見地的設備退化物理學。 重要的是，由移動離子遷移感應電場和載流子傳輸/複合之間的相互作用控制的電流密度 (J)-電壓 (V) 特性的滯後特徵包括 PSC 電特性的豐富和關鍵信息。結合 J-V 滯後和表徵實驗的耦合模型研究，我們將開發一種快速有效的器件缺陷診斷方法，包括分別在鈣鈦礦和界面處的體和表面陷阱輔助複合，以及 PSC 層的低電導率。該方法將適用於提供 PSC 降解起源的原位實時識別。非常需要在操作期間識別 PSC 損失及其變化。最終，我們將建立一個研究器件物理和 PSC 穩定性預測的平台，用於預測 PSC 的運行壽命和 PCE，從而實現協同實驗 PSC 優化。 因此，這項工作對於提高我們對 PSC 退化的理解以及優化操作穩定性的策略多樣化具有根本性和實際意義。

17200221.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17200221.value: 本研究擬提出一類新穎的「可計算自適應語義樹」（CAST）模型，整合建築信息模擬（BIM）及區塊鏈。在香港及全球建築業中，BIM技術已被廣泛地規範和採納，並成為了一項億萬產值的新興業務。然而，工程中基于「增量」的分佈式 BIM 協作實踐與集中式「存量」BIM文件存儲之間存有根本上的兩難困境。例如，在每個小修訂後需重複發送巨大的（假設500MB ）且冗餘的 「存量」BIM 文件；這對分解和驗證修訂來說既不高效（時間和存儲成本）也不準確。另外，諸如社會動盪和 2019 年冠狀病毒病 (COVID-19) 等一些外部風險因素，容易導致建築工程中近距密切合作不足，將加劇該困境的痛苦。因此，本研究擬提出一類新穎的CAST模型，將「增量」修訂語義從巨大且冗餘的BIM文件中提取出來（亦可逆向還原BIM），並整合分佈式部署的區塊鏈，最終形成「區塊鏈CAST」方案來解決這一兩難困境，服務於建築業數字化。

17200221.label: Realisation of objectives
17200221.value: 5.3.1 Scope of investigation  BIM is a multi-billion-dollar business in the architecture, engineering, construction, and operations (AECO) industry and has increasingly been mandated in many countries and regions. Hong Kong mandates BIM uses in all major (>HK$30M) public works by 2020 and all major private projects (>HK$300M) by 2026.  This project studies a novel computational adaptive semantic tree (CAST) model and blockchain 3.0/4.0 technology to building information modeling (BIM) collaboration for construction projects.  We define a theoretical CAST model for BIM exchange. In CAST, any BIM model or file is presented as a tree of semantics, including components, properties, relations, and combinations thereof.  We aim to apply CAST model to enhance BIM exchange for various construction management practice. Examples are information sharing, digital twinning, cross-chain synchronization, IoT synchronization, BIM schema extension, ESG reporting, etc. 5.3.2 Objectives achieved  Objective 1 was achieved sustainably [100%]. The BC-CAST model of BIM focuses on both graph presentation of BIM, graph computation, as well as exchange on blockchain. The initial graph model of CAST was preliminarily studied in a pilot paper (Xue and Lu 2020) which triggered this project. In this project, we extended the graph model in Xue and Lu (2020) to 3.0/4.0 tree models in five aspects: o Paper [8.1] [Note: Paper #1 in Sect. 8 (Journal/Chapter)] on Blockchain 3.0/4.0: Designed and compared Blockchain 3.0 for BIM-related construction digital twins, which yields big data volume and real-time exchange needs. We reported Blockchain 3.0 saved 99.2~99.8% of exchange latency. o Chapter [8.2] on cross-chain data exchange. o Paper [9.1] on paradigm comparison: Analyzed BIM collaboration on blockchain, with comparisons with centralized and decentralized cloud. o Paper [9.3] on BIM schematic extension: reported an BIM schema extension to get BIM blockchain-ready, and o Paper [8.4]: on open-source openBIMdisk to realize the BC-CAST model as Blockchain 3.0 paradigm. o Paper [8.5 (Minor revision)]: Finalized Blockchain 4.0 paradigm for BIM-related construction digital twins, which enhances Blockchain 3.0 with automated reasoning and alerts.  Objective 2 was achieved [100%]. Several tests were conducted on early versions of CAST for industrial BIM. Award [11.1] reported an integration of blockchain with open BIM in a MiC project, where the compression ratio was up to 99.9% and the best BIM change (in ifcJSON format) compression coding was gzip-base85. We have conducted several other experiments on the efficiency improvement of CAST with everyday uses, such as on a BIM virtual chain disk. Award [11.3] demonstrated another test of integrating CAST model and quality issues detected from 4D point clouds. Papers [8.1, 8.4, 8.5] reported the experimental metrics.  Objective 3 was achieved [100%]. Paper [9.2] has demonstrated that off-shore IoT updated project BIM can be applied to quality assurance platform with blockchain. Papers [8.3, 9.4] reported construction blockchain for accurate information sharing and ESG reporting with peer-to-peer stakeholder networks. Paper [8.4] develops a CAST-based virtual chain disk for main-stream BIM platforms, and shared it via GitHub and HKU’s repository. We chose OpenBIM standard to maximize the compatibility to all mainstream BIM platforms. Paper [8.5] will also share the software codes for dissemination on mainstream BIM platforms. 5.3.3 Deviations from the original plan  N.A. 5.3.4 Extensions and success beyond the original plan Apart from the successful execution of the project, we also looked into a few topics related to the project.  Most findings have been applied to an ITF project “’BIM Square’”: blockchain and i-Core-enabled multi-stakeholder building information modelling platform for construction logistics and supply chain management in Hong Kong” (ITP/029/20LP, HK$10.36M).  Journal paper [3] reported that blockchained BIM is strongly demanded for accurate information sharing in construction management according interviews with professionals. This paper also won the 2022 Best Peer Reviewed Paper Award from Journal of Management in Engineering (Impact factor = 7.4, ranked 6/139 in Civil Engineering), ASCE.  Conference Paper [6] led to another GRF project (No. 17212725) “A novel blockchain smart contract and zero-knowledge proof approach for accurate and secure access to building information models for multi-stakeholder collaboration”. The PI is the newly graduated PhD student trained through this GRF; now I serve as the Co-I for the new GRF.  A reaching out to several Chinese institutions for possible pilots of heritage BIM (HBIM) on chain cases: o Key Scientific Research Base of Application of Spatial Information Technologies in Cultural Heritage Conservation (Tsinghua), National Cultural Heritage Administration (NCHA), China o Guangdong OkayGIS Ltd. o The collaboration led to a prestigious National Social Science Foundation of China (NSSFC) Major Program project titled “Research on coordination mechanisms for the conservation and revitalization of urban cultural heritage” (25&ZD115, 2025-2028)

17200221.label: Major findings and research outcome
17200221.value: Executive summary of findings and outcome Orientation: This project aims to address the growing demand for efficient, trustworthy, and scalable Building Information Modeling (BIM) collaboration in the architecture, engineering, construction, and operations (AECO) industry. Note that BIM has become economical and increasingly mandated. This project has developed and validated new Blockchain 3.0/4.0 technologies based on our CAST model, with tests and findings on enhancing BIM exchange and construction management practices. Outputs: 5 journal/Chapter papers (4 published, 1 minor revision), 6 conference papers, 3 international academic Awards, 1 local award. PhD trained: 2 (graduated in 2023 and 2025, respectively) Theoretical findings: The primary theoretical contribution is the formalization of CAST as a semantic tree representation of BIM models, in which components, properties, and relationships are explicitly structured for computation and exchange. Building upon earlier graph-based studies, the project advanced CAST into adaptive tree models compatible with Blockchain 3.0 and 4.0 paradigms. These models enable semantic-level BIM transactions, cross-chain data exchange, schema extension, and automated reasoning, thereby overcoming the latency, redundancy, and Internet dependence that limit conventional blockchain and cloud-based BIM collaboration. (See journal/chapter papers 8.1-8.5) Empirical findings: The tests demonstrated impressive performance. Experimental tests across modular and industrial construction scenarios showed that Blockchain 3.0 implementation reduced BIM exchange latency by 99.2–99.8% and achieved compression ratios up to 99.9% for BIM changes; meanwhile, object-level semantic traceability was well maintained. The open-source virtual-disk-like implementation, openBIMdisk, helps average users as a Blockchain-based virtual disk; This virtual disk delivered millisecond-level response times and practical interoperability with mainstream openBIM standards. (See journal/chapter papers 8.1, 8.4) Interesting findings for future work: Beyond simple efficiency, we confirmed the applicability of CAST-based blockchain BIMs for higher-level construction management goals. Examples include IoT-synchronized digital twins, offshore-to-onsite quality assurance, peer-to-peer information sharing, and environmental, social, and governance (ESG) reporting. Extending further, the Blockchain 4.0 paradigm integrates automated machine learning–based prediction and interpretable reasoning, achieving high predictive accuracy (R² = 0.974) in distributed construction project management. (See journal/chapter papers 8.2, 8.3, 8.5, Conference 10.6, Awards 11.3, 11.4)

(No. 17212725) “A novel blockchain smart contract and zero-knowledge proof approach for accurate and secure access to building information models for multi-stakeholder collaboration”. Note: The PI is one of the newly graduated PhD students trained through this GRF; now I serve as the Co-I for the new GRF. - A prestigious National Social Science Foundation of China (NSSFC) Major Program project titled “Research on coordination mechanisms for the conservation and revitalization of urban cultural heritage” (25&ZD115, 2025-2028). The above three grants well articulate the future development of the research, i.e., (a) applications to local industry; (b) theoretical "digging" on exciting new topics (such as zero-knowledge proof); and (c) Extending to national/international Surveying disciplines.

17200221.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17200221.value: BIM is a multi-billion-dollar business in the architecture, engineering, construction, and operations (AECO) industry and has increasingly been mandated in many countries and regions. Hong Kong mandates BIM uses in all major (>HK$30M) public works by 2020 and all major private projects (>HK$300M) by 2026. This project studies a novel computational adaptive semantic tree (CAST) model as Blockchain 3.0/4.0 paradigms to leverage building information modeling (BIM) collaboration for construction projects. The CAST model exchange BIM with minimum redundancy, where any BIM model or file is presented as a tree of semantics, including components, properties, relations, and combinations thereof. We tested CAST in Blockchain 3.0/4.0 paradigms in several projects for enhancing BIM exchanges; source codes are open online. Recommended use cases are information sharing, digital twinning, cross-chain synchronization, quality assurance, BIM schema extension, ESG reporting, etc.

17200321.value: 具相干衍射和數字全息成像的計算高分辨率顯微鏡

17200321.label: Project Objectives
17200321.value: The first objective of the project is to achieve high-resolution imaging containing amplitude and phase information through designing robust and computationally efficient phase retrieval algorithms. This involves further developing our dual alternating direction method of multipliers (D-ADMM) approach for this inverse imaging problem, and demonstrating its use through numerical simulation and optical laser experiment on two setups. The first one is the conventional coherent diffraction imaging, and the second one incorporates a reference, which results in interference and holographic data capture. We will perform extensive study to compare with results from these two setups, and the use of alternative phase retrieval algorithms. The second objective of the project is to broaden the imaging capability to extended objects through the technique of ptychography. With further derivation of our computational algorithm and extensive numerical simulation, we aim to achieve an optimal tradeoff in field-of-view overlap and algorithmic robustness, so that when used with radioactive sources such as x-ray, the overall dosage can be kept at minimum. A second part of the objective is to demonstrate the advantages of incorporating a reference in ptychographic imaging. Similar to the above, we will conduct both numerical simulation and optical laser experiments to provide feedback for us to fine-tune our approaches. We also aim to investigate multiplexing the illumination and capture in ptychography to further reduce the overall scan time. The third objective of the project is to make use of deep learning in pixelated reference design, and demonstrate that this can further improve quality and computational efficiency in reconstructing the complex information of the object. The numerical simulation will help provide labeled data, while extensive experiments will be carried out to verify the results. Furthermore, with ptychographic imaging we will also investigate using broadband sources and demonstrate applicability of our methods. This will enable the use of ultrafast laser for illumination, and consequently the imaging of quickly evolving phenomena at high resolution.

17200321.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17200321.value: In 2020, humanity experiences firsthand the devastating power of tiny viruses. Being able to observe them clearly is a key part of winning the battle. Indeed, probing into the microscopic world is essential in many domains, from inspecting crystal structures and integrated circuits to understanding biochemical phenomena at the cellular level. Specialized instruments such as scanning electron microscope and atomic force microscope are capable of delivering extremely high magnification, but they are bulky and expensive, and researchers continue to pursue optical technologies that can complement these tools. In this proposal, we aim at this goal from the perspective of computational optical imaging. This paradigm pushes the capability of imaging systems through a holistic co-design of computational algorithms and imaging architecture. Specifically, we aim to develop robust and efficient computational methods to tackle the phase problem, which is critical because phase contains important information about the object. However, it is lost in electronic detection as sensors typically capture only intensity data. Recovering the phase is challenging because the computational problem is non-convex and there is inherent ambiguity in the solution. Nevertheless, we have developed powerful optimization techniques that can be up to the task. Furthermore, this computational advance will integrate with development in the imaging system design. We target to combine two imaging techniques, namely, coherent diffraction and digital holography, where the latter complements the former by producing an interference pattern that better preserves the optical wavefront for the subsequent computational image reconstruction. Moreover, we will investigate three additional aspects. First is the extension to ptychography, which is a form of scanning coherent diffraction imaging to handle extended objects, and we aim to integrate it with holographic imaging in a similar manner. Second is the use of broadband source, where multiplexing of the ptychographic capture is needed and further development in the computational algorithm is also necessary. Yet, this will enable the use of ultra-short pulses, facilitating not only high spatial resolution but also high temporal resolution in the capture. Third is the holographic reference design, where we intend to leverage data-driven methods that are capable of delivering unconventional patterns. Through numerical simulations and optical laser experiments, we aim to establish our approach as a dependable addition to the arsenal of tools for computational high-resolution microscopy, and help to tackle scientific challenges where visualization at the micro- and nano-scale can bring new insights. 在2020 年，人類親身體驗微了細小病毒的毀滅性力量。能夠清楚地觀察它們是贏得這仗的關鍵。的確，探討微觀世界在許多領域都是不可或缺的，這包括檢查晶體結構和集成電路，以及了解細胞水平的生化現象。儘管掃描電子顯微鏡、原子力顯微鏡等專用儀器能夠提供極高的放大倍數，但它們體積龐大和昂貴，所以研究人員必須繼續探究以光學技術補足這些工具。 我們提議從計算光學的角度來達成這個目標。這種範式通過協同設計算法和成像架構，以增強成像系統的能力。具體來說，我們的目標是開發穩健有效的計算方法來解決相位問題，這是至關重要的，因為它包含拍攝對象的重要信息，但傳感器一般只能記錄光的強度。這當中挑戰很大，因為計算問題是非凸的，並且解決方案中固有歧義。儘管如此，我們已經開發了強大的計算優化技術，可以勝任這任務。此外，這將與成像系統設計的開發相結合。我們的目標是結合兩種成像技術，即相干衍射和數字全息，其中後者通過產生干涉圖案來補充前者，更好地保留了後續計算圖像的光學波前重建。此外，我們將致力另外三個方面。首先是重疊關聯成像的擴展，這是掃描相干衍射成像的一種形式處理擴展對象，我們的目標是將它與全息成像以類似的方式合成在一起。其次是使用寬帶源，其中需要多路復用重疊關聯成像，和進一步發展計算的算法。然而，這將使超短脈衝的使用成為可能，不僅可以提高空間分辨率，還可以提高時間分辨率。第三個是全息參考設計，我們打算利用數據驅動提供非常規模式的方法，通過數值模擬和光學激光實驗，我們的目標是建立用於計算高分辨率的工具，並幫助解決在微觀和可視化方面的科學挑戰，讓納米尺度的影像可以帶來新的知識。

17200521.value: 供应链规划与对冲：对联动供需风险的风险管理

17200521.label: Project Objectives
17200521.value: Solving a risk-neutral profit-maximization problem with multiple suppliers having random interdependent capacities and also demand-supply correlation, to develop ordering rule: which suppliers to be selected and order allocation to each selected supplier. With a CVaR objective without hedging, we will develop the ordering rule. The results will be compared to those from (1) to examine the effect of risk aversion on ordering decision. With a CVaR objective, the problem of jointly optimizing ordering and financial hedging will be solved to develop optimal hedging strategy and ordering rule. The results will be compared to those from (1) and (2) to examine how financial hedging affects the ordering decision and enhance CVaR. With a CVaR objective, the problem of determining optimal ordering policy with operational hedging will be solved. The results will be compared with (3) to identify situations under which one type of hedging dominates the other.

17200521.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17200521.value: The increasingly complex supply chain is vulnerable to uncertainties from both supply and demand sides. This can cause significant financial losses if the risk is not properly managed. Adding to the challenge is the fact that these uncertainties are usually correlated. On the supply side, many suppliers are impacted by the same set of factors, for instance, material flows, commodity prices, government policies, geographical factors, etc. Meanwhile, demand and supply uncertainties are well likely to be correlated when the entire supply chain is exposed to the same set of systematic events. For example, the recent COVID pandemic significantly impacts the supply chain: amid the widespread supply shortage, many industries also experience plunging demand while some others (e.g., personal protective equipment, food, home appliances) see demand spikes. Majority of extant literature that considers both supply- and demand-side uncertainties only focuses on risk-neutral profit maximization with assumption of independent supply and demand. We propose this research to tackle the problem of risk management for supply chain facing the correlated uncertainties from both supply and demand. The focus is on risk hedging and we will work with a general modeling framework capturing the interconnected uncertainties among the (unreliable) suppliers’ capacities and also between demand and supply. Specifically, a supply chain state and a financial component that each affects both supply- and demand- sides are modeled, along with noises/volatility specific to suppliers and demand. We will solve the risk management problem of maximizing Conditional Value at Risk (CVaR) over downside scenarios by jointly optimizing the ordering decision (i.e., which suppliers to be selected and how to allocate order among the selected suppliers) and a financial hedging strategy. Then, we will study how the risk aversion and financial hedging affect order decision compared to order-only (i.e., no hedging) profit-maximizing policy and enhance the CVaR. Parallel with financial hedging, we also consider an operational hedging strategy that allows postponement of some order at a cost. We will compare the two types of hedging strategies and identify the situations under which one dominates the other. We expect the outputs to benefit both financial firms and companies operating in complex supply chains. For the former, the results have the potential to add to their product portfolios. For the latter, the outputs equip the firms with risk management tools that enhance their resilience to adverse situations, thereby improving their sustainability in the long run. 供应链的逐渐复杂化使其对风险的承受力是脆弱的，且风险同时来自供应方和需求方。妥善风险控制的缺失将造成严重的经济损失，而供需双方的风险常是联动的，使风控本身更具挑战。对于供应方，很多供应商被同一组风险因子影响，例如原料流动，商品价格，政府政策，地理因素等。同时，当整个供应链暴露在同一系统性事件下时，需求与供应的不确定性很可能是联动的。 例如，近年来的新型冠状病毒疫情严重影响了整个供应链：在普遍的供应短缺中，众多产业同时遭遇需求下降期间，个别产业（例如救护器具，医疗卫生用品，食品，家电等）却经历了需求上涨。多数考虑供需两方不确定性的现有文献，仅关注风险中立的收益最大化，同时假设了供需两方的不确定性相互独立。我们计划在这个研究中解决对有联动的供需双方不确定性的供应链风险管理问题。 这项研究的关注点是风险对冲。我们将建立一个一般化的模型框架来捕捉供应商之间互相关联的不确定性，以及供需双方联动的不确定性。具体操作中，我们将用一个供应链状态量和一个金融风险量（其各自同时影响供应方和需求方）以及供需方各自的噪音来进行建模。我们会同时优化订货策略（选择哪些供货商以及怎样在被选择的供应商中分配订单）和金融风险对冲策略来最大化在负面情境下的条件风险值(CVaR)。并且，我们会研究风险厌恶与金融风险对冲如何影响订货策略与提升CVaR，并将其与无风险对冲的风险中立收益最大化策略进行对比。平行于金融风险对冲，我们也会考虑运营风险对冲。后者允许在增加成本的前提下推迟部分订单。我们会比较这两类对冲策略，并且识别出具体情况下的更优对冲策略。 我们预计这项研究的成果会使金融服务公司，以及在复杂供应链中运营的企业获得最大收益。对于前者，我们的研究成果有增益其产品组合的潜力。对于后者，我们的研究成果会提供风险管理工具，使得这样的企业在不利的情境中更具有弹性从而提高其长期的可持续性。

17200721.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17200721.value: 岩石受熱強化機理研究

17200721.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17200721.value: 隨著人類對地球深處的不斷探索，深地工程，諸如地熱開採、核廢料埋存等，開始在結晶岩地層中不斷湧現。地層溫度通常以3-4 oC/100 m 的速率向深處增加，從而對岩石的力學性能造成重要影響。早期研究表明，400 oC 以上的高溫能顯著降低岩石強度，主要原因為：(1) 高溫造成熱裂縫的萌生和擴展和 (2) 高溫加速化學反應。但是，對於大多數深地工程而言，埋深附近的地層溫度大約在25-175 oC ，例如瑞士Gotthard 基地隧道，埋深2450m, 溫度46 oC (Lucerne, Switzerland: AlpTransit Gotthard AG, 2016) 和南非Mponeng金礦，埋深4000m，溫度66 oC (Wadhams, 2011)。採取室溫或者400 oC 以上高溫條件下的岩石力學參數作為深地工程的設計依據可能並不合適。在25-175 oC 溫度範圍內，一些實驗研究表明岩石可被高溫強化，而不是被弱化。岩石受熱強化的機理何在？通過全面的文獻綜述並總結25-175 oC 溫度範圍內岩石細觀結構發生的變化，我們傾向於認為受熱強化是結晶岩的固有性質，涉及四個主要因素，即熱膨脹，溫度裂縫阻礙應力裂縫，水分蒸發和熱分解共同作用的結果。通過一系列前期室內試驗和數值模擬, 我們初步確認了大理岩熱強化現象。然而，上述四個因素的相互作用非常複雜，目前還無法揭示主導性因素以及熱強化的機理。本研究項目旨在 (1) 自主研發熱力耦合加載設備，具備施加圍壓的性能，進行熱力耦合室內試驗；(2) 開發數值模型，定性和定量地補充、驗證和延伸實驗結果。通過進行全面的岩石破壞檢測，我們可以孤立上述四個因素，並從細觀角度研究熱強化機理。據我們所知，本研究首次系統探索結晶岩熱強化背後的機理，深入理解25-175oC範圍內溫度對岩石力學性能的影響，研究結果可為深地工程進行安全、經濟的設計提供有力技術支撐。

17201221.value: 在线相关匹配理论以及在线算法中的应用

17201221.label: Project Objectives
17201221.value: OCS: Improve the design and analysis of OCS and its relaxation semi-OCS to achieve better lower bounds on level of correlation. Find hard instances that show matching upper bounds. Multi-way OCS: Introduce the definitions of multi-way OCS and its relaxation multi-way semi-OCS. Design the corresponding algorithms that achieve nontrivial level of correlation. Applications: Analyze the performance of the algorithms in AdWords and Display Ads utilizing the OCS and multi-way OCS algorithms obtained from the first two objectives. Design algorithms for Online Matching with General Vertex Arrivals and Online Makespan Minimization using OCS and multi-way OCS.

17201221.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17201221.value: 在线决策是计算机科学与运筹学中的核心问题。本项目研究一种名为《在线相关选择》的新技术。这项技术最近在《在线广告关键字》和《显示广告》等十几年以上的开放问题上取得了突破。在理论方面，本项目将致力于改进当前的在线相关选择算法及其分析，从而取的理论最佳的负相关性。在应用方面，本项目将进一步优化本技术在上述两个问题中的应用，并探索此技术在在线调度理论等其他在线优化问题中的应用。

17201221.label: Realisation of objectives
17201221.value: We have successfully achieved all three objectives stated in the proposal. # Objective 1 In our paper published in FOCS 2021, we characterized the optimal semi-OCS. We also designed a new OCS and showed a new impossibility result, both of which improve the previous work and remain state-of-the-art as of today. # Objective 2 In the same FOCS 2021, we designed the first multiway semi-OCS, and its guarantees remain state-of-the-art as of today. A research group from Stanford introduced the first multiway OCS in the same FOCS 2021 conference. We therefore turned to the stochastic setting and designed the first multi-way rounding algorithm for stochastic online matching. The results are published in STOC 2022. Subsequently, we improved the technique and introduced the Stochastic OCS in a paper published in FOCS 2024. # Objective 3 In the FOCS 2021 paper, we applied the improved OCS to obtain better results for Display Ads. In the FOCS 2024 paper, we applied Stochastic OCS to resolve two open problems related to AdWords and Display Ads, among other applications. We further have a manuscript in submission about the application of OCS in online scheduling, including makespan minimization.

17201221.label: Major findings and research outcome
17201221.value: We found that OCS is a powerful and very general technique. Using OCS, we resolved four major open questions related to AdWords and Display Ads, in both adversarial and stochastic models of online algorithms. Further, we demonstrated (in a manuscript under submission) that the technique can be applied to other online algorithm problems, such as online scheduling.

17201221.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17201221.value: - The extension to stochastic models, namely, Stochastic OCS, calls for further study. - Further applications of OCS on problems beyond matching are also in a preliminary stage and have much potential for future research.

17201221.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17201221.value: In summary, the project has systematically studied the design and analysis of Online Correlated Selection. This novel algorithm design technique converts fractional online resource allocation decisions into integral ones with minimal loss in efficiency. The project has successfully provided state-of-the-art algorithms and applied them to problems in online advertising, scheduling, and other areas.

17201421.label: Project Objectives
17201421.value: To construct lattice-based verifiable random functions (VRFs). We plan to construct verifiable random functions from standard lattice-based assumptions. As an intermediate result, we first investigate the construction of lattice-based NIWI proof system in the standard model. Then we will construct VRFs from the proposed NIWI proof system and conduct security analysis for the schemes. To construct lattice-based watermarkable pseudorandom functions (PRFs) with public extraction. We plan to investigate the construction of secure watermarkable PRF with public extraction from standard lattice assumptions. To achieve this goal, we would construct a new lattice-based functional encryption scheme that is able to run a specific algorithm on an encrypted PRF key, where the algorithm evaluates a PRF and compares the output with a given value. To design efficient and secure threshold signatures based on lattice. We plan to investigate methods to construct efficient and post-quantum secure threshold signature from lattice. This involves the design of full threshold protocols from lattice-based single-user signatures, including Dilithium and Falcon, two candidates of the NIST post-quantum standardization. In terms of efficiency, we will consider the balance of communication, computation, and rounds. We will also investigate the security of our lattice-based threshold signature in the quantum random oracle models, which provides a more reasonable and stronger guarantee of quantum-resistance than the classical random oracle. We will consider the concrete security under quantum attacks and finally conduct security analysis and complexity analysis. To construct a lattice-based non-interactive aggregate signature scheme. We plan to investigate the construction of lattice-based non-interactive aggregate signature scheme with logarithmic signature size. To achieve this goal, we would explore the possibility of constructing lattice-based aggregate signature from a lattice-based signature scheme and a succinct non-interactive argument. Moreover, we will also investigate the constructions of a lattice-based signature scheme supporting efficient verification and a specific succinct non-interactive argument suitable for our construction.

As an intermediate result, we first investigate the construction of lattice-based NIWI proof system in the standard model. Then we will construct VRFs from the proposed NIWI proof system and conduct security analysis for the schemes.

To construct lattice-based watermarkable pseudorandom functions (PRFs) with public extraction. We plan to investigate the construction of secure watermarkable PRF with public extraction from standard lattice assumptions. To achieve this goal, we would construct a new lattice-based functional encryption scheme that is able to run a specific algorithm on an encrypted PRF key, where the algorithm evaluates a PRF and compares the output with a given value.

To design efficient and secure threshold signatures based on lattice. We plan to investigate methods to construct efficient and post-quantum secure threshold signature from lattice. This involves the design of full threshold protocols from lattice-based single-user signatures, including Dilithium and Falcon, two candidates of the NIST post-quantum standardization. In terms of efficiency, we will consider the balance of communication, computation, and rounds. We will also investigate the security of our lattice-based threshold signature in the quantum random oracle models, which provides a more reasonable and stronger guarantee of quantum-resistance than the classical random oracle. We will consider the concrete security under quantum attacks and finally conduct security analysis and complexity analysis.

To construct a lattice-based non-interactive aggregate signature scheme. We plan to investigate the construction of lattice-based non-interactive aggregate signature scheme with logarithmic signature size. To achieve this goal, we would explore the possibility of constructing lattice-based aggregate signature from a lattice-based signature scheme and a succinct non-interactive argument. Moreover, we will also investigate the constructions of a lattice-based signature scheme supporting efficient verification and a specific succinct non-interactive argument suitable for our construction.

17201421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17201421.value: 公鑰密碼學對現代互聯網安全和隱私至關重要。然而，當今廣泛使用的所有公鑰密碼方案在量子計算面前都不安全。量子計算設備的快速發展，推動了抵抗量子計算攻擊密碼方案的研究、開發和標準化，該新興領域被稱為後量子密碼學 (PQC)。 本項目的研究重點是格密碼。格密碼是一種建立於被稱為格的幾何對象的密碼系列。格密碼是後量子密碼學的領跑者之一，在美國國家標準與技術研究院正在進行的後量子密碼算法標準化評估中，大部分的候選算法都基於格，最近，美國國家安全局發布了一份公開聲明，表示預計格密碼系統將被批准用於保護國家安全系統(NSS) 。 基於最近PQC的許多令人振奮的進展以及我們的前期工作，本項目旨在探索基於格的密碼學的最新技術。具體來說，我們將研究核心密碼學原語的新構造，包括偽隨機函數、電子水印和數字簽名。這些原語是安全電子商務、公鑰基礎設施以及區塊鍊和數字貨幣等新技術的重要組成部分。 本項目在問題的定義和解決方法方面都具有極高的創新性，其成果將對 PQC 產生重大影響。鑑於量子計算的發展以及數據的保質期的需求，及時完成本項目將協助提升現有的密碼系統以應對量子威脅。

17201421.label: Realisation of objectives
17201421.value: We have achieved all the objectives of this project. Specifically, our achievements for each objective are as follows. Objective 1. We proposed a lattice-based programmable hash function based on the NTRU lattice and the middle-product LWE assumption. This function can be treated as a pseudorandom function (PRF). We also proposed a new, efficient post-quantum zero-knowledge proof (ZKP) system by incorporating zero-knowledge into ethSTARK. Together, the programmable hash function and the ZKP enable the construction of lattice-based verifiable random functions (VRFs): the hash function serves as a generator of pseudorandom strings, and the ZKP produces proofs for the verifiable computation of the corresponding outputs. Objective 2. We proposed the first public-key watermarkable PRFs based on standard lattice assumptions. Specifically, we introduced a new framework that constructs watermarkable PRFs from (i) an unobfuscatable PRF with robust learnability and (ii) a new primitive called a hinting watermarkable PRF. The hinting variant relaxes standard watermarking by allowing the extraction algorithm to use an additional “hint” about the watermarked PRF key. Under this framework, we obtain (public-key) watermarkable PRFs with standard pseudorandomness from (public-key) hinting watermarkable PRFs with relaxed pseudorandomness. We then construct public-key hinting watermarkable PRFs from standard lattice assumptions, thereby resolving an open problem on constructing public-key watermarkable PRFs. In addition, we provide the first construction of a robust, unobfuscatable PRF, which is of independent interest. Objective 3. We investigated different approaches to constructing threshold signatures, namely, from linkable ring signatures, t-out-of-n proofs of partial knowledge, and secure 2-party computation. During this investigation, we developed (i) a new way to realize secure 2-party multiplication from additive homomorphic encryption and its associated zero-knowledge proof system, and (ii) a new framework for constructing linkable ring signatures (with instantiation combining hash functions and succinct zero-knowledge proof from hash functions). Concretely, a t-out-of-n threshold signature can be realised using t instances of linkable ring signatures over the same ring. Objective 4. We showed that a lattice-based aggregate signature can be constructed from a standard lattice-based signature scheme and a post-quantum zero-knowledge succinct non-interactive argument of knowledge system. We use our lattice-based programmable hash function as a building block to realise a lattice-based digital signature, and we augment ethSTARK with zero-knowledge to obtain a post-quantum zero-knowledge proof-of-knowledge. The combination of this non-interactive post-quantum proof-of-knowledge system with the lattice-based signature yields an aggregate signature scheme.

17201421.label: Major findings and research outcome
17201421.value: The major findings of the project include the following: verifiable randomness, watermarkable pseudorandom functions, threshold signatures, and aggregate verification mechanisms, which collectively form a comprehensive cryptographic toolkit capable of sustaining strong security in the quantum era. First, we introduced new programmable lattice based hash and pseudorandom functions built upon both the NTRU lattice and the middle product Learning with Errors (LWE) assumption. These primitives unify the functionality of randomness generation, verifiability, and adaptability across different cryptographic contexts. When integrated with our newly developed post-quantum zero-knowledge proof system (derived from ethSTARK with added zero-knowledge guarantees), these constructions yield the lattice-based verifiable random functions (VRFs) suitable for transparent, publicly auditable randomness in distributed and blockchain systems. Second, the project resolved a long-standing open question by demonstrating the existence of public key watermarkable pseudorandom functions (PRFs) under standard lattice assumptions. We developed a new theoretical framework that transforms hinting watermarkable PRFs with relaxed pseudorandomness into standard watermarkable PRFs, achieving both public extractability and robustness. This result establishes an essential theoretical bridge between lattice-based pseudorandomness and indistinguishability obfuscation, marking a major conceptual advance in the study of verifiable functional cryptography. Third, during the investigation of threshold signatures, we developed important improvements in one of the core building blocks, i.e., secure 2-party multiplication from additive homomorphic encryption. We consider various additive homomorphic encryption and their associated zero-knowledge proofs. They can be used for improved threshold signatures, and also standard-alone building block for other primitives such as verifiably encrypted signatures. Another way to construct threshold signatures is by stacking linkable ring signatures, and our investigation lead a new framework for linkable ring signatures of size O(loglog n), where n is the number of signing parties. Finally, our lattice-based programmable hash function leads to lattice-based signature in the stanard model. Combing this with our enhanced zero-knowledge proof system, we obtained a logarithmic-size non-interactive aggregate signature. We also investigated zero-knowledge proof with high prover efficiency from vector oblivious linear evaluation, which can be realised from the learning parity with noise assumption (LPN assumption), another post-quantum hardness assumption of growing interest from the cryptographic community. The research outcomes of this project resulted in the publication of conference papers presented at leading venues, including the ACM Conference on Computer and Communications Security (ACM CCS), the IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy (SP), Annual International Cryptology Conference (CRYPTO) and the European Symposium on Research in Computer Security (ESORICS).

17201421.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17201421.value: The research presented in this project provides a useful foundation for further work on lattice-based post-quantum cryptographic systems. Looking ahead, our focus will be on translating these building blocks into real-world applications, particularly in settings that require post-quantum security, verifiability, and accountability. Future work will explore application-driven deployments of lattice-based VRFs and verifiable computation with post-quantum zero-knowledge proofs, public-key watermarkable PRFs for model/IP protection and provenance in distributed software and AI supply chains, and lattice-based aggregate and threshold signatures for scalable authentication in large systems. We will also investigate how these primitives can be integrated into practical protocols and platforms such as secure identity and access control, auditable cloud services, and blockchain/Web3 infrastructure to provide post-quantum assurances while meeting real operational requirements.

17201421.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17201421.value: In this project, we develop new post-quantum cryptographic techniques aimed at maintaining digital security in the era of powerful quantum computers. Our research focuses on lattice-based cryptography, which is widely regarded as a promising defense against quantum attacks. We design several new cryptographic building blocks to strengthen privacy and trust in digital systems. First, we develop advanced hash functions and zero-knowledge proofs for generating verifiable random numbers. These outputs can be publicly checked for fairness, making them useful for applications such as secure voting, lotteries, and blockchain systems. Second, we develop watermarkable pseudorandom functions, which can support tracing and ownership verification of digital assets while keeping sensitive information private. Third, we study linkable ring signatures as a foundation for building signature systems that allow multiple users to authenticate data collaboratively, improving scalability in large systems. Finally, our programmable hash functions and post-quantum zero-knowledge proofs also support aggregate signature designs, which can compress many signatures into a single, compact proof to reduce storage and speed up verification. Overall, this project advances the development of quantum-resistant cryptographic techniques and provides practical foundations for future applications, including secure cloud services, privacy-preserving financial systems, digital identity, and trustworthy online communication in the post-quantum era.

17201721.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17201721.value: 鋰離子電池通常包含液態電解質，是一種最先進的電化學儲能技術，但由於固有的局限性使其很難達到更高能量密度。鋰金屬電池由於具有固態聚合物電解質和高壓的陰極，成為了下一代鋰電池的首選之一。然而，固態聚合物電解質很難同時滿足兩種要求，出色的電化學性能和熱穩定性。值得注意的是，單離子導體因其陰離子基團被固定在聚合物網絡中，與其他傳統的液體或者固體電解質相比有很多優點，例如電化學穩定性的提升，極化的減小以及對枝晶生長的高效抑制。但是，固態電解質較低的電導率和必要添加的有機溶劑仍限制了其在商業化器件中的應用。 本研究將應用一種新興的多孔材料來作為無溶劑的單離子聚合物電解質，使其具有改進的電化學性能和安全性。我們將通過兩種途徑來設計用於無溶劑單離子導電電解質的多孔材料：1）採用支化的有機交聯劑；2）插入含電荷的交聯劑。通過精心地設計材料的固有特性，我們將用這些材料製作電池原型，評估其作為全固態電池使用的能力。這些新型多孔材料不僅可以提高無溶劑單離子導體的性能，還可以為高性能固態電解質建立一個全面的設計準則。我們相信，我們的方法能夠幫助全固態電池向工業應用平滑過渡。此外，以全固態電池為特色的儲能電網建設將以其創新和先進的技術為香港成為世界領先的清潔能源城市作出貢獻。

17201721.label: Realisation of objectives
17201721.value: This research pursued a dual objective: 1) the synthesis of a novel class of anionic porous aromatic frameworks (PAFs), and 2) the validation of their utility within prototype battery systems. We have successfully realized the goals outlined in the original proposal, encompassing material design, rigorous characterization, and practical demonstration in energy storage contexts. The specific achievements are delineated below. Initially, to establish fundamental design principles for highly conductive electrolytes, we engineered a series of solvent-free anionic network polymers. These networks form a diamondoid architecture comprising borate anions bridged by ethylene glycol linkers with varying stoichiometric ratios, a strategy designed to modulate segmental mobility. Our findings indicate that enhanced segmental dynamics correlate directly with elevated ionic conductivity, suggesting that transport is governed largely by polymer chain mobility relative to interanionic spacing. Conversely, we observed that excessive free branching paradoxically restricts ionic transport despite faster segmental dynamics, likely due to kinetic frustration at the coordination sites. The optimal network configuration exhibited exceptional Li+ selectivity, high oxidative stability, and robust resistance to dendrite propagation during galvanostatic cycling, positioning these solvent-free polymers as promising solid-state electrolytes for lithium-metal batteries. Building upon these design rules, we subsequently developed microcrack-free anionic network polymer membranes via a facile one-step click chemistry approach. These membranes demonstrate superior electrochemical performance, characterized by a high cation conductivity of 3.1 × 10⁻⁵ S cm⁻¹ at elevated temperatures, a broad electrochemical stability window exceeding 5 V, and intrinsic non-flammability. We attribute these performance gains to the strategic tethering of borate anions within the defect-free lattice, which accelerates selective Li+ transport while mechanically suppressing dendritic growth. Consequently, Li-metal batteries incorporating these membranes achieved remarkable stability, retaining 92.7% capacity with an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.867% over 450 cycles at high thermal loads. Beyond energy storage, we expanded the scope of anionic functional materials to include novel energy harvesting mechanisms. Addressing the challenge of sustained, high-density power generation from low-humidity environments, we designed a moisture-activated electricity generator (MEG). By synergizing water flow with auxiliary anion migration within a salt concentration-gradient cationic gel, this system overcomes traditional limitations. The resulting MEG device delivers longevity exceeding 50 days and a substantial power density of 13.8 mW m⁻² even at 30% relative humidity. Furthermore, utilizing a modular stacking strategy combining serial and parallel configurations allows the system to meet the diverse power requirements of practical electronic appliances, highlighting the potential for ubiquitous, sustainable energy harvesting. Finally, we investigated the fundamental mechanisms of contact electrification, a phenomenon central to technologies ranging from energy harvesting to electrospraying. While electron transfer is traditionally viewed as the dominant mechanism in solid-solid contact electrification, the role of mobile ions remains a subject of intense debate. Investigating solid-ionomer interfaces, we provide compelling evidence that electrons and ions contribute concurrently to charge transfer, with their relative dominance modulated by environmental conditions. Our data reveal that ionic transfer significantly enhances electrification at humidity levels above 50% RH. Additionally, ion-doping of non-ionic polymer surfaces confers resistance to humidity-induced degradation of the triboelectric effect. Although less than 2% of available ions participate in transfer, these findings fundamentally reshape our understanding of contact electrification, suggesting that manipulating ionic contributions offers a new pathway to optimize electrostatic devices.

17201721.label: Major findings and research outcome
17201721.value: This study reports the successful development of a novel class of anionic porous aromatic frameworks tailored for advanced battery applications. These materials exhibit superior physicochemical properties, characterized by marked enhancements in ionic conductivity, high ion selectivity, and a broad electrochemical stability window, alongside robust lithium, thermal, and mechanical stability. A pivotal finding of this work is the critical influence of network architecture—specifically the control over interanionic spacing and the degree of crosslinking—on ion transport dynamics. We observed that increasing segmental mobility at a fixed interanionic distance results in a four-fold amplification of ionic conductivity, establishing a key design principle for future electrolytes. Furthermore, by mitigating microcrack formation and integrating immobile borate anions within the polymer matrix, we engineered microcrack-free anionic network polymer membranes that significantly elevate the safety and cyclability of Li-metal batteries at elevated temperatures. These systems outperform Li|electrolyte|LFP configurations utilizing state-of-the-art electrolytes. The tethered borate anions within the defect-free membrane structure serve a dual function: facilitating selective Li+ cation transport and providing exceptional suppression of dendrite propagation throughout prolonged cycling. Consequently, this strategy offers a versatile platform for improving the energy density and safety profiles of various storage systems, potentially establishing a new paradigm for the design of anionic electrolytes in next-generation lithium batteries. Based on these findings, we have been successful in publishing our results, as demonstrated by 4 publications and 1 manuscript in preparation in total. All findings from this project have been published in highly esteemed academic journals, including 2 in Advanced Functional Materials (IF=19.0), 1 in Advanced Science (IF=14.1), and 1 in Chemical Engineering Journal (IF=13.2). The findings have been publicized by PI and RPG students in 5 international conferences (2 of them are invited talks), such as MRS 2023 Spring, Nano Korea 2023, MRS 2023 Fall, MRS 2024 Spring, and NGPT 2024. Three students, Jingyi Gao, Wenyi Hu, and Haoyu Fu, are trained under the partial support of this project.

17201721.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17201721.value: In this project, we successfully developed interpenetrating network polymers as single-ion conducting (SIC) electrolytes for Li-metal batteries, demonstrating superior electrochemical, thermal, and ion-selective stability. However, a significant limitation persists: ionic conduction remains intrinsically coupled to the structural framework, resulting in restricted room-temperature ionic conductivities (<10^-5 S/cm) that fall below the threshold for practical high-performance batteries. While plasticizers can enhance conductivity, they compromise mechanical integrity and reintroduce safety risks associated with flammable solvents. To overcome this inherent trade-off between mechanical strength and ionic mobility, future research must focus on decoupling conduction pathways from the structural matrix. We propose leveraging high-entropy design principles—an approach proven to resolve strength-toughness conflicts in metallurgy and activity-selectivity issues in catalysis—to engineer novel SIC network polymers. We postulate that by systematically inducing local symmetry breaking within the ionic and non-ionic domains of highly crosslinked networks, we can disrupt the coupling effect. This high-entropy strategy aims to facilitate solvent-free, fast ionic conduction at room temperature without sacrificing the mechanical robustness required for scalable applications, thereby opening a new frontier in solid-state electrolyte engineering.

17201721.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17201721.value: To power the next generation of electric vehicles and sustainable cities, we need batteries that hold more energy without compromising safety. Traditional high-energy lithium-metal batteries have struggled with risks like flammability and internal damage caused by dendrites, which are spiky microscopic growths that ruin battery life. Our project tackles these challenges by replacing the dangerous liquid chemicals inside batteries with a new, advanced solid material. We engineered specific anionic network polymers that are flexible enough to allow energy-carrying ions to flow freely but strong enough to block harmful dendrite spikes physically. By refining the molecular structure to prevent microscopic cracks, we created a solid membrane that functions exceptionally well even at high temperatures and is naturally non-flammable. The results were significant: our new battery components maintained over 90% of their capacity after hundreds of charging cycles, far outperforming current standards. This technology offers a promising solution for making batteries that are not only powerful but also safe and long-lasting. Successfully deploying these materials represents a vital step forward in supporting Hong Kong’s transition to clean energy and green transportation.
