17201921.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17201921.value: Membrane-based water reuse has been widely practiced in many cities and regions facing severe water supply shortages. Nevertheless, commercially available reverse osmosis (RO) membranes often exhibit inadequate removal of organic micropollutants, including some highly toxic disinfection byproducts and endocrine disrupting compounds. Another critical challenge for membrane-based water reuse is the relatively high specific energy consumption (SEC). To produce one cubic meter of recycled water, approximately 1 kWh of electricity is required, which largely results from the low water permeance of RO membranes and their high propensity for fouling. This proposed project aims to address the critical needs of enhancing micropollutant removal and reducing SEC for water reuse by developing a novel RO membrane featuring an interlayered composite structure. We hypothesize that the inclusion of a highly permeable and selective interlayer in a thin film composite polyamide RO membrane can simultaneously increase the membrane water permeance, reduce its fouling tendency, and improve its selectivity. Specifically, the proposed project will be implemented through three inter-related work packages (WPs): (i) experimental investigation on how the interlayer affects membrane water permeance and fouling propensity, (ii) experimental evaluation of the role of the interlayer in membrane selectivity and rejection of pollutants, and (iii) theoretical modeling of the separation performance of interlayered RO membranes. Our preliminary experimental results show up to an order of magnitude improvement in membrane permeance through the inclusion of a simple interlayer coating, which is further supported by our initial modeling results. Such an increase in water permeance, together with the enhanced fouling resistance, can result in 50-80% reduction in SEC. The interlayered membrane structure offers further opportunities for enhancing the removal of toxic organic micropollutants, thereby leading to a breakthrough in membrane-based water reuse. The proposed project will establish a new theoretical framework to provide fundamental insights into the transport behavior of water, salts, and micropollutants in interlayered composite RO membranes. In addition, novel experimental methods will be developed for dissecting the role of the interlayer in membrane separation performance. The resultant high-performance RO membranes, with simultaneously optimized water permeance, fouling resistance, and membrane selectivity, can result in a quantum leap for water reuse, leading to a more sustainable water supply in Hong Kong and many other places. 膜法水回用技術在許多嚴重缺水的城市、地區得到了廣泛應用。然而現有的反滲透 (RO) 膜無法充分去除諸如消毒副產物、內分泌幹擾物等有毒有機微污染物。同時，傳統RO 膜水滲透性低而污染傾向高，導致其較高的特定能耗，生產一立方米循環水用電量高達 1 千瓦時。本項目將開發一種具有夾層複合結構的新型RO 膜來同時提高微污染物去除率和減少特定能耗。在薄膜複合聚酰胺 RO 膜中引入高滲透性、高選擇性夾層以增進膜的滲透選擇性和抗污能力。項目包含三個相互關聯的工作包：1. 研究中間層如何影響膜透水和污染傾向，2. 評估夾層在膜選擇性和污染物截留中的作用，3. 建立夾層RO膜分離性能的理論模型。初步實驗結果表明簡單的夾層塗層可將膜滲透性提高近一個數量級，而初步理論模型也支持了這一結果。膜滲透性和抗污性的增強有望使水回用的特定能耗減少50-80%，並更好的去除有機物微污染物。項目將為水、鹽、微污染物在夾層複合 RO 膜中的傳輸行為建立新的理論框架，同時開發新的實驗方法來剖析夾層在膜分離性能中的作用。由此產生的高性能 RO 膜將同時優化滲透性、選擇性、抗污染性，實現水回用技術的巨大飛躍以提供可持續的供水。

17201921.label: Realisation of objectives
17201921.value: 1. The first objective of this project is to perform an experimental investigation on how interlayers regulate water permeation in composite membranes and their role in water permeance and fouling propensity. We studied how porous substrates with lower porosity adversely impact the water transport pathways of conventional thin-film composite (TFC) membranes, resulting in reduced water permeance, uneven water flux distribution over the membrane surface, and more severe membrane fouling. Various interlayers were designed and synthesized, including (i) Fe (III)-tannic acid complex, (ii) natural silk nanofibers, (iii) 2D metal-organic framework, and (iv) polydopamine. The resulting interlayers and the interlayer-containing thin-film nanocomposite (TFNi) membranes were systematically characterized. Water flux measurements using cross-flow filtration experiments confirmed greatly enhanced water transport pathways, resulting in major enhancement in water permeance. The inclusion of interlayers also resulted in more uniform flux distribution over membrane surfaces, which helped to mitigate membrane fouling. By independently synthesizing polyamide rejection layers and the interlayers, the contributions of each layer were systematically identified. We show that the inclusion of an interlayer introduces greater permeance enhancement and fouling reduction for membranes with thin polyamide rejection layers and/or smaller substrate pores. These investigations result in fundamental insights to the funnel effect and gutter effect as well as practical strategies for membrane performance enhancement. As a result, the first objective has been successfully achieved. 2. The second objective of this project is to perform an experimental investigation on how interlayers influence the transport of solutes (particularly organic micropollutants (OMPs)) through the TFNi membranes and how they affect membrane rejection and selectivity. We performed systematic tests using Fe (III)-tannic acid complex and 2D metal-organic framework as model interlayer materials. For example, the research team applied TFNi of Fe (III)-tannic acid to remove various types of OMPs, such as endocrine disrupting chemicals (EDCs), pharmaceutically active compounds (PhACs), and perfluoroalkyl substances (PFASs). Compared to the pristine TFC membrane without interlayer, TFNi membrane exhibited crumpled morphology and its rejection layer was denser, better cross-linked and possessed smaller average pore size with narrower distribution. Significant enhancement in water-OMPs selectivity of PhACs and PFASs was observed. The mechanism lies in the effects of interlayer in improving the membrane permeance to water and meanwhile reducing the permeance to some OMPs by enhancing size exclusion effects. Similarly, the 2D metal-organic framework incorporated TFNi membranes exhibited improved rejections of OMPs, successfully demonstrating the great potential of using interlayers for enhancing pollutant removal. As a result, the second objective has been successfully achieved. 3. The third objective of this project is to develop a theoretical model of the transport behaviors and separation performances of TFNi membranes. The research team implemented a three-dimensional solution-diffusion model to analyze a geometry-induced funnel effect and an interlayer-promoted gutter effect, which was calibrated with the experimental results obtained in this project. The simulation results suggest that even an ultrathin interlayer of a few nanometers in thickness could serve as a low-resistance gutter layer, which minimizes the transversal water transport in the less permeable polyamide layer and thereby mitigate the unfavorable funnel effect. The research team then developed a simple analytical model to provide more intuitive understanding of the water transport and solute rejection in TFNi membranes. This simple analytical model confirms the critical importance of interlayer selectivity on the overall rejection of TFNi membranes. Our study establishes a theoretical framework for understanding the fundamental transport mechanisms in TFNi membranes, which provides important guidance on the future development of high-performance desalination membranes. As a result, the third objective has been successfully achieved.

17201921.label: Major findings and research outcome
17201921.value: Role of substrate on water transport and fouling. We investigated how porous substrates can regulate the water transport pathways, demonstrating more evenly distributed water flux at increasing substrate porosity (Publication #2). Higher substrate porosity effectively enhanced the membrane water permeance and alleviated membrane fouling. The substrate design is particularly important for ultrathin membranes (Publication #5), highlighting TFNi as a promising approach for overcoming the traditional permeance-selectivity upper bound (Publication #7). For the first time, we present a novel method to calibrate the intrinsic water permeability of TFC membranes by accounting for non-linear water transport pathways, revealing that the calibrated value can be several times of the apparent permeability (Publication #8). TFNi membrane synthesis and testing. (a) Polydopamine interlayer (Publication #8). By independently preparing the polyamide (PA) rejection layers and polydopamine interlayers, we demonstrated that the gutter effect is far more effective for membranes suffering from more severe funnel effect. For the thin-PA membrane with a low-porosity substrate, the water permeance was enhanced by approximately 75 % with the interlayer incorporation, while the flux reduction during the fouling test was significantly mitigated. (b) Silk interlayer (Publication #4). The silk-interlayer membrane achieved a water permeance of 96.2 ± 10 L m−2 h−1 bar−1 and a Na2SO4 rejection of 96.0 ± 0.6% under cross-flow filtration mode, offering close to 80% reduction in energy consumption. (c) Fe (III)-tannic acid interlayer (Publication #3). Compared to the pristine TFC membrane, TFNi membrane exhibited crumpled morphology and its rejection layer was denser, better cross-linked and possessed smaller average pore size with narrower distribution. Significant enhancement in water-OMPs selectivity of PhACs and PFASs was observed. (d) 2D MOF interlayer (Publication #6). The uniformly distributed MOF interlayers significantly improved pure water permeance from 10.6 to 32.1 L m⁻² h⁻¹ bar⁻¹ while maintaining a high rejection of 97.0% towards Na₂SO₄. Moreover, the optimized membrane showed significant improvements in OMP removal. Modeling. A three-dimensional solution-diffusion simulation using COMSOL Multiphysics show that interlayer can serve as a low-resistance gutter to minimize the transversal water transport in the less permeable polyamide layer and thereby mitigate the unfavorable funnel effect (Publication #1). A simple analytical model is also developed to provide more intuitive understanding of the water transport and solute rejection in TFNi membranes (manuscript under preparation).

17201921.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17201921.value: 1. The current project focused on the bench scale development of flat-sheet TFNi membranes. Future studies may further extend this strategy to synthesize hollow fiber TFNi membranes, which offers major additional advantages such as self-supporting nature, greater packing density, easier scaling up, potential for submerged operation in addition to traditional cross-flow operation. 2. Given the very high water permeance of some TFNi membranes (e.g., around 100 L/m2.h), non-conventional applications of these membranes may be further explored, such as vacuum-driven filtration. 3. The long-term fouling behavior of TFNi membranes may be further verified.

17201921.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17201921.value: Traditional thin-film composite membranes, widely used for water reuse applications, face limitations such as low removal of some toxic pollutants and high energy consumption. Aiming to address these critical challenges, this project develops a novel thin-film nanocomposite membrane featuring an interlayered structure (TFNi). The project was implemented through three inter-related work packages: (i) experimental investigation on how the interlayer affects membrane water permeance and fouling propensity, (ii) experimental evaluation of the role of the interlayer in membrane selectivity and rejection of pollutants, and (iii) theoretical modeling of the separation performance of interlayered RO membranes. We show that the inclusion of a highly permeable and selective interlayer in a thin film composite membrane can simultaneously increase the membrane water permeance, reduce its fouling tendency, and improve its selectivity. The resultant high-performance TFNi membranes can result in a quantum leap for water reuse, leading to a more sustainable water supply in Hong Kong and many other places.

17202121.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17202121.value: 自利性代理分配與選擇問題的分佈式協議：公平性、安全性與通訊效率

17202121.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17202121.value: This project will investigate distributed protocols that securely realize mechanisms for various allocation and selection problems among self-serving agents. In blockchain applications, an assignment protocol enables fair distribution of goods or chores among agents without any trusted central authority, and a selection protocol lets investors with conflicting interests decide which combination of crowdfunding projects to sponsor. In the literature, deterministic notions of fairness have been considered, but sometimes randomness is necessary. For instance, in the lottery problem, which is a special case of both assignment and selection problems, one prize is given to exactly one agent. The only reasonable mechanism is to select one agent uniformly at random as the winner. However, without a trusted authority, the agents themselves are responsible for generating the randomness in a distributed protocol. Unfortunately, standard cryptographic approaches such as secure multi-party computation require a majority of the agents to be honest, which is not a realistic assumption, because every agent might deviate from the protocol to increase its utility. Nevertheless, the lottery problem can be solved by the tournament tree protocol, which employs a commitment scheme based on standard assumptions such as one-way functions. Even though one cannot prove security in the strongest sense that the winner is unbiased, the tournament tree satisfies some game theoretic notions of security. For example, an honest agent following the protocol will be guaranteed at least the same probability of winning, even if all other agents conspire against it. Moreover, agents forming a coalition also cannot increase their combined chance of winning. Inspired by this framework, we will extend the game theoretic notions of security to protocols solving more general assignment and selection problems. However, unlike the lottery problem in which all agents have the same preference, it is known that the more complicated problem structure implies some impossibility results. For instance, even with a trusted authority, there is no mechanism for a general assignment problem that can achieve all the following properties simultaneously: truthfulness, Pareto optimality, equal treatment. Hence, even formulating the right security notions for protocols realizing the mechanisms for such problems is a challenging task. Finally, to have practical impacts, our protocols will also achieve communication efficiency. Since our preliminary work shows that the tournament tree protocol has optimal round complexity under some security requirement, we will explore approximate notions of security, and design protocols that have desirable tradeoffs between security and communication efficiency. 本課題將會進行關於自利性代理分配與選擇問題之安全實現機制的分佈式協議研究。在區塊鏈應用場景中，一個分配協議能夠在不依賴可信中央機構的情況下將物品或工作任務公平地分配予每一位代理，而選擇協議使得有利益衝突的投資者們作出對哪一眾籌組合進行贊助的決定。在文獻中，關乎公平的確定性概念已有所研究，不過，隨機性在一些情況下仍屬必要。例如，彩票問題作為一個結合分配與選擇問題的特殊例子，其規定一份獎品只能分配予僅一名代理。唯一公平並且合理的機制便是以同等機率隨機地抽選一名代理作為其得獎者。而在可信中央機構缺失的情況下，則需要由這些代理在分佈式協議中擔任生成該隨機性的角色。然而，標準的密碼學方法（如安全多方計算）要求參與協議的代理中有絕大部分代理會如實地執行協議。這個假設並不切合實際，因為每一名代理都有可能會為了增加自己的利益而背離協議。然而，彩票問題可以通過採用基於標准假設（例如單向函數）的承諾方案的競賽樹協議解決。儘管競賽樹協議不能證明獲勝者是無偏的這一事件在最強意義上的安全性，但它可以滿足博弈論中的一些安全性概念。例如，即使所有其他代理都密謀反對遵守協議的誠實代理，誠實代理都將至少有與協議保障的相同獲勝概率。此外，代理們組成聯盟也不能增加他們獲勝的總概率。受這個框架啟發，我們將把博弈論中的安全性概念擴展到解決更一般的分配和選擇問題的協議上。然而，與所有代理都具有相同偏好的彩票問題不同的是，更複雜的問題結構意味著一些不可能的結果。例如，即使有受信任的機構，也沒有機制可以為普通的分配問題同時實現以下的所有屬性：真實性，帕累托最優，平等對待。因此，即使為實現此類問題的機制的協議制定正確的安全性概念都是一項具有挑戰性的任務。最後，為了產生實際影響，我們的協議還將實現通信效率。由於我們的初步工作已經表明競賽樹協議在某些安全性要求下具有最佳的輪次復雜度，我們將探索近似的安全性概念，並且設計在安全性和通信效率之間具有理想平衡的協議。

17202921.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17202921.value: Additive manufacturing (AM, popularly known as “3D printing”) has already made a huge impact in many industries. Using computer programs to design and automated processes to manufacture endows 3D printing with enormous power to produce customized or personalized, complicated products/structures for meeting particular or individual needs. The emergence of 4D printing has led to 3D printed shape-morphing structures that can meet some demanding requirements in different industries. Based on 3D/4D printing and their developments, we have conceptualized 5D printing and this application proposes to investigate AM development of 5D printing. 5D printing will produce shape-morphing and information-embedded structures, with the information being delivered in situ during applications of these structures. Information, which is the 5th dimension in 5D printed structures, can be species that, upon their release, will cause changes in the environment (or 5D printed structures) to achieve what the particular 5D printing aims for. For biomedicine, this project will explore 5D printing for developing novel multilayered tissue engineering scaffolds for regenerating complex body tissue. In scaffold-based tissue engineering, scaffolds play vital roles for cell proliferation and differentiation and new tissue formation. Advanced scaffolds encapsulated with growth factors (GFs) can greatly enhance tissue regeneration. This project will investigate 5D printing of novel multilayered scaffolds for gastrointestinal (GI) tissue regeneration. It will employ 5D printing to produce shape-morphing, mesenchymal stem cell (MSC)-containing and biomolecule-delivering multilayered scaffolds modeled on GI tissue structure. According to scaffold design, different scaffold layers in multilayered scaffolds will have different architectures for fulfilling their respective function. A MSC-containing bioink will be used to print MSC-encapsulated struts in different scaffold layers for creating the cellular arrangement resembling GI tissue. Bioinks containing different GFs will be made to print GF-incorporated struts in different scaffold layers. Controlled in vitro or in vivo GF release will induce MSCs in corresponding scaffold layers to differentiate into target cells and stimulate them to proliferate. At 37 degrees Celsius, the shape-morphing scaffold layer will assist self-folding of 5D printed planar multilayered scaffolds into tubular scaffolds suitable for GI tissue engineering. This project will study the formation (via 5D printing), structures and properties (including biological performance) of various scaffolds, from simple to complex, which will be made during scaffold development, with the MSC- and GF-incorporated, multilayered scaffold being the ultimate structure to achieve. 17203321.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17203321.value: Faecal aerosols are suggested to play a role in transmitting SARS-CoV-1/CoV-2, evidenced by the detected positive samples of SARS-CoV-2 RNA in patients’ faeces and wastewater in building/urban drainage systems, and the observed association between the spatial distribution of infected flats and drainage systems in SARS and COVID-19 outbreaks in high-rise buildings in Hong Kong and Guangzhou. However, our understanding of the generation, transport, release and control of faecal aerosols in building drainage systems (stack aerosols) remains poor or non-existent. Studies suggest that the negative/positive pressure transients during the flushing period are responsible for the spread of stack aerosols, but the SARS and COVID-19 outbreaks thus far have revealed a particular spatial infection pattern that contradicts this theory: upper-storey flats were the most infected, whereas the pressure transient mechanism suggests that lower-story flats should be the most vulnerable. Our preliminary investigation of these outbreaks revealed evidence for a chimney effect of the drainage pipes during non-flushing periods, which is also supported by the measured lighter air (warmer and more humid during winter) within the drainage pipes. We thus hypothesise that the release of stack faecal aerosols through leaky pipes or dried water seals through the chimney effect is likely the physical mechanism of the pattern of upper-floor infection. Our aims in this proposed study will be to provide an in-depth understanding of the process and mechanisms of aerosol generation during flushing, the size and number of suspended aerosol droplets in the drainage pipe during non-flushing periods, the transport of airborne aerosols due to the chimney effect, and their eventual release into toilets at various heights of a high-rise building. We shall adopt an integrated engineering approach combining field tests, a simple experimental setup of discharging flows on aerosol generation, and mathematical modelling. We shall perform field monitoring of bioaerosols, temperature, humidity and airflow in two high-rise office buildings where we can remove the water seals to test various conditions, and we shall release bar-coded Lactobacillus bulgaricus, for which we have developed a quantitative polymerase chain reaction pipeline for reliable and accurate quantification. We shall develop a tool to predict the drainage natural ventilation by accounting for its interaction with the outdoor climate and multizone indoor conditions. Our new understanding will pave the way for the development of leak detection methods for drainage pipes and eventually engineering control methods for total elimination of stack aerosols or drain odours into flats in high-rise apartments. 科學家們在患者糞便和建築物/城市排水系統中檢測到 SARS-CoV-2 RNA 陽性樣本，而且在香港和廣州高層建築中COVID-19爆發中的受感染公寓空間分佈和排水系統觀察到一定的關聯關係。這說明糞便氣溶膠在傳播 SARS-CoV-1/CoV-2 中可能發揮作用。然而，我們對建築排水系統中糞便氣溶膠（煙囪氣溶膠）的產生、運輸、釋放和控制的了解仍然很少或根本不存在。現有研究表明，沖洗期間的負/正壓瞬變是煙囪氣溶膠擴散的原因，但迄今為止，SARS 和 COVID-19 爆發揭示了一種與該理論相矛盾的特定空間感染模式：高層公寓是大多數感染，而壓力瞬變機製表明低層公寓應該是最脆弱的。 我們對這些爆發的初步調查揭示了排水管在非沖洗期間煙囪效應的證據，這也得到了排水管內測量到的較輕空氣（冬季更暖和更潮濕）的支持。因此，我們假設通過煙囪效應通過洩漏的管道或乾燥的水封釋放排氣管糞便氣溶膠可能是上層感染模式的物理機制。我們在這項擬議研究中的目的是深入了解沖洗期間氣溶膠產生的過程和機制、非沖洗期間排水管中懸浮氣溶膠液滴的大小和數量、空氣中的氣溶膠傳輸煙囪效應，並最終釋放到高層建築不同高度的廁所室內。 我們將採用綜合工程方法，結合現場測試、氣溶膠生成排放流的簡單實驗設置和數學建模。我們將對兩座高層辦公樓的生物氣溶膠、溫度、濕度和氣流進行現場監測，在那裡我們可以去除水封以測試各種條件，我們將釋放條形碼保加利亞乳桿菌，我們為此開發了定量聚合酶鍊式反應測量，用於可靠和準確的定量。我們將開發一種預測方法，考慮排水自然通風與室外氣候和多區域室內條件的相互作用來預測排水自然通風。我們的新認識將為開發排水管道洩漏檢測方法和最終工程控制方法鋪平道路，以完全消除高層公寓中的煙囪氣溶膠或排水管異味。

17203321.label: Realisation of objectives
17203321.value: This research project investigated the role of high-rise building drainage systems in aerosol-mediated disease transmission, particularly during the COVID-19 pandemic. By achieving three objectives, the study provided insights into aerosol dynamics, natural ventilation, and fault detection, with implications for public health and building design in dense urban areas like Hong Kong. The project integrated field measurements, laboratory experiments, and advanced modeling to address aerosol and airflow interactions in drainage systems. Three journal papers have been published, with three more in preparation, and a report on air admittance valves (AAVs) and positive air pressure attenuators (PAPAs) for the Hong Kong Government awaits publication approval. Aerosol Dynamics and Prediction Model (Objective 1) The first objective was to compile a dataset on suspended stack aerosol droplets and develop a predictive model for faecal aerosols, considering building height, drainage design, and environmental factors. Monitoring was conducted in a low-rise test rig and two high-rise systems, with controlled experiments in a two-story lab setup replicating the twin-pipe drainage system of Luk Chuen House, implicated in a COVID-19 outbreak. Using an aerodynamic particle sizer, we measured aerosols from 0.5 to 20 μm. The low-rise test rig showed dominant concentrations in the 0.8–2 μm range, respirable sizes that can carry pathogens. High-rise systems exhibited a shift to submicron particles (<1 μm), likely due to stronger shearing forces over greater heights. During flushing, pressure fluctuations drove aerosol transport, with concentrations up to 4.5 #/cm³ at lower points under positive pressure, while negative pressure zones showed minimal detection (<0.5 #/cm³). Aerosols persisted over 200 seconds post-flush, peaking at 60–90 seconds. Low vertical dilution rates (0.09–0.24 #/cm³ per meter) allowed infectious concentrations across multiple floors. A sequential transport mechanism was identified: flushing water entrains aerosols downward, pushing them outward at lower sections; post-flush, temperature differences create a chimney effect, driving aerosols upward. This explains vertical transmission in high-rise outbreaks. The predictive model integrates building height, pipe design, and environmental factors, aiding risk assessment. Challenges included access issues at Yam Pak Building, where the terminal manhole was missing, and renovations at Haking Wong Building. Support from the Hong Kong SAR Building Department and University Estates Office enabled access to Tam Tower. We were unable to perform a full year monitoring, but we had access to two high-rises with unprecedented monitored data. Natural Ventilation and Stack Climate (Objective 2) The second objective aimed to understand natural ventilation in full-loop drainage systems and develop a prediction tool for non-flushing periods, considering heat transfer, climate, and building characteristics. Field measurements in 4- and 23-story systems, supplemented by a 2-story test rig, monitored temperature, humidity, airflow, and ventilation rates. Thermally stratified conditions contradicted uniform-temperature assumptions, which predict simple ‘top-outward, bottom-inward’ flows. An adapted MIX model, incorporating pipe friction and stratification, revealed complex airflow patterns: uniform conditions with a single neutral plane, stratification causing multiple neutral planes, and inversions leading to inward airflow at 80% of stack height. In the 23-story system, air outflow at middle (4th–10th) and upper floors (above 16th) spread leakage risk. Transient studies showed a 20th-floor flush generating 200 Pa positive pressures below the 12th floor, driven by air displacement. Simultaneous flushes doubled negative pressures, suggesting revised water seal designs. The prediction tool accounts for stratification and building characteristics, enhancing risk assessment. Renovations at Haking Wong Building delayed progress, but Tam Tower access helped our data collection. The Omicron wave also shifted focus, yet the dataset also helped. Application to COVID-19 Outbreaks and Fault Detection (Objective 3) The third objective applied integrated models to analyze COVID-19 outbreaks and improve fault detection in drainage systems, focusing on leak detection and sealing. This became the priority as vertical transmission was suspected in Hong Kong’s housing outbreaks. The Luk Chuen House outbreak (May 2020) affected nine individuals across seven households via a twin-pipe stack system. Tracer gas (SF6) experiments and the MIX model confirmed vertical spread from drainage stack leakage, with horizontal spread via corridor airflows. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) showed fourfold higher aerosol concentrations in flats opposite the index case (Flat 812) when doors were 20% open, published in Building and Environment (Cheng et al., 2022). The Tong Lau houses outbreak (February 2021) involved 34 cases in 80 subdivided units, with a 25.4% attack rate. Tracer gas measurements indicated stack aerosol spread, worsened by poor ventilation, published in J Roy Soc Interface Focus (Wang et al., 2022). Low-cost H2S and CH4 sensors, deployed in Yam Pak Building, aided leakage detection. AAVs and PAPAs were tested in 2-, 4-, and 23-story systems. AAVs were effective near negative pressure sources but showed “hunting” behavior; PAPAs were inadequate in high-rise systems. Our data was limited one set of devices only. Pipe size enlargement was more effective, detailed in Dung et al. (in preparation). Access issues at Yam Pak and prioritization of outbreak analysis posed challenges, but eventual access to Tam Tower helped the project. In summary, our project achieved its objectives, providing insights into aerosol transport, ventilation, and fault detection. Predictive models and sensor-based approaches offer possible solutions for safer drainage. Collaboration with HKU Estate office and Building Department overcame site access challenges. Our findings support updated building codes and future multidisciplinary research, enhancing public health in urban settings.

17203321.label: Major findings and research outcome
17203321.value: This project advanced the understanding of aerosol dynamics and ventilation in high-rise building drainage systems, elucidating their role in vertical disease transmission during COVID-19 outbreaks. Key findings across three objectives offer critical insights into aerosol transport, stack ventilation, and fault detection. Aerosol Dynamics and Prediction Model (Dung and Li, in preparation) Long-term monitoring in low-rise test rigs and high-rise systems revealed aerosol sizes of 0.5–20 μm, with dominant concentrations in the 0.8–2 μm range in test rigs, shifting to submicron particles in high-rise systems due to stronger interfacial shearing. During flushing, pressure fluctuations drove aerosol transport, with concentrations up to 4.5 #/cm³ at lower sampling points. Aerosols persisted beyond 200 seconds post-flush, peaking 60–90 seconds after flow cessation. Low vertical dilution rates enabled infectious concentrations over multi-story distances. A sequential transport mechanism was identified: falling water entrains aerosols downward, while post-flush temperature differences drive upward transport via the chimney effect, explaining vertical transmission in high-rise outbreaks. Natural Ventilation and Stack Climate (Dung and Li, in preparation) Field measurements in 4-story and 23-story systems revealed thermally stratified conditions, challenging uniform-temperature assumptions. A multi-zone model capturing thermal stratification and pipe friction identified complex flow patterns, including multiple neutral planes. In the 23-story system, air outflow occurred at middle and upper floors, distributing leakage risk. Transient airflow studies showed positive pressures (~200 Pa) below discharge floors in high-rise systems, driven by air displacement from falling water, contradicting steady-state models. Simultaneous flushing amplified negative pressures, doubling with multiple flushes, necessitating revised water seal designs. These findings underscore the need for transient-based ventilation models. Application to COVID-19 Outbreaks and Fault Detection (Wang et al., Dung and Li) Integrated models analyzed several outbreaks, confirming vertical and horizontal transmission via drainage stacks and corridor airflows. Tracer gas and CFD simulations validated aerosol leakage, with horizontal spread worsened by open doors. Low-cost H2S and CH4 sensors aided fault detection, identifying leakage sources. Pressure control devices (AAVs and PAPAs) showed limited efficacy; AAVs performed better near discharge floors, and pipe size enlargement outperformed PAPAs. These results highlight the need for advanced multi-zone models and updated design standards to mitigate transmission risks in high-rise drainage systems.

17203321.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17203321.value: The research has confirmed that drainage stack aerosols, driven by the chimney effect and airflow, facilitate vertical SARS-CoV-2 transmission in high-rise buildings. While our findings, alongside a CRF project, provide strong evidence for this transmission route, challenges remain in explaining mixed horizontal and vertical infection patterns observed in major Hong Kong outbreaks. Limited field data, particularly from underground sewer systems, hinders comprehensive analysis. Continued support from the Hong Kong SAR Building Department and local Estates Office is crucial for accessing these systems. The complexity of interconnected drainage networks, combining underground and above-ground pipes, poses significant design challenges, as current standards rely on outdated experimental data unsuitable for modern high-rise estates. Future research should focus on a multidisciplinary study integrating aerosol dynamics, fluid mechanics, and building design to develop predictive models for mixed transmission patterns. We propose collaborating with government and academic partners to conduct large-scale field studies, enhance sensor-based fault detection, and redesign drainage systems for high-rises. This will inform updated building codes, reducing disease transmission risks in dense urban settings.

17203321.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17203321.value: This research explores how tiny virus-carrying particles, called aerosols, can spread through the plumbing systems of tall buildings, potentially causing diseases like COVID-19 to spread between apartments. We studied how these aerosols move in drainage pipes when toilets are flushed and how air flows in these systems can carry them across multiple floors. By monitoring two real buildings and a controlled lab setup, we discovered that aerosols can travel long distances up and down pipes, driven by water flow during flushing and temperature differences afterward. We found that specific flushing patterns, like multiple toilets flushing at once, and poor ventilation increase the risk of aerosols leaking into homes. Current pipe designs, including devices meant to control air pressure, often fail to prevent these leaks. Our findings explain why some COVID-19 outbreaks occurred in high-rise buildings and highlight the need for better plumbing designs to keep residents safe. This work is crucial for improving building safety, protecting public health, and updating construction standards, especially in densely populated cities like Hong Kong. We also developed affordable sensors to detect plumbing issues early, helping prevent disease spread in homes.

17204021.value: NASA has defined goals for next generations of aircraft for commercial aviation, aiming to reduce noise by −71 dB, emissions by −75% and fuel burn by −70% in 2025, relative to the best data in 2005. While electric vehicles have been identified to be the greenest road transportation means, electric airplanes are our natural choice of development to achieve these goals. However, differing from vehicles and ships which have ground or seawater to support their weights, airplanes rely on using upthrust force to rise into the air so that the desired power-to-weight ratio (power density) is much more demanding. Solar Impulse, which completed the first circumnavigation of the globe with no fuel, seems very successful to indicate that electric airplanes are becoming practical. Air drones are so popular for aerial videography that electric airplanes seem to be practically viable. Actually, the corresponding technologies are not suitable for commercial electric airplanes, which desire electric motors possessing very high power density for electric takeoffs with a heavy loading. In recent years, high temperature superconducting (HTS) motors are becoming attractive for applications in megawatt levels because the HTS material cost as well as the necessary cryocooler’s weight and cost can well be offset by the improvement of power density and efficiency. Consequently, there is a consensus that HTS motors are the most suitable candidate to enable pure electric flight. Specifically, the electric loading and magnetic loading of HTS motors should be as high as possible while the weight should be as low as possible. In order to significantly reduce the motor weight, a fully ironless structure should be adopted. Hence, the electric loading of the HTS armature can be significantly increased without suffering from any magnetic saturation or iron loss. In order to eliminate the problems of transferring high field current or applying the coolant to the HTS rotor, the permanent-magnet rotor should be adopted. The purpose of this proposal is to develop a novel superconducting permanent-magnet ironless motor drive for electric aircraft. The corresponding objectives are: (1) develop a novel superconducting permanent-magnet ironless motor for electric airplanes; (2) develop a new multilevel inverter for the proposed motor; (3) analyze the electromagnetic, thermal and structural performances of the proposed motor; (4) devise the control system and strategy for the proposed motor drive; (5) design and construct the prototype of the whole motor drive for experimentation. 美國國家航空航天局為下一代商用航空飛機設定了目標，相對於 2005 年的最佳數據，目標是到 2025 年將噪音降低到 −71 dB，排放量降低到 −75%，燃油消耗量降低到 −70%。當電動汽車已被確定為最環保的道路交通方式，電動飛機是我們實現這些目標的自然發展選擇。然而，與有地面或海水來支撐其重量的車輛和船舶不同，飛機依靠使用向上推力升到空中，因此所需的功率重量比（功率密度）要求更高。“陽光動力”號在沒有燃料的情況下完成了首次環球航行，似乎非常成功地表明電動飛機正在變得實用。空中無人機在航拍中如此受歡迎，以至電動飛機似乎是可行的。實際上，其相關的技術並不適用於商用電動飛機，商用電動飛機需要電機具有非常高的功率密度，以用於大負載的電動起飛。近年來，因為高溫超導材料成本以及必要的低溫冷卻器的重量和成本可以通過功率密度和效率的提高很好地抵消，高溫超導電機在兆瓦級應用中變得越來越有吸引力。因此，人們一致認為高溫超導電機是實現純電動飛行最合適的電驅動裝置。具體而言，高溫超導電機的電負載和磁負載應盡可能高，而重量應盡可能低。為了顯著減輕電機重量，應採用全無鐵結構。因此，高溫超導電樞的電負載可以顯著增加，而不會遭受任何磁飽和或鐵損。為了消除傳送高勵磁電流或施加冷卻劑到高溫超導轉子的問題，應採用永磁轉子。這個項目的目的是開發一種用於電動飛機的新型超導永磁無鐵芯電機驅動。相應的目標是：（1）研製一種新型用於電動飛機的超導永磁無鐵芯電機；（2）為這個電機開發一種新的多電平逆變器；（3）分析這個電機的電磁、熱和結構性能；（4）為整個電機驅動設計控制系統和策略；（5）設計並搭建整個電機驅動的樣機進行實驗。

17204021.label: Realisation of objectives
17204021.value: The 1st objective has been fully achieved. Firstly, a comprehensive overview of high-temperature superconducting (HTS) rotating electrical machines has been conducted, covering over 100 superconducting machines that were prototyped in the 21st century [J2]. Various machine topologies including the synchronous, induction, claw-pole, homopolar, magnetic-geared, vernier, flux-switching, hysteresis and flux-modulation types are covered, and various potential applications are explained, including generators for wind turbines as well as motors for electric vehicles, electric ships and electric airplanes (EAs) [C1]. Following from the aforementioned overviews, a novel HTS permanent-magnet ironless (HTS-PM-IL) motor is proposed for electric aircraft, which can offer higher power density and higher efficiency than the existing HTS motors [J10]. The motor design is rated at 3 MW and 4500 r/min, which is based on NASA’s N3-X concept aircraft. The motor design adopts multiobjective optimization to explore the tradeoff between minimizing the active mass and minimizing the armature AC loss by using the optimization package “pymoo” in Python. It reveals that the motor with the lighter, yokeless topology does not have much higher armature AC loss than that with a yoke topology. The advent of HTS materials offers a promising pathway to significantly enhance wireless power transfer (WPT) performance by leveraging the nearly zero resistance and higher current-carrying capacity of HTS materials [J5]. Thus, the HTS-WPT is also proposed to wirelessly excite the HTS magnet instead of using PM material, in which the HTS receiver and HTS magnet can share the same cryogenic environment, leading to achieving higher power density as well as better flexibility and safety. The 2nd objective has been fully achieved. Although the proposed HTS-PM-IL motor takes the definite advantages of higher torque density, higher power density, and higher system efficiency, it relies on having a near-sinusoidal supply of three-phase stator currents. Thus, a new multilevel inverter is developed for this HTS motor, which can offer high efficiency, high power handling capability, low harmonic distortion and high fault tolerance for EA operation [C2]. Taking into account the tradeoff between performance and complexity, a new three-phase three-level T-type inverter having 27 switching states is purposely developed for the proposed motor. In case the HTS magnet is used to replace the PM in the rotor, the newly proposed three-phase three-level T-type inverter can be modified to provide HTS-WPT [J5]. Hence, the HTS magnet can be wirelessly excited with an ultrahigh current level without involving any slip rings and carbon brushes, leading to maintenance-free. The 3rd objective has been fully achieved. Both analytical and numerical approaches are developed to analyze the electromagnetic, thermal and structural performances of the proposed motor, including the eddy-current losses, thermal instability and mechanical integrity. Since superconductors are subjected to spatially non-uniform and time-varying external magnetic field as well as carrying a transport current in the proposed motor, variations in the integral method are reviewed [J3]. It is applied to calculate the AC loss in HTS tapes. Then, an integral method is newly extended to model HTS coils with different coupling scenarios, including uncoupled (insulated from each other), coupled at ends (coupled at the terminals of the cable), or fully coupled (electrically connected with each other along the whole length of the cable) [J4]. It is essential to model the HTS tapes stacked together to form cables which are then wound into coils for the HTS motor. Subsequently, a new integral method is proposed to model magnetization and transport AC loss of HTS tapes in the HTS motor by including the effect of external magnetic field acting on the ferromagnetic and HTS domains [J9]. The results agree closely with the widely used T-A formulation implemented in COMSOL. Moreover, both analytical and numerical computation of AC loss in multifilament MgB2 wires of HTS motors under arbitrarily time-varying transverse magnetic field are proposed [J7]. Analytical formulae are derived to calculate the coupling loss, eddy current loss and hysteresis loss of a multifilament superconducting wire. Then, the loss formulae are verified by numerical simulations done in the finite-element software COMSOL Multiphysics using an external magnetic field in HTS motor environment. Based on analytical loss formulas, the AC loss of four types of conductors: copper Litz wire, aluminum Litz wire, MgB2 multifilamentary wire, and REBCO tape are compared at different engineering current densities, temperatures, and external magnetic fields [J6]. It reveals that at 77.5 K, REBCO is not competitive against copper and aluminum Litz wires; at 20 K, on an individual conductor level, MgB2 and REBCO offer lower loss at their respective maximum achievable current densities than aluminum Litz wire. Besides the radial-flux topology, the HTS motor can be designed in terms of axial-flux topology. In order to handle the corresponding three-dimensional (3D) magnetic field analysis, a new quasi-3D analytical model is developed [J1]. The key is to divide the motor into several annular slices in the radial direction, and then apply the harmonic modelling method to solve the magnetic field in these slices. The effectiveness of the proposed quasi-3D analytical model is validated by using numerical finite element analysis. The 4th objective has been fully achieved. The control system and strategy for the proposed motor is developed by using MATLAB/Simulink based on the multilevel converter, which can provide the accurate torque control, fast speed response and versatile fault-tolerant control for EA operation. Wherein, both the direct torque control and field-oriented control are considered to justify the optimal performances of accurate torque control and fast speed response. In particular, the trade-off between the torque and speed control is made to maximize the whole system performance. On the other hand, the principle of fault-tolerant control is explored to achieve the fast identification of various system faults so that the motor drive can operate properly. In particular, the unknown load disturbance is so critical that it can lead to a speed drop, which is disastrous for EA operation. To solve this problem, a fast finite-time speed control of the three-phase three-level T-type inverter is developed [C2]. It combines with model predictive control of the current loop to ensure that the HTS motor can have the ability to resist load disturbances or changes. The 5th objective has been mostly completed. A testing platform consisting of a scaled-down version of the proposed HTS-PM-IL motor with REBCO armature and its associated liquid nitrogen (LN2) cryogenic system was designed. It was planned to measure the AC loss in REBCO armature by measuring the rate of evaporation of LN2. Nonetheless, it was found that the University of Strathclyde had measured AC loss of a REBCO armature coil of a similar HTS-PM motor, cooled in LN2. Instead of duplicating the testing platform and constructing a similar HTS-PM motor, which were very costly and time-consuming, it was decided to collaborate with them. The PhD student trained for this project spent a few months in the University of Strathclyde to conduct relevant experiments based on our design. The AC loss of a HTS coil wound from two parallel REBCO tapes stacked together is successfully measured [J8]. Three data processing techniques are also proposed to calculate the average power dissipation during the measurement process. Consequently, the performance indices including the power density, efficiency, controllability and reliability can be evaluated.

17204021.label: Major findings and research outcome
17204021.value: The research outcome is very fruitful, namely 10 international journal papers [J1]-[J10] and 2 international conference papers [C1],[C2]. Meanwhile, 1 PhD student has been trained. In the area of HTS machine design, an overview of HTS machines is comprehensively performed [J2] with emphasis on electric transportation [C1]. AC loss is identified as a unique feature for HTS machine design because the machine efficiency affects cooling requirements, which in turn affects the design of cryocoolers and thermal insulation, leading to the prevention of quenching and thus safety concerns. A novel HTS-PM-IL motor is proposed for EAs [J10], which reveals that the motor with a yokeless topology does not have much higher AC loss than that with a yoke topology. Also, HTS-WPT is identified to be promising for ultrahigh power excitation of HTS motors [J5]. In the area of HTS machine analysis, various integral methods are comprehensively reviewed [J3], which are much faster than the popular T-A formulation in COMSOL. An integral method is newly extended to model HTS coils with different coupling scenarios [J4]. Then, a new integral method is proposed to model magnetization and AC loss of HTS tapes in the HTS motor by including the effect of external magnetic field [J9]. Moreover, both analytical and numerical computation of AC loss in multifilament MgB2 wires in the HTS motor under arbitrarily time-varying transverse magnetic field are proposed [J7]. Based on analytical loss formulas, the AC loss of four types of conductors: copper Litz wire, aluminum Litz wire, MgB2 multifilamentary wire and REBCO tape are critically compared at different current densities, temperatures and external magnetic fields [J6]. It reveals that they have their individual pros and cons at various working conditions. Moreover, a new quasi-3D analytical model is developed [J1], which can effectively perform magnetic field calculation for axial flux motors. In the area of HTS motor control, a new three-phase three-level T-type inverter is developed [C2], Hence, by combining with model predictive control of the current loop, a fast finite-time speed control is developed to control this multilevel inverter so that the HTS motor can have the ability to resist load disturbances or changes. In the area of HTS motor experimentation, the AC loss of a REBCO coil in the HTS motor is successfully measured [J8]. Three data processing techniques are evaluated for calculating the power dissipation, indicating one is more reliable than the others for this measurement.

17204021.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17204021.value: In this project, four types of conductors: copper Litz wire, aluminum Litz wire, MgB2 multifilamentary wire and REBCO tape have been critically compared for application to HTS machines. Other types of HTS material should also be considered. Particularly, the hybridization of various conductors for HTS machines should be the area for further development, which can potentially optimize the machine performance when operating over a wide range of operating temperatures. While this project has identified that the concept of HTS-WPT is promising for ultrahigh power excitation of HTS motors, the realization of wireless HTS motors needs further development. For instance, the design of WPT frequency and the analysis of its AC loss for ultrahigh power excitation of HTS motors are challenging. Also, the integration of the HTS-WPT receiver into the HTS rotor of the HTS motor under the same cryogenic adiabatic chamber is very challenging.

17204021.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17204021.value: While electric vehicles have been identified to be the greenest road transportation, electric airplanes are our natural choice for next generation of commercial aircraft. However, current technologies are not suitable for commercial electric aircraft, which desire electric motors possessing very high power density for electric takeoffs with a heavy loading. In this project, a novel superconducting motor drive is proposed for electric aircraft. The core of the proposed motor is to adopt the superconducting armature, permanent-magnet rotor and fully ironless structure, leading to maximum electric and magnetic loadings while with minimum weight. The corresponding multilevel inverter and speed control system are also newly designed to achieve near-sinusoidal currents and the ability to resist load disturbances. As AC loss is identified as a unique feature for superconducting machine design, both analytical and numerical approaches are developed to calculate the AC loss of the proposed motor, hence evaluating its various performances. The significance and value of this project are tremendous which can fundamentally solve the long-term problems of electric aircraft, hence achieving outstanding power density and high efficiency. It also opens up a new research direction for the development of electric propulsion systems for electric aircraft.

17204521.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17204521.value: Taxis offer round-the-clock, comfortable, and direct transportation services but can significantly contribute to traffic congestion. In many cities, including Beijing, Hong Kong, Singapore, and New York, a large number of taxi drivers are rentee-drivers, who rent taxis from taxi owners. Therefore, an interaction exists between taxi owners and rentee-drivers. Taxi owners aim at maximizing their profit by setting the rent level for rentee-drivers and determining the number of taxis to purchase. Rentee-drivers rent a taxi from owners and drive on roads based on their preferred work (and rest) schedule, and are not mandated to join the market (become a rentee-driver). Instead, their supply is highly associated with the profitability of being a rentee-driver, which affects the profit of taxi owners as well. Meanwhile, the rise in ride-sourcing has introduced competition between taxi owners and ride-sourcing platforms and reduced the profitability of taxi drivers, and hence, that of taxi owners and taxi-labor supply. Although this competition has been considered and modeled previously, its effects on taxi-labor supply, different stakeholders in taxi markets (e.g., taxi owners, rentee-drivers, and customers), and system performance (social welfare) have not been duly considered. To effectively regulate taxi markets and investigate how different regulatory policies, including taxi-rent control and fare adjustments, affect stakeholders in taxi markets and social welfare, it is necessary to model both the interaction between taxi owners and drivers and competition between taxi owners and ride-sourcing platforms. However, these features have not yet been captured in a single taxi model. Moreover, the effectiveness of taxi-rent control is yet to be theoretically examined although it is found in practical scenarios. This project proposes a dynamic network modeling framework that will describe the decision-making process of taxi owners and their interaction with rentee-drivers, considering the competition resulting from ride-sourcing platforms and the work schedule of rentee-drivers. To make the framework more realistic, the congestion effects and externalities of traffic will also be captured. Using the proposed framework, different taxi market regimes will be analyzed. Using Hong Kong as a case study, the effects of policies such as taxi-rent control, fare adjustments, fleet-size restrictions, peak-period surcharges, and peak-period taxis on different stakeholders in taxi markets and social welfare will be investigated, thereby providing new insights to help the government in managing its taxi market and the taxi owners and ride-sourcing platforms in deciding their management strategies. 的士為市民提供全天候、舒適的點到點交通服務，但亦可能會嚴重加劇交通擁堵。在包括北京、香港、新加坡和紐約在内的許多城市，大部分的士司機是租車司機，他們從出租車主租用的士。因此，車主和租車司機之間存在一定的互動關係。車主旨在透過設定租車司機的租金水平以及決定自身購買的的士數量來實現利潤最大化。租車司機則從車主租用的士，並根據自身偏好的工作休息時間表提供的士服務，亦沒有被强制要求提供服務。的士司機供應與他們作爲租車司機的收益緊密聯繫，這亦會影響車主自身的收益。同時，共享出行的興起引發了車主和打車平台之間的競爭，亦降低了的士司機的收益，進而減少了車主的收益和的士司機供應。儘管之前已經有研究對這種競爭關係進行建模分析，但尚未充分考慮其對的士司機供應、的士市場中不同持份者（例如車主、租車司機和顧客）以及系統表現（例如社會福利）的影響。爲了有效規範的士市場，研究包括的士租金控制和車費調整在内的不同監管政策對市場持份者和社會福利的影響，有必要同時對車主和司機的互動關係、以及車主和打車平台的競爭進行建模分析。然而，這些特性尚未在單個的士模型中體現。此外，儘管在現實中發現了的士租金控制的有效性，但其仍有待理論上的驗證。 本項目提出了一個動態網絡建模框架，該框架不僅體現的士車主的決策過程及其與租車司機的互動關係，同時對車主與打車平台的競爭和租車司機的工作安排進行考慮。爲了使框架更符合現實情況，還會在框架中加入交通的擁堵效應和外部性。運用所提出的框架對不同的士市場制度進行深入分析。並以香港為例，研究的士租金管制、車費調整、車隊規模限制、高峰期附加費、高峰期的士等政策對的士市場各持份者和社會福利的影響，從而提供新的見解，以幫助政府管理的士市場，並輔助車主和打車平台決定其管理策略。

17205021.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17205021.value: 本研究運用可計算一般均衡模型（Computable General Equilibrium，CGE），對香港特別行政區與大彎區（Greater Bay Area，GBA）的地方和區域碳交易市場的潛在經濟影響進行研究。目前，香港僅採取傳統的“命令-控制”型措施以應對氣候變化，然而這些傳統措施效率低下，政策上亟需採取諸如排放交易體系（Emissions Trading Scheme, ETS）等基於市場的政策工具。ETS可使香港以更低的成本實現其減排目標。然而由於潛在的實施難度，相關ETS研究匱乏，本研究旨在填補這一空白。 本研究具有學術和政策雙重价值。首先，本研究的學術價值之一在於它融合了多方面的先進研究方法。傳統的CGE模型框架對於經濟活動產生的環境反饋分析存在不足，本研究通過將排放作為生產投入，在傳統的CGE模型框架基礎上獨創地引入碳約束結構。同時，考慮到建築部門的間接排放受排放限制約束，以往研究中由於數據和方法的局限性常常被忽略。本研究模型將“自下而上”的建築部門細節納入到“自上而下”的碳定價結構中，得以充分考慮建築部門的間接排放。大多數現有的研究模型本身僅僅提供較弱的區域視角，比如研究中將深圳市與廣東省合併為一，而且不包含香港和澳門。本研究的優越性在於，將GBA的關鍵城市作為單獨的區域以實現對地方和區域ETS情景的深入分析，彌補了以往的不足。 政策方面，本研究對正在進行的政策討論具有重要的潛在貢獻。ETS在決策圈受到關注較少，其根本原因在於香港的碳市場規模小。然而，可以參照深圳、北京和上海，通過對建築和能源生產部門的監管解決這一難題。另一個潛在的解決方案是與深圳和廣東兩個於2013年已經建立的ETS先行示範區協同建立區域碳市場。隨著中央對大灣區總體規劃的支持，大灣區的區域ETS理念的可行性得到進一步提升。本研究旨在提高公眾對香港與大灣區地方和區域碳市場需求的認識，通過為香港與大灣區地方和區域碳市場的經濟影響提供堅實的實證研究證據以激發相關政策探討。

17205021.label: Realisation of objectives
17205021.value: The main goal of this project is to examine the economic impacts of an integrated regional carbon market and emissions trading in China’s Greater Bay Area (GBA). In particular, this project has seven objectives and consists of two main tasks required for their achievement. The first main task is the development of a computable general equilibrium (CGE) model of Hong Kong and three other Chinese regional economies, titled GBAEM (GBA Energy Model) [Objective 1]. The second task is the application of the model to the analysis of multiple policy scenarios [Objectives 2 – 6] and the production of research outputs based on it [Objective 7]. All seven objectives of this project have been successfully achieved with key project outcomes, including a multi-region CGE model (GBAEM) and four peer-reviewed journal articles. [Objective 1]: The first objective has been achieved with the development of GBAEM, which is a multi-region, multi-sector, recursive-dynamic CGE model. The GBAEM includes eight regions in total—where Hong Kong (HKG), Shenzhen (SZH), the Rest of Guangdong (RGD), and the Rest of Mainland China (ROC) represent four separate regions—and it encompasses 16 production sectors. In essence, GBAEM is an economic simulation model for policy analysis, and can run counterfactual scenarios up to 2060 with a five-year interval, taking 2014 as the base year. As a “general” equilibrium model, GBAEM can comprehensively track the direct, indirect, and induced economic impacts of a given policy shock on multiple markets (e.g., commodity/service, labor, and capital markets). This aspect makes GBAEM superior to many “partial” equilibrium models that deal with a single market, which are also widely used for policy analysis. GBAEM ingeniously incorporates physical accounts (e.g., energy use and carbon emissions) into economic accounts and explicitly represents carbon mitigation/emissions trading structure within a CGE framework. This aspect distinguishes GBAEM from other conventional CGE models, which focus only on economic accounts expressed in dollar terms (e.g., national accounts and inter-industry/international trade). GBAEM also has strengths in regional policy analysis—an area that poses challenges for many existing CGE models in China’s GBA context, due to their coarse spatial resolutions. The model boasts a fine spatial resolution (e.g., HKG, SZH, and RGD as separate regions) and integrates substantial subnational level details on industry mix and energy consumption. These unique advantages offered by GBAEM allow the model to function as a comprehensive impact assessment tool for regional climate mitigation policies in the context of China’s GBA. [Objective 2]: Journal articles produced as an outcome of this project enrich the literature by filling the following gaps identified in existing studies. First, empirical studies on China’s carbon markets tend to focus solely on Mainland China, excluding Hong Kong from their analysis. Even those that consider Hong Kong often neglect subnational level linkage scenarios as intermediate steps towards China’s fully integrated national emissions trading scheme (ETS). Second, few existing studies on China’s GBA carbon markets incorporate their up-to-date carbon-neutrality targets, including long-term mitigation goals with specific timelines for carbon peak and neutrality. Finally, existing studies often conduct static analyses, overlooking the dynamic and cumulative dimensions of allocative efficiency losses under carbon constraints. [Objective 3]: We have tested multiple ETS linkage scenarios in the GBA context, such as independent carbon markets in each GBA stakeholder economy, the Hong Kong–Shenzhen ETS linkage (i.e., limited GBA carbon market), the Hong Kong–Guangdong ETS linkage (i.e., extended GBA carbon market), and the Hong Kong–Mainland ETS linkage (i.e., China’s extended national carbon market, fully integrating Hong Kong and Guangdong). Through journal articles, we have provided estimated economic impacts of each linkage scenario, with regional and sectoral details. We have also discussed the policy implications in terms of policy compliance costs (i.e., loss of gross domestic product) and climate mitigation efficiency (i.e., carbon intensity or carbon emissions per unit of gross domestic product). [Objective 4]: We found that all GBA stakeholder economies (i.e., Hong Kong, Shenzhen, and the rest of Guangdong) would gain from an integrated regional carbon market, but the distribution of the benefits is heavily biased toward Hong Kong. In other words, regional cooperation for a GBA carbon market will make Hong Kong—which sets an ambitious climate-mitigation target at the city level, despite its tiny local carbon market—the biggest winner. [Objective 5]: Our results demonstrate that all GBA stakeholder economies (i.e., Hong Kong, Shenzhen, and the rest of Guangdong) are better off with an integrated regional carbon market. This scenario provides all GBA stakeholder economies with a strong incentive to promote such a market. However, Hong Kong-biased benefits may require Hong Kong to be more proactive than any other potential stakeholders in making the GBA carbon market a reality. Its feasibility would partly depend on an institutional device to reduce the imbalance in benefit across regional stakeholders. [Objective 6]: Our results convey several policy implications for regional cooperation. As discussed above, the most important takeaway is that it is Hong Kong that needs to be more proactive than any other potential stakeholder in making the GBA carbon market happen in reality. Second, approaching the regional carbon market from a cross-border investment and carbon-leakage perspective may be appealing to Guangdong Province. In fact, Guangdong Province and Hong Kong have extended their regional cooperation on environmental agendas, such as air-quality monitoring and regulations, and associated initiatives for cross-border cooperation have been supported by China’s central government under the leadership of the GBA Development Office. Similarly, adopting a normative stance may complement the economic incentives for the GBA carbon market. Finally, Hong Kong can take a two-track approach to enhancing a regional carbon market—voluntary markets based on economic incentives, as well as compliance markets based on environmental norms. Its tapping into voluntary carbon-market opportunities may begin with those GBA entities that are not constrained by the compliance markets. As a global financial hub, Hong Kong already possesses competitive institutional and physical infrastructure, necessary to position itself as a center for international voluntary carbon markets. On its path to this role, Hong Kong may first focus on regional opportunities, in cooperation with Guangdong Province, and then consider extending its market reach at the national and international levels. [Objective 7]: Our final results have been shared with academic researchers and policy analysts through four peer-reviewed journal articles. In addition, we have actively engaged with academic and industry experts at various local and international conferences, promoting our key findings and collecting professional and public feedback through dissemination in working/conference paper formats or more accessible slide presentations.

17205021.label: Major findings and research outcome
17205021.value: We examine the potential economic impacts of local and regional carbon markets in Hong Kong and China’s GBA region, taking a CGE approach. We find that Hong Kong’s proposed carbon-neutrality target requires policy-compliance costs as large as ≤21.0% of its baseline gross domestic product, but regional cooperation can help reduce the costs substantially. For example, the costs will decline by ≤23.0% if Hong Kong forms an integrated carbon market with Shenzhen. The cost savings will further increase to ≤38.2% if Hong Kong cooperates with Shenzhen and Guangdong to create an extended regional carbon market. Such an integrated carbon market will be mutually beneficial, and will also help Shenzhen and Guangdong meet their own carbon-reduction goals at ≤13.9% and ≤5.2% lower costs, respectively. These regional cooperation scenarios, though benefiting all participants, will make Hong Kong—which sets an ambitious climate-mitigation target at the city level, despite its tiny local carbon market—the biggest winner. Accordingly, Hong Kong has a great incentive to promote an integrated regional carbon market, but increasing its feasibility may require an institutional device to reduce the imbalance in benefit across regional stakeholders. Our project contributes to the literature in several aspects. First, our analytic framework embodies a methodological advancement in representing carbon mitigation and emissions trading structures within a CGE framework. GBAEM, a key output of this project, also has strengths in regional policy analysis, as its fine spatial resolution integrates rich subnational level details on industry mix and energy consumption. Second, our focus on attention to subnational-level opportunities enriches the ETS linkage literature, which largely neglects them despite their importance. We test multiple subnational linkage scenarios in the GBA context as an intermediate step to China’s fully integrated national ETS, incorporating up-to-date official climate-mitigation targets within a dynamic framework. Finally, our findings convey crucial policy implications. A regional carbon market in China’s GBA region helps save substantial economic costs required for the region’s compliance with proposed climate mitigation targets, benefiting all stakeholder economies. However, China’s existing plans for national and local ETS linkages exclude Hong Kong, which will benefit most from them. Accordingly, Hong Kong needs to be more proactive in terms of cross-border cooperation for ETS linkages and to take the initiative in forming a regional carbon market.

17205021.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17205021.value: This project has successfully achieved its main objectives while also paving the way for future research. One avenue for further research development is to apply the model to other dimensions of the GBA regional carbon market, such as carbon tax revenue recycling. GBAEM is a methodological platform with flexibility, rather than a fixed model, and can easily be extended for other research purposes with a reasonable amount of time and effort. In addition, the GBAEM framework can be applied to other Chinese mega-city regions, such as Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei or the Yangtze River Delta. Another direction is to extend the model for detailed sectoral analysis. Each GBA stakeholder sets sector-specific mitigation targets, necessitating improvements in sectoral resolutions and sector-specific energy/trade flows. For example, GBAEM can be extended to assess the impacts of decarbonizing the local transport sector. This would involve a realistic representation of the household and commercial transport service sectors, including vehicle fleet details (e.g., internal combustion engines vs. electric vehicles) and their interactions with local energy sectors (e.g., electricity).

17205021.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17205021.value: The primary objective of this project is to assess the economic impacts of local and regional carbon markets in Hong Kong and China’s GBA. Our findings reveal three macro-level insights. First, compliance with proposed carbon-neutrality targets is extremely costly and introduces a huge shock to the regional economy. The magnitude of the shock is particularly large in Hong Kong, which cannot leverage China’s internal adjustment mechanisms. Second, these compliance costs can be significantly reduced through regional cooperation. An extended regional carbon market encompassing Hong Kong and the entire Guangdong Province holds particularly great potential, given its intra-regional economic complementarity. Such a market could enable the region to meet its region-wide mitigation goals at a substantially lower cost without causing significant adverse impacts on the rest of China. Finally, although a GBA carbon market is mutually beneficial to all regional stakeholders, the benefits are not evenly distributed—Hong Kong stands to gain much more than Shenzhen or the rest of Guangdong. This imbalance may potentially weaken economic incentives for a regional carbon market on the Mainland’s side, making it necessary for Hong Kong to be more proactive in bringing it to fruition.

17205321.label: Project Objectives
17205321.value: To demonstrate backaction force under CW/pulsed laser at different wavelengths and supercontinuum The proposed spatio-temporal optical pulling/pushing and spectroscopy (STOPS) system will manipulate the spatio-temporal property of a light beam. The implementation of this system will be conducted in two stages. In the first stage, STOPS will be operated under a CW/pulsed laser at different wavelengths. In the second stage, the STOPS system will be operated under supercontinuum regime. We will analyze the performance of STOPS under different regimes. This analysis will provide an essential foundation for the next stage of STOPS. We will first apply the CW/pulsed laser in the optical backaction experiment. Specifically, we plan to build all-fiber mode-locked laser sources operating at discrete wavelengths with a central wavelength between 1 µm and 2 µm. This includes the comparison of the backaction force performance on dielectric microparticles and on particles with different diameter/refractive index. Next, we will build the fiber-based supercontinuum source and apply it to mediate the backaction force. Therefore, all these will provide a well-characterized STOPS foundation that can be further explored for specific applications, such as spectroscopy for classifying microplastics in the later stage of the research. To demonstrate backaction force under counter-propagating beams After implementing and studying a basic configuration of STOPS in the first stage, we propose to demonstrate the spatial manipulation of backaction force under a counter-propagating beam. This is expected to empower STOPS to realize both optical pulling and pushing by tuning the counter-propagating beam. To do so, we will illuminate the suspension using beams at different wavelengths or coherence to avoid interference. The Brownian motion can then be controlled by adjusting the power ratio of the beams from opposite directions. Practically, we will also investigate the backaction force on the microparticles with irregular shape. This is interesting and important to real applications for pulling irregular-shaped microparticles required in the later stage of the proposal. This ability would, in general, slow down the motion dynamics of massive microparticles and aerosol droplets in parallel for particle imaging and spectroscopy. The inclusion of the supercontinuum source as the counter-propagating beam provides the possibility to measure the ultrafast single-shot spectrum of dielectric microparticles for the inspection of their chemical composition. To incorporate STOPS with ultrafast spectroscopy for the application on microplastics In stage three, an ultrafast STOPS system can be designed by leveraging PNJ-mediated backaction force in combination with ultrafast single-shot spectroscopy. Specifically, the single-shot spectroscopy will be investigated in both time-lens and time-stretch regimes to optimize its configuration. We will then incorporate such ultrafast single-shot spectroscopy for classification by leveraging machine learning algorithms, in particular, the identification of microplastics and aerosol droplets. Finally, we will apply STOPS on the microplastics investigation in water environment and also explore the tracking of aerosol to detect bacteria or viruses inside the droplets in collaboration with researchers in the respective fields.

To incorporate STOPS with ultrafast spectroscopy for the application on microplastics In stage three, an ultrafast STOPS system can be designed by leveraging PNJ-mediated backaction force in combination with ultrafast single-shot spectroscopy. Specifically, the single-shot spectroscopy will be investigated in both time-lens and time-stretch regimes to optimize its configuration. We will then incorporate such ultrafast single-shot spectroscopy for classification by leveraging machine learning algorithms, in particular, the identification of microplastics and aerosol droplets. Finally, we will apply STOPS on the microplastics investigation in water environment and also explore the tracking of aerosol to detect bacteria or viruses inside the droplets in collaboration with researchers in the respective fields.

17205321.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17205321.value: The momentum transferred from light photons to dielectric particles allows the remote manipulation of microparticles noninvasively. The radiation force exerted on a microparticle pushes it away from the light source, which could preferably empower versatile manipulation in spatio-temporal regimes. However, most of the demonstrated works on focused laser light have been confined to moving a single microparticle (or limited number of microparticles) in response to photon momentum change and scaling up to massive microparticles remains a great challenge. Another challenge is combining that large-scale manipulation with ultrafast optical spectroscopy technology especially in the context of identifying and removing microplastics widely scattered in the water environment. Therefore, large-scale microparticles manipulation in addition to distinguishing the type and chemical composition of the microparticles with light poses a great challenge in the community. The spatio-temporal optical pulling/pushing and spectroscopy (STOPS) system proposed in this project offers a promising platform for optical manipulation and monitoring in applications such as identifying and removing microplastics. Through a three-phase approach, we will demonstrate STOPS as a core technology to meet some of the critical challenges of ultrafast manipulation and monitoring. First, we plan to demonstrate photonic nanojet (PNJ)-mediated backaction force under continuous-wave (CW)/pulsed laser at different wavelengths and supercontinuum to quantitatively analyze and evaluate the performance of STOPS in terms of pulsewidth, peak/average power, and repetition rate etc. Second, we propose to demonstrate PNJ-mediated backaction force under counter-propagating beams. This is expected to empower STOPS to realize both optical pulling and pushing by tuning the counter-propagating beams. Its performance will be thoroughly characterized and further expanded to parallel microparticles manipulation and monitoring on a large scale based on the advantage of PNJ-mediated backaction force over the traditional optical force with confined tracking region. Third, we will incorporate the PNJ-mediated backaction force with single-shot time-lens/time-stretch spectroscopy for classification based on machine learning algorithms, particularly in the applications on microplastics and potentially aerosol droplets. The proposed project constitutes advancements in ultrafast optical manipulation and monitoring technologies in the context of identifying and removing microplastics widely scattered in the water environment and potentially tracking aerosol droplets as carriers of airborne viruses. 17205321.label: Realisation of objectives
17205321.value: 1. To demonstrate backaction force under CW/pulsed laser at different wavelengths and supercontinuum We have demonstrated the spatio-temporal optical pulling/pushing and spectroscopy (STOPS) system by manipulating the spatio-temporal property of a light beam. The specific implementation of this system was conducted in two stages. In the first stage, STOPS was operated under a CW/pulsed laser at different wavelengths. In the second stage, the STOPS system was operated under supercontinuum regime. We analyzed the performance of STOPS under these different regimes. This analysis will provide an essential foundation for the next stage of STOPS. 2. To demonstrate backaction force under counter-propagating beams We have demonstrated the spatial manipulation of backaction force under a counter-propagating beam to realize both optical pulling and pushing by tuning the counter-propagating beam. Specifically, we illuminated the suspension using beams at different wavelengths or coherence to avoid interference. The Brownian motion can then be controlled by adjusting the power ratio of the beams from opposite directions. In addition to that, we also investigated the backaction force on the microparticles with irregular shape, such as the biological cancer cells. This is interesting and important to real applications for pulling irregular-shaped microparticles required in the later stage of the proposal. 3. To incorporate STOPS with ultrafast spectroscopy for the application on microplastics We have demonstrated the reversible control over the microparticle motion, specifically by manipulating dielectric microspheres to swim towards the near infrared pulsed laser in response to the backaction force mediated by photonic nanoject (PNJ), and developed the counter-propagating beam scheme for reversible control of the particle motion directions. We have also initialized a rapid hybrid dual-comb coherent anti-Stokes Raman spectroscopy (CARS) system based on delay spectral focusing, targeting high wavenumbers for the imaging and differentiation of major microplastic species, in addition to the development of deep learning technique for the autofocusing task in predicting defocusing distance by specifically applying the quantized spiral phase modulation on the Fourier domain of the captured images before feeding them into a light-weight neural network. Therefore, these works will have important implications for microplastic detection and analysis protocols that are currently in use.
