17208121.label: Project Objectives
17208121.value: [To identify the multi-omics patterns unique to active growth and PHA accumulation states] Currently, there is no information on the corresponding epigenomes, transcriptomes and proteomes of PHA-producing bacterium. In particular, the epigenome profile that is unique to PHA accumulation state and active growth state remains unknown. Hence, this project will examine and compare the bacterium’s multi-omics profile during PHA production state (nitrogen-limiting condition) and active growth state (nitrogen-rich condition). This comparative study would enable multi-omic patterns, which are unique to each metabolic state, to be identified and defined for the first time. [To construct a methyltransferase interaction network using multi-omics approach and identify potential methyltransferase responsible for regulating PHA synthesis] At present, the interaction between methyltransferase (enzyme responsible for epigenetics modification) and PHA metabolism regulation is unknown. While the multi-omics data contains this information, manual curation of this big data would be impractical. As such, this project will encode the multi-omics features (obtained through Objective 1) into vectors and apply clustering algorithms to construct a methyltransferase interaction network. Through this network, the potential interactions between methyltransferase and the PHA metabolic/regulatory pathways would be disclosed. Furthermore, the potential methyltransferase responsible for regulating PHA synthesis would be identified. [To validate the epigenetic regulation of PHA production using methytransferase gene knockout mutant] Currently, there is no report of epigenetic-regulated PHA production. To establish the etiology of epigenetic effect on PHA production, this project will create methytransferase gene knockout mutant of P. putida NBUS12 based on the methyltransferase candidate identified in Objective 2. By cross-examining the multi-omics features and PHA biosynthesis ability of the mutant against the wildtype, this will establish the causality effect between epigenetics modifications and PHA production. Additionally, this project would unveil the mechanistic explanation for the role of epigenetics in PHA production regulation.

17208121.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17208121.value: In the last decade, global annual plastics production doubled to 359 million tonnes, placing enormous strains on non-renewable fossil fuel supply and the environment. Enhancing bacterial production of environmental-friendly bioplastic medium-chain-length polyhydroxyalkanoate (hereinafter referred to as “PHA”) would make it more cost-competitive, and help decrease mankind’s reliance on plastics while ushering in a new era of innovative applications in biomedical/pharmaceutical products. Key to this goal realization is the comprehensive understanding of PHA production regulatory mechanism. Here, we propose research to gain new and holistic insights on the epigenetic regulation of PHA production. PHA has attracted great attention due to its biodegradable and biocompatible properties. Its “plastic-like” and elastomeric properties meant that PHA is a strong contender to substitute conventional plastics. More importantly, PHA could be developed into commercial-valuable and high-end products such as, drug matrix encapsulation, soft tissue regeneration, bioartificial organs design, stem cell engineering. PHA production is typically triggered by an environmental stress signal such as nitrogen limitation. Upon sensing this signal, bacteria will switch its metabolism from active growth state to PHA production state. However, the low to mediocre levels of PHA accumulation (20-40% cell dry mass [CDM]) continues to hinder PHA commercialization. Incidentally, stress signals are also known to alter the bacterial epigenome. Epigenome is the chemical modifications of DNA (e.g., methylation) which plays an important role in gene expression regulation. Epigenetic modifications can transform the global cellular metabolism state and ultimately, phenotypes. However, the epigenetic effect on PHA production is currently unknown. This proposed research aims to delineate the role of epigenetics in PHA production regulation. With this knowledge, we could design strategies for more effective and prolonged activation of PHA synthesis. Our preliminary data prove that nitrogen stress resulted in differences in epigenome, gene and protein expression profiles for a model bacterium Pseudomonas putida NBUS12. Epigenetic modifications, which could alter gene transcription, were also observed. Building upon these findings, this project plans to (1) identify the multi-omics features (using epigenomics, transcriptomics and proteomics data) that are unique to growth state and PHA production state, (2) deploy a multi-omics clustering approach to identify the potential methyltransferase responsible for regulating PHA synthesis and (3) verify the epigenetic regulation and network using methyltransferase gene knockout mutant. The outcome of this project is expected to yield new possibilities for enhanced bacterial PHA production, and on the broader level, generate new interesting research topics regarding bacterial epigenetics and aromatics bioremediation. 在過去十年中，全球塑料年產量翻了一番，達到 3.59 億噸，給不可再生化石燃料供應和環境帶來了巨大壓力。增強環保型生物塑料中鏈聚羥基脂肪酸酯（以下簡稱“PHA”）的細菌生產將使其更具成本競爭力，並有助於減少人類對塑料的依賴，同時開啟生物醫學/醫藥產品創新應用的新時代。實現這一目標的關鍵是全面了解PHA生產調控機制。我們提出了此研究以獲得關於 PHA 生產的表觀遺傳調控的新的和整體的見解。 PHA由於其可生物降解和生物相容性的特性而備受關注。其“類塑料”和彈性特性意味著 PHA 是替代傳統塑料的有力競爭者。更重要的是，PHA可以開發成具有商業價值的高端產品，如藥物基質封裝、軟組織再生、生物人工器官設計、幹細胞工程等。 PHA 生產通常由環境壓力信號觸發，例如氮限制。檢測到該信號後，細菌會將其新陳代謝從活躍的生長狀態轉變為 PHA 生產狀態。然而，低至中等水平的 PHA 積累（20-40% 細胞幹質量 [CDM]）繼續阻礙 PHA 的商業化。 壓力信號也會改變細菌表觀基因組。表觀基因組是 DNA 的化學修飾（例如甲基化），在基因表達調控中起重要作用。表觀遺傳修飾可以改變整體細胞代謝狀態，並最終改變表型。然而，目前尚不清楚對 PHA 產生的表觀遺傳效應。 這項擬議的研究旨在描述表觀遺傳學在 PHA 生產調節中的作用。有了這些知識，我們可以設計更有效和更長時間激活 PHA 合成的策略。我們的初步數據證明，氮脅迫導致模型細菌惡臭假單胞菌 NBUS12 的表觀基因組、基因和蛋白質表達譜存在差異。還觀察到可以改變基因轉錄的表觀遺傳修飾。基於這些發現，該項目計劃 (1) 確定生長狀態和 PHA 生產狀態獨有的多組學特徵（使用表觀基因組學、轉錄組學和蛋白質組學數據），(2) 部署多組學聚類方法來識別負責調節 PHA 合成的潛在甲基轉移酶和 (3) 使用甲基轉移酶基因敲除突變體驗證表觀遺傳調控和網絡。該項目的成果有望為增強細菌 PHA 的生產提供新的可能性，並在更廣泛的層面上產生有關細菌表觀遺傳學和芳香族生物修復的新的有趣研究課題。

17208121.label: Realisation of objectives
17208121.value: All the objectives set out for this project have been achieved: (1) The multi-omics patterns, unique to Pseudomonas putida NBUS12’s active growth and PHA accumulation states (Objective 1), were elucidated through exposing the bacterium to nitrogen-rich and nitrogen-stress conditions, followed by a comparative multi-omics analysis of the changes to the bacterium at the DNA, RNA and protein level. A total of 990 genes were differentially methylated while 88% of the bacterium’s genes (5355 out of 6085 genes) and 2440 proteins was differentially expressed. Switching from an active growth to PHA biosynthesis state involved a change in energy substrate from styrene to nitrogen substrates. This was achieved through a down-regulation of the styrene catabolism pathway including the entry of styrene catabolite into the tricarboxylic (TCA) cycle, up-regulation of nitrogen uptake and catabolism, and a down-regulation of a part of the tricarboxylic (TCA) cycle (between 2-oxoglutarate and citrate) to preferentially favor the use of ammonium-generated L-glutamate for energy production to maintain life-sustaining processes and PHA production. The production of PHA was brought on by the up-regulation of de novo fatty acid and PHA synthesis pathways, channeling intracellular styrene catabolites towards PHA formation. Despite using styrene and ammonium as sole carbon and nitrogen substrates, similar metabolic switch was also observed for all other carbon substrates (glucose, fructose, benzoate, phthalate, glycerol) and nitrogen substrates (nitrate, nitrite) analyzed. Collectively, these results showed a system-level shift in the utilization of extracellular carbon sources for PHA synthesis and energy production towards the use of intracellular carbon for PHA synthesis and extracellular nitrogen as energy source. This work revealed that PHA production condition represents a distinct metabolic state from growth condition in P. putida NBUS12. The 5-methylcytosine (m5C) methylation was predominant among differentially-methylated genes, pointing to a potential role that C-5 cytosine-specific DNA methyltransferase plays in effecting the metabolic switch. Given that styrene, phthalate and benzoate are also compounds released from plastic products under pyrolysis, a study into the design of low-cost catalyst to achieve effective catalytic pyrolysis of plastic waste into pyrolytic oil product was also developed in tandem to pave the way for an innovative bio-thermochemical approach towards the transformation of non-biodegradable plastic waste into biodegradable PHA material. (2) A methyltransferase interaction network was successfully constructed and applied towards the prediction of potential regulators of PHA synthesis (Objective 2). This was done through the integration and harmonization of experimentally-obtained epigenomic, transcriptomic, and proteomic data using a knowledge graph data integration framework followed by knowledge graph link prediction, which predicated relationships within condition-specific regulatory modules, pointing towards potentially novel regulators of PHA synthesis. More specifically, the annotated genome of P. putida NBUS12 genome was integrated multi-omics data, creating position-aligned views of differentially expressed genes and proteins with DNA regulatory elements and epigenetic modifications. To add on information about the relationships between DNA methyltransferases, regulators, promoters, genes, and proteins, a Resource Description Framework (RDF) triplet structure approach, mirroring the cellular information flow between DNA and protein, was used. Through describing the known relationships between various omics entities, a harmonization of multi-dimensional heterogenous information can be achieved and systematically represented in the knowledge graph. Our network construction integrates two validated approaches: quantum-like decision-making model and Gaussian Boson Sampling (GBS) network analysis. The validated quantum model accurately simulates P. putida NBUS12's PHA production, achieving peak production of 13.81% cell dry mass at carbon-to-nitrogen (C/N) ratio 40:1. The GBS approach identified dense subgraphs representing integrated regulatory clusters involving the ribosome modulation factor (RMF) and PHA family proteins PhaF and PhaI, which encodes a PHA granule-associated protein phasin. The downregulation of rmf gene coupled with upregulation of its protein product indicated post-transcriptional mechanism which enhanced protein stability and translation efficiency during nitrogen stress, allowing rapid accumulation of RMF without the energetic cost of increased transcription. This post-transcriptional mechanism enables quick ribosome hibernation to conserve cellular resources for PHA biosynthesis while minimizing energy expenditure on new mRNA synthesis. C-5 cytosine-specific DNA methyltransferase was associated with changes in the gene and protein expression of RpoS (transcription regulator protein). A m5C methylation within the vicinity of the rpoS promoter region (-62 bp) was present only in PHA accumulation condition. It is probable that epigenetic modifications may play a role in modulating the binding of transcriptional regulator to gene promoter region, affecting the gene and subsequently, protein expression of RpoS. Collectively, our results suggested that PHA production could be regulated at both the epigenetic level (through C-5 cytosine-specific DNA methyltransferase) and protein translation level (through RMF). (3) To clarify the epigenetic regulation of PHA production, gene knockout of C-5 cytosine-specific DNA methyltransferase from P. putida NBUS12’s genome was conducted (Objective 3). However, the viability of the knockout mutant was found to be low. The mutant showed poor robustness during sub-culturing, making it challenging to achieve a viable knockout culture cell line for further study. This could be attributed to the role of m5C methylation in safeguarding the accuracy of DNA replication and repair. In the absence of this methylation, errors in DNA replication, particularly during cell growth and division, could have resulted in cumulative genetic mutations leading to cell lethality. To overcome this problem, we studied the rpoS knockout mutant of P. putida NBUS12, which was successfully created. Compared to wildtype which showed between 10 – 15% cell dry mass of PHA, the mutant had negligible amount of PHA content at the experimental endpoint of 48 hour. Time-series samples showed that rpoS-negative mutant was capable of accumulating PHA at levels similar to the wildtype during the bacterium’s exponential phase but unable to retain its PHA content after reaching stationary phase. This points to PHA degradation, which is tied to cell growth stage. This observation is in good agreement with existing published work, which reported an accelerated degradation of PHA due to an increased activity of PhaZ (a PHA depolymerization enzyme) coupled with an increasing limiting carbon availability at stationary phase (Raiger-lustman and Ruiz, 2008, FEMS Microbiol Lett 284, 218–224). Taken together, our work showed an involvement of C-5 cytosine-specific DNA methyltransferase in cell growth and division, and the role of RpoS in promoting PHA utilization in P. putida NBUS12. Given that the counteractive effects of nitrogen abundance and stress manifest as cell growth and PHA accumulation, respectively, it is plausible that the m5C methylation near rpoS promoter region could play an epigenetic regulatory role in this metabolic switch. Future studies using an emerging variable gene silencing approach could avoid the issue of non-viable cell line, allowing the role of C-5 cytosine-specific DNA methyltransferase to be comprehensively studied (refer to 6.2, point 1).

17208121.label: Major findings and research outcome
17208121.value: The project involves a substantial amount of experimental tests, bioinformatics analysis, knowledge graph construction and modelling prediction, leading to the following major findings and research outcomes: (1) Multi-omics analysis revealed new insights on the intricate regulation of carbon and nitrogen metabolism of P. putida NBUS12 to bring about PHA production under nitrogen-limitation conditions. Vermiculties-based catalyst, which achieved high selectively of plastic pyrolysis towards pyrolytic oil formation, was also developed to pave the way for an innovative bio-thermochemical approach towards the transformation of non-biodegradable polystyrene into styrene pyrolytic oil and eventually, biodegradable PHA (refer to Journal paper 1). (2) A comprehensive knowledge graph-based multi-layer network construction framework coupled with link prediction techniques for knowledge graph completion has been successfully developed for the integration of multi-omics data for regulatory network discovery in P. putida NBUS12. Key findings include the successful publication of our quantum modeling approach in Scientific Reports, demonstrating quantum-like decision-making in PHA production with validated parameters (kD/kN = 0.29512, θ = π) (refer to Journal paper 2, conference abstracts 1 and 2). Network analysis revealed post-transcriptional regulation of RMF during nitrogen stress and epigenetic-based transcriptional regulation of rpoS as potentially novel regulatory mechanisms for PHA biosynthesis control. The approach developed herein was also applied to the study of other microbes of interest leading to new metabolic insights (refer to conference abstract 3). 17208121.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17208121.value: 1. Based on the new insights uncovered through multi-omics analysis, we hypothesized that maintaining P. putida NBUS12 in a transition state between growth and PHA accumulation could facilitate an increased flow of extracellular carbon for PHA formation and supplementing energy production. Further development to test this hypothesis would include the use of variable gene silencing approach to achieve a tunable control over potential master regulator candidate gene(s). Developing ways to integrate multi-layer omics knowledge graph with quantum-like decision‑making model can enrich the model’s hidden layers of gene expression and regulation events, potentially modelling the transition state and parameters needed to achieve this state. Expanding current knowledge graph approach to include the integration of additional public databases/literature and large language models can automate the discovery process and strengthen the graph's predictive power. 2. Future efforts will be focused on testing the application of vermiculties-based catalyst to polystyrene, polyethylene terephthalate and complex plastic mixtures, followed by the testing of the resultant pyrolytic oil for PHA production to assess the effectiveness of the newly-developed catalyst over conventional non-catalytic pyrolysis. This endeavor will lay the foundation for a cost-effective way to upcycle plastic waste into renewable bioplastics.

17208121.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17208121.value: Bacteria can be harnessed to produce bioplastics, offering greener solution to conventional plastics. However, understanding how this process is controlled to maximize production is complicated due to complex gene-protein networks. We developed an approach which integrates information about DNA, gene activity, and protein production to reveal bioplastic formation process and the hidden network connections that control this process. Bioplastic production was found to be powered by nitrogen-based energy source instead of traditional carbon-based ones. The regulation of bioplastic formation likely involves a reversible chemical modification of the bacterium’s DNA that acts as a switch to (de)activate the production process. The project led to in-depth understanding of nitrogen’s dual role as the key energy source and environmental stress signal triggering bioplastic production. DNA modification is likely involved in translating stress information into adaptative genetic response for bioplastic formation. The a generic analysis framework developed has broad-based applicable to other regulatory mechanisms. We also developed a new and low-cost catalyst that could turn plastic waste into edible oil for bioplastic production. These developments lay the foundation for new strategies to improve bioplastic production and upcycle non-biodegradable plastics, presenting green solutions to alleviate the environmental impact of plastic waste.

17209021.value: 頭頸部癌症(HNCs)每年影響全球超過65萬人，其中HNC最常見的形式是鱗狀細胞癌，是全球第五常見的癌症。癌症的早期診斷和治療對於減少癌症進展至晚期需要侵襲性和毒性治療（如放療和化療）至關重要。上氣道內窺鏡檢查(如咽鏡和鼻咽鏡檢查)結合肉眼可疑病變的手術活檢是早期診斷的黃金標準。然而，喉嚨等管腔器官的病變往往起源於喉於上皮和上皮下結構，即使使用窄帶成像 (NBI)等輔助成像技術，在內窺鏡下也很難觀察到早期的癌前病變。因此，現時如光學相干斷層成像(OCT)的「光學活檢」方法已被採用，可以實時和無創地取得達致2.5mm深度的關鍵組織的高解析度一維組織深度圖。在內鏡檢查中，光學活檢應在內鏡檢查環境中進行。這衍生出一種對非接觸式光學活檢前視OCT探測儀器的需求。為了實現二維或三維成像，大多數現有的內窺鏡OCT技術採用微電子機械系統 (MEMS)方法，但該方法掃描距離小(<5mm)，掃描範圍小(<Ø3mm)，這嚴重限制了作為一種實用的，獨立的診斷系統，特別是因為掃描的穩定性和質量仍然高度依賴於臨床醫生的精確手動控制。此外，因為OCT圖像原位顯示缺乏病灶特異性路線圖顯示，在手術活檢或切除過程中同時使用是具有挑戰性的。 因此，本項目旨於開發和驗證一個三維前視內窺鏡OCT軟體機器人系統，用於原位內窺鏡擴增實境。提出的OCT引導的手術內機器人系統將包括兩個主要部分：i） 一個靈活的和可鎖定的軟體機器人內窺鏡用於到達口-下嚥區域的目標病灶，並為OCT掃描和擴增實境覆蓋提供穩定的平台；ii）一個精巧、於內窺鏡尖端軟體機器OCT探頭，用於實現大範圍掃描表面腫瘤三維成像。OCT激光探頭的精確及穩健轉向將由結合視覺伺服和光纖布拉格光柵(FBG)形狀傳感的實時編碼提供。隨後，利用人工智能驅動的視覺深度估計結合現場擴增實境的三維合成，可以實現在單目內窺鏡試圖下疊加OCT成像。該系統將於混合人工/體外口-下嚥模型中，然後在活豬標本中進行驗證。

17209521.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17209521.value: Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM) based nanorobots opens the doors for characterizing, modifying, assembling, and even fabricating high functional nano structures and devices. While manipulating, in-situ observation and characterization can be performed rather than off-line using SEM, TEM or other super-resolution microscopy. AFM-based nanorobots have been applied to numerous applications including MEMS fabrication, material characterization, biomedical studies, and nanometrology, etc. However, the existing motion control methods for AFM-based robots have mainly relied on position sensors and only considered the system kinematics. Due to the thermo drift and structure deformation, it is impossible to accurately measure the probe tip position in the sub-nano meter scale that is commonly demanded in applications nowadays. Furthermore, image-based control methods commonly used in AFM-based robots require to extract features from images to obtain position measurements in vector space. This process is time-consuming if the features are not explicit. In addition, with increasing demands on the motion speed and precision, it is necessary to consider the dynamics of the nano robotic manipulations that has been ignored in most of existing approaches. The challenge is to develop new image-based dynamics control method to achieve sub-nano meter motion accuracy and avoid tedious feature extraction. We propose to develop a semantic compressive feedback control method to meet the challenge. Considering AFM local scan images as sets, the motion control problem can be formulated in the space of sets instead of traditional vectors. All the intensity information of the image will be used for control. Therefore, no feature extraction is needed. In addition, the image feedbacks will be obtained using compressive scanning. As a result, both the sampling and computation time can be significantly reduced, which is crucial to a high accuracy dynamics motion control. A new semantic compressive sensing method is proposed to utilize the content information of images to further improve the quality of sensing. It can eliminate the image sparsity requirement, a major obstacle for the applications of compressive sensing. The proposed semantic compressive dynamics control method will provide high rate of real-time feedbacks, achieve sub-nano meter motion control accuracy, and eliminate the requirements for system calibration. The successes of the proposed project will provide an essential technology for nano manufacturing and biomedical industry. The results of this proposed project will pave the ways for the development of new instruments, tools and systems to significantly advance nano manufacturing, medical diagnostics as well as drug discovery. 基於原子力顯微技術 (AFM) 的納米機器人已被廣泛用於納米加工和測量，與基於電子掃描顯微鏡，和電子透視顯微鏡的納米操作技術相比，其有使用方便，可進行原位操作等優勢。現有的基於AFM的納米操作主要采用基於位置測量的反饋運動控制方法。但在納米尺度下測量位置是極爲困難的，現有位置傳感技術很難達到亞納米的測量精度。另外，前基於圖像的位置控制方案需要提取圖像特徵，然後得到位置向量，其計算量極爲費時。本項研究一種基於圖像集合的位置控制方法，直接反饋整個圖像利用圖像中全部信息進行位置反饋從而避免了特徵提取等耗時計算，同時由於直接反饋圖像可大大降低對系統較正的要求，並消除AFM探針彈性變成對位置定位精度的影響。除此之外，此項目將開發基於壓縮感知的掃描方法，從而大大降低掃描時間，採用壓縮後AFM圖像進行反饋控制可顯著提高反饋頻率從而改善位置控制精度。此項目將研究基於語義的壓縮掃描方式，根據圖像特徵進行壓縮從而提供壓縮率並改善壓縮圖像的質量，以提高反饋控制精度，實現亞納米級位置控制。此項目的預期成果可用於納米製造和生物醫學研究和開發，將為納米器件製造，醫療診斷和新藥開發提供新的技術手段和設備。

17209521.value: Please refer to the attached report on the last page. This report presents an AFM based nanorobotic control framework for the precise manipulation of nanoscale materials with sub-nanometer resolution. At the core of this robotic system are two key innovations: a semantic compressive visual servoing algorithm for the rapid updating of scan images, and a realtime non-vector control scheme to continuously compensates for drift and controls the probe's motion. This approach successfully reduces full image scan times to 10% of conventional methods and implements drift compensation, thereby maintaining nanomanipulation with a positional error of only a few nanometers. The framework's high efficiency is demonstrated through experimental results, including the automated tracking of DNA strands and the controlled assembly of nanoparticles.

17209521.label: Major findings and research outcome
17209521.value: This project delivers the first real-time control framework that closes the feedback loop directly on AFM image sets. By treating every local scan as a finite, we recast the AFM manipulator into a nonlinear “mutation” system whose state is the image itself; scanner drift, piezo creep and illumination changes are absorbed into this model, removing the need for ad-hoc feature extraction or task-space calibration. A Lyapunov functional defined by the squared Hausdorff distance between the current and target image sets yields a compact feedback law with proven exponential convergence that remains stable without linearization, so nanometer accuracy is retained even during extended experiments. For the semantic compressive-sensing scheme we developed, we could be able to compress the jointly learned binary sampling from 5% to 20% mask and paired low/high-resolution dictionaries cut the acquisition time to 100ms, while limiting reconstruction error to 2×10−3 nm and lifting PSNR by 5 dB. Because the observer and the NVS-compressive controller obey a separation principle in the set domain, convergence of the compressed set guarantees convergence of the full set. Simulations on carbon-nanotube maps show that compressed scans suppress a deliberately introduced rift to less than 3 nm. Experimental validation on established nanorobotic system corroborates the analysis. Closed-loop localization lowers root-mean-square probe error from 68 nm (open loop) to 4.8 nm on a 5 µm carbon-nanotube field and to under 1 nm on a 2 µm λ-DNA field. Employing the operate-then-scan cycle, the system rearranged sixteen 90 nm polystyrene beads to spell the letter “A” in fifteen minutes without any global re-scans, while a high frame rate 3d user interface streamed topography and force data for continuous operator oversight. Altogether the work achieves a 90 % reduction in imaging delay while maintaining sub 3 nm positioning precision, opening a path to high-throughput nanomanufacturing and single-molecule biophysics. Overall, the project delivers the first provably stable, semantically compressed, real-time image-set controller for AFM nanorobots, cutting scan time by >90 % while achieving sub-5 nm accuracy. These advances pave the way for high-throughput nanomanufacturing and single-molecule biophysics.

17209521.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17209521.value: For further development, the aspect is algorithmic. We will replace the fixed sampling mask with an adaptive variant that is learned in real time from the incoming data stream. Coupled with a multi-objective controller that balances speed, positioning error, and probe wear, the upgraded software is expected to push the frame time below 10ms. In parallel, extending the Lyapunov set framework to three dimensions will allow simultaneous control of lateral position and contact force. To translate these gains into practice, the entire reconstruction-and-control pipeline will be migrated from the host PC to a field-programmable gate array (FPGA). Adopting an FPGA will cut communication latency from 200 µs to less than 20 µs and will provide hardware acceleration for our fast-scan scheme. These technical advances will open three application fronts. In nanobiology, the faster, gentler touch will permit real-time observation of enzyme–DNA interactions. In the semiconductor field, the nanorobotic system will be further modified to assemble two-dimensional materials onto patterned electrodes.

17209521.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17209521.value: We have modified an atomic-force microscope that uses a tiny probe to map and manipulate nanoscale objects such as DNA strands and nanomaterials, allowing it to see and act much faster. Conventionally, the microscope must scan every pixel of an image before it knows where to place its probe. That process is slow, and the sample can drift while it waits. Our new method lets the probe automatically locate the region of interest and skip most of the unimportant areas, even when the sample is moving, so we can steer the probe in real time while the image is still incomplete. We also identified which few pixels matter most and created a smart “mask” that samples only about one-twentieth of the full image. As a result, a scan now finishes in less than 100ms yet recovers the same detail as a full scan. Tests show the probe’s average positioning error has fallen from hundreds of nanometers to three nanometers, which is small enough to arrange individual molecules or build tiny electronic parts. This leap in speed and accuracy will help researchers manufacture nanoscale devices and automate tasks that involve nanometer-scale objects.

17209721.label: Realisation of objectives
17209721.value: Objective 1 has been realized by the work ''EZCrop: Energy-Zoned Channels for Robust Output Pruning'' (WACV22) which establishes a newly proposed frequency-domain perspective for CNN channel pruning. Specifically, we analytically bridge the rank-based channel importance metric in the spatial domain to an energy perspective in the frequency domain, for the first time explaining the interesting constant-rank phenomenon in CNN feature map channels. The proposed FFT-based metric reduces computational complexity from O(n^3) to O(n^2 log n) while achieving better pruning performance. For example, on CIFAR-10 dataset, EZCrop achieves 94.01% accuracy with 58.1% FLOPs reduction on VGGNet, significantly outperforming previous methods. The algorithm's robustness is further demonstrated through repetitive pruning experiments where it consistently maintains high accuracy even after multiple pruning passes. To benefit the research community, we have open-sourced the implementation at https://github.com/ruilin0212/EZCrop. Objective 2 has been fully accomplished and extended through two complementary works. First, ''FAT: Frequency-Aware Transformation for Bridging Full-Precision and Low-Precision Deep Representations'' (IEEE TNNLS22) introduces a novel frequency mask inspired by the energy-based findings in Objective 1. This Frequency-Aware Transformation (FAT) achieves state-of-the-art quantization performance by identifying and preserving important frequency components before quantization. The implementation is publicly available at https://github.com/ChaofanTao/FAT_Quantization. Building upon these frequency-theoretic insights, our work ''Frequency Regularization for Improving Adversarial Robustness'' develops a strong defense mechanism against adversarial attacks. By aligning the spectral distributions between natural and adversarial inputs, we achieve 49.2% average improvements under white-box attacks and 21.7% under black-box attacks on CIFAR-10, while maintaining training efficiency comparable to natural training. Objective 3 is realized through ''Learning Spatially Collaged Fourier Bases for Implicit Neural Representation'' (AAAI24), which presents SCONE (Spatially Collaged cOordinate NEtworks) - a first-ever coordinate network that explicitly collages patches of different frequencies. Unlike existing approaches that employ a global combination of Fourier features, SCONE incorporates end-to-end learnable spatial masks to allocate specific Fourier bases to their corresponding regions, again based on the insights from Objectives 1&2. This novel architecture demonstrates superior performance across various computer vision tasks, improving image fitting PSNR by over 3dB and achieving state-of-the-art 3D reconstruction with 98.81% IoU and 0.0011 Chamfer Distance, surpassing traditional CNN counterparts. The implementation is available at https://github.com/jasonli0707/scone. The above works not only fulfill but substantially exceed the original objectives. Each paper advances the state-of-the-art in its respective area while maintaining strong connections through the underlying frequency-domain perspective. The public availability of all implementations promotes reproducibility and enables further advancement in frequency-based deep learning research. Moreover, these works have sparked new research directions in frequency-domain neural network design and analysis, as evidenced by follow-up works from our group within and beyond the project period. In particular, the seminal frequency-domain innovations established in the abovementioned key foundational papers have catalyzed several significant derivative works as follows: -- Building upon the frequency-energy based metrics introduced for channel pruning, ''Structured Pruning for Efficient Generative Pre-trained Language Models'' extends this concept to develop SIMPLE - a sparsity-induced mask learning framework that enables flexible pruning of attention heads, feed-forward networks, and hidden dimensions in large language models (LLMs). -- The frequency-domain understanding of dynamic range characterization has inspired ''Context-Aware Transformer for 3D Point Cloud Automatic Annotation,'' which introduces a novel split-encoder design to capture both local and global frequency-domain feature relations in point clouds, achieving state-of-the-art 3D box annotation without complex multi-stage processing. -- Meanwhile, the original work on homogeneous frequency-domain architectures has evolved into multiple efficient hardware implementations: ''An Isotropic Shift-Pointwise Network'' achieves near-100% RRAM crossbar utilization through an innovative mixed-signal design leveraging digital shifts for spatial mixing and analog operations for channel mixing, while the related paper ''A Unifying Tensor View for Lightweight CNNs'' provides valuable theoretical foundations by establishing connections between various tensor decomposition schemes and efficient CNN modules, including the first analysis of shift layer pruning. Then, ''PECAN: A Product-Quantized Content Addressable Memory Network'' proposes a novel content addressable memory (CAM)-based neural architecture that replaces standard convolutions with similarity-based lookup operations. -- The frequency-domain processing principles have also enabled breakthroughs in additional domains - ''Fast Classification and Action Recognition with Event-Based Imaging'' introduces an aligned compressed event tensor representation for efficiently processing high-temporal-resolution event camera data. -- Finally, ''Lite It Fly'' presents an automated framework for generating deformable butterfly chains, demonstrating how the core frequency-domain concepts can be systematically applied to create highly compressed yet accurate neural networks. Together, these works showcase how the foundational frequency-domain principles have enabled advances across model compression, efficient architecture design, and practical hardware implementation while maintaining or improving accuracy.

17209721.label: Major findings and research outcome
17209721.value: This project has successfully established a comprehensive frequency-domain framework for neural network design and optimization, yielding several breakthrough findings: First, we discovered a fundamental connection between channel importance in CNNs and their frequency-domain energy distribution. This led to EZCrop, which achieves state-of-the-art pruning performance while reducing computational complexity from O(n^3) to O(n^2 log n). The work provides the first theoretical explanation for the previously mysterious constant-rank phenomenon in CNN feature maps. Second, we developed Frequency-Aware Transformation (FAT), a transform-based quantization framework that bridges full-precision and low-precision representations through frequency-domain analysis. By identifying and preserving important frequency components before quantization, FAT achieves superior compression while maintaining model accuracy. This insight also enabled a novel defense mechanism against adversarial attacks through spectral distribution alignment. Third, we introduced SCONE (Spatially Collaged cOordinate NEtworks), pioneering the concept of spatially-aware frequency basis allocation in neural networks. This innovation significantly improves performance across various computer vision tasks, demonstrating gains of over 3dB PSNR in image reconstruction and state-of-the-art results in 3D shape modeling, overtaking their conventional convolutional neural network (CNN) counterparts.

17209721.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17209721.value: This GRF project has developed new ways to make artificial intelligence (AI) systems more efficient by analyzing them in terms of frequencies - similar to how music can be broken down into different notes. Just as some musical notes are more important than others in a song, we found that certain frequencies in AI systems carry more important information than others. This novel spectral (frequency-domain) insight allowed us to create new methods to compress AI systems by keeping only the most important frequencies, much like how digital music can be compressed while maintaining good sound quality. Our methods make AI systems up to 14 times smaller while maintaining their performance, enabling them to run on edge devices with restrictive compute and storage resources. The project has produced three journal papers, eight conference papers, and multiple open-source software tools that have sparked a series of follow-up works in frequency-domain AI optimization.

17209821.label: Project Objectives
17209821.value: Novel techniques to model type-directed computation algorithms and proofs: We will improve the state-of-the-art for modelling the semantics of type-directed computation in two ways. Firstly, instead of the current elaboration semantics approach, we will employ a more lightweight approach based on type-directed operational semantics. Secondly, we develop simpler algorithms for resolution and subtyping. Both of these advances will greatly simplify the current algorithms and proofs and enable introducing novel features of practical interest. Type-directed computation with subtyping, parametric polymorphism and recursive types: Our second objective is to extend the type-directed computation mechanisms developed in the OOPSLA work with practical language features such as parametric polymorphism (or generics) and recursive types. Both of these extensions are highly non-trivial and require careful analysis of their interaction with the features that are already modelled in our OOPSLA work. A prototype language for type-directed computation with subtyping. Finally, to demonstrate the potential of our work, we will develop a prototype programming language that implements the algorithms developed in the previous objectives. We will conduct several case studies illustrating the potential of type-directed computation for programming and modularity.

17210621.label: Realisation of objectives
17210621.value: The project faced challenges during the COVID-19 pandemic and emigration wave in Hong Kong, resulting in a difficult start. Between 2021-2022, technicians and research staff members left the group. The outbreak of the fifth wave of COVID-19 in March 2022, the principal investigator (PI) and research staff members were instructed to work from home, leading to the closure of the University and laboratory. Consequently, no experiments could be conducted during this period. However, research activities gradually resumed in the summer of 2022. Preliminary investigations and feasibility studies/experiments were initiated, aided by the arrival of a new PhD student, Mr Zhang Heng, in August 2022. Mr Zhang played a significant role in assisting the PI with theoretical analysis and hardware implementation. In the second year of the project, a series of printed circuit board (PCB) resonators were fabricated. The Substrate material and geometric design of the copper tracks have been examined. The use of PCB resonator to either enhance or diminish the magnetic field have been studied. An array form of resonators has been assembled as artificial magnetic metamaterials with controllable permeability. The performance of the metameterials in harnessing and manipulation of electromagnetic field, including the flux density, field strength, and shape have been investigated. Preliminary theory and mathematical models of the metamaterials have been formulated. In August 2023, the principal investigator (PI) resigned from the HKU and was deemed ineligible to continue as the principal investigator, as per the RGC's requirements. An early completion for this project was granted and approved. A comparative study on the efficiency improvement of a PCB resonator and a metamaterial slab in a two-coil wireless power transfer system has been carried out. This study reveals that the efficiency improvement varies depending on their relative position to the receiver. The metamaterial slab exhibits greater efficiency improvement when placed closer to the receiver, while the relay coil is more effective when positioned farther away. However, the metamaterial slab robustly retains its efficiency improvement capability within a range of relative position compared to the relay coil. This work addressed the project objective 1, and has been accepted to publish in an IEEE conference [1]. Insights have been gained regarding the use of metamaterial for efficiency improvement in WPT system. A passive relay resonator array has been developed, leverages the tailored magnetic properties of gradient metamaerials to enhance transfer efficiency and range without modifying the transmitter-receiver configuration. This robust WPT system maintains a load-independent constant current ratio between transmitter and receiver, regardless of variations in transfer distance. This study encompasses a comprehensive theoretical analysis, compensation parameter optimization for maximum transfer efficiency, and co-simulation verification. This work directly addressed project objective 2 and has been accepted for presentation at an international conference in October. [2]. Additionally, two wireless power transfer applications have been developed with the support of this RGC research fund. One of the applications is the wireless hybrid stepper motor (HSM) system, which has been proposed and implement [3]. This system provides high controllability of speed, direction, and position without requiring physical contact and electrical connection between the power source and the motor. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed system can handle a 1.5-N·m load at a speed of 430 rpm in full-step drive mode. Mover, the speed and rotor position can also be controlled without the need for sensors and feedback. This topology can also be extended to other types of stepper motors, such as VR stepper motors and unipolar PM stepper motor, and also other motors with unipolar windings. This significant work has recently been accepted for publication in the IEEE Transactions on Power Electronics. Capsule endoscopy, an emerging technology for the diagnosis and monitoring of gastrointestinal diseases, offers a non-invasive approach. However, this technology faces inherent limitations of short-range of investigation due to limited battery capacity and uncertainty of capsule’s position. Within the gastrointestinal tract. To address these challenges, the PI and his research student have developed a novel approach to seamlessly combine wireless battery charging, and 6 degrees of freedom tracking of capsule endoscopy, all within a single apparatus. A paper detailing this development has been submitted to the IEEE transactions on industrial electronics and is currently under review [4]. The project’s key research objectives have been successfully achieved, resulting in the production of two conference papers and two journal papers. The accomplishment fulfills project objective 3.

17210621.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17210621.value: Metamaterials have emerged as an innovative approach to enhance transfer efficiency in mid-range wireless power transfer (WPT). However, relying on specific negative permeability as a performance enhancement reference at optical and microwave frequencies becomes less effective for optimizing efficiency in WPT systems at lower operating frequencies in the near-field regime. The PI is currently investigating a new method that combining analytical criteria from a coupled-mode model and finite-element method (FEM) simulations. This method aims to determine the unit cell geometries of the metamaterials, the arrangement of cells within a finite metamaterial slab, and the optimal position of the slab. It has the potential to serve as a bottom-up optimization design methodology for metamaterial-based WPT systems.

17210621.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17210621.value: In this two-year project, our objective was to investigate the utilization of metamaterials in the design of coupled coils for inductive power transfer. Specifically, we aimed to focus and steer the magnetic field to a particular direction. This approach not only increases efficiency and transfer distance but also reduces the exposure of surrounding objects to the electromagnetic field. We formulated theories, methods and framework applicable for achieving these goals. Thanks to the support from the RGC research fund, the team has successfully produced two conference papers and two journal papers. Additionally, one PhD student received extensive training and emerged as a competent researcher, equipped with valuable knowledge and skills to contribute to the power electronics and wireless power communities. This project has opened up a new research area of metamaterials in low-frequency electromagnetic application. Long distance inductive power transfer technology is promising in biomedical applications such as capsule endoscopy and implantable medical devices. The continuous development of IPT technology will undoubtedly benefit various industries and advance human life.

17300021.label: Project Objectives
17300021.value: We investigate nonnegative low multi-rank transformed tensor approximation problem under the transformed tensor singular value decomposition. We develop and analyze algorithms for nonnegative low multi-rank transformed tensor approximation problem by using alternating projections. We study the tangent space of a point in the manifold in the transformed domain to approximate the projection onto the manifold in order to reduce the computational cost, and analyze the convergence results. 17300021.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17300021.value: Nonnegative data from many applications are represented as multi-dimensional data which refers to as nonnegative tensor, e.g., video data and hyperspectral data are nonnegative tensors. Nonnegative low rank tensor approximation for nonnegative tensors plays a key role in many image processing and analysis applications. The main aim of nonnegative low rank tensor approximation is to identify latent features for objects representation and preserve nonnegative data constraints. The classification and recognition analysis can be performed by using latent features. In classical nonnegative tensor factorization, a nonnegative tensor is decomposed into the product of several components (nonnegative low rank tensors and matrices) for finding latent features. In this project, we propose new models and algorithms for computing nonnegative low rank tensor approximation for nonnegative tensors. Our approach is to find a nonnegative low rank tensor such that the difference between nonnegative low rank tensor and the given nonnegative tensor is as small as possible. Here nonnegative constraints are preserved in low rank tensor approximation, but the underlying latent features are not necessary to be nonnegative. It is different from classical nonnegative tensor factorization where each factorization components are required to be nonnegative. In the proposed formulation, nonnegative constraints are less restricted. The low rank tensor approximation results and the resulting image analysis and recognition can be expected to be better. These results will be tested and demonstrated in the project. On the other hand, low rank tensor structure can become more obvious after suitable transformations are applied to tensors like imaging data. We propose and investigate nonnegative low rank transformed tensor approximation for nonnegative tensors under the transformed tensor singular value decomposition. We develop alternating projection algorithms for solving such nonnegative tensor approximation problem. The convergence analysis will be conducted by analyzing nonnegative constraints in tensor entries (the original domain) and low rank structure in the transformed tensor entries (the transformed domain). Note that singular value decomposition calculation can be quite expensive especially when there are many singular value decompositions are required for nonnegative low rank transformed tensor approximation. In this project, we will study the tangent space of a point in the manifold in the transformed domain to approximate the projection onto the manifold in order to reduce the computational cost, and analyze the convergence results. Furthermore, we investigate into our theoretical results and numerical algorithms in the application of multi-dimensional image processing with missing and noisy observations. 來自許多應用程序的非負數據表示為多維數據，稱為非負張量，例如，視頻數據和高光譜數據是非負張量。非負張量的非負低秩張量近似在許多圖像處理和分析應用中起著關鍵作用。非負低秩張量近似的主要目的是識別對象表示的潛在特徵並保留非負數據約束。可以使用潛在特徵進行分類和識別分析。在經典的非負張量分解中，非負張量被分解為幾個分量（非負低秩張量和矩陣）的乘積，以尋找潛在特徵。 在這個項目中，我們提出了新的模型和算法來計算非負張量的非負低秩張量近似。我們的方法是找到一個非負低秩張量，使得非負低秩張量和給定的非負張量之間的差異盡可能小。這裡在低秩張量近似中保留了非負約束，但潛在的潛在特徵不必是非負的。它不同於經典的非負張量分解，其中每個分解分量都必須是非負的。在建議的公式中，非負約束的限制較少。可以預期低秩張量近似結果和由此產生的圖像分析和識別會更好。這些結果將在項目中進行測試和演示。另一方面，在對成像數據等張量應用適當的變換後，低秩張量結構會變得更加明顯。我們提出並研究了在變換張量奇異值分解下非負張量的非負低秩變換張量近似。我們開發了交替投影算法來解決這種非負張量近似問題。收斂分析將通過分析張量條目（原始域）中的非負約束和轉換張量條目（轉換域）中的低秩結構來進行。請注意，奇異值分解計算可能非常昂貴，尤其是當非負低秩變換張量近似需要許多奇異值分解時。在本項目中，我們將研究變換域中流形中一點的切線空間，以近似投影到流形上以降低計算成本，並分析收斂結果。此外，我們研究了我們的理論結果和數值算法在具有缺失和噪聲觀測的多維圖像處理的應用中。

17300121.value: 通过对候选火山口的形态测量学、年龄、结构和地质背景的表征，探索古代火星上的爆炸性火山活动

17300121.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17300121.value: It is well known that Mars contains striking volcanic features including huge shield volcanoes, vast lava plains, and large, structurally complex calderas. In fact, the largest volcano and many of the most recognizable volcanic features in the Solar System occur on Mars. Study of Mars’ volcanic evolution has been critical to understanding crustal heat flow, large scale resurfaces, the generate of volcanigenic volatiles and links to greenhouse gasses and climate evolution, and many other far-reaching science issues. But, there is one major problem – a major contradiction exists. On one hand, decades of geologic mapping have shown clear, abundant and convincing evidence for widespread effusive volcanism on the red planet. On the other hand, modelling results indicate that volcanism should be much more explosive on Mars than on Earth due to lower pressure in the crust, resulting from lower gravity. Therefore, even mafic and ultramafic volcanoes that are generally the least explosive type of volcanoes on Earth should in fact be quite explosive on Mars. This presents a geologic puzzle with major implications. Has volcanism on Mars been less explosive than theory clearly suggests? Or do we have a biased view of Mars volcanic history based on empirical data because it is so much easier to identify and map effusive volcanoes than explosive ones? We know from our experience on Earth that explosive volcanism is not always obvious in the geologic record because the process is a destructive one that results in structurally collapsed features and ash deposits rather than easily spatially linked lava flows with shield-like mountain structures. This work will address the geologic puzzle by exploring for and evaluating evidence for previously unrecognized explosive volcanism on Mars. The project builds on previous results published by the PI in Nature several years ago, showing evidence for several very large, previously un-recognized calderas on Mars. In this work, the team will carry out a global survey for similar features with a clear aim to quantify the morphometrics of known calderas and candidate calderas. In other words, we will investigate enigmatic collapse features, irregular impact craters, and other depressions around the planet in order to quantitively assess whether there is evidence for explosive volcanism with these features. If our results reveal a previously unrecognized or largely under-appreciated explosive volcanic history of Mars, it would dramatically change our understanding of crust production, resurface, and evolution, as well as volcanically induced climate change. 众所周知，火星具有惊人的火山特征，包括巨大的盾牌 火山、广阔的熔岩平原和结构复杂的大型火山口。事实上，最大的 火山和太阳系中许多最知名的火山特征发生 在火星上。研究火星的火山演化对于了解地壳 热流、大规模重新地表、火山挥发物的产生和与 温室气体和气候演变，以及许多其他影响深远的科学问题。 但是，有一个大问题——存在着一个大矛盾。一方面，几十年 地质图已显示出清晰、丰富和令人信服的证据 红色星球上的火山活动。另一方面，建模结果表明 由于压力较低，火星上的火山活动应该比地球上的更具爆炸性 在地壳中，由于重力较低。因此，即使是镁铁质和超镁铁质 地球上通常是爆炸性最低的火山类型的火山实际上应该 在火星上很有爆发力. 这提出了一个具有重大意义的地质难题。拥有 火星上的火山活动没有理论明确表明的那么具有爆炸性？或者我们有 基于经验数据对火星火山历史的偏见看法，因为它容易得多 识别和绘制喷发火山而不是爆炸火山？我们从我们的 地球上的经验，爆炸性火山活动在地质记录中并不总是很明显 因为这个过程是一种破坏性的过程，会导致结构倒塌的特征 和灰烬沉积，而不是容易与盾状山在空间上联系在一起的熔岩流 结构。这项工作将通过探索和评估来解决地质难题 先前未被发现的火星爆炸性火山活动的证据。该项目建立在 PI 几年前在 Nature 上发表的先前结果，显示了 火星上有几个非常大的、以前未被发现的破火山口。在这项工作中，团队 将对类似特征进行全球调查，明确目标是量化已知破火山口和候选破火山口的形态测量学。换句话说，我们将 调查神秘的坍塌特征、不规则的撞击坑和其他凹陷 以定量评估是否有爆炸物的证据 具有这些特征的火山活动。如果我们的结果揭示了以前未被认识或在很大程度上 被低估的火星爆炸性火山历史，它将极大地改变我们 了解地壳的产生、重新表面和演化，以及火山 诱发的气候变化。

17300321.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17300321.value: 多價性描述了兩個分子之間多配體和多位點的同時結合。天然生物系統已廣泛利用多價性實現了高結合力、特異性，且可逆的分子相互作用。除了結合力和特異性外，多價相互作用也可能受到受體幾何結構和組織的影響，從而產生具有特定生物學功能的結構。生物學中有很多例子，比如中和病原體時免疫球蛋白與抗原的結合、引發病毒和細菌感染的病原微生物與宿主細胞之間多聚聚醣蛋白的識別，以及細胞表面的寡聚受體複合物與各種細胞外信號分子之間的相互作用。因此，開發多價相互作用的調節劑和抑製劑對於基礎生物學研究和藥物發現具有巨大的潛力。然而靶向多價系統的研究目前仍然非常困難。主要因為多價靶標上的單獨位點的親和力通常很低，結合位點相距較遠，使得多價配體的設計極具挑戰性。DNA編碼的化學文庫 (DEL) 是一種強大的高通量篩選藥物開發技術。本項目旨在開發一種適用於具有多價結合位點的蛋白質複合物的新型 DEL 方法，組裝與 DNA 共軛的單價配體，形成大規模 DEL，不僅可展示配體化學結構多樣性，還可展示配體構型多樣性。此外，可設計不同的 DNA 支架以匹配不同結合維度的價態和對稱性。本項目將 a) 針對多價生物系統實現大規模化學庫的高通量篩選；b) 利用 DEL 為多價配體開發提供有效方法；c) 使用 DNA 標記來編碼結合形成的復合物中配體的化學結構信息。我們的目標是利用DEL針對與人類疾病有關的各種蛋白質複合物做篩選，例如細菌毒素、細胞因子和病毒刺突蛋白。一方面，這部分研究將證明本申請所提出方法的通用性和性能；另一方面，這些靶標具有很高的生物學和治療意義，但在傳統高通量篩選方法中仍然難以處理，因此針對它們的篩選可能發展出新療法，為疾病治療帶來新的機會。綜上所述，本申請旨在開發一種新穎高效的工具來探索和開發針對多價生物系統的具有獨特空間結構的配體。 該方法不僅適用於申請中列舉的生物靶點，還可廣泛適用於其他生物靶點。 除了配體開發，本申請的研究成果還可以幫助闡明多價靶蛋白的多種生物學功能背後的分子機制。

17300321.label: Realisation of objectives
17300321.value: Objective 1, to develop a DNA-encoded library (DEL) method for assembling multivalent ligand libraries (DEMLs) with high structural and configurational diversities. The methodology was developed and validated using two model systems (streptavidin tetramer and HIV-1 protease dimer), involving extensive optimization of both library synthesis and selection protocols. This work has been published (Nat. Chem. 2024, 4, 21, 543-555). Furthermore, we developed two AI-based data analysis methods for accurate hit identification and validation post-selection, with findings published in ACS Omega (2023, 8, 21, 19057-19071) and under review at Bioinformatics. Leveraging this method, we constructed a series of multivalent DNA-encoded libraries and applied them against many multivalent biological targets, leading to the identification of potent and selective hit compounds and compound-DNA constructs for further biological evaluation. Objective 2, to design a series of library scaffolds matching the valency and symmetry of diverse multivalent biological systems. As recommended by the original proposal's referees, we focused on bivalent (D2MLs) and trivalent (D3MLs) DEMLs. For bivalent libraries, we designed and synthesized two types of DNA duplex-based scaffolds to target adjacent binding pockets on streptavidin tetramers and HIV-1 protease dimers. For trivalent libraries, we developed a scaffold based on 3-way DNA junctions to target the sialic acid binding pockets on influenza hemagglutinin (HA) trimers and COVID-19 glycospike protein (S-protein) trimers. Additionally, we prepared tetravalent library (D4MLs) scaffolds based on 4-way DNA junctions. Methodology development and validation in model systems have been completed for all scaffold types. Objective 3, to build a series of large-scale DEMLs at the multi-billion-compound scale. The bivalent libraries contain ~20 million compounds due to the relatively low dimension of diversity. The trivalent libraries contain ~370 million compounds in total, including ~190 million trivalent glycan libraries and ~280 million peptide libraries. The tetravalent libraries have a much greater number of compounds with ~1.1 billion peptides in total. As detailed later, selections were primarily performed using the bivalent and trivalent libraries. Objective 4, the development of a method capable of selecting DEMLs against multivalent biological targets. As mentioned above in Objective 1, we have developed an affinity-based selection method of these multivalent libraries against a variety of protein complexes including streptavidin tetramers, HIV-1 protease dimers, influenza hemagglutinin trimers, insulin receptor dimers, TPOR dimers, EGFR dimers, COVID-19 S-protein trimers, TNFα trimers, and the wheat germ agglutinin (WGA) tetramers. The selection method largely follows the experimental conditions and protocols of regular DELs, but we have performed extensive optimization to minimize the non-specific DNA-protein interaction, crucial given the large DNA scaffold molecules employed. Notably, selections can be performed with either purified proteins or membrane protein complexes directly on live cells (e.g., EGFR, insulin receptor, and TPOR dimers, and TNFα trimers). In addition, we have developed statistical and AI-based methods for data analysis, which can accurately identify multivalent binders from mono-valent binders and other binders with lower valencies. Objective 5, to identify potent and specific ligands for representative multivalent protein targets and also validate the biological functions of the identified ligands. In the abovementioned objectives, we have completed the design, preparation, and model studies of these multivalent libraries. In this objective, we have applied the libraries in the selections against a series of proteins and protein complexes. Novel binders have been identified in all selection campaigns. We have characterized the binding affinity and selectivity of the top hit compounds, followed by the validation of their biological activities. Of note, we indeed observed that some multivalent ligands only bind to the target without eliciting biological consequences, presumably due to that the binding site is not involved in the biological functions of the protein. Key findings from the selections have been published (Front. Pharmacol. 2025, 16, 1608156; J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2024, 146, 35, 24638–24653; Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2025, 64, 10, e202421172; Nat. Chem. 2024; 4, 21, 543-555). Additional manuscripts are still in preparation or under review. Objective 6, to summarize the results and identify future research opportunities for more in-depth studies, especially the ligands with potential for drug development. The research findings have been summarized in this report. We have selected a number of compounds for more in-depth in vivo studies (e.g., anti-cancer; Front. Pharmacol. 2025, 16, 1608156) and anti-viral drug development. We have submitted 6 patent applications to protect the potential drug candidates arising from this project (three applications are already published and three applications are under internal review before formal submission). 17300321.label: Major findings and research outcome
17300321.value: We developed a novel DNA-encoded multivalent library method, which enables the simultaneous selection of billions of multivalent ligands against protein complexes. Following the referees' suggestions, our work focused on bivalent and trivalent libraries while also exploring tetravalent systems. We demonstrated that DNA duplexes and multi-way DNA junctions function as robust and programmable scaffolds. These scaffolds display multiple ligands to interrogate protein complexes and, crucially, they encode not only the ligands' chemical structures but also their spatial arrangement. This provides a direct, rapid, and unambiguous approach for identifying true multivalent binders. The core methodology has been published (Nat. Chem. 2024, 4, 543-555; J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2024, 146, 35, 24638–24653), and another manuscript focusing on high-valency DELs is under preparation. We have built a series of multivalent libraries at billion-compound scale and applied these libraries in selections against a wide array of protein complexes. Targets were screened both in purified form and on live cells. The selections have identified potent and specific ligands, and we have characterized their biological activities and investigated their potential as drug candidates. Some of the findings have been included in methodology papers (Nat. Chem. 2024, 4, 543-555; J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2024, 146, 35, 24638-24653; Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2025, 64, e202421172). We have identified trivalent inhibitors against the influenza hemagglutinin trimer, which exhibited good efficacy in vivo against live viruses (manuscript in preparation). We have collaborated with clinicians and tested the inhibitors in ovarian granulosa cell tumors (Front. Pharmacol. 2025, 16, 1608156). We have filed 6 patent applications; 3 are published pending approval, and 3 are under review by our technology transfer office. We are pursuing partnerships with pharmaceutical and biotech companies to translate these findings into downstream drug development programs. Furthermore, the complexity of analyzing selection outputs required novel computational solutions. We therefore developed advanced statistical and AI-based data analysis methods specifically designed to deconvolute the selection data. These tools are particularly effective at identifying true multivalent binders amidst the background noise of monovalent and lower-valency binders and non-specific interactions. We have demonstrated that these analytical methods are compatible with data from cell-based selections, greatly enhancing their utility. These bioinformatics advances have been reported in a publication (ACS Omega 2023, 8, 19057-19071) and a manuscript currently under review (Bioinformatics).

17300321.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17300321.value: We will perform medicinal chemistry optimization on inhibitors showing strong therapeutic potential. For instance, we are collaborating with clinicians to test inhibitors in patient-derived ovarian granulosa cell tumor samples and with microbiologists to evaluate the anti-viral efficacy of trivalent hemagglutinin H3 inhibitors. Further downstream drug development will require collaboration and funding from external agencies and/or companies. We plan to apply for ITF seed funding to advance development for the most promising inhibitors. Methodologically, we envision extending this approach to other complex targets, such as ribonucleoproteins and misfolded protein fibrils and plaques, enabling DEL selections in more biologically relevant contexts. The libraries built in this project remain sufficient for hundreds of additional selections. Collectively, we expect the findings and chemical matter from this project to generate significant new research and development opportunities in drug discovery.

17300321.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17300321.value: Multivalency refers to the simultaneous binding of multiple ligands to multiple sites on a target, a strategy widely used in nature to create strong and specific molecular interactions that define biological structures and functions. Consequently, developing compounds that modulate these interactions holds great promise for biological research and drug discovery. DNA-encoded chemical library (DEL) technology is a powerful high-throughput method for finding drug leads. In this project, we created a novel type of DEL specifically designed to target complex biological structures like protein assemblies. Using multi-branched DNA nanostructures as scaffolds, we built libraries containing billions of potential drug combinations with two, three, or four binding elements. We then used these libraries to screen against various important protein complexes. This effort discovered new multivalent drug candidates, which were investigated for their biological activity and potential to treat human diseases like cancer and influenza. The outcome of this project provides a new tool to tackle complex drug targets that have been difficult to address with traditional methods.

17300521.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17300521.value: Over the past decade, the low-energy electronic band structure of graphene has drawn intense interest, not only because it has a linear energy-momentum dispersion, but also because it can be redesigned with a high degree of freedom. In particular, by exploiting van der Waals (vdW) interactions with other 2D materials, a variety of new band structures have been created, including the spin-orbit bands in graphene on transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs), minibands in graphene-hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) moiré superlattices, and flat bands in magic-angle-twisted graphene bilayers. All of these are new and highly tunable, allowing us to explore various new physics in the system. The field has been advancing at an impressive pace, but to continue its unprecedented progresses, it is now important to gain better understandings on the low-energy electronic dynamics and band structures of the system. For instance, existing studies on graphene-TMDC heterostructures have shown contradicting experimental evidence supporting a different type of spin-orbit coupling, either spin-valley Zeeman or Rashba, being dominant in the system. Since it determines electronic properties of the system, it is essential to clarify such discrepancies before moving forward. Moreover, nearly all experimental studies in graphene superlattices have so far focused on tracking the positions of the satellite Dirac peaks to estimate the shape of the moiré minibands while possible changes in electron scattering processes due to the appearance of the minibands is barely investigated. Here, we propose to tackle these issues by performing transverse magnetic focusing (TMF) experiments as it cannot only probe the Fermi surface profile, but it can also examine electron dynamics, such as estimating electron-electron scattering rate. This is possible because TMF originates from a cyclotron motion of an electron—i.e., the electron dynamics that is sensitive to the scattering events—under a perpendicular magnetic field that can “focus” electrons on a nearby “collector” at values determined by the electron momentum at a given energy. Thus, TMF can also probe the energy-momentum dispersion in the system. These unique features allow us to gain useful insights for microscopic structures of the spin-orbit bands in graphene-TMDC and minibands in graphene superlattices as well as their electron dynamics. Moreover, it can easily be employed in various device structures to investigate how diverse external control parameters, such as perpendicular electric field, in-plane magnetic field, twist angle, etc, change the band structures. 17300521.label: Realisation of objectives
17300521.value: All three objectives have been successfully achieved, resulting in six published papers and at least one manuscript currently in preparation. The Principal Investigator (PI) delivered ten invited and oral presentations at international conferences related to the project, and two PhD students in the group completed their degrees. Below, we summarize the accomplishments, challenges encountered, and strategies employed to overcome them. Objective 1: Studying Electron Dynamics and Spin-Orbit Bands in Graphene-TMDC Heterostructures To investigate electron dynamics and the Fermi surface profile of spin-orbit bands in graphene–transition metal dichalcogenide (TMDC) heterostructures, we fabricated high-quality graphene-WSe₂ devices with carrier mobility reaching up to 400,000 cm²V⁻¹s⁻¹. We studied ballistic transverse magnetic focusing (TMF) under low perpendicular magnetic fields (~300 mT) and observed a splitting in the first focusing peak, while the second peak remained intact. In collaboration with a theoretical group, we demonstrated that this behavior corresponds to band splitting in graphene induced by strong spin-orbit coupling (SOC) from the WSe₂, with a magnitude of 12~15 meV, and the dominating Rashba SOC term over the spin-valley Zeeman term. Temperature-dependent studies further indicated that electron-electron interactions are the primary scattering mechanism, with screening effects attributed to the high dielectric constant of WSe₂. Interestingly, Shubnikov–de Haas (SdH) oscillations in the same sample revealed SOC-induced band splitting of only ~5 meV. This discrepancy suggests that different measurement techniques—TMF at low fields (<300 mT) and SdH oscillations at higher fields (>3 T)—probe distinct aspects of SOC effect on charge transport in graphene. This insight underscores the importance of measurement methodology when estimating SOC strength experimentally and may explain the wide variation in reported values. These findings were published in Nature Communications 14, 6124 (2023). To further explore this discrepancy, we investigated Landau level (LL) crossings at high magnetic fields, where Zeeman energy splits LLs with different spins. Since SOC generates spin-polarized LLs at zero field, it modifies the LL crossing behavior depending on its strength. Comparing experimental data with a simplified theoretical model, we confirmed that Rashba-type SOC is stronger than spin-valley SOC, with total SOC strength in the meV range. This is in good agreement with our TMF study. This work was published in Physica Status Solidi B 261, 2300397 (2024). To investigate the LL crossing behavior more thoroughly, we are currently fabricating graphene-WSe₂ devices in Corbino geometry, which eliminates edge effects and enables bulk magneto-transport studies in the quantum Hall regime (ongoing). Objective 2: Developing Techniques to Study Ballistic TMF in Configurable Graphene Superlattices To investigate ballistic TMF in configurable graphene superlattices, we developed a microneedle probe method for van der Waals (vdW) stacking. This versatile tool functions as a high-precision cutter, wire bonder, and rotational manipulator for 2D materials. Using this method, we successfully rotated hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) flakes atop graphene layers to tune the moiré superlattice potential. Previously, such manipulation was only possible using atomic force microscopy (AFM), which requires advanced instrumentation. In contrast, our microneedle technique is simple and compatible with standard vdW assembly setups. This technique was featured as an Editor’s Pick in AIP Advances 14, 015333 (2024). Using this method, we fabricated various graphene superlattice structures, including configurable graphene-hBN heterostructures, graphene-hBN-graphene stacks to study Coulomb drag between moiré and graphene bands [Physical Review Letters 133, 186301 (2024)], small-angle twisted double bilayer graphene (in preparation), and precisely aligned WSe₂-graphene-graphene-WSe₂ moiré heterostructures (ongoing). In configurable graphene-hBN heterostructures, we observed that TMF signals from the moiré minibands and the density range at which the signals are suppressed vary with moiré lattice configuration, consistent with theoretical expectations. Similar effects were found in WSe₂-graphene-graphene-WSe₂ moiré systems. These studies are currently being finalized for publication. Objective 3: Exploring Spin-Valleytronic Devices Based on Graphene vdW Heterostructures We explored the potential of graphene vdW heterostructures for spin-valleytronic devices. A key challenge in spintronic applications is optimizing contact resistance between graphene and ferromagnetic metal electrodes to achieve sufficiently large spin injection and detection efficiencies. To address this, we proposed using hBN layers as tunable tunnel barriers as their atomic-layer thickness and high band gap allow precise control of the contact resistance. To implement this, we developed an optical characterization method to determine hBN thickness with atomic precision. By statistically analyzing exfoliated hBN flakes on 90-nm SiO₂/Si substrates, we found that red-filtered optical images provide the highest contrast, and second harmonic generation measurements confirm the exact layer count. This work was published in Nano Letters 24, 14774 (2024). We then fabricated graphene-WSe₂ heterostructures with ferromagnetic metal/hBN contacts to probe spin-dependent TMF signals. However, fine-tuning the spin orientation necessary to fully understand spin-dependent TMF required a system capable of varying magnetic field direction. We are currently collaborating with another experimental group equipped for such measurements. In parallel, we constructed graphene-2D magnet heterostructures to study magnetic exchange interactions via TMF. Initially, the 2D magnets heavily doped graphene and reduced carrier mobility. To overcome this, we designed a junction where only part of the graphene contacts the 2D magnet, allowing charge carriers to traverse graphene-2D magnet regime only in a short distance during TMF process. This enabled detection of finite TMF signals across the junction, and we are currently analyzing the data for probing and understanding exchange interaction effects on graphene band. Summary We successfully detected ballistic TMF signals in various vdW heterostructures, including graphene-WSe₂, configurable graphene-hBN, WSe₂-graphene-graphene-WSe₂, and graphene-2D magnet systems. In graphene-WSe₂ devices, the first TMF peak exhibited splitting due to strong spin-orbit coupling (SOC), while the second peak remained intact, indicating the dominance of Rashba-type SOC [Nature Communications 14, 6124 (2023); Physica Status Solidi B 261, 2300397 (2024)]. In configurable graphene-hBN and WSe₂-graphene-graphene-WSe₂ moiré heterostructures, TMF signals were observed in mini-band regimes, with signal suppression varying according to the moiré lattice configuration. In graphene-2D magnet junctions, we detected finite TMF signals and are currently analyzing the effects of magnetic exchange interactions. To explore potential spin-valleytronic applications, we first developed a method for identifying hBN thickness with atomic precision [Nano Letters 24, 14774 (2024)] as it can be used to optimize contact resistance between metallic ferromagnets and graphene to enhance spin injection/detection efficiencies. Furthermore, our microneedle probe technique [AIP Advances 14, 015333 (2024)] facilitated the construction of novel heterostructures, including graphene-hBN-graphene moiré systems for Coulomb drag studies [Physical Review Letters 133, 186301 (2024)].
