17300521.label: Major findings and research outcome
17300521.value: During the project, we published six peer-reviewed papers in leading international journals such as Nature Communications, PRL, and Nano Letters. Additionally, the PI delivered ten invited and oral presentations at major international conferences, including Graphene2024 and IUMRS-ICEM 2024. At least one additional manuscript is currently in preparation. Below, we summarize the major findings. First, we successfully fabricated high-quality graphene-WSe₂ heterostructures and observed clear TMF signals. Notably, the first TMF peak exhibited splitting, while the second remained intact. This indicates band splitting in graphene due to strong spin-orbit coupling (SOC) (~15 meV) with the Rashba term dominating over the spin-valley term (Nature Communications, 2023; Part C, No. 6). Further studies on SdH oscillation and Landau level crossings revealed different SOC strengths within the same system (Nature Communications, 2023; PSSB, 2024; Part C, Nos. 6 and 1). These results suggest that different measurement techniques probe distinct aspects of SOC and may explain large variation of SOC values in different experiments. To study this more, we are fabricating Corbino devices. Second, we extended our investigation to other graphene vdW heterostructures. In configurable graphene-hBN superlattices, where the top hBN flake was rotated using a microneedle probe (AIP Advances, 2024; Part C, No. 2), and in precisely aligned WSe₂-graphene-graphene-WSe₂ moiré structures, we observed TMF signals originating from moiré minibands. We also fabricated graphene-2D magnet heterostructures to explore magnetic exchange interaction effects via TMF. Although the 2D magnets degrad carrier mobility of graphene, we designed a junction between pristine graphene and graphene-on-magnet, enabling detection of finite TMF signals. Data analysis is ongoing. Third, we explored the use of graphene vdW heterostructures and TMF for spin-valleytronic devices. To optimize spin injection and detection, we developed a method to identify hBN thickness with atomic precision (Nano Letters, 2024; Part C, No. 4), enabling precise control of contact resistance between ferromagnetic metals and graphene. We fabricated devices and are collaborating with a group equipped to apply magnetic fields in multiple directions for advanced TMF measurements. Finally, the techniques developed during this project have opened new research directions. The microneedle probe method (AIP Advances, 2024; Part C, No. 2) enabled fabrication of graphene-hBN-graphene moiré heterostructures for Coulomb drag studies, demonstrating coupling between moiré and non-moiré bands (PRL, 2024; Part C, No. 5). Additionally, our fabrication and measurement techniques supported the development of a 3D-printed thermocouple array (Advanced Materials, 2023; Part C, No. 3).

17300521.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17300521.value: This project demonstrated that ballistic TMF is a powerful tool for probing electron dynamics and band structures in graphene vdW heterostructures. This technique can be applied to various systems, such as graphene-2D magnet heterostructures, where magnetic exchange interactions can alter graphene’s band structure, and graphene-based moiré systems, where moiré minibands exhibit novel quantum phenomena. Moreover, we devised a new method to investigate ballistic TMF in systems with low charge mobility by creating junctions with pristine graphene. This approach allows charge carriers to traverse shorter distances in low-quality regions during TMF, enabling TMF studies in a broader range of materials. Our findings also show that graphene-WSe₂ heterostructures are promising platforms for ballistic spin-valleytronics. For this, we believe that spin-dependent TMF can be used to detect and manipulate spin signals more precisely. In addition, by integrating 2D magnets, we can engineer graphene bands with specific spin alignments, paving the way for novel spin-valleytronic device applications. Our group is currently working on these directions to exploit high experimental flexibilties of 2D materials for developing new spin-valleytronic device applications.

17300521.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17300521.value: We explored how electrons move in ultra-thin materials made by stacking graphene with WSe₂. By fabricating high-quality devices, we observed unique quantum behaviors—ballistic transverse magnetic focusing (TMF)—which reveal how electrons respond to magnetic fields and spin-orbit coupling. Our study showed that WSe₂ induces strong spin-orbit coupling in graphene, splitting its energy bands by up to 15 meV. We also developed a microneedle probe technique to build and manipulate van der Waals heterostructures with high precision. This allowed us to rotate hBN layers atop graphene to create moiré patterns and study how TMF signals vary with the moiré lattice configuration. Additionally, we investigated graphene combined with magnetic materials to study magnetic exchange interaction effects—key ingredients for future spintronic devices. Our work resulted in six publications in top journals and ten invited talks at major conferences. The techniques we developed—such as microneedle probe manipulation technique and advanced TMF measurements—open new paths for quantum electronics and spin-valleytronics technologies.

17300621.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17300621.value: It is well established that inland waters are an important component of the global carbon (C) cycle, functioning as significant sources of greenhouse gases (GHGs) for the atmosphere. The total CO2 and CH4 emissions from global inland waters are estimated to be 3.9 PgC yr^–1. This is of the same order of magnitude as the oceanic and land sinks of anthropogenic CO2. Nevertheless, due to the lack of spatial sampling at the global scale and the widespread distribution of diverse inland water bodies, the estimated carbon flux remains largely uncertain, and the inclusion of spatially resolved measurements will likely result in an upward refinement. This is particularly true for the billions of small lentic water bodies worldwide. Previous studies on carbon cycling in inland waters were primarily focused on large to medium-sized water bodies, whereas small lentic water bodies (e.g., small lakes, reservoirs, and ponds) characteristic of high land-water connectivity have been seldom studied. These small water bodies typically exhibit different GHG dynamics to those of larger water bodies. Therefore, we urgently need to investigate the GHG emissions from small lentic waters and examine their responses to environmental factors and human impact. Understanding the underlying mechanisms that govern GHG concentrations and emissions in small lentic waters is critical for refining global and regional carbon budgets. This proposed project aims to conduct a comparative study of carbon cycling and GHG emissions of representative small lentic water bodies under contrasting settings of climate, hydrology, geomorphology, and human disturbance across the subtropical Dongjiang River basin and the arid Loess Plateau. We will quantitatively investigate the spatiotemporal variability of GHGs and major driving factors within these inland water bodies. By means of extensive field sampling and laboratory-based incubation experiments tailored for the selected water bodies, this proposal will also investigate the impact of human activity and climate change. The expected results will deepen our understanding of GHG emissions from small lentic water bodies and shed light on quantification of regional and global GHG emissions from inland waters. This will be one of the first integrated research projects to investigate GHG evasion from small inland waters under contrasting environmental settings. Building on our research experience, we will critically analyze carbon cycling processes and GHG evasion in small lentic water bodies and assess their biogeochemical implications. Particularly, the comparative studies involving contrasting environmental settings will enable us to better comprehend their potential responses to future climate change. 眾所周知，內陸水體是全球碳 (C) 循環的重要組成部分，亦是大氣中溫室氣體 (GHG) 的重要來源。全球內陸水體系統的 CO2 和 CH4 排放總量約為 3.9 PgC yr-1。這一數值與全球海洋生態系統和陸地生態系統吸收的碳匯通量具有相同的數量級。然而，由於缺乏全球尺度的空間採樣以及各種內陸水體在全球尺度上的廣泛分佈，目前針對內陸水體的碳通量估算結果仍存在巨大的誤差。隨著空間尺度上研究的不斷深入細化，將來的內陸水體碳通量將極有可能繼續增加。這對於全球數以十億計的小型靜態水體來說尤其如此。以往針對內陸水體碳循環的研究主要集中在大中型水體，而很少針對具有高陸-水連通性的小型靜態水體（如小型湖泊、小型水庫和池塘）來開展實測研究。這些小型水體通常表現出與大中型水體不同的溫室氣體動力學特徵。因此，我們迫切需要調查小型靜態水體的溫室氣體排放特徵，並研究其對環境因素和人類影響的響應。同時，理解控制小型靜態水體的溫室氣體濃度和排放機制也對於完善全球和區域碳收支預算具有至關重要的意義。 在氣候、水文、地貌和人類干擾等特徵迥異的亞熱帶東江流域和乾旱黃土高原地區，本研究項目擬選取具有代表性的小型靜態水體開展碳循環和溫室氣體排放的對比研究。我們將定量研究這些內陸水體中溫室氣體的時空變化特徵和其主要驅動因素。通過為選定的研究水體量身定制的現場採樣方案和基於實驗室的培養實驗，該研究還將調查人類活動和氣候變化對其碳循環的影響。本研究的預期結果將加深我們對小型靜態水體系統溫室氣體排放的理解，並對準確估算區域和全球內陸水體溫室氣體排放提供理論依據。 這將是針對不同環境背景下小型內陸水體溫室氣體排放研究的的首批綜合研究項目之一。基於我們的研究結果，我們將批判性地分析小型靜態水體中的碳循環過程和溫室氣體排放機制，並評估它們的生物地球化學影響。特別需要指出的是，針對不同環境背景下的碳循環對比研究將使我們更好地理解碳循環及溫室氣體排放對未來氣候變化的潛在響應。

17300621.label: Realisation of objectives
17300621.value: Lentic waters are key components of the global carbon (C) cycle, serving as significant sources of atmospheric greenhouse gases (GHGs), including carbon dioxide (CO2) and methane (CH4). Throughout this project, we conducted seven sampling campaigns, including four campaigns in the subtropical Dongjiang River Basin (DRB), which includes Hong Kong, and three campaigns in the (semi)arid Loess Plateau, which aimed to capture the seasonal variations in climate, hydrology, and human activities. We investigated 26 small lentic water bodies, including 6 lakes/reservoirs and 20 (aquaculture) ponds, to mechanistically understand their aquatic carbon cycling and GHG dynamics. Major research activities during the fieldwork included water/sediment/gas sampling, water quality monitoring, and in-situ measurement of GHG emissions. All datasets (3850 sets) have been achieved in the HKU DataHub. Below, I briefly summarize the state how and to what extent the four objectives have been achieved. For Objective 1: We found that the aquatic carbon cycling in both lakes/reservoirs and ponds exhibited pronounced spatial and temporal (seasonal and diel) variations. In the hard-water Nangou Reservoir (~0.3 km2) on the Loess Plateau, our results reveal extremely high dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC) concentrations (69.4–99.7 mg/L) with significant seasonal variations. The mean DIC concentration was 80.3 mg/L, approximately 10 times that of the corresponding dissolved organic carbon (DOC) concentration. In comparison, the average DOC concentration was 7.4 mg/L (see Ran et al., 2022. Journal of Hydrology, 608, 127652). Both DIC and DOC were characterized by pronounced seasonal variations, which were largely the combined results of shifts in hydrological regimes (e.g., surface runoff in the wet season vs. groundwater discharge in the dry season) and human activities (e.g., agricultural return flow and chemical fertilizer applications). A similar spatiotemporal pattern in dissolved carbon was also observed in the Pokfulam Reservoir, Hong Kong (see Chan et al., 2023. Science of the Total Environment, 856, 159047). In contrast, in two subtropical aquaculture ponds, DOC concentrations were significantly higher. For example, the DOC in a fishpond (in the New Territories, Hong Kong) ranged between 7.37 and 17.60 mg/L, and it ranged between 6.25 and 15.37 mg/L in a shrimp pond (also located in the New Territories, Hong Kong). We further performed a partial least squares path modeling analysis to determine the primary driving factors, and identified management practices (e.g., feeding and artificial aeration) as key drivers of the elevated DOC concentrations. Furthermore, the impact of internal production through phytoplankton growth was also substantial (see Yang et al., 2025. Aquaculture, 743401). For Objectives 2 and 3: Our study indicates that small lentic systems were typically oversaturated with dissolved CO2 and CH4 and acted as net carbon sources for the atmosphere. In the Nangou Reservoir on the Loess Plateau, surface water CO2 partial pressure (pCO2) ranged from 1076 to 4587 μatm, which was 2–11 times higher than the atmospheric pCO2 (i.e., 410 μatm). Although the reservoir is moderately to highly productive throughout the study period, it functioned as a net CO2 source with the CO2 emission rates (FCO2) in the range of 308–1753 mg C/m2/day. This high efflux suggests that productive waters are not necessarily CO2 sinks (see Ran et al., 2022. Journal of Hydrology, 608, 127652). Also, we observed significant seasonal and diel variations. High effluxes were observed during the ice-thaw period, which indicates the release of CO2 that was accumulated over winter. CO2 effluxes were typically higher during the nighttime driven by stronger aquatic metabolism, although episodic weather events (e.g., rainfall and strong winds) could enhance CO2 emissions and even reverse the diel pattern. Our study also shows that using daytime measurements alone would underestimate daily CO2 emissions by 9–25% (see Ran et al., 2022. Journal of Hydrology, 608, 127652; Ran et al., 2023. Earth’s Future, 11, e2023EF003602). Similarly, in a small subtropical reservoir within the DRB, our results reveal that a variety of metabolic, hydrological, and hydro-chemical processes played a critical role in regulating its carbon emission dynamics. The reservoir was an overall source of CO2 with an average ﬂux of 24.6 mmol/m2/day, but it occasionally functioned as a sink when primary productivity was high. This was attributable to the prolonged history of the reservoir and occasional undersaturation of CO2 in the water column. We also discovered pronounced differences in the underlying controls of CO2 dynamics between the reservoir and its upstream and downstream rivers, which highlights the importance of accounting for the distinct characteristics of lentic and lotic waters when evaluating catchment-scale CO2 budgets. For the two aquaculture ponds in Hong Kong, our study indicates that the fishpond exhibited high primary productivity and functioned as a net CO2 sink (-42.33±18.91 mmol/m2/day). However, the absence of draining-drying in the fishpond led to stronger CH4 emissions (29.41±27.53 mmol/m2/day). Conversely, intensive management practices in the shrimp pond, including draining, drying, and refilling, have disrupted its primary productivity and shifted it to a CO2 source (62.89±106.61 mmol/m2/day) while substantially reducing its CH4 emissions (see Yang et al., 2025. Aquaculture, 743401). Part of these results have contributed to broader syntheses on carbon biogeochemistry and GHG emissions (see Battin et al., 2023. Nature, 613, 449-459; Lauerwald et al., 2023.Global Biogeochemical Cycles, 37, e2022GB007657). For Objective 4: Ponds are typically isolated without strong connection to surrounding environments. Consequently, their biogeochemical carbon cycling tends to be controlled by human activities (e.g., land use, wastewater discharge, feed supply, dredging, etc.). By investigating 20 (sub)tropical aquaculture ponds with diverse culture systems, we assessed their future GHG emissions in response to climate change. Our findings show that rising temperature could substantially stimulate CH4 emissions, particularly via ebullition, with an 11% increase in CH4 emission rate (FCH4) per 1 °C rise in water temperature. This thermal sensitivity of FCH4 was further amplified in ponds with higher organic substrates, revealing a synergistic effect between temperature and substrate availability in promoting CH4 production (see Yang et al., 2025. Water Research, under review). Different from ponds, most carbon in lakes and reservoirs is ultimately derived from terrestrial ecosystems. We further examined human and hydroclimatic controls on CO2 and CH4 dynamics in the upstream and downstream rivers of reservoirs. We found that land use and aquatic metabolism played significant roles in regulating the spatiotemporal patterns of both gases. Dissolved oxygen, stable carbon isotope of DIC, proportion of impervious surface, and catchment slope were identified as the major predictors for pCO2. For the partial pressure of CH4 (pCH4), the major predictors were chlorophyll a and water temperature, which influence organic matter availability and methanogenesis (see Ran et al., 2022. JGR: Biogeosciences, 127, e2021JG006765; Chen et al., 2025. Water Resources Research, 61, e2024WR038341). Part of these results have contributed to a review on carbon emissions from Chinese inland waters (see Yang et al., 2024. JGR: Biogeosciences, 129, e2023JG007675). Overall, all the four research objectives have been successfully achieved. Our results have critically examined the aquatic carbon cycling and GHG emission dynamics in small lentic water systems across diverse environmental settings. These findings have not only filled the knowledge gaps regarding biogeochemical carbon cycling in currently under-represented small lentic water bodies, but also provided insights into future research on the carbon cycle in other inland water systems with similar environmental characteristics and anthropogenic pressures.

17300621.label: Major findings and research outcome
17300621.value: Our research on small lentic water bodies in the subtropical DRB and the semiarid Loess Plateau indicates that aquatic carbon cycling and GHG emissions exhibited pronounced spatiotemporal variations. For the subtropical aquaculture ponds, dissolved carbon was equally composed of DOC and DIC, with the DOC concentrations in fishpond and shrimp pond in the range of 6.25–17.60 mg/L. In comparison, the DIC concentration in the two ponds was 12.18 and 13.84 mg/L, respectively. In contrast, DIC was the dominant carbon species in the Nangou Reservoir on the Loess Plateau fed by carbonate-rich groundwater, with a mean concentration of 80.3 mg/L, which is ~10 times that of the corresponding DOC concentrations (average: 7.4 mg/L). This spatial discrepancy reflects the combined effects of hydrology, lithology, and human activities. Particularly, intensive management practices, such as high inputs of feeds and regular draining-drying-refilling in aquaculture ponds, have profoundly modified their biogeochemical carbon cycling. Most of the surveyed lentic systems are net carbon sources, despite pronounced seasonal variability. Our study shows that semiarid reservoirs can be important for regional carbon budgets due to strong CO2 emissions. Groundwater-derived DIC plays a central role in sustaining surface water pCO2 and modulating its seasonal variability. Also, metabolism of aquatic ecosystems regulates the diel pCO2 changes, producing a 6–13% difference over a 24-h time span. Although the Nangou Reservoir is moderately to highly productive, its strong CO2 emissions support previous findings that productive waters are not necessarily CO2 sinks. For the ponds within the DRB, our research provides insights into the impact of different management practices on CO2 and CH4 emissions. In the fishpond with low human disturbance, temperature was the primary factor in regulating its carbon emissions, either directly by controlling CH4 production or indirectly by affecting CO2 production through primary production. In comparison, in the shrimp pond that has undergone regular draining-drying-refilling, changes in water depth and nutrient levels were the primary factors in governing its C emissions. Theses results provide a mechanistic understanding of how different management practices mediate their aquatic carbon cycling and GHG emission dynamics. Based on this work, fifteen peer-reviewed research articles have been published in leading journals, and another manuscript is currently under review. I have also presented these results at three international conferences. The project has partially supported three postgraduate students. Of them, two PhD students have successfully graduated, and the third one has passed her probationary review.

17300621.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17300621.value: Our research on small lentic water bodies across contrasting environmental settings underscores their disproportionate contribution to inland water carbon emissions. A mechanistic understanding of their GHG dynamics is of paramount importance to assess their biogeochemical implications for global GHG budget and inform climate change mitigation. I plan to submit a GRF proposal entitled ‘Greenhouse gas emissions from global aquaculture ponds in a warming world’ in 2026. This research project will disentangle the combined impacts of natural drivers and human activities on aquatic carbon cycling and GHG (CO2, CH4, and N2O) emission dynamics in aquaculture ponds across diverse environmental settings. Furthermore, I aim to critically examine GHG production pathways and emission processes in global aquaculture ponds using machine learning and metagenomic sequencing techniques. I will also assess their biogeochemical implications for carbon neutrality goals and climate change mitigation. Within the DRB, reservoirs and ponds play a critical role for agriculture by supplying irrigation flows. Building on the research results arising from this project, I have submitted a GRF proposal on GHG emission dynamics in (sub)tropical agricultural ditches this year, which will systematically analyze biogeochemical cycling of carbon and nitrogen and evaluate their significance and role in landscape-scale GHG budgets.

17300621.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17300621.value: Growing evidence suggests that small lentic water bodies play a pivotal role in the global carbon cycle. They receive high inputs of external organic matter (OM) relative to the water volume. Microbial respiration of terrestrial OM elevates CO2 concentrations, whereas sediment respiration under anoxic conditions fuels CH4 production, resulting in high CH4 evasion. Consequently, these lentic systems are hotspots of GHG production and emissions, and constraining their carbon cycling is critical for accurate inland water GHG budgets. Based on intensive sampling in the subtropical Dongjiang River Basin and the semiarid Loess Plateau, our research reveals that aquatic carbon cycling and water-air carbon emissions exhibited pronounced spatiotemporal variability, which were collectively regulated by hydrology, climate, and human activities. Notably, relying on daytime measurements alone would underestimate daily CO2 fluxes by 9–25% due to significantly stronger emissions at night. In aquaculture ponds, intensive management can remarkably enhance CO2 production while suppressing CH₄ emissions. This study underscores the substantial impact of human disturbances, especially draining-drying-refilling practices, on carbon cycle in aquaculture ponds. Our findings reinforce the urgency to mechanistically understand the aquatic carbon cycling and GHG dynamics in small lentic systems and unravel their driving factors in a changing world.

17300721.value: 晝夜節律可被視為一個內部時鐘，它根據一個受光或溫度等環境刺激控制的二十四小時睡眠週期來調節其生理和行為。這種生理時鐘可以在脊椎動物中觀察到，也存在於植物和其他生物中，強調了它在晝夜調整中的核心重要性。然而，我們對野生物種生理時鐘的分子規律這方面認知甚少。擾亂晝夜節律會對健康產生嚴重影響，包括引致癌症或神經系統損壞等疾病，還可能對整個生態系統產生影響。同樣情況發生於人類旅行時，當我們的正常環境線索（例如光線）產生了變化，從而影響睡眠和新陳代謝，這就是所謂的時差。因此，對於野生生物，環境的變化也可能導致這關鍵的內部時鐘產生變化。鑑於世界正在經歷快速的環境變化，生物的生理時鐘，以及其生理和行為很可能會受到影響。當海洋生物曝露於更高的二氧化碳濃度時，正如氣候變化引起的海洋酸化所預測那樣，它們的自然行為和生理機能會被改變。有人發現珊瑚魚的這些變化跟調節其生理時鐘的主要基因表達變化有關。此發現表明了環境酸鹼值與晝夜節律之間存在聯繫。為了進一步了解，我們進行了一項水族館實驗，研究了 24 小時裡魚類的晝夜節律，這將能提供有關野生魚類生理時鐘的基線資料。為了直接測試酸鹼值對其生理時鐘的影響，我們將魚曝露於幾種不同的二氧化碳濃度中。此外，一部分魚類會被保存在黑暗中以避免其晝夜節律受光的控制，從而了解二氧化碳在生理時鐘同步中扮演的角色。 由於在分子層面中調節生理時鐘是複雜的，我們提議透過把魚曝露於不同的二氧化碳環境，從而研究多個層面的調節，這包括轉錄（基因表達），轉錄後修飾（選擇性剪接）和轉譯（蛋白質表達）。因此，這擬議的項目將結合受控的水族館實驗、高通量分子分析和計算分析，以探討珊瑚魚晝夜節律的複雜性以及更酸化水域對其內部生理鐘的影響。此項目不但能為我們提供有關野生脊椎動物晝夜節律在分子調節的寶貴資訊，更容許我們進一步評估環境中酸鹼值變化對這個調節行為、生理和健康的重要機制之潛在影響。

17300721.label: Realisation of objectives
17300721.value: All objectives were achieved. 1. Identify molecular rhythmic patterns in a coral reef fish across a zeitgeber time-course. This is the first study to ever look at gene expression across a timeline in a coral reef fish. We have fully achieved this objective as we exposed fish to different CO2 treatments and collected samples across a 24h (zeitgeber) timeline in the state-of-the -art sea simulator in Australia. • CONTROL condition: Representing the current day 400 µatm pCO2 found at the location of fish collection. • Stable 1000 µatm pCO2 treatment (FLAT): Representing the open-ocean, end-of-the-century projection typically used in ocean acidification experiments (Kroeker et al. 2013). • Cycling pCO2 treatment with an average of 1000 µatm pCO2 (FLUCT):The cycling pCO2 treatment matches the levels that have been observed in some tidal lagoons (Shaw et al. 2012). Although this level of FLUCTuation may seem extreme today, it may be more common in the future as a 3-fold amplification in diel pCO2 FLUCTuations is predicted by 2100 (Shaw et al. 2013). The low pCO2 peak is at 2 pm, and the high pCO2 peak at 2 am. • Cycling pCO2 with an average of 1000 µatm pCO2 and DARK treatment (DARK): Circadian cycles are also driven by light patterns. To be able to evaluate whether changes in gene expression patterns are triggered by an increase in CO2 levels or just by light intensity we included a DARK treatment in which the fish were kept at high pCO2 levels but in a DARK place to evaluate if rhythmic and regular FLUCTuations in pH can entrain the clock rather than the light/DARK cycle. • Reverse-cycling pCO2 treatment with an average of 1000 µatm pCO2 (OFF):In this treatment, pCO2 will be cycled throughout the day, but in reverse to treatment 3, with the lowest point at 2 am, and highest at 2 pm. This treatment tests the interaction between light and pH in the entrainment of the clock further. Light cycles are kept natural and pH FLUCTuates in reverse than on coral reefs naturally allowing to test the magnitude of effect of pH versus light. o The samples were collected every four hours at 2 am, 6 am, 10 am, 2 pm, 6 pm and 10 pm, across a 48-hour period. A large set of genes (2,692 genes) show rhythmic expression patterns in the brain of the coral reef fish Acanthochromis polyacanthus confirming the involvement of general vertebrate circadian genes in a wild coral reef fish. The functions associated with the rhythmic genes are related to circadian regulation, response to stimulus, but also GTPase regulator activity and oxidoreductase activity. We found that the changing-expression genes through the timeline in control (i.e. ambient CO2) are enriched in 785 Biological Process-related GO Terms. From these, 160 GO Terms are also enriched in changing-expression genes in one, some or all treatments. We even identified the core curdaian rhythm genes: Among the genes changing expression across timeline in CONTROL we found 24 out of 42 genes annotated with GO-terms containing the keyword circadian. As circadian genes have been duplicated across teleost fish evolutionary history, some of them could have lost their original function. Thus, we considered that the 24 genes changing expression across day-time in CONTROL are true circadian genes in A. polyacanthus. 2. Evaluate the influence of environmental pH as an entrainment factor for rhythmic processes in a coral reef fish. This objectives has also been achieved as we now know what processes are affected across a timeline with the different pH treatments. 24.2% (653 genes) of these naturally rhythmic genes lost rhythmicity if the fish were exposed to any of the low pH treatments. The functions of these genes altered by pH across the timeline are involved in response to stimulus, DNA photolyse and GTPase regulator activity among others. A further 1203 genes were significantly different across the zeitgeber timeline between the control samples and fish in low pH treatments, which did not reveal a rhythmic pattern in control. Notable functions of these genes are nervous system process and visual perception with synaptic plasticity, cell death and DNA repair being altered functions across three of the four pH treatments. For the four different pH treatments, 32 genes involved in (neural) development (dnm1a, cdh4, cdx4, zfhx3, cdkl5, pdgfra), immune response (c8b, spire1a), apoptosis (p2rx1, c1ptm1c, pkn1b) and synaptic plasticity (tbata, adgrb3 and kidins220a) were different in all pH treatments across the zeitgeber timeline compared to CONTROL. This shows a small core change across the timeline as the different pH regimes have a low pH at different times across the zeitgeber timeline. For the three fluctuating treatments (FLUCT, DARK and OFF) 60 genes were commonly altered across the timeline highlighting at least 22 genes involved in sensory perception such as rapgef2, rtp3, rho, wdr11, sox1a, snap25a and also including a circadian core gene cry1a and a circadian regulation gene ppp1caa. The biological processes affected by CO2 treatments include metabolic process, regulation of biological process, response to stimulus, and more specifically, response to light stimulus, indicating that as in the previous analysis the light-dependent biological processes could be affected by high CO2 levels. 3. Link the different molecular regulatory levels in the brain across a 24-hour timeline and explore the downstream processes driven by rhythmic regulation after different pH treatments. We were able to study the alternative splicing mechanisms as well as look at brain chemistry in addition to the gene expression patterns and connect them. Hence, this objective was achieved. While extremely tricky to measure brain pH and plasma in such a small fish, we managed to receive data on a subset of samples. This may not be the most powerful analysis, just due to the complication of the method on such small fish, however we saw a trend in the pHi levels in the brain between the low and high peak for the fluctuating treatment. In addition we were able study the alternative splicing related to the circadian rhythm as well as the pH treatments and found that: The temporal splicing pattern observed across a 24-hour period in fish from the control group was largely absent in those exposed to either stable or fluctuating elevated CO2 conditions. Splicing patterns were influenced not only by an overall increase in CO2 concentration but also by its stability, with 6am and 6pm emerging as key timepoints when the majority of aberrant splicing events were identified. We found that fish in fluctuating CO2 conditions exhibited increased temporal plasticity in splicing events compared to fish in stable CO2 conditions. This was especially notable for genes associated with neural functioning. Our findings suggest that natural temporal splicing patterns in fish brains are disrupted by elevated CO2 exposure, with CO2 stability also influencing molecular responses. The increased plasticity in temporal splicing activity observed in fish in fluctuating CO2 environments may provide greater flexibility in biological responses to external pH changes, potentially enabling them to better cope with future ocean acidification conditions.

17300721.label: Major findings and research outcome
17300721.value: • We study the effect of fluctuations in high CO2 levels on the patterns and levels of gene expression across a timeline in brains of a coral reef fish, Acanthochromis polyacanthus. • We found an effect of high levels of CO2 on the patterns of expression of genes related to vision independently of the actual fluctuating regime of the CO2 treatment. • The number of genes changing their expression levels at the time of changing from dark to light was drastically reduced (50% or more) in all CO2 treatments. • Independently of the treatment, few or no changes in gene expression were detected at night. • Overall, the results indicate that increasing fluctuating CO2 levels in the environment affect biological processes dependent on light. • The temporal splicing pattern observed across a 24-hour period in fish from the control group was largely absent in those exposed to either stable or fluctuating elevated CO2 conditions. • Splicing patterns were influenced not only by an overall increase in CO2 concentration but also by its stability, with 6am and 6pm emerging as key timepoints when the majority of aberrant splicing events were identified • The increased plasticity in temporal splicing activity observed in fish in fluctuating CO2 environments may provide greater flexibility in biological responses to external pH changes, potentially enabling them to better cope with future ocean acidification conditions. • Our findings suggest that natural temporal splicing patterns in fish brains are disrupted by elevated CO2 exposure, with CO2 stability also influencing molecular responses.

17300721.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17300721.value: As we found a clear connection of pH effects on the visual perception in the brain, the next step would be to evaluate the actual visual system. Hence, studying ocean acidification in the eye and the visual center of the brain would be key to identify the exact effects of the lowering of pH> This would then also help understand why some (visual) behaviours are more affected than others by ocean acidification.

17300721.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17300721.value: The uptake of anthropogenic atmospheric CO2 by oceans lowering pH levels, called ocean acidification, affects the physiology and behaviour of marine species. A mechanistic understanding of how environmental pH changes, in particular those predicted to occur by the end of this century due to climate change, are regulated in the brain of marine fish is key to understanding the behavioural impairments and their adaptive potential to climate change. We simulated different pH regimes, including pH fluctuations and entrained the coral reef fish Acanthochromic polyacanthus to these conditions for 14 days and collected 150 fish across a circadian timeline. More acidified waters (regardless of the pH regime) change the fish brain transcriptional program affecting processes involved in visual perception. Low pH therefore affects light-dependent biological processes with a link to specific times of the day in particular at dawn where transcriptional changes observed in control are hindered in low pH regimes. In the light of future climate change, changes in pH will interfere with light-dependent biological processes and circadian regulation of behaviour.

17300821.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17300821.value: Our warming planet is approaching to an unprecedented level in temperature, especially if we do not reduce our carbon dioxide emissions. Recent studies indicate that, in the tropics, these high temperatures are exceeding thermal optimum ranges of many species and causing a diversity decline. This decline is changing the pattern of global biodiversity, as exemplified by the latitudinal biodiversity gradient (LBG). The LBG is typically a unimodal pattern with a diversity highest near the equator and lowest near the poles. The exceedingly high present-day temperatures are causing LBGs to become bimodal with a substantial diversity dip in the tropics. To better understand how future climate change will affect the biosphere, we need to better understand the role of temperature on diversity in climate states warmer than present day. The geological record provides an opportunity to investigate such climate states. In particular, the greenhouse climate of the Eocene provides an example of the potential impact that extreme global warming may have on biodiversity. We propose to study global biodiversity variation in marine ostracods during the Eocene. Ostracods are the best-preserved arthropods in the fossil record and provide a robust proxy for changes in the marine ecosystem. We will also quantify sea-surface temperature and habitat complexity (coastline length as the proxy), two major controls on diversity, by using climate and tectonic models and available data compilations. The result will help us to answer major questions: Was the Eocene LBG strongly bimodal as projected for our future? Is temperature the main driver of large-scale marine diversity patterns in the past and future? Our preliminary data analyses suggest the answers are yes for both questions. Our formal analyses of new quantitative diversity data will give us robust answers based on large census dataset and sample size, sophisticated statistics and ecological modelling, and proxy-validated climate and geophysical models. The results will help us to better understand future biodiversity patterns under human-induced warming, especially to predict and quantify the magnitude of future tropical diversity loss. 我們變暖的星球正經歷前所未有的高溫水平，尤其是如果我們不減少二氧化碳的排放。最近的研究表明，在熱帶地區，溫度的升高超出許多物種的最佳溫度範圍，導致生物多樣性下降。這種下降正在改變全球生物多樣性的分佈模式，例如緯度生物多樣性梯度 。 緯度生物多樣性梯度通常是單峰模式，即赤道附近生物多樣性最高，兩極附近最低。當今極高的溫度導致緯度生物多樣性梯度變成雙峰模式，在熱帶出現顯著的多樣性下降。為了準確探究未來的氣候變化將如何影響生物圈，我們需要了解歷史上高溫時期的溫度對生物多樣性的作用。地質學記錄是研究高溫時期生物多樣性的途徑之一。特別是始新世的溫室氣候，為現在極端的全球變暖對生物多樣性的潛在影響，提供了絕佳例子。我們建議研究全球始新世海洋介形類的生物多樣性變化。因為介形類有保存最完好的節肢動物化石記錄，為海洋生態系統的變化提供魯棒性指標。此外，通過氣候和地質建模，結合可用的數據整理，我們還將量化分析兩個控制生物多樣性的主要因素——海面溫度和棲息地的複雜性（以海岸線長度作為指標）。 本研究結果將幫助我們回答兩個主要的問題：始新世緯度生物多樣性梯度是否如我們對未來的預測那樣是強雙峰的？ 溫度是過去和未來大規模海洋生物多樣性分佈模式的主要驅動因素嗎？ 我們的初步數據分析表明，這兩個問題的答案都是肯定的。基於大量統計數據集和样本收集，精細的統計數據和生態建模，結合指標驗證的氣候和地球物理模型，我們下一步進行的定量多樣性數據分析將對以上問題給予魯棒性答案。 本項結果將幫助我們深入探究人類引起的全球變暖下，未來的生物多樣性分佈模式，尤其是預測和量化未來熱帶生物多樣性減少的程度。

17300821.value: We obtained bunch of data on Eocene biodiversity and also compiled existing evidence. As the result, we now better understand large-scale biodiversity patterns well. Temperature was an important precondition for high biodiversity. Habitat size/complexity, too. Also we revealed biotic interaction played an important role. Our project substantially contributed for better understanding on Eocene biodiversity in large scales. We published 6 papers on top journals including Nature and did presentations in several international conferences.

17300821.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action

17300821.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17300821.value: We studied Eocene (the time period from 56 to 33.9 million years ago) biodiversity by using fossil records (ancient remains of marine organismal hard parts, shells). We understand overly high temperature could negatively affect marine biodiversity and their large geographical patterns. Other factors such as habitat size (eg size of continental shelf) and biological interactions (relationship among different animals) are also important. Our results contribute a better understanding on biological diversity in a warmer time than the present. This is important to think about our future as Earth is now under rapid warming by human-induced CO2 emission.

17301021.label: Project Objectives

17301021.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17301021.value: The era of big data provides new opportunities for the analysis of time series, most of which in real life are nonstationary. Meanwhile, researchers applying factor analysis to high-dimensional nonstationary time series often face a choice: keep the data in levels or first difference them. Recent work of the PI has shown that factor analysis applied directly to large nonstationary data might be spurious. Even in the absence of any factors, about 60% of variation of such data is “explained” by the first principal component and about 80% by the first three principal components. This raises the question of how to detect such spurious results. The project aims to propose tests that can formally detect such spurious factors through canonical correlation analysis. The first objective of the project is to detect spurious factors when the true factors are nonstationary. Under the null hypothesis of stationary idiosyncratic terms, the principal component estimators are consistent for the true factors. On the other hand, the estimators of the factors in the differenced data are consistent for the true differenced factors. Therefore, under the null hypothesis, the estimated factors from the data in levels and those from the differenced data should be well aligned with each other. A poor alignment would indicate the presence of spurious factors. The proposed test attempts to compare the estimated factors from the data in levels to those from the differenced data through their canonical correlation coefficients. The second objective of the project is to detect spurious factors when both stationary and nonstationary components exist in the true factors. Compared with the condition of nonstationary true factors, it is more practical to assume the existence of both stationary and nonstationary true factors. Under this assumption, the above approach would not work anymore and new ideas would be sought. 随着大数据时代的到来，我们日常生活中大多数的时间序列是高维且非平稳的。对这类数据的因子分析主要采取两种方法：直接分析或者一阶差分。本人最近的工作揭示了直接分析可能导致伪因子的产生，从而提出了一个问题：如何检测这些伪因子？本研究项目旨在通过典则相关系数分析来检测高维非平稳数据中的伪因子。

17301221.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17301221.value: “力敏团” 是一类能够响应机械力作用从而激活特定分子活动的复合物。由于机械力在诸多生命现象中起着重要作用，因此含“力敏团”的力响应智能材料在生物医学领域具有广阔的应用前景。然而，目前报道的 “力敏团”大多数基于化学共价键的断裂、形成或重排，因此不能可逆操作。此外，设计一种新型“力敏团”以触发特殊有趣的分子活动是一项挑战。本项目将为设计新型“力敏团”建立“模块化合成”方法。首先合成一种新型“力响应”分子胶（MR-Glue）作为“通用”力传感模块。这类MR-Glue是一种网络聚合物，由具有多个胍离子（Gu+）的胶链段以及具有α-环糊精（α-CD）环的聚轮烷（PRX）链段组成，且可沿PRX链段滑动。当胶链段通过多价盐桥作用粘附于客体分子上，分子功能会受到抑制。在强外力作用下，α-CD环被迫移动到胶链段并物理终止粘附作用，从而释放客体分子以重新活化。由于α-CD环势能不稳定，无法停留在胶链段上，因此在外力消除后，其会立即自发移回到PRX链段。因此，客体分子的功能可由机械力可逆控制。由于分子胶粘附作用的普遍性，广泛的客体分子可用于构建“力敏团”组装。作为概念研究，本项目将使用MR-Glue制备两种力响应水凝胶：（1）实时荧光响应的力致变色水凝胶和（2）自增强水凝胶。目标（1）将通过简单地加入各种具有不同发射波长的荧光染料作为功能模块来制备不同光学性质的力致变色水凝胶。由于其可逆性，此类水凝胶有望实现实时显示系统机械力。目标（2）将引入一种聚合络氨酸的酶-漆酶。当施加外力时，水凝胶将激活漆酶形成聚络氨酸，使凝胶硬化。因此应力集中区域水凝胶的力学性能将会增强。这种模块化合成方法将极大地扩展“力敏团”的可设计性，并为力响应智能材料开辟新的途径。

17301221.label: Realisation of objectives
17301221.value: [Achieved Objectives] [1] Due to synthetic challenges in the original molecular design, we conducted a redesign of the mechano-responsive molecular glue (MR-Glue). This enabled us to successfully develop the target MR-Glue hydrogel in a more scalable format. [2] We successfully achieved mechanical force-induced switching of enzymatic reactions simply by incorporating target enzymes and their substrates into the MR-Glue hydrogel. By modularly changing the incorporated enzymes and substrates, we were able to construct mechanoresponsive materials that exhibit outputs corresponding to the incorporated enzyme. [3] Instead of using small fluorescent molecules as modules, we successfully achieved visualization of mechanical loading history and real-time (reversible) visualization of load distribution through chemiluminescence by using enzymes that catalyze color reactions and chemiluminescent reactions as respective modules. [4] For easier handling, we switched from the laccase/tyrosine combination to the thrombin/fibrinogen as the module. As intended, we successfully induced fibrinogen hydrolysis and subsequent spontaneous polymerization into fibrin fibers under stress application, achieving self-growth that enhanced the hydrogel's mechanical strength by more than 5-fold. Additionally, using alkaline phosphatase/glycerophosphate to liberate phosphate from organophosphate substrates and induce spontaneous growth of calcium phosphate crystals, we successfully developed a hydrogel that self-heals beyond its original properties (more than 20 times stiffer and 4 times more stretchable) after cutting.

17301221.label: Major findings and research outcome
17301221.value: We successfully developed a universal mechanoresponsive hydrogel platform that can switch enzymatic reactions in response to mechanical force simply by introducing target enzymes and substrates into the hydrogel matrix. Using this hydrogel, we developed the following mechanoresponsive materials: (1) mechanochromic hydrogels that visualize mechanical loading history, (2) self-growing hydrogels that polymerize protein fibers and enhance mechanical strength in response to stress loading, (3) mechano-chemiluminescent hydrogels that can visualize reversibly equilibrated static stress distributions, and (4) hydrogels that promote biomineralization under stress and achieve self-healing beyond original strength. These achievements were reported in two papers (Journal of the American Chemical Society, 2024; Macromolecular Rapid Communications, 2025), with two additional papers currently in preparation for submission.

17301221.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17301221.value: The redox reaction-catalyzing enzymes used in the design of mechano-chemiluminescent hydrogels hold promise for broader applications due to their properties, and we are planning the following extended research: (1) mechanically switchable enzymatic batteries utilizing these enzymes as battery electrodes, and (2) gels containing redox-cleavable bonds within the gel network that undergo rapid, irreversible sol-gel transition under stress.

17301221.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17301221.value: We developed a new type of gel material that can respond to mechanical forces like compressing or stretching by using biological enzymes. These enzymes are proteins that help chemical reactions happen in living systems. Our key innovation is creating a simple platform where we can add different enzymes to make gels that respond to stress in different ways. We created four types of responsive gels: First, gels that change color to show where force has been applied, creating a visual record of mechanical stress. Second, gels that actually become stronger when stressed by forming protein fibers. Third, gels that glow to show real-time stress patterns. Fourth, gels that can heal themselves after being cut and become even stronger than before by forming minerals. This technology works by simply adding the right enzymes and their target molecules to our gel platform. The mechanical force switches on the enzyme reactions, which then produce the desired response - whether that's color change, strengthening, glowing, or healing. These materials could be useful in medicine for self-healing medical devices, in engineering for structures that can detect damage, and in robotics for components that adapt to their environment. Our research has been published in leading scientific journals, demonstrating its scientific value and potential for practical applications.

17301621.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17301621.value: Many compounds and natural products that display bioactivity have rings in their structures. This may be because the biological activities of the molecule depend on having polar residues and non-polar segments simultaneously interacting with more than one recognition site in the binding pocket of enzymes and proteins, and having those groups as parts of rings enjoy a good balance of rigidity and flexibility that enhance the interactions. Heterocyclic rings having atoms such as oxygen and nitrogen provide those groups which can interact by hydrogen bonding or electrostatics, making heterocycles particularly important in bioorganic and medicinal chemistry. The opportunity to chemically optimize these compounds for therapeutic purposes is contingent on the ability to synthesize functionalized ring structures in enantiomerically enriched forms and bearing a variety of substituents and heteroatoms. Cycloaddition reactions bring two compounds together to generate a ring by forming two bonds in one operation, which present efficiency and economies in reaction steps over making one bond with each reaction. For seven-membered rings, which are found in many natural products and bioactive molecules, the (4+3) cycloaddition is a convergent strategy to construct them. More concise methods to prepare the precursors, higher yields and selectivity, including enantioselectivity in the cycloadducts, and accessibility to varied scope in product structures are issues for research in this field. We have been studying epoxy and aziridinyl enolsilanes as the three carbon unit for (4+3) cycloadditions with various dienes to synthesized cycloheptenones. In this project we plan to explore allylsilanes, instead of enolsilanes, to deliver the nucleophilic reactivity in the dienophile. Unlike the enolsilane which must be generated by multiple steps, the allylsilane can be added as a preformed fragment, which will make the synthesis of this class of precursors more convergent and concise. The allylsilane also exhibits more structural variations compared with the enolsilane. The subsequent (4+3) cycloaddition directly provides methylenated cycloheptanes, which are found in many natural products. The (4+3) cycloadducts also bear hydroxy or amine substituents and are densely functionalized, with derivatization possibilities that will be useful for preparing intermediates for synthesis and other target compounds. Following up on the preliminary results, we will examine the (4+3) cycloaddition of epoxy and aziridinyl allylsilanes and its reaction parameters fully. 許多具有生物活性的化合物和天然產物的結構中都存在環狀結構。這可能是因為這些分子的生物活性取决於具有極性和非極性片段與酶和蛋白質的結合口袋中的多個識别位同時相互作用，而因有這些環的結構單元兼具剛性和靈活性的特點，加强了這相互作用。含有氧和氮等原子的雜環可以通過氫鍵或靜電相互作用，所以雜環化合物在生物有机和藥物化學中特别重要。為了達到治療的目的，我們常常需要對候選化合物進行化學優化，這取決於我們能否對影選擇性地合成含豐富官能團的雜環化合物，帶有各種取代基和雜原子。 環加成反應將兩種化合物結合在一起形成環，一次反應形成兩個化學鍵。相比逐步反應形成兩個化學鍵的反應來説，環加成反應明顯更加高效和更具經濟性。七元環廣泛存在於許多天然產物和生物活性分子中，(4+3) 環加成反應是構建七元環直接而高效的策略。對於(4+3) 環加成反應的研究，當下主要集中在發展更簡潔的前體製備方法，得到更高的環加成產物產率和選擇性，包括環加成產物的對影選擇性和更豐富官能團。 我們一直致力於研究環氧和氮丙啶烯醇硅醚作為(4+3) 環加成反應中的三碳單元，與各種二烯進行環加成合成環庚烯酮。在這項研究中，我們計劃用烯丙基硅烷代替烯醇硅醚，以提供親二烯體中的親核反應性。不像烯醇硅醚必須通過多步反應構建，烯丙基硅烷可以作為預先形成的結構砌块，這就使合成這一類反應的前體更加收斂和簡潔。烯丙基硅烷與烯醇硅醚相比，表現出更多的結構變化。隨候的 (4+3) 環加成反應生成的亞甲基化環庚烷，存在於許多天然產物中。(4+3) 環加成產物中帶有羥基或胺取代基，具備豐富的官能團，可以被進一步衍生化，這將有助於製備合成中間體和其他目標化合物。在已經取得的初步结果的基础上，我們將深入研究環氧和氮丙啶烯丙基硅烷的（4+3）環加成反應的反應條件和應用範疇。

17301621.label: Realisation of objectives
17301621.value: Although (4+3) cycloadditions have been known for nearly 70 years, the vast majority of them involve oxyallylic cations which are derived from enolate derivatives. Enolsilanes in particular are easily obtained, more stable versions of the enolates which can be applied in many (4+3) cycloadditions. Far fewer studies have involved their all-carbon counterpart, ie. the allylsilane derivatives. This is a study to investigate the scope, extent and outcomes related to the synthesis and reactivity of the allylsilane derivatives in (4+3) cycloadditions, in particular, those structures with epoxides as the electrophilic component. All of the revised objectives have been addressed and realized. Altogether this study represents the largest series of allylsilanes engaging in (4+3) cycloadditions investigated to date. 1. Epoxy allylsilanes represent a very different molecular family, for which methods from our previous studies that synthesized epoxy enolsilanes did not provide solutions. An added challenge was that these substrates were quite volatile and difficult to isolate except by distillation. Thus the syntheses of such precursors by various methods were designed all over again, and each was evaluated for yields, practicality, and handling over a range of scales. 2. The conditions for intermolecular cycloadditions were optimized over a number of reaction factors (temperature, concentration, amount of catalyst) and the best conditions for high yields were found. 3. Intermolecular cycloadditions of epoxy allylsilanes were evaluated for reactions with reactive dienes such as furans and cyclopentadiene, their yields and diastereomeric outcomes were found and compared with those of the epoxy enolsilanes 4. The synthesis of such complex allylsilanes tethered to furans and other dienes also required a redevelopment of the synthetic route, as the best option should also be amenable to the synthesis of optically enriched substrates. A route was found involving silylated vinyl organometallics, via their addition to chloroaldehydes. For optically enriched substrates, enantiomerically enriched alpha-chloroaldehydes needed to be synthesized. In this way, a series of epoxy allylsilanes tethered to furans, pyrroles, thiophenes and benzenoids were synthesized for study. 5. The (4+3) cycloadditions of the intramolecular substrates were studied. Each product was isolated, analyzed and characterized. The stereochemical outcomes and yields were obtained and compared. Moreover, we collaborated with computational chemists in a study to better understand the reaction features and the rather complex reaction mechanism.

17301621.label: Major findings and research outcome
17301621.value: 1. Various routes to the parent epoxy allylsilane were experimentally evaluated. New routes were designed for the synthesis of the intramolecular cycloaddition substrates. 2. Methylenated bicyclic cycloadducts were generated by the formal intermolecular (4+3) cycloadditions of epoxy allylsilanes with furans and cyclopentadiene. Although epoxy allylsilanes differ in reactivity compared with epoxy enolsilanes, they are nevertheless found to still be effective as dienophiles in this cycloaddition. The epoxy allylsilane, once activated by R3SiOTf, serves as a good electrophile, while the allylsilane moiety completes the cycloaddition through C-C bond formation with the desilylation of the (trimethylsilyl)methyl group. The yields of the cycloadditions are moderate to good. 3. The intramolecular cycloaddition generally proceeded well, and reaction with TESOTf results in the formation of the intramolecular cycloadducts with 5,7- and 6,7-fused bicyclic frameworks in moderate to good yields. The dr is also not as high but can be controlled by steric elements. The intramolecular cycloaddition is diastereoselective when R3 bears a substituent, providing only the exo cycloadduct. 4. Experiments with the optically emnriched epoxy allylsilane show that the reaction proceeds by the diene attacking the backside of the activated epoxide, allowing the synthesis of enantiomerically enriched cycloadducts. The dr and ee are consistent with a backside attack. Therefore, the synthesis of cycloadducts asymmetrically is possible. 5. We evaluated whether the methylenated cycloadducts could be derived from the typical oxyallylic cation cycloaddition products via methylenation reactions. These were found to be difficult as the cycloadducts are rather hindered; the Wittig reaction failed altogether. The Peterson olefination was slightly more effective, and in the course of these studies, we found mild conditions--cat. CuCl2-H2O in wet MeCN, to implement the desilylative dehydration step of the Peterson olefination. These conditions to produce a controlled amount of acid were mild and compatible with various functional groups, and produced methylenated products in yields better than those reported in the literature. 6. Our computational studies with collaborators revealed important characteristics and understanding of this reaction. Although generally, the yields and diastereoselectivity of this cycloaddition are not as high as that with epoxy enolsilanes, in fact, epoxy allylsilanes are more electrophilic and thus more reactive with the dienes, but the second bond formations have higher barriers. Thus the intermediates have a longer lifetime and may engage in side reactions--this is the reason most likely for the diminished yields.

17301621.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17301621.value: Based on the outcomes of this investigation, the conditions and the types of epoxy allylsilane substrates that would react to generate (4+3) cycloadducts have been found. These cycloadducts are even available in optically enriched forms. This reaction could be used for the synthesis of intermediates towards obtaining natural products and other bioactive, or medicinally significant compounds.

17301621.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17301621.value: The classical (4+3) cycloaddition typically involves oxyallylic cations as reactive intermediates. The use of allylsilanes instead of enolate derivatives in this reaction is not unknown, but greatly under-explored. This may be due to the increased difficulty to synthesize these substrates, as well as the poorer reactivities. However, this cycloaddition has the potential to provide methylenated cycloadducts, which are often hard to obtain via olefinations of the classical cycloadducts. This study represents the largest study reported to date on allylsilanes engaging in (4+3) cycloadditions, in terms of the number of allylsilane derivatives, the range of dienes investigated, and the accompanying computational work. Actually, the epoxy allylsilane is electronically more reactive compared to epoxy enolsilanes as electrophiles, but they were found to have additional reaction pathways other than cycloaddition to terminate their reactions, and thus their intermolecular and intramolecular (4+3) cycloadditions are not as high yielding, but nevertheless successful, so that moderate to good yields of cycloadducts are obtained. Generally their endo-exo selectivities are less high, but with steric control, good diastereoselectivities can still be obtained. This reaction and the cycloadducts could be used in synthetic schemes to procure intermediates for the synthesis of target molecules for drug discovery and material science.

17301721.value: 关联量子材料的数值研究

17301721.label: Project Objectives
17301721.value: The first objective is to develop new algorithms that solve long-standing problems in the quantum many-body and materials research. We will continue the success in the development of sweeping cluster algorithm which was developed by us and successfully solved the quantum dimer model which remain unsolved for more than 30 years. Our further development in this project will bring new insights into the fields of topological order and frustrated magnets, such that the new paradigm of quantum matter with its characteristic features of fractionalized anyon excitation and emergent gauge fields, can be addressed in unbiased manner with large-scale numerics. The second objective is to build the protocol of modern quantum material computation. Here we will follow our recent achievement in accurate model calculations for rare-earth magnet TmMgGaO4 (TMGO), see the publication Nature Communications 11, 1111 (2020) and HKU press release (Quantum Material research connecting physicists in Hong Kong, Beijing and Shanghai https://www.hku.hk/press/press-releases/detail/21179.html), and establish such protocol in the investigations of quantum magnets and twisted graphene heterostructures, to provide better understanding and modeling of such correlation-driven phenomena. Lastly, from a historical perspective, one sees that large-scale computational physics research has not particularly been strong in Hong Kong area. However, by virtue of the dedicated efforts of the PI and his collaborators and with the support of high-performance computing facilities (e.g. National supercomputer centers in Guangzhou/Shenzhen) and collaboration with nearby institutions (e.g. Songshan Lake Materials Laboratory and the China Spallation Neutron Source in Dongguan) , one can certainly envision to bring in new developments and change the landscape in quantum materials research in Hong Kong and the Greater Bay Area in the next 5 to 10 years.

17301721.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17301721.value: This project will focus on employing large-scale numerical simulations to investigate quantum many-body systems and quantum materials. Research on quantum materials propels the continuous development of human society, ranging from the next-generation AI computing chips that could go beyond Moore’s law, the high-temperature superconducting material which could potentially solve the energy crisis, to the topological matter that could be the building block of quantum computer. However, the difficulty of such research lies in the fact that the basic ingredients of quantum materials -- the electrons -- are subject to the mutual quantum mechanical interactions among millions of themselves and the complicated chemical and physical environment of crystals. The full quantum treatment of these many electrons is way beyond the time of paper and pencil, and instead requires modern computational techniques and advanced analysis. Thanks to the fast development of the supercomputing platforms and AI-inspired algorithms, quantum many-body simulations are becoming the most prominent and indispensable techniques to tackle such difficult problems and reveal new paradigms in the fundamental laws of physics. The PI is a pioneer in quantum many-body simulation and AI-inspired algorithm developments, and has acquired the unique ability and experience of working closely with both theoretical (both field theory and ab-initio calculation) and numerical scientists (both hardware and software). The target of this proposal is to develop and employ quantum many-body numerical methodologies upon several very important model systems that are critical for our understanding of correlated quantum materials. In particular, 1. Developing new algorithm solving long-standing problem: recently, the PI’s team developed a new algorithm – the sweeping cluster algorithm – that finally solved the long-standing problem of quantum dimer model which remain unsolved for more than 30 years (see the online postscript arXiv:2007.11161). In this project, we will continue develop the algorithm and open the avenue of the research on topological order and its material realizations in quantum magnets. 2. Building the protocol of modern quantum material computation: recently, the PI’s team achieved accurate model calculations for a rare-earth magnet TmMgGaO4 (TMGO) and predicted that the material could realize the long-sought-after 2D topological Kosterlitz-Thouless (KT) phase. See the publication Nature Communications 11, 1111 (2020) and HKU press release (Quantum Material research connecting physicists in Hong Kong, Beijing and Shanghai https://www.hku.hk/press/press-releases/detail/21179.html). In this project, such effort will be continued on the research of quantum magnets and twisted graphene heterostructures. 关联量子多体材料，包括量子磁性材料、重费米子、高温超导材料、量子摩尔材料等，是凝聚态物理研究的前沿和热点问题。对于关联量子材料展开研究和讨论具有重要的前沿科学意义和重大的应用前景。密度泛函理论和能带计算构成的量子材料计算的范式已无法适用于新型的强关联材料研究，一种新的研究范式亟待发展。本项目旨在通过发展量子多体计算方法，结合多种数值手段，实现强关联量子材料研究的多体计算范式。具体而言，计划综合利用量子蒙特卡洛、张量重正化群、随机解析延拓等计算技术，实现强关联量子材料热力学和动力学性质研究的多体计算范式。通过发展和应用精确高效的量子多体计算方法，深入分析热力学、动力学实验数据，并结合机器学习等方法高效拟合反推确定量子材料的微观模型。随后从微观哈密顿量出发，进一步分析材料的平衡与动力学量子物态性质，如自旋能谱中的新奇激发、量子涌现动力学和热力学规律等，展开数值和解析计算等开展深入分析，从而理解材料中涌现的量子多体物态与效应，并作出进一步的实验预言。

17301721.label: Realisation of objectives
17301721.value: The project has successfully achieved all three objectives outlined in the original application: 1, Development of new algorithms for quantum many-body and materials research: We advanced the sweeping cluster algorithm, originally developed by our team to solve the long-standing quantum dimer model. This work provided new insights into topological order and frustrated magnets, enabling the unbiased large-scale numerical study of quantum matter with fractionalized anyon excitations and emergent gauge fields. The progress is documented in our published works, including the development of a network-initialized Monte Carlo (NIMC) scheme based on generative neural networks, which significantly accelerates simulations for classical and quantum critical systems. 2, Establishment of a modern quantum material computation protocol: Building on our prior achievement in accurate model calculations for TmMgGaO₄ (published in Nature Communications, 2020), we extended this protocol to investigate quantum magnets and twisted graphene heterostructures. Our momentum-space quantum Monte Carlo method was successfully applied to realistic continuum models of twisted bilayer graphene, revealing interaction-driven insulating gaps and collective excitations with approximate valley SU(2) symmetry. These results provide a deeper understanding and modeling of correlation-driven phenomena in modern quantum materials. 3, Strengthening large-scale computational physics research in Hong Kong and the Greater Bay Area: Through dedicated efforts and collaborations with high-performance computing centers (e.g., in Guangzhou/Shenzhen) and nearby institutions (Songshan Lake Materials Laboratory, China Spallation Neutron Source), we have established a strong foundation for computational quantum materials research in the region. The project has produced high-impact publications, trained researchers, and fostered collaborations that are poised to influence the research landscape in Hong Kong and the Greater Bay Area over the next 5–10 years. All objectives were fully met, with no significant deviations or underachievements. The research outputs, including six peer-reviewed publications in prestigious journals, demonstrate the successful realisation of the project's aims.

17301721.label: Major findings and research outcome
17301721.value: This project has successfully addressed its core objectives through groundbreaking computational research on correlated quantum materials, yielding significant findings published in high-impact journals. The direct research output comprises 6 peer-reviewed publications, including 2 in Physical Review B (PRB), 1 in Physical Review Letters (PRL), 1 in Nature Communications, 1 in SciPost Physics, and 1 in Chinese Physics Letters. The major findings are synthesized below in a review of the project’s original objectives: 1. Development of Novel Algorithms for Quantum Many-Body Problems (Objective 1): We created advanced numerical frameworks that solve fundamental scalability challenges in quantum simulations. a, Neural Network-Accelerated QMC: We designed a generative neural network-based Monte Carlo (NIMC) scheme (Chin. Phys. Lett., 2022). This innovation produces statistically independent configurations, completely bypassing critical slowing down and autocorrelation, thereby dramatically accelerating simulations for both classical and fermionic quantum critical systems. b, Entanglement Spectrum Extraction via the “Wormhole” Effect: We developed a novel QMC scheme, underpinned by a path-integral “wormhole” interpretation, to reliably extract the low-lying entanglement spectrum for systems with large entangling boundaries (Nat. Commun., 2023). This work unlocked a general relationship between energy and entanglement spectra, extending the Li-Haldane conjecture beyond topological phases. 2. Establishment of a Modern Computational Protocol for Quantum Materials (Objective 2): We applied and validated high-fidelity computational protocols to decipher complex phenomena in two forefront material classes. a, Unraveling Twisted Bilayer Graphene (TBG): Utilizing our momentum-space QMC method, we investigated realistic continuum models of TBG. We revealed an interaction-driven insulating gap and discovered long-lived, sharp “valley-wave” collective excitations exhibiting an approximate SU(2) symmetry at charge neutrality (PRB, 2022). Furthermore, studying a TBG lattice model, we explained the finite-temperature fate of the topological Mott insulator (TMI), demonstrating how proliferating excitons drastically suppress its ordering temperature, thereby bridging a key gap between strong-coupling theory and experiment (PRL, 2022). b, Identifying a Dirac Quantum Spin Liquid Candidate: Through a combined theoretical and experimental study of the kagome magnet YCu₃(OH)₆Br₂[Brₓ(OH)₁₋ₓ], we provided compelling evidence—including a T2T2 specific heat dependence—consistent with a Dirac quantum spin liquid ground state, a phase hosting emergent gauge fields and Dirac spinons (PRB, 2022). 3. Strengthening Large-Scale Computational Physics in the Region (Objective 3): The project has elevated the profile of computational quantum materials research in Hong Kong and the Greater Bay Area. All publications acknowledge RGC support and are the fruits of sustained collaboration with major research institutions and supercomputing centers in mainland China (e.g., Songshan Lake Materials Laboratory, Chinese Academy of Sciences). The body of work—which also includes fundamental studies on scaling laws at deconfined quantum criticality (SciPost Phys., 2022)—demonstrates the establishment of a robust, internationally competitive research program that trains talent and fosters deep regional integration in cutting-edge computational physics. In summary, the project has fully achieved its aims by delivering both methodological innovations and substantive insights into correlated quantum matter, resulting in a suite of high-caliber publications that advance the field and strengthen the local research ecosystem.

17301721.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17301721.value: The research conducted under this grant opens several promising directions: 1. The generative neural network–based Monte Carlo methods can be extended to more complex fermionic and bosonic models, including frustrated magnets, disordered systems, and quantum moiré heterostructures. Further optimization and integration with quantum computing techniques could yield even greater acceleration. 2. The momentum-space QMC framework for twisted bilayer graphene can be adapted to other flat-band systems, such as twisted multilayer graphene and transition metal dichalcogenide moiré systems, to explore correlated insulating, superconducting, and topological phases. 3. The wormhole interpretation of entanglement spectra provides a new theoretical lens for studying topological order and quantum criticality. Future work could explore its implications for higher-dimensional systems, symmetry-protected phases, and out-of-equilibrium dynamics. We plan to pursue these directions through continued collaboration with experimental groups, leveraging high-performance computing resources, and seeking follow-up funding from RGC and other agencies to support postdoctoral researchers and graduate students.

17301721.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17301721.value: This research project used advanced computer simulations to explore exotic states of matter known as “quantum materials,” where electrons interact strongly and give rise to surprising behaviors like superconductivity and quantum magnetism. We developed new computational tools to solve complex quantum puzzles that have remained unsolved for decades. We applied these methods to understand novel materials, including twisted graphene layers and exotic magnets, revealing how their unique properties emerge from the collective behavior of electrons. Our work not only advances fundamental science but also helps lay the groundwork for future quantum technologies. Through collaborations across Hong Kong and mainland China, we have strengthened the region’s capacity in cutting-edge computational physics.

17302321.label: Major findings and research outcome
17302321.value: The major research outcomes are as follows. 1. big image results for subrepresentations in strictly compatible systems. 2. New irreducibility results for Galois representations attached to regular algebraic, polarized, cuspidal automorphic representations of GL_n over totally real or CM fields when n<=6. 3. New l-independence results for algebraic monodromy groups of some strictly compatible system of Q.

17302321.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17302321.value: The big image results for subrepresentations obtained is applied to study the l-independence and irreducibility conjectures of type A1 automorphic Galois representations. This is a joint work with my postdoc Dr. Wonwoong Lee (https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.12566).

17302321.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17302321.value: Galois group is an important tool in number theory. The significance and value of this project is to describe the largeness of Galois groups attached to some strictly compatible systems of Galois representations. This largeness is applied to study the irreducibility and l-independence conjectures of Galois compatible systems.

17302521.label: Project Objectives
17302521.value: To formulate appropriate generic settings for the optimal savings and the value of population (OSVP) problem, and study the qualitative and quantitative behavior of its solutions. Parabolic differential equations arising from economic context have many features different from that from physical sciences. For example, the economic rules generate unusual weights; the generic utilities in economic problems create singular nonlinearities that may blow up; the initial data for economic problems may satisfy some power laws that may grow at infinity, but the initial data in physical problems usually decay at the far field, etc. Therefore, formulating the OSVP problem in a well-posed and generic setup is subtle. To solve the OSVP problem in the generic setting, appropriate conditions have to be prescribed on the population drift rate, the possible choices of production functions, and the running and terminal utility functions, etc. Otherwise, unrealistic situations may occur under a wrong setting, such as the population and/or capital will probably blow up in a finite time. The correct and appropriate conditions must be imposed according to both the economic interpretations and mathematical analysis. Besides giving the generic setting appropriately, we also plan to show the qualitative and quantitative behavior of solutions via a priori estimates. For instance, we will show some “generalized power laws”, which not only have their own important economic interpretations, but are also important in proving the existence of weak solutions. To show the global-in-time well-posedness of weak solutions to the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) equations. A standard approach for solving stochastic control problems is to study the corresponding HJB equations, which the value function of the underlying control problem satisfies. For studying HJB equations, a standard method is to first prove the existence and uniqueness of viscosity solutions, and then show that the unique viscosity solution is indeed classical. This approach is relatively challenging for problems in higher spatial dimensions (e.g., the generic OSVP problem), since verifying the regularity of viscosity solutions is much harder in higher spatial dimensions. Instead, one of the most novel ideas in this project is to directly obtain the well-posedness of weak solutions (in weighted Sobolev spaces) via a hybrid approach that combines techniques in partial differential equations (PDE) and stochastic analysis. Unlike parabolic PDEs arising from physical context (which can be solved purely by using classical PDE techniques), the HJB equation for the generic OSVP problem has problematic terms arising from economic context, such as the mismatch of weightings due to the Cobb-Douglas production function, the nonlinearity due to the generic utilities, etc. Some new pointwise estimates (e.g., “generalized power laws”) will be derived by using the stochastic analysis techniques (e.g., Feynman-Kac representation), and used to control these problematic terms. To verify the regularity of weak solutions to the HJB equations. The weak solution to the HJB equation can be used to solve the original stochastic control problem if it is indeed classical, because additional regularity for the weak solution is required to show the verification theorem. To do so, we will adapt the standard approach for parabolic PDE to verify that the weak solution is in appropriate Holder space. Since the unique solution obtained in the previous objective is a weak solution in weighted Sobolev spaces (instead of a viscosity solution), showing the regularity of this weak solution will be relatively easier. To perform numerical simulations to verify the optimal strategies obtained in the project numerically. The approximate values of optimal strategies and value function of the stochastic control problems will be useful in understanding the qualitative and quantitative behavior of the solutions to the underlying economic models. The numerical investigations will be implemented by a combination of different numerical methods, such as cubature methods, finite-difference schemes, Monte-Carlo method, etc. To extend the above four objectives to the inter-temporal defined contribution pension fund management (IDCPFM) problem. The novel approach proposed in this project for solving the OSVP problem can also apply to the IDCPFM problem as well. Similar to the inter-temporal mutual fund management (IMFM) problem that the Co-I solved in his recent work, the IDCPFM problem also studies the optimal trading stochastic control problems for fund managers. These studies will provide a mathematical foundation for determining appropriate management fees, but are unfortunately missing in the existing literature. Compared with the IMFM problem, the HJB equation in IDCPFM problem has an extra free boundary, due to the no-borrowing constraint. Therefore, to solve the IDCPFM problem, besides using the hybrid approach, we will also have to use the penalized method as well as an extra iterative scheme to overcome this additional difficulty. After showing the convergence of this iterative scheme, we will obtain a weak solution as the fixed point. The regularity of weak solutions can be shown by the standard arguments in parabolic PDE theory as well.
