17302521.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17302521.value: Due to a tremendous amount of applications in mathematics, physical sciences and economics, parabolic partial differential equations (PDE) have been extensively studied for a long time. Semilinear parabolic PDE arising from physical applications are mostly well-studied, but that from economic context are not, due to some fundamental differences between them – the utilities in economic problems create singular nonlinearities, the economic structures generate unusual weights, etc. As a result, the classical approaches for studying semilinear parabolic PDE do not directly apply to the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) equations arising from economic context. The optimal savings and the value of population (OSVP) problem is long-lasting in macroeconomics, and has been investigated for long since Ramsey’s seminal work in 1928. The OSVP problem aims at understanding how an economy does its systematic planning for the future, so that the values of the whole society are maximized. For example, Arrow et al. (Econ Theory 2003; PNAS 2006) studied this question by formulating it as a deterministic optimal control problem, in which the capital and population are the state variables, and aiming to determine whether and to what extent the optimal consumption policy results in a gain in the aggregate welfare. In this project we will extend the models of Arrow et al. to a stochastic setting, so that uncertainties in the capital market and population can be reflected. The economic structures create non-canonical difficulties in applying the method of energy estimates, such as the mismatch of weightings coming from the Cobb-Douglas production function, the singular nonlinearity arising from the generic utilities, etc. To avoid the possible blowup of these singular coefficients/terms, some pointwise estimates (e.g, “generalized power laws”) will be derived by using techniques in stochastic analysis. Since the state dynamics is indeed two-dimensional, these pointwise estimates are not known in the existing literature. The existence of weak solutions (in Sobolev spaces) to the HJB equations will be obtained by using this hybrid approach that combines techniques in PDE and stochastic analysis, and the regularity of weak solutions will be shown by adapting standard arguments in parabolic PDE theory. This hybrid approach will also apply to study the inter-temporal defined contribution pension fund management problem, which includes both the running and terminal utilities of fund manager in a generic form. The corresponding mathematical study is important in mathematical finance, since it will provide a solid foundation for determining appropriate management fees in the theoretical point of view. 由於在數學、物理科學和經濟學中的大量應用，拋物偏微分方程 (PDE) 已被廣泛研究了很長時間。具有物理應用背景的半線性拋物 PDE 大多已得到充分研究，但在經濟學中相應的研究並不完善。這是由於它們之間存在一些根本差異—經濟問題中的效用會導致具有奇異的非線性結構、經濟結構亦會導致非一般的權重等。是故，研究半線性拋物 PDE 的經典方法並不直接適用於經濟背景下的 Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) 方程。 最優儲蓄和人口價值 (OSVP) 問題在宏觀經濟學中長期存在，自 1928 年 Ramsey 的開創性工作以來一直被研究。 OSVP 問題旨在了解一個經濟體如何對未來進行系統規劃，從而令整個社會的價值被最大化。例如，Arrow 等人（Econ Theory 2003；PNAS 2006）透過將其表述為以資本和人口作為狀態變量的確定性最優控制問題來研究這個問題，並旨在確定最優消費政策是否以及在多大程度上導致總體福利的上升。 在本項目中，我們將擴展 Arrow 等人的模型到隨機最優控制問題，以便反映資本市場和人口的不確定性。在應用能量估計方法時，經濟問題的獨特結構會造成非典型困難，如來自 Cobb-Douglas 生產函數所產生的權重不匹配、一般效用所產生的奇異非線性結構等。 為了控制這些奇異係數/項，我們將利用隨機分析技術推導出一些全新的逐點估計（如「廣義冪律」）。由於此問題中的動態過程是二維的，所以這些全新的逐點估計並未曾在現有文獻中出現。通過使用這種結合 PDE 和隨機分析技術的混合方法，我們將証明 HJB 方程（在 Sobolev 空間中）弱解的存在性，並將採用一些在拋物 PDE 理論中標準的論證方法來証明此弱解的正則性。 這種混合方法也適用於研究在一般形式的基金經理運行和終端效用之下的跨期固定繳款養老基金管理問題。相應的數學研究在數學金融中非常重要，因為它將為確定適當的基金管理費提供堅實的理論基礎。

17302521.label: Realisation of objectives
17302521.value: All project objectives have been fully achieved. Objective 1. The primary analytical challenges were twofold: (i) identifying appropriate growth condition(s) for the drift rate of the population dynamics, and (ii) establishing sharp pointwise lower and upper bounds for solutions. We found that these issues are intrinsically linked. Specifically, if the population drift grows faster than linearly in the population variable N, classical solutions to the OSVP problem may blow up in a finite-time, precluding meaningful global-in-time pointwise estimates. Accordingly, in Research Output No. 1 (in Part C, Section 8), Assumption II imposes Lipschitz continuity on the generic drift function f. This condition encompasses economically relevant models; see Remark 1.4 therein for instance. Under this structural assumption, and using techniques from stochastic analysis, we derived generalized power-laws (i.e., the bounds (*1)–(*3) in Theorem 1.7), which constitute a central contribution of the project. This completes Objective 1. Objective 2. We established existence and uniqueness of weak solutions to the nonlinear HJB equation in weighted Sobolev spaces. The analysis proceeds via considering the equation satisfied by v_K, and applying Schauder’s fixed-point theorem to a suitably chosen linearized problem. The technical difficulty lies in controlling singular coefficients in both the nonlinear and linearized equations. This was resolved by using new pointwise (generalized power-law) estimates. Concretely, assuming the input to the linearized problem satisfies these bounds, we proved that the corresponding solution (namely the output function) also satisfies the same bounds, thereby showing the mapping from the input function to the output function is a self-map, which is the most crucial step in the fixed-point argument. This step required a nontrivial synthesis of techniques from PDE theory and stochastic analysis; see Section 4-7 of Research Output No. 1 for more details. Objective 2 is therefore achieved. Objective 3. Verification of the value function requires sufficient regularity of solutions to the HJB equation. After establishing solvability of weak solutions to and pointwise estimates for the linearized problem, we applied the deep regularity results for parabolic PDE with rough coefficients (e.g., Nash-type estimates) to obtain local Hölder continuity. Interior Schauder estimates then improve regularity by one order in time and two orders in space. Iteration yields smooth solutions under appropriate smoothness assumptions on the structural coefficients; see Theorem 7.8 of Research Output No. 1 for details. This completes Objective 3. Objective 4. Numerical simulations were implemented using the Euler–Maruyama scheme for both capital and population dynamics. A key finding is the identification of transient overshoot and undershoot phenomena in the capital trajectory. We further analyzed the impact of stochastic noise, which can obscure these transient effects. Details are provided in Section 3 of Research Output No. 1. Objective 5. The analytical framework was extended to the inter-temporal defined contribution pension fund management (IDCPFM) problem. Compared to the OSVP model, the associated HJB equation includes a free-boundary feature, which we have addressed by using a penalization method. While the core analytical strategy parallels Objectives 1–3, the numerical implementation is substantially more complicated, due to the existence of free-boundary. We therefore developed a hybrid finite-element PDE and iterative scheme; see Section 5 of Research Output No. 2 for details. Moreover, some a priori estimates and analytical techniques developed in the OSVP and IDCPFM problems also applied to the liquidation problem (in mathematical finance) and the study of the Hunter–Saxton equation, leading to Research Outputs No. 3 and 4 (in Part C, Section 8) as well.

17302521.label: Major findings and research outcome
17302521.value: The major output of this project consists of four research papers in collaboration with international experts from China, Hong Kong, the UK, and the USA; see Part C for details. This project mainly focuses on solving highly nonlinear partial differential equations (PDE) arising from real-world applications, such as those in mathematical economics and finance. A central achievement of this project was the rigorous resolution of the Optimal Savings and the Value of Population (OSVP) problem. Unlike previous results in the literature, our framework incorporates random noise into both capital and population dynamics to accurately reflect uncertainties in financial markets and demographic shifts. Using techniques in both PDE theory and stochastic analysis (e.g., using weighted Sobolev spaces, the Feynman-Kac formula, etc.), we: (i) proved the global-in-time existence and uniqueness of classical solutions to the corresponding Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) equations; (ii) showed the verification theorem; and (iii) numerically validate our theoretical results and reveal the new “transient behavior”. A significant finding of this work is the identification of transient behavior over finite time horizons, and this behavior has not been observed in previous literature. In general, if the production function F is dominant, capital steadily reaches an equilibrium level. However, due to the nonlinearity and parabolic nature of the underlying HJB equations, we observed phase transitions where capital “overshoots” or “undershoots” the equilibrium level. Notably, the random noise oscillates these optimal paths, so a high volatility in the capital dynamics can detour the determination of the exact underlying equilibrium level. These findings are detailed in Item No. 1 of Section 8. Building on these techniques, we generalized our mathematical analysis to the Inter-temporal Defined-Contribution Pension Fund Management problem, which involves a highly nonlinear HJB equation with a free boundary. To tackle the free boundary, we implemented the penalized method as well as using our new techniques (developed while solving the OSVP problem), we proved the existence and uniqueness of classical solutions, established a verification theorem, and provided numerical simulations; see Item No. 2 of Section 8 for details. Furthermore, the PI’s team also adapted the new parabolic estimates to liquidation problems, as well as discovered that the lower-bound estimates derived in this project also play a crucial role in the study of the Hunter-Saxton equation. As a result, we also obtained results in Items No. 3 and 4 of Section 8.

17302521.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17302521.value: 1. Expansion of the Hybrid Analytical Framework A major contribution of this study is the development of a hybrid method—integrating PDE theory with stochastic analysis—to derive accurate pointwise estimates, such as the generalized power laws that we identified in the OSVP problem. We have demonstrated that this approach remains effective for HJB equations with multiple spatial variables (such as the capital K and population N in the OSVP problem). A key course of action is to adapt this new hybrid approach to other high-dimensional HJB equations and parabolic PDE with similar structures, particularly those where pointwise estimates have traditionally been difficult to derive. 2. Practical Application to Pension Fund Management Regarding the IDCPFM problem, our work has established a rigorous theoretical foundation for optimal control problem from the fund manager’s perspective. The next phase involves applying this mathematical model to develop a standardized, data-driven methodology for determining appropriate pension fund management fees. By bridging the gap between theoretical well-posedness and financial policy, this direction will advance both the mathematical theory of free-boundary problems and the practical efficiency of numerical simulations in actuarial science.

17302521.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17302521.value: This project developed new mathematical tools to solve partial differential equations (PDE) arising from economics and finance, such as models for long-term economic planning and pension fund management under uncertainties. At its heart was the “optimal savings and the value of population” problem, a classic question about how a society balances current consumption with savings for future generations. Unlike most previous models, this research introduced randomness to reflect real-life uncertainties in both financial markets and population changes. The economic models considered have non-canonical difficulties in applying standard methods, due to realistic features like human behavior (utility) and Cobb-Douglas production functions. These features cause mismatched weights and unusual nonlinearities that classical methods cannot directly apply. To overcome this, the project created a novel "hybrid approach" combining PDE and stochastic analysis techniques to prove the unique existence of solutions. In addition, this project verified that these solutions are smooth and well-behaved, and used numerical simulations to confirm the theoretical answer. Finally, the PI's team applied these new techniques to other real-world problems, such as the inter-temporal defined-contribution pension fund management problem, for which a mathematical foundation for determining appropriate management fees was rigorously provided.

17302621.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17302621.value: Chemical protein synthesis can be used to generate proteins that might otherwise be difficult to obtain using biological expression systems. The key to the modern chemical protein synthesis is the effective chemoselective peptide ligation which is capable of joining the side-chain unprotected peptide fragments together unambiguously at the C/N-termini with a natural peptide bond at the ligation site. More recently, our laboratory has found that side-chain unprotected peptide salicylaldehyde ester can react with another peptide with N-terminal cysteine or penicillamine to afford the N,S-benzylidene acetal intermediate. Subsequent acidolysis with TFA/H2O/EDT leads to Xaa-Cys/Pen linkage at the ligation site. Alternatively, the following desulfurization can generate Xaa-Ala/Val sites, respectively. We termed this method Cysteine/Penicillamine Ligation (CPL). In this proposed project, we aim to investigate the scope and limitations of CPL, explore its potentials for chemical protein synthesis, and extend the working principle for conjugation. 蛋白质化学合成是制备难以通过生物表达方式获取的目标蛋白的重要手段。现代蛋白质合成化学中的关键问题，是实现侧链非保护多肽片段的C端与N端之间以天然肽键形式高效选择性连接。近期，本课题组发现侧链非保护多肽C端水杨醛酯能够与另一多肽的N端半胱氨酸残基和青霉胺残基形成N,S-亚苄基缩醛中间体，进而经TFA/H2O/EDT酸解给出在连接位点具有半胱胺酸和青霉胺残基的连接产物。半胱氨酸和青霉胺残基经脱硫反应，可在连接位点处分别生成丙氨酸和缬氨酸残基。我们将该新型连接反应命名为半胱氨酸/青霉胺连接反应。在本课题中，我们将深入研究该反应的适用范围和潜在局限，进一步拓展其在蛋白质化学合成中的应用，同时探索基于该反应原理的新型缀合反应。​

17302621.label: Realisation of objectives
17302621.value: Objective 1) CPL for selective desulfurization To overcome the limitation of the traditional native chemical ligation (NCL) requiring an N-terminal Cys for peptide ligation, an Ala residue at the potential convergent ligation site can be mutated into Cys. After NCL, the mutated Cys can be desulfurized back to the original Ala residue. This NCL-desulfurization strategy has been widely and successfully used in chemical protein synthesis. However, to apply such NCL-desulfurization methods, selective desulfurization of the mutated cysteine or other thiolyated amino acids in presence of free sulfhydrdryl side chains of native Cys residues is very challenging, if not impossible. Thus, protecting groups (e.g., Acm) need to be used to mask the unused cysteine residue in the early stage during the solid phase peptide synthesis. However, such protection strategies cannot be used for expression-produced peptide segments with the internal cysteine residues, and cannot be used for chemical protein synthesis involving multiple ligations relying on both native Cys and mutated Cys residues. In other word, the native Cys and mutated Cys cannot be distinguished for selective desulfurization. The ligation intermediate, termed N,S-benzylidene thioacetals (NBTs), from our Cys/Pen ligation (CPL) was found to be stable towards desulfurization. Thus, we solved the selective desulfurization problem by using combining NCL with our Cys/Pen ligation (CPL), via ligation-desulfurization-acidolysis sequence. Furthermore, we discovered that methoxy-substituted NBTs (MeO-NBTs) undergo remarkably fast acidolysis—completing within minutes under mild trifluoroacetic acid (TFA) conditions—while native NBTs (H-NBTs) remain stable. This differential reactivity provides a powerful tool for selective cysteine manipulation in peptide synthesis.. This kinetic distinction enables precise control over cysteine deprotection, facilitating sequential disulfide bond formation, tandem acidolysis-desulfurization, and orthogonal protection strategies in complex peptide architectures. A key application of this strategy was demonstrated in the first total chemical synthesis of the native human PD-L1 immunoglobulin V-like (IgV) domain, a challenging hydrophobic protein involved in immune checkpoint regulation. Objective 2) CPL with thiolated amino acid and selenocysteine The CPL method allows ligation at Cys and penicillamine sites, and after desulfurization they can be converted into Ala and Val, respectively. Thiolated amino acids have been widely explored in native chemical ligation-desulfurization approaches for chemical protein synthesis. Preparation strategies of -thio Leu/Asn/Asp/Phe/Arg/Lys building blocks have been developed and applied in NCL-desulfurization approaches. In CPL, the N-terminal penicillamine (-thio Val) is just as effective as cysteine for mediating the chemoselective ligation, thus other thiolated amino acids would also work for CPL. Along this line, we also developed a superfast desulfurization method was developed, which occurs spontaneously under ambient conditions due to the free-radical initiation from NaBEt4 oxidation, and normally finishes in 15–30 s, without heating, irradiation, inert atmosphere protection, addition of thiol additives, or other complicated apparatus setup. Objective 3) CPL-solubilizing tags A major challenge in chemical protein synthesis is the poor solubility of peptide segments, which complicates purification and ligation steps. Traditional solubilizing tag strategies often require complex modifications or are incompatible with expressed protein segments. To address these limitations, we developed a novel approach using reducible solubilizing tags (RSTs) based on the non-reducing conditions during CPL, which significantly improves the synthesis of hydrophobic and membrane-associated proteins. The RST strategy involves attaching solubilizing tags—such as polyethylene glycol (PEG), polylysine (polyLys), or polyarginine (polyArg)—via disulfide bonds to either internal cysteine residues (introduced by mutation if necessary) or C-terminal salicylaldehyde (SAL) esters. These tags enhance peptide solubility during purification and ligation while remaining stable under standard peptide ligation conditions, including Ser/Thr ligation (STL) and Cys/Pen ligation (CPL). After ligation, the tags are easily removed using reducing agents like TCEP (tris(2-carboxyethyl)phosphine) or through radical-based desulfurization, restoring the native protein sequence. A key advantage of RSTs is their compatibility with both synthetic peptides and expressed protein segments, making them suitable for total chemical synthesis and semi-synthesis. The researchers demonstrated the method’s effectiveness by synthesizing three challenging proteins: the 2B4 Cytoplasmic Tail, the Membrane Protein FCER1G, and HMGB1. The RST strategy overcomes limitations of previous methods, such as backbone modifications or irreversible tag attachments, by providing a simple, late-stage functionalization approach. Another strategy to solve the problem of difficult protein synthesis developed in this project is tunable backbone modification (TBM) strategy, leveraging the reversible stability of Cys/Pen ligation intermediates to introduce solubilizing tags that facilitate both peptide synthesis and ligation. The TBM strategy involves the on-resin installation of a Cys ligation intermediate, which disrupts secondary structure and prevents aggregation during solid-phase peptide synthesis (SPPS). A key innovation was the discovery that acetylation of the phenolic hydroxyl group in the N,S-benzylidene acetal intermediate renders it acid-resistant, allowing selective deprotection under controlled conditions. This tunability enables the intermediate to serve as a solubilizing handle during synthesis while being removable post-ligation. The approach was first validated with the synthesis of IL-2’s problematic C-terminal segment, which was previously inaccessible due to poor solubility. By incorporating a solubilizing alkoxy chain into the TBM structure, the peptide could be efficiently synthesized, purified, and ligated. The full-length IL-2 was assembled via a convergent synthetic route, combining serine/threonine ligation (STL) and native chemical ligation (NCL). Initial attempts to ligate hydrophobic segments failed due to aggregation, but introducing TBM at multiple sites significantly enhanced solubility and reactivity, enabling successful NCL even at sterically hindered threonine sites. Following sequential ligations, the TBM groups were removed under mild acidic conditions, and the linear IL-2 precursor was refolded to form the native disulfide bonds. This work demonstrates the power of the TBM strategy in overcoming longstanding challenges in protein synthesis, particularly for hydrophobic and aggregation-prone sequences. Objective 4) Long-range thiol participation pathway analogous to CPL The CPL reaction proceeds through a reversible imine formation, followed by thiazolidine formation from the -thiol group, and then an irreversible 1,5-O-to-N acyl. We wondered whether a long-range or external thiol group could also be used to attack the in situ formed imine to mediate a subsequent O-to-N acyl transfer. To investigate this fundamental physical organic chemistry question, we propose several strategies to explore its feasibility and potential applications, including a relayed Lys acylation, an auxiliary-based ligation and intermolecular thiol-assisted peptide cyclization. For relayed Lys acylation, it involves a large ring transition state, a potential challenge was to establish the optimal length and spacer amino acids between the reacting Cys and Lys residues. Various peptide sequences have been attempted, but only trace of products have been observed. For auxiliary-based ligation, a thiophenol group as the auxiliary was first pre-installed at the amino acid backbone adjacent to the N-terminal amino acid. After the N-terminal amine of any amino acid captures the peptide salicylaldehyde ester via imine formation, the long-range thiophenol attacks the imine to mediates the O-to-N acyl transfer. Acidolysis can then generate the native peptide linkage at the ligation site. This strategy extended the CPL principle to other amino acids. Based on the principles of the CPL pathway, we expect that a peptide with a C-terminal salicylaldehyde ester and N-terminal amino group may undergo cyclization via an imine formation, and the addition of an external thiol moiety could attack the imine to convert sp2 N into sp3 N, initiating the O-to-N acyl transfer. This approach has allowed us to prepare various cyclic peptides.

17302621.label: Major findings and research outcome
17302621.value: The development of methods and strategies for chemical protein synthesis has allowed many proteins to synthetically accessible. However, proteins of large sizes and hydrophobic domains, as difficult proteins, still present a challenge for chemical synthesis. Towards this end, we developed Cys/Pen ligation (CPL) and explored its applications in this project. The CPL approach involves two distinct steps: 1) chemoselective ligation forming an N,S-benzylidene acetal intermediate, and 2) acidolysis to afford Xaa-Cys/Pen at the ligation site. It was found that the N,S-benzylidene acetal linked peptide product was stable enough under the reductive, basic and mild acidic conditions, de-Fmoc and desulfurization conditions as well as separation by reversed-phase HPLC purification. The major findings of this project include: 1) CPL could be combined with selective desulfurization to expand the ligation at other amino acid sites, such as Ala, Val, Phe and so on. Along this line, a superfast desulfurization method was developed (Chem. 2022; STAR Protocol 2023), which occurs spontaneously under ambient conditions due to the free-radical initiation from NaBEt4 oxidation, and normally finishes in 15–30 s, without heating, irradiation, inert atmosphere protection, addition of thiol additives, or other complicated apparatus setup; 2) CPL was further advanced with introduction of reducible solubilizing tags (RST) to facilitate synthesis of proteins with poor solubility. This strategy features operational simplicity and readily accessible materials. Both the protein 2B4 cytoplasmic tail and FCER1G protein have been successfully synthesized via this strategy (Chem Sci. 2022); 3) The CPL intermediate was found to disrupt the aggregation of the peptide to allow synthesize difficult proteins (J. Ed. 2023); 4) Leveraging the tunable stability of the Cys/Pen ligation intermediate, a tunable backbone modification (TBM) strategy was developed for readily introducing a solubilizing tag for both peptide purification and ligation processes. The effectiveness of this strategy was demonstrated by the chemical synthesis of interleukin-2 (Chem. Sci. 2023). 5) Peptide salicylaldehyde esters are the requisite coupling partner in Cys/Pen and Ser/Thr ligation reactions towards chemical protein synthesis. We discovered 2-(dichloromethyl)phenol as a reagent that can directly form peptide salicylaldehyde esters in an epimerization-free manner (Nature Syn 2024).

17302621.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17302621.value: The Cys/Pen ligation (CPL) method and its associated strategies—such as reducible solubilizing tags (RSTs), tunable backbone modification (TBM), and superfast desulfurization—have significantly advanced chemical protein synthesis. However, further optimization and expansion of these techniques could unlock even greater potential. One key area is the automation and scalability of CPL-based synthesis to facilitate high-throughput production of complex proteins, including membrane proteins and large multi-domain constructs. Another promising direction is the integration of CPL with other emerging ligation techniques, such as serine/threonine ligation or enzymatic methods, to expand the range of accessible protein structures. Computational modeling could also be employed to predict optimal ligation sites and minimize side reactions. Furthermore, applying these methods to the synthesis of post-translationally modified proteins, such as glycoproteins or phosphoproteins, would broaden their utility in biomedical research and therapeutic development. To achieve these goals, interdisciplinary collaboration between synthetic chemists, biophysicists, and engineers will be essential. Future research should focus on refining reaction conditions, developing new reagents, and validating the biological activity of synthetic proteins to ensure their functional equivalence to native counterparts. These efforts will solidify CPL as a cornerstone of next-generation protein synthesis.

17302621.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17302621.value: Scientists have made exciting progress in chemically synthesizing biologically active proteins, which will eventually allow to create artificial proteins in the lab. These efforts could help understand biological questions, develop new medicines and study diseases. However, making large or water-resistant (hydrophobic) proteins is still challenging at this stage. From this project, a new method called Cys/Pen Ligation (CPL) helps solve this problem by stitching together protein pieces in two steps, using a special chemical bridge that keeps everything stable. The key achievement in this project is the development of Cys/Pen ligation (CPL) method and its associated strategies to solve the problem of difficult protein synthesis. These strategies feature effectiveness and operational simplicity, enabling synthesis of several bioactive proteins which are difficult to access otherwise. Future work will focus on automating the process, making even larger proteins, and designing synthetic versions of natural proteins for medicine. This could lead to new treatments for diseases and better tools for biological research.

17302821.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17302821.value: 对被污染的城市河流进行生态修复已经成为建设复合型多功能的蓝绿基础设施（GBI）提供机遇。城市河流（蓝色基础设施）及河岸植被（绿色基础设施）能够为高度城市化地区和居民提供多种多样的环境、经济和社会效益，GBI得到广泛认可，是建设宜居、韧性及可持续城市的关键要素，也是应对气候变化和城市化相关问题的有效对策。尽管GBI至关重要，难以对GBI的社会经济效进行量化，影响了GBI价值的准确分析，也阻碍了GBI的建设和发展。 在不同的社会经济背景下对GBI环境效益以及其空间异质性进行定量化分析，能够为循证决策提供重要科学依据，这类决策包括如何优化GBI解决方案的投资策略，以及决定GBI特征（如水质、河岸景观以及游憩设施）的重要程度以实现GBI经济社会效益的最大化。除此之外，建立GBI效益和社会经济因素之间的联系，能够更有效地统筹在城市河流修复和GBI建设方面的社会意向偏好和政府决策。 空间特征分析（Spatial Hedonic Analysis）是一种经典而强大的环境经济学工具，它通过对购房者决策和GBI特征、分布的关联分析以进行环境效益定量化分析。这一方法采用空间计量经济学模型来挖掘和分析房屋市场固有的各种空间效应（自相关性和异质性）。目前在国际范围内与GBI相关的实证研究主要集中于发达国家的独立住宅，这意味着二维平面的空间效应已经有较为全面的研究技术支撑，而垂直维度（同一地点不同楼层的公寓单位）的潜在空间效应却极少被提及，这与现代城市愈发趋于垂直化发展的现状背道而驰。高层建筑有助于缓解全球范围内城市人口增长的压力，那么研究的关键问题就在于：如何将垂直维度融入计量经济模型以提高空间特征研究中空间分异的环境价值，以及异质化社会经济因素共同影响下的量化计算的可靠度。 该研究旨在将垂直纬度数据纳入空间特征分析来评估GBI设施在广州高层住宅价格中的资本转化情况以填补现有研究的空缺。从一系列以距离和聚类分析为基础的选项中用事前蒙特卡洛模拟并结合事后验证的方法确定来优化三维空间权重矩阵，并应用于住宅楼层之间的空间异质性和空间自相关分析。这一优化三维空间权重矩阵还将被纳入多层次回归框架中以建立图论模型，分析整个城市GBI的空间分布模式以及城市中不同区划单位社会经济特征影响。 该研究将推动空间特征模型和环境经济学方法和理论的构建，研究结果亦会对广州以及其他同时在水平和垂直方向扩张中城市的GBI规划和实施提供科学依据。

17303221.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17303221.value: A pulsar is a fast-rotating, highly magnetized neutron star born in a core-collapse supernova at the end point of massive stellar evolution. It can generate strong electromagnetic radiation beams co-rotating with the star. If the beams point towards the Earth, pulsating signals could be observed, which gives the name "pulsar". These objects have connection to many aspects of physics, including the most energetic events in the Universe, such as supernovae, gamma-ray bursts, and fast radio bursts, gravitational wave events, such as neutron star mergers. Some of these events are even related to the production of heavy elements in the Universe. In addition, some claimed signatures of dark matter could alternatively be explained by pulsars. It is therefore important to understand the distribution and birth properties of pulsars. Most pulsar population studies were carried out over a decade ago. There have been plenty of new developments in the field since then, including new theories, discoveries of new radio and gamma-ray pulsars that significantly expanded the sample, and new tools that can greatly speed up the simulation and fitting processes. In this proposal we aim to develop a state-of-the-art pulsar population model using novel techniques with the most updated physics inputs. Our model will account for both radio and gamma-ray pulsars in a self-consistent way. We will simulate pulsar location, spin period, magnetic field, and luminosity at birth, then trace the evolution of these parameters, and compare their present-day distributions with the observed pulsar sample. This will be the first study to employ a rigorous fitting procedure to constrain the model parameters and the pulsar birth rate. In addition, our radio and gamma-ray pulsar sample is also largest among any similar works. The results will allow new tests of pulsar physics that are not possible before. Specifically, we will be able to distinguish effects of magnetic field decay and evolution of magnetic axis inclination angle, and determine the best-fit empirical radio and gamma-ray luminosity laws. These will have important implications on pulsar detectability, critical for planning of future pulsar observations. Finally, we will apply our modeling to make predictions for on-going and upcoming pulsar surveys. This can help optimize the survey strategy. 脈衝星是一顆快速旋轉、高度磁化的中子星，誕生於大規模恆星演化終點的核心坍縮超新星中。它發射出與恆星共同旋轉的強電磁輻射束。如果光束指向地球，脈衝星的發射會以脈動信號的形式呈現給觀察者，因此得名“脈衝星”。這些恆星與物理學的許多方面都有聯繫，包括宇宙中能量最高的事件，例如超新星、伽馬射線暴和快速射電暴，以及引力波事件，例如中子星合併。其中一些事件甚至與宇宙中重元素的產生有關。此外，一些聲稱的暗物質特徵也可以由脈衝星來解釋。因此，了解脈衝星的分佈和誕生特性是解決這些問題的關鍵。 大多數脈衝星種群研究是在十多年前進行的。從那時起，該領域有了很多新的發展，包括新理論、新無線電和伽馬射線脈衝星的發現，大大擴展了樣本，以及可以大大加快模擬和擬合過程的新工具。在此提案中，我們的目標是使用具有最新物理輸入的新技術開發最先進的脈衝星種群模型。我們的模型將以自洽的方式解釋射電和伽馬射線脈衝星。我們將模擬脈衝星出生時的位置、自旋週期、磁場和光度，然後追踪這些參數的演變，並將它們目前的分佈與觀測到的脈衝星樣本進行比較。 這將是第一項採用嚴格擬合程序來約束模型參數和脈衝星出生率的研究。此外，我們的射電和伽馬射線脈衝星樣本也是同類作品中最大的。結果將允許對脈衝星物理學進行新的測試，這在以前是不可能的。具體來說，我們將能夠區分磁場衰減和磁軸傾角演變的影響，並確定最適合的經驗射電和伽馬射線光度定律。這些將對脈衝星的可探測性產生重要影響，對於規劃未來的脈衝星觀測至關重要。最後，我們將應用我們的模型來預測正在進行和即將進行的脈衝星調查。這有助於優化調查策略。

17303221.label: Realisation of objectives
17303221.value: Objective 1: Fully Achieved. We developed a comprehensive population synthesis framework that integrates the latest developments in the field. The key innovations include: 1. Magnetorotational Evolution: A force-free magnetosphere spin-down model with explicit dependence on the magnetic inclination angle, coupled with the evolution of both the magnetic field strength and inclination angle over time. 2. Magnetic Field Decay: Implementation of both exponential (Ohmic dissipation) and power-law (Hall effect) magnetic field decay models for direct comparison. 3. Emission Models: A sophisticated radio beam model with core and cone components and the latest empirical fundamental-plane relation for gamma-ray luminosity, creating a unified treatment for multi-wavelength detectability. 4. Ancillary Inputs: Updated distributions for natal kick velocities, the Galactic free electron density, and a realistic Galactic gravitational potential for dynamical evolution. Objective 2: Fully Achieved. We first expanded the pulsar sample by compiled the largest and updated sample of 1,859 normal pulsars from 14 major radio surveys, representing a significant expansion over samples used in many previous studies. Then we employed a rigorous, statistically sound fitting procedure. For the first time in pulsar population study, we utilized a high-dimensional Kolmogorov-Smirnov test to compare the distributions of four key observables (spin period, spin down rate, dispersion measure) between simulations and observations. For the model parameter estimate, we adopted a Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) technique within a Bayesian framework to efficiently explore the parameter space and determine the optimal values and robust confidence intervals for all free parameters, including those governing magnetic field decay and radio luminosity. Objective 3: Fully Achieved. We have successfully employed the model to test fundamental physics. The modeling results provided strong evidence for exponential magnetic field decay with a timescale of 8.3 Myr, which favors Ohmic dissipation in the crust as the dominant mechanism. We also confirmed the significance of magnetic inclination angle evolution, showing it leads to a predominance of aligned rotators in the observed population. In addition, we were also able to constrain the pulsar radio luminosity law and the birth rate. We show that the former modeling the former with a simple power law can well reproduce the observed P-Pdot distribution without an ad-hoc "death line." This also led to a revised and more accurate estimate of the Galactic pulsar birth rate of ~0.68 per century, which has important implications for supernova progenitor models. We applied the best-fit model to forecast the yield of several major upcoming surveys (e.g., FAST, SKA, MeerKAT). The results provided essential estimates of detectable pulsars to aid in observational planning. It also accurately reproduced the observed population of Fermi-LAT gamma-ray pulsars, demonstrating its predictive power across the electromagnetic spectrum. To conclude, all project objectives were not only met but exceeded. The development of a sophisticated, physics-based model, its rigorous constraint with a large observational dataset using advanced statistical methods, and its subsequent application to resolve open questions in pulsar physics and guide future observations, collectively represent a significant and comprehensive achievement in the field of astrophysics.

17303221.label: Major findings and research outcome
17303221.value: This research presents a comprehensive population synthesis of normal radio pulsars, leading to several key findings on their evolution and properties. The primary outcome is strong evidence for the decay of neutron stars' magnetic fields over million-year timescales. By comparing simulated pulsar populations with a large observational sample, the study demonstrates that an exponential decay model, motivated by ohmic dissipation in the crust, provides a significantly better fit to the data than a power-law model driven by the Hall effect. The best-fit exponential decay timescale is constrained to 8.3 million years, implying that magnetic field decay is a non-negligible process for the majority of pulsars. The model successfully reproduces the observed distributions of pulsar spin periods, spin-down rates, dispersion measures, and radio flux densities without needing to invoke a theoretical "death line" beyond which pulsars stop emitting. Instead, aged pulsars naturally fade beyond detectability due to the adopted radio luminosity law. Other major findings include: 1. Magnetic Alignment: The simulation confirms that the angle between a pulsar's magnetic and spin axes (the inclination angle) evolves toward alignment over time. This results in a large fraction of older pulsars being nearly aligned rotators. 2. Initial Properties: The initial magnetic field strength at birth is best described by a lognormal distribution with a mean of ~10^12.3 Gauss. The initial spin period distribution is broad, but less tightly constrained. 3. Gamma-Ray Predictions: Using the preferred "outer gap" model for high-energy emission, the simulation accurately predicts the observed number of gamma-ray pulsars detected by the Fermi telescope. 4. Birth Rate: The model estimates a Galactic pulsar birth rate of approximately 0.68 per century, which aligns reasonably well with independent estimates of the core-collapse supernova rate. In conclusion, this work provides robust, observationally-constrained evidence for exponential magnetic field decay in pulsars, highlighting ohmic dissipation as the dominant mechanism and offering a refined picture of their long-term magneto-rotational evolution.

17303221.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17303221.value: This research can be further developed in several key directions. First, the models for neutron star birth locations and spatial distribution are based on older data and could be updated with modern, larger observational samples. Second, our population synthesis results for magnetic field evolution can be independently verified using direct measurements from Cyclotron Resonance Scattering Features (CRSFs) in X-ray pulsar spectra. Finally, a promising path is to incorporate the microphysics of the neutron star crust into decay models. Instead of a full population synthesis, the well-defined boundaries in the P-P diagram, which this work shows are tightly constrained by magnetic field decay. It can be used to directly test and refine specific physical models of crustal evolution.

17303221.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17303221.value: Pulsars are the dense, rapidly spinning remnants of exploded stars. They act like cosmic lighthouses, sending beams of radio waves that sweep across the sky. By studying thousands of these objects, we can learn about the extreme physics inside neutron stars—matter so dense that a teaspoon would weigh billions of tons. This project builds a detailed computer model to recreate the entire pulsar population in our Galaxy. By comparing the simulated pulsars with real observations, the study reveals how pulsars are born, how they slow down, and how their powerful magnetic fields weaken over millions of years. One key finding is that a pulsar’s magnetic field fades significantly over time, which affects how long we can detect it and how it evolves. The model also predict how many pulsars are born every year and how do they travel in the Galaxy. All the results can help predict how many pulsars future telescopes or surveys such as FAST, are likely to discover. These predictions are valuable for planning observing strategies and maximizing scientific return. Overall, this research provides new insight into the life cycle of neutron stars and helps us understand some of the most extreme environments in the universe, linking cutting-edge physics with upcoming discoveries.

17303421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17303421.value: Research in molecular materials, especially those that contain all-carbon extended π-conjugation, has attracted enormous attention owing to their potential applications as functional materials. Their unique optical, electronic and charge transport properties have stemmed from the rigidity, extended π-electron delocalization and planarity of the π-system that give rise to various functional properties. On the contrary, relatively less attention was focused on the corresponding carbon-rich metal-containing derivatives. In this project, we will focus on carbon-rich metal-containing molecular materials with rigid structures. It is believed that carbon-rich metal-containing molecular materials hold great promises since the incorporation of transition metal centres may lead to unique optical, electronic and physical properties. While two-dimensional organic networks based on rigid structural motifs are known, most of the architectural designs are based on covalent chemistry and assembly of linear and branched structural motifs despite increasing efforts on the use of their linear or discotic shapes to give supramolecular ordering. Although there have been recent advances in the assembly and growth of supramolecular assemblies and polymers, the majority involves one-dimensional growth, with construction of two-dimensional architectures and networks mainly based on metal-ligand coordination and covalent bonding of linear and branched structural motifs. Corresponding works with non-coordination-driven two-dimensional supramolecular assemblies and networks are scarce and are still at its infancy. Corresponding studies involving metal complexes capable of assembly via non-covalent metal-metal interactions are even more scarce. Thus an exploration into the use of supramolecular strategies, especially those involving metal complex systems capable of self-assembly via non-covalent metal-metal interactions, in achieving two-dimensional periodic structures and network growth or tessellation would represent a challenging area of research. In this project, attempts will be made to achieve two-dimensional periodic structures, network growth or tessellation through the rational design and synthesis of metal complexes of different geometrical shapes for single-component supramolecular self-assembly. It is envisaged that with rational design and judicious choice of the ligand motifs, novel classes of hierarchical single-component metallosupramolecular self-assemblies and networks with interesting optical, luminescence and morphology can be obtained. Exploration of their functional properties will also be made. These may provide guiding principles for the rational design and synthesis of new classes of luminescent metallosupramolecular self-assemblies of controlled hierarchical structural order and alignment through manipulation of geometrical shapes of the metal-ligand structural motifs and tessellation of geometrically simple metal complexes capable of exhibiting non-covalent metal-metal interactions. 由於具有大的π共軛全碳分子材料展現出其在功能材料方面的潛在應用而受到廣泛關注。 剛性大π電子的離域以及π體系的平面性使它們擁有獨特的光學、電子和電荷傳輸性質，進而產生各種各樣的功能特性。 反之，對相應的富碳金屬衍生物所受的關注則相對較少。 本項目將重點研究具有剛性結構的富碳金屬分子材料。 團隊相信通過過渡金屬中心的摻雜能給這些碳材料帶來獨特的光學、電子和物理特性，為這些富碳金屬分子材料帶來廣闊的應用前景。雖然基於剛性結構基元的二維有機網絡已廣為人知，而針對利用其線型或碟型的形狀產生超分子排序的研究也越來越多，但大多數設計的結構都是基於共價化學以及線性和分支結構基元的組裝，儘管最近在超分子聚集體和聚合物的組裝和生長方面取得了一些進展，但大多數僅限於一維生長，而二維結構和網絡的構建主要還是基於金屬配體配位鍵以及線性和分支結構基元的共價鍵合。 由非配位鍵驅動組裝的二維超分子集合體和網絡相關的研究相對較少，目前還處於起步階段。 而金屬配合物通過非共價金屬-金屬相互作用組裝形成二維超分子集合體的相關研究則更為稀缺。因此，探索利用超分子的策略，尤其是通過非共價金屬-金屬相互作用能夠自組裝的金屬配合物體系來實現二維週期結構、網絡生長或密鋪，將是一個富挑戰性的研究領域。 本項目將通過合理的設計和合成不同幾何形狀的金屬配合物來實現單一組分超分子自組裝，從而形成二維週期性結構、網絡生長或密鋪。通過對配體基元的合理設計和選擇，預期可研發具有獨特的光學和發光特性，以及形貌的新型多級單組分金屬超分子自組裝和網絡。 與此同時，也將對它們的功能特性進行探索。 期望能通過操縱金屬配體結構基元的幾何形狀以及非共價金屬-金屬相互作用的簡單幾何金屬配合物的密鋪，能為合理設計和合成這類可控多級結構次序和排列的新型發光金屬超分子自組裝材料提供指導原則。

17303721.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17303721.value: 再保險是保險公司轉移部分風險和負債以實現償付能力和現金流穩定性和可預測性的重要手段。其重要性再怎麼強調也不為過，全球再保險市場規模充分體現了這一點，2018 年全球再保險市場規模估計約為 2500 億美元。系統和全面分析再保險市場參與者如何相互影響的框架。這相當於調查保險公司和再保險公司應採用的最佳策略，以及他們的風險狀況和風險偏好如何影響彼此的決策。最終目標是深入了解如何安排再保險，以便雙方通過實現最佳的利潤風險權衡來互惠互利。由於再保險的有效性會對保險和再保險公司的運營產生巨大影響，難怪優化再保險領域在過去幾十年中一直是精算科學中最受歡迎和最活躍的研究方向之一。 該提案的目標是為這一重要領域提供進一步和關鍵的發展。它加深了我們對如何通過應用現代數學和經濟工具在再保險市場中做出最佳決策的理解。提出了新穎、具體和實用的模型，以檢查在現有文獻中很大程度上被忽略的最優再保險問題的各個關鍵方面。該項目的這一目標將分兩部分實現。第一部分考察最適合保險公司風險狀況和風險偏好的再保險的真實需求，以及再保險策略應如何適應各種業務約束和風險管理考慮。第二部分研究了再保險產品整體設計的一般框架，包括賠償結構和定價，以便再保險公司能夠實現最佳的利潤風險權衡。逆向選擇等信息不對稱在保險市場中普遍存在且無法避免，長期以來一直被認為是保險和再保險公司在產品設計和定價階段面臨的主要挑戰之一。信息不對稱不僅會導致再保險效率的重大損失，而且如果不妥善解決和管理，還會使分出公司面臨重大的意外風險。儘管它很重要，但這一關鍵特徵尚未在最佳再保險文獻中得到充分關注。直到最近才在一些簡單的模型下對其進行了研究。該項目通過提出新穎的模型和解決方案技術來從戰略和實踐上解決這個問題，從而填補了這一空白。再保險業可以通過戰略性的產品設計和定價來緩解信息不對稱帶來的不利影響。 在整個項目中，將製定新的具體問題，開發新的通用數學技術，強調實際意義和與工業的相關性。它填補了文獻中的關鍵空白，指出了新的研究方向，並為再保險市場的參與者制定最佳策略提供了實用的商業指南。

17303821.label: Realisation of objectives
17303821.value: The research project (HKU 17303821), titled Deciphering Molecular Mechanisms of Site-Specific Radical-Mediated Tyrosine ortho-Nitrations Occurring via Phenoxy-Radical Intermediates In Vacuo, was funded under the 2021 Competitive Earmarked Research Grants application. Radical-mediated protein tyrosine nitration (PTN) is a hallmark indicator of nitrative stress. The complexity of radical-mediated PTN arises from the existence of multiple possible intermediates and the difficulty of generating transient species with well-defined radical sites, making experimental investigations particularly challenging. Consequently, little precise mechanistic insight has been obtained, partly due to the challenges in generating precursor and intermediate species and partly because of their fleeting nature.The widely accepted pathway for radical-mediated ortho-tyrosine nitration in vitro involves the transient formation of a phenoxyl radical on the tyrosine residue, which undergoes a radical recombination reaction between the nitrogen atom of a free •NO₂ species and the carbon atom at the ortho position of the phenol ring. This project achieved its core goals through an integrated experimental and theoretical approach, advancing the understanding of radical-mediated peptide chemistry. Three peer-reviewed studies established: (1) the structural features of radical precursors,(2) their atomic-level reaction pathways, and (3) a mechanistic model for site-specific phenoxy-radical intermediate formation. Objective 1 was achieved through the systematic design, synthesis, and investigation of model peptides containing tyrosine, phenylalanine, and tryptophan, along with structural analogues, using tandem mass spectrometry, IRMPD spectroscopy, and DFT calculations. In the presence of copper(II), these peptides underwent oxidative electron transfer dissociation. The resulting peptide radical cations were stabilized by delocalization of charge and spin facilitated by the aromatic ring. Previous studies established that the initial peptide radical cations are π-radicals, which can isomerize to other structures upon collisional activation. Attempts to generate radical cations from phenylalanine-containing peptides were less successful, likely due to weaker Cu(II) binding to the phenyl ring and the higher ionization energy of phenylalanine (I.E.(Phe) = 8.7 eV). These factors hinder the dissociative one-electron transfer to Cu(II) that produces the π-radical cations typically observed for tryptophan-containing peptides. Isotopic labeling experiments confirmed β-hydrogen rearrangement originating from the phenoxy radical—key to ortho-tyrosine nitration in vitro via radical recombination with •NO₂. A detailed structural and mechanistic study of tyrosine-derived radical cations, including β-radical pathways, was published: Characterization of glycylglycyltyrosine radical cations: Insights into β-radical formation and N–Cα bond dissociation at the tyrosine residue. International Journal of Mass Spectrometry, 506, 117351. Objective 2 focused on using isotopic labeling, spectroscopy, and computation to trace radical migration and atomic rearrangements with high precision (Research Outputs 1-3). We further identified the isomerization of phenoxyl to β-radicals and showed that metal–ligand coordination (Cu²⁺, Co³⁺, Fe³⁺) dictates radical structure. Unexpected α-carbon radicals observed in phenylalanine analogues refined our understanding of radical formation mechanisms. For example, the α-radical cationic isomer was stable against interconversion because its activation barriers exceeded the dissociation thresholds. Isomer population analyses independently confirmed these findings. Subsequent work on the model trysoine-containing peptide revealed that isomerization from the phenoxyl radical to the β-radical could be is a key mechanistic step linking radical intermediates to final PTN product formation, Objective 3 developed a mechanistic model explaining the site-specificity of protein tyrosine nitration. We demonstrated that the local chemical environment—especially metal cofactors and peptide flexibility—controls radical formation through competitive binding among carboxylate, phenolate, and guanidine groups. This provides the fundamental chemical principles governing tyrosyl radical reactivity and isomerization. The discoveries from Objectives 1 and 2 established the mechanistic framework for understanding biological PTN site-specificity. As reported in Research Output 2 (Understanding the Binding and Structures in Model Complexes of Polypeptides and Cofactors, ACS Physical Chemistry Au), metal–peptide complex studies showed that the immediate chemical environment dictates preferred metal-binding sites and thus the structure and reactivity of the radical cation. The principle of competitive binding—where carboxylate, phenolate, and guanidine groups compete for coordination—clarifies how local topology can either promote or inhibit phenoxyl radical formation at specific tyrosine residues. Ultimately, this project demonstrated that site-specificity in biological nitration arises not as an emergent biological phenomenon but as a direct consequence of fundamental chemical principles: competitive metal binding and radical stability governed by the local molecular environment.

17303821.label: Major findings and research outcome
17303821.value: This project has advanced the fundamental understanding of radical-mediated peptide chemistry by elucidating key principles that govern peptide radical formation, structure, and reactivity. Using prototypical gas-phase model systems relevant to protein tyrosine nitration (PTN), we demonstrated that the structure of the precursor metal–peptide complex determines the isomeric form and reactivity of the resulting radical cation. Competition among functional groups—such as carboxylate and phenolate—for metal binding (Cu(II), Co(III), Fe(III)) predefines the radical’s structure, establishing a general principle linking precursor conformation to reaction outcomes. Spectroscopic and computational analyses provided the first direct evidence of phenoxyl-to-β-radical isomerization in a model tyrosine peptide, clarifying a critical mechanistic step in the PTN pathway and confirming that phenoxyl radical formation precedes backbone cleavage. Furthermore, studies on phenylalanine-containing peptides revealed the formation of stable α-carbon-centered radicals instead of conventional π-radicals, challenging established assumptions about aromatic residue reactivity. Together, these findings redefine key aspects of peptide radical chemistry and provide a mechanistic foundation for understanding site-specific radical processes in biomolecules.

17303821.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17303821.value: The successful completion of this project has opened promising avenues for continued investigation into complex radical-mediated biological reactions, particularly their application to endogenous systems using multi-tyrosine peptides. This next phase will directly test the hypothesis that competitive binding, local topology, and peptide flexibility govern site-specificity in situ, allowing us to assess whether the principles identified in simplified model systems apply to more realistic biological sequences. Future work will also examine the kinetics and dynamics of the observed isomerization processes, including interconversion between metal-binding motifs and phenoxyl-to-β-radical migration. Determining the associated energy barriers and reaction rates will yield critical insight into the rate-determining steps of the overall PTN mechanism. These studies will build upon the ion-chemistry framework established in this project, aiming to bridge the gap between fundamental gas-phase chemistry and the complex biological processes underlying oxidative stress.

17303821.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17303821.value: Oxidative stress—a key factor in diseases such as stroke, Alzheimer’s disease, and diabetes—damages proteins through radical-mediated nitration. Yet it remains unclear why only specific regions of a protein are modified while others remain unaffected. This research provides a molecular-level understanding of this selectivity. By combining advanced gas-phase mass spectrometry with high-level computational modeling, we investigated model peptide segments in a solvent-free vacuum environment. This approach enabled us to isolate and observe the intrinsic chemical reactions responsible for protein damage, step by step, free from interference by solvent or cellular components. Our findings reveal the governing principles of this process: the initial conformation of the peptide motif, together with a specific amino acid side chain and its associated metal center, directs nitration to precise molecular sites. This discovery elucidates the long-standing question of site selectivity in oxidative protein damage and lays a critical foundation for developing targeted strategies to prevent or treat oxidative stress-related diseases.

17304021.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17304021.value: 溶液合成含有七边形-七边形庚二烯（heptalene）的稠环芳烃

17304021.label: Project Objectives
17304021.value: The aim of this research proposal is to establish the structure-property relationships of heptalene-embedded polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) and graphene nanoribbons (GNRs). The PI will address the trends in the band gaps and electronic structures caused by increasing the number of heptalene units and different topologies, in terms of optical/electronic properties and close-shell/open-shell characteristics, etc. We will also explore the synthetic feasibility of incorporating heptalene in π-extend systems such as in GNRs. Moreover, this work will also utilize the proposed PAHs and GNRs in different electronic applications, such as organic transistors and nonlinear optics. To achieve this goal, the PI will fully exploit the knowledge and experiences related to the solution-phase synthesis of PAHs to fabricate heptagon-heptagon pairs (heptalene units) and the precise incorporation of these units in graphene nanostructures – ranging from 0D PAHs to extended 1D GNRs (Fig. 1, Part II Section 2(c)). To this end, the specific objectives are described in the following sections. Objective 1: Synthesis of close-shell PAHs with heptalenes. The first objective will be to synthesize PAH 1 containing one heptalene and compound 2 with two heptalenes (Fig. 1), which will help to elucidate the effects of the number of heptalene units on their structural and physical properties. The solution processability of these heptalene-embedded PAHs should allow the study of their optoelectronic properties in organic solvents. The growth of single crystals of 1 and 2 will allow us to determine parameters such as bond length, aromaticity, and geometry. In addition to the number of heptalenes, the effect of different topologies will also be investigated. For example, a novel PAH 3 containing two contiguous heptalene units will be synthesized (Fig. 1). We can then investigate the local modulation of the physical and chemical properties of the heptalene-embedded PAHs. Objective 2: Synthesis of nitrogen-doped PAH with heptalenes. The introduction of heteroatoms into the lattice of sp2-carbon framework presents an effective strategy to tune the intrinsic physicochemical properties of PAHs, such as the chemical reactivity, energy gaps, and redox behavior. Bottom-up synthesis of well-defined nitrogen-doped PAHs (N-PAHs) represents a new era in the development of novel PAHs with improved electron affinities and luminescence behavior. Although significant efforts have been made in the past decade, the introduction of N atoms into non-hexagons has remained limited. In this project, the electron-rich pyrrole unit will be explored as a key building block to synthesize PAH 4 bearing two N-doped heptagons (Fig.1). The optical and electronic properties, and aromaticity of 4 will be compared with the heptalene-embedded PAHs in objective 1 to evaluate the effects of introducing N atoms into seven-membered rings. Objective 3: Synthesis of open-shell PAH containing heptalene units. Compared to the close-shell molecules discussed in objective 1, open-shell PAHs have a range of unique electronic and magnetic properties due to the spin-polarized states. Most recent works have focused on the open-shell PAHs with six-membered rings. In this objective, we will focus on the synthesis of heptalene-embedded PAH with open-shell characteristic. For instance, PAH 5 with two heptalene units will be developed (Fig. 1). According to Clar’s sextet rule, 5 should possess significant tetraradical characteristics as a result of gaining aromatic stabilization energy (5-1, Fig. 1). It will be rare to have spins located on the heptagons, which is largely unexplored in this field. The synthesis of such a model compound is expected to lead to the unprecedented synthesis of extended open-shell PAHs with non-alternant topologies. Objective 4: Synthesis of heptalene-embedded graphene nanoribbons. The motivation for this objective relates to the need to evaluate the effects of periodic heptalenes in terms of the structural, optical, and physical properties of π-expanded polymers. In this objective, the heptalene units will be introduced into structurally well-defined GNRs. The implementation of non-hexagonal rings into a honeycomb lattice represents a viable, albeit less explored route to tune the intrinsic optical and electronic properties of GNRs. Towards this end, GNR-1 and GNR-2 with periodically repeating heptalene units will be synthesized (Fig. 1), and the structural and electronic properties will be assessed to evaluate the effects of different topologies on GNRs. Objective 5: Spectroscopic studies and device applications based on the achieved PAHs and GNRs. The photophysical properties of the resultant PAHs will be well-studied by nano/femtosecond time-resolved spectroscopy (with Prof. David Phillips from the department), such as their excited state nature and dynamics, etc. To establish clear structure-property relationships for the application of heptalene-embedded PAHs, the relevant electronic devices will be fabricated through collaborations with partners of the PI. For example, the designed heptalene-embedded PAHs and GNRs are expected to possess low band gaps, making these materials potential candidates for the development of organic field‐effect transistors devices with substantially improved hole/electron mobility or balanced ambipolar charge-carrier transport properties. Open-shell model compounds can also be used to understand spin and electron density dependence in PAHs as potential “organic magnets” for spintronic applications.
rows: The aim of this research proposal is to establish the structure-property relationships of heptalene-embedded polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) and graphene nanoribbons (GNRs). The PI will address the trends in the band gaps and electronic structures caused by increasing the number of heptalene units and different topologies, in terms of optical/electronic properties and close-shell/open-shell characteristics, etc. We will also explore the synthetic feasibility of incorporating heptalene in π-extend systems such as in GNRs. Moreover, this work will also utilize the proposed PAHs and GNRs in different electronic applications, such as organic transistors and nonlinear optics. To achieve this goal, the PI will fully exploit the knowledge and experiences related to the solution-phase synthesis of PAHs to fabricate heptagon-heptagon pairs (heptalene units) and the precise incorporation of these units in graphene nanostructures – ranging from 0D PAHs to extended 1D GNRs (Fig. 1, Part II Section 2(c)). To this end, the specific objectives are described in the following sections.

Objective 1: Synthesis of close-shell PAHs with heptalenes. The first objective will be to synthesize PAH 1 containing one heptalene and compound 2 with two heptalenes (Fig. 1), which will help to elucidate the effects of the number of heptalene units on their structural and physical properties. The solution processability of these heptalene-embedded PAHs should allow the study of their optoelectronic properties in organic solvents. The growth of single crystals of 1 and 2 will allow us to determine parameters such as bond length, aromaticity, and geometry. In addition to the number of heptalenes, the effect of different topologies will also be investigated. For example, a novel PAH 3 containing two contiguous heptalene units will be synthesized (Fig. 1). We can then investigate the local modulation of the physical and chemical properties of the heptalene-embedded PAHs.

Objective 2: Synthesis of nitrogen-doped PAH with heptalenes. The introduction of heteroatoms into the lattice of sp2-carbon framework presents an effective strategy to tune the intrinsic physicochemical properties of PAHs, such as the chemical reactivity, energy gaps, and redox behavior. Bottom-up synthesis of well-defined nitrogen-doped PAHs (N-PAHs) represents a new era in the development of novel PAHs with improved electron affinities and luminescence behavior. Although significant efforts have been made in the past decade, the introduction of N atoms into non-hexagons has remained limited. In this project, the electron-rich pyrrole unit will be explored as a key building block to synthesize PAH 4 bearing two N-doped heptagons (Fig.1). The optical and electronic properties, and aromaticity of 4 will be compared with the heptalene-embedded PAHs in objective 1 to evaluate the effects of introducing N atoms into seven-membered rings.

Objective 3: Synthesis of open-shell PAH containing heptalene units. Compared to the close-shell molecules discussed in objective 1, open-shell PAHs have a range of unique electronic and magnetic properties due to the spin-polarized states. Most recent works have focused on the open-shell PAHs with six-membered rings. In this objective, we will focus on the synthesis of heptalene-embedded PAH with open-shell characteristic. For instance, PAH 5 with two heptalene units will be developed (Fig. 1). According to Clar’s sextet rule, 5 should possess significant tetraradical characteristics as a result of gaining aromatic stabilization energy (5-1, Fig. 1). It will be rare to have spins located on the heptagons, which is largely unexplored in this field. The synthesis of such a model compound is expected to lead to the unprecedented synthesis of extended open-shell PAHs with non-alternant topologies.

Objective 4: Synthesis of heptalene-embedded graphene nanoribbons. The motivation for this objective relates to the need to evaluate the effects of periodic heptalenes in terms of the structural, optical, and physical properties of π-expanded polymers. In this objective, the heptalene units will be introduced into structurally well-defined GNRs. The implementation of non-hexagonal rings into a honeycomb lattice represents a viable, albeit less explored route to tune the intrinsic optical and electronic properties of GNRs. Towards this end, GNR-1 and GNR-2 with periodically repeating heptalene units will be synthesized (Fig. 1), and the structural and electronic properties will be assessed to evaluate the effects of different topologies on GNRs.

Objective 5: Spectroscopic studies and device applications based on the achieved PAHs and GNRs. The photophysical properties of the resultant PAHs will be well-studied by nano/femtosecond time-resolved spectroscopy (with Prof. David Phillips from the department), such as their excited state nature and dynamics, etc. To establish clear structure-property relationships for the application of heptalene-embedded PAHs, the relevant electronic devices will be fabricated through collaborations with partners of the PI. For example, the designed heptalene-embedded PAHs and GNRs are expected to possess low band gaps, making these materials potential candidates for the development of organic field‐effect transistors devices with substantially improved hole/electron mobility or balanced ambipolar charge-carrier transport properties. Open-shell model compounds can also be used to understand spin and electron density dependence in PAHs as potential “organic magnets” for spintronic applications.

17304021.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17304021.value: 自 20 世紀初，E. Clar和R. Scholl的先驅工作以來，多環芳烴 (PAHs) 引起了人們廣泛的研究興趣。從那時起，許多具有不同尺寸、邊緣結構和幾何形狀的多環芳烴已經被人們設計和合成出來。特別是，一些多環芳烴形成盤狀液晶的超分子自組裝行為及其出色的載流子遷移率使多環芳烴成為未來有機納米電子學最有前途的材料之一。通常，PAHs 可視為兩個或多個稠合的苯環。除了典型的六元環多環芳烴外，在過去的 30 年中，人們對五邊形多環芳烴，如 C5v 對稱的心環烯和 C3v 對稱的碗烯，也進行了深入研究。由於其獨特的彎曲幾何形狀，七邊形嵌入的多環芳烴在過去十年中也引起了越來越多的關注，這為控制多環芳烴的光電特性提供了額外的途徑。特別是自 2019 年以來，五邊形-七邊形對（azulene unit）嵌入的 PAHs 受到了格外的關注。然而，儘管取得了很大進展，但包含非交替拓撲的新型 PAH 的合成仍然難以捉摸。例如，自 1991 年山本浩二報導了首例含有七元環-七元環（庚烯單元）的 PAH 以來，過去 30 年中僅實現了少量的庚烯嵌入 PAHs的合成（只有三個例子）。因此，對大型多環芳烴中庚烯單元的物理化學性質仍然知之甚少，這促使我們有必要從基礎科學和應用角度來闡明這些結構。在這項研究中，PI 提出了一條新的研究方向，即基於原子精確溶液合成庚烯嵌入的多環芳烴和 π 擴展的石墨烯納米帶 (GNRs)。該方法將為獲得新特性提供一條途徑，例如曲率、大的開殼雙自由基/四自由基特性、增加的化學活性以及用於有機場效應晶體管、非線性光學和自旋電子學等應用的新器件功能。為了實現本提案中的這些雄心勃勃的目標，PI 將利用不同的化學方法，包括有機化學、固態物理學和理論建模。

17304021.label: Realisation of objectives
17304021.value: Objective 1: Synthesis of close-shell PAHs with heptalenes. Realisation: In this Objective, we have successfully synthesized PAH 3 containing two contiguous heptalene units (four continuous heptagons). To gain insight into the effect on their electronic and optical properties via the introduction of four consecutive heptagons, various experimental measures, including cyclic voltammetry (CV), Raman, steady UV-vis absorption, and theoretical calculations were carried out on PAH 3 and its structural isomer bischrysene (1R) with only hexagonal rings. Compared with aromatic 1R, PAH 3 presents a distinct antiaromatic character, especially the inner heptalene core possessing clean antiaromatic nature. In addition, PAH 3 exhibits a narrower highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO)-lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (LUMO) energy gap than its benzenoid contrast 1R verified by theoretical calculation (PAH 3: 1.83 eV vs 1R: 2.62 eV) and CV measurement (PAH 3: 1.41 eV vs 1R: 2.28 eV). Our work herein not only provides a new way to the synthesis of novel PAHs with nonalternant topologies, but also offers the possibility to tune their electronic and optical properties. The related work has been published in Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. (Angew. Chem. Int. Ed., 2023, 62, e202217124; Featured as Front Cover). Objective 2: Synthesis of nitrogen-doped PAH with heptalenes. Realisation: In Objective 2, three novel topological nanographenes molecular models of nitrogen (N)-doped heptalene (also can be viewed as Stone-Thrower-Wales (S‒W) defect) were achieved through intramolecular direct arylation. Their chemical structures were unambiguously elucidated by single crystal analysis. Among them, threefold intramolecular direct arylation compound (C42H21N) is the largest nanographene bearing a N-doped nonalternant topology to date, in which the non-benzenoid rings account for 83% of the total molecular skeleton. The absorption maxima of this compound was located in the near-infrared region with a long tail up to 900 nm, which was much longer than those reported for similarly sized N-doped nanographene with six-membered rings (C40H15N). In addition, the electronic energy gaps of these series compounds obviously decreased with the introduction of nonalternant topologies (from 2.27 eV to 1.50 eV). It is noteworthy that C42H21N possesses such a low energy gap (Egopt = 1.40 eV; Egcv = 1.50 eV), yet is highly stable under ambient conditions. Our work described herein demonstrates that the nonalternant topology could significantly influence the electronic configurations of nanocarbons, where the introduction of a nonalternanting topology may be an effective way to narrow the energy gap without extending the molecular π-conjugation. The related work has been published in Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. (Angew. Chem. Int. Ed., 2023, 62, e202306890; Highlighted by WileyChem). Objective 3: Synthesis of open-shell PAH containing heptalene units. Realisation: In Objective 3, we synthesized compound 5, but it was extremely unstable and quickly decomposed. Consequently, we were unable to obtain its single crystal. Based on the above research, we rationally optimized the molecular structure and successfully synthesized a open-shell molecule with a 7-5-7 topology instead of 7-7 units, where the radical is localized on the seven-membered ring. Interestingly, this compound possesses a triplet diradical at the ground state. In this work, moving beyond the classic m-xylylene scaffold for high-spin organic molecules, 7–5–7-membered rings were introduced to create novel and exceptionally stable high-spin diradicals with half-lives (t1/2) as long as 101 days. Moreover, considering the remarkable spin relaxation of this compound, with a spin–lattice relaxation time (T1) of 53.55 ms and a coherence time (Tm) of 3.41 μs at 10 K, the compound shows great promise for applications in spin-based information retention and quantum computing. The related work has been published in Nature Communications (Nat. Commun., 2025, 16, 1006). Objective 4: Synthesis of heptalene-embedded graphene nanoribbons. Realisation: Due to the significant synthetic challenges associated with incorporating 7-7-membered rings (heptalene units) into fully conjugated graphene nanoribbons, this has not yet been successfully achieved in solution to date. After four years of persistent efforts, we have recently completed the synthesis and characterization of such graphene nanoribbons with 7-7 rings. We are currently compiling the findings from this work, applying for a patent for this graphene nanoribbon, and preparing the manuscript. Objective 5: Spectroscopic studies and device applications based on the achieved PAHs and GNRs. Realisation: We have recently succeeded in fabricating a memristor based on molecules containing 7-7-membered rings. This memristor, featuring such a topological molecular structure, exhibits bipolar behavior, capable of storing both electrons and holes, thus achieving a larger storage window compared to molecules composed solely of six-membered rings. We are currently compiling the findings from this work, and preparing the manuscript.

17304021.label: Major findings and research outcome
17304021.value: This project focused on synthesizing and characterizing polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) and graphene nanoribbons (GNRs) incorporating non-alternant heptalene (7-7-membered ring) topologies. In Objective 1, a closed-shell PAH (PAH 3) containing two contiguous heptalene units (four consecutive heptagons) was successfully synthesized. Comparative studies with its all-hexagonal isomer revealed that PAH 3 possesses distinct antiaromatic character, particularly in its core, and exhibits a significantly reduced HOMO-LUMO energy gap compared to the benzenoid analogue. This work demonstrates a novel synthetic route to non-alternant PAHs and a method to tune their electronic/optical properties, with findings published in Angewandte Chemie. For Objective 2, three nitrogen-doped topological nanographenes featuring heptalene units were synthesized via intramolecular direct arylation. The largest structure (C42H21N), with 83% non-benzenoid rings, shows an absorption tail extending to 900 nm and a remarkably low energy gap (~1.50 eV) while maintaining ambient stability. This highlights the efficacy of non-alternant topologies in narrowing energy gaps without extending π-conjugation, a result also published in Angewandte Chemie. Objective 3 targeted open-shell PAHs. Initial attempts with a heptalene-based compound failed due to instability. Structural optimization led to the successful synthesis of a stable open-shell diradical with a 7–5–7 topology, where the radical is localized on a seven-membered ring. This ground-state triplet diradical exhibits exceptional stability (half-life up to 101 days) and promising spin relaxation properties (spin-lattice relaxation time T₁ = 53.55 ms), indicating potential for quantum information applications. This work was published in Nature Communications. Objective 4 addressed the long-standing challenge of incorporating heptalene units into fully conjugated GNRs. After four years of effort, the synthesis and characterization of such heptalene-embedded GNRs have been completed. A patent application is underway, and a manuscript is in preparation. Finally, Objective 5 involves spectroscopic studies and device applications. A memristor fabricated from molecules containing 7-7-membered rings demonstrated bipolar behavior, storing both electrons and holes, which resulted in a larger memory window than devices based solely on hexagonal molecules. A manuscript on this work is currently being prepared. In conclusion, this research systematically explores heptalene-embedded nanocarbon systems, revealing how non-alternant topologies fundamentally alter electronic structures, inducing antiaromaticity, drastically reducing energy gaps, enabling stable high-spin states, and enhancing device performance. The work successfully transitions from fundamental molecular synthesis to demonstrating functional applications in electronics and quantum information science.

17304021.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17304021.value: Building upon this foundational work, significant potential exists for both fundamental exploration and technological application. The future research trajectory should focus on three interconnected fronts. First, a comprehensive investigation into the electronic and quantum properties of these systems is crucial, particularly the long-lived spin coherence observed in the diradical, to assess their viability as qubits or spin-based memory elements. Second, the molecular design space should be expanded by exploring diverse heteroatom doping (e.g., boron, nitrogen, or sulfur) and more complex non-alternant topologies to further engineer band gaps, magnetic states, and stability. Third, device performance must be optimized; this includes scaling up the synthesis of heptalene-embedded GNRs for thin-film studies and systematically integrating the novel PAHs into functional devices like memristors, transistors, or spintronic components to benchmark their performance against conventional materials. The proposed course of action involves a multi-pronged strategy: 1) Deepen physical measurements (e.g., advanced EPR, charge transport studies) on existing and new compounds to establish robust structure-property relationships. 2) Employ computational screening (like AI) to predict promising new structures with target properties before synthesis. 3) Collaborate with device engineers to fabricate and test prototype devices, moving from single-component proof-of-concept to integrated circuit demonstrations. This integrated approach from molecule to material to device will transition these scientifically intriguing nanostructures into candidates for next-generation electronic and quantum information technologies.

17304021.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17304021.value: This research explores a new way of building nanocarbons incorporating seven-seven-membered rings into their atomic structure, rather than using only the conventional six-sided ones found in graphite or graphene. We successfully created several new carbon-based molecules and ribbons featuring these seven-seven-membered rings. These novel structures exhibit remarkable and useful properties: they absorb different colors of light, can maintain stable magnetic states for remarkably long periods (over 100 days), and, when used in a prototype memory device, showed superior storage capacity. The fundamental breakthrough is that this specific seven-seven-ring architecture acts as a powerful tool to fundamentally re-engineer the material's electronic "personality." It allows scientists to fine-tune properties like color, stability, and magnetism in a way that is not possible with standard six-ring designs. This work, published in leading science journals, bridges the gap from designing novel molecules at the atomic level to demonstrating their tangible potential in next-generation electronics and future quantum computers.

17304121.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17304121.value: 香農在信息論一開始就考慮了連續時間高斯通道。連續時間高斯通道可以用高斯白噪聲表示，檢查這種通道的傳統方法是採樣方法，其中原始連續時間通道轉換為等效的離散時間通道，大量已建立的工具和方法可以被應用。然而，該方案的關鍵問題之一是連續時間反饋，記憶和乾擾不能被納入信道模型。 事實證明，這個問題可以通過考慮布朗運動來規避連續時間白高斯通道的公式。儘管如此，相對於高斯白噪聲公式，建立信息理論的鏈接布朗運動公式下連續時間通道之間的連接它的離散時間對應物長期以來一直缺失。在最近的一項工作中，我們通過在連續時間高斯反饋/記憶通道及其相關的離散時間版本採樣和近似定理的形式；此外，基於這些連接，我們提出了所謂的近似方法來處理許多問題 常規抽樣方法。事實證明，近似方法，輔以隨機微積分的相關工具，可以加深我們對連續時間高斯通道的理解，提供替代解釋歷史悠久的觀點，從新的角度恢復已知的結果，借助來自於連接帶來的洞察力和直覺獲得新的結果。 基於近似方法並受到初步結果的啟發綜上所述，本提議是對連續時間高斯函數進行深入研究反饋通道，在點對點或多用戶設置中，可能帶有帶寬限制和平均/峰值功率約束。本提案的目標可以簡單地概括為陳述如下： 1) 加強我們的逼近定理，使逼近方法可以達到更廣泛的應用； 2) 分析反饋如何影響多用戶中的連續時間高斯信道環境; 3）將現有結果擴展到連續時間平穩高斯通道； 4) 檢查具有帶寬限制的連續時間高斯反饋信道和峰值功率約束。 這個建議如果成功實施，將大大加深我們對連續時間高斯通道的幾個基本方面的理解。
