17304321.value: 從歐幾里德幾何人們過渡到黎曼幾何，在此可以通過黎曼度量去量度光滑流形上的長度與角度。歐氏空間以外存在著賦有對稱性的黎曼幾何的模型空間，即黎曼對稱空間，在二十世紀初被埃里卡當所分類。當中賦有共容的複結構的流形稱為埃爾米特對稱空間；對稱群為半單李群的屬於緊致類或者非緊致類，而有界對稱域為非緊致類埃爾米特對稱空間作為有界域的體現。不可約有界對稱域包含四組典型域與兩個例外域。作為模型黎曼流形或者作為有趣的代數幾何及數論研究对象的參數空間，有界對稱域都顯得特別重要。若把有界對稱域視為黎曼流形，則從微分幾何的視角存在著特異的複子流形，即全純全測地子流形。若把有界對稱域視為某些代數幾何研究對象的分類空間，那麼這些特異子流形往往是其所構成的集合中具有特殊性質的一類元的分類空間。例如，若以 H(g)標記主極化阿貝爾簇的參數空間，即秩為g的西格爾上半平面， 那麼，它的必然是對稱流形的全測地複子流形有時對應於具有額外自同構環的子集合，即作為特殊子簇的志川流形。最近，由於與模空間(例如 A(g) = H(g)/Sp(g,Z)) 上的特殊點與特殊子簇的關係，有界對稱域的全純全測地複子流形已成為流行的研究題材。它們是數論專家與邏輯學的模型論專家所研究的弱特殊子簇，雖然他們的研究甚少牽涉到全測地的性質。對於關乎超越函數論與多複變函數論均為重要的研究課題，我們提出運用複微分幾何的方法去刻畫全純全測地複子流形。除此以外，我們還將會研究某些對偶空間上的齊次有理子流形上的特異子簇。我們的研究關係到全純全測地複子流形作為有界對稱域上擁有(包含在或許具有無限體積的商流形內的)有限體積商空間的代數子簇的刻畫，雙曲Ax-Lindemann 猜想的某種複解析的推廣，雙曲 Ax-Lindemann-Bloch-Ochiai 類的猜想，以及關於具有秩虧損的兩個不可約有界對稱域之間的逆緊全純映照之結構的一個猜想。

17304421.value: 隱含條件矩及其在時間序列分析的應用

17304421.label: Project Objectives
17304421.value: To propose a novel method to obtain the implied conditional moments of a time series. These implied conditional moments will be constructed based on the conditional quantiles by using the idea of Cornish-Fisher expansion. Depending on how the conditional quantiles are chosen, these implied conditional moments will be computed without specifying any parametric specifications on the conditional moments, but with the ability to include exogenous information and handle nonstationary data. To construct new tests to check the validity of the quantile estimation methods and the implied conditional moments. A new back test to check the validity of quantile estimation at multiple-quantile levels will be given, and its asymptotics will be established. Furthermore, new regression-based tests will be offered to examine the validity of implied conditional moments, and their usefulness will be assessed by simulation studies. To apply the implied conditional moments to various applications. First, the implied conditional mean and variance will be used to study the linear or nonlinear volatility-in-mean effect. Second, the implied conditional variance, skewness, and kurtosis will be utilized to explore the parametric or nonparametric ``news impact functions''. Third, the implied estimation method will be extended to the multivariate case, and new but simple regression-based tests to detect the volatility, skewness, and kurtosis spillover effects as well as the financial contagion will be provided.

17304421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17304421.value: Conditional moments play a central role in plenty of time series applications. Traditionally, their dynamics are captured by some parametric time series models. However, the assumed parametric models may be mis-specified, and their calculation may be demanding and unstable. This project aims to provide a new novel method to estimate conditional moments by the so-called implied conditional moments, which are proposed based on the conditional quantiles. The implied conditional moments are easy-to-implement, and they can show great generality to handle complex data structure depending on how the conditional quantiles are chosen. Moreover, this project aims to examine the importance of the implied conditional moments by a myriad of applications in risk management, asset pricing, and financial economics. The resulting methodologies could serve as useful tools for many empirical studies, leading to useful insights or advice to policy makers, market participants, or ordinary citizens. 條件矩在許多時間序列分析的應用中起著核心作用。傳統上，它們的動態結構由一些參數時間序列模型描述。但是，這些假定的參數模型可能會被錯誤指定，並且其計算可能要求苛刻且不穩定。本項目旨在提供一種新的基於條件分位數的隱含條件矩來估計條件矩。我們的隱含條件矩易於計算，且在處理復雜數據結構時具有很強的通用性。此外，該項目旨在通過大量的應用來檢驗隱含條件矩在風險管理、資產定價和金融經濟學中的重要性。此新方法有望作為許多實證研究的有效工具，繼而為政策製定者、市場參與者和普通公民提供有用的見解或結論。

17304421.label: Realisation of objectives
17304421.value: 1. My submitted paper Zhang and Zhu (2024) to Annals of Applied Statistics has achieved the Objective 1. In this paper, my co-author and I have proposed a novel quantiled conditional moment (QCM) method to estimate the conditional variance, skewness, and kurtosis from the estimated conditional quantiles. This QCM method adopts the idea of Cornish-Fisher expansion to construct a linear regression model, and it then simply and simultaneously computes the QCM estimators of the conditional variance, skewness, and kurtosis from the ordinary least squares estimator of this regression model. Under certain conditions, we have established the consistency of the proposed QCM estimators. Simulations have shown the good finite sample performances of the proposed QCM estimators. 2. My published paper Zhu (2023) in Journal of Econometrics, published paper Yang, Zhu, Li and Zhu (2024) in Journal of Business & Economic Statistics, and submitted paper Zhang and Zhu (2024) have achieved the Objective 2. In Zhu (2023), some dynamic quantile tests have been proposed to examine the validity of the quantile model. Under certain conditions, the limiting null distributions of these tests have been established. Simulations have been conducted to examine their finite sample performances. In addition, Yang, Zhu, Li and Zhu (2024) have given the procedure to assess the validity of the estimated conditional moments via the total and predictive R square as well as some quantile-based risk measures. Moreover, Zhang and Zhu (2024) have designed the regression-based tests to examine the validity of the estimated conditional moments. 3. My published paper Zhu, Zhang and Zhu (2024) in Journal of Empirical Finance, published paper Yang, Zhu, Li and Zhu (2024), submitted paper Zhu and Zhu (2024) to Management Science, and submitted paper Zhang and Zhu (2024) have achieved the Objective 3. In Zhu, Zhang and Zhu (2024), my co-authors and I have proposed a new graph-based conditional moments (GRACE) method to do portfolio selection based on thousands of stocks or even more. The GRACE method first learns the conditional quantiles and mean of stock returns via a factor-augmented temporal graph convolutional network, which is guided by the set of stock-to-stock relations as well as the set of factor-to-stock relations. Next, the GRACE method learns the conditional variance, skewness, and kurtosis of stock returns from the learned conditional quantiles via the QCM method. Finally, the GRACE method uses the learned conditional mean, variance, skewness, and kurtosis to construct several performance measures, which are criteria to sort the stocks to proceed the portfolio selection in the well-known 10-decile framework. An application to NASDAQ and NYSE stock markets have showed that the GRACE method performs much better than its competitors, particularly when the performance measures are comprised of conditional variance, skewness, and kurtosis. In Yang, Zhu, Li and Zhu (2024), my co-authors and I have proposed a new conditional quantile variational autoencoder (CQVAE) model for asset pricing in the realm of big return data. The key idea of the CQVAE model is to use a step distribution function to approximate the unknown conditional distribution of the return, where this step function depends on different conditional quantiles of the return. By assuming each conditional quantile has a factor structure with dynamic loadings, we have investigated those different conditional quantiles via a new CQVAE network, which contains a factor network to learn latent factors by the VAE, and adopts a beta network with “multi-head” structure to learn different beta functions (factor loadings). Moreover, we have provided a two-step estimation procedure for the CQVAE network, given some regularization implementations for practical use, and discussed an extension model with quantile-dependent latent factors. Finally, we have used our CQVAE asset pricing model to analyze a large 60-year US equity return dataset, and shown its advantages over benchmark models. In Zhu and Zhu (2024), my co-author and I have proposed a novel graph-based quantiled (GRAND) conditional covariance matrix (CCM) estimator in the spirit of “divide and conquer”. By extracting information from the extensive asset features, the GRAND method leverages a new graph-based deep learning network, called the self-grouping autoencoder (SGA), to learn the conditional quantiles of returns. Using those learned conditional quantiles, the GRAND method further learns (co)variances of CCM element-wisely via the QCM method, and finally, it makes the resulting assembled CCM estimator positive semidefinite through a projection. From an extensive empirical analysis of the Chinese stock market, we have showed that the GRAND method can produce much better tangency portfolios than its competitors, and provide dynamic causal graphs to study variance and quantile connectedness of all stocks for interpreting the systemic risk. In Zhang and Zhu (2024), my co-author and I have applied the QCM method to check the form of the “news impact curve” functions for conditional variance, skewness, and kurtosis. Based on the QCM estimators, we have found that during the COVID-19 pandemic outbreak, the existing forms of “news impact curve” functions for the conditional skewness and kurtosis are unsuitable, whereas those for the conditional variance are acceptable for most examined exchange rates data.

17304421.label: Major findings and research outcome
17304421.value: This project has delivered 10 published papers and 2 submitted papers, including 1 published paper in Journal of the American Statistical Association (JASA), 1 published paper in Journal of Econometrics (JoE), 2 published papers in Journal of Business & Economic Statistics (JBES), 1 published paper in Journal of Empirical Finance (JEF), 1 published paper in Journal of Agricultural, Biological, and Environmental Statistics (JABES), 2 published papers in Statistica Sinica (SS), 2 published papers in Journal of Time Series Analysis (JTSA), 1 submitted paper to Annals of Applied Statistics (AOAS), and 1 submitted paper to Management Science (MS). For this project, the first major research outcome is from my submitted paper Zhang and Zhu (2024, AOAS). In this paper, the QCM method has been demonstrated with three interesting features: First, it allows for biased estimated conditional quantiles to deliver the consistent estimators of conditional moments; Second, it does not need to do any modelling for the conditional mean; Third, it is a supervised learning procedure without assuming any distribution on the data, so it has a substantially computational advantage to learn conditional moments for high-dimensional data. For this project, the second major research outcome is from my two published papers Zhu, Zhang and Zhu (2024, JEF) and Yang, Zhu, Li and Zhu (2024, JBES) as well as one submitted paper Zhu and Zhu (2024, MS). In Zhu, Zhang and Zhu (2024), the GRACE method has demonstrated its capacity to estimate conditional variance, skewness, and kurtosis of high-dimensional stock returns, so the big portfolios under four related performance measures can be constructed from thousands of stocks or even more. In Yang, Zhu, Li and Zhu (2024), the proposed CQVAE network allows asset characteristics to determine the structure of quantile-independent latent factors and quantile-dependent factor loadings, so it provides us a new way to do dimension reduction across quantile levels guided by observed covariates. Its advantage in portfolio selection has been illustrated in a large 60-year US equity return dataset. In Zhu and Zhu (2024), the GRAND method is showed to be blessing dimensionality for learning the CCM. This is because the GRAND method benefits by extracting information from the extensive asset features and exploring the causal relationships among all considered assets via the newly proposed self-grouping autoencoder (SGA), while it is computationally feasible due to the “divide and conquer” learning spirit and the used QCM method for estimating conditional variances. Owing to the financial support from this project, I also have many other interesting research outcomes in my other published papers. In Zhou, Jiang, Zhu and Li (2022, SS) and Jiang, Li, Li and Zhu (2023, SS), we have provided new statistical tools to study matrix time series. In Liu, Zhu and Zhu (2022, JTSA), we have proposed a new zero-one-inflated bounded Poisson distribution to study the normalcy-dominant ordinal time series. In Luo, Zhu, Gong and Li (2023, JBES), we have constructed new KSD tests to check error distributions in multivariate time series models. In Yu, Li, Jiang and Zhu (2024, JASA), we have proposed a new matrix GARCH model. In Zhang, Yu and Zhu (2024, JABES), we have raised a new framework of inverse difference-in-differences to study the effects of the “2+26” policy launched by the Chinese government. In Song, Jiang and Zhu (2024, JTSA), we have formed a new estimation method based on martingale difference divergence to study multivariate time series.

17304421.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17304421.value: Rooting in the current outputs from this project, I expect more QCM-related empirical research developments in future. For example, one of my on-going projects is to apply the QCM method to find synergistic formulaic alphas in finance. In this project, we reconsider the discovery of synergistic formulaic alphas from the viewpoint of sequential decision-making, and conceptualize the entire alpha discovery process as a non-stationary and reward-sparse Markov decision process. To overcome the challenges of non-stationarity and reward-sparsity, we propose the AlphaQCM method, a novel distributional reinforcement learning method designed to search for synergistic formulaic alphas efficiently. The AlphaQCM method first learns the Q function and quantiles via a Q network and a quantile network, respectively. Then, the AlphaQCM method applies the QCM method to learn unbiased variance from the potentially biased quantiles. Guided by the learned Q function and variance, the AlphaQCM method navigates the non-stationarity and reward-sparsity to explore the vast search space of formulaic alphas with high efficacy. Empirical applications to real-world datasets demonstrate that our AlphaQCM method significantly outperforms its competitors, particularly when dealing with large datasets comprising numerous stocks.

17304421.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17304421.value: How to learn the conditional variance, skewness, and kurtosis is very important in many financial applications. However, the existing methods towards this goal have two big issues: the risk of model mis-specification and the instability of model estimation, especially for the high-dimensional data. The proposed QCM method in this project overcomes the aforementioned issues. Moreover, the QCM method has been shown to be very useful in factor analysis (via the CQCAE model), large portfolio selection (via the GRACE method), and large CCM matrices learning (via the GRAND method). We could expect more useful empirical studies generated from the QCM method in future.

17304821.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17304821.value: A star wandering too close to the supermassive black hole in the center of a galaxy can be torn apart by the tidal force, producing a tidal disruption event (TDE). As the stellar debris accretes onto the black hole, a very bright flare is emitted, illuminating the previously dormant black hole. Therefore, it has long been proposed that TDEs can be used to probe the demographics of quiescent supermassive black holes. TDEs are predicted to happen in about every ten thousand years in one galaxy. So far, we have observed several dozens of TDEs mainly from all-sky transient surveys. The observed TDE rate, however, is about ten times lower than the predicted rate. The distribution of the host black hole mass also has some mismatch with the theoretical prediction. We propose that such discrepancies between TDE theory and observation can be largely explained with the new understanding of the stellar debris circularization / disk formation process. In the classical picture of TDEs, the debris quickly assembles a compact disk after returning to the vicinity of the black hole. The disk has a short inflow timescale, and its luminosity rises in months and then decays for a few years following a characteristic pattern. Recent hydrodynamical simulations, however, show that the stellar debris needs to lose orbital energy via collisions due to self-crossing, and such collisions are sometimes too weak to quickly “circularize” the debris. Such new findings challenge the classical picture that all TDEs can produce prompt, bright flares detectable by flux-limited transient surveys. Therefore, we propose to close the gap by performing a comprehensive, quantitative study addressing in which parameter space TDEs tend to have slow circularization / weak flares. Previously the PI has done first-order calculations on how the black hole mass and the stellar orbital parameter affect the TDE debris stream self-crossing radius and collision power. The PI has also used a rigorous general-relativistic ray-tracing code to study how black hole spin delays debris stream self-crossing. Furthermore, the PI and the team have conducted one of the best studies on TDE rates. We will apply all these repertoire built through previous studies to tackle this project. In the next few years, several ongoing and upcoming transient surveys will allow us to detect thousands of TDEs. 17304821.label: Realisation of objectives
17304821.value: The topic of study for this project is tidal disruption events (TDEs), in which stars wandering too close to the supermassive black hole in the center of a galaxy get torn apart by the tidal force exerted by the black hole. The focus of this project is to study how the rates of such events are affected by the TDE disk circularization physics, namely the stream self-crossing process (Objective 1). In particular, we want to understand the discrepancy between the theoretically predicted rates and the observed rates. The TDE circularization process can be largely determined by a few key parameters such as the mass and spin of the black hole and the properties of the disrupted star. Therefore, advancing our understanding of such processes will also help us probe the mass and spin distribution of massive black holes from TDE observations (Objective 2). This is a fundamentally important topic in astronomy and astrophysics. Objective 1 has been fully realized as we produced the first work on incorporating the effects of TDE debris disk circularization into the calculation of the observed TDE rates and demographics. Our work also naturally produces a solution to the discrepancy between the observed / theoretically expected TDE rates and distribution. Objective 2 has also been fully addressed as we have extensively explored how to use the observed TDE rates and properties to constrain the black hole parameters and demographics. In particular, we have also extended our methodology to the early universe and studied how to use TDEs to explore black holes and stellar populations in the early universe. We have also made extensions of the original research goals and explored how the rates of TDEs, coupled with gravitational lensing, can allow us to study black hole parameters. We will discuss these findings in detail in Section 6.1. In summary, all the objectives set out in this proposal have been successfully achieved.

17304821.label: Major findings and research outcome
17304821.value: Paper publication: In total 8 journal papers have been published on top journals including Nature Astronomy, The Astrophysical Journal Letters, etc. Two more papers are under review. We list the major findings briefly as below. In Publication 1, 5, 6, 8, we computed the rates of TDEs with the consideration of black hole parameters, galaxy structures and, very importantly, TDE physics such as the debris circularization process. We found that the debris circularization process can largely suppress the rates of TDEs from smaller black holes, as the general relativistic effects are weaker in such TDEs and the debris loses energy less efficiently through self-crossings. As a result, the overall rates of TDEs should be much lower than the previously theoretically expected rate. We also solved the important question on why the observed TDE mass distribution peaks around 10^6 solar masses, instead of leaning towards smaller black holes. In Publication 2, 3, 4, 9, we focused on studying how to use TDE observables to probe the parameters of black holes. For example, in a paper published on Nature Astronomy with the PI as one of the two corresponding authors, we showed that the optical polarization properties observed in TDEs proves the existence of a super-Eddington funnel. The production of such gas structures means that TDE debris must have circularzed efficiently in order to achieve a super-Eddington accretion rate. Similar results have been shown in Publication 9, a paper currently under review at Science. Furthermore, beyond the original objectives, we have further explored how the rates of TDEs can allow us to study black hole parameters when coupled with the technique of gravitational lensing. The results are in Publication 7 and 10. Conference talks: The PI has been invited to give a few review talks at the international conferences including the “European Astronomical Society Annual Meeting” (online 2021, the largest European meeting in astronomy and astrophysics), 15th Asia Pacific Physics Conference (online 2022), The 60th Anniversary of X-Ray Astronomy: X-ray Astronomy in the Time-domain & Multi-messenger Era (online 2022), The 32nd Texas Symposium on Relativistic Astrophysics (China 2023, the largest international meeting in high-energy astrophysics), “X-ray Quasi-Periodic Eruptions & Repeating Nuclear Transients” (Spain 2025), etc. Some of the results obtained from this project so far have been broadcasted in these talks. Student training: 2 students have been trained through this project, including Thomsen (PhD graduated), Thomas Wong (MPhil graduated). All students have published papers on top astronomy journals and delivered talks at international conferences based on the results obtained through this project.

17304821.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17304821.value: We plan to continue to explore how to use TDE rates to explore important topics such as galaxy structure and evolution, galaxies and black hole in the early universe, etc. The methodology and skills developed in this work will be very helpful for these future projects.

17304821.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17304821.value: In tidal disruption events (TDEs), stars wandering too close to the big black holes in centers of galaxies are torn apart by the tidal force from the black hole. The rates of these transient events are important for helping us probe the massive black hole population and their host galaxies. In this project we study how TDE rates can be affected by important physics in these events. By correcting these effects, we can learn how to recover the true black hole parameter distributions from TDEs.

17304921.label: Project Objectives
17304921.value: Propose a hybrid deep learning Markov Chain approximation approach to study the optimal insurance strategies. Optimal insurance strategies have been studied by many scholars and there is a huge amount literature on the topic. It is natural that in order to obtain closed form or analytical solutions, we need to use a simple model and/or some mathematical assumptions. There are various numerical methods proposed recently, however, when the control variables are many, the computation becomes problematic. Deep learning approach provides a way to overcome the issue. In this project we will focus on how to build a bridge between the traditional numerical and analytical methods and the deep learning approaches. We will consider various optimal insurance strategies including optimal dividend, optimal reinsurance, optimal investment and optimal financing. First, we will formulate the surplus process in a generalized way. Control variables such as reinsurance, investment, and dividend strategies will be described in this process. Then a specific objective function which represents the decision maker’s goal will be provided. The decision-maker will choose optimal strategies taking into account specific goals such as minimizing the risks of financial ruin, maximizing the benefit of the stakeholders, etc. We will adopt the most recent popular deep learning technologies to tackle the optimization problems. Under very general assumptions such as the convexity of the objective function, we can build deep neural networks to approximate the optimal controls directly and optimize a family of parametrized controls. Provide effective computation approaches for the optimal controls which incorporates ideas from deep learning. Comparing with the existing numerical methods on stochastic control problems, our proposed hybrid deep learning algorithm has two main advantages. First, the introduction of a hybrid deep learning framework enables us to improve the computation efficiency by using the two-scale numerical method. As it is well known, it is inevitable that one faces the problem of “curse of dimensionality” that the computation nodes grows exponentially when dealing with optimization problems with multiple control variables and states. Now we replace the optimization over the piecewise control grid for every state value by finding optimal parameters of neural networks for all state values. By using the stochastic approximation to calculate the optimum, the number of computation nodes increases linearly with respect to the number of points in the state lattice. In addition, the coarse-scale Markov chain approximation provides an initial value. Hence the computation efficiency for optimal controls can be largely improved. Second, the accuracy of numerical results can be improved by the developed algorithm. Traditional approximation methods generally use piecewise constant controls to approximate the optimal control. The accuracy of control strategy is subject to the denseness of the grid. On the contrary, neural networks allow the control strategy to take values in continuous range and will easily conquer the difficulty of effectively selecting the accuracy in control spaces with significant different scales. Obtain rigorous mathematical convergence analysis and rate of convergence. We will show that the approximating neural networks proposed in this project are proved to converge weekly to the optimal controls. The analysis of convergence rate will be investigated. Highlight some idea and methods which makes the theoretical results useful when we use big data, analytics, and deep learning to deal with actuarial science and insurance problems. Unlike in the literature, when we deal with insurance risk model, we assume a simple mathematical model and mathematical (probability) techniques are used to obtain analytical results for optimal investment, reinsurance and/or financing strategies. In this project, we shall use an empirical approach and the method will be data driving, but we still keep certain mathematical structure, and the analytical results and methods will be combined with data approach to obtain desired results. Back-test our approaches using real data and real problems. We shall use data to back-test our methods. Real world data will be applied in the deep learning algorithm when available. If there is insufficient real data, we will generate sufficient simulated samples by using quasi Monte Carlo method with filtered parameters from limited data set.

17304921.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17304921.value: In our previous work, we have investigated various models and considered various kind optimal insurance problems, such as, optimal investment, optimal dividend, optimal reinsurance and optimal financing policies. We have obtained a lot of considerable interesting results. In this project, we shall use a hybrid deep learning Markov chain approximation approach to tackle the optimal insurance policies. Our research will shed light on the applications of AI and big data analytics to actuarial science research. Markov chain approximation is a classical method to solve stochastic control problems numerically and is also applied to problems on optimal insurance strategies. A well-known drawback of the method is that when the dimensions of state variables, or the number of control variables is large, the computation becomes difficult and even impossible. In two of our recent papers, we propose a Markov chain approximation and stochastic approximation-based iterative deep learning algorithm to study problems of optimal insurance strategies. Approximations of the optimal controls are obtained by using deep neural networks. The framework of Markov chain approximation plays a key role in building iterative algorithms and finding initial values. Stochastic approximation is used to search for the optimal parameters of neural networks in a bounded region determined by the Markov chain approximation method. The convergence of the algorithm and the rate of convergence has been investigated. The proposed hybrid deep learning method has its advantages in both computation efficiency and accuracy comparing with the classical Markov chain approximation method. The methods in the two papers provide us the foundation for this proposal. We shall further extend the methods and idea there and consider more complex and realistic models in this proposal. Our model can include various control variables, such as dividend, investment, reinsurance and refinancing. Different assumptions on the control variables will lead to a regular control, singular control or impulse control. We shall implement this self-learning approach to approximate the optimal strategies and compare the learning results with existing analytical solutions. Numerical examples will be used to illustrate the idea and computation efficiency and accuracy. The research of this project will provide a new research direction, by building a bridge between the theoretical (or existing) results and the recent AI and big data approaches, considerable interesting results can be expected. We expect that outcomes of this project will have significant impact on insurance industry and actuarial education in the future. 在我們之前的工作中，我們研究了各種模型並考慮了各種類型最優保險問題, 如最優投資、最優分紅、最優再保險和最佳融資策略。我們獲得了很多有趣的結果。在這個項目中，我們將使用混合深度學習馬爾可夫鏈近似方法解決最優保險策略問題。我們的研究將对人工智能和大數據分析在精算科學研究中的應用有帮助。馬爾可夫鏈近似是解決隨機控制問題的經典數值方法，也適用於最優保險策略的問題。該方法的一個眾所周知的缺點是，當狀態變量的維數，或控制變量數多，計算難度大，甚至不可能的。在我們最近的兩篇論文中，我們提出了馬爾可夫鏈近似和基於隨機逼近的迭代深度學習算法研究最佳保險策略問題。最優控制的近似值使用深度神經網絡獲得。馬爾可夫鏈逼近的框架在構建迭代算法和尋找初始值方面起關鍵作用。隨機近似用於在有界區域內搜索神經網絡的最優參數。擬議的混合深學習方法在計算效率和準確性上都有其優勢與經典的馬爾可夫鏈近似方法比較。這兩篇論文中的方法為我們提供了這個項目的基礎。我們應該進一步擴展那裡的方法和想法，並考慮更複雜和現實的的模型。我們的模型可以包括各種控制變量，例如分紅、投資、再保險和再融資。對控制的不同假設變量將導致規則控制、單一控製或脈衝控制。我們應該實施這種深度學習方法來近似最優策略和將學習結果與現有的分析解決方案進行比較。數值例子將用於說明思想和計算效率和準確性。該項目的研究將提供一個新的研究方向，通過搭建理論（或現有）結果與最近的人工智能和大數據方法之間的橋樑，可以預期相當有趣的結果。我們期望這個項目的結果未來將對保險業和精算教育產生重大影響。

17304921.label: Realisation of objectives
17304921.value: We have addressed all objectives of this project and obtained satisfactory results. One paper using deep learning to detect insurance fraud has been published in a top actuarial/insurance journal (Journal of Risk and Insurance). This paper provides a method to help the insurance industry to detect insurance fraud using an unsupervised deep learning approach. The method proposed in the paper is practically useful. The paper uses three real data sets to test our approach and the results are very satisfactory. We recently completed another paper on optimal dividend and reinsurance using the hybrid deep learning Markov Chain approximation approach. We tested our approach using some examples and the results are very good. We also provided rigorous mathematical convergence analysis and the rate of convergence. The paper is under review in a top actuarial science journal now. We have also a paper on the optimal pension fund submitted for publication. We are working on another paper that deals with the optimal insurance portfolio strategy when the portfolio contains risk-free assets, risky assets, and equity-linked insurance products using a reinforcement deep learning Markov chain approximation approach. The paper develops a novel approach to deal with the portfolio optimization problem. the paper also contains numerical examples and convergence and convergence rate analysis. We are now working on another paper that considers an optimal dividend reinsurance problem. We assume that the company can control the dividend policy and that the dividend can be paid at any time according to an optimal strategy, but the reinsurance strategy cannot be updated continuously (as in real life, the reinsurance contract cannot be changed before it expires or reissue). This problem is mathematically challenging as it is a stochastic control problem with mixture controls (one control variable is continuous time and the other one is discrete time). We have obtained some interesting results in some simplified cases. We have also some other related working papers. The PI has presented 4 papers on the themes of this project at international conferences and three of them were keynote/plenary speeches, which the PI has acknowledged the support from this grant. The PI has also presented 3 papers on the themes of this project and acknowledged the grant in three universities.

We currently have three papers submitted for publication, and we also have three working papers on the topic of this project. We have obtained very satisfactory results and all the objectives of the project have been addressed carefully. The PI has presented 4 papers on the themes of this project at international conferences and three of them were keynote/plenary speeches, which the PI has acknowledged the support from this grant. The PI has also presented 3 papers on the themes of this project and acknowledged the grant in three universities.

17304921.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17304921.value: The approach we developed in this project has very broad applications and can be used to solve many problems in actuarial science and related subjects. We are now working on using the reinforcement learning Markov approximation approach to solve an asset allocation problem by considering the portfolio with equity-linked insurance products. The reinforcement learning approach should be able to solve more complex asset allocation problems. Another future research direction/problem is the problem involving continuous time models with both continuous and discrete control variables. This is a mathematically challenging problem and the study of this problem has the potential of developing some interesting mathematical methodologies which can be used to solve many related problems.

17304921.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17304921.value: In this project, we have developed a novel approach: deep learning Markov Chain approximation approach. This approach has been used to solve some important problems in actuarial science. Our approach combines the AI/big data idea/method with the well-known numerical method: Markov Chain approximation. The advantages of our approach are we can obtain more accurate results meanwhile, our proposed method can also handle the curse of dimensionality from which existing numerical methods are suffering. As AI and big data have become more and more important these days, we expect our research will simulate and bring some light to the study of actuarial science problems using AI/big data approaches.

17305321.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17305321.value: 落葉樹的葉片物候，包括葉片展葉、成熟、老化和休眠的季節性節律，對於調控森林生態系統的光合作用和營養循環至關重要。在過去的幾十年裡，越來越多的證據表明落葉樹的葉片物候對於氣候變化極其敏感，且不同植物物種的葉片物候對同一氣候變化的敏感性響應存在很大的差異性。儘管改進個體水平葉片物候變異的監測和理解被認為對於預測未來森林生態系統的組成和功能極為關鍵，但目前仍有兩個問題亟待解決。第一，有效且準確的手段來幫助實現大範圍個體水平的葉片物候監測仍然匱乏，因為以往基於地面/近地面/衛星的方法要么囿限於狹小的空間範圍，要么只能監測生態系統尺度而非個體水平的葉片物候。第二，對氣候以及關鍵植物功能性狀如何調控從個體到生態系統尺度的物候變異仍然缺乏全面的理解和評估。 為了解決上述問題，我們在此提出了一個綜合多種手段的研究方法。這種方法包含如下三個部分：1）依託我國從南到北的森林塔吊站點進行植物功能性狀和氣候因子監測，2）借助多尺度遙感平台（含物候相機、無人機、地面LiDAR和高分辨率衛星）刻畫個體水平的葉片物候和樹冠結構參數，以及3）基於上述數據進行統計建模和相關的假設檢驗。具體而言，我們首先將評估結合前沿的高分辨率PlanetScope衛星數據（3米空間分辨率和1天的重訪週期）與近地面無人機調查可否幫助在個體和生態系統水平上實現對葉片物候的準確、高效監測。其次，我們擬結合近地面/PlanetScope衛星得到物候數據以及地表觀測得到的氣候因子、植物冠層參數和植物功能性狀，分析站點內部的微觀氣候、植物功能性狀以及站點之間的宏觀氣候對森林內部以及森林之間葉片物候的調控。通過這種更為綜合的分析方法，我們旨在改進植物葉片物候從個體到生態系統水平的監測和機理理解，從而幫助更好地建模森林生態系統對氣候變化的響應。

17305321.label: Realisation of objectives
17305321.value: This project combines field and remote sensing data with statistical and process-based modeling to address three key objectives. Originally planned field campaigns in Mainland China for 2022 were halted by the global pandemic. We adapted by using multi-scale datasets from NEON (National Ecological Observatory Network) and PEP725 (Pan European Phenology Network), which matched the type and quality of the proposed data, ensuring the project’s objectives were achieved without compromising scientific rigor. The following sections outline methods, analyses, and results, underscoring the project’s success despite logistical challenges. Objective 1 was fully achieved, with results published in Remote Sensing of Environment (Zhao et al. 2022) and ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing (Song et al. 2022). The original plan to collect multi‑scale data at two sites in Mainland China in 2022 was halted by pandemic restrictions. We adapted by using NEON data, which integrate ground, phenocams, airborne (hyperspectral, LiDAR, RGB), and satellite data across diverse forest ecosystems, meeting all requirements for Objective 1. Our goal was to develop and validate a PlanetScope‑based method for monitoring deciduous leaf phenology from crowns to forest stands, yet existing methods often lack fine‑scale capacity. PlanetScope’s 3m resolution and near‑daily coverage offer a bridge between field data and broad‑scale monitoring, though its performance was untested. At six NEON sites in eastern North America, we integrated 0.1m airborne imagery and ground observations with PlanetScope time series. Crown‑level phenology metrics were aligned with field observations and evaluated across trees, species, and sites. Results showed PlanetScope (1) detected substantial individual‑tree variability (r=0.94 for spring MOS; r=0.83 for fall MOF), though accuracy fell when site‑climate effects were removed (r=0.42; r=0.39); (2) achieved higher species-level accuracy (r=0.76; r=0.82), likely due to reduced pixel/georeferencing errors; and (3) produced spatially explicit maps linking phenology variability to topography and traits. Overall, PlanetScope is promising for species‑level monitoring, though its resolution limits precise individual‑tree tracking (Zhao et al., 2022). To address resolution limits, we developed a high‑resolution approach using phenocam imagery and a deep learning model, i.e., the superpixel‑based Residual Network‑50 (SP‑ResNet50), for automated crown‑level monitoring across varied sites and camera systems. Using one year of data from six phenocams in two Panamanian forests, we built a library of leaf/non‑leaf pixels for training/testing. SP‑ResNet50 achieved 93% accuracy, performed robustly across evaluation levels, and quantified leaf phenology from crowns to ecosystems (Song et al., 2022). Collectively, Objective 1 delivered two complementary tools: PlanetScope for species‑level, broad‑scale monitoring, and deep learning–enhanced phenocam analysis for crown‑level detail. Together, they provide scalable pathways for linking fine‑scale phenological variability to ecosystem processes. Objective 2 was fully achieved, with results published in New Phytologist (Zhao et al. 2024, 2025; Wang et al., 2024) and Remote Sensing of Environment (Liu et al. 2023, 2024). Building on fine‑scale phenology mapping, we examined how abiotic (e.g., microclimate) and biotic (e.g., plant traits) factors shape phenological variability under comparable macro‑climatic conditions. Two approaches were used: (1) flat landscapes with minimal topographic variation to isolate biotic influences; (2) a subtropical forest plot with detailed micro‑environment, trait, and phenology data to assess combined drivers. At four NEON sites (8×8 km each) with negligible topography, we integrated satellite phenology maps, airborne hyperspectral imagery (foliar traits), LiDAR data (canopy structure), and USGS NLCD land‑cover data, standardized to 30m resolution. Results showed that biotic variables strongly influence phenology, with canopy height, plant area, and leaf-mass-per-area as dominant drivers. Trait–phenology relationships held for both multi‑year averages (Zhao et al., 2024) and interannual variability, the latter linked to ecosystem productivity stability (Zhao et al., 2025), underscoring the central role of traits in modeling deciduous forest responses to climate change. We also examined a 50‑ha plot at Heishiding Provincial Nature Reserve (ForestGEO network, China), linking PlanetScope‑derived phenological diversity to above‑ground biomass (AGB) via structural equation modeling (SEM). Results showed that both micro‑environmental and biotic factors shaped diversity; AGB correlated positively with diversity, but the relationship became non‑significant in SEM when accounting for driver interactions (Wang et al., 2024). Given challenges in collecting large‑scale trait data, Liu et al. (2023) demonstrated drone‑based hyperspectral imaging for high‑throughput crown‑scale trait monitoring, including physiological traits key to interpreting species‑specific variability. This approach was extended to Sentinel‑2 imagery, mapping 14 foliar traits at 10 m resolution from public satellite data (Liu et al., 2024). Collectively, Objective 2 advances understanding of phenology drivers, establishes scalable trait mapping from drones to satellites, and lays a foundation for future continental‑scale studies linking climate, traits, phenology, ecosystem function, and resilience, offering essential guidance for forest conservation and restoration under climate change. Objective 3 was fully achieved, with results published in Remote Sensing of Environment (Gu et al. 2023), New Phytologist (Gu et al. 2025a), and Methods in Ecology & Evolution (Gu et al. 2025b). Given limited availability of large‑scale trait datasets (see Objective 2), we examined macroclimate–phenology relationships via two approaches: (1) empirical evaluation of macroclimatic drivers, and (2) mechanistic refinement of spring phenology models. We assessed existing process‑based models using phenocam and satellite data from hundreds of U.S. forest sites. Results showed that current models systematically under‑represent solar radiation constraints (Gu et al., 2023). Extending analyses to the Northern Hemisphere revealed similar patterns across temperate forests, alongside pronounced water‑stress constraints in temperate grasslands (Gu et al., 2025a). These findings highlight solar radiation and water availability as key determinants of early‑season photosynthetic capacity, suggesting spring phenology reflects adaptive strategies to maximize carbon gain while minimizing frost risk. We then refined the optimality (OPT) framework, which models leaf‑out timing as a trade‑off between photosynthesis gain and chilling risk, by embedding a coupled Farquhar–Medlyn photosynthesis model. The new R‑OPT model, tested on PEP725 data (409,144 site–species–year records across Europe), consistently outperformed standard OPT and non‑optimality models. Accuracy gains were greatest in lowland, moist environments, with limits in high‑altitude, dry regions due to incomplete representation of constraints on carbon gain (Gu et al., 2025b). By explicitly incorporating solar radiation and water‑stress effects, the R‑OPT framework strengthens climate–physiology linkages and improves predictive capacity under climate change. While large‑scale trait data remain scarce, emerging drone‑ and satellite‑based trait mapping (Liu et al., 2023, 2024) will enable future climate–trait–phenology studies. Ongoing research led by Dr. Ying Zhao will expand this integration, with targeted submission in June 2026.

17305321.label: Major findings and research outcome
17305321.value: Accurate monitoring and modeling of forest leaf phenology are vital for predicting seasonal carbon and water fluxes and assessing ecosystem resilience under climate change. However, fine-scale satellite monitoring and mechanistic understanding of phenology drivers remain limited. This project integrated multi-scale remote sensing, field observations, and process-based modeling to address three objectives: (1) develop and validate fine-scale phenology monitoring methods; (2) identify microclimate–trait–phenology linkages within forests; and (3) assess macroclimate–phenology associations and improve model representation. Our research yielded three key findings: 1) innovative monitoring tools–Using NEON datasets, we validated 3m PlanetScope satellites for species-level phenology mapping, achieving strong agreement with ground-based tree-crown measurements. A complementary deep learning phenocam method (SP–ResNet50) achieved 93% accuracy in crown-level phenology monitoring across diverse forests. Together, these enable scalable phenology mapping from individual crowns to landscapes; 2) Biotic trait controls–At four NEON sites with minimal topographic variation, plant traits consistently regulated fine-scale phenology patterns across space and interannual climatic variability. In a subtropical ForestGEO plot, phenological diversity was also shaped by fine-scale microenvironmental variability alongside key trait influences; 3) Macroclimate drivers and modeling advances–Across the Northern Hemisphere, existing spring phenology models substantially underrepresented solar radiation and water stress constraints, likely because spring phenology reflects adaptive strategies to maximize carbon gain while minimizing frost risk. Incorporating a mechanistic photosynthesis model into the optimality principle framework produced the R–OPT model, which strengthens climate–physiology linkages and improves predictive capacity under climate change. Collectively, the project delivered scalable phenology and trait monitoring methods, clarified biotic and abiotic drivers from local to landscape scales, and improved process based models. These outcomes provide a robust foundation for forecasting forest ecosystem responses to climate change and for future continental scale climate–trait–phenology studies. Throughout the project’s implementation, we provided high quality research training to three PhD students (Yingyi Zhao, Yating Gu, and Shuwen Liu) and one postdoctoral researcher (Jing Wang). Dr. Wang is now an Associate Professor at Sun Yat sen University and a rising star in the ecological remote sensing field. Drs. Zhao, Gu, and Liu all graduated with excellence (top 10% at HKU). This project also produced fruitful research outcomes, with ten papers published in well regarded journals (details are shown in Section 5.3).

17305321.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17305321.value: The project has delivered accurate, scalable methods for fine scale phenology monitoring, clarified biotic and abiotic drivers within forests, and advanced macroclimate based phenology modelling. These achievements provide a strong foundation for next‑stage research explicitly linking climate, plant traits, and phenological sensitivity across spatial scales. A key opportunity lies in integrating our newly developed large‑scale trait datasets (Liu et al., 2023, 2024) into macroclimate–phenology analyses, enabling mechanistic pathways from climate → traits → phenology → ecosystem function to be quantified. This will support continental‑scale assessments of forest resilience and productivity under climate change, with direct applications in conservation planning and restoration prioritisation. Future work will focus on: (1) enhancing process‑based models (e.g., R‑OPT) by incorporating high‑resolution trait, radiation, and water‑stress data; and (2) extending analyses to under‑represented forest types, including tropical and boreal systems. Strategic collaborations with global networks (e.g., NEON, ForestGEO, PEP725) will maximise data coverage and methodological transferability.

17305321.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17305321.value: Forests play a crucial role in storing carbon, regulating water, and supporting biodiversity, but understanding exactly when trees grow new leaves or shed them, known as leaf phenology, is essential for predicting how forests respond to climate change. This project combined satellite data, ground observations, and computer models to better track and explain these seasonal changes. We developed new tools that can monitor leaf changes at both the individual tree and landscape level, using high-resolution satellite images and advanced camera-based AI methods with high accuracy. We discovered that tree characteristics, such as leaf and wood traits, strongly influence leaf timing, and that local microclimates also play a role. We also discovered that sunlight and water availability play bigger roles in leaf timing than many existing models assume, and improved these models to make them more accurate. These advances make it possible to forecast how forests will respond to shifting climates more accurately, helping guide conservation and climate adaptation strategies. The project also trained outstanding young scientists and produced ten high-quality publications, strengthening both scientific understanding and research capacity in ecological remote sensing.

17305521.label: Project Objectives
17305521.value: The long-term goal is to develop new, proprietary classes of metal-organic compounds of earth abundant metals having practical applications in materials science and organic synthesis. The approach is by design and combination of multi-dentate chelating ligands and metal ions to overcome the fast non-radiative decays and slow radiative decays of the excited states as well as to boost up the stability of base metal-organic compounds. In this proposal, we plan to develop the photochemistry and photo-physics of new classes of metal-organic compounds of Bi, Ni and Cu, and to perform application studies. Specific objectives are: [1] To prepare stable, luminescent Bi(III) complexes by using hexa-dentate chelating ligands and to examine their photo-physics/excited state properties. The hexa-dentate ligand scaffold has three bidentate chelating units containing N, O, and /C donor atoms. To increase the radiative decay rates, we plan to develop stable Bi(III)-TADF emitters by installing donor-acceptor substituents to the bidentate chelating units. The feasibility of luminescent bismuth(III) compounds as photo-sensitizers for visible light redox catalysts will be examined. [2] To develop stable, luminescent di-and poly-nuclear Cu(I) complexes using bridging N-heterocyclic carbene ligands. These Cu(I) complexes are designed to have long-lived 3MMLCT excited states and with vacant coordination sites for photochemical C-X bond activation. We envision the photochemistry and photo-catalysis of dinuclear [Cu(I)]2 photo-catalysts to be as versatile as [Au2(diphosphine)2]2+ that has been well documented in literatures to have practical uses in organic synthesis upon blue LED light irradiation. [3] To develop the photo-chemistry of Ni(II) complexes. The initial focus is on pincer Ni(II)-NHC complexes which has been shown by us to behave similarly as its cyclometalated Pt(II) analogues in visible-light-driven C-C bond formation reactions. [4] To further develop luminescent d0 metal emitters/TADF emitters of earth abundant metals. The initial focus to expand the scope of luminescent W(VI) complexes described in earlier works and to develop photo-chemically active V(V)=O systems for C-X activation.

17305521.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17305521.value: 光功能化合物/金属配合物是诸如光氧化还原催化、有机显示技术和发光传感等领域的基石，所有这些都引起学术界和工业界的广泛兴趣。该领域的重要发展在很大程度上依赖于我们通过优雅的分子设计来理解、掌控金属有机化合物激发态动力学的能力。一直以来，一个关键的关注点就是三重激发态，其很容易通过配合物中存在的金属离子自旋-轨道耦合获得。目前，广泛应用的发光金属络合物及其技术多基于贵金属铱和铂，很遗憾，这两种金属的地球丰度都非常低。基于可持续发展和增长的需要，采用地球蕴量丰富的金属（例如本计划中提及的金属）来替代这些贵金属则显得至关重要。这需要新的策略和创新研究来开发稳定的、具有与目前广泛使用的Ir(III)发光体/光催化剂相当性能的廉价金属发光金属配合物/光催化剂。本研究计划是基于本项目主持人最近的一项倡议，旨在开发基于地球蕴量丰富金属、可在实际应用中媲美广泛研究/使用的金和铂光发射体和光催化剂的新型光功能材料和催化剂。本研究计划基于主持人团队的研究成果，其显著特征包括具有 C 和 N 供体原子的新型多齿螯合配体，可显著提高所得廉价金属配合物（包括铋、镍、铜和铁）的稳定性、光致发光和光催化活性。选择六齿配体可显著抑制普通六配位金属配合物的非辐射衰减，并可通过热激活延迟荧光增加辐射衰减率。双成核/多成核N-杂环卡宾配体可用于开发稳定、发光的多核 d10 金属光催化剂。该类催化剂具有空配位点，可捕获自由基中间体，生成新的C-C 键，可用于合成化学中可见光驱动的有机氧化还原催化反应。 本计划描述的研究具有前瞻性。长远来看，本计划有望取得两个成果：一是为有机显示技术行业发现新的专有、廉价的金属发光体；另一个是成功开发基于地球蕴量丰富金属的用于有机合成化学的碳-碳键形成和碳-氢/卤化物键活化的光催化剂。这些成果的成功实现将同时伴随着将新的专有技术应用在有机电子器件和精细化学品/制药行业中。

17305521.label: Realisation of objectives
17305521.value: All the objectives of this project have been achieved. We have published 1 paper in Angewandte Chemie International Edition, 1 paper in Chem, and 1 paper has recently been accepted in Nature Communications. Three presentations were delivered in international conferences. This GRF grant has been acknowledged in all publications and presentations. The manuscripts for the unpublished works are also attached, and they will be submitted for publication within this year. One of the Co-Is, Dr. T.-L. Lam, has left The University of Hong Kong. The responsibilities previously held by Dr. Lam have been undertaken by the other Co-I, Dr. W.-P. To. The findings are summarized below: Objectives 1 and 3: We prepared a panel of air-stable two-coordinate binuclear Cu2(I,I) N-heterocyclic carbene complexes with short intramolecular Cu–Cu (2.75–2.88 Å) and Cu–arene (2.61–2.65 Å) distances. These Cu2(I,I) complexes exhibit highly emissive metal-metal-to-ligand charge transfer excited states (emission quantum yields up to 0.67; lifetimes ranging from 2.9 to 36.1 microseconds in solution) which can cleave strong R–X (X = Br or Cl) bonds to give mixed-valence [X–Cu1.5 Cu1.5–Y]+/2+ (Y=X or solvent) species and carbon-centered radicals via an excited state halogen-atom transfer mechanism. The spin-delocalized [X–Cu1.5 Cu1.5–X]+ species (X = Br or Cl) have been characterized by single-crystal XRD, EPR spectroscopy, and density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Complex Cu3 has been demonstrated as an efficient photocatalyst for C–C coupling reactions with aryl/alkyl halides under 390 nm LED irradiation. This work has been published in Chem.(Output 1). We prepared a series of carbene-copper(I)-amide (CMA(Cu)) emitters by using modified carbazole donor ligands, and quinoxaline-fused NHC ligands. These complexes show blue to deep-red TADF emission (470–677 nm) in thin films with emission quantum yields of up to 0.90, short lifetimes of < 1.2 µs, and large radiative decay rate constant (kr) of 1.2–2.7 × 10^6 s-1. OLEDs based on these complexes as emitters exhibit electroluminescence with maximum external quantum efficiencies (EQEmax) as high as 24.0%, with efficiency roll-off as small as 0.6% at 1000 cd m-2 and brightness up to 265,000 cd m-2. Notably, the operating lifetime (LT95) of these Cu-OLEDs can reach 3582 hours at an initial luminance (L0) of 1000 cd m-2. This LT95 value is one of the few best values reported in the public domain for all organic TADF and metal-TADF emitters. Efficient and robust TSF-OLEDs using Cu(I) sensitizer and alpha-NAICZ as red fluorescent emitter achieved narrowband electroluminescence (FWHM of 33–38 nm), high EQE (reaching 21.9%), brightness up to 162,000 cd m-2, and LT95 up to 3689 h at 1000 cd m-2. The manuscript of this work has recently been accepted in Nature Communications.(Output 3). Objectives 1 and 4: We prepared a series of dinuclear Ni2(II,II) complexes using strong σ-donating, carbene-phenyl-carbene (C^C^C) pincer ligands. These dinuclear formamidinate/α-carbolinato-bridged Ni2(II,II) complexes exhibit short Ni-Ni distances of 2.947–3.054 Å and singlet metal-metal-to-ligand charge transfer (1MMLCT) transitions at 500–550 nm. One-electron oxidation of these Ni2(II,II) complexes produces valence-trapped dinuclear Ni2(II,III) species, which were characterized by EPR spectroscopy. These Ni2(II,II) complexes exhibit phosphorescence in the NIR (800–1400 nm; lifetime ranging 2.6–8.6 μs) spectral region in 2-MeTHF and in the solid state at 77 K. Combined with DFT calculations, the NIR emission is assigned to originate from the 3dd excited state. The dinuclear Ni2(II,II) complex can sensitize the formation of singlet oxygen and catalyze the oxidation of cyclo-dienes under light irradiation. This work has been published in Angewandte Chemie International Edition.(Output 2). We prepared a series of mononuclear and dinuclear Ni(II) isocyanide complexes supported by carbene-phenyl-carbene (C^C^C) pincer ligand. π-π stacking interactions were observed between the CCC ligand planes for all the mononuclear Ni(II) complexes (interplanar distances ranging from 3.256 to 3.546 Å), while a short Ni-Ni distance (<3.5 Å) is only observed in the dinuclear complex 8 (3.151 Å, intramolecular). Some of the mononuclear Ni(II) complexes undergo self-assembly in water-acetonitrile mixture, and exhibit photoluminescence (quantum yield: 0.013-0.027%, lifetime: 67-698 ns) in the Vis-NIR (600-1200 nm) spectral region from 3dd excited state (kr = 387-2090 s-1) at room temperature. Femtosecond time-resolved transient absorption difference (fs-ta) measurement revealed that the excited state lifetimes increased from tens of picosecond to several nanoseconds upon aggregation. These complexes exhibit NIR emission in the solid state at room temperature with lifetimes of up to 0.72 μs. Notably, at 77 K, complex 4-PF6 exhibit NIR emission with a quantum yield of 21% and lifetime of 99 μs, both of which are the highest values among reported Ni(II) complexes. These findings are described in Ms. Mengyue Gao’s PhD thesis. Objectives 1 and 2: A series of stable hemi-caged tris(8-hydroxyquinolinato) Bi(III) complexes were prepared and characterized by single crystal X-ray analysis. These complexes are stable in solutions and exhibit dual fluorescence (lifetime=2-204 ps) and phosphorescence (lifetime=0.17-7.4 μs) at room temperature with quantum yields of up to 0.35% in degassed THF solutions. DFT /TDDFT calculations indicate that the luminescence of these complexes originates from intraligand charge-transfer excited states. The dual emission of complex BiL2 has been utilized as self-referenced ratiometric temperature sensor. In aerated CHCl3 solution, complex BiL5 sensitized the generation of singlet oxygen with a quantum yield of 52%. BiL5 was found to catalyse light-induced oxidative amine functionalization, reductive homocoupling of benzyl bromide, and [2+2]-cycloaddition reactions. BiL5 was also used as an emissive dopant in OLEDs fabricated through vapor deposition. These findings are described in Ms. Mengyao Chao’s PhD thesis. A manuscript is in preparation.(Output 4). Objectives 1 and 5: We designed and synthesized a series of W(VI) Schiff base complexes by intergrating planar N-donor units (such as acridan and carbazole units) with phenoxide units to form a twisted donor-acceptor ligand. This structual design eliminates the dimethylphenyl spacer present in the reported tungsten(VI) TADF emitter, thereby reducing the molecular weight of the complexes, facilitating sublimation. These W(VI) complexes exhibit TADF, with high emission quantum yield up to 92% and large kr up to 10^6 s-1. The new molecular design enabled the first vacuum-deposited OLEDs based on W(VI) emitters, which showed a EQEmax of 13.9% and an operational lifetime LT50 of 1350 h at 1000 cd m-2. These findings are described in Mr. Wenquan Lai’s PhD thesis. A manuscript is in preparation.(Output 5) Objectives 1 and 5. We synthesized decavanadate [((n-C4H9)N)3][(V10O28H3)] ([V10]) and vanadium(V) oxido chelate complexes ([VOLF]) and investigated their photocatalytic activity in light-induced aerobic oxidation reaction. They showed excellent performance in the light-induced aerobic oxidation of secondary alcohols to ketones (18 examples, up to 98% yield), the oxidation of C(sp3)-H bond of benzylic methylenes (4 examples, up to 91% yield) and benzylic primary C(sp3)-H bonds (8 examples, up to 84% yield). DFT calculations revealed that the catalytically relevant high-lying triplet state corresponds to an oxygen-to-vanadium ligand-to-metal charge transfer (LMCT) with oxyradical character, which likely acts as the reactive state initiating the photochemical process. However, this excited state exhibits low quantum efficiency due to its fast excited state decay. These findings are described in Ms. Mengyao Chao’s PhD thesis. A manuscript is in preparation.(Output 6).

17305521.label: Major findings and research outcome
17305521.value: [1] We have published one paper in Angewandte Chemie International Edition, and one paper in Chem. One paper has recently been accepted in Nature Communications. Three presentations have been given in international conferences. [2] We developed a class of highly emissive air-stable two-coordinate binuclear Cu2(I,I) N-heterocyclic carbene complexes which are the first examples of binuclear Cu(I) complexes displaying MMLCT excited state in solution. One of these complexes has been demonstrated as an efficient photocatalyst for C–C coupling reactions with aryl/alkyl halides.(Output 1) [3] We developed a series of carbene-copper(I)-amide (CMA(Cu)) emitters exhibiting TADF emission with high quantum yields (up to 0.90), and short lifetimes of < 1.2 µs. OLEDs fabricated with these Cu(I) emitters demonstrated excellent electroluminescence performance, achieving high EQEmax (up to 24.0%), and unprecedentedly long device lifetime (LT95 reaching 3582 hours at L0 of 1000 cd m-2).(Output 3). [4] We prepared a series of dinuclear Ni(II) complexes with excited state lifetimes of up to 743 ps in solutions at room temperature. Notably, these complexes display phosphorescence (τ=2.6–8.6 μs) originating from the 3dd excited state in the NIR (800–1400 nm) spectral region in 2-MeTHF and in the solid state at 77 K. This represents the first report of an unambiguously confirmed emission from Ni(II) complexes.(Output 2) Furthermore, we prepared a series of mononuclear and dinuclear Ni(II) isocyanide complexes. Some of the mononuclear Ni(II) complexes undergo aggregation in water-acetonitrile mixtures, and exhibit NIR photoluminescence originating from 3dd excited state, which is the first observation of phosphorescence from Ni(II) complexes in solution at room temperature. Additionally, in the solid state at 77 K, these complexes display NIR emission with quantum yields of up to 21%, which is the highest value known for Ni(II) complexes in the literature. [5] Compared to the reported un-caged tris(8-hydroxyquinolinato) Bi(III) complexes, the hemi-caged tris(8-hydroxyquinolinato) Bi(III) complexes studied in this project exhibit improved air- and solution-stability, providing a proof-of-concept for how ligand design can improve the properties of metal complexes. The applications of these complexes as self-referenced ratiometric temperature sensor, photocatalysts, and an OLED emitter have been explored.(Output 4) [6] A series of W(VI) TADF emitters have been prepared. They show record-high emission quantum yields and kr of up to 0.92 and 1x10^6 s-1, respectively,in thin films at room temperature. Importantly, we have achieved for the first time the realization of sublimable W(VI) emitters for OLED applications.(Output 5)

17305521.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17305521.value: Results from this project demonstrate that, through careful ligand design, earth-abundant metal complexes can exhibit strong photoluminescence, and their excited states can be utilized for various applications. Our work on binuclear Cu(I) carbene complexes uncovers the capacity of Cu(I) complexes to undergo inner-sphere atom transfer reactions, a reaction previously observed only in binuclear Au(I) and Pt(II) complexes. The discovery of highly efficient carbene-copper(I)-amide (CMA(Cu)) emitters highlights the bright prospect and competitiveness of Cu(I) emitters in OLED display technology. The observation of phosphorescence from Ni(II) isocyanide complexes in water-acetonitrile mixtures suggests that aggregation may serve as an effective strategy to suppress excited-state non-radiative decay of Ni(II) complexes. The discovery of sublimable W(VI) emitters suggest that further ligand modification may enable efficient tungsten-based vacuum-deposited OLEDs. Based on these results, we will expand the structural diversity of these earth-abundant metal complexes and perform in-depth studies on their photophysical properties. This will deepen our understanding of their excited state properties and provide guidance for optimized ligand design. Our goal is to design ligands that can suppress excited-state non-radiative decay, thereby improving the emission quantum yields of the metal complexes at room temperature and uncovering new excited-state reactivity and applications.

17305521.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17305521.value: Luminescent metal complexes widely used in applications such as organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs), photocatalysis, and sensing are primarily based on rare and expensive precious metals like platinum, gold, and iridium. However, the reliance on these metals gives rise to challenges regarding cost and sustainability. In this project, we have developed luminescent metal complexes based on earth-abundant metals, including copper, bismuth, nickel, and tungsten. Our findings demonstrate that it is possible to prepare efficient luminescent metal complexes from these environmentally sustainable elements. These complexes show promising applications in optoelectronic devices and photocatalysis, providing viable alternatives to traditional precious metal-based materials. This research not only reduces the dependence on rare metals but also advances the development of sustainable materials for important light-related applications.

17306121.value: Settle down the proposed quantile index regression model. It includes to choose a suitable quantile function, and to discuss its relationship with the commonly used linear quantile regression model and extremal quantile regression model. Establish the asymptotic properties of the composite quantile regression estimation. It includes to solve the identification problem, and to derive the consistency and asymptotic normality. 17306121.value: Quantile models and quantile regression estimation are highly related to the risk measure, and have played an important role in a variety of areas, including finance, biomedical imaging, machine learning, etc. In the meanwhile, the corresponding inference may have an arbitrarily low efficiency when the data around target quantile levels are sparse. Unfortunately, in real applications of quantile regression, much interest concentrates on such type of levels, such as high and/or low quantiles. For example, financial institutions and regulatory authorities want to measure the risk of high loss for investments, such as the Value-at-Risk (VaR) and Expected Shortfall (ES). The quantile regression can be used, but the resulting inference can be very unstable. On the other hand, in the big data era, we may have a huge number of covariates, and this makes the inference not feasible in solving real problems. This project assumes that the response follows a quantile function with an explicit form, and then takes its parameters as a function of covariates. More importantly we only require the model holds on a quantile interval rather than the whole [0,1], and this makes the model much more flexible. In real applications, we may assume a structure to the tail part, and then the information on high and/or low quantile can be obtained by extrapolation. The proposed model actually is partially parametric. For low-dimensional covariates, this project attempts to establish the asymptotic properties of the composite quantile regression estimation. While the non-asymptotic properties hopefully can be derived for the high-dimensional covariates. 17306121.label: Major findings and research outcome
17306121.value: 1) This project proposes a reliable method for the inference at extreme quantiles with both low- and high-dimensional covariates. The main idea is first to conduct a composite quantile regression at fixed quantile levels, and we then can extrapolate the estimated results to extreme quantiles by assuming a parametric structure at tails. The Tukey lambda structure can be used due to its flexibility and the explicit form of its quantile functions, and the success of the proposed methodology has been demonstrated by extensive numeral studies; see Zhang, Zhu, Si and Li (2025) at Part C. 2) For panel data models with subgroup effects, this project considers a non-parametric method to explore the relationship between response and predictors, which can avoid the wrong grouping results due to possible model misspecification. In addition, quantile regression is also employed to detect different pursuit results at various quantile levels. More importantly, these two features are both supported by the real analysis on a climate dataset. A concave fused penalty is used to select the groups and estimate models simultaneously, and the corresponding oracle properties are hence expected. Moreover, the developed ADMM algorithm can be used to efficiently solve the pairwise fusion penalized minimization problem; see Zhang, Wang, Lian and Li (2023) at Part C. 3) This project also proposes the quantile GARCH model, a new conditional heteroskedastic model whose coefficients are functions of a standard uniform random variable. A sufficient condition for the strict stationarity of this model is derived. To estimate the unknown coefficient functions without any moment restriction on the data, we develop the self-weighted QR and CQR methods. By efficiently borrowing information from intermediate quantile levels via a flexible parametric approximation, the CQR method is more favourable than the QR at high quantile levels. Our empirical analysis shows that the proposed approach can provide more accurate conditional quantile forecasts at high or even extreme quantile levels than existing ones; see Zhu, Tan, Zheng and Li (2023) at Part C.

17306121.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17306121.value: The proposed idea can be improved and extended in the following directions. Firstly, the estimation of the asymptotic covariance matrices for the QR and CQR estimator are complicated due to the unknown conditional density function. As an alternative to the kernel density estimation, an easy-to-use bootstrap method such as the block bootstrap and random-weight bootstrap may be developed, and asymptotically valid bootstrap inference for the estimated coefficient functions and conditional quantiles can be further studied. Secondly, it is worth investigating whether it is possible to construct a debiased CQR estimator that is provably no less efficient than the proposed biased estimator at high quantile levels. Thirdly, the expected shortfall, defined as the expectation of the loss that exceeds the VaR, is another important risk measure. It is also of interest to forecast the ES based on the proposed quantile GARCH model. Lastly, the parametric method to model the tails based on the flexible Tukey-lambda distribution is efficient and computationally simple. It can be generalised to other high quantile estimation problems for various data settings.

17306221.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17306221.value: The emergence of remarkably organized functional structures from solutions in nature has fascinated both cell biologists and materials scientists. To introduce heterogeneity into an otherwise homogeneous solution, new and immiscible solution phases are required. One way to induce the appearance of such phases is through a liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) process, where the formation of a coacervate phase is triggered by a change in the solution composition, temperature, or pH. The resulting coacervate droplets can be used for compartmentalization. Thus, LLPS has aroused immense interest among scientists interested in understanding the origin of life, as well as biologists interested in understanding the intracellular transfer of molecules and information. LLPS can be classified into segregative LLPS and associative LLPS, with the driving force for phase separation arising from repulsive and attractive interactions, respectively. As a common segregative LLPS system, the aqueous two-phase system has been extensively used to fabricate controlled droplets, particles, and capsules, as well as jets and fibers, with biocompatible and dynamic properties. However, despite its prevalence in cell biology, for instance, in intracellular liquid organelles, associative LLPS has scarcely been investigated for the fabrication of materials with unique properties in such systems. For instance, although such molecular arrangements as the RNA sequence are known to affect the phase separation process, these sequence-specific molecules have not been systematically applied in assembly using associative LLPS systems. The inclusion of molecular arrangements as a parameter will provide more precise control over the assembly and properties of the resultant structures. A comprehensive understanding of associative LLPS will enable the engineering and design of coacervates and coacervate-templated materials with more sophisticated morphologies and functions. The aims of the proposed project are to (1) investigate the physics behind the assembly across the aqueous-aqueous interfaces of associative phase separation systems, (2) elucidate the role of sequence-specific molecular interactions in determining the phase separation dynamics and resultant droplet morphology, and (3) devise an associative phase separation-induced precision assembly (APSPA) platform for formulating novel and dynamic hierarchical materials. In the short term, the project will provide a fundamental understanding of the effect of macromolecular interactions between different molecules on associative LLPS and the APSPA of hierarchical structures with sequence-specific properties. In the long term, it will lay a foundation for understanding the emergence of functional hierarchical structures in solutions and for fabricating nature- and cell-inspired assembly, promising more coherent integration at the synthetic and natural interface. 自然界溶液體系中高度有序功能結構的產生廣受細胞生物學家及材料學家的關注。溶液體系異質性的形成需要新的非混溶液相的引入。液液相分離（LLPS），即通過改變溶液組成、溫度或pH條件觸發形成團聚體相，是引入非混溶液相的方式之一。產生的團聚體液滴可以對溶液體系實現分區化。因此，LLPS不僅受到不同領域研究者的強烈興趣，包括致力於探索生命起源的科學家，以及致力於理解細胞內分子或信息傳遞的生物學家。根據相分離驅動力的不同（排斥作用或吸引作用），LLPS可以分為排斥型LLPS和締合型LLPS。作為一種常見的排斥型LLPS體系，雙水相體系已經被廣泛應用於製備具有生物兼容性和動態特性的液滴、顆粒、膠囊以及射流和纖維。但是，儘管其普遍存在於細胞生物學體系，例如細胞內的細胞器液滴，締合型LLPS鮮被用來製備特殊性質的材料。例如，儘管分子排佈如RNA序列被認為可以影響相分離過程，但這些具有特定序列的分子尚未被系統應用到締合型LLPS體系的組裝中。將分子排布作為一個參數可以更精確控制終端結構的組裝和性質。對締合型LLPS體系的全面了解有助於設計和構建具有更加精緻形貌和功能的團聚體或團聚體衍生材料。 本項目的主要目的是：（1）研究締合型相分離體系跨液-液界面組裝的物理機制；（2）闡明特殊序列分子作用對相分離動力學和終端液滴形貌的影響；（3）提出一種締合型相分離誘導的精確組裝方式來構建新型動態多級材料。 從短期看，本項目可促進對大分子相互作用對締合型LLPS的影響的理解，提出了一種締合型相分離誘導的精確組裝方式來構建具有序列特異性的多級結構。從長期看，本項目為理解溶液體系多級結構的產生以及自然或細胞啟發的組裝結構的構建奠定了基礎，進一步促進合成與自然界面的相干積累。

17306221.label: Realisation of objectives
17306221.value: 1. We have developed a novel segregative-associative (SA) aqueous droplets as membraneless organelle mimics, and investigated the intermolecular assembly mechanisms driven by weak segregative and associative interactions. Different from coacervates and liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS), the assembly of SA droplets requires a combination of electrostatic associative and segregative interactions for LLPS. These findings explain the complex dynamics of membraneless organelles and guide their flexible programming. 2. We have successfully elucidated how the trade-off of different types of molecular interactions (electrostatic, π–π, cation–π) dictate the solid/liquid phase transitions and macroscopic morphologies of condensates under solvent perturbations. We have also revealed sequence-dependent nucleic acid–polypeptide interactions that generate multiphase condensates, with RNA and DNA segregating into distinct phases. These findings provide molecular principles for programming responsive and hierarchical biomaterials. 3. We have designed a coacervate-lipid vesicle hybrid functional systems by the associative phase separation-induced assembly. The clustering and dispersing behaviors between coacervates and lipid vesicles have been fully explored, attributed to the weak electrostatic interaction environment. The material formation provides a reasonable model for studying and simulating relevant cellular dynamics, such as synaptic-like clustering of lipid vesicles.
