17501421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17501421.value: Platform (or two-sided market) is becoming an increasingly popular business model and has been adopted by many firms. Platform owners often charge at least one side of their users to fund their business operations and potentially make profits. For instance, leading mobile app stores such as Apple App Store and Google Play charge a 30% commission on paid app downloads and one-time in-app purchases. In 2020, several mobile app developers publicly criticized Apple for its high commission rate and monopoly position in the mobile economy. In this proposed research, to better understand the implications of platform pricing decisions, I utilize a natural experiment to investigate the impact of a change in the platform commission rate on the dynamics of the mobile ecosystem. On June 13, 2016, Apple App Store reduced its commission fee from 30% to 15% for any subscription-service renewals made by app users after their first year of subscription. First, I examine how this reduction affects the performance (measured by daily active users and downloads) of mobile apps. Second, I investigate how mobile app developers may react to this policy change differently, e.g., reducing the app download price or investing more to improve the app quality. Finally, I investigate how this event affects the three types of app revenues: download revenue, in-app purchase revenue, and ad revenue. This empirical study contributes significantly to the platform literature and provides guidance for the development of effective pricing strategies by platform owners. 平台（或双边市场）正在成为一种越来越流行的商业模式，并已被许多公司采用。平台所有者通常至少向其一侧用户收取费用，以资助其业务运营并可能获利。例如，Apple App Store 和 Google Play 等领先的移动应用商店针对付费应用下载和应用内一次性购买向应用开发商收取 30% 的佣金。 2020年，多个移动应用开发商公开批评苹果公司在移动经济中的高佣金率和垄断地位。在这项研究中，为了更好地理解平台定价决策的影响，我们利用一个自然实验来研究平台佣金率的变化对移动生态系统动态的影响。 2016 年 6 月 13 日，Apple App Store 将应用程序用户在订阅第一年之后进行的任何订阅服务续订的佣金费用从 30% 降低到 15%。首先，我们量化这种佣金减少如何影响移动应用程序的表现（以每日活跃用户数和下载量衡量）。其次，我们分析移动应用程序开发人员如何对这一政策变化做出不同的反应，例如，降低应用程序下载价格或投入更多资金来提高应用程序质量。最后，我们研究此事件如何影响平台的三种类型的收入：应用程序下载收入、应用内购买收入和广告收入。这项实证研究将对平台文献做出重大贡献，并为平台所有者制定有效的定价策略提供理论指导。

17501421.label: Realisation of objectives
17501421.value: In this project, we utilized Apple's 2016 policy change to examine the impact of lowered commission rates on mobile ecosystem dynamics. On September 1, 2016, Apple decreased its commission rate from 30% to 15% for revenues generated from users' subscription renewals that lasted at least a year. This policy change served as a quasi-natural experiment, allowing us to employ a Difference-in-Differences (DID) research design to investigate the effects of reduced commission rates on mobile app performance, such as the number of downloads, daily active users, app quality, and revenue streams. We designated apps with in-app subscriptions as the treatment group, as they were affected by Apple's commission reduction policy. The control group consisted of apps offering in-app purchases but lacking subscription services, sharing a similar business model without being influenced by the policy change. To ensure comparability between the treatment and control groups, we conducted propensity score matching (PSM) based on observable characteristics and growth trends prior to the policy change. Following the matching process, we performed DID analyses to compare the dependent variables for both groups over the years before and after the policy implementation. After presenting our research findings at conferences and seminars, we recognized the importance of understanding how commission policy changes can incentivize developers' value creation, thereby promoting platform growth. Existing literature on mobile platform governance emphasizes the role of platform pricing strategies in fostering app development and innovation, which is crucial for developers' value creation and platform growth. However, there is limited empirical evidence demonstrating how developers actually respond to platform commission rate reductions. Theoretical models within two- or multi-sided economies primarily focus on platform revenue maximization and participant welfare balance, assuming that reduced platform commission fees result in increased profit margins for sellers or producers. This, in turn, encourages them to join platforms and engage in transactions with buyers. Based on these studies, lowering commission fees appears to be an effective financial strategy for motivating developers to improve their app development and innovation. However, a wider examination of empirical research in policy interventions and strategic management reveals diverse possibilities regarding the impact of financial incentives on investment and innovation. Business owners or managers might perceive potential increases from financial incentives as temporary windfalls, retaining additional revenues for themselves instead of reinvesting in product development and innovation. Additionally, they might face resource constraints and cognitive inertia, hindering their ability to develop and innovate their products in response to financial incentives. Finally, they may anticipate fewer growth opportunities and potential market distortions due to financial incentive policies, leading to reduced investment in enhancing product quality. These perspectives suggest various ways app developers might adjust their strategies in response to commission reductions, thus motivating us to empirically investigate the impact of platform commission reduction on app development and explore its contingencies.

17501421.label: Major findings and research outcome
17501421.value: This project examines the impact of lowering platform commission rates on app development and innovation, using the Apple App Store's commission reduction policy as a quasi-experiment. The findings show that reducing platform commission rates leads to a significant increase in app updates, suggesting that such a policy incentivizes developers to invest more in maintaining and innovating their apps. However, this impact is contingent on several factors, including an app's in-app purchase revenues, the developer's portfolio size, and market concentration. Apps without in-app purchase revenues showed less pronounced increases in update frequency compared to apps with in-app purchase revenues. Apps from developers with multiple apps exhibited a smaller increase in updates compared to single-app developers. Interestingly, apps in highly concentrated markets showed an insignificant increase in updates and a significant decrease in updates that introduced new features. Furthermore, additional developer-level analysis indicates that lowering commission rates enhances both new app releases and overall updates of existing apps among developers. These findings provide valuable insights into how platform pricing strategies can stimulate mobile app development and innovation. The project also contributes to the literature by highlighting the importance of contextual factors, such as apps' in-app revenues, developers' portfolio size, and market concentration, in affecting the effectiveness of platform pricing. It also enriches research on revenue-sharing strategies in two-sided platform economies by combining insights from strategic management and policy intervention research. The findings have important managerial implications for platform owners, app developers, and policymakers. Platform owners need to consider these factors when evaluating and refining commission policies to build a more vibrant and sustainable platform ecosystem. Developers, meanwhile, could use these insights to make strategic decisions about app development and innovation. Policymakers could also draw from these findings to guide their regulatory efforts in the mobile app industry.

17501421.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17501421.value: This project has several limitations that could be addressed in future research. First, we focus on the commission reduction policy in a particular digital platform environment. Future research can investigate the consistency of our findings across different types of digital platforms. Second, this study observes the outcomes following the specific reduction in the commission rate from 30% to 15%. Future research can explore the consequences of a broader range of commission rate adjustments for app development and innovation activities. Third, a richer dataset is needed in future research to explore how the platform commission reduction policy affects the actual profits of apps and the revenue growth of platforms.

17501421.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17501421.value: This project investigates the impact of lowering commission rates on app development using Apple's App Store as a case study. It focuses on how app developers react to changes in commission rates, which are important for platform owners' revenue and developers' satisfaction. Apple's commission reduction policy was implemented in 2016, lowering the rate from 30% to 15% for certain subscription-based apps. The findings show that the policy leads to an increase in app updates, suggesting that developers are more motivated to invest in their apps. However, the impact varies depending on factors such as in-app purchase revenues, developer portfolio size, and market concentration. Apps without in-app purchase revenues and those from developers with multiple apps show a smaller increase in updates. In highly concentrated markets, the policy doesn't significantly increase updates and even results in fewer updates with new features. This project contributes to the understanding of platform governance by exploring the effects of financial incentives on app development and innovation. It highlights the importance of considering contextual factors when evaluating the effectiveness of platform pricing strategies. The findings can help platform owners, app developers, and policymakers in refining commission policies to build a more vibrant and sustainable platform ecosystem.

17501521.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17501521.value: Transportation infrastructure is often viewed as being essential for economic growth, especially in developing countries. According to the China Statistical Yearbooks, the total length of general roads in China more than doubled from the 1990s to 2008, thanks to the large investment in transportation infrastructure. The total length of highway also jumped, from 147 kilometers in 1988 to more than 50,000 kilometers in 2007. In fewer than 30 years, the comprehensive transportation system in China evolved into a new modern stage, with much better level of technology, service capabilities, and coverage. During the same period, we observe a large decline in firms’ inventory—to--sales ratios and a substantial increase in markup, especially in areas with fast improvement of road infrastructure. The proposed project aims to investigate the effect of highway development on firm performance, especially how it affects firms’ dynamic decisions on pricing, production, inventory stock and, as a result, margins. The development of transportation infrastructure can influence firms’ dynamic decisions on inventory stock, which can have a large impact on firms’ dynamic decisions on pricing, production, and margins due to the impact on operating costs. On the one hand, improved transportation infrastructure reduces shipping time; therefore it reduces the inventory holding necessary to satisfy given demand. On the other hand, improved transportation infrastructure also reduces shipping costs, which may affect optimal inventory holding. The changes in shipping time, shipping costs, and the resulting changes in inventories can substantially affect firms’ pricing and markups. The proposed project aims to examine the causal impact of the development of transportation infrastructure on inventory and markup. We will develop a theoretical model to characterize how the development of transportation conditions affects firms’ inventory facing uncertain demand, which further influences pricing and markup. The model implies the correct measure of markup in the presence of uncertain demand and inventory heterogeneity. Empirically, we will test the inventory mechanism through which transportation affects markup and evaluate its contribution to the increase in markup of Chinese manufacturing firms during the data period. The findings will deepen our understanding of the importance of inventory dynamics and the economic impact of government investment in transportation infrastructure on firm performance. This can have direct implications for many government policies that are related to investment in transportation infrastructure. 交通基礎設施是經濟發展的必要條件，其在發展中國家尤爲重要。据中國統計年鑒顯示，由於大規模的交通基礎設施投資，中國的一般公路總里程數從1990年代到2008年翻了超過一番。而高速公路總里程數也從1988年的僅僅147公里，迅速增長到2007年的超過5萬公里。在不到三十年的時間裏，中國的交通系統迅速實現現代化，在技術、服務能力、和覆蓋範圍都取得了長足的進步。同一時期，製造業企業持有的存貨大幅下降，加成率顯著提高。這一現象在公路基礎設施發展較快的地區尤其明顯。本課題旨在研究高速公路的發展對企業績效的影響，尤其是對企業的動態定價決策、生產、存貨、以及加成率的影響。交通基礎設施的發展能直接影響企業的多項決策，比如定價、生產、運營成本，從而影響企業的盈利能力和績效。一方面，交通基礎設施的改進能降低運輸時間，從而降低企業為滿足需求而持有的存貨。另一方面，交通基礎設施的改進也能降低運輸成本，從而影響企業的最優存貨決策以及其他運營決策。運輸時間、運輸成本的改變，以及由此導致的最優存貨的改變會直接影響企業的定價決策和加成率。本課題旨在研究交通基礎設施的改進對企業存貨和加成率的因果影響。我們首先會建立一個理論模型來闡述交通基礎設施的發展如何影響企業的存貨決策和面臨的需求不確定性，以及他們如何影響企業的定價和加成率。此模型會為準確測度面臨需求不確定性並持有不同水平存貨的企業的加成率提供理論指導。實證方面，本課題會檢驗交通基礎設施的改進對中國製造業加成率的影響，以及存貨的改變在此過程中發揮的作用。本課題的研究結論能加深我們對企業存貨的重要性以及政府對交通基礎設施投資的經濟影響的理解。這些結論對政府交通基礎設施投資方面的決策有直接指導意義。

17501521.label: Realisation of objectives
17501521.value: We achieve these objectives nicely in two research papers. The first (Paper 1) is "How Do Large Epidemics Redistribute Market Power: Evidence from the 2003 SARS Shock in China" (Hongsong Zhang and Yating Jiang), in which we examine the impact of a significant pandemic shock on firms' inventory, demand uncertainty, and markup. We find that road distance (measured by road infrastructure) has a significant impact on firms' inventory and markup. In the second paper (Paper 2), "Market Access through Production Networks: Impact of Highway Development on Firm Performance", we examine more closely the impact of transportation infrastructure on firms' general performance, including productivity, markup, etc. Moreover, we explore the problem through the lens of production network and find that firms' market access through the production network and road construction substantially improved firms' performance in China. Based on these two papers, we achieved all the objectives listed above both theoretically and empirically. Specifically, paper 1 developed a theory of firms' dynamic decisions of production, pricing, and optimal inventory holding in the presence of uncertain demand. The theory has direct implications for Objectives 2, 3, and 4. Notably, the theory proposes a new methodology for estimating firms' markup (market power) in the presence of demand uncertainty and dynamic decisions regarding production, pricing, and inventory. This new measure utilizes commonly available data, requires minimal assumptions, and as a result, can have wide applications in future research. The two papers also provide detailed empirical evidence for Objectives 1, 2, and 3, using firm-level data from Chinese manufacturing industries. While Paper 1 utilizes the SARS shock in China in 2003 as a shock to identify the effects, Paper 2 instead directly studies the impact of the rapid development of highways in China. The empirical results are established using multiple empirical methods, including reduced-form analysis (Difference-in-differences) and structural estimation based on the theoretical model. The empirical results in both papers have policy implications to achieve Objective 5. In particular, Paper 2 suggests that government investments in the highway system have a significant impact on firms located near the highway, providing supporting evidence for the benefits of government investment in infrastructure. The paper also developed a new measure of firms' market access by combining the production network with the traditionally considered transportation network, emphasizing the insight that transportation infrastructure can improve firms' market access only if it connect firms to their suppliers/buyers.

17501521.label: Major findings and research outcome
17501521.value: Paper 1 examines the impact of large economic shocks (such as serious epidemics) on the redistribution of market power in manufacturing industries, and the roles played by inventory and demand uncertainty as important mechanisms. We developed a model of firms’ dynamic decisions on production, pricing, and inventory holding, and applied the model to the Chinese firm-level data in the manufacturing industries. There are four major findings. First, we demonstrate the importance of inventory stock and demand uncertainty in understanding market power. Second, we propose a new measure of market power in the presence of demand uncertainty and dynamic production, pricing, and inventory decisions. Third, we find that the 2003 SARS shock in China significantly reduced the market power of firms in SARS-impacted areas. This effect is long-lasting. Fourth, SARS also substantially increased the inventory of affected firms, which partially contributed to the redistribution of market power. Paper 2 examines how improved market access, induced by transportation development – alleviates these distortions and impacts firm performance. We emphasize the importance of input-output networks, as expanding transportation infrastructure into regions with richer trade links brings larger shifts in market accessibility. Our findings reveal several main findings. First, improved market access to upstream suppliers and downstream buyers significantly boosts firm productivity and markups while reducing input prices. Second, these gains are partly offset by intensified within-industry competition resulting from enhanced transportation networks. Third, overall, the expansion of China’s expressways between 1998 and 2007 increased firm productivity by approximately 40%, raised markups by 1.7%, and reduced input prices by 17%. Fourth, firms initially at a disadvantage benefited disproportionately more from the expressway improvements, fostering convergence in firm performance within and across regions. We show that reduced distortions through enhanced market access is a critical mechanism for firm-level gains.

17501521.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17501521.value: The new methodology for measuring markup in the presence of demand uncertainty and dynamic production, pricing, and inventory holding can be applied to many other applications. The new measure of firms' market access by combining the production network with the traditionally considered transportation network also has wide applications. We are now utilizing these methodologies in a new project to assess the impact of place-based industrial policy in China.

17501521.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17501521.value: This project explores how transportation infrastructure affects firms' inventory, market power, and performance, especially during large shocks like the SARS epidemic or significant changes in transportation networks. We develop two new methodologies: one to measure firm-level market power accounting for demand uncertainty and dynamic decision-making, and another to assess market access through production networks. These measures address limitations of traditional metrics and have broad applications. Our analysis shows that transportation infrastructure significantly influences firm behavior. Demand uncertainty and initial inventory levels shape production and pricing strategies. Large negative shocks, such as SARS, lead firms to reduce prices and alter production, impacting long-term performance. Conversely, positive shocks—like improvements in transportation—expand market access, boosting productivity, sourcing costs, market power, and inventory management. Overall, transportation development enhances firms’ ability to adapt and thrive amid economic disruptions. Policy implications are also evident: government investments in highway infrastructure benefit firms near roads and improve overall market efficiency. Additionally, integrating production networks with transportation infrastructure enhances firms’ market access—especially when infrastructure connects firms to their suppliers and customers.

17501721.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17501721.value: There is a long-lasting debate concerning the pros and cons of the visible hand and invisible hand. Market failure is the reason why all kinds of regulation should intervene. Information asymmetry used to be considered one of the most important factors leading to market failure. However, this study aims to challenge the traditional view. We hypothesize that after removing the mandated human screening policy (the visible hand) on crowdfunding platforms, the quality of projects raising enough funds will be improved. We also suggest that the underlying mechanism is free competition (the invisible hand). Although there are many low-quality projects on the platform, they will be naturally screened out by the market. We analyzed data collected from Kickstarter and the preliminary results supported our hypotheses. Further theoretical development and validation tests are proposed. 有形之手與無形之手的爭論持續已久。市場失靈是各種監管規則應當存在的原因，而信息不對稱時常被認為是導致市場失靈的重要原因之一。本研究挑戰此傳統觀點。我們假設眾籌平臺在取消強制的人工審核政策（即有形之手）後，能夠籌集足夠資金的項目的品質將會提高。我們提出此結果的內在機制是自由競爭（即無形之手）。儘管眾籌平臺上有很多低品質的項目，但它們會被市場自然淘汰。我們分析了從眾籌網站Kickstarter上搜集的數據，初步的分析結果支持了我們的假設。本研究將提出進一步的理論拓展和驗證測試。

17501721.label: Major findings and research outcome
17501721.value: Throughout our analysis, we found compelling evidence supporting the positive effects of relaxing listing requirements on project quality and backer satisfaction. The expansion of the choices pool and the provision of personalized options cater to the individual preferences and autonomy-needs of backers. According to Self-Determination Theory, this increased autonomy and sense of control over their investment decisions lead to higher levels of satisfaction. Backers appreciate having a diverse array of projects to choose from, aligning with their interests and allowing them to support initiatives that resonate with them on a personal level. The relaxation of listing requirements also opens doors for a broader range of creators, giving them the opportunity to showcase their ideas and receive support from backers who might not have been otherwise engaged. The findings of our research highlight the importance of platforms adopting more flexible listing requirements to foster a thriving crowdfunding ecosystem and maximize backer satisfaction. We found that the effect can be explained by the effective communication between project creators and backers. Our analysis revealed that communication fosters engagement, trust, and a sense of community among backers. Specifically, according to Self-Determination Theory, communications between creators and backers can enhance basic psychological needs of competence and relatedness of bakers. As effective communication allows backers to feel engaged and involved in the project. Likewise, by sharing updates, seeking feedback, and involving backers in decision-making processes, project creators make them feel like active participants rather than just passive funders, further on, backers feel more confident in the project's development and are reassured that their support is being valued. This sense of involvement increases backers' satisfaction as they become more invested in the project's success. Also, by providing regular updates, addressing inquiries, and actively engaging with backers, project creators create an environment of openness and authenticity. Therefore, our research emphasizes the significance of nurturing effective communication channels between project creators and backers to enhance satisfaction.

17501721.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17501721.value: Further research will be conducted on the communication strategies on crowdfunding platforms. We will explore how cultural factors, norms, and regional variations impact backer satisfaction and the implementation of these strategies. Comparative studies across different countries and cultures would provide insights into the adaptability and effectiveness of these factors in diverse contexts.

17502721.label: Project Objectives
17502721.value: Over the past three decades, the Chinese economy has been characterized by rapid GDP and productivity growth, widening income inequality (Ding and He (2018)), and lower social mobility (Fan, Yi, and Zhang (forthcoming)). Investment in human capital is believed to play a key role in determining aggregate productivity growth, inequality, and social mobility. However, in China, the less market-oriented labor market and greater difficulties in gaining access to higher education can distort human capital investment choices. For example, performance-linked compensation schemes are much rarer in state-owned enterprises (SOEs) than in privately-owned enterprises (POEs) (Ge and Yang (2014); Liu and Otsuka (2004)), which may imply that salaries earned by SOE-workers are less dependent on their human capital. Hence, in an economy that is dominated by SOEs, such as China in the early 1990s, since the reward to skills was small, people may have had weak incentive to invest human capital. Similarly, limited opportunity to access higher education could substantially discourage parental investment in children’s human capital. Two reforms took place in China almost simultaneously in the 1990s and have gradually liberalized the country's labor market — a market-oriented reform that led to the rise of the private sector and increased job mobility, as well as a large-scale public college expansion program. Both reforms can potentially increase investment in human capital by incentivizing parents to invest more in their children’s skills. Using household-level data on China, we show that the returns to human capital are higher for individuals working in the private sector than in the state-owned sector, and also increase with education levels. This suggests that an economic reform that leads to the expansion of the private sector would increase human capital investment by incentivizing parents to invest more in their children’s human capital. More importantly, we find that the increase in the returns to human capital with higher levels of education is greater for individuals working in the private sector than in the state-owned sector. This implies a potential complementarity between the two reforms. The market-oriented reform that led to the rise of POEs and provided people with more opportunities to work in POEs can incentivize individuals to attend college. Similarly, those with a college degree would consider working for POEs more attractive, which means that the college-expansion scheme would lead to more people working in the private sector. The joint effect of the two reforms is likely to be greater on labor reallocation and human capital investment, compared with the sum of the separate effects. Motivated by these novel empirical findings, we extend an otherwise standard heterogenous-agent overlapping-generations general equilibrium model to incorporate two margins: (1) altruistic parents who invest in their children’s human capital through multiple stages of childhood development, which determines children’s chance to be admitted by colleges as well as life-time earnings; and (2) multi-sectors: each individual can endogenously choose to work between the state-owned sector and the private sector based on her human capital and education level. After estimating the model using Simulated Method of Moments, we plan to use this model to quantify both the macroeconomic and distributional consequences of the market-oriented reform and the college expansion program as well as the effects of the complementarity between the two on labor reallocation, human capital investment, economic growth, inequality, and intergenerational mobility. The economic growth in the model results from an increase in the aggregate human capital, an input of firms’ production, driven by both reforms, together with the labor (human capital) reallocation from the less productive state-owned sector toward more productive private sector. The main channel through which the reforms lead to rising income inequality and intergenerational persistence works through the uneven distribution of the increase in the aggregate human capital investment across households. College-educated parents with high human capital level have greater resources to spend on their children, so they and their off-springs benefit disproportionally from the reforms. Consequently, parents with high levels of human capital and education are more likely to transmit their socioeconomic status to their children, compared with prior to the reforms. There are three major contributions of this project. First, we contribute to the literature that studies China’s rapid economic growth by exploiting the channel through how labor market liberalization reforms affect parents’ incentive to invest in their children’s human capital, thus impacting labor (human capital) reallocation. Second, this project will be the first paper that provides a theory and a quantitative general equilibrium model to explain why economic reforms lead to the rise of inequality and the decline of intergenerational mobility jointly. Third, we extend a heterogeneous-agent life-cycle model with endogenous human capital formation à la Lee and Seshadri (2019) into the context of developing economies like China by incorporating two new elements: (1) multi-sectors; and (2) a human-capital-based selection mechanism that determines individuals’ college attendance probability.

17502721.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17502721.value: Over the past three decades, the Chinese economy has been characterized by rapid economic growth, widening income inequality, and lower social mobility. This project studies how labor market liberalization reforms drive these trends by impacting people's incentives to invest in human capital through the lens of a quantitative general equilibrium framework. In particular, we focus on two reforms that took place in the 1990s in China: a market-oriented reform that led to the rise of the private sector and increased job mobility as well as a large-scale public college expansion program. These reforms may have changed parents’ incentive to invest in children’s human capital substantially, which is very likely to be a quantitatively powerful channel to explain the rapid economic growth, rising inequality, and lower intergenerational mobility jointly. Using household-level data, we show that the returns to (pre-labor-market) human capital are higher for individuals working in the private sector than in the state-owned sector, and also increase with education levels. This suggests that reforms that lead to the expansion of the private sector and increase the capacity of college respectively would increase human capital investment by incentivizing parents to invest more in their children’s human capital. More importantly, we find that the increase in the returns to (pre-labor-market) human capital with a higher level of education is greater for individuals working in the private sector than in the state-owned sector. This implies a potential complementarity effect between the two reforms on labor reallocation, college attendance, and human capital investment, which may have both macro and distributional implications. Motivated by these empirical findings, we extend an otherwise standard heterogenous-agent overlapping-generations general equilibrium model to incorporate two margins: (1) intergenerational linkages: altruistic parents who invest in their children’s human capital through multiple stages of childhood development, which determines the children’s chance to attend college as well as life-time earnings; and (2) multi-sectors: a state-owned sector and a private sector so that each individual can endogenously choose where to work based on her human capital level and education level. We plan to estimate the model using simulated method of moments (SMM) to match Chinese data at both the macro and micro levels. Finally, we plan to quantify both macroeconomic and distributional impacts of the market-oriented reform and the college expansion scheme as well as the potential complementarity between the two on labor reallocation, human capital investment, economic growth, inequality, and intergenerational mobility. 在过去的三十年里，中国经济在高速增长的同时也伴有收入不平等性的加剧以及社会流动性的下降。本项目依托于量化动态一般均衡模型的帮助来研究劳动力市场自由化改革是如何通过改变人们对于人力资本的投资进而影响中国经济的增长以及不平等问题。我们主要集中讨论发生在上世纪九十年代中国的两个改革：一个是增加工作流动性的企业私有化改革，另一个是大规模高等教育扩招改革。这些改革改变了父母对于子女人力资本投资的激励机制，很有可能成为一个能够同时解释经济快速发展，不平等问题加剧，以及代间流动性降低的重要途径。 我们通过微观数据发现人力资本在私有企业的回报比在国有企业的回报要更高，并且会随着教育程度的提高而提高。更为重要的是，我们发现企业私有化改革和大规模高等教育扩招改革会对劳动资源再配置，大学录取率，以及人力资本投资有一个互补性的效应。 基于我们从数据中的发现，我们在一个标准的 heterogeneous agent overlapping generations一般均衡性模型里加入了两个重要元素：（1）代间的联系：父母通过对孩子在不同阶段的投资进而影响孩子能否上大学的几率（2）多种经济体制：国有和私有。我们计划用simulated method of moments (SMM) 这一方法估计模型。最后，我们计划用估计好的模型去量化本项目研究的两种劳动力市场自由化改革之间的互补性，以及它们对于劳动资源再配置，人力资本投资，经济增长，不平等以及代间流动性的影响。

17502721.label: Major findings and research outcome
17502721.value: This project eventually produces two high-quality research papers. One is "The Macroeconomic Consequences of Competition for College Admissions" which is currently 3rd-round revise and resubmit in International Economic Review, and the other is "When Meritocracy Fails: College Expansion and the Rise of Intergenerational Persistence" which is already submitted and currently under review. 1. The Macroeconomic Consequences of Competition for College Admissions: To study how competition in college admissions drives parental investment and informs child development policies, we develop a heterogeneous-agent life-cycle model in which parents invest in their children’s human capital not only to increase future labor productivity but also to compete for limited college seats. Inefficiency arises because each family takes the admissions threshold as given and thus does not internalize how its own investment raises the admissions bar for others. Estimating our model with Chinese data, we find that a significant portion of parental monetary investment is driven by this competition-induced externality. Policies that reduce competition can deliver sizable welfare gains by correcting the externality, but their long-run effects are also shaped by intergenerational dynamics: lower investment today can worsen the human capital distribution of future generations. We show that a policy mix---taxing private education spending while subsidizing public investment---optimally balances the efficiency gains from externality correction against the need to sustain long-run human capital accumulation, thereby improving overall welfare. 2. When Meritocracy Fails: College Expansion and the Rise of Intergenerational Persistence: This paper evaluates the quantitative impacts of college expansion when admissions are purely merit based and competitive. We develop a heterogeneous agent life cycle model in which parents invest in their children’s pre-college human capital at multiple stages to compete for limited college slots. Applying this framework to China, where admissions rely solely on score ranks and enrollments have grown tenfold over 25 years, we find that score-based meritocracy amplifies the importance of cultivated human capital at age 18 relative to initial skill, sorting children not only by merit but also by affluence. Expanding college access under such a scheme worsens intergenerational mobility because wealthier families respond by disproportionately increasing pre-college investments, strengthening the correlation between child achievement and parental income. Counterfactuals show that without endogenous parental investment responses, mobility would improve with college expansion.

17502721.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17502721.value: Our current research focuses on education and human-capital development, with an emphasis on their implications for inequality and intergenerational mobility in China. Going forward, we plan to broaden this agenda by studying the interaction between these forces and long-run growth—particularly how education reforms and family policies interact with technological change, industrial upgrading, and related structural transformations.

17502721.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17502721.value: To study how competition in college admissions drives parental investment and informs child development policies, we develop a heterogeneous-agent life-cycle model in which parents invest in their children’s human capital not only to increase future labor productivity but also to compete for limited col- lege seats. An inefficiency of overinvestment arises because each family takes the admissions threshold as given and thus does not internalize how its own investment raises the admissions bar for others. Estimating our model with Chinese data, we find that, for an average household, over 60% of parental monetary investment is driven by this competition-induced externality. Poli- cies that reduce competition can deliver sizable welfare gains by correcting the externality, but their long-run effects are also shaped by intergenerational dynamics: lower investment today can worsen the human capital distribution of future generations. We show that a policy mix—taxing private education spending while subsidizing public investment—optimally balances the effi- ciency gains from curbing overinvestment against the need to sustain long-run human capital accumulation, thereby improving overall welfare.

17502921.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17502921.value: 通过移动触摸体验设计助推健康行为

17502921.label: Project Objectives
17502921.value: 1) Design mobile interaction to enhance users’ self-regulation and promote users’ subliminal healthy behavior. Health wellbeing is very important to every citizen. In recent years, mobile health interventions, that is, interventions designed to improve users’ health status via mobile technologies, have attracted an increasing amount of research attention (Loef and Walach 2012; Murray et al. 2016). Previous studies have yielded considerable knowledge on how to promote healthy behavior by drawing users’ conscious attention to explicit mobile interventions, such as push notifications, personalized reminders, and social support features, and recent advances in health psychology has suggested the possibility that people are often susceptible to technological nudges (Hollands et al. 2016; Rebar et al. 2015; Sheeran et al. 2013). . Hence, our study aims to investigate how to design mobile interaction, i.e., digital nudge, to enhance users’ self-regulation and subliminal engagement in healthy behavior. 2) Develop a framework of mobile touch experience design by conceptualizing touch gesture and haptic feedback. Different from traditional inputs involving a computer keyboard or mouse, mobile interaction changes users’ touch experience by allowing them to operate apps using their hands directly. In general, two major types of technologies can influence users’ touch experience, i.e., touch gesture and haptic feedback. On one hand, sensors can detect movements, pressure, and duration, thus enabling different touch gestures, such as long touch, hover touch, and deep touch. On the other hand, haptic feedback engines allow users to receive notifications and confirmations with vibrations. However, prior research on mobile technologies has yielded fragmented findings on different aspects of mobile touch experience. Hence, an important objective of this project is to theorize mobile touch experience by synthesizing touch gesture design and haptic feedback design in order for researchers and practitioners to effectively generate novel mobile touch experience for users. 3) Empirically test the effects of touch gesture and haptic feedback in different health-related contexts and introduce embodied cognition as a theoretical lens to guide mobile interface design . Mobile touch experience design does not only affect the usability of mobile applications, but also may changes users’ cognition and behavior. Embodied cognition theory, which highlights the importance of bodily actions and feelings in shaping human cognition, provides a theoretical lens to guide natural interface design. According to the theory, people will automatically infer meanings from bodily actions and feelings, and that the embodied meanings will further affect their subsequent behavior. For example, a stream of research draws on natural body movements and motor-conceptual associations to design mobile, wearable, and other body-controlled user interfaces (Dourish 2004; Marshall et al. 2013). However, these studies have focused on using motor-conceptual associations to improve usability, but neglected the potential effect of embodied cognition on users’ perceptions, decisions and behaviors in focal tasks. In this project, we will empirically test the role of touch gesture and haptic feedback in several health-related contexts (e.g., mobile food ordering, mobile fitness management and mobile personal hygiene training) and demonstrate that the way in which we interact with digital systems can shape users’ cognition, affect their self-regulation, and thus promote healthy behavior. 4) Produce high-quality research papers that reveal how the embodiment effects differ among users with varying levels of health consciousness and provide a guideline for customized mobile touch experience design. The embodied cognition literature has also indicated that embodiment effects are contingent on some boundary conditions (Meier et al. 2012; Niedenthal et al. 2005). In the healthcare context, users’ health consciousness has been regarded as an important moderating factor that affects the effectiveness of health interventions (Mai and Hoffmann 2015). We conjecture that people with different levels of health consciousness may interpret and use the embodied meanings differently in health-related decisions. Therefore, this study will reveal how the embodiment effect of touch gesture and haptic feedback on users’ healthy behavior is moderated by their health consciousness. By doing so, we can customize designs for users with different levels of health consciousness to enhance the effectiveness of mobile apps in different healthcare contexts.

In recent years, mobile health interventions, that is, interventions designed to improve users’ health status via mobile technologies, have attracted an increasing amount of research attention (Loef and Walach 2012; Murray et al. 2016). Previous studies have yielded considerable knowledge on how to promote healthy behavior by drawing users’ conscious attention to explicit mobile interventions, such as push notifications, personalized reminders, and social support features, and recent advances in health psychology has suggested the possibility that people are often susceptible to technological nudges (Hollands et al. 2016; Rebar et al. 2015; Sheeran et al. 2013). . Hence, our study aims to investigate how to design mobile interaction, i.e., digital nudge, to enhance users’ self-regulation and subliminal engagement in healthy behavior.

2) Develop a framework of mobile touch experience design by conceptualizing touch gesture and haptic feedback. Different from traditional inputs involving a computer keyboard or mouse, mobile interaction changes users’ touch experience by allowing them to operate apps using their hands directly. In general, two major types of technologies can influence users’ touch experience, i.e., touch gesture and haptic feedback. On one hand, sensors can detect movements, pressure, and duration, thus enabling different touch gestures, such as long touch, hover touch, and deep touch. On the other hand, haptic feedback engines allow users to receive notifications and confirmations with vibrations. However, prior research on mobile technologies has yielded fragmented findings on different aspects of mobile touch experience. Hence, an important objective of this project is to theorize mobile touch experience by synthesizing touch gesture design and haptic feedback design in order for researchers and practitioners to effectively generate novel mobile touch experience for users.

3) Empirically test the effects of touch gesture and haptic feedback in different health-related contexts and introduce embodied cognition as a theoretical lens to guide mobile interface design . Mobile touch experience design does not only affect the usability of mobile applications, but also may changes users’ cognition and behavior. Embodied cognition theory, which highlights the importance of bodily actions and feelings in shaping human cognition, provides a theoretical lens to guide natural interface design. According to the theory, people will automatically infer meanings from bodily actions and feelings, and that the embodied meanings will further affect their subsequent behavior. For example, a stream of research draws on natural body movements and motor-conceptual associations to design mobile, wearable, and other body-controlled user interfaces (Dourish 2004; Marshall et al. 2013). However, these studies have focused on using motor-conceptual associations to improve usability, but neglected the potential effect of embodied cognition on users’ perceptions, decisions and behaviors in focal tasks. In this project, we will empirically test the role of touch gesture and haptic feedback in several health-related contexts (e.g., mobile food ordering, mobile fitness management and mobile personal hygiene training) and demonstrate that the way in which we interact with digital systems can shape users’ cognition, affect their self-regulation, and thus promote healthy behavior.

4) Produce high-quality research papers that reveal how the embodiment effects differ among users with varying levels of health consciousness and provide a guideline for customized mobile touch experience design. The embodied cognition literature has also indicated that embodiment effects are contingent on some boundary conditions (Meier et al. 2012; Niedenthal et al. 2005). In the healthcare context, users’ health consciousness has been regarded as an important moderating factor that affects the effectiveness of health interventions (Mai and Hoffmann 2015). We conjecture that people with different levels of health consciousness may interpret and use the embodied meanings differently in health-related decisions. Therefore, this study will reveal how the embodiment effect of touch gesture and haptic feedback on users’ healthy behavior is moderated by their health consciousness. By doing so, we can customize designs for users with different levels of health consciousness to enhance the effectiveness of mobile apps in different healthcare contexts.

17502921.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17502921.value: Much research attention has been devoted to designing and evaluating mobile health interventions that aim to explicitly motivate and remind users to maintain a healthy lifestyle, such as personalized notifications and reminders. However, it has been reported that explicit interventions with obvious persuasive intent are often neglected and can even causes users’ psychological reactance. Hence, it is important for researchers and practitioners to understand how to tactfully and effectively promote users’ healthy behavior. This study aims to investigate how to leverage mobile touch experience designs, i.e., digital nudges, to promote users’ healthy behavior implicitly. Specifically, we conceptualize two essential elements constituting mobile touch experience, i.e., touch gesture and haptic feedback. Touch gesture refers to the actions users perform to interact with their mobile devices. Nowadays, mobile devices detect and respond to different touch gestures. While normal touchscreen devices can differentiate long touch and normal touch, the newly launched Huawei Mate 40 Pro can recognize users’ gestures when they move their hands in the air (hover touch). The Xiaomi Black Shark 2 can sense the pressure users apply on the touchscreen and thus enables deep touch. In addition to supporting different touch gestures, the vast majority of mobile devices are equipped with haptic feedback actuators, which can apply forces, vibrations, or motions to users’ skin. Drawing on the theory of embodied cognition, we propose that different touch gestures and haptic feedback will embody different meanings, such as task importance, determination and sense of support, and that these embodied meanings will subliminally influence users’ self-regulation in health behavior. We plan to conduct a series of laboratory and field experiments to test our theoretical model in three contexts, including food ordering, fitness management, and personal hygiene education, with different touch gesture and haptic feedback designs. We expect to examine how different mobile touch experience designs affect users’ food choice, physical exercise and personal hygiene practice and how the effects may change across people with different levels of health consciousness. The experimental results will enrich our theoretical understanding of how people incorporate the embodied meanings in interacting with mobile devices on health-related decision-making. The findings will also have significant practical implications for policy makers and designers about how to create effective digital nudges to enhance users’ health wellbeing with smart mobile touch experience designs. 很多研究关注于设计和评估一些旨在明确激励和提醒用户保持健康生活方式的移动健康干预措施，如个性化的通知和提醒。然而，据报道，具有明显说服意图的明确干预措施往往被忽视，甚至会引起用户的心理抗拒。因此，对于研究人员和从业人员来说，了解如何巧妙地、有效地促进用户的健康行为非常重要。 本研究旨在研究如何利用移动触摸体验设计，即数字助推，来隐含地促进用户的健康行为。具体来说，我们将构成移动触摸体验的两个基本要素概念化，即触摸手势和触觉反馈。触摸手势是指用户与他们的移动设备进行互动的行为。如今，移动设备可以检测并响应不同的触摸手势。普通的触摸屏设备可以区分长触摸和普通触摸，而新推出的华为Mate 40 Pro可以识别用户在空中移动双手时的手势（悬停触摸）。小米黑鲨2可以感知用户在触摸屏上施加的压力，从而实现深度触摸。除了支持不同的触摸手势外，绝大多数移动设备都配备了触觉反馈执行器，可以向用户的皮肤施加力、振动或运动。 借鉴具身认知理论，我们提出不同的触摸手势和触觉反馈将体现不同的意义，如任务的重要性、决心和支持感，这些具身的意义将潜移默化地影响用户在健康行为中的自我调节。我们计划进行一系列的实验室和现场实验，在三种情境下测试我们的理论模型，包括订餐、健身管理和个人卫生教育，并采用不同的触摸手势和触觉反馈设计。 我们期望研究不同的移动触摸体验设计如何影响用户的食物选择、体育锻炼和个人卫生实践，以及这些影响在不同健康意识水平的人群中会有什么变化。 实验结果将丰富我们对人们在与移动设备互动时如何将具身意义纳入健康相关决策的理论理解。这些研究结果也将对政策制定者和设计者产生重要的实际意义，即如何通过智能移动设备的触摸体验设计来创造有效的数字助推，以提高用户的健康福祉。

17502921.label: Realisation of objectives
17502921.value: We have achieved our research objectives. We study how user can be implicitly persuaded by a proper mobile interaction design. Specifically, in Li et al (2023), we investigate the impacts of two touch modes that are supported by force-based interaction technology, i.e., pressing and tapping. Drawing on the theory of embodied cognition, which suggests that people automatically infer meanings from their bodily actions, we conjecture that pressing, compared with tapping, enhances self-regulation because the action of pressing on the touchscreen embodies resolute approach motivation toward goals. We test our hypotheses in three experiments. The first experiment investigates beverage choices on a mobile app; the second experiment examines goal setting on a fitness app; and the third experiment focuses on personal hygiene learning on a mobile education app. The results from the three experiments show that pressing actions can improve users’ self-regulation in selecting a healthier but less tasty beverage (Study 1), setting higher exercise goals and performing more physical exercise (Study 2), and reducing lapses in maintaining personal hygiene (Study 3). In addition, such effects were more salient among users with a higher level of health knowledge and a promotion-focused health orientation. This study contributes to healthcare IT research by showing that mobile interaction can be leveraged to nudge users toward enhanced self-regulation. Our research outcomes have been accepted by major conferences and journals. We have been invited to present at research seminars in different institutions and have also developed related research projects based on the initial proposal.

17502921.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17502921.value: This research examines how the way people physically interact with their smartphones can subtly influence their self-control and healthy behavior. Many mobile apps try to encourage healthier choices—such as exercising more or eating better—by sending reminders or notifications. However, people often ignore these messages or find them annoying. This project explores a different approach: using simple design features of touchscreens to nudge people toward better decisions without pressure. Specifically, the research studies two common touchscreen actions—tapping and pressing—and shows that pressing, which requires more physical effort, can make people feel more determined and motivated. Across several experiments involving food choices, fitness goals, and hygiene practices, the findings show that pressing on a screen can help users resist temptation, set more ambitious health goals, and follow through on good habits. The significance of this research lies in showing how small, low-cost design changes in digital systems can improve well-being in everyday life. The findings provide practical guidance for designing healthier, more effective mobile apps in healthcare, education, and public policy.

17503121.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17503121.value: 通过激发依赖性自我构建来减少食物浪费: 一个资源再分配的视角

17503121.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17503121.value: Dr Gao, Huachao Prof Kim, B. Kyu

17503121.label: Project Objectives
17503121.value: The proposed research aims to contribute to the reduction of food waste, which is a very crucial issue on a global scale. The Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations reports that about 1.6 billion tons of foods are wasted worldwide every year (Gustavsson et al. 2011). In Hong Kong, 3,900 tons of foods are wasted every day (Environment Bureau of Hong Kong 2014). Food waste imposes a myriad of challenges on companies, society, and consumers. Wasted foods represent a waste of resources used in the manufacturing process, such as oil, fresh water, and electricity. Landfilled food wastes adversely influence the environment through polluting the land and ground water and emitting greenhouse gas. A typical American household loses money between $1,560 and $2,275 every year due to uneaten foods (Gunders and Bloom 2017), while many other people are still living in food insecurity. One key driver for food waste in modern society is feelings of abundance (Porpino, Wansink, and Parente 2016). Especially in industrialized countries, consumers generally experience an abundance of available resources (Mehta and Zhu 2016; Zhu and Ratner 2015). The proposed research will shed light on how marketers and public policy makers could mitigate the undesirable consequence of resource abundance on food waste. Theoretically, the proposed project aims to contribute to the emerging stream of research on food waste from a behavioral perspective. Extant research across different disciplines has mainly examined determinants of food waste on the supply side (e.g., manufacturing process and sales promotions). In contrast, behavioral research on what factors contribute to food waste on the consumer side has been scant in the marketing and consumer research literatures until recently (Porpino 2016). This emerging stream of behavioral research has focused on how various cues related to marketing offerings, such as the materials used for food containers (Williamson, Block, and Keller 2016), the visual contrast between labels and food left in containers (Huang et al. 2019), and the visual appearance of food (Grewal at el. 2019), can influence consumers’ food waste. In the proposed research, we extend this emerging stream of behavioral research with a fresh perspective and shift the research focus from marketing offerings onto consumers’ self-view as a determinant of food waste. Specifically, we will explore how an interdependent (vs. independent) self-construal attenuates food waste among resource-abundant consumers. The proposed research is also intended to add to the broad literature on self-construal. We propose that compared to an independent self-construal (i.e., a self-view built on one’s distinctiveness from other people), an interdependent self-construal (i.e., a self-view built on ones’ connectedness with other people) will reduce food waste because an interdependent self-construal activates a sharing obligation. We predict that this sharing obligation will propel consumers to reduce food waste so that they can save more financial resources from their own food consumption and thus be able to re-allocate these resources to help significant others who are in need. Through examining this proposed process, our research aims to highlight sharing obligation as a new mechanism that explains how accessible self-construal influences consumer behavior. Managerially, the proposed project aims to provide highly actionable implications for marketers and public policy makers through examining self-construal as a determinant of food waste. The malleable nature of self-construal makes it possible to situationally activate a specific self-construal through well-conceived marketing communications (Aaker and Lee 2001). One important objective of the proposed research is to create a set of highly actionable marketing interventions based on self-construal, which could be directly applied to relevant consumption contexts, in which food is consumed and could be potentially wasted, such as when consumers dine in restaurants and when consumers watch TV or surf the internet. For example, in a set of field and lab experiments, we will empirically test whether highlighting words such as “we,” “our,” and “us” (vs. “I,” “my,” and “me”) on serving tray liners will effectively reduce the amount of food left uneaten in restaurants and whether showing family-themed (vs. individual-themed) video ads can reduce food waste when consumers stream videos. Moreover, based on our findings, we aim to generate insights into market segmentation and targeting that facilitate food waste reduction initiatives, given that accessible self-construal is associated with a set of cultural and demographic variables, such as country (Eastern vs. Western), ethnicity (Hispanic vs. Caucasian), gender (female vs. male), and area of residence (rural vs. urban; Aaker and Lee 2001; Escalas and Bettman 2005; Winterich et al. 2015; Winterich, Mittal, and Ross 2009). Given the associations between self-construal and these easily identified variables, the findings of the proposed research regarding self-construal will set meaningful directions for marketers and public policy makers to allocate more dedicated effort to the target consumer segments with an independent self-construal and encourage these consumers to make the best use of available food resources rather than waste them.

17503121.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17503121.value: Food waste has a huge impact on the environment, society, and individual consumers. Despite the increasing severity of the food waste problem on a global scale, behavioral research has been scant until recently on what factors influence food waste on the consume side in the marketing and consumer research literatures. One key contributor to food waste is consumers’ possession of abundant financial resources relative to food prices, especially in industrialized countries and emerging economies. The proposed research aims to provide a theoretical analysis of how consumers’ self-view influences their food-wasting behavior. Based on this theoretical analysis and empirical tests with a combination of field experiments, lab experiments, and country-level secondary analysis, we will offer insights into how marketers and public policy makers could attenuate food waste under resource abundance. We propose that compared to an independent self-construal (i.e., a self-view built on distinctiveness from other people), an interdependent self-construal (i.e., a self-view built on connectedness with other people) will reduce individual consumers’ waste of food under resource abundance because an interdependent self-construal activates a sharing obligation. We propose that this activated sharing obligation propels consumers to reduce food waste so that they can save more financial resources from their own food consumption and thus be able to re-allocate these resources to help significant others who are in need. The proposed research aims to make theoretical contributions to the related literatures. Whereas prior research has focused on how factors related to marketing offerings could influence individual consumers’ food waste, the proposed research will contribute to the emerging literature on food waste from a behavioral perspective by identifying self-construal as a consumer-related determinant of food waste. Our findings will also contribute to the self-construal literature by demonstrating that an interdependent (vs. independent) self-construal activates a sharing obligation, which serves as a new mechanism through which self-construal influences consumer behavior. The proposed research will also provide highly actionable implications for marketers and public policy makers in the food and catering services sectors by designing a set of marketing interventions based on self-construal and by demonstrating the effectiveness of these marketing interventions in field experiments in collaboration with restaurants. Through examining self-construal at multiple levels, including the situational, individual, and cultural levels, the proposed research will also shed light on effective segmentation and targeting for food waste reduction initiatives by identifying which segments of consumers are more likely to waste food under resource abundance. 食物浪费对于环境、社会、个体消费者都有着巨大的影响。尽管在全球层面上食物浪费现象日益严重，营销和消费行为文献中直到最近才开始出现有关消费者层面因素如何影响食物浪费行为的研究。 食物浪费的重要诱因之一是相对于食物价格消费者拥有富足的消费资源，这种情况在工业化国家和新兴经济体中尤为突出。本研究的目的在于从理论上分析消费者的自我构建如何影响食物浪费行为。通过这些理论分析，并结合基于实地实验、实验室实验和二手数据的实证检验，我们将为营销人员和政策制定者就如何在资源富足的情况下减少食物浪费行为提供建议。 我们提出相比于独立性自我构建(强调与他人的差异性)，依赖性自我构建(强调与他人的关联)在资源富足的情况下能够通过激发起消费者的分享义务进而来降低食物浪费。我们指出被激发的分享义务会驱使消费者减少食物浪费，从而他们可以从自己的食物消费中节省出消费资源，并将这些资源分享给其他需要帮助的亲朋好友。 我们的研究着眼于对现有的文献做出几个方面的贡献。已有的研究考察了营销层面有关因素如何影响个体消费者的食物浪费行为，本研究则将识别出消费者的自我构建作为影响食物浪费行为的一个个体层面因素，进而从行为学视角延伸了新兴起的有关食物浪费的研究。我们的研究结论也将对自我构建的文献有所贡献。我们的研究将显示依赖性自我构建(相对于独立性自我构建)会激发起更强的分享义务，进而揭示一条自我构建如何影响消费行为的新路径。 同时，我们的研究将为食品餐饮业的营销人员和政策制定者提供具有高度可执行性的建议。通过与餐厅合作的实地实验，我们将基于消费者自我构建设计出一系列营销干预手段来减少食物浪费。通过在情境、个体、文化等多个层面探索自我构建的影响，我们的研究也将识别出哪些消费者在资源富足的情况下更有可能浪费食物，从而为致力于减少食物浪费的营销活动在市场细分和目标市场确定等方面提供理论依据。

17503121.label: Realisation of objectives
17503121.value: ----In relation to Objective 1 stated in Section 5.1, through the projects supported by this GRF, the PI and collaborators have provided solutions regarding how marketers and public policy makers could mitigate the undesirable consequence of resource abundance on food waste. Effective solutions include inducing a scarcity mindset, activating an interdependent self-construal, and activating a sharing mindset. ----In relation to Objective 2 stated in Section 5.1, the projects supported by this GRF advance our understanding of how an interdependent (vs. independent) self-construal attenuates food waste among resource-abundant consumers. Specifically, an interdependent (vs. independent) self-construal reduces consumer food waste through activating sharing obligation. Because consumers need to save resources to share with others in need, sharing obligation reduces consumer food waste. ----In relation to Objective 3 stated in Section 5.1, our research provides direct evidence for the role of sharing obligation as a novel mechanism through which self-construal exerts its effect on consumer food waste. Importantly, self-construal and sharing obligation are two distinctive constructs. That is, only under an abundance mindset will interdependents have a stronger sharing obligation. In contrast, under a scarcity mindset when there is no resource to share, interdependents tend to show a similarly low sharing obligation as independents. Our findings have laid a foundation for future studies to draw on the sharing obligation mechanism to explain other effects of self-construal. ----In relation to Objective 4 stated in Section 5.1, the projects supported by this GRF provide highly actionable implications for marketers and public policy makers. Specifically, activating an interdependent (vs. independent) self-construal could be done by highlighting culture-associated icons, customizing marketing communications, or using a specific language when communicating to bilingual individuals. As shown in our field experiment, marketers could easily activate an interdependent self-construal by highlighting collectivistic values with keywords or slogans on food packages or in-store displays to effectively mitigate food waste. Furthermore, we show that making the sharing concept salient also helps mitigate consumer food waste. Marketers may print sharing-related concepts or words on stickers or brochures. Similarly, public policy makers may encourage the promotion of sharing-related messages by offering sharing-related stickers to consumers or encouraging the printing of sharing-related words on food packages to help mitigate food waste. Emphasizing others’ food needs, such as through a reminder of the current food insecurity reality, can also help reduce food waste. ----In relation to Objective 5 stated in Section 5.1, our findings generate insights into market segmentation and targeting that facilitate food waste reduction initiatives. First, in developed countries such as the U.S., most consumers have an abundance mindset due to living in a relatively affluent society with a wide availability of foods, which results in unnecessary consumer food waste. A scarcity mindset could be easily activated by recalling a personal scarcity experience, by reminders of financial deprivation, or by news about economic downturns. Thus, marketers and public policy makers in developed countries may mitigate consumer food waste by using these strategies to activate a scarcity mindset. For instance, restaurants can serve food on larger plates to mitigate food waste by inducing perceived scarcity, similar to what we did in our field experiment. In addition, since certain consumer segments, such as male (vs. female), Caucasian (vs. Hispanic), and Western (vs. Eastern) consumers, typically have a stronger independent self-construal, special initiatives should be designed to mitigate food waste in these segments.

17503121.label: Major findings and research outcome
17503121.value: Supported by the GRF, the PI and collaborators have completed two projects, which create food waste reduction approaches at the different stages of customer journey. ----The first project has been published in the Journal of Marketing Research (one of the top four journals in the field of marketing) in 2024: Gao, Huachao, He (Michael) Jia, and Bingxuan Guo (2024), “Resources Available for Me versus Us: Implications for Mitigating Consumer Food Waste,” Journal of Marketing Research, 61 (4), 619–37. This paper focuses on food waste reduction at the consumption stage. This paper demonstrates that activating an interdependent (vs. independent) self-construal mitigates food waste among consumers with an abundance mindset, such as those in developed countries. Furthermore, enhancing sharing obligation by highlighting the role of the sharing concept or others’ needs can reduce food waste of independent consumers to a quasi-interdependent level. ---- The second project has been published in the Journal of Business Research (one premiere journal in the field of business) in 2022: Choi, Kang Jun, He (Michael) Jia, Jae Young Lee, B. Kyu Kim, and Keunwoo Kim (2022), “Hedonic Myopia: Emphasizing Hedonic Benefits of Non-Perishable Food Makes Consumers Insensitive to Expiration Dates in Food Purchase,” Journal of Business Research, 138, 193–202. This paper focuses on the food waste reduction at the purchase stage. Consumers have an aversion to near-to-expiry foods that are still safe to eat, consequently leading to a huge amount of safe-to-eat foods not purchased and thus wasted. This project demonstrates that framing foods as hedonic can increase consumers’ purchase of near-to-expiry foods that are still safe to eat. This research has profound implications for reducing food waste at the purchase stage. --In addition, the PI presented the major findings in the Journal of Marketing Research “Mitigation in Marketing” Conference.

17503121.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17503121.value: First, the current GRF-supported projects have examined consumer food waste mitigation at the purchase stage (e.g., encouraging purchases of near-to-expiry foods) and the consumption stage (e.g., saving leftovers for a next meal). Future research may examine other consumer decisions that may result in food waste, for instance, over-acquisition of food. Second, the current GRF-supported projects have developed actionable interventions based on resource mindset, interdependent self-construal, and sharing obligation to mitigate consumer food waste. Future research may create other easy-to-implement interventions based on our theory, which can be effectively tailored to settings where food waste mitigation is relevant and imperative. Third, the current GRF-supported projects have examined how demographic variables, such as nationality as a proxy for self-related cultural values, influence consumer food waste. Future research could further explore other managerially actionable variables that determine consumer food waste, which can facilitate targeting decisions and the design of interventions to reduce consumer food waste.

17503121.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17503121.value: Food waste has a huge impact on the environment, society, and individual consumers. This GRF contributes to the marketing literature by examining factors that reduce consumer food waste at the different stages of customer journey. At the purchase stage, framing food items as hedonic can encourage consumer purchases of near-to-expiry products, thereby reducing food waste. At the consumption stage, activating an interdependent self-construal can effectively reduce food waste. The research findings generate novel theoretical insights into consumer food waste mitigation. Managerially, the findings from this GRF provide actionable implications for marketers and public policy makers regarding effective interventions to mitigate consumer food waste. For instance, our findings suggest that at the purchase stage, marketers may emphasize hedonic features of near-to-expiry food to reduce food waste. At the consumption stage, marketers can reduce food waste through inducing a scarcity mindset, activating an interdependent self-construal, and activating a sharing mindset. The findings of this GRF contribute to an effective guiding framework for consumer food waste mitigation at the different stages of customer journey.

17503221.label: Project Objectives
17503221.value: Build a quantitative model of firm sourcing differentiated products and study the impact of communication costs on sourcing behavior. Derive firm-level predictions as well as aggregate implications on trade and welfare. Consolidate and clean a large transaction-level trade data. Use the transaction-level data to estimate key model parameters. The model can be used to (1) isolate communication costs from overall trade costs, and (2) evaluate the impact of communication cost on trade and welfare. Provide complementary reduced-form evidence using exogenous variation caused by a particular airline regulation. By combining this with the structural model, we plan to estimate the additional communication costs of such regulations and conduct a counterfactual experiment by removing such costs.

17503221.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17503221.value: Trade economists have long been interested in the sources of trade costs. Despite the rapid development of globalization in the past few decades, foreign goods still account for a small share of domestic absorption, especially in large economies. Inferences based on standard trade models imply large trade costs, but the observed transportation costs and tariff barriers in industrial countries are much lower than the inferred ones. A gap therefore exists that may be explained by other costs. In this project, we use theoretical tools, granular firm import transaction data and exogenous variation caused by flight regulation to quantify the importance of communication barriers as a source of trade costs. We build a quantitative model of firm input sourcing and show that differentiated products rely more on communication and are thus more affected by communication costs. We use this property to isolate communication costs from other trade costs. The model can be quantified and used to study the general equilibrium effects of reductions or increases in communication costs. We complement the quantitative analysis using reduced-form evidence that exploits an exogenous variation in flight regulations. 贸易经济学家长期以来一直对贸易成本的来源感兴趣。尽管过去几十年全球化快速发展，外国商品仍占国内消费的一小部分——在大型经济体中更是如此。这导致从标准的贸易模型出发，推算出的贸易成本较大，且远高于能直接观察到的工业国家的运输成本和关税壁垒。因此我们需要其他的成本来解释这两者之间的差别。在本项目中，我们使用理论工具、微观的公司进口交易数据和航班管制造成的外生冲击，来量化沟通成本在贸易成本中的贡献。我们建立了企业采购中间品的定量模型，证明了差异化产品更依赖于沟通，因此更容易受沟通成本的影响。基于这点，我们可以将沟通成本与其他交易成本隔离开来。我们的模型可以量化沟通成本，并对沟通成本的增加进行一般均衡效应的分析。最后，我们利用航班管制规则中的外生变化对我们的模型提供简化形式的证据。

17503521.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17503521.value: Many financial products are complex and the need for protecting financial consumers is widely recognized. However, how to better protect financial consumers is less clear. One measure adopted in many countries is to allow financial consumers to lodge a complaint with the regulator about financial service providers. Regulators differ in how to use such complaint information to the benefit of consumer protection: it may be held internally only for regulatory use, or it can also be made available to the public. Advocates for the latter argue that the complaint information enables financial consumers to better assess the service quality of financial institutions so that financial institutions being complained about can suffer a reputation damage, which in turn constitutes a deterrent for financial institutions. In the aftermath of the 2008 global financial crisis, the creation of the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) authorized by the 2009 Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act in the US and the CFPB’s open-data initiative on disclosing consumer complaints against banks is just an example of this approach. Nevertheless, there is little evidence on whether financial consumers systematically pay attention, and respond, to regulator disclosed complaint information and whether there is a stigma attached to the financial institutions being complained about. We examine these questions in the context of insurance consumption. Due to the complex and contingent nature of contracts, insurance, particularly long-term insurance involving lumpy investment, is well suited for this investigation because insurance is prone to mis-selling ex ante and unfair rejections of claims ex post. We will use proprietary insurance transaction data obtained from a large nationwide insurance company in China and regulators disclosed consumers’ insurance complaint data for the investigation. Studying this topic in large emerging financial markets like China is particularly important because compared to developed markets, insurance consumers in developing markets are more vulnerable to mis-selling and unfair treatment because consumers are less financially literate and insurance market regulation is less developed. Academically, our study adds to the scant research on whether financial consumers pay attention, and respond, to public regulatory disclosure of complaint information – a practice advocated in many countries. In addition, the study has important policy implications for financial regulators including that in Hong Kong – an international financial center that has attracted a large insurance demand from the mainland China, but currently does not have a mechanism to publicly disclose insurance complaints against insurance companies. 很多現代金融產品都很複雜，學界、業界和政策制定者對於消費者在購買金融產品時處於弱勢地位因而需要適當的保護已有鮮有爭議， 但關於如何保護金融消費者則無共識。其中一項舉措是很多國家允許不滿意的消費者向監管當局投訴相關的金融機構，監管當局可以將收到的投訴資訊只作內部使用、也可公之於眾。贊成公之于眾的人士認為這樣可以幫助消費者瞭解不同金融機構的服務品質並從聲譽上懲罰服務品質不高的金融機構，從而促使金融機構有誘因提升服務品質。2008年金融危機後， 美國成立了金融消費者保護局 (the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, CFPB)。 該局加強消費者保護的一項重要舉措就是公開收到的消費者關於銀行的投訴資訊。 雖然如此， 我們並不知道消費者是否留意到監管當局公佈的投訴資訊並在夠買金融產品和服務時回避相關金融機構、從而為相關金融機構造成聲譽損失。 圍繞這一主題, 本研究以保險投訴與消費為分析的視角。長年期的保險產品涉及複雜的條款、其回報具有很大的不確定性，消費者購買產品時容易被仲介誤導、索賠時容易被保險公司拒賠。保險投訴與消費因此提供了一個獨特的分析視角。本課題利用專有的保險資料研究在中國內地保險投訴是否會損害相關保險公司的聲譽並影響其保單銷售。這一問題的答案並不清楚，因有研究表明很多消費者可能不會留意相關資訊、認知上也有局限性。本課題對於香港特別行政區進一步提升作為國際金融中心的地位也有借鑒意義，因香港目前還沒有將公開保險投訴作為保護消費者的一種手段。
