17609521.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17609521.value: The importance of investing in the early years of childhood development is no longer a matter of debate. The significance of nurturing care in this period is highlighted by research documenting both the influence of early stimulation on brain development and the economic returns of attending early childhood education (ECE) programmes. Furthermore, global recognition of the importance of early childhood for human and societal development is reflected in the United Nations Sustainable Development Goal Target 4.2, which focuses exclusively on early childhood development (ECD) and ECE. About 32% of the world’s under-19 population lives in China and India, and millions of children under 5 years in these countries will not achieve their potential because of poverty and stunting. Understanding the factors that promote ECD – from both theoretical and practical perspectives – is therefore valuable. Extant literature documents the positive impact of public policy and developmentally appropriate early learning environments on early childhood outcomes. One of the best predictors of ECD is maternal education, and mothers who have completed school provide more stimulating home learning environments than do their less-educated peers. Against this background, we examine the impacts of maternal education (which influences home learning environments) and policy (education, health, fertility) on indicators of ECD (under-5 mortality, stunting) over time in the world’s population billionaires. Female literacy has increased and under-5 mortality and stunting have decreased in both countries. However, China shows improvements that are more marked than India in indicators of child well-being. We will leverage data from repeated nationally representative surveys to detail changes in ECD indicators over time. In addition, country case studies (including documentary analyses and intergenerational interviews) will analyse the impact of educational policies related to girls’ education, public health strategies and ECE attendance on ECD. We predict that maternal education will be positively related to stimulating home learning environments, but that the impact of maternal education on child development will vary across policy contexts. Specifically, when public health systems are inadequate, maternal education may be a stronger predictor of ECD in poorer, larger and rural families than other families. Findings will illuminate contextual differences in perceptions of benefits of educating girls across and within two countries that traditionally have a strong son preference. The project is also timely as it is estimated that globally about 20 million girls will drop out of school because of the impact of the CoVID-19 pandemic. 投資於兒童早期發展的重要性已無需爭辯。大量研究已經充分證明早期刺激對大腦發展的重要影響以及就讀幼兒教育課程的經濟回報。這些結果突顯了在早期階段對兒童進行養育性照護（nurturing care）的重要性。此外，主力關注早期兒童發展和幼兒教育的《聯合國可持續發展目標4.2》也反映出國際認同早期階段對個體和社會發展的重要性。 全球有大約32%的19歲以下人口居住在中國和印度，而當中有數以百萬計5歲以下兒童可能因為貧窮和發育遲緩而無法達到預期發展水平。因此，從理論和實踐的角度去了解促進早期兒童發展的因素是相當有價值的。已有文獻記錄了公共政策和適齡的學習環境對幼兒期發展有正面影響。其中，母親的教育程度是對早期兒童發展最有影響力的預測指標之一：完成學校課程的母親比起其他年齡相若但教育程度較低的母親，更能為幼兒提供具啟發性的家庭學習環境。 有鑒於此，我們的研究關注隨著世界人口增長，母親教育程度（與家庭學習環境相關）和公共政策（教育、健康、生育率）對早期兒童發展關鍵指標（5歲以下兒童死亡率及發育遲緩）的影響。無論在中國還是印度，女性的識字率都有所提高，而5 歲以下兒童的死亡率和發育遲緩度均有所下降。然而，中國在兒童身心健康和福祉指標方面的進步比印度更為顯著。我們將利用重複進行且具有全國代表性的調查數據來考察早期兒童發展指標的變化趨勢。此外，我們將運用國家層面的個案研究（包括文件分析和跨代訪談）分析與女童教育、公共衛生策略和幼兒教育入學率的相關教育政策對早期兒童發展的影響。我們預測，母親教育程度將有助於提供具刺激性的家庭學習環境，但母親教育程度對兒童發展的影響會因政策背景而有所不同。具體而言，當公共衛生系統不理想時，與其他家庭相比，在較貧窮、家庭成員較多的農村家庭中，母親教育可能對早期兒童發展更有影響力。 研究結果將有助於闡明兩個在傳統上傾向重男輕女的國家對女童教育的看法和相關的背景差異。本研究也具有及時的現實意義，因為由於新冠肺炎疫情的影響，全球估計約有二千萬女童將面臨輟學的危機。

17609921.label: Project Title(Chinese)

17609921.label: Project Objectives
17609921.value: To synthesize the current English language scholarship on postgraduate legal education reform in China, Japan and Korea, and augment and reshape these perspectives by cross-referencing native language scholarship that has hereto been overlooked in international evaluations. To use qualitative interview data to map the specific local and international networks by which lawyer and non-lawyer reformers in each country came to form their opinions about postgraduate legal education, its potential as a mechanism for social change, and how reform challenges and the ongoing crisis in American postgraduate legal education have subsequently influenced such opinions. To establish the regional interconnections between Japanese, Korean and Chinese scholars on legal education reform, and promote awareness of parallel regional reforms by organizing the first East Asian conference on postgraduate legal education reform including scholars from countries beyond the region considering such reforms. To contextualize the Korean, Japanese and Chinese reform experiences in larger debates about the role of modern lawyers and legal reform in East Asian countries, and how these experiences potentially inform global debates occurring about the political and economic relevance of lawyer regulation. To strengthen engagement between academic and non-academic audiences concerned with lawyer regulation by integrating relevant regional governmental, bar association, and civil society groups with each other and those working on legal education reform internationally. To produce one chapter, three articles, a book proposal and one edited volume of internationally-leading caliber publicized through presentations at leading conferences and professional associations all of which will collectively provide a comprehensive state-of-the-art assessment of the empirical evidence regarding the impact of postgraduate legal education reform on the East Asian legal professions and various social outcomes as well as a corollary set of best practices for future postgraduate legal reforms efforts.

17609921.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17609921.value: This project is concerned with evaluating the modern legal education reforms undertaken by three East Asian countries—Japan, Korea and China—meant to improve their legal professions by emphasizing postgraduate legal education. A generally strong consensus exists today that legal institutions are crucial to economic and political development. For lawyers, legal education serves as a foundational element in their training and orientation, and thus it has become common globally for reforming legal education to be seen as an effective policy response to reshaping national legal professions. In Korea, reform was absolute—undergraduate law programs were eliminated in favor of postgraduate law degrees. In Japan, reform was mixed—postgraduate law programs now co-exist with undergraduate faculties. In China, reform was milder—postgraduate programs were introduced while most lawyers still pursued undergraduate degrees. Reform outcomes have been hotly contested, leaving reformers unsatisfied, lawyers facing new anxieties, and further reform efforts stymied. The project will be the first to move beyond evaluating reform outcomes to explaining how postgraduate legal education initially came to be seen as a common regional solution. The project’s hypothesis is that transnational communication between domestic reformers and international policy entrepreneurs produced distorted understandings of such reforms' potential impact influenced by stylized views of the American postgraduate model—now undergoing an existential crisis casting doubt on its use as a model for reform. This project will provide an interdisciplinary, comparative study using a novel focus on the formation of reform agendas by key domestic reform constituencies. It will cross-reference extant international studies with native language scholarship often neglected by foreign researchers. Field visits to law schools to gather interview data will augment this synthesis by documenting how views regarding postgraduate legal education’s potential for change were formed, mapping the transnational legal networks which shaped these views, and revealing how they have been affected by reform frustrations. This research will ground regional comparison between all three countries, further comparisons across East and Southeast Asia, and integrate these experiences into international debates about legal education reform. Understanding distortions in transnational legal communication will enable the formulation of recommendations for improving international legal collaboration, provide specific calibrations for these three national legal education reforms projects, and challenge existing presumptions in the wider scholarship. Furthermore, the one book chapter, three articles, and edited volume produced by the project will show how these reform efforts speak to larger and ever more pressing global debates over the role of lawyers in political change and economic globalization. 该项目涉及评估三个东亚国家, 日本、韩国和中国, 进行的现代法律教育改革，旨在通过强调研究生法律教育来改善他们的法律专业。今天普遍存在强烈共识，即法律制度对经济和政治发展至关重要。对于律师而言，法律教育是其培训和定位的基础要素，因此将法律教育改革视为重塑国家法律职业的有效政策反应已成为全球普遍现象。 在韩国，改革是绝对的, 取消了法学本科课程，取而代之的是法学研究生学位。在日本，改革是混合的, 法学研究生课程现在与本科院系共存。在中国，改革较为温和, 引入了研究生课程，而大多数律师仍在攻读本科学位。改革成果众说纷纭，改革者不满，律师面临新焦虑，进一步改革受阻。 该项目将是第一个超越评估改革成果，解释研究生法律教育最初如何被视为共同区域解决方案的项目。该项目的假设是，国内改革者和国际政策企业家之间的跨国交流对此类改革的潜在影响产生了扭曲的理解，这种理解受到美国研究生模式风格化观点的影响, 现在正经历着一场生存危机, 人们对其作为改革模式的使用产生了怀疑。 该项目将提供跨学科的比较研究，重点关注国内主要改革支持者的改革议程的形成。它将与外国研究人员经常忽视的母语奖学金交叉引用现存的国际研究。实地访问法学院以收集采访数据将通过记录有关研究生法律教育变革潜力的观点是如何形成的，绘制当时形成的跨国法律网络，并揭示这些观点如何受到改革失败的影响，从而加强这种综合。这项研究将为所有三个国家之间的区域比较、东亚和东南亚的进一步比较奠定基础，并将这些经验与关于法律教育改革的国际辩论相结合。 了解跨国法律交流中的扭曲将使 PI 提出改善国际法律合作的建议, 为这三个国家法律教育改革项目提供具体校准，并挑战更广泛学术界的现有假设。此外，该项目制作的一本书一章、三篇文章和编辑过的卷将展示这些改革努力如何与关于律师在政治变革和经济全球化中的作用的更广泛、更紧迫的全球辩论相联系。

17610321.label: Project Title(Chinese)

17610321.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17610321.value: 快速的工业化与城市化使得中国成为世界上最大的能源消耗者和二氧化碳排放者之一。中国城市作为消耗能源经济活动集中的中心，自然成为控制二氧化碳排放的焦点。本研究旨在探讨中国近年来低碳城市发展的现状，过程与成效。研究的目的要三个：1）刻划中国低碳城市发展的特征与过程；2）探索低碳城市发展牵涉的利益主体及其策略；3）评估低碳城市发展的经济，社会与地理空间效应。本项目的研究方法包括国家层面系统的城市统计资料分析和特例（深圳与沈阳）详尽田野社会调查。 通过系统的统计资料分析，个案调查，田野和深入面谈，此项研究旨在揭示中国新兴的低碳城市发展的形态，特征，形成机制，空间分异及成败规律，更新并提高对中国城市研究的理论水平和方法，并为低碳城市发展规划与政策的制定及实施提供科学的知识基础。；

17610921.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17610921.value: 預防為主，防治結合——對建立“一帶一路”爭端預防機製的評估

17610921.label: Project Objectives
17610921.value: Drawing on a qualitative, triangulating approach analyzing public facilitation policy design and case-based implementation, this project will examine the research question of whether, and if so how the design of multi-stakeholder community-investor public facilitation mechanisms contribute to the prevention and early resolution of infrastructure disputes and advancement of sustainable development objectives along the Belt and Road. It will compare the efficacy of mandated preventative tools (early stage community facilitation) with elective late stage post-conflict grievance mechanisms (mediation/arbitration) to answer the overarching question of whether ‘an ounce of prevention is worth a pound of cure?’ in community-investor dispute resolution. In particular, it will assess indicators of mandatory early stage engagement (ADB's Safeguard Policy Statement ('SPS') project information disclosure and consultation processes; and AIIB's project based Stakeholder Engagement Plans ('SEP')) alongside elective late stage engagement mechanisms (IFC) to understand the impact of elective or mandatory mechanisms on the subsequent incidence, frequency and resolution of project related disputes. In so doing, the project will contribute to more effective research and practice in public infrastructure dispute resolution. In particular, the project will pursue the following objectives: · Theorize the dynamics of community-investor dispute prevention and resolution by identifying policy and substantive principles observed from practice · Analyze and compare the efficacy of preventative tools (i.e. mandated early stage public facilitation through ADB's SPS disclosure and consultation processes and AIIB's SEP engagement plans) with elective late stage post-conflict approaches (IFC's mediation/arbitration mechanism) through indicator analysis, case studies, interviews and surveys of neutrals and legal professionals along the Belt and Road corridor · Contribute to the development of case insights regarding conditions for successful community engagement through the identification of contributions, challenges and lessons learned in community-investor public facilitation mechanisms from a comparative, devolved and policy oriented perspective · Apply case insights to the development of policy recommendations for Hong Kong, Qianhai and the greater China region · Disseminate the findings in the form of a research monograph, journal articles and conference presentations

17610921.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17610921.value: This project will explore the development of community-investor dispute prevention and facilitation mechanisms in the context of the Belt and Road Initiative (“BRI”). As an infrastructure financing initiative, the BRI aims to strengthen infrastructure linkages along the Belt and Road corridor spanning Asia, Africa and Europe. Given the wide-scale impact of China’s multi-jurisdictional development initiative, understanding how best to coordinate with local communities is vital to realizing the benefits of sustainable growth. In the 20 years since the development of the first multilateral community-investor dispute resolution mechanism – established by the International Finance Centre/World Bank ("IFC") – much has been learned about public facilitation, community engagement and dispute prevention during the early stages of major infrastructure development programs. With the creation of the International Commercial Dispute Prevention and Settlement Organization under the China Council for the Promotion of International Trade in April 2019, dispute prevention through community engagement has taken center stage in China’s dispute settlement policy and has become a mandatory pre-infrastructure project assessment requirement. Thus far, only limited systematic examination has been undertaken of the contours of community-investor dispute prevention, its relationship with formal dispute resolution mechanisms, and overall contribution to sustainable development in the context of the BRI. To address this gap, the present research will be the first comprehensive study of its kind to analyze mandatory BRI dispute prevention mechanisms within the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank ("AIIB") and the Asian Development Bank ("ADB") to determine whether ‘an ounce of prevention is worth a pound of cure?’ in community-investor dispute resolution. In particular, it will assess the impact of the nature of community engagement (elective/mandatory) on the incidence, frequency and subsequent resolution of project related disputes. Drawing on a case-based methodology, it will explore the achievements, challenges and lessons learned in community-investor dispute prevention and resolution for major infrastructure projects with a view to providing relevant recommendations from a devolved collaboration perspective. The project will result in new insights regarding the conditions for successful community-investor engagement applicable not only in the greater China region but beyond. The findings will be disseminated through a research monograph, journal articles and conference presentations. 本項目旨在探討在“一帶一路”倡議的背景下建立社區-投資者爭端預防和促進機製的可行性。作為一項基礎設施建設融資倡議，“一帶一路”旨在加強橫跨亞洲、非洲和歐洲的“一帶一路”經濟走廊在基礎設施建設方面的聯系。鑒於中國的多管轄區發展倡議產生的廣泛影響，了解與當地社區進行協調的最優方式，對於實現整體利益最大化至關重要。自國際金融中心/世界銀行製定的第一個多邊社區-投資者爭端解決機製建立以來的20年裏，我們在重大基礎設施發展項目的早期階段，在公共便利、社區參與和爭端預防等方面收獲良多。隨著2019年4月中國國際貿易促進委員會下屬的國際商事爭端預防與解決組織的成立，爭端預防在中國的爭端解決政策中占據了核心位置。然而，到目前為止，對於社區-投資者爭端預防的框架、其與正式爭端解決機製的關系以及在“一帶一路”背景下對可持續發展的整體貢獻等方面，系統性地研究非常有限。為了彌補這一空白，本項目將是第一個對亞洲基礎設施投資銀行和亞洲開發銀行框架內現有的“一帶一路”投資爭端預防機製進行的全面研究。本項目將基於案例分析的研究方法，探討在重大基礎設施建設項目的社區-投資者爭端預防和解決方面的成就、挑戰和經驗，以期從權力下放的合作角度提供相關建議。該項目將就投資者與社區成功合作的條件提出新的見解，並且不僅適用於大中華地區，也將適用於其他地區。研究結果將通過專著、期刊文章和會議展示來傳播。

17610921.label: Realisation of objectives
17610921.value: Each of the research objectives of this project has been achieved. They will be discussed in detail below: I. First Objective: Drawing on a qualitative, triangulating approach analyzing public facilitation policy design and case-based implementation, this project will examine the research question of whether, and if so how the design of multi-stakeholder community-investor public facilitation mechanisms contribute to the prevention and early resolution of infrastructure disputes and advancement of sustainable development objectives along the Belt and Road. Realization of Objective I: The culminating output of the project, An Ounce of Prevention: Dispute Mitigation in Multilateral Infrastructure Development in the Asia Pacific Region (Cambridge University Press, forthcoming) drew on a multi-method research approach to examine policy design and case-based practice of community-investor dispute prevention and facilitation mechanisms employed by multilateral and national development banks operating in the Asia Pacific region. Drawing on 12 case studies, project statistical analysis and survey data, it explores the achievements, challenges and lessons learned in community-investor dispute prevention and resolution in infrastructure development projects and provides relevant recommendations. The findings confirm the adage that an ounce of prevention is in fact worth a pound of cure in the infrastructure context, yet challenges remain in facilitating effective preventative measures. II. Second Objective: Theorize the dynamics of community-investor dispute prevention and resolution by identifying policy and substantive principles observed from practice Realization of Objective II: The second objective is realized in the forthcoming CUP Publication. It finds that while infrastructure development theory has largely extended beyond an emphasis on top-down approaches to planning and implementation with growing recognition of the importance of community engagement to advance project sustainability, legitimacy and responsiveness, much of this research has been conducted in western contexts. Limited evidence of impacts of community-based engagement on dispute prevention is available in the Asia Pacific region. This study demonstrates that where practices of community engagement through consultation, information sharing, grievance mechanisms and accountability are robust, a higher incidence of project completion and dispute mitigation is reported. It likewise traces the significant role of decentralized and joint knowledge generation amongst independent accountability mechanism professionals within multilateral and national banking institutions, NGO’s and community groups in contributing to increasingly harmonized legal and policy innovations for expanded community access and accountability. These findings are consistent with prior research on the efficiency gains of cohesive, inclusive and meaningful local partnerships and the significance of decentralized transnational legal ordering. III. Third Objective: Analyze and compare the efficacy of preventative tools (i.e. mandated early stage public facilitation through ADB's SPS disclosure and consultation processes and AIIB's SEP engagement plans) with elective late stage post-conflict approaches (IFC's mediation/arbitration mechanism) through indicator analysis, case studies, interviews and surveys of neutrals and legal professionals along the Belt and Road corridor Realization of Objective III: The third objective of this project is addressed in Part II of the book, An Ounce of Prevention which explores community engagement statistics, case studies and survey findings in the Asia Pacific region before 2013 when pre-project community engagement practices were largely discretionary to post-2013 when more robust mandatory procedures were introduced. Project data, survey findings and comparative case studies suggest that the introduction of heightened pre-project community consultation and grievance mechanisms within global multilateral development banks in the mid 2010-20’s have corresponded with a drop in the percentage of grievances per project from 15.4% in 2019 to 7.1% in 2021. While this downward trend has been followed by a slight resurgence simultaneously after 2021, the lack of consultation, disclosure or due diligence was no longer the single most cited cause of grievances amongst project affected communities. Greater attention to pre-project due diligence and community awareness of grievance channels appear to account for these findings. Survey findings of 55 practitioners engaged in infrastructure related dispute prevention in the Asia Pacific region likewise demonstrated that prior community consultation was considered the most effective approach to preventing infrastructure disputes and that overall, most disputes arose because of lack of adequate consultation with members of the community. Similarly, the 12 community-investor dispute case studies show that in circumstances of increasingly heightened standards for mandated community consultation as compared with ad-hoc discretionary consultation practices, the number of stalled/cancelled and litigated case declined by 33%, the percentages of cases referred to local courts declined by 16%, and the number of cases pursuing party agreement through mediation or negotiation increased by 50%. Overall, these findings provide measured evidence supporting the development of increasingly robust community consultative engagement channels, particularly for multilateral and national banks which have not yet implemented such policies. Such engagement channels, far from aggregating complaints, conversely correlate with a reduction in the overall proportion of project disputes. IV. Fourth Objective: Contribute to the development of case insights regarding conditions for successful community engagement through the identification of contributions, challenges and lessons learned in community-investor public facilitation mechanisms from a comparative, devolved and policy-oriented perspective Realization of Objective IV: The book resulted in the following case insights regarding challenges and conditions for successful community engagement. Key challenges included insufficient community consultation, lack of environmental planning, inadequate compensation for relocation, damage to local resources including water and farmland, economic harm, forced land transfer, duress, undue influence, lack of consent and limited external monitoring, obfuscation of facts and ‘uni-directional’ rather than multi-directional consultation. Factors associated with successful community engagement included heightened precision in consultation, diligence and grievance mechanisms and common identification of issues of community concern, higher pre-project diligence and screening standards, ongoing environmental and technical monitoring, locally trained mediators, consultation skill development, a longer term view of community welfare and responsive grievance remedies, early stakeholder involvement, involvement of local government, transparency, application of appropriate consultation standards relative to project risk. V. Fifth Objective: Apply case insights to the development of policy recommendations for Hong Kong, Qianhai and the greater China region Realization of Objective IV: The study provides a set of five recommendations that are relevant to the greater China region and beyond including national bank training, model standards development and case information sharing. Drawing on BRI cases in Chapter 7 examining the contributions and challenges in advancing sustainable development along the BRI and efforts at engagement with local communities, the study confirms that when project funders reference robust host country ESG standards with higher pre-project diligence and accountability requirements, disputes tend to be avoided, while conversely when referencing lax host country standards, gaps in diligence often give rise to disputes. 6. · Disseminate the findings in the form of a research monograph, journal articles and conference presentations The project resulted in 1 book (ranked A* by RQF); 2 Edited Volumes (A RQF); 7 journal articles/book chapters and 22 conference contributions.

17610921.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17610921.value: Directions for continued research include identifying relevant principles that may guide the community consultation processes in diverse cultural settings; examining the forms of community representation that result in manageably sized groups to advance high quality decision making; exploring the type of preparation necessary to ensure that individuals have the requisite skills and capabilities to constructively engage in the consultation process; exploring the safeguards needed to protect the integrity and objectivity of the consultation process and prevent it from fraud and coercion; exploring how consultation may interface with the precautionary principle to fill in knowledge and policy gaps, examining the type of systems that can track effective implementation and the potential interface with AI and ethics. No doubt, shared learning amongst members of the infrastructure development community to advance genuine consultative engagement for community prosperity will strengthen the beneficial impact of such projects.

17611321.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17611321.value: 親國民黨報刊中的「文革」話語：以《香港時報》與《萬人雜誌》為例

17611321.label: Project Objectives
17611321.value: By considering newspapers as “a structure of meaning” (Hall, 1975) and historicizing the production of newspaper messages in the changing ideological milieu of Hong Kong, Taiwan, and mainland China during Cold War, I will interpret representations of CR and the narration of local/national identities in HKT/PM in the 1960s and 1970s. As both these publications were pro-KMT, this will allow me to expand on my ECS project, which mainly focused on left-wing periodicals’ interpretations of CR. The project will go beyond traditional studies of KMT–Hong Kong relations that have taken a “national-to-local” approach and consider KMT as a regime that carried out national missions and achieved political goals in Hong Kong society through its work with refugees, labor unions, educational circles, and other communities. It will take a localizing (在地化; Chan 2014) approach that emphasizes local appropriations of KMT nationalist ideology in HKT and PM. The project will treat HKT’s and PM’s representations of CR as a discourse and illuminate how CR intensified the confrontations and dialogues between (1) two sociopolitical-cultural movements: KMT’s Chinese Cultural Renaissance Movement (CCRM, 中華文化復興運動) and CCP’s CR; (2) two polarized ideologies: KMT’s ethnic nationalism and Communist class-inflected nationalism; (3) three political regimes: Communist, KMT, and the colonial government; and (4) two ideas: Hong Kong as a battlefield of “anti-Communism and national restoration 反共復國” and Hong Kong as home. The project will explore the complexity of Chinese nationalism in the political, ideological, ethnical, cultural, economic, and geographical senses. Through the lens of CR discourse, this project will examine how Chinese nationalism was appropriated to imagine a certain Hong Kong identity in the 1960s and 1970s against the background of emerging local consciousness and colonialism in order to illustrate the complex interconnection of local-national identification. The project will explore how representations of CR were signified by HKT and PM differently according to KMT nationalism against the local/colonial context, with the aim of discussing how HKT/PM promoted a certain kind of Hong Kong identity for the local Chinese community through an anti-CR narrative, their reliance on KMT nationalism as an ideological source, their promotion of Taiwan’s government as a model utopian society, and their appropriation of KMT’s anti-Communist tactics and alliances for their local purposes. This project will critically revisit the prevailing view that Hong Kong identity formation in the 1960s and 1970s resulted from successful colonial welfare policies instituted during the MacLehose period (1971–1982) and highlight the role of the complexity of Chinese nationalism, which has been marginalized in scholarship on the Hong Kong identity formation process in the 1960s and 1970s. The neglect of Chinese nationalism results in what Lui Tai-Lok (2013) calls “a time gap” in Hong Kong’s history between the 1967 riots and the mid-1970s, when a local identity emerged. By illustrating the multifaceted nature of Hong Kong identity formation in that period, this GRF project, together with my ECS, will underscore the continuity of Hong Kong history in the 1970s. This project will write Hong Kong into the studies on global Maoism by offering a new perspective on the study of “CR in Hong Kong”. Existing studies on CR in Hong Kong focus on the 1967 riots, a mass movement influenced by CR, but rarely discuss the ideological conflicts related to CR in local print media. The project will highlight the spread of CR ideology and Maoism and their encounter with KMT nationalism in Hong Kong. This will provide interesting comparative insights for the studies on the global history of Maoism by exploring the idea of “reception as resistance” and by demonstrating how the two publications mobilized anti-Communist narratives to develop local/national identification. For example, HKT incorporated an anti-CR perspective into its KMT nation-building project, while the reception of Maoism in PM was also a form of resistance to it. The project will illustrate the distinctiveness of Hong Kong during Cold War and highlight Hong Kong as a “liminal space” where concepts such as Chinese nationalism (in various forms), “free China 自由中國”, and “totalitarianism” coexisted with and contested each other, transcending the traditional opposition between communism and capitalism. The project will address the KMT’s response to CR and highlight the overlooked role of CR in intensifying the ideological confrontations in the colony during Cold War, foregrounding the specific experience of Cold War in the Hong Kong context.

17611321.value: 目前有關「文革在香港」的研究，因主要聚焦在香港「六七暴動」，故此傾向將「文革」視為一場社會政治運動，並在很大程度上忽略「文革」加劇香港左派與親國民黨媒體之間的意識形態衝突的作用。雙方在冷戰期間透過不同的「文革」表述，向特定的讀者群，宣傳不同的國族身份。秉承對現代中文報紙的研究傳統，本計劃是首個透過親國民黨報刊對「文革」的解讀，探討香港的國族及本土認同轉變的歷史考察，關注點是國民黨的意識形態如何論述某種香港身份，同時，此研究不同於現存「國民黨在香港」的研究集中在「難民」及「勞工」這兩方面。 本計劃研究的兩份刊物雖然都擁護國民黨民族主義，卻對國民黨政權及本地事務持不同的態度。此點最能說明國民黨官方與非官方視點如何在香港表述「文革」。作為國民黨喉舌的《香港時報》，將「文革」視為對「民族復興」的威脅，並利用「中華文化復興運動」對抗「文革」，從而促進國族認同的構建；《萬人雜誌》既視「文革」為本地華人的「自由」危機，亦藉著「文革」批評國民黨的怯懦，它希望透過支持國民黨民族主義，將香港建立為一個能夠安置中國難民的地方。《萬人雜誌》與其他親國民黨報刊的不同之處，在於其對毛主義修辭的諷刺性運用，展現出其以批評的方式來「接受」毛主義。 殖民語境及港人在七十年代以後對本地事務的日益關注，是香港身份認同話語不可或缺的一部份。《香港時報》徘徊於反共任務與本地問題之間，它既默許殖民統治的不平等，並在不知不覺間成為英國反共的共謀，同時又批評殖民統治以吸納本地華人的支持。《萬人雜誌》則透過抨擊「文革」及殖民統治的不公義，連結及團結台灣與香港人民，以在本地建立一個更好的社會。通過反「文革」話語，本計劃認為香港認同是一種協商於國族及本土之間的話語，貫穿在政治、意識形態、族群、文化、經濟及地理形式的身份爭論之中。 在我的「傑出青年學者計劃」的研究基礎上，本計劃的原創性在於利用國民黨的民族主義、反共策略及盟友等元素，與1960至1970年代香港人身份認同興起的時間點作出對話。本計劃將利用較少人研究的報刊、檔案及訪問，揭示國民黨的意識形態與「文革」的思想對話是香港身份認同形成的其中一個重要因素。相關的學術成果，亦會進一步推動大眾對香港歷史及報刊文化的認識。

17612621.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17612621.value: 老人雙眼視覺系統的知覺學習及可塑性

17612621.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17612621.value: Dr Ban, Hiroshi Prof Cheong, Ming Yan Allen

17612621.label: Project Objectives
17612621.value: Objective 1 (Task 1). To characterise the nature of the binocular (stereoscopic) visual improvements that can be attained with perceptual learning in the aging brain. -In this task, we will behaviourally characterise the plasticity of the aging binocular (stereoscopic) system, using psychophysics to ask whether signal-noise or fine discrimination depth training can drive improvements in depth sensitivity in those aged 60-80 years. As these two tasks are assumed to target different mechanisms underlying perceptual efficiency (fine: feature-specific representations; signal-noise: external noise filtration), the degree of learning that can be attained should reflect the relative plasticity of these two mechanisms. Learning effects will be compared to those attained for younger adults Objective 2 (Task 2). To characterise the neural mechanisms underlying the decline of binocular (stereoscopic) function in aging, and to reveal the neuroplastic substrates underlying perceptual training-driven changes. -In this task, we will use whole-brain functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) to image blood-oxygen-dependent (BOLD) activity before and after perceptual training in older and younger observers.

17612621.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17612621.value: The world’s population is aging and it is therefore of particular importance to both understand the consequences of aging on the nervous system and to develop methods that may help mitigate against age-related functional decline. It is well-demonstrated that the capacity to visually detect or discriminate both monocular (e.g., orientation, motion) and binocular (e.g., depth) features decline with age. Importantly, these declines are not the product of changes in the optical machinery (i.e., the aging eyes), but rather reflect changes at the cortical level, potentially reflecting declines in inhibitory, GABAergic mechanisms. Here, we aim to test the role of perceptual learning in driving visual (stereoscopic) plasticity in the aging brain, integrating behavioural and neuroimaging (fMRI/MRS) methods in order to characterise not only the nature and extent of learning that can be achieved through perceptual training, but the neuroplastic mechanisms underlying these changes. The eventual goal of this work is to springboard methods that can be developed to help mitigate against age-related perceptual decline, and by extension to ameliorate quality of life. 世界人口正在老化，因此了解神經系統老化帶來的影響，以及研發如何緩和與老齡有關的功能減退尤其重要。已有的研究證實了視覺偵測和區辨單眼（例如：方位和運動）及雙眼特徵（例如：深度）的能力會隨著年齡的增長而衰退。重要的是，這些衰退不是由光學器質的變化（眼睛老化）而引起的，而是可能與大腦皮層的抑制性神經遞質γ-氨基丁酸的機能下降有關。本研究的目的是測試知覺學習在誘發老年人大腦的立體視覺可塑性中所發揮的作用，並結合行為和神經影像（功能性磁力共振影像）的方法來描述知覺學習的性質和可達到的程度，並進一步研究引起這些變化背後的神經可塑性機制。此項工作的最終目標是以此研究為跳板，研發緩和與老齡相關知覺減退的方法，進而改善生活質素。

17613121.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17613121.value: 改造工具箱 2.0：鄉村建築更新後的的可持續性評估

17613121.label: Project Objectives
17613121.value: To document cases where villagers adapted vernacular dwellings to better suit the realities of their modernized daily lives: In our preliminary GRF research we already discovered surprising renovation strategies by villagers in three different rural regions in China. It was the residents themselves who made intelligent changes to their vernacular dwellings in order to accommodate new forms of living. We eventually came to understand some of these transformations as quite successful solutions in bringing together vernacular and industrialized building methods and in combining traditional cultural values and contemporary lifestyles. To identify and catalogue renovation strategies and adaptations utilizing photography and technical/architectural drawing: We aim to identify renovation strategies that exemplify a delicate symbiosis of vernacular building knowledge and modern lifestyle, and develop a more precise understanding of how informal design decisions relate to both daily lives and the larger socio-demographic changes taking place in rural China. To design a more comprehensive framework for the assessment of environmental sustainability, cultural sustainability and social sustainability: We want to bring together three different perspectives on sustainability to refine the standard framework of a ‘sustainability assessment’. Environmental sustainability in this framework demonstrates efficient use of energy and involves measuring several key environmental values, including daylight, ventilation, heat and the comfort zone of the selected house. Social sustainability assesses the renovation strategy in relation to the ability for future generations to maintain a healthy community. Cultural sustainability examines how local building knowledge as an integral part of cultural identity is preserved through spontaneous renovation. We aim to supplement existing sustainability assessment methodologies and develop a framework for the specific context of adapted vernacular houses. To develop sustainability using architectural drawings and diagrams as analytical tools: We will indicate the sustainability of the case studies in all three sustainability aspects through diagrams and drawings, and, in doing so, aim to underline the value of renovation as opposed to demolition. By focusing on the house, we are choosing to address a scale that village dwellers and policy makers can relate to, rendering the topic of sustainability more tangible. We suggest that new notions of sustainability need to be engendered amongst villagers, practitioners and the public, instead of purely among those in positions of power. To identify the best strategies that have a combination of three aspects of sustainability: environmental, cultural and social: We will select the three best cases that can lead to innovative adaptations and verify their effectiveness in sustainability. To compile our findings into a guide book, showcasing the best renovation strategies and their assessment, narrating through drawings and interviews how these adaptations combine environmental, social, and cultural values: As local villagers renovate the vernacular houses, they could be assisted via the findings in the guide book. The guide book will be made accessible to diverse actors, including local builders, government policymakers, and architects elsewhere interested in vernacular architecture, and may inform continuing renovations.

17613121.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17613121.value: For hundreds of years, innovation in the architecture of housing has happened without architects. Vernacular architecture is understood as the ‘built tradition’: bound to a specific place that developed over long periods, and reflecting local conditions concerning climate, landscape, available material, craft, and social structures. Throughout China, traditional dwellings are being abandoned and replaced by formulaic concrete houses that are fast and cheap in construction but may not respond to climatic and cultural conditions, and as lifestyle and family structures have changed, these spatially generic houses no longer reflect the lives being lived within them. However, in parallel with this gradual abandonment of old houses, there are some remarkable hybrid experiments taking place where rural builders use modern materials and construction methods to transform their vernacular dwellings. In these intelligent house adaptations, owners manage to implement their contemporary way of living within a traditional building. We refer to these hybrids as “adapted vernacular houses”. This proposal describes the second phase of an inquiry initiated with the GRF funded research “Renovation toolbox: strategies for adapting vernacular architecture in rural China”. This time we will expand our research to the traditional Tibetan houses of Shangri-La, in Yunnan Province. In this region, with cold but sunny winters, people radically transform their traditional mud houses by adding steel and glass structures, forming large greenhouses. These “adapted vernacular houses” may be a viable solution for combining traditional houses with the convenience of newer concrete or steel houses. In this second phase of “Renovation Toolbox”, we propose a framework for assessing the sustainability of these adapted vernacular houses. To better suit vernacular conditions, our framework combines and balances the measurements of sustainability of three aspects of sustainability - environmental, social, and cultural. We will conduct a sustainability evaluation of 3 sets of buildings: one traditional Tibetan house, one generic concrete house, and nine vernacular houses that have been adapted in different ways. Sustainability will be evaluated through architectural diagrams and drawings. In this way, the benefits of adapted vernacular houses in terms of their environmental, cultural, and social sustainability will be rendered legible. By providing an assessment revealing the sustainability of “adapted vernacular houses”, we can influence policy-making and raise awareness amongst local builders. This research considers the adaptation of vernacular houses as a viable alternative to demolition, and to create new possibilities for China’s villages where tradition often helps to shape the future. 數百年來，住宅建築的創新是在沒有建築師的情況下發生的。鄉村建築被理解為“建造傳統”的传承：建造工藝和當地的發展有著長遠的關聯，它反映當地的氣候、景觀、可用材料、工藝和社會結構。 在整個中國，傳統住宅正在被廢棄，取而代之的是建造快速、成本低但可能不適應氣候和文化環境的制式化混凝土房屋。隨著生活方式和家庭結構的變化，這些空間通用的制式化房屋不再能準確反映人們的日常生活。然而，在逐漸廢棄舊房的同時，出現了一些引人注目的混合實驗，其中當地的建造者使用現代的材料和建築方法來改造他們的鄉村住宅。在這些充滿智慧的房屋改造中，屋住設法在傳統建築內實現他們的現代生活方式。我們將這些混合建築方式稱為“鄉村房屋的更新”。 本專案是由 GRF 資助的研究：“改造工具箱：中國農村鄉土建築的適應策略”的第二階段。這次我們將研究範圍擴大到雲南香格里拉的傳統藏族民居。在這個地區，冬天雖然寒冷但陽光明媚，人們通過增加鋼結構和玻璃從根本上改變了傳統的藏式夯土屋，形成了大溫室。這些“鄉村房屋的更新”可以為傳統房屋與新型混凝土或鋼結構相結合的建造方式提供可行解決方案。 作為“改造工具箱”的第二階段，我們提出了一個評估框架，來測評這些改造過的鄉土房屋的可持續性。為了更好地適應本土條件，我們的框架結合並平衡了三個方面的可持續性測量——環境可持續性、社會可持續性和文化可持續性。我們將對 三組建築進行可持續性評估：第一組為傳統藏式房屋，第二組為普通制式化混凝土房屋以及第三組為九幢不同的經過改造的鄉村房屋。可持續性將通過建築圖和圖紙進行評估和表達。這樣，經過改造的鄉村房屋在環境、文化和社會可持續性方面的好處將變得清晰可見。 通過展示“適應性鄉村房屋”可持續性的評估，我們可以嘗試影響當地房屋政策的制定並提高當地建造者的可持續性意識。不同于將傳統房屋粗暴的拆除，本研究將鄉村房屋改造視為可行的替代方案，並希望有助於塑造中國鄉村的未來，為鄉村的創造活力提供可能性。

17613221.value: 無法容忍不確定性和負面的後設認知理念對癌症復發恐懼的影響：一項縱向研究

17613221.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17613221.value: Dr Chan , Wendy Wing Lok Dr Foo, Chi Chung Prof Kwong, Ava Dr Liao, Qiuyan Prof Ng , Simon Siu Man

17613221.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17613221.value: While some concern about the potential threat of cancer recurrence is a normal, realistic response, excessive fear of cancer recurrence (FCR) is detrimental, affecting individuals’ quality of life and functional capacity. Locally, one in three cancer survivors reported high fear of cancer recurrence. While our recent study and others implicate metacognition in FCR, a large proportion of FCR variance remains unexplained. It is, therefore, imperative to identify other potential contributory factor(s) in FCR. Intolerance of uncertainty (IU) has been found to play a variable role in explaining transdiagnostic anxiety-related disturbances. As the unpredictable nature of cancer recurrence raises significant uncertainty this suggests IU is a prime candidate in FCR. While metacognitive beliefs about worry have been examined in the context of FCR, little is known about the role of IU in FCR. While cognitive attentional syndrome (CAS) has been studied in FCR, neither the relationship between IU and FCR nor a simultaneous investigation of IU, negative metacognition beliefs, CAS, and FCR has been tested. The present study aims to address these surprising literature gaps. This longitudinal study proposes to examine the role of IU, negative metacognitive beliefs, and CAS in FCR among cancer survivors. Eligible participants are Chinese patients recently completing treatment for breast or colorectal cancers. Approximately 106 patients from each cancer type (N=213) will be recruited. Eligible patients will be approached within three months of completing cancer treatment. Willing participants will complete interviews at baseline and at 3-month (FU1), 6-months (FU2), and 12-months (FU3) post-baseline follow-ups. At baseline, we will assess metacognitive beliefs, intolerance of uncertainty, cognitive attentional syndrome, and fear of cancer recurrence; follow-ups assess fear of cancer recurrence. Validated subject-reported questionnaire will be used to assess the study variables. Latent growth mixture modelling will be used to examine the growth trajectories of fear of cancer recurrence, as well as to test if metacognitions and intolerance of uncertainty at baseline predict the growth trajectories (i.e. the slope) of distress by regressing the slope of fear of cancer recurrence on baseline metacognitions and intolerance of uncertainty. A series of mediational models will be specified to determine the interrelationships between negative metacognitive beliefs, IU, CAS, and FCR. 癌症患者輕微擔憂癌症復發是真實和正常的反應。然而，過分的癌症復發恐懼是有害的，可能會導致生活質量下降和引起功能障礙。在本港，有三分之一的癌症倖存者對癌症復發有高度的恐懼。我們最近的研究和其他研究結果部分證實後設認知對癌症復發恐懼的影響，但仍未能完全地解釋不同的癌症患者在癌症復發恐懼程度上的差異。因此，了解其他癌症復發恐懼的潛在風險因素是必須的。數項研究結果均證實無法容忍不確定性對情緒障礙的影響，及其跨診斷性質。後設認知對癌症復發恐懼的重要性已廣被證實，相反，無法容忍不確定性如何影響癌症復發恐懼卻知之甚少。認知注意力綜合症對無法容忍不確定性和癌症復發恐懼兩者間的關係的影響亦尚未被研究。迄今為止，沒有任何一項研究同時了解無法容忍不確定性、負面的後設認知理念、認知注意力綜合症和癌症復發恐懼四者之間的關係。本研究旨在填補現有文獻的空白。因此，擬議的縱向研究旨在了解無法容忍不確定性和負面的後設認知理念對癌症倖存者的癌症復發恐懼的影響。參加者必須是最近完成乳癌或結直腸癌治療的中國患者。本研究將會招募213名癌症患者，包括106名乳癌患者和106名結直腸癌患者。符合條件的患者將會在完成癌症治療後三個月內獲邀參加本研究。同意參與本研究的參加者需要完成一個訪談（基線），並在基線完成後3個月（FU1）、6個月（FU2）和12個月（FU3）完成另外三個跟進訪談。在基線訪談中，我們會評估參加者的後設認知理念、無法容忍不確定性、認知注意力綜合症和癌症復發恐懼；跟進訪談則會評估他們的癌症復發恐懼。已經驗證的問卷將用於評估這些研究變數。潛變量混合增長模型將用於了解癌症復發恐懼的增長軌跡，以及利用迴歸分析方法測試基線的後設認知理念和無法容忍不確定性是否能夠預測癌症復發恐懼的增長軌跡（即坡度）。一系列的中介模型亦會用來確認無法容忍不確定性是否透過認知注意力綜合症影響癌症復發恐懼的坡度。

17613521.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17613521.value: 【背景】 小兒濕疹是一種慢性皮膚病，影響超過三成的香港兒童，並對該兒童及其父母照顧者帶來不利的影響，因此需要以家庭為本的系統性介入模式。然而，大多數非藥物的培訓課程側重於症狀管理，很少關注父母的社交心理健康。本研究團隊為患有濕疹的兒童及其家庭所開展的綜合身心靈全人健康（下稱身心靈）介入模式取得了不錯的成果。與候補名單對照組相比，身心靈介入組的兒童及其父母的幸福感得到明顯的改善。然而，目前尚不清楚，在改善孩子和父母的情緒調節和生活素質方面，僅向父母提供的身心靈介入是否：(1) 與向父母和孩子一起提供的身心靈介入一樣有效，以及 (2) 比僅向父母提供的健康教育更有效。此外，至今仍沒有研究探討兒童在介入後獲得的改善是否與父母所獲得的改善有連繫。 【目的】這是一項三臂、等隨機、平行隨機對照的試驗。本研究比較了兩種身心靈介入（一種提供給父母和孩子；一種僅提供給父母）與一種健康教育積極對照組（僅提供給父母）在促進香港濕疹兒童及其父母照顧者適應性情緒調節和生活素質的功效。本研究還旨在探討兒童與其父母的基線主要結果和介入後主要結果的變化的連繫。 【方法】本研究將透過香港的醫院和非政府社區志願組織招募192對父母和孩子。每對親子參與者將完成個人小組前篩選面試。每對符合條件的親子參與者將按 1:1:1 的比例被隨機分配到三種組別之中的一組。每組包括六節課程，每星期一節。隨機分組將由電腦進行。本試驗的主要研究變項是生活素質和情緒調節，並會在基線、介入即時結束時和介入結束6 週後分別進行評估。基於治療意向分析法，本研究將利用混合因子共變異數分析測試兩種身心靈介入模式的有效性。本研究亦將利用結構方程模型測試親子相互依存的介入效果。 【涵義】這是首個探討濕疹兒童與其父母照顧者在心理社交介入後結果變化的相互依賴的研究。研究結果將為未來以家庭為本的系統性心理社交濕疹介入模式設計提供信息，從而增強濕疹兒童和其家庭的護理。

17614621.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17614621.value: Temporarily abstained from tobacco use during hospitalisation is a teachable moment to provide support to maintain and prolong the abstinence after discharge. Although clinical guidelines recommend offering smoking cessation counselling and pharmacotherapy, many patients continue to smoke after discharge. We propose to use a brief face-to-face cessation intervention model plus mobile health (mHealth) instant messaging (IM) for providing personalised support to maximise clinical applicability of current practice. No similar mHealth trials for post-discharge patients are found in PubMed, Cochrane Library or trial registries (ClinicalTrials.gov & ISRCTN). This proposed study is based on the success of our IM chat-based trial for community smokers and feasibility survey in an in-patient setting. Smoking patients proactively recruited from in-patient and follow-up services will be individually randomised into Intervention (n=385) or Control group (n=385). Both groups will receive brief face-to-face advice using the standard 5As model (Ask, Advice, Assess, Assist, and Arrange) and a self-help e-booklet at baseline. Intervention group will further receive 12-weeks chat-based personalised behavioural support guided by the Capability-Opportunity-Motivation Behaviour model and coded using Behavioural Change Techniques (BCTs) for a systematic analysis of active components. The chat-based personalised behavioural support will be tailored according to smoking behaviours and health conditions to provide real-time interaction to handle craving and situation barriers and offers of active referral to existing smoking cessation services. Control group will receive regular IM text messages on general health and follow-up reminders for attention control. The primary outcomes will be biochemically-validated abstinence (exhaled carbon monoxide < 4 ppm and salivary cotinine < 10 ng/ml) at 6- and 12-months after treatment initiation, and the secondary outcomes (designed to measure mediators) include self-reported past 7-day abstinence, 24-weeks continuous abstinence, smoking reduction, quitting self-efficacy, intention to quit, quit attempts, and smoking cessation service use at 6- and 12-months. Qualitative interviews (with BCTs taxonomy), intervention compliance (compliance average causal effect), mediation, and economic analyses will be conducted to understand the efficacy and cost-effectiveness of the intervention mechanisms. Chatting log will be recorded and analyzed for triangulating intervention compliance and identifying effective components. The outcome assessors and data analysts will be blinded to group allocation. We will follow the CONSORT-EHEALTH statement strictly. The study will inform a practical mHealth behavioural change model with application to link post-discharge smokers to community smoking cessation services and will guide the implementation of remote cessation support during pandemic and under the “New-normal” where face-to-face counselling was hard to achieve.

17614921.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17614921.value: Our study will investigate the emerging phenomenon of self-governance in the digital economy, which has seen an ever-increasing number of online platforms relegating the authority to make rules and adjudicate disputes to platform participants. Today’s thriving online platforms face complex governance issues, giving them the appearance of sovereignty to a large extent. Platform operators have traditionally adopted a centralized model of governance: they propose transactional rules for participants, apply and enforce those rules, and mediate and adjudicate conflicts when they arise. In recent years, however, many large Chinese online platforms, including Taobao, JD.com, Didi, WeChat, and Zhihu, have quietly initiated experiments to decentralize their law-making and dispute resolution functions. We are interested in exploring these Chinese innovations within platform governance, the driving forces behind the adoption of the new mechanisms, and their associated merits and challenges, together with their legal and economic consequences. We plan to formulate game-theoretical models of the mechanism designs of these innovations and empirically evaluate their effectiveness. We also plan to conduct a comparative study of platform governance in the United States and China to explore how institutional factors can influence the governance of online platforms in different jurisdictions. Our project represents the first systematic effort to examine the various decentralized governance schemes that Chinese online platforms have introduced. It will contribute to several strands of existing literature, particularly research on platform governance, online dispute resolution, and law and technology. Our findings will offer practical insights for online platforms that desire to improve their governance structures to ease tension and resolve conflicts among their users. The research will also assist policymakers in evaluating the effects of different governance mechanism designs, helping them to make more informed decisions about whether, when, and how to regulate online platforms. We plan to write three articles systematically analyzing the phenomenon and consequences of decentralized platform governance and submit them to leading international peer-reviewed journals. 我们的研究将调查数字经济中新兴的去中心化的治理现象，其中越来越多的在线平台将制定规则和裁决争议的权力下放给平台参与者。如今蓬勃发展的网络平台面临着复杂的治理问题，在很大程度上赋予了它们类似国家主权的权力。平台运营商传统上采用集中式治理模式：他们为参与者提出交易规则，应用和执行这些规则，并在冲突出现时进行调解和裁决。然而，近年来，包括淘宝、京东、滴滴、微信、知乎在内的许多中国大型网络平台，都在悄悄地开展立法和争议解决功能下放的实验。我们有兴趣探索这些中国在平台治理方面的创新、采用新机制背后的驱动力、相关的优点和挑战，以及它们的法律和经济后果。我们计划制定这些创新机制设计的博弈论模型，并根据经验评估其有效性。我们还计划对美国和中国的平台治理进行比较研究，以探索制度因素如何影响不同司法管辖区的在线平台治理。

It also offers practical insights to platform operators on improving their governance structures. The research outputs include two peer-reviewed papers published in Management Science, a leading business and management journal, and a book chapter in the principal investigator's new book, "High Wire: How China Regulates Big Tech and Governs Its Economy." 17614921.label: Major findings and research outcome
17614921.value: Crowd-Judging on Two-Sided Platforms: An Analysis of Ingroup Bias Disputes over transactions on two-sided platforms are typically resolved through customer service or third-party providers. This paper explores "crowd-judging," where users volunteer as jurors to resolve disputes on the Taobao e-commerce platform. The study focuses on in-group bias, where jurors favor their group (buyers or sellers). Sellers believe this bias undermines the legitimacy of crowd-judging due to the majority of jurors being buyers. Empirical findings show that seller jurors are 10% more likely to favor sellers, with bias more pronounced in close decisions and perceived threats to in-group interests. However, bias decreases with juror experience, reducing by nearly 95% as experience grows. Simulations reveal three insights: in-group bias affects less than 2% of cases under current policies, increasing crowd size is inefficient in reducing bias, and dynamic case allocation can mitigate bias and sustain a juror pool. Improving Dispute Resolution in Two-Sided Platforms: The Case of Review Blackmail This study examines dispute resolution mechanisms for handling malicious reviews and blackmail on two-sided platforms. A game-theoretic model illustrates interactions between sellers and potentially malicious consumers, who may post negative reviews to demand ransom. Malicious consumers can significantly reduce seller profits, especially with high product quality uncertainty. A centralized dispute resolution mechanism, where platforms judge review disputes, can restore some efficiency but requires quick and accurate judgments. A decentralized mechanism, allowing sellers to remove reviews with potential penalties for wrongdoing, proves more effective and reduces the need for swift platform judgments. Properly implemented decentralization may thus offer a more efficient dispute resolution approach. Book Chapter: Decentralizing Platform Governance The chapter discusses how Chinese online platforms are decentralizing governance to address government intervention and market fraud concerns. It highlights innovative dispute resolution schemes by Taobao and other platforms, showing how crowd-sourcing mechanisms enhance efficiency and procedural justice in dispute resolution. This approach aims to diffuse tensions and improve platform governance.

17614921.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17614921.value: With the advent of GPT-like services, it will be important and interesting to explore the role of artificial intelligence in resolving internal platform disputes, as well as the role of internal platform governance in resolving disputes in relation to the use of artificial intelligence.

17614921.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17614921.value: This research explores innovative mechanisms for dispute resolution and governance on Chinese e-commerce platforms like Taobao. By studying crowd-judging, where users volunteer as jurors to resolve disputes, the research reveals significant in-group bias, with seller jurors 10% more likely to favor sellers. This bias, however, diminishes by nearly 95% as jurors gain experience. Simulations suggest that while in-group bias affects less than 2% of cases, increasing juror numbers is inefficient, and dynamic case allocation can better reduce bias. Additionally, the research examines handling malicious reviews and blackmail, showing that fake negative reviews can harm profits. A centralized system for judging disputes requires quick and accurate decisions, but a decentralized approach, allowing sellers to remove reviews with penalties for misuse, proves more effective. Lastly, the research discusses how Chinese platforms are decentralizing governance to address government intervention and market fraud, using crowd-sourcing to enhance dispute resolution efficiency and procedural justice. Together, these studies highlight the potential of crowd-sourcing and decentralization in improving platform governance, provided they are implemented carefully to mitigate biases and enhance fairness.

17615021.value: To analyse how the EU and key member states respond to major changes in the international order and the increasing tensions around digital technologies ('tech war'). To examine empirically - through extensive documentary analysis - how the EU and key member states (Germany, France, Netherlands) have shifted their positions on the regulation and taxation of digital technology companies, how they have accommodated the role of digital technology in the conduct of diplomacy (in particular with the US and China), and how they are seeking to adapt their economic policies to safeguard their technological edge in a more hostile global geopolitical environment. To critically reflect on the changing nature of technology in the conduct of foreign affairs: digital technology companies are not only an object of economic and industrial policy as well as of export promotion, but also a central national security concern, as well as an instrument of political and diplomatic communication. To analyse the difficulties and limitations of regulating powerful and globally active digital technology companies that are protected by foreign countries, have a very significant political influence, as well as very substantial economic clout. To reconceptualise the role of digital technology plays in major theoretical explanations for the behaviour of states in International Relations theory, through a social constructivist critical hermeneutic of formal and informal political discourse. To publish three articles with a high-impact journals (Journal of Common Market Studies, West European Politics, International Affairs) on thematic case studies linked to the EU's diplomatic, national security, and global regulatory responses to the 'tech wars'.

17615021.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17615021.value: This research project critically examines the impact of the China-US ‘tech war’ on the EU and its member states. It conducts a social constructivist critical hermeneutic of formal and informal political discourse in the EU and three member states (France, Germany, Netherlands) on Europe’s entanglement in the intensifying rivalry between the US and China on digital technologies. This makes it possible to illustrate important rhetorical and political shifts taking place inside the EU about how diplomatic ties with the US and China are being recalibrated, how the EU responds to a more ‘techno-nationalist’ and protectionist global economic environment, how the EU and national parliaments seek to regulate digital technology companies, and how political communication in the EU is influenced by the very same digital technological platforms it struggles to regulate. The analysis compares three member states with distinct economic, diplomatic and regulatory traditions to elucidate how global level contestation about digital technologies is impacting on national and local politics in Europe. The research project makes a timely and highly significant contribution to understanding one of the most pressing and urgent political problems facing the EU. It does so by developing a new conceptualisation of the global ‘tech war’ that transcends the vertical compartmentalisation of explanatory frameworks into three distinct diplomatic/geostrategic, economic/regulatory, and political/communicative realms. Building on insights into communicative action from ‘Copenhagen School’ critical security studies and social constructivism in International Relations, this project investigates the changing European diplomatic, economic, and regulatory posture in the context of the global ‘tech war’. The project contributes a rich empirically-driven conceptualisation of the mutual constitution of speech acts and policy behaviour in relation to digital technology companies that are simultaneously actors, objects and instruments of Europe's policy response. By producing three journal articles for high-impact journals (JCMS, West European Politics, International Affairs), this research project makes a tangible and visible contribution to scholarship on one of Europe’s most intensely debated strategic challenges. The PI’s ability to examine primary sources in English, French, German, Spanish and Dutch, as well as his research exposure in Europe and Asia are key advantages for developing a more compelling account of the EU’s diplomatic, strategic, economic, and regulatory behaviour in a fast-changing geopolitical context. 這一研究項目審視中美「科技戰爭」對歐盟及其成員國的影響。它對歐盟和其三個成員國（法國、德國及荷蘭）關於歐洲捲入中美在數碼科技上日益激烈的競爭中的正式和非正式的政治論述進行社會建構主義批判性解釋。 這就有可能說明歐盟內部正在發生的重要論述和政治轉變，包括與美國和中國的外交關係如何重新調整，歐盟如何應對「科技民族主義」和保護主義盛行的全球經濟環境，歐盟和國家議會如何試圖監管數碼科技公司，以及歐盟內的政治傳達如何受到其難以規範的數碼科技平台的影響。 這項目分析比較了三個具有獨特經濟、外交和監管傳統的成員國，以闡明全球數碼科技競爭對歐洲國家和地方政治的影響，並為理解歐盟面臨的最迫切的政治問題之一作出了及時和重大貢獻。 這項研究通過發展全球「科技戰爭」這新概念，將縱向的解釋框架劃分為三個不同的外交/地緣戰略、經濟/規範和政治/溝通領域。 本專案以「哥本哈根學派」批判安全研究和國際關係中的社會建構主義對交往行為的見解為基礎，調查在全球「科技戰爭」背景下不斷變化的歐洲外交、經濟和監管態勢。 數碼科技公司既是歐洲政策制定的參與者、監管對象和執行工具。這項目為言語行為和政策行為在數碼科技政策領域中的相互構成提供一個實證主導的概念。通過在高影響力學術期刊（JCMS、西歐政治、和國際事務）刊登三篇論文，這個研究專案將對最備受重視之一的歐洲戰略挑戰作出切實和顯注的學術貢獻。 這項目的首席研究員能審閲英文、法文、德文、西班牙文和荷蘭文的原始資料，加上他在歐洲和亞洲的研究體驗，這些都是此項目的關鍵優勢，為歐盟在瞬息萬變的地緣政治背景下其外交、戰略、經濟和規範行為提供更具說服力的說明。

17615921.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17615921.value: 代你決定：在華人社會為無精神行為能力人士做的最佳利益判斷

17615921.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17615921.value: The overarching research aim of this project is to develop a unified, coherent and principled concept of “best interests” for the purpose of decision-making on behalf of individuals without mental capacity in Chinese jurisdictions. This project will have a significant and demonstrable impact in Hong Kong, China and Taiwan, where developments on this issue have been minimal. It is a fundamental legal and ethical principle that all adults with mental capacity should be able to make decisions about their lives. Where an individual is deemed to lack mental capacity to make certain decisions, however, and the power to do so is taken out of her hands, a question arises as to how these decisions should be made on her behalf. Of the two major forms of substitute decision-making, decision-making on the basis of “best interests” has been the form of choice in western jurisdictions such as the United Kingdom, Australia and Canada (with the United States as a notable exception), and in Chinese jurisdictions such as Hong Kong, China and Taiwan. While the jurisprudence on best interest determinations in western jurisdictions has developed vastly over the past few decades, the developments in the Chinese context have been very limited. Although the “best interests” principle is often prominently featured in legislative provisions relating to mental health or guardianship, jurisprudence on what the concept entails is minimal, and the views and wishes of the individual are not consistently consulted. Because of the wide range of decisions that are frequently made on behalf of those without mental capacity, this is a gap that needs to be addressed urgently. My comparative project will be the first to systematically address this issue, and will do so in several stages. The first will involve mapping out what the current concepts of “best interests” are in the various Chinese jurisdictions, namely Hong Kong, China and Taiwan. The second stage will involve a consideration of the ethical underpinnings of these concepts in the Chinese context, exploring the extent to which they have been influenced by Chinese values and norms. The third stage will evaluate the extent to which these concepts are compliant with international and local legal obligations, and the final stage will involve the development of a unified, coherent concept of “best interests” sensitive to the Chinese context. I will write at least 2 journal articles and 1 conference paper to disseminate my research findings. 此研究的主要目的是要建立一套完整、有系統、具連貫性的「最佳利益」概念，為華人社會裡無精神行為能力的人作決定，從而推動香港、中國內地和台灣在「最佳利益」概念方面的發展。 不管是在法律還是道德的角度，任何具有精神行為能力的成年人都應該被賦予為自己生活作決定的權利，但當遇上沒有精神行為能力的人，我們應該怎樣為他們作決定呢？替代決策一般有兩種形式，其中一種是考慮沒有精神行為能力人士的「最佳利益」---- 這種方式在香港、中國內地、台灣、英國、澳洲和加拿大比較常見。綜觀過去數十年，在「最佳利益」概念的發展上，西方國家遠遠超越了中方國家。雖說「最佳利益」一概念經常出現在與精神健康和監護制度有關的法律上，清晰界定「最佳利益」的案例非常少，亦沒有一貫的考慮缺乏精神行為能力人士的意願；當法庭又常常要為這些人作一系列的決定時，必須馬上釐清與「最佳利益」概念相關的問題。 這將會是第一份有系統地探索「最佳利益」概念的比較研究，並分為幾個階段。第一階段將探討現時香港、中國內地和台灣對「最佳利益」的理解；第二階段將考慮「最佳利益」在中方背景下的倫理基礎，深入分析中方價值觀和規範對「最佳利益」的影響；第三階段將評鑑這些概念是否符合國際、以至本地的法律責任；第四階段將構思出一套適合華人社會的「最佳利益」概念。研究成功之後，將出版最少兩份期刊文獻和一篇會議論文。

17616221.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17616221.value: Road traffic injuries inflict tremendous economic and social costs on society. Yet, they are avoidable. Despite an overall trend of reduction in road fatalities worldwide, we are still very far from achieving the “Vision Zero” objective of eliminating road fatality. This project attempts to address the safety of buses in large metropolitan cities. In view of the efforts to promote sustainable urban transportation, buses hold unique promise as a mass public transport mode. Apart from being more efficient in the use of road space, electric buses also have great potential to reduce roadside pollution and achieve transport decarbonisation. Nonetheless, buses navigating on urban roads can pose an imminent threat to other road users due to the huge mass of buses as heavy vehicles. Hence, traffic crashes involving buses are more likely to cause multiple casualties and fatalities. Making use of the track record of the PI, this project attempts to further advance and integrate spatial road safety models with video analytics and artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms. Specifically, through integrating the geo-validated road crash data and other geospatial datasets, her team will first identify the mode-specific dangerous road locations in Hong Kong. It is expected that these hazardous road locations will exhibit different characteristics that point to relevant risk factors of bus crashes. Nonetheless, conventional road safety models based on historical crash data are post-crash analysis only. Videos captured by bus cameras can record the concurrent road and pavement conditions, as well other road users’ behaviour, while buses are in motion. With the support of the largest franchised bus company in Hong Kong, the PI’s team will use these bus videos for avoiding bus crashes in the future. Through a pilot project, her team has developed AI models for extracting (e.g. object detection), processing (e.g. image classification), and analysing (e.g. generating summary critical value statistics) selected bus videos. With this full-scale research project, the PI’s team can devote time to overcome the technical and methodological difficulties for up-scaling and widening the analysis. Moreover, these results will be compared with the empirical hot zones to generate insights on specific risk factors and to recommend site-specific countermeasures. The PI’s team will develop associated AI unsupervised learning algorithms to identify distinctive clusters of bus crashes by different combinations of environmental and behavioural factors. With improvement measures implemented, this project will conduct systematic before-after analysis so that the impact can be scientifically evaluated. 道路交通傷害給社會造成了巨大的經濟和社會代價。然而，它是可以避免的。儘管全球道路死亡人數總體呈下降趨勢，但我們離實現消除道路死亡的“零願景”目標還很遙遠。本項目專注於改善大城市的道路安全問題。在大城市中，巴士作為大眾公共交通方式有助於推動可持續城市交通。除了更有效地利用道路空間外，電動巴士在減少路邊污染和實現交通減碳方面也具有巨大潛力。儘管如此，由於作為重型車輛的巴士體積巨大，在城市道路上行駛的巴士可能會對其他道路使用者構成較大的危險。涉及巴士的交通事故也更有可能造成多人傷亡。本項目利用首席研究員的研究經驗與成果，進一步推進道路安全的空間分析並將其與電腦視頻分析和人工智能演算法相結合。具體來說，通過整合經過地點驗證的道路碰撞數據和其他地理空間數據庫，她的團隊將首先確定香港巴士碰撞的高危道段。然後以道路安全模型分析這些巴士高危道段的不同特徵，查出巴士碰撞的相關風險因素。儘管方法上的創新，基於過往碰撞數據的傳統道路安全模型只能局限於分析已發生碰撞後的交通事故。現今香港已進入科技創新時代，在巴士攝像頭拍攝的視頻已可以記錄巴士行駛時同步的道路和路面狀況，以及其他道路使用者的行為。在香港最大的專營巴士公司的支持下，首席研究員會使用這些巴士視頻來分析和改善香港巴士安全。通過處理和分析選定的巴士視頻，她的團隊已可對視頻中所有的人和車作匿名處理並初步開發了用於提取（例如對象檢測）、處理（例如圖像分類）和分析（例如生成匯總臨界值統計數據）的人工智能模型。通過本研究項目，首席研究員的團隊將更全面的克服技術和方法上的困難，以擴大分析範圍和深化分析方法。此外，她的團隊將會對基於人工智能的研究結果與基於空間分析的高危路段安全模型結果進行比較，以深入瞭解特定的風險因素並推薦針對特定地點和巴士安全的對策。 首席研究員的團隊將開發相關的人工智能無監督學習演算法，以通過環境和行為因素的不同組合來識別不同的巴士碰撞集群。隨著改進措施的實施，本項目將進行系統的前後分析，以便科學評估影響。

17616421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17616421.value: In many business and employment relationships--particularly in industries where the work and services require creativity, the qualities of the final outputs are subjective. From advertising agents to architects, actors to designers, consultants to scriptwriters, they all serve clients and bosses who may disagree with them on the qualities of the work. Dealing with these disagreements is an important part of the contract design because it affects the incentive of participants of the relationship, and therefore, the efficiency of the relationship. The existing economics literature has not focused on the process leading to the final output--the back and forth between the contracting parties before the final output is realized. The purpose of the project is to explore one aspect of this process, namely, that the principal (boss/manager/client) may ask the agent (worker/subordinate/service provider) to produce multiple versions of the output until she is satisfied or the deadline is reached, and we study its implications on optimal contract design. Pop culture is littered with stories in which demanding principals ask for the agent to revise their product. James Wong, the preeminent songwriter of Hong Kong in the last century, once recounted a story in which he had to write a song seven times before the director Hark Tsui approved the final version. Urban legend has it that Pepsi China once asked an advertisement company to revise 48 times of a design before finally signing off. While this process of extensive revisions may be an integral part of generating a great final output, it also entails inefficiencies. In particular, the principal typically doesn’t incur the full cost of revision, and she may ask for too much revision. Moreover, and somewhat paradoxically, if the agent anticipates the principal to ask for too much rework, he may choose to put in low effort levels in the initial stages, justifying the principal's request for rework, and causing delays in the completion of the task. Contracts, by specifying the costs of the principal to ask for revisions, can improve the efficiency of the contracting relationship. We show, for example, efficiency may be enhanced if the contract specifies an early completion bonus for high quality. We also find that the principal may gain by committing not to ask for revisions and arrange the work in the form of a tournament. 当委托人可以要求代理人修改他的工作时，我们研究了带有主观评价的最优合同问题。修订的可能性引入了一个双边的多任务问题并产生了一个三难困境：最优合同不能同时提供有效的修订、有效的努力和最小的事后剩余破坏。

17616421.label: Realisation of objectives
17616421.value: We have achieved all of the objectives by achieving the following. We have developed a model on subjecive contracting, which provides a comprehensive analysis of revision-based contracts and their efficiency implications. By developing a theoretical framework that captures the dynamic interaction between principals and agents during contract revisions, we demonstrate how different contract structures affect incentives and outcomes. The model explicitly accounts for the costs and benefits of revision requests, revealing that while revision opportunities can improve output quality, they may also introduce strategic delays and inefficient effort allocation. The paper's key contribution lies in characterizing the optimal contract design that minimizes these inefficiencies. Through comparative analysis of common subjective contracts used in practice, we identify the conditions under which different contract structures perform best. These results provide practical guidance for organizations designing subjective contracts, particularly in settings where output quality is difficult to verify objectively.

17616421.label: Summary of objectives addressed

17616421.label: Major findings and research outcome
17616421.value: We study the design of with subjective evaluation when the principal can ask the agent to revise his work. The possibility of revision benefits the principal by providing the option value of making another attempt at the work. But it also introduces a new type of incentive problem for the principal: She may ask for revision even if it is inefficient to do so. This new incentive issue for the principal also affects the incentive of the agent: He may procrastinate his effort in anticipation of excessive revision. This results in a trilemma: The optimal contract cannot simultaneously provide for efficient revision, efficient effort, and minimal ex-post surplus destruction. The optimal contract will of necessity contain at least one of the following problems: revision–the principal asks for excessive revision; procrastination—the agent shirks in the early stage; or punishment—excessive surplus destruction at low-quality final output.

17616421.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17616421.value: We can broaden the finding both in theory and in practice. In theory, it is useful to think of this problem in a repeated game, as we're currently working. Alternatively, we can think of how the behaviors of the agents vary under different types of contracts. This will better connect our work to empirics.

17616421.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17616421.value: Why are people getting increasingly busy in today's workplace? One key factor, particularly in knowledge work, is the cycle of endless revisions. Workers often face numerous requests to modify their work, sometimes to an excessive degree. This inefficiency stems from a fundamental misalignment of incentives: the client requesting revisions bears littel of the actual costs - whether in time, effort, or resources. The worker, anticipating excessive revision requests, may initially hold back their best work or submit incomplete versions. This defensive behavior, in turn, justifies the client's demands for more revisions, creating a self-perpetuating cycle. One might think that charging clients for revision requests could solve this problem. However, we show that this approach leads to another problem: the overall quality of work suffers. When clients must pay for revisions, they become hesitant to request necessary improvements, potentially settling for subpar results. Essentially, this setting creates an inevitable inefficiency: either accepting lower quality work or enduring excessive revisions.
