17616621.label: Realisation of objectives
17616621.value: Objective 1: To compare the typologies of COVID-19 social policy responses adopted to support low-income families in East Asia (Hong Kong, Japan, mainland China, Singapore, South Korea, and Taiwan) under a global context using latent class analysis To empirically investigate typologies of COVID-19 social policy responses, we use the data from the ILO’s Social Protection Monitor that captures social protection responses to the COVID-19 crisis. We capture social policy responses to COVID-19 via three dimensions: the total number of policy responses, the types of social policy tools (e.g., social insurance, income and job protection, food and housing protection, and children and family support programs), and the type of policy adjustment (e.g., new programs or existing program adjustments). Using these indicators, we further conduct latent class analysis (LCA) to investigate the typologies of social policy responses worldwide. We find three typologies: Low-level responses relying on new programs, medium-level responses emphasizing income protection programs (including Hong Kong and Taiwan), and high-level responses with balanced policy approaches (including Mainland China, Japan, Singapore, South Korea). Social democratic countries did not have to adopt high levels of responses, while other welfare states had to adopt high levels of responses. Countries under insecurity regimes are more likely to adopt low-level of social policy response. Objective 2: To investigate the adequacy, coverage, and stratification effects of COVID-19 social policy responses in East Asia through collecting model family data and using regression analysis We scrutinize COVID-19 social policy responses targeting low-income families in the urban centers of East Asian societies. It investigates their generosity, coverage, and potential for poverty reduction using a model family approach. We (1) compare their welfare systems during COVID-19 and (2) assess how they changed from before (2019) to during the pandemic crisis (2020-21). The model family approach entails collecting income-packaging data for hypothetical income levels and family types, including information on labor income, welfare benefits, tax and social security contributions, and costs. We collected model family data and analyzed these primary data (n=2,094) through descriptive statistics and regression analyses. We found that three societies instituted the most changes in welfare measures during COVID-19: Hong Kong adopted multidimensional responses, Taiwan adopted generous responses, and Singapore adopted coverage responses with low generosity. The other three societies adopted fewer changes with varying characteristics: Japan exhibited an inactive response with high generosity, Korea had an inactive response with low generosity, and mainland China displayed an inactive response with low coverage. Our cross-national comparisons can expand conceptualization of East Asian welfare models to a shock-response context and provide evidence for governments to improve their shock-responsive social protection systems. Objective 3: To examine the timeliness of COVID-19 social policy responses adopted to address low-income families in East Asia under a global context using sequence analysis To study the timeliness of social policy responses, we use data from the Oxford COVID-19 Government Response Tracker (OxCGRT). Each country has information in two categories: no income support and the government providing income support. The time dimension of policy responses is captured through the number of days since the first death stemming from COVID-19. We adopted sequence analysis, and countries' timeliness in policy adoption across time was clustered into four groups: limited responses, transient responses, slower responses (including Mainland China, Japan, Singapore, South Korea, Taiwan), and fastest responses (including Hong Kong). Our study is one of the first to compare the speed of social policy responses during crises across countries. Developed welfare institutions are less likely to adopt limited or transient responses. With regard to the relationships between timeliness and typologies of responses, countries providing low-level welfare support are strongly related to offering transient or limited responses to provide income support. Countries that offer high-level welfare provision during COVID-19 are more likely to act relatively slower rather than faster. Overall, this project yielded six manuscripts to date, with two papers being published, two papers under review, and two papers in the process to be submitted for publications. In addition, we presented findings from this study at more than ten conferences and seminars, including the leading policy conferences such as the Association for Public Policy Analysis & Management and the East Asian Social Policy Network Annual Conference. The findings were also presented in seminars in leading institutions, such as University of Oxford, University of York, National University of Singapore, and Tokyo Metropolitan University.

17616621.label: Major findings and research outcome
17616621.value: To empirically investigate typologies of COVID-19 social policy responses, we use data from the ILO’s Social Protection Monitor. This captures responses to the COVID-19 crisis through three dimensions: the total number of policy responses, types of social policy tools, and the type of policy adjustment. Using these indicators, we conduct latent class analysis to identify typologies of social policy responses worldwide. We find three typologies: low-level responses relying on new programs, medium-level responses emphasizing income protection (including Hong Kong and Taiwan), and high-level responses with balanced approaches (including Mainland China, Japan, Singapore, South Korea). Next, we examine COVID-19 social policy responses targeting low-income families in East Asian urban centers, focusing on their generosity, coverage, and potential for poverty reduction using a model family approach. We compare welfare systems during COVID-19 and assess changes from before (2019) to during the pandemic (2020-21). The model family approach involves collecting data on labor income, welfare benefits, taxes, social security contributions, and costs for hypothetical income levels and family types. We analyzed these data (n=2,094) using descriptive statistics and regression analyses. We found significant welfare measure changes in three societies during COVID-19: Hong Kong adopted multidimensional responses, Taiwan adopted generous responses, and Singapore adopted coverage responses with low generosity. Japan, Korea, and Mainland China made fewer changes with varying characteristics. Our cross-national comparisons expand the conceptualization of East Asian welfare models in a shock-response context and provide evidence for improving shock-responsive social protection systems. To study the timeliness of social policy responses, we use data from the Oxford COVID-19 Government Response Tracker (OxCGRT), categorizing each country’s income support responses. We capture the time dimension through the number of days since the first COVID-19 death. Sequence analysis reveals four groups based on response timeliness: limited responses, transient responses, slower responses (including Mainland China, Japan, Singapore, South Korea, Taiwan), and fastest responses (including Hong Kong). Our study is among the first to compare the speed of social policy responses during crises across countries. Overall, this project has yielded six manuscripts: two published, two under review, and two in the process of submission. We presented findings at over ten conferences and seminars, including the Association for Public Policy Analysis & Management and the East Asian Social Policy Network Annual Conference, as well as at institutions such as the University of Oxford, University of York, National University of Singapore, and Tokyo Metropolitan University.

17616721.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17616721.value: 古代法典（1280-1520 年）手稿：生產及其用途

17616721.label: Project Objectives
17616721.value: To analyse and categorise bibliographic, codicological (manuscript construction), and palaeographical (script and organisational) features of the genre of manuscripts known as Statuta Vetera. This will involve: a. Establishing a comprehensive list of the surviving manuscripts produced c.1280-1520 that may appropriately be categorised as Statuta Vetera collections (estimated at approximately 200 items). b. Describing and cataloguing in new detail the physical features of these manuscripts, as well as their textual content and internal organisation, and any evidence of ownership. c. Constructing a comprehensive relational database of the bibliographic, codicological and palaeographic features of the Statuta Vetera genre. To uncover data on the history of the production, geographical distribution, ownership and use of Statuta Vetera manuscripts, in order to better understand the public and private uses to which they were put, and their value to medieval readers and book owners both within and beyond the practice of the English common law. To develop new knowledge on the legal history of the long fourteenth century using methods and insights from book history and manuscript studies, especially as this knowledge relates to practitioners’ and public perceptions of statute law, and quotidian uses of legislative text and commentary. To challenge the perception that Statuta Vetera manuscripts were exclusively or even predominantly lawyers’ reference-books; and to demonstrate in consequence the significance of their place in and influence on a broad swath of English culture, and conversely, the engagement of a broad medieval public with the written law. To demonstrate the significant impact of legal manuscript production—in aesthetic, linguistic and intellectual terms—on the nature and development of the English book in the era before print. To publish at least three articles in international peer-reviewed journals on the findings of the study and the significance of these findings for our understanding of legal history and textual culture in medieval England. To produce the much-needed scholarly resource of a ‘Digital Statuta Vetera’ website. This will make widely accessible for the first time facsimile images of representative manuscripts, accompanied by hyperlinked, searchable versions of their standard texts (with English translations and introductory critical commentary). It will also provide a detailed, comprehensive and searchable database of surviving Statuta Vetera manuscripts in global collections, which will allow new research questions about English legal history and textual culture to be asked and answered.

17616721.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17616721.value: This project provides new insight into English manuscript culture and the history of English law (c.1280-1520) via analysis of manuscripts containing common-law statute collections. It demonstrates the importance of legislative text to the growth of English written culture, and reveals the diversity and depth of early public engagement with the common law. Approximately 200 manuscripts of England’s ‘Ancient Statutes’ (Statuta Vetera) survive from the late thirteenth to the early sixteenth centuries. They generally contain Magna Carta and other major thirteenth-century statutes, along with a more variable collection of additional statutes, tracts and treatises. Statuta manuscripts were among the most popular secular books in medieval England. They were produced commercially in large numbers for a diverse audience: landholders and ecclesiastics, merchants and public officials, judges and common lawyers. These manuscripts witness a significant burst of English legislative production and represent the single most common technology through which late medieval readers interacted with written law. They thus record public engagement with the common law at a formative stage in its development as a national legal tradition. The manuscripts also stand as an important part of English written culture: they were an early and influential model for English book production, often contain all three of England’s languages (Latin, Anglo-French and English), and reveal a busy network of private book commissioning, production, distribution and use. Yet these manuscripts have been little studied—especially compared with the enlightening scholarly attention devoted to (for example) literary manuscripts and lavishly decorated medieval prayer books. No comprehensive study of the format and content of Statuta manuscripts has been undertaken; their practical function within the legal system remains without detailed clarification; and they are often overlooked or elided in accounts of English manuscript history. To address this gap in knowledge, I ask two complementary questions. How can the Statuta advance our understanding of the history of late-medieval English law and legal culture? And what do these legal collections reveal about the development of the English book before the advent of print? This research (conducted comprehensively here for the first time) will involve examining the manuscripts as physical objects, and collecting and analysing evidence of their production, ownership, circulation and practical use. Dissemination via scholarly articles and an online research resource will establish new knowledge about the influence of this medieval legal bestseller on the English common law in its formative years, and on the growth of English book culture. 該研究項目透過分析包含普通法文本的手稿，提升我們對英國手稿文化及英國法律歷史（約 1280-1520 年）的認知。項目不僅展示法律文本對英語書面文化發展的重要性，而且揭示早期公眾對普通法的參與之多樣性和深度。 現時大約有二百份英格蘭 “古代法典”（Statuta Vetera; 十三世紀晚期至十六世紀早期）手稿倖存下來。它們多數包含《大憲章》和其他十三世紀的主要法規，但亦會包含不同類型的法律文本。 古代法典手稿是中世紀英格蘭最受歡迎的通俗書籍之一。它們的讀者種類甚廣，包括土地擁有人、神職人員、商人、公職人員、法官和律師。 這些手稿見證了英國法律文本大量形成的時期，亦是中世紀晚期讀者與法律文本互動的最常見媒體。因此，它們記錄了早期公眾對普通法的參與。這些手稿對英語書面文化的發展亦有深遠影響：它們包含三種語言（拉丁語、法語和英語），提供書籍生產的早期樣板，並展示了早期出版行業之不同業務過程 （例如委託、生產、分銷和使用）。 然而，相比起文學手稿和中世紀祈禱書， 古代法典很少被研究。在英國手稿歷史的記載中，它們經常被忽視。而且，現時學術界並沒有對這些手稿的格式和內容進行全面分析，亦沒有探討它們在法律體系中有甚麼實際功能。為了填補這些研究空白，本項目將集中探討兩個問題： 古代法典如何促進我們對中世紀晚期英國法律歷史和法律文化的理解？及這些法律文本如何增加我們對英語書籍發展 （尤其在印刷術出現之前）之認知？本項目將全面考查手稿實物，分析其生產、擁有者、流通和實際使用之狀況，並通過學術文章及網上平台發佈研究成果，提升我們對古代法典、英國普通法發展以及英語書籍文化發展的知識。

17616921.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17616921.value: The latest violent contention between the state and society in Hong Kong was a far cry from the “economic city” of the 1970s and even the 1980s when the reunification issue first arose. Back then, most Hong Kong people, faced with the political uncertainty of the handover, either voted with their feet or passively accepted the political arrangement imposed by the British and Chinese governments. While a civil society was burgeoning, the average citizen seemed too disquieted to make their voice heard. Fast forward thirty odd years, we witnessed an unprecedented level of popular mobilization in the anti-extradition bill movement in 2019, in which the ardent desire for democracy and embracement of liberal values could be heard loud and clear. The anti-extradition bill movement was only the latest episode of the prodemocracy movement. While the escalation of conflict could be attributed to immediate causes such as police brutality, unresponsiveness of political leaders toward popular demand, and public anxiety over civil rights under threat, in the medium term, the insurgency was closely linked to the Occupy Central movement and Umbrella movement of 2013 to 2014. The latter movements, in turn, were about a constitutional promise made in the Basic Law that remained unrealized, ie. to ultimately implement universal suffrage in Hong Kong under “One Country, Two Systems”. As a case of democratization, Hong Kong started off with a pacted transition that was largely imposed from above in the 1980s, transitioning to protracted transition as the democratization process was arrested in 2004, and finally to democratic backsliding as civil and political rights deteriorated rapidly after the Umbrella Movement in 2014. This inevitably prompts the research questions of this proposal: How can the comparative democratization literature make sense of Hong Kong as a case of failed democratic transition? what are the essential actors, variables, and events that have affected the substantive change in the Hong Kong society over the course of the past five decades, and through what causal mechanisms and dynamics have such change been brought about? To adequately study such a complex case, I plan to write a book that will engage the literature on comparative-historical analysis and comparative democratization, taking 1970 to 2020 as the timeframe for study. 香港近期社會與國家的武力抗爭，和七十年代的經濟城市狀況相距甚遠。八十年代，當回歸問題出現時，香港人面對政治前景不明朗，大多選擇移民或 被動地接受中英兩國的安排。當時公民社會已經冒起，但一般市民並不勇於發聲。三十多年後，我們見證了2019年反修例運動前所未有的社會動員，和市民對民主自由的強烈訴求。香港的民主化過程，始於八十年代一個協議下的民主過渡。 2004年後轉變成曠日持久的民主過渡； 2014年後公民和政治權利更急速倒退。本計劃的研究問題是：比較民主化的文獻如何理解香港作為一個失敗的民主化個案？ 香港過去五十年的轉變，和哪些行動者，變項，和事件有關？是透過哪些因果機制和動力？ 我計劃寫一本書，以比較歷史分析方法和比較民主化理論，分析從1970到2020年的轉變，以理解香港作為民主化一個複雜和偏差的個案。

17616921.label: Realisation of objectives
17616921.value: Please note that I resigned from The University of Hong Kong in 2022 (last date of employment: December 31, 2022), after which I no longer had access to my grant and institutional support from the university. Therefore, this project is technically incomplete. I am still working on this project in a personal capacity and aiming to complete a book manuscript for publication. However, my report here will only reflect what was partially completed up to my last day of employment. Also, since this research proposal was originally written for a book project, it would be difficult to discuss the findings of each objective mechanically and separately from the others. Instead, I will offer a condensed causal narrative and conclusion to illustrate my findings. In the historical analysis of societal mobilization for democracy, the 1966 and 1967 riots were generally regarded as a watershed. The riots reflected the discontent of young people with the colonial government and the rage of the working class over the lack of labor protection. I reviewed historical archives such as newspapers and university magazines extensively, and found that on the eve of the riots, there was keen social awareness of the impermanence of Hong Kong’s colonial status. Among university students and social elites there were active inquisition and discussion about the political future of the city, including democratization and the pursuit of political independence. Based on the historical data on GDP, Hong Kong in the 1960s could be regarded as a middle-income economy which, according to modernization theory, is the most likely category of countries to undergo democratization. The colonial government dramatically improved its capacity and performance in the 1970s, thus counterbalancing the effect of rising education level and middle-class sector The suppression of the 1967 riot played a crucial role in the demobilization of labor activism and anti-colonial resistance. A limited group of students, public intellectuals, and middle class professionals became the major agents of social activism, whose capacity was not enough to mobilize a city-wide movement for democracy. I compiled protest event data from this period, which showed a rising number of social protests. The political engineering project of the colonial state allowed the latter to successfully cope with rising societal demand. The political stability in the 1970s was a transient state of demobilization. The consequence was the undermobilization of the democratic movement in the critical moment of transition toward 1997. This situation proved to be transient. Protest event data show that societal mobilization over political issues became more frequent and intense. June 4th was the critical event that normalized contentious politics and brought societal mobilization to a new normal. On the whole, the political transition leading up to 1997 saw a peculiar combination of the rapid development of civil society, the rise in liberal rights consciousness, and the under-mobilization of the pro-democracy movement. By the late 1980s, Hong Kong was one of the few high-income industrialized economies that remained undemocratic. The Asian financial crisis coincided with the onset of postmodernization. The structural dislocation caused by the economic shock preceded the mass rally on July 1, 2003, in which over half a million people turned out to protest against a widely opposed local legislation on national security. The event has been regarded as the watershed for the development of civil society and state-society relations. The massive turnout was a response against civil liberties and a collective venting of grievance against the poor performance of the government in the economic recession. The destabilization of the materialist ideology was what enabled the construction of new meanings. The younger generation, in particular, constructed new political subjectivity through articulating the relationship between postmaterialism and postcolonialism. This signifies a generational shift from the liberal patriotism of the June 4th generation, a burgeoning subjectivity similar to the nativist identity in anti-colonial resistance. In the decade after 2003, civil society became increasingly contentious, with activists coming from university and secondary school students. Pro-democracy parties were fragmented into moderates and radicals. The radicalization of civil society accelerated after 2012, precipitated in the Umbrella movement, the rise of localism, and the Anti-ELAB movement in 2019. The theoretical significance can be discussed from several perspectives. Hong Kong can be fruitfully compared with other Asian tiger economies that are distinguished by shared experiences of colonialism and modernization. Colonialism offered the institutional apparatus for modernization, albeit with a different impact on democratization. For Taiwan, Singapore, and South Korea, colonialism left an institutional apparatus that enabled rapid state-led industrialization in the postcolonial era. Modernization was fostered by a repressive developmental state within a short period of time. For Taiwan and South Korea, the legitimacy deficit of the developmental state and its repressive policies elicited strong social uprising. For Singapore, the hegemonic one-party regime endures, while economic development has bred a conservative pro-regime middle class. For Hong Kong, economic development and protracted decolonization offered favorable conditions for civil society and pro-democracy values to develop, while paradoxically demobilizing anti-colonial forces. In sum, the case of Hong Kong illustrates how the timing and sequence of decolonization, industrialization and postcolonial state formation affect democratic mobilization. The case illustrates on how important factors affecting democratization may have different trajectories of development, resulting in distinct conjunctural effects. Due to the different timing of political liberalization and democratization, civil society and opposition parties have divergent paths of development, resulting in problems of disunity. It shows how liberal autocracy can be conducive to pluralism but not necessarily the development of a strong organizational infrastructure for pro-democracy movement. In the transitology literature, authoritarian breakdown is expected to be caused by elite rupture and the coalescence of opposition parties. For Hong Kong, the instability of liberal autocracy under protracted democratization leads to a “double” breakdown: on the one hand, the social bases of the ruling circle are successively undermined as it becomes more and more exclusive; on the other hand, the opposition parties and civil society become more seriously divided as protracted democratization leads to serious internal frame disputes. As a result, both the authoritarian institutions and the political opposition suffer breakdown. The case demonstrates the significance of temporal ordering of processes. Hong Kong is a deviant case where democratization started long after modernization, with a modern bureaucracy and a rule-based governance structure already well-developed. As a result, the authoritarian state is afforded robust administrative institutions with strong infrastructural power to withstand crises and shocks. All these increase its endurance hence the difficulty for civil society and political opposition to challenge the regime. Hong Kong offers an excellent case for investigating the significance of events in affecting democratization. Since the 1980s, people have experienced the June 4th crackdown in 1989; the mass rally on July 1, 2003 against the national security legislation; the Umbrella Movement in 2014; and the Anti-ELAB movement in 2019. Each of them involves the creation of new meanings, significations, and rituals and culminates in structural transformations. Each is preceded by structural dislocation that opens actors to new ways of expressing their demands and new articulation of identity.

Civil society development in the postcolonial period has strong continuity with its development in the colonial period, and testifies to the endogenous relationship between modernization and democratization. Hong Kong offers an illuminating case on how important factors affecting democratization may have different trajectories of development, resulting in distinct conjunctural effects. As a result, the authoritarian state is afforded robust administrative institutions with strong infrastructural power to withstand crises and shocks. All these increase its endurance hence the difficulty for civil society and political opposition to challenge the regime. Lastly, Hong Kong offers an excellent case for investigating the significance of events in affecting democratization. 17616921.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17616921.value: The latest violent contention between the state and society in Hong Kong was a far cry from the “economic city” of the 1970s and even the 1980s when the reunification issue first arose. The rapid radicalization of the younger generation after 1997 was actually the culmination of long-term development of civil society that can be traced back to the 1960s. Society in Hong Kong went through a decade of demobilization in the 1970s when the late colonial state carried out a state-building project that resulted in the improvement of government performance on various fronts. As a result, Hong Kong people were ill-prepared for the 1997 issue and the belated birth of the pro-democracy movement, and were disempowered during the critical moment of the political transition. The rise of youth activism testifies to the effect of long-term economic development on the political values of the new generation. In the course of the struggle between the society and the state, both eventually suffered breakdown.

17617021.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17617021.value: 《巴马丹拿集团（P&T Group)：一段关于香港与亚洲建筑企业文化的历史》

17617021.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17617021.value: P&T Group: A History of Corporate Architectural Culture in Hong Kong and Asia offers the first critical architectural history of one of the oldest and most prolific architectural firms in Asia and the world at large. Long overlooked in the history of modern architectural design and practice, the P&T Group has been an active and influential force in architectural and urban design throughout Hong Kong, greater China, and the Asia-Pacific region since its founding over 150 years ago. The firm’s longevity, coupled with the expansive geographic scope and sheer quantity of its work, make it an important subject of inquiry in relation to Hong Kong and the study of global modes of architectural practice and corporate design as they developed during the late-nineteenth, twentieth, and early twenty-first centuries. A study of the P&T Group offers valuable insight not only into how the firm operated, but into the broader processes of architectural design that took shape within the colonial and post-colonial contexts of Hong Kong, greater China, and Asia. In particular, a history of the firm contributes to our understanding concerning the international history of corporate architectural activity, the circulation of architects and ideas through the region and the professional networks that enabled them over the course of the late nineteenth and twentieth centuries, and the expansion of professional architectural services around the world more generally. Existing architectural historical analysis of Hong Kong tends to be organized around standard disciplinary frameworks such as typology, scale, and style. These studies have enriched our understanding of Hong Kong’s built environment, but their emphasis on the physical and visual nature of architectural expression has obscured other key influences specific to the discipline’s history. In contrast to these approaches, my project’s focus on architectural practice will illuminate the historical relationship between architecture and business—a study not simply of what architects designed, but how they worked and for whom, the ways in which architectural offices were structured, systematized, managed, and operated, and the effects of corporate activity on architectural and urban production. This project will rely on a range of previously unexamined primary and secondary visual and textual sources, interviews, as well as buildings to argue for a conception of modern architecture as more than a series of monumental forms or images, but rather as a set of specific and unique methods of thinking and making that transformed how people worked and lived. 《巴马丹拿集团 (P&T Group)：一段关于香港与亚洲建筑企业文化的历史》 是首个关注亚洲乃至世界范围内最古老、最多产的建筑企业之一建筑历史的研究。虽然巴马丹拿集团自其150多年前成立便大力推动香港、大中华以及亚太地区的建筑与城市设计，却长久被现代建筑设计与实践历史书写所忽视。巴马丹拿的长寿、业务广以及高产使它成为探寻十九世纪晚期、二十世纪以及二十一世纪早期香港和趋全球化建筑实践与企业设计模式的研究的重要线索。 一个围绕巴马丹集团的研究无疑会提供宝贵的视角——不仅能探究一个企业是如何运作，而且能宏观地展示殖民与后殖民时期语境下的香港、大中华与亚洲地区的建筑设计进程。一个企业的历史尤其会帮助我们了解建筑企业活动的国际历史，十九世纪晚期至二十世纪时期区域性与职业上的关系网是如何促成建筑师与建筑想法的流动以及广义上职业建筑服务在世界范围内的拓展。 目前关于香港建筑历史的研究分析大多没有走出标准学科框架，例如：类型、尺度以及风格。虽然这些研究毫无疑问丰富了我们对于香港建筑环境的理解，但它们都过多侧重于建筑表达上的实体性与视觉性。而这恰恰也模糊了其他可以影响这个学科历史的因素。相较于之前那些研究方法，我的研究则关注于建筑实践本身，从而更能够阐释建筑与商业之间的历史关系。不仅关于建筑师设计了什么，而且也探究他们是如何工作，为谁工作，以及建筑企业是如何组成，系统化，管理以及运营；同时，这个研究也着眼于企业活动在建筑与城市生产上给出的效果。 这个研究项目会依据部分此前并未讨论过的一手资料与二手图片和文字材料、采访以及建筑本身，进而探讨一个现代建筑的概念——现代建筑的解读不只局限于纪念碑性的样式或表象，而是一系列极具特征的思考和制作方式。同时，这些方式也转化了人们是如何工作和生活的。

17617421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17617421.value: My project focuses on contemporary self-reflexive map texts: current literary texts that engage fictional maps and mapping practices to effect change. Specifically, this project examines how contemporary postcolonial authors deploy fictional maps to speak with and against the written text. This practice “propositions” (Wood 2010: 56) certain futures or aspirational models of belonging, invites readers to map their worlds differently, and intervenes in the prefigurative politics in the present. While cartography has traditionally been associated with imperial knowledge-making (Harley 1988), its ability to produce authoritative, representational realities can be subverted to create alternative narratives of space and different political imaginaries. Contemporary self-reflexive map-texts, I claim, bring these avenues of subversion into being. Together, map and text mutually reinforce, contest, and contradict each other in order to explore spatial identities outside of the power dynamics of nationalist frameworks of understanding. Fictional maps in novels are by no means new, and most scholarship of map-literature relationships tends to cover periods up to modernism. Although this work provides an important background for contemporary literary studies, it leaves the explosion of self-reflexive map texts in recent literary production unexplored. From the hand-drawn maps of Karachi in Kamila Shamsie’s Kartography (2002) to the reinvented shapes of European nations drawn by the narrator of Xiaolu Guo’s A Concise Chinese-English Dictionary for Lovers (2007), maps take center stage in key contemporary fictions. My study of self-reflexive map texts in contemporary postcolonial literature rectifies this omission in the history of literary geography. In doing so, this project enhances our understanding of the cartographic imperative by showing how contemporary fiction generates alternative geo-bodies that confront dominant structures of spatial imagination such as the ‘grid’ or the nation state. Informed by an interdisciplinary methodology that combines postcolonial studies (Bhabha, 1994; Said,1978), spatial theories (Soja, 1989) and critical geography (Dodge et al 2011,), this project demonstrates that contemporary self-reflexive map-texts advocate for a new kind of spatial literacy: I propose a visual-textual method that emphasizes the importance of place from the perspective of those marginalized from dominant geographical imaginations. At stake in this project is a strategy to understand and denaturalize the primarily Western spatial and geographical attributes in order to make and reclaim space for minority experiences. Emplacement rather than mobility, this project claims, has emerged as one of the dominant, critical modes of political imagination in the present. 本研究項目聚焦於當代自省性地圖文本：即當下通過虛構地圖和製圖實踐以產生變化的文學文本。具體而言，本研究探索當代後殖民作者如何利用虛構地圖同書面文本進行對話和反駁。這種實踐「提出」（Wood 2010: 56）某種未來或理想化的歸屬模型，邀請讀者以不同的方式繪製他們的世界，並干涉當下的前喻政治。雖然製圖學在傳統上與帝國主義知識生產（Harley 1988）息息相關，但其製造權威性、代表性現實的能力可以被顛覆，並用於創造替代性空間敘事和不同的政治想象。我認爲，當代自省性地圖文本為進行這種顛覆提供途徑。地圖與文本相互强化、相互競爭、相互矛盾，以便在民族主義理解框架下的權力動態之外探索空間身份。 小説中的虛構地圖絕非新鮮事物，大多數關於地圖與文學關係的學術研究涵蓋了到現代主義之前的時期。這些研究雖然為當代文學研究提供重要背景，但并未對近年文學創作中激增的自省性地圖文本進行討論。從Kamila Shamsie的《Kartography》（2002年）中的手繪卡拉奇地圖到郭小橹的《戀人版中英字典》（2007年）中由敘述者繪製重塑的歐洲國家版圖，地圖在主要當代小説中占據關鍵位置。我對當代英語文學中自省性地圖文本的研究彌補了文學地理學史中的空白。在此過程中，本研究展示了當代小説如何生成對抗諸如網格或民族國家一類主流空間想象的替代性地緣機體，並以此提升我們對製圖必要性的理解。 本項目采用跨學科的研究方法，將後殖民研究（Bhabha，1994；Said，1978），空間理論（Soja，1989）和批判地理學（Dodge et al，2011）相結合，證明當代自省性地圖文本倡導一種全新的空間運用素養：我提出了一種視覺-文本方法，强調主流地理想象中邊緣人物視角下的地點重要性。本項目的利害關鍵在於一種策略，即理解並將主要來自西方的空間和地理屬性去自然化，以便為少數群體經驗創造並恢復空間。本項目認爲，目前主要的批判性政治想象模式之一是安置而非流動。

17617421.label: Realisation of objectives
17617421.value: Objective 1: Define and critically analyze an archive of self-reflexive map texts illustrating generic expectations, characteristics and political effectiveness. This objective was achieved by reading a range of map texts and establishing a canon despite the diversity of contemporary map texts available. The introduction to my monograph outlines the characteristics of a map text; their relationship to plot; and the political goals and agendas they can be said to achieve. Of note is the project’s establishment of contemporary map texts in a global context. 2. Develop a new interdisciplinary theoretical framework that synthesizes critical geography, postcolonial studies, and spatial theory for analyzing self- reflexive map texts in a global context. The second objective was achieved by reading interdisciplinarily specifically within the context of literary geography which explicitly seeks to wed literary studies with human geography. The introduction to the project outlines the intersection between spatial literary studies, the geographic/spatial politics of postcolonial theory and the history of cartography. Each chapters is framed by its own theoretical introduction necessary to the reading of the literature. 3. Revise and update a history of map-literature relationships to include research into self-reflexivity; agency and map-making; and mapping practices as postcolonial forms of resistance. The introduction to the monography clearly lays out the history of the study of maps in literature related to making literary and spatial sense of realism and modernity; to the need for cognitive mapping to locate oneself within capitalism’s rewriting of space; and distant reading as a more sociological spatial analysis of literary works. However, the urgency of living in a map-able present where we are inundated with new mapping technologies enabled by digital mapping devices has resulted in a renewed and concentrated cartographization of literary texts. Locating the book’s argument within existing conversations in critical geography and post-representational theory, I chart the aesthetic and political labor performed by map texts and the participatory possibilities for readers they open up that, in turn, produce the spatial practices that make up new political identities. Complete a draft of a critical monograph that demonstrates the crucial role self- reflexive map texts play in our understanding of the contemporary period. The draft of the monograph has been completed. Two chapters are “publication ready” and have been sent to a number of publishers. A book proposal was also completed. The remaining chapters of the monograph remain in draft form and will be revised after peer review. 5. Prepare the monograph for submission to internationally ranked presses for publication. The book proposal and supporting materials have been favorably received by Wales University Press and Ohio State University Press. I am moving forward with formal peer review with Ohio State University Press which is a leading publisher in narrative theory.

17617421.label: Major findings and research outcome
17617421.value: Map-ability: The Imperative to Map in Contemporary Literature identifies the emergence of a new, distinct literary form fueled by dramatic, recent transformations in the experience of geopolitical space. The twenty-first century has witnessed a large-scale shift in the both spatial technologies available and the cultural dynamics through which space is given meaning—from the ubiquity of GIS in our daily lives to its use in the redrawing of coastlines by climate change; from rescripted spatialities generated by migration and ethno-nationalism to radical reinventions of scale and distance caused by the pandemic. Contemporary literature has registered and responded to these transformations, I argue, through the creation of what I call map-ability: formal reading strategies that develop, sharpen, and even re-invent the spatial literacies necessary to navigate this current cultural phenomenon. Self-reflexive in nature, the map text stages a deliberate collaboration between text and map where mapping explicitly drives the plot and each form comments on the other, modeling and requiring an act of doubled reading. When these texts harness the map – sometimes hand-drawn by the author from a character’s perspective, often reproduced from official sources – to interrogate how space is claimed, they demonstrate how political agency might be enabled or even curtailed in the performance of map-ability. This new aesthetic lexicon both reflects and advances what might be called the political theory of map making. Critical geography has long insisted on the role of cartography in imperial knowledge-making , and scholars interested in the post-representational qualities of maps have demonstrated how decolonial and feminist practices of countermapping can create alternative narratives of space and different political imaginaries. Map-ability illuminates the way these avenues of subversion materialize in new ways, as map and text mutually reinforce, contest, and contradict each other and spatial identities come to be legible outside of hegemonic cartographic imaginaries. While contemporary map texts show how rights, belonging, identities and politics can no longer be understood nor contained by spaces tied to the ideology of territory, map-ability forms a visual-textual practice that can claim new versions of the future or aspirational models of belonging and invites readers to map their worlds differently. Map-ability offers a crucial rethinking of the “agency” of maps by shifting the study of place in literary texts to a more vigorous consideration of the role that maps play in prefigurative politics.

17617421.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17617421.value: The monograph will be sent to review in venues such as ASAP, Contemporary Literature, Studies in the Novel, as well as Literary Geographies, Progress in Human Geography, and The Cartographic Journal. Popular blog sites such as “The Map Room: A Weblog about Maps”; “Progressive Geographies” and the “Livingmaps Network” would be interested in promoting and reviewing the book for a more general readership. Beyond the promotion of the book, further research developments include the study of contemporary map art and artifacts – a project I am well-suited to develop as Editor-in-Chief of ASAP/Journal.

17617421.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17617421.value: Maps can be used to serve the interests of the nation state; they can establish sovereignty and shore up the power that institutions impose on our experiences of space. When embedded in literary works, however, maps can be manipulated differently: they become more creative, more subversive, and can interfere with such power, often in unexpected ways. Pairing map-texts by Xiaolu Guo, Kamila Shamsie, Wayde Compton, Dung Kei-Cheung, China Miéville, and Christopher Priest, with graphic novels, literary atlases, cartographic art, and performance, we can discern a new literary form of political empowerment. By defamiliarizing conventional map features such as borders and denaturalizing territorial and maritime boundaries, map-texts help navigate challenging political landscapes, weaken structures that remain preserved by investments in cartography, and locate places to resist. By developing and honing readers’ spatial literacy, what I call “map-ability”, map-texts train readers to interpret and critique multiple visual registers that reveal spatial injustice and invisible geographies of power. Map-ability shows contemporary literature’s growing capacity for changing readers’ relationships to their world as geopolitical agents in it.

17617721.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17617721.value: Technology-facilitated sexual abuse (TFSA) refers to a range of behaviours in which digital technologies are used to facilitate both virtual and face-to-face sexually based harms. The proliferation of smartphones and high Internet penetration rates across the globe have made it easier for individuals to both perpetrate and become victims of TFSA. This emerging form of interpersonal abuse has attracted considerable attention from both academics and the general public. However, empirical studies of TFSA remain limited in the academic arena. Whilst our society is well aware of the female victims of sexual abuse, male victims are often forgotten or neglected. In academia, such topics as men who have sex with men (MSM), who are disproportionally affected by various kinds of abuse, including sexual abuse, have received insufficient research attention. Another topic that requires more research is the influence of smartphone dating applications (apps) on TFSA. In recent years, dating apps have become very popular, especially among MSM, because they are convenient and easy to use and provide access to a large pool of MSM nearby. However, forensic evidence and criminology theories such as O’Connell’s typology of online grooming and Suler’s online disinhibition effect suggest that the use of dating apps may increase the risk of TFSA. In addition, DeKeseredy’s male peer support theory is an important ecological theory for explaining the causes of sexual abuse, but has rarely been applied to understanding sexual abuse perpetration among MSM. The aim of the proposed project is to address the research gap concerning TFSA among MSM by adopting a mixed-methods approach in three studies. Study 1 will focus on developing instruments to measure TFSA and negative peer support. Study 2, a quantitative study, will explore the factors associated with TFSA victimisation and perpetration. Study 3, a qualitative study, will explore the contexts and experience of TFSA among victims, as well as perpetrators’ TFSA perceptions and motives. The research will be novel in a number of respects. It will be: • the first quantitative study of TFSA among MSM; • the first quantitative study of the links among dating app use, negative peer support and TFSA; and • the first qualitative exploration of the experience of TFSA among MSM. As well as informing public health guidance, social policy and sexual minority-targeted interventions, the findings will also contribute to research in three areas: sexual abuse, communication studies and homosexuality. 科技促成的性侵犯（Technology-facilitated sexual abuse；TFSA）指一系列以數位科技促成，線上及面對面之性侵害。現時智能手機在全球各地普及，互聯網滲透率高，使人更容易干犯及受害於TFSA。是項新興的侵害形式備受學界及公眾關注；然而，現時學術界有關TFSA的實證研究仍然有限。 儘管社會充分意識到性侵犯之女性受害者，男性受害者往往被遺忘或忽略。在學術界，主題諸如男男性接觸者（men who have sex with men；MSM）並未得到足夠的研究關注，而這一群人遭受各種形式的侵犯，包括性侵犯的比率卻特別高。另一個需要更多研究的主題則為交友軟體對TFSA的影響。近年，交友軟體變得非常普及，於MSM之間尤甚，原因是這些軟體方便及容易使用，他們能輕易與大量就近的其他MSM聯繫。但是，法醫證據及犯罪學理論，例如O’Connell 的網絡性誘拐類型學及Suler 的網絡去抑制效應皆指出，使用交友軟體或增加遭受TFSA的風險。此外，DeKeseredy 男性同儕支援理論是解釋性侵犯原由的一重要生態理論。但是，此理論卻甚少被用作理解MSM之間的性侵犯。 本擬議計劃的目的是採取混合研究方式，以三項研究填補有關MSM間之TFSA的研究缺口。研究一將重點討論開發測量TFSA及負面同儕支援之工具。研究二為定量研究，將探討與干犯及受害於TFSA有關的因素。研究三則為定性研究，將探討受害者的TFSA背景及經歷，以及干犯者對TFSA的看法和動機。本計劃在數方面均是新穎的。它將會是： · 第一項關於MSM間之TFSA的定量研究； · 第一項關於使用交友軟件、負面同儕支援及TFSA之關聯的定量研究；及 · 第一項探討MSM間之TFSA經歷的定性研究。 除了為公共衛生指引、社會政策以及對性小眾的針對性干預措施提供依據，是項研究的成果亦會對三個研究領域作出貢獻，包括：性侵犯、傳播學和同性戀研究。

17617921.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17617921.value: My overarching research question is how the state and law interact with homeowners' self-governance effort in China's urban residential neighborhoods. Neighborhood governance in urban China has come to a new age featuring a fundamental governance crisis. Compared to what urban neighborhoods were twenty years ago when most private housing projects were newly constructed, they are facing more urgent governance problems arising from both building aging and deterioration and inadequate institutional infrastructure. The last three years have witnessed both national and local legal and policy initiatives to address such an urban governance crisis. The proposed research project coins the term "authoritarian commons" to capture the dynamic interactions between the authoritarian state and homeowners’ effort to create liberal commons in their neighborhoods. Condominium ownership is the only legal form of urban housing ownership in China’s Property Law and the new Civil Code. Common property rights shared by all homeowners include not only the right to manage common space but also the right to form an autonomous institution, i.e., a homeowners' association ("HoA"), to govern their own neighborhoods. Yet, such urban commons grow in an authoritarian state whose tradition is to exercise monopolistic control by relying on either local government agencies or real estate management companies to manage neighborhoods. The implementation of homeowner self-governance depends largely on each municipality. According to the data verified in a pilot project, 94% of the condominium neighborhoods in Shanghai have set up homeowners’ associations, compared with 41% in Shenzhen and 12% in Beijing. Different municipal governments adopt different approaches to deal with homeowner self-governance due to their varying capacity to govern, the risk to social stability and local economic conditions. Based on these three variables, I will investigate the law and practice of HoAs in six Chinese cities, including the three megacities above. I will conduct the first-ever study digging into the two-decade development of homeowners’ associations in urban China to examine the interplay between the authoritarian state and communities. This research project will be a natural extension of my previous well-noted study on Chinese small/informal property that elucidates the co-evolution of law and social norms. Drawing on mixed methods including a comprehensive examination of national and local legislative and judicial data, ethnographic fieldwork and questionnaire surveys, this project endeavors to further my co-evolution theory by examining the interactions between state and communities in China's ongoing urban governance crisis. 本项目计划研究在中国主要城市小区治理面临的挑战及解决办法，特别关注其中国家和社会的互动。拟在多个城市进行深入的田野调查，同时系统分析相关的立法和司法实践。理论上计划对法律与社会共同演进的框架予以拓展。

17617921.label: Realisation of objectives
17617921.value: This project has comprehensively achieved the four primary objectives stated in the original grant application. The objectives have been systematically pursued through rigorous methodological triangulation, including ethnographic research, large-scale questionnaire surveys, archival analyses, and a sophisticated survey experiment. We’re still processing the last payment to a survey company and it would be highly appreciated if the account is not closed before the payment is delivered. Below is a detailed evaluation of the achievement status of each objective. Objective 1: To comprehensively examine legislative and judicial data on neighborhood governance at national and local levels, understanding interactions between national and local authorities and variations across different Chinese cities. Achievement Status: Fully achieved with minor methodological adjustment. Explanation: The objective was largely realized through extensive archival research and qualitative analysis of selected key judicial decisions rather than a systematic quantitative analysis of all judicial cases. The team conducted comprehensive analyses of legislative documents at both national and local levels, focusing on interactions between different government tiers and variations across four representative cities: Beijing, Shanghai, Shenzhen, and Wuhan. While the initial proposal explicitly outlined a systematic quantitative analysis of judicial documents, practical constraints necessitated a methodological adjustment. As a result, the project performed preliminary data organization and initial analyses of judicial cases, but a comprehensive quantitative analysis remains to be completed in future research phases. Currently, the team has conducted substantial qualitative examinations of particularly influential or representative judicial cases, supplemented by AI-driven preliminary document analysis, which provides foundational insights for future quantitative research. In-depth ethnographic research and analysis of influential judicial cases provided critical qualitative insights into real-world interactions between local authorities, courts, homeowners, and management companies. Interviews with legal professionals, judges, and government officials validated and deepened our understanding of these judicial contexts. Furthermore, documentary evidence such as HoA meeting minutes, city regulations, and internal archives corroborated these findings, thus fulfilling the goal of achieving a nuanced, multi-dimensional perspective despite the methodological adjustment. Objective 2: To investigate the development of neighborhood governance in different types of Chinese cities over the past two decades, particularly homeowners' varying approaches to self-governance. Achievement Status: Fully achieved. Explanation: The comparative aspect of neighborhood governance was meticulously addressed through in-depth ethnographic research complemented by extensive quantitative data from a large-scale survey of 3341 respondents across the three selected cities. These cities represented varying levels of economic development, governance capacity, and political significance. The ethnographic research involved 224 interviews with diverse stakeholders, including homeowner activists, government officials, real estate managers, and legal experts. Interviews were conducted systematically, using referrals, snowball sampling, and direct engagement with homeowner organizations, thus ensuring the representation of a wide range of perspectives. This robust qualitative and quantitative framework clearly mapped distinct governance models emerging over the past two decades, highlighting differences in how homeowners organize, mobilize, and interact with local authorities. The findings have been successfully disseminated through leading journals, notably the publication in the American Journal of Comparative Law (2023), recognized by the prestigious Hessel Yntema Prize, confirming the scholarly significance and rigor of the project. Objective 3: To distill practical lessons from urban neighborhood governance, generating impacts within and beyond academia, including recommendations for legal reforms and practical advice for Chinese homeowners. Achievement Status: Fully achieved and ongoing dissemination. Explanation: The project has successfully distilled practical insights that benefit both academic circles and broader society. Central to this objective is the newly released book, The Authoritarian Commons: Neighborhood Democratization in Urban China (Cambridge University Press, January 2025). This volume systematically synthesizes lessons drawn from comprehensive empirical research, offering actionable recommendations for legal reforms and practical guidance for homeowner associations and local authorities. The findings were further enriched by a survey experiment titled Democracy Premium in an Unlikely Place?, whose preliminary results have already garnered recognition by the Harvard Urban China Conference (scheduled May 2025), underscoring the real-world relevance of the project’s outcomes. Moreover, extensive outreach activities are planned, including book presentations at internationally esteemed institutions such as Duke, Yale, Stanford, Columbia, Chicago, NYU, Penn, McGill, the American Bar Foundation, Harvard-MIT Urban China Series, and Peking University. These engagements will further amplify the practical impact and ensure broad dissemination of the findings and recommendations. Objective 4: To deepen theoretical understanding of the co-evolution of law and social norms through analysis of interactions between state and community in neighborhood governance. Achievement Status: Fully achieved. Explanation: The theoretical dimension of the research significantly expanded the understanding of the interplay between formal legal institutions and informal social norms within an authoritarian context. Drawing on extensive qualitative insights from ethnographic fieldwork—first conducted in Beijing, Shanghai, and Shenzhen, and subsequently in 2023 extending to Wuhan and additional cities during the COVID-19 lockdowns—the research captured nuanced dynamics of cooperation, resistance, and state-community negotiation under evolving legal frameworks. Empirical findings led to notable theoretical contributions, prominently featured in peer-reviewed journals, including the articles published in Urban Studies (2025), American Journal of Comparative Law (2023). These publications received significant academic attention, including winning Hessel Yntema Prize awarded by American Society of Comparative Law (2024), underscoring the project's success in contributing to broader theoretical debates about governance, authoritarianism, democratization, and legal development.

17617921.label: Major findings and research outcome
17617921.value: This research explores how urban homeowners' associations (HoAs) in China assert property-based autonomy (dominium) that potentially challenges the authoritarian state's broader authority (imperium). The major outcomes and findings include: • Divergent Paths of Neighborhood Democratization Comparative research across Shanghai (94% HoA establishment), Shenzhen (41%), and Beijing (12%) revealed distinct local strategies for managing neighborhood democratization, reflecting differing perceptions of risk and local governmental capacities. These findings have been extensively detailed in the award-winning article, The Authoritarian Commons: Divergent Paths of Neighborhood Democratization in Three Chinese Megacities (American Journal of Comparative Law, 2023, recipient of the Hessel Yntema Prize, 2024). • Democracy Premium and Conditional Legitimacy Using an innovative survey experiment involving 3,341 residents across three major Chinese cities (conducted in 2024 and accepted for the Harvard Urban China Conference, May 2025), the study examines the “democracy premium”—the notion that democratic processes enhance citizen compliance even in authoritarian contexts. The findings show that democratic decision-making within neighborhoods significantly increases compliance when supported by local judicial authority, nearly matching compliance levels observed with state-issued directives. However, absent clear legal support—even with majority homeowner backing—compliance markedly decreases. This reveals that democratic decision-making alone is insufficient in authoritarian settings without accompanying legal recognition. • Political Trust and Governance Outcomes Neighborhoods with effective homeowner associations (HoAs) experience superior governance outcomes—including increased democratic participation, stronger community identity, and notably greater trust in local authorities. These findings challenge traditional assumptions that authoritarian states uniformly suppress or co-opt civic engagement. Instead, political trust emerges from positive experiences with local democratic governance. (Communities Built on Political Trust, Urban Studies, 2025). Together, these studies highlight a nuanced reality: authoritarian states can derive significant legitimacy benefits from permitting localized democratic governance; Further, empowered civic communities can evolve into influential actors capable of both cooperating with and resisting state authority, redefining state-society relationships under authoritarian conditions.

17617921.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17617921.value: Future research can build on these outcomes through: • Long-term Effects of Democratic Experiments Conducting longitudinal studies to evaluate whether democratization experiences—such as those observed during China’s COVID-19 lockdowns—result in sustained civic engagement and enhanced political trust beyond immediate crises. The key question is how will the downturn of China's real estate sector influence HoA development. With declining local government resources, authorities will likely shift more responsibilities onto homeowners, potentially heightening neighborhood conflicts. Consequently, I predict intensified neighborhood disputes, increased state attention to HoAs, and an enhanced but cautious governmental effort to simultaneously support and control neighborhood self-governance. While central coordination may standardize certain governance practices, regional variations will likely persist. • Future Effect inherent in homeowner self-governance While homeowner mobilization has introduced valuable democratic checks against government and corporate dominance in urban China, the movement may disadvantage property-less residents, mirroring debates around NIMBYism ("Not in My Backyard") in other contexts. Balancing inclusive governance while avoiding exclusionary tendencies remains an essential challenge for further inquiry. Proposed Action: The next phase of research will include follow-up survey experiments, comparative fieldwork, and scholarly engagement through planned presentations at prestigious institutions.

17617921.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17617921.value: This research investigates how homeowners in China’s megacities democratically manage neighborhood issues through homeowners' associations (HoAs), despite the country's authoritarian political system. Typically, authoritarian governments are thought to suppress civic organizations, seeing them as threats to central authority. However, Chinese HoAs have thrived, becoming vibrant examples of local democracy. The study reveals that neighborhoods with effective democratic self-governance not only manage communal issues better but also develop stronger community bonds and higher trust in local authorities—a phenomenon termed the "democracy premium." Crucially, the research finds that residents follow democratic neighborhood decisions as strongly as government commands—but only when these decisions have clear legal backing. Without explicit legal support, democratic decisions lose effectiveness, highlighting that the rule of law is critical even in authoritarian settings. Comparing major cities like Shanghai, Beijing and Shenzhen, the study illustrates how local government capacities and judicial institutions shape these grassroots democratic practices. Ultimately, this work shows the complex balancing act China faces between promoting effective local democracy and maintaining authoritarian control, reshaping how we understand democracy and civic engagement under authoritarian regimes.

17618121.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17618121.value: Linear Programming is a well-known methodology in business data analysis. In economics, the application of linear programming includes binary choice models, partially identified models, etc. Linear programming is formulated as minimizing a linear cost function of unknown vectorized variable subject to a set of linear inequality constraints of the vector of variable. However, viewing the linear programming as an operator that maps the input, including the cost function and the set of constraints, to the output, the solution, this operator is not differentiable. Rather, this operator is piecewise linear. We consider the setting where all the input are estimated with asymptotically Gaussian errors. Given that the operator is only piecewise linear and therefore, non-Hadarmard differentiable, the inference of the solution is irregular and its asymptotic distribution is non-Gaussian. Such a problem is challenging as it poccesses the feature of irregular inference. It becomes even more difficult when the number of parameters and constraints are large compared to sample size. First, we propose a method to perform inference conditional on the active set, i.e., the set of binding constraints. We show that the distribution of solution is truncated Gaussian. Second, we proposal a novel algorithm to sample from truncated Gaussian distribution in order to obtain cut-off values for valid inference. We plan to further investigate a unified robust approach for inference unconditional on the set of active sets, including theoretical results and fast algorithms. 線性規劃是商業數據分析中眾所周知的方法。在 經濟學，線性規劃的應用包括二元選擇模型，部分 識別模型等。線性規劃被公式化為最小化線性成本 受一組線性不等式約束的未知矢量化變量的函數 變量的向量。然而，將線性規劃視為一個運算符 將輸入（包括成本函數和約束集）映射到輸出，即 解，這個算子是不可微的。相反，這個運算符是分段線性的。我們 考慮使用漸近高斯估計所有輸入的設置 錯誤。鑑於運算符只是分段線性的，因此，非 Hadarmard 可微，解的推論是不規則的，其漸近分佈為 非高斯。這樣的問題具有挑戰性，因為它涉及不規則的特徵 推理。當參數的數量和 與樣本量相比，約束很大。首先，我們提出一種方法來執行 以活動集為條件的推理，即綁定約束集。我們證明 解的分佈是截斷的高斯分佈。其次，我們提出了一種新穎的算法 從截斷的高斯分佈中採樣以獲得截止值 有效推論。我們計劃進一步研究一種統一的、穩健的推理方法 對活動集的集合是無條件的，包括理論結果和快速算法。

17618621.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17618621.value: The nature of the movement that led to the commencement of the 1899 Hague Peace Conference that created the Permanent Court of Arbitration (PCA) has been described as obscure (Grant & Temperley 1952 at 581-82). This project will clarify the nature of that movement, not only to fill a gap in the literature but also to better understand whether this event that started reliance on law in resolving international disputes has its roots in elitism or majoritarianism, which arguably would add to the legitimacy of international dispute settlement. This will be done by focusing on, inter alia, the 1898-1899 conference proceedings and diplomatic correspondence of France, Germany, The Netherlands, the United Kingdom and the United States like never before. Some commentators see the commencement of the conference and the PCA's creation as arising out of an aristocratic movement to unify European states, not out of the more universal, grassroots peace movement that tried to replace war with law and the application of law through international arbitration (Caron 2000 at 5-6; Tyron 1916 at 513-15). Peace activist James Tryon eloquently explained the distinction between these two peace movements: While European states were busy concluding the Holy Alliance and other alliances among themselves to try to bring peace to Europe, “the desire for peace was [being] cultivated by another kind of Holy Alliance far more consistent in its methods than the first,” which was a global Holy Alliance of “the goodly company of thoughtful men and women who saw the folly of war and educated public opinion against it” (Tryon 1911 at 359). Some commentators have assumed the influence of the grassroots movement on the conference and the PCA’s creation without recognizing the possibility that there was a competing elitist movement that equally could have been the influence (Roberts 2001 at 201); van den Dungen 1995 at 17). From the perspective of that time, one would have expected for these two events to mark the apex of the aristocratic movement, given how Tsar Nicholas of Russia called the conference, aristocratic states had relied on arbitration to a large degree prior to this point, and aristocrats and those under the aristocratic order were among the plurality at the conference. This project will explore the impact of these two movements on the creation of the PCA. 1899年海牙和平会议的召开成功设立了常设仲裁法院（PCA），然而这场和平运动的本质却始终处于不为学界所清楚探知的状态（Grant & Tempeley 1952 at 581-82）。该项目旨在阐明该运动的本质。其意义不仅仅为了填补现有研究的空白且为了更好地理解这一首次依靠法律手段解决国际争端的事件是否源于精英主义或多数主义。该项目将有助于提高国际争端解决的合法性。为此，该项目将前所未有的将自1898至1899年法国、德国、荷兰、英国和美国的会议记录和外交信函做为重点研究对象。 部分评论家认为1899海牙和平会议的召开及常设仲裁法院的设立缘起于统一欧洲的贵族运动，而非源于更具普遍性的，试图以法律取代代替战争并通过适用法律的国际仲裁的草根和平运动 (Caron 2000 at 5-6; Tyron 1916 at 513-15)。和平活动人士James Tryon反复解释了这两类和平运动的区别：当欧洲国家忙于缔结神圣同盟，其他联盟也试图将和平带至欧洲的同时，另一种其方法更为一致的，由考虑周全的，见识到战争的愚蠢并教育公众反对战争的男女们所组成的全球神圣同盟兴起了(Tryon 1911 at 359)。虽然部分评论家假设了草根运动对于1899海牙和平会议的召开及常设仲裁法院的影响，一个同样能对此造成影响的精英运动的可能性却没有被充分认知 (Roberts 2001 at 201; van den Dungen 1995 at 17)。 从当时的角度来看，鉴于俄国沙皇如何称呼1899和平会议，这两个件事（1899海牙和平会议的召开及常设仲裁法院的设立）标志着欧洲贵族运动的巅峰。贵族国家于1899年之前就在很大的程度上依赖仲裁解决争端，且贵族及贵族秩序下的人在该和平会议中占多数。该项目旨在于探究1899和平运动及1899海牙和平会议对于设立常设仲裁法院的影响。

17618621.label: Realisation of objectives
17618621.value: This project has produced five deliverables. The first deliverable a complete book manuscript (entitled Discreet Charm in the Republican Creation of the Permanent Court of Arbitration), which consists of 92,695 words or 206 pages, not including a bibliography, index or appendices. It was written with a co-author Guillermo Coronado Aguilar. The book currently is under consideration with Cambridge University Press. The second deliverable is a sole-authored article (entitled The Permanent Court of International Justice in Global History), which consists of 12,780 words or 29 pages. It was published volume 33 of the Duke Journal of Comparative & International Law in 2023, and it appeared on pages 151 to 179. The third deliverable is a complete article (entitled Aristocrats in Arbitration: Did Political Institutions Affect Inter-State Arbitration Before or After the 1899 Hague Peace Conference), which consists of 24,041 words or 68 pages. It was written with two co-authors Arthur L.W. Cheung and Bryane Michael. The article currently is under consideration with the American Journal of International Law. The fourth deliverable is a paper presentation on a panel (entitled “The Role of Peace Movements in the 1899 Creation of the Permanent Court of Arbitration”), which was presented at the International Conference at City University London and London School of Economics entitled “International Rethinking the Past and Present of Liberal Internationalism,” in London, United Kingdom on May 11-13, 2023. This paper was co-authored by Guillermo Coronado Aguilar. The fifth deliverable is another paper presentation on a panel (entitled “The Role of Peace Movements in the 1899 Creation of the Permanent Court of Arbitration”), which was presented at a Swiss National Science Foundation Workshop entitled “New Directions in the Theory & History of International Law” at the Graduate Institute of International and Development Studies, Geneva, Switzerland, on June 2-3, 2022. This paper was a sole-authored paper. I also have been able to enter into collaboration concerning this project while on sabbatical leave from September to December 2023, both as a Weatherhead Scholar at the Weatherhead Center for International Affairs at Harvard University and as a Visiting Scholar at the Saltzman Institute of War and Peace Studies at Columbia University. I have been able to share my research and ideas on this project with other Scholars and faculty members at Columbia and Harvard. It has helped me develop my research and develop my network of colleagues at Harvard and elsewhere. These five deliverables make it so that I have far exceeded the objectives of this project, which only envisioned one article and one conference. With a total of 129,516 words with just the book and article and a grant of HK$291,904, I was able to produce 1 word for every HK$2.25 of grant money. I would be surprised if this rate does not rank towards the top of grant holders. I was not able to publish the book and second article in time for this report because editors take their time in reviewing manuscripts, and it is difficult to rush them. I have done my best to get these deliverables to the publishers as soon as possible. I am confident that they will be published with an excellent publisher and journal. Had I been granted the full amount of time that I originally requested, I would have had these publications in time for the final report. I have done my best with the limited time that I was allotted. I also would note that my wife had a sudden cardiac arrest in May 2023 while on annual leave. This meant that I needed to spend time with her and my children in the hospital while she was recovering. I am unsure of how much this impacted my timeline. Nevertheless, I did the best I could in meeting, even exceeding, the objectives of this project. As the project stands now, everything is finished, and I am just waiting to hear back from editors and publishers with their decisions on the book and one article. They may ask for changes to the manuscripts, and I will deal with those requests when they arrive. I do not anticipate it being a problem meeting their expectations.

17618621.label: Major findings and research outcome
17618621.value: 1. Sole-Authored Article entitled "The Permanent Court of International Justice in Global History" The Permanent Court of International Justice’s contributions often are overshadowed by the fact that it was the predecessor of the overwhelmingly important International Court of Justice. This article is the first to look at the Permanent Court’s possible contribution to global history in its own right. It provides compelling support for liberal institutionalism and the notion that global history has been influenced by actors other than states, even though states remain the main shapers of global history. 2. First-Author Co-Authored Book Manuscript entitled Discreet Charm in the Republican Creation of the Permanent Court of Arbitration This book takes a deep dive into the historical archives to determine the relative influence of the elite-driven aristocratic peace movement and the republican peace movement on the Permanent Court of Arbitration’s creation. With data from historical archival materials pointing the way at every stage, this book shows that the PCA’s creation story is more about the success of the republican movement than the aristocratic movement. 3. First-Author Co-Authored Article entitled “Aristocrats in Arbitration: Did Political Institutions Affect Inter-State Arbitration Before or After the 1899 Hague Peace Conference? In a way that aims to be accessible to non-statisticians, this article has shown that there is a statistically significant relationship between respondent-appointed aristocratic arbitrators on a tribunal and outcome against the aristocratic party, as well as a statistically significant relationship between no respondent-appointed aristocratic arbitrators on a tribunal and outcome in favor of the claimant, but only in inter-state arbitrations before the 1899 Hague Peace Conference for both of these relationships. Non-statistical qualitative work by the corresponding author elsewhere suggests that that change might have been due to an increase in competition in the inter-state-arbitration space coming from non-aristocratic elements in society, mostly right before, during, and after the 1899 Hague Peace Conference. At or around that time, aristocratic arbitrators collectively realized that they needed to stop finding against the aristocratic parties who kept appointing them in the first place, signaling an end to or at least a softening of their full commitment to the idea of noblesse oblige in this context.

17618621.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17618621.value: I envision writing another book that continues on from the one associated with this project. The Netherlands’ political capital of the Hague hosted a watershed peace movement between the end of the 19th century and the first quarter of the 20th century. The resulting accomplishments from that movement represent some of the key normative and institutional developments that govern international law and international relations today. American industrialist Andrew Carnegie features prominently in the history of that peace movement, inasmuch as he donated a vast sum for the creation of the Peace Palace, among other things. Historians largely have overlooked the contributions of other Americans to this peace movement. The future project will uncover and analyze the contributions of residents of the New York City area to this peace movement, with the hypothesis being that New Yorkers provided crucial intellectual and financial leadership to this effort. Given the emphasis on international arbitration in the New York City area and in the Hague peace movement during this period, it even may be possible to see the Hague peace movement as an extension of what was occurring in New York City at that time.

17618621.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17618621.value: All of the deliverables for this project have pushed the boundaries of our understanding concerning (1) the social forces at play on the Hague Peace Movement at the turn of the 20th century, and (2) the norms that came out of that Movement. In particular, the Hague Peace Movement created the Permanent Court of Arbitration, the Permanent Court of International Justice, and the Peace Palace, all of which have fulfilled an important role in our international legal order. By better understanding these social forces and the impact of these institutions, they gain greater legitimacy and we gain greater understanding of how decisions in these types of institutions are made.

17618821.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17618821.value: This project addresses a set of inquiries in what can broadly be defined as the studies of the history of the self in China and the West through the prism of diary - as a genre of autobiography and as the micro-macro link of historical research. It grew out of my recent effort to produce an annotated volume of the newly discovered diaries by Qing women (in press). Methodological questions that arose during the course, such as those concerning the generic fluidities and transformations of diary over time, or the nature of diary as a “historical” source, have intrigued scholars in an expanding field of study on diary in the Chinese tradition. These questions can be most fruitfully examined beyond a single cultural framework. The lack of attention to gender as a critical angle in the field, in particular, can only be redressed through engaging with discussions that include feminist approaches to the history of the self and studies of women’s autobiographical practices embedded in various sociohistorical specificities. The aim of the present project is to rethink some of the most fundamental questions and assumptions in the field by bringing women diarists into the center of a dialogue in methodology. I begin by untangling a key misconception in comparative analyses of diary, namely, the public/ private binary used to distinguish the Chinese tradition of semi-public daily documents of scholar-officials from the Western diary-writing tradition rooted in confessions. This paves the way for a dialogue in methodology in two major directions. First, questioning “naïve” assumptions about the public/ private nature of diary opens a window into the intellectual shifts in the West during the 1970s. Diary, like other genres of autobiography or “self-writing,” stimulated a new scholarly interest in its devices for mediating between the internal and external, self-creation and social norms, and microcosms of individual lives and broader historical change. These discussions crossed cultural borders during the 1980s, generating intense scholarly debates till today. Second, feminist critiques of these intellectual shifts went beyond the polemics of challenging the exclusion of women diarists from the history of the self. Diary suggested a terrain for developing fresh angles to the “ideologies” of feelings that naturalized the demarcation of public/ private spheres and that attributed “secret” records of inner lives increasingly to women’s diaries. Mapping strategies for re-inscribing dominant ideologies comprise the latest efforts to examine women’s diaries and autobiographical practices in multiple contexts. 本課題通過日記這一視角探討中西方個人史研究中的問題，其中對日記的理解是自傳文類的一種和歷史研究中微觀、宏觀層面的連接點。課題的構思來源於近期對新近發現的清代女性日記的整理（點校稿待出版）。整理過程中產生的方法論層面的疑問已在中國日記傳統這一研究領域獲得關注，例如有關日記文體“不確定性”和文體衍變的疑問，以及有關日記何以成爲“史料”的疑問。這類疑問應當超越某個特定的文化框架才能得到最富有成效的探討。如能納入不同社會歷史框架下女性主義對個人史的回應，與之進行對話，這一領域中性別視角的缺乏尤其能夠得到修正。本課題的目的是將女性日記視爲對話的核心關注，以便重新思考研究中最基本的問題或假設。 第一步是嘗試解開對中西日記傳統的比較分析中一個關鍵誤解，即，用公開/私密的二分法來區別兩種傳統，認爲中國傳統中的士人日記具有半公開性，而西方日記傳統則植根於宗教懺悔的私密性。由此展開兩個主要方向的方法論對話。其一，質疑上述簡單化的二分法為觀察上世紀七十年代西方學術思想的變化打開一個窗口。如同其他自傳文類一樣，日記的寫作機制激發了新的研究興趣，包括協調内在與外界、自我創造與社會規範、個人微觀世界與宏大歷史變化之間的機制。這類探討在八十年代跨越了文化邊界，引發的激烈爭論延續至今。其二，針對上述學術思想變化的女性主義批評並不停留於對將女性日記排除在個人史之外的批評。日記揭示了發展新的研究視角的可能，如公開/私密的劃分源自有關情感的特定思維模式，將所謂内心生活的“秘密”記錄日益加諸於對女性日記的闡釋。而最新關於不同語境下女性日記與自傳寫作的研究則致力於發現其中改寫占主導性思維模式的策略。
