18610121.value: 研究指出，在經濟發達國家中，至少有30%的幼童表現出自我調節問題（即難以管理自己的行為、認知和情緒）。自我調節能力可算是斷定入學準備度、學業成就和人生幸福的最重要預測因素。大型縱貫性研究指出，較強的自我調節能力可以對幼童的不佳發展起緩衝作用，尤其對於社經背景較低的幼童。因此，辨認有效幫助自我調節能力的早期介入措施至關重要。「節奏與動作活動促進自我調節」（RAMSR）是一個較新的課堂介入措拖。其建基於認知、治療及教育等方面的關鍵知識，這措施能促進神經認知發展。RAMSR與其他西方和東方國家使用與音樂相關的措拖相類似，皆顯示出對幼童自我調節能力的正面影響 (Williams & Berthelsen, 2019)。 我們的研究指出，香港幼稚園老師：(1) 由於準備有限，甚少在課堂上進行與協調性相關的律動活動；(2) 缺乏支援幼童自我調節能力的教學策略；和 (3) 認同RAMSR在香港幼稚園的可行性及與本地課程的一致性。這些研究成果顯示出，我們急需設計與課堂介入措拖如RAMSR相關的教師培訓課程。這些介入措施旨在增加幼童對節奏與動作的接觸，並有可能增強他們的自我調節能力。為了定制能在本地使用的RAMSR，我們的團隊正在進行先導研究，並將開發一個低成本、易於擴展且可持續的網上課程。這個課程結合了與大學研究人員的同步及非同步交流，並提供多種工作嵌入式協作學習機會及獨立學習的學習資源。 透過在14間服務低社經背景幼童的幼稚園進行一連串對於介入措拖的隨機對照試驗，我們將探討： 1） 網上培訓課程對於提升教師實行RAMSR的有效性，並以自我反思和專家觀察衡量； 2） 於不同等級影響執行忠實度的各個因素； 3） 老師實行的RAMSR對K1幼童自我調節能力的即時／六個月後的影響。 針對提升幼童自我調節能力的教師網上培訓之效用，此計劃能夠填補與之相關的知識缺口。研究完成後，我們將對香港的幼稚園發佈相關網上教學套材，並提供政策改善建議，以達到維持和進一步加強相關培訓工作的成果。RAMSR能夠提升香港幼童的自我調節能力，並將有助於解決社經背景差異相關的問題及大大減低社會成本。

18610421.label: Project Title(Chinese)
18610421.value: 獨處卻快樂？獨處與幸福感關係的跨年齡差異

18610421.label: Co - Investigator(s)
18610421.value: Prof Chou, Kee Lee Prof Fung, Helene Hoi-lam

18610421.label: Project Objectives
18610421.value: (a) Humans are social animals. Because social activities are important to a wide range of outcomes, numerous studies have examined the antecedents and consequences of different types of social interaction. Remarkably, few studies have investigated situations in which individuals do not engage in social interaction, despite the fact that we spend a large percentage of our time (33% in younger adulthood vs. more than 50% in older adulthood) in solitude—defined as the absence of any social interaction—in everyday life (Jiang et al., 2019; Long et al., 2003). However, similar to affective experiences during social interactions, affective experiences in solitude are associated with a wide range of outcomes, from individual well-being to interpersonal relationships (Jiang et al., 2019). Because individuals in solitude are much less likely to seek and receive support than those who have social partners, they may be more vulnerable to emotional and behavioral disorders, and even suicide (Baruk, 1984). Therefore, understanding solitude situations and well-being in solitude are as important as understanding social interaction situations. The proposed studies aim to understand well-being in solitude. Facing the challenge of a globally aging populations, governments worldwide have implemented a variety of policies in elder health care to promote physical and psychological well-being in older adults. Taking Hong Kong as an example, HK$23.9 billion (approximately US$3 billion) was spent on services related to elderly health care in 2014–2015 and the number is estimated to triple by 2064–2065 (Legislative Council Secretariat, 2018). To help older adults maintain better well-being, enormous financial and manpower resources have been spent on encouraging older adults to participate in more social activities, such as volunteering and social gatherings. However, the beneficiaries of most intervention programs for promoting social activities are older adults who are already socially active. Because of age-normative changes, such as a reluctance to get to know potential social partners and physical constrain, some older adults may be more likely than younger individuals to stay alone (Pauly et al., 2017). Notably, it is equally important to protect the mental and physical health of older adults who are not as active in society. In addition, because of their increased vulnerability to COVID-19, older adults may need to be socially distant for long periods (Berg-Weger & Morley, 2020). Little is known about how governments can provide more appropriate services for older adults who choose or need to remain in solitude. Thus, the findings of the proposed project are expected to provide evidence-based policy guidance to promote well-being for a large portion of the aging population. Aging is perceived as a lonely process, at least in part because older adults spend more time in solitude. However, older adults report more positive and less negative affect than their younger counterparts in solitude (Jiang et al., under preparation; Lay, Fung, Jiang, et al., 2020). Understanding the mechanisms underlying age differences in well-being in solitude has significant implications on promoting well-being in solitude in older adulthood and across the lifespan. Inspired by the ECS project of the PI and results of two pilot studies, we aim to further clarify the mechanisms by arguing that older adults report better well-being in solitude because solitude facilitates the selective social and cognitive processing that is consistent with emotionally meaningful goals. At the theoretical level, the proposed studies will contribute to the literature on the psychology of aging by clarifying their underlying mechanisms on age differences in the relationship between solitude and well-being using experience sampling and experimental designs. At the practical level, the proposed project will provide evidence-based guidance for elderly care services by shedding light on the factors that may buffer against the negative consequences of solitude. These methods may be developed into informative interventions to promote well-being in older adulthood. At the methodological level, the manipulation methods used in the proposed study can be adopted by future empirical studies with a lifespan sample. (b) Objectives 5. To examine age-related differences in the association between solitude and well-being, and the moderating roles of reaffiliation motivation, positivity bias, mindfulness, and nostalgia in an experience-sampling study (Study 1). 2. To clarify the influence of older adults’ low reaffiliation motivation and positivity bias on age-related differences in well-being in solitude (Study 2)

18610421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18610421.value: 人們通常相信獨處（被定義為無社會交往的情境）會引發孤獨感降低幸福感。然而比起年輕人，老年人在獨處中體驗到更多積極情緒，更少消極情緒和更少孤獨感 (e.g., Jiang, Fung, & Lay, under preparation; Lay et al., 2018)。獨處與幸福感的跨年齡差異被解釋為老年人更優先有意義的情緒目標：因為老年人更為強調情緒意義目標，所以他們會更因為這些目標的激勵而調節情緒。然而，少有實證研究驗證這一解釋在獨處情景中是否適用。但是因為獨處情境中的積極或者消極情緒與很多重要結果相關，比如心裡健康等 (Chou et al., 2011, 2014; Jiang et al., 2019)。 現有研究大部分旨在研究如何降低獨處情境出現的頻率(e.g., Jiang… Chou., 2020a, 2020b)。雖然這些策略有效，他們無法直接解決如何提高人們在獨處中的幸福感這一關鍵問題。 在一項由傑出青年學者計劃 (ECS), 首席研究員已經檢驗了三種經典的在獨處情境中更容易實現的有意義的情緒目標是否能夠解釋獨處與幸福感關係的跨年齡差異。這些機制主要基於老年人在獨處中的幸福感更強主要是因為獨處的情景與這些情緒目標尤為相關。這些機制已經被相關數據支持。然而，情緒目標不止影響人們喜歡哪些情境，還影響人們在特定情境中的選擇性的社會和認知加工過程，比如動機、記憶、和想法(Sims et al., 2015)。在之前的工作中，研究團隊和其他人提出並且驗證了幾種收到情緒目標影響的社會和認知加工過程。更為重要的是，獨處而非社交情境會增進這些過程的發生。與年輕人相比，老年人表現出更低的親和動機 (Fung et al., 2008; Jiang et al., 2015)，更高的正念體驗(Prakash et al., 2017)，和更多的懷舊情緒(Hepper et al., 2020)。目前尚無關於研究獨處與幸福感關係的跨年齡差異是否因為這些過程的不同的相關文章發表。然而，我們的預實驗數據支持了相關想法。因此，在這個項目中，我們將要繼續研究獨處與幸福感關系的跨年齡差異及其相關機制。我們將使用經驗取樣法和實驗相結合。這些研究將1）推進關於老年人在何時及如何可以在獨處中保持幸福感的認知，2）提升對提高獨處中心理健康重要性的認知，3）提供研發介入的理論支持。

18611121.label: Project Title(Chinese)
18611121.value: 被物化對陰謀論信念的影響

18611121.label: Project Objectives
18611121.value: To examine whether objectification increases people’s conspiracy beliefs. To examine the psychological mechanism underlying the objectification-conspiracy link. To examine whether post-objectification increases in conspiracy beliefs motivate unethical behavior. To examine whether a situational intervention weakens the effects of objectification on conspiracy beliefs and unethical behavior.

To examine the psychological mechanism underlying the objectification-conspiracy link.
To examine whether post-objectification increases in conspiracy beliefs motivate unethical behavior.
To examine whether a situational intervention weakens the effects of objectification on conspiracy beliefs and unethical behavior.

18611121.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18611121.value: Objectification refers to a person being treated as an object for the instrumental gain of another person. Prior studies have built up knowledge about its impacts but have mainly been confined to sexual contexts, such as men treating women as objects to fulfill their sexual demands. Nonsexual objectification has seldom been investigated, although it commonly occurs in a wide variety of contexts, such as the workplace (e.g., discrediting a subordinate’s work to augment one’s own achievement), schools (e.g., befriending hard-working classmates to get a free ride), and close relationships (e.g., demanding a spouse to provide monetary resources). To fill this knowledge gap, this research tests whether nonsexual objectification increases conspiracy beliefs, reveals the underlying psychological mechanism and the behavioral consequences of the objectification-conspiracy link, and identifies ways to weaken the effect of objectification on conspiracy beliefs. Objectification occurs when people are treated as instrumental tools for achieving another person’s own purposes and are evaluated merely based on their usefulness to that person. Following objectification, people feel threatened because they are deprived of autonomy, needs, and opportunities. Consequently, objectified people may have a greater need for closure, which refers to a cognitive state wherein people have a greater desire to seek answers to questions and make sense of uncertainties. We propose that in such a state, objectified people may endorse conspiracy beliefs to comprehend the causes of threatening situations and identify possible dangers without exerting too much cognitive effort. Therefore, we predict that objectification increases conspiracy beliefs through the need for closure. We also examine whether post-objectification increases in conspiracy beliefs motivate people to behave unethically. Because conspiracy theorists often perceive others as possessing malevolent intentions, we predict that objectification increases unethical tendencies through conspiracy beliefs. When objectified people’s conspiracy beliefs are weakened through interventions, they may not behave unethically. Adopting a multi-method approach, this research tests the effect of objectification on conspiracy beliefs and its underlying psychological mechanism, demonstrates how post-objectification increases in conspiracy beliefs influence unethical behavior, and investigates methods to weaken the effects of objectification on conspiracy beliefs and unethical behavior. Objectification, conspiracy beliefs, and unethical behavior are ubiquitous in everyday life; hence, it is of significant impact to examine their relationships. A thorough understanding of the mechanism underlying the relationships between objectification, conspiracy beliefs, and unethical behavior can facilitate the development of theory-driven interventions to combat the negative consequences following objectification and form harmonious social interactions within our society. 被物化是指人被別人當作是可以利用來獲得利益的物件。以往的研究對於被物化的影響累積了一定的基礎知識，但主要側重於與性物化有關的範疇，例如男性把女性視為滿足其性需求的對象。與性無關的被物化則甚少被研究，儘管它經常出現於各種社交場合中，例如在工作上不認可下屬的功勞以增加自己的成就，在學校裏與勤奮的同學交朋友以便不勞而獲，以及在親密關係中要求伴侶提供金錢資源等。為填補文獻中的知識缺口，本研究旨在探討被別人物化會否提高人們的陰謀論信念，揭示這關係背後的心理機制，以及其導致的行為後果，並找出干預方案來減弱被物化對陰謀論信念的影響。由於被物化者往往被視為協助實現別人目標的工具，他們的存在價值只建基於他們對別人來說有用與否。當人們被物化後，他們的自主權、基本需求和機會被別人剝奪，因此他們會感受到威脅及變得脆弱。我們提出被物化會增加人們的結論需求，令人們有更大的動機去尋求問題的答案及處理環境中的不確定性。按照這個邏輯，本研究提出被物化或會提高人們的陰謀論信念。在被物化後，人們希望以較少的認知資源來辨識環境中的潛在危險和理解事件背後的原因。因此，被物化會增加人們的結論需求，從而增加陰謀論信念。本研究還會更進一步探討陰謀論信念會否促使被物化者做出不道德行為。由於相信陰謀論者經常會認為他人懷有惡意，被物化後所增加的陰謀論信念或會鼓勵人們進行不道德行為。當被物化後所產生的陰謀論信念被干預方案削弱時，被物化的人應該不會進行不道德行為。我們將採用多重研究方法，以探討被物化對陰謀論信念的影響，揭示兩者之間的心理機制，分析陰謀論信念如何使被物化者傾向做出不道德行為，並尋找干預方案以減弱被物化對陰謀論信念和不道德行為的影響。物化、陰謀論信念和不道德行為在日常生活中無處不在，剖析三者之間的關係具有重大的社會意義。 本研究亦能推動介入措施的發展，以幫助人們更有效地應對被物化所帶來的負面後果，有助建構社會和諧。

18611521.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18611521.value: 國際化在高等教育中越來越受歡迎。雙語課程在 第二語言被用作教學媒介的地區風靡已久。內容（即學科知識）和語言（即第二語言）整合學習就是其中一種雙語課程。內容和語言整合學習在各地中小學的研究及實踐成果豐碩，但在大學階段的相關研究卻有待發展。研究表明，以英語為教學媒介的護理學教育常因語言障礙效果欠佳。鑑於研究空白及在新冠肺炎後醫護教育的重要作用，我們迫切需要在護理學教育中進行內容和語言整合教學的研究。 因此，本研究將調查內容和語言整合學習對准護士內容知識和語言發展的影響，其中使用的內容和語言整合教學法將借鑒跨語言和跨符號的最新理論發展進行設計。本研究將採用準實驗設計，招募五名在香港以英語教學的護理學院教職員工及其教授的兩組准護士參加。其中，研究團隊將與護理學教職員設計兩個主題的課程，並使用跨語言和跨符號化啟迪下的內容和語言結合教學法作為教學幹預。第一研究階段將側重與護理學教職員分享內容和語言整合教學的原則。第二階段，在研究團隊的支持下，參與的教職員將實施兩個單元的教學干預。第一組准護士在第一個學習單元為實驗組，第二組准護士則為對照組。而在第二個學習單元中，對照組與實驗組互換。第三階段是評估階段。研究團隊將通過前後測、師生訪談及課堂互動記錄評估在該護理學課程中內容和語言整合教學的有效性。研究結果將促進雙語大學教育、護理學教育的教學效能，以及推進跨語言和跨符號的理論與實踐發展。

18612721.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18612721.value: 去人性化是對他人的人性的否認。其施行者的親社會行為較弱、反社會行為較強，以及對社會政策常有負面想法，而去人性化的受害者則常有心理及適應困擾，引致嚴重後果。研究指出去人性化呈現於不同文化內，受影響的對象包括少數族裔、性別群組及低社經地位群組，但有關共融環境內的特殊教育需要學生的研究，數量不多。本研究建基於去人性化的雙軌模式，以辨別人性特性及特質，並透過混合研究方法，探討不同持份者對特教學生去人性化的觀感、分析其對心理健康及適應的角色，及探討消減去人性化的有效策略。研究首階段，將會邀請特教學生及其同學、家長及教師填寫問卷，以了解特教學生有否及如何自我去人性化、與及有關的心理及學校適應。又邀請其他社會人士進行調查，以了解他們如何產生對特教學生的去人性化，及有關偏見與政策支援。第二階段的實驗設計，將透過培訓，以促進特教學生對人性化的觀感，並評估訓練成效。本研究的結果，將會顯示去人性化的普遍率及有關心理及適應問題，並期望能提供建議及解決方法，以消減對有特殊教育需要學生的自我去人性化及他人去人性化的影響。

18612721.label: Realisation of objectives
18612721.value: The team conducted two stages of data collection to fulfil the 5 proposed research objectives. In the first stage in 2022, more than 1,000 invitation letters at different stages were sent out to Hong Kong secondary schools for recruiting subjects with identifying SEN in schools. Upon requests, school visits for the briefing were also arranged. Finally, we recruited 125 SEN students, 274 parents, 141 teachers and 266 non-SEN peers in 11 mainstream secondary schools with the inclusive practices. For the later stages, the resources and materials for the experiment and intervention were designed and validated. It aimed at further understanding how to help reduce dehumanization towards SEN in the public. A group of parents of children with SEN (N=75) were interviewed and information was collected for the production of the intervention materials. Finally, video clips and reading materials were produced for the study 2. More than 1000 invitation letters and calls were sent to mainstreaming secondary schools in Hong Kong. However, only less than 10 schools indicated positive responses. After the school visits and briefing, we successfully recruited 99 SEN students and 82 non-SEN peers, as well as 316 non-SEN undergraduate students to evaluate the objectives 4 & 5. Objective 1: The results showed that non-SEN peers attributed significantly more mental capacity to others than students with SEN, demonstrated dehumanization towards them (p < .001, M=2.10) (above 2 indicates attributing less humanization to SEN peers); however, students with SEN did not demonstrate significant self-dehumanization (p < .001, M=1.88). The non-SEN peers attributed higher mental capacity to others than SEN peers (p < .001). This indicated a perception discrepancy between students with SEN and their peers. Regarding humanness, the results demonstrated that students with SEN attributed more humanness to themselves than their non-SEN peers attributed to SEN peers (p < .001), which is consistent with the results of mental capacity attribution. In addition, for both SEN peers and non-SEN peers, students attributed less human uniqueness to SEN peers compared to human nature. This is consistent with previous findings that human uniqueness was emphasized in the Chinese culture (Haslam & Loughnan, 2014). Objective 2: The results showed that parents of children with SEN did not attribute mental capacity to their children differently (p= .13). Parents of non-SEN children significantly attributed higher mental capacity to their own children compared to children with SEN (p <.001). This phenomenon indicated the existence of other-dehumanization from parents of Non-SEN peers, but the evidence of dehumanization from parents of children with SEN was absent. Regarding humanness, the results suggested that parents of children with SEN and those of children without SEN demonstrated a similar pattern, in which parents perceived children with SEN lack human uniqueness as compared to human nature (p < .001). This is consistent with the student sample as well as previous findings in the literature. Teachers in our sample attributed significantly higher mental capacity to non-SEN students than students with SEN (p < .001), indicating the teachers dehumanize students with SEN in terms of their mental capacity. They also attributed less human uniqueness to those students than human nature (p < .001), suggesting the teachers perceived students with SEN processed less human uniqueness than human nature. The results were also consistent with previous findings. Objective 3: A significant correlation between mental capacity and humanness measures (i.e., HU & HN) indicated the validity of the dehumanization of students with SEN. There was also a negative association (p < .01) between mental capacity and school functioning, indicated that for students with SEN, if they perceived others as having higher mental capacity than themselves, they tended to have poorer school functioning. Parents who attributed higher humanness (in either human nature or human uniqueness) tended to perceive less discrimination in daily life, as well as less social distance from society. Among the teachers, attributing higher mental capacity to students with SEN was associated with stronger public policy support (supporting government bills to help students with SEN); attributing more human uniqueness and human nature indicated less discriminative views of students with SEN. These preliminary findings demonstrated the consequences of dehumanization and promising directions for cognitive interventions to battle against dehumanizing perceptions. Objective 4: Manipulation checks were conducted across conditions (HU video vs. HN video vs. control; HU reading vs. HN reading vs. control) for the evaluation of HU and HN questionnaires of the public before the intervention, there was no significant difference between any of the conditions (ps > .05). After watching the video on demonstrating Human uniqueness in SEN student, undergraduate students rated SEN students having more HU than controls (p= .022). This indicates the effectiveness of using experiments to reducing other-dehumanization of SEN students. However, the reading materials on HU and HN did not show a significant effect on increasing humanization in undergraduate students; Moreover, there was no significant difference between the rating of HN in SEN students after watching the HN video. There was a marginally higher rating of HU in the HU video watching group than the control for SEN students, indicating that the video could effectively promote HU in SEN students. However, there were no significant differences between conditions for non-SEN peers. To sum up, the video of HU has an effect to promote HU in students instantly. Further studies could extend the length of the video for intervention purposes. Objective 5: The findings of this study demonstrated the high prevalence of dehumanization of SEN students among non-SEN peers, parents, teachers and the public. The experiment designed in the study shown a potential effect of reducing dehumanization through presentation of short-video materials that emphasize the human nature/uniqueness of SEN students. To be specific, the effectiveness of videos on human uniqueness (HU) was more profound. One of the reasons was specified in the results of stage 1: for both SEN peers and non-SEN peers, students attributed less human uniqueness to SEN peers compared to human nature. Therefore, the video provided information and knowledge on the human uniqueness of SEN students could have an immediate effect to reduce dehumanization among the non-SEN students. Since the design of short videos was to capture the trend in popular culture (e.g. Instagram videos), dissemination of videos of information emphasizing humanness of SEN students could be spread on Internet. For example, popular KOL (Key opinion leaders) could be invited to post relevant information on their platform which could increase the knowledge of the public towards SEN students. Other recommendations for minimizing dehumanization of SEN students could be through education programs or seminars in schools. Future intervention programs shall consider using the form of videos to maximize the effectiveness of the resource materials.

18612721.label: Major findings and research outcome
18612721.value: Based on the survey data, other-dehumanization towards SEN students is widely seen in people around them, such as their non-SEN peers, parents of non-SEN children, and teachers. However, self-dehumanization was not perceived by the SEN students themselves. It indicates a significant prevalence of other-dehumanization of SEN students in Hong Kong context. Moreover, when investigating the humanness in SEN students as perceived by others, lack of human uniqueness was demonstrated consistently across groups (i.e. non-SEN peers, parents of non-SEN children and teachers). Results showed that compared to human nature characteristic, SEN students were perceived as lack of human uniqueness by their surroundings. This may be due to the lack of understanding and connection between the SEN students and their surroundings. For SEN students, they tended to have poorer school functioning in general but higher life satisfaction than their non-SEN peers. In particular, students who self-attributed more human nature and human uniqueness tended to have better school functioning. However, SEN students who have discriminative life experience has a higher tendency for self-dehumanization. Parents of SEN children tended to perceive less discrimination in daily life and less social distance from the society if they attributed higher humanness towards SEN students. However, for parents of non-SEN children, there was no correlation between dehumanization and humanness attribution. Among the teachers, attributing higher mental capacity to students with SEN was associated with stronger public policy support (supporting government bills to help students with SEN); attributing more human uniqueness and human nature indicated less discriminative views of students with SEN. These findings demonstrated the consequences of dehumanization and promising directions for cognitive interventions to battle against dehumanizing perceptions. By comparing the effectiveness of intervention of presenting videos or reading paragraphs on humanness of SEN students, the short videos are effective in promoting humanness, particularly human uniqueness, of SEN students in undergraduate students (representing the public). Moreover, with an increased humanness perception in SEN students, undergraduate students also attributed more mental capacity to SEN students and demonstrated less negative discrimination towards SEN students. The findings would implicate suggestions/expectation for further studies on intervention of dehumanization towards SEN students that the form of presenting information matters as well as human uniqueness is what the intervention should be focused on. The outcome leads to two manuscripts in refereed journals (BMC Psychology and Hong Kong Special Education Journal. The findings and implications have been presented in different international and local conferences.

18612721.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
18612721.value: Based on the findings of the current study, dehumanization towards students with SEN is prevalent, which significantly impacts their educational experience and social integration. Additional research should be conducted in diverse educational settings to explore the mechanisms underlying dehumanization towards individuals with SEN. Another significant finding from the research is that other-dehumanization can be alleviated through short video presentations, which indicates an immediate positive effect of targeted intervention. Based on the video clips developed in this study, further studies are needed in assessing the potential to reduce dehumanization. Furthermore, additional educational materials aimed at promoting the recognition of humanness in individuals with SEN are needed. These resources could be designed for use in both educational and clinical settings, fostering empathy and understanding among peers and educators alike. For the teacher training in inclusion, teachers will be informed of the research findings and trained of using the ready-made video resources for supporting the diverse learners in schools. In the ISNIE, training courses will be organized on the topic for the teachers and parents in the coming years. For research advancement, partners in Special Education Department of UAE university, Brunei University and Radboud University indicate the interests for a cross-culture study.

18612721.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
18612721.value: This study examined the prevalence of dehumanization towards SEN students in Hong Kong context as well as explored the potential intervention strategy to alleviate dehumanization. Questionnaire were collected in Stage 1 from 118 SEN students (aged from 13 to above 18), 274 parents, 141 teachers, and 220 non-SEN peers. The findings reveal that many students and teachers tend to see SEN students as lacking human uniqueness, which can lead to dehumanization. This is significant because it highlights a serious issue in how young people perceive and interact with their classmates who have different needs. In Stage 2, short video clips and reading materials introducing the humanness in SEN students were designed and presented to non-SEN and SEN students. It was evident that showing short videos with emphasis on the human uniqueness of SEN students can quickly reduce the negative perceptions towards them from the non-SEN students. This suggests that simple but effective intervention can make a difference. This study highlights the importance of studying dehumanization. It sheds lights on the intervention strategies in reducing dehumanization and its negative impact in inclusive settings. Regarding to the findings and intervention strategies, workshop training becomes more substantial and comprehensive to teachers and parents.

21100521.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21100521.value: Protein translation is one of the most essential biological processes in cells, and is executed by ribosomes. Ribosomes are composed of numerous RNAs (i.e., ribosomal RNAs or rRNAs) and protein that form large complexes to perform protein synthesis. rRNA accounts for the majority of RNA molecules in any given cell; this is largely due to the unusually high numbers of copies of genes encoding rRNA (i.e., rDNAs) which are arranged in tandem arrays in genomes. The highly repetitive nature of rDNA and its tandem arrangement has prevented the precise determination of rDNA and its surrounding sequences. The major hindrances to resolving rDNA and its flanking sequences lie in the technologies that are currently used to generate genomic sequences. For example, next-generation sequencing (NGS) has played a dominant role over the past decade in producing the draft genomes of various species. However, although NGS works relatively well for small genomes with low sequence complexity, most eukaryotes have relatively large genomes with numerous repetitive sequences, some of which are arranged in tandem arrays (e.g., rDNA) and thus cannot be correlated to their respective chromosomes using NGS alone. This inability to precisely locate rDNA location and its sequence variants significantly inhibits the functional characterisation of rDNA and its regulatory mechanisms. We have developed a pipeline to accommodate variation calling and assembly of tandem repeat regions using nanopore long reads. Using this pipeline, we have reconstructed almost the entire rDNA cluster of the C. elegans genome. We have located the variable region by using several transgenic strains to provide ‘anchor’ sequences for the tandem arrays of rDNA clusters. Comparative analysis of C. elegans wild isolates has revealed a novel 5S rDNA unit, characterised by 30-bp deletions from the ‘reference’ unit, that is related to copy number variations in 5S rDNA. These findings will enable the study of the rDNA replication mechanism in C. elegans. We hypothesise that the sequence variations in the rDNA cluster reveal replication origins and pause sites of different efficiencies, thus linking them to rDNA replication. This hypothesis will be tested by capturing nascent intermediates of rDNA replication using nanopore sequencing of both wild isolates and transgenic strains containing different rDNA units. The proposed research will provide insights into the structure and function of rDNA clusters in eukaryotic species. The methods built to assemble the rDNA clusters will also be used to study rDNA repeats in other species. 由核糖體執行的蛋白質翻譯是細胞中最重要的生物過程之一。核糖體由許多 RNA （即核糖體RNA 或 rRNA）和蛋白質形成大復合物以進行蛋白質合成。rRNA是細胞内RNA的主要成分，其高表達依賴於與其在基因組上的高拷貝數。這些編碼rRNA的基因（核糖體DNA，rDNA）集中在基因組的特定部分，以串聯重複序列的形式進行排列，其最小單元幾乎是完全相同的。這種複雜的串聯重複序列形式阻止了人們瞭解基因組上rDNA區域的實際組成和功能。 解決 rDNA及其側翼序列的主要障礙在於目前用於基因組測序的技術。二代測序（NGS） 在過去十年中在生成各種物種的基因組草圖方面發揮了主導作用。然而，雖然NGS對序列複雜性較低的小基因組效果相對較好，但大多數真核生物的基因組規模相對較大，具有許多重複序列，其中一些被排列在串聯重複（例如rDNA）中的序列無法被組裝到染色體中。無法精確定位rDNA的位置，加上無法得到其序列組成，妨礙了我們研究rDNA的功能及其調控機制。 我們開發了使用Nanopore長讀段解決串聯重複序列組成及組裝的分析流程。通過該流程，我們得以重建C. elegans基因組中全長的rDNA串聯重複序列。另外，我們以轉基因插入序列為 錨，定位了C. elegans基因組中rDNA的可變區域及保守區域。我們發現了一個新的5S rDNA 最小單元，其序列相對公認的5S單元，存在一個30 bp的序列缺失。這個新單元的存在與否和不同C. elegan品系中5S 拷貝變異存在相關。這些發現將有助於C. elegans的rDNA複製機制研究。我們提出一個假説， rDNA 最小單位的序列變異可能提示了不同效率的複製起始和結束位點，從而影響了rDNA的最終拷貝數。爲了驗證該假説，我們會嘗試在帶有不同rDNA最小單元的C. elegans品系中，使用Nanopore測序捕獲 rDNA 複製的中間體。中間體的解構直觀的反映rDNA序列變異與其複製之間的關係。 本研究將會為真核物種中rDNA串聯重複序列的結構和功能的關係提供新的解釋。本研究提出並改進的rDNA序列組裝方法也可以用於其他複雜基因組物種中串聯重複序列的組裝。

21100521.label: Realisation of objectives
21100521.value: Objective 1: Determine the structure of rDNA clusters in different species. This objective has been achieved by establishing a robust nanopore long‑read sequencing and bioinformatics workflow to resolve highly repetitive rDNA arrays that are typically difficult to assemble with short‑read sequencing. We generated long-read datasets and performed repeat-aware analyses to delineate the architecture, unit composition, and copy-number/ordering variation of rDNA clusters in Caenorhabditis species and strains, with a particular focus on the 5S rDNA cluster as a tractable entry point and a foundation for subsequent mechanistic work. Key accomplishments include: 1.High-resolution characterization and assembly of 5S rDNA clusters. We profiled the 5S rDNA cluster structure and variation in C. elegans and C. briggsae by classifying individual repeat units based on diagnostic sequence variants and leveraging long reads that span many consecutive repeats. This enabled reconstruction of long contiguous segments of rDNA arrays and systematic comparison across strains/species. These findings were reported in the peer‑reviewed publication on the genomic architecture and variation of the 5S rDNA cluster (Ding et al., 2022). 2.Experimental validation and gap‑closing support through dedicated primer design. We developed primerdiffer, a command‑line module tailored for large‑scale primer design in haplotype genotyping, to validate unit presence/organization and support long‑range PCR strategies relevant to repetitive regions (Ren et al., 2023). 3.Platform adaptation to ensure data quality across changing nanopore chemistries. During the project period, ONT sequencing chemistry and basecalling models evolved rapidly (e.g., R9 → R10). We conducted systematic benchmarking of flow cells and sequencing strategies to maintain continuity and reliability of variant and modification calling, which directly supported the rDNA analyses and downstream mechanistic assays (Ni et al., 2023). 4.After the changing to R10, we revisited the quality of 5S and 18S rDNA clusters in our previous study. And we are able to exclude some minor 5S subtypes with the highly accurate R10 platform. The issues in nanopore sequencing, including the homopolymer issue (Li et al., 2025), can be fixed by applying an additional polishing step. Collectively, the project delivered both biological results (resolved rDNA architecture/variation across species/strains) and generalizable enabling tools (repeat‑aware validation and nanopore benchmarking) that make the determination of rDNA structure feasible and reproducible in other complex genomes. Objective 2: Determine the replication mechanism of rDNA clusters in Caenorhabditis elegans. This objective has been achieved by completing the development and application of a BrdU‑based nascent DNA labeling and direct nanopore signal detection workflow to capture rDNA replication intermediates and reconstruct replication behavior within rDNA arrays in C. elegans. Building on the structural baseline established under Objective 1, we: 1.Completed BrdU detection on nanopore raw signals and established a robust end‑to‑end analysis pipeline. The BrdU detection method was developed on top of nanoCEM (Tan et al., 2024; Guo et al., 2024, NARGAB), leveraging signal-level “current event” features to detect BrdU incorporation directly from nanopore reads. The BrdU workflow includes model calibration/validation, signal‑level feature extraction, and mapping of BrdU‑enriched segments back onto rDNA repeat frameworks. 2.Applied the BrdU/nanoCEM workflow to rDNA clusters to elucidate replication mechanism. Using appropriately designed C. elegans samples/strains with rDNA marker, we obtained single‑molecule–level evidence of nascent DNA incorporation patterns within rDNA arrays, allowing us to infer replication dynamics (initiation/elongation behavior and replication intermediates) within rDNA clusters. We discovered that only two types of 5S rDNA units are dynamic, and the replication-initiating copy in the 18S rDNA cluster has been defined. We have prepared a manuscript describing the replication mechanism study. While the manuscript is still pending for resubmission, the experimental and analytical work has been completed and constitutes a major research outcome directly aligned with Objective 2. The nanoCEM-based BrdU pipeline and the resulting replication maps provide the mechanistic framework requested in the original objective.

21100521.label: Major findings and research outcome
21100521.value: This project resolved key “genomic dark matter” questions surrounding ribosomal DNA (rDNA) in Caenorhabditis by combining ultra‑long Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT) sequencing with repeat‑aware computational analysis. First, we determined the architecture and variation of rDNA clusters across species/strains, focusing on the 5S rDNA cluster as a high-copy tandem repeat whose organization is both biologically important and technically challenging. By classifying individual repeat units using diagnostic sequence variants and leveraging long reads spanning many repeats, we reconstructed long, ordered segments of rDNA arrays and compared rDNA organization between C. elegans and C. briggsae and among C. elegans strains. These results established a concrete structural baseline for rDNA organization and evolution. Second, to support validation and scalable analyses in highly similar repeat contexts, we developed primerdiffer, a dedicated primer‑design workflow for haplotype genotyping, which was used within the project for rDNA unit validation and long‑range PCR design in repetitive regions Third, the project addressed an important practical barrier: the rapid evolution of ONT chemistry and basecalling. We benchmarked ONT R9.4.1 versus R10.4/R10.4.1 for genetic and epigenetic variation calling, providing best‑practice guidance that improved the reliability of downstream rDNA and signal-level analyses. Finally, we completed the rDNA replication mechanism study in C. elegans by developing a BrdU detection workflow built on nanoCEM and applying it to map nascent DNA incorporation and replication intermediates within rDNA clusters at the single‑molecule level. The replication manuscript is pending, but the method and results constitute a core, completed outcome directly arising from this project. Together, these outcomes deliver: (i) resolved rDNA cluster architectures across species, (ii) validated computational/experimental toolchains, and (iii) a completed mechanistic framework for rDNA replication in C. elegans.

21100521.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21100521.value: The immediate next step is to finalize and publish the pending manuscript on BrdU-based rDNA replication mapping, including full benchmarking, documentation, and public release of the nanoCEM‑based BrdU detection workflow to facilitate adoption by the community. In parallel, we will extend the same replication mapping framework from the 5S rDNA cluster to the larger 18S rDNA arrays, and apply the strategy comparatively across additional Caenorhabditis species/strains to test how replication dynamics relate to rDNA structural variation. Methodologically, the nanoCEM/signal-level pipeline can be expanded to support additional analogues or replication-associated signatures and integrated with targeted long-read enrichment strategies (e.g., adaptive sampling) to increase effective coverage in highly repetitive rDNA regions. These directions will consolidate rDNA structure-to-mechanism links and generalize the approach to other difficult tandem repeats in complex genomes.

21100521.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21100521.value: Ribosomes are the cell’s protein-making machines, and the DNA that encodes ribosomal RNA (rDNA) is present in long, near-identical repeats. These repeats are essential for life, but they are notoriously difficult to assemble with standard DNA sequencing because short reads cannot reliably span long repetitive blocks. In this project we used nanopore long-read sequencing, which can read very long DNA molecules and can also preserve information in the raw electrical signals, to “see through” these repeats and map how rDNA copies are arranged in the genome of the nematode worm Caenorhabditis elegans and related species. We developed analysis workflows that use small sequence differences between repeat copies as fingerprints, allowing us to reconstruct large portions of the 5S rDNA repeat array and compare repeat organization across strains and species. Our results show that rDNA repeat structure and stability can differ substantially between laboratory and wild genetic backgrounds, providing a new foundation for studying genome stability and evolution. The project also produced open, reusable software tools for primer design and for interpreting nanopore signals, which will help other researchers validate repeat structures and study DNA/RNA modifications using long-read sequencing.

21104221.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21104221.value: Donkeys are a crucial species for both production and draft work globally, with an estimated 50.4 million animals worldwide. Lameness is a significant problem for these animals, with prevalence rates of up to 100% in some populations. This results in poor welfare and reduced productivity for animals used for the production of meat and dairy and for animals used for draft and pack uses in poor communities. Lameness in donkeys is frequently associated with hoof problems. Preliminary data suggests that longer toes may be protective for lameness in the donkey, which is markedly different to current knowledge of their nearest relative, the horse. This suggests a fundamental difference between the species in terms of hoof morphometry and lameness, likely anatomical or biomechanical. However, the biomechanical principle for this is not understood as the donkey is a significantly under studied species. The interaction between hoof and surface is of critical importance to ungulates, as adaptations for efficient locomotion has resulted in a lack of dynamic adaptation to the external environment during locomotion. Part one of this study will compare hoof contact and kinetic parameters between the donkey and the horse to provide an insight into normal locomotion in this under-studied species. This will be achieved by using body-mounted inertial measurement units to quantify speed and gait symmetry (i.e., freedom from lameness). High-speed motion capture and high-fidelity pressure mats and measure hoof contact and hoof pressure alongside stride parameters. Comparisons will be made between ten horses and ten donkeys, as horses are a well-established research animal and biomechanical knowledge of this species is advanced. Part two will compare hoof contact and kinematic parameters between donkeys with normal hoof conformation and donkeys with abnormal hooves in order to establish which hoof morphologies are the most significant and require interventions for correction. This will allow targeted health interventions, resulting in increased production, improved welfare and improved outcomes for stakeholders such as donkey farmers and those reliant upon donkeys for traction and draft work. 驢是全球生產和起草工作的重要物種，全世界估計有 50.40 萬隻動物。跛行是這些動物的一個重大問題，在某些種群中患病率高達 100%。這導致用於生產肉類和奶製品的驢，以及用於在貧困社區運輸的動物的福利下降和生產力降低。跛行常常與驢蹄問題有關 。初步數據表明，擁有較長的腳趾可能對驢的跛足有保護作用，這與其近親馬的現有知識明顯不同。這表明物種之間在蹄形態測量和跛行方面存在根本差異，很可能是解剖學或生物力學。然而，這方面的生物力學原理尚不清楚，因為驢是一種研究不足的物種。蹄和地面之間的相互作用對有蹄類動物至關重要，因為對有效運動的適應導致在運動過程中缺乏對外部環境的動態適應。本研究的第一部分將比較驢和馬之間的蹄接觸和動力學參數，以深入了解這一研究不足的物種的正常運動。這將通過使用安裝在身體上的測量單元來量化速度和步態對稱性（例如，免於跛行）來實現。高速動作捕捉和高保真壓力墊，測量蹄接觸和蹄壓力以及步幅參數。本研究將對十匹馬和十匹驢之間進行比較，因為馬是一種成熟的研究物種，並且對該物種的生物力學知識很先進。第二部分將比較具有正常構象的驢蹄和具有異常的驢蹄之間的蹄接觸和運動學參數，以確定哪些蹄形態最重要及需要進行干預。這將允許有針對性的健康干預，從而增加產量、改善福利及利益相關者的結果，例如養驢和依賴驢進行牽引和運輸的人。

21200921.label: Project Objectives
21200921.value: Establish a novel microfluidic inflammatory tumor model for in vitro study of toxicity or synergy effects in the discovery of antimicrobial combinatorial treatment. The microfluidic inflammatory tumor model will combine the advantages of microfluidics and integrated in vitro systems for point-of-care drug testing and discovery. The parameters of the inflammatory tumor model to be optimised include the type of bacteria and the site of infection. Dimensions of the microstructures will be relevant to micrometastasis formed in vivo. Conditions optimal for tumor growth will be incorporated by the integration of components previously optimised with our patient-derived models, which had been shown to predict the overall outcome and survival of cancer patients. The inflammatory tumor model will capitalise on the versatility of microfluidics to integrate tumor conditions such as oxygen gradients and co-culture with tumor-associated immune cells within a single biomedical device. The integration of components serves to promote the generation of bacteria-tumor clusters for the rapid and high throughput evaluation of treatment strategies. Such advancements will have a significant impact on the pharmaceutical and clinical biomedical industries. The proposed microfluidic inflammatory tumor model will comprise specially designed tapered microwell arrays with dimensions suitable for the consistent formation of micrometastasis (Figure 6) (1-6 months). Validate clinical relevance of the proposed inflammatory tumor model for monitoring drug response within the microfluidic device, and characterize the responses of cancer and bacteria cells during the drug screening process. The multi-component inflammatory tumor model will first be generated using human-derived tumor-associated immune cells (U937) and bladder cancer cell lines (UMUC3). Proportions of immune cells to bladder cancer cells will be comparable to tumors in patients with stage III or IV bladder cancer. The ratio of immune cells to cancer cells in a tumor usually increases with cancer staging. The viability of the co-cultures will be determined by live/dead staining assays. Co-cultures will be maintained under hypoxic conditions to resemble the tumor microenvironment. The uniformity of cell distribution, cluster size, and density will be determined. We expect a high degree of uniformity using tapered microwell array, which has previously been shown to generate consistent cell clusters from liquid biopsy samples from patients. After 24 hours, the bacteria will be introduced into the established co-culture cell clusters at different infection rates. We aim to validate the model with Gram-negative bacteria, which constitute the majority of systemic infections in cancer patients and is a key factor in high mortality. Drugs will be introduced after another 24 h. We will first validate the inflammatory tumor model based on the quantification of half-maximal inhibitory concentration (IC50), using anticancer drugs with definite toxicity values (Figure 7) (6-18 months). Examine the important factors (e.g., the period of drug exposure and spatial heterogeneity of bacteria distribution) involved in the inflammatory tumor model for drug screening. As a proof of concept, established anti-cancer drugs such as doxorubicin will be used to examine these factors. Different exposure periods of the drugs will be evaluated. The impact of spatial heterogeneity of bacteria distribution (intratumor or outside of the tumor) in the inflammatory tumor model will be evaluated. Different types of Gram-negative bacteria (intracellular and extracellular modes of infection) will be evaluated to demonstrate the wide applicability of the model for drug discovery (Appendix, Figure 2) (18-24 months). Investigate the impact of antimicrobial combinatorial treatment within the inflammatory tumor model, and automate the operation procedures with computer-controlled programming for clinical and biomedical industries. As a proof of concept, established anti-microbial agents such as gentamycin will be used in combination with doxorubicin. The toxicity or synergy of this combination therapy will be evaluated by the characterization of tumor morphology, cancer cell viability, colony-forming unit and IC50 value. Our team members have expertise in computer control programming to automate operating procedures. Automation includes colorimetric analysis of the fluorescence output of cancer cell characterization after exposure to drugs. The aim of this objective is to enable ease of operation, robust performance, and direct readouts of the assay to supplement routine use in clinical and biomedical industry environments. Overall, we expect that this research can identify a novel means to evaluate anti-microbial combinatorial treatment in a clinically relevant bacteria-tumor model. Cell lines can be replaced with patient-derived samples (out of the scope of this proposal) to allow evaluation of cancer patients with systemic infections and help narrow the scope of drug targets that can be used in clinical trials. This work may also provide further important insights for our comprehensive understanding of bacteria-tumor interactions and for novel drug discovery in pharmaceutical industries (Figure 8)(24-36 months).

21200921.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21200921.value: In cancer patients, systemic bacterial infections are serious complications during chemotherapy, affecting patients' prognosis and survival. Clinical studies have demonstrated a correlation between bacterial infection and tumour progression. However, due to the inherent heterogeneity and complexity of bacterial infections, both cancer-promoting and anticancer effects have been reported in the presence of bacteria-mediated inflammation. A well-defined model is needed to perform quantitative and dynamic analyses of bacteria–tumour interactions to accurately assess tumour response under bacteria-mediated inflammation. Due to its rapid processing rate, small size and multiplex assay capabilities applicable even to patient blood samples, microfluidics technology is important for advancing point-of-care testing. In vitro drug screening platforms can be beneficial for personalised medicine because they integrate the microenvironmental cues that mimic the tumour microenvironment. In previous studies, we demonstrated the use of integrated microfluidic platforms to establish patient-derived tumour models and develop downstream drug screening applications. However, it is extremely technically challenging to evaluate the effects of tumour-related microbiomes on drug efficacy, which limits the efficacy of conventional treatment methods in the presence of systemic infections. Therefore, it is necessary to develop new combinatorial treatments that use antibacterial agents to improve prognoses and outcomes. In the proposed project, we will develop a microfluidic inflammatory tumour model by combining the advantages of microfluidics and integrated in vitro systems to realise point-of-care drug testing and discovery. The parameters of the inflammatory tumour model will be defined by considering the types of bacteria and the sites of infection. The dimensions of the microstructures should be relevant to the micrometastasis formed in vivo. Moreover, the conditions optimal for tumour growth will be incorporated alongside the integrated components previously optimised using our patient-derived models. Systematic studies will be conducted to obtain quantitative outputs that provide insights into how bacterial distribution in tumour tissues affects cancer cell phenotypes and tumour progression. Although cellular drug concentrations in vivo are influenced by clinical pharmacokinetics, in vitro tools remain pivotal for predicting tumour response to new combinatorial treatments that focus on toxicity or synergy by assessing the half-maximal inhibitory concentration (IC50). The microfluidic bacteria–tumour platform will be automated through computer-controlled programming to realise the continuous monitoring of tumour dynamics under the influence of bacterial infection. In sum, the proposed novel microfluidic inflammatory tumour model will provide a unique means to evaluate the combination of anticancer and antimicrobial drugs, thereby advancing automated medical technology for point-of-care testing. 在癌症患者中，全身細菌感染是化療過程中的嚴重並發症，影響患者的預後和生存。臨床研究證明，細菌感染與腫瘤進展之間存在相關性。然而，由於細菌感染固有的異質性和復雜性，在細菌介導的炎症存在的情況下，已經報導了促癌和抗癌作用。細菌-腫瘤相互作用的定量和動態分析需要一個定義明確的模型，以便準確評估細菌介導的炎症下的腫瘤反應。在之前的研究中，我們展示了使用集成微流體平台來構建源自患者的腫瘤模型並開發下游藥物篩選應用程序。然而，評估腫瘤相關微生物組對藥物療效的影響在技術上極具挑戰性，這限制了傳統治療方法在全身感染存在的情況下的療效。因此，有必要開發新的聯合療法並使用抗菌藥物來改善預後和結果。在擬議的項目中，我們將結合微流控技術和體外集成系統的優勢，開發微流控炎症腫瘤模型，實現即時藥物測試和發現。將進行系統研究以獲得定量結果，以深入了解腫瘤組織中細菌的分佈如何影響癌細胞表型和腫瘤進展。儘管體內細胞藥物濃度受臨床藥代動力學影響，但體外工具仍然是通過評估半數最大抑制濃度 (IC50) 來預測腫瘤對側重於毒性或協同作用的新聯合療法的反應的關鍵。總之，所提出的新微流體炎症腫瘤模型將為評估抗癌和抗菌藥物的組合提供一種獨特的方法，從而推進自動化醫療技術的即時檢測。

Systematic study on optical and electrical properties of alloyed PtxPd1-xSe2 2D semiconductors. 21201821.label: Realisation of objectives
21201821.value: Realisation of objectives This project has successfully achieved and, in several aspects, exceeded its primary objectives. The planned research on alloyed two-dimensional (2D) materials for high-performance long-wave infrared (LWIR) photodetectors was systematically executed, leading to significant scientific outputs and technological demonstrations. The realisation of each key objective is detailed below: Objective 1-3: Synthesis and Basic Characterization of Alloyed 2D Materials for LWIR Detection Planned Action: Synthesize narrow-bandgap alloyed 2D crystals and investigate their fundamental properties. Achievement and Degree: Fully Achieved. Details of Realisation: Synthesis: We successfully synthesized two target alloy systems, Pt0.86Pd0.14Se2 and PtS2xSe2(1-x), via the chemical vapor transport (CVT) method. Ultrathin nanoflakes were reliably obtained via mechanical exfoliation for device fabrication. Characterization: The fundamental electrical and optical properties were thoroughly investigated. Temperature-dependent electrical measurements confirmed the n-type semiconducting nature of Pt0.86Pd0.14Se2 and extracted its small bandgap of ~20 meV. Photoresponse measurements demonstrated that Pt0.86Pd0.14Se2 devices are sensitive up to 12 µm, firmly establishing their potential for LWIR photodetection Similarly, PtS2xSe2(1-x) devices exhibited n-type behavior and a clear photoresponse at the communication wavelength of 1550 nm. 2. Objective 4-5: Performance Enhancement through Nano-Optics Planned Action: Design and fabricate optical cavity substrates and nano-antennas to enhance photodetector performance. Achievement and Degree: Partially Achieved / Work in Progress. Details of Realisation and Path Forward: Design and Simulation: The objective was fully met in the design and simulation phase. We successfully designed optical cavity substrates (Au/Al2O3) and performed simulations to optimize the Al2O3 thickness for maximizing IR light absorption in both Pt0.86Pd0.14Se2 and PtS2xSe2(1-x) nanoflakes. Furthermore, specific optical nano-antenna geometries were designed and simulated, showing a significant enhancement in localized light intensity. Reason for Partial Achievement: The full integration and experimental testing of these nano-optical structures with the 2D materials are planned for immediate future work. The delay was primarily due to the time-intensive nature of the nano-fabrication processes and the parallel, highly successful exploration of other material systems (e.g., SexTe1-x). We have overcome this by completing all critical design and simulation steps, providing a clear and optimized pathway for fabrication. 3. New Objective 1: Design and fabrication of novel alloyed systems and device applications based on 2D SexTe1-x Planned Action: Explore new material systems and their integration into functional electronic devices. Achievement and Degree: Exceeded. Details of Realisation: New Material Synthesis: We developed a novel precursor-confined Chemical Vapor Deposition (CVD) method to grow single-crystalline SexTe1-x alloy nanosheets, a system not initially detailed in the original objectives. Functional Devices: This led to a significant expansion of the project's scope and impact. We systematically characterized the electrical performance of SexTe1-x -based Field-Effect Transistors (FETs), identifying an optimal composition at Se ~30% that offers a superior trade-off between on/off ratio and hole mobility. CMOS Circuit Demonstration: Crucially, the p-type behavior of Se0.3Te0.7 effectively mitigated the high dark current issue associated with pure tellurium's small bandgap. We leveraged this to demonstrate a fully functional 2D complementary inverter by integrating p-type Se0.3Te0.7 with n-type MoS2, achieving a high voltage gain of ~30. This work was published in ACS Nano (ACS Nano 2024, 18, 17293-17303). 4. New Objective 2: Development of 2D materials based advanced optoelectronic devices for intelligent computing Planned Action: Leverage 2D materials for advanced computing concepts like in-sensor and neuromorphic computing. Achievement and Degree: Exceeded. Details of Realisation: The project successfully fabricated multiple reconfigurable and programmable optoelectronic memory devices, demonstrating functionalities beyond initial expectations. A tellurium-based memory device was used to implement an in-sensor reservoir computing system at 1550 nm, showcasing the potential for edge signal processing. This work has been published in Advanced Materials (Adv. Mater. 2023, 35, 2211598). We developed a simplified reconfigurable memory device (RMD) based on a MoS2/CuInP2S6 heterostructure. Through defect engineering, this device achieved all-in-one sensing, memory, and computing for applications like medical image diagnosis and gesture recognition This work has also been published in Advanced Materials (Adv. Mater. 2024, 36, 2403785). Using selenium-based heterostructures, we created a programmable optoelectronic sensor that enables in-sensor data compression and convolution operations, significantly advancing intelligent machine vision at the edge. This work has published in Nature Communications (Nat. Commun. 2025,16, 3836). 5. Dissemination and Community Contribution Planned Action: Publish findings and train researchers. Achievement and Degree: Fully Achieved and Exceeded. Details of Realisation: Publications: The project has resulted in numerous high-impact publications in prestigious international journals, including Nature Communications, Advanced Materials, ACS Nano, Advanced Functional Materials and Applied Physics Letters. Review Articles: We provided two comprehensive review articles that serve as foundational references for the community: one on IR photodetectors based on 2D materials and nano-photonics (Adv. Funct. Mater. 2022, 32, 2111970), and another on the electronics and optoelectronics of 2D Tellurium (Adv. Mater. 2024, 36, 2408969). Research Training: The project successfully supported the graduation of three PhD students, fulfilling the human resource development objective. Summary In conclusion, all primary technical and scientific objectives of the project have been successfully realised. The synthesis, characterization, and device demonstration using alloyed 2D materials for IR detection were fully accomplished. The objective on nano-optics is well-advanced through completed designs and simulations, with fabrication imminent. The project's outcomes were significantly enhanced through the development of novel material systems (SexTe1-x) and the demonstration of groundbreaking device concepts in neuromorphic and in-sensor computing, which have led to an exceptional record of publications and human capital development.

21201821.label: Major findings and research outcome
21201821.value: This research program has driven significant progress in the synthesis of two-dimensional (2D) materials and their integration into next-generation electronics and optoelectronics. Our key achievements are outlined below. First, we developed novel alloyed 2D crystals, including Pt0.86Pd0.14Se2 and composition-tunable PtS2xSe2(1-x), which exhibit exceptional performance in long-wave infrared photodetection. By designing nano-optical structures to enhance light–matter interactions, we realized highly sensitive photodetectors, establishing a robust materials platform for advanced infrared sensing. We also achieved controlled synthesis of single-crystalline SexTe1-x nanosheets using a precursor-confined chemical vapor deposition (CVD) approach. These alloyed nanosheets were engineered into high-performance p-type transistors with tunable bandgaps and electrical characteristics. Furthermore, we successfully fabricated complementary inverters by integrating these p-type devices with n-type semiconductors, a key milestone toward practical all-2D electronics. This work was published in the high-impact journal ACS Nano. Second, we pioneered reconfigurable optoelectronic memory devices based on 2D materials for in-sensor computing. We demonstrated an electronic/optoelectronic memory operating at telecommunications wavelengths, capable of long-term potentiation and depression via voltage pulses, as well as short-term potentiation via 1550 nm laser pulses, thereby enabling in-sensor reservoir computing. These results were published in Advanced Materials. Through defect engineering, we further developed a multifunctional device that functions not only as a non-volatile electronic memory but can also be reconfigured into optoelectronic memory or synaptic modes by controlling ferroelectric polarization in CuInP2S6. This structurally simple device was successfully applied to complex neuromorphic computing tasks, and the work was published in Advanced Materials. More recently, by incorporating photoinduced memory behavior within a 2D memory cell, we demonstrated a programmable sensor for in-sensor data compression. The device operates in sensor mode with only optical stimulus and in memory mode under electro-optical co-stimulus, supporting the development of efficient intelligent vision systems at the edge. This work appears in Nature Communications. Finally, we consolidated our expertise alongside broader field advancements through comprehensive review articles on infrared photodetectors and 2D tellurium-based electronics and optoelectronics, published in Advanced Functional Materials, Advanced Materials, and Applied Physics Letters. Collectively, this body of work, disseminated in high-impact journals including Nature Communications, Advanced Materials, Advanced Functional Materials, and ACS Nano, provides a comprehensive framework for material innovation, device design, and system-level application of 2D materials.

21201821.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21201821.value: This project possesses significant potential for further development, primarily in two key directions. First, the research on long-wave infrared photodetectors based on 2D narrow-bandgap alloys will be deepened. The immediate course of action is to experimentally implement the pre-designed nano-optical structures, such as optical cavities and nano-antennas, with the synthesized Pt0.86Pd0.14Se2 and PtS2xSe2(1-x) crystals. This effort aims to significantly boost photoresponsivity and validate the simulated performance enhancements, moving towards practical device applications. Second, the intelligent computing devices based on 2D heterostructures, which have shown promise at the single-device level, will be advanced to the array level. The future work will focus on fabricating and integrating these functional memory and sensing cells into larger-scale arrays. This crucial step is proposed to address the challenge of real-time processing, enabling the implementation of complex in-sensor and neuromorphic computing tasks for intelligent machine vision and edge computing, thus fully realizing their potential.

21201821.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21201821.value: This project explored a new family of ultra-thin materials to develop next-generation infrared vision and intelligent computing technologies. We successfully created and studied several novel materials, including platinum-palladium and sulfur-selenium alloys (Pt0.86Pd0.14Se2 and PtS2xSe2(1-x)), which are exceptionally good at detecting long-wave infrared light—the same kind of heat radiation used in night-vision goggles. This paves the way for future infrared sensors that are more sensitive and compact. Additionally, we engineered another material combination (selenium-tellurium, SexTe1-x) to build tiny, energy-efficient electronic chips, similar to those in your smartphone but with enhanced capabilities. Beyond sensing, we designed innovative memory cells basing on 2D materials (e.g., Se, Te, CIPS, graphene and MoS2) that can both sense light and process information simultaneously, mimicking the human brain's efficient way of working. This breakthrough is crucial for developing smarter, faster, and lower-power artificial intelligence systems for applications like autonomous driving and advanced robotics. In summary, our work provides new material solutions and device concepts that will help make future electronic devices smarter, more versatile, and more efficient.

21205021.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21205021.value: 全球的移動數據流量的指數級增長推動了無綫技術的發展。雖然5G網絡仍然在部署中，但是5G系統預計將在其推出後的十年内達到其性能極限。爲了維持無綫網絡的可持續性和可拓展性，業界和學術界正在下一代無綫網絡，即6G無綫網絡。與當前的5G網絡相比，6G網絡將實現1000倍的性能提升。通信頻段處於0.1THZ至1THz的太赫茲（THz）通信是6G網絡的關鍵使能因素。豐富的頻譜資源使得太赫茲通信可以支持高達1Tbps的極高數據速率。并且由於太赫茲通信的強方向性，弱干擾和較短的傳輸距離，使得超密集網絡部署成爲可能。 本項目旨在開發易於處理的分析框架，以評估太赫茲網絡的性能，如可達速率，覆蓋率和中斷概率。該分析框架應包含詳盡的太赫茲頻段傳輸特性，取得準確的結果，并且可以適用於多種太赫茲無綫網絡應用。由於太赫茲信號複雜的傳播特性，太赫茲無綫網絡的性能分析仍然是一個懸而未決的問題。我們想通過干擾分佈的截斷正交級數展開式來解決這個瓶頸。基於這個方法，系統設計這可以通過選擇展開項數來動態控製評估系統的可處理性和準確性。最後作爲本項研究的應用， 我們將使用該分析框架去評估基於太赫茲的定位算法的性能。 項目負責人將會使用香港城市大學提供的測量儀器驗證所提出的理論信道模型和實際測量信道結果的一致性。該項目有望為6G無綫網絡建立起理論基礎，提供性能基準，并實現6G系統通信技術的優化設計。此項目將有助於香港在無綫通信行業的全球競爭力。

21205021.label: Realisation of objectives
21205021.value: This project aimed to advance the understanding and deployment of terahertz (THz) frequency bands for next-generation wireless communication systems by focusing on three key objectives: 1) characterizing the spectral efficiency and coverage performance of THz networks, 2) investigating the impact of various network deployment methods on end-to-end performance, and 3) assessing the efficacy of THz-based localization algorithms. This report details the research outcomes for each objective, highlighting their achievement and implications for future wireless technologies. Objective 1 (O1): Performance Characterization of THz Networks The first objective was to quantify the transmission performance of THz networks using a stochastic geometric framework to evaluate achievable rate and coverage probability in indoor and outdoor environments. We achieved this objective through three IEEE journal publications, summarized below: [Ref. 1] C. Wang and Y. J. Chun, "Stochastic Geometric Analysis of the Terahertz (THz)-mmWave Hybrid Network With Spatial Dependence," in IEEE Access, vol. 11, pp. 25063-25076, 2023. [Ref. 2] C. Wang, J. He, W. Xiong, H. C. So and Y. J. Chun, "Received Signal Strength Characterization in Mixed LOS and NLOS Environments," in IEEE Transactions on Aerospace and Electronic Systems, vol. 60, no. 4, pp. 5613-5620, Aug. 2024. [Ref. 3] C. Lenong and Y. J. Chun, "SNR Threshold Scheduling for IoT Uplink Network," in IEEE Internet of Things Journal, vol. 11, no. 14, pp. 25124-25135, July 15, 2024. In [Ref. 1], we analyzed a hybrid THz-mmWave network where THz base stations form a Poisson Cluster Process around mmWave nodes, modeled as a Poisson Point Process. We incorporated propagation models, including multi-level flat-top and distance-dependent blockage, deriving closed-form expressions for association and coverage probabilities. A Python-based testbed showed that this framework improves coverage by tuning cluster parameters to mitigate blockage, outperforming traditional independent networks. In [Ref. 2], we characterized Received Signal Strength (RSS) under line-of-sight (LOS) and non-line-of-sight (NLOS) conditions using a Boolean line model. We developed a stochastic reflection model to evaluate specular reflection points and reflection probability, formulating a statistical RSS model. Validated by real-world measurements, this model accurately captures RSS distribution, critical for hybrid mmWave-THz networks reliant on NLOS links. In [Ref. 3], we proposed a stochastic geometry framework to assess SNR-based threshold scheduling in uplink networks. The transmission success probability metric, accounting for fading and spatial distribution, enhances energy efficiency and resource optimization, compensating for severe THz propagation losses. Objective 2 (O2): Investigation of Various Network Deployment Methods The second objective evaluated the impact of network deployment strategies, focusing on intelligent reflecting surface (IRS)-aided THz networks, including passive, active, and hybrid IRS architectures. Three IEEE publications achieved this objective, detailed below: [Ref. 4] Y. Li and Y. J. Chun, "Analysis of IRS-Assisted Downlink Wireless Networks Over Generalized Fading," in IEEE Transactions on Wireless Communications, vol. 23, no. 8, pp. 10182-10197, Aug. 2024. [Ref. 5] Y. Li, C. You and Y. J. Chun, "Active-IRS Aided Wireless Network: System Modeling and Performance Analysis," in IEEE Communications Letters, vol. 27, no. 2, pp. 487-491, Feb. 2023. [Ref. 6] Y. Li and Y. J. Chun, "Geometric View on Integrated Cascaded Channel of IRS-Aided Communications," in IEEE Transactions on Wireless Communications, vol. 23, no. 9, pp. 11662-11677, Sept. 2024. In [Ref. 4], we analyzed passive IRS-assisted multi-cell networks, addressing complex channel modeling with a mixture Gamma distribution to approximate direct and cascaded channels with high accuracy. This unified framework enabled evaluation of spectral efficiency and outage probability, validated through simulations, overcoming limitations of prior oversimplified models. In [Ref. 5], we studied active IRS deployment in a single-cell network with Nakagami-m fading. Using mixture Gamma approximation, we derived mean SNR expressions and found that optimal spatial throughput requires balancing active-IRS density, differing from centralized passive-IRS schemes. In [Ref. 6], we explored hybrid IRS networks combining passive and active elements. Using geometric models (Cassini oval and Ellipse), we developed an opportunistic association policy that significantly outperforms conventional nearest association, particularly for hybrid and active IRS setups, as validated by simulations. Objective 3 (O3): Assessment of THz-based Localization Algorithms The third objective assessed THz-based localization algorithms by evaluating L-localizability and Cramer-Rao lower bound (CRLB) distribution across TOA-, AOA-, TDOA-, and RSS-based schemes. Three SCI journal publications achieved this objective, outlined below: [Ref. 7] J. He and Y. J. Chun, "Performance Analysis for AOA-Based Localization Under Millimeter-Wave Wireless Networks," in IEEE Access, vol. 10, pp. 17221-17230, 2022. [Ref. 8] J. He, Y. J. Chun, and H. C. So, "Modeling and performance analysis of blockchain-aided secure TDOA localization under random internet-of-vehicle networks," Signal Processing, vol. 206, pp. 108904, 2023. [Ref. 9] J. He, D. K. C. Ho, W. Xiong, H. C. So and Y. J. Chun, "Cramér–Rao Lower Bound Analysis for Elliptic Localization With Random Sensor Placements," in IEEE Transactions on Aerospace and Electronic Systems, vol. 60, no. 4, pp. 5587-5595, Aug. 2024. In [Ref. 7], we developed a stochastic framework for AOA-based localization in mmWave networks, deriving L-localizability and CRLB approximations considering directional antennas and NLOS effects. The framework accurately characterized localization performance under random spatial distributions. In [Ref. 8], we analyzed blockchain-aided TDOA localization in internet-of-vehicle networks, developing a framework to assess computational delays and derive TDOA-based CRLB. Simulations showed robust performance against malicious attacks, ensuring accurate position estimation. In [Ref. 9], we investigated time-sum-of-arrival-based elliptic localization for wireless sensor networks and bistatic radar. We derived a simple CRLB approximation under white Gaussian noise, validated by simulations, providing insights into localization performance with random sensor placements. Conclusion The project successfully met its three objectives, advancing THz-based communication systems. We characterized spectral efficiency and coverage, demonstrating superior hybrid network performance and NLOS handling. Network deployment studies, particularly IRS-aided systems, optimized end-to-end performance, with hybrid IRS outperforming traditional methods. Localization algorithm assessments established reliable metrics for AOA, TDOA, and elliptic schemes in random networks. Supported by nine peer-reviewed publications, these outcomes provide a robust foundation for future THz network research and deployment, enabling high-capacity, resilient, and precise wireless systems.

21205021.label: Major findings and research outcome
21205021.value: The research project on terahertz (THz) frequency bands for next-generation wireless communication systems achieved its three core objectives, significantly advancing the field through nine peer-reviewed IEEE and SCI journal publications. Objective 1 focused on characterizing the spectral efficiency and coverage performance of THz networks using a stochastic geometric framework. In [Ref. 1], a hybrid THz-mmWave network model was developed, employing a Poisson Cluster Process (PCP) where THz base stations are scattered around mmWave nodes, outperforming traditional Poisson Point Process (PPP)-based frameworks. This model incorporated multi-level flat-top (MLFT) and distance-dependent blockage models, deriving closed-form expressions for association and coverage probabilities, demonstrating enhanced resilience against blockages. A Python-based testbed validated these results, showing improved coverage through tunable parameters like scattering variance and bias ratio. [Ref. 2] introduced a Boolean line model (BLM) to characterize Received Signal Strength (RSS) in mixed line-of-sight (LOS) and non-line-of-sight (NLOS) environments, capturing specular reflection points and reflection probabilities with high accuracy, validated by real-world measurements. [Ref. 3] proposed an SNR-based threshold scheduling framework for uplink IoT networks, optimizing energy efficiency and resource allocation to mitigate severe THz propagation losses. Objective 2 explored network deployment strategies, focusing on intelligent reflecting surface (IRS)-aided architectures. [Ref. 4] developed a unified analytical framework using mixture Gamma distributions to model direct, cascaded, and mixed channels in passive IRS-assisted networks, achieving precise metrics like spectral efficiency and outage probability with minimal approximation error. [Ref. 5] analyzed active IRS deployment in single-cell networks, identifying optimal IRS density to maximize spatial throughput, contrasting with passive IRS’s centralized deployment preference. [Ref. 6] introduced a hybrid IRS model combining passive and active elements, leveraging geometric path loss models (Cassini oval and Ellipse) and a novel opportunistic association policy, significantly outperforming conventional nearest association strategies. Objective 3 evaluated THz-based localization algorithms, including angle-of-arrival (AOA), time-difference-of-arrival (TDOA), and elliptic localization. [Ref. 7] derived tractable L-localizability expressions for AOA-based localization under mmWave networks, accounting for directional antennas and NLOS effects. [Ref. 8] proposed a blockchain-aided TDOA localization framework for secure positioning in random internet-of-vehicle networks, demonstrating robustness against malicious attacks. [Ref. 9] developed a performance bound for elliptic localization, unifying wireless sensor and bistatic radar scenarios, with accurate Cramer-Rao lower bound (CRLB) approximations for random sensor placements. These comprehensive outcomes establish robust frameworks for THz network performance, optimized deployment, and precise localization, paving the way for high-capacity, resilient next-generation wireless systems.

21205021.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21205021.value: The research on terahertz (THz) frequency bands presents significant opportunities for further advancement, particularly in improving network scalability, practical deployment, and localization accuracy. Future efforts should prioritize integrating advanced machine learning techniques to dynamically optimize THz network parameters, tackling challenges such as adaptive blockage mitigation and efficient resource allocation in ultra-dense networks. Extending stochastic geometric frameworks to incorporate multi-user MIMO and non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) could enhance spectral efficiency and enable massive device connectivity critical for 6G systems. For intelligent reflecting surface (IRS)-aided networks, exploring self-sustaining active IRS designs with energy harvesting capabilities could improve deployment viability in resource-limited settings, reducing dependency on external power sources. Furthermore, enhancing localization algorithms with AI-driven predictive models could significantly improve precision in dynamic, non-line-of-sight (NLOS)-dominant environments, such as urban internet-of-vehicle (IoV) networks. The proposed course of action includes conducting large-scale field trials to validate theoretical models across diverse real-world scenarios, fostering industry partnerships to develop standardized THz hardware, and creating open-source simulation platforms to promote collaborative innovation. These steps will help accelerating the deployment of high-capacity, resilient THz-enabled 6G networks.

21205021.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21205021.value: This research project investigated terahertz (THz) frequency bands, an advanced technology poised to revolutionize wireless communication for future networks, such as 6G. THz waves are high-frequency signals capable of transmitting vast quantities of data, enabling significantly faster and more reliable internet connectivity. The project pursued three primary objectives: firstly, it evaluated the performance of THz networks in indoor and outdoor settings, developing methods to enhance signal strength and mitigate obstructions, such as physical barriers. Secondly, it examined intelligent reflecting surfaces (IRS), which redirect signals to optimize connection quality, determining that hybrid configurations of these surfaces yield superior results. Thirdly, it refined techniques for accurately locating devices, which is critical for applications like autonomous vehicles. Through nine peer-reviewed publications, the research demonstrated that its approaches improve network speed, efficiency, and resilience in challenging environments. This work is significant as it establishes a foundation for next-generation wireless systems, capable of supporting numerous devices, delivering ultra-high-speed connectivity, and enabling innovations like smart cities and self-driving cars. It represents a vital advancement toward a future of seamless, high-capacity global communication networks.
