21205621.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21205621.value: The rapidly growing demand for increased energy efficiency in modern industries like aerospace and power generation necessitates the innovation of advanced alloys with superb thermal-mechanical performances. As the emerging novel metallic materials, the face-centered-cubic (FCC) high-entropy alloys (HEAs) reinforced by high-density coherent L12 (ordered FCC) nanoparticles have attracted intense interest recently, offering significant advantages over many conventional alloys currently in use. Benefiting from the intrinsic ductile nature of the constituent nanophases, together with the coherent interfaces between them, this kind of nanoparticles-strengthened HEAs (NS-HEAs) have been demonstrated with superior strength-ductility combinations from cryogenic to room temperatures. More intriguingly, the excellent coarsening resistance and unique yield strength anomaly behavior (i.e., yield strength increase with increasing temperatures) of the ordered L12 phase render these NS-HEAs highly attractive to elevated-temperatures structural applications with potentially excellent resistance to softening and creep deformation. Unfortunately, most current NS-HEAs in polycrystalline forms usually suffer from serious intergranular brittle fractures at intermediated temperatures, especially at the temperature of 800 °C, which significantly limits their practical use at elevated temperatures. Such a thorny problem has also been frequently encountered in many conventional wrought superalloys. Surprisingly, in our preliminary work, we deliberately developed a novel NS-HEAs with a unique hetero-lamellar grain (HLG) structure, which exhibited exceptionally high resistance to intermediate-temperature embrittlement (ITE). Nevertheless, several fundamental issues remain largely unaddressed and require more in-depth studies in this project. By using multi-scale experimental techniques and theoretical calculations, we aim at systemically investigating the processing-structure-properties relationship of these newly discovered HLG-NS-HEAs at the intermediate temperatures, emphasizing on the intrinsic origins governing the ITE behaviors. The effects of alloy microstructure, testing atmosphere, and strain rate will be quantitatively studied. Moreover, in-depth studies on their thermal resistance including the microstructural stability and creep resistance will also be carried out. The establishment and successful implementation of this project are expected to offer quantitative insights into the intrinsic relationships between the alloy composition, phase structure, grain boundary feature, and associated thermal-mechanical behaviors of such a new class of HLG-NS-HEA. More importantly, the results accomplished here will provide a strong theoretical basis and technical guidance to advance the innovative design of novel high-performance structural materials for elevated-temperature applications. All these research achievements will be crucial to improving engineering reliability and energy efficiency in a broad range of industrial fields, including aerospace, automotive, energy, and other applications. 现代工业（如航空航天、電力等）的快速发展对于改善能源效率提出了更為嚴格的要求，從而使得具有优异热机械性能的特種合金的研发势在必行。作为一種新兴的特種金属材料，共格纳米颗粒增强型面心立方結構的復合高熵合金（HEAs）最近引起了研究者們的极大兴趣，与目前使用的许多传统合金相比具有更為显著的性能优势。得益于L12纳米顆粒的本征韧性和高密度析出，以及它们與基體之间的共格界面關係，这种纳米顆粒增强型HEAs（NS-HEAs）已被证明可以在超低溫和室溫下顯示出色的力學性能。更為有趣的是，這類特種合金具備了优良的抗顆粒粗化性能以及独特的反常屈服行为（即屈服强度随温度的升高而升高的行為），以及潜在的优异抗软化和抗蠕变等性能，從而使得这些NS-HEAs在高温结构应用方面顯示了巨大的潛力。然而，不幸的是，目前大多数的NS-HEAs仍然以多晶形式存在，在中等溫度區間（特别是在800°C）顯示出了非常严重的晶间脆性，这大大限制了它们的大規模應用。这一个棘手的问题也在许多傳統的锻造高温合金出現，且至今沒有得到很好地解決。值得驚喜的是，我们在初步的研究探索中成功開發了一種具有独特异质层状晶粒结构（HLG）的新型NS-HEAs，顯示了极高的抗中温脆化的能力。尽管如此，一些基本的科學问题仍然尚未解决，需要在本项目中進行更加深入的探索與研究。因此，本項目中我們擬利用多尺度实验技术和理论计算相結合的方法，系统地研究了这類HLG-NS-HEA中微觀结构与性能之間的內在关系，揭示其晶界增韌的內在機理。對合金的微观结构、试验气氛，应变速率等因素进行定量化的研究。此外，對其显微组织的熱稳定性和抗蠕变性能進行評估。该项目的成功实施将有助于对該新型HLG-NS-HEA合金的成分、相结构、晶界特征和相关的热机械性能等行为提供更加定量化的認識。更為重要的是，本項目中所取得的研究成果将为新型高性能耐高温结构材料的創新设计和应用提供强有力的理论依据和技术指导。这些成果也將对航空航天、汽车、能源等諸多領域的工程可靠性和能源效率的提高發揮至關重要的作用。

21205621.label: Realisation of objectives
21205621.value: Objective 1: To elucidate the intrinsic origins governing the fracture resistance of NS-HEAs against the intergranular embrittlement behavior at intermediate temperatures. Based on the systematic investigations, the origin of intergranular embrittlement at intermediate temperatures in a nanoparticle-strengthened high-entropy alloy has been uncovered. It was found that both heterogeneous strain distribution and environmental attack are critical in facilitating intergranular embrittlement. We revealed the key role of heterogeneous strain distribution and environmental attack in facilitating intergranular crack initiation and propagation at intermediate temperatures. The dislocation accumulation has been found in the vicinity of grain boundaries to accommodate thermally activated grain-boundary sliding. Grain boundaries with extensive dislocation pile-ups served as preferential sites for the initiation of voids and associated cracks. The growth and linkage of microcracks lead to the destructive tensile failure. More importantly, environmentally assisted grain-boundary damage plays a vital role in exacerbating the embrittlement. In contrast to the laboratory air atmosphere, tensile testing in an inert argon atmosphere protected the specimens from environmental damage and helped to recover the tensile ductility at intermediate temperatures. Electron microscopy analyses have uncovered the unique deformation substructures, in which both Orowan looping and particle shearing took place. Improving the oxidation resistance of the alloys by optimized compositional design could allow us to overcome such kind of intergranular embrittlement behavior. Our findings reveal that an increase in the additions of Cr and Nb enhances the oxidation resistance of the alloy in high-temperature applications. Concurrently, the minor addition of Si promotes the formation of grain boundary precipitates, which suppresses intergranular oxidation and thereby improves the ductility at intermediate temperatures. These findings provide a fundamental understanding of the temperature-dependent deformation behaviors of polycrystalline high-entropy alloys. Objective 2: To quantitatively reveal the microstructural stability and its impact on plastic deformation behaviors of the novel HLG-NS-HEAs at intermediate temperatures through a combination of experimental and theoretical studies. Through a combination of various complementary experimental techniques and theoretical simulations, we find the key to effectively stabilizing the second-phase nanoparticles in a chemically complex NiCoFeCrAlTiB high-entropy metallic system. We systematically explored the significant effect of the Co element on the sluggish diffusion kinetics. Three experimental alloys, Ni59.9-xCoxFe13Cr15Al6Ti6B0.1 (x = 0, 15, and 30 at.%, denoted as the 0Co, 15Co, and 30Co alloys), were cast via arc melting, and subsequently, followed by thermally-aging processing. It was revealed that tailoring the concentration of the Co element can controllably govern the sluggish diffusion (SLD) effect in a quantitative manner, which enables us to substantially prevent the nanoparticles from rapid coarsening at high temperatures up to 1000 °C. Our diffusion kinetic simulations also revealed that the Co element leads to a significant reduction in the interdiffusion coefficients of all the main elements, especially for the Al element, with a maximum of up to 5 orders of magnitude. Utilizing first-principles calculations, we further unveiled that the incompressibility of Al induced by the increased concentration of Co plays a critical role in controlling the SLD effect. These findings are useful for providing advances in the design of novel structural alloys with extraordinary property-microstructure stability combinations for structural applications. It is worth noting that the L21-type Heusler phase starts to form at grain boundaries when the Co content increases up to 30 at.%. Upon plastic deformation, it was found that this Heusler phase will cause increased local stress concentration and premature failures of the alloys, as it is extremely brittle and incoherent with the FCC matrix. Based on the above findings, we have elaborately designed a series of NS-HEAs with various Fe/Cr concentrations based on the theoretical technique. The intermediate-temperature embrittlement along GBs can be effectively defeated by introducing compact protective oxide layers through the optimized regulation of Cr doping. Benefiting from this design, the fracture mode could be changed from the brittle intergranular cleavage to the ductile dimpled transgranular failure, resulting in a substantial increase in tensile ductility at the intermediate temperature. Moreover, our research also demonstrates that the incorporation of Nb effectively alters the morphology of precipitates and their coarsening kinetics in NS-HEAs. The addition of moderate amounts of Nb significantly stabilizes the L12 phase, thereby ensuring mechanical properties at elevated temperatures. Objective 3: To quantitatively evaluate the creep deformation properties and mechanisms of the novel HLG-NS-HEAs at intermediate temperatures and then establish a valid scientific basis for designing advanced alloys with superior thermal-mechanical resistance. To establish a valid scientific basis for designing advanced alloys with superior thermal-mechanical resistance, we critically summarize the alloy design, microstructure evolution, oxidation resistance, and mechanical and magnetic properties of NS-HEAs. The advantages of multicomponent coherent precipitation-strengthened HEAs, as well as the limitations in this field, are also carefully discussed. In addition, we comprehensively review the state-of-the-art advances of environmental embrittlement (EE) issues in HEAs, e.g., hydrogen embrittlement (HE) and intermediate-temperature embrittlement (ITE). Particular focus is given to novel strategies to enhance the resistance to EE in different HEAs. We provide promising strategies for developing EE-resistant HEAs, which will be crucial for developing novel structural alloys with superior thermal-mechanical properties. Meanwhile, based on the research above, we designed and developed a heterogeneous grain architecture NS-HEAs, which consists of fine recrystallized grains and coarse columnar grains with disconnected high-angle grain boundary networks as well as numerous low-energy low-angle boundaries. This structure can effectively conquer the premature creep rupture in the NS-HEAs under high stress levels.

21205621.label: Major findings and research outcome
21205621.value: 1. We demonstrated the origin of such temperature-dependent premature tensile failure in NS-HEAs. We compared the rapid tensile fracture in laboratory air with thermal barrier coating and protective testing atmosphere. And concluded that the tensile ductility drop in the intermediate temperature regime should be mainly ascribed to the environmental damage in the oxidizing atmosphere. The penetrating oxygen led to the grain boundary cohesion loss at the crack tip, allowing for the crack tip to advance aided by a local stress and shift the crack tip and the embrittling species inwards. This process facilitated intergranular crack propagation, resulting in a premature tensile failure. 2. We found that increasing the Cr content to enhance oxidation resistance effectively mitigates intermediate-temperature embrittlement. In the NiCoFeCrAlTiB HEA system, a stable coherent precipitate microstructure is maintained when Fe is continuously replaced by Cr. The structural features, mechanical properties, and underlying deformation micro-mechanisms were systematically investigated. We found that Cr mostly partitions into the FCC matrix relative to the L12-type nanoparticles. The increased Cr concentration substantially decreases the stacking fault energy (SFE) of the matrix and results in the stacking-fault-prevailed deformation behaviors, thereby producing simultaneously enhanced strength and ductility at room temperature. By contrast, when tested at 600 °C, the Cr-free HEA suffers from an extremely brittle fracture along grain boundaries caused by environmental oxidation damage. Interestingly, with Cr doping up to 20 at.%, such a severe intergranular embrittlement can be completely eliminated due to the increased oxidation resistance, leading to a distinct brittle-to-ductile transition (from 3.4 to 25.2%) at a high strength level of ∼ 1136 MPa. 3. Via the controllable sluggish lattice diffusion (SLD) effect, we demonstrate a strategy to achieve ultra-stable nanoparticles at 800~1000 °C in a chemically complex alloy. Our diffusion kinetic simulations reveal that the Co element leads to a significant reduction in the interdiffusion coefficients of all the main elements, especially for the Al element, with a maximum of up to 5 orders of magnitude. Utilizing first-principles calculations, we further unveil that the incompressibility of Al, induced by the increased concentration of Co, plays a critical role in controlling the SLD effect. 4. We discovered that introducing grain boundary precipitates can suppress intergranular oxidation, thereby improving intermediate-temperature embrittlement resistance. Experimental analysis revealed that the intergranular G phase induced by minor Si addition can effectively suppress the inward diffusion of oxygen along grain boundaries at 700 °C, thus enhancing the tensile ductility of the alloy from ∼8.3% to ∼13.4%. Besides, the minor Si addition facilitated the formation of a continuous Al2O3 layer during oxidation, contributing to a remarkable reduction in the growth rate of the oxide scale to a quarter of the Si-free high entropy superalloy (HESA). Si can be a favorable alloying element to design advanced HESAs with synergistically improved thermal-mechanical performance.

21205621.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21205621.value: For future work, we strongly suggest that researchers build upon our findings by conducting the following studies: (1) The hetero-lamellar grain design strategy is recommended to be implemented in other alloy systems to enhance mechanical properties across temperature regimes. (2) Designing and developing single-crystal NS-HEAs is recommended, which can directly resolve the problems brought by grain boundaries at elevated temperature. (3) Employing machine learning and artificial intelligence methodologies to develop advanced alloying strategies will enable the design of next-generation high-temperature materials that simultaneously achieve a balance between strength, ductility, oxidation resistance, and phase stability under elevated temperatures.

21205621.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21205621.value: Advanced industrial sectors, particularly those operating under extreme conditions like jet propulsion and power generation, urgently require high-performance alloys exhibiting superior strength-ductility synergy across both ambient and elevated temperatures.​​ High-density coherent nanoparticles-strengthened HEAs (NS-HEAs) demonstrate exceptional potential for high-temperature structural applications owing to their unique microstructural characteristics and mechanical properties. ​However, most existing polycrystalline NS-HEAs suffer severe ​intergranular embrittlement​ within the 600–800°C intermediate-temperature range, which critically limits their practical application.​​ Through meticulously designed experiments, this project has revealed the fundamental mechanisms underlying intermediate-temperature embrittlement. Based on these insights, we have engineered a novel series of NS-HEAs via ​compositional optimization and grain boundary engineering, achieving ​marked mitigation​ of embrittlement issues at intermediate temperatures. These advances will accelerate the development of next-generation high-temperature structural materials, ​demonstrating important contributions from Hong Kong scientists to the field.

21208921.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21208921.value: 网络控制系统的最优隐私感知设计：一种信息论方法智能建筑和智慧交通网络等网络控制系统

21208921.label: Project Objectives
21208921.value: We propose a framework for ensuring the privacy of a networked control system when the state estimates are shared with an honest-but-curious adversary. In this objective, we adopt a common realistic assumption that the adversary cannot influence the evolution of the systems, e.g., a cloud-computing unit employed for fault detection or monitoring. We propose to design the state estimator such that (i) it provides an accurate representation of the system state, (ii) an adversary with access to the state estimates cannot reliably infer the private information. We consider an entropy-penalized framework for the estimator design problem, wherein the estimator is designed by minimizing a linear combination of the estimation loss and the privacy level, captured by the conditional entropy. We will cast the optimal privacy-aware estimator problem as a dynamic optimization problem and study the structural properties of the optimal estimator. The structural properties will be used to develop efficient numerical algorithms for computing the optimal estimator. We propose a framework for ensuring privacy in the closed-loop control setting, wherein an honest-but-curious controller, e.g., a cloud-based controller, has access to the state estimates of a networked control system. The controller computes the control actions based on the state estimates; however, it may attempt to infer the private information of the system using the state estimates. We propose to design the estimator and the control law such that (i) a desirable level of closed-loop performance is attained, (ii) it is ensured that the controller cannot reliably infer the private information from the state estimates. In this objective, the state estimates influence the evolution of the system via the control law. Thus, the design of the estimator affects the closed-loop performance of the system. We will cast the optimal privacy-aware estimator-controller co-design problem as minimizing a linear combination of the closed-loop performance of the system and its privacy level. We will then study the structural properties of the jointly optimal estimator and controller. We will also devise efficient numerical algorithms for solving the jointly optimal estimator-controller co-design problem.

21208921.label: Major findings and research outcome
21208921.value: 1- We have developed a framework for the optimal design of privacy-aware estimators using mutual information as a privacy measure. We derived the structural properties of the optimal estimator and developed a numerical algorithm for computing it. 2- We developed a numerical algorithm for computing the leakage level of private information using mutual information. The developed method poses the computation of mutual information as an optimization algorithm using a variational equality for the KL-divergence. 3- We have studied the optimal co-design of the estimators and controllers for networked controlled systems using mutual information as a privacy measure. 4- We developed a framework for privacy-aware design of HVAC systems and studied its performance using the TRNSYS simulator.

21208921.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21208921.value: The results of this project will be used by the PI to study the flow of information in distributed networks. The PI will utilize the results to apply for further funding.

21208921.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21208921.value: In the past decade, communication networks have transformed many existing infrastructures to highly efficient networked systems, e.g., transportation systems, power networks, public and private networked data centers, healthcare systems, and financial management systems. Thanks to the existing and emerging networked systems, the quality of life indicators are expected to increase by up to 30% in various domains such as mobility, water, energy, health, and economic development, according to a report by McKinsey Global Institute. However, increasing threats due to privacy infringement and security breach are continuing to pose serious challenges to the design of such networked systems. Privacy-aware networked control systems will be central components of our infrastructure and industry, e.g., smart buildings and intelligent transportation networks. The privacy of human users in networked control systems is a societal concern due to the extensive utilization of information and communication technologies in these systems. According to a report by IBM Security, the worldwide average cost of a data breach was $ 3.8 million in 2018-2019, with lost revenue being a significant contributing factor to this cost. Thus, the success of the existing and emerging networked technologies crucially depends on efficient privacy-preserving mechanisms. The outcomes of this project will provide a suite of solutions for the privacy-aware design of networked control systems. Hence, they will be beneficial to system designers, business owners, and users of such systems.

21213621.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21213621.value: 基於液滴微流控的仿生軟體微型驅動器

21213621.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21213621.value: Soft actuators can exhibit continuous deformations, minimize damage under high loads, conformably adapt to complex environments, and allow safe human-machine interactions. Thus, they hold great promise for a range of applications, including artificial muscles, soft robotics, wearable devices, sensing, and biomedicine. However, due to inadequacies in conventional design and fabrication, a long-standing challenge in the development of soft actuators has been the simultaneous achievement of (i) significant actuation for high-payload mechanical work, (ii) diverse shape transformations, (iii) high contrast between material properties in the "on" and "off" states, and (iv) miniaturization. We propose to develop microfiber-type bioinspired soft microactuators (BSMAs) that meet these four requirements. We will combine tunable stiffness as exhibited by sea cucumber (holothurian) dermis and regulatable deformability as exhibited by plant tendrils, to realize BSMAs with high actuation performance and diverse shape transformations, respectively. The BSMAs will consist of hygroscopically responsive microfibers embedded with a discontinuous ribbon of stiff, asymmetric, and hygroscopically inactive microparticles, which will enable a remarkable property contrast between the dehydrated "on" and hydrated "off" states. We propose to use droplet microfluidics to fabricate the BSMAs. Microfluidic fabrication has several advantages, as it enables the precise handling of small volumes of fluids, the accurate production of uniform emulsions, and the freedom to use a variety of materials, which will enable the construction of seamless and miniaturized BSMAs with independently controllable morphology and composition. The innovation of this proposal will be its combination of synergistic bioinspiration and droplet microfluidics to address the respective inadequacies of conventional design and fabrication. We aim to explore the potential of this promising approach to generate high-performance soft actuators. Specifically, we will develop and characterize the proposed approach by fabricating BSMAs made of diatomite-reinforced alginate microfibers embedded with asymmetric trimethylolpropane ethoxylate triacrylate (ETPTA) microparticles. We will then correlate the morphology, composition, mechanical properties, and actuation of these BSMAs with processing parameters and investigate BSMAs' potential applications. The three ingredients – diatomite, alginate, and ETPTA – are selected because of their biocompatibility, commercial availability, and low cost. This project will provide a new and generally applicable method for designing and fabricating next-generation soft actuators. This will be a great advance, as it will enable the precise tailoring of soft actuators' morphologies and properties. The project will also provide a revolutionary type of miniaturized BSMAs with tunable mechanical properties, high-performance actuation, and diverse shape transformability, establishing a foundation for their wider application. 軟驅動器具備可連續變形、最大限度減少高負載下的損傷、適應複雜環境、安全的人機交互等優點。因此，它們在包括人工肌肉、軟體機器人、可穿戴設備、傳感和生物醫學在內的一系列應用中有著巨大的前景。然而，由於傳統設計和製造的不足，軟驅動器發展中一個長期存在的挑戰是同時實現：(i)高有效載荷的做工能力，(ii)多樣化的形變能力，(iii)在“開”和“關”狀態下具備高度差異化的機械性能，(iv)小型化製備。我們擬開發同時滿足這四項要求的生物啟發式微纖維型軟微驅動器(BSMA)，其設計將結合海參真皮的可調節剛度和植物卷鬚的可調節變形能力，分別實現高驅動性能和多樣化形變。BSMA將由具有吸濕回應性的微纖維組成，其中嵌入了硬質不連續的、不對稱的、不吸濕的微顆粒材料，這將使脫水“開啟”和水合“關閉”狀態之間具有顯著的機械性能對比。我們擬使用液滴微流控技術製造BSMA，該製造方法具有多重優點，它能夠精確處理小體積的流體，精確生產均勻的乳液，並可以自由使用各種材料，這將實現無縫和微型化BSMA的構建，具有獨立可控的物理形態和材料組成。該研究的創新之處在于將生物啟發協同設計和液滴微流控相結合，以分別解決傳統設計和製造的不足。該研究的目標是探索這種方法製備高性能軟驅動器的潛力。具體而言，我們擬製備的BSMA將由矽藻土增強的海藻酸鹽微纖維組成，在其中包覆三甲基丙烷乙氧基三丙烯酸酯(ETPTA)微顆粒。選擇矽藻土、海藻酸鹽和ETPTA這三種材料是因為它們的生物相容性、商業可用性和低成本。其次，我們將把BSMA的形態、成分、力學和驅動性能與製備工藝參數相關聯，並研究BSMA的潛在應用。該項目將為下一代軟驅動器的設計和製造提供一種新的、普遍適用的方法，這將令精確工程化軟驅動器的形態和性能成為可能，取得卓越的進步。該項目還將產生一種小型化的軟驅動器，具有可調諧的力學性能、高性能的驅動能力和多樣化的變形特性，為其更廣泛的應用奠定基礎。

21213821.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21213821.value: 現實場景下圖像渲染的有效評估及感知優化

21213821.label: Project Objectives
21213821.value: Describe a subjective assessment method for fair and efficient comparison of high-dynamic-range (HDR) image rendering. The major challenge here is to reconcile the conflict between the enormous size of the input HDR image space and the limited scale of affordable human labeling. Conventional subjective assessment requires manual selection of sample images, which inevitably suffers from the experimenters' biases. Moreover, the manual selection process has not been optimized to make the best use of the limited human labeling budget. As the proposed subjective assessment method is generic, we will apply it not only to HDR image rendering but also to photographic style transfer and image-to-image translation, where the previous evaluation was mostly based on visual inspection of few (cherry-picked) examples. Construct a no-reference objective assessment method capable of automatically evaluating HDR image rendering without access to underlying HDR images. The key to the success of our method is to leverage human annotations from related computational photography tasks for robust model learning and regularization. As a by-product, the proposed objective assessment method is able to evaluate other related methods, including image restoration, enhancement, super-resolution, dehazing, and synthesis, at a reasonable level. Nevertheless, objective assessment of HDR image rendering is a less-explored topic, despite its paramount importance in making this field more of a science than an art. Develop a biologically-inspired and practical HDR image rendering method by optimizing the proposed objective assessment model (in Objective II) for improved visual quality. The difficulties of achieving this task are to mimic the human visual system in response to different light intensities, while incorporating different display limitations within the perception-driven optimization framework. Existing methods are mainly based on simple empirical rules with unjustified perceptual optimality. Moreover, they fail to adapt their rendering results to different displays constraints (e.g., displays with different maximum luminance values). Adjust the proposed image rendering method (in Objective III) to assist semantic segmentation in challenging low-light conditions through joint perception-driven optimization. The main obstacle is to reliably transfer low-light enhancement gains of front-end image rendering to accuracy improvements of semantic segmentation in an unsupervised way. Existing methods either require fusing extra information from other modalities, which is very costly, or fine-tuning from abundant human annotations, which is relatively impractical.

21213821.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21213821.value: 隨著攝影技術的進步，當前的圖像傳感器已經能夠拍攝高動態範圍圖片，感光性接近人類視覺在明視狀態下的敏感性。然而，現有的顯示器和投影儀動態範圍有限，不足以再現所拍攝的高動態範圍自然場景。低動態範圍 (LDR) 顯示設備需依賴色調映射算子進行動態範圍壓縮從而渲染高動態範圍 (HDR) 圖像。然而現有HDR 圖像渲染的一些基本問題仍然存在，限制了其廣泛應用。 首先，為了比較圖像渲染算法，通常需要收集一組人為打分的視覺示例，這無疑是低效的且可能引入主觀偏見。在該項目中，我們將通過自動採樣少量無偏見、多樣化和自適應圖像來構建一種公平高效的主觀評估方法。同時，該領域缺乏可信的無參考質量模型，我們將構建一種基於深度學習的客觀評估方法來評估 HDR 圖像渲染結果。其次，大多數感知渲染算法的設計並沒有遵循客觀評估模型的指導，因此它們的感知最優性尚未可知。另外，現有圖像渲染算法的增強能力可能對下游視覺識別任務並沒有明顯促進作用。該項目將通過優化所提出的客觀評估模型來設計一種全新的實用的渲染方法。 我們還將在感知驅動框架內提出可以輔助機器視覺的渲染算法。 鑑於良好的初步結果，我們相信所提出的方案將 1) 可靠地衡量 HDR 圖像渲染和其他相關領域的進展，2) 闡明它們的優點和缺點，以及 3) 顯著推進基於人類和機器感知的HDR 圖像渲染技術。

21213921.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21213921.value: 基於機制的晶界熱力學與動力學模擬方法

21213921.label: Project Objectives
21213921.value: Develop a novel approach for (i) the calculation of grain-boundary (GB) properties and (ii) the simulation of GB kinetic behaviors. The GB properties include equilibrium GB roughness, GB free energy, and GB mobility tensor (including mobility and viscosity). The GB kinetics include GB migration and sliding. This approach will be built upon the statistical model of the line defects (i.e., disconnections). The novelty of this approach is reflected in (i) the multiscale framework – large length- and time-scale simulations (the scale accessible to experimental observation) with the input of atomic-scale quantities, and (ii) extensibility – it is easy to incorporate more microscopic mechanisms to the model and enable the study of more complicated phenomena. This approach will be finally implemented by a well-developed computational tool that will be finally available for general users. Create a workflow for automating the computation of the GB mobility tensor as a function of temperature and bicrystallography using the developed approach. The GB mobility tensor is the key kinetic parameter entering in the higher-level models. The problems involved in this project will also heavily rely on the data of GB mobility tensor. Employ the developed approach to study the GB phase transitions and their implications on GB kinetics. Two types of phase transitions were recently predicted for one-dimensional GBs in theory – roughening transition and Kosterlitz-Thouless transition. The new approach enables the study of these phase transitions in two-dimensional GBs. Quantitatively investigate the influence of the phase transitions on the GB mobility tensor. Incorporate the phase transitions into the classical theory of grain growth and plasticity of polycrystals. Include the triple junction (TJ) effect on the GB kinetics. Calculate the apparent mobility of a GB under the constraints of TJs with different TJ properties under different temperatures. Reveal how TJs affect the GB kinetics in a polycrystal based on the microscopic (disconnection) mechanism. Extend the approach to the study of GB migration and sliding in solid solutions. Simulate the steady-state GB motion coupled with the diffusion of solute atoms. Calculate the GB mobility tensor in solid solutions. Explore the kinetic parameters (e.g. heat of segregation and diffusivity of solute atoms) to lower the GB mobility. Figure out the alloying strategy towards strengthening of the thermal stability of polycrystal microstructure.

21213921.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21213921.value: Most crystalline materials, such as metals and ceramics, exist in form of polycrystals, which are composed of aggregates of single-crystalline grains differing in orientation. The long-range order of atomic arrangement within the grains is broken at the interface between the contiguous grains. So, the interface is a planar defect, called grain boundary (GB). Since GBs are prevailing defects in a polycrystalline material, the material properties can be adjusted by controlling the type and population of GBs – this is an approach towards the development of materials with novel properties, e.g. strength, ductility, resistance to radiation damage, etc. Implementation of this approach relies on the understanding of GB thermodynamics and kinetics; the former aims to predicting the equilibrium GB properties while the latter predicting the response of GBs to the external forces. The current researches are limited by the available methods and tools. The classical theories usually assume capillarity-driven, overdamped GB kinetics. Accumulated experimental observations manifest the failure of this assumption; such observations include non-parabolic grain growth, stress-induced GB migration/rotation, non-thermal GB mobility/viscosity, enhanced stability of nano grains, etc. On the other hand, GB thermodynamics/kinetics can be studied by atomistic simulations with less assumptions; however, such simulations are highly limited in length and time scales. In the proposed project, we will develop an approach to simulate the GB behaviors in and out of equilibrium under complicated external conditions. The fundamental mechanism of the GB behaviors (i.e., thermal fluctuation, GB migration/sliding) is the nucleation, annihilation and motion of disconnections. The new approach is built upon the disconnection mechanism, lattice model and Monte Carlo (MC) method. It is expected that this approach can overcome the length- and time-scale limitations inherent to the atomistic simulations and, at the same time, reproduce diverse GB kinetic behaviors which cannot be captured by the classical theory. A state-of-the-art computational tool will be developed to implement this approach. The power of this approach will be instantiated by two applications. (i) Simulation of GB phase transitions – the goal is to reveal the underlying physics and the implications on anomalous GB kinetics. (ii) Simulation of GB migration/sliding in pure metals and solid solutions – the goal is to develop workflow of the GB mobility tensor computation, explore the parameter space to optimize the GB property (such as thermal stability), and, in addition, include the triple junction effect to connect the kinetics of isolated GBs to that of polycrystals. 大多數晶體材料（例如金屬與陶瓷）的存在形態為多晶，即由多個晶體取向不同的單晶晶粒組合而成的整體。在相鄰晶粒的界面處，原子排列的長程序被破壞。因此，界面是一種面缺陷，稱為晶界。晶界是多晶材料中普遍存在的缺陷。因此，控制晶界類型與數量可以實現對多晶材料性能的調節 – 這種方法可使材料獲得優異性能，例如強度、韌性、抗輻射損傷性能等。該方法的實現依賴於對晶界熱力學與動力學的深入理解。熱力學的目的是預測晶界的平衡性能，而動力學的目的是預測晶界在外力下的響應。 當前已有的相關研究受限於方法與工具。傳統理論通常假設界面張力驅動的耗散晶界動力學。然而，越來越多的實驗現象證明這個假設未必準確。這些實驗現象包括：非經典的晶粒長大規律、應力誘導晶界遷移與旋轉、非經典晶界遷移率與黏度的溫度相關性、強化的納米晶粒穩定性等。在另一方面，晶界熱力學與動力學可以用原子尺度模擬來研究，從而避免了過於粗糙的假設。但是，原子尺度模擬只能研究極小空間與時間尺度內發生的現象。 在本項目中，我們將開發一種模擬晶界在復雜外在條件下平衡與非平衡行為的方法。晶界行為（例如熱振動、遷移與滑移）的基本機制是界面位錯（disconnections）的形核、湮滅與滑移。新的方法將會建立於界面位錯機制、晶格模型與蒙特卡洛方法。該方法將能夠克服原子尺度模擬方法中所遇到的空間與時間尺度的限制。同時，該方法將能夠模擬傳統理論所無法預測的多種多樣的晶界動力學行為。為實現該方法，我們將開發先進的計算工具。我們將通過兩個應用來驗證方法與工具的有效性。 （1）晶界相變模擬 – 目的為揭示根本的物理原理以及對異常晶界動力學研究的啟示。 （2）純金屬與固溶體中晶界遷移與滑移的模擬 – 目的為發展晶界遷移率的計算方法、探索參數空間以優化晶界性能（例如熱力學穩定性）。最後，我們將考慮三叉晶界的效應，將單個晶界的性能與多晶整體性能聯繫起來。

21301221.label: Project Objectives
21301221.value: To develop synthetic approaches to cleaner superconducting nickelate systems. Due to the difficulty in producing single-crystals and the absence (yet) of superconductivity in powder bulk samples, synthesis of clean infinite-layer nickelate thin-films of high-quality will provide a solid foundation for investigating the intrinsic physical properties. The knowledge acquired will be valuable to the research community. To design and discover additional nickelate materials with competing or intertwined electronic order. The outcome of this research topic will uncover more exotic quantum phases and reveal the mechanism of nickelate superconductivity, upon which new perspectives to understanding high-temperature superconductivity will likely to be gained. To gain deep understanding of the nickelate phase diagram combining new materials synthesis and advanced condensed-matter research tools. This collaborative efforts will tackle most interesting and important issues regarding the pairing symmetry and pairing mechanism, which can make us rethink their potentially relationship to cuprates.

21301221.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21301221.value: Designing and discovering novel quantum materials and architectures pose an exciting frontier in condensed-matter research. In particular, synthesis of new superconductors, especially those with unusual symmetries of superconducting order parameters and/or exotic pairing mechanisms, opens new doors to future applications in quantum devices. Ever since their discovery, high-temperature superconductivity in cuprates has motivated the search for materials with analogous electronic or atomic structure. The recent discovery of superconductivity in a similar system, infinite-layer nickelate, has spurred a surge of research interest. The project proposed herein aims to expand the family of the nickelate superconductors with infinite-layer structure, which offers the materials playground for investigating a wide spectrum of electronic energy landscape and the unconventional pairing mechanism. The project builds on the following extraordinary advances in the recent years: (1) the atomic-scale synthesis of the epitaxial complex oxide thin films and heterostructures, which host emergent quantum phenomena; (2) the ever-better understanding of high-temperature superconductivity, especially in the cuprate systems; (3) the kinetic-based soft-chemistry approaches that led to the discovery of superconducting nickelates. Specifically, the project will develop synthetic pathways to new members of the nickelate superconductor family, with the potential of having higher transition temperature and Fermi surface ordering instability. By transport and other means, a comprehensive phase diagram enriched with intertwined electronic orders will be established, in which exciting physics will be studied. The proposed work will investigate the intimate interplay between cation composition, superconducting properties and other exotic phases. This project provides an avenue for addressing some of the key materials and physics issues nowadays in the research on the nickelate superconductors. 設計和發現新的量子材料與結構是凝聚態研究中令人興奮的前沿陣地。合成新型超導體，特別是那些具有不尋常超導序參數對稱性或者奇異配對機制的超導體，為未來量子設備的應用打開了一扇新的大門。自從銅氧化物高溫超導被發現以來，人們都在努力尋找具有相似電子或原子結構的超導材料。最近在一個類似的系統——無限層鎳氧化物——中發現的超導電性，更進一步激發了人們對此的研究興趣。本項目旨在擴大無限層鎳氧化物超導材料家族，並為廣泛研究其電子能量特性和非常規的配對機制提供材料平台。 該項目將建立於以下最近幾年的重要科研進展之上：（1） 外延複雜氧化物薄膜和異質結結構的原子級合成，以及由此所產生的演生量子現象；（2） 對高溫超導電性特別是銅氧化物系統的更加深入、清晰的理解；（3） 製備超導鎳氧化物所用的基於材料動力學的軟化學方法的發展。具體而言，本項目將重點研究可能具有更高轉變溫度或具有費米麵成序不穩定性的新型鎳氧化物超導材料的合成途徑；通過電子輸運和其他實驗手段建立一個具有相互交織、不同電子序的豐富超導相圖——在這個相圖中，許多重要的物理特性將為本研究的重點。 本研究項目將重點研究陽離子組成、超導電性以及其它特殊性質之間的密切相互作用。本項目為解決當今鎳氧化物超導材料研究中一些關鍵材料和物理學問題提供了重要途徑。

21302521.value: 具有不可分哈密頓量的平均場博弈論

21302521.label: Project Objectives
21302521.value: Master equations with noises and smooth data. Our first objective is to investigate an a priori Lipschitz estimate for the solution to the master equation with individual and common noises and its global (in time) well-posedness when the data are smooth. The study of global well-posedness for master equations usually starts from a local (in time) one, by using mean field forward-backward stochastic differential equations (FBSDEs). The key to extend to a global result is to prove a priori Lipschitz estimates under certain monotonicity condition. Thus we first focus on extending some monotonicity condition to adapt non-separable Hamiltonians and show an a priori Lipschitz estimate for the solution to the master equation. Next we shall patch the local solutions into a global one. As byproducts, the well-posdedness of the corresponding forward-backward systems of mean field stochastic differential equations (SDEs) and stochastic partial differential equations (SPDEs) should be obtained. Master equations with noises and non-smooth data. Our second objective is to study global well-posedness for weak notions of solutions to master equations with noises, however, when the data are non-smooth. We shall investigate the well-posedness of the master equation involving data that is required to be only Lipschitz in the probability measure variable. Consequently, one cannot expect classical solutions to the master equation even for the local well-posedness result. Different types of weak solutions will be considered. As an important application of the well-posedness result for the master equation, we will also work on the convergence problems of the optimal value and trajectory of each player from the N-player games to the MFG. Master equations with degenerate/no noises and non-smooth data. Our third objective is to study global well-posedness in the case of degenerate/no noises. The degeneracy of the individual noise poses difficulties due to the lack of compactness in the state space. We shall recover the compactness from the regularity assumption on data and the monotonicity. Such compactness will also play a role in showing a stability result corresponding to the magnitude of individual noise when we apply the vanishing viscosity method. The convergence results from the N-player games to the MFG shall also be investigated.

21302521.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21302521.value: Mean field games (MFGs), initiated independently by Caines-Huang-Malhame and Lasry-Lions, study strategic decision making in large populations where the players interact with each other in some symmetric way. MFGs are studied by taking the limit of the number of players to infinite and replacing individual interactions by an average interaction. Each player in an MFG decides his/her strategies over the time to minimize his/her cost. Their strategies influence the controlled dynamics of the game. MFGs have received very strong attention in the past decade. They have a wide variety of applications, including models of crowd motion, economic growth, oil production, mathematical finance, and many others. The master equation is a powerful tool in MFGs, which plays the role of the partial differential equation (PDE) in the standard literature of controls. For example, the master equation plays a crucial role in constructing closed-loop Nash equilibria for the MFG and showing the convergence from the N-player games to the MFG. The main feature of the master equation is that its state variable include a probability measure, so it can be viewed as a PDE on the Wasserstein space (an infinite dimensional space of Borel probability measures). Though many serious efforts on the study of master equations have been made in the past years, due to the technical reasons the studies of the master equation with arbitrary time duration are limited to the case that the Hamiltonians are separable. In fact, it is very natural to consider non-separable Hamiltonians for MFG problems since usually the control of each player depends on the distribution of the other players or/and the distribution of the other players' strategies because of resource limitation. There are many MFG models in economics and finance, and also MFGs of congestion where the Hamiltonians are in general non-separable. However the general theory for master equations with non-separable Hamiltonians seems missing in the literature. Our current proposed project is devoted to the systematic study of master equations with non-separable Hamiltonians and their applications in MFGs (especially in showing some convergence results from the N-player games to the MFG). The key is to provide certain monotonicity condition for the non-separable Hamiltonians. A mean field game is described through a mean field game system, a forward-backward system of mean field stochastic differential equations (SDEs) or equivalently of (stochastic) partial differential equations (SPDEs). Monotonicity conditions ensure that this system admits a unique solution. 由Caines-Huang-Malhame和Lasry-Lions獨立發起的平均場博弈論是研究在人口群體中的玩家以某種對稱方式互動的戰略決策。平均場博弈論是通過將玩家數量變為無窮大並用統計量代替樣本量來進行研究。在平均場博弈中的每個玩家都會以最大程度降低自己成本來決定自己的策略。他們的策略會影響博弈的受控動態。在過去的十年中，平均場博弈論受到了極大的關注。它們具有廣泛的應用程序，包括人群運動模型，經濟增長模型，石油生產模型，金融模型等。 主方程是平均場博弈論中的一個強大工具，其作用類比於一般偏微分方程在經典控制/博弈論的作用。例如，主方程在構造平均場博弈論中的閉環納什均衡，並在從多人博弈到平均場博弈的收斂性的研究中起著至關重要的作用。主方程的主要特徵是其狀態變量包含概率測度變量，因此可以將其視為在Wasserstein空間（無窮維的Borel概率測度的空間）上的偏微分方程。儘管在過去的幾年中主方程的研究有許多進展，但是由於技術原因，對主方程的研究僅限於哈密頓量可分離的情形。實際上，對於平均場博弈論中的問題哈密頓量是天然不可分的，因為通常每個玩家的控制都取決於其他玩家的分佈或其他玩家策略的分佈。在經濟學和金融學中的很多平均場博弈模型和很多擁堵平均場博弈模型中，哈密頓量一般是不可分的。然而，過去對於具有不可分哈密頓量的主方程的理論研究是空白的。 我們當前提出的項目致力於系統性研究具有不可分哈密頓量的主方程及其在平均場博弈論中的應用。其中的關鍵是提出對不可分哈密頓量的單調性條件。平均場博弈是通過一個正倒向平均場博弈系統，該系統可為平均場隨機微分方程或為（隨機）偏微分方程。單調性條件可確保該系統存在唯一解。

21302521.label: Major findings and research outcome
21302521.value: Major findings and research outcome in Objective 1: The PI began by extending monotonicity conditions to accommodate non-separable Hamiltonians. Using these new conditions, we established an essential a priori Lipschitz estimate for the master equation's solutions under both individual and common noises. This estimate was then applied in extending local solutions to a global one. As a direct consequence, we also established the global well-posedness of the corresponding mean field game system. In summary, Objective 1 has been fully achieved. Major findings and research outcome in Objective 2: The PI first characterized an appropriate notion of weak solutions for the master equation using forward-backward stochastic differential equations. We then established the key prerequisite for global well-posedness with Lipschitz continuous data: an a priori Lipschitz estimate for these weak solutions in the probability measure variable. This estimate ultimately enabled the extension of local weak solutions to a global one, thereby establishing the global well-posedness of the master equation for non-smooth data. In summary, Objective 2 has been fully achieved. Major findings and research outcome in Objective 3: The PI leveraged the convexity of the Hamiltonian and the terminal cost to derive an a priori convexity estimate for the solution, implying a lower bound of zero on its second-order derivative. By then applying the standard semi-concavity estimate from control theory, we established a corresponding upper bound. This two-sided control of the solution's regularity was the key to restoring compactness in the state space—a property absent due to the lack of individual noise. This approach ultimately enabled us to demonstrate global well-posedness for the master equation with degenerate noises and non-smooth data, thereby fully achieving Objective 3.

21302521.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21302521.value: Potential for further development of the research: Currently, the global well-posedness of the master equation is only established under specific monotonicity conditions, such as those of Lasry-Lions, displacement, and anti-monotonicity. These are known to be sufficient. However, it is also well-known that without such conditions, the equation is generally ill-posed over long time horizons. Consequently, identifying the necessary and sufficient conditions for well-posedness is the primary goal for our future research. Proposed course of action: The master equation is always locally well-posed. However, extending this solution globally is based on our ability to bound the Lions derivative of the solution and prevent its divergence. The purpose of all known monotonicity conditions is precisely to enforce such a bound. In the further development, we will investigate the evolution of the solution's Lions derivative along its characteristic curves. By identifying the specific term that drives its growth, we will derive a necessary and sufficient condition to control the derivative, thereby establishing the global well-posedness.

21302521.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21302521.value: This research successfully created a set of mathematical strategies to ensure that complex models of interacting systems produce stable, long-term forecasts, even when faced with significant challenges. The PI developed new ways to prove that a model's solution remains well-behaved and doesn't spiral out of control over time. We achieved this by first adapting existing rules to handle systems with random enviroment, then by inventing a more flexible concept of a "solution" to work with non-smooth data, and finally by using the system's features to maintain control in the worst scenarios. By guaranteeing this stability, we were able to combine short-term predictions into reliable, global solutions for a wide range of previously unsolvable problems.

21302721.label: Project Objectives
21302721.value: Development of comprehensive theory for resonant nonlinear spectroscopic probes with quantum light. Particularly, we will (i) Develop the microscopic theory for quantum nonlinear coherent spectroscopic signals, using the real-time Green’s function technique; (ii) Elaborate the generic relationship between the resonant quantum probes and microscopic dynamics of molecules in nanoscale. In particular, we will essentially designate the signals using quantum-light probes to track the dynamical information of molecules we are interested in. Development of resonant incoherent signals using multi-photon counting for molecular polaritons. Particularly, we will (i) Extend the results and approaches obtained in Objective 1, to develop resonant incoherent nonlinear spectroscopic probes with time- and frequency-gated photon-coincidence counting; (ii) Study the spectroscopic applications of post selection of photon emissions; (iii) Investigate the resonant multi-photon coincidence counting signals for resolving the cooperativity and the entanglement in molecular polaritons. Effective theory for polaritonic relaxation of molecules in condensed phase. Particularly, we will (i) Develop the effective theory for the cooperative dynamics of molecules strongly interacting with the photons in confined geometry, i.e., electromagnetic nanostructure and microcavities; (ii) Explore the theoretical approaches including the modified Redfield equation and the quantum Langevin equation for molecular polaritons; (iii) Apply to long-range coherence in cooperative electron transfer. Quantum-light resonant signal analysis of molecular dynamical processes. Particularly, we will (i) Study the spectroscopic features of the microscopic dynamics obtained in Objective 3; (ii) Explore how to improve the selectivity and resolution of the information as wanted, through the new control knobs, i.e., entangled time and squeezing, provided by the quantum states of light; (iii) Explore the time-resolved resonant signals with nonlinear interferometry.

Particularly, we will (i) Extend the results and approaches obtained in Objective 1, to develop resonant incoherent nonlinear spectroscopic probes with time- and frequency-gated photon-coincidence counting; (ii) Study the spectroscopic applications of post selection of photon emissions; (iii) Investigate the resonant multi-photon coincidence counting signals for resolving the cooperativity and the entanglement in molecular polaritons.

Effective theory for polaritonic relaxation of molecules in condensed phase. Particularly, we will (i) Develop the effective theory for the cooperative dynamics of molecules strongly interacting with the photons in confined geometry, i.e., electromagnetic nanostructure and microcavities; (ii) Explore the theoretical approaches including the modified Redfield equation and the quantum Langevin equation for molecular polaritons; (iii) Apply to long-range coherence in cooperative electron transfer.

Quantum-light resonant signal analysis of molecular dynamical processes. Particularly, we will (i) Study the spectroscopic features of the microscopic dynamics obtained in Objective 3; (ii) Explore how to improve the selectivity and resolution of the information as wanted, through the new control knobs, i.e., entangled time and squeezing, provided by the quantum states of light; (iii) Explore the time-resolved resonant signals with nonlinear interferometry.

21302721.value: 基于量子力学规律的微观粒子展现出鬼魅般的性质，其中一个显著的特征就是光子间的纠缠。这引起了一些领域的兴趣：保密通讯、计算和材料探测。更多地，光量子态的非经典谱性质一直被认为是量子优化应用的潜在力量。近期大量的研究已经证实纠缠光子具有提高灵敏度和信噪比的优势。 尽管已有的研究给出利用量子特性优化材料探测的一些远景，量子光仍然被认作是光谱学中的“量子空白”。这是因为传统光谱学的研究目标与量子光学不同。材料特性的光谱研究因此会不可避免地受限于所使用的经典光场。经典光脉冲存在分辨率和灵敏度的局限，进而成为未来光谱技术发展的主要瓶颈。本项目的目标在于通过发展复杂分子体系的新型量子非线性光谱来突破该瓶颈，因为光量子态为光谱技术提供了新奇的控制参数如纠缠时间和压缩比。另一方面，本项目将利用格林函数技术发展完整的非线性信号的理论，以期能够纳入复杂的分子动力学。作为提高分辨率和灵敏度的新探测方案的一部分，我们将进一步结合非线性干涉方法。这里核心的挑战是多粒子及强光-物质耦合效应导致的非线性，进而需要超越分子的三阶响应的知识内容。为此目的，并考虑到分子与光学微腔/纳米电磁结构强耦合导致的极化激元效应，我们需要在本项目中发展非微扰方法。另一方面，本项目将着重探索分子极化激元的弛豫以及电子的超快动力学，特别是对于存在非均匀退相干和多粒子激发所致的非线性的情况。作为理解纳米尺度下分子弛豫的重要组成部分，我们将发展一类量子非线性光谱技术用来在时域上捕获分子极化激元的动力学。 未来本项目成果将是发展出原则上可行的量子非线性光谱技术，进而大大突破经典光谱技术带来的时间-频率分辨以及灵敏度极限。我们希望揭示纳米材料中电子和分子振动的新效应。这些将会极大地推进纳米光学及微观物质量子成像领域的发展。

21302821.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21302821.value: Photoelectrochemical (PEC) solar water splitting can directly converts solar energy into chemical fuel, which is however limited by its lower efficiency compared to current solar cell technologies. Finding the suitable light-harvesting semiconductors as photoelectrode holds the key towards high-performance PEC water splitting. The key requirements for semiconductors include suitable bandgap, efficient charge separation, high charge transport, high charge transfer kinetics at the semiconductor-electrolyte interface (SEI) and good stability. Recently, two-dimensional (2D) transition metal dichalcogenide (TMDs) have gaining increasing interest in solar energy conversion owing to their strong light-matter interaction, diverse and tuneable electronic structures, high carrier mobility, and more importantly, efficient charge separation and transport, which readily fulfil most of the requirements. Due to the generally low-quality of wet-chemistry-based TMDs which are often associated with defects, mixed crystal phases, and complex interfaces, it is highly desirable to investigate the PEC activities of TMD nanosheets at individual nanosheet level. On-chip electrochemical microdevice is an emerging interdisciplinary platform that shows remarkable advantages in probing complex electrochemical interfaces at microscopic level, which are often inaccessible to conventional electrochemical methods. In this project, we aim to establish a universal on-chip platform of photoelectrochemical microdevices (PEMs) which integrates electronic device with high-precision PEC measurements. Hybrid optoelectronic and PEC measurements will be employed to investigate the PEC solar water splitting of 2D TMD semiconductors and their van der Waals heterostructures (vdWHs). By ensuring an optimal electrical contact via contact engineering and in-situ electrical measurements, we aim to find the intrinsic PEC performance of TMD nanosheets for both hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) and oxygen evolution reaction (OER) in a half-cell setup. The influence of thickness, defects, co-catalyst, and backgate modulation of TMD nanosheet, as well as the operational stability will be studied. In addition, we will investigate the PEC activities of vdWH, a very promising superstructure, that offers freedom in superlattice structure, atomically smooth interface for efficient charge separation, short carrier diffusion length, and tuneable band structures. Last, we will realise high-resolution and scanning probe-free PEC mapping technique that is especially desirable for investigating the PEC activities of 2D nanosheets and vdWHs. Instead of aiming at high performance, this project will advance our understanding of the PEC mechanism and decouple the important fundamentals of SEI under light. And hopefully, we will uncover key characteristics that bottleneck the efficiency of current PEC technologies and pave way for their practical application. 21303221.value: 研究摘要 作為防曬霜的有效成分，每年有超過14,000噸有機紫外防曬劑在使用過程中被釋放到海洋環境中。有報道顯示在某些海灘及汙水中的防曬劑濃度可高達數百微克每升。某些防曬劑亦是內分泌幹擾物。此外，防曬劑在紫外線照射下所產生的光解產物可能具有未知的毒理特性。防曬劑逐漸升高的環境濃度將會對海岸生態環境造成潛在的危害。 當前針對防曬劑的生態毒理學研究大多基於淡水魚類模型，甚少有基於海洋生物的研究。在環境相關的條件下，對防曬劑的光解反應及其產物的研究亦不多。更為重要的是，當前針對防曬劑的生態毒理學風險評估並沒有考慮其自然光解產物，亦無考慮紫外線及光氧化加劇其生態毒性的可能性。此類針對防曬劑的認識盲區，可能會削弱環境風險評估的可靠性，低估防曬劑的環境危害。 本項目著重研究兩款常見的防曬劑，二苯酮-3(BP-3)及甲氧基肉桂酸辛酯(EHMC)。我們預期使用細胞實驗及海洋魚類模型暴露實驗，詳細研究BP-3及EHMC在自然條件下的光解產物及內分泌幹擾效應。我們將首先使用紫外、過氧化氫體系模擬自然條件下的自由基光解反應過程，並運用細胞實驗，從時間架構上解析其光解產物的發生過程及相應的內分泌幹擾毒性。而後，通過海水青鳉的魚卵及成魚暴露實驗，運用基因轉錄組及組織學方法解析本體及光解產物混合物的毒理特征。 綜上，本項研究結合光化學及生態毒理學手段，深入探究防曬劑BP-3及EHMC的環境風險，重點關註其光解條件下的環境轉化，及其產物的內分泌幹擾毒性。本項研究的成果將會為防曬劑的風險評估提供關鍵信息，以便我們更好地保護海洋生態環境。本項研究亦可促進針對新興有機汙染物自由基光氧化方面的相關研究。

21304421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21304421.value: Solid particles can assemble at the interface between two immiscible liquids, thereby reducing the interfacial energy. This phenomenon has drawn much attention in the past two decades owing to the fast development of nanotechnology. It is believed that the use of nanoparticle (NP) self-assembly is a promising method for fabricating large-scale and defect-free 2D and 3D hierarchical functional and structural materials. Moreover, rich behavior is exhibited during the self-assembly process of NPs at the liquid interface owing to complex energy landscapes associated. Therefore, understanding the self-assembly of NPs at the liquid interface is of great interest to both academia and industry. However, the lack of experimental methods to directly image NPs assembled at the liquid interface with good spatial and temporal resolution hinders the understanding of this important phenomenon at the single-particle level. This proposed project will aim to explore the use of in situ atomic force microscopy (AFM) to directly image the self-assembly process of NPs at the water–oil interface with spatial and temporal resolution. Specifically, we will first put effort into conducting time-resolved AFM on NPs assembled at the water–oil interface in situ. We will then apply time-resolved AFM to a model system including hydrophilic charged NPs and oil-soluble surfactants with opposite polarity. This model system has been demonstrated to be highly tunable and non-equilibrium, thereby exhibiting rich behavior. We will systematically study the adsorption kinetics of NPs to the water–oil interface and the in-plane dynamics of NPs at the water–oil interface. The successful completion of the proposed project will provide new insights into the self-assembly process of NPs at the liquid interface at the single-particle level, particularly for systems trapped in non-equilibrium states. It will also encourage more researchers to consider the use of AFM to study the self-assembly of various nanomaterials at the liquid interface, including 2D superlattices, 2D polymers, and 2D transition metals, among others. We envision that with the combination of ultra-fast AFM imaging techniques, the in situ liquid interfacial imaging system will ultimately provide exceptional spatial and temporal resolution, thereby enabling us to capture unprecedented details of the self-assembly of nanomaterials at liquid interfaces. 固体颗粒可以在两相不混溶液界面聚集，从而降低界面能。由于纳米技术的迅速发展，这一现象在过去的二十年中引起了极大的关注。人们普遍认为利用纳米粒子自组装是一种制备大尺度、无缺陷 2D 、3D多级功能、结构材料的有效方法。另一方面，由于复杂的相互作用力，纳米粒子在液体界面的自组装表现出了丰富的物理学行为。因此，学术界和工业界都对纳米粒子在液体界面的自组装产生了浓厚的兴趣。目前，由于缺乏高时-空分辨的成像方法，我们对于纳米粒子在液体界面自组装行为的理解还远远不够，特别是在单粒子层面。 本项目旨在探索利用原子力显微镜(AFM)直接对水-油界面处纳米粒子的自组装过程进行原位成像。具体来说，我们将探索开发利用AFM对水-油界面自组装进行具有时-空分辨的成像方法。我们将选用具有相反极性的亲水性带电纳米粒子和油溶性表面活性剂为研究模型，并对该系统开展原位AFM成像研究。该模型系统已被证明具有较高的可调性和非平衡性，因此具有丰富的物理学行为。我们将系统地研究包括纳米粒子在水-油界面的吸附动力学和纳米粒子在水-油界面的面内动力学。 该项目的成功实施将从单粒子层面对纳米粒子在液体界面的自组装提供新的理解，特别是处于非平衡态的系统。同时，这也将鼓励更多的研究人员使用 AFM 来研究各种纳米材料在液体界面的自组装，包括二维超晶格、二维聚合物和二维过渡金属等。可以想象通过结合超快AFM成像技术，原位液体界面成像系统最终将为我们提供卓越的时-空分辨能力，从而使我们能够捕捉到纳米材料在液体界面自组装过程中前所未有的细节。

21304421.label: Realisation of objectives
21304421.value: In Objective 1, we set out to use time-resolved AFM to probe the self-assembly of nanoparticles (NPs) at liquid interfaces. We designed sample cells and geometries tailored for in situ AFM at liquid–liquid interfaces. We also developed data-analysis protocols for quantitative processing of time-series AFM images. These protocols capture both static structures and dynamic processes. As a result, we can now obtain time-resolved, three-dimensional information on NP assemblies at liquid–liquid interfaces. In Objective 2, we leveraged these advances to probe interfacial assemblies at the single-particle level. We studied NPs at water–oil interfaces, NPs at water–water interfaces, and polymers at water–oil interfaces. Across these investigations, in situ AFM provided unprecedented detail on interfacial structures and dynamics. Consider ferrofluids as an example. These liquids contain magnetic NPs. External magnetic fields can reshape them. Once the field is removed, surface tension smooths the interface. To retain field-programmed shapes, we combined interfacial reshaping with interfacial jamming. Magnetic NPs sculpt the ferrofluid/surrounding-liquid interface under a field. Non-magnetic NPs jam the interface and preserve the shape after the field is removed. AFM resolved the microscopic assemblies at the water–oil interface. These findings guided fine-tuning of ferrofluid compositions and improved performance (Nano Letters 2022, 22 (13), 5538–5543). In another study, we examined gold NPs with cationic polymer surfactants at the water–oil interface. The NPs did not assemble at the interface. Instead, they transferred from water to oil by an unconventional pathway. Surfactants with finite water solubility partition into the aqueous phase. They rapidly adsorb onto negatively charged NPs and neutralize their charge. The NPs first aggregate and transiently accumulate at the interface, where the polymers are compact in water. As the oil phase, a good solvent, promotes expanded polymer conformations, the NPs disperse into the oil as individual particles. This mechanism offers a strategy to transfer large gold NPs across liquid–liquid interfaces. Our in situ AFM identified the dispersion states across phases and clarified the transfer pathway (Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2023, 62 (38), e202308853). Many practical polymers are not interfacially active. We addressed this limitation with a universal strategy that uses tailored “chaperone” solvents. In situ AFM directly visualized polymer assembly at the water–oil interface. The images revealed distinctive spherical aggregates at the water-oil interface (Nature Communications 2024, 15 (1), 7423). We then extended our studies to water–water interfaces formed by liquid–liquid phase separation. This advance enabled progress in all-liquid 3D printing. Conventional all-liquid printing relies on interfacial jamming. That jamming often suppresses cross-interface diffusion. We introduced a dual interfacial-assembly strategy to decouple these functions. One mode ensures jamming and structural integrity. The other independently modulates cross-interface transport. To test this framework, we extended in situ AFM beyond water–oil systems. For the first time, we directly visualized NP assemblies at water–water interfaces. The observed morphologies and interparticle spacings distinguished the two assembly states. These data supported the dual mechanism and enabled optimization of printing parameters (Science Advances 2024, 10 (17), eadk4080). In summary, we achieved our objectives. The in situ, time-resolved AFM platform advances understanding of soft matter assembly at liquid interfaces. It enables quantitative, three-dimensional, single-particle–level insights across diverse interfacial systems.

21304421.label: Major findings and research outcome
21304421.value: In this project, we advanced in situ AFM imaging to reveal nanoscopic details of soft-matter self-assembly at liquid–liquid interfaces. Conventional ferrofluids can be magnetically deformed but lose their programmed shapes once the field is removed. We overcame this limitation by introducing interfacial co-assembly of nanoparticles (NPs): the intrinsic magnetic particles in the ferrofluid enable shape modulation under a field, while added non-magnetic particles assemble at the interface to “lock in” the shape after the field is turned off. The resulting shape reconfigurable ferrofluids can be reprogrammed repeatedly, requiring a magnetic field only during reshaping (Nano Letters 2022, 22, 5538–5543). We further discovered that adding oppositely charged surfactants not only promotes NP assembly at liquid–liquid interfaces but can also drive NP transfer between phases. Contrary to the common view that interfacial aggregation signifies failed phase transfer, we identified an unusual pathway for moving large gold NPs from water to oil: dispersed in water to aggregated at the interface to redispersed as individual particles in oil (Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2023, 62, e202308853). Because many polymers are not inherently interfacially active, we developed a universal interfacial-assembly strategy using a “chaperone” solvent that solvates the target polymer, carries it to the immiscible interface, and enables assembly there; this approach generalizes to virtually any polymer given compatible liquid pairs and an appropriate chaperone solvent (Nature Communications 2024, 15, 7423). Building on dense NP interfacial assemblies for all‑liquid 3D printing, we introduced a dual interfacial‑assembly approach that separates structural jamming from cross-interface transport. One mode preserves mechanical integrity; the other independently controls diffusion. This approach broadened the functionality of all‑liquid 3D printing. In addition, we realized the first AFM imaging of NP self‑assembly at the water–water interface (Science Advances 2024, 10, eadk4080). We also reviewed recent advances in soft‑matter self‑assembly at liquid–liquid interfaces (J. Mater. Chem. A 2023, 11, 21009–21028; Nano Today 2024, 54, 102073).

21304421.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21304421.value: The successful completion of this project led to the advancement of our in situ AFM imaging technique that allows us to directly visualize the self-assembly of soft matter at liquid–liquid interfaces. In the future, we will further advance our in situ AFM method to achieve better performance—for example, higher spatial and temporal resolution and expanded mechanical measurement capabilities. In addition, we will use the understanding we have gained to guide more practical applications based on the self-assembly of soft matter at liquid–liquid interfaces.

21304421.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21304421.value: When two liquids don’t mix—like oil and water—they form a boundary called a liquid–liquid interface, where many materials gather and organize, either naturally or with assistance. This phenomenon is important in industries such as food production, petroleum processing, cosmetics, and medicine, so understanding how materials assemble at liquid–liquid interfaces matters. We developed an in situ AFM imaging technique that lets us watch nanometer-scale materials assemble directly at the interface in real time—something standard optical or electron microscopes cannot do. Using this capability, we have gained a much deeper understanding of interfacial behavior and are translating it into practical “all-liquid” technologies, such as ferrofluids that retain patterned shapes even without an external magnetic field and all-liquid structures with tunable permeability printed inside another immiscible liquid. These advances open the door to new materials and devices made entirely from liquids.

21501821.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21501821.value: In some occasions, classified information about new products may be leaked to the public via online forums or news websites before the products are officially introduced. For example, more than 2 months before the planned release for iPhone 12 by Apple in October 2020, information about the product line-up, features, prices, and tentative launch dates were already circulating online (Entrepreneur 2020). I refer to this phenomenon as product leak announcements. Product leaks are typically viewed negatively, and companies often go to great lengths to prevent such leaks. For example, Apple operates a “Worldwide Loyalty Team”, consisting of undercover agents who pose as normal employees to identify suspects who leak new product information to outsiders (Apple Insider 2009). Attempts to prevent product leaks are not isolated to the consumer electronics industry - automobile companies often camouflage their new car models when they drive them out for test runs to prevent design features from being leaked (Autoblog 2014). Despite the aversion towards product leaks, its actual impact on businesses has not been empirically examined from a marketing perspective. For example, it is possible that product leak announcements may generate more anticipation and interest in the unreleased products. Conversely, product leak announcements may also take away the excitement and novelty when the products are subsequently introduced, resulting in lower product demand. The present research aims to help companies understand how product leak announcements affect online word-of-mouth, consumer demand, and firm value (i.e., three separate studies). In addition, the research will also examine how these impact vary based on characteristics of the announcement (i.e., type of information leaked, source of leak, timing) and leaked product (i.e., incremental vs radical innovation, stage of production). A better understanding of these factors would help companies plan their course of action in the event of a product leak. Findings from this research may also have important implications for hiring employees and sourcing for manufacturing partners. The impact of product leak announcements would be investigated using real-world data. Product leak announcements from relevant websites, forums, and social media will be collected, and this will be combined with online word-of-mouth, product sales, and financial data. An instrumental variable approach will be used to address endogeneity issues due to unobservable confounding factors, and some supply chain variables (e.g., number of manufacturing partners / employees) are proposed as instruments. 在某些情况下，新产品的机密信息可能会在产品正式推出之前通过在线论坛或新闻网站泄露给公众。例如，在 Apple 计划于 2020 年 10 月发布 iPhone 12 之前的两个多月，有关产品阵容、功能、价格和暂定发布日期的信息已经在网上流传（Entrepreneur 2020）。我将这种现象称为产品泄漏公告。 产品泄漏通常被认为是负面的，而且公司通常会竭尽全力防止此类泄漏。例如，Apple 运营着一个“全球忠诚团队”，由伪装成普通员工的卧底特工组成，以识别向外界泄露新产品信息的嫌疑人（Apple Insider 2009）。尝试防止产品泄漏并非仅限于消费电子行业 - 汽车公司也经常在新款车试运行时对汽车外观进行伪装，以防止设计功能泄漏（Autoblog 2014）。 虽然产品泄漏有一定的负面印痕, 从营销角度来说，它对企业的影响还未进行实际的检验。例如，产品泄漏公告可能会引起对产品的加强期待和兴趣。相反的，产品泄漏公告也可能会带走产品随后推出时的兴奋和新颖性，从而导致产品需求下降。 本研究旨在帮助公司了解产品泄漏公告如何影响在线口碑、消费者需求和公司价值（i.e., 三项独立研究）。此外，研究还将考察这些以下因素如何的影响变化 - 例如公告的特征（i.e., 泄露的信息类型、泄露源、时间）和泄露的产品（i.e., 增量创新与激进创新、生产阶段） 。更好的了解这些因素将有助于公司计划在发生产品泄漏时的行动方案。这项研究的结果也可能对雇用员工和寻找制造合作伙伴具有重要意义。 使用真实数据考察产品泄漏公告的具体影响, 这项研究将收集相关网站、论坛和社交媒体的产品泄漏公告，并结合在线口碑、产品销售和财务数据。

21502921.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21502921.value: Network analysis has become a popular research area over the past few years, with applications and contributions from many disciplines including statistics, computer science, social sciences, physics and biology. Bipartite graphs are popular data in many fields, such as recommendation system, statistical physics, proteomic parsimony. In this project, we propose to study a fundamental concentration inequality on bipartite graphs, then apply the theoretical result to a series of statistical models, with application to various fields. The random matrix theory on unipartite networks has been well studied, but the application of the existing results on bipartite graphs usually gives suboptimal results. Therefore, we will develop some fundamental concentration inequalities on random bipartite graphs. Our proving skills will based on classical techniques on sparse random graph and recent development in Hanson-Wright inequality. Furthermore, we will apply the concentration inequality for random bipartite graphs on statistical learning in bipartite networks. We will focus on subspace estimation, Bernoulli mixture models and stochastic block models. Our goal is to obtain optimal error rates using appropriate algorithms for different tasks. 網絡分析在過去幾年已成為一個熱門的研究領域，其應用和貢獻來自許多學科，包括統計學、計算機科學、社會科學、物理學和生物學。二部圖是許多領域的流行數據，例如推薦系統、統計物理學、蛋白質組學簡約。在這個項目中，我們建議研究二部圖上的基本濃度不等式，然後將理論結果應用於一系列統計模型，並應用於各個領域。 單部網絡上的隨機矩陣理論已經得到很好的研究，但是將現有結果應用於二部圖通常會給出次優結果。因此，我們將在隨機二部圖上開發一些基本的集中不等式。我們的證明技巧將基於稀疏隨機圖的經典技術和 Hanson-Wright 不等式的最新發展。 此外，我們將隨機二部圖的濃度不等式應用於二部網絡中的統計學習。我們將專注於子空間估計、伯努利混合模型和隨機塊模型。我們的目標是使用適合不同任務的算法獲得最佳錯誤率。

21502921.label: Realisation of objectives
21502921.value: This project has made significant progress towards achieving the original objectives outlined in section 5.1, with some modifications based on insights gained during the research process. Objective 1: Concentration of bipartite random graphs We have successfully shown that bipartite random graphs concentrate near their expectation under mild assumptions on the sparsity and parameters of the graph. By adapting techniques from the classical proof of concentration for random graphs and leveraging recent advances in sparse Hanson-Wright inequalities, we derived novel concentration inequalities tailored to the bipartite setting. These results provide a solid theoretical foundation for the subsequent objectives. Objective 2: Regularization procedure for sparsity Building upon the concentration results from Objective 1, we developed a new regularization procedure to mitigate the stringent conditions on graph sparsity required for desirable concentration properties. The key idea is to judiciously modify the graph parameters in a data-driven manner to ensure concentration holds. We proposed and analyzed algorithms for automatically determining the optimal regularization parameters based on the observed graph structure. Empirical evaluations on both synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in handling sparse bipartite graphs. Objective 3: Improved subspace estimation We applied the proof techniques and concentration inequalities derived for bipartite random graphs to the problem of subspace estimation. By carefully exploiting the bipartite structure, we obtained improved error rates compared to existing results in the literature. Under certain assumptions on the parameter space, we proved that our estimator achieves the minimax optimal rate. These theoretical advances lead to more sample-efficient and accurate algorithms for subspace estimation in practice. Objective 4: Spectral algorithms for mixture models We developed spectral algorithms for learning parameters in Bernoulli mixture models and bipartite stochastic block models. By leveraging the concentration properties of the adjacency matrix and optimizing the choice of tuning parameters, our algorithms achieve minimax optimal misclassification rates under suitable identifiability conditions. Extensive numerical simulations corroborate the theoretical findings and showcase the superiority of our approach over competing methods in a wide range of parameter regimes. In summary, this project has largely fulfilled its original objectives, with the results obtained under each objective either meeting or exceeding our initial expectations. The only minor deviation was in Objective 2, where in addition to the proposed regularization procedure, we also developed data-driven algorithms for parameter tuning, which were not explicitly mentioned in the original objective but arose naturally during the course of research. Despite the technical challenges posed by the intricate probabilistic analysis required for deriving concentration inequalities and minimax rates, we were able to overcome these hurdles through a combination of novel proof techniques, careful optimizer design, and empirical validation. The project outcomes advance our understanding of bipartite graph models and provide principled methods with theoretical guarantees for learning in these structured domains.
