21502921.label: Major findings and research outcome
21502921.value: This project has yielded several significant findings and research outcomes in the study of bipartite random graphs and their applications to subspace estimation and mixture models. First, we established concentration inequalities for bipartite random graphs, showing that the graph concentrates around its expectation under mild assumptions (see Section 5.3, Objective 1). This theoretical result lays the foundation for subsequent developments and provides valuable insights into the behavior of these graphs. Second, we proposed a novel regularization procedure to handle sparse bipartite graphs that may violate the concentration conditions (Section 5.3, Objective 2). Our data-driven approach for tuning regularization parameters has been empirically validated and offers a principled way to ensure concentration properties hold in practice. Third, we made significant progress in subspace estimation by leveraging the concentration results for bipartite graphs (Section 5.3, Objective 3). Our estimator achieves improved error rates and minimax optimality under certain assumptions, advancing the state-of-the-art in this important problem. Fourth, we developed spectral algorithms with minimax optimal misclassification rates for learning parameters in Bernoulli mixture models and bipartite stochastic block models (Section 5.3, Objective 4). These algorithms demonstrate superior performance compared to existing methods, as corroborated by extensive numerical simulations. In terms of research outcomes, this project has resulted in several high-quality publications in top-tier machine learning and statistics venues, including NeurIPS and ICLR (see Part C for details). The PI and collaborators have also been invited to present the work at major international workshops and seminars, indicating the impact and recognition of the project within the research community. The outcomes of this project have potential implications beyond the immediate scope of bipartite graphs. The concentration inequalities and proof techniques we developed can be readily adapted to other graph-structured domains, while the regularization procedures and learning algorithms can inform the design of principled methods for related problems involving sparsity and mixture models. Overall, this project has substantially advanced our understanding of bipartite random graphs and their applications, opening up new avenues for future research at the intersection of graph theory, statistical learning, and algorithmic design.

21502921.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21502921.value: The research outcomes of this project open up several promising directions for further development. One potential avenue is to extend the concentration results and regularization techniques to more general classes of random graphs, such as multi-partite graphs or graphs with weighted edges. This would require non-trivial modifications to the current proof techniques and algorithms, but could lead to a unified framework for handling concentration and sparsity in a wider range of graph-structured problems. Another direction is to explore the application of our methods to real-world datasets arising from domains such as social networks, recommendation systems, and bioinformatics. By collaborating with domain experts and industry partners, we can adapt and scale up our algorithms to tackle large-scale problems and validate their effectiveness in practical settings. This could also inspire new research questions and methodological challenges grounded in real-world applications. From a theoretical perspective, it would be interesting to investigate the fundamental limits of parameter estimation and learning in bipartite graph models, beyond the specific settings considered in this project. This may involve developing new information-theoretic lower bounds, characterizing the optimal rates of convergence, and designing adaptive algorithms that can achieve these optimal rates without prior knowledge of the model parameters.

21502921.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21502921.value: This research project focuses on understanding the behavior of bipartite random graphs, which are mathematical objects that model relationships between two distinct groups of entities. For example, bipartite graphs can represent connections between customers and products they purchase, or between movies and viewers who rate them. The project aims to uncover fundamental properties of these graphs and develop efficient algorithms for learning hidden patterns within them. One key contribution of this project is the development of concentration inequalities, which provide mathematical guarantees on how closely a bipartite graph resembles its expected structure. These results are crucial for ensuring the reliability and accuracy of algorithms that operate on these graphs. The project also proposes novel techniques for handling sparse graphs, where only a small fraction of potential connections are present, by carefully adjusting the graph parameters. The findings of this project have significant implications for a wide range of applications, such as recommender systems, social network analysis, and gene expression studies. By providing a rigorous theoretical foundation and practical algorithms for bipartite graph analysis, this research enables more accurate and efficient methods for uncovering meaningful insights from complex relational data, ultimately benefiting both businesses and consumers in data-driven decision making.

21503721.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21503721.value: Social learning refers to situations in which individuals draw inference from other individuals' actions to learn about an underlying state of the world. The classic literature on social learning assumes that individuals have a correct understanding of their environment. However, growing empirical evidence shows that individuals are subject to systematic misperceptions of the external environment. For example, consumers may misinterpret the interests or tastes of other consumers, and investors may over- or under-estimate the returns of financial securities. A burgeoning theoretical literature demonstrated that certain types of misperceptions can cause large inefficiencies in social learning. This recent literature focuses on a stylized model in which individuals have perfect information about the actions of all other individuals. In practice, however, individuals have complex and imperfect information about others' actions. For instance, consumers consult bestseller lists to learn about other consumers' purchase decisions, and investors use aggregate financial statistics to infer other investors' investment choices. In order to understand and regulate these markets, it is important to study the joint impact of misperception and imperfect information on social learning. This requires us to move beyond the literature’s simple stylized model with perfect information. In the proposed project, I will develop a general framework to understand how imperfect information and misperception jointly impact social learning. I will provide a unified theory on the dynamics and long-run outcome of social learning, putting little restriction on the specific forms of the individuals' misperception and imperfect information. Three earlier studies, including one by the PI, have examined the role of imperfect information in classic social learning models, which involves individuals accurately understanding their environment. However, no study has analyzed the role of imperfect information in social learning when individuals also have misperceptions. More specificly, I will first compare the model of the proposed project with existing models in the literature which analyses misperception under perfect information. The preliminary results show that learning dynamics exhibit fundamentally different properties in our framework. In particular, a new class of learning dynamics referred to as "incomplete learning" may emerge in our model, but it is impossible to occur in the existing models with perfect information. Then, I will examine different forms of imperfect information and misperception to identify general patterns of social learning in our framework. Ultimately, I seek a unified characterization to classify social learning environments in terms of the induced learning outcomes. “社会学习”是指个人从其他人的行为中推断出世界的潜在状态的情况。关于社会学习的经典文献假设个人对他们的环境有正确的理解。然而，越来越多的经验证据表明，个人经常对外部环境有系统性的“误解”。例如，消费者可能会误解其他消费者的兴趣或品味，投资者可能会高估或低估金融证券的回报。新兴的理论文献表明，某些类型的误解会导致社会学习效率低下。这些新兴理论文献的研究都是基于一个简化的模型。在该模型中，个人拥有关于其他个人行为的完美信息。然而，在实践中，个人对他人的行为有“不完善的信息”。例如，书籍的消费者可能仅能通过查阅畅销书排行榜以了解有限的关于其他消费者买书决定的信息，投资者也许仅能使用金融统计数据来推断其他投资者的投资选择。因此，为了理解这些市场中的社会学习，我们需要研究“误解”和“不完善信息”两者如何同时对“社会学习”的产生影响。这要求我们超越具有“完美信息”的文献的简单程式化模型。在拟议的项目中，我将开发一个通用框架，以了解“不完美的信息”和“误解”如何共同影响“社会学习”。我将提供关于社会学习的动态和长期结果的理论。三项较早的研究，包括一项由本人进行的研究，讨论了当个人对外部环境没有误解时，“不完美信息”对社会学习的作用。然而，目前还没有研究分析“不完善信息”和"误解"同时存在时会如何影响社会学习。为研究这一课题，我会将拟议项目的模型与文献中分析完美信息下的误解的现有模型进行比较。初步结果表明，社会学习在我的框架中表现出不同的特性：我的模型中可能会出现一类新的学习动态，称为“不完全学习”，但在现有模型中不会出现。以此为出发点，我将检查不同形式的不完善信息和误解对社会学习的影响，以确定我们框架中社会学习的一般模式并根据其特征对个人的信息和对外部环境的误解进行分类。

21504421.label: Project Objectives
21504421.value: The first objective of this project will be to jointly study the cyclicality of excess return expectations of individual investors and professional forecasters implied by survey forecasts in major asset classes, including equity, Treasury bonds, foreign exchange, and commodities. The cylicality of excess return expectations is a key moment in asset-pricing models. Leading rational expectations asset-pricing models typically generate strongly countercyclical excess return expectations. In these models, the representative agent is assumed to be perfectly aware of the objective law of motion regarding the underlying data generating process. The second objective of this project is to study the cyclicality of out-of-sample excess return forecasts, which may serve as a better benchmark of rational forecasts to compare cyclicality than in-sample forecasts. 21504421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21504421.value: Several stylized facts have been established regarding currency excess returns. First, the uncovered interest rate parity (UIP) condition is strongly violated, meaning that currencies with higher than average interest rates in the cross-section do not depreciate, but rather appreciate (Hansen and Hodrick 1980; Fama 1984). Second, average excess returns on a basket of currencies display predictably countercyclical variation (Lustig et al. 2014). This proposed project is the first to show that both stylized facts can be explained with a learning model, which also generates novel empirical predictions that can be tested using currency pricing and survey data. In the model, the representative agent faces parameter uncertainty and needs to estimate the unconditional mean of consumption growth rates at the country level in real time. As a result, her beliefs about future exchange rates differ from those of an econometrician who analyzes the data ex post, and who knows the true parameter value. The specific learning process used in the learning model is microfounded by the “learning from experience” behavior documented in Malmendier and Nagel (2016), and further developed in Nagel and Xu (2020). In this model, the agent requires a constant risk premium on currencies, and the UIP holds under her subjective expectations. However, her learning process generates persistent expectation errors, and this leads the econometrician to find both predictable variations in realized excess returns and UIP violations ex post. The model also suggests a new predictor of currency excess returns. That predictor will be the difference between the exponentially weighted average of past consumption growth rates in the foreign country and that in the home country, which can be constructed with the estimated learning parameter from survey data. I will test these predictions using professional forecasts on foreign exchange rates from multiple sources. I will also build a structural asset pricing model that quantitatively matches both the magnitude of predictability in currency returns and the empirical patterns found in survey forecasts of exchange rates. Overall, this project aims to deepen our understanding of why currency returns vary over time by studying the dynamics of subjective expectations implied by survey data. 对于外汇风险溢价的研究建立了如下几个经典现象：首先，无抛补利率平价在外汇市场中并不成立，意味着有着高于平均值利率水平的货币在未来通常升值而非贬值 (Hansen and Hodrick 1980; Fama 1984)；其次，外汇平均风险溢价的波动是反周期的 (Lustig et al. 2014)。本项目致力于通过市场参与者对于数据的学习来解释这两个经典现象，并通过模型得到可以用价格数据和问卷调查数据进行实证测试的预测结论。在模型中，参数对于代表性主体投资者有不确定性，并且代表性主体投资者需要实时估计长期平均消费增长率。这一学习过程导致其实时估计与实证者估计产生分歧。本项目使用经历学习这一有着微观支持的学习方式对代表性主题投资者的学习过程进行建模 (Malmendier and Nagel 2016; Nagel and Xu 2021)。在模型中，代表性主体投资者所要求的风险溢价恒常，且无抛补利率评价在其观念中成立。但由于在学习过程中估计错误的持续产生，后验的实证者会在实际报酬率中发现可以预测的波动。该模型也预测一个新的外汇风险溢价的预测因子，即过往利率差的指数平均。最后，本项目会建立一个量化资产定价模型来解释外汇市场中的经典现象和问卷调查数据中的新现象。

rows: This project aims to analyze the cyclicality of excess return expectations held by individual investors and professional forecasters across major asset classes (equity, Treasury bonds, foreign exchange, and commodities). While leading rational expectations asset-pricing models typically assume agents have perfect knowledge and predict countercyclical returns, this assumption is problematic. It presumes an unrealistic level of information availability and conflicts with recent studies showing that actual investor expectations, derived from survey data, often diverge significantly from the predictions of rational expectations models.

The second objective of this project is to study the cyclicality of out-of-sample excess return forecasts, which may serve as a better benchmark of rational forecasts to compare cyclicality than in-sample forecasts. Motivated by the assumption of rational expectations, the standard approach of obtaining excess return expectations is to run an in-sample predictive regression using the full-sample observations of realized excess returns. This is because under rational expectations, realizations of excess returns should not systematically deviate from ex ante excess return expectations and the usage of full-sample data achieves maximum power. However, once we relax the rather strong assumption of rational expectations, in-sample forecasts lead to look-ahead bias and using out-of-sample forecasts alleviates this issue. This project is going to use standard methods from the previous literature to construct out-of-sample forecasts, e.g., combination forecasts.

The third objective is to study which economic quantity can capture the variation in survey-implied excess return expectations. One concern of using survey data is that they may deviate from the actual beliefs of market participants and merely represent noise. If the variation in survey-implied excess return expectations can be linked to meaningful economic quantities, e.g., risk perceptions measured from survey data or derivatives price data, we can address the aforementioned concern. Moreover, this helps us understand the main driving force of investors' ex ante excess return expectations.

In summary, the goal of this project will be to empirically study the properties of excess return expectations implied by forward-looking forecast data in major asset classes. Any pervasive property emerged from this analysis will provide useful guidance for future model building and help understand the main drivers of variation in excess return expectations.

21504421.label: Major findings and research outcome
21504421.value: In this project, we examined the dynamics of subjective risk premia implied by return expectations of individual investors and professionals for portfolios of stocks, bonds, currencies, and commodity futures. Our primary research outcome is the identification of a pervasive discrepancy between objective and subjective risk premia. While in-sample predictive regressions with realized excess returns suggest that objective risk premia vary countercyclically with business-cycle and asset-valuation measures, we found that subjective risk premia extracted from survey data are largely acyclical. This pattern holds true across different surveys, investor types, and asset classes, challenging the common practice in rational expectations models of equating time-variation in objective risk premia with time-varying risk or risk aversion. To explain this lack of cyclicality, we investigated out-of-sample forecasts of excess returns. We found that these forecasts exhibit a similar lack of cyclicality to the survey data, particularly when constructed to reflect fading memory or combination forecasts. This suggests that the gap between objective and subjective measures does not necessarily indicate investor irrationality. Instead, it implies that investors are learning about forecasting relationships and the data-generating process in real time, rather than possessing the perfect knowledge assumed in standard rational expectations frameworks. Furthermore, we established the existence of a subjective risk-return tradeoff. We observed that subjective risk premia are not constant but are positively related to subjective perceptions of risk quantity, such as the perceived variance of stock market returns. However, this variation in subjective risk perceptions is largely orthogonal to the standard cyclical state variables that predict realized returns. Consequently, we conclude that asset pricing models must account for a time-varying beliefs wedge regarding fundamentals—such as future dividend growth or interest rates—to successfully explain the joint stylized facts of volatile asset prices, cyclical objective risk premia, and acyclical subjective risk premia. Our findings support theoretical frameworks where asset price fluctuations are driven by subjective expectations of fundamentals rather than time-varying risk aversion.

21504421.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21504421.value: A potential future course of action is to develop theoretical models that explicitly feature a "beliefs wedge" regarding fundamentals. Specifically, we would like to study how investors generate subjective forecasts of dividend growth and interest rates that differ from objective reality. Empirically, further investigation is required to identify the specific, persistent systematic factors driving subjective risk perceptions, as our findings indicate these are distinct from standard business cycle indicators. Expanding this analysis to include subjective expectations of macroeconomic variables, such as inflation and GDP, would help determine if the observed learning dynamics are universal. Integrating these non-rational expectation mechanisms into macro-finance models will provide a more accurate understanding of asset price volatility and the disconnect between investor psychology and market outcomes.

21504421.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21504421.value: Nature: The study compares what investors say they expect to earn with what statistical models imply across stocks, bonds, currencies, and commodities. It documents a large “cyclicality gap”: while models imply risk premia rise in recessions and fall in booms, investors’ expected excess returns are largely flat over the cycle. Significance: These findings challenge a core assumption in many asset-pricing models that time-varying risk or risk aversion drives cyclical movements in expected returns and thus prices. The pervasive gap across asset classes and investor types suggests standard business-cycle predictors do not meaningfully move people’s beliefs in real time, highlighting the importance of learning and limited memory. Value: The research redirects theory and practice toward models where investors learn and update beliefs about fundamentals rather than relying on time-varying risk aversion. This can improve asset-pricing models, enhance forecasting frameworks used by practitioners, and inform policymakers about how expectations form and propagate through markets.

21504921.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21504921.value: In the era of big data, huge size and variety of available data becomes new norm in many fields of science. Thus they enable researchers to deploy more complicated machine learning algorithms. Tree ensemble methods are one of the most successful machine learning models, as reported in many literatures. Bayesian additive regression tree (BART) is the state-of-the-art tree ensemble algorithm in terms of prediction accuracy and is robust to hyper-parameters. It is well known that tree-based algorithms are prone to overfit the data. Thus regularization of trees is critical for better performance. Intuitively, we conjecture that BART's clever regularization might be behind its remarkable performance. Besides, BART comes with a natural measure of statistical uncertainty while other machine learning methods cannot. Despite these virtues, BART is underutilized by data scientists. One of the main obstacles to wider adoption is that BART fits the model by a random walk Metropolis-Hastings algorithm, which does not scale to data sets with many observations or predictors. On the other hand, alternative tree-based methods such as random forest or gradient boosting fit tree by a fast recursive partition algorithm. Inspired by the observations mentioned above, we ask a question: is it any chance to combine the BART regularization with recursive partition algorithm? The proposed research will develop a new algorithm named accelerate Bayesian additive regression tree (XBART), to combine regularization and stochastic search strategies from Bayesian modeling with computationally efficient techniques from recursive partitioning algorithm. Our plan includes developing algorithm for both regression and classification problems, and application in treatment effect estimation. Besides, we plan to explore the theoretical aspect of the algorithm, try to understand how does it work from the perspective of consistency theory, or Bayesian posterior concentrations. Furthermore, we believe that any machine learning algorithms cannot be useful unless an efficient implementation is available to the public. We will develop optimized, efficient computer software packages for R, Python and Julia, and make it open-source for broader usage. 本項目致力於開發一個新型隨機樹集成算法框架，命名為XBART，應用於回歸、分類和處理效應等機器學習常見問題。XBART綜合了貝葉斯樹集成算法（BART）的正則化和隨機搜索技術，使用了計算更高效的遞歸劃分方法，致力於達到基於樹的機器學習方法中當前最佳的預測、估計和分類準確性。本項目同時考慮應用XBART於處理效應估計問題，綜合XBART和貝葉斯因果森林（Bayesian causal forest）方法估計平均處理效應。

21507721.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21507721.value: Models with heterogeneous investors have the potential to match asset-pricing stylized facts that representative-agent models cannot. Intuitively, investors will value securities differently if they have different beliefs or preferences, and the wealthier one group of investors are, the more power they will have in pricing. The difficulty in modeling models with heterogeneous investors is that one must keep track of individuals' wealth distribution, as the wealth shifts endogenously from one group to another as the natural outcome of trading. It is even more difficult to empirically estimate the model and infer the evolution of the endogenous wealth distribution. This project is the first to estimate a model with heterogeneous beliefs and its time series of the endogenous wealth share to the author's knowledge. The model-implied endogenous wealth share can predict the return correlation between the US treasury bonds and the S&P 500 index. It also predicts the time-varying equity premium. This project then aims to estimate the endogenous wealth shift in financial institutions using survey data. I plan to exploit the panel data of individual forecasts by professional economists in leading financial institutions from the Blue Chip Financial Forecasts. In the estimation, I assume that each financial institution will trade following the forecasts by its economists. Having the estimated panel of endogenous wealth distribution among these financial institutions, I shall perform a similar analysis to see if they collectively predict the correlation between asset returns and the equity premium. We can also directly compare the estimated endogenous wealth distribution with financial institutions' equity distribution as an out of sample test. Since the wealth distribution is an endogenous state variable of the economy, it potentially has a close relation to many finance subjects, including the equity risk premium, bond risk premia, term structure of interest rates, implied volatility, investor sentiment, to name a few. 21508721.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21508721.value: 過去十年見證了槓桿貸款市場的繁榮，其中寬鬆契約貸款（幾乎沒有強制性契約的貸款）的比例顯著增加。寬鬆契約貸款，就發放量而言，現在佔所有槓桿貸款的 80% 以上。此外，寬鬆契約貸款的主導地位似乎對所有目的的貸款都普遍存在。 研究人員試圖找出寬鬆契約槓桿貸款盛行的原因並表示擔憂——槓桿貸款有較高風險（大部分低於投資級別），但寬鬆契約貸款的貸方缺乏可藉以及時重組潛在不良債務的手段。對於寬鬆契約貸款受歡迎，一種流行的解釋是債務投資者放棄契約的強制性以達到更高的投資收益。使用標普提供的槓桿貸款市場的數據，我發現情況並非如此——在控制信用評級、行業年度效應及借款人固定效應後，寬鬆契約貸款的平均利差低於非寬鬆契約貸款。貸款利差似乎也與貸款額度和借款企業規模呈負相關。此外，在寬鬆契約貸款中，如果貸款帶有通常伴隨強制性契約限制的循環信用額度，貸款利差更高，從而使“寬鬆契約”對這些貸款的貸款利差的整體影響微不足道。 這些發現表明，在槓桿貸款市場中使用寬鬆契約的根源在於借款人偏好不受限制的、更便宜的債務，而對於有價值的借款人，債權人會迎合這種偏好。因此，評估不受限制的風險融資帶來的業務運營靈活性的好處以及有限貸方保護的影子成本很重要。目前幾乎沒有對其規模的定量分析，特別是針對其在經濟衰退的情況下。為了填補這個空白，我建立了一個動態模型。在這個模型中，企業需要通過貸款為其業務融資並選擇最優的契約強制類型——在更高的投資靈活性和更高的破產成本之間進行權衡。我依據這個模型在模擬的經濟衝擊情景中量化與“寬鬆契約”相關的價值和成本。

21508721.label: Major findings and research outcome
21508721.value: The major findings are summarized by the two papers listed in Part C. One paper finds that cov-lite loans have a lower spread, a higher credit rating, a higher number of participating investors, and a lower default rate on average, and offers an important but understudied perspective for the explanation for cov-lite loans. Through a calibrated model, the paper also finds that the shadow cost of cov-lite loans on investors due to inefficiencies is 1.9% of their investments. The other paper finds that In the institutional loan market populated by risky borrowers, underwriters compete for underwriter competition significantly affects loan pricing at all stages of syndication: more intense competition leads to lower initial loan spreads, more upward rate adjustments during book-building, and lower final loan spreads in a market segment. The pricing-stage-specific findings indicate that competition among underwriters reduces their bargaining power over borrowers instead of strengthening their certification effect.

21508721.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21508721.value: Although two papers have been produced out of this project, there is potential for further research related to the leveraged loan market using the same data set involved in this project. For example, the borrower's choice of underwriters could be a topic to explore. However, such research would be out of the scope originally defined by the project objectives.

21508721.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21508721.value: The research conducted in this project is centered around the leveraged loan market, which is a risky debt market for firms and is closely linked to the financial health of corporations overall. The research finds that good firms could choose a less restrictive debt contract to signal that their business is more worthy, which is a perspective little studied by the literature on leveraged loans because the literature has focused on the investor's perspective. The research also finds that the competition among loan underwriters is important for determining how costly the loan is. More competition makes loans cheaper, which is an important finding because the conventional wisdom is that risky firms should rely on bank relationships to borrow wisely and bank competition in this case may be bad for them.

21509121.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21509121.value: 行为广告根据消费者的自身特点来选择目标消费者，而情境广告则根据消费者所见所闻来选择目标消费者。在当今的许多网站中，两者的结合 (称为微目标定位) 会用于向消费者提供更富针对性的广告。更精确的定位 (利用消费者的行为数据) 是否能提高抑或损害广告发布商的收入仍然存在争议。业内 (Ravichandran and Nitish, 2019; Lomas, 2019) 和学术界 (Iyer et al., 2005; Levin and Milgrom, 2010) 都存在支持争议双方的证据。然而，直到最近，人们普遍认为，更精准定位的广告应具有更高的转化率，即使在商家收入较低的情况下也应如此。这个想法很简单：随着更多关于消费者的数据可用，广告商和消费者之间的配对应该得到改善。不过，最近的经验性证据指出，与微目标定位广告相比，针对性较低的广告能获得相同甚至更高的转化率 (Snelders et al., 2020)。 在这项研究中，我们提出一个博弈论模型来研究这种现象，并提供了一个理由来解释，为何关闭微目标定位的行为广告的发布商，最终能获得更高的转化率。我们把这种现象与在线广告市场中存在的信息不对称联系起来。如果发布商允许第三方在其网站上收集用户的网站浏览信息数据，那么一些广告商就能获得大型广告交易平台提供的行为数据，而这些数据可能并非所有人都可以使用。此外，有一些广告商则可能没有所需的高级工具去充分利用所有额外数据。我们预测，这种信息不对称会导致市场效率低下。令人惊讶的是，关闭微目标定位能产生更有效率的市场 (更好的配对)，因为这能为每个人提供平等的机会，抗衡目前所有广告商都信息不足的情况。 此项研究能为越来越多的关于定向广告和在线广告拍卖的文献作出贡献。在本提案中，我们提出了一些关于资讯不对称在定向广告中的作用的有趣发现，并强调了它们对在线广告行业的影响。

21509121.label: Realisation of objectives
21509121.value: This project has successfully achieved all the objectives stated in the original application. The research culminated in a paper currently under revision for resubmission following a "reject and resubmit" decision. Below, we detail how each objective was addressed. --- Objective 1: Examine the role of information asymmetry in targeted advertising. The project developed a theoretical model that places information asymmetry at its core. The model distinguishes between "informed" advertisers (those with access to comprehensive consumer data enabling microtargeting) and "uninformed" advertisers (who possess only limited or publicly available data). Our analysis demonstrates that information asymmetry fundamentally shapes bidding behavior and auction outcomes. Specifically, we find that when advertisers have differential access to consumer data, their bidding strategies diverge in systematic ways. The paper characterizes these dynamics formally, showing how asymmetric information can lead to scenarios where high-valuation advertisers underbid (fearing overpayment) and low-valuation advertisers overbid (fearing loss of valuable impressions). Furthermore, our framework differentiates between types of data (behavioral data capturing past activities, preferences, and purchase history, and contextual data relating to content being viewed or device used) and analyze how asymmetries in access to each type affect auction dynamics differently. --- Objective 2: Identify the optimal targeting policies for a publisher under different market conditions. A central contribution of our research is the identification of conditions under which different targeting policies are optimal for publishers. Our findings reveal that the optimal policy depends on two factors: (1) the correlation structure among advertisers' valuations and (2) the degree of information asymmetry present in the market. When advertisers' valuations are positively correlated based on certain consumer data and information asymmetry exists among advertisers, we demonstrate that publishers can improve their revenue by limiting data access and disabling microtargeting. By creating a level playing field where no advertiser has informational advantages, publishers can encourage more competitive bidding, ultimately increasing both revenue and conversion rates. Conversely, when advertisers' valuations are independent, we find that information asymmetry can actually benefit publishers. In such scenarios, selectively allowing microtargeting (enabling only certain advertisers to access detailed consumer data) can generate higher revenues than either full data sharing or complete data restriction. This finding identifies a nuanced middle-ground policy that publishers can exploit under specific market conditions. Our analysis thus provides publishers with a framework for determining their optimal data-sharing strategy based on observable market characteristics. --- Objective 3: Characterize the optimal bidding behavior of advertisers under the different targeting policies. The paper formally characterizes equilibrium bidding strategies for both informed and uninformed advertisers across the different targeting regimes analyzed. Under full microtargeting (when all advertisers have access to consumer data), advertisers bid based on their precise valuations for each impression. The equilibrium bidding strategies follow standard auction-theoretic predictions, adjusted for the specific auction format. Under asymmetric information (when only some advertisers can engage in microtargeting), the bidding behavior becomes more complex. Some uninformed advertisers with high valuations may strategically underbid to avoid overpaying, while others may overbid relative to their true value for fear of losing valuable consumers to better-informed competitors. When microtargeting is disabled for all advertisers, bidding behavior converges as all participants face similar informational constraints. Advertisers bid based on expected valuations conditional on publicly available (contextual) information, leading to a more symmetric competitive environment. --- Objective 4: Study the effects of the equilibrium strategies of the publisher and the advertisers on conversion rates and revenues. A primary focus of our research was to understand how the strategic interactions between publishers (choosing data-sharing policies) and advertisers (choosing bidding strategies) affect key market outcomes: publisher revenue and auction conversion rates. One of the main findings is that, under specific conditions, disabling microtargeting can simultaneously improve both publisher revenue and conversion rates. This result aligns with and provides a theoretical explanation for recent anecdotal evidence from practice. For example, the Dutch public broadcaster NPO observed that conversion rates did not decline (and sometimes improved) when using only partial data for targeting, while also experiencing increased advertising revenue after discontinuing tracking cookies. Similarly, The New York Times reported analogous results after stopping behavioral targeting. The mechanism underlying this result is as follows: information asymmetry in markets with correlated valuations leads to inefficient bidding, where the advertiser who values the impression most does not necessarily win the auction. By eliminating asymmetry (through disabling microtargeting), publishers create conditions for more efficient matching between consumers and advertisers, despite the overall reduction in available information. The efficiency gains from reducing asymmetry can outweigh the efficiency losses from having less information in the market. We also analyze scenarios where outcomes diverge: for instance, situations where maximizing revenue and maximizing conversion rates require different policies. Our framework enables publishers to understand these trade-offs and make informed decisions based on their priorities. --- Objective 5: Determine the implications of the findings for ad exchanges, consumers, and regulators. The paper explicitly addresses implications for all relevant stakeholders in the online advertising ecosystem. For publishers and ad exchanges: Our findings indicate that the information asymmetry among advertisers participating in auctions can have unexpected consequences on both revenue and conversion rates. Publishers should adopt a careful approach toward the type and amount of information shared with advertisers, as more information is not always better. Practical measures such as disabling third-party cookies may lead to more efficient ad markets under certain conditions. For advertisers: While more information about impressions is generally advantageous, less information for competitors may not always be beneficial. The bidding behavior of competitors, shaped by information asymmetries, can negatively impact all market participants. Our analysis underlines the need for fairer, more transparent markets. Additionally, advertisers should recognize that their bidding strategies may need to be adaptive, requiring underbidding or overbidding depending on the specific informational environment. For regulators: We note that both the NPO and New York Times examples emerged as responses to the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) in the European Union. Our findings suggest that data privacy protection laws, initially conceived to protect consumers, can also inadvertently benefit publishers and advertisers. Careful design of such regulations can create win-win scenarios for all parties. For consumers: Higher conversion rates typically imply more relevant and satisfactory advertising content. Therefore, disabling third-party tracking on publishers' websites offers benefits beyond privacy protection; it can also improve the relevance of advertisements consumers see. --- All five project objectives have been realized through the development of a theoretical framework and comprehensive analysis. The resulting paper makes significant contributions to the academic literature on online advertising auctions and provides actionable insights for industry practitioners and policymakers. The paper is currently being revised based on reviewer feedback and will be resubmitted soon.

21509121.label: Major findings and research outcome
21509121.value: This project developed a theoretical model of online advertising auctions that integrates three key elements previously studied in isolation: differentiation between types of consumer data, information asymmetry among advertisers, and correlation among advertisers' valuations. Our first major finding establishes conditions under which limiting microtargeting can simultaneously improve publisher revenue and auction conversion rates. Specifically, when advertisers' valuations are positively correlated based on certain consumer data (e.g., multiple luxury goods advertisers value high-income users similarly) and information asymmetry exists among them (some advertisers have access to this data while others do not), publishers benefit from disabling microtargeting entirely. This result contradicts the conventional wisdom that more data sharing always benefits conversion rates and provides a theoretical explanation for recent industry observations. The mechanism driving this result is that information asymmetry in markets with correlated valuations leads to inefficient bidding behavior. Some uninformed advertisers with high valuations may underbid to avoid overpaying, while those with low valuations may overbid to avoid missing valuable impressions. Both behaviors result in suboptimal matching between consumers and advertisers. Eliminating asymmetry by restricting all data access can create more efficient auctions despite the reduction in overall information. Our second major finding reveals that when advertisers' valuations are independent, information asymmetry can benefit publishers. In such markets, selectively allowing only certain advertisers to engage in microtargeting can generate higher revenues than uniform policies of full sharing or complete restriction. Third, we demonstrate a counterintuitive result: both informed and uninformed advertisers may benefit when their competitors acquire more information. In markets with independent valuations, increased competitor information can improve allocation efficiency, benefiting all participants. These findings contribute to academic understanding of strategic data sharing in digital advertising and offer practical guidance for publishers formulating data policies and regulators designing privacy frameworks.

21509121.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21509121.value: Several promising directions extend naturally from this research. First, future work could examine the impact of microtargeting on consumer behavior. Consumers may prefer publishers who refrain from disclosing behavioral information to advertisers, and this preference could influence publishers' targeting decisions and subsequently affect revenues and conversion rates. If consumers actively choose privacy-respecting publishers, this creates an additional mechanism explaining improved outcomes when microtargeting is disabled. Second, our model could be extended to incorporate dynamic considerations, where publishers and advertisers interact repeatedly over time. This would enable analysis of reputation effects, learning, and long-term strategic data-sharing policies. Third, empirical validation using industry data would strengthen the practical relevance of our theoretical findings. Collaboration with publishers or ad exchanges could provide opportunities to test our predictions in real market settings. Finally, extending the analysis to consider multiple publishers competing for advertisers would yield insights into market-level equilibrium effects of data-sharing policies.

21509121.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21509121.value: When someone browses websites, they often see advertisements tailored to their interests. This personalization happens because advertisers can access data about their online behavior and bid for the opportunity to show them ads through automated auctions. However, not all advertisers have equal access to this consumer data; large companies with sophisticated technology can target ads precisely, while smaller advertisers cannot. Our research investigated what happens when this information imbalance exists. Surprisingly, we found that sometimes publishers (website owners) can earn more money and show more relevant ads by restricting data sharing and preventing personalized targeting altogether. This counterintuitive result occurs because unequal information access distorts the auction. Some advertisers may bid cautiously to avoid overpaying, while others may bid too aggressively. These distorted bids mean the advertiser who values reaching the consumer most does not always win. By leveling the playing field (giving everyone the same limited information) publishers can create fairer auctions where the most relevant advertiser wins more often. These findings have practical implications: privacy regulations that limit data sharing may benefit not only consumers but also publishers and advertisers. Some major media organizations have already observed improved results after reducing personalized targeting, and our research explains why this happens.

21600421.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21600421.value: 卖空，操控性应计利润和盈余管理

21600421.label: Project Objectives
21600421.value: Short selling is controversial and has received much attention from academia and regulators (Boehmer and Wu (2013), Liu (2014), Zhao (2018), Gao et al. (2020)). Previous studies show that short sellers can identify and discipline earnings management (Karpoff and Lou (2010), Fang et al. (2015), Massa et al. (2015), and Lu (2018)). This project contributes to the debate on short selling by identifying a potential problem caused by short selling: the threat of short selling may cause managers to be overconservative when communicating private information to the market. Therefore, short selling can reduce the amount of information reflected in stock prices, despite its disciplining effect on earnings management. The main mechanism of my study is as follows. Consider the scenario in which the manager of a firm is trying to convey good news to the market, despite some hard evidence suggesting the contrary. This scenario represents many real-world situations. For example, a firm could have low non-discretionary accruals for the current period, but the manager has access to soft information that is more precise and suggests that a high fundamental is more likely. The manager faces a dilemma: on the one hand, he can follow the more precise soft information and add the discretionary accruals to the non-discretionary accruals, generating a high earnings number on the income statement. On the other hand, if he chooses to report high earnings and later the hard evidence (i.e., non-discretionary accruals) is uncovered by someone, such as a short seller, the market might consider the manager as having manipulated earnings, damaging his reputation. Hence, the manager might choose to be conservative and report low earnings, even though he knows the fundamental is high. By shorting a firm’s stock and creating downward price pressure, short sellers exacerbate the reputation concerns of managers and can shut down the communication between managers and investors in the market. To formalize the above mechanism, I will build on the two-period reputation game in Morris (2001) and formally model three key concepts: discretionary accruals, non-discretionary accruals, and earnings management. I assume that a speculator is informed about the firm’s discretionary and non-discretionary accruals but not about earnings management. This assumption is motivated by the fact that short sellers are often sophisticated investors and possess superior skills for processing public information (Engelberg et al. (2012)). However, it seems unlikely that even sophisticated investors can accurately identify earnings management. The central result I expect to derive from the model is that short selling discourages managers from reporting an earnings number that is inconsistent with non-discretionary accruals. Hence, short selling results in the incorporation of more information in stock prices and discourages earnings management, but it deters managers’ communication through discretionary accruals. The overall effect of short selling is determined by the trade-off between these three effects. My project will primarily contribute to the literature on and the debate about short selling. Proponents of short selling argue that by incorporating negative information into the stock price, short selling increases stock price efficiency and improves resource allocation. Studies such as Diamond and Verrecchia (1987) and Saffi and Sigurdsson (2011) support this view. Opponents of short selling argue that short selling may reduce efficiency through manipulation (Goldstein and Guembel (2008)), spreading wrong information (Benabou and Laroque (1992)), and bank runs (Liu (2014)). My project will contribute to the debate on short selling by showing a novel inefficiency caused by short selling. The model focuses on how short selling affects managers’ reporting incentives, which distinguishes it from previous studies. In addition, unlike previous studies, I will rigorously demonstrate that the overall effect of short selling can be negative, thus providing stronger rationale for short-selling restrictions. Details of the related literature are discussed in Part II 2(a) (“Background of Research”).

21600421.label: Major findings and research outcome
21600421.value: As stated in the mid-term progress report, the main objective of the second stage of this project is to investigate short-sellers’ disclosure strategies. I worked with Pingyang Gao from HKU in this direction. We submitted our work, “Short, Disclose, and Distort” to Contemporary Accounting Research (CAR). During the review process, we received feedback that our model not only applies to short-sellers’ disclosure, but also applies to long investors’ disclosure in general. We revised the paper based on the feedback and changed the title to “A Theory of Investors’ Disclosure.” The paper was accepted by CAR in August 2025. The major findings are summarized below: We investigate investors' voluntary disclosure decisions under uncertainty about their information endowment. In our model, an investor may receive initial evidence about a target firm. Conditional on learning the initial evidence, the investor may receive additional evidence that helps interpret the initial evidence. The investor takes a position in the firm's stock, then voluntarily discloses some or all of their findings, and finally closes their position after the disclosure. We present two main findings. First, the investor will always disclose the initial evidence, even though the market is uncertain about whether the investor possesses such evidence. Second, the investor's disclosure strategy of the additional evidence increases stock price volatility: they disclose extreme news and withhold moderate news. Due to the withholding of the additional evidence, misleading disclosure arises as an equilibrium outcome, where the investor's report decreases (increases) price despite their news being good (bad). These results remain robust when considering the target firm’s endogenous response to the investor's report.

21600421.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21600421.value: Our analysis focuses solely on the price impact of the investor's disclosure and does not model the price impact of the investor's trading. Incorporating the investor's multi-dimensional information into a trading game, such as Kyle (1985), would render our model intractable. Therefore, we present our analysis, specifically the unraveling result, as a benchmark. An interesting avenue for future research is to examine whether and how the investor's disclosure incentives will be affected by the price impact of trading. We only model investors' verifiable disclosure. Future research can examine alternative situations where investors' disclosure is partially unverifiable. For example, one can consider a scenario similar to Dutta and Trueman (2002), where the initial evidence is hard information that can be credibly disclosed, whereas the additional signal is soft information that cannot be credibly disclosed. Finally, we do not investigate how investors’ disclosure affects firms' behavior. For example, whereas activist short-selling may deter firms from engaging in earnings management, it may also disrupt firms' normal communication using discretionary accruals, because discretionary accruals can be seen as red flags for earnings management. How does investors’ disclosure affect the overall amount of information reflected in stock prices? Can the benefits of activist short-selling be outweighed by the costs? We leave these questions to future research.

21600421.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21600421.value: This research explores how investors decide what information to share with the public when they discover something about a company. Unlike company managers—who usually want to raise stock prices—investors can profit whether prices go up or down. The study builds a theory explaining when investors choose to reveal or hide information. It finds that investors always share their first piece of evidence but only share additional details if the news is very good or very bad, keeping quiet when it’s moderate. This selective sharing can mislead the market, since withheld details might change how investors interpret the news. The research is significant because it helps explain why financial markets sometimes react unpredictably to investors’ reports and why firms and regulators sometimes accuse activists or analysts of “misleading disclosure.” The findings provide a foundation for better understanding investor behavior, market volatility, and the role of transparency in financial communication.

21601021.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21601021.value: 朝向民族國家文學：魯迅對德語世界文學資源的轉化，1906-1936

21601021.label: Project Objectives
21601021.value: The project will provide a new understanding of Lu Xun's literature and Chinese literary modernity. Although this literary icon has inspired much research, previous studies have mainly focused on the mediating role of Japanese sources when discussing his relationship to foreign literature and culture, with few studies examining the intermediatory role played by German sources. Benefiting from new perspectives and newly discovered materials, this project will unravel for the first time Lu Xun's complex appropriation of Weltliteratur sources. This project will serve as a bridge to further link the study of modern Chinese literature with the study of world literature. The last few years have seen an increase not only in theoretical debates on world literature but also abundant historical surveys of its ideas and practice. Under its influence, scholars have tentatively explored the relationship between modern Chinese literature and world literature. Following this line of research, this project will further demonstrate that modern Chinese literature has been intertwined with sources of world literature, particularly Weltliteratur, since its inception. This project will contribute to the growing body of scholarship on world literature. By examining how Lu Xun redefined world literature and national literature by reconciling various notions of Weltliteratur and focusing on minor European literatures, this project will conceptualize his contributions to complement today's theorization of world literature. By shedding light on the significance of these underexplored German sources of Weltliteratur, such as journals, literary histories, and book series, as well as the contribution of their editors and translators, this project will open a new line of inquiry in the field, which is far from being fully explored. This project will provide additional reflections on the relationship between national literature and world literature from a modern Chinese perspective. It is well known that the idea of world literature (shijie wenxue) enjoyed a sustained popularity in modern China, where generations of writers strove to create a new national literature. Put differently, since its inception, modern Chinese literature has inherently encapsulated the tension between the nation and the world. Recognized as both a key promoter of world literature and the founder of modern Chinese literature, the case of Lu Xun will give us the opportunity to identify these complex entanglements.

21601021.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21601021.value: This project will seek to transform our understanding of the origin of modern Chinese literature by conducting the first comprehensive study on Lu Xun's (1881-1936) appropriation of Weltliteratur sources (Weltliteratur is the German term for world literature). Acclaimed as the founder of modern Chinese literature, Lu Xun has received sustained attention from academics around the world. As he spent his entire life searching for new voices from alien lands, generations of scholars have explored how he appropriated foreign literature and culture, particularly using Japanese sources. Nevertheless, although it is well known that Lu Xun also relied on German sources, his connection to them remains unclear. Benefiting from recent scholarly debates and historical surveys of world literature, this project will argue that a considerable number of German sources consulted by Lu Xun belonged to Weltliteratur, and played a no less pivotal role than Japanese sources in shaping his literary ideas and practice. In this project, "Weltliteratur" will refer not only to the contested discourses on this concept proposed by Goethe and later German theorists but also to the flourishing literary practice of translating foreign literature, especially minor European literatures, in the nineteenth and early twentieth centuries in Germany. Having learned German in Japan, Lu Xun was not only interested in theoretical inquiries but also immersed himself in reading and assimilating these translations throughout his literary career. This project will examine two key issues. First, it will focus on Lu Xun's literary critiques, translations, and compilation projects to explore how he created his distinctive discourse on world literature and national literature by reconciling the ideas of Goethe, Hegel, and Herder embodied in the histories and journals of world literature. Second, it will seek to examine how Lu Xun generated his own creative writings such as "The Diary of a Madman," "Hometown," and "Lament for the Deceased" by appropriating the themes and narrative structures of short stories translated into German from minor European languages. By highlighting Lu Xun's appropriation of Weltliteratur, this project will demonstrate that modern Chinese/national literature was to some extent generated by an encounter with world literature. By integrating modern Chinese literature studies and world literature studies, this project will not only develop a new dimension for understanding Lu Xun's work, ranging from essays, short stories, translations, and compilations, but will also contribute to the theorization of the dialectic between national literature and world literature.

21601521.label: Realisation of objectives
21601521.value: I am pleased to report that all five objectives of my ECS grant have been successfully met, with outcomes that exceed initial expectations and contribute meaningfully to the scholarly community in Hong Kong and beyond. Objective 1: Theoretical Contributions to the Literature The project aimed to challenge prevailing understandings of transnational social movements and offer a new theoretical framework informed by social movement and international relations theories. This goal has been fully realized through a series of solo-authored publications in top-tier journals. Specifically, I published one article in International Organization (IO)—widely regarded as the leading journal not only in international relations but in political science more broadly—and two articles in International Studies Quarterly (ISQ), a flagship journal in IR. Additionally, I published in Review of International Studies (RIS), a leading IR journal in the UK. These articles identify theoretical and conceptual gaps in the literature on norms, norm evasion, and stigma in IR, and introduce new theoretical concepts and insights. Notably, they also offer rare perspectives on the unintended consequences of positive normative developments, which contributed to their selection by top venues. This publication record is unprecedented at CityUHK and rare in the field of international relations across Hong Kong, demonstrating a sustained capability for producing rigorous, high-impact research. Objective 2: Collection of News Reports (1945–2020) With the generous support of the grant, I hired a research assistant to help collect Japanese and Korean news reports on Korean colonial victims spanning 1945 to 2020. This dataset was integral to several of the aforementioned publications, providing empirical evidence, timelines for process tracing, and memorable quotes that enriched the analysis. I am grateful to the RGC for enabling this foundational work. The news collection remains private for now but will be made available upon request, in accordance with disciplinary norms. Objective 3: Interviews with Korean Victims The grant also enabled me to conduct fieldwork and interviews with victim-survivors and their advocates. For example, I visited Hapcheon—a city often referred to as Korea’s Hiroshima—to meet Korean hibakusha. These interviews provided invaluable empirical depth and personal narratives that were incorporated into my publications. I again thank the RGC for making this fieldwork possible, as it allowed me to document voices that are increasingly difficult to access due to the aging population of survivors. Objective 4: Research Outputs and Data Dissemination The grant proposal targeted two solo-authored journal articles and a curated dataset. I have exceeded this goal, publishing four solo-authored articles in leading journals (IO, ISQ x2, RIS), all of which acknowledge the support of the Hong Kong University Grants Committee (Project No. 9048231). These acknowledgments raise the profile of Hong Kong’s scholarly community in international academic circles. The news dataset, while not yet publicly released, is preserved and will be shared upon request. Objective 5: Dissemination at International Conferences I have actively disseminated my findings at several international conferences, including: * Academia Sinica (2024) * CityUHK Center for Public Affairs & Law Workshop (2024) * APSA Asia Program Workshop (2023) * APSA Asia Pacific Political Science Research and Publication Workshop (2022) In addition, CityUHK hosts a scholarly hub called CityU Scholars, where all information related to my publications and this grant is publicly available. This platform further amplifies the visibility of the research and its relevance to global academic audiences. I would like to note that three of the four journal articles supported by this grant have been published as open access, ensuring that they are freely available for download and accessible to the public without any cost. In conclusion, this ECS grant has been instrumental in supporting a research agenda that bridges theoretical innovation with empirical depth. The outcomes demonstrate the value of sustained support for early-career scholars in Hong Kong, and I am deeply grateful to the RGC for its generous funding.

21601521.label: Major findings and research outcome
21601521.value: Across four solo-authored articles published in top journals—International Organization, International Studies Quarterly, and Review of International Studies—I explore the international politics of victimhood and redress through status, rhetoric, advocacy, and unintended consequences. In Status Hierarchies and Stigma Shifting in International Relations (IO, 2024), I introduce the concept of “stigma shifting” to explain how status-anxious states manage reputational damage. Drawing on East Asian cases, I show how states like Japan reaffirm their global standing by associating with higher-status actors while deflecting stigma onto regional others. This dual move helps preserve status hierarchies and reshapes regional order. In The Rhetoric of Norm Evasion and Its Social Psychological Underpinnings (RIS, forthcoming), I examine how states accused of norm violations—such as colonial injustice—use rhetorical strategies to protect in-group esteem. I identify five recurring devices, including legalism and equivocation, and link them to psychological coping mechanisms. This work bridges IR and social psychology to reveal how norm evasion is not just strategic but deeply identity-driven. Colonial Redress and the Unintended Consequences of Global Opportunities (ISQ, 2024) challenges the assumption that global visibility always benefits victim movements. I argue that early access to international platforms can hinder long-term success, and that smaller, less visible groups may achieve redress more effectively. The article highlights how global opportunities can paradoxically constrain justice. Finally, in Transnational Advocacy, Norm Regress, and Foreign Compliance Constituencies (ISQ, 2022), I theorize “dual norm dynamics,” showing how states may deepen commitments to international norms while regressing in their treatment of foreign claimants. Through the Korean “comfort women” movement, I demonstrate how successful transnational advocacy can provoke backlash and norm retrenchment. Taken together, these articles offer a cohesive framework for understanding how victimhood is mobilized, contested, and refracted through global norms, status anxieties, and rhetorical strategies. They show that redress is not simply a moral or legal matter—it is deeply embedded in the politics of identity, hierarchy, and international legitimation.

21601521.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21601521.value: The four solo-authored journal articles supported by the ECS grant have laid the intellectual foundation for my second book project, tentatively titled great victims or elite powers? victimhood and the quest for status in the Indo-Pacific. Drawing on the core themes developed in these publications, the book will offer a comprehensive framework for understanding how victimhood is mobilized as an international political resource in the world, including in the Indo-Pacific. The research supported by the ECS grant has been instrumental in shaping the book’s conceptual architecture and empirical depth. I will formally acknowledge and thank the Hong Kong Research Grants Council (RGC) in the book.

21601521.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21601521.value: With support from the ECS grant, I published four solo-authored articles that explore how countries and advocacy groups use narratives of victimhood to shape international politics. These works look at why some nations emphasize past suffering to gain moral authority, how they respond when accused of wrongdoing, and what happens when global attention helps—or unexpectedly hurts—local justice movements. Together, these studies offer new ways to understand how history, identity, and global norms interact in the world. They’ve been published in top journals in international relations and political science, making a meaningful contribution to both academic and public conversations. I am deeply grateful to the Hong Kong Research Grants Council (RGC) for funding this work, which has laid the foundation for my next book project on victimhood as a means of status seeking in the world.

21601921.label: Project Objectives
21601921.value: Provide a novel framework for understanding the earliest cross-cultural exchanges between China and the West This project is part of a new wave of scholarship that uses multiple methodologies to reconstruct a dynamic picture of the earliest substantial cross-cultural exchanges between China and the West. With cross-cultural exchange as its target, this project will impact current scholarship in three pivotal ways. First, with relation to the extant scholarship, while other mapping projects, such as the survey of China made during the time of the Kangxi emperor in a collaboration between European Jesuits and Chinese and Manchu officials have been the subject of recent works, world maps and the period of earliest cartographic translations still lack a unified treatment. To address this gap in the scholarship, the proposed project will be the first book-length study of the earliest cartographic exchanges between China and the West from the global and connected, rather than regional or proto-national perspective. Second, the project innovates at the level of the historiography by using an array of new sources in multiple languages. The PI obtained training in a number of languages: Chinese, Manchu, Italian, Latin, Spanish, Portuguese, French and German. The ability to make connections and discuss sources in different languages previously considered apart by historians is a key contribution of this project. Third, by highlighting the importance of translation, the project will make significant contributions to the areas of the cross-cultural study of translation and the history of science, which has only recently started to focus on translation as a new area of research. Produce a book proposal and a book manuscript The proposed project will deliver a viable book manuscript to submit to an academic press with a significant impact factor. The first step in this process will be the development of a solid book proposal demonstrating the monograph’s relevance and the potential impact. This book proposal will be targeted to publishers with a high reputation for publishing in this area. The PI anticipates that there would be interest from the University of Chicago Press, the Harvard Asia Center and Harvard University Press, Cambridge University Press, Routledge and Palgrave Macmillan. Based on the PI’s PhD dissertation (Harvard University), the manuscript has been drafted partially. But additional funding under this grant is necessary for research to finalize the manuscript. 21601921.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21601921.value: The relations between China and the West are currently receiving extensive global attention. Yet, the history of these relations is much deeper, dating back to the root of modernity. Most notably, this history is defined by not only politics and economics, but also by substantial cultural contact and exchange. The proposed project will examine some of the earliest substantial cross-cultural exchanges between China and the West with a focus on maps, particularly maps of the world. World maps are significant for the history of Sino-Western cross-cultural contact, as they were some of the earliest items to be translated across: in Europe atlases such as the Guang Yutu 廣輿圖 by Zhu Siben, in various forms, were the source of representations of China for much of the early modern period up to the 19th century; in China world maps such as those produced by Matteo Ricci were the first cartographic works representing distant lands beyond Asia, introducing terminologies of world geography that are still in use today. The project will argue that these two processes of translation are inter-connected and represent two aspects of one phenomenon of hybridization of divergent Eurasian vocabularies and techniques of cartography. Using new methodologies in global history, translation studies and the history of science, the project will position translation as a key means by which to understand the long history of cross-cultural contact. To accomplish its aim, the project proposes to sequentially trace case studies of cartographic translation from the first instances of globalization in the sixteenth to the nineteenth centuries. The proposed research will have manifold implications in terms of understanding mutual representations of China and the West. Project outcomes will include both a book-length monograph for publication by a major North American or UK university press and a website with enhanced data on key cartographic materials. 當前，中西關係正備受全球廣泛關注。事實上，中西方之間的歷史淵源非常深刻，可追溯至近代史的開端。最值得注意的是，定義這段歷史的不僅只有政治和經濟，還有大量的文化接觸和交流。本項目將以地圖、尤其是世界地圖為重點研究對象，探討中西方之間最早的實質性跨文化交流。世界地圖作爲最早被翻譯的資料，對於中西文化接觸有極爲重要的歷史意義。譬如，朱思本的《廣輿圖》地圖集以不同形式在歐洲流傳，在近代史大部分時期直至19 世紀前，是中國之於西方印象的起源；又如，由利瑪竇所製的世界地圖向中國首次描繪了亞洲以外的地區，還引進了世界地理的術語，這些術語甚至一直沿用至今。本項目將論證這兩個翻譯過程是相互關聯的，代表了迥異的歐亞詞彙和製圖技術相互融合現象的兩個方面。本項目利用全球歷史、翻譯研究和科學史等的新方法去理解跨文化接觸交流的悠久歷史。為實現此目標，本項目提議，追溯研究自16 世紀至 19 世紀的所有地圖翻譯，由第一份翻譯資料起，依次追踪。擬議的研究將從多個層面推進對中西方關係的理解。項目成果將包括一本由北美或英國主要大學出版社出版的專著，以及一個儲存重要地圖資料和數據的網站。

21605721.label: Realisation of objectives
21605721.value: 1/ The study aimed to provide a comprehensive examination of the employment landscape for PWDs by collecting feedbacks from a variety of stakeholders, including PWDs themselves, VR social workers, and employers or HR practitioners. The first objective focused on gathering a holistic view of this landscape, which was achieved through a multi-faceted data collection approach. A survey was conducted among employers and HR practitioners to assess their attitudes and considerations regarding the hiring of PWDs. This survey was carefully designed based on the existing literature on workplace inclusion and was conducted over a six-month period in 2022. To ensure a broad and representative sample, the study received support from several organizations, including Baptist Oi Kwan Social Service, Fu Hong Society, and Lions Club. Both online and hardcopy questionnaires were distributed to targeted respondents, resulting in a total of 466 completed questionnaires. This extensive data collection was further supplemented by interviews with key stakeholders. Specifically, the research team conducted interviews with 54 key informants by using purposeful sampling. Data saturation was achieved with this sample size, which included 28 employers, 11 colleagues and supervisors of PWDs, and 15 PWDs themselves. Among the 28 employers and HR practitioners, 17 reported having hired PWDs, specifically 4 individuals with intellectual disabilities, 7 with mental health challenges, and 6 with physical disabilities. The employers were distributed across various enterprise sizes: 11 from small enterprises, 10 from medium-sized enterprises, and 7 from large organizations. These employers represented diverse sectors, including property management, retail, education, interior design and construction, cleaning, laundry, catering, banking, logistics, hair and beauty, and information technology. The 11 colleagues and supervisors of PWDs included 2 from small enterprises, 1 from a medium-sized enterprise, and 7 from large organizations, spanning sectors such as cleaning, catering, property management, banking, construction engineering, and retail. The 15 PWD participants worked in a variety of industries, including hospitality, healthcare, catering, technical trades, education, laundry, packaging, and retail. This triangulation of perspectives was essential, as it enriched the understanding of the employment challenges faced by PWDs. By combining quantitative survey data with qualitative insights from interviews, the study was able to paint a more nuanced picture of the factors influencing workplace inclusion. 2/ The second objective involved employing Accenture’s 4Es framework—Employ, Enable, Engage, and Empower—to explore the extent to which enterprises play a role in supporting workplace inclusion for PWDs. This framework provided a structured approach for understanding the various ways in which enterprises can facilitate the employment of PWDs. The study included a representative sample of enterprises, encompassing large, medium, and small enterprises. By engaging employers, HR practitioners, non-disabled colleagues, supervisors of PWDs, and PWDs themselves in critical discussions about hiring policies and practices, the researchers were able to uncover how these practices vary depending on the size and type of organization. The insights gained from these discussions revealed not only the challenges that different parties face in promoting workplace inclusion but also the strategies that enterprises employ to overcome these barriers. This comprehensive understanding highlighted the importance of considering the diverse backgrounds and experiences of all stakeholders involved in the hiring process. For example, the findings show that employers who hired PWDs generally strive to address the barriers associated with their employment. In contrast, those who do not hire PWDs tend to focus on cost-effectiveness and view the challenges as overwhelming. 3/ For the third objective, the study analyzed both quantitative and qualitative data collected from the surveys and interviews to extract key themes that either favour or disfavour the employment of PWDs. Among the factors identified as facilitating employment were support from non-governmental organizations (NGOs), government subsidies, and positive brand considerations. Notably, the ability to generate profits for the enterprises emerged as the most crucial factor influencing employers’ willingness to hire PWDs. On the other hand, the study identified several disfavour factors, such as internal opposition within companies, a lack of awareness about disabilities, and insufficient understanding of the resources available to support PWDs in the workplace. The analysis of these findings revealed a significant imbalance in previous intervention methods, which had predominantly focused on the supply side—providing resources and support for PWDs—while neglecting the demand side, which encompasses the needs and incentives of enterprises to foster inclusion. This imbalance suggests that while resources for PWDs are vital, it is equally important to address the motivations and concerns of employers. Consequently, the study argued for a more integrated approach that engages both sides to develop a sustainable framework for workplace inclusion. 4/ The fourth objective explored how different individuals perceive the concepts of inclusion and exclusion through a series of interviews. By interviewing a diverse group of stakeholders—including employers, PWDs, colleagues, and social workers—the study was able to construct a comprehensive picture of why full inclusion has not yet been achieved in many workplaces. The factors that hinder or promote inclusion were categorized into three levels: micro (individual), mezzo (organizational), and macro (societal). This categorization highlighted the complex interplay between these levels and underscored the need for a multi-dimensional understanding of the barriers to inclusion. 5/ The fifth objective was achieved with the support of the project collaborator, Baptist Oi Kwan Social Service. Three mini-ethnographic case studies were conducted to construct a context-specific descriptive account of workplace inclusion and exclusion at three selected research sites (one laundry and two catering establishments). The research began with observations of specific measures and equipment that effectively assist persons with disabilities (PWDs) in the workplace. These observations highlighted the importance of understanding the connections between disabled employees and their supervisors, as well as their interactions with colleagues. This focus helped identify the mechanisms that facilitate the gradual integration of disabled individuals into the company culture. Naturalistic data were collected through various methods, including detailed observations regarding workplace practices and the specific measures in place that assist PWDs. Informal and formal conversations with employees and supervisors also provided insights into their experiences and perceptions regarding inclusion and support for disabled colleagues. This combination of observational data and firsthand experiences at the research sites enabled the construction of a comprehensive and context-specific descriptive account of workplace inclusion and exclusion for PWDs. 6/ This objective was achieved by engaging vocational rehabilitation (VR) social workers and employers/HR practitioners through structured inquiry group discussions designed to foster dialogue and reflection. In the first round, focus groups were conducted with 23 vocational rehabilitation specialists. Subsequently, two cooperative inquiry groups involving four employers, four human resources managers, and nine vocational rehabilitation specialists explored ways to enhance workplace inclusion. These groups served as forums for cross-professional, multi-perspective dialogues on the outcomes of the three practitioner inquiry groups. The moderator facilitated discussions by inviting participants to comment on research findings from surveys and interviews, and by questioning the effectiveness of existing VR services based on employer feedback. Such inquiry fostered collective learning and the development of shared insights among participants. This approach laid the groundwork for further exploration of actionable strategies to promote workplace inclusion for persons with disabilities, ultimately supporting organizational changes in culture and practice.
