21605721.label: Major findings and research outcome
21605721.value: The major qualitative findings can be categorized into two main sections: one focusing on the initiatives taken by enterprises to promote workplace inclusion, and the other concerning how VR social workers provide interventions to facilitate workplace inclusion. The findings of this study emphasize the need for enterprises to adopt a strategic approach to fostering inclusive workplaces for persons with disabilities (PWDs). A clear vision for inclusion, articulated by senior management, is essential for creating an environment that values diversity. This vision should be effectively communicated across all levels of the organization, highlighting the collective responsibility of all employees in promoting inclusion. While enhancing corporate brand reputation can motivate enterprises to pursue inclusion, it is not a sustainable long-term strategy. Mutual understanding among employees is critical for integrating PWDs into the workplace. Misconceptions about disabilities often lead to resistance and discrimination from colleagues. To address this, the study advocates for inclusive training programs and support systems, such as buddy programs, which encourage interaction between disabled and non-disabled employees. Networking events outside of work can also help bridge gaps and foster relationships. Successful workplace inclusion requires specific supportive measures, including appropriate accommodations and barrier-free environments. Engaging in open communication with PWDs to understand their unique needs is vital. By providing the necessary resources and support, enterprises can empower PWDs to thrive and contribute meaningfully in their roles. The findings also inform vocational rehabilitation (VR) practices, particularly the prevalent “Place-then-Train” model. This model prioritizes job placement as a cornerstone of workplace inclusion, with VR social workers acting as essential connectors between employers and individuals with disabilities. These professionals leverage their expertise to provide insights that extend beyond government services, focusing on securing employment through comprehensive vocational training and ongoing support. Regular job coaching reinforces the skills of PWDs and facilitates collaboration with colleagues. Despite the significance of job placement, many enterprises struggle to prepare adequately for hiring individuals with disabilities. VR social workers play a crucial role in assisting enterprises in creating inclusive environments and shifting corporate culture. In contrast, the “Change-then-Place” model, which emphasizes modifying workplace conditions before placement, is less developed among VR practitioners. Although there is a desire to enhance employer awareness regarding disability inclusion, practitioners face challenges such as resistance and insufficient regulatory support. Overall, a multifaceted approach combining clear vision, mutual understanding, and robust support systems is essential for achieving workplace inclusion.

21605721.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21605721.value: Future research should prioritize qualitative investigations that delve into the lived experiences of disabled employees in various work environments. Such studies can illuminate the challenges they face, the support systems in place, and the factors that contribute to their success or barriers to their advancement. Additionally, research should focus on identifying best practices from companies that excel in employing and engaging PWDs. By documenting these successful strategies, a framework can created that other enterprises may adopt to enhance their inclusivity. Another critical area for exploration is the role of VR social workers in this context. Investigating how these social worker interventions can effectively influence employer attitudes and practices is essential. Research should aim to analyze existing intervention models and develop theoretical frameworks that empower social workers to engage proactively with employers, rather than only providing support post-placement. A new concept of “change-then-place” emerges in this study as a promising avenue for research. This concept requires further exploration to develop actionable strategies that can be tested and refined through practice. By focusing on these areas, future research can significantly contribute to dismantling the systemic barriers that prevent the full inclusion of disabled individuals in the workforce.

21605721.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21605721.value: The employment of individuals with disabilities has been advocated for years, yet results remain disappointing. This study identifies key issues that impede progress. A survey with 466 completed questionnaires and insights from 52 key informants highlighted the challenges. Three inquiry groups and two cooperative groups were formed to explore the issue. The findings reveal that many enterprises remain superficial in their efforts to promote an inclusive culture, lacking comprehensive strategies for effective inclusion. Many employers are uncertain about how to hire or support individuals with disabilities, and resistance from frontline staff contributes to this oversight. There is also a need for NGOs to take a more active role in supporting enterprises to enhance their readiness to employ persons with disabilities. Social workers tend to focus on individual cases; even when engaging with enterprises, their work is often limited to following up with employed service users rather than assisting enterprises in changing their corporate culture. Instead of primarily following the “place-then-train” approach, the findings advocate for a “change-then-place” approach for VR practice, emphasizing the necessity of first assisting enterprises in fostering an inclusive culture before facilitating the employment of individuals with disabilities.

21608421.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21608421.value: 威權政體的分配困境：中國的精英特權和公共福利的擴張

21608421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21608421.value: Maintaining the cohesiveness of the ruling coalition is a fundamental challenge for the survival of autocracies. One theory assumes that political elites join the ruling coalition for the exclusive privileges that they cannot enjoy as non-coalition members. However, this raises questions about the durability of such strategies, because autocrats also face pressures to liberalize the state and the economy for the general public in exchange for political obedience and cooperation. What strategies are used to recruit and retain political elites while maintaining a continuous expansion of public benefits and access to the state and economy? What are the consequences of such strategies? This project proposes a new theory to understand these choices, provide observable propositions, and test these on new evidence. I argue that autocrats use three strategies to create new benefits for elites while avoiding harming public support. First, autocrats create circumstances in which membership of the ruling coalition can be regarded as a positional good and is thus associated with an increase in social status rather than actual material benefits. Second, autocrats institutionalize the rewards and make credible commitments to regime allies. Third, autocrats deprive the public of benefits in less salient areas to compensate the political elites for their losses in salient areas where they no longer have exclusive privileges. Based on my previous studies and dissertation, this project adopts a mixed-methods design on the case of China. A qualitative analysis of interviews and archival documents will be conducted to explore how the CCP has been able to distribute goods to party members even as it has continuously opened access to many privileges to the public. A series of survey experiments and a conjoint experiment on the public’s perception of these new strategies will complement the qualitative findings and evaluate the effectiveness of the strategies in balancing the needs of retaining elites and appeasing the public. The proposed study provides new material for analysis of the recruitment and retention of political elites in authoritarian regimes when they need to offer more public goods. More broadly, it reveals the strategies used by autocrats to address the incompatible needs of elites and the public. It also has practical implications, given that China’s policymaking in relation to balancing the conflictual interests is a key aspect to understanding China’s public policy, which is critical for a range of stakeholders, including people from Hong Kong, who frequently conduct business with China. 對於威權整體，維持統治集團的內部穩定是其面臨的一項根本挑戰。現有理論認為，政治精英加入統治集團，以換取普通大眾所不能獲取的特權和特殊待遇。然而，這一理論的可持續性日益受到挑戰。大量研究證實，威權政體也需要不斷向公眾開放市場和政治體制，以換取社會穩定。那麼，在不斷擴大公眾福利和政治參與的同時，威權政體如何維持其對政治精英的吸引力呢？本研究項目提出一個新的理論以探究這個問題。具體而言，本研究認為威權體制可以通過三個策略維持其對政治精英的吸引力。首先，可以將統治集團的成員身份與社會地位掛鉤。其次，通過更制度性的分配和激勵機制向政治精英提供更可信的承諾。最後，可以通過適當的減少公眾不敏感的領域的公共品投入來補貼政治精英因為失去特權而遭受的損失。本研究計劃在中國大陸利用訪談、檔案調查及問卷調查實驗等多種方法驗證上述理論猜想。本研究對威權整體如何招募和維繫政治精英的忠誠提供了新的證據。同時，本研究也試圖回答威權政體如何在精英和大眾互相矛盾的訴求之間做出平衡和取捨。此外，本研究的發現對於理解中國社會和公共政策的制定也有重要的意義。

21610321.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21610321.value: Digital communications technology now plays an influential role in language teaching. In particular, the use of video is becoming widespread and yet teachers still know relatively little about how effective videos are designed. The importance of adopting online videos for teaching is highlighted in the post-COVID world whereby teachers all around the world have to create online video lessons. Nevertheless, teachers’ lack of understanding and training in video production has become a challenge. The proposed project will focus on online language teaching videos created by experts and semi-professionals alike, an underexplored area at the intersection of technology and language teaching. There is a general lack of understanding of the design of language teaching videos, how expertise is constructed by online teachers, and how these videos afford opportunities for learning. The proposed project will aim to fill these gaps by focusing on: 1) identifying and explaining the ‘teaching architecture’ of selected online language teaching videos based on a list of quantitative and qualitative criteria that showcase best practice; 2) explaining how expertise is constructed discursively and multimodally by online teachers; and 3) identifying instances of learning to shed light on the pedagogic effectiveness of these videos. 20 videos showcasing best practice will be analysed using multimodality and translanguaging. Multimodality is an approach to communication which focuses on the affordances of a range of semiotic resources and is helpful in systematically accounting for the multiple modes used in creating the videos. Translanguaging is an approach that foregrounds the creative and strategic deployment of the social actors’ full repertoire of resources. This will be used to make sense of the complex process of meaning-making which involves the mobilisation of resources that these online teachers possess over time. In addition to the analysis of videos, 10 online teachers will be interviewed in order to unpack how these social actors orchestrate multimodal resources, and how their life experiences and histories play a role in the design of the videos. Comments generated by the 20 selected videos will be analysed using interactional analysis. The findings of this project will lead to the development of a pedagogical model for online teaching video production that can serve as a blueprint for other teachers to follow. The project findings will also increase online teachers’ profile as legitimate stakeholders in language teaching. The project will also provide a new theoretical model of using multimodality and translanguaging to analyse teaching videos. 隨著數碼化溝通科技的普及，語言教學影片的使用變得尤其重要。然而，教師對如何設計有效的教學影片的認知仍然相對較缺乏。在新冠疫情後，世界各地的教師都需要製作網上影片課堂，因此，採用網上影片教學的重要性變得更為顯著，而教師缺乏對影片製作的理解和訓練在目前已經成為了一個挑戰。是次研究將集中分析由專家和半專業人士等人所創造的網上語言教學影片，藉此探索科技跟語言教學兩者當中的關係。在此學術範疇仍須多作探究的包括語言教學影片的設計、網上教師如何建構和展現自身的專業知識和技能，以及這些影片如何提供學習機會。此研究旨在針對這些被忽略的範疇，專注研究：1) 基於一列於定性和定量標準中展現最佳實踐的網上語言教學影片，辨別及解釋指定網上語言教學影片的教學結構；2) 解釋網上教師是如何利用語言與多模態資源建構和展現自身的專業知識和技能；以及3) 識別學習例子以解釋這些影片的教學有效性。 此研究會使用多模態和超語理論框架來分析二十個展現最佳實踐的影片。多模態研究是一個分析溝通的途徑。它集中研究一系列符號所提供的資源，有助系統性地解釋創造影片所運用的多種模態。而超語實踐則強調具創意地和策略性地運用語言使用者的全部溝通資源。製造意義是一個複雜的過程，包含著組織與運用網上教師隨著時間而擁有的資源。運用超語理論框架對此過程進行分析時，它將變得容易理解。除影片分析外，是次研究中也會訪問十名網上教師，以剖析他們如何利用多模態資源，以及了解他們的人生經驗和歷史如何融入到影片設計。至於對二十段被選影片的觀眾評論，將會採用話語分析的方法作更深入的研究。 此研究計劃的調查結果將能促使網上教學影片製作的教學模型的發展，並作為藍圖供其他教師參考。是次研究亦可以提升網上教師的形象，使他們成為語言教學中得到認可的持分者。而且，是次研究計劃也可以提供一個新的理論模型，展現如何利用多模態和超語理論框架來分析教學影片。

21612321.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21612321.value: 美國的"中國情結"：五四研究在美國的初步考察

21612321.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21612321.value: Questions about how to interpret the nature of the May Fourth Movement, arguably the most important sociopolitical and cultural-intellectual movement in modern Chinese history, have been essential to many debates on the development of Chinese history, culture, and politics. In Chinese-language scholarship, particularly from mainland China, “May Fourth studies” is very nearly a research field in its own right. The field covers a wide spectrum of social, political, cultural and literary issues arising from the historic student protest of 1919 and extending into the mid-late 1920s. While the studies of this movement and its legacy continue to receive attention from intellectual communities and even from the Chinese government, whether it is possible to identify and account for a similar body of literature that can be categorized as “May Fourth studies” in the United States has not yet been the subject of a more serious academic discussion. This proposed project will articulate the history of “May Fourth studies” in the U.S. to shed light on how “China” was perceived, portrayed, and interpreted in the Anglophone world. It will demonstrate how U.S.-based scholars, writers, journalists and activists addressed and conceptualized a changing China over the course of the twentieth century through their interpretations of the nature of the May Fourth movement, which had a sweeping impact on China’s later development. By investigating how the May Fourth movement was narrated and evaluated by American cultural elites, this study will enrich our understanding of the global and transnational dimensions of this movement and why these manifold impacts have remained valuable across many different contexts. Through an analysis of the movement’s transnational implications and its international reception, this proposed project will also provide historical depth and ideological complexity to the mutual perceptions of China and the U.S., which are necessary to understand and enhance contemporary Sino-American exchanges. 過去一個世紀以來，關於“五四”的研究一直是探討中國文化、政治、歷史發展的辯論焦點之一，但在二十一世紀的今日，“五四研究”卻面臨多重的挑戰，近年來常有論者認為“五四運動”是個被過度詮釋、過度評價的運動，“五四研究疲乏說”因此成為部分論者的時髦論調。本研究以“五四研究”在美國的興起與衰落為例，說明“五四研究”在二十一世紀的三大挑戰：（一）國際情勢丕變、（二）舊五四關鍵詞的觀點限制、（三）以及新論述典範的崛起。本研究認為美國“五四研究”的興起與衰落與冷戰有著密切的關聯，該領域因此是特定時空與歷史脈絡的產物，如何因應新的國際情勢與在地的文化政治因而是“五四研究”的新課題與存活關鍵。

21614021.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21614021.value: 當代儒家政治哲學：其限制與貢獻

21614021.label: Project Objectives
21614021.value: Main reasons for undertaking the project: - To seek to understand clearly the importance of Confucianism for contemporary politics and social development, especially in the context of East Asia. - To assess the prospects of Confucian political philosophy, given that it is attracting increasing attention from scholars across different areas of study (in particular, political philosophy, Chinese philosophy, and East Asian studies). - To achieve cultural and historical self-understanding through careful study of some of the classical texts of Confucianism and recent scholarly work on Confucianism. (The PI is Chinese in origin, and one major targeted beneficiary of the project is the Chinese public in Hong Kong, especially those among them who are more educated.) Key issues in the project: - To seek to identify the limitations and positive contributions of Confucianism for East Asia’s future political and social development - To provide a systematic analysis of the recent work on Confucian political philosophy - To read closely some of Confucianism’s classical texts; in particular, The Analects, Mencius, Xunzi, and Waiting for the Dawn: A Plan for the Prince (with specific attention to how Confucianism might improve our political thinking and enrich our concepts for social criticism) - To examine the plausibility of political perfectionism (i.e. the philosophical view that the state may promote the good life for its citizens), since many contemporary Confucian political philosophers base their arguments on this philosophical view Possible significance of the project: - In the short term, some significant academic contributions can be made to the continuing debates about Confucianism’s importance for contemporary political and social development. - In the long term, my research on Confucian political philosophy may improve the historical as well as cultural self-understanding of the local Chinese public, given that Confucianism has deeply influenced China’s historical development as well as individual Chinese people’s personal development. - In addition, more Chinese people (and hopefully more non-Chinese East Asians) may learn from my research about how Confucianism can broaden and improve their thinking about politics and social development. (For more details, see “Pathways to Impact Statement”.)

21614021.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21614021.value: 摘要： 儒家大約在二千五百年前的中國誕生。到了今天，許多人對它有兩種極爲不同的看法：一方面，孔子學院遍佈世界各地，儒家被認爲是中國專政的擴張。另一方面，對某些享負盛名的儒家學者來説，儒家是中國乃至東亞積極的政治改革的希望。 我認爲以上兩個觀點尚未能掌握儒家政治思想對於當代世界的重要之處。 本研究計劃嘗試從哲學的角度去分析儒家學説對當代政治與社會發展的重要之處，類似研究並不多。這項研究將針對一個頗具爭議性的學術觀點：儒家對東亞未來的政治發展有舉足輕重的重要性。基於筆者以前的研究，筆者會嘗試説明： 一、儒家學説中某些觀點確能改善當代人對政治的本質、各種政治體制、各種社會發展等事物的理解。因此，以爲儒家學説只代表了專政思想，這是過分簡單的觀點。 二、然而，由於當代的宗教和道德的多樣性，當代國家不能合理地預期它的市民必須擁護儒家價值。因此，我們不能斷定儒家學説對於東亞未來的政治發展有舉足輕重的重要性。 三、也由於宗教和道德的多樣性，當代國家不應擁護儒家學説而非任何其它整全的道德立場（如基督教和穆斯林）。 四、儒家中某些道德和政治理念能為當代政治改革（例如民主改革）和社會發展（例如如何改善和理解公民教育）提供某些寶貴的指引。這些理念亦能幫助人們（特別是成長於東亞的人）去理解和批評社會之中各種不公正。 五、東亞各政府能促進人們對儒家學説具反省性的理解，從而促進他/她們對自身文化與歷史的理解，這亦有助他/她們批評社會之中各種不公正。

21614021.label: Realisation of objectives
21614021.value: A. Realisation of objectives - achievements (1) The project has achieved the proposed research objectives. It has led to the publication of four items, all of which are peer-reviewed articles. They are: 1. Mang, F., and Chan, J. (2022). ‘Perfectionism’. In W.R. Thompson (Ed.), Oxford Research Encyclopedia of Politics. Oxford University Press. [Online]. (The PI is the first author). 2. Mang, F. (2023). ‘Confucianism and Public Political Discussion’. Comparative Political Theory, 3(2), 154-168. 3. Mang, F. (2023). ‘Perfectionism, Public Reason, and Excellences’. Analysis, 83(3), 627-639. 4. Mang, F. (2024). ‘Perfectionism, Political Justification, and Confucianism’. In J.D. Rooney and P. Zoll (Eds.), Freedom and the Good: Beyond Classical Liberalism. Pp. 130-144. Routledge. (2) In addition, the PI was invited to discuss the importance and limitations of Confucian political thought by delivering a keynote presentation titled ‘What Can Political Philosophy Teach Hong Kong Today? Political philosophy and the Relevance of Confucianism’ for the Oxford Hong Kong Forum, on June 26, 2022, via Zoom broadcasting. The presentation attracted over two hundred attendees, most of whom were Chinese students and scholars with interests in Chinese social and political development. (3) In the process of writing the above four articles, especially ‘Confucianism and Public Political Discussion’ and ‘Perfectionism, Political Justification, and Confucianism', the PI has gained a much deeper understanding of the significance of Confucianism for contemporary politics and social development, particularly in East Asia. This is one of the main research objectives. Moreover, the PI closely read some of Confucianism’s classical texts, notably The Analects, Mencius, and Xunzi, and this is another primary research objective. (The above two published works argue that Confucianism can enhance our political thinking and enrich our concepts for social criticism, although they also point out that any state committed to basic liberal values has little or no reason to promote Confucianism as a comprehensive moral doctrine or expect citizens to endorse it.) (4) The two articles, ‘Confucianism and Public Political Discussion’ and ‘Perfectionism, Political Justification, and Confucianism’, evaluate the prospects of Confucian political philosophy, which is receiving increasing attention from scholars across various areas of study. This meets one of the major research objectives. (5) During the writing process, including the final stage of revising the papers for publication, the PI has gained a deeper cultural and historical self-understanding through careful study of classical Confucian texts and recent scholarly work on Confucianism. This accomplishes one of the primary research objectives. (6) The mentioned articles, particularly ‘Confucianism and Public Political Discussion’, aim to identify the limitations and positive contributions of Confucianism to the future political and social development of East Asia. This successfully addresses one of the main research objectives. (7) It is also worth noting that my article ‘Confucianism and Public Political Discussion’ provides a systematic analysis of recent work on Confucian political philosophy. Notably, it includes discussions on the writings of Joseph Chan and Sungmoon Kim, who are among the most distinguished scholars in the field of Confucian political philosophy. (8) Additionally, some of the PI’s works published during the two-year research period—specifically, ‘Perfectionism’ and ‘Perfectionism, Public Reason, and Excellences’—examine the plausibility of political perfectionism (i.e., the philosophical viewpoint that the state may promote the good life for its citizens). In this way, the PI has fulfilled one of the stated research objectives, as the research proposal indicated an aim to examine the plausibility of political perfectionism, upon which many contemporary Confucian political philosophers base their arguments. (9) Regarding the possible significance of the project, three points are worth noting: (a) The research has already achieved its short-term goal of contributing to ongoing debates about Confucianism’s significance for contemporary political and social development through the publication of the above four articles in reputable venues. Notably, ‘Perfectionism, Political Justification, and Confucianism’ has been published by Routledge in the book Freedom and the Good: Beyond Classical Liberalism, alongside works by some of the most renowned political philosophers, including Philip Pettit (ANU/Princeton) and Steven Wall (Arizona). (b) Given the publication of works in high-impact venues, the PI can, in the long term, contribute to improving the historical and cultural self-understanding of the local Chinese public. This is one of the key objectives of the research project. Furthermore, the PI’s keynote presentation on ‘What Can Political Philosophy Teach Hong Kong Today? Political Philosophy and the Relevance of Confucianism’, delivered for the Oxford Hong Kong Forum on June 26, 2022 (via Zoom), attracted more than two hundred attendees, predominantly Chinese junior scholars and senior scholars interested in Chinese social and political development. Thus, the research has achieved short-term significance and is likely to have a long-term impact on the ongoing academic debate over the importance of Confucian political philosophy and public interest in its significance and its limitations. B. Regarding the unspent balance is 37.72% (over 30%) -- justification: A certain amount of funding was intended to use for presenting papers in conferences. The PI originally planned to attend two international conferences (mainly in the UK, with the possibility of attending one in the US) during the research period. However, the PI was not able to attend these conferences because he would like to look after his father, Mr. MANG Tat Chook, who was terminally ill from 2022 July to 2024 May (subsequently diseased in Tin Shui Wai Hospital on on the 4th of May 2024). Regarding the unused funding related to my education plan, please refer to "11. Realisation of the education plan."

21614021.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21614021.value: Further development of the research: 1. Expand comparative studies: To further the research, there could be a development of comparative studies between Confucian political philosophy and other prominent philosophies that influence contemporary political and social development. This can illuminate diverse philosophical explorations that may converge or diverge from Confucian thought, fostering a global dialogue. 2. Technology and Confucianism: Exploring the intersection between technology, ethics, and Confucian values could be an innovative direction for further research. For example, investigating how Confucian ethics might inform the development and use of emerging technologies like AI. Proposed course of action related to the research: 1. Public lectures and workshops: Organizing a series of public lectures and interactive workshops aimed at diverse audiences, including policymakers, educators, and the general public, could enhance the historical and cultural self-understanding of Confucian philosophy. 2. Collaboration with cultural and academic institutions: Seeking to establishing partnerships with cultural and academic institutions to create exhibitions, conferences, or online platforms focused on the relevance of Confucian philosophy in today’s world can significantly extend the reach of the research.

21614021.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21614021.value: This research project aims to explore the continuing relevance of Confucianism in today's political and social contexts. By publishing articles in esteemed journals, the principal investigator (PI) has initiated discussions among scholars and the public about how ancient Confucian ideas can inform modern politics and society. The publications include a book chapter accompanying works by top global philosophers, highlighting the project's significant contributions to the field. Additionally, the PI has delivered an engaging presentation at the Oxford Hong Kong Forum, attended by over two hundred individuals. The purpose of the presentation, as well as the scholarly work, extends beyond academic pursuit; it is about enhancing the cultural understanding of people in contemporary settings, demonstrating how Confucianism, as an ancient wisdom, can guide current and future generations. Simultaneously, it addresses why the political relevance of Confucianism should not be overstated. In this way, the research is valuable to both scholars and everyday individuals who are trying to understand the role of traditional philosophies in the modern world.

22300221.value: 基於鈣鈦礦半導體的太陽能電池是一種顛覆性光伏技術。然而，當前鈣鈦礦太陽能電池的發展依然受限於兩個基礎問題：一個是其通常具有大於1.45電子伏特的非理想帶隙，而另一個則是其通常包含具有揮發性的有機組分。該項目擬通過研究理想光學帶隙全無機鈣鈦礦半導體的晶界科學來解決以上問題，從而有望實現性能接近於理論極限且穩定的鈣鈦礦太陽能電池。 晶界是鈣鈦礦半導體最重要的微觀形貌特征，但鈣鈦礦晶界的基礎研究依然處於相對初級的階段。尤其是，已報道的晶界研究多聚焦在有機-無機雜化鈣鈦礦。儘管領域普遍認同，在鈣鈦礦半導體中，晶界可作為非輻射復合中心以及離子或分子輸運通道，從而對電荷輸運性能和化學穩定性產生不利的影響。但是針對於鈣鈦礦晶界具體參數的量化研究依然非常少見。並且，已報道的晶界研究多基於鉛基鈣鈦礦，很少涉及錫缺陷的探討。後者則很可能是理想光學帶隙全無機鈣鈦礦性能的關鍵。 本項目致力於理想光學帶隙全無機鈣鈦礦半導體的晶界研究，主要包括在納米尺度解析晶界構效關係、開發新型晶界調控方法，以及改善器件性能。值得一提的是，項目負責人在相關研究方向已有了較好的前期結果，為項目開展和完成提供了可靠的基礎。 本項目的預期成果將不僅對開發高性能鈣鈦礦太陽能電池產生重要的影響，更重要的是，通過這一基礎研究，有望挖掘出與鈣鈦礦半導體材料家族的微觀結構、缺陷以及性質相關的新物質科學，從而對包括紅外發光以及探測等各類光電器件應用產生更為廣泛的影響。

22300221.label: Realisation of objectives
22300221.value: We have fully completed the project objectives through successful fundamental and engineering research works. Overall, we have successfully mitigated the two significant issues (non-ideal bandgaps and relatively low stability) in state-of-the-art perovskite solar cells by understanding and tailoring grain boundaries in the inorganic-based, ideal-bandgap halide perovskites (e.g., CsPb₁₋ₓSnₓI₃) and related perovskite compounds, which is consistent with Objective 1. We then performed fundamental characterization studies on the grain-boundary microstructures of CsPb₁₋ₓSnₓI₃ perovskites and related perovskite compounds using scanning electron microscopy (SEM), transmission electron microscopy (TEM), and atomic force microscopy (AFM). The grain boundary microstructure was well visualized and analyzed, which was then linked to its electronic and optical properties, including photoluminescent properties and charge transport. These results led to the realization of Objective 2. We also fabricated perovskite thin films using various grain boundary engineering approaches, which showed improved charge-transport properties and chemical stability. These films have enabled the fabrication of solar cells with power conversion efficiencies exceeding 18% and good stability. These results fulfilled Objectives 3 and 4.

22300221.label: Major findings and research outcome
22300221.value: 1. We established a set of methods for characterizing the perovskite grain boundaries and interfaces at the nanoscale, especially the low-dose scanning transmission electron microscopy (TEM) (Cai et al., J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2022, 144, 1910), in-situ light-incorporated TEM (Duan et al., ACS Energy Lett. 2023, 8, 3048-3053) and X-ray ptychographic tomography (Zhou et al., J. Energy Chem. 2022, 73, 639). We also developed a liquid-phase transfer method to prepare TEM sample specimens for perovskite characterization (Guo et al., Adv. Opt. Mater., 2024, 12, 2301255). 2. We developed several new methods for tailoring the perovskite grain boundary and related interface microstructures (e.g., grain boundary grooves) based on novel additives (Hao et al. Adv. We reported inorganic ideal-bandgap perovskite solar cells with power conversion efficiencies up to 15.04%, the highest reported so far for inorganic perovskite devices with sub-1.4 eV bandgaps. Furthermore, the T90 lifetime of these devices can exceed 1000 hours upon light soaking in a nitrogen atmosphere, demonstrating the potential advantage of all-inorganic lower-bandgap perovskite solar cells. (Hu et al. J. Energy Chem. 2023, 72, 487). We have further improved the power conversion efficiency of inorganic ideal-bandgap perovskite solar cells to exceed 18% and applied this technology to high-efficiency inorganic all-perovskite tandem solar cells (manuscript in preparation). 4. As an early-career project, the research works have led to numerous inspirations and findings that have contributed to impacting the long-term career of the PI and the general field of perovskite optoelectronics. The outcomes of this project will have far-reaching impacts, not only in the development of high-efficiency and stable perovskite solar cells (PSCs) that approach the Shockley–Queisser limit but also in uncovering new physical phenomena related to the broader family of perovskite materials, particularly concerning their microstructures, defects, and properties. 22300921.label: Project Objectives
22300921.value: We shall study the asymptotic eigenvalue distribution of the Toeplitz-like matrices arising from solving time-dependent differential equations, including but not limited to fractional differential equations. We shall develop effective preconditioners for the nonsymmetric ill-conditioned Toeplitz systems of interest, and analyze the spectral property of the preconditioned systems. We shall generalize the aforementioned preconditioning results to nonsymmetric block Toeplitz systems as well as nonsymmetric multilevel Toeplitz systems, and theoretically prove the fast convergence of our developed iterative solvers with the proposed preconditioners.

22300921.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
22300921.value: In this project, we develop efficient iterative methods for Toeplitz-like systems arising from solving time-dependent partial differential equations (PDEs). These PDEs arise in numerous areas in applied science and engineering, with a growing list of crucial applications such as image processing, numerical solution of convolution integral equations, queueing networks, and option pricing, just to name a few. When it comes to solving differential equations, one common numerical approach is to first discretize the equation by a mesh and then solve the corresponding linear system. One needs to further refine the mesh in order to obtain more accurate approximations. The following two main reasons motivate the development of this proposed research project. On one hand, solving those linear systems is often computationally challenging due to their enormous size. On the other hand, in a myriad of applications, the linear systems to be inverted are frequently Toeplitz-like. Therefore, it is of high importance to develop efficient solvers which provide fast computations for these systems. One of our main contributions is to propose novel numerical linear algebra solver for the Toeplitz-like systems and theoretically prove their rapid convergence rate. To the best of our knowledge, our proposal is the first attempt to employ the minimal residual method (MINRES) with non-circulant preconditioners for a large class of nonsymmetric ill-conditioned Toeplitz systems in order to achieve theoretically guaranteed convergence. Such an approach is in stark contrast to most existing iterative methods utilizing the generalized minimal residual method whose preconditioning based largely on heuristics. Based on our experience with Toeplitz-like systems, we first study and identify the asymptotic eigenvalue distribution of the linear systems arising from the PDE problems of interest, including fractional differential equations. With such knowledge about eigenvalues, we construct accordingly effective preconditioners. Then, we will theoretically prove that the eigenvalues of the preconditioned matrix are clustered around ±1, which entails rapid convergence of MINRES. Preliminary results show that our designed preconditioners can lead to significant improvement in convergence, which outperform several existing circulant preconditioners. The spectra of the preconditioned matrices in the examples are observed to be clustered, which is in accordance with our proposed preconditioning theory.

22300921.label: Realisation of objectives
22300921.value: The PI is pleased to report that all objectives outlined in Section 5.2 have been fully achieved. The following provides a detailed account of how each objective has been realized, including the key theoretical and computational advancements made during the project. Objective 1: Asymptotic Eigenvalue Analysis of Toeplitz-like Matrices The PI successfully investigated the asymptotic eigenvalue distributions of a class of Toeplitz-like matrices arising from the discretization of time-dependent differential equations, with an emphasis on fractional differential equations. This included a rigorous spectral analysis of matrices generated by various time-stepping schemes. Key accomplishments include: 1. Derivation of asymptotic spectral distributions using the framework of Generalized Locally Toeplitz (GLT) sequences for a class of block Toeplitz-like structured matrices, which have applications in solving parabolic, wave, and fractional differential optimal control problems. 2. Dissemination of results through peer-reviewed journal articles and conference presentations. Objective 2: Development and Analysis of Preconditioners The PI developed a suite of efficient preconditioners for nonsymmetric and ill-conditioned Toeplitz systems. These preconditioners were designed to exploit the inherent structure of the matrices while ensuring accelerated convergence of iterative solvers. Key accomplishments include: 1. Construction of preconditioners based on Tau matrix approximation as well as symbol-based strategies. 2. Theoretical analysis demonstrating that the eigenvalues of the preconditioned systems cluster favorably, ensuring rapid convergence. 3. Comprehensive numerical experiments confirming the robustness and efficiency of the preconditioned solvers (e.g., MINRES and GMRES). Objective 3: Generalization to Block and Multilevel Toeplitz Systems The PI extended the developed preconditioning techniques to nonsymmetric block Toeplitz matrices and multilevel Toeplitz systems, which commonly arise in multi-dimensional and coupled problems. Key accomplishments include: 1. Design of block preconditioners exploiting Kronecker product structures and block-circulant approximations. 2. Spectral analysis based on block GLT theory and matrix theory, providing theoretical support for the convergence of iterative methods. 3. Implementation and testing of these techniques in practical scenarios, confirming the scalability and performance of the proposed methods. Conclusion: All project objectives have been fully achieved. The PI has delivered significant theoretical contributions and practical tools for solving Toeplitz-like systems derived from time-dependent differential equation problems, including parabolic, wave and, fractional models. These outcomes have been disseminated through scientific publications and conference engagements. No major challenges were encountered; minor technical issues were resolved through methodological refinements and continued collaboration with experts in the field.

22300921.label: Major findings and research outcome
22300921.value: This research project has yielded substantial theoretical and computational advancements in the analysis and solution of Toeplitz-like systems, especially those arising from time-dependent partial differential equation (PDE) problems. The major findings are organized according to the revised objectives in Section 5.2: Objective 1: Study the asymptotic eigenvalue distribution of Toeplitz-like matrices. 1. We investigated the spectral distribution of nonsymmetric Toeplitz matrices and their preconditioned counterparts, especially those derived from all-at-once formulations of evolutionary PDEs. 2. Asymptotic results were rigorously established using the GLT theory and spectral analysis, confirming the clustering or boundedness of eigenvalues, which is essential for ensuring fast convergence of Krylov subspace methods. 3. Objective 2: Develop effective preconditioners for nonsymmetric ill-conditioned Toeplitz systems and analyze the spectral property of the preconditioned systems. 1. We developed and analyzed a wide range of preconditioners, including band-Toeplitz, circulant, multilevel Tau, and $\epsilon$-circulant matrix based methods, tailored for different PDE structures. 2. These preconditioners significantly improved the condition number and convergence rates of iterative solvers such as GMRES and MINRES. 3. Spectral analysis verified the optimality or spectral equivalence of the preconditioned systems. 4. Key references: - Huang et al., Numer. Linear Algebra Appl., 2025. - Lin, Li*, and Hon, J. Sci. We extended the preconditioning framework to higher-dimensional and block structures, including block $\omega$-circulant and block $\epsilon$-circulant matrices. 2. These were applied to multi-dimensional fractional PDEs, parabolic/wave optimal control problems, and wave equations, with theoretical and empirical evidence showing fast solver convergence. 3. Theoretical analysis of asymptotic spectral behavior supported the generalizations and validated the robustness of the proposed methods in multilevel and block settings. 4. 22300921.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
22300921.value: The research outcomes open up several promising directions for further development: 1. Parallel Implementations: To handle large-scale and high-dimensional problems, we propose developing efficient parallel and distributed implementations of the proposed preconditioners. This includes matrix-free Krylov solvers, domain decomposition techniques, and GPU-accelerated algorithms to ensure scalability on modern high-performance computing platforms. 2. PDE-Constrained Optimization Problems: Building on our success with optimal control of parabolic and wave equations, we aim to extend the preconditioning framework to more general PDE-constrained optimization problems. These problems often lead to large, ill-conditioned block saddle-point systems, for which specialized block Toeplitz and circulant preconditioners can be highly effective. Proposed Course of Action: We will develop robust and scalable software implementations, supported by theoretical analysis, and seek interdisciplinary collaborations to apply our methods in computational science and engineering.

22300921.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
22300921.value: This research project focuses on improving how we solve complex mathematical equations that describe how things change over time—such as how heat spreads, how fluids flow, or how materials react. These equations are used in many real-world fields, including physics, engineering, and finance. When scientists and engineers try to solve these equations using computers, they often face very large and difficult systems of equations that are slow and expensive to solve. Our research developed faster and smarter ways to solve these systems by designing special mathematical tools called preconditioners. These tools help computer algorithms work more efficiently, saving both time and computing resources. We focused on a particular group of problems where the systems have a special repeating structure (called Toeplitz systems), which appears in many time-dependent and space-fractional models. We also extended our methods to more complex cases involving blocks and multiple levels of structure. The value of this work lies in its ability to make solving large-scale scientific and engineering problems much faster and more reliable. Our methods can be applied in simulations of waves, heat, and chemical reactions, and have potential impact in areas such as medical imaging, material science, and environmental modeling.

22500521.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
22500521.value: 與死亡相關的產品和服務的市場是巨大的。每個人在某個時候都需要消費其中的一些。這些產品旨在幫助人們為死亡來臨之前（例如人壽保險）、之中（例如臨終關懷），和之後（例如葬禮服務）做準備。儘管在非必要時提前考慮與死亡相關產品和服務的益處頗多，但消費者通常拒絕接收有關死亡相關產品和服務的營銷信息。 銷售人員的溝通方式可能可以有效減少消費者對銷售該類產品信息的抵製或迴避，提高他們對與死亡相關產品或服務的購買意願。現有營銷研究文獻已證實銷售人員所傳達的銷售內容會顯著影響消費者的購買意願，然而相對較少的研究考察銷售人員所使用的語言如何決定消費者的消費行為。我們旨在通過研究銷售人員使用的語言（意即使用的是目標客戶的外語或母語）如何影響消費者購買與死亡相關的產品和服務，從而填補這方面的研究空白。 綜合市場營銷、心理學和語言學的有關理論，我們建議銷售人員使用外語來說服雙語消費者。基於恐懼管理理論和情緒心理學的研究，我們認為消費者考慮自己的死亡是可怕的，因此會觸發迴避型防禦系統。但是，如果銷售人員對消費者使用外語（而非母語），則可以通過減輕消費者對死亡的恐懼來減少消費者對銷售信息的迴避並增加他們的購買意願。正如外語文學研究中已有的證據所揭示的那樣，在交流中使用外語（而非母語）可以減弱接收者的情緒。在交流與死亡相關的產品或服務時，外語似乎同樣可能會降低與死亡相關記憶的可及性和死亡圖像的生動性，並增加消費者與死亡威脅的心理距離，每一種都會讓他們減少對死亡感到的恐懼。 為進一步探究這種語言策略的作用，我們還考慮了一些潛在的調節因素，包括產品功能、銷售人員與客戶互動的強度和媒介，以及消費者特質。具體而言，我們提出對於具有死後超越感的產品或具有視覺處理信息傾向的消費者，外語效應可能會減弱。相比之下，如果產品需要客戶參與或銷售過程涉及面對面的互動，則效果可能會更強。我們已經進行了初步研究；我們計劃進行六項進一步的研究，包括實驗室和現場實驗，以檢驗我們的觀點和假設。

22500521.label: Major findings and research outcome
22500521.value: Theory wise, our research posits an important phenomenon that consumers often resist marketing information about death-related products and services (DRPS), let alone purchase them. Yet there is a massive market and universal necessity for DRPS offerings like life insurance and funeral services. In our research, we advocate that consumer proactively consider DRPS in advance to better prepare for death and its aftermath. Our research builds on terror management theory and the literature on language use and psychological distance to propose a language-based sales communication strategy for DRPS. In the journal publication manuscript, we included a comprehensive empirical package of eight studies, including two field experiments and an eye-tracking study. Those studies indicate that DRPS sales messages appear in consumers’ second (vs. native) language (e.g., using muerte, Spanish for death, when talking to a native English speaker whose second language is Spanish) decreases consumers’ fear of death by creating greater psychological distance to death, which in turn induces more consumption (e.g., actual purchases). However, this effect becomes attenuated when consumers perceive high control over death or when the DRPS feature transcendence after death. In contrast, the effect is amplified for DRPS that require an intermediate level of customer participation. As reported in Part C, these findings directly resulted in one research output (a conditionally accepted article in the Journal of Marketing Research) and indirectly contributed to three additional relevant publications in the Journal of Marketing, International Journal of Research in Marketing, and Psychology & Marketing, respectively. The findings were also shared and discussed at two prestigious conferences in the marketing research discipline. Together, these results offer novel insights into how marketers and policymakers can encourage consumers to consider DRPS earlier and engage in more proactive decision-making.

22500521.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
22500521.value: Future research will examine whether the observed language effect extends to other fear-based consumption contexts, such as risky financial investments, property insurance, or non-DRPS products linked to different emotions (e.g., embarrassment in condom purchases). We or other researchers could also explore contexts where the proposed effects of psychological distance and fear of death diminish or reverse—particularly when the threat of death is imminent, as in terminal illness. Further studies should test whether L2 benefits extend beyond initial adoption stages to later phases like after-sales or service recovery, and investigate how setting characteristics (offline vs. online, formal vs. informal) moderate the effect. Future work could also examine how individual differences—such as age of acquisition, mode of acquisition, and language proficiency—shape emotional access and influence the strength of the language effect. Additionally, research could explore how chronic worries, gender, or topic sensitivity impact attrition and response patterns, and experiment with strategies like pre-warnings to reduce online dropout. Finally, future studies should incorporate monitoring technologies to detect translation tool use and seek corroboration of self-reported behavioral outcomes (e.g., organ donation registration) with official or objective data sources.

22500521.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
22500521.value: Most people feel uneasy when talking about death, even when making practical decisions like buying life insurance or planning a funeral. This discomfort often stops them from preparing for the future, leaving families unprepared and causing challenges for the global market of death-related products and services. Our research explores a simple but powerful idea: the language used to discuss death can change how people react to it. Across eight studies in different countries and languages, we found that when sales messages about death-related products are presented in a person’s second language (for example, Spanish instead of English), people feel a bit more emotionally distant. This emotional distance reduces fear and helps them think more calmly and rationally about the benefits of planning ahead. The approach works especially well for DRPS that require an intermediate level of customer participation, such as life insurance or funeral planning. It is also effective when consumers are deciding for close family members, such as parents. By changing how these sensitive topics are communicated, this research shows a new, practical way for marketers and policymakers to help individuals make more proactive choices that bring peace of mind and ease the burden on families.

22500921.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
22500921.value: Why is insider trading illegal? There has been considerable debate within academia over the costs and benefits to society of insider trading. Previous work looks at whether traders are made better or worse off by insider trading but ignores others that are affected. Many look to asset prices for information before making real economic decisions. Those who use prices for information have not been closely examined in the literature. While it is clear they would prefer prices be more informative rather than less, it isn’t clear their preference over the dynamics of market learning or what policies a regulator can implement to maximize their welfare. Consider how insider trading regulation affects market price learning. Without insider trading, prices gradually come to account for the collective information of countless traders. Prices are constantly moving by small amounts to incorporate information from trades. With insider trading there is a crowding out effect as analysts and other outsiders no longer find it profitable to compete. This effect leads to relatively infrequent trading and price movements, but when trades happen they contain more information on average and lead to larger price movements. Not only the amount of information revealed in prices but also the dynamics of the learning process are important. Stock prices play an critical role of aggregating and conveying information. There are many economic players that look at stock prices to make decisions other than investing in the stock (managers, regulators, banks, etc.). The debate on insider trading is lacking a serious study of these decision makers that watch stock prices to gather information. Naturally, these decision makers would prefer prices to convey more information rather than less, but do they care about how this information is learned? What sort of price process would these players most benefit to learn from? My project will explore when these decision makers would prefer infrequent sudden market learning caused by insider trading or continual gradual learning caused by outsiders. In the short run, this project will generate at least one paper to be published in a top international journal in the fields of economics or finance as well as several presentations at conferences and seminars. In the longer run this project will help inform policy makers about the optimal regulation of insider trading, and the ideas of this project will be further explored by others seeking to understand the full impact of insider trading. 为什么内幕交易是非法的？关于内幕交易对社会的成本效益，学术界的讨论不绝于耳 。之前的学术研究更多的着眼于，通过内幕交易的交易者，他们的经济状况是否变得 更好或是更糟，但忽略了其他受影响的交易者。许多交易者在做真正的经济决策前， 往往通过资产价格获取信息。而这些从价格中获取信息的交易者在以往文献中没有被 仔细地研究过。虽然可以清楚地知道他们对价格可以提供更丰富信息的偏好，但并不 清楚他们对于动态市场学习的偏好，以及监管机构可以实施哪些政策去最大化他们的 福利。 考虑内幕交易监管如何影响市场价格学习。在没有内幕交易的情况下，价格逐渐成为 无数交易者的集体信息。价格的不断小幅波动收录着交易信息。内幕交易会产生挤出 效应，因为分析师和其他外部交易者发现不再有利可图。这种效应会导致相对不频繁 的交易和价格变动。但当交易真正发生时，平均而言，交易包含着更多信息并会导致 更大的价格变动。因此，不仅价格所显示的信息很重要，而且学习过程的动态性很重 要。 股票价格在汇总和传达信息方面发挥着关键作用。除了投资股票之外，还有许多经济 参与者（经理、监管机构、银行等）会根据股票价格做决策。关于内幕交易的讨论缺 乏对这些观察股价以收集信息的决策者的认真研究。当然，这些决策者更喜欢价格传 达更多信息而不是更少信息，但他们是否关心这些信息是如何获得的？学习什么样的 价格过程能让他们最受益？我的项目将探讨这些决策者何时偏好由内幕交易引起的少 见且突然的市场学习，何时偏好由外部交易者们引起的持续渐进学习。 在短期内，本项目将会产生至少一篇在经济或金融领域的国际顶级期刊上发表的论文 ，并在会议和研讨会上发表演讲。从长远来看，该项目将帮助政策制定者了解内幕交 易的最优监管模式，并且本项目的研究方向可以被其他学者进一步探索，以了解内幕 交易的全面影响。

22500921.label: Realisation of objectives
22500921.value: This project has generated a working paper that I believe achieves all of the objectives set out in the grant proposal. Section 6.1 explains the findings of the paper. Here I will note how these findings address each of the stated objectives. 1. To extend our understanding of how market prices aggregate information: In general classes of market microstructure models, I show an equivalence of information aggregation into prices across any distribution of private information among traders. 2. To explore how regulation affects the dynamic informational efficiency of prices: Regulation of insider trading restricts a small very well informed group of traders, empowering a much larger group of analysts to trade on their lesser information. I show a channel through which this can lead to more informationally efficient prices. 3. To attack the longstanding and important debate on insider trading from a new angle to gain further insight: It has long been thought that allowing insider trading would reduce liquidity, lowering the profits of traders, but also improve price informativeness potentially helping others such as managers. By focusing on the distribution of information acquisition, I show a channel through which allowing insider trading leads to the opposite result, namely improving liquidity and harm price informativeness. Tis because informed trading is more concentrated in a smaller number of traders. These traders now face a larger share of the cost from reduced liquidity. Therefore, they choose to acquire less information. In short, acquiring information has the negative externality of harming liquidity. When informed trading is more disperse, there is more of an overproduction of this externality. 4. To confirm the generality of preliminary results to many types of markets: The proposal gave a very simple example some similar results. The current working paper is able to show these results hold for general classes of Kyle models and Glosten and Milgrom models. 5. To understand how policy can best help people that have been previously ignored: The model shows that “noise traders” or “liquidity traders”, who are typically left unmodelled can be helped by allowing insiders to trade on their information. This is through the added liquidity. The paper also shows that insider trading can harm price informativeness to the detriment of managers and others who use prices as signals of information. Thus, the policy that helps one of these groups will harm the other.

22500921.label: Major findings and research outcome
22500921.value: The major findings of the paper are on the distribution of private information and opportunities to acquire such information among traders and the effect this distribution has on the financial market. The findings have implications for the regulation of insider trading. Using a general Kyle model and a general Glosten and Milgrom model, I first show an equivalence on market outcomes across distributions of private information (e.g. between two informed traders with independent pieces of information and a single informed trader with both pieces of information.) However, the equivalence fails when comparing distributions of opportunities to acquire information (e.g. two traders with the opportunity to acquire costly pieces of independent information and a single trader with the opportunity to acquire both pieces of information.) Liquidity is a public good that is reduced by the presence of private information. Multiple traders will over acquire information ignoring the negative externalities on other traders through these liquidity eﬀects. Hence, a more dispersed distribution of information acquisition opportunities leads to lower liquidity, harming traders, but greater informativeness of prices as the traders choose to acquire more information. These results are exactly opposite to most intuition on insider trading and its regulation. Insiders are a small group of traders that, if permitted, would have the opportunity to acquire a large amount of information. It is supposed that insider trading would crowd out some analysts trading and information acquisition (a large number of traders with comparatively fewer opportunities to acquire information). Common arguments for and against allowing insider trading include more informative prices (from the information generated by these insiders) and lower liquidity (the “insider trading tax” from people being reluctant to trade against insiders.) While not meant to overturn that intuition, my project does show a channel through which insider trading has the complete opposite effects. These findings have already been presented at an international conference and generated a working paper to be submitted soon.

22500921.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
22500921.value: This project has created a good theoretical understanding of a channel through which insider trading has an opposite effect of those previously understood in the literature. In the near future, a working paper will be submitted to an international peer reviewed journal such as American Economic Review: Insights or Journal of Finance. In the longer term, I plan to work with empirical coauthors to explore related topics such as the distribution of price informativeness and liquidity across assets in a financial market both before and after that country first passed and began to enforce insider trading legislation. These distributional statistics will help inform a future research direction.

22500921.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
22500921.value: This project explores a new channel through which insider trading and other informed trading can affect the market and participants. When some trader obtains information pertaining to the value of an asset, others will become reluctant to trade that asset. The fact that a well-informed trader is willing to buy the asset from me might mean they have good information about its value. Thus, I don’t really want to sell. This leads to less liquidity in the market and is harmful to all traders. When there are many traders that have to potential to research and uncover information, each trader acquires a lot of information because they only have to bear a small amount of the cost of reducing liquidity. In a market with fewer traders acquiring more information, each trader bears more of this liquidity cost of their own information acquisition. Thus, when information acquisition opportunities are more dispersed, more information will be acquired and revealed. This will come at the cost of lower liquidity, harming traders' profits. Insiders are a small group of traders with a large amount of information. Allowing insider trading would be the less dispersed example. This channel has not previously been discussed.

22501621.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
22501621.value: One way through which firms can obtain external knowledge is by acquiring other firms or even competitors so that they would be able to access ‘everything’ from the acquired firms. Accordingly, each party (i.e., buyer [acquirer], seller [target]) should actively engage in pre- and post-integration process in order to facilitate internalization of the newly obtained resources and further the organization (e.g., Villalonga & McGahn, 2005). While previous studies predominantly have highlighted successful innovation outcomes, and the importance of acquiring external technology/products via M&As, surprisingly, very little research has been conducted on the possibility that acquired technology or products can be exposed by some risks such as product quality failures, i.e., product recall. Although the acquisition can be an effective way to obtain newly, innovative products from the sellers right away, however, it does not necessarily guarantee that the buyers would understand ‘everything’ about the acquired resources. In this proposal, I examine how firms’ efforts to acquire technology and products from external markets through acquisitions could affect their innovation failure rates, which is measured by product recall hazard. Although pursuing acquisitions for external knowledge can be an effective way to speed up the innovation processes of firms competing in high-tech industries, it also may raise other underexplored issues around the management of acquired resources or further organizations. Generally, searching for and coordinating new technologies require heavy investments of time and resources. Acquiring firms may not fully understand or may inaccurately evaluate external knowledge ex ante. Furthermore, organizational dissonance may be created, and the benefit of gaining new resources from acquisitions may decrease ex post. For instance, acquisitions create disruptions among R&D employees that often lead to the loss of specific human capital, subsequently harming post-acquisition innovation performance (e.g., Kapoor & Lim, 2007). Given the complexity of managing the acquisition process and that understanding resources originating from other organizations may be more difficult than understanding resources from inhouse R&D efforts (e.g., Makri, Hitt, & Lane, 2010), managers may be challenged in trying to understand and manage the acquired organization and technology properly to achieve innovation. By incorporating research on value-destroying acquisitions, I propose and empirically test underlying mechanisms that explain the relationship between acquisitions and product failures. I suggest that adverse selection and post-acquisition integration problems impose substantial costs on firms pursuing acquisitions. Externally acquired new technology is an important resource in innovation and new product development in high-technology industries. Although the importance of balancing between external acquisition and internal development has been well documented, there has been little empirical research on the impact of an acquisition decision on new product development and its management. Are there any negative impacts of acquisitions made to obtain new innovative products from the external market? Do acquiring firms have thorough understandings of the technological features of the new products they acquire? In this proposal, applying firm-, product- and patent-level analyses regarding acquisitions and product recalls in the U.S. medical device industry, I will try to find evidence that acquired technology/products via technology acquisitions are more likely to have more ‘quality problems’ since ‘acquisition’ itself is exposed to many problems such as coordination, asymmetry information, and disrupt organization routines and so on.

22602521.label: Project Objectives
22602521.value: -To contribute to ongoing scholarly and popular debates regarding the metaphysics of personal identity (as opposed to, say, the psychological or sociological study of personal identity). -To canvass the relevant philosophical and scientific considerations bearing on the central questions regarding the metaphysics of personal identity, and to make novel contributions to our evaluation of the competing views regarding the metaphysics of personal identity. In particular, I plan to develop an exhaustive trichotomy of possibilities regarding the metaphysics of personal identity (namely, that the self is either simple, composite, or non-existent), and develop novel arguments against each of the possibilities. -To assess the impact of my arguments for agnosticism with respect to the metaphysics of personal identity for our evaluation of certain religious doctrines, including those directly concerned with the nature of the self (e.g., the Buddhist non-self doctrine), as well as religious doctrines concerning the existence (or non-existence) of an afterlife (e.g., the doctrine, common among Abrahamic religions, that human beings will take part in a general resurrection of the dead at some point in the future). -To promote engagement by English-language philosophers with the history of Buddhist philosophical thought, especially as it relates to questions regarding the metaphysics of personal identity. This goal is part of a wider nascent trend within English-language academic philosophy from the last decade or so: English-language philosophers are beginning to move beyond the standard Western philosophical canon to interact with ideas and arguments from other philosophical traditions (e.g., classical Indian Buddhist philosophy). -To assess the impact of my arguments for agnosticism with respect to the metaphysics of personal identity for the feasibility and desirability of emerging technologies, especially cryonics, whole-brain emulation, and the growth of so-called “mini-brains” in labs. -To explore issues relating to moral decision making under conditions of uncertainty. For example, the moral status of abortion is, I will argue, directly related to what we should think about the metaphysics of personal identity (e.g., the question of when we begin to exist, where this is a separate question from when “life” begins to exist, as well as the question of when the developing fetus becomes a “person”). One implication of my arguments is that we should be agnostic regarding the answers to those questions regarding the metaphysics of personal identity which are relevant to the moral status of abortion. I plan to address the question of how we should approach the question of the moral status of abortion, given this uncertainty regarding the metaphysics of personal identity, insofar as that uncertainty is itself a morally relevant consideration which should impact our assessment of the moral permissibility of abortion. -To produce a monograph and a stand-alone article on these issues.

22602521.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
22602521.value: There are two main questions philosophers address when they address the (metaphysical) nature of personal identity: 1.under what conditions is a person at some time identical with someone at some other time? 2.what are we? (Are we, e.g., immaterial souls, physical bodies, brains, something else?) These questions have drawn the attention of philosophers for thousands of years. But, I plan to argue, there are major obstacles to our finding the correct answers to these questions. For there are three exhaustive possibilities, each of which is problematic: 1.we are simple (i.e., things without parts); 2.we are composite (i.e., things with parts); 3.”we” aren’t anything, because we do not exist. Our inability to choose among these three possibilities results in agnosticism with respect to the metaphysics of personal identity. My arguments for this agnosticism are entirely original, and to some extent build off of some of my previous work (especially my “Mereological Nihilism and Personal Ontology”, published in The Philosophical Quarterly). A particularly novel contribution to the ongoing debates regarding personal identity is this: surprisingly, those considerations which have convinced most philosophers to reject the idea that we are each a simple immaterial soul also seem to undermine the standard alternative, that we are each a composite physical object. I will also engage at length with Buddhist arguments for the non-self doctrine, arguments almost completely neglected by English-language philosophers working on the subject of personal identity. My conclusions regarding personal identity have implications which are of broad general interest, both inside and outside of academia. This is because the answers to the central questions regarding personal identity have important practical and moral ramifications, and I plan to discuss at length the implications of my agnosticism regarding personal identity for what we should think of those ramifications. The ramifications include: what religious beliefs to endorse (insofar as certain religions – e.g., Buddhism, Roman Catholicism – take a definitive stance on questions regarding personal identity); whether life after death is possible; whether “cryonics” (freezing dead bodies for future resuscitation), “mind-uploading” (which usually involves whole-brain emulations – i.e., computer simulations of the physical structures associated with a particular human brain), and other transhumanist/futurist approaches to surviving death are feasible and morally permissible; whether the very recent production of “mini-brains” (brain structures grown in labs) is morally problematic; whether abortion is morally permissible. The goal of the project is to produce a monograph and one paper on these subjects. 當哲學家論述人格同一性的（形而上）性質時，他們主要涉及兩個問題。第一，在甚麼情況之下，一個人在某個時間可能與另一個在另一時間是相同？第二，我們是甚麼？例如是非物質的靈魂、物理上的身體、腦袋，或其他？哲學家研究這些問題已有數千年，然而我將會論證，我們就這些問題找尋正確答案會存在的主要障礙。在三個窮盡式可能性中，每一個都存在著問題。第一，我們是簡單的，即是沒有部份的物體。第二，我們是合成的，即有身體部份的物體。第三，「我們」不是任何東西，因為我們沒有存在。我們不可能這三個可能中選擇，導致我們在研究人格同一性的形上學中跌進不可知論。 筆者對不可知論的論證完全是原創的，並部分建基於筆者早前的研究，特別是在The Philosophical Quarterly期刊發表的《分體虛無主義和人格本體論》一文。關於這場對人格同一性的持續不休的辯論，筆者在此給予一個特殊的原創貢獻——在此之前的大部分哲學家在研究此問題時均出乎意外地否決了我們每人都有一個簡單而非物質的靈魂的想法，而這個想法也同時削弱了另一個標準的選擇，即是我們每人都有一個組構而成的物體。筆者亦會在詳細地以佛教的無我教義作為論證，此部分幾乎為以英語為主的研究人格同一性的哲學家所忽視。 筆者相信本研究的成果將對學術界及非學術界均有影響，這是因為對上述關鍵問題的答案均會衍生出實際的和道德上的結果和隱含的後果。筆者將在研究中詳細討論就人格同一性的不可知論，我們應如何處理這些可能的後果和衍生的問題，諸如贊同甚麼宗教信仰（現時部分宗教對人格同一性仍抱有既定的立場，如佛教和羅馬天主教），死後的生命是否可能，人體冷藏學（冷藏死人以待將來科學先進後可以復活的技術）、意識上傳（包括全腦仿真技術，即用電腦模擬已連繫某大腦的運作），或其他超人類主義或未來主義的方法去起死回生等是否可行及在道德上是否可接受，或最近研究的類人腦（在實驗室培育的腦組織）在道德上是否有爭議性，墮胎在道德上是否可接受等。 此研究的目標為出版一本專著和一份學術論文，內容將會探討上述的課題。

22602521.label: Realisation of objectives
22602521.value: My main goal for the project when the project was initiated was to produce a monograph and one stand-alone paper on the topics of the research project. This initial goal has been achieved. I produced a monograph, titled "Personal Ontology: Mystery and Its Consequences," which was published by Cambridge University Press in 2024. And I produced not one, but three stand-alone papers. The papers are titled "Presupposition Failure and Compatibilist Semantics in Ontology", "Personal Identity, Fission, and Arbitrary Pairing", and “Sense Perception and Mereological Nihilism”. The first two papers are not yet published, but they are currently under review by leading academic journals. The third paper has been published in the journal The Philosophical Quarterly. One objective which I modified was the following: I decided not to write about the ethics of abortion under conditions of uncertainty regarding relevant facts regarding personal identity. It turns out I just didn't have anything new to say on the topic which was sufficiently interesting to publish. I say more about this in my mid-project report. However, one of the new papers I wrote which I did not initially plan to write is indirectly related to the ethics of abortion. It discusses, among other topics, whether the possibility of twinning prior to the first 14 or so days of development after fertilization indicates that the zygote prior to that stage of development is not numerically identical with the fetus into which develops. The notion that the zygote this early in fetal development is not numerically identical with the fetus into which it develops is commonly cited as justification for the moral permissibility of the destruction of the zygote prior during the first 14 or so days of development. This idea in turn is commonly cited as justification for policies enacted in many countries which restrict human embryo experimentation to the first 14 days of development. Thus my work on this topic has far-reaching implications for ethics and public policy.

22602521.label: Major findings and research outcome
22602521.value: The major findings of my monograph are conveyed well in the summary of the book: “What are we? Are we, for example, souls, organisms, brains, or something else? In this book I argue that there are principled obstacles to our discovering the answer to this fundamental metaphysical question. The main competing accounts of personal ontology hold that we are either souls (or composites of soul and body), or we are composite physical objects of some sort, but, as I show, arguments for either of these options can be parodied and transformed into their opposites. I also examine arguments for and against the existence of the self, offers a detailed discussion of the metaphysics of several afterlife scenarios - resurrection, reincarnation, and mind uploading -- and consider whether agnosticism with respect to personal ontology should lead us to agnosticism with respect to the possibility of life after death.” Regarding the non-self doctrine, I argue that standard arguments for the non-self doctrine fail, and we have good reason to believe in the self. I also argue that agnosticism with respect to personal ontology should not lead us to agnosticism with respect to the possibility of either resurrection or reincarnation, but that mind uploading has a dubious personal ontology. The content of my three-standalone papers are, in brief: 1.”Sense Perception and Mereological Nihilism”: In the debate over the existence of composite objects, it is sometimes suggested that our perceptual phenomenology justifies belief in composite objects. I argue that this is not the case. 2.”Personal Identity, Fission, and Arbitrary Pairing”: In cases of fission a thing or person splits into two things or persons. It is often thought that in cases of fission the thing or person which fissions could not be numerically identical with one result of fission rather than the other, on the grounds that it would be objectionably arbitrary for the thing or person to end up as one result of fission rather than the other. I show that this sort of argument fails. 3.”Presupposition Failure and Compatibilist Semantics in Ontology”: Call such attempt to reconcile the truth of ordinary assertions with the falsity of the ontology apparently implied by those assertions “compatibilist semantics.” In this paper I develop and defend a compatibilist semantics by appealing to the notion of truth despite (ontological) presupposition failure.

In the monograph which I wrote for this research project I aimed to contribute to these ongoing investigations regarding the metaphysics of personal identity. 22602621.label: Project Objectives
22602621.value: To capture and preserve Hong Kong soundscapes as intangible heritage: There have been few projects on soundscapes in Hong Kong, and there are some institutions which show interest in promoting an awareness of the importance of sound as a way to characterise a sense of place and community. This project aims to further develop this idea through the recording and preservation of sound, with various high quality recordings reflecting different contexts and environments in Hong Kong, and a more comprehensive and systematic approach in data collection. This project aims to encourage the preservation of soundmarks, sounds of local cultural activities, natural and urban sounds, as well as potentially disappearing sounds. It aims to record sounds from the environment, but also to create an oral history archive of Hong Kong by interviewing inhabitants to share stories about places, memories, and their relations with sounds. This project will therefore create an intangible heritage archive about Hong Kong for future generations. To create an accessible online portal for a unique 3D binaural sound experience of Hong Kong: One of the research outputs will take the form of a web-application that will be used to organise, display and experience the different data collected. This online sound map project will create the possibility to experience a sense of place through recordings in binaural audio for headphone listening. With a high degree of accessibility through its online presence and distribution under a Creative Commons copyright license, it will be possible to experience and reuse the work anytime and anywhere, allowing a strong international dissemination of the research. To examine the use of 3D sound to create a tool for interdisciplinary soundscape research and educational purposes: No comprehensive large corpus of ambisonic sound recordings made in Hong Kong exists so far. Once decoded for an array of speakers, or for binaural headphone listening, ambisonic sound will provide a deep engagement for the listeners through an enhanced immersive sense of place. With the help of other data such as the sound level at the time of the recording, it is possible to simulate similar experiences of sound as it would have been experienced in the real location. Thus, this project will become a tool for other researchers in acoustics, urban studies or ethnography to assess and study different sounds or different locations through comparative listening. Because of its accessibility, this research output can also be widely used as educational material for various topics such as audio cultures, geography, ethnography, ecology, tourism or any other field that is related to Hong Kong studies and soundscape studies. To create a digital sound archive of Hong Kong in the 21st century: An archive is not only about the preservation of documents from the past, but in its most interesting definition, it is also a platform to generate new knowledge through various ways of making sense of it, and by creating new forms of engagement with it to reinterpret its content. With the use of metadata that will characterise and be associated with each sound file, this archive could be browsed through various keywords to create or reveal new relations as a way to change the paradigm of the usual simple locative navigation of sound maps. To make a meaningful contribution to positive social change towards sustainable development: Urban planners and policy makers increasingly recognise the role of sound for the well- being of people and for the creation of favourable environments. Providing materials that achieve a great sense of place will be a powerful apparatus for these professionals to investigate both the qualitative and quantitative characteristics of the different locations presented through the variety of the sonorous material presented in the project. To generate innovative ideas for creative art practices: There is a long tradition of sound composition using environmental sound, from concrete music to acousmatic music or soundscape compositions. This archive will be disseminated online under a Creative Commons copyright license, so that other researchers and artists can make use of the sounds to generate new art works with this high-quality sonorous material. One example could be the use of this archive for films, videos or VR works, for instance.
