22602621.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
22602621.value: This research is rooted in both soundscape studies for its research methodology and data collection, and media arts for its outcomes. The field of soundscape studies and acoustic ecology has contributed to raise awareness on our complex relationship with our environment and sense of place through sounds, as well as on the value of sound preservation. In addition, media arts practices such as sound compositions, installations or immersive audio-visual works have also contributed to open up our perception and understanding of environmental sounds. With this particular background, this research project aims to create an online and offline digital archive to experience, reimagine and reinterpret soundscapes from Hong Kong as intangible heritage using 3D sound recording and reproduction technologies. This will be achieved through the use of state-of-the-art ambisonic sound recording technology. Five representative types of landscapes in Hong Kong (new town, old town, village, industrial town, natural environment) will be documented to form the foundation of an archive to preserve the sounds of Hong Kong. Specific metadata will serve to navigate the two actualizations of this archive: a sound map of Hong Kong as a web-application with binaural sounds and a multichannel ambisonic sound installation for an embodied immersive experience. To lead this project successfully different taskforces will be set up to work in parallel. The first phase of the project (2 months) will focus on consolidating the Research Assistant team, selecting the different locations, and to conform the precise protocol to collect data. The second phase of the project (15 months) will be dedicated to field work to capture, edit, analyse, and catalogue the soundscapes and oral histories using metadata. The third phase of the project (11 months) will focus on the creation of the interfaces for both the web application and the interactive sound installation. With the involvement of various grassroots’ communities, cultural organisations, and professional societies in the data collection and as identified users, the project will raise awareness on the importance of studying soundscape not only in terms of noise pollution but also in terms of an interdisciplinary and positive understanding in its role in regards to new form of knowledge of a place, well-being and sustainability. This comprehensive digital archive will not only preserve the sound of Hong Kong as an historical document, but also support creative and interdisciplinary research by contributing material under the Creative Commons License, and a framework to be transferred to different geographical contexts. 三維香港地形圖 本研究以聲景研究和媒體藝術為基礎，前者是研究法及數據收集的依據，後者則為研究結果的呈現。聲景研究與聲學生態有助加深人們對聲音的認識，包括透過聲音與環境及地方感建立的複雜關係，以及保育聲音的價值。另一方面，聲音作品、聲音裝置或沉浸式視聽作品等媒體藝術實踐，均有助打開我們對環境聲音的感知和瞭解。 本研究項目在這種特定背景下，旨在於線上和線下建立一個數碼資料庫，利用三維錄音和重播技術，從非物質遺產的角度體驗、重新想像重新詮釋來自香港的聲景。項目將使用最先進的環境聲音錄音科技來實現。資料庫的基礎將取材自五種代表香港的聲景，包括新市鎮、舊城區、村落、工業城、大自然環境，以紀錄形式保存香港的聲音。資料庫將包括以雙耳聲音建成的網絡版香港聲音地圖，並加設獨特的元數據為使用者導航。 本項目將設多個工作小組同期工作，以實現成功領導。項目首階段為期兩個月，將集中於整合研究助理團隊、選擇不同地點，以及遵從收集數據的精確協定。第二階段為期15個月，將專注於實地工作，收錄、編輯和分析聲景和口述歷史，再以元數據分類。第三階段將為期11個月，主要為網絡版本建立介面。 本項目將有多個基層社群、文化機構和專業團體參與，他們既參與數據收集，也是指定用家。人們可透過本項目更明白聲景研究的重要，瞭解其角色不僅關乎噪音，也是某個地方、其健康狀況和可持續發展上的新型知識，具有跨學科的正面意義。這個全面的數碼資料庫除了可以保存香港的聲音以作為歷史文獻，也可以在共享創意許可下貢獻出材料，再配合一套框架傳送到不同地理環境，支持創意及跨學科研究。

22604221.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
22604221.value: 動畫是不分種族、地理位置、階級、年齡和性別的一種跨國視覺語言。 它跨越國界和地方産業，通過流行的視覺文化將人們聯系在一起。 這一點在以互聯網爲基礎的平台上表現得尤爲明顯。這些平台提供了新的跨國聯系、溝通和合作方式。 對年輕的政治運動人士來說，特別是自2019年3月以來，日本動畫幫助他們表達了對香港政治變化的感受。 實際上，這就形成了新的跨國界的港日社交網絡。 在街頭和互聯網上，視覺文化在抗爭、政治活動和公衆參與中都發揮了至關重要的作用。 通過線上線下的視頻、海報、口號、表情包、繪畫和塗鴉等形式，跨國流行元素已經成爲了政治運動流行肖像學的一部分。 在這一跨國的融合中，日本科幻動畫占據了突出的位置，特別是《星際牛仔》(1998)、《新世紀福音戰士》(1995)、《機動戰士GUNDAM》(1979)和《海賊王》(1999)。 動畫有自己的時空。 因此，它爲創造不同的世界、現實和社會秩序提供了一個文化空間。 基于Sho Konishi的研究，我認爲這種對時間、空間和社會秩序的不同表達能力給動畫賦予無政府主義的意義。 “無政府主義”在這裏指的是一種由平等、合作和互助塑造的另一種世界觀。 這個項目是第一個運用無政府主義的跨國視角來研究動畫和流行視覺文化以了解香港人如何在逆境中通過視覺文化來展開合作的學術研究。 我的主要研究問題有: 1. 香港政治運動人士和非運動人士是如何運用日本動畫來建立跨國網絡，傳播無政府主義價值觀和建立另類的社會秩序與現實思想以挑戰現有的社會秩序呢? 2. 香港正湧現出哪些新的港日跨國關系、文化潮流和網絡的形態? 3. 通過將流行視覺文化視爲超越語言的跨國界語言，我們可以確定哪些新的交流和文化形式; 基于這些觀察，我們可以做出哪些新的理論幹預，這如何挑戰現有的流行視覺文化研究的學科方法，以及它的曆史、社會和文化意義?

22606121.label: Project Objectives
22606121.value: Produce the first comprehensive scholarly monograph about the earliest railroads of Ottoman Anatolia – two lines connecting the port city of Izmir with its fertile hinterland – grounded in an engagement with underutilized Ottoman and European sources. Advance unconventional interdisciplinary perspectives in historical research by exposing the impact of infrastructure’s spatiality on quotidian lifeways and mobilities of the past. My book will foreground histories of technology, environment, tourism, archaeology and the senses. Highlight the complex interplay between the multiple Ottoman and British agencies within the colonialist context of the 19th-century Middle East through an investigation of expertise and failure during major engineering and construction enterprises. Visualize and share multimodal primary sources through a prototype online digital humanities website that will map the historical development of western Anatolian infrastructure. Engender research on the Middle East within the East Asian scholarly community by promoting a comparative approach that explores connections and overlapping processes and actors operating in both West and East Asia during the 19th century.

22606121.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
22606121.value: This research project focuses on the production of railway spaces in western Anatolia (Turkey) during the second half of the 19th century, with an emphasis on how spatial practices were altered with the advent of railways in the region. Understanding the railroads as a cultural as well as a material phenomenon, this work approaches the western Anatolian railways through a series of interdisciplinary vignettes that juxtapose the histories of the built environment with histories of technology, environment, archaeology, travel, and the senses. The primary goal of this project is to complete, for submission to book publishers, a manuscript that explores early Ottoman railroads from multiple historical perspectives. A secondary product will be a prototype digital humanities website for organizing, mapping, and sharing the key primary sources that support the book’s narrative history. In an effort to modernize its transportation infrastructure, the Ottoman government granted the first railway concessions in Anatolia to two British companies. The Izmir-Aydın and Izmir-Kasaba lines connected the prominent eastern Mediterranean port city of Izmir to the fertile valleys of the Gediz and Menderes rivers. The construction of railways was an intensely material act, requiring not only the laying of tracks and the construction of station buildings, but the alteration of a whole landscape. The railroads changed the commercial transportation networks of the region that had depended for centuries on camel caravans traveling along well-established but flexible pathways. People also found a new mobility in the train, including masses of tourists who partook in the ready access to some of the best known ancient and Biblical places of archaeological significance. The railways incited new archaeological explorations that expanded knowledge and facilitated the acquisition of antiquities for museums, private collections and even as construction materials. Additionally, railroads brought with them novel sensory perceptions. From the moment when the first locomotive whistle was heard in Izmir to the illumination of the night, a new and industrial sensorium was woven onto the existing sensory geography of the region. This project aims to produce the first comprehensive scholarly introduction to these early railways, placing their historical significance within a global 19th century. The book will also contribute to the advancement of alternative theoretical frameworks – such as histories of mobility and the senses – thus serving as a resource for scholars working on similar topics in other geographies. The digital humanities companion will invite the public to engage in this history. 這項研究項目將探討安納托利亞西部（土耳其）十九世紀晚期創設的鐵路空間，並分析鐵路的出現如何改變地區的空間實踐 。該項研究將建築環境的歷史與科技、環境、考古、旅遊和感官歷史並列，以跨學科角度理解安納托利亞西部的鐵路為一種文化和物質現象，其中的主要目標是完成一份多角度探索早期鄂圖曼帝國鐵路的手稿以提交給出版商。而研究項目附属的網站可用作組織、標示和提供書中重要的一次文獻資源，並作數位人文學中的范例。奧斯曼政府為了交通基礎設施現代化，把安納托利亞的首個鐵路特許權供讓兩家英國公司。伊茲密爾-艾登線和伊茲密爾-卡薩巴線連通了地中海東部的核心港口城市伊茲密爾和格地茲和曼德列斯河旁肥沃的山谷。鐵路建設改變了整個地區的景觀，除了鋪設軌道和建造車站大樓，亦令當地的商業交通網絡受到很大轉變。 鐵路建設前的幾個世紀，人民一直依賴駱駝商隊沿著完善而靈的道路行駛。然而鐵路提供了更高的流動性，包括大量遊覽著名古蹟和具考古意義聖地的遊客 。鐵路促進了新的考古探索，擴大了文物歷史知識，促進了博物館和私人古物收藏，甚至增加了古物作建築材料的收購。鐵路建設帶來了新的感官知覺，夜幕中第一聲伊茲密爾機車汽笛響起，一個全新的工業感官體驗就融入了當地的感官地理。該項目旨在首次於學術界全面地介紹這些早期鐵路， 將其於歷史意義置於全球化的十九世紀。這本書亦有助于非傳統理論（如流動性和感官歷史）框架的發展，成為研究其他地區相類主題學者的資源。數位人文學的部分更鼓勵公眾與這段歷史增進交流。

22607221.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
22607221.value: The use of prepared musical instruments, or ‘impossible objects’ as I refer to them conceptually, to compose music is not a new phenomenon. However, the existing studies have a limited scope from a single perspective: experimental practices, organology, sound art, instrument building or composition. The proposed research seeks (1) to bridge the gap between these perspectives by articulating a practical and theoretical framework to design, build and compose music using modified instruments; (2) to build upon my past experiences and on existing creative research practices and methods to expand the concept of ‘impossible objects’ by transitioning towards a sculptural approach to music composition, where these objects are recontextualized as sound sculptures within a complex structure as sound installations; and (3) the composition of new chamber works for the JACK Quartet and Vertixe Sonora. In order to produce modified musical instruments and to transition towards an expanded approach where these objects are reimagined as constituent parts within sound installations, in which the physical performance space is also transformed, it is essential to understand their mechanics, therefore collaborating with ensembles, luthiers and instrument makers in the form of experimentation and testing sessions is a fundamental part of the process. In these sessions, the effectiveness, practicality, portability and invasiveness of the objects and structures will be assessed. A comprehensive catalogue of research and audio-visual materials will be compiled and the findings will be outline in three journal articles. In the first one I will propose a practical and theoretical framework to articulate the relationship between sound, music, noise and experimental practices. The second one will be devoted to present the findings and implementation of the research and the third will focus on the collaborative aspects of this kind of project. Finally, as an artist-researcher, my compositional ideas are in constant dialogue with past and future works, hence I organize my pieces as musical cycles. To date BURSZTYN, Spatio-Temporal Cartographies and Archipelago Sierpinski. This project is at the centre of my creative practice as research, and each subsequent development of the processes and approaches will be unequivocally linked to the development of these cycles. I plan to compose two chamber works. The tentative titles of these works are Cartography of Ephemeral Spaces and Aira/Sonora. These works will be performed by the JACK Quartet and Vertixe Sonora as part of their respective concert seasons. The use of prepared musical instruments, or ‘impossible objects’ as I refer to them conceptually, to compose music is not a new phenomenon. However, the existing studies have a limited scope from a single perspective: experimental practices, organology, sound art, instrument building or composition. The proposed research seeks (1) to bridge the gap between these perspectives by articulating a practical and theoretical framework to design, build and compose music using modified instruments; (2) to build upon my past experiences and on existing creative research practices and methods to expand the concept of ‘impossible objects’ by transitioning towards a sculptural approach to music composition, where these objects are recontextualized as sound sculptures within a complex structure as sound installations; and (3) the composition of new chamber works for the JACK Quartet and Vertixe Sonora. In order to produce modified musical instruments and to transition towards an expanded approach where these objects are reimagined as constituent parts within sound installations, in which the physical performance space is also transformed, it is essential to understand their mechanics, therefore collaborating with ensembles, luthiers and instrument makers in the form of experimentation and testing sessions is a fundamental part of the process. In these sessions, the effectiveness, practicality, portability and invasiveness of the objects and structures will be assessed. A comprehensive catalogue of research and audio-visual materials will be compiled and the findings will be outline in three journal articles. In the first one I will propose a practical and theoretical framework to articulate the relationship between sound, music, noise and experimental practices. The second one will be devoted to present the findings and implementation of the research and the third will focus on the collaborative aspects of this kind of project. Finally, as an artist-researcher, my compositional ideas are in constant dialogue with past and future works, hence I organize my pieces as musical cycles. To date BURSZTYN, Spatio-Temporal Cartographies and Archipelago Sierpinski. This project is at the centre of my creative practice as research, and each subsequent development of the processes and approaches will be unequivocally linked to the development of these cycles. I plan to compose two chamber works. The tentative titles of these works are Cartography of Ephemeral Spaces and Aira/Sonora. These works will be performed by the JACK Quartet and Vertixe Sonora as part of their respective concert seasons.

22607421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
22607421.value: In the past several decades, the overall proportion of women in parliaments worldwide has increased substantially and global-level empirical evidence has demonstrated that greater proportions of women in the legislature lead to more promotion of women’s issues, e.g. increased maternity leave, women’s career advancement, domestic violence reduction, or abortion rights. Clear benefits offered to women voters notwithstanding, no systematic research has been conducted to examine the relationship between female legislators’ promotion of women’s issues and its career consequences. To fill this gap, the project investigates to what degree and through what mechanisms female legislators’ face electoral disadvantages when they support issues concerning women voters; moreover, it also examines how the policy-career trade-offs pertinent to women’s issues differs between legislators elected at districts and those elected through party lists. The project focuses on two under-explored countries in the gender politics literature—South Korea and Taiwan—and examines the period between 2008 and 2020. During this period, both counties have seen a substantial increase in women’s presence in the legislature who on average were much more active than their male legislators in promoting women’s issues. In addition, the two countries have adopted a mixed electoral rule (which is composed of district tier and party list tier) during the selected period which allows a rare opportunity to test the influence of electoral systems on legislative behavior as well as related electoral consequences. The proposed project combines both quantitative and qualitative methods to examine the degree and mechanism of policy-career trade-offs. For the quantitative analysis, the project measures the level of legislators’ commitment on women’s issues by creating a dataset that considers both quantity and quality of women’s issue legislation supported by legislators during the period. After that, statistical techniques will be applied to test to what degree a female legislator’s increased level of legislative commitment on women’s issue leads to decrease in her re-election chance. Informed by the results from the quantitative analysis, the qualitative analysis will open up the “black box” of policy-career trade-offs by examining the related mechanisms. For this goal, elite interviews will be conducted with various types of South Korean and Taiwanese legislators to identify how exactly the electoral disadvantages manifest in politics and how informal rules, norms, and practices play a role. The sample will be confined to those who were active in promoting women’s issues during their tenure but faced different electoral fortunes in the subsequent election. 在過去的幾十年裡，世界各地議會中女性的總體比例大幅增加，全球層面的經驗證據表明，立法機構中女性比例越多，更能促進女性的議程，例如增加產假、婦女職業上的發展、減少家庭暴力或墮胎權。儘管這能為女性選民帶來明顯的好處，但尚未有一種系統性的研究, 來查証女性立法者在促進女性的議程及其職業影響之間的關係。為此，該項目調查了在支持與女性選民有關的問題時, 女性立法者在何種程度上以及通過何種機制會面臨選舉劣勢；此外，該項目還研究了與婦女性的議程相關的權衡職業政策在地區選舉的立法者和通過政黨名單當選的立法者之間有何不同。 該項目重點關注性別政治文獻中兩個未被充分探索的國家——韓國和台灣——並考察了 2008 年至 2020 年之間的時期。在此期間，這兩個國家立法機構中的女性人數均大幅增加，她們比男性立法者更積極地推動女性的議程。此外，兩國在選舉時期採用了混合選舉規則（由地區層級和政黨列表層級組成），這為檢驗選舉制度對立法行為的影響以及相關選舉後果提供了難得的機會。 是次擬定計劃了定量和定性研究方法，以驗証權衡職業政策-的程度和機制。於定量分析，本計劃通過創建一個數據集來衡量立法者對女性的議程的承諾兌現程度，該數據集同時考慮了立法者在此期間支持的女性的議程立法的數量和質量。之後，將應用統計技術來測試女性立法者在多大程度上對女性問題的立法承諾會導致其連任機會減少。根據定量分析的結果，定性分析將通過檢查相關機制打開權衡職業政策-的“黑箱”。為此，將與韓國和台灣的各類立法者進行精英訪談，以確定選舉劣勢在政治中的具體表現以及非正式規則、規範和實踐如何發揮作用。樣本將僅限於那些在任職期間積極推動女性的議程但在隨後的選舉中面臨不同選舉命運的人。

22610121.value: 香港同樂運動會語言地景研究

22610121.label: Project Objectives
22610121.value: Deliver in-depth sociolinguistic insights into mass-scale events from an empirically grounded study of the linguistic landscape of the Gay Games 11, an LGBT+ sporting and cultural festival to be held for the first time in Hong Kong in 2020. Draw on these insights to authenticate evidence of the effects the Gay Games event may have on material and symbolic transformations in the host city, its communities, and the wider region. Verify from a discourse analytical perspective how mass-scale events concerned with social emancipation foster actions can help build alignments and solidarities across diverse communities of the city and beyond. Provide data-driven evidence to stakeholders on the impact and benefits of the event, for example by enhancing Hong Kong’s international standing as a forward-thinking global city. Establish the efficacy of team-focused collaborative methods in the research of mass-scale events that capture the dynamic nature of their linguistic landscapes in offline and online spaces from multiple and intersecting perspectives. Improve institutional pedagogy in experiential learning by training local university students in critical language research methods, including ethnographic (digital) linguistic landscape approaches and multimodal discourse analysis.

22610121.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
22610121.value: Mass-scale international events, e.g. festivals or sporting tournaments, temporarily take over their host cities. As such, these events often bring about material benefits in the form of increased visitor numbers and capital, along with symbolic and discursive changes, as host cities are rebranded as modern and attractive spaces/destinations. Language is integral to these spatial/discursive practices, as the ‘linguistic landscape’ (LL) of these events is shaped by various semiotic actions that not only promote but also redefine the places in which the event is held. This project focuses on the LL of an international sporting and cultural LGBT+ event, the Gay Games 11, that will take place in Hong Kong in 2022. As this is the first time that such a major LGBT+ event will be held in Asia, it is expected that the LL of the Games will be constructed via considerations of the local. That is, the Games, conceived in the West and defined by its core messages of modernity, e.g. inclusivity and diversity, will be redefined as it crosses into the more ‘traditional’ Hong Kong space; a local space which, like all spaces, is intimately linked to broader phenomena including discourse, identity, and politics. However, as above, this redefinition also brings with it the potential for transformation. In other words, ‘traditional’ or ‘fixed’ understandings of Hong Kong, its citizens, its communities and its identities, may be re-imagined through the Gay Games event and the emancipatory messages it brings. In order to investigate these potentials, and their effects on images of Hong Kong and Asia, I focus on the actions of those who construct and interact with the LL of the Games. Using a multi-sited ethnographic approach, I will track these actions across the LL from intersecting perspectives, engaging with both the organisers of the games and its participants/spectators, and drawing on data from both offline and online spaces. Experiential participation in the LL is key to this project, and so I operationalize a team-focused approach to data collection by working with a group of 10-15 student participants who will record their experiences of the LL collaboratively, using traditional and digital tools. Accordingly, the analysis will be conducted from these multiple and intersecting perspectives, allowing for in-depth insights into how the actions, brought about by this mass-scale queer event, may redefine the local, and foster a legacy of material and symbolic transformation in Hong Kong and beyond. 節慶和體育等大型國際活動對主辦城市影響甚大，這些活動不但吸引訪客和資本，帶來物質利益，同時主辦城市透過舉行活動，定位成現代化及具吸引力的地方，從象徵和話語上帶來改變。由於這些活動的「語言地景」是由不同的符號行為塑造而成，它們既具推廣作用，亦重新定義舉辦活動的空間，故此語言對空間／話語的實踐不可或缺。 本計劃集中於國際LGBT+活動第十一屆同樂運動會的語言地景，該次運動會將於2022年在香港舉行。由於亞洲首次舉行此類大型主要LGBT+活動，預期同樂運動會語言地景的建構，亦會考量到本地情況。同樂運動會源自西方，主要信息為包容及多元，而當進入香港相對「傳統」的空間，這些核心信息也會隨之重新定義。 一如其他空間，本地空間同樣與廣泛現象環環相扣，例如話語、身份及政治，然而，如上所述，重新定義亦會帶來改變的潛力。換而言之，隨著同樂運動會的活動及其解放的信息，對香港及其市民、社群、身份的「傳統」和「既有」理解，也會因而重新受到想像。 為了研究此活動的潛力，以及它們對香港及亞洲形象的影響，我將集中研究建構同樂運動會語言地景，以及與之互動的人。本研究將採取多點民族誌的方式，從不同角度的交匯點，追蹤過些在語言地景的行為，接觸同樂運動會的主辨者、參與者及觀眾，並研究線上及線下空間的資料。在語言地景的體驗式參與是本研究的重心，因此我將邀請十至十五位學生，以小組方式參與收集資料，使用傳統及電子工具，紀錄他們在語言地景的參與。研究將通過這些多點及交匯的角度進行分析，進而深入了解是次大型的酷兒活動，如何重新定義本地，以及促進活動對香港及其他地方帶來在物質及符號上的影響。

22611821.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
22611821.value: 在过去的几年中，经济全球化的进程明显放缓，甚至出现了逆全球化的趋势。在这个大背景下，本文首先试图解释这种看似退步的逆全球化现象是否可能是某种基本面变化所引发的理性选择， 同时也试图提供在逆全球化过程中关于政府干预的政策建议。 本项目将通过构造一个多国家多部门的经济周期模型，量化考察逆全球化对某一国家经济波动风险的影响。设想在一个国际化的经济体中，其基本面的变化由两种因素引起，一是以国家为单位的冲击，二是以产业为单位的冲击。同时，不同国家的不同产业由全球供应链连接起来，从而进一步传导或放大基本面冲击的影响。在这种经济环境中，我们发现参与逆全球化进程有可能是一个国家的理性选择。 当一个国家更多地参与到全球产业链的分工当中，那么发生在其自己国家的冲击所带来的影响将很大程度上被规避。但同时，当进入全球化分工，一个国家将自然地按照比较优势的理论专注于一个或几个特殊的产业，同时这个国家将对基于产业的冲击非常敏感。相反地，当一个国家退出全球产业链的分工，它将被迫进入到多种行业的生产。这将导致其对于基于本国的国家性冲击非常敏感，但同时可以规避很多基于具体产业的冲击。一种可能的情形是在过去十年中，基于产业的冲击成为基本面的主要因素。在这种情况下，如果一个国家政府的目标是降低本国国内生产总值的波动时，那么逆全球化将成为最优的政策选择。更为重要的一个观察则是逆全球化会增加还是降低一个国家经济波动的风险取决于政府政策对于逆全球化趋势的应对。 作为一个参考标准，我们首先考察一个没有任何政府干预的基准模型。为了与其相比较，我们将拓展基准模型使其允许发生三种不同的政策干预：第一种是财政政策干预，政府可以使用财政支出和转移支付熨平经济波动。这种政策更多的是在国家宏观层面施行，因而对于降低以国家为单位的冲击更为有效。第二种是贸易政策，例如关税或进出口配额。这种政策可以相对灵活的针对具体产业和具体国家，因而对于降低以产业为单位的冲击和其他国家的国家性冲击更为有效。第三种是给与个别产业税收优惠或补贴的产业政策。这种政策可以调节不同产业之间的相对重要性，从而规避以产业为单位的冲击。这些分析表明在全球化或者逆全球化的进程中，一个国家经济波动的变化将依赖于政府经济政策的类型和经济政策施行的强度。

22611821.label: Realisation of objectives
22611821.value: 1. To build a simple multi-country multi-sector business cycle model. To derive the additive decomposition of sector-country specific shocks into sector-level shocks and country-level shocks. To fulfill the first objective, I developed a 27 country, 28 sector business cycle model that embeds dynamic capital accumulation, contract based labor, an Armington specification for final demand, iceberg trade costs, and a fully articulated input output network. The model is solved with two complementary methods: (i) log linearizing the equilibrium conditions to obtain a first order system characterized by an impact matrix, and (ii) computing an exact “hat algebra” solution that provides a nonlinear benchmark against which the linear approximation is validated. To derive and implement the additive decomposition of country–sector productivity shocks, I first compute Solow residuals from the KLEMS input–output data. Each residual is then factorized into a country component, a sector component, and an idiosyncratic remainder. Estimating this specification in rolling ten year windows over 1970–2020 produces a time series profile of volatility that cleanly separates sector level from country level contributions. 2. To quantitatively evaluate the response of GDP fluctuation to country-sector specific shocks. To take a stand on global influence matrix. To explore the logic behind the trend of deglobalization. To evaluate the response of GDP fluctuation to shocks, I first established a tractable impulse response apparatus by deriving both a static mapping, and a dynamic law of motion for labor and capital that nests within this mapping. The static component provides closed form elasticities of every country–sector output with respect to any granular productivity shock, while the dynamic one extends the framework to include adjustment in factor inputs over time . Armed with these formulas, I fed in (i) actual TFP, country level and sector level shocks recovered from the KLEMS–WIOT data set, and (ii) a battery of counterfactual unit shocks, allowing them to compute the full distribution of model implied GDP volatilities under unilateral and multilateral trade cost scenarios. Central to the exercise is the general equilibrium “global influence matrix.” Unlike a conventional Leontief inverse, this matrix embeds price feedbacks and trade share reallocations that arise because intermediate input costs and final good prices co move with shocks. The paper formally derives this object and shows how the additional price terms alter propagation relative to a pure quantity network. The empirical section documents a post 2010 surge in the ratio of sector level to country level volatility, signaling a heightened macroeconomic cost of specialization. Concurrently, tariff data reveal that most countries raised barriers after 2010. Model simulations rationalize these patterns: because trade openness amplifies GDP volatility—especially when sector shocks dominate—countries whose output is more sensitive to country level shocks still gain from openness, whereas those exposed primarily to sector shocks reduce trade to mitigate risk. Hence, the observed “de globalization” is interpreted not as a reversal of comparative advantage but as an endogenous policy response to a shifting shock structure. 3. To extend the benchmark model to allow active policy interventions. To see that with active policy interventions, what is the impact of deglobalization on GDP volatility? On the other hand, to investigate what intensity of policy intervention reverses globalization versus deglobalization choice. I generalized the benchmark production network framework by making trade cost from an exogenous calibration to a fully manipulable policy variable. I coded an algorithm that, for any tariff vector, recomputes a new steady state, updates trade shares and prices, and then feeds these values into both the linear impact matrix solution and an exact hat algebra check. Because the solver accepts arbitrary tariff vectors, it accommodates unilateral moves (one country alone adjusts its barriers) as well as symmetric multilateral shifts in which all partners alter tariffs by the same proportion. Simulations under the contemporaneous 2011 20 shock process revealed that, for nearly every economy, higher trade costs muted the amplification effect of sector level shocks and hence reduced real GDP volatility. The model was run on a fine grid of tariff changes ranging from a 50 percent cut to a 50 percent hike around the zero cost baseline, executed in both unilateral and multilateral modes. Results indicate that in economies whose volatility is dominated by sector level shocks, even a modest 10 percent tariff cut raises volatility enough to make further liberalization unattractive, whereas country shock dominated economies require tariff reductions of roughly 20 percent before the gains from trade begin to offset the heightened risk. 4. To discuss the optimal policy where a combination of fiscal, trade and industry policies is available to the policy makers. I formalized government behavior by adding a simple loss function—minimization of real GDP volatility—to the production network model and by elevating bilateral iceberg tariffs parameters to policy levers. The project shows, in numbers, how tariff changes affect GDP volatility and identifies the break point tariff at which each country would choose to open up or pull back. Fiscal and industrial policies, however, are not yet modeled, so this objective is only partly achieved. This was intentional: (a) tariffs are the quickest and most widely used lever for redirecting trade flows, and (b) fiscal and industrial measures work over much longer horizons. To keep the study focused and practical, they were left for future work.

22611821.label: Major findings and research outcome
22611821.value: I build a data driven, multi country–multi sector production network model (27 countries × 28 sectors, 1970 2020) that nests dynamic capital, contract based labour and observed input output linkages. A new additive decomposition breaks country sector TFP shocks into clean country level and sector level components, estimated from EU/World KLEMS and WIOT data. This yields a 10 year rolling time series that tracks the rise and fall of sector level risk relative to country level risk—falling through the 1980 2000 globalization wave and climbing sharply after 2010, consistent with today’s “deglobalization” narrative. Closed form static and dynamic impulse response formulas give an exact global influence matrix. Feeding empirical shocks into the model reproduces observed GDP volatility. The key quantitative result is that greater trade openness always raises GDP volatility once real world trade shares replace the “cheapest supplier” assumption; diversification gains cannot offset the amplification of shocks. Policy experiments promote bilateral tariffs to active instruments. Simulations of the actual post 2010 tariff hikes show that most countries lowered GDP volatility by raising barriers, precisely because sector level shocks had become more important. A grid search identifies tariff thresholds: a 10% cut is enough to raise volatility in sector shock sensitive economies, while country shock sensitive economies require 20–30% cuts before trade gains exceed added risk . These findings overturn the recent claim that openness stabilizes GDP through country diversification. Instead, both country and sector shocks increase volatility, but their relative weights drive heterogeneity in policy responses. The study also offers the first quantitative evidence that the current swing toward deglobalization is a rational attempt to dampen volatility, not a purely political reversal.

22611821.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
22611821.value: Future work can broaden the model along three fronts. 1.Policy scope: One can embed budget balanced fiscal tools (counter cyclical transfers, consumption taxes) and sector specific subsidies in the optimization. 2.Risk return trade offs: A welfare module can be added so that policy is chosen to maximise expected utility—trading off mean growth against volatility—rather than minimising volatility alone. 3.Financial and regional channels: Introducing international borrowing constraints and sub national input output data can reveal how credit frictions and local clusters amplify or dampen shocks.

22611821.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
22611821.value: Why do some countries suddenly talk about “deglobalizing”—raising tariffs and pulling factories back home? Our research shows it often comes down to swings in economic risk. Using detailed records for 27 countries and 28 industries since 1970, we built a computer model that tracks how shocks—such as an oil price spike or a war—spread through global supply chains and shake national GDP. The model lets us “turn the dial” on tariffs and watch what happens to each country’s economic ups and downs. We find that opening trade usually raises volatility, especially when shocks hit specific industries (think microchips or oil). After 2010 those industry level shocks grew larger, so many governments rightly raised tariffs to calm the turmoil. Our work gives policymakers a clear dashboard: it quantifies how much a tariff cut or hike will change GDP stability and pinpoints the tipping point tariff at which their country should switch between “globalize” and “protect.”

22612121.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
22612121.value: Hong Kong schools are becoming increasingly digitized and beginning English language (EL) teachers need to develop appropriate skills to respond to such digital needs. The integration of technology into primary and secondary EL classrooms has been promoted by the Education Bureau and its utilization is growing with digital technologies becoming embedded in teachers’ practices (Hong Kong Education Bureau, 2014). Furthermore, EL teachers have a prominent role in developing students’ digital literacies and competencies with an overall aim of the English Language Education Key Learning Areas Curriculum (Hong Kong Education Bureau, 2017) being, “to enable every student to prepare for the changing socio-economic demands resulting from advances in information technology…”. However, research shows that Hong Kong EL teachers feel unprepared to utilize technology (Bai et al., 2019). If beginning teachers do not feel adequately prepared, this may affect their self-efficacy, quality of teaching, their commitment to the profession, and, ultimately, students’ learning experiences. Despite the prominent role technology is increasingly playing in language classrooms, there is no context and subject-specific framework detailing the digital competencies Hong Kong EL teachers need to ensure readiness for the teaching profession. This study aims to identify the competencies beginning EL teachers’ need in order to be ready for schools, while proposing ways to address gaps in beginning teachers’ competencies. Teacher professional digital competencies (PDC), the mastery of “a range of teacher competencies such as being able to teach in a digitally infused context, manage digital learning environments and carry out the broader professional work of being a teacher” (Starkey, 2020, p49), provides a theoretical foundation for this study. • In the first stage, a survey and follow-up interviews will be conducted with EL teachers in Hong Kong to better understand the current digital practices in schools and the PDC teachers are required to master upon entry to the profession. • In the second stage, documents pertaining to EL teacher education programmes (e.g. BEd & PGDE) in Hong Kong will be analyzed, along with focus group interviews with teacher educators, pre-service teachers and beginning teachers. Combined, these will be used to evaluate how current teacher education programmes support teachers in developing PDC. Ultimately, this study will provide insights into how programmes can better prepare teachers. The study is unique in that it will generate a context and subject-specific PDC framework, that can ensure teacher preparation programmes meet the needs of increasingly digitized schools. 香港學校越來越數碼化，初級英語 (EL) 教師需要發展適當的技能來應對此類數碼需求。教育局已提倡將科技融入中小學英語課堂。隨著數碼科技融入教師的課堂，科技的使用不斷增加 (Hong Kong Education Bureau, 2014). 此外，爲了課程的總體目標以實現英語重點學習領域，初級英語教師在培養學生的數碼閲讀和數碼能力方面發揮著重要的角色 (Hong Kong Education Bureau, 2017)，讓每個學生都能為科技資訊進步而不斷變化的社會經濟需求做好準備然而，研究顯示香港初級英語教師覺得還有未充分準備好使用科技 (Bai et al., 2019) 。如果新教師沒有充分做好準備，可能會影響他們的自我效能感、教學質素、他們對專業的承諾，並最終影響學生的學習體驗。儘管在語言課堂中善用科技越來越重要，但沒有具體的背景和特定學科框架詳細說明香港初級英文教師的專業需要，確保為作爲教師的職業做好準備。 本研究旨在確認初級英語教師需要具備的能力，以便為教學做好準備，並同時提出解決初級教師能力差距的方法。 教師專業數碼能力 (PDC)，本研究提供了基礎理論 以提供 “一系列教師須有的能力，例如能夠在數碼化環境中教學、管理數碼學習環境，以及開展更廣泛的教師專業工作”之掌握。（Starkey，2020， p49)， • 第一階段會與香港的初級英語教師進行調查和跟進訪談，以便更深入地了解學校目前的數碼學習情況及教師在踏入該行業時必須掌握的教師專業數碼能力。 • 第二階段將分析與香港 初級英語 教師教育計劃（例如 BEd 和 PGDE）有關的文件，以及與教師導師、職前教師和新教師進行焦點小組訪談。 綜合起來，這些將用於評估現時老師培訓課程怎樣支持及培育教師的專業數碼能力。 最後，這項研究將提供見解以闡述相關課程如何可以有效地幫助老師準備數碼能力。 該研究的獨特之處，在於它將為背景和相關學科的教師專業數碼能力做出一個框架，可以確保教師培訓課程可以滿足學校日益數碼化的需求

22612121.label: Realisation of objectives
22612121.value: Overall, the three research objectives were achieved. As reported in the mid-term report, activities related to the first stage of the study pertaining to objective 1 and objective 2 were carried out and successfully addressed the objectives. In the second stage, activities pertaining to the third objective were conducted and addressed the objective. Some additional activities were added to enhance the original study design to achieve the objectives better. Furthermore, during the project period, there were significant technological advancements in generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) that could impact on English language teachers' contextual and subject-specific professional digital competencies in Hong Kong. This led to additional research questions being added in the second stage to explore the ways teacher education programs have been affected by GenAI and early-career teachers' readiness for using GenAI in language teaching. The details of each study stage and related objectives are presented below. Some of the stage one details were provided in the mid-term report for the period ending 30-9-2022. Stage One In stage one, objectives one and two were addressed: 1. An extensive literature review of literature about English language teachers' use of digital technologies for teaching was conducted. This included a systematic review of technology reviews in language teaching and learning journals using professional digital competence (PDC) as a conceptual framework to understand the knowledge provided in the reviewed articles and its usefulness for teaching with technology. These reviews helped inform the development of the research tools and the framework referred to in objective 2. This additional research activity enhanced the study and achievement of objectives 1 and 2. 2. The survey tool was designed, piloted, and disseminated to the target participants. The tool went through two rounds of piloting. In the first round of piloting 5 teacher educators reviewed the draft survey and gave comments on its completeness, comprehensiveness and clarity. It was then piloted with 10 English language teachers. It was revised and finalized. It was finally disseminated to the target participants from April to May 2022. In total 83 valid responses to the survey were received. This was below the target number of 300, but due to the qualitative nature of the survey design, the responses provided a rich description of the use of technology by teachers in Hong Kong schools. The demographic information showed the dataset reflected the teaching context in Hong Kong. The survey results have been analyzed with a context-specific and subject-specific PDC framework for beginning EL teachers developed. 3. Follow-up interviews were conducted in July-August 2022. In total 22 teachers were interviewed. This was above the original target of 20 teachers. The interviews were conducted either face-to-face or via video-conferencing software following the preferences of the interviewees. The interviews lasted between 30-55 minutes and were audio-recorded and transcribed. The interviews were analysed. 4. The data collected through the literature review, survey, and follow-up interviews has allowed for the identification of the professional digital competencies beginning English language teachers in Hong Kong need to enter schools that are becoming increasingly digitized and the development of a context and subject-specific PDC framework that details the competencies beginning English language teachers are expected to master upon completion of initial teacher education. In total, three research articles have been published regarding the findings from the first stage of the study, including an article presenting the PDC framework. Stage Two In stage two, objective three was addressed: 1. Policy and curriculum documents of the four publicly funded teacher education institutions were reviewed. This included programme websites, student handbooks and course descriptions to understand how teacher education programmes are preparing pre-service teachers for use of technology. We were able to successfully gather documents from all four institutions from official sources e.g., program websites. The documents were subjected to content analysis with an overview of each institution created. These included number of technology-related mandatory and elective pedagogical courses and programme and course learning outcomes related to technology. 2. Focus group and individual interviews: As the documents reflected the intended policies and curriculum, interviews with teacher educators, beginning teachers and first-year teachers were also conducted. The data were analysed inductively using thematic analysis approach proposed by Braun and Clarke (2006). a. Thirteen teacher educators representing all four teacher education providers were interviewed. Although initially, I planned to conduct focus group interviews, they were interviewed individually due to scheduling challenges. Semi-structured interviews were conducted between 19 April and May 11, 2023. An interview guide was developed for the study based on the document review, stage one findings, and relevant literature. Additional questions pertaining to GenAI and teacher education were added to reflect technological advancements. b. Ten beginning teachers and seventeen first-year English language teachers were interviewed in groups or individually, depending on preference and availability. Two similar interview guides were developed for the two groups to reflect the differences in the stage of their teaching career (pre-service /in-service). Additional questions pertaining to GenAI and teacher education were added to reflect technological advancements. For example, the guide for first-year teachers asked if they had used GenAI tools in their teaching or if their students had used GenAI tools and how they were used. The questions helped guide the interviews however, each interview was unique, and the researcher used the participants’ responses as springboards for more profound reflections and responses. The interviews were conducted in English and lasted between 30 and 65 min. They were audio-recorded and transcribed verbatim for analysis. In total, two research articles have been published regarding the findings from the second stage of the study.

22612121.label: Major findings and research outcome
22612121.value: (1) The study identified how English language teachers' use technology in their professional practices and the context and subject-specific bidirectional relationship between digital tools, their affordances, and teachers' professional tasks. These findings can inform school leaders and teacher education on ways to prepare teachers for different technological realities. These findings were reported in Moorhouse and Yan (2023). (2) The study identified the professional digital competencies beginning English language teachers need to begin teaching in Hong Kong and developed a competency framework. The framework consists of five aspects: Technological proficiency; Pedagogical compatibility; Preparing students for the digital world; Risk, well-being and ethical awareness and Professional work. Each aspect includes ability statements. The framework can be used to evaluate existing teacher education programmes, support the development of pre-service English-language teachers and facilitate teacher assessment. The elements of PDC can be converted into programme- and course-level learning. In addition, the methods used to develop the framework can be used by scholars to develop localised frameworks. The findings were reported in Moorhouse, Kohnke, and Chiu (2024). (3) The study provided a comprehensive review of the digital tools available for use by English language teachers, including the features and pedagogical uses of these tools. The review also provided insights into the genre of technology reviews and the content of these reviews, with recommendations on how the reviews can better meet the needs of teachers. The findings were reported in Moorhouse, Kohnke and Wan (2023). (4) The study found that initial teacher education programs in Hong Kong are not fully developing beginning teachers’ PDC. Most programmes do not having a specific course or learning outcomes about technology. However, there are differences between different institutions. Teacher educators acknowledge the need for increased emphasis on PDC development. The development of GenAI has accelerated this need. The findings can inform teacher educators on how to integrate PDC development into programmes and courses. Findings were reported in Moorhouse and Kohnke (2024). (5) The study found that beginning English language teachers in Hong Kong do not feel prepared to use technology for teaching. However, first-year teachers have found that Generative AI can assist them in adapting to school contexts. The findings suggest teacher education programmes need to integrate GenAI competence development into learning outcomes, courses and programmes to increase students’ readiness for teaching with GenAI. Findings were reported in Moorhouse (2024)

22612121.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
22612121.value: Given the rapid development of technology and its implication for language teaching and learning, there is substantial scope for further development of this research. As the study found, the development of GenAI is having a profound effect on initial language teacher education, bringing both affordances that pre-service teachers can be prepared to utilize, as well as disruptions, which teachers need awareness of and skills to address. This study was conducted as these technologies were emerging. There is a need for further studies to explore how these technologies may be changing language teachers' professional practices and what this means for pre-service language teacher education. The next step would be to examine the utilisation of these technologies in school contexts to assist teachers in implementing good practices, in order to, understand how they can be effectively deployed in English language educational contexts. To this end, I have submitted a GRF proposal to explore how GenAI can facilitate differentiated instruction. Such explorations can inform teacher education programs on how to prepare pre-service teachers to use GenAI and other technologies to support their professional practices.

22612121.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
22612121.value: The study explored the context‐ and subject‐specific professional digital competence (PDC) beginning English language teachers in Hong Kong need to begin their careers in teaching and how teacher education programmes are preparing pre-service teachers' PDC. The study included a two-stage research design using multiple data collection methods. The study identified how English language teachers’ use technology in their professional practices and the context and subject-specific bidirectional relationship between digital tools, their affordances, and teachers’ professional tasks. It led to the development of a context and subject-specific PDC framework consists of five aspects: Technological proficiency; Pedagogical compatibility; Preparing students for the digital world; Risk, well-being and ethical awareness and Professional work. In addition, it was found that initial teacher education programs in Hong Kong are not fully developing beginning teachers' PDC, and beginning teachers do not feel fully prepared to use technology for language teaching. The effects of generative artificial intelligence on language teacher education and language teachers' readiness to use these technologies for teaching were also explored. The study has implications for the initial education of language teachers, providing suggestions for ways teacher education programs can integrate the aspects of PDC into learning outcomes, program content, and classroom activities.

23100221.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
23100221.value: 野生動物種群的管理常受限於缺乏對多種人為和自然因素的了解。為了有效管理受到多種因素威脅而日益減少的野生動物種群，我們必須了解這些因素對種群的相對影響以及它們之間的關係。 香港瘰螈是香港唯一的有尾目動物，近年研究發現，自然因素如棲息地森林覆蓋率是決定該物種生存率的重要因素。香港瘰螈種群受到多種人為因素（例如森林砍伐、路殺、河流污染）的威脅。儘管如此，上述人為因素的實際影響以及化學防禦（即河魨毒毒性）、疾病和寄生蟲等自然因素的作用在很大程度上是未知的。我計劃通過繼續和擴展香港瘰螈的標放研究，結合長期數據、遙感、疾病篩查、寄生蟲移除實驗，了解人為因素和自然因素對香港瘰螈種群的相對強度和動態。 使用綜合研究方法（生態學、生物化學、環境研究和統計學），我希望發現有關香港蠑螈的新生態知識。這項研究將嘗試了解新出現的野生動物疾病對其原生宿主的影響以及野生動物種群的自然和人為因素之間的動態關係的重要性。更重要的是，這項研究的結果將使地方當局能夠實施針對特定物種的保護措施，以防止這種受威脅物種的進一步減少，並指導未來對當地瀕危野生動物的研究

23100221.label: Realisation of objectives
23100221.value: To accomplish the proposed objectives, we rely mainly on conducting mark-recapture surveys in breeding pools of Hong Kong newt populations and collecting samples to determine their skin toxicity and disease prevalence. In addition to the mark-recapture surveys, we also conducted systematic surveys to determine the magnitude and severity of an anthropogenic threat (i.e. roadkill). An MPhil student was recruited to carry out most of the data collection and subsequent analyses. We have conducted various research activities and accomplished most of the objectives that we initially set out. Objective 1 (Addressed 100%) We conducted field surveys to assess the ectoparasite burden and prevalence of salamander chytrid fungus (Bsal) in wild Hong Kong newt populations. In total, 2,273 adult Hong Kong newts from 6 populations were sampled during three consecutive breeding seasons. The number of water mites on each newt and morphological data (i.e., body size and weight) of the newts were recorded. In terms of ectoparasite burden (represented by the count of water mites), there were apparent temporal and spatial variations among the six populations examined. Prevalence is high (84.2-100%) in three populations, and mites were not detected at all (prevalence 0%) in the other three populations. The infestation intensity of both life stages of water mites increased gradually during the breeding season of P. hongkongensis, indicating that the parasitism pattern is dynamic rather than static. This data has been used in the modeling done in objective 4. We collected 127 skin swaps from 5 populations to test for salamander chytrid fungus (Bsal) using a nested PCR primer set described in Guo et al. (2023). None of the skin swaps we collected were positive for Bsal. This is not surprising, given that the prevalence of Bsal in Hong Kong is known to be very low (<2%) in the 15 populations surveyed previously for a territory-wide survey (Guo et al., 2023). Chytrid was absent in 12 out of 15 populations sampled and detected only in 5 out of 293 samples collected. In the present study, we surveyed 5 out of the 15 sites previously sampled by Guo et al. (2023), including one known positive site. Our results further confirm the prevalence of Bsal in Hong Kong newt populations, but it also means that the disease is unlikely to be a significant factor for survival of the newts. Objective 2 (Addressed 80%) We attempted to quantify the skin toxicity of Paramesotriton hongkongensis using three different non-invasive sampling methods. The first method involved taking a small skin biopsy from the dorsal side of the animal using a biopsy punch. The skin biopsy will then be stored in a microcentrifuge tube containing an acetic acid solution until further processing. The second method involved placing the animal in a clear plastic bag for 1 minute while applying gentle pressure to simulate toxin secretion, which is visible as white mucus. Plastic bags containing toxin secretion were transferred back to the laboratory, where they were air-dried. The dried white mucus from each plastic bag was then transferred to microcentrifuge tubes containing an acetic acid solution until further processing. The third method involved placing the animal on a transparent plastic plate. Gentle pressure was applied, and the secretion was collected similarly to the second method. In total, 1081 skin biopsy samples were collected with the first method, and 386 and 20 skin secretion samples were collected with the second and third methods, respectively. The first method was a non-invasive method described in a paper by our collaborator at UC Davis, and it has since been used by several other researchers interested in skin toxicity in salamanders. The second and third methods were new methods designed to bypass the biopsy procedure, which could be stressful for the animal. All the toxicity samples were sent to our collaborator in UC Davis for quantification using High Performance Liquid Chromatography-Mass Spectrometry (HPLC-MS). We were able to quantify the amount of TTX in 1081 biopsy samples (method 1) processed following the procedures described in Bucciarelli et al. (2014). Unfortunately, despite repeated attempts to condition the samples collected with methods 2 and 3 for HPLC-MS, we failed to detect TTX in those samples. For unknown reasons, the skin secretion did not dissolve in the acetic acid. We did not pursue other methods for quantifying TTX concentrations in our skin secretion samples. Despite that, we were able to assess and quantify TTX concentration of over 1000 wild Hong Kong newts from 6 populations using the method described in Bucciarelli et al. (2014). This data has been used in the modeling done in objective 4. Objective 3 (Addressed 100%) Other than deforestation, roadkill has been identified as a main anthropogenic threat to Hong Kong newts. Mass mortality events have been documented in various sites where tens to hundreds of newts are killed by crossing vehicles. To better understand the magnitude of this problem, we systematically surveyed four sites during the migration season to quantify the number of roadkill in Hong Kong at each site. Using the data collected, we were able to identify factors that contribute to the probability of a mass mortality event (MMEs) for this species. The model suggested that relative humidity and traffic contributes to increased probability of MMEs. Objective 4 (Addressed 75%) Our data from three years of capture-mark-release surveys in 4 Hong Kong newt populations enable us to assess the effects of ectoparasite burden (Objective 1) and skin toxicity (Objective 2) on the survival probability of Hong Kong using Cormack-Jolly-Seber mark-recapture models. This work has not been completed because we are still waiting for our collaborators from the US to send us the toxicity data from the biopsy samples collected in our third-year survey (October 2024 to January 2025). A preliminary analysis has been done with the incomplete data set. Results from this analysis indicate that skin toxicity (TTX concentration) and body condition (measured with scaled mass index) both had positive effects on the survival of newts. The remaining analysis will be completed once we have the whole data set, preferably by the end of Q2 2025. Objective 5 (Addressed 50%) The salamander chytrid disease does not appear to be a primary threat to this species, given the low prevalence found in an earlier study and from our sampling conducted for this project. We suspect that Hong Kong is a ‘cold spot’ for this disease, and until other evidence (e.g., repeated observations of symptomatic individuals in the wild) suggest otherwise, regular monitoring and a dedicated disease monitoring protocol may not be necessary for this species. Currently, there is no conservation action plan for this species, as their populations are thought to be stable. We have reached out to Agriculture, Fisheries and Conservation Department about the possibility of formulating an action plan but there was no there seemed to be no interest. We were told that the department has conducted disease monitoring for local amphibians, but they have no intention to make such data publicly available. We are planning to conduct a press release to about our recommendations on roadkill mitigation measures in Q2 2025.

23100221.label: Major findings and research outcome
23100221.value: We quantified population-level tetrodotoxin toxicity of Hong Kong newts by taking skin biopsy samples from >1000 wild newts. Their skin toxicity appears to be comparable to species of newts in Japan and the US. Skin toxicity varied significantly within and among populations. Male newts also exhibited a phase-specific difference in their TTX concentration (i.e., individuals collected in terrestrial phase were 3 times less toxic than those collected in aquatic phase), which, to the best of my knowledge, has not been documented in any other toxin-bearing amphibians. This finding highlights the complexity of the dynamics of amphibian defensive compounds and hints at additional functions (e.g., interspecific communication) played by these compounds. A paper is being prepared for the journal Toxicon and will be submitted for review in Q2/3 2025. This process is delayed because we discovered an error in unit conversion while preparing the manuscript for submission. This discovery significantly altered the paper's narrative, so we must rewrite the entire discussion section. Another significant finding from this research is the population dynamics of the parasitic water mite that parasitizes newts. We learned that the population size of these parasites oscillates with that of their host salamanders, and the presence and intensity of host-parasite association of a given population tend to be consistent over time. Interestingly, we observed water mites attached to juvenile Hong Kong newt, which has not been reported elsewhere. To our surprise, the water mite does not appear to be affected by the newt’s toxins, and the newt does not seem to be affected negatively by the mites. We suspect the water mites may have site-specific mutations in their voltage-gated sodium channels, enabling them to withstand toxins from their host. This will be further investigated in an upcoming project, pending approval from the funding body. A paper is being prepared for the journal International Journal for Parasitology: Parasites and Wildlife. It will be submitted for review in Q2/3 2025. Compared to diseases, roadkill is a more significant threat to the species. Our roadkill surveys recorded just over 1,000 roadkill individuals in 4 weeks. This will likely lead to long-term population decline if no mitigation measure is taken. We found that roadkill tends to happen on days with high relative humidity, and a model can be used to predict mass-mortality events accurately. A separate paper is being prepared and will be submitted for review in Q3/Q4 2025.

23100221.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
23100221.value: The findings from this project transpired into additional research projects on the biology of newts and their parasitic water mites. The first project focuses on determining the source of tetrodotoxin in these salamanders. It has been hypothesized that the newt themselves do not produce the toxins; instead, they are sequestered/acquired from symbiotic bacteria hosted by the newt. A study in the US found that some bacteria isolated and cultured from an American newt species can produce TTX. We are funded by the RGC to conduct a similar study on the Hong Kong newt. Another project will investigate whether the water mites possess TTX-resistance mutation in their voltage-gated sodium channels. RGC is currently considering this project. Through this ECS project, we have established research collaboration with two leading researchers (Gary Bucciarelli from UC Davis and Rebecca Tarvin from UC Berkley) who work on TTX in amphibians. They have visited our university to give talks and interact with our students and faculty. I have also made plans to collaborate with Dr. Kanta Nishikawa and Dr. Tom Schmidt, who are working on parasitic water mites on other newt species.

23100221.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
23100221.value: The Hong Kong newt is an amphibian named after Hong Kong and it is the only species of salamander found in the city. It is protected from predators by a lethal neurotoxin (tetrodotoxin, or TTX), the same toxins found in pufferfish. It is also the host of a parasitic water mite, which can be found in high abundance on the salamander. This study examined the skin toxicity and parasite burden variations of the Hong Kong newts, with the intention of undercovering the ecological significance of such variations. We learned that the skin toxin level fluctuates seasonally in the newt, but only in males not females. Surprisingly, we also learned that parasite and disease have surprisingly little negative impact on these animals. Instead, roadkill by car is a major anthropogenic factor threatening this species. We created a model that can predict the probability of roadkill based on rainfall and traffic projections, which can be used to determine the best time for intervention aimed at reducing roadkill. Lastly, the toxicity and parasite data we collected are important foundation for advancing our understanding of the ecological and evolutionary processes between the newt, their parasites, and the environment.

23501521.label: Project Title(Chinese)
23501521.value: 在送禮中避免極簡設計

23501521.label: Project Objectives
23501521.value: Because gifting helps establish and maintain relationships, choosing an appropriate gift is important for consumers. The proposed research will aim to better understand consumers’ gifting decision-making and inform companies on how to cater to gifting occasions. Visual design plays a pivotal role in consumer decision-making; however, little is known about consumers’ visual preferences in selecting gifts. This research will investigate what types of visual design gift givers like or dislike when they purchase a product to be sent as a gift, and especially their preference for minimalist visual design. This research will contribute to the gifting literature in marketing (e.g., Belk, 1996; Steffel & LeBoeuf 2014; Ward & Broniarczyk, 2016; Zhang & Epley, 2012). This research into the novel consequences of gifting will stimulate future research to explore other visual preferences in gifting. It will also have implications for practitioners, as the findings will help companies strategically design their products. This research will examine how products’ visual design influences consumers’ product perception and purchase intention. Recent years have witnessed a rising trend in minimalist design. Many companies have adopted minimalism in their product design. However, little research has explored the factors that influence people’s perceptions of and preference for minimalist design, especially in the consumer research arena. Given that visual design is an important dimension of product esthetics, it is crucial for consumer researchers to fully understand how and why consumers react to products with minimalist design. The proposed research will examine consumers’ preference for a product with minimalist visual design when they purchase it as a gift to others. I will examine consumers’ perceptions of minimalist design in the context of gifting and suggest that consumers believe that minimalist design diminishes the sense of personalization and sends a signal that the gift giver has a poor understanding of the recipient’s preferences and tastes. The proposed research will contribute to our understanding of preference in minimalist design and visual marketing (e.g., Hoegg, Alba, & Dahl, 2010; Jiang et al., 2016; Patrick & Hagtvedt, 2011). This research will provide knowledge that will help companies design their products more strategically. The findings of the proposed research will have significant implications for marketers and should help companies strategically manage their products’ visual design. In recent years, minimalist design has been widely used because marketers believe that minimalism can induce positive responses from consumers, because it is environmentally friendly and reduces distractions. Despite the common use of minimalist marketing strategies, the proposed research will suggest that minimalism may not be an appropriate strategy in all contexts. The findings of this research will reveal that consumers have a lower preference for minimalist visual design in the context of gifting. Marketers may consider promoting products with less simple visual design for gifting occasions such as Mother’s Day, Father’s Day, Valentine’s Day, and Christmas. In contrast, marketers should avoid using minimalism as a selling point when their products are being promoted for gifting purposes.

23501521.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
23501521.value: Gifting is a prevalent phenomenon in our daily life. It has been estimated that approximately 10% of the total retail market in the United States derives from consumers’ gift purchases (Unity Marketing Gifting Report 2007). Gift-giving plays an important role in establishing, maintaining, and strengthening social relationships. Gift-giving occasions are also major opportunities for companies to increase their sales. The proposed research will offer new insights into consumers’ gifting decision-making and help companies design products that are more suitable for gifting occasions. Given that visual design plays a pivotal role in consumer decision-making, this research will investigate which types of visual design gift givers like or dislike when considering purchasing a gift, and in particular their preference for minimalist product design. I propose that consumers are more likely to avoid minimalist product design when they purchase a product to be sent as a gift to others. Indeed, I posit that this effect occurs because gift givers are motivated to personalize their gift for an intended recipient, which results in avoidance of products with minimalist design, because this type of design diminishes the sense of personalization. The proposed research will contribute to the emerging literature on gift giving, visual marketing, product design, and personalization. It will also have significant implications for marketing practitioners, and help companies strategically manage their products’ visual design to ensure they are suitable for gifting occasions. 送禮是我們日常生活中普遍存在的現象。送禮在建立、維持和加強社會關系方面發揮著重要作用，同時它也是企業增加銷售額的重要機會。本研究將為消費者的送禮決策提供新的見解，並幫助公司設計更適合送禮場合的產品。鑒於產品外觀設計在消費者購買決策中起著重要作用，本研究將致力於研究送禮者在禮品購買時喜歡或不喜歡什麽樣的產品外觀設計，尤其是對極簡設計的偏好。本研究提出消費者在給他人購買禮物時更可能避開極簡的產品設計，這是因為送禮者想為收禮者選擇個性化的禮物。由於極簡的設計削弱了個性化的感覺，所以送禮者不願選擇極簡設計的產品。本研究將增加我們對送禮、視覺營銷、產品設計和產品個性化等研究領域的認知，同時對營銷從業人員和產品設計有著重要的實踐意義。

23501521.label: Realisation of objectives
23501521.value: This project was executed as planned, primarily utilizing experimental methodologies. We conducted more experiments than originally proposed, and the findings strongly supported our hypotheses. Additionally, we discovered new insights beyond the initial hypotheses. Given the success of the experiments, this research can realize the objectives set in the proposal. First, this research helps understand consumers’ gifting decision-making and informs companies on how to cater to gifting occasions. The current research also contributes to the gifting literature (e.g., Belk 1996; Flynn and Adams 2009; Gino and Flynn 2011; Givi 2020, 2021; Givi and Galak 2022; Liu and Baskin 2021; Steffel and LeBoeuf 2014; Ward and Broniarczyk 2011, 2016) by highlighting a novel product-design factor that influences consumers’ gift choice. This research into the novel consequences of gifting will stimulate future research to explore other visual preferences in gifting. In the extant gifting literature, researchers have demonstrated the impact of overall visual attractiveness of the gift (Rixom, Mas, and Rixom 2020; Yang and Urminsky 2018). However, what is missing in this stream of literature is how specific visual patterns (and the signaled meanings behind them) influence consumers’ gift choices. Aiming to fill this research gap, in the current paper we go one step further to study how a specific and increasingly popular visual pattern (i.e., minimalistic visual design), which can be independent of overall visual attractiveness, could influence gifting behavior. It will also have implications for practitioners, as the findings will help companies strategically design their products. Second, this research examined how products’ visual design influences consumers’ product perception and purchase intention. Especially, it contributes to the investigation of design minimalism in the literature of visual marketing (e.g., Millburn and Nicodemus 2015; Min et al. 2021; Obendorf 2009; Pracejus, Olsen, and O’Guinn 2006; To and Patrick 2017; Wilson and Bellezza 2022) by demonstrating the contextual variation of consumers’ preference for minimalistic product design. In contrast to the generally positive reactions to minimalism documented in prior literature (e.g., Min et al. 2021; Pracejus, Olsen, and O’Guinn 2006), only recently have researchers started to explore the potential negative side of utilizing minimalistic product designs. For instance, in a recent conference paper, To and Patrick (2017) identified a moderator of preferences for minimalistic design, that is, social power. Adding to this stream of research, our work identifies a novel context in which minimalistic product design could lead to a detrimental effect on consumer reactions—gifting choice. We show that, different from the situation when one purchases for oneself, gift senders are reluctant to present minimalistic gifts to others, presumably because this type of gift signals to recipients a lack of intention to individualize the gift. Third, the findings of the current research can provide knowledge that will help companies design their products more strategically. The findings of the current research have important managerial implications. First, marketers may wish to strategically incorporate the minimalism concept in their marketing. In recent years, minimalism has become increasingly popular, and many companies utilize the concept in their marketing strategies, such as incorporating minimalism in brand positioning, brand logo design, product design, and promotion strategies. These strategies are utilized because marketers believe that minimalism can induce positive responses from consumers. Notably, the current research suggests that this may not always be the case. Our results reveal that these minimalism-related strategies may not be effective in gifting-related products and contexts, such as gift cards or holidays. Second, another potential tactic for marketers involves providing gift buyers with tailored design recommendations based on the preferences and characteristics of their intended recipients. For example, retailers can suggest non-minimalistic designs for close recipients but minimalistic designs for more distant recipients. They can also suggest minimalistic gifts to gift givers in situations where the givers intend to send a gift to multiple recipients or when selecting a gift for themselves. On the other hand, retailers who predominantly sell minimalistic products may increase the appeal of their products in the gifting season by providing alternative personalization options, such as name-engraving services. Third, many companies highlight the concept of symbolic individualization in their marketing strategies (e.g., using the advertising appeal “Especially for You”) since they believe that an individualization effort will be appreciated by consumers. But consumers may not always trust companies’ individualization-related claims. Our findings suggest that consumers consider products with a minimalistic design to be less suited for symbolic individualization. However, as indicated in one of our studies, marketers can enhance the appeal of their minimalistic products as gifts by providing consumers with alternative options for personalization, such as name-engraving services or customizable color choices.

23501521.label: Major findings and research outcome
23501521.value: The present research found that consumers tend to avoid choosing products with a minimalistic design when they are to be presented as gifts to others, compared to when the product is purchased for self-use. Six studies provide convergent evidence for this minimalism-avoidance effect in gifting and its underlying mechanism. Study 1: Through evaluating consumers’ actual and planned product purchase for gifting or self-use, Study 1 provides initial evidence for our proposed effect that compared to self-use, gifting leads to a lower likelihood of purchasing products with a minimalistic design. In addition, analyses on the control variables measured in this study show that the observed effect is less likely to be driven by the differences in perceived product quality and/or product attractiveness in these two purchasing contexts. Study 2: Study 2 replicates this finding in a controlled experiment with incentive-compatible real consumer choices. With incentive-compatible real consumer choices, this study’s results support the proposed causal link between gift purchase and consumers’ attitude toward products with a minimalistic design. Consistent with our hypothesis, we found that participants were less likely to choose a product with a minimalistic design when they intended to give the product to others (vs. self-use). Study 3: Study 3 provides direct mediational evidence for our proposed underlying mechanism. That is, gifting (vs. self-use) increases consumers’ product-individualization motive, which then leads to a lower likelihood of choosing products with a minimalistic design. Study 4: Study 4 shed further light on the underlying process of the effect we observed. We found that when product individualization can be expressed in alternative ways (e.g., engraving the recipient’s name on the gift), the difference in the likelihood of choosing gifts with a minimalistic design was eliminated, which is consistent with the motivated-individualization process we predicted. Study 5: Study 5 tests another potential moderator of the observed effect: the closeness between the gift giver and recipient. It showed that the minimalism-avoidance effect was mitigated when product individualization was deemed less important (e.g., when choosing a gift for a socially-distant other). Study 6: Study 6 demonstrated an interpersonal consequence of the observed effect: gift givers believe that gift recipients will like a minimalistic (vs. non-minimalistic) gift less; however, gift recipients do not show significant difference in attitudes toward minimalistic and non-minimalistic gifts. In other words, gift givers seem to underestimate gift recipients’ evaluation of minimalistic gifts.

23501521.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
23501521.value: 1. Future research can further explore moderators of the observed minimalism-avoidance effect in gifting. One moderator could be the perceived social riskiness of sending non-minimalistic gifts. In our studies, we carefully selected scenarios and stimuli to ensure that non-minimalistic options were not perceived as risky gifts. The design elements used in both minimalistic and non-minimalistic designs are abstract shapes without specific cultural or identity-related meanings. 2. Future researchers can also investigate consumers’ other visual preferences (e.g., shape, color, symmetry, and general visual aesthetics) in the gifting context. The gifting context may affect consumers’ preference for other visual elements in addition to visual minimalism. Take color saturation as an example: since highly saturated colors are more likely to catch recipients’ attention and leave a deeper impression in their mind, consumers may prefer a product with highly saturated colors when it is intended as a gift for others. 3. Future research can explore how other social contexts influence consumers' preferences for minimalistic designs, such as in joint consumption or donation contexts. For instance, it would be interesting to investigate how a joint consumption context, as opposed to solo consumption, affects consumers' preferences for minimalistic designs.

23501521.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
23501521.value: This research looks at how the context of gift-giving affects consumers’ preference for products with a minimalistic design. We found that when choosing gifts for others, people tend to avoid minimalist designs. This happens because, in a gifting situation, gift givers feel a stronger need to personalize the gift for the recipient. However, the tendency to avoid minimalistic designs changes in certain situations. For example, if the gift can be personalized in other ways, such as engraving the recipient’s name on it, people are more likely to choose a minimalist design. Similarly, if the gift is for someone they don’t know well, the need for personalization is less, and they might opt for minimalistic products. The findings of the current research have important managerial implications. In recent years, many companies utilize the concept in their marketing strategies, such as incorporating minimalism in brand positioning, brand logo design, product design, and promotion strategies. Our results reveal that these minimalism-related strategies may not be effective in gifting-related products and contexts, such as gift cards or holidays.
