23501721.label: Project Objectives
23501721.value: Advance the empirical understanding of consumer structure motivation based on psychological theories and experimental methods via two subprojects and multiple types of data (field, lab, and neuroimaging). In Subproject 1, distinguish between two types (i.e., open and closed) of structure and identify the important motivational predecessors of different types of structure-seeking behavior (i.e., what causes consumers to seek different types of structure). Building on the motivations identified, explain various (sometimes seemingly contradictory) consumer behaviors. For instance, why consumers sometimes prefer products that embody a fully developed, closed structure and why some prefer to leave it open, or why there are concurrent tendencies in collectors to complete or expand a collection. Provide practical insights for marketers into (1) how businesses should structure their products (e.g., as open or closed series) and (2) what appeals (security vs. curiosity) to consumers when marketing closed- vs. open-structure products. In Subproject 2, show that when the consumption of a product is accompanied by a diminishing structure, consumers tend to maintain the structure, exhibiting varied behavioral patterns depending on the stage of consumption. By achieving point 5, complement the structure-seeking literature, which focuses on the building and refining of structure, by examining the largely uncharted consumer behavior related to the undermining and destruction of structure. Help marketers make robust predictions of how consumers will behave as they consume structured products so they can adjust marketing strategies accordingly.

23501721.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
23501721.value: 在心理學和消費者研究中，“結構”是指用以概括和組織信息的心理表徵。人類强烈地依賴結構來減少認知負荷、解釋新信息並對未來事件做出預測。由於其在於認知方面的這些重要意義，人類很自然地產生了與結構有關的動機。結構動機對營銷具有重要意義，尤其是是對產品的展示（比如產品的定位、設計、包裝等方面）以及對特定市場（比如收藏）的認識而言。然而，學界目前對消費者結構動機的研究非常有限並且只集中在數個主題上（比如控制感）。為了彌補這一現狀，在本提案中，PI提出了兩個子項目，並希望藉此可以為消費者結構動機研究提供新的思路。其中，子項目 1 從人類基本動機的角度來考察結構動機的前置環節。具體而言，PI 提出：安全動機可以導致消費者對封閉結構（既已完成且無空間添加新内容的結構）的需求，而探索動機可以引發對開放結構（仍在構建中的結構）的需求。該子項目在理論上區分了兩種不同結構，並試圖研究消費者何時會偏愛一種結構而不是另一種。該項目的潛在發現有助於解釋一些看似矛盾的消費者行為（例如，收藏者有時會試圖完成他們的收藏，而另一些時候則故意不將其完成），并爲業界提供營銷建議（譬如應當如何構建產品，或應當用什麽方式營銷具有結構的產品）。另一方面，子項目 2則試圖研究結構動機的下游環節—結構維持。具體而言，PI提出，當對某一產品的消費會損毀該產品之中的結構之時，消費者將試圖保護並維持這一結構。結構維持具體采取何種形式取決於消費的階段（即，消費開始之前還是之後，以及剩餘的結構是否仍然可以補救）。由於現有關於結構的文獻主要集中於結構的建構與發展，子項目 2對結構破壞的研究由此可以彌補現有文獻中一個空白。另外，在消費行爲會導致產品內部結構遭到破壞的情形下，子項目 2 的結果對預測消費者行爲也具有重要意義。此外，該子項目還能夠幫助營銷人員識別產品設計中可能會損害消費和未來消費的陷阱，並能提供具體的營銷策略以規避此類陷阱以及鼓勵購買後的產品消費。

23501721.label: Realisation of objectives
23501721.value: In a nutshell, this project has facilitated the fruition of the following publications and working papers: 1. Cao, C. Clark, Merrie Brucks, and Martin Reimann (2025), “Seeking Structure in Collections: Desire for Control Motivates Engagement in Collecting,” ed. Linda L. Price, June Cotte, and Simona Botti, Journal of Consumer Research, 52(3), 480–501. This paper has been published in the Journal of Consumer Research. It demonstrates that desire for control drives collectors’ motivation to engage in collecting, such that a complete collection embodies a well-developed structure (referred to as a “closed structure” in the proposal). This project thus advances understanding of when and why consumers pursue closed structures and the behavioral consequences of such pursuits, drawing on both field and laboratory data. In doing so, it also offers actionable insights for marketers regarding the development of collectible products and the strategic leveraging of consumers’ control motivations. Taken together, this project contributes to the achievement of Objectives 1, 2, 3, and 4. 2. Cao, C. Clark, John Yi, and Darren W. Dahl, “My Never-Ending Story: Why, How, and When Incompleteness in Product Sets Signals Self-Growth,” working paper. This working paper was submitted to the Journal of Marketing Research but was unfortunately rejected, and the team is currently revising the manuscript for resubmission. The project has been presented at the 2024 Association for Consumer Research Annual Conference in Paris, as well as the 2021 Society of Consumer Psychology Annual Conference (online). This research examines “set products” (e.g., collections of wines, candles, books, or albums), which consist of discrete items that are collectively perceived as a coherent whole. While prior research has established that consumers favor complete sets, our findings, based on both laboratory and field data, demonstrate that incompleteness in sets (referred to as an “open structure” in the proposal) can also be appealing. We show that such incompleteness signals self-expansion, an innate human motivation to acquire and internalize resources that foster personal growth in abilities, capacities, perspectives, and related domains. Moreover, we find that preferences for incomplete sets emerge only with sufficient experience with the items and strengthen as experience accumulates. These findings provide novel theoretical insights and practical implications for consumer research and marketing practice, particularly in product design, positioning, and promotion. Taken together, this project contributes to the achievement of Objectives 1, 2, 3, and 4. 3. Cao, C. Clark, Liang Huang, and Wilson Bastos, “Keeping It Intact: Structure Maintenance Behavior During Consumption,” working paper. This working paper is currently being prepared for submission to the Journal of Marketing. It has also been presented at the 2025 Global Brand Conference in Porto, Portugal, as well as the 2021 Society of Consumer Psychology Annual Conference (online). This project examines a common marketing practice of presenting products in structured sets (e.g., Marvel action figures or Diptyque fragrance collections) to capitalize on consumers’ preference for structure. However, the research identifies and experimentally demonstrates a potential downside of this strategy. Specifically, consumers become more reluctant to consume products when they are framed as part of a structured set, an effect we term “structure maintenance.” We further show that this reluctance arises because consumers derive possession value not only from individual items, but also from preserving the integrity of the overall structure, which is compromised through consumption. Importantly, we demonstrate a boundary condition that mitigates this effect: structuring products around usage-related elements can reframe consumption as an act of structure building rather than structure dismantling, thereby encouraging engagement and facilitating repurchase. Taken together, this project contributes to the achievement of Objectives 1, 5, 6, and 7.

23501721.label: Major findings and research outcome
23501721.value: First, the project establishes desire for control as a central psychological driver of collecting behavior. As shown in Cao, Brucks, and Reimann (2025) reported Part C, published in Journal of Consumer Research, we demonstrate that consumers are motivated to complete their collection because a complete collection embodies a clear and well-defined structure (“closed structure”). Second, as shown in Cao, Yi, and Dahl (working paper) described in Part C, we show that incompleteness in product sets (“open structure”) can be desirable, particularly among experienced consumers. This is because such incompleteness signals self-expansion, an innate human motivation to acquire and internalize resources that foster personal growth in abilities, capacities, perspectives, and related domains. Third, as shown in Cao, Huang, and Bastos (working paper) described in Part C, consumers become more reluctant to consume products when they are framed as part of a structured set, an effect we term “structure maintenance.” We further show that this reluctance arises because consumers derive possession value not only from individual items, but also from preserving the integrity of the overall structure, which is compromised through consumption. Crucially, the project identifies a practical mitigation strategy: organizing products around usage-based structures can reframe consumption as structure building rather than structure dismantling, thereby encouraging engagement and repeat purchase. Collectively, these outcomes fulfill Objectives 1–7 by integrating motivational theory with collecting, set consumption, and marketing strategy, while producing one top-tier publication and two advanced working papers. Additionally, this grant also funds another top-tier publication at Nature Communications (Sun, Cao, Liu, Li, and Ma 2024 in Part C). This work demonstrates that during peer review of academic papers, authors addressing reviewers using second-person pronouns receive fewer questions, shorter responses, and more positive feedback. Further analyses suggest that this shift in the review process occurs because “you” (vs. non-“you”) usage creates a more personal and engaging conversation.

23501721.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
23501721.value: Further development of this research will first focus on publishing the two advanced working papers in B+ journals or above. This will involve further refinement of the theoretical frameworks in response to prior review comments. In addition, while Cao, Brucks, and Reimann (2025) examined the role of desire for control in motivating engagement with closed structures, whether closed structures themselves directly enhance perceived control remains an open question. Accordingly, future research will investigate perceived control using behavioral measures as well as neuroimaging methods. Moreover, a more nuanced relationship between motivational states and structural forms warrants further exploration. For example, open structures may also signal mastery (such as anticipated mastery of future items or a sense of ownership progression) and may therefore satisfy motivations related to mastery or control. Examining these alternative motivational pathways represents an important direction for future research.

23501721.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
23501721.value: Structure emerges when distinct yet interrelated items come together to form a coherent whole. In the marketplace, such structures are ubiquitous—but what psychological effects do they have on consumers? Our research shows that the answer depends on the type of structure involved. Closed structures, which are complete and well defined, help consumers cope with control-related motivations—that is, the desire to bring events and outcomes under one’s control. In contrast, open structures, which are incomplete but open to future additions, help consumers satisfy their need for growth, exploration, and experience. Additionally, while the benefits of structure are well established, we also uncover an unexpected downside. When products are organized into neat sets, consumers may hesitate to use them because doing so would “break” the set. This reluctance helps explain why some people save products rather than enjoy them. Overall, this research sheds light on everyday, structure-related behaviors and provides practical insights for businesses seeking to design products, experiences, and reward systems that consumers genuinely value.

23601021.label: Project Objectives
23601021.value: To examine the complexities and dynamics of digital platform work in relation to the gig economy by investigating how workers make moral sense of their experiences. To understand how workers perceive the moral meaning of platform work, and how they shape the everyday practices of platform work. To comprehend in what ways platform workers justify platform work and the gig economy. To investigate how platform workers define and aspire their relationships with other workers, platforms, and the government. To draw policy implications for the governance of platform work and the gig economy in the context of Hong Kong’s policies, and to inform the international epistemic communities.

23601021.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
23601021.value: 在金融危機及疫情的影響下，數碼平台與零工經濟在全球日趨流行，愈來愈多工人透過應用程式及網站為線上平台工作。當這些平台經濟活動創造了新的生計機會，它們同時對工人產生新的挑戰，企業更可能轉嫁經營成本與風險予工人身上。近年在香港及其他地區，工人與服務平台之間都出現了一連串關於公平性的爭議，包括條款及工人的法定地位。不過，縱使存在著工作與收入的不穩定性，為何工人仍參與平台工作與零工經濟，他們又如何理解這些新形式的工作? 是項研究將探討一個在工作社會學較受忽視的範疇：平台工人實踐的道德基礎，即工人的規範性考慮如何影響他們與平台及工作的日常互動。首先，有論者提出時間彈性及金錢利益，是驅使工人從事平台工作的主要原因，但其實平台工人的動機與決定遠不止於理性選擇。其次，現存文獻並不清楚工人對平台工作規範與規則的道德概念。特別是當西方社會關於平台工作的道德爭論，涉及長期的勞工運動及就業保障經驗，香港的平台工人似乎展現較強的個體化特徵及較弱的制度化傾向。從什麼方面平台工作受工人的道德思考影響，它如何鑲嵌在一個非西方的社會脈絡，構成了工作平台化的理論空隙及難題。 透過將經濟社會學及道德經濟的框架連繫至平台工作，這研究將使用道德鑲嵌性的概念檢視：(1)道德意義如何形塑平台工作的實踐；(2)平台工人如何合理化平台工作與零工經濟；(3)平台工人如何定義與期許他們和平台之間的關係。計劃將採用質性方法，就三類的平台工作進行深入訪談，72位受訪者分別來自食物運送、叫車服務及照顧與家務工作。這研究將提升我們對工人道德信念及工作實踐的知識，貢獻於工作社會學及社會政策。同時，研究結果亦可對政策制定提供啟示，以推動香港及其他地區發展更平衡的勞工-仲介關係。

23601021.label: Realisation of objectives
23601021.value: 1. To examine the complexities and dynamics of digital platform work in relation to the gig economy by investigating how workers make moral sense of their experiences. The research team has conducted in-depth interviews to investigate the views and experience of 36 food delivery and 36 care platforms workers. The data revealed how digital platforms organised labour services and manage workers as independent contractors without offering any occupational welfare, aided by digital technologies and the algorithmic power. Also, interviewees explained the reasons for and meanings of engaging platform work, despite the platforms’ domination in their contractual agreements. Therefore, this objective has been fully achieved. 2. To understand how workers perceive the moral meaning of platform work, and how they shape the everyday practices of platform work. The data suggested that interviewees upheld various moral meanings of platform work and practised their platform work differently. First, both food delivery and care workers understood that their rights had been deprived based on their self-employed status claimed by platforms, who possessed employers’ power in the absence of employers’ responsibilities. Second, while food delivery workers contested the algorithms used by platforms and expressed the sense of unfairness about the falling piece rate offered by food delivery platforms, care workers were less unsatisfied with care platforms. It was related to the different market conditions in the catering and care sectors. For food delivery workers, they faced a more monopolised market and the platforms that imposed stronger labour control; care platform workers had more choices in the market driven by several platform intermediaries, with more frequent everyday interaction with clients that shifted their job dissatisfaction. Overall, this objective has been met. 3. To comprehend in what ways platform workers justify platform work and the gig economy. Through in-depth interviews, interviewees suggested various reasons justifying platform work and the gig economy. First, autonomy and time-based flexibility was pursued by workers in general, in which some workers even considered the temporal flexibility an occupational welfare favouring greater work-life balance. Additionally, food delivery workers mentioned the negative impact of COVID-19 on labour market and the opportunities created by the platform business, with low entry barriers. Second, some older care platform workers mentioned that after being forced to quit by care homes after aged over 60, they could only find precarious jobs opportunities offered by platforms to extend their working lives. Consequently, on the one hand, online platforms boosted the quantity of short-term and mini jobs, with stronger time-based flexibility and lower requirements. On the other hand, the quality of platform work, including food delivery and care, appeared to be declining in the form of independent contractors, involving false self-employment and undermined occupational welfare. Hence, this objective has been fully achieved. 4. To investigate how platform workers define and aspire their relationships with other workers, platforms, and the government. Through conducting in-depth interviews and organising the local conference with stakeholders, we managed to understand how platform workers defined and expected their relationships with workers, platforms, and the government. Interviewees tended to see other workers as members of the platform instead of contenders. Despite the implicit competitive relationships, platform workers put more emphasis on their common interests, especially facing the reduced pay caused by platforms’ changing algorithms. Some food delivery workers even mobilised and carried out collective actions to oppose platforms’ unilateral decision making. In contrast, care platform workers adopted a more individualised approach to bargaining with platforms for better terms and conditions. Overall, food delivery and care platform workers preferred maintaining the status of independent contractor but expected stronger insurance against occupational risks. This called for special policy arrangements for the labour protection that categorised platform workers in between employees and self-employed workers, which required government’s legal re-classification and re-regulation. The research team has met this target of investigating workers’ perceived social relationships. 5. To draw policy implications for the governance of platform work and the gig economy in the context of Hong Kong’s policies, and to inform the international epistemic communities. Informed by the research findings, this research project formulates some policy suggestions for the government and engages in the international epistemic communities. As mentioned, there are three main policy recommendations made by the research team. First, the government could consider reclassifying platform workers as a new employment category between employees and self-employed workers in the labour legislation framework. While the employee status embodies clear employment relations, the self-employed status is void of any occupational welfare. Like the cases in the United Kingdom and Taiwan, a new category of ‘worker’ represents the dependent self-employment based on workers’ reliance on platforms. Under the new classification, platforms do not need to be entirely responsible for all employers’ costs but must enhance the insurance for workers’ risks of injuries. This could keep the flexibility for both workers and platforms in the limited mutual commitment, improving workers’ preferred injury compensation, given that they do not want to enter a formal employment relationship with platforms. Second, the government may strengthen the existing central compensation policy, for example, the Traffic Accident Victims Assistance Scheme, suggested by interviewees. The extra public spending could be funded by the tax or charges specially targeting food delivery platforms. Third, apart from online food delivery platforms centred on algorithms in organising work, the possibilities of false self-employment do appear in the care sector and the government should enforce the labour inspection and monitoring, increasing the penalty of false self-employment to reduce the business risks and costs shifted to platform workers. Finally, to deal with the power and data asymmetries between platforms and workers, the government should promote more and better ‘social dialogue’ for platforms and workers to bargain about pay and working conditions, avoiding unnecessary workplace conflicts. These insights have been presented to the Hong Kong government through research team’s policy report and media responses. They also reached the international epistemic communities via international conference and seminar.

To comprehend in what ways platform workers justify platform work and the gig economy.
To investigate how platform workers define and aspire their relationships with other workers, platforms, and the government.
To draw policy implications for the governance of platform work and the gig economy in the context of Hong Kong’s policies, and to inform the international epistemic communities.

23601021.label: Major findings and research outcome
23601021.value: The major findings of this project could be classified into three themes. First, the data suggested that both food delivery and care platform workers could not access to the occupational welfare offered by platforms due to their ambivalent employment status. In other words, the existing legal framework allowed platforms exercising power to define platform work’s terms and conditions. While platforms possessed employers’ power to assign work and discipline workers, they were not required to exercise employers’ responsibility in labour compensation. Workers considered time-based flexibility as their occupational welfare gained by platform work, while they did not prefer the conventional employment relationship with platforms but expected more from the platform-provided insurance against the injury risks. Second, the digitised competition in the labour market was intensified by platforms’ technological dominance of algorithms and ownership of app-based network. Food delivery platforms’ automated organisation of work enabled them to expand or contract the labour demands at no costs. Platforms’ algorithmic opacity and continual cutback of pay fuelled workers’ perceived unfairness, contestation, and even limited collective actions. Care platforms’ scalable connectivity also boosted their on-demand workforce supply through adopting communication apps and social media groups in recruiting workers, in which the competition for care jobs was synchronised. However, platform workers also practised multi-platforming strategies to cope with platforms’ control. Finally, the institutional embeddedness of platform work did shape interviewees’ experiences and expectations of their work. Due to the current minimal regulation of platform work, the lack of occupational welfare and precarity experienced by workers was institutionalised. While the quality of food delivery service was less affected by the on-demand nature of platform work, the findings suggest that the quality of care could be undermined in the platform-mediated market, given the government’s marketisation policy approach to care sector. This was reflected in platforms’ promotion of care workers’ replaceability and the trial-and-error approach. Consequently, the platform-mediated care could generate care precarity as service users may encounter strong uncertainty and limited trust in the care relations. Overall, this project has contributed to academic publications (see Part C). Informed by the findings, the PI has commented on related issues on the mass media. In terms of outcomes, despite the lack of fundamental policy changes, the government has enhanced the public education about the employment rights of platform workers and freelancers to avoid false self-employment.

23601021.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
23601021.value: While this research project has investigated food delivery and care platform workers’ experience, it mainly focused on Chinese workers in Hong Kong. Hence, more attention should be paid to the experience of non-Chinese workers and how their ethnic communities shape the organisation of workers. Besides, this project was conducted during the COVID-19 pandemic, in which the food delivery market was expanding. It is central to identify the ways platforms responded to adverse economic conditions in the post-pandemic era. While this study adopted the moral economy framework to understand the normative foundation of platform work, how platform capitalism is institutionalised in the domestic political economy remains under-studied. For example, the findings of this project suggested that care platform work was embedded in the subsidised care sector. Therefore, the knowledge about platform work should be situated in broader policy and sector-based contexts. The last research implication lies in comparative studies to explain varying institutional configurations of platform work, for example, the role played by welfare states and labour regimes, which goes beyond the prevailing literature focusing on the labour process at the micro level. Further research should incorporate more case studies and introduce longitudinal analysis to trace how platform work evolves.

23601021.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
23601021.value: Informed by the moral economy of work, this research project investigated why and how workers engaged in the platform economy. The findings suggest that both food delivery and care platform work involved the possibility of false self-employment in the name of independent contractors, in which online platforms could control workers, but they did not take employers’ responsibilities to offer occupational welfare. While food delivery workers valued the time-based flexibility of platform work, they were dissatisfied with platforms’ domination of digital technologies and declining pay. Some care workers gained job opportunities after retirement age via on-demand platforms. Although the quantity of work was boosted by platforms, they did not guarantee the quality of work. Interviewees generally did not prefer maintaining formal employment relationships with platforms, while they expected stronger labour insurance against the injury risks. Therefore, policy suggestions are made by the research team. First, the government should consider introducing a new category of worker in between employees and self-employment, enhancing the labour protection while maintaining certain degree of flexibility. Second, the government should review the current regulatory approach to platform economy and how it governs and subsidises the public services increasingly relying on digital platforms.

23603221.label: Project Objectives
23603221.value: To amalgamate disparate developments in the literature into a precise, flexible and elegant mathematical framework for semantic expressivism for basic epistemic vocabulary (epistemic modals, probability operators and indicative conditionals). To motivate and introduce extensions of this baseline framework that accommodate linguistic devices that present special challenges for semantic expressivism: attitude ascriptions, quantified claims, the ‘must’ operator, and subjunctive conditionals. To reevaluate, in light of the above proposals, the classic conceptual puzzles in the philosophy of language that have hobbled the development of semantic expressivism, such as the Frege-Geach problem (applied to epistemic vocabulary). To present the above results at a number of top venues (leading conferences and journals), in order to advance the development of semantic expressivism as a serious rival to the dominant foundational paradigms in formal semantics.

23603221.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
23603221.value: Intelligent agency (e.g., decision-making, planning, and explanatory reasoning) depends on the ability to think and talk about alternative ways the world could be. In particular, it requires information management: the ability to systematically consider the possibilities that are compatible with one’s knowledge of the world, and the ability to signal one’s knowledge and ignorance to others. Our ability to entertain hypothetical scenarios, and communicate uncertainty, is exemplified by our use of modal language such as ‘The train might be late’, probabilistic language such as ‘The train is probably late’, and conditional language such as ‘If the track is damaged, the train is late’. The broad aim of the current project is to study foundational issues concerning the semantics (i.e., the literal meaning/content) of this kind of language, and its role in communicating grades of uncertainty. More specifically, the project aims to advance a relatively underdeveloped foundational view – semantic expressivism – which opposes the dominant paradigms in the formal semantics literature – descriptivism and pragmatic expressivism. Descriptivists claim, roughly, that the basic conversational role of modal, conditional and probabilistic language is (like straightforwardly descriptive language) to express that the speaker knows certain propositions. In contrast, expressivists insist that these claims canonically express epistemic attitudes that are not outright knowledge. For instance: ignorance, relative and imperfect confidence, and conditional knowledge. Controversially, semantic expressivists add that the compositional meaning of a claim should be identified with the type of mental state it expresses. Even more specifically, the project aims to clarify and address several phenomena that seem, on their face, to be major obstacles for semantic expressivists in particular: the difference between knowing and merely believing modal, probabilistic and conditional claims; the difference between asserting ‘The train is late’ and ‘The train must be late’; the continuity in meaning between indicative and subjunctive conditionals; and the classic conceptual problem known as the Frege-Geach problem. Methodologically, the investigation will proceed in the broad tradition of formal semantics and formal epistemology. In particular, the aim is to develop mathematically precise compositional semantic frameworks (for associating simple and complex sentences with the mental features they express). The criteria for success includes mathematical and conceptual coherence, and basic empirical predictions that match uncontroversial data concerning competent ordinary speech. 摘要：智能主体（比如，决策，规划和解释推理）依赖于思考和谈论世界另一面的能力。特别地，它要求信息管理能力：能够去系统地考虑与一个人对这个世界的认知一致的可能性，以及能够去表达一个人对其他人的认识和无知。 我们考虑假设情境的能力，以及交流不确定性的能力通过我们对模态语言的使用反映出来，比如“这辆火车可能晚点”，通过使用概率语言反映出来，比如“这辆火车大概会晚点”，以及通过条件式语言体现出来，比如“如果轨道被损坏，火车会晚点”。研究这类语言的语义（也就是文字意义/内涵），以及它在表达不确定性的等级上起的作用是这项研究的大致目标。更具体地，这项研究旨在推动一个相对还未发展起来的基本观点——语义表达主义，这种观点反对在形式语义文献中的主流观点——描述主义和语用表达主义。描述主义大致上宣称，模态、条件式和概率的语言的基本对话作用是去（就像直接地描述性的语言）表达说话者知道了特定的命题。相反地，表达主义者强调这些断言规范地表达了那些并非是完全知识的认知态度。比如：无知，相关的、不完美的自信心，以及条件式的知识。颇有争议的是，语义表达主义者进一步认为一个断言的组合意义应该等同于它表达的心智状态的类型。 更进一步具体地说，这项研究旨在阐明和设法解决一些表面上对于语义表达主义者来说似乎是主要障碍的现象，尤其是：在知道和仅仅相信模态，概率和条件式断言上两者的区别；断言“这辆火车晚点了”以及“这辆火车肯定晚点了”之间的区别；在直陈和虚拟条件句含义上的连续性；以及以弗雷格-吉奇问题著称的经典概念性问题。在方法论上，这项调查研究会遵循形式语义和形式认识论的大致传统来展开。特别地，研究目的是发展出数学上严格的组合式语义架构（为了将简单和复杂句子和它们表达的心智特征相关联）。达到目的的标准包括了数学的和概念的一致性，以及基本经验预测要和关于足够平常的言语的那些无争议性数据相匹配。

23603221.label: Realisation of objectives
23603221.value: 1. The project developed, in stages, a novel and mathematically precise foundational semantic framework for modal and conditional logic, contributing to a broad tradition of 'information-sensitive' semantics in the literature. I call this framework 'Fragmented Semantic Expressivism'. Its chief precursor is a 'state-based' approach to semantic expressivism that I developed in prior work; the most fundamental innovation of the new framework is its incorporation of topic-sensitive content and fragmented information states (generating various subtle effects and theoretical decision-points for even the most basic epistemic vocabulary, such as epistemic modals). The project's paper outputs chart the evolution of this framework, with the latest paper - 'Fragmentation and Expression' - presenting the framework in an advanced and perhaps fully realized form. In the run-up to this, the paper 'Stable Acceptance for Mighty Knowledge' works with a more austere version of Semantic Expressivism; the paper 'Modal Knowledge for Expressivists' incorporates and exploits the key features of Fragmented Semantic Expressivism - topic-sensitive content and fragmented information states -- in a preliminary form; the paper 'Truth, Topicality, and Transparency' focuses on and defends the topic-sensitive theory of content that Fragmented Semantic Expressivism ultimately incorporates. 2. The project's paper outputs present semantic frameworks that successfully incorporate linguistic devices that have raised conceptual and technical challenges for cruder forms of semantic expressivism. Each of the papers 'Stable Acceptance for Mighty Knowledge' and 'Modal Knowledge for Expressivists' tackles a (I believe ultimately related and highly generalizable) logical conundrum that crude forms of expressivism face when attempting to combine attitude ascriptions (e.g., knowledge ascriptions or belief ascriptions) with epistemic possibility operators like 'might'. The basic difficulty in each case is that it is unclear how a system in the expressivist ballpark can meet a short list of basic logical desiderata (as critics have been keen to emphasize). The first paper resolves the condundrum it analyzes with a sophisticated account of knowledge ascription, interacting in subtle ways with an expressivist semantic foundation; the second paper resolves the logical conundrum it analyzes with a sophisticated account of semantic expressivism, incorporating topic-sensitive content and fragmented informations states. The project's latest paper, 'Fragmentation and Expression', motivates important refinements for the topic-sensitive and fragmented approach: in particular, it is argued that an apt combination of semantic expressivism and fragmentation evades objections to the latter that are devastating for a simpler development. It is then shown that the resulting system -- Fragmented Semantic Expressivism -- can be equipped with a natural account of the epistemic necessity operator 'must', making important progress in capturing the subtle logic of ordinary 'must' claims. Along the way, the paper considers and answers a prima facie objection to its approach that arises when it is generalized to quantified claims, offering an opportunity for preliminary discussion on the best way to incorporate quantification into the system in question. Together, the discussion across these papers covers almost the full roster of epistemic vocabulary I hoped to tackle. However, I am still in the process of writing a paper that applies the project's proposed system to conditional claims (this paper focuses on the interaction between indicative and subjunctive conditionals). Thus, though I expect this remaining work to bear fruit in the near term, this last category of linguistic device is yet to receive proper attention in a dedicated paper. 3. The paper succeeds in tackling and, I think, answering core conceptual puzzles for semantic expressivists that have been emphasized by their critics. The papers 'Stable Acceptance for Mighty Knowledge' and 'Modal Knowledge for Expressivists' tackle different elements of a prominent objection to expressivist approaches to epistemic modals: namely, the objection that combining them in a straightforward way with knowledge and belief ascriptions results in a highly unorthodox (indeed, highly implausible) account of the logic of attitude ascriptions. Each paper is concerned to (i) sharpen the alleged objection to expressivism into a mathematically precise set of desiderata, (ii) emphasize the generality of the respective challenge, broadening it beyond the expressivist's purview, and (iii) develop a sophisticated form of expressivism that demonstrably answers the sharpened challenge. Meanwhile, the final paper in the project's series, 'Fragmentation and Expression', shows how a sophisticated form of expressivism offers promising tools for answering conceptual challenges in other areas (e.g., a classic objection to fragmentationist accounts of informational content; the classic problem of 'logical omniscience' for knowledge ascriptions; the preface paradox), while also readily answering an outstanding objection to the expressivist's approach to epistemic necessity operators like 'must' (namely, the objection that expressivists are committed to the implausible view that 'it must be that P' is essentially equivalent to just stating P, without the necessity modal). The total series of project papers may be regarded as contributing to answering (what many consider to be) the overarching challenge for expressivist semantic frameworks: the Frege-Geach challenge, understood as the challenge of providing an expressivist semantics that composes readily and naturally with straightforwardly descriptive vocabulary, basic logical operations, and other straightforward ordinary vocabulary. The systems proposed in the project papers are precise, fully compositional, combine freely with descriptive vocabulary, and incorporate logical devices (knowledge operators, 'must' operators etc.) that, as mentioned, have traditionally been considered problematic for expressivists. 4. The project has achieved its aim of presenting its results at leading conferences and in leading journals in the area. As hoped, the project has produced papers that have been accepted by generalist philosophy journals (namely, Philosophical Studies) and papers that have been accepted by specialist journals that reach an interdisciplinary audience (the Journal of Philosophical Logic is read widely by logicians, working in diverse areas like philosophy, computer science, or linguistics; the journal Linguistics and Philosophy is well-regarded and widely read by both philosophers of language and linguists that work in the area of formal semantics). A similar effect has been achieved by the project's conference output: I presented some of the project's output at one of the largest annual philosophy conferences in the world (namely, the 2023 Pacific APA meeting) and I presented some of the projects output at the long-running Theoretical Aspects of Rationality and Knowledge conference (this year held at Oxford University), a self-consciously interdisciplinary conference that showcases research from computer scientists, economists, linguists, logicians, and philosophers.

23603221.label: Major findings and research outcome
23603221.value: The principal achievement of the paper 'Truth, Topicality, and Transparency' is a novel defense of the theory of content that I deploy in subsequent papers. The paper isolates and carefully articulates a small set of basic principles that together entail the core thesis of the theory. The paper contrasts this argument with alternatives that the literature gestures at, but aren't (the paper argues) particularly effective on closer inspection. The principal achievements of the paper 'Stable Acceptance for Mighty Knowledge' are: first, the presentation of a novel logical paradox concerning the interaction of knowledge ascriptions and ordinary epistemic possibility (`might') claims. This is inspired by a line of criticism that is usually aimed specifically at expressivist semantics, but in fact represents a broader paradox. Second, the paper proves that various influential semantic theories do not successfully answer the paradox. Third, the paper motivates a particular strategy for answering the paradox and introduces a novel stated-based expressivist semantic framework that, the paper proves, successfully executes this preferred strategy. The prinicpal achievements of the paper 'Modal Knowledge for Expressivists' are, first, a more precise explication of a well-known objection to semantic expressivism (amounting to the objection that semantic expressivism offers an implausible account of the logic of knowledge ascriptions) and, second, the introduction of a novel semantic expressivism that, the paper proves, evades the objection (by generating a more satisfactory theory of the logic of knowledge ascriptions). The crucial feature of this framework is its incorporation of topic-sensitive content and fragmentated information states. One interesting result of the paper is that these devices do not, by themselves, completely succeed in evading the objection: a subtler residual form of the objection remains. However, the paper proves that incorporating independently motivated context-sensitive elements into its basic framework helps to resolve this outstanding worry. The principal achievements of the paper 'Fragmentation and Expression' are, first, the identification of a severe objection to standard 'fragmentationist' accounts of mental content (where 'fragmentationism' is the view that mental content generally divides into individually logically coherent but often mutually incoherent information islands); second, the development of a new form of fragmentationist account, that utilizes semantic expressivism to evade the aforementioned objection; third, the paper applies the resulting framework to help resolve some stubborn conceptual puzzles, for example on the behavior of 'must'. In total, the paper makes a case that fragmentation and semantic expressivism are a mutually beneficial pairing.

23603221.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
23603221.value: The project's results provide ample opportunity for further research. The net result of the project's output is the introduction and motivation of precisely defined semantic frameworks, aimed at modeling and explicating the meaning and logical subtleties of our ordinary language for communicating knowledge and ignorance through possibility claims, necessity claims, attitude ascriptions, and suppositional reasoning. The motivation provided thus far rests largely on mathematical proofs, demonstrating that these frameworks display properties of crucial conceptual import and in prima facie alignment with ordinary linguistic data. Much work remains. First, a variety of linguistic devices should be incorporated into the framework (in detail) and stress-tested: subjunctive conditionals, normative language, truth operators, and deontic modalities are obvious targets, given their crucial roles in the ongoing debate on expressivism. Second, a systematic, purely mathematical investigation of the meta-logical and computational properties of our systems is of interest (for example, can the logic generated by such systems be efficiently automated?). Third, a more comprehensive linguistic investigation is desirable, bolstering the prima facie linguistic data that the project has so far relied on with rigorous empirical studies of ordinary speakers. For my part, ongoing research is currently focused on the first set of outstanding issues.

23603221.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
23603221.value: This project contributes to a broad area of interdisciplinary research that tackles key questions about rational agency: exactly what resources does ordinary language provide for communicating that someone knows, or doesn't know, the answer to a certain question? How do these resources interact with our ability to reason hypothetically? In particular, what is the role of possibility locutions like 'it might be raining' or necessity locutions like 'it must be raining' in reporting knowledge or ignorance? The present project fortifies an iconoclastic theoretical line known as 'expressivism for epistemic vocabulary'. According to expressivists, claims like 'it might be raining' or 'it is likely to be raining' are not descriptions (and so do not obey the classical rules of logic of descriptions, and have a complicated relationship with concepts like 'truth'). Rather, they serve to directly express a speaker's uncertainty. The project developed new, precise forms of expressivism that evade objections that some critics have considered lethal for the entire expressivistic project: in particular, objections stemming from the expressivist's treatment of knowledge ascriptions like 'Ann knows that it might be raining' or necessity claims like 'it must be raining', and its treatment of the interaction between straightforward descriptions and non-descriptive locutions.

23604921.label: Project Title(Chinese)
23604921.value: 真理的碎片 圖靈脫大公會議後的圖像、物品和話語

23604921.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
23604921.value: In an early-modern Europe shaken to its core by the religious Reformation, Catholics and Protestants were constructing competing versions of theological and historical truth, redefining certainties and beliefs at a time of profound spiritual and political divisions. They faced for the first time the epistemological problem of truth, reality and language that, emerged at a crucial conjuncture in European history, still is an important element of the modern intellectual landscape. This project investigates one aspect of the problem of truth, that of historical truth and historical narration, filtered in particular through the eyes of post-Reformation Catholic artists and antiquarians. It explores specifically how the notion of the truth-value of history and its relation to narrative representation, both textual and visual, was shaped in the latter part of the sixteenth century by the debate on the Christian past and its material and artistic legacy. In the aftermath of the Council of Trent (1545-1563) – the monumental effort of the Church of Rome in response to Protestant attacks against its theology and liturgy – Catholic culture struggled to prove the legitimacy of the Roman Church. Theologians sought to demonstrate the authenticity of Catholic liturgical practices in accordance with the teaching of the early apostolic Church, while antiquarians and historians dig into the past to find evidence to support the authenticity of Catholic beliefs. Similarly, artists conjured images of Early Christianity to make the past visible and demonstrate the continuity of the spiritual life of the Roman Church. Images and objects were used to shape history, knowledge and, ultimately, people’s beliefs. It was a huge intellectual and political responsibility in a world where disintegrating certainties and conflicting truths pushed confessional preoccupations, historical criticism and visual rhetoric to the fore of the intellectual discourse of the time. By analyzing how intellectuals and artists in post-Tridentine Rome, at the very center of the Catholic world, negotiated ideas of truth with the reality of history and its narrative representation, this research brings to light the crucial contribution of antiquarian studies and visual arts to the early-modern European debate of what makes things true, factual and historical. It also highlight how strategies of that era used to give shape to truth and knowledge may still be relevant to our present and its acute need for perspectives on how to navigate a time of competing truths. 在早期現代歐洲，宗教改革撼動了神學和歷史真理的核心，故而天主教徒和新教徒開始構建一套能與之抗衡的理論，為的是在內心世界和政治架構嚴重分裂的時期，重新定義客觀事實和信仰。這是他們首次面臨真理、現實和語言的認識論問題，它在歐洲歷史的關鍵時刻出現，至今仍是現代知識領域的一個重要因素。本項目研究了真理問題的其中一個方面，即在後宗教改革時代的天主教藝術家和古物學家們的眼中，歷史真理和敘事究竟作何模樣。另外，本項目具體探討了在16世紀後半葉，基督教歷史及其物質和藝術遺產相關的辯論怎樣塑造了歷史真理的價值觀及其與文字和視覺敘事的關係。圖靈脫大公會議（1545-1563）是羅馬教會為應對新教徒對其神學和宗教禮拜儀式的攻擊而做出的巨大努力，在此之後，天主教文化一直在竭力證明羅馬教會的正統性。神學家試圖用早期使徒教會的教義證明天主教禮拜儀式的真實性，古文學家和歷史學家則挖掘過去，尋找證據支持天主教信仰的真實性。同樣地，藝術家用筆幻化出早期基督教的圖像，使過去的一切變得清晰可見，證明羅馬教會的精神生活從古至今，一直綿延不變。圖像和物品塑造了歷史和知識，最終形成人們的信仰。在當時風雲變幻的大千世界中，大眾所篤信的客觀事實被不斷推翻，各自信奉的真理也針鋒相對，這些都將人們在信仰崩塌後的懺悔自白、歷史批評和視覺修辭推到了當時知識論述的前沿，也是一個巨大的知識和政治責任。本項目通過分析圖靈脫大公會議之後身處天主教世界中心的羅馬知識分子和藝術家們是如何協商真理、歷史及其敘事表現的，揭示了古物研究和視覺藝術對歐洲早期現代關於真理、事實和歷史辯論的重要貢獻。同時，本項目還重點論述了那個時代塑造真理和知識的策略如何與現在仍然相關，以及如何為這個競相爭奪真理詮釋權的時代找到前行的方向，這種觀點是目前世界迫切需要的。

24100421.label: Project Title(Chinese)
24100421.value: 阿黴素破壞線粒體和基因引致心臟衰老

24100421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24100421.value: 阿黴素是一種有效的化療藥物，可用於治療多種惡性腫瘤，但可引起致命的心臟毒性。儘管動物模型的研究表明阿黴素可以引起心臟衰老，但對其機制知之甚少。我們假設基因和線粒體毒性是阿黴素誘導的心臟衰老的主要因素。我們會使用我們新開發的人類多能幹細胞心臟細胞 hPSC-CMs 模型研究阿黴素的心臟毒性。有別於傳統模型，我們的hPSC-CMs富含線粒體和對阿黴素更敏感。我們會通過藥物抑制基因和腺體的毒性來確定他們對心臟衰老的影響。我們的結果將增加我們對心臟衰老的了解，並確定基因和腺體毒性對這種病態的重要性，期望從而研發出對阿黴素引起的心臟衰老的治療方案。

24101921.label: Project Title(Chinese)
24101921.value: 由UBAP1基因突變導致的遺傳性痙攣性截癱的功能機制研究

24101921.label: Project Objectives
24101921.value: To establish the pathogenicity of a truncated UBAP1 variant in cellular studies: Human neural progenitor cells harbouring a patient-specific recurrent heterozygous UBAP1 mutation have been generated using CRISPR/Cas9 technology. Functional alterations resulting from the truncated UBAP1 protein, including abnormal endosomal clustering and impaired binding capacity to ubiquitinated proteins, will be assessed. Defective interactions of the truncated UBAP1 with its functional partner proteins, as compared to those of wildtype UBAP1, will be investigated using proteomic studies. Abnormal cytoplasmic accumulation of ubiquitinated proteins in UBAP1 mutant cells will be evaluated. To investigate potential behavioural deficits and axonal degradation in mice harbouring a recurrent Ubap1 variant: A mouse model harbouring the patient-specific recurrent heterozygous Ubap1 mutation has been generated. Potential behavioural deficits accentuated by gait impairments in these Ubap1 mutant mice will be investigated using the beam walk assay, hindlimb clasping test, and evaluation of the onset of a resting tremor. The potential retrograde degeneration of long corticospinal tract axons will also be examined from cross-sections of the lumbar spinal cords of the mutant mice. The characteristic “dying back” phenomenon, which refers to the prominent axonal pathology preceding cell body losses in HSP patients, will be studied. Potential axonal degeneration in the spinal cord will also be traced via injection of an anterograde axonal tracer. Axonal degeneration is expected to occur mainly in the corticospinal axons of Ubap1 mutant mice.

24101921.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24101921.value: 運動神經退行性疾病是一種致殘且死亡率高的進行性神經系統退化疾病，患者會因為運動神經元退化而出現肌肉無力和一系列運動相關症狀，其中上運動神經元退化可導致痙攣和反射異常，而下運動神經元退化則可導致肌肉萎縮和肌束震顫。運動神經退行性疾病的全球發病率在過去二十年中顯著增加；據香港醫院管理局統計數據顯示，本港運動神經退行性疾病患者在2011-2015年間較1997-2002年間增加了約四倍。由於有關此類疾病的分子病因學分析尚未滿足醫學臨床需求，針對其治療的特異性靶點亦尚待確定，所以至今仍缺乏對運動神經退行性疾病的特異性致病機制的了解和針對該疾病的有效治療方法。 目前已知有害基因突變可以引起包括遺傳性痙攣性截癱在內的一些運動神經退行性疾病，其中遺傳性痙攣性截癱由有害基因突變導致的皮質脊髓上運動神經元的軸突退化引起，但尚有超過一半的患者無法獲得明確的分子診斷。本研究組與其他組的最新研究分別透過全外顯子組測序分析鑑定了由UBAP1基因突變導致的新型常染色體顯性遺傳的遺傳性痙攣性截癱，所有攜帶UBAP1有害突變的患者均於兒童期出現非綜合型遺傳性痙攣性截癱的病徵。 本研究組希望在細胞與動物模型中構建帶有患者中反復出現的UBPA1突變，開展針對遺傳性痙攣性截癱等運動神經元病的分子病理學研究。目前，本研究組已成功建立了帶有患者特異突變的神經袓細胞，並會以此為基礎展開針對UBAP1突變的功能特徵研究。此外，我們亦已經建立了相應的小鼠模型，並準備透過小鼠模型展開臨床前研究，了解UBAP1突變以何種機制導致患者出現下肢痙攣，步態異常，及皮質脊髓上運動神經元軸突退化等徵狀。 本課題除了將闡明UBAP1突變的致病性及其功能特徵，更會為日後有關此類疾病的治療課題整理及羅列相關的生理狀況和建立臨床前模型。本課題的成功將有助進行針對運動神經退行性疾病的病理研究和治療方案的開發。

24105721.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24105721.value: Infection with severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) virus may be asymptomatic or lead to critical illness with Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19). About 1 out of 3 patients hospitalized for COVID-19 require admission to Intensive Care. Even with life support, mortality be as high as 61.5%. Unfortunately, we do not know why many patients infected with SARS-CoV-2 remain asymptomatic whilst others develop life threatening illness. Moreover, corticosteroid is the only drug shown to improve survival. Understanding factors that determine severity of COVID-19 may reveal potential therapeutic targets. An emerging approach to understand human disease is through interactions between host and microorganisms that reside in the human body. Healthy respiratory tract contains a diverse population of microorganisms called microbiome. Lung microbiome is changed in lung diseases such as asthma. In return, changes in lung microbiome can cause further lung inflammation and worsen lung disease. Since COVID-19 causes respiratory tract inflammation, it may also affect respiratory microbiome. Currently there are only 2 descriptive respiratory microbiome studies in COVID-19 patients. These were small studies of 8 to 20 patients, and one of them only included patients who died from COVID-19. It remains unclear whether change in respiratory microbiome is associated with severity of lung disease in COVID-19. To address this knowledge gap, we performed a pilot study on nasopharyngeal microbiota from 21 patients with COVID-19. Our preliminary results demonstrate differential microbial communities between nasopharyngeal swab and nasopharyngeal throat swab specimens, while patients with severe COVID-19 had higher abundance of Escherichia coli. Based on our pilot study, we propose a prospective observational cohort study on 120 patients with SARS-CoV-2 infection to identify the associations between upper respiratory tract microbiome and clinical outcomes. We will analyze upper respiratory microbiome in nasopharyngeal samples collected from hospitalized patients for SARS-CoV-2 infection. Bioinformatics will be used to evaluate microbiota with COVID-19 severity category (asymptomatic, mild symptomatic, severe/critically ill) and viral load. Our aims are to (1) describe longitudinal changes in upper respiratory tract microbiome in COVID-19 during hospitalization, (2) determine if upper respiratory tract microbiome is associated with severity of COVID-19, and (3) compare upper respiratory tract SARS-CoV-2 viral load with microbiota. The impact of this study is to provide insight on respiratory tract microbiome across the full severity spectrum of COVID-19. Our results may guide further research into potential therapies that target respiratory microbiome to prevent severe disease and treat critically ill patients with COVID-19. 嚴重急性呼吸系統綜合症冠狀病毒 2 (SARS-CoV-2)感染患者可無症狀或可患2019 年冠狀病毒病 (COVID-19) 的危重疾病。 大約三分之一因 COVID-19 住院的患者需要入住重症監護病房。 即使有器官支援，死亡率也高達61.5%。 然而，為什麼許多感染了 SARS-CoV-2 的患者卻沒有症狀，而其他人則發展為危及生命的疾病的原因還是不明確。 此外，類固醇是唯一能提高生存率的藥物。 進一步了解 COVID-19 嚴重程度的因素可能會揭示潛在的治療目標。 人體內微生物興人的相互作用是一種新的方法去了解人類疾病。 健康的呼吸道包含稱為微生物組的多種微生物群。 肺部微生物組會在哮喘等肺部疾病中發生變化。 此外，肺部微生物組的變化會導致進一步的肺部炎症並使肺部疾病惡化。 由於 COVID-19 會引起呼吸道炎症，因此它也可能影響呼吸道微生物群。 目前只有 2 項針對 COVID-19 患者的描述性呼吸道微生物組研究。 這些是針對 8 到 20 名患者的小型研究，其中一項僅包括死於 COVID-19 的患者。 目前尚不清楚呼吸道微生物組的變化是否與 COVID-19 肺部疾病的嚴重程度有關。 為了進一步了解COVID-19呼吸道微生物組的變化，我們對 21 名 COVID-19 患者的鼻咽微生物群進行了初步研究。 我們的初步結果表明，鼻咽拭子和鼻咽喉拭子標本之間存在不同的微生物群落，而重症 COVID-19 患者的大腸桿菌豐度更高。 根據我們的前導研究，我們提出一項針對 120 名 SARS-CoV-2 感染患者的前瞻性觀察隊列研究，以確定上呼吸道微生物組與臨床結果之間的關聯。 我們將分析從 SARSCoV-2 感染住院患者收集的鼻咽樣本中的上呼吸道微生物組。 生物信息學將用於評估具有 COVID-19 嚴重程度類別（無症狀、輕度症狀、重度/危重病）和病毒載量的微生物群。我們的研究目標是 (1) 描述住院期間 COVID-19 上呼吸道微生物組的縱向變化，(2) 確定上呼吸道微生物組是否與 COVID-19 的嚴重程度相關，以及 (3) 比較上呼吸道 SARS CoV- 2 病毒載量與微生物群。 這項研究的影響是提供COVID-19呼吸道微生物組的見解。 我們的結果可能有助於深入了解呼吸道微生物組是否 COVID-19 嚴重程度的生物標記。

24105721.label: Realisation of objectives
24105721.value: Study Recruitment/Sample Size The target project sample size was 120 participants. By completion of the project, we recruited 197 participants. OBJECTIVE 1: Describe longitudinal upper respiratory tract microbiome changes in COVID-19 during hospitalization: A) Use 16S rRNA sequencing to profile microbiota of serial nasopharyngeal and throat samples from hospitalized patients confirmed with SARS-CoV-2 infection The target 16s rRNA sequencing sample size was 360 samples. By completion of the project we performed 16S sequencing on 394 samples including 314 nasopharyngeal and throat swabs and 80 tracheal aspirate samples. B) Analyze specie diversity and abundance over time using three time points: at hospital admission, within the first week of hospitalization and last sample before discharge or death We found that longitudinal change in upper respiratory tract species diversity and abundance was significantly affected by antimicrobial use during hospitalization in COVID-19 patients. Overall, assessment showed that upper airway microbiota alpha and beta diversity did not change overtime during 2 weeks of hospitalization in antibiotic-naïve hospitalized COVID-19 patients and healthy individuals (Research Output 1 Figure 3 and Figure S5). C) Compare plasma cytokine profile with changes in respiratory microbiome In the project proposal we planned for 120 patients that included multiple time points (total 210 samples). Cytokine analysis was performed for 122 study participants. Since upper respiratory microbiota remained stable during the first 2 weeks of hospitalization, we reduced the cytokine analysis to only samples taken within 1 week of early upper respiratory microbiota. This resulted in 90 COVID-19 patients who had cytokine levels measured within 1 week of upper respiratory microbiota sampling. Using a Negative Binomial Generalized Linear Model, changes in numerous cytokine factors were significantly associated with clinical factors (Manuscript 1 Figure 6). Specific correlations between upper respiratory tract microbiota and plasma cytokine levels were identified (Manuscript 1 Figure S7, Table S5). Most of the pair-wise associations were not directly between microbiota and cytokines that were individually associated with COVID-19 severity. After excluding samples taken after antimicrobial therapy, we found that only Acinetobacter, Hespellia and Campylobacter were associated with MIG, IL-18, Fractalkine and IL-1β (Manuscript 1 Figure 7). OBJECTIVE 2: Determine if upper respiratory tract microbiome is associated with severity of COVID-19: A) Categorize patients into different three severity levels of COVID-19: (1) asymptomatic, (2) mild symptomatic, and (3) severe/critically ill and analyze upper respiratory tract microbiota in different severity of COVID-19. We selected the earliest collected NPSTS samples from each subject (hospitalized COVID-19 = 171, non-COVID-19 ICU = 11, healthy = 15) to profile the upper airway microbial communities. The median time interval between time of hospitalization and sampling time of first sample was 3 days. Firmicutes was the most abundant microbial phyla in the surveyed samples (mean relative abundance ± sd of 34.70 ± 1.20%), followed by Bacteroidota (30.06 ± 1.30%), Proteobacteria (17.86 ± 1.32%) and eleven other phyla. Proteobacteria were lower in both hospitalized COVID-19 (17.70 ± 1.44%, Mann-Whitney U test p < 0.01) and non-COVID-19 ICU patients (6.52 ± 2.10%, p <0.001) compared to healthy volunteers (27.95 ± 3.62%). Alpha diversity as measured by Shannon, Simpson and Evenness was progressively reduced as severity of COVID-19 increased (Research Output 1 Figure 2A, Figure S3A). Similarly, distinct clustering of the microbial communities from COVID-19 patients, in particular those with severe/critical severity, from healthy controls was observed in weighted GUniFrac, unweighted GUniFrac and Bray-Curtis distance at the ASV level (p < 0.001). Antibiotics treatment (Yes vs No) was consistently the most significant covariate that had the largest effect on the overall structure of the upper airway microbiota in all beta diversity metrics (Research Output 1 Figure 2A, Figure S3B, Table S2). Similarly, the microbial community was also significantly affected by intubation (Yes vs No) and ICU admission (Yes vs No). The effect of severity (severe/critical vs non-severe/critical), peak CRP (≤ 7 vs > 7), hospitalized time (≤ 1 vs ≥ 2 weeks) and antivirus treatment (Yes vs No) on structure of microbial community was not detected in all measures of beta diversity (Research Output 1 Figure 2A, Figure S3C). Because antimicrobial use was the most significant factor that affected upper airway microbiota dysbiosis, we further assessed the difference in microbiota without the effect of antimicrobials. All measures of alpha diversity were no longer significantly different across COVID-19 severity groups when confounding by antimicrobial was removed (Research Output 1 Figure 2B, Figure S4A). After exclusion of samples taken after antimicrobials, microbiota from severe/critical COVID-19 patients still showed dispersive distribution by beta diversity analysis when compared to other groups but the differences were reduced (Research Output 1 Figure 2B, Figure S4B). B) Association between specie diversity and abundance with severity of COVID-19 Differentially abundant bacterial genera associated with demographic and clinical variants were characterized using linear discriminant analysis by LEfSe in the surveyed NPSTS samples from COVID-19 patients in an exploratory analysis (n = 171) (LDA score > 2, p < 0.05) (Research Output 1 Figure 4, Table S3). Since 63% (32/51) of severe/critical COVID-19 patients in this study were admitted to the ICU, we further selected early NPSTS samples prior to antimicrobial use within the 1st week of hospitalization (n = 116) to identify bacterial markers that may be used to predict need for ICU admission (Research Output 1 Figure 5). A total 13 discriminative bacterial genera were observed using linear discriminant analysis. The differential abundances of these 13 bacterial genera in the upper airway tract within the first week of hospitalization predicted the need for ICU admission with a combined AUC of 0.95 (95%CI of 0.91 – 0.99). Comparatively, prediction based on clinical demographics and comorbidity (age, gender and Charlson’s comorbidity index) only achieved a combined AUC of 0.71 (95%CI of 0.57 – 0.85). Combination of clinical and microbiota (AUC of 0.96 (95%CI 0.93 – 1.00) did not improve on the predictive performance compared to use of microbiota alone (Research Output 1 Figure S6, p = 0.486). OBJECTIVE 3: Compare upper respiratory tract SARS-CoV-2 viral load and other microbiota: A) Assess correlation between specie abundance with maximal upper respiratory tract SARS-CoV-2 viral load quantified by reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction We found that median [IQR] maximal SARS-CoV-2 viral load in the upper respiratory tract was similar across the different severity groups (asymptomatic 27.3 [20.3-29.6], mild/moderate 21.5 [17.1-27.6] and severe/critical 20.2 [18.2-25.5], p = 0.086). On multivariate analysis, maximal viral load was not related with upper respiratory microbiota after controlling for important confounders such as antibiotic and tracheal intubation (Research Output 1 Figure 2B).

24105721.label: Major findings and research outcome
24105721.value: 1. [Antimicrobial therapy is the major confounder of upper respiratory microbiota in hospitalized patients with COVID-19] Our carefully constructed cohort showed that removal of the confounding effect of antimicrobial therapy resulted in completely different interpretations of abundance and diversity measurements in COVID-19 (Objective 2A). Many previous studies have highlighted specific changes in upper respiratory microbiota but adjustment for confounding factors such as antimicrobial use and mechanical ventilation were often not performed. This study demonstrates that careful considerations on study design and data interpretation are required when assessing the validity of COVID-19 related microbiota study results. 2. [Alpha diversity is similar across severity of COVID-19] Many studies suggest reduced alpha diversity in upper respiratory microbiota is a hallmark of higher COVID-19 severity. In contrast we showed that alpha diversity was similar across severity of COVID-19 if samples taken after antimicrobial therapy were excluded (Objective 2A). 3. Beta diversity is different in severe/critical COVID-19 compared to either asymptomatic or mild/moderate COVID-19 The difference in beta diversity in severe/critical COVID-19 was reduced but remains significant after exclusion of samples taken after antimicrobial therapy (Objective 2A). 4. [Upper airway microbiota in COVID-19 patients remained unchanged during 2 weeks of hospitalization if antimicrobials were not used] Our data suggests that previous studies which reported changes in upper respiratory microbiota over time in COVID-19 were likely confounded by medical interventions such as antimicrobial use and tracheal intubation (Objective 1). 5. [Early hospitalization upper airway microbiota may be associated with severity of COVID-19] We found 13 bacterial genera from the early upper airway microbiota which were associated with need for ICU admission (Objective 2B). Our study suggests sampling upper respiratory microbiota alone may be able to predict subsequent severity of COVID-19. 6. [Upper respiratory microbiota in COVID-19 is not associated with peak viral load] Peak viral load was not a significant confounder in differences in beta diversity across severity of COVID-19 (Objective 3) 7. [Plasma cytokine levels may not directly reflect the local inflammation profile in upper respiratory tract dysbiosis in COVID-19] Significant pair-wise associations between microbiota and cytokines were different to microbiota and cytokines that are individually associated with COVID-19 severity (Objective 1C).

24105721.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24105721.value: Although our study included one of the largest sample of comprehensively characterized cohort of COVID-19 patients, there are several limitations. First, this was a single center study on patients of Southeast Asian descent which may limit the generalizability of our results. Second, we did not analyze viral or fungal microbiota. Third, change in SARS-CoV-2 variant may affect the association between COVID-19 and respiratory tract microbiota. Fourth, all patients in this cohort were unvaccinated for COVID-19. Fifth, the exploratory findings on association between upper respiratory bacterial genera and severity of COVID-19 requires future validation. We suggest further research in different healthcare settings and ethnicity of patients with larger sample sizes are needed to validate our findings. In addition, how upper respiratory microbiota changes due to emerging SARS-CoV-2 variants and vaccination status should be assessed. Lastly, further prospective studies are needed to confirm if early upper respiratory tract bacterial microbiota can predict subsequent severity of disease in COVID-19. This may lead to intervention trials to robustly test whether targeting microbiota may be a therapeutic option to prevent development of severe critical COVID-19.

24105721.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24105721.value: Our research project evaluated the microbiome in the nose and throat of hospitalized patients with coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19). Upper respiratory tract microbiome is the community of micro-organisms that resides in the nose and throat. We showed that microbiome of upper respiratory tract in COVID-19 is greatly affected by use of antimicrobial therapy. This highlights the importance of study design and data interpretation in clinical research in respiratory microbiome. COVID-19 patients with severe disease have a distinct microbiome pattern in the upper respiratory tract. Specific bacteria detected from the upper respiratory tract in COVID-19 patients during early phase of infection may predict the chance of developing severe or critical disease. Furthermore, upper respiratory tract microbiome remains stable during hospitalization if antimicrobial therapy is not used. Further research is needed validate these findings and assess whether targeting microbiota may be a therapeutic option to prevent development of severe critical COVID-19.

24106321.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24106321.value: 白果內酯（Bilobalide，簡稱BB）是一個具有六個連續手性中心和高氧化態的倍半萜烯類化合物。儘管 BB 已顯示出有潛力的神經保護和心臟保護作用，但其具體的作用機制 (MoA)尚不明確。由於BB的結構複雜性和不穩定性，迄今為止，有關BB結構-生物活性關係（SAR）的深入研究也尚未見報導。為了深入研究BB的生物活性作用機制並拓展其治療潛力，本研究擬開發穩定的 BB 類似物，以期作為化學探針和潛在的心臟保護劑。初步研究顯示，我們通過三個高產合成步驟，成功地將 BB 直接多樣化轉化為穩定的非天然內酰胺類似物，並通過X 射線晶體學確定了其化學結構。更重要的是，我們發現其中一種 BB 類似物在人類多能幹細胞衍生的心臟毒性模型中顯示出有潛力的心臟保護活性，而結構不穩定的 BB 則並無活性。合成的BB類似物顯示出的高穩定性和高生物活性，因此，我們擬開發更多具有新穎化學結構的BB 類似物，以期開發一類全新的心臟保護藥物。 基於前期的研究數據，我們將合成四個系列結構多樣的 BB天然產物類似物，並評估它們的心臟保護活性、代謝穩定性和腸道通透性。這些新型類似物包括O-烷基化類似物、環氧化和二羥基化類似物、N-烷基化和N-芳基化內酰胺類似物。我還將創建光親和及“可點擊”類似物來闡明其分子作用機制（MoA），並進行深入的結構-生物活性關係（SAR）研究以優化 BB 類似物的藥效。這項工作將創造具有多樣化功能、新穎化學結構和具心臟保護作用的BB 類似物，將為開發新穎心臟保護藥物鋪平道路。

24106321.label: Realisation of objectives
24106321.value: To fulfill the objectives, we started with the synthesis of bilobalide analogues (objective 1). This is the foundation for the biological assays outlined in objective 2. We synthesized four series of structurally diverse, pseudo-natural product analogues of BB and evaluate their cardioprotective effects. These novel analogues include O-alkylated analogues, epoxidated and dihydroxylated analogues, N-alkylated and N- arylated lactam analogues. We synthesized approximately 15–20 analogues in each series. By using advanced analytical techniques, such as LC-MS, HPLC, 1D and 2D NMR as well as X-ray crystallography, the absolute and relative configuration of the synthesized analogues were analyzed. In summary, a drug library of around 40 bilobalide analogues has been achieved during the funding period. Next, the evaluation of cardioprotective effects, metabolic stability, and intestinal permeability of bilobalide analogues have been examined (objective 2). We evaluated the cardioprotective effects of the analogues using our established hPSC-CM model of Dox-induced cardiomyopathy. The specific methodology is as follows: In the initial screening step, hPSC-CMs were co-treated with Dox and a four-point dosage of the selected compounds for viability measurements. Next, cardioprotection were assessed, based on the abilities of these compounds to ameliorate Dox-induced changes in mitochondrial morphology and function. Dexrazoxane were used as a positive control. The proportion of hPSC-CMs with fragmented or depolarized mitochondria were measured by mitochondrial staining. Changes in mitochondrial depolarization were imaged and quantified using a plate reader. Finally, sarcomeric disarray was evaluated by measuring the proportion of hPSC-CMs with disorganized sarcomeres. The top 10 candidates with the most potent cardioprotective effects were subjected to subsequent evaluation for their metabolic stability and intestinal permeability. The instability of BB has greatly hindered its SAR study, and more importantly, its clinical application. However, our stable lactam analogues of BB may effectively resolve this hinderance. In collaboration with Prof. Joan Zuo (CUHK), who possesses considerable expertise in drug metabolism studies, we investigated the metabolic stability of the BB analogues in vitro using human serum and liver microsome (objective 2). The stability profiles of the first batch of analogues guided further structural optimization, thus leading to compounds with enhanced drug-likeness. Specifically, the BB analogues and human serum/liver microsome were incubated together at 37°C. Samples were taken at different time intervals followed by precipitating the proteins and extracting the BB analogues with acetonitrile. The samples were centrifuged, and the resulting supernatants were analyzed by HPLC-MS. Compounds with a half-life at least twice that of BB were selected for subsequent intestinal permeability assay. Intestinal permeability is a critical property of orally delivered drugs. The in vitro Caco-2 monolayer model serves as a powerful human small intestinal mucosal model for evaluating the intestinal permeability of small-molecule inhibitors. The selected BB analogues were evaluated and fine-tuned as guided by this assay in collaboration with Prof. Joan Zuo (CUHK) (objective 2). The specific methodologies were as follows: In the bi-directional transport study, the BB analogues were loaded onto the apical or basolateral chamber as in our established Caco-2 monolayer model. Next, aliquots of samples were collected from the receiver side at different time intervals to analyze the concentrations of BB analogues. For analogues that yield an efflux transport ratio > 2, the potential role of the efflux transporter were evaluated by comparing the efflux transport of the drug candidate in the presence and absence of various transporter inhibitors (e.g. MK571 as a MRP inhibitor and verapamil as a Pglycoprotein inhibitor). The permeability coefficients (Papp) of the analogues were calculated as described previously. The five analogues with the highest in vitro Papp values were subjects of future in vivo investigation. In addition, the Papp values of the analogues supported the SAR studies to provide medicinal chemistry efforts for structural optimization. Based on the above findings, we synthesized four series of structurally diverse, pseudo-natural product BB analogues to conduct SAR studies (objective 3). The new analogues included (i) N-alkylated analogs on the lactam nitrogen of the D-ring, (ii) N-arylated analogs on the lactam nitrogen of the C-ring, (iii) N-alkylated analogs on the lactam nitrogen of the D-ring and O-alkylated analogues at the C10 hydroxyl group, and (iv) dibenzoylated (diBz) Bilobalide analogues. We synthesized approximately 5–10 analogues in each series. By using analytical techniques, such as LC-MS, HPLC, 1D and 2D NMR as well as X-ray crystallography, the absolute and relative configuration of the synthesized analogues were analyzed. In summary, a library of around 30 bilobalide analogues has been achieved during the funding period. Finally, mechanism of action of these analogues were studied. As ferroptosis is linked to cardiovascular diseases, we hypothesized that the cardiovascular protective effects from our pilot study are linked to ferroptosis. Therefore, our drug library was screened against ferroptosis. Using ferroptosis inducer RSL3, we established cell line-based assays to screen for anti-ferroptotic activity of BB analogues. All of the three cell lines, including HT22, along with HMC3 and BV-2. The cells were pre-treated with RSL3 (200 nM for HT22 and HMC3, 500 nM for BV-2) for 2 hours, followed by the treatment of bilobalide analogues (50 µM) for 22 hours. Then we further tested anti-ferroptotic activity of BB analogues with different doses and found BB10, the most potent anti-ferroptotic inhibitor. To gain insights into the mechanism of action of BB10 against the RSL3-induced ferroptosis, we performed immunoblotting to evaluate the GPX4 level using the HMC3 cell model. Additionally, we tested the level of the key autophagy marker microtubule-associated protein 1 light chain 3 beta-II (LC3-II) to see whether BB10 could inhibit the RSL3-induced autophagy. To further explore the efficacy of BB10, we established cellular rescue assays using well-studied ferroptosis inducers that target different stages of ferroptosis, including FIN56, a distinct ferroptosis inducer that depletes GPX4 levels, and System Xc- inhibitors erastin.

24106321.label: Major findings and research outcome
24106321.value: 1.We have successfully transformed bilobalide into a series of unique lactam analogs. These molecular editing strategies hinge on the discovery of the simple yet unexpected reactivity of the synthetic intermediates, ultimately enabling the construction of valuable libraries that originated from bilobalide. (JACS Au, 2024) 2. We developed a doxorubicin (DOX)-induced cardiomyopathy model on cardiomyocytes from hiPSC derived from breast cancer patients to preliminarily investigate the cardioprotection effect of BB analogues upon modification. The hPSC-CMs was co-treated with DOX and the selected compounds for viability measurements. Next, cardioprotection was assessed, based on the abilities of these compounds to ameliorate DOX-induced cardiotoxicity. Cardioprotection was quantified using prestoblue staining. As expected, BB rescued the cardiomyocytes against DOX. In which, we found the potency of BB analogue to demonstrate the protective effect. We further performed an in-depth evaluation. At 0.1-10 μM, it demonstrated a up shift dose-dependent manner, and BB analogue of 10 μM gave a relatively higher value of prestoblue staining. BB analogue of 100 μM decreased the value which was speculated to be due to the high concentration affecting the normal biological process in cardiomyocytes. Besides, BB10 primarily undergoes enzyme-mediated hydrolytic metabolism. 3. Structure-activity relationship analysis revealed that R1 is 3,4-dihydroxyphenylethyl and R2 is benzoyl, indicating that the BB analog exhibits the best activity. The scaffold of BB is crucial for activity; if the scaffold was damaged, activity was lost. 4. As ferroptosis is linked to cardiovascular diseases, phenotypic screening led to the discovery of BB10 with anti-ferroptotic activity across multiple cell lines. BB10 significantly reduced key ferroptosis markers, and notably counteracted GPX4 degradation induced by RSL3. Therefore, modification of BB analogs provides a scaffold derived from natural products for developing drug candidates in the treatment with cardiovascular diseases and neurodegenerative diseases.(JACS Au, 2024)

24106321.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24106321.value: In this project new drug candidates derived from Bilobalide against cardiovascular disease were probed. During the project, we developed new synthetic routes for modification. To ensure the identity, the molecular structure of the drugs was determined by state-of-the-art techniques. These drug candidates were designed from scratch, produced and tested to investigate the cardioprotection effect. We also unexpectedly discovered that these compounds possess anti-ferroptosis activity which is linked to cardiovascular diseases and neurodegenerative diseases.
