24107121.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24107121.value: Over the past two decades, global adult alcohol consumption per capita had been increased steady from around 5.9L to 6.5L; and it is predicted to rise further to 7.6L by 2030. This implies that the World Health Organization global targets in reducing the harmful use of alcohol are unlikely to be achieved. Longitudinal studies indicated that chronic and over-consumption of alcohol is a risk factor for accelerated brain aging and cognitive decline. More intriguingly, a recent study also suggested that the effect of alcohol is accumulative over life—for each gram of alcohol consumed per day it is associated with 0.02 years of increased relative brain age. Clearly, alcohol (ethanol) is a potent neurotoxin; but the trajectories of molecular events underlying its effect on accelerating brain aging remained unclear. By analyzing both the pubic human and mouse transcriptomes and our own neuronal metabolomic array datasets, we revealed that ethanol hijacks the entire aerobic glycolytic landscape in neurons; matching with the global changes found at brain tissue level. Ethanol metabolism, in a prioritized and uncontrolled manner; contributes carbon to excessive citrate biosynthesis. Accumulation of citrate in both cytosol and mitochondria respectively inhibits glycolysis and Krebs cycle; yet this promotes de novo lipogenesis; leading to ectopic accumulation of lipid species and oil droplets in neurons. On the other hand, impaired oxidative phosphorylation is consistently ranked the first among all downregulated pathways from the transcriptome dataset; which global promoter analyses indicated that the loss in nuclear respiratory factor-1 (NRF1) activity is the most likely link behind. Our preliminary data indicated that NRF1 co-activator PGC1α level reduces significantly as its stabilizing partner NQO1 is deactivated upon the exhaustion of NADPH by the uncontrolled ethanol metabolism. Together, these reprogramming of the central carbon metabolism resulted from ethanol oxidation is associated with the acquisitions of insulin resistance and related senescence phenotypes in neurons—a phenomenon contributes to accelerated brain aging and functional decline as we previously reported. In this proposal, our first goal is to trace longitudinally in vivo on how chronic ethanol consumption is related to brain senescence load; behavioral and histological changes in a transgenic mouse model that enables fluorescent labelling of cells that are turning senescent. Secondly, mechanistic investigation on how ethanol-derived metabolites induce neuronal metabolic reprogramming; insulin resistance and senescence will be performed. Finally, anti-diabetic and senolytic drug candidates will be tested for their potentials in reversing ethanol effects on cell physiology and overall brain functions. 在過往的二十多年間，全球成人人均酒精消耗量從 5.9升穩步增長至6.5 升；並預計在2030 年間進一步上升至 7.6升。這意味著世界衛生組織定下對減少全球有害使用酒精的相關目標不太可能實現。近年有縱向性臨床研究指出，長期及過度飲酒是加速大腦老化和認知能力下降的危險因素。而其他研究亦表明，酒精的影響能終生累積，大概每一克酒精可增加若0.02年的大腦年齡。毫無疑問，酒精（乙醇）是一種神經毒素，但它作為加速大腦衰老危險因素背後的分子機制仍有代注釋。透過分析人類和小鼠大腦轉錄組公共數據以及神經元代謝組學數據；我們發現乙醇能”騎劫”神經元的糖代謝功能，而這種細胞上的轉變亦反影在大腦組織分析中。乙醇代謝會以優先和不受控的模式，在人類細胞中產生大量的檸檬酸鹽。後者在細胞質和線粒體中的積累會分別抑製糖代謝和三羧酸循環；但同時會促成脂肪合成，以油滴狀態異位積累在神組元中。另一方面，人鼠大腦轉錄組數據富集分析均顯示氧化磷酸化為首要受減弱的細胞功能；而啟動子分析表明，核呼吸因子-1 (NRF1) 活性的喪失是最有可能的成因。我們的初期數據指出，長期分解酒精會耗儘神經細胞中的NADPH分子，使NQO1活性下降並喪失其穩定PGC1α蛋白的功能，繼而令PGC1α蛋白過度降解。由於PGC1α是NRF1 共激活因子，這些變化從而令NRF1活性下降。這一系列由乙醇氧化引起的中央碳代謝重編過程與細胞產生胰島素抵抗及衰老表型有密切的關係。這些細胞層面上的生理變化正如我們早前發表的發現一樣，會加速大腦衰老和功能衰退。在這份提議書中，我們的第一研究目標為利用熒光轉基因小鼠模型並分析其行為及組織學變化；縱向追踪慢性乙醇代謝與大腦衰老細胞負荷之間的關係。而第二研究目標為分析乙醇及其衍生代謝物如何誘導神經元進行代謝重編程的機制。最後，我們將測試現有抗糖尿病和抗衰老候選藥物在逆轉及延緩乙醇對細胞和大腦功能損害的潛力。

24113221.label: Project Objectives
24113221.value: RA is the commonest inflammatory arthritis with prevalence varies from 0.13% to 0.9%. Although the control of disease improved significantly with the introduction of biological or synthetic targeted therapy, a significant proportion of patients remain burdened by the joint symptoms and long term medication side effects. The disease also incurs high societal costs as a result of the disability caused and expensive advanced treatment required. The exact pathogenesis of this systemic autoimmune disease is unknown. Although an interplay of genetic and epigenetic as well as environmental components leading to autoimmunity has been postulated, whether bone or synovium is the primary site of the resultant inflammation is yet to be confirmed. An important advance in RA research recently has been the delineation of the pre-clinical phase of the disease which opens up the window of opportunity for early treatment and even disease prevention. Previously studies have demonstrated the possibility of delaying the onset of arthritis in susceptible patients with pharmacological interventions. An accurate biomarker capable of identifying these individuals “at risk” of progressing to inflammatory arthritis is thus of upmost importance. Bone changes have been found to occur very early in the disease course of RA even before any detectable clinical inflammation. High resolution peripheral quantitative computer tomography (HR-pQCT) is a novel imaging technique which is capable of offering excellent non-invasive assessment of micro-structural bone changes. It could be the ideal modality to detect the early bone abnormalities, which could be serve as a biomarker for predicting RA, in the pre-clinical phase of the disease. In the current study, we would like to test the hypothesis that early HR-pQCT detected changes could predict the development of inflammatory arthritis in patients presenting with joint pain. The conclusion drawn from the study could be practice changing. We could potentially utilize HR-pQCT to detect early micro-structural changes in patients presenting with joint symptoms which could in turn stratify their risk of developing inflammatory arthritis. Thus, personalized early or even preventive treatment could be given to patients at imminent risk of arthritis which might dramatically modify the disease course. The use of expensive targeted agents can also be prioritized. Further structural changes and thus non-reversible damage might be abrogated as a result of early intervention. The ultimate goal will be to achieve a cure of the disease and remove the negative impact of chronic arthritis on individuals and the health care system. The detailed examination of the early microstructural bone changes in at risk individual in this study can also improve our understanding the pathogenesis of RA which would be provocative for further mechanistic research. The unique patient cohort and serially collected clinical data of this study are important assets for further investigations into the pathophysiology of the transition from pre-clinical to clinical stages of RA. The current largely investigational role of HR-pQCT might also be changed in the future. Its potential use as a non-invasive bio-marker for inflammatory arthritis in daily clinical practice should not be underestimated. On top of its academic and scientific significance, the results of this study will also be of educational value as well as public interest. This might be an example of how translational research could impact health for students. The potential use of HR-pQCT detected bone changes as biomarkers might allow clinicians to practice precision-based medicine offering risk-appropriate and cost-effective treatments to our patients.
rows: RA is the commonest inflammatory arthritis with prevalence varies from 0.13% to 0.9%. Although the control of disease improved significantly with the introduction of biological or synthetic targeted therapy, a significant proportion of patients remain burdened by the joint symptoms and long term medication side effects. The disease also incurs high societal costs as a result of the disability caused and expensive advanced treatment required.

The exact pathogenesis of this systemic autoimmune disease is unknown. Although an interplay of genetic and epigenetic as well as environmental components leading to autoimmunity has been postulated, whether bone or synovium is the primary site of the resultant inflammation is yet to be confirmed. An important advance in RA research recently has been the delineation of the pre-clinical phase of the disease which opens up the window of opportunity for early treatment and even disease prevention. Previously studies have demonstrated the possibility of delaying the onset of arthritis in susceptible patients with pharmacological interventions. An accurate biomarker capable of identifying these individuals “at risk” of progressing to inflammatory arthritis is thus of upmost importance.

Bone changes have been found to occur very early in the disease course of RA even before any detectable clinical inflammation. High resolution peripheral quantitative computer tomography (HR-pQCT) is a novel imaging technique which is capable of offering excellent non-invasive assessment of micro-structural bone changes. It could be the ideal modality to detect the early bone abnormalities, which could be serve as a biomarker for predicting RA, in the pre-clinical phase of the disease.
In the current study, we would like to test the hypothesis that early HR-pQCT detected changes could predict the development of inflammatory arthritis in patients presenting with joint pain.

The conclusion drawn from the study could be practice changing. We could potentially utilize HR-pQCT to detect early micro-structural changes in patients presenting with joint symptoms which could in turn stratify their risk of developing inflammatory arthritis. Thus, personalized early or even preventive treatment could be given to patients at imminent risk of arthritis which might dramatically modify the disease course. The use of expensive targeted agents can also be prioritized. Further structural changes and thus non-reversible damage might be abrogated as a result of early intervention. The ultimate goal will be to achieve a cure of the disease and remove the negative impact of chronic arthritis on individuals and the health care system.

The detailed examination of the early microstructural bone changes in at risk individual in this study can also improve our understanding the pathogenesis of RA which would be provocative for further mechanistic research. The unique patient cohort and serially collected clinical data of this study are important assets for further investigations into the pathophysiology of the transition from pre-clinical to clinical stages of RA. The current largely investigational role of HR-pQCT might also be changed in the future. Its potential use as a non-invasive bio-marker for inflammatory arthritis in daily clinical practice should not be underestimated.

On top of its academic and scientific significance, the results of this study will also be of educational value as well as public interest. This might be an example of how translational research could impact health for students. The potential use of HR-pQCT detected bone changes as biomarkers might allow clinicians to practice precision-based medicine offering risk-appropriate and cost-effective treatments to our patients.

24113221.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24113221.value: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is the commonest inflammatory arthritis affecting 0.35% of the population in Hong Kong. Although the control of disease improved with the introduction of biological or synthetic targeted therapy, a significant proportion of patients remain burdened by the joint symptoms and long-term medication side effects. The disease is also associated with high socioeconomic costs as a result of the disability caused and expensive advanced treatment required. A recent breakthrough in RA research has been the delineation of a pre-clinical phase of the disease which gives rise to the opportunity for early personalized treatment and even disease prevention. An accurate biomarker capable of identifying individuals “at risk” of progressing to arthritis is highly sought after. Bone changes have been found to occur very early in RA even before any detectable clinical inflammation. High resolution peripheral quantitative computer tomography (HR-pQCT) is a novel imaging technique which is capable of offering excellent non-invasive assessment of micro-structural bone changes. It could be the ideal modality to detect the early bone abnormalities in the pre-clinical phase of RA. In this study, we would like to investigate the role of micro-structural bone changes on HR-pQCT in predicting the development of inflammatory arthritis (IA) in patients with joint pain but no clinical joint inflammation. Two hundred patients complaining of joint pain without clinical inflammation will participate in this 2-year prospective, observational, multi-centered cohort study. IA is defined as the development of clinical arthritis (tenderness and swelling). HR-pQCT examination of the 2nd-4th metacarpophalangeal and 5th metatarsophalangeal joints will be performed at baseline. Bone erosions, volumetric bone mineral density, joint space as well as the micro-architectural bone parameters will be assessed. The participants will be followed up for the development of IA for 2 years. The primary outcome is the difference in the proportion of participants developing IA after 2 years between those who have and those who do not have baseline erosion on HR-pQCT. Secondary outcomes include the odd ratio of bone erosion for the development of IA after controlling other clinical variables, association of other baseline structural changes with the development of IA, correlation of the bone changes with serological or inflammatory markers, and Kaplan-Meier analysis examining the IA-free survival time for the HR-pCT changes. The results of this study could improve our management of patients at risk of RA and advance our understanding in the pathogenesis of the disease.

24115121.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24115121.value: Background: Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is a common neurodevelopmental disorder with elusive etiology. Patients with this childhood onset disease suffer from inattention, hyperactivity and impulsivity, which have significant impact on the functioning in daily life. Emerging evidence from the study of gut-brain axis provides opportunities to explain the pathogenesis of this debilitating condition. Methylphenidate is a commonly used stimulant medication for treatment of ADHD with 70% response rate though gastrointestinal side effects are common. However, the relationship of gut microbiome and methylphenidate in ADHD patients, and whether gut microbiome affects treatment response and gastrointestinal adverse events of methylphenidate has not been comprehensively studied. Hypothesis: We hypothesize that gut microbiome may play a role in the pathogenesis of ADHD, and gut microbiome may also contribute to treatment response of methylphenidate and its gastrointestinal side effects in attention deficit hyperactivity disorders (ADHD) Aim: Being the first study of gut microbiome in patients with ADHD in Hong Kong, we aim at generating essential information to allow an evidence-based evaluation of the role of gut microbiome in the pathogenesis of ADHD and explore specific gut microbiome signatures accounting for treatment response and gastrointestinal side effects. Objectives: 1. To identify the gut microbiota profile of ADHD cases and controls 2. To identify the potential specific gut microbiome signature accounting for treatment-response in ADHD patients on methylphenidate 3. To compare the gut microbiome profile in ADHD patients with or without gastrointestinal side effects due to methylphenidate Design: Objective 1. The study is a case-control study of 160 cases of ADHD and 160 age-matched and sex-matched controls. Objective 2 and 3. The study is a prospective study to study the potential specific gut microbiome signature accounting for treatment response in ADHD patients on methylphenidate and to compare the gut microbiome profile with or without gastrointestinal side effects due to methylphenidate Significance: The research findings from this study will to help in the in-depth understanding of the role of gut microbiota in ADHD patients and explore new microbiota-based tools for predicting treatment response and novel microbiota-based interventional strategies for ADHD. 背景: 專注力失調及過度活躍症是一種常見的神經發育障礙，病因不明。患者會專注力不足、過度活躍和衝動，令他們的日常生活出現問題。來自腸腦軸研究的新證據提供了解釋病症發病機制的機會。鹽酸甲酯是常用於治療專注力失調及過度活躍症的中樞神經刺激劑，有百分之七十的治療反應率, 常見的副作用包括胃腸道副作用。然而，專注力失調及過度活躍症患者的腸道微生物群與鹽酸甲酯的關係，以及腸道微生物群是否影響鹽酸甲酯的治療反應和胃腸道副作用尚未得到全面研究。 研究假設: 我們假設腸道微生物群可能在專注力失調及過度活躍症的發病機制中發揮作用，腸道微生物群也可能影響鹽酸甲酯的治療反應及胃腸道副作用。 目的: 作為香港第一項針對專注力失調及過度活躍症患者的腸道微生物組的研究，我們旨在評估腸道微生物組對專注力失調及過度活躍症的發病機制中的角色，並探索特定的腸道微生物組特徵來解釋治療反應和胃腸道副作用。 目標: 1. 確定專注力失調及過度活躍症病例和對照的腸道微生物群譜 2. 確定潛在的特定腸道微生物組特徵，說明專注力失調及過度活躍症患者對鹽酸甲酯的治療反應 3. 比較經歷和沒有經歷鹽酸甲酯引起的胃腸道副作用的專注力失調及過度活躍症患者的腸道微生物組譜 設計: 第一目標: 本研究是對160名專注力失調及過度活躍症患者和160名年齡和性別匹配的對照組進行的病例對照研究。 第二和第三目標: 該研究是一項前瞻性研究，旨在研究可能導致專注力失調及過度活躍症患者對鹽酸甲酯治療反應的特定腸道微生物組特徵，並比較有或沒有鹽酸甲酯引起的胃腸道副作用的腸道微生物組特徵。 意義: 本研究的研究結果將有助於深入了解腸道微生物群在專注力失調及過度活躍症患者中的作用，並探索新的基於微生物群的工具來預測治療反應的工具和基於微生物群的專注力失調及過度活躍症的干預策略。

24115421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24115421.value: Background: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) is a prevalent cancer in the southern parts of China and Southeast Asia. It is among the ten most common types of male cancer in Hong Kong. Despite advances in treatment, cancer recurrence still occurs in approximately 25% of patients after curative-intent treatment and this contributes to the majority of disease-associated mortality. Early recognition of tumour recurrence is critical to the implementation of salvage treatment for disease control. However, there are intrinsic drawbacks with the current surveillance modalities including endoscopy and magnetic resonance imaging and this often leads to a delay in the diagnosis of NPC recurrence. While plasma Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) DNA is a well-established blood-based biomarker of NPC, the diagnostic performance for detecting recurrent NPC via commonly used polymerase chain reaction-based analysis is substantially lower compared to that for primary, treatment-naïve NPC. There is thus an urgent need for a reliable tool to enhance the surveillance of NPC recurrence. Objectives: This project aims to analyse the molecular profiles of plasma EBV DNA in post-treatment patients with recurrent NPC and those without recurrence. Based on such knowledge, we aim to develop a sequencing-based plasma EBV DNA assay for detection of recurrent NPC. Experimental plans: A case-control analysis of post-treatment patients with or without recurrent NPC is proposed. Sequencing analysis of plasma samples from the two groups of post-treatment patients will be performed to study the differentiating molecular features of plasma EBV DNA between them. An enrichment step of EBV DNA molecules in plasma samples will be performed via the capture-probe system to facilitate the downstream molecular analysis. Expected outcomes: This study will fill knowledge gaps in the molecular profiles of plasma EBV DNA from patients with recurrent NPC. These data will be valuable for the development of a molecular assay to improve the diagnostic performance (both sensitivity and specificity) for detection of recurrent NPC. Preliminary findings: Three patients with recurrent NPC and 4 patients without recurrent NPC have been analysed. Specifically, the molecular features including the quantitative and size profiles of plasma EBV DNA were studied. Of note, plasma EBV DNA from patients with recurrent NPC demonstrated a characteristic nucleosomal size pattern with a modal peak at about 160 base-pairs. In contrast, plasma EBV DNA from patients without recurrent NPC did not have such nucleosomal size pattern. 背景：在中國南部及東南亞，鼻咽癌是一種常見的癌症。在香港，它是屬於十種最常見的男性癌症之一。儘管治療上的進步，約百分之二十五的病人在根治性的治療後仍會有癌症復發，而這亦導致大部分的與疾病相關聯的死亡。及早找出腫瘤復發對進行挽救治療和疾病控制至關重要。可是，現在的復發檢測方法（包括內窺鏡和磁力共振）存有缺陷，因而導致診斷鼻咽癌復發的延誤。當血漿EB病毒（EBV）DNA是一個得到公認的，血液中的鼻咽癌生物標誌物，透過常見的聚合酶鏈式反應分析去檢測鼻咽癌復發的診斷性能，較原發的，未接受治療的鼻咽癌的為低。因此，我們對一個可靠的工具去加強鼻咽癌復發的檢測，有著逼切的需要。 目標：這個項目的目標是分析有復發和沒有復發的鼻咽癌患者的血漿EBV DNA的分子特徵。基於以上的分析，我們希望研發出一個以測序為基礎的血漿EBV DNA測試，作檢測鼻咽癌復發的用途。 實驗計畫：我們提出以病例對照研究方式，去分析有和沒有復發的鼻咽癌患者。這兩組病人的血漿樣品，會以測序分析，去研究這兩組之間具區分性的血漿EBV DNA的分子特徵。在血漿樣品的EBV DNA分子，會通過捕獲探針去增加數量，以促進之後的分子分析。 預期結果：是次研究有助增進我們對在鼻咽癌復發患者的血漿EBV DNA的分子特徵的認知。這些資料對於研發測試，旨在改善鼻咽癌復發檢測的診斷性能（包括靈敏度和特異性）有莫大裨益。

24115421.label: Realisation of objectives
24115421.value: The two project objectives as stated in the proposal had been successfully achieved. The goal of the current project is to evaluate and enhance plasma Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) DNA as a cancer biomarker for surveillance of nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) recurrence. NPC is a prevalent type of cancer in the southern parts of China including Hong Kong. Despite advances in treatment, there are still approximately 20% of patients who suffer from locoregional or distant recurrence after treatment of curative intent. Plasma EBV DNA is a well-established biomarker of NPC. The diagnostic performance of quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR)-based analysis of plasma EBV DNA is superior for the detection of primary, treatment-naïve PC, with both sensitivity and specificity reported to be greater than 90%. However, the utility of PCR-based plasma EBV DNA analysis for surveillance of NPC in the post-treatment setting has been compromised by its comparatively inferior performance. The sensitivity for detection of stage I or II NPC recurrence was reported to be about 50% only. Objective 1: To investigate the molecular characteristics of circulating Epstein-Barr virus DNA in the plasma of post-treatment nasopharyngeal cancer patients with or without tumour recurrence Differential quantitative, size and end motif profiles of plasma EBV DNA between NPC patients with or without tumour recurrence We have conducted a case-control study encompassing NPC patients with or without recurrence, as stated in the project proposal. For those patients with cancer recurrence, the blood samples were collected after biopsy confirmation. In order to study the molecular characteristics of plasma EBV DNA, targeted EBV sequencing was performed for enrichment of EBV DNA molecules in plasma. In the case cohort of 32 patients with NPC recurrence and 77 patients without recurrence, we analysed the molecular characteristics of plasma EBV DNA including quantitation, size and end motif. In the quantitative analysis by targeted EBV sequencing, the number of EBV and autosomal DNA fragments were quantified and the proportions of plasma EBV DNA fragments over the total number of on-target DNA fragments (including both autosomal and EBV DNA) for all the blood samples analyzed. The median proportions of EBV DNA of those patients with recurrence were significantly higher than those without recurrence. Regarding the size analysis, as reported before, plasma EBV DNA in patients with an established diagnosis of NPC was shown to exhibit a mononucleosomal size pattern, with a peak frequency at about 160 bp. In the current cohort, for patients with NPC recurrence, plasma EBV DNA was also found to have a mononucleosomal size pattern. In contrast, plasma EBV DNA from patients without recurrence did not have such a size pattern. Based on the observation of the size difference, we have previously developed a metric, namely the EBV DNA size ratio, which was defined as the relative proportion of short EBV DNA fragments (80 – 110 bp) normalized by that of short autosomal DNA fragments within the same size range. The recurrence group yielded significantly lower EBV DNA size ratio than the non-recurrence group. Additionally, we proposed to analyse the end motif of plasma EBV DNA, as another fragmentomics biomarker, in the current cohort. Fragmentomics analysis of plasma (human autosomal) DNA, with size profiling as one form of such analysis, has demonstrated its utility for both understanding the fragmentation biology and informing the diagnosis of a wide spectrum of diseases. In such an attempt, we first evaluated if any differences in the plasma EBV DNA end motif profiles existed between patients with an established diagnosis of NPC and non-NPC subjects as an exploratory analysis. Therefore, we retrieved the plasma EBV DNA sequencing data from a previous, non-overlapping cohort, which included 31 NPC samples and 63 non-NPC samples. The 2-mer end motifs of plasma EBV DNA for all the NPC and non-NPC samples were analyzed and the relative proportion of each end motif among all the 16 combinations were deduced. There were 8 end motifs (TT, AT, GT, TC, CT, TG, AA, and TA) which showed higher median proportions among the NPC samples in this exploratory cohort (grouped as ‘NPC-enriched end motifs’). In contrast, 2 end motifs (CC and GG) yielded lower median proportions among the NPC samples (grouped as ‘NPC-depleted end motifs’). We proposed a new metric, namely NPC-associated EBV DNA end motif score, which was defined as the relative ratio of the proportion of NPC-enriched end motifs to the proportion of NPC-depleted end motifs in plasma EBV DNA. In the current cohort, those subjects with NPC recurrence were found to have a significantly higher NPC-associated EBV DNA end motif score than non-recurrence patients. To summarize, plasma EBV DNA from the patients with NPC recurrence exhibited distinct molecular characteristics, including quantity, size profile and end motif, from those without recurrence. For the newly reported molecular feature of plasma EBV DNA end motifs that were associated with NPC, these findings were included in the manuscript currently under review in Cancer Cell (Section 8, item 1). Objective 2: To develop a sequencing-based plasma Epstein-Barr virus DNA assay with improved diagnostic performance for surveillance of recurrence of nasopharyngeal cancer With the above-mentioned findings, we evaluated the diagnostic performance of sequencing-based quantification and size profiling for differentiating recurrence and non-recurrence samples with the receiver operating characteristics (ROC) analysis. We have also performed qPCR-based detection of plasma EBV DNA for all the samples. Targeted sequencing-based quantification of plasma EBV DNA achieved an area-under-the-curve (AUC) value of 0.88, and incorporating the size analysis further enhanced the AUC value to 0.92. Remarkably the performance of this sequencing-based plasma EBV DNA analysis was superior to the PCR-based detection of plasma EBV DNA, with a corresponding AUC value of 0.73 for the same cohort. These findings have also been reported in the manuscript currently under review (Section 8, item 1). In addition, we have demonstrated the clinical value of serial monitoring of plasma EBV DNA with the proposed sequencing-based assay. We have analysed the serial samples collected at 6-week and 6-month post-radiotherapy of 90 NPC patients in the NPC 0502 trial. Based on the quantitative level of plasma EBV DNA defined by sequencing in the 6-week samples (i.e. proportion of plasma EBV DNA), these 90 patients were categorized into 4 groups, i.e. <0.1% (n=24), 0.1 – 1% (n=36), 1 – 10% (n=23) and >10% (n=7). In each subgroup, we evaluated and compared the progression-free survival of these patients who had an increase versus those with a decrease in the proportion of plasma EBV DNA in the subsequent post-radiotherapy 6-month sample. Of note, in the subgroups of patients with 0.1 – 1% and 1-10%, those who had a decrease in the proportion of plasma EBV DNA at 6 months post-radiotherapy enjoyed a better progression-free survival than those who had an increase. All these findings suggested the clinical utility of the proposed sequencing-based plasma EBV DNA analysis for monitoring of recurrence in NPC patients.

24115421.label: Major findings and research outcome
24115421.value: In this Project, the differentiating molecular features of plasma EBV DNA between patients with NPC recurrence and those without recurrence were revealed, including quantitation, size and end motif. NPC patients with recurrence had higher quantitative level of plasma EBV DNA as measured by targeted sequencing compared to the non-recurrence group. In addition, plasma EBV DNA from patients with recurrence was shown to exhibit a mononucleosomal size pattern, which was absent in the non-recurrence group. In addition, we have discovered that the end motif of plasma EBV DNA, as another fragmentomics biomarker, was informative of the NPC status. In an exploratory analysis, we have demonstrated the difference in the plasma EBV DNA end motif profile between patients with an established diagnosis of NPC and non-NPC subjects. There were end motifs that were preferentially enriched (as ‘NPC-enriched end motifs’) and depleted (as ‘NPC-depleted end motifs) among NPC patients compared to non-NPC subjects in the exploratory cohort. Based on the discovery of these differentiating molecular features, we have developed a targeted sequencing-based assay for differentiating recurrence and non-recurrence samples. The sequencing-based analysis (incorporating quantitation and size analysis) of plasma EBV DNA yielded a superior diagnostic performance for recurrence detection compared to quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR). These findings were reported in the manuscript currently under review in Cancer Cell (Section 8, item 1). In addition, we have demonstrated the clinical value of serial monitoring of plasma EBV DNA with the proposed sequencing-based assay through analysis of the archived samples from the prospective NPC 0502 cohort. The subgroups of patients who had a drop in the quantitative level of plasma EBV DNA as defined by sequencing enjoyed a more favourable prognosis. This thus provided the proof-of-concept for adopting the proposed sequencing-based assay for monitoring of NPC recurrence. We have also filed patent applications on the sequencing-based methodology for NPC surveillance (Section 10, item 1). The findings have also been presented in the conferences as listed in Section 9.

24115421.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24115421.value: The differentiating molecular features of plasma EBV DNA between the recurrence and non-recurrence groups revealed through this study contributed to the superior diagnostic performance of the proposed sequencing-based analysis compared to PCR. In future studies, the dynamics of these various molecular features of plasma EBV DNA in the post-treatment period could be explored to enhance the clinical utility. This would further provide the basis for designing biomarker-driven studies by sequencing-based plasma EBV DNA analysis to guide adjuvant treatment (escalation or de-escalation). The superior diagnostic performance of the sequencing-based analysis of plasma EBV DNA for detection of NPC recurrence suggests its potential utility for surveillance of other EBV-associated malignancies. In EBV-associated lymphoma, though the quantitative level of plasma EBV DNA by PCR could inform the prognosis, its clinical utility for surveillance of recurrence was also limited by the low sensitivity and specificity. We could similarly evaluate and compare these molecular features of plasma EBV DNA in lymphoma patients with and without recurrence. Such analysis would potentially extend the application of sequencing-based plasma EBV DNA to patients with the virus-associated lymphoma.

24115421.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24115421.value: Circulating Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) DNA in blood plasma is a well-established biomarker of nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC). However, its clinical utility for detection of NPC recurrence has been limited by the low diagnostic performance with the conventional testing methodology. Through this research project, the differentiating molecular features of plasma EBV DNA from patients with NPC recurrence, including quantitation, size and ends, were revealed. Such discovery was translated into the development of a next generation sequencing-based assay of plasma EBV DNA analysis, which was shown to be more accurate for detection of NPC recurrence compared to the conventional polymerase chain reaction (PCR)-based detection. This proposed sequencing-based assay would have the potential to be incorporated into the NPC surveillance protocol and facilitate early detection of recurrence. This would potentially bring about treatment options of curative intent, instead of palliative nature, if the recurrence is identified early enough.

24118521.value: INTRODUCTION Acute pancreatitis is one of the most common gastrointestinal diseases requiring emergency admissions to the hospital. 10-20% of these patients develop pancreatic necrosis and subsequent walled-off pancreatic necrosis (WON) and is associated with a mortality of 20-30%. Grade 1A evidence exists to support an initial minimally invasive drainage approach to infected WON. However, the optimal approach and timing of necrosectomy remains unaddressed. The current suggested approach in international guidelines is the endoscopic step-up approach. However, recent evidence from large national cohorts support the use of direct endoscopic necrosectomy (DEN) at the time of stent placement, resulting in earlier resolution of WON and less number of necrosectomies. OBJECTIVE This study aims to investigate the clinical outcomes of the DEN versus the step-up approach for necrosectomy after endoscopic drainage of WON. HYPOTHESIS The hypothesis is that DEN at the time of LAMS placement improves clinical outcomes after endoscopic drainage of WON as compared to the endoscopic step-up approach. DESIGN AND SUBJECTS This is a multicentre international randomized controlled trial. Patients with suspected or confirmed infected or symptomatic WON on computed tomography (CT) and who are deemed feasible for endoscopic drainage will be included in the study. Endoscopic drainage with lumen-apposing metal stents (LAMS) will be performed. Patients will be randomised to either the endoscopic step-up approach or direct endoscopic necrosectomy (DEN) approach. The primary endpoint is a composite of major complications or death within 6 months after randomisation. Secondary endpoints include time to resolution of WON, pancreatic functions, biliary strictures, need for necrosectomy, total number of interventions, length of hospital and ICU stay, recurrence of WON and unplanned readmissions related to WON. We assumed a reduction in cumulative primary endpoint with the DEN approach by 22.4% (32.2% to 9.8%) in comparison to endoscopic step-up approach. With a 2-sided significance level of 5% and power of 80%, taking into account a 5% drop-out rate, a total of 108 patients was required to demonstrate this effect. Study collaboration has been established with four other international centres. A estimation of 3 years is required to complete study recruitment.

24200521.label: Project Title(Chinese)
24200521.value: 可光調控的印刷憶阻器

24200521.label: Project Objectives
24200521.value: Inkjet printing of flexible memristors from solution-processed inorganic-organic halide perovskites, targeting a switching voltage of <1 V, a switching speed of <0.1s, widespread programmable resistance states with a switching ratio of >10^3, and an ultralow-power consumption with standby power of <10^-6 W. Establishing an understanding of the underlying switching mechanism of the printed memristors, more specifically: 1) how the charged species such as the halide ions and vacancies migrate and redistribute in the printed perovskite layer to induce the switching, and 2) how the work function of the electrodes impacts charge injection/ejection and thus, the switching. Validating the capability of the printed memristors to emulate the biological synapses, and achieving the essential artificial synaptic functions, including the spike-timing-dependent plasticity and the spiking-rate-dependent plasticity. 24200521.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24200521.value: Memristors are resistive switching devices capable of storing and processing data in high efficiency. In a recent collaboration, we have demonstrated printing of flexible memristors from solution-processed molybdenum disulfide (MoS2). The devices exhibited high-performance switching and allowed emulation of the biological synapses, offering an exciting prospect for neuromorphic engineering development. Limited by the properties of the solution-processed MoS2, in this project, we propose to adopt this method to inkjet-printing of perovskites to realise light-mediated memristors. Perovskites are promising switching materials. Their charged species such as halide ions and vacancies are ready to migrate and redistribute under bias to induce the switching, while their efficient photoresponse can potentially impact this process for switching modulation. We will first adapt inorganic-organic halide perovskites to inkjet printing to fabricate memristors. We will study the switching characteristics and the corresponding chemical element distribution in the printed perovskite layer to establish an understanding of the underlying switching mechanism, more specifically, how the migration and redistribution of the charged species, as well as the work function of the electrodes, define the switching. This understanding will shed light on materials and device engineering for memristor optimisation. Then, we will investigate synapse emulation from the optimised memristors, aiming to achieve the essential artificial synaptic functions, including the spike-timing-dependent plasticity and spiking-rate-dependent plasticity. After successful emulation, we will explore light illumination for memristor modulation. We aim to achieve wavelength-dependent modulation of the switching and synaptic functions and on this basis, light-mediated synaptic logic gates. We believe our project, in a long-term, will be impactful for widespread flexible neuromorphic technology development from biomimetic sensors and prosthetic visual systems to microprocessors and brain-computer interfaces, and even brain chips. 憶阻器是一類能高效地進行數據運算及存儲的電阻式開關器件。在最近的一項合作中，我們實現了基於液相剝離二硫化鉬的柔性印刷憶阻器。該憶阻器實現了高性能的開關，並模擬了生物突觸功能，展示了它在神經形態計算應用中的前景。受限於液相剝離二硫化鉬的材料性質，在此項目中，我們提出沿用該印刷憶阻器的製備方法於鈣鈦礦材料中，以噴墨印刷實現可光可調的憶阻器。 鈣鈦礦是一類具有前景的憶阻器開關材料：鈣鈦礦的導電物質例如鹵化物離子和空穴在偏壓下能進行遷移及重新分佈來切換材料的電阻率，而它們高效的光響應可能進一步調控該電阻率的切換。首先，我們將噴墨印刷無機/有機鹵化物鈣鈦礦來製備憶阻器器件。我們將研究器件的開關特性和相應的鈣鈦礦印刷層中化學元素的分佈，以了解器件開關的潛在機制。更具體地說，這包括鈣鈦礦導電物質的遷移和重新分佈，以及器件導電電極功函數的影響。這種理解將反饋於材料和器件結構的調控和優化。然後，我們將研究憶阻器的生物突觸仿生功能，旨在實現基本的突觸功能，比如不同尖峰時長和頻率下的電阻可塑性。在此基礎上，我們將研究憶阻器的光調控功能。我們希望實現不同波長下的光調控機制，並在此基礎上實現可光可調的邏輯門單元。從長遠來看，我們相信該項目將裨益於從仿生傳感器和視覺系統到微處理器和腦機接口甚至腦芯片等多種神經形態計算的研究和開發。

24205021.label: Project Title(Chinese)
24205021.value: 重新想像X.509公開金鑰基礎架構之設計

24205021.label: Project Objectives
24205021.value: To improve the overall quality of implementations and applications of the public key infrastructure (PKI), by pruning away or redesigning complex but rarely used features in the existing design of X.509, and investigating formats and encoding algorithms that are more effective and can facilitate the development of robust implementations of parsers, decoders and the certificate validation logic. The central premise of this is that by reducing the complexity of a widely used and security-critical design, it is possible to achieve greater assurance of correctness in different aspects including implementation, configuration and management. The success of this project can also demonstrate to the wider protocol design/standardization community the importance of keeping things simple and taking implementation trade-offs into consideration. To identify features of X.509 that are particularly tricky to implement or seldom used in practice, by evaluating both existing data sets of X.509 certificates as well as software implementations that are in charge of processing and validating X.509 certificate chains. Examples of theoretical designs that make sense on pen and paper but failed to gain momentum in achieving the intended properties can help illustrate the gap between theory and practice, and shed light on what needs to be removed or simplified in the context of a functioning PKI. To investigate the level of support with respect to the lesser-used features of X.509 being implemented in common certificate-using systems, by designing a practical testing and analysis framework that can be applied on different system implementations and configurations. This could potentially lead to the discovery of new interoperability issues, which could in turn be leveraged to guide the design simplification effort and improve the overall robustness of software implementations of the PKI. To investigate the possibility of making the encoding format of certificates more effective in representing identities and also easier to parse and decode for specific application scenarios, such that existing tools including parser generators and theorem provers can be used to deliver implementations of certificate parser and decoder that have higher levels of correctness assurance. Additionally, investigate how such tools can be used to exploit the reduced complexity of the PKI to also deliver implementations of the certificate validation logic with a high degree of assurance. To provide hands-on training for research students to evaluate the design and specification of a security-critical infrastructure, as well as opportunities to test concrete software implementations for security and interoperability issues. These skills are valuable for becoming a successful security researcher who might one day get involved in the specification and standardization of system designs. The results of this project can also educate the wider application developer community on the subtle standard compliance and interoperability pitfalls that they might need to be aware of when they make use of the X.509 PKI.

24205021.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24205021.value: As consumers are becoming increasingly aware of the needs to protect the confidentiality and integrity of their data, the use of cryptography prevailed in the last decade. One fundamental challenge in networked systems is how to cryptographically verify the identity of the communication peer, which is often solved by using a Public Key Infrastructures (PKI). Among the handful of historic proposals, the X.509 PKI emerged as the dominant choice, as evidenced by its adoption in TLS, one of the most widely used network security protocol, and other application scenarios including code signing and electronic mails. Popularity, however, does not always imply robustness. Over the years, researchers identified various implementation, deployment and management issues surrounding the X.509 PKI. The central premise of this project is that while X.509 is designed to be flexible, the complexity of its design has become an obstacle towards achieving security, and many applications today would benefit from a more optimized design. Examples of the harms of complexity are abundant in the context of X.509. For instance, certificates can contain many optional but critical extensions that need to be enforced, but some of them have proven to be tricky and uninviting for developers to implement. Another source of complexity is the directory model that X.509 inherited from early network services, where the support for numerous data types and localized strings greatly complicates the implementations, hurting both security and interoperability. Furthermore, due to the fear of potential service disruption, outright disabling certificate validation is a practice sometimes embraced by users and administrators in actual deployments. In this project, we want to revisit and rethink the design of X.509. First we will identify features that are tricky to implement or seldom used in practice, and examine whether common implementations of X.509 actually deliver full support for such features. This would help the community better understand potential interoperability issues, and provide technical justifications to why certain well-intentioned features in the original design should be simplified or removed. We will then investigate formats and encoding techniques that are more effective in representing core features of X.509 required by specific applications, while facilitate the development of robust parsers and decoders for consuming certificates. Finally, we will also investigate the possibility of exploiting the new encoding format and reduced feature set to deliver new PKI implementations with high assurance of correctness backed by code generators and theorem provers. 隨着消費者越加注意保護數據私隱及完整性，密碼學的應用在過去十年間非常盛行。網絡系統中的一項基本挑戰是如何使用密碼學手段來認證通信雙方的身份，而此問題經常通過利用公開金鑰基礎架構來解決。傳輸層安全協定(TLS)作為其中一個最為被廣泛使用的網絡安全協定，經常採用X.509來解決身份認證的問題。其他對安全保護較為敏感的應用場景，例如代碼簽章和加密電郵，亦經常依賴X.509為其安全性能提供基礎。不同系統與協定的一致採用使得X.509成為歷史上最為成功和重要的一個公鑰基礎架構提案。 遺憾地，X.509的廣泛部署並不代表它是一個安全耐用的架構。過去數年間，不同的研究分別在X.509的管理、部署設置及代碼實現中發現了威脅安全性的多種問題。基於這些觀察發現，這個研究項目的中心假設如下：X.509設計中的技術細節十分具有彈性，但隨之而來的複雜度反而成為了實現安全保證的絆腳石。因此，一個更為優化的設計能夠為很多不同的應用帶來好處。 在使用X.509的環境中，其複雜性引致損害的例子比比皆是。最簡單的例子包括X.509數碼證書上非必要但對保障安全性至關重要的各項擴充。這些擴充需要代碼配套來貫徹執行設計中的原意，但很多擴充由於太過複雜，不少開發人員在編寫代碼的過程中犯錯甚至索性放棄部分功能，導致這些擴充反而成為安全漏洞及兼容性問題的來源。另一個X.509甚為複雜的原因是因為它繼承了早期網絡協定中常用的目錄概念，而其中牽涉到的各種數據類型和字串編碼往往需要十分繁瑣的代碼來實現，於是進一步引發更多安全及兼容性問題。由於害怕對所需的應用或服務造成滋擾及麻煩，一些用家和服務管理人員甚至直接忽略並停用相關系統中對X.509數碼證書的檢查及認證，繼而完全放棄X.509本身應提供的安全保障。 在這個研究項目中，我們希望進一步探討並重新想像X.509的設計。首先，我們會識別出X.509中一些不常用或者難以實現的功能，並考查一些較為普遍的系統是否有正確實現並使用這些功能。這能夠幫助研究及開發社群進一步認清潛在的安全及兼容性問題，並提供技術性的理由去解釋為何一些本意良好的設計應該在協定標準中被簡化甚至移除。我們亦會研究哪些格式及編碼手法能夠更為有效地為X.509數碼證書的核心功能提供支持，並由此開發更為穩定可靠的語法剖析器及解碼器。最後我們會尋求使用代碼生成技術及定理證明來配合簡化過的X.509設計及新的編碼格式，從而為檢查及認證X.509數碼證書這一關鍵任務提供更高的正確性保證。

24205621.label: Project Title(Chinese)
24205621.value: 信息論中的有限塊長度編碼方法

24205621.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24205621.value: Channel coding, a central problem in information theory, concerns the setting where the encoder transmits a message to the decoder through a noisy channel. The key performance metrics are the rate (the number of message bits transmitted per channel use), the error probability (probability that the decoder fails to recover the message), and the blocklength (the number of channel uses needed). The blocklength is crucial to practical applications since it directly affects the time delay needed. For example, real time communications (e.g. voice transmission and teleconferencing) require a low latency. The prevalence of connected devices (e.g. Internet of things) also increases the need for technologies supporting the transmission of short messages with negligible delay. The goal of this project is to investigate the fundamental limits of communication settings in information theory where the blocklength (or delay) is bounded, and to develop efficient implementations of schemes with performance close to the fundamental limits. Shannon’s channel coding theorem, a classical result in information theory, is inapplicable since it requires the blocklength to tend to infinity. While finite blocklength schemes for the original channel coding setting have been widely studied, the cases for more complex channel models (e.g. channels with state and/or feedback, broadcast channels, interference channels) are less well-understood. By studying the trade-off between delay and transmission rate of these channel models, and designing efficient coding schemes, we aim at providing solutions to various challenges in modern communication tasks, which not only have adequate practical performance, but are also supported by theoretical guarantees. 信道編碼是信息論的中心問題。在此問題當中，發送端向接收端透過有噪信道傳送信息。此問題的主要考量是信息傳輸的速率（即每次使用信道所傳送的位元數量），錯誤機率（接收端無法解讀信息的機率），以及塊長度（需要的信道使用次數）。在實際應用當中，塊長度是重要的考量，因爲它直接影響了信息傳輸的延遲。舉例來說，實時通訊（譬如語音傳輸及視像會議）需要較低的延遲。可連綫裝置的普及（譬如物聯網）也增加了低延遲的短信息傳輸科技的需求。 此研究項目的目標是探討在塊長度（或延遲）受限的情況下的通訊的基本限制，以及設計能接近基本限制而高效率的編碼算法。香農的有噪信道編碼定理，信息論的經典定理，並不能在此應用，因爲它需要塊長度趨向無限。雖然在傳統信道編碼中，有限塊長度編碼已被廣泛研究，但對於更複雜的信道模型（譬如具有狀態或反饋的信道，廣播信道，干擾信道），有限塊長度編碼並未被完全瞭解。透過研究這些信道模型中延遲與傳輸速率的取捨關係，以及設計高效率的編碼算法，我們希望對各種現代的通訊挑戰給出既有實際性能，也有理論保證的方案。

24207621.label: Project Title(Chinese)
24207621.value: 基於資本利得稅的高維連續時間投資組合選擇問題

24207621.label: Project Objectives
24207621.value: We plan to propose a continuous-time portfolio selection framework with capital gains tax and time-periodicity. Under this framework, we plan to propose two models. The first one features stochastic labor income, a progressive tax system, and a time-varying capital gains tax rate. The second one includes the explicit characterization of annual tax exempt amount. We plan to study the theoretical characterization of the framework, including establishing the connection between the value function and the corresponding HJB equation based on the penalty approximation and fixed point iteration, as well as deriving theoretical properties of the optimal trading and consumption strategies. Due to the high dimensionality of the proposed models, we plan to propose and implement an efficient DNN-based procedure to obtain numerical approximations of the optimal strategies. We plan to study economic insights from the proposed models. For the first proposed model, we plan to study the dependence of investors' optimal trading and consumption strategies on the current capital gains tax rate and anticipation on the future rate. For the second proposed model, we plan to study the effects of the annual tax exempt amount on the investors' optimal strategy and gains realizations.

24207621.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24207621.value: Investors' trading decisions are affected by the financial market frictions such as transaction costs and capital gains taxes, and modeling market frictions is important for understanding investors' decisions and providing insights on the market characteristics and asset pricing. Imposed on the realized profit from selling financial assets, the capital gains tax has a cost rate that is typically much larger compared to other market frictions, and it has a first-order effect on investors' investment behavior. While modeling capital gains tax in continuous-time portfolio selection is crucial for explaining many empirical findings including the patterns of capital gains and losses realizations, it is methodologically challenging due to the high model dimensionality from the numerical perspective and the degeneracy in the singular control formulation from the theoretical perspective. In this project, we propose a high-dimensional continuous-time portfolio selection framework with capital gains tax, featuring time-periodicity as a result of the periodic taxation of aggregated capital gains and possible tax rate changes at the end of tax years. To tackle the high dimensionality, we propose a procedure based on deep neural networks to derive approximations of investors' optimal investment strategies, which is tailored to singular control with discontinuous strategies and time-periodicity. To overcome the challenge of degeneracy and periodicity in the singular control formulation, we propose a general viscosity-solution-based method combining penalty approximation with fixed point iteration to obtain theoretical characterization of the optimal strategies. Under this framework, we plan to study two high-dimensional models that embody the time-periodicity of the capital gains tax. Featuring the interaction between stochastic labor income and the progressive tax system, the first model focuses on the implications of investors' anticipation on the time-varying tax rate. The second model studies the impact of the annual capital gains tax exempt amount on the gains realization. We expect that these models can explain the empirically documented impact of time-periodicity of capital gains tax on investors' decisions and market characteristics. 投資者的交易決策受到諸如交易費或者資本利得稅的市場摩擦的影響，因此市場摩擦的建模對於理解投資者的決策、市場特徵以及資產定價至關重要。資本利得稅基於賣出資產時實現的收益徵收，它的費率往往比其他市場摩擦要大很多，並且它對投資者的交易行為有一階影響。因此，資本利得稅的建模在連續時間投資組合選擇問題中對於解釋諸如獲利或損失的實現等眾多實證現象發揮關鍵性的作用，然而它在技術上充滿挑戰：從數值方法角度看，問題的維數高；從數學理論角度看，在奇異控制的框架下存在退化性。 本項目提出一個基於資本利得稅的高維連續時間投資組合選擇框架。由於年末資本利得累計計稅以及潛在的稅率變化，該框架包含時間週期性。為了克服問題中的高維數，本項目提出針對奇異控制、非連續策略、時間週期性的基於深度神經網絡的數值算法，並以此方法得到投資者最優投資策略的估計。為了克服奇異控制問題的退化性以及處理時間週期性，結合懲罰估計以及不動點迭代，本項目提出一般化的基於粘性解的理論刻畫方法。在此框架下，本項目計劃研究體現資本利得稅時間週期性的兩個高維模型。模型一結合了隨機收入和累進稅率系統來探索投資者對未來稅率變化預期的金融意義。模型二研究年度資本利得稅免稅額對利得實現帶來的衝擊。我們預期這兩個模型可用作解釋實證研究中發現的資本利得稅時間週期性造成的對投資者交易策略以及市場特徵的影響。

24207621.label: Realisation of objectives
24207621.value: The PI has realized Objective 1. The PI has proposed a continuous-time portfolio selection framework with capital gains taxes, featuring time-periodicity arising from various practical features of capital gains taxes. In Research Output 8 Item 1, a portfolio selection model incorporating the year-end taxation rule is proposed, where capital gains and losses are accumulated throughout the year, but the taxes are calculated and paid on a yearly basis. This creates time-periodicity with each tax year as a period. This model is also flexible to incorporate features such as transaction costs and tax step-up treatment. In Research Output 8 Item 4, a portfolio selection model with a time-varying capital gains tax rate is proposed and studied, in which the tax rate varies across periods throughout the years, which covers tax rate changes not only due to the tax policy changes but also the investor's shifts between tax brackets due to the change in labor income under a progressive tax system. When the next tax period is sufficiently near, the investor has the knowledge about the tax rate effective for the next tax period; when the next tax period is still far away, the investor can also have an anticipation of the next tax rate. Research Output 8 Item 4 studies the optimal tax timing under a time-varying tax rate, including both these scenarios as the pre-implementation and pre-announcement periods. Research Output 8 Item 6 presents a portfolio selection model under capital gains taxes with an annual tax exempt amount and explores its impact on the optimal tax-timing strategies of investors with different wealth levels. The PI has realized Objective 2. In Research Output 8 Items 1 and 4, the portfolio selection models are formulated as singular stochastic control problems and studied through dynamic programming. The corresponding HJB equation is derived, and the value function is characterized as viscosity solution of the HJB equation through a fixed-point argument based on the penalty approximation. The PI has studied the time-homogeneity of the models, as well as the structure of the optimal strategy based on the HJB equation and its behavior near the end of periods. Furthermore, a similar fixed-point argument is also demonstrated to be effective in Research Output 8 Item 2 for partial differential equations with periodic structures arising from the valuation of periodic cash flow streams. The method developed for the capital gains tax problems with a nonconcave value function for the singular control problem is further used to establish the well-posedness of another related singular stochastic control problem involving nonconcave utility maximization, and to develop an associated algorithm based on the penalty approximation in Research Output 8 Item 3. The PI has realized Objective 3. Research Output 8 Item 6 proposes a DNN-based numerical method that uses deep learning for solving the portfolio selection under capital gains tax, which features the inclusion of an additional classification network to identify the transaction types that are essential to singular stochastic control problems. The developed method is demonstrated to be effective in obtaining the optimal portfolio strategies. The deep-learning method is applied in Research Output 8 Item 5 to study a related singular stochastic control problem on the portfolio selection under market illiquidity, to derive a numerical approximation for the high-dimensional model used as a benchmark to test the accuracy of the approximate optimal strategy based on asymptotic expansion. The PI has realized Objective 4. Based on the proposed models, we found in Research Output 8 Item 1 that under year-end taxation, the presence of even a tiny transaction cost can affect the investor's optimal tax timing and lead to significant deferral of capital losses, and such effects are robust to a zero interest rate environment or a tax step-up treatment. We found in Research Output 8 Item 4 that the investor's anticipation of the future tax rate leads to a transitory effect that impacts the tax timing. When the tax rate for the next period is announced but not yet implemented, the investor is incentivized to deviate from the optimal strategy under the current rate and account for the new rate, especially when the announcement time is imminent. When the new rate is not yet known, the investor who is uncertain about the direction of future tax rate changes will adopt a strategy that prepares for all potential directions of future tax rate changes. In Research Output 8 Item 6, we found that the relative magnitude of tax exempt amount compared to the investor's wealth significantly affects the tax timing strategy, and that a relatively large exempt amount encourages the investor to realize even large capital gains.

24207621.label: Major findings and research outcome
24207621.value: There are several research outcomes from the project. Research Output 8 Item 1 is accepted by Management Science, a flagship journal in Financial Engineering. The paper proposes a portfolio selection model with capital gains tax featuring year-end taxation, showing that even small transaction costs can have large impacts on investors' tax-timing strategy, encouraging them to defer significant capital losses. Research Output 8 Item 4 is submitted and received a Major Revision from Management Science, where we propose a portfolio selection model with a time-varying tax rate and find that the investor's anticipation of the uncertain future rate has profound impacts on the current tax-timing strategy. Research Output 8 Item 6 is in preparation for submission to a top journal in Financial Engineering, which proposes a deep-learning method for portfolio selection problems under taxes, tailored for singular stochastic control problems. The method is demonstrated to be effective and used to study tax models with market regime switching and exempt amount. Both Items 4 and 6 will be part of theses of two PhD students supervised by the PI; see Research Output 10 Items 1 and 2. Research Output 8 Item 2 is published in Mathematical Finance, a top journal in Financial Mathematics area, where we study the design of a financial product whose payoff cash flow features time-periodicity. Using the project's theoretical methodology on periodic problems, we characterize the product value using PDEs with periodic structure and prove the existence of a unique fixed point. Research Output 8 Item 3 is accepted by SIAM Journal on Financial Mathematics, a top journal in Financial Mathematics area, which studies portfolio selection under market frictions similar to the project. We formulate the model as a singular stochastic control problem with a nonconcave objective, closely related to the problem in the project, and establish the connection between the value function and the HJB equation. Research Output 8 Item 5 is submitted and received a Minor Revision from Management Science, studying portfolio selection featuring time-varying market liquidity resembling the first model in the project. Consistent with the project's findings, the investor's anticipation of future liquidity as a market friction has significant effects on the current strategy. Also, for the singular stochastic control problem in this paper, the deep-learning method detailed in Item 5.3 of Part B is used as an effective benchmark. Three PhD students have (expected) finished their theses under the project's support.

24207621.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24207621.value: Based on the results obtained in this project, a potential research direction is to apply the DNN-based algorithm to study other high-dimensional continuous-time portfolio selection problems under market frictions and analyze the impact of practical features of the frictions on investors' strategy. Another potential follow-up research topic is to study general nonconcave singular stochastic control problems with time periodicity.

24207621.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24207621.value: Capital gains taxes are taxes levied on investors' capital gains from their financial investments. As a result, they significantly affect investors' trading decisions, especially when deciding when to sell assets to realize capital gains. However, incorporating the practical features of capital gains taxes poses challenges for modeling due to high dimensionality. This project aims to overcome these challenges and to uncover the effects of the practical features of capital gains taxes on investors' portfolio strategies. The PI found that small trading costs can incentivize investors to defer the realization of losses. Furthermore, investors will adjust their portfolio strategy under the current tax rate if they anticipate a change in the tax rate in the coming years. Results from this study provide important insights for understanding investors' trading behavior under the influence of various features of capital gains taxes.

24208921.label: Project Objectives
24208921.value: Develop a hierarchical multiscale modeling method to predict the temperature fields, degree of curing (DOC) for thermoset materials, thermo-viscoelasticity and thermo-plasticity of woven carbon fiber reinforced plastic (CFRP) parts during resin solidification, considering non-orthogonal yarn angles and non-uniform fabric structures caused by preforming. Study the thermal, chemical, viscoelastic and plastic properties of resin and fiber yarns with various temperatures and DOCs during resin solidification. For resin, the properties will be characterized experimentally. For fiber yarns, the properties will be calculated by conducting micromechanical analysis using experimental data of resin and unidirectional (UD) CFRPs, and the obtained yarn properties will be input to representative volume element (RVE) models of woven CFRPs. The RVE models will then be validated, and calibrated if essential, using experiments. Analyze stress and DOC fields of woven CFRPs, both of which depend on temperature and deformation paths, during solidification at material-level and part-level. At material-level, the analysis will be conducted via simulation of RVEs that have variations in fabric structure and yarn direction caused by preforming. At part-level, the analysis will be conducted by combining the RVE simulation with a deep learning gated recurrent unit (GRU) model. Investigate preforming effects at material-level on fabric structure, heat transfer, chemical shrinkage and mechanical stiffness of woven CFRPs after resin solidification by conducting experiments on non-orthogonal samples with uniformly distributed yarn directions. The experimental results will also be used for validation and possible calibration for the RVE models of woven CFRPs. Establish a modeling method of CFRP performance integrated with thermoforming so that yarn angles, geometry and compression stiffness of parts with various DOCs can be predicted. Prediction accuracy of the integrated modeling method will be validated by experiments using 2x2 twill and 5-harness satin weave thermoset CFRPs with single-dome and tetrahedron benchmark part geometries.

24208921.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24208921.value: The goal of this proposal is to experimentally investigate and numerically predict preforming effects on resin solidification of woven carbon fiber reinforced plastics (CFRPs). To achieve this goal, we will establish (1) a novel multiscale modeling approach for resin solidification of preformed CFRPs, and (2) an innovative modeling method of CFRP performance integrated with thermoforming effects, such that both the solidification process and its end-product performance can be analyzed coherently. CFRPs are light-weight, high-strength materials that can bring great economic and environmental benefits. One of the most promising techniques for mass-production of woven CFRP parts is thermoforming, which includes preforming followed by resin solidification. Due to the ample design freedom in thermoforming process, compounded with the complexity of composite materials, effective and efficient numerical simulations are highly desirable. Previous works on thermoforming modeling have mostly been centered on preforming. However, for resin solidification, existing numerical modeling methods do not consider the preforming effects, including the variations in yarn angle and fabric structure, although our preliminary study has shown that such variations can cause over 70% difference in residual stress after solidification. The major challenge to include the preforming effects in modeling resin solidification is considering yarn angle, fabric structure, temperature path and deformation path in simulating response of woven CFRPs. To tackle this challenge, a multiscale modeling method stemmed from the PI’s previous work is proposed. The proposed method concentrates on heat transfer, chemical reaction, viscoelasticity and plasticity of CFRP parts that have been preformed and compacted. Novelty of the proposed approach lies in (1) the identification of temperature and deformation response of CFRPs using the representative volume element (RVE) simulations and deep learning; (2) the reconstruction of RVEs via simulation of preforming and compaction; (3) the integration of preforming and solidification effects into the performance analysis of final parts; (4) the development of the fabrication technique that can produce resin and CFRP samples with various solidification status; and (5) the characterization of properties of fiber yarns that are difficult to be extracted from CFRPs and made into samples small enough for certain standard experiments. Upon completion, the proposed method can replace expensive thermoforming experiments for efficient process optimization and analyze mesoscopic material behaviors given part-level conditions, assisting flexible design of CFRPs based on process and performance requirements. These benefits will alleviate the technical obstacles in implementing CFRPs in large-scale production of lightweight vehicles, reducing greenhouse gas emission and increasing sustainability of global ecosystem. 本項目的目標是通過試驗研究以及數值模擬預測預成型過程對編織碳纖維增强塑料預浸料樹脂固化過程的影響。為完成該目標，本項目將建立（1）一種原創的針對預成型后預浸料樹脂固化的多尺度模擬方法，以及（2）一種創新的將熱成型製造過程的影響結合在最終產品性能預測中的模擬方法，從而能夠同時分析樹脂固化過程及其產物的機械性能。 由於其輕量化，高强度的特點，碳纖維增强塑料能夠帶來巨大的經濟和環境效益。最有潛力大規模生產編織碳纖維增强塑料零件的技術之一即是包括預成型及其後的樹脂固化兩個步驟的熱成型工藝。由於熱成型工藝涉及大量參數，而且複合材料本身也具有較複雜的内部結構及成分，因此對此過程的分析和優化亟需高效率高精度的數值模擬方法。過去對於熱成型模擬的工作主要集中在對預成型的分析，然而對於樹脂固化，目前已有的數值模擬方法并未考慮纖維角度及纖維内部結構由於預成型產生變化的影響。根據目前已完成的初步分析，這些由於預成型導致的變化會給固化後材料内殘餘應力帶來超過70%的不同。 將預成型的影響集成在固化模擬中的主要挑戰在於如何把纖維角度，纖維結構，固化溫度曲綫以及變形曲綫同時考慮到編織碳纖維增强塑料的力學響應模擬中。爲了解決該問題，該項目將會依托項目申請人過去的經驗，開發出一種多尺度的模擬方法。該方法的主要關注對於已經預成型及壓縮後的碳纖維增强塑料在固化時熱傳導，化學反應，粘彈性，以及塑性的模擬。該模擬方法的主要創新點集中在（1）使用代表躰元有限元模擬結合深度學習完成材料溫度及變形響應的辨識；（2）通過預成型及壓縮模擬重構代表躰元内部結構；（3）將預成型及固化的影響結合至最終產品的性能分析中；（4）開發出能夠製造具有不同固化狀態的樹脂及碳纖維增强塑料樣品的方法；以及（5）表徵難以從碳纖維增强塑料中抽取的纖維束的性能，并且製造足夠小的纖維束樣品以滿足標準實驗測試的要求。 完成之後，本項目提出的模擬方法將能夠取代昂貴的熱成型實驗，有效進行製造過程優化，并且在介觀尺度分析製造過程給材料帶來的影響，從而能夠依據工藝及性能要求對碳纖維增强塑料進行可高度定制化的設計。這些益處能夠幫助掃清相關技術障礙，促進碳纖維增强塑料在大規模生產的交通工具中的應用，從而降低溫室氣體的排放，保障全球生態環境的可持續發展。

24208921.label: Realisation of objectives
24208921.value: For Objective #1: The multiscale modeling method has already been developed and it can effectively consider the chemical-thermal-mechanical coupled response of the preformed composite during curing with less than 6.7% of error. For Objective #2: Experimental approaches, such as the standard and bespoke non-contact ones, have been established to systematically characterize chemical-thermal-mechanical properties of the prepreg resin under various conditions. Curing properties of the yarns have been correctly determined via experiments and micromechanics in the Laplace domain, leading to modeling error of less than 6.4%. The yarn and resin properties have been utilized to build the woven RVE models, resulting in modeling error of less than 5.0% after calibration of the yarn-to-yarn and yarn-to-matrix interaction under specific curing conditions. For Objective #3: combining the RVE simulation with a deep learning gated recurrent unit (GRU) model. Multiscale modeling for curing of the preformed woven CFRPs have been achieved through combination of the finite element analysis and long-short term memory model, resulting in modeling error of less than 6.7% for viscoelastic stress-strain response of the preformed CFRP parts under various curing conditions. For Objective #4: Chemical, thermal and viscoelastic properties of the prepreg samples deformed to various yarn angles via the picture-frame fixture have been measured via both standard and bespoke experiments under different curing degrees and curing temperatures. The results have been utilized for modeling validation and some calibration. For Objective #5: Capability of the preforming-curing-performance integrated modeling method has been validated through process and performance experiments of the selected thermoset CFRPs with the benchmark 3D part geometries.

At material-level, the analysis will be conducted via simulation of RVEs that have variations in fabric structure and yarn direction caused by preforming. At part-level, the analysis will be conducted by combining the RVE simulation with a deep learning gated recurrent unit (GRU) model.

Investigate preforming effects at material-level on fabric structure, heat transfer, chemical shrinkage and mechanical stiffness of woven CFRPs after resin solidification by conducting experiments on non-orthogonal samples with uniformly distributed yarn directions. The experimental results will also be used for validation and possible calibration for the RVE models of woven CFRPs.

Establish a modeling method of CFRP performance integrated with thermoforming so that yarn angles, geometry and compression stiffness of parts with various DOCs can be predicted. Prediction accuracy of the integrated modeling method will be validated by experiments using 2x2 twill and 5-harness satin weave thermoset CFRPs with single-dome and tetrahedron benchmark part geometries.

24208921.label: Major findings and research outcome
24208921.value: Outcome 1 To bridge the gap that most standard characterization methods for resin and composites focus on properties of the completely cured materials, a set of testing methods were developed systematically for the materials being cured. For specimen preparation to test characteristics depending on degrees of curing (DOCs), partially cured materials with various DOCs were produced for, according to curing kinetics of the materials. In addition, a novel non-contact method was established to measure thermal expansion and chemical shrinkage of the being-cured resin and prepregs with excessive creep (J. Manuf. Sci. Eng., 2022). Outcome 2 Using Laplace transform, constitutive law of the partially cured UD composites could be derived from the resins’ viscoelastic properties and carbon fibers’ elastic properties in the Carson domain and then transformed back to the time domain, bypassing complex dynamic mechanical analysis for the composites (Composites Science and Technology, 2022). Next, the constitutive law was implemented into the finite element analysis (FEA) for curing through further integration with the DOC- and temperature-independent chemical and thermal properties of the composites. Validation experiments confirmed the model's predictive capability, demonstrating ≤8.9% deviation in curing-induced deformation (CID) for UD composite parts under various curing conditions. Outcome 3 The LSTM models were developed to achieve fast prediction of CID for the composite laminates. The LSTM models were trained on datasets generated from the multi-field FEA curing simulation with corresponding weaving patterns and length-scales. Combination of the LSTM model for UD composite curing with a genetic algorithm enabled over 99.9% faster optimization for laminate stacking sequences versus the conventional FEA (Composites Part A, 2024). Moreover, the LSTM model for mesoscopic representative volume elements (RVEs) of woven composites effectively alleviated the computational cost challenge for high-fidelity multiscale curing simulation (Composites Part A, 2024). Outcome 4 The multiscale LSTM-FEA framework was established to capture relaxation stiffness of the preformed woven composites during curing. The relaxation stiffness is highly sensitive to preforming and curing conditions, such as yarn angles, DOCs and temperatures. RVE models considering these conditions were generated through innovative geometric modeling and yarn constitutive law calibration (Composites Part A, 2023), and then utilized to train the LSTM model for the relaxation stiffness. Afterwards, the LSTM-predicted stiffness was implemented into FEA via user-defined subroutines, achieving average error of 6.62% in stress-strain prediction for composite samples under non-uniform yarn angles from preforming and various curing conditions (Composites Part A, 2024).

24208921.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24208921.value: The material characterization methods from Outcome 1 and micromechanics in the Laplace domain from Outcome 2 will help establish a robust platform for investigating next-generation aircraft-grade composites with specially design constituents, particularly for material systems where direct experimental characterization of modified resin matrices, such as those with excessive viscosity, remains impractical. Future research will also extend AI applications in finite element analysis (FEA) modeling to industrial-scale components with non-uniform curing conditions and nonlinear multi-field coupling. Existing practices typically employ AI networks in Python/MATLAB to predict viscoelastic response at discrete material points or specific time increment. When modeling evolving material properties during curing, however, data transfer between the AI network and FEA solvers creates computational inefficiency due to limited cross-environment scalability. To address this limitation, the LSTM model from Outcome 4 will be transfer into Fortran and can directly become one part of the user-defined subroutines for the FEA software. This integration enables the FEA software to directly provide temperature, DOC, yarn angle, time, etc. at each integration point and time step to the LSTM, which can then return corresponding stiffness components for stress updates in the same environment - achieving seamless cross-scale and concurrent computation.

24208921.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24208921.value: Current production for lightweight carbon fiber reinforced polymer (CFRP) composite parts remains limited by costly trial-and-error approaches to design the crucial resin curing stage, where unwanted curing-induced-deformation (CID) occur. This project tackles the manufacturing challenge for curing of the CFRP parts mainly from 3 points: • For thermoset resins under curing conditions, a system of characterization methods was developed to reliably measure their chemical-thermal-mechanical coupled properties for CID modeling. • Using Laplace transform, viscoelasticity of thermoset resins and their composites can be efficiently converted in Carson domain based on micromechanics, ensuring simple and convenient measurement for DOC- and temperature-dependent mechanical response of the materials during curing. • Combining the FEA-driven virtual testing with artificial intelligence algorithms to digitally predict CID of the composites at multiple length-scales, particularly addressing how material deformation during preforming affects post-curing part quality. Commercially, the research outcomes can efficiently eliminate time-consuming experimental trials by enabling manufacturers to numerically optimize design before actual production. Some specialized equipment and tooling during establishment for the CFRP manufacturing can be replaced by accessible software. Environmentally, this research could assist large-volume production and application of lightweight CFRP parts in transportation vehicles, greatly reducing their greenhouse gas emission and carbon footprint.
