24209021.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24209021.value: Enabling collaborative dual-arm mobile manipulation robot to work in a potential hostile and hazardous environment is a demanding application field, especially for the inspection and inspection and maintenance applications. TELE-LEARN aims to develop a new paradigm in assistive teleoperation, with tight coupling between the mechatronic (sensing and actuation) and cognitive (learning and adaptation) parts of the system. Teleoperation will be treated as a human-robot collaboration problem in which robots and users work in concert, with distinct or overlapping roles. The fusion of the human and robot sources of information (for both control and perception) will be achieved in a modular manner. The proposed toolkit will combine different shared control and shared perception components, where the combination is formalized mathematically as a product of experts by considering variation and uncertainty information. This approach will allow an efficient fusion of teleoperation commands with a modular exploitation of multiple adaptive control and perception techniques. TELE-LEARN will facilitate the teleoperation of robots, allowing the coordination of virtual and human operators, whose different roles include motion operators (shared control) and perception operators (shared perception) when robot is interacting with the environment or even human beings. To address these issues, we propose a modular teleoperation toolkit to reduce operator workload and enhance operator and system performance by: • Increasing the collaboration between teleoperators and teleoperated system, instead of giving full control autonomy to either of the two. This can, for example, release the teleoperator from reasoning about lowlevel obstacle avoidance and robot configuration problems. • Extending collaboration to perception with (potentially multiple) assistive perception experts using augmented virtuality to reduce the requirement for the main teleoperator to interpret raw perception data. • Enabling the robot to provide assistance on specific task aspects and objectives through rich behaviors like exploitation of movement options and variations, redundancy resolution and impedance (e.g. stiff along some directions and compliant along those that the operator controls). • Leveraging torque-controlled, redundant mobile robots (wheeled, legged, etc.) to allow multiple solutions for a task (e.g. for obstacle avoidance, optimal push/pull actions) and exploitation of contacts (e.g. for stabilization) The proposed technology can benefit a wide range of applications in teleoperation, including inspection and maintenance, surgery, healthcare, manufacturing, agri-food. We propose to test the developed toolkit in the context of inspection and maintenance, a field of applications that requires various forms of telemanipulation, where we will consider a set of representative tasks for the validation of such technology. 雙臂協作移動機械人代替人進入危險環境中實行自主複雜作業，尤其是檢視和維護作業，是一項極有意義的應用。針對這樣的場景，本項目旨在研究一種新型的基於共享控制和共享感知的協助機械人遠程操作方法，即通過人類的遠程操作示教來教會機器人雙臂協同操作技能。為此，項目將研究並解決三個關鍵技術問題。首先，實現機械人遠程操作技術，使得機器人和人可以進行角色切換，發揮各自的優勢，實現共享控制。其次，進一步共享人類示教過程中所觀察的場景，教會機器人針對場景來實現相應操作技能學習。再次，進一步融合機械人各種基本功能專家控制器，形成綜合的頂層控制框架。該項目計劃將研究的關鍵技術應用到一台雙臂協作移動機械人並在相關場景中進行測試驗證。

24300321.label: Project Title(Chinese)
24300321.value: 行為韌力：未來的氣候挑戰將如何影響螺類的生存和覓食？

24300321.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24300321.value: Organisms display complex patterns of behaviour, which are modified by the surrounding environment. In turn, changes in organism behaviours will affect their performance and survival, ecosystem role via shifts in species interactions, and the provisioning of services to human societies. The marine environment is currently undergoing long-term global change due to human activities, with key modifications being ocean acidification and warming. Given the potential plasticity of behavioural traits, they are an important way organisms can adjust to environmental change, with initial results indicating they will be affected by ocean acidification and warming. Of particular relevance are behaviours related to: 1) organism competence, as disruptions to these will alter an organism's capacity to fill their functional role, and 2) species interactions, as these can influence the performance of both species involved. Here, I propose to quantify the effects of climate change on behaviour via mesocosm-based experiments examining the responses of an important gastropod species, Monodonta labio, to ocean acidification and warming. This gastropod is abundant on rocky shores throughout Hong Kong where it plays a key role in structuring ecosystems by feeding on biofilm species, including turf algae. In the absence of effective herbivores, ocean acidification and warming are expected to drive the expansion of algal turfs at the expense of macroalgae and corals. Initial experiments suggest short-term exposure to ocean acidification and warming can modify the competence and feeding behaviours of these gastropods, potentially altering their role in the ecosystem. Consequently, understanding if this herbivorous gastropod will continue to fill its functional role, and constrain the species it consumes under longer-term change, is of ecological significance. To test if prolonged exposure alters behaviours, first I will quantify the key competence responses of individual gastropods exposed to altered climates (i.e. retraction/extension, righting, lateralisation). I will then measure the response of behaviours associated with its key species interaction, specifically herbivory (i.e. feeding rates, movement), and whether this is affected by direct or indirect pathways. By quantifying these responses, I will be able to provide information required to refine predictions of individual competence and herbivory behaviours under future climates. Finally, I will use a meta-analysis to highlight links from behavioural changes of organisms, to changes in ecosystem services and anthropogenic socio-economic systems. By examining the interplay between environmental change, organism behaviour, and impacts on human societies, I will strengthen our understanding of the role of these organisms in the future era of global change. 物種擁有由周邊環境塑造出的豐富行為習性。因此改變物種的行為習性將會影響牠們的生存表現、物種之間的關係以及牠們提供人類社會的生態服務。由於人類的活動，現時全球的海洋生態正受到長時間的變遷，其中包括海洋溫度升溫和海洋酸度化。物種的行為特質擁有潛在的韌力以應對環境變遷。初步的結果顯示其行為將受海洋溫度升溫和酸度化所影響。被受影響的行為包括：1）生存能力（環境擾亂令物種角色出現變異）；以及 2）物種關係（雙方物種將受影響）。此研究目的是利用中型生態池實驗和單齒螺（Monodonta labio) 以量化氣候邊遷所導致的物種行為變異。單齒螺是香港石灘上常見的物種，牠們覓食藻類等生物膜維生並在生態系統上建立重要的角色。缺乏草食動物的情況下，海洋溫度升溫及酸度化將導致微藻類生長加速，從而危害其他大型藻類和珊瑚群落。初步實驗顯示短期的海洋溫度升溫及酸度化影響了螺類的生存及行為，有機會使其生態角色出現變異。因此了解草食性螺類能否達到其生態角色，以及平衡其覓食物種的數量為其重要。此研究將首先量化個別螺類的生存反應，例如縮回、延伸、復位以及側化表現。然後，此計畫將評估草食性螺類的覓食速度及行動，以了解牠們將如何直接和間接地影響其他物種。透過量化以上數據，此項目將協助估計未來氣候對個別物種的生存及行為影響。最後，此研究會利用大型分析顯示出物種的行為變化、生物系統服務的改變以及人類的社會經濟系統。這將有助了解未來氣候中海洋物種的角色。

24301021.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24301021.value: 動理學模型在很多重要領域都被廣泛應用，例如稀薄氣體、等離子物理、天文物理，以及一些新興領域例如半導體、環境、社會和生物科學。動理學模型的不確定量化是一類重要的問題，然而直到近幾年才被關注，該領域值得被深度挖掘和推進。鑑於動理學理論在數學物理，偏微分方程（兩個菲爾茲獎得主P.L.Lions和C.Villani的相關工作）和多尺度計算的重要性，以及動理學模型建模背後固有的不確定因素，研究帶有隨機參數的動理學模型及其數值方法是尤為重要的，並可以幫助我們驗證和提高模型的準確度。我們將從分析和數值的角度研究帶有隨機參數的多尺度動理混合物模型，並致力設計出創新有效（包括侵入式和非侵入式）的數值方法。 基於hypocoercivity理論下的動理學模型及其數值方法的局部敏感度分析，解的正則性和數值分析，為我們研究帶隨機參數的動理學方程提供了強大的工具。對於確定性的動理學問題，hypocoercivity提供了一套完善和成熟的理論。對於帶有隨機參數的問題，PI之前做出了主要貢獻，因此為分析和數值方面克服擬課題的困難奠定了堅實基礎。至今，從確定性到不確定性動理學模型問題的拓展只限於單個模型和周期型邊界問題。我們將致力解決更有趣和更具挑戰性的新問題，包括：研究帶有隨機變量的氣體或等離子體的動理混合物方程；帶邊界的或定義域是無限區域的問題；對於高效的，隨機框架下漸進保持數值算法的關於物理和隨機空間的誤差分析；以及對於帶有高維隨機參數的動理模型的多重保真方法。 我們提出的課題，如果能成功，將推進人們對動理混合物模型的不確定量化問題的理解，並為解決例如稀薄氣體、等離子物理、半導體和環境科學等複雜的實際問題提供先進的數值計算方法。

24302721.value: 太陽是一個強烈的伽馬射線源（1GeV - 100GeV），但太陽的溫度本身不足夠產生高能伽馬射線。 然而，宇宙中充滿著來自超新星遺跡的高能量宇宙線。這些宇宙線能量極高，甚至高達100000000000GeV。這些宇宙射線與太陽大氣的碰撞令太陽成為伽馬射線源。 利用費米伽馬射線望遠鏡，太陽伽馬射線最近得到精準的觀察。有趣的是，太陽的伽馬射線比以前的理論預期高出甚多。在後續的工作上也發現更多太陽伽馬射線有趣的特徵，如時間變性，硬能譜，能譜特徵，和表面光源分佈等。這些觀測結果顯示太陽的伽馬射線產生機制比之前想像中的更複雜更有趣。 太陽伽馬射線產生機制最複雜之處在於太陽磁場的影響。 太陽磁場控制著太空天氣，包括太陽閃焰等有可能破壞人類基建的太陽活動。複雜的太陽磁場也會影響宇宙線在太陽大氣中的的傳播和伽馬射線的產生。最近的研究已經發現太陽日冕磁場能影響太陽伽馬射線生產，但只限10GeV 以下。 在這個項目，我們將指出太陽光球層以下的磁場能導致高能太陽伽馬射線(>10GeV)的產生。這不單有可能能全面解決太陽伽馬射線產生之謎，也能反映出伽馬射線能作為探測光球層以下的磁場的可能性。現有的觀測方法並不能有效地探測這些深入太陽的磁場，因此，高能伽馬射線有望能成為一個新的研究太陽的工具，並提供關於太陽磁場新的重要信息。

24302721.label: Realisation of objectives
24302721.value: We have completed the semi-analytical modelling of sub-photospheric magnetic fields effects on the production of TeV solar gamma rays. This result was published in Physical Review Letter [2]. This fully completed our objective (1) and (3). Our model provides a viable explanation for the TeV gamma rays discovered by HAWC, highlighted the importance, and even the necessity of strong sub-photospheric magnetic fields on the production of TeV solar gamma rays. As traditional solar magnetic field probes cannot see below the photosphere, this means that TeV solar gamma rays can indeed provide new information on these hidden magnetic fields. This fully completes objectives (2) and (5). In collaboration with HAWC, we discovered TeV solar gamma rays, this work is now published in Physical Review Letter [1], since the last project report. While this is not clearly stated in the original objective, it advanced this area of research significantly, and contributes to objective (5) for new observations that our model needed to be compared. As reported in the mid-term report, a PhD student has been recruited to work on the simulation code G4Solar. He is now in his 5th year in PhD, and this work will be his main thesis. With G4Solar, we verified that strong sub-photospheric fields can indeed enhance the gamma-ray production. In addition, we isolate and identify that sub-photospheric fields actually have limited effect on the low energy (~ 1GeV) solar gamma ray production, which turns out was dominated by corona magnetic fields. Sub-photospheric fields are dominant only when the particle energies are high enough to ignore the corona fields, and when they can penetrate deep enough to the strong field regions. With our new G4Solar simulations, we further identify that the time variation of ~1GeV solar gamma rays directly correlates with the time variations in the open field area, providing a new interpretation of these observations. This result is surprising, and will allow ~ 1GeV gamma rays as a new probe for the coronal magnetic fields. This results has been reported in several conferences, the paper is in the polishing stage, and will be submitted to top journals this year. With this, we fully completed objective (4) In 2024, we successfully applied to join the LHAASO collaboration, with the primary goal of searching for gamma rays from the Sun. With the large exposure of LHAASO, it is likely that it will produce new information (spectral or timing) that could be used to construct and test TeV solar gamma ray production models. The collection of all the works above completed objective (6), showing that game rays is a promising and unique tool for probing solar magnetic fields. 24302721.label: Major findings and research outcome
24302721.value: In research output publication [1], in collaboration with HAWC, we discovered TeV solar gamma rays for the first time. This not only is the most energetic light even seen from the Sun, its high flux tells us that there are strong magnetic fields that can reflect 10 TeV comsic rays propagating in the solar atmosphere, and its soft spectral index tells us that the gamma-ray escape efficiency drops rapidly. This paper expands the window of solar observation with gamma rays, and also demonstrated for the first time the possibility of observing the Sun with ground based gamma-ray telescopes. In research output publication [2], together with Prof. Andrew Hillier from Exeter University, and Prof. Shinichiro Ando from University of Amsterdam, I developed a semi-analytic modeling, showing that sub-photospheric horizontal internetwork magnetic fields could have the required surface coverage, field strength, and field configuration to reflect 10 TeV cosmic rays, resulting in the observed TeV solar gamma-ray flux by HAWC. As these fields are conjectured, but cannot be observed with traditioanl optical methods, this shows that solar gamma rays could be a novel probe of solar magnetic fields.

24302721.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24302721.value: There are two major directions that we plan to follow up with the science of this project. 1) New observations HAWC's discovery reuslts are still missing key information such as time variation and a more detail spectral description. With LHAASO, we aim to further characterize these properties by utilising its larger collection area compared to HAWC. 2) Deeper connection with solar physics community We demonstrated, as a proof of concept, that strong sub-photospheric fields are responsible for the high-energy gamma rays observed from the Sun. To maximize the physics potential of using solar gamma rays, we plan to simulate the production of solar gamma rays using realistic solar magnetic field conditions produced in MHD simulations. We also plan to investigate the impact of magnetic field turbulence in the observation. These are important steps towards understanding the time variation and morphology of solar gamma rays.

24302721.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24302721.value: The Sun emits photos that are billions to trillions more energetic that visible light because of energetic cosmic particle hitting the solar atmosphere. In order to produce these photons, strong magnetic fields are needed to revert the directions of the cosmic particles in the solar atmosphere. However, the exact nature of these magnetic fields has been an unsolved problem. In this project, we use the HAWC gamma-ray observatory, for the first time, discovered the highest energy light that has ever detected from the Sun. Furthermore, we have developed a theoretical model showing that if there are strong horizontal magnetic fields just underneath the surface of the Sun, they could led to the production of these high energy photons. These magnetic fields are hidden from traditional methods of solar observation. Therefore, we showed that high-energy solar photons could be a new way to detect solar magnetic fields. Solar magnetic fields are the origin of solar weather, which has significant impact to earth infrastructures and space missions. A better understanding of solar magnetic fields will allows us to better understand how the Sun and space weather works, and better prepare for it.

24304621.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24304621.value: 流體運動的研究在數學中有著悠久的歷史。特別是，自由邊界問題的研究在過去二十年左右蓬勃發展。然而， 這項活動的大部分重點是研究不可壓縮的自由邊界歐拉方程。可壓縮自由邊界歐拉方程的理論，特別是那些模擬液體（而不是氣體）的模型遠沒有那麼發達。我們對液體的運動域是無界的水波問題感興趣。本項目重點研究可壓縮水波運動的數學理論。我們不能簡單地將可壓縮的水波視為不可壓縮的水波的概括因後者的一些關鍵技術不能適應了前者。因此，PI 將採用幾何分析技術在半空間中研究可壓縮運動的局部和長時間方面水波。即使可壓縮水波方程不存在直接在幾何表述，事實上，它們與幾何有很深的聯繫，尤其對自由邊界的研究起到重要作用。 該提案由兩個主要部分組成。首先，PI 想了解可壓縮重力水波運動的局部（時間）適定性在表面張力的影響。從物理上來說，這是非常重要的，因為真正的水波同時考慮了重力和表面張力，表面張力使自由表面具有凝聚力。在數學上，表面張力 可以解釋為移動表面邊界上的自然邊界條件從而穩定運動。其次，PI 想開發新技術最終可以解決一個無旋初始數據的可壓縮水波小解的長期適定性。這裡值得一提的是，與不可壓縮的情況不同，我們無法把可壓縮的水波運動邊界方程直接寫在邊界。因此，必須採用一套全新的技術發明來研究可壓縮水波的長期存在。

24304621.label: Realisation of objectives
24304621.value: All objectives have been thoroughly researched, and each has been linked to corresponding research papers. The first objective is addressed in the paper titled "Compressible Gravity-Capillary Water Waves with Vorticity: Local Well-Posedness, Incompressible and Zero-Surface-Tension Limits," authored by the PI and J. Zhang. We demonstrate the local well-posedness of the 3D compressible gravity-capillary water waves with a fixed flat bottom at finite depth and vorticity. This is achieved by introducing carefully designed approximate equations that are asymptotically consistent with the a priori energy estimate. In addition to well-posedness, we show that the a priori energy estimate remains uniform in both Mach number and the surface tension coefficient, assuming the initial Rayleigh-Taylor sign condition. Consequently, we present a robust framework that allows for the simultaneous derivation of the incompressible and zero surface tension limits. This being said, the result of our work not only addresses Objective 1 but also provides a unified approach for proving the local well-posedness of both incompressible and compressible water waves, with and without surface tension. The second objective is addressed in the paper titled "A Generalized Beale–Kato–Majda Breakdown Criterion for the Free-Boundary Problem in Euler Equations with Surface Tension, " authored by the PI and K. Zhou (PI's postdoc). We present a new breakdown criterion for 3D free-boundary incompressible Euler equations that reduces to the celebrated Beale-Kato-Majda criterion if the kinematic boundary condition on the free boundary reduces to the slip boundary condition, in which case the free boundary becomes fixed. In addition to the boundedness of the L_t^1 L^∞-norm of the vorticity, we find that the solution of the free-boundary incompressible Euler equations can be extended to a later time provided that the geometry, velocity, and acceleration of the free surface boundary stay bounded. Finally, the PI realized, after lengthy discussions with his collaborators, that the statement of the third objective is not physical; it involves modifying the usual slip boundary condition on the fixed boundary. Nevertheless, it only makes sense to study the free-boundary Euler equations modeling water waves, rather than designing a toy model in a domain with a fixed boundary. Alternatively, the PI has authored another paper concerning the long-time behavior of water waves. In "Small Scale Creation for 2D Free Boundary Euler Equations with Surface Tension," authored by the PI, Z. Hu, and Y. Yao, we demonstrate the instability of rotational water waves. It is well known that the motion of 2D and 3D water waves described by the free-boundary Euler equations admits a long-time solution provided the initial data is (sufficiently) small and irrotational. However, it is unknown whether the corresponding solutions for generic rotational small initial data always remain small. In the present paper, we give a negative answer to this question in capillary water waves. We show that there exists a small rotational initial velocity with a flat initial interface, such that the vorticity gradient of the corresponding solution grows double-exponentially over time. This sharply contrasts with the irrotational case, where the size of the solution remains small for all times. The final paragraph of this section is devoted to justifying the low expenditure. The PI was unable to travel outside Hong Kong to attend conferences, and his collaborators could not visit the PI either due to the COVID-19 pandemic. All joint research was conducted online via Zoom meetings during this period. Additionally, although the PI had hired RAs (i.e., the MPhil and Ph.D. students of the PI), the Department of Mathematics funded both of them under a graduate student fellowship. In short, the PI did not have any chances to spend this grant until 2023.

24304621.label: Major findings and research outcome
24304621.value: In "Compressible Gravity-Capillary Water Waves..." (paper No.2 in RO), the PI and his collaborator developed a new framework to study the unified local existence of free-boundary compressible fluid equations. This framework is robust in that it allows for the simultaneous investigation of the well-posedness of both incompressible and compressible free-boundary Euler equations, with and without surface tension. It can also be readily extended to analyze other free-boundary fluid equations, e.g., compressible MHD (see, for instance, arXiv:2312.11254v3 and arXiv:2405.00421 by J. Zhang), as well as elastodynamics (the thesis problem of the PI's Ph.D. student H. Wang). It is worth noting that part of the unified framework is developed in "Zero surface tension limit...." (paper No.1 in RO). In "A Generalized Beale-Kato-Majda Breakdown Criterion..." (paper No.3 in RO), the PI and his postdoc provide a faithful extension of the celebrated Beale-Kato-Majda breakdown criterion to the free-boundary Euler equations modeling the motion of water waves. Specifically, we can recover the original BKM criterion as long as the free boundary becomes rigid (in the sense that the kinematic boundary condition reduces to the slip boundary condition). Recently, Hao and Yang have extended the results of this paper to ideal MHD equations (arXiv:2312.09473). In "Small Scale Creation...." (paper No.4 in RO), Z. Hu, Y. Yao, and the PI demonstrate the instability of rotational water waves. This result is the first to examine the long-term dynamics of water waves with generic rotational initial data, paving the way for further exploration of stability and instability in rotational water waves. In particular, new tools have been developed, including a rigidity analysis of the moving interface and the approximate Biot-Savart law for free-boundary problems.

24304621.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24304621.value: First, the PI aims to continue studying the incompressible limit, particularly with ill-prepared initial data. This is, in fact, the main objective of the PI’s newly awarded project CUHK-14304424. On the other hand, both "A Generalized Beale-Kato-Majda Breakdown Criterion..." (paper No. 3 in RO) and "Small Scale Creation...." (paper No. 4 in RO) pave the way for discovering new mechanisms that lead to the formation of singularities on the moving boundary. For instance, one possible direction involves understanding whether the vorticity can cause significant deformation of the free interface. Additionally, it is also quite intriguing to explore the long-term stability of water waves with certain sufficiently small and rotational initial data (e.g., vortex patches with prescribed symmetry).

24304621.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24304621.value: This project aims to understand the motion of water waves (e.g., ocean surface) from a mathematical perspective. In the first part of this project, we demonstrate that the motion of water waves is accurately described by both the compressible and incompressible Euler equations through a unified well-posedness theory, at least within a short time interval. In the second part of this project, we study the long-term dynamics of water waves, particularly when the fluid's velocity is rotational. We conclude that it is the rotation that generates instability in the water waves, even when the initial velocity and the moving interface are sufficiently small.

24305521.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24305521.value: How do earthquakes initiate? Answering this fundamental question is critical for our understanding of earthquake physics and predictability. It has long been observed that earthquakes are often preceded by smaller earthquakes known as foreshocks. However, the underlying physical processes remain unresolved. One perspective is that earthquakes begin as slow slip. The accelerating slow slip drives nearby small fault patches to rupture as foreshocks. In this case, foreshocks and slow slips could forewarn an impending large earthquakes. Another perspective is that foreshocks are no different from other earthquake clusters, and the largest earthquake that follows is simply a random outcome of interevent stress triggering. In this case, foreshocks would have no predictive value. At oceanic transform faults (OTFs), studies have suggested that large earthquakes are preceded by significantly more foreshocks compared to continental faults. The foreshocks have been successfully used to retrospectively predict a few larger earthquakes and inferred to possibly reflect precursory slow slips, although this remains debated. Studies have also suggested that on average, plate motion on oceanic transform faults is primarily accommodated by slow slips instead of earthquakes. However, there is significant variability between fault segments. These characteristics make OTFs unique laboratories for probing the physical processes underlying foreshocks, how earthquakes and slow slips interact, as well as the factors controlling variability in fault slip behaviour. Due to their remoteness, most studies on OTFs have relied on far-field data, resulting in poor spatial resolution of seismic properties. Our proposed study will leverage publicly available data from a one-year deployment of 54 ocean-bottom seismometers along the Blanco Transform Fault in the northeast Pacific Ocean. This is only the second large-scale deployment of seismometers along an OTF system to date. We will use state-of-the-art techniques to produce a high-resolution earthquake catalogue and search for various manifestations of slow slip transients. We will also produce a longer-term earthquake catalogue using sound waves recorded by hydrophones permanently deployed on nearby submarine observatories since 2015 with publicly available real-time data. Combining these catalogues, we will analyse the spatiotemporal evolution of foreshock sequences in detail and quantify how foreshock activity and its predictive value vary spatially. We will also examine the interaction between earthquakes and slow slip transients, and investigate the factors contributing to variability in fault slip behaviour. The results will improve our understanding of earthquake physics and have implications for seismic hazard assessment along continental faults that present major hazard to the society. 解開地震如何成核的謎團對於理解地震物理機制以及預測地震具有重要的意義。在大地震發生之前，有時會觀測到一些小地震，被稱之為前震。一種觀點認為前震是被大地震慢滑移成核階段所觸發的，因此有可能預測即將發生的大地震。另一種觀點認為，前震與其他的震群沒有實質性區別，而最大的地震只是相鄰地震間應力觸發的隨機結果。因此，前震並沒有預測主震的作用。海洋轉換斷層與大陸地震相比有更多的前震。在部分海洋轉換斷層，前震也已被證明有預測大地震的效用，並被認為與大地震前的慢滑移有關。這些特徵使海洋轉換斷層成為探測前震的物理過程以及地震和慢滑移相互作用的天然實驗室。我們將分析沿東北太平洋布蘭科轉換斷層的海底地震儀數據來構建一個高精度地震目錄。利用這地震目錄，我們將系統地表徵沿布蘭科轉換斷層的各種滑移活動，並對不同前震機制模型進行分析及釐清地震與慢滑移之間的相互作用。

24307121.label: Project Title(Chinese)
24307121.value: 辛解消的幾何和表示理論及其乘法類似物

24307121.label: Project Objectives
24307121.value: Study special structures arising in mirror symmetry for symplectic resolutions. Conical symplectic resolutions a remarkable class of algebraic symplectic varieties including the Springer resolution, Nakajima quiver varieties and hypertoric or toric hyperkähler varieties. By either quantising the ring of functions on symplectic resolutions or considering algebras of correspondences acting on their cohomology, one finds geometric incarnations of much of classical representation theory, and a wealth of new and unexplored algebras and categories. They are thus a wonderful organising principle in modern geometric representation theory. Homological mirror symmetry, in its most basic form, is an equivalence between the derived category of coherent sheaves on a variety X and the Fukaya category of Lagrangian branes on a symplectic manifold Y. Motivated by questions from modular representation theory, we seek to understand special structures and features of mirror symmetry for a symplectic resolution X. These include exotic t-structures on the derived category of coherent sheaves and their mirrors, categorical stable envelopes, dilating C* actions and the equivariant quantum connection. This promises to give new perspectives on modular representation theory, the equivariant enumerative geometry of symplectic resolutions and quantum integrable systems. Dolbeault analogues of symplectic resolutions. In order to study mirror symmetry for a symplectic resolution X, we must introduce three multiplicative analogues: a `Betti analogue' which behaves like the moduli of local systems on a curve, a `de Rahm analogue' which behaves like the moduli of flat connections on a curve, and a `Dolbeault analogue' which behaves like the moduli of Higgs bundles on a curve. The Betti and de Rahm analogues are relatively well studied, but the Dolbeault analogues remain mysterious, except in the hypertoric case where they have been defined by Hausel and Proudfoot and studied by the PI and his collaborators. The PI proposes to define and study them in greater generality. Of special interest is the construction of an integrable system on the Dolbeault space analogous to the Hitchin system on the moduli of Higgs bundles, a non-abelian Hodge theory for the de Rahm and Dolbeault spaces and a Riemann-Hilbert correspondence from the de Rahm to the Betti space. With these in hand, one can also investigate the perverse filtration on cohomology induced by the integrable system and its relation to the weight filtration on the Betti space cohomology. Also of potential relevance to mirror symmetry is the quantisation of the integrable system, p-adic integration along its fibers, and the relation of the deformation quantisations of the three spaces. Finally, we can ask how our new Betti, de Rahm and Dolbeault spaces relate to the classical moduli of harmonic bundles for special choices of group and Riemann surface.

24502821.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24502821.value: This project aims to investigate trade compression as an alternative to central clearing. Since the 2008 financial crisis, regulators have turned to central clearing in an effort to reduce counterparty risk in over-the-counter derivative markets. Central clearing essentially routes all trades through a single central counterparty (CCP). Any proposed bilateral trade between A and B is replaced by two trades: one between A and the CCP and a second between the CCP and B. The CCP, by being the counterparty to all trades, is then in a unique position to provide stability to the market. It effectively nets all payment obligations, eliminating the risk arising from having to make large payments even when the net payments are small. Furthermore, through a default fund and loss mutualization, the CCP can absorb and spread defaults, reducing the chance of a chain of defaults. However, central clearing is not without its downsides. The CCP is systemically important; by construction its failure could cause a complete collapse of the market. Furthermore, the existence of the CCP introduces a classic moral hazard problem. Loss mutualization and the default fund partially insulate agents from their counterparties, thereby reducing the incentive for them to seek high quality counterparties. Trade compression provides an alternative method to improve resiliency in the over-the-counter derivatives markets. Compression involves a third party observing all bilateral trades and then offering a new set of bilateral positions. These new contracts have the ability to offer substantial netting benefits. Furthermore, if done correctly, the netting can reduce counterparty risk by reducing gross exposures and distributing risk across several counterparties. The main goal of this project is to generate a framework for evaluating compression as an alternative to central clearing. The first step is to generate a tractable model for analyzing default risk; existing methods in the literature are too simple to make progress for this question. Within this framework, we can then investigate several important questions: 1) setting aside the moral-hazard issue, what type of compression achieves an optimal or near-optimal risk profile for the system; 2) how does this compare with central clearing; and 3) can we improve on the moral hazard problem using compression? With these questions answered, we can then make recommendations for real-world improvements using compression. 本項目旨在研究交易壓縮作為中央結算的替代方案。自2008年金融危機以來，監管機構已轉向中央結算，以降低場外衍生品市場的交易對手風險。中央結算本質上將所有交易通過中央結算對手(CCP)進行。 任何擬議的介於A與B之間的雙邊貿易由兩個交易替代: 一個交易介於A與CCP, 另一個交易介於CCP與B。作為所有交易的交易對手，CCP擁有為市場提供穩定性的獨特地位。CCP有效地對所有支付義務進行淨額結算，從而消除了即使淨付款很小也必須進行大額付款所產生的風險。此外，通過失責基金和損失共擔，CCP可以吸收和分散失責，減少連鎖失責的機會。 然而，中央結算並非沒有其弊端。CCP在系統裡至關重要，它的角色決定了若CCP失敗，整個市場將可能崩潰。此外，CCP的存在引入了一個經典的道德風險問題 - 損失共擔和失責基金部分地將代理人與其交易對手隔離開來，從而減少了他們尋求高質量交易對手的激励。 交易壓縮提供了一種提高場外衍生品市場韧性的替代方案。壓縮涉及通過第三方對所有雙邊交易進行觀察，進而由第三方向交易雙方提供一組新的雙邊交易。這些新的交易合同可以提供極大的淨額結算益處。此外，如操作適當，該淨額結算可以通過降低總額風險並在多個交易對手之間分配風險的方式降低對手風險。 本項目的主要目標是生成一個框架，以評估壓縮作為中央結算的替代方案。第一步是生成一個易於處理的模型來分析失責風險。目前文獻中的現有方式過於簡單，無法在這個問題上取得進展。在這個框架內，我們可以進一步分析幾個重要問題: 1) 如暫撇開道德風險問題不談，哪種類型的壓縮可以實現系統的最佳或接近最佳的風險狀況? 2) 這種風險狀況與中央結算下的風險狀況相比如何？3)我們是否可以使用壓縮來改善道德風險問題? 回答完這些問題後，我們就可以就使用交易壓縮為現實情況改進提出建議。

24502821.label: Realisation of objectives
24502821.value: We have made substantial progress with the first three objectives and are still working on the remainder. We provide a tractable model for evaluating the risks involved with different network topologies (objective 1). A full network model with defaults and spillovers due to partial repayments is not analytically tractable, due to the complicated interdependence of default boundaries. Our key contribution is the simplification we make to attain tractability. By focusing only on the spillover generated by the most salient default, we remove the complex interdependence of default boundaries while keeping the most important non-linearities that drive differences in risk across different network topologies. This simplification is slightly similar in spirit to, but very different from, tractability simplifications made in linear networks, where some papers only focus on the first-order spillover effects. This model is in some sense complete, so in a sense we have completed objective 1, but we are still looking to see if we can get an even better approximation. For objective 2, we provide three main insights. The first is that any optimal network removes all cycles. That is, any optimal post-compression network does not contain any positions where 1 is long with 2, 2 is long with 3, ...n-1 is long with n, and n is long with 1 for any n >= 2. These cycles create possibilities for defaults to spill over (contagion) without providing any benefits. The second is that the optimal network has a sense of transitivity/ordering. Mathematically, each market participant’s position is characterized by a Lagrange multiplier. Optimal post-compression positions "flow" from larger values to smaller values. That is, all post-compression positions are of the form where the long party always a (weakly) higher Lagrange multiplier than the short party. As a direct corollary, this means that (in general) maximum compression is not optimal: we can have participants intermediating some of the trades. Interestingly, though having a higher multiplier is necessary to have a link, it is not sufficient. As discussed below, there are cases where higher multiplier participants do not trade directly with lower multiplier participants. The third insight is the optimal network trades off the benefits of distributing the cost of defaults across a larger set of participants with the increased possibility of contagion. Mathematically, though in the optimal network higher Lagrange multiplier participants typically have a long position with lower multiplier participants, the first- and second-order conditions do not require the link to have positive size. Through numerical illustrations, we do indeed obtain cases where in the optimal network 1 is only directly long with 3, despite the existence of a participant 2 with Lagrange multiplier strictly in between 1 and 3. This happens when 1 and/or 3 are highly direction (need to take large long or short positions) and at least one of them is very risky. The benefit of having some trades routed through 2 (which arise from 2's ability to absorb some losses and reduce the amount of loss transmitted through the system) are outweighed by the increased risk that 2 faces to the point where even a marginal exposure is suboptimal. As a corollary to our third insight: we obtain an interesting non-monotonicity result. Consider again the same 3-participant setup where 1 needs a large long position and 3 needs a large short position, with 2 as a potential intermediary. Initially, when we increase the size of the desired position, the optimal position between 1 and 2 (and 2 and 3) increases. However, once the sizes of the positions become too large, any increase in the desired size comes with a decrease in the amount optimally intermediated by 2. This is due to 1 and 3 becoming riskier, and the benefits of intermediation being outweighed by the default risk imposed on 2. Compared to central clearing, we find numerical evidence that there are cases where compression is optimal relative to central clearing (objective 3). This follows from the third insight in objective 2 above. When participants are highly risky, it can be optimal to shield other participants from their defaults rather than getting them involved. Central clearing necessarily involves all participants equally, and so therefore can lead to suboptimally high levels of contagion. We are still in the very beginning stages of objective 4. There are two questions where we would ideally make contributions. The first is whether ex-post optimal compression distorts the ex-ante incentives to trade in a way that affects stability. The second is whether participants have private incentives not to disclose or allow certain compressions that benefit the whole system. Due to a lack of data, we have made no progress on objective 5. As described in our previous progress reports, the data provider was no longer willing to share what they initially said they could provide. The coarse summary statistics we were able to obtain previously (namely, power-law distributions of positions) are insufficient for analyzing optimality of trade compression. Our theoretical results highlight the interplay between position sizes, directions, and the riskiness of each of the participants. Simply observing their overall position sizes does provide much insight into the benefits of compression. As outlined below, we are in discussions with a regulatory body to obtain relevant data that will allow us to examine the empirical relevant of our model and insights. We did consider an application to cryptocurrencies, as proposed in the previous intermediate progress report. However, our model and insights are relevant for contracts that feature long-term payments, such as swaps, other derivatives, and debt. The open questions in cryptocurrency markets are more related to the efficient clearing and compression of spot transactions, which our model does not speak to. As a result, we have gone back to considering just traditional markets. We are currently working with researchers at a large regulatory body to obtain data on all positions in a large derivative market involving the regulator's currency. This derivatives market is highly relevant to our model, as it involves long-dated positions and limited scope for central clearing. My understanding is that our work has been approved by the regulator's research body, and we are currently working with one of their researchers to obtain relevant empirical facts that can inform our models application. Due to us being unable to obtain the data we were initially promised, we have not had a chance to use the funds provided for this project. Our funds were for the hiring of (a) research assistant(s) to help with data analysis or substantial simulation work based on data. As we were unable to obtain the data during the project's funding period, we were unable to make use of the funding.

24502821.label: Major findings and research outcome
24502821.value: Through our model, of which a version is presented in the draft and poster both included in Part C, we find that trade compression can provide similar benefits to central clearing, and sometimes outperform it. Whereas central clearing pools all risk together, thereby effectively meaning that everyone intermediates everyone, trade compression allows for trading off the benefits of intermediation (more risk sharing) with the costs (more contagion). When done optimally trade compression can achieve similar outcomes to central clearing when all participants are of low to moderate risk, and can actually outperform central clearing when some participants are highly risky. We characterize optimal trade compression through a novel model that maintains tractability while still including the most salient non-linear payoffs generated by defaults. We find that the optimally compressed network features no cycles and features transitivity/directionality: there is an ordering and participants only trade in the direction of the order. As a result, optimal compression is generally not maximal compression. Keeping some intermediation (less directional participants sitting between more directional participants) is generally optimal: participants offer their capital as a buffer to absorb some of the losses created by default. Through numerical examples, we show two interesting features of optimal compression. The first is a non-monotonicity result. In the presence of enough risk, as the total amount of trades increases, the amount optimally intermediated first increases and then decreases. The intuition is that intermediation is initially beneficial (due to increased risk sharing) but eventually the system becomes so risky that it is optimal to shield the potential intermediaries by compressing them out altogether. The second is that optimal compression can outperform central clearing. When some participants are particularly risky, optimal compression will reduce intermediation to insulate other participants from their defaults. Central clearing, by pooling all the risk together, exposes everyone to the risky participants, thereby effectively creating too much intermediation. Our numerical illustrations further suggest that when participants are not too risky, optimal compression can achieve outcomes close to central clearing. Our research suggests that trade compression can be a valuable tool not only for reducing costs and regulatory capital, but also for reducing risk in a system. The flexibility of trade compression allows us to balance the benefits of intermediation with the costs of exposing more participants to risk.

24502821.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24502821.value: We are currently in discussions with a regulatory body to obtain more detailed data for a large and relevant class of derivatives. This may require deeper collaboration with their researchers but will provide the type of data that our model can speak to. Beyond empirics, we are working on tightening the theory. Right now, some of the insights can still only be demonstrated numerically. This means we do not have a clean characterizing of our central tradeoff: the benefits from intermediation obtained through risk sharing vs. the cost of increased contagion. We are also working to see if a special case with a power-law distribution of trade sizes (as is empirically relevant) leads to sharper insights. More long term, we are working on examining distortions to incentives. As described in 5.3. realization of objectives, we are interested in the ex-ante incentives to trade in the presence of ex-post compression, and we are interested in seeing if there are any private incentives not to fully participate in compression (by not participating at all, setting non-truthful risk limits, or only partially revealing positions). Depending on the results, this spawn separate research papers.

24502821.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24502821.value: Financial institutions trade long-term contracts such as swaps, other derivatives, and long-term debt. Over time, the system accumulates offsetting and redundant trades, which increases costs and fragility of the system. One solution to this problem is central clearing. In a centrally cleared environment, all market participants only trade with a central counterparty. Offsetting trades are automatically torn up, and risk is shared among all participants. However, central clearing is not always feasible, and it may create more risk by concentrating risk in the central counterparty. We instead examine the ability of trade compression to reduce risk in the system. Compression involves participants submitting their existing positions to a third party, who then suggests participants tear up their existing contracts and replace them with a new set of more efficient contracts. Through our model, we find that optimal trade compression can provide similar or even better reductions in overall risk as central clearing. In cases where market participants are not too risky, similar levels of risk reduction as central clearing can be achieved by not compressing too aggressively. When some market participants are risky, trade compression can beat central clearing by shielding the system from riskier participants.

24600321.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24600321.value: To meet our social and economic challenges with a STEM workforce, we need to improve the recruitment and retention of students with a STEM major in the university and job market. Current international research in school STEM education advocates integrated STEM (iSTEM) – i.e. inter- and trans-disciplinary, rather than multi-disciplinary approaches – for quality learning. These challenges have been reflected in student entries for Hong Kong public examinations. Secondary school students prefer to study business and economics rather than science, advanced mathematics and technology, and there are no trends showing an increase in the number of students opting for STEM subjects. A strong and positive STEM interest and identity is a predictor of future study and career choice in a STEM field. A possible solution to the challenges is iSTEM programmes. However, existing studies of STEM education that address multiple disciplines seem insufficient, with mixed findings and inadequate direction for iSTEM advancement. Those studies in the development of STEM interest and identity have: (i) ignored the integrated nature of STEM, and focused on multiple disciplines; (ii) focused on equity, particularly underrepresentation by gender, race and language; and (iii) examined the effect of role models and mentors in the informal setting. As a result, we still understand little about how students develop their interest and identity in iSTEM classrooms. Literature suggests that Self-Determination Theory (SDT) provides an understanding of motivational processes that influence the development. Hence, this study employs the three psychological needs – autonomy, relatedness and competency – in SDT and the development of STEM interest and identity to propose an SDT approach to an iSTEM programme, by redesigning a non-SDT-based iSTEM programme: Hong Kong Sustainable City. It aims to investigate the effectiveness of the proposed 10-week programme on development, and understand how the three psychological needs support development. The study will employ a sequential explanatory mixed-method design study – an experiment with semi-structured interviews. Participants will comprise 300 Secondary Three students and 9 STEM teachers from three Hong Kong schools with different levels of academic achievement. Quantitative and qualitative analyses will be used to assess the study goals. Essentially, this study will significantly impact, in the short term, teachers and policymakers by enhancing their knowledge of STEM interest and identity, in the medium term, academia by contributing to the related theory and studies, and in the long term, the economy and society as a whole by improving student social mobility. 香港公開考試的學生報名情況反映了社會對未來科學、科技、數學和工程(STEM)人材需求的挑戰，大多數的中學生喜歡修讀商業和經濟學，而不是STEM 的科目，而且選擇 STEM 科目的學生人數沒有明顯增長的趨勢。為了應付這挑戰，我們需要吸引多些中學生在STEM領域進修及就業，以增加有關的人材。學生對STEM 的興趣和身份認同感是STEM 領域未來學習和職業選擇的預測指標，加上以跨學科進行綜合 STEM (iSTEM)是國際研究的方面，以實現優質學習。然而，現有針對個別學科的 STEM 教育研究似乎還不夠充分，研究結果參差不齊，未能充分發展iSTEM。還有這些關於 STEM 興趣和身份認同感發展的研究： (i) 忽視了 STEM 的綜合性，側重於個別多學科； (ii) 注重公平性（特別是性別、種族和語言的代表性不足）；和 (iii) 了解行為榜樣和導師在非課室環境中的作用。 因此，我們對學生如何在 iSTEM 課堂中培養興趣和身份認同感仍然知之甚少。文獻表明，自我決定理論 (SDT) 提供了對學習動機發展過程的理解。因此，本研究利用 SDT 中的三種心理需求 (自主性、歸屬性和勝任)設計以SDT為本 的 iSTEM教學，並以十星期的時間教授學生香港城巿的持續性，目的是促進並了解該心理需求如何支持學生的STEM 興趣和身份認同感的發展。這項研究將採用問卷調查及訪談的研究方法，參加者是300名中三學生和9名STEM教師，他們來自香港三所不同學術水平的學校。這項研究將通過增強學生對 STEM 興趣和身份認同感的了解，在短期內能向教師和教育政策制定者提供重要的資訊，並能在中期時間對相關理論和研究做出貢獻，長期來看，這研究能夠提高學生的STEM人材社會流動性，促進經濟。

24600321.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24600321.value: This project has five major areas for future research, and the PI already took action for one of them. • The PI submitted a GRF proposal to investigate how generative artificial intelligence tools support student needs satisfaction in STEM education, resulting in stronger STEM interest and identity. This GRF proposal is a continuation of this ECS project - From teacher support to generative artificial intelligence support. • Different age groups require different levels of needs support, with different subsequent effects. Future development should understand how needs satisfaction affect older students, such as senior secondary and higher education. • The gender difference in STEM interest and identity development was not examined in this project. Future studies should use different strategies to explore how different genders perceive teacher needs support. • Student interest and identity develop and change over time, and a short period may not be long enough to reveal this development. Therefore, longitudinal studies over 2 years are recommended to track how student STEM interest and identity can be fostered over time. • Artificial intelligence education could be seen as STEM education. Future development can be considered to understand if the proposed SDT program can work on emerging technologies.

24600321.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24600321.value: To solve our social and economic challenges with a STEM workforce, we must increase recruiting and retention of STEM majors in universities and the labor market. Current international research in school STEM teaching promotes integrated STEM (iSTEM)—that is, inter- and transdisciplinary rather than multidisciplinary approaches—for better learning. Student entries for Hong Kong public examinations reflect these challenges. A strong and positive STEM interest and identity predicts future STEM studies and job choices. Therefore, this project uses the three psychological needs of self-determination theory (SDT) to develop an iSTEM program aimed at fostering a stronger STEM interest and identity. The findings suggest that the SDT needs satisfaction is related to the development of STEM interest and identity in junior secondary students. They also our designed program effectively fosters stronger STEM interest and identity, resulting in more students choosing STEM subjects for further studies. Essentially, this project significantly impacts teachers and policymakers by enhancing their knowledge of designing iSTEM programs and their understanding of student development; academia by relating interest and identity development to SDT; the economy and society as a whole by improving student social mobility.

24601621.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24601621.value: The caregiving burden experienced by parents of children with special health care needs (SHCN) is known to be significant and its impact tends to be exacerbated when an outbreak of a novel infectious disease occurs. As shown in this coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic, with the prolonged disruptions of individualized rehabilitation/supporting services which cannot be substituted by digital/remoted format and the unprecedented economic hardship, many parents of children with SHCN are under psychological distress, affecting parenting behaviours and child well-being. The pandemic offers a unique opportunity to develop and evaluate mental health interventions for parents of children with SHCN, so that evidence arising could contribute the development of preparedness and emergency response plan for this vulnerable group if other waves of COVID-19/outbreaks of the novel infectious disease occur. However, existing interventions in literature only serve for suspected/infected cases/healthcare workers. Many interventions were developed without a conceptual understanding of what/how the proposed active/therapeutic ingredient(s)/process(es) could lead to desired outcomes. Our previous work includes an international, longitudinal survey aiming at understanding the psychological sequelae of COVID-19 in parents across 21 countries. This study informs the development of a conceptual model, showing that two psychological constructs, namely psychological flexibility (a therapeutic process measure in Acceptance and Commitment Therapy) and prosociality (an attitude and/or a behaviour that orient(s) toward the welfare of others and society) played significant roles in mitigating the adverse impact of COVID-19 on parental mental health. Based on this model, the proposed study will use a randomised controlled trial design to determine the efficacy of a 12-week, smartphone-based Prosocial-orientated Acceptance and Commitment Training (PACT) programme plus age-appropriate positive parenting advice for 98 randomly-assigned parents of children with SHCN, in comparison to a control group (n =98) receiving positive parenting advice only from the smartphone application. Online modules plus group-based video conferencing sessions will be offered. The mental well-being of parent-child dyads (primary outcomes), the psychological flexibility, prosociality, parenting competence of parents and family functioning (secondary outcomes) will be assessed at immediate, 3-, 6- and 12-months post-intervention. Changes in mean outcome scores within-between groups across time/measurements will be examined using adjusted generalized estimating equation models. Using the trial data, path analyses will be adopted to identify causal mechanical pathways of how PACT programme targeting psychological flexibility and prosociality contribute to desired outcomes. A total of 15-20 parents will be purposely sampled for individual interviews to explore their experiences after participating in the PACT programme.

24602421.label: Realisation of objectives
24602421.value: The research, guided by three core objectives, has successfully achieved the intended outcomes, with all objectives fully realised. Objective 1: This component situates China’s regulatory and policy framework for renewable energy integration within the broader context of electricity market reform, drawing on literature primarily focused on liberalised models in the EU and US. It establishes a theoretical foundation for understanding the similarities and differences between China’s reforms - particularly rules governing generator access to the transmission network - and the third-party access regime in more liberalised systems. This theoretical lens enables a more critical and in-depth analysis of China’s approach to integrating renewable energy. Objective 2: The case studies offer empirical insights into the implementation of national renewable energy laws and policies, the causes of renewable energy curtailment, and how these issues are addressed in practice. Fieldwork included interviews in selected provinces that either produce or consume renewable energy. Given the scarcity of primary data and the rapid evolution of the regulatory landscape, this empirical research fills key information gaps, supports the doctrinal analysis in Objective 1, and grounds the project's conclusions and recommendations in real-world practice. Objective 3: Building on the doctrinal and empirical findings, the project contributes to ongoing policy discussions on how regulatory frameworks in China can be improved to better support renewable energy integration. These discussions are developed through critical legal analysis and are reflected throughout the research outputs.

24602421.label: Major findings and research outcome
24602421.value: The research outcomes of this project include: (i) a research monograph published by Cambridge University Press; (ii) three peer-reviewed journal articles; (iii) a book chapter in an edited volume co-edited with four leading energy law scholars, and another chapter currently in production and scheduled for publication in 2026; and (iv) presentation of research findings at international and regional academic conferences and seminars, engaging both academic and policy audiences. The major findings of the project are as follows: (i) China’s Renewable Energy Law has introduced a range of financial and regulatory incentives that have significantly expanded the installed capacity of modern renewable energy, particularly wind and solar. These incentives are designed around a market-oriented approach that assumes the presence of a electricity market based on a liberalised model. Doctrinal analysis reveals that China’s electricity market reform, and reforms across its network-dependent energy sectors, are influenced by liberalised market structures. However, implementation has been slow and uneven, resulting in a ‘hybrid’ market where regulatory and market mechanisms coexist. This hybrid system, combined with unclear rules on grid access and coordination, has constrained large-scale integration of renewable energy. Despite rapid capacity growth, renewable energy consumption remains suboptimal due to persistent curtailment, particularly in provinces with rich renewable resources. (ii) To address the inadequacies of market reform, the central government has introduced targeted regulatory interventions, such as mandatory renewable energy targets, capacity monitoring, and consumption quotas. These measures have proven effective in reducing curtailment and improving utilisation rates. However, the long-term viability of such top-down mechanisms remains uncertain, raising concerns about institutional sustainability and the potential for policy fatigue. (iii) A notable shift in recent years has been the increasing prioritisation of renewable energy within the trading component of China’s electricity market. New regulatory provisions now allow renewable sources preferential access to the grid to meet demand. Of particular significance is the revival of policies supporting direct power trading for solar energy at the distribution level. This suggests a move toward embedding renewable integration within market mechanisms rather than relying solely on administrative mandates, offering a more durable and scalable pathway for accelerating China’s energy transition.

24602421.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24602421.value: Building on these findings, future research could explore the evolving relationship between regulatory interventions and market-based mechanisms in supporting renewable energy integration. In particular, further analysis is needed to assess the long-term effectiveness and adaptability of China’s hybrid electricity market, especially as it seeks to balance administrative controls with market liberalisation. A comparative study of emerging regulatory models in other jurisdictions may also offer insights into best practices for aligning renewable energy policy with grid and market reforms. The next phase of research will focus on analysing recent developments in direct power trading and their implications for decentralised energy systems. This will involve interdisciplinary methods combining legal analysis, policy evaluation, and stakeholder interviews to understand institutional dynamics and regulatory capacity. Findings will support policy recommendations for building a more coherent and flexible regulatory framework that can sustain higher levels of renewable energy integration over time.

24602421.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24602421.value: This research project examines how China is trying to increase the use of renewable energy, such as wind and solar power, and the legal and regulatory tools it uses to achieve this goal. While China has made impressive progress in building renewable energy capacity, much of this energy is not fully used because of problems in how the electricity market works. The study shows that although the government has introduced financial support and policies to promote renewables, the existing electricity market system - partly controlled and partly market-based - creates barriers to using this energy efficiently. The research is important because it explains why simply building more renewable energy is not enough; effective rules and market structures are also needed to deliver clean energy to users. It highlights how government regulatory policies and market reforms must work together to reduce energy waste and support a greener economy. The project adds value by offering a clearer understanding of how laws and regulations affect the success of clean energy transitions. It also provides useful insights for other countries facing similar challenges in balancing government control and market forces to promote sustainable energy use.

24604521.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24604521.value: A prevalent artistic style can be seen in paintings of the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries across China, Japan, and Korea. Scholars conventionally believe that this “international” style originated from a group of professional painters, the so-called “Zhe school,” in China and rapidly disseminated to Japan and Korea through sinophile envoys, merchants, and painters. However, previous studies seldom examined the Hongzhi emperor (r. 1488–1505), who arguably was the most politically and culturally influential art patron, and his favorite court painters, who were the most prestigious painters of the time, in the context of Ming court painting, let alone exploring their contribution to forming a contemporary East Asian visual culture. The Hongzhi emperor, a renowned painter himself, was the only Ming emperor who left abundant records directly indicating his preference for a painting style deriving from the Southern Song court and his admiration for court painters’ craftmanship and artistic creativity. Due to the lack of his extant painting, the Hongzhi emperor was overshadowed in modern scholarship by Xuande and Chenghua, the other two artist emperors of the Ming whose paintings have been well preserved and studied. Since the end of the last century, more and more court painters of the Hongzhi reign have been identified from textual records, and more paintings have been reattributed to them. These discoveries have finally accumulated sufficient evidence for this project to substantially portray the artistic features, social history, and cultural legacy of Hongzhi court painting in the contexts of Ming court art and East Asian visual culture. This project aims to analyze the production, reception, and adaptation of Hongzhi court painting by closely reading into textual records and extant paintings in China, Taiwan, the United States, and Japan. Historical documents, art critiques, painting inscriptions, and formal properties of extant paintings will be carefully scrutinized to understand the artistic features of Hongzhi court painting and the fluidity of artistic styles and court art’s cultural significances crossing the boundaries between inside and outside the court and between China and the rest of East Asia. The outcomes of this project will be two peer-reviewed journal articles, focusing on the Hongzhi emperor’s art patronage and the distribution and appropriation of Chinese painting of the sixteenth century in East Asia, respectively, and a book proposal submitted to an academic publisher, which will be the first monograph on the Ming court painting of the Hongzhi reign. 於15-16世紀的中國、日本、朝鮮繪畫中可見一種常見的藝術風格。學者們普遍認為此一「國際性」的風格起源於一群在中國被統稱為「浙派」的職業畫家之間，再迅速地藉由燕行使、遣明使、商人、畫家流傳至日本、朝鮮。然而前人研究甚少檢視弘治皇帝（1488–1505年在位）與其所偏愛的宮廷畫家於明代宮廷繪畫史中具有的重要地位，更別提探討他們在形成此一普及於東亞各國間的視覺文化中所做出的貢獻，雖然有證據顯示弘治可能為當時最富政治、文化影響力的藝術贊助者，而他所偏愛的宮廷畫家於當世也是最富盛名的畫家。 弘治本身即具畫名，也是唯一一位明代帝王留下豐富記載直接指出他喜愛源於南宋宮廷的繪畫風格，以及他曾對宮廷畫家之畫技、創意表示高度讚許。由於弘治的繪畫作品現已不存，在現今學者的研究中，弘治所受到的關注不如另外兩位作品受到了良好的保存與研究的明代藝術家皇帝——宣德、成化。自上世紀末以來，越來越多弘治朝宮廷畫家的身份由文獻中被辨識出，也有越多的作品被重新認定為這群畫家的作品。這些新發現為此研究計畫累積出充足的證據，能夠從明代宮廷藝術史以及東亞視覺文化的角度，去描繪弘治朝宮廷繪畫的藝術特徵、社會歷史與文化遺產。 此研究計畫欲藉由檢視文獻與現存於中國、臺灣、美國、日本的畫跡，分析弘治朝宮廷繪畫的生產、接受與轉借。研究將透過對歷史文獻、藝評、題跋等文字與現存畫跡形式特徵的審視來理解弘治朝宮廷繪畫的藝術特徵，以及藝術風格與宮廷藝術之文化意涵於宮廷內外、中國與東亞各國間的跨界流動。此計畫預計的學術成果為兩篇分別以弘治皇帝的藝術贊助，與中國繪畫於十六世紀東亞的傳播與挪用為主題的同行評審期刊論文，以及首見以弘治朝宮廷繪畫為主題的學術專論書稿。

24604821.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24604821.value: 背景 當代大學生日漸依賴互聯網尋求幫助；與此同時，許多大學老師，在教授大課時，鼓勵學生在網絡課堂論壇中提問、尋求學業幫助(academic help seeking)。過往研究顯示，幫助者（helper，即提供幫助的源頭)對求助結果的質量，有至關重要的作用。但目前大部分在線論壇，問題和幫助者的匹配，在很大程度上是低效且隨意的。首先，我們通常鼓勵知識淵博的同學成為課程論壇中的主要幫助者，然而大部分論壇只是按照發帖的時間順序排列學生提問，並沒有特別的機制為那些問題找到合適的回答者（幫助者）。其次，有些提問可能超出了學生的知識、技能或意願，無法實現同學互助；這種情況下，老師往往依靠手動監控論壇，根據個人經驗決定是否干預（參與討論）。這種問題-幫助者匹配方式略顯隨意且低效，不利於學生獲得及時且適應性的學業幫助；因此，我們需要更加智能的工具來支持學生的在線學業求助。 目的 本設計研究通過學習分析工具來改善課程論壇中的問題-幫助者匹配，從而提升在線學業求助的質量。在適應性學業求助理論框架的指導下，本研究將開發：1，一套基於本體的推薦系統來提升匹配效率；2）一套異常檢測算法來輔助教師干預。在這套學習分析工具的幫助下，學生更有可能與合適的幫助者產生更具成效的互動，接收到高質量的幫助，並提升自己適應性學業求助能力。 研究計劃 這一套學習分析工具將通過兩個設計研究週期在兩堂大課中實施，並通過混合方法收集和分析數據。具體而言，我將通過准實驗量化比較實驗組和對照組的學業求助效率；我將採用質化方法分析學生學業求助的過程和策略，以及這一套學習分析工具怎樣支持或阻礙師生參與。 意義 這項研究通過智能化的問題-幫助者匹配機制，為促進學生適應性學業求助提供了一套新穎可行的方案。該研究將加深我們對在線環境中學業求助行為的理解，並提取出大課環境中學習分析工具和課程論壇開發的設計原則。

24604821.label: Realisation of objectives
24604821.value: The project successfully implemented an analytics-enhanced course forum and evaluated its impact on students’ educational experiences in large-size colleague classes. Below is an assessment of how the four research objectives were realized, along with challenges encountered and strategies to address them. Objective 1: The analytics-enhanced forum was deployed in a large engineering course on engineering design thinking (approximately 400 students each course) over two iterations of design-based research (DBR). The system provided structured question-helper matching and adaptive support for student help-seeking, improving the organization and efficiency of peer support. Students engaged in more targeted and meaningful interactions, reducing the randomness of traditional forum participation (Dai & Lin, 2022). Challenges & Mitigation: - Initial forum adoption was slower than expected, as students were accustomed to unstructured help-seeking. To address this, we provided scaffolded onboarding, including guidelines and instructional sessions on effective help-seeking practices. - Some students hesitated to engage in peer support, preferring instructor responses. We refined forum prompts and participation incentives to foster a more collaborative learning culture. Objective 2: The project successfully integrated two learning analytics components: 1, Ontology-based recommender system for peer matching; 2. Anomaly detection algorithms to identify timely instructor intervention needs (Dai & Lin, 2022). These tools were developed, tested, and refined through classroom implementation, ensuring their alignment with real-world teaching and learning needs. Pilot testing in the first DBR cycle helped refine the ontology, leading to improved matching accuracy and usability in the second iteration. Challenges & Mitigation: - The ontology-based recommendation system required continuous refinement, as early iterations struggled with semantic mismatches in student queries. We addressed this by incorporating machine learning techniques and manually curating common query patterns. - The anomaly detection mechanism initially flagged false positives, leading to unnecessary instructor interventions. Further training on the detection algorithm reduced false alerts and enhanced system reliability. Objective 3: The effectiveness of the forum was assessed through a comparative study, comparing the analytics-enhanced forum with a conventional forum (control group). Results demonstrated that students learning with the analytics-enhanced forum demonstrated significantly higher degrees of design practices (specifically, empathize, define, ideate, and test), collaborative learning, and course satisfaction (Dai et al., 2024). Challenges & Mitigation: - The effectiveness of the forum was assessed through a historical comparison rather than a quasi-experimental study, as the course instructor prioritized ensuring all students received the best possible learning experience and did not want to designate a control group. Instead, we compared student responses from the current implementation with those from the previous year's course, which used a conventional forum without analytics enhancements. Objective 4: Through the two iterations of DBR, the project generated actionable design principles for integrating learning analytics into course forums. Key insights include: ontology refinement is crucial for ensuring accurate peer matching in large-scale learning environments; balancing machine-driven assistance with peer interactions requires careful scaffolding and explanation to gain student trust ; instructor dashboards for anomaly detection should be adaptive to avoid excessive or unnecessary interventions. These findings contribute to deeper understandings about designing AI-enhanced educational tools that support adaptive learning in large classrooms.

24604821.label: Major findings and research outcome
24604821.value: Upon implementing the analytics-enhanced course forum, the study found significant impacts on students' academic performance, collaborative learning, and course satisfaction (Dai et al., 2024). Regarding student performance in engineering design thinking, the students in the enhanced forum, compared to those in conventional forums, demonstrated a higher ability to understand user needs (Empathize) (t(591) = 6.19, p < .001), more effectively define problems (t(591) = 4.61, p < .001), and generate creative ideas (Ideate) (t(591) = 7.96, p < .001). These findings indicate that structured question-helper matching facilitated deeper engagement in problem-solving, allowing students to articulate their thoughts more effectively and explore a broader range of solutions. However, the forum had a more limited impact on the Prototype (t(591) = 1.64, p > .05) and Test (t(591) = 2.40, p < .05) phases of design thinking. These findings suggest that while the forum effectively supported early-stage problem-solving, further refinements may be needed to enhance prototype development and testing practices within the learning environment. Beyond design thinking, students in the analytics-enhanced forum reported significantly higher collaborative learning (t(591) = 5.73, p < .001). Additionally, course satisfaction was notably higher in the enhanced forum (t(591) = 4.19, p < .001), suggesting that students appreciated the adaptive support mechanisms and structured help-seeking process enabled by the forum. From the qualitative investigation, students reported faster response times and improved interaction quality due to the peer-matching system. The analytics-enhanced forum ensured relevant peer matches, leading to more meaningful discussions. Additionally, the forum exposed students to diverse perspectives, enriching their design thinking process through varied peer insights. Instructors also benefited from analytics-driven alerts, allowing timely interventions without manual monitoring. However, challenges emerged. Some students initially distrusted peer support, preferring immediate responses from the teaching assistants or instructors. The instructor intervention system initially flagged excessive alerts, later refined to reduce false positives. Despite these hurdles, refinements ensured effective adoption, demonstrating the forum’s potential for improving adaptive help-seeking and collaborative learning in large college courses.

24604821.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24604821.value: The next phase of research will explore the integration of large language models (LLMs), generative AI, and AI tutors to further enhance adaptive online academic help-seeking. The goal is to establish a multi-layered support system that seamlessly integrates AI assistance, peer support, and instructor interventions, ensuring that students receive timely and contextually relevant help. This layered approach will incorporate LLM-powered AI tutors to provide instant, adaptive guidance, assisting students with explanations, problem-solving, and content generation. AI-driven peer-matching and scaffolding mechanisms will ensure that students connect with relevant peers for collaborative learning, enhancing knowledge exchange. Additionally, the anomaly detection system will be further refined to trigger instructor interventions only when necessary, preventing over-reliance on AI while ensuring expert guidance where needed. Future research will focus on prototyping and evaluating this hybrid model, examining its impact on learning outcomes, engagement, and trust in AI-mediated academic help-seeking. The integration of AI tutors alongside peer and instructor support holds significant potential to improve scalability, efficiency, and personalized learning in large college courses, contributing to the broader evolution of AI-enhanced education.

24604821.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24604821.value: In large college classes, students often struggle to find the right help when they need it. Traditional online discussion forums allow students to ask questions, but responses can be slow, unorganized, and sometimes unhelpful. This research project aimed to improve online academic help-seeking by developing a structured course forum that uses a ontology-based recommender system and an anomaly detection algorithm to connect students with the best available support—whether from peers or instructors. The forum included a smart matching system that directed student questions to knowledgeable peers and an alert system that notified instructors when their intervention was needed. Results showed that students who used this system had better learning experiences, engaged in deeper discussions, and collaborated more effectively. Looking ahead, the project will further refine the peer-matching system and enhance instructor intervention strategies to improve response quality and timeliness. The structured approach—combining peer learning and instructor guidance—will help students get the right support at the right time, improving their learning efficiency and problem-solving skills. The findings from this research contribute to creating more responsive and effective learning environments that can be used in large university courses and beyond.
