24607321.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24607321.value: Zoroastrianism, while still a lived religion today, sees its practitioners as small in number, and increasingly scattered around the globe. Indian Zoroastrians, Parsis, are known in India for their wide spread philanthropy as well as the endurance of the traditional Zoroastrian mortuary practice of dokhmenashini, wherein the corpse is placed in large towers to be eaten by vultures and other carrion birds. This funerary practice of excarnation, has been consistently practiced by the majority of the community in Bombay-Mumbai as one of the most important Zoroastrian rituals to be performed. The towers and the mortuary infrastructure are supported through communal giving and the instrument of the charitable trust. As merchant trade and the British Empire brought Parsis to settle in various entrepots, they brought with them these funerary rites, which actually established many early forms of communal associations in the diaspora. While many settlements (Hong Kong, Delhi) moved toward cemeteries to bury the dead where excarnation was unviable, the existing literature on Zoroastrian funerals, continues to focus solely on dokhmenashini, and hence there is no scholarship on the ritual adaptations performed with burials and other alternatives. In contrast, this project broadens the focus and wishes to ethnographically investigate the practices associated with cemetery burials and a very recent move to cremation, as well as the finance supporting these alternate mortuary infrastructures. Due to the unviability of excarnation in the present even the Parsis in Mumbai are now moving away from dokhmenashini and seeking alternatives. This research will investigate how this transition away from millennia old ritual practice is not simply due to the reduced viability of excarnation outside of a few places, but also due to the newly acquired financial and political strength of diaspora groups particularly Hong Kong and the UK within the global Zoroastrian community. The research aims to produce two peer-reviewed journal articles as well as a book proposal to be submitted to a prestigious university press. 瑣羅亞斯德教（Zoroastrianism）雖然在今天仍然是一個活生生的宗教，但其信徒數量很少，而且越來越分散在全球各地。印度的瑣羅亞斯德教徒巴斯人（Parsis）在印度以其廣泛的慈善事業，以及喪葬實踐的持續而聞名——在這一被稱為dokhmenashini的儀式中，屍體被放置在大塔中，供禿鷹和其他腐肉鳥類食用。孟買（Bombay-Mumbai）的大多數社群一直將這種喪葬習俗作為最重要的瑣羅亞斯德教儀式之一來進行。塔樓和殓葬基礎設施由公共捐贈和慈善信託工具支持。隨著商人貿易和大英帝國將巴斯人帶到各個轉口港定居，他們帶來了這些喪葬儀式，因而實際上在散居地建立了許多早期形式的社區協會。雖然在許多dokhmenashini不可行的定居點（香港、德里），巴斯人轉向以墓地埋葬死者，但是現有的瑣羅亞斯德教喪禮文獻仍然只關注 dokhmenashini，因此缺乏關於以埋葬和其他替代方式進行的適應性喪禮儀式的研究。 相比之下，本研究擴大了關注範圍，希望從民族誌角度考察與墓地埋葬及非常近期才出現的火葬相關的實踐，以及支持這些替代性殮葬基礎設施的資金。由於dokhmenashini的不可行，即使是在孟買的巴斯人，現時也正在尋求替代方案。本研究將考察這種數千年的古老儀式實踐的轉變——這不是簡單基於dokhmenashini（在除少數幾個地方以外）的可行性的降低，亦與在全球瑣羅亞斯德教社群中，尤其是香港及英國的僑民群體所新近獲得的金融與政治實力相關。該研究旨在產出兩篇同行評審的期刊文章以及一份提交給著名大學出版社的書籍提案。

24607321.label: Realisation of objectives
24607321.value: One overarching obstacle to the realization of the research objects was the severity and duration of the Covid-19 pandemic. While the effects of the pandemic were part of the research objectives themselves, the realities of government travel regulations and health safety of PI and interlocutors both in Hong Kong and India were major concerns and caused significant delays to the project undertaking. As such very little fieldwork was able to be completed outside of Hong Kong for over one year due to the travel restrictions. The approval of two 6-month extensions was greatly appreciated. I will address the objectives in the following sections: Objective 1. I had to first collect data on the existing practices of dokhmenashini, where the corpse is interred in large towers and the flesh eaten by carrion birds like vultures. Even with funerary ritual alternatives, this practice remains the preferred practice for Zoroastrians when and where it is available. This fieldwork was conducted in Mumbai, India, one of the few remaining sites of dokhmenashini in the world. The fieldwork included site visits, interviews with priests, as well as lay practioners. From my research trips and online research, I am now able to map the availability of each different funerary alternative across India, and in many sites of the Zoroastrian diaspora. The rituals within each funerary choice are slightly different due to the historical specificity of migration patterns in the diaspora. One critical issue is the availability of priests in each site. For example, in Hong Kong, where burial and cremation are available, there is only one priest and no corpse bearers. Hence, lay Zoroastrians have to fulfill these roles and as such shifts in considerations of ritual purity and pollution do occur. Objective 2. I have published one article on charity and ritual practice. I have given many talks that are now being written up and will be submitted as articles and be a part of my second book project, entitled, Necrofinance: Death and the Diaspora, which examines the role of law and philanthropy in supporting funerary infrastructure, what I conceptualize as necrofinance. As this research traces the Inter-Asian networks of such necrofinance between Bombay-Mumbai, Hong Kong, and the rest of the Zoroastrian diaspora, it promises to deepen our understanding of how religious rituals of giving become a transnational idiom of placemaking. It will be one of the first texts to research and analyze all three funerary options of Zoroastrian death practices. Objective 3. During the course of my research, I also published my first book which relates the importance of charities and the technology of the charitable trust in managing and shaping Parsi (Indian Zoroastrian) life and death (Vevaina 2023). My research for this ECS project has deepened my understanding of the role of charitable giving and ritual itself, both in terms of ritual performance and ritual space. All of the Zoroastrian ritual spaces visited for fieldwork were managed by charities or religious corporations which also come under the umbrella of charities. All ritual spaces themselves were founded, built and supported by charitable giving, either on a small scale through communal subscriptions or on a large scale by single large donations. Their continued maintenance as critical sites of ritual heavily depends on the ongoing donations of community members as well as the sound financial investments made by the trustees of these charities. I found that ritual spaces in India are under threat from spatial encroachment, lack of funds for maintenance, as well as becoming defunct in areas where there is low Zoroastrian demography. The ritual spaces in the diaspora, were newer, smaller and had much more financial support, often coming from Hong Kong. Objective 4. & 5. In many of the sites visited in the diaspora (London, San Francisco, Southern California, Singapore) I learned through interviews and analysis of historical documents held at the charities that it was funds from Hong Kong at several historic moments that have been key to the survival of these diaspora groups’ settlement and continued ritual practice. From trustee interviews in Hong Kong as well as financial ledgers, I learned that the community was very conservative in giving on finishing funds to a project which had to prove that it was well on its way. Doing field interviews in Singapore and viewing historical documents, I learned that it was funds from Hong Kong in the early 20th Century that allowed the community to settle. The first Parsi known in Singapore convinced the Parsi traders in Canton to buy a burial ground in Singapore. After raising funds, a plot was bought at Shenton Way near the harbor what is today the banking district. As the Singaporean government needed the plot for urban expansion, the Parsis were given a compensation and the cemetery moved. It was these compensation funds that later supported the community, but all stemmed from the first purchase of a cemetery plot with funds from Hong Kong. Objective 6. This objective was analyzed through each field research trip both in India, Hong Kong, and the rest of the diaspora through interviews and research on government policies. In each site, the respective government authorities took diverse measures to manage funerals of the dead, especially those that were infected with the virus. In India, regulations were extremely strict and the traditional and most popular funerary choice of dokhmenashini was banned for a period of time and all deceased had to be cremated. This led to a petition by some Zoroastrians to the Indian Government to allow the traditional funerary practice to continue which was later allowed when the pandemic threat had decreased. Sites with extant cremation and burial did not have much regulation on the form of funeral but much regulation on the practices of mourners who had to remain absent or had to follow strict social distancing protocols while at a funeral. Priests as well had to be trained to follow social distancing as well as wear appropriate protective equipment. This period was noted as being especially difficult for mourning family members as they often could not follow the communal practices with others such as joint prayer, funerary meals, etc. Apart from the funerary regulations, the pandemic exposed the government’s reliance on Zoroastrian charities to fulfill many other welfare tasks in India. For example, all vaccine drives, grocery and medical provisions were taken over by charities during the pandemic. Objective 7. This analysis came from interviews with priests, charity officials, and lay Zoroastrians in each fieldwork site. The biggest finding was the intensity of the regulations in India with the ban on dokhmenashini. All sites had minor changes due to social distancing and other pandemic protocols that diminished the communal practices at funerals which are so critical to grieving mourners. I attended two funerals that were on Zoom with varied ritual procedures due to social distancing. The biggest change brought more implicitly was the further familiarizing of the majority of Indian Zoroastrians with the new funerary alternative of cremation which many still believe is irreligious, as the only option during the pandemic in Mumbai. After the pandemic many have returned to dokhmenashini but the cremation option has become a bit more common choice.

24607321.label: Major findings and research outcome
24607321.value: - each of the three funerary options: dokhmenashini (sky burial), burial, and cremation were all robust and existing in various sites of Zoroastrian life around the world. - the research showed that historically the establishment and financing of funerary grounds was key to the first geographic and residential settlement of the community, showed critically by the cases of Mumbai, Delhi, Nagpur and Singapore. The PI has further developed the concept of necrofinance from this research. - The funerary options available in each site were based on factors such as 1) history and duration of settlement; 2) level of conservativeness of priests and lay Zoroastrians; 3) government regulations wherein some only allow one option for example, burial in Singapore. - while cremation was mandated during Covid 19, Zoroastrians in Mumbai quickly returned to dokhmenashini when it became available again, even if seen as not working due to lack of vultures - through death ritual we can see the new contours of community boundary making especially in terms of access to rituals for Zoroastrians that marry out the community, non-Zoroastrian spouses and other family members, and children of intermarried Zoroastrians. Each research site had a slightly different set of access rules depending on the historical strength of more ritually conservative priests and members. - while the Indian Government had banned dokhmenashini in India during Covid, they left all implementation for death rituals and other social services to the main charities that manage ritual spaces showing the importance of charity groups in community management and vaccine implementation - North American Zoroastrians seem to prefer cremation and burial equally, with funerary choice based on personal preference and not on ritual belief. The researched communities did not have chosen funerary practice as a cleavage within the community. Either choice was considered valid and neither irreligious. Non-Zoroastrian family members were welcomed at the either funerary option if the family wished it. - the availability and level of conservativeness of priests was a critical factor in funerary options in each site. When only one priest is available, lay Zoroastrians fill in shifting the purity and pollution boundaries. - Hong Kong Zoroastrian charities have become critical for the support of the diaspora and Zoroastrian life in India. This has been true historically with the case of Mumbai in the late nineteenth century through today, and also Singapore, San Francisco, and Southern California.

24607321.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24607321.value: The PI has developed the concept of necrofinance, which connects death and funerals to their financial infrastructure. This concept will be developed and expanded in the PI’s second book as well as be applicable to the study of death in many other contexts. This research has much potential for further investigation in a few directions. Firstly after a very successful Workshop on Death, Funerals, and Ghosts in December 2024 at Chinese University, workshop participants have decided to host another workshop in Fall 2025 to focus more death care workers across Asia. This brings the research to shift from funerals and finance to work on care and labour by the actors in the funerary industry. The PI has applied for funds from CUHK Faculty of Arts to support this endeavour. The PI will also teach a course in the Anthropology Department on Death and Ritual which will showcase much of this research as well as develop methodologies for the study of death, ritual, funerals and finance. Focusing this course on death in Asia will also deepen the Inter-Asia perspectives on how death rituals and finance are another avenue of historical and contemporary connection across Asia.

24607321.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24607321.value: Having a good death is critically important to most people around the globe. For contemporary Zoroastrians this has become more complicated with new ritual alternatives to their ancient funerary tradition of dokhmenashini, or sky burial. This traditional practice was endangered during the COVID-19 pandemic. In different places in the Zoroastrian diaspora the communities have developed other alternatives like burial and now cremation. This research project has investigated various sites in India and in the global diaspora to see how this micro-minority religious community is dealing with ritual adaptation in its death ceremonies. The research showed the historical and contemporary significance of the Zoroastrian community in Hong Kong to the survival of other communities in the diaspora. By focusing on death ritual and the infrastructure that supports it (priests, space, etc) this research has shown the importance of charity within the community to keep traditional practices alive as well as develop new alternatives for Zoroastrians to have what they consider a good death in the contemporary world.

24607921.label: Project Title(Chinese)
24607921.value: 隨視啟動的輸入增顯形電腦輔助閱讀對第二語言詞匯搭配學習效果的研究

24607921.label: Project Objectives
24607921.value: As well documented, the ability to comprehend and use collocations accurately and appropriately is crucial to functioning as a competent and communicatively proficient second language user (Saito, 2020; Siyanova-Chanturia & Martinez, 2014). However, L1 Chinese speakers have been reported to suffer from persistent difficulty in acquiring English collocations (Fan, 2009; Liang, 2015; Lu, 2016), underscoring the need for an effective pedagogical approach to assist teaching and learning of collocations. Textual modification such as input enhancement has been proposed as a potential way to facilitate the learning of collocations from reading (Sonbul & Schmitt, 2013), but empirical evidence is only scanty. In addition, amidst the rapid development of technology and the growing importance of online learning and digital literacy, technology-enhanced and adaptive learning has received increasing attention in the field of second language studies. Recently, within the gaze-contingent paradigm, researchers began exploring whether the eye-tracking technology can be used to trigger learners' attention to target linguistic constructions and thereby promote implicit and incidental language learning from computer-mediated reading (Révész et al, 2019). Against this background, the proposed research project attempts to examine the impact of gaze-contingent input enhancement on learning of collocations from computer-mediated L2 reading. To be more specific, the primary objective of this project is to investigate: (a) whether highlighting and gaze-contingent highlighting can trigger learners’ attention to target collocations, as reflected in learners’ eye-movements and stimulated recall comments; and (b) whether highlighting and gaze-contingent highlighting can promote development in receptive and productive knowledge of the target collocations. Considering the importance of language learning aptitude in L2 learning (e.g., Li, 2015) as well as the centrality of working memory in L2 reading (e.g., Harrington & Sawyer, 1992) and L2 learning (e.g., Miyake & Friedman, 1998), the present study further aims to explore: (c) whether learners’ language learning aptitude moderates the impact of highlighting and gaze-contingent highlighting; and (d) whether learners’ working memory capacity moderates the impact of highlighting and gaze-contingent highlighting. The novelty of the proposed study is to explore the pedagogical potential of the gaze-contingency paradigm (Révész et al., 2019) in promoting the acquisition of collocations in the context of computer-mediated L2 reading. The proposed research is also among the first to (a) examine the pedagogical value of input enhancement on learning of L2 collocations (e.g., Choi, 2017; Sonbul & Schmitt, 2013; Szudarski & Carter, 2016), (b) triangulate learners’ eye-movement data with their stimulated recall comments (e.g., Jung & Révész, 2018; Peters, 2012), and (c) incorporate both input-based and individual-difference factors as potential moderating variables for a nuanced understanding of L2 collocational learning (e.g., Boers et al., 2017; Pellicer-Sánchez, 2017). The findings of this study will be presented at international conferences in the field of Applied Linguistics and Second Language Acquisition (SLA), such as the American Association for Applied Linguistics (AAAL) and the European Second Language Association (EuroSLA). At the same time, to reach a wider audience, two articles will be published in peer-reviewed journals, such as Applied Linguistics and Language Teaching Research. In close alignment with the PI’s primary research interest, findings from the present project are expected to generate the following implications. Theoretically speaking, this study will make a meaningful contribution to the existing literature on the learning of L2 collocations from reading, especially in relation to the impact of input enhancement. On a methodological front, this study will confirm the usefulness of eye-tracking technology as an innovative, unobtrusive, and powerful research tool in examining learners’ online reading processes, when triangulated with stimulated recall comments. In addition, within the gaze-contingency paradigm, this study will also extend the line of research on the potential of eye-tracking technology as an instructional tool. Last but not least, the findings of this study will generate pedagogical guidance to language teachers and curriculum/ textbook developers with respect to how to design and manipulate computer-mediated L2 reading materials to better support collocational learning.

24607921.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24607921.value: Collocations are strings of words that habitually appear together to convey a message as in “make a bed” or “bumpy ride” (Cowie, 1981). It is generally accepted that having a good command of collocations is crucial to functioning as a proficient language user (Saito, 2020). However, second language (L2) learners experience persistent difficulty in acquiring collocations. A likely reason for this is that, even when exposed to collocations, learners often process the words in them as separate entities rather than a single unit (Tsai, 2015). In order to address this issue, the proposed study aims to investigate whether input enhancement, through making collocations salient through typographical manipulation, can promote L2 learning in the context of computer-mediated L2 reading. The novelty of the study is that it tests whether input enhancement, achieved via adaptive gaze-contingency, can increase L2 development. Gaze-contingency will be operationalized as using eye-tracking technology as an instructional tool, highlighting collocations in response to learners’ eye movements while reading. Frequency of target collocations and learners’ working memory capacity will be included as moderating variables. Participants will be 75 undergraduate students in Hong Kong, whose first language (L1) is Cantonese. They will read two English texts that contain six adjective-pseudonoun collocations (e.g., “old holter”), under one of the following conditions: control (reading unmodified texts), input enhancement (target collocations highlighted), and gaze-contingent input enhancement (target collocations highlighted when eye-fixation is made on them). In one of the reading texts, the target collocations will appear five times, whereas in the other, two times. While reading, participants’ eye-movements will be captured using an eye-tracker. After reading, the participants will respond to unannounced true-and-false reading comprehension statements and complete a set of posttests that measure receptive and productive knowledge of the target collocations. Also, a subset of participants from each group will participate in a stimulated recall session, where they will be asked to recall their thoughts while reading, prompted by the recordings of their eye-movements. One week later, the participants will take the posttests again, and complete working memory tasks. Results obtained through mixed effects modelling and qualitative analyses will inform theoretical models describing cognitive processes entailed in collocation learning through reading, contribute to advances in research methodology through combining eye-movement data with stimulated recall comments, and yield pedagogical implications for supporting collocational learning in computer-mediated contexts.

24611921.label: Project Objectives
24611921.value: Identification of the tax challenges arising from the digitalisation of the economy for the Chinese government in relation to both foreign businesses operating inside China and Chinese enterprises operating inside and outside China, by examining whether the current tax rules (for both direct and indirect taxation) are sufficient to protect the related tax revenue and whether there is a need for specialised tax rules for taxing digitalised businesses; Comparative and critical analysis of multilateral and unilateral measures that have been proposed or adopted by different jurisdictions for tackling the tax challenges of digitalisation, especially the measures adopted by jurisdictions showing similarities with China in respect of the domestic e-commerce market and established digitalised industries; Proposal of a set of appropriate tax rules to enable the Chinese government to properly tax the digitalised economy and comply with international commitments while maintaining the attractiveness of the Chinese market and competitiveness of Chinese enterprises.

24611921.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24611921.value: The development of information and communications technology (ICT) has significantly changed how business is conducted. China has also undergone rapid digitalisation of its various economic sectors, but has not enacted any special digital tax rules in this respect. This research will attempt to identify a suitable taxation policy from the perspective of China. Digitalisation expands the reach of business operations far beyond national boundaries. Nevertheless, both digitalisation and globalisation confront national tax authorities with significant challenges. In regard to international taxation in particular, these challenges have been overwhelming, because the allocation of taxing rights on cross-border economic activity relies on an explicit physical connection between the taxable subject and the taxing jurisdiction. The difficulty of properly taxing multinational enterprises (MNEs) has been exacerbated by the increasingly digitalised economy. International organisations and individual states have therefore been forced to take action. The first part of the project will examine the current tax regime in relation to the digitalised economy, in particular cross-border businesses based in China from two perspectives, namely inbound and outbound digitalised economic activity. The business models reviewed include China-based enterprises investing in domestic and overseas e-commerce markets and foreign enterprises doing business in and with China. This indicates that the challenges in regard to taxation could be manifold, involving direct taxation (individual and enterprise income taxation) and indirect taxation (value-added tax, excise tax and so on). The goal is to establish what challenges the Chinese tax authorities face when attempting to tax digitalised economic activity. The second part of the research will use comparative legal analysis to investigate the special tax rules or proposals that have been adopted or suggested by international and regional organisations and individual jurisdictions to tackle the tax challenges posed by the digitalised economy. The comparison will focus on jurisdictions that share similarities with China in terms of the development level of the digitalised business sector. The analysis will consider the specific economic and taxation situation in the examined jurisdictions to analyse their perceived issues and countermeasures. Using the findings of the first two parts, the third part will consider how China could most efficiently and effectively tax the digitalised economy. The research aims to propose a suitable plan for the government to properly exercise its taxing power, at the same time complying with relevant international treaty obligations as well as maintaining the vitality of the domestic market and competitiveness of the digitalised industry. 現代社會信息和通信技術的發展極大地改變了商業的運作模式。中國經濟的各行各業也經歷了快速數字化發展，但尚未針對經濟數字化製定任何特殊的稅收規則。本研究將嘗試從中國的角度出發探討相應的稅收政策。經濟的數字化使得商業運營的範圍不再受到國界或地理位置的限制。然而，經濟的數字化和全球化都為各個國家的稅務機關帶來重大挑戰。特別是在國際稅收的管理方面，這些挑戰是巨大的，因為跨境經濟活動的徵稅權的傳統分配方式依賴應稅主體和稅收管轄區之間的明確實體性的聯繫。而日益數字化的經濟加劇了對跨國企業適當徵稅的困難。因此，在國際組織和不同國家的層面都提出了新的應對方法。該研究項目的第一部分將從兩個角度，即對內和對外數字化經濟活動，審查與數字化經濟相關的現行的中國稅收制度。待研究的商業模式包括投資國內外電子商務市場的中國企業和在中國做生意的外國企業。這意味著數字經濟化對稅收方面的挑戰可能是多方面的，包括直接稅收（個人和企業所得稅）和間接稅收（增值稅、消費稅等）的問題。這一部分的研究目標是確定中國稅務機關在嘗試對數字化經濟活動徵稅時面臨哪些挑戰。該研究的第二部分將使用比較法律分析的方法來研究國際和區域組織以及不同國家和地區在應對數字化經濟帶來的稅收挑戰時，已採用或建議的特殊稅收規則。這一部分的比較研究將側重於在數字化經濟的發展水平方面與中國相當的國家或地區。該研究的第三部分將基於前兩部分的研究結果，探討中國如何有效地對數字化經濟進行徵稅管理。該研究旨在為政府建議適當的稅收政策和規則，一方面有利於稅務機關適當行使稅收權力，同時可以使中國遵守相關國際條約義務，以及保持國內市場的活力和數字化產業的競爭力。

24614521.label: Project Title(Chinese)
24614521.value: 語言和電子學習：關於香港青年數字素養及資源不平等分配的調查

24614521.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24614521.value: The recent shift to online learning in Hong Kong because of the COVID-19 pandemic has laid bare a tremendous digital divide. One in 10 primary and secondary school students do not own an electronic device and 40% have to share devices with family members. These issues of unequal access and connectivity impact not only the capacity of students to participate actively in online classes but also the extent to which they develop digital literacies that enable self-directed learning. Dispelling the myth that all youth are “digital natives”, this research recognizes that the acquisition of valued digital literacies depends on access not only to material devices, but also to social, linguistic and semiotic resources. Mentors, peers, language resources and literacy tools shape the ways students participate in online spaces, locate and evaluate information on the internet where majority of content is in English. Despite the significance of language skills in developing digital literacies, majority of e-learning research in the context of Hong Kong tend to adopt quantitative methods that involve university students, and do not make connections to their unequal linguistic repertoires. To fill this gap, this qualitative research adopts a critical lens to compare and contrast the in- and out-of-school digital practices of 12 secondary students from an aided Chinese medium of instruction school in Tin Shui Wai and a direct subsidy scheme English medium of instruction school in Mong Kok. Through interviews of students, teachers, and parents, observations of digital practices, and the collection of digital artefacts, this connective case study examines to what extent students with unequal access to material, linguistic and social resources develop different digital literacies. Recognizing that students will have different levels of English competence, it explores how this difference shapes the way they use these technologies to access knowledge and develop social networks. By focusing on these issues in the context of English Language Education in Hong Kong, this research will draw conclusions that can reshape educational policy, curricula, and pedagogy. A critical awareness of how students can be socialized into different digital practices can challenge teachers’ assumptions of what these “digital natives” already know and enable the design of more inclusive teaching approaches. Understanding these gaps will help identify the digital genres, online conventions and language strategies that comprise the communicative competence Hong Kong students will need to participate agentively in a globally networked world. 最近，由於新冠肺炎的流行，香港轉向了在線學習，這無疑暴露了一個巨大的數字鴻溝：每十個中小學學生中就有一個沒有電子設備的學生，導致百分之四十的學生不得不與家庭成員共享設備。這些不平等的訪問和連接問題不僅影響了學生積極參與在線課程的能力，而且還影響到他們發展數字素養的程度。培養數字素養，實現自主學習是香港的當務之急，本研究破除了“所有年輕人都是數字原住民”的神話，並進一步提出獲得有價值的數字素養不僅取決於對物質設備的使用，而且還取決於對社會、語言和符號資源的使用。導師、同齡人、語言資源和識字工具等等共同塑造了學生參與的在線空間、定位和評估互聯網上的信息的方式，而其中大部分內容都以英文為承載媒介。 儘管語言技能在發展數字讀寫能力方面具有重要意義，但香港背景下的大多數電子學習研究都傾向於採用定量研究方法，儘管這些研究讓廣大的大學生參與其中，卻並沒有將個體間存在差異的不平等的語言變體與其研究結果聯繫起來。為了填補這一空白，本定性研究採用批判性的角度比較和對比了天水圍的資助中文教學學校和旺角的直接資助計劃英文教學學校的十二名中學生的校內和校外的數字實踐。本聯繫性案例研究通過採訪學生、教師和家長，觀察他們的數字實踐成果，探討了在何種程度上那些在物質、語言上得不到平等機會的學生在多大程度上發展了不同的數字素養。認識到學生有不同程度的英語能力，本研究更進一步探討了這種差異如何影響他們使用這些技術來獲取知識和發展社交網絡的方式。 通過關注香港英語語言教育背景下的這些問題，這項研究將從中得出結論以重塑當下的教育政策、課程和教學法，從而提高廣大教育界對學生如何在不同的數字實踐中進行社會化的批判意識。本研究旨在挑戰教師對這些數字原生代的現有假設，幫助其設計出更具包容性的教學方法，因為了解教師認知和實際數字實踐情況的差距將有助於確定數字體裁、在線溝通慣例和語言策略，而這些構成了香港學生所需的交際能力，從而進一步提高香港學生在全球網絡化世界中的積極參與。

24619021.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24619021.value: This research analyzes the history of radical social movements established and supported by transnational ecumenical networks in colonial Hong Kong during the 1960s and 1990s. The three selected Christian-based non-governmental organizations (NGOs) to be examined are the Tsuen Wan Ecumenical Social Service Centre (TWESSC) active between 1973 and 1997, the Hong Kong Christian Industrial Committee (CIC) founded in 1966, and the Society for Community Organization (SoCO) founded in 1971. All three NGOs were founded by progressive Protestants and Roman Catholics with the expressed purpose of empowering the poor; while a number of social and economic issues were addressed, housing and labour concerns were paramount. Their progressive social actions for the betterment of the poor were largely influenced by the larger ecumenical Urban Industrial Mission network in Asia and intellectually influenced by the American radical activist Saul Alinsky, the father of grassroots community organizing in the world. These three NGOs created action space that challenged existing neoliberal government policies and were in turn formally identified as pressure groups by the colonial government in the mid-1970s. For this historical study, some important questions are addressed. First, what was the theological rationale of these ecumenical organizations, both international and domestic, to encourage radical social movements in colonial Hong Kong (HK)? Second, to what extent and what forms did transnational ecumenical church networks support the development of radical social movements in late-colonial era? Third, how did local progressive activists adopt and re-adjust social action practices in the context of colonial governance? Fourth, political stability was of paramount importance to the colonial government, so what practices were employed to de-legitimize these three NGOs which simply viewed their work as moral opportunities to improve the lives of the poor? This research adopts a multidisciplinary approach. Within the field of Hong Kong Studies, this research engages the disciplines of political studies, sociology, human geography, social work, and theology. 本研究計劃旨在探究跨國性的基督教普世教會網絡如何有助促成和發展1960至1990年代殖民時期的香港基進社會運動歷史，所選取的三個與基督教有關連的非政府組織分別是：荃灣合一社會服務中心(1973–1997)、香港基督教工業委員會(1966年成立)和社區組織協會(1971年成立)。以上三個機構均是由進取的基督新教徒和天主教徒成立，旨在為貧窮人充權，關注社會民生議題，其中以房屋和勞工權益為主。他們以基進的社會行動改善貧窮人的福祉為使命，乃受著亞洲普世教會網絡城市工業使命和美國基進社會運動家阿林斯基，世界基層社區組織之父所薰陶和影響。有趣的是，這三個機構開創的香港社會行動空間，正好挑戰新自由主義的殖民政府施政，在1970年代末更被認定為壓力團體。我們希望透過這歷史研究回應以下問題：(一) 這些組織帶有什麼神學理念去推展基進的社會行動﹖是受國際影響還是本地因素所致﹖(二)探看普世教會網絡如何影響和支持香港基進社會行動的發展。(三)在面對香港特殊的殖民管治下，本地基進行動者如何吸收和調適社會行動的策略。(四)當三個機構高舉改善貧窮人權益的道德旗幟時，殖民政府如何打擊它們的合法性，以維護政治穩定性﹖在香港研究的基調下，本歷史研究連繫多種學科的研究成果包括政治學、社會學、人文地理學、社會工作和神學。

24619521.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24619521.value: More than 380,000 foreign domestic workers (FDWs) work in Hong Kong (HK), of which the majority are from the Philippines. The number is expected to increase continuously as the Hong Kong population is rapidly ageing. Previous surveys have found that the FDWs have poorer mental health compared to the general population in HK. However, there is a shortage of mental health interventions dedicated to them, not to mention evidence-based interventions. Nonetheless, some FDWs have made use of social media, specifically Facebook, to initiate peer-support groups for each other. Those groups are self-initiated and self-managed by FDWs and have gained wide popularity, especially when FDWs’ regular day-off gatherings in public places are restricted because of the social unrest or the COVID-19 pandemic. These bottom-up groups offer a promising, culturally sensitive, and low-cost intervention approach to help FDWs. However, their group dynamics, function mechanisms, and effects are not clear. By working together with members of one of the largest online peer-support groups for FDWs in HK, the proposed project aims to systematically map out Filipino domestic workers’ pathways of using those groups to address their mental health needs. The project adopts the Critical Theory paradigm to use the research as a means to empower disadvantaged people and co-construct new knowledge and a new intervention model. The project includes two studies; the first will use text mining and content analysis methods to identify FDWs’ mental health needs as expressed in the peer-support groups, and how those needs are being addressed by other peer members’ comments and replies. The second study will conduct in-depth interviews with around 50 members of the online peer-support groups. For each member, at least one more follow-up interview will be conducted about 12 months later to observe their experienced changes over time. The data collection and analysis of Study 2 will follow the grounded theory methodology. The project will provide crucial insights to conceptualize Filipino FDWs’ mental health needs and in what circumstances the online peer-support groups can (or cannot) address those needs. It will contribute to the trending research topics on co-creation of digital services and online peer-support. In addition, the project will demonstrate how co-creation can be actualized in a bottom-up fashion to pursue social inclusion and justice and add new knowledge to social service and social administration research.

24620421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24620421.value: 《論靈與字句》之研究及拉丁文、中文雙語對照版註譯 本研究項目旨在﹝一﹞對奧古斯丁的《論靈與字句》作處境與思想源流上的研究，從而提供一個較全面的框架去理解這本在第五世紀初柏拉糾爭議中至為重要的著作，以及﹝二﹞為 《論靈與字句》作翻譯及註釋，將成果以拉丁文、中文雙語對照版呈現於漢語世界 成書於公元412/413年的《論靈與字句》是一本對西方神學及哲學影響深遠的經典之作。在此著作中奧古斯丁為人的自由與上帝的預定之間的張力，提供了一個揉合了聖經及哲學的解釋，其觀點塑造了整個羅馬天主教以及更正教這兩大基督教傳統，影響深遠。雖然如此重要，此書的獨特性在以往的研究未獲重視，歸根究底，乃學術界對奧古斯丁公元410至413年這段期間還未有作深入探究。有見及此，本研究會以奧氏這段時期約48篇書信及38篇講章為文獻基礎，仔細分析這段期間的思潮及事件怎樣塑造《論靈與字句》的論點，並會特別關注奧古斯丁思想中多納徒主義與伯拉糾主義兩者存在著怎樣的關係。這個分析不單會為奧古斯丁研究帶來新的切入點，它也能為基督教對自由與命運這哲學命題的理解之起源﹝奧古斯丁與伯拉糾主義﹞，提供一個堅實的處境分析。 本研究項目也會對《論靈與字句》作註譯。這將會是《論靈與字句》的第一本中文翻譯註釋本，同時也會是在漢語世界第一本西方經典的拉丁文、中文雙語對照版。其目的將這經典引進漢語世界，並透過雙語版本，提升漢語讀者的拉丁文能力，讓學者、學生、以及大眾能在中文翻譯的輔助之下，親身閱讀西方拉丁文經典，從而促進中西文化的對話與交流。

24621821.label: Project Title(Chinese)
24621821.value: 中央控制和地方發展如何協調？ 關於中國地方政府三種職業流動機制的模型和一個案例分析

24621821.label: Project Objectives
24621821.value: Develop a NEW theoretical framework to understand how centralized political control and effective local governance can be reconciled in China through the lens of personnel management practices in local governments. This theoretical framework includes: o A NOVEL four-cell typology of positions based on two dimensions of position characteristics: local knowledge stock and spatial transfer prospect; o A NEW model of three mobility regimes summarizing heterogeneous career patterns, incentives, and economic influences across the four types of positions in Chinese local governments. This theoretical framework contributes to comprehending the distinct roles of local bureaucrats in different mobility regimes in preserving communist political order in China against the backdrop of power decentralization and market expansion. Conduct a mixed-method case study to provide empirical evidence for evaluating the validity of the proposed theoretical framework. This research will have three inter-connected studies: o Study 1: Use unsupervised K-Means clustering method to classify elite positions in local governments based on their supply flow and exit flow, and identify the three mobility regimes in local governments. This analysis will draw on a UNIQUE dataset that documents mobility records of all elite bureaucrats across all jurisdictions in the entire Jiangsu province; o Study 2: Conduct panel data analysis to examine the heterogeneous economic influences of bureaucrats in different mobility regimes, using the same Jiangsu bureaucratic dataset and an additional self-compiled dataset of socio-economic indicators of all jurisdictions in Jiangsu over the same period; o Study 3: Carry out an ethnographic study to inspect career incentives of bureaucrats in different mobility regimes. The ethnographic study is necessary because career incentives would be hard to be assessed using quantitative methods. Prior studies usually analyze career incentives by examining the promotion criteria of local bureaucrats. This approach, however, leads to controversies more than yielding consensus findings, because there may be reverse causation between performance and connections. Based on the identified mobility regimes across positions, the ethnographic study will inspect variations of bureaucrats’ incentives across different regimes by observing their interactions when formulating economic policies and conducting economic activities, paying special attention to their dynamics when there are controversial economic policies or activities. These dynamics can better reveal their actual incentives.

24621821.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24621821.value: China’s spectacular economic growth since the 1980s has contradicted much wisdom in the study of development and authoritarian regimes. It has also posed many theoretical and empirical paradoxes (Whyte 2009). One major paradox is how the Chinese state maintains centralized political control while also facilitating effective local governance to promote economic development. Against the backdrop of extensive power decentralization from the central to local governments, current studies have focused on the career incentives of local bureaucrats. This literature provides two dominant theoretical arguments: one emphasizing the meritocratic promotion principle, which motivates local bureaucrats to develop local economy; the other emphasizing the clientelist promotion principle, which maintains local bureaucrats’ political loyalty. These studies, however, do not provide a coherent theory compatible with all empirical facts related to the control-development paradox. Moreover, they all imply homogeneous career incentives within a local government. Following a sociological approach that examines communist political order through the lens of heterogeneous career mobility in state agencies, I propose a model of three mobility regimes in local governments. Each regime supports a different fundamental objective pursued by the state. Specifically, a loyalty-based regime ensures the obedience of high-level local leaders in following orders from above and supervising local practices; a performance-based regime promotes effective local governance and regional growth; and a stakeholder regime maintains a cluster of local stakeholders as informed actors who can effectively monitor government actions and policy makers. This theoretical model is represented by a four-cell typology of local government positions based on the local knowledge stock and the spatial transfer prospects of their general occupants. I also hypothesize the systematic variation of the position occupants’ career patterns, incentives, and capacities across these regimes. Empirical analyses will employ both quantitative and qualitative methods. For the quantitative analyses, I will (1) use data-driven clustering techniques to categorize positions in local governments based on their career mobility patterns, as specified in the theoretical typology, and identify their respective mobility regimes; and (2) examine the heterogeneous economic influence of bureaucrats in different mobility regimes by analyzing their replacement effects. These analyses will draw from a unique dataset that contains comprehensive mobility records of all major bureaucrats in Jiangsu Province between 1990 and 2010. Based on the identified mobility regimes across positions, an ethnographic study will be carried out to understand the variation of bureaucrats’ incentives across different regimes, which is difficult to be assessed using quantitative methods alone. 自 1980 年代以來中國經濟的快速增長與發展和專制政權研究中的許多理論相矛盾。它還提出了許多理論和經驗悖論（Whyte 2009）。一個主要的悖論是，中國政府如何在保持中央政治控制的同時保持有效的地方治理以促進經濟發展。改革開放以來，中央向地方政府廣泛下放權力。在此背景下，關於“控制-發展”悖論，當前的研究集中在地方官員的職業激勵上。這些文獻提供了兩個主要的理論論點：一個強調中國官僚體制內以經濟增長為政績的晉升原則，它激勵地方官員發展地方經濟；另一個強調官員庇護的晉升原則，它維持地方官員對上級的政治忠誠。然而，這些理論並不能完全解釋“控制-發展”悖論下的大量經驗事實。此外，它們都假設地方政府內部的職業激勵措施是同質的。在社會學領域，學者們在研究威權國家的政治秩序時，通常認為國家機構內部的職業流動是異質的。基於這個理論視角，我提出中國地方政府中存在三種不同的職業流動機制，而不同的流動機制支持了國家管理的不同目標。具體而言，以忠誠為基礎的機制確保地方高層領導服從上級命令並監督地方政策施行；以績效為基礎的機制促進有效的地方治理和區域發展；利益相關者機制將一群當地利益相關者作為知情參與者，他們可以有效地監督政府和政策制定者的行為。這三種流動機制在地方政府內的不同職位中有系統性的差異。基於地方政府內部不同職位在（1）地方知識儲量和（2）空間流動前景上的差異，我將它們分為四種類型，并對不同類型職業的流動模式、激勵方式、和官員影響力提出假設。實證分析將採用定量和定性相結合的方法。首先，對於定量分析，我將 (1) 使用聚類分析的方法，根據理論模型中的職業流動模式對地方政府的職位進行分類，並確定各自的流動機制； (2) 通過分析官員的更替效應，考察不同流動機制下官員對當地經濟影響的差異。這些定量分析將基於1990 年至 2010 年江蘇省大部份主要官僚的流動記錄。此外，在定量分析的基礎上，我將進行民族志研究，以了解不同流動機制的職位上官員激勵方式的差異。

24622121.label: Project Title(Chinese)
24622121.value: 香港公共房屋的中介空間：高密度城市與社交互動的數據導向分析

24622121.label: Project Objectives
24622121.value: To analyse and understand the spatial parameters of high-density urban in-between spaces that impact human experience and social interaction, through the application of a computational spatial analysis method, developed from existing methodologies for visibility graph analysis and network connectivity analysis. To document and understand the spatial and temporal distribution of social activities across a combined series of open spaces within a case study housing estate, through qualitative and quantitative observation studies and the spatial mapping and statistical analysis of their findings. Based on the findings of (1 and 2), compare the data about spatial qualities of estate spaces and their usage statistics, to formulate insights into which spatial qualities of in-between spaces can be correlated with different types of social interaction. 24622121.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24622121.value: As Hong Kong constructs increasingly high-density, high-rise public housing estates to increase land use efficiency, public in-between spaces are becoming more constrained, which impacts the quality of social relations, movements and daily practices of residents (Shelton et al. 2011). While there are several ecological and logistical benefits to building compact cities (Burgess 2002; Lau & Chiu 2004), researchers have identified increased risks of social pathologies, such as reduced health, family relations or social participation, related to poor planning of high-density urban environments (Tang et al. 2019). The Hong Kong Housing Authority has adopted new data-driven planning methodologies to improve micro-climates in estates (Ng 2010; Yeh & Yuen 2011), but there is a lack of knowledge around the sociological impact of spatially compressed, highly connected and overcrowded in-between spaces. Visibility and connectivity have been established as reliable parameters to predict movements and interactions in public spaces (Hillier & Hanson 1984; Batty 2001; Stamps 2005). Recent software and hardware improvements have enabled more detailed studies including visibility analysis in three-dimensions, which can offer a better understanding of people’s feeling of surveillance, privacy or control within urban spaces. These methods have been used to analyse building interiors (Lu & Ye 2017) and urban spaces (Suleiman et al. 2013; Lonergan & Hedley 2016; Kim et al. 2019), but not yet to analyse spaces for social interaction in residential neighbourhoods. This project will (A) adapt and develop methods for visibility and connectivity analysis, to identify morphological aspects that impact the visual perception of complex, three-dimensional in-between spaces in Hong Kong’s high-density housing estates. The study will then (B) employ field observation studies documenting co-presence and social activities, to understand the spatial and temporal distribution of interactions across a series of spaces. It will then (C) analyse correlations and formulate recommendations on how to improve the quality and social effectiveness of open spaces in public housing. This study will provide detailed, evidence-based insights into which attributes and configurations of urban in-between spaces provide comfort and opportunities for social activities, which can lead to increased social and community engagement. This knowledge can contribute to planning processes for new housing estates across Hong Kong, or in other international locations with similar high-density planning. It can contribute to Chapters 4 and 11 of Hong Kong’s Planning Standards and Guidelines (‘’Recreation, Open Space and Greening’’ and ‘’Urban Design Guidelines’’), and to the government planning framework ‘’HK2030+”, which aims towards more inclusive and supportive urban environments. 為提高土地使用效率，香港的公共房屋建築高度及密度有增無減。因此，公共中介空間受到了更多束縛，影響到市民日常外出及社交生活 (Shelton et al. 2011)。 雖然建造密集都市在生態及物流上有一定好處 (Burgess 2002; Lau & Chiu 2004)，但是，有研究發現規劃欠佳的高密度城市會提高導致病態社會的風險，包括對個人健康、家庭關係、社區參與度等的負面影響 (Tang et al. 2019)。香港房屋委員會近年採用了新的數據導向規劃來改善公共屋邨的微氣候 (Ng 2010; Yeh & Yuen 2011)，但對於人多擠逼、高度連貫的中介空間之社會影響認知依然不足。 可見性和連通性作為可信的參數，能預測公共空間的人流及社交互動 (Hillier & Hanson 1984; Batty 2001; Stamps 2005)。近年來軟件及硬件上的進步使研究做得更詳細，如三維空間的可見性分析，可深入了解人們對於監控、私隱或自主城市空間的理解。這些研究方法通常運用在分析室內 (Lu & Ye 2017) 及城市空間 (Suleiman et al. 2013; Lonergan & Hedley 2016; Kim et al. 2019)，卻未曾用作分析住宅區的社交空間。 是次項目會（A）運用及開發可見性和連通性分析，指出影響香港公共屋邨複雜、三維的中介空間視覺感知之形態。研究將（B）進行實地觀察，紀錄共存及社交活動之現象，從而了解一系列空間中，人際互動的時空佈局。接著（C）進行關聯性分析，就如何改善公共屋邨開放空間的質素及互動性提出建議。 是次研究將為提升城市中介空間的舒適及互動性提出詳細、循證的見解。此研究有助提升社區參與度。研究成果將惠及香港未來的屋邨規劃及世界各地類近的高密度發展；亦能惠及《 香港規劃標準與準則》第四和十一章（康樂、休憩用地及綠化和城市設計指引），以及旨在建立共融互助城市的政府規劃策略「香港2030+」。

24622421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24622421.value: 家庭背景——尤其是家庭社會經濟地位 (SES) 和居住狀況（城市/農村）——如何影響學生的學業成就和抑鬱水平？社會學家早已熟知，與來自高社會經濟地位和/或城市家庭的優勢學生相比，來自弱勢家庭背景的學生（即來自低社會經濟地位和/或農村家庭的學生）學業成就較低、抑鬱水平較高。然而，迄今為止的研究有兩個主要局限。第一個局限是，關於弱勢學生和優勢學生在學業成就上的差距是否類似於他們在抑鬱水平上的差距，我們知之甚少。比較這些差距可以說明家庭背景在社會不平等的不同領域（即教育與健康）中的作用是相似的還是不同的。第二個局限是，當前的文獻忽略了不同家庭背景下學業成就與抑鬱水平之間關係可能存在的異質性。與優勢學生相比，弱勢學生有著更多的風險因素和更少的緩衝因素，並且生活在不同的社交網絡中。所有這些因素都表明，來自有利和不利家庭背景的學生在學業成就和抑鬱水平的關係上可能有所不同。 為此，本研究將利用中國教育追踪調查的數據，檢驗不同家庭背景的學生在學業成就、抑鬱水平以及兩者關係方面的差異。研究結果將有助於揭示家庭背景對社會不平等的多個維度（教育與健康）的不同影響，並闡明具體教育系統中相異家庭背景學生的不同處境，同時也有助於揭示學業成績和抑鬱水平在不同情境下的互動關係。

24622421.label: Realisation of objectives
24622421.value: This project set out to examine how family background influences adolescents’ educational achievement and mental health (i.e., depression), and to explore how these two outcomes interact within China’s exam-oriented education system. Drawing on nationally representative longitudinal data and advanced analytical methods, the project successfully met all six proposed objectives, making significant scholarly and practical contributions. 1. The first objective—clarifying the role of family background in shaping both educational outcomes and psychological wellbeing—was achieved through two complementary studies. The first, based on the China Education Panel Survey (CEPS), found that family background—particularly parental education and residential status—had a stronger effect on academic performance than on depression. The second study, using data from the China Family Panel Studies (CFPS), extended this work by analyzing the role of parent-perceived academic achievement and its association with children’s depressive symptoms over time, with findings highlighting particularly strong effects in socioeconomically disadvantaged families. Together, these analyses offer a multidimensional view of adolescent inequality and the distinct ways that educational and mental health outcomes are shaped by structural conditions. 2. The second objective—evaluating both the upward mobility potential and psychological costs of the exam-oriented education system—was effectively addressed. While the system enables merit-based mobility for disadvantaged students, it imposes emotional burdens, especially when parents perceive their child’s performance as inadequate. This pattern reveals how parental pressure can contribute to students’ psychological distress, highlighting key trade-offs in competitive education systems. 3. The third objective—examining heterogeneity in the link between academic achievement and depression—was met through both studies, though findings varied by measurement type. In CFPS, the link between perceived underachievement (from parents’ perspective) and depression was strongest among socioeconomically disadvantaged students. In contrast, CEPS findings show that socioeconomically advantaged students were more likely to experience depression when their actual standardized test scores were lower than their peers’—reflecting internalized pressure. These contrasting patterns underscore how subjective perceptions and objective outcomes matter differently across social groups in shaping educational and wellbeing inequality. 4. The fourth objective—developing a multilevel explanatory framework—was met by combining family-level, institutional, and individual perspectives. Both studies employed longitudinal data and robust modeling strategies to untangle how macro and micro factors interact over time. School fixed-effects in CEPS and random-intercept cross-lagged panel models in CFPS allowed for careful attention to temporal order, selection effects, and within-person change. This multilevel approach contributes to a more integrated understanding of how structural inequalities unfold in daily life. A key theoretical contribution of the project is the concept of the “advantage trap”—the finding that socioeconomically advantaged students may be especially vulnerable to psychological distress when falling behind their peers academically. This idea extends beyond the Chinese context and has potential relevance for other high-pressure educational systems globally. Future research could apply this framework to different cultural and institutional settings, exploring how privilege interacts with performance pressure and how emotional costs are distributed across social groups. In doing so, the project lays a foundation for comparative studies and encourages more integrated research on education, inequality, and adolescent mental health. 5. The fifth objective—identifying particularly vulnerable students—was achieved by highlighting two at-risk groups: (1) socioeconomically disadvantaged students whose parents perceive them as performing poorly in school; and (2) socioeconomically advantaged students whose standardized test scores are lower than their peers’, leading to psychological distress. These findings point to the need for targeted interventions addressing both material and emotional vulnerability. 6. The sixth objective—translating research into policy and practice—was actively pursued. The project’s findings were shared at multiple major conferences, including the Comparative and International Education Society (CIES), the American Sociological Association (ASA), the Chinese Sociological Association (CSA), and the International Chinese Sociological Association (ICSA). These conferences brought together scholars, educators, and policymakers, facilitating engagement with a diverse and international audience. In particular, the CIES presentation enabled dialogue with educational practitioners and development professionals. Two manuscripts have been completed and are currently under review at Society and Mental Health and the Journal of Applied Developmental Psychology, both respected journals in their fields. Minor challenges arose during the course of the project, which contributed to the lower-than-expected grant expenditure. Initially, I had selected my PhD student as the research assistant (RA) for the project. At the time of selection, she was receiving funding from the department, which was expected to end during the project period. To support both her continued PhD study and her role in the project, I planned to reserve the RA budget from this grant for her use once her departmental funding expired—allowing for continuity in staffing and ensuring the project could be completed as proposed. However, just as her funding was nearing its end, she unexpectedly decided to graduate immediately and left the program without any prior notice. This sudden change required me to identify and train a new RA under tight time constraints. I also had to increase my own involvement in the project to maintain continuity and ensure timely progress. As a result of this shortened RA engagement period and the delayed start with the replacement assistant, only a portion of the allocated budget was ultimately used—resulting in over 30% of the total grant remaining unspent. Despite this unforeseen disruption, the project was completed on schedule. Thanks to the dedicated efforts of the new RA and my own increased time commitment, all planned objectives were met, and the scope and quality of the research were fully maintained. The research design was also expanded beyond the original plan in response to feedback from conferences and recent methodological advances. A second dataset (CFPS) and more sophisticated models (e.g., random-intercept cross-lagged panel models) enhanced analysis of within-person change over time. In sum, despite these adjustments, the project produced two full-length research papers and fully achieved all objectives. It deepened understanding of how family background shapes adolescent inequality, illuminated the psychological costs of exam-driven education, and provided insights relevant to education reform and youth mental health policy in China and beyond.

24622421.label: Major findings and research outcome
24622421.value: This project investigated how family background shapes both educational achievement and adolescent mental health (i.e., depression) in China’s exam-oriented education system. Two studies were completed using nationally representative longitudinal data. The first study (Paper 1: The Advantage Trap) used the China Education Panel Survey (CEPS) to compare inequality in academic performance and depression. It found that family background had a stronger influence on academic achievement than on mental health. Interestingly, socioeconomically advantaged students reported higher levels of depression when they performed poorly, leading to the concept of the “advantage trap.” This challenges the assumption that disadvantaged students always face the greatest psychological risk. The study also showed that low achievement affected mental health through increased pressure from parents, more frequent teacher criticism, and peer unfriendliness—especially for high-SES students. The second study (Paper 2: Dynamic Interplay Between Parent-Perceived Academic Achievement and Children’s Depression) drew on three waves of the China Family Panel Studies (CFPS) to examine the reciprocal relationship between parent-evaluated academic achievement and children’s depression. A significant two-way link was found: lower parent-perceived achievement predicted higher depression in children, and depression in turn lowered future parental evaluations. This cycle was especially strong in low-SES families, where academic outcomes are seen as critical to mobility. Mediation analyses found no support for child-perceived academic pressure or confidence in the future as explanatory pathways. Together, these findings reveal that both low- and high-SES students are vulnerable, but in different ways. The “advantage trap” underscores the emotional toll on high-SES students when their standardized test scores fall behind those of their peers, reflecting the pressure of status-based comparisons. In contrast, disadvantaged students face cumulative risks driven by negative feedback loops between parental perceptions, achievement, and wellbeing. Methodologically, the project also contributes by applying school fixed effects and random-intercept cross-lagged panel models. Findings were presented at major international conferences, including the Comparative and International Education Society (CIES) and the American Sociological Association (ASA) annual meetings, reaching international audiences of scholars, educators, and policymakers. Two papers are under review at peer-reviewed journals (Society and Mental Health and Journal of Applied Developmental Psychology). Overall, the research advances understanding of how social background influences both educational and emotional outcomes. It calls for more differentiated policies that support not only disadvantaged students academically, but also address the mental health needs of all students navigating high-pressure educational systems.

24622421.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24622421.value: This project lays the foundation for future research. First, the concept of the “advantage trap” can be further tested and refined across different educational systems and cultural settings. While the current findings are based on China, the psychological burden faced by high-SES students in high-pressure environments may also be present in other exam-driven or competitive systems, such as those in East Asia, Europe, or North America. Comparative studies could explore the generalizability of this concept and assess how institutional features shape its impact. Second, the interplay between perceived academic achievement and mental health identified in this project points to the need for more in-depth exploration of mediating mechanisms. Future work could investigate the role of family dynamics, school climate, or digital/social media pressures in this feedback loop. Building on these findings, the next phase of research will aim to secure larger-scale funding to conduct cross-national comparisons and school-based fieldwork. The goal is to develop a more comprehensive understanding of how educational inequality and emotional wellbeing co-evolve, and to inform policies that balance academic excellence with psychological health for students from all backgrounds.

24622421.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24622421.value: This project examines how family background influences both academic performance and mental health among adolescents in China. It focuses on students’ emotional responses to underachievement and how these responses differ between socioeconomically advantaged and disadvantaged groups. The study finds that students from socioeconomically advantaged families—who typically perform well—are more likely to experience depression when their standardized test scores fall behind those of their peers. This phenomenon, known as the “advantage trap”, suggests that these students are especially sensitive to academic setbacks and status-based comparisons. In contrast, students from less privileged backgrounds face a different challenge: when parents perceive them as underperforming—regardless of their actual results—it can increase the risk of depression. This emotional strain may further reinforce parents’ negative views, creating a harmful feedback loop. These contrasting patterns show that academic pressure affects students across the socioeconomic spectrum, but through different mechanisms. The study highlights the need to consider both objective performance and subjective perceptions when addressing student wellbeing. Its findings can inform more supportive school policies and family practices, helping educators, parents, and policymakers foster healthier learning environments for all children.

24622721.label: Project Title(Chinese)
24622721.value: 申命記派歷史的政治潛意識

24622721.label: Project Objectives
24622721.value: To conduct a detailed textual analysis of the key texts (Deut 17:14–20; Judg 8–9, 17–21; 1 Sam 8–12; 1 Kgs 1:1–12:24) that display the uneasy coexistence of seemingly pro-monarchic and anti-monarchic motifs in the so-called Deuteronomistic (Hi)Story (hereafter DH), a coherent literary unit identified by biblical scholars as Deuteronomy–Kings. To unpack the imperial/anti-imperial ideologies embedded in DH in general and the key texts in specific, with respect to the historical contexts of Yehud (Persian Judah), to which the composition of DH is situated. To search for parallel motifs of monarchism and political ambiguity between DH and texts that may have propagated in Yehud’s cultural surroundings (Greece, Neo-Assyria, Neo-Babylonia, and Egypt) and around the time of DH’s composition (the sixth century to the third century BCE). To determine the plausible direction of influence between the parallel motifs with respect to the literary and material developments of these civilizations. To analyze the influence of Persian imperialism and Hellenism on the signifying practices of the Deuteronomist (the authorial collective of the DH) and their original readers/audience, the imperialized Yehudites (Persian Judeans), from a historical perspective. To offer a postcolonial-psychoanalytic perspective with Homi Bhabha’s critical concepts of “ambivalence” and “unhomeliness” (Bhabha 2004) and a contemporary Freudian model of fantasy (Freud 1953: 160, 491–492, 550–572; cf. Sandler and Sandler 2003) on the impact of Persian imperialism on the identity formation and psychology of the imperialized Yehudites, in particular their ambivalent attitude towards their imperializer as reflected in DH, and their appropriation of Hellenic/Hellenistic resources in their literary production to express their unconscious desire and derision of the imperializer’s dominant position. To analyze, with respect to the parallel motifs identified and the effects of relevant ancient imperialisms, the psychic mechanisms (such as condensation, displacement, projection, introjective identification, and semiotization) involved in the conflicting portrayal of monarchy in the key texts and offer new insights on the political ambiguity in DH from a postcolonial-psychoanalytic perspective. To argue, with joint force of objectives 1 to 6, that the political ambiguity of DH is rooted in the imperialized Yehudites’ political unconscious, that is their desire to be take their imperialized dominant position and at the same time to express their contempt against the imperializer’s exploitative and oppressive acts in a roundabout way.

24622721.value: 此研究項目採用後殖民主義及精神分析的進路來分析「申命記派歷史」中的政治含混性。希伯來聖經學者普遍認同由申命記至列王紀的一系列書卷原是一個整全性的文學著作，並稱之為「申命記派歷史」（Deuteronomistic (Hi)Story；以下簡稱 DH）。尤利烏斯．威爾豪森（Julius Wellhausen 1871: ix–xi）於十九世紀末注意到撒母耳上七章至十二章對君主制存著相互矛盾並搖擺不定的觀點。威爾豪森認為該段經文可以工整地劃分為五個段落，其中支持君主制的內容源自猶大國君王時期，而反對君主制的內容則寫於猶大國亡國後，兩者交替出現。過往的歷史鑑別學者習慣地將意識形態兩極化，並將對立的意識形態分別歸納於兩個缺乏張力和含混性的陣營。按這種二元邏輯，反君主制的觀點必然是在國家滅亡後，即人民對君主制的信念全然瓦解後才出現。威爾豪森這個二源假說其後引發了不少對DH作者（即負責著作的群體或集合）對君主制所持摸棱兩可、具含糊性的立場的爭議和濃厚的研究興趣。爭論也擴大至涵蓋 DH 中的其他有類似政治張力的經文（申十七14~20；士八章至九章、十七章至二十章；王上一1~十二24；參 Gerbrandt 1979）。 雖然學者曾嘗試就DH中的政治含混性提供其他解釋，其後的解釋繼承了之前的二元論述的邏輯思維，繼續將政治立場兩極化。透過此研究項目，PI將以嶄新的角度，以後殖民和精神分析理論分析DH中的政治含混性。這個進路將考慮到波斯帝國主義對作者及原初讀者所屬被帝國化的猶大群體的身份形成、心理狀況、和文學創作的影響。 PI 將分析作者在文本中如何將大帝國的形象投射到自身民族的君主制度內，以及當中所涉及的心理機制。透過研究DH所產生的波斯猶大省的歷史場景，PI 將追溯達至這個「移情」（transference）產生的的材料來源，並從猶大省周邊的古希臘和近東文化中，尋找與DH屬同一時期的文本中的平行母題。PI 認為 DH 的政治含混性是波斯猶大省人政治潛意識的表徵，反映他們對波斯帝國模棱兩可的態度，既嚮往帝國者的的主導地位，又鄙視他們所引申的社會弊病。 本研究項目將為DH 的政治含混性提供一個符合歷史情理且有理論依據的解釋。它將展示受古代帝國主義所影響的文學著作同樣地擁有一些現代殖民論述中所觀察到的特徵。

25200821.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25200821.value: Social media platforms provide individuals with rich and fresh information; meanwhile, the explosive growth of online contents has far outpaced human beings' capacity to read and understand them. To help people access the information they need, it presents a pressing need to develop automatic social media language understanding (SMLU) methods for various compelling applications, such as content recommendation, short text classification, and microblog search. However, the existing SMLU methods mostly focus on the end-to-end training of task-oriented neural networks. Such training not only relies on large-scale task-relevant data labeled by human annotators, but also requires extensive manual efforts for model architecture design and parameter tuning. In the recent years, the pre-trained language representation models (such as BERT) have revolutionized the training paradigm of natural language understanding (NLU) in common domains, e.g., Wikipedia and news articles. Built upon their success, the state-of-the-art performance of diverse NLU tasks has been advanced forward via fine-tuning models over a small set of labeled data. Nevertheless, most pre-trained models are developed in formally-written, context-rich, and text-only scenarios, inadequate to handle social media language because of the following challenges. (1) The informal writings render the difficulty to figure out what is important and make sense of the noisy user-generated contents. (2) The existing language representation learning methods largely rely on context modeling while the limited words in social media posts usually exhibit short contexts. (3) The prominence of cross-modality expressions requires the multi-modality understanding beyond textual signals. In light of these concerns, we formulate a deep pre-training framework for SMLU. It explores language representations in social contexts with transformer encoders (henceforth social-transformers). Under the framework, three novel self-supervised learning tasks are proposed based on hashtag-enhanced cloze, interaction structure prediction, and cross-modality semantic modeling, each customized to handle the aforementioned challenges (1), (2), and (3), respectively. To support empirical studies, large-scale data will be gathered from both English and Chinese social media platforms to allow the pre-training of our social-transformers. For model evaluation, we will first investigate how our social-transformers can help boost the performance of eight important downstream tasks via fine-tuning --- four fundamental SMLU tasks and the other four popular social media applications. Then, a benchmark will be designed with a public leaderboard to further evaluate our potential to advance downstream tasks, which will fill in the gap of the lack of well-reputed SMLU benchmark and build global impacts. 眾所周知，社交平台能夠為人們提供豐富的最新信息，然而與此同時，在線內容的爆炸式增長也已經遠遠超過了人類閱讀和理解內容的能力。為了幫助人們更有效地獲取他們所需要的信息，我們迫切需要研究自動社交媒體語言理解方法，從而幫助推進多種的社交媒體下游應用的發展，例如內容推薦、短文本分類和微博搜索。然而，現有的社交媒體語言理解方法，大多面向任務，對神經網絡進行端到端的訓練。這種訓練不僅依賴於大規模人工標註的任務相關數據，還需要大量的專家來參與模型架構設計和參數調整。 近年來，預訓練語言表示模型（如 BERT）的橫空出世，徹底改變了常見領域（例如維基百科和新聞文章）中自然語言理解的訓練框架。在他們成功的基礎上，通過在少量標記數據上微調模型，很多自然語言理解任務的最先進性能都得到了一定程度地提升。然而，大多數預訓練模型是在正式編寫、上下文豐富和純文本的場景中開發的，它們在處理社交媒體語言中不可避免地會面臨巨大的挑戰。 (1) 社交語言的非正式寫作風格可能使得模型難以區分重要信息，從而無法理解用戶生成的嘈雜內容。 (2) 現有的語言表示學習方法很大程度上依賴於上下文建模，而社交媒體的消息往往內容簡短，從而無法提供豐富的上下文用於語義挖掘。 (3) 跨模態表達在社交媒體上非常普遍，這就需要模型具有多模態理解的能力而非僅僅能夠處理文本信號。 鑑於以上問題，我們為社交媒體語言理解制定了一個基於深度學習的預訓練框架。它使用transformer編碼器探索社交環境中的語言表示。在該框架下，我們提出了三個新穎的自監督學習任務，基於話題標籤增強的完形填空、交互結構預測和跨模態語義建模，每個任務分別用於應對上文提出的挑戰（1）、（2）和（3）。為支持實驗研究，我們將從中英文社交平台上收集大規模的數據，以便推進社交語言模型的預訓練實踐。對於模型評估，我們將首先研究我們的預訓練模型如何通過微調來幫助提高八個重要下游任務的性能——四個基礎的社交媒體語言理解任務和四個流行的社交媒體應用任務。在此基礎上，我們將設計和推廣一個帶有公共排行榜的基準，以進一步評估預訓練模型推進社交媒體下游任務的潛力，這將填補社交媒體語言理解領域內知名基準的空白，並有利於打造全球影響力。

25201221.label: Project Objectives
25201221.value: To develop new approximate techniques with accuracy guarantees for high-order proximity queries, so as to reduce the overheads on GPUs and increase the level of parallelism. In particular, computing exact answers for high-order proximity queries is theoretically intractable and expensive, even on moderate-sized graphs with powerful GPUs. Thus, we resort to approximate query processing paradigm, and plan to conduct comprehensive algorithmic analysis and develop approximate techniques, which, at the cost of negligible bounded error, can boost efficiency on GPUs. To design GPU-based parallel solutions with compact indexing schemes, load-balancing techniques, and advanced GPU features, so as to adapt the approximate techniques in Objective 1 to GPU architecture and efficiently handle high-order proximity queries on billion-scale graphs in practice. In particular, GPUs yield different architecture compared to that of CPUs, meaning that it is non-trivial to directly apply the approximate techniques on GPUs. Thus, we plan to develop practical solutions catered for GPU architecture, to fully stimulate the parallel power of GPUs and handle massive graphs. To investigate advanced settings including batch processing with high throughput and dynamic graph handling on GPUs, so as to further enhance the power and utility of our solutions. In particular, in real-world applications, queries are generated in batches and graphs are dynamically changing, which may cause serious performance issues. Luckily, GPUs are inherently throughput-oriented processors. Thus, we will empower our GPU-based solutions with the capability to efficiently handle these situations. To implement our solutions into a system and conduct extensive evaluations on real-world graph data, and also cooperate with our industrial collaborators at Lenovo Machine Intelligence Center (Hong Kong) to facilitate the deployment of our solutions in their industrial platforms, so as to demonstrate the superiority of our solutions and to benefit scientific and industrial areas, including online marketing, fraud detection, business intelligence, biological analysis, and so on.

25201221.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25201221.value: Graph is an expressive data model that represents objects and their relationships as nodes and edges respectively. Graphs are ubiquitous with many applications, such as online advertisement on Twitter social network, fraud detection on Alipay transaction network, biological network analysis, and web search services. To support these applications, a common and fundamental task is to query the high-order proximity between nodes based on multi-hop relationships over graphs. There are three important types of high-order proximity queries: single-pair queries, top-k queries, and single source queries. Despite the significant values of these queries, the challenges are three-fold: (i) computing exact high-order proximity values is theoretically intractable, (ii) graphs are in massive volume with billions of nodes/edges, and (iii) graphs are dynamically changing and queries are issued in batches. Existing CPU-based solutions are inefficient to handle billion-scale graphs, while response time is crucial in real-world applications. Meanwhile, CPU performance has stagnated. Recently researchers have resorted to GPUs for efficiency and made considerable progress. However, the high-order proximity queries remain largely unexplored on GPUs, and it is non-trivial to design new solutions on GPUs that yield different architecture. Bearing in mind the theoretical and practical challenges above, we plan to leverage both novel algorithmic designs and practical system engineering on GPUs, and aim to design GPU-based approximate solutions for high-order proximity queries over billion-scale graphs. Specifically, we will tackle each of the three challenges as follows. First, instead of expensively computing exact answers, we will conduct comprehensive algorithmic analysis and develop approximate techniques (e.g., sketches), which will potentially reduce overheads and increase parallelism on GPUs, at the cost of negligible bounded error. Second, we will practically adapt these approximate techniques to GPU architecture by compact index schemes, load-balancing designs, and advanced GPU features. Third, we plan to investigate techniques to handle batch processing and dynamic graphs on GPUs. Lastly, we will implement and evaluate our solutions over real-world billion-scale graphs. We will also work with our industrial collaborators to test our solutions on enterprise-level big data platforms and demonstrate the superiority of our solutions. The success of our research will benefit many scientific and industrial areas, including e-commerce, biology, FinTech, and business intelligence, so as to provide faster and better services to global and Hong Kong people. We will push the frontier by producing a rich set of advanced techniques, laying down a basis for future research. 图模型包含了节点和边，用于描述实体和实体间的关系。图数据无处不在，有着广泛的应用，例如推特等社交网络的广告推荐、支付宝交易网络的异常检测、生物信息网络分析、互联网搜索服务等等。在这些应用中，一个重要的任务是利用高阶图拓扑结构衡量节点之间的相似度。有多种重要的高阶相似度查询，包括点之间的相似度查询、top-k相似节点查询和单源相似度查询。 尽管这些查询有着重要的价值，如何高效的处理这些查询面临诸多挑战。第一，计算精准的高阶相似度理论复杂度很高；第二，图数据往往规模巨大，包含数十亿节点或边；第三，图数据往往动态变化，且查询量巨大。查询处理时间在真是应用中非常重要，但是传统基于CPU设计的方法不能够快速的处理数十亿规模大图。近期利用GPU进行大规模并行计算的科学研究取得了一定进展。但是，针对高阶相似度查询的GPU算法仍然需要深入研究。由于GPU有截然不同的计算架构，设计基于GPU的高阶相似度查询算法很有挑战性。 综合考虑到上述理论和实际挑战，我们计划利用新的算法设计和基于GPU的系统实现，设计基于GPU的近似算法，以期在数十亿规模大图上高效处理高阶相似查询。具体来说，首先，我们将通过算法分析设计近似技术对高阶相似度进行估算，以此减少计算复杂度并提升GPU并行度；其次，我们将针对GPU的计算特性，设计实用的技术将近似技术匹配到GPU架构。第三，我们计划针对批处理和动态图查询设计高效的GPU处理方案。最后，我们将会在真实的大规模图数据上对提出的算法进行测试。我们也会与业界合作伙伴进行密切合作实现算法落地。本项目的成功实施有助于多个科研和业界领域，包括电子商务，金融科技，商业智能等，能够提供更快更好的在线服务，并推动相关科研领域的进展。
