25203721.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25203721.value: In recent years, China has devoted enormous resources to civil space exploration programs, including the missions of Tiangong space stations, Chang'e lunar probes, and Tianwen-1 Mars rover. Hong Kong academia shall seize the opportunity and play an active role in this effort. In the aforementioned missions, the vehicles need to fly in the atmospheres of Earth and Mars at hypersonic speeds (greater than five times the speed of sound). The success of these missions and the design of next-generation hypersonic systems require a deep understanding of hypersonic aerodynamics and aerothermodynamics. In this project, the fundamental flow problem of shock-wave/boundary-layer interaction (SWBLI) will be the focus, which is frequently encountered during hypersonic flight. SWBLI can lead to high localized heating rates and pose serious damage to a hypersonic vehicle, for example, the accident of the X-15 experimental aircraft. Particular emphasis is given to the formation of streamwise streaks in heat flux and wall temperature that are extensively observed in hypersonic laminar interactions. The streamwise streaks can further enhance the aerodynamic heating level and trigger laminar-turbulent transition, both of which are critical to the design of any vehicle flying at hypersonic speeds. However, such phenomena are still poorly understood, and the underlying physical mechanisms remain unknown. In this project, the formation of streamwise streaks in hypersonic SWBLI will be investigated by a combination of theoretical, numerical, and experimental means. Linear stability analysis and direct numerical simulations will be performed to shed light on the relevant flow physics. Meanwhile, wind tunnel experiments will serve as a supplement to the existing experimental studies and a benchmark for numerical validation. The outcomes of this project are expected to identify the origin of the streamwise streaks and gain insight into the process of laminar-turbulent transition in hypersonic SWBLI. 近年來，中國投入了大量資源用於開展航太探測任務，包括天宮空間站、嫦娥系列月球探測器和天問一號火星探測器。香港學界應把握機遇，積極參與祖國航太事業發展。在上述任務中，飛行器需要以高超聲速（大於五倍聲速）穿越地球和火星大氣。深入理解和掌握高超聲速空氣動力學和氣動熱力學成為確保這些任務成功的關鍵所在。高超聲速激波/邊界層干擾是一種重要的基本流動現象，普遍存在于各類高超聲速飛行器的流場中。本項研究聚焦高超聲速激波/層流邊界層干擾于再附區誘發三維流向條帶結構這一流動失穩問題。該條帶結構廣泛存在於各類激波/層流邊界層干擾流動中，可導致再附區局部熱流增大甚至誘發邊界層轉捩，其產生機制尚存爭議。本項研究採用全域穩定性分析、直接數值模擬和風洞實驗對該問題開展全面的理論、數值和實驗研究。所得成果將有助於揭示流向條帶的產生機理和轉捩過程。

25203721.label: Realisation of objectives
25203721.value: The project has been completed successfully. All the project objectives have been achieved. For objective 1, a systematic study was conducted to investigate the onset of global instability in hypersonic compression corner flow. First, we fixed the Mach number and Reynolds number and varied the ramp angle. A series of base-flow solutions was generated using our in-house code called PHAROS, based on which global stability analysis (GSA) was conducted. To further understand the physical mechanisms that drive the global instability of the separation bubble, an energy budget analysis was performed, and we found that the production term is localized near the primary vortex core, which confirms that the instability arises from the separation region. We found that the onset of global instability is highly related to the emergence of secondary separation beneath the primary bubble and therefore inferred that the global stability boundary can be well correlated with a scaled ramp angle according to triple-deck theory. A criterion was therefore established to predict whether the flow is globally stable or unstable, which is dependent of freestream and geometric conditions only. For objective 2, we investigated the flow unsteadiness induced by the intrinsic instability using direct numerical simulations (DNS). The streamwise streaks observed in the wind tunnel experiments were successfully reproduced. The reattachment point, the surface heat flux, and the boundary-layer streaks post reattachment exhibit unsteady behaviors, which can be directly linked to the oscillatory unstable modes identified by the GSA. We also demonstrated that the intrinsic instability in SLBLI can trigger transition to turbulence independently through the breakdown of streamwise vortices. For objective 3, we conducted a series of compression corner and double-wedge experiments in the wind tunnel at the Polytechnic University at various ramp angles. The flow was visualized using Schlieren imaging, Rayleigh scattering, infrared imaging, and pressure-sensitive paint. Surface pressure measurements were also made using dynamic pressure transducers. The flow patterns in the transitional region were observed and compared with flow stability results and numerical simulations. For objective 4, we extended our global stability analysis to the high-enthalpy regime by considering five-species air chemistry and vibrational relaxation. It was found that the onset of incipient separation, secondary separation, and global instability is insensitive to thermochemical nonequilibrium models, which allows a direct extension of the global stability boundary established based on triple-deck theory. The project has successfully developed many theoretical and numerical tools and generated valuable theoretical, numerical, experimental data for the study of high-speed flow. The outcomes have advanced the understanding of the underlying physical mechanisms.

25203721.label: Major findings and research outcome
25203721.value: 1. When the ramp angle is beyond a critical value, the flow becomes unstable to three-dimensional (3-D) perturbations. At small angles, the leading mode has a large spanwise wavelength comparable to the size of the separation bubble. At large angles, a small-wavelength mode dominates over the large-wavelength mode. 2. The onset of incipient separation, secondary separation, and global instability is insensitive to thermochemical nonequilibrium models. 3. The production term that drives the global instability is localized near the primary vortex core, which allows us to establish a criterion based on asymptotic theory to predict the onset of global instability. 4. Global instability can induce streamwise streaks in the reattached boundary layer, which explains the experimental observation. 5. As the ramp angles increases, the transition mechanisms vary from oblique breakdown of Mack’s first mode to the breakdown of streamwise streaks.

25203721.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25203721.value: In future study, we will further extend GSA to chemically reacting flow to investigate the interaction between hydrodynamics and combustion instabilities, which is of significant importance to high-speed propulsion systems.

25203721.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25203721.value: Understanding and predicting laminar‒turbulent transition in supersonic flow is of vital importance to the development of future high-speed transportation systems. Transition to turbulence greatly increases the frictional drag and surface heating, resulting in a considerable decrease in the payload capacity. Our current understanding of transition is limited to simple geometries, such as flat plates and sharp cones. In practical engineering, complex configurations can be encountered. In this project, we consider compression ramps, which mimic inlets and control surfaces of high-speed vehicles. Compared to simple geometries, compression ramps significantly increase the complexity of the flow, inducing flow separation and shock waves. We systematically investigated the flow instability with a combination of theoretical modeling, numerical simulations, and wind tunnel experiments, providing valuable insights into the intrinsic instability and its physical mechanisms.

25209221.label: Project Objectives
25209221.value: To develop physics-guided data mining and modeling approaches for integrating heterogeneous multi-source mobility data and to formulate practical guidelines for the collection and management of real-world data in Hong Kong. To develop the individual-oriented dynamic network models and the corresponding data-driven estimation framework for both passenger flow and vehicle flow, followed by the development of an optimal management framework that minimizes total passenger travel costs instead of minimizing the total vehicle travel costs. To build a testbed for evaluating the performance of the proposed individual-oriented network models using both real-world data and simulated environments; conduct case studies in Hong Kong on a small road network in order to validate the proposed framework and on a medium-sized road network to demonstrate the efficiency of the proposed approach.

25209221.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25209221.value: With the rapid development of the emerging communication technologies (e.g., mobile internet), sensing technologies (e.g., cameras), and mobility services (e.g., personalized mapping services), urban road transportation systems have become completely different over the past decade, and the drastic changes have created opportunities and challenges for better transportation network modeling and management framework. On the one hand, the involvement of not only public agencies (e.g., Transport Department) but also private sectors (e.g., Google Maps, Uber) has diversified travel modes, so travelers’ behaviors become personalized and can vary drastically depending on their sociodemographic backgrounds, mapping services, and travel purposes. Since traditional transportation network models focus on vehicles and depict the behaviors of aggregate vehicle flow, there is a great need for a better understanding of the individual-level behaviors and flow dynamics. On the other hand, multi-source mobility data become affordable and accessible in the connected era. The heterogeneous data include traditional traffic data (e.g., traffic speed and counts) and individual mobility data (e.g., Wi-Fi and mobile phone data). The integration of multi-source data enables high-granular modeling and management of each traveler. In Hong Kong, managing the movement of individuals instead of vehicles is particularly important since its average vehicle occupancy is three times those of the US and Europe. In view of this, this project aims to develop an individual-oriented dynamic network modeling and management framework for road networks, in which the spatio-temporal flows of both individuals and vehicles are modeled using the heterogeneous multi-source data. Firstly, the project team has collected multi-source mobility data in Hong Kong, and its characteristics will be studied. An open-sourced database for Hong Kong and the corresponding guidelines will be published. Subsequently, the individual-oriented network modeling and management framework will be developed. Through international and multi-disciplinary collaborations, novel approaches will be developed to advance the theories in multi-source mobility data learning, dynamic network modeling, and data-driven system management on road networks. Additionally, case studies will be conducted on two networks in Hong Kong using both real-world data and simulated environments. The individual-oriented and vehicle-oriented management frameworks will be compared to demonstrate the advantages of the proposed framework. This project can contribute to and serve as a building block for the smart city initiatives in Hong Kong. The research output can help both public agencies and private sectors understand the values of the emerging mobility data in system-level management, and further promote collaborations between both parties. 隨著如移動互聯網等新興通信技術、信息采集技術和手機移動服務的快速發展，城市道路交通系統在過去十年裡發生了翻天覆地的變化，並且對已有交通網路建模與管理理論提出了機遇和挑戰。一方面，隨著包含運輸署在內的公共機構和包含谷歌地圖、優步在內的私營部門的共同參與，個體出行方式變得多樣化、個性化，並且可能會由於社會人口背景、地圖服務以及旅行目的而產生巨大的差異。傳統交通網絡模型聚焦於車輛且描繪了車流整體的行為，而新型模型需要能夠對個體出行行為及動力學性質進行建模。另一方面，多源交通數據在互聯網時代變得更易於獲取，其中包括含交通流量、速度在內的傳統交通數據以及含Wi-Fi、手機信令在內的個人出行數據，這些數據使對個體出行者的高精度細粒度建模與管理成為可能。在香港，由於其平均車輛載客數是美國和歐洲的三倍，因此相比管理車輛出行，管理個體出行顯得尤為重要。鑒於此，本項目針對交通路網研究個體出行視角下的動態網路建模與管理方法，並利用多源異構數據對個體和車輛的時空交通流進行建模。首先，項目組收集香港多源交通數據並對其特徵進行研究，相對應的開源數據庫和數據應用指南也將隨之發佈；其次，項目組將開發面向個體出行的網路建模與管理方法。透過國際與多學科合作，所開發方法可以推進多源數據融合、動態網路建模以及數據驅動的交通管理理論的發展。此外，項目組還將利用真實交通數據和仿真環境在香港路網上進行案例研究，同時還將比較面向個體和面向車輛管理方法的差異，並以此展示新方法的優越性。本項目可為香港智慧出行方案做出貢獻並提供基礎數據支撐。研究成果可幫助公共機構和私營部門瞭解新興數據在交通系統管理中的價值，並進一步促進雙方合作。

25210821.label: Project Title(Chinese)
25210821.value: 基于图的异常检测系统在结构性攻击下的对抗稳健性研究

25210821.label: Project Objectives
25210821.value: Understanding the vulnerabilities of existing GAD systems under the new structural attacks. That is, we aim to understand to what extent an attacker can evade a GAD system by manipulating the graph structure. This problem is significant in that undetected attacks could bring considerable profits to attackers, giving them full motivation to evade detection tools. However, research on this topic is severely lagging behind especially when more new techniques (e.g., graph mining [1], structured machine learning [20], graph representation learning [15], etc.) are used by GAD. Furthermore, structural attacks are unique for graph data and have a distinctive combinatorial nature – attacker often needs to choose a subset of edges from the graph to manipulate. This makes previous research that mainly focuses on manipulating the continuous node attributes hard to be applied. Third, edges in the graph encode a variety of relations, activities, and signals in various domains, which allows the attacker to easily manipulate in the physical world, making structural attacks practical. We propose to investigate the vulnerabilities via designing efficient structural attacks from an optimization point of view. Specifically, a structural attack is cast as an optimization problem, where an attacker tries to find the optimal graph structure to evade detection. The key element is to design the objective function that can mathematically characterize the attacker’s goal of evading detection (for example, minimizing the anomaly score of a target). The resulting combinatorial optimization problem is often hard to be solved optimally. Thus, designing effective approximation algorithms is a major research challenge. Developing empirically robust GAD systems that can defend against specific structural attacks. That is, we aim to develop robust GAD systems which the previously generated structural attacks cannot evade. We propose to realize this objective through a two-step defense strategy. Specifically, structural attacks exist because the attacker can pollute the graph data via tampering with the data collection process. Thus, the first direct combat is to invest resources (e.g., manpower) to reliably collect data with the goal of reducing the amount of pollution in the data. The key elements are quantifying the data utility and subsequently using limited resources to collect highly-valued data in an adversarial environment. As we cannot guarantee that all the collected data are reliable due to limited resources, the second step is to develop GAD models with robust parameters from partially polluted data. We propose to use game theory [24] to model such interaction – a defender selects robust parameters facing a strategical attacker who can manipulate the data based on which the parameters are selected. The key element would be designing efficient algorithms to solve the game, whose outcome is a robust GAD model. Achieving provable robustness for a few representative GAD systems against typical structural attacks. That is, we aim to develop GAD systems that have this property: it can be mathematically proved that any kind of structural attacks cannot evade such systems as long as the attacker’s ability is bounded. The previously developed empirically robust GAD systems have one limitation. Specifically, the optimization-based approach will generate different structural attacks, depending on the objective functions selected. Consequently, a robust GAD system can usually defend against only one specific structural attack it is designed for. We thus aim to achieve provably robust GAD systems to alleviate this issue. Notably, regardless of the types of structural attacks, the attacker’s ability could be mathematically bounded. For example, a typical bound is that the attacker can modify at most k edges, while structural attacks differ in which k edges the attacker will choose. Then provably robustness makes this theoretical guarantee: any types of structural attacks cannot evade the detection as long as the attacker cannot delete more than k edges. We propose to achieve this objective by applying a recently proposed randomized smoothing technique [11], which is specially designed for classification tasks on continuous non-relational data. The key element then is to adapt this technique to discrete graph data and more general numeric functions (other than the classification function) involved in GAD tasks, such that a larger bound on the attacker’s ability can be guaranteed.

25210821.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25210821.value: Graph-based Anomaly Detection (GAD) stands on the front line in defending against cybercrime, due to its superior power of spotting unusual patterns from relational data represented as graphs. As such, it can detect and thus prevent various forms of malicious activities that could have caused substantial losses. Indeed, GAD is widely applied in detecting fraud in the financial industry, botnet in communication networks, and spams on the Web, etc. Studying the adversarial robustness of anomaly detection is of profound significance: it allows us to understand how attackers can conduct malicious activities without being detected, and subsequently enables us to improve the systems to better detect those anomalies. Unfortunately, current research on the adversarial robustness of GAD is severely inadequate. First, GAD exposes a new attacking surface, ironically due to its unique advantage of being able to exploit the connections among data (i.e., edges in graphs). For example, an attacker can inject normal transactions in online payment systems (i.e., add edges) to make a malicious trader less suspicious. That is, adversaries now can evade GAD via manipulating the graph structure (i.e., structural attacks). Second, previous works mainly focus on non-graph data. The discrete nature of modifying graph structure makes applying previous solutions extremely challenging. Third, as our knowledge in attacking GAD is already limited, research in developing more robust GAD under new structural attacks is still in its infancy. Thus, we aim to develop robust GAD systems under the new threat through three coherent tasks: designing effective structural attacks to understand the vulnerabilities of GAD, developing practically robust GAD that can defend against prior attacks, and achieving provable robustness for the developed GAD systems, which provides a theoretical guarantee that any kind of structural attacks cannot evade detection as long as the attacker’s ability is bounded. The expected outcomes have profound practical implications. Robust GAD allows us to more effectively detect anomalies, mitigating various cybercrime in critical domains. Moreover, provably robust GAD is promising in ending the arms race between the defender and attacker as it provides the guarantee to defend against any attacks. Based on our preliminary studies, we propose a series of new approaches to accomplish the three tasks. We will evaluate those approaches on standard datasets as well as through real-world experiments. The outcomes are expected to significantly advance the state-of-the-art knowledge in attack and defense on intelligent systems, allowing using AI reliably to enhance cybersecurity. 基于图的异常检测系统（后简称为“图系统”）能从关系型数据中侦测出异常的模式，进而防范各类形式的有可能造成重大损失的恶意犯罪行为，立于抵御网络犯罪的前线。事实上，图系统被广泛的应用于检测金融行业的诈骗，通信系统中的僵尸网络，以及垃圾邮件等等与安全息息相关的实际场景中。 研究异常检测系统的稳健性有着极其重要的意义, 这使得我们能够掌握攻击者逃逸检测系统的攻击方法，从而进一步提高检测系统，使其能更优的检测出异常行为。然而不幸的是，现行的对异常检测系统的稳健性研究严重不足。首先，图系统的独特优势是能利用数据间的联系（即图中的边），然而正是这一优势暴露出了图系统的一个新的攻击突破口。例如，在在线支付平台中，攻击者能够注入一些正常的交易记录（即在图中插入一些边）来降低某些恶意交易者的可疑性使其逃避检测。概括来说，攻击者现在能够通过改变图的结构来对图系统进行攻击，我们称这类攻击为结构性攻击。其次，以往对异常检测系统的研究专注于非图的数据模型。然而，结构性攻击本质上体现出一种离散性的行为，这使得将以往的研究结果迁移到图上变得十分困难。最后，由于对结构性攻击的了解已经十分有限，针对结构性攻击的防御的研究更是处于起步阶段。 基于此，我们以研发出稳健的基于图的异常检测系统为目标，我们通过三个紧密相连的任务来实现这一目标：设计有效的结构性攻击来探究图系统的薄弱点, 设计实际有效的稳健的图系统来抵御之前的结构性攻击，以及进一步实现理论上可论证的稳健的图系统。其中，可论证的图系统的意义在于，只要攻击者的能力被限制在某一范围之内，那么我们就能理论上证明该图系统不可被攻击。该研究预期的结果有着深远的实际意义。 稳健的图系统能更有效的检测出异常，降低各类网络犯罪的危害性。实现可论证的稳定的图系统能够提供对抵御各类攻击的理论上的保证，能有效的终结攻击者与防御者之间的拉锯战。基于我们前期的一些工作，我们在此项目中提出一系列新的思路与方法来完成以上的三个任务。 我们将通过各类实验来对我们提出的方案进行充分的论证。 项目预计的结果能够极大的促进对智能系统的攻击与防御的认知，增强人工智能技术在网络安全领域应用的可靠性。

25210821.label: Realisation of objectives
25210821.value: 1. Objective 1: Understanding Vulnerabilities via Structural Attacks (1) Proposed Aim: To investigate the vulnerabilities of GAD systems by designing efficient structural attacks from an optimization perspective, addressing their unique combinatorial nature. (2) Realization and Key Achievements: This objective has been fully and extensively achieved. The project team designed a comprehensive suite of novel structural attack frameworks that systematically expose the fragility of various graph analysis systems, including but not limited to anomaly detection. -- Attack Formulation & Efficiency: We cast structural attacks as sophisticated optimization problems, as proposed. Key publications demonstrate this: (i) [J4] & [C1] introduced a bi-level to one-level optimization framework specifically for poisoning Graph-based Anomaly Detection (GAD), dramatically improving attack efficiency and effectiveness. (ii) [J7] proposed Coupled-Space Attacks against random-walk-based centrality measures (a core component of many GAD systems), successfully hiding nodes from detection by manipulating both local and global graph properties. -- Broadening the Attack Surface: The research significantly exceeded the initial scope by applying the "structural attack" philosophy to a wider range of graph-based tasks, demonstrating the universality of the threat: (i) Attacks against signed graph analysis ([J6], [C3], [C6]), targeting trust/link prediction. (ii) Attacks against recommendation systems viewed as a fraudster detection task ([J5]). (iv) Cost-aware ([C4]) attack strategies. 2. Objective 2: Developing Empirically Robust GAD Systems (1) Proposed Aim: To develop robust GAD systems through a two-step defense strategy involving strategic data collection and game-theoretic robust training. (2) Realization and Key Achievements: This objective has been substantially achieved, with research outputs covering both proposed defense steps and extending into related robust learning paradigms. -- Data Sanitization (Step 1): The direct combat against data pollution was realized. FocusedCleaner [J3] is a direct embodiment of this step. It "sanitizes poisoned graphs" by identifying and cleaning malicious edges, which is precisely the goal of investing resources to collect reliable data. It prioritizes cleaning efforts, aligning with the proposed "quantifying data utility." -- Game-Theoretic & Adversarial Training (Step 2): We developed models robust to strategic attackers. The core idea of using game theory to model attacker-defender interaction was successfully executed in [J1], which formalizes hiding from centrality as a Stackelberg game. This work provided the foundational model. [J5] operationalized this for adaptive fraudster detection in recommendation systems, implementing a robust model that accounts for an adversary who adapts to evasion attempts. [J6] introduced secrecy-aware attacks and defenses for signed networks, incorporating strategic reasoning about what the attacker knows, a nuanced extension of the game-theoretic concept. 3. Objective 3: Achieving Provable Robustness (1) Proposed Aim: To develop GAD systems with mathematical guarantees of robustness against bounded structural attacks by adapting randomized smoothing techniques to graph data. (2) Realization and Key Achievements: This objective has been achieved with notable success, though the initial plan required significant adaptation to the graph domain. The project produced pioneering work in the field of certifiably robust graph machine learning. -- Adaptation of Randomized Smoothing: We made fundamental contributions to adapting certification techniques to graphs. [C5] Node-aware Bi-smoothing and [C7] Collective Certified Robustness are landmark publications that directly address the proposal's goal. These papers introduce novel smoothing techniques specifically designed for graph injection attacks (a type of structural attack), providing the first strong robustness certificates for node-level tasks on discrete graph data. [J2] further applied this line of thinking towards certified robustness in adversarial AIoT environments, demonstrating the applicability to real-world scenarios. -- Provable Guarantees Attained: These works deliver exactly the promised property: a mathematical proof that no attacker can change the model's prediction (e.g., "anomalous" to "normal") as long as the number of added/perturbed edges is bounded by a computed, certifiable budget (k). This guarantee holds for any attack strategy within that budget. Therefore, while the objective is achieved for foundational classification-based GAD formulations, the full generalization to all numeric anomaly scoring functions represents the frontier of current research, beyond the scope of this single project. The outputs [C5] and [C7] published at top security (IEEE S&P) and ML (ICML) venues are clear indicators of the groundbreaking success achieved in this direction. Overall, the project exceeded expectations in Objectives 1 and 2, producing a prolific body of work that defines the state-of-the-art in structural attacks and empirical defenses for graph analysis. For Objective 3, the project achieved its core, pioneering goal of providing provable robustness for graph models against structural attacks, producing research that has shaped a new subfield.

25210821.label: Major findings and research outcome
25210821.value: This project has yielded fundamental insights into the security of graph-based learning systems, with outcomes spanning vulnerability discovery, defense development, and theoretical guarantees. 1. Foundational Vulnerability of Graph Systems: We established that graph-based anomaly detection (GAD) and related systems are highly susceptible to carefully crafted structural perturbations. Our research produced efficient optimization frameworks for structural attacks, demonstrating that adversaries can reliably evade detection by manipulating a minimal subset of edges. This vulnerability proved universal, extending to signed network analysis for trust prediction [J6, C1, C3] and recommendation systems [J5, J8], thereby exposing a critical systemic risk. 2. Effective Empirical Defenses via Strategic Design: We successfully developed robust countermeasures. By modeling the conflict as a Stackelberg game [J1], we created effective empirical defenses. These include the FocusedCleaner sanitization method for repairing poisoned graph data [J3] and adversarially robust models for adaptive fraud detection [J5]. These defenses significantly raise the cost and difficulty of successful attacks, providing practical solutions for enhancing system resilience. 3. Pioneering Provable Robustness for Graphs: In a major theoretical advance, we achieved certifiable robustness for graph models against structural attacks. We successfully adapted randomized smoothing to the discrete graph domain, resulting in the first certified defenses against graph injection attacks. Our Node-aware Bi-smoothing [C5] and Collective Certified Robustness [C7] frameworks provide mathematically guaranteed security: model predictions are provably stable against any adversarial effort within a quantifiable perturbation budget. Collectively, these findings form a comprehensive research pipeline—from vulnerability exposure to practical and provable hardening. The outcomes, documented in high-impact publications, provide the community with essential attack benchmarks, robust defense frameworks, and foundational certification tools, significantly advancing the field of adversarial graph machine learning.

25210821.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25210821.value: This research has established a critical foundation, yet several high-impact avenues for further development remain. First, we will extend certified robustness from node classification to broader GAD tasks, focusing on certifying continuous anomaly scores and subgraph-level detection. This addresses the key limitation identified in our current work. Second, we aim to develop a unified theoretical framework for graph adversarial robustness, generalizing our findings across attack types (evasion/poisoning, structure/feature) and graph tasks. This will provide principled guidelines for designing inherently secure graph algorithms. Third, we propose transitioning to real-world validation and deployment, particularly in cybersecurity and financial fraud detection domains. This involves creating standardized robustness benchmarks and testing our defenses in operational environments against adaptive adversaries. The ultimate goal is to translate our theoretical and empirical advances into practical, trustworthy graph analytics systems.

25210821.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25210821.value: This research is about making AI systems that analyze networks more secure and reliable. Think of systems that detect fraud in financial networks, spot malicious activity in computer networks, or recommend products online—they all work by analyzing connections (or "graphs"). We discovered that these systems can be surprisingly fragile. A bad actor could subtly alter just a few connections in the network to hide fraudulent activity or manipulate recommendations, "tricking" the AI. Our project first exposed how easily this can be done. More importantly, we then created solutions. We developed new methods to "immunize" these AI systems against such trickery, making them robust. Furthermore, we pioneered techniques to provide mathematical proof of their security, guaranteeing that the system's decisions won't change unless an attacker makes very large, detectable changes. The value of this work is building more trustworthy AI. It helps ensure that the automated systems protecting our money, security, and online experiences are not only smart but also resilient against manipulation, making our digital world safer.

25211321.label: Project Title(Chinese)
25211321.value: 带有组合约束的公平分配问题的算法研究

25211321.label: Project Objectives
25211321.value: 1. Knapsack Constraints. Our first objective is to provide a comprehensive understanding of the algorithmic fair division problem with knapsack constraints, where the model is abstracted in the way that items have sizes, and agents have knapsacks with fixed capacities. Knapsack constraint requires that the total size of items allocated to every agent does not exceed her capacity. Key issues and elements: (a) Under knapsack constraints, define proper fairness notions, as well as their relaxations, to capture the desired properties for a fair allocation to satisfy. (b) Given the characterization of fairness, explore to what extent and under what conditions a fair allocation is guaranteed to exist. (c) Design (polynomial-time) algorithms to (approximately) compute fair allocations for various settings (from restricted to general). (d) Investigate the relationship (such as compatibility and implication) between various fairness and efficiency criteria (such as Nash optimality and Pareto optimality). (e) Design algorithms to compute allocations that are simultaneously (and approximately) fair and efficient. The outcome of this part will include novel fair division models that incorporate knapsack constraints, novel algorithms to compute fair allocations, and theoretical studies on the relationships between our definitions and other criteria. 2. Scheduling Constraints. Motivated by real-world situations where one single parameter cannot characterize the essential properties of items, our second objective is to extend our findings for knapsack constraints to job scheduling constraints, where each item is modeled as a job that has release time, processing time, and deadline. Scheduling constraint requires that the items allocated to any agent cannot have overlap. Our goal is to expand the theory of scheduling to the field of fair division. The key issues and the elements in this part share a similar structure with knapsack constraints. We first define fairness concepts for the setting with scheduling constraints, and then design algorithms to compute (approximately) fair allocations and identify tricky instances to show inherent difficulties of the problem such that no algorithm can perform better beyond a certain fairness degree. The relationship among various criteria will be studied. The outcome of this part will contain another fair division model where knapsack constraints are expanded to scheduling constraints. Novel algorithms with techniques from the theory of scheduling will be designed to find fair allocations. 3. Extensions. The ultimate goal of this project is to initiate the study of fair division under combinatorial constraints and expand the combinatorial optimization problems to the field of fair division. Based on the findings from the above two parts, we will extend our study to the following settings. I. Incorporating Multiple Constraints. Beyond the study of each individual type of constraints, we will also investigate more complicated settings when the allocation needs to satisfy multiple constraints such as the situation when items have sizes and are endowed by agents. II. Divisible Resource Division. For ease of exposition, our previous study is focused on the case of indivisible goods. The second extension of this project is to expand our previous findings to the case of divisible resources where the items can be arbitrarily divided and shared among the agents, such as the funding distribution problem abstracted from RGC. III. Fair Chore Division. Finally, we will extend our previous findings to the case of chores, where agents incur costs for completing their assigned items and thus want to obtain as few items as possible. For each of these three extensions, our high-level objective in this part is to characterize the corresponding fair division problems under various combinatorial constraints, and design new algorithms or adapt algorithms from previous settings to compute fair and efficient allocations.

25211321.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25211321.value: Fair division is an important research field in multi-agent systems that integrates computer science and social science. A traditional fair division problem is often modeled as allocating a set of resources to a set of agents, where each agent’s absolute value depends on her own allocated resources, but her relative happiness depends on the comparison of her due share with others’. Fairness is mostly captured by envy-freeness and proportionality in the literature. Although an exact envy-free or proportional allocation always exists when resources are divisible (such as funding and land), it merely exists when resources are indivisible (such as equipment and labor). Accordingly, for indivisible resources, an extensively studied subject is to investigate that to what extent the relaxations of these fairness notions can be satisfied by either designing (approximation) algorithms or identifying tricky instances to show the inherit difficulties of the problem so that no algorithm can be better than a certain performance. This project aims at expanding the theory of algorithmic fair division by considering combinatorial constraints over agents and items. Despite rapid progress in fair division, the vast space where problems are under practical constraints remains highly unexplored. In real-world scenarios, however, agents’ satisfaction on the final allocation depends not only on items’ generic value but also on the constraints induced by items’ essential properties, which form the basis of agents’ reasoning and largely affect the whole system’s structure and performance. For example, items may actually have price or physical size and agents have budget or capacities to support the assigned items accordingly, in which situation the constraints can be abstracted as knapsacks. There are also more complicated situations when the items' properties cannot be described by a single parameter, such as job scheduling constraints and incentive compatible constraints. In this project, we will first characterize proper fairness notions for combinatorially constrained settings and then investigate to what extent fairness as well as classic efficiency criteria can be guaranteed by designing algorithms and analyzing limits of algorithms. Next, we will extend our results to related settings including chore allocation (where agents want to receive fewer items) and divisible resource allocation. Our project will make contributions to the field of fair division and multi-agent systems in general, and is expected to further strengthen connections between computer science and social science. 公平分配是多智能体领域涉及计算机科学和社会学的重要问题之一。经典的公平分配问题是研究如何将资源分配给若干用户，每个用户对所得到的资源的满意程度既取决于资源本身的价值，也与她对其他用户所得到的资源的价值相关。两种有关公平性的定义是无嫉妒和按比例。虽然在资源可分割的时候（例如资金和土地）无嫉妒和按比例的分配方式一定存在，但是当资源是不可分割的时候（例如设备和员工）绝对公平性很难被满足。从而关于不可分割资源分配的一个热点问题是讨论如何松弛公平性条件从而使得近似公平的分配方式是存在的，并设计高效算法求解公平分配。 本项目旨在考虑带有组合约束的公平分配问题。虽然公平分配问题近年来得到了广泛的关注，但是对于带有约束的情况还没有深入了解。在现实生活中，用户可以得到的资源可能受到其本身的性质的限制。例如，每个物品有自身的价格或尺寸，而每个用户有固定的预算或容量从而限制了她可以得到的资源范围；这种情况可以被刻画为背包约束。还有一些更为复杂的情况，其约束并不能被单一参数刻画，例如在工件调度问题中，要求分配给每个用户的工件可以被有效执行。 在本项目的研究中，我们首先为不同约束下的分配问题设计适合的公平性的解概念，然后讨论他们的存在性及与有效分配的兼容性，并设计（近似）算法求解公平分配。最后我们将结果拓展到相关的设置中，例如任务的分配（用户希望得到尽可能少的任务）和可分割资源的分配。

25211321.label: Realisation of objectives
25211321.value: Objective 1: Comprehensive Understanding of Fair Division with Knapsack Constraints The first objective was to develop a comprehensive understanding of the algorithmic fair division problem under knapsack constraints. In this model, items are characterized by their sizes, and agents are equipped with knapsacks of fixed capacities. The knapsack constraint stipulates that the total size of items allocated to any agent must not exceed her capacity. Achievements (a) We introduced and formalized appropriate fairness notions tailored to the knapsack setting, including both envy-based and share-based concepts. Notably, we defined envy-free up to one item (EF1) with charity, which ensures that agents do not envy each other (including the charity) up to one item, subject to knapsack constraints. We also studied maximin share fairness (MMS), providing a robust framework for fair allocation. Our fairness notions have been extended in subsequent works to stronger versions, such as EFX, and the MMS concept has been generalized to hereditary constraints. (b) We developed polynomial-time algorithms to compute approximately EF1 and MMS fair allocations across various settings. Our algorithms leverage the combinatorial structure of knapsack constraints and pairwise agent comparisons. For example, for EF1 fairness and identical valuations, we designed a polynomial-time algorithm achieving a 1/2-approximate EF1 allocation for any number of agents. For identical agents and for two agents, we provided efficient algorithms for exact EF1 allocations. For MMS fairness, for arbitrary values and sizes, our algorithm computes a 4/15-MMS allocation. For two agents, we improved the approximation ratio to 2/3. When items have identical sizes for all agents, we further improved the ratio to 0.387. (d) We investigated the interplay between EF1 fairness and Nash social welfare/Pareto optimality. In the general setting with heterogeneous valuations and budgets, we proved that a budget-feasible allocation maximizing Nash social welfare achieves a 1/4-approximation of EF1. This result extends to arbitrary monotone subadditive valuations. The approximation ratio improves as the budget-cost ratio increases, converging to 1/2 for large ratios, and to 1 for identical valuations. Objective 2: Comprehensive Understanding of Fair Division with Scheduling Constraints The second objective of our project was to extend our theoretical and algorithmic findings from knapsack constraints to more complex scheduling constraints, motivated by real-world scenarios where items (jobs) are characterized by multiple parameters: release time, processing time, and deadline. Achievements Our work on this objective is structured around three main fairness and efficiency notions: Maximin Share (MMS), Envy-Freeness up to one item with Pareto Optimality (EF1+PO), and Envy-Freeness up to one item with Individual Optimality (EF1+IO). Regarding MMS fairness, we developed an algorithmic framework that guarantees a 1/3-approximate MMS schedule for arbitrary instances. Our algorithm, with minor modifications, achieves a 0.24-approximate MMS allocation in polynomial time, without requiring valuation oracles. For rigid jobs (processing time equals deadline minus release time), our problem generalizes interval graph partitioning, and we designed approximation algorithms for flexible jobs and arbitrary agent numbers. Regarding EF1 and PO, we proved that no algorithm can guarantee EF1 and PO for all instances, even with rigid jobs and unary valuations. However, for jobs with unit processing time and (weighted) identical valuations, an EF1 and PO schedule exists and can be computed in polynomial time. For general instances, we established the existence of a 1/4-approximate EF1 and PO schedule, matching what we have obtained for the knapsack constraints. For unit jobs, the approximation improves to 1/2 and maximizing Nash social welfare yields schedules that are PO and achieve these EF1 approximation ratios. Beyond the interval scheduling constraints, we also studied the fair scheduling of jobs across groups of unrelated machines, with a focus on achieving maximin share (MMS) fairness at the group level. We initially introduced this model in 2023, where each group contains several identical machines (or machines identical except for varying speeds), and the group’s cost is defined by the minimum makespan required to complete all assigned jobs. The case where machines within each group are unrelated remained an open question. In our recent work, we address this gap by presenting a polynomial-time algorithm that computes a 2-approximate MMS allocation using linear programming methods. We further demonstrate that no algorithm can achieve better than a (2 − 1/n)-approximate MMS, where n is the number of machines, making the ratio of 2 asymptotically optimal. For groups of identical machines, we improve the approximation ratio to 4/3. Objective 3: Based on the study from the above two objectives, we have extended our study to the following settings. Extension I. We have extended our research to a range of constraints and more complex allocation scenarios involving multiple requirements. For example, we studied connectivity constraints, where items are nodes in a graph and each agent must receive a connected subgraph, reflecting situations where resources are interdependent. We also examined orientation constraints, where agents are vertices and items are edges, and each agent can only be assigned edges incident to them, which is relevant in network allocation problems. Furthermore, we explored more advanced settings such as the online setting, where items arrive over time and must be allocated without knowledge of future arrivals, the strategic setting, where the agents’ valuations are their private information, and the weighted setting, where agents have different entitlements or priorities. Extension II. We studied fair allocation in more settings with both divisible and indivisible goods. While strong fairness notions like envy-freeness (EF) and proportionality (PROP) are always achievable for divisible goods, only relaxed versions (EF1, PROP1) apply to indivisible goods. To bridge this gap, we introduced “up to a fraction” relaxations, where the fraction depends on the proportion of indivisible goods (the indivisibility ratio). These new fairness concepts are tailored to individuals’ indivisibility ratios and include asymmetric conditions. We established tight upper and lower bounds for the required fraction to satisfy fairness, with results tight up to a constant for EF and asymptotically tight for PROP. Extension III. We extended our study to chore allocation, where agents want to minimize their assigned items. For bin packing model, items have associated sizes, and agents must pack their assigned items into bins while aiming to minimize the number of bins used, which defines the agent’s cost. For job scheduling model, each agent is responsible for managing a set of (unrelated) machines. When jobs are assigned, the agent schedules them across her machines to minimize the makespan. In the vertex cover model, the items being allocated are the edges of a graph, and agents have costs associated with each vertex. Upon assigned a set of edges, an agent must choose a subset of vertices (at minimum total cost) that covers all the assigned edges. For each of these settings, we designed constant approximate MMS allocation. We further generalized our results to submodular and subadditive valuations, showing that for binary submodular costs, no algorithm can achieve better than a min{n, log m/log log m}-approximation. However, for separable piecewise-linear concave (SPLC) valuations, a constant approximation is achievable.

The ultimate goal of this project is to initiate the study of fair division under combinatorial constraints and expand the combinatorial optimization problems to the field of fair division. Based on the findings from the above two parts, we will extend our study to the following settings. I. Incorporating Multiple Constraints. II. Divisible Resource Division. III. Fair Chore Division.

25211321.label: Major findings and research outcome
25211321.value: Our research provides a comprehensive understanding of fair division under combinatorial constraints, with advances across three main objectives. Objective 1: Knapsack Constraints We formalized fairness notions tailored to knapsack settings, including envy-free up to one item (EF1) with charity and maximin share (MMS) fairness. We designed constant approximation algorithms for computing MMS and EF1 fair allocations under both general and restricted settings (such as two agents, identical valuations). We also proved the allocation that maximizing Nash social welfare is approximately EF1 and PO. Our results have been published in AAMAS 2023 [9.2] and Information and Computation. We also considered the dorm assignment setting, where each dorm has a fixed capacity. For various solution concepts, we have proved the extent to which fairness can be satisfied. The result is published by JAIR [8.2]. Objective 2: Scheduling Constraints We extended our framework to scheduling settings. In the first version, as the preliminary results of this project, the jobs have compatibility constraints. For MMS fairness, we designed algorithms guaranteeing a constant approximate MMS schedule and proved that such an allocation can be found in polynomial time. This result has been presented at NeurIPS. The second setting considers scheduling jobs among agents, where each agent controls a set of machines. Each agent’s cost is determined by the minimum makespan to complete all assigned jobs. For the machines are heterogeneous, we designed a polynomial time 2-MMS algorithm and proved that this approximation ratio is asymptotically tight. For the case of homogeneous machines, the approximation ratio is improved to 4/3. Our results have been published by NeurIPS 2023 [9.6] Objective 3: Extensions We further explored fair allocation under other combinatorial constraints: - Connectivity Constraints [8.5, 9.5, 9.8] - Vertex cover Constraints [9.7] - Bin Packing Constraints [9.6] - MST Constraints [9.3] Besides the classic settings, we have extended our research to more advanced settings: - Online Setting (where items arrive dynamically) [8.3] - Strategic Setting (where agents’ valuations are private information) [8.6, 9.9] - Partial Information (where the algorithm only knows limited information about agents’ valuations) [8.6, 9.1] - Asymmetric Agents (where agents may have different entitlements) [8.4, 9.4] - Mixed Items (where the items consist of both divisible and indivisible items) [9.10] Besides the above technical results, we also completed a comprehensive survey for algorithmic fair division, which is published by Artificial Intelligence 2023 [8.1].

25211321.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25211321.value: Our research uncovers several promising directions for further development. First, while we have studied various solution concepts (such as MMS and EF1) for additive valuations, the study of more general valuation classes remains an important challenge. Developing improved algorithms or impossibility results for these settings would significantly advance the field. Second, extending our frameworks to dynamic and strategic environments is a natural next step. This includes designing fair allocation mechanisms that are robust to agents’ strategic behavior, and adapting our algorithms to online and stochastic settings where items and agents arrive or depart over time. Third, practical implementation and empirical evaluation of our algorithms in real-world applications—such as resource allocation in cloud computing, scheduling in shared facilities, or fair division in collaborative projects—will help validate and refine our theoretical findings. Our proposed course of action is to pursue these directions by (1) deepening the theoretical analysis for broader valuation classes, (2) developing strategyproof and online algorithms, and (3) collaborating with domain experts to pilot our methods in practical allocation scenarios, ensuring both theoretical rigor and real-world impact.

25211321.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25211321.value: Fair allocation is a significant problem in the field of multi-agent systems, intersecting both computer science and economics. This project aims to address fair allocation problems with combinatorial constraints. In real-world scenarios, the resources a user can receive may be limited by the nature of the resources themselves. For example, each item may have a price or size, and each user may have a fixed budget or capacity, restricting the range of resources they can obtain; this situation can be modeled as a knapsack constraint. There are also more complex cases where constraints cannot be characterized by a single parameter, such as in job scheduling problems, where the allocated jobs must be executable by each user. In this project, we first designed suitable fairness solution concepts for allocation problems under various constraints. We then investigated the existence of such solutions and their compatibility with efficient allocation, and developed (approximate) algorithms to solve the fair allocation problem. We have also extended our results to related settings, such as task allocation (where users prefer to receive as few tasks as possible) and the allocation of divisible resources.

25216121.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25216121.value: Efficient utilization of green energy resources is imperative to the sustainable development of our society. Although lithium ion batteries have played a vital role in powering portable electronic devices in past decades, their application in grid-scale energy storage is hindered by the limited lithium resources. Lots of attention has been paid to post-Li batteries, among them, calcium ion battery is considered promising because the divalent nature of Ca2+ charge carrier and the low reduction potential of Ca2+/Ca (-2.9V vs. standard hydrogen electrode) close to that of lithium would induce breakthrough in energy density. The high abundance of calcium (the 5th rich element in Earth crust) also suggests lower cost batteries. However, the development of calcium battery is stalled by the lack of suitable electrodes. For anode materials, for the first time, the PI has recently demonstrated reversible calcium intercalation in graphite enabling a high capacity of 97 mAh g-1 and high-rate capability up to 2 A g-1. The intriguing findings in anode demonstrate that calcium ion batteries can be practically feasible. However, the progress in cathode material is sluggish due to challenges in overcoming sluggish kinetics and large structural changes accompanying with the intercalation of large-size and divalent Ca2+. Few reported cathodes can exceed 100 cycles with large overpotentials and limited capacities. Thus, this clearly calls for the development of reliable cathode materials or strategy to mitigate above issues. In this project, we propose to develop and probe into a stable intercalation cathode with a rigid open framework and high voltage to pair with the as-established graphite/calcium anodes for high-energy calcium ion full cells. Based on the PI’s preliminary study, vanadium fluorophosphate (VPF) is a promising model system with fast cation diffusion paths and multi-electron transfer capability. Specifically, we will (1) elucidate the structure-property-performance relationship of VPF cathode by tuning the chemical compositions of VPF to correlate electrochemical performance with the host structures, (2) investigate the calcium storage mechanics and migration dynamics by synchrotron X-ray techniques and density functional theory calculations, (3) optimize the VPF cathodes by nanostructural engineering and carbon coating, (4) realize full cells by pairing the proposed cathodes with graphite or/and calcium anodes and compatible electrolytes. The success of this work will fill the knowledge gap of divalent calcium ion insertion/extraction in a stable intercalation cathode, also will contribute practically to the development of low-cost, high-energy and safe calcium rechargeable batteries. 綠色能源的高效利用是滿足社會可持續發展的必然要求。儘管過去幾十年鋰離子電池在為便攜式電子設備供電方面發揮了至關重要的作用，但有限的鋰資源阻礙了鋰電池在大規模儲能體系中的應用。在受到越來越多關注的非鋰電池體系中，鈣電池被認為是最有前途的之一，因為鈣離子的二價性質、低還原電位，將帶來能量密度上的突破。地殼中高豐度的鈣也預示著低成本的鈣電池。然而，由於缺乏合適的電極材料，鈣電池的發展停滯不前。對於負極材料，申請人近期研究發現鈣離子能够在石墨中可逆脫嵌，並實現 97 mAh g-1的高容量和2 A g-1的高倍率性能。負極材料的成功表明鈣離子電池是可行的。然而，由於鈣離子緩慢的扩散動力學和大尺寸鈣離子嵌入导致较大結構變化，正極材料研究進展緩慢，很少有報導的正極可以穩定循環100次。 在本項目中，我們提出開發一種具有剛性開放框架和高電壓的穩定插層正極，並與現有的石墨或鈣負極配對，構建高性能鈣離子全電池。申請人初步研究表明氟磷酸釩 (VPF) 是一種很有前途的正極結構，具有快速的陽離子擴散路徑和多電子轉移能力。具體而言，我們將(1)通過調整 VPF 的化學成分以將電化學性能與主體結構相關聯來闡明VPF正極的材料結構-材料性能-電化學性能關係，(2)通過同步加速器X射線衍射實驗和密度泛函理論計算研究VPF的儲鈣機理和遷移動力學，(3)通過納米結構工程和碳塗層優化VPF正極，(4)將所提出的正極與石墨或鈣金屬負極和兼容的電解質配對實現鈣離子全電池。這項工作的成功將填補穩定插層正極材料中鈣離子嵌入/脫出機理的認知空白，也將為低成本、高能量和安全的可充電鈣電池的發展做出實際貢獻。

25216121.label: Realisation of objectives
25216121.value: This project successfully achieved its objectives by developing high-performance vanadium fluorophosphate cathodes for calcium-ion batteries, elucidating their structure-performance relationships, and demonstrating their practical viability in full-cell configurations. The following sections detail the realization of each objective. 1: To elucidate the structure-performance relationship for vanadium fluorophosphate cathodes by tuning chemical compositions. This objective was fully achieved. A clear relationship between fluorine content, operating voltage, and structural stability was established, identifying key parameters governing calcium storage. We synthesized a series of vanadium fluorophosphates with tailored compositions, specifically Na1V2(PO4)2Fx (x=1, 1.4, 3). Systematic electrochemical analysis revealed a direct correlation between fluorine content and the average discharge voltage. The N1VPF3 (x=3) cathode delivered a high voltage of 3.5 V versus Ca2+/Ca, significantly higher than the 3.0 V for the N1VPF1 (x=1) sample. This was attributed to the enhanced inductive effect of the highly electronegative fluorine, which stabilizes the redox couple and elevates the working potential. This work was published in Small, 2022, 2107853. To further improve the redox voltage of polyanionic cathodes, we further developed a polyanionic K-vacant KxVPO4F (x~0) (designated as K0VPF), characterized by plentiful interstitial spaces, as a high-voltage and ultra-stable cathode material. In CIBs, the working voltage of the K0VPF is determined to be 4.2 V vs. Ca2+/Ca, representing the highest value reported for CIB cathode materials to date. The experimental and theoretical investigations revealed that the minimal volume changes and low cation diffusion barriers within the interstices are the origins contributing to the extraordinary stability and high-power capabilities of K0VPF. The K0VPF//Ca full cells display extraordinarily high discharge voltages of 3.8 V and a reasonable cycle life of 40 cycles with 70% retention. This work was published in Advanced Energy Materials 2024, 14, 2302700 and featured as a front cover. Polyanionic cathodes usually exhibit single-electron transfer per unit, rendering limited specific capacity and energy densities. We then proposed a new cathode of CaxNaV1.5Cr0.5(PO4)3 (0 ≤ x ≤1.4) (N1VCP) for high-capacity and ultra-stable CIBs by unlocking 1.87-electron transfer per vanadium redox center during Ca-ion insertion. Through strategic Cr-doping and initial extraction of two Na⁺ ions from Na3V1.5Cr0.5(PO4)3 parent host, we obtain a framework that facilitates asymmetric charge compensation during the subsequent Ca2+ intercalation. The inclusion of Cr, with its additional valence electron ([Ar]3d⁵4s¹) than V ([Ar]3d34s2), significantly enhances the ionic diffusion kinetics. This design allows multielectron reactions of 1.87-electron transfer per vanadium redox center to participate in the electrochemical reactions, achieving a remarkable capacity of 162 mAh g−1 and a record-high energy density of ≈400 Wh kg−1. This work was recently published in Advanced Materials 2025, 37(41), e06603. 2: To disclose calcium storage and diffusion behaviors by in-situ characterizations and calculations. This objective was comprehensively achieved. We have established in-depth understandings of the calcium storage mechanism and ion transport kinetics by a suite of advanced characterization techniques. In situ X-ray diffraction was crucial for monitoring the structural evolution of cathodes like K0VPF, N1VPF3 and N1VCP during cycling, directly revealing an ultra-low volume change (1.9% for K0VPF, 1.8% for N1VCP and 0.9% for N1VPF3), which explains the exceptional cycling stability. X-ray absorption spectroscopy at the V K-edge confirmed the reversible redox activity of vanadium during Ca2+ (de)intercalation, showing clear shifts in absorption edges corresponding to the V3+/V4+ redox couple for K0VPF and N1VPF3, and multielectron transfer of V2+/V3+ and V3+/V4+ redox couple for N1VCP. The presence of V2+ in the C1.4N1VCP structure was confirmed by 23Na nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) measurement. The local structural evolutions associated with the VO6 octahedra were examined by extended X-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) analysis. First-principles density functional theory calculations complemented experimental findings by identifying favorable Ca2+ diffusion pathways along the open framework of the NASICON structure and determining relatively low energy barriers (e.g., ≈0.75 eV for K0VPF, ≈0.74 eV for N1VCP and ≈0.79 eV for N1VPF3), which rationalize the decent rate capabilities in Ca-ion cells. The insertion of Ca ions in the about polyanionic structures were directly visualized using atomic-resolution iDPC-STEM. Different from the Z-contrast characteristic of high-angle annular dark-field (HAADF) STEM imaging, iDPC-STEM enables the simultaneous visualization of both light and heavy elements. To elucidate the Ca ion diffusion kinetics in C1.4N1VCP, we employed GITT to calculate the Ca ion diffusion coefficients, which results were verified by DFT calculations. 3: To construct Ca-ion full cells with optimal cathodes for high energy density and stability. This objective was substantially achieved in terms of energy density but partially achieved regarding long-term cycle life. The project successfully constructed and evaluated calcium metal full cells by pairing the optimized vanadium fluorophosphate cathodes (K0VPF, N1VPF3 and N1VCP) with Ca metal anodes. The N1VPF3//Ca full cells delivered an initial energy density of 342 Wh kg-1, 318 Wh kg-1 for N1VCP//Ca, and ≈300 Wh kg-1 for K0VPF//Ca. Taking the N1VCP//Ca full cell as an example, we utilized 0.5 M Ca[B(hfip)4]2 DME electrolyte that enables reversible Ca metal plating/stripping reactions and presents a high oxidation stability (>4 V). This Ca metal full cell delivered a notable cycle life of 50 cycles with energy densities of above 300 Wh Kg−1, representing an unprecedented achievement for Ca metal full cells thus far. Although this cyclability is far from satisfactory to meeting the practical application requirement, it stands at the frontier in the emerging field of Ca metal batteries. In the future, intensive efforts are required to develop suitable electrolytes that are compatible with reversible Ca metal stripping and plating reactions and meet the high voltage requirement for our successfully demonstrated polyanionic cathodes. Overall, we have successfully realized the three main objectives in this project. It elucidated the critical structure-performance relationships in vanadium fluorophosphates, provided a deep mechanistic understanding of calcium storage, and demonstrated the potential for high-performance Ca metal batteries. While challenges at the anode-electrolyte interface require further development, achievements in this project mark significant progress toward the emerging calcium-ion battery technology.

25216121.label: Major findings and research outcome
25216121.value: Major findings: This project achieved significant advances in the development of high-performance polyanionic cathodes for calcium-ion batteries (CIBs) by integrating rational materials design, in-depth mechanistic investigation, and full-cell demonstrations. Through systematic compositional tuning of vanadium fluorophosphates, we established clear structure–property relationships governing Ca²⁺ storage. Increasing fluorine content was shown to elevate operating voltages and enhance structural robustness, enabling the development of high-voltage materials such as Na1V2(PO4)2F3 (3.5 V vs. Ca²⁺/Ca).[1] Building on these insights, we designed a K-vacant KxVPO4F (x ≈ 0) [2] framework featuring abundant interstitial sites, achieving a record-high potential of 4.2 V and exceptional structural stability arising from minimal volume change and low Ca-ion diffusion barriers. To overcome the intrinsic capacity limitations of polyanionic compounds, we further introduced a multielectron-active CaxNaV1.5Cr0.5(PO4)3 cathode, [3] in which Cr doping and Na extraction activate 1.87-electron transfer per vanadium, resulting in a high capacity of 162 mAh g⁻¹ and an energy density of ~400 Wh kg⁻¹. Comprehensive in-situ characterizations, including XRD, XAS, EXAFS, and atomic-resolution iDPC-STEM, elucidated the structural evolution and redox processes during Ca-ion (de)intercalation. Complementary DFT calculations and electrochemical measurements revealed favorable Ca²⁺ transport pathways with low activation barriers (~0.74–0.79 eV), consistent with their appealing rate performance. Leveraging these optimized materials, Ca-metal full cells were constructed, delivering state-of-the-art energy densities of ~340 Wh kg⁻¹, which establishes a strong foundation for future realization of high-energy CIBs. Under the support of this project, we have also developed high-capacity 9,10-phenanthrenequinone (PQ) and tetracarboxylic diimide (PTCDI) [4] small molecule cathodes in Ca-ion batteries, summarized the state-of-the-art progress in Ca metal batteries,[5] and investigated amorphous iron molybdate cathodes with multi-mechanistic insertion reactions.[6] Research outcome: During the operation of this project, we have published six papers in top journals like Advanced Materials (two papers), Advanced Energy Materials (front cover paper), Advanced Functional Materials (two papers), Small, and Small Methods. We have also been actively attending conferences, seminars, and workshops to disseminate the interesting research findings, including the Electrochemical Society (ECS) meeting.[7] Two PhD students were trained during this project, one of which was awarded by a PhD degree at PolyU and another passes the PhD Confirmation Examination.[8]

25216121.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25216121.value: The global shift towards sustainable energy sources like solar and wind demands affordable energy storage systems to ensure continuous power supply. The intrinsic abundance makes Ca batteries promising for cost-effective, large-scale and sustainable energy storage applications. In this project, we have successfully developed ultrastable, high-voltage, and high-energy polyanionic cathode materials for Ca ion batteries. Nevertheless, the intercalation-type cathodes suffer challenges of limited capacities and sluggish insertion kinetics. In addition, suitable electrolytes that can simultaneously meet the high-voltage stability for cathodes and be compatible with Ca metal stripping/plating reactions are still inaccessible. To further propel the realization of practical Ca ion batteries, we plan to develop high-capacity organic cathodes and new electrolyte systems by applying CRF and GRF projects, considering the multifaceted challenges of the emerging multivalent metal battery system.

25216121.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25216121.value: The global imperative for sustainable energy solutions and pervasive electrification necessitates the development of more affordable and reliable energy storage devices than that our current lithium-ion batteries can offer. Calcium ion battery is a promising solution to this challenge. Calcium is over 2600 times richer than lithium in the Earth’s crust and possesses dendrite-free deposition in anodes, thus ensuring battery affordability and safety. Nevertheless, the implementation of calcium batteries suffers the lack of suitable cathode materials to successfully accommodate calcium ions during discharge and charge. This project has developed a series of advanced cathodes featured with high-voltage, high-capacity, and ultralong life, all of which are important to high-performance calcium ion batteries. Apart from demonstrating advanced energy storage materials, this project also reveals previously unknown science that governs the divalent metal ion storage behaviors.

25218321.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25218321.value: Data-driven, real-time, and collaborative decision support systems will be indispensable in the near future. The airspace is divided into several parts and managed by different air traffic control (ATC) centres. The runway and waypoint arrival time of an approaching path are regulated by the ATC, and the pilot follows the suggested arrival time and determines the approach speed. A pilot could make up the arrival time by speed acceleration or at economic speed based on the required dynamic time of arrival and airline fuel consumption policy. Therefore, it would be very challenging for an ATC tower to make the terminal traffic flow decision preciously based on the constantly changing terminal airspace traffic in the rudimentary spacing measure of a terminal manoeuvring area (TMA). We could utilise the benefits of advanced automatic surveillance-broadcast technology to envisage terminal traffic flow decision-making and terminal airspace congestion control in a collaborative model. This project aims to develop calibrated mathematical models and an on-line algorithmic framework supporting the terminal traffic flow decision with regional aeronautical information from adjacent flight information regions (FIRs) and data from real-time surveillance-broadcast technology. The collaborative decision-making and situational awareness in ATC can enhance the visibility of flight activities and facilitate the estimation of incoming traffic in the area control jurisdiction. In the planning stage (usually few hours before the actual operations), effective management of demand and capacity optimisation could ensure better allocation of safety and capacity reservation on landing slot, flight separation distance and capability of recovery from major distributions. At the operational level, the terminal airspace congestion control, capacity management and safe separation can be adjusted in the collaborative air traffic management. This research would help foster further harmonious research on adaptive decision-making in ATC and will contribute to both theory and practices in promoting a next-generation air transportation system. 為決策支持系統配備數據驅動、實時反饋以及協同決策能力已成為一種发展趨勢。針對終端區域內的交通流量管制問題，需要設計穩健的終端空中流量調度方法，以提升整個空中及地面交通的流通量。同時，為了提供實時或近實時的解決方案，需在多部門之間(空中交通管制、飛行員、航空公司等)進行協同決策，並提出相應的智能決策算法。具體而言，將空中管制中的不確定性因素以極端情景進行分析，從而定制穩健的航班調度方案。此方案能大大提高空中及地面交通的流通量，確保航班之間的有效安全距離及提供充足的調度緩衝空間。若出現航班延誤、延誤傳播及飛機升降供求失衡的情況，此方案能為空中交通管制人員迅速恢復航班的流通量及機場運作的一般容量。本項目擬采用創新的“協同運作-航班軌跡實時預測模型-在線校準模型”框架，有效提升終端內航班實時監控的能力，同時提升航班軌跡預測準確率、及對空中延誤及延誤傳播等現象提出更有效的解決方案。其次，本項目擬根據“鄰近飛行資訊區域情報和自動監控-廣播技術”，設計一種實時監控方法，提出面向空中交通管制問題的數據驅動決策方案。所采用的技術能夠提升標準進場程序的穩健性及網絡強韌性，形成全局時域空域的決策概念，降低運行偏差以確保空管決策質量。最後優化算法設計，確保算法的決策參數具有高度適應性，能在有效的決策時間內為各類型決策場景提供最優或近似最優解。本項目的研究成果有望將為未來基於數據驅動的終端交通流量模型設計、以及空中交通管制系統構建提供基礎。

25218321.label: Major findings and research outcome
25218321.value: In this research, we developed several novel optimisation methods and modelling approaches to enhance runway throughput and terminal traffic flow capacity. Runways are consistently the bottleneck in aircraft arrival and departure management. We sought to further improve capacity by advancing dynamic wake separation, gate assignment, and terminal traffic flow management, taking into account the stochastic and robust nature of operational uncertainties. The following objectives were achieved through this project: (1) the development of real-time and near-real-time decision-making tools for tactical terminal airspace operations; (2) the design and development of novel mathematical models and online-calibrated models to improve the robustness of airspace solutions and network resilience in pre-tactical phases; and (3) the creation of innovative algorithmic components to achieve better algorithm convergence and computational performance. The key contributions of this research are the enhancement of decision-making quality through data-driven optimisation methods and the mitigation of the adverse effects of uncertainty on air traffic operations. The Principal Investigator has published eight journal articles and several conference papers as part of this project, with two further manuscripts currently under review. One PhD thesis has been completed, and partial fulfilment of a second PhD award is expected by December 2025. In total, two PhD students have been trained and supported through this project.

25218321.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25218321.value: There are several avenues for future research building on this project. Hong Kong airspace is located in the subtropical zone, and various climatic and weather hazards can affect the effectiveness and safety of air traffic control in this region. Therefore, further research into atmospheric science and satellite observation has the potential to contribute to the nowcasting and projection of weather hazard dynamics, and to assess their impact on arrival and departure management. This direction could significantly enhance the resilience and safety of air traffic operations in the region.

25218321.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25218321.value: Aircraft arrival and departure operations are highly sensitive to congestion in the airspace, runways, and airports. On one hand, it is important to rely on real-time and re-optimised approaches to resolve potential conflicts and coordinate airfield resources. On the other hand, making good use of flight and airport operational data allows us to project future airspace congestion levels and plan ahead to avoid delays and inefficiencies in flight operations. This project aimed to estimate the required aircraft wake separation, predict potential flight delays, and support the design and development of advanced solutions for gate assignment, flight transit services, aircraft scheduling and sequencing, and terminal traffic flow. By applying stochastic programming, robust optimisation, and distributionally robust optimisation, we addressed various types of operational delays. The project has successfully tackled these operational challenges and improved the efficiency and reliability of flight operations.

25220021.label: Project Objectives
25220021.value: Design and manufacture an X-ray transparent rotary shear experimental apparatus that is coupled with X-ray micro-computed tomography (micro-CT) technology for in situ observation of rock joint evolution under shearing. This experimental set-up will be the long-term research platform for the applicant’s group to conduct research on various engineering and scientific topics related to rock discontinuities. Use the newly developed experimental apparatus to directly observe rock joint roughness evolution and associate it to the variation of the shear strength. This will provide the first systematically in situ observation of rock joint surface roughness evolution under different stress conditions. Based on this observation, a new shear strength constitutive model considering the evolving roughness will be formulated. Investigate the seismic signatures associated with the rock joint surface evolution using acoustic emission (AE) monitoring and correlate these seismic characteristics of AE activities to the surface roughness evolution process and shear behaviour. The established correlation will support the assessment of joint condition through seismic monitoring.
