25220021.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25220021.value: Rock joints largely determine the strength and stability of a rock mass. Landslides caused by rock slope failure are one of the most common geo-hazards. It is a worldwide problem, especially for hilly regions, causing thousands of fatalities and can have a significant economic impact. The current landslide monitoring and early warning systems use information such as rainfall and surface mapping. This is helpful because rainfall is one of the most important factors that trigger the catastrophic failure on critically weakened rock joints. However, how the rock joints weaken over time and how we can infer this weakening process are questions still unclear. The major limitations being that we cannot see through the rock, and the rock joint surface conditions cannot be examined. A large number of laboratory and field studies suggested that joint surface roughness controls the failure process, and this process is usually accompanied by seismic signals (micro-earthquakes). However, a quantitative relationship among joint surface roughness, joint shear behaviour, and seismic characteristics have not yet been found. In this proposed project, a new experimental apparatus will be developed to quantitatively investigate the weakening process of rock joints. This apparatus will be X-ray “transparent”, to allow the deformation and surface roughness evolution of the tested rock joint to be directly observed using X-ray micro-computed tomography (micro-CT) technology. In addition, specialised sensors (acoustic emission sensors) will be used to monitor the micro-earthquakes associated with the imaged joint evolution process. With this innovative combination of technologies, we will explore the correlations between joint surface roughness, joint shear slip behaviour, and seismicity. A series of experiments at different stress conditions will be conducted on synthetic rock (cast gypsum) and Hong Kong granite samples. Two key questions will be addressed: (1) How the rock joint surface roughness evolves with increasing slipping displacement and how it influences the shear behaviour? and (2) What are the seismic signatures associated with this evolution process? This proposed project will establish an innovative experimental platform and make significant advancement in the understanding of joint evolution process. The outcome of this project will be the first step towards inferring joint surface maturity (i.e., surface roughness and stress condition) using seismic monitoring. These findings could facilitate more reliable rock slope failure monitoring and early warning approaches. 岩石节理很大程度上決定了岩體的强度。岩石滑坡是最常見的地質災害之一。岩石滑坡帶來的災害在全世界都是一個挑戰，特別是地貌崎嶇的地區。這些災害導致嚴重的社會影響和經濟損失。現有的岩石節理滑坡檢測和預報系統，大多基於降雨和對岩石斜坡表面的分析。這是因爲降雨是觸發滑坡的重要因素。然而，我們對岩石節理面的损伤、磨蚀和弱化過程還所知甚少。因爲岩石是非透明介質，所以我們無法直接觀察節理面的變化。大量實驗室研究表明，节理面在剪切过程中的力學性質和表面粗糙度有直接聯係，同时伴随微地震现象。這些現象之間的定量聯係的研究還不完備。 本項目以此爲背景，通過自主研發一套CT原位環剪試驗設備來定量研究節理漸進破壞過程。這套設備可以在CT掃描下直接連續觀察測試試樣。我們還會結合聲發射探頭來監測微地震事件和節理表面損傷以及節理力學性質的聯係。我們會對不同的岩石樣品進行一系列的測試來回答兩個關鍵問題：（1）岩石節理粗糙度如何隨著剪切距離的增加而變化，以及該變化如何影響節理的力學性質？（2）在節理損傷演化過程中，微地震信號的特徵如何改變？ 該項目可以建立一個長期試驗平臺，對提高岩石節理破壞機理有重要意義。該項目的成果是聯係岩石節理破壞程度和微地震信號的第一步，在岩石邊坡檢測和滑坡預報中有很大的應用前景。

25220021.label: Realisation of objectives
25220021.value: A micro-CT system with in situ loading test capacity has been set up, providing us with a powerful tool for imaging and analysing samples in three dimensions. This directly aligns with Objective 1 of developing experimental and observational platforms for detailed study of rock joint evolution. In addition to the setup of the micro-CT system, students and postdocs have been trained to use it effectively, ensuring that the system can be used to its full potential. Preliminary results were obtained and published in international conferences in the first half of the project (See Conference Papers C2, C4&C5 in Part C), and developed into full journal papers as described below. The PhD candidate trained in this project will graduate in 2026. We investigate the problem in a multiscale approach. At mm-scale (micro-scale), we leverage advanced numerical modelling (hybrid finite-discrete element method, FDEM) and high-resolution imaging (surface scans and micro-CT) to digitise, simulate and analyse the progressive damage and seismic activity on rock shear surfaces. By capturing the heterogeneity of damage and seismic events at asperity contacts, our research provides critical insights into the mechanisms controlling shear strength and roughness evolution, which supports Objective 2: formulating constitutive models that incorporate evolving surface roughness. The identification of different failure mechanisms (crushing, fracturing) and their spatial distribution offers empirical data and conceptual frameworks necessary for model development (See Journal Paper J3 in Part C). At cm-scale (i.e., mesoscale), we use laboratory direct shear tests to complement the above research by focusing on direct laboratory experiments with acoustic emission (AE) monitoring during shear tests involving proppant. This experimental approach addresses the project Objectives 2&3 to observe and quantify the relationship between surface roughness, shear behaviour, and seismic activity in real time. The detailed analysis of AE event patterns—distinguishing between proppant slipping, crushing, and asperity failure—demonstrates how seismic signals can be used to infer the stages of shear and the evolving condition of the fracture surface. This directly addresses the third objective, which is to correlate AE characteristics with surface evolution and shear behaviour, enabling seismic monitoring as a diagnostic tool (See J4 in Part C). Pertaining to Objective 2, we conducted a series of experimental studies to investigate rock joint roughness evolution and associate it with the variation of the shear strength under different stress conditions (See J1 & C1 in Part C). Rock joints that draw scientists’ and engineers’ attention are typically filled will granular materials (i.e., gouge material), which are weaker and less understood. We systematically investigated the impact of the granular filling material on the shear deformation of fractures and the potential consequent-induced shear failure. We explore the systematics of frictional behaviour, deformability, and dilatancy of filled fractures to define the complex response to different fracture roughness and filling material. We conducted shear experiments on rough granite fractures to investigate the effect of granular filling material on the shear deformation of fractures. Our results show that granular filling material reduces cohesion and internal friction, reduces the shear stiffness, delays the shear displacement to diminished peak strength, reduces the magnitude of shear dilation, and promotes ductile shear failure that is analogous to aseismic creep. We also found that the presence of granular filling material reduces shear dilation. A systematic transition in shear behaviour occurs from fracture-roughness-dominant to filling material-dominant with the increased amount of the granular filling material that is augmented by increased grain size. Long-wavelength fracture undulations may engage at large shear displacements, causing increased frictional resistance. This suggests an intrinsic scale effect. Thus, the convolved interactions between the granular filling material and fracture roughness require careful assessment of their impact on creating and sustaining permeability and modes of aseismic versus seismic ruptures. To achieve project Objective 3, we use the developed in situ testing (See J3, C2, C4 & C5 in Part C). Previous studies suggest that granular filling material plays a significant role in joint shear behaviour. We performed an experiment on a sheared granular laboratory joint that was time-lapsed imaged with an X-ray micro-CT and continuously monitored for stress, torque, displacement, and acoustic emissions (AEs). The experiment exhibits stress relaxation accompanied by AEs. We used a three-dimensional micro-CT model coupled with a hybrid continuum-discrete numerical method to reproduce the experiment. Burger’s contact model is applied to the grain contacts to describe the rheological behaviour of the granular filling material. The evolution of the model microstructures, including coordination number, contact force, and anisotropies of the contact force chain, are monitored during relaxation. We also calculated the energy budget to study the energy release characteristics of AEs. The results show that an exponential decay model can properly describe long-term stress relaxation. Sudden stress variations corresponding to AE bursts are observed in laboratory and numerical experiments and exhibit a decay event rate that follows Omori’s law. Two types of AEs with distinguished signal characteristics are captured both in the laboratory experiment and numerical simulation. We identified that high-frequency events are induced by contact failures within the granular layer, while low-frequency events are related to the interaction between joint walls and filling granular particles. In addition, we developed a novel machine learning-based roughness analysis tool (See C3 in Part C). Roughness is important in determining the shear strength of rock joints. Using optical surface scanning technology and machine learning, we propose a new machine learning method to characterise 2D rock joint roughness. Rough rock joint surfaces are scanned and digitized using a 3D surface scanner, and 2D profiles are extracted from the 3D surface for roughness analysis. The profiles are stored in the form of one-dimensional vectors and then separated into a training set and a validation set randomly for further training, prediction, and verification. Convolutional neural networks (CNN) are established and fine-tuned in MATLAB software to train and predict roughness parameters of each profile such as root mean square roughness (RMS), root mean square of profile slopes (Z2), skewness (Rsk), and kurtosis (Rku). The trained models build relationships between different morphologies of rock joints and their corresponding roughness parameters. The proposed method provides a fast and accurate approach to determining the rock joint roughness without sophisticated empirical or statistical roughness analysis. Moreover, we investigated the characteristics of AE for different rock types during fracturing (See J2 in Part C). We conducted a comparative laboratory investigation of the cracking behaviour of granite, marble, and sandstone using semi-circular bending (SCB) tests on pre-notched specimens with acoustic emission (AE) monitored. We analysed and compared the spatial-temporal evolution, relative amplitude, and source mechanisms of the AE events. The temporal evolution patterns of AE events are generally similar among the three rocks. We found that the differences in the quantity, distribution, and source mechanisms of AE events are related to the distinct microstructural characteristics of the three rocks. The results provide valuable insights into the understanding of the correlation between rock microscopic features and characteristics of AE activities that may facilitate more rigorous AE analysis in rock engineering practice.

25220021.label: Major findings and research outcome
25220021.value: The research has yielded several significant findings and outcomes that advance the understanding of rock joint evolution and mechanics. The establishment of a micro-CT system with in situ loading capacity has provided a powerful platform for three-dimensional imaging and analysis of rock samples under mechanical stress, directly supporting the development of advanced experimental and observational capabilities (see C2, C4, C5 in Part C). This system has enabled detailed visualisation of internal damage processes and facilitated the training of researchers in cutting-edge imaging techniques. A major outcome is the multiscale investigation of rock joint behaviour. At the micro-scale, the integration of high-resolution micro-CT imaging with hybrid finite-discrete element modelling (FDEM) has allowed for the digitisation and simulation of progressive damage and seismic activity on rock shear surfaces. This approach has revealed the heterogeneous nature of damage mechanisms (e.g., crushing and fracturing) at asperity contacts, providing critical empirical data for the formulation of constitutive models that account for evolving surface roughness (see J3 in Part C). These insights are essential for predicting shear strength and roughness evolution in natural and engineered rock systems. At the mesoscale, laboratory direct shear tests with acoustic emission (AE) monitoring have clarified the relationship between surface roughness, shear behaviour, and seismic activity. The research has distinguished AE signatures associated with proppant slipping, crushing, and asperity failure, demonstrating that AE monitoring can serve as a diagnostic tool for tracking fracture evolution in real time (see J4). Another key finding is the impact of granular filling materials on joint shear behaviour. Systematic experiments have shown that granular fillings reduce cohesion, internal friction, and shear stiffness, delay peak strength, and promote ductile, aseismic shear failure. The transition from roughness-dominated to filling-dominated shear behaviour, influenced by filling amount and grain size, highlights the complex interplay between fracture morphology and infill properties (see J1, C1). In situ micro-CT experiments, combined with numerical modelling, have captured stress relaxation and AE bursts that follow Omori’s law, identifying two distinct AE types linked to different microstructural processes (see J3, C2, C4, C5). Additionally, a novel machine learning-based tool for rapid 2D roughness characterization has been developed, offering fast and accurate analysis using optical scanning and convolutional neural networks (see C3). Finally, comparative AE studies on granite, marble, and sandstone during fracturing have revealed rock-type-dependent AE distributions and mechanisms, deepening the understanding of how microstructural characteristics influence AE activity and providing a foundation for improved AE analysis in rock engineering applications (see J2).

25220021.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25220021.value: The research outcomes present substantial potential for further development. The integration of micro-CT imaging with in situ testing and advanced numerical modelling offers a robust framework for exploring more complex rock joint systems, including those with heterogeneous mineralogy or multi-phase fillings. Coupled hydro-mechanical-chemical processes could be investigated. Future work could expand to larger-scale experiments and field applications, validating laboratory findings under natural conditions. The established correlations between acoustic emission signatures and fracture evolution could facilitate predictive monitoring systems for rock stability in engineering and geohazard contexts. The proposed course of action includes scaling up experimental campaigns, enhancing machine learning models with diverse data, and collaborating with industry partners to implement these diagnostic tools in real-world scenarios. This approach will bridge laboratory research with practical applications, advancing both scientific understanding and engineering practice.

25220021.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25220021.value: This research project focuses on understanding how discontinuities in rocks change and behave under different conditions. Using advanced imaging technology, especially micro-CT scans. This technology allows us to see inside rocks in three dimensions as they are being loaded. This helps us to observe how cracks form, grow, and interact during the rock failure process. We also use computer models and machine learning to analyse the roughness of rock surfaces and predict how they will respond to loading. The significance of this work lies in its ability to reveal hidden details about how rocks are damaged and break, which is important for building safer slopes, tunnels, dams, and other structures, as well as for understanding earthquakes. Overall, this research provides valuable tools and knowledge that can improve safety and efficiency in construction, mining, and natural disaster prevention.

25503621.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25503621.value: With the upcoming next-generation 5G networks, the amount of online content explodes, which forces consumers to either cut down their mobile data consumption or purchase expensive data plans with more gigabytes. In order to stimulate consumers to use more data, Internet service provider (ISP) is investigating new business models that encourage the content provider (CP) to sponsor data for consumers. To get compensated by the CP, consumers are obliged to opt in incentivized value-exchange advertising. This new business model facilitates a value exchange between the ISP, the CP, marketing practitioners, and consumers by turning mobile data into currency, so that the entire mobile ecosystem operates on an unparalleled mobile engagement platform. This study investigates this phenomenon using a game-theoretical framework incorporating both sides of the market, whereby on one side marketing practitioners deploy incentivized ads on CP’s platform; while on the other side consumers are heterogeneous in the intrinsic valuation they derive from the consumption of CP’s premium content. In particular, this study aims at investigating the optimal strategies for the content provider and the ISP in the mobile ecosystem and providing practical implications for the marketing practitioners to deploy incentivized advertising on content provider’s platform. The result of this study will also provide managerial insights for policymakers to regulate the telecommunication market and enhance consumer welfare, which is a critical issue in the upcoming 5G era. 随着即将推出的下一代 5G 网络，在线内容的数量呈爆炸式增长，这迫使消费者要么减少移动数据消耗，要么购买具有更多流量的昂贵数据计划。为了刺激消费者使用更多数据，互联网服务提供商 (ISP) 正在研究鼓励内容提供商 (CP) 为消费者赞助数据的新商业模式。为了获得 CP 的补偿，消费者需要与激励性的价值交换广告互动。这种新的商业模式通过将移动数据转化为货币，促进了 ISP、CP、营销从业者和消费者之间的价值交换，从而使整个移动生态系统在一个前所未有的移动参与平台上运行。本课题使用包含双边市场的博弈论框架来研究这一现象，一边是在 CP 的平台上部署激励广告的营销从业者；而另一边是从消费CP的内容获得异质的内在价值的消费者。本研究旨在调查移动生态系统中内容提供商和互联网服务提供商的最佳策略，并为营销从业者在内容提供商的平台上部署激励广告提供实际指导意义。作为即将到来的 5G 时代的一个关键问题，这项研究的结果还将为政策制定者规范电信市场和提高消费者福利提供管理建议。

25503621.label: Realisation of objectives
25503621.value: Achievement of Project Objectives The project has successfully fulfilled all five stated objectives through the development and analysis of a stylized game-theoretical model grounded in two-sided market theory. The model captures the strategic interactions among content providers (CPs), mobile network operators (MNOs), advertisers, and consumers, and offers nuanced insights into the emerging business model of sponsored data enabled by value-exchange advertising. The extent to which each objective has been achieved is elaborated as follows: 1. To conduct a game-theoretical analysis of the mechanism behind sponsored data via value-exchange advertising This objective was fully achieved through the construction of a multi-stage game-theoretical model that characterizes the behaviors of key stakeholders in the telecommunications ecosystem. The model integrates the dynamics of sponsored data provision, advertising revenue generation, and consumer utility. It differentiates between traditional advertising and value-exchange advertising (e.g., reward tasks), allowing a rigorous exploration of the economic mechanisms underlying the adoption and impact of this new business model. The analysis identifies how different revenue models and pricing schemes influence each player’s strategy, and reveals the endogenous tensions and trade-offs that emerge in a sponsored data environment. 2. To investigate the marketing practitioners’ optimal choice of content providers and advertising pricing The project demonstrates that the CP’s optimal pricing and subsidization decisions are critically dependent on the revenue potential of different advertising formats. Contrary to prior assumptions in the literature, the results show that an increase in reward-task advertising revenue does not necessarily motivate CPs to expand subsidization. Instead, it prompts a strategic recalibration in response to anticipated changes in the MNO’s pricing behavior. The model provides clear implications for marketing managers in terms of selecting advertising partners and pricing schemes under varying market conditions and revenue structures. 3. To explore content providers’ optimal subsidization rate for sponsored data This objective was achieved through a detailed analysis of the CP’s optimization problem. The study identifies a non-monotonic relationship between advertising revenue and the CP’s decision to subsidize data access. Specifically, while higher revenue from traditional advertising leads to increased subsidization (as it improves the return on investment in user acquisition), higher revenue from reward-task advertising results in lower optimal subsidization, due to increased data prices imposed by MNOs. This highlights an important strategic consideration for CPs balancing user engagement and cost-efficiency. 4. To investigate the Internet service provider’s optimal data-sponsoring scheme and data pricing decisions The MNO’s decision-making was modeled as a strategic response to the CP’s subsidization and advertising choices. The analysis uncovers a critical insight: when CP revenue from reward tasks is relatively low, aggressive pricing by MNOs can lead to a loss in profit for both parties, creating a lose-lose outcome. However, when CP revenue is sufficiently high, both parties benefit. These findings suggest that MNOs must adopt a calibrated pricing strategy rather than pursue maximal extraction. The model thus provides prescriptive guidance on optimal price-setting in sponsored data markets. 5. To examine the effects of sponsored data on consumer surplus and social welfare The project rigorously assesses the welfare implications of sponsored data. It reveals that, contrary to the common narrative, sponsored data may reduce consumer surplus under specific conditions—particularly when the CP’s traditional advertising revenue is low relative to reward-task revenue. In such scenarios, consumers may face a higher marginal cost of data (either monetary or effort-based), leading to reduced welfare. Furthermore, the analysis highlights potential regulatory concerns, particularly regarding competition among CPs of varying sizes. Large CPs benefit disproportionately from subsidization schemes, potentially entrenching market dominance and reducing entry opportunities for smaller players. These insights inform both welfare analysis and policy discourse. In conclusion, the project has comprehensively met its objectives by advancing theoretical understanding, offering empirical predictions, and identifying actionable insights for industry practitioners and policymakers. The findings contribute to the academic literature on digital platform economics, sponsored data mechanisms, and mobile advertising strategies, and provide a solid foundation for future research and regulatory evaluation.

25503621.label: Major findings and research outcome
25503621.value: When the revenue rate of the content provider (CP) increases, one may expect a rise in the CP’s optimal subsidization rate to motivate consumers to consume more content, generating more profit for the CP. However, interestingly, we show that the CP’s optimal subsidization rate decreases with the revenue rate of reward tasks (Proposition 1). This surprising result reveals the unexpected effect of the CP’s revenue rates of reward tasks and traditional advertising on its willingness to provide sponsored data. It implies that, counterintuitively, the CP should offer a low subsidization rate when the marginal revenue of reward tasks is high. Intuitively, a higher revenue rate could potentially generate higher profit for the CP. However, our analysis shows that the effect of the revenue rate of reward tasks on the CP’s profit is not monotone (Proposition 2). A practical insight of this result is that the mobile network operator’s (MNO’s) excessive extraction of the CP’s revenue from reward tasks could discourage the CP from subsidizing consumers with sponsored data, which leads to less consumption of digital content by consumers and hurts the profit of both the CP and MNO. Our analyses reveal that introducing sponsored data from the CP does not necessarily increase consumer surplus (Proposition 3). Our results demonstrate that while the new business practice of rewarding consumers with sponsored data after they accomplish some tasks could be welfare-enhancing for customers, this is not always the case. Thus, although this business practice is promoted by major MNOs who claim the business model to be welfare-enhancing, it requires attention from policymakers to decide whether to allow sponsored data under certain market conditions.

25503621.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25503621.value: Potential for Further Development and Proposed Course of Action Building on the current analytic framework, the research holds strong potential for further development through empirical validation and model extension. In future work, we propose collaborating with mobile network operators (MNOs) and content providers (CPs) to conduct field experiments that test our theoretical predictions in real-world settings. This will allow us to examine actual user behavior, advertiser response, and pricing strategies under various reward-task and subsidization scenarios. Additionally, the model can be extended to incorporate consumer heterogeneity, multi-homing behavior, and competition among CPs or MNOs, thereby capturing more complex market dynamics. Such extensions will enhance the robustness and applicability of our findings to policy and managerial decision-making. These efforts will deepen our understanding of value-exchange advertising and its implications for market efficiency, consumer welfare, and platform competition, and contribute novel insights to both the academic literature and industry practice.

25503621.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25503621.value: This research explores a new business model in the mobile internet world, where users can receive free mobile data by completing simple reward tasks—such as watching short ads or playing trial games. We studied how companies like telecom operators and app providers decide how much free data to give, how much to charge for ads, and how these decisions affect their profits and users’ experience. Using mathematical models, we found that giving away free data is not always beneficial to users or companies. In some cases, it may actually reduce user benefits, especially when users must do too many tasks for little reward or when prices rise because of increased demand. We also found that big companies might gain more from this model than smaller ones, potentially hurting competition. This research is important because reward-based data sponsorship is becoming more common in mobile apps and services. Our findings can help companies make better pricing and marketing decisions, and guide policymakers in ensuring fair competition and consumer protection. Overall, this project helps us understand how digital content can be delivered more efficiently and fairly in today’s mobile-driven world.

25505121.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25505121.value: 华尔街分析师在一个充满金融风险的环境中工作。然而，人们对他们自己的个人风险偏好以及这如何影响他们的研究知之甚少。理解这一点很重要，因为机构投资者严重依赖卖方分析师的研究，并且需要了解风险偏好如何影响研究产出、质量和覆盖范围。我的兴趣在于分析师适应个人风险偏好变化的策略是否适用于他们的专业研究选择。由于卖方分析师的风险偏好是不可观察的，在我的实证检验中，我依靠个人财富冲击来识别可能增加风险厌恶情绪的分析师。特别是，我推测相对于其他分析师，遭受个人财富冲击的分析师更有可能寻求研究策略来管理其职业声誉和职业的下行风险。 分析师可以使用许多此类策略。首先，分析师可以改变他们研究的极端程度；例如，他们可以发布不那么大胆的预测和建议，以降低出现大预测错误的风险。此外，他们可以在其他分析师之后而不是在其他分析师之前发布研究报告，以便根据更完整的信息集进行预测。其次，他们可以使他们的研究生产多样化；例如，发布更广泛的研究成果，以减少任何一个预测的权重。分析师还可以在预测范围内进行多样化；例如，他们可以每月更新而不是每季度更新以降低时间风险。第三，在覆盖方面，分析师可以形成风险较小的覆盖投资组合，甚至可以将现有覆盖公司的研究工作重新分配给波动较小的公司。我推测这些策略以及其他策略可以帮助分析师管理职业风险。当然，许多相同的策略会影响他们研究的增量价值。因此，我的论点的关键是，考虑到他们的个人财富受到冲击，分析师的行动将受到保护职业和声誉的下行风险的驱动。 总的来说，我有两个目标。第一，研究分析师风险偏好的个人特征，这种研究对资本市场研究来说是新颖的、并且是机构投资者感兴趣的。其次，研究个人特征的外生变化是否会影响分析师工作——这解决了大多数现有分析师特征和特征研究中的固有选择问题。

25505121.label: Realisation of objectives
25505121.value: This project set out to accomplish two primary objectives: (1) to examine audit partners’ risk preferences—a largely underexplored individual trait in the audit literature—through the lens of personal wealth shocks, and (2) to investigate how such risk preferences influence audit quality. We have successfully achieved both objectives through the development and implementation of a novel empirical design. Objective 1: Examine an audit partner’s risk preference using personal wealth shocks as a proxy We addressed this objective by constructing a unique and credible identification strategy based on exogenous negative wealth shocks. Specifically, we used the change in housing wealth experienced by U.S. audit partners during the 2007–2009 financial crisis as an instrument to capture shocks to personal wealth. Homeownership constitutes a major component of individual wealth in the U.S., and the financial crisis provides an unexpected, exogenous macroeconomic event with significant variation in local housing returns. By using hand-collected data on audit partners’ real estate holdings, we computed partner-specific wealth shocks. Our design allows for heterogeneous treatment intensities and captures how the severity of past negative wealth shocks influences long-term risk preferences. The identification strategy is conceptually grounded in utility theory, which posits that individuals with declining wealth exhibit increased risk aversion. It also draws on imprinting theory and the experience effects literature, which suggest that salient personal experiences can have enduring impacts on behavior. Our empirical evidence is consistent with these theories, suggesting that greater personal wealth losses during the financial crisis imprint audit partners with greater risk aversion that persists over time. Objective 2: Explore the impact of audit partners’ risk preference on audit quality We assessed the long-term impact of these personal wealth shocks on audit quality by examining restatement rates for audits conducted between 2016 and 2021. Using a large sample of over 10,000 audit engagements linked to nearly 2,000 unique engagement partners, we find that the likelihood of financial statement restatements decreases with the magnitude of negative housing returns experienced by the audit partner during the crisis. This finding suggests that wealth shocks in the distant past lead to more conservative and risk-averse behavior in the audit setting, thereby enhancing audit quality. To isolate the risk aversion mechanism, we conducted several cross-sectional analyses. The effect is more pronounced among audit partners who are likely to be more innately risk-averse (e.g., women, and those from countries with high uncertainty avoidance), in higher-risk engagement environments (e.g., clients with greater audit risk or stronger external monitoring), and in higher-risk institutional settings (e.g., firms with greater litigation or regulatory exposure). These results collectively support the interpretation that wealth shocks alter auditors’ risk preferences, which in turn shape their professional judgments. Our findings are robust to alternative model specifications (e.g., probit, logit) and audit quality measures (e.g., discretionary accruals, restatements due to fraud, audit fees, and the Financial Statement Divergence Score). We also address alternative explanations, such as audit partner ability, early-career recession exposure, and legal infractions, and demonstrate that our results are not confounded by these factors. Summary and Reflection Overall, the project objectives have been fully realized. We developed a novel and credible empirical design that identifies the causal effect of personal wealth shocks on risk preferences, and we documented their long-term implications for audit quality. The primary challenge lay in the data collection effort, particularly the manual matching of engagement partners to property records and the construction of housing returns. We overcame this challenge through systematic and rigorous procedures, achieving a high match rate (89%) for engagement partners. This study contributes to the growing literature on auditor heterogeneity by introducing a behavioral perspective grounded in personal economic experiences. It also advances the broader research agenda on experience effects, risk preferences, and professional decision-making.

25505121.label: Major findings and research outcome
25505121.value: We produced a complete working paper. The paper examines whether personal wealth shocks experienced by U.S. audit partners in the remote past have a long-term effect on their audit quality. To investigate this question, we hand-collect data on U.S. engagement partners’ real estate properties and use their housing returns during the 2007–2009 financial crisis as exogenous shocks to their personal wealth in the past. Analyzing audit engagements starting from 2016, we find that the likelihood of restatements by client firms decreases with the magnitude of negative housing returns experienced by engagement partners during the financial crisis, suggesting that past personal wealth shocks leave an imprint on audit partners and affect their audit quality over the long term. This effect is more pronounced when audit partners are more innately risk-averse, when audit firms face greater regulatory or litigation risks, when clients pose elevated audit risks, and when the risks of audit failures being exposed are higher, suggesting that increased risk aversion is the potential mechanism through which audit partners’ past personal wealth losses influence the quality of their future audits. Together, these findings underscore how past personal wealth experiences shape auditor partners’ risk preferences, which in turn influence their risk-taking behaviors in audits over time.

25505121.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25505121.value: This project explores whether personal financial experiences affect how auditors do their jobs. Specifically, we study U.S. audit partners who owned homes during the 2007–2009 financial crisis—a time when housing prices fell sharply. We examine whether those who suffered bigger losses in their home values became more cautious in their professional work years later. We find that audit partners who experienced greater declines in their housing wealth during the crisis are less likely to approve financial statements that later turn out to be wrong. This suggests they became more risk-averse due to the financial setback, and this change influenced how carefully they reviewed their clients’ accounting. Our study is important because it shows that personal financial experiences can have a long-term impact on professional decision-making—even in fields like auditing, which are governed by rules and procedures. It also highlights that not all auditors think or behave the same way, and these differences can affect the quality of financial reporting that investors and regulators rely on. In short, this research helps us understand how life events can shape professionals’ behavior, with meaningful implications for audit quality, investor protection, and financial market trust.

25601321.label: Project Objectives
25601321.value: To challenge the centrality of media-specific research when analyzing printworks. Chinese art historiography has privileged the approach of medium specificity in analyzing and interpreting art works. This methodology is entrenched in the discipline of Chinese art history, but nonetheless insufficient on its own for interpreting the cross-medial and visually hybrid experience in the prints by Hon Chi-fun, Van Lau and Cheung Yee. To supply an established methodology which formerly has not been utilized to analyze printworks. By examining printmaking in different cultural media, I explore how the basic component of this process of art — the printing block — operates as a tool to translate the physical characteristics of art from one medium to another. In doing so, I pinpoint the mechanism of cross-mediality for printmaking. To investigate the unique socio-political environment of post-1949 Hong Kong with respect to cross-media artistic practice. The printworks of Hon Chi-fun, Van Lau, and Cheung Yee were created in Hong Kong at a time when its environment functioned as an incubator for cross-media artistic practices. I discuss this context, focusing on how the city’s lack of a cultural foundation necessitated that artists seek inspiration from diverse array of sources, including art and non-art objects. This search for inspiration in Hong Kong’s environment is a precondition for the hybridization of media contained in these artists’ printworks. To initiate the development of a corpus of Hong Kong-based archival materials on alternative media, cross-mediality, and global contemporary margins. I intend to initially assemble primary research materials from a generation of senior and other respected artists, art practitioners, and their spouses, who were born in the first half of the twentieth century. In the context of this proposal, I will produce one peer-reviewed article for submission to a top-ranked journal in art history.

25601321.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25601321.value: This research project examines print art produced in Hong Kong from the 1960s to the 1970s through the lens of cross-mediality, a conceptual construct and methodological apparatus necessary for understanding printworks of this era. Chinese art history has long privileged medium-specificity as a research methodology — painting as distinct from sculpture, for instance, but this research approach has proved insufficient for interpreting print art on the whole, and in particular, the work produced by three first-generation Hong Kong modernist artists: Hon Chi-fun (1922–2019), Van Lau (b. 1933), and Cheung Yee (1936–2019). Their prints manifest distinct visual qualities — tonal for Hon, optical for Van, and sculptural for Cheung — that evoke the artists’ styles observable in their non-print works. In this way, their prints transcend the physical boundaries of different media because they borrow techniques from other artistic genres or non-art media. Consequently, these works warrant being examined with cross-medial methodology, both to shed light on their complex artistic contributions and to analyze the inevitable multimedia experiences the works construct for their viewers. Each of these three artists’ prints demonstrates a hybridization of a broad range of media, drawing both from institutional categories of the fine arts to techniques of traditional Chinese cultural production and contemporary culture of local food making. The act of viewing these works is also hybridized, mediated by the physical characteristics of and contexts surrounding borrowed media. I argue that these artists’ prints wove together a wide spectrum of media, whose nexus was the print itself, but which extended beyond the print’s frame to other media. Consequently, each print comes into being based upon the artist’s personal style of using the printing block. Furthermore, cross-media prints also naturally emerge from a complex field of social and cultural dynamics in 1960s–1970s Hong Kong: notions of modernizing art began to clash, prompting different ways of deploying Chinese culture, causing seismic shifts in the boundaries between the fine and vernacular arts. Medium specific interpretations are no longer sufficient to interpret the arts created by this generation of Hong Kong artists. Ultimately, this research seeks to prove the hypothesis that cross-mediality embodies each artist’s unique experience of “in-betweenness,” a socio-cultural condition of being situated somewhere between two recognized categories. Moreover, this work shows the way in which cross-mediality restores the reality of a rich artistic landscape in 1960s-1970s Hong Kong, which media specific interpretations had called a “cultural desert.”

25601921.label: Project Objectives
25601921.value: The aim of this study is to investigate a hybrid face-to-face and online mode of delivering a Mindfulness-Based Dementia Caregiving Programme (MBDCP) for family caregivers of persons with dementia. The following hypotheses will be explored: Family caregivers of persons with dementia (PWD) who will have received the MBDCP will demonstrate a significantly greater improvement in perceived stress (primary outcome), depressive symptoms, the positive aspect of caregiving, burden, dyadic relationship, and heart rate variability immediately after the intervention (T1), and at the 6-month follow-up (T2), compared with the control participants, who will have received basic education on dementia caregiving. The care-recipients of family caregivers who have received the MBDCP will demonstrate a significant greater improvement in neuropsychiatric symptoms after the intervention (T1), and at the 6-month follow-up (T2), compared with the control recipients. In addition, qualitative data will be collected on the participants in the MBDCP to identify the strengths, limitations, and therapeutic components of the intervention.

25601921.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25601921.value: 認知障礙症影響超過全球5000 萬人口,是一項需要優先處理的公共衛生問題。認知障礙症患者的家庭照顧者需要執行不同的護理工作，以及面對患者病情的不確定性，令他們承受高水平的壓力，對他們的健康及家庭關係構成威脅。研究顯示靜觀介入能有效減低照顧者的壓力，但同時亦有一些限制: 第一，靜觀導師需要經過長時間的培訓(例如2-3 年)，這將會阻礙靜觀的普及化。其次是過往高強度及長時間的靜觀課程（例如，8 週內 26 小時的靜觀減壓訓練）不太合乎成本效益及不足以容納社會上不斷增加的照顧者。此外，家庭照顧者需要處理大量的照顧工作，在參加面對面的培訓課程時經常遇到時間上的困難。最後，過往的靜觀課程不是專為認知障礙症照顧者以設，因此教學與照顧工中遇到的壓力問題並無太大關係（例如，如何平靜的回應被患者的行為問題）。因此有必要為認知障礙症的家庭照顧者制定一個簡化的靜觀課程，並可以交由非專業人士推行，同時可隔入日常照顧工作。 調查以面授和在線混合模式教授靜觀為本的認知障礙症護理計劃，以了解它對於減輕家庭照顧者壓力的成效。 本研究採用雙臂隨機對照試驗設計，將招募 126名認知障礙症家庭照顧者，他們會隨機分配到干預組，接受 6 次（每週一次，每次 1.5 小時）靜觀為本的認知障礙症護理課程或對照組接受關於認知障礙症的簡短教育課程。課程的第一、二、六節和第三、四、五的分別以面對面及在線方式進行。照顧者的壓力（主要結果）、抑鬱症狀、照顧的積極方面，負擔、二元關係、正念水平、心率變異性，以及被照護者的神經精神症狀會在干預後(T1和 6 個月後的隨訪中測量，並與基線 (T0) 進行比較。我們將會以廣義估計方程式模型，比較組別內及不同組別之間，所有研究變數隨時間發生的變化（即時間效應，組別效應，組別*時間效應） 這項研究將有助我們更有效運用靜觀，以減底認知障礙症患者的家庭照顧者的壓力，從而加強基層對照顧者的支援。

25609921.label: Project Objectives
25609921.value: To uncover and analyze the experience of reading pre-Tang poems among different late imperial readers from the beginning of the sixteenth century to the end of the nineteenth century. To explore reading materials included in late imperial poetry anthologies that contain numerous variations of pre-Tang poems by developing and applying a digital analytical tool. To digitize materials essential to the studies of literary anthologies and reception of early Chinese poetic tradition. Such materials include (1) prefaces and postscripts included in late imperial literary anthologies authored by editors, printers, and readers of the anthologies, and (2) pre-Tang poems selected in different anthologies, together with the textual variations found in them. 25609921.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25609921.value: This project develops and applies digital approaches to examining the practices of reading pre-Tang poetry anthologies from the 1500s to the 1800s. It aims to offer new perspectives and methods for studying the reception of early poetry in late imperial China. Along with the rise of print culture in late imperial China, pre-Tang poems became widely available and easily accessible via a large number of newly compiled literary anthologies, which often served as the primary reading materials for various reading publics, affording them with access to the pre-Tang poetic tradition. Actual readers of pre-Tang poetry anthologies include, for example, established elites, ordinary literary men, and young children. The late imperial practices of reading pre-Tang poems via anthologies thus remain essential to the study of the reception of early poetry. However, though current scholarship has investigated the late imperial interpretation of pre-Tang poetic tradition, the late imperial people’s reading practices and reading materials remain understudied. This project seeks to remedy this scholarly oversight. By digitizing and analyzing prefaces, postscripts, and other paratextual materials alike in 100 literary anthologies, this project discovers diverse readers’ reading experience and responses to the early poetic tradition, aiming to chronicle the gradual expansion of readership of pre-Tang poetry from the 16th century to the 19th century. With the development and application of a digital analytical tool, this project also restores the reading materials accessible to late imperial readers through identifying and comparing textual variations of similar pre-Tang poems selected in different Ming and Qing anthologies, seeking to uncover the impact of textual variations upon different interpretations of poems. This project is different from the PI’s doctoral dissertation. While the PI’s dissertation mainly focuses on the production side of pre-Tang poetry anthologies, including the compilation and publication processes, this project turns the attention to the consumption side of these books such as the practices of reading. While the PI’s dissertation analyzes materials included in poetry anthologies without inspecting the selected poems, this project extends to the investigation of the selected pre-Tang poems in anthologies. In sum, by developing new digital tools and approaches to explore the reception of early poems via anthologies in late imperial China, this project contributes to the studies of literary anthologies, Chinese literature, and print culture, shedding new light on the contributions of literary anthologies to the reception of literary tradition in the age of print culture. 本課題旨在開發並應用數字人文方法來研究中國明清時期16世紀至19世紀對先唐詩歌總集的閱讀實踐，旨在為研究中國早期詩歌在明清兩代的接受史提供新的視角和方法。 伴隨印刷文化在明清時期的興盛，先唐詩歌通過大量新編的文學選集流通並且容易為讀者獲得，這些選集因此往往成為各種閱讀群體的主要閱讀材料，使他們能夠接觸到先唐詩歌傳統。 明清兩代，先唐詩歌總集的實際讀者群體多種多樣，包括士人精英、普通文人，以及幼童。 因此，探索先唐選集的閱讀實踐對於研究早期詩歌於明清兩代的接受至關重要。 然而，儘管目前學界已探尋了明清時期對先唐詩歌傳統是如何詮釋的，但是時人的閱讀實踐以及他們的閱讀材料仍然沒有得到充分研究。本課題試圖彌補這一學術上的空白。 通過對大約100種文學選集中的序、跋和其他副文本材料進行數字化和分析，本課題旨在發掘不同讀者對早期詩歌傳統的閱讀體驗和反應，旨在記錄16世紀至19世紀先唐詩歌讀者群的逐漸擴大這一趨勢。通過數字分析工具的開發和應用，本課題還通過識別和比較不同明清選本中相同先唐詩的版本，還原明清讀者當時可獲得的真實閱讀材料，試圖揭示文本版本如何影響詩歌的詮釋。 本課題與課題主持人的博士論文不同。 課題主持人的博士論文主要關注先唐詩歌選集是如何生成的，包括選集的編纂和出版過程，而本課題則將注意力轉向探討這些書籍是如何被消費的，也就是讀者的閱讀實踐。 課題主持人的博士論文分析了詩歌選集中所包含的副文本材料，但未探索選集中所選的詩歌，而本課題則將研究對象擴展到對選集中所選先唐詩歌的分析和版本比較。 總之，本課題通過開發新的数字工具和方法，通過分析詩歌選集探尋早期詩歌於明清的接受。 本課題因此期望對文學選集、中國文學和印刷文化諸方面的研究做出貢獻，也希冀為文學選集如何在印本時代影響文學傳統的接受提供新的啟示。

26100521.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26100521.value: Eukaryotic phytoplankton production is central to global climate and fisheries, and thus, underpins a sustainable healthy ocean. Understanding the factors controlling their productivity, such as temperature, light, salinity, and viral lysis, is essential for predicting how the ocean ecosystem will respond to environmental changes. With the recent advancements in sequencing technology in the last decade, studies have shown that eukaryotic phytoplankton exhibit an enormous species richness, displaying a range of phylogenetic, morphological, and physiological diversity, and are prevalent in the global ocean. Despite their important ecological roles, eukaryotic phytoplankton, except for the bloom-forming algae, remain understudied in subtropical waters. Early metabarcoding studies have suggested that the South China Sea shelters highly diverse eukaryotic phytoplankton populations. However, until now, none of the eukaryotic phytoplankton hosts and viruses have been isolated from the northern South China Sea. The lack of cultivated eukaryotic algae-virus model systems hinders our understanding of the physiology and ecological functioning of these important algae, as well as how viruses and environmental factors shape their population dynamics. In the proposed project, (i) we will study how physiochemical factors affect the diversity and activity of eukaryotic algal hosts and viruses in the coastal South China Sea by directly sequencing the environmental DNA and RNA. In parallel, (ii) we will establish algae-virus models by isolating eukaryotic algal strains and their viruses from the same water to perform manipulative experiments in a controlled laboratory setting, and (iii) we will use these newly established algae-virus models to investigate the impact of environmental stresses on algal growth and viral replication. We aim to reveal the underlying mechanism of the host response by identifying genes that are associated with stress response or viral infection. The proposed project will provide a better understanding of the ecology of eukaryotic algae and viruses in the South China Sea and how the eukaryotic algae respond to environmental changes and viral infection. Using the environmental sequencing data and eukaryotic algae-virus model, we can better predict how eukaryotic algae will respond to climate change and other anthropogenic changes as well as their influence on primary productivity and biogeochemical cycles. 真核浮游植物生產力對全球氣候和漁業至關重要, 並同時支撐著可持續發展的海洋。因此了解控制其生產力的因素，如溫度、光照、鹽度和病毒裂解，對於預測海洋生態系統將如何應對環境變化十分關鍵。隨著近十年來測序技術的進步，研究顯示真核浮游植物有豐富的物種, 並且在全球海洋中普遍存在著系統發育、形態和生理上的多樣性。儘管它們具有重要的生態價值，但除了形成水華的藻類外，真核浮游植物在亞熱帶水域仍未得到充分研究。早期的宏條形碼(Metabarcoding)研究表明，南中國海有著高度多樣化的真核浮游植物種群。然而，到目前為止，還沒有研究從南中國海北部分離到真核浮游植物宿主和其他病毒。缺乏可培養的真核藻類-病毒模型系統阻礙了我們對這些重要藻類的生理學和生態功能的理解，並使病毒和環境因素如何塑造種群動態變得難以研究。在這項研究中， 我們將(i)通過對環境 DNA 和 RNA 的直接測序來研究環境因素如何影響南中國海沿岸真核藻類宿主和病毒的多樣性和活性；(ii)通過從同一水中分離真核藻株及其病毒來建立藻類病毒模型，以在實驗室環境中進行受控實驗；以及 (iii)使用這些新建立的藻類病毒模型來研究環境壓力對藻類生長和病毒複製的影響。我們期望通過識別和應激反應或病毒感染相關的基因來揭示宿主反應的潛在機制。該研究將有助於更好地了解南中國海真核藻類和病毒的生態，以及真核藻類如何應對環境變化和病毒感染。利用環境測序數據和真核藻類-病毒模型，我們可以更好地預測真核藻類將如何應對氣候變化和其他人類活動及其對初級生產力和生物地球化學循環的影響。

26201721.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26201721.value: This project aims to advance the understanding and management of the sustainable promotion of in-building decentralized water conservation systems such as rainwater harvesting and greywater recycling. Decentralized water (DW) systems provide alternative water sources to supplement centralized water systems (i.e., centralized water supply system for delivering drinking water and centralized wastewater treatment system for collecting wastewater). In Hong Kong, the annual mean rainfall is 2,400 mm. Moreover, around 50% domestic freshwater used for bath and laundry can be collected for greywater recycling. The large-scale implementation of DW systems could facilitate the utilization of these plentiful greywater and rainwater resources, which reduce the total water demand, improve the reliability of water supply, and mitigate the environmental impacts of urban water consumption. The promotion of DW systems involves a complex and dynamic process, including 1) The decision of adopting a DW system is controlled by individual buildings as opposed to the water utility. Therefore, the number of buildings adopting the decentralization determines the scale of implementation; 2) On urban scale, geographical locations can affect whether DW systems are more environmentally sustainable and economically viable to supplement the services from existing centralized water systems. The potential negative impact of DW systems on the operation of existing water systems should be considered, as it decreases the flow of the entire system. These critical decisions or issues have not been well examined in managing the sustainable promotion of DW systems. Our research objectives include: 1) Examination of how decisions of buildings affect the market demand and spatial distribution of DW systems; 2) Identification of optimal selections of buildings to install DW systems; and 3) Evaluation of financial incentives that may effectively promote sustainable adoption. We will develop a new integrated approach through (1) studying the spatial patterns of adoption (i.e., which buildings will adopt DW systems) and diffusion (i.e., when buildings will adopt DW systems) using a spatial agent-based model (ABM) that simulates the decisions of buildings; (2) applying spatial optimization techniques to identify the optimal distribution (i.e., which buildings should use DW systems); (3) leveraging ABM and spatial optimization to design and evaluate financial incentives. A U.S. city and a Hong Kong New Town using freshwater for toilet flushing will be used to develop and verify our integrated approach. Ultimately, this proposed research will improve the decision-making process and support know-how of the sustainable promotion of DW systems in cities. 該研究致力於進一步理解和管理建築分佈式水設施（包括雨水收集和灰水回用）的可持續推廣。分佈式水設施能夠提供額外的用水，補充集中式供水和污水處理設施。香港年平均降雨量約2400毫米。居民用水的50%主要用於洗澡和洗衣物，處理後可以實現灰水回用。大規模的分佈式水設施的推廣應用可以充分地利用這些寶貴的灰水和雨水資源，從而減低城市的總用水量，提供城市供水的可靠性，緩解城市水消耗的環境影響。 分佈式水設施的推廣是一個複雜動態的過程，其中包括1）是否採用分佈式水設施是由每個建築決定的，而不是供水公司。有多少建築採用分佈式水設施決定了應用的規模。2）在城市尺度，地理位置影響分佈式水設施是否更環境可持續、更經濟有效地補充現有集中式的供水和污水處理。分佈式水設施的大規模應用導致整個供水和污水處理系統的水流量下降，對集中式的供水和污水處理造成負面影響。這些關鍵的決策或者問題在分佈式水設施的可持續推廣研究中還尚未得到檢驗。 該項目的研究目標包括1）檢驗建築對分佈式水設施的使用決策如何影響分佈式水設施的市場需求和空間分佈；2）優化識別適宜採用分佈式水設施的建築；3）評價資金激勵對可持續推廣的效果。該項目將建立一套綜合性分析方法，首先構建個體模型模擬建築的決策過程，研究分佈式水設施使用的空間分佈和推廣；然後利用空間優化技術識別分佈式水設施的優化佈局；最後耦合個體決策模擬和空間優化設計和評價資金激勵的效果。該項目選擇美國城市和香港的新市鎮作爲研究案例完成分析方法的構建。該項目將有助於城市可持續地推廣分佈式水設施。

26201721.label: Realisation of objectives
26201721.value: Over the course of this four-year project, all stated objectives have been fully achieved. The research has significantly advanced the understanding of decentralized nonpotable water supply systems in urban environments through the development of two key modeling tools: a spatial agent-based model for projecting adoption patterns and a city-scale spatial optimization algorithm for infrastructure planning. These tools were applied to two contrasting case study cities—Hong Kong and Boston—to evaluate the performance and feasibility of decentralized water technologies under varying urban conditions. The findings have been disseminated through three peer-reviewed journal publications, including articles in Environmental Science & Technology and Water Research. For Objective #1, an integrated framework was developed to support sustainable planning and promotion of decentralized water technologies. The spatial agent-based model incorporates survey-based choice modeling, population synthesis, and techno-economic analysis to estimate adoption patterns. The spatial optimization algorithm includes modules for quantifying environmental and climate-related constraints of existing water systems, performing techno-economic modeling of decentralized systems, and formulating optimization strategies for siting and sizing facilities. Under Objective #2, we analyzed the spatial adoption and diffusion of decentralized water technologies. In Boston, early adoption was projected to occur in less developed neighborhoods. In contrast, in Hong Kong, strong demand was observed in newly developed areas, indicating a preference for integrating decentralized systems during the construction phase of urban development. Objective 3 focused on the spatial optimization of decentralized facility installations. In Boston, analysis indicated that to reduce energy use for water supply, decentralized systems should be installed in neighborhoods located farther from central treatment plants and with high nonpotable water demand, such as for landscape irrigation. In Hong Kong, spatial optimization identified cost-effective planning strategies for wastewater reuse, which included the installation of large facilities on Hong Kong Island and in Kowloon. For Objective 4, we integrated the spatial agent-based adoption model with the optimization analysis to evaluate alignment and trade-offs. In Boston, the agent-based model indicated early adoption in lower-income neighborhoods, while the optimization model recommended initial investment in affluent areas with higher energy footprints. This misalignment highlights equity concerns: while incentivizing adoption in wealthier neighborhoods may yield environmental benefits, it can also exacerbate social inequality in access to water services. Therefore, policies that require nonpotable water supply in high-consumption areas, coupled with efforts to reduce technology costs, should be considered. In Hong Kong, energy intensity for water supply is higher on Hong Kong Island and in Kowloon, while development is expanding in the northern region. Despite the demand for decentralized systems in the north, maximizing energy savings will require identifying ways to reduce energy intensity while ensuring the safety of nonpotable water reuse. Objective 5 involved a cross-city comparison to assess the feasibility and applicability of our integrated modeling framework. Through comparative studies in Boston and Hong Kong, we demonstrated the usefulness of this approach in identifying opportunities for decentralized water infrastructure. The findings also reveal how urban form influences technology suitability. In Boston, a low-density and sprawling city, rainwater harvesting is the preferred strategy. In contrast, Hong Kong’s high-density and compact urban form makes greywater recycling and wastewater reuse more appropriate. With capital subsidies, greywater recycling emerges as the more favorable option due to its lower capital and operational costs compared to wastewater reuse. This project also provided significant training opportunities for students. The Principal Investigator mentored both postgraduate and undergraduate students who played vital roles in this interdisciplinary, knowledge-driven research. One PhD and one MPhil student successfully completed their degrees as part of this project. This project has successfully delivered a comprehensive modeling framework and a set of analytical tools that can guide the planning and promotion of decentralized water infrastructure in urban environments. The insights gained from Hong Kong and Boston provide a foundation for extending this research to other global cities, supporting sustainable water strategies in the face of urbanization and climate change.

26201721.label: Major findings and research outcome
26201721.value: This research focused on the planning and optimization of decentralized water facilities, with the aim of understanding the potential of such technologies in urban neighborhoods. To this end, we developed a spatial agent-based model that integrates survey-based choice modeling, population synthesis, and techno-economic analysis to project the adoption of decentralized systems. This modeling approach is adaptable and can be applied to both decentralized water and energy technologies (Ghasemi, 2022). In Hong Kong, our analysis revealed strong demand for greywater recycling and wastewater reuse, particularly in new building developments. The model demonstrates that subsidizing capital investment can significantly accelerate adoption, with greywater recycling emerging as the preferred option due to its lower capital and operational costs. We also developed a spatial optimization framework, which includes modules for quantifying environmental and climate constraints of existing water systems, conducting techno-economic modeling of decentralized facilities, and formulating multi-objective optimization models. This framework was applied to study the optimal planning of building-based rainwater harvesting and greywater recycling systems in Boston (Li, 2022). Results from the Boston case study show that rainwater harvesting is significantly more applicable than greywater recycling for single-family residential communities. When analyzing the Pareto-front of solutions, two distinct clusters of census blocks emerged based on changes in the proportion of households selected for investment in decentralized systems at varying cost scenarios. One cluster consistently ranked higher in priority for deploying rainwater harvesting systems. Using a Random Forest classifier, we identified the key factors that explain why certain census blocks were prioritized. These include greater demand for nonpotable water, longer distances from centralized treatment facilities, and larger rooftop areas suitable for rainwater collection. In a separate study, we applied the optimization framework to evaluate the optimal degree of decentralization for wastewater reuse in Hong Kong (Li, 2024). The cost-effective solutions identified strategic locations for decentralized wastewater treatment plants in Kowloon and Hong Kong Island—areas where nonpotable water demand is high and electricity consumption for freshwater and seawater supply is significant. The optimized system indicates potential savings of approximately 6% in freshwater and 29.4% in seawater, though it would result in a 20.7% increase in electricity consumption. These findings highlight the importance of spatially informed planning in promoting decentralized water infrastructure and balancing environmental, economic, and energy trade-offs in urban water supply systems.

26201721.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
26201721.value: This project evaluated the potential of decentralized water technologies in urban neighborhoods. While technology-specific challenges such as reducing treatment costs and energy use are important, effective planning requires addressing broader system-level questions. These include the impact of large-scale deployment on existing infrastructure, planning under demand uncertainty and future land use changes, and assessing localized costs and energy intensities of decentralized systems in Hong Kong and the region. Such questions demand interdisciplinary knowledge integration and systems thinking, which often fall outside the scope of discipline-specific research. However, the General Research Fund (GRF) of Hong Kong’s Research Grants Council (RGC) is evaluated through a discipline-based framework, making it difficult for cross-disciplinary researchers to sustain research that bridges engineering, urban planning, and sustainability science. As a result, the Principal Investigator has relocated to Canada and secured funding from the Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council of Canada (NSERC) to continue this line of research, which strongly aligns with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) on water, infrastructure, and urban resilience. The PI remains sincerely grateful for the RGC-funded project, which provided a crucial foundation during the tenure-track period in Hong Kong and enabled the continuation of this important work.

26201721.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
26201721.value: This research project developed innovative modeling approaches to assess the potential of decentralized water technologies—specifically rainwater harvesting, greywater recycling, and wastewater reuse—in urban neighborhoods. We created a spatial agent-based model integrating survey-based choice modeling, population synthesis, and techno-economic analysis to project technology adoption. In Hong Kong, strong demand was identified for greywater recycling and wastewater reuse in new building developments. In contrast, rainwater harvesting was preferred in Boston. These differences highlight the critical role of urban form in shaping the feasibility and desirability of decentralized systems, as well as the value of our modeling framework for city-specific planning. We also developed a spatial optimization model to explore how decentralized water technologies can be strategically deployed to reduce freshwater use, minimize energy consumption, and maintain financial sustainability. The model identified optimal facility locations in both cities, offering actionable insights for integrating decentralized systems with existing infrastructure. Together, these methods provide a system-level understanding of how decentralized water solutions can enhance urban resilience. Our findings support cities in planning a transition toward more sustainable, climate-adaptive water systems—demonstrating the importance of interdisciplinary tools in addressing complex infrastructure and environmental challenges.

26202321.label: Project Objectives
26202321.value: Multi-task scene understanding at the representation learning level: Developing a generic probabilistic deep framework for cross-task structured learning via jointly modelling task-specific latent representations, latent dynamic kernels, and latent cross-task attentions, to learn rich cross-task relationships (e.g. consistency and complementarity) for effectively learning structured representation refinement of each individual task in a principled manner; Multi-task deep scene understanding at the network structure learning level: Instead of utilizing hand-crafted structures as in existing works, we explore effective and efficient network architecture search schemes to automatically discover multi-task deep scene understanding network architecture for simultaneously handling a bunch of challenging scene understanding tasks. We propose to jointly discover decoding network branches to enable robust task-specific representation learning, and branch connections among tasks to allow for highly effective cross-task information passing. Besides, we will develop efficient architecture search in the multi-task setting using well-designed differentiable dynamic graph sampling strategies for search space optimization; Multi-task deep scene understanding at the framework design level: Towards learning with least efforts of data labelling, we target at designing weakly- or self-supervised multi-task deep frameworks to model and learn multiple scene understanding tasks. We propose an instantiation of a self-supervised multi-task scene understanding framework, which learns a non-rigid scene model with a simultaneous reconstruction of dynamic foreground and static background via dense pose estimation and can jointly deal with several complex 2D and 3D tasks including object semantic understanding without any ground-truth supervision. The developed ideas in objective (i) and (ii) can be transferred here to boost the cross-task learning of deep representations and structures; Multi-task deep scene understanding at the application level: Transferring the developed models, algorithms, and frameworks from the above-mentioned objectives for building real-world Artificial Intelligence (AI) applications in scenarios such as self-driving, robotics navigation, and AR/VR.

26202321.value: 場景理解是計算機視覺領域極具挑戰性的範疇，其在各種現實智能應用中也起到基礎性的重要作用，包括自動駕駛、機器人導航以及虛擬或增強現實。高層次的場景理解系統例如自動駕駛通常需要同時學習和預測多種不同的關鍵性任務元素如場景三維深度、攝像機姿態、語義、輪廓和物體等。這些任務元素高度關聯同時本質上相互補充。多任務深度場景理解目的在於學習並利用跨任務關係如一致性和互補性來實現任務間的交互，從而使得單個任務的學習和預測性能得到有效提升。由於它的單次訓練達到多任務聯合預測推導的特性以及對於不同應用環境的高泛化性能力，多任務學習是朝向真正人工智能的重要途徑。存在的研究工作主要開展對於表徵融合、參數共享以及基於人工定義網絡結構的經驗探索，較大程度上限制了多任務理解框架的能力和應用靈活性。 該項目的研究目的是通過學習高效的跨任務深度交互來顯著提升多任務場景理解。主要的研究目標包括三個方面：（1）表徵層面：開發一個通用的概率深度框架實現原則性地建模和學習豐富的多任務間隱結構化關係，從而有力促進單個任務的表徵提煉；（2）結構層面：設計和實施神經網絡結構搜索策略來自動挖掘多任務場景理解網絡結構，實現最優化地構建具體任務相關的解碼分支以及跨任務的網絡連接來獲得有效的任務間信息傳遞；（3）框架層面： 創建弱監督或自監督的非剛性場景理解模型來聯合處理多個複雜的二維或三維場景理解任務，最大程度減少依賴任何昂貴的任務標記數據。在（1）和（2）層面提出的模型和算法亦可靈活地應用到框架層面來極大地增強跨任務表徵和結構學習。 項目預期會在多任務深度聯合學習、自動深度網絡結構優化以及場景理解方面帶來重要影響力。項目也會通過基於原則性建模指導深度神經網絡設計和理解來擴大其前沿研究領域，並對多任務深度場景理解任務做出顯著的理論和應用層面的技術貢獻。於所提出研究目標上的初步實驗結果展示了在多個具高度挑戰性的室內和室外場景理解評測基準上的顯著性能提升。

26202321.label: Realisation of objectives
26202321.value: The proposed project pursues four major objectives. To tackle these objectives, we developed a range of innovative research solutions, and published fourteen research papers at top-tier conferences and journals in the field, including CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, ICLR, and TPAMI. Below, we provide detailed descriptions of the research outputs corresponding to each objective. Objective 1: Develop a generic probability deep framework for cross-task structured learning. To achieve the first objective, we developed a diffusion-denoising probabilistic framework [4] for multi-task learning. This framework introduces a unified diffusion and denoising paradigm capable of modeling potential noise in task predictions or feature maps, thereby generating rectified outputs for multiple tasks. To further enhance multi-task consistency during the denoising process, we propose a multi-task conditioning strategy. This approach implicitly leverages the complementary relationships among tasks, facilitating the learning of unlabeled tasks and yielding substantial improvements in denoising performance across various dense prediction tasks. Objective 2: Discover automatically multi-task deep scene understanding architectures to simultaneously handle a bunch of challenging scene understanding tasks. To address this objective, we introduced a novel memorial mixture of experts structure [5] that automatically learns and assembles network modules to construct a dynamic multi-task network architecture. This approach enables effective cross-task interaction and delivers superior multi-task performance compared to previous static frameworks across challenging benchmarks. For 3D dense prediction, we proposed a generalized binary search network [6], achieving highly accurate scene depth estimation. Recognizing the widespread adoption of transformer architectures in perception tasks due to their powerful global modeling capabilities—crucial for multi-task interactive modeling—we further enhanced their effectiveness by designing an inverted pyramid structure combined with an attention-guided automatic token selection strategy, ensuring high efficiency in multi-task dense predictions [2, 7]. To further strengthen cross-task interactions, we developed a plug-and-play task prompting strategy [8]. This strategy can be seamlessly integrated into any transformer-based multi-task framework, enabling unified modeling of both task-generic and task-specific representations as well as cross-task interactions, all without the need for hand-crafted, task-specific structural designs. Objective 3: Explore multi-task scene understanding with least effort of data labeling, considering different weakly- or self-supervised multi-task deep frameworks. To accomplish this objective, we leveraged large-scale cross-modal foundation models, such as text-to-image models, to generate dense semantic masks and, subsequently, to synthesize images from these masks [9]. This strategy enabled us to significantly expand our training data, resulting in substantial improvements in semantic dense prediction performance. Additionally, we developed various auxiliary tasks that enhance semantic segmentation using only image-level labels, thereby greatly reducing annotation costs [12]. Furthermore, with only image-level labels available, we introduced novel multi-modal and multi-class-token designs for weakly supervised joint dense object classification and localization [1, 13]. These approaches significantly advanced state-of-the-art performance in these tasks and have become essential baselines for future research in this area. Objective 4: Transferring the developed models, algorithms, and frameworks to build real-world AI applications. We developed an innovative talking head generation system tailored for AR/VR applications, leveraging a unified 2D and 3D perception and generation framework [3, 14]. Our system predicts detailed 3D facial depth information, which is then used to condition the generation of talking face videos. This geometry-aware approach ensures consistent 3D facial structure throughout the video synthesis process, significantly enhancing realism and fidelity. The project has garnered substantial recognition, with nearly 1,000 stars on its GitHub repository and over 200 academic citations. Notably, the technology has been successfully transferred and deployed within Ali-Cloud, powering a range of digital human AR solutions. This demonstrates both the research impact and real-world applicability of our system in next-generation digital human applications. 26202321.label: Major findings and research outcome
26202321.value: The proposed project focuses on four primary objectives. To address these goals, we developed a range of innovative research solutions and frameworks: For the first objective, we designed a novel diffusion-denoising probabilistic framework for multi-task dense scene understanding. This framework effectively models cross-task relationships and generates high-quality predictions through its denoising process, even when task annotations are partially available. For the second objective, we introduced a series of methods that automatically discover dynamic network structures for effective cross-task interactions, as well as modules for task-specific and task-generic learning. These strategies can be broadly integrated into various multi-task learning frameworks to enhance both representation learning and prediction performance. For the third objective, we explored label-efficient multi-task learning in self-supervised and weakly supervised settings. Our methodologies leverage cross-task relationships to achieve high-performance multi-task prediction, even with limited supervision. We built a codebase for multi-task scene understanding based on transformers, which has gathered more than 300 stars and has become a popular codebase for research and development in this field. As a result of these advances, we have published eleven research papers in top-tier conferences and journals, including CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, ICLR, and TPAMI, establishing a clear impact in the field.

26202321.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
26202321.value: In future research, several promising directions can be pursued to advance multi-task visual scene understanding. A robust multi-task system must effectively manage a wide range of distinct tasks—both continuous and discrete—that require diverse forms of supervision. This calls for the system’s capability to automatically construct heterogeneous structures and representations, each tailored to the specific requirements of different tasks. Developing methodologies for building and optimizing these heterogeneous structures is essential for efficient multi-task learning. Moreover, a comprehensive multi-task dense understanding system demands pixel-level predictions and interactions across multiple tasks, which leads to significant computational overhead. This overhead poses a serious challenge to model scalability, especially in resource-constrained environments. To address this, it is crucial to harness task complementarity, enabling the system to reduce redundancy and computational cost while maintaining, or even enhancing, overall multi-task performance.

26202321.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
26202321.value: Multi-task visual scene understanding is a foundational research area in computer vision, crucial for enabling intelligent applications like autonomous driving, robotics, and AR/VR. Recent advances in deep learning have significantly elevated scene understanding performance. In practical scenarios, systems often need to perform multiple correlated tasks—such as depth estimation, semantic parsing, object detection, camera pose prediction, and 3D reconstruction—simultaneously for tasks like indoor or outdoor localization and navigation. Addressing these problems through multi-task deep scene understanding offers notable advantages for industrial applications. With a single training process, a unified model can handle all tasks, thus greatly reducing training time and computational resources compared to developing separate models for each task. Joint training allows for shared network structures and representations, leading to lower model capacity and facilitating efficient compression, which is vital for deployment on resource-constrained devices. Furthermore, sharing domain information and learned features across tasks enhances the model’s generalization ability in complex environments. Collectively, these benefits underscore the high value and impact of research in deep multi-task scene understanding for both academic advancement and practical industry deployment.
