26205921.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26205921.value: Urban mobility needs and patterns are evolving dramatically. Starting with innovations in digital channels, further spearheaded by the introduction of shared mobility, people’s modes of travel are changing from conventional single-mode transportation to multimodal transportation. Currently, multimodal transportation often requires travelers to book and pay separately for each segment of the journey, making services troublesome to use and difficult to coordinate. The emerging transport concept - Mobility-as-a-Service (MaaS) promises to solve this issue. Rather than buying transport services from individual transport service providers (TSPs), MaaS enables travelers to buy all forms of public transport and diverse car-based services (e.g. ridehailing, carsharing) through a single platform, thus increasing flexibility and improving travel experience for travelers. The integrated platform also helps TSPs to coordinate better with each other, increases rates of utilization and solves the first-and-last-mile problem for public transport services. A MaaS operator sits between travelers and TSPs, acting as a broker who purchases mobility resources from individual TSPs, constructs seamless transport services, then sells them to travelers in response to their demand. To ensure the sustainability of such a two-sided platform, the key challenge lies in matching travelers to TSPs so that travelers’ individual needs are satisfied, TSPs gain nonnegative profits and system efficiency is achieved. We aim to develop auction-based mobility resource allocation and pricing mechanisms to solve this matching problem. The research activity includes: First, we will develop a matching model to optimally allocate travelers to paths taking travelers’ strategic behavior into account. Travelers’ truthful requirements and valuations are elicited through an auction mechanism. We will develop an efficient algorithm to solve the matching model and design pricing rules to achieve system efficiency. Next, we will consider a scheme in which TSPs strategically report their operational costs and capacity to enable a better allocation. We will develop a double auction mechanism to determine the optimal matching, pricing and reward allocation. We will then develop an online auction mechanism which can be adopted readily in a dynamic environment. We propose a random permutation model-based dynamic algorithm to solve it. The algorithm will ensure computational efficiency and an acceptable approximation of the optimal offline system efficiency. This project will investigate theoretically interesting and practically important issues in multimodal mobility resource integration, allocation and pricing for a MaaS platform in both static and dynamic environments. We will conduct simulation experiments using real data sources to demonstrate the efficiency of the proposed auction mechanisms. 近年來，城市交通需求和出行特徵發生了巨大的變化，隨着通訊技術的發展和共享出行的推進，人們的出行方式由傳統的單一交通工具出行逐步轉變為多交通模式組合出行。而目前，多模式出行往往要求出行者單獨預定及支付各類交通工具，這種單獨運營的模式不僅增加了用戶負擔，而且使得各交通模式之間難以協調。旨在解決這一問題的「出行即服務」（Mobility-as-a-Service，簡稱MaaS）商業模式應運而生。MaaS平台整合了多種交通模式，包括公共交通、網約車、共享汽車等，出行者僅需通過一個平台即可享受綜合的出行服務，這不僅提高了消費用戶的出行靈活性，優化了出行體驗，也促進了各個交通運營商之間的協同合作，對提高汽車利用率和解決公共交通的「最後一公里」問題有重要意義。 MaaS 平台運營商居於出行者和各交通運營商之間，充當中間商的角色，從交通運營商處購買各類交通方式出行資源，整合後為消費者提供無縫銜接的出行服務以滿足他們的出行需求。要確保這樣一個雙邊平台的可持續發展，關鍵在於匹配出行者和各類交通模式，既要滿足出行者的個性化出行需求，又要確保個體交通運營商不虧本，同時整個系統能夠高效運轉。我們通過基於拍賣理論的交通資源分配和定價策略來解決這一匹配問題，研究內容主要分為以下三個方面： 首先，我們將構建考慮出行消費者博弈行為的匹配模型，對他們的出行路徑進行優化，而拍賣機制將確保每位用戶誠實地申報他們的出行需求及競價。我們所提出的算法能夠有效解決這一匹配問題，同時為了確保MaaS系統的高效性我們將設計相應的定價策略。 其次，考慮到各交通運營商的博弈行為，他們可能有策略地報告各種交通模式的運營成本及通行能力，以獲取更高的收益，我們擬提出一種雙向拍賣機制來決定交通資源的分配、出行者的收費定價及各交通運營商的收益分配。 然後，為了適應動態環境下的需求，我們將提出一種在線拍賣機制並設計相應的基於隨機排列模型的動態算法，同時確保計算高效性和解的準確性。 本項目從理論角度探究了MaaS平台在靜態和動態環境下的多模式交通資源整合、分配和定價問題，並通過真實數據進行模擬實驗，驗證所提出拍賣機制的有效性。

26208821.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26208821.value: 函數式編程已經在工業界迅速崛起。特別是在 Facebook、Twitter 和 Netflix 等科技巨頭公司中，越來越多的關鍵業務邏輯開始使用函數式編程實現。例如，Facebook 完全用 Haskell 實現了其關鍵的垃圾郵件檢測基礎設施；還開發了一種名為 ReasonML 的 OCaml 新方言用於 Web；並收購了 WhatsApp，這是一款用 Erlang 編寫的消息應用程序。函數式編程使編寫和推理代碼變得更簡單、並且減少了軟件和產品的缺陷以及進化和維護的成本。 儘管有這些好處，函數式程序往往比用傳統命令式語言編寫的同等解決方案運行得更慢、消耗的資源更多。C 和 C++ 等語言的現代編譯器在優化命令式程序方面已經非常成熟，它們通過先進的基於圖的中間表示來表示其控制和數據流。然而，這些技術面對函數式編程中的高階函數、惰性求值和不可變數據結構等方面並無長處。現有函數式編譯器還沒有跟上：因為它們通常仍然基於簡單的表達式樹表示，而這限制了其優化能力。這是迫切需要解決的問題，因為目前函數式程序的低效率無法讓工程師們更廣泛地採用函數式編程；同時，因為現有的函數式系統不必要地低效率，消耗了大量的計算資源，從而增加了像 Facebook 這樣公司的花銷。 在本提案中，我們提出了一種基於圖數據結構的優化函數式程序的新方法。這種方法很大程度上受到了早期的關於 λ 算子（函數式編程的形式基礎）的最優圖規約研究的啓發。該領域之前的工作完全集中在為函數式語言設計替代運行時系統上。本方法的主要創新之處在於將類似的方法應用於靜態編譯器的優化設計，這在以前是從未嘗試過的。我們的主要想法是，在優化圖規約過程用中常用的保留共享 β 規約計算的機制也可以用於在編譯時優化函數式程序。這提供了優秀的部分求值性能，同時避免過多的代碼重復。 此項目已經是現有的和微軟研究院持續合作的一部分，同时 Glasgow Haskell 編譯器的主要開發者也對我們的方法所提供的承諾表現出濃厚的興趣（見附錄中的合作函）。

26300721.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26300721.value: Asymmetric organocatalysis is among the most important research fields in synthetic chemistry. Many excellent catalytic asymmetric strategies have been developed for enantioselective chemical synthesis over the past 10 years. Asymmetric electrochemical catalysis, for example, has emerged as a promising method due to its enabling unprecedented tuning of reactivity and selectivity. Conventionally, enantiospecific electrocatalysis is achieved by a chiral bias imparted by a chiral reactant/catalyst/solvent/electrode via the “lock and key” mechanism. However, only a few examples of highly enantioselective electrosyntheses have been reported, and new generalized reaction strategies and mechanisms are required. To this end, a new concept was recently demonstrated in which controlled electron spin was used to obtain enantiospecificity in synthetic organic reactions. This new strategy is enabled by the electronic interaction between chiral auxiliary molecules and distinct enantiomers via their spin-polarized electrons, by means of the so-called chiral-induced spin selectivity (CISS) mechanism. However, spin-induced enantioselective chemical synthesis remains in its infancy, with enantioselectivity remaining low due to the low magnitude of spin polarization. More recently, we have demonstrated that spin polarization was highly efficient (>90%) in a system that integrated an inorganic metal-halide framework with a chiral organic sublattice. In this system, the embedded chiral organic moieties induced a chiroptical response from the inorganic metal-halide sublattice, which led to these two components combining to form chiral hybrid semiconductors. However, the structural interplay between the chiral organic molecules and the inorganic sublattice, as well as their potential to enable spin control via the CISS mechanisms, require exploration in a broader material scope. In addition, the application of controlled spin for asymmetric electrochemical reactions awaits further exploration. In this proposed study, we will address these important limitations and knowledge gaps by the following strategies: (1) developing a library of chiral hybrid metal-halide materials (solid state and nanocrystals) and investigating the chirality transfer mechanism between the inorganic and organic subunits; (2) investigating the effects of CISS via compositional tuning of the proposed and developed chiral hybrid metal-halide semiconductors; and (3) exploring enantioselective electrocatalysis by controlling spin states using the proposed chiral metal-halide materials. The findings of this proposed study will provide new reaction strategies for highly enantioselective electrocatalysis based on spin control, shed light on our mechanistic understanding of chirality transfer from the atomic scale to the nanoscale, and provide a quantitative understanding of the CISS effect. 不对称催化一直是合成化学中最重要的领域之一。近十年来，我们见证了不对称催化策略的长足发展。例如，不对称电催化由于可以同时调控反应的活性和选择性而逐渐成为一个较有前景的不对称合成方法。传统的不对称电催化策略利用引入手性的反应底物/催化剂/溶剂/电极等通过具有空间选择性的“锁钥模型”机理实现手性合成。然而，这类方法的底物选择具有明显的局限性，目前只有少数几个选择性高的不对称电催化反应被证实。因此，研究开发普适的、通用的不对称催化新策略和机理具有十分重要的意义。 近年来，一个新的概念，即利用可控的电子自旋态来实现不对称合成的策略被初步证实了其可行性。这个新策略利用自旋极化的电子和底物/中间体对映体的不同电子相互作用而非空间相互作用来实现手性合成。自旋极化电子可以通过引入手性分子，利用手性诱导自旋选择效应（chiral-induced spin selectivity，CISS）来实现。然而，通过电子自旋诱导手性合成策略目前刚刚起步，诸多科学问题仍然有待解决，且由于手性分子的低自旋极化率，目前的反应手性选择性仍然较低。 最近，我们的研究证明电子自旋在手性金属卤素杂化半导体中可以实现极高的自旋极化率（>90%）。在这类杂化半导体中，手性的有机分子嵌入无机金属卤化物中并自组装成杂化半导体，同时手性的有机组分赋予了无机组分光学活性。然而这类新材料中有机-无机组分的相互作用和手性转移机理仍然不清晰，同时，利用手性杂化材料通过手性诱导自旋选择实现自旋调控仍然急需进一步探索其内在机理和潜在应用。例如，利用自旋调控实现不对称电催化反应仍然有待研究。针对以上几个科学问题和研究现状，我们提出以下策略：（1）开发一系列手性金属-卤素杂化材料（固态和纳米晶）并研究其中有机-无机组分手性转移的机理；（2）通过调控组分和开发光谱表征手段揭示手性诱导自旋选择效应机理；（3）探索基于手性金属-卤素杂化材料的自旋调控于不对称电催化中的应用。我们拟开展的研究将为高效不对称电催化合成提供新的思路，揭示从分子到纳米多尺度手性转移的机理，并为手性诱导自旋选择效应的机理提供重要的实验模型。

26300721.label: Realisation of objectives
26300721.value: We have successfully realized all proposed objectives, including the design and synthesis of various chiral metal-halide semiconductors, study of structure-chiroptical-activity relationships, and selective electrocatalysis using spin-polarized electrons. 1. We have successfully developed a series of 2D, 1D, and 0D chiral metal-halide bulk crystals based on Pb, In, Sb, Cu, and Ag-Fe (double perovskite). They exhibit very interesting chiroptical activity (circular dichroism and circularly polarized luminescence). In addition, we also developed chiral perovskite nanocrystals, which display tunable and efficient circularly polarized luminescence in the blue, green and red regions. We have discovered new strategies for chirality transfer that give rise to chiral functional materials. 2. We have systematically studied the macroscopic, electronic, and structural origin of chiroptical activity in chiral metal-halide materials. By combining spectroscopic measurements and Mueller matrix analysis, we discover that the previously reported “apparent” anisotropy factor measured from circular dichroism (CD) in chiral MHS thin films is not an intrinsic chiroptical property, but rather, arising from an interference between the film’s linear birefringence (LB) and linear dichroism (LD). We combined magnetic circular dichroism (MCD) and reveal the key structure-chiroptical-activity relationship. We also design new chiral metal-halide materials that display efficient circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) and uncover the structure-CPL relationships. Our study has unveiled the fundamental mechanisms that govern the chirality transfer and chiroptical activity in these materials. 3. We have studied the spin polarization effect in novel chiral semiconductors using magnetic conductive-probe atomic force microscopy (CP-AFM) and transient absorption spectroscopy. We have revealed the microscopic mechanism of chiral induced spin selectivity in chiral metal-halide materials. 4. We have tested chiral hybrid compounds for electrocatalytic oxygen evolution reaction, which is a spin-selective process. Our chiral catalyst is demonstrated to display superior oxygen evolution activity and suppressed H2O2 byproduct compared to the achiral ones. Thus, asymmetric electrochemical synthesis can be achieved by chiral catalyst via the chiral induced spin selectivity.

26300721.label: Major findings and research outcome
26300721.value: This project has yielded substantial research outcomes, including the publication of 18 peer-reviewed journal articles and the delivery of 8 invited talks at both national and international conferences. Additionally, we have successfully trained 5 PhD students and 10 undergraduate students, equipping them with valuable skills and knowledge in the field. Notably, each postgraduate student funded by this project has published between 3 to 4 first-author papers, demonstrating a strong commitment to advancing their research. Our major findings have been highlighted in prestigious journals, showcasing the impact of our work. These publications include articles in leading journals such as JACS (2), Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. (2), Adv. Mater. (2), Nat. Sci. Rev. (1), Chem. Sci. (1), Adv. Funct. Mater. (1), ACS Nano (1), Adv. Opt. Mater. (2), and Nano Lett. (1). 26300721.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
26300721.value: This project has developed a series of unconventional semiconductors that enable control over light, charge, and spin states. These hybrid organic-inorganic semiconductors combine the properties of small chiral organic molecules with those of extended inorganic semiconductors, resulting in both semiconducting and chiroptical activity. We systematically investigated the structural origins of the emerging chiroptical activity and established key structure-property relationships, leading to design rules for achieving exceptional chiroptical effects, such as circular dichroism and circularly polarized luminescence. Additionally, the structural asymmetry facilitates spin control through the interaction between chirality and spin, known as chiral-induced spin selectivity (CISS). Using a wide range of spectroscopic techniques, we probed the fundamental mechanisms underlying CISS and demonstrated that spin-polarized electrons can be utilized for chemo-selective electrocatalysis. Overall, this project has resulted in the discovery of new materials and enhanced understanding of chirality and spin, paving the way for future advancements in spin-optoelectronics based on these chiral semiconductors.

26303921.label: Project Objectives
26303921.value: Objective 1: Build and analyze the non-local RNN to explicitly model two interacting areas and apply it to solve tasks using biologically plausible learning. Aim 1.1: Develop examples of non-local RNN that solve tasks such as associative memory, generating sequence, and coding. Aim 1.2: Analyze the dynamics of the non-local RNNs in terms of the connectivity and dynamic parameters, such as local and between connections, neuronal nonlinearity, and time constants. Aim 1.3: Explore biologically plausible learning algorithms, such as Hebbian learning and reinforcement learning, to establish the between-area connectivity in non-local RNN for solving tasks. Objective 2: Characterize spatial variability structure within and between interacting brain areas in the non-local RNN. Aim 2.1: Characterize the spatial variability in feedforward models at a fixed point and its relation to connectivity parameters. Aim 2.2: Generalize the results of Aim 2.1 to bidirectional non-local RNN and along a temporal trajectory of activity. Aim 2.3: Based on results from Aim 2.1, 2.2, make experimentally testable predictions on spatial variability and develop analysis methods that are suitable for single-trial activity data.

26303921.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26303921.value: Theoretical neuroscience has been very successful in understanding the dynamics of a local neuronal circuit and has been crucial for analyzing and interpreting experimental data. Recent technological advances have made it possible to record many neurons' activity across multiple brain areas simultaneously. Taking full advantage of such data requires quantitative understandings of neural dynamics and its relationship with connectivity beyond local circuits, a field that remain largely open. We propose to study a new model with two interacting brain areas, the non-local recurrent neural network (non-local RNN). Here the essential recurrent connections responsible for dynamics and functions arise from the feedback loop of between-area connections. In contrast, the local connectivity within each area is kept minimal (e.g., none, uniform, or random). This setup is motivated by recent experimental findings that computations previously thought to be carried out in local neuronal circuits, such as working memory, may largely depend on interaction loops with other brain areas. We will also build on the results and analysis methods of a recent line of theoretical breakthroughs. The authors studied a local circuit model with low rank connectivity that can be interpreted as a special case of the non-local RNN involving a simplified auxiliary population of neurons. Importantly, this indicates that the non-local RNN can support rich dynamics and, at the same time, allows for in-depth analyses of how the emerged dynamics (e.g., fixed points vs. chaos) depend on the connectivity parameters. The non-local RNN naturally points to new theoretical questions, such as adding nonlinearity to the auxiliary population. Our preliminary results suggest that this can improve the robustness of the fixed points useful for storing memories. We will also use the new model to address the lack of biological explanations of the low rank connectivity in existing work. In particular, we will study how to use biological learning to construct the between-area connections to solve tasks such as generating sequences. By explicitly modeling the two areas, the non-local RNN facilitates connecting theory to biological data and is particularly suited to study interactions between areas. One intriguing feature revealed by recent experiments is a low dimensional "interaction subspace," where a mechanistic explanation is missing. We will build on our previous work on the variability of neural activity to address this in the non-local RNN, leading to new testable predictions and analysis methods for experimental data. 理論神經科學可以成功地理解局部神經元迴路並且為分析和解釋實驗數據提供重要支持。近期的實驗技術進展讓同時紀錄大量、多個腦區的神經元活動成為可能。要充分利用這類數據，就需要在超出局部迴路的情形中，定量地理解神經動力學性質和連接結構的關係。這是一個有大量未知問題的研究方向。 我們提出研究一類新的兩個腦區相互作用的模型—非局部回返神經網絡。在此模型中對動力學和功能起核心作用的是區域間連結所形成的反饋環路。與此相對的，區域內的局部的連接則被設計為最簡（例如沒有連接、平均連接、或隨機連接）。這樣的設計是基於近期實驗中發現的一些原本被認為由局部迴路所負責的計算功能（如工作記憶）在很大程度上可能是依賴於腦區間的作用迴路。 我們還將基於並拓展一項近期的理論突破中的方法和結果。這些工作研究了一種具有低秩連接矩陣的局部網絡。這種網絡可以通過添加一族輔助神經元被解釋成非局部回返神經網絡的一個特例。重要的是，這些相關研究說明了非局部回返神經網絡可以支持豐富的動力學，而且又可以進行深入的理論分析來解釋其產生諸如不動點、混沌等現象與連接參數的關係。 非局部回返神經網絡自然地指向新的研究問題，例如對輔助神經元添加動力學方程所帶來的影響。我們的初步結果顯示這可以增強用來存儲記憶的不動點的魯棒性。我們還將用這個模型來解決在已有工作中所欠缺對低秩連接如何形成的生物學上的解釋。對此我們將研究如何用生物學習算法來建立區域間連接，使得網絡可以完成序列生成等任務。 通過在模型中顯式地描述兩個區域，非局部回返神經網絡可以更好地將理論和生物數據相聯繫，並且特別適合研究腦區間的相互作用。近期實驗中揭示的一個引人深思的現象是腦區間的低維度相互作用空間，而其尚缺乏機制上的解釋。我們將基於已有的對神經元活動差異性分析的工作來研究非局部回返神經網絡，並提出新的可檢驗的預測和分析實驗數據的方法。

26304221.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26304221.value: Two-dimensional (2D) metals realized on kagome lattice provide a rich platform to engineer novel quantum phases of matter, such as Chern insulators and unconventional superconductivity, through the combination of their unique electronic states with magnetism, spin-orbit coupling and electronic interactions. The intensifying research efforts on this topic, which touches on condensed matter physics and materials science, are also driven by the perspective application of these materials in energy-efficient electronic devices and quantum information processing. Experimental investigations of 2D kagome metals revealed their unique electronic structure and found signatures of topological electronic transport even at room temperature. Technologically relevant advances were made in the fabrication of these compounds, such as iron-tin (FeSn), via epitaxial growth, promising technological applications based on this scalable material platform. Nonetheless, little is known about the intricate interplay of their microscopic magnetic properties with Dirac electrons towards engendering topological states. The domain of interaction driven quantum phases that emerge from flat band electrons remains unexplored, too. Therefore, more experimental investigations on the microscopic origin of correlated and topological quantum states in these compounds are required. In this project, we propose to visualize the emergent quantum phases that are predicted to occur in 2D kagome metals using ultra-low-temperature scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) experiments. The unique combination of high-resolution spectroscopic capabilities with spin-sensitive measurement techniques and surface sensitivity will allow us to generate unprecedented experimental insight on their microscopic electronic and magnetic properties, which cannot be obtained through other experimental means. To this end, we will fabricate ultra-clean thin films of FeSn, cobalt-tin (CoSn) and FeXCo1-XSn using molecular beam epitaxy down to the monolayer limit, where STM experiments can access the entire 2D system. Finally, we will explore whether other 2D kagome metals with tailor-made electronic and magnetic properties can be synthesized by combining different transition metals, such as Ru and Rh, with the carbon group elements Sn and Pb, respectively. Our efforts will be complemented with electron transport and magnetometry experiments performed in collaboration with Prof. Rolf Lortz (HKUST). Photo-electron spectroscopy experiments will be conducted in collaboration with Dr. Niels Schroeter (PSI, Switzerland), and analytical model calculations and density-functional theory simulations will be done with Dr. Lukas Muechler (Flatiron Institute, USA). Our comprehensive approach will generate new microscopic insights into the electronic and magnetic properties of 2D kagome metals. Moreover, our work can potentially discover topological and correlated quantum phases of matter in this system. 擁有籠紋晶格結構的二維金屬具備獨特電子態。透過其與磁性、自旋-軌道作用和電子相互作用的組合，籠紋金屬為陳絕緣體，或非傳統超導體等新穎量子相物質提供設計平台。此研究課題涉及凝聚態物理和材料科學。而其在節能電子設備和量子信息處理中的應用前景，亦推動了對此課題的深入研究。對於二維籠紋金屬的實驗研究，亦揭露其獨特電子結構，以及室温具備拓撲電子傳輸的特徵。儘管在利用外延生長製造這些化合物（例如鐵-錫 (FeSn)）方面取得的技術進步使這種技術的可能應用充滿前景，但關於其微觀磁性與狄拉克電子對產生拓撲狀態的複雜相互作用知之甚少，從平帶電子中出現的相互作用驅動的量子相領域亦仍未被探索。因此，我們需要對這些化合物中關聯性和拓撲量子態的微觀起源進行更多的實驗研究。 在這個項目中，我們提議使用掃描穿隧顯微鏡 (STM) 實驗來可視化預測發生在二維籠紋金屬中的新興量子相。光譜高分辨率與對自旋敏感的測量技術，以及對金屬表面敏感的獨特結合，為我們提供對二維籠紋金屬的微觀磁性和電子特性前所未有的實驗見解，而這並無法透過其他實驗方式得到。為此，我們將使用達至單層極限的分子束外延以製造鐵-錫 (FeSn)、鈷-錫 (CoSn) 和FeXCo1-XSn 的超潔淨薄膜，並利用 STM 實驗以測量整個二維系統。最後，我們將探討是否可透過將不同的過渡金屬（如 Ru 和 Rh）與碳族元素 Sn 和 Pb 分別結合來合成其他具有定制電子特性和磁性的二維籠紋金屬。我們將與香港科技大學的洛鶴夫教授合作進行電子傳輸和磁力測定實驗。光電子能譜實驗將與瑞士Paul Scherrer Institute的 Niels Schroeter 博士合作進行，而分析模型計算和密度泛函理論模擬將與美國Flatiron Institute的 Lukas Muechler 博士合作進行。 我們的綜合方法將對二維籠紋金屬的電子特性和磁特性產生新的微觀見解。此外，我們的工作可能會發現該系統中物質的拓撲和關聯量子相。

26304221.label: Realisation of objectives
26304221.value: 1. We have realized the molecular beam epitaxy (MBE) of FeSn and CoSn. For the molecular beam epitaxy of FeSn, we have successfully adopted a recipe by the Chekeslky group (Appl. Phys. Lett. 115, 072403 (2019)) and realized high quality thin films of FeSn on the surface of SrTiO3 wafer pieces (size 5x5 mm2) cut in the (111) direction. The growth details are described in detail in the supplementary materials of our related publication (Physical Review X 14, 021046 (2024)). We were the first group to report the MBE growth of the kagome flat band material CoSn. We developed the epitaxy of CoSn along the (0001) crystallographic direction on Nb-doped SrTiO3 (111) substrate as described in detail in the supplementary materials of our related publication ((Physical Review Research 4, 043269 (2023))). 2. Right after the start of this project, several STM studies appeared that explored the electronic and topological properties of FeSn thin films and the phsics of the Dirac point (e.g., Scientific Reports 12, 14525 (2022), Communications Physics 5, 235 (2022)). Hence, we decided to first focus on the exploration of the electric material properties of FeSn using nonlinear Hall measurements. It had been predicted by a colleague at HKUST that the high symmetry of antiferromagnets can support Berry curvature multipoles that can give rise to higher order nonlinear anomalous Hall effects. Berry curvature multipoles appearing in topological quantum materials have recently attracted much attention. Their presence can manifest in novel phenomena, such as nonlinear anomalous Hall effects (NLAHE) which may also enable future applications in energy harvesting and high-frequency technology. It was shown that a Berry curvature dipole can give rise to a second-order NLAHE in materials of low crystalline symmetry. Here, we demonstrate a fundamentally new mechanism for Berry curvature multipoles in antiferromagnets that are supported by the underlying magnetic symmetries. Carrying out electric transport measurements on the kagome antiferromagnet FeSn, we observe a third-order NLAHE, which appears as a transverse voltage response at the third harmonic frequency when a longitudinal ac drive is applied. Interestingly, this NLAHE is strongest at and above room temperature. We combine these measurements with a scaling law analysis, a symmetry analysis, model calculations, first-principle calculations, and magnetic Monte Carlo simulations to show that the observed NLAHE is induced by a Berry curvature quadrupole appearing in the spin-canted state of FeSn. At a practical level, our study establishes NLAHE as a sensitive probe of antiferromagnetic phase transitions in other materials—such as moiré superlattices, two-dimensional van der Waal magnets, and quantum spin liquid candidates, which remain poorly understood to date. More broadly, Berry curvature multipole effects are predicted to exist for 90 magnetic point groups. Our work opens a new research area to study a variety of topological magnetic materials through nonlinear measurement protocols. The related manuscript was published in Physical Review X 14, 021046 (2024). 3. It has been demonstrated by Sales and coworkers that all solid solutions of Co1-xFexSn can eralized using bulk crystal growth (Phys. Rev. Materials 5, 044202 (2021)). We have successfully established the molecular beam epitaxy of Fe-doped CoSn by co-evaporating Fe during the growth of CoSn with doping ratios 0≤x≤0.24. The details of the growth procedure, structural and chemical characterization using X-ray diffraction, atomic force micoscopy, and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy are shown in the Supplementary Materials of the related publication (arXiv preprint arXiv:2409.06933 (2024)). In brief, we find that Co1-xFexSn forms homogeneous solutions without the formation fo subphases or clustering. The film morphology of Co1-xFexSn reproduces the flat top island characteristics of undoped CoSn and are ideally suited for the STM investigation. 4. Coulomb interactions can give rise to captivating phenomena such as quantum criticality, Mott-Hubbard states, and unconventional superconductivity. The appearance of these characteristics in kagome flat bands requires a detailed understanding of the flat band electronic structure and a detailed understanding of the real-space distribution of the electronic states of kagome flat bands has not been developed yet. Consistent with results from model calculations, we find that the measured local density of states associated with the kagome flat bands appearing in STM measurements exhibits a unique real-space distribution by which it can be distinguished from the local density of states of dispersive electron bands and trivially localized states, such as well-localized orbitals and surface resonances. Our findings provide fundamental insight into the electronic properties of kagome metals have been published at Physical Review Research 4, 043269 (2023). We then investigated the low-energy electronic structure of Fe-doped CoSn using the STM. We find experimental evidence for a cascade of strongly correlated states appearing in the partially occupied kagome flat bands of Co1−xFexSn whose filling can be controlled by the Fe-doping level x. At elevated temperatures (T≥16K), we detect a nematic electronic state across a broad doping range 0.05<x<0.25. The comparison with model calculations reveals that strong Coulomb interactions (U>100 meV) blend the states of two 3d-orbital derived flat bands and impart a nematic order parameter. This state serves as the parent phase of a strongly correlated phase diagram: At lower temperatures T<16K, we find spectroscopic evidence for an orbital-selective Mott state enabled by the 3d-orbital degeneracy of the Co atom. This state can only be detected in samples with ideal Fe doping (x=0.17) and descends into a correlated metal phase upon electron and hole doping at T<16K. Our observations demonstrate that the electronic ground state of the CoSn FB sensitively depends on the complex interplay between geometric frustration, strong Coulomb repulsion, 3d orbital degeneracy, and filling fraction at different temperatures. More broadly, our research establishes kagome lattice materials as a unique platform for novel quantum states that arise from strong electronic correlations in a topologically nontrivial FB and that can be controlled by the FB filling fraction (under review at Physical Review X, arXiv preprint arXiv:2409.06933 (2024). 5. We also successfully developed the molecular beam epitaxy of the Weyl ferromagnet Fe3Sn. We established a buffer layered growth using 5nm thin Pt(111) buffer layers, which enables us to synthesize high-quality thin films of Fe3Sn (typical thickness 30-60 nm). This material is of high interest, because topologically nontrivial electronic states, such as Weyl fermions, can give rise to novel anomalous Hall effects. The potential appearance of these effects at room temperature holds promise for their application in magnetic sensing, spintronics, and energy harvesting technology. The anomalous in-plane Hall effect (IPHE) is predicted to arise in topological magnetic materials when an external magnetic field is applied within the sample plane. Because of stringent symmetry requirements, the conclusive detection of the anomalous IPHE induced by topological electronic states remains challenging. Combining molecular beam epitaxy of the kagome metal Fe3Sn with measurements of the electric Hall effect and theoretical calculations, we propose and experimentally demonstrate that the interplay of the kagome lattice motif with spin-orbit coupling and canted ferromagnetism with large exchange interactions gives rise to the anomalous IPHE at room temperature that is induced by topological Weyl points in the electronic band structure. Our work establishes a design paradigm for topological magnets and heterostructures to discover and control novel anomalous Hall effects toward their use in technological applications (under review at Nature Communications, preprint: arXiv:2501.13602 (2025)).

26304221.label: Major findings and research outcome
26304221.value: We have combined molecular beam epitaxy with scanning tunneling microscopy and measurements of the electric Hall effect to examine the emergence of correlated and topological electronic states in transition metal-based kagome metals. Transition metal (X) based kagome metals of the XaYb family are an interesting material family because they allow for the realization of various electronic and magnetic ground states by controlling the chemical composition (X=Co, Fe, Ni, Y=Sn, Ge, In) and stoichiometry (a, b). We have successfully synthesized epitaxial thin films of various members of this material family and we were the first to experimentally realize the molecular beam epitaxy of the kagome flat band material CoSn and the doping series of CoSn with Fe, as well as the Weyl ferromagnet Fe3Sn. Conducting scanning tunneling microscopy measurements on the kagome metal CoSn, we were the first to demonstrate the real space localization of kagome flat band states and we found direct evidence for the lattice frustration-driven localization mechanism on the kagome lattice that manifests in a compact localized state (Physical Review Research 4, 043269 (2023)). Using chemical doping with Fe, we succeeded in realizing partially filled kagome flat bands in CoSn. Our high-resolution spectroscopic measurements with the STM show evidence for a cascade of strongly correlated quantum states, such as a nematic order parameter and an orbital-selective Mott state (under review at Physical Review X, preprint: arXiv preprint arXiv:2409.06933 (2024)). These states appear at different flat band filling fractions and temperatures and our results suggest that they originate from strong electron-electron interactions. Performing measurements of the electric nonlinear Hall effect, we demonstrated the presence of a Berry curvature quadrupole in the kagome antiferromagnet FeSn (Physical Review X 14, 021046 (2024)). This multipole arises from the high symmetry of FeSn in combination with antiferromagnetism and spin-orbit coupling and gieves rise to a 3rd order nonlinear anomalous Hall effect at room temperature. Our results establish a novel mechanism for nonlinear anomalous Hall effects in antiferromagnetic materials that could facilitate energy-harvesting and high-frequency elecronics applications. Finally, we also demonstrated the anomalous in-plane Hall effect at room temperature in epitaxial thin films of the kagome ferromagnet Fe3Sn (under review at Nature Communications, preprint: arXiv preprint arXiv:2501.13602 (2025)). The combination of ferromagnetism and spin-orbit coupling gives rise to Weyl points near the Fermi energy which facilitate an anomalous Hall effect when the magnetic field is applied within the sample plane.

26304221.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
26304221.value: The results of this project enable several interesting future research opportunities. First, the discovery of strongly correlated states in Fe-doped CoSn highlights the potential of this material for the emergence of novel quantum states. We anticipate that a reduction in impurity levels realized via modulation doping of CoSn with FeSn realized with molecular beam eptaxy will enable the appearance of even more quantum many body states. Second, our study of novel anomalous Hall effects appearing in wafer-scale kagome magnets at room temperature highlight the potential of this material platform for possible applications. It will be interesting to test various applications such as high-frequency detection and magnetic field sensing based on kagome Hall bar devices.

26304221.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
26304221.value: Kagome lattice materials are ideal candidates to host novel quantum material properties that are engendered by the interplay of lattice frustration, a unique lattice structure, and electrostatic Coulomb interactions between charge carriers at microscopic length scale. Using molecular beam epitaxy, we have realized a variety of transition metal based kagome metal thin films at wafer scale. Examining the microscopic and macroscopic material properties of these kagome thin films, we found evidence for novel quantum states arising from electron-electron interactions and discovered changes in the electric resistivity of these materials at room temperature that are induced by the geometry of the quantum-mechanical wave function of the electron. Our results highlight the potential of kagome lattice materials for the discovery of novel quantum phases of matter and alreay now chart a path toward their potential integration into futures electronic devices, such as high-frequency electronics and and magnetic field sensing.

26304921.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26304921.value: Halocarbons have been recognized for their role as major ozone depletion substances (ODSs) since the 1970s, while some of them also function as greenhouse gases (GHGs). International agreements, such as the Montreal Protocol, Kyoto Protocol, and Paris Agreement, were established for worldwide cooperation to gradually reduce the production and use of halocarbons. Initial success was achieved in phasing out global chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) productions, but recent studies found an unexpected slowdown in the decline of the atmospheric concentration of trichlorofluoromethane (CFC-11) after 2012. Based on measurements from several locations in East Asia combining with global background observations, the increase in CFC-11 emissions from eastern China was suggested to account for up to 60% of the total increasing emission worldwide. However, the remaining fraction is unexplained because of the lack of long-term measurement. Historically, halocarbons have been emitted from various anthropogenic sources (e.g., dry cleaning industry, electronic industry, and refrigeration) in Hong Kong. Emission sources in the Pearl River Delta (PRD) region, such as chemical manufacturing, also have remarkable impacts on the ambient halocarbons in Hong Kong. The ambient mixing ratios of major CFCs were declining in Hong Kong and the PRD region before 2010. However, no continuous measurements on ambient halocarbons were conducted in Hong Kong after 2010. Given that CFC emissions from the PRD region account for up to 25% of their total emissions in China, any unexpected CFC emissions in the recent year can introduce significant impacts on atmospheric abundances of halocarbons worldwide. In this work, we propose to set up a framework for long-term measurement on ambient halocarbons, and generate 3-year data on ambient abundance of major ODS and GHGs at our supersite. The goal is to study the temporal variability of ambient halocarbons and estimate their source origins using multiple modeling approaches. The contribution from local and regional sources to their ambient presence will be investigated. 自 1970 年代以來，鹵代烴因作為主要臭氧損耗物質(ODS)得到重視，其中一些物種還具有溫室氣體(GHG)的功能。蒙特利爾議定書、京都議定書、巴黎協定等國際協議，引導了在全球範圍內開展合作，逐步減少鹵代烴的生產和使用。世界各國在逐步淘汰氯氟烴(CFCs)的生產方面取得了初步成功，但最近的研究發現，2012 年後三氯氟甲烷(CFC-11)大氣濃度的下降速度出乎意料地減慢。根據位於東亞幾個站點的測量結果並結合全球背景觀測，有研究認為中國東部CFC-11排放量的增加佔全球排放總量增加的比例高達60%。然而，由於缺乏長期測量，其餘增長部分無法得到解釋。 歷史上，香港的各種人為來源(例如乾洗業、電子業和冷藏)都排放了鹵代烴。珠江三角洲地區的排放源(如化工製造)，對香港環境中的滷代烴也有顯著影響。 2010 年之前，香港和珠三角地區主要CFCs的環境濃度呈下降趨勢。但 2010 年之後，香港沒有對鹵代烴進行連續測量。鑑於珠三角地區的CFCs排放量在中國的總排放量中佔比達到25%，近年來任何意外的CFCs排放都將對全球鹵代烴的大氣濃度產生重大影響。我們計劃對香港大氣環境中的滷代烴進行為期 3 年的連續測量。目標是研究這些鹵代烴的時間變化，並使用多種方法估計它們的來源，研究本地和區域不同來源對其環境濃度的貢獻。

26304921.label: Realisation of objectives
26304921.value: The project has successfully achieved all four stated objectives and established a new, long-term framework for halocarbon observations and source analysis in Hong Kong. For objective (1), a comprehensive measurement infrastructure was set up at the HKUST Air Quality Research Supersite, comprising a canister-based sampling system and a multi detector GC platform (GC–ECD, GC–FID, GC–MS and GC–PLOT) specifically configured for halocarbon analysis. Standard operating procedures were developed for every stage of operation, including canister evacuation and leak checks, timed sampling using calibrated flow restrictors, chromatographic separation, detector selection, and data processing. The analytical performance was quantified through detailed method detection limits and replicate precision tests for 18 halocarbon species, following US EPA TO 15A and PMF uncertainty guidance, providing one of the most complete QA/QC characterisations of halocarbons in the region. This platform, developed with technical support from the UCI group, has been operating stably since August 2020 and now functions as the first dedicated long-term halocarbon observation system in Hong Kong, enabling continuous monitoring beyond the project period. For objective (2), the generation of a 3 year observational dataset of ambient halocarbons at the supersite, has also been fully accomplished and represents a unique regional resource. From January 2022 to December 2024, 3,285 canister samples were collected and fully analysed, providing three full years of high time resolution data for 18 species that include Montreal Protocol banned compounds, controlled replacement refrigerants and non regulated short lived solvents. This is, to our knowledge, the first continuous, multi year halocarbon record at a coastal background site in southern China, resolving both background levels and episodic enhancements under different monsoon regimes. The methodology and core results have already been disseminated in peer reviewed article by Cao et al. (2023, 2025), which presents the first integrated characterisation and source origin analysis of halogenated hydrocarbons in Hong Kong based on this long term dataset. Additional papers arising directly from this project (e.g. Sun et al., 2024 a&b; Mai et al., 2025) extend this new dataset to VOC–halocarbon source apportionment and health relevant species, demonstrating its broad scientific value. For objective (3), which aims to analyse the observation data and assess how halocarbon concentrations have changed in relation to emission and transport activities, has been comprehensively addressed and has yielded several new findings. By classifying the 18 species into Montreal Protocol banned, controlled and non regulated groups and analysing seasonal time series from 2022 Winter to 2024 Winter, the project reveals clear and differentiated temporal behaviours across these regulatory categories at a coastal East Asian site. The data show that while banned CFCs (e.g. CFC 11 and CFC 12) continue to decline, a set of non regulated chlorinated solvents, particularly CH₂Cl₂ and CHCl₃, exhibit strong increases and high temporal variability, demonstrating an emerging dominance of short lived, largely uncontrolled halocarbons in the regional budget. This shift in relative importance between legacy ozone depleting substances and new solvent type compounds has not previously been documented with comparable temporal detail in Hong Kong. Furthermore, by combining seasonal analysis with detailed backward trajectory statistics, the project quantifies how changes in dominant transport pathways from the Pearl River Delta, Guangdong and more distant inland provinces modulate these trends, thereby providing the first process based linkage between regional circulation regimes and multi year halocarbon variability at the HKUST site. For objective (4), the identification of major emission sources and the evaluation of local and regional contributions during episodic events, has been fully realised and has produced several novel source diagnostic insights. Pearson correlation matrices reveal distinct and previously unreported clusters among refrigerants, industrial solvents and brominated species at this coastal background site, providing new evidence for mixed anthropogenic–marine influences on specific brominated compounds and co usage patterns among chlorinated solvents. Positive Matrix Factorisation applied to enhancement concentrations of 16 halocarbons (after subtraction of global backgrounds) resolves five dominant factors – cleaning agents, electronic industry solvents, marine emissions, industrial and domestic solvents, and refrigerant residues and products – and quantifies their year to year evolution. The analysis shows that refrigerant residues and products account for roughly 45–49% of total halocarbon enhancements over 2022–2023, establishing, for the first time in Hong Kong, a quantitative estimate of the relative contribution of legacy and replacement refrigerants to the local halocarbon burden. Solvent related factors (cleaning agent; industrial and domestic solvent) emerge as the second largest contributor and display measurable interannual changes, indicating shifts in industrial practices and regional emissions that had not been explicitly captured in earlier regional studies. Backward trajectory frequency analysis further demonstrates that large episodic enhancements in these factors are associated with air masses passing over the Pearl River Delta and central China, directly linking factor resolved sources to specific transport corridors. These new source apportionment and transport diagnostic results have been communicated in the paper by Cao et al. (2023) and related publications arising from this project, and together they provide the first integrated, observation based picture of halocarbon sources and dynamics in Hong Kong and the Greater Bay Area.

26304921.label: Major findings and research outcome
26304921.value: The project has produced a comprehensive and regionally unique dataset of 18 halocarbon species measured at a coastal supersite in Hong Kong, allowing detailed assessment of regulatory effectiveness, emission patterns and source origins. Montreal Protocol banned species such as CFC 11 and CFC 12 exhibit modest but consistent declines over 2022–2024, confirming the impact of the global phase-out, whereas several controlled species (for example, HFC 134a and HCFC 142b) show increasing trends, reflecting their continued use as replacement refrigerants. Non-regulated, short-lived halocarbons, particularly chlorinated solvents such as CH₂Cl₂ and CHCl₃, display the highest concentrations and strongest temporal variability, highlighting the growing importance of uncontrolled solvent emissions in the region. Correlation analysis reveals distinct clustering of species that reflects both regulatory status and shared usage patterns. Strong to moderate correlations among controlled refrigerants point to common applications in air conditioning and refrigeration, while groups of chlorinated solvents display co-variability indicative of shared industrial and cleaning uses in the Pearl River Delta region. Banned species show weaker linkages to other groups, consistent with residual “bank” emissions rather than active production, while certain brominated compounds exhibit patterns suggestive of mixed anthropogenic and marine influences. PMF source-apportionment identifies five robust source categories – cleaning agents, electronic-industry solvents, marine emissions, industrial and domestic solvents, and refrigerant residues and products – and quantifies their interannual variations. Refrigerant residues and products form the dominant factor, increasing from about 45% to nearly 49% of total halocarbon enhancements between 2022 and 2023, underscoring the importance of legacy and replacement refrigerants as a continuing source of ozone-depleting potential and climate forcing. In contrast, the contribution from cleaning agents declines over the same period, suggesting possible changes in local industrial practices or partial adoption of less harmful alternatives. Backward-trajectory analysis shows that halocarbon levels at the HKUST site are influenced by both local Hong Kong emissions and regional transport from the Pearl River Delta and more distant inland provinces. The highest frequency transport pathways concentrate over Guangdong, consistent with the identified solvent and electronic-industry sources, while lower-frequency trajectories from central China indicate episodic contributions from long-range transport events. Collectively, the project outputs – including peer-reviewed publications and conference presentations – provide a unique baseline for halocarbon pollution in southern China, support evaluation of Montreal Protocol implementation, and offer scientific evidence to inform future regulation of currently unregulated halocarbon species.

26304921.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
26304921.value: The established halocarbon monitoring framework and multi-year dataset provide a solid basis for continued long-term observation and expanded research on halogenated species in Hong Kong and the Greater Bay Area. Extending the analysis to the full 3‑year period and maintaining ongoing measurements will enable more robust trend detection and evaluation of policy impacts, particularly for emerging replacement refrigerants and non-regulated solvents. Future work can integrate these in situ observations with regional chemical transport models and satellite products to better quantify emissions, constrain regional inventories, and assess downwind impacts on ozone and climate.​ At the process level, further development of source-apportionment approaches, including multi-pollutant PMF and Bayesian inversion methods, would refine estimates of local versus regional contributions and improve sectoral attribution. Expansion of the monitoring network to include complementary urban, roadside and marine platforms will help to characterise spatial variability and link halocarbon distributions to specific activity patterns and regulatory measures. The project has also trained a cohort of postgraduate students and produced several publications, providing a strong foundation for future proposals targeting halocarbons, VOCs and related climate-relevant species in southern China.

26304921.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
26304921.value: This project studied a group of gases called halocarbons in the air over Hong Kong. Some halocarbons damage the ozone layer and warm the climate, and many of them are controlled by the international Montreal Protocol, while others are still widely used as industrial and cleaning chemicals. Using specialised instruments at a coastal research station in Sai Kung, the team collected and analysed thousands of air samples over several years to measure 18 different halocarbon species.​ The results show that levels of older banned substances, such as traditional CFC refrigerants, are slowly going down, which means global regulations are working. However, several newer replacement gases and many unregulated solvents remain high or are even increasing, especially those linked to cleaning, industry and air conditioning. By applying advanced statistical methods and computer models, the project identified the main human and natural sources of these gases and showed how air pollution from the Pearl River Delta and other parts of China can be transported to Hong Kong. These findings provide important scientific evidence to support future air-quality and climate policies and highlight the need to better control certain currently unregulated chemicals.

26305621.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26305621.value: 磷是生命必不可少的元素，其稀缺性限制了淡水和沿海海洋环境的生物生产力。浮游植物是初级生产力的主要贡献者，它能够将这一关键营养元素储存为一种称为多聚磷酸盐 (多聚磷,polyP) 的高能化合物，使浮游植物能在外部磷含量很低时也能茁壮成长。因此，浮游植物细胞除了能将通常测量的可溶性活性磷作为生物可利用磷含量的指标外，其内部隐藏的polyP很可能是海洋生物地球化学循环的关键组成部分。 PolyP 的动态存储和使用可能会推动初级生产的动态。然而，学界目前对 polyP动态的了解仅限于细胞内，并且研究依赖于受控封闭系统的细胞培养，而封闭系统的实验条件与自然环境明显不同。环境研究至关重要，但又极为稀少，致使PolyP在生态系统规模的磷循环中的作用至今难以捉摸。对于polyP研究的缺乏使我们无法了解动态系统（例如河口和沿海海洋）中的磷循环，而这些系统的生物地球化学循环日益受到气候变化和人类影响的影响。 本工作将珠江口和南海沿岸邻近水域作为研究系统，来研究动态的物理和生物地球化学过程导致的营养水平的时空变异及其对polyP动态乃至整个磷循环的影响。我们将研究三个不同盐度、营养水平和动态以及初级生产力的地点，在一年内多次采集样本以调查季节性的差异，并调整采样间隔以捕获例如由于台风引起的动态。我们的主要目标是 1) 量化水体中的polyP、其空间和季节性变化以及对生物可利用性磷的贡献； 2) 识别参与polyP 储蓄的浮游植物并研究它们的 polyP 代谢如何响应营养元素含量的变化； 3) 研究polyP动态如何在生态系统尺度上调节磷循环。我们将结合现场采样观测以及实验室工作，包括化学分析、流式细胞测量、显微镜观测、连续流动培养实验，最后数据整合分析等来测试我们的假设。拟议项目具有跨学科的特点，将支持跨学科教学，并培养具备海洋化学、生物地球化学和浮游植物生态学知识和科研能力的研究生。研究成果将为广泛的科学界包括海洋生物地球化学循环、营养物质和富营养化以及浮游植物生态等领域提供有价值的科学见解。

26305621.label: Realisation of objectives
26305621.value: Objective 1: Quantify polyphosphate (polyP) and its contributions to the bioavailability of phosphorus in coastal oceans by using the Pearl River Estuary and its adjacent coastal areas in the Northern South China Sea as a study system and investigate the spatial and seasonal variability of polyP at this dynamic land-sea interface. - We have collected polyP samples from 25 locations the Pearl River Estuary region, including several sites where seasonal sampling has been conducted. We have achieved this objective by the following findings: Spatial variability: we observed that polyP accumulation increased seawards as bioavailable P became more depleted. Temporal variability: we observed that polyP varied seasonally responding to phosphorus levels. Low P levels during summer trigger polyP accumulation deficiency response mechanism. During winter mixing, the nutrient-rich bottom waters are mixed to the surface, triggering polyP luxury accumulation in microorganisms. Objective 2: Identify polyP accumulators and investigate how their polyP metabolisms respond to nutrient variations by conducting both field and laboratory studies. - Through our field measurements of polyP, we identify that both phytoplankton and heterotrophic bacteria are capable of accumulating polyP in the Pearl River Estuary region. Picoplankton, likely heterotrophic bacteria, are the most active polyP accumulators. Taxonomy analysis further confirmed the close relationship between polyP dynamics and community compositions. - We have conducted batch culture experiments for several species of algae and heterotrophic bacteria to study how nutrient stoichiometry affect their intracellular polyP dynamics. We found that polyP not only serve as nutrient reserve for microorganisms, but also energy reserve for some heterotrophic bacteria. The diverse roles of polyP influence the competitiveness and interactions of microorganisms in aquatic environments under various nutrient conditions. Objective 3: Estimate the recycling efficiency of polyP and investigate how the dynamics of polyP regulate phosphorus cycling at the ecosystem scale. - We found that polyP was actively recycled and remained relatively stable compared to other particulate P forms even under P deficiency. This means that accumulation of polyP would increase overall P recycling efficiency in the water column. - We also found that the recycling of polyP was linked to many functional cellular metabolic pathways, including the cycling of phosphorus and nitrogen, further linking polyP to other ecosystem functions.

26305621.label: Major findings and research outcome
26305621.value: 1. We have developed a sensitive and reliable method for extracting and quantifying polyphosphate in natural samples from aquatic environments. This method is a major breakthrough overcoming the challenges faced by other existing methods, and will first time make absolute quantification of polyphosphate possible for natural environments. The method will be shared to the international polyphosphate community at FEBS 2023 workshop (selected for oral presentation). The student (Xingyu Yang; supported by this project) also receives a competitive traveling grant (only three awardees globally) from the organizer. We have also published a paper in Environmental Science and Technology to report the methods (Yang et al. 2024a, EST). 2. We have collected polyP samples from 25 locations the Pearl River Estuary region. We observed that polyP accumulation increased seawards as bioavailable P became more depleted. We found that polyP was actively recycled and remained relatively stable compared to other particulate P forms even under P deficiency. The recycling of polyP was linked to many functional cellular metabolic pathways. Taxonomy analysis further confirmed the close relationship between polyP dynamics and community compositions. Together, these findings further advance our understanding of the multifaceted functions of polyP in aquatic ecosystems under P-limitation conditions. We are currently working on a manuscript to report this finding. 3. We have conducted batch culture experiments for several species of algae and heterotrophic bacteria to study how nutrient stoichiometry affect their intracellular polyP dynamics. We found that polyP not only serve as nutrient reserve for microorganisms, but also energy reserve for some heterotrophic bacteria. The diverse roles of polyP influence the competitiveness and interactions of microorganisms in aquatic environments under various nutrient conditions. One paper has been published in Environmental Microbiology (Gao et al 2025), and another paper is under preparation. 4. We have taken monthly-bimonthly water samples from several locations in the eastern coastal waters in Hong Kong, and seasonal samples (every 3- 4 months) from 3 locations in the western coastal waters. We have completed all the analyses and is now working on two manuscripts . 5. Supported by the novel method we developed (see #1), we collaborated with scientists from the University of Minnesota to work on polyP in the largest freshwater ecosystem the Great Lakes. A paper has been published in Limnology and Oceanography Letters (Yang et al. 2024b L&O).

26305621.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
26305621.value: This project successfully overcame a major community challenge by developing a robust method for quantifying polyP, which took us ~ 2.5 years of dedicated effort. This foundational achievement now unlocks significant potential for future research. While initial applications in the Pearl River Estuary and Great Lakes demonstrate the method's utility, the limited scope precluded a sophisticated investigation of polyP's ecological roles and dynamics in natural environments. The proposed course of action is to leverage this novel methodology for a comprehensive research program. Future work should systematically explore diverse aquatic systems to elucidate the environmental drivers, cycling, and ecological significance of polyP. This will transform our understanding of phosphorus biogeochemistry, with critical implications for water quality management and nutrient cycle modeling.

26305621.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
26305621.value: In this project, we studied a special storage molecule, called polyphosphate (polyP), that microbes like algae and bacteria use to store nutrients. Our first big breakthrough was solving a long-standing problem: we created a reliable new method to measure polyP in water samples. This new tool, which we are sharing with scientists worldwide, opens the door for new discoveries. Using our method in Hong Kong's Pearl River Estuary, we saw that microbes store more polyP as they get closer to the nutrient-poor open ocean. This storage acts as a survival kit, helping them weather periods of starvation. We also found that polyP isn't just a food reserve; for some bacteria, it's a battery storing energy. By also studying the Great Lakes, we are helping to paint a global picture of how this hidden molecule is key to ocean biogeochemical cycling, influencing which microbes thrive and how ecosystems function.

26308021.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26308021.value: One of the most famous concepts kindling the development of quantum mechanics is the wave-particle duality, which concerns fundamental particles like the electron. The insulating or conducting property of a material exemplifies such a duality: while electrons in a conventional insulator could be readily pictured as immobile particles localized in space, the conducting electrons in a metal are more customarily viewed as delocalized waves, which possess well-defined (quasi-)momenta instead of positions. The interplay between these two narrations plays a central role in the quantum description of electrons in a crystal. This is especially in topological materials, which do not admit a simple real-space description. The electronic band theory for solids, naturally formulated in the momentum space, provides a proper quantum-mechanical starting point for the description of electrons in a crystal. The incorporation of topological ideas into the band theory has resulted in the repaid development of the relatively young field of topological materials in the past two decades. An important step forward is to consider the effect of electron-electron interactions, which are, however, challenging to incorporate fully in an unbiased manner within a band-theoretic treatment of a material. Yet, the effects of such interactions are oftentimes readily understandable in the real space. For instance, the strong electron-electron repulsion favors a Mott insulating ground state in which the electrons seek to minimize their spatial overlaps. It is an interesting outstanding problem to address how such interactions will modify the materials predictions from topological band theory. The present project seeks to take a first step towards answering this question. Our key observation is that the real-space narration is not only natural for understanding the effects of electronic interactions, but is also a tenable starting point for the description of topological phases of matter. This is reflected in the success of the recently developed classification framework for topological crystalline insulators, which, instead of localizing individual electrons, also consider the localization of emergent phases of electrons in the real space. This framework subsumes the conventional picture for electrical insulators, which could be viewed as a special case for which the building blocks are zero-dimensional, and could be reconciled with filled electronic orbitals. In this project, we will explore how such a real-space approach could also inform us on the interaction effects in moderately correlated, two-dimensional materials, and subsequently advance our understanding on the exceptionally rich phase diagrams displayed by moiré heterostructures. 波粒二像性是啟發量子力學發展的其中一個重要概念。作為一種基本粒子，電子亦帶有波粒二像性的特質: 在一般絕緣體之中電子的表現就有如被緊緊㧓牢的粒子一樣，但在金屬之中它們卻有如在空間中擴散的水波一樣具有明確的動量而沒有特定的位置。電子的波粒二像性帶來了拓撲材料的可能性。在這些材料之中，電子只有波狀特性而沒有簡單的實空間粒子描述。 對應動量空間的電子能帶理論是描述電子在晶體中運動的一個理想出發點，而對電子能帶的拓撲特性的研究則在過去二十年間帶動拓樸材料領域的急速發展。在這個領域中的一個重要議題是電子之間的相互作用如何改變我們對拓樸材料的理解。但是，一般而言電子之間的相互作用在實空間中會較為容易理解。譬如說莫特絕緣體(Mott insulator)可以簡單地描述為電子因互相排斥而導致它們在實空間中盡量遠離對方。如何系統性地把在實空間中我們對電子相互作用的直觀理解和動量空間中的拓撲電子能帶理論結合是一個未解決的重要問題。 這個研究項目將推動我們對這個問題的初步理解。我們的研究方法建基於在實空間中構建的拓撲物質相理論，就有如在近年取得成功的拓撲結晶絕緣體分類理論一樣。在這觀點之中，我們可以在實空間以低維的拓撲物質相作為材料去構建高維的拓撲絕緣體。一般的絕緣體則可以理解成單單以電子作為材料去構建絕緣體的一個特例。我們將在這個項目中研究如何把這個抽象的描述與現實中的電子相互作用結合。

26308021.label: Realisation of objectives
26308021.value: The present project aims to develop real-space theoretical methods for describing an understanding two-dimensional topological materials with a moderate degree of electronic correlations. The project is divided into three objectives, which progress from studying the general trends of how electron interactions affect the topological phases realized (objective 1), to the study of real-space framework for describing gapless phases of matter (objective 2), and lastly to study the phases realized across the correlation spectrum with reference to those realized in moiré materials (objective 3). This grant had supported the work of the PI and his team in four peer-reviewed publications and six additional arXiv preprints which are either in preparation for submission or are already under review. A detailed description of how each of the objectives have been realized can be found below. Objective 1 This objective is realized by developing tensor network methods for studying phases of moderately correlated electrons. The tensor network ansatz provides a systematic way to represent quantum many-body states. This general approach has two key advantages: first, the state can be constructed explicitly in the real space which help reveal the pattern and extent of quantum entanglement in the system; second, the state is described using a much smaller number of parameters compared to the exponential growth of parameters in the many-body Hilbert space with the physical system size. While tensor network representations have been successfully applied to spin systems with bosonic degrees of freedom, their applicability to fermionic systems, like electronic materials, is relatively under-explored. In this project, the PI and his team develop a new approach to construct tensor-network representation of free-fermion states in the real space. Here, free-fermion states correspond to fermionic Gaussian states with particle number conservation, which can include ground states of moderately correlated materials within a mean-field treatment. Unlike traditional approaches which rely on variational energetic minimization to determine the ground state of a given Hamiltonian, our approach is constructive in nature and utilizes the Wannier orbitals of the filled bands, defined in the real space. Our contribution lies in the recognition each of the Wannier orbitals can be described by a tree tensor network, which can be explicitly constructed, and that the full state can be obtained by stacking all these small tree tensors together in the real space. This provides a real-space method for describing electronic ground states of phases admitting a full set of Wannier orbitals, which include obstructed atomic insulators. These results have been published in Phys. Rev. Res. 6, L022016 (2024). In addition, in collaboration with experimental groups we have also contributed to the study of phases realized in correlated materials. In Phys. Rev. Res. 5, 043269 (2023), we provide theoretical support to the study of the effective electronic orbitals in the kagome metal CoSn, which features a pair of flat bands close to the Fermi energy. The real-space charge profile of the flat bands was studied using scanning tunneling microscope (STM), and the experimental observations matched well with our theoretical models which predicted a characteristic charge profile with the electrons localized not on the atoms but within the hexagon rings in the lattice. Objective 2 Built on the methods we developed under objective 1, this objective is realized by extending the approach to capture gapless phases. We demonstrated that the real-space tensor network approaches can also be fruitfully applied to gapless phases of matter, even when correlation effects are incorporated. The starting point is a free-fermion tensor network state which approximates a gapless critical state. While such states are typically described in the momentum space, the tensor network provides a complementary real space description in which correlation effects can then be naturally incorporated. For instance, the mutual electric repulsion between electrons implies there is an energetic penalty for two of them to occupy the same site in a lattice. Thanks to the real space description, the penalty can be readily incorporated by reducing the relative weight of electronic configurations with double occupancy. This approach was demonstrated in Phys. Rev. Res. 7, 013182 (2025), in which we consider the Gutzwiller projection of one-dimensional Fermi surface states. In particular, we studied the case when there are multiple pairs of Fermi points in the pre-projection state and revealed how that modified the tendency of the system to develop charge density waves. In addition, we have also explored other aspect of gapless crystalline phases and their manifestation in the real space. In the preprint arXiv:2206.11761, we developed a systematic approach to perform real-space entanglement renormalization on gapless phases of electrons, which provide a way to construct tensor network representations with a bond dimension which scales polynomially with the system size. In arXiv: 2501.16792, we also provided a simpler theoretical framework for understanding the origin of quantum oscillations in systems without a Fermi surface in the zero magnetic field limit. Lastly, in arXiv:2501.05317, we discussed how crystalline symmetries can protect double Majorana vortex flat bands in a Dirac superconductor which are detectible in the real space using an STM. Objective 3 The last objective was realized by studying the electronic phases, including those that are observed in moiré materials, that could be realized across the correlation spectrum. In Phys. Rev. B 106, 115109 (2022), we developed a method for performing Jordan-Wigner transformation in higher dimensional lattices which keep all spatial symmetries manifest. While the distinction between fermions, like electrons, and bosons, like spins, is one of the most fundamental distinctions between elementary particles, the modern understanding on topological orders have provided a new way to bridge the two. In this work, we showed that any local fermionic Hamiltonians defined on suitable lattices can be consistently mapped to a bosonic quantum magnet problem on the same lattice with a background topological order. Our approach went beyond earlier works in that both internal and spatial symmetries are explicitly maintained in the bosonic problem. While the original version of our manuscript was more formal focusing on the mathematical equivalence of the fermionic and bosonic problems, the present ECS grant supported the revision of this paper in which we added a new discussion connecting our formalism to the spin liquid phases proposed to be possibly realizable on moiré triangular lattices. We have also investigated the emergence of correlated electronic phases in related material systems. In the preprint arXiv:2510.14593, we conducted a systematic investigation of the Hartree-Fock mean-field phase diagram of partially filled kagome flat bands and identified the intersublattice interaction as the driving force for the development of nematic symmetry breaking phases in Fe-doped CoSn. In another direction, we also developed a real-space perturbation approach in arXiv:2509.12621 addressing how physical observables could be computed when a stabilizer state is perturbed, which would be the case for realistic spin liquid models close to a stabilizer fixed point. In collaboration with experimentalists, we have also helped analyze how a flux defect could trap an electronic bound state in the correlated chiral flux phase in arXiv: 2503.19032.

26308021.label: Major findings and research outcome
26308021.value: This project focuses on developing real-space theoretical frameworks to understand two-dimensional topological materials with moderate electronic correlations. The project has supported the work of the PI and his team in four peer-reviewed publications and six additional preprints which are either in preparation for submission or under review. This has contributed to the global research effort on advancing our understanding of topological quantum materials. One of the main research findings is that tensor network states can be obtained in a constructive manner for suitable families of free-fermion states even in higher than one spatial dimension. Conventionally, such constructive approach is limited to one spatial dimension or, as a generalization, to a tree tensor network. The PI and his team developed a new real-space tensor-network representation of free-fermion states by expressing each Wannier orbital as a tree tensor network and combining them to represent electronic ground states. This method provides an efficient and explicit representation of correlated electron systems, particularly obstructed atomic insulators. These results were published in Phys. Rev. Res. 6, L022016 (2024). Another significant research finding concerns how these tensor network techniques can be extended to gapless and critical systems, demonstrating how real-space tensor networks can capture correlations in systems without an energy gap. Using a Gutzwiller projection approach on free-fermion states, the team revealed how multiple Fermi points enhance the tendency toward charge density wave formation (Phys. Rev. Res. 7, 013182 (2025)). A real-space entanglement renormalization of gapless phases approach has also been developed (arXiv:2206.11761). Electronic phases across the correlation spectrum have also been investigated. The project supported the PI and his student to apply the higher-dimensional Jordan–Wigner transformation they developed to concrete models of spin liquid phases of relevance to the triangular lattices realized in moiré materials (Phys. Rev. B 106, 115109 (2022)). Additional studies addressed nematic symmetry breaking in partially filled kagome flat bands (arXiv:2510.14593) and real-space perturbations near stabilizer spin liquids (arXiv:2509.12621). Together, this project has helped advance our understanding of correlated topological phases and contributed to the research toolkit for utilizing real-space approaches in analyzing the electronic phases that are realized in topological materials.

26308021.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
26308021.value: The works produced in this project open several interesting directions for future research in the study of correlated topological materials. First, the real-space tensor network framework developed for both insulating and gapless phases can be extended to incorporate stronger electronic correlations beyond mean-field treatments. This has already been demonstrated in one spatial dimension in the project, and the natural next step is to extend the method to higher spatial dimensions. Furthermore, by combining with the higher-dimensional Jordan-Wigner transformation, the approach could be applied to study fractionalized topological phases like spin liquids. Moreover, aside from studying electronic materials, the methods developed in the present project could also facilitate new ways to simulate fermionic systems on near-term quantum simulators based on bosonic qubits. The theoretical methods developed for studying specific materials, like Fe-doped CoSn, could also be used for studying other quantum materials.

26308021.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
26308021.value: This project aims to understand and predict the behavior of novel quantum materials in which the quantum mechanical nature of electrons is highlighted and leads to novel electrical properties. The laws of quantum physics imply a direct simulation of the system is impossible even on the most powerful supercomputers which exist. This project helps tackle this challenge by developing suitable real-space methods which allow for both a conceptual understanding on how electrons interact and move in these systems as well as providing practical methods for simulating these systems on classical computers. Aside from the theoretical development, the project team also worked closely with experimental teams to explain real-world observations in cutting-edge materials, such as flat-band metals and quantum semiconductors. This research provides a clearer, more intuitive understanding of complex electronic behavior that was previously hard to model. The methods and insights developed here could help guide the design of next-generation materials and devices, including those that may form the basis of emerging quantum technologies.

26501021.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26501021.value: 供应链弹性是保证商业运作可持续发展中越发重要和关键的决定性因素。在过去的几十年，无论是实践还是学术领域，注意力都集中在如何通过运营策略提升运营效率，这些策略包括全球化采购和精益化生产。实践证明，诸如此类的运营效率的确是可以经济上非常有效，然而也不可避免的增加了产业链在多方面的脆弱性，尤其是中小供应商违约风险方面。 为了有效地对冲供应商的违约风险，一个被业界广泛采用的运营效率是构建分散化的供应商池子来降低单个供应商的违约风险。分散化的确可以有效的对冲单独影响每个供应渠道的非系统性风险，比如某个供应商内部物流网络的脆弱性。然而，这样的分散全球化供应商池子面临着诸多挑战。首先，位于其他远距离国家的供应商会增加运送时间，这会极大降低了供应链的应变能力，所以这样的策略并不适合去满足需要及时快速服务的当地新增需求。其次，分散化策略并不能对冲影响所有供应商的系统性风险。类似于金融领域的期权衍生品，供应期权合约是一个企业可以通过支付保费提前预定供应产能并且在需求实现之后拥有按照预先合约规定的价格执行购买不超过预定产能的产量。类似于金融市场的衍生品，供应期权合约有可能会是对冲供应链网络系统性风险的高效低成本的工具。 在这个项目中，我们计划去研究如何在具有产能违约风险和需求不确定性的背景下构建通过供应期权和分散化竞争的运营效率来有效提升供应链弹性。我们将应用经济学博弈论理论来学习供应商的竞争博弈行为，并且刻画采购商如何选择供应商和预定产能的采购策略。其次，我们将量化供应商违约风险对采购商采购成本的影响，通过数值试验和公司数据做大数据分析来展示供应期权和分散化策略对于采购商采购成本和风险规避的影响。我们的研究结果可以给公司和政策制定者在提升产业链弹性的设计上提供具体的指导性建议。

26501021.label: Realisation of objectives
26501021.value: The objectives of the ECS research project (26501021) have been fully achieved. Below, we summarize the research activities and outcomes related to the initial proposal's objectives. First, we developed an analytical model to assess the impacts of supply options within a multi-sourcing framework, where a procurement agent purchases identical products from multiple suppliers with varying lead times, production costs, and default risks. For suppliers with differing lead-time responsiveness, we formulated the problem using stochastic dynamic programming, fully characterizing the optimal procurement strategy with supply option contracts. Our numerical analysis indicates that dual sourcing with supply options can reduce procurement costs by up to 7% by sourcing less than 20% from expedited suppliers. Second, when suppliers have the same responsiveness but differ in production costs and default risks, we formulated the strategic interactions in a two-tier supply chain as a Stackelberg game, with suppliers as leaders and the buyer as a follower. We characterized the equilibrium behavior of both suppliers and the buyer, finding that the cost of capacity reservation significantly influences equilibrium structure. We established conditions under which supply options create a “win-win” outcome for all supply chain members through two channels: a higher price (the price effect) and lower capacity (the capacity effect). Third, we show that key economic drivers for suppliers' option offerings include the cost of capacity reservation and the reliability of suppliers. Fourth, we also examined how the supply portfolio affects the value of supply options across various supplier risk profiles. Our findings demonstrate that supply options can enhance both profitability and resilience -- measured by fill rate -- in global supply chains facing disruptions. Extensive numerical analysis reveals average improvements of 48.7% when both suppliers are unreliable, 30.5% when both are reliable, and 17.7% when one is reliable and the other is not. Finally, we further explored the impacts of supply options in more complex three-tier supply chain networks, where default risks extend to top-tier suppliers, as well as in e-commerce platforms where sellers sell products directly to consumers. Due to COVID-19, the PI was unable to travel or invite colleagues for discussions during the project period, leading to most expenses being allocated to hiring and supporting research assistants.
