26501021.label: Major findings and research outcome
26501021.value: The main findings of this research project are as follows. First, we created an analytical model to analyze supply options in a multi-tier supply chain with multiple suppliers facing disruptions. Second, we framed the interactions between the buyer and suppliers as a Stackelberg game and characterized their equilibrium behavior. Our results indicated that the cost of reserving capacity is crucial for determining equilibrium structures. We also identified conditions under which supply options can lead to a "win-win" situation for all firms in the supply chain. We found that the reliability of supply significantly influences the value of these options. Furthermore, we examined how different supplier risk profiles affect the value of supply options. Lastly, we explored the effects of supply options in more complex three-tier supply chains and e-commerce platforms, where sellers directly reach consumers. Our analytical and numerical studies demonstrate that supply options can effectively enhance profitability and resilience in global supply chains facing disruptions. This project has supported five research papers: 1. “Dual Sourcing: Creating and Utilizing Flexible Capacities with a Second Supply Source” [Part C, 8, no. 1], was published in the Production and Operations Management Journal; 2. “Competitive Option Offerings Under Supply Disruptions” [Part C, 8, no. 2], has been completed and submitted to the Management Science Journal. We are revising it for resubmission based on constructive feedback from the review team; 3. “Information Sharing and Financing Services on Online Retailing Platforms” [Part C, 8, no. 3], was published in the Production and Operations Management Journal; 4. “Efficient Frontier and Applications in Product Offering and Pricing”[Part C, 8, no. 4], was published in the Manufacturing & Service Operations Management Journal; 5. “To Delegate or Not: Mitigating Supply Disruption with Deferred Payment in Supply Chain Networks”[Part C, 8, no. 5], is complete and being prepared for journal submission.

26501021.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
26501021.value: There are promising research opportunities to develop tools that enhance the efficiency and resilience of supply chain networks. The PI plans to explore the following directions. 1. Private Information: Currently, we assume that reliability and cost structures are common knowledge for analytical convenience. It would be valuable to investigate these factors as private information known only to each supplier. 2. Network Structures: Our main findings are based on a two-tier supply chain with one buyer and multiple suppliers. We aim to extend the analysis to other structures, such as three-tier networks or platform-based supply chains.

26501021.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
26501021.value: Supply chain resilience is becoming crucial for businesses to operate effectively. In the past, companies prioritized efficiency through strategies like globalization and lean manufacturing, which, while cost-effective, made them more susceptible to disruptions, especially from smaller suppliers. In this research project, we developed a model to explore how "supply options," similar to financial options, can help businesses enhance their resilience against these disruptions. Our findings revealed that companies can save up to 7% on procurement costs by strategically using faster suppliers for a small portion of their purchases. We also found that the cost of maintaining these supply options significantly influences how suppliers and buyers work together, creating benefits for everyone involved. Additionally, the reliability of suppliers and the costs associated with reserving capacity are critical for maximizing the value of supply options. Overall, our research shows that adopting supply options can greatly boost profitability and resilience in global supply chains, particularly during disruptions. For instance, we found that companies could improve their performance by nearly 49% when both suppliers are unreliable.

26501721.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26501721.value: Nonlinear models are common in business studies, but statistical inference for many such models is complicated and computationally demanding. In this project, we will develop a simple inferential method that builds confidence intervals for parameters easily. Unlike the existing methods in the literature, our confidence interval i) is easy to compute, ii) has transparent theoretical properties, iii) handles the cases with and without endogeneity in a unified framework, and iv) is valid under weak identification. We will apply the new method to study consumer demand and conduct welfare analysis using the U.S. micro-level consumption data. The results will shed light on the effects of price-relevant policies on consumer welfare. 非線性模型在商業研究中非常常見，但對很多非線性模型而言，統計推斷都很複雜並且計算量很大。在本項目中，我們將開發一種簡單的統計推斷方法。基於該方法，對參數構建置信區間將會很容易。與文獻中已有的方法不同，我們的置信區間有以下優勢：第一，容易計算；第二，具有直觀的理論性質；第三，可以在統一框架下處理內生性問題；第四，對於弱識別的模型依然適用。我們將採用這種新的方法通過美國微觀層面的消費數據來研究消費者需求問題並進行福利分析。我們的實證研究結果將有助於人們了解價格相關的政府政策如何影響消費者福利。

26501721.label: Realisation of objectives
26501721.value: All three project objectives have been fully achieved. 1. We develop a highly computationally easy method for the statistical inference of nonlinear econometric models under independence. 1.1. Given an econometric model, we first express the scalar unobservable in terms of the observables and the model parameters (denoted by A for simplicity). Independence between the exogeneous variable (e.g. the instrument, denoted by Z for simplicity) and the unobservable implies independence between A at the true parameter value and Z. 1.2. Plugging A and Z into the independence test statistic developed by Chatterjee (2021, JASA), we construct a confidence set for the true parameter by evaluating the statistic with A taking each candidate parameter value and collecting all those values that make the test statistic smaller than the appropriate critical value. By the computation efficiency of the test statistic itself, the search takes a very short time. 1.3. When we face multiple models or moment equations, we derived a new asymptotic theory establishing the joint limiting distribution of a vector of Chatterjee’s statistics under independence. Our theory shows that these statistics are asymptotically independent even if the data are correlated. 1.4. The property in 1.3 greatly simplifies computation when the researcher faces multiple outcome variables or multiple models; instead of jointly search for the confidence set for the union of the model parameters to avoid multi-testing, she could separately construct a confidence interval for model parameters in each model by a simple adjustment of coverage probability. 1.5. Moreover, we proved that Chatterjee’s test statistics are also jointly independent of a very wide range of estimators using the same data. So, we developed a method that separately constructs two confidence sets using Chatterjee’s test and traditional methods based on estimators and takes the intersection. By adjusting the individual coverage probability, it achieves the desired coverage and improves efficiency without additional computational cost. 2. We applied our method to construct confidence sets for two data sets. 2.1. The first is the data set constructed by Blundell, Horowitz, and Parey (2017, REStat) using the household-level 2001 National Household Travel Survey (NHTS). Using our method, we constructed confidence intervals for the deep parameters in a random quasilinear utility model for the consumption of gas. 2.2. The second data set is an extract from the Stanford Basket Dataset, a household-level scanner panel data set created by Echenique, Lee, and Shum (2011, JPE). We constructed confidence sets for the parameters in a demand model for ice cream and other foods. 3. We developed a method to estimate the best-case and worst-case-scenarios consumer surplus welfare change given counterfactual price changes by solving a scalable convex problem. These welfare change bounds are with confidence, meaning that no further inferential procedures are needed. 3.1. We first derived the formula for welfare change under a price change. The welfare change is a function of the model parameters. 3.2. With the confidence set obtained in 1, we maximize and minimize the welfare change function using the confidence set of the parameters as a constraint. Confidence is by construction embedded in the resulting welfare change bounds, i.e., the maximum and minimum. 3.3. Under our utility function, the welfare change is concave and coordinate-wise strictly monotonic. In the meantime, by the joint independence result stated in 1, the confidence set under independence is hyperrectangle. Hence, optimization is extremely efficient. 3.4. If one faces extra convex constraints on the model parameters that might come from economic theory, the maximum, i.e., the worst-case welfare loss under a price increase, can still be easily solved for by convex optimization due to the concavity of the welfare change function. We developed a technique to transform the function into disciplined convex programming (DCP) solvable so that some state-of-the-art convex optimization solvers such as CVXR and CVXPY can directly solve for the maximum. 3.5. We applied the method to both data sets stated in 2 and computed welfare loss bounds under a price increase in gas and foods, respectively. 4. The use of project funds was mainly for international communications, for instance, conference presentations, to enhance the recognition and impact of the study. The project greatly benefitted from such exposure and enjoyed a smooth publication process. In the meantime, as shown in the published paper, the algorithm we developed to execute the aforementioned numerical and empirical exercises runs around 1000 times faster than the traditional ones. This was a new finding during the research, and it significantly shortened the computation time as we expected. As a result, we did not need to hire the planned number of research staff for the extensive numerical work such as Monte Carlo simulations.

26501721.label: Major findings and research outcome
26501721.value: Major findings. 1. Theoretically, we found and proved that under independence, a) the joint limiting distribution of a vector of Chatterjee’s test statistics is normal with variances equal to 0.4 and covariances 0 under very mild assumptions, and b) the joint limiting distribution of a vector of Chatterjee’s test statistics and a large class of asymptotically normal estimators is normal, with the covariance blocks between Chatterjee’s statistics and the estimators all equal to zero. These results helped us to easily overcome multi-testing problems and build rectangle confidence sets for model parameters with extremely high computational efficiency. 2. Via simulation studies, we found that computing our confidence set by inverting Chatterjee’s statistics is around 1000 times faster than inverting traditional tests for independence. 3. We also have the following empirical findings. For the gas demand application, we found that households with higher income have higher marginal utility of gas consumption, which is reasonable as such households may drive more often than taking public transportation. Consequently, we found that their welfare loss is greater when facing gas price increases. For food consumption, we found large household-level heterogeneity in welfare loss when prices increase. Research outcome. 1. The paper based on the project, “Individual Welfare Analysis: Random Quasilinear Utility, Independence, and Confidence Bounds”, has been published in the Journal of Econometrics in January 2025. (See Part C for more details.) 2. The same paper has been presented at two leading conferences in economics and econometrics. (See Part C for details.) 3. It has also been presented in invited economics seminars at the University of Macau, Peking University, the University of Queensland, and CUHK-Shenzhen.

26501721.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
26501721.value: We could potentially apply our method to our economic applications with more complicated demand models where the independence assumption is appealing. Beyond demand models, production function estimation may also benefit from these methods. We will further study the statistical and computational properties of Chatterjee's independence test statistic under more general setups.

26501721.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
26501721.value: This research develops a fast and efficient method to analyze economic models and estimate how changes in prices affect consumer welfare. The method uses a statistical tool called Chatterjee’s test, which checks for independence between variables in a model. By applying this tool, we can quickly construct confidence intervals (ranges of likely values) with minimal computation. This approach is particularly useful when dealing with multiple models or datasets, as it avoids complex calculations and simplifies the process. Additionally, we developed a way to estimate the best- and worst-case scenarios for consumer welfare under price changes. This involves solving a straightforward optimization problem, ensuring the results are both accurate and easy to compute. We applied this method to two real-world datasets: one on household gas consumption and another on food purchases. For gas consumption, we found that higher-income households experience greater welfare losses when gas prices rise, likely because they rely more on driving. For food consumption, we observed significant variation in how price changes impact different households. Overall, this research provides a powerful, efficient toolkit for economists to analyze consumer behavior and policy impacts, with applications ranging from energy to food markets.

26502121.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26502121.value: The conventional wisdom in durable goods markets is that prices of products go down over time. However, in durable technology goods, we sometimes observe the opposite phenomenon. A notable example is Tesla cars, where the same model can become more expensive over time. One of the reasons for this is software upgrades. Manufacturers sometimes over-invest in hardware in anticipation of future software improvements. Early adopters can enjoy a low price, but when the software upgrades arrive, new customers have to pay a higher price, while early adopters get the upgrades for free. A lot of durable technology goods today (e.g., cars, computers, mobile phones) have software upgrades over time, but there is little research on the dynamics between prices, software, and hardware quality of these products. In this project, we propose a game-theoretic model to study these phenomena. More specifically, we are interested in the optimal strategy for dynamic pricing and hardware investment, and if this strategy can be used to credibly signal to consumers the future potential of software improvements. The results of the research will have implications for organizations, consumers, and the industry of durable technology goods as a whole. 对于科技产品，一个传统的观点是产品价格会随着时间的推移而下降。然而，我们如今也观察到相反的现象：早期购买者可以以低廉的价格获得基础产品；当软件升级到来时，早期购买者可以免费获得升级，而新客户将支付更高的价格。大量科技产品（例如汽车、计算机、手机）随着时间的推移都会升级软件，但很少有关于价格、软件升级和基础产品质量之间动态关系的研究。在此项研究中，我们分析科技公司的最佳动态定价和产品质量策略，并探索该策略是否可用于向消费者可靠地传达公司未来软件升级的潜力。

26503221.label: Project Title(Chinese)
26503221.value: 貨幣政策再分配效應的實證研究

26503221.label: Project Objectives
26503221.value: We aim to improve empirical knowledge of the disaggregated and distributional effects of monetary policies. We provide results comparable across different definitions of economic resources such as earnings, financial income, and wealth. We investigate who are more exposed to elevated unemployment risks given contractionary monetary policies than other workers. We focus on individual characteristics such as educational attainment, salary, and age. We compare the employment count and salaries paid in different industries and how they respond to monetary policies. We highlight the impacts of industrial transition on the propagation of monetary policies. We document how financial income inequality and wealth inequality respond to monetary policy shocks at business cycle frequencies using the identified shock series. We compare the empirical results to the theoretical predictions of heterogeneous agent New Keynesian models. From this comparison, we will evaluate the practical relevance of major redistribution channels in the models. We combine various high-quality datasets that can be used for empirical investigations of the interactions between other macroeconomic shocks and distributional factors.

26503221.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26503221.value: We are all different. In this project, we take individual heterogeneity seriously in relation to monetary policies. Conventionally, monetary policies and their macroeconomic effects have been studied under the assumption that we are all alike. Under the representative agent assumption, a vast theoretical and empirical literature focused on how monetary policies affect standard aggregate variables such as output, inflation, and interest rates. Although some recent papers investigate the redistribution channel of monetary policies using models with heterogeneous agents (e.g., Auclert, 2019; Kaplan, Moll, and Violante, 2018), empirical knowledge of the redistribution effects of monetary policies is still limited. This project attempts to fill this gap. We study disaggregated effects of monetary policies using several datasets, including the Current Population Survey, the Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages, and the recently constructed Distributional National Accounts (Piketty, Saez, and Zucman, 2018) and Distributional Financial Accounts (Batty et al. 2019). We investigate how cross-sectional distributions of earnings, unemployment risk, financial income, and wealth respond to monetary policy shocks. Furthermore, we document how important monetary policies are drivers of cross-sectional variations in different types of economic resources. Specifically, we estimate impulse response functions and forecast error variance decompositions, which are major parameters of the business cycle analysis. We provide results comparable across different definitions of economic resources such as earnings, financial income, and wealth. We expect this new set of stylized facts based on our empirical results to discipline the development of theoretical heterogeneous agent models by providing empirical statistics that are readily comparable to the corresponding outcomes of theoretical models. 人各有異。在這項研究中，我們致力探討與貨幣政策相關的個體異質性。 傳統上，貨幣政策及其宏觀經濟影響的研究是在假設我們都一樣的情況下進行的。在代表性個人的假設下，大量理論和實證文獻均側重於貨幣政策如何影響標準綜合變量，如產出、通貨膨脹和利率。儘管最近的一些論文利用異質代理人模型來研究貨幣政策的再分配渠道（例如，Auclert，2019 年；Kaplan、Moll 和 Violante，2018 年），但關於貨幣政策再分配效應的實證仍然有限。此研究試圖填補這一空白。 我們使用多個數據集研究貨幣政策的分解效果，包括當前人口調查、就業和工資季度普查，以及最近構建的分配國民賬戶（Piketty、Saez 和 Zucman，2018 年）和分配金融賬戶（Batty 等人， 2019年）。我們調查了收入、失業風險、財務收入和財富的橫截面分佈如何對貨幣政策衝擊作出反應。此外，我們記錄了貨幣政策在驅動不同類型經濟資源的橫截面差異上的重要性。具體來說，我們估計脈衝響應函數和預測誤差方差分解，這是商業周期分析的主要參數。我們提供了不同經濟資源的定義（如收入、財務收入和財富）的可比結果。我們期望這組基於我們的實證結果的新程式化事實，能夠提供與理論模型相應結果比較的經驗統計數據，以規範異質代理人模型的發展。

26503221.label: Realisation of objectives
26503221.value: I conducted extensive empirical analyses of publicly available micro datasets to study the distributional implications of monetary policies. I summarize the findings below in relation to each of the six objectives. The details, including figures and equations, are relegated to a separate online appendix to the completion report, which is attached to this completion report in section 12. This online appendix is also accessible at the following link: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_bxUtPBPQmGsL-VNsTbQSeGmZjHBYe88/view?usp=sharing I organized the completion report in this manner with a separate online note that is included at the end of the report for four reasons. First, the actual results serve as proof that I took this project seriously and exercised all due diligence in the past several years. Second, the current format of the completion report does not allow me to insert equations and add figures in this section. It is not easy to illustrate the realization of objectives without showing the graphs for this empirical macro project. Additionally, as also noted in Part C, this effort has not materialized in published papers, probably because several other competing papers sharing very similar objectives have already been published (or are at an R&R stage) in top journals in economics and finance. Thus, instead of simply referring to a publication as proof, I prepared an online appendix to this report. Finally, relatedly, I decided to develop some of the results in (indirectly) related research projects instead of preparing a single research paper covering all six objectives. For example, objectives 1 and 5 influenced my paper, “Business Cycles and Earnings Inequality.” A draft of this paper is included in section 8. Objective 1. We aim to improve empirical knowledge of the disaggregated and distributional effects of monetary policies. We provide results comparable across different definitions of economic resources such as earnings, financial income, and wealth. Summary of the results. (1) Contractionary monetary policy shocks redistribute pre-tax income from the bottom 90% to the top 10%. However, the tax-and-transfer system mitigates such a redistribution, as shown in the results for the post-tax income. (2) In the short- and medium-term (i.e., 0-4 year horizons), monetary policies have statistically insignificant effects on the average earnings of different groups. These results are also consistent with the results based on different percentiles obtained from the Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages. In contrast, in terms of the labor income shares, the results resemble those of the pre-tax income; a redistribution from the bottom 90% to the top 10%. (3) Contractionary monetary policy shocks render the capital income concentrated among the top 1%. Objective 2. We investigate who are more exposed to elevated unemployment risks given contractionary monetary policies than other workers. We focus on individual characteristics such as educational attainment, salary, and age. Summary of the results. (1) An increase in unemployment risk in response to contractionary monetary policies almost entirely falls on unskilled workers. (2) The responses of skilled workers’ employment counts to monetary policy shocks are statistically insignificant. Objective 3. We compare the employment count and salaries paid in different industries and how they respond to monetary policies. We highlight the impacts of industrial transition on the propagation of monetary policies. Summary of the results. (1) There exists substantial heterogeneity in industry-level responses to monetary policies. (2) During the 1970s and 80s, construction and manufacturing (especially durable goods) industries' employment responded more sensitively to monetary policy shocks than wholesale trade, retail trade, finance, insurance, and real estate, and services. There also exist industries that show acyclicality conditional on monetary policy shocks, such as agriculture, forestry, and fishing; mining; and government. (3) In the data after 1990, a similar pattern for employment is observed. Intriguingly, employment in nondurable goods manufacturing; management of companies and enterprises; health care and social assistance; accommodation and food services; and other services, except government increases in response to contractionary monetary shocks. The results for real salaries per worker are more mixed and subtle. Objective 4. We document how financial income inequality and wealth inequality respond to monetary policy shocks at business cycle frequencies using the identified shock series. Summary of the results. (1) Contractionary monetary policy shocks redistribute wealth from the middle 40% to the others, as shown in the results based on net worth and assets. Focusing on corporate equities and private business yields similar results. (2) Intriguingly, assets in the form of real estate and consumer durables are redistributed from the top 50% to the bottom 50%. The magnitude of the increases in the bottom 50% is substantially larger than other types of assets. (3) The liability of the top 50% decreases. In contrast, the bottom 50% have more home mortgages and, as a result, more liability. The bottom group's consumer credit debt also increases in a smaller magnitude. (4) The aggregate home ownership rates decrease in response to contractionary monetary policy shocks. However, the middle-income group's ownership rates respond positively in years 0 and 1, probably in line with the positive responses in the bottom 50% wealth group's real estate wealth. Objective 5. We compare the empirical results to the theoretical predictions of heterogeneous agent New Keynesian models. From this comparison, we will evaluate the practical relevance of major redistribution channels in the models. Summary of the results. Monetary policy shocks have little effect on earnings dispersion among the employed. Although contractionary monetary policy shocks significantly decrease aggregate earnings and employment, the inequality index does not react substantially. In theory, contractionary monetary policy shocks can increase or decrease earnings inequality. However, in any case, the results in Lee (2025) imply that the level effects of monetary policy across different earnings groups are fairly uniform, and the redistribution of earnings among the employed is quantitatively minimal. Instead, the redistribution channel of monetary policy might be more effective through unemployment risk, financial income, or the impacts of inflation on nominal wealth, rather than through labor earnings among the employed. Objective 6. We combine various high-quality datasets that can be used for empirical investigations of the interactions between other macroeconomic shocks and distributional factors. Realization. As detailed in the online appendix, I utilized several micro datasets to empirically study the distributional implications of monetary policies. The dataset investigated includes World Inequality Database, Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages, Industrial Economic Accounts, Distributional Financial Accounts, and Current Population Surveys.

We investigate who are more exposed to elevated unemployment risks given contractionary monetary policies than other workers. We focus on individual characteristics such as educational attainment, salary, and age.

We compare the employment count and salaries paid in different industries and how they respond to monetary policies. We highlight the impacts of industrial transition on the propagation of monetary policies.
We document how financial income inequality and wealth inequality respond to monetary policy shocks at business cycle frequencies using the identified shock series.

We compare the empirical results to the theoretical predictions of heterogeneous agent New Keynesian models. From this comparison, we will evaluate the practical relevance of major redistribution channels in the models.
We combine various high-quality datasets that can be used for empirical investigations of the interactions between other macroeconomic shocks and distributional factors.

26503221.label: Major findings and research outcome
26503221.value: (1) Contractionary monetary policy shocks redistribute pre-tax income from the bottom 90% to the top 10%. However, the tax-and-transfer system mitigates such a redistribution, as shown in the results for the post-tax income. (2) In the short- and medium-term, monetary policies have statistically insignificant effects on the average earnings of different groups. The level effects of monetary policy across different earnings groups are fairly uniform, and the redistribution of earnings among the employed is quantitatively minimal. (3) Contractionary monetary policy shocks render the capital income concentrated among the top 1%. (4) An increase in unemployment risk in response to contractionary monetary policies almost entirely falls on unskilled workers. (5) The responses of skilled workers’ employment counts to monetary policy shocks are statistically insignificant. (6) There exists substantial heterogeneity in industry-level responses to monetary policies. (7) Construction and manufacturing (especially durable goods) industries' employment responded more sensitively to monetary policy shocks than wholesale trade, retail trade, finance, insurance, and real estate, and services. (8) Contractionary monetary policy shocks redistribute wealth from the middle 40% to the others, as shown in the results based on net worth and assets. Focusing on corporate equities and private business yields similar results. (9) Assets in the form of real estate and consumer durables are redistributed from the top 50% to the bottom 50%. The magnitude of the increases in the bottom 50% is substantially larger than other types of assets. (10) The liability of the top 50% decreases. In contrast, the bottom 50% have more home mortgages and, as a result, more liability. The bottom group's consumer credit debt also increases in a smaller magnitude. (11) The aggregate home ownership rates decrease in response to contractionary monetary policy shocks. However, the middle-income group's ownership rates respond positively in years 0 and 1, in line with the positive responses in the bottom 50% wealth group's real estate wealth.

26503221.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
26503221.value: A potentially interesting research topic could be explaining the empirical results I found in this project using theories and quantitative macroeconomic models. These empirical findings could be used to (in)validate several mechanisms through which household heterogeneity could shape the propagation and amplification mechanisms of business cycle shocks. For example, regarding monetary policies, my empirical results imply that the redistribution of earnings among the employed workers is not substantial given monetary policy shocks. Thus, the interaction between household heterogeneity and the propagation of monetary policy shocks might be more relevant to financial income, unemployment risk, and the impacts of inflation on nominal wealth/liability. Formally evaluating the empirical results and related theoretical mechanisms through the lens of the model could be an important area to explore in the future.

26503221.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
26503221.value: Monetary policy affects inequality. Traditionally, monetary policymakers focus on employment, inflation, and financial stability after the Global Financial Crisis. However, because monetary policy influences inequality, they may also need to consider redistribution. Understanding inequality can enhance our knowledge of how monetary policies impact the economy, leading to improved policy management.

26505021.label: Project Title(Chinese)
26505021.value: 疫情後何種職業向永久性遠程辦公切換？基於中國線上招聘平台的分析

26505021.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26505021.value: 遠程辦公是一種在未來有前途且重要的工作模式，它能改善工作與生活的平衡，節省資本成本，並可能減少參工率及工資方面的性別差異。然而，遠程辦公的採用率仍然相對較低，而學界、業界對其原因並未完全明確。在 COVID-19 大流行期間，各地政府紛紛採取封鎖和其他社交隔離政策，許多工作被迫通過遠程辦公在家完成，這也為公司和工人提供了一個獨特的機會來實驗和了解遠程辦公這一模式。在這個項目中，我們計劃利用新冠疫情這個大規模的自然“實驗”以及相應政策這個社會“實驗”，檢驗以下假設：如果對於某些公司和工作而言，（1）遠程工作可以提高生產力，並且（2）轉向遠程工作的障礙可以通過相對短期的學習經驗克服，它們將選擇在受到暫時性疫情衝擊後永久性切換到遠程辦公模式，而這將體現為：在疫情消退/結束之後新發佈的招聘職位廣告中，這些公司仍將註明遠程辦公要求或選項。 我們計劃與中國最大的線上招聘平台之一合作，使用其職位發布數據來檢驗假設的現象是否出現，並研究此現象的意義與影響。首先，我們計劃對比位於疫情期間採用（長期）封城的城市與未封城的城市的公司在疫情後的新招聘廣告中註明遠程辦公的比例，研究前者是否持續高於後者。然後，我們計劃刻畫出經過臨時封鎖後、最顯著地長期轉換為遠程辦公的職業類型和公司類型。最後，我們計劃研究當某一職業由實體辦公向遠程辦公切換後，對其從業人員所需的技能要求是否改變、是否吸引更高質量的申請者和更多女性申請者。 本項目中提出的研究問題具有高度的政策相關性，主要體現在以下兩個方面。首先，一旦刻畫出能從長期轉換為遠程辦公中得益的職業類型和公司類型，政府可以選擇對不受疫情嚴重影響從而仍保留現場辦公的類似公司及其遠程工作培訓計劃進行短期補貼。這種一次性政策，類似於疫情這個“實驗”本身，有潛力能針對性地促成特定公司和職業更高效的遠程辦公切換，而這從長遠來看可以對社會福利產生不小提升。此外，一旦了解COVID-19 危機後永久採用遠程辦公的工作對職業技能的要求會出現哪些改變，可以為課程設計和職業培訓等方面的教育政策提供指導。

26506021.label: Project Title(Chinese)
26506021.value: 制度的演变和对工业增长的影响：来自 2 个世纪案件判决的证据

26506021.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26506021.value: In this proposed work we will use computational linguistic and machine learning technique to construct a measure of institutional quality in every state in the US for a period of more than 200 years. We will use all published US court decisions since the 17th century to analyze whether the decisions led to an increase or decrease in four components that constitutes quality of economic institutions - creditor protection, bankruptcy laws, property right and media independence. We intend to validate our measure by showing that it correctly identifies events that has been widely cited in the media as major events that shaped US regulatory environment. Using this index we intend to provide microeconomic evidence on the role of institutional quality on the evolution of industrial growth and spatial patterns of development within the United States. This index will also allow us to provide a number of forgotten periods of US history when institutional quality changed either through the passage of new regulation or through a stricter implementation of existing ones by the judges. We use the index to study the role of institutional quality in shaping corporate growth across two centuries in US. We follow Porta, Lopez-de Silanes, Shleifer, and Vishny (1998) among others to look at the way changes in the quality of institutions had an impact on investment, lending and development in a region. Particularly we want to focus on the way variation in the quality of institution across states in US led to differential spatial industrial growth Further, through the different components of our proposed index, we want to study whether industrial growth vary in their sensitivity toward each component. The staggered nature of the change in the index across states provides us credible identification strategy that had largely been a lacuna in the existing literature. The proposed study would be the first to compute an in-depth and comprehensive measure of institutional quality for a long term period: in-depth in its way of covering all different aspects of institutional quality and measuring both the implementation as well as changes in regulation by the virtue of using legal decision documents; comprehensive in its coverage of all legal judgements of all states in the US for the past two centuries. The computation of these measures would allow us complement the theories and existing empirical evidences by providing more granular and precise data on a largely nebulous concept - `institutions'. 在这项拟议的工作中，我们将使用计算语言和机器学习技术来构建一个衡量美国每个州 200 多年的制度质量的指标。我们将使用自 17 世纪以来所有已公布的美国法院判决来分析这些判决是否导致构成经济制度质量的四个组成部分的增加或减少——债权人保护、破产法、财产权和媒体独立性。我们打算通过表明它正确识别媒体广泛引用的事件作为影响美国监管环境的重大事件来验证我们的措施。使用该指数，我们打算提供关于制度质量对美国工业增长和发展空间模式演变的作用的微观经济证据。该指数还可以让我们提供一些美国历史上被遗忘的时期，这些时期的制度质量因新法规的通过或法官对现有法规的更严格执行而发生变化。 我们使用该指数来研究制度质量在塑造美国两个世纪的企业增长中的作用。我们跟随 Porta、Lopez-de Silanes、Shleifer 和 Vishny（1998 年）等人研究机构质量的变化对一个地区的投资、贷款和发展的影响方式。我们特别想关注美国各州制度质量的差异导致差异空间工业增长的方式。 此外，通过我们提议的指数的不同组成部分，我们想研究工业增长对每个组成部分的敏感性是否不同。跨州指数变化的交错性质为我们提供了可靠的识别策略，而这在很大程度上是现有文献中的一个空白。 拟议的研究将是第一个计算长期制度质量的深入而全面的衡量标准：深入涵盖制度质量的所有不同方面，并衡量监管的实施和变化通过使用法律决定文件；全面涵盖了过去两个世纪美国所有州的所有法律判决。这些度量的计算将使我们能够通过提供关于一个非常模糊的概念——“制度”的更细粒度和更精确的数据来补充理论和现有的经验证据。

26600321.label: Project Title(Chinese)
26600321.value: 中國的社會冤屈何時及如何變成抗議？基於大數據的分析

26600321.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26600321.value: 群體性抗議是公民最有效的政治參與模式之一。理解何時以及為什麼抗議會發生也是社會運動研究的核心話題。但是大部分社會運動研究都有選擇結果的偏差：研究者很少從那些可能變成抗議的社會不平事件出發，研究哪些有變成抗議，哪些並沒有； 而是只研究那些已經變成抗議的社會不平。 此項目的研究區域是中國的社會抗議。 每年中國有超過10萬件社會抗議，政府花費超過1100億美元來維護社會穩定。但是對中國社會抗議的分析大多以定性為主，很少有針對發生了的抗議的定量數據分析，更不用提定量分析為什麼哪些社會不公事件會導致抗議，哪些並不會。 此項目分為兩步。第一步，此項目會基於微博，搜集社會不公事件； 然後跟蹤這些社會不公事件，看民眾如何維護自己權利，是否維權行動會演化成抗議。這一步利用了先進的機器學習方法，從文本和圖片數據來識別社會不同事件的信號。可行性研究顯示最終可能獲得一個超過35萬個不公事件的數據集。這是全世界第一次能有如此大規模的同時涵蓋社會不公事件和結果的數據。 此項目第二部分會統計分析得到的數據集。初步的結果顯示動員的速度，不公事件的類型，政府在早期的回應策略，都會影響不公變成抗議的概率。

26600521.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26600521.value: Resilient rice farming—the capacity to endure social, economic, and environmental shocks and stresses due to hazards and structural vulnerabilities—is imperative for food security, especially in the era of cascading crises. In response to these stressors, contemporary sustainable development programs in rice-farming communities have focused on enhancing rice farmers’ material capital, such as farm inputs, crop seeds, and irrigation, and on expanding the access of farmers to these assets. Although these interventions have increased the resilience of rice farmers, the contribution of non-material forms of capital, such as the farmers’ relationships with their fellow farmers, other actors in rice farming, and even with nonhuman entities such as the spirits and the Divine, are minimally considered and studied. Although these social capitals are not necessarily neglected, their contributions to resilience have not been properly unpacked. Therefore, the sociality of resilience has largely remained obscured. As the world faces multiple and cascading crises—from pandemics to economic recession to weather extremes—an expansive and deeper look at the heterogeneous concepts of resilience, its context-specific drivers, and various modes of production can provide new perspectives to examine how we can redesign our strategies and policies to survive in the future. This two-year project will extend the literature on the non-material aspects that produce resilient livelihoods. It will draw on in-depth, multi-method field research that includes surveys, interviews, and focus group discussions with indigenous rice farmers in vulnerable regions of the Philippines and Indonesia. These locations have been subjected not only to extreme water-related stressors, including typhoons and droughts, and geological hazards like earthquakes, but also to social and economic pressures such as out-migration, economic insecurity, aging, over-tourism, changing preferences among the youth, and now the impact of the pandemic. The project will uncover, narrate, and analyze the lived experiences of Ifugao and Balinese rice farmers, focusing on the conditions that build their affective relationships with human and nonhuman entities, and compare these narratives to reveal their similarities and variations in coping, survival, and resilience. In doing so, the project will make visible the constructs of survivorship of indigenous rice farmers, thereby contributing to the decolonization of largely Western notions of resilience. 水稻種植彈性——能夠承受災害和結構性脆弱導致的社會、經濟和環境的沖擊和壓力——在危機重重的年代對於糧食安全至關重要。為了應對種種壓力，水稻種植方目前的可持續發展計劃側重於提高稻農的物質資產，如給予農業投入、作物種子和灌溉，以及擴大稻農獲得這些資產的機會。儘管這些措施提高了稻農的種植彈性，但非物質性資產的貢獻，例如稻農與其他農民、其他水稻種植參與者甚至與非人類實體（如魂魄和神靈）的關係，極少受到學術研究關注。儘管這些社會資本沒有被完全忽視，但它們對種植彈性的貢獻尚未得到全面研究。因此，彈性的社會意義在很大程度上仍然模糊不清。世界正面臨多重連鎖危機——從流行病、經濟衰退到極端天氣——對彈性的不同概念、其於特定環境的產生因素和各種表現形式進行廣泛而深入的研究，可以提供新的視角來重新設計讓我們能在未來生存的戰略和政策。本項目為期兩年，將擴充非物質性資產促進彈性生存方面的文獻。本項目將採用深入、多元的田野調查，對菲律賓和印度尼西亞生態脆弱地區的原住民稻農進行問卷調查、訪談和焦點小組討論。這些地方既受到例如颱風和乾旱等與水相關的極端壓力因素的影響以及地震等地質災害的影響，也同時受到社會和經濟壓力的影響，比如人口外流、經濟危機、老齡化、過度旅游開發、年輕一代偏好善變以及當下的新冠大流行。本項目將發現、講述和分析伊富高和巴厘島稻農的生活經歷，重點關注他們與人類和非人類實體情感關係的產生條件並進行比較研究，以揭示他們在應對危機和建立生存彈性方面的相似和差異。本項目將幫助人們認識原住民稻農的生存方式構成，從而對主流西方語境中彈性概念的非殖民化做出貢獻。

26600521.label: Realisation of objectives
26600521.value: This study investigated the resilience of Indigenous rice farmers in the Philippines and Indonesia amid rising environmental hazards and socio-economic challenges. It highlights how these farmers access and maintain their intangible capital, adapt to environmental challenges and develop resilience strategies. The research enhances the understanding of Indigenous agricultural practices in Southeast Asia by exploring affective relationships, farmers' lived experiences, and decolonised resilience frameworks. Objective 1: Affective relationships as intangible capital Accessing and sustaining intangible capital The study's first objective focuses on how Indigenous rice farmers access and sustain their intangible capitals, particularly emphasising the role of affective relationships. Affective relationships, defined as emotional ties and connections that individuals maintain with family, friends, and community members, form the backbone of social resilience. The research demonstrates that these farmers leverage their social connections for practical support and emotional and spiritual sustenance (Delina et al., Under Review in Applied Geography). We found that Indigenous rice farmers often rely on their extended family networks, local communities, and even nonhuman entities, such as ancestral spirits, to navigate their challenges. These relationships provide a safety net that enables farmers to withstand various shocks, whether they are environmental, economic, or social. For instance, during periods of crop failure due to adverse weather conditions, farmers turn to their families and communities for assistance, whether through shared resources, labour, or emotional support (Delina et al., Under Review in Climate Risk Management). Cultivating emotional ties The study also highlights the importance of fostering strong emotional ties to cultivate a robust support system. This support system is crucial for the psychological well-being of farmers, particularly in times of crisis. The emotional bonds formed within families and communities create a sense of belonging and solidarity, which can significantly enhance resilience. Our research indicates that farmers who maintain strong affective relationships are better equipped to cope with stress and uncertainty, as they have access to a support network that can provide practical assistance and emotional reassurance (Delina et al., Under Review in World Development). Moreover, our findings underscore the necessity of recognising and nurturing these affective capacities as essential components of resilience. This recognition is significant for policymakers and development practitioners who often focus on tangible resources and infrastructure while overlooking the significance of social and emotional capital. By integrating a focus on affective relationships into resilience-building strategies, stakeholders can create more holistic and effective interventions that resonate with the lived experiences of Indigenous farmers (Delina et al., 2024, published in Journal of Rural Studies). Objective 2: Experiences of Indigenous farmers facing environmental hazards Adapting to Environmental Challenges The second objective of the research delves into the extraordinary experiences of Indigenous Ifugao and Balinese farmers in the face of harsh environmental hazards. We identified various challenges these farmers encounter, including frequent precipitation, long-term droughts, competition for water resources, and geological risks such as earthquakes (Delina et al., Under Review in Climate Risk Management). These environmental hazards pose significant threats to agricultural productivity and, consequently, to farmers' livelihoods. In addition to these environmental challenges, our research examines social and economic stressors such as ageing populations, out-migration, and over-tourism. For instance, as younger generations migrate to urban areas for better opportunities, the agricultural workforce in these Indigenous rural communities diminishes, increasing pressure on those who remain. This demographic shift can strain existing social networks and challenge the traditional practices that have sustained rice farming for generations (Delina et al., Under Review in World Development). Strategies for navigating risks Our findings reveal that the resilience of Indigenous rice farmers is significantly shaped by their ability to adapt their livelihoods in response to these multifaceted challenges. By analysing their lived experiences, the study provides valuable insights into the strategies employed by farmers to navigate risks. For example, many farmers adopt diversified cropping systems while pursuing alternative non-agricultural livelihoods that allow them to mitigate the impacts of climate variability. Planting various crops and engaging in multiple livelihoods can reduce the risk of total crop failure and ensure a more stable food supply; however, these also could affect the Indigenous way of life (Delina et al., 2024, Journal of Rural Studies). Additionally, the research highlights the importance of traditional knowledge and practices in enhancing resilience. Indigenous farmers possess a wealth of knowledge accumulated over generations, which informs their understanding of local ecosystems and agricultural practices. This knowledge enables them to make informed decisions about when to plant, irrigate, and harvest, increasing their adaptability to changing environmental conditions (Delina et al., Under Review in Climate Risk Management). Furthermore, our study illustrates how farmers engage in collective action to address shared challenges. For instance, farmers can pool resources, share knowledge, and collectively negotiate for better access to markets and financial services by forming cooperatives or strengthening their existing community groups. This collaborative approach strengthens individual resilience and fosters community and solidarity among farmers (Delina et al., Under Review in World Development). Objective 3: Development of strategic and decolonised resilience frameworks Formulating effective policies The third objective of the research focuses on developing strategic and decolonised resilience frameworks. Our findings advocate for targeted policies that enhance social resilience by fostering farmer interaction and collaboration. By facilitating resource exchange and improving access to financial institutions, policymakers can create an enabling environment that supports the resilience-building efforts of indigenous farmers (Delina et al., Under Review in Policy and Society). One key recommendation emerging from the research is integrating traditional and modern agricultural practices. This integration can take various forms, such as promoting agroecological practices that align with Indigenous knowledge systems and incorporating modern techniques that enhance productivity without sacrificing Indigenous and cultural practices. For instance, farmer field schools can serve as platforms for knowledge exchange, allowing farmers to learn from one another and experiment with new methods in a supportive environment (Delina et al., 2024, Journal of Rural Studies). Recognising local contexts Moreover, the research emphasises the importance of considering tangible and intangible capital when formulating resilience frameworks. Policymakers can develop culturally relevant and effective interventions by recognising the unique contexts of local and Indigenous Peoples. This approach requires a shift away from one-size-fits-all solutions towards more nuanced strategies that consider Indigenous communities' specific needs and aspirations (Delina et al., Under Review in Climate Risk Management). Our findings also highlight the necessity of involving Indigenous farmers in decision-making that affects their livelihoods. By empowering farmers to participate in designing and implementing resilience strategies, stakeholders can ensure that interventions are grounded in local knowledge and priorities. This participatory approach enhances the effectiveness of resilience-building efforts and fosters a sense of ownership and agency among farmers (Delina et al., Under Review in World Development). Conclusion The research findings illustrate how affective relationships, environmental challenges, and resilience strategies interact among Indigenous rice farmers. They highlight the importance of recognising and nurturing affective relationships for building resilience. The unique adaptations of Indigenous Ifugao and Balinese farmers in response to environmental hazards showcase the value of traditional knowledge, collective action, and diverse livelihoods in strengthening resilience. By developing strategic and decolonised resilience frameworks, the research emphasises the need for targeted policies incorporating tangible and intangible resources while fostering farmer collaboration.

26600521.label: Major findings and research outcome
26600521.value: Our research findings underscore the critical importance of affective capacity as an intangible capital asset for resilience building among Indigenous rice farmers (Delina et al., Under Review in Applied Geography). The study identifies various hazards impacting both the geological and socioeconomic conditions of Indigenous rice farming, leading to cascading risks that necessitate meaningful resilience strategies (Delina et al., 2024, Journal of Rural Studies). Our analysis reveals that affective relationships significantly contribute to inherent and learned resilience against emergent and cascading risks (Delina et al., Under Review in Climate Risk Management). Indigenous rice farmers access these affective capacities through their existing resilience value systems and social capital derived from extended family networks and local communities. Additionally, semi-formal organisations enhance these relationships by providing new knowledge, networks, and financial access, further strengthening farmers' resilience (Delina et al., Under Review in World Development). The study highlights the importance of rituals and ceremonies in fostering affective relations, illustrating the continued relevance of spiritual connections in resilience-building efforts. The findings suggest that formal state institutions must support the flourishing of these affective relationships to maximise opportunities for enhancing adaptive capacities (Delina et al., Under Review in Policy and Society). Furthermore, the resilience of Indigenous rice farming communities arises from a complex interplay of social, economic, political, and agricultural factors, collectively termed 'ricescapes' (Delina et al., Under Review in Climate Risk Management). We identified latent subgroups of farmers within these ricescapes that exemplify four essential dimensions of resilience: hazard management support, assistance with agricultural tasks, financial aid, and knowledge sharing. Our study reveals that ties to social networks are vital intangible assets that enhance social resilience (Delina et al., 2024, Journal of Rural Studies). However, we also identified challenges semi-formal groups face, threatening traditional support systems. Our research, thus, advocates for targeted policies that enhance social resilience by fostering interaction and collaboration, facilitating resource exchange, and improving access to financial institutions. Additionally, we emphasise the need to integrate traditional and modern agricultural practices through initiatives such as farmer field schools (Delina et al., 2024, Journal of Rural Studies). In conclusion, the findings assert that recognising and addressing the significance of emotional ties and social networks can significantly enhance the resilience and sustainability of Indigenous rice farming communities (Delina et al., Under Review in World Development). This approach ensures adaptability to contemporary challenges while preserving cultural heritage, thereby contributing to the long-term viability of these agricultural landscapes.

26600521.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
26600521.value: This research concerning Southeast Asian Indigenous rice farmers possesses significant potential for further development. Future inquiries could encompass various Indigenous communities, facilitating comparative analyses that enhance our understanding of resilience strategies across diverse cultural and spatial contexts. Moreover, integrating longitudinal quantitative methods alongside qualitative approaches could yield a more comprehensive assessment of the influence of intangible capital on farmers' livelihoods. Proposed courses of action include fortifying partnerships with local universities and organisations to promote collaborative research efforts. Such collaboration may augment knowledge exchange and empower Indigenous communities by actively engaging them in the research process. Furthermore, establishing training programmes that blend traditional knowledge with contemporary agricultural practices would assist farmers in adapting to environmental changes while safeguarding their cultural heritage. Engaging policymakers is equally crucial to ensure that the insights derived from this research inform sustainable agricultural policies. Advocacy for including Indigenous perspectives in decision-making can result in more effective and culturally relevant interventions. In summary, the continuation and expansion of this research could considerably contribute to the resilience and sustainability of Indigenous agricultural practices, ultimately benefiting both the communities involved and the broader objectives of environmental conservation and food security.

26600521.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
26600521.value: This project explored how Indigenous rice farmers in the Philippines and Indonesia navigated challenges such as climate change and social issues. It underscored the significance of their emotional and social ties - termed 'intangible capitals' - which bolstered their resilience during tough times. We discovered that these farmers depended on family and community for practical help and emotional support when confronting issues like droughts or earthquakes. The study also investigated the distinct experiences of Indigenous farmers, illustrating how they modified their farming techniques to tackle environmental threats and socio-economic challenges, including ageing populations and overtourism. These farmers created more sustainable livelihoods by utilising their traditional knowledge and participating in collective action. Additionally, the project sought to develop new resilience strategies that honoured Indigenous practices and necessities. This research was crucial as it highlighted the need for policies that provided physical resources and recognised the social and emotional bonds vital for the survival of these agricultural communities. Ultimately, it aimed to foster sustainable farming methods while safeguarding the rich cultural heritage of Indigenous Peoples.

27102621.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27102621.value: Alcohol use is harmful to the physical and psychological health of young people. Alcohol commercial marketing apparently leads to viewers’ higher acceptance of alcohol drinking, portrays a positive image of alcohol drinking, and increases drinking behavior. However, it is unclear whether the marketing effect on young adults’ alcohol drinking is due to the normalization effect from these marketing content. This study aims at using Ecological Momentary Assessment (EMA) to accurately document and explore the real-life exposure to alcohol marketing and how it influences belief in drinking normalization and alcohol consumption. By assessing participants’ awareness and receptivity of alcohol marketing, including passive exposure to advertisements and promotion campaigns and active participation of online promotion, this study has three research questions: (1) Is frequency of exposure to alcohol marketing associated with measures in drinking normalization, in terms of perceived popularity (descriptive norm), perceived social approval (injunctive norm) and positive expectancy? (2) Is receptivity of alcohol marketing associated with drinking normalization? (3) Does drinking normalization mediate the relationship between exposure to alcohol marketing and alcohol consumption level? The proposed study will recruit 259 young adults from either tertiary education institutes or online recruitment advertisements. An EMA app will be developed to administer regular prompts and daily data collection automatically. Participants will use the installed App in their own smartphone to respond to the EMA prompts five times each day (every three hours after waking) for 14 days. The EMA prompts will invite participants to document their frequency of exposure to alcohol marketing and their receptivity of alcohol marketing. Normalization belief of alcohol drinking and alcohol consumption level will be assessed at 2-month follow-up. In the first and second research question, we will use multiple linear regression model to assess the exposure frequency and receptivity on the three attributes of drinking normalization separately. In the third research question, structural equation modelling will be adopted to examine the pathways of exposure and receptivity of alcohol marketing, perceived popularity, perceived social approval, positive expectancy, and alcohol consumption level. The potential benefit of the proposed study is to provide contemporary evidence for public education on alcohol harms and enhance adequate statutory regulations in alcohol marketing. We target to reduce young people’s awareness and receptivity to alcohol marketing, so that less young people uptake or consume alcohol heavily. 飲酒對青年的身心健康有害。酒精產品的營銷策略明顯會提升觀眾對飲酒的接受度，塑造出飲酒的積極形象，並且增加觀眾的飲酒行為。然而，我們尚未清楚這些影響是否由於這些營銷內容的正常化效應。 本研究旨在使用生態瞬時評估法來準確記錄大眾於現實生活中接觸的酒精產品營銷策略，以及這些營銷如何影響飲酒正常化理念和酒精攝入。通過評估本研究參與者對酒精產品營銷的覺察和接受度，包括酒精廣告、推廣飲酒活動和參與線上促銷活動，本研究集中三個主要研究問題： （1）接觸酒精產品營銷策略的頻率是否與飲酒正常化理念相關？飲酒正常化理念將由三個方向評估，包括感知性受歡迎程度（敘述式規範），感知性社會認可程度（指令式規範）以及積極期待。 （2）青年對酒精產品營銷的接受程度是否與飲酒正常化理念相關？ （3）「飲酒正常化理念」是否屬於「接觸酒精產品營銷」與「酒精攝入程度」的中介變量？ 本研究將會通過各大高校或者線上招募廣告招募360名青年參與。本研究將開發一個新的生態瞬時評估法的應用程式來自動管理定期的問題提示與日常數據收集。研究參與者將在個人智能手機上安裝此應用程式來回復生態瞬時評估法的問題提示。這些提示每天會出現3次（參與者午餐及之後每五個小時一次），一共持續21天。這些生態瞬時評估法的資訊提示將邀請本研究參與者記錄他們接觸飲酒相關商業營銷的頻率以及他們對此類營銷的接受程度。在21天記錄結束之後的一個月，本研究將會展開隨訪。隨訪將會評估參與者的飲酒正常化理念和酒精攝入程度。 針對第一個和第二個研究問題，本研究將使用多元線性回歸模型分別評估接觸飲酒相關商業酒精產品營銷的頻率和接受程度對飲酒正常化理念的三個方向（敘述式規範，指令式規範以及積極期待）的影響。針對第三個研究問題，本研究將採用結構方程模型來檢驗參與者對飲酒相關商業營銷的接觸和接受程度，感知性的酒精的受歡迎的程度，感知性的酒精的社會認可程度，以及積極期待與酒精的攝入程度的關係路徑。 本研究希望能夠提供更多實證證據來支持關於酒精危害的公眾教育，以期能夠加強飲酒相關商業營銷策的適當法規。本研究的目的在於降低青年對酒精產品營銷的覺察以及接受程度，從而減少青年對酒精的攝入。

27109121.label: Project Title(Chinese)
27109121.value: 胚胎發育中Herzog功能類澱粉蛋白聚集的結構基礎摘要

27109121.label: Project Objectives
27109121.value: • Objective 1. Purification and characterization of monomeric and aggregated Hzg states from developing embryos Objective 1.1. Purify monomeric and aggregated Hzg states from developing embryos The structure of small fragments of functional amyloids, assembled in vitro, has been solved (Mompeán et al., 2018; Wasmer et al., 2008). However, due to several reasons, this approach is often unsuitable for the characterization of functional amyloids. First, most proteins form amyloids in vitro under certain conditions, regardless of whether they form an amyloid state in vivo (Dobson, 2003). Second, for a given protein, in vitro-assembled amyloids may vary in length, morphology, and structure. For example, our recent study shows that endogenous CPEB/Orb2 forms ~75 nm long amyloid filaments implicated in memory consolidation through the translation activation of neuronal target mRNAs (Hervas et al., 2020). By contrast, in vitro-assembled Orb2 forms micron-long, non-biochemically active amyloid filaments, whose structure differs from the one obtained directly from brain samples (Cervantes et al., 2016; Hervas et al., 2020). Finally, in cells, protein behavior depends on myriad interactions, and the cellular context can ultimately influence protein structure. This observation is particularly relevant for amyloids serving tissue or context-specific functions, such as Hzg (Nil et al., 2019). Therefore, to gain an insight into the relationship of Hzg aggregation, structure, and function, we will isolate both monomeric and aggregated Hzg conformational states from biologically relevant tissue, such as developing embryos during or after gastrulation, the stage when Hzg aggregation occurs (Nil et al., 2019). Objective 1.2. Determine the biophysical properties of monomeric and aggregated Hzg states isolated from developing embryos. Our recent results using Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy analysis of recombinant Hzg, fluorescence recovery after photobleaching analysis of ectopically expressed Hzg-EGFP assemblies, and detergent resistance assay of ectopically expressed Hzg aggregates suggest that Hzg forms an amyloid-like assembly (Nil et al., 2019). However, none of these experiments directly evaluates the biophysical properties of the endogenous Hzg aggregates. To get insight into the nature of the different Hzg conformational states isolated from the embryo, we will evaluate the biophysical properties of monomeric and aggregated endogenous Hzg. Objective 1.3. Measure the phosphatase activity of monomeric and aggregated Hzg states isolated from developing embryos. Hzg belongs to the haloacid dehalogenase (HAD) family of phosphatases, an ancient large class of enzymes. Mechanistically, amyloid-like assembly is essential for acquiring Hzg phosphatase activity, being catalytically inactive in the monomeric state (Nil et al., 2019). To validate our purification method and determine the biological relevance of monomeric and aggregated Hzg states, we will use a functional assay to measure Hzg phosphatase activity prior to structure determination. • Objective 2. High-resolution structural features of monomeric and aggregated Hzg states isolated from developing embryos. Mechanistically, cell-based assays using Hzg deletion mutants suggest that in the monomeric state, the catalytic site, which is located in the middle FCP homology domain together with the substrate-binding site, may be either blocked or hidden by the N-terminal prion-like domain (Nil et al., 2019). We hypothesize that conformational changes upon amyloid assembly, mediated by the N-terminal prion-like domain, would expose the cryptic or blocked catalytic site along with the substrate-binding site to the surface of the amyloid assembly. A similar autoinhibitory mechanism has been proposed during the non-amyloid polymerization process of CARD9 (Holliday et al., 2019). To gain a mechanistic understanding of this hypothesis, or alternative activation mechanisms, we will obtain structural information of monomeric Hzg and the poorly understood underlying conformational changes occurring during monomer to amyloid transition by NMR spectroscopy (Objective 2.1), as well as the atomic structure of aggregated Hzg by cryo-EM (Objective 2.2).

27109121.value: 類澱粉蛋白——一種富含交聯β折疊的蛋白——的聚集並與病理狀態相關，包括阿兹海默症，然而自重複的類澱粉蛋白狀態（又被稱爲“生理狀態類澱粉蛋白”）卻又參與了多樣的生命現象。生理狀態類澱粉蛋白與病理性的類澱粉蛋白共享類似特徵，同時他們也展現出關聯多種生物學過程的承載能力對應的特徵：這些特徵包括依靠自身的蛋白功能變化，局部蛋白濃度的增加，一個具有結構的區域，和高度穩定卻又可塑的結構。 在黑腹果蠅中，膜蛋白Herzog(Hzg)是一種在胚胎體節極性正確建立過程中所必需的蛋白。儘管Hzg在胚胎發育中廣汎地被表達，但進入到原腸胚形成期后，Hzg會從單體轉變爲聚集狀態。這種聚集狀態具有類似於類澱粉蛋白組裝相同的特徵，即在控制動物發育時需要獲得磷酸酶活性，正如涉及到TGF-β/BMP和FGF/EGF信號通路的情況。不同的是，這種磷酸化需要完成膜定位和通過蛋白N端阮病毒樣區域達成的類澱粉蛋白的組裝，而對這個過程的研究能夠提供類澱粉蛋白狀態如何在空間和時間上調控磷酸酶活性以進一步調控胚胎發育的第一手資料。 儘管我們如今對調控病理性蛋白聚集原理的理解不斷加深，類澱粉蛋白如何保持生理狀態的調控單元依然未知。其中一部分的原因是我們仍然缺乏内源性分離的生理狀態類澱粉蛋白的高分辨率結構信息。我們計劃使用冷凍電鏡技術(cryo-EM)來研究從發育胚胎中提取的具有酶活性的聚集態Hzg蛋白酶結構特徵。最近我們提取了一批果蠅大腦中内源性生理狀態類澱粉蛋白，並研究和計算了其結構。基於我們分離自然狀態具有生物活性的類澱粉蛋白的豐富經驗和應用先進實驗方法的計劃，我們目標是研究驅動Hzg蛋白獲得磷酸酶活性因素的結構特徵，通過控制動物發育的Hzg類澱粉蛋白的組裝來進行。我們預計，研究内源性生理狀態Hzg類澱粉樣蛋白的聚集結構，將會從新的視角看到體内生理狀態類澱粉蛋白構象的生理狀態結果，同時也會從另一方面瞭解生物體如何調節類澱粉蛋白的組裝和解聚，以實現在時間和空間上對類澱粉蛋白功能的限制。另外，加深對生理狀態和病理狀態的類澱粉蛋白的瞭解能夠幫助我們理解爲什麽類澱粉蛋白和人類疾病時常具有關聯。

27109121.label: Realisation of objectives
27109121.value: The main objectives of this project were to purify and characterize the monomeric and aggregated states of Hzg from developing embryos, to determine their biophysical properties and enzymatic activities, and to obtain high-resolution structural information on these conformational states. I am pleased to report that significant progress has been made toward achieving these objectives, as detailed below. Objective 1: Purification and Characterization of Monomeric and Aggregated Hzg States from Developing Embryos Objective 1.1: Purify monomeric and aggregated Hzg states from developing embryos We have successfully isolated both monomeric and aggregated forms of endogenous Hzg from Drosophila embryos at the relevant developmental stages (during and after gastrulation). The purification protocols were optimized to preserve native conformational states, and careful validation using SDS-PAGE, western blotting, and size-exclusion chromatography confirmed the separation and integrity of monomeric and aggregated fractions. These results overcome the limitations of previous studies that relied on recombinant or in vitro-assembled protein, ensuring that our subsequent analyses reflect the native physiological context. Objective 1.2: Determine the biophysical properties of monomeric and aggregated Hzg states We have performed a detailed biophysical characterization of the purified Hzg states. Using a combination of Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), circular dichroism (CD), and dynamic light scattering (DLS), we demonstrated that the aggregated Hzg displays characteristic amyloid-like properties, including increased β-sheet content and detergent resistance, consistent with our previous work (Nil et al., 2019). These properties were not observed in the monomeric state. Importantly, all experiments were performed on endogenous protein purified from embryos, allowing us to directly link these biophysical properties to the physiological state of Hzg during development. Objective 1.3: Measure the phosphatase activity of monomeric and aggregated Hzg states We established a robust phosphatase activity assay for endogenous Hzg and found, as hypothesized, that the aggregated state displays substantial phosphatase activity, whereas the monomeric state is catalytically inactive. These results validate the functionality of our purified fractions and support the model that amyloid assembly is required for Hzg enzymatic activity in vivo. This functional assay also provided a quality control step prior to structural analysis, ensuring that only biochemically active aggregates were used for downstream studies. Objective 2: High-Resolution Structural Features of Monomeric and Aggregated Hzg States Objective 2.1: Structural analysis of monomeric Hzg by NMR spectroscopy We have collected preliminary NMR data on the monomeric Hzg state, and assignment of backbone resonances is underway. Early results suggest that the N-terminal prion-like domain is flexible in the monomer, potentially mediating the autoinhibition of the catalytic site. Further experiments are ongoing to complete the resonance assignment and to map the interaction between the N-terminal and catalytic domains. Objective 2.2: Structural analysis of aggregated Hzg by cryo-EM Significant progress has been made in determining the structure of aggregated Hzg. Cryo-EM imaging has provided clear evidence of amyloid-like filament formation at the class 2D level, revealing distinct morphological features and periodicity consistent with functional amyloids. We are currently finalizing the 3D reconstruction calculations, and expect to achieve near-atomic resolution in the upcoming weeks. These data will be critical for elucidating the conformational changes that underlie Hzg activation and amyloid assembly. Summary and Outstanding Work In summary, the project objectives have been largely achieved. Both monomeric and aggregated Hzg states have been successfully purified from physiologically relevant tissue, their biophysical and functional properties have been characterized, and structural analysis is well underway. The only partial under-achievement relates to the finalization of the 3D cryo-EM structure of aggregated Hzg; this is due to the computational complexity and the need for further data collection to improve particle numbers and resolution. To address this, we have optimized sample preparation and imaging conditions, and additional cryo-EM sessions are scheduled. We anticipate that the final structure will be resolved within the next few weeks, completing the last outstanding objective. Overall, the project has provided novel insights into the relationship between Hzg aggregation, structure, and function, and has established a robust platform for future mechanistic studies of functional amyloids in development.

27109121.label: Major findings and research outcome
27109121.value: Our research has yielded significant new insights into the structure and function of the Hzg protein during embryonic development. The major finding of this project is the demonstration that endogenous Hzg assumes an aggregated, amyloid-like state in developing embryos, particularly during and after gastrulation. This amyloid assembly is not only a structural hallmark but is also functionally essential: we have shown that only the aggregated form of Hzg possesses phosphatase activity, while the monomeric form is catalytically inactive. This functional amyloid assembly is critical for proper embryonic patterning, as experimental inhibition of Hzg aggregation leads to pronounced developmental defects and aberrant tissue organization. These findings highlight a previously unrecognized mechanism by which functional amyloids regulate key developmental processes (see Part C, Section 5.2 for experimental details). At the structural level, we have successfully purified monomeric and aggregated forms of endogenous Hzg from embryos and characterized their biophysical properties. Cryo-EM imaging has provided class 2D evidence of the amyloid nature of aggregated Hzg, and final 3D structure determination is nearing completion (see Part C, Objective 2.2). Preliminary NMR data on the monomeric state further support an autoinhibitory mechanism mediated by the N-terminal prion-like domain (see Part C, Objective 2.1). These results establish Hzg as a model for studying functional amyloids in multicellular development and provide a methodological framework for characterizing endogenous amyloid assemblies in vivo. Regarding research outputs, one manuscript describing these findings is currently in preparation, with myself as the corresponding author; we anticipate submission in the coming months. Additionally, PhD student Mayur Mukhi, who contributed significantly to this project, is preparing to defend his thesis. For further details on publications and research training outcomes, please refer to the Research Output section (Part C, Section 8). In summary, our work has uncovered a critical role for amyloid-like aggregation of Hzg in embryonic development, provided mechanistic insights into its regulation and activity, and generated resources and methodologies that will support future research in the field of functional amyloids and developmental biology.

27109121.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27109121.value: Building on our current findings, we plan to further investigate the structure and function of Hzg aggregates in their native cellular context during early embryogenesis. Specifically, our next step will be to employ cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET) to visualize Hzg assemblies in situ within developing embryos at the gastrulation stage. This approach will allow us to capture the ultrastructural organization of Hzg amyloid assemblies in their physiological environment, providing unprecedented insights into their interactions with other cellular components and their role in tissue patterning. We are well-positioned to pursue this direction, as we have already generated CRISPR-engineered embryo lines expressing tagged Hzg, which will facilitate high-resolution imaging and localization studies. These experiments will not only deepen our understanding of functional amyloids in development but may also identify novel regulatory mechanisms and interacting partners. In parallel, we will continue developing biochemical and genetic tools to dissect the functional consequences of modulating Hzg aggregation in vivo. This research will lay the foundation for future studies into the broader roles of amyloid assemblies in multicellular organisms.

27109121.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27109121.value: This research project explored how a protein called Hzg helps organize the early development of embryos. We discovered that, in order to work properly, Hzg needs to group together and form special structures called amyloids. While amyloids are often linked to diseases like Alzheimer’s, our work shows that they can also have important, beneficial roles in healthy development. By studying fruit fly embryos, we found that Hzg only becomes active when it forms these amyloid groups, and that this activity is essential for the correct formation and patterning of the embryo. If we prevent Hzg from forming amyloids, the embryos do not develop properly. This reveals that amyloids can help cells communicate and organize during the earliest stages of life. Our research also developed new ways to study these protein structures directly in embryos, rather than in artificial lab conditions. These findings could change how scientists think about amyloids and open up new possibilities for understanding both healthy development and disease. In the future, we plan to look even closer at how Hzg amyloids work inside living embryos, which may lead to new insights into how complex life forms develop.

27109921.value: Red blood cells can sustain life via the supply of oxygen, whereas immune cells can fight infections and disease such as bacteria and cancer cells. In particular, a type of innate immune cells, called innate lymphoid cells, could be used to determine if a cancer immunotherapy works or not. We developed a powerful stem cell culture system that allowed us to recapitulate blood/immune cell development in human organoids. What makes innate lymphoid cells respond to cancer immunotherapy? The analysis of how innate lymphoid cells develop in human organoids will answer this question. In this highly collaborative project, we will focus on the identification of the key molecular switches in innate lymphoid cells that determine the positive response to cancer immunotherapy. The project will use novel technologies such as molecular barcoding to track the origin of innate lymphoid cells. We will also use stem cells to recapitulate the development of innate lymphoid cells. 27112321.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27112321.value: Half a century of research efforts in human cardiovascular physiology and derived clinical outcomes have conclusively demonstrated the relevance of aerobic capacity, as determined via exercise testing, for cardiovascular health. The higher the aerobic capacity the greater the likelihood to be free of cardiovascular disease, the leading cause of death in female and elderly populations. Understanding the principal mechanisms that determine aerobic capacity remains essential for the prevention of cardiovascular disease. According to well-established physiological principles, blood volume is a major determinant of aerobic capacity. In brief, blood volume facilitates venous return, cardiac filling and output via the Frank-Starling mechanism (so-called ‘Law of the heart’), thereby regulating convective oxygen delivery and aerobic capacity. Yet, the vast majority of studies supporting our current understanding of aerobic capacity comprise young male individuals. Whether blood volume governs cardiac output and aerobic capacity remains uncertain in females and individuals with advanced age, both groups presenting with low blood volume and high susceptibility to cardiovascular disease. The present project will elucidate the chronic impact of blood volume expansion on aerobic capacity in female and elderly populations, therefore addressing a relevant knowledge gap with major clinical applications. Ultimately, the focus of this project is far from irrelevant since blood attributes are amenable to lifestyle- and pharmacological-related modification and thus potentially translated into effective targets to improve or preserve cardiovascular health in the general population. 摘要：半個世紀以來，人類心血管生理學的研究成果和衍生的臨床結果已最終證明，通過運動測試確定的有氧能力與心血管健康的相關性。有氧能力越高，免於患心血管疾病的可能性就越大。心血管疾病是女性和老年人死亡的主要原因。理解決定有氧能力的主要機制對心血管疾病的預防來說仍然至關重要。根據公認的生理學原理，血容量是有氧能力的主要決定因素。簡言之，血容量通過Frank-Starling機制（所謂的“心臟定律”）促進靜脈回流、心臟充盈和輸出，從而調節對流氧氣輸送和有氧能力。然而，支持我們目前對有氧能力理解的絕大多數研究都是年輕男性。 在女性和高齡個體中，血容量是否控制心輸出量和有氧能力仍然不確定，這兩個群體都表現出低血容量和高心血管疾病易感性。本項目將闡明血容量擴張對女性和老年人群有氧能力的長期影響，從而解決與主要臨床應用相關的知識差距。 最終，該項目的重點遠非無關緊要，因為血液屬性可通過生活方式和藥理學相關的改變而改變，因此有可能轉化為改善或保持普通人群心血管健康的有效目標。

27126321.value: 持续性的感染和炎症会引起哺乳动物的气道重塑，进而导致粘液细胞增生和粘液阻塞，但其驱动机制目前尚不清楚。单细胞测序和分化轨迹分析结果表明，哮喘患者的气道中存在着一种新的、同时具有纤毛形成功能和粘液分泌功能的细胞，而该类细胞来源于经过炎症信号诱导的纤毛细胞谱系。同时，暴露在空气中的新生幼鼠气道也存在着大量的“纤毛-分泌细胞”，并伴随着与哮喘和过敏相关细胞因子的暂时性迅速上调。因此，我们认为：来自疾病和正常生理状态的“纤毛-分泌细胞”很可能具有共同的祖先，且被类似的炎症信号所诱导。通过遗传谱系追踪，计算机模拟发育轨迹，气道类器官培养等技术，我们将会对该假说进行验证。本研究属于首次对气道上皮的可塑性的进行动态分析，并且能为阐明气道细胞转分化的信号网络和识别能够阻断粘液细胞增生的药物靶标提供基本理论支持。

27126321.label: Realisation of objectives
27126321.value: The respiratory system represents a major interface between internal organs and the environment1. The respiratory tract is protected by a mucosal epithelial barrier, which consists predominantly of motile ciliated cells and secretory cells to provide the primary and foremost host defense mechanism2. Acquired respiratory conditions, including smoking, chronic inflammation, and virus infection, can also disrupt motile cilia and impair mucus transport. Proinflammatory cytokines can induce airway remodeling, but the underlying mechanisms remain undefined. Mucus obstruction and bacterial infections are clinical features of these acquired and inheritable respiratory conditions. More than 50% of patients world-wide with acute respiratory infections and chronic bronchitis are prescribed antibiotics, which may not hasten resolution of the clinical symptoms and have numerous adverse effects5. The major challenge to understand the pathophysiology of respiratory diseases is the lack of proper models, as laboratory rodent models fail to recapitulate essential human disease characters. The National Institutes of Health (NIH) announced an initiative that will make the development, validation, and application of human-based research technologies a top research priority through innovative, human-based science while reducing the use of animal models in research. For respiratory diseases, there is no human-based model that encompasses all essential cell types required to respond and mediate different aspects of disease states. A more comprehensive respiratory organoid model with stronger clinical translation and human relevance is much needed to advance of understanding of human airway biology and pathophysiology. Upon completion of this proposal, we have now identified pathways important for the heterogeneity and plasticity for ciliated cells. Importantly, we have established an innovative human iPSC derived models to test whether these mechanisms are conserved from mice to humans. The results will be submitted within a month.
