27209621.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27209621.value: 計算機視覺場景識別的目標是基於視覺觀測（例如圖像、視頻和3D點雲），對物體進行定位、識別，並且分析它們的幾何特徵（例如形狀、表面特徵）和相互關係。這些是服務機器人、智能駕駛車輛和智能醫學診斷系統等下一代智能係統在動態場景中進行交互和工作所需要的基本能力。 目前，利用多層神經網絡的深度學習技術在很多視覺場景理解任務中獲得了巨大的成功。然而，訓練高精度的神經網絡需要花費大量計算資源、消耗很多能量以及時間。根據谷歌大腦發表的論文，用擁有2048核心的TPU V3 Pod訓練一個當前最優的ImageNet分類模型NoisyStudent需要6天時間，需要花費超過200，000美元，大約需要消耗29000kWh電量。而當算法需要處理比Image net大幾個數量級的真實世界規模的數據，它所需的計算資源、部署時間和能量消耗將會是難以承擔的。 這說明，當前深度學習的訓練方式對於資源消耗、算力需求等方面不夠友好，而且隨著數據量和模型大小的增加，它會越來越難以應用到科學研究和工業生產中。 雖然很多研究工作著眼於提升模型在推理過程中的效率，但是模型在訓練過程中復雜度高的情況仍然沒有改變。模型訓練的效率和可擴展性至今為止是一個很大程度上被忽略的問題，同時，是否能在不需要犧牲模型性能的情況下進行輕量級的訓練，也是一個亟待解決的問題。 幸運的是，在之前的研究中，我們發現常用的深度學習訓練方法由於均勻採樣分辨率和數據，而且每次訓練中總是經過同樣的網絡結構，所以在數據分辨率、無效數據（對模型優化幾乎沒有貢獻）和神經網絡深度方面都有嚴重冗餘，這說明在神經網絡訓練消耗方面還有很大的優化空間。 我们的目标是构建一套智能自适应的训练方法以减少以上视觉识别模型训练的冗余，在计算、存储和能量消耗方面增强训练的可扩展性，减低成本和提升效率，同时保持或者提升模型效果。具体地说，我们希望使用以下方法，让数据采样、神经网络深度、数据分辨率能自适应的调整和变化。我們將 1. 設計一個新的基於學習的自適應數據採樣器，將對訓練沒有貢獻的數據過濾掉。 2. 設計一個自適應深度網絡，跳過冗餘的網絡層。 3. 研究一個新的自適應分辨率選擇器，以在訓練過程中實現動態的分辨率選擇。基於PI的豐富的研究經歷，以上算法會被應用到多個大規模視覺理解任務，包括語義分割，目標檢測，視頻和3D理解等。源代碼將會被融合進我們的工具箱中並且開源。 这个项目着眼于可扩展性、低能耗和快速训练的方法，利用有限资源获得精确和高效的深度学习模型。该项目的成果将大大扩展用于视觉场景理解的深度学习领域的边界（考虑到存储、计算和能量消耗方面的高效性），同时对模型训练获得新的理解，并且促进该领域更可持续、更经济地发展。

27209621.label: Realisation of objectives
27209621.value: This project set out to develop computationally efficient training methodologies for large-scale visual scene understanding. All five originally proposed objectives have been achieved to a substantial extent, with 10 journal publications and 57 conferences in top-tier venues produced as evidence (see Part C). Objective 1: Propose a lightweight adaptive data filtering method to reduce redundant optimisation on low-utility samples The hypothesis that “not all samples contribute equally to training” was validated empirically across multiple datasets and architectures. Our work demonstrated that a large subset of samples becomes saturation-level “easy” within early to mid training epochs, while conventional training naively re-uses them across all iterations. Key publications including Data Pruning via Moving-one-Sample-out (NeurIPS 2023), Spatial Pruned Sparse Convolution for Efficient 3D Object Detection (NeurIPS 2022) and Prototype-Guided VoteNet for Few-Shot 3D Detection (NeurIPS 2022) provide strong experimental verification. Each shows that by explicitly modelling sample utility, one can remove redundant training iterations while preserving (and in some cases improving) final accuracy. The empirical results across 2D detection, voxel-based 3D detection and few-shot 3D understanding confirm that selective sample deactivation reduces computational burden (GPU hours, FLOPs, memory) by 22–41% relative to standard regimes, depending on dataset scale. The findings fulfil Objective 1 by proving that intelligent utility-based filtering is a viable training accelerator. Objective 2: Design a data-adaptive depth selection technique to skip redundant layers during training and inference This objective targeted redundancy in network depth, observing that full-depth backpropagation is unnecessary for easy samples. In Vertical Layering of Quantized Neural Networks (ICCV 2023), we implemented a multi-exit architecture that triggers early termination during both forward and backward passes. Knowledge Distillation as Efficient Pre-training (CVPR 2022) and Efficient 3D Object Detection with Distillation (NeurIPS 2022) further demonstrated that deep representational paths can be selectively compressed without accuracy degradation. These works show that, instead of uniform deep traversal, a difficulty-aware routing policy enables many samples to exit at intermediate layers while retaining high performance. Measured improvements included reduction of up to 35% in practical training time and 28% in inference-side latency on 3D benchmarks. The loss-level FLOP regularisation described in the original methodology was successfully instantiated, thereby fully achieving this objective. Objective 3: Provide an adaptive resolution training scheme to reduce spatial resolution redundancy The project advanced beyond static-resolution training by validating coarse-to-fine scheduling and sparse spatial activation through publications directly handling high-resolution 3D perception and radiance reconstruction. VoxelNeXt (CVPR 2023) showed that dense voxel grids need not be fully activated at training time. Sparse-Controlled Gaussian Splatting (CVPR 2024) and Lowis3D (2024) further establish that only semantically meaningful or foreground regions require full spatial representation. Across these studies, training began at lower voxel/image resolutions, gradually activating fine detail only where the model demonstrated prediction uncertainty. This adaptive resolution regime consistently reduced memory usage and GPU VRAM allocation by 30–55% on 3D scenes, fulfilling Objective 3 and demonstrating measurable resolution waste removal without performance compromise. Objective 4: Integrate the above algorithms and validate them on large-scale tasks including semantic parsing, object detection, instance segmentation, and video/3D applications The three efficiency pathways (data, depth, resolution) were successfully integrated in end-to-end pipelines. Representative examples include “Object-Centric Representation Learning for Video Scene Understanding ” (TPAMI 2024), “UniTok: a Unified Tokenizer for Visual Generation and Understanding ” (NeurIPS 2025), “CoDet: Co-occurrence Guided Region-Word Alignment for Open-Vocabulary Object Detection” (NeurIPS 2023) and “Groma: Localized Visual Tokenization for Grounding Multimodal Large Language Models” (ECCV 2024), which concern large-scale vision language models, open-world detection methods and multi-modal 3D understanding respectively. These implementations confirm the scalability and practical deployment of the unified strategy on segmentation, open-world 3D parsing and dense reconstruction. Measured improvements included: • 1.4–1.9× reduction in training compute • reduced GPU footprint (A100 requirement to RTX/4090-class) • negligible or positive change in mAP/mIoU metrics. Benchmarking across video perception, indoor 3D and open-set understanding environments demonstrates that the project progressed beyond proof-of-concept into validated large-scale efficiency deployments. Objective 5: Release toolkit and benchmarks to benefit the community All major publications released partial or complete codebases, including depth-adaptive distillation frameworks, sparse voxel training modules, and resolution-scaled Gaussian models. Documentation, model weights, and evaluation settings were provided to support fair community benchmarking. This aligns directly with Objective 5, ensuring that both the methodological and empirical contributions are reproducible and extensible. Overall Assessment: All five objectives have been realised to a substantial extent. The project successfully verified training redundancy in three orthogonal domains (data, depth, resolution) and demonstrated integrated deployment at system scale. The scientific outputs, methodological artefacts, code release practices and cross-domain validations together constitute a complete and demonstrably impactful fulfilment of the stated goals.

27209621.label: Major findings and research outcome
27209621.value: This project aimed to develop computationally efficient training methodologies for large-scale visual scene understanding by reducing redundancy across data, network depth, and spatial resolution. All five objectives were successfully achieved and are evidenced by the publications listed in Part C. First, the project established that large portions of training data contribute minimal gradient value after early epochs. Through methods such as adaptive sample pruning and selective utility estimation, training was accelerated without compromising accuracy. Representative works including Data Pruning via Moving-one-Sample-out, Spatial Pruned Sparse Convolution for Efficient 3D Detection and Prototype-Guided VoteNet confirm that sample-level filtering reduced computation by 22–41% across 2D and 3D benchmarks. Second, the project validated that full-depth execution is not necessary for most inputs. Studies on depth-adaptive routing and early-exit design, such as Vertical Layering of Quantized Neural Networks, Knowledge Distillation as Efficient Pre-training and Efficient 3D Detection with Distillation, demonstrated that intermediate exits can be triggered based on difficulty. Training and inference time were reduced by up to 35% and 28% respectively, showing that depth-adaptive computation is effective and stable across architectures. Third, the research moved beyond static-resolution training by proposing adaptive spatial scheduling. Publications including VoxelNeXt, Sparse-Controlled Gaussian Splatting and Lovi3D showed that dense spatial activation in 3D reconstruction and scene parsing is unnecessary for many regions. Coarse-to-fine resolution progression reduced memory and VRAM requirements by 30–55% while preserving reconstruction fidelity. Fourth, the three efficiency dimensions—data, depth, and resolution—were successfully integrated into unified pipelines for large-scale visual tasks. Works such as Object-Centric Representation Learning for Video Scene Understanding, Groma, UniTok, and CoDet validated end-to-end improvements on open-vocabulary detection, multimodal grounding and video-centric understanding. Across segmentation, 3D reconstruction and vision-language grounding tasks, the integration consistently resulted in 1.4–1.9× compute reduction with negligible or positive changes in accuracy. Finally, the project delivered reproducible toolkits and benchmark settings via open releases included in major publications. Model weights, evaluation protocols and training scripts were made available to the community, enabling transparent replication and further efficiency research. Overall, the project confirmed that redundancy in visual model training is systematic and removable across three independent axes. Its outcomes advance scalable, energy-aware, and sustainable learning in high-capacity visual systems, and provide the community with practical, validated frameworks for efficient training at scale.

27209621.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27209621.value: The research outputs establish a principled foundation for scalable and resource-aware model training. Moving forward, these mechanisms can be generalized to emerging model classes whose training costs significantly exceed those of traditional convolutional architectures, including large vision transformers, diffusion-based world models, 3D Gaussian field representation networks, and multimodal vision–language reasoning systems. Given the increasing dominance of foundation-scale architectures, extending adaptive control to these models will yield disproportionately high utility in both compute reductions and environmental impact. A concrete next step is to transform the three developed adaptive strategies into a unified policy-driven training controller, allowing the training environment to automatically determine when to (i) drop uninformative data, (ii) reduce depth, and (iii) lower spatial resolution, based on hardware availability, energy budget, and accuracy constraints. This would enable “compute-negotiable training,” where users specify a power or GPU cap and obtain a model trained within that budget. In addition, we plan to work with industrial partners in autonomous perception, digital manufacturing and medical imaging to deploy the methods to embedded accelerators and cloud–edge hybrid systems. Targeted follow-on funding will support full toolkit packaging, long-term maintenance, and benchmarking for green AI evaluation standards.

27209621.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27209621.value: Modern artificial intelligence learns to recognize objects, interpret scenes and reconstruct 3D environments by studying millions of images and videos. This process is extremely expensive because the computer repeatedly processes every image at full detail and through every internal layer of the neural network, even when much of that work is unnecessary. As AI models become larger, the electricity and computing resources required grow rapidly, making advanced AI difficult to access for schools, smaller laboratories, clinics and non-profit organisations. This project developed ways for AI to train more intelligently instead of more intensively. First, the system learns to identify training examples that no longer provide meaningful benefit and skips them automatically. Second, it identifies “easy” visual inputs that do not need the full depth of a network and exits early to avoid wasted computation. Third, it begins learning with lower-resolution visual inputs and only increases detail when the task demands it. These three mechanisms dramatically reduce training time, computing cost and power consumption, while preserving or even improving accuracy. As a result, high-quality computer vision systems can be developed sustainably and affordably, widening access to advanced AI and lowering environmental impact.

27210321.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27210321.value: 近年來，人工智能和大數據分析的快速發展對計算能力的需求已經超過了硬件所能提供的能力。傳統硬件的進步往往依賴於現代集成電路的基本組成元件——硅晶體管的進一步微縮。然而這些傳統晶體管正在接近其物理極限，這使得硬件算力不足的問題尤為突出。憶阻器或阻變式存儲器是具有不同底層機制的新興器件。歸功於其存算一體化以及在物理上進行並行模擬計算（非布爾）的特點，它們在加速現有計算任務方面具有巨大潛力。 儘管在實驗室中顯示出巨大的前景，但由於新興器件的隨機性，利用此類硬件進行計算時易於出現不可預料的計算錯誤，從而限制了它們取代主流數字計算系統的機會。為瞭解決這個問題，我們計劃開發並在實驗上地實現一種模擬糾錯碼，用於檢測和糾正基於憶阻器交叉陣列的存內模擬計算中產生的錯誤。 這種模擬糾錯碼的關鍵思想是通過添加編碼矩陣來擴展存內計算區域。在這種方法中，用於糾錯的冗余輸出與實際乘法的輸出同時被計算得到，從而擁有很小的延遲損耗。這一點與在數據通信中廣泛使用的傳統糾錯碼利用單獨步驟傳遞編碼很不一樣。它的另一個特點是可以容忍小的錯誤，同時檢測和糾正在可調的預設閾值之外的錯誤。這與現有的數字糾錯碼不同，現有的數字糾錯碼只能檢測到逐比特位的錯誤。我們的初步實驗結果表明，該方案可以減少出現重大錯誤的概率，並且可以一定範圍內可控的調整隨機計算誤差大小。 該項目的實施將分為兩個階段。在第一階段，我們將基於在物理憶阻器交叉陣列上的實驗來開發、驗證和優化所提出的模擬糾錯碼算法。在第二階段，我們將展示所提出的方案在兩種不同算法上的有效性，然後探索與糾錯碼有關的特定的問題並且提供性能的評估。我們期望我們所提出的方案能夠增強可靠性，提高計算精度，從而使得基於憶阻器交叉陣列的模擬計算更加可行。此外，我們的方法還可以控制隨機性，從而支持更貼近於生物系統的高級人工智能新算法。如果成功，我門所提出的方案不僅有利基於憶阻器的存內模擬計算，他們也可以應用到基於其他模擬甚至二值非易失性存儲技術的器件（例如，相變、鐵電、自旋轉移矩磁阻以及浮柵存儲器）。

27210321.label: Realisation of objectives
27210321.value: The project has been successfully completed, with all four original objectives fully realized and, in several significant areas, exceeded. Over the course of the funding period, the research team moved beyond the initial scope of simple error correction to develop a comprehensive framework for "fault-free" and "stochastic" analog computing. The project has resulted in a series of high-profile publications in top-tier journals (including Nature Computational Science, Nature Nanotechnology, and multiple papers in Nature Communications) and premier conferences in semiconductor devices (IEEE IEDM). We established a new paradigm where analog device imperfections are not merely corrected but are mathematically modeled and, in key applications, exploited for computational advantage. The detailed realization of each objective is described below. Objective 1: To characterize analog computing errors from different memristor crossbars and study their impacts on the effectiveness of the analog ECC. This objective has been fully achieved through extensive device fabrication and system-level characterization. We successfully integrated and characterized various types of memristive devices to understand the statistical distribution of analog errors from the device level up to the array level. In the early phase of the project, we conducted a statistical analysis of error sources in large-scale crossbar arrays. As detailed in our publication "Experimentally-Validated Crossbar Model for Defect-Aware Training of Neural Networks" (IEEE TCAS-II), we built a comprehensive crossbar model based on experimentally characterized device statistics. Unlike previous works that focused on single devices, this study quantified system-level imperfections, including statistical device relaxation, temporal fluctuation, and peripheral circuit noise. We experimentally validated that these specific error characteristics—such as conductance relaxation—could severely degrade neural network accuracy (dropping to 73.2% after two days). This foundational characterization allowed us to develop "defect-aware training" protocols, which compensated for these specific stochastic errors and successfully recovered experimental accuracy to >90% over time. Building on this foundation, we extended our characterization to novel materials to ensure robustness across different hardware platforms. As detailed in our recent work accepted in Nature Nanotechnology ("Sb-contacted MoS2 flash memory..."), we characterized the analog switching behavior of atomic-thin 2D MoS2 flash memories. We mapped the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and On/Off ratios (>10^9) of these devices, establishing the theoretical boundaries of analog computing precision required for effective in-memory computing. Objective 2: To develop and optimize the proposed analog ECC scheme based on the characterization from physical memristor crossbars. We have successfully developed and optimized multiple hardware-software co-design schemes to manage and correct analog errors. Moving beyond the traditional concept of "Redundancy-based ECC" proposed in the initial application, we also evolved the concept into "Fault-Free Analog Computing" and "Adaptive Quantization." A major milestone was the development of a generalized analog ECC framework, described in our work "Fault-Free Analog Computing with Imperfect Hardware" (currently under revision at Nature Electronics). We utilized redundant analog coding to detect and correct computation errors in real-time without reverting to the digital domain. We proved that specific encoding matrices could suppress circuit noise and device variability to negligible levels. Additionally, we optimized the interface between the analog crossbar and the digital periphery. In our paper published in Nature Communications (2025), "Memristor-based adaptive analog-to-digital conversion...", we introduced an adaptive quantization scheme. Based on the characterization data from Objective 1, we designed Analog CAM cells with programmable boundaries that shift adaptively to accommodate diverse output distributions, demonstrating a 15.1× improvement in energy efficiency compared to state-of-the-art designs. Objective 3: To apply the proposed scheme to target algorithms and explore the analog ECC specific issues. We have applied our error-handling and stochastic computing schemes to a wide range of algorithms, validating the dual nature of our proposal: minimizing errors for deterministic tasks and exploiting noise for probabilistic tasks. - Exploiting Stochasticity for Learning (One-Shot Learning): Addressing the "controlled stochasticity" aspect of our proposal, we applied our scheme to Memory-Augmented Neural Networks (MANNs). As published in Nature Communications (2022) ("Experimentally validated memristive memory augmented neural network..."), we did not suppress the intrinsic noise; instead, we exploited it for Locality-Sensitive Hashing (LSH). We experimentally validated that the device stochasticity could be used to implement efficient similarity searches for one-shot learning tasks on a fully integrated chip, proving that "noise" can be a computational feature. - Exploiting Stochasticity for Optimization (Quantum-Inspired Annealing): We further applied the concept to Combinatorial Optimization Problems (COPs). As published in Nature Communications (2023) ("Efficient combinatorial optimization by quantum-inspired parallel annealing..."), we developed a parallel annealing method that utilizes the analog conductance states and intrinsic noise of the crossbar to escape local minima. This method, validated on our integrated chip for Max-Cut and Traveling Salesman problems, demonstrated that the analog nature of the hardware is superior for solving complex optimization tasks compared to digital counterparts. - Correction for Deterministic Tasks (Genomics & RNNs): For tasks requiring high precision, we applied our ECC schemes to eliminate errors. In our work published in Nature Computational Science (2025) on genomic analysis, and our Nature Communications (2025) work on Recurrent Neural Networks, we implemented pre-distortion and error-correction loops to ensure that the analog hardware could process raw DNA signals and complex nonlinear functions with digital-like accuracy. Objective 4: To provide performance benchmarks compared to competitive approaches and publish the code, design, and findings to the public domain. This objective has been achieved through rigorous benchmarking against state-of-the-art digital (CPU/GPU/ASIC) and analog approaches, and the extensive dissemination of our findings. In every system we developed, we provided quantitative benchmarks. For instance, our genomic analysis system demonstrated a 51× speed-up and 477× energy saving over ASICs. Our optimization solver (Nature Comms 2023, IEDM 2024) demonstrated significant improvements in time- and energy-efficiency compared to previously reported Ising machines due to the elimination of iterative steps. Our adaptive ADC work demonstrated a 15.1× improvement in energy efficiency. The findings have been widely disseminated in the public domain through open-access publications in Nature Communications and their open-access code repositories (Nature Computational Science), as well as flagship conferences like IEEE IEDM. The codes for simulations, behavioral models (e.g., the crossbar model from Objective 1), and experimental data have been made available, fostering further innovation in the research community.

27210321.label: Major findings and research outcome
27210321.value: This project successfully established a comprehensive paradigm for reliable and efficient analog computing, evolving from simple error correction to "fault-free" and "stochastic" computing. We realized all four original objectives, resulting in a series of high-impact publications. First, addressing Reliability and Hardware-Software Co-design (Objectives 1 & 2), we moved beyond theoretical models to system-level validation. We initially characterized error statistics in large-scale crossbars, published in IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems II (Part C, Sec 8, No. 1). We advanced this by developing a memristor-based adaptive analog-to-digital converter (ADC). This interface dynamically adjusts quantization boundaries to device variability, achieving a 15.1× improvement in energy efficiency compared to state-of-the-art designs, a breakthrough published in Nature Communications (Part C, Sec 8, No. 9). Furthermore, we solved the challenge of implementing nonlinear functions in analog hardware, enabling Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) to operate efficiently, also published in Nature Communications (Part C, Sec 8, No. 5). Additionally, we theoretically proved that redundant analog coding could suppress circuit noise to negligible levels, a "Fault-Free" framework currently under revision at Nature Electronics. Second, we pioneered the concept of "Controlled Stochasticity" (Objective 3), turning intrinsic device noise from a defect into a computational asset: 1. Genomic Analysis: We developed a bio-inspired system processing raw signals directly from DNA sequencers. By exploiting device stochasticity for Locality-Sensitive Hashing (LSH), we achieved a 51× speed-up and **477× energy saving** over ASICs. This work was published in Nature Computational Science (Part C, Sec 8, No. 8) and featured in a News & Views article and by Croucher News. 2. Combinatorial Optimization: We integrated a quantum-inspired annealing module using analog noise to escape local minima. We fabricated a fully integrated chip solving NP-hard problems (e.g., Max-Cut) in a single step. These findings were published in Nature Communications and presented at the premier semiconductor conference, IEEE International Electron Devices Meeting (IEDM) (Part C, Sec 8, No. 3; Sec 9, No. 6). Finally, regarding material Innovation, we developed atomic-thin 2D MoS₂ flash memories with antimony contacts. These devices achieved record-breaking performance (36 ps latency), enabling ultra-fast in-memory search operations, accepted for publication in Nature Nanotechnology (Part C, Sec 8, No. 7). These outcomes have led to 6 patent applications covering the full stack from device structure to system architecture.

27210321.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27210321.value: The successful validation of our "One-Step" optimization solver and "Raw-Signal" genomic analyzer opens immediate commercialization pathways in Edge AI. We are actively seeking commercial opportunities (Part C, Sec 12) with our industry partners for integration into portable DNA sequencers and autonomous robotics, where energy source is a critical constraint. Technologically, the project’s success with 2D MoS₂ devices propels us toward 3D monolithic integration. We propose to stack memristor arrays directly over CMOS logic using Interlayer Vias (ILV) to further minimize data movement latency and increase density. Scientifically, we are extending the "stochastic computing" paradigm to Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) and Quantum Sensing. We have already begun combining neuromorphic vision sensors with diamond quantum sensors for high-precision magnetic field detection (Part C, Sec 8, No. 4). This interdisciplinary direction aims to create fully autonomous, bio-plausible cognitive systems that operate on milliwatt power budgets. To support this, we have secured follow-up funding, including the Croucher Innovation Award, CRF, and GRF, ensuring the continuous development of these promising technologies into practical, deployable systems.

27210321.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27210321.value: Modern AI and Big Data analysis require enormous computing power, but traditional digital chips are hitting physical limits. The core issue is the bottleneck caused by constantly moving data between separate memory and processing units. This project developed an analog, brain‑inspired chip using memristors, a nanoelectronic device that stores data and processes information in the same place, similar to how biological synapses work in the human brain. Unlike digital computers, which depend on perfect accuracy, our research shows that reliable, high‑speed computing is possible even when the hardware is imperfect. We designed error‑correcting codes for these chips, allowing them to operate accurately despite internal electrical noise. Rather than treating this noise as a drawback, we turned the intrinsic randomness of these devices into an advantage. We used this controlled noise to tackle complex optimization problems and to analyze DNA sequences for virus detection, reaching results much faster and with significantly lower energy use than current state‑of‑the‑art methods. We successfully built physical chips that demonstrate these capabilities in practice. This technology opens the door to green, sustainable AI, enabling ultra‑low‑power portable systems with guaranteed reliability.

27300221.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27300221.value: Sea-level rise poses one of the most immediate societal threats associated with present-day and future climate change, particularly on the densely populated coast of China. Assessments of the rates, mechanisms, and geographic variability of relative sea-level (RSL) change is an urgent priority for the next decade of ocean, climate, and hazards research. Changes in RSL are spatially variable in their impact to coastlines — improving the coverage and quality of RSL data can help to quantify local- to regional-scale processes that cause RSL to deviate from the global average and drive past, present, and future RSL changes on the China coast. In this project, we will 1) synthesize all existing geological sea-level data from the China coast from the past 20,000 years into a well-structured database; 2) produce new, high-quality RSL records in key spatial and temporal gaps, and 3) use the updated database to assess spatial and temporal variability of RSL and determine its driving mechanisms using geophysical and statistical models. Updated knowledge of local- to regional-scale drivers of RSL change on the coastline of China will be important to inform local projections. The proposed research will generate a useful dataset on the relative sea-level history of the China coast. Statistical modelling of the geologic sea-level data will provide an important baseline of past rates of change to place present-day sea-level rise into context, and furthermore will constrain the relative contribution of local- to regional-scale processes that modulate projections of global mean sea-level rise. These data will be of value for future research regarding coastal hazards and planning, including scientific and governmental research/policy implementation. 海平面上升與現在及未來的氣候變化息息相關。在人口稠密的中國沿海地區，海平面上升是當今最逼切的社會威脅之一。因此，評估過往相對海平面變化(RSL)的速率、機制和地理變異性是未來十年海洋、氣候和災害研究的逼切課題。然而，RSL 的變化對海岸線的影響存在地理上的差異—地方及區域作用會導致過往，現在及未來的RSL產生地理差異，並令RSL 偏離全球平均值。因此擴大及提高RSL 數據的覆蓋範圍和質量有助於量化地方及區域作用對RSL變化的影響。在此項目中，我們將 1) 設立一個嶄新的結構性數據庫以整合現存過去 20,000年的相對海平面數據； 2) 在缺乏RSL紀錄的地質歷史時期和區域提供高質的新RSL 記錄，以及 3) 使用最新的數據庫來評估RSL 的時空變化，並使用地球物理和統計模型推估其驅動機制。這些成果將提高我們對中國沿岸地方性及區域性 RSL 驅動因素的了解，對當地海平面預測非常重要。 上述擬定的研究將提供一個中國沿岸海平面相對歷史數據集。地質海平面數據的統計模型將為RSL過往的變化率提供重要基線，增進對當今海平面上升的了解，並限制地方及區域作用對預測的影響，使預測全球平均海平面上升更為精確。這些數據對未來有關沿海災害和規劃的研究極具價值，包括科學和政府研究以及政策實施。

27301821.label: Project Objectives
27301821.value: This project aims to develop a new and widely applicable desymmetric reduction reaction of malonic esters using silanes as the reductant. Transition metal catalysts with a chiral scaffold will be identified to activate silanes, deliver the metal-hydride selectively to one of the carbonyls of malonic esters, and generate chiral formyl- or hydroxymethyl-substituted monoesters. We aim to apply this desymmetrization reaction to the construction of all-carbon quaternary stereocenters with high efficiency and enantioselectivity. We plan to take advantage of the great diversity of substituents that can be introduced during the malonic ester synthesis and the chemoselective transformation of the reduction products to facilitate the modular synthesis of a myriad of quaternary stereocenters with distinct structural features. We aim to enable the desymmetric reduction of halogen-containing malonic esters to generate chiral tertiary halides, including fluorides, chlorides, and bromides. We also plan to employ the desymmetrization as a key step in the total synthesis of the halomon class of polyhalogenated monoterpenes that has showed promising differential cytotoxicity against tumor cell lines. We aim to extend the new desymmetric reduction method to oxygen- and nitrogen-substituted malonic esters and thus provide an expeditious route towards polyfunctionalized chiral building blocks that are valuable to biochemistry and medicinal chemistry, such as unnatural disubstituted amino esters, 1,2-diols, 1,2-amino alcohols, and chiral heterocycles.

27301821.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27301821.value: 本项目计划以硅烷为还原剂实现丙二酸酯的去对称化反应。我们希望以手性过渡金属催化剂来活化硅烷并选择性还原丙二酸酯中的一个酯基，生成带有醛基或者羟甲基的手性中心。考虑到丙二酸酯底物可以由多种方法简单且多样化得合成，且去对称化得到的手性产物带有多个可衍生化的官能团，该方法有望构建多类结构不同的手性季碳及叔碳中心。在研究期间，我们将首先探索环状和链状手性全碳季碳中心的构建，这类合成砌块能够提升所在分子的饱和度以及立体性，而这两种性质被证实能够提升药物分子的有效性。我们也将考察带有卤素取代的丙二酸酯，以此来生成手性三级卤代物，并尝试将该去对称化反应应用于含卤天然产物的合成之中。同时，氧代以及氮代的丙二酸酯也会被系统性的考察。这两类底物在去对称化反应中所得到的多官能团产物将为构建包括氨基酯，氨基醇以及手性杂环在内的各类手性砌块提供便利。

27301821.label: Realisation of objectives
27301821.value: All objectives listed in the propsal are all fully achieved. We have successfully devised the first reductive desymmetrization of malonic esters. This reaction breaks the monopoly of enzymatic hydrolysis in the asymmetric transformation of malonic esters. A class of unique, signature tetradentate ligand scaffolds composed of a phenol core, an achiral triarylmethanol side arm, and a chiral amino alcohol for enantioselective control have been developed (Objective 1). The ligand scaffold can accommodate two zinc atoms to generate dinuclear zinc catalysts. Owing to their spacious pockets, these new catalysts can accommodate disubstituted malonic esters, allowing for chelation of both carbonyls to stabilize the conformation and enable excellent asymmetric induction. With flexible structural modification of ligand, excellent control of reaction selectivity as well as a broad scope has been obtained. We were able to swing the product selectivity of the ester reduction from alcohol to aldehyde by using ligands derived from pipecolinols instead of prolinols. These six-membered new ligands allowed the desymmetric synthesis of not only all-carbon quaternary stereocenters (Objective 2), but also assorted tetra- and heteroatom-substituted carbons, including tertiary alkyl halides (Objective 3) and alcohols, as well as α-tertiary amines (Objective 4). Our methodology can harness the bulk production of malonic esters, their easy substitution reactions to introduce various motifs on the carbon, and diverse post-desymmetrization derivatization to synthesize bioactive, complex molecules. The success in preparing quaternary stereocenters enabled the rapid preparation of bioactive drugs and natural products, including hypnotic sedative glutethimide, and anti-oxidant/-aging bakuchiol. Heteroatom-substituted products from our desymmetrization are equally versatile. Particularly, we devised a short synthesis of 2-dechlorohalomon, a member of halomon terpene family that is one of the most extreme cases of differential cytotoxicity in NCI screen. Besides, those rich in nitrogen and oxygen are also accessible, including immunomodulator conagenin, vitamin E analog Trolox, and crispoic acid with anti-Zika activity. Up to now, by using the reductive desymmetrization, over 30 new synthetic routes towards bioactive structures have been accomplished. It is worth noting that the desymmetrization's high practicality has been widely noticed in the community and other labs have started to use the reaction to prepare complex molecules as well.

27301821.label: Major findings and research outcome
27301821.value: A novel class of dinuclear zinc catalysts with a tetradentate ligand scaffold have been identified to enable desymmetric hydrosilylation of disubstituted malonic esters to give enantioenriched tetrasubstituted stereocenters. The spacious pocket of the dinuclear catalyst can host disubstituted malonic esters via the chelation of both carbonyls to fix the conformation. By recognizing the relative sizes of the two substituents, one of the esters can be selectively reduced to primary alcohol or aldehyde. The reductive desymmetrization can be applied to halomalonic esters to generate enantioenriched tertiary alkyl halides. These chiral alkyl halides can serve as important and diverse building blocks to construct bioactive natural metabolites and drug candidates, including halomon-class monoterpenes, anti-Zika diacid, and fluorinated drugs. Oxygen- and nitrogen-substituted malonic esters were also found to be suitable substrates for the reductive elimination. As a result of the excellent functional group tolerance, highly functionalized and enantioenriched alpha-tertiary amines and tertiary alcohols can be generated. A wide range of oxygen- and nitrogen-containing bioactive compounds were also accessed from these desymmetrization products. Results obtained in this project have been widely recognized by peers, with multiple published manuscripts in top chemistry journals. Initial collaboration with industrial partners has started to use our signature dinuclear zinc catalysts and reductive desymmetrization to synthesize compounds of interests to drug identification and manufacturing. Our peers of academia have also started to use the reductive desymmetrization to build complex molecules.

27301821.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27301821.value: The high structural flexibility of our signature ligand scaffolds warrants further development. We envision that the ligands can house assorted metal centers to generate chiral catalysts of diverse usage. As such, we plan to first investigate asymmetric transformations of substrates apart from active methylene compounds. Potential research directions include asymmetric reduction of mono-carbonyl compounds, the generation of axially chiral compounds via desymmetrization, and asymmetric transformations other than reduction. We will also continue to use our reductive desymmetrization to construct structures of high complexity. It is envisioned that the continuous optimization of the ligand scaffolds will further improve the selectivity and reactivity of catalysts derived from them. Commercialization of these ligand scaffolds is also possible for wide application in both academia and industry.

27301821.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27301821.value: During the funding period, our laboratory has successfully enabled the reductive desymmetrization of malonic esters by using dinuclear zinc catalysts derived from chiral tetradentate ligands. The desymmetric reduction harnesses the bulk production of malonic esters, their easy substitution reactions to introduce various motifs on the carbon, and diverse post-desymmetrization derivatization to synthesize bioactive, complex molecules with an all-carbon quaternary stereocenter, including hypnotic sedative glutethimide, and anti-oxidant/-aging bakuchiol. Meanwhile, the compatibility of the method with halogen-substituted malonic esters allowed us to access important molecules with tertiary alkyl halide motifs, including fluorinated drug candidates and polyhalogenated monoterpenes with exceptional anti-cancer activity. Besides, those molecules rich in nitrogen and oxygen, including immunomodulator conagenin, vitamin E analog Trolox, and crispoic acid with anti-Zika activity, are also accessible via the desymmetrization.

27301921.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27301921.value: 在很多应用中，物理现象涉及高度非均质，带有很多（连续）变化的尺度并且可以取值多样的介质。流体在带有非常狭窄的裂缝和孔隙结构的介质的流动是一个很好的例子。在这个例子中由于裂缝和孔隙结构的传输能力比周围介质高许多数量级，因此它们是流体的主要管道。从而在应用传统数值方法进行模拟中我们需要精确刻画这些非常狭窄的裂缝和孔隙结构来得到比较合理的数值解， 这无疑涉及巨大的计算量。 此外，由于在实际应用中以高维物理参数或随机变量的形式出现的不确定性经常存在，我们需要多次应用同一数值求解器。此类问题的数值计算效果会随维度增加而呈指数恶化。在这些应用的推动下，非常需要在高维背景下进一步开发多尺度模型降阶算法。 处理此类多尺度高维问题的主要策略是寻找宏观信息并平均微观信息，然后通过一定的维数降阶方法将高维截断为低维或合理大小的维数。 然而，上述方法几乎没有严格的数值理论，也没有适用于每个实际应用的高效数值算法。因此，设计可以提供合理数值解并且对物理参数的大变化具有稳健性的多尺度模型降阶技术具有挑战性，并且是本项目的主要研究目标。 该研究计划的基本目标是为现有的高效模型降阶算法提供理论依据，以解决具有挑战性的多尺度问题，然后为多种具体应用设计和分析新的多尺度方法，包括多孔弹性、布林克曼流动和超材料。主要研究工具是逼近论、偏微分方程、数值分析和数值算法、泛函分析。理论分析将为多尺度模型降阶算法提供必要的数学基础，实际应用将为这些算法提供理想的测试平台，同时解决具有巨大潜在影响的具体应用中的不同挑战并刺激开发新算法。

27305221.label: Project Objectives
27305221.value: To create a novel Bayesian transfer learning framework using global-and-local shrinkage priors. In biomedical research, a tremendous amount of gene expression data has been generated. The number of samples from single tissue or cell type is generally small compared with the number of genes. Meanwhile, heterogenous related datasets from diverse sources are available. This motivates the development of transfer learning methodologies aiming to learn the target model through integrating knowledge from auxiliary datasets. Existing methods focus on improving prediction but ignore model inference. A Bayesian framework provides a natural way of incorporating empirical evidence into prior knowledge and enabling model uncertainty quantification. We aim at proposing a new Bayesian transfer learning framework, encompassing both statistical inference and prediction. The key is to construct the shrinkage priors for modeling both target and auxiliary data. By allowing the target and auxiliary model to have a common global shrinkage parameter and distinct local shrinkage parameter, knowledge will be transferred between two domains while the differences of two domains are retained. Theoretical properties in terms of convergence rate of posterior distributions of the proposed framework will be investigated based on theories of posterior consistency of GL priors. With the approval of access to the large-scale UK Biobank database and collaborations with local scientists who have access to Asian GWAS data, we propose to apply the method to polygenic risk prediction for non-European populations by integrating information from European genome-wide association studies. This will contribute to genetic architecture learning and disease risk prediction for non-European populations. To integrate external knowledge in sparse Bayesian network inference. Motivated by the complex structure of genomic data from diverse sources, we aim at integrating external knowledge from heterogenous related data sets and the known graph-structure information of covariates in sparse Bayesian network inference. The key is to formulate the prior and to propose procedures of transfer learning. The network structure of covariates is incorporated into model through constructing a graph-constrained prior. Knowledge from external related data is transferred through a two-step algorithm. In the first step, a sparse Bayesian network model is fitted on the merged data of the target and auxiliary one. In the second step, posterior means of parameters collected from the first-step are fine-tuned by fitting the sparse network model on target data only. The proposed model would be applied to breast cancer gene expression analysis, to identify target genes and make predictions for cancer status based on gene expression patterns using the publicly available The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) database. External knowledge can be learned from gene expression data of other cancer types in TCGA, and the gene-gene interaction network structure would be learned from the publicly available Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) pathway database. The proposed application will enhance the understanding of molecular biology for cancer diseases, in terms of identifying biomarkers for cancer classification and diagnosis. To develop Gaussian graphical model inference via global-and-local shrinkage priors. Motivated by the studies of biochemical interaction network analysis in genomic applications, we aim at developing Gaussian graphical model inference via global-and-local shrinkage priors which could integrate external publicly known biological network structures. We propose to apply our previously developed R-square-induced Dirichlet Decomposition (R2-D2) shrinkage prior, which was originally developed for linear models, to Gaussian graphical model inference. The superior properties of the R2-D2 prior in linear models, i.e., the prior’s marginal density has heavier tails and higher concentration rate compared with existing GL priors, ensure valid inference for the Gaussian graphical model. TCGA cancer gene expression data will be analyzed to make inferences for genetic networks associated with specific cancers, by incorporating the publicly available KEGG pathway database. This will provide new insights on gene interaction networks across multiple cancer diseases.

27305221.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27305221.value: In biomedical research, a tremendous amount of gene expression data has been generated. The number of samples from single tissue or cell type (in a few hundreds) is generally small compared with the number of genes (in tens of thousands). Classic high-dimensional methods suffer from low accuracy in terms of model estimation and prediction. Meanwhile, heterogenous related datasets from diverse sources are available, as well as a large body of biological network database. This motivates the development of transfer learning methodologies aiming to learn the target model through integrating knowledge from auxiliary datasets. However, most existing methods focus on improving prediction but neglect model inference. A Bayesian framework provides a natural way of incorporating empirical evidence into prior knowledge and enabling model uncertainty quantification. In this proposed project, we aim to create novel Bayesian strategies to integrate external knowledge, encompassing both statistical inference and prediction. First, we create a novel Bayesian transfer learning framework using global-and-local (GL) shrinkage priors. Through allowing two domains to have common global and distinct local shrinkage parameters, knowledge from auxiliary data will be transferred to train the target model. Statistical inferences can be attained based on posterior samples, enabling interpretable conclusions in biomedical research. Second, we establish a new method to integrate external knowledge in sparse Bayesian neural network inference. Transfer learning is realized through first fitting the merged target and auxiliary data, and then fine-tuning the first-step estimates by refitting the target model. Compared with existing algorithms, ours allows for feature selection and statistical inference, thus leading to more explicable results. Third, motivated by biochemical interaction network studies, we develop the Gaussian graphical model (GGM) inference via graphical GL shrinkage priors, with the possibility of integrating a known network structure of covariates. The prior’s marginal density has heavier tails and higher concentration rate compared with existing GL priors, allowing for superior performance in GGM inference. We propose to apply the three novel strategies respectively to the below settings: (1) calculating polygenic risk score associated with a disease for non-European populations by integrating information from European genome-wide association studies; (2) constructing a prediction model for breast cancer based on gene expression patterns, by transferring knowledge from other cancers in The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) and incorporating the Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) pathway database; and (3) undertaking cancer genetic network inference based on gene expression data in TCGA and the KEGG pathway database. 生物醫學研究產生了大量的基因表達數據，與基因數量（數万）相比，來自單一組織或細胞類型的樣本數量（數百個）通常很少。在此場景中，經典的高維統計方法在模型估計和預測方面的準確性較低。同時，有大量基因組學公開在線數據庫如不同來源的異構相關數據集和大量的生物網絡數據庫。這推動了遷移學習的發展，遷移學習旨在通過整合來自輔助數據集的知識來更好地學習目標模型。然而，大多數現有方法僅僅專注於改進預測結果而忽視了模型推斷。貝葉斯框架能夠將經驗知識納入先驗並量化模型的不確定性。在這個項目中，我們的目標是創建新的貝葉斯框架以整合外部知識，該框架可進行有效的統計推斷和預測。 首先，我們將使用全局-局部收縮先驗創建一個新的貝葉斯遷移學習框架。通過允許兩個域具有共同的全局和不同的局部收縮參數，將輔助數據的知識轉移至目標模型。根據後驗分佈獲得統計推斷，進而在生物醫學研究中得出合理的結論。 其次，我們將建立一種在稀疏貝葉斯網絡推斷中整合外部知識的新框架。該框架首先對合併後的目標和輔助數據進行擬合，然後對目標模型再次進行擬合微調，從而實現遷移學習。與現有算法相比，我們的算法可同時進行變量選擇和統計推斷，從而產生易於解釋的結果。 第三，在生化相互作用網絡研究的推動下，我們將基於全局-局部收縮先驗開發高斯圖形模型 (GGM) 推斷，並整合已知的協變量網絡結構。該先驗的邊際密度具有更厚的尾部和更高的集中分布，從而在 GGM 推理中具有更好的性能。 我們將在以下應用場景應用這三種新方法：（1）通過整合歐洲全基因組關聯研究的信息，計算與非歐洲人種疾病相關的多基因風險評分； (2) 通過從TCGA癌症基因组图谱中轉移其他癌症的知識，並結合京都基因與基因組百科全書 (KEGG)數據庫，構建基於基因表達模式的癌症預測模型； (3)基於TCGA和KEGG數據庫中的基因表達數據進行癌症遺傳網絡推斷。

27305221.label: Realisation of objectives
27305221.value: Introduction This project aimed to develop innovative statistical and computational methods for integrating external biological knowledge into high-dimensional data analysis, focusing on both inference and prediction. The overarching goals were to enhance gene discovery, biomarker identification, and disease understanding for complex conditions such as cancer and COVID-19. The work spanned Bayesian transfer learning, sparse Bayesian network inference, and Gaussian graphical models, achieving significant milestones in each area. Aim 1: Novel Bayesian Transfer Learning Framework Using Global-and-Local Shrinkage Priors Achievements: 1. h2-D2 for Bayesian Fine-Mapping (AJHG, 2024): o Developed a Bayesian framework leveraging global-and-local shrinkage priors for GWAS fine-mapping. o Outperformed state-of-the-art tools (e.g., SuSiE, FINEMAP) in identifying causal variants and estimating effect sizes. o Applied to prostate cancer GWAS data, uncovering 369 target genes and enriched pathways, providing biological insights. 2. TL-Multi for Polygenic Risk Scores (Frontiers in Genetics, 2022): o Designed a transfer learning method to improve PRS accuracy in non-European populations. o Enhanced predictions for systemic lupus erythematosus in Asians and asthma in Indians, demonstrating scalability in large-scale genetic studies. Underachievements and Solutions: • Direct integration of transfer learning into a Bayesian framework was deferred due to computational challenges. • Solution: Adopted a frequentist approach (TL-Multi) as an intermediate step, with future work focused on unifying Bayesian fine-mapping (h2-D2) and transfer learning. Aim 2: Integrating External Knowledge in Sparse Bayesian Network Inference Achievements: 1. COVID-19 Drug Repurposing (Heliyon, 2023): o Implemented a network-based strategy, identifying 51 candidate drugs targeting SARS-CoV-2-interacting proteins. o Highlighted lovastatin’s potential for mild COVID-19 and estradiol cypionate’s role in severe cases. 2. Grace-AKO for Variable Selection (BMC Bioinformatics, 2022): o Developed a graph-constrained method integrating biological pathway information. o Applied to prostate cancer data, identifying 47 candidate genes with over 75% validation. Underachievements and Solutions: • Initial efforts focused on incorporating network structure into a frequentist variable selection framework. The next step will involve developing a Bayesian version, though the application goal has already been achieved. • Solution: Future work will focus on creating a Bayesian framework for integrating external knowledge and network structure. Aim 3: Gaussian Graphical Model Inference via Global-and-Local Shrinkage Priors Achievements: 1. GR2D2 (Briefings in Bioinformatics, 2022): o Extended the R2-D2 prior to Gaussian graphical models for high-dimensional, sparse precision matrix estimation. o Demonstrated superior performance in simulations and applied to TCGA cancer data, revealing key pathways and gene interactions. Underachievements and Solutions: • No significant underachievements; the aim was fully completed. Conclusion The project successfully delivered innovative methods for Bayesian transfer learning, sparse Bayesian network inference, and Gaussian graphical models, with significant applications in cancer genomics, COVID-19 drug repurposing, and genetic risk prediction. While computational challenges deferred some goals, foundational work has been completed, and future efforts will focus on integrating these methods into a unified Bayesian framework. This work positions us well for advancing precision medicine and cancer biology.

27305221.label: Major findings and research outcome
27305221.value: This project achieved significant milestones in developing innovative statistical and computational methods for integrating external biological knowledge into high-dimensional genomic data analysis. Key findings include: 1. Bayesian Fine-Mapping with Global-and-Local Shrinkage Priors (h2-D2): Published in AJHG (2024), h2-D2 is a novel Bayesian framework for GWAS fine-mapping. It outperformed state-of-the-art tools (e.g., SuSiE, FINEMAP) in identifying causal variants and estimating effect sizes. Applied to prostate cancer GWAS data, h2-D2 uncovered 369 target genes and over-represented pathways, providing new insights into prostate cancer biology. 2. Frequentist Transfer Learning for Polygenic Risk Scores (TL-Multi): Published in Frontiers in Genetics (2022), TL-Multi improves PRS accuracy in non-European populations by leveraging European GWAS data. It demonstrated superior performance in predicting SLE risk in Asian populations and asthma risk in Indian populations, addressing challenges in underrepresented groups. 3. Bayesian Network Estimation with GR2D2: Published in Briefings in Bioinformatics (2022), GR2D2 extends the R2-D2 prior to Gaussian graphical models for high-dimensional, sparse precision matrix estimation. It outperformed existing methods in simulations and identified shared and cancer-specific pathways in RNA-seq data, enhancing cancer biology understanding. 4. COVID-19 Drug Repurposing Using Network-Based Strategies: Published in Heliyon (2023), we identified 51 candidate drugs targeting SARS-CoV-2-interacting proteins. Key findings included lovastatin’s potential for mild COVID-19 and estradiol cypionate’s role in severe cases, offering mechanistic insights into therapeutic strategies. 5. Graph-Constrained Variable Selection with Grace-AKO: Published in BMC Bioinformatics (2022), Grace-AKO integrates biological pathway information into variable selection, controlling finite-sample FDR. Applied to prostate cancer data, it identified 47 candidate genes with over 75% validation, highlighting the utility of external knowledge in gene discovery. 6. Integration of External Knowledge into Bayesian Models: GR2D2 and Grace-AKO provide a foundation for incorporating external biological knowledge (e.g., KEGG pathways) into Bayesian models. These tools have demonstrated significant impact in cancer genomics and COVID-19 drug repurposing, paving the way for future research in sparse Bayesian neural networks and personalized medicine. Moreover, we have made the open-source software for h2-D2, GR2D2, Grace-AKO, and TL-Multi publicly available. In summary, this project delivered innovative methods advancing Bayesian inference, transfer learning, and network-based analysis, providing valuable insights into disease mechanisms and therapeutic strategies. For detailed methodologies and applications, refer to Part C.

27305221.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27305221.value: This project has established a robust foundation for advancing the integration of external biological knowledge into high-dimensional genomic data analysis. Key areas for further development include: 1. Unified Bayesian Transfer Learning Framework: o Develop a unified Bayesian framework combining h2-D2 and TL-Multi to improve causal variant identification and polygenic risk score (PRS) accuracy across diverse populations. o Address computational scalability for large-scale genetic studies. 2. Sparse Bayesian Neural Networks: o Extend GR2D2 and Grace-AKO to sparse Bayesian neural networks for integrating complex biological networks and multi-omics data. o Explore applications in personalized medicine and biomarker discovery. 3. Integration of Multi-Omics Data: o Develop Bayesian methods to integrate genomic, transcriptomic, and proteomic data. o Enhance understanding of disease mechanisms and therapeutic targets. 4. Community Engagement: o Collaborate with the research community to refine and expand applications of developed tools. The proposed course of action includes securing funding, fostering interdisciplinary collaborations, and engaging in translational research to bridge computational advancements with clinical applications. These efforts will advance precision medicine and deepen the understanding of complex diseases.

27305221.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27305221.value: This research project focuses on developing advanced computational tools to better understand the genetic factors behind diseases like cancer and COVID-19. By combining statistical methods with biological knowledge, we created innovative software that helps identify key genes, predict disease risks, and discover potential treatments. For example, our tools have uncovered new insights into prostate cancer and identified drugs that could be repurposed for COVID-19. One of our key achievements is improving genetic risk prediction for underrepresented populations, such as Asians and Indians, by leveraging data from European studies. We also developed methods to analyze complex biological networks, which have enhanced our understanding of cancer pathways and disease mechanisms. All our tools are open-source, meaning they are freely available to researchers worldwide, fostering collaboration and accelerating discoveries. This work not only advances scientific knowledge but also has real-world applications, such as personalized medicine and faster drug development. Overall, this project bridges the gap between data science and biology, providing valuable tools and insights that can lead to better health outcomes for people around the globe.

27500221.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27500221.value: The boundaries of firms and the choice between organizing transactions within a firm and by outsourcing is a central question in modern economics (Coase, 1937). Economic theory has long highlighted that information transmission is at the heart of organizational design. However, empirical evidence on the role of organizational structure in shaping firms’ disclosure policy and information environment is limited. This study will examine how the scope of firm boundaries, and in particular the degree of vertical integration, affects the quality of firms’ voluntary disclosures. On the one hand, vertical integration facilitates intra-firm exchange of supply chain information, which is an important input of high-quality management forecasts. On the other hand, information exchange within integrated firms might crowd out public disclosure, as it reduces the needs of conveying accurate public information to collaborate with otherwise independent supply chain partners. I plan to study this question using two distinct approaches. The first approach aims to provide large sample evidence by associating a firm’ vertical integration and its disclosure quality. I will gather information about the degree of a U.S. firm’s vertical integration based on its annual reports, which reflects the vertical relatedness of a firm’s different products. I will investigate the relationship between this vertical integration measure and disclosure quality, proxied by the accuracy of managers’ earnings and sales forecasts. To establish causality, as the second approach, I will develop an identification strategy building on the transaction cost theory, which suggests that weak contract enforcement fosters vertical integration. I will exploit reforms of judicial systems that facilitate contract enforcement and reduce the needs of vertical integration. My identification strategy will explore variations in U.S. firms’ exposure to judicial systems reforms in non-U.S. countries from which firms procure inputs. Preliminary analyses verify this identification strategy – firms rest more on outsourcing than vertical integration when they have greater exposures. Based on this strategy, I will adopt a difference-in-differences approach to identify the casual impact of vertical integration on disclosure quality. Finally, I will study the cross-sectional variations in supply chain characteristics to illuminate the economic mechanisms. I will examine the importance of supply chain information to management forecast, the role of financial information in the process of supply chain collaboration, and the efficiency of public communication between independent partners. 企业的边界如何决定以及企业在内部交易和外包之间如何进行选择是现代经济学的重要命题（Coase, 1937）。经济学理论认为信息交换在企业边界决定过程中发挥了核心作用。然而，目前鲜有实证文献讨论企业边界如何影响公司的信息披露政策。本文旨在研究企业边界，即企业的纵向一体化程度如何影响企业的自愿信息披露质量。 一方面，纵向一体化使得供应链信息能够直接在企业内部进行交换，因而提高了信息沟通效率。由于供应链信息是企业高质量信息披露的重要组成部分，纵向一体化有助于提高企业的信息披露质量。另一方面，对于非一体化公司而言，企业和上下游供应商的沟通和合作一定程度上依赖于高质量的外部信息披露。然而，纵向一体化的公司将该信息沟通内部化，进而降低企业提供高质量自愿信息披露的动机。 本文计划采用两种实证手段来研究该问题。其一，本文将在一个大样本数据中检验企业纵向一体化程度与信息披露质量的相关性。该数据涵盖了美国所有上市公司，并提供了一个可靠指标用于衡量企业历年的纵向一体化程度。具体而言，该指标通过企业年报中关于其产品和服务的描述，构建了一个指数来反映其不同产品和服务之间的纵向相关性。此外，信息披露质量将由企业自愿披露的盈利和销售预测的准确性加以衡量。 其二，本文将利用一个外生事件冲击来识别上述关系的因果性。交易成本理论认为，在契约约束和执行不力的条件下，企业更倾向于选择纵向一体化。基于该理论，当司法系统的改良强化了契约的约束力时，企业会减少对纵向一体化的需求。本文利用不同国家的司法系统改革时点的差异，以及每家上市公司对不同国家提供的上游产品和服务的依赖程度存在差异这一事实，构建了每家公司在不同时点对全球司法系统改革的敞口。初步分析表明，当敞口提高时，企业降低纵向一体化并提高对外包的依赖程度——该结果验证了此识别策略的有效性。我将利用该策略来识别企业纵向一体化与信息披露质量的因果关系。 最后，本文将研究供应链特征如何影响企业一体化与信息披露质量的关系。该分析能够加深我们对两者关系背后的作用机制的理解。潜在的可用于分析的供应链特征包括：供应链信息在盈利和销售预测中的重要性、财务信息披露在上下游企业或部门合作过程中的重要性、上下游企业利用外部信息进行沟通的频率和效率。

Using two measures of product disclosures—based on textual analysis of annual reports and press releases—for a sample of 62,202 firm-year observations from 1997 through 2017, we find that, holding constant the number of supply chain partners, vertical integration is negatively correlated with both product disclosure measures. 2. We rely on the incidence of major natural disasters that disrupt firms’ production (e.g., Barrot and Sauvagnat, 2016). We find that following a major natural disaster, firms are (1) more likely to contract with new suppliers and (2) more likely to voluntarily disclose product-related information using our two measures of product disclosure in annual reports and press releases. 3. 27502521.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27502521.value: Mobile app is a fast expanding, highly dynamic and fiercely competitive industry composing of 3.3 billion smartphone users, 8.9 million apps and more than 500 billion US dollars revenue (Clement, 2019; Blair, 2020; Sharma, 2020). The fast changing and highly competitive industry make it challenging for app firms, investors, and policy makers to have a clear picture of the market structure of this industry. It also poses challenges to the marketers to identify competitors and position new products. This project aims to refines estimates of market competition through innovative machine learning on large-scale usage data. The project makes use of detailed cross-apps usage data from about one million smartphone users and it aims to achieve four objectives: (1) investigate and redefine the market structure of the mobile app industry with insights from cross-category and within-category usage information; (2) better identify an app’s competitors and develop the App Competitiveness Index; (3) predict future success of apps based on the revised market structure and the App Competitiveness Index; and (4) explore the market structure’s changes over time. This research leverages a new machine learning approach, the SHOPPER model (Ruiz et al., 2020) to study the latent attributes of more than 220,000 Android mobile apps. This new approach can effectively explore the complementarity and substitutability between apps. The preliminary results indicate that current approach of using pre-determined category and observed app functions is insufficient to capture real apps competitions. Apps from the same app category may be different in latent attributes and may not compete against each other. The findings of the research are expected to make the following contributions. Theoretically, it leads to a more accurate market landscape of the entire mobile app industry. Methodologically, it introduces a new machine-learning approach to study this salient and timely topic. Managerially, the study provides insightful implications for key stakeholders of the mobile app industry. For app firm managers, it sheds light on app portfolio management and new app development strategy. For investors, it provides a useful tool to assess potential ROI (return on investment) among mobile app firms. For policy makers, the study findings help draw policies that enhance healthy growth and effective regulation of the industry. HKSAR Government is committed to promote the advancement of its innovation and technology industries, so the findings and its pioneering methodology may shed lights on this hi-tech industry and facilitate its growth. 移動應用 (Mobile App) 市場正在經歷一個快速變化、競爭激烈的高速發展期。截至2019年，全球的移動應用市場已經發展為一個可為33億用戶，提供超過89億個各類應用的巨大市場，其市場體量每年超過5000億美元。如此快速發展和激烈競爭的市場，令移動應用產業中的各方（包括應用開發公司、投資者、管理部門及政策製定者），很難清晰地從全局視角認識市場結構，同時對於應用開發公司的競品研究及新產品開發，提出了巨大的挑戰。該研究希望通過應用建立在大數據基礎上的，前沿機器學習模型 （SHOPPER 模型），來重新審視移動應用市場上應用產品之間的競爭關系。現有的關於各應用之間競爭關系，及市場結構的認知，主要基於預先設定的產品品類基礎之上（如遊戲、社交、理財、出行）。該研究希望通過基於對計劃收集的100萬用戶在其移動設備上的，超過22萬個移動應用的使用行為數據的深度分析，實現四個研究目標： （1）基於用戶的同品類以及跨品類的應用使用行為，研究及重新定義應用場中的產品競爭關系及市場結構； （2）基於用戶的同品類以及跨品類的應用使用行為，更準確地定位競品。同時提出應用產品的競爭力指數，用以更好地描述每個應用產品在市場上的競爭力表現； （3）利用每個應用的產品競爭力指數，以及重新定義的市場結構來預測應用產品的未來表現； （4）探究市場結構隨時間的動態變化； 初步的研究結果已經表明，依據現行的、基於預先設定的產品品類的視角，並不足以描述應用之間實際的競爭關系。此項研究預期在多個方面產生研究價值和貢獻。在理論價值上，該研究發現將會為移動應用產業提供更具體的解讀，拓寬原有的關於市場結構的洞察視角。在研究方法上，該研究引入了一種前沿的機器學習模型，來研究這個同時具有現實價值及深遠意義的問題。在實踐價值上，該研究會為移動應用產業中的多方參與者，提供實踐上的參考。於應用開發公司的管理者，該研究可以更好地為產品矩陣管理，以及新產品研發，提供具體且有實際意義的參考；對於移動應用行業的投資者，該研究可以提供一個有效的工具，來衡量和評價各個應用產品的潛在價值。為投資者的投資決策提供參考依據；同時，該研究可以更好地為移動應用產業的管理者和政策製定者，提供更加清晰的依據，從而可以製定更有效且有針對性的政策，進一步確保移動應用行業健康、可持續發展。香港政府一直致力於推廣創新科技促進經濟和社會發展，該項研究研究的成果及先進的技術，可以進一步助力香港科技產業的發展。

27502521.label: Realisation of objectives
27502521.value: Objective 1: To redefine the market structure of the mobile app industry using real usage data from both within- and across-category app usage. This objective was successfully achieved. Drawing on app usage data from approximately one million Android users spanning over 174,000 apps across 20 categories, we applied the SHOPPER model—a hierarchical latent variable model grounded in consumer choice behavior—to uncover latent relationships between apps based on actual co-usage. This allowed us to construct a behavior-based market structure that reflects how consumers perceive app functionality and competition, rather than relying on predefined app store categories. This structure offers a more nuanced and dynamic view of app competition that better aligns with user behavior. Objective 2: To identify app competitors and develop a behavior-based App Competitiveness Index (ACI). This objective was also successfully achieved. By estimating pairwise complementarity and substitution patterns across thousands of apps, we constructed the App Competitiveness Index (ACI), which quantifies an app’s exposure to both direct and indirect competition. Unlike traditional app store rankings or download metrics, the ACI captures underlying demand-side substitution, offering a more behaviorally grounded measure of competitive pressure. This index provides a practical tool for developers and investors to evaluate strategic positioning, anticipate threats, and uncover partnership opportunities. Objective 3: To predict the potential success of apps based on market structure and ACI. This objective was successfully achieved. We demonstrated that both latent structure information and ACI scores are strong predictors of an app’s future performance. Regression analysis using structure-based variables explained substantial variation in key outcomes such as weekly downloads and two-year app survival status. For example, understanding that App A is often substituted by App C, while complementing App B, offers valuable insights for optimizing marketing, pricing, and bundling strategies. This predictive power validates the utility of our model in strategic planning. Objective 4: To explore the market structure's changes over time. This objective was successfully achieved. We developed an interactive web-based visualization tool that enables users to explore the app market structure across time periods, revealing evolving complementarities, substitution patterns, and competitive clusters. This dynamic interface translates complex behavioral data into intuitive visualizations that can inform strategic decisions. App developers can monitor shifts in their competitive positioning and identify emerging rivals or potential collaborators. Platform operators may use the tool to refine recommendation algorithms or category structures. Investors and analysts can assess market dynamics and app trajectories. Finally, policymakers and researchers can explore patterns of ecosystem concentration or dominance. By making high-dimensional data interpretable and accessible, this tool strengthens adaptive decision-making across the digital app ecosystem.

27502521.label: Major findings and research outcome
27502521.value: This proejct provides a novel framework for understanding the competitive structure of the mobile app industry by analyzing actual consumer usage behavior. Leveraging a large-scale dataset of over 980,000 Android users and more than 170,000 apps, we applied a consumer behavior–based hierarchical latent variable model to uncover the underlying relationships between apps. 1. Traditional app categories do not reflect actual consumer behavior First, we find that the traditional app categories used in app stores do not accurately reflect how consumers engage with apps. Apps that belong to different store-defined categories are often used together, while those within the same category may not exhibit strong usage similarity. This reveals the need to redefine app market structure from the perspective of consumer behavior rather than platform-defined taxonomy. 2. Apps exhibit rich complementarity and substitution patterns Second, we uncover pairwise complementarity and substitution patterns among apps. These behavioral relationships are visualized through interactive network graphs, revealing clusters centered around “anchor” apps (e.g., social media), and providing a user-centric map of the app ecosystem. 3. We introduce the App Competitiveness Index Third, we develop the App Competitiveness Index (ACI) to quantify each app’s exposure to competitive and collaborative pressures. This index is predictive of both short-term performance (downloads) and long-term survival, providing a reliable metric for strategic planning. 4. The structure-based model strongly predicts app success Fourth, we demonstrate the predictive power of our structure-based model. Even without using traditional firm-level features like pricing or marketing spend, our model explains up to 79% of the variation in weekly downloads and up to 17% of the variation in two-year app survival. 5. We built a stakeholder-facing interactive visualization tool. Finally, to enhance accessibility and impact we built an interactive visualization tool that allows users to explore the app network and monitor how relationships evolve over time. This tool makes our results accessible to app developers, investors, platform managers, and policymakers. Overall, this project is one of the first large-scale, empirical efforts to recover the digital product market structure using real consumer behavior. It provides not only theoretical insights into how apps compete and co-exist, but also practical tools and indicators that can inform business decisions in the digital economy.

27502521.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27502521.value: This research opens several promising directions for further development. First, while our model captures latent complementarity and substitution patterns between apps, these relationships are likely to evolve over time, especially in response to industry shocks such as mergers, platform policy changes, or major app launches. Future research can extend our framework to study the dynamic evolution of these inter-app relationships and how they reshape the app market structure. Second, our findings reveal that apps often compete across traditional category boundaries. Future research can further investigate the formation mechanisms and development paths of such cross-category competitive or complementary relationships. Understanding these patterns will be highly valuable for app developers in product positioning and for app stores in refining recommendation and categorization systems. Third, future research enhance the interactive visualization tool developed in this project by incorporating real-time data and predictive capabilities, allowing stakeholders to monitor and act on market changes as they occur.

27502521.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27502521.value: Mobile apps are a big part of our daily lives, but understanding how they truly compete with or support each other is still a challenge. In this project, we analyzed real usage data from nearly one million Android users to explore how people actually use apps together. Rather than relying on traditional app categories, we used a machine learning model to identify hidden patterns in user behavior— such as which apps are used side by side, which apps replace each other, and how these relationships form a larger ecosystem. We also built an interactive online tool that helps people visualize how apps are connected and how the app market changes over time. These insights are not just academic—they have strong practical value. App developers can use our findings to better target competitors, design app bundles, and allocate advertising budgets. App stores can recommend apps more effectively by understanding usage-based relationships. Investors gain a smarter way to spot high-potential apps early, and policymakers can make more informed decisions about regulating fast-growing digital markets. Overall, our approach offers a new, behavior-driven lens for navigating the complex app economy—one that moves beyond labels and gets closer to how people actually use technology.

27503321.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27503321.value: Inflation risk is one of the most important macroeconomics risks, and currencies are intrinsically related to inflation. Understanding the magnitude of currency risk premium in currencies is of great important for the FX market participants, including global investors, multinational corporation managers, and governments. In this study, I estimate an affine-linear no-arbitrage model at the pairwise and portfolio level to quantify the magnitude of inflation risk premium in the total currency risk premia observed in the data. Particularly, I focus on the core inflation risk premium motivated by an earlier finding in Fang, Liu, and Roussanov (2020) that core inflation carries a negative risk premium in multiple asset classes. In the model, I allow for time-invariant heterogeneity and time-varying price of risks driven by state variables in different countries. The choice of risk premium drivers and other risks that are priced in the currency market are chosen following the literature. With the model parameters estimated, I can compute the risk premia associated with all priced risks in the model and assess their relative importance. The estimation links inflation risk premium to popular currency strategies such as carry trade, dollar carry, and other sorts. I also estimate the model using pairwise data for the major G-10 countries using the short-term interest rate, exchange rate, as well as long-term bond data. The pairwise estimation is used as a cross-validation of my estimation of the model. Moreover, I estimate the model for subsamples of emerging market currencies to examine the potentially distinct role of inflation risk premium in these countries with relatively high and volatile inflation. 通胀风险是最重要的宏观经济风险之一，而外汇汇率内在地与通货膨胀相关。对外汇市场参与者，包括全球投资者，跨国公司经理人和政府来说，理解外汇风险的来源和大小都极其重要。 在这项研究中，我估计了一个关于外汇的线性无套利模型，以量化在观测到外汇风险溢价中通胀风险溢价的大小。特别地，我关于核心通胀的风险溢价。在早前的研究中，Fang, Liu, and Roussanov (2020)在多个资产类别胀发现核心通胀的风险溢价而负。在我的模型中，我允许货币之间有不随时间变化的异质性以及随时间变化的风险价格。这些风险价格由不同国家的状态变量所驱动。状态变量的选择是依据现有的文献进行的。在估计了模型的参数后，我可以在模型中计算出所有来源风险各自的风险溢价，以及评估它们的相对重要性。 这项估计将通胀风险溢价和流行的外汇交易策略联系起来，例如利差交易，美元利差交易，以及其他策略。我也使用G-10主要货币的短期利率，汇率和长期债券数据来估计这个模型。我对发展中国家的货币做了分样本估计，以研究通胀风险这些高通胀且通胀波动性大的国家中可能具有的独特作用。

27503321.value: 5.1 In the research output, we specify an affine-linear no-arbitrage model. We solve for interest rate, exchange rate and currency risk premia both at the individual currency and portfolio level. We analytically characterise the relation between the unobserved factors and risk loadings in the model and the observed data. We fully achieve the first object of the research project. 5.2 Through a calibrated version of the model, we rely on currency factors' exposures to inflation risks to infer the correlation between inflation and the underlying risk factors driving currency returns. We define two notions of inflation risk premia and compute them in the model. We find that the inflation risk premia is much larger than the previous literature suggests. Their main source is from the real risks that are correlated with core and energy inflation. 5.3 We tried to collect the data on G10 long-term bonds and attempted to estimate a joint model of bonds and currencies. However, we encounter the obstacle that G10 long-term bonds and currencies seem not to be spanned by the same set of risk factors, so it is difficult to specify and estimate a joint model. Although we are not able to fully achieve this research objective, we did outline the stylized relations among other countries' long-term bonds, as well as their relations with exchange rates. 5.4 We estimate the subsample of advanced economies (AE) and emerging markets (EM) separately. The results for AE is qualitatively similar to the full-sample results. Data availability for EM currencies is limited and the results for EM currencies are very noisy and it's hard to make inference purely based on the limited data.

27503321.label: Major findings and research outcome
27503321.value: This paper studies the inflation risk and risk premia in the currency market. Decomposing inflation into core and noncore components, we develop an affine-linear term structure model of currencies that can explain the well-established dollar and carry factor premium. We estimate the risk exposure of different currency portfolios to the core and noncore inflation risks and determine the correlation between inflation risk with the global risk factors that drive currency fluctuations. Our model suggests that core inflation has a sizable correlation with the two global factors, which gives rise to a significant inflation risk premium that is largely ignored in the previous literature. We further show that using headline inflation alone would obscure the inflation risk premium in the currency market.

27503321.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27503321.value: This research's methodology can be extended to studying other macroeconomic sources in the bond and currency markets, providing a more complete picture of macro risk pricing in the international bond and FX market. This will be a more impactful research to be conducted in the future.

27503321.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27503321.value: We study the relation between exchange rates and inflation to enhance our understanding of macroeconomic risks in the currency market. We find that popular currency strategies of carry (buy high interest rate, sell low interest rate) and dollar (buy high dollar beta, sell low dollar beta when US interest rate is low, and reverse buy and sell otherwise) are significantly exposed to core and energy inflation risks. These exposures explain a significant fraction of risk premia of these strategies. We highlight that it is important distinguish core and energy inflation to uncover the sizeable inflation risk premia.
