27504221.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27504221.value: The rise of matching platforms such as Uber, Airbnb, Upwork, and Tinder has changed the way we commute, travel, work, and date. Central to the success of these platforms is the role of information: what information to provide and how much to provide. Both conventional wisdom and extensive prior literature suggest that more information leads to a better outcome. Information helps to resolve uncertainties, provide signals, and assist learning. Recent literature on information provision strategy, information design, and optimal information disclosure already identify circumstances where more information may be counterproductive. In this project, we study the role of information on matching platforms, emphasizing how the amount of information about the other side influences the matching outcomes. Using data on user search and matching histories from an online dating site, we find empirical evidence that is contrary to conventional wisdom: more information about the other side may make matching outcomes worse. This effect is mainly driven by the misaligned preferences (i.e., preference mismatch) between the two sides. Our preliminary findings suggest that there exists an optimal amount of information that the platform should provide to each side before a match is proposed. The project will be carried out in three phases. In Phase I, we will leverage the existing data to provide more evidence on consumer behaviors and test out alternative explanations. In Phase II, a consumer theory model will be developed to rationalize the behavior. A model is needed to identify conditions and boundaries of optimal information provision under preference mismatch on matching platforms. In Phase III, we will collaborate with the platform to conduct field experiments by varying the amount of information shown to the users. This approach will enable us to quantify the impact of information on user behaviors, matching outcomes, and platform revenue. The proposed project contributes to the literature on information economics and platform design in general and to matching platforms in particular, and is especially relevant for platforms such as dating websites where the preferences of the two sides may not be aligned. This knowledge will help matching platforms increase matching rates and generate more revenue. The users on the platform also will benefit by having better matching outcomes. Additionally, our research also sheds light on platform design in non-commercial settings where preference mismatch may exist, like school choice, student-teacher, and government job matching platforms. Uber、Airbnb、Upwork和Tinder等匹配平台的崛起，改變了我們通勤、旅行、工作和約會的方式。這些平台成功的核心是信息的作用：提供什麼信息以及提供多少信息。傳統智慧和大量的前期文獻都表明，更多的信息會帶來更好的結果。信息有助於解決不確定性，提供信號，並幫助學習。最近關於信息提供策略、信息設計和最优化信息披露的研究表明，在很多情况下更多信息可能产生適得其反的情況。在這個研究課題中，我們研究信息在匹配平台上的作用，強調对另一方信息了解的多少如何影響匹配結果。利用一個在線約會網站的用戶搜索和匹配歷史數據，我們从数据中發現了與傳統智慧相反的结论：了解對方更多的信息可能會使匹配結果變得更糟。這種影響主要是由雙方之間不一致的偏好（即偏好错配）驅動的。我們的初步研究結果表明，当一方提出匹配请求的时候，存在一個最佳的信息量平台应该提供给请求方。該研究課題將分三個階段進行。在第一階段，我們將利用現有數據提供更多關於消費者行為的證據並測試替代解釋。在第二階段，我們將建立一個消費者理論模型來合理化行為。該模型有助于識別匹配平台上偏好错配下最優信息提供的條件和邊界。在第三階段，我們將與平台合作，通過改變向用戶顯示的信息量來進行實地實驗。這種方法將使我們能夠量化信息對用戶行為、匹配結果和平台收入的影響。擬議的研究課題主要会贡献信息經濟學和平台設計的文獻，特別是这些文献里和匹配平台相关的。这个研究课题还對約會網站等雙方偏好可能不一致的平台具有重要意義。這些知識將幫助匹配平台提高匹配率，創造更多的收入。平台上的用戶也會因為有更好的匹配結果而受益。此外，我們的研究也為可能存在偏好错配的非商業環境中的平台設計提供了啟示，比如學校選擇、學生和教師匹配以及政府工作等匹配平台。

27504221.label: Realisation of objectives
27504221.value: Realisation of Research Objectives Objective 1: Empirically Examine the Role of Information Provided by a Matching Platform on the Final Matching Outcomes (a) Demonstrate the existence of preference mismatch between the two sides Achievement: The research provides robust empirical evidence of preference mismatch in two-sided online dating markets. Using a rich dataset from a large Chinese online dating platform, the authors construct attractiveness scores for candidates based on estimated mate preferences. The study demonstrates that, in practice, the preferences of the two sides (e.g., male and female users) are often misaligned. This is shown both at the overall attractiveness level and at the attribute level (e.g., height, age, income, education). For instance, the paper finds that men and women have systematically different ideal preferences for height difference, and that candidates who reply to proposals are usually not the focal users’ original top choices. These findings empirically confirm the presence and significance of preference mismatch. (b) Explore the interaction effect between preference mismatch and the amount of information provided by the platform on the final matching outcomes Achievement: The paper rigorously investigates how varying the amount of information available to users (i.e., partial information via short profiles vs. complete information via long profiles) influences the matching process and outcomes in the presence of preference mismatch. The authors find that providing more information does not necessarily increase the likelihood of a successful match. Instead, they uncover a “less information is more” effect: users achieve better matching outcomes when they make decisions based on partial information. The study further shows that more information exacerbates the degree of preference mismatch, leading users to select “best” candidates who are less likely to reciprocate, while potentially ruling out the “right” matches who would have resulted in successful pairings. Conclusion for Objective 1: This objective has been fully achieved. The paper provides comprehensive empirical analyses that not only demonstrate the existence of preference mismatch but also clarify how the amount of information provided interacts with this mismatch to shape matching outcomes. Objective 2: Provide a Theoretical Framework to Rationalize the Behavioral Pattern Observed in the Data (a) Build a stylized model to understand the role of preference mismatch on two-sided platforms Achievement: The research is supplemented with a stylized analytical model (presented in the online appendix) that formalizes the concept of preference mismatch in two-sided matching markets. The model illustrates how differences in ideal preferences between the two sides generate regions where preference mismatch occurs, and how this affects the probability of a successful match. (b) Understand how the amount of information provided to each side impacts the matching outcomes Achievement: The theoretical model is used to rationalize the empirical findings, showing that as more attributes are revealed (i.e., more information is provided), the likelihood of preference mismatch increases. The model predicts and explains why partial information can lead to better matching outcomes in the presence of mismatched preferences, thus providing a theoretical foundation for the observed “less information is more” effect. Conclusion for Objective 2: This objective has been fully achieved. The paper successfully builds and applies a theoretical model that explains the empirically observed behavioral patterns, thus bridging theory and data. Objective 3: Make Managerial Recommendations Regarding the Information Design of Matching Platforms Achievement: Based on empirical and theoretical findings, the paper delivers clear managerial implications for online matching platforms. It recommends that platforms should not always strive to provide maximal information to users. Instead, platforms should consider limiting the amount of initial information shown to users, especially where preference mismatch is likely, to maximize the probability of successful matches. The paper further suggests that attributes associated with little or no preference mismatch should be prioritized in profile design, and that platforms should assess mismatch costs when designing information disclosure policies. The findings are extended to other two-sided markets (e.g., Airbnb, Upwork), with caveats regarding platform structure, communication cost, and bargaining power. Conclusion for Objective 3: This objective has been achieved. The research provides actionable recommendations and discusses boundary conditions for the applicability of its findings, offering valuable guidance for platform managers and designers. Summary Statement Overall, all the research objectives outlined in the proposal have been successfully realized in the research paper. The study makes significant empirical, theoretical, and practical contributions to the understanding of information provision, preference mismatch, and optimal platform design in two-sided matching markets.

27504221.label: Major findings and research outcome
27504221.value: This study investigates how the amount of information provided affects matching outcomes in two-sided markets, focusing on online dating platforms. The authors find that there is a significant preference mismatch between users on opposite sides of the market, with users often proposing to candidates who are less likely to reply back or like back. Importantly, the research demonstrates a “less information is more” effect: users achieve better matching outcomes when making decisions based on partial information (short profiles) rather than full information (long profiles). More detailed information increases the likelihood of preference mismatch and reduces the probability of a successful match. The study suggests that onlineplatforms can improve match rates and overall platform value by strategically limiting the amount of information disclosed to users, rather than providing complete profiles. These findings have practical implications for the design of online dating and other matching platforms, highlighting the need to balance information provision with communication and mismatch costs. The authors also identify opportunities for future research on profile design, the effects of recommendation algorithms, and psychological factors influencing preference mismatch. Overall, the research highlights the critical importance of optimal information design in enhancing matching efficiency and outcomes in two-sided markets .

27504221.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27504221.value: The article highlights several promising avenues for further development of this research. One potential direction is to investigate how allowing users to control which information is disclosed in their profiles may influence matching outcomes and user satisfaction. Additionally, exploring the integration of advanced recommendation algorithms that account for preference mismatch could improve the effectiveness of matching platforms. The study also suggests examining psychological factors, such as social conformity or uniqueness-seeking, that may affect users' preferences and responses to information disclosure. Future research could extend the analysis to other types of two-sided platforms beyond online dating, such as job matching or rental services, to validate and generalize the findings. The proposed course of action involves conducting experimental and field studies to test the effects of various information disclosure strategies and profile designs. Collaboration with platform operators could facilitate large-scale field experiments, enabling the assessment of practical impacts on user engagement and match rates. Overall, advancing this line of inquiry will provide deeper insights into optimal information design and help platforms tailor their strategies to maximize user value and matching efficiency.

27504221.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27504221.value: This research looks at how much information online dating apps should show about potential matches to help people find better connections. It found that when users see too much information about others, they often end up choosing people who are less likely to reply or “like back,” because everyone’s preferences are different and can clash. Surprisingly, showing just a little bit of information—like a photo and a few basics—actually leads to more successful matches than showing full, detailed profiles. This “less is more” effect means that dating apps can help people connect more successfully by limiting what users see at first. The research is important because it challenges the common belief that more information is always better when making decisions. Its value goes beyond dating, as the findings can help other platforms—like those for finding jobs or renting homes—design better ways for people to connect. By understanding how much information is just right, these platforms can improve match rates, user satisfaction, and overall success. The study helps both users and companies by showing how the right information strategy makes for better matches and happier experiences.

27505021.label: Project Title(Chinese)
27505021.value: 面部表情的力量：CEO 的面部表情会向资本市场传递信息吗？

27505021.label: Project Objectives
27505021.value: To test whether CEOs display emotions during public appearances such as TV interviews: CEOs are trained specifically by personnel in Public Relation (PR) agencies of firms to appear neutral when communicating with market participants as overtly optimistic or pessimistic displays can be inferred in an unintended manner by stakeholders. This can further lead to costs for firms such as litigation costs and reputation costs. However, human nature dictates that it is very hard to maintain a single form of composure when interacting with others about important issues such as discussions about a firm’s performance. My first objective through this study is to test whether CEOs systematically display forms of facial emotions such as happiness and sadness that reflect their underlying belief about a firm’s performance or whether they appear to maintain a neutral composure throughout their public appearances. To test whether such non-verbal expressions provide information to market participants: I plan to test this by studying the impact of CEO emotions on changes in stock prices. There is a nascent literature that looks at how non-verbal forms of communications by managers affects market participants (Mayew and Venkatachalam, 2012). The earlier studies have focused on verbal cues (i.e. changes in tone of managers when they speak) and have studies market implications of such changes in verbal cues. However, studies till date have not looked at whether market participants react to facial expressions of CEOs, and whether such information is incorporated into stock prices. By focusing on CEOs’ facial expressions, I can extend the literature by adding an interesting dimension of impact of facial emotions in conveying information to capital market participants. This study would focus on CEO interviews that are broadcast on television and explore whether the stock market participants respond systematically to the visual display of affect during these interviews. By using a novel dataset of videos of CEO interviews on CNBC, Bloomberg, and other news channels over past 15 years, I expect to analyse facial expressions of CEOs during the interviews in order to measure the extent of positive and negative emotions conveyed by CEO facial expressions. I expect that affect displayed by a CEO (e.g. happiness, sadness) is an additional signal that is disseminated when the CEO interacts with investors, analysts, and other stakeholders, which can be taken into consideration when pricing the information content of the interaction. Test how and when information intermediaries such as analysts update their forecasts based on CEOs’ non-verbal information cues (facial expressions): Information intermediaries such as analysts update their beliefs about firm valuation based on a number of information sources released by firms such as earnings announcements and annual reports. While analysts react to information released in aforementioned sources, it is not clear if analysts also react to, and update their beliefs, about information contained in non-verbal forms of communications such as facial expressions. On one hand, analysts might incorporate insights gleaned from such non-verbal expressions, and update their beliefs about firm valuations. On the other hand, analysts might find this information to be hard to incorporate in their valuation models and hence would leave out such information from their formal valuation methods. It then becomes an empirical question whether information intermediaries such as analysts fully impound the information that is conveyed by non-verbal forms of communications or if they leave out such information from their valuation methodologies.

27505021.label: Realisation of objectives
27505021.value: Realization of Objectives I started this research project with three primary objectives: 1. To test whether CEOs display emotions during public appearances such as TV interviews 2. To test whether such non-verbal expressions provide information to market participants 3. To test how and when information intermediaries such as analysts update their forecasts based on CEOs’ non-verbal information cues (facial expressions) All three objectives have been successfully achieved, and the study has generated robust empirical evidence addressing each in turn. I briefly discuss each of them below: Objective 1: To test whether CEOs display emotions during public appearances such as TV interviews This objective was met by creating an extensive and novel dataset of CEO television interviews conducted on CNBC between 2009 and 2018. The sample comprises 2,239 usable observations after merging with market and accounting data, with interview videos covering a wide range of industries, firm sizes, and contexts, including both earnings announcement and non-earnings announcement periods. To measure CEO emotions, the project employed Microsoft’s Face API, a sophisticated facial-recognition tool capable of detecting emotional states such as happiness and sadness. Each video was processed into one-second image frames, allowing for precise measurement of facial affect over the course of the interview. The resulting variables — HAPPINESS, SADNESS, and the net measure OVERALL (happiness minus sadness) — quantify the proportion of interview time during which each emotion was displayed. The results confirmed that CEOs do indeed display emotions during public appearances, despite the expectation that they are trained to maintain a neutral or positive demeanour. On average, CEOs exhibited happiness in 19% of frames and sadness in 2.6% of frames, with the net affect being strongly positive. Objective 2: To test whether such non-verbal expressions provide information to market participants This objective was addressed through an extensive empirical analysis linking CEO facial emotion variables to stock market performance. The study measured short-run cumulative abnormal returns (CAR(0,1)) and long-run returns (CAR(2,60)) around the interview date, controlling for firm characteristics, verbal tone, and vocal cues to isolate the incremental effect of facial expressions. The findings show a clear and statistically significant relationship between CEO facial affect and short-term market reactions: a. Happiness is positively associated with short-run abnormal returns, indicating that investors interpret happy facial expressions as a positive signal about the firm’s prospects. b. Sadness is negatively associated with short-run abnormal returns, suggesting that investors view sadness as a negative signal. c. The net affect measure (OVERALL) is also positively associated with short-run returns. The study further examined how these effects vary with the level of scrutiny CEOs face. Happiness has the strongest positive effect in low-scrutiny contexts, while sadness has the most pronounced negative impact in high-scrutiny contexts — for example, when earnings results fall short of analyst expectations. This provides strong support for the hypothesis that non-verbal cues in CEO public appearances convey meaningful, incremental information to investors, over and above the spoken content and vocal tone. Objective 3: To test how and when information intermediaries such as analysts update their forecasts based on CEOs’ non-verbal information cues This objective was met by examining analyst activity following CEO interviews, using two measures: a. Forecast Revision (FREV) — the change in analysts’ earnings forecasts in the quarter following the interview compared to the latest forecast prior to the interview. b. Forecast Issuance Likelihood (FRACTION) — the proportion of analysts who issued a forecast both before and after the interview. The results indicate that analysts do not incorporate CEO facial expressions into their forecast revisions or issuance decisions. Instead, analyst activity is more strongly influenced by the verbal tone of the interview — specifically, the use of positive words. The broader finding is consistent with prior research showing that analysts rely more on verbal and quantitative disclosures than on non-verbal cues when updating their models. This outcome highlights an important distinction between investor and analyst behavior: while investors appear to trade on non-verbal signals in real time, analysts tend to ignore them in their formal forecasting processes, possibly due to the lack of standardized models for incorporating affective cues into earnings estimates. Challenges and Effort Required While all objectives were achieved, the data collection and processing stages proved far more challenging and time-consuming than anticipated. There is no readily available database of CEO interviews, so videos had to be manually identified and extracted from the Internet Archive’s TV News section. This involved sifting through over 14,000 search results to isolate actual CEO interviews, downloading video and transcript files, and coding start and end times. The subsequent processing — breaking videos into one-second frames, running them through the Face API, and averaging emotion scores — required significant computational resources and careful data management to ensure accuracy. Integrating these emotion measures with CRSP stock return data, Compustat financials, and I/B/E/S analyst forecasts added further complexity. Despite the challenges, the resulting dataset is uniquely rich and enables analyses not possible with traditional disclosure formats. The effort invested in this stage is a major reason why the objectives could be met in full. Feedback and Strategic Reorientation Toward ESG Following presentations of the paper at multiple universities and research seminars, the project received valuable feedback from faculty and peers. A recurring suggestion was to strategically align the research with the ESG (Environmental, Social, and Governance) space, given the current prominence of this theme in both academic and practitioner circles. The link between non-verbal cues, trust, and credibility is particularly relevant for ESG disclosures, where the risk of “greenwashing” — making misleading claims about sustainability — is high. Investor confidence in ESG statements often hinges not only on the factual content but also on the perceived sincerity of the speaker. Facial expressions could serve as an important credibility signal in this context, especially when verbal claims are difficult to verify in the short term. A revised version of the paper could focus on CEO emotional displays during interviews or public appearances where ESG topics are discussed, testing whether these cues influence investor reactions differently than in purely financial contexts. It could also examine whether certain emotional patterns correlate with later revelations of greenwashing or with third-party ESG ratings. This strategic pivot would broaden the appeal of the research, connect it to pressing contemporary debates about corporate accountability, and open up new opportunities for contribution to the ESG and sustainability literature. Next steps: 1. Expanding the dataset to include CEO appearances discussing ESG and sustainability topics. 2. Applying the same emotion-detection methodology to these interviews. 3. Testing whether facial cues influence investor reactions, ESG ratings, and greenwashing risk. Given the uniqueness of the dataset, the robustness of the methodology, and the relevance of the revised focus, the paper is well-positioned for submission to a leading accounting or finance journal in the coming year. The planned submission timeline is next year, following the completion of the ESG-focused revisions. This will allow the research to appeal to a broader audience, contribute to timely debates, and extend the impact of the project’s core findings.

27505021.label: Major findings and research outcome
27505021.value: Major Findings 1. Facial Expressions Have Market Impact: The study finds that CEO facial emotions displayed during live CNBC television interviews have a measurable impact on stock prices. Happiness is associated with positive short-term abnormal returns, while sadness is linked to negative short-term returns. These effects occur within a two-day window and do not reverse later, indicating that investors treat these emotional signals as meaningful information rather than transient sentiment. 2. Differential Effects Based on Scrutiny: Investor reactions vary depending on the level of scrutiny CEOs face. Happiness has the strongest positive impact in low-scrutiny situations, while sadness exerts the most negative influence in high-scrutiny contexts—such as following disappointing earnings announcements. 3. Incremental Information Beyond Words and Tone: The results hold even after controlling for the verbal content and vocal cues of the interviews, suggesting that facial expressions provide incremental information to the market. This highlights the importance of non-verbal communication as part of corporate disclosure. 4. No Long-Term Price Reversals: The study finds no association between CEO facial emotions and long-run returns, implying that the market quickly incorporates the information conveyed by these visual cues. Research Outcome The paper has been presented at multiple academic institutions, where it received constructive feedback from faculty and researchers. One recurring suggestion was that the research could be strategically developed to focus on the ESG (Environmental, Social, and Governance) space. In particular, the themes of trust and greenwashing—critical issues in ESG communications—align closely with the study’s core insights on how non-verbal signals affect credibility and investor perception. Shaping the paper toward ESG would involve examining CEO facial expressions in contexts where firms discuss sustainability initiatives, social responsibility, and governance practices. This could reveal whether emotional cues influence investor trust in ESG disclosures, help detect insincerity or “greenwashing,” and identify market reactions to credible versus potentially misleading ESG claims. Given the growing investor demand for trustworthy ESG information, and the heightened scrutiny over corporate sustainability promises, repositioning the paper in this direction would not only expand its relevance but also increase its contribution to understanding how leadership communication—both verbal and non-verbal—affects market trust in the era of responsible investing. This strategic refocusing could open a valuable research stream connecting behavioral finance, ESG disclosure credibility, and market outcomes.

27505021.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27505021.value: Updated Proposed Course of Action (ESG & Greenwashing Focus) 1. Integrate ESG Disclosure Context: Extend the research to CEO interviews and public appearances where environmental, social, and governance (ESG) topics are discussed. Measure whether facial expressions during ESG-related discussions influence investor perception and market reaction differently than in financial contexts. 2. Detect Emotional Cues in Potential Greenwashing: Analyze whether CEOs display distinct emotional patterns (e.g., nervousness, incongruence between verbal positivity and facial affect) when making ESG claims that may later be identified as misleading or “greenwashing.” 3. Link Emotions to ESG Ratings and Outcomes: Compare CEO emotional displays in ESG contexts to subsequent third-party ESG ratings, sustainability performance, and controversies, to assess whether facial cues can serve as early signals of credibility or risk. 4. Investor Sensitivity to ESG Emotions: Examine whether investors—especially ESG-focused funds—react more strongly in ESG-related interviews. Proposed course of action: Build a targeted dataset of CEO video appearances covering ESG topics, apply emotion-detection tools to identify affect patterns, and link these to market reactions, ESG ratings, and greenwashing incidents. This would advance understanding of how non-verbal signals shape trust, credibility, and valuation in the sustainability space.

27505021.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27505021.value: This research looks at how the emotions a CEO shows on their face during live TV interviews can influence their company’s stock price. Using thousands of CNBC interviews between 2009 and 2018, the study uses advanced facial-recognition technology to measure how much happiness or sadness a CEO displays while speaking. It then compares these emotional signals to stock market reactions, controlling for what the CEO actually says and how they sound. The findings show that investors respond quickly to these visual cues: happiness tends to boost stock prices, while sadness can lower them. These effects happen within a couple of days and don’t reverse later, meaning the market treats CEO facial expressions as real information rather than fleeting sentiment. The impact is stronger in certain situations — eg, sadness matters more when the CEO is under heavy scrutiny after disappointing earnings. This work is important because it reveals that investors pay attention not only to numbers and words, but also to subtle non-verbal signals. It highlights live TV interviews as a valuable but underexplored form of corporate disclosure and shows that facial expressions carry market-moving information, offering new insight into how leadership communication affects firm value.

27602621.label: Project Title(Chinese)
27602621.value: 示範性和附帶影響力：中國自1949年以來的國際發展戰略

27602621.label: Project Objectives
27602621.value: Develop a theoretical framework that clarifies the ways in which states’ international development strategies and behavior affect their pursuit of influence in developing countries. Provide an exhaustive account of China’s changing international development strategy since 1949 using a combination of Chinese- and English-language archival and other primary and secondary source evidence. Conceptually and empirically connect changes in China’s development strategy to different types of Chinese overseas development activities. Contribute to ongoing debates about the nature and extent of Chinese influence in the Global South by rigorously surveying individual reactions to Chinese-financed development activities. Expand previous evidence on public opinion toward Chinese international development projects beyond primarily African cases by studying public attitudes towards Chinese-financed development activities in Southeast Asia, specifically, Indonesia and Vietnam.

27602621.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27602621.value: How do powerful states approach international development, and how do these states gain and lose influence in developing countries? While the “Global South” has returned as an arena for geopolitical competition between China, the United States, and a host of “emerging” and “traditional” powers, theoretical and empirical international relations research has struggled to answer these questions. In particular, existing research has neglected two potentially important processes: how states’ development strategies shape the ways in which they pursue influence abroad, and how popular reactions in developing countries contribute to or detract from states' influence. These processes are arguably especially critical for understanding China’s growing but controversial role in international development. This project will address these gaps by making three contributions. First, it will develop a theoretical framework that explains how shifts in development strategies affect how states pursue influence overseas. The framework highlights two channels: “Demonstrative” influence involves visible activities such as prominent development projects and new technologies that affect popular perceptions of powerful states abroad. “Incidental” influence refers to unintended changes in public sentiment toward a state resulting from commercial activities of quasi- and non-state actors. I argue that these channels are particularly important for “emerging” powers like China, India, Russia, and Saudi Arabia given these states’ high levels of economic integration with developing countries. Second, I will apply this framework to understand how the most consequential rising power in international development—China’s government—has pursued influence in developing countries since 1949. My multi-method research plan includes qualitative analysis of archival and primary source documents as well as the creation of an original dataset on Chinese development activities and influence channels in over 100 developing countries. Third, this research will provide some of the first rigorous evidence on whether and how China’s development activities generate popular influence on the ground. A set of original surveys conducted in Indonesia and Vietnam—two important but understudied host countries for Chinese development activities—will experimentally test the efficacy of various influence channels. Qualitative interviews and fieldwork in China, Indonesia, and Vietnam will complement these large-N surveys. The project will yield three research articles to be published in leading international relations and China journals (4*/3*). Research findings will be presented annually at a leading political science conference. I have a clear track record of producing rigorous, policy-relevant research on Chinese development finance, and am confident that I can complete the research as scheduled.

27603121.label: Project Title(Chinese)
27603121.value: 莎士比亞晚期劇作的復活情節

27603121.label: Project Objectives
27603121.value: The project will reassess the nature and significance of Shakespeare’s late plays, which have been much contested in scholarship. It aims: (a) To use close literary analysis to explain how and why Shakespeare’s use of resurrection alters his dramaturgy in the late plays – unsettling genre, character, self, time, and narrative structure. (b) To thereby explain how and why Shakespeare moves away from tragic drama’s emphasis upon a central dominating consciousness (the tragic hero) to his strangely discontinuous and diffused romance characters. The project will shed new light on the relationship between early modern religion and the period’s supposedly secular drama. (a) It will undertake new historical research into sermons, tracts, poems, liturgy, and religious practice in order to build a picture of early modern thinking about resurrection. It will investigate how this thinking influences early modern theatre and literature and explore its influence on ideas of history and personhood; including how resurrection: o bends time and inspires non-linear modes of thinking about the past; o involves the death, mortification, even annihilation, of the self; o calls for a certain type of attentiveness – one that involves hearing and turning to a stranger or other – which is relevant to questions of theatrical affect or emotion. (b) The project will contribute to ongoing historical debates about “secularization” by assessing what Shakespeare draws from his religious culture and how he transforms it. It will demonstrate the ways in which our intellectual histories of early modern religion are incomplete without due consideration of the period’s dramatic writing. A third, concluding, aim relates to Literary Studies more broadly: to explore how Shakespeare’s resurrections – including his own reanimations of seemingly defunct poetic and theatrical forms – provide tools for literary criticism’s attempts to bring to life the literature of the past. The project will thereby contribute to the resurgent, if often ill-defined, interest in “aesthetics” in Literary Studies, and open up pathways to impact in teaching and community engagement by using resurrection to explore a temporal paradox at the heart of criticism: how a historical artifact, so embedded in its historical moment, can also be our contemporary, alive in our present lives.

27603121.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27603121.value: The project investigates a striking religious feature of Shakespeare’s late plays (ca.1607-1612): his staging of resurrection scenes in which the (apparently) dead return in fear and wonder. Scholarship has paid little attention to Shakespeare’s use of resurrection and thereby overlooked a key historical and theatrical driving force behind the final stage of his career – along with his contribution to early modern religious culture. The project will analyse Shakespeare’s “resurrection events” through a range of literary, historical, and philosophical tools, thereby reassessing our understanding of the late plays and enhancing our understanding of Shakespeare’s complex relation to early modern religion. The nature of Shakespeare’s late plays, or romances, has long been contested. Much of the confusion stems from his shift in character-creation. We struggle to understand why, after the most extraordinary run in English literary history – Hamlet, Othello, Lear, Macbeth – Shakespeare abandons his well-rounded, psychologically complex tragic figures in favour of the strangely discontinuous, fragmentary characters of the late plays. The project argues that Shakespeare’s “resurrection events” lie at the heart of his shift to the generically mixed modes of the romances. Through detailed literary analysis, it explores how these “resurrections” radically alter Shakespeare’s treatment of character, narrative time, and theatrical form – prompting the disintegration of the individual and its rebirth through a wondrous, if manipulative, theatrical moment of collective reunion. The project thereby gives a fresh understanding of the end of Shakespeare’s career and helps invigorate and theorise the “aesthetic turn” in criticism. The project will undertake new historical research into discourses and practices surrounding resurrection and assess how they impact early modern conceptions of time, selfhood, and affective response. It will assess the significance of these sources for our understanding of Shakespeare’s late plays and of early modern drama and subjectivity more generally. The aim is to show that, despite the so-called “turn to religion”, scholarship is yet to fully appreciate the way religious ideas and practice influence the apparently secular dramatic technologies of the period’s theatre – or to the way religious ideas are transformed by drama. The project thereby contributes to broader debates about “secularization” in early modern studies: it shows both how Shakespeare engages in a creative dialogue with his religious culture and how religious ideas moved beyond organised religion into popular culture, imagination, and narrative. It demonstrates that our histories of early modern religion remain incomplete without due consideration of the period’s drama. 本研究探討莎士比亞晚期劇作（約1607-1612年）的宗教特點︰安排角色復活的情節，令（顯然）已逝者在瀰漫恐懼和驚異的氣氛中復活。學術界一直鮮有留意莎翁的晚期創作生涯中以復活為題，背後的歷史及戲劇方面的推動力，及他對近世（early modern）宗教文化的影響。本研究運用一眾文學、史學、哲學概念，分析莎翁晚期劇作中的復活情節，藉此重新審視後世對這些晚期作品的理解，包括莎翁與近世宗教間錯綜複雜之關係。 莎翁的晚期劇作（尤指愛情劇）一直備受爭論，大多源於他改變了塑造角色的手法。《哈姆雷特》、《奧塞羅》、《李爾王》、《馬克白》均是英語文學鉅著。然而，莎翁其後筆鋒一轉，捨棄「四大悲劇」中，刻劃完整、內心深沉而複雜的悲劇人物，改以性格前後不一、刻劃零碎的角色領銜。箇中原因，令人大惑不解。本文主張，莎翁轉為兼融不同題材如愛情等，其「復活情節」是關鍵。本研究遂以仔細的文學分析，探討這些復活情節如何令莎翁的人物刻劃手法、故事時序設定和劇作種類呈現巨變。他先促使個體瓦解（disintegration of the individual），後鋪設角色於戲劇性及超現實的「復活」情節中重圓的情節。本研究盼以嶄新的角度重新審視莎翁晚期的寫作生涯，為晚期莎劇呈現的「美學轉向」（“aesthetic turn”）確立理論基礎，以新見解貢獻文學評論。 本研究採用新的歷史研究觀點，探討關乎「復活」的論述和禮俗，兩者如何影響近世社會對時間觀念、自我概念和情感反應，從而加深後世理解莎翁晚期劇作、近世戲劇的宏觀及主觀性。縱有所謂的「回歸宗教」（turn to religion）的主張，學術界仍未全然循戲劇層面探討宗教思想和風俗與世俗化（secularization）的關係，或戲劇如何改變宗教思想。故此，本研究擴充近世研究中關乎「世俗化」的討論，展示莎翁如何藉創作反思自身的宗教文化，反映宗教思想如何跨越有組織的宗教，走進流行文化、個人想像及敍事領域。此研究旨在引證，如要更全面了解近世的宗教歷史，探討同期的戲作確實是不可缺少的一環。

27603421.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27603421.value: 類風濕性關節炎作為最常見的炎性關節疾病，為個人及社會帶來了沉重負擔。疾病調節抗風濕藥物中，生物製劑的出現為“達標治療”（Treat-to-target）及患者生存質量提供了明顯改善。儘管如此，生物製劑高昂的費用可能限制患者的使用同時影響公費資助政策的制定。近年出現的生物仿製藥，具有和原生物製劑等同的安全性和療效性，因其相對低廉的價格，有望節省藥物及其他醫療花費，並促進藥物可及性。現階段鮮有生物仿製藥及原研藥的成本效益研究。 此項研究中，我們將建立一個基於Markov模擬隊列的決策模型（Markov cohort simulation model），用來模擬香港風濕性關節炎病人疾病的發展過程並預測其終生的健康及經濟結局。我們將從全社會角度來考慮三種治療方案的成本效益，包括原研生物製劑，生物仿製藥及非生物製劑。模型中的相關變量將從“臨床研究及報告系統”(CDARS)，病人問卷調查，及已發表的系統綜述以及臨床研究中獲取。CDARS擁有1100萬香港居民去識別化的公共電子醫療記錄。CDARS所具備的詳細處方記錄，診斷記錄及醫療資源使用情況為模型提供了重要的真實世界證據。這些數據資源填補了現有模型單純依賴臨床實驗數據和 假設推斷的不足。 模型預測的首要結果為遞增成本效果比值（ICER），暨每獲得一個質量調整生命年所需要的增量成本。如果某治療方案的ICER低於預先設定的支付意願（willing-to-pay）閾值將被認為具備成本效益。模型擬合的次要結局包括終身醫療成本，生產力損失相關成本，預期生命年，疾病緩解天數及嚴重安全事件的數量。所有輸出變量都將在三組治療間進行比較。我們將用情景分析，單因素及概率性靈敏度分析檢測模型預測結果的穩定性。本研究所建立的真實世界數據主導的成本效益分析模型將為生物製劑及生物仿製藥在類風濕關節炎病人中的應用提供及時的證據及決策支持。此項研究也將為真實世界證據在衛生經濟學研究中的應用帶來更廣泛的討論。

27603421.label: Realisation of objectives
27603421.value: Objective 1 We have successfully developed and validated a population-specific markove model simulated the disease progression and outcomes of patients with RA in Hong Kong. The study has been officially published in peer-reviewed journal JAMA Network Open (Impact factor 13.8 in 2023). Objective 2 From local electronics medical record database, we have successfully identified 25099 patients with RA and their corresponding prescription records, diagnosis and death information were retrieved retrospectively since 2009. Using this cohort, we generated market share, treatment switch or discontinuation rate, and the disease-related healthcare resource utilization to fit the model in a local setting. Objective 3 For the input parameters not available from local electronics medical records (e.g., treatment effectiveness and patients' reported quality of life). We conducted systematic literature review identify these parameters from landmark clincal trials and network meta-analysis. Objective 4 In original proposal objective 4, utility of disease stage is expected to be sourced from local community-based patient survey, however, We found utility generated from randomized controlled trial fit our model best, as it could adjust patients disease severity precisely, while utilities from community-based patient survey lack the supplementary information about disease severity. Utility parameters were therefore retrieved from landmark clinical trials. Objective 5 In accordance with achievements in objective 1, we successfully compared the lifetime health and economic outcomes for RA patients receiving treatment sequence started with biosimilar DMARDs versus leflunomide (non-biologic treatment). The biologic originators were put in the subsequent treatment line because of their low subsidy priority due to expensive drug cost. Objective 6 Incremental costs, incremental QALY, and incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (ICER) were computed by comparing treatment sequences initiated with biosimilar DMARDs vs leflunomide. ICERs were subsequently compared against a willingness-to-pay threshold (WTP) of a 1-time gross domestic product (GDP) per capita in Hong Kong in 2022 (US $48 555 per QALY gain), according to the World Health Organization recommendation. All biosimilar DMARDs have ICER lower than this threshold thus considered as cost-effective treatment strategies in Hong Kong healthcare setting. Objective 7 Our sensitivity analysis shows the most important factors influencing the cost-effectivenss of biologic medicine were cost of biosimilar DMARDs, drug discontinuation rate of leflunomide, and cost of visiting community-allied physiotherapy health service in sequence.

27603421.label: Major findings and research outcome
27603421.value: In the base-case analysis, the lifetime health care cost and quality adjusted life years (QALYs) for the treatment sequence initiated with leflunomide were US $154 632 and 14.82 QALYs, respectively; for biosimilar infliximab, they were US $152 326 and 15.35 QALYs, respectively; and for biosimilar adalimumab, they were US $145 419 and 15.55 QALYs, respectively. Biosimilar treatment strategies presented lower healthcare costs and greater quality of life improvement than leflunomide. The projected budget saving was US$ 2306 and US$ 9213 per patient treated for biosimilar Infliximab and biosimilar adalimumab, respectively. The cost-effectiveness conclusion is robust from various scenarios analysis and sensitivity analysis. The cost of biosimilar disease-modifying antirheumatic disease drugs (DMARDs) was identified as the most influential factor to study conclusion. In review from global perspective, the price of biosimilar DMARDs in Hong Kong falls within the mid-range (rank 14 among 29 high-income countries/regions) globally. In summary, the study findings suggest the need to update clinical treatment guidelines for initiating biosimilars immediately after the failure of methotrexate for patients with RA.

27603421.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27603421.value: A budget impact analysis (BIA) is an economic assessment that estimates the financial consequences of adopting a new intervention. A BIA is usually performed in addition to a cost-effectiveness analysis. In our case, the potential further direction of the study is to promote the inclusion of biosimilar DMARDs in Hong Kong drug formulary, to doing so, a BIA can inform healthcare decision maker understand the healthcare expenditure required to subsidy biosimilar DMARDs in Hong Kong. The brife action plan includes: 1: Predicting the prevalence of RA in Hong Kong for a timescale of 10 years and estimated the proportion of patients need to access the biosimilar DMARDs 2: Incorporate the economic model in this study to simulates the healthcare expenditure with different uncertainties

27603421.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27603421.value: Our findings suggest biosimilar disease-modifying antirheumatic disease drugs (DMARDs) are likely to be cost-effective alternatives to leflunomide in managing patients with inadequate response to methotrexate. The cost savings came from well-controlled disease activity that prevented the requirement of hospitalisation, emergency room attendance and the need for supportive care, such as physiotherapy. Echoing the current treatment guidelines, our study provides economic evidence supporting early access to cheaper bDMARDs to achieve treatment targets and improve patient outcomes. In a global context, biosimilar DMARDs have great potential to be cost-effective, which could spark new research interests for policymakers worldwide. In summary, our study is a good attempt to apply health technology assessment (HTA) for informed decision-making. This systematic evaluation process helps decision-makers assess the value, efficacy, and cost-effectiveness of new treatments by providing transparent and evidence-based insights. Efficient HTA mechanisms can significantly reduce drug approval and patient access time by streamlining the evaluation process. Moreover, robust HTAs can promote transparency in decision-making, foster stakeholder engagement, and optimise resource allocation in healthcare systems.

27603721.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27603721.value: Is the idea of precedent anathema to socialist legality? If so, is the aversion to case law merely superficial or is it instantiated by judicial practice and legal outcomes? And what do the answers to the questions tell us about how legal ideas morph and spread throughout the globe? This project explores the receptivity of socialist legal systems to the common law notion of precedent. In contrast to common law jurisdictions like the United States, the United Kingdom, and Hong Kong, socialist and civil law regimes do not recognize judicial opinions as establishing a legal rule for future cases. Under socialist legal ideology, judges administer the rules laid down by legislatures but do not pretend to expound them. Because judicial opinions are binding only on the disputing parties, cases do not alter the legal fabric. Recent legal developments in the Socialist Republic of Vietnam and the People’s Republic of China are blurring the divide between legal systems that are built on precedent and those that are not. Over the last decade, the supreme courts of the two socialist regimes have sought to interpret and unify national law by promulging cases that all judges must take reference from. In contrast to the Vietnam, however, reception of this innovation in China has been lukewarm. According to empirical studies conducted by researchers at the City University of Hong Kong, Peking University and Stanford University, Guiding Cases are very rarely cited in Chinese judgments. The divergence between China and Vietnam might be due to the former’s commitment to socialist legality and the latter’s estrangement from it. But geo-political stature and ambition may also furnish an explanation. We revisit conventional wisdom about the Chinese resistance to precedent by applying computational methods to study how the Guiding Cases shape legal disputes and discourse in the lower courts. This project traces the influence of Guiding Cases by looking beyond citations—overt references—to search for echoes of their reasoning—or implicit references—in the decisions of lower courts. It also explores the impact of a Guiding Case on the kinds of disputes that are channeled into the judicial system. The novel approach taken here promises not only to illuminate the practical operation of the Chinese legal system but also to contribute to a more sophisticated understanding of how legal concepts and values travel and how they are transformed. 先例的概念与社会主义法治相抵触吗？如果是这样，对判例法的排斥仅仅是表面上的呢？还是由司法实践和结果所导致的？这些问题的答案能告诉我们法律概念是如何在全球范围内演变和传播的吗？这个课题探讨和洞察社会主义法律体系对普通法先例概念的接受程度。与美国、英国和香港这样的普通法系辖区不同，社会主义和大陆法系不将司法判决看作是为未来的案件建立法律规则的一种正式的法律渊源。在社会主义法律意识形态下，法官执行运用立法机关制定的规则，但并不佯装对其进行延展。由于司法判决仅对争议双方具有约束力，因此案件并不会改变法律原有的结构和规则。 越南和中国最近的法律发展正在模糊建立在先例基础上的法律体系和没有先例的法律体系之间的界限。在过去的十年中，这两个社会主义国家的最高法院通过颁布指导性案例来解释和统一国家的法律，而这些案例是要求所有法官在类似案件中必须参照的。然而，与越南相比，中国法院对这一改革的采纳程度不高。从香港城市大学、北京大学和斯坦福大学的学者的实证研究结果来看，中国的判决中很少引用指导性案例。中国和越南之间的分歧可能是由于前者对社会主义法制的坚持，而后者则与之逐渐失和。但地缘相关的政治地位和追求也可以阐释这一差异的体现。 我们通过计算机科学来探讨最高法院公布的指导性案例是如何影响下级法院所处理的法律纠纷，从而重新审视之前有关地方法院抵触先例的研究结果的可靠性。该项目通过跟踪下级法院的判决中对指导性案例明示的引用或默示的参照，来量化指导性案例在地方法院审判实践中的影响。我们的课题也将探讨指导性案例对今后在法院起诉的纠纷类型所产生的影响。课题中所采用的机器学习这一前沿的研究方法不仅有望阐明中国的司法实践过程，而且有助于我们更深入地理解法律概念和价值是如何传播以及如何转化的。

27603721.label: Realisation of objectives
27603721.value: 1. The first objective was fully accomplished. By adapting the Basic Local Alignment Search Tool (or BLAST) algorithm, typically used to compare genetic sequences, for Chinese characters, the investigators were able to identify unattributed references to the Supreme People’s Court’s Guiding Cases in the judgments of Beijing and Shanghai courts. These unattributed references were then validated by human labellers and analyzed. Quantitative findings at various stages of the study were presented at the Conference on Empirical Legal Studies in Asia, hosed by Academica Sinica in Taipei and Computational Legal Studies, hosted by Singapore Management University. The methodology and results are published in the article “Detecting the Influence of the Chinese Guiding Cases: A Text Reuse Approach” which appeared in Artificial Intelligence and Law in May 2023. 2. The second objective was partially accomplished. By estimating document embeddings from a corpus of Beijing and Shanghai court judgments, investigators were able to generate clusters of similar cases. However, these clusters were not sufficiently discriminating to be reliable for social scientific causal inference. Moreover, the drawing of causal inferences, even from big data, requires identifying assumptions that may or may not obtain. Some of the challenges are described and illustrated in the article “Data Still Needs Theory: Collider Bias in Empirical Legal Research” which appeared in the Hong Kong Law Journal in December 2023. 3. The third objective was fully accomplished. By using regular expressions to count the number of attributed references in the same corpus of Beijing and Shanghai judgments, the investigators were able to give some indication of the extent to which the previous studies underestimate the significance of Guiding Cases. Contrary to the literature, the results of this project suggest that the Guiding Case System is neither marginal nor dysfunctional. These arguments and their implications for our understanding of the PRC legal system were explored in a seminar given at the Southwestern University of Finance and Economics and summarized in a blogpost by the European Chinese Law Research Hub, housed in the University of Cologne. 4. The fourth objective was fully accomplished. Through a close reading of the matches generated by the BLAST algorithm, the investigators discerned two techniques that PRC judges employ to implement a Guiding Case without citing to it: statutory ventriloquy and jurisprudential retracing. These phenomena indicate that the doctrinal rejection of cases as precedent may be more form than substance. These arguments and their implications for the comparative study of law and legal institutions were explored in seminars given at ETH Zurich and Durham University. 5. The fifth objective was not substantially accomplished. Given (1) the limited utility of document embeddings in making fine distinctions between cases, as related above, (2) the overarching purpose of the project and (3) the timeframe of the project, the investigators determined that effort and resources would be better allocated to more promising avenues of inquiry illuminated by the successful application of text reuse methods to judicial documents.

27603721.label: Major findings and research outcome
27603721.value: Jurisprudentially, cases are not a source of law in socialist legal systems, including that of the People’s Republic of China. In 2011, however, the Supreme People’s Court introduced the Guiding Case system. Guiding Cases are selected by the Supreme People’s Court and must be referred to by courts at all levels when adjudicating similar controversies. The practical impact of Guiding Cases on judicial practice has however been called into question by many legal scholars and commentators. Previous studies almost uniformly find that citations to Guiding Cases are sparse, and many Guiding Cases are not cited at all (Daum 2017; Zhang 2018). The ‘extremely low’ incidence of citations is taken as symptomatic of ‘the dysfunction of the [G]uiding [C]ase system as a type of case law’ (Wang 2019) and as proof of the incongruity of case-based adjudication in China (Ahl 2014; Zuo & Chen 2015; Finder 2017; Jia 2016). However, citations might not be an accurate measure of the influence of cases. The premise of our research is that reuse of text uniquely ascribable to the Main Points of Adjudication is a strong indicium of the influence of Guiding Cases on judicial decision-making. The Basic Local Alignment Search Tool or BLAST algorithm is employed to search for text reuse in local court decisions. Ultimately, we find more instances of unattributed text reuse than citations for the Guiding Cases examined. A close reading of local court decisions reveals that it is not uncommon for them to cite statutory or regulatory instruments for propositions reproduced from a Guiding Case (“statutory ventriloquy”). In addition, rather than quote the Main Points of Adjudication as directed by the Supreme People’s Court’s Detailed Rules, many judgments simply repeated the various legal arguments adduced in the Guiding Case (“jurisprudential retracing”). To conclude, previous studies report that Guiding Cases are rarely cited in judicial decisions, suggesting that their practical effect is negligible. The anaemic impact of Guiding Cases has sometimes been taken as demonstrating the fundamental incompatibility between socialist legality and judicial precedent. We demonstrate, however, that Guiding Cases are more influential than conventionally thought. By uncovering how the Guiding Cases are referred to other than by name, we not only illuminate the operation of Chinese law but also inform debates about legal traditions, cultures, and transplants.

27603721.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27603721.value: Most immediately, the research can be developed in two major directions. The first direction is to broaden the scope of the study to include other subnational jurisdictions beyond Beijing and Shanghai. Variation between jurisdictions might uncover the social, economic, and cultural factors that animate the refusal to cite Guiding Cases even when they are being adhered to. The second direction is to test text reuse algorithms other than BLAST, for instance, Smith-Waterman algorithm. The Smith-Waterman algorithm is supposed to be more accurate but also more computationally expensive than the BLAST algorithm. A comparison between BLAST and Smith-Waterman could generate insights into the trade-offs between the two algorithms in the context of PRC legal text. Efforts have been taken to further the research along these dimensions. Recently, the investigators have obtained access to a database that contains decisions from local courts in all provinces. The reliability and completeness of this database is still being accessed and lies outside the parameters of the funded project. In the longer term, researchers may consider applying the techniques developed in this research to investigate the influence of cases in other jurisdictions that do not recognize precedent as a source of law.

27603721.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27603721.value: In socialist legal systems like that of the People’s Republic of China, cases are not traditionally considered a source of law. However, in 2011, the Supreme People’s Court introduced the Guiding Cases system. Guiding Cases are selected by the Supreme People’s Court and must be referred to by lower courts where relevant. The practical impact of the Guiding Cases has been widely questioned. Previous studies report that they are rarely cited, suggesting their lack of importance. We adopt a novel approach to analyse the influence of Guiding Cases. Instead of counting citations, we examine local court decisions for the reuse of text from the Guiding Cases. We find many instances of such reuse, indicating a subtle but distinct influence of Guiding Cases on how local courts decide disputes. We also find that local courts often apply Guiding Cases by copying their legal reasoning or mixing-and-matching language from other sources. In so doing, local courts avoid citing Guiding Cases even when they are following them. In conclusion, the Guiding Cases are more significant than they might seem at first glance. This and other discoveries enrich our understanding of diverse legal traditions and cultures.

27603921.label: Project Title(Chinese)
27603921.value: 美國基金會、印度表演藝術與文化發展的源流

27603921.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27603921.value: On 11 December 1992, the UN Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali and the Director-General of UNESCO, Federico Mayor, proposed an independent ‘World Commission on Culture and Development’ in response to the necessity for an appraisal of existing development methods that had rendered the 1980s a ‘lost decade’. The commission argued that culture was a critical determinant, if not the essence, of sustainable development as it was at the heart of production, an ecologically sustainable economy, the consolidation of peace between ethnic, religious and nationalist groups, and all human activity. Since then, the concept ‘cultural development’ has become ubiquitous in development literature and the policy-thinking of supranational, national, and regional organizations as diverse as the European Union National Institutes for Culture (EUNIC), the Aga Khan Trust for Culture, and the Asian Cultural Council. However, the origins, evolution and long-term effects of this concept have a much longer history — one that has not received thus far a fraction of the attention as its sister-term ‘cultural diplomacy’. This three-year research project will provide the first in-depth history of ‘cultural development’, a paradigm that constituted a distinctive component of American Cold and post-Cold War diplomacy. It will examine how the performing arts were instrumentalized as tools for development in emerging countries, a legitimation narrative for culture that facilitated heterogeneous objectives — from national ‘modernisation’ projects, ‘soft’ or ‘smart’ power activities to international cooperation. Due to its strategic location, non-aligned political status, and symbolic value as the world’s largest democracy, India functioned, in the words of a Ford Foundation officer, as a ‘guinea pig’ for this ‘cultural development’ experiment. Drawing on interviews and primary sources from the Rockefeller Archive Center, Indian and U.S. government archives, and private collections, the project analyses how the performing arts were posited by politicians, foundation officers, scholars, and artists as key drivers of productivity and economic growth in India, a model that was subsequently replicated and transposed to other cash-strapped emerging countries. By tracing the institutional development of theatre in universities, government centres, and NGOs, the growth of an epistemic community of state and non-state actors, and the reciprocal flows of knowledge between India and the U.S., the findings of this project in book and article forms will provide a comprehensive, archive-based re-evaluation of the history of the performing arts in the ‘Global South’ during and after the Cold War. 一九九二年十二月十一日，聯合國秘書長布特羅斯．布特羅斯-加利（Boutros Boutros-Ghali）和聯合國教科文組織總幹事費德里科．馬約爾（Federico Mayor），倡議設立獨立的「世界文化與發展委員會」（World Commission on Culture and Development），以回應當時的發展模式之弊病，已令一九八〇年代過了儼如「失落的十年」（lost decade）。委員會認為文化乃可持續發展（sustainable development）之關鍵（如非最重要的）因素，皆因文化對生產（production）、生態上可持續的經濟、維繫各種族、宗教、國族間的和平，以至一切人類活動都極為重要。自此，「文化發展」（cultural development）此概念無處不在，遍佈有關發展的文獻以及一眾跨國、國家和區域組織的政策研究，諸如歐盟國家文化研究中心（European Union National Institutes for Culture, EUNIC）、阿加汗文化信託基金會（Aga Khan Trust for Culture）、亞洲文化協會（Asian Cultural Council）。然而，文化發展的源流、演變、長遠影響等源遠流長，但受關注的程度卻大大不及其相關詞「文化外交」（cultural diplomacy）。 是次研究為期三年，將首次發表詳盡的「文化發展」史——此乃美國冷戰及後冷戰外交的重要部分。本研究探討後進國家如何應用表演藝術，達到為促進多元的文化正名（legitimation）之目的，例如國家「現代化」計劃，展示「軟」實力（‘soft’ power）或「巧」實力（‘smart’ power）的行動，乃至國際間之合作。印度的地理位置具戰略意義，政治上不結盟的政治取向，亦為象徵世上擁有最大民主人口的國家。故此，引一名福特基金會（Ford Foundation）人員的說法，印度儼如這場「文化發展」的試驗對象。本研究徵引訪問和一手資料，包括洛克菲勒檔案中心（Rockefeller Archive Center）、印度與美國政府檔案，以及私人檔案，分析從政者、基金會、學者、藝術家的構思，如何以表演藝術驅動，使印度的生產力提升和經濟增長。此模式其後獲財政緊拙的後進國家仿效。本文追溯三大範疇的發展：戲劇在大學、政府、非政府組織團體內的發展；國家行為者（state actors）與非國家行為者（non-state actors）的知識社群（epistemic community）發展；以及印度和美國之間的知識交流。是次研究徵引資料豐富的檔案資料，重新審視冷戰期間和其後「南方世界」（Global South）的表演藝術。研究者會將成果發表成書和論文。

27604721.label: Project Title(Chinese)
27604721.value: 渐近线网格建筑围护结构-自由曲面结构的简化制作和安装

27604721.label: Project Objectives
27604721.value: Develop a computational workflow for the design of asymptotic structures, that integrates geometric modelling, structural form-finding and analysis within one digital environment for architects and engineers (Rhinoceros 3D). (In collaboration with software engineers, Kai Uwe Bletzinger, TUM) Create a robust and sustainable construction system for building envelopes through the systematic development and testing of two full-scale prototypes for (a) a vertical curtain wall module and (b) a horizontal roof structure. These prototypes fulfil the following purpose: a) to verify the computational workflow (objective 1) b) to develop a material solution for lamella grids (comparing timber, GRP, steel, and composites), which offers to combine an elastic formation with a rigid structural behavior. c) to develop resilient cladding strategies for planar glass, elastic polycarbonate and pre-stressed-membranes, which take advantage of the specific geometrical properties of asymptotic networks. (with support of an expert in applied geometry, Helmut Pottmann, KAUST) d) to establish a low-cost and high precision process of fabrication, logistics and assembly. (with support of an industry partner, Sam Hsu, GOMORE, Taiwan) e) to test their structural and functional performance. (with support of an expert in computational mechanics, Xiaowei Deng, HKU) Establish architectural applications by designing urban scenarios for asymptotic building envelopes, investigate their geometric limits and evaluating their functional qualities. Disseminate our knowledge through peer-reviewed articles as well as conference presentations, exhibitions, workshops and digital media for the academic and professional community.

27604721.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27604721.value: This proposal aims to enhance a new, sustainable approach to design lightweight free-form structures whilst embracing simple, repetitive fabrication and assembly. Doubly curved structures, such as shells or membranes, carry loads through tension and compression using substantially less material than bending-active plate or beam systems. Nonetheless, their application in architecture remains rare, as their free-form geometry often lacks to integrate with the built environment, and creates high costs in the fabrication, logistics and assembly of individual and spatially complex parts. In 2017, a geometric design method was developed by the PI, using asymptotic curve networks to enable a simple fabrication from straight and flat lamellas and repetitive orthogonal joints. The use of slender lamellas facilitates a self-forming erection process and offers structural resilience as both gridshell and grillage, thus allowing for a smooth transition from curved to flat design. Initial built examples of asymptotic structures have verified the advantages for fabrication, assembly and load-bearing behavior. However, so far the technology has only been used for free-standing sculptures of up to 6 m span without cladding system and thus remains in an experimental stage of design. We aim to develop a low-cost, low-skill construction system for doubly curved building envelopes. For this purpose, two full-scale prototypes, a vertical curtain-wall module and a horizontal self-supporting roof segment, will be constructed and tested in close collaboration with the building industry (GOMORE) and the Department of Civil Engineering, HKU. Furthermore, the design process is currently still complex and time-intensive. In order to open up this approach to the architectural community, we propose to develop a computational workflow that integrates the topological grid definition, structural form-finding and analysis, and fabrication planning within one digital environment (Rhinoceros 3D) using Iso-geometric Analysis (IGA) for seamless NURBS modelling. Finally, we develop architectural design scenarios, that illustrate the geometric performance and functional integration into the built environment. These scenarios pave the way for further research beyond the scope of this proposal. In the future, we aim to procure an urban site and implement a case study in order to evaluate the performance, exhibit the system to the public and collect user feedback. By creating the constructive and computational method to design low-cost, light-weight asymptotic building envelopes, this study will become a building block for sustainable and affordable architectural applications for the twenty-first century. It thus offers an alternative to the extravagant and bespoke design solutions currently used for free-form construction. 本申请旨在提出一种设计轻质自由曲面结构的新型可持续方法，同时采用简单、可重复性的制作和安装。 与主动弯曲板或主动弯曲梁体系相比，双曲结构（如壳体或膜结构）主要通过受拉和受压来承担荷载，这样也因此使用更少的材料。然而，他们在建筑领域的应用依然很少，因为它们的自由几何形式通常无法与建筑环境相集成，并且在单个和空间复杂的多个部件的制造、运输和安装方面产生了高昂的成本。 2017年，本申请人开发了一种几何设计方法，通过使用渐进曲线网格，实现了从平直的片状构件以及可重复的节点构造来简单快速地建造建筑物。细长薄板的使用可以促成自动成形的安装过程，并提供格栅式壳和格栅式梁的结构承载能力，从而实现从弯曲设计到平面设计的转换。 渐近线结构的初步建造实例验证了制作、安装和结构承载性能的优势。然而，到目前为止，该方法仅运用在一个不包含围护面板的跨度为6m的雕塑，因此仍处于试验阶段。 我们的目标是开发一种低成本、技术要求低的双曲面建筑围护结构体系。为此，将与建筑公司（GOMORE）和香港大学土木工程系密切合作，建造并测试两个足尺模型：一个垂直幕墙体系和一个自承重的水平屋面体系。 此外，目前的设计过程仍然比较复杂耗时。我们提出一种新的数字设计方法，该方法运用等几何分析(IGA)的计算方法，在一个数字建模平台（Rhinoceros 3D）中集成拓扑网格定义、结构找形和分析、以及建造施工设计，以实现基于NURBS的无缝建模。 最后，我们开发了建筑设计场景，以将几何性能和功能集成到建筑环境中去。这些场景为本申请范围之外的进一步研究铺平了道路。在未来，我们的目标是努力获得一个城市场地并开展案例研究，以对性能进行评估、并向公众展示该系统并收集用户的反馈。 通过创建具有建设性的数字设计方法来设计低成本、轻质化的渐近线建筑围护结构，本研究将成为二十一世纪可持续性和经济性的建筑应用的基石。因此，它将提供目前用于自由形式建筑的奢华定制设计的替代方案。

27604821.label: Project Title(Chinese)
27604821.value: 教育擴張，大學溢價和社會流動：一項關於香港和台灣青年的比較研究

27604821.label: Project Objectives
27604821.value: The first analytical objective is to examine the college premium in first job socioeconomic status in Hong Kong and Taiwan based on analysis of the data from the Hong Kong Panel Study of Social Dynamics (HKPSSD) and Taiwan’s Panel Study of Family Dynamics (PSFD). Using conventional logit models, we will explore the inter-cohort difference in the relative probability of converting a college education into a middle-class (i.e., professional or managerial) occupation when people first enter the labor force, and investigate the potential influence of the college expansion on younger cohorts. The second analytical objective is to examine the college premium in wages in Hong Kong and Taiwan based on analysis of the data from multiple waves of the HK census/by-census and the Taiwan Social Change Survey (TSCS). Using a hierarchical age-period-cohort (APC) model, we will be able to disentangle the cohort effect from the age and period effects. We will examine the temporal change in the college-high school wage gap by age group, and investigate the potential influence of college expansion on younger workers. The third analytical objective is to examine the college premium in intergenerational mobility among young people (aged 20–29) in Hong Kong based on analysis of data from the HK census/by-census and the TSCS. Using rank-rank regression models, we will be able to capture the level of social fluidity in a way that is independent of cohort-specific occupational structure. We will examine the real change in circulation mobility in terms of occupational socioeconomic status (SEI) among young college graduates and non-college graduates, and investigate the potential influence of the college expansion on the upward mobility chances of young people, especially those from low-socioeconomic status (SES) families. The last analytical objective is to conduct a comparative study of the roles of macro-level factors that shape the diversity in college expansion processes and outcomes in Hong Kong and Taiwan. Both of these Chinese societies have been transforming their higher education system from elite to massive ones within a short period of time, but exhibit substantial heterogeneity in terms of their admission process, higher education governance and expansion strategies.

27604821.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27604821.value: A college degree has long been believed to be the key to socioeconomic success and a “great equalizer” that effectively promotes social mobility. However, the hypothesis that the expansion of higher education necessarily leads to an increase in income levels and a reduction in inequality has recently been challenged. In particular, the younger generations who have benefited from expanded educational opportunities may enjoy far less of a college premium and lower chances of mobility compared with earlier cohorts because of the oversupply of college graduates relative to demand and the deterioration in their average quality. In the proposed study, we will focus on two unique empirical cases that offer an ideal setting for investigating the link between college expansion and social mobility in recent cohorts: Hong Kong and Taiwan. The study of these two Chinese societies will provide us with a valuable comparative perspective, as both shifted from elite to mass higher education systems within a short period but exhibit substantial heterogeneity in terms of admission processes, higher education governance and expansion strategies. We will use four longitudinal datasets in Hong Kong and Taiwan to address the following questions: 1) How does the college premium in first job socioeconomic status vary by cohort, and has the premium become substantially smaller for recent cohorts affected by the college expansion? 2) How does the college premium in wages vary by age group, and has the premium become substantially smaller for younger workers affected by college expansion? 3) What is the difference in intergenerational mobility between young workers with and without a college degree, and has the college premium in mobility become substantially smaller since the college expansion? 4) How the diversity of college expansion processes and outcomes are shaped by contextual differences between the two education systems? The proposed project will make three potential contributions. Theoretically, we will bridge an important gap in the literature by systematically examining the interplay between educational expansion and cohort transformations in the college premium. Methodologically, taking advantage of long-term repeated cross-sectional datasets that span over four decades, we will use hierarchical age–period–cohort and rank–rank regression models to control for confounding factors in the cohort analysis related to age, period or changes in occupational structure. Practically, the cross-Strait comparative understanding gained through this project will help government and non-governmental agencies in both regions develop effective education and employment policies to resolve their youth problems. 大學文憑向來被看作是獲得社會經濟成功的關鍵和促進社會流動的“均衡器”。然而，最新的一些研究挑戰了大學擴張必然帶來收入水平上升和不平等下降的假設。特別是，由於大學畢業生的供過於求和綜合素質下降，青年一代雖然受益於擴增的教育機會但可能面臨大學溢價的下降。 在是項研究中，我們將關注兩個特別的案例，即香港和台灣，來探討在最近的世代中大學擴招和社會流動的關係。對這兩個華人社會的研究將會給我們提供一個寶貴的比較視角，因為她們都在很短的時間內實現了從精英教育到大眾教育的轉變，但同時在錄取過程，高校管理和擴張策略上又有很大的差異性。 我們將會使用到在香港和台灣的四個縱貫數據來回答以下問題：1）在初職地位獲得上的大學溢價是如何隨世代變化的，並且這一溢價是否受大學擴招影響而在最近的世代中顯著下降了？ 2）在工資收入上的大學溢價是如何隨年齡組變化的，並且這一溢價是否受大學擴招影響而在年輕的年齡組中顯著下降了？3）在有大學文憑和沒有大學文憑的年輕人中，他們的代際流動有何差別，並且在社會流動上的大學溢價是否在大學擴張以後顯著下降了？4） 兩個不同的教育體系的宏觀差異是如何形塑大學擴招過程和結果上的不同的？ 是項研究將做出三方面可能的貢獻。從理論而言，我們將會系統地檢驗教育擴張和大學溢價的世代變遷二者之間的關係，從而填補文獻中的重要空白。從方法而言，利用橫跨四十年的長期重複截面數據，我們將會使用多層APC模型和排序回歸模型來控制在世代分析中由於年齡，時期或者職業結構變遷所帶來的混淆因素。從現實而言，通過這一項目獲得的跨海峽比較理解將可以幫助兩地的政府和非政府組織完善其教育和就業政策以應對其青年問題。

27606721.label: Project Title(Chinese)
27606721.value: 酷兒理論和女性主義，日常生活，現代日本的女作家

27606721.label: Project Objectives
27606721.value: To contribute queer feminist research on Japanese women writers receiving limited attention in English-language research. In the form of a book monograph and article, my project on Japan will offer new perspectives from outside of an Anglocentric framework for English-language queer studies. Also, I will disseminate knowledge of these writers through a monthly podcast and public talks for general audiences. To promote knowledge of prominent Anglo-American queer and feminist theories of affect and the everyday that are largely unutilized in both English- and Japanese-language scholarship on Japanese literature. In addition to my English-language monograph, article, and presentations, I plan to give a series of Japanese-language talks for literary and activist communities dedicated to feminist and LGBTQ issues in Japan. To use a queer approach to fill in a gap in research on female homosocial and homoerotic relations in Japanese literature, complicating existing scholarship on gender that tends to assume a homogeneous female reading community centered on Japanese women’s writing. Moreover, existing queer scholarship in Japanese studies often deals with male homosocial and homoerotic relations. To complicate expectations concerning the “feminist” nature of literary production by Japanese women. Attention to Japanese women writers often takes the form of canonization premised on their critique of gender and sexual norms. Instead, I focus on making visible sexist biases in both intellectual and popular discourses related to aspects of the everyday associated with women, such as conventionality, routine, lack of progress, and the trivial. To touch upon related developments in Japan surrounding transnational flows of women’s writing, feminisms, and translation. Research findings from my article will inform my promotion of women’s literary voices through new networks of translators, writers, readers, activists, and scholars in Japan and Hong Kong.
